study.system: yellow-bellied marmots; DNA methylation from 73 females

editor_summary: Needs responses to reviewer criticisms and editorial concerns, and agreement among reviewers that hibernation slows ageing in marmots; highlight all changes in Word.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, informative and exceptionally novel study of a putative mechanism, but questions whether the epigenetic clock is autocorrelated.
strengths: some of the first data exploring putative mechanism

comments.issue: Selecting CpG sites that relate to chronological age may make the clock autocorrelated or self-fulfilling.
comments.request: Provide independent assurance that the clock relationship is not an artifact of site selection.
comments.quote: I think my real question is that are the authors autocorrelating? In Fig. S2, examples of CpG sites that do not relate to chronological age are provided.

comments.issue: Not all hibernators are long lived; short-lived species are not represented.
comments.quote: Not all hibernators are long lived and I would think the authors may wish to look at some of the shorter lived species

comments.issue: The 2018 Bieber et al. paper linking hibernation, reproduction, aging and mast-year resources is not addressed.
comments.request: Address Bieber, Turnbill and Ruf 2018 in the manuscript.
comments.quote: Claudia Bieber, Chris Turnbill, and Thomas Ruf published a paper in 2018 (Scientific Reports) that should be addressed.

comments.issue: The predictable RMBL climate may limit the reliability of the clocks in more variable climates.
comments.request: Discuss whether the clocks would break down in more variable climates.
comments.quote: if you were to take a hibernator that lived in a more variable climate, would there be a breakdown in the reliability of the EC and EPM?

comments.issue: The claim that energy use is mainly lipid based ignores carbohydrate-dominated interbout arousals.
comments.request: Revise the energy-metabolism passage to include interbout arousals.
comments.quote: carbohydrate metabolism dominates in the interbout arousal and since ~70% of seasonal energy stores are consumed in these IBAs

reviews.assessment: Unique, important dataset and intriguing analysis, but the main hibernation-stasis result may be an artifact of cyclic cubic splines.
strengths: likely to interest ecological/evolutionary epigenetics researchers

comments.issue: Cyclic cubic splines must meet at year endpoints, so unsampled hibernation may be fitted with an artifactual decreasing trend.
comments.request: Test the claim with analyses not relying on cyclic splines.
comments.quote: the result in figure 2b could be a consequence of the usage of cyclic cubic splines, combined with the absence of samples during hibernation, rather than evidence for a slowing of aging itself.

comments.issue: The power and false-positive simulations could not be replicated because they failed with convergence errors.
comments.request: Fix the simulations and provide reproducible power/false-positive estimates.
comments.quote: in trying to recreate these simulations from the R code provided, I was unable to complete more than a small number of simulations

comments.issue: The hypothesis can be tested by comparing epigenetic states of animals just before versus just after hibernation.
comments.request: Compare pre-hibernation and post-emergence epigenetic states directly.
comments.quote: comparisons of partial epigenetic states just prior to entering hibernation should be significantly higher, on average, than those for animals just emerging

comments.issue: Longitudinal within-individual trajectories across seasons are not analysed, and the number of repeated samples is unclear.
comments.request: Analyse repeated measures longitudinally and report samples per individual.
comments.quote: repeated measures within the same individuals could reveal how an individual's epigenetic trajectory changes longitudinally across seasons

comments.issue: It is not shown that nonlinear/spline fits significantly improve over simple linear fits.
comments.request: Quantitatively compare spline versus linear fits for clocks, EPM and sites.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to see direct, quantitative comparisons that show that more complex nonlinear/spline fits actually significantly improve over simple linear fits

comments.issue: Gene set enrichment with only 126 associated CpGs and >60,000 tested sets is likely poorly calibrated.
comments.request: Drop gene sets with few tested sites and uninterpretable terms.
comments.quote: I am concerned that these results stem from poorly calibrated tests where only a small number of sites are even associated with a given functional term.

comments.issue: Quality control criteria used to exclude 11 samples are not described.
comments.request: Describe the quality control that excluded the 11 samples.
comments.quote: Lines 85: What quality control was performed to exclude the 11 samples?

comments.issue: The significance threshold is used without justification.
comments.request: Justify the chosen significance threshold.
comments.quote: Lines 226: Why was this significance threshold chosen?

comments.issue: Non-linear age-methylation patterns may be technical rather than biological, so the conclusion is not definitive.
comments.request: Pull back on the non-linear aging conclusion throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: The fact that 66% of age-associated sites had an EDF>2 could be consistent with either, but is not necessarily definitive effective of non-linear aging

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-presented case study with only minor suggestions about the methylation array and additional reporting.
strengths: interesting case study not previously explored

comments.issue: The Illumina array's CpG selection may guarantee enrichment for polycomb targets and developmental pathways.
comments.request: Discuss whether enrichment would persist with non-targeted CpG selection.
comments.quote: due to the selection of CpG sites in the Illumina array, the sites used for an epigenetic clock under this system will always be enriched for polycomb complex targets

comments.issue: Whether negatively correlated CpG sites were included in the clock is unclear.
comments.request: State whether negatively correlated sites were included.
comments.quote: Line 123. Were sites with a negative correlation also included?

comments.issue: The motivation for using a generalized additive mixed model is not explained.
comments.request: Add one or two sentences explaining why a GAMM was used.
comments.quote: 1-2 sentences of why a Generalized Additive Mixed Model was used may help readers who are not familiar with the method

comments.issue: The clock's median absolute error rate and relative error are not reported.
comments.request: Report median absolute error and relative error for the clock.
comments.quote: Can the authors also provide the median absolute error rate and relative error?

comments.issue: The number of promoter CpGs hypermethylated with age is not given.
comments.request: Provide the specific number of hypermethylated promoter CpGs.
comments.quote: ‘Most CpGs in promoter regions were hypermethylated with age’ – can the specific number be provided?

title: Hibernation slows epigenetic ageing in yellow-bellied marmots

study.system: grassland aboveground biomass; meta-analysis of drought experiments and observations

editor_summary: Editor flags Reviewer 2's concern that observational and experimental systems represent different community types (different species richness), which complicates the conclusions, and expects additional or modified analyses.

reviews.assessment: Well-conducted and refreshingly nuanced, but the novelty claims, introduction framing and the experiment-versus-observation asymmetry need work.
strengths: appreciation of benefits of experiments despite limitations

comments.issue: Observational studies may overestimate drought effects because droughts co-occur with correlated factors such as heatwaves.
comments.request: Reflect on the possibility that observations overestimate drought effects, not only that experiments underestimate them.
comments.quote: droughts almost never come alone, but are often accompanied by other extreme events, such as extremely high temperatures

comments.issue: The introduction is too methodological and lacks ecological reasons why drought effects may differ between approaches.
comments.request: Add ecology-driven hypotheses, for example about edge effects in small experimental plots.
comments.quote: The introduction is rather methodological, but would be more interesting if also more attention was spent on ecological reasons on why effects of drought may differ

comments.issue: The introduction is unclear about the novelty because it says both that no comparison exists and that few exist.
comments.request: Clarify what exactly is novel about the comparison.
comments.quote: at some point, the authors mention that no other study has compared the drought effects between observational and experimental studies using a meta-analysis

comments.issue: The claim at L73-74 that synthesis studies have not compared the two approaches contradicts the earlier text about existing comparisons.
comments.request: Make the statements consistent and explicit about existing comparisons.
comments.quote: synthesis studies have not compared these two approaches”: this seems to somewhat contrast with “A recent overview of ecological responses to global change found that an overwhelming majority of meta-analyses covered either experimental or observational

comments.issue: It is not stated explicitly that the comparison corrects for confounding factors such as drought severity and duration.
comments.request: State explicitly that the reported comparison is after correcting for confounding factors.
comments.quote: I assume this is after correcting for confounding factors, such as drought severity, duration, etc, right?

comments.issue: The phrase 'positively related to' is ambiguous for negative drought effects and prone to misinterpretation.
comments.request: Use clearer wording such as less negative or more negative.
comments.quote: since effects of drought on biomass are typically negative, I am not sure whether “positively related to” in this context relates to less negative, or more negative

comments.issue: The cited meta-analysis on warming effects is based on a small fraction of the literature and other reviews show a more nuanced picture.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited evidence base and the more nuanced findings of other reviews.
comments.quote: the given meta-analysis was based on a very small fraction of the literature that is actually available, and some other reviews point at a more nuanced picture

comments.issue: A study was excluded because precipitation exclusion happened in winter, but in some climates winter is the main dry season.
comments.request: Re-check the excluded study and exclude it only if winter drought is irrelevant there.
comments.quote: I saw that one study was excluded because it assessed precipitation exclusion in winter. In some climates (e.g. in eastern South Africa) winter is the main dry season.

comments.issue: An existing synthesis of observational and experimental droughts is listed but not distinguished from the current study.
comments.request: Make clear how the current manuscript differs from this existing work.
comments.quote: Since one other study “Studies synthesising both observational and experimental droughts” is listed, it would be good if it becomes clear how the current manuscripts differs from this existing work.

comments.issue: Studies in the supplementary material are not cited in the main text, so their authors do not get credit.
comments.request: Cite these studies in the main text as well.
comments.quote: personally, I think it’s good if these studies are cited in the main text as well (not only in the supplement), so that the authors of the original studies get credit for their work

reviews.assessment: Important question and very well written, but potentially fundamental flaws in the analyses and data representation must be addressed.

comments.issue: The analyses and representation of the data contain potentially fundamental flaws that threaten the bold claim.
comments.request: Address these flaws to support the claim that experiments underestimate drought effects.
comments.quote: there are a few potentially fundamental flaws in the analyses and representation of the data that need to be addressed

comments.issue: Details omitted from the methods, results and figures make the results difficult to interpret.
comments.request: Provide the missing methodological and reporting details.
comments.quote: there are a number of details that have been omitted in the methods, results, and figures that make interpretation difficult

reviews.assessment: Very positive about the meta-analytic handling and reporting, with a few comments on response variables, scale and the generality of the conclusion.
strengths: exemplary search, data handling, statistics and sensitivity analyses

comments.issue: Only aboveground biomass and NPP are analysed, so it is unknown whether the experiment-observation difference holds for other responses.
comments.request: Analyse other frequently measured response variables to test whether the difference is general.
comments.quote: I am pretty sure that other response variables have been measured frequently in these experiments and it would be very informative to see whether the observed differences are general across responses

comments.issue: The discussion lists many differences but does not make the small-plot edge-effect difference explicit.
comments.request: Make the main scale difference between experiments and observations explicit.
comments.quote: why it is not be made more explicit (row 148ff talks about a lot of differences, but does not make the main difference very clear)

comments.issue: The proposed edge-effect explanation could be directly tested using experiments of different sizes and estimates of natural drought extent.
comments.request: Test plot-size effects and estimate the spatial extent of observed droughts.
comments.quote: if there would not be a way to directly test this - at least experiments of different size must exist and it may be possible to also estimate the spatial extent of observed droughts

comments.issue: The claim that experiments underestimate global-change effects is less general than stated, since experiments can exaggerate treatment differences.
comments.request: Nuance the claim and discuss the contrasting evidence from other studies.
comments.quote: this is less general than stated here. Experiments tend to overdo the differences between treatments and control

comments.issue: The highly relevant Korell et al. 2020 paper is missing from the discussion.
comments.request: Include Korell et al. and shift the discussion to why drought experiments especially underestimate effects.
comments.quote: The Korell paper is so close to the topic here that it should be included in the discussion.

title: Field experiments underestimate aboveground biomass response to drought

study.system: tadpoles; lab gut-microbiota depletion, thermal and fitness assays

editor_summary: Agrees with R3 that microbiome-diversity causality is not shown, but frames it as a clarity issue: distinguish manipulation of diversity as a treatment from diversity as a driver, especially in title and Conclusion.

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the study and its physiological depth but asks for clearer caveats, replication and methodological detail before extrapolating to natural conditions.
strengths: important steps linking host microbiome and ectotherm fitness

comments.issue: Effect size for thermal tolerance is small relative to acclimation and evolutionary adaptation, yet results are extrapolated to natural conditions.
comments.request: Discuss and acknowledge the small effect size before extrapolating to natural conditions.
comments.quote: the effect size of thermal tolerance is small (expected) compared to acclimation responses and because of evolutionary adaptation. This should be discussed and acknowledged.

comments.issue: Pond water storage alters the microbial community, so the seeding treatment may not represent natural exposure.
comments.request: Discuss how storage affects the microorganisms used for exposure.
comments.quote: storage of the pond water affects the microorganisms, which should be discussed.

comments.issue: The autoclaved-versus-natural pond water approach is not discussed relative to alternatives.
comments.request: Add a section comparing this approach with microbiome transplantation or single strains.
comments.quote: The ms would benefit on a section discussing this approach compared to e.g. transplantation of gut microbiomes or single strains.

comments.issue: 16S profiling reported at phylum level is uninformative; finer taxonomic resolution is possible.
comments.request: Add a supplementary table or heat map with ASVs identified to the lowest taxonomic level.
comments.quote: authors could include a table/heat map (in supplementary) with ASV identified to the lowest possible taxonomic level or classes

comments.issue: Sample sizes per trait are scattered across legends and text, with some missing.
comments.request: Add a short methods section summarising sample sizes for all traits.
comments.quote: To me it was difficult to get an overview of the sample size for the different traits investigated

comments.issue: Single clutch and n=11 for thermal tolerance may make the estimates pseudoreplicated.
comments.request: Clarify the unit of replication and address the pseudoreplication concern.
comments.quote: given that (as I understand it) a single clutch of eggs was used, n=11 for thermal tolerance estimates is somewhat low.

comments.issue: Key papers linking microbiomes to conservation are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Cite and discuss the relevant conservation-microbiome literature.
comments.quote: From a conservation point of view several papers nicely address and discuss this and should be acknowledged

comments.issue: Stress proteins such as Hsp70, potentially relevant to thermal responses, were not investigated.
comments.request: Consider investigating the role of stress proteins in this setup.
comments.quote: Hsp70 has been found important for thermal stress responses and could be relevant in your setup as well.

comments.issue: Manuscript is repetitive across methods, results and discussion.
comments.request: Shorten the manuscript and remove repetitions.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors shorten the ms. There are some repetitions when comparing M&M and the result/discussion section and in M&M.

comments.issue: Discussion of the small differences and buffering by aquatic environments is underdeveloped.
comments.request: Expand this passage on effect sizes and implications.
comments.quote: The differences are small compared to what researchers have found in other systems, but an aquatic environment is also more buffered, so it may have important implications.

comments.issue: Statement at L261 lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Include references.
comments.quote: L. 261: Include references.

comments.issue: Mortality difference rests on a single replicate with n=39.
comments.request: Repeat the experiment at least three times.
comments.quote: Given that n=39 and there is a difference of dead individuals of 2-3 between treatments when exposed to 32C for ten days it would be nice to replicate the experiment at least three times.

comments.issue: Infection could affect the conclusions and is not ruled out.
comments.request: Rule out effects of infection on the conclusions.
comments.quote: L. 361: Can you rule out any effects of infection affecting your conclusions?

comments.issue: Rationale for conducting two experiments is explained too late.
comments.request: Explain early why two experiments were conducted.
comments.quote: L. 534-538: At an early stage it should be made clear why two experiments were conducted.

comments.issue: Rabbit chow use may affect the conclusions.
comments.request: Address whether rabbit chow affects the conclusions.
comments.quote: L. 589: Could the use of rabbit chow potentially affect the conclusions?

comments.issue: The measured endpoint (time or temperature) is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify what is measured and the endpoint.
comments.quote: L. 606: So what do you measure? Endpoint? Time or temperature? Specify.

comments.issue: No explanation is given for measuring facial symmetry.
comments.request: Add a brief methods sentence explaining why facial symmetry is measured.
comments.quote: L. 620: Maybe include a brief sentence in M&M as to why facial symmetry is measured.

comments.issue: Intestine splitting procedure and which parts were used are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how the intestine was split and which parts were used.
comments.quote: L. 638: Split in what way? Were all parts of the intestine included for both traits?

comments.issue: Figures do not report means or medians for all traits.
comments.request: Present the mean or median for all traits.
comments.quote: Figures: Could you present the mean or median for all traits?

reviews.assessment: Well-written and valuable study; asks to rename the depleted treatment and discuss bacterial sources plus a few method details.
strengths: appropriate methods, experimental design and statistics

comments.issue: The label depleted is misleading because bacterial load is similar to the colonized group.
comments.request: Rename the treatment, for example to disrupted.
comments.quote: Flow cytometry cell counting indicates that bacterial load is similar in both “depleted” and “colonized” groups.

comments.issue: Sources of gut bacteria in the depleted group are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss possible sources such as spore-formers or egg-associated bacteria.
comments.quote: Could you add a discussion on the possible sources of the gut bacteria in the depleted tadpole group?

comments.issue: DNA was extracted directly from water without concentration; references for this are missing.
comments.request: Provide references for studies extracting DNA directly from water samples.
comments.quote: Can the author provide references for other studies that extracted DNA directly from the water samples?

comments.issue: Number of water samples per group is missing from Supplementary Figure 3c.
comments.request: Indicate sample numbers for the Fresh and Stored groups.
comments.quote: please indicate the number of water samples in each group (“Fresh” and “Stored”)

reviews.assessment: Recommends rejection: the causal claim for microbiome diversity is conceptually flawed and unsupported, with many statistical, reporting and framing problems.

comments.issue: Treating biodiversity as a causal object with properties independent of its constituents is conceptually erroneous.
comments.request: Reframe biodiversity as a phenomenon rather than a causal agent.
comments.quote: there is a tendency towards the reification of biodiversity as a real object with causal properties (in the Lockean real, essential sense)

comments.issue: Effect could be caused by one bacterial species rather than community diversity.
comments.request: Test piecemeal addition of different bacteria before claiming a diversity effect.
comments.quote: it is possible that only one bacteria species/genus is causing the response of interest (e.g. thermal tolerance), and not necessarily an increasingly diverse community

comments.issue: Links to climate change and warming are overstated.
comments.request: Tone down the climate-change framing.
comments.quote: I also have raised issues (below) pertaining to overstated links to climate change/warming and concerns with some of the analyses.

comments.issue: Analysis code is not provided (also requested at L631-635, L666-670, L785-786), so the analyses cannot be evaluated.
comments.request: Share the R code via GitHub or a similar repository.
comments.quote: Importantly, I could not find the code used for the analyses used in R. I cannot fully evaluate your manuscript until I am able to see how you did your analyses.

comments.issue: Experimental designs are complicated and lack an overview.
comments.request: Add a figure or table giving an overview of the experimental designs.
comments.quote: It would also be useful to include a figure or table giving an overview of your experimental designs.

comments.issue: Global conservation priority is used as scientific impetus instead of biodiversity phenomena.
comments.request: Reframe the study justification around biodiversity science.
comments.quote: Biodiversity in an ecological or evolutionary context certainly is a phenomena of scientific and biological interest and I think it would be best to reframe your study justification around this.

comments.issue: Role of commensal bacteria in ectotherms is understudied rather than unknown.
comments.request: Avoid claiming the role is unknown.
comments.quote: Is the role of commensal bacteria really unknown in ectotherms? Or just understudied?

comments.issue: Results do not support causal claims about climate change.
comments.request: Remove the extension to causal climate-change claims.
comments.quote: Additionally, your results do not readily expand to causal claims of climate change.

comments.issue: A mosquito study is poor justification for a vertebrate ectotherm study.
comments.request: Better justify the hypotheses.
comments.quote: While insects are certainly ectotherms, this seems like a poor justification for a study examining vertebrate ectotherms and their susceptibility to global warming.

comments.issue: Focus on global conservation priorities rather than mechanisms of biodiversity change.
comments.request: Change the focus to mechanisms of biodiversity change.
comments.quote: Again, I would change your focus on global conservation priorities to the mechanisms of biodiversity change.

comments.issue: Importance of individual thermal tolerance for conservation is not justified.
comments.request: Justify why individual thermal tolerance matters for populations and species.
comments.quote: you need to better justify why the thermal tolerance of individuals are important for conservation and biodiversity, which is (normally) the domain of populations and species.

comments.issue: Plasticity is introduced but not developed throughout the paper.
comments.request: Discuss plasticity more, including in the discussion.
comments.quote: Yes! Plasticity is important but could be talked about more throughout, including the discussion.

comments.issue: Abstract exaggerates novelty by equating lack of complete understanding with unknown.
comments.request: Revise the abstract and avoid exaggerating novelty.
comments.quote: I know it makes your paper sound less exciting, but we should be cautious of exaggerating the novelty of results.

comments.issue: Corals and sea anemones discourse may not be helpful.
comments.request: Reconsider the relevance of this literature.
comments.quote: Is a discourse on corals and sea anemones really that helpful?

comments.issue: What counts as a manipulative study is left vague.
comments.request: Define what is meant by a manipulative study.
comments.quote: What do the authors consider a manipulative study? This seems vague.

comments.issue: Effects of the whole microbiome versus constituent bacteria are conflated.
comments.request: Clarify which level of effects the study addresses.
comments.quote: Effects of the microbiome as a whole? Effects of constituent bacteria of a given microbiome on the host? This sentence needs more clarification as there is much nuance here.

comments.issue: No standard is given for calling the experiment manipulative.
comments.request: State the standard by which the experiment is manipulative.
comments.quote: The authors claim their experiment is manipulative. By what standard?

comments.issue: Diversity was depleted but total bacterial abundance apparently stayed similar, so the treatment label is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify that diversity, not abundance, was depleted.
comments.quote: you should clarify that diversity was depleted, as your flow results seem to indicate total abundances stayed similar.

comments.issue: Results may reflect one bacterial species rather than microbial community diversity.
comments.request: Acknowledge that the demonstration does not establish a diversity effect.
comments.quote: I would argue that your results do not necessarily support this demonstration. Instead of microbial communities (and by proxy microbial community diversity), it could conceivably be only one bacteria species causing the thermal-tolerance results.

comments.issue: Link to global climate change and warming is overstated.
comments.request: Tone down the climate-change link.
comments.quote: Also, I think the link to global climate change/warming is overstated and should be toned down.

comments.issue: Keeping pond water at 4C altered the microbial community used for seeding.
comments.request: Assess and discuss how cold storage changed the seeding community.
comments.quote: you kept the pond water at 4C which almost certainly had an affect on the resulting microbial community present to seeding.

comments.issue: Rationale for reducing microorganisms is unclear and the cited paper used no such dilution.
comments.request: Explain why dilution was used despite the citation mismatch.
comments.quote: Why did you want to reduce the microorganisms available for colonization? The cited Knutie et al. paper doesn’t use the dilution that you performed as far as I can tell.

comments.issue: Timing of adult exposure and tadpole spawning relative to treatments is unclear.
comments.request: State when adults and tadpoles entered each treatment.
comments.quote: Were all adults kept in diluted pond water? Or were the adults partitioned into the respective treatments post-capture?

comments.issue: 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing is mislabelled; RNA is not sequenced (also at L274-275).
comments.request: Use 16S rDNA or 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing.
comments.quote: I would change “16S rRNA amplicon sequencing” to either “16S rDNA amplicon sequencing” or “16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing”. You’re not sequencing RNA.

comments.issue: Fresh and stored pond water communities differ substantially, but richness was not compared.
comments.request: At minimum compare richness between fresh and stored pond water communities.
comments.quote: You should at minimum do a richness comparison to see to what extent you are introducing the same bacteria species that are from the pond

comments.issue: Phylum-level comparisons cannot support claims that treatments represent the pond community.
comments.request: Use the higher-resolution data instead of phylum-level comparisons.
comments.quote: Your are claiming the concerns raised above are okay because there is similar phyla representation? You have higher resolution data and should use that.

comments.issue: The stability sentence is unclear about what stability means.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of stability after 4C storage.
comments.quote: I don’t understand this sentence. Stability of what? Do you mean temporal compositional stability post-4C storage? This needs to be clarified.

comments.issue: Stability after 4C storage suggests the seeding community is not representative of the source pond.
comments.request: Discuss the consequences of using a non-representative seeding community.
comments.quote: Also, I would think being more stable post 4C storage indicates that the seeding community you are using is not functionally representative of the pond from which the frogs originally came from.

comments.issue: It is unclear when the microbiome was altered relative to treatment.
comments.request: Clarify the timing of microbiome alteration after treatment.
comments.quote: Altered the microbiome after your treatment? This is related to line 95-96 comments.

comments.issue: Significant beta-dispersion differences undermine the PERMANOVA results (also flagged at L137, L140-142, L277-279).
comments.request: Reanalyse accounting for heterogeneous group dispersions.
comments.quote: All of your beta dispersion results indicate significant differences. This indicates that significant differences in your PERMANOVA analyses are the results of differences in group dispersions.

comments.issue: Dispersion differences do not support the claim of different beta-diversity.
comments.request: Revise the beta-diversity claim.
comments.quote: The significant dispersion results do not support your claim of significantly different beta-diversity.

comments.issue: High-temperature treatment description is misleading; figures show differences shrink as temperature rises.
comments.request: Correct the misleading statement and show the analysis code.
comments.quote: I think this is misleading for the high temp treatment. The supp figs 3a-d seem to show a decreasing temperature effect between the to two treatment groups as temp increases

comments.issue: Increased beta-dispersion is not evidence of reduced diversity.
comments.request: Reinterpret the result in terms of within-group dispersion.
comments.quote: This doesn’t really mean reduced diversity. It means more within group dispersion differences.

comments.issue: Speculative material at L143-147 belongs in the discussion.
comments.request: Move the speculation to the discussion.
comments.quote: This seems speculative and should likely be in the discussion.

comments.issue: Direction of causation between host and microbiome is inconsistent across the paper.
comments.request: Make the assumed direction of effect clear.
comments.quote: Does the host regulate the microbiome, or the microbiome regulate the host? You seem to be switching your story throughout.

comments.issue: Focus on phylum-level differences instead of genus-level data.
comments.request: Shift the analysis to genus-level differences.
comments.quote: I think you need to shift your focus to genus level differences instead of phylum level (you have the data!)

comments.issue: Supplementary Table 2 headers suggest treatments were confounded with temperature.
comments.request: Correct the table headers and clarify which genera were affected.
comments.quote: The Table headers seem off. It looks like you had only the colonized treatment at 14C and only the depleted treatment at 22C. Is that right?

comments.issue: FDR correction method is not stated (also at L926).
comments.request: State the FDR method used, for example BH.
comments.quote: In the legend you indicate you did an FDR correction, please indicate the method used (assume BH?).

comments.issue: Speculative material at L154-157 belongs in the discussion.
comments.request: Move the speculation to the discussion.
comments.quote: This is speculative and should be in the discussion.

comments.issue: Claim that total bacterial numbers are unchanged despite diversity differences is doubtful.
comments.request: Clarify how diversity can change while total abundance stays the same.
comments.quote: You are claiming the total number of bacteria in the gut, between treatments, (even with different diversity, if true) is unchanged!!!

comments.issue: Claim that the experiment represents the wild is doubtful given 4C storage of pond water.
comments.request: Soften the claim that conditions represent the wild.
comments.quote: There is doubt about your claim that this represents “the wild” due to the issues with the pond water being stored at 4C.

comments.issue: Alternative trade-off explanation for accelerated growth and developmental defects is not considered.
comments.request: Discuss the predation-benefit versus developmental-defect trade-off.
comments.quote: This seems like a trade-off: as a faster time to larger size could be protective against predation, but coming with the trade-off of developmental defects.

comments.issue: A direct link between microbial communities and thermal tolerance is not conclusively shown.
comments.request: Remove or qualify the direct-link claim.
comments.quote: No, you don’t conclusively show this “direct” link! (host-associated microbial communities and thermal tolerance)

comments.issue: Observed changes may be due to a single bacterial species, not community diversity.
comments.request: Acknowledge the single-species alternative.
comments.quote: The changes you observed may be due to only one bacterial species, and having nothing to do with community diversity per se.

comments.issue: Claim at L261-264 is speculative and unsupported by the data.
comments.request: Remove or support the speculative claim.
comments.quote: This claim seems speculative and is not well supported by your data.

comments.issue: Conservation framing and species-level threat language are inappropriate for the study.
comments.request: Focus on biodiversity rather than species conservation.
comments.quote: Some species do better. Also, a threat to species imparts an ethico-normative claim which has problems as previously discussed.

comments.issue: Fitness is not defined or measured explicitly.
comments.request: Define and state how fitness is measured.
comments.quote: Line 270: How are you defining/measuring fitness?

comments.issue: The second experiment is not a repeat; it uses different pond water and geography (LA versus PA).
comments.request: Stop describing the second experiment as a repeat.
comments.quote: No! First this is not a repeated experiment as it is a different experiment (different pond water origins, from a very different geography, LA vs PA).

comments.issue: Ten-day extreme temperature exposures are unrealistic and not relevant to climate scenarios.
comments.request: Remove or justify the extreme-temperature section.
comments.quote: These are all very extreme temps for long periods of time (10 days). Under what scenarios do you expect to see this outside of a lab?

comments.issue: Emphasis on microbial community treatments is questionable given confounding with temperature.
comments.request: Reconsider the interpretation of the community treatment effect.
comments.quote: This makes me question the emphasis you put on microbial community “treatments”.

comments.issue: Claim at L317-318 is not supported by the results.
comments.request: Remove or support the claim.
comments.quote: Lines 317-318: No, you didn’t show this.

comments.issue: Heatwave projection is cited from gray literature and lacks daily temperature fluctuations.
comments.request: Cite the technical document and clarify whether fluctuations are included.
comments.quote: The publication you cite does show a high estimate of ~34C in SE and SW PA, but does this include daily temperature fluctuations? The publication you cite is gray literature.

comments.issue: Claims about microbial speciation on hosts are speculative with too much uncertainty.
comments.request: Remove or substantially qualify the speculation.
comments.quote: This is speculative, and there is too much uncertainty to make this claim.

comments.issue: Causality is again assigned to the entire community (also at L405).
comments.request: Stop attributing causality to the whole community.
comments.quote: The same issue of assigning causality to the entire community is still relevant to this section.

comments.issue: Body size may also be important for predator escape, an alternative explanation not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss body size effects on predator escape.
comments.quote: Increased body size is also likely important to predator escape.

comments.issue: Something in the autoclaved water could cause the observed differences.
comments.request: Test or discuss the autoclaved-water alternative.
comments.quote: Line 464-467: Something in autoclaved water causing the differences?

comments.issue: Results in this section undermine the earlier claims.
comments.request: Reconcile these results with the earlier claims.
comments.quote: Lines 486-490: These results seem to undermine your claims on the previous section.

comments.issue: Diversity was not conclusively shown to be the causal factor.
comments.request: Withdraw the claim that diversity is causal.
comments.quote: NO! Diversity was not conclusively shown to be the causal factor for your results!

comments.issue: Claim that work on siblings directly informs climate-change responses is not established.
comments.request: Qualify the link between individual-level results and climate responses.
comments.quote: But you seem to be claiming earlier in your paper (CHECK WHERE) that your work focused on individuals (siblings in this case) directly informs climate change responses, which is not well established.

comments.issue: Collection location is not reported.
comments.request: Report GPS coordinates or add a map in the supplement.
comments.quote: Please report the location. GPS coordinates would suffice, a map in supplemental would be even better.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether fresh pond water was extracted before or only after cooling.
comments.request: Clarify whether the -80C samples were used for the fresh comparison.
comments.quote: If you didn’t do an extraction immediately from pond water (or frozen pond water), but only after cooling, then you didn’t look at the fresh pond water microbial community.

comments.issue: Bacteria transferred on embryos from parents could confound treatment differences.
comments.request: Test parent-derived bacteria or discuss this alternative.
comments.quote: How can you be certain that the differences you are seeing between the pond water treatments are not from some interaction with this seeded host microbiome?

comments.issue: Sibling-based results may not represent the population.
comments.request: Discuss the limited genetic variation and representativeness.
comments.quote: what if the various stress responses and heat tolerances you see are not representative of the population but rather a small section of a distributional tail (siblings)?

comments.issue: Acute assay ramp rate of 0.5C per minute is too rapid to support climate-warming claims.
comments.request: Justify or revise the assay and its relevance to warming.
comments.quote: Acute thermal tolerance assay at a temperature increase of 0.5C/minute seems too rapid for making claims about climate warming. Is this realistic?

comments.issue: n used as a random effect may be too low for lme4; model comparisons and AICs are not reported.
comments.request: Report model comparisons and AICs and justify the random-effect structure.
comments.quote: Your n designated as a random effect might be too low for the numerical methods used in lme4. Also, did you compare different factors in your models? Do you have AICs you could report?

comments.issue: Log transformation is not shown to normalise cell counts and is not justified (also at L824).
comments.request: Show that the log transform improved normality and justify its use.
comments.quote: Did the log transform actually normalize your cell counts? Can you show us in supplemental?

comments.issue: Gosner stage is missing for 12 of 48 samples in the Zenodo raw data.
comments.request: Explain why Gosner stage is NA for these samples.
comments.quote: Why is Gosner stage NA for 12/48 in your Mitochondrial Enzyme Assay raw data sheet on Zenodo?

comments.issue: Whether sample pooling is reflected in the enzyme results is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how pooling is reflected in the enzyme activity results.
comments.quote: Is the pooling of samples reflected in your results of mitochondrial enzyme activity?

comments.issue: Pooling procedure is insufficiently described; averaging may propagate error.
comments.request: Describe the pooling procedure and address error propagation.
comments.quote: More details on your pooling procedure needs to be given. Using averages in models which are then used for statistical comparisons may lead to error propagation.

comments.issue: Outlier removal criterion is not explained.
comments.request: State how outliers were identified before removal.
comments.quote: How was the outlier determined prior to removal from analysis?

comments.issue: No mortality at 22C is not reported in the results.
comments.request: Report the absence of mortality at 22C in the survival results.
comments.quote: Did you mention the no mortality at 22C in your results for survival under heat stress?

comments.issue: Carry-over from the previous experiment and captivity could confound the metabolic rate results (also L831-833).
comments.request: Be transparent about reusing animals and address carry-over effects.
comments.quote: Do possible changes in the microbiome in these samples from the previous experiment carry over to the results of this experiment?

comments.issue: Switching to additive models at this point is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the use of additive models.
comments.quote: Why did you decide to start using additive models here?

comments.issue: Rarefaction is used without justification amid ongoing debate.
comments.request: Justify why the data were rarefied.
comments.quote: I think you need to better justify why you rarefied your data.

title: Experimental manipulation of microbiota reduces host thermal tolerance and fitness under heat stress in a vertebrate ectotherm

study.system: E. coli toxin-antitoxin ParE3-ParD3; deep mutational scanning

reviews.assessment: High-quality, systematic study; asks for more biological context, clarification of experimental conditions, and several minor analyses.
strengths: systematic, quantitatively detailed dissection of suppressor mutations
model distinguishing specific and non-specific suppressors

comments.issue: The Introduction omits Diss and Lehner (2018), a directly relevant DMS study of an interacting protein pair.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Diss and Lehner in the Introduction.
comments.quote: The Diss and Lehner (elife, 2018) paper is relevant here but is not cited directly in the Introduction.

comments.issue: Conclusions and even the model R-squared closely resemble Diss and Lehner (2018) but this overlap is not commented on.
comments.request: Comment on the overlap with Diss and Lehner in Results or Discussion.
comments.quote: Even the R-squared value for the model here (89%, Ext. Data Figure 9) is similar to that for the corresponding model from Diss and Lehner 2018

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'as above' refers to and how the suppressor-scan antitoxin concentrations relate to the antitoxin DMS concentration.
comments.request: Clarify the antitoxin concentrations and their relation to the DMS scan.
comments.quote: Firstly, it is not clear what ‘as above’ is referring to as the section immediately above describes the DMS screen performed in the absence of the antitoxin

comments.issue: Concentrations used are not related to natural [antitoxin]:[toxin] ratios; natural antitoxin excess could buffer disruptive mutations and remove the need for suppressors.
comments.request: Discuss the concentrations relative to physiological ratios and this buffering possibility.
comments.quote: Finally – and most importantly – it is not clear how these two antitoxin concentrations relate to the [antitoxin]:[toxin] ratios we would expect to see in nature under physiological conditions.

comments.issue: The paper emphasises non-specificity but does not discuss the small fraction of neutral toxin mutations that can suppress disruptive antitoxin mutations.
comments.request: Discuss these fractions explicitly, including their therapeutic implications.
comments.quote: virtually no emphasis has been placed on the fraction of neutral toxin mutations that can serve as either type of suppressor

comments.issue: The wording about mutations that 'arise' is misleading because the study concerns mutations that can be tolerated by selection.
comments.request: Reword the sentence for clarity.
comments.quote: The current wording is misleading as this manuscript is not about which mutations arise spontaneously but instead about mutations that can arise and be tolerated by selection.

comments.issue: An oligomerization region is referenced before ParD3-ParE3 oligomer formation has been introduced.
comments.request: Describe oligomer formation and its role earlier in the manuscript.
comments.quote: This sentence refers to an oligomerization region but the fact that ParD3-ParE3 even forms oligomers is not mentioned before this point in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Growth loss can reflect interface perturbation or loss of antitoxin stability, but the growth assay cannot distinguish them.
comments.request: State this limitation explicitly early in the section.
comments.quote: the loss of growth can result either from the direct perturbation to the interface or from the loss of antitoxin protein stability

comments.issue: Whether non-binding toxin substitutions unfold the toxin, destabilise the interface, or block DNA gyrase binding is unresolved.
comments.request: Use structural bioinformatics such as FoldX to distinguish these possibilities.
comments.quote: For example, by using FoldX to (try and) identify mutations that destabilise the interface without destabilising the toxin by itself.

comments.issue: The arrow in Figure 2c is mislabelled.
comments.request: Relabel the arrow as 'toxic + non-binding T*'.
comments.quote: The arrow in Figure 2c is mislabelled? It should be ‘toxic + non-binding T*’

comments.issue: The difference between the two distributions in Extended Data Fig. 4g looks weak and is not tested.
comments.request: Report proportions above a growth threshold and test the difference with Fisher or chi-squared tests.
comments.quote: I would like the authors to state the proportion of mutants above a delta growth rate threshold (e.g. 4) for the two distributions and then to calculate if the difference is significant using a Fisher test / Chi-squared test.

comments.issue: The claim of robustness to expression conditions conflicts with the larger differences visible in Extended Data Fig. 9I and 9J.
comments.request: Explain and discuss this discrepancy briefly.
comments.quote: However, the data in Extended Data Fig. 9I and Extended Data Fig. 9J reveal larger difference between the two expression conditions?

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits: ungrammatical Extended Data Fig. 2b legend, typo 'revealig', and wrong figure cross-reference (Fig 4c vs 6c).
comments.quote: There is a typo in Extended Data Figure 10 legend b: ‘revealig’ instead of ‘revealing’

comments.issue: The weak correlation in Extended Data Fig. 12f between experimental and model-inferred toxin effects is not explained.
comments.request: Briefly describe the relevance or meaning of this correlation.
comments.quote: in Extended Data Figure 12f, there seems to be a weak correlation between toxin mutant effect inferred from experiments and the toxin mutant effect inferred from the model

reviews.assessment: Valuable whole-protein interaction map, but the novelty of promiscuity is overstated and the proposed evolutionary scenario is questioned.
strengths: first whole-protein-scale sequence-function map of a protein-protein interaction
valuable dataset for molecular evolution and binder design
illuminates the fitness landscape of protein-protein interaction

comments.issue: Non-interface mutations promoting ligand promiscuity are common in directed evolution, so this emphasis is not novel.
comments.request: Tone down the emphasis on non-interface mutations promoting promiscuity.
comments.quote: The emphasis of finding non-interface mutations that promote ligand promiscuity should be tuned down as such tendency has been observed frequently in directed evolution of enzymes and protein binders.

comments.issue: Mostly interface residues covary in the toxin-antitoxin system, questioning the relevance of non-interface mutations to natural evolution.
comments.request: Estimate selective pressure per residue to test this relevance.
comments.quote: the fact that coevolution of the toxin-antitoxin system involves mostly interface residues cast doubt on the relevance of non-interface mutations to natural evolution.

comments.issue: Non-specific toxin mutations would threaten pair persistence; non-specific antitoxin mutations are the more plausible evolutionary scenario.
comments.request: Explore the evolutionary implications of non-specific antitoxin mutations instead of the current direction.
comments.quote: A more plausible scenario should be that non-specific mutations in an antitoxin allow it to detoxify its toxin partner as well as other toxin variants.

comments.issue: The term 'non-specific' would be better replaced by 'promiscuous'.
comments.request: Replace 'non-specific' with 'promiscuous' in the title and manuscript.
comments.quote: It might be better to replace “non-specific” by “promiscuous” in the title as well as the manuscript content.

comments.issue: The terms beneficial, deleterious and toxic are used confusingly without an early clear definition.
comments.request: Define beneficial, deleterious and toxic early in the study.
comments.quote: the authors should provide a clear definition of what beneficial, deleterious, and toxic means in this study early on

comments.issue: Figure 1d could aid the visual explanation of the section at lines 166-178.
comments.request: Consider citing Figure 1d in that section.
comments.quote: Line 166-178: Would Figure 1d assist visual explanation for this section?

comments.issue: R-squared is unsuitable for nonlinear models.
comments.request: Report MAE or RMSE instead.
comments.quote: Line 203 & Extended Data Fig. 9b: R-squared unsuitable for nonlinear models. Report MAE or RMSE instead here.

comments.issue: Figure 3a legend refers to a Fig. 1f that does not exist.
comments.request: Correct the cross-reference in the Figure 3a legend.
comments.quote: Figure 3a legend mentions Fig. 1f which doesn’t exist.

comments.issue: Figure 6e legend refers to Fig 2 instead of Fig 3.
comments.request: Correct the cross-reference in the Figure 6e legend.
comments.quote: Figure 6e legend refers to Fig 2 which should be Fig. 3 instead.

comments.issue: The order in which ParD3 (antitoxin) and ParE3 (toxin) appear is inconsistent throughout the text and figures.
comments.request: Use a consistent order for the toxin and antitoxin names.
comments.quote: However, the order of their appearance is inconsistent and can cause confusion throughout the text.

comments.issue: The term 'rewired AT' in Figure 6g is not defined anywhere in the text.
comments.request: Define or explain 'rewired AT'.
comments.quote: Figure 6g: What does “rewired AT” mean here as this term does not appear elsewhere in the text.

reviews.assessment: Impressive, rigorous experimental and modelling work; only clarity improvements and a few additional analyses are suggested.
strengths: impressive amount of experiments, modelling and analysis
rigorous, with data and evidence for all claims
exemplary growth-rate modelling and uncertainty reduction

comments.issue: Relevant references on protein structure prediction and coevolutionary analysis are missing from the Introduction.
comments.request: Add the missing Onuchic and Weigt group references.
comments.quote: Some relevant references related to protein structure prediction and coevolutionary analysis are missing from this discussion.

comments.issue: The claim that coevolution models cannot identify non-obvious restorative mutations may be specific to this system, not general.
comments.request: Discuss this counterexample and cite the recent repressor study.
comments.quote: Although it is evident that this is true for this particular Toxin-Antitoxin system, this might not be a general claim.

comments.issue: The phrase 'in some cases all' of the disruptive mutations is self-contradictory.
comments.request: Rephrase to clarify whether some or all mutations are restored.
comments.quote: It is not clear to me what do they mean by “in some cases all” of the disruptive mutations.

comments.issue: The coevolution models' poor performance may reflect too few and insufficiently diverse sequences rather than model inadequacy.
comments.request: Discuss this possibility and test whether adding restorative sequences to the MSA helps.
comments.quote: I wonder if the lack of predictive capabilities of EVcouplings and VAE is due to the limited number of sequences.

comments.issue: It is untested whether the coevolution models can predict neutral rather than disruptive mutational effects.
comments.request: Test the models' ability to predict the neutral mutational effects observed.
comments.quote: Did the authors also looked at the predictive capabilities of such models to identify the neutral mutational effects observed?

comments.issue: The title suggests generality, but increased robustness and promiscuity may be specific to the antitoxin-toxin system.
comments.request: Comment on whether these properties extend to other protein-protein interactions.
comments.quote: I wonder if some of the observations of increased robustness to mutations, an evolution towards promiscuity and non-specificity of interactions could be particular to this AT-T system and not a general property of PPIs.

comments.issue: The model of non-specificity is only explained in Methods and Extended Data, harming the flow of the Results.
comments.request: Explain the non-specificity model in more detail in the Discussion.
comments.quote: spending a bit more space explaining in the discussion could benefit the flow when reading the results

comments.issue: The EVmutation and VAE computational sections only cite the original papers and are not self-contained.
comments.request: Provide the minimum methodological details for readers unfamiliar with those references.
comments.quote: the authors should make an effort to provide the minimum details for someone who has not read those references.

comments.issue: The Uniprot codes for the ParE3 and ParD3 sequences used with JackHMMER are not given.
comments.request: Provide the Uniprot codes for ParE3 and ParD3.
comments.quote: In Coevolution analysis, please provide the Uniprot codes for ParE3 and ParD3 used along with JackHMMR.

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: underlined colons in two methods headings and a website citation instead of the proper HMMER citation.
comments.quote: In materials and methods, section “Calibrated uncertainty:” and “Posterior predictive checks:” they underline the colon, please remove

title: Co-evolution of interacting proteins through non-contacting and non-specific mutations

study.system: brown algae; comparative RNA-seq across 8 species

reviews.assessment: Detailed, well-written study with noteworthy convergence findings, but figure clarity and an adaptation-versus-random-evolution analysis need attention.

comments.issue: Whether monoicous species are UU is not addressed, leaving the female-like expression of cosexuals less interpretable.
comments.request: Discuss whether monoicous species are UU.
comments.quote: Are monoicous species UU? If this is unknown the authors could at least discuss this question.

comments.issue: Sex-biased expression is read as adaptation although it could reflect random expression evolution under weak selection.
comments.request: Analyse rates of expression evolution for orthologues where they are not sex-biased, following Scharmann et al 2021.
comments.quote: sex-biased expression could be the result of random expression evolution under low selective pressures for non pleiotropic genes

comments.issue: Unclear whether Figure 2E correlations account for phylogenetic non-independence.
comments.request: Apply PGLS to the Figure 2E correlations.
comments.quote: Were Figure 2E correlations corrected for phylogeny using PGLS?

comments.issue: Convergence in GO terms appears in only two of four species and no test shows the overlap is non-random.
comments.request: Provide a statistical test that shared GO terms are non-randomly found in common.
comments.quote: maybe the authors could find a more convincing statistical way to say that the terms are non randomly found in common in the different species?

comments.issue: Remarkable-convergence claim overstated: a few shared genes suffice for a GO term to recur across species.
comments.request: Soften the remarkable-convergence statement at line 303.
comments.quote: I wouldn't speak about remarkable convergence because it seems to me that just a few sex-biased genes involved in a similar function are enough for the term to appear in multiple species

comments.issue: Figure 3A is unintelligible; which intersect it shows is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what intersect Figure 3A represents.
comments.quote: I don't understand FIgure 3A, what intersect is it representing?

comments.issue: No control for potential expression normalization issues using unbiased genes.
comments.request: Show Figure 4A for unbiased genes to check normalization.
comments.quote: I would like to see Figure 4A for unbiased genes, just to check for any potential expression normalization issues.

comments.issue: Sex-biased genes show non-significant differences in Figure 4A and tests appear unpaired although sex expression is paired.
comments.request: Use paired tests in Figure 4A and resolve the inconsistency.
comments.quote: Are statistical tests paired in Figure 4A across genes? The statistical test should be paired because gene expression in females is dependent on gene expression in males.

comments.issue: The female-closeness conclusion is drawn from descriptive Figure 4A rather than from Figure 4B.
comments.request: Remove the conclusion from that paragraph and rely on Figure 4B.
comments.quote: I think in this paragraph the authors should not conclude that monoicous expression is closer to female, this conclusion rather comes from Figure 4B

comments.issue: Line 187 misstates the comparison: expression differs significantly between herbacea females and the monoicous species.
comments.request: Rephrase line 187.
comments.quote: Line 187 the expression levels are significantly different between herbacea females and the corresponding monoicous species, please rephrase

comments.issue: Figure 4B is too condensed; Pearson coefficients for males, females and gene sets cannot be separated.
comments.request: Show all Pearson coefficients separately for males, females and each gene set.
comments.quote: All pearson coefficients should be shown separately for males and females and also for different gene sets (MBG, FBG and unbiased genes)

comments.issue: Unclear whether delta x in Figure 4C was computed separately for dioicous males and females.
comments.request: Clarify this in the methods and main text.
comments.quote: Was delta x computed separately for dioicous male and female expression? This was very unclear from the methods and main text and should be clarified.

comments.issue: Graphs lack on-graph color legends and detailed axis names, making them hard to read.
comments.request: Add color legends on the graphs and more detailed axis names.
comments.quote: the Figures would benefit from additional color legends directly on the graphs and more detailed axis names because many graphs cannot be understood without reading the legend

comments.issue: The pattern at lines 209-211 may be a normalization artifact: abundant sex-biased genes deflate Pearson coefficients.
comments.request: Add a few words discussing this normalization issue.
comments.quote: Could this be due to a normalization issue? When many genes have sex-biased expression they affect other genes expression because they take up a high proportion of transcripts per million, making pearson coefficients drop?

comments.issue: Calling monoicy epigenetic sex determination is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain or correct the use of epigenetic sex determination.
comments.quote: Why is monoicy called epigenetic sex determination?

comments.issue: Monoicous species are not identifiable in Figure 1.
comments.request: Add a color code for monoicous species to the legend.
comments.quote: what species are monoicious on Figure 1? Please add color code in the legend.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and novel, highly relevant to sex-system evolution; the main concern is overstated GO-term convergence evidence.
strengths: high relevance to evolution of sex and asexuality

comments.issue: Evidence for functional convergence is weak: GO terms appear in only two of four species and metabolism terms in both sexes.
comments.request: Tone down convergence statements in the Results and Discussion.
comments.quote: the evidence for convergence in sex-biased gene function is not very strong and the authors are overstating the results in Lines 165-171 and Lines 302-311

comments.issue: Fig. 3C and Table S5 disagree; cilium assembly enrichment for S. firma is missing from the table.
comments.request: Resolve the discrepancy between Fig. 3C and Table S5.
comments.quote: There is also some inconsistency between results in Fig. 3C and Table S5. For example, in Fig. 3C male-biased genes of S. firma are enriched for 'cilium assembly', however this is missing from Table S5.

comments.issue: Fig. 3C's weak evidence does not warrant a main-text position.
comments.request: Consider moving Fig. 3C to the supplementary material.
comments.quote: I would suggest perhaps even moving Fig. 3C to the supplementary material.

comments.issue: Large differences in predicted and expressed gene numbers within species pairs are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the gene-number differences for the species pairs in Table S1.
comments.quote: What do the authors think are the reasons for the large differences in the number of predicted genes and the number of expressed genes within some of the species pairs?

comments.issue: The 5th-percentile TPM expression threshold is unjustified relative to the TPM > 2 used elsewhere.
comments.request: Justify the choice of the 5th-percentile expression threshold.
comments.quote: How did the authors decide on the threshold of 5th percentile of TPM distribution, considering that other studies use a TPM > 2 threshold for calling a gene expressed?

comments.issue: The expression-filtering choice may affect differential expression and orthology analyses; sensitivity is untested.
comments.request: Assess how expression filtering influences downstream analyses.
comments.quote: I wonder how much the choice of expression filtering influences downstream analyses such as the differential gene expression and the orthology analyses

comments.issue: Fig. 1E x-axis values are mixed up between species, invalidating the regression.
comments.request: Correct the values and redo the linear regression.
comments.quote: I think with the exception of D. herbacea, the values on the x-axis are mixed up between the species.

comments.issue: S. rigidula has the fewest expressed and sex-biased genes and may drive the Fig. 2E correlation.
comments.request: Test whether the Fig. 2E correlation holds without S. rigidula.
comments.quote: Does the correlation in Fig. 2E become significant if S. rigidula is removed from the linear regression analysis?

comments.issue: Expression criterion contradicts itself: minimum 2 samples (lines 110-111) versus 1 sample (lines 393-395).
comments.request: State which criterion is correct and how replicate samples were handled.
comments.quote: However, in Lines 393-395 a minimum of 1 sample is mentioned. Which one is correct?

comments.issue: Fig. S2 is wrongly cited at lines 111-112; that figure concerns GO enrichment.
comments.request: Correct the Fig. S2 reference.
comments.quote: I do not think Fig. S2 should be referenced here as that figure relates to the GO enrichment analysis.

comments.issue: Fig. 1 legend does not identify the colors for dioicous and monoicous species.
comments.request: Add the color coding for sexual systems to the Fig. 1 legend.
comments.quote: It would be useful to mention in the Fig. 1 legend which color represents species with dioicous systems and which represents those with a monoicous system.

comments.issue: Text percentages of sex-biased genes differ from Fig. 2A because calculation methods differ.
comments.request: Use a single method for calculating sex-bias percentages throughout.
comments.quote: For consistency, I suggest that the same method of calculating the percentage of male- and female-biased genes should be used throughout

comments.issue: Purpose of black highlighting for unbiased FC > 2 genes in Fig. 2B is unclear.
comments.request: Show these unbiased genes as gray points.
comments.quote: I do not understand the purpose of highlighting in black the unbiased genes with a FC > 2

comments.issue: Table S3 female:male cell-size ratios are wrong for S. firma and S. rigidula.
comments.request: Correct the ratios in Table S3.
comments.quote: the ratio of female:male for S. firma should actually be 1.1 instead of 0.9, and for S. rigidula the ratio should be 1 instead of 0

comments.issue: Lines 176-177 likely cite the wrong figure (Fig. 2A instead of Fig. 4A).
comments.request: Correct the figure reference.
comments.quote: Maybe the authors meant to refer to Fig. 4A here instead of Fig. 2A?

comments.issue: Reason for using two different transcriptome assemblers is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain why two different transcriptome assemblers were used.
comments.quote: Lines 374-376: Why were two different transcriptome assemblers used?

comments.issue: The rule for choosing among duplicated sequences is not stated.
comments.request: State which duplicated sequence was chosen and why.
comments.quote: Lines 432-433: In these cases, which of the duplicated sequences was chosen and why?

reviews.assessment: Very well presented and enjoyable; comments are minor and aim to improve accessibility and discussion of drivers.

comments.issue: dioecy/dioicy and dioecious/dioicous are not explained and 'dioecy' is misapplied to brown algae.
comments.request: Explain the terminology early and clarify its correct use.
comments.quote: I hope that the difference between the terms 'dioecy' and 'dioicy' (e.g. line 87), as well as between 'dioecious' and 'dioicous' etc. can be explained early on and in a bit more detail.

comments.issue: The study is descriptive; expectations and testable hypotheses are not laid out early.
comments.request: State early what expectations and major hypotheses the dataset can test.
comments.quote: the study is overall very descriptive. It would be interesting to learn early on what expectations exist and/or what major hypotheses can be tested with this exciting dataset.

comments.issue: Evidence for sexual selection in brown algae, invoked to explain the absent correlation, is not discussed in detail.
comments.request: Discuss the evidence for sexual selection in more detail.
comments.quote: What evidence is there in these organisms for sexual selection? This aspect is taken up a bit later in the discussion but without providing much detail

comments.issue: Alternative drivers and underlying factors of sex-biased expression evolution are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss possible alternative drivers of sex-biased gene expression evolution.
comments.quote: Also, are there possible alternative drivers of sex-biased gene expression evolution in brown algae? Evidence for selection driving sex-biased gene expression evolution is strong – what are the underlying factors and drivers?

comments.issue: Whether sex-biased expression correlates with U/V chromosome or SDR size is not examined.
comments.request: Test for a correlation with SDR size or gene content.
comments.quote: I wonder whether levels of sex-biased gene expression are correlated with size of U and V chromosomes, specifically the sizes of (or numbers of genes in) the SDR?

comments.issue: Direction of change for male-biased genes in monoicous relatives is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether these genes are down-regulated in monoicous species.
comments.quote: Do I understand correctly that these genes are in many cases down-regulated in the monoicous relative?

comments.issue: The two panels of Fig. 4C labelled Male and Female are not understandable.
comments.request: Clarify the two panels of Fig. 4C.
comments.quote: I struggle with Fig. 4C. I do not fully understand the two panels labelled 'Male' and 'Female'.

comments.issue: Fig. 4C results get little attention in the Results despite their prominence in the Discussion.
comments.request: Cover these results more fully in the Results section.
comments.quote: these results receive little attention in the results section, despite their prominence in the discussion

comments.issue: The gamete-size reminder sketched below the Fig. 4C x-axis per the legend is not visible.
comments.request: Fix or clarify the gamete-size sketch in Fig. 4C.
comments.quote: I fail to see the reminder of differences between male and female gamete size mentioned in the legend to Fig. 4C

comments.issue: How the transition occurs and the genetic difference between unisexual and co-sexual species are not explained.
comments.request: Explain how such transitions occur and the relevant genetic differences.
comments.quote: one does not learn how such transitions occur – or at least, what the relevant genetic difference(s) between unisexual and co-sexual species is

title: Selection drives convergent gene expression changes during transitions to co-sexuality in haploid sexual systems

study.system: blue tits; long-term body-size data, simulations and literature survey

reviews.assessment: Well-written and superbly documented study with two major advances; only a few minor figure and consistency issues.
strengths: two major advances in dealing with environmentally skewed data
superbly documented in methods and Github site

comments.issue: Text refers to Figure 1C while the figure is labelled with numbers.
comments.request: Make text and figure panel labels consistent.
comments.quote: Line 81 Figure 1C is referred to in the text, but the Figure is labeled with numbers.

comments.issue: Reported heritabilities above 1 contradict the results shown in Figure 6.
comments.request: Reconcile the heritability values with Figure 6.
comments.quote: Line 156-157 Heritabilities are >1, which dose not match the results in Figure 6.

comments.issue: Figure 6 is confusing and reads like a table; the dashed line's meaning is unstated.
