comments.quote: This sentence seems isolated here, I believe you can keep this statement here but improving its link with the surrounding text.

comments.issue: Reference 43 (Allen et al. 2017) is suitable at Line 94 but missing.
comments.request: Add reference 43 together with reference 17.
comments.quote: I think that reference 43 (Allen et al. 2017) is suitable here, together with reference 17.

comments.issue: Recent references on diversity-stability links are missing from Lines 109-114.
comments.request: Cite Jucker et al. 2014 and Loreau and de Mazancourt 2013.
comments.quote: This section is well explained but I missed some recent references.

comments.issue: The term 'spatially explicit' may confuse readers because it means something else in modelling.
comments.request: Write about predictions in space instead.
comments.quote: I am not sure if “spatially explicit” is a good choice of words to bring the concept of predictions in space.

comments.issue: The phrase 'stable climatic conditions' conflicts with positive climate-change effects on FD and FRed and weak climate correlations.
comments.request: Drop 'stable climatic conditions' from Line 329.
comments.quote: I think it is safer to drop “stable climatic conditions” from here because the effects of the changes in climate on FD and FRed were positive in most cases.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether plot size was standardized.
comments.request: State whether plot size was standardized.
comments.quote: Line 526: have you standardized the plot size too?

comments.issue: The spatial-autocorrelation approach at Lines 528-530 needs more detail.
comments.request: Give more details about this approach.
comments.quote: I understood how did you did it, however, I suggest giving more details about this approach.

comments.issue: Testing inclusion of random effects is unnecessary because they are part of the study design.
comments.request: Do not test random-effect inclusion.
comments.quote: Because you added the random effects structure to deal with spatial autocorrelation, the random effects are now part of your study design, therefore it is not necessary to test its inclusion.

comments.issue: Posterior density plots for each coefficient are missing.
comments.request: Add posterior density plots to the supplementary materials.
comments.quote: It would be good the see the posterior density plots of each coefficient in the supplementary materials (at least).

comments.issue: The priors are not clearly described; the 2.5 and 10 values are scale adjustments, not prior scales.
comments.request: Clarify the prior scales and that 2.5 and 10 only adjust them.
comments.quote: These values, 2.5 and 10, were used the adjust the scale/variance based on the data and are not the scale/variance of your prior distributions.

comments.issue: The number of iterations differs between models (10000 vs 5000) without explanation.
comments.request: Explain why the number of iterations differed.
comments.quote: Why did the number of iterations changes from 10000 in line 538 to 5000 in line 569? Convergence problems?

comments.issue: The prior distribution for the error term is not stated.
comments.request: State which error prior was used.
comments.quote: Which prior distribution you used for the error? Exponential? Normal?

comments.issue: The absence of an overall index across the three functional groups is not explained in the methods.
comments.request: Make this explicit in the methods section.
comments.quote: I presume that you have not calculated an overall index encompassing the three functional groups together because of the sampling differences between them.

comments.issue: How delta AGB was calculated is not described in enough detail.
comments.request: Provide more details about the AGB calculations.
comments.quote: Section of line 559: How exactly the delta AGB was calculated?

comments.issue: The blue line in Figure 1B is difficult to see.
comments.request: Change the blue color.
comments.quote: The blue line is difficult to see here, I think the figure will improve if you change the blue color.

comments.issue: The nutrients functional group is empty in Table S2.
comments.request: Complete the nutrients functional group in Table S2.
comments.quote: Table S2: nutrients functional group is empty

comments.issue: Text is missing from the Table S3 header.
comments.request: Complete the Table S3 header.
comments.quote: Table S3 – missing text in the header.

reviews.assessment: Well written, impressive dataset and a timely question, but trait timing, the resilience definition and map uncertainty need revision.
strengths: impressive amount of data across tropical forest plots
addresses a key and timely issue

comments.issue: Traits collected after the 2015 ENSO are used to explain biomass changes after that event, creating circularity.
comments.request: Use only traits measured before the ENSO or rethink the resilience analysis.
comments.quote: This means that some of the trait values that fed the model may have been affected by the drought caused by ENSO already.

comments.issue: The term 'resilience' is used without a clear definition.
comments.request: Define resilience clearly, ideally when the hypotheses are stated.
comments.quote: I think the authors should clearly state what they mean by “resilience”.

comments.issue: Calibration plots are not mapped, so the uncertainty of the maps cannot be assessed.
comments.request: Add the distribution of calibration plots as supplementary information.
comments.quote: it is difficult to assess their uncertainty as 1) calibration points (plots) are not mapped

comments.issue: Areas outside the calibration range are not distinguished on the maps.
comments.request: Mark areas outside the calibration range in Figures 3 and 4.
comments.quote: fig 3 and fig 4 could differentiate those areas with values outside the calibration range

comments.issue: The concept of resilience should be introduced with the hypotheses and defined as ecosystem-functioning resilience.
comments.request: Introduce resilience in the hypothesis at Lines 147-150.
comments.quote: Maybe in this hypothesis the concept of resilience can be introduce, as resilience in ecosystem functioning (which is not necessarily resilience in keeping its original floristic composition).

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the statement at Line 60 applies to all plants or only trees.
comments.request: Clarify whether it concerns all plants or only trees.
comments.quote: is this statement true for all plants or only trees? Please clarify

comments.issue: 'Long-term MCWD' is imprecise; 'long-term mean MCWD' should be used throughout.
comments.request: Use 'long-term mean MCWD' throughout.
comments.quote: I think it would be better if the authors use the term “long-term mean MCWD” rather than long-term MCWD as it is more precise

comments.issue: 'As drought decrease' wrongly frames the comparison of forests across a spatial water gradient.
comments.request: Change to 'towards drier forests'.
comments.quote: Maybe change “as drought decrease” by “towards drier forests”, because you are comparing forests across a water gradient, wetter vs drier.

comments.issue: The statement about higher FD in wetter areas is obvious from the map, and a MCWD map would help readers.
comments.request: Add a MCWD map to identify drier and wetter areas.
comments.quote: I think a map of MCWD could help the reader to identify those drier/wetter areas.

comments.issue: Biomass plots are all African while trait-climate calibration used traits collected in 2015-2017, so traits postdate the biomass change.
comments.request: Be cautious about claiming traits explain biomass change measured earlier.
comments.quote: plots used for biomass are all from Africa for which all the trait-climate calibration is based on traits collected 2015-2017

comments.issue: The ENSO effects on Africa are not described.
comments.request: Briefly describe the ENSO effects on Africa.
comments.quote: I think the reader will gain much more from this discussion if the ENSO effects on Africa are briefly described (i.e. dry).

comments.issue: The majority increase in biomass and the few losses in high FD and FRed areas deserve more discussion.
comments.request: Discuss this biomass increase pattern more.
comments.quote: it seems that the majority of plots experienced an increase of biomass, and the very few plots that lost biomass are in areas of high FD and FRed

comments.issue: What a resilient tropical forest means is unclear.
comments.request: Spell out the definition of a resilient tropical forest.
comments.quote: could the authors please clarify what a resilient tropical forest is?

comments.issue: The implication that the Amazon is within the drier range is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether the Amazon is meant to be in the drier range.
comments.quote: I am not sure I follow this, are the authors implying that the Amazon is within the drier range?

comments.issue: 'The higher diversity in these forests' is ambiguous because both wet and dry forests were mentioned.
comments.request: Replace with 'wet forest'.
comments.quote: maybe replace with wet forest? Because in the previous sentence the author refers to both wet and dry forests

comments.issue: A comma is missing after 'Amazonia' at Line 347.
comments.request: Add the comma.
comments.quote: L. 347. Add a comma after “Amazonia”.

comments.issue: It is questionable that biomass-focused resilience results inform biodiversity conservation rather than ecosystem conservation.
comments.request: Reconsider whether the implications concern ecosystem rather than biodiversity conservation.
comments.quote: Is it really that your resilience results will contribute to biodiversity conservation if they are focused mostly on biomass?

comments.issue: The claim at Lines 400-402 lacks evidence because traits were measured after the extreme event.
comments.request: Temper this claim accordingly.
comments.quote: Not sure you have the evidence to show this based on the points I raised about traits being measured after the extreme event.

comments.issue: No map shows the locations of the plots used.
comments.request: Add a supplementary map with plot locations.
comments.quote: Could the authors please add a map in supplementary material with the location of the plots used for this study?

comments.issue: Q is mentioned at Lines 479-480 but D is not, although both appeared in the previous paragraph.
comments.request: Mention both consistently only once.
comments.quote: L. 479-480, Q is mentioned here but not D, although both are mentioned in the previous paragraph

comments.issue: The statement 'The MCWD was calculated ref. 13' seems incomplete.
comments.request: Complete this statement.
comments.quote: “The MCWD was calculated ref. 13”. I think something is missing here?

comments.issue: 'Mean of the full term' at Line 506 needs rephrasing.
comments.request: Rephrase and check the rest of the manuscript.
comments.quote: L. 506. Maybe rephrase as “mean of the full term” (also check the rest of the manuscript).

comments.issue: The averaging period for MCWD and VPD should be restated at Line 514.
comments.request: State 'mean MCWD and VPD for the period 1958-2017'.
comments.quote: Although defined in the previous section, maybe worth to sy “mean MCWD and VPD for the period 1958-2017”

comments.issue: The phrase at Line 527 ('Effects on?') is incomplete.
comments.request: Complete the sentence.
comments.quote: L. 527. Effects on?

comments.issue: The direction of the ENSO trend (increase in droughts) is not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention the ENSO trend here or in the results and discussion.
comments.quote: L. 561. Either here or in results/discussion mention what the trend of the ENSO was (increase in droughts)

comments.issue: The reference at Line 637 needs updating as it is now published.
comments.request: Update the reference.
comments.quote: L. 637. Update reference as it is published now.

comments.issue: The contrasting spatial patterns of morphological and nutrient FD are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss why the two FD types show different patterns.
comments.quote: What I am missing here is a discussion about the difference in the spatial patters of morphological vs nutrient FD as they are quite different.

comments.issue: The blue line in Figure 1 is hard to see.
comments.request: Use a lighter grey for the other lines.
comments.quote: It was difficult to see the blue line, could the authors please use a lighter grey for the other lines?

comments.issue: The difference between Figure 1a and 1b is not explained in the text.
comments.request: Explain panels a and b separately in the text.
comments.quote: Also, it took me a while to understand the difference between a and b. Could you explain them in the text separately please?

comments.issue: Values outside the calibration range in Figure S1b need masking or highlighting.
comments.request: Highlight regions outside the calibration range.
comments.quote: there are areas with values outside the values used to calibrate the model

comments.issue: The caption of Supplementary Table S3 is incomplete.
comments.request: Complete the caption.
comments.quote: Suppl Table S3, caption is incomplete.

comments.issue: Supplementary Table S4 refers to Figure 3 where Figure 5 is meant.
comments.request: Correct the figure reference.
comments.quote: Suppl Table S4, figure 3 is mentioned here but is should be figure 5?

comments.issue: Some references in the supplementary material have inconsistent captions.
comments.request: Make supplementary reference captions consistent.
comments.quote: References in the supl mat. Some references have a different caption

reviews.assessment: Relevant and timely questions, but the approach cannot answer them properly given missing hydraulic traits, soil controls and MCWD limitations.
strengths: potentially relevant to management and conservation of tropical forests

comments.issue: Traits are not linked to hydraulic traits or strategies, so direct relationships with climate cannot be established.
comments.request: Include hydraulic traits and trait combinations representing strategies.
comments.quote: None of the traits used is directly linked to plant hydraulic traits and strategies (such as hydraulic resistance, capacitance, root depth, stomata density/size and regulation, deciduousness, NSC, etc)

comments.issue: Soil fertility, often more important than climate, is not controlled, so the climate responses may be wrong.
comments.request: Control for soil fertility and climate-fertility interactions.
comments.quote: Without a proper control of fertility, it is not possible to know if the responses to climate shown here are correct.

comments.issue: MCWD ignores groundwater, soil retention and topography, so climate-functional associations remain uncontrolled.
comments.request: Account for groundwater, soil texture and topographic variation.
comments.quote: MCWD is used as the sole representation of water availability to plants. However this metric misses completely the contribution of key hydrological sources to the soil water profile, such as groundwater

comments.issue: The hypothesis that FD always increases resistance or resilience ignores the direction of climate change.
comments.request: Model the direction of change of climate and trait distributions.
comments.quote: The hypothesis that functional diversity is necessarily tied to higher resistance or resilience to climate change, without consideration of the direction of the climatic change, seems naïve.

comments.issue: 'Low functional composition' misuses the composition concept, which has no direction.
comments.request: Replace with an appropriate expression such as low trait variation or diversity.
comments.quote: L62. “low functional composition” – there is no such thing. Composition does not have a direction of change, one composition can be different from another, but can´t be higher or lower.

comments.issue: Trait variation can be detrimental when environmental change moves toward the optimal trait values.
comments.request: Justify the assumption that low FD and FRed reduce the capacity to respond.
comments.quote: If the environmental change goes in the direction of improving the fit of the average (“optimal”) trait values displayed by a community, trait variation is actually bad for the adjustment

comments.issue: Wetter forests may be more resilient because of lower climatic variation rather than because of their traits.
comments.request: Disentangle trait effects from climatic-variation effects.
comments.quote: it might be difficult or impossible to disentangle what is the cause of forest responses – are the wetter forests more resilient because of the traits or because of the lower climatic variation itself¿

comments.issue: MCWD measures climatic water deficit, not soil water availability as claimed.
comments.request: Refer to MCWD only as an index of climatic water deficit.
comments.quote: MCWD is not an index of soil water availability. It misses completely the contribution of key hydrological sources to the soil water profile, such as groundwater

comments.issue: Presenting MCWD and VPD as effective drought-stress indicators captures only part of the story.
comments.request: Qualify the claim that MCWD and VPD indicate drought stress.
comments.quote: “The MCWD and VPD are effective indicators of drought stress for plants” this is just part of the story, as indicated above.

comments.issue: The expectation about wet forests holds only if climate alone drives composition, but soil fertility is the dominant filter.
comments.request: Revise the expectation to account for soil fertility.
comments.quote: This expectation would be true only if climate alone determined the functional composition and diversity. But we already know this is not the case: several studies show how soil fertility is a key determinant of plant trait filtering

comments.issue: Only 11 of 74 plots are moist, so the sample misrepresents the tropical forest realm and may bias the patterns.
comments.request: Add a MCWD histogram and address the underrepresentation of moist forests.
comments.quote: This sample does not do a good representation of the dominant moist climates in the tropical forest realm.

comments.issue: The GEM protocols used for trait collection are not cited.
comments.request: Give the source for the GEM protocols.
comments.quote: “All traits were collected following the GEM network standardised methodology across plots” Give the source for these protocols

comments.issue: The number of species sampled and the species-diversity coverage are not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of species and discuss species coverage.
comments.quote: “This represented a total sample of 2461 individual trees across the tropics” – and how many species? Probably there is very little coverage of species diversity

comments.issue: It is not stated whether all campaigns used the same laboratory methods for chemical traits.
comments.request: State whether the same lab methods were used across campaigns.
comments.quote: Need to state if all the different collection campaigns use the same lab methods for the extraction and measurement of these chemical properties

comments.issue: Genus-level gap-filling conflicts with the claim that traits came from abundant species covering 70% basal area.
comments.request: Reconcile the gap-filling procedure with the stated sampling approach.
comments.quote: This is at odds with the affirmation “We collected plant functional trait measurements from the most abundant species that would cover at least 70% of plot basal area”

comments.issue: Hydraulic evidence contradicts the hypothesis, and hydraulic strategies are absent from the trait set.
comments.request: Include hydraulic traits and reconsider the hypothesis in light of hydraulic evidence.
comments.quote: None of the traits is directly linked to plant hydraulic traits and strategies. The evidence from hydraulics go in the opposite direction to the hypothesis proposed here.

comments.issue: LDMC, LWC, DM and FM express the same thing and inflate the functional space.
comments.request: Remove redundant traits or account for their redundancy.
comments.quote: Four traits are only different ways of expressing the same thing (LDMC, LWC, DM, FM) and as such inflate the calculation of the functional space without a real contribution to the functional diversity.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether CWD and MCWD were computed on each plot's hydrological year.
comments.request: Clarify whether the hydrological year was used.
comments.quote: Was CWD and thus MCWD calculated based on the hydrological year of each plot¿ Necessary to clarify and account for that, as hydrology is not defined by the calendar year

comments.issue: The definition and justification of the time periods seem arbitrary.
comments.request: Define periods that reflect known climatic variation.
comments.quote: This definition of periods seems odd, and the justification too. The periods should reflect known patterns of variation in climatic trends

comments.issue: The results repeat the approach instead of restating the question before the answer.
comments.request: Restate the question before giving the answer.
comments.quote: Instead of an unnecessary repetition of the approach, would be better for the reader if the question is restated before the answer is provided.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the creative, compelling analysis but wants clearer description of the functional components and species identity.
strengths: creative use of long-term forest plot and climate data

comments.issue: FD and FRed are conflated and written as always moving in the same direction.
comments.request: Distinguish the metrics and write 'high functional diversity and high functional redundancy'.
comments.quote: In many places in the text it is written as if functional diversity and functional redundancy are linked and always go in the same direction

comments.issue: The introduction does not explain how FD and FRed relate to species richness.
comments.request: Expand the introduction on the FD-FRed-species richness relationship.
comments.quote: I do believe that more text in the Intro needs to explain the relationship between functional diversity and functional richness.

comments.issue: It is doubtful that functional redundancy is always a good proxy for climate resilience, given its dependence on species richness.
comments.request: Discuss whether FRed always proxies climate resilience.
comments.quote: Therefore, is functional redundancy always a good proxy of climate resilience?

comments.issue: The metric used is functional dispersion, but it is called functional diversity, a broader term.
comments.request: Call it functional dispersion throughout.
comments.quote: The measure of functional diversity is functional dispersion, based on the centroid. So why not call it functional dispersion throughout the manuscript?

comments.issue: Trait coverage is uneven across plots, with few photosynthetic traits, and its influence is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the traits chosen and the influence of uneven trait coverage.
comments.quote: in Table S1, you can see that most plots have nutrient traits and only a few plots have photosynthetic traits. How does this unevenness in trait data influence the results and interpretation?

comments.issue: The moisture-change result could imply less resilience, contradicting the resilience interpretation.
comments.request: Justify why this result indicates more rather than less resilience.
comments.quote: One key result was that larger changes in moisture lead to more functional dispersion and less functional redundancy—so I could see how this situation would be less resilient and not more resilient

comments.issue: Species identity is missing, including species and family lists.
comments.request: Add a supplementary table of species and family.
comments.quote: What are the tree species in these plots, especially in relation to traits? There should be a supplementary table with species and family.

comments.issue: Continental differences in families and genera, such as dipterocarp-rich Asia, may bias redundancy patterns.
comments.request: Discuss these continental biases in the Discussion.
comments.quote: More thought is needed in the Discussion about how the continental differences in families and in number of species/genera might influence the results.

comments.issue: Figure 6 is confusing about whether the top panels represent the three continents.
comments.request: Clarify what the three figures in Figure 6 represent.
comments.quote: Figure 6 is confusing. At the top, are the three figures supposed to represent the 3 continents of South America, Africa, and Asia as in the preceding figures?

comments.issue: The site headings in Table S3 are unclear.
comments.request: Add detail to Table S3.
comments.quote: Table S3, what are the site headings? More detail is needed to understand what is in that table.

comments.issue: Table S1 contains a typo.
comments.request: Fix the typo in Table S1.
comments.quote: Table S1 has a typo—period and not period.

title: Functional susceptibility of tropical forests to climate change

study.system: ungulates; comparative phylogenetic path analysis of migration traits

editor_summary: Reviewers 1 and 2 consider the main evolutionary claims about timing of migration tenuous given limits of phylogenetic path analysis; asks to tone them down and add confidence intervals on ancestral estimates.

reviews.assessment: Calls it a nice study with reasonable conclusions but says it lacks a broadly important conclusion and misuses path analysis for timing claims.

comments.issue: Phylogenetic path analysis does not use timing and cannot identify the original cause or event order.
comments.request: Tone down claims about evolutionary origins and timing of migration.
comments.quote: While phylogenetic path analyses are a useful tool for assessing the causal relationship between variables, they do not, like line 155 suggests, use the timing across the phylogeny to determine those relationships.

comments.issue: The paper lacks a broadly important conclusion needed for this journal.
comments.request: Strengthen the general significance of the conclusions.
comments.quote: this paper lacks a broadly important conclusion that may be needed for Nature EcoEvo.

comments.issue: Model construction and averaging in the path analysis are not explained, and the model set is incomplete.
comments.request: Describe how all models were created and why they were averaged.
comments.quote: More details are needed on the path analysis, specifically how they created all models and why they averaged them (line 412-413).

comments.issue: Supplemental data table is not provided as a machine-readable file.
comments.request: Provide the data table as a csv or Dryad link.
comments.quote: Making the data table in the supplement a csv or a Dryad link would be helpful

comments.issue: Figure 3 trees would be clearer as pairwise plots against migration.
comments.request: Show each variable tree paired with migration as pairwise plots.
comments.quote: It could be useful to have these trees as pairwise plots, with each variable tree and migration as a comparison

comments.issue: The claim about insects and cognitive maps is questionable and unsupported.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the cognitive-map statement for insects.
comments.quote: line 226 Insects migrate, do they form cognitive maps?

comments.issue: Cultural transmission and cultural evolution are raised although the manuscript does not address them.
comments.request: Remove the unmotivated cultural-evolution discussion.
comments.quote: There isn’t anything in the manuscript that addresses cultural transmission/cultural evolution, seems odd to bring this up

comments.issue: Body mass was not log-transformed although this should be done regardless of the range.
comments.request: Log-transform body mass in the analyses.
comments.quote: Log-transforming body mass should be done even if masses didn’t span three orders of magnitude

comments.issue: Ancestral state reconstructions are highly uncertain and should be viewed sceptically without fossil data.
comments.request: Treat ancestral estimates sceptically and integrate fossil information if possible.
comments.quote: ASRs are extremely uncertain and usually only account for a portion of the true uncertainty, often assuming the model is true or adequate.

comments.issue: Alpha parameter values for the OU models are not reported.
comments.request: Report the alpha values used in the OU models.
comments.quote: line 379-381 & supplemental table 2. What were the values for the alpha parameter in the OU models?

comments.issue: The specific OU model used is not identified.
comments.request: State which OU model was used.
comments.quote: line 380-382 Which OU model was used?

reviews.assessment: Finds the manuscript clear and well written with mostly appropriate methods, but flags misinterpretation of PPA and overconfident ancestral and extinction results.

comments.issue: PPA is misunderstood: it does not estimate ancestral states or character transitions, so precedence claims are unsupported.
comments.request: Be cautious about claims that traits preceded others and add ancestral state evidence.
comments.quote: PPA does not perform any sort of ancestral state estimation, does not estimate character transitions, and makes no claims about e.g. the state at the root.

comments.issue: Ancestral phenotype estimates are phylogeny-weighted averages, unreliable in deep time, and fossil evidence is ignored.
comments.request: Add nuance about the unreliability of ancestral estimates and fossil evidence.
comments.quote: These estimates are basically phylogeny-weighed averages of the extant phenotypes, and are especially unreliable in deeper evolutionary time.

comments.issue: The MCRA estimate is close to 50:50, so the non-migratory conclusion is unwarranted.
comments.request: Admit the ancestor state is unresolved and add confidence intervals.
comments.quote: the authors state that MCRA of extant ungulates was most likely non-migratory, but their estimate is so close to 50:50 that they should instead admit that they cannot tell one from the other.

comments.issue: Transition numbers are sensitive to tree topology but phylogenetic uncertainty is not considered.
comments.request: Consider uncertainty in the phylogeny when counting transitions.
comments.quote: The number of transitions is especially sensitive to the tree topology, so I recommend the authors consider uncertainty in the phylogeny.

comments.issue: The term ancestral reconstruction should be replaced by ancestral estimation.
comments.request: Use the term ancestral estimation instead of ancestral reconstruction.
comments.quote: More generally, I would recommend the authors use the term "ancestral estimation" instead of "ancestral reconstruction", which is now quite common and helps to emphasize the inherit uncertainties in these methods.

comments.issue: Extinction differences rest on only 10 extinct ungulates, which is too small a sample.
comments.request: Perform a more meaningful analysis such as BiSSE extinction-rate estimation.
comments.quote: The authors estimated the migratory phenotype of 10 extinct ungulates, but this is clearly too small a sample to draw strong conclusions from, as their own stats confirm.

comments.issue: Extinction speculation about human migration and megafauna is off-topic.
comments.request: Reduce the speculation that is unrelated to the paper.
comments.quote: There is a lot of speculation about these extinctions in the discussion, with mention of human migration and mega-fauna, but this all has little to do with the current paper.

comments.issue: Unstated assumptions about which traits are genetic versus environmental.
comments.request: Discuss traits versus environmental factors and note genetic or non-genetic inheritance.
comments.quote: There are a lot of unstated assumptions about what kind of traits are likely to be "genetic" and which aren't.

comments.issue: The discussion order differs from Figure 1.
comments.request: Follow the same order as Figure 1.
comments.quote: This discussion follows a different order than figure 1, it can be clearer if it follows the same order.

comments.issue: Interactions cannot be modelled in PPA, a limitation not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge that PPA cannot model interactions.
comments.quote: I note that interactions can't be modeled in PPA.

comments.issue: PPA is nine years old, so presenting it as novel is not justified.
comments.request: Do not present PPA as a novel method.
comments.quote: PPA is now 9 years old, so perhaps not so novel!

comments.issue: The R package paper is cited instead of the original PPA methods paper.
comments.request: Cite Von Hardenberg & Gonzalez-Voyer 2012 instead of the package paper.
comments.quote: Instead of citing the R package paper here, the authors should cit the methods paper that introduced PPA: Von Hardenberg & Gonzalez-Voyer 2012, Evolution.

comments.issue: Results at line 92 are not discussed in the same order as Figure 2.
comments.request: Discuss the results in the order of Figure 2.
comments.quote: Perhaps discuss these results in the same order as figure 2.

comments.issue: Swapped figure cross-references (2d/2e) and a redundant 'that' at line 238.
comments.request: Fix the figure cross-references and remove the redundant word.
comments.quote: 95. I think 2d should be 2e. 98. I think 2e should be 2d.

comments.issue: It is unclear what is meant by derived at line 127.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of derived in this context.
comments.quote: As discussed above, it is hard to tell what is "derived" here.

comments.issue: Repeated convergence in migratory behaviour conflicts with the reported excess of losses.
comments.request: Reconcile the convergence claim with the loss-gain counts.
comments.quote: I don't follow why there would be "repeated convergence upon migratory behavior", as the authors describe more losses than gains.

comments.issue: Calling resource-wave models not well supported understates their outright rejection.
comments.request: State plainly that the models are all rejected.
comments.quote: This is an understatement bordering a falsehood. The models are all rejected (p < 0.01).

comments.issue: The negative result for extinct ungulates is not taken seriously under the testing framework.
comments.request: Take the negative result of no difference in extinct ungulates seriously.
comments.quote: suggest" is doing a lot of work here. Since the authors use a null-hypothesis testing framework, they should take their negative result of no difference in migratory behavior of extinct ungulates more seriously.

comments.issue: The word any is overly optimistic given only tip-level data are used.
comments.request: Qualify the claim that relies on any species.
comments.quote: any" is perhaps overly optimistic, as only tip-level data is used.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether full or conditional averaging was used.
comments.request: Clarify whether full or conditional averaging was used.
comments.quote: The authors should clarify whether they used full or conditional averaging.

comments.issue: The paired t-test is inappropriate because the dependent variable is binary.
comments.request: Justify the paired test or use a suitable model for binary data.
comments.quote: I don't understand how this can be a paired test. What are the pairs? I also don't understand why this would a t-test, isn't the dependent variable binary (migratory vs non-migratory)?

comments.issue: Exact p-values are not reported at lines 597 and 598.
comments.request: Report actual p-values instead of significance thresholds.
comments.quote: The actual p-values can be reported here instead of p < 0.05 and p >= 0.05.

comments.issue: Figure 2 regression lines extend beyond the data and lack confidence intervals.
comments.request: Limit regression lines to the data range and add confidence intervals.
comments.quote: I recommend limiting the regression lines to the range of the data (x-axis), and including confidence intervals.

comments.issue: Overlap of standard errors with zero is wrongly treated as indicating non-significance.
comments.request: Use confidence intervals rather than standard-error overlap.
comments.quote: I don't understand why the authors think that an overlap of the standard errors with 0 indicate non-significance. If they aim to use the parameter range this way, they should use confidence intervals instead

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the clear, thorough and visually pleasing study, the first to combine phylogenetics and path analysis for migration, and asks only clarifying questions.
strengths: first to combine phylogenetic information and path analyses for migration

comments.issue: Statements about road and barrier impacts on migration are conflicting between lines 61 and 281.
comments.request: Clarify the wording around barrier impacts on migration.
comments.quote: but on line 281, the authors mention that ungulate migrations are under severe threat from factors including barriers

comments.issue: Whether latitude should be considered a trait rather than an environmental proxy is unclear.
comments.request: Reconsider or justify calling latitude a trait.
comments.quote: I was wondering if latitude considered a trait in ecology? In the context of geographic range or climatic niche it could potentially be considered a trait

comments.issue: Whether the findings extend to elevation migrants is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether the results provide insight into elevation migration.
comments.quote: I was wondering if the authors considered elevation migrants? Do you think that your findings could provide insights into this type of migration, where animals move up and down terrain, rather than across latitude?

comments.issue: Partially migratory species are classified as migratory, and intraspecific patterns are not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss whether the results inform intraspecific partial-migration patterns.
comments.quote: I was wondering about those partial migrant species where some individuals or populations are migratory and others are resident (e.g. Odocoileus virginianus). Do you think your results can provide insights into these intra-specific patterns?

comments.issue: The colour scales on the axes of Figure 2 are not described in the caption.
comments.request: Add a caption sentence explaining the colour scales or remove them.
comments.quote: What do the colour scales on the x and y-axes illustrate? There was no description for them in the figure caption.

title: Evolutionary causes and consequences of ungulate migration

study.system: polar phytoplankton, Microglena and diatoms; metagenomics and lab experiments

editor_summary: Editor sees potential but flags substantial reviewer concerns; a replacement biogeochemist reviewer will be enlisted to check the PISCES model if resubmitted.

reviews.assessment: Hypothesis-driven analyses prove the hypothesis rather than test it, and the link between zinc-finger expansion and zinc demand is unsupported.
strengths: combination of global analysis with laboratory experiments

comments.issue: There is no evidence that expanded zinc-finger proteins contribute meaningfully to the zinc quota; a few abundant proteins dominate zinc demand.
comments.request: Quantify putative Zn-binding protein abundance by proteomics and analyse all potential Zn-binding proteins.
comments.quote: Therefore, these expanded zinc-finger families may contribute a trivial amount to the zinc requirements of these phytoplankton. This issue was not addressed.

comments.issue: Expanded zinc-finger families may be favoured by environmental stress or gene-regulatory advantages rather than zinc availability.
comments.request: Compare zinc-finger expansion against other nutrient gradients, seasonality and temperature.
comments.quote: The selective advantage of expanded gene families may be environmental stress and the advantage of expanded gene regulatory circuits rather than availability of zinc.

comments.issue: The zinc-finger/zinc correlation appears stronger in the southern hemisphere and may not hold independently in the north.
comments.request: Calculate correlations for the southern and northern hemispheres separately.
comments.quote: If the authors calculate correlations for the southern and northern hemispheres independently, is there still a significant correlation between zinc-finger domains and zinc in the northern hemisphere?

comments.issue: The dN/dS result may be a general feature of gene family expansions rather than specific to phytoplankton zinc-finger proteins.
comments.request: Test whether the dN/dS pattern is specific to these proteins and taxa.
comments.quote: With respect to the dN/dS analysis, is this result a general trend for gene family expansions rather than a specific phenomenon involving phytoplankton and zinc-finger proteins?

comments.issue: The distribution of cell sizes underlying Fig. 7A is not shown.
comments.request: Give the distribution of cell sizes for Fig. 7A.
comments.quote: Distribution of cell sizes should be given for Fig. 7A.

comments.issue: Mg and the other algae were grown under different temperature and light conditions, confounding zinc physiology with these differences.
comments.request: Match growth conditions or account for temperature and light differences.
comments.quote: it is very difficult to attribute zinc-related observations to inherent physiology versus differences in temperature and light intensity

comments.issue: Accession numbers or strain designations for the green algae used in the laboratory experiments are missing.
comments.request: Provide accession numbers or strain designations for the algae.
comments.quote: Accession number/ strain designations should be given for the green algae used in the laboratory experiments.

reviews.assessment: Skillful, coherent synthesis of immense work with high-quality data; two concerns on genome size and repeat content plus many clarifications.
strengths: immense amount of work amalgamated into a coherent story
detailed comparative genomics of polar versus non-polar phytoplankton

comments.issue: The estimated ca. 1 Gbp genome size is inconsistent with the 577.93 Mbp chromosome-level assembly, suggesting an overestimate.
comments.request: Re-estimate the genome size and reconcile it with the assembly size.
comments.quote: It is a little strange that the estimated genome size is ca. 1Gbp, while the size of the chromosome-level Hi-C genome assembly (which should be close to complete) is 577.93 Mbp

comments.issue: Chicken is an unusual reference standard for flow-cytometric DNA content estimation in a green algal cell.
comments.request: Use a more closely related plant or algal reference or justify the choice.
comments.quote: It is a little unusual to use chicken as a reference (instead of a more-closely related plant or algal species) when analysing DNA content in a green algal cell via flow cytometry

comments.issue: Genome size was estimated from a single k-mer value rather than systematically across k values, and may be inflated.
comments.request: Estimate size across k = 17 to 31 and average; try GenomeScope2 and smudgeplot.
comments.quote: a more-systematic approach is to do that across different k values

comments.issue: The reported 84.45% repeat content is unexplained, may include paralogous genes, and is inconsistent with Fig. 3A.
comments.request: Explain how repeat content was calculated and provide a repeat landscape with RepeatMasker.
comments.quote: In L207-208, a very high extent of repeat content (84.45% of the genome sequences) is described. How was this result generated?

comments.issue: The exact source of the 11 eukaryote-enriched metagenomes is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the source here or in the Methods.
comments.quote: while the details of the 72 metatranscriptome data are summarised in Table S1, the exact source of the 11 eukaryote-enriched metagenomes is unclear

comments.issue: Fig. 1B does not explain how the difference is calculated or what the standard deviation represents, and the unlinked sites make the difference questionable.
comments.request: Clarify the calculation and consider presenting a ratio instead.
comments.quote: It is unclear how this difference is calculated, and what the standard deviation represents.

comments.issue: The different shades of green in the Fig. 1C inset heat map are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the colour shades in the heat map.
comments.quote: what do different shades of green represent in this heat map?

comments.issue: The sentence at L196 cites Fig. S2 for Microglena genome information that the figure does not contain.
comments.request: Cite an appropriate figure or correct the statement.
comments.quote: Fig. S2 does not show any information about the Microglena genome as this sentence is suggesting.

comments.issue: At L212-213 Fig. S2 is cited too late and does not show the expected transcriptome details.
comments.request: Cite Fig. S2 right after the gene count and check its content.
comments.quote: “Fig. S2” is better cited right after “19,596 protein-coding genes”.

comments.issue: The 4dtv analysis behind Fig. S3E and S3F is not described in the Methods.
comments.request: Describe how the 4dtv analysis was done.
comments.quote: please clarify in the Methods (in L701-709) how the 4dtv analysis was done

comments.issue: It is unclear what the density plotted in Fig. S3E and S3F represents.
comments.request: Define the density metric in the legend.
comments.quote: what does the density represent? Percentage of homologous/syntenic gene pairs?

comments.issue: About fifteen line-level copy edits: Table S3 'STAR Methods', 'see Ref. 32', 'multi-fasta', a missing object at L624, 'August' for AUGUSTUS, RAxML spelled out, 'Microgelna', 'all-by-all', 'media' for value, kit name, prime symbols, tense mixing, 'chlorophyll a' and 'freeze-dried seaweed'.
comments.quote: L539: “multi-fasta” -> “fasta”? “Multi-” is redundant

comments.issue: Reference sources for the dinoflagellate data (Polarella and its non-polar relatives) are not cited at L270.
comments.request: Cite the reference sources for these data.
comments.quote: please cite the reference sources for these dinoflagellate data (i.e. Polarella and its non-polar relatives)

comments.issue: The Fig. 4 legend does not explain how I-IV indicate four pairs of amino acids when each spans two pairs.
comments.request: Clarify the labelling of amino acid pairs in the legend.
comments.quote: it is unclear how “I, II, III and IV indicates the four pairs of amino acids”, because each of I, II, III and IV spans across four (two pairs of) amino acids

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the yellow bars not enriched in the polar diatom or Microglena in Fig. 5A are largely driven by Polarella.
comments.request: Add a brief explanation of the pattern in the middle chart.
comments.quote: Does this mean that a large proportion of yellow bars (polar species) in the middle chart, particularly for domains not enriched in the polar diatom or Microglena, are largely represented by Polarella?

comments.issue: The Fig. 5 legend describes green and red bars while the figure uses blue and yellow.
comments.request: Correct the legend colours.
comments.quote: The bars are in blue and yellow (not green and red as the legend text suggests)

comments.issue: The number on each curve in Fig. 6A is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify in the legend what the number represents.
comments.quote: It is not immediately clear what the number on each curve represents. Please clarify in the legend.

comments.issue: Fig. 6B uses 'GP' instead of 'Gp' and leaves Ts, Ol and Cv undefined in the legend.
comments.request: Fix 'Gp' and define Ts, Ol and Cv.
comments.quote: “GP” should be “Gp” (L349). Also, Ts, Ol and Cv are not defined in the legend.

comments.issue: 'Freezing temperature' at L332 is vague.
comments.request: State the actual temperature.
comments.quote: L332: “freezing temperature” is vague. L353, Fig 6C legend

comments.issue: It is unclear what the letters on error bars in Fig. 6C and Fig. 7 legends represent, and whether shared letters mean non-significance.
comments.request: Explain the letter scheme in the legends.
comments.quote: it is a little unclear what do the different letters on error bars represent, because it is not clear what do “statistically significant differences” represent

comments.issue: The statistical significance threshold in the Fig. 7 legend is not stated.
comments.request: State the significance threshold.
comments.quote: What is the threshold for statistical significance here?

comments.issue: Fig. S4B is never cited in the main text.
comments.request: Cite Fig. S4B or remove it.
comments.quote: Fig. S4B is never cited in the main text.

comments.issue: 'At least twice as much zinc' at L390 is not anchored to a reference value.
comments.request: State what the comparison is relative to.
comments.quote: “at least twice as much zinc” – relative to what? From 10 to 20 nM Zn?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the non-polar species at L462-463 have strain or isolate names.
comments.request: Give strain or isolate names for the non-polar species.
comments.quote: do the non-polar species have specific strain/isolate names?

comments.issue: The genomic DNA extraction method is not described.
comments.request: Describe how genomic DNA was extracted.
comments.quote: L591: How was the genomic DNA extracted? L595: “more than 100 Gb”

comments.issue: The sequencing depth 'more than 100 Gb' at L595 is not specific.
comments.request: Report the exact sequencing depth.
comments.quote: L595: “more than 100 Gb” -> can you be more specific?

comments.issue: The PacBio platform used (RS II, Sequel or Sequel II) is not specified at L605.
comments.request: State which PacBio technology was used.
comments.quote: L605: it is unclear which PacBio technology did you use here – RS II, Sequel, Sequel II?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether weights were used when integrating three methods in EVidenceModeler at L685-686.
comments.request: Clarify any weighting used in EVidenceModeler.
comments.quote: Did you use any weighting when integrating the results from three methods using EVidenceModeler? This should be clarified.

comments.issue: The RAxML substitution model and whether non-parametric bootstrap was run are not stated at L700.
comments.request: Report the RAxML model and bootstrap procedure.
comments.quote: for RAxML, which model did you use? Did you also do non-parametric bootstrap?

comments.issue: The phrase 'alignments between Microglena and C. eustigma OrthoFinder' at L788 is unclear because OrthoFinder is a program.
comments.request: Reword this sentence.
comments.quote: It is not clear what do you mean by “alignments between Microglena and C. eustigma OrthoFinder”, since OrthoFinder is a computer program.

comments.issue: The sentence comparing mu in rice at L795-796 may be unnecessary.
comments.request: Consider removing the rice comparison.
comments.quote: although I am not entirely sure if this sentence comparing mu in rice is necessary

comments.issue: The growth conditions at L840-842 are not directly relatable to the LT, HT, HS and LS acronyms.
comments.request: Align condition names with the acronyms used in Fig. 6.
comments.quote: it would be more consistent if the different conditions are directly relatable to the acronyms of LT, HT, HS and LS

comments.issue: The subheading 'PacBio full length transcriptome sequencing' and the term 'RNA-seq' are used inappropriately at L870-872.
comments.request: Use 'PacBio full length transcriptome sequencing' and 'full-length transcriptome library'.
comments.quote: “PacBio full length transcriptome sequencing” is more appropriate in the subheading. “RNA-seq” is a specialised term for the technology from Illumina.

comments.issue: The annotated genome has not been deposited in NCBI GenBank.
comments.request: Deposit the annotated genome in NCBI GenBank.
comments.quote: it would be great if the annotated genome could be deposited in NCBI GenBank

comments.issue: The red and orange dot colours in the Fig. S6 tree do not match the legend shades for Microglena sp. and Volvox carteri.
comments.request: Make the tree dot colours match the legend.
comments.quote: the colour of the red and orange dots shown in the tree is not in the same (shade) as those shown in the legend for Microglena sp. and Volvox carteri

title: The role of zinc in the adaptive evolution of polar phytoplankton

study.system: polar bears and brown bears; ancient genome population genetics

editor_summary: Editor asks to resolve concerns about robustness of the ancient admixture conclusions with further analysis, as suggested by referees.

reviews.assessment: Generally positive; the genetic analysis meets field standards, with metadata as the only major concern and a few minor queries.
strengths: genetic analysis done to field standards

comments.issue: Sample metadata are not clearly described or matched to the SRA, and traceable specimen and geographic information is lacking.
comments.request: Provide an official specimen number and geographic data in the text and with the SRA bioproject.
comments.quote: More information is in the supplement, but is there an official specimen number and geographic data for the sample?

comments.issue: Once the SRA is public, it must be clear which SRR corresponds to the bleach-treated sample.
comments.request: Clearly mark which SRR matches the bleach-treated sample in the SRA release.
comments.quote: When the SRA data are released, I hope the authors will clearly mark which SRR matches to the bleach treated sample (1/6 aliquots).

comments.issue: MSMC-IM may lack resolution to pinpoint admixture timing, and mutation-rate uncertainty could shift the chronology.
comments.request: Acknowledge the timing limitations or provide error estimates excluding alternative timings.
comments.quote: I am unsure whether MSMC-IM has the resolution to pinpoint the timing of admixture well enough to support precise inference.

comments.issue: Ancient mtDNA clustering could be influenced by DNA damage rather than reflecting real differences.
comments.request: Comment on whether the mtDNA differences are real or damage-driven.
comments.quote: If the authors can comment on the likelihood of whether these are real differences or driven by damage I would appreciate it.

reviews.assessment: Values the ancient genome but has several issues, especially the robustness of the ancient gene-flow signal, which must be addressed properly.
strengths: high value on producing the ancient genome
study of its evolutionary history worthwhile

comments.issue: Laboratory work and data processing show unusual features and are not described in sufficient detail.
comments.request: Describe the laboratory and data-processing methods carefully and in detail.
comments.quote: Laboratory work and data processing parts show a few unusual features. I request the authors to carefully describe their methods in detail.

comments.issue: Terminal misincorporation rates are surprisingly low for Bruno's age and single-stranded libraries show unexpected G>A damage.
comments.request: Explain the damage patterns and the missing USER treatment.
comments.quote: the damage patterns shown in the extended data Figure 2 show in general surprisingly low terminal C>T and/or G>A misincorporation rates (overall < 10%), given Bruno's age

comments.issue: The insert size distribution shows anomalous periodicity with multiple peaks and gorges.
comments.request: Explain why the insert size distribution has such periodicity.
comments.quote: it shows multiple small peaks and gorges with a period. Please explain why there is such a periodicity.

comments.issue: Reads shorter than 35 bp can be microbial DNA misaligned to the target genome, and the 25 bp cutoff deviates from field standards.
comments.request: Re-analyse the data after discarding reads shorter than 35 bp.
comments.quote: most studies use longer cutoffs ranging between 30-35 bps (35 bps is recommended). Please re-analyze data after discarding reads < 35 bps to fit to the field standard.

comments.issue: Mapping quality cutoff 20 may be too lenient when mapping to a same-species reference.
comments.request: Check whether findings hold with a more stringent mapping quality cutoff of 30.
comments.quote: I would like the authors to check if their findings are robustly held with a more stringent cutoff 30.

comments.issue: No quantitative read-level measure of Bruno's divergence from present-day polar bears is provided.
comments.request: Provide overall read-level mismatch rates, especially transversions, for Bruno and other polar bears.
comments.quote: Please provide the overall mismatch rate (especially transversions) between the polar bear reference and Bruno's read data (and other polar bears').

comments.issue: Final variant and genotype calls are not thoroughly checked for biases that affect downstream analyses.
comments.request: Apply and describe QC on genotype calls.
comments.quote: the final variant and genotype calls need to be checked thoroughly to remove biases and errors that critically affect the downstream population genetic analysis

comments.issue: Low-coverage European brown bears may have lower-quality, reference-biased diploid calls.
comments.request: Test low- and high-coverage individuals for symmetric relatedness to the polar bear reference, e.g. with f4.
comments.quote: Because diploid calls of the low-coverage data will have lower quality and more reference bias, it is important to check the quality of genotype calls.

comments.issue: Diploid genotype calls are not cross-validated against an independent data type.
comments.request: Compare diploid genotype calls with single read pulldown data.
comments.quote: Another way would be to compare diploid genotype calls with a single read pulldown data.

comments.issue: The admixture claim relies on DFOIL while Patterson's D shows no signal; the power explanation is unconvincing.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy between DFOIL and D statistics convincingly.
comments.quote: they do not find a corresponding admixture signal using Patterson's D statistic. They claim that this is likely due to higher statistical power of DFOIL as claimed in the original DFOIL study, but I am not convinced by this explanation

comments.issue: DFOIL depends on population-specific variants that are especially susceptible to ascertainment, sample size and reference bias.
comments.request: Provide independent lines of evidence for the ancient introgression.
comments.quote: Considering the issues raised in the points #1-#2, I request independent lines of evidence to support the ancient introgression.

comments.issue: The F4/D test was run per individual, but ancient gene flow is best detected with all individuals pooled.
comments.request: Calculate F4(all present-day polar bears, Bruno, all present-day brown bears, black bear).
comments.quote: Per-individual results interestingly show overall negative results, suggesting the opposite pattern from DFOIL results. Please calculate F4(all present-day polar bear, Bruno, all present-day Brown Bear, Black Bear).

comments.issue: DFOIL results vary with the LCA construct, and the explanation is unconvincing because LCA construction should remove low-frequency introgressed alleles.
comments.request: Reconsider the LCA-based DFOIL results and their interpretation.
comments.quote: The way they built LCA removes such low-frequency alleles and thus LCA will even less useful to detect such introgression – but the results are the opposite.

comments.issue: The lower Dxy with Bruno is circular because it uses the same windows selected to support gene flow.
comments.request: Do not present this Dxy result as independent support.
comments.quote: these results are based on the genomic windows they detect to support such a gene flow. Therefore, this does not provide extra evidence supporting their claim.

comments.issue: Window-based DFOIL is more vulnerable than whole-genome statistics to incomplete lineage sorting and technical issues.
comments.request: Address the window-level vulnerability of DFOIL in the robustness assessment.
comments.quote: Incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) and technical issues can affect individual windows more strongly than the whole genome. This further questions the robustness of the DFOIL analysis.

comments.issue: The ancient gene flow is supported only by DFOIL; MSMC is consistent but does not test it directly.
comments.request: Provide additional independent evidence, e.g. explicit demographic modelling with MoMi or rareCoal.
comments.quote: I request the authors to provide additional independent evidence supporting the ancient gene flow other than DFOIL results.

reviews.assessment: Well-written; conclusions are well supported and of broad interest, with suggestions on DFOIL robustness, multiple testing and selection analyses.
strengths: conclusions well supported by the analyses

comments.issue: DFOIL windows may be too small given recombination, so results may not be robust to window size.
comments.request: Check robustness to window size, using windows where rho > 4,000 as the original DFOIL paper suggests.
comments.quote: The original DFOIL paper (PMID: 25888025) suggests using windows where rho > 4,000 (rho = 4*N_e*r*L). The authors should check to ensure their results are robust to the window size.

comments.issue: The p-value cutoff of 0.01 for significant DFOIL windows does not account for the total number of tests.
comments.request: Adjust the cutoff for multiple testing using FDR or Bonferroni correction.
comments.quote: the p-value cutoff should adjust for the total number of tests (e.g. using a false discovery rate or a Bonferroni correction).

comments.issue: Lining up PSMC curves to account for branch shortening is heuristic and unsatisfactory.
comments.request: Convert fossil ages to generations and use that to shift the PSMC curve.
comments.quote: I wonder if the authors could do a little bit better by converting the estimated age from the fossil (74Kya and 110Kya) to a time in generations and use that to shift the PSMC curve.

comments.issue: Selection against polar bear ancestry in brown bears, the reverse direction of the reported selection, is not considered.
comments.request: Test for deserts of polar bear ancestry near genes in brown bears following Sankararaman et al. 2016.
comments.quote: One way to test this is to follow Sankararaman et al 2016 Current Biology (PMID: 27032491) and test for a depletion (i.e. deserts) of polar bear ancestry near genes in brown bears using the existing local ancestry calls from IBDmix.

comments.issue: No explanation is given why reconstructing the LCA from the most common allele controls for sample age.
comments.request: Add a short explanation of the LCA reconstruction rationale.
comments.quote: it may be helpful to readers to have a short explanation why reconstructing the LCA using the most common allele at each locus is expected to control for the age of the sample

comments.issue: The meaning of 'archaic' versus 'ancient' in the title and text is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the intended meaning and usage of archaic versus ancient.
comments.quote: it was not clear to me what is meant by the use of 'archaic' versus 'ancient'

title: A polar bear paleogenome reveals extensive ancient gene flow from polar bears into brown bears

study.system: two sympatric Asian oak species; population genomics and introgression analyses

editor_summary: Need to provide details of the methods and results for the multiple instances mentioned by the reviewers; highlight all changes in Word.

reviews.assessment: Methods appropriate and analyses very complete; asks for clarifications and a few additional analyses on the genome, sampling and signals.
strengths: very complete in angles of introgression evaluated

comments.issue: The new reference genome is only described in supplementary material.
comments.request: Describe the genome size, chromosome sizes and statistics in the text.
comments.quote: it would be useful to have a brief description of the reference genome that was generated in this study, as it becomes a very hidden part of the supplementary material

comments.issue: Whether sample relatedness was considered and related individuals removed is unclear.
comments.request: State whether related individuals were removed.
comments.quote: It is not clear if the relatedness between samples was considered. Can the authors specify if related individuals were removed from the analysis?

comments.issue: The re-sequencing coverage is not reported.
comments.request: Report the re-sequencing coverage.
comments.quote: What’s the re-sequencing coverage?

comments.issue: Q. variabilis is represented by far fewer individuals than Q. acutissima.
comments.request: Discuss how the low Q.v. sample number affects analyses.
comments.quote: The number of Q.v individuals is very low compared to Q.a. How can this affect the analyses?

comments.issue: The loci and site counts used for phylogenetic reconstruction are not described.
comments.request: Describe the loci, sites and genes used for the phylogeny.
comments.quote: What type of information/sites/loci were used to make the phylogenetic reconstruction? How many sites? Concatenated genes?

comments.issue: JJL is as divergent as the removed ZJS and TMS populations but was retained.
comments.request: Explain why JJL was retained while ZJS and TMS were removed.
comments.quote: JJL is a very different population based on fig 1c as well. Why was this not removed and ZJS and TMS were?

comments.issue: The proportion of SNPs under diversifying selection and the total SNP count are not reported.
comments.request: Report total SNPs and the proportion under diversifying selection.
comments.quote: What is the proportion of SNPs under diversifying selection? The total number of SNPs is not easy to find in the text.

comments.issue: Northern populations show high fd signals without admixture in Fig. 1c.
comments.request: Explain this apparent inconsistency.
comments.quote: How do you explain that the northern populations have such high fd signals and they are not showing any admixture in fig.1c?

comments.issue: Long introgressed tracts shared between sympatric pairs raise the question of independent versus old events.
comments.request: Comment on the age of these events, e.g. with the f-branch test.
comments.quote: The size of the chromosomic tracts harboring the adaptive introgressed regions are remarkably long – several Mb. Plus, some are shared between pairs of sympatric populations. Does this suggest these are independent events or an old event?

comments.issue: Other selection estimators around the introgressed loci are not examined.
comments.request: Report other selection estimators such as Tajima's D.
comments.quote: I wonder how other selection estimators look, for example, genetic diversity, Tajima’s D, or is there any sing of balancing selection around those loci?

comments.issue: The selective sweep analysis is barely described.
comments.request: Describe the selective sweep analyses in detail.
comments.quote: There is no description of the selective sweep analysis more than a statement that his was performed with his on L.548.

comments.issue: No summary figure shows the lack of overlap between sweeps and introgressed windows.
comments.request: Add Manhattan plots comparing sweeps and introgressed windows.
comments.quote: Manhattan plots could be a good way of showing the lack of overlap between sweeps and introgressed windows, at least in the relevant chromosomes (10, 11, 12).

comments.issue: Whether the TEs on chromosomes 10-12 are present in all populations is not checked.
comments.request: Confirm TE presence across populations.
comments.quote: Are these TE present in all the populations? Could their presence be confirmed?

comments.issue: Potential chromosome inversions are mentioned without explaining how they were identified.
comments.request: Explain what the potential inversions are and how they were identified.
comments.quote: L 308-313: what do you mean by potential chromosome inversions? How were these inversions identified?

comments.issue: The developmental stage chosen for DGE is not justified for the environmental effects evaluated.
comments.request: Justify the developmental stage used for DGE.
comments.quote: The selected stage for the DGE analysis is not necessarily informative considering the environmental effects evaluated here. How is this developmental stage justified?

comments.issue: Figures could be more informative about the distribution of introgression signals.
comments.request: Add Manhattan plots of Fd values.
comments.quote: One very useful image could include Manhattan plots with the Fd values to have a visual image of the distribution of the introgression signals.

comments.issue: Legends lack information, e.g. Fig. 3b colour codes and dot sizes and Fig. S1 connectors.
comments.request: Improve the figure legends and explain these elements.
comments.quote: The legends most be improved as the information is not enough to understand the figures.

comments.issue: Population codes are hard to follow in the text.
comments.request: Simplify the population codes.
comments.quote: The code used for the populations is very hard to follow in the text. I am not sure if there’s any way this could be simplified.

comments.issue: iHS and fd are not plotted together for easy comparison.
comments.request: Add combined plots of iHS and fd.
comments.quote: Plots of iHS and fd would help to contrast both analyses easily.

reviews.assessment: Interesting paper and nice dataset with a good approach, but major analyses need more detail and one result needs discussion.

comments.issue: How the demographic model was chosen, including whether population relationships were pre-set, is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the demographic model and its parameters were chosen.
comments.quote: I did not find that there was enough detail to show how that particular demographic model was chosen.

comments.issue: The model predicts nearly equal gene flow within and between species, which is implausible and undiscussed.
comments.request: Discuss the implausible equal gene-flow prediction.
comments.quote: This is a pretty big red flag to me for how accurate the model is and is not actually discussed.

comments.issue: How D outlier windows were detected using block standard errors needs more detail and citations.
comments.request: Describe the D outlier window method in more detail.
comments.quote: The description of how D outlier windows were detected needs greater detail.

comments.issue: How the overlap between environmental SNPs and introgression windows, and the 78% figure, were computed is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the 78% overlap was calculated.
comments.quote: I find it challenging to understand exactly how the overlap between environmental adaptation snps and introgression windows was done (Line 290). Where does 78% come from?

comments.issue: The Delly-based inversion detection lacks details such as which samples were used.
comments.request: Describe how inversions were detected and which samples were used.
comments.quote: The authors use short reads and Delly to identify inversions, but have almost no details on how they did this. Did they use all samples or just a few?

comments.issue: Short-read inversion calls may be unreliable if only a few were hand-picked from many candidates.
comments.request: Quantify and validate the inversion calls.
comments.quote: In my experience with detecting inversions in plant genomes, these approaches find thousands of possible inversions with questionable credibility.

comments.issue: Whether environmentally associated SNPs are enriched in cis-regulatory elements is untested.
comments.request: Test enrichment of environmentally associated SNPs in cis-regulatory DNA.
comments.quote: Are environmentally associated SNPS more likelye to be in cis-regulatory DNA?

comments.issue: Conserved expression of introgressed genes could instead reflect homogenisation of expression.
comments.request: Consider the alternative that introgression homogenises expression.
comments.quote: The authors suggest that genes that introgress have conserved expression. An alternative is that introgression homogenizes expression between species.

comments.issue: It is unchecked whether BayeScan picks up more SNPs in low-recombination regions.
comments.request: Check BayeScan SNP numbers in low-recombination regions.
comments.quote: Are there more SNPs picked up by BayeScan in regions of low recombination?

comments.issue: Window-size differences may reflect statistical properties such as SNP density rather than fragment size.
comments.request: Test whether smaller windows inflate significant window counts.
comments.quote: Is the difference in the number of introgressed windows with different window sizes a matter of introgressed fragment size or statistical properties of the test?

comments.issue: The values at line 400 are not compared with other species.
comments.request: Compare these values with other species.
comments.quote: Line 400: How do these values compare to other species?

comments.issue: The phrase at line 588 is unclear.
comments.quote: based on phylogenetic and population admixture analysis

comments.issue: Fig. 3b does not state whether points are windows or SNPs, how a BF is obtained, or what Fd weight is.
comments.request: Clarify the points and define Fd weight in Fig. 3b.
comments.quote: Is each point a window or individual SNP? Looks like it has to be a window but I don’t know how to get a single BF for a window. What is Fd weight?

comments.issue: Terms in Table 3 are undefined.
comments.request: Define the terms in Table 3.
comments.quote: Table 3: Define terms

comments.issue: PIG in Table S7 is undefined.
comments.request: Define PIG in Table S7.
comments.quote: Table S7: What is PIG?

reviews.assessment: High-standard, novel analysis marking a significant advance, but detached from natural history and needing many clarifications.
strengths: completed to a very high standard
significant advance for analyses in hybridizing plant species

comments.issue: The analysis and results are detached from the natural history of the oak system.
comments.request: Describe how the species are distinguished and their habitats in sympatry.
comments.quote: My main criticism is that the analysis and results are largely detached from the natural history of the oak system studied.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether species are more distinguishable in north-eastern sites and whether high-introgression sites are hybrid swarms.
comments.request: Discuss these patterns at high-introgression sites.
comments.quote: Also, were the two species more easily distinguished in the north-eastern sympatric populations, than at sites where introgression was greater? At these latter sites, were populations more like hybrid swarms?

comments.issue: Only K=5 and K=6 ADMIXTURE plots are shown, limiting visualisation of hybrid ancestry.
comments.request: Add ADMIXTURE plots for K=2, 3 and 4.
comments.quote: it would have been helpful to have ADMIXTURE plots for K=2, 3 and 4, in addition to K=5 and 6

comments.issue: No non-sympatric Q. acutissima samples were included as a non-introgressed baseline.
comments.request: Include non-sympatric Q. acutissima samples as a yardstick.
comments.quote: I found it surprising that no samples of Q. acut. were taken from the region where it is not sympatric with Q. var.

comments.issue: Adaptive introgression is inferred from indirect evidence with no direct tests.
comments.request: Attempt direct tests of adaptive introgression in future work.
comments.quote: No direct tests of adaptive introgression were conducted, which is understandable as they lie outside the scope of the paper. Nonetheless, for completeness, attempts to undertake such tests should be made in the future.

comments.issue: The English needs brushing up in early sections, with further copy edits provided in the marked-up PDF.
comments.quote: The English required a brush-up in some early parts of the paper. I have provided some edits in the marked-up pdf attached

comments.issue: The abstract claim is not true for the majority of groups where hybridization does not occur.
comments.request: Temper the claim with the cited literature.
comments.quote: This might be true in some groups but not in the majority where hybridization does not occur (Mallet 2005; Whitney 2010).

comments.issue: The Introduction overstates how widespread hybridization is and should be tempered.
comments.request: Temper the statements about hybridization prevalence.
comments.quote: Although considered more common than previously, there remains a lack of evidence for hybridization occurring in many plant and animal groups.

comments.issue: Reference 7 lists the wrong author name.
comments.request: Correct reference 7 to Anderson, E.
comments.quote: 87. Reference 7. In references should be ‘Anderson, E.’ not ‘Edgar, A.’

comments.issue: Grant 1981 is a better reference than Mallet 2007 for plant speciation.
comments.request: Use Grant 1981 instead of Mallet 2007.
comments.quote: I consider that ‘Grant, V. Plant Speciation, 2nd edition. 1981. Columbia University Press, New York’ is a better reference than ‘Mallet, 2007’.

comments.issue: The passage at lines 107-113 is well known and overly long.
comments.request: Delete or shorten this passage.
comments.quote: This hardly needs mentioning as well known. Either delete or make more brief.

comments.issue: How environmental divergence could have a role is not elaborated.
comments.request: Elaborate briefly on the role of environmental divergence.
comments.quote: It would be worthwhile here to elaborate briefly on how environmental divergence might have a role. Otherwise the reader is left unsure of this.

comments.issue: DFE is not defined.
comments.request: Define DFE.
comments.quote: 134. Define ‘DFE’

comments.issue: GERP is not defined.
comments.request: Define GERP.
comments.quote: 135. Define ‘GERP’

comments.issue: Kim et al. 2008 on functional mutations in non-coding regions is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Kim et al. 2008 at this point.
comments.quote: This was also indicated by the study by Kim et al. (2008) Science 322: 1116-1119, i.e. that functional mutations occur in non-coding regions

comments.issue: The claim that many parts of genomes are interfertile lacks a reference.
comments.request: Provide a reference for this claim.
comments.quote: 147-148. Provide a reference in support of

comments.issue: Mixed and single-species populations are hard to distinguish in Fig. 1A.
comments.request: Use a clearer colour scheme in Fig. 1A.
comments.quote: It is very difficult to distinguish the mixed from the single species populations. Please use a colour scheme that distinguishes these populations more clearly.

comments.issue: The result's surprisingness differs for the four northernmost Q. acutissima populations and BWL.
