comments.quote: Suggest including the Sulawesi samples as well as the Bajo in Figure 1.

comments.issue: The wording of the f4 pair description is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the wording of the f4 pair sentence.
comments.quote: “All pairs had the form f4(Mbuti, test; New Guinea Highlanders, ancient Wallacean) and always included Amis or ancient Vanuatu (2900 BP) vs. other Asian-related groups as test.” – clarify wording?

title: Ancient genomes from the last three millennia support multiple human dispersals into Wallacea

study.system: pharaoh ant brains; single-nucleus transcriptomics across castes and sexes

reviews.assessment: Interesting questions and approach, but cross-species comparisons, weak statistical support and missing sampling details undermine the claims.
strengths: broadly interesting study questions and system

comments.issue: Datasets from species collected and analysed with different protocols are compared without clarifying re-analysis.
comments.request: Clarify whether the Drosophila dataset was re-analysed and address protocol biases.
comments.quote: It is problematic to compare datasets between species that were collected and analyzed with different protocols.

comments.issue: Inferred cluster numbers are parameter-dependent and lack statistical support such as bootstrap values.
comments.request: Provide statistical support for the clustering analysis.
comments.quote: inferred cluster number is somewhat arbitrary and it does not necessarily reflect biological differences

comments.issue: Drosophila age categories were lumped in Figure 2, reducing variation between pools.
comments.request: Explain or avoid lumping Drosophila age categories.
comments.quote: why were age categories in the Drosophila dataset lumped together in Figure 2, likely contributing to relatively very little variation between pools?

comments.issue: Student's t-tests are used where GLMs are used later, without justification.
comments.request: Use a consistent and more appropriate test such as a GLM.
comments.quote: Why is a Student’s t-test used when more appropriate tests (GLM) are used later (L798-804)?

comments.issue: scRNA-seq is a roundabout way to estimate neuropil volume, which could be measured directly.
comments.request: Quantify neuropil volume directly, e.g. by confocal microscopy or microCT.
comments.quote: using scRNA seq seems like a rather roundabout way of estimating the relative volume of neuropils within the brain

comments.issue: Ant-fly differences cannot be attributed to social organization because the species differ in many other ways.
comments.request: Soften sociality claims or add broader comparisons.
comments.quote: it is not reasonable to suggest that any differences (e.g., in the relative size of certain neuropils, or in scRNA seq clusters, etc.) are caused by differences in social organization

comments.issue: Drosophila is treated as the ancestral state and Monomorium as derived despite Drosophila's derived features.
comments.request: Remove the ancestral-versus-derived framing.
comments.quote: Drosophila also has many well-known derived features, so it does not make sense to suggest that Drosophila represents the insect ancestral state and Monomorium the derived state

comments.issue: Worker age and task variation are not controlled, though age polyethism is strong in this species.
comments.request: Report worker collection details and control for age or task.
comments.quote: Further details are necessary regarding how workers were collected (inside the nest, outside the nest?), and worker age or at least task should be controlled

comments.issue: Brain pooling per replicate, batch effects, replicate definition and gyne mating status are unclear.
comments.request: Report replication, batch effects, colony origin and gyne mating status.
comments.quote: precisely how many individual brains were pooled per replicate? What were the mentioned batch effects? Where did the biological replicates come from

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed the paper; an interesting take and great fit, with major statistical and comparative concerns to address.
strengths: interesting take on sociality and brain cell composition
extensive dataset useful for the social insect community

comments.issue: Ant-fly divergence makes sociality conclusions unjustified without closely related solitary species.
comments.request: State throughout that the sociality connection is merely suggestive.
comments.quote: it is impossible to say whether the differences between these two groups are linked to sociality or not without comparing ants to more closely related solitary species

comments.issue: Quasibinomial GLMs on cell type proportions ignore the compositional nature of the data.
comments.request: Use compositional methods such as Dirichlet multinomial or kNN testing.
comments.quote: Cell type proportions are compositional data, meaning that an increase in the proportion of one cell type will always lead to the decrease in the proportion of other cell types

comments.issue: KC homology conclusions contradict established honeybee knowledge and need cautious presentation.
comments.request: Present the KC homology evidence more carefully.
comments.quote: Given that the results presented in this paper contradict the current knowledge, I suggest being especially careful in presenting the evidence.

comments.issue: AUROC scores for KC homology are mostly low outside the diagonal.
comments.request: Reassess the homology evidence given the low AUROC scores.
comments.quote: AUROC scores do not seem very high to me, except the edges between c13/c21 and a’b’. In extended fig. 2e, I see a lot of 0.7-0.8 scores outside the diagonal line.

comments.issue: The Drosophila dataset choice matters because KCs show strong batch effects in Davie et al.
comments.request: Check results with both Davie and Croset datasets.
comments.quote: which Drosophila data set did the authors use? Davie et al. may not be the best for KCs as KCs exhibit strong batch effects in those data

comments.issue: Correlations were not validated with individual Drosophila marker genes.
comments.request: Validate correlations with marker genes such as Imp.
comments.quote: did the authors validate the correlation results by looking at individual marker genes known in Drosophila?

comments.issue: The published honeybee single-cell data were not used for comparison.
comments.request: Compare with the Traniello et al. honeybee data.
comments.quote: perhaps the authors could compare their data to the honeybee single-cell data published by Traniello et al. 2020 (PMID: 32080242)

comments.issue: Defining Class II as non-lKC cells may mix Class II, sKCs and mKCs.
comments.request: Use positive markers to separate Class II, sKCs and mKCs.
comments.quote: the authors define their Class II cells as everything that does not express lKC markers. Technically, this can be a mixture of Class II, sKCs, and mKCs

comments.issue: Outdated Drosophila atlases were used to assign optic lobe cell identities.
comments.request: Try the newer Drosophila optic lobe atlases.
comments.quote: the authors appear to have used somewhat outdated Drosophila atlases to assign cell type identities to their ant clusters

comments.issue: The longevity link feels artificial and disconnected from the rest of the manuscript.
comments.request: Reduce the longevity emphasis to a passing mention.
comments.quote: the link to longevity in the end and in the abstract feels somewhat artificial and separated from the rest of the manuscript

comments.issue: Typo at line 42: 'generalized reminiscent' should be 'generally reminiscent'.
comments.quote: Line 42: “generalized reminiscent” -> “generally reminiscent”

comments.issue: The Introduction omits that ants and flies have similar brain cell numbers.
comments.request: Mention this similarity based on Godfrey et al.
comments.quote: I would mention here that ants seem to have the same number of brain cells as flies (based on Godfrey et al., which is already cited elsewhere).

comments.issue: Stating that only workers were sequenced in Harpegnathos is misleading.
comments.request: State that Harpegnathos compared workers and pseudo-queens.
comments.quote: Saying that only workers were sequenced in Harpegnathos is somewhat misleading, I would say that it was a comparison between workers and pseudo-queens.

comments.issue: Extended Fig. 1e lacks a negative control and its informativeness is unclear.
comments.request: Add a negative control or justify these plots.
comments.quote: I cannot help but wonder how a “negative control” would look like - would worker sn data correlate equally well with queen bulk data? Are these plots really informative?

comments.issue: How the optimal clustering resolution was chosen is not explained in Methods.
comments.request: Explain how the optimal clustering resolution was chosen.
comments.quote: could the authors perhaps explain in the methods section in more detail how they chose the optimal clustering resolution?

comments.issue: GO enrichment for PR axon guidance and eye development may be artifactual.
comments.request: Verify which genes drive these GO enrichments.
comments.quote: I suggest verifying which specific genes drive the enrichment of these GO-terms in these clusters, and whether this makes sense.

comments.issue: Downsampling does not equalise the shallower Harpegnathos data, so the KC diversity claim is unsupported.
comments.request: Account for sequencing depth differences beyond downsampling.
comments.quote: Downsampling is not enough to support the statement about the higher diversity of KC clusters in Monomorium because Harpegnathos data are not just represented by fewer cells, they are also much shallower

comments.issue: The T4/T5 motion detection role required for mating is not mentioned.
comments.request: Add the role of T4/T5 in motion detection.
comments.quote: The authors may add that T4/T5 perform motion detection in Drosophila - a task required for successful mating.

comments.issue: The claim that worker phenotypes did not exist before superorganismality is disputed by polyethism in primitively social species.
comments.request: Reconsider the claim that worker phenotypes are novel.
comments.quote: Primitively social species exhibit polyethism, meaning they go through phases where they do more “worker-like” and more “queen-like” things at different stages of their life.

reviews.assessment: Ample data and interesting results, but framing, unsupported claims and replicate reporting need substantial improvement.
strengths: findings corroborated with anatomical and physiological data
results of great interest to hymenopterists

comments.issue: The social brain hypothesis introduction focuses on primates and neglects social insect literature.
comments.request: Integrate social insect background and justify studying this ant species.
comments.quote: It will be important for the authors to integrate more background on the study of the social brain hypothesis and social insects in particular into their introductory framing.

comments.issue: Background on H. sal and M. pha social structure, including gamergates, comes too late for Figure 2.
comments.request: Introduce species differences and gamergates before Figure 2.
comments.quote: I recommend that the authors provide more background on the differences in social structure between H. sal and M. pha before the presentation of this figure

comments.issue: 'Frequency' is used imprecisely and may imply unsupported claims.
comments.request: Edit the text to avoid misinterpretation of 'frequency'.
comments.quote: the authors use the word “frequency” in a way that is imprecise, non-specific, or misleading

comments.issue: Basic behavioural-ecology claims lack references throughout.
comments.request: Add references for these behavioural claims.
comments.quote: References and background need to be strengthened throughout the text to give evidence to the authors’ claims and improve data reporting.

comments.issue: Claims about vision and rhythmic behaviour are broad and poorly supported.
comments.request: Support or qualify these claims and detail the GO annotations.
comments.quote: I found several of the claims regarding neural activity or behavior to be interesting ideas but poorly-supported by references or the data presented.

comments.issue: The claim that all differences reflect use of the same cell types is stronger than the data allow.
comments.request: Soften this claim to a possibility.
comments.quote: More accurately, the data presented can only suggest this possibility.

comments.issue: The 'opposite' and 'mirror image' statements about worker and male brains are unsupported without functional data.
comments.request: Soften these statements and contextualise them.
comments.quote: I don’t think the statements “worker brains are almost the opposite of male brains” (line 352) or “male and worker brains are functionally each other’s mirror image” (line 360) are adequately supported by their data or discussed.

comments.issue: The gyne-queen 'transition' language implies the transition period was directly studied, which it was not.
comments.request: State precisely that gynes and queens are compared.
comments.quote: The authors need to be very precise in language here that they are comparing gynes and queens, not directly probing the transition period.

comments.issue: The 'disposable and replaceable' statement contradicts the complementary phenotype results.
comments.request: Clarify or revise this claim.
comments.quote: I think that their results more strongly support the opposite—that the neural phenotypes found in M. pha greatly complement each other

comments.issue: The Discussion does not contextualise findings within the social brain hypothesis for social insects.
comments.request: Contextualise the findings in this framework.
comments.quote: The Discussion should contextualize the main findings in the framework of the social brain hypothesis in social insects to strengthen the authors’ arguments

comments.issue: Biological replicate reporting is unclear and inconsistent between text and Methods.
comments.request: Present replicate information clearly and consistently.

comments.issue: Animal details are scattered and it is unclear whether replicates are 30-50 brains or single individuals.
comments.request: Consolidate animal details and state gyne/male mating status.
comments.quote: It’s challenging to piece together the biological attributes of the animals used for study

comments.issue: Bold claims at lines 436-437 and 562-564 lack information on age determination, lifespan and gyne mating.
comments.request: Report age determination, lifespan and how gyne mating was prevented.
comments.quote: Can the authors please comment on how ages of the samples were determined (line 592-693), typical lifespan for the different phenotypes, how they ensured that gynes didn’t mate

comments.issue: The in-house script at line 627 may not be publicly available.

comments.quote: Line 627: is the in-house script publicly available?

comments.issue: Figure 2 dots may be pooled samples rather than individuals, and bar spreads exceed the data points.

comments.issue: Whether cluster 31 is absent or rare in males is unclear.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Figure 4d dots represent individuals.

comments.quote: Figure 4d: the dots here seem to represent individuals—please clarify in legend and methods if so

comments.issue: Yolky oocyte identification for the dopamine experiment is not described.

comments.quote: they should expand on identification of yolky oocytes in the methods and provide images

reviews.assessment: First comprehensive ant brain atlas and an important addition, but several major analysis and interpretation concerns.

important addition for insect brain function and evolution

comments.issue: Conclusions from cluster numbers are not solid because clustering depends on resolution and cell number.
comments.request: Reconsider the cluster-number claim and add validation.
comments.quote: It is difficult to make a solid conclusion just based on cluster number, without functional validation.

comments.issue: snRNA-seq versus scRNA-seq sampling bias and incomplete OPN annotation affect ant-fly composition comparisons.
comments.request: Account for platform biases and annotation completeness.
comments.quote: current study used snRNAseq and Davie et al. 2018 used scRNAseq. scRNAseq, compared with snRNAseq, may have sampling bias.

comments.issue: Conserved axon guidance genes mean the photoreceptor axon guidance GO term need not reflect eye function.
comments.request: Verify and qualify the eye-function interpretation.
comments.quote: many axon guidance genes are conserved across different brain regions; so the GO term “photoreceptor cell axon guidance” doesn’t necessarily mean it is specifically linked to eye functions

comments.issue: The newer and more comprehensive Fly Cell Atlas male-female comparison is not referenced.

comments.issue: Detected photoreceptors may reflect dissection bias rather than real ant brain composition.

comments.quote: It is possible that the detected PRs from ant brains are mostly reflect dissection bias, but not real cell type composition. The authors should validate this part.

comments.issue: The source of gyne-to-queen cell frequency changes, neurogenesis or cell death, is unclear.

comments.quote: where are these cell frequency changes coming from? Is there neurogenesis or programmed neuronal death during the transition from gynes to queens? If yes, more evidence or clarification should be provided.

comments.issue: The dopamine section does not distinguish composition-level from expression-level comparisons.
comments.request: Clearly distinguish the two comparison levels.
comments.quote: The Authors need to clearly distinguish these two types of comparison.

title: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas tracking the neural basis of division of labour in an ant superorganism

study.system: soil phosphorus and plant productivity; global biodiversity manipulation experiments

editor_summary: Editor invites major revision: reviewer concerns limit the strength of the study and require additional work, especially accounting for low sample size, imbalanced study designs and interpretation issues.

reviews.assessment: Not novel or important enough for the journal, and the biased conclusions reflect heterogeneity, missing information and low statistical power.
strengths: topic can interest plant diversity and soil P researchers

comments.issue: 'Soil P availability' is never defined and different variables lead to different conclusions.
comments.request: Define whether soil P availability is total P, available P or phosphatase activity.
comments.quote: The authors should define “soil P availability” first. It is indicated by soil total P, available P, or phosphatase activity? Different variables resulted in different conclusions.

comments.issue: Great heterogeneity makes some results, such as the small rhizosphere changes, not robust.
comments.request: Test and report the robustness of these results given the heterogeneity.
comments.quote: Given great heterogeneity in the data, some of the results are not robust, resulted in more confusions than conclusions.

comments.issue: Explanations for the key findings lack direct evidence and ignore the mass-balance constraint on soil P pools.
comments.request: Provide direct evidence for the proposed explanations of increased soil P.
comments.quote: Explanation of the key findings are reasonable (L135-146), but lack direct evidence from the current study.

comments.issue: A 7.3% increase in soil total P under mixtures cannot be explained without identifying the P source.
comments.request: Explain where the increased soil total P comes from.
comments.quote: Basically, 7.3% higher in soil total P under plant mixture than under monoculture can’t be reasonably explained by biodiversity effect. Where the increased total P comes from?

comments.issue: Non-significant effects are interpreted as no effect although results likely reflect insufficient data and power.
comments.request: Acknowledge low statistical power and avoid biased conclusions.
comments.quote: In my view, results in the present study is at least partly because of lack of data and statistical power, and the conclusion reached in biased.

comments.issue: The description of data collection is completely missing.
comments.request: Describe how the data were collected.
comments.quote: Did I miss the description of data collection? There is not description of data collection.

comments.issue: 'A study' is not defined and species levels may wrongly be treated as separate studies.
comments.request: Define the study unit, normally an experiment at a site.
comments.quote: “a study” should be defined. Different species levels are different studies? It should be not treated so. Typically, experiment at a site is treated as a study.

comments.issue: It is unclear which phosphatases the activity measurements represent.
comments.request: Note the methods used to measure phosphatase activity.
comments.quote: Methods used to measure phosphatase activity should be noted. Phosphatase indicates acid or alkaline phosphomonoesterases, or phosphodiesterase, or all?

comments.issue: Diversity level should be treated as a nested random factor, not only study.
comments.request: Include diversity level as a nested random factor.
comments.quote: Not only “study” but probably also “diversity level” should be treated as a random factor in nested way.

comments.issue: A positive phosphatase-productivity association does not show that phosphatase causes higher productivity, as the reverse is usual.
comments.request: Avoid causal wording about phosphatase driving productivity.
comments.quote: Positive associations between soil phosphatase activity and plant productivity does not necessarily mean “the positive effects of plant diversity on soil phosphatase activity lead to increased plant productivity”

comments.issue: The statement at L78-97 is reasonable but not robustly tested by this study.
comments.request: Temper the statement or support it with tests.
comments.quote: L78-97: this is a reasonable statement, but not robustly tested by the current study either.

comments.issue: The results at L117-121 likely reflect heterogeneity and low statistical power.
comments.request: Attribute these results to heterogeneity and power.
comments.quote: L117-121: very likely due to great heterogeneity in the data and low statistical power.

comments.issue: Soil depth is not reported at L123-124.
comments.request: Give soil depth, at least for bulk soil.
comments.quote: L123-124: soil depth should be given, at least for bulk soil.

comments.issue: The results at L175-187 suffer from lack of statistical power.
comments.request: Acknowledge the power limitation for these results.
comments.quote: L175-187: lack of statistical power.

comments.issue: Findings at L212-215 come from previous papers and concern increased biodiversity, not biodiversity loss.
comments.request: Correct the attribution and the direction of the biodiversity change.
comments.quote: L212-215: your findings in previous papers not in the current paper. Findings on increased biodiversity, not biodiversity loss.

comments.issue: Plant P uptake is not a P output except in croplands or pasture.
comments.request: Reconsider labelling plant P uptake as P output in Figure 1.
comments.quote: Fig. 1. I would not take plant P uptake as “P output”, unless you are studying croplands or pasture.

comments.issue: Non-significant mixture effects in Figure 2 may reflect weak power from smaller sample sizes.
comments.request: Consider statistical power when interpreting Figure 2.
comments.quote: Fig. 2. Is it possible that insignificant effect of plant mixture on soil total P and available P are due to weak statistical power (smaller sample size).

comments.issue: Support for diversity effects in Figure 3 is statistically weak and trends are not obvious.
comments.request: Report the weak statistical support in Figure 3.
comments.quote: Fig. 3: weak support (statistically insignificant or marginally significant) of diversity effects on soil total P and available P. Trends are not obvious.

comments.issue: Increased phosphatase activity does not demonstrate increased soil P availability.
comments.request: Do not equate phosphatase activity with P availability.
comments.quote: Increase in soil phosphatase activity does not indicate increase in soil P availability.

comments.issue: The phosphatase-productivity correlation in Figures 3 and 4 cannot establish direction of causation.
comments.request: Avoid causal interpretation of the correlation.
comments.quote: Fig. 3 and 4: increase in soil phosphatase activity aids productivity, and vice versa. Therefore, positive correlation between productivity and phosphatase activity does not necessarily mean increase in soil phosphatase result in increase in productivity.

reviews.assessment: Impressive data basis and novel insights for a broad audience, but the imbalanced data and confounded designs demand more cautious evaluation and interpretation.
strengths: clearly structured, well written and to the point

comments.issue: Rhizosphere and bulk soil studies come from different sites, so rhizosphere-bulk contrasts are confounded by site effects.
comments.request: Back up bulk-rhizosphere statements using the seven studies with both at the same site.
comments.quote: Studies on rhizosphere soil were not located at the same sites as were studies on bulk soil. This renders the interpretation of rhizosphere-bulk contrasts ambiguous because of potential confounding (unknown) study site effects.

comments.issue: Ecosystem type and species richness are confounded, so richness effects may reflect generally higher phosphatase activity in grasslands.
comments.request: Assess the original data and reinterpret richness effects against this confounding.
comments.quote: It seems like ecosystem type and species richness are confounded (Supplementary Figure 2): lowest species richness in croplands/forests only and high species richness solely in grasslands.

comments.issue: The composition of the data basis in duration, ecosystem type, soil pH and climate is not shown transparently.
comments.request: Illustrate the composition of the data basis transparently.
comments.quote: the authors need to (i) illustrate the composition of their data basis in terms of experimental duration, ecosystem type, soil pH and climate more transparently

comments.issue: Alternative imbalance-derived explanations are not thoroughly explored or dismissed.
comments.request: Account for the unbalanced design and dismiss alternative explanations.
comments.quote: properly account for the unbalanced design – that is admittedly inherent to many meta-analyses –, by thoroughly exploring and ideally dismissing alternative, imbalance-derived explanations.

comments.issue: The ecosystems included are not specified at Line 19.
comments.request: Specify the ecosystems included (forests, grasslands, croplands).
comments.quote: 19 Specify here what ecosystems are included in this study (forests, grasslands, croplands).

comments.issue: The reported plant diversity effects of 10% or less seem small and their relevance is unclear.
comments.request: Assess and discuss the relevance of these small effects.
comments.quote: 20 These plant diversity effects (10% or less) seem rather small. How relevant are they?

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits: a superfluous article, a redundant word and a typo.
comments.quote: 22 ‘with increasing’ (delete ‘the’)

comments.issue: The meaning at Line 24 is unclear and seems to contradict the stated conclusion.
comments.request: Clarify whether mixture effects decrease with species richness.
comments.quote: 24 I do not get the meaning: mixture effects on soil P availability are positive in low-diverse mixtures and negative in high-diverse mixtures?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the statement at Lines 28-29 is an own finding or an inference from the literature.
comments.request: Rephrase to distinguish own findings from literature inference.
comments.quote: 28-29 Unclear: is this your own finding or an inference from literature, please rephrase.

comments.issue: A reference corroborating P limitation of growth is missing at Line 36.
comments.request: Add a reference on P limitation of growth.
comments.quote: 36 reference to corroborate limitation of growth by P is missing

comments.issue: The phrasing at Line 37 about hydrolysing should be reworded.
comments.request: Rephrase to 'both plants and soil microbes are able to hydrolyze'.
comments.quote: 37 rephrase: ‘both plants and soil microbes are able to hydrolyze’

comments.issue: The citation at Line 47 is rather old.
comments.request: Replace it with more recent references such as Fornara et al. 2011.
comments.quote: 47 Replace rather old citation by more recent ones (e.g., Fornara et al. 2011, Ecological Research;

comments.issue: The wording about N2 fixation at several lines is imprecise about symbiotic bacteria.
comments.request: Check and rephrase the N2 fixation statements.
comments.quote: 80, 89, 178, 348 Cautious: N2 is fixed and this fixation is done by bacteria that form a symbiosis with plants.

comments.issue: Symbiotic N2 fixation also requires P, which may constrain facilitation effects.
comments.request: Clarify how the P demand of N2-fixing symbioses constrains facilitation.
comments.quote: But symbiotic N2 fixation also requires energy (ATP) and thus, P. Therefore, plants in symbiosis with Rhizobia also require more P and therefore, exploit P resources -> constrain of facilitation.

comments.issue: The link between Lines 107-113 and the earlier expectations is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether biodiversity effects are assumed stronger than time, ecosystem type, parent material and climate.
comments.quote: How does this link to the expectations mentioned earlier (l. 82-97)? Do you assume that biodiversity effects are stronger than those of time, ecosystem type, parent material and climate?

comments.issue: Productivity-related citations are used where own data in Figure 5 could be cited.
comments.request: Include your own data from Figure 5 instead of citing productivity studies.
comments.quote: 126, 154 Instead of citing productivity-related studies include your own data (Fig. 5).

comments.issue: Complementary P uptake should decrease soil total P, so the statement at Lines 138-140 is wrong.
comments.request: Rephrase the niche partitioning and complementary uptake statement.
comments.quote: 138-140 Niche partitioning and complementary P uptake (more complete = increased plant P uptake from soil) decreases total P! Rephrase.

comments.issue: The increase and decrease at Line 148 are hardly visible in Figures 3d and 3f.
comments.request: Make these patterns visible in the figures.
comments.quote: 148 This increase and decrease is hardly visible in Fig. 3d and 3f.

comments.issue: The relevance of the increase and decrease at Line 148, e.g. the regression slope, is unclear.
comments.request: Report the regression slope or effect size.
comments.quote: More critically: how relevant is this (e.g., in terms of the regression slope)?

comments.issue: The eutrophication statement at Lines 172-173 misrepresents P transport, which occurs mainly via erosion rather than leaching.
comments.request: Correct the explanation of P transport to surface waters.
comments.quote: 172-173 Surface water eutrophication is mostly a result of particle-bond P transport via erosion from croplands to adjacent water bodies. Leaching plays a negligible role because of the poor mobility of P (see introduction). Clarify.

comments.issue: The phosphatase-productivity relationship is a hen-and-egg problem that bivariate correlations cannot resolve.
comments.request: Tone down the final conclusion about phosphatase driving productivity.
comments.quote: 191-192, 198-202 This is a hen-and-egg problem: phosphatase activity can be regarded either as a result or a driver of plant productivity. This problem cannot be solved by bivariate correlations.

comments.issue: Lines 207-210 nearly reproduce wording from Oelmann et al. 2021 without citing it, which is plagiarism.
comments.request: Cite the source and rewrite the passage.
comments.quote: 207-210 Nearly exact wording as in Oelmann et al. 2021, yet reference missing. Plagiarism!

comments.issue: Units and whether P values are concentrations or stocks are not stated, and buffer differences among studies are unaccounted for.
comments.request: State the units, clarify concentrations versus stocks, and explain how buffer differences were handled.
comments.quote: 233 Maybe I have overlooked this, but do you state anywhere in the manuscript/supplemental what units were used? Do total P and bioavailable P refer to concentrations or stocks?

comments.issue: The basis for fractional functional richness values such as 1.8 in Figure 3 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how functional richness values were derived.
comments.quote: Figure 3: What is the basis for rational numbers (e.g., 1.8) in the functional richness?

comments.issue: Small SEM coefficients suggest important drivers of productivity and enzyme activity are missing.
comments.request: Elaborate on the missing drivers in the text.
comments.quote: Small coefficients (0.16 to 0.34) suggest that important drivers of responses of productivity and enzyme activity are missing in the structural equation model.

comments.issue: The sample size for productivity measures is not reported.
comments.request: Add the productivity sample size and flag it in Supplementary Table 4.
comments.quote: What is the sample size for the productivity measures? Add here (and indicate productivity measurement in Supplementary Table 4 as well).

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Supplementary Table 1 shows individual models for each factor.
comments.request: Clarify this in the caption.
comments.quote: I assume that these represent individual models for each factor? Please clarify in caption.

comments.issue: Effects of the factors on productivity are missing from Supplementary Table 1.
comments.request: Add the effects of these factors on productivity.
comments.quote: Add the effects of these factors on productivity as well.

comments.issue: The factors in Supplementary Table 1 may be interrelated and are not assessed against species and functional group richness.
comments.request: Assess relationships among the factors and with richness.
comments.quote: However, these factors might be interrelated. For example, the ecosystem type depends on mean annual temperature and aridity. Please thoroughly assess relationships among these factors as well as their relationship to species and functional group richness

comments.issue: Aridity and soil pH are nearly significant and deserve exploration in the main text.
comments.request: Explore the aridity and soil pH effects in the main text.
comments.quote: Aridity and soil pH nearly significant. This is worth exploring also in the main text

comments.issue: Supplementary Table 4 lacks parent material, climate zone and duration information.
comments.request: Add these fields or provide a table of sample sizes per factor.
comments.quote: Supplementary Table 4: Add information on parent material (calcareous vs. non-calcareous), climate zone and duration of experiment

comments.issue: Supplementary Figure 1 lacks sample sizes for the ecosystem types.
comments.request: Add sample sizes for the different ecosystem types.
comments.quote: Supplementary Figure 1: add sample sizes for the different ecosystem types.

comments.issue: Species richness is confounded with ecosystem type in Supplementary Figure 2, so richness statements could be cropland-grassland contrasts.
comments.request: Replace richness statements with cropland-grassland contrasts or account for the confounding.
comments.quote: Supplementary Figure 2: It seems like species richness is confounded with ecosystem type (low species richness = croplands; high species richness = grasslands).

comments.issue: Supplementary Figure 5 is missing.
comments.request: Provide Supplementary Figure 5.
comments.quote: Supplementary Figure 5 is missing.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and useful meta-analysis, but it omits soil organic P, background soil P and the complementarity-facilitation distinction.
strengths: helps understand relationships between soil P cycling and plant diversity

comments.issue: Soil organic P, the substrate hydrolysed by phosphatase, is not addressed.
comments.request: Address soil organic P or explain its omission.
comments.quote: however, the study does not address the soil organic P

comments.issue: The focus on phosphatase activity rather than other P-mobilizing strategies is not justified.
comments.request: Elaborate in the Introduction why phosphatase activity is the focus.
comments.quote: In the Introduction, it would be nice to elaborate why the study focuses on the soil phosphatase activity rather than other P-mobilizing strategies.

comments.issue: Background soil P level is not considered although phosphatase exudation is expected under low P.
comments.request: Consider background soil P level in the analysis.
comments.quote: I also wonder whether the background soil P level is considered in the analysis since the exudation of phosphatase is expected under low soil P conditions.

comments.issue: 'Complementarity effect' is used for outcomes rather than the mechanism and is conflated with facilitation.
comments.request: Use the term cautiously and distinguish it from the underlying mechanism.
comments.quote: “Complementarity effect” (Line 55) is used to represent the outcomes rather than the mechanism, and in previous studies “complementarity” is used as both a cause of enhanced ecosystem functioning and a consequence of some community process

comments.issue: The reasoning at Lines 69-71 is flawed because mobilized P enters the soluble pool and should decrease through plant uptake.
comments.request: Revise the reasoning about increased available P under complementarity and facilitation.
comments.quote: Under these two mechanisms, all mobilized P will go to the soil soluble P pool. So the available P would decrease due to plant P uptake.

comments.issue: 'Effect' in 'Direct facilitation effect' could be misread as an interaction outcome.
comments.request: Remove 'effect' at Line 57.
comments.quote: Line 57: I suggest the authors to remove “effect” from the “Direct facilitation effect”

comments.issue: The abbreviation N is not used consistently after its definition.
comments.request: Use N consistently after defining it at Line 80.
comments.quote: Line 80: Abbreviation “N” should be used after definition and use it consistently afterwards.

comments.issue: The reference is missing at Line 84 and the assumed similarity between N and P dynamics is unexplained.
comments.request: Specify the reference and explain why P should follow N.
comments.quote: Line 84: Here needs to specify the reference. And why similar?

comments.issue: 'Producing' and 'synthesizing' are inappropriate word choices at Line 90.
comments.request: Replace producing and synthesizing with proper wording.
comments.quote: Line 90: “producing acid-soluble P and synthesizing phosphatase enzymes”, producing and synthesizing are not proper words here.

comments.issue: The Line 165-168 explanations rely on a complementarity-facilitation distinction that cannot be made clearly.
comments.request: Revise the explanations based on complementarity and facilitation.
comments.quote: See previous comments, not only facilitation contributes to increased soil P availability in the bulk soil, but complementarity also contributes to the increased soil P availability, and we cannot separate them clearly.

comments.issue: Litter-return explanations may not hold in croplands where crop biomass is removed.
comments.request: Qualify the litterfall explanation for cropland conditions.
comments.quote: Line137: This is true for litterfall, but maybe not true for the conditions in croplands, since the crop biomass is removed and will not be returned to the soil.

comments.issue: Limited phosphatase mobility due to soil particle absorption is another possible reason.
comments.request: Consider adding this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Line 158: Another reason could be the limited mobility of phosphatase because of the absorption of soil particles.

comments.issue: The number of data records for the distinct observations is not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of data records at Lines 243-245.
comments.quote: Line 243-245: how many data records for the distinct observations?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the sensitivity analysis covered both Figure 3 and Figure 4.
comments.request: State whether the sensitivity analysis was applied to both analyses.
comments.quote: Line 247-248: Was this sensitivity analysis applied both for the analysis in Figure 3 and Figure 4?

comments.issue: Data points are missing from Figure 4.
comments.request: Add the data points to Figure 4.
comments.quote: It would be nice to have the data points in Figure 4, although the data points have been shown in Figure 3.

comments.issue: It is unclear which phosphatase type the measurements represent and how differing total P methods were handled.
comments.request: Specify whether acid, alkaline or phytase activity is represented.
comments.quote: Line 257: Total P is also determined with different methods, as well as phosphatase activity. Does the phosphatase represent acid phosphatase or alkaline phosphatase or phytase in this meta-analysis?

comments.issue: The two sentences at Lines 268-271 are confusing.
comments.request: Rephrase, e.g. modify 'annual aridity index data' as suggested.
comments.quote: Line 268-271: These two sentences are confusing. Please rephrase them, for instance, modify “annual aridity index data” as “The data for calculating annual aridity index data”.

comments.issue: The ecosystem type statement appears too late for readers to grasp the dataset.
comments.request: Move the ecosystem type statement to where the dataset is described, e.g. Line 242.
comments.quote: Line 266: I suggest the authors to move the statement of ecosystem type forward where the dataset is described (e.g. Line 242), so the readers can be clear about the whole dataset

title: Meta-analysis shows that plant mixtures increase soil phosphorus availability and plant productivity in diverse ecosystems

study.system: coral Vibrio isolates; prophage induction, competition and infection experiments

editor_summary: Reviewers question the advance over earlier work and the strength of novel conclusions; editors reject because ecological implications for wild corals are too preliminary.

reviews.assessment: Relevant topic and strong microbiology, but coral infection experiments have low replication, qualitative results and a possible dsbA confound.

comments.issue: Coral infection experiments central to the colonization argument are poorly replicated: Figure 1 is n=1 and Figure 5 has only 5 replicates with no quantitative results.
comments.request: Increase replication and provide quantitative results for the coral infection experiments.
comments.quote: The first experiment (Figure 1) is not replicated (n=1). The final colonization experiment (Figure 5) has only 5 replicates per treatment and no quantitative results are shown.

comments.issue: Microbiology experiments use co-cultures while coral infection experiments use monocultures, leaving a disconnect.
comments.request: Bridge the co-culture and coral infection experiments.
comments.quote: There is also some disconnection between the microbiology experiments, which are focused on co-cultures, and the coral infection experiments, which are only performed with monocultures.

comments.issue: dsbA expression is a potential confounder because the prophage integrates into its promoter and dsbA is redox-regulated.
comments.request: Quantify dsbA expression with replicated, quantitative assays.
comments.quote: There is also a potential confounding factor involving expression levels of the gene dsbA because the prophage integrates in the promoter region of this gene.

comments.issue: GfP2 may not be the only difference between the Vibrio strains; genome identity and differing regions are not reported.
comments.request: Report genome identity and the genomic differences between the strains.
comments.quote: the prophage GfP2 may not be the only difference between these Vibrios. Their genomes have been sequenced (Line 148) but information on the percentage of genome identity or the genomic regions that are different in both are not provided.

comments.issue: The claim that Vc swimming is inhibited by Vs is not evident from the qualitative colony pictures.
comments.request: Quantify the motility results.
comments.quote: there does not seem to be any difference in the size of the Vc colony in the picture. The strains that seem to show some differences are Vs. Yet, these results are qualitative, so it is hard to tell.

comments.issue: The Figure 4c induction experiment is uninformative because the prophage-free strain cannot show induction.
comments.request: Compare wild-type Vs induction with and without Vc and with an inducing agent.
comments.quote: it is unclear what this experiment is showing, as a strain without the prophage (DeltaGfP2) is not expected to show any induction.

comments.issue: Intrinsic growth rates in monoculture are not quantified, so abundance differences could reflect growth effects rather than killing.
comments.request: Compare cell abundances and growth rates in mono- and co-cultures.
comments.quote: there is no quantification of their intrinsic growth rates when the strains are grown separately. This is important because the presence of prophages can affect multiple bacterial phenotypes, including energy metabolism and growth.

comments.issue: Bar plots hide individual data points and replicate numbers are only given at the end of legends.
comments.request: Show individual data points and clarify replicate numbers per experiment.
comments.quote: The figures with quantitative analyses use bar plots instead of formats that show individual data points, which are the standard for the journal.

comments.issue: The term lytic conversion is used instead of the accepted term induction, risking confusion with lysogenic conversion.
comments.request: Use the term induction throughout.
comments.quote: I suggest the use of the more widely accepted term “induction” to avoid confusion with “lysogenic conversion” which refers to a change in phenotype caused by prophage integration.

comments.issue: The claim that prophage induction is the main source of free phages in coral viromes is not supported by the two cited references.
comments.request: Provide references that support the statement.
comments.quote: The first line of the discussion states that prophage induction is the main source of free phage particles in coral viromes. However, neither of the two references provided support this statement.

reviews.assessment: Finds the hypothesis interesting and the work well executed, but says it lacks an ecological dimension and contains overreaching statements.

comments.issue: The work lacks an ecological dimension because experiments use pure cultures and lab conditions that may not mimic the coral environment.
comments.request: Assess how representative the cultured fraction is of the natural community.
comments.quote: the work lacks a clear ecological dimension since all the experiments have been carried out with pure cultures and/or manipulated strains, very often in laboratory conditions that not necessarily mimic the coral environment

comments.issue: The rationale for the isolation medium and colony selection is missing.
comments.request: Explain the medium choice and how colonies were selected.
comments.quote: Information is missing regarding why this particular medium was used for isolation (why not TCBS for vibrios, for instance?) and how the colonies were selected.

comments.issue: Constantly dominant bacteria cannot be identified without quantitative data.
comments.request: Provide quantitative abundance data.
comments.quote: In the absence of quantitative data, it is difficult to ascertain whether some bacteria were “constantly dominant”.

comments.issue: The sequenced Vd43009 genome could give a more complete taxonomic assignment of the new isolate.
comments.request: Use the Vd43009 genome for taxonomic assignment.
comments.quote: Vd43009 genome has been sequenced. Couldn’t this be used to provide a more complete taxonomic assignment of this new isolate?

comments.issue: Isolation details for Vc43001 are not provided.
comments.request: Provide information on the isolation of Vc43001.
comments.quote: Please, provide information on the isolation of Vc43001.

comments.issue: Submerging coral in 10^7 CFU/ml is an extremely high concentration with no evidence it occurs in the coral environment.
comments.request: Justify the dose or use an environmentally realistic concentration.
comments.quote: Coral pieces were submerged in a culture containing 107 UFCs/ml. This seems an extremely high concentration. Is there any data indicating that this concentration is reached in the coral environment?

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks a quantitative infection measure, misses reference 31 in the legend and leaves the Pf4302 effect unclear.
comments.request: Add a quantitative infection measure, the reference, and clarify the Pf4302 effect.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to have a quantitative measure of infection. Please, provide the reference (31) in the figure legend (line 785). Which is the effect of Pf4302?

comments.issue: The claim of strong colonizing ability and colonization resistance is not backed by any colonization analysis.
comments.request: Show the colonization analysis or temper the claim.
comments.quote: I don’t see any colonization analysis here. Please, explain.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Vs43009 was deliberately co-grown or arose from confluent plating.
comments.request: Explain how the Vs43009 co-culture arose.
comments.quote: Was Vs43009 co-grown on purpose with other previously isolated strains or this is just the natural sample plated at a dilution that did not allow the growth of individual colonies but only confluent growth.

comments.issue: The use of however at line 188 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the however at line 188.
comments.quote: Line 188.: Why “however”?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether viruses from plaques were re-isolated to purity and how many plaques were studied.
comments.request: Report plaque re-isolation and the number of plaques studied.
comments.quote: Were viruses from plaques re-isolated until purity? How many plaques were studied?

comments.issue: Clear plaques imply a susceptible sub-population that does not carry the prophage, which needs explanation.
comments.request: Explain why part of the population apparently lacks the prophage.
comments.quote: If clear plaques are formed, there is a susceptible sub-population in the assayed culture which implies that part of the population does not carry the prophage. This needs some explanation.

comments.issue: The claim that the genome is circular needs support, since P2 phages may have linear genomes, and assembly details are missing.
comments.request: Provide assembly details and support for the circular genome.
comments.quote: How do the authors know that the genome is circular (P2 phages may have a linear genome)? Details of assembly are needed.

comments.issue: Integrase annotations in Figure S2 are unexpected and unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the integrase annotations.
comments.quote: Why are there genes annotated as “integrase” in this figure?

comments.issue: The claim that GfP2 forms viral particles in natural communities is not shown because the coral virus assemblage was not characterized.
comments.request: Provide virus assemblage data or temper the claim.
comments.quote: I think this has not been shown here, since no data on the actual composition of the coral virus assemblage is shown.

comments.issue: Figure 3a legend is not self-explicative and does not define abbreviations.
comments.request: Define all abbreviations in the figure legend.
comments.quote: Figure legends must be self-explicative. Please, provide the meaning of all the abbreviations.

comments.issue: The point of the artificial prophage-cured strain is unclear when natural prophage-free cells exist, and off-target effects were not checked.
comments.request: Justify the artificial strain and confirm no off-target effects.
comments.quote: If, as discussed above, there are Vs43009 cells which naturally lack the prophage, which is the point of making an “artificial” strain? Did the authors make sure that there were no off-targets affected in the strain construction?

comments.issue: The nutrient-acquisition advantage claim depends on plate assays mimicking the gastric cavity.
comments.request: Support the conditional fitness advantage claim.
comments.quote: Not necessarily, the conclusions of the experiment shown here depend on how well these plate assays (Figure S5) mimic the conditions encountered by the vibrios inside the coral gastric cavity.

comments.issue: Figure S6 needs a more detailed description and explanation of the clearance zone and halos.
comments.request: Describe the figure and explain the clearance zone and halos.
comments.quote: Please, provide a more detailed description of the figure (see note on figure 3a). Were phage particles detected in the clearance zone? What are the halos in Vc43001-DeltaGfP2.

comments.issue: Figure S7 is missing a y-axis label on the right panel, NAC is undefined and excision rates lack an informative unit.
comments.request: Label the axis, define NAC and express excision rates as a fraction of cells.
comments.quote: The y-axis labeling is missing on the right panel. Please, provide the meaning of NAC.

comments.issue: The suggestion that strains gain higher fitness when cohabiting needs more experimental support.
comments.request: Provide additional support for the cohabiting fitness claim.
comments.quote: Line 290 “gain a higher fitness when cohabiting”: This suggestion needs more experimental support.

comments.issue: The claim that prophage induction is commonly used in competition in the coral microbiota overreaches the laboratory results.
comments.request: Temper the claim to what the lab experiments show.
comments.quote: This seems overreaching. These results show that under lab conditions Vs34009 and the “artificial” strain DeltaGfP2 interact in different ways with some strains

comments.issue: The GWAS analysis is not described.
comments.request: Describe how the GWAS was performed.
comments.quote: GWAs: Please, provide more data on how this analysis was performed.

comments.issue: It is not evident how Figure S7 shows that Vc killing of Vs is reduced.
comments.request: Explain how the figure supports the claim.
comments.quote: I do not see how this figure shows this ability. Please, explain.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the Vc concentration is physiological or ever reached in the gastric cavity.
comments.request: Justify that the concentration is physiological.
comments.quote: Is this a physiological concentration? Does ever a single strain of Vc reach these numbers inside the gastric cavity?

comments.issue: In situ prophage induction and community changes due to lodAB were not tested.
comments.request: Compare in situ induction between wild-type and manipulated Vc and check community changes.
comments.quote: Why not looking at in situ prophage induction comparing Vc43001 wild type and the manipulated strain? Is there any change in the microbial community of the coral that could be due to lodAB?

comments.issue: Whether Vs43009 produces catalase and why it is not protective is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss catalase production and its efficiency in Vs43009.
comments.quote: Does Vs43009 produce catalase? (All vibrios do, as far as I know). Is it not efficient enough?

comments.issue: The discussion contains many overreaching statements about proven implications.
comments.request: Temper the overreaching discussion statements.
comments.quote: There are many overreaching statements regarding the proven implications of the work (lines 427-431, 446-447, etc.)

comments.issue: The sequencing strategy using only PacBio without short reads is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the sequencing strategy.
comments.quote: Please, explain the sequencing strategy. It is unusual to use only PacBio without combining it with shorter reads lower error strategies.

comments.issue: The phage DNA purification method is not described.
comments.request: Describe how the phage DNA was purified.
comments.quote: How was the pahge DNA purified?

comments.issue: References are missing for the statements at line 575 and lines 593-597.
comments.request: Provide the missing references.
comments.quote: Line 575 (“as reported previously”), lines 593-597: Please, provide references.

reviews.assessment: Calls it a very nice, well-executed and well-written study, but says the mechanism is not novel and the wild relevance is thin, with major interpretation issues.
strengths: well written and easy to follow
little criticism on the technical and experimental level

comments.issue: The mechanism is not novel; Silva et al. described similar hydrogen-peroxide-mediated phage induction between commensal and pathogen, but this is cited only indirectly.
comments.request: Acknowledge the prior similar work directly.
comments.quote: Although the mechanism identified is interesting, it is not novel, and the authors are not very straightforward about this aspect.

comments.issue: Evidence that the interaction matters in the wild is thin, with no data on colonization and unknown importance of the commensal vibrio.
comments.request: Provide data on the natural relevance and colonization effects.
comments.quote: The evidence that this interaction matters in the wild is thin at best. There is no data demonstrating that the interaction between the “commensals” and the pathogen makes a difference in the colonization.

comments.issue: Culturing assays can overestimate vibrio abundance and only culture-based abundance data are cited.
comments.request: Include culture-independent abundance data.
comments.quote: The authors only use culturing assays, which can tremendously overestimate the abundance of vibrios.

comments.issue: The title claim that the interaction determines coral health is not supported.
comments.request: Revise the title to remove the unsupported health claim.
comments.quote: The title is frankly inappropriate. The assertion that the interaction “determines coral health” is not supported.

comments.issue: The abstract is similarly leading about health, and heat-stress changes cannot be answered by this paper.
comments.request: Temper the abstract's health claims.
comments.quote: The abstract is similarly leading in the aspect of health. The changes during heat stress are likely very complex and cannot be answered by this paper.

comments.issue: What is meant by normal microbiota is undefined and Vibrio percentages from culture-independent methods are missing.
comments.request: Define normal microbiota and report culture-independent Vibrio percentages.
comments.quote: What is meant by “normal” microbiota. Also, what percent Vibrio is present when assessing diversity with culture-independent methods?

comments.issue: The claim that vibrios are symbionts is questionable; the cited paper only shows N-fixing ability.
comments.request: Correct or support the symbiont claim.
comments.quote: I would challenge that vibrio have been detected as symbionts. The paper cited shows N-fixing ability in some isolates.

comments.issue: How the dominance of Vibrio and Pseudoalteromonas was assessed is unclear and key culturable-fraction data are missing.
comments.request: Show quantitative data on dominance and culturable fractions.
comments.quote: How was the dominance of Vibrio and Pseudoalteromonas assessed? Some key data are missing here both regarding the culturable fraction and the culturable fraction of the total.

comments.issue: It is unclear what makes the strains representative.
comments.request: Explain how strain representativeness was ensured.
comments.quote: Again, what makes the strains representative?

comments.issue: It is unclear by what measure things were called comparable.
comments.request: State the measure of comparability.
comments.quote: comparable by what measure? Visual inspection?

comments.issue: The evidence for a beneficial effect at line 178 is not provided.
comments.request: Provide evidence for the beneficial effect.
comments.quote: What is the evidence for a beneficial effect?

comments.issue: Phage particle formation in the gastric cavity is assumed but not demonstrated.
comments.request: Demonstrate or qualify phage particle formation in the gastric cavity.
comments.quote: Although it can be assumed that the phage can form particles in the gastric cavity, this has not been demonstrated here.

comments.issue: Swimming and biofilm formation may not be independent traits.
comments.request: Account for the non-independence of motility and biofilm traits.
comments.quote: Swimming and biofilm formation may not be independent traits here.

comments.issue: The promoter assay is not very quantitative.
comments.request: Make the promoter assay more quantitative.
comments.quote: Although a minor detail, the promoter assay does not seem very quantitative.

comments.issue: Motility's role in colonization is complicated by ciliated coral tissue and particle-based entry, so the phenotype-competition link is unclear.
comments.request: Reconsider how the motility phenotypes affect competition in coral tissue.
comments.quote: The role of motility in coral tissue colonization is a bit more complicated than in other tissues. Corals are ciliated and research by Orr Shapiro has shown that this defends the tissue quite well from direct colonization.

comments.issue: The claim that V. coralliilyticus conclusively invades by competitive killing of resident vibrios is disputed.
comments.request: Remove the conclusiveness of the competitive-killing claim.
comments.quote: I strongly disagree that the authors have conclusively demonstrated that V. corallilyticus invades by competitive killing of resident vibrios.

comments.issue: The advantage statement at line 439 is oversimplified and depends on conditions.
comments.request: Qualify the advantage statement by conditions.
comments.quote: The advantage will depend on the conditions. This statement is too simplified.

comments.issue: It is unclear where commensal vibrio colonization resistance has been demonstrated.
comments.request: Provide evidence for commensal colonization resistance.
comments.quote: Where has it been demonstrated that commensal vibrio can confer colonization resistance?

reviews.assessment: Interesting work but the Results are hard to follow for a non-expert, sample size is low and flow cytometry details are missing.

comments.issue: The Results are difficult to follow because the rationale is not clear.
comments.request: Rewrite parts of the Results, stating the hypothesis and test at the start of each paragraph.
comments.quote: I had a very difficult time reading through the results as a non-expert. The experiments seem to follow a certain rationale, but this is difficult to assess in its current state.

comments.issue: No overview sketch of the experiments is provided.
comments.request: Provide a sketch illustrating the experimental overview.
comments.quote: I’d ask the authors to provide a sketch that illustrates the experimental overview, so that readers can keep track while reading the results.

comments.issue: The actual sample size is quite low despite the many experiments.
comments.request: Increase the sample size.
comments.quote: Another concern I have is that although the authors performed many experiments, the actual sample size is quite low.

comments.issue: Flow cytometry laser and detector bandwidth details are missing.
comments.request: Add laser and detector bandwidth details.
comments.quote: What laser and detectors (bandwidth) are you using? Please add these to the manuscript.

comments.issue: The FWS=50 threshold choice is not justified and lacks a negative control.
comments.request: Justify the threshold and show a negative control.
comments.quote: How did you decide on the threshold FWS = 50 to remove the background? Do you have a negative control sample to illustrate this threshold?

comments.issue: Replicate samples were not measured for robust GfP fraction estimates.
comments.request: Measure replicate samples to improve GfP fraction estimates.
comments.quote: Did you consider measuring replicate samples, in order to get more robust estimates of the GfP fractions?

comments.issue: It is unclear when flow cytometry versus microscopy is used and how the two correspond.
comments.request: Clarify and quantify the correspondence between flow cytometry and microscopy.
comments.quote: It is not always clear to me when flow cytometry is used and when microscopy. Also the correspondence between the two is not clear to me. Can you quantify this?

title: The coral pathogen Vibrio coralliilyticus kills non-pathogenic holobiont competitors by triggering prophage induction

study.system: GFP directed evolution in E. coli; high versus low expression promoters

reviews.assessment: Interesting question and model, but serious experimental and simulation flaws leave the main conclusion in doubt.
strengths: valid and interesting question about expression and evolvability
unexpected finding of more neo-functionalizing variants at low expression

comments.issue: The selective scheme keeps the top fraction of genotypes instead of making survival proportional to fitness, allowing low-fitness genotypes to persist.
comments.request: Repeat the simulations with survival probability proportional to fluorescence.
comments.quote: The correct way a simulation for selection should instead be carried out is that the probability of surviving is proportional to the fitness (fluorescence).

comments.issue: The observed phenomenon is mislabelled 'abundance-stability compensation'; it actually reflects increased tolerance due to large variance.
comments.request: Rename and reframe the mechanism accordingly.
comments.quote: This should not be call an “abundance-stability compensation”, it should be call “increased tolerance due to large variance”.

comments.issue: The ultimate cause of the observation is never explained in the Introduction or Abstract, which keep using the misleading term.
comments.request: Explain the actual cause in the Introduction and Abstract.
comments.quote: the authors have also failed to explain this ultimate cause (“increased tolerance due to large variance”) of their observation in Introduction or Abstract

comments.issue: The simulation mixes expression noise with among-individual variation in mean expression, so the selective agent is instantaneous rather than mean expression.
comments.request: Use mean expression as the selective agent in the simulation.
comments.quote: The selective agent (trait being selected) should not be the instantaneous expression of a cell, which is heavily influenced by the expression noise.

comments.issue: Strong GFP signal in the high-expression group overlaps the cyan channel and can mask neo-functionalizing mutations, weakening selection for cyan in H relative to L.
comments.request: Address the spectral overlap and unequal selection between groups.
comments.quote: the H group GFP could be so strong that its signal on the cyan channel is already strong enough to mask any neo-functionalizing mutations

comments.issue: Evolvability of a highly correlated trait may differ fundamentally from that of an orthogonal trait, which is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how trait correlation affects the generality of the results.
comments.quote: I believe evolvability for a highly correlated trait can be a totally different story, compared to the evolvability for an orthogonal trait.

comments.issue: Table S3 is confusing because a single mutation such as D113N has very different effects in H and L, which should not depend on expression level.
comments.request: Explain the differing mutation effects between H and L.
comments.quote: How can a single mutation have such different effects (especially D113N) between H and L?

comments.issue: Small sequence differences among variants could cause heteroduplexes and sequencing errors before SMRT sequencing.
comments.request: Explain how heteroduplex and sequencing-error problems were corrected.
comments.quote: The sequence difference among variants is quite small, which could lead to heteroduplexes during PCR before SMRT sequencing, and increase sequencing error therein.

comments.issue: 'Compensated' at line 62 is undefined in terms of what is being compensated.
comments.request: Specify what compensated refers to (fitness, molecules or fluorescence).
comments.quote: Line 62, “compensated” in terms of what ? fitness? amount of functional molecules ? fluorescence intensity ?

comments.issue: Fig. 3D and 3E are confusing: the difference between the gray contrast and the dashed vertical line is unclear, and the light gray label should be black.
comments.request: Clarify the two selection representations in Fig. 3D/E.
comments.quote: Also, Fig3D and E is confusing, what is the difference between the gray-color contrast and the dashed vertical line ?

comments.issue: Reference 11 concerns mistranslation-induced misfolding; a different reference is more accurate if only misfolding is discussed.
comments.request: Cite PMID:20959819 if discussing misfolding only.
comments.quote: If the authors are mostly talking about misfolding only (regardless mistranslation), I believe PMID:20959819 is a more accurate reference.

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits: T230S/T203S, wrong figure mentions at lines 223, 262 and 288, 'variant'/'variants', missing 'low' in Supplementary line 74, and empty bracket in Figure S6C.
comments.quote: Line 223 “Figure 3D” should be a wrong mention

reviews.assessment: Interesting and well-supported finding with no critical comments, but presentation and framing need precision; title and terminology mislead readers.
strengths: interesting basic finding that low-abundance proteins are more evolvable
surprising and well-supported explanation via reduced stability
logic and technique of the study sound

comments.issue: Box plots appear to represent only four data points, and the underlying points are not shown.
comments.request: Show the four underlying data points (jittered) or state what they represent.
comments.quote: I would much rather see the underlying four data points for each (maybe jittered to show the distribution).

comments.issue: Fonts are inconsistent within panels, across panels and across figures.
comments.request: Make fonts consistent across all figures.
comments.quote: Many of the figures have inconsistent fonts, both within and across panels in single figures, and across figures.

comments.issue: The straight lines (sometimes dashed) in Figure 3C and 3G are unexplained and may be artifacts.
comments.request: Describe the meaning of these lines or remove them.
comments.quote: I can’t tell whether these are meaningful or if they are visual artifacts. If they are meaningful, please describe what they mean, if not, please remove.

comments.issue: The argument at lines 201-208 and the log-normal point are hard to follow, and Figure 3G does not convey them.
comments.request: Improve Figure 3G and the explanation of the log-normal point.
comments.quote: The log-normal shape seems to be critical based on lines 206-208, but I don’t understand this point, a good figure would make a big difference, but Fig 3G isn’t cutting it.

comments.issue: The title is misleading: low expression does not mitigate folding defects; defective proteins simply fail selection.
comments.request: Rewrite the title to state that high abundance weakens selection on stability.
comments.quote: Perhaps this is a major point: the title of the paper should be rewritten. It’s misleading.

comments.issue: The abstract sentence about folding defects accumulating at high expression is confusing and suggests misfolding rates increase with expression.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract sentence to explain the fitness equation result clearly.
comments.quote: In the abstract, the following is really confusing given my prior assumptions about unrelated questions in the field

comments.issue: 'Abundance-stability compensation principle' is misleading and asymmetric; the inability to compensate is what causes evolvability, and this language recurs in the Introduction and Discussion.
comments.request: Revise this framing throughout the abstract, Introduction and Discussion.
comments.quote: The fact that they __cannot__ compensate is what makes them evolvable!

comments.issue: The last abstract line 'to help' implies agency for the proteins.
comments.request: Replace 'to help' with 'by which'.
comments.quote: And the last line of the abstract: “to help” -> “by which”, since the lowly expressed proteins do not have agency in their evolution.

reviews.assessment: Nice contribution with sound analysis and conclusions; suggests clearer writing around time scales and drift robustness.
strengths: clear Discussion of how the system fits together

comments.issue: Abstract statements such as folding defects accumulating at high expression can confuse readers and seem to contradict accepted results.
comments.request: Clarify the abstract wording.
comments.quote: readers could be confused by statements such as “proteins with folding defects preferentially accumulate when a protein is highly expressed”

comments.issue: The dependence of the findings on short time scales is not emphasised throughout the paper.
comments.request: Add 'over short time scales' where appropriate.
comments.quote: I would like to encourage the authors to read the entire paper carefully and see whether there are places where they can emphasize the time scale dependence.

comments.issue: The claim that selection against toxic misfolding is absent is not explained.
comments.request: Add one or two sentences explaining why this selection pressure is absent.
comments.quote: when the authors state that selection against toxic misfolding is not present in their system, they could add 1-2 explanatory sentences explaining why we think this selection pressure isn't there

comments.issue: The situation resembles the drift robustness idea of LaBar and Adami, with low-expression genes drift-robust and high-expression genes buffered, but this is not discussed.
comments.request: Consider discussing the drift robustness analogy and reference.
comments.quote: If this is correct, then the entire situation reminds me a bit of the idea of drift robustness discussed by LaBar and Adami

title: Low protein expression enhances phenotypic evolvability by intensifying selection on folding stability

study.system: AM fungi; greenhouse 33P tracer with European field soils

editor_summary: Editor: main shared concern is limited agricultural implications from using a non-crop plant; expects toning down and reframing plus additional soil microbial community data and modified isotope reporting.

reviews.assessment: Good addition with impressive spatial coverage, but major concerns about the model plant's representativeness, unreported microbial results, and pot limitations.
strengths: impressive diversity of soil samples at a broad spatial scale

comments.issue: Plantago lanceolata may not represent crop hosts, and no rationale is given for using it on crop soils instead of wheat.
comments.request: Explain the choice of P. lanceolata or add a crop species.
comments.quote: they did not provide any explanation on the rationality of planting P. lanceolate into crop soils. I wonder why not also use wheat as a target since this study mainly focuses on crop production.

comments.issue: Higher 33P recovery in grassland soils could reflect more host-specific AMF for P. lanceolata there rather than land-use effects.
comments.request: Consider host specificity of AMF as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: There could be simply more host-specific AMF that could interact with P. lanceolate in the grassland sites than croplands

comments.issue: Soil microbial diversity and composition were analysed but the mycorrhizal results are not reported, limiting the conclusions.
comments.request: Report the mycorrhizal composition and plant-microbe interaction results.
comments.quote: The lack of results on mycorrhizal compositions and plant-microbial interactions limited the reliability of the conclusions.

comments.issue: Crop management may affect microbes that cannot interact with P. lanceolata, so weaker cropland effects are expected.
comments.request: Account for the mismatch between affected soil microbes and those interacting with the focal plant.
comments.quote: those, at least many of them, were not the microbes that could interact with P. lanceolate

comments.issue: Twelve weeks is too short for a perennial plant to respond, so growth effects cannot be tested.
comments.request: Acknowledge the short experimental period or extend it.
comments.quote: 12 weeks was not a sufficient time period for P. lanceolate to respond to these treatments

comments.issue: Sustainable crop production is discussed throughout although no production difference was found.
comments.request: Temper the sustainable crop production claims to match the results.
comments.quote: Sustainable crop production has been mentioned throughout the whole ms, but no production difference was found in this study.

comments.issue: The pot volume is too small for P. lanceolata roots and shoots, so the pots limited growth regardless of treatment.
comments.request: Acknowledge or address the pot size limitation.
comments.quote: This volume is not appropriate to plant P. lanceolate, as their roots could reach to 60 cm, and shoot could be 20 to 50 cm.

comments.issue: The 90% figure is exaggerated: reference 7 has no such description and reference 8 reports 75%.
comments.request: Correct the 90% figure and its citations.
comments.quote: 90% is a little bit exaggerated, no relevant descriptions in ref7, and in ref8 the number is 75%

comments.issue: Cultivar and host genetic variation are ignored although host properties are major determinants of AMF.
comments.request: Consider cultivar dependence and genetic variation across the surveyed area.
comments.quote: In the experimental design, the authors focused on context-dependence, but cultivar dependence was ignored.

comments.issue: Only shoot biomass was analysed although roots interact with AMF and root biomass matters.
comments.request: Analyse root biomass as well.
comments.quote: why only shoot biomass analyzed? Roots are the part that interact with AMF, and root biomass could also important.

comments.issue: Missing values were not simply set to NA even though R handles NAs well.
