comments.request: Set missing values as NA instead of removing or imputing them.
comments.quote: Why not simply set the missing values as NA? R could handle NAs very well.

comments.issue: Lines 280-283 repeat lines 249-252.
comments.request: Remove the repetition.
comments.quote: L280-283: repeated with L249-252?

comments.issue: Other soil microbes besides AMF could also contribute to P transfer.
comments.request: Consider other soil microbes that could help with P transfer.
comments.quote: Apart from AMF, are there any other soil microbes that could help with P transfer?

comments.issue: Fig. 4B significance notation differs from the other figures and tables.
comments.request: Change Fig. 4B to p < 0.001 for consistency.
comments.quote: Fig 4B change to p < 0.001, in line with other figure and tables.

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the paper and values the wide soil collection, but finds novelty and agricultural relevance overblown and the isotope reporting and host genotype issues important.
strengths: large suite of real agricultural and grassland soils

comments.issue: Novelty and direct relevance to agricultural applications of mycorrhizal fungi are overblown.
comments.request: Temper the claims of novelty and agricultural relevance.
comments.quote: I think the novelty and direct relevance of this research to agricultural applications of mycorrhizal fungi are a bit overblown.

comments.issue: Several relevant citations are missing.
comments.request: Cite the missing relevant literature.
comments.quote: Several relevant citations are missing (see list of specific points below).

comments.issue: Plantago is not an economically significant crop, so applicability to agricultural systems is limited.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limits of a non-crop host for agricultural inferences.
comments.quote: it comes a bit late and limits the interpretation and applicability of these data to agricultural systems somewhat given that Plantago is not itself an economically significant crop

comments.issue: Inferences about relevance to agricultural mycorrhiza application are highly speculative.
comments.request: Tone down the speculative agricultural inferences.
comments.quote: the inferences made about the relevance of these findings to application of mycorrhizal fungi in agricultural systems comes across as highly speculative and need to be toned down

comments.issue: Host genotype is unknown, so soil environment cannot be shown to be the sole driver of mycorrhizal function differences.
comments.request: Report the genetic background of the Plantago plants used.
comments.quote: it is not possible to determine from the data provided that it is only the soil environment that is driving the differences in mycorrhizal function

comments.issue: Recently published work on crop genotype variation in mycorrhizal function is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Thirkell et al. 2020, Thirkell et al. 2021 and Elliott et al. 2020.
comments.quote: Research published relatively recently, but which is not cited, highlights this important point which is particularly pertinent to agricultural plants.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the fungi colonising plant roots were identified, although root fungi may differ from soil DNA.
comments.request: Identify the fungi colonising plant roots.
comments.quote: it is not clear whether the fungi colonising the plant roots in the experiments were also identified. This would be key in assessing how the soil environment affects mycorrhizal function

comments.issue: The amount of 33P diffusion into root compartments in controls is not quantified, and 'very little' is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify control diffusion and show the proportion of 33P in the supplementary information.
comments.quote: It is not clear what proportion of 33P tracer is meant by "very little", perhaps this could be shown in the supplementary information.

comments.issue: The radioactivity introduced into each experimental system is not reported.
comments.request: State how much radioactivity (KBq or MBq) was added to each system.
comments.quote: I would have expected to see explicitly how much radioactivity (in KBq or MBq) was introduced into each experimental system.

comments.issue: 'Recovery of 33P (%)' is hard to interpret and cannot be compared with other P data.
comments.request: Recalculate 33P as mg and mg per gram of plant tissue.
comments.quote: I would urge the authors to recalculate these figures, and those from their experiments to express 33P in mg and in mg per gram of plant tissue

comments.issue: 'Assimilates' at line 60 is vague; photoassimilates may be meant.
comments.request: Specify what type of assimilates are meant.
comments.quote: be specific, what sort of "assimilates"? do you mean photoassimilates?

comments.issue: Economic and environmental production costs are not mentioned at lines 63-64.
comments.request: Add production costs to the discussion.
comments.quote: Ln 63-64: and production costs (economic and environmental)

comments.issue: AM symbiosis is presented as the sustainability factor, overlooking other interventions and variable AMF benefits.
comments.request: Acknowledge other management options and variation in AMF benefits.
comments.quote: AM symbiosis is one potential factor to promote in improving sustainability – there are lots of other interventions/management techniques and soil microorganisms that would also play a role in tandem with AMF.

comments.issue: The point at line 70 should also cite Thirkell et al. 2020.
comments.request: Add the Thirkell et al. 2020 reference.
comments.quote: Ln 70: see also Thirkell et al 2020, GCB

comments.issue: The symbiosis statement needs a reference and the possibility that above-ground selection acted against AMF responsiveness is not considered.
comments.request: Cite Leake et al. 2004 and discuss selection against AMF responsiveness.
comments.quote: selection for above-ground traits mean traits like AMF responsiveness etc may have even been inadvertently selected against

comments.issue: References are missing at line 74.
comments.request: Cite Helgason et al. 1998.
comments.quote: Ln 74: missing references here – Helgason et al 1998. Nature, 394(6692), pp.431-431. Could be a good choice?

comments.issue: It is unclear why a weedy forb was chosen after extensive agricultural background.
comments.request: Justify the choice of Plantago as host plant at this point.
comments.quote: its not clear here why Plantago is the choice of host plant for these experiments. A lot of agricultural background but then a weedy forb is chosen.

comments.issue: Only P is discussed, although much work addresses N and non-nutritional benefits.
comments.request: Mention N and non-nutritional benefits.
comments.quote: why just P? lots of work on N, also worth mentioning non-nutritional benefits

comments.issue: Specific activity, total activity per pot and total 33P mass are not reported.
comments.request: Provide specific activity, total activity per pot and total 33P in mg.
comments.quote: How much 33P in mg? provide the specific activity here, total activity per pot and total 33P (mg).

comments.issue: Scintillant type, amount per sample and replicate numbers are not reported.
comments.request: Report scintillant details and sample replication.
comments.quote: Tyoe of scintillant used? How much per sample? How many reps?

comments.issue: Results are given as recovery rates rather than 33P amounts, and decay correction and control subtraction are not mentioned.
comments.request: Provide 33P in mg or mg per g and describe decay correction and control subtraction.
comments.quote: Provide amount of 33P in mg or [33P] in mg g-1. the. recovery rate doesn't mean much to a reader.

comments.issue: The data cannot be interpreted without amounts or concentrations of mycorrhizal-acquired versus total P.
comments.request: Report mycorrhizal-acquired 33P relative to total plant P.
comments.quote: It is is difficult to interpret the meaning of these data without some numbers relating to amounts/concentratiosn of 33P (ie mycorrhizal-acquired) : total P (ie AMF + plant-acquired).

comments.issue: The lines 290-293 result should be linked to Sallach et al. 2021.
comments.request: Cite Sallach et al. 2021 here.
comments.quote: interesting! This relates strongly to work by Sallach et al

comments.issue: Whether plant P uptake compensates for diminished AMF 33P uptake is not addressed.
comments.request: Test whether plant P uptake compensates for reduced AMF P uptake.
comments.quote: Does plant P uptake compensate for diminished AMF-33P uptake?

comments.issue: The line 336 statement is an overstatement given the non-agricultural study species.
comments.request: Temper the line 336 statement.
comments.quote: I think this might be an overstatement given the species investigated here are not agriculturally relevant.

comments.issue: Sallach et al. 2021 is not cited at lines 369-370.
comments.request: Add the Sallach et al. 2021 reference.
comments.quote: Ln 369-370: also see Sallach et al. 2021 (PPP)

comments.issue: Without total 33P by mass, the contribution of AM-acquired P to plant P nutrition cannot be assessed.
comments.request: Calculate and present total 33P by mass.
comments.quote: because total 33P by mass has not been calculated or presented it is impossible to get an idea of how much AM-acquired P contributes to total plant P nutrition

comments.issue: Recent evidence on pharmaceutical fungicides and AMF function is not cited at lines 432-434.
comments.request: Cite Sallach et al. 2021.
comments.quote: See Sallach et al 2021 for recent demonstration of pharmaceutical fungicides and AMF function. Supports this study.

comments.issue: Inadvertent fungicide contamination via waste water or slurries is not considered at lines 445-447.
comments.request: Add inadvertent contamination pathways to the discussion.
comments.quote: there are also inadvertent fungicide (and other chemicals) contamination via applications of waste water or slurries (human and animal waste)

comments.issue: Farmers are expected to maintain P application rates, and plant P uptake seems to compensate for inhibited AM P uptake.
comments.request: Reconsider the claim that reduced AMF P uptake would change farming practice.
comments.quote: Well, no, farmers will maintain current P application rates. Plant P uptake seems to compensate for inhibition of AM P uptake

comments.issue: The compounds discussed can also inhibit mycorrhiza formation.
comments.request: Acknowledge inhibition of mycorrhiza formation.
comments.quote: Ln 452-453: These can inhibit formation of mycorrhizas though

comments.issue: Crop genotype effects are not investigated, so the importance for agriculture is overstated at lines 453-456.
comments.request: Temper the agricultural importance claims.
comments.quote: I think the importance of these data to agricultural scenarios are overstated here

comments.issue: The point at lines 458-460 is not new and lacks references.
comments.request: Add references or remove the claim of novelty.
comments.quote: Ln 458-460: I don't think this is new? References needed

comments.issue: The line 463-464 statement is speculative with no evidence linking the processes.
comments.request: Remove or support the speculative statement.
comments.quote: This is too speculative. No evidence for these being linked is presented here at all.

reviews.assessment: Well written, concise and clear; wishes for crop-plant replication and more microbial characterization details, and questions some statistics.
strengths: other than the comments, well done

comments.issue: Experiments were not replicated with a crop plant, reducing relevance to sustainable agriculture.
comments.request: Consider replicating the experiment with wheat, barley or oat.
comments.quote: I do wish the experiments had been replicated with at least one of the crop plants (wheat, barley, oat).

comments.issue: Glomeromycota richness in crop versus grassland soils is not discussed although fungi were sequenced.
comments.request: Report and discuss Glomeromycota richness and composition between treatments.
comments.quote: I also don't understand why there was not a discussion of Glomeromycota richness in crop vs grassland soils given that fungi were sequenced.

comments.issue: The microbial characterization methods need more detail.
comments.request: Add details on the microbial characterization in the methods.
comments.quote: I would like a few more details about the microbial characterization in the methods.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether grassland sites are comparable to the cropland fields and why they were chosen.
comments.request: Explain the selection and comparability of the grassland sites.
comments.quote: are the grassland sites of similar genera or families to the cropland fields? Why were they selected as comparisons?

comments.issue: Whether P. lanceolata grew natively at the sites is unknown, and one context-dependent species may not capture AMF capacity.
comments.request: State whether P. lanceolata occurred at the sites and justify or replace the single-species design.
comments.quote: Since AMF are so context-dependent, isn't it difficult to estimate this capacity with a single species? Why wouldn't you use wheat or barley or oat?

comments.issue: The plant composition of the non-cropped grasslands is not described.
comments.request: Describe which plants grow in the non-cropped grasslands, including P. lanceolata.
comments.quote: Lines 106-107: what plants are in these non-cropped grasslands? Is Plantago lanceolata in them?

comments.issue: Molecular and bioinformatic methods lack detail on quality filtering, taxonomy assignment, rarefaction and alpha diversity.
comments.request: Add these details, in the supplement if needed.
comments.quote: there isn't enough detail here to accurately assess the molecular and bioinformatic methods. There is nothing on the bioinformatics used, type of quality filtering, how taxonomy was assigned, if data were rarefied or not, how alpha diversity was assessed, etc.

comments.issue: The justification for choosing P. lanceolata appears only later, not where the species is introduced.
comments.request: Move the justification for the host plant choice to line 171-172.
comments.quote: no explanation of why Plantago lanceolata was chosen – ok I see it is later given in lines 212-215, but should be places here instead

comments.issue: Details of the X-ray sterilization (gamma rays, duration) are missing.
comments.request: Describe the X-ray sterilization procedure.
comments.quote: Lines 191- 192: details of X-ray sterilization needed – gamma rays and duration

comments.issue: Lines 362-372 claim benefits although Figures 2B and 2C show no higher biomass or P uptake; what the P provides is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss or speculate what benefit the P provides if not larger shoots, and move this discussion earlier.
comments.quote: Figures 2B and C undermine your results a bit so I would discuss it and at least speculate what benefits the P is providing if not larger shoots.

comments.issue: Whether AMF richness differed between cropped and non-cropped grasslands is not reported from the sequenced fungi.
comments.request: Use the fungal sequencing data to test AMF richness differences.
comments.quote: but did AMF richness differ between cropped and non-cropped grasslands? If you sequenced Fungi from those samples wouldn't you at least be able to tell this?

comments.issue: The AMF genera present are not identified from the fungal sequencing.
comments.request: Report which AMF genera were present.
comments.quote: but shouldn't you at least be able to tell what AMF genera were present if you sequenced fungi?

comments.issue: 'Phytometer' is used in Figure 1 without definition.
comments.request: Define phytometer.
comments.quote: Figure 1: what's a phytometer?

comments.issue: The Figure S2 significance pattern is implausible and the statistics are questioned.
comments.request: Verify and clarify the Figure S2 statistics.
comments.quote: I'm a little confused how that is possible, are you quite sure the stats are right here?

comments.issue: The purple, red and pine lines in Figure S7 are unexplained and their purpose is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the Figure S7 lines or remove them.
comments.quote: I don't understand what the purple, red and pine lines are on this figure. Why are they needed?

title: Agricultural management and pesticide use reduce the functioning of beneficial plant symbionts

study.system: zebra finches; wind-tunnel flocking with cameras and microphones

editor_summary: Reviewer concerns regarding statistical and analytical treatments need special attention in the revision.

reviews.assessment: Very novel study with many interesting findings; suggests restructuring and more general context, all easily addressed.
strengths: wind tunnel enabled the novel insight

comments.issue: The results-heavy format buries interpretation among descriptive detail.
comments.request: Separate the paper into traditional Results and Discussion sections.
comments.quote: Separating things into a more traditional Results and Discussion would help to reduce some of the descriptive detail, and give more airtime to the interpretation of the results.

comments.issue: When collisions with flock mates are likely in general, and the selective pressure involved, is not discussed.
comments.request: Give more general consideration of collision likelihood.
comments.quote: I also think it would be good to give more consideration of when collisions with other birds are likely in a general sense, in order to provide more context about the selective pressure for collision avoidance mechanisms.

comments.issue: The similarity of solo-position variability to homing pigeons is not noted.
comments.request: Cite Garde et al. 2020 on pigeon positional variability.
comments.quote: it might be of interest that the increased variability of bird position when flying solo is consistent with that seen in homing pigeons as reported by Garde et al 2020

comments.issue: Average figures are reported without variance, making them hard to interpret.
comments.request: Add an indication of variance for these averages.
comments.quote: it’s hard to tell whether these average figures are meaningful without an indication of the variance

comments.issue: Camera field of view is partial and the time birds spent in view is not reported.
comments.request: Report how much flight time birds were in view.
comments.quote: It looks as though there is only a partial field of view of the cameras from panels B and C. How much of the flight time were birds in view of 1 or both cameras?

comments.issue: The number of collisions and total group flight time are not given.
comments.request: Report collision counts and total flight time.
comments.quote: it would be clearer to give the number of collisions and the total flight time for group flights. The absolute number of collisions is also a point of interest

comments.issue: The evidence on Distance and Stack call functions is not summarised.
comments.request: Expand on the evidence for call function.
comments.quote: it would be useful to have more information about the body of evidence about the function of Distance and Stack calls (ref 15)

comments.issue: Energy conservation due to high metabolic flight costs is not considered as an explanation.
comments.request: Consider energy conservation as an additional explanation.
comments.quote: it could also be beneficial to conserve energy during flight, due to the high metabolic costs

comments.issue: The P13 paragraph on aviary visibility is disconnected from the following explanation.
comments.request: Connect this descriptive paragraph to the explanation on p15.
comments.quote: Is the transparency of the left panel and the ability to see the aviary relevant to the birds calling less from this position? I don’t see how this paragraph follows from the previous one.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether stack calls in sustained flight come mainly from one individual.
comments.request: Break down calls by individual and position.
comments.quote: to what extent were the stack calls in sustained flight produced by one individual? Can you break down the number of calls across individuals and contexts (i.e. positions) within sustained flights?

comments.issue: General rules linking positional changes and calling are not extracted.
comments.request: Discuss the general rules that emerge from the results.
comments.quote: are there any other positional changes that you would predict might be accompanied by a call? I guess I’m asking about the general rules that you can extract from your results.

comments.issue: Whether other birds call in flocks and whether the results inform general mechanisms is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss other species' calling and general mechanisms.
comments.quote: I would still value more information on (i) the extent to which other birds call when flying in a flock and (ii) some consideration of whether their results could provide insight into general mechanisms

reviews.assessment: Great, innovative manuscript, but repeated-measures pseudoreplication and a cause-effect concern are barriers to publication.

comments.issue: Why only 4 of 13 flight sessions were analysed, and what the other sessions were, is unclear.
comments.request: Break down the analysed and excluded sessions in a table.
comments.quote: Why were only 4 of 13 flight sessions analysed? Were the other 9 the low-level light sessions? If you could break down what these sessions were, that would be most helpful.

comments.issue: The asocial versus social positional-change data are not plotted and the Hz meaning is not explained.
comments.request: Add the plot and explain what Hz means here.
comments.quote: Is it possible to add a graph of the data from the asocial vs social horizontal positional changes to the supplementary materials?

comments.issue: Whether individual flight signatures and positions are consistent across trials is not checked.
comments.request: Check consistency of flight signatures across trials.
comments.quote: Were these, and the positioning of the individuals consistent across trials?

comments.issue: Cognitive load or unsustainable calling may explain the drop in vocalisations better than predator avoidance.
comments.request: Consider alternative explanations for reduced calling.
comments.quote: Might the cognitive load and need to prioritise focus on processing visual information be taking priority?

comments.issue: The impact of take-off calls on group order and organisation is not addressed.
comments.request: Address take-off calls or flag them as future work.
comments.quote: What impact of take-off calls on group order and organisation? This seems likely to be the most data-rich area of the study, but is largely ignored.

comments.issue: It is unexplained why collision rate did not rise in low-light and noise-masked trials.
comments.request: Explain why collision rate did not increase in those trials.
comments.quote: can you venture any explanations for why collision rate did not increase during the trials with low light levels and masking noise?

comments.issue: The link between the most vocal bird and its typical position may confuse cause and effect.
comments.request: Test whether results are driven by this bird's position.
comments.quote: But could you not be confusing cause with effect? Might your results be driven by the fact that your most vocal bird just happened to typically fly in this location?

comments.issue: Analyses ignore repeated measures of the same individuals, creating pseudoreplication.
comments.request: Use analyses that account for repeated measures.
comments.quote: Throughout the manuscript you use analyses that do not take into account that the data is derived from multiple trials involving the same individuals.

comments.issue: Wording suggestion at Page 3 Line 7.
comments.request: Change to 'adapt their own movements'.
comments.quote: Page 3 Line 7: Suggest changing to ‘adapt their own movements’

comments.issue: Hz is not explained as cycles per second.
comments.request: Explain that Hz refers to cycles per second.
comments.quote: It would be valuable to highlight that Hz refers to the number of cycles per second

comments.issue: The front/middle/back positional consistency could be summarised for clarity.
comments.request: Summarise positional consistency of front and back birds.
comments.quote: You could aid clarity here by summarising that birds at the front of the flock stayed at the front of the flock, and that those in the middle/back did likewise.

comments.issue: The cutoff used to define alignment versus misalignment is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the alignment/misalignment cutoff.
comments.quote: In this section alignment and misalignment are reported, but without specification of what the cut off for this is.

comments.issue: Whether the brief alignment period exceeds chance expectation is untested.
comments.request: Test alignment against chance expectation.
comments.quote: does this period of alignment fall outside what would be expected by chance? It only requires a momentary alignment of 4 individuals

comments.issue: How consistent the wind-tunnel conditions are is not described.
comments.request: Describe wind-tunnel condition consistency.
comments.quote: Having never used wind tunnels myself, how consistent are the conditions they generate?

comments.issue: The 24Hz sampling statement conflicts with the 120Hz recordings and should be clarified.
comments.request: State that recordings were subsampled from 120Hz to 24Hz.
comments.quote: This contrasts with the opening lines (Page 4 Line 6), where you state that you samples the video recordings at 24Hz.

comments.issue: The number of trials per low-light condition is not stated in the results.
comments.request: Add trial numbers per low-light condition.
comments.quote: Can you add the number of trials that you performed for each of the low light conditions?

comments.issue: Wording suggestion at Page 22 Line 9.
comments.request: Use 'Whether' rather than 'If'.
comments.quote: Page 22 Line 9: ‘Whether’ rather than ‘If’, would probably be a better opening to this sentence.

comments.issue: Figure S3 red dots are hard to see and wind direction is not marked.
comments.request: Enlarge the red dots and add the wind direction.
comments.quote: Can you make the red dots in this plot slightly larger? I had difficulty making them out unless I zoomed in to 200%.

reviews.assessment: Useful, elegant study, but universality claims are overstated and the f-based statistics may need recalculation.
strengths: confidently and elegantly shows visual and vocal coordination
great job tackling hard experimental challenges

comments.issue: The paper implies universality across taxa and links results to large-scale group decisions, both of which are unjustified.
comments.request: Rephrase claims about universality and large-scale decisions.
comments.quote: the observed phenomena could be universal across different taxa performing collective motion and (ii) the observed flight coordination is in relation to the large scale movement decision of a group

comments.issue: The title, abstract and introduction overstate the scope of the findings.
comments.request: Make the title, abstract and introduction more specific.
comments.quote: I suggest that the title should be more specific about the observed phenomena and the main findings, and the abstract and the introduction should also be corrected

comments.issue: Oscillatory flight may be a wind-tunnel artefact rather than natural zebra finch behaviour.
comments.request: Explain whether this oscillation occurs in natural free flight.
comments.quote: Does this occur in natural free flying zebra finch flocks? Or could this be an artificial effect (some stress induced or attempted escape reaction) that is caused by flying in the wind tunnel?

comments.issue: Inter-individual distances in the wind tunnel are not compared with natural free-flight densities.
comments.request: Compare wind-tunnel spacing with natural free flight.
comments.quote: it is not clear that how does the typical inter-individual distance in the current wind tunnel experiment relate to typical values for free flying groups of zebra finches

comments.issue: The periodicity value f does not indicate whether oscillation is present and misses harmonics.
comments.request: Use power spectrum strength and recalculate f-based statistics.
comments.quote: The periodicity value given by f does not capture whether the oscillation is present or not.

comments.issue: The data points used in statistics and the number of independent points are unclear.
comments.request: State n and ensure only independent points are used.
comments.quote: For some of the reported statistics, it is not clear what was used as “data points”. There are several places where n is not reported

comments.issue: The correlation description misleadingly implies birds move uncorrelated most of the time.
comments.request: Clarify that the shared flight direction makes motion highly correlated.
comments.quote: I think the description gives a misleading impression that during most parts of the flight the birds move in an uncorrelated way.

comments.issue: The meaning of the spatial coordinates and 'arbitrary unit' is not defined.
comments.request: Explain the coordinate units and parallax effects.
comments.quote: I did not find the definition about the meaning of the spatial coordinates. On the figure “arbitrary unit” is being used

comments.issue: The origin of the 209 ms value for Stack calls is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain where the 209 ms value comes from.
comments.quote: I did not find (and I found puzzling) where does the value of 209ms originate from (Page 13 Line 16) in relation to Stack calls

comments.issue: A non-significant Rayleigh test does not show uniformity for bimodal data such as Fig. 3D.
comments.request: Use a more appropriate circular test such as Hermans-Rasson.
comments.quote: The authors state that based on the non-significant Rayleigh test the distribution is uniform. This is problematic and I suggest rewriting this sentence

comments.issue: Panels with multiple plots rely on legend left/right and top/bottom labels.
comments.request: Add more panel and text labels to the figures.
comments.quote: the readability could be a bit better supported by using more panel labels and/or text labels on the panels

comments.issue: A value at Page 15 Line 3 is miscalculated and over-precise.
comments.request: Correct the average and consider reporting the sum.
comments.quote: I think the value given there has a typo, as the average of the 4 numbers given in the bracket is 10.25 and not 10.025.

comments.issue: Fig. S2 has positions outside the given range and it is unclear how missing points affect analyses.
comments.request: Explain the missing points and their effect on the periodogram.
comments.quote: here several positions are outside of the given range. Is this a results of the plotting, or the tracking is not available for these parts? How do such missing points impact the periodogram analysis?

comments.issue: The bottom plot of Fig. S7 is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what the bottom plot of Fig. S7 shows.
comments.quote: Fig. S7. It is not clear what is shown on the bottom plot?

comments.issue: The relative distance score divided by maximum distance is outlier-sensitive.
comments.request: Justify the relative score or use absolute distances.
comments.quote: Why is there a need for using a relative score that is divided by the maximum distance? This makes these relative values very sensitive to large outliers.

title: Vision and vocal communication guide three-dimensional spatial coordination of zebra finches during wind-tunnel flights

study.system: mammal lice and their hosts; phylogenomics of 17 louse species

editor_summary: Editor requires other methods as described by Reviewer 2, including alternative cost values and distance-based methods, before publication can be offered.

reviews.assessment: Sound and engaging study whose novel Afrotherian origin finding merits publication after minor issues are fixed.
strengths: large volume of new data including hard-to-reach louse species
novel finding of interest to a broad audience

comments.issue: The expression 'uniformly widespread' in the abstract is unclear and obscures that bird louse lineages are fewer than mammalian ones.
comments.request: Modify the abstract wording to make the bird-mammal contrast clearer.
comments.quote: The expression “uniformly widespread“ is a bit unclear here.

comments.issue: The text claims five branch rearrangements, but Figure 1 shows seven dashes for ML nodes absent from the coalescent tree.
comments.request: Reconcile the count of rearrangements with Figure 1.
comments.quote: But in Fi. 1 I found seven cases of dashes indicating ML nodes not present in the coalescent tree?

comments.issue: The abbreviation MPRs is first used when describing Figure 2 results without explanation.
comments.request: Define MPRs at first mention.
comments.quote: When describing the Fig. 2 results the abbreviation MPRs is mentioned for the first time in the text. It could be confusing for the readers.

comments.issue: The possible role of extinct mammal groups in louse evolution is not discussed.
comments.request: Add a carefully worded discussion of extinct host groups and testable predictions.
comments.quote: I wonder if a brief discussion on a possible role of extinct mammal groups in the louse evolution could be included.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether any model fitting or site-heterogeneity testing was performed for the phylogeny.
comments.request: Report model fitting and tests for site heterogeneity; ASTRAL does not address misspecification.
comments.quote: For the phylogenetic reconstruction, was any model fitting preformed? Was a possibility of site heterogeneity somehow tested?

comments.issue: The AIC likelihood test scores from the ace function are not reported.
comments.request: Report the AIC test scores in the supplements or Figshare.
comments.quote: Results of the AIC likelihood test scores from the “ace” function are not reported anywhere (in Supplements or Figshare).

comments.issue: The dashed line connecting Haematomyzus to the elephant seems to lead to trichodectids rather than Rhynchophthirina, and the Rh. abbreviation is unclear.
comments.request: Correct the dashed line and make the Rh. abbreviation visible.
comments.quote: In Fig. 1 a dashed line connects Haematomyzus with an elephant (host), but it seems to lead to trichodectids, not Rhynchophthirina. The Rh. abbreviation is poorly visible.

comments.issue: Gene trees and the concatenated dataset are not accessible in Figshare, producing an EntityNotFound error.
comments.request: Make the gene trees and concatenated dataset available.
comments.quote: Individual trees in Figshare were available but genetrees and the concatenated dataset were not

reviews.assessment: A fine contribution to cophylogeny of interest to a wide readership, but the single cost-based reconstruction and unjustified costs weaken robustness.
strengths: sheds light on the origins of mammalian lice
of interest to a wide readership and host-parasite coevolution researchers

comments.issue: The historical reconstruction rests on a single cost-based method, and alternative cost values are not explored.
comments.request: Explore alternative cost values and present the results as supplementary material.
comments.quote: their historical reconstruction of host-parasite associations is based on a single cost-based method

comments.issue: The choice of cost values is not sufficiently justified even though results depend on the a priori costs.
comments.request: Justify the cost scheme and its effect on the inferred scenario.
comments.quote: The authors do not sufficiently justify their choice of cost values and this is important because the results may vary depending on the costs assigned a priori to each evolutionary event.

comments.issue: No distance-based approach is used, although it could reveal deep incongruences and evaluate phylogenetic uncertainty.
comments.request: Add a distance-based method alongside the cost-based reconstruction.
comments.quote: The authors should also consider using a distance-based approach. Distance-based methods have been proven useful to reveal deep incongruences between phylogenetic trees

comments.issue: The number of louse genera analysed is not indicated although analyses are mostly at generic level.
comments.request: Indicate the number of louse genera analysed.
comments.quote: it would be appropriate to indicate the number of louse genera analysed

comments.issue: The proposed host-switching mechanism via a single prey escaping a raptor is implausible given that switches require sustained host-host interactions.
comments.request: Revise the mechanism toward frequent escapes maintaining straggler populations.
comments.quote: I wonder whether this is a figure of speech, but I find it hard to believe that a single prey escaping a predator would lead to a host-switching event.

title: Phylogenomics reveals the origin of mammal lice out of Afrotheria

study.system: German cockroach Blattella germanica; RNAi, pheromone and behaviour assays

reviews.assessment: Praise for the originality, breadth and robustness of the work, with requests to explain the counterintuitive JH rescue and verify RNAi knockdowns.
strengths: wide variety of approaches conferring robustness

comments.issue: Exogenous JH rescuing the effects of Kr-h1 RNAi is counterintuitive if JH signalling is impaired.
comments.request: Explain the rescue, preferably with experimental data, such as Kr-h1 expression after dsKr-h1 plus JH.
comments.quote: I found intriguing that an exogenous JH treatment rescues the effects of Kr-h1 RNAi knockdown (in terms of C29 methyl ketone production).

comments.issue: Verification that each dsRNA treatment depleted the targeted transcript is generally missing (also at lines 360 ff).
comments.request: Report quantitative transcript depletion values for the RNAi experiments.
comments.quote: I miss, in general, the verification of the decrease of the targeted transcript after each treatment with dsRNA.

comments.issue: The sex differentiation section is not didactic and the male-specific dsx repression of CYP4PC1 is hidden.
comments.request: Clarify the dsx/tra explanation and highlight the male dsx result.
comments.quote: The explanation of the game of dsx and transformer (tra) in both sexes is not diaphanous.

comments.issue: GenBank accession MZ962381 is not available.
comments.request: Make the CYP4PC1 sequence available in GenBank.
comments.quote: “CYP4PC1 (GenBank no. MZ962381)”. MZ962381 not available in GenBank.

comments.issue: Claiming CYP4PC1 controls the hydroxylation step is too specific at this stage.
comments.request: Use a more prudent statement about a possible hydroxylation role.
comments.quote: Perhaps too early to make such a specific statement.

comments.issue: Silenced is not appropriate for RNAi, which only partially depletes transcripts; used repeatedly (lines 136, 190).
comments.request: Replace silenced with a more appropriate term such as knockdown or depletion.
comments.quote: “silenced” is not an appropriate word to define the results of RNAi, as this technique always produces a partial depletion of the targeted transcript.

comments.issue: Drosophila should be specified as Drosophila melanogaster.
comments.request: Use the complete species name.
comments.quote: I presume the authors refer to the species Drosophila melanogaster. If so, please indicate this complete specific name, as the genus Drosophila includes ca. 1,450 described species.

comments.issue: The meaning of the phrase about DsxM being a primary mediator is unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase the unclear expression.
comments.quote: I don't quite understand what that expression means.

comments.issue: The male mechanism at lines 216-218 is not given a specific treatment like the female mechanisms.
comments.request: Give the male mechanism its own clearly highlighted treatment.
comments.quote: This is another mechanism, in males, different from those explained so far, in females, which would deserve a specific treatment.

comments.issue: The phrase to modulate implies teleology, incompatible with natural-selection language.
comments.request: Replace the teleological wording.
comments.quote: “To modulate” implies a purpose, which is teleological, incompatible with the language formally used in natural selection based phenomena as this one.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 225-228 is convoluted.
comments.request: Reword the sentence.
comments.quote: In addition to the convoluted phrase, I wonder why Kr-h1 expression was not downregulated in the antenna after depleting dsxF.

comments.issue: Kr-h1 expression was not downregulated in the antenna after dsxF depletion, which is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain why dsxF depletion did not reduce antennal Kr-h1.
comments.quote: I wonder why Kr-h1 expression was not downregulated in the antenna after depleting dsxF. Any explanation?

comments.issue: Targeting Kr-h1 is a less specific way to remove JH than targeting JHAMT.
comments.request: Consider targeting JHAMT with RNAi to specifically remove JH.
comments.quote: Perhaps it would be more elegant targeting JHAMT with RNAi in order to specifically remove the JH.

comments.issue: The speculation about feral male-male behaviour is unnecessary and contrasts with the robust data.

title: A single gene integrates sex and hormone regulators into sexual attractiveness

study.system: Afrotropical secondary forest chronosequence; nutrient budgets

editor_summary: Both referees want more methodological detail and greater transparency about the study's limitations.

reviews.assessment: Well-designed and enjoyable study; asks for clarity on the irregular time scale, the controversial P-limitation framing, and the burning explanation for P.
strengths: experiment very well designed and complete
text flows well and ideas are well connected
attention to elements other than N and P

comments.issue: The irregular time scale (0, 5, 12, 20, 60, 150 years) is not addressed, and it is unclear whether log-transformation handles it or only the distribution.
comments.request: State how the non-constant time scale was handled in the statistical analysis.
comments.quote: I noticed the time scale isn’t regular and increases kind of exponentially along time (0, 5, 12, 20, 60, 150), is this what you are correcting with the log-transformed response variable or it is just the data’s distribution?

comments.issue: The suggestion that the site is not P limited is controversial given evidence for widespread tropical P limitation, and this angle is underplayed.
comments.request: Highlight the P-limitation controversy more, possibly in the title.
comments.quote: Consequently, I believe this paper could be benefited of highlighting even more this issue, even considering to include it on the title.

comments.issue: Burning cannot increase total P in a closed Congo system unless biomass is declining and concentrating P.
comments.request: Clarify whether biomass is decreasing or explain how burning raises P deposition.
comments.quote: In this case there is no space for increasing P, unless the biomass in Congo is decreasing concentrating the P in the remaining biomass.

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'cycled conservatively' means and through which processes.
comments.request: Define conservative cycling and the processes involved.
comments.quote: Line 58-59: What does cycled conservatively means in this context? Through which processes?

comments.issue: The mechanisms of the canopy trapping hypothesis, which is central to the paper, are not summarised.
comments.request: Add a brief summary of the canopy trapping mechanisms.
comments.quote: I would appreciate (and I think also the readers) a bit summary of the mechanisms of the canopy trapping hypothesis, which is quite relevant along the paper.

comments.issue: There are no statistically significant trends at line 166.
comments.request: Correct or qualify the trend claim at line 166.
comments.quote: Line 166: Statistically speaking there is no significant trends there.

comments.issue: The choice of 150 years as the oldest age at line 481 is not justified.
comments.request: Explain why the maximum age is set at 150 years.
comments.quote: Line 481: Why this age is set in 150 years?

comments.issue: The calculation of root, leaf and other tissue turnover for nutrient demand is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how tissue turnover was calculated.
comments.quote: Methods, Nutrient demand to sustain primary productivity: How do you calculate the turnover of roots, leaves etc

comments.issue: The Figure S1 legend cites a paper 71 that does not exist.
comments.request: Provide the correct reference.
comments.quote: Figure S1: The legend refers to a paper 71 which it doesn’t seems to exist. Please provide it.

comments.issue: Figure 2b and Figure S9 lack the trend lines shown in previous figures.
comments.request: Add trend lines to Figure 2b and Figure S9 if appropriate.
comments.quote: Figure 2b and figure S9: Should they have a trend like in previous figures?

reviews.assessment: Important and well-written study of an understudied cation; needs site history detail, a better justified dry deposition method, and attention to multiple comparisons.
strengths: important question for secondary tropical forests and global carbon budgets
multiple methods triangulate the limiting element
Ca depletion finding cautions against C-N-P-only explanations
effective discussion of Ca and succession

comments.issue: The term 'partial nutrient budget' implies a half-hearted attempt.
comments.request: Explain once that dominant inputs and outputs were used, then call it a nutrient budget or balance.
comments.quote: I am not sure that I like the term “partial nutrient budget”, it seems to imply that you only made a half-hearted attempt to quantify inputs and outputs.

comments.issue: Site history is insufficient: whether the patches are swidden fallows, fallow lengths, why some regenerate for 60 years, and rotation numbers are unclear.
comments.request: Describe the swidden history and fallow management of the plots.
comments.quote: It is not clear from the main text whether the secondary forest patches that were studied are part of the swidden agriculture practice, and if so, what is the range of fallow lengths?

comments.issue: The calculation of dry deposition from throughfall concentrations is not explained, and canopy leakage could contaminate the signal.
comments.request: Explain how dry deposition is calculated and separated from canopy leaching.
comments.quote: a reader wants to know if the nutrient inputs being attributed to dry deposition indeed come from dry deposition and are not somehow leaked from the forest canopy, and I felt it was glossed over

comments.issue: Many non-independent quantities are regressed against forest age with no apparent correction for multiple comparisons.
comments.request: Address the multiple comparisons problem.
comments.quote: Was there any attempt to address the issue of so many multiple comparisons that do not feel “independent”?

comments.issue: The total number of plots is not stated at line 77.
comments.request: State the total number of plots.
comments.quote: Line 77. How many plots total? Line 89.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'litter turnover' in the context of tissue stoichiometry is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether senesced-leaf stoichiometry or decomposition is meant.
comments.quote: Do you mean nutrient concentrations and stoichiometry of senesced leaves or do you mean decomposition processes which is what I think of with the term “litter turnover”?

comments.issue: Waring et al. 2015 on cation use efficiency in regenerating tropical dry forest is relevant but not cited at line 92.
comments.request: Cite Waring et al. 2015.
comments.quote: This study looked at cations over succession as well.

comments.issue: The abbreviation 'excluding' at line 93 should be spelled out.
comments.quote: Line 93. Spell out “excluding” entirely

comments.issue: The statement at lines 110-111 is unclear, including whether net balances range from negative to positive and what the ranges are.
comments.request: Clarify the statement and give the ranges of values.
comments.quote: That for some of the older forest ages N, K, Ca, and Mg net balances ranged from negative to positive? What were the ranges of values?

comments.issue: 'An increase in fine root N and K supply' at line 122 is unclear, possibly meaning supply from fine root decomposition.
comments.request: Clarify what this phrase means.
comments.quote: It is not clear what you mean by “an increase in fine root N and K supply”.

comments.issue: The term 'partial balance' at line 180 seems strange.
comments.request: Revise the term.
comments.quote: Line 180. The term “partial balance” seems strange here.

comments.issue: The discrepancy between increasing available P and lower pH/increased Fe and Al mobilization is left unresolved.

comments.quote: Can you try to suggest a mechanism here? Or maybe you can be more forceful here in pointing out that for the reasons you suggest above the commonly held assumption does not apply here.

comments.issue: At line 205 it is unclear whether increasing N results from litter and fine root turnover or causes it.
comments.request: Clarify the direction of the relationship.

comments.issue: 'Slash and burn' at line 254 should be replaced by 'swidden agriculture'.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the three plots per age class came from the same or different patches, and plot distances, patch sizes and a site map are missing.

comments.quote: it is not clear to me whether the three plots per age class were collected from the same vegetation patches or different patches?

comments.issue: The dry deposition method must account for nutrient leaching from foliage, epiphytes and canopy soil, and better differentiate dry deposition from leaching.
comments.request: Justify the method and articulate how dry deposition is distinguished from leaching.

comments.issue: The word 'experimental' before 'plot' at line 360 is inappropriate because no treatments were applied.

comments.quote: Why do you have only four values for litter stoichiometry but five for the other tissues?

comments.quote: I am not sure I understood from the methods how you measured the total nutrient stocks to 1 m depth.

title: Increasing calcium scarcity along Afrotropical forest succession

study.system: Carassius fish; comparative genome assemblies of tetraploid and hexaploid species

editor_summary: Editor sees considerable potential interest but substantial concerns; cannot accept, would consider a revised version addressing the serious concerns.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the rare hexaploid result but raises ten major technical concerns about genome size estimation, assembly quality, phylogeny and validation.
strengths: impressed by results given the rarity of hexaploids
study contributes to understanding polyploid vertebrate evolution

comments.issue: Genome size estimates depend strongly on k-mer size; only 17-mer was used.
comments.request: Perform a k-mer size simulation to estimate genome sizes.
comments.quote: The estimated genome size is much affected by k-mer size in the k-mer analysis. They used 17-mer to estimate the genome size of C. auratus and C. gibelio.

comments.issue: The new C. auratus assembly is smaller than previous ones, possibly causing artificial gene losses.
comments.request: Compare all available C. auratus assemblies using RNA-seq, read and EST/cDNA alignments to demonstrate quality.
comments.quote: the authors should perform comprehensively comparisons of all available C. auratus assemblies, including RNA-seq alignment, genome read alignment, and EST/cDNA alignment, to demonstrate the quality of this new assembled genome of C. auratus

comments.issue: The placement of C. molitorella conflicts with Xu et al. 2019, which showed it as outgroup to subgenomes A and B.
comments.request: Re-examine the phylogenetic location of C. molitorella.
comments.quote: Xu et al. (Nature Communication, 2019, Figure 2a) showed that Cirrhinus molitorella was the outgroup of subgenomes A and B. The authors should carefully examine the phylogenetic location of Cirrhinus molitorella.

comments.issue: Subgenome division was validated only with subgenome-specific TEs.
comments.request: Validate subgenome division with Chen et al.'s read-alignment method using a close diploid.
comments.quote: the author should further validate the accuracy of subgenome division according to Chen et al.'s method (Chen et al., PNAS, 2020), which utilized the alignment read number from close diploid fish

comments.issue: Orthology analysis used 1:1:1 gene families rather than families retaining all subgenome copies.
comments.request: Use 1:1:1:1:1:2:2:2 gene families and report how many were found.
comments.quote: I suggest that they should select the 1:1:1:1:1:2:2:2 gene families having a single gene in each diploid, 2 common carp genes, 2 C. auratus genes, and 2 C. gibelio genes.

comments.issue: The 1.86% gene exchange frequency was not tested against a null and could reflect tree error.
comments.request: Test significance and validate exchanges with Poropuntius read numbers on homoeologues.
comments.quote: Was this frequency significantly different from the null hypothesis? To demonstrate the real signals rather than the phylogenetic tree error, the author should validate these exchanges by comparing the aligned Poropuntius huangchuchieni read numbers on the homoeologues from two subgenomes.

comments.issue: Error bars in Figure 2C and D are undefined and significance is not analysed.
comments.request: Define the error bars and analyse statistical significance.
comments.quote: In Figure 2C and D, the author should define the error bars and analyze whether there existed statistical significances.

comments.issue: Genome sequencing method information for C. auratus is missing from the supplement.
comments.request: Add and rewrite the C. auratus sequencing methods.
comments.quote: In Supplementary file, I did not see the genome sequencing method information on C. auratus. The author should rewrite it.

comments.issue: It is unclear which common carp assembly was used; ENSEMBLE annotations come from GCA_000951615.2, not the stated GCA_018340385.1.
comments.request: Clarify and correct the common carp assembly and annotation versions.
comments.quote: The ENSEMBLE transcript annotations were based on the assembly of GCA_000951615.2, rather than GCA_018340385.1 that they stated in line 181 in Supplementary file.

comments.issue: The nomenclature in Extended Data Table 6 is confusing.
comments.request: Define the CaiJi and YinJi subgenome labels.
comments.quote: The nomenclatures in Extended data Table 6 were confusing. What are 'CaiJi_A', 'CaiJi_B', 'YinJi_A', and 'YinJi_B'?

reviews.assessment: Exciting unisexual hexaploid model, but the gene conversion evidence is doubtful and the adaptive implications are speculative.

comments.issue: The almost 200-fold variation in gene conversion rate among individuals may be artifactual.
comments.request: Investigate whether the extreme gene conversion rates are real or technical artifacts.
comments.quote: The extremely large variation of gene conversion rate (almost 200 fold difference among individuals) is concerning

comments.issue: Figure 5E is hard to interpret: it is unclear why gene conversion would not affect the entire region or what causes the green genotypes.
comments.request: Show read alignments for the region so the three karyotypes can be confirmed.
comments.quote: This is quite difficult to understand - wouldn't be gene conversion affect the entire region? is there another mechanism underlying the changed genotype (green) other than gene conversion?

comments.issue: Gene conversion identification is crude: deletions and coverage variation could be mistaken for conversion.
comments.request: Show phased haplotype blocks at conversion boundaries containing converted and non-converted sites.
comments.quote: More evidence is needed to define gene conversion, for install, showing three PHASED haplotype blocks at the gene conversion boundary containing non-conversed and conversed sites.

comments.issue: It is not explained why an elevated gene conversion rate would be adaptive.
comments.request: Explain the adaptive benefit of elevated gene conversion.
comments.quote: I wonder how elevated gene conversion rate is necessarily adaptive - this is not well explained in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Whether elevated gene conversion is a derived feature of C. gibelio is untested.

comments.issue: Support for the 13 alternative gene tree topologies is unclear and ancestral gene flow or incomplete lineage sorting were not assessed.
comments.request: Assess topology support and alternative explanations for the gene exchange signal.

comments.issue: The species is popular in countries beyond the one stated at L52.

comments.issue: Awkward sentences and English usage need polishing throughout.

comments.issue: The hierarchical assembly strategy is unclear and Extended Fig. 2 only shows the long-read workflow.

comments.issue: How the level of redundancy was measured is unclear.

comments.issue: The claim at L186 that this is the only reason for the disparity may be too strong.

comments.issue: The L192 legend needs more details.

comments.issue: Fig. 3C appears to show only one example.

title: Comparative genome anatomy reveals evolutionary insights into a unique amphitriploid fish

strengths: results supported by clear and succinct figures

comments.quote: I also wonder how different habitat groups differ in their level of mean climate matching.

comments.issue: Decoupling may reflect increased adaptive capacity rather than an added burden.

comments.quote: it may also represent increased adaptive capacity, which should be addressed as an alternative explanation to the “additional burden” highlighted by the authors

comments.issue: Spatial patterns of decoupling and mean matching, and their drivers, are not shown.

comments.quote: I would be interested to see spatial patterns of climate decoupling, as well as mean levels of climate matching.

comments.quote: it would be useful to highlight a few examples of species that exhibit high and low climate decoupling

comments.quote: Results can be just stated as “Based on simulation scenarios, we did not find any effect of abundance on climate matching trends.”

comments.issue: 'Steepness' at line 86 could be replaced by a simpler term.

comments.quote: “Magnitude” may be a more appropriate (simpler) term than “steepness.”

comments.issue: Text at lines 103-111 belongs in the discussion.

comments.quote: Most of this text belongs in the discussion section. Alternatively, results and discussion sections could be combined.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 164-166 has mismatched subject and introductory phrase.
comments.request: Reformulate the sentence.
comments.quote: Sentence is poorly formulated. The subject (“our results”) does not match the introductory phrase (“their high dispersal ability”).

comments.issue: It is unclear that climate decoupling equates to an added burden.
comments.request: Clarify or revise the 'additional burden' framing.
comments.quote: Again, it is not clear that climate decoupling equates to an “additional burden.”

comments.issue: The dataset start year should be stated as 1989, not 1982.

reviews.assessment: Concise, well-executed study with a strong message; mainly asks for clearer description of analyses and several wording fixes.

liked the paper more with each reading

comments.issue: The paragraph at L101 belongs in the discussion.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether L114 relationships are assessed across species or within species.

comments.quote: Again, it needs to be made more clear if these relationships are being assessed across all species, or if this is done for each species indivdiually.

comments.issue: It is unclear why a specialized R package was needed for what sounds like a regression slope.

comments.issue: Growth is mentioned at L264 but not examined.

comments.issue: It is not clear at L275 that topics are explained later.

comments.issue: Calling Spearman's coefficient a pseudo R-square is questionable.

comments.issue: 'Regularly spreading' at L304 is vague.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and interesting, but BBS sampling biases, missing literature, phylogeny and the dispersal proxy raise major concerns.
strengths: well written and enjoyable to read
addresses two important and interesting questions

comments.issue: BBS detection and uneven sampling are not addressed and sites appear treated as randomly distributed.
comments.request: Discuss BBS sampling and detection problems.
comments.quote: I’m worried that the authors have treated the sites as if they are randomly distributed.

comments.issue: Trends are not validated against other BBS-based studies.
comments.request: Check trends against other BBS papers.
comments.quote: It would reassure me a bit if the authors checked whether their trends in bird species abundance and occupancy roughly match what other papers using the BBS data have found

comments.issue: The body of BBS abundance/occupancy modelling literature is not cited.
comments.request: Cite the BBS modelling literature (Clement, Smith & Edwards, Sauer & Link).
comments.quote: There is a whole body of literature concerned with modelling abundances/ occupancy from the BBS data (e.g. unevenly distributed data, sampling/ detection effects) and I am a bit concerned that it has not been cited

comments.issue: The migration database and how migrants were classified are not described.
comments.request: Describe the migration database and migrant definition.
comments.quote: Could you please describe the underlying database for migration. How did the original authors determine whether a species is a migrant? Was it based on observations or was it based on range maps.

comments.issue: The binary migrant category may be an insufficient proxy for dispersal ability.
comments.request: Consider alternative dispersal measures (Eyres, Laube, Sheard).
comments.quote: I wonder whether this binary category does not provide enough information about dispersal ability. Please consider looking at alternative sources of information

comments.issue: Breeding-range climate alone ignores migrants' wider non-breeding climatic tolerances.
comments.request: Discuss fundamental versus realised niches for migrants.
comments.quote: I wonder whether by looking at the conditions in the breeding range, you miss a part of the conditions that a migratory bird is able to tolerate (i.e. fundamental niche).

comments.issue: No phylogenetic control is used and patterns could be driven by particular species or groups.
comments.request: Control for phylogeny in the statistical framework.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to control for phylogeny in your statistical framework? I am concerned that the patterns could be driven by particular species or groups.

comments.issue: Representativeness of the 110 species and their phylogenetic spread are not described.
comments.request: Describe species representativeness and family-level variability.
comments.quote: However, there is no information about the representativeness of the species in the study or an idea of how evenly they are spread across the phylogeny.

comments.issue: Line 13 could be rephrased for clarity.
comments.request: Rephrase as suggested about variation across species.
comments.quote: Consider rephrasing to something along the lines of“, but how this varies across different species is less well understood”

comments.issue: The abstract loses the cause-versus-effect nuance between performance and decoupling.

comments.quote: It’s hard to know whether decreasing performance causes or is caused by climatic decoupling. I think this nuance has been lost in the abstract.

comments.issue: The prediction that larger, better-thermoregulating species track climate better is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the body-size prediction more clearly.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I follow the argument that species with larger body size and thus higher thermoregulatory capacity are predicted to more efficiently track suitable environmental conditions and better readjust distribution.

comments.issue: How climate matching change through time was quantified is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether consecutive years or other time gaps were used.
comments.quote: Could you please clarify exactly how you did this? Was it the difference between each consecutive year? Did you experiment by looking at different time gaps (in case there is a time lag?)

comments.issue: The equilibrium assumption and realised versus fundamental niche are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss realised versus fundamental niches.
comments.quote: I think a discussion of realised vs fundamental niche might be valuable here.

comments.issue: Non-climatic drivers such as insectivore declines are not considered.
comments.request: Consider other drivers, citing Bowler et al. 2019.
comments.quote: or something else other than climate is behind their decline? E.g. lots of these species are insectivores. See Bowler et al (2019).

comments.quote: Figure 3 caption: semi_open → semi-open

comments.issue: Figures 3 and 4 do not give N for each category.

title: Increasing climatic decoupling of bird abundances and distributions

study.system: bulb mite Rhizoglyphus robini; experimental evolution and genome resequencing

editor_summary: Editor requires all reviewer concerns to be addressed in a revision before a final decision can be made.

reviews.assessment: Important study supporting sexual selection and genic capture theory, with a few minor comments on interpretation and presentation.
strengths: important study that will garner interest
novel results supportive of sexual selection and genic capture theory
well-known system used in a trait-based design

comments.issue: The claim of focusing on selection on the SST is unconvincing because condition-dependent traits and the changed mating environment also select on condition and vigor.
comments.request: Acknowledge that more than direct selection on an SST is occurring.
comments.quote: If the trait is condition dependent and condition has a substantial genetic basis (both supported here and elsewhere), haven’t you selected on condition?

comments.issue: Extinction material in the introduction and conclusions is distracting and not supported by the cited meta-analysis and review.
comments.request: Stick more closely to the results in the conclusions.
comments.quote: I don’t think on close inspection the Cally meta-analysis or the AREES review by Rowe and Rundle indicates any support for a consistent effect

comments.issue: Information about the nature of variation in the SST is scattered through the manuscript instead of introduced early.
comments.request: Collect known information about SST variation into a brief paragraph early on.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful if early in the manuscript the nature of variation in the SST was explained.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive experiments and sensible analyses, but the study system's relevance and several analyses need clearer justification.
strengths: analyses sensible and conclusions supported by the data

comments.issue: The relevance of the bulb mite system and divergent selection to the study questions is unclear and needs a pre-results paragraph setting predictions.
comments.request: Add a paragraph before the results explaining the system and its predictions.
comments.quote: I found it very difficult to understand how the bulb mite system, and the divergent selection undertaken, were relevant to the questions that I took from the background information on the opening pages.

comments.issue: Previous work showing that sexual selection eliminates mutation load is dismissed or ignored without convincing arguments.
comments.request: Engage with this previous work instead of dismissing it.
comments.quote: You repeatedly explicitly dismiss (or ignore) previous work that has clearly demonstrated the role of sexual selection on males in eliminating mutation load

comments.issue: The MSB argument predicts new mutations accumulating in S but not F after 29 generations, which is not tested.
comments.request: Test whether new SNPs accumulate in S, e.g. by lowering the allele frequency threshold.
comments.quote: then after 29 generations, you should have a glut of new SNPs in the S but not F populations. Can your analysis address that question, or are loci invariant at F1 not analysed?

comments.issue: Eliminating S males fundamentally alters natural selection, so SNP evolution may reflect an artificial pressure cooker rather than natural processes.

comments.issue: The colon sentence at Line 24 is hard to follow and the second clause seems unrelated to genetic variation.

comments.issue: No citation supports the claimed general fitness effect of sexually selected traits at Line 24.

comments.issue: The meaning of SST shaping fundamental evolutionary processes at Line 42 is unclear.

comments.issue: The methods open with bewildering plaster-of-Paris detail that cannot be understood before later information.

comments.issue: It is unclear why later generations are included in Figure S2 when genetic data stop at generation 29.

comments.issue: Sperm volume and storage duration differences are not considered as alternative explanations at Line 148.

comments.issue: 'Cut off not of' at Methods line 205 is unclear.

comments.issue: The fecundity assay text at Lines 328-332 reads defensively and buries the pertinent details.

comments.issue: The number of replicate populations is not stated explicitly in the main text.

comments.issue: 'Across the three generations' at Line 451 may wrongly suggest pooled generations.

comments.quote: to avoid confusion over whether samples from different generations were pooled

comments.issue: The very rapid phenotypic response, with F at high frequency by generation 7, is not noted where relevant.

comments.issue: The analysis underpinning the Lines 63-65 statement is unclear and does not match the figure legend's t-tests.

comments.issue: A t-test is used for data displayed as boxplots where Kruskal-Wallis would be more appropriate.

comments.issue: The plural 'SSTs' and the treatment names imply multiple traits and unclear persistence, confusing the morph dichotomy.

comments.issue: 'Functionally important' in Figure 3 is undefined.

comments.issue: Survival beyond 7 days seems irrelevant to genomic divergence, and differences in the relevant window are not reported.

comments.issue: Indirect selection on maturation rates and fast versus slow investment could also produce genome-wide divergence.

comments.issue: The prediction at Line 118 is not framed against the background of Ne effects until much later.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the median and both confidence intervals can share the same value.

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'significance' and 'observed pattern' refer to at Line 141.

comments.issue: The upper confidence interval being lower than the lower interval at Line 147 suggests an error.

comments.issue: Punctuation at Line 484 leaves the 'including' clause ungrammatical.

comments.issue: The distinction between trait-specific and total sexual selection at Lines 180-181 seems inconsistent with the condition-based purging argument.

comments.issue: The Methods section at Line 267 repeats the Results and adds no detail; the space could describe bulb mite sexual selection and a schematic timeline.
comments.request: Replace the section with useful background and a schematic timeline.
comments.quote: Line 267: This Methods section is not at all useful. It repeats information that already appears in the Results section, and does not provide any useful additional detail.

reviews.assessment: Interesting evolve-and-resequence study with a non-model organism, but key genome information, validation and data accessions are missing.
strengths: interesting E&R study with a non-model organism

comments.issue: The assembled 307 Mb genome is three times larger than related mite genomes, which is remarkable and unvalidated.
comments.request: Perform k-mer and/or flow cytometry analyses to confirm the genome size.
comments.quote: However, the 307 Mb genome is 3x larger than the genome of a closely related mite (Tyrophagus putresencentiae (Acaridae), +/- 100 Mb)

comments.issue: Details and accessions for the RNAseq data and proteins used, and transcriptome assemblies, are missing.
comments.request: Provide accession numbers or proteome versions, assembly details and assembled transcriptomes.

comments.issue: The genome is only on the ORCAE server without reviewer access, and the genome and gff are not uploaded to NCBI.
comments.request: Upload the genome and gff annotation to NCBI.

comments.issue: 'Demonstrate' at line 157 overstates the evidence since 0.12 is only marginally lower than 0.13.

comments.quote: I think "indicate" instead of "demonstrate" is more appropriate here (as 0.12 is marginally lower than 0.13)

comments.issue: The XO sex determination system is asserted on the basis of a personal communication only.
comments.request: Provide evidence or arguments instead of personal communication.
comments.quote: A personal communication is poor evidence for stating that R. robini has a XO determination system, please provide evidence or arguments (instead of pers. communication) why the R. robini has a XO determination system.

comments.issue: The methodology for identifying X-linked contigs is not supported by references or previous literature.
comments.request: Support and justify the X-linked contig identification method.
comments.quote: how confident are the authors that their methodology is able to correctly identify X-linked contigs (as no references/previous literature is cited in this section)

comments.issue: Paragraphs about X-linked contigs are highly speculative because identification relies solely on read-coverage differences.
comments.request: Remove these speculative paragraphs.
comments.quote: As the identification of X-linked contigs is solely based on read-coverage difference, I think these paragraphs are highly speculative and would better be removed.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the genome-sequenced R. robini population was included in the E&R experiment.
comments.request: State clearly whether this population was part of the E&R stock.
comments.quote: I am a bit confused whether the R. robini population of which the genome was sequenced was also included in the E&R experiment.

comments.issue: NCBI accessions for the unpublished RNAseq data and IDs of the 13,389 autosomal genes are not provided.
comments.request: Provide accession numbers and gene IDs.
comments.quote: Authors should at least provide NCBI accession numbers for these unpiblished data (even if not yet publicly available)). In addition, they should provide IDs of the 13,389 "autosomal" genes.

title: Genomic evidence that a sexually selected trait captures genome-wide variation and facilitates the purging of genetic load

study.system: ecological literature; meta-analysis of research waste and missing studies

editor_summary: Editorial requests: simplify the title (no punctuation) and add a full Methods section with search strings; notes R2's framing concerns about research practice and cost-effectiveness.

reviews.assessment: Very positive review with detailed suggestions on terminology, code reproducibility, wording and additional context.
strengths: a lot of work has gone in

comments.issue: R code does not include the meta-analysis, only figure plotting, and data names differ from the code.
comments.request: Package the code reproducibly (renv or docker) and align data and code names.
comments.quote: I note that the R code does not include the meta-analysis but only the plotting of the figures from the data.

comments.issue: Calling the work a systematic review is inaccurate: only WOS was searched and no critical appraisal was done (also line 12 and Fig. S1 legend).
comments.request: Clarify that this is not a systematic review.
comments.quote: It is important that it is made clear that this is not a "systematic review" (it is a review that has been done systematically).

comments.issue: Numerous line-level copy edits: wording changes, capitalisation, punctuation and typos (ramming, 20020, tree, filed).
comments.request: Make the suggested line-level corrections throughout.
comments.quote: Line 355 and throughout - Perhaps these stages should be capitalised so “Study Planning Stage”, “Result Reporting” etc.

comments.issue: Saying unpublished papers will be detrimental is too strong.
comments.request: Change to likely be detrimental.
comments.quote: I think to say they will actually be detrimental is too strong

comments.issue: The new term at lines 38-42 is never developed and the paragraph may be unnecessary.
comments.request: Consider removing the paragraph.
comments.quote: I am not convinced you need this paragraph to make the important and compelling argument you make throughout.

comments.issue: Lines 83-84 and 112-113 repeat earlier material.
comments.request: Move these sentences to the first mention of Jennions & Møller.
comments.quote: This is a bit repeatitive from the above. Can you move these sentences up to where you first mention Jennions & Møller

comments.issue: The Figure 2 and Figure S4 y-axis shows proportion, not percentage.
comments.request: Change the y-axis label to proportion.
comments.quote: the y axis is not showing percentage but proportion - this needs to be changed

comments.issue: Low-powered studies can report effects in the wrong direction, so the reviewer disagrees with the paper's argument here.
comments.request: Acknowledge the questionable value of evidence from low-powered studies and discuss better designs.
comments.quote: a low powered study could report a negative effect where there is in fact a positve one (or visa versa)– the value of the evidence is therefore questionable.

comments.issue: Open access publishing costs exclude scientists in developing countries or without funding.
comments.request: Mention the barrier of open access publishing costs.
comments.quote: It would be good to mention here that open access publishing costs mean that it is not always an option for developing world scientists or those without funding.

comments.issue: Open Access is only part of Open Science; FAIR data, lay summaries and culture change are missing.
comments.request: Discuss the broader Open Science agenda and cultural change.
comments.quote: Open Access is only a part of Open Science – I think we need to educate more people about FAIR data and perhaps apply the principles to manuscripts.

comments.issue: It is not reported how many of the studies were computationally reproducible.
comments.request: Report the number of computationally reproducible studies.
