comments.request: Test the OxCal model against one produced with ChronoModel to detect artificial precision.
comments.quote: I would suggest that the authors test their OxCal model against one produced with ChronoModel to test their initial results and evaluate whether they are working with a chronology that is artificially precise.

comments.issue: Radiocarbon calibration issues, including underestimation by IntCal09 and IntCal13, are not addressed.
comments.request: Correct and address the calibration issue, e.g. using IntCal20.
comments.quote: This issue, though, is not addressed in the article, so it would be good to see that corrected in order to add weight to the foundational chronological aspects of this study.

comments.issue: The robustness of correlations with the Greenland chronology is not discussed despite counting errors of ca. 1500-1700 years.
comments.request: Discuss why the archaeological-climatic correlations are thought robust given the counting errors.
comments.quote: it would be good to see a discussion of why the correlations between archaeological intervals or transitions and Greenland climatic chronology are thought to be robust

comments.issue: Conclusions depend on archaeological-palaeoclimatic associations that are not yet solidly demonstrated.
comments.request: Demonstrate the associations more solidly before drawing conclusions.
comments.quote: we must be entirely convinced that our conclusions are drawn from correct associations between the archaeological record and the corresponding paleoclimatic context

reviews.assessment: Highly robust, objective study with no major problems; remaining points are clarification questions about methods, equations and faunal evidence.
strengths: objective approach that genuinely tests the hypothesis
caveats and limitations made very clear

comments.issue: 'Moments' is not the best term for the temporal units.
comments.request: Use 'periods' or 'phases' instead of 'moments'.
comments.quote: Line 86 (etc.) You refer to 'moments' - maybe 'periods' or 'phases' would be better.

comments.issue: The decrease in resource availability in the Eurosiberian region is not marked on Figure 3.
comments.request: Explicitly mark the decrease in resource availability on Figure 3.
comments.quote: it would be useful to expliictly mark the decrease in resource availability on Figure 3

comments.issue: How radiocarbon dates from the same site or stratigraphic layer are treated is not described, risking over-representation of heavily sampled sites.
comments.request: Discuss the treatment of multiple dates from the same site in the main Methods.
comments.quote: I couldn't find anything about how radiocarbon dates are treated when they come from the same site (or same stratigraphic layer).

comments.issue: The parameters and distances in Equations 1 and 2 are undefined.
comments.request: Define S1, S2, p, u, v and what 'raw-data distance' means.
comments.quote: What are S1, S2, p, u, and v? Presumably S1 and S2 are time series 1 and 2, so is p the length of the time series, with u and v values from each time series?

comments.issue: The value of parameter k in Equation 3 and its selection are not reported.
comments.request: State the value of k and justify its choice.
comments.quote: Equation 3: What value of the parameter k is actually used? How and why was this value chosen?

comments.issue: Equations 5 and 6 take very different forms although both are delta corrections.
comments.request: Explain why the two delta corrections have different forms.
comments.quote: Equations 5 and 6 have very different forms, yet they are delta corrections of temperature and precipitation respectively. Why do they have such different forms?

comments.issue: Overall herbivore biomass may mask species-specific abundances that could differ between Neanderthals and AMH.
comments.request: Consider species-level faunal assemblages from Neanderthal and AMH sites.
comments.quote: What if it is not overall THB that is important, but the abundances of particular species (and what if this differs between Neanderthals and AMH)?

comments.issue: Archaeological faunal assemblages are biased by hunting selectivity and do not reflect overall faunal abundances.
comments.request: Discuss this bias briefly in the main Methods.
comments.quote: it is not a reflection of overall faunal abundances in the region (because there is likely to be some selectivity in hunting strategies, which biases species representation in archaeological assemblages)

title: Ecosystem productivity affected the spatiotemporal disappearance of Neanderthals in Iberia

study.system: naturalized alien floras; colonial legacy analysis across regions

reviews.assessment: Fascinating, rigorous study; most comments are suggestions about scope, data limits and figure clarity.

comments.issue: Why only four empires were chosen, and whether France was excluded for lack of data, is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the selection of the four empires.
comments.quote: I wonder why the authors specifically focused on these "empires". Was the lack of data a reason for not including, e.g. France, Germany or Belgium?

comments.issue: Other empires such as Japanese, Soviet and Ottoman are not mentioned even as future work.
comments.request: Mention these empires as future work.
comments.quote: Also personally I would also have liked to the influence of Japanese colonisation of parts of Asia, the Soviet Empire or even the Ottoman empire.

comments.issue: Data completeness gaps in South America, Africa and Asia are not acknowledged as distorting results.
comments.request: Discuss how data completeness may distort the results.
comments.quote: the author fail to mention how data completeness likely might distort their results

comments.issue: Colonisation eras and types may confound the results, e.g. botanical gardens emerging during British rule.
comments.request: Discuss how colonisation era and type may influence the results.
comments.quote: Also I wonder how the different colonisation eras or types might influence the results here.

comments.issue: East India Company regions could proxy commercial interest but are not used.

comments.issue: Figure 3 is confusing and hard to read.

comments.issue: Figure 4 labels are only partly connected to dots.

comments.issue: The range used to estimate mean annual temperature is unclear.

comments.issue: A citation is missing at Ln 87-88.

comments.quote: Ln 87-88 “All these factors drove

title: Naturalized alien floras still carry the legacy of European colonialism

study.system: plant communities; NEON data across US ecosystems

editor_summary: Editor notes R2 is largely positive, R3 questions the hierarchical data and SEM appropriateness, and R1 raises major limitations, novelty concerns and missing ecological interpretation that are addressable.

reviews.assessment: Valuable large-scale dataset on a timely question, but novelty, missing ecological interpretation and data limitations weaken the contribution.
strengths: potential to address generality of stabilizing effects

comments.issue: It is unclear what is newly learned given that other studies have addressed scale-dependence of diversity-stability relationships, including at broad scales.
comments.request: Clarify the specific advance and contrast it with Patrick et al. 2021 and Catano et al. 2020.
comments.quote: My major concern is it isn’t clear what new is learned from this study.

comments.issue: Biological and ecological interpretation is almost completely missing, including any explanation for the stronger beta-diversity effect.
comments.request: Provide ecological mechanisms and grounding, explaining the beta-diversity result.
comments.quote: There are no other biological mechanisms presented to help explain/interpret their results.

comments.issue: A key claimed novelty, communities linked by dispersal, is unsupported because dispersal was not measured.
comments.request: Either measure dispersal or temper the dispersal-related novelty claim.
comments.quote: they mention a key novelty of their study is that they measure diversity across communities linked by dispersal, but they didn’t measure dispersal

comments.issue: Plant cover is used as a surrogate for biomass or productivity although cover can differ by orders of magnitude in biomass.
comments.request: Qualify the cover-function assumption and discuss its caveats.
comments.quote: the extent to which cover approximates productivity or biomass can vary substantially depending on other plant traits like plant height, growth rates, dry matter content and energy inputs/resources, etc

comments.issue: The distribution of time series lengths across sampling units is not reported and it is unclear whether lengths were considered in the models.
comments.request: Report time series length distributions and their treatment in models.
comments.quote: It isn’t reported (unless I missed it) what the distribution of time series lengths are across the sampling units. It also isn’t clear that this is considered in the models

comments.issue: Short time series of about four years may bias stability estimates because life-history differences such as perennials versus annuals are ignored.
comments.request: Discuss and account for short time series and life-history variation.
comments.quote: communities dominated by longer lived perennials may appear more stable (because many of the same individuals span the entire sampling frame) than those dominated by annuals with higher turnover rates

comments.issue: The abstract does not define what stability is measured for and uses community and ecosystem stability interchangeably.
comments.request: Define the stability measure and distinguish the two concepts.
comments.quote: The abstract should define what stability is measured for (composition? aggregate properties like density or biomass? etc).

comments.issue: The abstract does not explain what is new or how the results fit the current literature.
comments.request: State what was learned and whether it matches other studies.
comments.quote: It is also not clear how the results fit into the current understanding of the field (what new was learned? does it match with what other studies have found? Why does this matter, specifically?).

comments.issue: The last abstract sentence about extending practical diversity-stability theory and sustainable management is vague.
comments.request: Make the abstract's closing claims specific to the results.
comments.quote: The last sentence of the abstract is vague; how do these results “extend a practical diversity stability theory”?

comments.issue: The claim at Lines 51-53 that scaling remains poorly resolved lacks context from existing experimental and observational studies.
comments.request: Add context and cite the relevant scale-dependence studies.
comments.quote: I agree there are relatively few of the latter relative to the former, but I think a statement like this requires context given the appearance of other studies

comments.issue: The claim at Lines 67-68 that no study quantified scale dependence of beta-diversity effects ignores work on beta-diversity and spatial asynchrony.
comments.request: Add nuance and cite studies linking beta diversity to spatial asynchrony.
comments.quote: Is it really true that no study has quantified whether beta-diversity’s effect on stability changes with scale?

comments.issue: The novelty is hung entirely on the scale of the data although other studies quantified diversity-stability at broad scales.
comments.request: Reassess the novelty claims at Lines 77 and 221-224 in light of these studies.
comments.quote: it appears the authors hang all the novelty and value of the study on the scale of the data, but see above other studies for studies that have quantified diversity-stability across scales in large, environmentally heterogenous ecosystems

comments.issue: The beta-diversity and beta-stability relationships in Figure 2D,E may not be linear, and residual diagnostics are not reported.
comments.request: Confirm homogeneous errors and linearity through residual diagnostics.
comments.quote: Did the authors confirm through residual diagnostics (or other approaches) that linear models with homogenous errors?

comments.issue: It is unclear how Figure 2 and Figure S3 differ or why their results differ slightly.
comments.request: Explain the difference between Figure 2 and Figure S3 in the legends.
comments.quote: Why are fig 2 and figS3 different? I can’t tell for the legends what is different about the data and why some of the results differ slightly?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether SEM data were aggregated to 36 points and whether 17 path coefficients can be estimated without overfitting.
comments.request: Explain the SEM data structure, sample sizes and overfitting checks.
comments.quote: Or was the data at each scale aggregated so that there is 36 data points for each path? If the latter, is there enough data to estimate 17 different path coefficients?

comments.issue: The path from the initial meta-model to the final SEM is not described.
comments.request: Describe model evaluation and selection, including AIC or parsimony.
comments.quote: How did you work form the initial meta-model down to the final model? Were early models evaluated and modified and the final model chosen based on parsimony (AIC)?

comments.issue: Presenting simple linear models before the more comprehensive SEM is confusing.
comments.request: Consider running the SEM first and showing individual paths as partial regression plots.
comments.quote: It also seems odd to present simple linear models first, then to do a more comprehensive structural equation model which includes these linear models plus a number of other correlation structures and variables.

reviews.assessment: Well written and statistically appropriate, with a large dataset supporting generality; acceptance recommended after clarifying a few details.

comments.issue: 'Species stability' is used in the supplement but never defined.
comments.request: Define species stability.
comments.quote: In the SM, there are several places where the authors mentioned “species stability”. But this term was never defined.

comments.issue: The p-value at L132 tests all three slopes jointly, so pairwise slope differences remain unknown.
comments.request: Report pairwise comparisons between slopes, e.g. quadrat versus site.
comments.quote: the p value here only give a overall comparison between all three slopes, but we do not know the pairwise difference between any two slopes

comments.issue: The cross-reference at L142 seems to mean Figure 3 rather than Supplementary Figure 3.
comments.request: Correct the cross-reference at L142.
comments.quote: L142: You mean Fig. 3 rather than Supplementary Fig. 3, right?

comments.issue: Supplementary Tables 4/5 and S6/S7 have identical captions.
comments.request: Add explicit descriptions stating how the models differ.
comments.quote: The caption of Supplementary Table 4 is the same as that of Supplementary Table5. The same is for Table S6 and Table S7.

comments.issue: The 'opposite directions' at L216 are not specified.
comments.request: Specify what the opposite directions are.
comments.quote: L216: what are the “opposite directions”, to be more specific here.

comments.issue: MAT and MAP were fitted separately, leaving a possible interaction untested.
comments.request: Test the interactive effect of MAT and MAP.
comments.quote: I wonder if there is any interactive effect of tem.

comments.issue: With one stability value per site and scale, it is unclear how averaged slopes could be calculated.
comments.request: Explain how averaged slopes were obtained.
comments.quote: So there will be only one slope for each sptail scale. How could you calculate the “averaged” slopes?

comments.issue: The formula at L300 is unclear and symbols are undefined.
comments.request: Replace the formula with text or define the symbols.
comments.quote: L300: replace the formula with general text or define the symbols.

comments.issue: It is unclear how multiple slopes could be obtained at L302.
comments.request: Explain the multiple slopes at L302.
comments.quote: L302, same as Q7, I can not understand how you could get multiple slopes.

comments.issue: The GitHub repository contains only SEM R code, not the linear model code.
comments.request: Update the repository with the linear model codes.
comments.quote: L315: I can only find the R codes for SEM in the GitHub depository, please also update the codes for the LMs.

comments.issue: It seems there is only one model when fitting the OLS at L446.
comments.request: Clarify the number of OLS models fitted.
comments.quote: L446: Again, I think there is only one model when you fit the OLS.

comments.issue: The dark shading and bars in Figure 3 are redundant and confusing.
comments.request: Remove one of the redundant elements.
comments.quote: The Dark and bars seems redundant and somehow confusing at first glance. It looks very similar to the figures that always used for bayesian regressions. I suggest the authors remove one of them.

comments.issue: It is surprising that R2 equals 1 for stability at plot and site scale in Figure 4.
comments.request: Explain why R2 is 1 at plot and site scales.
comments.quote: I am curious why the R2 for the stability at the plot and site scale is 1.

comments.issue: The point colour meaning in Supplementary Figure 1 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain what the point colours represent.
comments.quote: Supplementary Fig 1: what does the color of the points represent?

comments.issue: The title of Supplementary Figure 3 is identical to Figure 2, obscuring the use of partial regression models.
comments.request: State in the title that partial regression models were used.
comments.quote: Supplementary Fig 3: The title of the figure looks identical to that of Fig. 2.

comments.issue: Supplementary Figures 5-6 are never mentioned in the results or discussion.
comments.request: Mention them or consider removing them.
comments.quote: Supplementary Fig 5-6 were not mentioned in the result and discussed. Consider removing them.

reviews.assessment: Important question with a well-suited dataset, but the SEM ignores data hierarchy, spatial autocorrelation and soil confounding, so its inferences may mislead.
strengths: dataset with spatial scales far larger than experiments

comments.issue: The hierarchical data were aggregated to site level and analysed with simple linear models, losing information and ignoring nested random variation.
comments.request: Account for the nested design in piecewiseSEM, including random variation among sites.
comments.quote: I only discovered from the deposited R code that the data was aggregated on the site level and simple linear models were used to understand the direct and indirect relationships

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation in the data was neither checked nor accounted for in the SEM.
comments.request: Provide spatial autocorrelation diagnostics and account for it in the SEM.
comments.quote: The data is spatial but the authors did not check for nor accounted for spatial autocorrelation in the data.

comments.issue: Seasonality measures of precipitation and temperature were calculated but not entered into the SEM.
comments.request: Consider including temperature and precipitation variability in the SEM.
comments.quote: In the methods, it is stated that also measures of variability were calculated (seasonality of precipitation and temperature seasonality), however, these were not entered into the SEM.

comments.issue: Soil properties are ignored although they may confound both plant diversity and stability.
comments.request: Consider a multi-level model where soil properties affect quadrat and plot levels.
comments.quote: This has the potential to be an important confounder since soil properties may influence both the plant diversity (higher diversity on less productive soils) as well as their stability

title: Consistent stabilizing effects of plant diversity across spatial scales and climatic gradients

study.system: Anopheles mosquitoes; wind tunnel, field and electrophysiology experiments

editor_summary: Reviewers raised a number of concerns; in particular, the revision must robustly address Reviewer 3's concerns about controls.

reviews.assessment: Congratulates the authors on a thorough and difficult study whose negative result settles the question of long-range male pheromones, with only wording comments.
strengths: extensive experimental design with lab and field observations

comments.issue: The keyword mosquito control does not match the behavioural content of the paper.
comments.request: Replace or remove the keyword mosquito control.
comments.quote: Keywords: “mosquito control” - the paper does not deal with mosquito control, but with mosquito behavior

comments.issue: The term individual at Line 34 is imprecise.
comments.request: Use species-specific or drop the term individual.
comments.quote: Line34: individual  better: species-specific or drop the term “individual”

comments.issue: Line-level wording edits: replace since with as at Line41, and avoid thanks to at Lines 284 and 345.
comments.request: Make these small wording replacements.
comments.quote: Line 284: replace “thanks to” by “via two different”

comments.issue: Chemical cues at Line 56 should be specified as chemical mating cues.
comments.request: Use chemical mating cues to distinguish from host-seeking and oviposition cues.
comments.quote: Line56: chemical cues  replace by “chemical mating cues” Anophelines use a large variety of chemical cues for host seeking, oviposition etc. hence a specification here is required.

reviews.assessment: Calls the results unequivocal and the approach exhaustive, but asks to present them more objectively and reduce anecdotal comments on a contradicted prior study.

comments.issue: The paper focuses too much on a previous contradicted study instead of presenting its own results objectively.
comments.request: Reframe around the negative result and reduce anecdotal comments.
comments.quote: Overall, I consider that the authors focus too much on a previous paper contradicted by their results.

comments.issue: English style needs editing, including avoiding conjunctive adverbs at the start of phrases.
comments.request: Edit the text for English style.
comments.quote: I recommend that the text is edited for its English style to avoid distractions not related to the science being presented.

comments.issue: The statement at Line 67 about natural conditions lacks references.
comments.request: Provide references for the statement at Line 67.
comments.quote: Line 67, please provide references to this statement

comments.issue: The hypothesis at Line 76 could instead consider males as the sex attracted to male-emitted volatiles.
comments.request: Consider the alternative hypothesis that males are attracted to male volatiles.
comments.quote: if joining larger male swarms is advantageous, would it be reasonable to instead hypothesize that males could be the sex attracted to potential male-emitted volatiles?

comments.issue: Host cues combined with swarm signals may explain the earlier positive result and should be considered.
comments.request: Consider whether host cues plus swarm signals explain the Mozuraitis result.
comments.quote: could the simultaneous presence of these host cues added to swarm-emitted signals (not necessarily chemical) explain why females were attracted in the study by Mozuraitis and collaborators?

comments.issue: The syntax of may allow at Line 97 implies pheromones exist.
comments.request: Replace may allow with could allow.
comments.quote: I suggest replacing “may allow” with “could allow”, as the current syntax seems to indicate sex pheromones do exist.

comments.issue: The phrase at Line 101 unnecessarily implies a potential role.
comments.request: State simply that female behavioural responses to male swarm headspace were investigated.
comments.quote: I suggest just stating “First, we investigated female behavioral responses to the headspace of male swarms in an olfactometer.”.

comments.issue: Antenna-electrophysiological should be the standard term electroantennographic.
comments.request: Replace antenna-electrophysiological with electroantennographic.
comments.quote: I suggest replacing “antenna-electrophysiological” with the more standard expression “electroantennographic”.

comments.issue: Minor differences and abundance claims at Lines 128-131 are made without statistical tests.
comments.request: Remove or revise these unsupported comments.
comments.quote: the authors mention minor differences but no statistical tests are presented to support the claim.

comments.issue: Reporting of negative EAG results is wordy and over-detailed.
comments.request: Simplify the reporting of inconsistent deflections.
comments.quote: The current version is unnecessarily wordy and gives too many details about the sparse inconsistent deflections observed

comments.issue: Receptivity should be responsiveness at Lines 187-189.
comments.request: Replace receptivity with responsiveness.
comments.quote: Lines 187-9, I suggest replacing receptivity with responsiveness.

comments.issue: The text speaks of quantities although compound presence itself was not reproducible.
comments.request: Refer to compound presence rather than quantities.
comments.quote: It is not compound quantities that were inconsistent, but compound presence itself was not reproducible in all cases.

comments.issue: Copy edits: verb tenses at Lines 226-229, add microscope after binocular, and correct gaz to gas in Figure 6.
comments.request: Make these small corrections.
comments.quote: Lines 226-9, please correct verb tenses as they were alternated in the same phrase.

comments.issue: The phrases at Lines 229-232 are speculative and uninformative.
comments.request: Remove or revise these phrases.
comments.quote: Lines 229-32, these phrases seem too speculative and poorly informative.

comments.issue: A paragraph starting at Line 233 begins with However, and a long unnecessary phrase follows.
comments.request: Avoid starting the paragraph with However and shorten the following phrase.
comments.quote: Line 233 onwards, please avoid starting a paragraph with the expression “However”.

comments.issue: The possibility that males need a host odour background to trigger emission is not considered.
comments.request: Suggest the host-odour-background possibility for future studies.
comments.quote: Why did the authors avoid considering the possibility that males may need a host odor background to trigger potential emissions?

comments.issue: No positive control confirms that females respond to other volatiles in the olfactometer.
comments.request: Add a positive control such as host odours and present it.
comments.quote: has any positive control been performed to confirm that females do respond to other volatiles, e.g. host odors, presented in such olfactometric conditions?

reviews.assessment: Finds the experiments straightforward and the writing clear, but says important controls and details are lacking across bioassays, chemistry and electrophysiology.
strengths: use of different collection methods appreciated

comments.issue: It is unclear whether fan acoustics were measured and whether they biased behaviour; the air-vent distance is missing.
comments.request: Report acoustic measurements and the air-vent distance.
comments.quote: were the acoustic measurements from the fans conducted, and could they have biased the behavioral results? The distance for the air vent leading to the olfactometer is needed.

comments.issue: Semi-volatile pheromones may crash out in the air tubing and it is unclear whether this was accounted for.
comments.request: Address potential compound loss in tubing and state whether tubing was cleaned.
comments.quote: Many insect pheromones are semi-volatile compounds that easily crash-out inside the air tubing. It's unclear if the authors accounted for this.

comments.issue: Positive controls demonstrating the olfactometer works are missing.
comments.request: Use positive controls such as host odour or CO2.
comments.quote: The authors are urged to also use positive controls in their bioassays (host odour or CO2) to demonstrate that the olfactometer works.

comments.issue: The olfactometer tubing and cage dimensions are not described.
comments.request: Report the olfactometer, tubing and cage dimensions.
comments.quote: Last, more information is needed on the olfactometer, including the tubing and cage dimensions (not described in the methods).

comments.issue: No internal standard was used, preventing cross validation across collection methods.
comments.request: Add an internal standard to allow cross validation.
comments.quote: The authors did not try to use an internal standard in any of their collection methods, which would have allowed cross validation in their collections.

comments.issue: The amounts of Porapak and Tenax in collection tubes are not described.
comments.request: Report the sorbent amounts used in the collection tubes.
comments.quote: it's unclear how much poropak is used in their collection tubes, and no where is it described how much tenax or poropak material is needed for the concentration levels emitted by the mosquitoes.

comments.issue: VOC mass spectra analysis and compound identification criteria are unclear.
comments.request: Describe identification criteria, including standard co-injection and NIST validation.
comments.quote: it's unclear how the VOC mass spectra were analyzed and compound identification took place. Were pure standards co-injected with the sample? Where criteria were used to validate the putative compounds from the NIST database?

comments.issue: EAG analyses lack average deflections with standard deviation and positive controls.
comments.request: Calculate mean deflections with SD and show positive controls.
comments.quote: In the analyses, calculating the average deflections to each of the compounds (and standard deviation), and showing positive controls (host odor, or synthetic standards from compounds identified in the VOC analyses) would strengthen this section of the manuscript.

comments.issue: Single EAG traces are shown without population-level analysis of variance.
comments.request: Plot the mean EAD response across all antennae.
comments.quote: In addition, plotting the mean EAD response across all antennae would demonstrate the variance in the responses. Showing one single trace without any population-level analyses, is not enough.

title: No evidence for long-range male sex pheromones in two malaria mosquitoes

study.system: 199 ecology and evolution journals; retraction and open data policy data

reviews.assessment: Concise and useful contribution whose findings would likely hold, but the paired analysis and framing of implementation dates need attention.

comments.issue: Article corrections, not only retractions, may also increase with open data policies but were not analysed.
comments.request: Consider analysing article correction notices.
comments.quote: My first thought is that it would be interesting to also look at article correction, as well as retraction.

comments.issue: The reasoning for focusing on retractions rather than corrections is not made clear.
comments.request: Make the rationale for focusing on retractions clearer.
comments.quote: If that’s part of your reasoning, then that message could be clearer.

comments.issue: A before/after paired permutation test is questionable for journals with no implemented policy, where the 2016 cut-off was imposed.
comments.request: Reconsider the paired analysis for journals without an implemented policy.
comments.quote: I’m just not entirely convinced that a before/after paired analysis is the way to go, when the cut-off has been imposed for one group.

comments.issue: Figure 1 shows only 1 of 8 box plots because of the scale and abundance of zeros.
comments.request: Redesign Figure 1 so all groups are visible.
comments.quote: Due to the scale and abundance of zeros, we can only see 1 of the 8 box plots.

comments.issue: A retraction rate versus year plot with four panes would better show time patterns and avoid imposing 2016.
comments.request: Plot retraction rate against year, marking actual implementation years.
comments.quote: If possible, I’d prefer to see a plot with retraction rate (y axis) vs Year (x axis).

comments.issue: The mandatory open data group already had higher retraction counts before policy implementation, suggesting pre-existing differences between journals.
comments.request: Address the pre-existing group differences regardless of policy.
comments.quote: I note also that the Mandatory open data group already had higher retraction count before these policies were implemented.

comments.issue: The claim that ecology and evolution particularly faces FAIR data hurdles is unsupported, and the cited preprint makes no cross-discipline comparison.
comments.request: Revise the language at line 26.
comments.quote: I’m not convinced it is ‘particularly’ true in this discipline, and from a quick read, the preprint cited does not make a comparison with other disciplines

comments.issue: Calling the assigned comparison point an 'implementation date' is confusing when nothing is implemented.
comments.request: Use clearer terminology at line 54.
comments.quote: I think calling it “implementation date” when nothing is being implemented is a bit confusing.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the 20.1% of journals with mandatory open data compares with other disciplines.
comments.request: Compare this proportion with other fields or cite estimates.
comments.quote: How does this compare to other disciplines? I imagine 20% is relatively high, has this been estimated elsewhere?

comments.issue: The Vazire reference placement implies she argues science is self-correcting, whereas she argues it relies on researchers' efforts.
comments.request: Move the reference to the end of the next sentence.
comments.quote: As written, this suggests that Vazire is making this point in her article (that science is self-correcting), when she is primarily arguing that it relies on the efforts of researchers to correct it

comments.issue: The line 79 statement provides evidence of retraction (major corrections) only, not correction generally.
comments.request: Qualify the statement to refer to retractions.
comments.quote: It provides evidence of retraction (major corrections). Would also be interesting to look at other corrections.

comments.issue: Assigning a comparative implementation date to journals with no data policy may be inappropriate, and alternative analyses are not discussed.
comments.request: Consider and discuss alternative ways of analysing these journals.
comments.quote: I just wonder about assigning a comparative implementation date to journals with no data policy. I’d be interested to hear if you’d considered other ways of analysing this.

reviews.assessment: Likes the dataset and idea but doubts the causal claim, citing multiple confounders and questionable statistical choices.
strengths: fully agrees with the authors' assumptions
likes the compilation of the dataset
living database of policies would be very useful
idea of looking at retraction rates is appealing

comments.issue: The paper makes a causal claim, starting from the title and throughout, that the observational dataset and analysis may not warrant.
comments.request: Temper the causal claim and language throughout.
comments.quote: The paper, at least implicitly, makes this causal claim, starting with the title itself, and causal language throughout the paper.

comments.issue: Co-interventions at journals occurring alongside data policy changes could explain the results.
comments.request: Address co-interventions in the analysis.
comments.quote: It could be an effect of co-interventions at the journal, occuring at the same time as the data policy has been changed.

comments.issue: Increasing scrutiny over time could produce the retraction increase independently of data policies, and this could be controlled in a joint model.
comments.request: Control for the time effect by analysing all data in a joint model.
comments.quote: Time as a confounder: Maybe more and more error checkers "went into business" over the years; so the increase is simply due to higher scrutiny (independent of the data policy).

comments.issue: Journals adopting mandatory open data may also be more willing or faster to retract papers.
comments.request: Address willingness to correct/retract as a confounder.
comments.quote: Maybe journals with a change in mandatory open data also have a higher willingness (and speed) to retract papers.

comments.issue: Journal impact factor correlates with retractions and is only indirectly controlled by the tier categorization.
comments.request: Add direct statistical control for journal impact factor.
comments.quote: The categorization in the four tiers somewhat controls for the JIF, but a more direct statistical control would be preferable.

comments.issue: Imputing the data policy change date is questionable given that 71% of journals have no date.
comments.request: Justify or improve the date imputation.
comments.quote: The imputation of the data policy change is questionable, given that 71% of journals have no date.

comments.issue: Corrections were not used even though they have lower hurdles and may be a better indicator than retractions.
comments.request: Add a supplemental analysis using correction data.
comments.quote: I thought that this would even be a better indicator than retractions.

comments.issue: There is a one- to two-year lag between policy effectiveness and publication of papers subject to the policy, which is not accounted for.
comments.request: Consider the submission-to-publication lag in the analysis.
comments.quote: When a policy becomes effective, there is a time lag of, say, 1 to 2 years until newly submitted papers (to which the policy now applies) are published.

comments.issue: Absolute raw retraction numbers per tier are not reported and strong conclusions from such rare events are doubtful.
comments.request: Report raw numbers and temper conclusions from p-values.
comments.quote: Please report the absolute raw numbers of retractions before and after policy change for each tier.

comments.issue: An inferential analysis would be better as a joint model across tiers, e.g. Poisson or zero-inflated with a policy break-point.
comments.request: Model all tiers jointly with count models and a break-point.
comments.quote: I’d try to model the data of all tiers in a joint model; maybe trying to model the absolute count of retractions in a Poisson (or zero-inflated?) model, using the date of policy change as a break-point.

comments.issue: Direct evidence that retractions were only possible because of open data is missing; the retraction notes could be analysed.
comments.request: Analyse retraction notes to test the direct open-data effect.
comments.quote: Is there *direct* evidence for the beneficial effect of open data on the frequency of spotted errors (which then lead to retractions)?

comments.issue: It is unclear how 'living' the database is, whether it is a snapshot, who maintains it, and how up to date it is.
comments.request: Explain the database maintenance and updating.
comments.quote: "living database": How living is it? Or is it rather a snapshot for one moment in time?

comments.issue: The text does not specify whether pre/post classification uses the retraction date or the date of the retracted paper.
comments.request: State clearly which date is used for classification.
comments.quote: The text is not clear whether the classification of a retraction to the pre vs. post-period is done based on the *retraction date* or the *date of the retracted paper*

title: No evidence that mandatory open data policies increase error correction

study.system: ants Monomorium pharaonis and Acromyrmex echinatior; developmental transcriptomes

editor_summary: Editor asks to address the reviewers' concerns and some editorial concerns before a final decision on the manuscript.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset with landmark potential, but key results need statistical support and the purifying-selection claim and possible confounds need attention.
strengths: potential to be a landmark in sociogenomics
mechanistic data from hormone and RNAi manipulations

comments.issue: Library quality may covary with developmental stage, which could explain part of the canalization pattern.
comments.request: Provide analyses confirming that technical variation does not drive the pattern.
comments.quote: If (due to e.g. lower yield during extraction) there is more technical variation in the earlier brood stages (smaller individuals), this could explain at least a part of this observation.

comments.issue: The distribution of discarded low-quality transcriptomes across life stages and castes is not reported.
comments.request: Report how discarded transcriptomes are distributed across stages and castes.
comments.quote: Please also provide information on how the numbers of discarded transcriptomes due to low quality were distributed across life stages and castes.

comments.issue: Many key results rest on visual inspection rather than statistical analysis.
comments.request: Provide statistical support and clear descriptions of the statistical tests.
comments.quote: many of the key results seem to be based on visual inspection of patterns (Especially figure 1, but also Figure 3 and Extended data figure) rather than statistical analyses

comments.issue: Cross-species stage matching based on similarity makes the later similarity claims circular.
comments.request: Explain whether stage matching creates circularity.
comments.quote: I wonder whether there is an element of circularity in making claims on transcriptome similarities across species at any developmental stage, when the developmental stages are matched based on their similarity in the first place

comments.issue: Excluding samples that do not correlate with their sample class may bias the variation results.
comments.request: Justify excluding low-correlation samples.
comments.quote: is it appropriate to exclude samples that do not correlate highly enough with other samples in their samples class. Please justify.

comments.issue: The jump from results to purifying selection as the evolutionary cause is too long.
comments.request: Tone down the purifying-selection claim or support it with analyses.
comments.quote: the logical jump from presented results to purifying selection being the evolutionary cause for the patterns is a quite long. This should be toned down or supported more strongly with analyses.

reviews.assessment: Exciting, comprehensive and novel dataset that sets the standard; comments concern definitions, statistics reporting and table/figure clarity, and can be fixed with minor revisions.
strengths: novel analysis clearly lacking from existing research
sets the standard for future work
well written and exciting to follow

comments.issue: Canalization is not defined in the introduction, only later in the results.
comments.request: Explain what canalization means early in the paper.
comments.quote: Canalization is not defined in the introduction, with the definition only given on line 218 within the results section

comments.issue: The null hypothesis and expectations for diverging castes are not stated.
comments.request: State the null hypothesis and what is expected as castes diverge.
comments.quote: what is the null hypothesis? What would we expect to find in two castes that are becoming more different over developmental time?

comments.issue: The source of the canalization definition is unclear.
comments.request: Give a reference for the definition or state that it is new.
comments.quote: I cannot find the source of this definition in the literature. Is this your own definition or is there a reference?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether key adult caste genes change at early stages.
comments.request: Consider a time-course analysis of gene expression, e.g. with Mfuzz.
comments.quote: I feel with this data you could have provided information about the way gene expression changes over time.

comments.issue: The genome-wide developmental potential statistic is not defined in the main text.
comments.request: Explain how the developmental potential statistic was calculated.
comments.quote: statistic needs to be better defined in the main text, as to how this has been calculated, as it is critical to understanding the figure 3

comments.issue: How hymenoptera-specific genes were determined is not described in the methods.
comments.request: Describe how hymenoptera-specific genes were identified.
comments.quote: Line 317: How did you work out if a gene was hymenoptera specific. I couldn't find this in methods, but may have missed it.

comments.issue: Supp. figure 6 does not show that gyne canalized genes are specifically upregulated in the ovary; gynes are the background.
comments.request: Revise the claim about ovary-specific upregulation.
comments.quote: Supp figure 6 does not really show that gyne canalized genes are specifically upregulated in ovary.

comments.issue: The Figure 1a legend does not explain what edge lengths mean.
comments.request: Explain edge lengths in the Figure 1a legend or methods.
comments.quote: However, I feel the legend is not clear enough and I was initially confused by what is shown. There is no explanation for what the length of edges mean in legend or methods

comments.issue: The Figure 1a legend omits that the network is undirected, so sample positions are arbitrary.
comments.request: Add the undirected-network caveat to the Figure 1a legend.
comments.quote: The legend should also include the comment from the methods, that the plot is of an 'un-directed network', so the positioning of samples is somewhat random

comments.issue: The Figure 1b PCA is confusing: whether species matrices were merged and how PC dimensions were handled is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the Figure 1b PCA construction, including ortholog numbers.
comments.quote: I was really confused by PC1. Does this mean that you merged the two species gene expression matrices before running the PCA?

comments.issue: Figure 3a shows many large BPA-predicted workers at the third instar that disappear by the pre-pupal stage, which is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what happens to these large predicted workers.
comments.quote: Can you explain why we see this pattern, did these individuals die?, did they convert into gynes later on? Or do you think they were wrong predictions of their future caste.

comments.issue: Extended Data Fig. 6 is not shown for A. echinatior.
comments.request: Show the same plot for A. echinatior, even if not significant.
comments.quote: Is there a reason not to show the same plot for A. echinatior. Even if it does not show the same pattern, I think it is important to see if there is some similar trend

comments.issue: Many worker canalized genes are unannotated LOC genes of possibly unknown function.
comments.request: Provide more information about these unannotated genes.
comments.quote: does this suggest that a lot of the genes maybe species specific or have unknown function in drosophila

comments.issue: It is unclear whether all genomes and annotations are publicly available; the A. echinatior files say 'in house'.
comments.request: Provide archive links for all genomes and annotations.
comments.quote: Are all the genomes and annotations used in this paper publically available. E.g. genome and annotation file for Acromyrmex echinatior, say 'in house'. I cannot find the link to an archive in methods.

comments.issue: 'Low RNA quality (RIN < 4)' is undefined; filtered individual numbers are missing and removing low-similarity individuals may hide non-canalized cases.
comments.request: Explain RIN < 4 and report the filtered individuals and what removing them may hide.
comments.quote: It is a shame just to remove individuals with less than 0.8 similarity, these could have been interesting too, and could potentially show that some individuals are not canalized.

comments.issue: Supp. table 1 headers suggest adult caste comparisons, so the 1st instar difference is unclear; tabs for other stages may be missing.
comments.request: Clarify the Supp. table 1 contents and add missing stage tabs.
comments.quote: In the main text, line 171, you suggest there is a difference between 1st instar caste phenotypes, is that what is shown in Supp table 1, the headers suggest this is a caste gyne/worker (maybe adults)?

comments.issue: The contents of each supplementary table are confusing without a readme.
comments.request: Add a readme for the supplementary tables.
comments.quote: Supplementary tables need a readme, either within the files or elsewhere (if not already). I am confused about the contents of each Supplementary table.

comments.issue: How the 65 conserved genes were derived from the FDR tables, and which genes they are, is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the derivation of the 65 conserved genes and list them.
comments.quote: E.g. on line 237 you refer the 65 conserved genes between the two species, yet in this table, we have the FDR pvalues (with tabs for each stage) in both species

reviews.assessment: Easy to follow and interesting, with a valuable Freja discovery; interpretation of JH timing, the master regulator claim and sample timing need attention.
strengths: Freja discovery is a valuable contribution

comments.issue: Whether the findings apply to all ant colonies is doubtful because M. pharaonis has unique canalization and blastogenic caste determination.
comments.request: Discuss caste determination in both study species and the scope of the framework.
comments.quote: M. pharaonis, which they focus on in this study, seems to have undergone some unique canalization events that make the larval stages more robust to environmental cues. How is caste determined in A. echinatior?

comments.issue: Caste determination of the two species is buried in the methods instead of introduced early.
comments.request: Discuss caste determination of the two species at the beginning of the paper.
comments.quote: I think caste determination of the two species they use might be something that they might want to discuss at the beginning rather than bury in the methods.

comments.issue: The names of the two species are not given at line 38.
comments.request: Provide the names of the two species.
comments.quote: Line 38: Please provide the names of the two species

comments.issue: E93 is labelled Eip93F in Fig. 3c.
comments.request: Use E93 consistently in Fig. 3c.
comments.quote: Fig. 3c: It looks like the graph for E93 is labeled Eip93F. To keep things consistent, I suggest using E93 for this.

comments.issue: The data show a heterochronic shift in JH shutdown timing, not the JH pathway as the key regulator of canalization.
comments.request: Consider the heterochronic-shift interpretation instead of the key-regulator framing.
comments.quote: rather than the JH signaling pathway acting as "a key regulator for caste canalization in ants" (line 263), the heterochronic shift in the timing of shutdown of JH is the critical switch between worker and gyne differentiation

comments.issue: The master regulator claim for Freja is weak because RNAi gives intermediate, not worker, phenotypes.
comments.request: Weaken the master regulator claim or examine canalized genes in Freja knockdowns.
comments.quote: They claim that this gene is a master regulator of queen phenotype, but I think the evidence is somewhat weak to make this claim.

comments.issue: No evidence is presented for feedback from body size to JH signaling.
comments.request: Provide evidence for body-size feedback or remove the claim.
comments.quote: I am not sure the authors have presented evidence that there is feedback from body size.

comments.issue: The methods are written in active voice, unlike the usual convention.
comments.request: Clarify whether active voice is intentional.
comments.quote: The methods section is written in active voice. Was this intentional? Typically, methods section is written using passive voice

comments.issue: The timing of larval sample collection within an instar is unclear, which could bias transcriptome similarity estimates.
comments.request: Describe the larval sampling timing and discuss potential over- or underestimation.
comments.quote: Based on the Extended Data Table 1 and 2, the exact timing of when samples collected for larval transcriptomes is not clear.

title: Canalized gene expression during development mediates caste differentiation in ants

study.system: deer mice; population genomics and long-read inversion detection

reviews.assessment: Very well written and comprehensive study; a few suggestions on rationale, references and figures.
strengths: very well written and a pleasure to read
complete picture of origin, diversity and adaptive function

comments.issue: Why analyses were run per population or population pair rather than across all populations is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for population-wise analyses.
comments.quote: what is the rationale for performing this analysis in individual populations or population pairs, instead of across all the populations at once?

comments.issue: The reference cited at page 3 line 4 is not the most appropriate.
comments.request: Cite lostruct (Li and Ralph 2019) or Todesco/Huang.
comments.quote: I am not sure this is the most appropriate reference – I think it would make more sense to cite lostruct (Li and Ralph 2019)

comments.issue: Deleterious-mutation accumulation is not compared between inversion and non-inversion regions.
comments.request: Compare load in inverted versus non-inversion regions.
comments.quote: another important comparison would be with non-inversion regions of the genome, which would tell whether either or both orientations of the inversion experience increased accumulation of deleterious mutations due to the reduction in their effective population size

comments.issue: The 2.2M-generation forest-prairie split conflicts with Hager et al.'s 10-15KYA estimate.
comments.request: Explain the difference between the two divergence estimates.
comments.quote: Hager et al., 2021 places instead the diverge at 10-15KYA. What is the difference between the two estimates?

comments.issue: Divergence estimates for individual inversions are not provided.
comments.request: Estimate divergence dates for individual inversions.
comments.quote: having divergence estimates for the different inversions (as done in Hager et al. 2021 for inv 15.0) would be of interest

comments.issue: The thin yellow and orange lines in Figure 3A look like single-strand overhangs.
comments.request: Clarify what the thin lines represent.
comments.quote: the thinner yellow and orange lines in the left panel (NHEJ) make it look like those are single-strand overhangs – is that the case (are those meant to represent microhomology regions)?

comments.issue: The tan outline in Figure 4A is unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify whether the tan outline is the species range.
comments.quote: I am guessing the tan outline on the map represents the range of P. maniculatus?

comments.issue: Figure 4B does not highlight focal populations and its black outlines are hard to see.
comments.request: Highlight focal populations and use brighter outlines.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to highlight the focal populations in red also in this panel

reviews.assessment: Clear, well-organized study with striking results; only minor comments on context, overstatement and wording.
strengths: important reference point for future studies

comments.issue: The introduction lacks detail on prior studies (refs 12-15) to frame the work.
comments.request: Add detail on previous studies to put the work in context.
comments.quote: It would be helpful in the introduction to provide more detail on the results of studies to date to put this work in context, particularly refs 12-15.

comments.issue: The discussion does not give the % of the genome involved or comparison with other systems.
comments.request: Give the % of the genome and comparisons with other systems.
comments.quote: A reminder for the reader of the % of the genome that is involved along with context on findings from what few systems do have data is needed.

comments.issue: Calling the finding 'remarkable' while prevalence remains elusive is inconsistent.
comments.request: Clarify the basis for calling the system remarkable.
comments.quote: how do we really know if this system is “remarkable”?

comments.issue: The 'evolutionary histories' sentence raises expectations not met by the analyses.
comments.request: Reword this section to be less speculative.
comments.quote: I was expecting to see data on estimates of ages or origins of inversions or analysis of selection, etc. That may be out of scope, but rewording of this this section is needed to make it less speculative.

comments.issue: The claim that most inversions are unlikely to be strongly deleterious is overstated.
comments.request: Soften the claim and describe the two interrupted genes.
comments.quote: I agree with this sentiment, but this seems like a bit of an overstatement.

comments.issue: The choice of mutational-load approach versus a TE-based one is not justified.
comments.request: Discuss why this mutational-load approach was chosen.
comments.quote: another approach to investigating mutational load in inversions uses TEs (as in ref 30). It would be useful to discuss why this specific approach was chosen.

comments.issue: The sunflower (ref 30) parallel is not acknowledged.
comments.request: State the shared hypothesis explicitly, citing ref 30.
comments.quote: This hypothesis is intriguing and seems testable using a simulation approach.

comments.issue: Statements about recombination suppression and high homozygosity appear contradictory.
comments.request: Clarify how both statements hold together.
comments.quote: Both of these statements can be true and are not necessarily in opposition, but there is an opportunity to be very clear and careful

comments.issue: Whether homozygosity mitigates suppressed-recombination impacts is not simulated.
comments.request: Simulate the mitigation by homozygosity.
comments.quote: This also seems like an opportunity to use simulations to determine how much the expected impacts of suppressed recombination are mitigated by homozygosity.

reviews.assessment: Well written with valuable inversion descriptions, but the 'massive' headline and the hypothesis framework need fixing.
strengths: careful description of inversion locations relative to centromeres and telomeres
tremendous genomic resources for the species

comments.issue: The 'massive' inversion headline ignores the >1Mb detection filter, making it like a one-tailed test.
comments.request: Amend the headline and title to reflect the search filter.
comments.quote: Given the filtering, this is a little akin to a one tailed test, and given the authors never considered ‘small’ inversions, I think this general headline (its stated like this in the title, which should be corrected)

comments.issue: The overlap with previous cytogenetic studies and detection bias are not analysed.
comments.request: Compare with prior studies and discuss detection bias.
comments.quote: How many were previously detected but were not found in this study, and why do the authors think they were able to discover 20 additional ones?

comments.issue: The hypothesis-testing framework at the end of the introduction lacks rigour and detail.
comments.request: Describe the rationale and testing framework rigorously.
comments.quote: the hypothesis testing framework that is described at the end of the Introduction lack rigour and detail

comments.issue: Impacts on 3D chromosome structure, accessibility and expression are not discussed in detail.
comments.request: Discuss 3D structure and expression impacts in more detail.
comments.quote: All of this will likely have a pronounced influence on the gene expression. I think that the authors should discuss this in much more detail.

comments.issue: The relationship between overdominance and mutational load is not plotted.
comments.request: Plot heterozygote frequency against mutational load.
comments.quote: What is the relationship between the mutational load in inversions that are overdominant, i.e. where inversion heterozygotes are common? Can this be plotted (frequency of hets vs mutational load)?

comments.issue: The magnitude of significant trait effects, e.g. tail length, is not quantified.
comments.request: Report exact effect sizes for significant traits.
comments.quote: It is stated that inversions have a significant impact on some phenotypic traits, such as tail length. Can more exact measures please be provided? What is meant by significant? 2% or 20%?

comments.issue: Missing article at page 7 line 40.
comments.request: Add 'a' to 'with a mean length'.
comments.quote: Page 7, line 40, add a to state ‘with a mean length’

comments.issue: Smaller <1Mb inversions are not flagged as future work.
comments.request: Add smaller inversions to the discussion as future work.
comments.quote: Future work should start to explore the role of smaller <1MB inversions I think.

title: Chromosomal inversion polymorphisms shape the genomic landscape of deer mice

study.system: tropical peatland soils; 15N tracer incubations plus nosZ community sequencing

editor_summary: Editor reports the work was very well received but reviewers ask for a number of methodological clarifications that must be addressed before publication.

reviews.assessment: Well-conceived, important study of understudied tropical peatland soils; needs clarifications on controls, statistics, figures and methods details.
strengths: well conceived design tested main hypotheses

comments.issue: Unclear whether non-sterilized control soils also received the NO2 spike, and the term untreated is ambiguous between gamma-sterilized and Zn-treated soil.
comments.request: Clarify the treatments and the meaning of untreated.
comments.quote: are the non-sterilized control soils also receiving the NO2 peak? Because their methods include a mixture of gamma-sterilized soil and Zn treated soil, the term untreated is confusing in the text

comments.issue: The different methods and the data they generate are hard for readers to follow.
comments.request: Add a schematic figure describing the methods.
comments.quote: authors could make a schematic figure to describe their methods. It could help the readers understand the goal of using these different methods and the data generated by the distinct methods.

comments.issue: The Fe2+ versus N2O production analysis uses a subset of samples and sample size differs between text and legend.
comments.request: Include all samples unless there is a reason to subset, and explain n.
comments.quote: did authors select for a subset of samples (in the text you write n = 6 while in the figure legend n=4)? Why?

comments.issue: The very high R2 for Fe2+ and N2O production may be driven by low values plus a single very high value.
comments.request: Evaluate the relationship separately in Fe-rich and Fe-poor soils, showing individual points.
comments.quote: The very high R2 might be driven by having very low values and a single very high N2O production value.

comments.issue: Unclear whether non-irradiated soil also received 100 uM NO2.
comments.request: State this in the sentence describing the incubations.
comments.quote: is the non-irradiated soil also receiving 100uM of NO2? If yes, add this information in this sentence

comments.issue: Not every panel of Supplementary Fig. 2 shows grey values for non-irradiated samples at the high-NO sites.
comments.request: Explain or add the missing non-irradiated data.
comments.quote: Why not every figure from Sup. Fig2 has gray values (corresponding to the non-irradiated samples for the FCA and SCB sites -high NO sites)?

comments.issue: Table 1 gives averages of three samples without any measure of variability.
comments.request: Add standard deviation or 95% confidence intervals.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to see also the standard deviation or the 95% confidence interval of these values.

comments.issue: The claim of N2O reduction at low pH overlooks earlier reports, such as Palmer et al. 2020.
comments.request: Cite Palmer et al. 2020.
comments.quote: This is not the first study to report N2O reduction at low pH, please refer to the article of Palmer at al 2020

comments.issue: No statistics support the statement that consumption rate gradually increased with nosZ clade II.
comments.request: Show statistics supporting the statement.
comments.quote: Right now there is no result supporting this specific statement.

comments.issue: Ordination plots appear to show site averages of four replicates, hiding variability.
comments.request: Show all samples or add standard deviation to site positions.
comments.quote: are the position for the samples the average of 4 replicates? One suggestion would be to show the position to all samples or add standard deviation

comments.issue: Unclear whether chemodenitrifiers outcompete canonical denitrifiers or the environment selects for chemodenitrifiers because abiotic NO2 reduction is fast.
comments.request: Discuss which scenario is more likely.
comments.quote: Would chemodenitrifiers outcompete canonical denitrifiers or would this specific environment select for chemodenitrifiers as abiotic NO2 reduction occurs at high rates?

comments.issue: In Figure 4 a crossed box for gene absence overlays the presence symbol and is counter-intuitive.
comments.request: Use an empty square to show absence of the gene.
comments.quote: personally I find counter intuitive that the crossed box indicate absence of the gene. Maybe an empty square would be a clear representation

comments.issue: The discussion does not address differences between nosZ clade I and II and their consequences for N2O consumption.
comments.request: Add discussion of nosZI versus nosZII differences with relevant literature.
comments.quote: I would add some statements to discuss the differences authors observed between nosZI and nosZII groups and what are the consequences for the N2O consumption rates

comments.issue: Unclear whether Fe measurements were made on intact soil or after Zn addition.
comments.request: State how Fe was measured.
comments.quote: are the Fe measurements performed in intact soil cores or after the addition of Zinc?

comments.issue: Primers for the nosZI and nosZII qPCR assays are not reported.
comments.request: Report primers and reference literature.
comments.quote: please mention the primers that were utilized for nosZI and nosZII qPCR assays and the reference literature

comments.issue: No qPCR inhibition test is reported although humic-rich peat extracts may inhibit amplification.
comments.request: State whether an inhibition test was run.
comments.quote: Have authors performed an inhibition test before running a qPCR assay? It is highly recommended to run an inhibition test when samples might contain co-extractants

comments.issue: The sequence read archive bioproject number is missing.
comments.request: Add the SRA bioproject number.
comments.quote: Line 496: Please add your SRA bioproject number

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-designed study with excellent site coverage, but missing net N2O flux data and misleading wording must be fixed, plus method details added.
strengths: integration of tracer process studies with nosZ community data

comments.issue: Net N2O fluxes from the soil surface were not measured, yet motivation and implications rely on peatlands as atmospheric N2O sources.
comments.request: Describe how production and consumption measurements differ from net flux to the atmosphere.
comments.quote: is build upon the role of tropical peatlands as important atmospheric N2O sources, but net N2O fluxes from soil surface were not measured

comments.issue: Main text gives no description of how production and consumption were measured, leaving readers with false impressions about the data.
comments.request: Add a short description of production and consumption methods in the main text.
comments.quote: there should be a short description of the methods used to study the production (line 121->) and consumption (line 175).

comments.issue: Wording such as N2O flux implies in situ net flux measurements although data come from soil incubations.
comments.request: Replace flux wording with production and consumption throughout.
comments.quote: Any wordings hinting towards net N2O flux measurements from soil surface should be removed throughout the text, and the authors should instead use the correct terms production and consumption instead of N2O flux

comments.issue: Real in situ N2O flux data from these sites, if available, are not reported.
comments.request: Report any published or unpublished in situ flux data from the field sites.
comments.quote: If any real in situ flux data N2O from any of these field sites are available, either previously published or unpublished, they should be reported.

comments.issue: The scaling of fluxes at lines 323-329 is problematic because net N2O fluxes were not studied, and its calculation is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the back-of-the-envelope calculation and its inputs in main text and Methods.
comments.quote: The flux scaling on lines 323-329 seems problematic to me, since net N2O fluxes were not studied.

comments.issue: The role of nitrification in N2O production is ignored because it was not directly studied.
comments.request: Acknowledge the role of nitrification where appropriate.
comments.quote: Please acknowledge the role of nitrification in appropriate palces, it should not be ignored just because it was not directly studied here.

comments.issue: The motivation lacks references and quantitative estimates for N2O emissions from the tropics and tropical peat soils.
comments.request: Add references and quantitative estimates.
comments.quote: Add ref and some quantitative estimate for N2O emissions from tropics; also some numbers for tropical peat soils would be good to have.

comments.issue: Main text does not say whether the peatlands were pristine, drained or cultivated, or received external N inputs.
comments.request: State peatland condition and N inputs in the main text.
comments.quote: Here, it would we very important to know if these peatlands were pristine or managed, e.g. drained? Did they receive external N inputs?

comments.issue: It is not described how even mixing of the isotope label was achieved.
comments.request: Describe the mixing in the methods.
comments.quote: Even mixing of the label is important for reliable results. How was this achieved? Please describe in the methods section.

comments.issue: Absence of biological activity in sterilized controls is not shown to be confirmed, for example by CO2 flux.
comments.request: Describe in the methods how absence of biological activity was confirmed.
comments.quote: Was the absence of biological activities confirmed somehow, e.g. by checking the CO2 fluxes? Please describe in the methods section.

comments.issue: The Fe2+ regression is driven by the two highest points, so it is unclear whether the correlation is real.
comments.request: Use a log-log scale to assess the correlation across the low range.
comments.quote: This regression is very much driven by the two highest points. Using log-log scale would give a better spread for the data in the low range

comments.issue: The regression is reported without p-value or confidence interval.
comments.request: Give the p-value and confidence interval.
comments.quote: Please give also the p-value, and confidence interval for the regression.

comments.issue: Complete denitrification is not defined (NO2- to N2, measured as N2O consumption?).
comments.request: Define complete denitrification.
comments.quote: Please define what you mean with complete denitrification here, from NO2- to N2 (measured as N2O consumption)?

comments.issue: The idea in lines 130-132 is unclear.
comments.request: Reword the passage.
comments.quote: The idea here does not become clear, needs some rewording.

comments.issue: Temperature dependence of abiotic versus biotic production and its implications are not elaborated.
comments.request: Elaborate on temperature dependence and implications.
comments.quote: This should be elaborated a bit, e.g. is abiotic as biotic production dependent on temperature and how? And what are the implications?

comments.issue: Deep groundwater used in incubations may contain more reduced Fe2+ and enhance chemodenitrification; its treatment and chemistry are unreported.
comments.request: Report filtering and Fe2+ and mineral N content of the water and comment on possible effects.
comments.quote: Ground water from deep peat layers was used for soil incubation with top soils. Was this water filtered somehow prior to use, and were Fe2+ and mineral N contents similar to those in your soil sample material?

comments.issue: Incubation temperature is not reported or compared across sites.
comments.request: Report the temperature and whether it was similar across sites.
comments.quote: What was the approximate temperature, and was in similar at all sites?

comments.issue: A method is described only elsewhere, with no summary of its main principles.
comments.request: Add a short summary of the main principles.
comments.quote: A short summary about the main principles would be good even if is is described in detail elsewhere.

comments.issue: Only summary tables and graphics are made available rather than full data tables.
comments.request: Make the full data tables available.
comments.quote: In addition to summary tables and graphics, also the full data tables should be made available

comments.issue: Sequencing data are not in a public database.
comments.request: Deposit sequencing data in a public database.
comments.quote: and sequencing data should be added to a publicly available database

reviews.assessment: Timely, novel and important study with strong breadth and mechanistic depth; only superficial weaknesses in presentation and some method clarifications.
strengths: integration of isotopic, flux and molecular measurements

comments.issue: Lines 57-64 are hard for non-experts to follow, including the significance of the clause about low steady-state concentrations.
comments.request: Revise for readability.
comments.quote: sentence construction means that the text is a bit more difficult to understand for non-experts who are unfamiliar with the details of N cycling and abiotic reactions

comments.issue: If Mn(IV) is scarce, it is unclear whether NH2OH conversion to N2O is less common than the NO-N2O reaction.
comments.request: Clarify the relative importance of the two pathways.
comments.quote: If Mn(IV) is generally only present in sparing amounts, does this mean that the conversion of NH2OH to N2O is less common than the

comments.issue: It is unclear whether chemodenitrification includes NH2OH conversion to N2O via Mn(IV) reduction.
comments.request: Clarify what chemodenitrification covers.
comments.quote: chemodenitrification is referenced but it is not clear if this umbrella term also includes the conversion of NH2OH to N2O via reduction of Mn(IV)

comments.issue: The range of peatland types sampled, including high elevation sites, is not highlighted.
comments.request: Highlight the span of peatland types in the text.
comments.quote: It is worth highlighting that the peatlands sampled in this paper span a range of different types, including high elevation peatlands.

comments.issue: The broad distribution and types of sampled peatlands are not reiterated where they support representativeness.
comments.request: Highlight the breadth of peatland sampling to support representativeness.
comments.quote: the broad distribution and types of peatlands you have collected samples from, as it helps add weight to the argument that this study is broadly representative of a range of different tropical peatland ecosystems

comments.issue: The 15NO2- spike may exceed background concentrations and stimulate dose-dependent reactions, inflating rates relative to field conditions.
comments.request: State whether the tracer amount was within the observed range and acknowledge caveats.
comments.quote: Was the amount of 15NO2- added within the observed concentration range? The way this is phrased in the text (i.e. ten-fold spike) suggests that the amount of 15N tracer added could have exceeded the background concentrations

comments.issue: The site-specific corrections are not explained.
comments.request: Add a brief conceptual explanation of the corrections.
comments.quote: Can the others briefly explain what the site specific corrections entail? A brief conceptual explanation would be sufficient for this section of the text.

comments.issue: Sample size in the text (n=6) conflicts with the supplementary figure legend (n=4) for Supplementary Fig. 1.
comments.request: Correct the inconsistency.
comments.quote: in the main text it says that the n=6 for Supplementary Fig. 1, whereas in the figure legend in the supplementary materials n=4

comments.issue: It is unclear how N yield was calculated for chemodenitrification, and Supplementary Fig. 2 shows progress curves rather than yield.
comments.request: Explain the N yield calculation.
comments.quote: How is the N yield calculated for the chemodenitrification reaction? Also, Supplementary Fig. 2 shows progress curves, but not N yield.

comments.issue: Apparent low-pH tolerance may reflect microsite heterogeneity or microbes altering their micro-environment rather than true tolerance.
comments.request: Consider microscale pH heterogeneity as an explanation.
comments.quote: To what extent could the apparent tolerance of low pH conditions (e.g. at the SJO study site) be due to heterogeneity in environmental conditions at the aggregate or consortium scale?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether consumption exceeded production significantly at FCA and MEL, since error bars seem to overlap.
comments.request: Test or state whether consumption significantly exceeds production.
comments.quote: Was consumption significantly greater than production for FCA and MEL? The means look marginally higher but the error bars seem to overlap

comments.issue: How the correction factor is calculated is insufficiently described.
comments.request: Expand the description, in the supplement if needed.
comments.quote: Could the authors please expand on the description of how the correction factor is calculated?

title: Coupled abiotic-biotic cycling of nitrous oxide in tropical peatlands

study.system: Astatotilapia calliptera cichlids; lake and river populations, methylome and transcriptome

editor_summary: Editor rejects the paper: reviewers find the work of potential interest but the strength of the novel conclusions is insufficient, so it cannot be published in Nature Ecology & Evolution.

reviews.assessment: A timely addition to epigenetics and speciation, but design and methods issues, especially sample mismatch and low WGBS sample size, prevent publication in its current shape.
