comments.quote: I doubt the feasibility in linking data from smartphone apps to TRY data, because TRY data has many criterions, such as natural biomes or common garden, adult trees or small trees, sun leaves or shade leaves.

comments.issue: The high correlation is unsurprising because the data span many climate zones, and climate could drive the correlation.
comments.request: Test or discuss climate as the driver of the correlation.
comments.quote: the high correlation between these two sets of data is normal, because the data used in this manuscript is from lots of climate zones, and climate can shape this correlation

comments.issue: The manuscript lacks novelty given a previously published Scientific Reports paper with similar ideas.
comments.request: Clarify the advance relative to Schiller et al. (2021) or justify novelty.
comments.quote: Third, this manuscript seems lack of novelty. I found one paper published before in Scientific Reports, which also showed the similar ideas.

title: Citizen science plant observations encode global trait patterns

study.system: Nematostella and sea urchin; Brachyury ChIP-seq and knockdown

editor_summary: Editor sees considerable potential interest but substantial concerns; cannot accept but would consider a revised version addressing the serious concerns.

reviews.assessment: A great job overall, though the sea urchin summary figure is interpreted differently and binding-site and motif clarifications are requested.
strengths: well pointed out Bra function in stomodeum invagination

comments.issue: The number of putative Brachyury binding sites differs greatly between Nematostella (2389) and Strongylocentrotus (490).
comments.request: Explain the difference in binding site numbers.
comments.quote: In contrast that approximately 2389 putative biding sites in Nv, only 490 sites were found in Sp. Please explain this difference.

comments.issue: The proposed Bra-FoxA-Wnt circuit is not supported by showing Bra-binding motifs in FoxA and Wnt genes (or in Bra itself).
comments.request: Show FoxA binding sites in Fig. 3 and Bra-binding motifs in FoxA, Wnt and Bra genes.
comments.quote: the reviewer would like to see the present of Bra-biding motifs or sequences in FoxA and Wnt genes

comments.issue: Figure 7 combines two different sea urchin GRNs and may mislead on Brachyury function and evolution.
comments.request: Revise Figure 7 so the distinct archenteron and stomodeum GRNs are not conflated.
comments.quote: this figure which combined two different GNR stories likely mislead the evolutionary developmental expression and function of deuterostome Brachyury

comments.issue: The discussion does not consider that the caudal tip forms late in vertebrate gastrulation, beyond the main blastopore and notochord expression.
comments.request: Frame the discussion with the timing of caudal-tip formation in mind.
comments.quote: caudal-tip is formed at later phase of gastrulation in vertebrates, beside major expression and function of Brachyury in blastopore and notochord, or contiguous to the blastopore. Therefore, discussion should be done with this point in mind.

reviews.assessment: Impressive work whose first claim is well substantiated, but the analyses behind the second and third claims need new analyses, toning down and clearer limitations.
strengths: potentially of great importance to a broad audience

comments.issue: Datasets are not comparable: mouse data come from in vitro NMPs and FACS-purified T+ cells while other species use whole-embryo homogenates, and stages may differ.
comments.request: Clarify the profiled cell states and stages, add a schematic, discuss impacts, or generate matching mouse ChIP-seq data.
comments.quote: Clearly, to reach the conclusions it is of pivotal importance that genomics experiments are carried out on comparable cell populations (both spatially and temporally). However, this is not necessarily the case here.

comments.issue: Conclusions rest on a single mouse ChIP-seq dataset.
comments.request: Repeat the analyses with other published mouse Brachyury ChIP-seq experiments such as Lolas et al. 2014.
comments.quote: the authors should perform the same analyses using other published mouse Brachyury ChIP-Seq experiments (at least Lolas et al, PNAS 2014 comes to mind) to see if their conclusions hold up and substantiate the claims

comments.issue: It is unclear whether cross-species target differences reflect lack of regulation or lack of expression.
comments.request: Provide pairwise analyses of direct and indirect targets detected in each species using RNA-seq.
comments.quote: could the authors provide detailed pair-wise analysis which of the direct and indirect Brachyury targets identified in one species are also detected (so not necessarily regulated) in the other species (at the RNA level using the RNA-seq data)?

comments.issue: Sequencing depth and library preparation details are missing and could cause the observed differences.
comments.request: Report sequencing depth and library prep strategy for all samples.
comments.quote: the authors should provide information regarding sequencing depth, library prep strategy, etc of all the samples, to exclude that these have caused the observed differences

comments.issue: The Nematostella mRNA-protein discrepancy is unexplained and the home-made antibody may detect only a specific isoform.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy and verify antibody specificity across isoforms.
comments.quote: How did they ensure that this is not due to the home-made antibody only detecting a specific Brachyury isoform (if there are actually different isoforms of Brachyury in Nematostella?)

comments.issue: The expansion of the Brachyury domain upon knockdown is surprising and protein-level knockdown is unconfirmed.
comments.request: Confirm spatially resolved Brachyury protein down-regulation in vivo.
comments.quote: It would be important to confirm that Brachyury is indeed down-regulated at the protein level (in vivo and spatially resolved).

comments.issue: Neural gene repression occurs in the aboral domain where Brachyury is absent, so the link to cell-intrinsic NMP-like repression is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether repression is cell-intrinsic and direct, and distinguish anterior versus posterior neural fate.
comments.quote: Thus, it is unclear to me how the authors relate the function of Brachyury in vertebrate NMPs to the observed neural gene repression in Nematostella?

comments.issue: Figure 6 conclusions depend on marker lineage allocation that contains obvious errors.
comments.request: Reassign marker lineages carefully, e.g. using single-cell compendia.
comments.quote: the conclusions drawn from the analysis are highly dependent on the accuracy of lineage allocation of the markers. Unfortunately, there are obvious problems here.

comments.issue: Co-factors at palindromes versus half-palindromes are not examined.
comments.request: Check for different co-factors in palindromes versus half-palindromes and their functional relevance.
comments.quote: Could the authors check for different co-factors in palindromes vs half-palindromes? Could this provide functional relevance?

comments.issue: Whether peaks with distinct co-factors correspond to different target classes is untested.
comments.request: Relate co-factor classes to target gene classes such as GO category or activation status.
comments.quote: Do the peaks with distinct co-factors relate to different classes of target genes? (GO category? Activated/repressed?).

comments.issue: Co-factors specific to Brachyury-mediated repression or activation are unknown.
comments.request: Perform split motif analysis for up- and down-regulated direct targets.
comments.quote: could the authors perform a split motif analysis for up-regulated and down-regulated direct targets of Brachyury to identify co-factors specifically associated with Brachyury-mediated repression or activation?

comments.issue: No cross-species panel shows Brachyury mRNA and protein across developmental stages.
comments.request: Add a Brachyury expression panel and a schematic of stages and cell populations analysed.
comments.quote: It would be very helpful to add a panel with Brachyury expression (mRNA and protein) in all species analysed (including e.g. mouse, Xenopus) across developmental stages

comments.issue: The NMP introduction implies all cited studies show all tissue contributions and omits Wymeersch et al.
comments.request: Clarify which study shows what and cite Wymeersch et al. 2016 and 2019.
comments.quote: to my knowledge not all show contribution to all these tissues, and it should be made clear which study shows what

comments.issue: Default parameter settings are not reported.
comments.request: Provide the exact default settings for reproducibility.
comments.quote: For reproducibility reasons the authors should provide the exact default settings.

comments.issue: The in-house python script for MEME-ChIP is not available.
comments.request: Deposit the script on GitHub or a similar repository.
comments.quote: For reproducibility reasons this script should be deposited on e.g. GitHub repository

comments.issue: 85 differentially expressed ChIP targets are reported, but 44 plus 46 sums to 90.
comments.request: Correct the inconsistent target numbers.
comments.quote: The authors mention 85 differentially expressed ChIP targets, but indicate that 44 and 46 are down- and up-regulated respectively, which sums to 90.

comments.issue: Penetrance of ISH and IF staining or phenotypes is not reported.
comments.request: Report numbers of samples with observed staining or phenotype per number analysed.
comments.quote: For all ISH & IF experiments the penetrance of the observed staining / phenotype should be provided (number of samples with observed staining / number of samples analysed).

comments.issue: Figure 6 gene counts in the text do not match the figure (27/4 versus 25/3).
comments.request: Check and correct the numbers related to Figure 6.
comments.quote: they mention 27 genes in node V of which 4 are neural markers, whereas I count 25 and 3 respectively.

comments.issue: Vertebrate endoderm markers are missing from the analysis.
comments.request: Complement the analysis with vertebrate endoderm markers.
comments.quote: it would be of utmost interest to complement the analysis with vertebrate endoderm markers

comments.issue: The 23-27% of peaks without a Brachyury motif are suggested to be indirect binding, but the mediating co-factors are not defined.
comments.request: Define putative co-factors and test whether these peaks represent a different target class.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to define putative co-factors that mediate indirect Brachyury binding (through motif analysis), and perform e.g. GO analysis to test if these binding peaks encompass a different class of targets

comments.issue: The reasoning that Tbx6 is negatively regulated by Brachyury does not follow; positive regulation with feedback is equally possible.
comments.request: Clarify the logic of the Tbx6 regulation argument.
comments.quote: I don't understand the reasoning. Brachyury could still positively regulate Tbx6 expression, but then be repressed by Tbx6 in a negative feedback loop?

comments.issue: The mesp and twist observation could be substantiated by checking for putative Brachyury motifs.
comments.request: Check for Brachyury motifs near mesp and twist to test whether binding or binding sites evolved.
comments.quote: Are there putative Brachyury motifs in the vicinity (regulatory regions) of mesp and twist in Nematostella or Strongylocentrotus?

comments.issue: The neural-to-mesodermal rewiring discussion is too limited.
comments.request: Provide more examples and discuss how such rewiring might have been achieved.
comments.quote: Could the authors provide a more extensive overview of such examples and discuss how such rewiring might have been achieved?

comments.issue: The dense computational analyses are hard to follow.
comments.request: Add analysis workflows to the main figures and schematic illustrations of sub-conclusions.
comments.quote: To increase manuscript readability it would help to add a workflow of each analysis pipeline to the main figures, and illustrate each sub-conclusion with a schematic.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and thorough, but the circuitry claims and the direct-repression interpretation need discussion and toning down.
strengths: thorough analyses combining ChIP-seq with functional studies

comments.issue: The effects of Wnt and FGF signalling and FoxA on Brachyury itself are not addressed, so the circuitry claim is one-sided.
comments.request: Discuss the feedback on Brachyury and tone down the circuitry claims.
comments.quote: the effects that Wnt (and FGF) signalling and FoxA have on Brachyury itself have not been specifically addressed in this study

comments.issue: The neural gene increase may reflect indirect axial misspecification via Wnt signalling rather than direct repression by Brachyury.
comments.request: Discuss how to disentangle direct repression from indirect axial misspecification and tone down the claims.
comments.quote: it is quite likely that the observed effect on neuronal specification is in fact indirect, and due to a more global misspecification of patterning along the primary axis (due to disruption in Wnt signalling)

comments.issue: A more recent OMA reference exists.
comments.request: Cite the newer OMA reference.
comments.quote: Line 182: a more recent reference for OMA is https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkaa1007

comments.issue: The python script is not provided.
comments.request: Provide the python script.
comments.quote: Line 228: please, provide the python script.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether embryos of both species were treated the same way.
comments.request: Clarify the embryo treatment for both species.
comments.quote: Line 246: it is not clear whether the embryos of both species were treated in the same way.

comments.issue: The fraction of genes not associated with active chromatin is given without numbers.
comments.request: Provide percentages or numbers for this fraction.
comments.quote: Line 368: please provide % or numbers for the fraction of genes not associated with active chromatin.

comments.issue: The asymmetric Brachyury antibody localization around the blastopore may be an artifact.
comments.request: Clarify whether the asymmetric localization is artifact or reproducible biology.
comments.quote: Figure 1b: the Brachyury antibody shows an asymmetric localization around the blastopore. Is this an artifact, or a biologically reproducible pattern?

title: An ancestral Wnt–Brachyury feedback loop in axial patterning and recruitment of mesoderm-determining target genes

study.system: Enterobacteriaceae carrying pOXA-48; clinical isolates and fitness assays

reviews.assessment: Fantastic, rigorous paper well suited for publication; mainly minor clarifications about resolution, variants and conjugation.
strengths: clearly highlights a significant knowledge gap
well-suited for publication in this journal

comments.issue: Large evolutionary claims exceed the discrete-time-point resolution and detection limits of the data.
comments.request: Estimate heterogeneity, clarify temporal resolution and avoid over-claiming.
comments.quote: The authors make large evolutionary claims about within-host changes over time, yet it is not entirely clear what level of resolution they have by which to draw these insights.

comments.issue: The criteria for selecting the 14 PV variants are only in the methods.
comments.request: Justify the variant selection in the results section.
comments.quote: Although the criteria is discussed in the methods, a brief discussion of which variants and why they are chosen deserves to be in the results section to justify the significance of the later findings.

comments.issue: The role of conjugation in the observed results is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how important conjugation is for the results.
comments.quote: it’s unclear how important the authors interpret conjugation to impact the results that they see

reviews.assessment: Impressive amount of work, but the novelty and importance of the conclusions do not match the effort invested.

comments.issue: The conclusions are largely unsurprising and the advance does not match the effort.

comments.quote: the novelty and importance of the conclusions the authors are able to reach do not seem to match the effort put in

comments.issue: The promised new infection-control strategies never feature in the Discussion.

comments.quote: The authors claim that the data generated will lead to new strategies for infection control and so I was keen to see what was suggested based on the reported findings but this did not appear to feature in the Discussion.

comments.issue: When the plasmid variants appeared in each patient's journey is not emphasised.

comments.quote: it would be quite interesting to think about the time profile for each patient and the points at which the characterised plasmid variants were found

comments.issue: The L171-173 description of same-clonal-background isolates carrying different PVs is ambiguous.

comments.quote: it seems that it is vital that what it means is crystal clear because it is central to analysing how the evolution of plasmid variants have evolved

comments.issue: PCN not correlating with fitness cost is surprising and unexplained.

comments.quote: On L135-136 it seems surprising that PCN does not show a correlation with fitness cost.

comments.issue: The double potentially/potential at L181-182 weakens the suggestion.

comments.quote: the double potentially/potential “potentially involved in the potential within-patient evolution events” considerably weakens what the authors are suggesting

comments.issue: The J53 model-host limitation only appears in the Discussion.
comments.request: Raise the J53 point in the Results section.
comments.quote: The point about J53 not being a good model host was not something that I picked up from reading the Results section

comments.issue: Carrying strains may be those with the least burden, predicting burden variation across Enterobacteriaceae.
comments.request: Test burden variation across the patients' Enterobacteriaceae.
comments.quote: This would predict that if the range of Enterobacteriaceae from these patients were tested there would be significant variation in the burden caused by the plasmid.

comments.issue: Complex figures would benefit from short panel titles.
comments.request: Add one- or two-word titles to each panel.
comments.quote: It would be good if the Figures were made more friendly.

reviews.assessment: Exceptional, innovative study of the highest scientific quality; only minor wording, statistics and framing suggestions.
strengths: suitable for the broad readership of NatEcoEvo

comments.issue: Capitalisation at line 26.

comments.quote: line 26 should read "Antimicrobial"

comments.issue: It is not explained that the study focuses on one plasmid with multiple variants.
comments.request: Add a short statement for general readers.
comments.quote: for a general audience it would be helpful to offer a short statement explaining that you are focusing on a single plasmid but that there are multiple genetic variants across the collection

comments.issue: PV selection criteria are not stated at line 103.
comments.request: State the PV selection criteria briefly here.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to briefly state here what the PV selection criteria were to save readers diving into the methods

comments.issue: 'PVs carrying J53 genomes' at line 106 does not make sense.

comments.issue: The use of non-parametric tests is not justified.

comments.quote: I wondered why you had resorted to non-parametric tests; explain here or in the methods

comments.issue: Wording issue at line 122.
comments.quote: line 122 "rates"

comments.issue: Separate pairwise correlations versus a multiple regression are not justified.
comments.request: Explain or use a multiple regression.

comments.issue: Redundant wording at line 181-182.
comments.quote: line 181-182 "potentially involved in the putative"

comments.issue: The result referred to at line 339 is not recapped.
comments.request: Recap the actual result being referred to.

comments.issue: The classic test of expression cost (Nguyen et al. 1989) is not cited.

comments.quote: this paper is a really neat direct test of the cost of expression

comments.issue: The effect at lines 345-348 depends on the frequency of antibiotic selection.

comments.quote: surely this effect would be dependent on the frequency of antibiotic selection, i.e. the non-resistant variant could completely displace the resistance variant given long enough in the absence of antibiotics

comments.issue: Source-sink plasmid dynamics are not mentioned at lines 352-362.

comments.quote: perhaps mention here source-sink plasmid dynamics

title: Within-patient evolution of plasmid-mediated antimicrobial resistance

study.system: Timema stick insects; climate adaptation genomics across species

editor_summary: Editor requires reviewer concerns and editorial points to be addressed in a revision before a final decision can be made.

reviews.assessment: A thorough and integrative study with sound analyses, but it lacks interpretation, discussion of caveats and generalization to other systems.
strengths: comprehensive analysis of repeated evolution in response to climate
liked the study design and analysis

comments.issue: The limitations of inferring parallelism from 100 kb windows, which cannot show same-allele parallelism, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of the windowed approach.
comments.quote: The limitations of a windowed approach should be discussed somewhere in the paper.

comments.issue: There is no discussion of why parallelism patterns differ among PCs or why PC3 shows the strongest pattern.
comments.request: Explain the PC-specific parallelism patterns, especially PC3.
comments.quote: There was also no discussion of why the parallelism patterns differed for the different PCs or why PC3 showed the strongest pattern.

comments.issue: The differing genetic-ecological distance relationships across PCAs, including the PC3 pattern opposite to most taxa, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss why the genetic-ecological distance relationships differ among PCAs.
comments.quote: There was no discussion of why the relationship between genetic and ecological distance differed for the different PCAs (positive for one, negative for the other and flat for the third?!)

comments.issue: The overall magnitude and biological relevance of parallelism are never assessed or discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether the observed parallelism is biologically meaningful and predictable.
comments.quote: There was also no comment or discussion on the overall magnitude of parallelism, which is usual for these types of papers.

comments.issue: Divergence times among taxa are not given or considered as a driver of the patterns.
comments.request: Report estimated divergence times and discuss their role, including variance among pairs.
comments.quote: There was no mention of the divergence times between the taxa or whether that could have driven some of the observed patterns.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the patterns generalize to other systems, such as those with recent divergence and gene flow.
comments.request: Generalize or compare the findings to other well-studied systems.
comments.quote: at the end of the paper I didn’t have a good sense whether the patterns described here were representative of what we would expect in other systems

comments.issue: Figure 2 is cited before Figure 1 in the text.
comments.request: Swap the order of Figures 1 and 2.
comments.quote: Figure 2 is referred to before Figure 1 in the text and thus it would be better to swap the order.

comments.issue: It is not stated which climatic variables or PCs are most closely associated with the altitudinal cline.
comments.request: Add a sentence linking the experiment's altitudinal cline to specific climatic variables or PCs.
comments.quote: a sentence should be added indicating which climatic variables/PCs are most closely associated with the altitudinal cline of the experiment?

comments.issue: The enrichment test gives no insight into the fraction of adaptive variation evolving in parallel versus uniquely.
comments.request: Quantify the fraction of adaptive variation that is parallel.
comments.quote: However, we are not getting any insight on the relative amount of parallel evolution going on in this system (vs unique adaptation).

comments.issue: Some taxa were analysed with as few as 3,074 SNPs, and SNPs per window are not reported.
comments.request: Report SNPs per window and assess whether low counts affected observed parallelism.
comments.quote: For most of the taxa the analyses were based on relatively few SNPs (as little as 3,074) – how many SNPs were there generally in a window? If it was 1 or 2 could this have affected the level of observed parallelism?

reviews.assessment: A strong, novel multispecies comparison with clear methods and figures, but key terms and their framing need revision.
strengths: strong analytical approach for window comparison
large dataset in taxa and sequence data
methods clearly described and figures clear

comments.issue: CHC comparison is absent from the introduction although it forms a key part of the results, and its rationale regarding elevation is unclear.
comments.request: Introduce the CHC analysis and explain its rationale earlier.
comments.quote: CHC comparison was not brought in at all in the introduction but then forms a key aspect of the results. The reader needs much more information on this.

comments.issue: The climate variables used and their relevance are not introduced, nor is the distinction between climate and geographical variation.
comments.request: Provide background and justification for the climate variables in the introduction.
comments.quote: I would like more information about the climate variables that were included and why they are relevant in the species.

comments.issue: It is unclear what the background population structure at L177 is compared against.
comments.request: Clarify what the focal species is compared to in the background structure.
comments.quote: is the background population structure all other populations combined in comparison to the focal species, or what is the species compared to?

comments.issue: Largely allopatric elevational and climatic variation is called parallel evolution at the organismal level.

comments.quote: I would not call (largely allopatric) variation along an elevational and climatic distribution ‘parallel evolution’ at the organismal level.

comments.issue: Climatic niche differences are equated with 'divergence in ecology' and similarity with 'shared ecology', although ecology differs from climatic tolerance.

comments.issue: 'Divergence in genetics' is not standard terminology for genome-wide genetic divergence.

comments.quote: I found the term “divergence in genetics” not very standard or intuitive; ‘genome-wide genetic divergence’ or ‘evolutionary divergence’ or other terminology around shared phylogeny and history would be more representative, in my opinion.

comments.issue: The relevance of 'probability' to repeated genomic patterns in climate adaptation is unclear in the text and short title.

comments.quote: I don't see how “probability” per se is particularly relevant to the repeated use of genomic patterns in climate adaptation eg line 25 and the short title.

comments.issue: The focus on PC3 is unmotivated and the claim that PC1 and PC2 show the same patterns conflicts with Figure S5.

comments.quote: The reasoning for focusing on PC3 for the shared windows analysis is not clearly motivated and I’m not sure it’s fair to say that PC1 and PC2 show the same patterns

comments.issue: 'Moreover' at line 55 is confusing given the preceding sentence.

comments.quote: line 55: the word ‘moreover’ is a bit confusing given the preceding sentence. I suggest you revise.

comments.issue: At line 76 it is unclear whether parallel evolution refers to phenotypes or genomics.
comments.request: Clarify line 76.
comments.quote: Line 76: it's not clear here if parallel evolution is talking about phenotypes or genomics. I suggest revise.

comments.issue: The possibility that environments themselves change over time is not mentioned at line 79.
comments.request: Note that environments may change over time.
comments.quote: Line 79 also the environments themselves may change over time.

comments.issue: The referent of 'in different taxa' at L77 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether ecotypes or lineages are meant.
comments.quote: L 77 I am not clear what "in different taxa" refers to.

comments.issue: The word 'thus' at Line 132 is unnecessary and confusing.
comments.request: Remove or revise 'thus'.
comments.quote: Line 132 I don't think the word thus is needed here and is confusing.

comments.issue: Statistics at Line 162 are reported without degrees of freedom.

comments.issue: It is unclear at line 178 whether the analysis is SNP-based or window-based.

comments.quote: line 178 I thought we were looking at windows rather than individual SNPs (preceding paragraph) so I am not clear if this is SNP-based or not

comments.issue: More information on the elevational differences at line 290 would help.

comments.quote: line 290: more information on the elevational differences would be useful here

comments.issue: How three compounds and two sexes make six CHC traits is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the CHC trait count at Line 308.
comments.quote: Line 308 I'm not familiar particularly with CHC analyses but I don't see how three compounds analysed and males and females makes six traits for CHC

comments.issue: The lack of introgression is interpreted in a way that ignores selection's role in parallel evolution.
comments.request: Rephrase what the lack of introgression says about selection.
comments.quote: I think introgression also shows a role of selection in driving parallel evolution therefore I suggest rephrasing exactly what the lack of introgression is saying about selection at this point.

comments.issue: T. podura may have only one individual per population across 12 populations, and supplementary numbers differ.
comments.request: Flag the limited sampling and check the supplementary numbers.
comments.quote: L416 is it the case that T. podura has only one individual per population x 12 populations? This is very limited for a genomics of divergence/ response dataset, and should be flagged in the related results.

comments.issue: Four reads per allele is very low coverage.
comments.request: Raise or justify the read coverage threshold.
comments.quote: L635 4 reads for an allele is very low coverage.

reviews.assessment: Creative and interesting analyses, but the null expectation, climate-as-ecology proxy, introgression conclusions and circularity need stronger support.
strengths: interesting attempt to partition ecology and genetics contributions
addresses an important question with a good system

comments.issue: The null expectation for overlap is based on sample size rather than permuted environmental data, and randomizations occur after the genetic associations.
comments.request: Permute environmental data before genetic associations and redo the overlap test.
comments.quote: there is no way of truly knowing what the actual null expectation in overlap of climate-associated SNP windows should be unless you perform the same test on permuted data

comments.issue: Using climate as a proxy for shared ecology may fail in systems where similar species occupy different niches within the same climate.
comments.request: Discuss whether the climate proxy for shared ecology is appropriate for this system.
comments.quote: I wonder how using climate data as a proxy for shared ecology would be limited in cases such as these.

comments.issue: Lack of contemporary introgression does not exclude historical gene flow, whose timing and magnitude could affect parallelism.
comments.request: Discuss the timing, magnitude and duration of past gene flow as relevant parameters.
comments.quote: You infer that since there is not strong evidence for contemporary introgression, then it must not have played a role in parallel evolution

comments.issue: The x-fold excess measure may not represent parallelism and the model explaining it with shared ecology and genetics is potentially circular.
comments.request: Repeat the analysis with permuted data to rule out statistical artifacts.
comments.quote: I am wary about what the measure of x-fold excess in shared top SNP windows represents and if it truly embodies a measure of parallelism, and if it should somehow be explained by both ecology and genetics

title: Climatic similarity and genomic background shape the extent of parallel adaptation in Timema stick insects

study.system: humans; ancient/modern genomes and forward simulations of sweeps

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of some interest but raise concerns about the advance over earlier work and the strength of the novel conclusions, which preclude publication.

reviews.assessment: Finds the premise valuable but says the claims are grander than warranted, the literature review one-sided, and key figures and analyses misinterpreted.
strengths: adds to the growing literature on demography and selection interpretation
SweepFinder2 robustness to bottlenecks, missing data and errors shown

comments.issue: The paper frames its importance around Harris et al. 2018 but omits the rebuttals by Garud et al. 2021 and Feder et al. 2021, giving a one-sided literature review.
comments.request: Cite Garud et al. 2021 and explain whether and why the paper disagrees.
comments.quote: If this paper is going to frame its importance around Harris et al.2018, then it is important to also cite Garud et al. 2021 and explain if this paper disagrees with the conclusions of Garud et al. 2021 and why.

comments.issue: The paper is not at odds with evidence that soft sweeps are common; both hard and soft sweeps could have been common.
comments.request: Acknowledge that both hard and soft sweeps are possible.
comments.quote: In fact, hard sweeps could have been common in the past and soft sweeps could have been common in contemporary populations. Thus, acknowledging that both can be a possibility is a fairer treatment of the literature.

comments.issue: SweepFinder2 can also detect soft sweeps, so calling the detected sweeps hard is unjustified.
comments.request: Justify how detected sweeps are classified as hard.
comments.quote: Thus, how can we conclude that these sweeps that the authors have detected are hard to begin with?

comments.issue: The prevalence of past soft sweeps cannot be assessed without a soft sweep scan.
comments.request: Run a soft sweep scan to establish how common soft sweeps were.
comments.quote: it is unclear how common soft sweeps were in the past without a scan to demonstrate it.

comments.issue: The motivation and conclusion of the SGV versus de novo analysis in Figure 6 are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the purpose of the SGV analysis.
comments.quote: Thus, I am not sure what the motivation or conclusion is for this analysis.

comments.issue: The admixture explanation is not compared with non-admixture factors such as recombination and de novo mutations that also reduce sweep signals.
comments.request: Compare the admixture scenario with the non-admixture case.
comments.quote: Admixture may be one important factor decreasing the signal of selective sweeps, but how does this scenario compare to the case of non-admixture, where other factors such as recombination and de novo mutations reduce the sweep signal.

comments.issue: Figure 2B shows post-admixed samples performing equally well at Q=0.01, contradicting the conclusion that pre-admixture sweeps cannot be detected.
comments.request: Explain the choice of Q values and reconcile the conclusion with Figure 2B.
comments.quote: if using a reasonable Q value of 0.01, then the postadmixed seem to do equally well if not outperform the admixed populations. Thus, I do not understand why the authors conclude that they cannot detect hard sweeps that originated pre-admixture.

comments.issue: The sweep age classification yields only four sweeps at ~30 ka, which seems insufficient to claim local sweeps are more susceptible.
comments.request: Justify the claim about local sweep susceptibility.
comments.quote: Why is this enough to suggest that local sweeps should be more susceptible to post-admixture signal degradation?

comments.issue: The poor power in steppe populations (only WGS) is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the poor power in the steppe populations.
comments.quote: The authors do not seem to explain the poor power in the steppe populations – only WGS.

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 4 do not distinguish admixed from pre-admixed populations.
comments.request: Delineate and group admixed and pre-admixed populations on the figures.
comments.quote: First, in Figures 2 and 4, it is difficult to keep track of which populations are admixed and which ones are pre-admixed. Could the authors delineate (and perhaps even group) the populations as such on their figures?

comments.issue: It is hard to know which populations to inspect for recent sweeps and how Figure 4A matches the axis of 4B.
comments.request: Clarify the population mapping and axis correspondence.
comments.quote: I cannot keep straight which populations I should look at for sweeps starting within the last 35Kyrs. How do I match Fig 4A with the x-axis of Fig. 4B?

comments.issue: Figure 4C sweep numbers cannot be matched to Figure 4A.
comments.request: Make sweep numbering consistent between panels.
comments.quote: Figure 4C, unclear how to match the sweep numbers with that of Fig 4A

comments.issue: Figure 5 panel C is referenced but missing.
comments.request: Add the missing panel C.
comments.quote: Figure 5: panel C is referenced but is missing.

comments.issue: The SweepFinder2 citation is missing.
comments.request: Cite DeGiorgio 2016 for SweepFinder2.
comments.quote: Cite DeGiorgio 2016 for SweepFinder2?

comments.issue: The statement about distortion of sweep signals should be explicitly tied to age classification.
comments.request: Clarify that the statement concerns classification of sweep age.
comments.quote: Clarify that the following statement is with regards to classification of the age of a sweep

reviews.assessment: Likes the rigorous and valuable study, but asks for clearer writing and figures and justification of simulation and demographic modelling choices.
strengths: rigorous and valuable for the community
uses forward simulations and analytical methods

comments.issue: The paper assumes detailed knowledge of human populations, limiting accessibility.
comments.request: Add background for readers unfamiliar with these populations.
comments.quote: Currently the paper is written assuming that one knows everything about human populations and that can be an impediment for researchers who are not familiar with these populations.

comments.issue: Text and figure legends are often unclear about what was done, and the manuscript lacks line numbers.
comments.request: Make the text and legends much clearer.
comments.quote: The text and figure legends need to be much clearer about what exactly was done. In the present state, it is sometimes very hard to understand what you exactly did.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether SLiM forward simulations used region-specific recombination rates.
comments.request: Use the specific recombination rates for the 57 sweep regions.
comments.quote: While performing the forward simulations in SLiM, did you account for the specific recombination rate in those regions of the 57 sweeps?

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not make the populations or their connection to Figure 2 understandable.
comments.request: Provide a more elaborate figure showing populations and demographic events.
comments.quote: Fig1 is nice but it’s really difficult to understand the actual populations and how they connect to Figure 2.

comments.issue: The diversity trough coincides with lower recombination, which seems opposite to sweep evidence.
comments.request: Explain how the trough supports a sweep rather than reduced recombination.
comments.quote: My reading of the Figure is that the trough in diversity coincides with the decrease in recombination rates, so how is that an evidence of a sweep? It seems exactly the opposite, in fact.

comments.issue: The assumption that selection pressure changes at the admixture event is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the change in selection pressure and add a figure showing where it is modelled.
comments.quote: Can you justify a change in selection pressure coincident with an admixture event a bit more? I’m a bit unsure about why that is.

comments.issue: The origin of the demographic history is not stated and appears to come from another manuscript.
comments.request: State clearly that the demographic history was taken from another study.
comments.quote: I believe you did not estimate this demographic history and are using it from another manuscript, right? If yes, please mention it here clearly. In general it was unclear how you obtained it.

comments.issue: The claim that MHC signals likely went unnoticed is too strong because no one examined those ancient populations.
comments.request: Soften the claim about going unnoticed.
comments.quote: I think that is a bit strong. Hasn’t it gone unnoticed because no one has looked at these ancient populations?

comments.issue: AMH is not defined.
comments.request: Define AMH.
comments.quote: Page 9, “AMH occupation” -> what is AMH?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the SGV versus de novo probabilities assume demographic equilibrium.
comments.request: State the demographic equilibrium caveat if applicable.
comments.quote: Are these calculated assuming demographic equilibrium? If yes, that caveat should be mentioned.

comments.issue: The information that 41 sweeps have s > 1% appears too late.
comments.request: Move this information to the beginning of the results.
comments.quote: I was wondering about this the entire paper. It would be much better if this information showed up right at the beginning of the results section.

reviews.assessment: Finds the question interesting but considers the study setup inconsistent and calls for sanity checks on demographic model specification.
strengths: interesting question about admixture and sweep detection

comments.issue: The study treats the three ancestral populations as un-admixed, although they were themselves mixtures, making the setup inconsistent.
comments.request: Justify or reconsider treating ancestral populations as discrete units.
comments.quote: Specifically, they consider the three ancestries that gave rise to modern Europeans, and imagine those to have persisted long enough for beneficial alleles to ascend from rare to fixation.

comments.issue: Given continuous mixing, hard sweeps may not be the right model for strongly beneficial alleles.
comments.request: Consider whether quasi-Mendelian adaptations are being missed.
comments.quote: given that mixing of divergent groups was the norm throughout human evolution, likely at rates higher than the time scale is takes for a rare mutation to reach fixation (~50,000 years?), are hard sweeps even the right model

comments.issue: Misspecification of the demographic model for ancestral populations could cause false positives, but no sanity checks address this.
comments.request: Run sanity checks and assess model fit at neutral sites.
comments.quote: Given that mis-specification of the demographic history is a huge issue in that regard, some sanity checks are in order.

comments.issue: The 56 non-MHC sweep signals are not described beyond higher Fst to Yoruba.
comments.request: Report where these sweeps are and whether they are plausible candidates.
comments.quote: it seems a weird omission that the authors don’t tell us about 56 of the 57 sweep signals not in the MHC, other than that they have higher Fst to Yoruba: where are they? are they plausible candidates etc?

comments.issue: The mutational-basis section omits literature on previously deleterious mutations becoming favoured and being indistinguishable from hard sweeps.
comments.request: Cite Orr & Betancourt 2001 and Teshima et al. 2006 and discuss this alternative.
comments.quote: the section on the mutational basis of sweeps is missing previous references about what happens when previously deleterious mutations become strongly favored, and how these are not distinguishable from hard sweeps

title: Admixture has obscured signals of historical hard sweeps in humans

study.system: humid tropical vertebrates; forest integrity and IUCN status

reviews.assessment: Well-written and statistically sound, but the novelty over existing degradation work is unclear and the index components are not disentangled.
strengths: very well written and statistically sound
interesting use of novel forest condition metrics

comments.issue: The importance of intact, high-integrity forests for biodiversity is already well known, so what the new metrics add is unclear.
comments.request: Outline more clearly what is novel about these findings.
comments.quote: I find the use of novel metrics of forest condition and how they relate to population trends very interesting, but I wonder what it adds to what we already know?

comments.issue: Composite indices may drive relationships through a single component, but component importance is not assessed.
comments.request: Analyse the relative importance of the index components, e.g. in an SI chapter.
comments.quote: the analysis leaves me wondering which component of the index explains the relationships found

comments.issue: The relative importance of stand height, tree cover and time since disturbance for the SCI-population trend relationships is unknown.
comments.request: Assess the relative importance of the SCI components.
comments.quote: Specifically, what is the relative importance of stand height, tree cover and time since disturbance for relationships between SCI and population trends?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the time since disturbance component accounts for natural disturbances.
comments.request: Clarify whether natural disturbances are included.
comments.quote: Does the time since disturbance component also take natural disturbances into account?

comments.issue: The relative importance of the human-pressure component within FSII is not analysed, making the role of pressure versus structure unclear.
comments.request: Analyse the relative contribution of the human-pressure component.
comments.quote: However, the relative importance of the index` human-pressure-component for relationships between FSII and population trends is not analyzed.

comments.issue: Relating SCI to potential structural complexity (Ehbrecht et al. 2021) could disentangle condition from pressure but is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss relating SCI to potential structural complexity.
comments.quote: Would relating the SCI to the potential structural complexity (actual structure/potential structure) help to further disentangle the roles of structural condition and human pressure?

reviews.assessment: High-value findings with sound methodology, but the FSII is dominated by the Human Footprint Index, confounding structure with pressure.
strengths: high-value findings for future discussions and target-setting
no further recommendations on the analytical front

comments.issue: The HFI weighting caps FSII at 3.6 for any HFI above 4, so the conclusion that structure and pressure both matter may actually reflect pressure alone.
comments.request: Add an HFI analysis to separate structure and pressure effects.
comments.quote: This means that the HFI strongly influences the scale of FSII, and the conclusion that structure AND pressure strongly influence the species’ conservation status could mean that it is mainly pressure that influences conservation status.

comments.issue: The conclusions are limited to forest species although structure and pressure may matter in all habitat types.
comments.request: Expand the conclusions to suggest considering structure and pressure for all habitat types.
comments.quote: could be expanded to be more daring and suggest that structure and pressure should be explored and considered when setting conservation targets for all habitat types, not just forests

comments.issue: The terms structural condition and structural integrity are confusing because both contain 'structure'.
comments.request: Use more descriptive terms such as 'structure' and 'pressure'.
comments.quote: I find the terms structural condition (structure) and structural integrity integrity (pressure) to be confusing when used in the text.

comments.issue: The correlation at line 46 between forest composition and extinction risk does not establish causation.
comments.request: Soften the causal interpretation.
comments.quote: There definitely is a correlation, but this may not be sufficient to conclude causation.

comments.issue: Figure 1 is abstract and hard to interpret, and log odds might work better on the y axis.
comments.request: Improve Figure 1 and consider swapping its order with Figure 2.
comments.quote: Would the figure be more understandable if log odds was on the y axis? Also, I find the figure to be strongly abstract and hard to interpret.

comments.issue: HFI is absent from Figure 1 even though it effectively weights the SCI within FSII.
comments.request: Add HFI to Figure 1 and the analysis.
comments.quote: I would like to see HFI added to this figure and analysis, as it can help interpret the differences seen between SCI and FSII.

comments.issue: It is unclear why the pattern at line 84 is considered inconsistent with expectations, since degradation and pressure may be indirect correlates.
comments.request: Clarify the expectation behind this statement.
comments.quote: It is not entirely clear why this is inconsistent with expectations.

comments.issue: The gradient description at line 87 is unclear and endemic versus non-endemic vertebrates could be simplified.
comments.request: Rephrase the gradient description more clearly.
comments.quote: I also feel this can be phrased to be more clear. E.g. endemic and non-endemic vertebrates could be simplified to simply vertebrates.

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: 'log osdds' in Figure 1 and CI unexplained at line 71.
comments.quote: Fig 1: “log osdds” → “log odds” Fig 1: Would the figure be more understandable if log odds was on the y axis?

reviews.assessment: Interesting and potentially advancing work, but range overlap independence and confounding of forest structure with recent forest loss could affect the core findings.
strengths: high conservation relevance to tropical forest conservation
potential advance using new forest integrity metrics
sensitivity analyses around mapping error and criterion B listings

comments.issue: Overlapping ranges across over 30,000 species cause repeat sampling, and residual spatial structure and IID assumptions are untested.
comments.request: Show that model residuals have no spatial structure and are IID.
comments.quote: However, it will be critical for the authors to show that model residuals do not have spatial structure, and that model residuals are IID.

comments.issue: Forest structure and integrity variables may be correlated with recent forest loss, so declines could be attributed to structure when forest loss is the cause.
comments.request: Separate the effects of recent forest loss from structure and integrity.
comments.quote: there is a substantial risk of concluding that species’ endangerment is caused by reductions in forest structure and/or integrity when the cause could at least be partially forest loss in recent decades

comments.issue: Recent forest loss (2000-2017) is included as a component of forest structure change, conflating degradation with land-use change.
comments.request: Explain SCI clearly or build it without recent forest loss.
comments.quote: It is questionable to include recent forest loss (2000-2017) as a component of forest structure change.

comments.issue: The spatial scale of the SCI and FSII indices (local versus landscape) is not clarified early.
comments.request: Clarify the scale of these indices as early as possible.
comments.quote: I suggest that you clarify as early as possible the scale of these indices.

comments.issue: IUCN reptile assessments are notoriously incomplete.
comments.request: Drop reptiles from the analysis or provide assurances that the data are sound.
comments.quote: The IUCN lists for reptiles are notoriously incomplete. I suggest dropping for analysis.

comments.issue: The modeling methods at L58 are described in only one sentence, leaving the sample unit and range overlap handling unclear.
comments.request: Describe the modeling framework and sample unit in more detail.
comments.quote: It would be useful to have slightly more in the way of modeling methods here than one sentence indicating that you used a “generalized linear modeling framework”.

comments.issue: Genuine changes in IUCN status (uplisting/downlisting) were not considered as a response variable.
comments.request: Consider examining genuine IUCN status changes, possibly via the static mapping approach.
comments.quote: A strong test is to determine whether areas of high forest integrity affect genuine changes in IUCN status (i.e., uplisting/downlisting).

comments.issue: The conservation rationale for testing integrity-by-cover interactions (land sharing versus sparing) is not explained in the introduction.
comments.request: Explain the conservation relevance of the interaction tests in the introduction.
comments.quote: you should make it clearer in the introduction why you did this (i.e., the conservation relevance)

comments.issue: The reason for the criterion B sensitivity analysis at L133 is not explained in the main text.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for the sensitivity analysis in the main text.
comments.quote: You should make it clearer in the main text why you did this.

comments.issue: Forest cover was treated as static rather than dynamic, even though recent loss rates may drive the patterns.
comments.request: Consider dynamic forest cover (lost or gained over 20 years) in the analysis.
comments.quote: I wonder why you did not consider forest cover as a dynamic variable in your analysis (i.e., how much forest cover has been lost or gained over the past 20 years)?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the negative interactions mentioned at L97 are three-way interactions, and readers must consult the SI.
comments.request: Clarify the interaction structure in the main text.
comments.quote: are these 3-way interactions? This should be clarified without needing the reader to flip to the Supplementary Materials.

comments.issue: The line of causation at L149 could be reversed, with species in intact forests inherently more sensitive and thus listed at higher risk.
comments.request: Consider and address the reverse causation possibility.
comments.quote: Is it possible that you have the line of causation the wrong way around here?

comments.issue: The climate change statement at L150 lacks original references on edge effects on microclimate and biodiversity.
comments.request: Cite original research on edge effects.
comments.quote: you could cite some original research showing negative effects of edges on tropical forest microclimate and biodiversity

comments.issue: The inference about re-establishing landscape connectivity at L189 is not supported by any connectivity data.
comments.request: Remove this inference leap.
comments.quote: You don’t present any information on connectivity in your paper, so I suggest that you not include this inference leap here.

comments.issue: The remote sensing data underlying SCI and FSII are not described in enough detail.
comments.request: Describe the remote sensing inputs to SCI and FSII in more detail.
comments.quote: Much more detail should be provided on the sorts of remote sensing data going into SCI and FSII.

comments.issue: It is not made clear that subsetting SCI to values above 2 removes the confounding effect of recent forest loss, nor is the rationale given.
comments.request: Make the SCI subsetting and its rationale explicit.
comments.quote: that should be made very clear, as well as the rationale for doing this (i.e., removing the potentially confounding effect of recent forest loss)

comments.issue: Covariate correlations in the models are not reported.
comments.request: Report covariate correlations at least in the appendices.
comments.quote: How correlated are the covariates in your models? Please report this in appendices at least.

comments.issue: Several line-level edits: break the long L31 sentence, terminology preference at L52, and punctuation at L. 65.
comments.quote: L52. This might be just me, but I prefer to use the term “endemic” to refer to a geographic location where a species is found

title: Humid tropical vertebrates are at lower risk of extinction and population decline in forests with higher structural integrity

study.system: Late Devonian actinopterygian fossil; phylogenetics and diversification

editor_summary: Editor asks to address the reviewers' criticisms and some editorial concerns before a final decision on the manuscript.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, publication-ready work on End-Devonian survivorship; the only pause concerns incomplete Carboniferous sampling and its caveats.
strengths: effectively ready for publication as is
broad implications for mass extinction studies

comments.issue: Incomplete Carboniferous sampling and excluded faunas may obscure higher Tournaisian diversification rates.
comments.request: Make the caveats about Carboniferous sampling and early Carboniferous diversification rates more explicit.
comments.quote: I do worry that exclusion of some faunas, such as the Tournaisian fishes of the Upper Witteberg of South Africa and some of the stranger faunal components of Visean/Serpukhovian faunas

reviews.assessment: Anatomical description is well-executed, but several claims need support and the figures and terminology require clarification.

comments.issue: 'Ornament' is a diagnostic feature but is not figured in the main manuscript.
comments.request: Figure the ornament and make the main-taxon figures more informative.
comments.quote: 'ornament' (presumably of dermal cranial elements? – this should be specified) is used as a diagnostic feature for the new taxon, but is not figured in the main ms.

comments.issue: The claim that the new taxon may be a juvenile lacks supporting detail on the relevant features.
comments.request: Detail which specific features support juvenile status.
comments.quote: The authors do indicate that the new taxon may be a juvenile; this should be supported by more detail on which specific features support this

comments.issue: Small body size could reflect juvenile status or selection for small size in early actinopts.
comments.request: Clarify whether small size is due to juvenile status or selection.
comments.quote: whether the quite small body size of the new taxon they describe is because it is a juvenile, or a reflection of selection for small body size in early actinopts

comments.issue: What counts as small, medium-sized and large body size is not defined.
comments.request: Define the body size categories.
comments.quote: a more specific indication re what the authors think is small vs. medium-sized vs. large body size should be included

comments.issue: Vague terms like 'multiple lineages' and 'a handful' are not quantified.
comments.request: State what number of lineages these terms denote.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to know what to the authors constitutes e.g. 'multiple lineages' vs. 'a handful' in terms of actual numbers

comments.issue: It is unclear how many Devonian lineages are based on fossils versus model predictions.
comments.request: Report how many lineages are fossil-based versus predicted.
comments.quote: How many of the lineages present in the Devonian are based on actual Devonian fossils vs. predictions based on their model?

comments.issue: The claim that the new taxon has uniquely unanticipated features is weakened by sporadic occurrences in other Devonian actinopts.
comments.request: Quantify how many features are unanticipated and what constitutes sporadic presence.
comments.quote: I was not completely convinced by the authors' assertion that the new taxon uniquely has a substantial list of features that are 'unanticipated' in a Devonian actinopt.

comments.issue: It is unclear which actinopterygian crown group members are shown as present in the late Devonian in Fig. 4D.
comments.request: Clarify the crown group members present in Fig. 4D.
comments.quote: Which members of the actinopt crown group were present in the late Devonian, as shown on Fig. 4D?

comments.issue: Fig. 4D shows the sarcopterygian total group going extinct before the end of the Devonian.
comments.request: Check and correct the sarcopterygian total group range in Fig. 4D.
comments.quote: On Fig. 4D the 'sarcopterygian total group' appears to go extinct before the end of the Devonian.

reviews.assessment: Important and methodologically solid, but the description is verbose and the treatment of Late Devonian extinction complexity and narrative structure need work.

comments.issue: The Abstract and Introduction present the consensus view at length before overturning it, instead of framing the new data as the departure.
comments.request: Restructure the Abstract and Introduction to start from the new data suggesting a different pattern.
comments.quote: the consensus view is presented as if it is preparing the reader for the content of the manuscript, and only later in those sections is that view shot-down as out-of-date

comments.issue: The descriptive section is too verbose for non-specialists, lacks comparative context, and dominates over the interpretation of character evolution.
comments.request: Omit uninformative details and add comparative detail on the most phylogenetically important features.
comments.quote: the description would be better if uninformative details (eg. "Maxillary teeth are arranged in a row along the ventral margin of the bone") were omitted, and more comparative detail provided on the phylogenetic importance of the features of greatest interest

comments.issue: The manuscript treats the end-Devonian extinction as a single event rather than part of a prolonged series.
comments.request: Clarify whether the totality or only the end-Devonian part of the event is considered and avoid simplifying it.
comments.quote: The end-Devonian event was a part of a prolonged series of events, and it is not clear if the manuscript is considering the totality of the Late Devonian event, or only the end-Devonian piece of it.

title: A Late Devonian actinopterygian suggests high lineage survivorship across the end-Devonian mass extinction

study.system: Indonesia's mangroves; spatial restoration prioritization and policy review

reviews.assessment: Useful, well-documented contribution that should be published, with minor text, figure and grammar suggestions.

comments.issue: The title promises 'risks' where the paper is really about challenges of failing targets.
comments.request: Rename to 'opportunities and challenges in achieving SDGs...'.
comments.quote: I wonder if the paper really does address risks, or rather challenges? The risks seem to be about failing to achieve the targets rather than risks more broadly defined.

comments.issue: Reference superscripts need reformatting and several line-level wording fixes are listed (Ln 118, 119, 148, 149, 340).
comments.quote: there are numerous instances of reference superscripts needing reformatting

comments.issue: Ln 66 does not make clear the statement is global rather than Indonesia-only.
comments.request: Insert 'global' at Ln 66.
comments.quote: Ln 66 - insert word ‘global’ here to make clear you are talking about world not Indonesia only

comments.issue: Comparing mangroves to 'upland forests' at Ln 73 is nonsensical.
comments.request: Use 'compared with terrestrial forests'.
comments.quote: Text does not make sense, since mangroves are not ‘upland’? why not just ‘compared with terrestrial forests’?

comments.issue: Figure 1 uses two different schemes for restoration priority without legend explanation.
comments.request: Explain how the schemes are combined in the legend.
comments.quote: two different schemes used in the same figure to refer to restoration priority

comments.issue: Line 128 should state that rehabilitation success refers to global experience.
comments.request: State that the rehabilitation reference is global.
comments.quote: worth stating here that you are referring to rehabilitation globally

comments.issue: Figure 2 is hard to interpret without panel headers.
comments.request: Add headers or labels above each of the four panels.
comments.quote: It would help the reader to give a little more guidance, for example by putting headers/labels above each of the four panels of the figure stating what they refer to

comments.issue: Heading at Ln 210 needs revision.
comments.request: Revise the Ln 210 heading.
comments.quote: Ln 210 - Implications for international environmental agendas

comments.issue: The NDC term is not written out fully in text or figures.
comments.request: Use 'Nationally Determined Contributions' throughout.
comments.quote: here and elsewhere, including in figures, the term should be Nationally Determined Contributions

comments.issue: The expert assessment process, including who and how many experts, is not described.
comments.request: Describe the expert assessment process and participants.
comments.quote: we need a little more information about the expert assessment process described here

comments.issue: How carbon scores influence potential scores, and why potential is out of 15 not 20, is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how carbon scores feed into potential scores.
comments.quote: It is not clear how these things align, or how you used the score given for carbon in S5 to influence the potential scores, which seem to be out of 15 not 20.

reviews.assessment: Significant advancement ready for publication after moving background text, explaining estimates and rerunning maps.
strengths: significant advancement in identifying restorable mangrove regions
fulfils a critical need in the mangrove conservation community

comments.issue: Historical policy and general introduction material sits in the results/discussion sections.
comments.request: Move lines 152-173 and 174-197 to the introduction.
comments.quote: Several portions of the results/discussion section should be moved to the introductory section, as they do not directly relate to the findings of this paper

comments.issue: How the 71 million benefited people estimate was reached is unexplained.
comments.request: Describe the derivation of the 71 million estimate.
comments.quote: The estimate of 71 million benefited people is repeated several times throughout the paper, but it is unclear how this estimate was reached, or if it comes from other literature.

comments.issue: Giri et al. baseline maps could be replaced by GMW maps for comparison.
comments.request: Rerun the models with GMW maps if time permits.
comments.quote: I recommend rerunning these models (if time permits) under GMW maps instead to compare results.

comments.issue: Figure 3 is background material and does not show this paper's results.
comments.request: Move Figure 3 to supplementary and highlight hotspot regions.
comments.quote: Figure 3 should be moved to supplemental figures, as it does not directly represents the results of this paper

comments.issue: The paper gives no path forward for the unreachable 70% of the restoration target.
comments.request: Suggest productive uses of the remaining resources.
comments.quote: consider including suggestions for how to harness the rest of the proposed national resources and energy for mangrove conservation productively

reviews.assessment: Exceptionally well written, but the scoring-based prioritization raises major concerns that require methodological updating.

comments.issue: The prioritization does not ensure adequate restoration of multiple species, community or habitat types.
comments.request: Incorporate representation targets or explain why not.
comments.quote: It is not clear to me how the prioritization would achieve adequate restoration of multiple mangrove species, community types, or habitat types.

comments.issue: A scoring system is used despite such systems being biologically ineffective and economically inefficient.
comments.request: Replace the scoring system with systematic conservation planning.
comments.quote: such scoring systems defy contemporary planning approaches, and have repeatedly been shown to identify priorities that are biologically ineffective and economically inefficient

comments.issue: Scoring systems fail to provide coverage of multiple features such as species, ecosystem types and bioregions.
comments.request: Ensure the prioritization covers multiple features.
comments.quote: scoring systems fail to identify prioritizations that provide adequate coverage (or restoration) of multiple different features (e.g. species, ecosystem types, and bioregions)

comments.issue: Score assignments are arbitrary, e.g. erosion = 1 versus climate event = 5 with no justification.
comments.request: Justify score differences or avoid arbitrary scoring.
comments.quote: an area with "erosion" was assigned a score of 1, and an area with a "climate event" classified was assigned a score of 5

comments.issue: Scoring involves hidden value judgments because no explicit measurable objectives are set.
comments.request: Set explicit and measurable objectives.
comments.quote: scoring systems involve hidden value judgments. This is because they do not involve setting explicit and measurable objectives

comments.issue: Modern systematic conservation planning tools and objectives are not used.
comments.request: Use Marxan, Zonation, ConsNet or prioritizr with SDG-derived objectives.
comments.quote: I would recommend using a modern systematic conservation planning approach to address these issues (such as using Marxan, Zonation, ConsNet, or prioritizr).

comments.issue: Uncertainty in expert judgments is not accounted for in the prioritization.
comments.request: Account for expert-judgment uncertainty, e.g. via ranges.
comments.quote: I could not determine how the prioritization accounted for uncertainty in expert judgments.

comments.issue: Line 30 appears to be missing a word.
comments.request: Fix 'Despite being 30% than the'.
comments.quote: I think "Despite being 30% than the" might be missing a word?

comments.issue: References at lines 40, 80, 67 and 130 contain a redundant 'ref.'.
comments.request: Remove the 'ref.' prefixes.
comments.quote: References contain a "ref." in addition to the number (e.g. "ref.2" instead of "2").

comments.issue: 'CO2eq' should be 'CO2' at lines 66 and 68.
comments.request: Correct to 'CO2'.
comments.quote: "CO2eq" should be "CO2" I think?

comments.issue: Base maps in Figure S3 may require attribution.
comments.request: Check and provide base map attribution if needed.
comments.quote: Base maps (i.e. the background of the figure showing labels and land masses) often require some form of attribution

reviews.assessment: Well-written and timely resource; asks for clarification of carbon accounting, terminology and policy details.
strengths: good resource for demonstrating SDG and climate targets

comments.issue: Whether soil carbon is included in emissions and carbon stock estimates is unclear.
comments.request: State at the outset whether soil carbon is included.
comments.quote: Please clarify if soil carbon is considered in the emissions and carbon stock estimates at the outset to give a better understanding of the full carbon mitigation potential.

comments.issue: 'Restoration' and 'rehabilitation' are used inconsistently and defined late.
comments.request: Define both terms early and use them consistently.
comments.quote: The definition and usage of terms for “restoration” and “rehabilitation” would also benefit from being integrated in the early part of the paper for clarity and consistency.

comments.issue: The range of SDGs directly and indirectly supported is not specified.
comments.request: Specify direct and indirect SDG contributions.
comments.quote: it might be useful to specify the range of SDGs that mangrove restorations contribute to both directly and indirectly

comments.issue: Whether avoided loss is included in the land-sector emission reduction is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify if avoided loss is included.
comments.quote: Does the “national land-sector emission reduction” also include avoided loss?

comments.issue: The Aichi Targets' replacement by the Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework is not noted.
comments.request: Note the forthcoming Post-2020 GBF at CBD COP15.
comments.quote: Indicate that the Aichi Targets will soon be replaced by the Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework targets and goals

comments.issue: A typo in the last purple box of the line 206 graph and missing frameworks.
comments.request: Fix the NDC typo and add the CBD framework and UN Decade of Ocean Science.
comments.quote: A typo was spotted on the graph in line 206 in the last purple box, it should be Nationally Determined Contributions.

comments.issue: The permanent Presidential moratorium may be missing from Table S1.
comments.request: Consider adding the moratorium to Table S1.
comments.quote: Should the Presidential moratorium of all new permits on primary forests and peatland be included in the Table S1 list?

comments.issue: SDG13 adaptation and resilience elements are not covered.
comments.request: Add resilience/adaptation contributions.
comments.quote: SDG13 is also inclusive of adaptation and resilience elements in addition to mitigation actions, recommend adding resilience/adaptation contributions here

comments.issue: The treatment of mangroves in Indonesia's NDC, mitigation versus adaptation, is imprecise.
comments.request: Clarify that mangroves are specified for adaptation, not mitigation.
comments.quote: Indonesia’s NDC doesn’t explicitly include mangroves in its mitigation activities(for avoided emissions or mangrove rehabilitation). However, mangroves are specified for adaptation benefits in coastal zone management and ecosystem restoration.

comments.issue: Overlap with the FCPF Emission Reduction program in East Kalimantan is not considered.
comments.request: Discuss potential overlap with the FCPF ER program.
comments.quote: Should there be any special consideration for overlap with the program area from the Forest Carbon Partnership Facility (FCPF) Emission Reduction (ER) program in East Kalimantan

title: Challenges and opportunities for achieving Sustainable Development Goals through restoration of Indonesia’s mangroves

study.system: synthetic human gut bacterial communities; fibers and constituent sugars

editor_summary: Editor asks for a deeper exploration of the underlying mechanisms, in particular to better interpret whether complexity is truly driving growth restriction in this system.

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastically supports publication of this rigorous and impressive study, with major comments only on interpretation and modeling details.
strengths: thoroughly carried out and rigorous analysis
important contribution to community dynamics rules

comments.issue: It is not evident how the molecular-structure-based carbohydrate complexity metric connects mechanistically to growth restriction.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism linking structural complexity to growth restriction.
comments.quote: I can see the rationale of their metric, which seems to be defined based on the complexity of the molecular structure. However, it is not entirely evident to see how the metric connects to growth restriction.

comments.issue: Results may reflect growth restriction generally rather than carbohydrate complexity, since positive interactions also increase without carbohydrates.
comments.request: Test and discuss whether points 2-3 apply to any growth-limiting nutrient, not specifically complex carbohydrates.
comments.quote: It appears that the authors’ analysis indeed points to the role of growth restriction, instead of the restriction by complex carbohydrates

comments.issue: Recent work using nutrient quality to control positive interactions, such as Wu et al. 2022, is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Wu et al. Nat Chem Biol 2022.
comments.quote: One example is Wu et al Nat Chem Biol 2022 (Modulation of microbial community dynamics by spatial partitioning), where nutrient quality was used to control the relative importance of positive interactions in a synthetic community of auxotrophs.

comments.issue: It is unclear why two model formulations are needed, and the interaction-free MCR model capturing robustness may negate the gLV interaction result.
comments.request: Explain the distinct roles and consistency of the gLV and MCR models.
comments.quote: Why are two model formulations needed to make two different points regarding the community dynamics.

comments.issue: The invasion result may simply reflect complex carbohydrates being suboptimal food for both residents and invaders.
comments.request: Rule out the naive interpretation by checking invader growth in different media.
comments.quote: a naïve interpretation is that complex carbohydrates are just suboptimal foods for everyone (resident or invader). I believe this naïve interpretation should be ruled out.

comments.issue: The responder and non-responder analysis is described cryptically and its contribution to the main points is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the responder analysis and its relevance.
comments.quote: The analysis of responders and non-responders is interesting, but the description was somewhat cryptic.

comments.issue: How positive and negative interactions are scored in the gLV model, and whether fractions use the best fit or an ensemble, is unclear.
comments.request: Explain interaction scoring and whether fractions come from best-fit or ensemble parameters.
comments.quote: While I understand the rationale of the gLV modeling and parameter fitting – how positive and negative interactions are scored should be more clearly explained.

comments.issue: The figure caption may contain typos, and strong and weak interactions seem to share a threshold.
comments.request: Check the caption and clarify the strong/weak interaction thresholds.
comments.quote: I suspect there’re some typos in the figure caption but not quite sure – the strong and weak interactions have the same interaction strength threshold?

comments.issue: There are quite a few typos throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: There are quite a few typos throughout the manuscript.
