reviews.assessment: Impressive experiments but the manuscript is hard to read and the interpretation is not always convincing, with results driven by a few fiber-degrading species.
strengths: very much appreciated the fiber versus constituent sugar comparison
impressive number of experiments and computational work

comments.issue: An alternative explanation is that only a few species break down the polymers while species growing on other substrates take over, in a media-specific way.
comments.request: Consider and rule out this alternative interpretation of Figures 1 and 2.
comments.quote: Very few can break down these complex polymers; species that grow on something else (whatever there is in the media that it is not a sugar) take over, but it seems very media-specific.

comments.issue: The role of the few fiber-degrading species is not tested by removing DP and EL or extending the dilution period.
comments.request: Test communities without DP and EL and with longer dilution periods.
comments.quote: What happens when DP and EL are excluded from the community? What happens if a longer dilution period is imposed?

comments.issue: The absence of cross-feeding is unsurprising because the most abundant species on xylan and laminarin also grow without sugars and drive the results.
comments.request: Assess how much of the result is guided by species that grow without sugars.
comments.quote: It doesn’t seem very surprising since basically the most abundant species in the fibers xylan and laminarin are those that grow even in the absence of sugars.

comments.issue: Percentages of interaction signs hide the strength of interactions across media.
comments.request: Report average absolute interaction coefficients with standard errors.
comments.quote: I would be curious to see the average of the absolute value of interaction coefficients and their std error to compare the different conditions

comments.issue: It is unclear whether interaction counts in panel D are standardized by the number of species in a niche.
comments.request: Standardize or clarify the number of interactions per niche.
comments.quote: Is the number of interactions standardized by the number of species in a specific niche?

comments.issue: Reproducibility appears to depend on the number of responders, which could change the interpretation of the results.
comments.request: Test whether more responders reduce reproducibility, including in fibers.
comments.quote: Reproducibility seems to depend on the number of responders. If more responders were present, would we see less reproducibility even in the fibers?

comments.issue: The number of fiber responders among invaders and their ability to grow without carbohydrates are not reported.
comments.request: Report invader growth on fibers and without carbohydrates.
comments.quote: Invasion experiment: how many responders to fibers there were among the invaders? How many could growth in the absence of carbohydrates?

comments.issue: The mortality term in the MacArthur resource model equation appears wrongly placed inside the parentheses and may be confounded with the dilution rate.
comments.request: Correct the mortality term and confirm which version was simulated.
comments.quote: In Fig 3C equation describing the model and in supplement: I don’t think that the mortality term should be in the parentheses.

comments.issue: The number of species at steady state is bounded by the supplied resources, so the model's appropriateness depends on how many resources were included.
comments.request: State how many resources were modeled and justify the model's use.
comments.quote: In this model, at steady state the number of species in the community is bounded by the number of resources that are supplied, right? How many resources were being included in your modeling?

comments.issue: The carbon sources used are not described in the main text, and Table 3 does not give compound names and complexity indices.
comments.request: Describe the carbon sources and their complexity indices before the results.
comments.quote: I would appreciate a thorough description of the carbon sources used in the experiments in the main text, before results are presented.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the four bars per species in Figure 1B represent concentrations or compound types.
comments.request: Clarify what the four bars in Figure 1B represent.
comments.quote: it is not clear from Fig. 1B whether the four bars for each species refer to the concentrations tested (as the figure caption states) or the type of compound on which the species grew

comments.issue: The meaning of the four conditions per sugar in Figure 3B is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the four conditions in Figure 3B.
comments.quote: Same problem in Fig. 3B. Why 4 conditions for each sugar? Concentrations?

comments.issue: Panel B lacks the OD in media without carbohydrates.
comments.request: Add the OD without carbohydrates to panel B.
comments.quote: I encourage the authors to add to panel B the OD in the media without carbohydrates.

comments.issue: The second introduction paragraph omits recent work on resource effects on community assembly.
comments.request: Cite Pacheco et al., Dal Bello et al. 2021 and Pollak et al. 2021.
comments.quote: The second paragraph of the introduction is under-cited.

comments.issue: Four line-level copy edits: capitalization, a typo, a superfluous word and a preposition.
comments.quote: Line 95: used TO decipher

comments.issue: It is unclear which aspect of competitive interactions is highlighted at Line 113.
comments.request: Clarify and rephrase the sentence at Line 113.
comments.quote: I wasn’t sure which aspect of competitive interactions you were trying to highlight

comments.issue: The three fibers are not listed and readers would benefit from background on the fibers and their monomers.
comments.request: List the fibers and provide background on them and their monomers.
comments.quote: Might be nice to list the three fibers that you are considering.

comments.issue: Whether species can grow on other carbon sources in the media is not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention growth on other carbon sources at Line 169.
comments.quote: Can these species grow in this media on some other carbon source? Probably worthwhile to mention this in the text.

comments.issue: The 'In sum' sentence at Line 239 summarizes the previous paragraph and is confusing.
comments.request: Reposition or rewrite the summary sentence.
comments.quote: I found this sentence confusing because the summary was about the previous paragraph.

comments.issue: The phylogenetic trees in Figure 1 panels A and B differ, confounding comparisons.
comments.request: Use the same tree in panels A and B.
comments.quote: the phylogenetic tree of the 10 species in panel A and B should be the same, in order to avoid confounding

comments.issue: Panel A does not show species names with initials.
comments.request: Add species names with initials to panel A.
comments.quote: in panel A I would add the species names with their initials

comments.issue: The legend colours in panel D differ slightly from the colours used.
comments.request: Match the legend colours to panel D.
comments.quote: the colors in the legend of panel D are slightly different from the colors actually used in panel D

comments.issue: The phylogenetic tree in Figure 4 panel A is not readable.
comments.request: Make the tree in Figure 4A readable.
comments.quote: the phylogenetic tree in panel A is not readable

comments.issue: Figure S2 panel D axis labels lack absolute abundance.
comments.request: Add absolute abundance to the axis labels.
comments.quote: panel D: add absolute abundance on the axis’ labels

comments.issue: The white bands in Figure S11 are not defined.
comments.request: Define which species the white colour represents.
comments.quote: what species is the white color? There are white bands that are not defined.

title: Carbohydrate complexity limits microbial growth and reduces the sensitivity of human gut communities to perturbations

study.system: vertebrates; method for error-corrected protein convergence rates

reviews.assessment: Ingenious and rigorous method likely to be widely adopted, but the statistical power and genotype-phenotype claims need clarification and better support.
strengths: convincing analyses of robustness to false positives
avoids problems of previous convergence measures

comments.issue: The method's statistical power and false-negative properties are barely addressed.
comments.request: Add a simulation study of the convergent substitutions needed to detect significance.
comments.quote: While there is a lot of focus on reducing false positives, I could find very little on reducing false negatives, or the statistical properties of omega_C overall.

comments.issue: No guidelines are given for deciding when omega_C is significant, and usage differs between the top 1% and neutral simulations.
comments.request: Clarify the recommended significance criteria for omega_C.
comments.quote: But this just begs the question: how does a researcher know when omega_C is significant? I saw nothing that provided guidelines for this.

comments.issue: Convergent proteins are not shown to be linked to any particular phenotype despite genotype-phenotype claims.
comments.request: Support or remove the genotype-phenotype association claims.
comments.quote: While I am convinced the method found truly convergent proteins, I am not convinced that they were linked to any particular phenotype, or could be shown to be.

comments.issue: How convergence without a pre-specified phenotype would identify overlooked phenotypes is unclear, especially on internal branches.
comments.request: Explain how the method leads to increased understanding of genotype-phenotype associations.
comments.quote: But which ones? How would we identify these phenotypes?

comments.issue: Key references for the genotype-phenotype approach, PhyloG2P and phyloGWAS, are missing.
comments.request: Cite Smith et al. 2020 TREE and Pease et al. 2016 PLoS Biology.
comments.quote: I think there are two key references missing: Smith et al. (2020, TREE) on the “PhyloG2P” approach, and Pease et al. (2016, PLoS Biology) on the “phyloGWAS” approach.

comments.issue: The paralog convergence search is barely described: whether only cross-species paralogs or all pairs are compared is unclear.
comments.request: Describe how paralogs were compared.
comments.quote: While I do see how a search for convergent evolution between gene duplicates would be very useful, I had a bit of trouble figuring out how this was actually done (there was very little description).

comments.issue: Requiring two duplication events to separate paralogs is not biologically justified; one duplication plus speciation seems more plausible.
comments.request: Justify or revise the DD requirement.
comments.quote: Similarly, why require two duplication events to separate paralogs (”DD”)? It seems biologically more plausible that duplicates separated by only one duplication event (plus one speciation) would be more likely to converge

comments.issue: It is unclear how convergent substitutions are assigned to gene trees with missing genes or losses.
comments.request: Explain how branches are compared fairly in trees with missing genes.
comments.quote: Also, how do you assign convergent substitutions to gene trees with missing genes?

comments.issue: Neutral evolution is misused as meaning no selection or constraint.
comments.request: Use the correct definition: absence of positive selection.
comments.quote: Neutral evolution does not mean “no selection” or “no constraint”—it means the absence of positive selection

comments.issue: The neutral expectation of omega_C being 1 is conflated with omega=1, and the simulations actually used omega=0.5.
comments.request: Distinguish the two uses of neutral expectations.
comments.quote: the neutral expectation of omega_C *is* 1, because it is a ratio of convergent substitutions of each type. But this expectation does not require that omega=1, even though this is what is said (line 159).

comments.issue: The Theoretically Neutral line in Figure 1D for dN_C and dS_C is unexplained, and the Bustamante citation misrepresents the McDonald-Kreitman test.
comments.request: Explain why these metrics would have an expectation of 1 and correct the citation.
comments.quote: Similarly, it is not clear to me what the line for “Theoretically Neutral” is pointing to in the panels of Figure 1D with dN_C and dS_C in them. Why should these two metrics have an expectation of 1?

comments.issue: dN and dS are distances, not rates.
comments.request: Correct the terminology.
comments.quote: -dN and dS are not rates, they are distances.

comments.issue: The purpose of the high-confidence convergent lineages section is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what this section demonstrates.
comments.quote: I am not sure what the section on “Extracting a high-confidence set of convergent lineages” (starting line 287) shows, exactly.

comments.issue: The relationship to the metric of Burskaia et al. 2020 is not discussed.
comments.request: Comment on the relationship to Burskaia et al. 2020.
comments.quote: Could the authors comment on the relationship of the metrics they use to the one proposed in Burskaia et al. (2020, GBE)?

comments.issue: Figure S3C shows sensitivity of omega_C to codon model misspecification.
comments.request: Mention this sensitivity in the main text.
comments.quote: Figure S3C seems to show quite a bit of sensitivity of omega_c to misspecification of the codon model. Maybe this should be mentioned in the main text?

comments.issue: Whether the expression changes are adaptive is unclear; testis expression overlap may accumulate neutrally.
comments.request: Address the neutral accumulation alternative for expression changes.
comments.quote: It was not clear to me that the expression changes detected are adaptive. What if there is a lot of overlap with testis expression because this pattern accumulates at high (neutral) rates?

comments.issue: Figure 3 is not informative; more detail on expression patterns and less on protein structures would help.
comments.request: Revise Figure 3 accordingly.
comments.quote: Figure 3 was not very informative. Maybe some more detail on the expression method/patterns, and less on protein structures?

comments.issue: No formula is given for the number of independent branches in trees of different sizes.
comments.request: Provide a formula for the branch count.
comments.quote: Is there a formula for number of independent branches in different sized trees? I’m just wondering whether there’s an easy way to get the number laid out starting on line 446

comments.issue: The branch-and-bound algorithm is actually a greedy algorithm.
comments.request: Correct the algorithm description.
comments.quote: The “branch-and-bound” algorithm described seems to be in fact be a greedy algorithm.

reviews.assessment: Robust, well-implemented method likely to become standard, but thresholds, gene-duplication handling and exploratory analyses need justification.
strengths: robust and performs well in tests
notably well organized code, easy to install
multiple example datasets and well organized wiki

comments.issue: The approach has low power with few convergent substitutions; aggregation approaches such as Marcovitz et al. 2019 and INSIGHT are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss limitations and possible extensions such as aggregation by functional class.
comments.quote: this approach can have low power when there are only one or a few convergent substitutions in a protein.

comments.issue: It is unclear how well the exploratory analysis without candidate genes works, and the results relate more to gene duplication than genotype-phenotype links.
comments.request: Add analyses demonstrating the exploratory potential.
comments.quote: However, it is not particularly clear from the results the authors' present how well this works.

comments.issue: The distribution of excess-convergence counts across species pairs is unknown, and the herbivore analysis count of 352 exceeds the average.
comments.request: Analyse whether species pairs with known convergent phenotypes have higher counts.
comments.quote: Do species pairs with well-known convergent phenotypes tend to have higher-than-average numbers of genes with excess convergence?

comments.issue: A genome-wide unbiased screen for 3- or 4-way convergence in mammals is missing.
comments.request: Run an unbiased screen for higher-order convergence in the mammalian tree.
comments.quote: a genome-wide, unbiased screen for say 3- or 4-way convergence in the mammalian tree (something that has not really been possible before CSUBST) could be extremely informative

comments.issue: Many CSUBST options are unclear and undocumented.
comments.request: Add a readme describing the submodules and the options users are likely to change.
comments.quote: the program has a huge number of options that are not clear how to set or use, many of which I presume the user will rarely, if ever, want to modify.

comments.issue: omega_C and observed thresholds are chosen without justification, vary between searches, and key examples do not pass them.
comments.request: Explain and justify the thresholds and consider permutation-based P-values.
comments.quote: However, there is little/no discussion in the paper of why these thresholds were chosen (unless I missed it, in which case I apologize). I think this really needs to be clearly explained and justified.

comments.issue: How large gene families with speciation and duplication events are analysed is confusing; SS branch pairs may actually involve paralogs.
comments.request: Add a supplemental diagram and a filter for MRCA speciation events.
comments.quote: I am a little bit confused about how large gene families with speciation and duplication events are being analyzed.

comments.issue: Convergence between paralog copies is classified as SS, and what an SD event means is unclear.
comments.request: Classify branch pairs by whether their common ancestor is a speciation or duplication event.
comments.quote: It would perhaps be more intuitive to classify branch pairs by whether their common ancestor is a speciation or a duplication event

title: Detecting macroevolutionary genotype–phenotype associations using error-corrected rates of protein convergence

study.system: global terrestrial and coastal ecosystems; NCP mapping

editor_summary: Editor notes Reviewers 1 and 3 are positive while Reviewer 2 is skeptical of the approach and validity of ecosystem service estimates, especially pollination.

reviews.assessment: Ground-breaking global mapping with profound policy implications; asks for terminology, dryland and presentation improvements.
strengths: ground-breaking study mapping global NCP hotspots
important findings with profound global policy implications
well-prepared supplemental material documenting enormous data sources and analyses

comments.issue: 'Critical natural assets' can be confused with the established but different concept of Critical Natural Capital.
comments.request: Consider 'natural asset hotspots' or another more accurate term.
comments.quote: “Critical natural assets” can be easily confused with “Critical Natural Capital”.

comments.issue: The term NCP hardly differs from ecosystem services, and it is odd to call InVEST outputs NCP.
comments.request: Reconsider the NCP terminology and its use with InVEST outputs.
comments.quote: But it’s a bit odd that you’re using InVEST on the one hand, and call its outputs NCP, on the other hand.

comments.issue: Most global drylands are labelled non-critical natural assets even though drylands cover 41% of land and host 35% of the population.
comments.request: Make explicit comments on the status of drylands.
comments.quote: it’s worrisome to see that most global drylands are mapped as “non-critical natural assets”

comments.issue: The main text lacks organization, and the term critical natural assets is defined repeatedly.
comments.request: Add headings and define the term once.
comments.quote: The main text lacks clear organization or structure. Adding a few headings would be helpful.

comments.issue: Spatial resolution, pixel size and key scale-sensitivity findings are only in the supplement.
comments.request: Move this important information into the main text.
comments.quote: some important information, such as the spatial resolution of data/pixel size and key findings of scale sensitivity, should be included in the main text

comments.issue: It is unclear whether critical natural assets include nature reserves and protected areas.
comments.request: State clearly in the main text whether reserves and protected areas are included.
comments.quote: it should be stated clearly in the main text if the critical natural assets include nature reserves and protected areas

comments.issue: It is ambiguous whether each of the 12 NCP must reach 90% or whether the 90% applies to the lumped total.
comments.request: Clarify how the 90% target is applied across the 12 NCP.
comments.quote: does this mean each of the 12 NCP is to be maintained at/above the level of 90%?

reviews.assessment: Policy need acknowledged, but the NCP models are simple land-cover reclassifications whose estimates are hardly credible for priorities and beneficiaries.
strengths: understands the policy need for such an analysis ahead of the Global Biodiversity Framework

comments.issue: Global mapping of NCP with simple land-cover proxies is of doubtful validity and needs expert assessment.
comments.request: Have experts in ecosystem service modelling evaluate the NCP models.
comments.quote: I suspect that it does not make sense to map these NCP globally using simple proxies, mostly based on global land-cover maps.

comments.issue: Pollination cannot be modelled from natural habitat within 2 km alone; pesticides, landscape features and management are ignored.
comments.request: Incorporate the missing drivers or acknowledge the model's limitations.
comments.quote: I can say with absolute confidence that calculating the amount of ‘’natural habitat” in a radius of 2km around a cropland pixel is in no way sufficient to model pollination service.

comments.issue: Because the models are land-cover reclassifications, the mapped priorities, beneficiary numbers and provision extents are hardly credible.
comments.request: Reassess the credibility of these model outputs.
comments.quote: This makes them hardly credible both in terms of spatial location of priorities (Fig 1c and Fig 3), the amount of people benefiting (Fig 2)

comments.issue: Log-linear interpolation of species ranges lacks ecological foundation and empirical evidence for sufficiency.
comments.request: Justify this approach or use empirically based representation targets such as Red List Criteria.
comments.quote: You used the log-linear interpolation of species ranges that many before you have used, but that has no ecological foundation behind it.

comments.issue: The choice of 90% provision directly determines the 30% and 44% area requirements, but the implications of this threshold are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss implications of the 90% choice and what information would define a target level.
comments.quote: This, however, affects your conclusion about the 30% or 44% area requirement, because you choose to focus on the 90% provision.

comments.issue: Font types and sizes change across the supplementary materials as if text were copy-pasted unchecked.
comments.request: Standardize fonts in the supplementary materials.
comments.quote: In various parts of the supplementary materials the fonts type and size changes, as if the text was copy-pasted and not checked.

comments.issue: The text at lines 1022-1040 belongs under data limitations.
comments.request: Move this text under data limitations.
comments.quote: The text at lines 1022-1040 would be best placed under data limitations

comments.issue: The overlap statistics at lines 130-135 are unclear, including the meaning of endemic and whether any overlap counts.
comments.request: Define the endemic unit and the overlap counting rule.
comments.quote: These statistics on overlap are not clear. E.g. endemic, are you referring to country endemics? Or other administrative or biogeographic unit?

comments.issue: Line 930 gives the wrong definition of the minimum set problem, describing maximizations without constraints.
comments.request: Correct the definition of the minimum set problem.
comments.quote: This is not the definition of a minimum set problem. The correct definition (in a spatial planning context) is the set of grid cells that (if protected) satisfies all conservation targets at a minimum cost (in this case area).

comments.issue: Extended data figures are repeated at small and full page sizes, legends are missing, and colour codes need explanation.
comments.request: Remove duplicate figures and add complete legends.
comments.quote: The extended data figures seem to be repeated, first in small size then in full page. In addition, the legend is missing

reviews.assessment: Most comprehensive global NCP mapping to date, well written with documented methods; only a couple of minor comments.
strengths: most comprehensive global approach for mapping NCP areas
well written and easy to follow
methods clearly documented and sensitivity appropriately tested

comments.issue: The main text lacks discussion of valuing nature beyond its usefulness to humans, although this is discussed in the SI.
comments.request: Move this discussion, or part of it, to the main text.
comments.quote: I felt there was a lack of discussion about how nature can be valued for reasons beyond it’s ‘usefulness’ to humans

comments.issue: O'Connor et al. 2021 found little overlap between biodiversity and cultural/regulating NCP priorities in Europe, contradicting this manuscript's findings.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy and whether global aggregation masks regional differences.
comments.quote: in that study the authors find little overlap between priority areas for biodiversity and cultural and regulating NCP. This is somewhat at odds with the findings in this manuscript.

comments.issue: Typo 'percnt' in panel b of Figure 1.
comments.quote: There is a typo in panel b of figure 1 ‘percnt’ should be ‘percent’.

title: Mapping the planet’s critical natural assets

study.system: urban greenspaces; global soil biodiversity and multifunctionality survey

editor_summary: Editor asks to avoid 'global' and novelty claims, rethink multifunctionality framing since several variables are only proxies, and split Results and Discussion with subheadings and more interpretation.

reviews.assessment: Appreciative of the global survey and clear analyses; only minor concerns about hypothesis precision and rare-taxa classification.
strengths: global field survey across six continents
appropriate statistical analyses and clear figures

comments.issue: The first hypothesis is imprecise: whether 'number' means abundance, richness or both is unclear, and composition is omitted.
comments.request: Clarify the hypothesis wording and specify expectations for different soil organism groups.
comments.quote: First, it is not clear to me if the authors here mean abundance, richness or both.

comments.issue: A high percentage of fungal classes and invertebrates are classified as rare taxa, which seems questionable for groups such as annelids.
comments.request: Explain the rare-taxa classification in Tables S3 and S4.
comments.quote: I would expect annelids as common taxa given that earthworms represent the major soil animal biomass in most terrestrial temperate ecosystems.

reviews.assessment: Impressive, valuable global survey with no major concerns beyond the overlong, hard-to-follow results and discussion.
strengths: rather complete data set on soil biodiversity and functioning
great number of study sites across the globe
well written and easy to read

comments.issue: The results/discussion section is too long and dense, making the reader lose track, and lacks clear specific interpretation of findings.
comments.request: Restructure and shorten the results and discussion, adding clear interpretation.
comments.quote: in the current version I lost track in places and I also missed a clear specific interpretation of the findings in the discussion section

comments.issue: The meaning of 'provided with original soil amendments' is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what is meant by original soil amendments.
comments.quote: L164: What do you mean by "provided with original soil amendments"

comments.issue: The claim of generally positive above- and belowground biodiversity relationships needs a reference and is not universally true.
comments.request: Split the long line, add a reference, and acknowledge non-positive relationships.
comments.quote: On a global scale relationships between above- and belowground biodiversity are not necessarily positive (De Deyn and van der Putten, 2005, TREE).

comments.issue: The claim that mowing disturbs positive BEF relationships conflicts with evidence that such disturbances can stimulate plant contributions.
comments.request: Reconsider the mowing claim and cite Bardgett and Wardle 2003.
comments.quote: why would mowing disturb positive BEF relationships? I think these kind of disturbances (also grazing) do not per se reduce the contribution of plants to ecosystem services

comments.issue: Labile carbon is used as a carbon sequestration measure although the two are not equivalent, and sandy soils complicate MAOM as a storage measure.
comments.request: Justify or reconsider the carbon sequestration indicators, possibly using total C.
comments.quote: why is labile carbon content a measure for carbon sequestration? Are labile C and MAOM related to each other?

comments.issue: What the multifunctionality thresholds represent is not fully clear.
comments.request: Explain carefully what the thresholds mean, e.g. 25% of maximum capacity.
comments.quote: it does not become fully clear what the thresholds really are. This needs to be explained more carefully.

comments.issue: Multiple testing correction for the many relationships tested is not stated.
comments.request: State whether multiple testing was corrected for, including in Fig. 6.
comments.quote: also in Fig. 6 it seems many relationships were tested and only few are shown – did you take multiple testing into account?

comments.issue: The results and discussion lacks broader context and specific implications, and includes too many detailed descriptions.
comments.request: Add context and implications, present results per research question, and reduce detailed descriptions.
comments.quote: I think this section could be improved if one more "digestion" step is made and the results and discussion are presented in line with the research question.

reviews.assessment: Highly critical: hypotheses are ungrounded, novelty unclear, sample numbers low, and the multifunctionality and C-sequestration metrics are conceptually flawed.

comments.issue: Grounded hypotheses are lacking despite existing BEF knowledge; it is unclear why urban systems should differ.
comments.request: Develop hypotheses from theoretical and empirical understanding rather than stating that knowledge is lacking.
comments.quote: the lack of grounded hypotheses are disturbing given the knowledge we have on BEF and ecosystem multifunctionality

comments.issue: The novelty is unclear because results align with what is known from other systems.
comments.request: Articulate the novelty relative to existing BEF studies.
comments.quote: Further the novelty is unclear. The results align what is known from other systems.

comments.issue: 56 samples, of which 27 were sequenced, is a very low number for a global survey.
comments.request: Tone down the worldwide and global claims.
comments.quote: In any case, both 27 and 56 is a very low number for a global survey. Please tone down the "worldwide" and "global" aspects.

comments.issue: Carbon pools such as labile C and mineral-associated C are not functions or C sequestration, and ARG control is a gene pool, not a function.
comments.request: Stop treating pools as functions and be more critical about sequestration proxies.
comments.quote: These properties are not functions. Pools are not functions unless changes in pools are measured.

comments.issue: The merit of the multifunctionality metric is debated and which functions to include is unsettled and varies across studies.
comments.request: Justify the selected functions and consider how other choices would change the outcome.
comments.quote: The merit and relevance of this metric is actually rather debated. Moreover, it has not been settled which functions that are relevant to included when determining multifunctionality

comments.issue: How climatic variables were collected is not described.
comments.request: Describe the collection of climatic variables.
comments.quote: It is not described how climatic variables were collected.

comments.issue: Gene annotation is not described in enough detail, and database annotations are often incorrect.
comments.request: Describe the gene annotation procedure in more detail.
comments.quote: Please describe in more detail how the genes were annotated. Note that many genes are incorrectly annotated in databases.

comments.issue: Studies on agricultural soils, coastal areas and managed grasslands are not mentioned.
comments.request: Cite relevant studies such as Garland et al. Nature Food.
comments.quote: There are studies on agricultural soils, see Garland et al Nature Food for a recent example. There are also studies on highly impacted coastal areas as well as managed grasslands.

comments.issue: Symbiotic plants such as AM, ECM and diazotrophs are not considered.
comments.request: Consider plants with symbiotic relationships in the analyses or discussion.
comments.quote: What about plants that have symbiotic relationships? For example AM, ECM and diazotrophs?

comments.issue: The proposed explanation seems implausible for forested systems, whose management is unlikely to differ so radically.
comments.request: Reconsider the explanation for forested systems.
comments.quote: Is this explanation plausible also for the forested systems; sounds unlikely that management of those systems would be so radically different from other managed systems.

comments.issue: The point at l.256 is already shown in other systems, so the novelty is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the novelty of this result.
comments.quote: This is unclear. It is shown in other systems so what is the novelty here.

comments.issue: The choice of a 7.5 cm soil depth and the accuracy of its measurement are not explained.
comments.request: Justify the soil depth and how it was measured.
comments.quote: Why was a soil depth of 7.5 cm chosen? And could soil depth be measured with that accuracy?

comments.issue: Few soil properties were measured and total C, SOC or SOM are missing despite being strong determinants of soil biodiversity.
comments.request: Add more soil properties, at minimum total C, SOC or SOM.
comments.quote: At a minimum total C, SOC or SOM should be added since C/N is typically a very strong determinant of soil biodiversity and composition of soil biota

comments.issue: The soil texture analysis lacks an original reference.
comments.request: Cite an original reference for the soil texture analysis.
comments.quote: Was there something special with the soil texture analyses. Otherwise, I would recommend citing an original reference here.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether reads shorter than 50 bp were used, which would be rather small.
comments.request: State the read length filtering threshold.
comments.quote: Were reads <50 bp used? Unclear, and if so that is rather small.

comments.issue: Grammatical errors throughout, including the non-existent term 'soil biotas'.
comments.request: Check the English and correct 'soil biotas' to 'soil biota'.
comments.quote: Please check the English, there are grammatical errors throughout the text. For example, the term soil biotas do not exist, should be soil biota.

title: Soil biodiversity supports the delivery of multiple ecosystem functions in urban greenspaces

study.system: soil microbes; 200-day temperature-regime incubations

editor_summary: Work of considerable potential interest but with substantial concerns that must be addressed; revision invited although the current version cannot be accepted.

reviews.assessment: Clear, novel and valuable study, but statistical treatment of replication and several interpretations raise serious doubts.

comments.issue: Site and technical replicates are not independent, yet means of all samples are compared across treatments.
comments.request: Re-analyse with mixed-effects models accounting for non-independence.
comments.quote: Those are not independent (the site replicates are not independent from each other and the technical replicates are not independent from each other either).

comments.issue: Three assay temperatures are analysed separately, adding little beyond a single temperature.
comments.request: Derive Q10 or Arrhenius parameters from the assays.
comments.quote: I don’t really understand the value of having 3 essay temperatures if you analyse those separately.

comments.issue: Figure 2 relationships look U-shaped and may need polynomial rather than linear fits.
comments.request: Test second-degree polynomial fits.
comments.quote: It really looks like for all essays temperatures, Rmass decreases from temperature variations of 0 to 5 and then increases from temperature variations 5 to 10.

comments.issue: When microbial community composition was measured, start or end of incubation, is unclear.
comments.request: State the timing of community composition measurement.
comments.quote: it is not possible to determine whether microbial community composition were analysed at the beginning or the end of the incubation period, or both

comments.issue: Species turnover cannot be inferred without initial community composition.
comments.request: Rephrase to microbial community composition instead of turnover.
comments.quote: how can you know which species have turned over if you don’t know the initial composition?

comments.issue: Glucose addition is a strong selective pressure that could confound temperature effects.
comments.request: Acknowledge the glucose selection caveat in the discussion.
comments.quote: the addition of a single substrate could be a very strong selective pressure (in addition to temperature regimes) on microbial communities

comments.issue: Studies showing adaptation can enhance the climate feedback are not mentioned.
comments.request: Add this perspective, e.g. Karhu et al. 2014.
comments.quote: some studies (including some cited in your manuscript, example Karhu et al 2014) find that adaptation may lead to an enhancing effect, therefore strengthening the feedback overt time

comments.issue: Crowther et al. 2016 is misattributed as being about adaptation.
comments.request: Correct or remove the citation.
comments.quote: citation 12 (Crowther et al 2016) is not about adaptation and does not say what you attribute to it

comments.issue: Recent MMRT thermal-adaptation papers are missing.
comments.request: Cite Arcus et al. 2016, Alster 2020/2022 and Moinet 2021.
comments.quote: Generally speaking, you are missing a few nice recent papers with an interesting perspective on thermal adaptation using MMRT

comments.issue: One versus two incubation experiments is described inconsistently at L103.
comments.request: Make the number of incubations consistent.
comments.quote: you mention here 1 incubation experiment, but then describe two incubations experiment in figure 1 and L131

comments.issue: Regular glucose addition is not clear from the methods section.
comments.request: State glucose addition clearly in the methods.
comments.quote: good to see that you added glucose regularly. This is really not clear when reading the method section.

comments.issue: The sentence at L160 is unclear.
comments.request: Use the suggested rewording about temperature variation.
comments.quote: the sentence is unclear; I suggest: “suggests that shifts in temperature variation is more likely to shape the adaptation of respiration than shifts in mean temperature”.

comments.issue: The Table 1 description is wrong: Mantel r for bacteria is similar in MT and VT.
comments.request: Correct the description of the Mantel results.
comments.quote: Most importantly, The Mantel r value is basically the same for bacteria in MT and VT, in table 1, so I don’t think the statement is true here.

reviews.assessment: Well-written study with well-described methods, but hypotheses and a results mismatch need fixing.

comments.issue: The hypotheses referred to at line 100 are not clearly detailed in the introduction.
comments.request: State the hypotheses clearly in the introduction.
comments.quote: the hypotheses should be more clearly detailed in the introduction because it is not fully clear the hypotheses that the authors are referring to in line 100

comments.issue: Table 1/Figure S1 contradict the results described in lines 184-188.
comments.request: Resolve the mismatch between text and figures.
comments.quote: there is a mismatch between the results shown in Table 1 and Figure S1 and described in lines 184-188

comments.issue: Figure S1 panel order differs from the rest of the article.
comments.request: Order mean temperature before temperature variation.
comments.quote: I recommend that authors maintain in Figure S1 the order follow in the rest of the article (i.e., first the results of changed mean temperature and then those of temperature variation).

comments.issue: Line 112 uses 2d instead of 48h.
comments.request: Change 2d to 48h.
comments.quote: Line 112: Change 2d for 48h to be consistent with Figure 1 and the rest of the article.

comments.issue: ANOVA summaries behind Figures 2 and 3 are not available.
comments.request: Add supplementary ANOVA tables with estimates and p values.
comments.quote: The article would acknowledge the inclusion of some supplementary tables showing the summary of the ANOVA analyses that led to the results of Figure 2 and 3 so that the readers could know the real estimates and p values.

comments.issue: Figure 3 caption does not describe the figure because Rmass is not shown.
comments.request: Rewrite the Figure 3 caption.
comments.quote: Figure 3 caption title (lines 169-170) is not properly describing the figure because Rmass is not directly shown on it.

comments.issue: Wrong preposition at line 226.
comments.request: Replace 'of Rmass' with 'on Rmass'.
comments.quote: Line 226: Replace of Rmass by on Rmass as it seems that Rmass is the one causing the effects instead of “receiving” them.

comments.issue: Arrow widths in the figure at lines 237-238 are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Make arrow width differences clearer.
comments.quote: The different arrow widths are difficult to distinguish; could you change the figure so that the differences on the arrow width are clearer?

comments.issue: Line 281 refers to a nonexistent Figure 6a.
comments.request: Correct the figure reference.
comments.quote: Line 281: There is no Figure 6a, what figure are you referring to?

comments.issue: Figure S2 colour-dose correspondence is impossible to follow.
comments.request: Make line and error-bar colours match the glucose doses.
comments.quote: It is impossible to know what colour correspond to what glucose dose because the lines are in a colour corresponding to one of the doses

comments.issue: Reference 20 misspells Blagodatskaya.
comments.request: Correct the reference author name.
comments.quote: Reference number 20 has a spelling mistake. The first author of that reference is Blagodatskaya, E.

comments.issue: Replicate number per sampling plot is not stated.
comments.request: Report replicates per sampling plot.
comments.quote: Lines 515-517: How many replicates did you collect for each sampling plot?

comments.issue: Sample storage time at 4C before incubation is not reported.
comments.request: Report storage duration before incubation.
comments.quote: I wonder how long where the samples stored at 4ºC between sampling and the incubation experiment as it could influence soil microbial community.

comments.issue: TC, TN and DOC methods and the fumigant used are not described in detail.
comments.request: Describe these methods and the fumigation agent.
comments.quote: The methods used to determine total carbon and nitrogen content and DOC should be described in more detail than just mentioning the device you use for measured them.

comments.issue: The lines 535-542 explanation is misleading about the methodology.
comments.request: Add information to clarify the methodology here.
comments.quote: You did a good description of the experiment in Figure 1 caption and lines 130-142, include some extra information here to clarify the methodology.

comments.issue: Line 579 uses an abbreviated method name.
comments.request: Use 'chloroform-fumigation extraction method'.
comments.quote: Line 579: Replace the fumigation method with the chloroform-fumigation extraction method.

comments.issue: Storage between incubation and analyses is not described.
comments.request: Report storage conditions and duration.
comments.quote: Were the samples stored between the end of the incubation and these analyses? In what conditions? For how long?

comments.issue: Line 662 implies only SEM analyses used R.
comments.request: Clarify that all analyses were conducted in R.
comments.quote: Line 662: All the analyses were conducted in R not only the SEM ones, right? If so, clarify this point.

comments.issue: Data needed to reproduce the analyses are not available.
comments.request: Make the data available or modify the statement.
comments.quote: the data needed to reproduce your analyses are not available either in the main text or in the supplementary

comments.issue: H.Y. is not in the author list at line 681.
comments.request: Correct the initials, likely H.C.
comments.quote: Line 681: H.Y. is not included in the author list. Do you mean H.C.?

comments.issue: J.L., B.L. and C.F. are not mentioned in the contributions section.
comments.request: Include all authors in the contributions.
comments.quote: I believe that you should specify that all authors include J.L., B.L., and C.F. as they are not mentioned anywhere else in the authors contribution section.

reviews.assessment: Important empirical dataset, but the mechanistic explanation of enzyme parameters and the ratio-based analysis need rethinking.
strengths: compelling design varying versus mean temperatures

comments.issue: Vmax changes are interpreted as adaptive responses although Vmax depends on enzyme amount.
comments.request: Reconcile the Vmax interpretation with enzyme biomass.
comments.quote: The issue here of course is that Vmax is dependent on the amount of enzyme present.

comments.issue: The unexpected lack of Rmass response under mean temperature regimes is never explained against biochemical theory.
comments.request: Discuss the lack of Rmass response under mean temperature.
comments.quote: At the moment, you present no discussion in light of that theory that explains this lack of Rmass response under the mean temperature regimes imposed.

comments.issue: 'Substrate binding' and 'enzyme affinity' are used as opposites though synonymous.
comments.request: Define how these terms are used.
comments.quote: your use of terms such as “substrate binding” and “enzyme affinity” is confusing because they often seemed to be presented as opposite, when in fact we would normally see them as synonymous

comments.issue: Analysing Rmass as a derived ratio obscures hypothesis testing.
comments.request: Re-analyse with biomass as a covariate.
comments.quote: you divide respiration by biomass and then do the analysis on this derived response

comments.issue: When assays were conducted relative to glucose addition and incubation end is unclear.
comments.request: State the assay timing clearly.
comments.quote: But it was unclear when you conducted your assays. Was it at a single point immediately at the end of the 200-d incubation? You need to state this.

comments.issue: No explanation is given for why constant warming did not reduce Rmass, contrary to expectations.
comments.request: Explain the lack of response to constant warming.
comments.quote: you do not address why your constant temperature regime incubations show no response, contrary to the results of so many others in soil

comments.issue: How laboratory versus soil replicates were handled in models is not stated.
comments.request: State and justify how the 336 assays were handled.
comments.quote: You state you had 336 assays, but these include 3 laboratory replicates as opposed to soil replicates, so how were they handled.

reviews.assessment: Interesting experiment, but timescale, temperature-variation definition and heterotrophic-only scope need clarification.
strengths: detailed assays across six temperature regimes

comments.issue: The timescale over which the results apply is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss applicability to longer or shorter timescales.
comments.quote: My main critique is that the authors haven’t elaborated on the timescale of these changes. Can the results be applied to longer/shorter timescales?

comments.issue: What 'variation in temperature' means in magnitude is unclear.
comments.request: Define how high or low the temperature variation is.
comments.quote: the authors need to clarify what they mean by variation in temperature. How high or how low?

comments.issue: Only heterotrophic respiration is measured, yet conclusions are linked to soil respiration and ESMs.
comments.request: Acknowledge the heterotrophic-only caveat.
comments.quote: this work is only evaluating heterotrophic respiration (brought about by microbes) but soil respiration includes both autotrophic and heterotrophic respiration

comments.issue: Jian et al. 2022 is not used to frame the discussion.
comments.request: Use Jian et al. 2022 in framing the discussion.
comments.quote: I would also recommend that the authors look at Jian et al. 2022 https://www-nature-com.ezproxy.callutheran.edu/articles/s41467-022-29391-5 to frame some of these discussions.

comments.issue: The sequencing work adds no extra dimension to the manuscript.
comments.request: Drop the sequencing or present it in more depth.
comments.quote: The sequencing work is not adding any extra dimension to the manuscript.

comments.issue: Sequence accession numbers and analysis code are not provided.
comments.request: Deposit sequences publicly and provide analysis code.
comments.quote: the authors need to provide accession number to the sequence data (and host it on a public database). Please also provide codes for data analysis.

comments.issue: 'Changes in temperature variation' at line 27 reads awkwardly.
comments.request: Reword the phrase.
comments.quote: changes in temperature variation reads weird. Variation means change, so change in temperature change?

comments.issue: The meaning of temperature variation at line 32 is undefined.
comments.request: Define temperature variation.
comments.quote: 32: what do the authors mean by temperature variation?

comments.issue: Sample number used in the SEM at line 41 is not stated.
comments.request: Report the SEM sample size.
comments.quote: 41: how many samples were used in SEM?

comments.issue: Which microbial community at line 55 is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify the microbial community.
comments.quote: 55: which microbial community?

comments.issue: The lines 57-59 sentence is unclear and its 150 Pg C baseline is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence and the overestimation baseline.
comments.quote: this sentence is unclear and weirdly placed. Will be estimated? Or has the no adaptation scenario already over estimated soil carbon loss.

comments.issue: The range and timescale of temperature variation at lines 67-84 are not bounded.
comments.request: Define whether variation is daily or monthly.
comments.quote: what is the range of this temperature variation? Are the authors suggesting daily changes? Monthly?

comments.issue: 'Pattern of temperature variation' and stationary conditions at lines 86-92 are undefined.
comments.request: Define these terms and conditions.
comments.quote: what is meant by pattern of temperature variation? And is it related to stationary and non-stationary conditions? What are these conditions?

comments.issue: Lines 142-144 belong in the methods, not results.
comments.request: Move lines 142-144 to the methods.
comments.quote: Line 142-144: Part of methods. Remove from Results.

comments.issue: What Rmass represents and how many values it yields at line 146 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain Rmass and the number of data points.
comments.quote: So is Rmass the difference in respiration between mean and varied temperature? If yes, does this mean there are 6 Rmass numbers to be reported?

comments.issue: The timescale issue at line 149 and its effect on extrapolation are unaddressed.
comments.request: Discuss whether results change with timescale.
comments.quote: again, what is this timescale and why? Will the results change if the timescale changes?

comments.issue: The main takeaway at lines 156-159 is not highlighted.
comments.request: Make it its own paragraph.
comments.quote: This is the main takeaway of the paper. I recommend highlighting this as it’s own paragraph starting with these lines.

comments.issue: SEM sample size at line 195 is not given.
comments.request: Report how many samples were included in the SEM.
comments.quote: Line 195: How many samples were included in the SEM?

comments.issue: The 'mid-long-term' timescale at line 536 is undefined.
comments.request: Define the timescale and highlight it in the introduction.
comments.quote: Please elaborate about the ‘mid-long-term’ timescale. This needs to be highlighted in the intro

comments.issue: Whether microbial biomass was measured per replicate or per soil type is unclear.
comments.request: State the biomass measurement unit.
comments.quote: Was the soil microbial biomass estimated for each replicate (each jar) or each soil type, and then applied to the respective jars?

comments.issue: Whether the line 606 analysis covered all 336 samples is unclear.
comments.request: State the sample number.
comments.quote: Line 606: Was this done for all 336 samples?

comments.issue: Codes and sequence data files with accession numbers are missing.
comments.request: Provide codes and deposited sequence data.
comments.quote: please provide codes and sequence data files. For any sequence work, it is imperative that sequences be deposited in a public database and provide accession number.

comments.issue: Microbial strategists are not defined.
comments.request: Define microbial strategists in the introduction.
comments.quote: Define the microbial strategists in the introduction.

comments.issue: NMDS results and PERMANOVA values are not reported.
comments.request: Show NMDS results and PERMANOVA values and driving variables.
comments.quote: Can the authors show the NMDS results and report PERMANOVA values? I did not find them in the main text or supplement.

title: Temperature fluctuation promotes the thermal adaptation of soil microbial respiration

study.system: deciduous forests; leaf phenology and net CO2 assimilation datasets

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but substantial concerns must be addressed; the manuscript cannot be accepted but a revised version is invited.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic but reservations remain about indicator validity, inconsistent method definitions and confounding by climate.
strengths: use of both in situ and remote sensing phenology data

comments.issue: Anet is not a direct indicator of leaf longevity and the carbon sink saturation threshold is unknown.
comments.request: Use a direct indicator of leaf longevity or temper the sink-saturation interpretation.
comments.quote: the growing season net CO2 assimilation (Anet) is not a direct indicator for leaf longevity, and we also do not know the actual saturation threshold of carbon sink

comments.issue: Advanced EOS is ascribed to accelerated carbon sink saturation without controlling for climate.
comments.request: Include climatic controls before attributing advanced EOS to sink saturation.
comments.quote: it might be unfair to simply ascribe the advanced EOS to the accelerated carbon sink saturation, with the absence of climatic controls

comments.issue: Mixing two phenophases each for leaf-out and senescence may introduce uncertainty into Figures 1 and 2.
comments.request: Clarify and justify the phenophase mixtures.
comments.quote: The authors used a mixture of two phenophases for leaf-out (e.g., first or 50% visible leaf stalks) and leaf senescence (e.g., 50% leaf coloring or fallen), respectively.

comments.issue: APAR is not directly measured, and fAPAR was arbitrarily set to 1.0.
comments.request: Justify or correct the fAPAR assignment at lines 204-207.
comments.quote: The absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (APAR) is not a direct measure from the datasets of WATCH-WFDEI and WorldClim2. The authors arbitrarily assigned the value of fAPAR to 1.0

comments.issue: The growing season is defined inconsistently across photosynthesis estimations.
comments.request: Use one consistent growing season definition.
comments.quote: The idea of growing season is not consistently defined throughout the estimation of photosynthesis

comments.issue: Key steps from Zani et al. are omitted when the work is repeatedly mentioned.
comments.request: Present the Zani et al. steps more clearly in the methods.
comments.quote: The authors have mentioned the work of Zani et al., for many times and omitted some key steps

comments.issue: The relative magnitude of the Anet-EOS relationship at decadal versus interannual scales is not compared, leaving the timing of acclimation relief unclear.
comments.request: Compare the magnitudes across scales and clarify how quickly relief becomes visible.
comments.quote: they are encouraged to compare the relative magnitude of such relationship between decadal and interannual scale

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the perfect linear relationships in Figures 1 and 2 are concept diagrams or real observations.
comments.request: State whether Figures 1 and 2 are conceptual or empirical.
comments.quote: These are concept diagrams or derived from actual observations?

comments.issue: Anet and EOS are not independent and both are affected by previous climate, so only co-variation is shown.
comments.request: Incorporate previous temperature and precipitation into the LMMs.
comments.quote: the calculation of Anet might be not independent to EOS, see lines: 205-207. Moreover, both Anet and EOS are affected by previous climate, e.g., temperature and precipitation. The authors should also incorporate these factors in LMMs.

reviews.assessment: New and noble question with clear methods, but the model-based conclusion needs observational backing and several methodological details.
strengths: new and noble question and hypothesis

comments.issue: The conclusion relies on modeled photosynthesis and is not validated against observational data.
comments.request: Back up the conclusion with eddy covariance and FACE data.
comments.quote: I think their conclusion should be backed up by observational data, such as data from eddy covariance tower networks and Free-Air CO2 Enrichment Experiments.

comments.issue: Many methodological details are missing.
comments.request: Provide the missing methodological details.
comments.quote: In the meantime, a lot of methodological details are missed.

comments.issue: The described EOS-SOS anomaly relationship at L101 seems to indicate earlier EOS when SOS is early.
comments.request: Clarify the direction of the EOS-SOS anomaly relationship.
comments.quote: L101: Am I missing something? There is a positive relationship between EOS and anomalies in SOS, meaning earlier EOS when SOS is early.

comments.issue: Data cleaning is not described and no map shows the distribution and density of the data.
comments.request: Add data cleaning sentences and a distribution map in the supporting materials.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to add one or two sentences about “data cleaning”, and a map showing geographical distributions and densities of the data in the supporting materials.

comments.issue: A parenthesis at the end of the sentence at L202 appears to be a typo.
comments.request: Fix the parenthesis typo at L202.
comments.quote: L202: A parenthesis at the end of the sentence seems a typo.

title: Acclimation of phenology relieves leaf longevity constraints in deciduous forests

study.system: forest litter decomposition; 194 European plots, three experiments

editor_summary: Referees disliked the Gordian knot title (and titles cannot include punctuation); Referee 2 wants spatial autocorrelation addressed and limitations discussed (plot randomness, full decomposition process).

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive and well-replicated study with excellent data, but the artificial substrates, title and some clarity points need fixing.
strengths: well-replicated with broad macroclimate and vegetation coverage
followed decomposition to the same mass loss across sites

comments.issue: The negligible micro-environment effect is questionable because artificial substrates were used to assess it.
comments.request: Reassess the micro-environment conclusion using real leaf litter.
comments.quote: The influence of the decomposition micro-environment is found to be negligible, but this result is questionable because artificial substrates (paper and wood sticks) were used to assess this factor.

comments.issue: The title alludes to cutting a Gordian knot rather than stating the main finding.
comments.request: State the main finding in the title.
comments.quote: I recommend that the authors clearly state this finding in their title, instead of an allusion to cutting a Gordian knot, which this study does not do.

comments.issue: The Summary does not explain how the study addresses the critique that within-site variability is collapsed, overestimating climate influence.
comments.request: Clarify in the Summary how the study addresses this issue.
comments.quote: clarify in the Summary how their study addresses the issue about ‘collapsing within-site variability into single mean values which overestimate climate influence’

comments.issue: The intractable-problem framing is not useful because the dominant factor reflects study scale and site combination.
comments.quote: Whichever factor appears most influential overall in a given study reflects the scale of the study and the particular combination of sites.

comments.issue: Figure 5 SEM is the most critical contribution but is not clear enough.
comments.request: Label the boxes with Decomposability, Decomposition environment and Realistic decomposition.
comments.quote: The SEM in Figure 5 is the most critical contribution of the study and needs to be clearer.

comments.issue: Several line-level insertions/clarifications suggested for lines 77, 78, 81, 88, 96, 99 and 100.
comments.request: Add the suggested clarifications to these lines.
comments.quote: Line 78 also consequences of climate-related species shifts

comments.issue: Lines 154-159 contain too much, and long-term adaptation and microclimate need better explanation.
comments.request: Split and clarify this sentence.
comments.quote: There is too much in this sentence – if ‘long-term adaptation’ and microclimate aspects are central to the point being made, they need to be better explained.

comments.issue: Line-level edits at lines 178, 185, 193, 214 and 216 (wording, remove both 'differents', verb tenses).
comments.request: Make these line-level corrections.
comments.quote: Line 185 state more clearly the relationship between LAI and decomposition

comments.issue: Results from paper and wood sticks do not justify claiming that standard litters across sites give misleading results.
comments.request: Separate standard-litter and artificial-substrate issues and temper the claim.
comments.quote: So I don’t think your results from paper and wood sticks justify a suggestion that comparing standard litters across sites gives misleading results.

comments.issue: More information about the wood sticks is needed.
comments.request: Describe the wood sticks in more detail.
comments.quote: Line 364 we need more information about the wood sticks.

reviews.assessment: Impressive design and novel results, but SEM spatial autocorrelation, confounding, non-random plots and early-stage focus raise significant concerns.

comments.issue: PiecewiseSEM cannot fully account for spatial autocorrelation, which may bias results.
comments.request: Account for spatial autocorrelation in the SEM.
comments.quote: I am not fully convinced of the SEM results from PiecewiseSEM since it can not fully account for spatial autocorrelation, which might bias the results.

comments.issue: Only the early decomposition stage (40% loss) was studied, which cannot represent the whole process.
comments.request: Discuss the limitation of focusing on early-stage decomposition.
comments.quote: The experiments only focused on the early stage of decomposition (40% loss) and can not represent the whole decomposition process.

comments.issue: The statistics section is confusing, mixing mixed-effect models and SEM, and interactions are absent from the SEM.
comments.request: Rewrite the statistics section and incorporate interactions into the SEM.
comments.quote: The statistic part needs a rewrite to make it clearer. For example, putting mixed effect model and SEM together is confusing.

comments.issue: The absence of a direct index of the local decomposer community weakens the study.
comments.request: Include a direct decomposer community index.
comments.quote: lack direct index of local decomposer community lowers the significance of this study.

comments.issue: The zero effect of standard litter on realistic decomposition is unexplained and only speculated, and different sampling times add uncertainty.
comments.request: Explain the zero effect and calculate k values for the plots.
comments.quote: It is hard to understand why standard litter decomposition had no effect (0) on realistic decomposition. The explanation in the ms is speculated and makes one of the three complementary experiments useless.

comments.issue: Litter characteristics and macroclimate are confounded, with multicollinearity driven by plant composition.
comments.request: Address the confounding and multicollinearity between litter PC1 and macroclimate.
comments.quote: It seems like litter characteristics and macroclimate are confounded. Plant composition is highly dependent on macroclimate.

comments.issue: FunDivEUROPE plots are not randomly selected and the tree diversity gradient is not modelled.
comments.request: Assess whether non-random plot selection affects results and include the diversity gradient.
comments.quote: Plots in FunDivEUROPE are not randomly selected. They are selected to test the tree diversity/composition effect. Would this affect the results?

comments.issue: Whether the dominant macroclimate role holds with tropical forests included is unknown.
comments.request: Add tropical forest data or discuss this limitation.
comments.quote: I am also interested in whether the dominant role of macroclimate will become more pronounced or weaker if the tropical forests data are included.

comments.issue: The challenge at lines 13-14 is not specified.
comments.request: Clarify what the challenge is.
comments.quote: Line 13-14 what is this challenge, please clarify.

comments.issue: The climate-centred view is used at line 30 without introduction.
comments.request: Introduce the climate-centred view before using it.
comments.quote: Line 30 the climate centred view has not been introduced

comments.issue: The sentence at line 38 about uncertainty and implications needs rewriting.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: Line 38 uncertainty has important implications? Please rewrite

comments.issue: Soil C and N were not included as soil characteristics in the PCA.
comments.request: Include soil C and N in the PCA.
comments.quote: Line 107 why not also included soil C and N as the soil characteristics in the PCA, similar to litter characteristics

comments.issue: The causal use of because at lines 154-159 is unjustified.
comments.request: Remove or correct the causal connective.
comments.quote: Line 154-159 Why use “because”? there is no causal relationship between these two sentences,

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the three experiments ran at the same time.
comments.request: State the timing of the three experiments.
comments.quote: Line 350-376 did these three experiments conduct at the same time?

comments.issue: Multiple sampling and k values would better represent decomposition rates.
comments.request: Use multiple sampling and calculate k values.
comments.quote: Line 421-423 use multiple sampling and calculate k should be better to represent the decomposition rate

comments.issue: Temperature is not considered in the model, although aridity only represents water availability.
comments.request: Consider including temperature in the model.
comments.quote: Line 503 aridity index is generally used to represent water availability. What about temperature, why not also consider the temperature in the model?

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation at line 511 is not considered.
comments.request: Consider spatial autocorrelation.
comments.quote: Line 511 spatial autocorrelation need to be considered

comments.issue: The species composition per plot at line 515 is unclear.
comments.request: State the species composition of each plot.
comments.quote: Line 515 what is the specie composition here.

comments.issue: Removing non-significant terms to minimize AIC is not appropriate model selection.
comments.request: Use model selection tools such as random forest or dredge.
comments.quote: Line 518 why remove non-significant terms to reach lowest AIC? You should used model selection packages such as random forest or dredge

comments.issue: The region interaction at lines 519-522 is not statistically correct given many possible causes of regional differences.
comments.request: Clarify and justify the interaction term.
comments.quote: Line 519-522 There are many reasons that could cause the differences among regions (such as different soil properties). why added the interaction? It is not statistically correct.

comments.issue: Mixed model and SEM steps are presented together and the order is unclear.
comments.request: Separate the mixed model and SEM procedures and state which comes first.
comments.quote: Line 524 please separate mixed model process and SEM process. Putting them together is confusing. Which is the first step? mixed effect model or SEM?

reviews.assessment: Questions the direct/indirect framing and the novelty, and cannot see how the study cuts the Gordian knot it sets up.

comments.issue: Dividing climate effects into direct and indirect is conceptually wrong because climate is an integrative expression.
comments.request: Reconsider the direct/indirect framing of climate effects.
comments.quote: I can’t agree with the idea to divide the effects into direct and indirect. Both macroclimate and microclimate are the integrative expression of temperature, precipitation, radiation and others.

comments.issue: The title is attractive but not specific to the most novel observation.
comments.request: Use a title displaying the most novel observation.
comments.quote: However, I prefer a specific one which displayed the most novel observation.

comments.issue: The challenges at lines 13-14 are unspecified.
comments.request: Specify the challenges, possibly climate change effects.
comments.quote: Line 13-14, what challenges? How about the “climate change effects”?

comments.issue: The European study area is limited with respect to climate change.
comments.request: Discuss the limited spatial scale.
comments.quote: I know the field work is not easy, but the scale area of European is limited with climate change.

comments.issue: The indirect control observation is not novel; no study neglected local plant and decomposer effects.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution beyond the indirect control claim.
comments.quote: this is not a novel observation. No study has neglected the so called indirect control of “local plant and decomposer”.

comments.issue: The Summary paragraph should be more specific.
comments.request: Make the Summary paragraph more specific.
comments.quote: In the whole, I suggest the “Summary paragraph” should be more specific.

comments.issue: Local factors at line 37 are undefined.
comments.request: Define local factors.
comments.quote: Line 37, how to define “local factors”?

comments.issue: The apples-with-oranges critique ignores that contributions of imperfect observations still matter.
comments.request: Acknowledge the contributions despite imperfect designs.
comments.quote: I agree with the uncertainty, but we also consider the contributions of these observations.

comments.issue: The Gordian knot framing is confusing because decomposition environment and decomposer are closely related and decomposers are not considered.
comments.request: Address the decomposer community in the framing and analysis.
comments.quote: I can’t fully understand the “Gordian knot” because decomposition environment is closely related to decomposer. I have not seen the authors considered decomposer in the description.

comments.issue: Continental European scale and six regions cannot resolve climate control; reasons for site selection are missing.
comments.request: Explain the choice of study regions.
comments.quote: Only “a continental scale for European forest ecosystems” and “six regions” can’t resolve the climate control. I want to know more about the reasons in choosing the study regions.

comments.issue: Paper sheets and wood sticks may have different responses than leaf litter.
comments.request: Justify the choice of artificial substrates.
comments.quote: Line 86, why use “paper sheets and wood sticks”? Different substrate may have different responses.

comments.issue: Why macroclimate had no significant influence despite strong climatic differences is not explained.
comments.request: Explain this result.
comments.quote: Line 152-153, “macroclimate had no significant influence despite the pronounced climatic differences among regions at the scale of Europe8”, why?

comments.issue: The results and discussion section reports too many statistics and too few mechanisms.
comments.request: Add mechanisms and reduce statistical detail.
comments.quote: there are too many statistical results in the description, maybe some more mechanisms should be better.

comments.issue: Results and discussion are mixed, making the main idea hard to follow.
comments.request: Separate results and discussion.
comments.quote: Due to the mixed writing in results and discussion, I can’t make clear what are results and what are discussions. I can not follow the main idea in this way. I suggest to separate them

comments.issue: The study provides no new information and the stated conclusions are insufficient.
comments.request: Strengthen the novel contribution and conclusions.
comments.quote: I can not get new information from the whole study.

comments.issue: Why decomposition was compared at 40-50% mass loss rather than at the same time is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the mass-loss-based comparison.
comments.quote: I can not understand why "within each region reached 40-50% mass loss"? why not check the decomposition in the same time?

comments.issue: The choice of 30 x 30 m spatial scale is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the definition of the 30 x 30 m spatial scale.
comments.quote: line 450, "Definition of spatial scales", why "30 x 30 m"?

title: Resolving the intricate role of climate in litter decomposition

study.system: released pheasants; spatial memory and home range tracking

editor_summary: Editor flags statistical reporting and reproducibility issues, weak framing and predictions, unacknowledged alternatives, and doubts about small sample size and idiosyncratic sex differences.

reviews.assessment: Elegant and rare free-ranging experiment, but framed against the wrong gap with response variables that do not capture home range formation.
strengths: very elegant experiment with a rare free-ranging component
comprehensive chain from cognitive tests to space use to predation

comments.issue: The experiment is framed against the wrong knowledge gap, with weak hypotheses and predictions and mostly result explanation rather than discussion.
comments.request: Reframe the study around suitable hypotheses, predictions and state-of-the-art knowledge.
comments.quote: This to me means that the output of the experiments have been put to demonstrate ‘the wrong’ knowledge gap

comments.issue: Central recent work on the link between space use and memory is missing from the theoretical framing.
comments.request: Use Merkle et al., Schlägel et al. and Avgar et al. to frame the background.
comments.quote: Some central, recent work contributing to the establishment of the link between space use and memory is indeed not used to frame the theoretical background of the study

comments.issue: Two-day kernel UDs are dynamically explored units of space rather than established home ranges, so the response variables do not measure home range formation.
comments.request: Reformulate the terminology and add spatial-explicit analyses of overlap and revisits.
comments.quote: Kernel UDs computed on subsequent intervals of 2 days are possibly ‘units of space used and explored’, rather than a restricted, established and familiar area

comments.issue: Development rate may be an artifact of the cumulative computation of kernel UDs.
comments.request: Run a sensitivity analysis to discard this possibility.
comments.quote: a sensitivity analysis should be run to discard this possibility

comments.issue: How 'eventual stable' home ranges were assessed and whether early-predated birds were discarded is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify stability assessment and comparability between survivors and early-predated birds.
comments.quote: How was this stability addressed? How is this metric comparable between individuals survived for the entire length of the experiment (120 days) and others predated early on?

comments.issue: The claim that larger home ranges mean better fitness is overturned by the results and not supported by the cited references.
comments.request: Revise this claim and its literature justification.
comments.quote: I found the statement that large home ranges correspond to better fitness particularly critical.

comments.issue: Resource distribution in the release landscape is unknown and not accounted for in the space-use analyses.
comments.request: Reconstruct resource or habitat patch distribution and incorporate it.
