comments.issue: Second- and third-generation reads in Fig. S1 are not defined.
comments.request: Specify what these reads are.
comments.quote: Fig S1: Specify what 2nd and 3rd generation reads are.

comments.issue: Fig. S11 has no legend for its colours.
comments.request: Specify what the colours represent.
comments.quote: Fig S11: Specify what the colors represent (there's no legend here).

comments.issue: Typo in Table S3.
comments.quote: Table S3: Typo - "Un-unchored"

comments.issue: Table S5 lacks read accession numbers.
comments.request: Add read accession numbers for each individual.
comments.quote: Table S5: Add read accession number(s) for each individual to ensure data can be tied back to samples.

reviews.assessment: Elegant, state-of-the-art study of broad significance; minor comments to sharpen interpretation and presentation.
strengths: rare evidence of inbreeding depression affecting wild population dynamics

comments.issue: The interaction between extrinsic and intrinsic factors is not explicitly highlighted.
comments.request: Highlight how extrinsic mortality and fecundity can drive inbreeding.
comments.quote: The interaction between extrinsic and intrinsic factors could be more explicitly highlighted – increase in extrinsic mortality/reduced fecundity could be key to driving inbreeding and thus intrinsic genetic effects on population dynamics.

comments.issue: Short ROH from ancestral founder effects in high-latitude populations are not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention short ancestral ROH (Foote et al. 2021).
comments.quote: the genomes of high latitude killer whale populations have been characterised as containing many short ROH associated with ancestral founder effects (Foote et al. 2021)

comments.issue: The Figure 1 colour key is small and embedded in panel B.
comments.request: Move the key beside the figure and enlarge it.
comments.quote: the colour key is embedded within panel B and is very small. Can the authors place the key so that it is to the side of the figure and larger/easier to read.

comments.issue: Large and jumping Ne confidence intervals in Figure 1D are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what drives the Ne uncertainty.
comments.quote: I couldn’t see any explanation given for this. It would be helpful to have some information on what might drive this uncertainty

comments.issue: Sample sizes behind the page 6 estimates appear small and caveats are missing.
comments.request: Provide sample sizes and uncertainty caveats.
comments.quote: Could the authors provide sample sizes in the text and add any appropriate caveats regarding uncertainty due to sample size, if necessary.

comments.issue: The 'constant environment' characterisation of the last 40 years should be moderated.
comments.request: Moderate the constant-environment text.
comments.quote: There has, to the best of my knowledge, been fluctuations in key environmental variables that are thought to have influenced population growth over the last 40 years.

comments.issue: The 'No inbreeding' simulations are presented as predictions rather than a null model.
comments.request: State that these simulations are a null model.
comments.quote: I would argue that the ‘No inbreeding’ simulations are a useful null model for that argument, rather than accurate prediction of growth rates in the real-life SRKW population in the absence of inbreeding.

comments.issue: Grammar error at the last line of page 7.
comments.request: Change 'influence' to 'influenced'.
comments.quote: Last line Page 7 ‘influence’ should be ‘influenced’

comments.issue: Non-geneticist readers may not know that fixed deleterious alleles cannot be purged without outbreeding.
comments.request: Add this clarification.
comments.quote: the authors could highlight for non-geneticist readers that once fixed deleterious alleles cannot be purged without some form of genetic rescue/outbreeding

comments.issue: The share of fixed deleterious alleles in ROH by length category is not reported.
comments.request: Report fixed deleterious alleles in ROH by length.
comments.quote: it would be useful to know what percentage of fixed deleterious alleles were found in ROH, and how this varies with length category

comments.issue: Page 11 gives the impression that killer whale populations are largely doing well.
comments.request: Acknowledge the mixed population picture and ongoing threats.
comments.quote: The authors should better acknowledge the mixed picture of population dynamics and that most of the stressors are still present in many populations and of on-going concern

comments.issue: Previous examples of inbreeding depression, such as the West Coast Community, are not compared.
comments.request: Draw comparisons with the West Coast Community example.
comments.quote: Additionally, the authors could comment upon/draw comparisons with previous suggested examples of inbreeding depression.

comments.issue: Reference 38 in the supplement is formatted differently and missing from the reference list.
comments.request: Fix the reference formatting.
comments.quote: there is a reference (38) cited using a different format and not in the references

comments.issue: The cited Moura et al. data lacked repeat masking and many SNPs are in poorly mappable regions.
comments.request: Note the repeat-masking and mappability problems.
comments.quote: The cited Moura et al. paper did not include any repeat masking or filtering. Re-analyses of their data found approximately half the SNPs were in regions identified by repeatmasker and/or GATK callableloci to be in regions of poor mapabillity

comments.issue: The first killer whale recombination map coordinates and rates are not provided.
comments.request: Provide the recombination map as a supplementary text file.
comments.quote: Could the authors please make the coordinates and rates available as a supplementary text file?

title: Inbreeding depression explains killer whale population dynamics

study.system: coastal invertebrates on plastic debris; North Pacific Subtropical Gyre

editor_summary: Editor asks to edit the title (no punctuation), declare competing interests including Ocean Cleanup Foundation donors, and reduce display items to six by moving Figures 1-2 to supplementary information; reviewer comments are minor.

reviews.assessment: Really interesting and well-written paper with no major concerns, only a few minor points of curiosity.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether consumption by larger fish or mammals is a possible fate of the debris or is included in the listed scenario.
comments.request: Clarify whether consumption is included in the scenarios at P3 Ln17.
comments.quote: P3 Ln17. Is another possible scenario that the materials are eaten by larger fish or mammals? Or is that included in (2)

comments.issue: Invertebrate dominance of biofouling is not discussed and it is unclear whether macroalgae colonised the debris.
comments.request: Comment on invertebrate dominance and the apparent absence of macroalgae.
comments.quote: Were there no macroalgae colonising the plastic debris and I was hoping there might be space to comment on this invertebrate dominance in the discussion.

comments.issue: It is not indicated whether the recorded coastal species include known invaders introduced via biofouling.
comments.request: Note which coastal species are known invasive or introduced via biofouling.
comments.quote: I was wondering if the coastal species identified in this study had members that are known to be invasive/have been introduced to new areas via biofouling

comments.issue: The paper does not discuss whether other ocean gyres would support similar communities.
comments.request: Expand on other gyre systems and their expected communities.
comments.quote: I'd also like to know a bit more about the other ocean gyre systems and whether they would be expected to support similar communities.

comments.issue: The 15-minute search effort lacks justification, and its coverage and potential bias are unclear.
comments.request: Justify the search effort and assess sampling bias.
comments.quote: Could you provide a little more justification for a 15 minute search effort. What proportion of the community did that sample and would you expect a bias against any groups of species?

comments.issue: It is unclear why two debris items were unfouled.
comments.request: Explain why two debris items were unfouled.
comments.quote: Was there any obvious reason why two of the debris items were unfouled?

reviews.assessment: Interesting observations, but the pumice argument is under-evidenced and the mechanisms, consequences and implications need much more discussion.
strengths: noteworthy evidence of reproduction by coastal taxa on debris

comments.issue: The claim that most pumice is small, rare, ephemeral and unable to support biodiversity is an under-evidenced assumption.
comments.request: Provide evidence on pumice abundance, size and rafting capacity.
comments.quote: Without more evidence, this seems too big an assumption: that most pumice is small, perhaps not especially abundant, relatively ephemeral in a marine context, and cannot support much biodiversity.

comments.issue: Barnes and Fraser 2003 on rafting by five phyla on man-made flotsam is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Barnes and Fraser 2003.
comments.quote: Please also see Barnes, D.K.A., Fraser, P.P., 2003. Rafting by five phyla on man-made flotsam in the Southern Ocean.

comments.issue: No mechanism is offered for why unusual landings occurred in recent years but were not documented before.
comments.request: Explain the likely mechanism or major change behind recent landings.
comments.quote: can you provide an explanation as to why this has occurred in recent years, but otherwise hasn’t been documented? What is the likely mechanism, or major change that’s taken place?

comments.issue: The species richness paragraph lacks insight into underlying mechanisms and consequences.
comments.request: Discuss the mechanisms and consequences of the richness patterns.
comments.quote: this paragraph summarizes your findings for species richness, but again, doesn’t provide much insight into the underlying mechanism and/or consequences of what you’re reporting.

comments.issue: The novel reproduction finding is not revisited, and its implications for biodiversity and invasion, e.g. Stenothoe gallensis, are barely discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of widespread reproduction by coastal species.
comments.quote: Given coastal species were so widespread and clearly capable of breeding in the locations which you found them, what does this mean for biodiversity?

comments.issue: Line 9 on P11 and P12 is redundant and causes confusion.
comments.request: Remove or reconcile the redundancy between P11 and P12.
comments.quote: Please note line 9 on P11 and P12 are somewhat redundant, this contributed to the confusion.

title: Extent and reproduction of coastal species on plastic debris in the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre

study.system: peer review outcomes; 300K manuscripts and 541 journals

reviews.assessment: Applauds the depth but has mixed feelings because the limited data cannot yet distinguish real bias from expected outcomes.
strengths: arguably the best review on potential biases in peer review to date
in-depth analysis of a fundamental problem

comments.issue: Analyses rest on very few papers, so conclusions may be driven by a few datasets and lack experimental evidence.
comments.request: Acknowledge the data limitation and the risk of bias from few papers.
comments.quote: There is a limitation in the data, that can be seen by the relatively few papers used to examine the biases in outcome in the review process (e.g. 10 papers in the file “final decision problem”).

comments.issue: Raw journal data would have added rigor beyond the meta-analysis of published studies.
comments.request: Consider using raw data from journals.
comments.quote: I expected authors to use raw data from journals, not from previously published studies.

comments.issue: Countries where English is not a primary language is not an appropriate proxy; percent of population speaking English works better.
comments.request: Replace the language variable with the percent of the population speaking English.
comments.quote: Something that needs to be corrected is that the authors keep refereeing to “countries where English is not a primary language”, and as others have founds (e.g. Tatsuya Amano work), this is not fully apropiate.

comments.issue: It remains unclear whether the patterns reflect real bias or expected outcomes, so conclusions and recommendations are premature.
comments.request: Gather more solid data before making conclusions and recommendations.
comments.quote: My experience tells me that the problem is largely driven by conscious and unconscious biases, but I think that we need more solid data before we make conclusion and recommendations.

reviews.assessment: Important contribution with sound data and analyses, but questions the concept of bias and wants deeper theoretical engagement and a broader literature search.
strengths: builds on and expands prior work
adds important knowledge about the peer review system
no issues detected with the data or statistical analyses

comments.issue: The focal concept bias may be the wrong term because bias, inequality and disparity have different meanings.
comments.request: Rethink and justify the use of bias versus inequality or disparity.
comments.quote: My major concern is whether the focal concept in this paper, “bias”, makes sense.

comments.issue: Theoretical discussions from scientometrics and sociology are not engaged, as references are mostly biological and multi-disciplinary.
comments.request: Draw on information science and sociological literature for deeper discussion.
comments.quote: I thus urge the authors to go through these domains to seek more in-depth discussions (and implications).

comments.issue: The Web of Science search strategy may be inaccurate.
comments.request: Expand the search via citing papers and consult domain experts with the search terms and results.
comments.quote: I'm not sure whether the proposed way of doing a search using the Web of Science database (L. 398 - L. 401) is accurate.

comments.issue: The journal selection ignores ecology and evolution papers published outside the targeted journals, affecting generalisation.
comments.request: Assess the impact of excluding these papers on the results and their generalisation.
comments.quote: this may ignore articles in ecology and evolution domains that didn't go to an ecology and evolution journal

comments.issue: The editor gender homophily and reviewer/author homophily findings are surprising and need more study.
comments.request: Investigate homophily further.
comments.quote: The findings about editor gender homophily and reviewer/author homiphily were surprising. I suspect that this needs more study.

title: Peer review perpetuates barriers for historically excluded groups

study.system: global lizards; biophysical thermal performance model and traits

editor_summary: Editor requires substantial new analyses, including sensitivity tests and spatial autocorrelation checks, before the findings can be considered robust.

reviews.assessment: Potentially useful mechanistic study, but key model assumptions are unvalidated and the improvement over simple trait-climate correlations is unproven.
strengths: potentially very useful mechanistic understanding of global ectotherm trait variation

comments.issue: The key assumption that predicted body temperatures match observed temperatures is validated only in Fig. S1 for 6 species and without performance estimates.
comments.request: Report a quantitative validation (e.g. R2) of predicted versus observed body temperatures.
comments.quote: To be exploitable (and for extrapolation across 6600 species), the model should provide a high R2 between predicted and observed body temperature for all the test species, but this test is lacking.

comments.issue: Validation is not assessed at the within-species, among-population and among-species levels, and within-species correlation appears weak.
comments.request: Report correlations between observed and predicted temperatures at all three levels.
comments.quote: we can imagine three different assessments: correlation between observed and predicted temperature between records within species

comments.issue: Trait-sensitivity relationships may simply reflect trait-climate collinearity rather than a mechanistic improvement.
comments.request: Compare trait-sensitivity relationships against simple trait-climate correlations.
comments.quote: Are relationships between traits and sensitivity stronger than the ones observed between traits and “simple climatic data”?

comments.issue: Residual spatial autocorrelation would inflate significance values.
comments.request: Test residuals for spatial autocorrelation and use methods that account for it.
comments.quote: Are the residuals of models spatially autocorrelated? If this is the case (as often happens), I urge the authors using approaches that take autocorrelation into account

comments.issue: The variance explained by the models, including partial R2 for sensitivity, is not reported.
comments.request: Report variance explained and partial R2 values.
comments.quote: What is the amount of variance explained by the models? (eg partial R2 explained by sensitivity)

comments.issue: The body mass relationship is significant but has near-zero R2, implying no biological importance.
comments.request: Interpret effect sizes, not just significance, for such large samples.
comments.quote: the relationship between body mass and body mass sensitivity is perhaps significant (at P = 0.007) but, from the plot, the R2 of the model looks to be nearly zero

comments.issue: The first Results paragraph may be a by-product of model definition rather than a true result.
comments.request: Clarify how much of this result is independent of model construction.
comments.quote: I wonder how much this is a true “result” or just a by-product of how the model is defined

comments.issue: It is unclear how robust the results at L170-177 are to variation in species richness across communities.
comments.request: Test sensitivity of these results to community richness.
comments.quote: how much are these results robust to variation in species richness across communities?

comments.issue: Activity period is defined coarsely by latitude, ignoring strong within-latitude variation such as lowland versus mountain conditions.
comments.request: Use a finer season-length assessment based on thermal limits.
comments.quote: This is a very rough approximation as at the same latitude we can see very strong variation of activity (eg between lowland and mountains)

comments.issue: Field body temperature cannot substitute for Tpref without slope = 1 and intercept = 0, not merely a positive correlation.
comments.request: Test slope and intercept before treating body temperature as Tpref.
comments.quote: A positive correlation between body temperature and Tpref is not enough to use the 2 variables interchangeably, as this would also require a slope = 1 and intercept = 0

comments.issue: The paragraph at L425-442 is very unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite this paragraph more clearly.
comments.quote: at a first read, this paragraph was very unclear to me. The paragraph can be definitely improved.

comments.issue: The term 'sensitivity' conflicts with its usual ecological meaning and should be reconsidered.
comments.request: Use a less ambiguous term or define it explicitly.
comments.quote: I’m not sure “sensitivity” is the best term through the text. In the ecological literature the “sensitivity” term is often used with a completely different meaning

comments.issue: Phylogenetic imputation is extreme for key traits (84% and over 95% imputed) and its performance is never reported.
comments.request: Report imputation performance (e.g. cross-validation) and justify or reduce the imputation.
comments.quote: For some key traits the % imputed traits is very large (84% for field body temperature, and >95% for preferred temperature, cold tolerance and heat tolerance)

comments.issue: Supplementary cross-references are wrong at L356 and page 4, and the Fig. S1 legend cannot be read correctly.
comments.request: Correct the supplementary references and the Fig. S1 legend.
comments.quote: Pag 4 : here you refer to Fig. SX, please correct it (it should be Fig S1)

comments.issue: The supplementary material at page 7, L100-103 is very difficult to follow, with undefined Fig. Sx and Table Sx references.
comments.request: Correct and reorganize these supplementary references.
comments.quote: Pag 7 L 100-103: here you refer to another Fig Sx and to Table Sx. It is very difficult to follow the supplementary material.

reviews.assessment: Well-implemented biophysical approach, but fitness relevance, extrapolations and the underwhelming trait relationships temper enthusiasm.
strengths: biophysical approach well described, motivated and implemented
appreciates estimating sensitivity to trait values
using biophysics to explain macro patterns

comments.issue: The performance metric is mostly sprint speed, whose relevance to fitness is not justified relative to activity time, energetics or assimilation.
comments.request: Justify the fitness relevance of the performance metric and consider assimilation.
comments.quote: The relevance of the manuscript to selection hinges on the performance metric being relevant to fitness. This requires further justification.

comments.issue: Whether the assumed months of activity influence conclusions near the latitudinal cutoffs is untested.
comments.request: Test sensitivity of conclusions to the activity-month assumptions.
comments.quote: I also wondered whether the assumed months of activity substantially influence the conclusions, particularly near the latitudinal cutoffs for different assumptions.

comments.issue: Many poleward regions in Figure 2 have few or no lizard species, which could distort the analyses.
comments.request: Limit analyses to regions with a minimum species richness.
comments.quote: I am concerned that there are few or no lizard species in many of the poleward regions mapped in Fig 2. I would be inclined to limit the analyses to regions with some minimum richness.

comments.issue: The species in Figure 3 do not cover some sensitivity ranges well, such as Tpref.
comments.request: Add a supplementary map showing where the data derive from.
comments.quote: A related concern is that the species represented in Figure 3 don’t cover some of the sensitivity ranges well

comments.issue: Trait values are projected across species ranges despite substantial intraspecific variation.
comments.request: Address intraspecific trait variation in the assemblage analyses.
comments.quote: I am also concerned that trait values are projected across the range of species given the likely substantial intraspecific variation

comments.issue: Extensive phylogenetic extrapolation, in places from only 2.6% of species, is concerning given clustered data.
comments.request: Assess the robustness of the imputed extrapolations.
comments.quote: I appreciate the phylogenetic-imputed methods as an approach but am concerned with the extensive extrapolations (e.g., extrapolating from 2.6% of species)

comments.issue: Species richness thresholds within grid cells for the variance analysis are unclear.
comments.request: State and justify the richness thresholds.
comments.quote: I also wonder about thresholds for species richness within grid cells for the variance analysis.

comments.issue: The baseline for the sensitivity analyses is unclear and seems to involve random sampling from distributions.
comments.request: Explain the sensitivity analysis baseline and add latitudinal trait patterns.
comments.quote: I’m not sure what the baseline for the sensitivity analyses were. I think the values were randomly sampled from distributions.

comments.issue: The NicheMapR parametrization, especially lizard height and ground contact, is not specified in the supplement.
comments.request: Describe the microclimate model parametrization.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to also specify the parametrization in the supplement

comments.issue: Body size may be a consequence of temperature-dependent development rather than a direct target of selection, which matters because performance is most sensitive to body size.
comments.request: Discuss the developmental rate-body size link and cite Kearney et al.
comments.quote: Body size may be more a consequence of the temperature dependence of developmental rate than directly subject to selection.

comments.issue: The temporal aspect of thermoregulation and whether intermediate temperatures between sun and shade are allowed is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the thermoregulation assumptions.
comments.quote: It would seem more biologically realistic to allow the lizards to choose the temperature closest to the preferred temperature in the range between the sunny and shady operative temperature.

comments.issue: The shaded solar radiation estimates may not be empirically realistic at lizard-relevant scales.
comments.request: Justify or refine the shadiness estimates.
comments.quote: I wondered how empirically realistic the estimates are since the scale seems much larger than a lizard moving in and out of shade.

comments.issue: The Huey et al. work on thermal tolerance, thermoregulation and shade across latitudes is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the Huey et al. analysis.
comments.quote: The Huey et al. analysis of lizard thermal tolerance and the role of thermoregulatory ability and shade availability across latitudes seems worth discussing.

comments.issue: Extrapolating the findings to ectotherms generally rather than lizards is a stretch.
comments.request: Refer to lizards rather than ectotherms where appropriate.
comments.quote: I found the extrapolation to refer to ectotherms rather than lizards a stretch in places and think it would sometimes be better to refer to lizards.

title: Climate drives global functional trait variation in lizards

study.system: SodFM superoxide dismutases; phylogenetics and biochemistry of metal preference

editor_summary: Editor asks to address the reviewers' criticisms and some editorial concerns before a final decision on the manuscript.

reviews.assessment: Methods are appropriate, results convincing and clearly discussed; recommends publication.
Very interesting and well-supported study, highly suitable for the journal, with minor comments on trees, trait reconstruction and overstated statements.
strengths: one of very few studies of a biochemical phenotype across a phylogeny

comments.issue: The paper jumps between Extended Data figures and does not go through them in order.
comments.request: Order the Extended Data figures as they are discussed.
comments.quote: One problem is that the paper frequently jumps between different Extended Data figures and that it does not go through them in order.

comments.issue: The model selection criterion used in IQ-tree is not described.
comments.request: State the IQ-tree model selection criterion.
comments.quote: What was the model selection criterion in IQ-tree. I assume it was BIC. This should be described

comments.issue: The trees in main-text Figures 1 and 2 lack scale bars.
comments.request: Add scale bars to Figures 1 and 2.
comments.quote: The trees in the main text figures 1 and 2 lack a scale bar.

comments.issue: Semi-circle tree representations are very hard to read.
comments.request: Switch to a left-to-right tree representation.
comments.quote: I would urge the authors to switch from a semi circle representation of the trees to a normal 'left to right' representation.

comments.issue: The cambialism score is not plotted as a log score, making Fe versus Mn comparison harder.
comments.request: Use a log-scale cambialism score.
comments.quote: The cambialism score should be a log score. The authors already plot it on log scales in various figures. It is much easier to compare relative preferences between Fe and Mn on a log scale

comments.issue: Figure 2C is overloaded with colours and hard to understand.
comments.request: Simplify Figure 2C.
comments.quote: Figure 2C overloaded me with different colors and I had to stare at it for a long time to understand what it is supposed to convey.

comments.issue: The assumption that observed preferences are optimal for each environment cannot be made without environmental metal abundances.
comments.request: Remove or qualify the optimality assumption.
comments.quote: There is an assumption in the paper that the observed preferences are somehow optimal for each environment. I'm not sure that statement can be made without knowing the environmental abundances of these metals

comments.issue: The evolution of metal specificity is discussed without explicit ancestral trait reconstruction.
comments.request: Perform trait reconstruction (parsimony or Gaussian model) at internal nodes.
comments.quote: I think the authors should consider performing a trait reconstruction using their data (i.e. use parsimony or a gaussian model to infer the aCR ratio at internal nodes of their protein tree).

comments.issue: Correlations between amino acids and aCR ratio ignore phylogenetic relatedness.
comments.request: Perform a phylogenetic regression or modify the correlation language.
comments.quote: A straight correlation ignores the relatedness of the sequences of the tree and can lead to erroneous inferences of correlations.

comments.issue: 'Evolutionary hotspot' is used for taxonomic groups, conflicting with its protein-region meaning.
comments.request: Reconsider the use of the term evolutionary hotspot.
comments.quote: this term has previously been used to describe regions of proteins where important changes tend to happen. In order to avoid confusion, perhaps the use of this term could be reconsidered.

comments.issue: The selection-for-cambialism statement at line 278 is not supported by the data.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the line 278 statement.
comments.quote: I could not understand how the data support this statement. Either it needs clarification or be removed.

comments.issue: The closing discussion sentences about global warming and epidemics are over the top.
comments.request: Remove the grandiose closing statements.
comments.quote: I found the last few sentences of the discussion a bit over the top. I don't understand how these proteins have anything to do with global warming or epidemics.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive, well-supported study of broad interest; notes that epistatic effects and peroxide resistance were not explored further.
strengths: figures quite good and text accessible

comments.issue: Considerable epistatic effects on metal preference are suggested but not further considered.
comments.quote: This suggests the impact of considerable epistatic effects, which were not further considered here.

comments.issue: Peroxide poisoning resistance of Mn-specific enzymes is not considered in the context of evolutionary selection.
comments.quote: Further, all Mn-specific enzymes are resistant to peroxide poisoning; this was not further considered in the context of evolutionary selection.

title: An ancient metalloenzyme evolves through metal preference modulation

study.system: prokaryotes; 22,000 environmental sequencing samples; niche breadth

reviews.assessment: Interesting approach, but the SNB score needs consistent interpretation, clearer thresholds and better-described data handling.

comments.issue: Thresholds for low/high diversity, SNB and specialist categories are undefined.
comments.request: Clarify the thresholds used in the text.
comments.quote: In the results section there are remarks as low/high local diversity, low/high social niche breadth, low/high diversity specialists but the thresholds for these delineations are not clear to the reader.

comments.issue: At family level Pelagibacteraceae spans marine and freshwater and may be a generalist.
comments.request: Reconsider the family-level specialist classification.
comments.quote: One would argue that at the family level Pelagibacteraceae should be rather generalist than specialist.

comments.issue: The section title contradicts the dominance of the taxa identified as specialists.
comments.request: Reconcile the section title with the results.
comments.quote: does not seem to corroborate with the dominance of what you identify as specialists in the paragraph before (i.e., Pelagibacteraceae and Prochlorococcus)

comments.issue: The MGnify data types and analysis steps for metagenomes, amplicons and metatranscriptomes are not described.
comments.request: Describe the data types and pipelines and their comparability.
comments.quote: add a brief description of the type of data they obtain from MGnify regarding the community composition and what are the main steps in these analyses

comments.issue: Genomes are not reconstructed from the same datasets used for community comparisons.
comments.request: Discuss how source differences affect pangenome and genome-size interpretations.
comments.quote: each piece of data is collected from a different source and as I understand genomes are not reconstructed from the same datasets used for community comparisons how could this affect the interpretations of the pangenome, genome size, etc.

comments.issue: The 'unknown' experiment-type category is confusing.
comments.request: Clarify what 'unknown' means and its impact.
comments.quote: it is confusing as to what authors mean by category “unknown”? this could be very confusing and could potentially affect the results in ways that are difficult to discuss or conclude.

comments.issue: Metatranscriptome abundances are not comparable because activity affects representation.
comments.request: Remove metatranscriptomes from the study.
comments.quote: I would not say that abundance calculations based on metagenomes and amplicon is comparable to those calculated from metatrnscriptomes.

comments.issue: The saline/non-saline threshold is unclear and may lump a wide salinity range.
comments.request: Define the salinity threshold and its range.
comments.quote: What is the threshold for differentiating between saline and non-saline. Does this refer to marine salinity or hypersaline?

comments.issue: Alternative treatments of unknown ranks and taxa are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how different unknown-taxa approaches affect results.
comments.quote: It would be great if authors discuss how different approaches they have tested for dealing with the unknown taxa would affect their results and conclusions.

comments.issue: Figures are too small and packed with data points.
comments.request: Make plots larger and less compact.
comments.quote: All figures are packed with datapoints but presented in very small sizes both for the main figures and the supplementary figures.

comments.issue: The first abstract sentence is disconnected from the rest.
comments.request: Connect the opening sentence to the abstract.
comments.quote: I find the first sentence of the abstract disconnected from the rest of the abstract text

comments.issue: Low turnover cannot be inferred without time-series data.
comments.request: Clarify how turnover rate is inferred from alpha/beta diversity.
comments.quote: Maybe this could be concluded if these datasets are timeseries of the same sampling point otherwise how the comparison of alpha and beta diversity could signal low turnover rate?

comments.issue: The low-beta-diversity sentence should compare samples within a biome.
comments.request: Reformulate the sentence accordingly.
comments.quote: It could be reformulated to mention that these biomes have low beta diversity indexes in comparison with each other inside one biome

comments.issue: The microbiome biosensor statement lacks references.
comments.request: Add references for the biosensor statement.
comments.quote: We used the observation that microbiomes are biosensors Please add references

comments.issue: Clumping high taxonomic ranks such as Proteobacteria is misleading.
comments.request: Reformulate this paragraph.
comments.quote: I still feel resistance towards how this sentence in formulated. Clumping these high taxonomic ranks specifically for ubiquitous phyla such as proteobacteria with high diversity of ecological strategies in their representatives could be very misleading.

comments.issue: The over-representation of the four phyla is not only due to study effort.
comments.request: Correct the explanation for phylum representation.
comments.quote: I don’t think the higher representation of these taxa in solely due to them being more studied.

comments.issue: 'Established' phyla and the candidate phyla status effect are unclear.
comments.request: Define 'established' and clarify candidate phyla radiation.
comments.quote: What do you mean by established? Maybe validly described?

comments.issue: No statistics are given on how prevalent specialized genera are.
comments.request: Provide statistics on specialized genera prevalence.
comments.quote: Please provide stats on how prevalent specialized genera are in these phyla compared to the phyla with more generalized genera

comments.issue: What 'genomically more similar' means is undefined.
comments.request: Define the genomic similarity measure.
comments.quote: What do you mean here, genome size? Pangenome size? Genomic content and functions?

comments.issue: Coding-density and streamlining section does not name the relevant taxa.
comments.request: Name the taxa and their streamlining routes.
comments.quote: please add the name of relevant taxa. Are these specialists animal associated groups with streamlined genomes or free living groups with streamlined genomes such as SAR11?

comments.issue: Whether these groups have specific hosts or diverse partners is not addressed.
comments.request: Use the data to test partner specificity.
comments.quote: I am curious as your data could provide any hint towards whether these groups have specific hosts or rather a diverse range of partners in different environments?

comments.issue: 'Taxonomic taxa' is undefined.
comments.request: Use 'taxonomic affiliation'.
comments.quote: What do you mean by taxonomic taxa? Taxonomic affiliation maybe?

comments.issue: The 50% function-presence threshold is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain whether this refers to the core genome.
comments.quote: This sounds odd to me. Do you mean as a part of the core or in general? This threshold needs more explanation to make the logic clearer.

comments.issue: Typo: 'false discover rate'.
comments.request: Change to 'false discovery rate'.
comments.quote: carried out via the false discover rate (FDR) as suggested in discovery

reviews.assessment: Exciting metric that needs clearer conceptual grounding, terminology and figure presentation before it can be adopted.
strengths: concise and globally easy to read

comments.issue: SNB and metabolic niche breadth are conflated, and generalist/specialist and diversity terms are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Disambiguate SNB from niche breadth and standardize terminology.
comments.quote: with sometimes an ambiguity between the “metabolic” niche breadth (the historical definition of niche breadth, i.e. similarly to Hutchinson niche; also sometimes called “general niche breadth” in the manuscript) and the SNB introduced in this work

comments.issue: SNB is only described in the methods, without background where it is introduced.
comments.request: Add background on SNB at its first mention in the results.
comments.quote: Although it is the right place to present the formular, a bit of background (for example stating that SNB is a dissimilarity score based of Spearman correlation) would be useful at the beginning of the results, where the score is introduced.

comments.issue: How SNB fills an ecological gap and compares with other niche and network metrics is not explained.
comments.request: Describe SNB's advantages relative to the state of the art.
comments.quote: How is SNB score filling a gap in ecological studies? How does is compare to trophic niche breadth or habitat niche breadth, etc, that are named in the introduction?

comments.issue: Whether SNB captures fundamental or realised social niches, and whether partner lists saturate, is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the fundamental versus realised social niche question.
comments.quote: Similarly, are you scoring the fundamental social niche breadth? I have the sensation that you are hypothesizing that the sum of all realized social interactions found in your 22 thousand of sample results in the fundamental social niche?

comments.issue: The postulates behind SNB are not formalised.
comments.request: State the assumptions behind SNB explicitly.
comments.quote: What are the postulates in the background of SNB? Probably at least that genetic information of the SSU summarize the metabolic capacity of an organism and that metabolic capacity determines the biogeographical distribution of the taxon.

comments.issue: The strong statement about quantifying similarity between categorical biomes lacks support.
comments.request: Justify or reference this statement.
comments.quote: Strong statement such as “Also, it remains difficult to quantify the degree of similarity between categorical biomes.” would deserve a justification or a good reference.

comments.issue: Data interpretation appears in figure captions rather than the main text.
comments.request: Move data interpretations into the text.
comments.quote: Data interpretations better read in the text than in the figure captions.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the SNB versus metabolic-niche comparison validates the metric.
comments.request: State whether this analysis validates SNB.
comments.quote: Is this paragraph, for the authors, a kind a validation that their SNB score is accurate to determine niche breadth?

comments.issue: The generalizability claim requires demonstrating a genomic signature of SNB first.
comments.request: Demonstrate the genomic signature before claiming generalizability.
comments.quote: This hold true only if you demonstrate first that SNB scores have a genomic signature.

comments.issue: How Figure 3b supports younger specialists is not traceable.
comments.request: Explain how the age conclusion follows from the figure.
comments.quote: Can you explain how you conclude that from this figure? I was unable to track this information.

comments.issue: The metrics and statistical test behind community and genomic heterogeneity are unclear.
comments.request: Define the metrics and test used.
comments.quote: I don’t know where to find that in the data. What are the metrics used to assess “community heterogeneity” (SNB?) and “genomic heterogeneity” (heterogeneity of the independent genomic features?). Which statistical test was used?

comments.issue: Whether SNB can proxy metabolic niche breadth is left without conclusion.
comments.request: Draw a clear conclusion about SNB as a niche proxy.
comments.quote: This is a very important step to know if SNB is a metrics that allow to characterize the specificity of community assembly or of SNB can also be used as a proxy for metabolic niche breadth.

comments.issue: Domain-level SNB differences and the 223 bacteria-free samples are not examined.
comments.request: Check archaeal versus bacterial SNB and the bacteria-free samples.
comments.quote: have you seen a difference in average SNB at the domain level between archea and bacteria, as archea are supposably a very specialized domain? It seems that you have sample with no bacteria (22 518 – 22 295 = 223), are they archea-only samples?

comments.issue: Figure legends are too long and contain interpretations.
comments.request: Keep only panel descriptions in the legends.
comments.quote: To shorten the rather long legends of this manuscript, I would recommend to only keep the descriptions of each panel and remove all interpretations from the legends.

comments.issue: The colour gradient in Figure 2b prevents comparison of SNB across taxonomic levels.
comments.request: Re-scale colours within each taxonomic level.
comments.quote: it leads to a representation where it is almost impossible to compare SNB scores across a taxonomical level due to the color gradient constrain (phyla are all orange, species are all blue)

comments.issue: Main text and supplement methods are poorly partitioned, with unused methods presented.
comments.request: Move unused methods to the supplement and describe only the selected ones.
comments.quote: The partitioning of information in the Methods section in the main text and in supplemental should be revised. For example, 10 methods to measures community composition dissimilarity are presented in the main text, but only one is used.

comments.issue: The criteria for selecting the 10 dissimilarity methods, and why sparCC was not used, are unclear.
comments.request: State the criteria for method selection.
comments.quote: The rather well accepted sparCC methods (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002687) has been demonstrated to be very robust to compositional data, and sometimes better that bray-curtis, spearson or pearson. On which criteria were the 10 presented methods selected?

comments.issue: DNA presence is treated as active presence, though activity is part of the niche definition.
comments.request: Discuss the DNA-versus-activity caveat and necromass DNA.
comments.quote: No discussion is provided about the fact that a DNA sequence is not the demonstration of the active presence of an organism. Yet, the active presence is included in the original definition of ecological niche and is partially used by the authors

comments.issue: 'Tree of life' in the title oversells the scope.
comments.request: Rephrase to avoid overselling.
comments.quote: “tree of life” in the title and elsewhere make readers expect something different than what is presented in this work. Please rephrase to ovoid this kind of overselling.

comments.issue: Terms such as 'as expected' and 'strikingly' should be removed.
comments.request: Remove these evaluative terms.
comments.quote: Remove the terms such as “as expected”, “strikingly”, etc.

comments.issue: Whether microbiomes detect disease or are biomarkers rather than biosensors is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the biosensor versus biomarker framing.
comments.quote: Are microbiomes really capable of detecting disease state? Isn’t it rather the disease state and its biochemical consequences that select for a different microbiome? Similarly, are microbes biosensors or biomarkers?

comments.issue: 'Diverse sample' is ambiguous.
comments.request: Define whether diverse means rich, numerous or compositionally different.
comments.quote: “organisms that occur in diverse sample”: Does ‘diverse’ mean here with a high biodiversity/richness or in a high number of sample or even compositionally different?

comments.issue: The type of turnover behind the statement is unspecified.
comments.request: Define whether turnover is species or cell level.
comments.quote: Do you mean a turn over in the species composition

comments.issue: 'Consistent' microbial composition is too strong a claim.
comments.request: Soften or clarify this statement.
comments.quote: I am a bit uncomfortable with this statement, as ‘consistent’ is a bit too strong. It can also be that number of taxon of the accessory community is small relative to the number of taxon making the core community

comments.issue: The biosensor observation lacks a reference.
comments.request: Give a reference for the biosensor statement.
comments.quote: observation from who? Depending, please give a reference.

comments.issue: The link between cultivation difficulty and low SNB is unclear.
comments.request: Explain or remove this link.
comments.quote: The link between being difficult to cultivate and low SNB is unclear to me as the authors as using sequencing data from environmental sample, and as such, that did not require cultivation steps.

comments.issue: 'Have relatively generalised genera' needs rewording.
comments.request: Rephrase the phrase.
comments.quote: “have relatively generalised genera”: please rephrased.

comments.issue: 'Ubiquitous taxa' is undefined and unreferenced.
comments.request: Clarify whether this means cosmopolitan and add a reference.
comments.quote: “At the generalist end of the spectrum are ubiquitous taxa”: Do you mean cosmopolitan? Is there a reference for that?

comments.issue: The dominance statement needs qualification by stable conditions.
comments.request: Add 'in stable conditions' or similar.
comments.quote: Please, add ‘in stable conditions’ or something similar.

comments.issue: 'Local community' is undefined.
comments.request: Define what a local community is in this work.
comments.quote: “Whereas local communities are typically dominated by generalists”: what is a local community in the context of your work?

comments.issue: The r/K-selected statement lacks a reference.
comments.request: Add a prokaryote-specific reference.
comments.quote: can you please add a reference, maybe specific to prokaryotes?

comments.issue: 'Genomic features' is undefined and their number is unstated.
comments.request: Explain genomic features and how many are used.
comments.quote: At first instance “genomic features” is used in the text, please add a few words to explain what is meant, and how many independent features are considered.

comments.issue: The text says genus rank but Figure 3b shows family level.
comments.request: Clarify the taxonomic rank of the age result.
comments.quote: Figure 3b is displaying the data at the family level, so at the taxonical rank just above. So is it at the family of genus rank that social specialists are found younger than social generalists?

comments.issue: The claim that previous genome-size suggestions are biased should be rephrased.
comments.request: Rephrase since all work carries bias.
comments.quote: please rephrase this sentence, as every work has its own inherent bias, including the present work.

comments.issue: The Polyangium example lacks its SNB score.
comments.request: Add the SNB score for Polyangium.
comments.quote: Can you add the SNB score too, so it reads “for example the genus Polyangium with a mean genome size of 12.7Mb and a SNB of XX”.

comments.issue: Whether the 5-read threshold is total or per sample is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the scale of the read threshold.
comments.quote: 5 reads in the total dataset or per sample?

comments.issue: Which ecological dissimilarity measures use few taxa is unclear.
comments.request: Identify the affected dissimilarity measures.
comments.quote: “For some of the ecological dissimilarity”: which ones?

comments.issue: The 'pairwise comparisons can be based on few taxa' phrasing is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the intended meaning.
comments.quote: Do you mean that it is the case “pairwise comparisons was based on a reduced number taxa”, or that even with a reduced number of taxa the analysis is robust or meaningful

comments.issue: Shannon entropy is represented twice by colour and size.
comments.request: Justify or remove the duplicate encoding.
comments.quote: “Both colour-coding and size of markers represents the Shannon entropy”: Why depicting the same metrics twice?

comments.issue: Alpha diversity colour gradient lacks a scale.
comments.request: Add a colour scale for alpha diversity.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to add a color scale as the alpha-diversity is here represented by a color gradient.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether biomes are ordered by cumulative or average alpha diversity.
comments.request: Specify how biomes are arranged.
comments.quote: is it the cumulative alpha-diversity of all samples of the biome (Boolean ‘or’) or the average alpha diversity?

reviews.assessment: Original and important empirical contribution with state-of-the-art methods; only wishes the figures were less data-dense.

comments.issue: Some figures are too data-dense for straightforward interpretation.
comments.request: Provide more interpretable summary figures.
comments.quote: I found some figures very data-dense, which somewhat hinders their straightforward visual interpretation (e.g. fig 4d or Fig 5).

reviews.assessment: Interesting and broadly relevant topic, but the conclusions require much stronger support and robustness checks.
strengths: highly interesting and potentially broad-interest topic
differences in abundance profiles and pangenome structures

comments.issue: The rank-correlation SNB metric is unreliable when many community members are low abundance.
comments.request: Justify the formula and test sensitivity to metric choice.
comments.quote: A rank correlation based metric needs to be used with much caution when several members of the community are very low abundance

comments.issue: Microbial niche alteration by secreted molecules is a potential confounder.
comments.request: Discuss metabolic interactions and their implications.
comments.quote: Another potential confounder is the niche alteration by microbes – many microbes secrete small molecules like amino acids that can alter the niches.

comments.issue: The challenge to classical specialist-versus-generalist theory is not discussed prominently.
comments.request: Lay out both sides of the argument and pitfalls.
comments.quote: The manuscript seems to question the “classic” ecological theory that specialists have fitness advantage at the expense of versatility.

comments.issue: Metatranscriptomes add confounders and 16S and shotgun estimates are pooled.
comments.request: Analyse 16S and shotgun separately and drop metatranscriptomes.
comments.quote: it is unclear how 16S vs shotgun metagenomics estimates are pooled together. I recommend analysing the two separately to check the robustness of the conclusions.

comments.issue: Effect sizes are not clearly reported despite being modest and sensitive.
comments.request: Report effect sizes clearly.
comments.quote: The manuscript is poor on clearly reporting the effect sizes, which are modest in many cases and thus potentially sensitive to the choices of the metrics and any biases in the data.

comments.issue: Main analyses are not repeated in subsets of habitats.
comments.request: Repeat analyses in subsets of habitats.
comments.quote: Repetition of the main analyses in a subset of habitats would be very insightful in testing the robustness/generalisation of the conclusions drawn.

comments.issue: Whether the functional taxonomic unit should be strain or subspecies is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the appropriate functional taxonomic unit.
comments.quote: it becomes imperative to discuss whether the “true functional taxonomic unit” should be the sub-species/strain rather than species or higher

comments.issue: The enrichment analyses are descriptive with long lists in the main figure.
comments.request: Move long lists to supplementary and present a summary.
comments.quote: The enrichment analyses in the last figure are way to descriptive without any insights.

comments.issue: Classic niche occupation and competitive exclusion theory are not introduced.
comments.request: Mention classic theory and explain niche breadth usage.
comments.quote: Introduction would benefit from explicit mentioning of classic ecological theory re. niche occupation & competitive exclusion

comments.issue: Growth-rate prediction is tricky and alternative metagenomic estimates exist.
comments.request: Use growth rates from tools such as coptr or iRep.
comments.quote: the growth rate prediction is a tricky business. Why not use growth rates calculated from metagenomic samples with tools like coptr, iRep etc.?

comments.issue: 'Low diversity specialists' is undefined.
comments.request: Define the term clearly.
comments.quote: Terms like “low diversity specialists” are unclear and warrant clear definitions.

comments.issue: Figure captions are sometimes unclear, e.g. the letter key in Fig. 2e.
comments.request: Improve figure captions and citation consistency.
comments.quote: Figure captions are sometimes unclear (e.g. Fig.2 panel e: what is the key for the letters?).

comments.issue: The hypothesis behind variable genome sizes in generalist genera is not stated.
comments.request: State the hypothesis and literature and functions involved.
comments.quote: Regarding the genomes in generalist genera being more variable in size, what is the hypothesis? What is the literature suggesting? What functions are coded on these variable regions?

comments.issue: Code and results are not shared in a repository.
comments.request: Create a GitHub repository for code and results.
comments.quote: Please consider making a github repository to share the code and the results

comments.issue: Why Lachnospiraceae have high SNB, and what high/low diversity habitats mean, is unclear.
comments.request: Define high and low diversity habitats.
comments.quote: Why Lachnospiraceae have a high SNB, where the diversity of their habitats come from? In general these concepts of “high diversity habitats” and “low diversity habitats” are not completely clear.

comments.issue: The '(but see 48)' reference is not explained.
comments.request: State explicitly what the reference points out.
comments.quote: Please state explicitly what authors what to point out fro the reference.

title: A social niche breadth score reveals niche range strategies of generalists and specialists

study.system: academic awards in ecology and evolution; journal and society award data

editor_summary: Editor invites a revision addressing all reviewer comments and editorial points before a final decision on publication.

reviews.assessment: A well-thought, well-written and striking study, with a major criticism about its binary treatment of gender and a few other points.
strengths: striking results that could transform award policies

comments.issue: The manuscript lacks line numbers.
comments.request: Add line numbers.
comments.quote: The line numbers would have helped me to a great extent

comments.issue: Gender is treated as a male-female dichotomy, making non-binary and LGBTQ people invisible.
comments.request: Correct the binary framing, e.g. by analysing LGBTQ inclusion in diversity statements.
comments.quote: while the authors discuss gender disparity, they stick with the traditional male and female dichotomy of sex, ignoring the people defining themselves beyond restrictive gender norms

comments.issue: The statement on page 18 omits LGBTQ people from the list of systemically disadvantaged groups, and the limitations only mention non-binary people in parenthesis.
comments.request: Add LGBTQ people to the statement and expand the limitations section.
comments.quote: By correcting the statement on page 18, application 1:

comments.issue: The link between open science practices and a more equitable scientific environment is not established.
comments.request: Explain how transparency and reproducibility promote equity.
comments.quote: I think the authors should also establish a link between how transparency and reproducibility of research activities promote a more equitable scientific environment

reviews.assessment: Agrees on the issue's importance and is receptive to suggestions, but flags design, analysis and interpretation issues in award selection and gender assignment.
strengths: glad for data to motivate change

comments.issue: Open science is evaluated above other practices without clear justification of the criteria.
comments.request: Justify the open science category and specify the criteria used.
comments.quote: the inclusion of OS as a category for evaluation *over any other scientific practice we wish to encourage* isn’t particularly well justified

comments.issue: Open science may be absent as a criterion simply because journal policies already require it.
comments.request: Consider that journal open-data policies may explain the absence of OS criteria.
comments.quote: It may be that open science isn’t specifically listed as an assessment criterion for “best papers” because any article under consideration has already done so because of publishing in the journal

comments.issue: Adding open science as an evaluation metric may be counterproductive for ECRs in the Global South.
comments.request: Consider the potential negative consequences of the OS criterion.
comments.quote: for many ECRs, especially those in the Global South, there may be some very legitimate concerns regarding sharing data and other OS practices, so it is possible that adding this as an evaluation metric is counterproductive to the goals

comments.issue: Indirect gender assignment is ethically fraught, ignores non-binary identities and is error-prone outside Western names.
comments.request: Survey awardees and ask them their gender instead of assigning it indirectly.
comments.quote: The indirect assignment of gender is fraught with ethical concerns, fails to consider beyond the binary, and as alluded in the paper, may have higher error rates outside of Western names/identities

comments.issue: Excluding journals for narrow scope (e.g. ornithology, systematics, botany, and J Ecology) leads to odd and inconsistent decisions.
comments.request: Reconsider the journal inclusion criteria and include major subdiscipline journals.
comments.quote: I think a major shortcoming of the study is the selection of journals / societies for inclusion, for two reasons.

comments.issue: Excluding smaller or more focused societies and journals reduces the dataset and may omit societies ahead on equity criteria.
comments.request: Include prizes from smaller and more focused societies and journals.
comments.quote: This brings me to the other reason I think it is a mistake to exclude the prizes from smaller or more focused societies and journals.

comments.issue: Geography is not included as a response variable despite the global south push and intersectionality emphasis.
comments.request: Include geography as a response variable.
comments.quote: I was surprised not to see geography included as a response variable, given the increased push to have authors, editors, speakers, etc. from the global south.

comments.issue: No statistical tests are performed on the gender data.
comments.request: Run binomial or chi-squared tests on the gender data.
comments.quote: It may seem like proving the obvious, but some statistical analyses are necessary – e.g., some binomial or chi-squared tests on the gender data, etc.

comments.issue: The age-cutoff recommendation ignores that donor intent and legal structures may make changes impossible or unethical.
comments.request: Acknowledge constraints on changing age cutoffs.
comments.quote: I believe the ESAs Mercer Award has the 40-year age cutoff because that was the wish of the donors that established the award and supporting fund in honor of their son in 1948.

comments.issue: Assessing achievements relative to opportunity is theoretically beneficial but practically impossible without clear operationalization.
comments.request: Explain how achievements relative to opportunity could be assessed in practice.
comments.quote: This recommendation strikes me as theoretically beneficial but practically impossible.

comments.issue: Replacing vague assessment terms with concrete metrics is not straightforward because quantifiable criteria are also biased.
comments.request: Propose alternative criteria that avoid both vagueness and quantifiable bias.
comments.quote: I agree that these terms are vague and subjective – but so is the scientific evaluation. What alternative criteria do you propose?

comments.issue: Subsuming mentoring, service and advocacy into research awards is problematic and separate awards would be better.
comments.request: Create separate awards for non-research contributions instead.
comments.quote: I think that it we want to value and recognize mentorship, community service, or advocacy, then we should create awards recognizing it.

comments.issue: Eliminating letters is not straightforward because letters can reveal resource inequities; cultural differences in letters are the real issue.
comments.request: Ask referees for specific information instead of eliminating letters.
comments.quote: In short, there is a cost-benefit to the use of letters, so rather than their elimination I would advocate for asking referees for the specific information the committee needs.

comments.issue: The authors omit easier steps such as sampling all student-submitted papers and running webinars on competitions.
comments.request: Consider automatic nomination of student papers and application webinars.
comments.quote: We found that the pool of outstanding articles making the short list for consideration for the best student paper prize went up by sampling considering every paper submitted by a student.

comments.issue: The abstract states gender bias as fact although the objective is to test for it.
comments.request: State it as potential gender bias in the abstract.
comments.quote: Abstract: Would suggest stating as *potential* gender bias, since the objective is to test for it.

comments.issue: 'This rises a new question' is ungrammatical and the wording could be clearer.
comments.request: Reword as suggested at the start of the introduction.
comments.quote: Perhaps reword as “This raises a new question: are early- and mid-career academic awards awarded equitably?”

comments.issue: Some sentences state possibilities as if they were demonstrated.
comments.request: Review wording to distinguish possibility from evidence.
comments.quote: I think it is important to write in a way that makes clear when something is possible vs. when there is evidence for it.

comments.issue: The circle figure is inaccessible to red-blind protanopia and green-blind deuteranopia readers.
comments.request: Use X's, checks and question marks instead of coloured circles.
comments.quote: The figure with the circles is not accessible to those with red-blind protanopia and green blind deuteranopia (two forms of color blindness) based on running through a simulator.

reviews.assessment: An important, forward-looking and readable study with useful guidelines, though the award scope and some methods details need work.
strengths: addresses an important yet neglected topic
forward looking and easy to read

comments.issue: Only research and publication grants are considered, omitting other grant types targeting other outputs or backgrounds.
comments.request: Analyse whether other grant types increased and whether their winners balance the biased main awards.
comments.quote: I am unclear as of why were only those grants that are given for Research and Publication considered.

comments.issue: War is not mentioned as a possible reason for a career break.
comments.request: Mention war as a career-break reason on page 4.
comments.quote: page 4, when discussing eligibility cut-off (in the Introduction) maybe mention as one reason for a career break a war

comments.issue: The last introduction paragraph could start with 'Our work'.
comments.request: Start the last introduction paragraph with 'Our work' or similar.
comments.quote: Last paragraph of the intro, suggest starting with ‘Our work’ or similar.

comments.issue: The pre-registration link requires authorisation and cannot be checked.
comments.request: Provide accessible pre-registration documentation.
comments.quote: I could not check the pre-registration as the link required authorisation of the access.

comments.issue: Search and screening details are only in the supplement and hard to evaluate.
comments.request: Move more search and screening information into the main file.
comments.quote: I suggest moving some more info on how the search and screening was conducted from the Supplement to the main file.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'regional' grants is unclear, including how large a region must be.
comments.request: Define what counts as a regional grant.
comments.quote: It is unclear what does it mean under ‘regional’ grants. How big does the region have to be to be considered a region.

comments.issue: Prize criteria may have changed over time, especially for awards dating from the 1980s.
comments.request: Check and account for historical changes in prize criteria.
comments.quote: How do we know that the Prize did not change its criteria over time over time (I see some are from 80ties).

comments.issue: The introduction does not justify why open science practices are increasingly important and scored.
comments.request: Add more on open science practices and their growing valuation by funders.
comments.quote: I would suggest including more on Open science practices in the Intro.

comments.issue: Some figures could be removed, combined or converted to tables.
comments.request: Consider moving Figures 3 and 5 to the supplement or presenting them as tables.
comments.quote: My feeling is that some figures could be removed to supplement if necessary, or presented within one figure.

comments.issue: It is unclear why geographical bias was assessed this way, when affiliation at award time would be easy to use.
comments.request: Assess geographical bias using awardees' affiliations at the time of winning.
comments.quote: I am unclear of why was geographical bias of awardees assessed? This would be easy to do based on the affiliation of the awardees at the time of winning the award.

comments.issue: The first sentence of the 'Award characteristics' discussion section is unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite the first sentence of the Award characteristics section.
comments.quote: I do not understand the first sentence of the section ‘Award characteristics’ (discussion)

comments.issue: The influence of including only English-language grants is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how the English-only selection may have influenced the results.
comments.quote: More discussion on how concentrating on English only grants could have influenced the results.

comments.issue: Presenting Figure 7 as steps implies a ranking of importance.
comments.request: Consider another representation for Figure 7.
comments.quote: I think it would work better if it was not presented as steps, as these evoke some kind of ranking of the importance of these different steps

title: Little transparency and equity in scientific awards for early- and mid-career researchers in ecology and evolution

study.system: yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae; ortholog replacement and growth assays

reviews.assessment: Interesting ortholog-swap study with implications, but the fast-evolution inference and higher-order epistasis claim need better support.
strengths: interesting study swapping orthologs from diverse organisms
implications for how essential orthologs evolve

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the selected genes are 1:1 orthologs or have duplicates, and no classification by protein interactions is provided.
comments.request: Clarify ortholog status and classify genes by whether they act alone or in protein-protein interactions.
comments.quote: Are the selected set of genes 1:1 orthologs or have duplicates in either lineage?

comments.issue: The gradual versus fast-type classification as slow and fast evolving is not explained and may rest only on complementation assays.
comments.request: Provide an independent estimate of evolutionary rate beyond complementation.
comments.quote: The assumption that genes belonging to gradual-type vs. fast-type are slow and fast evolving genes are not well explained.

comments.issue: The word change in essential genes can change quickly is undefined and may imply functional change without evidence.
comments.request: Define what change means and provide evidence for functional change.
comments.quote: It is unclear what the word "change" actually means. Does the "change" refer to change of function? If so, have the authors provided evidence?

comments.issue: In pairwise complementation it is unclear whether the co-expressed partner is an ortholog and the only known interactor.
comments.request: State whether co-expressed partners are orthologs and the only known interactors.
comments.quote: In the case of pair-wise complementation assays, is the co-expressed protein also an ortholog? And is the co-expressed protein the only interacting partner known based on biochemical assays?

comments.issue: Higher-order epistasis stabilising interactions is inferred solely from growth rate comparisons.
comments.request: Provide direct evidence for the higher-order epistasis mechanism.
comments.quote: The notion that higher order epistasis stabilizes interactions, enabling compatibility is solely based on the growth rate comparisons and seems farfetched.

reviews.assessment: Likes the clean experiments but considers the evolutionary pace concept misleading and the higher-order epistasis interpretation unclear.

comments.issue: The tempo of evolutionary incompatibility is misleading because scenarios are derived from single mutational events but presented as a linear timeline.
comments.request: Clarify the tempo concept and show that incompatibilities arise through different mechanisms in parallel.
comments.quote: I believe that the tempo of evolutionary incompatibility is a bit misleading as is.

comments.issue: APC11 orthologs may derive from different hybrid lineages, which would explain the incompatibilities without fast evolution.
comments.request: Check the hybrid-lineage origin of the APC11 orthologs.
comments.quote: I wonder in this case if the APC11 gene from N. cas is derived from the K. lac lineage, while the APC11 gene of S. cerevisiae is derived from the Z.rox lineage.

comments.issue: Mutations may simply fail to fold in some backbones rather than cause higher-order interaction defects.
comments.request: Show the specific additional interaction affected by the mutations.
comments.quote: Rather, it is possible that those mutations simply do not fold (or whatever) in some backbones. The authors would have to show the specific additional interaction being tweaked for their claim.

comments.issue: How higher-order epistasis accelerates evolution is undefined (sequence evolution or incompatibility emergence).
comments.request: Clarify what acceleration means and note that complexes often evolve slowly.
comments.quote: I'm also confused by how higher-order epistasis accelerates evolution. Maybe they need to clarify what the mean (sequence evolution? Incompatibility emergence?).

comments.issue: Viability on 5-FOA could reflect URA3 mutations rather than plasmid loss.
comments.request: Add doxycycline or another control to confirm rescue by the orthologous gene.
comments.quote: How do the authors confirm that viability on 5-FOA is by plasmid loss? Sometimes mutations in the URA3 marker also show this phenotype.

comments.issue: The electroporation protocol lists 200 W, which may be a typo for resistance.
comments.request: Correct or clarify the electroporation parameters.
comments.quote: The electroporation protocol is listed as 1.8 kV, 200 W, 20 uF. Is wattage actually the parameter controlled or is this a typo?

comments.issue: The essential gene list may contain mistakes, as MET4 is not essential.
comments.request: Verify the essential status of the genes used.
comments.quote: Did the authors verify that the genes they used are actually essential? The list of essential genes from the deletion collection is well known to have some mistakes (even in S288C).

comments.issue: How statistical significance for growth rates was established is unclear, causing confusion in Figure S3c.
comments.request: Clarify the statistical significance criteria.
comments.quote: The authors should probably clarify how they establish statistical significance for growth rate measurements.

reviews.assessment: Praises the technical achievement and mechanistic insight, but asks for a clearer intro question and more rigorous support for the higher-order epistasis claim.
strengths: dozens of transgenic allele replacement strains
insight into mechanisms of protein complex divergence

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a clear statement of the question of interest.
comments.request: State the question of interest clearly in the introduction.
comments.quote: The work could be improved by a clear statement in the intro about the question of interest, and by improvements to the rigor of the data interpretation in the molecular portion of the study.

comments.issue: Detailed replicate measurements and statistics are missing from the screening and rescue analyses (Figure 1, Table S1, Table S5).
comments.request: Report replicate measurements and statistics for these tables.
comments.quote: more detailed replicate measurements and statistics should be reported here

comments.issue: The higher-order epistasis interpretation goes beyond the data, assuming an interface mechanism not demonstrated.
comments.request: Quantify Apc2 affinities with other APC subunits or de-emphasise the higher-order epistasis claim.
comments.quote: However, the authors’ interpretation of this in my view goes beyond what is rigorously defensible

comments.issue: Supporting data for Figure 4 are not provided.
comments.request: Provide the supporting data for Figure 4.
comments.quote: The last section of the manuscript describes other incompatibilities in APC between yeast species (supporting data for Figure 4 should be provided)

title: Multiple intermolecular interactions facilitate rapid evolution of essential genes

study.system: forest restoration finance; semi-structured interviews with investors

reviews.assessment: Appropriate qualitative methods but findings largely coincide with existing literature; results need restructuring and deeper analysis for novelty.
strengths: methods appropriate, adequately described, with sufficient sample size
broad findings consistent with the literature

comments.issue: The broad findings coincide with the existing literature and are not innovative in themselves.
comments.request: Develop specific points in more depth to provide original insights.
comments.quote: The broad findings coincide with the existing literature on this topic and are not in themselves innovative

comments.issue: Three areas could yield more innovative insights: respondent-type differences, intrinsic versus financial motivations, and production versus offset areas.
comments.request: Analyse these three areas in more depth.
comments.quote: Areas that may provide more innovative insights with deeper analysis include (i) the differences in perspectives between the three principal types of respondents and the implications of these

comments.issue: The results sections are not consistently organized, with chunks of text in the wrong section and almost no material on practitioners.
comments.request: Restructure the results, e.g. by respondent group, and include practitioner perspectives.
comments.quote: if this is the case, various chunks of the text are in the wrong section

comments.issue: Incentive categories overlap and mix direct financial with intrinsic motivations, and the relationship between the two levels is not explored.
comments.request: Reorganize the categories and analyse the relationship between motivation levels.
