comments.quote: The categories of incentives in the first section are overlapping (the first two could also be presented as subcategories of three) and they include both direct financial incentives and deeper intrinsic motivations (mitigating climate change).

comments.issue: ROI is absent from the incentives section although it is the strongest incentive in the second section.
comments.request: Explain why ROI is not included in the first section.
comments.quote: I am not sure why ROI isn't including in this section, even though it comes through as the strongest incentive in the second section.

comments.issue: It is not stated what kinds of staff were interviewed from corporations.
comments.request: State the corporate staff roles interviewed.
comments.quote: The only added detail that I think is needed to the description of methods is to state what kinds of staff were interviewed from corporations.

comments.issue: Whether the same interview guide was used across respondent types is not stated explicitly.
comments.request: State whether the interview guide was the same for all respondent types.
comments.quote: I assume the same interview guide was used for the different types of respondents but it would be useful to state this explicitly.

comments.issue: The public policy and green finance section focuses on financial incentives only, which conflicts with the earlier mix of financial and non-financial motivations.
comments.request: Reconcile and nuance this section, e.g. noting agroforestry combines food and income production.
comments.quote: The section on public policies and green finance focuses almost entirely on the need for financial support and incentives, which is difficult to reconcile with earlier statements about the mix of financial and non-financial incentives.

comments.issue: The conclusion about expanding markets ignores that carbon markets provide no return beyond rising share prices.
comments.request: Discuss whether markets can really be expanded given this limitation.
comments.quote: The conclusion that new, expanded markets need to be developed needs to be discussed in relation to the fact carbon markets and similar trading schemes do not provide a return other than as a result of rising share prices

comments.issue: The ethical statement is incomplete: the review board name and consent, confidentiality and data protection measures are missing.
comments.request: Provide the full ethical review board name and the measures for consent, confidentiality and data protection.
comments.quote: Finally, a more detailed statement of ethical practice is needed, including the full name of the ethical review board that approved the study and what measures were put in place in relation to consent, confidentiality and data protection.

reviews.assessment: Great read and enjoyable paper; main critique is that the three proposed interventions need a more nuanced, expanded discussion of pitfalls.
strengths: great example quotes and interesting insights

comments.issue: The definition of 'corporation' should appear at first use for non-specialist readers.
comments.request: Move the corporation definition up to its first mention.
comments.quote: Perhaps it would be useful to move your definition/description of what a 'corporation' is to up here, when you first use the term

comments.issue: The rationale for distinguishing corporates from asset managers is not explained.
comments.request: Add a sentence on why the two groups are distinguished.
comments.quote: could you add a sentence about why you chose to make the distinction between corporates & asset managers?

comments.issue: FLR is not written out in full in Table 1.
comments.request: Write out FLR in the Actor column.
comments.quote: could you write out in full what “FLR” stands for in the “Actor” column of the “Agroforesty initiative”?

comments.issue: The supplementary quote table is under-used and its sections are not labelled for citation.
comments.request: Refer to the example quotes more and label the table sections.
comments.quote: I think there's an opportunity to refer more heavily to the table/those quotes in these paragraphs here to support your points

comments.issue: It is unclear whether capability barriers, such as the environmental-financial background gap, were acknowledged.
comments.request: Discuss capability barriers among asset managers if supported by interviews.
comments.quote: I would be interested to know whether any capability barriers were acknowledged when discussing asset managers & the “lack of standardisation and knowledge”

comments.issue: The discussion of the three interventions lacks nuance about potential pitfalls and the need for scientific and regulatory safeguards.
comments.request: Expand the interventions section with measured statements on pitfalls and safeguards.
comments.quote: I do strongly feel that this section needs to take a more nuanced, expanded view to ensure that the suggestions you are making are firmly worded

comments.issue: The meaning of the different arrow colours in Figure 1 is not described.
comments.request: Describe the arrow colours in the Figure 1 caption.
comments.quote: In the figure caption for Figure 1 could you describe what the different colours of the arrows mean, especially since you don't use coloured arrows in Figure 2?

comments.issue: The figures are not referred to in the text.
comments.request: Cite the figures in the text to ground them.
comments.quote: It would be good to refer to the figures in-text to ground them a bit more. At the moment they just pop out of nowhere.

comments.issue: The final paragraph lacks a sentence on why corporations and asset managers differ.
comments.request: Add a sentence explaining the difference between the two private sector classes.
comments.quote: it would be good to have a sentence about why these two classes of the private sector are different (as when you introduce them at the beginning)

comments.issue: Software references for Otter and NVivo are missing.
comments.request: Provide software references for Otter and NVivo.
comments.quote: Please provide software references for Otter & NVivo.

comments.issue: Bias-accounting details in the Reporting Summary could be useful to readers.
comments.request: Consider including some bias-accounting details from the Reporting Summary.
comments.quote: you have some really neat details in the Reporting Summary about the way you accounted for bias that could be interesting for the reader

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits: 'Principles for Responsible Investment' plural, 'recognised', a missing colon, 'too low an ROI', and a missing 'b' in 'timber'.
comments.quote: No "s" at the end of "Principles for Responsible Investment"

reviews.assessment: Timely, novel and clearly written; asks for more background on actors and a substantially expanded barriers-reduction section.
strengths: timely, novel and clearly written manuscript

comments.issue: The goals, objectives and operating constraints of each actor type are not described for non-specialist readers.
comments.request: Add enough detail on asset manager, NGO and corporate motivations.
comments.quote: additional description of the actors goals, objectives, and operating constraints would be useful because the audience of this paper may not know what objectives an asset manager is pursuing

comments.issue: Public goods are not defined or contrasted with private goods.
comments.request: Define public goods and contrast them with private goods.
comments.quote: Public goods should be defined and contrasted with private goods to help readers understand why the provision of public goods poses a challenge for financing restoration with private funding.

comments.issue: The section on actions to reduce barriers is too brief, does not explain how green bonds work, and gives no guidance on engaging governments or creating markets.
comments.request: Expand the section with concrete guidance on instruments and government engagement.
comments.quote: The section describing actions to reduce barriers should be expanded. I found the discussion to be be too brief and lacking in detail.

title: Incentives and barriers to private finance for forest and landscape restoration

study.system: Castle Bank, Wales; Middle Ordovician soft-bodied fauna

editor_summary: Editor rejects: reviewers are enthusiastic about the deposit but unanimous that imaging quality cannot support the interpretations; open to reconsideration if imaging improves.

reviews.assessment: Exceptional deposit that showcases well, with three major points on preservation, SEM-EDS reporting and locality data plus many minor suggestions.

comments.issue: Preservation at lines 202-206 differs from other Ordovician BST deposits and deserves expansion.
comments.request: Expand the discussion of the unusual preservation.
comments.quote: it would be great if the authors to expand on this, as the preservation is remarkedly different than in most other Ordovician BST deposits, but similar to many Cambrian ones

comments.issue: SEM-EDS methods give only instruments, not operating parameters or hosting facilities.
comments.request: Report SEM-EDS operating conditions and instrument facilities.
comments.quote: The information for the SEM-EDS analyses only mentions the instruments and is missing the parameters that were used to analyse specimens.

comments.issue: Locality information is extremely vague and inconsistent between text and Extended Data caption.
comments.request: Include more locality information despite the landowner request.
comments.quote: The locality information in the paper is extremely vague. It says 'The site is located near Llandrindod, central Wales, UK' in the main text and 'Builth Inlier, Wales, UK' in the Extended Data figure caption.

comments.issue: Early sediment cementation is still debated and should be acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge the debate over early sediment cementation.
comments.quote: While peculiarities of ocean chemistry are very likely part of the preservation pathway, the early sediment cementation is still debated.

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits and sentence splits.
comments.quote: I would break the sentence into two if possible, as it is a lot of information in one sentence.

comments.issue: Graptolite and lithostratigraphic identifications lack a reference or figured specimen.
comments.request: Add a reference or figure Didymograptus murchisoni.
comments.quote: Is there a reference for the graptolites and lithostrat or could you figure a specimen of Didymograptus murchisoni?

comments.issue: It is not stated whether the ash layers have been dated.
comments.request: State whether the ash layers have been dated.
comments.quote: Line 68: Has someone dated the ash layers?

comments.issue: Outcrop and bed photographs are not shown.
comments.request: Add outcrop pictures, e.g. in Extended Data Figure 1.
comments.quote: Could you show some of the beds and maybe outcrop pictures in the Extended Data Figs?

comments.issue: The basis for saying the deposit is not metamorphosed or deeply weathered is not given.
comments.request: Explain the basis for the non-metamorphosed claim.
comments.quote: What are you basing this observation on?

comments.issue: Lines 78-80 belong in the methods section.
comments.request: Move the lines 78-80 content to the methods.
comments.quote: This feels like it belongs in the methods section rather than here.

comments.issue: Carapaces with posterior spines and complex forms are not figured.
comments.request: Figure one or more of these specimens.
comments.quote: Could you figure one or more specimens of the: 'carapaces with at least a posterior spine, and other, more complex forms.'

comments.issue: Sponges in other BST deposits are locally abundant in a few beds, not throughout.
comments.request: Soften the sponge abundance generalisation.
comments.quote: In many BST deposits sponges are locally abundant, usually only in a couple of beds, not throughout the deposit.

comments.issue: Scavenging rather than transport could explain the remains.
comments.request: Consider scavenging as an alternative to transport.
comments.quote: Could it be that instead or on top of transportation, that we are looking at scavenging remains?

comments.issue: It is unclear which animals 'worms' refers to.
comments.request: Clarify whether worms means palaeoscoleids or other vermiform animals.
comments.quote: Does 'worms' refer to palaeoscoleids or other vermiform animals?

comments.issue: The slug-like animal with radula could be a halkieriid, Armilimax-like or Calvapilosa-like rather than new.
comments.request: Clarify the affinity of the slug-like animal.
comments.quote: Is it a Halkieriid, something similar to Armilimax or Calvapilosa, or something new?

comments.issue: The graptolite abundance statement is ambiguous about locality within the formation.
comments.request: Rephrase the graptolite abundance sentence.
comments.quote: You mention in line 65 and line 158 that graptolites are abundant, is that in other parts of the formation, or here. I would recommend to rephrase this sentence.

comments.issue: The Extended Data Fig. 5d specimen is not a convincing Margaretia-like tube.
comments.request: Consider not mentioning the Margaretia-like tube.
comments.quote: the specimen in Extended Data Fig. 5d is not a very convincing Margaretia-like tube

comments.issue: Extended Data Fig. 6c resembles Herpetogaster more than Siphusauctum.
comments.request: Reconsider the affinity of the Extended Data Fig. 6c specimen.
comments.quote: Extended Data Fig. 6c reminds me more of Herpetogaster than Siphusauctum, but Fig. 3c has some similarities.

comments.issue: No close-ups of the microscopic fossils are provided.
comments.request: Add one or two close-ups of the microscopic fossils.
comments.quote: Could you add a close-up or two of the microscopic fossils?

comments.issue: Fossil levels are not indicated on the stratigraphic column.
comments.request: Indicate fossil levels on the stratigraphic column and caption.
comments.quote: Could you indicate the levels on the stratigraphic column and add information in the figure caption from which level the fossils come?

comments.issue: No species-level list is available for palaeoecological comparisons.
comments.request: Add a species list table to the supplement.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to add a table with a species list to the supplement

comments.issue: Kimmig et al. 2019, which lists Ordovician Konservat-Lagerstatten, is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Kimmig et al. 2019.
comments.quote: it might be worth citing Kimmig et al 2019, as it has all of the Ordovician Konservat-Lagerstätten listed in it

comments.issue: Other systematic biases in preservation and sampling are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge other systematic biases and cite Whitaker and Kimmig 2020.
comments.quote: there are several other systematic biases that can be introduced, and have been introduced (see Whitaker and Kimmig 2020 Pal Elec)

comments.issue: A mix of buried-alive and recently dead animals is more likely than a single preservation pathway.
comments.request: Consider exposure time and mixed death assemblages.
comments.quote: They might have been exposed for a couple of days to have the level of preservation that is shown, you are likely looking at a mix of buried alive and recently dead animals

comments.issue: The wiwaxiid mention at line 219 repeats earlier text.
comments.request: Remove the repeated wiwaxiid mention.
comments.quote: You mention that wiwaxiids have been mentioned from the Valongo Fm before earlier, maybe remove the mention here.

comments.issue: Brachiopods and other shelly taxa are systematically under-collected in Laurentian BST deposits.
comments.request: Treat the shelly taxon pattern with caution and cite Whitaker and Kimmig 2020.
comments.quote: Brachiopods, and other shelly taxa have been systematically under collected in most Laurentian Cambrian BST deposits

comments.issue: The abundance of benthic organisms argues against a major role for transport.
comments.request: Reconsider the importance of transport.
comments.quote: Due to the relatively large amount of benthic organisms in the deposit, I am not convinced transport played a major role.

comments.issue: A boom-bust or palaeonursery setting is an unexplored alternative.
comments.request: Consider boom-bust or palaeonursery evidence.
comments.quote: Is there any evidence that we might be dealing with a boom and bust or paleonursery, similar to the Haiyan Lagerstätte (Yang et al. 2021)?

comments.issue: Some specimen photographs lack contrast and appear blurry.
comments.request: Improve photograph contrast, possibly using diluted alcohol.
comments.quote: Some of the pictures need contrast improvement, as it can be hard to see parts of the fossil and some specimens appear a bit blurry.

comments.issue: Many figure panels have missing or duplicate scale bars, unlettered insets or excessive matrix.
comments.request: Fix scale bars, labels and cropping across the figure panels.
comments.quote: Extended Data Figure 6b and 6d: Inset has no letter and no scale bar

comments.issue: It is unclear whether phosphate is absent from the palaeoscolecid plates.
comments.request: Address the phosphate question in Extended Data Figure 10.
comments.quote: Extended Data Figure 10: Is there no phosphate in the palaeoscolicid plates?

reviews.assessment: Recommends rejection: the well-written paper's interpretations are not confidently verified by the illustrations, and taphonomic influences are not evaluated.
strengths: some important fossils with definitive morphologies

comments.issue: Illustrations do not confidently verify several identifications, a significant limitation.
comments.request: Provide considerably more documentation of the interpretations.
comments.quote: in several cases the illustrations do not confidently verify the identifications made, and this provides a significant limitation to the paper

comments.issue: The xiphosuran interpretation of Fig. 1a-c is not proven by the photographs.
comments.request: Provide better documentation or temper the xiphosuran claim.
comments.quote: I find the assertion that this is a xiphosauran to be possible but not proven.

comments.issue: Definitive opabiniid and cephalocarid identifications rest on few photographs of single specimens.
comments.request: Temper the opabiniid and cephalocarid claims or add documentation.
comments.quote: Stating 1g to be a definitive opabiniid and 1h to be a definitive cephalocarid on the basis of these few photographs of one specimen of each is, in my view, too bold a claim

comments.issue: Large grain sizes mean compaction and diagenesis likely distorted soft tissues and obscured details.
comments.request: Assess the influence of grain size and diagenesis on the features.
comments.quote: Part of the problem is that the grain sizes of the surrounding minerals are so large that re-arrangements among grains of any kind (compaction, diagenesis etc.) would likely distort and deform the soft tissues obscuring key details.

comments.issue: The evidence presented is insufficient for the confidence expressed in the manuscript.
comments.request: Reduce the confidence of interpretations or add evidence.
comments.quote: I am not saying that the interpretations are wrong or without justification – rather I am saying that the evidence presented here is insufficient to establish the case with the degree of confidence expressed in the MS.

comments.issue: No strategy or counts are given for excluding taphonomic influence on features.
comments.request: Document how taphonomy was excluded and how often structures were preserved.
comments.quote: I would like to know the general strategy by which the influence of taphonomy was excluded, information on how many times a structure was preserved in different specimens before it was accepted as original.

comments.issue: The proportion of collected specimens well enough preserved to assign is unknown.
comments.request: Report what proportion of specimens can be assigned to a recognized form.
comments.quote: I wonder how what proportion of the total number of specimens collected are sufficiently well preserved to be assigned to a recognized form of any kind?

comments.issue: General conclusions are published before almost any descriptive work on the fauna.
comments.request: Publish detailed descriptive studies before a general overview.
comments.quote: Here the authors seem to be seeking to publish general conclusions about the fauna before almost any of the descriptive work is published.

reviews.assessment: Largely well written with interesting finds, but critical concern about overinterpretation of fossils and the true scale of biological fidelity.
strengths: Castle Bank placement in geologic time of note

comments.issue: Line-level edits: extra comma before citations and 'micron-scale' wording.
comments.quote: Line 39: There is an extra comma before the reference citations

comments.issue: BST preservation is described as a single consistent phenomenon rather than a suite of variable phenomena.
comments.request: Rephrase to say the phenomena responsible for BST preservation are not fully understood.
comments.quote: I would argue that it is not one single, consistent phenomenon responsible for BST preservation, but rather a suite of probably variable phenomena.

comments.issue: The Gaines cementation model has irregularities and alternative sediment chemistry references are omitted.
comments.request: Rephrase and add Orr 1998, Ross Anderson 2018 or Butterfield 2012.
comments.quote: there are numerous irregularities of the Gaines early carbonate cementation model as cited here, perhaps suggesting that it isn't the most uniformly applicable model

comments.issue: The graptolite-based age is not cross-checked radiometrically.
comments.request: Cross-check the age with radiometry of the ash laminae.
comments.quote: could/should this be confirmed or cross-checked with radiometry of the ash laminae/tuffs in the section?

comments.issue: Whether preservation relates to event deposition or ash fall is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the role of event deposition and ash fall in preservation.
comments.quote: is the preservation herein in any way related to the event deposition and/or frequent ash fall?

comments.issue: Transport is first mentioned late instead of in the geologic setting.
comments.request: State transport directly earlier, in the geologic setting.
comments.quote: This appears to be the first mention of transport to the depositional setting, though it could be inferred as these represent event beds. I think this should be directly stated earlier

comments.issue: The polygonal prosoma sculpture is very hard to see and may be a photo-resolution artifact.
comments.request: Provide a higher-resolution image of the polygonal sculpture.
comments.quote: I find it exceedingly difficult to observe the polygonal sculpture on the prosoma. This may be an artifact of the photo resolution as included in the pdf

comments.issue: The colours in Fig. 1e are not explained in the caption.
comments.request: Explain the colours in the Fig. 1e caption.
comments.quote: Fig. 1e: What do these colors mean? Not noted in the caption.

comments.issue: The higher magnification insets in Fig. 1f and g add little.
comments.request: Improve or remove the low-value insets.
comments.quote: The higher magnification insets do very little (perhaps only at this figure resolution) to contribute to the understanding of these fossils.

comments.issue: High reflectivity obscures features in Fig. 1h and Fig. 2c.
comments.request: Re-photograph these specimens to reduce reflectivity.
comments.quote: There is very high reflectivity in the host rock matrix on this photo that renders it quite difficult to see the features as drawn in Fig. 1i.

comments.issue: The scale of biological fidelity is questionable and small features such as chaetal bundles may be overinterpreted.
comments.request: Clarify imaging methods and demonstrate that small features are not overinterpreted.
comments.quote: Could, then, any smaller features, such as the chaetal bundles in 2i for example (which I cannot make-out, even with the arrows for guides), be overinterpreted?

comments.issue: The Fig. 3b inset is barely larger than the original.
comments.request: Enlarge the Fig. 3b inset or remove it.
comments.quote: The magnified insets do show a bit more detail here as compared to those in Fig. 1, but I note that the inset in 3b is not really much larger than shown originally

comments.issue: Neural tissue is drawn in Fig. 4g although overall preservation is poor.
comments.request: Justify how neural tissue could be preserved in this specimen.
comments.quote: I can very faintly see the features drawn here, although the overall preservation of the organism is quite bad, which begs the question as to how neural tissue could be preserved.

comments.issue: Well-preserved fossils are relegated to the supplement.
comments.request: Move at least one or two well-preserved specimens into the main text.
comments.quote: Some very well-preserved fossils are relegated to the supplement, and perhaps should be in the main text!

comments.issue: Photography conditions such as cross-polarized light are not reported.
comments.request: Note the conditions under which specimens were photographed.
comments.quote: Please also note any other information necessary to interpret the conditions of these photographs. E.g., cross-polarized light in any cases?

title: A Middle Ordovician Burgess Shale-type fauna from Castle Bank, Wales (UK)

study.system: tomato phyllosphere; Pseudomonas experimental evolution and competition

editor_summary: Reviewers generally supportive; additional data to demonstrate genetic change are welcome but not required for publication.

reviews.assessment: Elegant, clear and succinct study with compelling conclusions; only minor clarifications are requested.
strengths: novel niche expansion result with broad implications

comments.issue: The 'early colonizer' characterization of Pa. dispersa is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the basis for calling it an early colonizer.
comments.quote: Did the authors conduct a preliminary experiment to access colonization over time? Or does this characterization come from other research?

comments.issue: The life-cycle and spatial-localization differences between the strains are not described or referenced.
comments.request: Describe or reference these spatial differences.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to know what these differences are or at least include a reference so readers can look this up

comments.issue: Plant performance per treatment was not reported in the initial experiment.
comments.request: Report plant growth and disease prevalence per treatment.
comments.quote: it would be informative (to me at least) to know how plants fared in each treatment as well

comments.issue: A figure reference is missing at the end of the sentence at lines 85-87.
comments.request: Add the figure reference.
comments.quote: Line 85-87 - Fig reference should be added to end of sentence

comments.issue: Whether cross-contamination actually occurred at line 244 is not stated.
comments.request: State explicitly whether cross-contamination occurred.
comments.quote: it was mentioned that cross-contamination was monitored but whether or not cross-contamination occurred was not explicitly stated

comments.issue: The y-axis titles in Fig. 1C&D and Fig. S4 suggest Pa. dispersa colonization rather than competitor invasion.
comments.request: Switch or clarify the y-axis titles.
comments.quote: I think my confusion comes from the axis titles “Pa disp invasion resistance” - which made me think I was looking at Pa. disp colonization ability rather than the competitor’s ability to invade when Pa. disp was added first.

reviews.assessment: Interesting finding, but the evolutionary interpretation is circumstantial and the paper's fit for a general audience is uncertain.
strengths: interesting and generally relevant main finding
broadens the scope of eco-evolutionary priority effects

comments.issue: Ancestral-versus-evolved differences may reflect non-evolutionary plasticity rather than genetic change.
comments.request: Provide genetic or other evidence that evolution occurred.
comments.quote: without genetic data and/or some other evidence for evolutionary changes as opposed to non-genetic plastic changes, we cannot be very certain if evolution actually happened

comments.issue: The niche shift may not be the true cause of priority-effect changes; other changes such as chemical alteration could explain them.
comments.request: Rule out alternative causes of the priority-effect changes.
comments.quote: Is the niche shift really the reason for changes in the strength of priority effects, or could there be some other changes, e.g., chemical alteration of the phyllosphere, that might explain the changes in priority effects?

comments.issue: No control experiment kept Ps. syringae always present during the cultivation.
comments.request: Run the suggested control or engineering experiments.
comments.quote: evidence that would strengthen the conclusion could have come from conducting the six-week cultivation the same way as it was done in the study, except with P. syringae always present

comments.issue: The paper is written for microbiome researchers and does not engage the general ecology and evolution audience.
comments.request: Frame a knowledge gap relevant to general ecology.
comments.quote: the whole paper, especially the motivation and significance of the work explained in the first three paragraphs of the main text, is written mostly for microbiome researchers. It does not reach out to the general ecology and evolution audience.

comments.issue: The abstract conclusion sentence is too vague.
comments.request: Rephrase as suggested, e.g. 'resident species appear to have shifted to a new niche'.
comments.quote: I found the following sentence a bit too vague: "yet we conclude that host habitats can offer alternative evolutionary opportunities, complicating the application of existing theory to the community ecology of microbiomes."

comments.issue: The claim that the majority of taxa are culturable is unsupported.
comments.request: Demonstrate the culturability claim with data or references.
comments.quote: Is it really true? If true, I think that this observation should be demonstrated (present data or cite references that present data) rather than just claimed.

comments.issue: Selection pressure from Ps. syringae is not considered as a reason the ancestral strain is not endophytic.
comments.request: Consider Ps. syringae pressure as an additional explanation.
comments.quote: I wonder if the pressure from Ps. syringae itself may be another reason, particularly if Pa. dispersa encounters Ps. syringae frequently enough for Ps. syringae to exert strong selective pressure.

comments.issue: Equal competitive ability does not guarantee the antibiotic-resistant strain is otherwise identical.
comments.request: Address or explain the potential trait differences of the resistant strain.
comments.quote: equal competitive ability as measured here may not necessarily guarantee that the strains have all identical traits other than antibiotic resistance, complicating interpretation of results

title: Within-host adaptation alters priority effects within the tomato phyllosphere microbiome

study.system: green algae; multicellular group formation experiments and lake surveys

editor_summary: Editor invites a revision addressing all reviewer comments and editorial points before a final decision on publication.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset but the paper is descriptive, correlational and vague about mechanisms, so the advance is not fully convincing.
strengths: large-scale effort to characterize uni- to multicellular transitions

comments.issue: The study is not seen as a sufficiently important advance for the community.
comments.request: Clarify and strengthen the conceptual advance of the study.
comments.quote: I am not convinced it provides a sufficiently important advance to the community

comments.issue: Conclusions rest on correlations, and the cell biology and mechanisms of group formation are not analysed.
comments.request: Provide causal or mechanistic analyses of group formation rather than only correlations.
comments.quote: the conclusions are based on (admittingly highly replicated/large datasets) correlations rather than causality

comments.issue: The link between palmelloids and multicellular groups is unclear, including their origin, composition and relationship.
comments.request: Explain what palmelloids are, how they originate and how they relate to multicellular groups.
comments.quote: I could not understand the link between palmelloids and multicellular groups

comments.issue: The main conclusions in several sections are very vague.
comments.request: Make the conclusions concrete and informative.
comments.quote: The main conclusions in several sections in the paper are very vague

comments.issue: It is unclear how growth rate is distinguished from predation, since reduced cell numbers could reflect predation rather than slower growth.
comments.request: Distinguish predation losses from growth-rate effects.
comments.quote: how do you know that reduced number of cells are not the result of predation

comments.issue: The claims that palmelloids have higher fitness and that ECM drives increased fitness are speculative and unsupported by results.
comments.request: Show the fitness evidence for palmelloids and ECM or temper these claims.
comments.quote: Where are the results showing that there is higher fitness in palmelloids and where is the evidence that ECM is the driver of the increased fitness? This is very speculative.

comments.issue: The data supporting the statement that multicellular group formation occurred in 91% of strains are not identified.
comments.request: Point to the data supporting the 91% statement.
comments.quote: where is the data supporting this statement? In supplemental table?

comments.issue: The last introduction paragraph does not align with the results section and references tables too early.
comments.request: Reorganize the introduction's closing and table references.
comments.quote: Last paragraph of introduction explains how the paper is organized but this is uncoupled with the results section. It is weird to have reference to Tables in the end of introduction.

comments.issue: The dataset used in the first results sentence is unclear.
comments.request: State which dataset the first results sentence refers to.
comments.quote: In the first sentence in the results section, it is unclear what dataset was used.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether multicellular groups in Supplementary Table 4 mean more than four cells, excluding palmelloids.
comments.request: Define multicellular groups versus palmelloids in the tables.
comments.quote: when you mention multicellular groups you mean more than four cells (so not palmelloids)?

comments.issue: The bimodal distribution of predator growth rate in Figure 2 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the bimodal predator growth rate distribution.
comments.quote: Figure 2 - How do the authos explain the bimodal distribution of predator growth rate?

comments.issue: The premise for expecting that strains with more multicellular groups reduce predator growth is not given.
comments.request: State the premises behind this prediction.
comments.quote: “We also examined if strains with a higher prevalence of multicellular groups reduced the growth of predators.” – what are the premises to expect this???

comments.issue: No results relate to obligate multicellularity, and facultative versus obligate species are not identified.
comments.request: Clarify obligate versus facultative multicellularity and where the relevant results are.
comments.quote: I don’t see any result related to “obligate multicellularity” and which species are facultative or obligate multicellular in your experiment?

comments.issue: The link between ECM, palmelloid persistence and nitrogen availability is based only on correlations.
comments.request: Present causal evidence or temper the ECM-nitrogen link.
comments.quote: The link between ECM, palmilloid persistence and nitrogen availability put forward by the paper is is based on correlations, no causal links are presented unless I missed it.

comments.issue: Three typographical errors: a figure title, a table legend and the abstract.
comments.quote: Extended figure 3 – typo in title

comments.issue: The larger turbulence and nitrate effects are only referenced in a supplementary table.
comments.request: Show the turbulence and nitrate effects in a figure.
comments.quote: why not show this in a figure? (reference only to a supplemental table)

comments.issue: Legends of supplementary tables are incomplete, e.g. SGR is undefined in Table S1.
comments.request: Complete the supplementary table legends and define abbreviations.
comments.quote: Legends of supplemental tables are incomplete. For example what does “SGR” mean in Table S1?

reviews.assessment: Clear writing, rigorous experiments and cautious interpretation, with requests to improve the clarity of statistics and supplementary tables.
strengths: impressive experimental design with many strains and conditions

comments.issue: The distinction between plastic and evolved changes could be clearer throughout.
comments.request: State clearly which changes are plastic and which are evolved.
comments.quote: I feel that the distinction between plastic and evolved changes could have been clearer.

comments.issue: Supplementary tables look like raw statistics output, with unexplained tests, undefined headings and unspelled abbreviations.
comments.request: Make the supplementary tables publication-ready with explained tests and defined terms.
comments.quote: The supplementary tables need much more explanation. These look like raw output of statistics software, not publication-ready tables.

comments.issue: The reported statistics, such as posterior mode, are opaque and their meaning is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what the reported statistics mean.
comments.quote: I found the statistics reported in the manuscript opaque. I don’t know what a posterior mode of 32.3 means.

comments.issue: Key methods information appears too late in the paper.
comments.request: Move some methods information, especially the experimental design, earlier.
comments.quote: I would suggest moving some of the information in the Methods earlier in the paper.

reviews.assessment: A tour-de-force analysis with well-done experiments, clear results and adequate interpretations, needing only very minor comments.

comments.issue: The title does not specify the taxonomic group.
comments.request: Add 'in green algae' to the title.
comments.quote: Because the work is specific to this taxonomic group, I propose "Single cell adaptations shape evolutionary transitions to multicellularity in green algae" or something similar.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the apparent lack of benefits at Line 151 refers to this or other studies.
comments.request: Clarify the source of the apparent lack of benefits.
comments.quote: I am not sure what they mean here. From this study? From other studies?

comments.issue: The gene co-option statement at Line 153 should clarify that this was shown in green algae.
comments.request: Clarify that the co-option evidence comes from green algae.
comments.quote: I think this has been shown in green algae. This should be clarified..

comments.issue: The multicellular group formation statement at Line 237 is not restricted to green algae.
comments.request: Specify that the work concerns green algae, while allowing speculation about other taxa.
comments.quote: The authors can hypothesize or discuss whether this may also be relevant to other multicellular acquisitions, but their work is limited to green algae.

comments.issue: 'Bacterial symbioses' at Line 270 mislabels the cited work on bacterial interactions.
comments.request: Use 'bacterial interactions' instead of symbiosis.
comments.quote: The work cited is about “bacterial interactions”. I propose using that instead of symbiosis.

title: Single-cell adaptations shape evolutionary transitions to multicellularity in green algae

study.system: GBIF species records; voucher vs observation coverage, global

reviews.assessment: Finds the global comparison of voucher and observation biases valuable but raises circularity and data-gap queries plus several clarifications.
strengths: more global and taxonomically diverse than previous work
first comparison of voucher and observation record biases
results relevant for using species records in ecological studies

comments.issue: Expected range maps based on expert opinion may be circular and biased, making comparisons against them non-robust.
comments.request: Discuss the circularity and biases of expected range maps, potentially in the supplement.
comments.quote: My concern is that if expected range maps are biased, and are not consistently an over-estimate of species distributions (i.e. they include omission as well as commission errors), then a comparison against them would not be robust.

comments.issue: Spatial data gaps in Figure 1 are unexplained; cells with no data should have index values.
comments.request: Explain how data were used and why some cells have no data.
comments.quote: I was surprised to see spatial data gaps in the maps in Figure 1. I suspect this reflects my lack of understanding of exactly how data were used, and it would be helpful for this to be clarified.

comments.issue: The sentence at L98-99 about >10% of species does not address gaps in taxonomic coverage.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence to clarify the meaning.
comments.quote: This sentence doesn’t make sense to me. >10% of species represented by at least one record doesn’t say anything about gaps in taxonomic coverage

comments.issue: The claim that vouchers have higher temporal coverage for most species is contradicted by the reported median intervals.
comments.request: Reword the statement to match the data.
comments.quote: The data therefore do not appear to support the statement that voucher records showed higher temporal coverage than observation records for most species, and so the text needs rewording.

comments.issue: The Figure 5 interpretation suggests more consistent patterns than the data show.
comments.request: Revisit the Figure 5 interpretation.
comments.quote: I’m not entirely convinced by the interpretation of Figure 5; I felt like the summary conclusions in the text suggested more consistent patterns that I can see in the data.

comments.issue: The direction of the explanatory variable scales in Figure 5 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the scales of wilderness and airport proximity variables.
comments.quote: The scales of explanatory variables need to be explained, i.e. does a higher score for wilderness mean that the area is more remote, and does a higher score for proximity to airports mean closer to airports?

comments.issue: Table S4 only presents taxonomic coverage models, not geographic and temporal coverage results.
comments.request: Present the geographic and temporal coverage model results.
comments.quote: Only the model results for taxonomic coverage of grid cells are presented in Table S4; what about the geographic and temporal coverage result?

comments.issue: The source of the wilderness data is missing.
comments.request: Provide the source of the wilderness data.
comments.quote: Table S5: The source of wilderness data is missing.

comments.issue: The discussion does not emphasise how to address the identified biases in ecological practice.
comments.request: Expand the discussion on addressing biases and the relevance for ecological studies.
comments.quote: a greater emphasis in the discussion on how to address the issues identified (i.e. biases in observation records, and a shift away from collecting the more representative voucher records)

reviews.assessment: Ambitious and novel global assessment, but methodological circularity, temporal coverage and trait choices undermine the ability to draw convincing conclusions.
strengths: global assessment of coverage and socioeconomic factors interesting and novel

comments.issue: Expected patterns may have been informed by the same GBIF data, creating circularity.
comments.request: Comment on potential circularities in using expected patterns derived from these sources.
comments.quote: We question to what extent the expected patterns have been informed by the GBIF data used in this study? Can the authors comment on whether there are potential circularities in the reasoning here?

comments.issue: Methods lack justification and detail, so the analyses cannot be reproduced; taxa, trait, data-deficient and phylogenetic index choices are unexplained.
comments.request: Describe and justify the methods fully, possibly in supporting information.
comments.quote: Many of the decisions taken in the methods section require full justification and the methodological description requires further details. We do not feel that we would be able to reproduce these analyses on the basis of the methods as described

comments.issue: Voucher and observation datasets are often similar, so the title's message of failure to represent patterns needs more nuance.
comments.request: Add nuance and assess whether record-type differences support the claim.
comments.quote: both datasets are not so different (I.e. the lambda and Moran’s I values in Figure 1 and 2 are closer to each other than they are to 0 or 1). More nuance is required in the discussion

comments.issue: The Results and Discussion lack in-depth explanation of why coverage patterns appeared and their implications.
comments.request: Expand the recommendations into a full paragraph and discuss implications.
comments.quote: The Results and Discussion section of the article would benefit from a more in-depth description of why the observed patterns in coverage appeared and their implications for future studies.

comments.issue: Observation records are equated with citizen science although many come from professional field studies.
comments.request: Distinguish citizen science from professional observation records and note spatial-temporal variation.
comments.quote: The authors equate observation records with records obtained through citizen science projects. However, many (albeit a minority of) observation records available in GBIF are the product of field studies carried out by professional scientists and researchers.

comments.issue: Temporal coverage starting in the 1700s overestimates bias for occurrence records that only became abundant after 1970.
comments.request: Limit the temporal analyses to 1950 to present.
comments.quote: Therefore, the approach used to calculate temporal coverage (with a starting point in the 1700s) does not account for the fact that large-scale collections of occurrence records did not begin until after 1970s and yields prevalent gaps for occurrence records.

comments.issue: Median intervals per species likely come from skewed data.
comments.request: Provide 25/75% quartiles for the intervals.
comments.quote: Given the distribution of records over time, the median intervals of records per species (L147-149) are likely to be derived from very skewed data – can you provide 25/75% quartiles for these too?

comments.issue: Present-day socioeconomic values are related to records dating back to 1700, which may be inaccurate.
comments.request: Match socioeconomic data temporally to the records or discuss the mismatch.
comments.quote: Are the values for the socioeconomic factors derived from present day data? If so, since the occurrence records used in the study can date back to 1700, the relationship between record coverage and socioeconomic factors may be inaccurate.

comments.issue: Co-variation among socioeconomic factors is not reported.
comments.request: Report co-variation between socioeconomic factors.
comments.quote: Is there any co-variation between the socioeconomic factors used in the analyses?

comments.issue: Trait coverage choices are inconsistent: no mammal diet, and butterfly flight period is missing.
comments.request: Include mammal diet and butterfly flight period as traits.
comments.quote: Why was diet type included for birds, but not mammals (we would like to have seen mammal diet included as a trait too).

comments.issue: Extinction risk is not technically a species trait.
comments.request: Reconsider the classification of extinction risk as a trait.
comments.quote: We understand the motivation for including extinction risk in the analyses, but technically this is not a species trait.

comments.issue: The relevance of in the Anthropocene in the title is questionable.
comments.request: Reconsider the Anthropocene wording in the title.
comments.quote: Title: Is “in the Anthropocene” relevant for the title (see also comment on temporal coverage above)

comments.issue: Better coverage at line 23 is not defined against a comparator.
comments.request: State what better coverage is compared to.
comments.quote: Line 23: “better coverage” - better than what?

comments.issue: Underrepresented at line 26 is undefined and appropriate representation is unclear.
comments.request: Define underrepresented and the appropriate representation.
comments.quote: Line 26: What do you mean by “underrepresented”? What representation is appropriate for different biodiversity data sources?

comments.issue: Sentences are repeated: lines 32-33 repeat lines 16-17, and lines 79-83 repeat lines 23-26.
comments.request: Remove the duplicated sentences.
comments.quote: Line 32-33: The same sentence is repeated in lines 16-17.

comments.issue: The claim of reduced voucher collection conflicts with GBIF data showing more vouchered records per year now.
comments.request: Reconcile the statement with the GBIF trend.
comments.quote: our quick analyses of global GBIF data suggest that the number of vouchered records (on GBIF) are actually higher (per year of collection) now than in the past. No doubt this is due to recent records being digitized more readily.

comments.issue: The correlation coefficient and p-value for the weak observation association at line 113 are not shown.
comments.request: Show the correlation coefficient and p-value.
comments.quote: Line 113: The correlation coefficient and p value should be shown for the “weak association” of observation records as well.

comments.issue: The implications of bird occurrence data having higher coverage than bird vouchers are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of this pattern.
comments.quote: Line 118: What are the implications of bird occurrence data having higher coverage than bird vouchers?

comments.issue: The idea at lines 138-141 duplicates lines 120-124 and may belong in the conclusion.
comments.request: Move or merge the duplicated discussion.
comments.quote: Line 138-141: The idea discussed in this paragraph is largely similar to the one presented in line 120-124. Would this be better suited for the conclusion?

comments.issue: Whether remote and wilderness areas are more biologically meaningful is questionable.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of biologically meaningful at line 202.
comments.quote: Line 202: Are remote and wilderness areas really more “biologically meaningful” than less remote regions?

comments.issue: The pattern at lines 211-214 lacks explanation and implications.
comments.request: Explain the emergence and implications of this pattern.
comments.quote: Line 211-214: This pattern is interesting but there is no explanation provided for its emergence and implications.

comments.issue: Overthrown at line 229 may be the wrong word; overwhelmed may fit better.
comments.request: Correct the wording at line 229.
comments.quote: Line 229: Perhaps vouchers are being “overwhelmed” by observations in occurrence data sets (rather than “overthrown”?

comments.issue: Valid geographic localities at line 479 is undefined.
comments.request: Define valid geographic localities.
comments.quote: Line 479: What is meant by “valid geographic localities”?

comments.issue: The trait values and phylogeny at line 541 are unspecified.
comments.request: State which trait values and phylogeny are used.
comments.quote: Line 541: What traits values, and what phylogeny are referred to here?

comments.issue: Extinction threat is measured differently for plants than other groups at line 582.
comments.request: Explain why extinction threat was measured differently for plants.
comments.quote: Line 582: Why was extinction threat measured differently for plants than for the other groups?

comments.issue: Well-sampled regions show no data at the 1600 km grid size in Figures S2, S3 and S5.
comments.request: Explain the missing data in the figure legends.
comments.quote: Fig S2, S3, S5: Why are well sampled regions (e.g. Europe, N America) showing as having no data at the 1600 km grid size? An explanation could be provided in the figure legends.

comments.issue: Source and resolution of the Wilderness data are missing from Table S5.
comments.request: Provide the source and resolution of the Wilderness data.
comments.quote: Table S5: Please provide source and resolution of the Wilderness data

reviews.assessment: Praises the writing and impressive scale but finds the messages already known, the title disconnected and the figures uninformative, with no high-impact message emerging.

comments.issue: The title does not relate to the analyses and the main messages are already well known.
comments.request: Reconsider the Anthropocene framing and articulate what is new.
comments.quote: Reading the paper, the first observation is that the title doesn't relate to the analyses. I was very confused by what this paper conceptually had to do with the Anthropocene at all.

comments.issue: Many figures are elaborate but uninformative and do not convey the key results.
comments.request: Redesign the figures to communicate the main findings.
comments.quote: Moreover, many of the figures are fancy without being informative. Even after examining them for quite a while, they don't lend a lot of insight into the (very large) datasets.

comments.issue: The per-record analysis is driven by known biases and does not break new ground.
comments.request: Move beyond known per-record biases to new analyses.
comments.quote: There is frequently the issue that the analysis is on a "per record" basis, and is strongly driven by the popularity of citizen science in recent years, urban areas, and for charismatic taxa. This is well known.

comments.issue: Converting shapefiles to a grid creates false precision and visible artefacts.
comments.request: Address the artefacts of the shapefile-to-grid conversion.
comments.quote: This creates both the appearance of more precision than there actually is in the analysis as well as many visible artefacts of this choice.

comments.issue: No main message worthy of a high-impact journal has emerged despite the impressive scale.
comments.request: Develop a clearer high-level message from the giant datasets.
comments.quote: In my view this is an analysis of very impressive scale, but a main message worthy of a high impact journal has not yet emerged from the analysis.

title: Mass production of unvouchered records fails to represent global biodiversity patterns

study.system: captive great apes; repeated cognitive task testing

reviews.assessment: Suitable analytic approaches and clear writing, but the paper is method-oriented and several analyses and assertions need reframing or removal.
strengths: data analytic approaches well suited to the questions
study of 43 great apes with repeated cognitive measures

comments.issue: The paper is more method-oriented than problem-oriented.
comments.request: Focus on the questions about cognition and what different findings would mean.
comments.quote: First, to my mind, this paper seemed more method-oriented than problem-oriented

comments.issue: The assumption-testing framing needs justification that these assumptions were untested, and the key Kaufman et al. (2019) paper is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Kaufman et al. (2019) and broaden the literature review beyond great apes.
comments.quote: one key paper that the authors did not cite was that by Kaufman et al. (2019)

comments.issue: The importance of group-level performance stability and the expectation of shared age trajectories across groups or species are not explained.
comments.request: Spell out why group-level stability matters and its theoretical basis.
comments.quote: I failed to grasp the importance of the analyses/question about the “stability of group-level performance”

comments.issue: The most important finding, that variance is mostly consistent between-individual rather than transient, lacks prominence.
comments.request: Give this result at lines 275-280 more prominence.
comments.quote: The best evidence that these are traits or trait-like is that most of the variance was not due to transient, situational factors, but consistent between-individual variance. This needs more prominence.

comments.issue: The claim that the study addresses associative learning is unsupported, and the statement at lines 352-353 is a bare assertion.
comments.request: Omit this text or back it with evidence.
comments.quote: The second statement (lines 352-353) is simply an assertion with nothing backing it.

comments.issue: The comparative method is introduced too late and without the relevant references.
comments.request: Bring up the comparative method sooner with brief citations.
comments.quote: The comparative method could be brought up sooner. A brief mention and citation of the other approaches that you refer to with relevant references is all that is necessary.

comments.issue: References are missing at the end of the line 76 sentence.
comments.request: Add references at line 76.
comments.quote: l 76: References are needed for the end of this sentence.

comments.issue: Terminology varies between 'assumptions' and 'problems'.
comments.request: Use 'assumptions' consistently throughout.
comments.quote: I think it would be better to refer to “assumptions” and stick to that. Something other than “problems” would be advisable in any event, and please be consistent with the terminology throughout

comments.issue: The text at lines 140-142 is repeated.
comments.request: Remove the repeated text.
comments.quote: ll 140-142: This text is repeated. ll 143-145

comments.issue: The intraclass correlation literature is not linked at lines 143-145.
comments.request: Link to Shrout and Fleiss (1979) and/or Nakagawa and Schielzeth (2013).
comments.quote: I would link this back to the common language to describe intraclass correlations, such as Shrout and Fleiss (1979) and/or Nakagawa and Schielzeth (2013).

comments.issue: The axes of Figure 3 should be flipped.
comments.request: Flip the axes of Figure 3.
comments.quote: Figure 3: Please flip the axes. l 165

comments.issue: 'A lesser extent' at line 206 is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the comparison for 'a lesser extent'.
comments.quote: l 206: A lesser extent to what? l 213

comments.issue: The level of correlation described as 'substantial' at line 213 is undefined.
comments.request: Use the correlation cut-offs from Cohen (1992).
comments.quote: What level of correlations is described as “substantial”. Please refer to the language/cut-offs in Cohen (1992).

comments.issue: The Figure 4B correlation matrix would be easier to use as a table.
comments.request: Present Figure 4B correlations as a table.
comments.quote: I am afraid that I have an aversion to a correlation matrix presented in anything other than a table. It makes it easier to obtain those correlations from papers, too

comments.issue: About sixteen line-level copy edits across the manuscript (wording, hyphenation, capitals, formatting and acronym use).
comments.quote: l 58: Do not hyphenate “nonhuman”. Also, change “such as” to “this”.

reviews.assessment: Novel and much-needed test of cognitive research assumptions, elegantly executed; asks mainly for species-difference discussion and small clarifications.
strengths: novel and much-needed findings on implicit assumptions in ape cognition research
elegant and thorough test of critical assumptions
broad interest across anthropology, psychology and evolutionary biology

comments.issue: Species differences are combined and their (lack of) stability and reliability is not explicitly discussed.
comments.request: Address the stability and reliability of group and species differences.
comments.quote: The only more substantial point is that I would like to see some more explicit discussion of the (lack of) species differences reported.

comments.issue: The 14 variables referred to at line 110 are not listed in the Introduction.
comments.request: Mention which 14 variables are meant.
comments.quote: Perhaps you can mention which 14 variables you refer to somewhere in the Intro?

comments.issue: The overall length of the two phases is not given.
comments.request: Add the duration of both phases.
comments.quote: Please add info on the overall length of the two phases.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not explain what Session 1 and Session 2 mean or whether there is a break.
comments.request: Explain the session structure in the main text.
comments.quote: Please briefly explain what Session 1 and Session 2 mean? Is there a break between two sessions?

comments.issue: It is not explained why the delay of gratification task was only run in Phase 2.
comments.request: Explain the phase restriction of this task.
comments.quote: Why is ‘Delay of gratification’ only done in Phase 2? Please explain.

comments.issue: Whether group-level differences are stable and reliably measured is not addressed at lines 136-137 and is ordered oddly.
comments.request: Address group-level difference reliability at this point in the results.
comments.quote: Are group level differences stable and measured reliably? I would like to see this addressed somewhere around here.

comments.issue: The finding that species differences are not reliably measured receives too little attention in the Discussion.
comments.request: Discuss the unreliable species differences more.
comments.quote: The finding that species differences are not reliably measured should could receive some more attention in Discussion.

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: missing 'do' at line 165 and the superscript formatting of 'median sample size = 7' at line 306.
comments.quote: L 306: ‘median sample size = 7’ not in superscript

reviews.assessment: Very valuable, unprecedented contribution recommended for publication; main concern is the unwarranted interpretation of stable variation as cognitive traits.
strengths: impressive body of research at an unprecedented scale
most tests show no learning effects, supporting repeated assays
potential new gold standard for validating cognitive methods

comments.issue: Stable performance differences may reflect stable motivation or attention rather than the cognitive abilities being measured.
comments.request: Use value-neutral labels (stable versus occasion-specific variation) and discuss alternative explanations.
comments.quote: Why shouldn’t motivational differences between individuals remain stable over time?

comments.issue: One task is relegated to the supplementary materials, losing the contrast between a meaningful and a less meaningful test.
comments.request: Include discussion of this task in the main body.
comments.quote: A secondary comment concerns the relegation of one of the tasks to the supplementary materials. I think it is a pity not to include the discussion of this task in the main body of the paper.

comments.issue: The statistical methods require specialist review.
comments.request: Obtain review by a statistical expert.
comments.quote: The paper needs to be reviewed by a specialist statistician, as I am not expert enough to evaluate the specific methods used.

reviews.assessment: Interesting psychometric advance, but assumptions are unjustified, proper models are hidden in supplements, and small groups limit the analyses.
strengths: interesting study advancing the field methodologically
attempt to apply state-of-the-art statistical methods
ambitious structural equation modeling of great ape cognition

comments.issue: The three assumptions structuring the manuscript are taken for granted without justification or relation to standard psychometric quality criteria.
comments.request: Justify the assumptions and link them to reliability, objectivity and validity.
comments.quote: The authors take this for granted and don't provide a justification.

comments.issue: Group-level stability is judged from simple means that ignore time series structure and statistical uncertainty, and the stability claim is not supported for all tasks.
comments.request: Report models with standard errors and time-series-aware tests in the main text.
comments.quote: For investigating the first assumption of stable group-level results, they rely on simple means per time point and species, completely ignoring the time series nature of the measures and statistical uncertainty of the estimates.

comments.issue: Lagged correlations ignore autocorrelation, uncertainty and measurement error, and learning and memory effects violate the parallel-measures requirement.
comments.request: Use appropriate reliability models rather than lagged correlations.
comments.quote: This is simply not the case here. We probably have learning effects, memory effects and autoregressive effects and so on, so that the correlations are not useful for assessing reliability.

comments.issue: Sophisticated analyses are confined to the supplement while oversimplified estimates appear in the main text.
comments.request: Move the proper analyses to the main text and descriptive statistics to the supplement.
comments.quote: In my opinion, it should be the other way round. Additional descriptive statistics can be shown in supplemental materials but the proper analysis should appear in the main text.

comments.issue: Group sizes are very low, the simulation ignores them, and some group comparisons use fewer than five individuals.
comments.request: Address group sizes, species differences and small-group comparisons.
comments.quote: Third, the group sizes are really low and this may be problematic for the statistical models and the generalizability of the results.

comments.issue: The LST models and manifest indicators are only described in the supplement.
comments.request: Briefly introduce the models and indicators in the main text.
comments.quote: The LST models used in the main text are only described in the supplemental materials. Please briefly introduce the models that were estimated and the manifest indicators used with a couple of sentences in the main text

comments.issue: Figure 2 does not show uncertainty for the means.
comments.request: Add standard errors or confidence intervals to Figure 2.
comments.quote: Figure 2: Please add standard errors or confidence intervals for the means

comments.issue: Figure 3 is counterintuitive, has interchanged axes, and its correlation display and confidence bands are problematic.
comments.request: Interchange the axes and reconsider the display and confidence bands.
comments.quote: Figure 3 to me is counterintuitive and difficult to read. And it violates standard ways of displaying information.

comments.issue: Reliability, stability and structure are used with meanings that differ from standard psychometric definitions, and LST terms are introduced but not used consistently.
comments.request: Align the terminology with psychometric definitions and use the technical terms consistently.
comments.quote: These terms have a clear meaning in psychometrics, but this is sometimes not in line with the way the authors use these terms.

comments.issue: Several typographical fixes: p.7 l.120 wording, repeated lines at p.9 l.140-142, and inconsistent LSTM/LST abbreviation.
comments.quote: Sometimes “latent state-trait models (LSTM)” is used and sometimes LST models is used as abbreviation. Please make consistent.

title: Great ape cognition is structured by stable cognitive abilities and predicted by developmental conditions

study.system: archaic hominins; SpliceAI predictions of splice-altering variants

editor_summary: Editor asks to address the reviewers' criticisms and some editorial concerns before a final decision on the manuscript.

reviews.assessment: Of general interest with novel insights and generally robust results, but several analyses on allele polarity, tissue activity and protein impact need refining.
strengths: novel insights on archaic versus modern human phenotypes
results generally robust and in line with previous findings

comments.issue: Alleles where archaics are REF/REF but the alternative allele is frequent in Africans are not considered.
comments.request: Assess how including high-frequency African alternative alleles changes the interpretations.
comments.quote: I would be curious to see how the interpretations would be changed if the authors included alleles where the 4 archaics are REF/REF, but the alternative allele is at high frequency in African populations (eg. AF>80%)

comments.issue: It is not assessed whether SpliceAI predictions inform on the tissues affected by splicing events.
comments.request: Assess tissue-specific activity of SAVs using GTEx and test for enrichment by SAV class.
comments.quote: I wonder whether splice AI informs on the tissues affected by the Alternative splicing event ?

comments.issue: The consequences of predicted SAVs for protein function are not quantified by variant class.
comments.request: Report the percentage of SAVs causing modified protein sequences and loss of function per class.
comments.quote: the percentage of the identified SAVs that lead to (i) a modified protein sequence, and (ii) a loss of function

comments.issue: No comparison is made with deleterious missense variants expected in modern humans for the same genes.
comments.request: Compare with deleterious missense variants expected when sampling four modern humans.
comments.quote: it would be interesting to have, as a comparison, the number of deleterious missense variants expected among the same 246 genes when sampling 4 modern humans of various ancestries

comments.issue: Two different counts of archaic variants analysed are given (1.5M or 1.6M).
comments.request: Correct or clarify the two archaic variant counts.
comments.quote: the authors provide two distinct numbers for the archaic variants analyzed (1.5M or 1.6M). they should either correct this, if it is a mistake, or clarify the nuance

comments.issue: The rationale for analysing the two introgression datasets separately rather than combined is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why the two introgressed variant datasets were not combined.
comments.quote: Could the author explain their rationale for analyzing the two datasets independently, rather than combining them and considering the union of the two datasets as the set of introgressed variants ?

comments.issue: The range considered consistent with neutral evolution and the percentage of neutral sites are not specified.
comments.request: State the neutrality threshold and quantify the percentage of neutrally evolving sites.
comments.quote: Could the author specify what range they consider as consistent with neutral evolution (i.e where they place the threshold), and quantify the % of neutrally evolving sites.

comments.issue: The absence of a DELTA_max-frequency relationship for ancient SAVs is unexplained.
comments.request: Test the most deleterious ancient SAVs for a relationship with allele frequency.
comments.quote: Could the author test this hypothesis by focusing on the subset of ancient SAVS predicted to be the most deleterious, to see if we do find a relationship with allele frequency ?

comments.issue: The meaning of 'correctly predicted' acceptor loss at line 291 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what 'correctly predicted' means in this context.
comments.quote: why do the authors state that the acceptor loss is «correctly predicted » ? what does it mean in this context ?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the 35% at line 386 refers to archaic or ancient SAVs.
comments.request: Clarify whether 35% refers to ancient SAVs.
comments.quote: We found that 35% of archaic SAVs were identified in modern humans in GTEx ». Do the authors mean 35% of ancient SAVs ?

reviews.assessment: Fascinating and challenging study; assumptions about SpliceAI transferability, variant definition and phenotypic effects should be listed as limitations.

comments.issue: Unprovable assumptions are not discussed or listed as limitations.
comments.request: Discuss and list the key assumptions as limitations.
comments.quote: The authors make a number of assumptions that, while plausible, are not provable and should be discussed and listed as limitations.

comments.issue: SpliceAI was trained on modern human data, so archaic splice machinery differences could increase prediction errors.
comments.request: Comment on the transferability of SpliceAI to archaic genomes.
comments.quote: it is conceivable that the splice machinery in Neanderthals and Denisovans differs in some ways from our own. Thus it is likely that SpliceAI may make more incorrect predictions on this dataset

comments.issue: SpliceAI performance on common, non-disease SAVs is uncharacterised and the 0.5 SAP cutoff is arbitrary.
comments.request: Correlate SpliceAI predictions with GTEx splicing data or known splice QTLs to calibrate the cutoff.
comments.quote: It would be good for the authors to characterize the performance of SpliceAI on the subset of SAVs common to modern humans and analyze what the relation is between spliceAI preedictions and alternative splicing

comments.issue: 1000 Genomes is outdated for defining archaic-specific variants.
comments.request: Use GnomAD to define archaic-specific variants.
comments.quote: The 1KG project is no longer state of the art. The authors should instead use data from the GnomAD project to characterize variants that are specific or nearly so to archaic hominins.

comments.issue: It is uncertain whether common SAVs affect isoform function or phenotype, which should be a limitation.
comments.request: List the uncertainty about phenotypic effects as a limitation.
comments.quote: it is not certain that the variants have any effect at all on the phenotype, and this should be listed as a limitation

comments.issue: The choice of hg37 instead of the current hg38 genome version is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why hg37 was used instead of hg38.
comments.quote: Why did the authors choose to use hg37 instead of the current genome version, hg38, that was released in 2014?

title: Resurrecting the alternative splicing landscape of archaic hominins using machine learning

study.system: environmental DNA; human genetic bycatch from water, sand, air samples

editor_summary: Data may be unsuitable for the privacy claim; lab contamination hard to resolve; a purpose-designed programme integrating ethics approval for human eDNA would be valuable; decision negative.

reviews.assessment: Commends the reuse of turtle eDNA data for an urgent question, but contamination risks and sample size prevent recommending publication.
strengths: very urgent and important research topic
important idea to study human DNA in eDNA

comments.issue: The study design and sample size of the reused samples are inadequate for the question posed.
comments.request: Address the design and sample-size limitations.
comments.quote: I, however, see a few problems in the study design and sample size for answering the posed question.

comments.issue: Sand negative controls were designed for turtle DNA and expectedly contain human DNA, so sampling contamination cannot be ruled out.
comments.request: Rule out or discuss contamination during sampling, and explain the sand control pattern.
comments.quote: The negative controls (especially from the sand samples) have been taken as negative controls for the sea turtle, which means that this sample expectedly contains human DNA and contamination during sampling can not be ruled out

comments.issue: Wild versus tank water differences could reflect the sequencing platform (NovaSeq versus HiSeq) rather than real human DNA differences.
comments.request: Investigate whether the sequencing platform explains the pattern.
comments.quote: It is also striking that the human DNA content in wild vs. tank water samples could be explained by the employed sequencing machine, i.e. NovaSeq vs HiSeq.

comments.issue: The water negative control has 3,184 human-aligned reads (strong contamination) but is not discussed; the reported 1.59% also mismatches 3,184/196,876.
comments.request: Discuss this contamination result and check the percentage calculation.
comments.quote: However, 196,876 reads have been obtained for this negative control, out of which 3,184 align to the human genome - which suggests strong human contamination.

comments.issue: The sample size is too small for a landmark study; technical, spatial and temporal replicates are needed.
comments.request: Add replicates and study the spatial gradient of human DNA.
comments.quote: I however think that the sample size of this study is too small to create such a landmark study

comments.issue: Reads may map to other mammals, which could explain differences in human read assignment from the Y chromosome.
comments.request: Run a metagenomic mapping against a database of expected mammals.
comments.quote: Have the authors conducted a metagenomic mapping approach against a database of expected mammals? I am wondering if some reads would map to other mammals in such an approach

comments.issue: Human genome coverage in the shotgun data, e.g. mitochondrial fraction, is not characterized.
comments.request: Report genome coverage and what information is retrievable.
comments.quote: Have the authors looked into coverage of the human genome in their shotgun data? It would be interesting to know if most of it is, e.g., mitochondrial

comments.issue: The introduction does not connect the shift from metabarcoding to shotgun sequencing with individual identification.
comments.request: Rewrite the introduction to make this connection clear.
comments.quote: I would suggest rewriting the introduction a bit to make clear that it is the shift from metabarcoding-based approaches to shotgun sequencing that potentially enables retrieving enough genetic data

comments.issue: Correlating susceptibility loci with pathogen load is very difficult given pooled samples and high variance, and this caveat is missing.
comments.request: Discuss the difficulties of this proposed application.
comments.quote: I think it's necessary to discuss that this is a very difficult endeavor given that each sample is a pooled sample with intrinsically high variance in both phenotypic as well as genotypic measurements
