comments.quote: The gray scale figures do not well visually distinguish the treatments of interest, especially in e.g. Figure 2A.

comments.issue: PyOM is introduced but never measured, while pH is.
comments.request: Streamline PyOM mentions to reflect measured data.
comments.quote: PyOM is introduced, leading readers to think that it will be important for the study but it not returned to with data/results.

comments.issue: How rRNA and rDNA sequences were used to assess fire survival is not described; using rRNA alone could be a fundamental flaw.
comments.request: Explain how rRNA and rDNA sequences were used.
comments.quote: this would be a fundamental flaw for interpretation, as sequence counts of rRNA without reference to rDNA are not interpretable as proxies for relative abundance of the organisms

comments.issue: The number of moist cores remaining after exclusion is not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of moist cores remaining.
comments.quote: If the cores that did not reach >50 were omitted, how many “moist” cores were left?

comments.issue: Sample sizes are not apparent in the text or figure legends.
comments.request: Report sample sizes per experiment and condition.
comments.quote: Generally, sample sizes are not apparent in the text or reported with the figure legends.

comments.issue: Box plots do not show individual points.
comments.request: Plot individual points on box or violin plots.
comments.quote: It also would be good to plot each discrete point on the box plots (or, alternatively, use violin plots with points overlay to convey each distribution quickly).

comments.issue: Assessing trade-offs between non-mutually exclusive traits is conceptually questionable.
comments.request: Justify assessing trade-offs between non-exclusive traits.
comments.quote: a bigger question is whether it makes sense to assume/assess trade-offs for traits that are known to be not mutually exclusive?

comments.issue: Field-lab correspondence is not quantified and the p-value at L304 is missing.
comments.request: Quantify the overlap and report the p-value.
comments.quote: The “good correspondence” could be statistically supported? Could the authors report the % overlap in community composition between the field and lab

comments.issue: Figure 3 ordinations are hard to interpret and the organic/mineral split is unmotivated.
comments.request: Separate lab and field ordinations and motivate the split.
comments.quote: It is hard to interpret these figures. Perhaps the lab and field samples could be separated out into their own ordinations

comments.issue: Recovery/resilience of the field dataset is not quantified.
comments.request: Quantify recovery or resilience for the field data.
comments.quote: The authors could quantify the degree of recovery (or similar metric of resilience) for their field dataset.

comments.issue: Community size is inferred from DNA concentration, which is an imprecise proxy.
comments.request: Acknowledge the imprecise size proxy.
comments.quote: Community size (number of cells/individuals) was not directly measured? DNA concentration was, and I agree that this may proxy size/biomass, but not precisely.

comments.issue: Read fractions per trait are confounded by changes in community biomass and size.
comments.request: Standardize read fractions to DNA concentration or qPCR.
comments.quote: Could these charts also be provided with a y-axis standardized to the total DNA concentration or perhaps qPCR of housekeeping or even 16S genes

comments.issue: Statistics for differences among lab time-point communities are not reported.
comments.request: Report lab community-structure statistics or discuss them.
comments.quote: are the statistics reported that show whether there are differences in community structure across the 24 h, 5-week, and 6-month communities in the lab?

comments.issue: Figure 7 and its analyses are not conclusive for assessing relative trait strength.
comments.request: Strengthen or omit the relative-strength analysis.
comments.quote: I’m not sure that Figure 7 and associated analyses are conclusive for assessing “relative strength” of traits.

comments.issue: The dataset is under-analyzed; community and carbon stability, resistance and resilience are not quantified per treatment.
comments.request: Quantify recovery and stability metrics for each treatment.
comments.quote: The rich dataset presented is a bit under-analyzed as far as relating the community assembly patterns to ecological outcomes of both community and carbon stability, resistance, resilience for each treatment

comments.issue: SRA project SUB11346170 cannot be found.
comments.request: Provide an accessible SRA accession.
comments.quote: The SUB11346170 project was not found on SRA

comments.issue: The ESS-DIVE data repository link is broken.
comments.request: Fix the ESS-DIVE link.
comments.quote: The link to the ESS-DIVE data repository did not work and returned an error.

comments.issue: The GitHub repository lacks a readme, input/output files and OTU tables.
comments.request: Add readme, input/output files and OTU tables.
comments.quote: it would strongly benefit from a readme file to orient users to reproduce the analysis. The input and output files for each R script are not available

reviews.assessment: Well-designed and very well written study; suggests title and boreal-context improvements only.
strengths: nice integration of functional ecology and biogeochemistry
exciting field and lab experimental designs

comments.issue: The title does not reflect the functional resilience results.
comments.request: Consider reflecting functional resilience in the title.
comments.quote: whether the title of the paper would be more impactful if it also reflected the results on functional resilience (i.e., CO2 flux or C mineralization)

comments.issue: The boreal-forest context of the results is lost in the discussion.
comments.request: Place results in boreal forest context before general discussion.
comments.quote: the idea that the results could be more representative of Boreal forests was a bit lost

reviews.assessment: Significant and sound work, but the trait conceptualisation needs revisiting and key methodology needs clearer presentation.
strengths: significance across fire ecology, soil carbon and climate fields
critical experimental evidence for ecological theory

comments.issue: Mapping traits onto the YAS framework is flawed: dormancy is not a C-cycling strategy and YAS ignores temporal resource fluctuations.
comments.request: Revisit the trait mapping onto the YAS framework.
comments.quote: The main issues is that the YAS system is specifically for unpacking C cycling strategies - and dormancy (one of the authors traits) is not an C cycling strategy.

comments.issue: Trade-off hypotheses are problematic if dormancy and fast growth belong to one life strategy.
comments.request: Revisit hypotheses in light of the shared life strategy.
comments.quote: hypothesis 1 (that fire survival as a trait would be replaced in importance by fast growth in structuring bacterial communities) becomes problematic if these two traits are part of the same life strategy as does the hypothesis regarding trait trade-offs

comments.issue: Lab sampling, horizon definitions and differing sample numbers cannot be reconciled from the text.
comments.request: Clarify lab sampling, horizon definitions and sample numbers.
comments.quote: I cannot easily reconcile (even after viewing the supp data) statements like Ln 130: “N=19 sites, N=57 organic horizons, N=36 mineral horizons for all analyses unless otherwise stated”

comments.issue: The trait assignment process is unclear and cannot be reproduced from the supplement.
comments.request: Describe trait assignment clearly and list ASVs with assignments.
comments.quote: even with the supplementary data the current description does not allow researchers to easily corroborate the authors trait assignments or check for themselves taxa associated with each trait

comments.issue: OTU is used when ESV/ASV is meant.
comments.request: Replace OTU with ESV/ASV throughout.
comments.quote: OTU should really be replaced with ESV/ASV throughout. Taxonomic assignment to OTUs holds a distinct meaning and is not what was done.

comments.issue: The discussion justifying empirical trait measures against predictive traits is unnecessary.
comments.request: Consider removing the justification of empirical trait measures.

title: Experimentally determined traits shape bacterial community composition one and five years following wildfire

study.system: ecology literature (5 journals); survey of ecologists

editor_summary: Reviewers find the study interesting and timely; editor asks to tone down effect-size and power claims, justify journal and practice choices, provide metadata, and remove the survey, whose methods Referee 4 judged not rigorous.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, important and broadly relevant, but the utility of the average effect size and the power conclusions is overstated and needs caveats.
strengths: large sample of recent ecology literature
useful evidence on selective reporting and data archiving

comments.issue: Utility of the average effect size as a power benchmark is overstated.
comments.request: Moderate the conclusions and acknowledge shortcomings of the data.
comments.quote: as I discuss in more detail in several places below, I think the authors have overstated the utility of this approach

comments.issue: The claim that most ecology studies are underpowered rests on an unsupported assumption.

comments.quote: this statement rests on an important assumption that I don’t think is sufficiently supported and therefore I think this statement should be moderated somewhat

comments.issue: Statement that power interacts with publication bias is too strong.

comments.issue: Wording implies empirical results are the only essential component of advancement.

comments.quote: ideas, hypotheses, models etc. are also important. Maybe you could say something like “an essential component of advancement”

comments.issue: Overgeneralises that all ecologists inform management.

comments.quote: 26: maybe “and often to inform” (not all ecologists are doing these things)

comments.issue: References 2-4 address publication bias, not the incentives that drive it.
comments.request: Use references giving contrasting perspectives on incentives.
comments.quote: references 2-4 are a surprising choice to support your statement about debate about incentives

comments.issue: 'Imply' understates what the results demonstrate.
comments.request: Replace 'imply' with 'demonstrate'.
comments.quote: 42: you might consider replacing “imply” with “demonstrate”

comments.issue: Paragraph mixes all three aims instead of focusing on the second.
comments.request: Restrict the paragraph to the second aim.
comments.quote: 52: it seems to me that this paragraph would be best if it addressed just your second aim

comments.issue: Important statements lack explanation for a naive reader.

comments.issue: The 'Thus' conclusion does not follow clearly from the preceding statement.
comments.request: Clarify the logical link.
comments.quote: your “Thus” statement here is not sufficiently clearly linked to the prior statement

comments.issue: Average effect size includes trivial effects, so power is underestimated and 0.2 is not a meaningful target.

comments.issue: Claim that power is overestimated is likely wrong; the bias is toward underestimation.

comments.issue: Effect size 0.2 is labelled large but is usually considered moderate.

comments.quote: 163: instead of “only the large effects”, maybe you should say something like “mostly the large effects”

comments.issue: Fig 2 estimates assume power to detect trivial effects, skewing the range and underestimating WAAP.

comments.issue: Statement overstates how universally applied ecology is.
comments.request: Rephrase as 'a field where results often have application'.
comments.quote: some ecology is applied, but it is not universally an applied field

comments.issue: Power is not primarily about magnitude, so the paper misrepresents magnitude bias.

comments.issue: 'Necessarily' and 'not' appear reversed, changing the meaning.

title: Empirical evidence of widespread exaggeration bias and selective reporting in ecology

study.system: gorillas; whole-genome sequences, ABC demographic modelling

editor_summary: Reviewers overall positive, but besides technical criticisms there are concerns about novelty and degree of advance; recommends attending to Reviewer 3's suggestions for additional analyses.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic, but the ABC ghost models are assumed rather than data-suggested, fixed parameters are subjective, and supplementary references are confused.
strengths: interesting manuscript on an important topic
applies the approach from the authors' previous Pan study

comments.issue: The two ghost introgression models appear assumed rather than data-suggested, and model selection needs more justification.
comments.request: Run exploratory phylogenomic analyses to narrow gene-flow scenarios and clarify model choice.
comments.quote: the two ghost introgression models should be suggested by data, rather than simply assumed as it appeared to me. At the very least, more background information and more clarification should be provided for the model selection.

comments.issue: Fixing most null-model parameters assumes ghost introgression barely affects them, though some are clearly affected.
comments.request: Justify the fixed parameters and estimate the affected ones (Ne, divergence time).
comments.quote: By keeping most parameters of the null model as fixed in the two ghost introgression models, you implicitly make a big assumption that ghost introgression has little influence on these parameters.

comments.issue: Tables S4-S8 are never cited and some supplementary table references are misplaced.
comments.request: Correct the supplementary table citations.
comments.quote: you made no reference to Table S4-S8, and some references to supplementary Tables in the manuscript seem misplaced, causing much confusion and even misunderstanding.

comments.issue: Figure S4 places ghost introgression in the common ancestor of all gorillas, contradicting the legend and main text (L189, L191).
comments.request: Fix Figure S4 or the text so the model placement matches.
comments.quote: In your Fig. S4, the ghost introgression was placed in the common ancestor of all gorillas, not in the western common ancestor as claimed in the legend or main text (see LINE 189 and LINE 191).

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the mutation rate is per year or per generation.
comments.request: Specify the units of the mutation rate.
comments.quote: LINE 454: The mutation rate is per year or per generation? Please specify.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and plausible findings with good reproducibility; wants simulations and additional checks to confirm the ghost admixture is robust to model misspecification.
strengths: extensive work with scripts provided for reproducibility

comments.issue: Supplementary tables are numerous and non-intuitively named, with unclear units.
comments.request: Merge prior/posterior tabs and add an explanation column.
comments.quote: The authors provide a detailed overview in the supplement of all their analysis and there are a lot of tabs to go through plus the naming is not intuitive.

comments.issue: Fixing parameters at point values may lead to a local optimum; w_lowl_t0 is fixed despite uncertainty in the null model.
comments.request: Refit ghost models using the null-model posterior ranges as priors.
comments.quote: For instance the parameter “w_lowl_t0” is set to 64.7488. However if I look in “4.null.posteriors” this parameter also has uncertainty (23.758 - 95.9855). What happens if you use this range as a prior when fitting parameters for ghost admixture?

comments.issue: Some parameters are always fixed while others vary, and the estimated gorilla split time (965 kya) conflicts with previous estimates.
comments.request: Explain the fixed-versus-free parameter choices and the divergence-time discrepancy.
comments.quote: The estimate value is 965,481 years ago which is very different from previous estimates of 261,000 years ago (McManus et al. 2015) and 429,000 years ago (Scally et al. 2012).

comments.issue: Adding ghost admixture always improves fit because it adds flexibility, so robustness to model misspecification must be shown.
comments.request: Test whether the inferred ghost admixture survives model misspecification.
comments.quote: When one adds a ghost admixture one allows some extra flexibility in the model so scenarios with ghost admixture almost always fit the data better because there will always be some deeply divergent haplotypes present.

comments.issue: Simulations tracking true introgressed segments under high-ILS conditions are needed to test detection.
comments.request: Simulate msprime data with maximal ancestral Ne and test hmmix/S* detection.
comments.quote: The advantage of using msprime is that you can keep track of the introgressed segments and evaluate how well you are doing in identifying them!

comments.issue: It is unknown how much false ghost admixture the methods detect in a no-ghost high-ILS scenario.
comments.request: Run hmmix/S* on both scenarios and compare inferred ghost admixture.
comments.quote: Now if you run hmmix or sstar (which ever one is easiest to run) on both scenarios using the same approach as you describe in the supplement how much “ghost admixture” does the model identify in ScenarioX vs ScenarioY?

comments.issue: False positive and false negative rates for introgressed segment detection are not quantified.
comments.request: Report error rates and segment length distributions for the simulations.
comments.quote: For ScenarioY where you know which segments are actually introgressed what is the false positive, false negative rates of identifying these segments?

comments.issue: Trained hmmix parameters and their consistency with ABC inferences are not reported.
comments.request: Provide the hmmix-trained parameters and compare them with the ABC estimates.
comments.quote: Further I was wondering why you don't train the parameters using hmmix. This should give you the coalescent time to the outgroup for 'gorilla' and 'ghost' segments. Can you provide the trained parameters?

comments.issue: Mapping to human hg19 rather than the gorilla reference may bias results.
comments.request: Justify or redo mapping with gorGor6.
comments.quote: Why are you mapping Gorilla shotgun reads to the human reference hg19 - why not use the gorilla reference genome (gorgor6 is the latest version I believe).

comments.issue: S* and hmmix are not truly complementary as both rely on clustered SNP density of outgroup-absent variants, so overlap is expected.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between the two methods.
comments.quote: However the main signal for both of them is SNP density of variants not found in an outgroup and the fact that these variants are somewhat clustered. So it is not surprising that they overlap!

comments.issue: The source of the 37-41 kya introgression time estimate cannot be found in the supplement.
comments.request: Provide the derivation of the introgression time estimate.
comments.quote: Where does the 37-41 kya come from? I could not find that in the supplement.

comments.issue: The supplement has missing figure references and vague quantifiers such as 'often'.
comments.request: Fix the missing reference and quantify 'often'.
comments.quote: The authors also write "Haplotype networks of putatively introgressed regions often show expected patterns (Fig. S12)," - what does often mean? 50% of the time, 90% of the time?

comments.issue: Figure S11 does not highlight the discussed individual and the font is too small.
comments.request: Highlight the relevant individual and enlarge the font.
comments.quote: Figure S11 - could you please highlight the individual you are discussing? The font is very small and its hard to make out the relevant individuals like Gorilla_beringei_beringei-Bwiruka in panel A for instance.

reviews.assessment: Conceptually sound and well written, but largely recapitulates previous gorilla demography; suggests additional selection and regulatory analyses to add novelty.
strengths: provides another example of archaic admixture in mammals

comments.issue: The number of variants included in the population cluster analysis is not stated.
comments.request: Report how many variants were analyzed.
comments.quote: Eastern gorillas form two population clusters/Data processing: How many variants are included in this analysis?

comments.issue: Readers unfamiliar with the methods are not warned that particular demographic events are hard to infer.
comments.request: Note the limitations of inferring ghost introgression for non-specialists.
comments.quote: It may be worth noting here for readers less familiar with these methods that particular demographic events (e.g., ghost introgression into the gorilla common ancestor) are not easily inferred.

comments.issue: Figure 2 panel B x-axes do not use the units of panel A.
comments.request: Use consistent units across Figure 2 panels.
comments.quote: Figure 2: I recommend using the units from panel A for the x-axes in panel B.

comments.issue: The length distribution of hmmix-inferred introgression tracts and its variation by subspecies are not reported.
comments.request: Report introgression tract length distributions by subspecies.
comments.quote: What is the distribution of inferred lengths of these introgression tracts from hhmix? How do they differ by subspecies?

comments.issue: Figure 3 needs a dendrogram in panel A, clearer matching details in panel B, and a more visible grey box in panel E.
comments.request: Improve Figure 3 panels and describe the random-region matching.
comments.quote: A dendrogram may be useful for panel A. Did the authors match for any characteristics of introgressed regions in the random regions aside from length in panel B? The grey box in panel E is difficult to see.

comments.issue: Regulatory elements and per-gene mutational tolerance or conservation are not examined for archaic introgression depletion.
comments.request: Analyze regulatory elements and refine the genic-region analysis.
comments.quote: What about regulatory elements? Garcia-Pérez et al. 2021 recently annotated gorilla regulatory elements and these regions may exhibit depletion of archaic alleles as has been described for archaic variants in modern humans.

comments.issue: Figure 4 does not include the adaptive introgression segments.
comments.request: Add adaptive introgression segments to Figure 4.
comments.quote: Figure 4: The authors may consider adding the adaptive introgression segments to this plot.

comments.issue: Mapping failure rates to hg19 are not reported despite two gorilla reference genomes being available.
comments.request: Report mapping failure and consider gorGor5/gorGor6.
comments.quote: How often did reads fail to map to this reference? Certain regions of the gorilla genome may map poorly to a human reference and two recent high-quality gorilla reference genomes are available: gorGor5 and gorGor6.

comments.issue: The choice of 40 kbp fragments for S* is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the 40 kbp fragment size.
comments.quote: Why did the authors choose 40 kbp for simulating and identifying fragments with S*? Archaic fragments in modern Eurasians are approximately this size, on average and I would expect a similar size distribution for archaic tracts in gorillas.

comments.issue: Beyond ghost admixture evidence, the study largely recapitulates previous gorilla demography and underinterprets selection results.
comments.request: Add additional interpretation and analyses to increase the novel advance.
comments.quote: Beyond evidence of archaic introgression, this manuscript largely recapitulates previous findings of gorilla demography where power allows.

title: Ghost admixture in eastern gorillas

study.system: 1.64 Ga Barney Creek Formation biomarkers; Chlorobi carbon fixation

editor_summary: Four reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns that must be addressed; a revised version addressing these serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Important and well-written study constraining rTCA acquisition; major discussion needed on biomarker origin and the isotopic consequences of incomplete pathways.
strengths: well written with clearly described experiments
constrains the acquisition date of the complete rTCA cycle

comments.issue: Chlorobactane may not be exclusive to Chlorobi, so its origin as a biomarker is uncertain.
comments.request: Discuss whether the biomarker could come from PSB or cyanobacteria.
comments.quote: One major concern is the origin of chlorobactane itself. How can one tell this biomarker is actually not from PSB or cyanobacteria?

comments.issue: The key prediction linking incomplete rTCA to depleted carbon isotopes is unsupported and unexplained.
comments.request: Provide references and a detailed explanation of this prediction.
comments.quote: How is that predicted? There is no reference cited in the text, and this definitely deserves a more detailed explanation as it is the key argument of the paper.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the autotrophy-heterotrophy transition is clear-cut or stepwise as DIC-fixing enzymes are acquired.
comments.request: Clarify the transition model and the possible mixotrophic scenario.
comments.quote: do the authors consider the transition to be a clear-cut with two different signatures for autotroph and heterotroph, or rather a step-by-step increase of 13C composition as DIC-fixing enzymes are acquired?

comments.issue: Isotope fractionation enzymes may have evolved over time, so enzyme acquisition alone may not explain isotopic composition.
comments.request: Discuss the evolution of fractionation enzymes, as for Rubisco.
comments.quote: Furthermore, one cannot dismiss the hypothesis that the enzymes responsible for the 13C-fractionation in rTCA have evolved with time, therefore impacting the isotope fractionation associated with CO2 fixation.

comments.issue: No modern isotope data from organisms with an incomplete rTCA cycle are used as validation.
comments.request: Add isotope data from modern incomplete-rTCA organisms if available.
comments.quote: Analyzing 13C isotope composition of chlorobactene, or other isoprenoids, from present organisms using an incomplete rTCA cycle would definitely help solving these issues.

reviews.assessment: Impressive methods and thorough isotope data, but terminology misuse and logical gaps make the manuscript unsuitable in its current form.
strengths: hydrocarbon purification method valuable and impressive
carbon isotope data thorough and logical

comments.issue: Photoautotrophy and photoheterotrophy are used inconsistently and incorrectly throughout.
comments.request: Use the terminology consistently and correctly.
comments.quote: There is a complete lack of consistency throughout the manuscript in the usage of the terminology “photoautotrophy” and “photoheterotrophy” and, apart from the confusion that this leads to in following the narrative, it is misleading and incorrect.

comments.issue: Iron as an electron donor for Chlorobiales is never mentioned; only sulfide oxidation is considered.
comments.request: Discuss iron as a possible electron donor.
comments.quote: The authors also exclude any mention of iron as an electron donor for the Chlorobiales in the Barney Creek Formation and only focus on sulfide oxidation.

comments.issue: Modern photoheterotrophic Chlorobiales do not directly support the inference that incomplete rTCA causes photoheterotrophy.
comments.request: Address the evolutionary time frames of photoheterotrophy pathways.
comments.quote: The fact that there are modern Chlorobiales species that perform photoheterotrophy with an incomplete rTCA cycle does not directly support the idea that an incomplete rTCA cycle would lead to photoheterotrophy

comments.issue: Several sentences contain spelling or grammar errors; line numbers are missing.
comments.request: Copy-edit the manuscript and add line numbers.
comments.quote: Double-check the writing throughout the manuscript as there are quite a few sentences with spelling or grammar errors.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and interesting study; only asks for a sentence on the absence of eukaryotic isotopic signatures.
strengths: well written with clearly defined setup and questions
interesting read contributing to Proterozoic microbiology

comments.issue: The absence of eukaryotic isotopic signatures (no steranes) is not commented on.
comments.request: Add a sentence about this near the C30 ab hopane discussion.
comments.quote: The only thing missing, in my opinion, would be a comment on the isotopic signatures from a eukryotic source (or lack thereof for BCF).

title: Late acquisition of the rTCA carbon fixation pathway by Chlorobi

study.system: soundscapes and bird point counts; 8,023 recordings, four regions

reviews.assessment: Important and timely demonstration of soundscape limitations; only minor general comments and specific text corrections are requested.
strengths: demonstrates lack of transferability of soundscape methods
sensible suggestion to use soundscapes for community similarity
welcome direction for focused passive acoustic studies

comments.issue: The comparably good Taiwan-to-India transfer performance is not explained.
comments.request: Discuss possible reasons such as shared soundscape or geographic features.
comments.quote: In Figure 1d, it appears that the performance (R2) of the machine learning model trained on the Taiwan dataset and tested on the India dataset was comparable to the within dataset performance of for the USA.

comments.issue: Transferability of the learned feature method within biomes or habitat types is not tested.
comments.request: Comment on testing transferability within biomes or habitat types.
comments.quote: Would the authors be able to comment on whether there would be merit in testing the transferability of the learned feature method within biomes, or habitat types?

comments.issue: N line-level copy edits: sentence flow, word choices, sentence-initial numerals, typos.
comments.quote: Suggest adjusting to improve sentence flow - “In all four datasets, four learned features and no soundscape indices correlated with avian richness (Fig. 1b)

comments.issue: Figure 1a legend lacks a label for the brown bars.
comments.request: Add a legend label for the brown bars.
comments.quote: Figure 1a: Please include a label for the brown bars in the legend.

comments.issue: The type of 'interventions' referred to is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify the interventions, e.g. conservation interventions.
comments.quote: Please be specific about what type of “interventions” are being referred to here, e.g. “conservation interventions”.

comments.issue: Recorder positions are subjective (e.g. 'at chest height') and not repeatable.
comments.request: Provide recorder heights in metres for each region.
comments.quote: The description of the position of the acoustic recorder as “at chest height” is subjective and not repeatable. Please provide the height in metres.

comments.issue: The reason for downsampling audio to 16kHz for VGGish is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why 16kHz was chosen.
comments.quote: Please could the authors explain why the audio was down sampled to 16kHz for the VGGish CNN.

comments.issue: Point counts were split randomly rather than by site, which may inflate model performance.
comments.request: Explain why a random rather than site-based split was used.
comments.quote: Please could the authors explain why for each dataset point counts were split into training and testing sets randomly, rather than by site, which is generally considered to be a more robust method.

reviews.assessment: Praises the novel multi-dataset strategy and analysis but sees dataset heterogeneity and detectability differences as a main weakness that may explain the results.
strengths: suitable and novel strategy combining distinct audio datasets

comments.issue: Dataset differences in sampling, survey methods and equipment may explain the lack of transferability instead of the analytical approach.
comments.request: Acknowledge or address the unharmonized data collection.
comments.quote: I found this the main weakness of the study as someone can question whether the lack of generalisable estimates might be due to the absence of an harmonized data collection rather than an inefficient analytical method.

comments.issue: Detectability differs between point counts and recordings, which may bias comparisons.
comments.request: Derive richness from the recordings themselves for a fair test.
comments.quote: bird surveys differ from soundscape recordings in species detectability, as the surveys conducted were based on both aural and visual detection, while audio recordings only captured signals from acoustically active species

comments.issue: Settings, parameters and preprocessing of the 60 acoustic indices are not reported.
comments.request: Report index settings and preprocessing steps.
comments.quote: Among the 60 indices used, they are highly variable and often require specific settings or parameters to be computed that should be reported in the manuscript

comments.issue: Unbalanced sample sizes across regions (147-6734) are not addressed in analyses or discussion.
comments.request: Discuss and account for unbalanced sampling in cross-dataset validation.
comments.quote: Another noticeable characteristic of the database is that contains a clearly unbalanced number of observations among regions (from 147 to 6734).

comments.issue: Datasets with higher uncertainty, e.g. Taiwan's temporally mismatched recordings, may warrant exclusion.
comments.request: Consider excluding high-uncertainty datasets as an alternative approach.
comments.quote: An alternative approach would be to select some of all datasets, excluding those with higher uncertainty.

comments.issue: 'Ground-truth calibration data' is used throughout but never defined.
comments.request: Define and consistently explain the concept.
comments.quote: I think authors should also clarify a concept they often refer throughout the manuscript (almost in all sections) – “ground-truth calibration data” – but it is likely unclear for most of the readers

comments.issue: Copy edit in the Abstract.
comments.quote: Please check: “By better understanding how to use interpret data reliably

comments.issue: The claim that training datasets are taxonomically biased is disputed.
comments.request: Revise the claim that training data imply taxonomic bias.
comments.quote: I do not think the need of training (or annotated) data implies that those datasets are taxonomically biased.

comments.issue: It is not stated that the univariate analysis was within each dataset.
comments.request: Add 'within each dataset' or 'for each region independently'.
comments.quote: I would add “within each dataset” or “for region independently” at the end of the sentence to clarify the approach

comments.issue: 'Correlated with' should specify statistical significance.
comments.request: Add 'significantly' to the sentence.
comments.quote: I suggest to add “significantly” to the sentece

comments.issue: The sentence on how numbers varied by dataset should be rephrased.
comments.request: Rephrase as suggested.
comments.quote: greatly depending on the dataset (Fig. 1a). However, only four

comments.issue: 'Most features' does not make clear that both indices and learned features are included.
comments.request: Use 'soundscape features' or another inclusive term.
comments.quote: I suggest to use “soundscape features” or any other term to ensure the reader understand that they include both “soundscape indices and learned features”, and not only “learned features”.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'x' in '105 x LFs, 43 x SSIs' is unclear.
comments.request: Remove the 'x' as in the figure caption.
comments.quote: It is unclear to me what “x” mean here. 105 LFs? If so, I would remove “x” (as in the caption of Fig. 1).

comments.issue: R2 is not indicated for the predictive models.
comments.request: Indicate R2 for these models.
comments.quote: Please also indicate R2 for these models

comments.issue: Panel A y-axis scale is missing.
comments.request: Add the y-axis scale.
comments.quote: Could you add the scale in y-axis of the panel A?

comments.issue: Sample sizes are not shown in panels A, C and E.
comments.request: Add N to each sub-panel or the caption.
comments.quote: Could you also add sample size (N) in each sub-panel of panel A, C, and E, or in the caption?

comments.issue: Panel B is hard to understand and single bars hide variation across dataset combinations.
comments.request: Explain panel B and show means with error bars.
comments.quote: there are several possible combinations of dataset to be compared and then I would expect to see a mean and bar error in the figure (rather than a single bar)

comments.issue: Whether datasets were combined for new correlations is not explained in Methods.
comments.request: Explain how panel B correlations were computed.
comments.quote: Alternatively, have you combined datasets in a single one and compute new correlations? I do not find this explained in Methods.

comments.issue: The discussion's last paragraph is vague and confusing.
comments.request: Rephrase and expand it with concrete proposals.
comments.quote: Please consider rephrase and/or expand the last paragraph, and particularly the third sentence, which is unclear to me.

comments.issue: Point count methods are not presented consistently across regions.
comments.request: Use the same information and order for each region.
comments.quote: For the sake of consistency, I suggest the first section “Avifaunal point counts” to include the same information and following the same order for each region.

comments.issue: India section omits separation distance and number of species counted.
comments.request: Add separation distance and number of species counted for India.
comments.quote: Please add “separation distance” between sites (at the end of the second sentence) and “number of species counted” (at the end of the second paragraph), as reported for Malaysia.

comments.issue: It is not stated that the Tascam recorder has omnidirectional microphones.
comments.request: State that the Tascam recorder is omnidirectional.
comments.quote: Malaysia. Indicate that Tascam recorder includes omnidirectional mics.

comments.issue: Taiwan and USA paragraph order differs from the other regions.
comments.request: Reorder the paragraphs to match previous regions.
comments.quote: I would change the position of the second and third paragraphs to follow the same order than in the previous regions.

comments.issue: The polar pattern of the Gras microphone is not stated.
comments.request: Indicate the microphone polar pattern.
comments.quote: Indicate the polar pattern of the Gras microphone

comments.issue: The phrase 'shorter than 30 minutes' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what this phrase means.
comments.quote: and shorter than 30 minutes” I do not understand what you mean

comments.issue: The choice of only two features for the polynomial fit lacks rationale.
comments.request: State that only two features were selected and why.
comments.quote: Here I would indicate that you selected only two features and the rationale of that choice.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Euclidean distances were computed in 188 dimensions.
comments.request: Clarify the dimensionality used for Euclidean distances.
comments.quote: Are the Euclidean distance calculated within a 188-dimension space?

comments.issue: Models used only one feature type (LFs or SSIs) rather than both.
comments.request: Explain why feature types were not combined and whether that would help.
comments.quote: I am wondering why ML models were fitted with only one type of features (LFs or SSIs), instead of both together. Would not this potentially improve their predictive performance?

title: Limits to the accurate and generalizable use of soundscapes to monitor biodiversity

study.system: soil prokaryotes; NEON survey of 236 communities across the United States

editor_summary: Editor invited revision: reviewers find the work of interest, but Reviewers 2 and 3 request supporting analyses and clarifications to bolster the results and impact.

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic; praises the thorough bias control and analytical toolkit, offering only minor suggestions on variance visualization and observational caveats.
strengths: great analytical tools of broad interest
detailed analysis of niche breadth in soil prokaryotes

comments.issue: Rationale for calculating node degree in Python is unclear.
comments.request: Explain why node degree was calculated in Python.
comments.quote: Minor comment: any reason that node degree was calculated in Python?

comments.issue: Niche breadth variance is not shown; variance reveals whether specialization is consistent across axes.
comments.request: Amend Fig. 1e and f with variance and a density plot.
comments.quote: Could Fig. 1e and f be amended to include niche breadth variance?

comments.issue: Soil spatial heterogeneity limits niche shape inference to controlled experiments, a caveat not discussed.
comments.request: Acknowledge this observational caveat.
comments.quote: there is a very large degree of spatial heterogeneity even within small soil samples

reviews.assessment: Sees value but has substantial methodological doubts about whether proportional similarity measures tolerance and whether the dataset can identify multidimensional specialists.

comments.issue: Research questions overlap with Sriswasdi and Xu; unclear how per-axis categorization advances knowledge.
comments.request: Clarify the advance over Xu et al.'s geographic categorization.
comments.quote: the research questions posed by Sriswasdi et al. and Xu et al. may be similar to those of this study

comments.issue: Proportional similarity may not measure the range of conditions a taxon tolerates.
comments.request: Justify or reinterpret the niche breadth metric.
comments.quote: I do not agree that the measured proportional similarity corresponds to the range of environmental conditions the taxon can tolerate

comments.issue: Single-axis specialists may be misclassified as multidimensional depending on habitat definition and rarity.
comments.request: Demonstrate that multidimensional specialists are restrictive on all axes.
comments.quote: a specialist taxon for a particular axis only (generalist for other axes) may be classified as a multidimensional specialist

comments.issue: Only 2-8 plots per habitat on average may not capture enough variation to identify specialists.
comments.request: Provide information supporting the validity of specialist identification.
comments.quote: This limited number of plots per habitat may not account for enough variation to accurately identify multidimensional specialists

comments.issue: Less abundant taxa are more likely classified as specialists due to proportional similarity.
comments.request: Apply LOD and statistical guidance (e.g. Finn et al.).
comments.quote: the more different a taxon's proportion is from the habitat proportion (less abundant), the more likely it is to be identified as a specialist

comments.issue: Constrained specialists should be detected in very few plots; this prediction is not tested.
comments.request: Investigate specialist occupancy to support the conclusions.
comments.quote: I suspect that these severe constraints limit each specialist taxon to being only significantly detected in a very limited number of locations or plots

comments.issue: Concluding sensitivity to all seven factors requires many habitat combinations that may be absent.
comments.request: Explain how sensitivity to all seven axes is established.
comments.quote: many possible combinations of the 7 factors are needed to conclude that a taxon is sensitive to all 7

reviews.assessment: Values the elegant three-pronged analysis but finds the analysis limited and the network methods too poorly described to interpret.
strengths: useful conceptual framework for microbial niche breadth
rare taxa as network hubs interesting and timely

comments.issue: It is unclear how niche breadth advances predictive understanding, conservation or management of soil communities.
comments.request: Explain the practical and predictive value of this framework.
comments.quote: it is not clear how this can be used to further our predictive understanding of soil communities or our conservation and management of them

comments.issue: Multi-year NEON data omitted; temporal associations and within-site variability not analyzed.
comments.request: Analyze and report temporal associations between taxa and environment.
comments.quote: there are multiple years of NEON data, and I wonder what the temporal associations between taxa and environmental parameters would show re: niches

comments.issue: Dispersal mode and range, relevant traits for microbial lineages, are not explored.
comments.request: Explore and report dispersal mode and range.
comments.quote: certainly dispersal mode and range is often an important trait for microbial lineages, such that it is probably worth exploring and reporting here

comments.issue: Environmental axes chosen are all growth-suitable; other characteristics such as metals or texture untested.
comments.request: Discuss this limitation and consider other environmental characteristics.
comments.quote: Niche breadth was also calculated with environmental factors that are actually all pretty much suited to supporting bacterial growth (as far as I can tell)

comments.issue: It is unclear at what taxonomic scale the generalist/specialist bifurcation disappears.
comments.request: Test the pattern across taxonomic scales.
comments.quote: At what taxonomic scale does the generalization/speciation bifurcation break down?

comments.issue: Methods do not state how many samples define a taxon's niche breadth within a site.
comments.request: Report sample numbers and habitat breadth details.
comments.quote: it is not clear how many samples were used for a taxon to determine it's "niche breadth" within a site

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation in community composition may create similar habitats and communities within sites.
comments.request: Describe how spatial autocorrelation was accounted for.
comments.quote: many plots within a site have similar habitats and communities, simply because of spatial autocorrelation (not because of environmental niches, per se)

comments.issue: Network inputs (samples, filtration cutoffs, taxa counts) are missing, risking spurious correlations.
comments.request: Report network construction details.
comments.quote: If too many taxa were used for too few samples, then the network will show spurious correlations

comments.issue: Taxonomic resolution used to build the networks is not stated.
comments.request: State the network taxonomic level.
comments.quote: What level of taxonomy was used to build the networks? ASVs, genera, etc?

comments.issue: Consistency of nodes and node functions across compared networks is unknown.
comments.request: Check and report node consistency across networks.
comments.quote: How consistent are nodes/node functions across networks that are being compared?

comments.issue: Whether network conclusions hold in a continental network with all samples is untested.
comments.request: Run a continental network analysis.
comments.quote: Do the network conclusions still hold when making a continental network with all samples?

comments.issue: Impacts of taxa on ecosystem functions cannot be isolated without a controlled experiment.
comments.request: Rephrase as correlations or relationships.
comments.quote: There is no way to isolate the "impacts" of specialist/generalist taxa on ecosystem functions in the absence of a controlled experiment

comments.issue: Taxonomic resolution used in the first analysis is not stated.
comments.request: Specify the taxonomic resolution throughout.
comments.quote: What taxonomic resolution is being used for this first analysis?

comments.issue: Standard cutoff may not be right; unidimensional specialists deserve characterization.
comments.request: Identify and explain the unidimensional specialist taxa.
comments.quote: In Figure 1a, it does look like quite a few taxa are unidimensional (or maybe bidimensional) specialists, which is pretty cool.

comments.issue: Unclear whether environmental correlations are across sites while niche breadths are within site.
comments.request: Clarify analysis levels and cite Figure S4.
comments.quote: Are the environmental correlations across sites, whereas the niche breadths were within site?

comments.issue: Figure 5 does not make the functional aspects of taxa clear.
comments.request: Illustrate functional aspects on the main figure.
comments.quote: It's not clear to me how Figure 5 shows these functional aspects of the taxa

comments.issue: Batch differences between Argonne and Battelle 16S libraries are unaddressed.
comments.request: Explain how the batch effects were handled.
comments.quote: 16S datasets from NEON are very different between the Argonne libraries (2015 and prior) and the Battelle libraries (after 2015). How did the authors handle these methodological/batch effects?

comments.issue: Averaging subsamples discards data; rationale versus repeated-measures analysis is missing.
comments.request: Provide rationale or run repeated-measures analysis.
comments.quote: Could you please provide rationale for why this approach was taken, rather than including as much data as possible and conducting repeated measures analysis?

comments.issue: Rationale for the 30-bin habitat definition is not given.
comments.request: Justify the number of bins.
comments.quote: Why were 30 bins chosen to construct "habitats" along environmental axes?

title: Multidimensional specialization and generalization are pervasive in soil prokaryotes

study.system: tetrapods; 7,009 species in 56 clades, biogeographic models

reviews.assessment: Substantial, easy-to-follow study with three main contributions, though some methods descriptions are unclear and Figure 2 needs improvement.
strengths: new insights into trait-shaped biogeography at global scale
successful application of cutting-edge biogeographic and phylogenetic methods
thorough data collection and in-depth interpretation

comments.issue: MDMMs and BioGeoBEARS models are not described; unclear what ecological processes they estimate.
comments.request: Add short model descriptions and details on trait incorporation.
comments.quote: Methods like MDMMs and the BioGeoBEARS models would benefit from a short description like those found in the previous work Weil et al. Without prior knowledge it is not clear what exact ecological/biological processes these models are estimating.

comments.issue: Body size and life history are inferred latent traits, not directly observed, and the PFA is not explained early enough.
comments.request: State this early and explain latent factors and loadings.
comments.quote: it should be stated earlier that body size and life size history are not directly observed but inferred traits

comments.issue: The meaning of 'extreme' in Fig 2b,c and the models behind Fig 2c AICc are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the figure and specify the tested models.
comments.quote: Figure 2 can be improved. I only figured out the meaning of “extreme” in 2(b)(c) much later in the text. Also, which specific models were tested to get the AICc results in 2(c)?

comments.issue: It is not explained why PFA is run per clade rather than once per tetrapod class.
comments.request: Justify the per-clade PFA choice.
comments.quote: Why PFA is applied to all clades separately, instead of one PFA per major class (amphibians, mammals, birds, reptiles)?

comments.issue: Clades may be treated as independent in the regressions, ignoring evolutionary relationships.
comments.request: Justify the independence assumption or account for phylogeny.
comments.quote: In the regression analysis to detect factors affecting the trait-dispersal links, are clades treated as independent of each other? If so, the authors should justify why ignoring the evolutionary relationship here is not a problem.

comments.issue: 'Better biogeographic models' is vague and lacks performance details.
comments.request: Use specific statistical language or report performance.
comments.quote: I suggest changing wording like “better biogeographic models” to more specific statistical language, or adding some performance details when claiming “better models”.

comments.issue: AICc is not spelled out at first use.
comments.request: Spell out AICc at first appearance.
comments.quote: AICc should be spelled out when it first appeared in the text.

reviews.assessment: Original, significant and well-executed study with appropriate methods and valid conclusions, though some claims are overgeneralised and the text needs clarification.
strengths: considers confounding variables such as phylogenetic uncertainty

comments.issue: Macroevolutionary dispersal is conflated with ecological/population dispersal in the introduction and conclusion.
comments.request: Define the dispersal type studied and distinguish the two concepts.
comments.quote: The authors study macroevolutionary/lineage dispersal, but in several places in the introduction and conclusion, it is confounded with ecological/population dispersal.

comments.issue: Global claims about traits shaping the diversity of life are overgeneralised from two trait syndromes and one clade.
comments.request: Tone down claims and use precise trait terms in title and conclusion.
comments.quote: This should be toned down; with all due respect for this large analysis and the effort involved, the authors have only studied two trait syndromes and one (comparatively small) small clade of life on earth.

comments.issue: Clade crown ages differ and may drive the signal; they are not reported or controlled for.
comments.request: Report crown ages and consider them as control variables.
comments.quote: I miss some awareness and discussion of phylogenetic scale: The crown divergences of the different clades studied probably differ quite a lot – how could this have affected the analysis?

comments.issue: Phylogenetic uncertainty, notably in Natricinae, is concerning; node support is not used as a control.
comments.request: Include average node support as a control variable.
comments.quote: The impact in Natricinae on the conclusions is somewhat concerning but I do understand the computational limitations. Could one rough approach to account for uncertainty be the inclusion of average node support as control variable in the downstream analyses?

comments.issue: Adding any free parameter improves fit, so trait effects may be spurious type I errors.
comments.request: Discuss this risk and consider hidden-state models.
comments.quote: I also wonder about the risk of inferring spurious trait effects (type I error) simply because any free parameter added generally improves model fit in macroevolution.

comments.issue: Extinction could affect the results, including possible tradeoffs with dispersal traits, but is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how extinction could shape these relationships.
comments.quote: I would like to see at least some discussion of how extinction could have impacted the results – the models used also estimate an extinction parameter, e.

comments.issue: Effect sizes are not translated into real-world numbers such as extra dispersal events.
comments.request: Translate dispersal-rate effects into real-world numbers.
comments.quote: It may be useful for the reader to translate the parameters and effect sizes estimated (i.e. dispersal rate) into real-world numbers in the discussion.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 16-19 is long and convoluted.
comments.request: Split it in two.
comments.quote: 16-19 - long, convolute sentence, split in two?

comments.issue: Statements about dispersal are not scoped to tetrapods versus all organisms.
comments.request: Clarify what applies to tetrapods.
comments.quote: it should be made clear here what applies to tetrapods vs. animals or all organisms. Eg. line 32 (“Short-distance dispersal is primarily determined by active movements”) certainly does not apply to plants!

comments.issue: 'General trait-dispersal bias' is unclear.
comments.request: Reword this phrase.
comments.quote: Line 47, “general trait-dispersal bias” – not clear to me what bias is meant here, can you reword?

comments.issue: The 'significant' small number of nodes and the vague following sentence may be unnecessary.
comments.request: Clarify or remove this passage.
comments.quote: Line 113 - Why is the small number of nodes “significant” here? As the following sentence seems quite vague to me, I wonder if this part is really necessary.

comments.issue: 'Class' is ambiguous with trait classes; 'tetrapod class' would be clearer.
comments.request: Use 'tetrapod class' throughout.
comments.quote: the use of “class” is sometimes confusing, as one could think of the trait bins/classes. Maybe use “tetrapod class” throughout for clarity?

comments.issue: The estimated parameter of interest (dispersal rate d?) is not named.
comments.request: Name the dispersal-rate parameter in DEC and other models.
comments.quote: it would be useful here for the reader to name the parameter of interest (dispersal rate – d?) that is estimated in DEC and the other models.

comments.issue: The model selection is problematic because models differ in node events and vicariance types, not free parameters.
comments.request: Use one model or include model type as a control variable.
comments.quote: Model selection is problematic here because these models do not differ in their free parameters, only in the events allowed at nodes

comments.issue: Missing 'of' at line 597.
comments.request: Fix the sentence.
comments.quote: 597 - The effect - "of" missing

comments.issue: Fig 1 inset phylogenies and maps are too crammed; simpler colour codes, ages and species numbers would help.
comments.request: Simplify Figure 1.
comments.quote: Fig. 1 - The small inset phylogenies and the maps are not really helpful, too much information crammed in.

comments.issue: Fig 2 needs a common colour legend; 2a requires the caption.
comments.request: Add a shared colour legend.
comments.quote: Fig. 2 - a common colour legend would be helpful. For 2a the reader has to refer to the caption.

comments.issue: The 50% line is not highlighted in Fig 2c.
comments.request: Highlight the 50% line.
comments.quote: Fig 2c - it would be helpful to highlight the 50% line.

comments.issue: Fig 2d symbols for rows and columns may not match the legend's combinations.
comments.request: Check the symbols against the legend.
comments.quote: Fig. 2d - check if the symbols for rows and columns make sense – according to the legend, they indicate _combinations_ of body size and life history.

comments.issue: Fig 3a has lots of white space and could be larger.
comments.request: Increase the figure size.
comments.quote: Fig 3a - could the figure size be increased? Lots of white space.

comments.issue: Extended data table 1 is missing; only its caption appears.
comments.request: Provide the missing table.
comments.quote: Extended data table 1 is missing, I only see the caption.

title: Body size and life history shape the historical biogeography of tetrapods

study.system: East African proboscideans; 26 Myr dental morphology, diet and climate proxies

editor_summary: Reviewers raise concerns to address; editor notes reviewer 2's point about lack of causal evidence without phylogenetic tests and reviewer 1's request to discuss grass phytoliths and dust; otherwise minor comments.

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the contribution but finds the article type unclear and the flow inconsistent.
strengths: will contribute largely to understanding habitat and diet roles in elephant dental evolution

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the paper is a review or a research report, and key guiding sections are not clearly outlined, making the flow inconsistent.
comments.request: Clarify the article type and outline the key sections.
comments.quote: However, it is not clear if this aper is a review article or a research report because key sections that would guide the reader are not clearly outlined.

reviews.assessment: Sound, elegant analysis with convincing patterns, but causal and key-innovation language must be toned down.
strengths: solid and fascinating methods and evidence

comments.issue: The language claims key innovations and definitive causation although the analysis only shows strong correlations and no phylogenetic tests were done.
comments.request: Soften the causal and key-innovation language or add phylogenetic tests.
comments.quote: I would strongly suggest the authors back down a bit on the language suggesting key innovations or that this pattern is definitively causative because their analysis does not show either of these things

comments.issue: 'Preadaptation' is a problematic and teleological construction that can be misinterpreted.
comments.request: Rethink or replace the preadaptation sentence.
comments.quote: Further, this MS uses an awkward sentence referring to 'preadaptation', which is a problematic and teleological construction

comments.issue: Grammatical changes are suggested throughout the text.
comments.request: Implement the suggested grammatical changes.
comments.quote: I have made suggestions in the text for some grammatical changes as well.

reviews.assessment: Ambitious, accessible work with only minor taxonomy and wording issues; recommends minor revision.
strengths: ambitious work tracing proboscidean dental evolution
unexpected results taken at face value

comments.issue: Taxonomy is inconsistent: family lists, figures and tables use different classifications, and paraphyletic 'Gomphotheriidae' is used without qualification.
comments.request: Use consistent taxonomy and qualify gomphothere usage.
comments.quote: Obviously, “Gomphotheriidae” in the figure and tables corresponds to ‘gomphotheres’ as used throughout the text, i.e. a paraphyletic assemblage and should probably be replaced with the latter to avoid confusion.

comments.issue: Third molars are meant at l. 149 but this is only stated much later at l. 612.
comments.request: Mention the third molars at first use.
comments.quote: l. 149: obviously third molars are meant but this is only mentioned on l. 612.

comments.issue: Whether the loph increase was also connected with aridification in Stegodontidae is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of this pattern.
comments.quote: l. 247/8: was increase in loph connected with aridification in Stegodontidae too?

comments.issue: Whether the statement at l. 269 applies to Elephantidae only or to elephantoids generally is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the taxonomic scope.
comments.quote: l. 269: I am not quite sure if this relates to Elephantidae only or to elephantoids in general?

comments.issue: The reference to true elephants at 9 Ma needs a clarification or reminder at l. 346.
comments.request: Add a clarifying reminder.
comments.quote: l. 346: Since there are no known true elephants at 9 Ma I suppose this relates to lines 147-149

comments.issue: The idea of Tetralophodon as elephant stem group traces at least to Pascal Tassy's mid-1980s work, which is not acknowledged.
comments.request: Cite the earlier work.
comments.quote: The idea of Tetralophodon as the stem group of elephants can be traced, I believe, at least to the mid-80s, in a works by Pascal Tassy.

comments.issue: 'Loph-like structures called lophids' is unclear; lophs belong to upper and lophids to lower teeth.
comments.request: Correct the terminology.
comments.quote: l. 45, “loph-like structures called lophids”: I am not sure what is meant here. Lophs are structures of the upper teeth, and lophids of the lower ones.

comments.issue: 'Lamellae narrower' at l. 58 means antero-posteriorly shorter but is potentially confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: l. 58: lamellae narrower – obviously, antero-posteriorly shorter is meant but can be potentially confusing in my opinion.

comments.issue: Sanders et al. (2010) on late Miocene Stegodon in Africa is not cited.
comments.request: Add the Sanders et al. (2010) citation.
comments.quote: l. 60: for late Miocene Stegodon in Africa see e.g. Sanders et al. (2010)

title: Fluctuating climate and dietary innovation drove ratcheted evolution of proboscidean dental traits

study.system: Australian frogs and chytrid fungus; occurrence records, niche hypervolumes and BACI analysis

editor_summary: All three referees enthusiastic; address Referee 3's concern over not using a standard niche-dynamics protocol, improve figure presentation (Referees 1 and 3), and respond to all criticisms before a decision.

reviews.assessment: Innovative in scale but not original, with the robustness of the detected signals limited by sampling-bias and variable-selection concerns.
strengths: addresses the emerging role of biotic interactions in realized niches
innovative implementation across large geographic, temporal and taxonomic ranges
comprehensive dataset with contemporary modelling techniques

comments.issue: The paper is innovative in scope but not original, as similar assessments already exist.
comments.quote: The paper is innovative but not original. That is, the authors did a fair work to acknowledge similar work by others in this type of assessment.

comments.issue: Constant sampling effort is assumed for all taxa and areas; ignoring surveillance bias reduces transparency.
comments.request: Address variation in surveillance and underreporting.
comments.quote: A major assumption in the study is a constant sampling effort for all taxa across all study areas

comments.issue: Temperature, moisture and elevation variables are likely correlated, and the selection of the three variables is not justified.
comments.request: Provide a correlation test and justify variable selection.
comments.quote: Generally it would seem like 'Annual Mean Temprature' 'Mean Temp of the Driest Quarter' and 'Elevation' would all be correlated in some way, and if that is the case only one of them should be used.

comments.issue: Bioclimatic variables combining temperature and precipitation contain known errors, and variable choice may drive the signals.
comments.request: Run models with different variable combinations to test robustness.
comments.quote: The study requires more models with different variable combinations to determine the extent to which the signals of niche contraction remain constant no matter the environmental parameters used.

comments.issue: Directionality of niche centroid shifts was not tested statistically; interpretation relies on visual inspection.
comments.request: Test the directionality of niche centroid shifts statistically.
comments.quote: Directionality of the 'niche centroid shifts' was not measured statistically. In fact, interpretation of this and other patters was based on a hunch or limited to visual inspection of plots.

comments.issue: Maps are severely lacking for a paper comparing geographic and environmental expansion and contraction.
comments.request: Add maps of geographic and environmental change.
comments.quote: There is severe lack of maps, which seems strange for an article comparing geographic and environmental expansion/contraction.

comments.issue: The mapping method is one of many; the niche-versus-range contraction conclusion may not hold with other methods.
comments.request: Compare species ranges using additional mapping methods.
comments.quote: main conclusion of the paper regarding higher niche contraction than geographic contraction could not remain consistent under other strategies to map the species ranges

comments.issue: Figures are poorly informative; Fig. 2's horizontal layout makes relative changes hard to see.
comments.request: Redesign Fig. 2 so changes can be compared easily.
comments.quote: Figures are poorly informative. For example, figure 2 suggests a negative change for both impacted and non-impacted groups, seeing the changes relative to one another is somewhat difficult with the figure set up horizontally as it is now.

comments.issue: Fig. 5 interpretation is based on a hunch without supporting values and is hard to interpret.
comments.request: Quantify arrow lengths or use another display summarizing the findings.
comments.quote: Figure 5, the whole point and interpretation is based on a hunch. Authors do not provide values to sustain the patterns discussed. This figure is particularly unclear and hard to interpret.

comments.issue: Criteria defining impacted versus non-impacted species are unclear and require reading another paper.
comments.request: State the impacted and non-impacted species criteria.
comments.quote: The criteria used to define impacted vs not impacted species are unclear in the present study. It seems that another papers must be read to understand a fundamental step in this paper.

comments.issue: 'Niche' is not explicitly defined as the ecological niche.
comments.request: Define niche explicitly as the ecological niche.
comments.quote: 'niche' should be more explicitly defined, hopefully referring to the "ecological niche"

comments.issue: 'Recipient ecological communities' is left undefined in this context.
comments.request: Define the term or use alternate phrasing.
comments.quote: 'Recipient ecological communities' on line 99 should also either be defined in this context, or alternate phrasing should be used.

comments.issue: βdiversity is not defined like βrichness and βreplacement, and βreplacement is vague; 'space between hypervolumes' is unclear.
comments.request: Define βdiversity and βreplacement clearly.
comments.quote: In your results, βdiversity should be parenthetically defined on line 147 as βrichness and βreplacement are defined. Additionally, βreplacement is defined vaguely throughout

comments.issue: Line 332 wording is confusing about why some EOOs were larger post-chytrid and how this was addressed.
comments.request: Clarify these sentences.
comments.quote: line 332, the wording is somewhat confusing and does not clearly explain i) why some EOOs were larger post chytrid or ii) how this was addressed.

comments.issue: The 0-1 ratio method for niche centroid shift direction is unclear; an in-text formula would help.
comments.request: Add an in-text formula and a clearer explanation.
comments.quote: the later half of the paragraph on Niche Centroid Shifts (beginning on line 343) where you define the methods you use to calculate the 0-1 ratio indicating the direction and extent of the niche shift is unclear

comments.issue: Unclear why full EOO values were used for lines 228-341 but not earlier.
comments.request: Explain the change in EOO usage.
comments.quote: Lines 228-341: Unclear. Why were full EOO values used here but not before?

comments.issue: How and why 200 post-Bd models were constructed is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the construction of the 200 post-Bd models.
comments.quote: It is unclear how/why were 200 post-Bd models constructed

comments.issue: Measurement of niche centroid directionality is not understood; an equation or diagram would help.
comments.request: Add an equation or diagram for the centroid directionality measure.
comments.quote: The way to measure the directionality of niche centroids is intriguing but I am not sure I understand how this was measured and what it means biologically.

reviews.assessment: Fascinating, sound study; asks for minor edits plus framing conservation implications earlier and adding comparative predictions.
strengths: logic sound and methodological approaches appropriate

comments.issue: Conservation and management implications are not foreshadowed in the introduction or flagged in several sentences (L68, 88, 91, 93, 95).
comments.request: Add conservation-planning context early and expand the relevant sentences.
comments.quote: The implications for species conservation planning should be foreshadowed in the introduction to keep that context in sight for a sector of readers that need the "so what" explained early.

comments.issue: The discussion does not compare this story with other adaptations seen in response to Bd waves.
comments.request: Compare these findings with other documented adaptations to Bd.
comments.quote: At the end, I wanted a comparison of this story with other adaptations being seen in response to Bd waves.

comments.issue: A prediction about how Bd itself might evolve (reduced virulence, changed niches) is missing from the conclusion.
comments.request: Add predictions about pathogen evolution, including possible leap-frogging adaptations.
comments.quote: Also, a prediction missing at the conclusion of the paper is how the threat agent itself also would be expected to evolve: for reduced virulence, for changed realized niches to follow hosts, possibly both.

comments.issue: The abstract sentence at lines 62-63 is hard to parse and should be simplified.
comments.request: Simplify and reword the abstract sentence.
comments.quote: I had to read this a couple of times to get it straight before I read the paper. Could simplify/reword

comments.issue: A conceptual schematic of how heterogeneity retains resilience could help convey the message.
comments.request: Consider developing a conceptual schematic figure.
comments.quote: I wonder if you could develop a conceptual schematic figure?

comments.issue: The upcoming Red List status update paper (Luedtke) is not cited.
comments.request: Cite the Red List status update if accepted.
comments.quote: Upon revision, contact Jennifer Luedtke to see if her Red List status update paper is accepted; should be cited here, if so.

comments.issue: Olson et al. 2021 on Bd climate niches is not mentioned in the introduction or discussion.
comments.request: Reference Olson et al. 2021 and discuss continental differences and Bd variants.
comments.quote: this paper may warrant referencing at the end of the Discussion because it shows that the Bd climate niche in Australia has differences from other continents

comments.issue: Red-green and yellow colours are not colourblind-safe or legible, and a colour index and visible centroids are needed (L138, L572, L590, L613).
comments.request: Use colourblind-safe colours, add a colour index and outline centroids in black.
comments.quote: the red-green contrast needs to be changed in first figure and you can't just name the colors in the caption if red-green colorblind readers aren't able to distinguish them

comments.issue: A sentence noting that the directional arrows concur with the previous result should be added.
comments.request: Add a sentence about the concurring directional patterns.
comments.quote: This concurs with previous result, so worth pointing it out.

comments.issue: Only an association is shown, so cause-effect language must be toned down to a conditional context.
comments.request: Tone down causal language at line 181 and elsewhere.
comments.quote: You have compelling data, but at the heart of the analyses, you still just have an association, so you need to be careful of the inference you are making, and cause-effect language needs to be toned down to a conditional context.

comments.issue: 'Loss of species' is unclear as a biological or spatial unit.
comments.request: Clarify or replace the unit of loss.
comments.quote: 'loss of species' is not sounding right to me, it's the right biological unit, I think, or the spatial unit needs more clarification

comments.issue: Landscape genetics follow-up work in the study area is suggested as future research.
comments.request: Consider landscape genetics follow-up in the study area.
comments.quote: Would be cool to follow up with landscape genetics work in your study area.

comments.issue: Additional analyses (fragmentation statistics) could test whether the swiss-cheese niche changes are detectable another way.
comments.request: Apply fragmentation statistics to the authors' own data as a cross-check.
comments.quote: Could you suggest application of fragmentation statistics/analytics to tease apart spp spatial heterogeneity patterns?

comments.issue: Precipitation seasonality is not explained where first used and may not be intuitive.
comments.request: Define precipitation seasonality in the text.
comments.quote: insert clarification so reader doesn't need to go to Methods to understand this metric

comments.issue: Using temperature range instead of the chosen measures might change the result.
comments.request: Test whether using Temp Range changes the results.
comments.quote: I do wonder if you would have gotten a different result if you had used Temp Range, which came up in that Olson et al. 2021 paper as the main predictor of Bd occurrence in Australia.

comments.issue: How precipitation seasonality was calculated is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how precipitation seasonality was calculated.
comments.quote: Here, explain how precip seasonality was calculated. This metric may not be intuitive to some readers.

comments.issue: 'Systematic range expansion' on line 314 is not defined.
comments.request: Clarify what systematic range expansion means.
comments.quote: also what do you mean by "systematic range expansion"

comments.issue: The first sentence of the line-613 caption is convoluted.
comments.request: Simplify the caption's first sentence.
comments.quote: First sentence of caption could be simplified as follows to make less convoluted

comments.issue: Supplementary Fig. 1 is faint and would be valuable in the main paper; 'crosses' should be 'X's and the wording needs fixing.
comments.request: Move Fig. S1 to the main text, fix colours and wording.
comments.quote: I wanted this image in the main paper! Yellow is not coming through on my screen very well, extremely faint color.

comments.issue: Supplementary Fig. 2 would also be valuable in the main paper, and years should be added to its caption or index.
comments.request: Move Fig. S2 to the main text and add years to the caption or image.
comments.quote: I wanted this figure in the main paper too! Caption seems to say colors relate to years, so can you put years in the caption or index on the image?

comments.issue: Many line-level copy edits across the review (grammar, tense, word choice, hyphens, italics, punctuation).
comments.quote: 83: change to plural "phenomena" to sync with plural "niche shifts" on previous line

reviews.assessment: Interesting contribution, but the data partitioning, non-standard niche-dynamics protocol and niche representation raise major concerns.
strengths: relevant for amphibian conservation and global change
comparison of impacted and non-impacted related species is cool and useful

comments.issue: The 'pre' niche uses the full time period plus a post-emergence subset, which may mask expansions and shifts and is not justified (also L306-309, L336-338, L364, L374-379).
