comments.request: Analyse true pre- and post-emergence subsets or justify the partition.
comments.quote: I think, this partition could mask the actual dynamics of both ranges and niches, overlooking for example cases of niche expansion or range shifts.

comments.issue: The approach departs from the standard COUE niche-dynamics protocol without justification.
comments.request: Justify using the implemented approach instead of COUE.
comments.quote: given the frequent use of COUE for this kind of studies, would be nice to justify why the method you chose is more appropriate for your purposes

comments.issue: Bivariate panels of the same niche are hard to interpret, and Fig. 5 suggests changes in both groups may be random; a full multivariate representation is needed.
comments.request: Show full multivariate hypervolumes for pre and post periods.
comments.quote: Please consider to provide also a full representation of the niche where the reader could be able to see the magnitud and direction of shifts in the full environmental space.

comments.issue: Line 57 should say 'one of the key mechanisms' to reflect the multifactorial nature of global change.
comments.request: Reword to 'one of the key mechanisms'.
comments.quote: I would say 2 "one of the key mechanisms", to recognize the multifactorial nature of global change and biodiversity re-configuration.

comments.issue: The type of niche (climatic) should be stated explicitly throughout the manuscript.
comments.request: Add 'climatic' when referring to niches.
comments.quote: I would suggest adding "climatic" when referring to niches through the MS. We know how broad the definition of niche is

comments.issue: The implication that species pushed to niche edges face higher extinction risk is not highlighted.
comments.request: Discuss edge-of-niche conditions and extinction risk.
comments.quote: it would be good to highlight here the issue associated to the fact of species being pushed towards the edge of their known niches (and likely physiological tolerances)

comments.issue: Pathogens and emerging diseases as a component of global change are not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention pathogen-driven emerging diseases in the invasion context.
comments.quote: it is worth to mention the specific case of pathogens and emergent diseases as a component of global change that require special attention

comments.issue: Anderson (2017) on biotic interactions in niche models is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Anderson (2017) here or nearby.
comments.quote: Anderson, R. P. (2017). When and how should biotic interactions be considered in models of species niches and distributions?

comments.issue: The contribution of studying native hosts rather than alien species is not emphasized.
comments.request: Highlight that the study addresses the native side of novel interactions.
comments.quote: A relevant contribution of your work is looking at the other side of the coin, the native species which implicitly involves a novel interaction

comments.issue: The prediction that lower extinction risk follows proportionately smaller niche reductions ignores habitat availability and carrying capacity.
comments.request: Adjust the prediction or explain it better.
comments.quote: I am not fully convinced with this argument: "In contrast, if niche reductions are proportionately less than range reductions, the risk of extinction may be lower".

comments.issue: The late-1970s introduction date lacks a precise citation.
comments.request: Cite a precise source for the introduction date.
comments.quote: I think the supposed date of introduction (late 1970s) requires a more precise citation.

comments.issue: Contractions attributed to Bd cannot be fully separated from other drivers.
comments.request: Strengthen attribution of contractions to Bd rather than other drivers.
comments.quote: From the beginning I was wondering whether you were able to tease apart niche or range contractions attributed to Bd to those related to other drivers.

comments.issue: Selection of the two species shown in Fig. 1 is not justified as representative of the general trend.
comments.request: Justify the species choice and its representativeness.
comments.quote: It is also worth to better justify the selection of the two species included in Fig.1. Are them representative of the general trend found?

comments.issue: The minimum sample size for including or excluding species is not stated.
comments.request: Specify the minimum sample size threshold.
comments.quote: Please specify the minimum sample size considered to include/exclude a species in/from the analysis.

comments.issue: Unclear whether the other species' realized niches are pre- or post-chytrid, and why the comparison is informative.
comments.request: Clarify and justify these comparisons.
comments.quote: The realized pre or post chytrid niches of the other species? Please clarify and justify for what this would be informative.

comments.issue: The roughly 200 km buffer may be too large for these species, and 50% polygon increases near coasts may fall in the ocean.
comments.request: Justify the buffer distance and coastal handling.
comments.quote: 2 degrees is approximately 200km, is not that too much considering both the dispersal abilities of these species and the well documented distributions of amphibians in Australia?

comments.issue: The decision at L274-275 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain that the decision follows the climatic data resolution.
comments.quote: I suppose this decision was taken based on the resolution of the climatic data, right? Maybe good to add it here to justify this action.

comments.issue: The Supplementary Fig. 2 legend lacks the estimated year of Bd emergence.
comments.request: Add emergence years to the legend.
comments.quote: the legend includes the names of the regions, but it lacks the estimated year of emergence of Bd

comments.issue: Using the full record set as the 'distribution before BD' is not justified.
comments.request: Justify or change the pre-BD baseline.
comments.quote: Not completely clear why assuming the full set of records as the "distribution before BD". Please elaborate more on this and ideally provide a solid justification.

comments.issue: The weak elevation-temperature correlation should be checked with an independent climatic dataset.
comments.request: Repeat the correlation test with CHELSA as a sensitivity analysis.
comments.quote: it is worth to double-check if this weak correlation is consistent using a different climatic dataset such as CHELSA. It would be useful as sensitivity analysis

comments.issue: The argument at L311-314 lacks empirical support; pre- and post-BD occurrences are not plotted.
comments.request: Plot pre- and post-BD occurrences, for example as supplementary maps.
comments.quote: The argument presented here should be ideally supported with empirical evidence. One easy way to do it is to simply plot the pre and post BD occurrences for each species with different colors.

comments.issue: Why 200 post-BD hypervolumes were generated is unclear given the resampling was based on post-BD occurrence numbers.
comments.request: Explain the 200 hypervolume resampling procedure.
comments.quote: Not clear why did you get 200 post-BD hypervolumes if the resampling was conducted on the full dataset based on the number of post-BD occurrences.

comments.issue: Using post-BD occurrences for both niche definitions and EOOs may be redundant.
comments.request: Clarify whether this reuse is redundant.
comments.quote: I am still dealing with understanding whether is an issue of redundancy to use twice the post BD occurrences for the definition of niches and EOO's.

comments.issue: Detected reductions may reflect lack of sampling rather than true extirpations, and sampling effort differs among regional timeframes.
comments.request: Assess sampling completeness and account for regional timeframes.
comments.quote: Do you have information on the status of all pre-emergence populations to ensure that the reductions detected correspond to data partitioning true extirpations and not lack of sampling?

comments.issue: The combined effects of invasion and climate change on biota reconfiguration are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss invasion plus climate-change effects.
comments.quote: it would be nice to go mention the combined effects of invasion and climate change in the reconfiguration of biotas

comments.issue: Climatic refugia from disease and the Puschendorf et al. reference are missing.
comments.request: Discuss climatic refugia and cite Puschendorf et al.
comments.quote: persistence could be dictated by the existence of climatic refugia from disease

comments.issue: Re-colonization of upland areas under warming is not considered.
comments.request: Discuss expected re-colonization of uplands as temperatures increase.
comments.quote: Again, would you expect a re-colonization of upland areas, as temperature increase?

comments.issue: The upland climatic variability argument needs a citation or empirical support.
comments.request: Add a citation, or map/regress climatic variability against elevation.
comments.quote: would be good to provide a citation. In the worst case, you could easily provide evidence of this by simply mapping climatic variability through the region

comments.issue: Well-known statements at L211-212 lack citations.
comments.request: Add citations.
comments.quote: L211-212: This is well-known but please add citations.

comments.issue: The inputs needed to estimate niche dynamics and their feasibility for most species are not provided.
comments.request: Provide what is needed for the niche dynamics estimation.
comments.quote: I think it is worth to provide what is needed for the estimation of niche dynamics proposed to inform how realistic and feasible it would be for most species.

title: An invasive pathogen drives directional niche contractions in amphibians

study.system: kākāpō population genomics; whole-genome sequencing, GWAS

editor_summary: Editor: three reviewers raised concerns needing revision, plus editorial concerns; invites revised manuscript with responses and highlighted changes.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and original study; wants clearer management use of GWAS results, more on outlier regions, ROH distributions and enrichment analyses.
strengths: results highly pertinent to kākāpō conservation
broad implications for endangered species genomics

comments.issue: The discussion lacks specific detail on how GWAS results will be used in management.
comments.request: Describe concrete management applications of the GWAS results.
comments.quote: I would be nice to see more specific detail in the discussion about how the GWAS results in particular will be used.

comments.issue: Local PCA outlier regions are never characterized or explained.
comments.request: Report what is in the outlier regions and why.
comments.quote: the authors mention outlier regions from their local PCA method, but never say anything more about what is in those regions, or why they would be outliers

comments.issue: Only the mean ROH length is reported; the distribution would better reveal inbreeding effects.
comments.request: Analyse the distribution of ROH lengths.
comments.quote: I think looking at the distribution of ROH, rather than just the mean, would be more informative to infer any effects of inbreeding.

comments.issue: No enrichment analysis tests whether GWAS gene lists over-represent pathways.
comments.request: Run a pathway enrichment analysis.
comments.quote: perhaps undertaking an enrichment analysis would be interesting to see if there are any over-represented pathways in the lists of genes

comments.issue: Line numbers are missing throughout.
comments.request: Add line numbers.
comments.quote: Line numbers would have been useful throughout – hopefully it will be clear what my comments are pertaining to in text

comments.issue: It is unclear whether hatching/embryo failures are attributed to inbreeding.
comments.request: State the attribution of these failures.
comments.quote: Kakapo have a low reproductive rate – are the hatching failure/embryo failures attributed to inbreeding?

comments.issue: Figure 1 colours are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Improve the colour scheme.
comments.quote: Fig 1 – the colours are a bit difficult to tell apart

comments.issue: DeepVariant coverage up to 1000x and GQ 10 filtering seem too permissive for confident regions.
comments.request: Justify or tighten the filtering thresholds.
comments.quote: retaining coverage up to 1000x seems high as most people use 2X average depth. Using a minimum GQ score of 10 also seems low, would it not be better to use very strict filtering to identify the ‘confident regions’?

comments.issue: The phrase 'For the other phenotypes' does not clearly define which phenotypes.
comments.request: List the phenotypes meant.
comments.quote: Under the section ‘phenotype collection and processing’, the start of the paragraph ‘For the other phenotypes’ is unclear. You mean all phenotypes excluding egg shape and aspergillosis susceptibility?

comments.issue: The supplementary aspergillosis methods contain 'n=xx' placeholders.
comments.request: Replace with actual numbers.
comments.quote: In the supplementary methods for ‘Aspergillosis susceptibility’ it says ‘n=xx’ twice where I assume there are supposed to be actual numbers?

comments.issue: The founding heterozygosity value 0.238 may be a typo for 0.233.
comments.request: Check this value.
comments.quote: Heterozygosity of the founding population is 0.238 in the table, which is higher? Or is this a typo and it is supposed to be 0.233?

comments.issue: It is unclear why Tajima's D decreased only for generation 3.
comments.request: Explain this pattern.
comments.quote: Also Tajima’s D only decreased for generation 3

comments.issue: Fig S6 is cited for founder relatedness but does not show it; raw numbers would help.
comments.request: Correct the reference and show raw values.
comments.quote: ‘Relatedness of the original founding individuals are seen in Fig S6’ – that isn’t what that plot shows, isn’t that the heatmap in figure 1 in Box 1?

comments.issue: Heritability values are in supplemental Table 3, not 2, and bold formatting is unexplained.
comments.request: Fix the reference and explain the bolding.
comments.quote: Heritability estimates – are supplemental table 3 not 2. Why are some numbers in bold, is this for a reason?

comments.issue: BayesC and TASSEL heritability ranges differ markedly for some traits, with no explanation.
comments.request: Explain the method differences and their implications.
comments.quote: heritability estimate ranges with BayesC and TASSEL quite different in some cases (particularly growth parameter M). Is there a reason for this, or any implications of this?

comments.issue: Multiple top GWAS sites fall in the same genes; it is unclear whether one site, linkage or a haplotype matters.
comments.request: Discuss linkage and haplotype interpretation.
comments.quote: Is it likely just one site in each gene that is important and the others are significant due to linkage, or is it a haplotype that is important?

comments.issue: Surviving embryo and fertile egg traits show many intergenic sites; the link to lower heritability is unclear.
comments.request: Explain this pattern.
comments.quote: Surviving embryo and fertile egg appear to have a lot of intergenic sites when compared to the other traits? Could this have something to do with the lower heritability estimates or something else?

comments.issue: The dots in Figure 3 are not explained in the legend.
comments.request: Add them to the legend.
comments.quote: I assume the dots next to the violin plots are the raw data points? Needs adding to the legend.

comments.issue: Supplemental Figures Sa-Sb referenced in the text appear to be missing.
comments.request: Provide the missing figures.
comments.quote: Where are these supplementary figures? I think they are missing.

comments.issue: TASSEL found no aspergillosis heritability, which conflicts with GWAS-associated genes.
comments.request: Reconcile this apparent contradiction.
comments.quote: Also Tassle suggested no heritability of asperigillosis susceptibility – so is this untrue given the GWAS found genes associated with the disease susceptibility?

reviews.assessment: Milestone resource with excellent breeding-value work, but wants more interpretation of population-genetic results and an expanded genetic-load analysis.
strengths: breeding values to predict phenotype excellent

comments.issue: Why less than 2% of indels were retained after filtering is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the indel filtering.
comments.quote: You retained less than 2% of the indels after filtering. Why?

comments.issue: The positive Tajima's D (especially Stewart Island) needs an explanation in the text.
comments.request: Explain the Tajima's D pattern.
comments.quote: Tajima’s D is positive, indicating an excess in relative heterozygosity (compared to the number of segregating sites). It is especially high in Steward Island. Please give explanation in text.

comments.issue: Whether the ROH length reduction is significant, and FROH for both groups, are not reported.
comments.request: Test significance and calculate FROH.
comments.quote: Is the reduction in ROH length between founders and offspring significant? (I would think it is). If so, can you also calculate the FROH of both groups?

comments.issue: ROH and SNP/indel densities are not related to putative recombination sites.
comments.request: Regress densities against recombination sites.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to regress the ROH density (or length) against density of putative recombination sites.

comments.issue: The variant-effect census lacks comparisons of impact classes and realised load between founders and offspring.
comments.request: Expand the genetic load analysis.
comments.quote: I would like to know how many high-, medium- and low-impact variants are there detected in the founders vs offspring?

comments.issue: How heritability estimates correlate between BayesC and TASSEL is not shown.
comments.request: Compare the methods' estimates.
comments.quote: How does the heritability estimates correlate between the methods?

comments.issue: Correlations of FROH/heterozygosity and realised load with fertility and embryo survival are untested.
comments.request: Test these relationships.
comments.quote: How does FROH, heterozygosity, etc. correlate with egg fertility and embryo survival? Also, what is the realised load of these individuals (Richard Henry's descendants)?

comments.issue: Whether Richard Henry's offspring load is largely masked is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss masked versus realised load (Bertorelli et al. 2022).
comments.quote: I think it would be worth checking (or at least discussing) the likelihood that the genetic load in his offspring is largely masked.

comments.issue: Figure 1's inbreeding legend lacks F-coefficients.
comments.request: Add F-values to the legend.
comments.quote: Fig. 1. Add F-coefficients to the inbreeding legend so readers can see the F-value of the colours.

comments.issue: Figure 2's CIRCOS plot lacks a colour legend and SNP-density range.
comments.request: Add a legend and SNP-density range.
comments.quote: Fig. 2. The CIRCOS plot also needs a legend to indicate the values of the various colours. Indicate the range of SNP densities in 100kb windows.

reviews.assessment: Strongly positive; finds the small-population approaches exemplary and offers only minor suggestions on citations, terminology and clarity.
strengths: careful approaches for small population sizes
useful guide for integrating genomics into conservation

comments.issue: The Tasmanian devil program's use of genomics with pedigrees is not cited.
comments.request: Cite McLennan et al. 2018 and Wright et al. 2021.
comments.quote: One other program that has been remarkably successful in leveraging genomic data alongside pedigrees, demographic and life history data is the Tasmanian devil program

comments.issue: How GWAS data could re-prioritize urgent veterinary interventions is unclear.
comments.request: Elaborate or choose a clearer example.
comments.quote: The connection between GWAS and “urgent veterinary interventions” was not entirely clear to me (page 4).

comments.issue: 'Small sample sizes' may be intended as small population sizes (page 4).
comments.request: Use the correct term.
comments.quote: On page 4, you start the last paragraph of the Intro with “small sample sizes” (in the second sentence also). Do you mean small sample sizes or small population sizes?

comments.issue: The proportion of the extant population sampled is not reported.
comments.request: Report it in the Discussion or Methods.
comments.quote: Can you include, either in the first sentence of the Discussion and/or in the Sample Collection Methods, the proportion of the extant population that was sampled?

comments.issue: The mutational-load paragraph's 'no longer detected' phrase and its link to annotation quality are confusing.
comments.request: Explain this and its relevance to fitness.
comments.quote: the beginning of that paragraph (page 17) was a little confusing to me. Additional detail about what you mean by “no longer detected” and in what way that is related to annotation quality would be helpful

comments.issue: Figure 3's legend does not explain the dots.
comments.request: Describe the dots and their position.
comments.quote: In the legend for Figure 3, it would be helpful to include a statement indicating what the dots are (and that they are to the left of the respective violin plots).

title: Species-wide genomics of kākāpō provides tools to accelerate recovery

study.system: primate molar morphology; 480 extant and extinct species, phylogenetic comparative models

editor_summary: Editor notes the interdisciplinary paper required five reviewers and that reviewer and editorial concerns must be addressed before publication can be offered; a revision with responses is invited.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting attempt to link quantitative genetics models to macroevolution; agrees with the message but the results are too technical for a broad readership.
strengths: links quantitative genetics models with modes of phenotypic variation

comments.issue: Results and discussion are too technical and telegraphic; model-selection criteria are buried in methods and supplement.
comments.request: Make results accessible and explain the model-selection criteria.
comments.quote: most of the results and discussion are highly technical, considering a broader readership. Especially the results section is very telegraphic.

comments.issue: Traits and areas contain size while ICM variables do not, and morphospace dimensionality differs, complicating model comparisons.
comments.request: Explain how variable types and dimensionality affect the models.
comments.quote: This presumably means that the morphospaces for traits and areas contain absolute size information, which might make the required genetic models more complex than for the ICM?

comments.issue: The approach assumes a linear genotype-phenotype map while acknowledging nonlinearity, raising questions about what non-developmental models measure.
comments.request: Clarify the linearity assumption and consider non-linear GP approaches.
comments.quote: The basic logic of the approach used is based on the linear assumption of the genotype-phenotype (GP) map, while at the same time the authors seem to acknowledge that in practice these are non-linear

comments.issue: ICM variables come from the empirical morphospace rather than the strict ICM rule.
comments.request: Acknowledge this distinction explicitly.
comments.quote: It is perhaps worth pointing out that the ICM variables are based on the data plotted in the empirical morphospace and not on the strict ICM rule

comments.issue: Fig. S1 likely mislabels the ICM values as 1.3x instead of 1.1x and 1.2x.
comments.request: Correct the Fig. S1 labels.
comments.quote: A small remark about Fig. S1: The ICM part is probably meant to state 1.1x and 1.2x (not 1.3x).

reviews.assessment: Interesting, sound study with a large sample; only a few points need clarification, mainly methods details.
strengths: results are new and interpretations sound

comments.issue: The micro/macro distinction is presented as fixed rather than relative to time scale and fossil availability.
comments.request: Note that the micro/macro distinction is relative.
comments.quote: the concepts of macroevolution and microevolution are correctly described in the general sense, but it might also be useful to state that they are relative.

comments.issue: "Absent an understanding" is unclear phrasing.
comments.request: Rephrase "absent an understanding".
comments.quote: I am not sure to understand "absent an understanding". Did you mean "in absence of understanding"?

comments.issue: "Once emerged" is inaccurate since tooth crowns form long before eruption.
comments.request: Say "Once formed, each molar crown" instead.
comments.quote: Instead of "Once emerged" it would be more accurate to say "Once formed, each molar crown

comments.issue: The claim that teeth are available for all taxa is not true for several primates.
comments.request: Tone down the sentence about fossil tooth availability.
comments.quote: As far as I know, there are no fossils known (or clearly identified) for Gorilla, only three upper teeth of Middle Pleistocene Pan (and nothing earlier), and many primates do not have fossil representatives known so far.

comments.issue: Why biologically naïve morphospaces favour model complexity over landmark-based analyses needs explanation.
comments.request: Explain why naïve morphospaces favour model complexity.
comments.quote: I am curious as to why biologically naïve morphospaces favor model complexity with respect to landmark-based GM analyses?

comments.issue: The drift-versus-stabilizing-selection sentence and its link to Fig. S7 are not understandable.
comments.request: Explain this sentence and what in Fig. S7 supports it.
comments.quote: However, I do not understand the following sentence "However, drift alone would generate more variation than the total observed disparity during the period in which primates have evolved (Fig. S7)

comments.issue: Relevant studies on stabilizing selection and drift in hominins are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the Rathmann, Monson and related studies.
comments.quote: This is interesting and it was already suggested that these were the main acting factors at micro- and mesoevolutionary scales in hominids/hominins, but these studies are not mentioned and discussed.

comments.issue: How occlusal area was measured is not described in the main text.
comments.request: Describe how tooth crown area was assessed.
comments.quote: However, there is no mention of the exact way indicating how tooth crown area was assessed.

comments.issue: No test compares picture-based with caliper-based measurements; observer errors are not evaluated.
comments.request: Test agreement between the three measurement sources.
comments.quote: Considering that you have three sources of data (MD and BL diameters from the literature, measured on extant specimens and estimated based on pictures of fossil specimens), intra- and inter-observer errors should be evaluated

comments.issue: Allometry is a potential confound of tooth morphology that is not tested.
comments.request: Test the influence of allometry.
comments.quote: I would suggest to at least test the influence of allometry (that should be easy with the metric data currently available by the authors). If you can exclude the influence of allometry, then the interpretations of the results would be much stronger.

comments.issue: Lambda values are missing and the kappa selection procedure and its homoplasy implications are unclear.
comments.request: Report lambda values and clarify kappa selection.
comments.quote: The lowest kappa value is very low in Table S5, meaning that there probably is a lot of homoplasy, but it is not clear to me what is meant by lowest and highest examined.

comments.issue: The letter k denotes both trait dimensionality and Blomberg's kappa.
comments.request: Use different symbols for k and kappa.
comments.quote: In the methods, you mention k-dimensional multivariate trait and use the letter k in lower case (e.g., line 241), and in the Supplementary tables, you use the same letter to refer to Blomberg's kappa parameter.

reviews.assessment: Refreshing, well-written study, but the broad merit and operationalization beyond teeth are unclear and the discussion is lacking.
strengths: refreshing attempt to connect micro and macro evolution
well-written, carefully illustrated and logically presented

comments.issue: Unclear whether the approach applies to anything beyond the simple inhibitory cascade system.
comments.request: Discuss applicability beyond the inhibitory cascade.
comments.quote: can this be applied to anything else other than the inhibitory cascade, which is relatively simple, using numerator/denominator values of teeth?

comments.issue: Not convinced the paper offers a framework to integrate evo-devo into the Modern Synthesis or beyond teeth.
comments.request: Discuss the broader framework and its operationalization.
comments.quote: I'm not convinced this presents a framework to integrate evo-devo into the MS, nor a way that could be operationalized beyond this example of teeth.

comments.issue: The title implies the inhibitory cascade is specific to primate dentition.
comments.request: Revise the title.
comments.quote: Title, the inhibitory cascade is not just relevant to primate dentition

comments.issue: Key works by Laland, Pigliucci, Leroi and Jablonka are missing.
comments.request: Cite these works.
comments.quote: Key works by Laland, Pigliucci, Leroi, Jablonka and others are missing here and should be cited.

comments.issue: The Modern Synthesis concerns are stated too vaguely.
comments.request: Explicitly state the relevant MS concerns.
comments.quote: the main concerns with the Modern Synthesis (MS) relevant to this manuscript could be noted explicitly here rather than a quite vague statement on the complexities surrounding this topic.

comments.issue: "Specifically what parameters" on line 22 is unexplained.
comments.request: Specify the parameters meant on line 22.
comments.quote: line 22: specifically what parameters? Line 32: again, here, many pivotal references are missing.

comments.issue: Pivotal references on line 32 are missing.
comments.request: Cite Love, Waddington and Gilbert.
comments.quote: Line 32: again, here, many pivotal references are missing. For example, Love, Waddington, Gilbert

comments.issue: The implied one-to-one genotype-phenotype mapping and simple micro-macro connections are unsupported.
comments.request: Temper this claim.
comments.quote: I don't think we have any evidence that there exist simple connections between micro and macro, or the implied one-to-one mapping of genotype to phenotype

comments.issue: The form of the genotype-phenotype non-linearities is not described.
comments.request: Note examples of the form of these non-linearities.
comments.quote: perhaps it's worth to also note the form of these non-linearities, for example – most simply - we know that large genetic changes can have no appreciable impact on the phenotype

comments.issue: "Morphospaces" is used on line 36 before its definition on line 48.
comments.request: Define morphospace before first use.
comments.quote: Line 48: morphospaces is used on line 36 prior to this definition

comments.issue: "Biologically naïve" is not exemplified and the narrow definition fits poorly with comparative anatomy studies.
comments.request: Define and exemplify biologically naïve morphospaces.
comments.quote: some examples of what the authors mean by 'biologically naïve' need to be provided here. Do quantitative descriptors of biological form require a mechanistic connection to process in order for them to define an informed space?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether teeth are the only system meeting the requirements.
comments.request: Name other systems meeting the requirements.
comments.quote: is it the only study system, though? Can the authors define others meeting these requirements?

comments.issue: Calling adult morphospace "evo-devo inspired" needs rephrasing.
comments.request: Rephrase the evo-devo inspired space claim.
comments.quote: all adult data represent the terminal point of ontogeny, the emergent phenotype is one that has progressed along an ontogeny, making an adult morphospace, arguably, implicitly 'evo-devo inspired'. I think this needs to be re-phrased.

comments.issue: "This regime" and "this morphospace" on line 100 are ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify what "this" refers to.
comments.quote: please clarify what 'this regime' and 'this morphospace' refers to, what is 'this' here?

comments.issue: Relative molar length measures are constrained and share m1 as the denominator.
comments.quote: these are univariate measures of relative molar length, m3 or m2 can only be similar/larger or smaller than m1. M1 is further the denominator for both axes.

comments.issue: The "biologically-informed quantification based on evo-devo" sentence is strange.
comments.request: Rephrase this sentence.
comments.quote: I think this sentence is a bit strange, 'biologically-informed quantification based on evo-devo'

comments.issue: It is unclear how the approach translates to other systems or complex 3D data.
comments.request: Give concrete examples of translation to other systems.
comments.quote: I struggle to see how, explicitly, this can this be translated to anything else, including the myriad emergent properties that are studied through comparative anatomy.

comments.issue: The many calls for synthesis extensions are inadequately referenced.
comments.request: Reference these authors and note the marginalization of morphology.
comments.quote: yes, evolutionary synthesis extensions have been called for many times, the authors need to more adequately reference the many prominent authors who have raised these issues

comments.issue: The number of newly measured specimens is not given.
comments.request: Report the sample size of newly measured specimens.
comments.quote: provide sample size (n) for how many were newly measured.

comments.issue: Many specimens in the supplementary data have NA identifiers.
comments.request: Provide locations and identifiers for these specimens.
comments.quote: the supplementary data file contains many specimens with NA for their ID, please provide the location of these specimens and an identifier

comments.issue: The data sheet lacks a source column linking entries to studies or collections.
comments.request: Add a source column to the data sheet.
comments.quote: Please add in another column to the data sheet with 'source' – i.e., literature, which study? Or personally collected using calipers from a physical specimen or digitized from a study.

comments.issue: "Biologically informed space" and "evo-devo inspired" are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: Here the authors use 'biologically informed space' yet also in the manuscript refer to 'evo-devo inspired'.

comments.issue: Fig. S1 lacks percent variance for PC axes.
comments.request: Add % variance for PC1 and PC2.
comments.quote: Figure S1 – please provide % variance for PC1 and PC2 axes for each of these plots.

comments.issue: Differing dimensionality across morphospaces, with m1 as shared denominator for ICM, may affect model results.
comments.request: Discuss the effect of differing dimensionality on results.
comments.quote: The authors need to comment on the fact that these spaces are inherently comprised of different dimensions and how this may impact the results.

comments.issue: Disparity differences between ICM and area/distance measures in Fig. S8 are noted but not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of these disparity differences.
comments.quote: The authors have noted, but not discussed, the implications of these differences for their model.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-done study with a beautiful dataset, but dense jargon and unclear writing make it hard to follow.
strengths: beautiful dataset of molar measurements across 480 species

comments.issue: The introduction is full of vague jargon and is hard to follow for non-specialists.
comments.request: Rewrite the introduction around a specific problem and hypothesis.
comments.quote: The introduction is difficult to understand for someone who is not specifically in the field of reconciling micro- and macro- evolution.

comments.issue: The paper does not note that the general OU model has almost the same BIC as the microevolutionary OU model.
comments.request: Report the similar BIC of the general OU model.
comments.quote: the authors write that the ICM morphospaces is best modeled by an OU process that incorporates microevolutionary assumptions but fail to note that the OU model without the microevolutionary assumptions has almost the same BIC score.

comments.issue: The many moving parts could be simplified by reframing the experiment around two questions.
comments.request: Reframe the analysis around the two questions.
comments.quote: It seems this could be simplified with the following reframing of experiment:

comments.issue: Searching for the best multi-regime model is hard and its biological interpretation is difficult.
comments.request: Reconsider or justify the multi-regime model search.
comments.quote: I don't know how necessary it is to do a search for the best multi-regime model given that it is really difficult to search across all spaces of possible multi-regimes

comments.issue: The ellipses in Figure 2 are unexplained; which models A and B represent is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the Figure 2 ellipses.
comments.quote: I'm not sure exactly what the ellipses in Figure 2. Is A a pure BM model and B the OU model?

comments.issue: Why the ICM constrains ratios but not lengths or areas is not intuitive.
comments.request: Explain why ICM constrains ratios but not lengths or areas.
comments.quote: I would love a few more sentences about the ICM evodevo model and why this suggests that the ratios of the molars should be constrained but not the lengths or areas.

reviews.assessment: Valuable, convincing framework, but the methodology is inaccessible and key information is missing.
strengths: cool topic of interest to a wide audience

comments.issue: The methodology is inaccessible and key information is missing, so achievements are hard to appreciate.
comments.request: Improve the accessibility of the methods.
comments.quote: My main concern is that in its current form the methodology is pretty inaccessible. Even reading through the methods several times, I had a hard time putting things together. Some of this is because there is key information missing.

comments.issue: The dataset is not described: sources, amount of new data, final taxa count and time span are missing.
comments.request: Describe the dataset, sources, size and time span.
comments.quote: there's no description of the data. It says that new data has been added - but from where and how much? How many taxa are in the final dataset?

comments.issue: A PCA is shown in Fig. S2 but never described, and dimensionality reduction seems unnecessary for 2D ICM.
comments.request: Describe the PCA analysis or justify it.
comments.quote: PCA analyses are suggested through Fig. S2 but there's no description of such analysis. Moreover, the ICM measurement is in two dimensions only so a reduction of dimensionality should not be needed.

comments.issue: "Evo-devo" applies to two different analysis layers, which is initially confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the two evo-devo layers and add a methods overview.
comments.quote: Something initially confusing is that the "evo-devo" component applies to two different layers in the analysis

comments.issue: Fig. S2 points are colour coded with regimes from non-evo-devo models in Fig. 1, without justification.
comments.request: Justify the Fig. S2 colour coding.
comments.quote: what is the justification for the points in fig. S2 to be colour coded using the regimes identified using the mixed (i.e. non evo-devo) models in fig. 1?

comments.issue: Fig. S1 and S2 are more interesting than Fig. 3 but are relegated to the supplement.
comments.request: Move versions of Fig. S1 and S2 to the main text.
comments.quote: suggest including some version of Fig. S1 and S2 in the main text. To me, this fig seemed more interesting than fig 3.

comments.issue: The claim that the ICM space is less patchy rests on visual inspection only.
comments.request: Test the patchiness statistically.
comments.quote: you state that visual inspection suggests that the ICM space is less patchy - could this be tested statistically?

comments.issue: The modelling framework is not described at the start of the results.
comments.request: Describe the modelling framework at the start of results.
comments.quote: include a description of the modelling framework at the beginning of the results in the main text - in its current form it would be difficult for practically anyone to understand the paper without reading the supplementary material.

comments.issue: A companion paper in revision has an extremely similar title; overlap and differences are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the difference from the companion paper.
comments.quote: There's a paper cited as in review with an extremely similar title: Developmental processes mediate alignment of the micro- and macroevolution of primate molars. Evolution (In revision).

comments.issue: It is hard to imagine applying the framework again on another taxon.
comments.request: Discuss other possible examples.
comments.quote: Are there other examples of things like the ICM? I'm having trouble imagining when we could ever apply this framework again, on another taxon.

comments.issue: How to reconcile complex models for regular morphospace with simpler models for informed morphospace is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss whether the complex models remain useful.
comments.quote: How do we reconcile the complex macroevolutionary models that fit regular morphospace, with the simpler models that fit developmentally informed morphospace? Are the former still useful/meaningful?

title: Rules of teeth development align microevolution with macroevolution in extant and extinct primates

study.system: GloNAF alien plants; global naturalization and human-history data

editor_summary: Editor notes referees 1-3 are enthusiastic with mostly minor comments (referee 3 wants data limitations explicit); referee 4 wants limitations of population estimates discussed, model diagnostics and R code in the revision.

reviews.assessment: Outstanding global test of the evolutionary imbalance hypothesis; concerns are limited to clarifying the novel approaches.
strengths: outstanding contribution to understanding invasion drivers
focus on mechanisms behind biogeographic patterns
comprehensive accounting for anthropogenic and climatic confounds

comments.issue: Biogeographic syndromes are never clearly defined, especially in the main text.
comments.request: Define biogeographic syndromes clearly from the start.
comments.quote: Only after looking into Supplementary Data 3 it became clear to me that these biogeographic syndromes are basically different combinations of TDWG level 1 regions that account for the native distribution of different plant species.

comments.issue: No visual examples of biogeographic syndromes are provided.
comments.request: Include maps of a few biogeographic syndromes in the supplement.
comments.quote: I suggest including a few examples of biogeographic syndromes displayed on maps (probably included as Supplementary Material due to manuscript length restrictions).

comments.issue: How the biogeographic syndromes were constructed is not explained sufficiently.
comments.request: Describe which distribution parameters were used in the construction.
comments.quote: Second, I suggest including more information on how these biogeographic syndromes were constructed. Which species distributions parameters were considered? Only the extent of their native distribution?

comments.issue: The "observed naturalized" component of regional naturalization success is not described in a logical order.
comments.request: Describe observed naturalized after expected naturalized and clarify its meaning.
comments.quote: Third, for regional naturalization success, I suggest describing the “observed naturalized” component of the equation for Naturalization success (line 386) after describing the “expected naturalized” component (Lines 390-392).

reviews.assessment: Well-written, data-rich study that is nearly ready; native-status circularity and the rationale for expected naturalization rates need attention.
strengths: vast global data with extensive socio-economic variables
clear explanation of results and good discussion

comments.issue: Species treated as native may include archaeophytes, making the argument that wide native ranges drive success circular.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limitations of native-status assignment and the dataset.
comments.quote: However, I wonder if some of the species considered native in this analysis may actually be ancient introductions, such as archaeophytes.

comments.issue: The rationale for assuming an equal expected naturalization rate for all species in a bioregion is not explained.
comments.request: State the rationale for the equal expected naturalization rate.
comments.quote: The authors defined the expected naturalization rate as equal for all species in a bioregion. I found the rationale behind this is not well explained in the text.

comments.issue: Imbalanced alien origins could reflect the uneven global distribution of taxa, habitats or traits rather than evolutionary imbalance.
comments.request: Discuss how taxa, traits and habitat availability may shape alien origins.
comments.quote: I wonder if the imbalanced origin of alien species could be explained by the uneven global distribution of taxa, habitats, or species with certain traits.

comments.issue: The definition of expected regional naturalization success is hard to parse.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence as suggested.
comments.quote: This is a bit difficult to understand. I am wondering if “For regional naturalization success, the expected proportion was the proportion of species, that have naturalized in the region, in the global flora

reviews.assessment: Likes the rigorous global test but wants the data and inference limitations stated more clearly.
strengths: extensive database and rigorous multivariate analysis
tests the mechanisms from the 2014 EIH paper

comments.issue: Coarse within-continent aggregation limits strong inference, so global analysis is not automatically more robust than regional studies.
comments.request: Avoid implying global analyses are inherently more robust.
comments.quote: In other words, a global scale analysis is not necessarily more robust than the 'regional' studies for testing EIH, as implied here.

comments.issue: Naturalization events are not an accurate proxy for the absolute fitness differences that EIH invokes.
comments.request: Clarify what the results mean in the EIH context.
comments.quote: Naturalizations (defined as when plants 'establish populations beyond their native distributions') are readily available in global databases but not an accurate proxy of differences in absolute fitness between native and non-native species, which is what EIH invokes (line 69).

comments.issue: The analysis ignores recipient-region properties, creating a conceptual discrepancy with EIH's donor-recipient imbalance.
comments.request: Explain this discrepancy from the outset.
comments.quote: In making the present analysis 'global', the authors have chosen to ignore properties of the recipient region, or, if I'm understanding the analysis correctly, have created a global average recipient region.

comments.issue: Habitat modification, arguably the main reason human-used plants spread, is not discussed.
comments.request: Consider habitat modification as a driver of naturalization.
comments.quote: In the discussion of human impacts on naturalizations, I'm surprised that habitat modification is not considered (eg line 207).

comments.issue: The point at lines 136-140 about aggregating to biogeographic syndromes is not understood.
comments.request: Clarify why aggregation was necessary for standardizing the response.
comments.quote: 136-140 I don't understand this point. It seems the necessity of aggregating to biogeographic syndromes was necessary for standardizing the Y variable, yes?

comments.issue: The connection to Vavilov's domestication mechanisms and intraspecific diversity is not made.
comments.request: Consider making this connection.
comments.quote: 216 this gets close to mechanisms for domestication suggested by Vavilov involving intraspecific genetic diversity, may be worth making the connection (or perhaps this is done elsewhere)

comments.issue: Line-level copy edit at line 493 (complimentary for complementary).
comments.quote: 493 complimentary -> complementary

reviews.assessment: Ambitious and convincing study, but population data limits, the PCA-based analysis and absent model diagnostics need work.
strengths: ambitious and compelling evaluation of EIH
analysis mostly sound and conclusions follow from results

comments.issue: Long-term HYDE 3.2 population estimates carry admitted uncertainty and add limited interpretability.
comments.request: Emphasize the limitations of the population data.
comments.quote: I don’t think anyone working in the sciences of human history or archaeology take long-term population estimates from the HYDE 3.2 dataset seriously with any precision or accuracy

comments.issue: The chosen population periods are arbitrary and Eurocentric, occurring at different times across continents.
comments.request: Reduce the periods to two or three aligning with prehistoric and recent.
comments.quote: the authors should probably reduce these periods to two or three aligning with “prehistoric” and more recent.

comments.issue: Using PCA vectors as predictors trades away interpretability; dropping correlated variables would be preferable.
comments.request: Consider dropping or merging correlated predictors instead of using PCA vectors.
comments.quote: The authors resort to running regressions with PCA vectors as predictors given the multicollinearity in their selected explanatory variables (see Extended Data Figure 3). This is less than ideal for several reasons, the most being the loss of interpretability.

comments.issue: Strong correlation among population periods may be an artifact of HYDE hindcasting and temporal autocorrelation.
comments.request: Treat the correlation among periods as a possible artifact.
comments.quote: The strong correlation between population periods is likely due in part to how the HYDE 3.2 dataset “hindcasts” population estimates

comments.issue: Model diagnostics are insufficient: no goodness-of-fit, residual phylogenetic variation, spatial autocorrelation or overdispersion checks.
comments.request: Report these diagnostics in the supplement.
comments.quote: However, there are insufficient model diagnostics. There is no evaluation of goodness-of-fit, of residual phylogenetic variation or spatial autocorrelation, or overdispersion (for guidance, see Bolker et al. 2009; Ives and Helmus 2011).

comments.issue: The R code is not available and supplementary naming is inconsistent.
comments.request: Provide the R code and consistent supplementary naming.
comments.quote: I could not find the R code to evaluate the analytical procedures further. Naming of supplementary information does not appear consistent across documentation.

title: Evolutionary imbalance, climate and human history jointly shape the global biogeography of alien plants

study.system: woody plants; global trait, phylogeny and distribution data

editor_summary: Editor says referees 1 and 2 see potential interest, but referee 3, an expert in traits and machine learning, raises major concerns about the analysis approach that undermine the robustness of the conclusions; manuscript rejected.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and current topic; the sample size and tools are adequate and support the conclusions, but carbon metabolism and NSC should be discussed in more detail.

comments.issue: The link between carbon metabolism, NSC and survival under drought is not discussed in enough detail.
comments.request: Discuss carbon metabolism and NSC more, starting from the suggested references.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors consider this aspect in a little more detail in this text. References like these are a good start for them to introduce a topic

reviews.assessment: Well written, interesting and timely; no concerns about data, analyses or interpretation; only suggests flipping the colour scale in Figure 2a.
strengths: integrates an updated global hydraulic trait database

comments.issue: Figure 2a colour scale is not intuitive relative to Figure 2b: more negative P50 values should share the green-blue colour.
comments.request: Flip the Figure 2a scale so more negative P50 values use the same colours as larger HSMs in Figure 2b.
comments.quote: in figure 2a I suggest flipping the scale so that areas with more negative P50 values are represented in green blue to match how the color scheme has been used in Figure 2b

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic, but the conclusions are neither novel nor robust; the global upscaling and DIM analysis are questioned and the work should focus on smaller regions.

comments.issue: Upscaling to a global scale is doubted because there is no grid-scale species composition map and only some plots in boreal Asia were used.
comments.request: Justify or redo the upscaling with appropriate species composition data.
comments.quote: I doubt that because there is no species composition map on grid-scale and authors only used some plots in boreal regions of Asia

comments.issue: A spatial HSM map is provided for human-disturbed regions such as croplands and cities without sampling there.
comments.request: Explain why mapping unsampled human-disturbed regions makes sense.
comments.quote: the authors are very ambitious to provide the spatial HSM map, even for the human-disturbed regions (e.g., croplands and urban)? Why does this make sense if you do not have samplings?

comments.issue: The global HSM map largely follows climatic variables and lacks reasonable heterogeneity, with a single value for the whole Amazon.
comments.request: Show that the map is informative rather than a reflection of climate.
comments.quote: the patterns largely follow some climatic variables (for example, Fig. 2f), and the map did not show reasonable heterogeneity

comments.issue: It is unclear whether drought-induced mortality refers to grasslands, shrublands or forests, and ecosystem differences are not considered.
comments.request: Clarify which ecosystems the mortality analysis applies to and account for differences among them.
comments.quote: when the authors talk about drought-induced mortality, does that mean grassland, shrubland, or forests?

comments.issue: Drought duration and intensity both affect mortality, and severe droughts can kill even tolerant species, but this is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how drought duration and intensity affect mortality, including for tolerant species.
comments.quote: drought duration and drought intensity both affect vegetation mortality. For example, for the species with high hydraulic tolerance, server drought events are also able to kill the trees

comments.issue: The global-scale approach is premature.
comments.request: Focus first on small regions to study hydraulic risk and forest mortality.
comments.quote: Overall, the authors should deeply think about their work and focus on some small regions to study the relations between hydraulic risk and forest mortality first rather than on a global scale

title: Increased hydraulic risk in assemblages of woody plant species predicts spatial patterns of drought-induced mortality

study.system: megaherbivores and alien plants; multi-scale field data across India

editor_summary: Editor says the meta-analysis and global projections do not add sufficiently robust analysis and should be removed; reformat as a Brief Communication and improve the conceptual framework's clarity.

reviews.assessment: Important question and impressive dataset, but the megaherbivore inference is confounded, the conceptual framework too simplistic and the global projection unclear.
strengths: positive about the aims and scope

comments.issue: The correlative megaherbivore inference is confounded by unaccounted factors such as smaller herbivores.
comments.request: Address confounding by smaller herbivores.
comments.quote: the (correlative) inference about the role of megaherbivores per se is confounded by factors not accounted for

comments.issue: The global projection in Fig. 3 is unintelligible and its methods and results are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the global projection.
comments.quote: the 'global projection' in Fig. 3 is unintelligible to me, as currently presented

comments.issue: The Fig. 1 conceptual framework is too simplistic and the feedback and hysteresis arguments are not well supported.
comments.request: Refine the conceptual framework.
comments.quote: I think the schematic in Fig. 1, presented as the guiding conceptual framework for the study, is too simplistic, and in general that the arguments about feedbacks and hysteresis are not particularly well supported by the data.

comments.issue: Writing is unclear, word choice implies unwarranted certainty, and procedures are not fully described.
comments.request: Increase clarity and modulate the tone.
comments.quote: The manuscript is not very well written, and this stems from both inopportune word choice (often implying more certainty than is warranted given the more speculative nature of the interpretation) and inadequate clarity/fullness of the description of procedures.

comments.issue: "Exponential" is used loosely without a citation.
comments.request: Define or cite the exponential claim.
comments.quote: Are you using the word 'exponential' precisely or loosely here? Citation?

comments.issue: The claim that large-bodied herbivores have broader diets is not supported by recent evidence.
comments.request: Revise the diet breadth-body size claim.
comments.quote: Although it is indeed commonly assumed that large-bodied species have "broader more generalist diets," there is actually no strong evidence for this in terrestrial vertebrate herbivores.

comments.issue: "Will" on L62 implies more certainty than warranted.
comments.request: Change "will" to "could" or "might".
comments.quote: Change "will" to "could" or "might"

comments.issue: The hypothesized feedback loop may not be general and needs alternative scenarios and nuance.
comments.request: Present 3-4 alternative feedback scenarios.
comments.quote: I'm not entirely convinced that the hypothesized feedback loop in Fig. 1 is likely to be general. If megaherbivores are capable of suppressing invasive plants, then it is not clear that invasive plants will necessarily make the habitat less hospitable.

comments.issue: Reference 16 does not pertain to megaherbivores specifically.
comments.request: Check or replace reference 16.
comments.quote: I don't think reference 16 pertains to megaherbivores per se (as opposed to herbivores in general)?

comments.issue: "Which theory" on L75 is not identified.
comments.request: Specify which theory is meant.
comments.quote: L75. Which theory? L91-92. Give body size ranges or maximum/median/mean body size for each of these species.

comments.issue: Body size ranges for the study species are not reported.
comments.request: Report body size ranges for each species.
comments.quote: Give body size ranges or maximum/median/mean body size for each of these species.

comments.issue: The Guinness record claim lacks a citation.
comments.request: Cite the Guinness world record.
comments.quote: Cite Guinness world record book with the pertinent record. Also, "this big data set".

comments.issue: Fig 2 is overly complicated with an unclear caption and unexplained elements.
comments.request: Improve Fig 2 and its caption.
comments.quote: this figure is so complicated that it is very difficult to follow, especially without a more clearly written caption.

comments.issue: The modeling approach (number of models, contents, evaluation) is not described in the main text.
comments.request: Describe the modeling approach in the main text.
comments.quote: I would like to see just a bit more description of your modeling approach here in the main text (how many models were built, what did they include, how did you evaluate relative performance).

comments.issue: Megaherbivore occurrence is confounded with other variables, especially small and medium herbivore densities.
comments.request: Address confounding at this analysis.
comments.quote: A critical question that I think you must address is the extent to which megaherbivore occurrence is correlated (confounded) with other variables that could be generating the observed associations

comments.issue: Percentage values for areas without megaherbivores are missing.
comments.request: Give the comparison percentages.
comments.quote: Give the percentage values for areas without them, for comparison.

comments.issue: The "threefold" result lacks visible evidence and magnitude information.
comments.request: Show the evidence and magnitude for this result.
comments.quote: Where do we find evidence for this important result? It's hard to make sense of "threefold" given the lack of information about the magnitude of the difference in the previous sentence.

comments.issue: The quadratic relationship was not anticipated in the conceptual framework.
comments.request: Provide conceptual context for the nonlinearity.
comments.quote: The quadratic form of the relationships in Fig. 2D-F is empirically convincing; was this anticipated, and on what grounds?

comments.issue: P = 0.026 is weak support for calling the relationship positive.
comments.request: Soften or qualify the relationship claim.
comments.quote: with P = 0.026, it's a stretch to call this "a positive relationship", because the statistical support for the existence of any relationship at all is very weak.

comments.issue: The pattern could be an artifact of megaherbivore scarcity at productivity extremes.
comments.request: Discuss this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Is this simply an artifact of the fact that megaherbivores are scarce in extremely low and extremely high productivity ecosystems?

comments.issue: The method outline is missing from the main text.
comments.request: Add a method outline to the main text.
comments.quote: At least the outlines of the method used here is needed in the main text for it to be comprehensible.

comments.issue: Not all species included reach the stated 1000 kg megaherbivore criterion.
comments.request: Reconcile the definition with the species included.
comments.quote: I think that all of these species can fairly be labeled megaherbivores, but not all of them reach 1000 kg body mass, which is the criterion you state in your introduction.

comments.issue: The L220 language implies certainty for a speculative interpretation.
comments.request: Use hedging language.
comments.quote: As this interpretation is plausible but nonetheless speculative, you choose words accordingly.

comments.issue: Additional empirical nuance from Koerner et al. and Ratajczak et al. is missing.
comments.request: Cite these studies.
comments.quote: See e.g. the study by Koerner et al. 2018 NEE (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41559-018-0696-y) and Ratajczak et al. 2022 PNAS

comments.issue: Fig. 3 mixes areas with and without megaherbivores, making it hard to interpret.
comments.request: Clarify the figure or the modeling overview.
comments.quote: I have a hard time interpreting this figure because of the way it mixes together areas where megaherbivores are extant and areas where they are not.

comments.issue: It is unclear where the 68-77% result is shown and what the metric means.
comments.request: Explain the invasion proportion values.
comments.quote: Where can we see this result? I'm confused in part because the "Invasion proportion" scale in Fig. 2E, G only goes up to 50

comments.issue: The L257-258 language implies too much certainty.
comments.request: Temper the language.
comments.quote: Again here, I think the language throughout this paragraph implies more certainty than is appropriate for this plausible but speculative interpretation.

comments.issue: Model selection rationale and a comparison table with AIC and R2 values are missing.
comments.request: Provide model details and a comparison table.
comments.quote: How many different competing models, what was the rationale for choosing predictors, determining fixed vs. random effects, and where is the supplementary table showing all of the models, their AIC, and their conditional/marginal R2 values?

comments.issue: The projection analysis objective, procedure and interpretation are insufficiently described.
comments.request: Describe the projection analysis fully.
comments.quote: The description of this "projection" is insufficiently detailed. Just as I was confused by by Fig. 3, I still don't understand the objective, modeling procedure, or interpretation of this analysis.

comments.issue: Publication bias may skew a meta-analysis of only 13 studies.
comments.request: Comment on publication bias.
comments.quote: Perhaps comment somewhere on the possibility that publication bias has skewed a meta-analysis with only 13 studies?

comments.issue: Table S4 contains typos in species names.
comments.request: Correct the species names.
comments.quote: There are at least 2 typos in the species names in this table.

reviews.assessment: Impressive data strongly support megaherbivore effects, but the meta-analysis, global extrapolation and conceptual framework need rework.
strengths: impressive data-sets with a broad geographic footprint
results strongly suggest a positive megaherbivore impact

comments.issue: The meta-analysis and global extrapolation rest on many assumptions and are not statistically robust.
comments.request: Consider removing the meta-analysis and global extrapolation.
comments.quote: these two facets make many assumptions and are much less statistically robust

comments.issue: Statistical relationships from India are extrapolated to the entire globe despite regional megafauna divergence.
comments.request: Restrict or justify the global extrapolation.
comments.quote: I think it's fairly inappropriate to take statistical relationships from a single region and apply it to the entire globe.

comments.issue: The meta-analysis correlation depends entirely on two data points.
comments.request: Remove or strengthen the meta-analysis.
comments.quote: The statistical significance of that relationship (Figure 3G) rests entirely on two data-points (with high predicted effects).

comments.issue: The framework contradicts itself: invaders as forage for control versus invaders harming megaherbivores.
comments.request: Resolve the contradiction in the framework.
comments.quote: These two ideas are in direct contradiction. For megaherbivores to provide biotic control, the invasive species much be a viable source of forage, and if so, then they would not negatively affect megaherbivore growth.

comments.issue: Negative and positive feedback are used incorrectly; the sign depends on the starting state.
comments.request: Use feedback terminology correctly.
comments.quote: I think the authors are probably misusing the terms negative and positive feedback. Whether a feedback is positive or negative depends on the starting state of the system.

comments.issue: Non-native species are assumed to all be invasive.
comments.request: Use "non-native" instead of invasive.
comments.quote: it's a bait and switch to measure non-native species and then assume they are all invasive.

comments.issue: Percentages for native and invasive richness are not reported like the cover percentages.
comments.request: Report percentages for richness too.
comments.quote: it could be especially important to report these same percentages for native and invasive species richness, which currently is not done in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Some Fig 2 arrows lack effect sizes, e.g. herbivores to NC.
comments.request: Add the missing effect sizes.
comments.quote: It appears that effect sizes may be missing from some arrows, for instance, from herbivores to NC. It would be helpful to know these.

comments.issue: The manuscript uses too many acronyms.
comments.request: Reduce the number of acronyms.
comments.quote: The manuscript has a large number of acronyms, which I found hard to keep track of. Are all these acronyms really needed?

comments.issue: The reported megaherbivore effects on cover are very small in magnitude.
comments.request: Acknowledge the small effect magnitudes.
comments.quote: To be fair, this is a very small impact, magnitude-wise.

title: Megaherbivores provide biotic resistance against alien plant dominance

study.system: primate brains; single-cell transcriptomes and co-expression networks

editor_summary: Three reviewers raise concerns needing revision; editor asks for responses to criticisms and editorial concerns and for all changes to be highlighted in Word.

reviews.assessment: Great, substantial body of work, but the text lacks cohesion and many analysis details and figure captions need clarification.
strengths: great and substantial body of work
authors experienced with the data and analyses

comments.issue: The text lacks cohesion, details are missing and figure captions are minimal, making analyses and outcomes hard to follow.
comments.request: Improve cohesion and add details and explanations throughout.
comments.quote: the text lacks cohesion and details are lacking in some parts, clarification is required in some parts of results and methods sections

comments.issue: Methods are not referenced for measurements and analyses.
comments.request: Refer to the relevant method sections and describe all analyses clearly.
comments.quote: please try to refer to the relevant method section for various measurements and analyses

comments.issue: Figure 1A elements such as the colour bars are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the elements in Figure 1A.
comments.quote: Figure 1A: Please consider explaining the elements in the figure. For example, what do the colour bars refer to?

comments.issue: Figure 1B elements such as the lines are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the elements in Figure 1B.
comments.quote: Figure 1B: Please consider explaining what different elements in the figure represent. For example, what are the lines in the left figure?

comments.issue: Figure 2C plot dimensions are not stated.
comments.request: Mention the dimensions of each plot.
comments.quote: Figure 2C: Please mention what are the dimensions in each of the plots.

comments.issue: Figure 2E and 2B references do not point to the methods or citation for reproducibility.
comments.request: Refer to the methods section or citation used for measuring reproducibility.
comments.quote: when referring to these Figures, please refer to the methods section or citation used for measuring the reproducibility

comments.issue: Figure 5A gene counts disagree with the methods section on calculating the expressolog score.
comments.request: Reconcile the gene counts between the figure and methods.
comments.quote: Figure 5A: inconsistency for count of genes for pseudo-bulk expression in the diagram and the methods section

comments.issue: The process of building aggregate coexpression networks is unclear, including pseudocell definitions and how cell splits were aggregated.
comments.request: Clarify how the aggregate coexpression networks were built.
comments.quote: the exact process of building these networks is unclear to me

comments.issue: Paragraphs 3 and 4 of the conservation section are disconnected or abrupt.
comments.request: Link these paragraphs to the section and title.
comments.quote: relates to other parts of this section or to what the title implies

comments.issue: The interpretation of coexpression conservation between networks (Figure 4C) is not elaborated.
comments.request: Elaborate on how these measurements can be interpreted.
comments.quote: please elaborate on how these measurements can be interpreted

comments.issue: The choice of 4500 genes for coexpression analysis and 3000 for subclass label transfer is not justified.
comments.request: Explain how these gene counts were selected.
comments.quote: how was the count 4500 selected for the coexpression analysis, and why is the count 3000 selected for the subclass label transfer?

comments.issue: Compound words are inconsistent: 'pseudobulk'/'pseudocell' versus 'pseudo-bulk'.
comments.request: Use consistent compound wording.
comments.quote: Inconsistency in compound words - Figure 4A, 5A, “pseudobulk” and “pseudocell” vs. “pseudo-bulk” in the text.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic and impressive team, but analytical threads are hard to follow and methods lack reproducibility details.
strengths: interesting topic using new data modalities

comments.issue: Many analysis steps from raw data to the 57 homologous cell types lack the detail needed for clarity and reproducibility, including prior-knowledge neighbourhoods, label transfer, QC and normalisation.
comments.request: Provide the missing methodological details throughout.
comments.quote: The authors need to provide more details in the methods and / or elsewhere to ensure that these analyses are clear and reproducible.

comments.issue: Using cell subclass labels from the motor cortex (M1) to annotate MTG is not justified and not mentioned in the Results.
comments.request: Justify the M1 label transfer and mention it in the Results.
comments.quote: What is the justification for using cell subclass labels from an entirely different brain region (M1) to annotate MTG and why is this not mentioned in the Results?

comments.issue: How the 3000 highly variable genes were defined is unclear and they are not listed.
comments.request: Define and list the highly variable genes used.
comments.quote: How exactly were these 3000 highly variable genes defined? Are they listed anywhere?

comments.issue: The QC and normalisation procedures and parameters are not described.
comments.request: Describe the QC steps and normalisation parameters.
comments.quote: What kind of QC and how was this done? Any normalization parameters?

comments.issue: CCA, clustering, cluster QC and merging criteria are not described, and referring to a dense preprint is unhelpful.
comments.request: Describe these steps in detail instead of referring to a preprint.
comments.quote: How was CCA performed? How was clustering performed? What type of cluster QC was performed? What were the merging criteria?

comments.issue: The code underlying these steps does not appear to be available in the GitHub repo.
comments.request: Make the analysis code available.
comments.quote: It does not seem that the code underlying the steps described above has been made available in the GitHub repo or elsewhere

comments.issue: The relationship between AUROC thresholds, significance and multiple testing is unaddressed.
comments.request: Establish significance of AUROC thresholds via empirical null distributions and address multiple testing.
comments.quote: can one establish the ‘significance’ of arbitrary AUROC thresholds (e.g., 0.6 used for cross-species clustering) based on empirical null distributions of AUROC using permuted data, or otherwise?

comments.issue: Cell type replicability underpins all conclusions and needs stronger validation.
comments.request: Validate cell types in independent datasets or with histology.
comments.quote: showing the existence of cell type replicability is paramount

comments.issue: The most obvious evolutionary evidence may lie in non-homologous cell types that are hard to compare, which the study does not examine.
comments.request: Discuss what could be learned from non-homologous cell types.
comments.quote: Is there anything to be learned by studying the transcriptional phenotypes of non-homologous cell types?

reviews.assessment: Well-written and sound analysis, but the coexpression network results may overestimate conservation due to marker selection and tissue heterogeneity.

comments.issue: Figure 4D conservation may be overestimated because marker gene selection could favour pan-neuronal coexpression sets.
comments.request: Test sensitivity to marker gene selection and characterise the marker set.
comments.quote: I wonder whether the extent of conservation is overestimated because of the way the analysis is set up

comments.issue: Coexpression networks built from many tissues, not just brain, may depress conservation scores for neuronal genes.
comments.request: Repeat the analysis using networks built from bulk brain data only.
comments.quote: A critical issue may lie in the fact that the coexpression networks are built from bulk RNAseq data from a variety of tissues, not just brain.

comments.issue: The analysis is human-centric; it is unknown whether other species-centric analyses would yield similar divergence.
comments.request: Assess whether gorilla- or marmoset-centric analyses show similar numbers of diverging genes.
comments.quote: What would we see with, say, a gorilla-centric, or a marmoset-centric analysis?

title: Comparative single-cell transcriptomic analysis of primate brains highlights human-specific regulatory evolution

study.system: Arabidopsis thaliana accessions; competition experiment and genome-wide association

editor_summary: Particularly concerned about statistical support for indirect genetic effects as discussed by reviewers; all issues related to that must be fully addressed.

reviews.assessment: Innovative study with minor concerns; asks to clarify intraspecific interactions and the competition-versus-altruism framing.
strengths: exciting topic rarely studied in plants

comments.issue: Inter- and intraspecific interactions are confused throughout the manuscript and results are interpreted in the wrong context.
comments.request: Clarify the interaction type throughout and revise the interpretations.
comments.quote: The first aspect is the potential confusion between inter vs intraspecific interaction in the manuscript.

comments.issue: The term plant-plant competition is used for patterns ranging from competition to altruism.
comments.request: Differentiate competition from altruism in the text and interpretations.
comments.quote: My gut feeling is that your results show different patterns from competition (negative IGE, positive DGE) to altruism (positive IGE, negative DGE).
