comments.issue: The importance of understanding IGEs in intraspecific interaction is not explained at L47-51.
comments.request: Explain why intraspecific IGEs matter.
comments.quote: I missed the explanation of the importance of understanding IGE involved in intraspecific interaction.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'the size variation' at L82 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify this phrase.
comments.quote: The meaning of “the size variation” is unclear here.

comments.issue: Reference mismatch at L255: Baron et al. 2015 mentioned but Libourel et al. 2021 cited.
comments.request: Fix the reference.
comments.quote: There is a problem with the reference. You mentioned Baron et al. 2015 (IGE in intra & interspecific context), but cited Libourel et al. 2021 in the reference section

comments.issue: The nature of the accessions used could be an alternative explanation for the L257-260 pattern.
comments.request: Consider accession provenance as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Is the nature of accession used could be an another potential explanation?

comments.issue: What 'monoculture' means in the methods is unclear.
comments.request: Define the monoculture treatment.
comments.quote: What do you call monoculture in the method section? Is it the presence of 2 individuals from the same accession (two individuals per pot), or the absence of competition (single individual per pot)?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the GWA package controls for population structure (L368).
comments.request: State how population structure was controlled.
comments.quote: Is the package used for performing GWA controlled for the structure of population?

comments.issue: The choice of A. lyrata in the introgression model at L405 is unexplained.
comments.request: Justify using A. lyrata.
comments.quote: Why did you use A. lyrata in the model testing for introgression from relicts?

comments.issue: The size window at L420 is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the choice of size window.
comments.quote: Why did you choose this size window?

comments.issue: LD was not calculated from the study's own 83 accessions (L431).
comments.request: Explain why LD was not calculated from this dataset.
comments.quote: Why you didn’t calculate the LD based on your dataset of 83 accessions?

reviews.assessment: Interesting but flawed in places: model comparisons favour direct effects, multiple testing is unclear, and kin selection literature is ignored.

comments.issue: The claim that IGEs were mostly applied to animal breeding is historically incorrect; plant breeding came first.
comments.request: Correct this history and cite Bijma 2014 and Kawano & Thung 1982.
comments.quote: Historically, the IGE framework has been mostly applied to animal breeding

comments.issue: Missing word at line 35.
comments.quote: Line 35: insert ‘with’ to read ‘with DGEs’

comments.issue: A. thaliana's strong selfing syndrome makes IGE responses resemble DGEs, questioning the system's suitability.
comments.request: Discuss the consequences of selfing for IGE inference.
comments.quote: A. thaliana is not an ideal species for this study despite it being a model plant system.

comments.issue: Regions containing IGEs are not discussed alongside other genes found in the same regions by prior GWAS.
comments.request: Discuss overlap with other GWAS findings in these regions.
comments.quote: some discussion of the regions identified here as containing IGEs with other genes found in those same or in adjacent regions ought to be a part of this study

comments.issue: Including direct effects in every model biases detection toward direct effects and makes IGEs ancillary.
comments.request: Test a model with indirect effects only.
comments.quote: Including direct effects in every model biases the detection of effects toward direct and away from indirect effect.

comments.issue: Whether a Bonferroni correction was used for the SNP associations is unclear; linkage among loci also complicates inference.
comments.request: Clarify multiple-testing correction and compare DGE/IGE GWAS.
comments.quote: It was not clear from my reading whether a Bonferroni correction was used regarding multiple comparisons.

comments.issue: Bonferroni correction for nearly 1,000 climate comparisons and LD among the five loci are not addressed.
comments.request: Report multiple-testing correction and account for LD.
comments.quote: It is not clear from my reading whether a Bonferroni correction was used in assessing the significance of these nearly 1,000 comparisions nor how the association between the five putative loci (LD) was taken into account.

comments.issue: Studies of kin selection and cooperation in plants are not cited.
comments.request: Cite Dudley 2015 and Murphy et al. 2017.
comments.quote: The authors have ignored reference to a number of studies of 'kin selection' in plants that ought to be cited in the Introduction and Discussion.

comments.issue: Environmental divergence cannot be distinguished from isolation by distance when climate covaries with geography.
comments.request: Address this confounding.
comments.quote: it becomes difficult to distinguish divergence owing to environmental factors from isolation by distance, especially when environmental variables covary with geographic distance

reviews.assessment: Excellent design and questions, but not confident the GWAS conclusions, especially the 61.1% variance claim, are supported.
strengths: present study novel and of high added-value

comments.issue: The data come from an already published experiment, but this is not stated at L72.
comments.request: State the data source and cite the reference.
comments.quote: The data are from an experiment that was already published [ref 39]. It would be appropriate to say so L72 and provide the reference there.

comments.issue: Ref 39 mapped a nearby major locus with the same data; the discrepancy is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss why the same major-effect loci were not recovered.
comments.quote: I would have expected the same major-effect loci to be identified (on chr 3 and on other chromosomes too)

comments.issue: Using indirect breeding values instead of the available phenotype is surprising and can bias results with unequal accuracies.
comments.request: Justify or replace the breeding-value approach.
comments.quote: This approach is very surprising given that the phenotype is available, and likely suboptimal.

comments.issue: DGE and IGE are correlated, so DGE should be fitted in the null model of the igeGWAS.
comments.request: Fit DGE in the null model.
comments.quote: Hence I believe DGE need to be accounted for in the igeGWAS by fitting DGE in the null model.

comments.issue: The 61.1% variance claim is a count of positive loci, ignoring effect sizes, and conflicts with the Manhattan plot.
comments.request: Recalculate the variance explained using effect sizes.
comments.quote: it does not take into account the effect size of each locus. It is merely a count of the number of positive [significant] IGE loci per accession.

comments.issue: LD between the IGE locus and the GEA locus is not reported.
comments.request: Report LD, ideally in the RegMap panel.
comments.quote: it would be good to know the linkage disequilibrium (in the RegMap panel ideally) and very close markers can have low LD

comments.issue: The L169-170 climate conclusion rests on only five significant loci.
comments.request: Consider aggregate genetic effects and genetic correlations with climate.
comments.quote: this conclusion is supported by five significant loci only. It would be best to consider aggregate genetic effects and genetic correlations with climatic factors

comments.issue: Light response gene analyses lack statistical inference (P values, enrichment).
comments.request: Provide statistical inference for these analyses.
comments.quote: Analysis of light response genes is missing statistical inference (no P value or enrichment provided).

comments.issue: Light-related genes at IGE loci may deal with daylight exposure rather than neighbours.
comments.request: Consider the daylight-exposure alternative explanation.
comments.quote: the most likely explanation, to me, seems to be that these genes are involved in dealing with different daylight exposures, rather than neighbours

comments.issue: The positive IGE allele on Chr3:16035170 may have arisen independently in relicts and non-relicts.
comments.request: Consider independent origin of this allele.
comments.quote: Is it possible that the positive IGE allele on Chr3:16035170 arose independently in Relicts and non-relicts to reach intermediate/high frequencies (Fig 3e)?

study.system: reverse TCA cycle metabolites in aqueous microdroplets; origin-of-life chemistry

reviews.assessment: Intriguing microdroplet chemistry, but two major issues, possible electrochemistry during nebulization and unquantified, unconfirmed products, must be resolved.
strengths: highly interesting idea of primitive anabolism in microdroplets
spectacular results such as reductive carboxylation of succinate
impressive hydration/dehydration reactions at room temperature

comments.issue: Reactions may be driven by the high nebulization voltage rather than by droplet confinement, implying reductive electrochemistry.
comments.request: Experimentally rule out electrochemistry during nebulization as the source of reactivity.
comments.quote: what evidence is there that the reactions are being induced by the confinement of the microdroplet and not by the extremely high voltage applied during nebulization

comments.issue: Products are only detected by MS and never quantified, unlike previous reverse-Krebs studies.
comments.request: Quantify the products, for example using calibration curves.
comments.quote: In general, the products are only detected by MS, and they are not quantified.

comments.issue: The identity of the reductive carboxylation products of alpha-ketoglutarate is uncertain; an isomeric compound could give similar MS/MS spectra.
comments.request: Use LC-MS or GC-MS to confirm retention time and product identity.
comments.quote: I am not convinced that the identity of the products derived from the apparent reductive carboxylation reaction of alpha-ketoglutarate have been correctly identified.

comments.issue: The NMR check for ketoglutarate in the succinate sample is less sensitive than MS and misses the same control by MS.
comments.request: Search for ketoglutarate in the succinate starting material by MS.
comments.quote: why not search for ketoglutarate in the succinate sample using the same technique used to search for it in the reaction?

comments.issue: An alternative mechanism via succinic anhydride followed by reductive carboxylation is not considered.
comments.request: Consider and test the succinic anhydride mechanism.
comments.quote: I wonder if the mechanism might involve an initial dehydration of succinate to succinic anhydride

comments.issue: The Fig. 3 'conversion ratio' is not a true conversion ratio because compound-specific response factors were not calibrated.
comments.request: Quantify with calibration curves and rename the measure accordingly.
comments.quote: the value obtained cannot be described as a conversion ratio. It is simply a qualitative measure of conversion.

comments.issue: Dissolved CO2 lowers pH, so acidity rather than CO2 presence could explain the observed difference.
comments.request: Control for the pH change caused by dissolved CO2.
comments.quote: how can one rule out the difference is just due to the droplet being more acidic, rather than solely to the presence of CO2?

comments.issue: The glyoxylate-plus-pyruvate to malate result was already reported in reference 17 and is not cross-referenced.
comments.request: Cross-reference and mention the earlier report.
comments.quote: This was already reported in ref. 17, so the authors should cross-reference it here and mention it.

comments.issue: Aldol reactions with activated substrates occur in water without droplets, so droplet-specific controls are needed.
comments.request: Run control experiments with and without droplets to show the outcome differs.
comments.quote: the authors need to be careful to do the necessary control experiments showing that the outcome is notably different with and without droplets

comments.issue: Table 1 yields are unreliable because response factors per compound were not accounted for, making the data misleading.
comments.request: Determine yields using calibrated response factors.
comments.quote: I don’t know how yields can be determined in the table if the response factors for each compound were not taken into account.

comments.issue: Impurities in the starting material were checked by NMR rather than the more sensitive MS.
comments.request: Use MS analysis of the starting material to rule out impurities.
comments.quote: MS analysis of the starting material, rather than NMR, should be used to rule out impurities in the starting material.

comments.issue: Figure captions ambiguously suggest products were characterized by NMR when only pure starting material was measured.
comments.request: Clarify explicitly in the figure captions that NMR shows only starting material.
comments.quote: the reader might get the impression that the products were characterized by NMR, which is not the case

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-designed study with the important controls, but the electron source, replication and CO2-free controls need clarification.
strengths: premise and conduct thought out well

comments.issue: The electron source for the reductive carboxylation reactions is not identified or discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the source of electrons, such as water splitting.
comments.quote: what is the considered electron source in these reductive carboxylation reactions?

comments.issue: The number of repetitions per experiment is not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of repetitions for each experiment.
comments.quote: The number of repetitions per experiment is not clear.

comments.issue: It is not clear that CO2-free control experiments were performed, and this crucial control should be more prominent.
comments.request: Clarify the CO2-free controls, ideally for every reaction, and present them prominently.
comments.quote: I would clarify that these controls took place, ideally for every single reaction performed

comments.issue: Supp. Fig. 3 suggests the product peak is smaller without voltage, raising possible voltage artefacts.
comments.request: Perform experiments without high voltage to exclude artefacts.
comments.quote: Why couldn’t all experiment be performed without high voltage to exclude artefacts there if the setup can be used without high voltage?

comments.issue: Isotope-labelled CO2 experiments that would verify the mechanism have not been done.
comments.request: Perform 13CO2 or 14CO2 tracing experiments.
comments.quote: There might be critics asking for 13CO2 or 14CO2 experiments to ensure the mechanistic integrity of the observed reactions.

comments.issue: A catalytic role of trace metal ions in the microdroplets cannot be excluded.
comments.request: Test water purity, e.g. by ion chromatography, to exclude metal catalysis.
comments.quote: the claim that this works without metals is a very strong one so it should be thoroughly excluded

comments.issue: The rationale for using NMR rather than the more sensitive MS to check contamination is unclear.
comments.request: Explain that NMR checks are an additional precaution on top of MS controls.
comments.quote: I don’t necessarily understand why NMR is used to look for contamination – isn’t the detection limit of MS quite a bit lower than NMR?

comments.issue: Overall language editing is needed; several sentences are hard to understand (also 'superiority' on line 84 and 'Bulking blocks' on line 79).
comments.request: Edit the manuscript for language throughout.
comments.quote: I would just really recommend an overall editing for language

comments.issue: The line 45 sentence is unclear and the Evans citation may not support the statement about electron sources.

comments.issue: Lines 101-105 do not explain where CO2 enters the setup, hindering understanding.

reviews.assessment: Topically important, but the claims lack originality and empirical support, and the manuscript is poorly written with citation problems.
strengths: important topic in prebiotic origin of metabolism
CO2 incorporation into the reverse Krebs cycle is novel

comments.issue: Originality is limited because microdroplet reverse-Krebs reactions were partly reported before, and major claims lack empirical support.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution relative to Lee et al. (2019).
comments.quote: this manuscript lacks enough orginality and dose not provide enough empirical evidences to support their major claims

comments.issue: The manuscript is written very poorly and needs extensive language improvement.
comments.request: Vastly improve the writing.
comments.quote: the manuscript is written very poorly and needs vast improvement

comments.issue: Citations and credit to previous research are inadequate and rely too much on self-citation.
comments.request: Improve citations and reduce self-citation.
comments.quote: The citations and credits to the previous researches need to be improved with less self-citation.

comments.issue: No molecular-level evidence shows that exogenous CO2 is incorporated into succinate or alpha-ketoglutarate.
comments.request: Provide molecular-level evidence of exogenous CO2 incorporation.
comments.quote: this manuscript fails to provide molecular-level evidences that exogenously introduced atmospheric or dissolved CO2 is incorporated into the substrate of the interest, succinate, and alpha-ketoglutarate

comments.issue: Control experiments with single reactants are missing.
comments.request: Include control experiments with single reactants.
comments.quote: The reactions must include the control experiments with single reactants.

comments.issue: Mass spectra only span the desired products; full spectra, including unexpected products, are needed.
comments.request: Provide and explain the whole spectra, especially for CO2-bound products.
comments.quote: Authors need to provide the whole spectra of the acquired product, especially for CO2-bound products and needs to explain the spectra.

comments.issue: CO2-incorporated compounds could arise from hydrolysis and condensation of species rather than from reaction with exogenous CO2.
comments.request: Provide a molecular signature such as isotope-labelled tracing.
comments.quote: It cannot be ruled out that the observed CO2-incorporated compounds can originate from those reactions, not formed by the reaction of succinate and alpha-ketoglutarate with exogenous CO2.

comments.issue: No rationale is given for the choice of succinate and alpha-ketoglutarate as substrates.
comments.request: Provide a rationale for the substrate choice.
comments.quote: Authors need to provide a rationale for the substrate of their choice.

comments.issue: Other rTCA-cycle compounds and the cellular substrate succinyl-CoA were not tested with CO2.
comments.request: Examine and compare reactivity of other rTCA compounds and succinyl-CoA.
comments.quote: It is aso recommended that the authors need to compare the reactivity of the compounds with the cellular substrate such as succinyl-CoA

comments.issue: Tandem MS fragments showing only H2O and CO2 loss cannot confirm product identity.
comments.request: Provide additional evidence confirming product identity.
comments.quote: These types of fragments do not provide any structural information about the products and do not confirm the molecular identity of the products.

comments.issue: The droplet size range of 1-100 μm is asserted without supporting data.
comments.request: Provide data supporting the droplet size claim.
comments.quote: The authors needs to provide the data on their argument “ Typically, the size of droplets ranged from 1 to 100 μm

comments.issue: 'Triphosadenine (ATP)' is incorrect terminology.

comments.quote: “triphosadenine (ATP)” need to be changed to adenosine triphosphate.

comments.issue: The sentence about five-carbon to six-carbon conversion in microdroplets lacks references.
comments.request: Provide references for this sentence.
comments.quote: In aqueous microdroplet-MS, there has been observed that five-carbon 9 could be converted to six-carbon intermediates without the need of enzymes.

comments.issue: Conversion efficiency for the Figure 2 reactions is not described.
comments.request: Describe the conversion efficiency in Figure 2.
comments.quote: Describe the conversion efficiency in the reactions in Figure 2.

comments.request: Provide or discuss this mechanism.
comments.quote: Provide or discuss the mechanism for the diameter-dependence of the conversion ratio in Figure 3b.

comments.issue: The claim that CO2 molecules were loaded at or near the air-water interface has no solid basis.
comments.request: Support or remove this claim.

reviews.assessment: Important evaluation of preprocessing and resilience indicators; the simulation set-up needs clarification and several settings should be explored.
strengths: validates resilience indicators where in-situ validation is challenging

comments.issue: The simulation set-up is unclear and its realism for global satellite time series is not demonstrated.
comments.request: Clarify how the simulations represent real satellite series and test sensitivity to seasonal patterns.
comments.quote: My main concern is the set-up of the simulations, which is not entirely clear to me (line 282 – 290). How do you ensure that the simulated time series realistically represent satellite time series?

comments.issue: Trend agreement does not prove trends are correct, and anthropogenic effects cannot be fully excluded.
comments.request: Discuss this limitation of trend agreement.
comments.quote: Although a mismatch between the lag-one autocorrelation and variance is an indication of unreliable estimates, the agreement of trends is not necessary a proof that the trends are correct.

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks variability around the average AC1.
comments.request: Add variability around the average AC1 to Figure 1.

comments.issue: The time series length and number of observations used in the gap analyses are not stated.

comments.quote: It could perhaps be interesting to add a plot to S11 and S12 with the number of VI’s that agree on the trend direction.

reviews.assessment: Well-done analysis with solid recommendations, but it needs more theory, caveats on critical slowing down, and comparison with previous estimates.
strengths: supports the overall objectives and main messages
important steps advancing spatial resilience metrics

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a theoretical discussion of critical slowing down, autocorrelation, variance and the restoring versus recovery rate.
comments.request: Add a conceptual paragraph and figure on these concepts.
comments.quote: There should be more of a theoretical discussion in the introduction about critical slowing down, autocorrelation, variance, and the recovery rate

comments.issue: The criteria of rising variance and autocorrelation could reflect other system dynamics that are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Highlight that the criteria are only one potential interpretation of the dynamics.
comments.quote: I think the paper needs to highlight that the criteria they set based on rising variance and increased autocorrelation could indeed reflect critical slowdown, but there are other potential system dynamics that are equally important to acknowledge

comments.issue: Whether the systems identified as reliably slowing down actually show the assumed behaviour and alternative stable states is not assessed.
comments.request: Assess the feedbacks and alternative stable states of the identified systems.
comments.quote: are these vegetation types actually known to follow the behaviour assumed by the model and demonstrate alternative stable states?

comments.issue: The added value relative to the many similar published analyses is not demonstrated by comparing spatial patterns.
comments.request: Compare the spatial patterns and findings with previous studies.
comments.quote: there is very little done to actually compare the spatial patterns of this study and to identify the added value of this study compared to previous ones

comments.issue: The processes potentially governing the key spatial patterns are barely discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the processes potentially governing the key patterns.
comments.quote: only very little attention is provided to explaining the potential processes that potentially govern the key patterns

reviews.assessment: Solid technical contribution to CSD detection, but the introduction overstates CSD as measuring resilience and the main message is misplaced.
strengths: solid technical contribution to CSD detection

comments.issue: The introduction equates CSD indicators with resilience although resilience is not well defined and the link is far from unequivocal.
comments.request: Stop stating that CSD indicators measure resilience.
comments.quote: if CSD is well-defined, ‘resilience’ is not, so directly stating that CSD indicator is measuring ‘resilience’ as it is done throughout the introduction section is far-fetched

comments.issue: The paper's main contribution, the closed-form results and the AC1-variance agreement condition, is not presented as the main message in the introduction.
comments.request: Present the main message earlier in the paper.
comments.quote: However, I didn't take this as the main message of the paper in the introduction section, but rather later in the paper. Other readers may also miss it

comments.issue: Whether the derivations leading to Eqs 4-8 are original is not clarified.
comments.request: Clarify the originality of Eqs 4-8 and add references if needed.
comments.quote: the authors should clarify whether results leading to Eqs 4 to 8 are original or not. In the first case it is an achievement, while in the second references are needed

comments.issue: The explanation at L113 comes too late.
comments.request: Move this explanation earlier.
comments.quote: L113 It’s useful, but it’s quite late to explain that

comments.issue: No reference is provided for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
comments.request: Provide a reference for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
comments.quote: L117. Please provide here a reference for Orstein Uhlenbeck processes

comments.issue: The paper keeps implicit the important point that the CSD-resilience relationship is not unequivocal.
comments.request: Make this caveat explicit.
comments.quote: This is suggesting that the relationship between CSD detection and resilience quantification is far from being unequivocal. This important point is unfortunately kept implicit in the paper.

comments.issue: The link to biomass is stated more closely than the evidence supports.
comments.request: Soften the claim about the biomass relationship.
comments.quote: L124 It is indeed related to biomass but not as ‘closely’ as suggested.

comments.issue: The index-independent problem in tropical forests implies the issue is intrinsic to dense canopies.
comments.request: Make explicit that the problem is intrinsic to dense canopies.
comments.quote: So the problem is intrinsic to dense canopy.

comments.issue: Figure 4 colours the Sahara grey but not central Australia, without explanation.
comments.request: Explain why the Sahara but not central Australia is grey in Figure 4.
comments.quote: Fig4. Why is Sahara gray and not central Australia?

comments.issue: The meaning of 'baseline values' is unclear.
comments.request: Define what 'baseline values' means.
comments.quote: What is meant by ‘baseline values’ is unclear for me

comments.issue: The claim that the methodology behaves 'perfectly' is too assertive given it is tested only on paradigmatic simulated data.
comments.request: Use a less assertive tone.
comments.quote: A less assertive tone would be welcome. Indeed, it behaves ‘perfectly’ with respect to a particular type of ‘paradigmatic’ simulated data.

comments.issue: The criterion used to assess 'confidence' in the calculations is not specified.
comments.request: State the criterion used to assess confidence.
comments.quote: ‘Confident calculation’. Which criterion is used to assess ‘confidence’?

comments.issue: No explanation is offered for why closed-canopy tropical forests are problematic, and the issues at L216 lack references.
comments.request: Explain the tropical forest problems and cite the relevant issues.
comments.quote: Could you propose some explanation why close canopy tropical forest also raises problems?

comments.issue: Areas showing increased resilience are not mentioned or discussed.
comments.request: Mention and discuss the areas of increased resilience.
comments.quote: Some other areas seem to show increased ‘resilience’. Why not mentioning and discussing them?

comments.issue: GPP is advocated strongly despite the earlier statement that all MODIS indices perform poorly for dense vegetation.
comments.request: Reconcile the strong GPP advocacy with the earlier statement.
comments.quote: It was stated above that all MODIS indices poorly perform wrt dense vegetation (moreover also recalled in the next sentence). Why here advocating GPP so strongly?

comments.issue: The script language used for the analyses is not stated in the paper.
comments.request: Specify the script language without requiring readers to consult Zenodo.
comments.quote: What was the script language used? Just specify to let the reader know without having to turn to Zenodo

comments.issue: Established results lack references and original results are not highlighted at L322 onward.
comments.request: Provide references for established results and highlight original ones.
comments.quote: For already established results some references should be provided (eg for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes) this is an ecology and evolution journal

title: Reliability of vegetation resilience estimates depends on biomass density

study.system: microbial communities; statistical inference of function landscapes from published data

reviews.assessment: Very well-written, valuable and timely contribution with reproducible methods and acknowledged limitations; only minor revisions.
strengths: methods described in a usable and reproducible way

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the datasets measured priority effects or whether absence of priority effects is an assumption.
comments.request: Clarify whether priority effects were measured or assumed.
comments.quote: Did any of the datasets you used in this analysis measure or study priority effects or is this an assumption?

comments.issue: The environmental origin of the datasets is not reported, so their breadth of environments is unclear.
comments.request: Add dataset environments as a column in Table S1.
comments.quote: While these datasets represent a broad spectrum of community functions, I think it would be helpful for the reader to also know if they come from a variety of environments.

comments.issue: 'High-function' and 'low-function' communities are not defined.
comments.request: Define these terms for the reader.
comments.quote: What do you mean when you refer to “high-function” and “low-function” communities? It might just help to define this for the reader.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether gLV and CRM model data are hypothetical and how they were generated.
comments.request: Clarify the data source and generation for these models.
comments.quote: Do the datasets used for the gLV and CRM models come from hypothetical datapoints and not the datasets used for the earlier section of the manuscript?

comments.issue: The green dot in Fig 4B is not accessible to colour-blind readers.
comments.request: Change the green dot to blue.
comments.quote: I would consider changing the “green dot” in Fig 4B to blue to make the image accessible to those with color blindness.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the method scales to very large, phylogenetically underdispersed and functionally redundant communities.
comments.request: Discuss how large environmental communities can be handled.
comments.quote: I am curious about landscapes generated for environmental microbial communities which can be extremely diverse (>500 taxa) and phylogenetically underdispersed with functionally redundant taxa.

comments.issue: The minimum measurements needed to apply the method are not summarized.
comments.request: Restate the minimum required measurements for new users.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful for any potential readers who would like to apply your method to their systems, if you could summarize or restate what measurements people would need at minimum.

comments.issue: Computational requirements of the modelling are not stated.
comments.request: Report whether a personal computer or HPCC is required.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to know how much computational power was required to model your datasets—could they be analyzed on a personal computer, or did they require a HPCC?

reviews.assessment: Well-conducted and interesting study, with questions about the ruggedness assumption, applicability beyond experimental communities and functional redundancy.

comments.issue: The method assumes non-rugged landscapes; it is unclear whether this holds for communities beyond those analysed.
comments.request: Address how the ruggedness assumption applies to other communities.
comments.quote: To me it seems that the method relied on the assumption that the landscapes are not rugged meaning “that they largely lack high-order epistatic contributions that would be difficult to fit with limited data”

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the approach works beyond simplified experimental communities without complex or antagonistic interactions.
comments.request: Explain the method's applicability to more complex communities.
comments.quote: Would this approach work beyond these exact experimental communities? In experimental work communities often tend to be simplified and very complex or antagonistic interactions are not desired since it makes experimenting more difficult.

comments.issue: How the analysis handles different species performing the same function is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how functional redundancy is handled.
comments.quote: This might be a detail, but how would your analysis deal with different species but the same function in the community?

reviews.assessment: Important contribution with findings relevant to a broad audience; several dataset, model and terminology points should be addressed.
strengths: commonness of smooth landscapes validated across community types
identification of interaction network types where the method works

comments.issue: The xylose oxidation measurement combines redox dye and biomass absorbance, which should be stated, along with the timepoint analysed.
comments.request: State the confound explicitly and specify the timepoint analysed.
comments.quote: I believe that the function that was effectively reported was the combined effect of the redox dye and the community biomass on the culture’s (600nm) absorbance.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the Sanchez-Gorostiaga dataset is combinatorially complete; incomplete data should be acknowledged.
comments.request: Clarify completeness or analyse the complete dataset in the supplement.
comments.quote: Isn’t the dataset in Sanchez-Gorostiaga et al. combinatorially complete? If the dataset is indeed incomplete or partially unavailable, this should be mentioned in the Methods.

comments.issue: It is unexplained why only 160 of the 225 Diaz-Colunga consortia were used for biomass.
comments.request: Explain the exclusion of the remaining consortia.
comments.quote: The dataset in Diaz-Colunga includes 164 consortia from one set of experiments and 61 from another set. Why only 160 were here considered for the biomass function?

comments.issue: The text should state more directly that any scenario well modelled by a second-order model can be inferred by cutting at second order.
comments.request: State this implication and confirm the reasoning.
comments.quote: the landscape of any scenario that is well modelled under a different second-order model (such as the gLV model) can be inferred with the presented method, cutting it at the 2nd-order.

comments.issue: The gLV simulations vary only a subset of parameters; reciprocity and carrying capacity spread should also be swept.
comments.request: Add supplemental analyses varying these parameters.
comments.quote: For completeness, it would be appropriate to include some supplemental analysis in which the reciprocity and the carrying capacity spread parameters vary.

comments.issue: Low-diversity consortia cannot show higher-order interactions and may bias higher-order betas towards zero.
comments.request: Test this bias, compare residuals, and colour Fig 2 by species number.
comments.quote: I wonder if this significantly biases the training of the model, since all of these communities might weight the betas (average contribution of an interaction) of higher order towards zero.

comments.issue: The paper implies any function is emergent, but biomass is not emergent by the standard definition.
comments.request: Define emergent function specifically and revise the text.
comments.quote: Across the text, the authors seem to imply that any community function is an emergent community function. From my perspective, biomass, for example, is generally not an emergent function.

comments.issue: The discussion of complementarity between functional landscapes and global epistasis models could be extended.
comments.request: Expand this discussion with the suggested questions.
comments.quote: Given that many of the authors are involved in both the present work and the work on global epistasis in Diaz-Colunga et al., I believe that their discussion about the complementarity of functional landscapes and global epistasis models could be extended.

comments.issue: The sentence misleads readers into thinking R^2 is ~0.8 for all first-order models.
comments.request: Revise the sentence.
comments.quote: Line 152, please revise this sentence. The reader might interpret that R^2 coefficients are around 0.8 for all first order models, which is only true for all the second order models presented.

comments.issue: The claim that Kehe et al. is an exception is questionable; the trend across panels could be gradual.
comments.request: Revise the sentence accordingly.
comments.quote: I am not sure that the results for Kehe et al. are an exception. Figure 2 seems to present the results ordered by the relative contribution of order 1 vs order 2.

comments.issue: The symbol r is called both roughness and ruggedness.
comments.request: Unify the terminology.
comments.quote: Lines 216-217, r is referred to as roughness and ruggedness. Perhaps unify terminology?

comments.issue: How the method works at line 279 may not be obvious to readers.
comments.request: Clarify with a simple three-species example.
comments.quote: it might not be obvious to the reader how this works. Would you consider to clarify with a simple example e.g. for 3 species?

comments.issue: Averaging realisations with different initial abundances may favour the model's apparent success under alternative stable states.
comments.request: Mention this caveat for future users.
comments.quote: averaging the outcome of realizations that vary in initial relative abundances, but not in presence/absence, goes in favor of the model’s success as it is assessed in this work

title: Statistically learning the functional landscape of microbial communities

study.system: fossil synapsids; metatree, jaw length and diet data

editor_summary: Reviewers are extremely enthusiastic about the data resource, but the analyses and the analytical question itself need shoring up; revise addressing all reviewer and editor comments.

reviews.assessment: Praises the impressive metatree and sound approach, but asks to fix results statements that do not match Supplementary Table 1 and to credit earlier proposals.

comments.issue: Several results statements about group breakdowns and trend significance do not match Supplementary Table 1.
comments.request: Correct or clarify the statements that conflict with Supplementary Table 1.
comments.quote: there are a couple of statements in their results section which don't seem to match the data in Supplementary Table 1 provided

comments.issue: Wording implies a completely novel proposal that small body size drove mammalian-phenotype evolution, though this was proposed before.
comments.request: Acknowledge the previous authors who proposed this idea.
comments.quote: it seems to suggest that they are making a completely novel proposal, but this has already been explicitly proposed by previous authors

comments.issue: R code is not included in the supplementary data.
comments.request: Include the R code in the supplementary data.
comments.quote: The only addition I would like to see if their R-code, which I recommend should be included in the supplementary data

comments.issue: The number of published character matrices is misstated as 270 instead of 269.
comments.request: Correct the count to 269.
comments.quote: "based on 270 published character matrices" Comment: I think this should be 269?

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: bold formatting at line 97 and a missing space in a reference at line 221.
comments.quote: I think this is not meant to be in bold type.

comments.issue: Therocephalia and Anomodontia trends are called significant but Supplementary Table 1 shows they are not especially significant.
comments.request: Correct or explain the significance statements in light of Supplementary Table 1.
comments.quote: According to Sup Table 1 they are not especially significant (although I guess it depends what you are calling significant

comments.issue: The higher significance value for gorgonopsians may reflect the small sample size, as for Ophiacodontids.
comments.request: Incorporate the small-sample caveat into the relevant statements.
comments.quote: As for Ophiacodontids, the higher significance value for gorgonopsians could be due to the small sample size.

comments.issue: The Multituberculata omnivore-to-herbivore trend is called significant although Supplementary Table 1 reports 0.198 r2 and 0.147 p-value.
comments.request: Explain or correct the claim of a significant trend.
comments.quote: Sup Table 1 records 0.198 r2 and 0.147 p-value, which is not especially significant

comments.issue: The metatherian faunivory pattern statement is not a result and is misplaced in the results section.
comments.request: Move this statement to the discussion.
comments.quote: Perhaps more appropriate for the discussion than the results section, as this is not a result.

comments.issue: The opposite body-size outcomes of the end-Guadalupian and Permo-Triassic extinctions are not reconciled and sound self-contradictory.
comments.request: Add a sentence explaining why one mass extinction had the opposite effect.
comments.quote: I think a sentence here to explain why one mass extinction event had the opposite effect to another is necessary

comments.issue: Lautenschlager et al. (2018) is under-credited and the endothermy link to miniaturisation is not mentioned.
comments.request: Reword to credit Lautenschlager and cite miniaturisation-endothermy work.
comments.quote: Although Lautenschlager is referenced here, the wording at present doesn't give enough credit to their work.

comments.issue: Brocklehurst et al. (2021) is not cited for the conclusion that removing incumbents starts diversification.
comments.request: Cite Brocklehurst et al. (2021) in support of this conclusion.
comments.quote: I think you ought to cite Brocklehurst et al. (2021) here.

comments.issue: The Figure 1 caption phrase 'smaller, straight lines' is confusing and implies only the smallest lines are meant.
comments.request: Remove or reword the 'smaller, straight lines' phrase.
comments.quote: This confused me, it read as though you are singling out only the smallest straight lines

comments.issue: The first four radiations are paraphyletic grades; whether this affects their results versus the fifth group is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss whether the paraphyletic grades affect these results.
comments.quote: I wonder if you think this has any effect on your results for those groups versus the 5th (and final) group?

reviews.assessment: Well-written and visually appealing study, but the framing, the undefined 'small-bodied faunivore' concepts and coarse PBDB diet data raise substantial doubts.

comments.issue: Clade specialists familiar with their groups' body sizes may not find the results particularly surprising.
comments.quote: these results may well not seem particularly surprising to researchers working on each of these five clades

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the aim is absolute small body size or progenitors being smaller than descendants (Cope's rule), and 'small' is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify the aim and define what counts as a 'small-bodied' organism.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me whether the authors main aim is to test whether the progenitors of ARs are objectively, biologically 'small-bodied'

comments.issue: The ancestral state reconstruction results are barely discussed and only mammaliaform and therian values are cited.
comments.request: Discuss the ASR results more and compare them with the OUM5 optima and Table 1.
comments.quote: the results of this are barely discussed and only the numbers for the mammaliaform and therian clades are cited in the text

comments.issue: The hypothesis that faunivory is the most generalist ecology is not justified, and it contradicts a null hypothesis of omnivore generalism.
comments.request: Justify why faunivory is considered the most generalist ecology, or revise the hypothesis.
comments.quote: Can the authors justify why faunivory is hypothesised to be the most 'generalist' ecology

comments.issue: Morphological specialisation is conflated with ecological specialisation; key innovations may have made mammals better generalists.
comments.request: Clarify whether the innovations reflect ecological or only morphological specialisation.
comments.quote: I wonder if the key innovations they discuss make the organism more ecologically specialized or only more morphologically specialised

comments.issue: Lumping true carnivores with insectivores (and browsers/grazer with frugivores) into faunivore and herbivore conflates distinct ecological niches.
comments.request: Justify combining these niches or analyse finer dietary categories.
comments.quote: there would seem to be a big difference ecologically between a 'true' carnivore and an insectivore

comments.issue: The mvOUM results are treated as secondary even though they are the more interesting part of the paper.
comments.request: Bring the mvOUM results more to the forefront of the paper's question.
comments.quote: The more interesting mvOUM methods seem secondary to these findings, so it might be beneficial to bring these results more to the forefront

comments.issue: The mvOUM models were not tested on trees with the alternative topologies discussed in the supplement.
comments.request: Test the mvOUM models on alternative topologies and present that tree.
comments.quote: it would strengthen confidence in the results to test at least the mvOUM models on a tree with these alternative topologies

comments.issue: The metatree in Figure 2 is too small to assess the topology because tip species names are missing.
comments.request: Provide a larger metatree figure with species names at the tips.
comments.quote: I would like to see a larger version of the metatree in Figure 2 in the supplement, with species names at the tips.

comments.issue: PBDB feeding ecology assignments are troublesome because many are inferred at genus, order or clade level rather than for the species.
comments.request: Vet assignments not sourced at species or genus level and annotate the notes.
comments.quote: I would suggest not relying on the PBDB alone where the source is anything other than the species or genus

comments.issue: The main text does not state that some jaw lengths are estimated from regressions.
comments.request: Note in the main text that some jaw lengths come from regressions.
comments.quote: It would be nice for the authors to indicate in the main manuscript that some of these jaw lengths are obtained from regressions

comments.issue: PGLS was not used to account for phylogenetic relationships when testing body size evolution against time.
comments.request: Explain why PGLS was not used, or apply it.
comments.quote: Is there a reason that the authors do not use PGLS to test the relationship between body size evolution and time for the different clades?

comments.issue: The assumption that the oldest regime state is stationary is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what this assumption means and why it is warranted.
comments.quote: Can the authors better explain what is meant by 'we assumed the oldest regime state to be stationary' and why that was warranted?

comments.issue: Results of poorly fitting models are not reported, contrary to checklist point 3b.
comments.request: Provide the results of the rejected models in the supplement.
comments.quote: The authors do not report the results of models that are poor fits to the data

comments.issue: No ancestral state reconstruction on diet was performed, so the ancestral faunivore state cannot be verified.
comments.request: Reconstruct ancestral diet states and map them onto the tree.
comments.quote: The authors do not perform an ancestral state reconstruction on diet. This would be extremely beneficial and strengthen their paper.

comments.issue: ASR jaw sizes and branch tip jaw sizes are not represented graphically.
comments.request: Add these values graphically to a supplementary figure.
comments.quote: Authors should also consider representing ASR jaw sizes and branch tip jaw sizes graphically

comments.issue: The SBF acronym for 'small-bodied faunivore' is unnecessary and makes the manuscript harder to read.
comments.request: Do not use the SBF acronym.
comments.quote: I do not find it necessary to use an acronym for 'small-bodied faunivore' (SBF)

comments.issue: The text does not make clear that the pelycosaur trend is non-significant.
comments.request: State explicitly that the pelycosaur results are non-significant.
comments.quote: perhaps should be emphasised that the results are non-significant for pelycosaurs

comments.issue: It is unclear which regressions demonstrated the mammaliaform pattern and how they relate to the non-significant Kendall correlation.
comments.request: Explain which regressions are meant and how the non-significant correlation fits.
comments.quote: Which regressions, in what way? (Please explain RE mammaliaform non-significant kendall rank correlation etc.)

comments.issue: The different model variations tested are not listed.
comments.request: List all the variations tested.
comments.quote: Line 414: 'as well as different variations..'. Can you list them all please.

comments.issue: Points of different clades obscure each other in Figure 1b and the number of overlapping points is unclear.
comments.request: Jitter points by clade and indicate overplotting counts.
comments.quote: Can you jitter points for every other clade. Oldest Therapsid (blue) dots seem to be obscured by Pelycosaur (black) dots

comments.issue: The layout of Table 2 is difficult to understand, with optima estimates seemingly only for pelycosaurs.
comments.request: Centre the results and extend arrows to the grouping lines.
comments.quote: it took me some time to understand how the table layout worked

comments.issue: Many line-level copy edits: reference-name and reference-list errors, missing space, bold formatting, 'Hanson' for Hansen, and a duplicated book date.
comments.quote: Line 230: 'Brocklehurst et al. 2021' does not appear in the reference list.

reviews.assessment: A broad-interest analysis worth publishing, but the missing phylogenetic correction, coarse diet categories and sparse Cenozoic sampling need attention.
strengths: much larger dataset than prior work

comments.issue: The title uses jargon ('faunivore', 'synapsid') that few readers outside vertebrate palaeontology will understand.
comments.request: Choose a title accessible to non-specialists.
comments.quote: The paper's title does not help its cause. "Faunivore" and "synapsid" are both technical jargon of obvious meaning to mammalogists

comments.issue: No criterion or numerical justification is given for focusing on the five listed radiations.
comments.request: Provide numerical justification for focusing on these five groups.
comments.quote: The list of five radiations given on p. 3 seems arbitrary. No criterion is given for focusing on them.

comments.issue: The placental radiation is not analysed even though the dataset extends into the Eocene.
comments.request: Explain why the placental radiation was not analysed.
comments.quote: Given that the data set runs into the Eocene, why was the placental radiation not also analysed?

comments.issue: How 'matrix reuse' is defined, why publication year is used as a criterion, and how matrix size factors into the metatree are unclear.
comments.request: Explain matrix reuse, the year criterion, and how matrix size is used.
comments.quote: it would be nice if the authors could say a little more about how "matrix reuse" is defined and why publication year is a criterion

comments.issue: The PaleoDB is presumed comprehensive, and valid species absent from it are discarded instead of getting ages from primary literature.
comments.request: Justify the assumption or source ages for excluded species from the primary literature.
comments.quote: So what motivates this assumption? And when valid species are present in matrices but not in the PaleoDB, then why throw them out instead of doing the hard work and getting their age ranges from the primary literature?

comments.issue: The Sidor and Hopson (1998) backbone is very old and no explanation or newer alternative is given.
comments.request: Use a more recent backbone or explain the choice.
comments.quote: Speaking as a fossil myself, Sidor and Hopson (1998) is ancient (if absolutely classic).

comments.issue: The three-way diet classification (faunivore/omnivore/herbivore) is an oversimplification of mammal dietary diversity.
comments.request: Use finer dietary categories (e.g. Pineda-Munoz et al.) and justify the scheme.
comments.quote: The paper rests on a three-way classification of diet (faunivore/omnivore/herbivore) that is a real oversimplification.

comments.issue: More than half of the dietary assignments come straight from the PaleoDB, whose categorisation is more comprehensive than the three-way split.
comments.request: Use the more detailed dietary categories available in the PaleoDB.
comments.quote: Seemingly more than half of the dietary assignments are straight from the Paleobiology Database.

comments.issue: Many PaleoDB diet categories are inferred from assignments to inclusive higher taxa rather than direct species data.
comments.request: Prefer direct dietary data over inferred higher-taxon assignments.
comments.quote: The PaleoDB assignments apply directly to particular species in some cases, but in many cases categories are inferred based on states assigned to inclusive higher taxa.

comments.issue: Cenozoic mammal representation is sparse and idiosyncratic, with major clades represented by only a handful of species.
comments.request: Improve taxonomic coverage of Cenozoic mammals, especially carnivorans and others.
comments.quote: Representation of Cenozoic mammals is sparse and idiosyncratic. Major clades are in some cases represented by just a handful of species.

comments.issue: The regression analyses ignore phylogenetic non-independence of the sampled points.
comments.request: Use methods such as independent contrasts or PGLS to account for phylogeny.
comments.quote: The regression analyses don't account for phylogenetic non-independence of points at all.

comments.issue: The choice of Kendall rather than Spearman coefficients is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the choice of Kendall coefficients.
comments.quote: Why were Kendall coefficients used instead of Spearman coefficients (line 395)? Please explain.

comments.issue: The correlations and p-values are unimpressive and two clades in the key diet analyses are marginal; p-value precision is inconsistent.
comments.request: Discuss the marginal support and report p-values with consistent precision.
comments.quote: The correlations and p-values are unimpressive (Table 1).

comments.issue: Plain regression was used instead of a GLM with a quasibinomial link for the binary diet trends.
comments.request: Reanalyse with an appropriate GLM (quasibinomial link).
comments.quote: why was plain regression used (illustrated in Fig. 1) instead of a GLM with a quasibinomial link?

comments.issue: Brownian motion is biologically wrong for body size; Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics should have been used for ancestral values.
comments.request: Use Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics for ancestral size estimates.
comments.quote: Brownian motion is certainly wrong for body size, or else the world would be full of football-stadium sized shrews and mite-sized elephants.

comments.issue: Some imaginable model combinations involving Td are missing from Table 2.
comments.request: Explain why these model combinations were not tested.
comments.quote: Some imaginable combinations involving Td are left out of Table 2: OUNM2_Td_Cy, OUNM2_Td_Mf, etc. Why?

comments.issue: Three models are within the conventional AICc range yet only one is focused on.
comments.request: Justify focusing on one model when three are within delta AICc ~2.
comments.quote: It's conventional to start worrying about AICc differences only if they're about two units or more

comments.issue: Alroy et al. (1998) and Alroy (2000) on Cope's rule and trend dynamics are not referenced.
comments.request: Cite Alroy et al. (1998) and Alroy (2000) here.
comments.quote: There's no Alroy et al. (1998) in the references (lines 225 - 226).

comments.issue: The 'Cretaceous Terrestrial Revolution' is a dubious concept that should not be invoked.
comments.request: Remove or replace this term.
comments.quote: What "Cretaceous Terrestrial Revolution" (line 231)? This is a molecular hallucination. Best to ignore it.

comments.issue: Dedicated vertivory is lumped into faunivory and implicitly treated as unspecialised, which is unjustified.
comments.request: Treat vertivory as potentially specialised and test with finer categories.
comments.quote: I think it's quite strange to implicitly assume that dedicated vertivory, lumped in here as faunivory, is somehow "unspecialised"

comments.issue: The specialisation/generalisation distinction is unresolvable yet the title, abstract and key passages dwell on it.
comments.request: Focus on the facts (body size and diet) rather than this distinction.
comments.quote: the distinction is unresolvable and therefore not very important, but the title, abstract, and other key passages all dwell on it

comments.issue: The Conclusions section largely restates earlier points.
comments.request: Condense or remove the Conclusions section.
comments.quote: The "Conclusions" section could be condensed or removed because it largely restates points made earlier.

title: Derived faunivores are the forerunners of major synapsid radiations

study.system: tropical reef fish; depth zonation; 35 Pacific islands

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns; the manuscript cannot be accepted now, though a revised version addressing the serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Good, well-written basin-scale study; asks for methodological detail, clarification of biomass zonation framing and many line-level edits.

comments.issue: Survey methods and consistency of fish identification and length measurement are not described enough.
comments.request: Add methodological detail on the survey and measurement consistency.
comments.quote: More methodological information, especially in relation to the survey method and how consistency in fish identification and fish length measurements was achieved

comments.issue: The Bayesian modelling could not be evaluated by this reviewer.
comments.request: Have a statistician familiar with the method review the models.
comments.quote: I would advise having someone familiar with this method to review the statistical methodology used.

comments.issue: 'Depth zonation' will be read as community-composition zonation; the biomass/trophic scope should be clear in the title.
comments.request: Clarify the title and term usage.
comments.quote: I think it is important to clarify even in the title that this concerns zonation in biomass and/or trophic groups

comments.issue: 'Deep-water' is not defined at L67.
comments.request: Define deep-water or rephrase.
comments.quote: Line 67. Define deep-water (e.g. >200m)

comments.issue: 'Shallow-water' is not defined at L70.
comments.request: Define shallow-water.
comments.quote: Line 70. Define shallow-water

comments.issue: The L82 term has been argued to refer to one ocean and should be clarified.
comments.request: Clarify the term with the cited source.
comments.quote: This is because it has been argued to refer to one ocean

comments.issue: 'Predictably' does not belong in the Results section.
comments.request: Remove 'predictably' at L116.
comments.quote: Line 116: I would remove “predictably” as it’s the results section

comments.issue: Table 1 underlines negative associations instead of using minus signs.
comments.request: Use minus signs in front of numbers.
comments.quote: I would change underlining negative associations to adding a - in front of numbers

comments.issue: Figure S1 duplicates important information better shown with Figure 1.
comments.request: Merge Figure S1 with Figure 1.
comments.quote: I would merge it with Fig. 1 as they both show important information.

comments.issue: Lines 203-214 belong in the methods or introduction.
comments.request: Move this text out of the Results.
comments.quote: This would fit better in the materials and methods or introduction section.

comments.issue: The L224 variance result may already be captured elsewhere.
comments.request: Remove or clarify the redundancy.
comments.quote: Is that not already captured in lines 261-218?

comments.issue: Site-scale variance estimates differ between locations in the text and are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the estimation and mention probabilities in the main text.
comments.quote: Why does the site-scale variance here (38-64%) differ from that at line 25-52%?

comments.issue: Goreau 1959 and similar studies concern species composition, not biomass zonation.
comments.request: Represent these studies accurately.
comments.quote: Some of those studies, e.g. Goreau, 1959 talk about zonation focusing on species composition rather than changes in biomass.

comments.issue: L245 should be hedged as 'To our knowledge'.
comments.request: Rephrase to 'To our knowledge, this is the first time'.
comments.quote: Line 245: I would rephrase to “To our knowledge, this is the first time

comments.issue: L255 statement may not apply to all cases.
comments.request: Clarify whether only unpopulated sites are meant.
comments.quote: Line 255: Only unpopulated?

comments.issue: The L304-306 steepness explanation needs expansion.
comments.request: Expand this passage.
comments.quote: Can you expand a little bit more here?

comments.issue: The L307 difference is mainly in absolute values; depth-related changes in biomass remained.
comments.request: Rephrase to reflect the smaller difference.
comments.quote: For most part the depth-related changes in biomass remained the for trophic groups, it’s just the absolute values that were reduced, no?

comments.issue: L333-334 refers to species although the study focuses on trophic groups.
comments.request: Mention trophic groups instead.
comments.quote: Would mentioning specific trophic groups that peform distinct functions be more accurate?

comments.issue: Refs 6 and 25 concern species-composition zonation, not trophic-group biomass.
comments.request: Describe these references accurately.
comments.quote: Again refs 6 and 25 concern zonation because of changes in species and not trophic group biomass.

comments.issue: The difference between populated and unpopulated islands is presented as larger than it is; directions are the same.
comments.request: Present the difference more accurately.
comments.quote: The direction of change was the same though. I know you mention it, but the way it’s presented both here and in the discussion, is like it is very different.

comments.issue: L386-388 cites ecological paradigms without examples.
comments.request: Add examples of the paradigms.
comments.quote: Can you add eamples of ecological paradigms that are included in the refs you cite, here?

comments.issue: Why island-scale variance is lower than site or ecoregion variance, and its conservation implication, is unexplored.
comments.request: Discuss this variance hierarchy.
comments.quote: Why was variation between islands less than between sites or between ecoregions?

comments.issue: Whether the same divers conducted all surveys, and observer variability in identification, is unaddressed.
comments.request: Report diver teams and acknowledge identification variability.
comments.quote: Where all the surveys conducted by the same team of divers? If not, then authors must acknowledge the variability in species identifications.

comments.issue: No references support the SPC survey method.
comments.request: Cite studies using this method.
comments.quote: Can the authors cite other studies that have used this method?

comments.issue: Underwater length estimation to the nearest centimetre may be strongly biased at distances up to 15 m.
comments.request: Explain how length-measurement consistency was assured.
comments.quote: I am struggling to understand how this could be achieved underwater without a significant amount of bias given that some fish could be as far away as 15m.

comments.issue: Whether the 400 m buffer was cross-checked against sites, islands' opposite sides, and reef flat/crest zones is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the buffer definition and checks.
comments.quote: Does this mean that 400m was cross-checked against all surveyed sites to make sure it does not include opposite sides of the island?

comments.issue: The model type used at L444-451 lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Cite one or two references for the model.
comments.quote: Can you cite 1-2 refs for the type of model you ended up using?

comments.issue: The criterion for an acceptable proportion of zeros at L480 is unstated.
comments.request: State the criterion.
comments.quote: What criterion was used to determine if the propotion of zeros was low enough?

reviews.assessment: Well-designed, interesting and well-written study; main concerns are species filtering and comparability with the MacNeil et al. baseline data.

comments.issue: Excluding all sharks and jacks removes ecologically important top predators and may bias results.
comments.request: Reconsider the exclusion and filter more selectively.
comments.quote: I ask that the authors reconsider removing the entire group of sharks and jacks and be more selective in their filtering

comments.issue: Species filtering differs from MacNeil et al., making the unfished-biomass baselines incomparable and potentially biased.
comments.request: Justify filtering or match the baseline study's approach.
comments.quote: It does not seem like the authors in this study used the same filtering process to exclude the same species.

comments.issue: Whether patterns hold within each ecoregion is not explored.
comments.request: Add discussion on consistency within ecoregions.
comments.quote: Are the patterns consistent within each ecoregion?

comments.issue: The biomass density unit at L445 is ambiguous.
comments.request: Use g m-2.
comments.quote: Line 445 – (biomass density; g-m2) do you mean g m-2

comments.issue: Figures appear low resolution and slightly blurry.
comments.request: Confirm figure quality for publication.
comments.quote: the figures appear to be low resolution and slightly blurry

comments.issue: Aguijan's classification as 'Populated' is questioned; it may reflect proximity to Tinian and Saipan.
comments.request: Clarify the population classification.
comments.quote: Table S1 – Aguijan categorized as “Populated”? I assume this is due to its proximity to Tinian and Saipan rather than its small resident population?

reviews.assessment: Questions whether the study is sufficiently novel for this journal and criticizes the lack of covariates and coarse human-pressure categorization.
strengths: modern analytical techniques with convincing depth gradients
interesting steepness finding at rare scale

comments.issue: Depth zonation and human homogenization are well known; the study may not be sufficiently novel or consequential for the journal.
comments.request: Demonstrate a stronger contribution or reframe the question.
comments.quote: I question whether this elevates the paper to one that should be published in Nature Ecology & Evolution

comments.issue: Human population pressure is reduced to a binary populated/unpopulated category.
comments.request: Model population pressure as a continuous variable with trends and thresholds.
comments.quote: why not consider population pressure as a continuous variable and look at more general trends and thresholds?

comments.issue: Benthic assemblage differences are ignored; coral cover or habitat type could isolate the depth signal.
comments.request: Include a benthic metric such as coral cover in the analyses.
comments.quote: why not include a basic metric like coral cover (or even habitat type) in the analyses to better isolate the depth signal?

comments.issue: Readily available covariates (net primary productivity, temperature, wave exposure, island type) are absent, leaving drivers speculative.
comments.request: Add key environmental covariates to the models.
comments.quote: had the models included covariates of e.g. net primary productivity, temperature, or wave exposure (all of which are relatively straightforward to obtain)

title: Local human impacts disrupt depth-dependent zonation of tropical reef fish communities

study.system: ancient human genome; Buran-Kaya III, Crimea, Gravettian context

editor_summary: Finds the work of considerable potential interest but requires revision addressing all reviewer concerns before it can be reconsidered.

reviews.assessment: Finds the results worth publishing but demands a fundamental rewrite of the archaeological framing, terminology and Gravettian attribution.
strengths: new genome from an important site

comments.issue: The title and opening sentence imply a naive, essentialist approach ignoring the aDNA-archaeology debate.
comments.request: Rethink the title and first sentence and avoid misrepresenting archaeological cultures.
comments.quote: The use of the term "the origin of the Gravettians" in the paper title, as well as the first sentence of the paper in particular, suggest a rather naïve approach to archaeological understandings of past populations

comments.issue: Technocomplex is treated as synonymous with archaeological culture, and key terms are undefined.
comments.request: Use archaeological terminology correctly and define 'materially defined culture' and similar phrases.
comments.quote: a technocomplex is not synonymous with an archaeological culture (see Clarke 1968), and it is not clear what is meant by e.g. "materially defined culture" or "archaeologically defined material industries".

comments.issue: The Gravettian overview cites work only up to 1996 and focuses on Central Europe instead of more relevant eastern regions.
comments.request: Update the literature and discuss the records of Ukraine, Moldova, Russia and Romania.
comments.quote: the most recent work cited here is from 1996 (!) and the abundant work from the last two decades on these questions is ignored

comments.issue: Kostenki 14 is wrongly said to be in the Borshchyovo archaeological complex.
comments.request: Correct the Kostenki-Borshchevo error at lines 72-73.
comments.quote: Kostenki 14 is not "found in the Borshchyovo archaeological complex", the area is known as Kostenki-Borshchevo

comments.issue: Crimea is treated as Eastern Europe although it is geographically and ecologically part of the Caucasus.
comments.request: Regroup Buran-Kaya III with Caucasus sites rather than the Russian Plain.
comments.quote: Crimea is better treated from a geographical standpoint as being the northwesternmost extension of the Caucasus

comments.issue: The European EUP is Aurignacian without backed lithics; backed-lithic assemblages appear later.
comments.request: Reflect this chronology and the questionable old dates in the argument.
comments.quote: at EUP sites in the rest of Europe we do not have backed lithics: the sites are Aurignacian

comments.issue: Buran-Kaya III is presented as Gravettian as if accepted fact, contrary to Hublin (2015).
comments.request: Stop treating the Gravettian attribution as established.
comments.quote: I am questioning whether we should automatically describe these assemblages as Gravettian

comments.issue: The Caucasus-Gravettian link rests only on shared backed lithics without broader assemblage study.
comments.request: Study lithic technology, ornaments and other assemblage aspects before linking them.
comments.quote: we need a better understanding of all aspects of the assemblages (lithic technology, personal ornaments, etc) that goes beyond the basic observation of the shared presence of backed lithics

comments.issue: 'Early Gravettian' is already established for later assemblages and should not be used for these.
comments.request: Use a neutral term such as 'Caucasus backed lithic assemblages'.
comments.quote: I plead with the authors *not* to use the term Early Gravettian as they do in this paper, since that term is already well established

comments.issue: The link between Crimea/Caucasus and European Gravettian is presented as fact rather than hypothesis.
comments.request: Present the link as a hypothesis tested with genetic evidence, requiring a fundamental rewrite.
comments.quote: Therefore, the link between them should be treated as a hypothesis rather than as simple fact.

comments.issue: Sungir' is misclassified as Gravettian despite lacking backed blade(let)s.
comments.request: Describe Sungir' as Streletskian and avoid 'Eastern Gravettian'.
comments.quote: Sungir' is *not* Gravettian according to the authors' own definition of Gravettian, and it should not be presented as such.

comments.issue: The cautious 'attributed to Gorodtsovian' label for Kostenki 12 is unwarranted.
comments.request: Describe Kostenki 12/Ia as Gorodtsovian without hedging.
comments.quote: Kostenki 12 is frequently described as "attributed to Gorodtsovian" rather than just "Gorodtsovian" (e.g. Supp Table 6) – why the extra caution concerning this attribution?

comments.issue: The Discussion at lines 266-287 is difficult to understand, including the significance and robustness of comparisons.
comments.request: Revise the Discussion for clarity and sentence structure.
comments.quote: the text in the Discussion lines 266-287 is rather difficult to make sense of and I would strongly recommend that it be revised for clarity and sentence structure

comments.issue: The Gravettian characterization at lines 29-32 is unsupported; only backed lithics characterize all Gravettian sites.
comments.request: Add references and correct the shared-innovations claim.
comments.quote: the only thing that characterizes all Gravettian sites is the presence of backed lithics

comments.issue: The radiocarbon calibration at lines 32-33 is incorrect.
comments.request: Correct the calibration: 21 ka 14C BP is ca. 25.5-25 ka cal BP.
comments.quote: The calibration is incorrect here: 21ka 14C BP calibrates to ca. 25.5-25 ka cal BP in OxCal using IntCal13.

comments.issue: The claim that the Gravettian blossomed in Central Europe is superficial and unsupported.
comments.request: Revise the Central European zenith claim and the classical Gravettian characterization.
comments.quote: while early Gravettian assemblages across Europe are often described as "Early Gravettian", the middle/later Gravettian is not the "classical Gravettian". This is a strangely superficial reading of the complexity of the Mid Upper Palaeolithic.

reviews.assessment: Admires the technical approach but says several genetic comparisons are overinterpreted given overlapping confidence intervals and low data.
strengths: sensitive methods for poorly preserved DNA

comments.issue: The claimed lower affinity to GoyetQ116-1 is not significant because confidence intervals overlap and D-statistics show no difference.
comments.request: Reassess the exclusion of GoyetQ116-1 and the Vestonice16 allele-sharing claim.
comments.quote: the confidence intervals of this statistics overlap with those of Vestonice16 and Kostenki14 (as it is shown in the Figure S3., with both Mbuti and Han as outgroups)

comments.issue: The informative statistic D(BuranKaya, X; Y, outgroup) is missing without explanation.
comments.request: Present D(BuranKaya, X; Y, outgroup) tests.
comments.quote: The statistics that would be highly informative for resolving these relationships in more detail, and that I haven't seen presented, is D(BuranKaya, X; Y, outgroup).

comments.issue: Comparisons using ~50 SNPs and small-data individuals produce large statistical noise; the 30% cutoff is untested and N(SNPs) undefined.
comments.request: Focus analyses on higher-coverage individuals and explain the SNP count and cutoff.
comments.quote: Having 50 SNPs used for the comparisons is far too few to make general conclusions.

comments.issue: Buran Kaya shares more drift with Muierii2 than Kostenki12, a result not explained and inconsistent with the conclusions.
comments.request: Explain the Muierii2 and related results and interpret low-coverage statistics cautiously.
comments.quote: it would seem that Buran Kaya actually shares more drift with Muierii2 than with Kostenki12 both when looking at all SNPs and transversions only. This statistics is not explained anywhere in the text.

comments.issue: The claim of no genome-wide allele sharing with Natufians conflicts with the higher f3 for Natufian9 than Paglicci133.
comments.request: Correct the Natufian statement in the Discussion.
comments.quote: the statement in the Discussion, lines 291-293 about not detecting genome-wide allele sharing between Buran Kaya and the Natufians would not be correct as the f3 between Buran Kaya and Natufian9 is higher than the one from Paglicci133.

comments.issue: Comparing f3 point estimates without significance testing is an inappropriate way to draw conclusions.
