comments.request: Test connections with D-statistics rather than comparing f3 point estimates.
comments.quote: Doing most of the comparisons with just f3 statistics and then comparing f3 point estimates to each other is less appropriate way of drawing conclusions.

comments.issue: Individual order on the X-axis varies between figures.
comments.request: Fix the individual order consistently across figures.
comments.quote: It would be more helpful to have the same order of individuals on the X-axis throughout different figures

comments.issue: Figure S6 is more informative than the main Figure 4.
comments.request: Replace main Figure 4 with Figure S6.
comments.quote: For the paper and the conclusions drawn it would be more informative to have the Figure S6. replacing the main figure 4.

comments.issue: Figures S3 and S4 do not mark the Gravettian-associated individuals.
comments.request: Add boxed names for Gravettian individuals in Figures S3 and S4.
comments.quote: For the figures S3. and S4., there are no boxed names indicating the individuals associated with the Gravettian.

comments.issue: Ancestry-informative SNPs can inflate Neandertal ancestry estimates.
comments.request: Estimate Neandertal ancestry using direct f4-ratios with two high-coverage Neandertal genomes.
comments.quote: using ancestry informative SNPs for calculating the proportion of Neandertal ancestry can inflate these values. You can try to calculate the proportion of Neandertal ancestry with the direct f4-rations by making use of the two high coverage Neandertal genomes instead.

comments.issue: Two copy edits: UNG versus UDG at line 105, and Fu et al. year at line 221.
comments.quote: Line 105 - should UNG be UDG?

reviews.assessment: Values the new genome but considers several major claims unsupported by the low-coverage data, recommending reanalysis with shotgun data.
strengths: novel genomic data naturally very exciting
expected damage patterns and negligible contamination

comments.issue: The unit of the Neanderthal ancestry 95% CI is unclear, mixing percentage and fraction.
comments.request: Clarify the CI unit.
comments.quote: it is a bit unclear what the unit of the 95% CI is, as the point estimate is reported as percentage but the CI as fraction

comments.issue: Low-coverage comparisons are too noisy to support claimed affinities; Kostenki12/Pavlov1 error bars overlap Tianyuan's.
comments.request: Restrict conclusions to high-coverage comparisons.
comments.quote: the standard errors for the corresponding outgroup-f3 statistic of those individuals entirely overlap those for Tianyuan, a 40kya East Asian individual

comments.issue: Using the full 3 million SNP set across different capture panels introduces ascertainment bias in f3 estimates.
comments.request: Restrict analyses to SNPs covered in all compared individuals.
comments.quote: As the ascertainment differs between the different capture panels, this can cause systematic bias in the shared drift estimated by f3

comments.issue: The basal Eurasian and Villabruna results may reflect insufficient power rather than real absence.
comments.request: Acknowledge power limits and consider outgroup attraction.
comments.quote: the standard errors are high due to low coverage, so this might also just be an issue of insufficient power to detect this ancestry in BuranKaya3A

comments.issue: Shotgun sequencing data are not fully exploited to maximize resolution.
comments.request: Reanalyse with shotgun-sequenced samples and a 1000 Genomes reference SNP set, pooling Sunghir individuals.
comments.quote: I suggest the authors re-analyze their data in the context of the other shotgun-sequenced samples (e.g. Kostenki 14, Ust’Ishim, Sunghir, Loschbour) using an extended reference SNP set (e.g. those from the 1000 Genomes project) to maximize power.

comments.issue: Table S2 reports reads mapped but not average genomic coverage.
comments.request: Add average genomic coverage to Table S2.
comments.quote: it would be good to also report average genomic coverage in addition to the total number of reads mapped

comments.issue: Z-scores clutter the outgroup f3 plots.
comments.request: Remove Z-scores from the outgroup f3 plots.
comments.quote: Z-scores for the outgroup f3 plots are not really necessary and can be removed from the plot, makes them easier readable

title: Genome sequences of 36,000- to 37,000-year-old modern humans at Buran-Kaya III in Crimea

study.system: African striped mouse (Rhabdomys pumilio) and lab mice; developmental genetics, RNA-seq, modelling

editor_summary: Rejects: the novel conclusions are too weak, there is no ecological or evolutionary analysis of Sfrp2 conservation or regulatory elements, and the study better fits a development, skin or pigmentation journal.

reviews.assessment: Significant model system, but recommends rejection: the candidate-gene focus, mismatch between Sfrp2 knockout and predicted phenotype, and inadequate data reporting undermine the conclusions.
strengths: compelling interest for developmental and pigmentation biology

comments.issue: The supplementary gene expression table reports identical baseMean values across samples, indicating a data reporting error.
comments.request: Check and correct the baseMean values reported in the supplementary table.
comments.quote: The gene expression data provided in the supplementary table show the same “baseMean” regardless of the samples considered

comments.issue: The RNA-seq and Figure 2 analyses are not unbiased but focused from the start on the single candidate gene.
comments.request: Present an unbiased analysis rather than focusing on Sfrp2.
comments.quote: What should be unbiased data analysis in experiments related to Figure 2 directly focuses on the effect of that single gene.

comments.issue: The reviewer recommends against publication here, seeing the work as suited to development or pigmentation rather than ecology and evolution.
comments.quote: I would recommend against publication in its current for the following reasons

comments.issue: Sfrp2 knockout does not prevent stripes as theorized in Figure 3, so the model must be adapted.
comments.request: Adapt the model to match the knockout observations.
comments.quote: Ablation of Sfrp2 subsequently does not show the phenotypic outcome theorized in Figure 3 when depleted in vivo: the stripe pattern is not prevented.

comments.issue: Embryonic placode features are not examined in Sfrp2 knockouts even though they are central to the first part of the study.
comments.request: Depict related embryonic features in Sfrp2 knockout embryos.
comments.quote: The authors focus their attention on the developing hair placodes in the first part of the study but fail to depict any related embryonic features upon Sfrp2 KO

comments.issue: Differential hair length between dark and light stripes is never examined in Sfrp2 knockouts.
comments.request: Assess whether the stripe hair-length difference persists in Sfrp2 knockouts.
comments.quote: No mention of this feature is looked at upon Sfrp2 KO.

comments.issue: The nomenclature change in Figure 4 breaks the link to the embryonic stripes R1-R4 shown in Figure 1.
comments.request: Keep a consistent stripe nomenclature across figures.
comments.quote: The link between the embryonic features depicted in Figure 1 between embryonic stripes R1, R2, R3 and R4 is lost when the authors change their nomenclature in Figure 4

comments.issue: Stripes occur on Rhabdomys trunk skin but not the head and neck, and these intrinsic differences are not investigated.
comments.request: Investigate and address the absence of stripes from the head and neck.
comments.quote: The stripes of the Rhabdomys pumilio are located on the trunk skin, but not in the head and neck region.

comments.issue: Ubiquitous unregulated Sfrp2 overexpression in lab mice does not match the claimed fibroblast-specific gradient expression.
comments.request: Use regulated, fibroblast-specific expression that reproduces the endogenous gradient.
comments.quote: The authors use an unregulated ubiquitous overexpression of Sfrp2 in laboratory mice, in an attempt to phenocopy their striped animal model

comments.issue: Wnt suppression of hair follicle placode formation is already known, so this aspect adds little novelty.
comments.quote: Wnt signalling suppression is already known to repress hair follicle placode formation.

comments.issue: Differentially expressed genes are defined only by p-value, with no FDR or fold-change cutoffs reported.
comments.request: Report the FDR and fold-change cutoffs used to define differentially expressed genes.
comments.quote: No FDR or FC cutoff information is provided to define differentially expressed genes

comments.issue: No detailed depiction of the data is provided, not even in the supplement.
comments.request: Provide detailed depictions of the data as supplementary material.
comments.quote: No detailed depiction of the data is provided, even as supplementary material.

comments.issue: Representative histology of the dissected R stripes is missing from the supplement.
comments.request: Add representative histology of the various dissected R stripes as supplementary data.
comments.quote: Representative histology of the various dissected R stripes would be useful in supplementary data.

comments.issue: Anatomically distinct embryo parts were pooled for sequencing, losing cell-type and location information.
comments.request: Avoid pooling distinct regions and distinguish cell types by anatomical location.
comments.quote: Anatomically distinct parts of the embryo were down sampled and pooled during for sequencing.

comments.issue: The tSNE plot colour palette does not match its legend, making the annotation unreadable.
comments.request: Make the tSNE colour palette match the legend.
comments.quote: The color palettes of the tSNE plot and its legend don’t match and make the annotation irrelevant.

comments.issue: If only fibroblasts matter, the fibroblast population was not analysed on its own.
comments.request: Perform unsupervised subclustering and analysis of the fibroblast population.
comments.quote: unsupervised subclustering and analysis of the fibroblast population should be performed.

comments.issue: Sample allocation information is missing from the supplementary material.
comments.request: Give the sample allocation information in the supplement.
comments.quote: Sample allocation information should be given in supplementary.

comments.issue: No scale bars are provided for the macroscopic pictures.
comments.request: Add scale bars to all macroscopic pictures.
comments.quote: no scale bar is provided for all the macroscopic pictures

comments.issue: The microscopy magnification cannot resolve cellular gene expression.
comments.request: Use a magnification that shows cellular resolution.
comments.quote: magnification is inappropriate to depict cellular resolution of gene expression.

comments.issue: The gene legend does not match the Ctnnb1 expression images.
comments.request: Correct the legend so it matches the Ctnnb1 images.
comments.quote: Microscopy: magnification is inappropriate to depict cellular resolution of gene expression. Gene legend doesn’t match Ctnnb1 expression images.

reviews.assessment: A landmark application of molecular tools to evo-devo, but the early Sfrp2 gradient role, the timing of pattern determination and the modelling need better evidence.
strengths: landmark application of molecular and genetic tools to evo-devo
clear finding that follicle formation varies with stripe pattern
broad interest across fields and to the public

comments.issue: Evidence that the early Sfrp2 gradient defines stripes is lacking in the knockouts.
comments.request: Test knockout embryos for broader placode formation or equalised hair-fibre lengths, e.g. by whole-mount in situ hybridisation.
comments.quote: the evidence for this early effect in the Sfrp2 knockout mice is lacking

comments.issue: Overall pigmentation lightening from dermal papilla Sfrp2 could by itself reduce the apparent width of dark stripes.
comments.request: Distinguish whole-skin lightening from an effect on apparent stripe width.
comments.quote: couldn’t this effect of Sfrp2 expression in the dermal papilla alone reduce the apparent width of the dark stripes?

comments.issue: It is not stated whether P4 Sfrp2 expression is restricted to the dermal papilla.
comments.request: State the expression domain and show lower-magnification in situ images.
comments.quote: is Sfrp2 expression in P4 skin entirely restricted to the dermal papilla or not?

comments.issue: The modelling is under-described and the reason the modulator gradient is required in Figure 3c is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the model and whether the gradient is only the symmetry-breaking source.
comments.quote: The modelling is a little unclear, I see only “Model preliminaries” in the methods

comments.issue: Dissections may not have followed the R1-R4 boundaries, so the RNA-seq may sample only a dorsal-ventral gradient.
comments.request: Verify or re-describe region boundaries and explain the missing placode-gene differences.
comments.quote: it appears more likely that the dissections did not follow the boundaries of these regions R1-R4 accurately

comments.issue: Regional differences from the single-cell data and the existence of periodic stripe-respecting expression are not stated.
comments.request: Report per-region single-cell expression differences and state whether periodic expression exists.
comments.quote: They should also specify any differences in gene expression by region (R1, R2 and R3) from the single cell sequencing

comments.issue: The lack of periodic expression may reflect analysis at too late a developmental stage.
comments.request: Examine Dkk4 whole-mount expression earlier, e.g. at E12.5 and E14.5.
comments.quote: Is the pattern determined prior to the appearance of hair follicle placodes at E16.5

comments.issue: The distinct, non-conserved mouse versus cat colour-patterning conclusion is underplayed.
comments.request: Emphasize the non-conserved patterning-system conclusion.
comments.quote: I think much more could be made of this point of major interest.

comments.issue: The assumption of a Turing system rather than positional information from overlapping gradients is not justified.
comments.request: Explain why a Turing system is assumed over positional information.
comments.quote: Why assume that a Turing system operates to produce the striped pattern at all, rather than a positional information based on overlapping gradients?

comments.issue: Whether timing differences between stripes produce different hair types and pigmentation is untested.
comments.request: Pluck hairs and compare types and pigmentation across stripes.
comments.quote: This is readily determined by plucking hairs and examining them individually.

comments.issue: The Figure 2k line of best fit does not match the data, which suggest a rise-then-fall trend.
comments.request: Refit or discuss the non-monotonic Sfrp2 expression pattern.
comments.quote: the line of best fit used does not match the data points (E13.5 specifically)

comments.issue: The Sfrp2 gradient is not demonstrated convincingly in Figure 2.
comments.request: Improve the gradient demonstration using antibody or whole-mount in situ hybridisation.
comments.quote: A better demonstration of the Sfrp2 gradient would improve figure 2

comments.issue: The Sfrp2-expressing fibroblast subset is poorly described.
comments.request: Characterize the subset and discuss the deeper-dermis expression and transgene mismatch.
comments.quote: More information on the subset of fibroblasts is Sfrp2 expressed in should be added.

comments.issue: The Figure 4c mutant image is angled, making stripe alignment difficult.
comments.request: Correct the angled Figure 4c image.
comments.quote: it is hard to line up the stripes as the image seems to be angled for the Sfrp2 mutant

comments.issue: The significance of GFP detection in Figure 2l and the transgene are not described in the legend.
comments.request: Mention GFP detection and briefly describe the transgene in the legend.
comments.quote: The significance of GFP detection in figure 2l should be mentioned in the legend

comments.issue: No reference is given for the single-cell cluster annotations in ED Table 1.
comments.request: Provide a reference for the diagnostic genes of the clusters.
comments.quote: A reference for the single cell RNA cell clusters and corresponding diagnostic genes in ED Table 1 should be provided.

comments.issue: Mpz and L1cam are used as lymphatic markers although both are also Schwann-cell markers.
comments.request: Clarify the lymphatic marker assignments and whether MPZ occurs in lymphatics.
comments.quote: Why are Mpz and L1cam the only lymphatic markers but are both also Schwann cell markers?

comments.issue: 'WNT inhibitors' mislabels the functional class because not all these molecules are inhibitors.
comments.request: Use 'WNT modulators' instead of 'WNT inhibitors'.
comments.quote: “WNT inhibitors” is used to refer to a functional class of molecules, not all of which are inhibitors.

comments.issue: Tyrosinase is called rate-limiting although 'essential' is the more accurate description.
comments.request: Change the description to 'essential'.
comments.quote: Tyrosinase is described as being “rate limiting” for melanin production but it is more relevant to say it

title: A multifunctional Wnt regulator underlies the evolution of rodent stripe patterns

study.system: planarian flatworms; head regeneration, RNAi and phylogenetics

reviews.assessment: Landmark comparative resource with convincing regeneration findings, but the Wnt-reproduction trade-off model lacks functional support and has interpretation problems.
strengths: convincing evidence for repeated loss/gain of head regeneration

comments.issue: The Wnt-from-reproductive-system model is contradicted by sexual Smeds regenerating normally with high ophis-dependent β-catenin.
comments.request: Provide functional support, e.g. via ophis inhibition assays.
comments.quote: the burden of proof rests on the authors to show functional support for the idea that Wnt levels from the sexual reproduction system participate can interfere with head regeneration in any flatworm species.

comments.issue: Whole-animal β-catenin levels may largely reflect reproductive tissue and not the signalling relevant to head-tail fating.
comments.request: Clarify what fraction of β-catenin is relevant to regeneration.
comments.quote: there is an ambiguity in the interpretation of whole tissue or whole animal beta-catenin levels that affects the tests of the main hypothesis. How much of the beta-catenin measured here is relevant for head/tail regeneration?

comments.issue: The abundant literature on Wnt roles in planarian head/tail regeneration is inadequately cited.
comments.request: Cite and discuss the broader Wnt literature.
comments.quote: I must say that the manuscript really inadequately references the very relevant and abundant scope of literature revealing the roles for Wnt signaling in head and tail regeneration in planarians.

comments.issue: The monoclonal antibodies should be deposited in a hybridoma bank for reproducibility.
comments.request: Deposit both antibodies in a public bank.
comments.quote: The monoclonal antibodies described here, both the antibody newly reported for yolk proteins and the antibody described in 2017 for beta-catenin, should be deposited to a commercial or public hybridoma bank.

comments.issue: EO95 antibody production is not described in the methods.
comments.request: Describe its production rather than citing prior work.
comments.quote: More information about production of the EO95 antibody is needed in the methods, rather than citing prior work with the antibody core facility.

comments.issue: Figure 6f and 6i lack y-axis labels and red line definitions.
comments.request: Add labels and define the red lines.
comments.quote: Figure 6f and 6i need y-axis labels and red lines defined (are these means, medians, etc).

comments.issue: The head-tail β-catenin gradient is claimed from data not shown.
comments.request: Show the data or remove the statement.
comments.quote: the authors refer to data not shown of a head-tail beta-catenin protein gradient present in most of the species investigated here. The authors either need to show the data or remove the statement

comments.issue: Fig 5 likely shows a tail gradient rather than an animal-wide β-catenin gradient.
comments.request: Report which adjacent regions differ significantly.
comments.quote: I’m not sure that the data in Fig 5 really show a gradient of beta-catenin protein throughout the body of the asexual Smed strain.

comments.issue: The RNAi failure in P. tenuis could reflect ineffective dsRNAs rather than a general lack of RNAi.
comments.request: Temper the claim, which rests on negative data.
comments.quote: Is it possible that the particular dsRNAs chosen for these experiments might simply be ineffective, or that the target proteins have a particularly long half-life, or tissues themselves undergo very slow turnover etc

comments.issue: Typo 'iapable' on p.6.
comments.request: Fix the typo.
comments.quote: Typo p6 "iapable"

comments.issue: The p.10 statement is a hypothesis; the bypass-suppression alternative should be considered explicitly.
comments.request: Frame the analysis as a test of both possibilities.
comments.quote: it seems the authors should consider at this point the alternative of bypass suppression and present the subsequent analysis more explicitly as a test of these two possibilities.

comments.issue: Language about support versus refutation is biased; the abstract claims unconfirmed predictions.
comments.request: Revise to state that the hypothesis remains unresolved.
comments.quote: Please modify the language used to describe whether the model has been supported versus refuted. The statement describing the statistical test in beta-catenin levels reflects a bias in study design.

reviews.assessment: Conclusive demonstration that Wnt/β-catenin drives head regeneration loss, with two areas needing clarification about phylogeny and alternative drivers.
strengths: conclusively shows Wnt/β-catenin causes regeneration loss

comments.issue: Ancestral-state analyses are obtuse and it is unclear how regeneration data were used.
comments.request: Clarify how regeneration data enter the reconstruction.
comments.quote: The analyses described in the results are obtuse and fails to build a clear picture about the evolutionary history of regeneration.

comments.issue: Alternative drivers such as predation are not discussed and the reproduction-habitat correlation is stretched.
comments.request: Discuss predation and other selection pressures.
comments.quote: The tradeoff between regeneration and reproduction is one of the possibilities driving regeneration, but there can be others like predation which need to be considered and discussed as part of working models/hypotheses.

comments.issue: Figure 3 phylogenetic trees are hard to read and low resolution.
comments.request: Improve their resolution.
comments.quote: Figure 3: Phylogenetic trees are hard to read, and they are of low resolution.

comments.issue: Whether P. tenuis has duplicate β-catenin genes is not addressed.
comments.request: Check for β-catenin gene duplicates in this species.
comments.quote: P. tenuis was not susceptible to ß-catenin(RNAi) is cool. Are there duplicate genes for ß-catenin in this species?

comments.issue: Whether posterior heads formed in the RNAi experiments is not reported.
comments.request: Report posterior head formation across species.
comments.quote: In these ß-catenin(RNAi) experiments, did the animals form a head at the posterior blastema in the different species tested?

comments.issue: The control C. robusta in Fig 4C appears to have two pharynges.
comments.request: Clarify whether this specimen has two pharynges.
comments.quote: In Fig 4C, does the control C. robusta animal have 2 pharynges?

comments.issue: Fig 4C reports animals with no head rather than animals showing the phenotype.
comments.request: Report the number of animals with the shown phenotype.
comments.quote: In Fig 4C, please indicate number of the animals with the shown phenotype rather than number of animals with no head.

comments.issue: Whether yolk production requires Wnt/β-catenin outside planarians is unknown.
comments.request: Discuss whether this function is conserved across metazoans.
comments.quote: Is WNT/ß-catenin signaling known to be required for yolk production in other animals? Is that a conserved function across metazoans?

comments.issue: Whether Wnt pathway expression in the reproductive system is conserved across planarians is unclear.
comments.request: Examine conservation across multiple species.
comments.quote: Is the expression of WNT pathway members in the reproductive system conserved across multiple planarian species?

reviews.assessment: Interesting, high-quality study of broad interest, with major suggestions on gene content, signalling components and neoblast biology.
strengths: pioneering effort closing a knowledge gap
impressive field collection and lab culture system

comments.issue: Wnt signalling gene content across species is not examined, including ligand losses that may mark transitions.
comments.request: Map Wnt component presence, expansion and loss across species.
comments.quote: Since the authors focused on canonical Wnt signaling and already have high-quality transcriptome data, it would be great to see the distribution of Wnt signaling components across planarian species.

comments.issue: Wnt antagonists such as notum were not examined across the collection.
comments.request: Check antagonist expression at the transcriptome level.
comments.quote: Did the author check the expression of Wnt antagonists? For example, at the transcriptome level, do some flatworms have more Wnt antagonists than others?

comments.issue: Wnt ligand expression in muscle cells and its relation to the reproductive system are not explored.
comments.request: Examine muscle Wnt ligand expression across species.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to see how major Wnt ligand orthologs are expressed in the flatworm collection. And how are these muscle cells correlated to the reproductive system?

comments.issue: Fission and damage-induced regeneration are treated as the same process.
comments.request: Distinguish them and consider three reproduction modes.
comments.quote: I am not sure if fission (spontaneous "pinch off") and regeneration (damage and then wound responses) are the exact cellular and molecular processes. It seems that the authors consider them the same thing.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether synapomorphy was considered in ancestral state reconstruction.
comments.request: Clarify the ancestral state methodology.
comments.quote: When reconstructing the ancestral state, did the authors consider the synapomorphy of flatworms? i.e., which clade shares the derived trait of regeneration? This is not very clear in the current manuscript writing.

comments.issue: Neoblasts are largely ignored in the evolutionary model.
comments.request: Incorporate neoblast distribution and germline dynamics.
comments.quote: A fundamental component largely ignored in this study is the neoblast, the source pluripotent stem cells that provide all differentiating cell types.

comments.issue: Figure 1 regeneration groups are not colour-coded.
comments.request: Colour-code the dots across panels.
comments.quote: It would be easier for readers to understand different regeneration groups if the authors could color-code the dots in panel a and provide color-coded dots in panels b–d.

comments.issue: Figure 5b lacks a tree and group highlights, and its font is too small.
comments.request: Revise Figure 5b as suggested.
comments.quote: It is recommended to add a tree to the clades on the left. It would also be helpful to highlight group A and fissiparous reproduction. Overall, the font size in Figure 5 is too small to read.

comments.issue: Canonical Wnt signalling and its link to β-catenin are not explained for readers.
comments.request: Explain this background in the Introduction.
comments.quote: In the Introduction, please explain canonical Wnt signaling and how it is linked to beta-catenin to help readers without this background.

comments.issue: Eight line-level copy edits (species name abbreviations and acronym spell-outs).
comments.quote: Replace Smed with S. mediterranea to have consistency across all flatworm species.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of whole-body regeneration across planarian flatworms

study.system: bacterial HpnP genes; Proterozoic–Phanerozoic 2-methylhopane rock record

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers are largely positive; asks authors to address reviewer 2's concerns about the marine sedimentary record and prior work (moving some discussion to Supplementary Information) and reviewer 3's phylogenetics comments.

reviews.assessment: Exciting, well-written paper that puts 2-methylhopanes back on centre stage, with robust results and only clarifications and extra discussion requested.

comments.issue: The 2-methylhopane uptick attributed to HpnP-bearing Alphaproteobacteria could instead reflect a shift to more productive, oxic oceans.
comments.request: Consider and discuss this alternative driver of the uptick.
comments.quote: However, I am not seeing a reason why this couldn’t alternatively be linked to a shift to more productive (more P rich) and more oxic oceans.

comments.issue: No information is given on the marine ecology and biomass share of HpnP-containing Alphaproteobacteria.
comments.request: Add information on their abundance in typical marine environments.
comments.quote: what portion of the microbial biomass are HpnP-containing Alphaproteobacteria in typical marine environments?

comments.issue: The debated biomarker record is introduced with very limited discussion in the main text.
comments.request: Expand this section, including evidence for robust typical steranes in the Precambrian.
comments.quote: But it is entering into a fairly debated topic with very limited discussion in the main text

comments.issue: The B12 hypothesis section leaves the reader looking for more information.
comments.request: Expand this section and support it with references.
comments.quote: But I was left looking for more information. I would suggest taking text to ref

comments.issue: 'Symbiosis' is used loosely for algae and B12-producing bacteria although the term has strict definitions.
comments.request: Avoid or carefully define symbiosis for the algal-B12 bacteria relationship.
comments.quote: I am not sure I would use symbiosis when talking about algae and B12 producing bacteria.

comments.issue: The method for the pyrolysis experiments is insufficiently described.
comments.request: Provide more methodological detail on the pyrolysis experiments.
comments.quote: It would be good to see more information about method for the pyrolysis experiments

reviews.assessment: Supports publication but raises two major issues: the marine depositional context of the 2-methylhopane record and inadequate discussion of prior work.
strengths: significant question on the origin of hpnP
case for a predominantly cyanobacterial source before 750 Ma

comments.issue: The absence of 2-methylhopanes in extant marine cyanobacteria implies the record depends on depositional setting, which is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this prominently, including its implications for the marine record.
comments.quote: The problem that 2-methylhopanes are not actually found in extant marine cyanobacteria (Elling et al., 2020; Naafs et al., 2021) needs to be discussed in detail

comments.issue: Rokubacteria are excluded as a marine source for lacking marine representatives, yet hpnP-containing cyanobacteria also lack them.
comments.request: Reconcile this inconsistency in the source attribution.
comments.quote: the authors exclude Rokubacteria as a source of 2-methylhopanes in marine environments because they have no marine representatives but the same is actually true for hpnP-containing Cyanobacteria

comments.issue: Why 2-methylhopane biosynthesis was lost during the emergence of marine cyanobacterial lineages is not addressed.
comments.request: Explain the apparent loss of the pathway during that radiation.
comments.quote: Why was 2-methylhopane biosynthesis lost during that radiation if it was previously a pervasive feature?

comments.issue: The 750-500 Ma shift may be biased by different depositional settings, since coastal sites receive freshwater or tidal input.
comments.request: Assess whether the shift is biased by depositional setting.
comments.quote: I wonder if the shift in 2-methylhopane abundance during that time is biased by different depositional settings for these records?

comments.issue: Prior work is discussed summarily instead of study by study, particularly Ricci et al. (2015).
comments.request: Discuss and refute the arguments of previous studies individually.
comments.quote: Therefore, the arguments and merits of previous studies should be discussed and refuted individually, not summarily as presently done

comments.issue: The implication that most cyanobacterial lineages contain SC and hpnP contradicts earlier findings that hpnP is absent from marine cyanobacteria.
comments.request: Reconcile this contradiction with the published literature.
comments.quote: The authors seem to imply that the majority of cyanobacterial lineages/species/genomes contain SC and hpnP, whereas previous studies have found the opposite to be true

comments.issue: The hpnP phylogeny differs from earlier studies that placed cyanobacterial sequences within Alphaproteobacteria; the impact is not assessed.
comments.request: Discuss how alternative phylogenies would affect the conclusions.
comments.quote: the phylogeny of hpnP derived by the authors differs to some extent from previous studies, some of which placed the cyanobacterial hpnP sequences within alphaproteobacteria

comments.issue: The choice of substitution model and phylogenetic methods is not discussed or compared with previous work.
comments.request: Provide a more robust justification and comparison of the phylogenetic methods.
comments.quote: A more robust discussion on the choice of substitution model/phylogenetic methods and comparison to previous works is warranted here

comments.issue: The occurrence in Actinobacteria at lines 94-96 is described without citing Naafs et al. 2021 and Elling et al. 2022.
comments.request: Add these citations at lines 94-96.
comments.quote: Line 94-96: Occurrence in Actinobacteria described in Naafs et al. 2021 (Fig. 5 and supplement) and Elling et al. (2022, Fig. S2)

comments.issue: The physiological roles of hopanoids at lines 107-110 are not credited to earlier work.
comments.request: Cite Doughty et al. 2009 and Wu et al. 2015.
comments.quote: Line 107-110: The physiological roles of hopanoids have been explored in some detail (e.g., Doughty et al., 2009; Wu et al., 2015).

comments.issue: The argument at lines 204-207 was previously made by Ricci et al. (2015) and earlier by Summons.
comments.request: Credit the earlier work here.
comments.quote: Line 204-207: This argument was previously made by Ricci et al. (2015), based on earlier work by Summons, which should be credited here.

comments.issue: The McArthur basin depositional setting is not discussed as a possible bias given the coastal or freshwater habitat of hpnP cyanobacteria.
comments.request: Discuss the depositional setting and possible biases at line 270.
comments.quote: Line 270-271: Here or elsewhere the depositional setting of the McArthur basin formation should be discussed in the light of possible biases in the 2Me record

comments.issue: The statement at lines 346-350 is speculative.
comments.request: Tone down this statement.
comments.quote: Line 346-350: This statement is speculative and could be toned down.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, welcome integration of phylogenetics and geobiology making an important contribution, but the reconciliation analyses have gaps that should be plugged.
strengths: welcome combination of phylogenetic and geobiological analyses
important contribution to the early bacterial fossil record

comments.issue: Reconciling the gene tree against a species tree containing only HpnP-bearing cyanobacteria underestimates losses and biases the dating.
comments.request: Reconcile against the full cyanobacterial species tree and report loss estimates.
comments.quote: why was the gene tree reconciled against a species tree that only contained Cyanobacteria that have HpnP?

comments.issue: No equivalent reconciliation for Alphaproteobacteria, which would empirically test the deeper origin of the gene in cyanobacteria.
comments.request: Perform the same analysis for Alphaproteobacteria.
comments.quote: On a related note, why not perform the same analysis for Alphaproteobacteria?

comments.issue: Rokubacteria may carry an ancient gene, but no reconciliation tests whether it was present at their root.
comments.request: Perform the same gene tree-species tree analysis for Rokubacteria.
comments.quote: It would be worthwhile performing the same analysis here as for Cyanobacteria (and, in my view, Alphaproteobacteria)

comments.issue: Line-level edits: 'transferred vertically' should be 'inherited vertically', and Eremiobacterota is possibly misspelled.
comments.request: Make these wording and spelling corrections.
comments.quote: "transferred vertically" - avoid, maybe "inherited vertically".

comments.issue: Figure 4 legend does not state that both the topology and the species tree dates come from the cited recent study.
comments.request: Modify the legend to indicate the source of both.
comments.quote: I would modify the Figure 4 legend slightly to indicate that both the topology and the inferred species tree dates are based on the recent study cited.

reviews.assessment: Nice work with valuable phylogenetic and biomarker contributions; the only critique is the interpretation of high Phanerozoic 2-MHI and missing discussion of related work.
strengths: valuable phylogenetic and molecular clock analyses
revised contamination-free 2-MHI dataset is a great contribution

comments.issue: Naafs et al. (2021), a very similar study linking Phanerozoic 2-methylhopanoids to the marine nitrogen cycle, is not mentioned.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Naafs et al. (2021).
comments.quote: Naafs et al., (2021, Geobiology) conducted very similar works, including phylogenetic analyses of HpnP, biological production of 2Me-hopanoids and the geological record of 2-MHI

comments.issue: The interpretation of high Phanerozoic 2-MHI ignores its coincidence with marine anoxic events and the nitrogen cycle role of alphaproteobacteria.
comments.request: Discuss anoxic events and nitrogen cycling as alternative explanations.
comments.quote: the coincidence of extreme high 2-MHI with marine anoxic events and the ecological role of alphaproteobacterial in marine nitrogen cycle can be further discussed

comments.issue: Garby et al. (2022) found cyanobacterial dominance under harsh conditions; environmental stress is not discussed.
comments.request: Add discussion of environmental stress influencing 2-methylhopanoid distribution.
comments.quote: Another recent publication, Garby et al. (2022, EMR), reported the dominant 2Me-hopanoids contribution by cyanobacteria over alphaproteobacteria under harsh/extreme conditions.

comments.issue: Typo at line 39: 'form' should be 'from'.
comments.request: Correct the typo.
comments.quote: Line 39, typo, change ‘form’ to ‘from’

comments.issue: Figure 1 shows only 27 SC-containing and 10 HpnP-containing phyla; the basis for these numbers is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the numbers of phyla shown in Figure 1.
comments.quote: Line 93-94, only 27 phyla containing SC and 10 of HpnP are shown in Figure 1

comments.issue: It is unclear how the statement at lines 104-105 was inferred.
comments.request: Explain how this was inferred.
comments.quote: Line 104-105, it is not clear to me how this is inferred.

comments.issue: No discussion of whether microbes recycle fossil hopanoids.
comments.request: Discuss possible microbial recycling of fossil hopanoids.
comments.quote: Line 131-133, Any studies have reported or discussed fossil hopanoids recycling by microbe?

comments.issue: The estimated percentage of gene loss is not reported at line 181.
comments.request: Provide the estimated percentage of gene loss.
comments.quote: Line 181, please provide the estimated percentage of gene loss.

comments.issue: Two sentences at lines 207-214 do not fit the context of this subsection.
comments.request: Move or remove these sentences.
comments.quote: these two sentences do not fit very well to the context of this subsection

comments.issue: GC-APLI-TOF sensitivity is documented only for polyaromatic hydrocarbons, not for 2-methylhopanes.
comments.request: Support or qualify the GC-APLI-TOF sensitivity claim.
comments.quote: GC-APLI-TOF was only reported to be highly sensitive for polyaromatic hydrocarbons detection, probably because they are preferentially ionized than others.

comments.issue: Text at line 230 says 'and possibly Rokubacteria' without supporting data.
comments.request: Delete 'and possibly Rokubacteria'.
comments.quote: Line 230, delete “and possibly Rokubacteria”, because there is no data to support this.

comments.issue: Figure 4A is not cited in the bracket at line 247.
comments.request: Refer to Fig. 4A in the bracket.
comments.quote: Line 247, please refer to Fig. 4A in the bracket.

comments.issue: The calculation of the Fig. 4 node bars (a, b, c) is described neither in the text nor the caption.
comments.request: Describe how the node bars were estimated in the text and Fig. 4 caption.
comments.quote: The calculation of these node bars (a, b and c) is very important for this work. However, the nodes estimation is neither well described in text nor the caption of Fig. 4.

comments.issue: Triangles in Fig. 4A are red, not brown as stated at line 253.
comments.request: Correct the colour description.
comments.quote: Line 253, those triangles are in red not brown in Fig. 4A.

comments.issue: It is not made clear at line 636 whether nodes a, b and c represent Be, Ni and Me.
comments.request: Clarify what nodes a, b and c represent.
comments.quote: Line 636, do nodes a, b and c represent Be, Ni and Me, respectively?

comments.issue: The last sentence of Supplementary Text 3 is flagged, apparently over its claim about a functional group in the A-ring.
comments.quote: , which do not possess a functional group in the A-ring,

title: Genetics re-establish the utility of 2-methylhopanes as cyanobacterial biomarkers before 750 million years ago

study.system: E. coli; random de novo gene library selected against MazF

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns; editor cannot accept, invites a revision addressing the serious concerns.

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the manuscript and has no major concerns, but suggests softening claims about randomness and growth defects.
strengths: very much enjoyed reading the manuscript

comments.issue: 'Random' is used for natural non-genic sequences, which are shaped by selection and mutation bias.
comments.request: Replace 'random' when referring to natural sequences.
comments.quote: the use of the word “random” implies that non-genic sequences have random sequences (even if I am quite sure that is not how you mean it)

comments.issue: Implications of non-random extragenic sequence composition for proto-gene composition and solubility are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether extragenic composition affects proto-genes.
comments.quote: could the sequence composition of extragenic sequences affect the composition or length of possible proto-genes?

comments.issue: Suggests a one-step arabinose-based screen design for future work.
comments.quote: I think you could have reduced the need for the secondary screen (with the Pvan-mazF construct) if the initial screen would have been done with arabinose as sole carbon source

comments.issue: Promoter-specific hits are dismissed despite being meaningful de novo peptide examples.
comments.request: Characterize and discuss the promoter-specific hits more.
comments.quote: I think even the many hits that appear to be specific towards the Para promoter are interesting and worthy of more characterization.

comments.issue: The comparison with other de novo genes misrepresents their conditional fitness effects.
comments.request: Add nuance about condition-dependent deleterious effects.
comments.quote: you highlight the fact that ramF does not cause any substantial growth defect while other de novo genes isolated by others from random libraries do. Isn’t this a bit misrepresenting?

comments.issue: The no-growth-defect claim is not supported by growth rates or competition experiments.
comments.request: Run competition assays or downplay the claim.
comments.quote: I have reservations against the claim that ramF does not cause any substantial growth defect. In figure 3 there is no major effect at 37 degrees but you do not report any growth rates, making it difficult to judge.

reviews.assessment: Acknowledges technically sound, well-described work but finds key conclusions unsupported, the indirect mechanism under-discussed and significance overstated.

comments.issue: RamF's effect on MazF is indirect, and calling it 'function' overstates the activity.
comments.request: Discuss the indirect effect and call it activity rather than function.
comments.quote: this therefore represents an indirect physiological effect and I think this should be a lot more discussed in the manuscript

comments.issue: Chaperone binding specificity is not tested against other random proteins.
comments.request: Repeat the pull-down with 5-10 random hit sequences.
comments.quote: an important experiment (that is missing) would be to perform the pull-down mass spec analysis (presented in Fig. 3C) with 5-10 sequences randomly selected from the ~2,000 pool of initial hits

comments.issue: Protease degradation experiment lacks a control for FLAG-RamF stability.
comments.request: Monitor FLAG-RamF stability across protease mutants.
comments.quote: The experiment is missing a control where the effect of the proteases on RamF (a new protein species that could be subject to degradation) would be verified.

comments.issue: The claim that proteases are more active without Lon lacks a reference.
comments.request: Add a reference supporting this claim.
comments.quote: It is hypothesized that some of the proteases are more active in the absence of Lon (but a reference for such claim is missing).

comments.issue: Fig. S5D lacks the control with all three constructs expressed.
comments.request: Examine cells expressing mazF, pinA and ramF in Fig. S5D.
comments.quote: A similar control is also missing in the experiments in Fig S5 – in panel D, cells expressing all mazF, pinA and ramF should be examined.

comments.issue: The manuscript's description of Knopp et al.'s growth effects conflicts with their published statements.
comments.request: Double-check the facts and cite previous studies correctly.
comments.quote: Unless I overlooked something, this seems to conflict with what Knopp et al. stated in their paper in both cases.

comments.issue: The claim of no substantial growth effect contradicts Fig. 3B, which shows growth-rate effects.
comments.request: Revise the claim of no substantial growth effect.
comments.quote: the statement that the cell growth is not substantially affected in this manuscript is (in the light of the evaluation of Knopp et al. study) also not precise

comments.issue: Figure legends lack detail on gel labels and controls (e.g., EV).
comments.request: Expand the figure legends.
comments.quote: The legends of the figures should include more detail, especially on the labels of the gels and the controls used.

comments.issue: Statistical tests are missing for important data such as Fig. 3B right.
comments.request: Add significance tests to these data.
comments.quote: Some important data are missing statistical tests of significance, e.g. Fig. 3B right.

reviews.assessment: Finds this experimental test of gene evolution very interesting but wants more direct experiments, fuller data description and a re-focused discussion.
strengths: very interesting experimental test of how a gene might evolve

comments.issue: Descriptions of results in Figures 2 and 3 are convoluted at times.
comments.request: Clarify the description of these results.
comments.quote: the descriptions of the results in Figures 2 and 3 at times seem convoluted

comments.issue: RamF's specific effect on chaperones is unexplained, including whether co-purifying chaperones reflect RamF misfolding.
comments.request: Address the specificity questions and the misfolding alternative.
comments.quote: Given that tagged RamF is much less active, what is evidence that the chaperones that co-purify are not just a consequence of a significant fraction of RamF being misfolded?

comments.issue: RamF effects on other known DnaKJ clients are not examined.
comments.request: Test RamF effects on other DnaKJ clients.
comments.quote: the authors should examine RamF effects on other known DnaKJ clients.

comments.issue: The FtsH-degradation claim is not tested in ∆clpP and sfhC∆ftsH backgrounds.
comments.request: Test MazF turnover in ∆clpP and sfhC∆ftsH backgrounds.
comments.quote: The authors should examine the RamF-dependent effects on MazF turnover in ∆clpP and sfhC∆ftsH backgrounds to better support their statement

comments.issue: Effects of growth temperature on MazF levels and the panel F/G experiments are untested.
comments.request: Assess temperature effects on MazF levels and panels F and G.
comments.quote: How are MazF levels affected by growth at different temperatures. How does growth at different temperatures affect the outcome of the experiments shown in panels F and G.

comments.issue: Whether the L16R+L17R mutation affects DnaK co-purification is untested, and the GroEL interaction is unpredicted.
comments.request: Test the mutant's co-purification and discuss the GroEL prediction.
comments.quote: Is RamF co-purification with DnaK affected by the L16R+L17R mutation? How is RamF predicted to interact with GroEL?

comments.issue: The optimized RamF derivatives section reads as an add-on and the derivatives are under-characterized.
comments.request: Characterize the optimized derivatives further and integrate the section.
comments.quote: this section felt like an add-on. Given that a major focus of this study is how new genes evolve and then are optimized, this contribution would be more substantial if the authors further characterized these optimized RamF derivatives.

comments.issue: Only a few significantly changing transcripts are reported, making the selection look cherry-picked.
comments.request: Report more of the significantly changing transcripts.
comments.quote: The authors should label and/or provide information about more of the transcripts whose levels change significantly so that the ones chosen for further study do not seem “cherry picked”.

comments.issue: The mass spec dataset is under-described and Table S2 cannot be found.
comments.request: Describe the mass spec dataset fully and provide Table S2.
comments.quote: the mass spec data set should be more fully described so that the reader can evaluate the specificity of chaperone co-purification (I could not find Table S2)

comments.issue: Why RamF fails to inhibit ChpB and the ECOR27 homolog is not explained.
comments.request: Discuss AlphaFold structural differences as possible explanations.
comments.quote: It was surprising that RamF did not inhibit Mg1655 ChpB or the close homolog from ECOR27.

comments.issue: Concluding ClpX involvement from ∆clpP phenotypes is not warranted since ClpP acts with ClpA or ClpX.
comments.request: Soften the ClpX conclusion.
comments.quote: the authors need to be more cautious about concluding ClpX involvement based on the phenotypes of the ∆clpP deletion

comments.issue: The choice to focus on FtsH despite ClpP also affecting MazF levels is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain why FtsH was the focus.
comments.quote: Given that ClpP and FtsH both affected MazF levels, why did the authors decide to focus on just FtsH.

comments.issue: The discussion ends on unfollowed-up PBAD promoter effects instead of the big picture.
comments.request: Restructure the discussion to end with the big picture.
comments.quote: The authors may want to consider restructuring their discussion to end with the big picture rather than effects on the PBAD promoter which were not followed up in the study.

comments.issue: Loading controls in Fig. 2G and 4B are overexposed and the Coomassie control is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the loading controls and reduce overexposure.
comments.quote: Some loading controls are overexposed. It is not clear why the authors used a Coomassie stained gel as the loading control (was this after transfer?).

comments.issue: Differences between plates in Fig. S5B are not obvious.
comments.request: Quantify expression with a b-galactosidase assay.
comments.quote: The differences between the plates are not obvious. The authors could easily carryout a b-galactosidase assay to quantitate the expression.

title: Selection of a de novo gene that can promote survival of Escherichia coli by modulating protein homeostasis pathways

study.system: gut bacterium Bacteroides fragilis; mouse experiments and models

editor_summary: Editor finds the work of considerable potential interest but says substantial concerns must be addressed; a revised version addressing these serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Interesting study; asks for adult age details, more precise clone reporting, and experimental biofilm validation of the model.

comments.issue: Adult ages are not reported and it is unknown whether GA3-negative prevalence varies across the adult age span.
comments.request: Report adult ages and test whether GA3 loss varies with age.
comments.quote: for adults this information should also be clearly indicated

comments.issue: Mouse experiments used only adult mice, so effects in younger mice are unknown.
comments.request: Speculate on outcomes if younger mice were used.
comments.quote: The authors should at least speculate on what would happen if the experiments were performed in younger mice

comments.issue: The claim that findings mirrored the resistant-strain study ignores exceptions such as the 80% producer strain.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence to acknowledge the exceptions.
comments.quote: should be rephrased given that there are exceptions (e.g. in Fig. S5, a producer strain reaches 80%)

comments.issue: It is unclear which mice the analysed producer clones came from and whether the 80% strain was sequenced.
comments.request: Number the mice and state the origin of each analysed clone.
comments.quote: The information on the analysed clones should be more precise.

comments.issue: The in-silico predictions are not validated with an experimental biofilm model.
comments.request: Test the simulations using an in vitro biofilm model.
comments.quote: it would be important to test the in-silico predictions using an experimental biofilm model

comments.issue: Figure 1 panel e is hard to read and the legend uses '©' instead of (e).
comments.request: Increase the font and fix the legend label.
comments.quote: In Fig. 1, panel e is difficult to read, the font should be increased. In the legend, “©” should be (e).

comments.issue: The Fig. S6 legend cites Fig. 2 where Fig. 3 is meant.
comments.request: Correct the figure reference.
comments.quote: In the legend of Fig. S6 “WT clones were isolated from the last fecal pellets of the two six months experiment (Fig.2 and Fig.S5).” Fig. 2 should be Fig. 3.

reviews.assessment: Extremely interesting and worth publishing, but cohort confounding, missing mechanism and absent model validation leave answers lacking.

comments.issue: Age differences in T6SS prevalence may be driven by cohort differences between HMP and DIABIMMUNE rather than age.
comments.request: Tone down the language and test the pattern in other cohorts.
comments.quote: These results are compelling, but could equally be driven not by age but by other differences between the two cohorts.

comments.issue: No mechanism is provided for why the cost of T6SS production would differ between young and old hosts.
comments.request: Link the initial observations to the later experiments and propose a mechanism.
comments.quote: they don’t convincingly show that this is different in young mice, or really provide a mechanism for what could underlie the observed pattern

comments.issue: The model's core conclusion about resource competition is not tested experimentally.
comments.request: Test the in vivo costs in vitro by manipulating resource availability.
comments.quote: Given the core conclusion that the relative importance of resource competition is really key to whether production is costly, it would’ve been great to see this experimentally tested.

comments.issue: Co-culture experiments are better fitness measures but are not in the main text.
comments.request: Move co-culture experiments into the main text and figures.
comments.quote: I would include the co-culture experiments in the main text/figures rather/alongside the growth assays, as these are a better measure of fitness differences

comments.issue: The later increase in producers is underemphasised in the main text.
comments.request: Discuss the increase in producers more in the main text.
comments.quote: It would be nice to bring this up more in the main text

reviews.assessment: Well-written, novel study; major comments concern the closed-system model, clonal redundancy and unclear reporting in supplementary tables.
strengths: first study addressing T6SS producer dynamics

comments.issue: The model and mouse experiments are closed systems; invasion by strains with competing T6SS was neither tested nor modelled.
comments.request: Model such invasions or state the closed-system limitation.
comments.quote: At a minimum, please state that the model, and the in vivo studies, are closed systems where no new organisms are introduced.

comments.issue: Clonal isolates from the same individual were not removed, biasing genomic analyses toward repeatedly sequenced genotypes.
comments.request: Remove clonal redundancy from the genome set.
comments.quote: This creates a bias toward the genotype of strains repeatedly sequenced.

comments.issue: Supplementary Table 2 does not contain the information described in the text about GA3-positive 'false' genomes.
comments.request: Describe what is lacking for each genome, e.g. locus loss or frame shifts.
comments.quote: Supplementary Table 2 does not contain what is stated in the text.

comments.issue: It is unclear which antibiotic-resistant strains were used in mice, and resistance markers could affect fitness.
comments.request: List the strains used per experiment and discuss the marker caveat.
comments.quote: At a minimum, list very clearly exactly what strains (from Supp Table 4) were introduced into mice in each of the experiments, and if there are differences in the antibiotic resistance genes.

comments.issue: Actual cfu and microbiota percentages of the producer and resistant strains are not reported.
comments.request: Report cfu and percentage of microbiota for these strains.
comments.quote: In Fig 3, the relative abundances of the producer and resistant are shown, but what were the actual cfu of these strains? What percentage of the microbiota did they represent?

comments.issue: The abstract should clarify that the study addresses only the GA3 T6SS, not GA1 or GA2.
comments.request: Clarify the T6SS type in the abstract.
comments.quote: On Line 27 of abstract it is important to clarify that this study addresses the GA3 T6SS

comments.issue: Saying T6SS is 'repeatedly lost' is too loose; inactivating mutations may be meant.
comments.request: Use more precise wording about loss versus mutation.
comments.quote: This term seems too loose. Are they actually lost or do you mean inactivating mutations occur? Please be more precise in the wording.

comments.issue: The outdated name Bacteroides vulgatus is used instead of Phocaeicola vulgatus.
comments.request: Use the accepted designation Phocaeicola vulgatus.
comments.quote: It is highly recommended that the new designation of Phocaeicola vulgatus, rather than Bacteroides vulgatus be used in this manuscript.

comments.issue: Line 103 does not specify whether the GA3 T6SS or strains containing it are lost.
comments.request: Clarify the wording at line 103.
comments.quote: Line 103 – is this loss of GA3 T6SS, or strains containing GA3 T6SS?

comments.issue: The short-term nature of in vitro growth assays is not noted relative to long-term colonization.
comments.request: Note this limitation at line 178.
comments.quote: Please include here that the in vitro growth conditions are very short-term analyses in consideration of the long- term colonization of these bacteria in the human gut.

comments.issue: The antibiotic regimen is not listed and only a previous study is cited.
comments.request: List the antibiotic regimen at line 560.
comments.quote: Line 560 – please list the antibiotic regimen here rather than referring only to a previous study.

comments.issue: Nomenclature differs between Supp Tables S3 and 4 (BF9343_RS vs BF9343_XXXX).
comments.request: Use the standard BF9343_XXXX nomenclature consistently.
comments.quote: In Supp Table S3 the BF9343_RS nomenclature is used, whereas in Supp Table 4, the more standard BF9343_XXXX nomenclature is used. Please be consistent.

comments.issue: The wording at lines 352 about 'losing the pathway' should be tightened.
comments.request: Clarify whether pathways are lost or mutations acquired.
comments.quote: again the wording here should be tightened. Do they really “often lose the pathway”? Maybe acquire inactivating mutations?

editor_summary: Reviewer 1's concerns about the limited advance over earlier work (Geltsch et al. 2017; co-authors' prior work) and the strength of the novel conclusions preclude publication.

comments.quote: There is already a prior paper on this topic, that spans a 100 year long period, and shows that host-parasite mimicry co-evolved towards better match over the time

comments.issue: Color plays a critical role in this mimicry system but is not fully considered in the analyses.
comments.request: Consider color traits alongside pattern complexity.
comments.quote: color plays a critical role in your study systems' mimicry but it is not considered in my judgement here fully in this paper

comments.issue: Collection specimens fade over decades, so the trait set may be affected by storage time.
comments.request: Explain how storage-related fading was corrected or shown to be irrelevant.
comments.quote: we know that collection specimens fade a lot over years/decades compared to fresh eggs from the field. How did you correct for that factor

reviews.assessment: Values the joint host-parasite approach and clear data, but finds the rapid-evolution claim unsupported and wants process-focused analyses.
strengths: considers both host and parasite eggshell phenotypes
does not assume host phenotypes are static

comments.issue: Statements that parasites evolve toward hosts and hosts away are untested; equal complexity does not imply matching patterns.
comments.request: Test directly whether hosts evolve away, and justify complexity as a proxy for pattern match.
comments.quote: I didn’t recall seeing a test that showed parasites evolving “toward” hosts or hosts “away” from parasites

comments.issue: Rapid evolution is claimed repeatedly but the complexity changes are modest and fidelity did not change.
comments.request: Remove 'rapid' from the title and emphasize the evolutionary process instead.
comments.quote: You referred to rapid evolution repeatedly (title and lines 26, 28, 69, and 88); however, I saw no evidence of this.

comments.issue: Constant mimetic fidelity is over-emphasized as the conclusion; chase-away processes should take the focus.
comments.request: Shift emphasis from the null fidelity result to the chase-away process.
comments.quote: I think that this model is much more powerful as an “alternative” process, and that more emphasis is needed on the evolutionary processes

comments.issue: The point that eggshell patterns are imperfectly matched is introduced too briefly to register with readers.
comments.request: Explain more clearly that eggshell patterns, unlike colors, cannot be matched.
comments.quote: These concepts are only quickly introduced (lines 44-47), but I suspect that the importance of these lines will be lost on most readers.

comments.issue: Linear year models ignore non-continuous sampling and fluctuating complexity; tracking analyses better match the hypothesis.
comments.request: Analyze how the parasite population tracks the host population over time.
comments.quote: I do struggle to understand why complexity would be linearly related to “year” or how that might relate to your underlying hypothesis.

comments.issue: Alternative explanations such as Red Queen dynamics, rainfall or ENSO are not given attention.
comments.request: Discuss alternative explanations for the parallel fluctuations.
comments.quote: I would appreciate more alternative explanations. For example, red queen dynamics seem like a feasible explanation of the observed patterns.

comments.issue: The dataset comes from two active collection periods, which has statistical implications for long-term claims.
comments.request: Exhibit caution about claims given the two collection periods.
comments.quote: your dataset has two periods of active collection. While this has some statistical implications, I think this suggests you should exhibit some caution on such claims.

comments.issue: Despite spanning five decades, the time series has good sampling in only a few years.
comments.quote: Upon closer inspection, it is clear that you have good sampling in only a few of these years.

comments.issue: Presenting log-scale complexity values as percentages is unclear and potentially misleading.
comments.request: Report effect sizes in original units or as odds ratios.
comments.quote: It isn't clear to me how you are presented complexity (log scale) as a percentage.

comments.issue: Why a linear increase in complexity is expected under the chase-away model is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why chase-away predicts a linear trend rather than fluctuations.
comments.quote: A chase-away model would imply that complexity -changes- not necessarily gets more complex.

comments.issue: Log-scale estimates with confidence intervals are not retained in the presentation of the results.
comments.request: Keep log-scale values with CIs and add odds ratios.
comments.quote: I would prefer for these data to remain in the log scale with the appropriate CI.

comments.issue: Unclear whether the greater variance in hosts reflects chase-away dynamics or is a statistical artefact.
comments.request: Clarify the source of the greater host variance.
comments.quote: Is the greater variance in the host population actually a feature of the chase-away model, or simply a statistical (/practical) artefact?

comments.issue: The numbered points '1' and '2' in the sentence are unnecessary.
comments.request: Remove the '1' and '2'.
comments.quote: It may be my preference, but I do not think that the 1 and 2 are really necessary.

comments.issue: Interpretation at lines 65-67 is premature and alternative explanations at 62-64 are over-condensed.
comments.request: Merge lines 68-75 into line 60 and rework the surrounding text.
comments.quote: you may benefit from merging the content from current lines 68-75 on line 60

comments.quote: a 0.04 difference is not the same thing as a 4% increase.

comments.issue: Curly brackets in the confidence interval presentation are awkward to read.
comments.request: Present intervals in the form 0.38 to 0.55.
comments.quote: For your confidence intervals I like to present these as 0.38 to 0.55.

comments.quote: it isn’t quite clear to me how this relates to your main hypothesis.

study.system: native and non-native animals; global meta-analysis of responses to extreme climate events

reviews.assessment: Commends the multi-pronged meta-analysis but reports serious reproducibility problems: unstable estimates, unreplicated tests and duplicated analyses requiring a streamlined reanalysis.

comments.issue: The mean effect glosses over the many positive effect sizes for both native and non-native species.
comments.request: Summarise the numbers of positive, negative and neutral effect sizes and discuss winners and losers.
comments.quote: there are a large number of positive effect sizes for both native and non-native species. One weakness of meta-analysis is that it can gloss over this important nuance in pursuit of a general (mean) effect.

comments.issue: Results could not be reproduced from the provided data and code; DataS1 may not be the file the results are based on.
comments.request: Ensure the correct data file underlies the results and provide it plus code as an R script.
comments.quote: When I ran the data and code, I was unable to reproduce the exact values for every test I conducted.

comments.issue: Model estimates are unstable across reruns, with mean effects varying by 0.4% to 27%.
comments.request: Assess model reliability more sharply, e.g. with narrower credible intervals.
comments.quote: I fitted the land model (Inter.e31) five times and the mean effect for each comparison varied by 0.4% to 27% between min and max values.

comments.issue: No diagnostics for model fit, such as trace plots, Gelman-Rubin statistics or posterior predictive checks, are reported.
comments.request: Conduct and report model checks to ensure the models fit the data adequately.
comments.quote: The manuscript doesn’t say anything about diagnostic checks for model fit, such as inspecting trace plots to ensure chains have adequately mixed, use of the Gelman-Rubin statistic, and posterior predictive checks.

comments.quote: it is curious that the native vs non-native comparison is not significant for heatwaves on land, but is for cold spells and droughts. Is the notation correct?
