comments.issue: The choice of the Tasmanian devil genome rather than an available northern quoll reference genome is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the reference genome choice.
comments.quote: would this be more or less appropriate to align spotted-tailed quoll reads to than the Tasmanian devil genome, and why?

comments.issue: Sequencing effort is not reported: total reads and percentage demultiplexed are missing.
comments.request: Report total sequenced reads and demultiplexing success.
comments.quote: total number of sequenced reads should be presented (either in Extended Data or here)

comments.issue: The 50% missing data threshold is high; removing worst individuals or showing a missingness histogram is suggested.
comments.request: Reduce missing data or add a missingness histogram.
comments.quote: 50% missing data in one or more individuals is quite high, can the authors remove a small number of individuals with the most missing data to reduce that to say 30%?

comments.issue: It is unclear how the top ten models were selected, e.g. whether they had delta AIC below 2.
comments.request: Clarify the model selection criterion in methods and results.
comments.quote: So were these top 10 models those with delta AIC < 2? Please clarify how these 10 were picked.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether pRDA and GDM tolerate missing data.
comments.request: Confirm the missing data requirements of pRDA and GDM.
comments.quote: Can the authors confirm that these pRDA and GDM analyses do not require no missing data?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether generations diseased refers to quoll or devil generations.
comments.request: State that generations diseased is the collection year of the quoll sample.
comments.quote: it would be clearer to state that generations diseased is the collection year of a given quoll sample. Readers don't know if devil generations are the same as quoll generations.

comments.issue: The phrase generations diseased is confusing; time since DFTD arrival would be clearer.
comments.request: Replace generations diseased with time since DFTD arrival.
comments.quote: change "devil density and generations diseased have independent effects" to "devil density and time since DFTD arrival have independent effects"

comments.issue: The number of latent factors used in the LFMM analysis is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the number of latent factors.
comments.quote: Can the authors specify the number of latent factors (presumably 3) used here?

comments.issue: The LFMM testing function and false discovery rate control are unclear; q values need explanation.
comments.request: Explain the LFMM test and FDR correction used.
comments.quote: Wouldn't the authors have used the 'lfmm2.test' function here, which produces p-values? And was there a false discovery rate used for this lfmm?

comments.issue: The pRDA acronym should be written out in the figure title.
comments.request: Write out the full pRDA title.
comments.quote: Better to write out the full pRDA title than use the acronym.

comments.issue: The figure label generations diseased needs explanation.
comments.request: Explain generations diseased in the figure.
comments.quote: Also worth explaining what 'generations diseased' means, i.e. time since arrival of disease in Tasmanian devils.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the 189 individuals in the figure are quolls or devils.
comments.request: Label the panel spotted-tailed quoll individuals.
comments.quote: better to say "spotted-tailed quoll individuals", as I was initially unsure whether the 189 individuals were quolls or devils

comments.issue: The table caption lacks detail, including which species is analysed, and threshold meanings are unclear.
comments.request: Expand the table caption and clarify thresholds.
comments.quote: Table caption needs more detail, e.g. which species is being analysed.

comments.issue: Extended Data Figure S3 has low resolution and surfaces extending into the ocean.
comments.request: Improve resolution and clip surfaces to the Tasmania outline.
comments.quote: Can the authors improve resolution and clip the predicted surfaces to the outline of Tasmania?

comments.issue: Metadata, bioinformatics scripts and R code are not publicly archived.
comments.request: Publish metadata, scripts and code on Dryad or Zenodo.
comments.quote: I recommend that the authors publish all relevant metadata and bioinformatics scripts and R code on Dryad/Zenodo or something similar.

reviews.assessment: Sound and interesting study that should be published, though the trophic cascade terminology needs clarification.
strengths: sound scientific study with interesting results
landscape community approach demonstrates the potential of landscape genomics

comments.issue: The resubmission contains only minor changes with no proper response letter, making it hard to verify that previous comments were addressed.
comments.request: Provide a proper point-by-point response letter.
comments.quote: Without any proper response letter to reviewers it is difficult to address which changes have been done and how and if all comments have been addressed sufficiently

comments.issue: The trophic cascade terminology is used incorrectly: this is a change in an existing cascade rather than the creation of one.
comments.request: Clarify or correct the trophic cascade terminology throughout.
comments.quote: I think this needs some clarification at this place and elsewhere as the terminology is not clearly used

comments.issue: It is unclear what explains the three genetic clusters in quolls, and more context is needed for general readers.
comments.request: Explain the factors behind the three quoll genetic clusters.
comments.quote: I am lacking a bit of information why you find three different genetic clusters in the quolls

comments.issue: The lower dispersal pressure explanation implies the pattern is not landscape resistance; quoll density data are needed.
comments.request: Support the resistance interpretation with quoll density data.
comments.quote: Are you saying that because there are less devils there is lower pressure to disperse, so more quolls could be in that given area?

comments.issue: The statement at line 210 is too general and the contribution to conserving both species is unclear.
comments.request: Temper the statement and explain the conservation contribution.
comments.quote: And how do you see that your results contribute to the conservation of both species in Tasmania?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether figure panels A and B represent the whole quoll range, since southwestern Tasmania appears unoccupied.
comments.request: Clarify the spatial coverage of the figure panels.
comments.quote: Are Figure panels A and B representing the whole range of the quolls?

comments.issue: The variables used at line 589 and the reasons for selecting them are not stated.
comments.request: List the variables and justify their selection.
comments.quote: 589 which are the variables and why did you select those?

reviews.assessment: Novel and clearly written study; results need to be interpretable to non-geneticists and the trophic cascade terminology corrected.
strengths: novel link between dominant competitor loss and mesopredator genetic structure
appreciates the framing around specific hypotheses

comments.issue: Main results are hard to interpret for readers without genetics training, which is needed for a broad ecology journal.
comments.request: Make the main results, including Figure 2, more accessible to non-geneticists.
comments.quote: the main results (including figure 2) need to be more easily interpretable by readers without training in genetics

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the effect sizes are biologically significant compared with impacts of human hunting or habitat loss.
comments.request: Help readers interpret the biological significance of the effect sizes.
comments.quote: There should also be more help interpreting if the effect sizes shown are biologically significant

comments.issue: Calling devils top predators is inaccurate since they are small scavengers; dominant competitor is more accurate.
comments.request: Call devils a dominant competitor throughout.
comments.quote: They should more accurately call devils a dominant competitor throughout the manuscript

comments.issue: The described interaction is mesopredator release, not a trophic cascade, which requires three trophic levels.
comments.request: Remove the trophic cascade term throughout.
comments.quote: What the authors describe in this paper is the definition of mesopredator release, not a trophic cascade

comments.issue: Species diets and weights are not given, so the ecological rationale for the interactions is missing.
comments.request: Add species diets and weights.
comments.quote: Add species diets and weights somewhere to provide biological/ecological rationale for their interactions.

comments.issue: The last sentence of the introduction is a result and does not flow as a single sentence.
comments.request: Restructure the closing of the introduction.
comments.quote: Last sentence is results. This is normally a short paragraph in Nature Comms but this single sentence

comments.issue: The results would benefit from plain-language explanation of what the genetic changes mean.
comments.request: Add lay explanations of the genetic changes.
comments.quote: would benefit from more laymen's explanation/interpretation of what the genetics changes mean

comments.issue: Figure 1C smooth curves are idealized trends, so calling them results is misleading.
comments.request: Relabel or reframe Figure 1C.
comments.quote: These smooth PowerPoint curves are more like hypothesized relationships (or idealized trends). Calling them "results" could be misleading.

comments.issue: Figure 2C does not state that lower AICc is better, and the best model is not marked.
comments.request: State that lower AICc is better or mark the best model.
comments.quote: need to add that lower AICc is better somewhere. OR maybe put a star over the best model?

title: Disease-driven top predator decline affects mesopredator population genomic structure

study.system: western US forests and shrublands; satellite ET, fire severity, drought

editor_summary: Both reviewers see improvement but raise remaining points, including fire-ecology terminology and ET methods detail; authors must respond and highlight changes.

reviews.assessment: Supports publication and praises the improved caveats, but requests critical fixes to terminology, figures, citations and a few interpretations.
strengths: valuable contribution on combined drought and fire effects on ET recovery
good response to initial comments, including multiple landcover datasets
improved caveats and limitations without drawing assumptions
value to fire ecology, ecohydrology and remote sensing communities

comments.issue: Units are reported in imperial system; acres should be hectares or square kilometres.
comments.request: Convert imperial units to metric throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: Some units are currently reported in imperial system and should be converted into metric.

comments.issue: Figure 2 axis titles, legend and legend text are too small.
comments.request: Enlarge the axis and legend text in Figure 2.
comments.quote: Figure 2: needs larger axis title text, larger legend and legend text.

comments.issue: The caption does not explain why -0.5 SPEI, marked by the dashed red line, matters.
comments.request: Explain the significance of the -0.5 SPEI threshold in the caption.
comments.quote: Add short reminder in caption of why the number -0.5 SPEI (labelled with the dashed red line) is a significant number to be highlighted.

comments.issue: Figure 2 bar plots show no variability; error bars or boxplots with individual fires are needed.
comments.request: Add error bars or replace bar plots with boxplots showing per-fire variability.
comments.quote: Bar plots on all panels should include error bars, or even better, be replaced with a statistical representation that better depicts the variability between all the fires considered

comments.issue: Figure 3b regression lines lack confidence intervals.
comments.request: Plot confidence intervals around the regression lines in panel (b).
comments.quote: Figure 3: needs confidence intervals plotted bracketing the regression lines in panel (b).

comments.issue: The 'SG' legend code for non-forest is unclear.
comments.request: Relabel non-forest in the legends, using 'non-forest' instead of 'SG'.
comments.quote: Suggest using a different code on legends for non-forest (such as “non-forest” instead of “SG”.

comments.issue: Grassland, shrubland, rangeland and non-forest are used interchangeably and confusingly.
comments.request: Use grassland and shrubland in methods and 'non-forest' elsewhere; avoid 'rangeland'.
comments.quote: the authors need to be more consistent with the terms for non-forest pixels – grassland, shrubland, rangeland, and non-forest are often used interchangeably throughout the manuscript

comments.issue: The term 'fire regime' is misused, e.g. 'post-fire regime' does not exist.
comments.request: Check every use of 'fire regime' against its fire-ecology definition.
comments.quote: The authors still mis-use the word “fire regime” in many instances.

comments.issue: 'Suppression' is used for ET reduction although it has a specific fire-ecology meaning.
comments.request: Use a different word than 'suppression' for reductions in ET.
comments.quote: Suggest using a different word other than “suppression”, as this word has a very specific and different meaning in fire ecology

comments.issue: Overall treatment of fire-ecology terms and concepts is not sufficiently informed.
comments.request: Revise fire-ecology terminology and concepts throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: In general, in the revision I would like to see the authors use a more informed treatment of the fire ecology terms and concepts that they explore in the paper.

comments.issue: No justification for using LANDFIRE as the base vegetation classification for comparison.
comments.request: Explain why LANDFIRE was chosen as the base classification.
comments.quote: An explanation is needed as to why LANDFIRE was chosen as the base existing vegetation classification

comments.issue: Unclear whether the '2020 burns not unprecedented' statement downplays the high-severity ET results.
comments.request: Review this paragraph for a correct, clear interpretation.
comments.quote: It’s unclear to me if this statement is included to downplay the ET results related to the high severity 2020 fires in the PNW?

comments.issue: Statement is unclear and seems implausible for high-severity fires with overstory mortality.
comments.request: Clarify whether the statement applies only to low-severity fires.
comments.quote: This statement is unclear. Is this specifically for low severity fires?

comments.issue: The final clause implies climate change despite the study not incorporating it.
comments.request: Remove the final clause of this sentence.
comments.quote: This study does not incorporate climate change and as such I suggest removing the final clause of this sentence.

comments.issue: No citation or rationale for the specific thresholds used.
comments.request: Provide citations and/or a rationale for these thresholds.
comments.quote: Provide citation for the use of these specific thresholds and/or provide a rationale for their selection.

comments.issue: Numerous grammatical errors throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: There are several grammatical errors throughout the paper and it needs to be carefully proofread

reviews.assessment: Finds the author responses mostly sufficient, but several statements about ET models are misleading or incomplete and need elaboration.
strengths: responses to earlier reviewer questions mostly sufficient
adequate descriptions and sources to back up claims
clear explanation that OpenET ET and SPEI should not be compared

comments.issue: Validation details are missing: flux closure and flux-footprint pixel selection are not described.
comments.request: Describe eddy covariance validation in more detail and cite examples.
comments.quote: it would have been nice to see the authors spend a little more time describing the specifics of the eddy covariance approach since it can vary in how researchers apply it

comments.issue: Sentence implying DisALEXI prefers transpiration over evaporation is misleading; allocation follows LAI.
comments.request: Correct the misleading statement about DisALEXI's T/E allocation.
comments.quote: DisALEXI does not give preference to T or E, it is simply based on the LAI signal.

comments.issue: Saying LST directly constrains sensible heat and net radiation oversimplifies the energy-balance model.
comments.request: Elaborate and correct the description of how the model partitions LST.
comments.quote: their statement is misleading as there is no direct partitioning of solar radiation

comments.issue: How the different ET products were harmonized temporally is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how Landsat ET estimates are aggregated to monthly values.
comments.quote: Are values interpolated to daily then summed to the monthly timescale?

comments.issue: Deep rooting cannot explain post-fire ET when there are no leaves; rapid undergrowth is an alternative.
comments.request: Address this alternative explanation for elevated post-fire ET.
comments.quote: the deep rooting depth won’t necessarily allow the forested ecosystem to meet ET demands

comments.issue: DisALEXI daily interpolation is misdescribed; iterative adjustment to ALEXI is not daily interpolation.
comments.request: Correct the description of how daily ET estimates are produced.
comments.quote: the iterative adjustment of air temperature to match ALEXI pixel scale ET is not a means to interpolate to a daily estimate

comments.issue: How ET products are aggregated to monthly values is not specified.
comments.request: Specify how ET products are aggregated to monthly values.
comments.quote: I think authors need to specify just how they aggregate ET products to monthly values.

title: Droughts impede water balance recovery from fires in the Western United States

study.system: prokaryotic pangenomes; comparative genomics of gene gain and loss

editor_summary: Reviewers raised concerns and requested clarifications regarding methods and terminology; editor asks to reformat as an Article with subheadings and a 200-word abstract.

reviews.assessment: Substantial contribution and mostly well written; asks for terminology precision, interpretation fixes, and a clearer methods section.

comments.issue: Selection is discussed ambiguously, conflating selection on gene content with selection on amino acids.
comments.request: Explicitly distinguish selection on gene content versus within-gene selection.
comments.quote: I feel that the authors should go through the text and explicitly talk about selection on gene content, or selection on the retention or loss of genes.

comments.issue: Claim that rare genes have high turnover is logically contradictory.
comments.request: Revise this statement about rarity and turnover.
comments.quote: If a gene is rare, then by definition it does not have a high turnover rate.

comments.issue: Inferring dubious adaptive value from low gene frequency is a logical error.
comments.request: Remove or justify the "dubious adaptive value" inference.
comments.quote: I cannot figure out why the authors are inferring that a gene with a low frequency has a dubious adaptive value.

comments.issue: Lines 48-49 leave unclear whether selection acts on gene retention or on amino acids.
comments.request: Clarify which type of positive selection is meant.
comments.quote: It's really not clear that we are talking about positive selection on the retention of the gene or a positive selection on the amino acids within the gene.

comments.issue: Percentage of intact singleton genes is ambiguous; the denominator appears to be all genes, not singletons.
comments.request: State explicitly what this percentage represents.
comments.quote: I think it would be really important to clarify what you mean by percentage of intact Singleton genes at this point.

comments.issue: The provenance of line 51 numbers from downsampled pangenomes is not signposted.
comments.request: Point readers to the methods at line 51.
comments.quote: At this point online 51 you should really point the reader to the method section so that they can understand that these numbers come from downsampled Pangenomes.

comments.issue: Copy edits: "Chlamydia" misspelled in several places; line 319 likely contains a typo.
comments.quote: Chlamydia is spelt incorrectly in a few places.

comments.issue: No explanation why singletons and doubletons are analysed but not tripletons or other cut-offs.
comments.request: Explain the choice of frequency cut-offs.
comments.quote: Could the authors include some explanation for high most of the paper deals with singletons but part of the paper deals with doubletons

comments.issue: Fluidity measure is absent for singletons; the extent of this deficiency is unclear.
comments.request: Comment on the consequences of this missing measure.
comments.quote: On page 4 lines 89, 90 and 91 there is in noticeable absence of any fluidity measure for singletons.

comments.issue: Framing neutrality as something to prove rather than to test is wrong.
comments.request: Reframe neutrality as a hypothesis to be tested.
comments.quote: I don't think it's the right way to think that you should be trying to prove neutrality. Surely neutrality should be a hypothesis to be tested rather than approved?

comments.issue: "Evolving neutrally" will be confused with dN:dS-based neutral evolution of protein-coding genes.
comments.request: Refer instead to pseudogene presence-absence changes and drift.
comments.quote: I suggest changing it so that we are talking about pseudogene presence-absence changes being neutral or entirely driven by random drift.

comments.issue: dS is only a partial measure of neutral variation; selection on silent sites is ignored.
comments.request: Add a caveat about synonymous codon usage.
comments.quote: This is really only partially true, particularly in highly expressed genes, where there is substantial selection on silent sites to conform to the optimal codon usage of the genome.

comments.issue: The sentence spanning lines 202-204 is incomprehensible.
comments.request: Rewrite this sentence.
comments.quote: I have read the sentence that spans lines 202 203 204, and I'm afraid I really could not understand what it means. Could the authors please rewrite this sentence?

comments.issue: Claim of strong evidence against a fully neutral model is not supported by any analysis.
comments.request: Rewrite to reflect the actual evidence presented.
comments.quote: There is no part of this paper as far as I can read that even supports a partial neutral model of prokaryote pangenome diversity.

comments.issue: No evidence that rare genes are only "slightly adaptive"; they may be essential.
comments.request: Revise this claim about slightly adaptive functions.
comments.quote: I don't believe that there is evidence that the presence of these rare genes only confers a slightly adaptive function.

comments.issue: Line 324 "under selection" should specify selection for retention in the genome.
comments.request: Change to "selection to be retained in the genome".
comments.quote: Online 324 you say the rear accessory genes are under selection. I suggest you change this to indicate that they are under selection to be retained in the genome.

comments.issue: Line 350 "pseudogene diversity" should specify presence-absence diversity.
comments.request: Change the wording accordingly.
comments.quote: Online 350 I suggest third pseudogene diversity could be changed so that it explicitly says that it is pseudogene presence or absence diversity.

comments.issue: Methods calculations are ambiguous and hard to reproduce.
comments.request: Rewrite the methods so other researchers can reproduce the results.
comments.quote: I would therefore suggest that they go through their method section making it easier for the reader to reproduce what they have done.

reviews.assessment: Innovative approach with long-term impact, but writing needs a complete overhaul and the nine-genome subsampling undermines rare-gene claims.
strengths: innovative approach with potential long-term impact
clever comparison of intact and pseudogene frequencies

comments.issue: Writing requires complete revision; manuscript reads like documentation or a non-final draft.
comments.request: Revise writing style to make the manuscript accessible to readers.
comments.quote: in my opinion, the manuscript needs a complete revision of writing style and making it more accessible to readers.

comments.issue: Two distinct pseudogene-based methods (si/dp ratio; category prediction) are not clearly distinguished.
comments.request: Clearly separate and explain the two methods.
comments.quote: the manuscript actually presents two methods to make use of pseudogenes as a reference. The si/dp ratio is one method and the prediction of intact vs pseudogene based on categories is a related but different approach.

comments.issue: Abstract duplicates the first paragraph verbatim.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract so it does not repeat the opening paragraph.
comments.quote: The abstract and the first paragraph are identical.

comments.issue: Writing styles switch without sections or paragraphs; sections are hard to find and flow is poor.
comments.request: Add headings and improve structure and flow.
comments.quote: The text switches between different writing styles without any sections or paragraphs. It is thus impossible to find the relevant sections fast when reading the manuscript and in the single text block "main" there is often no flow.

comments.issue: Reading flow breaks from lines 44-45 and 70-79 where topics are reintroduced.
comments.request: Reorganize these passages to maintain the narrative flow.
comments.quote: For example from line 44 to line 45 the reading flow is interrupted.

comments.issue: No clear one-message-per-paragraph structure; section headings are missing.
comments.request: Structure the text with headings and one message per paragraph.
comments.quote: I would prefer one message per paragraph and structured sections.

comments.issue: Information is scattered and topics reappear unexpectedly, e.g. selenocysteine at line 327.
comments.request: Consolidate scattered information into the relevant sections.
comments.quote: Some information is scattered across different parts of the manuscript or a topic that has previously been touched suddenly reappears.

comments.issue: Sentences are cluttered with means and SDs in brackets; a table would display these better.
comments.request: Move these numbers into a table.
comments.quote: There are many sentences with lots of mean numbers and their SD in many brackets.

comments.issue: Numbers at line 184ff would be clearer in a table.
comments.request: Present the line 184ff numbers as a table.
comments.quote: line 184ff using a table might be better

comments.issue: The page 8 clustering paragraph interrupts the functional-category narrative.
comments.request: Move or reorder the clustering paragraph.
comments.quote: page 8: the clustering paragraph interrupts the story about the functional categories that are under stronger selection.

comments.issue: Lines 252-257 read like a technical manual; "across these three partitions" is unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite this passage more clearly.
comments.quote: line 252 - 257 is written in a very technical manual-like style and is hard to follow.

comments.issue: Subsampling to 9 genomes makes intermediate-frequency genes appear as singletons, so results do not reflect rare genes.
comments.request: Use subsamples of size 20 to investigate truly rare genes.
comments.quote: here the repeated subsampling to 9 genomes results in many genes of intermediate frequency showing up as singletons

comments.issue: Subsamples of size 3 would target intermediate-frequency genes; differences between groups remain untested.
comments.request: Compare subsamples of size 3 versus 20.
comments.quote: Similarly subsamples of size 3 would focus more on intermediate-frequency genes. It would be great to see if there are differences between these two groups.

comments.issue: Singleton enrichment of pseudogenes may stem from clustering artifacts rather than selection.
comments.request: Discuss whether clustering issues explain this enrichment.
comments.quote: could you discuss in more detail whether pseudogenes are enriched as singletons due to clustering issues?

comments.issue: The si/sp ratio invariance discussion in lines 82-92 is confusing.
comments.request: Clarify that the ratio is unchanged whether numbers or percentages are used.
comments.quote: the si/sp ratio is the same, regardless of whether the number or percentage is considered. line 82 - 92 is thus confusing.

comments.issue: Missing alternative explanation that pseudogenes are more efficiently purged by selection.
comments.request: Add this alternative to line 122.
comments.quote: line 122f: add "or pseudogenes are more efficiently purged by selection."

comments.issue: Figure 4 lacks COG category labels and descriptions.
comments.request: Add COG category labels and descriptions to Figure 4.
comments.quote: please add the COG category labels/descriptions to Figure 4.

comments.issue: "Many" in line 28 is too vague.
comments.request: Quantify or specify what "many" means.
comments.quote: line 28: "many" could mean anything here

comments.issue: The argument in lines 146-150 is hard to follow; expected ratio behaviour is unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite the argument with clear, multiple sentences.
comments.quote: I do not completely get your point here even after reading this multiple times.

comments.issue: Line 153 frames the hypothesis as two exclusive scenarios, but both effects contribute.
comments.request: Rephrase to acknowledge that both effects contribute.
comments.quote: line 153 "hypothesis" sound like there are only two exclusive scenarios. But both effects will contribute (to a different degree).

comments.issue: Log scale in Figure 2 emphasizes outlier points.
comments.request: Justify or reconsider the log scale.
comments.quote: Figure 2: Why log scale? This emphasizes the outlier points

comments.issue: si/sp of 0.1 implies tenfold more pseudogenes than intact genes; plausibility unclear.
comments.request: Comment on whether such values are plausible.
comments.quote: Figure 2: si/sp of 0.1 means there are 10 times more pseudogenes than intact genes, correct? This seems like a lot. Could you comment on that?

comments.issue: Figure 3 has many degrees of freedom with few species; overfitting and taxonomic-class effects possible.
comments.request: Address overfitting and whether models fit only the largest class.
comments.quote: Figure 3: Why are there so many degrees of freedom? The number of species is only slightly above the number of parameters. That could be a problem for overfitting.

reviews.assessment: Important and compelling contribution; requests extra analyses and caveats about pseudogene neutrality and singleton benefits.
strengths: compelling use of pseudogenes as a neutral baseline
important contribution to gene-content population genetics

comments.issue: Pseudogene neutrality assumption may bias gene classes and the estimated proportion of beneficial genes.
comments.request: Show sp vs dS and assess how this bias affects estimates.
comments.quote: Would this imply that pseudogenes are biased in gene classes that are in fact neutral or deleterious? How would this affect the analysis, in particular the estimation of the proportion of beneficial genes?

comments.issue: High dN/dS values may drive Figure 2d patterns; log scale may exaggerate the correlation.
comments.request: Show the correlation without dN/dS>1 and on a linear scale.
comments.quote: Could you show the correlation if genomes with dN/dS>1 are removed (for example) and a plot on linear scale?

comments.issue: Unclear whether the si/sp relationship would strengthen for more common genes.
comments.request: Discuss expectations and extend the analysis to commoner genes.
comments.quote: What would the authors expect if this analysis was done with more common genes and pseudogenes (eg, present between 10-20% of genomes or even in an increasing number of genomes)?

comments.issue: Caveat needed that not all singletons are beneficial; most rare genes may be neutral.
comments.request: Caveat the claims about beneficial rare genes.
comments.quote: Although I would make sure to caveat that not all singletons would be expected to confer benefits, and not all singletons within a pseudogene-depleted category are necessarily beneficial.

comments.issue: si/sp calculation lacks a clear description and mathematical formula.
comments.request: Describe the calculation clearly and give the formula.
comments.quote: Could you make the descriptions for the calculation of si/sp clearer in the methods and include a mathematical formula?

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 2 points are not coloured by taxonomic group or labelled by species.
comments.request: Colour points by taxonomic group and identify key species.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to colour points in Figures 1 and 2 by taxonomic group (at least for the major groups, as in Figure 3) and to identify points corresponding to some species

comments.issue: L44 says adaptive-value genes can be identified, but none are identified.
comments.request: Clarify or correct this statement.
comments.quote: L44 mentions that genes that provide adaptive value can be identified, but no such genes are specifically identified here.

comments.issue: Species definition or identification problems may affect the analysis.
comments.request: Comment on how species assignment issues impact the results.
comments.quote: Could you comment on how problems with species definitions or identifications could impact the analysis?

comments.issue: Correlation coefficients at L118 and L119 are missing negative signs.
comments.request: Add the negative signs.
comments.quote: L118, L119 add a negative sign to correlation coefficients.

comments.issue: Figure 4 colours may be hard to distinguish for colour-blind readers.
comments.request: Increase contrast between Figure 4 colours.
comments.quote: to improve accessibility (colour blindness), make the colours in Figure 4 vary in contrast

comments.issue: Intact versus pseudogene ratios per species and p-values are not tabulated.
comments.request: Add a table with per-species values and p-values.
comments.quote: Could you include a table with these values for each species and the p-value

comments.issue: L319 needs clarification.
comments.request: Clarify this sentence.
comments.quote: L319 clarify this sentence.

comments.issue: Manual annotation at L451 is not described.
comments.request: Clarify what the manual annotation entailed.
comments.quote: L451 Clarify what the manual annotation entailed.

comments.issue: Redundant-copy pseudogenes might be a more neutral reference; this alternative is untested.
comments.request: Analyse or discuss results using only redundant-copy pseudogenes.
comments.quote: Would pseudogenes with a redundant copy be a "more neutral" reference? How do the authors expect the results to change if only this class of pseudogenes were taken for analysis?

comments.issue: ED Fig 7 shows non-redundant categories positively associated with pseudogenization; explanation missing.
comments.request: Explain these positive associations.
comments.quote: In ED Fig 7 a few categories in the non-redundant class seem to be positively associated with pseudogenization. Do the authors have an explanation for that?

title: Pseudogenes act as a neutral reference for detecting selection in prokaryotic pangenomes

study.system: Palaearctic, Nearctic and Australasian riverine fish communities; time series

reviews.assessment: Interesting, broad-interest study with a massive database and no major flaws, but several major doubts about model structure and clarity.
strengths: massive database across a large spatial scale

comments.issue: The conclusions are not considered extremely new, though they add important information.
comments.quote: Although I do not consider the conclusion to be extremely new

comments.issue: What counts as human pressure, and which layers the Human Footprint index uses, is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the Human Footprint and its component metrics in the introduction.
comments.quote: explain what was considered human pressure (in this case, human footprint)

comments.issue: No maps show how the Human Footprint changed between past and recent years.
comments.request: Provide past and recent HFP maps with the surveyed sites in the supplement.
comments.quote: would it be possible to draw the human footprint map: past (1997) and recent (2009)

comments.issue: The human footprint × time interaction is confusing because HFP and time are not independent and HFP has only two measurement dates.
comments.request: Explain or revise the interaction, perhaps using annual HFP values.
comments.quote: I have a concern/doubt about the structure of Bayesian models, especially the interaction between human footprint and time

comments.issue: Colours for non-native richness and abundance are swapped between Fig. 3 and the text.
comments.request: Fix the colour labels so figure and text match.
comments.quote: It appears that the authors have switched the colors of the proportion of non-native richness and abundance in Fig. 3 and in the text

comments.issue: The significant Time × stream position × past pressures slope suggests strong rather than moderate evidence.
comments.request: Consider upgrading “moderate evidence” to “strong evidence”.
comments.quote: Doesn't this indicate a strong effect of the past anthropogenic pressure on the non-native abundance in most downstream areas

comments.issue: The study is correlational, but this limitation is not acknowledged in the discussion.
comments.request: Add consideration of the correlational nature of the study.
comments.quote: Although remarkedly consistent, this study is correlational

comments.issue: “Higher degree of past anthropogenic pressures” on page 9 is unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase, e.g. as “increase in past anthropogenic pressures”.
comments.quote: What do you mean by “higher degree of past anthropogenic pressures”?

comments.issue: The claim that richness increases via non-native introductions contradicts Fig. 1, where non-native richness is flat and invasive abundance declines.
comments.request: Qualify the statement, e.g. to highly degraded rivers.
comments.quote: Doesn't this statement contradict the results of Fig. 1, in which the richness of non-native species does not change and the abundance of invasive species decreases over time?

reviews.assessment: Finds the work interesting and valuable but says data and methods are poorly described and robustness checks are largely missing.
strengths: valuable addition assessing non-native species trends
interactive map was a nice touch

comments.issue: The main text gives a limited description of what the data include and how analyses were carried out.
comments.request: Describe the data, coverage and analyses more fully in the main text.
comments.quote: I found it very challenging to fully understand what the data included and how the analyses were carried out from reading the main text of this manuscript

comments.issue: Stated coverage (“last 3 decades”, three realms) contradicts the methods and map, which include older data and other regions.
comments.request: Make the stated temporal and spatial coverage consistent with the data.
comments.quote: the last 3 decades is used consistently to describe the coverage, but the data used when you get to the method extends further back than this is some cases

comments.issue: Few sensitivity tests were run on these data; time series length, start year and region could influence results.
comments.request: Run and report sensitivity checks on time series length, start year and geographic region.
comments.quote: there very few explorations or tests carried out on the data used here to provide reassurance for the presented results

comments.issue: The abstract's data description is vague and does not list the realms or timescale.
comments.request: List the biogeographic realms and timescale in the abstract.
comments.quote: The description of the data is very vague. “across three biogeographic realms”, it would be good to list them here

comments.issue: “Repeatedly sampled over the last 3 decades” implies uniform start, end and duration.
comments.request: State variable durations and frequencies with actual years.
comments.quote: Rather than “the last 3 decades”, can you be specific about data coverage.

comments.issue: How human pressures changed over the study period in the sampled regions is not introduced.
comments.request: Add context on pressure trajectories, e.g. improving water quality in northern regions.
comments.quote: Expect to see something about how human pressures have changed over the time period assessed

comments.issue: Specialist terms such as longitudinal stream position, reach and Strahler order are not explained.
comments.request: Define the freshwater terminology for a broad audience.
comments.quote: Not clear to me what is meant by longitudinal stream position

comments.issue: The introduction gives no information on how the data were analysed.
comments.request: Add a sentence summarising the Bayesian hierarchical models.
comments.quote: No information on how the data were analysed

comments.issue: The first set of results is repeated in the first paragraph.
comments.request: Remove the first instance of the repeated results.
comments.quote: In the first paragraph, the first set of results are repeated, the first instance can be removed.

comments.issue: Switching between 80/90/95% evidence categories is unconventional and confusing without methods context.
comments.request: Explain the evidence approach in the main text or use one CI range.
comments.quote: Since this is not general practise and not often seen in papers, I think it might be best either to explain this approach in the main text

comments.issue: It is unclear what the models represent, and Fig. 1 legend contradicts the text on time as a predictor.
comments.request: Clarify the model structure and align the Fig. 1 legend.
comments.quote: time as a random slope, but Fig 1 legend says time as the only predictor

comments.issue: The typology section does not explain the method before presenting results.
comments.request: Briefly describe the clustering method and its purpose before the results.
comments.quote: Starting description could be altered to briefly describe the method and how/why it was used before going into the results

comments.issue: Figure 2 legend does not explain the cluster names, especially medium change.
comments.request: Describe the cluster names in the Fig. 2 legend.
comments.quote: description of cluster names might be helpful here, especially for medium change which is not very clear without reading the methods

comments.issue: Non-native abundance is described as orange in the figure but is actually yellow.
comments.request: Correct the colour description.
comments.quote: Non-native species abundance referred to as orange in the figure but it is actually yellow.

comments.issue: Figure S4 repeats non-native abundance; one panel should show richness and a ribbon plot would be clearer.
comments.request: Fix the duplicated panel and consider line and ribbon plots.
comments.quote: Figure S4 – repeat of non-native abundance. Think one should be richness.

comments.issue: The model behind the spatial drivers results is not stated, nor which variables are assessed.
comments.request: State the model and variables used in each case.
comments.quote: It is not clear what the model is that determines these results

comments.issue: It is unclear whether these models account for year of sampling.
comments.request: State whether year of sampling is included in the models.
comments.quote: Do these models account for year of sampling at all?

comments.issue: “Most upstream” should read “upstream-most”.
comments.request: Use “upstream-most”.
comments.quote: Most upstream rather than upstream-most.

comments.issue: The discussion does not address why these results differ from global biodiversity trends.
comments.request: Discuss the discrepancy with global trends.
comments.quote: Why do you think the results here differ from the global trends?

comments.issue: The choice of past time point could affect results and is not explored.
comments.request: Discuss and test the influence of baseline and reference points.
comments.quote: What about the time point chosen for the past? What impact could this have on results?

comments.issue: The text describes data from certain regions only, while the map shows additional regions.
comments.request: State clearly where all the data come from.
comments.quote: The description of the data suggest data from certain regions only, then the interactive map shows other regions are included. Please be clear about where the data are from.

comments.issue: A map of the study sites is missing from the main text.
comments.request: Add a map of the sites to the main text.
comments.quote: I think it would be useful to have a map of the sites in the main text.

comments.issue: What was sampled and potential biases in the data are not described.
comments.request: Describe the sampling approach and its potential biases.
comments.quote: What were the data sampling, were they sampling everything, certain species? Very little information to help understand the data and the potential biases.

comments.issue: Quantiles are presented where ranges would be more informative.
comments.request: Present ranges instead of quantiles.
comments.quote: The quantiles are presented for the data, I think ranges would be more informative.

comments.issue: The hierarchical structure of sites within basins is not well described.
comments.request: Improve the description of the hierarchical data structure.
comments.quote: The description of the hierarchical nature of the data, sites within basins (?) could be improved.

comments.issue: Dissimilarity uses the first year as reference, but first years vary among time series.
comments.request: Test whether the varying reference year influences results.
comments.quote: Dissimilarity – first year as reference, but first year varies between time series. Could this influence the results?

comments.issue: The links between research questions and the models run are unclear in the methods and introduction.
comments.request: Relate each question to the corresponding model more clearly.
comments.quote: would benefit from clearer relation of questions/areas being explored to the models being run

title: Past and recent anthropogenic pressures drive rapid changes in riverine fish communities

study.system: zokors; structural variation and hypoxia adaptation; genomics

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers raised a number of concerns that must be addressed before publication, and invites a revision responding to all reviewer and editorial comments.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive, well-executed study; main concern is missing multiple-testing corrections, plus minor suggestions.

comments.issue: CAFE, aBSREL and RNA differential expression analyses lack multiple-testing corrections.
comments.request: Correct for multiple testing and show quantile-quantile plots.
comments.quote: involve many comparisons but do not involve any corrections for multiple hypothesis testing

comments.issue: The three-tissue RNA-seq design could pool information to increase power.
comments.request: Explore mashr to increase power while controlling the false discovery rate.
comments.quote: I recommend that the authors explore using mashr

comments.issue: The LM/BM measure assumes isometric lung-body scaling, which may fail for extreme body sizes.
comments.request: Plot lung versus body mass for all species together.
comments.quote: the LM/BM measure is a crude measure as it assumes that lung mass scales isometrically with body mass across vertebrates

comments.issue: Line-level edits: stray '<fixed>' at L120 and the Fig. 3h caption wording.
comments.quote: Fig 3h. In the caption, suggest using “supports” instead of “proved”

comments.issue: The BluePippin size range setting at L275-277 is unstated.
comments.request: Report the size range setting.
comments.quote: Lines 275-277. What was the size range setting for BluePippin target selection?

comments.issue: Fig. 1d-e samples could be sorted by elevation to reveal the gradient.
comments.request: Sort samples by elevation.
comments.quote: Would suggest sorting the samples (particularly E. baileyi) by elevation, as there seems to be a neat altitudinal gradient.

comments.issue: Fig. 1f is hard to digest with arbitrary y-axis order.
comments.request: Consider presenting it as a table.
comments.quote: I find this a bit difficult to digest as the confluence of size/shapes/colors are hard to follow and the y axis order appears to be arbitrary. This is perhaps more useful in table form.

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed it and recommends publication after revision; main concerns are missing evolutionary context, E. smithi data gaps and multiple-testing corrections.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks the divergence and speciation context of Chinese zokors.
comments.request: Add statements on the evolutionary context of the highland species.
comments.quote: I would appreciate some evolutionary context in the introduction stating that the two highland sister species evolved from a group of lowland species and that E. fontanierrii is the oldest species within Eosplax.

comments.issue: Which of the two E. baileyi lineages was sampled, and how it relates to E. smithi, is unclear.
comments.request: State the sampled lineage.
comments.quote: It is not clear which of the two lineages the authors have sampled from and how these relate to E. smithi

comments.issue: Phenotypic and expression data for the highland sister species E. smithi are missing, so shared ancestral variation could explain the differences.
comments.request: Weigh the hypothesis that adaptations evolved in the shared highland ancestor.
comments.quote: the observed phenotypic/expression differences could be explained by genetic variation shared between the two highlander species

comments.issue: It is unclear whether multiple-comparison correction was applied, and significance is biased by the close relatedness of the four lowland species.
comments.request: Correct for multiple comparisons and account for phylogeny (e.g. PGLS).
comments.quote: significance is likely biased by the fact that the 4 lowland species are all more closely related to each other

comments.issue: Common garden experiments mentioned at line 118 are not described in the methods.
comments.request: Add a methods section for phenotypic data and common gardens.
comments.quote: Common garden experiments mentioned in line 118 are not explained in the methods.

comments.issue: The temporal scale of Qinghai-Tibet Plateau uplift is missing.
comments.request: Add the uplift timescale for context.
comments.quote: for clarity I would add the temporal scale for the uplift of the Qinghai-Tibet plateau

comments.issue: Fig. 1B is not credited.
comments.request: Add the image credit.
comments.quote: Fig 1 B needs to be credited.

comments.issue: Box plots lack error bar descriptions and one- or two-sided test information.
comments.request: Describe error bars and tests in all figures.
comments.quote: Box plots need further description for error bars and ranges and additional information on whether the statistics used were one-sided or two-sided needs to be provided

comments.issue: The number of individuals per species is missing at L265 and L365-6.
comments.request: Report individual counts per species.
comments.quote: for clarity I would add how many individuals from each of the 6 species

comments.issue: Extended Data Fig. 2 does not state which chromosome is displayed.
comments.request: Label the chromosome or explain panels a-m.
comments.quote: Extended Data Fig.2 should state which chromosome is being displayed in the x axis

comments.issue: Reference 1 is duplicated as reference 28.
comments.request: Fix the reference list.
comments.quote: Reference 1 is repeated as reference 28.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and novel study; asks for more detail on timescales, populations, tissues, RNA methods and oxygen measures.
strengths: addresses a previously unexplored aspect of high-altitude adaptation

comments.issue: The predicted time at high altitude for zokors is not indicated.
comments.request: Indicate the time span in Fig. 1A or the introduction.
comments.quote: can the authors please indicate the predicted length of time that this group has been at high altitude?

comments.issue: How isolated zokor populations are and whether they intermix or migrate is not described.
comments.request: Describe population isolation and mixing.
comments.quote: Please describe in the text how isolated the different zokor populations are from one another.

comments.issue: The tissue showing EGLN1 and HIF1A upregulation at L236-238 is not stated.
comments.request: Indicate the tissue.
comments.quote: please indicate which tissue the upregulation of EGLN1 and HIF1A were located in

comments.issue: Increased EGLN1 should decrease HIF1A protein activity, yet HIF blunting is the adaptive response; this regulatory interaction is not considered.
comments.request: Discuss the EGLN1-PHD2-HIF1A interaction and its implications.
comments.quote: if an increase in EGLN1 gene expression results in increased PHD2 protein expression, one might predict that this would decrease overall HIF1A protein expression

comments.issue: HIF2A, a key human adaptation gene, was apparently not analysed.
comments.request: Report whether HIF2A was analysed.
comments.quote: Did the authors look at the HIF2A gene in their analysis.

comments.issue: How hemoglobin concentration was measured, including blood collection and anticoagulant, is unclear.
comments.request: Provide measurement details.
comments.quote: please provide more detail about how hemoglobin concentration was measured. How was blood collected and was heparin or EDTA used?

comments.issue: RNA sequencing details (sample storage, RNA isolation, quality control, library prep, statistics, covariates) are missing.
comments.request: Describe the RNA-seq methods and statistical model fully.
comments.quote: Some important details are missing regarding the RNA sequencing analyses.

comments.issue: Fig. 1A presents atmospheric oxygen as percentages, which is constant at 20.95%; partial pressures are the relevant measure.
comments.request: Report partial pressures of oxygen at each elevation.
comments.quote: what the authors should provide here are partial pressures of oxygen at each elevation, which is the relevant measure of oxygen availability

comments.issue: Figure legends do not specify error bars or statistical tests.
comments.request: Specify error bars and tests in the legends.
comments.quote: Please specify in figure legends what error bars represent and which statistical test was performed for each comparison.

comments.issue: Why inversions in EGLN1 and HIF1A drive expression, and whether the telomere mechanism applies to both genes, is unclear.
comments.request: Speculate on the mechanism and clarify its scope.
comments.quote: Can the authors speculate on why the inversions in EGLN1 and HIF1A may help drive increased gene expression?

title: Genomic structural variation is associated with hypoxia adaptation in high-altitude zokors

study.system: Global bird assemblages in agriculture vs native forest; meta-analysis of 71 assemblages

editor_summary: Editor requests responses to the reviewers' criticisms and some editorial concerns, plus a revised manuscript, before a final decision.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and methodologically thorough, but the bias assessment is unconvincing and the novelty claim is inaccurate.

comments.issue: The publication-bias assessment is unconvincing; robustness should be tested with Egger tests, file-drawer analysis and Rosenberg fail-safe numbers.
comments.request: Add these publication-bias and robustness analyses.
comments.quote: I strongly recommend authors to assess publication bias using Egger tests, ’file drawer analysis’, and to calculate Rosenberg’s fail safe-numbers in order to assess the robustness of their results.

comments.issue: The statement that trait-based filtering has not been tested in large-scale agricultural deforestation assessments is inaccurate given existing studies.
comments.request: Acknowledge these broad-scale studies and revise the novelty claim.
comments.quote: This statement, used as a justification for the novelty of the article, is not accurate.

reviews.assessment: Praises the question, dataset and analyses but questions the habitat-variability covariates, the model-averaging approach and some overstated language.

comments.issue: Temperature variation across the annual cycle and annual precipitation are poor measures of habitat variability; precipitation seasonality may be better.
comments.request: Reconsider or replace the habitat-variability covariates.
comments.quote: Some habitats can experience high variation in temperature across the annual cycle but does that make the habitat itself variable?

comments.issue: Disturbance regimes such as hurricanes, flooding and fire are not captured; the metrics should be termed climate variability.
comments.request: Rename the metrics and ideally include disturbance measures.
comments.quote: I think these climate metrics are interesting, but I think they should be termed “climate variability” not “habitat variability”. Ideally, measures of disturbance would be included.

comments.issue: The main question is unclear from this sentence and 'features of agricultural systems' is undefined.
comments.request: State the main question and define the agricultural features.
comments.quote: From this sentence alone, I was unsure what the main question of the study was. What are “features of agricultural systems”?

comments.issue: No examples are given of how the proposed filters might operate.
comments.request: Add examples of the filtering mechanisms.
comments.quote: It would be good to have some examples of how these filters might operate.

comments.issue: Filtering removes species, so it should not increase trait space without immigration or adaptation, which are not filtering.
comments.request: Reconcile trait-space expansion with the filtering concept.
comments.quote: For trait space to expand would require either immigration of new species into the pool, or adaptation of species in the pool, but are either of these processes “filtering”?

comments.issue: Hand-wing index may capture dispersal ability better than migratory status, especially in the tropics.
comments.request: Consider hand-wing index as a dispersal trait.
comments.quote: It might we worth considering hand-wing index (Sheard et al., 2020, Nature Communications) for a continuous measure of avian dispersal ability

comments.issue: The meaning of this measure is unclear; is it just variation in the response variable?
comments.request: Explain what this measure represents.
comments.quote: What does this mean? Is it just a measure of variation in the response variable?

comments.issue: The positive response ratio for low MAP contradicts the prediction, so there is no evidence that impacts were less severe with greater habitat variability.
comments.request: Address this contradiction and correct the habitat-variability narrative.
comments.quote: There is therefore no evidence here that negative impacts were less severe with greater habitat variability.

comments.issue: An interesting and important finding is not emphasized in the main text.
comments.request: Emphasize this finding in the main text.
comments.quote: This is an interesting and important finding that should be emphasized more in the main text.

comments.issue: The agricultural-history results are overstated; only two trait centroids were significantly predicted.
comments.request: Soften 'overwhelmingly' and report only significant traits.
comments.quote: These results are over stated for agricultural history. Ag history significantly predicted the centroids of only two traits.

comments.issue: Higher trait dispersion in tolerant communities suggests limiting similarity rather than filtering.
comments.request: Consider limiting similarity as an alternative process.
comments.quote: If trait dispersion is higher in more tolerant communities, that actually suggests a process more like limiting similarity, not filtering

comments.issue: 'Clearly' is too subjective.
comments.request: Remove or replace 'clearly'.
comments.quote: “clearly” may be too subjective, it wasn’t always clear.

comments.issue: A recent study on how trait filters vary with landscape properties in urbanization is not cited.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Neate-Clegg et al. 2023.
comments.quote: But see this recent study (Neate-Clegg et al., 2023, Current Biology) which assessed how trait filters varied with landscape properties in the context of urbanization.

comments.issue: It is unclear how breeding season was determined for tropical sites.
comments.request: Explain this for tropical field sites.
comments.quote: How was this done for tropical field sites where the breeding season is less clear?

comments.issue: The definition of continuous forest seems to accept very small fragments.
comments.request: Justify the continuous-forest threshold.
comments.quote: Is that a reasonable definition of continuous forest? Seems like a fairly small fragment.

comments.issue: The traits and their reasons for inclusion are not listed here.
comments.request: List the traits and inclusion rationale.
comments.quote: I think it is important to list the traits here and their reason for inclusion.

comments.issue: The distance covariate needs a shorter, clearer name.
comments.request: Use an acronym for this covariate.
comments.quote: It may be easier to refer to this distance covariate by some kind of acronym.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the seasonality covariate makes sense and whether covariates were scaled.
comments.request: Clarify covariate scaling and seasonality logic.
comments.quote: Does that make sense for seasonality as well? Also, were the covariates scaled?

comments.issue: The plural 'models' is confusing; the number of global models is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how many global models were used.
comments.quote: “models”, was there more than one global model?

comments.issue: Model averaging is problematic because coefficients depend on other covariates; correlations under 0.52 can flip signs; AIC cutoff 2 is arbitrary.
comments.request: Report VIFs and justify averaging versus a single global model.
comments.quote: Model averaging coefficients is problematic (see Cade et al., 2015, Ecology).

comments.issue: Model formulae are not written out and trait transformations are not stated.
comments.request: Provide all model formulae and transformations.
comments.quote: It might be helpful to write out all the model formulae. Were any of the traits transformed e.g., log-transforming body mass?

comments.issue: It is unclear when PC1 was tested against deforestation tolerance.
comments.request: Specify where this test is reported.
comments.quote: At what point was PC1 tested for correlation with deforestation tolerance?

comments.issue: The calculation of functional dispersion is not described.
comments.request: Describe how functional dispersion was calculated.
comments.quote: Where does it say how functional dispersion was calculated?

reviews.assessment: Values the extensive meta-analytic dataset but flags strong assumptions, unclear metrics and underdeveloped conservation implications.

comments.issue: Inferring filtering impacts from response-ratio changes is a strong short-cut; other assembly processes such as competition can alter functional structure.
comments.request: Acknowledge alternative community assembly processes.
comments.quote: I think that it is a strong ‘short-cut’ and that the authors should acknowledge that a modification in the functional structure of bird assemblages under environmental change can be due to other community assembly processes

comments.issue: Using climatic variables as a proxy for habitat variability is misleading.
comments.request: Rename these variables as climatic conditions.
comments.quote: I was really confused with this terminology and I wonder why the authors use this term instead of just calling these variables ‘climatic conditions’

comments.issue: The trait-centroid metric underlying the conclusions is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the assemblage trait centroid was calculated.
comments.quote: many of the conclusion drawn relies on the analyses of assemblage-level trait centroid (Fig. 4, Fig. 5). However, it is not explained clearly how such metric was calculated.

comments.issue: The deforestation-tolerance metric is arbitrary and not grounded in ecological strategy theory.
comments.request: Conceptually justify the deforestation tolerance metric.
comments.quote: I found that metric a bit arbitrary and, to me, it is not relying on strong theoretical knowledge about the ecological strategy variation in bird species.

comments.issue: Metrics are only explained in the methods, making the results hard to follow.
comments.request: Briefly explain the metrics in the results section.
comments.quote: I think it is important to briefly explain the metrics used in the results’ section so that the reader can understand what have been done.

comments.issue: The meta-analytic nature of the study is not clear from the abstract or introduction.
comments.request: State in the abstract and introduction that 44 published studies are reanalyzed.
comments.quote: I think that the authors should make clear from the abstract or introduction that this study relies on data coming from 44 primary studies already published.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the study advances the conservation relevance of filtering and which species are threatened.
comments.request: Clarify the conservation implications and threatened species or strategies.
comments.quote: Which bird species and which functional strategy are particularly threatened by deforestation? To me these are essential questions that remain to be addressed.

comments.issue: The title implies impacts of biodiversity rather than impacts on biodiversity.
comments.request: Revise the title formulation.
comments.quote: I found the formulation ‘the biodiversity impacts of agricultural deforestation’ a bit misleading.

comments.issue: The claim that studies of agricultural features neglect filtering is not understandable.
comments.request: Clarify or rewrite this statement.
comments.quote: Why do you consider that studies testing the effects of agricultural features are neglecting the critical role of filtering? Not sure to understand that statement.

comments.issue: 'Contrast' is not defined in this context.
comments.request: Define what contrast means here.
comments.quote: L121: What do you mean by ‘contrast’ here?

comments.issue: 'Agricultural features' and 'natural habitat variability' are too vague.
comments.request: Be more precise about these terms.
comments.quote: ‘agricultural features’ and ‘natural habitat variability’ could be many things. I think you should be more precise here.

comments.issue: More recent studies on landscape heterogeneity effects are not cited.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Sirami et al. 2019.
comments.quote: Regarding the effects of landscape heterogeneity, you could refer to more recent studies e.g. Sirami et al. 2019

comments.issue: It is unclear whether past species assemblages are examined.
comments.request: Clarify whether past assemblages are studied.
comments.quote: Are you looking at past species assemblages in this study?

comments.issue: The mechanism by which climate shapes biodiversity responses is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the mechanisms at play.
comments.quote: How are climatic conditions shaping the response of biodiversity to agricultural deforestation? This is not obvious and I think you should explain the mechanisms at play here.

comments.issue: The cubes in Figure 1, panel B are not labelled.
comments.request: Add sub-titles for cubes (i), (ii) and (iii).
comments.quote: On that figure, you could perhaps add sub-titles for the cubes (i), (ii) and (iii) to help the reader understand what is represented here.

comments.issue: It is unclear how using birds avoids taxonomic-identity confounding of biodiversity responses.
comments.request: Explain this rationale.
comments.quote: Why and how ‘using birds’ allow you to avoid taxonomic identity confounding biodiversity responses?

comments.issue: It should be clarified whether the response ratio was calculated for species and for assemblages.
comments.request: Clarify the levels at which response ratios were calculated.
comments.quote: the response-ratio was not only calculated for each species but also for each assemblage right?

comments.issue: Using human population density is unusual; its justification and correlation with other landscape metrics are unclear.
comments.request: Justify this variable and report its correlations.
comments.quote: It is not common to use human population density to characterize the landscape. Why did you decide to use this variable?

comments.issue: No data are provided for greater vegetation-structure variation in more seasonal climates.
comments.request: Provide data supporting this claim.
comments.quote: Do you have data to back-up the fact that native forests in more seasonal climates have greater variation in vegetation structure in your dataset?

comments.issue: Latitude is not used in the analyses although discussed.
comments.request: Explain why latitude is not used.
comments.quote: Why not using latitude in your analyses then?

comments.issue: The time period used for agricultural history is not stated in the manuscript.
comments.request: State the period used for the history metric.
comments.quote: The length of agricultural history was calculated from when to when? I could not find that info in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Too little information on the methods and analyses is given in the introduction.
comments.request: Add methods information to the introduction.
comments.quote: I think that you should give a bit more information on the methods and analyses in the introduction otherwise it is very hard to grasp what have been done before reading the methods.

comments.issue: Seasonality and MAP may be correlated.
comments.request: Report and address their correlation.
comments.quote: L245: Are seasonality and MAP correlated?

comments.issue: 'More filtered systems' is undefined.
comments.request: Define this term.
comments.quote: L250: What do you mean by ‘more filtered systems’?

comments.issue: The sentence is very unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: L252-253: this sentence is very unclear to me.

comments.issue: Figure 3 panels are not labelled and the difference between A and B is unclear.
comments.request: Add sub-titles to Figure 3.
comments.quote: Again, you could add subtitles on that figure to help the reader understand what is represented, e.g what’s the difference between panels A and B.

comments.issue: The significance of panels C, D and E is unclear and the label on panel D is confusing.
comments.request: Report significance and fix the panel D label.
comments.quote: On the panels C, D and E, are these relationships significant? Why is it written ‘Proximity to native forest’ on D?

comments.issue: The subset analysis shown in Figure 3B is not explained in the results.
comments.request: Explain the subset analysis with Figure 3B.
comments.quote: you ran an analysis on a subset of assemblages that comprised species present at native forest sites. I think this should be better explained while explaining this figure in the results’ section.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether assemblage-level or species-level response ratios are examined first.
comments.request: Clarify the order of the response-ratio analyses.
comments.quote: Are you looking at assemblage-level RR or species-level RR first?

comments.issue: The trait describing forest association is not identified.
comments.request: State which trait represents forest association.
comments.quote: L291: Which trait describe forest association?

comments.issue: Figure 4 is complex and poorly explained in the legend and main text.
comments.request: Simplify or better explain Figure 4.
comments.quote: This figure is very complex – it contains many information that are not well explained either in the legend or in the main text.

comments.issue: 'The assemblage-level centroid of individual traits' is unclear.
comments.request: Explain this metric.
comments.quote: What do you mean by ‘the assemblage-level centroid of individual traits’? This is very unclear.

comments.issue: It is unclear what the centroid is of, and no explanation is given in the results.
comments.request: Briefly explain the centroid in the results.
comments.quote: It is the centroid of what? This should be briefly explained in the results.

comments.issue: The multivariate trait metrics are not introduced or explained.
comments.request: Introduce and explain these metrics in the results.
comments.quote: What are these multivariate trait metrics? I am aware that the methods are presented at the end of the manuscript but the analyses should be introduced in the results

comments.issue: PC1 of assemblage trait centroids is not explained.
comments.request: Explain this metric where it is first used.
comments.quote: What is ‘PC1 of assemblage trait centroids’? Again, this was not explained at all before.

comments.issue: Hypervolume metrics would be more relevant for detecting trait shifts and clustering under filtering.
comments.request: Consider using hypervolume metrics.
comments.quote: I was surprised that you did not used the hypervolume metric in that study

comments.issue: 'Stronger natural and anthropogenic filtering' is undefined.
comments.request: Define this phrase.
comments.quote: What do you mean by ‘stronger natural and anthropogenic filtering’?

comments.issue: It is unclear why PC1 of centroids is related to functional indices, and conclusions from these relationships are doubtful.
comments.request: Explain the logic and consider direct analyses of these indices.
comments.quote: I was completely lost with this part. I don’t understand why you are looking at the relationships between PC1 of trait centroids and functional richness, functional dispersion and functional redundancy?

comments.issue: Describing the study as based on an extensive global database is misleading; it is a meta-analysis.
comments.request: Describe the study accurately as a meta-analysis.
comments.quote: It is misleading to say that your study is based on an extensive global database. Your study is a meta-analysis that draw conclusion from many datasets coming from previous studies.

comments.issue: 'Filtered ecosystems' is undefined.
comments.request: Define this term.
comments.quote: L386: What do you mean by ‘filtered ecosystems’?

comments.issue: The sentence is very unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: L414-416: This sentence is very unclear to me.

comments.issue: Species richness and presence/absence results are missing and should be presented at least in the SI.
comments.request: Present these results in the supplementary materials.
comments.quote: The results on species richness or presence/absence should be presented in the Supplementary materials I think. These are also important results that cannot be omitted from my point of view.

comments.issue: 'Extended recent history' is unclear and the duration is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the duration.
comments.quote: It is not clear what you mean by ‘extended recent history’. Please specify the duration here.

comments.issue: Oil palm and orchard tree crops are excluded without justification.
comments.request: Justify their exclusion or include them.
comments.quote: Why did you not include oil palm and orchard tree crops? I would have considered oil palm plantation as a crop, such as coffee or cocoa plantation.

comments.issue: It is unclear why only coffee and cocoa count as agroforestry when other crops are shade-grown.
comments.request: Justify the agroforestry classification.
comments.quote: Could you please justify why coffee and cocoa only were considered as agroforestry if these crops are shade-grown? What about the other crops?

comments.issue: Robustness to excluding the two secondary forest sites has not been tested.
comments.request: Run the analysis without the secondary forests.
comments.quote: Have you ran the analyses without the 2 secondary forests sites to see if the results remain similar? I think this should be done.

comments.issue: 'Constituent species' is undefined.
comments.request: Define this term.
comments.quote: L475: What do you mean by ‘constituent species’?

comments.issue: The period used to calculate agricultural history is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the period considered.
comments.quote: Could you please specify the period considered to calculate the agricultural history metric?

comments.issue: Table S3 does not explain how the traits relate to bird responses to deforestation.
comments.request: Add brief explanations of each trait's role.
comments.quote: In that table, you could briefly explain how the traits considered are involved in the response of birds to deforestation.

comments.issue: 3 line-level copy edits: title wording, one word choice, and a figure cross-reference.
comments.quote: L204: ‘biodiversity impacts of agricultural deforestation’ should be ‘response of biodiversity to agricultural deforestation’ no?

title: Ecological filtering shapes the impacts of agricultural deforestation on biodiversity

study.system: European Alps flora; species distribution and conservation prioritization simulations

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers find considerable potential but raise substantial concerns; invites revision, asks to highlight changes and ensure all data are fully available.

reviews.assessment: Likes the topic and setup but finds the approach hard to follow, methods inconsistent, figures unclear, and caveats missing.
strengths: appreciates the amount of work that went into the study

comments.issue: The level of methodological detail is inconsistent across sections, making the approach hard to follow.
comments.request: Make the level of information consistent across sections and move parameter details to supplements.
comments.quote: I am mostly recommending to keep the level of information consistent across sections
