comments.issue: Species distribution models, habitat suitability maps and habitat suitability map predictions are used interchangeably.
comments.request: Pick one term, define it and use it consistently.
comments.quote: I would recommend picking one term, define it, and consistently use it throughout

comments.issue: It is hard to keep the components straight without a workflow schematic.
comments.request: Add a workflow schematic, at least as a supplementary figure.
comments.quote: A workflow schematic might help, some text on how the levels of complexity fit together would be ideal

comments.issue: No caveats or potential shortcomings of the work are discussed.
comments.request: Add a discussion of caveats.
comments.quote: there was no discussion of any caveats of this work

comments.issue: True Skill Statistic and Boyce Index are unexplained and ~0.6 is wrongly called very good performance.
comments.request: Explain both metrics and correct the performance interpretation.
comments.quote: I think some explanation of True Skill Statistic and Boyce Index are necessary if you call them out

comments.issue: Figure S1 panels show four lines while legends show three and two, and scenario versus SSP colours are unclear.
comments.request: Fix the Figure S1 legends and clarify colour meanings.
comments.quote: there are at least 4 lines in each figure. The legend shows 3 lines and 2 lines.

comments.issue: The Figure S2 legend does not explain symbols, acronyms or value ranges.
comments.request: Expand the Figure S2 legend.
comments.quote: the figure legend does not sufficiently explain what a reader sees in the figures

comments.issue: Figure 3 is nearly impossible to decipher even after reading the legend.
comments.request: Rethink and redesign Figure 3.
comments.quote: I have read the legend several times and stared at the figure, but can't say that I really understand what I am seeing here

comments.issue: The spatial hierarchy of local versus regional conservation is unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase to make the spatial levels clearer.
comments.quote: In a spatial hierarchy local usually goes below regional, or a region covers more area than local

comments.issue: Figure 4 combines at least three figures' worth of content.
comments.request: Split Figure 4 and reconsider which parts belong in the main text.
comments.quote: These are at least 3 figures in one and I would consider splitting them up

comments.issue: The observation data sources in Table S2 are given as acronyms without descriptions or processing details.
comments.request: Describe the data sources and processing protocols.
comments.quote: The data sources need to be described. Acronyms alone are not sufficient.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the data and cleaned data are freely available to readers.
comments.request: State and enable data availability.
comments.quote: Are the data freely available? Are the cleaned data available to readers?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether land cover data were used as provided or processed.
comments.request: Describe any land cover processing steps.
comments.quote: were the data described used as is from the data provider or were any processing steps necessary

comments.issue: It is unclear whether observation density was computed per species or across all species, and whether that is valid.
comments.request: Describe and justify the observation density calculation.
comments.quote: was the observation density calculated on a species basis or across all observations?

comments.issue: The rationale for point process models over Maxent and the handling of absences or quadrature points are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the model choice and the absence/quadrature issue.
comments.quote: please explain why point process models were used here and not more standard methods such as maximum entropy models

comments.issue: How the scenarios were generated, how many exist and which variables were used is not straightforward to find.
comments.request: Explain the scenario generation and variables used.
comments.quote: please explain how the individual scenarios were generated, how many there where, and which variables were used for which model/scenario

comments.issue: The projection section is hard to follow.
comments.request: Add a supplementary schematic of models, maps and scenarios.
comments.quote: I found the description in this section hard to follow

comments.issue: The phrase further processed according to previous literature is vague.
comments.request: State exactly what processing was done.
comments.quote: "further processed (a) according to previous literature" is vague. What exactly did you do here?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether simple or realistic dispersal models were used.
comments.request: Clarify which dispersal models were used.
comments.quote: "with simple dispersal models" and mention of "realistic dispersal" in the next line is not clear

comments.issue: It is unclear what the four additional suitability maps are and why 1711 species were kept.
comments.request: Explain the additional suitability maps and the species filtering.
comments.quote: what were the four additional suitability maps? 1711 species were kept is also not clear

comments.issue: The term realistic dispersal is unexplained and overstates what the model predicts.
comments.request: Explain or rename it, e.g. predicted or restricted dispersal.
comments.quote: The term 'realistic dispersal' needs to be explained. What exactly do you mean by this?

comments.issue: The best TSS threshold is not reported anywhere.
comments.request: Report the best TSS threshold, e.g. in a supplementary table.
comments.quote: What was the best TSS threshold? You need to report that threshold somewhere

comments.issue: It is unclear whether MigClim parameters were consistent across species or species specific.
comments.request: State whether MigClim parameters were species specific.
comments.quote: Where MigClim parameters consistent across species or species specific?

comments.issue: The heading should read systematic conservation planning.
comments.request: Correct the term to systematic conservation planning.
comments.quote: System Conservation Planning – should be systematic conservation planning.

comments.issue: The choice of Zonation over Marxan or prioritizr is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the software choice for the reader.
comments.quote: why did you choose the Zonation software and not Marxan or prioritizr?

comments.issue: The text mentions 52 prioritization scenarios while Table S9 holds only 26.
comments.request: Resolve the discrepancy between text and table.
comments.quote: you mention 52 prioritization scenarios but Table S9 only hold 26. Why the difference?

comments.issue: The planning section is too brief and the approach of investigating scenarios in isolation is questionable.
comments.request: Expand the planning section and consider linking current and future plans.
comments.quote: Why are planning scenarios investigated in isolation? Can you think about linking current and future plans?

comments.issue: Protected area dispersal estimates are not considered although species dispersal is modelled.
comments.request: Consider protected area dispersal or discuss the consequences of ignoring it.
comments.quote: wouldn't it also make sense to consider protected area dispersal estimates as well?

comments.issue: Available methods incorporating phylogenetic diversity, such as prioritizr and Hanson et al. 2017, are not used or cited.
comments.request: Consider methods that incorporate phylogenetic diversity and cite Hanson et al. 2017.
comments.quote: there are methods available that can incorporate phylogenetic diversity

comments.issue: The 30% area goal is handled in post-analysis rather than as a constraint in the prioritization.
comments.request: Include the area constraint directly in the prioritization analysis.
comments.quote: If the goal is to get to ~30% of the area, why not include this parameter right in the prioritization?

comments.issue: The EnviDat repository is hard to access in a useful way, preventing replication or reuse.
comments.request: Make data and code accessible following FAIR principles.
comments.quote: I am having a hard time accessing those data in a useful way and can't check whether I can replicate or reuse the work

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and robust approach, but novelty is unclear, the discussion generic, and the fit to this journal uncertain.
strengths: impressive, extensively filtered species occurrence dataset
best available climate and land cover projections and high-resolution soil maps

comments.issue: The main text lacks sufficient methods information on input data, SDM approach and prioritization to interpret the results confidently.
comments.request: Add more methods information to the main text.
comments.quote: I found the main manuscript text lacked sufficient reference to the methods to provide the information necessary for interpreting

comments.issue: It is unclear how the paper advances understanding beyond several older and recent Alps distribution and prioritization studies.
comments.request: Clearly express the study's novelty relative to prior work.
comments.quote: What was missing for me in this paper was a clear expression of novelty as to how this paper advances our understanding

comments.issue: The local, regional and transnational conservation discussion is generic and gives little guidance on implementation or comparison with other priorities.
comments.request: Provide concrete guidance and compare with other conservation priorities.
comments.quote: The discussion in these sections felt a bit generic and did not provide extensive guidance

comments.issue: There is no conclusion, leaving the ultimate goal of the paper unclear.
comments.request: Add a conclusion clarifying the paper's goal.
comments.quote: There was no conclusion to the manuscript, which left me wondering what the ultimate goal of the paper was.

comments.issue: The plant-diversity focus may fit a narrower journal unless a more compelling narrative is provided.
comments.request: Broaden the narrative and significance for this journal's readership.
comments.quote: the focus of the study on plant diversity might lend itself better to a journal with a slightly narrow focus

comments.issue: SSP585 is not necessarily the worst case scenario.
comments.request: Reword worst case SSP585 as more severe SSP585.
comments.quote: Consider rewording "worst case SSP585 scenario" as SSP585 is not necessarily the worst case

comments.issue: The sentences at lines 118 and 121 need rewording.
comments.request: Reword the sentences as suggested.
comments.quote: I think these sentences should read "the percentage of species losing/expanding the most of their suitable habitat

comments.issue: Figure 2 has y-axis, secondary axis, colour and scaling problems.
comments.request: Fix the Figure 2 axes and labels.
comments.quote: Figure 2 – y-axis should be "Elevation 95th Percentile (m)"

comments.issue: Only IUCN category I-II protected areas are used, excluding III-VI and uncategorised areas that also protect biodiversity.
comments.request: Include or justify the exclusion of other protected area categories.
comments.quote: Why are only IUCN category I-II PAs used in this analysis?

comments.issue: It is unclear what common spatial resolution was used given mixed-resolution input layers and 1 km climate data.
comments.request: State the common resolution and justify it.
comments.quote: What was the common spatial resolution used for the projections given that the input data layers are in several different spatial resolutions?

comments.issue: Only one SDM algorithm is used although algorithm choice can strongly influence results.
comments.request: Use multiple SDM algorithms and assess uncertainty to algorithm choice.
comments.quote: The results would be much more convincing if multiple SDM algorithms were used, and also so that uncertainty to the choice of algorithm could also be assessed

reviews.assessment: Potential for an important contribution, but dispersal assumptions, missing processes and analysis choices undermine confidence in the main findings.
strengths: potential to make an important contribution to biodiversity conservation over the European Alps

comments.issue: Fixed or default dispersal parameters in the realistic scenario may strongly affect the rate and direction of range shifts.
comments.request: Explore and discuss uncertainty in the realistic dispersal parameters.
comments.quote: The authors need to explore and discuss the potential uncertainties of dispersal parameters in the "realistic" scenario on the main results

comments.issue: Imposing no dispersal for low-elevation surrounding regions omits colonization and overestimates biodiversity loss.
comments.request: Include and discuss species dispersal from surrounding regions.
comments.quote: The omission of plant colonization from other regions would lead to an overestimation of the biodiversity loss, and undermine the validity of main findings

comments.issue: Land cover effects on biodiversity are discussed without actual data or comparison with historical evidence.
comments.request: Compare historical and future land-cover-driven biodiversity changes.
comments.quote: the authors discussed the impact of land cover change on future plant biodiversity changes, but there is no actual data on this effect

comments.issue: The omission of warming-induced tree upslope expansion may wrongly produce an increase rather than decline in endemism.
comments.request: Account for tree upslope shifts and their effect on rarity and endemism.
comments.quote: The omission of tree upslope might induce an increase instead of a decline in endemism at the taxonomic level as shown in Figure 1

comments.issue: The effectiveness of the expanded protected area network is unclear; gap species are not systematically assessed.
comments.request: Assess gap species, especially threatened and restricted-range species.
comments.quote: conducting a systematic assessment of gap species is crucial for effective biodiversity protection

comments.issue: Elevation and latitude shifts are analysed separately instead of jointly, fragmenting the understanding of migration.
comments.request: Analyse elevation and latitude changes together.
comments.quote: A comprehensive understanding of future plant migration can be achieved by analyzing the two-dimensional changes in elevation and latitude together rather than separately

comments.issue: The suggestion that little European coordination is needed contradicts expected cross-region plant migration.
comments.request: Reconcile the coordination message with cross-regional migration.
comments.quote: this contradicts the fact that plant migration is expected to occur across various regions and countries

comments.issue: Sensitivity tests for seed dispersal parameters such as dispKernel and barrier are missing.
comments.request: Add sensitivity tests for dispersal parameters.
comments.quote: Please include sensitivity tests for various parameters utilized in simulating seed dispersal, such as dispKernel, barrier, and others.

comments.issue: Details and reasoning behind combining 13 dispersal scenarios into three categories are missing.
comments.request: Add details and reasoning for each combining step.
comments.quote: This technique incorporates 13 different scenarios that can be grouped into three categories: realistic, unrestricted, and no dispersal

comments.issue: The causes of the variation in endemism across dimensions shown in Figure 1 are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the underlying causes of the endemism pattern.
comments.quote: What are the underlying causes of this pattern?

title: Transnational conservation to anticipate future plant shifts in Europe

study.system: Shiyu Palaeolithic site, China; radiocarbon, OSL and obsidian analyses

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers agree the manuscript improved; reviewers 2 and 3 are satisfied, but reviewer 1 still has concerns about chronology and obsidian provenancing that must be addressed before publication.

reviews.assessment: Chronology much improved, but MG quartz results should be rejected and the oldest-IUP claim and obsidian attribution need support.
strengths: consistency of radiocarbon and single-grain OSL ages
single-grain K-feldspar cross-check of all samples

comments.issue: MG quartz ages are scattered and unreliable; averaging their De is not meaningful.
comments.request: Reject MG quartz results and explain their scattering.
comments.quote: This suggests that the MG quartz results are unreliable, unless the authors can offer a reasonable explanation to why MG quartz data are more scattered than single grain data

comments.issue: Only two loess-layer samples were measured with single-grain quartz, while the poorly bleached Layer 2 samples were not tested.
comments.request: Measure single-grain quartz for more samples, at least the culture layer.
comments.quote: In addition to that, can the author clarify why only two samples from the loess layer were measured using single grain quartz.

comments.issue: The sigma-b value of 0.26 for the minimum age model is based on two samples without justification.
comments.request: Use the average OD of all well-bleached samples and MAM for SY-12.
comments.quote: They have used a sigma-b value of 0.26, based on the average of the OD values of 17.3% (SY-11) and 34.4% (SY-12), without explaining why.

comments.issue: The attribution of four obsidian pieces to Changbai Mountain and Gladkaya is not robustly distinguishable from other sources.
comments.request: Justify the provenance attribution with a robust statistical analysis.
comments.quote: I am not an expert in geochemistry, but the attribution of geographic locations of the 4 obsidian pieces is tenuous for me.

comments.issue: The main text says Shuidonggou is 3000 years younger than Shiyu while the supplement says its chronology is unresolved, so the title claim cannot be verified.
comments.request: Reconcile the Shuidonggou ages with the oldest-IUP claim.
comments.quote: This raises the question “is Shiyu really the oldest IUP in China”, as claimed in the title of the paper?

comments.issue: Two criteria are numbered as fifth in SI page 35.
comments.request: Renumber the second fifth criterion to (6).
comments.quote: SI Page 35 2nd para. There are two fifth criteria. Please change the 2nd one to (6).

comments.issue: How plateau values and their errors were determined in fig. C13 is unclear and unconvincing for some samples.
comments.request: Clarify the plateau determination and error.
comments.quote: SI page 40 fig. C13. Please clarify how the plateau values (dashed lines) were determined exactly? What is the error of the plateau?

comments.issue: The plateau test should not use the central age model for poorly bleached samples.
comments.request: Use the minimum age model for poorly bleached samples in plateau tests.
comments.quote: Additionally, the plateau test should not be based on CAM for the ‘poorly bleached’ samples (MAM should be used instead).

reviews.assessment: Earlier concerns fully addressed; recommends acceptance, only asking for cultural-model and Suyanggae checks.
strengths: previous concerns more than adequately addressed
study should be accepted for publication
important contribution despite small age differences

comments.issue: The paper applies a European cultural model to East Asia without noting East Asian perspectives such as the Korean two-stage model.
comments.request: Note the East Asian debates, including Seong's Korean two-stage model.
comments.quote: However, the authors should note that the leading Paleolithic archaeologist in Korea (Chuntaek Seong) strongly supports the two stage model (Early/Late Paleolithic) for Korea

comments.issue: Suyanggae is listed as an EUP site although no dates older than the LGM are known.
comments.request: Double check whether Suyanggae should be included as an EUP site.
comments.quote: That point aside, the authors should double check whether they should include Suyanggae (from Korea) as a supposed EUP site. I have not seen any dates older than the LGM for the site.

reviews.assessment: Improved version supporting publication; only the Shuidonggou source-point sentence and unreferenced sites need fixing.
strengths: expanded dating and bone tool sections strengthen the paper
obsidian long-distance exchange evidence supports publication

comments.issue: The claim that Shuidonggou cannot be a source point ignores ca. 45 ka dates and pending dating samples, and single source sites are hard to identify.
comments.request: Omit or temper the sentence at line 317.
comments.quote: I recommend caution here: first, the dates by Nian et al. (ref. 21) suggested an age of ca. 45 ka; and second, the recent excavations at Shuidonggou locality 1 did take several dating samples that are likely to be definitive.

comments.issue: Shimenshan and Gutougou are mentioned without references.
comments.request: Reference or omit the sites at line 355.
comments.quote: A small point: line 355 mentions the sites of Shimenshan and Gutougou. These should either be referenced or omitted.

title: Initial Upper Palaeolithic material culture by 45,000 years ago at Shiyu in northern China

study.system: squamate skull ontogeny; geometric morphometrics and phylogenetic comparative analyses

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers raised a few points that must be addressed before publication and invites a revision taking all reviewer comments into account.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, unique work with sound methods; only minor suggestions about broadening the discussion and clarifying Figure 4.
strengths: impressive amount of work across squamate taxa and ontogenetic stages
methods sound and state of the art
valuable new insights and data source

comments.issue: The paper rarely goes beyond its squamate phylogenetic scope, limiting its relevance to a larger audience.
comments.request: Add a broader-level discussion of the results.
comments.quote: the paper focuses very much on squamates, but rarely goes beyond its phylogenetic scope

comments.issue: Figure 4, especially panel 4B, is difficult to understand.
comments.request: Clarify Figure 4, particularly panel 4B.
comments.quote: I admit I had some trouble understanding figure 4, especially 4B

reviews.assessment: Strongly supportive and recommends publication, but asks for phylogenetic correction, clearer staging criteria, more comparison with other reptiles, and open data.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether developmental trajectory analyses and their correlations were phylogenetically corrected.
comments.request: Confirm or apply phylogenetic correction to all analyses.
comments.quote: Are the analyses concerning quantification of developmental trajectories of multiple systems and their correlation phylogenetically corrected?

comments.issue: The features used to homologize developmental stages among species are not explained in the main text.
comments.request: Explain the criteria for homologizing developmental stages.
comments.quote: can the authors explain the features that led them to homologize developmental stages among different species?

comments.issue: The squamate trend may reflect stronger negative allometry in non-snake squamates rather than a distinct pattern.
comments.request: Assess whether allometry explains the difference from birds and archosaurs.
comments.quote: Is this related to the different allometry (negative) that is simply more accentuated among non-snake squamates?

comments.issue: The discussion lacks comparison between squamates and other non-avian reptiles.
comments.request: Expand the comparison with other non-avian reptiles.
comments.quote: I did not see enough comparison between squamates and other non-avian reptiles in the discussion and I suggest to expand this

comments.issue: Segmented regions of interest are not publicly available despite the journal's open access policy.
comments.request: Make at least .stl files of the segmented regions available.
comments.quote: I would suggest the authors to make at least .stl files of the segmented regions of interest available to the public

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic; calls the paper a masterpiece with unique data, and gives minor suggestions on the introduction, modularity hypotheses, disparity, and data availability.

comments.issue: The introduction is repetitive and too focused on how understudied the topic remains.

comments.issue: Terms used later in the study (heterotopy, neomorphosis, heterochronic changes) are not defined in the introduction.

comments.issue: The end of the introduction reads like a conclusion instead of stating the objective and predictions.

comments.quote: The end of the introduction (line 130 to 140) is looking like a conclusion and I would prefer to see a well stated objective of the study with the predictions of the authors

comments.issue: Tables S28 and S29 on the a priori modularity hypotheses are hard to understand.

comments.quote: I don’t see anywhere the biological explanation of these hypotheses

comments.issue: Higher disparity in early stages could reflect differences in embryo position rather than biology.

comments.quote: I am wondering if the higher disparity found in early stages can be due to differences in embryo position (as embryos are really soft)?

comments.issue: The claim of rapid changes at lines 457 and 468 is not tied to specific results or a reference.
comments.request: Show which results support it or add a reference.
comments.quote: the authors wrote about rapid changes twice (line 457 and 468), which results can attest to that based on the analyses?

comments.issue: Superimposed landmarks, centroid size and the R script are not provided.

comments.quote: superimposed landmarks, centroid size, and the R script should be provided to ensure the repeatability of the study

title: Dynamic evolutionary interplay between ontogenetic skull patterning and whole-head integration

study.system: clonal Arabidopsis thaliana; microbe volatile priming with density and diversity treatments

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raised substantial concerns that preclude acceptance, while inviting a revised version addressing them.

reviews.assessment: Loves the creative experiment but says the inferences outrun the design, sampling effects are ignored, and methods and data are missing.
strengths: enjoyed it and wants to cite it

comments.issue: The manuscript infers too much about how microbe-induced phenotypes contribute to diversity-productivity relationships in natural systems.
comments.request: Temper the claims about natural systems.
comments.quote: I think the authors infer way too much about how this phenomenon might contribute to diversity productivity relationships in natural systems

comments.issue: The four microbes were selected for positive and maximally divergent effects and applied as volatiles only, unlike natural microbiomes.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited representativeness of the microbial treatments.
comments.quote: the microbial treatments are not very similar to the natural plant-microbiome context which contains hundreds or thousands of microbes that often have multiple effect mechanisms

comments.issue: In the field, co-occurring plants share microbe pools and the magnitude of microbiome effects relative to genotype or species effects is unknown.
comments.request: Discuss how field conditions and effect magnitudes could dampen or magnify the results.
comments.quote: individuals that closely co-occur (and therefore might drive phenotype-based overyielding) in the field are likely to be selecting microbes from an at least partially overlapping pool, which could minimize these effects

comments.issue: The contributions of sampling effects versus complementarity effects to transgressive overyielding are not evaluated.
comments.request: Add an analysis separating sampling from complementarity effects.
comments.quote: the authors do not evaluate the contributions of the sampling effect (selecting plants that had grown with the microbe with the most positive effects on fitness, etc) versus the complementarity effect to transgressive overyielding

comments.issue: Holobiont theory references are unsupported by the data and distract from the main point.
comments.request: Cut all references to holobiont theory.
comments.quote: I would recommend cutting all references to holobiont theory: it is unnecessary, distracts from the main point

comments.issue: The beginning and end of the main text feel cobbled together and contain too many ideas.
comments.request: Streamline the main text.
comments.quote: the beginning and end of the main text feel cobbled together. I think there are too many ideas, and that the authors should streamline.

comments.issue: Data for the main experiment and scripts for all analyses are missing despite journal policy.
comments.request: Provide the data and analysis scripts.
comments.quote: I cannot find data (for the main experiment) or scripts (all)

comments.issue: The methods are insufficiently detailed to understand the analyses.
comments.request: Improve the detail of the methods.
comments.quote: the methods are insufficiently detailed as written (or analyses are insufficient/incorrect, but given the quantity of science the authors include, I suspect details are just missing)

comments.issue: 'Massively codetermined' at L69 is too strong given host genotype contributions are usually larger.
comments.request: Tone down the wording at L69.
comments.quote: “massively codetermined” is perhaps to strong. Most studies find host genotype contributions are larger.

comments.issue: The claim that neighbouring identical genotypes interact with different microbes is unlikely given microbiome heritability and mycorrhizal networks.
comments.request: Reconsider the claim at L74.
comments.quote: This is unlikely to be true given that assembled microbiomes show observable heritability in host genotypes

comments.issue: 'Variations' at L89 should be 'variation'; the main text has many more grammar typos than the methods and supplement.
comments.request: Proofread the main text for grammar.
comments.quote: “variations” should be “variation.” This is trivially minor, but I am using this point to say that the main text has a lot more grammar typos this than the methods and supplement.

comments.issue: Other measured traits such as leaf angle are mentioned but not quantified.
comments.request: Provide quantitative information for these traits.
comments.quote: These changes are not obvious, so the authors should provide quantitative information.

comments.issue: 'Product' at L107 is used where 'average' is meant.
comments.request: Replace 'product' with 'average'.
comments.quote: “product” (multiplying all four together) is used where it should be “average”

comments.issue: The density manipulation is only revealed at line 344, making the main text confusing.
comments.request: State early that density was manipulated.
comments.quote: The authors should include the fact that they manipulated density early. Manipulating density is a key part of the study.

comments.issue: GLMM coefficients are not reported for the model in Table S3; Table S4 only exists for this reason.
comments.request: Report the GLMM coefficients, e.g. as a supplementary table.
comments.quote: the actual GLMM coefficients should be reported as an additional supplementary table

comments.issue: Interactive effects between density and diversity were not tested though ED Figs 4 and 5 suggest they exist.
comments.request: Test for density-by-diversity interactive effects.
comments.quote: why did the authors not test for interactive effects between density and diversity treatments?

comments.issue: The Figure 2 caption does not say which densities are included and whether control plants are included.
comments.request: State the densities and control treatment status in the caption.
comments.quote: Figure 2 caption: does not mention which plant density data treatments are included in each category.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether both timepoints are pooled in analyses, which would cause pseudoreplication.
comments.request: State which timepoint is analysed and avoid pooling.
comments.quote: this is the first mention of time, and it is not clarified whether both timepoints are included in the analyses for Figure 2 or otherwise (ideally not, due to pseudoreplication)

comments.issue: 'A direct function of' at L147 overstates moderate and marginally significant correlations, and ED Fig 6 does not support the claim.
comments.request: Tone down the claim at L147.
comments.quote: “a direct function of” is way too strong a wording for moderate correlations, especially when two are only marginally significant. This must be toned down.

comments.issue: Lines 152-154 and much of the main text are difficult to read.
comments.request: Proofread the main text for clarity.
comments.quote: I had to read this many times before I understood. In fact, much of the main text was a bit difficult to read.

comments.issue: The characterization of the field at L172 is unfair given the references supporting the next sentence.
comments.request: Skip this characterization.
comments.quote: I’m not sure this is a fair characterization of the field, given the many references I could think of to support the next sentence

comments.issue: 'Asynchrony' at L195 is an extraneous idea.
comments.request: Cut the asynchrony discussion.
comments.quote: “asynchrony” feels like another example of an extraneous idea that should be cut

comments.issue: It is unclear how plants were kept microbe-free and pots kept sterile in the main experiment.
comments.request: Describe the sterility procedures and address contamination risk.
comments.quote: how certain is it that the plants really did remain microbe free in the strain selection and main experiments?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the main-experiment traits were the same as those measured in the second-round screening.
comments.request: Clarify which traits were measured in each experiment.
comments.quote: It’s not clear if the traits measured for plants in the main experiment were the same ones the authors used in the second round screening

comments.issue: Equations at L407 and L415 are missing parentheses or compute different metrics than described.
comments.request: Correct the equations or the metric descriptions.
comments.quote: Both of these equations are missing parentheses, or they are calculating very different metrics than what is described.

comments.issue: The choice of RII instead of modelling treatment effects simultaneously is not explained.
comments.request: Justify RII or model (PW-PS) as a function of density.
comments.quote: I did not understand why RII was used instead of something taking into account the different treatments simultaneously.

comments.issue: Text at L420-424, L437-440 and L450-451 repeats earlier passages and is not methods content.
comments.request: Remove the repeated text.
comments.quote: L437-440: This repeats text found elsewhere, and is not methods.

comments.issue: The reason for log-transforming data and whether normality was achieved are not stated.
comments.request: Justify the log transformation and report whether normality was achieved.
comments.quote: why were data log-transformed? For normality? Was normality achieved by the transformation? It should be said.

comments.issue: Diversity and density were fitted as factors although they are quantitative.
comments.request: Fit diversity and density as numeric variables.
comments.quote: Diversity and density should have been fit as numeric variables since they have quantitative meaning.

comments.issue: The purpose of the two-sided T-test at L453 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what the T-test tested.
comments.quote: What is the two-sided T-test for? The correlation between RII and the phenotypic distance? I was not sure what analyses were being performed here.

reviews.assessment: Values the novel contribution, but the introduction overstates previous BEF assumptions and the facilitation and transgressive claims need care.
strengths: rigorous experiment controlling plant genetic diversity
novel and valuable contribution to BEF literature
first experimental isolation of these effects

comments.issue: The introduction overstates previous BEF studies' assumption that relationships arise only from genetic variation.
comments.request: Avoid these sweeping statements in the Introduction and Discussion.
comments.quote: it seems to overstate the assumptions of previous BEF studies, especially on lines 67-69 and lines 154-156

comments.issue: The introduction does not position the results among previous work on how overyielding arises.
comments.request: Introduce the ways overyielding can arise and why this mechanism is underappreciated.
comments.quote: the Introduction does not yet place these new results in the context of previous related work that has considered how overyielding might arise

comments.issue: Facilitation is claimed repeatedly but the evidence suggests mostly reduced competition, and RII values seem too uniformly positive.
comments.request: Distinguish reduced competition from facilitation and explain the RII pattern.
comments.quote: Facilitation and positive interactions are noted repeatedly in the results (e.g., L117, L120, L145), but I don’t see any clear evidence for this.

comments.issue: Transgressive overyielding is likely underestimated because the maximum monoculture was chosen a posteriori.
comments.request: Correct for this bias or acknowledge conservative estimates.
comments.quote: if one chooses the maximum monoculture a posteriori, then it tends to be an overestimated value

comments.issue: The Discussion claims these effects are as strong as other mechanisms, which was not directly tested.
comments.request: Avoid arguing equivalence with other mechanisms.
comments.quote: I recommend avoiding the arguments (e.g., L156-157, L176-178, L187) that these effects are as strong as those of other mechanisms

comments.issue: The holobiont definition is not recalled for readers at L71.
comments.request: Remind readers of the holobiont definition.
comments.quote: L71: Perhaps remind readers of the definition of holobiont.

comments.issue: 'Product' at L107 is not meant in the mathematical sense and should be replaced.
comments.request: Use another word in place of 'product'.
comments.quote: I suspect you do not mean ‘product’ of four replicates in the mathematical sense. To avoid confusion, I recommend using another word in place of ‘product’

comments.issue: The transgressive overyielding statement at L122 lacks a supporting display item.
comments.request: Refer readers to a figure or table supporting the statement.
comments.quote: Please refer to a display item that supports the transgressive overyielding results statement ending on this line.

comments.issue: Two- and four-phenotype treatments are lumped together although transgressive overyielding differs between them.
comments.request: Report the 2- and 4-phenotype treatments separately.
comments.quote: Given that there was much more transgressive overyielding for the 4-phenotypes than for the 2-phenotypes, I recommend reporting these separately, rather than lumping them all together.

reviews.assessment: Finds the study well written and important, but says the volatiles must be definitively identified with GC-MS before publication.
strengths: important perspective on the plant holobiont
topic of keen interest to many readers

comments.issue: Terms such as transgressive overyielding and biodiversity-ecosystem functioning are not defined for non-specialist readers.
comments.request: Define these terms for clarity.
comments.quote: I would benefit from more definitions of terms such as transgressive overyielding, biodiversity-ecosystem functioning, etc., to help with clarity

comments.issue: The experimental design remains opaque until the supporting information.
comments.request: Explain the experiment more fully in the main body.
comments.quote: I would suggest a more in-depth explanation of the experiment be incorporated in the main body of the paper to improve reader comprehension

comments.issue: Strain abbreviations such as F12 and F23 are too similar to distinguish.
comments.request: Use clearer indicators for strains.
comments.quote: The strain abbreviations “F12”, “F23”, etc. are quite similar and so difficult to discern.

comments.issue: It is untested whether motile microbes colonized the seedlings, so the volatiles-only assumption is unverified.
comments.request: Test for colonization or justify the volatiles-only assumption.
comments.quote: Some microbes are motile, did the authors test to see if microorganisms colonized their seedlings before planting in the common garden experiment?

comments.issue: The volatiles are only tentatively identified, which is insufficient for publication.
comments.request: Definitively identify the volatiles before publication.
comments.quote: However, I believe for the paper to be suitable for publication in this journal, additional work must be performed to definitively identify the volatiles that have so far only been tentatively identified.

comments.issue: PTR-MS is poorly suited to identifying unknown volatiles, so identification is unreliable.
comments.request: Add a complementary GC-MS analysis.
comments.quote: A complementary GC-MS analysis could ensure that at least the majority of putatively identified chemicals are indeed correctly identified.

title: Microbe-induced phenotypic variation leads to overyielding in clonal plant populations

study.system: tropical forest trees; 31 ForestGEO plots, mycorrhizal types

editor_summary: All three referees largely positive with mostly minor comments; R2 wants a more hypothesis-driven framework, R3 notes missing key references, and the editor requires the minimal dataset and code be made accessible.

reviews.assessment: Well-performed analyses and writing with no major suggestions; minor points on framing, candidate soil variables and access to the main dataset.

comments.issue: The statement at line 125 is misleading: EcM trees are a strong minority across much of the tropics, not only monodominant.
comments.request: Qualify this statement.
comments.quote: 125 this is misleading. There is much large overall area of tropical forests where EcM trees are in a strong minority compared to those sites where they form monodominant stands

comments.issue: Strong phylogenetic determination of mycorrhizal type in Pinaceae, Fagales and Dipterocarpaceae is not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention this phylogenetic context at line 137.
comments.quote: 137 could mention strong phylogenetic determination, esp. In Pinaceae, Fagales and perhaps Dipterocarpaceae.

comments.issue: The scales of the variables at line 158 are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the scales, e.g. in parentheses.
comments.quote: 158 Explain the scales; in parentheses could do.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the three sites at line 192 are exceptions where EcM presence depends on soil nutrients.
comments.request: Clarify whether any site showed significant relationships.
comments.quote: 192 Do I understand correctly that those three sites were exceptions, where EcM presence does depend on soil nutrients?

comments.issue: Trends for individual soil properties, as opposed to PC1 and PC2, are not reported.
comments.request: Report whether trends are evident when testing soil properties separately.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether specific soil properties are associated with absence of EcM trees.

comments.quote: 215 ok, but are there any specific properties, where EcM trees are lacking?

comments.issue: The possible situation in ultra-P-poor tropical soils, where non-mycorrhizal plants cope with fungal nutrient hoarding, is not discussed.

comments.quote: 220-5 of little relevance here. However, a similar situation may occur, at least theoretically, in ultra-P-poor tropical soils, where local prevalence of non-mycorrhizal plants may be a strategy to cope with fungal nutrient hoarding.

comments.issue: The newest estimate of ca 80 EcM fungal lineages (Tedersoo & Smith 2017) and related papers are not cited.

comments.quote: 229 newest evidence points to ca 80 (Tedersoo ja Smith in „Ecologial Studies“; 2017). This issue includes several other relevant papers that the authors might consider.

comments.issue: Coccoloba uvifera and Gymnopodium floribundum can be monodominant in the lowland neotropics, which the text omits.

comments.quote: 262 As an exception, Coccoloba uvifera and Gymnopodium floribundum can be monodominant in the lowland neotropics.

comments.issue: EcM Nyctaginaceae/Coccoloba may be more diverse than African Fabaceae+Uapaca, and Dicymbe/Guapira can be enormous trees.

comments.issue: The claim about undiscovered tropical lineages at lines 285-7 is considered irrelevant; only localised findings are likely.

comments.quote: 285-7 I do not consider this relevant. Very unlikely to find new tropical lineages of any major ecological importance or broad distribution.

comments.issue: Not all current models treat tropical forests as a single biome; several account for mycorrhizal-type abundances.

comments.quote: 291 not all current models treat tropical forests as a single biome and several account for mycorrhizal type relative abundances.

comments.issue: Other variables that could determine local EcM distribution are not hypothesised.
comments.request: Offer hypotheses about other determining variables.
comments.quote: 297 Any hypotheses what other variables could determine the local distribution of EcM plants?

comments.issue: The main dataset is not accessible, preventing single nutrient/element analyses.
comments.request: Provide access to the main dataset used in the analyses.
comments.quote: I feel that researchers should get access to the main dataset used in analyses to address, e.g. single nutrient/element effects.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important assessment, well written, but wants a hypothesis-driven test of EcM occurrence and less stretched interpretations.
strengths: very well written and easy to follow

comments.issue: The analysis is not hypothesis-driven: EcM occurrence at specific soil conditions should be tested before abundance analyses.
comments.request: Start by testing the occurrence hypothesis, then analyse abundance.
comments.quote: I would start with testing this hypothesis, and only then go into a deeper analysis of a soil properties being a predictor of EcM abundance.

comments.issue: Alternative explanations for tropical EcM distribution and comparisons with higher latitudes are not discussed.

comments.quote: authors do not suggest alternative explanations of EcM distribution in tropics, and do not discuss if EcM abundance drivers in tropics are different than those in higher latitudes

comments.issue: Lines 289-297 stretch conclusions about EcM dominance drivers into implications about EcM abundance.

comments.quote: This is not a proper interpretation of the results of this study, which has nothing to do with prediction of EcM plant abundance.

comments.issue: Two line-level language edits: 'ecosystem function' should be 'ecosystem functioning' (line 60), and 'imputation' should be 'input' (line 331).

title: Tropical tree ectomycorrhiza are distributed independently of soil nutrients

editor_summary: Editor: revise; address all reviewer and editor comments before a final decision on publication.

reviews.assessment: Important hagfish genome study; publication expected after clarifying comparisons with previous duplication models and fixing many details.
strengths: key hagfish genome for early vertebrate evolution

comments.issue: Comparisons with previous duplication models (Smith et al., Nakatani et al.) are insufficient; whether the hagfish analysis rejects them is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether the hagfish genome rejects the previously proposed models.
comments.quote: the authors’ analysis (Fig 4f) seems to be compatible with these previous models, and therefore it is important to discuss if the hagfish genome analysis can reject the previously proposed models.

comments.issue: If previous models cannot be rejected, the three alternative duplication scenarios and their assumptions are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss alternative scenarios, assumptions and significance in the Discussion or supplement.
comments.quote: If the hagfish genome analysis fails to reject the possibility of the previous models, the authors can discuss the three alternative duplication scenarios, underlying assumptions, methods, biological significance, etc. in Discussion or in Supplementary Information.

comments.issue: The number of 1R-to-2R fusions differs between studies (seven versus eight) and consistency with Sacerdot et al. is not checked.
comments.request: Check consistency by comparing Fig. 3D of ref 11 with Supplementary Figure 15.
comments.quote: Besides, the number of fusions between 1R and 2R is different (i.e. seven in ref 11 and eight in the authors analysis). Thus, it might be necessary to check consistency by comparing Fig 3D in ref 11 and Supplementary Figure 15.

comments.issue: Gene-tree duplication nodes may reflect progenitor species divergence (allotetraploidy) or diploidization rather than WGD timing, adding uncertainty.
comments.request: Acknowledge this additional dating uncertainty.
comments.quote: However, if 2R is allotetraploidy as suggested in refs 5 and 6, a “duplication” node in a gene tree might actually be species divergence of two post-1R/pre-2R ancestors that eventually underwent allotetraploidy.

comments.issue: Ref 60 (Smith et al. 2013), which also argued that 2R predated the gnathostome-cyclostome divergence, is missing at lines 81 and 85.
comments.request: Cite ref 60 at both places.
comments.quote: I think ref 60 also argued that 2R predated gnathostome-cyclostome divergence.

comments.issue: No sentences in refs 6 and 18 support the statement at lines 87-89; the papers may be misunderstood.
comments.request: Correct the citation and interpretation.
comments.quote: I could not find any sentences in refs 6 and 18 that support the authors’ sentence. It might be possible that the authors misunderstand those papers.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'assessment of the conservation of these events' at lines 91-92 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what the lack of the hagfish genome impeded.
comments.quote: The meaning of “assessment of the conservation of these events” is not clear to me. Is it possible to clarify what the lack of the hagfish genome has impeded?

comments.issue: The '++' notation at line 161 is undefined.
comments.request: Define the '++' notation.
comments.quote: Page 6, Line 161: “++81, ++86 and ++98” Where can I find the definition of “++”?

comments.issue: It is unclear that hexaploidization in ref 6 was counted as two separate WGD events.
comments.request: Clarify how the events were counted.
comments.quote: Please clarify that the authors counted hexaploidization proposed in ref 6 as two separate events here.

comments.issue: Missing citations at line 205: Putnam et al. 2007 and ref 6 with 18 ancestral chromosomes.
comments.request: Add these references.
comments.quote: Page 8, Line 205: “with either 10-13 (refs 4, 15)” The following paper should be included.

comments.issue: The exact sentences in ref 37 that justify the citation at lines 207-209 should be indicated.
comments.request: Point to the supporting sentences in ref 37.
comments.quote: I am grateful if the authors could indicate the exact sentences in ref 37 that justify this citation, since I don’t have time to confirm before the deadline for submitting this review.

comments.issue: Supplementary Table 34 compares refs 5, 11 and 6 but not ref 14.
comments.request: Include ref 14 in the comparison.
comments.quote: Supplementary Table 34 compares the reconstructions proposed in refs 5, 11 and 6 but not 14?

comments.issue: The observation at line 218 was previously linked to chromosome-scale duplications (ref 4), and ref 39 may not state what is claimed.
comments.request: Correct the citation and acknowledge the earlier interpretation.
comments.quote: Similar observation was previously said to be consistent with accumulation of chromosome-scale duplications as discussed in ref 4. Besides, I am not sure if ref 39 states that the presence of four or three paralogous chromosomes in chicken or gar confirms the 2R event.

comments.issue: 'Are compatible with 1R' at line 235 is ambiguous.
comments.request: Specify whether shared 1R is meant.
comments.quote: Page 8, Line 235: “are compatible with 1R” Are compatible with shared 1R?

comments.issue: The definition of 'cyclostome genes' is only in the figure legend.
comments.request: Define 'cyclostome genes' in the main text.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if the definition of “cyclostome genes” is described also in the main text (in addition to the description in the figure legend).

comments.issue: If the hagfish genome is not used for this analysis, the improvement over refs 5 and 6 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what the hagfish genome adds to this analysis.
comments.quote: If the authors decide to not use the hagfish genome for this analysis, what is the difference (or improvement) from similar analyses described in previous studies (refs 5 and 6)?

comments.issue: It is unclear how three WGD events were counted in ref 6 at line 261.
comments.request: Clarify the counting of WGD events in ref 6.
comments.quote: Three WGD events were suggested in ref 18, but it is not clear how the authors counted three WGD events in ref 6.

comments.issue: Which hagfish chromosomes are direct descendants of each AC, and what 'direct' means, is unclear.
comments.request: Identify the chromosomes and define 'direct'.
comments.quote: Which hagfish chromosomes (i.e. which Hi-C clusters) are direct descendants of each AC? What is the meaning of “direct” here?

comments.issue: The observation at lines 286-287 is consistent with chromosome-scale duplications proposed in refs 4 and 17.
comments.request: Acknowledge this alternative model.
comments.quote: This observation seems to be consistent with accumulation of chromosome-scale duplications proposed in refs 4 and 17.

comments.issue: The inference at lines 290-291 and 309-310 assumes chromosomes can only be duplicated by WGD, which is not stated.
comments.request: Add the 'assuming duplication only by WGD' clause.
comments.quote: It seems that other models proposed in refs 4, 6 and 17 are also possible. After thinking about this argument, I think it might be necessary to add a clause like “assuming that chromosomes can be duplicated only by WGD.”

comments.issue: 'All three of WGD events' at line 370 does not identify the events.
comments.request: Specify which three events are meant.
comments.quote: Page 13, Line 370: “all three of WGD events” Which three? 2R, CR1 and CR2?

comments.issue: If 2R was allotetraploidy, the inferred date may not correspond to the genome duplication event.
comments.request: Discuss this dating caveat.
comments.quote: Since refs 5 and 6 have suggested that 2R was allotetraploidy (i.e. hybridization of related species followed by genome doubling to recover the homologous chromosomes), it is not obvious that the inferred date corresponds to the genome duplication event.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'robust and accurate' at lines 379-380 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what robust and accurate refer to.
comments.quote: What is the meaning of robust and accurate here? Is it related to Page 54, Lines 1127-1128 in Supplementary Information?

comments.issue: Ref 13 may be missing at lines 381-382, and refs 5 and 6 could be mentioned.
comments.request: Add the missing references.
comments.quote: Maybe ref 13 is missing? Also, refs 5 and 6 can be mentioned around here?

comments.issue: Previously proposed models (refs 4, 6, 17) are not mentioned in the Discussion if they were not rejected.
comments.request: Mention these models in the Discussion.
comments.quote: I think that the previously proposed models (refs 4, 6 and 17) should also be mentioned in Discussion, if they were not rejected by the hagfish genome analysis.

comments.issue: Whether the CR events were autopolyploidy should be discussed before arguing that 2R differs from 1R and CR.
comments.request: Discuss the nature of CR events first.
comments.quote: It might be necessary to discuss if the CR events were auto-polyploidy before the argument that the 2R event is different from 1R and CR.

comments.issue: The inferred 2R timing is the progenitor divergence date, which may not match allotetraploidy timing, so all stem gnathostomes may not postdate 2R.
comments.request: Justify the assumption that stem gnathostomes postdate 2R.
comments.quote: The inferred timing of 2R is the date of divergence between the two progenitor species, which may not be close to the timing of allotetraploidy. Can we still safely assume that all stem gnathostomes post-dated 2R?

comments.issue: Figure 4a does not explain classification for 3-way paralogous trees and the arrow counting logic.
comments.request: Explain how 3-way paralogous trees are classified.
comments.quote: The figure explains the case for 4-way paralogous trees, but not for 3-way paralogous trees. If chicken chromosome 27 and gar LG15 are deleted from the figure, how do we classify the purple and yellow arrows in Fig 4a?

comments.issue: Fission simulations at all gene boundaries might be easier to understand than the quantile-based split.
comments.request: Consider performing fission simulations at all gene boundaries.
comments.quote: If we really need an upper bound or a conservative estimate, it might be easier to understand if fission simulations are performed at all gene boundaries.

comments.issue: The theoretical distribution of paralogous chromosome fusions could be calculated.
comments.request: Calculate the theoretical fusion distribution.
comments.quote: Is it possible to calculate the theoretical distribution of paralogous chromosome fusions?

comments.issue: The reason for choosing the four gnathostome species is not given.
comments.request: Explain the species choice.
comments.quote: What is the reason for choosing these four species?

comments.issue: The URL for downloading the supplementary files is missing.
comments.request: Add the download URL.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if the URL for downloading these supplementary files is written between Line 1966 and Line 1967.

comments.issue: HoxC6, C3, C1, D5 and D2 appear missing in the Crown Gnathostome Ancestor in Supplementary Figure 9.
comments.request: Check and explain these missing Hox genes.
comments.quote: Page 108, Supplementary Figure 9: HoxC6, C3, C1, D5 and D2 are missing in the Crown Gnathostome Ancestor?

comments.issue: The note in Supplementary Table 31 about chicken chrZ/LG4.2 and chr4.2/LG2.2 does not match the table, and 'orthologous' is misspelled.
comments.request: Check the table note and fix the spelling.
comments.quote: Is it correct? The table looks different. Also, please check the spelling of orthologous.

comments.issue: Numerous line-level copy edits and typos (e.g. 10-16, sum-rank, 'and than', species names, x10-5, e <= 10-6, WGDs, Branchiostoma, circus, orthologous).
comments.quote: Page 5, Line 132: “P<2.2×10-16, two-sided Wilcoxon sum-rank test” Please correct this typo: 10-16.

reviews.assessment: Should be published, but citation accuracy, the CR1/CR2 versus hexaploidy question and WGD dating need substantial improvement.
strengths: first published hagfish genome of intrinsic importance
genome useful for vertebrate comparative genomics

comments.issue: Existing literature is incorrectly or inconsistently cited, and the work of others is not adequately acknowledged.
comments.request: Systematically correct the citations and acknowledgments.
comments.quote: One consequence of this is that some of the existing literature is not correctly cited or is cited inconsistently (in some places of the manuscript, but not others even though some papers are cited), or not cited at all.

comments.issue: The manuscript does not flow well in places, figure legends are lacking and explanations are sparse.
comments.request: Improve flow, legends and explanations.
comments.quote: There are some parts where the manuscript doesn't flow well, where the figure legends are a bit lacking, and where the explanations too sparse.

comments.issue: Nakatani et al. (ref 6) is mis-cited: the additional cyclostome polyploidy was a triplication, not a duplication, and the 18-chromosome inference originates there.
comments.request: Cite Nakatani et al. accurately.
comments.quote: Nakatani et al (ref 6) had several findings that are mis-cited here: they showed that only the 1R WGD was shared with cyclostomes, and this finding was definitive due to the non-sharing of several chromosomal fusions that occurred after 1R but before 2R

comments.issue: The gene complement analysis would benefit from comparison with the whale shark paper.
comments.request: Compare with Tan et al. (whale shark).
comments.quote: Gene complement analysis (line 153 onwards) - this is interesting but it would benefit from a comparison with other results, for example those from the whale shark paper

comments.issue: The PVC/AC text is muddled: proto-gnathostome versus proto-vertebrate chromosomes are confused and the count varies between 16 and 17.
comments.request: Clarify the chromosome reconstructions and their counts.
comments.quote: The details of the PVCs are opaque and the text is muddled. The text talks about 17 inferred proto-gnathostome chromosomes, whereas it is clear from supp figure 5 that they are actually referring to proto-vertebrate chromosomes

comments.issue: It is unclear what the new AC/PVC reconstruction adds over published reconstructions, and the comparison is sparse.
comments.request: Demonstrate the advantage of the new reconstruction.
comments.quote: The authors clearly went to a great deal of effort to reconstruct these ACs/PVCs, but it isn't clear to me what they gain over using the available published reconstructions or how their method might be superior.

comments.issue: The paragraph at line 217 onwards is hard to follow and details of the pre-1R fusion are hard to find.
comments.request: Provide the pre-1R fusion details and improve clarity.
comments.quote: Given the proto-gnathosome/proto-vertebrate confusion I then find the rest of the paragraph (line 217 onwards) hard to follow.

comments.issue: The post-1R pre-2R fusions and the non-sharing inference were previously published but are acknowledged only in the supplement.
comments.request: Acknowledge the prior work in the main text.
comments.quote: With regard to the post-1R pre-2R fusions, these have been previously described, but this is only properly acknowledged in the supplement. This paragraph in the main text (line 222 and around) does not acknowledge this. This must be corrected.

comments.issue: The cyclostome data (maximal multiplicity 6, Hox clusters) are consistent with hexaploidy, but CR1+CR2 is favored without discussing this alternative.
comments.request: Analyse the data in light of the hexaploidy hypothesis or present evidence for CR1+CR2.
comments.quote: In the section on cyclostome-specific WGD (line 260 onwards) the data presented are consistent with genome TRIPlication (hexaploidy) as first proposed by Nakatani et al, but these authors do not discuss that.

comments.issue: The WGD dating approach is not conservative because species-tree posteriors constrain the dates; CR1/CR2 dating is inappropriate if CR2 is unsupported.
comments.request: Test dating with priors and show posteriors are diffuse; reconsider CR2 dating.
comments.quote: Dating the polyploidy: the approach is not invalid, but it is not conservative. It is not clear if the approach of using the posterior results from the species tree based dating is entirely appropriate.

comments.issue: Discussion claims about novelty are overstated: cyclostome divergence between 1R and 2R and additional cyclostome polyploidy were already reported.
comments.request: Temper the novelty claims.
comments.quote: In the Discussion (line 378 onwards) some of the claims are overstated in terms of novelty: It was previously demonstrated that cyclostomes diverged after 1R and before 2R; additional polyploidy in cyclostomes has previously been reported.

comments.issue: Studies on paddlefish and sturgeon, which experienced polyploidy without much morphological change, should be noted.
comments.request: Cite these studies in the uncoupling discussion.
comments.quote: With regard to the uncoupling of polyploidy and morphological evolution, note also the studies on paddlefish and sturgeon - sturgeon is one of those with hardly any morphological change yet has experienced polyploidy.

comments.issue: Nakatani was the first to infer 18 proto-vertebrate chromosomes, which should be attributed correctly.
comments.request: Correct the attribution at line 255.
comments.quote: line 255: Nakatani was the first to infer 18 proto-vertebrate chromosomes.

comments.issue: The sentence at line 324 has bad syntax or is incomplete.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: line 324: appears to be an incomplete sentence or bad syntax. Higher than what?

comments.issue: WGD is not always an appropriate acronym because not every polyploidy is a tetraploidy.
comments.request: Use a more appropriate term where needed.
comments.quote: note on nomenclature: WGD refers to 'duplication' but not every polyploidy is tetraploidy. (duplication) so sometimes WGD is not an appropriate acronym

comments.issue: The source of the Hox genes is not cited at line 660.
comments.request: Cite the Hox gene source.
comments.quote: line 660 : cite the study where the Hox genes were sourced

comments.issue: Fig. 4a appears to be missing purple and orange arrows and the legend term 'group' is unclear.
comments.request: Fix the arrows and explain the legend.
comments.quote: Fig 4a is confusing. I wonder if there are missing purple and orange arrows?

comments.issue: Fig. 4 shows only 16 ACs, which is never mentioned elsewhere in the main text.
comments.request: Explain the 16-AC count in the main text.
comments.quote: In fig 4 there are only 16 ACs presented but this is very confusing because there is no mention of there being only 16 anywhere else in the main text

comments.issue: Fig. 5e legend does not explain 'red', 'subf' and 'spec'.
comments.request: Define these terms in the legend.
comments.quote: Fig5e - explain 'red', 'subf' 'spec' in the legend

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits at lines 59 and 61.
comments.quote: line 59: add 'often assumed to be' before 'causally'

reviews.assessment: Highest interest to the journal's readership, but the manuscript needs rewriting for clarity and several analyses need clarification or expansion.
strengths: first hagfish genome analysis of highest interest
clarifies timing of WGDs in early vertebrates

comments.issue: The final genome assembly (v4.0) used for the analyses is not publicly available and accession numbers are missing.
comments.request: Make the assembly public and provide accession numbers.
comments.quote: The final assembly version used for the analyses in this manuscript (v4.0) does not seem to be publicly available yet and accession numbers for this final version are not available as far as I can tell.

comments.issue: Hagfish biology and the reduced cyclostome gene complement are not discussed in detail.
comments.request: Connect the reduced gene complement to hagfish morphological reduction.
comments.quote: I think it would have been interesting to discuss these results in more detail and connect them to the general understanding that cyclostomes and especially hagfishes represent rather morphologically derived and reduced lineages.

comments.issue: Whether the compared assemblies are chromosome-level is not stated; older elephant shark and lamprey assemblies are used.
comments.request: State assembly levels and discuss limitations of the assemblies used.
comments.quote: information should be added whether the included versions of these species are chromosome-level genome assemblies or not.

comments.issue: The WGD nomenclature is inconsistent: CR1/CR2 are the 2nd and 3rd cyclostome WGDs and should be CR2/CR3.
comments.request: Rework the vertebrate WGD nomenclature (e.g. V1R, G2R).
comments.quote: CR1 and CR2 hence are the 2nd and 3rd WGD in the cyclostome lineage and to me, it would make more sense to call them CR2 and CR3, respectively.

comments.issue: No model is provided for how six Hox clusters arose through the three cyclostome WGDs.
comments.request: Build a Hox cluster evolution model using the AC map.
comments.quote: The current study clarifies the orthology of the six hox clusters among cyclostomes. However, I could not find a model of how these six clusters were generated through the three cyclostomes WGDs.

comments.issue: How the conclusion that all non-cyclostome vertebrates are 2R-derived was derived is not clear.
comments.request: Explain the approach in more detail for non-experts.
comments.quote: I found this part particularly difficult to follow and to understand how its major finding was derived. Please discuss your approach in more detail and make it more clear how you derived this major conclusion.

comments.issue: The study does not infer the nature (auto- versus allotetraploidy) of 1R and 2R, although this matters for the morphological argument.
comments.request: Analyse whether the data support allotetraploidization for 2R and autotetraploidization for 1R.
comments.quote: The current study, however, does not make an inference for establishing the nature of the 1R and 2R events. I thus wonder if the current analyses are at least consistent with and/or supporting Simakov’s model?

comments.issue: The hexaploidization model of Nakatani et al. appears at odds with CR1-CR2 but is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss why hexaploidization was rejected.
comments.quote: Nakatani et al. 2021 conclude that following 1R, the extant cyclostome genome was generated by hexaploidization which appears to be at odds with the CR1-CR2 model derived here.

comments.issue: The definition of distal regions and whether they are scaled to genome size is unclear.
comments.request: Define distal regions and any scaling.
comments.quote: I was missing some clarity on the definition of distal regions among the different species analyzed for accessible chromatin regions. Have they been scaled in some way to genome size?

comments.issue: The description of the expected hagfish chromosome number (germline n=26, somatic n=18) is difficult to follow.
comments.request: Revise the karyotype description and expectations.
comments.quote: I found it difficult to understand the description of the expected hagfish chromosome number to which the assembly is matched. Please say it more clearly in the text.

comments.issue: The XY sex determination inference is too preliminary and may miss small sex-determining regions.
comments.request: Expand with sliding-window analyses or remove this part.
comments.quote: I think this part of the genome analysis is too preliminary and should either be expanded (e.g., by a sliding window analysis across clusters to identify potential regions with read-depth differences) or removed from the current study.

comments.issue: The predicted gene number is low and not compared with lamprey gene counts; genes may hide in hard-to-assemble microchromosomes.
comments.request: Compare gene numbers with sea and Arctic lampreys.
comments.quote: l. 109/110: 16,500 predicted genes seem a rather small number compared to gnathostomes. It would be good to compare here to the predicted total gene numbers in Sea and Arctic lampreys.

comments.issue: The statement that hagfish may be a better model than lamprey should be softened to complementary.
comments.request: Rephrase as complementary information.
comments.quote: I’d avoid this statement to say that hagfish may be a better model than lamprey. Later in the text, it is said that lamprey is more suited for other types of analyses (l.245-46).

comments.issue: The data underlying the Bayesian phylogenetic analysis are not stated in the text or Fig. 2 legend.
comments.request: Briefly state the data type used.
comments.quote: l. 144/145: Briefly say what type of data are underlying the Bayesian phylogenetic analysis, even if it is explained in more detail in the supplements or elsewhere. Figure legend 2 also doesn’t provide this information.

comments.issue: 'Lowest amount of gene losses' at line 158 lacks a comparison.
comments.request: Specify what the losses are compared with.
comments.quote: l. 158: lowest amount of gene losses among what?

comments.issue: The '++' notation should be defined at first use.
comments.request: Define '++' as highly retained novel gene families.
comments.quote: also known as novel core genes, i.e., genes that are not lost in descendant lineages, by convention indicated with ++

comments.issue: The text does not say that duplication types are not distinguished in the rate estimates.
comments.request: State that duplication types are not distinguished.
comments.quote: Say more explicitly here that you do not distinguish types of duplication (at least this is my understanding).

comments.issue: The observation at lines 196-197 could be highlighted as evidence for cyclostome monophyly.
comments.request: Make this implication explicit.
comments.quote: You could make it more explicit that this observation is another evidence for cyclostome monophyly.

comments.issue: The last sentence at lines 199-200 is vague and could be deleted.
comments.request: Clarify or delete the sentence.
comments.quote: This last sentence is confusing, as it is so vague – what is the point you want to make here? I think it could also just be deleted.

comments.issue: Whether 'pre-duplicative' means pre-WGD at line 203 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the term.
comments.quote: l. 203: with “pre-duplicative” do you mean “pre-WGD”?

comments.issue: The use of the sea cucumber genome as reference is not justified, and it may not be chromosome-level.
comments.request: Justify this reference choice over other non-vertebrate genomes.
comments.quote: l. 213: provide some justification for the use of the sea cucumber genome as reference here instead of some other possible non-vertebrate genomes

comments.issue: Why the lancelet gene number is mentioned at lines 223-224 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain or delete this information.
comments.quote: l. 223-24: Why is the lancelet gene number brought up, this is confusing. Either explain or delete the info.

comments.issue: Whether AC stands for amphioxus at line 226 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the AC abbreviation.
comments.quote: l. 226: Is AC = amphioxus? Please explain.

comments.issue: The switch to elephant shark as gnathostome representative is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the choice of elephant shark.
comments.quote: l. 233-34: Please explain the switch to elephant shark as gnathostome representative here.

comments.issue: No comparable OR value from another lineage with three WGD rounds (e.g. zebrafish) is given.
comments.request: Provide a comparable OR value.
comments.quote: l. 293: What would be a comparable OR value for a different vertebrate lineage that is derived from 3 rounds of WGD, e.g. in zebrafish?

comments.issue: The comparison at line 324 is not explicit (higher than amphioxus?).
comments.request: State the comparison explicitly.
comments.quote: l. 324, please explicitly say what your comparison is, higher than amphioxus?
