title: Multiple invasion routes have led to the pervasive introduction of earthworms in North America

study.system: plant-pollinator networks; 6-year field data, 12 communities

editor_summary: Editor invites revision after three reviewers raised concerns about circularity between abundance and persistence, unclear definitions of prediction and environmental change, and statistical accounting for repeated samples.

reviews.assessment: Timely and relevant empirical test of network theory, but abundance-driven circularity and insufficient sampling detail undermine its soundness.

comments.issue: Conceptual references are cited for knowledge gaps instead of explicit theory-empiry network studies, and the approach's uniqueness is not stated.
comments.request: Cite explicit theory-empiry studies and state the study's uniqueness.
comments.quote: It would thus be useful to refer specifically to such explicit theory-empiry studies for networks, rather than citing merely conceptual papers as evidence that there are knowledege gaps (Refs 18-20).

comments.issue: The empirical dataset section lacks summary statistics, spatial independence information and sampling details needed to judge quality.
comments.request: Report totals, spatial independence and sampling details in the Dataset section.
comments.quote: The empirical part sounds reasonable and the repeated sampling over six years (similar to Peralta et al. 2020) is a great data source, but lacks sufficent detail typical for emprical studies to evaluate the quality (Methods, Section Dataset).

comments.issue: Abundance may influence network parameters and persistence, inducing circularity for the main hypothesis if not accounted for.
comments.request: Explicitly test the extent to which abundance biases the results.
comments.quote: If so and if not properly accounted for, population abundance might induce a circularity for the main hypothesis that network properties stabilize populations

comments.issue: Opposing published views on the stabilizing function of nestedness, including connectance and abundance effects, are not addressed.
comments.request: Address the opposing views on nestedness and connectance.
comments.quote: On the proposed stabilizing function of “nestedness” there are also opposing views published in several papers, as it may mirror effects of connectance instead and because nestedness per se is a pattern driven by unequal abundances and neutrality.

comments.issue: Abundance and interaction frequency are assumed independent without demonstration, and Appendix D's abundance-persistence evidence is not critically discussed.
comments.request: Show the abundance-frequency relationship and discuss the circularity risk critically.
comments.quote: evidence for the relationship between abundance and persistence is shown in the Appendix D, but not picked up critically in the amin text; circularly would apply if the network parameters as such are similarly influenced by abundance

reviews.assessment: Cool study bridging empirical and theoretical network ecology, but circularity, vague 'environmental change' wording and repeated-sample statistics raise big concerns.
strengths: well-written and a pleasure to read

comments.issue: It is unclear whether model predictions are compared with independent data; aggregated yearly pollinator abundance is not independent of the fitted dataset.
comments.request: Use independent data or measures, such as pan traps, to test predictions.
comments.quote: Are you using the complete dataset to generate the results or are you using part of the dataset and then comparing the model prediction with the other, independent part, of the dataset?

comments.issue: Abundance is normalized by sampling effort only; estimators controlling for unobserved species are not used.
comments.request: Consider Chao abundance estimators or similar controls.
comments.quote: I wonder why the authors did not include additional controlling methods such as using the Chao abundance estimator or other metrics that control for potential unobserved species.

comments.issue: The headline result claims tolerance to environmental changes, but only temporal persistence is measured.
comments.request: Clarify how environmental change is measured or reword the claim.
comments.quote: it is unclear how the author measures environmental changes. From what I understand, it is more about temporal persistence not so much about environmental changes

comments.issue: Statements such as clearly distinguishing which species will persist or die out are far-fetched and unsupported.
comments.request: Focus on specific results and temper broad claims.
comments.quote: broad, empty statements such as “we can clearly distinguish which communities and which particular species will persist or will die out in the face of ever-present environmental variation”, but can we really?

comments.issue: Figure 1 legend and panel definitions of gamma conflict (empirical observations versus mutualistic gain), as do alpha definitions.
comments.request: Reconcile the gamma and alpha definitions between legend and figure.
comments.quote: In the legend gamma is defined as “Empirical observations determine the mutualistic interactions of our dynamical model”, but in the figure, it’s labeled as mutualistic gain. These are two different definitions, no?

comments.issue: Panel 2 states 'intra-guild' although empirical data were collected only for bees.
comments.request: Clarify the intra-guild terminology relative to the bee data.
comments.quote: In panel 2 it is stated “intra-guild” but the empirical data collected was only in regards to bees (according to line 264 in the methods). Can you please clarify?

comments.issue: Panel c shows higher reproductive rates associated with lower persistence, which appears counterintuitive.
comments.request: Clarify the panel c result.
comments.quote: According to the figure species with higher reproductive rates have a lower probability of persistence, which seems somewhat counterintuitive to me. Am I interpreting this wrong?

comments.issue: Correlations in Figure 2 ignore repeated samples; a mixed-effects model with species and site random effects may be more appropriate.
comments.request: Use mixed-effects models accounting for repeated samples.
comments.quote: First, I wonder if a mixed-effects model with a random effect of species and sites be more appropriate than a correlation. How are you accounting for repeated samples, that is, species that are seen in more than one site?

comments.issue: Figure 2 panel A points and the special status of site 12 are unclear, as is how repeated samples are handled.
comments.request: Improve the panel A legend and clarify repeated samples.
comments.quote: If this is correct, what I understand from the figure is that “site 12” (the last point in the upper right corner) has an overall higher average of pollinator probability of persistence in two years.

comments.issue: Figure 3 legend does not say dots are communities, and 'species richness' versus 'realized pollinator number' is inconsistent.
comments.request: State what dots represent and use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: I assume each dot is a community, but it should be stated in the legend. Also, in the text, it says "species richness" (line 204) but here it says realized pollinator number. Which one is it?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether species richness was controlled for and whether z-scores of nestedness were used; how nestedness is measured is not stated.
comments.request: Control for richness and explain how nestedness is measured.
comments.quote: Did you control for species richness for these results? It is a well-established pattern that larger habitat paths have a greater number of species, and that richness has a direct impact on nestedness, with larger networks usually being more nested.

comments.issue: How the variables at L201-206 are measured is not explained.
comments.request: Provide more information on measuring these variables.
comments.quote: L. 201-206. How to measure all these variables? I believe a bit more of information here would be helpful to the reader.

comments.quote: Finally, I would like to suggest that the authors take a look at Gaiarsa et al. (2021). These authors use a different approach to explore similar questions in relation to species persistence in ecological networks.

significant results for understanding early H. sapiens environments

comments.issue: 'Multi-stable isotope record' in the abstract is unclear and inconsistent.

comments.issue: Starting the sentence on lines 130-131 with 'otherwise' is confusing.

comments.issue: It is unclear which tissues were analysed for each isotope, with essential details left to the supplement.

comments.issue: It is unclear which values in the results and figures come from mandibular bone collagen rather than tooth dentine.

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not include GRIP or NGRIP records for comparison.

comments.issue: The full species name should be used at first mention on line 57.

comments.issue: Other environmental proxies supporting the open steppe interpretation are not referenced.

comments.quote: Are there other environmental proxies that can also be referred to support the hypothesis of an open steppe environment?

comments.issue: Isotope notation on line 326 is informal.

comments.issue: 'Tooth enamel specimens' would be a better term on line 327.

comments.quote: Line 327- ‘Tooth enamel specimens’ would be a better term to use here.

title: Stable isotopes show Homo sapiens dispersed into cold steppes ~45,000 years ago at Ilsenhöhle in Ranis, Germany

study.system: ancient DNA; medieval Soqotri people, Soqotra Island

editor_summary: Reviewers raised concerns that must be addressed before publication, along with editorial concerns; authors must respond to the criticisms and highlight all changes.

reviews.assessment: Valuable, well-written study of an underrepresented region, but the results are overlong and several inferences need more measured treatment.
strengths: valuable insights into an underrepresented region

comments.issue: Results section is too long and embeds discussion and interpretation, leaving the Discussion unengaging.
comments.request: Restructure the text, moving interpretive material to the Discussion.
comments.quote: Overall, I find the results section somewhat lengthy, with an excess of detailed discussion and interpretation embedded within it.

comments.issue: qpADM framework and specialized aDNA tools such as pairwise qpWave are not explained, making the text inaccessible to non-specialists.
comments.request: Briefly describe the analytical frameworks and tools used.
comments.quote: Within the main text, the author leverage from previous studies to outline the framework employed for the qpADM analyses, yet without providing even a brief description of what the framework entails.

comments.issue: Supplementary materials lack legends, for example Data Supp 5 and 6, so designations such as S1, S2, ANC1 and ANC2 are hard to understand.
comments.request: Add legends to the supplementary data files.
comments.quote: the lack of legend in Data Supp 5 and 6, make readers' understanding of designations like S1, S2, ANC1, and ANC2 difficult

comments.issue: No guidance is given on interpreting the ranges of significant p-values in Table 1.
comments.request: Explain how to interpret the p-value ranges.
comments.quote: There is also a lack of guidance on interpreting the various ranges of significant p-values in Table 1.

comments.issue: Population IDs such as ISR_Natufian_EpiP and TUR_Barcin_N are used throughout instead of intuitive names.
comments.request: Use intuitive population names in the main text.
comments.quote: I would find it more preferable to encounter more intuitive identifier within the main text of the full terms like "Neolithic Anatolian farmers".

comments.issue: A difference in ancestry proportions is used to favour one hypothesis of distinct farmer lineages over equally plausible alternatives.
comments.request: Explain the preference or reframe to accommodate multiple scenarios.
comments.quote: I recommend the authors to provide more comprehensive explanations for their inclination toward a particular hypothesis over others or consider reframing the text to accommodate multiple potential scenario

comments.issue: The strongest-evidence-to-date claim overstates the contribution; incomplete replacement is already evident from prior genetic studies.
comments.request: Temper the claim and its centrality in the paper.
comments.quote: The use of "strongest evidence to date" suggests that this inference is a central focus of the study, whereas I believe it doesn’t hold much relevance in the context of this study

comments.issue: Wording confines Natufian presence to the Pleistocene, although isolated Natufian-related groups may have persisted longer.
comments.request: Revise the wording to allow persistence beyond the Pleistocene.
comments.quote: the wording seems to confine the Natufians' presence to the Pleistocene era, overlooking the intricacies and nuances that might extend beyond a rigid timeframe

comments.issue: Uniparental marker results are scattered through the main text to support other inferences instead of being reported properly.
comments.request: Dedicate a separate paragraph to sex determination and uniparental markers.
comments.quote: However, these observations have been introduced briefly here and there in the main text to support other inferences, yet they warrant a more thorough examination.

comments.issue: The main text features the Karitiana-outgroup f3 statistics rather than the more comprehensive Mbuti-outgroup overview.
comments.request: Present the broader f3-statistics overview in the main text.
comments.quote: it would be more relevant to present in the main text more comprehensive f3-stats overview

comments.issue: A noteworthy affinity between medieval Soqotri and South Italy/Sardinia populations under the Mbuti outgroup is not mentioned or explored.
comments.request: Mention and explore the South Italy and Sardinia connection.
comments.quote: there is a noteworthy connection between medieval Soqotri and populations from South Italy and Sardinia that hasn’t been mentioned by the authors and merit further exploration

comments.issue: The manuscript has no line numbers, making commenting difficult.
comments.request: Add line numbers.
comments.quote: A bit challenging to report comments with no line numeration.

comments.issue: The abstract ending is incoherent and the last sentence is unnecessary.
comments.request: Revise or remove the abstract's final sentence.
comments.quote: I think the ending of the abstract is a bit incoherent. The last sentence required more perspectives in order for the reader to get its relevance. I don’t think that last sentence is needed.

comments.issue: Mention of the Periplus and the Christian Topography is confusing and adds nothing.
comments.request: Remove or clarify this mention.
comments.quote: there is mention of the Periplus and his Christian Topography which I think is a confusing details that doesn't bring anything to the study

comments.issue: The statement that skeletal material was collected to minimize disruption to burials is too vague to describe the sampling strategy.
comments.request: Give more sampling details or remove the sentence.
comments.quote: while this is important aspect of the sampling, it is very vague. I suggest the authors to give more details about the sampling strategy or to remove the sentence.

comments.issue: Family color codes in Figure 1 are hard to distinguish and tafone age is not shown; there is a typo in the legend.
comments.request: Improve colors, add tafone age, fix the typo.
comments.quote: The color code used for families in Figure 1 could be improved, as distinguishing between Family 1 and Family 4 is challenging

comments.issue: The sentence about gene flow in the last centuries is incomprehensible.
comments.request: Rewrite or explain this sentence.
comments.quote: I was not able to comprehend the following sentence

comments.issue: However introduces a contradiction between two statements where none is apparent.
comments.request: Clarify the logical structure of the sentence.
comments.quote: In that sentence, “However” is used to introduce a contradiction, but I don’t see any contradiction between both statement which confusing me

comments.issue: The relevance of the Iberomaurusian affinity of ISR_Natufian_EpiP is unclear and causes confusion.
comments.request: Explain the relevance or remove the statement.
comments.quote: I did not get the relevance of mentioning that the ISR_Natufian_EpiP exhibits an affinity to 15,000-year-old Iberomaurusian hunter-gatherers from Morocco.

comments.issue: The Arab slave trade example is not straightforward; how slavery both restricts and maintains Y lineages is unclear.
comments.request: Replace or explain the slave trade example.
comments.quote: I'm struggling to understand how slavery could both restrict the spread and yet maintain in the gene pool additional Y lineages at the same time.

comments.issue: A max Z of 4.3 is described as marginally passing the significance threshold, which understates it.
comments.request: Edit the sentence to reflect the strong significance.
comments.quote: I think a Z=4.3 is not marginally significant, it is already quite significant. The authors might want to edit that sentence.

comments.issue: Overlap in Figure 3A between real data and simulated first-cousin offspring is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the overlap seen in Figure 3A.
comments.quote: In Fig. 3A there seems to be an overlap between the real data and some simulated points of people who are children of first cousins. But I could not find an explanation for that observation in the main text.

comments.issue: The claim that traders and mariners did not contribute to gene pools contradicts the reported 14% Iranian-related and 2% Indian-related ancestry.
comments.request: Resolve the contradiction in the discussion.
comments.quote: I find these statements somewhat contradictory. Even though 14% and 2% are minor in comparison to the Natufians/Anatolian ancestry, it is still quite significant.

comments.issue: The meaning of reporting negative results in Supplementary Data 1 to prevent duplicative efforts is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I understand what it means.

reviews.assessment: Contributes to understanding past migrations but reports no groundbreaking discoveries and raises doubts about coverage, ROH reliability and reference populations.
strengths: new contribution to understanding past migrations and matrimonial exchanges in Southern Arabia

comments.issue: Sequencing coverage obtained from the Soqotri bones is not reported, and coverage is used loosely for targeted SNP data.
comments.request: Report the coverage values and clarify the term.
comments.quote: Coverage – it is not clear which coverage was obtained from the Soqotri bones.

comments.issue: If coverage is low, heterozygous variant detection is uncertain, so the ROH-based first-cousin inference may be unreliable.
comments.request: Show that low coverage does not compromise the ROH analysis.
comments.quote: Therefore, I wonder whether the analysis concerning the ROH (first cousin union) is based on reliable ground.

comments.issue: Ancestry is modelled with modern Yemeni_Desert, which may have received later inputs; an ancient Near Eastern reference might be more appropriate.
comments.request: Test modelling with an ancient reference population.
comments.quote: can be modern populations replaced by an ancient population living close by in the Near East?

comments.issue: The Community Engagement paragraph belongs in Materials and Methods rather than Results.
comments.request: Move the Community Engagement paragraph.
comments.quote: I think the paragraph reporting this should not be a part of the Results section, but rather Material and Methods.

comments.issue: Southern Oman does not border Hadramawt; it borders Al Mahrah.
comments.request: Correct the geography statement.
comments.quote: Southern Oman did not border Hadramawt but Al Mahrah.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the correct spelling is Karaitiana or Karitiana in Figure 1B and its legend.
comments.request: Correct the spelling of Karitiana.
comments.quote: Karaitiana or Karitiana? See Figure 1B and legend.

comments.issue: The carat symbol described for Figure 2B is not visible; only crosses and stars appear.
comments.request: Clarify or correct the Figure 2B symbols.
comments.quote: Figure 2B - what is “carat symbol” I can see simply crosses and stars.

comments.issue: The mtDNA haplogroup R2c was previously identified on Soqotra and reclassified under mtDNA tree Build 17.
comments.request: Update the haplogroup classification and cite the prior study.
comments.quote: In fact, R2c mtDNA haplogroup was identified in Soqotri island, see JX155271 previously determined as R2b2 Al-Abri A. et al.

comments.issue: Soqotri legends linked to Indian mythology also support links between Soqotra and India but are not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention the Soqotri legends and cite Botting (1958).
comments.quote: Links between Soqotra and India can be revealed also in some Soqotri legends related with Indian mythology, see Botting D. (1958).

comments.issue: Linguistic groupings may structure genetic relationships among South Arabian versus Arabic speakers but are not checked in the dataset.
comments.request: Check linguistic groupings in the genetic dataset.
comments.quote: It seems that peoples speaking South Arabian languages show some genetic differences in relationships to the Arabic speaking populations. Please, check this in your dataset.

comments.issue: Sex segregation should be examined chronologically because tafoni may have been reused after long periods, so burial contemporaneity is uncertain.
comments.request: Examine the sex segregation by chronology.
comments.quote: were all the samples of both sexes in the seven caves concerned buried at the same time?

comments.issue: Calling early Soqotri genetic affinities a mystery is wrong because several prior genetic studies found practically the same results.
comments.request: Acknowledge the prior genetic studies and revise the wording.
comments.quote: I really do not know if a “mystery” is right word because several genetic studies dealt with the population history of the Soqotra and showed practically the same results

comments.issue: The Introduction deals only with archaeology and lacks a paragraph on previous population-genetic studies of South Arabia.
comments.request: Add a paragraph on prior population-genetic studies.
comments.quote: A paragraph about previous population genetic studies in South Arabia might be added to the Introduction that it now dealing only with archaeological research.

comments.issue: Whole genome analysis is inaccurate because no whole genomes are in the dataset; genome-wide should be used.
comments.request: Use the term genome-wide analysis.
comments.quote: “whole genome analysis” or genome-wide analysis? Use genome-wide as you have no whole genomes in your datasets.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting article with commendable community engagement; offers minor archaeological, linguistic and terminological corrections.
strengths: careful consideration of Soqotran community sensitivities
close involvement of Soqotri men and women in the collection
important findings on mixed-sex burial and gene pool stability

comments.issue: The sentence about returning the dead to their home village should say home burial area; there is no evidence of interior villages.
comments.request: Revise the sentence to refer to the home burial area.
comments.quote: so (p.14) “if a member of a tribe died away from their village, they would be brought back to their home village to be buried if at all possible” should perhaps rather read

comments.issue: The gloss and etymology of the term tafoni may be incorrect; it more likely derives from √dfˀ or √dfn.
comments.request: Have the Soqotri team check the term in Arabic characters.
comments.quote: I would suggest that it is more likely to be derived from either √dfˀ ‘to block off, up, stuff, stop up (as hole, entrance)’, or √dfn ‘to bury; to cache’

comments.issue: The claim of a cultural preference for cousin marriage is not adequately demonstrated by the Naumkin table figures.
comments.request: Provide better evidence or qualify the claim.
comments.quote: the figures given in the table [Table S6. Recreation of Table 7.1 (Forms of Marriage) from Naumkin do not necessarily show this.

comments.issue: 2 line-level typos/wording problems on p. 9 and p. 14.
comments.quote: This practice of burying relatives in caves was reported to reflect family members having no strength left to dig graves due of epidemics or drought.

title: Medieval DNA from Soqotra points to Eurasian origins of an isolated population at the crossroads of Africa and Arabia

study.system: British birds, butterflies and plants; 50-year biodiversity records, land use and climate

editor_summary: Reviewers find the data valuable and impressive but raise major concerns about the advance over earlier work and the novel conclusions: robustness of models and uncertainty treatment (R1, R2) and insufficient exploration of climate-land-use interactions (R3).

reviews.assessment: Interesting study with relevant results, but major concerns about analysis robustness, presentation and interpretation.
strengths: many results relevant to the field

comments.issue: The butterfly CTI decrease is likely not robust due to recording bias (CI spanning 0) and collinearity, so those models may need excluding.
comments.request: Consider excluding the corresponding models and results.
comments.quote: So, I can’t help but question whether you should exclude the corresponding models and results from your work, as they come across as possibly not robust.

comments.issue: 'Baseline conditions' are not clearly defined in the main text, including whether baseline biodiversity was considered.
comments.request: Define baseline conditions clearly in the main text.
comments.quote: I think what the baseline conditions are needs to be defined in a clear way in the main text, given their importance in your analyses and results.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether microclimatic heterogeneity was a main aim or just a control.
comments.request: Clarify the role of microclimatic heterogeneity.
comments.quote: It is not clear to me whether investigating the effects of microclimatic heterogeneity on biodiversity change was one of the main aims of the study

comments.issue: The 'Dealing with collinearity' paragraph, especially its first point, is difficult to follow.
comments.request: Make the collinearity methods section very clear.
comments.quote: I found that some places a bit difficult to follow – in particular, the first point of the paragraph “Dealing with collinearity” line 643.

comments.issue: The synthesis figures do not show effect sizes.
comments.request: Display model effects, e.g. change figure 2 to show effect sizes.
comments.quote: Although I do appreciate the synthesis effort with figures 2, 3, 4, I would have liked to see some of the effect sizes.

comments.issue: The main limitations of the study are not highlighted.
comments.request: Highlight the main limitations in the discussion.
comments.quote: I suggest highlighting some of the main limitations of your study in the discussion part.

comments.issue: 'Land-use' is hyphenated even when not used as a compound adjective.
comments.request: Hyphenate 'land-use' only as a compound adjective.
comments.quote: I recommend hyphenating “land-use” only when used as a compound adjective (land-use change), not hyphenating otherwise.

comments.issue: It is unclear what is meant by land-use change being inferred using proxies.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning and the proxy types.
comments.quote: Line 27: “land-use change is generally inferred using proxies”- this is unclear to me.

comments.issue: The baseline environmental conditions are not specified at line 33.
comments.request: Specify the baseline conditions.
comments.quote: Line 33: maybe specify what these baseline environmental conditions are

comments.issue: 'Lower rates of biodiversity loss' seems to contradict the abstract's finding of increased richness.
comments.request: Reconcile the two statements.
comments.quote: “lower rates of biodiversity loss”: one of the main results presented in the abstract is increases in species richness, which seems to contradict this statement partly

comments.issue: The abstract ends without highlighting implications of the work.
comments.request: Conclude the abstract with key implications.
comments.quote: I wonder if you could conclude the abstract with a few words highlighting some important implications of your work.

comments.issue: Williams et al. (2019) on CTI across land-use types is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Williams et al. (2019).
comments.quote: Also see the work by Williams et al. (2019) on CTI in different land-use types

comments.issue: The distinction between climate warming and microclimate is not clarified.
comments.request: Highlight that land use affects local microclimatic conditions.
comments.quote: I suggest highlighting that this is due to land use affecting local, microclimatic conditions to clarify the distinction between climate warming and microclimate

comments.issue: Examples of the proxies used by other studies are not given.
comments.request: Add examples contrasting this study with proxy-based studies.
comments.quote: Line 74: what kind of proxies? Maybe add a few examples that can highlight how different your study is from these other studies based on proxies.

comments.issue: The number of considered species is not displayed.
comments.request: Display the sample sizes in the main text or a figure.
comments.quote: somewhere in the main text, I suggest displaying the sample sizes (number of considered species) – (or maybe in one of the figures?)

comments.issue: What biodiversity resilience means here is not defined.
comments.request: Define the resilience metric.
comments.quote: Line 85: what is biodiversity resilience here? Do you focus on a specific metric?

comments.issue: Lines 87 and 88 about mixed-effects models could be merged for brevity.
comments.request: Merge the two statements.
comments.quote: Lines 87 and 88: mixed-“effects” models. You could merge for brevity

comments.issue: It is unclear whether microclimate and baseline biodiversity are controlled in all models or only those for point (2).
comments.request: State which models include these controls.
comments.quote: Line 93/94: do you control for these in all the models, or just the models built to investigate point (2)?

comments.issue: 'Loss of spatial heterogeneity' at line 100 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: Line 100: unclear to me what is meant by “loss of spatial heterogeneity” here

comments.issue: The thermal niche underlying CTI is not explained in the main text.
comments.request: Explain the thermal niche and CTI more in the main text.
comments.quote: I think you also need to explain a bit more in the main text what the thermal niche of a species is here

comments.issue: The meaning of the results at lines 106-108 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what these results mean.
comments.quote: Line 106-108: what do these results mean?

comments.issue: The phrase 'consistent with a response to anthropogenic environmental change' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: “were consistent with a response to anthropogenic environmental change” I’m not sure what is meant by that

comments.issue: Results are described as strong determinants and driving mechanisms although the study is correlative.
comments.request: Report results as correlative.
comments.quote: I suggest reporting results as correlative, because your study doesn’t investigate mechanisms

comments.issue: 'And the changes that occurred' is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify whether environmental changes are meant.
comments.quote: here, do you mean changes in environmental conditions?

comments.issue: How enhanced stability was determined and how stability and resilience are defined is unclear.
comments.request: Define stability and resilience.
comments.quote: “enhanced stability”: how did you determine that? What is your definition of stability (and also resilience, elsewhere)

comments.issue: It is unclear whether improved and semi-natural grasslands are baseline conditions at line 141.
comments.request: Clarify the role of this category.
comments.quote: Line 141: “improved and semi-natural grasslands” here, as baseline conditions, right?

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits (stray letters, missing plurals, inconsistent Greek letters, duplicated wording).
comments.quote: Line 197 – delete the d in “land-use changed”

comments.issue: The possible role of biological invasions in richness increases is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether invasions partly explain richness increases.
comments.quote: Could observed increases in species richness partly be explained by biological invasions?

comments.issue: Using a 1930 survey to represent the 1960s land use may have drawbacks.

comments.quote: Do you mean that for the 1960 time period you approximate land use from the 1930s survey? Are there any drawbacks from using a 1930 survey for a period of time centred around the 1960s?

comments.issue: Different spatial autocorrelation approaches (Leroux, iCAR) are used across model sets without justification.
comments.request: Explain why different approaches were used for different models.
comments.quote: Why were these different approaches used for the species richness model and for the beta-diversity and CTI models (in models 1, 2 and 3)?

comments.issue: The spatial autocorrelation paragraph should be merged and does not describe the assessment as stated.
comments.request: Merge with the line 513 paragraph and clarify the basis for inclusion choices.
comments.quote: I suggest merging this paragraph with the paragraph on spatial autocorrelation line 513.

comments.issue: Recorder effort is included differently across the three model sets without explanation.
comments.request: Explain the differing treatment of recorder effort.
comments.quote: Why is recorder effort including differently in the first sets of models (1,2,3), in the second set of 18 models (597-602), and in the last model (line 693)?

comments.issue: What 'interpreted the results with caution' means for the results is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the consequences of the caution.
comments.quote: Line 628 “and interpreted the results with caution” I’m not sure what this means for the results

comments.issue: Why semi-natural grassland was excluded from the models after residualizing other covers is unclear.
comments.request: Explain why semi-natural grassland was not included.
comments.quote: I’m not clear with what “semi-natural grassland remained unregressed” mean.

comments.issue: Whether 'a species-poor site' means few but functionally unique species is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: Line 683- “a species-poor site”, with few but functionally unique species?

reviews.assessment: Exceptionally valuable dataset but findings are not novel and the key climate-land-use interaction is underdelivered; many presentation fixes needed.
strengths: methods sufficiently described to reproduce results
appropriate handling of spatial autocorrelation and collinearity

comments.issue: The findings are not novel and the climate-land-use interaction that would set the study apart is mostly neglected.
comments.request: Explore and present the climate-land-use interactions throughout the paper.
comments.quote: these findings are not novel, and – unfortunately – the one aspect which would have set this study apart from similar studies was mostly neglected in most parts of the paper

comments.issue: Main figures do not show data distributions, effect sizes or uncertainty, and legends are missing information.
comments.request: Show distributions, effect sizes and uncertainty in the figures.
comments.quote: the figures in the main paper do not show how the data was distributed, how large effects were and which uncertainty they had

comments.issue: Small differences may be statistically significant yet ecologically meaningless given the large sample sizes.
comments.request: Discuss biological significance alongside statistical significance.
comments.quote: even small differences may turn out to be “significant” if the sample size is large enough (which it probably is here)

comments.issue: The summary emphasizes climate-land-use interactions, but the rest of the paper does not meet those expectations.
comments.request: Align the summary with the delivered results.
comments.quote: The summary captures the main aspects of the manuscript, yet also puts a lot of emphasize on climate-land use interactions.

comments.issue: Terminology alternates between land-use/land use, climate-change/climate change, and similar pairs.
comments.request: Use one consistent convention.

title: Anthropogenic climate and land-use change drive short- and long-term biodiversity shifts across taxa

study.system: Lepidoptera; 210 chromosomally complete genomes

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers find the revision improved and the paper will be accepted in principle pending minor revisions and compliance with editorial and formatting guidelines.

reviews.assessment: Thanks the authors; the paper is improved and more balanced, with only a few remaining minor items.
strengths: addition of an additional chromosomal reconstruction method and bootstrap attempts

comments.issue: Supplementary Fig. 7 does not support calling Merian elements 'highly rearranged'; it shows clear correspondence with bilaterian linkage groups.
comments.request: Correct the statement about the degree of rearrangement.
comments.quote: from the Supplementary Figure 7 it is not correctly to say that the Merian elements are “highly rearranged”

comments.issue: A dotplot of ortholog distribution along chromosomes is needed to show how orthogroups map to Merian elements.
comments.request: Add a dotplot of ortholog distribution along the chromosomes.

comments.issue: The statement that Merian elements are 'distinct from, but retain signatures consistent with, the BLGs' is unclear, and the BLG-element correspondence is not specified.
comments.request: Clarify this statement and state which BLGs contribute to which Merian elements.
comments.quote: What does this mean, are they distinct or show retained signatures? If they show retained signatures, which BLGs contribute to which Merian elements?

comments.issue: The degree of 'breakage' that would warrant naming rearranged chromosomes neo-Merian elements is not defined.

comments.issue: The rationale for the name 'Merian elements' is not explained.

comments.quote: a short explanation as to why you call these linkages “Merian elements” might be useful

comments.issue: The 'uniform distribution' null expectation may be inappropriate given species sampling and evolutionary rate differences among taxa.

comments.quote: this might be primarily affected by the species sampling and evolutionary rates within each taxon that you study, as such the “uniform distribution” might not be the right null expectation

reviews.assessment: Satisfied that previous comments were addressed; the paper is much improved and an important step forward.
strengths: important step forward for comparative genomics of insect chromosome evolution

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the more thorough analyses and finds the manuscript improved, but the novelty of the findings is still overstated.
strengths: more thorough assessments of the Merian elements

comments.issue: The text claims 'discovery' of small chromosomes driving genome reorganization, but the pattern was previously published (e.g. Ahola et al. 2014).
comments.request: Reframe the findings as refining previous discoveries rather than discoveries.
comments.quote: In sum, your work does not “discover” that small fusions drive evol change, but rather refines previous discoveries by documenting the extent of a previously described pattern from both butterflies and moths.

title: Comparative genomics reveals the dynamics of chromosome evolution in Lepidoptera

study.system: eucalyptus seedlings, wallabies; odour-dispenser field experiment

editor_summary: Editor asks to tone down the paper: discuss management implications more cautiously given limited scalability, remove grandiose statements like "a huge leap forward", and acknowledge that findings are system-specific.

reviews.assessment: Novel, well-designed study with broad interest; only suggestions for making results more accessible and fully reported.
strengths: interest to ecologists and land managers
well designed study with adequately described methods

comments.issue: Most results are confined to supplementary materials and should be moved into the manuscript.
comments.request: Move key supplementary figures and tables into the main text.
comments.quote: Most of the results are in supplementary data. Unless there is a space limitation on the manuscript, I would recommend moving some of the results from supplementary figures and tables into the manuscript.

comments.issue: VOC results for Boronia pinnata are not reported in detail, including sampling date and wild versus greenhouse differences.
comments.request: Report VOC variation by site, season and rearing in a supplementary table.
comments.quote: The results of VOC analysis of Boronia pinnata are not reported in detail.

comments.issue: The wallaby density value is not given where the no-difference result is reported.
comments.request: Report the actual wallaby density.
comments.quote: Line 135 when it is reported that there was no difference in wallaby density across treatments report the wallaby density.

comments.issue: How the proportion of consumed biomass was quantified is unclear, and 97 percent seems implausible from camera data.

comments.quote: Lines 333-334 states that the proportion of E. puctata biomass consumed after first browsing visit was quantified. How was it quantified? Based on the camera data?

comments.issue: Results of the analysis of treatment and background wallaby activity on browsing at first visit are not reported.

comments.quote: Lines 354-357 describes the analysis of the effect of treatment and background wallaby activity on the proportion of palatable seedling browsed at first browsing visit but I cannot find where those results are reported.

comments.issue: Plots without wallaby camera records were removed from analysis, but whether any plots were actually removed is not stated.
comments.request: State whether any plots were removed from the analysis.
comments.quote: Line 341-342 state that any plots where wallabies were not recorded on camera traps either during the pre-trial period or main trial were removed from analysis.

reviews.assessment: Nicely written and thorough study, with a few methodological questions that need more context.
strengths: thorough investigation of plant chemistry as a mechanism

comments.issue: Whether the VOC-pair method is novel or already used in other systems is unclear, and the cited Webster et al. 2010 may not mention VOC pairs.
comments.request: Clarify the method's provenance and whether it has only been used in Eucalyptus.
comments.quote: I might have missed something but I can't find a mention of VOC pairs in the cited Webster et al. 2010. This is an interesting method, but it should be made clear if it has only been used in Eucalyptus.

comments.issue: It is unclear why final compound concentrations were not based on average proportions in the original data and why extra trials were needed.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for the chosen concentrations and extra trials.
comments.quote: I'm unclear on why the final concentrations of those compounds are not just based on the average proportions in the original data.

comments.issue: The effect size of the virtual neighbourhood should be reported relative to the procedural control.

comments.quote: Although the untreated control and procedural control are equivalent statistically, the effect size of the 'virtual neighborhood' should still be presented relative to the procedural control.

comments.issue: How the average dry weight of seedlings was determined is unclear.
comments.request: Report whether average dry weight came from prior trials.
comments.quote: L269: The plants are stated to be the same starting biomass, and I am assuming this is how biomass loss was calculated (L334). Was the average dry weight determined through prior trials?

reviews.assessment: Fascinating, elegant experiment, but the findings may be specific to this system and should not be over-generalised.
strengths: fascinating evidence for virtual plant effects
important control measurements of exact volatile proportions
well written with a nice narrative

comments.issue: Findings may be specific to this location and wallaby colony; odour combinations vary among plant populations.
comments.request: Be careful about generalising the findings beyond this system.
comments.quote: while the evidence for this particular study system is convincing, I would be careful with generalising the findings

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits (capitalisation of chemical names, awkward sentences, wording).

comments.issue: The day/night comparison appears without rationale or underlying hypothesis.

comments.issue: Claiming transferability to any vertebrate or invertebrate herbivore is doubtful, since species use different cues.

comments.issue: The paragraph at 154ff contains redundant statements and could be shortened.

comments.issue: The total number of wallaby individuals monitored is not reported.

comments.issue: The green and purple colours in Figure 1 are hard to differentiate.

comments.issue: Describing the effect as degraded "quality" may be wrong; it may reflect repellent odours without affecting quality.

comments.issue: What "x5" means in the Figure 2 and supplementary table 2 legend is unclear.

title: Olfactory misinformation provides refuge to palatable plants from mammalian browsing

study.system: Early Ordovician Cabrières Lagerstätte; soft-bodied fossils and taxonomy

editor_summary: Reviewers are enthusiastic about the contribution but feel the presentation, taxonomy and imaging need further work before publication.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting, significant new polar fauna; asks for more reserved preservation claims, stratigraphy and better figure clarity.
strengths: well presented new deposit with immense paleogeographic significance
well written and significantly increases knowledge of Ordovician diversity

comments.issue: Information from Extended Data Figure 2 is not in the text and the number of soft-bodied or soft-tissue taxa is not quantified.
comments.request: Move this information into the text and quantify the taxa.
comments.quote: It would be nice if the information from Extended Data Figure 2 would actually be in the text, as well as some quantification on how many taxa are soft-bodied or preserve soft-tissues.

comments.issue: Many figured soft-bodied fossils are incomplete or lack fine structures, so calling them exceptional is overstated.
comments.request: Use 'exceptional' more reservedly and distinguish it from soft-tissue preservation.
comments.quote: Many of the soft-bodied fossils that are figured are not really exceptionally preserved, as they are not complete

comments.issue: A detailed stratigraphy of the outcrop showing where soft-bodied fossils occur is missing.
comments.request: Add a stratigraphic figure in the style of Yang et al. 2021.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to have a detailed stratigraphy of the outcrop/outcrops highlighting the fossil occurrences?

comments.issue: Kimmig et al. 2019's updated Ordovician soft-bodied fossil chart and Moysiuk et al. 2022 are not cited.
comments.request: Consider adding these references.
comments.quote: Kimmig et al. 2019 Science of Nature had an updated version of Van Roys Stratigraphic chart showing the occurrences of soft-bodied fossils in the Ordovician, might be worth adding.

comments.issue: 'Exceptional biota/s' should be replaced by wording about biota preserving soft-bodied animals.
comments.request: Use the suggested phrasing from line 75 onward.
comments.quote: Line 75 and after: biota/s preserving soft-bodied animals instead of exceptional biota/s

comments.issue: The thickness, extent and number of preservation horizons are not described.
comments.request: Provide information on the preservation horizon.
comments.quote: Do you have any information on how thick the preservation horizon is, how far it extends, if there are different horizons preserving the soft-bodied fauna?

comments.issue: Lines 173-186 lack quantification.
comments.request: Add quantification for the reader.
comments.quote: Line 173-186: Some sort of quantification would help the reader here.

comments.issue: Indicated structures in the figures, especially Figure 5, are hard to see.
comments.request: Increase picture size or add close-ups.
comments.quote: many of the indicated structures are difficult to see. This is especially the case in Figure 5, were many of the indicated structures are not easily identifiable.

reviews.assessment: Clearly arranged, well written and well illustrated; results sufficiently backed, with only very minor changes attached.
strengths: results sufficiently backed with available data
good contribution to knowledge of this preservation type

reviews.assessment: Deserves publication but the iconic taxa and unique polar composition claims are not convincingly shown.
strengths: provides insights into Ordovician marine ecosystems

comments.issue: The manuscript fails to show iconic taxa, and the reported taxa are common across Cambrian-Ordovician Lagerstätten.
comments.request: Present the iconic taxa and strengthen the evidence for the polar ecosystem characteristics.
comments.quote: The manuscript was well written, but it at the present failed to show the iconic taxa from the new deposit.

comments.issue: The taxonomic work is not fully convincing; the lobopodian's diagnostic features and anatomical details are obscure.
comments.request: Strengthen the taxonomic evidence and illustrations.
comments.quote: Some of the taxonomic work in this research may be not very convincing.

comments.issue: The unique polar composition claim conflicts with the low-latitude Anji Biota and the polar Fezouata Biota.
comments.request: Discuss these discrepancies with published assemblages.
comments.quote: Furthermore, the Fezouata Biota located at the Ordovician polar area does not show the same taxonomic composition to the Cabrières Biota.

comments.issue: Composition differences may reflect redox conditions (sponges tolerate hypoxia) or the limited number of specimens.
comments.request: Provide geochemistry and acknowledge the sampling limitation.
comments.quote: It is generally believed that sponge animals are more tolerant of hypoxic environments, and the composition difference in various biotas was caused by the redox condition of water bodies.

comments.issue: The weathering-altered carbon means fresh material is needed for a comprehensive taphonomic analysis.
comments.request: Collect fossils from fresher, less weathered rock in the future.
comments.quote: the future collection of an expanded range of fossils from relatively fresh (low or moderately weathered) rock, will enable a more comprehensive taphonomic analysis of the modes and mechanisms of preservation within the Cabrières Biota

title: The Cabrières Biota (France) provides insights into Ordovician polar ecosystems

study.system: reef fishes and coral cover; meta-analysis of 75 studies

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers find the work of potential interest but raise substantial concerns; the manuscript cannot be accepted now, but a much-revised version addressing these serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Well-written, robust meta-analysis with interesting results, though the authors' questioning of fish-coral relationships is discordant with the findings.
strengths: robust analytical approach with PRISMA documentation

comments.issue: The manuscript repeatedly questions fish dependence on coral even though weak positive relationships are consistently present.
comments.request: Align the questioning of fish-coral dependence with the reported results.
comments.quote: Relationships are weak, but are irrefutably present for most of the analyses, yet the authors continually question the validity of fish dependence on coral.

comments.issue: The range of coral cover and non-linear relationships may drive variation but are not tested as moderators.
comments.request: Include coral cover range and cover midpoint as moderators.
comments.quote: Hence, I suggest the authors include range of coral cover and cover midpoint as moderators to explain variance in their results.

comments.issue: Physical structure and structural complexity, which are not always correlated with coral cover, may be more relevant to fish than living tissue.
comments.request: Include structural complexity in the analyses or discuss its importance.
comments.quote: If the authors are unable to include structural complexity in their analyses, some discussion about the importance of physical structures and structural complexity should be included.

comments.issue: The methods equations were pixelated and difficult to read in the PDF.
comments.request: Provide readable equations.
comments.quote: although these were pixelated in the

reviews.assessment: Interesting question and extensive compilation, but the correlation metric and the conclusion that coral does not matter much are poorly justified.
strengths: tackles a very interesting and relevant problem

comments.issue: The correlation coefficient may be the wrong metric; the slope better answers how much fish density changes with coral cover.
comments.request: Use a slope-based effect size instead of the correlation coefficient.
comments.quote: I find it much more compelling to ask “how much will fish density change” in response to a change in coral cover, than asking “how much of the observed variation in fish density can be explained by coral cover?”

comments.issue: An example shows r can be maximal while the biological effect is trivial, so the correlation fails to capture importance.
comments.request: Reconsider the effect size metric in light of this example.
comments.quote: In which case was coral “more important?” or in the words of the authors which case showed that “reef fishes need corals”?

comments.issue: A slope metric would summarise the studies more meaningfully but requires comparable units.
comments.request: Convert studies to comparable slope units.
comments.quote: Thus, I would encourage the authors to use a metric like the slope to summarize these studies.

comments.issue: For specialised coral-dependent fish a wedge-shaped relationship is expected, so small correlations do not imply coral is unimportant; the tested expectation is a strawman.
comments.request: Reframe the expectation to account for wedge-shaped relationships.
comments.quote: I think the most sensible expectation is a “wedge” (a triangular clustering of data) with no fish in the absence of corals, and a maximum number of fish when coral cover was high.

comments.issue: Fish populations show inertia and lag behind coral decline, so weak correlations can arise even when coral is important.
comments.request: Consider population lag as an explanation for weak correlations.
comments.quote: One is that the fish population has “inertia”, such that following a decline in coral cover, a fish population will persist for a while

comments.issue: Shelter persists after coral death, so a low correlation with live cover today does not mean fish do not need coral; this caveat is never discussed.
comments.request: Present the persistence of dead-coral structure as a caveat.
comments.quote: Thus, while “fish need coral”, they might show a very low correlation coefficient with live coral cover present today. I’m sure the authors appreciate this issue, but it is never discussed or presented as a caveat.

comments.issue: Partial correlations would likely be larger than Pearson's r because they absorb other variables adding noise.
comments.request: Compare partial r and R2 with Pearson's r and univariate R2.
comments.quote: I would expect that the partial r’s would be larger than the Pearon’s r, since they have already incorporated the effects of (some) other variables that add noise to the Pearson r relationship.

comments.issue: The term 'standardized correlation coefficients' is incorrect.
comments.request: Drop 'standardized' and call it the correlation coefficient.
comments.quote: I would encourage the authors to drop their reference to “standardized correlation coefficients”.

comments.issue: What 'the distribution' on line 334 refers to is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the distribution being described.
comments.quote: Is it the distribution of true r’s across papers; the variation within papers; or something else?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the credible interval concerns the mean effect or among-paper variation, and too much space covers general meta-analysis.
comments.request: Clarify the credible interval and focus on the core approach.
comments.quote: I’m not sure if the credible interval is a credible interval for the mean effect (across all combined studies) or is it a statement about the posterior distribution for the among-paper variation in effects?

comments.issue: How the branching versus mounding coral analysis was conducted is unclear.
comments.request: Be explicit about what the morphotype analysis compares.
comments.quote: I also was not able to discern how some of the supplementary analyses were conducted: e.g., the analysis contrasting branching vs. mounding corals.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Fig. S7 correlations use temporal or spatial-plus-temporal variation.
comments.request: Explain the data structure behind Fig. S7.
comments.quote: For Fig S7, are these r’s based on temporal variation or spatial combined with temporal variation

comments.issue: Figure S8 is hard to understand; sample sizes identical to Fig. S4 seem impossible and the disturbance approach is unclear.
comments.request: Elaborate how disturbance studies were handled.
comments.quote: For Figure S8, I don’t understand what is being done. For example, the sample sizes here are identical to those in Fig S4, but I’m not sure how that is possible.

comments.issue: Fitting one moderator at a time limits interpretation; morphology and family could be fitted simultaneously.
comments.request: Fit multiple moderators simultaneously.
comments.quote: Because the authors implement one moderator at a time, it’s hard to interpret some of the overall patterns

comments.issue: The labels 'weak', 'moderate' and 'strong' impose an arbitrary scale.
comments.request: Report effect sizes without these labels.
comments.quote: I also encourage the authors to drop reference to “weak”, “moderate”, and “strong”, which simply re-entrenches an arbitrary and fairly useless designation.

comments.issue: Code and data were not made available before review.
comments.request: Make code and data available prior to submission.
comments.quote: I would encourage the authors to make code and data available prior to submitting their paper for review.

comments.issue: The effect size interpretation and the general conclusion that coral does not matter much to fish are not well supported.
comments.request: Reconsider the interpretation and the general conclusion.
comments.quote: I don’t think they have thought through the interpretation of their effect size very carefully; nor do I think that the general conclusion that “coral doesn’t matter much to fish” is well supported.

title: Meta-analysis reveals weak associations between reef fishes and corals

study.system: 225 plots along 45 forest edge-to-interior transects, Europe

editor_summary: Two reviewers find considerable potential interest but substantial concerns; cannot accept but would consider a revision addressing them.

reviews.assessment: Timely contribution, but understory-only analyses may bias findings and need sensitivity tests.
strengths: timely contribution on forest edges versus interiors

comments.issue: Understory plants only; other forest strata ignored, potentially biasing findings.
comments.request: Include other forest strata in analyses or run sensitivity tests.
comments.quote: I only have a major concern that the authors used understory plants as their research targets and ignored other forest strata in their analyses.

comments.issue: Discussion should consider other edge types and their roles in soil nutrients.
comments.request: Discuss other edge types, e.g. island edges.
comments.quote: forest edges may enhance soil nutrient inputs from adjacent land use, while the authors could also discuss other kinds of edges and their roles in maintaining soil nutrients

comments.issue: Wording about forest borders being largely non-forest areas needs checking.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: do you mean 'where forests borders are largely non-forest areas.'?

comments.issue: Ecosystem functions and ecosystem services are used interchangeably.
comments.request: Use the two terms correctly and consistently.
comments.quote: Do you refer to 'ecosystem functions', or 'ecosystem services'? Please don't misuse these two terms.

comments.issue: Plant area index needs more explanation.
comments.request: Explain the term.
comments.quote: 'plant area index': need more explanations on this term

comments.issue: Ecosystem multifunctionality is mentioned but not quantified; trade-offs may be sensitive to index choice.
comments.request: Quantify multifunctionality and test sensitivity to index selection.
comments.quote: the authors mentioned 'ecosystem multifunctionality' several times in the text but didn't quantify it

reviews.assessment: Original and valuable question, but insufficient model reporting prevents assessment of validity.
strengths: interesting findings complementing prior BEF work

comments.issue: Data collection and procedural reasoning need more detail for reproducibility.
comments.request: Add details to the data collection descriptions.
comments.quote: the description of the data collection as well as the reasoning behind the use of some procedures needs to be backed up with some more details in order to increase the transparency and reproducibility

comments.issue: Model descriptions and result presentation do not allow assessment of validity.
comments.request: Provide enough model detail for readers to assess validity.
comments.quote: the descriptions of the models and analysis, as well as the presentation of the data and model results do not allow readers (including me with a very strong background in Bayesian statistics) to assess the validity of the results

comments.issue: Figures show only modelled relationships; no raw data points are presented.
comments.request: Show raw data alongside modelled relationships.
comments.quote: the authors only show the modelled relationships or effect sizes (e.g., Figs. 2, 3, S2, S3), but neither the main manuscript nor the Supplement present a single data point

comments.issue: Summary tables with estimates, uncertainty, R-squared and convergence diagnostics are needed.
comments.request: Provide full summary tables including PSRF and effective sample sizes.
comments.quote: These tables should include measures of central tendency and uncertainty for all model parameters (including fixed effects and variance components associated with random terms), as well as measures of model fit (R2-marginal and R2-conditional).

comments.issue: Default priors are unclear (non-informative, weakly or highly informative) and their effects unknown.
comments.request: Report and justify the priors used.
comments.quote: it remains unclear whether these priors were non-informative, weakly informative or highly informative and how this might affect the parameter estimates

comments.issue: Multivariate multilevel model implementation is unclear; equations or code needed.
comments.request: Provide model equations or code detailing the structure.
comments.quote: I would also like to encourage the authors to provide a detailed account of the model structure, either in the form of mathematical equations or computer code

comments.issue: Line 62 should mention the 45 transects alongside the 225 plots.
comments.request: Add the number of transects to this sentence.
comments.quote: In this sentence please also detail that 45 forest edge-to-interior transects were monitored

comments.issue: Should mention that models accounted for latitude and forest management.
comments.request: Add this information to the section.
comments.quote: It would be good to mention in this section (e.g., at the end) that the models accounted for the effects of latitude and forest management

comments.issue: Plant area index needs a clearer definition in the main text.
comments.request: Define plant area index for non-expert readers.
comments.quote: Plant area index needs to be defined more clearly in the main text so that non-expert readers do not need to consult the Methods section.

comments.issue: Relationships of PAI, shade-casting ability and Tmax to edge should be shown as a figure.
comments.request: Add an extended data or supplementary figure.
comments.quote: It would be good to show in how Plant area index, shade-casting ability and Tmax are related to forest edge as an Extended Data Figure or Supplementary Figure.

comments.issue: Table S1 suggests more than three stands per region; sampling design needs clarification.
comments.request: Clarify the number of stands per region.
comments.quote: Table S1 suggests that in some regions more than three forest stands have been established (e.g., Central Italy n = 9, Belgium n = 9, Central Norway n = 9).

comments.issue: Paragraph should state the total number of transects (45).
comments.request: Add the total transect count.
comments.quote: Please add in this paragraph how many transects have been established in total (looking at Table S1 it seems that it was 45 transects).

comments.issue: Distance metric for Rao's quadratic entropy is not specified.
comments.request: State the distance metric and any trait transformations.
comments.quote: Please provide information on the distance metric that was used to calculate Rao’s quadratic entropy. Were these gower distances or Euclidean distances?

comments.issue: Why leaf nitrogen is a proxy for nutrient cycling needs explanation.
comments.request: Add a brief explanation of the assumed relation.
comments.quote: It is not intuitively clear from this sentence, why nitrogen concentration in leaves is a good proxy for nutrient cycling.

comments.issue: Overlapping 9 m radii among the three nearest-edge plots make DBH measurements non-independent.
comments.request: Clarify whether overlapping measurements were reused.
comments.quote: If the DBH measurements in these radii were used in several plots the measurements are not independent. Could the authors please clarify this aspect?

comments.issue: Seedling recording details (timing, plot size) are missing.
comments.request: Describe when and how seedlings were recorded.
comments.quote: during which time of the year were the seedlings recorded and how? On the entire 3 x 3 m2 plots or in subplots?

comments.issue: Why sand percentage proxies soil texture needs explanation.
comments.request: Add a brief explanation.
comments.quote: Non-experts like myself might wonder why the percentage of sand is a good proxy for soil texture. Could you please add a brief explanation?

comments.issue: Rationale for choosing May 2018 as reference is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the choice of May 2018.
comments.quote: It is not entirely clear why May 2018 has been chosen as a reference. Was the data collected in 2018?

comments.issue: Transect and region random factors should be stated earlier in the model descriptions.
comments.request: Move this information to the model 1 and 2 descriptions.
comments.quote: This information should be stated earlier in the descriptions for models 1 and 2.

comments.issue: Poisson distribution for taxonomic diversity may be overdispersed; negative binomial may be better.
comments.request: Justify or change the distribution.
comments.quote: Is the use of a Poisson distribution for taxonomic diversity justified? It is not unlikely that these data are overdispersed, so that a negative binomial distribution might be more appropriate to account for overdispersion.

title: Trade-offs in biodiversity and ecosystem services between edges and interiors in European forests

study.system: seagrass herbivory experiment; 28° latitude, Western Atlantic

editor_summary: Both referees commend the study's scale; Referee 1 asks for re-analysis accounting for collinearity, Referee 2 requests terminology revision; editor also flags title and abstract format.

reviews.assessment: Enormous, carefully designed study; requests re-analysis for collinearity and a few clarifications before acceptance.
strengths: enormous and carefully designed field experiment
commendable number of treatments and replicates
high standards of statistical analysis and data visualization

comments.issue: Collinearity between latitude, temperature and light prevents all covariates in one model.
comments.request: Run a Partial Least Squares regression re-analysis.
comments.quote: I do believe the authors could conduct a re-analysis of the data given the collinearity between latitude, temperature and light

comments.issue: Separate models per season are less desirable than one general model with season as an effect.
comments.request: Add season as a fixed/random effect in a single general model.
comments.quote: I would also prefer seeing the season added as a fixed/random effect in the same general model, more than running separate models for each season

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 5 do not indicate whether points are raw data or partial residuals/model fits.
comments.request: Describe (and preferably show) partial residuals and model fits.
comments.quote: I'd like to know if the points in figure 2 and 5 are the raw data points with a ‘ggplot’ trend line or the partial residuals of the model

comments.issue: Generalization is risky because Thalassia testudinum is persistent and slow growing.
comments.request: Be more careful generalizing to other seagrass types.
comments.quote: The authors should be a bit more careful with this generalisation, since Thalassia testudinum is a ‘persistent’ and slow growing seagrass

comments.issue: Line-level edits: remove 'as' after Australia (L120) and 'seasonal' after Mean (L227).
comments.request: Apply these wording corrections.
comments.quote: Line 120. I think the word ‘as’ after Australia should be removed.

comments.issue: Why two separate models were used and the full list of response variables are not given at the end of the introduction.
comments.request: Explain the collinearity issue and list the response variables in the introduction.
comments.quote: I miss a bit of detail on why the authors used 2 separate models (i.e., the issue with collinearity), and also I miss a more thorough listing of the response variables studied

comments.issue: Results are hard to follow without the later methods (e.g. season and clipping duration unclear at L181-182).
comments.request: Make the results easier to read with brief context.
comments.quote: I didn’t understand if the effects of simulated grazing on seagrass productivity were only for the summer, or winter, or both

comments.issue: The insolation-grazing pattern (more summer insolation at high latitudes) is counter-intuitive and not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this pattern in the discussion.
comments.quote: when seagrasses at higher latitudes have more insolation than lower latitudes (in summer), they suffer more from intense grazing than those in lower latitudes

comments.issue: Results at L192-195 are not referenced to a supplementary table.
comments.request: Refer readers to the relevant supplementary table.
comments.quote: Can we find these results in one of the tables of the supplementary? Can you make reference to it?

comments.issue: The timing of TNC reserve sampling is not stated in the results, making them hard to interpret.
comments.request: State when reserves were measured in the results text.
comments.quote: since we don’t know yet when the TNC reserves were sampled (it’s said in the methods), it is difficult to interpret this result

comments.issue: Fig. 5 is mentioned before Fig. 4 in the text.
comments.request: Swap the figure order.
comments.quote: I think you mention Fig 5 before fig. 4 in the text. If that’s the case, you should swap them.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether results at L230-231 refer to leaf productivity.
comments.request: Specify the response variable.
comments.quote: These results refer to leaf productivity? It is not clear currently.

comments.issue: The limitation index is used in results before it is defined in the methods.
comments.request: Briefly define the limitation index in the results.
comments.quote: as a result of methods being afterwards, I think you should briefly define the limitation index here too. Otherwise, it is very difficult to follow.

comments.issue: Herbivory interacted with nutrients in the field but not in the enrichment experiment, without discussion.
comments.request: Discuss this discrepancy in the discussion.
comments.quote: How do you explain the fact that simulated herbivory interacted with nutrients under field conditions, but not when you experimentally enriched with nutrients?

comments.issue: Nutrient addition effects (lower density, thinner leaves, lower production) are opposite to expectation and not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the unexpected nutrient addition results.
comments.quote: As it is written, I understand that nutrient enrichment was linked to lower shoot density, thinner leaves and lower production. These results are quite the opposite I would expect

comments.issue: The overall trends in Fig. S3 are not commented on.
comments.request: Comment on the overall trends shown in Fig. S3.
comments.quote: the authors focus on some other details, and miss the opportunity of commenting on the overall trends shown in Fig S3

comments.issue: What 'controls' refers to (caged, uncaged, clipped, unclipped) is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify what the controls are.
comments.quote: Line 267. Please specify what you mean by controls

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Figure 2A excludes BOCA.
comments.request: State the BOCA exclusion in the figure legend.
comments.quote: Can you confirm if Figure 2A has BOCA excluded? If so, please state it in the figure legend.

comments.issue: Ambient nutrient availability is not plotted along the latitudinal gradient.
comments.request: Plot nutrients (and other responses) against latitude or on a map.
comments.quote: It would be nice to see it plotted. Either as nutrients vs. latitude or in a map with colour matching nutrients.

comments.issue: The role of rhizome carbohydrates as indicators of ecological resilience could be emphasized more.
comments.request: Emphasise rhizome carbohydrates as resilience indicators.
comments.quote: I think you could emphasise even more the importance of rhizome carbohydrates saying they can be indicators of ecological RESILIENCE for meadows facing tropicalisation

comments.issue: The types of disturbances affecting tropical seagrasses and the water-quality-resilience link are not made explicit.
comments.request: Specify the disturbances and spell out the water quality mechanism.
comments.quote: you should be a bit more specific with the type of disturbances that particularly influence tropical and subtropical seagrass meadows

comments.issue: The discussion is less broad than the introduction and extrapolates to seagrasses generally.
comments.request: Broaden the discussion and avoid over-extrapolating.
comments.quote: the authors should be careful when extrapolating their results to the seagrasses in general

comments.issue: Whether the site random effect was tested against a plain linear model is unclear.
comments.request: Test whether the random effect is needed.
comments.quote: Did you enter ‘site’ as a random effect by default, or did you test the random effects model vs. the plain linear model to see if including ‘site’ was really needed?

comments.issue: Results of the site-exclusion analysis are not provided as supplementary material.
comments.request: Add these results as supplementary material.
comments.quote: Might be worth adding these results as supplementary?

reviews.assessment: Very positive; commends the experiment and clarity, asking mainly for corrected geographic terminology and a few additions.
strengths: rich experimental network across 28° of latitude

comments.issue: 'Western Atlantic' is used as a synonym for 'North Western Atlantic'; the term is inaccurate and must be corrected.
comments.request: Correct the geographic terminology throughout the text and title.
comments.quote: the authors use “Western Atlantic” as a synonym for “North Western Atlantic” where this study was conducted

comments.issue: Chemical defenses modulating herbivory across latitudes are not discussed as an alternative hypothesis.
comments.request: Add this mechanism and literature to introduction and discussion.
comments.quote: I think a discussion on the role of chemical defenses in modulating herbivory across latitudes and how this can interact with tropicalization is needed

comments.issue: The last introduction paragraph lacks clear hypotheses or expected results.
comments.request: Rewrite it hypothesis-driven.
comments.quote: I believe the last paragraph of the introduction would benefit from a more hypothesis-driven writing.

comments.issue: Minimum temperatures are not considered although they likely vary strongly with latitude.
comments.request: Use minimum temperature as a predictor or show its variation.
comments.quote: How about the minimum temperature? I would expect them to be much lower as you move away from the tropics

comments.issue: The overgrazing-by-conservation argument is potentially inaccurate and better supported by fish than megaherbivore evidence.
comments.request: Balance and better support this argument.
comments.quote: authors imply that overgrazing is among the main causes of seagrass demise. I believe this is a dangerous and potentially inaccurate rationale

comments.issue: Photoperiod differences between summer and winter are not mentioned when discussing light gradients.
comments.request: Mention photoperiod differences in the discussion.
comments.quote: it would be worth it to mention the differences in photoperiods (shorter vs longer days) not only through the PAR across latitudes but also between summer and winter
