comments.issue: A relevant paper at L337 is not cited.
comments.request: Consider citing the suggested paper.
comments.quote: Line 337, consider looking at this paper: https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.15346

comments.issue: Generality of the conclusions to other seagrasses and plant-herbivore systems is not discussed.
comments.request: Add thought-provoking sentences on broader generality.
comments.quote: Although this study is focused on turtlegrass, it kept me wondering how general the conclusions would be to other seagrass species and for other plant-herbivore interactions

comments.issue: How closely simulated herbivory mimicked natural herbivory (plot size, blade height, scars) is not described.
comments.request: Describe the ecological realism of the simulation in the methods.
comments.quote: I think it would be worth to add to the methods to which extent the simulated herbivory mimicked the natural herbivory

comments.issue: 'Seagrass responses' at L483 are not named, forcing readers to look them up.
comments.request: Name the responses in brackets.
comments.quote: Please consider naming the responses within brackets so the reader does not have to go back to the results to figure out what was measured.

comments.issue: Main results of the site-exclusion reanalysis are not included as supplementary material.
comments.request: Add the reanalysis results as supplementary material.
comments.quote: I suggest them to include the main results of that reanalysis as a supplementary material. I thought it was a very elegant approach.

comments.issue: Figure 5 panel B lacks latitude values next to site acronyms.
comments.request: Add latitude after site acronyms in panel B.
comments.quote: Consider adding the latitude after the site acronym in the panel B of Figure 5 (e.g. PUER(X°N)).

title: Herbivore effects increase with latitude across the extent of a foundational seagrass

study.system: passerine birds; cognitive tasks, 203 birds, 15 species

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers found the work interesting and significant, with common concerns about statistical tests and figure legends, and R3 flagging issues with the measures used.

reviews.assessment: Clear reasoning and well-written paper, but the statistical analyses need phylogenetic control, clearer model description and multiple-testing correction.

comments.issue: Species-level Spearman correlations do not account for phylogenetic relationships among species.
comments.request: Show that species-level results hold with phylogenetic control.
comments.quote: this approach fails to account for the phylogenetic relationship among the studied species

comments.issue: Regression lines in figures lack details, and mixing correlation and regression results is misleading.
comments.request: Remove the regression lines from the figures.
comments.quote: Furthermore, it is misleading to mix the results of correlation and regression analyses. Therefore I suggest to remove these lines from the figures.

comments.issue: The MCMCglmm specification is unclear, including why individual-level data are analysed when key variables are species-level.
comments.request: Clarify the random factors and model structure.
comments.quote: What is the reason to analyse individual data in the case where variables of main interest (innovativeness, brain size) are only measured at the species level?

comments.issue: The analysis code is not available, hindering understanding of the models.
comments.request: Make the analysis code available.
comments.quote: The understanding of these analyses can significantly be helped by making the code of the analyses available.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether p-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons outside the cases mentioned at line 96.
comments.request: State and apply multiple-comparison corrections throughout.
comments.quote: the authors perform many statistical tests but it is unclear whether they used p-values adjusted for multiple comparison

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits: movie numbering at L80-81 and L85, and 'task' vs 'flask' at L546.
comments.quote: L80-81: "Extended Data Movie 5" should be "Extended Data Movie 7"

comments.issue: 'Associative learning' may be missing from the list at L120.
comments.request: Consider listing associative learning at L120.
comments.quote: L120: Shouldn't "associative learning" be listed here as well?

reviews.assessment: Exciting, formidable study with an impressive dataset; asks for consistent predictor directionality, sex-generalization caveats and many clarifications.
strengths: first link between cognitive task performance and brain size and innovation

comments.issue: Model directionality contradicts the title: innovation and brain size are treated as predictors of problem solving.
comments.request: Make innovation and brain size dependent variables and cognitive scores predictors.
comments.quote: yet language throughout the manuscript (e.g., L103, 162-163) and the MCMCGLMMs (L126-146, 638-651, Table 1, extended data table 3) contradict this

comments.issue: Almost all subjects were male, so results cannot be generalized to both sexes.
comments.request: Acknowledge the male bias explicitly throughout.
comments.quote: The results therefore cannot be generalized to both sexes, and the paper should acknowledge this more explicitly throughout.

comments.issue: Figures and tables lack species information, making the distribution of species hard to see.
comments.request: Number data points and link them to species names.
comments.quote: I wonder if the figures and tables could be enriched with species information so that readers can see how the species are distributed across a given variable.

comments.issue: The self-control, associative learning and reversal tasks are not described for visualization.
comments.request: Briefly describe these tasks in the introduction.
comments.quote: provide a few words to help the reader visualize what you mean by a self-control task, associative learning task, and reversal task, as has been done for problem-solving tasks

comments.issue: The introduction does not list factors linked to avian cognition, weakening the rationale for covariates.
comments.request: Add a sentence on factors such as urbanization.
comments.quote: it would be useful to include a sentence in the introduction to list some of the factors that have been linked to avian cognition in other studies (e.g., urbanization)

comments.issue: It is unclear what 967 refers to and what counts as a 'case'.
comments.request: Clarify the denominator and the unit of cases.
comments.quote: L71: 967 out of how many? By 'cases', do you mean species or examples of innovations?

comments.issue: No example or description of 'innovations' is given for non-specialists.
comments.request: Add an example of innovations.
comments.quote: for non-specialists, it would be helpful to include an example or brief description of 'innovations' to help them visualize what is being tested

comments.issue: The section at L119-125 may omit associative learning.
comments.request: Consider including associative learning.
comments.quote: L119-125: should this section not also include 'associative learning'?

comments.issue: The clause beginning '; and body condition' at L138 is awkward.
comments.request: Revise this clause.
comments.quote: L138: the clause beginning '; and body condition

comments.issue: It is unclear which assay tests which cognitive process, and the third assay is not mentioned.
comments.request: Specify the assays and include associative learning on L196.
comments.quote: should specify here which assay tests which of the cognitive processes mentioned here; also, what about the third assay used in the study - should it also be mentioned here; similarly, should associative learning be included on L196?

comments.issue: The dates of trials and whether they were restricted to the breeding season are not reported.
comments.request: Report trial dates and breeding-season confinement.
comments.quote: please provide range of dates per year when the trials were conducted, and whether trials were confined to the breeding season when male birds are easier to capture.

comments.issue: Housing conditions (individual vs social) are not clarified.
comments.request: State whether birds were housed individually or socially.
comments.quote: should clarify whether birds were housed individually or socially in each cage

comments.issue: It is not noted that birds were tested in their home cages.
comments.request: Note that birds were tested in home cages.
comments.quote: L459: should note here that birds were tested in their home cages

comments.issue: The number of birds succeeding on the confirmation trial is not specified.
comments.request: Specify how many birds succeeded.
comments.quote: L550-551: should specify how many birds were successful on the confirmation trial.

comments.issue: L569 may say 'day 1' where 'day 2' is meant to match L552.
comments.request: Check and correct the day reference.
comments.quote: L569: should this say 'day 2' rather than 'day 1' to match L552?

comments.issue: The scoring scheme for rewarded choices in trials 1-7 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the scoring scheme.
comments.quote: if a bird chose the rewarded colour in trials 1-7, would they be given a score of 1, 7, or 3.5. Should clarify scoring scheme.

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: typo 'residues' at L618 and MGMG vs MCMC at L645.
comments.quote: L645: typo - change MGMG to MCMC

comments.issue: The assumed linear relationship between innovation counts and research effort may not hold.
comments.request: Consider and address non-linearity with research effort.
comments.quote: is the relationship between # innovations and research effort necessarily linear? I would think that # of innovations would plateau with increasing effort

comments.issue: The source of body mass data and whether values are male-specific are unclear.
comments.request: Report the source and sex specificity of body mass data.
comments.quote: where did the body mass data come from, and were they specific to males given that most birds in the study were male?

comments.issue: The number of capture site categories is unclear, and shyness is included in neophobia models but not vice versa.
comments.request: Clarify capture site categories and the asymmetric covariate choices.
comments.quote: should specify how many categories there were for 'capture site,' since I thought all wild birds were captured at the same site (Rockefeller Field Station)

comments.issue: Dietary generalism is omitted from the sentence and its data source is not explained.
comments.request: Include dietary generalism and explain its data source.
comments.quote: this sentence should also include 'dietary generalism', and another sentence should explain where those data came from

comments.issue: 'Excluding seasonal migrants' is unclear because several study species are migratory at the site.
comments.request: Clarify what excluding seasonal migrants means.
comments.quote: L664: unclear what is meant by 'excluding seasonal migrants'. Aren't several of your species migratory at your study site (e.g., goldfinch, cowbird, sparrows, phoebe, catbird, wrens)?

comments.issue: Task names are inconsistent between 'lid-pulling'/'lid-knocking' and 'lid-flipping'.
comments.request: Use consistent task names.
comments.quote: tasks are described as 'lid-pulling' and 'lid-flipping', but as 'lid-knocking' and 'lid-flipping' elsewhere

comments.issue: Directional predictions in the Extended Fig. 3 caption lack rationale and the tests are not one-tailed.
comments.request: Provide rationale, use one-tailed tests or neutral wording.
comments.quote: the basis of those directional predictions is unclear. For example, why couldn't birds with better problem solving be bolder rather than shyer?

comments.issue: Extended Table 1 lacks a family column.
comments.request: Add a family column.
comments.quote: Extended Table 1: please add a column for family to help readers from outside ornithology

comments.issue: In Extended Table 3 model 25a the reward line is not bold.
comments.request: Bold the reward line in model 25a.
comments.quote: Extended Table 3: in model 25a, the line for 'reward' should be in bold

comments.issue: The review videos were grainy, especially the self-control ones.
comments.request: Provide higher-quality videos if available.
comments.quote: the versions I had for review were quite grainy; the two showing the self-control test, in particular, were difficult to see what was happening

reviews.assessment: Impressive, well-executed study and a major step forward; concerns about the pure neophobia measure and multiple-testing corrections.

comments.issue: Figure 1 ignores other factors such as persistence and exploration (neophilia).
comments.request: Include these factors in Figure 1.
comments.quote: One important factor is missing here as exploration (neophilia) has been repeatedly liked to problem-solving abilities

comments.issue: Neophobia and neophilia are treated as extremes of one continuum rather than independent motivations.
comments.request: Mention that they are independent motivations.
comments.quote: It should be mentioned that neophobia and neophilia are not the extremes along a continuum but represent independent motivations

comments.issue: The solid and hatched lines in Figure 1 are not explained.
comments.request: Explain what the lines mean.
comments.quote: it has nowhere been explained what the solid and hatched lines mean

comments.issue: Significance symbols are not explained in the legends of Figures 3 and 4 and Extended Data Fig. 2.
comments.request: Explain the symbols in the legends.
comments.quote: *, ** and *** are not explained in the legend.

comments.issue: No corrections for multiple testing appear to have been applied to the many Spearman correlations.
comments.request: Apply and report corrections such as sequential Bonferroni.
comments.quote: Many Spearman correlations were used resulting in type 1 errors. Were any corrections used (e.g., sequential Bonferroni adjustments) to account for this?

comments.issue: The y-axis label is missing from Extended Data Fig. 10.
comments.request: Add the y-axis label.
comments.quote: Extended Data Fig. 10: The y-axis label is missing.

comments.issue: No interaction terms are listed in Extended Data Table 3 although interactions were considered.
comments.request: Confirm or add meaningful interaction terms.
comments.quote: there is not a single interaction listed in the table. This is odd as it is difficult to imagine that there are no significant interaction terms.

comments.issue: Describing some relationships as weak is inconsistent with the highly significant problem-solving and shyness association.
comments.request: Explain the basis for judging relationships weak or strong.
comments.quote: I would not say that some of the relationships were weak associations as problem-solving and shyness for example were consistently highly significant.

comments.issue: The consistent link between problem-solving ability and shyness is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this link in the Discussion.
comments.quote: I think the consistent link between problem-solving ability and shyness needs mentioning and discussion.

comments.issue: Shyness is measured only once, so its consistency over time, essential for a personality measure, is not demonstrated.
comments.request: Test individual consistency or rename the measure.
comments.quote: Otherwise, this measure should not be called shyness, particularly as the used measure is quite unusual.

comments.issue: Pure neophobia was set to zero instead of using negative values when shyness exceeded neophobia.
comments.request: Repeat analyses with the correct negative values.
comments.quote: Why did you set neophobia to zero when the shyness measure was higher than the neophobia measure? The correct way would be to use the correct negative value.

comments.issue: Averaging neophobia across four days is not a true reflection of neophobia because shyness declines over days.
comments.request: Test alternative neophobia measures and their effects on results.
comments.quote: your pure neophobia measure using the average across the four days is not a true reflection of an individuals/species’ neophobia and should not be used

comments.issue: Individuals are not nested within species in the random effects structure.
comments.request: Consider testing individuals nested within species.
comments.quote: shouldn’t there be a nested approach be used with testing individuals within species to account for closely related individuals

title: Problem-solving skills are predicted by technical innovations in the wild and brain size in passerines

study.system: soil viromes; global soil metagenomes plus new Chinese samples

editor_summary: Editor requires revisions: remove 'across the globe' from the title; R1 questions data sufficiency, hypotheses and geographic bias/autocorrelation; R2 wants viral detection, low-coverage and search methods clarified, ideally with a PRISMA flowchart; R3 wants expanded discussion.

reviews.assessment: Questions whether current metagenomic data can support robust global conclusions on soil virome biogeography and finds the analysis descriptive and overinterpreted.

comments.issue: Sequencing depth is insufficient; the study addresses a small, possibly unrepresentative fraction of the soil virome.
comments.request: Acknowledge the sequencing-depth limitation and its consequences.
comments.quote: So my main concern is that this work addresses a small fraction of the soil virome, which may not be representative.

comments.issue: Strong geographic bias toward North America and China undermines the claimed global analysis.
comments.request: Acknowledge the geographic bias or temper global claims.
comments.quote: First there is a strong geographic bias towards N America and China, and I am concerned that the authors are reporting a global analysis.

comments.issue: Strong spatial autocorrelation in the data has not been accounted for.
comments.request: Account for spatial autocorrelation in the analyses.
comments.quote: This also introduces strong spatial autocorrelation in the data that has not been accounted for by the authors, and I am not sure if that is feasible.

comments.issue: Manuscript is highly descriptive with no theoretical framework, and the questions addressed are unclear.
comments.request: Add an explicit framework and state the questions.
comments.quote: Second I found the manuscript highly descriptive without any theoretical framework. It was also unclear what questions the authors want to address with their data.

comments.issue: Biotic-interaction results are overstated; correlations cannot rule out other factors and need experimental validation.
comments.request: Temper the biotic-interaction claims or validate them experimentally.
comments.quote: the authors have overstated their results on biotic interactions. This needs experimentation and validation in lab settings, and we cannot rule out the effects of other factors besides biotic interactions based on correlations.

comments.issue: Sampling protocols likely differ among biomes; it is unclear whether this was accounted for (L133).
comments.request: Explain how contrasting sampling protocols were handled.
comments.quote: L133 I assume that sampling protocol were quite contrasting between different biomes, did the authors account for that?

comments.issue: Sample storage and processing differences may affect viral DNA persistence and comparability (L141-142).
comments.request: Discuss storage and processing effects on viral DNA.
comments.quote: How about sample storage and processing? How persistent viral DNA is in soil and how these factors could affect it?

comments.issue: Unclear whether the described procedure completely removes sampling bias (L143-146).
comments.request: Clarify the bias-removal procedure and its limits.
comments.quote: Unclear to me, and would this completely remove the effect of sampling bias?

comments.issue: No rationale or hypothesis is given for analysing distance-decay similarity (L156-157).
comments.request: State the rationale or hypothesis for the distance-decay analysis.
comments.quote: That’s the definition of the distance-decay relationship. What is the authors’ rationale or hypothesis for the analysis of distance decay similarity for viral communities

comments.issue: The reported distance-decay pattern largely reflects sampling design and sample aggregation (L158).
comments.request: Address the sampling-design explanation.
comments.quote: I think that what you are reporting as a distance decay similarity pattern to a large extent reflects your study design.

comments.issue: Rationale for using the metacommunity framework for viruses is unclear (L177-178).
comments.request: Explain why the metacommunity framework applies.
comments.quote: Not clear to me. What is the rationale for using the metacommunity framework in studying viruses?

comments.issue: Statement at L196 with 'always' is overstated.
comments.request: Qualify the statement.
comments.quote: L196 I would not say always.

comments.issue: Claim at L197-198 appears to be speculation without support.
comments.request: Support or label the speculation.
comments.quote: L197- L198 Is this your speculation?

comments.issue: Rationale for calculating the ratios at L224-228 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for these ratios.
comments.quote: Again the rationale for calculating such ratios is unclear.

comments.issue: A simpler explanation at L227 is that virus abundance varies less than host abundance.
comments.request: Consider this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: To me a simple explanation is that virus abundance does not vary as much as their hosts.

comments.issue: Result at L285 may be a sampling artefact.
comments.request: Check for sampling artefacts.
comments.quote: L285 I am sceptical that this might be because of sampling artefact.

comments.issue: Unclear whether and how speciation was examined (L348).
comments.request: Clarify the speciation analysis.
comments.quote: I am not sure if and how the authors have examined speciation.

comments.issue: Chimeric sequence filtering is not reported (L390).
comments.request: State whether chimeras were filtered.
comments.quote: Did the authors filter the data for chimeric sequences?

comments.issue: 'Spatially explicit information' at L350 is undefined.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: What the authors mean by “spatially explicit information”

reviews.assessment: Substantial interest in the findings, but detection limits, low coverage and study-selection methods need clearer discussion and documentation.
strengths: schematic bioinformatics workflow (Ext Fig 1) is easy to follow

comments.issue: Likelihood of detecting non-dsDNA viruses is not discussed; an explicit exclusion or comment is needed (10kb cutoff already implies it).
comments.request: Discuss or explicitly exclude non-dsDNA viruses.
comments.quote: There should either be a discussion on the likelihood of detecting non-dsDNA viruses in their dataset, or at some point in their analysis, an explicit exclusion of any viruses identified as not dsDNA.

comments.issue: Low coverage limits virus detection across studies; random co-occurrence may reflect detection failure and undersampling (also L343-346).
comments.request: Discuss the impact of low coverage and undersampling.
comments.quote: The random detection of vOTUs across different studies could be due to the inability of total DNA metagenomics to sufficiently characterize the soil viral communities on an individual sample basis.

comments.issue: Proportion of size-selected viromes among the soil metagenomes is unknown (L91).
comments.request: Report the proportion of size-selected viromes.
comments.quote: It would be useful to know what proportion of these soil metagenomes were size-selected viromes.

comments.issue: GSV map allows infinite scrolling and users lose the sample-location map (L104).
comments.request: Improve the map navigation.
comments.quote: The GSV map could be improved to prevent infinite scrolling and the user losing the map that displays where the samples are located.

comments.issue: Search strategy is not specified; Antarctic virome studies exist (L94).
comments.request: Describe the search strategy.
comments.quote: What search strategy was used? Anarctic virome studies exist

comments.issue: 'Human-associated' at L134 is ambiguous; suggest agricultural land and artificial surfaces.
comments.request: Rename the category.
comments.quote: “human-associated” would normally be used to refer to environments associated with the human body. Perhaps just use agricultural land and artificial surfaces.

comments.issue: 'Family-level vOTU' is not clearly defined (L173).
comments.request: Define family-level vOTU.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if the term “family-level vOTU” could be defined more clearly within this section.

comments.issue: Fig 2b,c are largely unintelligible.
comments.request: Reduce the size of individual points.
comments.quote: Fig 2b + c are largely unintelligible. Consider reducing the size of individual points.

comments.issue: Fig 2d distance-decay relationships are hard to read.
comments.request: Replot with log distance and a fitted trend line.
comments.quote: Consider replotting these distance decay relationships with distance on a log scale and a fitted trend line to make the relationship clearer.

comments.issue: Pattern at L248-251 may reflect undersampling of viral diversity.
comments.request: Consider undersampling as an explanation.
comments.quote: L248-251 – Could this also be due to undersampling of viral diversity?

comments.issue: Fig 4b does not show the number of studies per environment, which affects connectivity.
comments.request: Display the number of studies per environment.
comments.quote: It would be useful to display the number of studies represented in each environment.

comments.issue: 'Deep-sequenced' is undefined and the virome exclusion needs earlier clarification (L307).
comments.request: Define deep-sequenced and clarify the exclusion.
comments.quote: define deep-sequenced. This point about excluding viromes needs clarification earlier in the manuscript.

comments.issue: File size at L378 is ambiguous; unclear whether it is per directional read.
comments.request: Clarify the file-size criterion.
comments.quote: I assume this file size is per directional read file size, i.e. the forward reads are >= 3Gb and the reverse reads are >= 3Gb per library. This could do with clarifying.

comments.issue: Study selection methodology is not described like a systematic search; only 11 studies and no Antarctic soils.
comments.request: Specify key terms and search methodology in detail.
comments.quote: Specify the key terms and methodology used to identify the studies selected for the meta-analysis. It would be good to see this described in a similar level of detail to a systematic literature search.

comments.issue: The 10kb contig threshold likely misses many ssDNA and RNA viruses; their proportions should be discussed (L454-455).
comments.request: Discuss the proportions and detection limits for ssDNA/RNA viruses.
comments.quote: Due to the constraints on contig length used (>=10kb), this dataset is likely to miss many ssDNA and RNA viruses. The relative proportions of dsDNA, ssDNA and RNA viruses in this dataset should be discussed.

comments.issue: Version numbers and settings of bioinformatics packages are not stated (MinCED, tRNAscan-SE, WisH, Cytoscape).
comments.request: State all package versions and settings.
comments.quote: Throughout the methods section, version number and settings of all bioinformatics packages need to be explicitly stated

comments.issue: No Antarctic studies passed the thresholds; more detail on study selection is needed (Ext Fig 2).
comments.request: Explain in more detail how studies were selected.
comments.quote: As mentioned earlier, am surprised that no Antarctic studies met the thresholds to be included in this study. More detail needed on how studies were selected.

comments.issue: Ext Fig 2 lacks an accumulation curve for Africa, which would highlight sparse sampling.
comments.request: Add the Africa accumulation curve.
comments.quote: It would be good to include the accumulation curve for Africa, even though it is sparsely sampled, as a way of emphasising the lack of sampling in this part of the world.

comments.issue: Ext Fig 5 data would be clearer as separate plots per biome.
comments.request: Use separate plots per biome.
comments.quote: This data would be better visualised on separate plots per biome.

title: Biogeographic patterns and drivers of soil viromes

study.system: agricultural landscapes; simulation model parameterized from literature reviews

editor_summary: Editor requires responses to reviewer criticisms and editorial concerns, plus a revised manuscript with all changes highlighted.

reviews.assessment: Compelling, well-documented simulation study, but the interpretation of results versus model assumptions needs more work.
strengths: well documented with a thorough code repository

comments.issue: Results may simply reflect model assumptions rather than emergent properties, and this distinction is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss which results are assumption-driven and which are emergent.
comments.quote: more discussion around where the results are simply a reflection of a given set of model assumptions and where they interesting emergent properties of the interacting parts of the system

comments.issue: The 5% production reduction example may follow by definition from the equation and is sensitive to model structure.
comments.request: Navigate parameter spaces instead of presenting single model-run outcomes as findings.
comments.quote: Is this not just by definition of your equation? What about under a different relationship curves/parameter values explored?

comments.issue: The archetypes are not explained in the main text and it is unclear what other archetypes exist beyond the three cases.
comments.request: Explain the archetypes in the main text and their relation to the wider parameter space.
comments.quote: The archetypes are helpful, but it doesn't, in its current form, feel clear what other archetypes might exist

comments.issue: The term opportunity cost for production loss is misleading and confusing relative to its common definition.
comments.request: Rename it production loss or justify the term clearly.
comments.quote: is there a reason to not just refer to it as "production loss"

comments.issue: Integrating biodiversity in the abstract is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase, e.g. considering feedbacks between biodiversity and production.
comments.quote: clarify what you mean by "integrating biodiversity" here

comments.issue: It is unclear whether multiple literature reviews are included.
comments.request: State how many literature reviews were conducted.
comments.quote: Reviews? Are there multiple lit reviews included?

comments.issue: Figure panels are not labelled, making it hard to follow which panel is referenced.
comments.request: Label panels A, B, C and reflect this in the captions.
comments.quote: its quite hard to follow exactly which panel you are referencing in some cases

reviews.assessment: Important, clearly written contribution; only minor suggestions on biodiversity measures, land use history and figure fonts.
strengths: important contribution of high global relevance

comments.issue: Only species richness is used as the biodiversity measure; alternatives and their implications are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the relevance and implications of alternative biodiversity measures.
comments.quote: the relevance and potential implications of (a) considering alternative biodiversity measures than species richness

comments.issue: Land use history and its implications are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the relevance and potential implications of land use history.
comments.quote: than species richness; and (b) land use history

comments.issue: Figure font sizes need improvement.
comments.request: Increase font sizes in the figures.
comments.quote: as well as to the figures (i.e. mainly related to font sizes)

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important topic, but the aim is unclear, case selection is insufficiently justified, and model definitions and scope need attention.

comments.issue: The paper is technical in places.
comments.quote: the paper is well written, although a bit technical in some places

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the aim is to describe a framework or to test how widespread intensification traps are.
comments.request: Clarify the main aim of the paper.
comments.quote: the exact aim of the paper is a bit unclear to me

comments.issue: The motivation for selecting the three archetypal landscapes and the limitations of this selection are not justified in the main text.
comments.request: Motivate the case study selection and its limitations in the main text.
comments.quote: I would have preferred to see a clearer motivation why the authors select specifically these three systems, and what limitations this selection implies

comments.issue: Relationship D implies intensification affects biodiversity only through fertilizers and pesticides, ignoring rotations, tillage, irrigation and other facets.
comments.request: Explain how other intensification facets are accounted for in the models.
comments.quote: intensification is much more multi-faceted that his, and includes crop rotations, frequency and magnitude of tillage

comments.issue: The origin of the 73% figure cannot be found in the Results and Discussion.
comments.request: Report where the 73% comes from.
comments.quote: Where does the 73% come from? I tried to find this in the Results and Discussion section

comments.issue: The term major calorie production systems is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what major calorie production systems means.
comments.quote: major calorie production systems" – Please explain what his means

comments.issue: The term conventional intensification is only meaningful in contrast to ecological intensification, which is not explained.
comments.request: Add sentences contrasting conventional and ecological intensification.
comments.quote: Please explain why you chose the term "conventional intensification". To me, this only makes sense in contrast to ecological intensification.

comments.issue: The biodiversity-dependent yield feedback is not explained at its first mention.
comments.request: Explain the feedback mechanism at this point in the text.
comments.quote: Please explain here why this is the case, i.e. that the yield is (at least partly) dependent on biodiversity through ecosystem functions

comments.issue: The intensification trap definition is inconsistent: the feedback-to-management sentence seems to define it, not the lose-lose situation.
comments.request: Reconcile the definition of an intensification trap.
comments.quote: To me, this would be the definition of an intensification trap (i.e. not the "lose-lose" situation that the authors use a s the definition

comments.issue: Whether ecological intensification could also lead to intensification traps is not assessed or discussed.
comments.request: Assess or discuss ecological intensification as another route to traps.
comments.quote: it would still be interesting to assess, or at lease discuss (!) if also ecological intensification might lead to intensification traps

comments.issue: The forest hundred returns statement depends on how forests were sorted, which is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how the forests were sorted.
comments.quote: But this depends on how they were sorted, right? Please clarify!

comments.issue: It is unclear whether only pollination and pest control (Relationship C) and only animal biodiversity (Relationship D) were included and how this affects results.
comments.request: Clarify the ecosystem services and biodiversity included and their influence on results.
comments.quote: Where only pollination and pest control considered as important ecosystem service in Relationship C?

title: Biodiversity–production feedback effects lead to intensification traps in agricultural landscapes

study.system: marine fishes; range shifts and abundance trends; global databases

editor_summary: Editor invites a revision addressing all reviewer and editorial concerns, with changes highlighted in the manuscript.

reviews.assessment: Intriguing finding on an important question, but normalisation, model choice and unstated data assumptions limit interpretation.
strengths: addresses a key uncertainty about climate adaptation

comments.issue: Centering and scaling each time series makes trends uninterpretable in biological units and hides within-population variation.
comments.request: Incorporate the coefficient of variation, perhaps scaling trends by it.
comments.quote: the population trends become impossible to interpret for biological meaning, as the trend estimate represents the annual change in abundance where the units are standard deviations unique to each population

comments.issue: Linear models with normal error are inappropriate because many abundance series have means near zero.
comments.request: Use GLMs with Poisson or negative binomial error.
comments.quote: A generalized linear model approach with either Poisson or negative binomial error structure would be more appropriate.

comments.issue: Parameter uncertainty is not incorporated, so uncertain trends may be over-weighted.
comments.request: Weight trends inversely by their standard error.
comments.quote: Without incorporating the parameter uncertainty, the strength of population declines or increases may be being over-weighted for populations with highly uncertain or even non-significant trends.

comments.issue: BioTime provides catch or observed counts, not true abundance, and the linear catch-abundance assumption is unstated.
comments.request: State the assumption and discuss hyperstability and hyperdepletion.
comments.quote: The authors need to clearly state that their analyses are not on true population abundances and that they are assuming catch and abundance are linearly correlated.

comments.issue: How populations were defined across survey stations, plots and repeated surveys is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how catch was combined across stations, plots and seasons.
comments.quote: It is unclear whether the authors are treating the catch of each species within each survey station as a unique population, or whether they are integrating estimates across all station within a survey.

comments.issue: BioShifts mixes centroid-based and presence-based range shifts whose estimates differ substantially.
comments.request: Clarify which type was used and consider the metric as a factor.
comments.quote: It is unclear if the authors only used one type of range shift estimate or both in their analyses.

comments.issue: Coefficients of variation and percent changes were not assessed.
comments.request: Report CVs and percent changes to aid interpretation.
comments.quote: What were the coefficients of variation for the populations? Did you assess the percent change in population across time for any of the populations?

comments.issue: Results were not compared between data-based shifts only and including SDM-based estimates.
comments.request: Run the comparison excluding model-based shifts.
comments.quote: Did you analyze the data including only the shifts estimated from actual data and compare the results to those derived when including both data-based and species distribution model based results?

comments.issue: Coarse fisheries categorisation cannot capture varying harvest impacts across jurisdictions and time.
comments.request: Recognise this heterogeneity when discussing fisheries results.
comments.quote: the coarse nature of your categorization may limit your ability to tease out any impacts of fisheries or fisheries management on trends

comments.issue: Normality of the linear trend models was not assessed.
comments.request: Check residuals and consider GLMs.
comments.quote: Did you assess the linear models of population trend for normality of residuals as you did for the GLMMs?

comments.issue: Figure 3 hides that data are sparse at the extreme ends.
comments.request: Add rug marks or data points.
comments.quote: Might be worth including rug marks along the x-axis indicating the deciles of your data points, or even including the data points on the plot

reviews.assessment: Unique, well-written and sound study; the main disagreement concerns the shift-and-collapse interpretation versus non-linear fast-shift scenarios.

comments.issue: Results need not reflect a shift-and-collapse scenario; they may indicate very fast range shift rates instead.
comments.request: Consider alternative hypotheses and scenarios for interpreting the findings.
comments.quote: the results that the author found in the end is not necessarily reflecting a shift and collapse scenario but rather hints for very fast range shift rates in marine ecosystems

comments.issue: A non-linear relationship is expected because very fast shifts can turn the former leading edge into a trailing edge.
comments.request: Consider this non-linear expectation.
comments.quote: populations located at the leading edge (cold edge) at high latitudes are replaced by populations from lower latitudes such that it becomes the rear edge

comments.issue: Expectations in Figure 1 panel C assume linearity; the poleward relationship should be hump-shaped under fast shifts.
comments.request: Consider this scenario seriously.
comments.quote: if you consider an additional scenario of very fast range shift rate, like in case the position of the trailing edge shifts up to the position of the formerly leading edge

comments.issue: The causal direction could be reversed, with population trend explaining range shift velocity.
comments.request: Discuss why this viewpoint was chosen and note the correlative nature.
comments.quote: But what about this opposite view of population trend being the causal effect explaining the velocity of range shift?

comments.issue: Equating climate winners with range expanders needs clarification.
comments.request: Clarify the definition.
comments.quote: Here climate winners in terms of population trend refer to range expanders in terms of species range shifts, right?

comments.issue: Line 9 wording about assumptions is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: Line 9: You mean contrary to “our assumptions”?

comments.issue: Marine ecosystems are missing from the keyword list.
comments.request: Add 'marine ecosystems' to the keywords.
comments.quote: Maybe add “marine ecosystems” in the list of keywords.

comments.issue: The statement about rapid shifts could be qualified for marine versus terrestrial systems.
comments.request: Add the marine comparison with Lenoir et al. 2020.
comments.quote: maybe add “and more rapid in marine than in terrestrial systems” (see Lenoir et al. 2020 that you cited just before)

comments.issue: The meaning of 'intolerance' on line 26 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether narrow thermal tolerance is meant.
comments.quote: What do you mean exactly by “intolerance”? Do you mean a narrow thermal tolerance?

comments.issue: Other range shift types such as the 'expand' model are not introduced.
comments.request: Introduce other range shift types, citing Lenoir and Svenning 2015.
comments.quote: I think it is worth introducing other types of rang shifts here in the introduction.

comments.issue: Unclear whether the scenario on lines 52-54 refers to the 'crash' type.
comments.request: Clarify the scenario.
comments.quote: Does that scenario refer to the “crash” type of range shift?

comments.issue: Reasoning on lines 57-59 is difficult to follow.
comments.request: Develop the reasoning.
comments.quote: I am not sure I follow the reasoning here. Could you please develop a bit?

comments.issue: Lines 64-65 about total abundance independence are confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the statement.
comments.quote: What do you mean by total abundance patterns across the range being independent of range shifts?

comments.issue: Figure 1 illustrates only the 'march' scenario.
comments.request: Illustrate the other scenarios too.
comments.quote: Figure 1 only displays expectations based on the “march” scenario, right? What about the other two scenarios?

comments.issue: A hump-shaped relationship between range shift rate and population trend was not tested.
comments.request: Test the non-linear relationship in the candidate models.
comments.quote: But what about testing a hump-shaped relationship between the rate of range shifts and the population trend?

comments.issue: The threshold defining sufficiently responsive species for inclusion is unclear and may seem arbitrary.
comments.request: Clarify the inclusion criterion.
comments.quote: How do you put the limit to define whether or not a given species is response enough to ocean warming for being included in the studied list?

comments.issue: Sampling intensity of the time series is not reported.
comments.request: Report maximum, mean and median numbers of resurveys.
comments.quote: Maybe you can provide some raw statistics here such as the maximum but also the mean and median number of resurveys for a given species at a given site or locality.

comments.issue: Fit quality of the trend models is not reported.
comments.request: Report R2 values of the linear models.
comments.quote: Do you have the R2 values of all you linear models? I think it would be nice to also report the quality of the fits used to estimate the population trends.

comments.issue: Time series resolution (number of resurveys) is not accounted for; long series with few visits may be over-weighted.
comments.request: Account for sampling intensity in the analyses.
comments.quote: not only the duration of the time series matter but also the resolution of this time series matter. Did you also account for that?

comments.issue: Units on line 115 need specifying.
comments.request: Add 'for latitudinal range shifts' after km/yr.
comments.quote: Add “for latitudinal range shifts” after “km/yr”?

comments.issue: Number of range shift rates and species extracted is not reported.
comments.request: Report these numbers.
comments.quote: How many range shift rates did you extract for how many species in total?

comments.issue: Reader should be informed about the choice made on lines 120-121 to avoid misinterpretation.
comments.request: State this choice explicitly.
comments.quote: Ok, I understand this choice but then it is important to keep the reader informed about this, to avoid misinterpretation of the results.

comments.issue: Unclear whether only fish or other taxonomic groups were included.
comments.request: Specify the groups included.
comments.quote: Do you mean “fish” species only or other groups as well, like algaea, polychetes, gastropods, etc.

comments.issue: Wording on line 140 is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: You mean “for the focal species” or “for a given species”, right?

comments.issue: A reference on line 150 is missing from the reference list.
comments.request: Add the reference.
comments.quote: Be careful, this reference is missing from the reference list at the end of your manuscript.

comments.issue: Relative longitudinal distance to the range centroid is not considered.
comments.request: Consider adding this variable.
comments.quote: What about the relative longitudinal distance to the range centroid?

comments.issue: Wording on line 163 is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: You mean “relative to the species’ latitudinal range size”.

comments.issue: Wording on line 167 is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: You mean “towards the poles relative to the latitudinal range centroid position”, right?

comments.issue: Wording on line 198 about commercial levels is ambiguous.
comments.request: Correct to 'The six commercial levels were'.
comments.quote: You mean “The six commercial levels were” instead of “The commercial level was”?

comments.issue: The chosen response-explanatory viewpoint is not justified and may imply causation.
comments.request: Explain the viewpoint and state that the link is correlative.
comments.quote: it would help the reader if you explain why you took this view point rather than the other way around

comments.issue: It is unclear whether region was fitted as a separate model, fixed effect or random effect.
comments.request: Write the actual model formula used.
comments.quote: Please write the actual formula you used here for this part of the analyses.

comments.issue: Line 249 is not crystal clear for the average reader.
comments.request: Write the statement in full.
comments.quote: If so, I would write it in full here to avoid any confusion as this is not crystal clear for the average reader, I’d say.

comments.issue: A second-order polynomial term for range shift velocity was not tried.
comments.request: Add a quadratic term to test the hump-shaped relationship.
comments.quote: Did you try to add the second order polynomial term for the velocity of range shift in the predictor terms here?

comments.issue: One typo on line 370.
comments.quote: Line 370: Correct “rage” by “range”.

comments.issue: Under a non-linear relationship, poleward declines at the leading edge are not unexpected.
comments.request: Frame the result accordingly.
comments.quote: the trend of population decline for species shifting rapidly poleward at the leading edge (cf. the cold front) is not unexpected

comments.issue: Negative population trends do not necessarily make fast shifters 'climate losers'.
comments.request: Rephrase this characterisation.
comments.quote: Not necessarily “climate losers” as such a negative population trend is expected for a very fast shifter.

comments.issue: A unimodal-to-bimodal distribution shift and range disjunction is an alternative scenario.
comments.request: Consider this alternative interpretation.
comments.quote: an alternative hypothesis is that you are witnessing the early signs of a unimodal distribution turning into a bimodal distribution

comments.issue: The statement on lines 425-426 ignores that locations may become local trailing edges.
comments.request: Qualify the statement.
comments.quote: Yes, until this location becomes so warm with very rapid climate change that it turns as a local trailing edge with early signs of decline in population trends.

reviews.assessment: Pattern may be real but is weak, variable and partly self-contradictory, undermining claims of generality.
strengths: abundance change combined with distribution shifts

comments.issue: Equatorward increases and poleward declines logically imply equatorward centroid shifts, contradicting the shift data.
comments.request: Reconcile this contradiction.
comments.quote: Increasing abundance at the equatorward side and decreasing at the poleward side of the global distribution of a species logically would produce an equatorward shift in the distribution centroid.

comments.issue: Effect explains only ~0.3% of variation, varies by region and latitude, and appears inconsequential.
comments.request: Temper claims of generality.
comments.quote: the overall weakness of response seems enough to make the effect appear inconsequential

comments.issue: For centroid shifts, spatial mismatch is collinear with spatial position, so its inclusion cannot improve the model.
comments.request: Reconsider the mismatch analysis.
comments.quote: for centroid shifts the spatial mismatch will be strongly correlated with spatial position in the geographical range

comments.issue: Ocean warming is spatially heterogeneous and short-term trends can be negative.
comments.request: Extract local temperature trends for the populations studied.
comments.quote: It would be instructive to extract the local temperature trends for the population changes used here to examine short-term variation in temperature over the course of the observations as a potential influence.

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 4 are virtually identical.
comments.request: Combine the two figures.
comments.quote: Figures 1 and 4 are virtually identical and should be combined.

comments.issue: GBIF-derived thermal limits are biased for poorly sampled species and regions.
comments.request: Spatially thin the GBIF data or use mapped distributions such as Aquamaps.
comments.quote: Species thermal limits derived directly from GBIF observations can be misleading for poorly sampled species and regions.

comments.issue: Spooner et al. 2018 relates collapses to temperature change rate, not climate velocity.
comments.request: Correct the citation or clarify the distinction.
comments.quote: The Spooner paper associated population collapses with the rate of change in temperature which is not the same as the velocity of climate

comments.issue: Many citations are incomplete or 'in press'.
comments.request: Complete and update the reference list.
comments.quote: Many incomplete and “in press” citations from some years ago.

comments.issue: Confidence intervals in Supplemental Table 3 have too few decimals to match coefficients.
comments.request: Report CIs with more decimals.
comments.quote: Confidence intervals need to be given with more decimals to match coefficients.

comments.issue: Minus signs are missing from AIC values in Supplemental Table 4.
comments.request: Correct the AIC values.
comments.quote: Minus sign missing from the AIC values for Models 1 and 2.

title: Marine fishes experiencing high-velocity range shifts may not be climate change winners

study.system: yeast population genomics; S. cerevisiae and S. paradoxus shared polymorphisms

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns that must be addressed before a revised version could be considered.

reviews.assessment: Well written and interesting; all suggestions are minor, mainly about making sensitive analyses clearer and better visualised.
strengths: results interesting to population genomics and evolutionary biology

comments.issue: The ~15 bp length criterion for diagnostic markers is not justified.
comments.request: Plot the distribution of diagnostic marker lengths.
comments.quote: not sure why the authors defined/emphasized genetic regions with the length of ~15 bp as diagnostic markers. I would be good to plot the distribution of the lengths of all diagnostic markers.

comments.issue: The S. cerevisiae consensus representatives are not labelled on the NJ tree.
comments.request: Label the representatives on the NJ tree.
comments.quote: If the authors could label these representatives on the NJ tree of 1673 S. cerevisiae strains so that readers, which would allow the readers know how diverse they are.

comments.issue: The criterion of at least five consecutive markers per block is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify the block definition.
comments.quote: Similar to the 1), why the authors defined the block with at least 5 consecutive markers. Please clarify this.

comments.issue: Coloured dots in Figure 3b are hard to see.
comments.request: Use different colours or sizes.
comments.quote: In the figure 3b, it’s hard to see the colored dots. Maybe you could use different colors or sizes.

comments.issue: No visual evidence of the competition experiments is shown.
comments.request: Include pictures before and after the competition experiments.
comments.quote: Can you include some pictures that have visual evidence before and after the competition experiments?

comments.issue: The paper has four main figures but no summary or model figure.
comments.request: Include a summary/model figure.
comments.quote: Given that this paper only contains four main figures, I would recommend that they include a summary/model figure, although this paper contains multiple diverse topics.

comments.issue: The introduction over-simplifies ILS and introgression.
comments.request: State this simplification clearly.
comments.quote: In the introduction, the description of ILS and introgression s over-simplified, this is okay at this point, but should be clearly stated.

reviews.assessment: Elegant, novel study of interspecific hybridization; minor comments on competition assay details and alternative explanations.
strengths: interesting novel insight into interspecific hybridization
corroborates the importance of hybridization in evolution

comments.issue: The competition assays lack detail, especially the selection coefficient calculation.
comments.request: Add details on the selection coefficient calculation.
comments.quote: For the competition assays, it would be good to include more details, especially the calculation of the selection coefficient of the functional PAD1-FDC1 gene cluster for the different stresses.

comments.issue: Why FDC1/PAD1 were not re-gained within S. cerevisiae by hybridization is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether intact clusters existed or the S. paradoxus copies are advantageous.
comments.quote: S. cerevisiae also has FDC1 and PAD1 genes. Why would these not be re-gained through hybridization

comments.issue: Human selection against 4VG is an unlikely explanation for the recurrent cluster loss.
comments.request: Consider environmental selection for loss of PAD1/FDC1 function.
comments.quote: Rather, the recurrent loss of this gene cluster seems to suggest that some environments (including industrial beer fermentations) may select for the loss of PAD1/FDC1 function.

comments.issue: The lower-selective-pressure explanation for Chinese ILS is unconvincing and alternative causes are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this uncertainty or provide more evidence.
comments.quote: The hypothesis that the ILS in the Chinese lineages is due to their presence in the original environment with lower selective pressure is somehow not very convincing

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and novel, but sampling bias in both species probably biased the findings.
strengths: very interesting study with novelties in both methods and results
well written with a broad readership

comments.issue: No Asian hybridization was detected although known Asian introgressions exist; sampling bias is likely.
comments.request: Include the documented Asian lineages.
comments.quote: The unexpected result is probably due to sampling bias. The majority of the documented Asian lineages of domesticated S. cerevisiae were not employed in this study.

comments.issue: An ancient Chinese S. paradoxus lineage was not compared, limiting validation of shared ancestral alleles.
comments.request: Compare this lineage in the analysis.
comments.quote: An ancient and highly diverged lineage of S. paradoxus found in China (DOI: 10.1002/yea.3688) was not compared in this study.

comments.issue: Why only the European S. paradoxus genome was used for genotyping is unclear, and the origin of Fig S1b data is unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify the genotyping approach.
comments.quote: I do not understand why only the European S. paradoxus (CBS432) genome was used for genotyping the diagnostic markers as shown in Fig. 1b.

comments.issue: The assumption that the ~24 kb region came from an extinct sister lineage is unreliable without full sampling.
comments.request: Consider the ancient Chinese lineage as a possible source.
comments.quote: Without a full sampling of S. paradoxus populations, it is not reliable to assume that the ~24 kb region on chromosome XI was introgressed from an unknown and possibly extinct S. paradoxus sister lineage.

comments.issue: The statement that Asian lineages came from temperate forests is factually incorrect.
comments.request: Correct the description of the CHN-I and CHN-IX habitats.
comments.quote: It is not correct to say “Asian S. cerevisiae lineages were isolated in a temperate forest environment.”

title: Ancient and recent origins of shared polymorphisms in yeast

study.system: early metabolism; network expansion simulations, KEGG/ATLAS biochemistry

editor_summary: Referees #1 and #2 worry about Calvin cycle artefacts and question novelty and robustness; #3 and #4 are positive, with #3 asking to tone down overinterpretation; revise before decision.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and technically solid, but the Calvin cycle result is unsupported and fold analyses are weak and potentially circular.
strengths: possible unprecedented support for mosaic/patchwork model

comments.issue: The main result lacks novelty.
comments.request: Clarify what is new relative to prior purine-autocatalysis work.
comments.quote: However, the main result does lack in novelty

comments.issue: The Calvin cycle as the first feasible carbon fixation pathway is highly unsupported and undermines the time-expansion proposal.
comments.request: Rework the Calvin cycle claim and its implications.
comments.quote: the final result presented (the Calvin cycle as the first feasible pathway to fix carbon) is extremely concerning, highly unsupported by recent and old work on early carbon fixation

comments.issue: Correlating expansion iteration with complexity is potentially circular because expansion necessarily introduces novelty.
comments.request: Address the circularity of the complexity-expansion correlation.
comments.quote: correlation between complexity and expansion iteration is potentially circular: novelty is necessarily introduced with expansion from a simpler seed set, and novelty is a requirement for complexity increase

comments.issue: Fold results are weak, the TIM barrel result is undermined by Fig. S5A, and the Mann-Whitney test may be inappropriate.
comments.request: Justify the statistical test and strengthen the fold analyses.
comments.quote: Finally, the results with folds are weak: the one with the TIM barrel becomes very much so when one examines Fig.S5A, the Mann-Whitney test may not be appropriate here and needs explanation.

comments.issue: The nucleotide-binding motif result is circular because ATP-binding folds are expected once ATP exists.
comments.request: Address the circularity of the ATP-binding fold result.
comments.quote: The result with nucleotide-binding motifs is potentially circular as well, e.g. folds that bing ATP are more prevalent when ATP exists. One would not expect the contrary under any type of selection pressure, or I may be missing some nuance.

comments.issue: The mapping between reactions and KO groups is heavily simplified and unclear, ignoring heteromeric enzymes, non-orthologous alternatives and EC ambiguities.
comments.request: Describe the reaction-KO mapping and its simplifications.
comments.quote: Technically, the results with folds are highly dependent on clustering, alignments, yet centrally on the mapping between reactions and KO groups. The latter is a very complex mapping that the authors seem to have heavily simplified (it is now unclear)

comments.issue: The fold-expansion work deserves a separate, deeper manuscript.
comments.request: Consider moving the fold-expansion work to its own paper.
comments.quote: The whole fold-expansion combined work seems to merit an independent, deeper and more careful exploration in a separate manuscript.

comments.issue: It is unclear why widespread network motifs are framed as a problem; conservation could instead resolve a composition question.
comments.request: Clarify or rephrase the framing of the continuity problem.
comments.quote: why is this a problem? Such a pattern of conservation seems to instead resolve a problem as to the composition of early chemical networks, or at least those of LUCA populations.

comments.issue: 'Uncover' overstates the result; purine autocatalysis has been known for a while.
comments.request: Soften the wording and acknowledge prior knowledge.
comments.quote: Line 92-93 "uncover" may be strong wording here. The fact that purines are autocatalytic has been known for a while.

comments.issue: Prior computational work on purine autocatalysis and on ATP/NAD requirements is not cited or contrasted.
comments.request: Cite and contrast Kun, Papp & Szathmáry 2008 and Xavier & Kauffman 2022.
comments.quote: A computational identification focused on purines using networks was done in (Kun, Papp and Szathmáry https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2008-9-3-r51) and should be cited and contrasted with this paper.

comments.issue: The ten central reactions should be listed in a main results item rather than only in the methods.
comments.request: Add a pathway drawing or table of the ten reactions in the main text.
comments.quote: only ten reactions, yet a central part of this work. Even though they are listed in the methods section, given the centrality appointed to this result by the authors

comments.issue: The coenzyme expansion result is already a key result in the cited ref 8.
comments.request: Acknowledge the overlap with ref 8 and distinguish the new contribution.
comments.quote: Line 177-180 - this is also a key result in ref 8 that the authors already cite. The 8 coenzymes added were also added in the food or seed set

comments.issue: It is not explained why Bertz complexity from 1981 was chosen over other metrics.
comments.request: Explain the choice and compare alternative metrics such as the Assembly Index.
comments.quote: Line 198 - Please explain or say a little more about Bertz complexity here and why this measure of 1981 was chosen instead of others, e.g. the recent Assembly Index that the authors cite.

comments.issue: The atmospheric redox change statement is loose and unsupported by details or evidence.
comments.request: Detail what changed, why, and what evidence supports it.
comments.quote: Line 206 - "signal of the atmospheric redox state changing throughout Earth’s history" can you detail a bit more about this change here? What and why changed, what actual evidence supports that

comments.issue: Tables S13-S14 are inconsistent; modules M00007, M00580 and M00167 are missing from Table S13, so the result cannot be verified.
comments.request: Check and fix the supplementary tables.
comments.quote: Tables S13-S14 - There is some problem/inconsistency here. E.g. TableS14 says M00007 emerges in iteration 8. When going to TableS13 to find out which module M00007 is, it is not listed there.

comments.issue: The Calvin cycle result puts the whole work under skepticism and is not explained; the anoxygenic version should be discussed.
comments.request: Explore why the Calvin cycle appears and discuss the anoxygenic version.
comments.quote: however it is heavily concerning and for any informed reader on early metabolism and biochemistry it does put the whole work and results under heavy skepticism

comments.issue: The rarity of primary metabolic extinction is already supported by several works; the added value is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how and why this work differs from previous conservation findings.
comments.quote: this is very interesting, yet it seems supported by several works that show conservation of core biochemistry across the tree of life. Please clarify how and why your work does different

comments.issue: The claim that this analysis is novel relative to Study 8 is wrong; Study 8 already used a biosphere-level network.
comments.request: Reword the comparison and consider that whole-KEGG analyses add noise of unknown age.
comments.quote: Line 322 - This needs to be reworded/rephrased. Study 8 did include an analysis of the kind made here, with a biosphere-level network (curated to exclude O2-dependent and eukaryotic metabolism).

comments.issue: The paper lacks recontextualization of how it fits with earlier network-expansion work (refs 17, 18).
comments.request: Add an essential discussion relating this work to refs 17 and 18.
comments.quote: finish the paper lacking a recontextualization of how this work fits with what was discovered earlier (refs 17 and 18).

comments.issue: Line 317 wording needs fixing.
comments.quote: Line 317 - "a sufficient"

reviews.assessment: Excellent, interesting paper recommended for publication, but the Calvin cycle ordering is likely a model artefact and the ending is weak.
strengths: excitingly concrete numbers on abstract ideas

comments.issue: Nunes Palmeira et al. (2022) on purine autocatalysis driving protocell growth, and the general-cofactor catalysis theme, are not engaged with.
comments.request: Touch on these prior results and the detrimental effect of specific catalysis.
comments.quote: For example Nunes Palmeira et al, Proc R Soc B 289: 20221469 (2022) shows that autocatalysis of purine synthesis via ATP (and also via GTP-derived cofactors, notably pterins and folates) can drive increased metabolic flux and an expanding protometabolism.

comments.issue: Harrison et al. (2022) on a purine-rich early metabolism structured around CO2 fixation is very relevant but not engaged with.
comments.request: Discuss Harrison et al. BBA Bioenergetics in relation to the central theme.
comments.quote: the temporal and biophysical patterns in the genetic code, which indicate that there was a purine-rich early metabolism which was structured around CO2 fixation and an expanding autotrophic protometabolism

comments.issue: Fig 4's ordering, with the Calvin-Benson cycle predating the acetyl-CoA and reverse Krebs cycles, is implausible and likely a model artefact.
comments.request: Reconsider and qualify the Fig 4 pathway ordering.
comments.quote: The idea that the Calvin-Benson cycle should predate the acetyl CoA pathway and the reverse (incomplete) Krebs cycle strikes me as absurd.

comments.issue: The seed set already includes all key acetyl-CoA and reverse Krebs intermediates, which must be made much clearer.
comments.request: State clearly that the seed set spans these carboxylic-acid intermediates.
comments.quote: This needs to be made much more clear in the final MS, as it is a far cry from a starting with sugars (conjouring up a primordial soup and heterotrophic origins which is still a current idea in the field)

comments.issue: Braakman and Smith (ref 62) and Camprubi et al. (2017) on chemical repetitiveness should be discussed in more detail.
comments.request: Expand the discussion of these references and clarify lines 300-301.
comments.quote: it is worth discussing Braakman and Smith (ref 62) in a little more detail and Camprubi et al IUBMB Life 69: 373-381 (2017) on the chemical repetitiveness of multiple steps through the acetyl CoA pathway

comments.issue: The ending is weak: it does not explain why a primordial purine synthesis pathway should be found, given reasons it would have been displaced.
comments.request: Strengthen the ending by addressing displacement of the purine pathway.
comments.quote: My only other point is that I found the ending very weak: why should we ever find a primordial purine synthesis pathway? There are many extremely good reasons why it would have been displaced

comments.issue: The abstract statement about missing stages is unclear; it should refer to stages missed through replacement by autocatalytic processes.
comments.request: Clear up the meaning of the abstract sentence.
comments.quote: I understand what they mean, but a continuous path must exist, that’s how life originated and well accepted. What they mean is whether there are any stages which are missed due to replacement by autocatalytic processes/elimination of alternate pathways.

comments.issue: 'Simple carboxylic acids' is vague; it is unclear whether it means formic/acetic acid only or longer chains.
comments.request: Specify which carboxylic acids are meant.
comments.quote: Line 33: Simple carboxylic acids might be a bit too vague. Does this only mean formic/acetic acid or does it include higher chain length species?

comments.issue: The statement that metabolism is a consequence of life is disputed.
comments.request: Reconsider the metabolism-life framing.
comments.quote: Lines 54-55: Well I obviously disagree with that, metabolism is life, not a consequence of it.

comments.issue: Lines 57-58 are not explicit; they suggest variant pathway forms while the references imply a distinct synthesis route (cyanide).
comments.request: Make the distinction explicit.
comments.quote: Lines 57-58: This could be more explicit. Initial reading I thought you meant variant forms of biosynthetic pathways. Instead your references imply a completely different synthesis route (cyanide)

comments.issue: No justification is given for why autocatalytic network motifs present a problem.
comments.request: Justify the claim that such motifs are problematic.
comments.quote: Lines 70-71: “The widespread occurrence of such (auto-catalytic) network motifs presents a problem for the initial emergence of ancient metabolism” – I would appreciate a justification for why the authors believe this.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 'high rates of extinction' means extinction events or selection.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of extinction here.
comments.quote: Line 71: “High rates of extinction” – As in extinction events or selection?

comments.issue: Self-citations dominate where other papers addressing similar questions should be included.
comments.request: Include additional relevant papers.
comments.quote: Line 74-75: The authors cite themselves here – fine – but there are definitely other papers which address similar questions which may be beneficial to include.

comments.issue: The topic summary is simplistic and the reference list could be expanded to primary literature.
comments.request: Expand the references, including Muchowska's reviews and primary literature.
comments.quote: Line 83-85: A simplistic summary of the topic. They could also expand the reference list, Muchowska reviews the topic, perhaps they should include some primary literature.

comments.issue: Lines 88-90 form a very complex sentence.
comments.request: Streamline the sentence for readers.
comments.quote: Line 88-90: A very complex sentence, could be streamlined for the reader. No issue with the content.

comments.issue: The '19 organic substrates' statement is ambiguous and conflicts with Fig 1's 21 CHO species.
comments.request: Resolve the ambiguity and the conflict with Fig 1.
comments.quote: Line 110: “19 Organic substrates abiotically producible starting with pyruvate and glyoxylate” – Is this ambiguous? It also appears to conflict with Fig 1 which states 21 CHO species

comments.issue: Table S6 was not provided in the documentation.
comments.request: Provide Table S6.
comments.quote: Line 111: I would like to have seen table S6 but was not provided it in the documentation.

comments.issue: The large database of hypothetical biochemistry may not have been curated for thermodynamic viability.
comments.request: Describe any curation or assessment of the hypothetical reactions.
comments.quote: Line 122-124: A database of hypothetical biochemistry is a very large domain to just include. Was there curation of these reactions to ensure that they are thermodynamically viable or any other assessment?

comments.issue: It is unclear how adding adenine compensates for the lack of PRPP, given the PRPP + adenine scavenging pathway.
comments.request: Explain the adenine network expansion mechanism.
comments.quote: I am confused here. Adding adenine to the seed results in a bigger network – but is this because it is making PRPP? From my understanding the scavenging pathway PRPP + Adenine -> AMP + PPi.

comments.issue: It is not surprising that only catalyst/hub nodes shape network dynamics.
comments.request: Acknowledge this result is expected.
comments.quote: Lines 170-172: Only the ones which act as catalyst or I bet nodes contribute to the network dynamics – is this surprising?

comments.issue: The statement that major coenzymes shape the peaks is tautological and grammatically off.
comments.request: Rewrite the coenzyme peak statement.
comments.quote: Line 186-187: “Production of major coenzymes are keyfactors shaping the observed peaks during expansion”

comments.issue: Copy edits: missing comma at line 191 and a typo in the cobalamin section.
comments.quote: Cobalamin, corrinoid and Cobamide biosynthesis reactions – typo in the first sentence?

comments.issue: Bertz complexity is not explained and no reference is given.
comments.request: Explain Bertz complexity and provide a reference.
comments.quote: Line 198-199: Bertz complexity could be explained here. There isn’t even a reference which one unfamiliar with it can refer to.

comments.issue: The alternate hypothesis for the redox/complexity trend is unclear, given the simplest possible starting materials.
comments.request: State what the alternative hypothesis would be.
comments.quote: Line 201-203: Fair enough. However, what would the alternate hypothesis be? You start from the simplest possible starting materials. There is little/no potential for the system to get simpler.

comments.issue: Starting from H2 and ammonia means reduction is the only possible direction, so the redox trend is expected.
comments.request: Acknowledge that the reducing seed set forces the trend.
comments.quote: Line 204-206: Again, you start from a seed set containing molecular hydrogen and ammonia (therefore an overall reducing system). The only potential is that reduction will take place.

comments.issue: The metal-replacement argument is weak; the stronger argument is autocatalysis outcompeting existing catalysts.
comments.request: Reframe the argument around autocatalytic competition.
comments.quote: Line 216-218: This is one (very important) part of the argument. However, we know metal ions would have already been replaced pre-LUCA. Perhaps the better argument is that an autocatalytic reaction would naturally out compete existing catalysts at some point.

comments.issue: The 'mosaic model' is not a model of metabolic pathway origins and is misunderstood here.
comments.request: Correct the mosaic model discussion and distinguish it from non-enzymatic/patchwork origins.
comments.quote: Lines 250-253: “The mosaic model” is not really a model of metabolic pathway origins. Mosaic is only mentioned in the Madea paper where they talk about plant primary metabolism given modules are derived from the 3 separate endosymbionts.

comments.issue: It is unclear what the cysteine synthesis pathway is.
comments.request: Provide details of the cysteine synthesis pathway.
comments.quote: Lines 268-269: Intrigued to see what the cysteine synthesis pathway is.

comments.issue: The result at lines 271-274 does not make sense and needs assessment.
comments.request: Assess and explain why this result occurs.
comments.quote: Lines 271-274: Now that doesn’t make sense. Will there be any assessment of why this is?

comments.issue: 'Species extinction' is a strange phrase; extinction event or natural selection?
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: Line 282-283: “Species extinction” is a strange phrase – are we referring to a widespread extinction event, or natural selection?

comments.issue: The bulk database pathways lack organismal context, so coalescence patterns may differ in real organisms.
comments.request: Acknowledge the bulk-database limitation.
