comments.issue: Onset choice and radiocarbon-based distribution bias produce inconsistencies visible in Figure 3B.
comments.request: Address these inconsistencies.
comments.quote: The inconsistencies resulting from the choice of the position of the onset of human influence and the biased distributions based on the locations of only radiocarbon dated individuals appear in Figure 3B.

comments.issue: Species names are wrong or misspelled: Strigops habroptila, Apteryx maxima, reversed Maori names, misspellings, inconsistent macrons (L392-393).
comments.request: Correct all names and diacritics.
comments.quote: Lines 392-393: The correct name for kakapo is Strigops habroptila and for great spotted kiwi, Apteryx maxima.

comments.issue: Last refugia at higher elevations simply reflect the habitat of the surviving species (L180).
comments.quote: The last refugia were at higher elevations in wet and cool climates because the last surviving populations were of species whose normal habitat was there.

comments.issue: Results are only internally consistent; no external checks against known moa biology are provided (L125ff).
comments.request: Add external validation.
comments.quote: Yes, the results may be self-consistent, but no external checks are provided.

comments.issue: Shared trait space of Dinornis is a null result; they were considered one species until 2003 (L131ff).
comments.quote: That the two island-endemic Dinornis shared a trait space envelope is basically a null result.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether results were validated externally or only internally (L140ff).
comments.request: Clarify the validation.
comments.quote: Were they “validated” against what is known about the moa themselves in the “real world” or just internally consistent within the statistical framework?

comments.issue: Habitat removal by fire would have driven declines regardless of breeding system or demographics.
comments.request: Consider habitat loss as the dominant driver.
comments.quote: Populations of moa of all taxa would have plummeted regardless of their breeding system or demographics.

comments.issue: Fig 2D distribution for P. geranoides is spurious: dates from three sites biased old, and occupancy conflicts with mapped range (L151).
comments.request: Correct the distribution and reconcile the occupancy claim.
comments.quote: The distribution shown in Fig. 2D is certainly spurious, based on actual records.

comments.issue: No fossil evidence supports higher Megalapteryx densities, and the neglected P. australis holds the youngest non-archaeological date.
comments.request: Correct the density claim and include P. australis.
comments.quote: There is no indication in the fossil record for Megalapteryx having higher population densities than say Emeus crassus in North Canterbury.

comments.issue: Euryapteryx likely followed the same trajectory as P. elephantopus under the same pressures.
comments.request: Reconsider the Euryapteryx result.
comments.quote: Euryapteryx in the eastern South Island would have followed the pattern of P.elephantopus, coming as it did under the same pressures at the same time.

comments.issue: Emeus crassus, an eastern-lowland species, is absent and would be a useful internal test of the methodology.
comments.request: Add Emeus crassus as a test case.
comments.quote: one might ask where is Emeus crassus in the analysis? Wouldn’t a species whose remains have been found only in the eastern lowlands not be a useful internal test for the methodology?

comments.issue: The E. c. curtus silhouette has absurdly long legs.
comments.request: Correct the silhouette.
comments.quote: As another aside, the silhouette of E. c. curtus has absurdly long legs

comments.issue: Fire-driven decline means the statistical analysis was not needed to conclude sympatric species died out together (L170ff).
comments.quote: it probably did not need the statistical analysis of spatiotemporal patterns of population extirpation to conclude that the sympatric species involved died out at the same time

comments.issue: Latitudinal centres are based only on the few dated individuals while large undated collections are ignored.
comments.request: Use the full museum collections.
comments.quote: Contracting to their “latitudinal centers (sic)” means little in the South Island, and is also, as noted before, the determination of those centres were determined only on the few dated individuals.

comments.issue: Anomalopteryx is omitted despite an abundant fossil record, though its trajectory matters for kakapo conservation.
comments.request: Include Anomalopteryx.
comments.quote: And there is no mention whatsoever of Anomalopteryx, which has an abundant fossil record but a slender radiocarbon-dated record.

comments.issue: Calling the mountains 'suboptimal habitats' is wrong for Megalapteryx and P. australis (L178-179).
comments.request: Correct this characterisation.
comments.quote: What is new is the proposal that these were “suboptimal habitats”. For Megalapteryx and P. australis those were their normal habitats.

comments.issue: Higher lowland population densities are not novel (L182-184).
comments.quote: This result, that lowland areas tended to have higher moa population densities, is not novel.

comments.issue: It is unclear how areas can be east and west of a latitudinal centre; the claim is an artefact of minimal data (L186).
comments.request: Clarify or remove the claim.
comments.quote: How can “these areas” be located “east and west” of the latitudinal centre for any of the three species?

comments.issue: Conservation implications are interpretations, not results, and belong in the discussion (L188).
comments.request: Move them to the discussion.
comments.quote: Are conservation implications really “results”? Surely they can only be interpretations which are best included and discussed in the section following.

comments.issue: Discussion repeats the Introduction and Results and is twice as long as needed (L201).
comments.request: Halve the discussion.
comments.quote: Much of what follows repeats matter in the Introduction and Results. It is 114 lines long and could easily be shortened by half.

comments.issue: The 'first evidence of interspecific variation' claim rests on under 5% of the available geographic information and restates what was known.
comments.request: Temper the novelty claim.
comments.quote: The claim that “process-driven modelling provides the first evidence of substantial interspecific variation in extinction trajectories” rests on the results of a study using less 5% of the available geographic information.

comments.issue: Low dispersal would make Euryapteryx more vulnerable, not better able to survive humans (L241-242).
comments.request: Re-examine this mechanism.
comments.quote: How could a low dispersive capacity, even if it had one, make a Euryapteryx population more able to survive the presence of an increasing human population living in the same area?

comments.issue: 'Overexploitation by expanding human populations' ignores wholesale forest removal by fire and the recent human population estimates (L247).
comments.request: Include fire and population estimates.
comments.quote: “Overexploitation by expanding human populations” ignores the reality of wholesale removal of the lowland forests by Polynesian fires

comments.issue: Overlap between surviving birds and high-altitude moa has little value for 'pathways of decline' when species already declined and drivers differ (L275ff).
comments.request: Clarify the added value.
comments.quote: Of what significance is showing that the distributions of surviving flightless birds are the same as those for (the high altitude-adapted) moa to “likely pathways of decline” for those species

comments.issue: Result at L280-282 was realised without this modelling.
comments.quote: This is hardly original: it was realised without the statistical modelling presented here.

comments.issue: No evidence that lowland species found last refuges in mountains; this was invisible because taxa were lumped (L288).
comments.request: Correct the statement.
comments.quote: There is no indication whatsoever that any of the lowland species found last refuges in the mountainous areas.

comments.issue: Too few Euryapteryx ages make North Island statistical differences meaningless; mapped distributions overstate occurrences.
comments.request: Qualify these results.
comments.quote: So few ages are available for Euryapteryx away from the extreme north make any statistical differences implied for the whole North Island meaningless.

comments.issue: 'Habitat suitability' is undefined while species habitats remain poorly known.
comments.request: Define habitat suitability and its basis.
comments.quote: How is “habitat suitability” defined and how can that be used when we are still in the process of working out species habitats in more than very general terms?

comments.issue: The basic occurrence plot indicates density of records rather than presence or abundance.
comments.request: Relabel or reinterpret the plot.
comments.quote: The basic plot is more an indication of density of records than presence or abundance of taxa.

reviews.assessment: Supportive with mostly descriptive clarifications and questions, which the authors should be able to address easily.

comments.issue: Introduction should emphasise that current-day drivers differ from those of moa and only geographic signatures are compared.
comments.request: Add this background point to the Introduction.
comments.quote: it would be useful to emphasize in the Introduction a background point made towards the end of the Discussion, which is that the “current-day drivers of decline of New Zealand’s native birds differ from those that drove the collapse and loss of moa”

comments.issue: The assumption that large samples overcome uneven sampling and taphonomy in presence-only niche estimation is not stated.
comments.request: State this assumption explicitly.
comments.quote: it may be worth explicitly stating the assumption that large sample sizes at broad spatial scales are expected to overcome factors, such as uneven sampling by researchers and taphonomy, that will interfere with identifications of the niche.

comments.issue: Whether uncertainty in spatially explicit climate projections is considered during the fossil-climate intersection is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how climate-projection uncertainty is handled.
comments.quote: Given that uncertainty in spatially-explicit climate projections likely vary across space and time, is uncertainty in the climate projections also considered during this intersection?

comments.issue: Edaphic conditions are not reconstructed through time; the constant-condition assumption and correlated edaphic variables are unaddressed.
comments.request: Justify the assumption and consider trimming correlated edaphic variables.
comments.quote: given that these conditions are not reconstructed through time, what evidence can be used to justify the assumption that these conditions did not change over recent millennia?

comments.issue: Egg harvest is modelled as a flat rate while bird harvest is density-dependent, though eggs should also be harder to find when birds are few.
comments.request: Justify or change the egg-harvest function.
comments.quote: I am curious why egg harvest (mentioned on line 359) was assumed to be at a flat rate in the presence of humans while bird harvesting considers a dependence on population density

comments.issue: The fraction of data excluded by the post-2008 reliability criterion is not reported, though reliable older dates exist.
comments.request: Report the excluded fraction and justify the criterion.
comments.quote: it would be useful to specify what fraction of the data are excluded based on the criterion that reliable dates are ones generated after 2008

comments.issue: Model evaluation against last known fossil locations is sensitive to the Signor-Lipps effect; preceding dated individuals should be considered.
comments.request: Evaluate using several preceding dated locations.
comments.quote: How would model evaluation change if the last known fossil locations changed with future work?

comments.issue: The link between simulated Maori expansion and commensal spread is unclear (L261).
comments.request: Develop or cut the commensal point.
comments.quote: It is currently unclear how the simulated past expansion of Maori populations is tied with the spread of commensals

comments.issue: The claim that ancient extinction dynamics can inform pathways of decline for extant species should be reworded to emphasise similar geographic patterns only.
comments.request: Reword the statement.
comments.quote: I recommend rewording the statement “Our integrative modelling shows how knowledge of the spatial dynamics of ancient extinctions can inform likely pathways of decline for extant species and vice versa”

comments.issue: Future research directions and which conclusions are likely stable under new data are not discussed.
comments.request: Add a future-research outlook.
comments.quote: I think that the thorough work gives an excellent opportunity to briefly highlight areas of future research that can improve the process-based models on New Zealand.

comments.issue: Line-level edits: L85 wording 'and their services to nature'; supplement 'orthographic'/'orographic', 'group'/'groups', 'SPEM'/'SEPM'.
comments.quote: Page 4 mentions “orthographic” – Should this be “orographic”?

comments.issue: Figure S6 colours are hard to read and the box/whisker parameters are unspecified.
comments.request: Choose clearer colours and explain the boxplot elements.
comments.quote: Figure S6 nicely uses the same coloring as Fig. 1, but the colors in the reordered boxplots are a bit harder to read, so it may be best to choose another set of colors.

comments.issue: Figure S13b shows postbomb extinction estimates; extinction estimates should be constrained to before present.
comments.request: Enforce the before-present requirement.
comments.quote: Figures S13b includes some postbomb extinction estimates in the sensitivity analysis for Pachyornis geranoides – What explains this unexpected result? A requirement that extinction estimates are before present should be enforced.

reviews.assessment: Great, clear, well-executed modelling paper with important conservation implications; only minor optional suggestions on differential extinction, context and overselling.
strengths: great paper with state-of-the-art pattern-oriented modelling

comments.issue: Why moa species and subspecies went extinct at different times is not explicitly evaluated (body size, life history, phylogeny; cf. Alroy 2001).
comments.request: Expand this evaluation and simulate current species in the model.
comments.quote: I would like to see a more explicit evaluation of why moas species and subspecies went extinct at different lines (perhaps expanding a bit and making more explicit the comments of lines 131-138).

comments.issue: The match between past hunter-gatherer threats and today's complex threats plus conservation actions is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the conservation context more.
comments.quote: how does the context of both extinctions or potential extinctions match?

comments.issue: The paragraph starting at line 252 is unfair to macroecologists and risks overselling the findings.
comments.request: Soften the framing of the contradiction.
comments.quote: Anyway, just a minor note to avoid “overselling” your nice findings.

title: Ecological dynamics of moa extinctions reveal convergent refugia that today harbour flightless birds

study.system: global extreme wildfires; MODIS satellite fire radiative power, 2000s–2022

editor_summary: Editor says reviewer concerns must be addressed along with editorial concerns; a revised manuscript with highlighted changes is required before a final decision.

reviews.assessment: Finds the paper interesting, well written and important for the wildfire debate, requesting only minor revisions and added references.
strengths: directly addresses the debate on changing wildfire frequency and magnitude

comments.issue: Additional United States references are needed to better contextualize the paper in the extant literature.
comments.request: Integrate the suggested United States references.
comments.quote: I have suggested a few additional references from the United States to improve the paper and context with the extant literature.

comments.issue: The manuscript needs a thorough revision to reduce passive voice and to replace 'fitted' with 'fit' throughout.
comments.quote: In general, I think the paper could use a thorough revision to reduce passive voice.

comments.issue: Recent extreme fire years, such as 2020 in the western US, are not discussed.
comments.request: Comment on recent extreme fire years in the results or discussion.
comments.quote: I also would like to see the authors comment on the most recent extreme fire years in the results/discussion.

comments.issue: A key reference on vapor pressure deficit effects on plants and fuel moisture is missing.
comments.request: Add the suggested vapor pressure deficit reference.
comments.quote: Be sure to add the reference below about vapor pressure deficit effects on plants and fuel moisture

reviews.assessment: Finds the study original, well-executed and widely interesting, with questions about continent definitions, event counting and satellite choice.
strengths: great interest to fire researchers and broader communities

comments.issue: 'Comprised' is used incorrectly in two sentences.
comments.request: Correct the usage of 'comprised'.
comments.quote: Lines 12 and 103- I don’t think “comprised” is used correctly in these sentences.

comments.issue: The paper understates that fires are regular, often beneficial ecosystem processes.
comments.request: State more strongly that many fires contribute to ecosystem health.
comments.quote: I think it would be great if the authors could make the point more strongly that fires can actually be beneficial for ecosystems

comments.issue: Including eastern Russia in Europe makes the continent analysis odd and potentially misleading.
comments.request: Put Russia with Asia, add a supplement map, or drop the continent analysis.
comments.quote: I think it’s quite odd to include eastern Russia in Europe, and I don’t understand why the authors would make the decision to use the United Nations designation of continents.

comments.issue: Consecutive-day extreme events may represent single fires, but their number is not reported.
comments.request: Report how many actual fire events underlie the patterns.
comments.quote: I’m curious how many “events” were the same cells on back-to-back days, representing potentially the same actual fire events.

comments.issue: Terra-alone data make the trend look more dramatic, creating a possible appearance of bias.
comments.request: Address the appearance of bias from selecting the steeper Terra trend.
comments.quote: I find the argument that using the Aqua data would unfairly down-bias the frequency of extreme events in 2001 unconvincing.

reviews.assessment: Finds the research important but raises serious concerns about Terra-only data, orbital drift and missing overpass corrections that may overstate extreme fire proportions.
strengths: important research question on extreme fire trends

comments.issue: MODIS product idiosyncrasies were not discussed with the scientists who generate the data.
comments.request: Consult the MODIS data producers about product idiosyncrasies.
comments.quote: There are many idiosyncrasies to the MODIS fire products that could have been exposed earlier had the authors reached out to the scientists behind these products.

comments.issue: Using Terra alone biases the results toward more extreme fire events and looks like cherry picking.
comments.request: Justify the Terra-only choice or include Aqua.
comments.quote: it appears that using Terra alone, from their own evidence, biases the results to show more extreme fire events and seems to be cherry picking

comments.issue: The extra Terra record is only about 18–20 months, not the longer period implied.
comments.request: Correct the claimed gain from the extended time frame.
comments.quote: The extended time frame the authors state to justify using Terra is 11/2000 – 6/2022, only 20 months

comments.issue: Terra has been drifting since 2020, altering observation timing and narrowing the swath.
comments.request: Account for Terra's orbital drift and reduced observations.
comments.quote: Not only does this impact the timing of events observed, but the swath is narrowing, meaning less observations.

comments.issue: Terra misses the afternoon peak of fire intensity that Aqua captures, confounding the analysis.
comments.request: Include Aqua data or address the missed afternoon peak.
comments.quote: Aqua’s early afternoon overpass time truly captures the more intense phase of wildfires and excluding this data could have confounding implications for your analysis.

comments.issue: Raw text files do not correct for more overpasses at higher latitudes, possibly overstating boreal fire proportions.
comments.request: Use overpass-corrected fire pixel counts following Giglio et al. 2006.
comments.quote: these text files do not account for a greater number of overpasses at higher latitudes

comments.issue: Terminology edits: 'radiative energy' should be instantaneous, and 'predicted' wildfires should be 'hot spots'.
comments.quote: 230 I would not use “predicted” wildfires as the definition implies something occurring in the future.

title: Increasing frequency and intensity of the most extreme wildfires on Earth

study.system: brittle star Amphiura filiformis; genome assembly and regeneration transcriptomics

editor_summary: Editor: reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns about the genome assembly and regeneration claims; a revised version would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Data-rich but the genome quality, novelty and functional support fall short of the claims.
strengths: plenty of genomic and transcriptomic data

comments.issue: Genome quality is doubtful: sperm DNA heterozygosity, unexplained diploid assembly and haplotype removal, insufficient quality assessment, and 20 versus 21 chromosomes.
comments.request: Thoroughly validate the assembly with different assemblers, individuals and quality metrics.
comments.quote: The genome quality is the core of the whole paper, yet there’re several spots make me concern about it.

comments.issue: Biological implications of Hox cluster rearrangements are not explored developmentally.
comments.request: Study Hox spatio-temporal expression in embryos, ideally with single-cell or spatial methods.
comments.quote: The manuscript would benefit significantly from a deeper exploration into the biological implications of Hox cluster rearrangements.

comments.issue: The tandem-duplication contribution to larval skeleton and bioluminescence is claimed without functional evidence.
comments.request: Provide functional evidence or temper the claim.
comments.quote: yet they fail to provide functional analysis or evidence to support this claim

comments.issue: The three-phase co-expression result is anticipated and lacks functional depth.
comments.request: Identify key genes functionally and validate with histological/functional studies.
comments.quote: The discovery of co-expression clusters corresponding to three phases of arm regeneration is somewhat anticipated

comments.issue: Whether conserved gene modules reflect ancestral origin or convergent evolution remains ambiguous.
comments.request: Provide evidence distinguishing the two hypotheses.
comments.quote: the evolutionary history behind this observation—whether it is ancestral origin or a product of convergent evolution—remain ambiguous

comments.issue: Bulk RNA-seq explants lack resolution and the five opposite-expression genes lack functional validation.
comments.request: Add functional assays for these genes.
comments.quote: The explant experiments conducted in the study rely predominantly on bulk RNA-seq, which lacks the resolution necessary for drawing definitive conclusions.

comments.issue: The biological significance and boundary features of the most-rearranged genome are not explored.
comments.request: Analyse rearrangement boundaries and discuss their evolutionary significance.
comments.quote: It's important to explore the biological significance of identifying the 'most rearranged genome' and the evolutionary reasons for this.

comments.issue: The proportion of expanded regeneration genes that are regulated, and their cluster distribution, is unclear.
comments.request: Report these proportions per co-expression cluster.
comments.quote: it is important to determine what proportion of these genes show significant regulation during the arm regeneration process

comments.issue: Different expansion patterns of gene families may indicate variation in regeneration capability that is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this possible variation among species.
comments.quote: Does this suggest a variation in regeneration capabilities among these species?

comments.issue: Wound-response genes are most highly expressed in the non-regenerating control, which is unexplained.
comments.request: Investigate this unexpected pattern.
comments.quote: the non-regenerating control group exhibits the highest expression levels of wound-response genes

comments.issue: Whether keratan sulfate gene expansion reflects specialization is not tested.
comments.request: Analyse these genes' expression during regeneration.
comments.quote: The author should examine the expression patterns of genes involved in keratan sulfate metabolism (Line 350) during regeneration

comments.issue: FGF signalling and alx1 roles reported in the authors' previous papers are not mentioned here.
comments.request: Discuss this discrepancy with previous work.
comments.quote: the authors suggest FGF signaling and alx1 genes play important roles during the regeneration process of brittle stars, which was neither discovered nor mentioned in this paper

comments.issue: The Annunziata et al. (2014) citation does not support the Hox7 statement; Li et al. (2018) is correct.
comments.request: Correct the citation.
comments.quote: However, it didn’t mention Hox7 at all in this cited paper. The correct citation should be Li et al. (Cell Discovery 2018).

reviews.assessment: Impressive datasets, but the narrative is disjointed and the proliferation and motif results are overinterpreted.

comments.issue: The two themes (echinoderm genomics and regeneration comparisons) are disjointed and the genome-centred framing is not justified.
comments.request: Strengthen narrative links and explain how the genome enables the regeneration analyses.
comments.quote: The rationale for linking these two themes within this same narrative, and how each section motivates the next, could be clearer.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether previous knowledge is broad, echinoderm-specific or brittle-star-specific, and what is genuinely new.
comments.request: Clarify these distinctions throughout.
comments.quote: it would be helpful for the statements to be more clear about this

comments.issue: The Fig. 4A schematic lacks known regeneration landmarks such as EdU results and blastema appearance.
comments.request: Expand the schematic with these landmarks.
comments.quote: expanding the schematic in Figure 4A depicting the transcriptomic sampling to include additional information corresponding to known features of regeneration relevant to the morphological stages

comments.issue: Shared proliferation modules are almost a null expectation given conserved proliferative machinery.
comments.request: Rewrite the interpretation of the proliferation results.
comments.quote: finding shared gene modules associated with proliferation would almost be a null hypothesis of sorts for this type of comparison

comments.issue: The earliest timepoint (48 hpa) may already miss the wound-induced signals that launch regeneration.
comments.request: Address the limitations of the existing timepoints.
comments.quote: it seems like the earliest time point sampled in this study (48 hpa) is nearing the end of the wound-healing phase and entering the proliferation phase

comments.issue: Wound-healing cluster genes are also highly expressed in control tissue, which is unexpected.
comments.request: Address this pattern.
comments.quote: the expression profiles of genes in clusters A1 and A2, which are proposed to correspond to the wound healing process, seem to also have high expression in the control tissue

comments.issue: Findings are not placed in the context of broader themes and modes of regeneration evolution.
comments.request: Discuss implications for regeneration evolution and other regeneration modes.
comments.quote: it might also be interesting to place these findings in the context of common themes in regeneration

comments.issue: The 6kb motif analysis may capture many irrelevant binding sites and is not checked against TF expression timing.
comments.request: Narrow to accessible regions and check TF expression timing.
comments.quote: a total of 6kb surrounding a TSS is likely to harbor many potential binding sites, especially if the regions have not been narrowed down to those that are accessible at a particular time

comments.issue: The rationale for the manually curated gene lists is not given.
comments.request: Justify the curated gene lists.
comments.quote: Why were these specific gene groups chosen for inclusion into manually curated lists?

comments.issue: Spatial Hox expression knowledge in brittle stars and echinoderms is not summarized.
comments.request: Add this context.
comments.quote: is there any knowledge about spatial expression in brittle stars, or more broadly other echinoderms?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the tandem duplications are a candidate case study or a genome-wide search.
comments.request: Clarify how these duplications were selected.
comments.quote: are there other examples of tandem duplications found in the genome, or were these two groups used as a candidate case study

comments.issue: The section would benefit from stating upfront that stages correspond to known regeneration phases.
comments.request: Add this framing sentence.
comments.quote: It could help set up the findings in this section to state at the beginning that the stages were chosen to correspond to the known regenerative phases from previous regeneration studies

comments.issue: Late axial specification is surprising and its consistency with previous brittle star reports is unclear.
comments.request: Compare with previous reports.
comments.quote: It seems surprising that axial specification would be occurring so late in regeneration, is this consistent with previous reports in brittle stars?

comments.issue: The criteria for considering a cluster co-expressed are not stated in the main text.
comments.request: State the co-expression criterion.
comments.quote: Being clearer in the main text about the criteria for considering a cluster to be co-expressed would help to understand the analyses in this section

comments.issue: Extending conserved proliferation to a common proliferative cell type is a stretch without cellular data.
comments.request: Soften this claim.
comments.quote: expanding the finding that proliferation seems conserved to talking about a common proliferative cell type seems like a stretch

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive, clear and well-written resource; asks for clarifications on gene counts, methods and sampling.

comments.issue: The number of regeneration-related genes in the genome versus expanded/contracted families is not reported, making the expansion claim hard to assess.
comments.request: Report total and per-GO-term counts of genes in expanded and contracted families.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to know how many total “regeneration-related” genes/genes annotated with the GO term “regeneration” there are in the A. filiformis genome overall.

comments.issue: Keratan sulfate metabolism is not defined and the expanded gene family is not named in the text.
comments.request: Define keratan sulfate and name the gene family.
comments.quote: For those who are not familiar with keratan sulfate metabolism, it might help to define it and explain that keratan sulfate is a glycosaminoglycan in the text.

comments.issue: How transcription factors were identified via PFAM domains is insufficiently described.
comments.request: Describe the PFAM search, parameters and curation.
comments.quote: Can this be described in more detail? How exactly did you run the PFAM search?

comments.issue: The difference between gene-list and gene-ontology enrichment tests is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the two enrichment tests.
comments.quote: Is there a difference between “Gene lists enrichment tests” and “Gene ontology enrichment tests”?

comments.issue: Three of the five opposite-expression genes are not discussed with respect to known vertebrate functions.
comments.request: Discuss these genes or expand the Discussion.
comments.quote: it would be nice if the other three genes could be more clearly discussed regarding if their functions are known from vertebrates or not

comments.issue: How the 43 explant groups relate to final samples and replication is unclear.
comments.request: Report replicates per timepoint and section and total samples sequenced.
comments.quote: I would like to know how many replicates were there for each time point and each section?

title: The brittle star genome illuminates the genetic basis of animal appendage regeneration

study.system: global pollen records; Holocene floristic diversity

editor_summary: Editor asks to add Neotoma data for better global coverage, implement additional diversity metrics, and explicitly examine human impact.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and thorough, but site exclusions lack transparency and key South African and Australian records are missing.

comments.issue: Which sites were excluded and why is not documented, including key South African and Australian sites.
comments.request: Provide a supplementary table of excluded sites and reasons.
comments.quote: there is a serious lack of transparency when it comes to which sites have been excluded and why

comments.issue: Dataset was compiled some time ago, so recently available Australasian sites are missing.
comments.request: Include the newly available Australasian sites.
comments.quote: the data gathering appears to have been carried out some time ago, as more sites are now available from the Australasian region and should be included

comments.issue: The phrase 'human-driven declines' at Line 38 is unclear.
comments.request: Specify what is declining.
comments.quote: Specific comments: Line 38: Human-driven declines in what?

comments.issue: The sentence at Lines 277-282 is very long.
comments.request: Rephrase the long sentence.
comments.quote: Lines 277-282: Very long sentence, consider rephrasing.

comments.issue: Legacy datasets may be outdated; recent Indo-Pacific Neotoma additions are missing.
comments.request: Update the dataset with recent Neotoma additions.
comments.quote: When was the last update of the Legacy datasets? Neotoma has seen many additions from the Indo-Pacific region over the last 2 years

comments.issue: The Indo-Pacific Pollen Database, part of Neotoma, was omitted.
comments.request: Include the Indo-Pacific Pollen Database.
comments.quote: The Indo-Pacific Pollen Database is also a constituent database in Neotoma and has to be included

comments.issue: Exclusion counts are unreported and key Australian and South African sites are missing.
comments.request: Report exclusion counts and include the missing key sites.
comments.quote: There are several key sites missing from Australia (e.g. Lynch’s Crater) and South Africa (e.g. Wonderkrater, any Drakensberg sites, etc.)

comments.issue: The minimum count cutoff of 500 grains is far too high.
comments.request: Justify or lower the 500-grain cutoff.
comments.quote: 500 is too high, many researchers choose to “only” count 300 grains. Why has 500 been chosen as the cutoff?

reviews.assessment: Extremely well-written and comprehensive with an important message, though the aims and abstract need clearer articulation.
strengths: will have general interest among readers

comments.issue: The question and aims are articulated too late in the manuscript.
comments.request: State the question and aims earlier.
comments.quote: I do feel that the question and aims could be articulated a little more effectively at an earlier stage in the manuscript

comments.issue: The abstract does not clearly state the question and main message.
comments.request: Clarify the question and main message in the abstract.
comments.quote: the abstract could benefit from the addition of some clarification of question and main message

comments.issue: The complex methods workflow is hard for non-specialists to follow.
comments.request: Add a conceptual workflow figure for non-experts.
comments.quote: The addition of a conceptual or workflow type figure (as an extended figure) would help to guide non experts through the process

comments.issue: Compositional turnover relies on abundance-based Bray-Curtis; a presence/absence metric is missing.
comments.request: Add a non-abundance-based turnover metric such as Jaccard.
comments.quote: the study would be more complete were it to include a non abundance based compositional turnover metric such as Jaccard

comments.issue: A key supporting reference for balanced gains and losses is missing.
comments.request: Cite Dornelas et al. 2019 for this argument.
comments.quote: Lines 43-46 suggest the inclusion of Dornelas et al 2019 [2] in support of the balanced gains and losses argument

comments.issue: No map shows the distribution of study sites by biome.
comments.request: Add a map of study sites by biome.
comments.quote: The addition of a map illustrating the study sites by biome might be nice (as an extended figure)

comments.issue: Vertical grey lines in the figures distract from the plotted results.
comments.request: Make the grey lines fainter.
comments.quote: maybe they could be a little fainter as I find them a bit distracting from the main result in the plot

reviews.assessment: Well-implemented analyses, but the study is not novel, the human-driver evidence is indirect and several interpretations are unspecific.

comments.issue: Human impact is claimed as a major driver but pollen-based human indicators were not used.
comments.request: Relate pollen-based human indicators to diversity changes.
comments.quote: As the author specifically targets human impact as a major driver it would have been nice to make use of human indicators contained in pollen records

comments.issue: No a priori testable hypotheses are set up.
comments.request: Set up testable hypotheses and expected differences among metrics.
comments.quote: Also setting up a testable hypothesis would have been nice. Eg which difference in the diversity changes among the alphadiversity measure would you apriori expect

comments.issue: No synthesis figure visualises the main findings.
comments.request: Add a synthesis figure of the main findings.
comments.quote: A synthesis figure visualizing the main findings of the paper would have been nice

comments.issue: The study is not really new; several previous pollen-diversity studies exist.
comments.request: Clarify how this study advances beyond previous work.
comments.quote: Overall such kind of study is not really new. Several previous studies investigated pollen diversity

comments.issue: Attribution to interacting earth-system components is unsupported; one factor alone might explain the pattern.
comments.request: Justify why interactions rather than single factors cause the differences.
comments.quote: it is not very clear how you came to the conclusion that the interactions among the different earth system components were causing the difference

comments.issue: Differing pollen archives and source-area sizes may bias diversity trends and were not tested.
comments.request: Test whether archive type or source-area size affects trends.
comments.quote: Pollen records originate from very different archives. It would have been nice to test whether or not this impact diversity trends

comments.issue: A direct comparison of the quantitative turnover results is missing.
comments.request: Add a direct comparison of turnover results.
comments.quote: Here a direct comparison of the quantitative turnover results would have been nice

comments.issue: The new finding is unclear and the conservation statement is not helpful.
comments.request: Explain what is new and how the study helps understand the complexity.

comments.quote: is Inslm specific to the neurohypophysis neurons or is it expressed also in other neuronal subpopulations?

comments.issue: A relevant study on the anterior patterning GRN is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Gattoni et al. 2023.
comments.quote: Gattoni et al (BioRxiv 2023, doi: https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.03.13.532359) report the GRN leading to anterior patterning. Should be cited

comments.issue: The claim that three CNS regions were already shown needs a reference.
comments.request: Add a supporting citation.
comments.quote: The authors state previous work has already shown the presence of three CNS regions characterized by distinct TF expression. This requires a reference.

comments.issue: The sentence comparing with sea urchin and sea anemone is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify whether in line with or in contrast to those results.
comments.quote: Does that mean, in line with those results or in contrast to those results. Please clarify.

reviews.assessment: Substantial problems: insufficient methodological documentation, confusing annotations and unrigorous cross-species comparisons undermine reliability.

comments.issue: Detailed cell-type assignments are undocumented and unvalidated, making the precise positions doubtful.
comments.request: Document the evidence for every cluster assignment, ideally with multi-marker ISH.
comments.quote: the manuscript presents no documentation as to how this was done, and consequently I am skeptical of the precise assignments

comments.issue: Figure 2 is never referenced or discussed.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Figure 2 in the text.
comments.quote: Figure 2 is never referenced nor explicitly discussed in the manuscript.

comments.issue: The developmental trajectories in Figures 3 and 4 are difficult to follow and compare.
comments.request: Improve the trajectory figures for readability.
comments.quote: I found the developmental trajectories in figures 3 and 4 to be difficult to follow and compare.

comments.issue: Trajectory labels are inconsistent and differentiated cells are labelled as early germ layers.
comments.request: Relabel end stages by organs, nervous system regions or cell families.
comments.quote: It would be more appropriate to label the end stages according to the differentiated organs, nervous system regions, or cell type families/classes

comments.issue: The cross-species comparison lacks a described basis, including AP-axis assignments and orthologue identification.
comments.request: Describe the comparison basis and use rigorous tools such as SAMap or SATURN.
comments.quote: it is unclear how these comparisons were done nor the basis for labeling homologous developmental trajectories

comments.issue: A similar published study is not mentioned or compared.
comments.request: Discuss and compare with Ma et al. 2022.
comments.quote: The manuscript makes no mention of a similar study published last year in cell reports (Ma et al. 2022).

reviews.assessment: The analyses, especially the inferred lineages and the cross-species comparison, do not sufficiently support the conclusions.
strengths: single-cell data quality better than existing amphioxus atlases
intriguing idea of distinct anterior and posterior neural origins

comments.issue: Lineage reconstruction relies solely on co-clustering without RNA velocity, method checks or validation against known lineages.
comments.request: Validate lineages experimentally or with other methods such as CellRank2.
comments.quote: the current analysis seems to exclusively rely on co-clustering of cells collected at different stages, which was not substantiated by RNA velocity analysis

comments.issue: The cross-species comparison hinges on a small manually selected gene set.
comments.request: Use computational approaches such as SAMap for whole-transcriptome comparison.
comments.quote: The comparative analysis of the paper also appears to hinge on a small, manually selected set of genes

comments.issue: The claim that whole-transcriptome comparison failed contradicts published homology among vertebrate embryonic cells.
comments.request: Discuss the discrepancy and rule out a methodological deficiency.
comments.quote: which seems to contrast the published studies indicating broad homology between vertebrate embryonic cells

comments.issue: The FoxQ2 and Bra knockout interpretations rest on low-resolution colour-metric ISH images.
comments.request: Strengthen or temper the mutant interpretations.
comments.quote: It takes substantial faith to believe the interpretation of FoxQ2 and Bra KO animals, which is difficult based on the low resolution color-metric in situ images

comments.issue: Higher-resolution images are needed to see which cell types and genes are lost in FoxQ2a knockouts.
comments.request: Provide higher-resolution ISH images.
comments.quote: Could the authors provide higher resolution images to show specifically which cell types and genes are lost or retained in FoxQ2a knockout?

comments.issue: Knocking out both Bra genes simultaneously is puzzling; lineage-specific TFs might be better targets.
comments.request: Consider knocking out TFs specific to each predicted lineage.
comments.quote: In order to confirm the split of lineages, is it better to KO TFs that are predicted to be more specific to each lineage?

comments.issue: Figure 2 is not discussed in the text and is hard to understand.
comments.request: Discuss and clarify Figure 2.
comments.quote: Figure 2 is not discussed at all in the main text, the figure itself is also hard to understand.

comments.issue: The boxes in Figure 4A and the gene spacing are unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify the boxes and add developmental time.
comments.quote: could the authors clarify what the boxes represent?

comments.issue: A reference for the apical organ across lineages is missing at line 172.
comments.request: Add the missing reference.
comments.quote: Line 172: Missing a reference for apical organ across lineages.

title: Evolutionary origin of the chordate nervous system revealed by amphioxus developmental trajectories

study.system: Komodo dragon and other reptile teeth; chemical and structural imaging

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable interest but raise substantial concerns; a revision is invited, specifically to broaden the comparative sample as recommended by reviewer 2.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and supported by advanced methods; asks for broader discussion of fossil varanids and squamates before recommending publication.
strengths: advanced technological methods justify the conclusions

comments.issue: Recently published Georgalis et al. (2023) on varanid tooth serration and pulp cavity is not mentioned.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Georgalis et al. (2023).
comments.quote: The authors were probably unaware of the very recently published paper of Georgalis et al. (2023), where there was documentation of the pulp cavity of extant Varanus and Lanthanotus with the aid of μCT scanning

comments.issue: Serrated teeth in fossil varanids, including the Greek occurrence with four serration types, are not discussed.
comments.request: Add sentences on fossil varanid tooth serration with references.
comments.quote: I suggest mentioning somewhere (perhaps in the Introduction or the Discussion) a couple of sentences about the presence of serrated teeth in fossil varanids.

comments.issue: Cutting edges of Lanthanotus, Shinisaurus, and helodermatids are not mentioned.
comments.request: Discuss these taxa with the suggested references.
comments.quote: I would suggest mentioning something also (what is known about the cutting edges) for Lanthanotus but also for Shinisaurus

comments.issue: The paper jumps from extant lizards to Cretaceous dinosaurs without discussing extinct varanoids or anguimorphs.
comments.request: Add extinct varanoid comparisons and cite primary references.
comments.quote: here, the authors “jump” directly from the extant lizards to the Cretaceous dinosaurs. It would be so good, in the intermediate, to mention what is the case with cutting edges in extinct varanoids

comments.issue: Agamidae indet. and Iguanidae indet. specimens lack provenance, age, and identification details.
comments.request: Provide provenance and identification details for these specimens.
comments.quote: There is no further information, geographic provenance, age (fossil or extant)?

reviews.assessment: Very interesting, well-executed study; figures need restructuring and the Discussion should address sources of uncertainty before acceptance.
strengths: results backed by multiple lines of evidence

comments.issue: Figures are cluttered and inconsistently lettered, making the arguments hard to follow.
comments.request: Restructure figures so they flow and are easier to read.
comments.quote: I found the figures in this paper cluttered and at times frustrating to read, since they are very dense with information

comments.issue: Dense figure plates should be split or supplemented with summary diagrams.
comments.request: Split dense figures and add summary diagrams.
comments.quote: I’d suggest some of the very dense figures be split into multiple figures so that the information can be presented to readers in a more step-wise fashion

comments.issue: Interpretations ignore sources of variation and uncertainty; conclusions risk appearing as a just-so story without discussion or analyses.
comments.request: Address the sources of uncertainty directly in the Discussion.
comments.quote: I have some concerns with the interpretations of the results and integration with the Discussion, at least insofar as they appear to ignore several sources of variation/uncertainty.

comments.issue: No comparisons with smaller theropods such as dromaeosaurs, which would best test the competing hypotheses.
comments.request: Add comparisons to smaller theropods such as dromaeosaurs.
comments.quote: at no point do you provide comparisons to smaller theropods (such as dromaeosaurs), which would seem to be the perfect test of the two hypotheses offered above by the authors

comments.issue: Lack of analytical comparisons to other squamates and no explanation for variable Fe coatings within Varanus.
comments.request: Add squamate comparisons and data on Fe-coating variability.
comments.quote: The lack of analytical comparisons to other squamates, and particularly a lack of discussion of the implications of Fe coatings being only variably present in different species of Varanus.

comments.issue: Direct mammalian comparisons and tooth-replacement strategies are barely examined.
comments.request: Discuss mammalian analogues and tooth replacement strategies.
comments.quote: The lack of direct mammalian comparisons (or other way to asses impact of tooth replacement as a component of the strategy underscoring the management of tooth wear).

comments.issue: Fossil versus modern comparisons are missing to test whether elemental patterns reflect fossilization.
comments.request: Test or discuss fossilization with fossil-modern comparisons.
comments.quote: A lack of comparison of fossil vs modern teeth of the same taxon (or close relative) to test some of the interpretations made concerning elemental concentration patterns in theropod tooth tissues being the result of fossilization.

comments.issue: Figure numbering errors in text (Figure 3 where 2 intended) and Extended Data 2 seems missing.
comments.request: Check and fix all figure and extended-data cross-references.
comments.quote: There may be a problem with figure numbering in the text, as I noticed that figure 3 was being called in-text a few times where I’m fairly sure Figure 2 was what was intended

comments.issue: Lines 258-260 present speculation in the Results rather than data-based findings.
comments.request: Move the speculation to the Discussion or test it.
comments.quote: this is probably better in the Discussion rather than Results, since it is mostly a speculation rather than something directly based on data

comments.issue: Ziphodont versus incrassate terminological distinction is not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge the terminology distinction somewhere.
comments.quote: I think they should at least acknowledge this terminology distinction somewhere

reviews.assessment: Well-done, interesting study; concerns about LA-ICPMS normalization and whether the tyrannosaurid iron coating is diagenetic.
strengths: meticulous characterization of chemical, structural and mechanical properties

comments.issue: Figure numbering is wrong; there are two figures labelled 1.
comments.request: Fix the figure numbering.
comments.quote: Figures: please check figure numbering, you currently have two figure(s) 1!

comments.issue: References 22 and 12 refer to the same paper.
comments.request: Merge the duplicate references.
comments.quote: References 22 and 12 are actually the same paper.

comments.issue: Zn role in amelogenesis literature (e.g., Müller et al. 2019) is not engaged; Zn/Fe distributions may have different roles.
comments.request: Read and cite Müller et al. (2019) on Zn in enamel.
comments.quote: I suggest the author to carefully read Müller et al. (2019, Geochim Cosmochim Acta 15:105-126), where Zn role is interpreted and descripted for humans.

comments.issue: Measured isotopes (m/z) rather than elements should be reported; unclear whether CRC was used for all analytes.
comments.request: Report measured isotopes and CRC use.
comments.quote: you need to report the measured isotopes (m/z) rather than the elements. Was the CRC used for all the analytes or Fe only?

comments.issue: Normalizing intensities to Ca (element/Ca maps) would be more robust than the current approach.
comments.request: Report element/Ca maps and compare them with corrected maps.
comments.quote: I find much more robust the protocol commonly employed in the geochemical community, namely reporting cps as normalized intensities to Ca

comments.issue: Cannot rule out that Fe and Zn distributions in Figure 3 result from diagenetic alteration; Fe and Y patterns suggest uptake.
comments.request: Report diagenetic markers and test for diagenetic alteration.
comments.quote: if you cannot rule out that the Fe and Zn distributions in Figure 3 are not the result of a diagenetic alteration of the outer enamel, it is difficult to fully support the hypothesis

title: Iron-coated Komodo dragon teeth and the complex dental enamel of carnivorous reptiles

study.system: adult baobabs in the Sahel; satellite imagery, deep learning, survey data

editor_summary: Requires responses to reviewers and editorial concerns: either cut to two figures for a Brief Communication or expand into a full Article with deeper social-science analysis, and better document the DHS survey data used.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the ambitious baobab mapping and socio-ecological analyses, but asks for clearer methods, attention to confounding and terminology, and better structure.
strengths: innovative mapping of a single tree species over a vast area with high granularity
deep learning methodology appears validated and credible
multiple empirical drivers of baobab distribution add value
illustrated, evidence-based mapping of a critical tree species

comments.issue: The word 'iconic' in the abstract is not part of the scientific name and should be removed.
comments.request: Remove the word 'iconic' from line 23 of the abstract.
comments.quote: Line 23 in the abstract remove the word “iconic” since it is not part of the scientific name that comes immediately after it.

comments.issue: The term livelihoods is repeated throughout but never illustrated with concrete examples.
comments.request: Give examples of the livelihoods in light of the maps, settlements and period studied.
comments.quote: From the heading to the references the word “livelihoods” counts seven times with five within the main text alone. However, no where in the paper examples of the livelihoods are given.

comments.issue: The paper lacks a concluding section identifying community, science and policy implications.
comments.request: Add a landing conclusion stating the community, science and policy implications.
comments.quote: The paper lacks a landing conclusion to effectively identify the community, science and policy implications of the paper.

comments.issue: Low dry-season NDVI is not exclusive to baobabs, so it may not discriminate the species from other trees.
comments.request: Explain how baobabs are distinguished from other vegetation with low NDVI.
comments.quote: The authors mention a low NDVI due to baobab leaf loss in dry periods, but this isn't exclusive to the baobab tree.

comments.issue: It is unclear which shadow features (size, shape) identify baobabs and whether they are consistent across training samples.
comments.request: Explain how shadow features capture baobab structure and test consistency across training samples.
comments.quote: How do the baobab shadow features, as viewed in the imagery, capture the unique and/or peculiar structure of the baobab's branches and trunk? Is it the size of the shadow? Shape? Is this consistent across training samples?

comments.issue: The baobab-vegetable consumption relationship does not control for climate variability, a potential confounder.
comments.request: Control for climate variability across the region in this relationship.
comments.quote: However, this does not seem to control for climate variability across the region. More vegetables are cultivated in the wetter parts of the Sahel, which also happen to have more baobab trees.

comments.issue: Spatial proximity to households does not necessarily imply access, which also depends on tenure and customs.
comments.request: Highlight to readers that proximity does not guarantee access to baobab resources.
comments.quote: spatial proximity does not necessarily imply access. Other factors such as land tenure/ownership laws and customs can determine whether a household/family can access a baobab tree resource or not.

comments.issue: Equating buildings with households is misleading because a household is a social construct.
comments.request: Avoid using the term 'household' when building footprints are the proxy.
comments.quote: equating ‘buildings’ to 'households' may be misleading. A 'household' can also be a social construct, and in Africa, a single 'household' can encompass multiple physical units and vice versa.

comments.issue: Sections on baobab-settlement, baobab-vegetable and driver analyses need better structuring, and the abstract omits the gradient-boosted models.
comments.request: Restructure these sections and add a concise objectives statement to the introduction.
comments.quote: The manuscript's sections on the relationship between baobab trees and rural settlements, baobab trees and vegetable consumption patterns, and the factors influencing baobab distribution need better structuring.

comments.issue: References cited in the third paragraph of lines 68-69 may not be appropriate.
comments.request: Review lines 68-69 and make sure appropriate references are cited.
comments.quote: Review lines 68-69 (third paragrap) and make sure appropriate references are being cited.

comments.issue: Potential implications for agroforestry and baobab distribution near agricultural fields are not discussed.
comments.request: Add commentary on baobab distribution in or near agricultural fields and agroforestry implications.
comments.quote: Lastly, it's curious that the authors, having taken the effort to tie baobab distribution to various anthropogenic drives, failed to discuss its potential implications in agroforestry.

title: Mapping every adult baobab (Adansonia digitata L.) across the Sahel and relationships to rural livelihoods

study.system: species interaction networks; birds, mammals, parasites across three datasets

editor_summary: Editor sees considerable potential interest but substantial concerns must be addressed; cannot accept, invites a revised version.

reviews.assessment: Main criticisms concern undefined success, inconsistent generalism terminology, missing key literature, and JSD not measuring specificity.

comments.issue: Song et al. (2022) addresses a very similar question with similar tools and reports seemingly opposed results but is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss Song et al. (2022) and reconcile the opposing results.
comments.quote: First, I was surprised to find no discussion of Song et al. (2022; 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010302), wherein a very similar question is addressed with very similar tools.

comments.issue: Ecological success is value-laden and left undefined, so what success means remains unclear.
comments.request: Unpack and define ecological success explicitly.
comments.quote: The idea of ecological success is a value-laden one, and the authors do not really spend time unpacking the definitions of success.

comments.issue: Links to previous conceptual literature on generalism are inadequate; Cavender-Bares et al. (2009) is missing.
comments.request: Connect the work to the conceptual literature on generalism.
comments.quote: Generalism is defined across multiple sources of measurement, but then again the links to previous conceptual literature is inadequate.

comments.issue: Generalism is used to mean different things, making the manuscript hard to read.
comments.request: Use generalism consistently and align with specificity language.
comments.quote: All things considered, this makes the manuscript difficult to read because “generalism” is often used to mean different things.

comments.issue: Specificity is both a measurable state and a driver of eco-evolutionary dynamics; this dual role is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss specificity as both state and driver.
comments.quote: One thing that the authors do not sufficiently address is that specificity is both a measurable state and a driver of eco/evo dynamics.

comments.issue: JSD is sensitive to other species and measures host selection, not specificity.
comments.request: Repeat SEM analyses with multiple specificity measures and test robustness.
comments.quote: The authors use the JSD as a measure of specificity, and I do not think it is one.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, original paper with impressive datasets, but causality direction, variable definitions and derived metrics need more support.

comments.issue: Causality is not demonstrated watertight; some correlations may represent reverse causality.
comments.request: Reconsider arrow directions and add tests confirming directionality.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors deeply consider the direction of their arrows in figure 1, and especially whether some of the correlations reported might represent reverse causality.

comments.issue: Variable definitions and calculations are unclear, making findings hard to interpret.
comments.request: Define and explain how each variable was calculated.
comments.quote: The ms is also quite difficult to read in places because the definition of variables and how they were calculated or estimated is not as clear as it could be.

comments.issue: Highly derived variables such as resource space may be sensitive to calculation decisions.
comments.request: Add sensitivity analyses or tests on less derived variables.
comments.quote: these seem potentially quite sensitive to decisions made in how they were calculated, so some additional sensitivity analysis or tests on less highly calculated variables might be nice to confirm that results aren’t artefacts

comments.issue: Hypotheses and conclusions overreach the data, invoking dispersal and colonisation without data.
comments.request: Tone down language and signpost speculatory processes.
comments.quote: I also think that some of the hypotheses and conclusions overreach the data. For instance, lines 129-135 invoke processes of dispersal and colonisation, but there are no data on this.

comments.issue: Species-level generalism may artefactually correlate with regional rather than local success.
comments.request: Calculate generalism at local as well as regional scale.
comments.quote: I feel that this result might therefore possibly be an artefact of the way generalism was estimated (at the species level).

comments.issue: Defining generalism at species level conflicts with the conclusion that generalism is not a species characteristic.
comments.request: Show variation in generalism across the range.
comments.quote: The practice of defining generalism at the species level is also particularly surprising given that one of the main conclusions of the study is that the results challenge the idea of generalism as a species charactersitc

comments.issue: Unclear whether host-perspective generalism definitions were reversed for the analysis.
comments.request: Explain how generalism types are defined with respect to hosts.
comments.quote: It is not clear from the methods whether the definitions then have been reversed for this analysis, i.e., phylogenetic generalism of hosts should reflect the phylogenetic distance of their parasites?

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation in host availability was not explored.
comments.request: Test for spatial autocorrelation in host availability.
comments.quote: Spatial autocorrelation in host availability - has this been explored?

comments.issue: Range size-regional generalism link can arise in either causal direction.
comments.request: Acknowledge the direction ambiguity for this relationship.
comments.quote: The link between range size and regional generalism is well established (e.g., Slatyer et al. cited in text) and can arise whether generalism is a cause or a consequence of range expansion.

comments.issue: Line 182-183: causality direction is not rigorously demonstrated; metrics may both be consequences of range size.
comments.request: Model local and regional scales to support causal inference.
comments.quote: I am not convinced this direction of causality has been rigorously demonstrated. The results in figure 2 seem to imply only that regional and resource-type generalism are positively correlated with each other

comments.issue: Line 366: range size derives from occurrence probability and study sites may be biased toward conspicuous species, creating spurious correlations.
comments.request: State this limitation in the main text and address site-selection bias.
comments.quote: it would be good to be upfront about that in the main text, as the locations under study might have been biased to maximise detection of some rather than other study organisms

comments.issue: Line 367-368: local abundance calculated from interaction counts may create spurious abundance-generalism relationships.
comments.request: Account for sampling decisions and host-specific abundance in the models or caveats.
comments.quote: Local abundance was calculated as the number of interactions observed in any host. This also seems potentially somewhat problematic and might also lead to spurious abundance / generalism relationships

comments.issue: Line 385: phylogenetic and functional niche breadth are not corrected for host richness; scale of calculation unclear.
comments.request: Correct niche breadth for host richness and state the scale used.
comments.quote: Calculation of phylogenetic and functional niche breadth are not corrected for host species richness, so in fact it’s very surprising that these are not more strongly correlated with regional richness.

comments.issue: Line 393: cutoffs for grouping hosts into modules/resource types are not described.
comments.request: Describe the module assignment cutoffs.
comments.quote: Line 393: Cutoffs for grouping hosts into modules/ resource types not described.

comments.issue: Resource space calculation and its dissimilarity matrix are opaque, so Figure 3 cannot be assessed.
comments.request: Describe how resource space was calculated and what it represents.
comments.quote: The calculation of resource space is opaque. The only description of this in methods is “As a result, the hosts in each module can be considered as a resource type

comments.issue: Lines 190-202: phylogeny, geography and traits should be modeled simultaneously to partition variance.
comments.request: Fit a joint model with random-effect distance matrices.
comments.quote: It would be better to model the impacts of phylogeny, geography, and functional traits simultaneously in the same model, e.g., using mcmcglmm and fitting random effect distance matrices as predictors, to thereby partition the variance.

comments.issue: Line 217 and Figure 3 title: 'geographical availability of hosts' is not defined in the methods.
comments.request: Define this term and its relation to sampling.
comments.quote: What is “the geographical availability of hosts”? A search of the document does not return anything for this term in the methods.

comments.issue: Lines 437-439: the 'generalisms model' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what the generalisms model is.
comments.quote: Lines 437-439 unclear. What is the ‘generalisms model’?

reviews.assessment: Impressive datasets and clear writing, but abundance data gaps, metric validity and causality inference raise major concerns.
strengths: big and welcome sensitivity analysis effort

comments.issue: Food webs and trophic interactions are absent from the datasets and discussion.
comments.request: Include a food-web dataset or revise wording about trophic interactions.
comments.quote: there is nothing about food webs. The use of a wide number of resources connects directly with trophic interactions, omnivores and several concepts widely studied in ecology and relevant to the research question.

comments.issue: Local abundance defined as number of interactions is poorly explained and ignores both species' abundances.
comments.request: Explain how local abundance was calculated.
comments.quote: Usually local abundance is the most important driver of species interactions in networks (Vázquez 2007, Verdú 2011), but interaction include two species, so the abundance of both needs to be consider for each pair-wise interaction.

comments.issue: Local abundance data are largely missing, so the generalism-abundance link cannot be validated; abundance is a major error source.
comments.request: Show that species abundances do not drive the results.
comments.quote: Authors need to do something to convince readers about species abundances (number of individuals per locality) not playing a significant role in their results.

comments.issue: All generalism metrics derive from number of interactions, so their correlations must be tested.
comments.request: Test correlations among all link-based variables and adjust SEMs.
comments.quote: I think it is necessary to test the correlation between all variables that are calculated considering the number of links (basically, all generalism metrics).

comments.issue: Resource types based on modularity are questionable: modularity is system-level, affected by supergeneralists and abundance.
comments.request: Justify the resource-type metric against alternatives.
comments.quote: I am not convinced about the use of resource types based on modularity analysis. I have included some minor comments with some concerns, but the biggest one is about its interpretation.

comments.issue: Models omit potentially confounding variables such as dispersal capacity and scale overlap.
comments.request: Discuss or account for omitted confounding variables.
comments.quote: Models do not include information on variables that could be important and confound the outcomes. For example, organisms dispersal capacity can influence local abundance and range size.

comments.issue: Species identity is not included as a random effect; repeated species values may be non-independent.
comments.request: Include species identity as a random effect.
comments.quote: why not include ‘species identity’ as a random effect? If one species appears in multiple localities, then we could expect to have similar values for multiple variables independently of the locality.

comments.issue: AIC comparison of whole SEMs may not be the best way to choose between models; indirect paths can drive AIC.
comments.request: Present both models with R2 values and path counts.
comments.quote: maybe AIC is not the best metric to measure which model is preferred. Main thing is to provide both models in the main text so readers can evaluate by themselves which one is better.

comments.issue: Discussion is over-simplistic and does not contextualize results with ecological theory or combine local and regional scales.
comments.request: Discuss results in the context of relevant ecological theories.
comments.quote: In general, I think discussion feels over simplistic. Authors do not discuss some of their results and/or do not put their results in context with some ecological theories (particularly related to diversity effects on fitness).

comments.issue: Observational datasets and AIC-based SEM comparison cannot demonstrate causality direction.
comments.request: Discuss limitations for causal inference and the need for more research.
comments.quote: Finally, my biggest concern with this work is about the capability of datasets and methods to demonstrate causality.

comments.issue: Fort 2016 is relevant and uncited.
comments.request: Cite Fort 2016 and consider its ideas.
comments.quote: As an extra, take a look to Fort 2016. Authors can take some ideas (and need to cite it, of course).

comments.issue: Title implies causality too strongly.
comments.request: Rewrite the title to reduce causal implications.
comments.quote: I will rewrite the title to reduce the implications of causality (see major comments)

comments.issue: Abstract statement is only known for the selected model; the other model is not reported.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract for clarity.
comments.quote: L22-24, this sentence is true, but we do not know if this is the case for the causal model, as results only show the best model. Rewrite abstract for clarity.

comments.issue: Functional traits and their variability are underused in the framing; relevant citations missing.
comments.request: Add comments on functional traits to the introduction and discussion.
comments.quote: In general, I feel functional traits can have more influence in this research question. Some comments on introduction and discussion on this will be welcomed.

comments.issue: If modules are determined by traits and phylogeny, including resource types needs justification.
comments.request: Justify the relevance of resource types in the analysis.
comments.quote: Then, what is the point of calculating the modules if that information is already included? Authors need to justify the relevance of including resource types in the analysis.

comments.issue: L67-70: abundance and widespreadness alone increase host encounters; no mechanism links this to generalism.
comments.request: Provide a mechanism for how success would increase host number.
comments.quote: This sentence says nothing about generalism because even if you are specialist, by being more abundant and widespread any species has more chances to find its host (even if it has only one host species).

comments.issue: L128-130: results for the other model, path significance and R2 are not reported, preventing comparison.
comments.request: Report results for both models.
comments.quote: great, but we do not have results for the other model. This path is significant? What is the R2? It is not possible to compare without the info from the other model.

comments.issue: L130-133: why locally abundant species interact with more species, and the role of dispersal capacity, are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism linking abundance to interaction diversity.
comments.quote: Why this should translate to interacting with a more diverse set of species (i.e. is the same for an abundant generalist and an abundant specialist)? What is the role of dispersal capacity?

comments.issue: L151-154: more than one causal direction is possible; parasite diversity can affect success.
comments.request: Acknowledge alternative causal directions.
comments.quote: I do not think there is only one causal direction. For example, parasite diversity can have an effect on species success (Sallinen 2023).

comments.issue: L164-168: result is expected if modules are functionally assembled and metrics correlated.
comments.request: Account for the correlation between modules and traits.
comments.quote: L164-168, this is straightforward if modules are functionally assembled and both metrics are correlated (see major comments).

comments.issue: L172-174: claim about versatile traits is not supported by the data.
comments.request: Remove or temper this unsupported statement.
comments.quote: L172-174, this is not supported by the data. There is no info about generalisms having more versatile or appropriate traits.

comments.issue: L353-355: correlations among multiple traits must be evaluated and methods corrected if present.
comments.request: Report trait correlations and correct methods accordingly.
comments.quote: when working with multiple traits is key to evaluate the correlation among them. Provide that info, and if there is correlation, correct the methods accordingly.

comments.issue: L397-399: significance values for modularity are missing; a non-significant result would preclude the metric.
comments.request: Provide significance values for modularity.
comments.quote: where are significance values provided? A significant result for modularity will be very welcomed to ease discussion. Personally, I think that a non-significant result precludes using this metric.

comments.issue: L418: count variables are not standardized for differing community richness.
comments.request: Consider transforming counts to proportions.
comments.quote: L418, why not transform count variables in proportions to standardize communities with different richness?

title: Generalism in species interactions is more the consequence than the cause of ecological success

study.system: Neotropical bats; sugar tolerance tests, genomics and gut anatomy

editor_summary: Editor finds the work of considerable potential interest but says substantial concerns must be addressed; cannot accept but would consider a revised version addressing these serious concerns.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the work and finds the gut-diet connection compelling, but worries diet effects are confounded by phylogeny and based on small samples.
