comments.quote: The authors simply state that ‘we removed seasonality and long-term trends’. This is not enough

comments.issue: A three-year moving window is too short for slow-growing woody ecosystems.
comments.request: Test additional moving-window lengths.
comments.quote: A three-year moving window was used for resilience estimates, which is rather short to assess recovery, particularly of slow-growing or woody ecosystems. Additional time windows should be assessed here for robustness.

comments.issue: Figure 2 forest-type distribution conflicts strongly with the original data publication's primary forest classification.
comments.request: Clarify or re-analyze the forest-type classification.
comments.quote: It looks like most of the area those authors classify as ‘primary forest’ are classified as ‘planted forest’ here. This is a really big discrepancy

comments.issue: Figure 3 decadal analysis may reflect timing of gain/loss or sampling bias rather than a resilience effect.
comments.request: Clarify Figure 3 and rule out sampling bias.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I totally understand Figure 3 – to me it seems clear that when forest gain/loss happened would influence TAC around that time

comments.issue: Supplementary Figure 5 makes the key point better than Figure 3 and should be in the main text.
comments.request: Move or promote Supp. Fig. 5 to the main text.
comments.quote: I think Supplementary Figure 5 should be highlighted in the main text – this really clearly shows the influence of changes in FC with TAC changes.

comments.issue: Supplementary Figure 6 sectors 1-8 are undefined although they underpin the Discussion.
comments.request: Define or redesign Supp. Fig. 6.
comments.quote: Supplementary Figure 6 is very unclear – the sectors 1-8 are not defined anywhere in the caption or on the figure.

comments.issue: Supplementary Figure 5 y-axes are not aligned at zero.
comments.request: Align the y-axes at zero.
comments.quote: Supplementary Figure 5 should have better centered axes – at least 0 should be at the same point for both y-axes so that it is easier to see where the dots are positive/negative.

comments.issue: NDVI is a fast chlorophyll response; a slower indicator such as VOD could capture longer recovery timescales.
comments.request: Consider VOD or slower indicators.
comments.quote: Could adding an additional slower data set to your analysis (e.g., VOD instead of NDVI to capture longer time scale recoveries in ecosystem function) help to expand this point about recovery timescales?

title: Asymmetric sensitivity of boreal forest resilience to forest gain and loss

study.system: national biodiversity plans; manual review of 20 NBSAPs against GBF targets

editor_summary: Editor rejects: reviewers find potential interest but question the strength of the analysis and utility; offers transfer to npj Biodiversity or a substantially revised resubmission with more NBSAPs.

reviews.assessment: Assessment is important, but coverage of only 20 NBSAPs and inappropriate assessment criteria make the conclusions incomplete.

comments.issue: Assessment criteria such as “degraded” cannot be defined uniformly across nations with different legal requirements.
comments.request: Adjust the methodology to reflect the various national situations.
comments.quote: The methodology of the manuscript needs to be adjusted to reflect the various situations in different nations.

comments.issue: Only 20 NBSAPs were covered while more than 150 have not been updated and analysed.
comments.request: Expand the analysis to more NBSAPs.
comments.quote: Its conclusions are incomplete because more NBSAPs (>150) have not been updated and analyzed.

comments.issue: The claim that the GBF first set quantitative biodiversity targets overlooks the Aichi Targets.
comments.request: Acknowledge earlier quantitative targets such as the Aichi Targets.
comments.quote: GBF was not the first time that quantitative targets for biodiversity conservation have been set. For instance, the Aichi Targets also have some quantitative targets.

comments.issue: Country boundaries in Figure 1 are incorrect for some countries.
comments.request: Correct the country boundaries in Figure 1.
comments.quote: the boundary of some countries in Figure 1 needs to be corrected

comments.issue: The section at lines 190-224 may be unnecessary because NBSAPs are strategic documents.
comments.request: Consider removing or condensing this section.
comments.quote: this section might be not necessary, because NBSAP is a strategic document

comments.issue: Spatially explicit plans may not be required in NBSAPs, as they can be separate documents.
comments.request: Reconsider this assessment criterion.
comments.quote: a spatially explicit plan to meet Target 2 and 3 might not be necessary for NBSAPs

comments.issue: Language needs much more improvement, including the misspelling “Montral”.
comments.request: Improve the language and fix the spelling.
comments.quote: The language of the manuscript needs much more improvement. For instance, Line 13, “Montral” should be “Montreal”.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and valuable if timely, but the NBSAP versions used and their provenance need documenting.
strengths: intelligent analysis of NBSAPs against criteria

comments.issue: Four analysed countries have NBSAPs predating the 2022 GBF, and the source of the NBSAPs is not documented.
comments.request: Document which NBSAP versions were used and where they were downloaded.
comments.quote: four of the countries analysed have not submitted an NBSAP that was written after 2022 (the finalisation of the GBF)

comments.issue: Most environment agendas are probably defined nationally and then fitted to international agendas.
comments.request: Revise the claim about agendas being defined in international fora.
comments.quote: I am not sure that most environment agendas are defined in international fora - most are probably defined nationally and then fitted to the international agendas

comments.issue: A word or more is missing at lines 285-287.
comments.quote: Lines 285-287 - a word or more is missing here

reviews.assessment: Findings likely true but the coding themes are oversimplified and the study yields little generalizable insight; methods need more detail.
strengths: climate-framework parallels are a step toward synthesis

comments.issue: The coding themes are broad and oversimplified; Target 3 elements such as connectivity and governance were not coded.
comments.request: Refine the themes so they comprehensively address Targets 2 and 3.
comments.quote: the themes the authors constructed are quite broad and oversimplified, and therefore do not comprehensively address those targets

comments.issue: The study generates little generalizable insight that could improve other countries' plans.
comments.request: Develop knowledge that can inform future plan development, e.g. lessons from the Aichi round.
comments.quote: the study does not generate much generalizable insight or knowledge that could be used to improve the plans of the other countries

comments.issue: How the 13 coding elements were chosen and why other aspects were excluded is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the 13 coding elements were derived.
comments.quote: more details were needed in terms of how the authors arrived at the 13 elements they chose for coding and why certain aspects were not included

comments.issue: Details of coder disagreement (questions, frequency, language of plans) are not reported.
comments.request: Report where and how often coders disagreed.
comments.quote: It would also be useful to know on what types of questions the authors had disagreement, how often disagreement occurred, whether it occurred for the English or Google interpreted plans

title: Ambitions in national plans do not yet match bold international protection and restoration commitments

study.system: cyanobacteria light-harvesting evolution; Archaean light simulations and phylogenetics

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers raised concerns that must be addressed before publication; invites a revision responding to all reviewer and editorial comments, with changes highlighted.

reviews.assessment: Exciting, impressive multidisciplinary study worth publishing; suggests additions on terrestrial cyanobacteria, Prochlorococcus, strain details and updated annotations.

comments.issue: Terrestrial cyanobacteria in the phylogeny are not discussed or shown in Figure 4.
comments.request: Discuss terrestrial cyanobacteria and add them to Figure 4.
comments.quote: Terrestrial cyanobacteria can be added to the discussion.

comments.issue: Prochlorococcus and its distinct pigment composition are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss Prochlorococcus as an adaptation to the modern white-light window.
comments.quote: The different pigment composition might be an adaptation to the modern ocean's white light window.

comments.issue: “a” in chlorophyll a is not italicized at lines 501 and 511.
comments.request: Italicize “a”.
comments.quote: Line 501 and 511: “a” in chlorophyll a should be italicized.

comments.issue: The source of the two cyanobacterial strains is not described.
comments.request: State whether strains were purchased or gifted.
comments.quote: Please describe the source of these two cyanobacterial strains (purchased from a culture collection center or gifted by other labs?)

comments.issue: Gloeobacter violaceus is a terrestrial strain and may not represent early ocean-dwelling cyanobacteria; classification details need updating.
comments.request: Reconsider the model organism and cite updated classification references.
comments.quote: Gloeobacter violaceus PCC 7421 was isolated from calcareous rock in Switzerland, not from the ocean. As the authors' model of cyanobacteria evolution is in the ocean, Gloeobacter violaceus PCC 7421 might not be an ideal model organism

comments.issue: Using different wavelengths (750 and 730 nm) for optical densities is unjustified.
comments.request: Justify the two wavelengths.
comments.quote: Please justify using two different wavelengths (750 nm and 730 nm) to measure the optical densities of G. violaceus and S. elongatus.

comments.issue: The CpcC sequence of Anthocerotibacter panamensis is now annotated as CpcJ.
comments.request: Update the annotation and cite Jiang et al. 2023.
comments.quote: The CpcC sequence of Anthocerotibacter panamensis used in the phylogeny has an updated annotation as CpcJ based on a recent publication last year.

reviews.assessment: Finds the evolutionary story fascinating but questions the simulation realism, possible confounds in the engineering experiment, and the phylogenetic inferences.
strengths: fascinating evolutionary hypothesis linking GOE and light environments

comments.issue: The light simulations may not reflect the dynamic Archean aquatic world (pH, ions, atmosphere, biota).
comments.request: Explain how the simulations capture real Archean conditions.
comments.quote: Could the simulation and calculation of light wavelength and light windows in different depths reflect the real situation of Archean aquatic world?

comments.issue: Transgenic growth changed water and medium colour, which may confound the light-adaptation experiment.
comments.request: Assess whether the colour change influences the results.
comments.quote: But the growth of transgenic cyanobacteria changed the color of water and culture medium. Will the changes influence the results of genetic engineering simulation of PE-contained Synechocystis sp. PCC6803?

comments.issue: It is unexplained why photosynthesizers use red rather than green light despite green light’s energy and spectral area.
comments.request: Address this apparent paradox.
comments.quote: I am very curious that green light occupied a large area of visible spectrum and have higher energy, but why did cyanobacteria and almost all the photosynthetic organisms choose the red light rather than the green light as one of the main energy sources?

comments.issue: Phylogenetic inferences rely on deduction; gene family divergence, duplication and gain-loss analyses are missing.
comments.request: Add analyses or discussion of gene family evolution, e.g. PE gene loss.
comments.quote: it is more convincing to add some analyses or discussion for the divergence, duplication and gain-and-loss events of gene families, rather than simple deduction

comments.issue: Line 592 lacks trimming and masking details needed for reproducibility.
comments.request: Describe the trimming and masking procedures.
comments.quote: There doesn’t seem to be enough details provided here to allow for reproducibility (how was the trimming, masking, etc, done?)

comments.issue: Only ultrafast bootstrap supports are reported.
comments.request: Add SH-aLRT branch supports.
comments.quote: Except the ultrafast bootstrap (UFBOOT), it would be useful to add the branch supports using SH approximate likelihood ratio (SH-aLRT test) approach.

comments.issue: Criteria for selecting representative sequences are unspecified.
comments.request: State the selection criteria.
comments.quote: What are the criteria for selecting representative sequences?

comments.issue: A published molecular clock is reused without checking whether the timeframe is robust.
comments.request: Infer divergence times from the study’s own dataset.
comments.quote: why a previously published molecular clock analysis is being used here, this time frame is robust? Perhaps using your dataset to infer divergence time is better.

comments.issue: Figure 3b’s Rod linker tree does not match the text and its legend is too limited.
comments.request: Explain the tree’s message and expand the legend.
comments.quote: What information does the Rod linker phylogenetic tree in Figure 3b intend to convey? It does not match the description in lines 606-624.

comments.issue: The exclusion rule for sequences outside PE/PC clades, with outgroup exceptions, is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the sequence exclusion criteria.
comments.quote: I do not understand why are the sequences outside the clades that contain known PE and PC proteins excluded, but the outgroup sequences, non-cyanobacterial PcyA/PebAB homologs and unknown CpcS Homologs are exceptions.

title: Archaean green-light environments drove the evolution of cyanobacteria’s light-harvesting system

study.system: horseshoe bats; comparative genomics and functional immune assays

editor_summary: Reviewers appreciate the genomic resources but raise substantial concerns; editor agrees further interspecific comparisons are needed to support unique viral tolerance in horseshoe bats.

reviews.assessment: Valuable genomes and assays, but the manuscript does not demonstrate that horseshoe bat immunity is exceptional and experiments are poorly integrated.
strengths: generation of several new high-quality genomes

comments.issue: The manuscript does not demonstrate that horseshoe bats or their immune genes are exceptional compared with other lineages.
comments.request: Add interspecific comparative analyses.
comments.quote: The manuscript on its own does not demonstrate that horseshoe bats are exceptional compared to other lineages, or that immune-related genes show exceptional evolution in horseshoe bats compared to other lineages.

comments.issue: All findings are interpreted as immune-related selection, ignoring other selective pressures.
comments.request: Consider alternative selective pressures.
comments.quote: all their findings are interpreted based on the assumption that all evolutionary selection in horseshoe bats is immune related

comments.issue: No comparative test shows immune gene expansion is exceptional; ANXA2R choice is arbitrary and the mammal p-value is missing.
comments.request: Quantify exceptionality with comparative tests.
comments.quote: do not include any analysis showing that horseshoe bats are exceptional compared to other bat lineages or other mammalian lineages

comments.issue: Rapid evolution of immune genes is expected in all mammals and does not by itself show horseshoe bat exceptionality.
comments.request: Compare immune gene evolution across lineages.
comments.quote: This is not surprising, because immune response genes are among the fastest evolving types of genes in any mammal lineage.

comments.issue: Experimental sections are hard to follow: acronyms unexplained, sample sizes and replicate types missing, cell-line and RfKT choices unjustified, no significance tests.
comments.request: Integrate experiments, define acronyms, report n and statistics.
comments.quote: The new experimental sections are not well integrated into the manuscript and are very difficult to follow

comments.issue: The IFN expression comparisons lack statistical analyses and the percentages are unexplained.
comments.request: Add statistical analyses and explain percentages.
comments.quote: there were no statistical analyses to support this and I don’t know what the percentages are

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 4 rely on colors only, reducing accessibility for color-vision-impaired readers.
comments.request: Use colorblind-friendly design.
comments.quote: The use of many different colors, and no other visual cues, in the figures (especially figures 2 and 4) will make them less accessible to people with limited color vision.

comments.issue: The abstract omits the number of genomes generated.
comments.request: Add genome count to the abstract.
comments.quote: The abstract does not include the number of genomes generated.

comments.issue: The chromosome-pair statement's meaning (match to published karyotypes or validation) is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the karyotype consistency statement.
comments.quote: does this mean the chromosome number matched the number previously reported? Or that the genome size was validated with the karyotypes somehow?

comments.issue: Divergence dates are not compared with previous sequence-based studies.
comments.request: Compare divergence estimates with previous studies.
comments.quote: I think there have been previous studies using sequence data that also investigated this, and it would be good to include a comparison to those as well

comments.issue: The resequencing dataset lacks detail (individuals per species, coverage, read length).
comments.request: Report resequencing dataset details.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to include more information about this data set in the main text, such as average number of individuals per species, the average / std dev of genome coverage per individual, and the read length.

comments.issue: Karyotype variation alone does not show chromosome rearrangements drove speciation; it could be a consequence.
comments.request: Temper or test the speciation role claim.
comments.quote: Karyotype variation is usually observed between species, so the observation of it here is not evidence on its own that chromosome rearrangement had a role in speciation.

comments.issue: Comparisons to inferred karyotypes by others (e.g. Damas et al. 2022) are missing.
comments.request: Compare with other inferred karyotypes.
comments.quote: cites the ancestral karyotype from a paper by the authors of this paper, but not comparisons to inferred karyotypes by others (e.g. Damas et al PNAS 2022)

comments.issue: Robustness of the chromosome evolution model is unclear; alternatives untested and SD comparisons not reported.
comments.request: Test alternative models and report SD comparisons.
comments.quote: I’m having trouble assessing how robust this analysis is. Is it just one of many possible models, or the only one that fit the observed data?

reviews.assessment: Large-scale genomics with experiments, but the ANXA2R link to viral suppression is not substantiated and claims need moderating.

comments.issue: The link between ANXA2R expansion and viral suppression is inadequately substantiated; SARS-CoV-2 is not a bat virus.
comments.request: Test broader bat viruses or moderate the claims.
comments.quote: linking the expansion of the ANXA2R gene family to the ability to suppress viral replication or even asymptomatic infection in these bats is not adequately substantiated

comments.issue: 'Suppressed viral infection' conflicts with the high viral diversity and abundance of these reservoir bats.
comments.request: Reconcile claims with reservoir viral diversity.
comments.quote: This raises doubts about whether 'enhanced antiviral immunity' is the correct interpretation.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and clearly presented genomics; methods can be improved and some analyses refined.

comments.issue: The agglomerative hierarchical clustering algorithm needs a citation if not new.
comments.request: Cite the original clustering algorithm.
comments.quote: Is the algorithm of “agglomerative hierarchical clustering” utilizing Hi-c data newly introduced by this study? If not, I recommend citing the original introduction of the algorithm.

comments.issue: LTR_finder is inappropriate for building a de novo repeat library and may cause false predictions.
comments.request: Revise the repeat library construction.
comments.quote: I think that constructing a de novo repeat library with LTR_finder is not appropriate.

comments.issue: How protein-coding regions were obtained from transcriptome data is unclear.
comments.request: Describe the protein-coding prediction.
comments.quote: Please classify how do you get the protein-coding regions from transcriptome data.

comments.issue: Masking all repeats may impair gene prediction accuracy.
comments.request: Explain repeat masking and its effect on gene prediction.
comments.quote: Do you mask all repeat sequences in the genome?

comments.issue: SEDEF would give more refined SD detection than WGAC with repeat masking.
comments.request: Use SEDEF or justify the current approach.
comments.quote: I recommend utilizing SEDEF for a more refined resolution of SDs.

comments.issue: 'Longest transcript' may include UTRs; 'longest protein-coding sequences' would be clearer.
comments.request: Clarify or rename the term.
comments.quote: Does the term 'longest transcript' include untranslated regions (UTRs)?

comments.issue: The Cafe version used is not stated.
comments.request: State the Cafe version.
comments.quote: Which version of Café do you use? Was it Café 5?

comments.issue: A uniform lambda across 20 mammals over >90 My of evolution is inappropriate.
comments.request: Allow lineage-specific lambda values.
comments.quote: I think it's not appropriate for the λ value to be uniform across the entire tree.

comments.issue: CmC and M2a_rel model names are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the model abbreviations.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful to add a small sentence explaining what these (CmC and M2a_rel) means.

comments.issue: The accession PRJCA023723 cannot be located; data and scripts may not be deposited.
comments.request: Upload data/scripts and fix accessions.
comments.quote: I can’t locate this project in the NCBI database with the accession number PRJCA023723.

comments.issue: Figure 2c does not show a chronological order of rearrangements.
comments.request: Show rearrangement order.
comments.quote: Is there a chronological order to these rearrangements between species?

comments.issue: Calling ACG-start genes pseudogenes is questionable since ACG starts occur in mammalian genes.
comments.request: Justify the pseudogene classification.
comments.quote: Could you comment on why you consider start codons with ACG sequences to be pseudogenes?

title: Comparative genomics provides insights into chromosomal evolution and immunological adaptation in horseshoe bats

study.system: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes; 634 genomes; population genomics

editor_summary: Three reviewers find potential interest but raise substantial concerns; selection-detection analyses (R1, R2) and the delimitation of African Aedes aegypti populations (R3) must be addressed.

reviews.assessment: Ambitious and important project with a nice demographic component, but the selection tests need to be improved and possibly redone.
strengths: well motivated for mosquito control and local adaptation

comments.issue: Diagnostic plots are missing for the outlier scan and selection statistics.
comments.request: Add diagnostic plots as extended data figures.
comments.quote: I'd suggest presenting a Mahanttan plot in Figure 3B - this will show much more clearly the results of the outlier scan

comments.issue: Individual pcadapt scores aggregate over all SNPs and may not be informative; the approach needs justification.
comments.request: Justify or revise the use of individual pcadapt scores.
comments.quote: My understanding is there is no particular reason to believe the score for any individual will be informative, since it aggregated over all SNPs

comments.issue: High piN/piS is more likely segregating deleterious variation than positive selection; PBS may be more appropriate.
comments.request: Use a branch-based statistic such as PBS or revise the interpretation.
comments.quote: I am not sure why high piN/piS ratios are interpreted as indicating positive selection

comments.issue: Readers may be surprised by the lack of SNP-number difference between sexes.
comments.request: Add a sentence explaining the lack of sex-chromosome differences.
comments.quote: not all readers will know that Aedes mosquitos lack heteromorphic sex chromosomes, and may be surprised by the lack of difference in SNP number between males and females

comments.issue: Raw SNP numbers are compared across populations with unequal sample sizes.
comments.request: Use sample-size-corrected diversity instead of raw SNP counts.
comments.quote: it can be misleading to compare raw SNP numbers between populations when sample sizes are not identical, since the more individuals you sequence in a population the more SNPs you will find

comments.issue: Reported pi values are implausibly high and likely erroneous.
comments.request: Check the nucleotide diversity calculations.
comments.quote: The reported pi values (0.67 and 0.34) are implausibly high, and from what I can see more than an order of magnitude higher than previous reports in Aedes aegypti

comments.issue: How the 1.5 million SNP subset was sampled is not stated.
comments.request: State how the SNP subset was sampled.
comments.quote: How are the 1.5 million SNPs sampled? I assume this is in part the result of LD pruning and perhaps additional random thinning, but this would be useful to state briefly here

reviews.assessment: Potentially interesting large-scale population genomics, but the domestication framing, selection evidence and functional claims are not convincing.
strengths: topic of potential interest for broad readership

comments.issue: The domestication concept is applied although domestication implies artificial selection.
comments.request: Limit claims to adaptation to anthropogenic environments.
comments.quote: I would suggest limit the scenario of this study to the adaptation to anthropogenic environments, or even strictly focus on the global dispersal (see below), to avoid overstatement.

comments.issue: Varying gene numbers are reported with no definitive consensus list of Aaa signature genes.
comments.request: Generate a consensus list of Aaa molecular signature genes.
comments.quote: I found many places (on pages 9 & 10) reporting varied gene numbers regarding such genes, but failed to get an ultimate list of these genes (with an exact number).

comments.issue: Non-coding selective sweeps reported in other species are ignored.
comments.request: Consider non-coding selective sweeps.
comments.quote: some studies about local adaptation in other species have found the top selective sweeps lie in non-coding regions, which seems to be ignored by the authors

comments.issue: Almost all genes appear selected, which is implausible for such a short-term episode; pN/pS is sensitive to low-frequency variants and the threshold is arbitrary.
comments.request: Cross-validate selection with multiple methods and revisit the threshold.
comments.quote: I'm surprised that so many (almost ALL) genes being selected during such a short-term episode.

comments.issue: Focal genes show allele frequency patterns suggesting relaxed rather than directional selection and were not tested for selection.
comments.request: Test the focal genes for selection and validate function.
comments.quote: I found many of them showing a wide distribution of allele frequency in out-of-Africa populations, indicative of selective relaxation rather than directional selection.

comments.issue: No functional data support the proposed functional relationships.
comments.request: Add expression profiling or functional validation.
comments.quote: At least, expression profiling data could be added to support the functional relationship.

comments.issue: Host adaptation claims lack behavioural host-preference evidence.
comments.request: Provide host preference data before claiming host adaptation.
comments.quote: claims about host adaptation need to be based on clear host preference background

comments.issue: It is unclear how domestication could be distinguished from local adaptation in the same dataset.
comments.request: Distinguish domestication from local adaptation.
comments.quote: it's unclear to me how the authors could differentiate “domestication” from local adaptation in the same data set

comments.issue: Public accessions for all reused data are not clearly documented.
comments.request: Add a data availability section with accessions.
comments.quote: It's better to add a data availability section to clearly show the public accessions of all data used in this study.

comments.issue: Aaf/Aaa and Africa/out-of-Africa nomenclature are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Use a consistent nomenclature.
comments.quote: It's unclear to me whether the forms of Aaf and Aaa exactly equal to the populations of Africa and out-of-Africa, respectively.

comments.issue: Parts of the text are descriptive with too many numbers and unexplained abbreviations.
comments.request: Reduce numbers and contextualise abbreviations.
comments.quote: the manuscript is a bit descriptive in places, particularly the sections of variants and molecular signature genes where I read too many numbers and non-contextual abbreviations

comments.issue: Fig. 1 uses too many indistinguishable and inconsistent colours.
comments.request: Revise Fig. 1 colours and highlight key populations.
comments.quote: too many colors here, indifferentiable to each other, and inconsistent across panels

comments.issue: Fig. D4c appears to lack non-Africa populations.
comments.request: Fix colours and missing populations in Fig. D4.
comments.quote: Fig. D4c - I failed to see non-Africa populations, although other symbols being indicated.

reviews.assessment: Robust population structure analysis, but the domestication topic is oversold and the population delimitation is not convincing.

comments.issue: The domestication framing oversells findings that mainly concern genomic divergence.
comments.request: Tone down domestication claims and reframe the title.
comments.quote: the authors tried to oversell their findings and failed short as they attempted to address a more complicated topic such as domestication, which is largely beyond the scope of their work

comments.issue: African samples may include recently reintroduced populations, so ancestral versus introduced discrimination is unconvincing.
comments.request: Validate the discrimination of ancestral and introduced African populations.
comments.quote: I am not convinced by the authors’ claim that they were able to discriminate between ancestral African populations and recently introduced populations based on population genetic structure analysis.

comments.issue: The enrichment analysis has limited power to test domestication hypotheses.
comments.request: Restrict conclusions about domestication.
comments.quote: the findings have very limited power to support hypothesis testing about domestication

comments.issue: Opportunistic sampling with uneven sample sizes and geography may bias statistics and interpretations.
comments.request: Acknowledge the opportunistic sampling caveat.
comments.quote: the paper used a more “opportunistic” sampling approach rather than a thoughtful collection of specimen for population genetic analysis

title: Adaptive genomic signatures of globally invasive populations of the yellow fever mosquito Aedes aegypti

study.system: mosquitofish; cognitive assays, mesocosm breeding and paternity analysis

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers find considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns; cannot accept but invites a revised version addressing them.

reviews.assessment: Interesting question, but several protocols may not measure cognition directly, and some statements and conclusions are over-interpreted.

comments.issue: The brain-size to cognitive-ability link is assumed but is still debated, and the cited reference does not support it.
comments.request: Add a reference supporting the brain size-cognition assumption.
comments.quote: there is a leap in logical flow here – the assumption is made that brain size is related to cognitive ability – but this link is still very much an active debate!

comments.issue: The link is to reproductive success, not fitness, which requires offspring surviving to reproduce.
comments.request: Correct the fitness terminology.
comments.quote: this is a link between cognition and reproductive success, not fitness. Fitness measures would be if those young produced survived to become reproductive adults

comments.issue: Prior studies linking cognition and reproductive success are not recognised, making this look like the only study.
comments.request: Acknowledge White et al. 2021, Cole et al. 2012, Smith et al. 2015, Ashton et al. 2018 and Szabo et al. 2022.
comments.quote: There are studies that have shown a relationship between reproductive success and cognition, so these should be recognised rather than this coming across as the only study to do it

comments.issue: No references identify the studies referred to as most relevant.
comments.request: Cite examples of these studies for context.
comments.quote: which studies are being referred to here by 'most of the relevant studies'? No references given.

comments.issue: The criterion for ecological or social relevance is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how ecological or social relevance was determined.
comments.quote: how do we determine which ones are most likely to be ecologically or socially relevant?

comments.issue: The emergence test is not a cognition test, so the assay count is four, not five.
comments.request: Correct the number of cognitive assays.
comments.quote: this does not seem to be a test of cognition (emergence). So the assay seems four tests, not five.

comments.issue: It is unclear how a realistic population density is defined.
comments.request: Define realistic population density.
comments.quote: L 92: how is a 'realistic population density' defined?

comments.issue: The cognitive tests lack pass/fail criteria and instead rely on improvement with repeated attempts.
comments.request: Define pass/fail criteria for the cognitive tests.
comments.quote: For a cognitive test, there should be a pass/fail criteria or similar not just getter better with repeated attempts.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether covariation is being sought or controlled for.
comments.request: Clarify the purpose of the covariation analysis.
comments.quote: are you looking for covariation or controlling for it?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the task tests learning or cognition and what criterion indicates passing.
comments.request: Clarify what is learned and the pass criterion.
comments.quote: learned what? Is this a test of learning or cognition? For cognition, there should be a criteria to pass.

comments.issue: The meaning of later trials and the trial protocol is not described.
comments.request: State the number of trials and whether all fish received the same number.
comments.quote: what does 'later trials' mean? How many trials on average? Were all given same number of trials, or was it trials until pass?

comments.issue: Swimming away sooner does not prove learning because fish may not have detoured successfully.
comments.request: Temper the learning interpretation.
comments.quote: This does not prove learning. They may have swum away, but not successfully detoured for example

comments.issue: Learning not to persist and learning to detour are conflated, and neither indicates inhibitory control.
comments.request: Separate these two abilities and avoid confounding them.
comments.quote: they can learn not to persist, but may not learn to detour: these are two different things and it is important that they are not confounded

comments.issue: The results do not evidence task-solving ability or spatial learning.
comments.request: Reconsider what these results say about spatial learning.
comments.quote: as per above this is not evidence of ability to solve the task: what does this tell us about spatial learning ability?

comments.issue: The learning criterion is not stated.
comments.request: State the learning criterion.
comments.quote: what was the learning criterion? This needs to be stated to give this context.

comments.issue: The manuscript says five assays in one place and four in another.
comments.request: Use a consistent assay count.
comments.quote: here you say four assays (which I agree with), above you say 5 (which I think is incorrect)

comments.issue: Time to solve since reaching the task would be more informative.
comments.request: Use time to solve as the measure.
comments.quote: the more informative measure here would be time to solve since reaching the task

comments.issue: Many correlations with body size etc. risk false positives and ignore repeated measures such as pond identity.
comments.request: Reduce the correlation tests and account for repeated measures.
comments.quote: why have so many correlations been run? With eg body size etc? This can lead to false positives, and also does not account for repeated measures such as Pond Id etc.

comments.issue: Figure 4 presents simple correlations rather than more informative statistical analyses.
comments.request: Use more advanced statistics than correlations.
comments.quote: terms are presented together as a series of correlations, which are not as informative as more advanced statistical analysis

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not address the main question and may belong in supplementary material.
comments.request: Consider moving Figure 3 to supplementary material.
comments.quote: Figure 3 may be better as SM? It doesn't seem to address the main question of the manuscript

comments.issue: The paragraph at lines 259-271 is poorly integrated with the literature and lacks references.
comments.request: Add supporting references to these statements.
comments.quote: this paragraph is poorly integrated with the primary literature. Statements are made that are not supported by references.

comments.issue: The statement at line 274 is unqualified.
comments.request: Qualify the statement.
comments.quote: L 274: this statement is unqualified.

comments.issue: The claim about sexual selection of or for cognitive ability needs justification.
comments.request: Explain and justify this statement.
comments.quote: this statement: Nonetheless, there will still be sexual selection of, if not for, cognitive ability – needs more explanation to justify it

comments.issue: Time leaving the starting point was measured instead of time interacting with the task, suggesting a methodological issue.
comments.request: Measure time interacting with or approaching the task.
comments.quote: this suggests a methodological issue rather than biological outcome: time leaving the starting point was measured, rather than time interacting with task

comments.issue: The phrase relevant data probably exist at line 318 is too vague.
comments.request: Make the statement specific.
comments.quote: L 318: 'relevant data probably exist' is too vague.

comments.issue: The main point of lines 332-341 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the point of this passage.
comments.quote: the main point being made here is unclear

comments.issue: Teaching males the detour when they fail biases the number of trials until solve; the same applies to maze and associative learning protocols.
comments.request: Avoid teaching during trials or account for it in the analysis.
comments.quote: teaching the males the detour if they did not solve it in a trial biases the data, since it affects the calculation of number of trials until solve

comments.issue: Giving all males ten trials may reduce motivation of males that solve but cannot access females.
comments.request: Justify or adjust the ten-trial protocol.
comments.quote: why are all males given ten trials? Those that solve repeatedly but can't access the females may have lower motivation as trials go on.

comments.issue: Males may see females at the end of the arm at the same time as the colour cue, confounding associative learning.
comments.request: Clarify or control the visibility of females during the cue.
comments.quote: could the males see the females at the end of the arm at the same time they could see the colour cue?

comments.issue: The purpose of the one-sided Poisson tests on learning criteria per day is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what these Poisson tests show.
comments.quote: we ran exact one-sided Poisson tests to determine if more fish meet the learning criteria per day (excluding day 1) than expected by chance given how many males were tested each day – what does this tell you?

comments.issue: Mixed models are stated in the analysis section but not presented; mainly correlations are shown.
comments.request: Present the mixed model results.
comments.quote: Although it is stated in the analysis section that a series of mixed models were run – these are not presented?

reviews.assessment: Ambitious, experimentally sound study and the best test of the hypothesis so far, but conceptual framing and analysis presentation need work.
strengths: experimentally sound with good defenses for design decisions
best test of sexual selection on cognition to date

comments.issue: Offspring production could also be affected by natural selection on females and male mate choice, which needs discussion.
comments.request: Discuss other sources of selection on offspring production.
comments.quote: production of offspring in this case could still be impacted by a number of other sources of selection

comments.issue: Strong language claiming no study has convincingly demonstrated sexual selection on cognition belittles prior work.
comments.request: Soften the primacy claims and acknowledge prior work.
comments.quote: given the very strong language in the introduction that "no study has convincingly demonstrated sexual selection on cognition" lending an air of superiority to this particular study

comments.issue: The introduction emphasises the study's primacy rather than explaining why sexual selection on cognition is expected.
comments.request: Explain the expected basis for sexual selection on cognition.
comments.quote: this introduction is primarily concerned with primacy of the study rather than advancing the science

comments.issue: Study design elements are scattered across several places, making the text fractured and inefficient.
comments.request: Present the study design coherently in one place.
comments.quote: the study design is mentioned in several places, but only specific elements are highlighted in each place. This is rather fractured and inefficient.

comments.issue: The analysis relies on rank correlations; selection differentials or gradients would support future meta-analyses.
comments.request: Add regression analyses estimating selection differentials or gradients.
comments.quote: it would be good to do regression analysis to estimate selection differentials or gradients

comments.issue: Alpha is applied inconsistently, with non-significant results treated as significant when convenient.
comments.request: Apply a consistent significance threshold.
comments.quote: my biggest issue with the presentation of results was a very inconsistent application of an alpha

comments.issue: It is unclear whether decision-making is the end result of all cognition.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of decision-making as a cognitive outcome.
comments.quote: is decision-making the end result of all cognition?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether energetic costs are the only costs of larger brains.
comments.request: Acknowledge other possible costs.
comments.quote: the underlying increase in brain size or complexity impose higher energetic costs" - are these really the only costs?

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: trades-off to trade-offs, Four to Fourth, grey to blue, individual to individuals, biological to biologically.
comments.quote: Line 23: Change "trades-off" to "trade-offs"

comments.issue: Single cognitive assays may tap multiple cognitive abilities, which should be noted.
comments.request: Note the multiple abilities tapped by single assays.
comments.quote: these single assays often are likely tapping multiple cognitive abilities

comments.issue: A non-significant correlation may still be biologically significant given its confidence interval and heritability-scale magnitude.
comments.request: Interpret this correlation in light of its confidence interval.
comments.quote: the confidence interval doesn't include zero and the correlation coefficient is on par with heritability estimates of behavior so may still be biologically significant

comments.issue: The emergence test should be described as a covariate in this sentence.
comments.request: State that emergence was measured as a covariate.
comments.quote: should say in this sentence this was measured as a covariate

comments.issue: Meta-analyses cannot rule out confounding variables in specific systems, so they are a weak defense of the method.
comments.request: Justify the method choice more directly.
comments.quote: Meta-analyses are great for describing general patterns, but not for ruling out confounding variables in specific systems

comments.issue: Controlling for covariation is limited and multicollinearity is not addressed.
comments.request: Address multicollinearity.
comments.quote: "controlled for covariation" - within limits; what about multicollinearity?

comments.issue: It is unclear what quantity at line 116 is being described.
comments.request: Clarify whether this is the fixed effect of trial.
comments.quote: What is this, the fixed effect of trial?

comments.issue: Males that died could not reproduce, which qualifies the claim that variation explained was almost none.
comments.request: Account for mortality in this interpretation.
comments.quote: except for the fact that males that died didn't reproduce, right?

comments.issue: The p-value for the non-significant effect is not reported.
comments.request: Report the p-value.
comments.quote: "but the effect was not statistically significant." What was the p-value?

comments.issue: The rationale for standardizing within ponds rather than across ponds is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the within-pond standardization.
comments.quote: it might help to explain why standardized within each pond and not across ponds

comments.issue: The sentences at lines 250-258 are unnecessary and unconvincing.
comments.request: Delete these sentences.
comments.quote: I would delete these sentences. None of this is necessary or convincing.

comments.issue: It is unclear what greater ability to learn means and how specific tasks relate to real life.
comments.request: Clarify what is learned and its real-life relevance.
comments.quote: "a greater ability to learn" - learn what though? Your tasks are very specific so how are they relevant to real life?

comments.issue: The claim of no autocorrelation may not hold if time was cut off at some point.
comments.request: Reconsider the autocorrelation claim.
comments.quote: "no autocorrelation" - there still could be if you cut off time at some point

comments.issue: It is unclear what was used in the paragraph above.
comments.request: Clarify what analysis was used.
comments.quote: So what did you use in the paragraph above?

comments.issue: The section at lines 325-350 is longer than necessary.
comments.request: Shorten this section.
comments.quote: Line 325-350: This section seems longer than necessary.

comments.issue: The two sentences at lines 349-351 do not follow given that body size was not a significant predictor.
comments.request: Revise these sentences for consistency.
comments.quote: In your study body size was not a significant predictor of mating success, though. I don't follow these two sentences.

comments.issue: It is unclear why food satiation needs controlling when the reward is females rather than food.
comments.request: Explain the food satiation control.
comments.quote: Why would you need to control for food satiation if the reward was not food, but females?

comments.issue: Fish spending more time at the barrier may experience negative reinforcement that influences learning speed, undermining the autocorrelation claim.
comments.request: Reconsider whether the design eliminates autocorrelation.
comments.quote: Fish that spent more time at the barrier initially (> impulsiveness) would have more negative reinforcement, which potentially could influence learning speed.

comments.issue: The pre-registration argument is weak because mechanisms exist to make changes.
comments.request: Delete the pre-registration sentence.
comments.quote: This is a weak argument as there are mechanisms to make changes if needed; otherwise what would be the point of pre-registration?

comments.issue: The composite-measure argument at lines 459-460 is weak.
comments.request: Delete this sentence.
comments.quote: This is a rather weak argument. I would delete this sentence.

comments.issue: The lack of correlation between impulsiveness, inhibitory control and spatial learning should be highlighted as supporting specificity.
comments.request: Remind readers of this lack of correlation.
comments.quote: This adds weight that you are testing spatial learning specifically with that test.

comments.issue: The trial protocol description comes too late.
comments.request: Move the trial description earlier.
comments.quote: Males were given 8 consecutive trials per day for a maximum of 10 consecutive days." This should come sooner.

comments.issue: The point at lines 539-541 needs more explanation.
comments.request: Explain this more.
comments.quote: Lines 539-541: Can you explain this more?

reviews.assessment: Impressive paternity dataset and good model system, but potentially major flaws in the cognitive and boldness measures preclude publication as is.
strengths: useful model system for the question

comments.issue: It is unclear which fry were counted for paternity, including fry produced during the first 8 weeks in the ponds.
comments.request: Clarify whether pond-produced fry were assessed for paternity.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me which fry were counted towards assigning paternity

comments.issue: Number of errors restricted to 0, 1 or 2 is not a valid measure of learning without prior validation.
comments.request: Validate the error score as a learning measure or use a better measure.
comments.quote: As a cognitive psychologist I would not use this as a measure of learning unless I had previously shown that it IS a measure of learning

comments.issue: The boldness measure lacks repeatability evidence and justification, and was taken from only one assay.
comments.request: Justify the boldness measure and test its repeatability.
comments.quote: Why use the mean boldness test from just one assay? This measure of boldness needs to be justified.

comments.issue: Assays ran in different orders across individuals, so habituation or learning could affect boldness scores.
comments.request: Control or discuss assay order effects on boldness.
comments.quote: What is individuals habituate or learn (which you are hoping they do), how might this affect the boldness score you used?

comments.issue: Raw data are not shown, so individual variation in learning scores cannot be inspected.
comments.request: Include raw data on individual learning scores.
comments.quote: please include some raw data so we can see the variation among individuals in their learning scores

comments.issue: The inhibitory control test did not use the standard opaque-barrier-first procedure, which would assess inhibition more controlledly.
comments.request: Adopt or justify the opaque barrier procedure.
comments.quote: This opaque barrier prior to transparent barrier procedure lets us assess inhibition in a more controlled way. Why was this method not used?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether males can see females from the start zone.
comments.request: Clarify the visibility of females from the start zone.
comments.quote: can the M see the F from the start zone?

comments.issue: The paragraph at lines 437 onward assumes the animal learns, which was not tested or shown.

comments.quote: this is an assumption that the animal learns, which has not been tested or shown

title: Paternity analysis reveals sexual selection on cognitive performance in mosquitofish

study.system: eukaryotic central carbon metabolism genes; phylogenomics

editor_summary: Editor notes considerable potential interest but substantial concerns; cannot accept, though a revised version addressing the serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the approach, but warns that modern lineages poorly represent ancestral states and that several phylogenetic and interpretive issues need fixing.
strengths: beneficial use of NCBI for sequence complementation

comments.issue: Modern Asgard genomes may not represent the ancestral host, so ancestral inferences need caution.
comments.request: Interpret phylogenies cautiously given genetic mosaicism and subsequent evolution.
comments.quote: two million years have passed since the origin of eukaryotes, and the lineages we currently sequence have undergone significant genetic changes involving losses and gains

comments.issue: Sequences below the 25% identity cut-off can produce extended branch lengths.
comments.request: Verify sequence identities across all phylogenies.
comments.quote: Instances where sequences fall below the 25% identity cut-off in KEGG groupings (which sometimes happens) could lead to extended branch lengths in phylogenetic trees

comments.issue: Combining sdhC and sdhD subunits, both typically below 25% identity, may compromise phylogeny reliability.
comments.request: Reconsider combining sdhC and sdhD in the phylogeny.
comments.quote: combining sdhC and sdhD subunits, each with identities typically below 25%, may compromise the reliability of the phylogeny if all sequences are included

comments.issue: References proposing subunit duplications and sdh/frd type B fusion were missed.
comments.request: Cite the earlier work on duplications and fusion.
comments.quote: The authors concluded duplications of the subunits in the prokaryotic domain, but missed references where this was proposed, together with their fussion in sdh/frd of type B

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'divergent SDH' refers to and which type they belong to.
comments.request: Clarify the divergent SDH group and its type.
comments.quote: And what are divergent SDH???? Which type do they belong to?

comments.issue: Eukaryotic clades are not consistently shaded grey, and green/blue branch ambiguity obscures monophyly.
comments.request: Shade clades consistently, improve colour clarity, and check if ambiguous branches are a distinct sdh type.
comments.quote: To enhance the clarity of supplementary phylogenetic information, shading Eukaryotic clades consistently in gray, as observed in some figures, would aid interpretation

comments.issue: Basal placement of Asgards may reflect a chimeric host, gene loss or lack of signal rather than ancestry.
comments.request: Consider alternative explanations for basal Asgard positions.
comments.quote: Wouldn’t a simpler explanation be the chimeric nature of the host? Or losses of genes with inevitable loss of history?

comments.issue: The claim about archaeal versus bacterial origin generalises beyond the carbon-metabolism data analysed.
comments.request: Revise the sentence and generalise cautiously pending broader analyses.
comments.quote: The results shown here are important and relevant, but generalizations about the predominant origin of eukaryotic metabolism should be made cautiously until a broader genomic analysis is conducted

comments.issue: Completeness and contamination levels of the source assemblies are not reported.
comments.request: Report assembly completeness and contamination.
comments.quote: Please include (when possible) information on the completeness and contamination levels of the assemblies containing the prokaryotic proteins, as assemblies may contain contaminants affecting the analysis

reviews.assessment: Commends the ambitious enterprise, but finds the text very difficult to follow and the phylogenetic evidence unconvincing.

comments.issue: The manuscript is very difficult to follow and needs extensive rewriting.
comments.request: Rewrite to convey the complex results intelligibly.
comments.quote: I found the text very difficult to follow.

comments.issue: Figures are unmentioned, do not show the stated results, or omit results entirely.
comments.request: Ensure figures are referenced and show the stated results.
comments.quote: Some figures are mentioned but do not show what is written in the text (ex. line 177 refers to Figure 3A but unclear why)

comments.issue: Phylogenetic evidence for the pathway origins is weak and trees are uninterpretable.
comments.request: Tone down origin claims or strengthen the phylogenetic evidence.
comments.quote: the phylogenetic evidence for inferring the origin of these pathways, which is one of the main results of the paper, is not convincing, at least as currently presented

comments.issue: Methods are described in only four lines, so readers cannot tell where gene families came from or how they were inferred.
comments.request: Explain the methods clearly and sufficiently.
comments.quote: Please explain briefly but clearly the methods, which for the moment sum up to four lines (105-108)

comments.issue: Results should start with the eukaryotic tree and pathway distribution; the first two paragraphs can be merged.
comments.request: Restructure the results as suggested.
comments.quote: I would first present the tree of Eukaryotes and the results of the distribution of the pathways mapped on to it

comments.issue: Figure 1a could merge with a simpler Figure 3a and Figure 1b moved to supplementary; origin colours are unreadable.
comments.request: Restructure the figures as suggested.
comments.quote: The authors could merge Fig. 1a and a simpler version of 3a (remove the colors indicating the potential origins as this will come later, and in any case, they are impossible to read)

comments.issue: The distribution of pathways across eukaryotes is under-discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the pathway distribution more in depth.
comments.quote: The distribution of these pathways across eukaryotes is per se interesting and a great resource for the community, and the authors may want to discuss it a bit more in depth

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 3B could be merged.
comments.request: Merge Figure 2 and Figure 3B.
comments.quote: Here the authors could merge Figure 2 and Figure 3B

comments.issue: Awkward terminology such as 'Jotnarlog' is used without explanation.
comments.request: Explain the terminology.
comments.quote: the authors use awkward terminology that is not explained (“Jotnarlog”?)

comments.issue: The post-LECA paragraph is dense and its examples cannot be seen in Figure 4.
comments.request: Simplify the paragraph and link examples to the figure.
comments.quote: This whole paragraph is very dense and hard to follow. Many examples are given but it is impossible to see them on the figure

comments.issue: Figure 4B duplicates Figure 3A, and Figure 4A is barely referenced.
comments.request: Remove 4B and reconsider the 4A/4B split.
comments.quote: Figure 4B looks very similar to Figure 3A and may be removed. The complex Figure 4A is only mentioned twice, and always together with B, so why making A and B then?

comments.issue: The Discussion refers to Figure 5 generically, without directing readers to panels.
comments.request: Describe Figure 5A and 5B separately.
comments.quote: please describe better Figure 5A and B separately, as you refer generally to Figure 5 but the reader does not know where to look at

reviews.assessment: Very rigorous and comprehensive work and a significant advance, though the intron analysis is weak and several clarifications are needed.
strengths: significant advance on a long-standing conundrum

comments.issue: 'Shared introns' is ambiguous: spliceosomal versus self-splicing, and conserved positions versus homologous introns.
comments.request: Distinguish intron types and clarify what 'shared' means.
comments.quote: Are the introns shared / conserved intron positions or demonstrably homologous introns? The distinction is extremely important when one considers inferring their evolution over long timescales

comments.issue: Recombination with a plastid group II intron cannot readily explain a shared spliceosomal intron at the same position.
comments.request: Explain how recombination could produce such a spliceosomal intron.
comments.quote: So are the authors considering homologous positions between spliceosomal introns and group II self-splicing introns?

comments.issue: How euk and prok introns were analysed and compared, including group II boundaries, is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify how introns were analysed and compared.
comments.quote: addressing how euk and prok introns were analysed and compared to one another

comments.issue: Deep intron conservation is controversial and the most relevant recent literature is not cited.
comments.request: Cite recent intron evolution work, e.g. by Scott Roy and colleagues.
comments.quote: They also don’t cite the most relevant intron literature, e.g., many recent comprehensive analyses by Scott Roy and colleagues

comments.issue: Intron 'sliding' is invoked in figures but never discussed, and the cited Vosseberg et al. paper does not cover it.
comments.request: Discuss the sliding inference and its support.
comments.quote: Santana-Molina et al. invoke intron ‘sliding’ in their figures, but do not discuss it elsewhere, and the Vosseberg et al. paper does not seem to touch this topic

comments.issue: The intron analysis oversteps its relevance and does not bolster the main conclusions.
comments.request: Remove or de-emphasise the intron analysis.
comments.quote: I think the authors are overstepping the bounds of relevance with their intron analysis

comments.issue: Figure 3 is hard to read: labels are far from the tree and group dividers are too subtle.
comments.request: Move labels closer and make data chunks more obvious.
comments.quote: With the taxon labels on the right of the figure, and the tree on the left, I find it difficult to see the presence/absence/potential origin data for each clade

comments.issue: The significance of cyanobacterial contributions for the plastid versus nucleocytoplasmic ancestry discrepancy is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the discrepancy and whether non-cyanobacterial EGTs link these groups.
comments.quote: the authors don’t specifically address the significance with respect to the discrepancy between the common origin of the plastid in the complex red lineages

comments.issue: Individual OTUs are not listed in Figure 3, so shared EGT patterns cannot be assessed.
comments.request: List OTUs or otherwise allow this assessment.
comments.quote: I can’t actually tell from Fig 3 because the individual OTUs are not listed

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'lu' means in cTP/luTP and whether bipartite leader sequences were accounted for in targeting predictions.
comments.request: Clarify 'lu' and the targeting prediction procedure.
comments.quote: I thus want to make sure that the authors have taken this into account when they did their protein targeting predictions for the phototrophs outside of Archaeplastida

comments.issue: The phrasing at Line 281 about relocation of 'nuclear' gene products is flagged.
comments.request: Revise the phrasing at Line 281.
comments.quote: relocation of ‘nuclear’ gene PRODUCTS to the photosynthetic organelle

comments.issue: Using 'primary endosymbiosis' for eukaryogenesis as well as canonical plastids is unconventional.
comments.request: Avoid 'primary endosymbiosis' for both events.
comments.quote: Is this the ‘right’ term to be using for the latter? Most people use ‘primary’ to refer to euk host, prok endosymbiont

comments.issue: Line 67 may be missing references after 'analyses' or have a punctuation issue.
comments.request: Check and fix Line 67.
comments.quote: Line 67. Missing references after “analyses”? Or just punctuation issue?

comments.issue: The statement about Excavata and Discoba at Line 88 needs correction.
comments.request: Revise the Line 88 statement.
comments.quote: Line 88. Excavata include Discoba SOME of which appear to have retained

comments.issue: 'LECA clades' is unclear and used throughout.
comments.request: Rephrase or define it at first use.
comments.quote: What is a LECA clade, exactly? Either change phrasing throughout, or stated it clearly at first usage what is intended

comments.issue: The 1996 reference for endosymbiotic gene transfer is out of date.

comments.issue: Wording at Line 263 about not encoding obvious targeting signals is flagged.

title: Chimeric origins and dynamic evolution of central carbon metabolism in eukaryotes

study.system: global terrestrial ecosystems; novelty maps from climate, defaunation, floristic data

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of interest but raise concerns that need addressing; editor requests a revised manuscript and responses to all comments.

reviews.assessment: Easy to read and important, with many comments to clarify the message and justify methodological choices.
strengths: important subject with consequences across disciplines

comments.issue: The novel-ecosystem definition involves thresholds precluding return to historical conditions; the approach's treatment of thresholds is unclear.
comments.request: Reflect on how the approach considers these thresholds.
comments.quote: the authors may want to reflect how their approach considers these thresholds

comments.issue: Line 48 should also mention subsequent abandonment of the land.
comments.request: Add the point about subsequent abandonment.
comments.quote: Line 48 - also subsequent abandonment of that land

comments.issue: Line 53 does not explain how knowing the drivers helps set conservation and restoration goals.

comments.quote: how does knowing what drives novel conditions help set conservation and restoration goals?

comments.issue: The meaning of 'ecosystem trajectory destabilising' at line 58 is unclear and seems to conflict with line 56.

comments.issue: The frame of reference for 'natural' (industrialisation or earlier) is not explained.

comments.issue: What is considered by 'intactness' is not stated.

comments.quote: I would explicitly state what is being considered by 'intactness'.

comments.issue: Natural disturbances are not considered in 'undisturbed habitat', and it is unclear whether intactness can increase.

comments.quote: can the change in intactness be anything other than negative?

comments.issue: How the two metrics per driver are combined into the >0.33 and >0.66 thresholds is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the metrics within a driver are combined.
comments.quote: how are the two metrics within it combined?

comments.issue: Line 123 repeats the previous sentence given climate change and defaunation show similar novelty.

reviews.assessment: Valuable and well-written contribution, with many requests on terminology, methods details, figures and data availability.

comments.issue: The terms drivers, indicators and dimensions of novelty are used inconsistently.

comments.quote: The terms “drivers of novelty”, “indicator of novelty” and “dimensions of novelty” are used in the manuscript, which seems confusing.

comments.issue: Statements about global human transformation in the summary and introduction lack literature support.

comments.quote: These sentences are not backed up by literature.

comments.issue: The apparent contradiction between natural landscapes and widespread novel ecosystems is not explained.
comments.request: Explain this contradiction to the reader.
comments.quote: how a landscape can still be natural while novel ecosystems are widespread?

comments.issue: The analysis is global at 10 km resolution but is described as local.

comments.quote: The analysis is rather a global one and your data has a resolution of 10 km x 10 km.

comments.issue: Protected areas and key biodiversity areas are only mentioned in the results.

comments.issue: The precise term 'annual precipitation sum' is missing in the fourth paragraph.

comments.issue: Annual precipitation sum may miss changes in temporal precipitation patterns.

comments.issue: The interrelatedness of climatic novelty, defaunation and floristic disruption is not considered.

comments.issue: Alien, nonnative and non-native are used interchangeably.

comments.issue: 'Wild and semi-wild' versus 'natural and semi-natural' terminology is inconsistent.

comments.issue: Regions with low data availability for nonnative species are included, making maps potentially misleading.

comments.issue: The hypothesis supposedly confirmed by the protected-area comparison is not stated in the main text.

title: Widespread ecological novelty across the terrestrial biosphere

study.system: global butterflies; range maps and phylogeny of 12,119 species

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raised substantial points that must be addressed; a revised manuscript addressing these concerns is requested.

reviews.assessment: Novel global assessment with impressive data, but the writing is hard to follow, the niche-erosion analysis is simplistic, and some novelty and claims are overstated.
strengths: novel global assessment of butterfly diversity and rarity
focus on different diversity measures and cross-taxon comparison
impressive data compilation and distribution maps
valuable databases for the scientific community

comments.issue: The writing is hard to follow and interpret throughout, which obscures the main points.
comments.request: Rewrite unclear passages to improve readability.
comments.quote: In general, the writing was hard to follow and/or interpret, which made the manuscript challenging to understand and greatly detracted from the main points.

comments.issue: The niche-erosion assessment ignores butterfly movement and microclimates, calling into question the mountain-trap conclusion.
comments.request: Integrate movement and microclimate effects, or temper the trap conclusion.
comments.quote: The assessment of niche erosion was not well integrated into the manuscript and was rather simplistic. It doesn’t account for movement of butterflies.

comments.issue: The novelty of mountains as butterfly hotspots is overstated, since high montane butterfly diversity is already known.
comments.request: Temper the novelty claims about mountain hotspots.
comments.quote: Some of the novelty is overstated. The finding that mountains are butterfly hotspots is not particularly novel

comments.issue: Calling 14–54% overlap a “small portion” misrepresents the reported values.
comments.request: Revise the wording about the size of the overlap.
comments.quote: those percentages are not really a “small portion”.

comments.issue: The text implies richness increases with elevation, but the pattern sounds like a common mid-elevation peak.
comments.request: Clarify whether the pattern is a mid-elevation peak rather than an increase.
comments.quote: Higher elevation is relative, and 2500 m is a mid-elevation in many places. The manuscript is suggesting richness increases with elevation based on how it is written, but this sounds more like a mid-elevation peak

comments.issue: Coarse 10-km resolution may misidentify elevational peaks and skew ranges toward higher elevations in complex terrain.
comments.request: Assess or acknowledge how coarse resolution affects elevational patterns.
comments.quote: it seems there could be issues identifying peaks in abundance across elevation given the course resolution of the distribution data. A 10 km-resolution could contain a broad range of elevations.

comments.issue: The range-rarity section shifts to discussing diversity without clarifying which diversity measure is meant.
comments.request: Clarify whether this refers to phylogenetic diversity.
comments.quote: the text shifts to discussing diversity (i.e. “Even stronger cross-taxon mismatches emerge when comparing the top 5% diversity centers per realm and taxon.”), which is confusing.

comments.issue: The claim that vertebrate-based priorities miss insect diversity rests on range rarity (endemism), not species diversity.
comments.request: Base safeguarding claims on species richness rather than endemism alone.
comments.quote: however, isn’t this statement based on range rarity (a measure of endemism) rather than species diversity per se? It seems that a better measure of safeguarding diversity of insects should be focused on species richness, not simply endemism.

comments.issue: Butterflies exceeding almost all studied taxa may simply reflect that other insects have not been assessed.
comments.request: Acknowledge that the cross-taxon comparison is biased toward vertebrates.
comments.quote: However, isn’t this simply because other insects haven’t been assessed? In other words, it’s not surprising this is the case given that most other globally studied animal taxa are vertebrates.

comments.issue: The Fig. 1 caption may say “in space” where “across latitude” is meant.
comments.request: Check and correct the figure caption wording.
comments.quote: Do the authors mean “across latitude” rather than “in space” in the figure caption?

reviews.assessment: Nice, impressive study with alarming findings that suits the journal, but writing and storytelling need major improvement before publication.
strengths: impressive variety of sources and methods

comments.issue: The writing is not clear enough and requires revision.
