editor_summary: Editor: rejects; reviewers find potential interest but question the advance over earlier work and the strength of the novel conclusions.

reviews.assessment: Exciting new applications, but the manuscript is hard to follow and conclusions sometimes overreach given very few samples.
strengths: exciting new applications from airborne eDNA
long-read sequencing rare in eDNA studies

comments.issue: The manuscript is hard to follow because sample subsets and which methods were applied to which samples are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sample subsets and method-sample mapping.
comments.quote: In places the manuscript is hard to follow because of the many subsets of samples and lack of clarity of which methods have been applied to which sets of samples.

comments.issue: Conclusions overreach given the very small number of samples.
comments.request: Temper conclusions to match the sample size.
comments.quote: The manuscript is descriptive/observational in the way that it draws conclusions, which is acceptable because the technology is very new, but at times it overreaches given the very small number of samples.

comments.issue: The description of metabarcoding needing a priori knowledge may confuse readers.
comments.request: Reframe around knowledge of broad taxonomic groups.
comments.quote: The description of metabarcoding needing a priori knowledge may be confusing to the general reader because not needing a priori knowledge is often cited as an advantage of metabarcoding.

comments.issue: What 'unaccounted genetic diversity' means is undefined.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: What does unaccounted genetic diversity mean? Not previously documented?

comments.issue: The tricorder comparison is meaningless to readers unfamiliar with it.
comments.request: Explain the specific capabilities being compared.
comments.quote: there will be readers who don’t know what the tricorder is or its capabilities, so this comparison is meaningless

comments.issue: Sample quantities are confusing; totals and consistent sample codes are missing.
comments.request: Head the methods with sample quantities and clear codes.
comments.quote: Generally I find the amount of samples collected quite confusing to understand and it would be best to head up the methods section with quantities of samples collected in total and of each kind

comments.issue: 'Sea turtle hospital indoor air samples' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sample description.
comments.quote: What are “sea turtle hospital indoor air samples”? Is this a language mistake or is it a hospital for turtles?

comments.issue: 70% ethanol is incorrectly described as removing DNA.
comments.request: Correct the method description.
comments.quote: 70% ethanol is not a method which removes DNA.

comments.issue: Molecular methods differ across sample types without justification.
comments.request: Justify the varying molecular methods.
comments.quote: Generally I find the molecular methods quite inconsistent between different sample types in ways that have not been justified.

comments.issue: 'Car-seq' adds unnecessary jargon.
comments.request: Avoid the term and describe swabbing precisely.
comments.quote: We don’t need more subject specific jargon in the discipline – please avoid the term car-seq

comments.issue: Standard kit instructions may not need repeating.
comments.request: Remove or condense the kit instructions.
comments.quote: These seem to be the standard kit instructions so do they need repeating?

comments.issue: It is unclear which methods were used for short- versus long-read sequencing and whether all samples had both.
comments.request: Organize the bioinformatics and sequencing sections by read type.
comments.quote: Can you organize the bioinformatics and sequencing sections so it is clear which methods were used for short and long read sequencing?

comments.issue: Tree-building parameters are not reported.
comments.request: Report the parameters for repeatability.
comments.quote: Any parameters involved in making this tree to make the description more repeatable?

comments.issue: Sample labelling is inconsistent between methods and results.
comments.request: Use consistent sample labels.
comments.quote: It would be great to have consistent and clear sample labelling between the methods and results sections.

comments.issue: Species richness numbers are not given.
comments.request: Give species richness values.
comments.quote: Line 106: Give numbers for species richness

comments.issue: The statement about different recovered timescales lacks evidence.
comments.request: Provide evidence or soften the statement.
comments.quote: Have you got any evidence for this statement (different recovered timescales)?

comments.issue: 'Unbiased representation' is questionable given species differences in eDNA shedding.
comments.request: Qualify the unbiased-representation claim.
comments.quote: Is it fair or clear to say an “unbiased representation of the original set of species” given the likely variation in eDNA shedding between species?

comments.issue: Samples are referred to in varying ways within the section.
comments.request: Use consistent sample references.
comments.quote: Some varying ways of referring to samples here in this section

comments.issue: The Illumina short-read sequencing description is missing from the bioinformatics.
comments.request: Describe the Illumina short-read methods.
comments.quote: Maybe I missed it, but where is the description of Illumina short read sequencing in the bioinformatics?

comments.issue: Read depth is not controlled when comparing relative human DNA abundance.
comments.request: Control for sequencing depth.
comments.quote: If comparing relative abundance of human DNA across samples, do you need to control for depth of sample reads?

comments.issue: The spatiotemporal comparison rests on two samples and cannot separate season from sample variation.
comments.request: Temper the spatiotemporal inference.
comments.quote: this is really stretching the limit of a spatialtemporal study, as you are comparing two samples at different times and different locations, with no understanding whether variation is due to the different seasons or just different samples

comments.issue: Suggesting all planetary genetic diversity will be lost is hyperbolic.
comments.request: Soften the claim.
comments.quote: I agree that the biodiversity crisis is severe, but probably hyperbolic to suggest that the genetic diversity of the planet will be lost entirely

comments.issue: Anole relative abundance inference is tenuous from a single sample.
comments.request: Temper the anole inference.
comments.quote: I think the inference about the relative abundance of anoles is tenuous given that you have only examined one sample.

comments.issue: Human ancestry analysis can only find SNPs, not ancestry combinations.
comments.request: Clarify the limitation of the ancestry analysis.
comments.quote: Human genetic ancestry assessment – correct me if I’m wrong but it can only find SNPs, so we don’t know the combinations of genetic ancestry belonging to each person?

comments.issue: Figure 2 caption uses two names for the same sample.
comments.request: Amend the caption.
comments.quote: Caption of Figure 2: 2 different names used for the same sample – please amend.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether figures refer to OTUs, reads per sample, or pooled samples.
comments.request: Clarify the units in the figures.
comments.quote: in general it needs to be clearer whether you are talking about OTUs or reads per sample or in all samples pooled together?

reviews.assessment: Rejects: no clear study design, replication or comparability; individual findings cannot support conclusions.

comments.issue: Extremely small sample size and heterogeneity across samples prevent any comparability across technologies, methods or scales.
comments.request: Standardise sampling, processing and analysis to allow robust comparisons.
comments.quote: One of the main limitations of the study is the extremely small sample size, and also the heterogeneity across the samples, which does not allow for any comparability

comments.issue: No comparison between shotgun and metabarcoding is included even though metabarcoding is the established standard.
comments.request: Add a shotgun versus metabarcoding comparison.
comments.quote: I am also confused that no comparison between shotgun and metabarcoding was included while metabarcoding is highlighted as the currently established standard in the field of non-invasive biodiversity monitoring by the authors themselves.

comments.issue: Manuscript organization obscures the study design, actual sample size, sample comparability and analysis results.
comments.request: Restructure the manuscript to make design and sample sizes clear.
comments.quote: The organization of the manuscript could also be changed substantially to also make the study design clearer

comments.issue: It is unclear which analyses used shotgun versus exome data and R9 versus R10 chemistry, or which basecalling was used.
comments.request: Specify the method and chemistry used for each analysis.
comments.quote: What analysis has been based on shotgun sequencing, what has been based on targeted exome sequencing? What has been based on nanopore R9, what on R10 chemistry

comments.issue: The nanopore versus Illumina comparison uses species already detected by nanopore, biasing the assessment.
comments.request: Use an unbiased comparison set of species.
comments.quote: it seems that these are the species that were detected by nanopore sequencing anyway, which would hugely bias the assessment of that approach?

comments.issue: The pipeline comparison rests on a single sample, which cannot support general conclusions.
comments.request: Increase replication for pipeline comparisons.
comments.quote: A sample size of one does not allow to make generalized statements about comparability of two pipelines.

comments.issue: Temporal and spatial analyses use only two samples without replicates, so no meaningful conclusions can be drawn.
comments.request: Add replication and technical replicates.
comments.quote: because of such a small sample size, neither the temporal nor the spatial study result in anything meaningful

comments.issue: The Deuterostome classification pipeline is not described, compared to CZID, or published as code.
comments.request: Publish the pipeline and code and compare with CZID.
comments.quote: Has the code been published to make the results replicable to the reviewers and future readers?

comments.issue: AMR detection appears to rely only on Illumina data despite available nanopore tools.
comments.request: Explain or extend AMR detection to nanopore data.
comments.quote: Is the entire AMR detection just based on Illumina sequencing (see Figure 4)? If so, why?

comments.issue: False positives, minimum alignment hit thresholds and database contamination are not addressed.
comments.request: Report thresholds and discuss false positives and contamination.
comments.quote: What was the minimum number of alignment hits to assume presence of a taxonomic group (no information provided?)?

comments.issue: Ethical approval for analysing human genomic data is not stated.
comments.request: State the ethical approval for human data.
comments.quote: Have ethical application been made to be allowed to analyze the human genomic data?

comments.issue: Results and discussion are mixed up; the discussion does not address the study's results and shortcomings.
comments.request: Restructure results and discussion.
comments.quote: Results and Discussions are mixed up; the Discussion in parts contains lots of information that I missed in the introduction

comments.issue: Key prior work (Clare et al. 2022; Reska et al. 2023) is not cited.
comments.request: Cite these studies.
comments.quote: I would also recommend referring to Clare et al. 2022 Current Biology

comments.issue: Library DNA concentrations and read length distributions are not reported.
comments.request: Report library concentrations and read length distributions.
comments.quote: some more details on final library DNA concentrations, and sequence read length distribution would be useful.

comments.issue: Whether only unique mappings were used, and handling of repeats, is not specified.
comments.request: Specify mapping filters or mask repeats.
comments.quote: It would be good to specify if you only used unique mappings here since multiple mapping can sometimes be caused by the presence of repeats.

comments.issue: Robustness of the detections is not checked.
comments.request: Report match details and check robustness.
comments.quote: These are interesting detections, which makes it important to check how robust they are.

comments.issue: The methods section needs restructuring by analysis.
comments.request: Split the section according to each analysis.
comments.quote: I would recommend restructuring this section and splitting it according to what it was done for each specific analysis.

comments.issue: Population genetic inferences are limited because pooled samples cannot be assigned to individuals.
comments.request: State this limitation.
comments.quote: the type of population genetic analyses that can be carried out accurately are greatly limited by the fact that within these pooled samples you can not assign genetic variability to specific individuals nor tell how many individuals got sequenced

comments.issue: The OTU grouping threshold used by CZ is not reported.
comments.request: Report the similarity threshold or mapping quality.
comments.quote: But under which threshold of similarity or mapping quality are these sequences grouped by CZ?

comments.issue: Figure 2B should also show read counts.
comments.request: Add read counts to the plot.
comments.quote: Would be nice to see this plot with read counts as well.

comments.issue: Figure 3A could show the proportion of reads mapping to Homo sapiens.
comments.request: Add this visualization.
comments.quote: In the case of chordata it could be interesting to here visualize the proportion of reads mapping to Homo sapiens.

comments.issue: Figure 5A does not specify the sequences or branch lengths used.
comments.request: Specify sequences and branch lengths.
comments.quote: It would be good to specify which exact sequences were used to build the tree and to specify the branch lengths.

title: Shotgun sequencing of airborne eDNA achieves rapid assessment of whole biomes, population genetics and genomic variation

study.system: Pleistocene South American proboscideans; fossils, isotopes, dental calculus, machine learning

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns; the manuscript cannot be accepted now, but a revision addressing the serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Multi-proxy dietary evidence for frugivory is compelling, but the inferred link between proboscidean extinction and plant extinction risk is not supported and is overstated.
strengths: multiple lines of evidence for high fruit consumption

comments.issue: No evidence links the higher extinction risk of megafauna-dispersed plants to the extinction of the studied proboscidean.
comments.request: Temper the causal claim linking proboscidean extinction to plant extinction risk.
comments.quote: The authors show a suggestive pattern of higher extinction risk in megafauna-dispersed plants but show no evidence to support that this pattern is related to the extinction of the studied species

comments.issue: The paper calls the connection a direct link, but the evidence is only suggestive.
comments.request: Soften the claim from a direct link to suggestive evidence.
comments.quote: I would not say that this is a direct link but suggestive evidence at best

comments.issue: The statement on lines 227-229 is highly overstated relative to the evidence.
comments.quote: Ln 227-229. This seems highly overstated

comments.issue: Changes in community structure and stability are claimed although they were not tested.
comments.request: Remove or support the claim about community structure and stability.
comments.quote: The changes in structure and stability of the community have not been tested

comments.issue: The line 238 claim is an overstatement not supported by the available evidence.
comments.request: Revise the overstatement on line 238.
comments.quote: This is also an overstatement based on the available evidence

comments.issue: 'Cascade of extinctions' is used incorrectly; the paper likely means secondary extinctions, not a cascading effect.
comments.request: Explain which extinctions are meant and use the term cascade correctly.
comments.quote: We usually refer to a cascading effect when it propagates through interactions via indirect paths

reviews.assessment: Well-structured and valuable multi-proxy test of the JMNA hypothesis, but the introduction is unbalanced and the criticism of previous work should be softened.
strengths: of interest to a wide readership
strongest paleobiological evidence for extensive frugivory

comments.issue: The dismissal of prior evidence for extensive frugivory is unjustified; frequent frugivory is the more parsimonious explanation.
comments.request: Tone down the criticism of previous work and present a more integrative view.
comments.quote: I don’t agree that the available evidence is insufficient to demonstrate extensive frugivory in megafauna

comments.issue: Phytoliths from pulp tissue are under-represented, so calculus analysis underestimates the fleshy fruit component of diets.
comments.request: Acknowledge this preservation bias when interpreting dental calculus data.
comments.quote: inferring the diet composition from dental phytoliths in calculus, as frequently done with fossil proboscideans, may result in underestimation of the fleshy fruit component of the diets

comments.issue: The introduction presents an unbalanced view, omitting studies supporting a key role of extinct megafauna.
comments.request: Balance the introduction with evidence supporting JMNA.
comments.quote: The authors somehow present an unbalanced view of the support and lack of support for JMNA in the introduction

comments.issue: Analyses cover just one species, so broad claims based on this case are limited even though geographic coverage is ample.
comments.request: Acknowledge the single-species scope when generalising.
comments.quote: This argument taming down is advisable also because the authors report analyses for just a single species, Notiomastodon platensis

comments.issue: The analogies and differences with extant elephants are not summarised in a table.
comments.request: Add a small table comparing these taxa.
comments.quote: It would be great to have a small table summarizing the main analogies/differences between these taxa

comments.issue: North-south dietary variation in Notiomastodon platensis is under-discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this large-scale dietary variation, comparing savanna and forest elephants.
comments.quote: one aspect I consider under-discussed in the text is the evidence that Notiomastodon platensis showed different dietary patterns in the northern areas vs the southern areas

comments.issue: Paleontological evidence of megafaunal frugivory, such as seed-bearing coprolites, is not cited.
comments.request: Cite coprolite and gizzard-content evidence of frugivory.
comments.quote: Some paleontological evidence exists of frugivory by megafauna: references to coprolites containing seeds

comments.issue: Reference #10, a pooled analysis, may obscure species-specific trends and does not support the claimed lack of megafauna effect.
comments.request: Reconsider this claim and cite contrary genetic evidence.
comments.quote: I’m unsure ref #10 provides well supported evidence for a lack of megafauna effect on generic diversity

comments.issue: The authors ignore positive evidence that extant dispersers cannot compensate for lost megafauna.
comments.request: Cite comparative and functional evidence supporting JMNA.
comments.quote: The evidence points to the contrary: it is hard to think how extant seed dispersers of megafauna fruit species could functionally compensate the loss of animals like the extinct megafauna

comments.issue: Long-term human harvesting of Jubaea fruit may have distorted any signal of megafauna extinction.
comments.request: Discuss human harvesting as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: The case of Jubaea is somehow special, in my opinion, due to its long-term fruit harvesting by humans (also “paleo-humans”) may have “interfered” with any possible signal of megafauna extinction

reviews.assessment: Interesting multi-proxy study with great potential, but the mainly central-Chile sampling should be complemented with discussion of the species' continental range and variability.

comments.issue: Sampling is mainly from central Chile while the species had a continental distribution with variable diet and climate.
comments.request: Add data and discussion covering the species' full range and variability.
comments.quote: This point would not be a problem if the proboscidean studied did not have a continental geographic distribution, with gradual variation in the composition of its diet

reviews.assessment: The machine-learning methods are described too briefly to judge their validity, and the 'deep learning' label is inaccurate.

comments.issue: ML methods are too briefly described: features, architecture, number of models and performance are missing.
comments.request: Provide full technical details of the machine-learning model and its performance.
comments.quote: In the section on methods for machine learning, the authors write too briefly to judge the validity of the methods

comments.issue: Calling the fully connected network 'deep learning' is inaccurate.
comments.request: Describe the approach accurately, as a typical machine-learning algorithm.
comments.quote: the statement of the “deep learning” approach is inaccurate, although the authors didn’t specify how many hidden layers were used

reviews.assessment: Thorough isotope analysis in a novel study, but the isotope-frugivory hypotheses need clearer presentation and key supplementary details should move into the main text.
strengths: interesting and novel paper with potentially major implications
thorough isotope analysis with excellent diagenesis tests

comments.issue: Hypotheses linking oxygen and carbon isotope expectations to frugivory are not clearly presented.
comments.request: State the expected isotope results for frugivory in the Introduction and Discussion.
comments.quote: I did, feel, however, that in some places in the Introduction and Discussion the hypotheses relating to the isotope analysis could be more clearly presented

comments.issue: Line 128 implies isotope analysis evidences frugivory, which it cannot do per se.
comments.request: Clarify that the isotope data do not directly evidence frugivory.
comments.quote: This reads as if it refers to the isotope analysis given its position in the paragraph but as the authors note elsewhere isotope analysis cannot evidence frugivory per se

comments.issue: The amount of fruit needed for an animal to be a relevant seed disperser is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss this threshold in the Discussion, comparing with elephants.
comments.quote: the question is, how much fruits would an animal have to eat to be a relevant seed disperser?

comments.issue: Whether atmospheric corrections were applied for comparability of carbon isotope values through time is only in the SI.
comments.request: State the atmospheric corrections in the main text.
comments.quote: I was left wondering if the appropriate atmospheric corrections had been performed to enable the carbon isotope values to be comparable through time

comments.issue: Standards, machines and calibration information are missing from the main text methods.
comments.request: Move this basic analytical information into the main text.
comments.quote: The basic information regarding standards, machines, calibration was also missing from the main text methods

comments.issue: The description of calibrating gomphothere diet with modern plants is vague.
comments.request: Describe the modern-plant calibration procedure more clearly.
comments.quote: the description regarding using modern plants to ‘calibrate’ gomphothere diet is also a bit vague

comments.issue: The Phillips equation reference is missing and its regional specificity is not discussed.
comments.request: Add the reference and discuss regional baseline variation.
comments.quote: The reference for the Phillips’ equation is not in the list. Is this regionally specific? Baseline data can vary subtly between regions so important to raise and discuss.

comments.issue: Discussion of appropriate enrichment factors for bioapatite sits only in the SI.
comments.request: Move the enrichment-factor discussion to the main text methods.
comments.quote: I would also move the discuss regarding appropriate enrichment factors for the bioapatite from the SI to the main text methods

comments.issue: The impact of temporal oxygen isotope change on using a modern elephant regression line and modern deer data is not discussed.
comments.request: Add a brief discussion of this caveat.
comments.quote: The authors do not really mention the degree to which oxygen isotope analysis and comparison through time might impact the use of a modern elephant regression line

comments.issue: Data are provided as Word documents/tables rather than reusable Excel files.
comments.request: Provide the data as Supplementary Excel files.
comments.quote: Having the data as Supplementary Excel files rather than word documents and tables/PDFS would be a great help for replication/future use of the data

title: Fossil evidence of proboscidean frugivory and its lasting impact on South American ecosystems

study.system: North American birds; eBird/GBIF distributions and climate niches

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise major concerns; revision invited to address the criticisms.

reviews.assessment: Methods seem correct and figures helpful, but novelty is limited for the journal and several analyses need justification or balancing.

comments.issue: Many studies already document climate-driven range shifts and climatic coupling, so novelty is limited.
comments.request: Demonstrate novelty beyond existing range-shift studies.
comments.quote: There are many studies showing how species have modified their distributions following climate change, usually with species moving northwards (or southwards in the southern hemisphere) or to higher elevations to compensate for climate warming

comments.issue: Niche axes are analysed individually, contradicting the n-dimensional niche concept; joint erosion should be estimated.
comments.request: Analyse niche erosion jointly across variables.
comments.quote: Although the authors might have reasons for this approach, it contradicts the classic view of the niche as an n-dimensional space.

comments.issue: The choice and computation of niche variables (EVI productivity, rainfall type) are not justified or detailed.
comments.request: Justify and detail niche variable choices.
comments.quote: Readers would appreciate a justification of the variables used to define the niche of species.

comments.issue: Results focus almost exclusively on temperature despite major precipitation changes.
comments.request: Balance reporting across the three niche variables.
comments.quote: Focusing almost exclusively on reporting the results for temperature does a disservice to this paper.

comments.issue: The potential role of land-use change in bird distribution shifts is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss land-use change effects.
comments.quote: at the very least, a discussion on the potential role of land-use changes in the changes of bird distributions is highly needed

comments.issue: Confidence intervals are not plotted, hiding uncertainty around regression lines.
comments.request: Add confidence intervals to figures.
comments.quote: Plotting confidence intervals in figures showing would help to visualize the uncertainty around the estimated regression line

reviews.assessment: Beautifully written and important results with no major issues; only minor requests for context and clarity.
strengths: clean demonstration of temperature increases across range-shifting patterns
of wide interest to the EEB community

comments.issue: How the approach controls for biases at L73-74 needs more context; observer bias may be temperature-dependent.
comments.request: Explain how biases are controlled.
comments.quote: In L73-74, slightly more context as to *how* the approach controls for these biases would be useful to the reader.

comments.issue: Which MaxDailyTemps are used and how North America is defined are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify temperature data and the definition of North America.
comments.quote: it’s a little unclear which MaxDailyTemps are being used

comments.issue: The negative correlations with migration distance and body mass deserve more discussion.
comments.request: Expand discussion of these trait correlations.
comments.quote: I’m so interested in these negative correlations with migration distance and body mass.

comments.issue: Figure 4 could incorporate more of the information from Figure S7.
comments.request: Expand Figure 4 with Figure S7 information.
comments.quote: I’d love to see a version of Figure 4 that incorporates more of the information from Figure S7.

comments.issue: The purpose and interpretation of the phylogenetic signal analysis is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the purpose of the phylogenetic signal analysis.
comments.quote: I’d be interested in more context for why you’re testing the phylogenetic signal of these traits. What purpose does this serve?

reviews.assessment: Interesting and well-written, but observer-behavior biases may not be fully controlled, casting doubt on the westward shift.

comments.issue: The analysis may not fully account for changing observer behavior in GBIF/eBird data.
comments.request: Use eBird data directly with best-practice filtering.
comments.quote: My main comment is about whether the analyses are able to fully account for changes in observer behavior over time.

comments.issue: The westward shift could arise from changes in the geographic distribution of observers rather than bird populations.
comments.request: Test the west shift with grid-cell occupancy or BBS data.
comments.quote: the result that most species are moving west shown in Figure 3 could arise from changes in geographic distribution of observers

comments.issue: August falls within migration for most North American species.
comments.request: Narrow the summer definition.
comments.quote: Right now the summer distribution is defined as June-August: I suggest using June-July, or perhaps even just June.

comments.issue: 'Niche retainer' and 'niche shifter' terms are confusing and arguably backwards.
comments.request: Clarify or rename the terms.
comments.quote: Niche retainer & niche shifter terms — these cause some confusion because a species with a range shift is a niche retainer, and a species with no range shift is a niche shifter.

comments.issue: Using max rather than mean temperature is not justified and may be driven by heatwaves.
comments.request: Justify using max temperature.
comments.quote: I suggest justifying the use of max temperature rather than mean temperature.

title: Geographic redistributions are insufficient to mitigate exposure to climate change in North American birds

study.system: bipartite ecological networks; machine-learning link prediction

editor_summary: Editor rejects: reviewers find potential interest but concerns about advance over earlier work and relevance to field ecology/conservation preclude publication; suggests transfer to Nature Communications after addressing concerns incl. a usable tool.

reviews.assessment: Sees merits but judges novelty and rigour insufficient for NEE, with comparison methods, missing-link simulation and packaging concerns.
strengths: new method using many interaction properties via machine learning
moderate performance increase, especially cross-network training

comments.issue: Existing structural models already capture known patterns such as nestedness and modularity, so the advance should be acknowledged as smaller.
comments.request: Acknowledge overlap with existing methods.
comments.quote: The ‘structural’ models used to predict links in many of the cited papers, already make use of known patterns (e.g. nestededness or modularity) observed across networks.

comments.issue: The model construction and feature list are not explained early enough; 103 features are hidden in the SI.
comments.request: Explain model construction and summarize the features early.
comments.quote: It would be particularly helpful to have a list (or at least a summary) of the features used in their ML models.

comments.issue: The paper reads like a physics/computer-science paper without ecological contextualisation or case studies.
comments.request: Add ecological context and specific case studies.
comments.quote: In general, this paper very much read like a physics/comp sci paper, without the direct contextualisation and specific case studies that can help ground an ecological method.

comments.issue: A marginal accuracy gain is unlikely to drive uptake, and potential uses are discussed only vaguely.
comments.request: Discuss concrete uses of the approach.
comments.quote: it is unlikely that a marginal improvement in the statistical accuracy will bring a meaningful change. Discussion of potential uses of the approach were pretty thin throughout, limited to fairly vague assertions.

comments.issue: No packaged pre-trained model is provided for wider use.
comments.request: Provide a packaged pre-trained model.
comments.quote: If it is intended and ready for wider use, providing a packaged pre-trained model to use would be a key step

comments.issue: The 103-feature list is buried in the SI and its inclusion is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the feature set and explore its ecological signal.
comments.quote: The ML models use 103 features, but this was only visible after clicking through to the SI.

comments.issue: Correlated predictors may undermine the feature-importance analysis, which was not checked.
comments.request: Check and address predictor collinearity.
comments.quote: strong correlations between predictors can cause issues when calculating feature importance (Figure S3). Was this issue checked for, or otherwise addressed?

comments.issue: Why network class could not be synthesized by the ML model is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this result.
comments.quote: I would be curious to see some discussion of why including the class of network as a predictor could not be synthesized by the ML to overcome the issues.

comments.issue: The comparison focuses on scores rather than on which interactions the new model uniquely identifies.
comments.request: Discuss the interactions newly identified by the model.
comments.quote: I would have appreciated a little more discussion about the properties of the interactions that were correctly identified by the new model, that weren’t well identified by existing models.

comments.issue: Comparison against inferior baselines instead of the best existing models is not justified.
comments.request: Compare with the best available models or justify the choice.
comments.quote: The paper doesn’t adopt the ‘best’ models from previous work for comparison (e.g. coupled models of completeness and SBMs, or the matching-centrality models), instead choosing simpler alternatives that are known to be inferior

comments.issue: Fully random deletion of links does not reflect that weak interactions are more likely unobserved.
comments.request: Use realistic missingness (e.g. subsampling) or justify random deletion.
comments.quote: The generation of artificial missing links was fully random deletion, which doesn’t likely represent the empirical ecological realities that infrequent (weak) interactions are much more likely to be unobserved missing links.

comments.issue: 'Vital' at line 2 is an overstatement.
comments.request: Soften the wording.
comments.quote: Line 2- ‘vital’ is probably an overstatement here – much good work has been done without predicting missed links.

comments.issue: The abstract lacks summary quantification of accuracy and relative improvement.
comments.request: Add these numbers to the abstract.
comments.quote: 9 – Some kind of summary quantification of the accuracy and the relative improvement would be good in the abstract.

comments.issue: Representative predicted networks are not plotted.
comments.request: Plot example predicted networks.
comments.quote: I would like to see some representative examples of predicted networks plotted out somewhere.

comments.issue: 'Consistently undersampled' at line 23 may be misinterpreted as undersampling is variable.
comments.request: Rephrase this statement.
comments.quote: 23: ‘consistently undersampled’ may be misinterpreted in this context – the extent of undersampling is likely pretty variable between networks.

comments.issue: Small network size is unlikely to be the problem; large networks would be harder.
comments.request: Reconsider this claim.
comments.quote: 28 – I’m not convinced the small size of a network is a problem for link prediction – surely the problem would be more difficult in very large networks

comments.issue: Unobserved true negatives and false negatives are not separated as causes of sparseness.
comments.request: Separate these concepts.
comments.quote: 28 – care needed here to separate unobserved true negatives and false negatives as reasons for sparseness.

comments.issue: Whether 90% of species in core areas exceeds chance is not tested.
comments.request: Test with null core areas of the same average size.
comments.quote: Is 90% more than what would be expected by chance? This can be tested by creating “null” core areas having the same average size of the true core areas

comments.issue: The rationale of the spatial-scale analyses is unclear.
comments.request: Better explain the rationale of the spatial-scale analyses.
comments.quote: The rationale of the analyses is not very clear to me and should be better explained.

comments.issue: That characteristic-species number predicts total richness seems an obvious expectation.
comments.request: Explain why this predictor result is non-trivial.
comments.quote: Is this surprising? If I correctly interpreted this analysis, this seems to be a quite obvious expectation.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the three variables entered the model jointly as independent predictors.
comments.request: Clarify how the three variables were included in the analysis.
comments.quote: I had the impression that the 3 variables were included jointly in the same analysis as independent, but I guess this is not the case

comments.issue: The dependent and independent variables at L197 are unclear.
comments.request: Explain the dependent and independent variables.
comments.quote: L 197: the variance of what? Please better explain the dependent and independent variables

comments.issue: The claim is based on averages across bioregions and was not tested within each bioregion.
comments.request: Test whether the pattern holds in each bioregion individually.
comments.quote: note that you did not test if this holds across all the bioregions – you calculated average values across all the bioregions

comments.issue: The sentence at L212-213 lacks references.
comments.request: Add references to the L212-213 sentence.
comments.quote: L 212-213: this sentence needs references

comments.issue: The hotspot reasoning at L233-235 is the original rationale for biodiversity hotspots and should be credited.
comments.request: Cite Myers et al. 2000 for the hotspot rationale.
comments.quote: this is the reason why biodiversity hotspots were originally defined (Myers et al 2000. Biodiversity hotspots for conservation priorities. Nature 403:853-858)

comments.issue: The explanation of non-characteristic species at L356-357 is too long and unclear.
comments.request: Define non-characteristic species earlier and use the term here.
comments.quote: this explanation of non-characteristic species is too long and makes it the sentence unclear

comments.issue: The formulas for the four metrics are not given, so values such as 1, 2 and 0.57 cannot be traced.
comments.request: Make the formulas explicit, starting in Fig. S1.
comments.quote: Formulas used to calculate the 4 metrics should be explicit in Fig S1.

comments.issue: Fig. S1 is important for understanding the four metrics, especially occupancy.
comments.request: Improve Fig. S1 and move it to the main text.
comments.quote: Fig S1 it is quite important to understand the meaning of the 4 metrics (particularly of occupancy). Consider improving this figure, and moving it to the main text

comments.issue: The cross-reference at L402 is wrong and absolute r values are the relevant ones.
comments.request: Cite Supplementary Tables 1-8 and report absolute r values.
comments.quote: L 402; this should be Supplementary Tables 1-8. Also note that the absolute value of r should be the relevant value here

comments.issue: The point about tiny biogeographical regions at L409 is unclear.
comments.quote: L 409: tiny biogeographical regions

comments.issue: The choice of approach for selecting the number of clusters is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the cluster-number approach and show goodness-of-fit plots.
comments.quote: Please explain why you used this approach, and not alternative approaches to the selection of the number of clusters.

comments.issue: The Calinski-Harabasz index gives very different cluster numbers than piecewise regression for several taxa.
comments.request: Show plots to evaluate the robustness of the selected thresholds.
comments.quote: the Calinski-Harabasz index produced rather different results (eg Amphibians: piecewise regression 8, Calinski-Harabasz index 2; Rays: 8 vs. 3)

comments.issue: How all cells were clustered for the global analysis is unclear given different spatial extents and grains across taxa.
comments.request: Explain the global clustering procedure across taxa.
comments.quote: How did you cluster all cells together for the global analysis? The spatial extent (and even the grain) is very different across taxa

comments.issue: The AMI approach at L431 lacks references.
comments.request: Add references for the AMI.
comments.quote: L 431: please add references for the AMI.

comments.issue: The dissimilarity at L511 is ambiguous: cells within a bioregion or roles within bioregions?
comments.request: Clarify what the dissimilarity at L511 refers to.
comments.quote: L 511: here do you mean dissimilarity between cells within bioregion? Or between “roles” within bioregions?

reviews.assessment: Very interesting work; asks to clarify “non-characteristic species”, rename “roles” and move Extended Data Figures 2-8 into the main text.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether “non-characteristic species” means non-endemic species.
comments.request: Clarify the definition of “non-characteristic species”.
comments.quote: I am not sure if this means non-endemic species? This should be clarified.

comments.issue: The word “roles” is awkward.
comments.request: Provide a better term than “roles”.
comments.quote: “Roles” (e.g., lines 78, etc.): this word seems a little awkward to me. I suggest the authors to provide a better one.

comments.issue: Extended Data Figures 2-8 are relegated to an appendix despite illustrating the results well.
comments.request: Incorporate Extended Data Figures 2-8 into the main text.
comments.quote: I find that the “Extended Data Figures 2-8” represent a great illustration of the results, and I don’t think it is appropriate to have them relegated to an appendix.

title: A general rule on the organization of biodiversity in Earth’s biogeographical regions

study.system: non-marine annelids (Clitellata); comparative genomes and RNA-seq stress experiment

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns; the editors cannot accept this version but would consider a revised manuscript addressing them.

reviews.assessment: Commends the resource-rich study but finds novelty, data description, evidence standards and speculation in Results to warrant many changes before publication.
strengths: two new genomes valuable to annelid genomics

comments.issue: A recent Lewin et al. paper already reports the macrosyntenic losses in earthworms and leeches, so this aspect is no longer novel.
comments.request: Credit the prior study and contextualise the novelty accordingly.
comments.quote: the text should adequately be rewritten to give proper credit to this study and to contextualise that this is no longer such a novel aspect.

comments.issue: The analysed data sets and species are not introduced explicitly; species numbers, clades and sequenced species names are missing.
comments.request: Describe the species, clades and newly sequenced genomes at the start of Results.
comments.quote: Describing in text at the beginning of the Results section the number of species they analyse and which clades within the Annelida phylum these belong to

comments.issue: Key datasets are only in Supplementary Table 5, so readers cannot see them at a glance.
comments.request: Move Supplementary Table 5 into the main text as Table 1.
comments.quote: Making Supplementary Table 5 into Table 1 in the Results section of the main text.

comments.issue: Species names lack proper nomenclature with authorities at first mention.
comments.request: Give full nomenclature with authorities at first mention.
comments.quote: Detailing the species name using the appropriate nomenclature the first time that they are mentioned

comments.issue: Some species names are unaccepted (e.g. Amphiduros pacificus should be A. fuscescens).
comments.request: Recheck all species names at GBIF or WoRMS.
comments.quote: I have found some unaccepted species names in the article. For example, Amphiduros pacificus should instead be Amphiduros fuscescens (Marenzeller 1875).

comments.issue: Original publications of the genome assemblies used are not cited in the main reference list.
comments.request: Add the source references for the genome assemblies used.
comments.quote: the articles that published the genome assemblies that the authors are using should be recognised and included in the list of references of the main text.

comments.issue: Fig. 4 relies on tiny species icons, and Fig. 2d tree tips lack taxa names.
comments.request: Add species names to Fig. 4 and taxa names to Fig. 2d.
comments.quote: In particular, Fig. 4 is very difficult to follow based exclusively off small species icons. These should complement and not replace the species name.

comments.issue: Fig. 1a does not indicate each species' ecological niche (marine, freshwater, terrestrial).
comments.request: Label species niches in Fig. 1a as done in Fig. 4.
comments.quote: Lastly, Fig. 1a could benefit from somehow including the ecological niche of each of the species shown (i.e., marine, freshwater, and terrestrial).

comments.issue: Assembly statistics and annotation characterisation of the two new genomes are described too briefly.
comments.request: Report assembly statistics and annotation analyses, such as a multi-genome orthologous-group PCA.
comments.quote: a brief description in text of some of the main genome assembly statistics (e.g., N50, assembly size, number of chromosomes and scaffolds, etc.)

comments.issue: The sentence introducing the transposable-element analysis is awkward and presupposes undefined repeat categories.
comments.request: Talk instead about repetitive elements subdivided into transposable elements and satellite DNA.
comments.quote: The sentence is complicated to follow and awkwardly laid out because the authors need to explain the two types of repeated DNA sequences.

comments.issue: No general description or cross-species comparison of the repetitive-element landscape is provided.
comments.request: Add pie/bar plots of unique versus repetitive DNA and superfamily comparisons.
comments.quote: I miss a general description of the repetitive elements landscape in the species that the authors analyse.

comments.issue: The C. matritensis CMC Chapaev-3 analysis is relegated to Supplementary Data 7 instead of Fig. 3a.
comments.request: Bring the C. matritensis analysis into Fig. 3a.
comments.quote: For clarity purposes, and to show the diversity of levels of CMC Chapaev-3 TE insertions, I’d recommend the analysis of C. matritensis to be brought to Fig. 3a.

comments.issue: Distribution of CMC Chapaev-3 in leeches and its overlap with centromeres are not shown.
comments.request: Add a supplementary figure on leech genomes.
comments.quote: Could the authors maybe quickly add to a Supplementary Figure their distribution across their genomes and whether these overlap with the centromeres?

comments.issue: The trimmed multiple sequence alignment and an MSA overview figure are not available.
comments.request: Provide the trimmed alignment files and an MSA figure.
comments.quote: provide as a Supplementary Files the multiple sequence alignment after trimming (in .fa and/or .aln formats) together with a Supplementary Figure that highlights the MSA for all the sequences included in the tree

comments.issue: Branch support values are not shown in Fig. 3c or Supplementary Data 7, so clade validity cannot be judged.
comments.request: Add support values, optionally with Bayesian posterior probabilities.
comments.quote: Could the authors highlight the branch support values (e.g., bootstrap values for maximum likelihood) in both Fig. 3c and Supplementary Data 7.

comments.issue: The Methods section on Hox gene inference is completely empty.
comments.request: Complete the Hox gene inference methods section.
comments.quote: Crucially, the Methods section on Hox genes inference is completely empty. This must be a mistake during the preparation of the manuscript.

comments.issue: D. gyrociliatus is absent from Fig. 4h and Supplementary Data 9.
comments.request: Add D. gyrociliatus to strengthen the Hox conservation claim.
comments.quote: I’m surprised that the authors do not include Dimorphilus gyrociliatus in Fig. 4h and Supplementary Data 9 (wrongly labelled as Supplementary Data 8).

comments.issue: Inter-chromosomal Hox interactions rest only on the small Fig. 4i circus plot, which could simply have been drawn.
comments.request: Provide further evidence, e.g. Hi-C maps between the chromosomes involved.
comments.quote: The only data support for the inter-chromosomal long-range interactions between Hox genes in clitellates is the small circus plot/drawing shown in Fig. 4i. Could the authors provide us with any further evidence?

comments.issue: Hi-C colour scales lack units, so what they represent is unclear.
comments.request: Add units and state what the colour scale represents.
comments.quote: The Hi-C maps currently lack units in the colour scales, could these please be added? What does the colour scale represent?

comments.issue: Fig. 4 niche schematics are not explained by a legend.
comments.request: Add a legend defining marine, freshwater and terrestrial drawings.
comments.quote: The schematical drawings of the 3 different ecological niches in the different panels may be misleading to some. Could a small legend be added to describe that the drawings mean “marine”, “freshwater”, and “terrestrial”?

comments.issue: Species icons in Fig. 4 panels are not accompanied by species names.
comments.request: Add species names to the figure panels.
comments.quote: As mentioned above, species icons should always be accompanied by species names in the figure panels. Would you be so kind so as to add them?

comments.issue: Gene names in Fig. 4g-i use uppercase HOX instead of invertebrate Hox nomenclature.
comments.request: Use Hox1, Hox2 style nomenclature.
comments.quote: In Fig. 4g, h , and i, the authors may want to adhere to the gene nomenclature (e.g., Hox1, Hox2, and not HOX1 or HOX2) that corresponds to these invertebrate taxa.

comments.issue: Non-Hox genes drawn as triangles in Fig. 4h are easily misread as long genomic stretches.
comments.request: Show them as rectangles of the same size as Hox genes.
comments.quote: In Fig. 4h, showing non-Hox genes as triangles may be misleading. I had misinterpreted those triangles as long stretches of genome between the genes.

comments.issue: Fig. 4g lacks gene models showing actual Hox locations relative to the TAD score track.
comments.request: Add gene models with Hox gene positions.
comments.quote: In Fig. 4g, below the TAD score track, would it be possible to add the gene models with the actual location of the Hox genes?

comments.issue: Fig. 4d macro/microchromosome colours are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Choose colours that are easier to distinguish.
comments.quote: In Fig. 4d, the colour differences between the macro and microchromosomes in the chicken genome are not easy to observe, even as someone without colour blindness.

comments.issue: The Supplementary Data 9 Hox phylogeny lacks branch support values.
comments.request: Add bootstrap or posterior support values.
comments.quote: In Supplementary Data 9, the phylogenetic tree for Hox genes inference should also have branch support values as in the CMC Chapaev-3 TEs phylogeny

comments.issue: Stress/niche-adaptation claims are speculative; were doubts not resolved, they should be removed from the paper.
comments.request: Support or remove statements linking these genes to niche adaptation.
comments.quote: If the authors are not able to reduce my doubts around this section, I believe that they should not include statements on how these genes are involved in the adaptation to their ecological niches

comments.issue: Stress experiment methods are relegated to the Supplementary Data instead of the main text.
comments.request: Move the stress experiment methods into the main text.
comments.quote: The Methods section for the stress experiments should be moved to the main text rather than be relegated to the end of the Supplementary Data section.

comments.issue: No RNA-seq analysis data, QC graphs or summary statistics are provided; the description is inadequate.
comments.request: Report RNA-seq summary statistics such as depth, library type and mapping rates.
comments.quote: The authors do not currently provide any data, graphs, supporting tables, or similar that describe the nature of the RNA-seq analysis and the differential expression analysis they carry out

comments.issue: No figure presents the stress experiment design (species, conditions, replicates, tissues).
comments.request: Add a design panel, e.g. a new Fig. 5a.
comments.quote: A small figure in Fig. 5 (e.g., a new Fig. 5a) that details the experimental design with the species involved, the conditions, the # of replicates/condition, the tissues that got analysed, etc.

comments.issue: No plots characterise the RNA-seq experiment, such as expression distributions or condition-versus-condition scatters.
comments.request: Add expression distribution plots and pairwise scatter plots.
comments.quote: A few plots to quickly characterise the RNA-seq experiment itself, such as histogram or density plots of the gene expression values, for example.

comments.issue: No supplementary table gives per-gene expression, fold-change and adjusted p-value annotations.
comments.request: Provide a full gene annotation table.
comments.quote: A Supplementary Table providing the full annotation of the genes.

comments.issue: The 0.001 FDR threshold is overly stringent and arbitrary given modern practice.
comments.request: Justify or relax the FDR threshold.
comments.quote: Why did you choose a 0.001 FDR threshold when modern omics analyses have concluded that after FDR correction, a 0.05 threshold is perfectly reasonable? I find this too stringent and arbitrary.

comments.issue: The four-fold (|log2FC| > 2) cutoff is stricter than the common two-fold change.
comments.request: Justify the four-fold change threshold.
comments.quote: Could the authors explain why you settle on a four-fold change (i.e., a |log2(fold-change)| > 2) rather than a more lenient one such as a very commonly used two-fold change

comments.issue: 'Several genes' is vague; counts, proportions and how they were obtained are not given.
comments.request: State gene numbers, percentages and selection procedure.
comments.quote: How many genes is several genes? And what % of the total gene set of differentially expressed genes do these represent? How were these obtained?

comments.issue: Claim that relocated genes gained new regulation through proximity is speculative and unevidenced.
comments.request: Show interaction similarity evidence or remove the claim.
comments.quote: Can they show evidence for this? Can they show that the interaction levels of the genes that are in the homologous regions in P. echinospica are similar to those where the transposed genes have ended up in the clitellates?

comments.issue: Several Results paragraphs are too speculative and lack sufficient evidential support.
comments.request: Rearrange and move the speculative passages to the Discussion.
comments.quote: A number of paragraphs included in the Results section of the paper are, in my view, too speculative and devoid of the enough level of evidential support to be include in the Results section.

comments.issue: Important figures are only Supplementary Figures, which reduces readability.
comments.request: Use up to 10 Extended Data Figures in the main article instead.
comments.quote: The authors could include up to 10 Extended Data Figures instead of Supplementary Figures, which would be part of the main article and would improve the reading.

comments.issue: Figure fonts are inconsistent and many panels appear squished by non-proportional resizing.
comments.request: Use one consistent font size and avoid squished panels.
comments.quote: The authors should make sure that the font size across the Figures is large enough and consistent and that no text or plots have been squished in non-proportional resizing.

comments.issue: No supplementary table lists the HOGs and their member genes, nor the genes behind Fig. 2e,f enrichment.
comments.request: Provide the HOG list, highlight lost HOGs, and name enrichment genes.
comments.quote: Could they please provide a Supplementary Table containing the full list of HOGs that are being analysed in the study, including the genes from each of the species of interest that belong to each HOG?

comments.issue: The annelid-versus-model-organism differences claimed from Fig. 4e are unclear; N. najaformis resembles the models.
comments.request: Elaborate on the differences and mark them in the figure.
comments.quote: the authors describe that the differences between annelids and the two model species they choose here were also detected in Fig. 4e as a curve of contact probability vs. genomic distance.

comments.issue: Fig. 4c does not seem to show inter-chromosome interactions as the text implies.
comments.request: Clarify the figure citation or content.
comments.quote: However, Fig. 4c does not seem to show the interactions between different chromosomes. Am I missing something?

comments.issue: Fig. 4g does not show long-range inter-chromosome interactions as cited.
comments.request: Correct the citation or clarify what the panel shows.
comments.quote: Page 9, at the end of the third paragraph, the authors cite Fig. 4g, but this doesn’t show any long-range interactions between chromosomes.

comments.issue: The x2/x12 polyploidy range is unclear and uses a letter x instead of the multiplication sign.
comments.request: Explain x2/x12 and use the × sign.
comments.quote: Could the authors kindly rewrite that sentences to specify what they mean by x2 or x12? Also, could they use the multiplication sign (×) instead of a letter x?

comments.issue: Supplementary Data 9 panels are cramped in one item.
comments.request: Split it into two Supplementary Figures.
comments.quote: Could Supplementary Data 9 potentially be split into two different Supplementary Figures for a better visualisation of both figure panels?

comments.issue: Chromanagenesis is introduced only in the Fig. 5 legend, before the Discussion, without earlier text introduction.
comments.request: Introduce the concept earlier in the text or remove it from the legend.
comments.quote: The authors introduce the concept of chromanagenesis in Figure 5 legend. Could this potentially be introduced earlier in the text?

comments.issue: Many grammar, punctuation, spelling, nomenclature and sentence-structure edits, including rewritten long sentences.
comments.quote: The authors currently overuse parentheses, sometimes even nested ones, throughout the text, to the point that it makes its reading quite complex.

reviews.assessment: Exciting, journal-suitable finding, but asks for discussion of rearrangement diversity and dating, justification of the stress experiment, and a completed Hox methods section.
strengths: well suited for the broad audience of the journal

comments.issue: Only a few genomes represent more than 3500 clitellate species; the diversity of rearrangements is undiscussed.
comments.request: Discuss known diversity of rearrangements within clitellates.
comments.quote: I would appreciate some discussion about the diversity of rearrangements within clitellates if there is something known.

comments.issue: Evidence for punctuated versus gradual change is anecdotal; diversification rate shifts and timing are untested.
comments.request: Test for rate shifts and date the marine-to-freshwater transition.
comments.quote: Evidence that the punctuated equilibrium model as opposed to gradual change underlies the evolution of clitellates seem intriguing but seems anecdotal.

comments.issue: 'Evolutionary distance' is mentioned repeatedly but its source is never explained.
comments.request: Explain where the evolutionary distance comes from.
comments.quote: the authors mention “evolutionary distance“ several times, but it is unclear where this distance is coming from.

comments.issue: The stress experiment's motivation is unexplained and Fig. 5 is not discussed, so its contribution is unclear.
comments.request: Outline the experiment's motivation and discuss it.
comments.quote: However, the motivation for this experiment is not outlined, coming basically out of the blue. The associated figure 5 is not even discussed in the discussion so it is unclear what it adds to the study.

comments.issue: The Hox gene analysis is entirely missing from the methods section.
comments.request: Add the missing Hox methods.
comments.quote: The hox gene analysis is completely missing from the methods section.

comments.issue: Genome sizes of the newly assembled species are absent from the methods.
comments.request: Mention the new genome sizes in the methods.
comments.quote: Genome sizes of the newly assembled species should be mentioned in the method section.

comments.issue: Experiment and genome assembly methods are not separated.
comments.request: Separate the experiment and assembly methods.
comments.quote: The method for the experiment and genome assembly should be separated, e.g. the RNA extraction section on page 23.

comments.issue: Confidence in neocentromere assemblies is unclear given PacBio Sequel data and TE-rich centromeres.
comments.request: Assess the assembly confidence of the neocentromere regions.
comments.quote: Given that the PacBio Sequel platform was used and the TE content of neocentromeres, how confident is the assembly of the latter?

comments.issue: The small-scaffold threshold of <30 Mbps looks implausible, suggesting a unit error.
comments.request: Check and correct the scaffold size threshold.
comments.quote: Page 30: Are small scaffolds really <30 Mbps?

reviews.assessment: Intriguing findings, but the WGD, chromatin architecture and adaptive novel-gene analyses are insufficiently supported and need quantitative, statistical testing.
strengths: findings intriguing and of interest to genome evolution readers

comments.issue: The catastrophic-shattering proposition is only qualitative; typical rates and rates needed to randomize genomes are unspecified.
comments.request: Quantify typical and required fusion/fission rates and compare with other rearranged genomes.
comments.quote: While this proposition is adequately presented as speculative and will remain difficult to test, it would be useful to be more quantitative.

comments.issue: The Ks mixture model lacks goodness-of-fit statistics and model comparisons; the plot does not clearly depart from an L-shape.
comments.request: Provide goodness-of-fit statistics and report other tested models.
comments.quote: I could not find any goodness of fit statistics related to the fit of the selected mixture model or any information about other tested models.

comments.issue: WGD inference relies solely on Ks distributions, which cannot separate WGD from bursts of small-scale duplications.
comments.request: Confirm the Ks results with gene tree-species tree reconciliation.
comments.quote: Confirm Ks plots results with complementary methods such as gene tree – species tree reconciliation

comments.issue: WGD claim lacks synteny evidence that duplicates are enriched on chromosome pairs.
comments.request: Do not claim WGD without synteny evidence for duplicate enrichment.
comments.quote: Refrain from claiming that these bursts of duplications correspond to WGD in the absence of synteny evidence demonstrating the enrichment of duplicates on chromosome pairs

comments.issue: Node 4 dating varies hugely with the species used, undermining the ordering of speciation and duplication events.
comments.request: Resolve the dating discrepancy and its implications.
comments.quote: there is a huge variation in the dating of node 4 depending on the species used, casting doubt over the relative dating of speciation and duplications events.

comments.issue: Rediploidization/gene-loss explanation is confusing because pseudogenization does not move genes across chromosomes.
comments.request: Explain how gene losses could produce the observed randomization.
comments.quote: Gene losses through pseudogenization do not move genes across chromosomes, so why might this explain the observed randomization?

comments.issue: Ancestral ClitLG inference is opaque; without outgroup conservation ancestral and derived arrangements cannot be distinguished.
comments.request: Detail how ClitLGs were inferred and justify the direction of rearrangements.
comments.quote: In the absence of macrosynteny conservation with non-Clitellates outgroups, how can one distinguish ancestral and derived chromosomal arrangements within Clitellates?

comments.issue: No test of whether duplicates sit on the predicted duplicated chromosome pairs, so the proposed WGDs remain unsupported.
comments.request: Test enrichment of duplicated genes on the predicted chromosome pairs.
comments.quote: In the absence of a statistically significant enrichment of duplicated genes on these chromosome pairs, the proposed WGDs events are not supported.

comments.issue: Increased gene losses may simply reflect a ~25% longer Clitellate branch; branch lengths appear arbitrary.
comments.request: Account for branch-length differences in the gene-loss comparison.
comments.quote: Are differences in branch lengths accounted for or could this be simply explained by the branch leading to Clitellata being ~25% longer than surrounding branches?

comments.issue: Some chromosomes carry two predicted centromeres, which is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the double centromere predictions.
comments.quote: On Fig3, why do some chromosomes have two predicted centromeres (for instance chr1 and chr2 of N. najaformis)?

comments.issue: Whether yellow clades in Fig. 3C are Clitellates or Annelids is contradictory between figure and caption.
comments.request: Reconcile the figure labels and caption.
comments.quote: Are yellow clades in Fig. 3C Clitellates or Annelids (the in-figure labels and caption text are contradicting each other)?

comments.issue: Concordance of repeat-based and Hi-C centromere predictions cannot be inspected by readers.
comments.request: Show Hi-C-derived centromere positions alongside repeat-based ones.
comments.quote: Were putative centrosome locations checked against Hi-C maps for validation? Reading the methods it seems that it was, but currently the concordance of the repeats and Hi-C analyses cannot be inspected by reviewers/readers.

comments.issue: Leech centromeric repeats are not examined; their presence or absence would date repeat acquisition relative to rearrangements.
comments.request: Check CMC-Chapaev-3 occurrence at leech centromeres.
comments.quote: What about centromeric repeats in leeches? If CMC-Chapaev-3 is not present at leeches centromeres this would suggest that earthworm divergent repetitive centromere content was acquired well after the ‘catastrophic’ Clitellate genome rearrangements.

comments.issue: A/B compartment inference appears qualitative; whether compartments were quantified is unclear.
comments.request: Quantify compartment organization and strength or state it was visual only.
comments.quote: Is this solely based on visual interpretation of the Hi-C maps or were any attempts made to infer compartment organization and quantify compartment strength in these genomes?

comments.issue: TAD presence rests on visual interpretation; it is not rigorously quantified or statistically tested.
comments.request: Test insulation score distributions or provide aggregated TAD plots.
comments.quote: Is this based on visual interpretation or was it rigorously quantified and statistically tested?

comments.issue: Inter/intra interaction fractions depend on signal/noise ratios that vary across Hi-C experiments.
comments.request: Account for signal/noise differences between Hi-C datasets.
comments.quote: These can vary across Hi-C experiments, even using Hi-C generated from the same protocols and with comparable sequencing depth.

comments.issue: The inter/intra-chromosomal interaction ratio computation is not reproducible and cannot exceed 1.
comments.request: Provide the script and explain the ratio computation.
comments.quote: I do not understand how the inter/intra-chromosomal interaction ratios were computed. How can it be > 1?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether non-significant contacts were retained and whether corrections for bin-pair numbers were applied.
comments.request: Clarify filtering and correction of inter- versus intra-chromosomal comparisons.
comments.quote: Were only statistically significant interactions retained (i.e. higher than the background noise) or were all bin pairs with > 0 normalised contacts retained? Were the results corrected for the higher number of inter as opposed to intra-chromosomal bin pairs?

comments.issue: T. lapidaria is treated as ancestral although its conformation could be recently derived, and marine genomes are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Test whether conclusions hold with both marine genomes in all analyses.
comments.quote: The authors seem to assume that T. lapidaria represents the ancestral chromatin conformation condition, but their less ‘intra-chromosomal’ conformation could very well have been recently acquired.

comments.issue: The per-ALG interaction metric is nonsensical because ALGs do not exist in rearranged Clitellate genomes.
comments.request: Provide a per-ALG contact map supporting the claims or reconsider the analysis.
comments.quote: I do not understand what the “per-ALG intra and inter-chromosomal interactions” mean. These chromosomal units do not exist in the rearranged genomes of Clitellates, so within-ALGs (intra) interactions should be mostly inexistent.

comments.issue: Terebella is absent from Figure 1, limiting assessment of ALG conservation.
comments.request: Include Terebella in Figure 1.
comments.quote: It would also be useful to include Terebella in Figure 1, to have an idea of ALGs conservation in this genome.

comments.issue: Long-range interactions are intra-chromosomal and cannot speak to the relative occurrence of inter-chromosomal contacts.
comments.request: Reconsider conclusions drawn from the Fig. 4e distance curves.
comments.quote: long-range interactions are only intra-chromosomal interactions (otherwise how would one compute a genomic distance between interacting regions, as shown in 4e?)

comments.issue: The claim of enrichment in long-range interactions lacks any statistical test.
comments.request: Provide a statistical test for the enrichment claim.
comments.quote: The authors state p9 “annelids were heavily enriched in long-range interactions compared to model organisms” but I could not see any statistical test supporting this.

comments.issue: Hox long-range interactions and centromere-centromere contacts are not tested against background noise.
comments.request: Test these interactions statistically above background.
comments.quote: Again, is this interaction statistically supported to be above background noise? This also applies to the detection of the putative centromere-centromere contacts.

comments.issue: The text gives only minimal information, hampering understanding and replication.

comments.quote: I encourage the authors to include additional information as supplementary material to make it easier for the reader to understand the results and facilitate the replication of the approach.

comments.issue: The link between R², RMSE and the type of trait distribution is difficult to grasp.
comments.request: Add explanation of the R²/RMSE-distribution link in the main text or supplement.
comments.quote: I found the link between R², RMSE, and the type of distribution difficult to grasp.

comments.issue: Site information is missing, so potential confounding from LUI-climate correlations and the spatio-temporal LUI distribution cannot be judged.

comments.issue: The SKR framework is not described in enough depth, including the steps to apply it and interpret results.
comments.request: Provide a more in-depth description of the SKR framework and its interpretation.
comments.quote: I think that the reader of this work would appreciate a more in-depth description of the SKR framework including the different steps to apply the method and how to interpret the results

comments.issue: The thresholds raise more questions than they answer; explanations and interpretations are underdeveloped.
comments.request: Strengthen and complement threshold explanations in the main text and supplement.
comments.quote: I encourage the authors to strengthened and complement the explanations and interpretations of the threshold both in the main text and in the Supplementary Material.

comments.issue: It is unclear what actually changed at the thresholds and what they mean for grassland structure and function.

comments.quote: What did actually change? Which species went extinct or colonized the system after the first and second threshold?

comments.issue: The meaning of the thresholds for multiple correlated traits and how SKR handles complex trait syndromes is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss thresholds and the SKR framework in the context of trait syndromes.
comments.quote: What do these thresholds mean when considering multiple potentially correlated traits driven by different environmental variables? Generally, how does the SKR framework deals with complex trait syndromes?

comments.request: Assess whether the thresholds are artefacts of the LUI index definition.

comments.request: Test robustness to window and gap sizes and discuss implications.
comments.quote: Why 400 grasslands? Are the results robust to different window sizes? If not, what does it mean for the conclusion?

comments.request: Justify the choice of RMSE.
comments.quote: Although I agree with the choice, I wonder why the authors chose RMSE instead of other similar metrics such as MAE?
