comments.issue: Positive spatial associations cannot be interpreted as positive interactions; exogenous explanations are not excluded.
comments.request: Address endogenous versus exogenous explanations.
comments.quote: it is not possible to evaluate to what extent the observed spatial patterns of plant association are endogenous or exogenous

comments.issue: The long history of succession research based on facilitation is not mentioned.
comments.request: Engage the succession literature.
comments.quote: no explicit mention is made on the concept of succession in the document

comments.issue: Recent indirect-facilitation papers (van Breugel et al. 2024; Danet et al. 2024) are not used.
comments.request: Cite and discuss these papers.
comments.quote: But they are not used in this contribution, neither in the introduction nor in the discussion.

comments.issue: The title's new "cooperation" term and "stable" wording are problematic.
comments.request: Reconsider the title terminology.
comments.quote: Why plant cooperation instead of plant interaction? Adding a new, not really used, term doesn’t simply the central message of the document.

comments.issue: Methods are very difficult to understand: plot characteristics, nurse size and roots, and the three sampling protocols are unexplained.
comments.request: Describe the sampling design and plots fully.
comments.quote: Methods: Very difficult to understand. No description of the type of plots, especially the size, the shape of the nurse, the absolute size of the nurse (size matters), the root system

comments.issue: The sentence at L255-257 is incomprehensible.
comments.request: Clarify this sentence.
comments.quote: woody plants are expected to have a very limited impact on the fitness of woody benefactors by herbaceous beneficiaries

title: Indirect reciprocal facilitation promotes species coexistence in plant communities worldwide

study.system: lagerpetids and early pterosaurs; Triassic palaeobiogeography and palaeoclimate

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns that must be addressed; the manuscript cannot be accepted now but a revised version would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the attempt but is disappointed by the climate-model-only interpretation and wants formation-level proxies and ecology.
strengths: attempt to link pterosaur dispersal to Late Triassic climate dynamics
integration of fossil occurrences with palaeoclimate data

comments.issue: The climate interpretation relies almost entirely on one model run without stratigraphic proxies beyond the humid Carnian.
comments.request: Reference actual formations and their proxy evidence to make interpretations credible.
comments.quote: you rely heavily on the results of the HadCM3L-M2 model run to interpret climate, but other than the humid Carnian interval, invoke no proxies from the stratigraphic record

comments.issue: The paper lacks an ecological viewpoint such as feeding and reproductive drivers of habitat occupation.
comments.request: Consider whether feeding strategy diversification allowed pterosaurs to occupy more environments.
comments.quote: Did pterosaurs evolve more diverse feeding strategies during the 20 My of their Late Triassic history? And would thse new strategies allow them to occupy more diverse environments?

comments.issue: The abstract claim of integrating fossil occurrences with palaeoclimate overstates the coarse model comparison.
comments.request: Describe the comparison more accurately.
comments.quote: Technically, no. The fossil occurrences are compared to a (very coarse resolution) paleoclimate model.

comments.issue: The climatic barriers said to constrain lagerpetids and pterosaurs are never specified.
comments.request: Specify which climate barriers are meant.
comments.quote: Do you ever specify what these climate barriers might be? Presumably drier climate presented a dispersal barrier to pterosaurs but not lagerpetids.

comments.issue: The abstract wording about an environmental disturbance is too vague.
comments.request: Name the disturbance, presumably the Carnian Pluvial Episode.
comments.quote: Very vague wording. To what environmental disturbance does this refer? The Carnian Pluvial Episode?

comments.issue: Specimen ages and formations are not referenced, e.g. the Rhaetian age of Caelestiventus.
comments.request: Cite the host formations and verify the ages.
comments.quote: Caelestiventus is from the Nugget Sandstone (a Wingate equivalent) and spans the Rhaetian to Hettangian boundary. It is found associated with Grallator tracks. Is the Rhaetian age confirmed?

comments.issue: Climate is assumed to be the only dispersal factor, ignoring feeding strategies such as aerial piscivory and cursoriality.
comments.request: Include feeding adaptations as an alternative driver of niche partitioning.
comments.quote: This assumes climate as the only factor involved in the dispersal of the pterosaurs, ignoring a primary factor in their niche partitioning – feeding strategies.

comments.issue: The oldest pterosaurs are already highly derived, making a short pre-fossil origin unlikely.
comments.request: Reconsider the claim that pterosaurs originated shortly before their first appearance.
comments.quote: The oldest pterosaurs found were already highly derived, so this is very unlikely.

comments.issue: The precipitation record shows only limited increases and widespread Norian drying, contrary to the climate-spread narrative.
comments.request: Revise the dispersal interpretation to include adaptations to different environments.
comments.quote: Thus, the dispersal of the pterosaurs very likely involves adaptations to different environments in addition to (or even instead of) the spread of more suitable climate habitat.

comments.issue: The literature search underpinning the fossil database is not cited.
comments.request: Provide citations for the literature search.
comments.quote: Citations for this literature?

comments.issue: Palaeoclimate model results are not evaluated against regional proxy records beyond the mid-Carnian.
comments.request: Check the model against proxy data from North America, South America and Europe.
comments.quote: Why not use at least some of these as a check on the model? The record of the Norian in particular is dynamic and complex than can be captured with a model of this resolution.

reviews.assessment: Finds the premise uninteresting, the presentation unconvincing, and the methods lacking quantitative results, sampling-bias tests and justification of the tree.
strengths: synthesizes recent work and makes interesting points on fossil occurrence distribution

comments.issue: The premise that flying pterosaurs and cursorial lagerpetids occupy different niches is trivial.
comments.request: Reframe the question so it is not akin to comparing mice and bats.
comments.quote: Pterosaurs were flying vertebrates, whereas lagerpetids were small cursorial animals – of course, they occupy different niches.

comments.issue: No sampling-bias metrics are included although fossil record bias is a major confounder.
comments.request: Include proxies of fossil record bias in the analyses.
comments.quote: They do not include any sort of sampling bias metric in their models and only briefly acknowledge the possibility that their results are influenced by “severe sampling biases”.

comments.issue: No parameter estimates or statistical tests support the claims; Δ-log likelihood values are absent.
comments.request: Report quantitative results and statistical tests for both analyses.
comments.quote: Inadequate quantitative results or statistical tests to back up the claims being made: “Δ-log likelihood” is discussed in the Palaeobiogeography results section, but no numbers are given – no parameter estimates are given anywhere.

comments.issue: The chosen phylogenetic tree does not appear to be used in any analysis.
comments.request: Clarify and correct how the tree enters the analyses.
comments.quote: Related to the above point, a phylogenetic tree is chosen but doesn’t appear to be used in any of the analyses. This is a major potential flaw.

comments.issue: “Stratigraphic” is used where “temporal” is meant.
comments.request: Use “temporal” for age disparity.
comments.quote: “Temporal” would be more appropriate than “stratigraphic” in this context as it is not referring specifically to rock or outcrop, but rather overall disparity in the age of fossils

comments.issue: The abstract contradicts itself by stating both gaps and long temporal overlap.
comments.request: Give specific geological time frames of overlap.
comments.quote: These two statements are opposite one another, so it would clarify things immensely to give some specific geological time frames when they do and do not overlap in time and space.

comments.issue: The statement about spatial segregation is abrupt and too definite.
comments.request: Add a lead-in such as “These findings suggest that…”.
comments.quote: This feels very abrupt and is perhaps too definite a statement. I would recommend adding nuance with some sort of lead-in

comments.issue: The stated lagerpetid age range ending in the late Norian is wrong; they persist into the Rhaetian.
comments.request: Correct the stratigraphic range of lagerpetids.
comments.quote: Lagerpetids do not go extinct until the end-Triassic (~201 Ma) and are shown in the Rhaetian map in Figure 1.

comments.issue: Northward spread is inferred from a single taxon, Arcticodactylus.
comments.request: Avoid overgeneralizing from one taxon.
comments.quote: One taxon, Arcticodactylus, occurs northward in the Rhaetian, but to say that pterosaurs are spreading northwards based on a single taxon feels like an overgeneralization.

comments.issue: Ancestral origins simply reflect where the fossils are found and need nuance.
comments.request: Acknowledge that origins depend on tree and fossil sampling.
comments.quote: Of course, this is where the model will place the origin of these groups, as this is where all the fossils are.

comments.issue: Four “outliers” make up about 14% of the 29-taxon dataset and may reflect sampling bias.
comments.request: Reconsider whether these are true outliers.
comments.quote: Four outliers is quite a large percentage of a dataset with only 29 taxa (~14%). Are they really outliers, or is this just another instance of sampling bias?

comments.issue: The supposed high-latitude occurrences lie at lower paleolatitude than the ancestral area near the Tethys.
comments.request: Correct the paleolatitudinal comparison.
comments.quote: These pterosaur occurrences are at a lower paleolatitude than the “ancestral area” near the Tethys.

comments.issue: The supplementary data show pterosaurs have a broader latitudinal range than lagerpetids, contradicting the text.
comments.request: Correct the statement about latitudinal ranges.
comments.quote: According to Figure 1 and the supplementary data, pterosaurs actually have a broader latitudinal range than lagerpetids by about 10 degrees (Lagerpetids: -49.13 to 34.8 paleolat; Pterosaurs: -47.18 to 43.91 paleolat).

comments.issue: Globally suitable Norian conditions yet Tethys-only occurrences point to sampling bias.
comments.request: Account for this discrepancy.
comments.quote: If there are plenty of “suitable conditons” found globally for pterosaurs in the Norian, but they are only found in the Tethys region, is that not very strong evidence for sampling bias?

comments.issue: Sampling bias impacts on results are not investigated despite being acknowledged.
comments.request: Apply approaches such as Dunne et al. 2021 and Gardner et al. 2019, or justify their exclusion.
comments.quote: I would like to see more investigation into how such biases impact the results and conclusions reported here. I recommend an approach outlined by Dunne et al. (2021)

comments.issue: The single randomly selected most parsimonious tree is poorly justified and its sensitivity untested.
comments.request: Discuss alternative trees, test different most parsimonious trees and a strict consensus.
comments.quote: The ability of the model to infer ancestral locations and dispersal rates is entirely dependent on the topology of the tree, especially for poorly sampled groups such as early pterosauromorphs.

comments.issue: Figure 1 makes the groups look like they almost always co-occur, undercutting the study's central sympatry point.
comments.request: Use zoomed panels, finer temporal resolution and show the lack of co-occurrence.
comments.quote: Despite limited sympatry of pterosaurs and lagerpetids being a central point of this study, Figure 1 makes it look like they almost always co-occur, and no statistics tests are given one way or another.

comments.issue: Faxinalipterus is tip dated at ~215 Ma although the locality has a U-Pb date of 225.42 Ma, which may impact results.
comments.request: Use the updated radiometric date in the analyses.
comments.quote: Faxinalipterus minimus is tip dated to ~215 Ma, but the most recent study for this taxon provides a U-Pb date of 225.42 for the locality that produced it (Kellner et al., 2022).

comments.issue: Biases such as specimen incompleteness and immaturity-driven basal positions can affect topology and hence biogeographic results.
comments.request: Discuss and test how these biases affect the analyses.
comments.quote: I would strongly encourage some nuanced discussion about how biases such as incomplete species and artificial basal position inferred for immature individuals might affect the results of the analyses that depend on tree topology.

comments.issue: British English spelling is inconsistent, including in the title.
comments.request: Use British English consistently throughout.
comments.quote: I would recommend using the British English spelling of “palaeobiogeography” for consistency.

comments.issue: Several line-level typos and wording fixes.
comments.quote: Line 52: “palaeogeogaphy”. Typo, should be “palaeogeography”

reviews.assessment: Positive: the work is well done and the conclusions reasonable, with only minor figure, data-availability and table issues.
strengths: effectively handles the results and reaches reasonable, well-founded conclusions
meticulously crafted with hypotheses grounded in robust, well-justified analyses

comments.issue: Maehary bonapartei, split from Faxinalipterus, is not shown in Fig. 1 and it is unclear whether it was analysed.
comments.request: Add Maehary to the figure and clarify whether it was included in the study.
comments.quote: at Fig. 1, the originally described material of Faxinalipterus (not Faxinalpterus as plotted in Fig. 1b) was disassociated into a new putative pterosauromorph, Maehary bonapartei by Kellner et al. (2022)

comments.issue: Climate niche analysis data on figshare are empty and the climatic suitability link in Data availability is missing.
comments.request: Upload the climate niche data and provide the missing link.
comments.quote: data of climate niche analysis is empty at figshare; link of climatic suitability analysis (in Data availability) is also missing.

comments.issue: The table contains a duplicated PULR 06 number for Lagerpeton chanarensis.
comments.request: Check and fix the duplicated specimen number.
comments.quote: at the table: there is a double PULR 06 (number) referred to Lagerpeton chanarensis to be checked (as mentioned by the authors); was this checked?

title: Climate drivers and palaeobiogeography of lagerpetids and early pterosaurs

study.system: Xanthomonas plant pathogens; T4SS and T6SS secretion systems

editor_summary: Concerns must be addressed; R1 wants virD4 and mutant-T4SS functions considered, R2 wants phylogenetic statistics, strain justification and toned-down redundancy claims, R3 wants fitness work and alternative hypotheses.

reviews.assessment: Well-developed study with rigorous data supporting the conclusions, needing only a few minor comments.
strengths: interesting findings on alternative secretion systems
adds significantly to understanding of bacterial competition

comments.issue: Mutant T4SS clusters may still build nanomachines supplying adhesin or other non-secretion functions.
comments.request: Classify virD4 and other T4SS mutations and consider alternative functions.
comments.quote: This raises the possibility that X-T4SSs lacking intact virD4 genes still elaborate X-T4SS nanomachines, and that such organelles contribute to Xanthomonas niche establishment not through effector secretion but instead the production of surface structures/adhesins.

comments.issue: The wording at L109 is confusing.
comments.request: Use the suggested rephrasing.
comments.quote: deletions of the T6SS-i3 or T6SS-i4 had no detectable effects on Xanthomonas virulence on barley or bacterial growth

comments.issue: Whether Xt UPB513 carries a mutant T4SS and where the mutation lies could explain its phenotype.
comments.request: Report the T4SS genotype of Xt UPB513.
comments.quote: Does the Xt UPB513 strain carry a mutant T4SS gene cluster? If so, where is the mutation?

comments.issue: The sentence at L127 should be rephrased.
comments.request: Use the suggested rephrasing.
comments.quote: In these competition assays, Xt LMG728 suppressed E. coli viability by four orders of magnitude, but neither Xt LMG728 nor the isogenic virD4 mutant showed any detectable growth defects.

comments.issue: Strains collected over 120 years do not establish an ancient presence.
comments.request: Avoid calling 120-year-old strains ancient.
comments.quote: the presence of X-T4SS in X. citri strains collected over the past 120 years hardly establishes this X-T4SS to be present in “ancient X. citri strains”

comments.issue: No timing is given for the split of clades 1 and 2.
comments.request: Estimate the timing of the clade split.
comments.quote: Can the authors assign a general time over evolution that the split of clades 1 and 2 occurred?

comments.issue: The mobile element profile of Xanthomonas is not described.
comments.request: Describe mobile elements in Xanthomonas.
comments.quote: What is the mobile element profile of xanthomonas – do these species carry lots (any?) conjugative plasmids or functional ICEs?

comments.issue: Mutant T4SSs may still supply important functions and thus pose a fitness cost.
comments.request: Reconsider the claim that mutant T4SSs carry no fitness cost.
comments.quote: The possibility that virD4 mutant T4SS gene clusters are expressed and supply unknown adhesin or other functions would argue against the notion that such mutant T4SSs do not pose a fitness cost to the cell

comments.issue: Conjugative plasmids could be a source for T6SS-i4.
comments.request: Discuss plasmids as a possible source of T6SS-i4.
comments.quote: In proteobacteria, F or other large conjugative plasmids can carry intact T6SS gene clusters; such plasmids could represent a source for T6SS-i4 if they found their way into Xanthomonas.

comments.issue: Extended data and supplementary figures are poorly resolved.
comments.request: Provide high-resolution supplementary figures.
comments.quote: most of the extended data and Supplementary Figures are poorly resolved in the pdfs. This is problematic and must be corrected.

comments.issue: Significance is shown with undefined a/b letters instead of asterisks.
comments.request: Use asterisks and define significance levels.
comments.quote: Why not use one or more asterisks as is commonly done to show statistical significance, as opposed to the “a” and “b” letters?

reviews.assessment: Good example of functional transfer between redundant systems, but incremental and with alternative hypotheses left unexplored.
strengths: good example of functional transfer between two redundant systems
T4SS replacement well supported by sound phylogenetic studies

comments.issue: The findings are incremental and do not support groundbreaking new concepts.
comments.request: Clarify the conceptual advance.
comments.quote: the findings do not really allow groundbreaking new concepts and at most is incremental

comments.issue: Distinct regulatory mechanisms, rather than energy costs, may explain maintaining multiple systems.
comments.request: Discuss regulatory mechanisms as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: the different systems might have distinct regulatory mechanisms controlling their expression or activity which is then more accountable for maintaining capabilities and sparing energy costs

comments.issue: Observed specificity in killing activity does not fully support functional redundancy.
comments.request: Reconcile the observed specificity with the redundancy claim.
comments.quote: the authors mention some level of specificity when comparing killing activity of the T6SS-i4 and T4SS (lines 221-224), which does not totally support redundancy

comments.issue: The toxins secreted by the different systems are not identified.
comments.request: Identify the toxins secreted by each system.
comments.quote: it would be very appropriate to go in somehow more depth in studying/predicting what are the toxins or putative toxins that are secreted by these different systems

comments.issue: A possible antifungal activity gain is not tested experimentally.
comments.request: Test the antifungal activity experimentally.
comments.quote: In fact, they also mentioned a possible antifungal activity gain, but this should be tested experimentally.

comments.issue: The role of T6SS-i3 is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the role of T6SS-i3.
comments.quote: Do the authors have any clue on the role of T6SS-i3.

comments.issue: Increased fitness after T4SS loss could be tested experimentally.
comments.request: Test the fitness effect of T4SS loss.
comments.quote: The authors suggest the possibility that loss of T4SS may provide increased fitness (line 260). This could be easily addressed experimentally.

comments.issue: The retained toxin might be secreted and redirected to another system such as T6SS.
comments.request: Discuss redirection of the toxin to T6SS.
comments.quote: Would it be possible that the toxin is still secreted and redirected to another system, e.g the T6SS?

title: Functional replacement of ancestral antibacterial secretion system in a bacterial plant pathogen

study.system: steroid receptor proteins; deep mutational scanning of DNA binding

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers raised a number of concerns that must be addressed before publication can be offered, and invites a revision addressing all reviewer and editorial comments.

reviews.assessment: Valuable genotype-phenotype maps, but the theoretical framing of 'bias' is flawed and leads to circular, uninformative interpretations.
strengths: experimental approach and results of enough quality and interest to consider publication
precise genotype-phenotype maps are valuable in their own right

comments.issue: The concept of 'bias' is problematic and used inconsistently; it is essentially equated with anisotropy.
comments.request: Stop using 'bias' and describe the structure of the GP map instead.
comments.quote: Most of that can be solved by not using the concept of bias at all and describe the results in a more theoretically sound way.

comments.issue: Bias requires an explicit expectation, but no meaningful expectation is stated, so claiming bias is not a result.
comments.request: State a meaningful expectation or drop the bias framing.
comments.quote: for the concept to be informative such expectations need to be stated explicitly and need to take some sense or be, at least possible

comments.issue: The structure of the GP map and natural selection are treated as alternative explanations, which is a type III error.
comments.request: Present the structure of the GP map and selection as non-alternative factors.
comments.quote: Notice, as I detail latter, that the structure of the GPM and natural selection are not alternative explanations to the observed evolutionary trajectories

comments.issue: The abstract's opening sentences about bias are bad theory and unrelated to the study.
comments.request: Delete the first two sentences of the abstract.
comments.quote: it is bad theory, and it is not that related to what the authors do in the article

comments.issue: The abstract conflates the GP map with a description of possible phenotypes.
comments.request: Correct the description of what a GP map is.
comments.quote: Notice that the GPM is about the relationship between possible phenotypes and genotypes (which ones are associated with which ones) not a description of the possible phenotypes

comments.issue: The abstract says the GP map encodes phenotypes, but a map does not encode anything.
comments.request: Delete the 'unequal propensity to encode' clause and rewrite.
comments.quote: The GPM is a map, a map between genotypes and phenotypes, it does not encode anything

comments.issue: The abstract should use 'anisotropy' rather than 'bias'.
comments.request: Use anisotropy, or neither term.
comments.quote: In the abstract I would rather use the word anisotropy than bias, or none of them all together

comments.issue: The sentence about the biased distribution of phenotypes means nothing.
comments.request: Delete or rewrite the sentence on line 31.
comments.quote: Simply delete this sentence. It means nothing.

comments.issue: The bias framing makes the first introduction paragraph vague and unscientific.
comments.request: Remove the bias framing from the paragraph.
comments.quote: the bias thing simply makes it rather vague and unscientific

comments.issue: The statement about phenotype production versus selection is contradictory; production and selection are not alternatives.
comments.request: Rewrite the paragraph so production and selection are not posed as alternatives.
comments.quote: Phenotypes have to be produced to be selected (as the authors clearly state in the first paragraph), so whether phenotypic production is important or not, is not a question

comments.issue: The line 68 sentence about biases in phenotype production should use a positive concept.
comments.request: Replace bias with mutational likelihood or variational properties.
comments.quote: Or any other replacement of bias with a positive concept that is not defined as a departure from something that is vague and undefinable

comments.issue: The section title 'Global bias in the AncSR1 GP map' misnames anisotropy.
comments.request: Rename the section, e.g. 'Global anisotropy in the AncSR1 GP map'.
comments.quote: The title of the section: “Global bias in the AncSR1 GP map” should be changed to “Global anisotropy in the AncSR1 GP map”

comments.issue: The measure of anisotropy is inconsistently called bias.
comments.request: Call the measure anisotropy or skewedness.
comments.quote: The first line of the paragraph talks about anisotropy but then the measure of anisotropy is called bias. They must call the measure anisotropy because that is what it is.

comments.issue: The claim that global bias imposes hard limits is circular, since evolve actually means arise by mutation.
comments.request: Rewrite to avoid circularity.
comments.quote: Again, when the authors say evolve they mean “arise” (by mutation) and then it becomes clear that the statement is circular.

comments.issue: Bias is treated as something that can favor or restrict evolution, which is a category error and an oxymoron.
comments.request: Delete or rewrite the paragraph on lines 178-189.
comments.quote: Bias is a statistical concept and as such cannot favor or restrict anything since it is itself based on which variation is being observed.

comments.issue: The section title 'Biases in the GP map affect phenotypic outcomes' should avoid bias.
comments.request: Rename the section, e.g. '(How) the GP map affects phenotypic evolution'.
comments.quote: The title “Biases in the GP map affect phenotypic outcomes of evolution” should be changed to something without bias

comments.issue: Describing the GP map as a bias is misleading and wrong.
comments.request: Replace 'biases' with 'the structure of the GP map'.
comments.quote: As stated describing the GPM as a bias is simply misleading and wrong.

comments.issue: The equilibrium-outcome statement is unclear and wrongly gives agency and constraint to the GP map.
comments.request: Rewrite without attributing agency or constraints to the map.
comments.quote: Moreover, an agency is given to the GPM, as if the GPM would be a process determining which phenotypes are possible while in fact it is just a mere description of the association between phenotypes and genotypes.

comments.issue: The local-bias consequence statement should refer to the structure of the GP map.
comments.request: Replace 'bias' with 'the structure of the GPM' or anisotropy.
comments.quote: Replace bias by “the structure of the GPM” or the anisotropy of the GPM or something a bit more substantial.

comments.issue: All remaining instances of 'bias' need replacing.
comments.request: Replace the rest of the bias instances.
comments.quote: The same goes for the rest of “bias” instances.

comments.issue: The model on line 330 is cryptic and the model itself is never described.
comments.request: Provide the details of the fitted model.
comments.quote: They say they fit a model but they provide no information about which is the model? This is rather mysterious.

comments.issue: The statement that biases increase production probability is circular.
comments.request: Rewrite the statement without circular bias logic.
comments.quote: This is again circular. Biases and GP map are increases (and decreases) in the production probability

comments.issue: The claim that the GP map can override selection is unsupported and conceptually wrong.
comments.request: Remove the claim that the GP map overrides selection.
comments.quote: First the authors have no data on the “GP map’s influence” itself. This is just wrong. The authors have data on the GPM

comments.issue: The statement about new biases is misleading; lineages simply change their phenotypic variability.
comments.request: Describe changing phenotypic variation rather than new biases.
comments.quote: There is no reason to describe this in a negative or bias-in-respect-to-some-unclear-expectation way and, doing so is misleading and unfaithful to reality.

comments.issue: The claim that anisotropy is near-universal is uninformative without mentioning that classical population genetics assumed otherwise.
comments.request: Note that some authors assumed isotropy and cite reference 41.
comments.quote: Just saying that GPMs are like that is not informative unless one mentions that some people though otherwise

comments.issue: The ancestral protein reconstruction approach needs more explanation.
comments.request: Explain whether it is phylogenetic reconstruction followed by mutational screening.
comments.quote: The reader may benefit from some more clarification on the “ancestral protein reconstruction” approach in the second paragraph of page 4

comments.issue: The fluorescence estimates statement would be clearer with numbers.
comments.request: Add numbers to the statement.
comments.quote: Adding some numbers to this statement may make things a bit clearer

comments.issue: The statement 'If the map is anisotropic...' is misleading because it also holds for isotropic maps, and 'evolve' is used loosely.
comments.request: Reword the statement about phenotypes more likely to evolve.
comments.quote: That is actually the case also if the map is isotropic.

comments.issue: Saying the direction of phenotypic evolution favours conservation treats direction as a force and the sentence is unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence on Fig. 3d/3c.
comments.quote: It is not very correct, biologically and logically, to say that the direction of phenotypic evolution favors conservation of the starting phenotype

comments.issue: Higher connectivity in AncSR2 is an observation, not a prediction, and its cause is unknown.
comments.request: Describe it as an observation rather than a prediction.
comments.quote: This is not really a prediction, it is simply an observation, they do not really know why this is the case

comments.issue: The statement that increased connectivity allows access to more genotypes is circular.
comments.request: Remove the tautological statement.
comments.quote: Has completely circular logic. An increase in connectivity is, by definition, being able to access more genotypes (and phenotypes).

comments.issue: The claim that phenotypes change at every step is not new and previous work is not cited.
comments.request: Cite previous work showing this.
comments.quote: Although I agree on that I would say that this is certainly not the first work showing that. In fact, it is kind of obvious. Perhaps cite some previous work.

comments.issue: The Figure 3 caption does not say model and observations are being compared.
comments.request: Mention the model-observation comparison in the caption.
comments.quote: In the caption of figure 3 it would be clarifying to explicitly mention that the results of the model and the observed measurements are being compared.

reviews.assessment: Valuable, high-quality dataset, but the claims about all possible phenotypes and a complete landscape are overblown and unsupported.
strengths: rigorous experimental approach and high-quality data

comments.issue: The claim of measuring 'all possible phenotypes' is far too broad; only 16 phenotypes at a 2-bp region of a 6-bp motif were measured.
comments.request: Narrow the claims to the phenotypes actually measured.
comments.quote: The authors are measuring 16 phenotypes, which correspond to all variants at a 2-bp region of a 6-bp motif. Clearly there are many other possible phenotypes that correspond to variants at other parts of this motif.

comments.issue: The 160,000 variants across 4 amino acid sites do not represent a complete GP landscape, and the bias may not hold in the fuller landscape.
comments.request: Restrict landscape-level claims to the measured submap.
comments.quote: the claim that the 160,000 protein variants the authors construct in each of two SR backgrounds represent a complete GP landscape is overly broad

comments.issue: Expression level of each SR variant was not measured and could bias the results.
comments.request: Measure expression levels of the SR variants.
comments.quote: it would be ideal to also measure the expression level of each SR variant, as this could bias the results

comments.issue: The broader phenotypic variation of AncSR2 might reflect non-specific stickiness rather than a real change in specificity.
comments.request: Test mutants at other RE sites and non-SR RE sequences.
comments.quote: it would also be nice to consider a couple mutants at other sites in the RE sequence, as well as other non-SR RE sequences, to test the hypothesis that this SR is simply more nonspecifically sticky

comments.issue: A word is missing on line 110.
comments.quote: missing word on line 110.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, well-written study with appropriately interpreted results; only a few points to consider in revision.
strengths: excellent contribution combining ancestral reconstruction and deep mutational scanning

comments.issue: The terminology 'multi-phenotype' is confusing because all 16 readouts are DNA recognition.
comments.request: Replace the non-standard multi-phenotype phrasing.
comments.quote: The terminology of ‘multi-phenotype’ is unnecessarily confusing. The authors looked at binding to 16 different DNA elements, but it’s still all DNA recognition.

comments.issue: Whether the substitutions from AncSR1 to AncSR2 arose via selection or drift is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss the role of selection versus drift in this transition.
comments.quote: The authors could say more about whether the substitutions leading from AncSR1 to AncSR2 were likely the product of selection or drift/chance.

comments.issue: Which of the 31 non-helix substitutions drive the GP map differences is not addressed.
comments.request: Say more about how many of these changes are relevant.
comments.quote: Of the 31 others, how many are likely relevant to the broad differences described here between AncSR1 and AncSR2?

comments.issue: 'AT' specificity may act as an intermediate between ERE and SRE but is barely discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the possible intermediate role of AT specificity.
comments.quote: Looking at much of the data in Fig 3 and 5 it appears that ‘AT’ specificity may have played a role as an intermediate specificity between the ERE and SRE.

comments.issue: The higher reachability in Fig. 5d is partly trivial because AncSR2 has more functional genotypes overall; the saturation rate is the key point.
comments.request: Normalise the y axis to the total functional genotypes/phenotypes per background.
comments.quote: It seems that a key point is that the rate of achieving saturation is also higher for AncSR2 than AncSR1 (you can achieve a maximum number of genotypes/phenotypes in fewer steps).

comments.issue: Panels and panel labels in Extended Data Fig. 1 do not match.
comments.request: Fix the mismatched panel labels.
comments.quote: Panels and panel labels in ED Fig. 1 don’t match up.

title: The structure of an ancient genotype–phenotype map shaped the functional evolution of a protein family

study.system: bat and mouse limb development; single-cell and transgenic analyses

reviews.assessment: Novel and thorough study, but several theoretical statements, analyses and manuscript structure need correction and clarification.
strengths: high novelty, of interest across evo-devo

comments.issue: SCTransform is described as an integration tool and IntegrateData as a method; the actual integration method is not reported.
comments.request: Check and correct the integration method description.
comments.quote: In line 108, please note that the SCTransform algorithm is not an integration tool, but a normalization method

comments.issue: Line 119 misdescribes Fig. 1E as top markers rather than annotation marker genes.
comments.request: Reword the statement about Fig. 1E.
comments.quote: I found out in the figure legends that Fig. 1E shows genes used to annotate the integrated cluster, rather than the top markers calculated based on integrated cross-species data.

comments.issue: Deep homology is wrongly invoked for homologous forelimb-derived structures; TF repurposing is the valid framing.
comments.request: Reformulate the deep homology discussion (lines 397-401).
comments.quote: The reference to deep homology as an explanation for cell type conservation, in this case, seems invalid.

comments.issue: Bat-mouse orthology mapping, essential for integration, is not described and one-to-one ortholog use is unclear.
comments.request: Provide the bat-mouse orthology table and describe how orthologs were called.
comments.quote: Please provide the bat-mouse orthology mapping table as supplementary data. In methods, please indicate how bat-mouse orthologs were called for cross-species integration.

comments.issue: Both hg19 and hg38 are used for the bat genome annotation without explanation.
comments.request: Verify and explain the use of two human references.
comments.quote: It is not clear why both human reference genomes hg19 and hg38 are used during C. perspicillata genome annotation

comments.issue: The expression pattern of Grem1 across clusters is not shown.
comments.request: Add a figure showing Grem1 expression per cluster for both species.
comments.quote: Adding an additional figure to show the expression pattern of Grem1 gene in each cluster for both species will be helpful.

comments.issue: Group-level rather than one-to-one cluster correspondence may be an artefact of using only the top 10 marker genes.
comments.request: Repeat the correlation with more marker genes and adjust the conservation statements.
comments.quote: However, this could also be because using only the top 10 marker genes reduced the sensitivity. Could the authors please try to use more marker genes to perform this correlation?

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a clear thesis statement, which appears only at the start of the Discussion.
comments.request: Move the research question and outline to the end of the introduction.
comments.quote: The introduction part (under “Main Text”) seems to lack a clearly defined thesis statement for this paper.

comments.issue: The second introduction paragraph mixes limb development background and the hypothesis.
comments.request: Split the paragraph at line 87.
comments.quote: the second paragraph could be split into two paragraphs at line 87

comments.issue: Claim that single-cell approaches apply to 'any' organism is an overstatement.
comments.request: Change 'any' to 'many'.
comments.quote: In line 97, single-cell approaches can be applied to “any” organism is an overstatement and “many” would be more appropriate.

comments.issue: Acronyms and cluster names are used inconsistently and are not explained in figure legends.
comments.request: Harmonize cluster names and 'log2FC', and define acronyms in legends.
comments.quote: The log fold change value of gene expression has a canonical acronym as “log2FC”, instead of “lfc”.

comments.issue: Slingshot and SCENIC are used without citations.
comments.request: Add citations for slingshot and SCENIC.
comments.quote: In line 186, slingshot could use a citation. In line 257 SCENIC could use a citation.

comments.issue: Line 267 does not specify that proximal markers are elevated in bat FL.
comments.request: Add 'in bat FL' after 'most upregulated genes'.
comments.quote: In line 267, could the authors please add “in bat FL” after the “most upregulated genes”

comments.issue: Figure 4C does not indicate which genes belong to the chiropatagium program.
comments.request: Mark the program genes in Fig. 4C.
comments.quote: Could the authors please mark genes from the chiropatagium gene program to Figure 4 C to make it easier to understand?

comments.issue: The GO enrichment pie chart in Fig. 4D is unconventional and its values are unexplained.
comments.request: Replace the pie chart with a dot or bar heatmap.
comments.quote: Using such a Pie chart to show GO can be confusing as it's fairly unconventional.

comments.issue: P-values in Fig. 4I-K are not explained and statistical tests are missing from the legend.
comments.request: Add statistical test details to the legend.
comments.quote: P-values in Fig. 4 I-K are not explained and please add details of the statistical tests to the legend.

comments.issue: Gene names are not italicized in the methods.
comments.request: Format gene names as in the main text.
comments.quote: Gene names are not in italic font in the methods, please format them like in the main text.

reviews.assessment: Nice job; clearly written and compelling, with mostly minor concerns about sample sizes, figure legends and mutant phenotype specificity.
strengths: large amount of data used to tell a compelling story
contributes to literature on deep homology and novelty

comments.issue: Numbers of embryos and mutants contributing to each experiment are not reported.
comments.request: Report sample sizes for all experiments and mutants.
comments.quote: It isn't clear from the descriptions in the results, figure captions, and methods, how many embryos contributed cells to the pools in the scRNA-seq experiments

comments.issue: Dashed line thresholds in Fig. 1G and S2A are not defined.
comments.request: State the thresholds in the legend.
comments.quote: Fig. 1G and S2A: What threshold do the dashed lines represent? Should be stated in the legend.

comments.issue: Colors in merged micrographs are not explained.
comments.request: Indicate what the colors represent.
comments.quote: The figure panels or legends should indicate what the colors in the merged micrographs represent.

comments.issue: Fig. S3E-H x-axis labels are stretched and hard to read.
comments.request: Reformat the x-axis labels.
comments.quote: Fig. S3E–H: The x-axis label text is stretched and difficult to read.

comments.issue: The bat hindlimb RA-id cluster appears absent, yet a comparison with the mouse cluster is shown.
comments.request: Clarify the hindlimb RA-id cluster annotation and comparison.
comments.quote: From these two panels, it looks like there is no clear RA-id cluster in the bat hindlimb

comments.issue: Typo in Fig. 2S: 'Maker' should be 'Marker'.
comments.request: Fix the typo.
comments.quote: Typo: In Fig. 2S, 'Maker' should be 'Marker'

comments.issue: The RNAseq track in Fig. 3J is partially cut off.
comments.request: Fix the cropped panel.
comments.quote: In my PDF, the bottom of the RNAseq track in Fig. 3J is partially cut off.

comments.issue: The choice to functionally test TBX3 rather than TBX2 or other co-bound TFs is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for selecting TBX3.
comments.quote: Could the choice to proceed with functional test of TBX3 be clarified?

comments.issue: Dashed lines in Fig. 4E are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the dashed lines in the legend.
comments.quote: Fig. 4E: What do the dashed lines represent? Should be explained in the legend.

comments.issue: Mutant phenotypes (reduced or extra digits) suggest non-specific patterning effects rather than a chiropatagium-like phenotype.
comments.request: Rule out non-specific patterning as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Should we worry that the phenotypic effects in these mutants, especially the syndactly, is more of a patterning issue and less of a chiropatagium-like phenotype?

comments.issue: ATAC-seq is described in the methods but absent from the results.
comments.request: Report the ATAC-seq results or remove the methods description.
comments.quote: Line 1115: ATAC-seq is described in the methods but I didn't see ATAC-seq in the results; did I miss it?

reviews.assessment: Incremental but well-written and convincing dataset; however, conclusions about apoptosis suppression and the transgenic phenotype are overinterpreted.

comments.issue: An apoptosis-suppressing mechanism in the bat proximal forewing is not excluded, so the conclusion that apoptosis cannot explain interdigital persistence is unsupported.
comments.request: Provide more convincing evidence against proximal apoptosis suppression.
comments.quote: an apoptosis-suppressing mechanism (e.g., in Meis2+ fibroblasts) is likely active in the bat proximal forewing and persists through subsequent developmental stages

comments.issue: The number of Aldh1a2/Rdh10-positive cells appears lower in bats than mice, and this is not addressed.
comments.request: Comment on the reduced numbers of these cells.
comments.quote: the number of Aldh1a2/Rdh10-positive cells appears relatively lower than in mice

comments.issue: Apoptosis inhibition could be a prerequisite for Meis2+ cell persistence, as in Rdh10 mutants.
comments.request: Exclude this alternative possibility.
comments.quote: Could the authors exclude the possibility that apoptosis inhibition is a prerequisite for the persistence and expansion of Meis2+ cells in the interdigit regions of both bats and Rdh10 mutant mice?

comments.issue: Active suppression of RA/BMP signaling at the origin of Meis2+ fibroblasts is not excluded.
comments.request: Test whether RA/BMP suppression is required for Meis2+ expansion.
comments.quote: it does not exclude the possibility that active suppression of RA/BMP signaling at the point of origin is required for Meis2+ fibroblast expansion

comments.issue: Suppression may occur in other populations; low Aldh1a2/Rdh10 expression elsewhere is not checked.
comments.request: Confirm absence or low expression of Aldh1a2 and Rdh10 in other clusters.
comments.quote: Can the authors confirm that Aldh1a2 and Rdh10 are absent in other clusters?

comments.issue: Grem1 could act as a diffusible anti-apoptotic paracrine signal; Bmpr1a expression is not assessed.
comments.request: Assess Grem1 paracrine effects and Bmpr1a expression.
comments.quote: as an extracellular and diffusible protein, Grem1 can exert a significant paracrine effect without being expressed in these cells

comments.issue: Persistent WNT pathway expression offers an alternative mechanistic explanation for interdigit retention.
comments.request: Compare WNT pathway components between species and link WNT to TBX3.
comments.quote: The persistence of WNT signaling pathway component expression in bat interdigits at later stages could provide an alternative mechanistic explanation for interdigit tissue retention in bat forewings.

comments.issue: Whether MEIS2 binds enhancers or promoters is unresolved.
comments.request: Provide a peak distribution plot.
comments.quote: It remains unclear whether MEIS2 predominantly binds to enhancers or promoters; a peak distribution plot would clarify this.

comments.issue: Bat MEIS2-bound elements are not characterized for conservation or proximal activity.
comments.request: Characterize conservation and activity of these regulatory elements.
comments.quote: Can the authors provide further characterization of bat MEIS2-bound regulatory elements?

comments.issue: Overlap of MEIS2 peaks with bat accelerated regions is not tested.
comments.request: Check overlap with BARs to support the Meis2 role.
comments.quote: Do MEIS2 peaks overlap with bat accelerated regions (BARs) identified in previous studies

comments.issue: What counts as interdigital retention is not defined beyond webbing.
comments.request: Define the interdigital retention phenotype.
comments.quote: it is difficult to determine what exactly is considered interdigital retention?

comments.issue: Tbx3 transgene expression is not shown.
comments.request: Show Tbx3 transgene expression and compare with Meis2.
comments.quote: Tbx3 transgene expression is not shown—does it behave in the same manner as the Meis2 transgene?

comments.issue: Sample sizes for the phenotype analyses in Fig. 4F/H are not documented.
comments.request: Report how many limbs were analysed and affected.
comments.quote: For Figure 4F/H, the sample size (n-values) is not well documented.

comments.issue: Fig. 4 and Fig. S9 3D panels show the same limb buds from different angles.
comments.request: Show different representative examples.
comments.quote: It seems the 3D imaging panels in Fig4 and Fig S9 are the same limb buds with different angles. Instead authors should show different representative examples.

comments.issue: The moderate phenotype may reflect elimination of Meis2+ cells by apoptosis rather than interdigit retention.
comments.request: Consider this alternative explanation for the phenotype.
comments.quote: The authors should consider alternative explanations; for instance, the moderate phenotype observed could be due to the elimination of Meis2+ cells by interdigital apoptosis.

comments.issue: Pooling developmental stages may dilute stage-specific differences.
comments.request: Perform a direct late-stage forelimb comparison.
comments.quote: The cluster comparison appears to be based on pooled developmental stages (Fig. 1 & Fig. S1), which could dilute key differences that may only become apparent at later, apoptosis-relevant stages.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'gene distance in bp' in Fig. 3F is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the term in the figure.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to clarify the exact meaning of this term

comments.issue: Lines 341 and 343 reference the wrong figure panels.
comments.request: Reference Fig. 4H and Fig. 4I-K.
comments.quote: Line 341: Should reference Fig. 4H.

title: Comparative single-cell analyses reveal evolutionary repurposing of a conserved gene programme in bat wing development

study.system: global soundscapes; 139 sites, passive acoustic recordings

editor_summary: Editor notes two reviews were obtained after a third reviewer was unavailable, apologises for the delay, and refers the authors to the reviewers' comments.

reviews.assessment: Praises the unique global dataset but finds the paper poorly written, several analyses flawed, and requiring significant reanalysis and a complete rewrite.
strengths: important message about soundscape rhythms and human noise
addresses a unique set of questions

comments.issue: The paper is poorly written and lacks the density, clarity, robustness and precision expected.
comments.request: Rewrite the prose to be precise, dense and robust.
comments.quote: I found the paper not to be well written; in fact, compared to most Nature/Science/Ecology Letter/PNAS papers I read, this paper lacks the high level of density, clarity, robustness and precision of the prose

comments.issue: Folksy, content-free sentences (for example 'No matter where we are and when we listen, there is sound') weaken the text.
comments.request: Remove folksy, non-scientific statements.
comments.quote: These rather “folksy comments” provide no factual content and are not very scientifically useful

comments.issue: The supplement is difficult to navigate (a supplement to a supplement).
comments.request: Restructure the supplementary material for easier navigation.
comments.quote: The core paper is easy to follow although the supplement got difficult to navigate at times (a supplement to a supplement was confusing).

comments.issue: Terms such as spectral and amplitude are used imprecisely.
comments.request: Follow the soundscape glossary and use terms precisely.
comments.quote: There are MANY terms (spectral, amplitude) not used very precisely either. I would highly suggest consulting the glossary of terms that are in Pijanowski and Rivas

comments.issue: Areas are vague and specifics of analyses and calculations are not described.
comments.request: Describe the analyses and calculations in detail.
comments.quote: There are areas that are quite vague and specifics of analyses and calculations are simply not described.

comments.issue: Large bodies of urban soundscape and biodiversity-assessment literature are missing.
comments.request: Cite urban soundscape (Brown, Kang, Axelsson) and related work.
comments.quote: A large body of literature (on urban soundscapes such as Lex Brown, Jian Kang and Ősten Axelsson and biodiversity assessments a la conservation biology work of say, Zuzana Burivalova) are missing

comments.issue: The take-home points are not made strongly.
comments.request: Strengthen the take-home messages.
comments.quote: the take home points are not made all that strongly

comments.issue: Anthropophony and technophony are conflated; human voices are mixed into the noise category.
comments.request: Clarify the category and focus on technophony as the noise component.
comments.quote: It should be made clear here if the authors truly mean anthropophony or technophony as their major sound source category.

comments.issue: The chorus paragraph lacks known specifics on dawn/dusk chorus composition and variation.
comments.request: Add specifics on chorus composition and latitudinal/seasonal timing.
comments.quote: It is known, for example, that birds and amphibians dominate the dawn chorus and that the dusk chorus is dominated by insects.

comments.issue: The claim that noise patterns are not diel is questionable; highway noise peaks with the working day.
comments.request: Acknowledge predictable diel patterns in traffic noise.
comments.quote: the sounds of highways are likely to be most loud prior to the start of the business/school day and then again most loud during the end of the business/school day. So, I’m not sure I agree with the authors.

comments.issue: The paragraph is too general; soundscape phenology and urban soundscape literature are absent.
comments.request: Describe soundscape phenology and cite urban soundscape research.
comments.quote: There is a lot of literature to support these kinds of patterns and they should be clearly described here. This is also the paragraph where a lot of the urban soundscapes research should be cited (Brown, Kang, Axelsson).

comments.issue: Work on US NPS soundscapes as a natural resource is not cited.
comments.request: Cite NPS soundscape work or reconsider the paragraph.
comments.quote: There is a lot of work done on the US NPS soundscapes as a natural resource

comments.issue: The terms metrics, features, descriptors and representations are used imprecisely and not found in the cited source.
comments.request: Clarify and consistently use these terms.
comments.quote: This paragraph does not precisely use the terms properly and so I was a bit confused with what they were referring to by “metrics”, “features”, “descriptors”, and “representations”

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not explain these terms and needs substantial work.
comments.request: Provide a diagram showing how the terms differ.
comments.quote: Figure 1 is referenced and that figure (which needs A LOT of work) does not provide the reader with what these terms refer to.

comments.issue: 'Voice abundance' is unclear; what is measured is BirdNET richness per recording and site.
comments.request: Rename the metric and justify using call data.
comments.quote: I am also confused by the use of the term “voice abundance”. Some researchers have used the term call rates.

comments.issue: The statement of the paper objectives is clumsy.
comments.request: Rewrite the objectives as suggested.
comments.quote: I am almost certain I know what you mean here in your statement of the paper objectives. But these are clumsy at best.

comments.issue: Human voices should be excluded from the anthropophony list.
comments.request: Remove human voices from the anthropophony category.
comments.quote: I’d exclude human voices from the list of anthropophony (by the way, anthropophony and anthrophony have been determined by a scholar in Latin-Greek to be synonymous).

comments.issue: Circadian, diurnal and diel are used inconsistently for daily rhythms.
comments.request: Use one term, preferably diel, consistently.
comments.quote: Authors have used diurnal through to now. Other researchers use diel which is probably the best term to use of the three. I’d stay consistent with the terminology throughout the paper.

comments.issue: Hourly patterns use local clock time, so diel comparisons across latitudes and dates are misleading.
comments.request: Index time to civil sunrise and account for chorus length.
comments.quote: Using just the local clock time is misleading. Instead, the authors should have indexed the time of the recording to be something of a standard “time since civil sunrise”.

comments.issue: 'Silence' is used incorrectly; silence means complete absence of sound.
comments.request: Replace 'silence' with 'quiet' and describe low amplitude.
comments.quote: I do no think that the use of the term “silence” is proper here. Silence refers to the lack of any sound. That only occurs in vacuums or anechoic chambers. Quiet is a better term

comments.issue: The call-rate findings are not placed in the large literature on bird responses to noise.
comments.request: Relate findings to work such as the Lombard Effect.
comments.quote: There are MANY papers that have described how birds are now calling at higher pitches, are louder or are more active at night in response to the heightened ambient sounds from humans.

comments.issue: The discussion needs a full rewrite; its subheadings pose questions that are not answered.
comments.request: Rewrite the discussion around the actual research questions.
comments.quote: Lines 454-560. The entre discussion needs to be rewritten.

comments.issue: The claim that the analysis pinpoints sound-producing agents is not supported.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the 'pinpoint the agents' claim.
comments.quote: How do the recordings and the analysis “pinpoint the agents that are making sounds

comments.issue: Weak correlations among indices are treated as a problem rather than as complementary measures.
comments.request: Reframe the interpretation of index correlations.
comments.quote: I also want to point out that the fact that the acoustic indices do not always strongly correlate is a GOOD thing. They each are measuring a different aspect of the soundscape.

comments.issue: BirdNET outputs with confidence below 0.50 are not trustworthy.
comments.request: Justify or raise the confidence threshold used.
comments.quote: First, I would not trust any output with confidence scores below 0.50 so I am not certain why they would consider anything less as these are neural net tools that learn threshold into binary output data

comments.issue: False negatives of BirdNET detection are not assessed.
comments.request: Develop and report false-negative assessment methods.
comments.quote: Second, one needs to develop methods that assess false negatives (a bird called and it was not detected at all).

comments.issue: Call rates vary taxonomically, so their use in the analysis is questionable.
comments.request: Reconsider using call rates until BirdNET data use is settled.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I would use call rates in the analysis until the research community can determine how to use BirdNET data that contains a lot of this information.

comments.issue: The implications section fails to explain why ecologists should care.
comments.request: Link results to biodiversity crisis, climate change, conservation and planning.
comments.quote: Why should ecologists care? I can think of dozens of reasons that rise to the very top of highly crucial issues but these are not included anywhere in this paper

comments.issue: The methods paragraph on lines 565-571 needs editing.
comments.request: Edit the paragraph.
comments.quote: Lines 565-571. Paragraph needs some editing.

comments.issue: A figure depicting the experimental design is missing.
comments.request: Add a figure of the experimental design.
comments.quote: A figure here that depicts the experimental designs would be helpful.

comments.issue: FFT window size and type are not described.
comments.request: Describe the FFT settings used.
comments.quote: FFT models are not described. What window size and type were used to process the wav file for use in the analysis?

comments.issue: Index parameter settings may be invalid for Audiomoths; values such as ADI look wrong.
comments.request: Run sensitivity analyses of key index parameters.
comments.quote: it is extremely important to (1) make sure the acoustic indices are given values that make sense (ADI does not look right to me) and (2) that a sensitivity analysis of key parameters be undertaken

comments.issue: A high-pass filter applied after recording is questionable and affects ADI and NDSI.
comments.request: Justify or remove the post-hoc high-pass filtering.
comments.quote: Finally, a high pass band filter applied AFTER the recordings are created does not make sense to me.

comments.issue: The statistical models are confusing and inadequately described; time scaling is unjustified.
comments.request: Rewrite the statistical methods with statistician input.
comments.quote: The statistical analysis section is one of the most confusing parts of the paper. I have no idea what kind of model is being developed.

comments.issue: The data likely violate the Poisson/count model assumptions; random forest is suggested.
comments.request: Check distributional assumptions or use a random forest model.
comments.quote: I am also very suspicious that these data follow any distribution that is part of the assumption of the models (Poisson and count data).

comments.issue: Landscape predictors such as road distance, elevation and vegetation cover are missing.
comments.request: Add landscape predictors extracted from Google Earth Engine.
comments.quote: Some of the predictors of the model should also be landscape features such as distance to road, elevation, slope, aspect, percentage of natural vegetation within fixed radii of the sensors, etc.

comments.issue: Natural sites may also be exposed to road noise, compromising the urban-natural contrast.
comments.request: Place sensors in natural-area interiors away from roads.
comments.quote: Sensors should have been placed in the interior of protected areas and inside (an core area) the natural area if that is a comparative type of location desired by the authors.

comments.issue: The acknowledgements should be shortened by about a third.
comments.request: Rewrite the acknowledgements more succinctly.
comments.quote: 863-897. This can be rewritten to be more succinct (reduce the length by about a 1/3rd).

comments.issue: 'Commented on the manuscript' does not adequately describe author contributions.
comments.request: Describe what each author contributed.
comments.quote: I find the term “commented on the manuscript” not to be very useful nor adequately describe their contribution.

comments.issue: Figure 1 is confusing; the caption omits key parts and panel B lacks a y-axis label.
comments.request: Revise Figure 1, label axes and clarify the table columns.
comments.quote: This is a mess. I’m confused by the three subfigures, especially B. The figure caption does not specify important parts of the diagram (why is the y-axis in B not labeled).

comments.issue: Skewed index distributions indicate incorrect parameter settings, including the ADI noise floor.
comments.request: Sensitivity-test noise floor and other index parameters.
comments.quote: Figure C is most informative as it tells me that the authors have not used acoustic indices properly. When any of these acoustic indices have highly skewed distributions, then the parameters that are used are not correct.

comments.issue: Latitudinal diel plots are suspicious because dawn timing depends on date and latitude.
comments.request: Re-express time relative to dawn before comparing latitudes.
comments.quote: These are very interesting plots. The ones on the left, however, are suspicious to me since the timing of dawn is a function of time of year and latitude.

comments.issue: The phenology curves lack context from global seasonal and climate regimes.
comments.request: Relate the phenologies to climate-driven seasonal patterns.
comments.quote: the acoustic phenology curves to the right, also very interesting, lack proper context

comments.issue: Figure 3B lacks an x-axis label.
comments.request: Label the x-axis in Figure 3B.
comments.quote: Most useful figure in the paper. Label the x-axis in Figure 3B.

comments.issue: Species-composition similarity between urban and natural sites is not quantified.
comments.request: Compute a Jaccard index of dissimilarity between sites.
comments.quote: I wonder if the authors should consider doing a Jaccard Index of Dissimilarity to determine how similar species compositions between sites are.

comments.issue: Whether the lines in Figure 4A and B are model fits is unclear.
comments.request: Explain or remove the reference lines.
comments.quote: For Figure 4A and B, is a linear model fit here or is that line just a reference point (at which case it should be removed or at least explained).

comments.issue: Dozens of colourful supplementary plots are presented without any description.
comments.request: Describe the plots and reorganize the supplements.
comments.quote: The lack of any description of the dozens of (colorful) plots is frustrating.

comments.issue: A mixture of index values is misinterpreted as indices being uninformative.
comments.request: Correct the interpretation of index correlations.
comments.quote: I’m confused by their general interpretation that a mixture of acoustic index values means that they are not informative.

comments.issue: Correlation significance levels and experimentwise error adjustment are not reported.
comments.request: Report significance and adjust alpha (Bonferroni or Dunn-Šidák).
comments.quote: Authors need to provide a level of significance and also adjust to the overall experimentwise error rate and use either the Bonferroni or Dunn-Sidik method to adjust the alpha significance level.

comments.issue: BirdNET validation shows only false positives and true positives, not false negatives.
comments.request: Assess false negatives and report producer/user error metrics.
comments.quote: However, these plots only illustrate False Positives and True Positives. We are finding False Negatives to be a huge problem with BirdNET.

comments.issue: Table S4 is useful and should be distributed as a spreadsheet.
comments.request: Keep Table S4 and provide it as an Excel spreadsheet.
comments.quote: This is a useful table and I suggest leaving this in and distribute as an Excel spreadsheet.

comments.issue: Figure S5 is unreadable and its axes are unlabelled.
comments.request: Label axes and make Figure S5 readable.
comments.quote: This was unreadable for me and given that axes are not labeled, I can’t comment on it.

comments.issue: The cross-reference 'TextS5' may be wrong.
comments.request: Check the supplement numbering.
comments.quote: TextS5 Should this be TextS6?

comments.issue: How habitat/trait variables are used and associated with bird species is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how habitat/trait variables enter the analysis.
comments.quote: I am not certain how these habitat/trait variables are used or are then associated with each species of bird (I assume that is what is being done here).

comments.issue: The cross-reference 'Table S5' may be wrong.
comments.request: Check the table numbering.
comments.quote: Table S5 Should this be Table S7?

comments.issue: The experimentwise error rate should be adjusted.
comments.request: Adjust the experimentwise error rate with statistician input.
comments.quote: Experimentwise error rate should be adjusted in my opinion. Please consult a statistician.

comments.issue: Important BirdNET tropical-performance results are buried in the supplement.
comments.request: Move these results to the main text as limitations.
comments.quote: Content like this should be placed in the body of the main text and placed in the context of limitations.

comments.issue: The table lists a team name instead of individual co-authors.
comments.request: List co-authors by initials instead of team name.
comments.quote: Useful table. The team name is not useful to readers. List co-author with their initials instead.

comments.issue: The site map lacks a legend and site names overlap; it looks unprofessional.
comments.request: Overlay sites on a continent map with a legend.
comments.quote: No legend is provided. Sites names run over one another. Overall, a very unprofessional map.

comments.issue: 108 multicoloured plots have no descriptions, y-axis labels or legend.
comments.request: Describe the plots or remove them.
comments.quote: A set of 4 x 27 = 108 plots are not described at all and none have a y-axis labeled.

reviews.assessment: Good, highly original global soundscape study; concerns are about substantiating conclusions and precision, fixable through text changes.
strengths: largest spatial and temporal soundscape survey to date
first large-scale partitioning of anthropophonic, geophonic and biophonic components
valuable baseline for future climate and migration studies

comments.issue: Text describes species diversity but only a richness proxy is analysed.
comments.request: Describe the metric precisely as richness.
comments.quote: Text describes an analysis of bird species diversity, but some some proxy of richness is analysed and reported.

comments.issue: Rationale for the nested design, and its advantage over global/national designs, is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the nested design rationale in one sentence.
comments.quote: Rationale for study design choices are not completely clear. In particular, what does the Nested design allow you to answer that Global and National do not?

comments.issue: Details of how the global periodic models were created are missing.
comments.request: Provide more detail on model construction.
comments.quote: Method: Modelling. Can you provide more details on how the global periodic models were created.

comments.issue: Rationale and assumptions behind frequency band choices are not stated.
comments.request: State the rationale for the frequency band choices.
comments.quote: spectral energy. Please state rationale for / assumptions behind frequency band choices.

comments.issue: The 300 Hz cut-off rationale is unstated; engine noise may be informative for anthropophony.
comments.request: Justify the 300 Hz cut-off.
comments.quote: Acoustic indices. Please state rationale for 300Hz cut off. If you are analysing anthropophony, is that not useful info – e.g. engine noise etc.

comments.issue: Whether acoustic index settings were matched to spectral-energy frequency values is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how index parameters were harmonised across taxa.
comments.quote: did you map settings of acoustic indices (BI, ADI and NDSI in particular) to these same values?

comments.issue: Whether YAMNet outputs were validated, and how, is not stated.
comments.request: State whether and how YAMNet was validated.
comments.quote: Acoustic event detection. Please state whether you validate the YAMNet outputs and how.

comments.issue: The predictability conclusion lacks a stated basis; richness has lower R² than speech or vehicle.
comments.request: Explain how metrics are shown to capture biophony.
comments.quote: Are you inferring predictability from total R^2? Bird species richness has a lower R^2 than speech or vehicle, and you state elsewhere that the soundscape metrics show relatively weak correlations with biodiversity.

comments.issue: The claim of a drastically different sound background than ever before lacks longitudinal data.
comments.request: Recraft the closing statement around the actual data.
comments.quote: But this is not a longitudinal study – afaics there are no data from which to infer a temporal change, it is just assumed.

comments.issue: The discussion opening sentence is not on point.
comments.request: Focus the opening on the key contribution.
comments.quote: Discussion opening sentence could also be more on point!

comments.issue: What counts as anthropophonic sound (vehicles and voices) is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the definition and label Supplementary Fig. S1.
comments.quote: As it is so central to main claim, please clarify what you mean by anthrophophonic sound – vehicles and voices?

comments.issue: 'Invaded' is a strange choice for anthropogenic sounds in urban green spaces.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: Similarly, you write “clearly invaded by anthropogenic sounds” – “invaded” seems a strange choice for urban green spaces?

comments.issue: 'Circadian' is used where 'diel' is meant; circadian implies endogenous rhythms.
comments.request: Use 'diel' rather than 'circadian'.
comments.quote: Main: para 2 & 3. Do you mean “diel” rather than “circadian” – the latter being endogenous?

comments.issue: Whether the soundscape is treated as subjective/perceptual or objective is not qualified.
comments.request: State and justify the soundscape perspective taken.
comments.quote: Note this depends a little on whether soundscape is considered from as a subjective/ perceptual phenomena or objective. Consider qualifying and confirming perspective taken here?

comments.issue: Other disruptions to diel patterns, such as light pollution, are not referenced.
comments.request: Cite work on light pollution and other disruptions.
comments.quote: Main para 3. Consider referencing other disruptions to usual diel patterns such as light pollution?

comments.issue: The phrase 'How green spaces can conserve acoustic environments' is oddly constructed.
comments.request: Reword the phrase.
comments.quote: “How green spaces can conserve acoustic environments” feels like a strange construction.

comments.issue: Soundscape terms ('acoustic world', 'acoustic landscape') are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Stick to the defined term 'acoustic environment' throughout.
comments.quote: Having defined soundscape as acoustic environment, suggest sticking to it throughout, rather than using “acoustic world”, “acoustic landscape” etc

comments.issue: Speech marks need checking.
comments.request: Check speech marks throughout.
comments.quote: Throughout: check speech marks.

comments.issue: Descriptors are called acoustic indices, soundscape indices and metrics interchangeably.
comments.request: Pick one term, e.g., 'soundscape metrics'.
comments.quote: Throughout: Pick one term for descriptors – e.g. “soundscape metrics” and use throughout. You use acoustic indices, soundscape indices, metrics etc

comments.issue: Whether absolute hour or time relative to sunrise was used is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the time variable and dawn adjustment.
comments.quote: Can you clarify whether absolute hour or time relative to sunrise were used? If the former, were results adjusted relative to dawn?

comments.issue: Figure 1B is hard to read.
comments.request: Represent Figure 1B more clearly.
comments.quote: Figure 1. B) is pretty hard to read, could this be represented more clearly?

comments.issue: 'Metric' would be a better column header than 'index' in Figure 1C.
comments.request: Rename the column header to 'metric'.
comments.quote: Fig1 C. Small, point, but would “metric” be a better column header than “index”? spectral energy is not really an index and you use metric in the text.

comments.issue: The latitude key in Figure 2 and its grouping are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify latitude ranges and grouping in Figure 2.
comments.quote: Fig 2. Can you clarify whether latitude in key refers to latitudinal range and how they are grouped for ease of cross-reference with S1

comments.issue: Units on the S1 y-axis are unclear; negative frequency is meaningless.
comments.request: Clarify units on the y-axis of S1.
comments.quote: S1. Please clarify units on the y-axis. It is not clear what negative frequency means on the spectral metrics

comments.issue: What 'animal' sounds in Figure 1B were dominated by is unclear.
comments.request: Report which animals dominated the sounds.
comments.quote: Fig 1 B. Do you have anything to add on what “animal” sounds were dominated by?

comments.issue: Subplots in S1 are not labelled for cross-referencing.
comments.request: Label the S1 subplots.
comments.quote: Please label subplots in S1 for ease of cross-ref.

comments.issue: Recent debate on the validity of foundational ecoacoustic theory is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Alcocer et al. 2022 in the introduction.
comments.quote: consider including recent debate over validity of foundational evolutionary and ecological theories of ecoacostics

comments.issue: Recent work qualifying the soundscape concept is not included.
comments.request: Cite Farina 2021 and Grinfeder 2022.
comments.quote: Main para 2. Consider including more recent work qualifying soundscape (see 7.1.1)

comments.issue: The Global Footprint Index lacks a reference in the methods.
comments.request: Cite a reference for the Global Footprint Index.
comments.quote: In methods – cite ref for Global Footprint Index

comments.issue: Main paragraph 5 needs a concise introduction to acoustic survey linking from the previous paragraph.
comments.request: Add a linking introduction to acoustic survey.
comments.quote: Main para 5. Needs a concise introduction to acoustic survey to link from previous paragraph.

comments.issue: Lellouch is not the best reference here.
comments.request: Consider Sueur and Farina 2015 instead.
comments.quote: Lellouch is not the best ref. here. Consider Sueur, J. and Farina, A., 2015.
