comments.request: Point out the relevant aspects of Fig. 2E and F.
comments.quote: The exact aspects of Figs. 2 E and F that tell us this should also be explicitly pointed out.

comments.issue: It is unclear how often genes are gained or lost and whether this is reliably inferable over long timescales.
comments.request: Assess the reliability of gain and loss inference over the plotted timescale.
comments.quote: It is not clear how often genes are gained or lost, and whether these changes can be reliably inferred over the large evolutionary times in the x axis of this figure.

comments.issue: Whether gains involve single genes or multi-gene events and their mechanisms is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss single-gene versus multi-gene gain events and their mechanisms.
comments.quote: It would also be good to discuss whether these are thought to involve individual genes or not; for instance, how many events were involved in gains of > 20 genes

comments.issue: Sex-limited genes should read genes with sex-limited expression.
comments.request: Correct the term sex-limited genes.
comments.quote: I think that genes with sex-limited expression is meant when “sex-limited genes” is used. If so, this should be corrected.

comments.issue: The meaning of newly acquired genes on the SDR is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what newly acquired genes refers to.
comments.quote: the meaning is not clear of “newly acquired genes on the SDR”

comments.issue: The anthropomorphic word co-option is unclear and should be replaced with evolutionarily correct wording.
comments.request: Replace co-option with evolutionarily correct terminology.
comments.quote: The anthropomorphic word “co-option” is also unclear in this text, and an evolutionarily correct form of words should be used.

comments.issue: TGRs is used without a definition.
comments.request: Define TGRs.
comments.quote: I could not find a definition of “TGRs”.

reviews.assessment: Very impressive and exciting dataset and analyses, but several claims need stronger statistical support and the methods and figures need clarification.
strengths: impressive amount of work on an exciting system
high-quality genomes for several brown algal species
key findings on the origin and trajectory of UV sex chromosomes

comments.issue: How the phylogeny was inferred and how reliable it is are not described, though this is key to interpretation.
comments.request: Describe how the phylogeny was inferred and assess its reliability.
comments.quote: How was the phylogeny inferred, and how reliable is it? This is key to the interpretation of the results and some information should be provided.

comments.issue: Using only Ks to infer strata is limited because mutation rates are noisy, and the combined evidence is not clearly presented.
comments.request: Present the strata analysis and its combined evidence more clearly.
comments.quote: The strata analysis is a bit confusing. Using only Ks to infer strata seems limited, given how noisy mutation rates can be.

comments.issue: The oogamy-PAR expansion claim rests largely on a single divergent branch, with confounds such as genome size.
comments.request: Provide stronger evidence or tone down the oogamy-PAR expansion conclusion.
comments.quote: I think that either stronger evidence needs to be provided or conclusions need toning down.

comments.issue: It is unclear how ancestral gene content and gene losses were inferred and what counts as a gene loss.
comments.request: Explain the ancestral content and gene loss inference and criteria.
comments.quote: I could not understand from the methods how the ancestral gene content, and the inference of gene losses, were done.

comments.issue: Predictions and patterns for the PAR and SDR are not clearly distinguished in the young gene and mutation rate discussion.
comments.request: Separate PAR and SDR predictions and patterns.
comments.quote: In the discussion of young genes and mutation rates, predictions and patterns for the PAR and SDR are not clearly distinguished, making it hard to interpret what could be driving these patterns.

comments.issue: Statistical test results are reported only in methods and supplements, not in the main text.
comments.request: Report statistical test results throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: Results of statistical tests should be reported throughout the manuscript to support the conclusions, and not just in the methods and supplementary materials.

comments.issue: Small circular plots are hard to read and the figures do not consistently show significant differences.
comments.request: Improve the circular plots and consistently illustrate significant differences.
comments.quote: I found the many small circular plots difficul to read. In general I thought the figures were beautiful but not always completely informative as to how the authors came to the conclusions in the text.

comments.issue: It is not clear which genome assemblies are new versus published, and quality measures for new assemblies are missing.
comments.request: State which assemblies are new and provide quality measures.
comments.quote: It was not clear from reading the text which genome assemblies were new and which were published. Some quality measures should also be provided for new assemblies.

comments.issue: A figure showing male and female coverage of the SDRs is missing.
comments.request: Add a supplementary figure of male and female SDR coverage or kmer equivalent.
comments.quote: Similarly it would be helpful to have a (supplementary) figure showing male and female coverage of the SDRs (or the kmer equivalent).

comments.issue: Several chromosomes in Fig. 1 appear inverted due to opposite assembly strands, and panels B and C lack Mb scales.
comments.request: Fix the inverted chromosomes and add Mb scales to panels B and C.
comments.quote: several chromosomes appear inverted (e.g. between Undaria and Fucus). I think this simply reflects the fact that opposite strands were assembled in their respective genomes, and not a biological difference.

comments.issue: The phrase genes had moved into the V-SDR implies gene movement rather than expansion of recombination suppression.
comments.request: Rephrase to say genes are included in the V-SDR.
comments.quote: this is a funny way to put it, as it implies gene movement as the mechanism, rather than expansion of recombination suppression

comments.issue: The claim that an event occurred between the split of two lineages is illogical because a split is one time point.
comments.request: Use 'after the split' instead.
comments.quote: I don't think something can occur between the split of two lineages, which is one time point. "after the split"?

comments.issue: The heading about expansions and gene gain should specify expansions of the non-recombining region.
comments.request: Make the heading explicit about what expands.
comments.quote: Is this meant to be “expansions of the non-recombining region”? I would make it explicit, otherwise it could mean gene family expansion through duplications.

comments.issue: Numbers are only in supplementary materials, forcing readers to switch back and forth.
comments.request: Provide the relevant numbers in the main text.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to provide numbers in the text, otherwise one must keep going to the supplementary materials to be able to follow.

comments.issue: It is not explicit which species have U chromosome assemblies.
comments.request: State explicitly which species the gene counts refer to.
comments.quote: I assume both species are Ectocarpus sp. 7 and D. herbacea, which seem to be the ones for which U chromosome assemblies are available? But maybe this could be more explicit.

comments.issue: The way strata were classified seems arbitrary, and it is unclear whether any statistics were used.
comments.request: Explain how the number of strata was determined and whether statistics were used.
comments.quote: This seems like a strangely arbitrary way of classifying things. How did you determine the number of strata? Were any kind of statistics performed?

comments.issue: A supplementary figure to Fig. 2F showing all genes in all SDRs, not just ancestral ones, is missing.
comments.request: Add a supplementary figure with all SDR genes.
comments.quote: it would be very helpful to see a (supplementary) figure to 2F for all the genes in all the SDRs, not just the ones that were inferred to be ancestral.

comments.issue: Figure S6 is impossible to read and interpret.
comments.request: Convert Figure S6 to standard plots with larger fonts.
comments.quote: I found these figures impossible to read and interpret. It may just be my tired eyes, but you maybe you could consider modifying them to more standard plots, and make sure the font size is large enough to be easily read?

comments.issue: The species used for Ks calculations in Figures S7-S9 are not stated.
comments.request: State which species were used for Ks calculations.
comments.quote: Figure S7-S9: can you state what species were used for Ks calculations?

comments.issue: The term inverted pattern is unclear.
comments.request: Use 'inverted gene order' instead.
comments.quote: Inverted pattern is not very clear; maybe something like “inverted gene order” would work?

comments.issue: Fig. 2C does not indicate which genes are ancestral versus independently acquired.
comments.request: Mark ancestral and acquired genes in Fig. 2C.
comments.quote: I can't see which genes are ancestral vs acquired in fig 2C. Is this information there?

comments.issue: The term sex-homolog is unclear and should be sex chromosome homolog.
comments.request: Use 'sex chromosome homolog'.
comments.quote: SDR genes remain in the sex-homolog of the species that have lost their UV system

comments.issue: The V-SDR size and sexual dimorphism correlation is based on too few datapoints and no statistics.
comments.request: Run statistics on the correlation or move the claim to the discussion.
comments.quote: How many datapoints do you have? Can you run statistics on this? Otherwise I would move this to the discussion, as it seems rather speculative.

comments.issue: Genome expansions could correlate with structural rearrangements that expand the SDR, confounding the dimorphism link.
comments.request: Consider genome expansions as an alternative driver of SDR expansion.
comments.quote: On a similar note, these species also apparently underwent genome expansions, which could correlate with stuctural rearrangments that expand the SDR.

comments.issue: The conclusion that V-SDR expansions support recurrent independent evolution of oogamy is speculative.
comments.request: Provide stronger support or tone down the oogamy evolution conclusion.
comments.quote: supports instead the recurrent, independent evolution of oogamy in the brown algal

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the male-biased gene enrichment is not on the female sex chromosomes.
comments.request: Clarify which sex chromosomes show the enrichment.
comments.quote: presumably not on the female sex chromosomes?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the generation-antagonistic selection model predicts patterns for the SDR, the PAR or both.
comments.request: State the model's predictions for SDR and PAR.
comments.quote: Does the model make predictions for the SDR or the PAR (or both)?

comments.issue: PAR and SDR are not separated in the Figure 3B violin plots.
comments.request: Separate PAR and SDR in the violin plots.
comments.quote: Similarly, can you separate the PAR and SDR in the violin plots in figure 3B?

comments.issue: Panel 3B does not specify how autosomes were chosen, and autosome 4 seems a poor comparison for D. dichotoma.
comments.request: Specify the autosome numbering and justify the chosen autosomes.
comments.quote: But how were the autosomes picked? For example, in D. dichotoma, the sex chromosome looks extremely similar to autosomes 1 and 3 -- why show autosome 4?

comments.issue: The sporophyte-biased gene enrichment evidence rests on a small number of data points.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited number of data points.
comments.quote: Again this seems like a small number of data points

comments.issue: In a fully non-recombining region, Ks values will be affected by linked selection, so Ks is not a clean mutation-rate proxy.
comments.request: Reconsider the use of Ks as a mutation-rate proxy in non-recombining regions.
comments.quote: I think that In a fully nonrecombining region, neutral mutations will necessarily be under the effect of linked selection, and will not behave neutrally.

title: Origin and evolutionary trajectories of brown algal sex chromosomes

study.system: global forests; lidar aboveground biomass and forest-cover maps

reviews.assessment: Well-written global analysis, but the spatial linear model may overestimate edge effects and misattribute other disturbances.

comments.issue: Model may misattribute agricultural, logging or climate disturbance near edges to edge effects.
comments.request: Separate pure edge effects from other disturbance sources.
comments.quote: This approach risks misattributing other disturbances (e.g., those related to agricultural cultivation or selective logging) as “edge effects.”

comments.issue: Static linear model cannot capture the non-linear decline of edge effects with distance.
comments.request: Use a non-linear model or another approach.
comments.quote: the impact near the edge (e.g., within a few meters) is disproportionately higher than at longer distances. A static linear model cannot accurately represent these dynamics.

comments.issue: Mechanisms behind the precipitation–edge effect relationship remain ambiguous.
comments.request: Include VPD in the analysis rather than speculating.
comments.quote: If VPD is the main driver, the authors should include it in the analysis rather than relying on speculative assumptions.

comments.issue: Climate and agriculture findings rely on a single AGB product.
comments.request: Test them with tree cover data to reduce bias.
comments.quote: The main findings related to climate and agricultural impacts on the forest edge effects should also be tested with tree cover data, to reduce the potential bias using one AGB product.

comments.issue: Agriculture data source and details are not introduced anywhere in the manuscript.
comments.request: Describe the agriculture data source and processing.
comments.quote: The data source and details about the agriculture data are not introduced in any part of the manuscript.

comments.issue: Leave-one-out description conflicts with the methods' 20% random-sample removal for R2.
comments.request: Clarify the leave-one-out procedure.
comments.quote: Leave-one-out is confusing, as in the method, the authors introduced about 20% random samples are removed for the calculation of R2.

comments.issue: Necessity of biome-level XGBoost models is unclear given the global-generic model.
comments.request: Justify the biome-level models or drop them.
comments.quote: Why biome-level XGBoost models are needed where a global-generic model can already work on understanding factors of edge effects?

comments.issue: Precipitation SHAP values differ between panels d and e–f.
comments.request: Present the same SHAP values across panels.
comments.quote: Why there are different SHAP values in e-f compared to d? Same SHAP values should be presented regarding contributions from mean annual precipitation.

reviews.assessment: Very relevant and impactful study; asks for deeper discussion of older maps, opposing field results, and omitted fine-scale drivers.
strengths: logical description of the complex methods

comments.issue: Some potentially relevant literature is missing from the introduction.
comments.request: Add the suggested references.
comments.quote: I was missing some potentially relevant literature at some points, which I added in my comments.

comments.issue: Results section is overlong and mixes results with discussion despite a separate discussion section.
comments.request: Shorten results and choose one structuring approach.
comments.quote: The results section is quite extensive and some parts can be removed to increase the focus of the story line.

comments.issue: Old Hansen/Harris maps (2000) may not represent current forest conditions.
comments.request: Justify use of older maps and discuss effects on outcomes.
comments.quote: I was wondering if there is not a more recent source available at a comparable resolution, and what effect this could have on your outcomes.

comments.issue: Recent European field studies find the opposite pattern of higher edge biomass.
comments.request: Discuss this discrepancy in the main text.
comments.quote: Recent field-based measurements in 9-m radius plots from across Europe, for instance, find an opposite pattern (higher biomass in the edges).

comments.issue: Fine-scale drivers such as soil and microclimate are omitted without discussion.
comments.request: Discuss these drivers and their potential influence.
comments.quote: fine-scale drivers such as soil parameters or forest microclimate were not included here

comments.issue: Recently published papers on edge-to-interior edaphic gradients are not cited.
comments.request: Cite these papers in the introduction.
comments.quote: There are also edge-to-interior grandients in edaphic conditions We have actually very recently published some articles around these topics

comments.issue: Additional literature could strengthen a specific point in the introduction.
comments.request: Consider these references here as well.
comments.quote: The additional literature that I have provided above, could actually also be very relevant here.

comments.issue: Hansen forest map dates from 2000; more recent sources may exist.
comments.request: Check for more recent sources and justify the choice.
comments.quote: I was just wondering if there is not a more recent source available as this map already dates from 2000?

comments.issue: Subfigure g is unclear, including whether agriculture is included.
comments.request: Clarify what subfigure g shows.
comments.quote: I'm not sure that I understand this subfigure g completely. Is agriculture also included? Could you clarify?

comments.issue: One sentence is overly complex with too many commas.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence.
comments.quote: I found this sentence rather complex with too many commas. Could you rephrase?

comments.issue: Results sections contain extensive discussion that duplicates the discussion section.
comments.request: Reduce discussion in the results.
comments.quote: There is already a lot of discussion in this part, intermixed with results.

comments.issue: Biome-level distinctions are repeated from earlier sections.
comments.request: Remove or condense the repetition.
comments.quote: I have the feeling these biome level distinctions were already discussed in the parts above.

comments.issue: Figure legend shows Tg in (a) but Pg in (b).
comments.request: Clarify the legend labels.
comments.quote: The figure legend in (a) seems to show Tg, but in (b) Pg is mentioned. Could you clarify?

comments.issue: The 58 Pg estimate is reported without uncertainty.
comments.request: Add uncertainty, e.g. SD.
comments.quote: 58 Pg, could you add uncertainty (eg SD)?

comments.issue: Opposite findings of Meeussen et al. at plot scale are not reconciled.
comments.request: Elaborate on why the patterns are opposite.
comments.quote: So, I was wondering how the fiend-based data replicated at continental scale and global data still give opposite patterns. Could you elaborate?

comments.issue: Wording at L249-250 is too strong.
comments.request: Use less strong wording such as 'is in line with'.
comments.quote: Please change to a less strong wording, e.g. is in line with or corroborates

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the map is the most recent available product.
comments.request: State that it is the best available and discuss newer maps.
comments.quote: Is this the most recent source available? If yes, I would highlight that in the text and write that it is the best available product at this moment and at this fine resolution.

comments.issue: Potential effects of small-scale drivers are not discussed.
comments.request: Add a few lines discussing soil and microclimate effects.
comments.quote: I was also wondering what the effect of small-scale driver would be, such as some soil parameters or even forest microclimate.

comments.issue: Biomass loss is not converted to carbon stocks.
comments.request: Convert the amount to carbon stocks for global C balance.
comments.quote: Maybe you could also convert this amount to carbon stocks in order to quantify the actual impact on the global C balance?

comments.issue: 19 line-level copy edits
comments.quote: “To do this”. I suggest to change this to: To this end

reviews.assessment: Important and rigorous global analysis; asks for deeper explanation of short edge-effect distances, cross-study differences, and the temperature mechanism.
strengths: important at biome and global scales

comments.issue: Short edge-effect distances conflict with cited tropical studies showing deeper effects.
comments.request: Explain the short distances and cite Broadbent et al. 2008.
comments.quote: What explains the “short” distance of edge effects? Working with data from tropical forests, Chaplin-Kramer, at al. (2019) that you cited shows edge effects that extend much deeper into the forest.

comments.issue: Consistent negative effects across biomes contrast with studies reporting different responses.
comments.request: Explain whether magnitude has been confused with direction.
comments.quote: What explains the difference between these results of consistent negative edge effects across biomes, and other studies have found a different response?

comments.issue: Temperature effect mechanism is unclear; environmental and edge-caused warming are confounded.
comments.request: Disentangle environmental from edge-caused temperature effects.
comments.quote: What is the mechanism of temperature effect on reduced aboveground biomass? I ask because there are two possible temperature effects that may be interacting.

title: A globally consistent negative effect of edge on aboveground forest biomass

study.system: migratory shorebirds; East Asian-Australasian flyway mortality surveys

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers raised concerns that must be addressed before publication; a revised manuscript with highlighted changes in Microsoft Word format is required.

reviews.assessment: Congratulates the authors on a timely, necessary and reproducible study with conclusions well linked to findings; recommends publication with minor revisions.

comments.issue: The term 'commoner species' at line 47 is undefined.
comments.request: Define what a commoner species means.
comments.quote: Line 47: how would you define what is a ‘commoner species’

comments.issue: Pollution as another hypothesis for the declines is not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention pollution among alternative hypotheses.
comments.quote: Line 59-60: other hypotheses to explain the declines that are being investigated is pollution of various forms and types.

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits requested (lines 60, 171, 250).
comments.quote: Line 171: perhaps add ‘per annum’ somewhere to make clear.

comments.issue: The effect of large congregations on trappability and population loss is not noted.
comments.request: Add this point about migratory congregations.
comments.quote: Also that migratory species congregate in large numbers, which means that attempts to trap them can eliminate a significant percentage of their populations.

comments.issue: Mortality estimates miss the unsurveyed migration window, and the size of this underestimate is unknown.
comments.request: Assess how much the unsurveyed window underestimates mortality.
comments.quote: Line 223: I would be keen to see to what extent we are underestimating mortalities by the migration window that was not surveyed.

comments.issue: Possible mitigation measures, such as larger or different mesh sizes, are not discussed.

comments.issue: Compensation payments are not explored as a policy option.
comments.request: Explore compensation payments.
comments.quote: Line 266: Perhaps that or other types of compensation payments can be explored.

comments.issue: The net-mapping approach could be applied in Vietnam, Thailand and Cambodia, which face similar threats.
comments.request: Highlight the approach's transferability to other countries.
comments.quote: Line 275: The authors’ approach to quantify the distribution and extent of nets can be used in countries like Vietnam, Thailand and Cambodia where the threats (from all three uses of nets) are fairly similar to that in China.

comments.issue: The discussion should revisit regulating net use, alternatives and livelihood issues as a human-wildlife conflict.
comments.request: Revisit this point in the discussion.
comments.quote: Actions are also (as you have pointed out earlier), needed to address and regulate the use of nets, find alternatives to existing net use, and address livelihood issues

comments.issue: It is unknown how often hunters removed birds before surveys started, biasing mortality estimates.
comments.request: Report how often carcasses were removed before surveys.
comments.quote: Line 353: How often did this happen where hunters removed the birds before you started the survey?

comments.issue: The other taxa affected at line 429 are not identified.
comments.request: Name the other taxa.
comments.quote: Line 429: What were the other taxa?

comments.issue: Whether the nets differ substantively in mesh size is unknown.
comments.request: Report structural differences between nets.
comments.quote: Line 437: I am keen to know if there are substantive structural differences between the nets in terms of mesh sizes.

reviews.assessment: Praises a well-executed, much-needed study but says the introduction's decline narrative is not fully supported and notes missed opportunities.
strengths: extends prior work in robustness, scope and scale
solid analyses of enormous field data
important new information on deterrence nets

comments.issue: The claim that Yellow Sea habitat destruction has slowed is unsupported by cited data.
comments.request: Provide support or soften this argument.
comments.quote: This sentence is implicitly arguing that habitat destruction in the Yellow Sea has slowed or stopped, but no supporting data for this idea are cited.

comments.issue: The blanket claim that shorebird populations continue to decline overstates the nuanced evidence.

comments.issue: Nets likely operate year-round, so summer and winter impacts may be missed.

comments.issue: The deterrence-net paragraph misses the chance to stress their mortality contribution, legal status and alternatives.
comments.request: Expand this discussion of deterrence nets.
comments.quote: This paragraph seems like a missed opportunity to emphasize the huge contribution of deterrence nets to overall mortality estimates.

comments.issue: How deterrence-net impacts might scale up along the coast given widespread aquaculture is not discussed.

comments.issue: Mortality from renewable energy infrastructure is not considered in the estimates.

comments.issue: Hunters may have changed net use after learning of the project, making hunting numbers conservative.

comments.issue: The claim at line 41 overlooks existing on-farm agroecological studies such as Rasmussen et al. 2024.

comments.issue: The grey colour in Figure 3A is undefined.

comments.issue: Prior work on coupling agroecology with habitat protection is not cited.

comments.issue: Site exclusion criteria and the unclear sentence at lines 504-508 leave the site selection unexplained.
comments.request: Describe the exclusion criteria clearly.
comments.quote: I think that you mean that after groundtruthing 28 potential ZBNF sites you excluded 15, leaving 13. However, the exclusion criteria at this point in site selection are not described and the sentence itself was not clear.

comments.issue: Subsistence farms are mentioned in the main text but not in the methods.
comments.request: Clarify subsistence farms in the main text methods.
comments.quote: main text mentions subsistence farmers as being different from agrichemical farms but but in methods no mention of subsistence farms are made, please clarify here (and not in the supplement alone)

comments.issue: What counts as a harvest and how different crops are combined in yield analyses is unclear.
comments.request: Define the harvest unit and explain how crops were combined.
comments.quote: Clarify whether a harvest refers to everything harvested from a plot of land over time, or whether each harvest (of successive crops) is considered and included separately, and if so how.

comments.issue: Matching and post-matching analyses are mixed together at line 591.
comments.request: Describe the matching procedure first, then the analyses.
comments.quote: this line is not clear to me. We matched and conducted post matched analysis. I think first you should just describe the matching procedure, and then later, describe the analyses.

comments.issue: The sequence of matching is unclear, including whether response variables were matched on.
comments.request: Add a flow diagram and clarify the matching procedure.
comments.quote: The sequence of matching is not really clear. I think that including a flow diagram would help.

comments.issue: The distance and genetic distance methods are not explained.
comments.request: Add brief explanations of these methods.
comments.quote: Brief explanations of the distance and genetic distance methods would be helpful

comments.issue: The 5 km landscape with 75% ZBNF is only described in the supplement.
comments.request: Move this key point into the main methods.
comments.quote: the important point about the 5 km surrounding landscape also having 75% ZBNF (for ZBNF farms) should be moved into main document methods

comments.issue: Supplement lines 380-384 contain information needed to follow the procedure.
comments.request: Move the relevant information to the main text.
comments.quote: Some of this information would have helped me to better understand the procedure used

comments.issue: Crop composition per sample type is not tabulated.
comments.request: Add a table of crops and their prevalence.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to have a list of crops and their prevalence in each sample type as a table

comments.issue: Figure S2 and S3 legends do not say which analysis they belong to.
comments.request: Specify the analysis (yield or profit) in each legend.
comments.quote: Figure S2 and Figure S3 legends should distinguish to which analysis they respectively apply (e.g. Yield, Profit).

reviews.assessment: Impressive and important study, but causal attribution, model complexity, seasonality, matching and outlier handling need major clarification.
strengths: rare link of farming practices to socio-economic and biodiversity outcomes

comments.issue: Results and discussion emphasize statistical results over biological interpretation.
comments.request: Add species- and trait-level examples and analyses, e.g. using AVONET traits.
comments.quote: Throughout the Results/Discussion, the language is overly focused on statistical results rather than the biological interpretation of these results.

comments.issue: Farm habitat structure (tree cover, hedgerows, ponds) is neither measured nor discussed.
comments.request: Measure or discuss habitat structure features on farms.
comments.quote: The authors never measure or discuss these habitat features, omitting an important aspect of farmland ecology.

comments.issue: A two-year snapshot without pre-ZBNF baseline cannot support causal or trend-stability claims.
comments.request: Acknowledge interannual confounding and temper causality.
comments.quote: A two-year snapshot, with no baseline (“pre-ZBNF”) data, makes it difficult to assert causality or trend stability.

comments.issue: Forest sites are treated as one type; quality, successional stage and disturbance history are not described or matched.
comments.request: Detail forest condition and address potential site-level confounders.
comments.quote: However, “forest” is treated monolithically. Forest quality, successional stage, and disturbance history are not detailed.

comments.issue: Handling of aural versus visual detections and distance confirmation for fast species is not described.
comments.request: Describe detection and distance protocols fully.
comments.quote: The paper does not fully describe how they handled aural vs. visual detections in distance estimates, or how they confirmed distances for fleeting or fast-moving species.

comments.issue: Grouping rare species for shared detection functions may bias densities if detectability differs.
comments.request: Check and adjust detection functions for habitat and flightiness.
comments.quote: If grouped species differ significantly in flightiness, detectability, or typical habitat strata, this approach can bias densities upward or downward for particular species.

comments.issue: Density models lack cross-validation and goodness-of-fit diagnostics beyond AIC.
comments.request: Add cross-validation and goodness-of-fit checks.
comments.quote: The paper does not mention cross-validation or goodness-of-fit diagnostics (beyond AIC). The authors should include these in the updated manuscript.

comments.issue: The many models are hard to follow, and how seasonal data enter them is unclear.
comments.request: Add a table or schematic of models and state how season is modelled.
comments.quote: It can be overwhelming and difficult to follow which question each model is answering.

comments.issue: Outlier removal thresholds and rationale are unspecified and could bias results.
comments.request: Report cutoffs, outlier distributions and analyses with and without outliers.
comments.quote: The authors do not specify what threshold or biological rationale guided these exclusions.

comments.issue: Little detail is given on how forest squares were chosen, though forest type affects bird communities.
comments.request: Describe forest site selection and control for forest type.
comments.quote: The authors provide little detail on how forest squares were chosen, yet the type/quality of forest strongly affects bird communities.

comments.issue: Guild grouping may mask species-level variation in detectability and habitat use.
comments.request: Consider multi-trait analyses and show which species were grouped and why.
comments.quote: I suspect important species-level variation is being lost by this grouping.

comments.issue: Season is not included as a random effect or interaction, so seasonal differences may be conflated with treatment.
comments.request: Model seasonality explicitly and report winter-summer shifts by system.
comments.quote: Without a seasonal random effect or a seasonal interaction with farming system, one might conflate differences that are purely seasonal with “treatment” effects.

comments.issue: A single ZIP zero-inflation process is assumed although ZBNF and agrichemical sites may differ in detectability.
comments.request: Allow or test for differing zero-inflation processes between systems.
comments.quote: If agrichemical vs. ZBNF squares differ systematically in vegetation or detectability, the zero-inflation component might conflate real biological absence with reduced detectability in certain habitats.

comments.issue: Species-specific random slopes are noisy and shrunken with many species and few replicates.
comments.request: Assess the reliability of species-level slope estimates.
comments.quote: the random-slope estimates can be noisy or heavily shrunken toward the overall mean, reducing confidence in species-level inference

comments.issue: Farmland structure is not a matching covariate, so ZBNF bird differences may be confounded by local habitat.
comments.request: Include habitat structure in matching or as covariates.
comments.quote: If these features differ systematically between ZBNF and conventional sites but were not used as matching covariates, the results attributing bird differences to “ZBNF” might be confounded by local habitat variations.

comments.issue: Forest points are not matched, so farmland-forest comparisons are purely observational.
comments.request: Acknowledge or address unmatched forest comparisons.
comments.quote: The forest points are not matched at all, only farmland squares are. So comparisons of farmland vs. forest bird communities are purely observational and could be influenced by local geography or other unmeasured factors.

comments.issue: Pesticides, insects and vegetation were not measured, so mechanisms for bird increases remain correlational.
comments.request: Temper mechanistic claims or add supporting measurements.
comments.quote: the authors did not measure pesticides, insect abundances, or vegetation composition. Therefore, the ZIP results remain correlational.

comments.issue: Figure 2a-b shading duplicates the credible interval information.
comments.request: Recolour by guild or habitat affinity instead.
comments.quote: the shading to show “strength” of trend duplicates information already reflected in the 95% BCIs. This visually overcomplicates the results without adding new information.

comments.issue: Claiming no negative yield effect in ZBNF ignores negative but non-significant slopes.
comments.request: Rephrase to say trade-offs are weaker but not absent.
comments.quote: the average trend lines (for all but one guild) are negative, just not statistically significant

comments.issue: Synergy claims rest on short-term data from a single taxon.
comments.request: Temper synergy claims and acknowledge limited biodiversity coverage.
comments.quote: Claims about “synergies” or “neutralizing trade-offs” with yield should be tempered by acknowledging that short-term partial data on a single taxonomic group (birds) may not reflect broader biodiversity or future yield stability.

comments.issue: “Uncertain” is not standard terminology for credible intervals overlapping zero.
comments.request: Use clearer wording such as “no detectable difference”.
comments.quote: However, “uncertain” is not standard terminology in ecology or statistics.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and worth publishing after revision, but the tone over-interprets results and key sampling and programme details are missing from the main text.
strengths: explores high-yield farming with limited biodiversity impacts

comments.issue: The tone over-interprets results, presenting win-win outcomes when relationships remain mainly negative.
comments.request: Temper the tone and describe outcomes as win-less-loss rather than win-win.
comments.quote: With regard to the tone used, authors tend to over-interpret their results sometimes verging on propaganda.

comments.issue: The sampling setup and ZBNF programme are described only in the supplement.
comments.request: Add a short complete sampling description early in the paper, possibly before the results.
comments.quote: A short but complete description of the sampling setup should appear from the outset of the paper to help readers understand the result section.

comments.issue: The measures supported by ZBNF and how farms differ from agrichemical ones are not specific.
comments.request: Describe the programme practices, including mulching and reduced tillage, in the main text.
comments.quote: authors should be more specific about the measures supported through the programme and how supported farms distinguish from ‘agrichemical’ ones

comments.issue: Pesticides are presented as the only driver of agricultural biodiversity loss, ignoring mechanization and landscape homogenization.
comments.request: Acknowledge other major drivers of biodiversity loss.
comments.quote: authors tend to present pesticides as the only driver of biodiversity loss in agriculture, ignoring other major drivers: mechanization, landscape homogenization, to only cite a few

comments.issue: Birds may not represent 500 m2 soil-focused practices; a soil-dependent taxon could be more appropriate.
comments.request: Justify the choice of birds as bio-indicators.
comments.quote: I question the choice of birds as bio-indicators as they are able to travel long distances, I wonder how they could be representative of 500m2 authors are comparing.

comments.issue: Including forests in the comparison adds little intellectual value.
comments.request: Justify or reconsider the forest comparison.
comments.quote: Additionally, I question the relevance to include forests in the comparison.

comments.issue: The claim of the world's largest agroecological programme lacks definition and references.
comments.request: Specify the metric and provide references.
comments.quote: how sure can you be that this is the largest agroecological programme worldwide? Is it ‘largest’ in terms of area covered?

comments.issue: The statement at line 41 needs nuancing.
comments.request: Use “a large share” and acknowledge systemic-approach research.
comments.quote: please nuance. ‘a large share’ would be more appropriate, but you could also acknowledge that a growing body of research is endorsing systemic approaches.

comments.issue: What “incentivised” means is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the incentives provided to farmers.
comments.quote: L54: what is meant by ‘incentivised’? To they give money? Training?

comments.issue: Birds are introduced too late as a study group.
comments.request: Introduce birds and their interest earlier.
comments.quote: L58: birds should be introduced earlier as why they would be an interesting group to study.

comments.issue: “Careful site selection” is not defined.
comments.request: State the site selection criteria.
comments.quote: L70: what is ‘careful site selection’? What are your selection criteria?

comments.issue: The share of ZBNF versus agrichemical fields and farm ownership are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify field numbers by system, ownership and crops.
comments.quote: please clarify the share of ZBNF and agrichemichal within your ‘206 harvests and 128 fields’. Please also clarify whether all those fields beyond to different farms.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 87-89 is unclear and the line 90 detail adds little.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence and reconsider the 2.6% detail.
comments.quote: L87-89: this sentence should be clarified. L90: the added value of mentioning where the 2.6% highest yield belonged to is questionable

comments.issue: “Perverse subsidies” is used without definition.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant by perverse subsidies.
comments.quote: ‘pervese subsidies’ are mentioned several times throughout the paper, please clarify what is meant by this.

comments.issue: Specifying “for marginalized smallholders in the tropics” is unnecessary for these general pillars.
comments.request: Remove or justify the smallholder qualifier.
comments.quote: these are central pillars of sustainable food production systems in general, in my sense, there is no need to specify ‘for marginalized smallholders in the tropics’

comments.issue: “Across heterogeneous conditions” is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning.
comments.quote: it is unclear what is meant ‘across heterogenous conditions’

comments.issue: Whether the same crop types are grown in ZBNF and agrichemical systems is unclear.
comments.request: Report crop types and intercropping by system.
comments.quote: same number of crops, what about crop types? Do they grow the same crop species between ZBNF and agrichemicals?

comments.issue: “Yield stabilizing effect” is undefined.
comments.request: Define what a yield stabilizing effect means.
comments.quote: 114: what is a ‘yield stabilizing effect’? L117: for this section about birds, since these can fly long distances in a short time frame, it should be clarified how ZBNF parcels are arranged in space

comments.issue: The spatial arrangement of ZBNF parcels is not described.
comments.request: Clarify whether ZBNF parcels are clustered or scattered.
comments.quote: it should be clarified how ZBNF parcels are arranged in space. Are they gathered together, offering a fairly large (how large?) plot of parcels under ZBNF or are ZBNF parcels scattered across the landscape within an agrichemical matrix?

comments.issue: Whether the 104 counts are temporal or geographical and include the 4x replication is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling counts.
comments.quote: temporal or geographical repeats ? Do the 104 count include this 4x replication?

comments.issue: Whether forests are included and how a point covers hectares is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify forest inclusion and the point-to-area conversion.
comments.quote: L119: what about forests ecosystems? L119: how does a “point” covers hectares?

comments.issue: “Functional traits governing their persistence” is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: unclear what is meant by ‘functional traits governing their persistence in agricultural landscapes’

comments.issue: Habitat preference is treated only in the supplement.
comments.request: Treat habitat preference in the main manuscript or drop it.
comments.quote: at this stage, ‘habitat preference’ is only treated in supplementary material, it should be treated in main manuscript as well (or drop it completely)

comments.issue: Farming-system and landscape-level scales are conflated.
comments.request: Clarify the two scales.
comments.quote: you mention both the level of the farming system and the landscape level, which are two different scales, please clarify

comments.issue: “An uncertain response” is unclear.
comments.request: Use a clearer term such as unsystematic.
comments.quote: L170: what is ‘ an uncertain response’? Unsystematic maybe?

comments.issue: Whether landscape-level estimates differ from harvest/field-level estimates is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between the estimate types.
comments.quote: you mention ‘landscape-level’ yield and economic profit assessment, while in L75 you mention harvest level yield and field-level economic profit assessment, are these different estimates or are landscape-level estimates extrapolations of the harvest/field ones?

comments.issue: Vertivore results are oddly opposite to all other guilds.
comments.request: Re-check the vertivore data and provide hypotheses for the contrast.
comments.quote: I would double check results for vertivores which is oddly opposite to all other guilds.

comments.issue: “Responded” implies causality.
comments.request: Use non-causal wording.
comments.quote: ‘responded’ sounds like it was a causal relationship, while itsn’t necessarily.

comments.issue: “Synergies” is inappropriate since birds remain negatively affected.
comments.request: Avoid the term synergies.
comments.quote: I would not use the term “synergies” since birds seem to remain negatively affected

comments.issue: “Community integrity” is undefined and “shifts” may be better as “declines”.
comments.request: Define community integrity and revise the wording.
comments.quote: L210: what is community integrity? L216: replace ‘shifts’ with ‘declines’?

comments.issue: Bar charts should be boxplots and colour codes specified.
comments.request: Replace bar charts with boxplots and specify colours.
comments.quote: L388: replace bar-chart by boxplot L408: specify color code

comments.issue: Species names are not shown directly in the figure.
comments.request: Add species names to the figure.
comments.quote: L409: wouldn’t it be useful to have sp names directly in the figure?

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits (redundant numerals at L202, missing “significantly” at L418, wording at L576).
comments.quote: L202: you have ‘25’ and ‘twenty five’ standing together

comments.issue: The methods section could be shortened for clarity.
comments.request: Condense the methods.
comments.quote: it feels like some parts could be shorten for the sake of clarity. Sometimes, ‘less is more’; too much information can blur the message.

comments.issue: The ZBNF village scale is only introduced late.
comments.request: State the village-scale criterion earlier in the paper.
comments.quote: authors should refer to this scale of analysis: ‘ZBNF villages with at least 80% farmers involved in the programme’ earlier in the paper, otherwise the readers thinks you compared isolated ZBNF parcels in a agrichemical landscape

comments.issue: “Semi randomised” and the range used for natural vegetation cover are unclear.
comments.request: Explain the semi-random design and the vegetation cover range.
comments.quote: L505: what is meant by ‘semi randomised’ L506: on which range is calculated this natural vegetation cover? The 500m2 plots?

comments.issue: Only 128 of about 4524 fields were sampled; representativeness is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain how the 128 sampled fields represent the others.
comments.quote: in L511 you mention that each square on average contains 174 fields, which leads to 26(squares)x174= 4524 fields in total approximately. How do you explain you only gathered information on 128 fields?

comments.issue: Fields within squares are pseudoreplicates rather than true replicates.
comments.request: Treat or model the nested structure appropriately.
comments.quote: L550: these are pseudoreplicates, not replications L553: contribution of authors to the different tasks should probably not be mentioned as part of the main text body

comments.issue: Author contributions are described in the main text.
comments.request: Move contributions to the authors' contribution section.
comments.quote: L553: contribution of authors to the different tasks should probably not be mentioned as part of the main text body, but can be kept to the ‘authors’ contribution’ section.

comments.issue: “Agroecological suitability” is undefined.
comments.request: Define agroecological suitability.
comments.quote: L601: what is ‘agroecological suitability’? L610-615: how do you justify you remove outliers?

comments.issue: Outlier removal is not justified; outliers should only be removed for demonstrable errors.
comments.request: Justify or avoid removing outliers.
comments.quote: Outliers are data, which should be treated as all other data, they can only be removed if you can be sure there are the results of sampling / measurement mistake

comments.issue: The fourth wheel description in the supplement is confusing and possibly reversed.
comments.request: Clarify the aeration-tillage relationship.
comments.quote: the fourth wheel ‘(4) ‘whapahasa’ – improving soil structure and reducing tillage through soil aeration’ isn’t clear. Isn’t the other way around: your increase soil aeration by reducing soil tillage?

title: India’s agroecology programme, ‘Zero Budget Natural Farming’, delivers biodiversity and economic benefits without lowering yields

study.system: 110 fungal species; phylogenomic timetree with fossil and HGT calibrations

editor_summary: Needs responses to reviewers and editorial concerns, especially justification for the specific enzyme families used as maximum-age constraints and the taxon sampling strategy; highlight all changes in the revision.

reviews.assessment: Careful, comprehensive and well-presented work with minor requests to explain screening, compare substitution models and expand the Neoproterozoic gap discussion.

comments.issue: 'Optimal metrics screening' for marker selection is not explained.
comments.request: Explain what optimal metrics screening is.
comments.quote: The authors should clearly explain what 'optimal metrics screening' is.

comments.issue: The C60 model's relative BIC and topology compared with other IQ-Tree models is not shown.
comments.request: Compare C60 with best-fitting non-site-specific models in BIC and topology.
comments.quote: How does this model compare to other models available in IQ-Tree, in terms of relative BIC?

comments.issue: 'Congruent with the bibliography' at line 120 is vague.
comments.request: Clarify what 'congruent with the bibliography' means.
comments.quote: what is meant by "congruent with the bibliography"?

comments.issue: The finding that slow/fast site selection barely affects age distributions belongs in the results.
comments.request: Mention this site-selection finding in the results.
comments.quote: This is an important finding and should be mentioned in the results

comments.issue: The Neoproterozoic gap between early associations and land plants is not explored against planetary history.
comments.request: Expand on the gap and possible connections such as Snowball Earth.
comments.quote: This is a striking observation, and should be expounded upon. How do these recovered ages map to planetary history in general?

reviews.assessment: Finds the study clear, robust and innovative, needing only clarification of pectin-based constraints and a few text and figure fixes.

comments.issue: Pectins may occur in more distant streptophyte and chlorophyte algae, affecting calibration scenarios A, A+calib and B+C.
comments.request: Clarify the biological basis of the pectin-based maximum age constraints.
comments.quote: a quick literature search suggests that pectins might also be present in other streptophyte and chlorophyte algae that are more distant than the LCA of Klebormidium and embryophytes

comments.issue: The effect of alignment site number on branch-length estimation and the variance are not reported.
comments.request: Report how site number affects branch-length variance and precision.
comments.quote: How were differences investigated when testing the effect of the number of alignment sites on branch length estimation? What happens to the variance?

comments.issue: 'Stem Fungi' is inappropriate because all sampled species are extant.
comments.request: Replace the term 'stem Fungi'.
comments.quote: The term ‘stem Fungi’ is inappropriate since these are all extant species.

comments.issue: The sentence conflates the LCA ages of Ascomycota and Basidiomycota with the ages of their crown groups.
comments.request: Check and correct the divergence ages sentence at lines 389-390.
comments.quote: The divergence of Ascomycota and Basidiomycota refers to the age of the LCA, whereas here the LCAs of their respective crown groups are provided.

comments.issue: 'Pre-embryophyte lineages' at line 454 is undefined.
comments.request: Define what pre-embryophyte lineages means.
comments.quote: Line 454. What do you exactly mean by pre-embryophyte lineages?

comments.issue: Many streptophyte algae live exclusively on land, so the terrestrial-adaptation claim needs nuance.
comments.request: Acknowledge fully terrestrial streptophyte algae such as Keblsormidiophyceae and Chlorokybophyceae.
comments.quote: Many streptophyte algae live exclusively on land (soils, rocks, crusts, etc.) such as members of Keblsormidiophyceae or Chlorokybophyceae

comments.issue: Clade names such as Holozoa and Holomycota are not annotated on the trees.
comments.request: Annotate all discussed clade names on the trees.
comments.quote: It would be good to annotate all the clade names discussed in the paper (Holozoa, Holomycota) onto the trees.

comments.issue: The standalone Figure 2 at the end of the manuscript appears corrupted.
comments.request: Fix the corrupted Figure 2.
comments.quote: The Fig. 2 at the end of the manuscript (not that embedded into the text) seems to have been somehow corrupted.

reviews.assessment: Sees an ingenious methodological advance but doubts the study fits the journal and argues the huge uncertainty and fossil evidence do not support the older crown-Fungi age.
strengths: ingenious way to improve divergence time estimation

comments.issue: The manuscript focuses on technicalities with little evolutionary or ecological result, so other journals may fit better.
comments.request: Add evolutionary or ecological results or consider a more suitable journal.
comments.quote: other journals such as Systematic Biology, or Molecular Biology and Evolution, seem to be a better fit for this study

comments.issue: Taxon sampling is low with no justification, despite many available fungal genomes outside Dikarya.
comments.request: Justify taxon selection, include more taxa, and state sampling in the methods.
comments.quote: I could not find any justification for the selection of these specific taxa. Also, the analytical methods they used does not prevent them to include more taxa.

comments.issue: Low taxon sampling with a concatenated dataset makes long-branch attraction more likely.
comments.request: Generate gene trees with CAT and build a species tree to avoid long-branch attraction.
comments.quote: Low taxon sampling can also lead to phylogenetic analyses that are more prone to long-branch attraction, especially when using a concatenated dataset.

comments.issue: The description of the failed alternative approach takes space better spent on the CAT model.
comments.request: Move the alternative approach to supplementary materials and use CAT in the main text.
comments.quote: It would be better to move to supplementary materials the description of the alternative approach that was used, but failed, when compare to the use of the well-established CAT model

comments.issue: Concatenated phylogenomic analyses can yield strongly supported but erroneous nodes in regions with short internodes.
comments.request: Use species-tree methods that analyse each gene separately, such as ASTRAL.
comments.quote: It seems that the phylogenomic tree generated by this study was using a concatenated dataset, which raises doubts about the quality and accuracy of the resulting topology.

comments.issue: HGT-based calibration placement depends on taxon sampling density, and the 17 constraints are sensitive to sampling.
comments.request: Use dense taxon sampling to support the HGT-based constraints.
comments.quote: I am concerned about using HGT to justify calibration points because the placement of these calibration points on the topology is likely to be dependent on the density of the taxon sampling.

comments.issue: Node age uncertainties of 400-800 Myr contradict the claim that HGT constraints reduce uncertainty and undermine the main conclusions.
comments.request: Reconcile the huge uncertainty with the claims about reduced uncertainty and older ages.
comments.quote: This level of uncertainty does not support their main conclusions that the crown age of Fungi is older than recently reported

comments.issue: The large uncertainty for Metazoa and Embryophyta casts further doubt on the fungal age estimates.
comments.request: Address why fungal estimates should be trusted given large Metazoa and Embryophyta uncertainty.
comments.quote: Yet, the uncertainty around divergence time estimates for Metazoa and Embryophyta shown on figure 2 are relatively large.

comments.issue: The new fossil records agree with previous age estimates and do not support the older ages reported.
comments.request: Reconsider whether the new fossils support older fungal ages.
comments.quote: the most reliable, new fossils of fungi, are in agreement with previous estimates of the origin and LCA of fungi, and don’t support the older age estimates reported by this study.

comments.issue: The embryophyte constraint may be a minimum rather than a maximum age, assuming fungi originated after embryophytes.
comments.request: Clarify the direction of the embryophyte age constraint and consider interactions with unicellular green algae.
comments.quote: Should this be a minimum age instead of a maximum age because embryophytes originated much earlier than the crown of that clade.

title: A timetree of Fungi dated with fossils and horizontal gene transfers

study.system: Drosophila melanogaster Ace resistance; lab assays and field mesocosms

editor_summary: Editor says the reviewers' concerns and some editorial concerns must be addressed in a revised manuscript with highlighted changes before a final decision.

reviews.assessment: Praise for a convincing, thorough study that may become a textbook example, with only minor wording and citation nit-picks.
strengths: clearly written and easy to follow

comments.issue: 'Erode such variants' is imprecise; it is variation, not variants, that is eroded.
comments.request: Correct the wording.
comments.quote: The point is that variation is eroded (not variants)

comments.issue: 'Protect these loci from selection' is off; the intended term is 'protected polymorphism'.
comments.request: Use the correct terminology.
comments.quote: Perhaps you're referring to "protected polymorphism" but the wording is off

comments.issue: 'Evidence remains elusive' implies no examples exist, although such examples are merely rare.
comments.request: Acknowledge existing examples early in the paper.
comments.quote: suggests that we have no examples. We do have them, they are just rare.

comments.issue: The 1963 citation is outdated given decades of subsequent work on the topic.
comments.request: Update the literature coverage.
comments.quote: 1963 was a long time ago and there has been much work on this topic since then, including over the last decade.

comments.issue: A more direct citation for the idea is missing.
comments.request: Cite Gillespie and Langley 1974 or Charlesworth and Charlesworth 2010.
comments.quote: A more direct citation to this idea is Gillespie and Langley (1974 Genetics 76:837-884) or pp. 81-82 of Charlesworth and Charlesworth (2010 Elements of Evolutionary Genetics)

comments.issue: Several good examples of maintained variation exist but are not made clear.
comments.request: Cite the Grieshop et al. review of clear examples.
comments.quote: I agree that clear examples are rare, but there are several good ones (the recent Grieshop et al review summarises them), which should be made clear.

comments.issue: The threshold for deciding that temporal fluctuations exceed the control SNP set is unspecified.
comments.request: State the threshold used.
comments.quote: I know p = 0.05 is arbitrary, but what is the threshold for determining whether temporal fluctuations are stronger than the control SNP set?

comments.issue: Claims about dominance reversal at L105 outrun the evidence presented at that point.
comments.request: Move or temper the dominance-reversal claim until the evidence is shown.
comments.quote: Can you make any statements about dominance (or dominance reversal, specifically) from the results you've presented so far? It's not obvious that you can up to this point in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not make clear that s and h describe resistance costs in pesticide-free environments.
comments.request: Clarify this in the figure caption.
comments.quote: please clarify in the figure that you're estimating s and h for resistance alleles in environments where pesticides are not present

reviews.assessment: Finds the evidence compelling and the approach comprehensive, but asks for pleiotropy emphasis, clearer spatial analysis, integrated fitness components and field-realism discussion.
strengths: compelling evidence for beneficial reversal of dominance
comprehensive combination of genomics, lab assays and mesocosms
direct measurement of selection and dominance under semi-natural conditions

comments.issue: The mechanistic basis of dominance reversal in pleiotropy is obscured, so readers may overgeneralize.
comments.request: Emphasize pleiotropy and the specific conditions enabling dominance reversal.
comments.quote: dominance reversals for resistance fundamentally depend on pleiotropy - a shift in the trait under selection (Muralidhar and Veller 2022)

comments.issue: Panels of Figure 1 differ in scale and the nested population-in-city-in-country structure is not addressed.
comments.request: Explain how country-level pesticide use predicts within-country population variation.
comments.quote: I noticed a scale mismatch between panels - Figure 1A shows one pie chart per country, while Figure 1B includes multiple data points per country

comments.issue: Fecundity and viability costs show different dominance, but no integrated fitness analysis is presented.
comments.request: Combine fitness components and discuss their relative importance in the field.
comments.quote: I'm curious about the differential dominance patterns observed between fitness components—specifically, why fecundity costs appear more recessive than viability costs for some resistance alleles.

comments.issue: The 7.5 ppm malathion dose is not compared with real field application rates or realistic exposure complexity.
comments.request: Discuss field application rates, patchiness and chemical rotations.
comments.quote: it would strengthen their argument to discuss how these experimental concentrations compare to typical field application rates

comments.issue: The 150-200% per-generation selection coefficients are unexplained and much smaller than lab values.
comments.request: Explain their calculation and reconcile field and lab estimates.
comments.quote: the authors claim selection coefficients (hs) "on the order of 150-200% per generation," but don't explain how these were calculated

comments.issue: Figure 3f is poorly labeled and does not show it depicts inferred resistance-cost parameters.
comments.request: Improve the labeling and description of Figure 3f.
comments.quote: Figure 3f needs better labeling and description, as it's not immediately clear from the figure alone that it shows the inferred model parameters for resistance costs.

comments.issue: Control SNPs also show a notable reversal pattern, which is not interpreted.
comments.request: Interpret the genome-wide reversal trend in controls.
comments.quote: there's a notable reversal pattern in the control SNPs as well. How do the authors interpret this genome-wide trend?

reviews.assessment: Adds valuable, thought-provoking empirical data, but asks the authors to clarify dominance concepts, dose relevance and the molecular basis.
strengths: valuable empirical data on resistance costs

comments.issue: Worldwide allele frequencies are discussed without keeping the diversity of selective chemicals in mind.
comments.request: Consider other selective chemicals when interpreting global frequencies.
comments.quote: It is fair to focus on this chemical, although it is probably worth keeping the diversity of selective chemicals in mind when considering the world wide frequency of alleles at this locus.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the study orchard uses malathion exclusively.
comments.request: Report the insecticide regime at Linvilla farms.
comments.quote: (do Linvilla farms use malathion exclusively?) supporting the contention that there is a cost to these variants

comments.issue: Dominance is defined graphically; transformation of the phenotypic y-axis might change dominance relationships.
comments.request: Show that phenotypes are appropriately scaled for all traits.
comments.quote: This representation raises the question of whether transformation (or not) of the y-axis (phenotypic value) might change the dominance relationships.

comments.issue: Dominance is summarized at LD50, but at higher doses heterozygotes die like susceptibles; LD50 may not be evolutionarily relevant.
comments.request: Assess whether LD90 or other doses change the dominance conclusion.
comments.quote: By using the LD50 the authors summarize a phenotype over multiple doses. But is the LD50 the most relevant dose evolutionarily speaking?

comments.issue: Wright's dominance and 'loss-of-function' are used without articulating the molecular basis of Ace-based dominance.
comments.request: Expound the molecular basis, including AChE dimers.
comments.quote: the molecular basis of Ace-based dominance is not articulated. We wonder whether it is worth expounding this further

comments.issue: Some mesocosm sample points in Figure 3a are not visible despite having great leverage.
comments.request: Make those data points clearer.
comments.quote: Some ‘sample points’ in the mesocosm cage experiments (Figure 3a) do not appear to be shown and yet they seem to have great leverage on the general pattern.

comments.issue: Error bars in Figure 2d and 2e are too small to see.
comments.request: Note the tiny error bars in the figure legend.
comments.quote: elsewhere (eg. Fig 2d and 2e) error bars are probably so small that they can not be seen- so if this is the case it should be noted in the figure legend.

comments.issue: The frequency and relevance of inversion 3R(K) in the LNP population and its linkage to Ace alleles are unknown.
comments.request: Report its frequency and whether it contributes to the sweep width analysis.
comments.quote: It is at such a low frequency in the DGRP it is barely worth mentioning; is it at higher frequency in the LNP population?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether R2 and R3 cost recessiveness differ significantly, which affects modelling costs as equal.
comments.request: Test the difference or justify modelling costs as the same.
comments.quote: Is the recessiveness of fitness costs of R2 significantly different to that of R3 as is implied in figure 2 h versus k and 2i versus l?

comments.issue: Other resistance loci, such as Cyp6g1, could be differentially sampled into the small recombinant populations.
comments.request: Check whether other resistance alleles differ across populations.
comments.quote: It seems possible that alleles at other resistance loci could be differentially sampled into the recombinant populations – particularly because of the small number of lines contributing to each population.

comments.issue: R1 alleles show no resistance and high costs, yet their persistence is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why R1 alleles are not lost and whether they are in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
comments.quote: It is extremely interesting that the R1 alleles do not show resistance in these experiments.

title: Beneficial reversal of dominance maintains a large-effect resistance polymorphism under fluctuating insecticide selection

study.system: passerine birds; whining calls, playback experiments and phylogenetics

editor_summary: Five reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns that must be addressed; the manuscript cannot be accepted but a revised version is welcome.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic with excellent figures and writing, but the evidence is haphazard, the whining call may be a general nest-risk signal, and conclusions need more caution.

comments.issue: Evidence is a haphazard amalgamation of small experiments in different regions designed to fend off critiques.
comments.request: Tighten and integrate the evidence into a coherent design.
comments.quote: The evidence brought together by the authors comes across as slightly haphazard, with a number of small experiments, conducted in widely different regions, designed to fend-off specific critiques.

comments.issue: Whining call is not limited to brood parasites; it is a general warning signal about risks to nest contents.
comments.request: Test and acknowledge the more general nest-risk function.
comments.quote: The whining call, in my experience, is not limited to the context of brood parasites. It seems to be used more generally as a warning signal in the context of risks to the nest contents

comments.issue: Snake presentation test has small samples and an immobile model may not elicit the same response.
comments.request: Use larger samples and more convincing predator presentations.
comments.quote: While this treatment did not seem to elicit whining notes, the sample sizes are not great and I am not sure that an immobile snake model elicits the same response as the more slithering variety.

comments.issue: If the call is a catch-all risk signal, the claimed symbolic association with brood parasitism weakens; learning may be universal rather than convergent.
comments.request: Consider the catch-all signal interpretation and revise the convergence claim.
comments.quote: It is necessary to consider whether we, as humans, may be superimposing the meaning of 'brood-parasite' onto the sound, whereas the organism is using the call as a catch-all signal to convey a variety of risks to nest contents.

comments.issue: Conclusions ascribe too much certainty; signal function needs testing across more hosts and predators.
comments.request: Add caution and acknowledge the need for broader testing.
comments.quote: I think the text needs some editing to add more caution to the conclusions, and to acknowledge that the function of the whining signal requires further testing in a broader array of host species

comments.issue: Non-host status is unreliable because hosts turn over and knowledge is biased; 'ghost of parasitism past' may retain responses.
comments.request: Discuss the pitfalls of assuming non-host status.
comments.quote: Some discussion of the potential pitfalls of inferring or assuming non-host status on the basis of current information is warranted.

comments.issue: Novelty of the finding and the speculative language-origin claim need verification by experts including linguists.
comments.request: Have the novelty claim checked and temper it.
comments.quote: Whether the finding is as novel as the authors state needs to be checked by experts in related fields, including linguistics.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive, well-designed and well-written study, but the central claim that whining calls are functionally referential and learned is not convincingly demonstrated.
strengths: important evolutionary question of broad interest
well-designed experiments with proper controls and excellent figures

comments.issue: Response difference to whining versus alarm calls is quantitative, not qualitative, so referentiality cannot be distinguished from urgency.
comments.request: Provide evidence of a qualitatively distinct response.
comments.quote: I don't think it is possible to distinguish between these possibilities with the data provided because the difference in response to whining calls and alarm calls was quantitative rather than qualitative.

comments.issue: Whining calls are occasionally produced to predator mounts, so they are not wholly specific to brood parasites.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited specificity of whining calls.
comments.quote: It is worth noting that whining calls were occasionally produced in response to the predator mounts too, which suggests that whining calls are not wholly specific to brood parasites.

comments.issue: No data show a qualitatively distinct response; breeding-season playbacks or prime-probe experiments would be needed.
comments.request: Run the suggested experiments (unique behaviour, season, prime-probe).
comments.quote: To convincingly show that the whining call is functionally referential to brood parasites, I think the authors would need to provide some data showing that birds respond in a qualitatively distinct manner to whining calls and alarm calls.

comments.issue: Cited studies only show learning that cuckoos are a threat; calls could be innately produced whenever birds are threatened.
comments.request: Separate learning of threat recognition from learning of call production.
comments.quote: If whining calls are a generic high-urgency call rather than referring specifically to cuckoos, then it is possible that fairy-wrens innately produce whining calls whenever they feel extremely threatened or upset

comments.issue: Absence of whining calls in species may reflect incomplete vocal repertoire data rather than true absence.
comments.request: Justify how non-production was determined.
comments.quote: how did you definitively determine that a species does NOT produce whining calls? Did you have comprehensive data on the vocal repertoires for all these species?

comments.issue: Line 243 does not make clear what the other species responded to.
comments.request: Clarify the playback stimulus involved.
comments.quote: You say that "more individuals from other species responded", but it is not clear from the way this sentence is worded what they responded to.

comments.issue: Species counts at lines 335-336 do not add up: 17 + 8 = 25, not 24.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy.
comments.quote: But 17 + 8 = 25, not 24. What explains this discrepancy?

comments.issue: Features used in the 85% accurate LDA are not specified.
comments.request: Clarify which features entered the LDA.
comments.quote: What features were included in this LDA (the one with 85% accuracy)? Was it the first 10 principal components? Please clarify this in the text.

comments.issue: Justification for 30 minutes between trials is missing.
comments.request: Justify the inter-trial interval.
comments.quote: How do you know that 30 minutes was enough time to wait in between trials? It doesn't seem like much time

comments.issue: Dryad data and code link did not work.
comments.request: Fix the data and code link.
comments.quote: When I tried to access the data and code through the link provided to Dryad, the link did not work.

reviews.assessment: Well-conducted and presented study with interesting results, but the referential-signaling argument is speculative and several statistical issues need attention.
strengths: combines network analysis with playback experiments

comments.issue: Network claim may be tautological because interactions are computed partly from vocal interactions.
comments.request: Clarify how the network is computed and validate independence.
comments.quote: But I thought that, by design, network interactions are computed, at least in part, based on vocal interactions, is this correct? If so, this entire claim feels a bit tautological.

comments.issue: Figure 2 title claims functional referentiality in multiple species but shows responses in only two.
comments.request: Show modesty in the claims and quantify panel K.
comments.quote: the title of figure 2 is "Whining vocalizations are functionally referential in multiple species", but in fact, all the figure shows is response to playbacks in two species

comments.issue: p values and chi2 are reported without group means throughout.
comments.request: Report means for each group consistently.
comments.quote: The authors have a bad habit of presenting p values and chi2 without presenting the means for each group.

comments.issue: Colormaps are unexplained and not linked to easily understood raw measures.
comments.request: Explain colormaps and relate them to raw values.
comments.quote: Furthermore, colormaps are often not explained and are not, in any direct manner related to raw measures that can be easily understood.

comments.issue: New acoustic measure lacks training/test separation, so its significance is not robust.
comments.request: Develop the measure on a training set and test it on independent data.
comments.quote: If this is a new measure, perhaps it would be better to develop it on a training set and testing it on a different experimental data set?

comments.issue: Exact procedure behind the LDA and emmeans analysis is not documented.
comments.request: Document the exact analytical procedure.
comments.quote: It is not enough to say you used a certain toolbox, you need to document the exact procedure here

comments.issue: Binarizing the acoustic data instead of using a PC3-based distance metric is questionable.
