title: Marine protected areas marginally offset anthropogenic declines in tropical reef fish contributions to nature and people

study.system: northern-hemisphere marine fish; long-term trawl survey biomass data

editor_summary: Reviewers raised a number of concerns that will need to be addressed before the paper can be offered publication in Nature Ecology & Evolution.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, novel and timely; the three-stressor approach is impressive and only very minor revisions are needed.
strengths: extensive high-resolution northern-hemisphere fish biomass database
novel disentangling of long-term warming, interannual variability and MHW responses
extremely well written, appropriately analysed and well contextualised
important contribution of interest to a broad readership

comments.issue: The claim that thermal position effects are rarely studied overlooks several recent studies on this topic.
comments.request: Revise the claim to acknowledge recent work on thermal position.
comments.quote: It could be argued that several recent studies have examined the importance of thermal position within a species range

comments.issue: The term 'unified study system' is not defined and is unclear to the reader.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant by a 'unified study system'.
comments.quote: Also I'm not what is meant by a 'unified study system' here?

comments.issue: Interannual temperature differences are not explained where they are first introduced.
comments.request: Explain the metric earlier or move its description up.
comments.quote: It wasn't clear to me what is meant by interannual temperature differences here, which is explained a little more in the following paragraph.

comments.issue: Subheading wording could better reflect that thermal position mediates MHW impacts.
comments.request: Change the subheading to 'Thermal position mediates impact of MHWs on fish biomass'.
comments.quote: I think the subheading would read better as: 'Thermal position mediates impact of MHWs on fish biomass'

comments.issue: Indirect effects and confounders such as productivity, food and predation are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether indirect effects are at play and how they differ among stressors.
comments.quote: It is not clear whether all biomass changes are to inferred to be a direct effect of temperature, or whether

comments.issue: Fishing pressure trends over the time series and their possible influence are not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss whether fishing pressure could explain declines.
comments.quote: Similarly, how has fishing pressure changed over the period of the time series?

reviews.assessment: Sees real novelty in disentangling three thermal stressors but has many concerns about methodological clarity, figure content, MHW detrending and non-running code.
strengths: novel disentangling of three thermal stressors
accounts for species responses across their ranges

comments.issue: Figure 3 uses mean seabed temperature rather than long-term temperature change, so long-term trend results are missing.
comments.request: Plot and report relationships with long-term temperature change rather than mean temperature.
comments.quote: Why plot and investigate relationships to mean seabed temperature rather than mean annual or decadal change in seabed temperature?

comments.issue: Fig. 4 shows species-specific results but does not generalise the pattern across all studied species.
comments.request: Provide results for all species in supporting material and extend Fig. 4 to slopes across species.
comments.quote: Fig. 4 presents concrete species-specific information but fail to generalise these results across all studied species.

comments.issue: Species-specific results are counterintuitively placed in the final figure as if they were the end point.
comments.request: Reorder so species-specific results precede the generic cross-taxa results.
comments.quote: I also find counterintuitive to present species-specific results as the final figure as this result is really the building block for the more generic results across all taxa.

comments.issue: The text does not give concrete examples of specific warm years.
comments.request: Provide concrete examples of specific warm years in the text.
comments.quote: can you btw provide some concrete examples in the text of specific warms years

comments.issue: Figures show only model fits; observed data distributions are needed to judge how models reflect the data.
comments.request: Show data distributions, for example heat maps, alongside model fits.
comments.quote: Presentation of data distribution across the cell*species combinations ("population samples" rather than "populations") seems mandatory for the reader to appreciate how the model reflects the patterns in the data.

comments.issue: Fig. 1 shows only metadata and temperature variables, not the biomass patterns being modelled.
comments.request: Add biomass long-term versus interannual changes to Fig. 1.
comments.quote: Fig. 1 only display metadata and temp-related variables (species richness and warming trends) so it does not capture the actual patterns that the paper attempts to model / explain.

comments.issue: The Max annual MHW frequency on Fig. 1 panel D is confusing and visually mixed with the dots.
comments.quote: I was confused with the Max annual MHW frequency on panel D (as it is somehow mixed up with the dots on the plot).

comments.issue: Fig. 2 shows only model outputs, not the actual biomass-change observations.
comments.request: Add observed biomass change, e.g. as a heat map of observation frequency.
comments.quote: Fig. 2 should display actual observations of biomass change (cf above comment). Possibly as an heat map showing frequency of observations.

comments.issue: Model residuals are not shown to confirm that a linear fit is appropriate for both relationships.
comments.request: Present model residuals supporting the linear specification.
comments.quote: need to present model residuals to confirm that linear fit is appropriate to model both relationships

comments.issue: Fig. 3 is unreadable: the x-axis appears to show seabed temperatures while the study concerns long-term change, and the purple points are unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify what is plotted and show observed data distributions via heat maps.
comments.quote: Fig. 3 is problematic. X-axis reads as seabed temperatures ranging from 0 to 25°c. My understanding is that these should correspond to long-term temperature change over the study period

comments.issue: Model evaluation, diagnostics and uncertainty around mean results are not presented or discussed.
comments.request: Present residuals, diagnostics and uncertainty in the methods and supporting material.
comments.quote: Model residuals and model diagnostics are not presented / described/ discussed in the Mat and Methods section.

comments.issue: Model results lack cross-validation.
comments.request: Cross-validate model results using independent folds.
comments.quote: You do have a large dataset so I would also appreciate some cross-validation of model results using independent folds.

comments.issue: Survey seasonality is unaddressed and survey random effects are not reported, potentially confounding biomass changes.
comments.request: Account for season when collating surveys and report survey random effects.
comments.quote: Surveys cover different seasons so how did you collate data across different surveys without explicitly accounting for season?

comments.issue: Detrending means MHW definitions differ through time, so equal thermal excesses are not flagged consistently.
comments.request: Justify the detrending approach and its effect on MHW identification.
comments.quote: the fact that you detrend the time series implies that the same thermal excess (beyond 95 temp percentile for more than 5 days) might flag a MHW at the start of the time series but not at the end

comments.issue: Results may depend on the detrending choice.
comments.request: Re-run the analyses without detrending to confirm robustness.
comments.quote: Can you re-run the analyses without this detrending and confirm that your results are robust to this choice?

comments.issue: 'Population' is used for single-species hexagon samples, which is misleading.
comments.request: Use 'population sample' or clarify the terminology.
comments.quote: I question whether one species within an hexagonal cell can be considered a population; or rather a population 'sample'.

comments.issue: Data filtering is inconsistent: fewer than three surveys per year versus four sampled hauls per year and hexagon.
comments.request: Make filtering consistent and remove year-hexagon units with fewer than four hauls.
comments.quote: you need to be consistent and filter out any year/hexagon with less than 4 hauls

comments.issue: Sensitivity of results to the 1.5 IQR outlier-filtering threshold is untested.
comments.request: Test sensitivity to the outlier threshold, including a higher threshold.
comments.quote: What's the sensitivity of your results to the 1.5 threshold the interquartile range chosen to filter out outliers?

comments.issue: The two temperature datasets used for thermal ranges and for time series are not clearly distinguished.
comments.request: Clearly explain the two temperature datasets and their separate uses.
comments.quote: Would be useful to further clarify the temp dataset for biogeographical definition of species thermal range Vs temp dataset for time series analysis.

comments.issue: The 'most parsimonious covariate' selection is unclear and the reviewer disagrees with it.
comments.request: Clarify and justify the covariate selection criterion.
comments.quote: You mention the selection of most "parsimonious" covariate (l. 322 and l. 328), which I disagree with. I am not even sure what a parsimonious variable here.

comments.issue: Code lacks printed model-comparison outputs even though AIC values drive model selection.
comments.request: Include printed AIC comparisons in the code.
comments.quote: so the 6th model does indeed yield the lowest AIC but you code should include a print of actual outputs showing this

comments.issue: The zero-inflated Gaussian model is unfamiliar and its formulation is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the full model formulation.
comments.quote: Can you specify actual model formulation for Zero-Inflated Gaussian model, which I have never heard of?

comments.issue: The description of weighted versus unweighted models and the AIC argument is incomprehensible.
comments.request: Explain the model weighting and the AIC-based compromise clearly.
comments.quote: not sure what this sentence means and how the AIC value suggests anything about compromise between over- or under-fitting of data???

comments.issue: Model assumption checks are not shown.
comments.request: Present model assumption checks in the supplementary material.
comments.quote: l. 353: model assumptions check. Can you present these in the supp mat?

comments.issue: Provided R code does not run: missing files, wrong extensions and missing setwd calls.
comments.request: Provide complete, runnable code and all inputs.
comments.quote: Several of the R codes provided do not run and I could not afford the time to debug them

comments.issue: It is unclear how a code stage helps with MHW variable selection.
comments.request: Explain the purpose of stage_R_1 for MHW variable selection.
comments.quote: effectively help with MHW variable selection

comments.issue: No knitted outputs are provided for reviewers to follow the analysis steps.
comments.request: Provide knitted HTML or PDF outputs for all .rmd files.
comments.quote: would be useful to get some 'knitted' outputs from all .rmd files (either as html or pdf) for a faster review of the different steps

reviews.assessment: Very positive; strong, transferable evidence with only minor presentational and explanatory suggestions.
strengths: strong empirical evidence for warm-edge MHW effects
quantification approach transferable to any system
useful management and intervention discussion for decision-makers
high-quality figures and comprehensive, accurately interpreted literature

comments.issue: Abstract wording implies 'up to' maxima, but the cold/warm-edge values are averages.
comments.request: Clarify that the values are averages, not maximum responses.
comments.quote: as you give the average long-term change (-0.4%) I think make clear these are also averages for the cold and warm edge

comments.issue: The three stressors are introduced without explaining why MHWs are distinct from interannual variability.
comments.request: Explain the three stressors at first mention and consider renaming them.
comments.quote: Could that explanation be add to the first mention of the three stressors?

comments.issue: Fig. 3 caption does not explain how the excluded estimates differ from the plotted estimates.
comments.request: Explain the difference between the excluded and the plotted estimates.
comments.quote: how are they different from the 707,692 population-level year over year estimates (shown in purple)?

comments.issue: The 95th percentile MHW threshold is justified only by its use in one previous study.
comments.request: Justify the choice of the 95th percentile threshold.
comments.quote: why was this needed to be done based on use by one previous study?

comments.issue: The claim that long-term change overwhelms short-term boosts ignores that large cold-edge boosts may sustain production.
comments.request: Explain the interaction between long-term decline and short-term boosts in more detail.
comments.quote: You suggest that long term change will overwhelm short term boosts, but if a boost is 180% at a cold edge

title: Long-term warming reduces fish biomass, but heatwaves shift it

study.system: global forests; kNDVI drought resilience, biodiversity, human pressure

editor_summary: Editor: reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns; the manuscript cannot be accepted, though a revised version addressing these serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Interesting joint analysis of climate, ecology and human pressure, but the method's validity and the human-activity interpretation raise major concerns.
strengths: jointly examining climate, ecological properties and human activities

comments.issue: Merging multiple sensors (GIMMS-3G+ kNDVI) may induce artifacts in autocorrelation signals.
comments.request: Assess or discuss whether sensor merging induces autocorrelation artifacts.
comments.quote: literature has suggested that using multi-sensor time series to diagnose autocorrelation signals may not be reliable

comments.issue: Climate imprint on TAC was not controlled, so low resilience may just reflect climate conditions.
comments.request: Control for climate imprint in the autoregressive signature of kNDVI.
comments.quote: The TAC estimates here are thus likely to suffer from a high risk of climate signal pollution

comments.issue: Temporal baseline inflates positive Delta TAC because of the underlying increasing trend; spatial baseline shows little change.
comments.request: Compare temporal and spatial baselines and account for the trend.
comments.quote: comparing to the temporal baseline would naturally lead to more positive TAC, indicating lower resilience, even if MYD did not alter resilience at all

comments.issue: Definition of the top 10 MYDs and Equation 3 weights and their optimization are not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the top 10 MYDs and Equation 3 coefficients were defined.
comments.quote: In the Methods, Equation 3 was not clearly explained. The rank itself was to be estimated

comments.issue: Unclear which year labels each MYD, affecting interpretation of resilience in the +/- years.
comments.request: State which year was used to label MYDs.
comments.quote: Which year did you use to label MYD? It affects the interpretation of resilience change in +2, +1, -1, -2 and etc. years

comments.issue: Species richness interactions with temperature and moisture are not examined, though these are top predictors; the richness-HFP interaction seems overemphasised.
comments.request: Examine richness interactions with temperature and moisture.
comments.quote: why not examine the interaction between species richness and temperature or moisture in its impact on Delta TAC?

comments.issue: Fig. 3c y-axis is always above zero, suggesting a sub-sample that is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify the sub-sample used for Fig. 3c.
comments.quote: It's also confusing why the y-axis of Fig. 3c is always above zero. Did you use a sub-sample set?

comments.issue: Fig. 4 distribution comparison is unclear; matched MF and IF distributions look similar but are claimed different.
comments.request: Clarify what is compared and show the matched difference distribution.
comments.quote: It is unclear which distributions are compared. I don't think the authors were directly comparing the distributions of Delta TAC of MF and IF

comments.issue: Discussion of reversed diversity effects is underdeveloped; acclimation and competition arguments do not explain the pattern.
comments.request: Strengthen or reconsider the explanations for the reversed diversity effect.
comments.quote: The discussion on the reverse impacts of species diversity on resilience seems underdeveloped (L251-261)

comments.issue: Fire and land-cover exclusion criteria are unclear given the resolution mismatch; sub-grid disturbance could alter AR1.
comments.request: Clarify the fire and land-cover exclusion criteria and thresholds.
comments.quote: What does no fire and no land cover change mean exactly, given the data resolution mismatch?

comments.issue: Caveats from fine-scale heterogeneity in kNDVI, resilience and succession are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how fine-scale heterogeneity might affect the findings.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to explicitly discuss the caveats and how they might affect the findings here

comments.issue: Definition of 'complete NDVI time series' and handling of missing values are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the complete-time-series criterion and missing-value handling.
comments.quote: by “only pixels with complete NDVI time series”, did you mean that any pixel with one missing value would be excluded?

comments.issue: Rationale for including both soil moisture and precipitation in the random forest model is missing.
comments.request: Justify including both soil moisture and precipitation.
comments.quote: What's the rationale for considering both soil moisture and precipitation in the random forest model?

comments.issue: Statistics on lines 161-167 are poorly defined; 'higher HFI' and the ranges are vague.
comments.request: Define the HFI categories and ranges.
comments.quote: The statistics in lines 161-167 are poorly defined. What HFI is considered “higher HFI”?

comments.issue: Description of excluded pixels as non-vegetated or unreliable is not technically correct.
comments.request: Revise the description of the excluded pixels.
comments.quote: the statement “indicative of non-vegetated or unreliable vegetation areas” is not technically correct

reviews.assessment: Valuable, ambitious and methodologically sound global analysis, but causal claims need cautious, descriptive framing and several clarifications.
strengths: valuable and ambitious contribution to global change ecology
rich dataset and innovative analytical approaches
among the first to assess NDVI-based drought resilience globally

comments.issue: Despite matching and DID models the study is observational; causal claims and alternative explanations need cautious framing.
comments.request: Present the study as descriptive and temper causal claims, including in the title.
comments.quote: Causal claims—such as the reversal of biodiversity’s positive effect under high human pressure—should be framed more cautiously

comments.issue: 'Forest management' is used broadly without specificity, though practices differ in their effects.
comments.request: Use a more nuanced management or land-use classification.
comments.quote: The term "forest management" is used broadly and lacks specificity

comments.issue: NDVI-based resilience does not necessarily measure community resilience or species composition.
comments.request: Clarify what NDVI-based resilience does and does not measure.
comments.quote: NDVI-based resilience does not necessarily reflect community resilience or recovery of original species composition

comments.issue: Functional types are not incorporated and could strengthen the analysis.
comments.request: Incorporate more functional types.
comments.quote: Incorporating more functional types could strengthen the analysis

comments.issue: Fixed temporal window may bias resilience estimates in slow-growing systems.
comments.request: Justify or adapt the temporal window for slow-growing systems.
comments.quote: a fixed temporal window may bias resilience estimates for slower growing dominated species

comments.issue: Reliance on pre-existing databases leaves sampling methodology, error estimation and assumptions opaque.
comments.request: Describe the source datasets' sampling, errors and assumptions.
comments.quote: critical details regarding sampling methodology, error estimation, and underlying assumptions are entirely absent

comments.issue: Statement that forests are adapted to drought misapplies the concept of adaptation.
comments.request: Reword to refer to drought tolerance of individual species.
comments.quote: The statement "forests are adapted to drought" is misleading. Forests are not units of selection

comments.issue: Carbon fertilization and overshooting effects are not discussed as alternative drivers of NDVI trends.
comments.request: Discuss carbon fertilization and overshooting effects.
comments.quote: The potential role of carbon fertilization and overshooting effects is not discussed

comments.issue: Top-down analysis could be complemented with bottom-up mechanistic models.
comments.request: Complement the analysis with mechanistic models such as DGVMs.
comments.quote: Complementing these top-down analyses with bottom-up mechanistic models (e.g., DGVM) could complement the empirical approach and help disentangle underlying processes

comments.issue: Focusing on fewer ecoregions with better quality data could improve the analysis.
comments.request: Focus on a few ecoregions with better quality data.
comments.quote: Also focusing on a few ecoregions for which better quality data is available

reviews.assessment: Interesting global analysis with meaningful variables; asks for fuller methods description and PSM bias diagnostics.
strengths: interesting global analysis of forest drought responses
meaningful variables such as diversity and human impacts

comments.issue: Grammar and small typos throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: A grammar check will be needed, there were small typos throughout

comments.issue: What constituted the human footprint needs a brief explanation in the intro or results.
comments.request: Add a brief explanation of the human footprint variable.
comments.quote: The reader will need a bit more explanation of what information or parameterization constituted the human footprint

comments.issue: Discussion focuses on literature rather than strength of inference and interactive effects.
comments.request: Focus the discussion on inference strength and interactive effects.
comments.quote: there are opportunities to focus on the strength of inference and interactive effects in the response of the diversity-to-resilience relationship

comments.issue: SPEI is undefined and its selection and calculation time scale are not justified.
comments.request: Define SPEI and justify its choice and time scale.
comments.quote: The drought index SPEI is undefined. Text is needed to articulate the selection of this index compared to alternates

comments.issue: How the SPEI time basis was adjusted to suit different forest types is not explained or justified.
comments.request: Explain and justify the SPEI time basis across forest types.
comments.quote: please explain in the ms how you dealt with adjusting the timeframe of SPEI calculation to be appropriate for the different forest types

comments.issue: Equation 2 and its data sources are not described in enough detail.
comments.request: Describe Equation 2 and its terms and data sources.
comments.quote: Equation 2 is not adequately described. Where exactly do the data for this come from

comments.issue: Unclear whether proximity and gradient metrics to human factors were used.
comments.request: Clarify whether proximity and gradient metrics were used.
comments.quote: Human pressure: Did you use proximity and gradient metrics to human factors?

comments.issue: Propensity score matching is not described well enough to understand how it was applied.
comments.request: Describe how PSM was applied and why variables were selected.
comments.quote: there is not enough description of it to understand how it was applied - was it only to select sites, or was bias removal imperfect and thus a weighting also used?

comments.issue: Bias is a major concern; standard PSM diagnostic plots are not reported.
comments.request: Provide PSM diagnostic plots in the supplement.
comments.quote: Bias is a major concern in the analysis, and diagnostic plots that are typically reported with PSM ought to be provided in Supplemental files

title: Human pressure and biodiversity modify forest resilience after extreme multi-year droughts

study.system: yeast experimental evolution; 10,000 generations, two species

editor_summary: Editor: three experts raised concerns that must be addressed before publication; revise the manuscript, highlighting all changes, to address all reviewer and editor comments.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and well presented but the results seem expected and descriptive, and the cross-species comparison is technically difficult.

comments.issue: The results are perhaps expected and remain descriptive, and the two systems are fundamentally different to compare.
comments.request: Strengthen the conceptual advance beyond descriptive comparisons.
comments.quote: The study is interesting and well presented, although I feel the results obtained are perhaps expected and remain descriptive

comments.issue: YPD is suboptimal for S. pombe, so it faces hypoxic stress plus suboptimal media; the two species experience different selection.
comments.request: Acknowledge and address this confounding difference in conditions.
comments.quote: the two species are not exposed to the same selection, so perhaps is normal to observe quantitative differences in accumulation of new mutations and different target genes

comments.issue: The rationale for measuring S. pombe fitness against S. cerevisiae rather than its own ancestor, and possible species interactions, is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the logic of the fitness assay in the text.
comments.quote: What is the rationale of measuring fitness changes of the Sp lines using the Sc and not the Sp ancestor?

comments.issue: Parallelism within and between the two systems is not quantified.
comments.request: Quantify how many parallel and different solutions exist within and between systems.
comments.quote: Is it possible to quantify the parallelism within and between the Sc and Sp systems (e.g. how many parallel and different solutions are there within and between systems)?

comments.issue: Aneuploidies are common in S. cerevisiae but likely inviable in S. pombe; ploidy of the lines is unstated.
comments.request: Report aneuploidy and ploidy status of the evolved lines.
comments.quote: Aneuploidies emerge often in Sc experimental evolution whereas are likely inviable in Sp - this could contribute to the overall adaptation dynamic.

comments.issue: Page and line numbers were not added to the manuscript.
comments.request: Add page and line numbers.
comments.quote: Page and line numbers should have been added - will help reviewers to direct comments

reviews.assessment: Very positive; finds the comparison important and novel, with only minor requests to expand methods and follow up on DNA repair.
strengths: literature well represented and discussion interesting

comments.issue: The molecular basis of background mutations in the two species may differ and could relate to DNA repair pathways.
comments.request: Analyse this further in the context of DNA repair pathways.
comments.quote: Perhaps this could be analyzed further in the context of DNA repair pathways.

comments.issue: Strain sources, genotypes and growth conditions are not clearly represented in the methods.
comments.request: Expand the methods and include the S. pombe strain genotype.
comments.quote: The methods could be expanded to clearly represent source of strains, genotypes, and growth conditions applied.

comments.issue: The S. cerevisiae GFP reference strain genotype uses unusual notation.
comments.request: Correct the marker notation (commas, D=delta, lowercase S. pombe genes).
comments.quote: Commas are not usually included after marker genes, D= delta, S. pombe genes are represented in lowercase letters.

reviews.assessment: Convincing and very interesting; several suggestions to improve discussion, figures and analysis details.
strengths: exciting link between life history, metabolism and oxidative-stress tradeoffs

comments.issue: Higher baseline growth rate of S. cerevisiae shortens its fermentation time, potentially confounding species differences.
comments.request: Discuss how growth-rate differences affect the comparison.
comments.quote: I wonder how much differences in the baseline growth rates of the two species create differences in the conditions and thus drive difference between the evolution of the species

comments.issue: 'Petite-positive' is not defined for non-yeast readers.
comments.request: Add a definition or reminder.
comments.quote: “petite-positive” - I think this could use a definition/reminder for non-yeast readers.

comments.issue: The sentence about short indels and frameshifts is confusing on first read.
comments.request: Rephrase to focus on the enrichment of frameshift-preventing indels.
comments.quote: Since the point of this sentence (I think) is that frameshift are under purifying selection, I might rephrase to exclude the piece about 1-2bp and focus on the enrichment of those that prevent frameshift.

comments.issue: Underlying species differences (e.g. genome duplication redundancy) driving coding vs non-coding targets need more explicit discussion.
comments.request: Discuss genomic context vs. life-history explanations more explicitly.
comments.quote: I would appreciate a more explicit discussion of these ideas and may also help inform how much the roles of genomic context vs. life history drive the differences

comments.issue: Supplementary Figure 1 shows 11 S. pombe points although only 10/15 populations reached 10,000 generations.
comments.request: Explain the 11 points in Fig. S1.
comments.quote: why are there 11 points in s. pombe? I assumed this was each population but only 10/15 made it to 10,000 generations?

comments.issue: Whether the lowest-fitness populations are the same as the least oxidative-stress populations is untested.
comments.request: Show this relationship to strengthen the tradeoff claim; check other populations otherwise.
comments.quote: Are the 3 populations with the lowest fitness gain the same as those with the least amount of oxidative stress?

comments.issue: Whether non-coding cis-regulatory regions were included in the multi-hit gene analysis is unexplained.
comments.request: State this explicitly in the main text.
comments.quote: It wasn’t immediately clear to me that non-coding cis-regulatory regions were included in the multi-hit genes analysis.

comments.issue: Mutation-detail paragraphs are long and dense, making key results hard to parse.
comments.request: Split them into multiple paragraphs with more signposting.
comments.quote: these detail some of the most interesting results of the paper, but it took some time for me to parse them. Consider splitting these into multiple paragraphs with a bit more signposting.

comments.issue: Table 1 lists only LOF information and lacks mutation kinds, regulator direction and gene categories.
comments.request: Enrich and reorganize Table 1 by mutation type and gene category.
comments.quote: Table 1 could be improved to include the kinds of mutations in/near each of these genes rather than just listing LOF information.

comments.issue: Which samples were selected for gene expression analysis is unclear from text and methods.
comments.request: Describe the expression sampling procedure in results and methods.
comments.quote: It was not immediately clear from the text nor methods which samples were selected for gene expression analysis.

comments.issue: Expression variability across all sequenced populations is not shown.
comments.request: Show gene expression variability among populations.
comments.quote: given the authors have gene expression data from all the populations, it would be of interest to show details on variability between the populations with regards to gene expression

comments.issue: Whether pyk1 downregulation is cis-driven or shows trans-regulatory effects in other populations is unclear.
comments.request: Test how many populations downregulate pyk1 and whether this tracks mutations in/near the gene.
comments.quote: if pyk1’s down-regulation is exclusive to those with mutations in/near the gene, suggesting it is driven primarily by mutations in cis-regulatory regions, or if there may be evidence for trans-regulatory effects in the other populations

title: Parallel but distinct adaptive routes in the budding and fission yeasts after 10,000 generations of experimental evolution

study.system: Chinese vascular plants; dated phylogeny and endemism centres

editor_summary: Reviewer 2 wants the drivers-of-diversification discussion amended; Reviewer 3 requests phylogenetic-uncertainty analysis, threshold rationale, range-size sensitivity and broader palaeoclimate discussion; editor asks for a more informative title.

reviews.assessment: Highly timely, methodologically sound study with only minor editorial and figure suggestions.
strengths: new checklist and dated phylogeny with improved representation
compelling case for Central China as an overlooked hotspot

comments.issue: Grammatical suggestion for the sentence on molecular data gaps at lines 88-89.
comments.request: Change 'reveals molecular data gaps among' to 'reveals gaps in available molecular data from'.
comments.quote: change "Our geospatial analysis reveals molecular data gaps among

comments.issue: Why competing land-use contributes to fragmentation is unclear.

comments.issue: TreePL's appropriateness for large phylogenies is not stated.

comments.issue: Mountain lines in Extended Data Fig. 1 are not consistently gray.

comments.issue: Extended Data Fig. 2 legend appears incomplete.

comments.issue: It is unclear what code files might be missing from the Scripts folder.

comments.issue: No README files or usage examples accompany the scripts.

comments.issue: Input data files and trees required by the scripts could not be found.
comments.request: Provide all input data files and trees.
comments.quote: data files and trees that need to be read into the scripts were not found by me. So while I could install the code, not everything was available to run the code.

reviews.assessment: Praises the monumental database and state-of-the-art analyses, offering suggestions on the drivers sentence, presentation and context.

comments.issue: The abstract omits the hotspot's species and endemic totals.
comments.request: Add these totals to the abstract.
comments.quote: the authors should include the total number of vascular plant species, and the total number of endemic species, for the new hotspot in the abstract.

comments.issue: 'Hengduan' is missing before 'Mountains' at line 57.
comments.request: Insert 'Hengduan'.
comments.quote: On line 57, insert the missing "Hengduan" before "Mountains".

comments.issue: Lines 57-59 pin speciation and endemism on uplift and monsoon intensification, ignoring other drivers and regions.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence to address these concerns.
comments.quote: I suggest the authors should rewrite lines 57-59. The sentence seems to pin the most important driver of speciation and endemism on uplift of the Quinghai-Tibet plateau and intensification of the monsoon.

comments.issue: Readers are not told where 'Central China' actually is.
comments.request: Describe its location (e.g., Hunan, Jiangxi) and area.
comments.quote: perhaps the authors might give the readers some idea of where "Central China" is, given that it's not in the actual center of the country

comments.issue: Median divergence ages of endemic versus non-endemic species are not stated in the text.
comments.request: State the 4.8 vs. 7.1 My medians in the text.
comments.quote: please state the median divergence ages of endemic vs. non-endemic species here (4.8 vs. 7.1 My)

comments.issue: 'An established method' conveys nothing about the method.
comments.request: Insert a clarifying phrase.
comments.quote: "an established method16" does not convey the substance of the method in any way. Can the authors insert a clarifying phrase here?

comments.issue: No table summarising area and species/endemic counts per hotspot.
comments.request: Insert such a table.
comments.quote: Suggest you insert a table giving area, number of species, and number of endemic species for each of these hotspots.

comments.issue: The Hu Huanyong Line is not shown or defined.
comments.request: Draw and define the Hu Huanyong Line on a map.
comments.quote: Suggest you draw the Hu Huanyong Line on one of the maps, so that those unacquainted with it can see where it is (and, in the caption, how it is defined).

comments.issue: The new hotspot's rank among global hotspots is not given.
comments.request: Report its ranking by species and endemic counts.
comments.quote: it would be nice to know where the new Central China hotspot sits on the ranked list of global hotspots, based on total number of vascular plant species and number of endemic species

comments.issue: The abstract does not mention the East Asian subtropical ecoregion.
comments.request: Mention the ecoregion in the abstract.
comments.quote: I also wonder whether the authors might mention in the abstract that this hotspot sits in "unique East Asian subtropical evergreen broad-leaved forest ecoregion" as well as the other items mentioned under point 1 above.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the scale and significance, but requests phylogenetic-uncertainty sensitivity, threshold justification, range-estimation checks and a more focused, better-framed discussion.
strengths: impressive data scale, major step forward

comments.issue: Sensitivity of the endemism conclusions to phylogenetic uncertainty is not demonstrated.
comments.request: Repeat CANAPE and endemism identification on bootstrap tree subsets.
comments.quote: I request a more explicit analysis of how sensitive your primary conclusions are to phylogenetic uncertainty.

comments.issue: The 23 Ma and 5 Ma thresholds lack biological justification for this dataset.
comments.request: Justify the cut-offs or discuss alternative thresholds.
comments.quote: The use of fixed temporal thresholds (23 Ma for genera, 5 Ma for species) in your robustness check, while following previous studies, requires a stronger biological justification

comments.issue: Coarse grid and county records may overestimate narrow endemic range sizes.
comments.request: Discuss the limitation and run a sensitivity analysis with finer range estimates.
comments.quote: the method for estimating species geographic ranges (based on 100 km grid cells and county-level records) could inherently overestimate the range size of narrow endemics

comments.issue: How the Central China boundary in Figure 4 was drawn is not described step by step.
comments.request: Describe the boundary delineation explicitly.
comments.quote: the process of drawing the final boundary in Figure 4 needs more explicit description in the main text or methods

comments.issue: Driver discussion remains correlative and not integrated with palaeoclimate/geology models.
comments.request: Link diversification peaks to regional palaeoclimate and geological models.
comments.quote: However, the discussion of the drivers remains somewhat correlative. I encourage you to more deeply integrate your findings with specific paleoclimatic and geological models for the region.

comments.issue: Central China's metrics are not quantitatively compared with other global hotspots.
comments.request: Add a comparative table or paragraph with other hotspots.
comments.quote: I recommend adding a comparative table or paragraph in the results/discussion. This should quantitatively compare Central China's metrics (species richness, endemism, habitat loss) with other established Global Biodiversity Hotspots

comments.issue: Conservation discussion lacks nuance on strategies and socio-economic context in a densely populated region.
comments.request: Discuss realistic strategies, connectivity and socio-economic literature.
comments.quote: it would be strengthened by a more realistic and nuanced discussion of the challenges and opportunities for conservation in this densely populated region

comments.issue: No dedicated limitations paragraph covering sampling gaps, record biases and dating markers.
comments.request: Add an explicit limitations paragraph to the discussion.
comments.quote: The manuscript would benefit from a dedicated paragraph in the discussion that explicitly outlines the key limitations of the study.

comments.issue: The discussion is unfocused and dwells on taxonomic vs phylogenetic endemism definitions.
comments.request: Streamline this explanation and emphasise the synthetic conclusion.
comments.quote: The discussion could be more focused. I suggest streamlining the explanation of the differences between taxonomic and phylogenetic endemism

title: A comprehensive dated phylogeny of China’s vascular plants reveals a hidden global biodiversity hotspot

study.system: fossil lycophytes; carbon isotopes, phylogeny, climate models

editor_summary: Editor invites revision addressing reviewer criticisms and editorial concerns; asks responses and changes highlighted in Word before a final decision.

reviews.assessment: Intriguing and impressive isotope study supporting CAM-like photosynthesis, but the broader claims need a mass-balance check.
strengths: interpretation of CAM-like photosynthesis is compelling

comments.issue: Low taxonomic resolution may skew ecophysiological interpretations.
comments.request: Assess whether poor taxonomic resolution could mislead interpretations.
comments.quote: I wondered if there is any risk that the conclusions may be skewed by the fact that the new morphology-based taxonomy lacks resolution

comments.issue: The claim that CAM plants dominated and controlled global carbon burial lacks a mass-balance estimate.
comments.request: Provide a mass balance for the CAM fraction of terrestrial biomass.
comments.quote: it would be helpful if information could be provided on what fraction of the terrestrial flora was composed of CAM-photosynthesizers at any given time

comments.issue: Line-level edits (remove 'dramatic', 'data are', comma, phrasing).
comments.quote: l. 31 and 49: the word ‘dramatic’ has no scientific meaning. You can delete it without loss of content.

comments.issue: Salinity heterogeneity in coastal lowlands could affect the analysis; additional evidence is needed.
comments.request: Provide evidence that salinity is not a concern.
comments.quote: coastal lowlands can be very heterogeneous in salinity, as they are located along the interface between freshwater and seawater. Can additional evidence be provided that salinity is not a concern for this analysis?

comments.issue: Non-lycophyte taxa are not specified, so it is unclear whether they could have used CAM.
comments.request: Specify the non-lycophyte taxa.
comments.quote: Maybe specify what the non-lycophytes are, so that the reader can be more certain that they could not have been performing CAM-based photosynthesis

comments.issue: Lines 462-465 are unclear and appear to contradict the positive-feedback statement at lines 454-456.
comments.request: Clarify the feedback logic.
comments.quote: Why would the absence of CAM plants have extended the hothouse conditions beyond 5 million years? This point seems to contradict the statement in ll. 454-456, which mentioned a positive feedback that increased warming

comments.issue: Figure 5 lacks numerical ages for readers unfamiliar with stage names.
comments.request: Add ages in numbers to Figure 5.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to add ages in numbers to make this figure easier to read for people who are not familiar with the stage names

comments.issue: Analytical reference materials, precision and accuracy are not reported.
comments.request: Report reference materials and analytical precision and accuracy.
comments.quote: Please provide information about analytical reference materials and report precision and accuracy of the data

reviews.assessment: Thought-provoking and plausible, but the isotopic evidence for CAM is not definitive and the temperature-tolerance argument needs unpacking.
strengths: field would benefit from seeing this in the literature

comments.issue: Carbon isotopes alone cannot definitively distinguish CAM from C3; non-lycophyte sample is small.
comments.request: Acknowledge these limitations and temper the CAM inference.
comments.quote: While C isotopes are a crucial piece of evidence for inferring CAM activity in deep time, they alone can’t be definitive, for a few reasons

comments.issue: Paper should be framed as a hypothesis paper rather than a definitive assessment.
comments.request: End the title with a question mark and frame it as a hypothesis.
comments.quote: I think the paper works well as a “hypothesis paper”, rather than a definitive assessment of the photosynthetic metabolism of fossil lycophytes

comments.issue: CAM has lower optimal growth temperatures than C3, so it does not explain survival at 45-65 C; mechanism is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism and reconcile it with temperature optima.
comments.quote: the cited paper (ref. 19) shows that CAM plants have lower optimal growth temperatures than C3, with only C4 having higher temperature tolerance. On this basis, it would seem that CAM does not help explain lycophyte survival

comments.issue: Discussion brings in tangential ideas (anti-heavy-metal antioxidant enzymes) not tied to the perturbations.
comments.request: Remove or link these tangential ideas.
comments.quote: also bring in tangential ideas such as “anti-heavy metal antioxidant enzyme systems” that are not clearly tied to the environmental perturbations being discussed

reviews.assessment: Exciting, novel and robust multi-faceted study, needing only clarifications on facultative versus obligate CAM and some consistency checks.

comments.issue: It is not stated whether the transition taxa are obligate or facultative CAM.
comments.request: Tighten the language to state obligate versus facultative CAM.
comments.quote: The overall suggestion throughout the manuscript is that the PT transition taxa are obligate CAM? yet it is not stated if the authors think they are obligate or facultative CAM

comments.issue: PCA groupings may reflect taphonomy or depositional environment rather than evolutionary differences.
comments.request: Code taphonomic and depositional facies in the PCA analysis.
comments.quote: Could an additional set of analyses be included which codes the fossil taxa in the PCA morphospace with taphonomic or depositional environment/ facies ?

comments.issue: CO2 trends in the introduction are inconsistent with those used in the HAD GCM analyses.
comments.request: Double-check and reconcile the CO2 trends.
comments.quote: There seems to be a small inconsistency in the CO2 trends described in the intro and those used for the HAD gcm analyses – please double check

title: CAM photosynthesis may have conferred an advantage during the Permian–Triassic mass extinction event

study.system: ancient humans; 133 genomes from the Bury megalithic tomb

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers agree the plague and population-decline narratives are overstated; encourages a revision that downplays plague and foregrounds the social-structure findings, then resubmission.

reviews.assessment: Calls the data robust and novel but says the plague narrative is unsupported and overshadows the truly groundbreaking social findings.
strengths: groundbreaking findings on half-sibling relationships and shifts in social organisation
half-sibling and social-organisation findings deserve greater attention

comments.issue: Framing plague as the key argument making Bury the missing link is not supported by only four positive individuals.
comments.request: Temper or support the claim linking Bury to Neolithic population decline via plague.
comments.quote: My primary concern is the focus on the plague pathogen as the key argument for positioning Bury as the missing link in explaining Neolithic population decline. This claim is not sufficiently supported, given that only four individuals tested positive for the pathogen.

comments.issue: The plague emphasis crowds out the groundbreaking kinship and social-organisation findings.
comments.request: Devote more space to presenting the site and archaeothanatological analysis.
comments.quote: This overemphasis on plague diminishes the significance of the truly groundbreaking findings from Bury, which deserve greater attention.

comments.issue: Dates alternate between BCE and BP, and between ranges and standard deviations.
comments.request: Apply a uniform approach to dating throughout.
comments.quote: The dates used throughout the paper are inconsistent, alternating between BCE and BP. Additionally, some individuals are presented with a date range, while others are listed with a standard deviation (±).

comments.issue: “Pedigree” and “family” are used interchangeably although Neolithic family structures are unknown.
comments.request: Consistently use the neutral term “pedigree”.
comments.quote: The authors use "pedigree" and "family" interchangeably, despite acknowledging that kinship and family structures in the Neolithic period remain unknown.

comments.issue: PCA is not defined at first use.
comments.request: Define PCA in the first paragraph of the genetic discontinuity section.
comments.quote: PCA (Principal Component Analysis): This should be defined in the first paragraph of the section Genetic discontinuity between two phases.

comments.issue: The reasoning behind “founding act” and “founder” is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify the criteria and state whether Pedigree 1 is the earliest phase.
comments.quote: The reasoning behind these terms is not clearly explained. The authors should clarify whether this designation is based on C14 dating, stratigraphic position, or other criteria

comments.issue: “Avuncular” in Figure 3 is not defined.
comments.request: Explicitly define avuncular.
comments.quote: “Avuncular” (Figure 3): This term should be explicitly defined.

comments.issue: “Dark Age” is tied to the Middle Ages and inconsistent with the paper's terminology.
comments.request: Use “Neolithic decline” consistently instead.
comments.quote: “Dark Age”: This term should be avoided, as it is heavily associated with the Middle Ages. Since the paper consistently uses “Neolithic decline”, this term should be maintained for consistency.

comments.issue: The demographic profile discussion lacks references in the text and supplementary information.
comments.request: Add references contextualising the demographic data.
comments.quote: Additional references are needed to contextualise the demographic data and their interpretation, in the text and in supplementary information 1.

comments.issue: The IBD and farming-ancestry discussion does not cite recent studies.
comments.request: Support the reference panel discussion with recent literature.
comments.quote: The discussion on IBD (identity by descent) and farming ancestry across Europe should be supported by recent studies.

comments.issue: Key comparative studies on social structure and social anthropology are not referenced.
comments.request: Cite Rivollat et al. 2023, Cassidy et al. 2020 and social anthropology work.
comments.quote: It is surprising that the authors do not reference recent publications addressing similar topics in either the same geographic area in earlier periods (e.g., Rivollat et al., 2023) or the same period and burial structure in a different region (Cassidy et al., 2020).

comments.issue: The simulation of discontinuity versus continuity scenarios is not detailed.
comments.request: Detail the simulation with references or a pointer to the methods.
comments.quote: Simulation of two scenarios (discontinuity vs. continuity): These should be explicitly detailed with appropriate references or a reference to the methods section.

comments.issue: The claim about social or cultural continuity in Phase 2 lacks literature support.
comments.request: Support the argument with relevant literature.
comments.quote: The argument that longer occupation suggests a greater role for social or cultural continuity should be supported with literature.

comments.issue: The claim that plague outbreaks led to site abandonment lacks comparable archaeological evidence.
comments.request: Cite comparable evidence of epidemic-driven abandonment.
comments.quote: However, this claim requires references to comparable archaeological evidence of epidemic-driven abandonment.

comments.issue: The Scandinavian Neolithic decline parallel lacks referencing and context.
comments.request: Provide proper references and context for this parallel.
comments.quote: The Scandinavian Neolithic decline: This parallel is mentioned but lacks proper referencing and context.

comments.issue: The strontium mobility analysis lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Add references strengthening the strontium interpretation.
comments.quote: Strontium analysis and broader mobility context (Supplementary Information 5): More references should be included to strengthen the interpretation of these findings.

comments.issue: One sentence remains incomplete and needs rephrasing.
comments.request: Rephrase the incomplete sentence for clarity.
comments.quote: Some editing is required. One sentence remains incomplete: “Recent research that is ‘Neolithic decline’

comments.issue: The site type name is not italicised.
comments.request: Write allée sépulcrale in italics.
comments.quote: Additionally, allée sépulcrale should be written in italics.

comments.issue: What constitutes a collective burial site and the main theories about them are not defined.
comments.request: Define collective burial sites and overview the prevailing interpretations.
comments.quote: The authors should provide a more detailed definition of what constitutes a collective burial site, along with an overview of the main theories regarding this type of site.

comments.issue: The evidence for population decline is asserted without referencing archaeological and demographic literature.
comments.request: Reference relevant literature and explain the evidence types used.
comments.quote: Regarding the evidence for population decline, the authors should reference relevant literature, including archaeological and demographic sources, to support their claims.

comments.issue: The site description lacks a detailed stratigraphic account demonstrating two occupations.
comments.request: Add context, stratigraphy and field documentation in the supplement.
comments.quote: The description of the semi-megalithic allée sépulcrale of Bury requires additional context and a more detailed stratigraphic account to demonstrate the presence of two distinct occupations.

comments.issue: The concept of a semi-megalithic structure is not defined.
comments.request: Explicitly define semi-megalithic structures.
comments.quote: Additionally, the concept of a semi-megalithic structure should be explicitly defined for clarity.

comments.issue: The demographic profile is given only for Phase 1, not Phase 2.
comments.request: Provide a comparable demographic analysis for Phase 2.
comments.quote: The demographic profile for the first phase is discussed, but there is no mention of the second phase. A similar analysis should be provided

comments.issue: It is unclear how sampling avoided testing the same individual twice in commingled contexts.
comments.request: Detail the sampling strategy for the 182 teeth from 179 individuals.
comments.quote: The authors present a sample of 182 teeth from 179 individuals. How was the selection made to ensure that the same individual was not tested twice?

comments.issue: Loose teeth listed alongside individual numbers in the Excel sheet are unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify the sample presentation and sampling strategy.
comments.quote: In the Excel sheet presenting the sample, some individual numbers are listed alongside loose teeth. However, this aspect has not been explained in the context of the burial

comments.issue: The male predominance claim is made without a full biological profile for the site or each phase.
comments.request: Provide a comprehensive biological profile.
comments.quote: The statement, “genetic sexing [confirmed] the high predominance of males in both phases,” is made without a full biological profile for the entire site or for each phase.

comments.issue: The Figure 1 caption omits the publication date.
comments.request: Add the publication date to the caption.
comments.quote: Figure 1: The publication date is missing in the caption.

comments.issue: The genetic ancestry determination is not contextualised in recent research.
comments.request: Provide more context on the rationale for the ancestry analyses.
comments.quote: Given that this study focuses on the end of the Neolithic (even during its decline), why should we still be looking for Anatolian farmer origins and Mesolithic populations?

comments.issue: “Three-quarters of individuals” would be clearer as exact numbers.
comments.request: Give precise percentages or counts.
comments.quote: Including precise percentages or actual numbers would enhance clarity.

comments.issue: The sampling strategy and why some individuals were not sampled or yielded no results are not explained.
comments.request: Describe the selection criteria.
comments.quote: A more detailed explanation of the sampling strategy would clarify why some individuals were not sampled or did not yield results. What were the selection criteria?

comments.issue: Contextual information on burial practices and funerary customs is missing.
comments.request: Provide context on burial practices and funerary customs.
comments.quote: The lack of contextual information regarding burial practices and funerary customs of the time.

comments.issue: Pedigrees are not summarised by generations or biological profiles.
comments.request: Add pedigree summaries in the supplementary information.
comments.quote: Regarding Pedigree 1.A, a summary would be helpful—such as the number of generations represented and a general biological profile of the individuals within this pedigree.

comments.issue: No overview of funerary practices, bone assemblage or their variation across phases is given for ID174.
comments.request: Provide the broader burial context.
comments.quote: the paper does not provide an overview of funerary practices, the bone assemblage at the site, or how these vary across different phases

comments.issue: Only an unsampled individual is proposed as the explanation for the ID185 genetic link.
comments.request: Consider alternative explanations such as adoption or fostering.
comments.quote: Could alternative explanations, such as adoption or fostering, be considered?

comments.issue: The rare half-sibling finding is not discussed or compared with other case studies.
comments.request: Discuss ID307 and ID276 in more detail against known cases.
comments.quote: This rare finding warrants a more detailed discussion and comparison with other known case studies, as it represents a significant outcome.

comments.issue: Body positions are not presented, so the claim of no link between kinship and burial placement cannot be evaluated.
comments.request: Provide body position data for each individual.
comments.quote: the study does not present body positions for each identified individual, making it difficult to evaluate the claim that there is no correlation between genetic relationships and burial placement

comments.issue: No general health status data for the population(s) are presented.
comments.request: Include health status information.
comments.quote: The paper does not provide any data on the general health status of the population(s).

comments.issue: Figure 7.7 could not be located.
comments.request: Provide or correct the missing figure.
comments.quote: Additionally, I was unable to locate Figure 7.7.

comments.issue: Reported case numbers (85 + 56 = 141) do not match any stated population totals.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancies in sample and case numbers.
comments.quote: The reported numbers (85 + 56 = 141) do not match the total population (n = 316), the sampled population (n = 179), or the number of teeth sampled (n = 182).

comments.issue: The paper's own counterarguments against a plague-driven end of Phase 1 rely on undocumented alternative explanations.
comments.request: Document the stratigraphic and population-increase alternatives or revise the argument.
comments.quote: the alternative explanations they propose—stratigraphic position and a significant population increase—are not well documented and require further evidence

comments.issue: The environmental data paragraph is poorly documented and not connected to Bury results.
comments.request: Connect the environmental section to the paper's data or remove it.
comments.quote: This paragraph is poorly documented and not well connected to the paper's results, as it does not include any direct data from Bury.

comments.issue: Disagrees that Bury is the missing link; no convincing evidence for a plague outbreak or its environmental impact.
comments.request: Support or remove the missing-link claim.
comments.quote: I disagree with the statement that Bury is the missing link in demonstrating the "Neolithic decline", as no convincing evidence has been presented to establish a plague outbreak, its environmental impact, or other contributing factors.

comments.issue: The Scandinavian parallel is weak and lacks references and examples.
comments.request: Strengthen the comparison with clear references.
comments.quote: The parallel drawn with Scandinavian data is weak, lacking sufficient references and clear examples that directly relate to what happened at Bury.

comments.issue: The overall discussion is a tentative, unsubstantiated attempt to link Bury to pan-European patterns.
comments.request: Ground the discussion in robust comparative evidence.
comments.quote: Overall, the discussion comes across as a tentative and unsubstantiated attempt to link Bury to broader patterns of Neolithic decline in Europe, rather than a well-supported argument grounded in robust comparative evidence.

comments.issue: The sample selection process is not outlined in the methods.
comments.request: Outline the sample selection process in the methods.
comments.quote: However, the sample selection process should be clearly outlined here.

comments.issue: Recent work on integrating juveniles into archaeological studies is omitted.
comments.request: Mention relevant publications from the last 10 years.
comments.quote: some relevant work has been published in the last 10 years that would be worth mentioning

comments.issue: Supplementary Information 4 seems irrelevant because its connection to Bury is unclear and its references are not cited.
comments.request: Clarify the connection to Bury and cite the references.
comments.quote: Although this section presents an interesting topic, its connection to Bury is not clearly explained, making it seem irrelevant to the paper.

comments.issue: Supplementary Information 5 does not explain why Le Tumulus des Sables is a relevant comparison.
comments.request: Explain the significance of the comparison.
comments.quote: This section is confusing, as it does not clarify why Le Tumulus des Sables is relevant for comparison with the Bury site.

reviews.assessment: Finds the claims strongly overstated, with incomplete genetic and pathogen evidence and insufficient methodological transparency.

comments.issue: No continent-wide IBD analysis places the Bury discontinuity in context, so the continental collapse claim is speculative.
comments.request: Provide pan-European IBD comparisons with contemporaneous populations.
comments.quote: The authors fail to provide a continent-wide IBD-sharing analysis to place the Bury discontinuity in context. Without comparison to other contemporaneous Neolithic populations, the claim of a continent-wide collapse remains speculative and unsupported.

comments.issue: The IBD comparison methodology with other sites is not transparently described.
comments.request: Describe the comparative IBD methodology and whether Bury differs from regional variation.
comments.quote: The methodology for comparing IBD-sharing between Bury and other Neolithic sites is not transparently described.

comments.issue: Referenced figures are missing or misnumbered, including Supplementary Figure 7.4.
comments.request: Fix the figure numbering and add the missing figures.
comments.quote: Supplementary Figure 7.4 (referenced for hierarchical clustering of IBD) is not present; Suppl. Information 6 only includes figures 6.1–6.7.

comments.issue: No Ne estimates, heterozygosity analyses or coalescent simulations support the population-decline claim.
comments.request: Add demographic modelling such as Ne estimates to support the decline claim.
comments.quote: The authors do not include demographic modeling such as Ne estimates, genome-wide heterozygosity analyses, or coalescent simulations. These are essential to support claims of population decline.

comments.issue: Genetic shifts coinciding with cultural change are interpreted as collapse, while the data point to cultural continuity.
comments.request: Consider cultural interaction rather than demographic collapse.
comments.quote: The persistence of distinct genetic profiles at Bury (e.g., minimal Steppe ancestry) argues against a collapse scenario and instead points to cultural continuity or interaction.

comments.issue: It is unexplained how conflicting outputs from five kinship programs were reconciled.
comments.request: State which kinship results were prioritised and why.
comments.quote: The authors used five different programs to estimate kinship—potentially increasing robustness—but failed to explain how conflicting outputs were reconciled.

comments.issue: Most individuals are not close relatives, yet family groups are extrapolated to the whole population.
comments.request: Acknowledge alternative explanations and avoid population-level extrapolation.
comments.quote: Most individuals are not closely related, contradicting the notion of a kinship-based burial pattern. Nevertheless, the authors generalize from a few family groups to the whole population

comments.issue: Female underrepresentation is used as evidence of patrilineal burial without addressing preservation, burial treatment or sampling alternatives.
comments.request: Address alternative explanations for the sex ratio.
comments.quote: The underrepresentation of females is presented as evidence of patrilineal burial, but other plausible factors—such as preservation bias, differential burial treatment, or sampling artifacts—are not addressed.

comments.issue: Y. pestis reads lack validation: no mapping statistics, coverage or comparisons ruling out contamination or misidentification.
comments.request: Provide read validation, coverage and comparisons with related bacteria.
comments.quote: No mapping statistics, depth coverage data, or comparison with related environmental bacteria (e.g., Y. pseudotuberculosis) are presented. Contamination or misidentification cannot be ruled out.

comments.issue: No coverage of key virulence factors, so disease potential of the strains cannot be assessed.
comments.request: Report coverage of pla, caf and ymt virulence factors.
comments.quote: There is no reported coverage of key virulence factors (pla, caf, ymt), making it impossible to assess whether the strains could cause disease.

comments.issue: No skeletal or burial evidence of rapid death or epidemic burial supports the outbreak claim.
comments.request: Provide osteological or burial evidence consistent with an epidemic, or temper the claim.
comments.quote: There is no skeletal evidence of rapid death, nor signs of epidemic burial (e.g., mass graves, irregular positioning).

comments.issue: No epidemiological modelling assesses the demographic impact of Y. pestis.
comments.request: Model the potential demographic impact of Y. pestis.
comments.quote: The study lacks any modeling to assess the demographic impact of Y. pestis, leaving its role speculative and unconvincing.

comments.issue: The reference genome and the positions used for pseudohaploid calling are not stated.
comments.request: State the reference genome and genotyping positions used.
comments.quote: The reference genome used for mapping (e.g., hg19) is not stated. It is also unclear which positions were used for pseudohaploid calling—was the 1240K panel used?

comments.issue: The ~6,000 merged samples are not specified by source, release or inclusion criteria.
comments.request: List the merged samples, their release and selection criteria.
comments.quote: The authors state that they merged their data with ~6,000 samples, but do not specify which samples, from which release, or on what criteria (e.g., geography, time period).

comments.issue: The PCA strategy, projection or combined dataset, is ambiguous.
comments.request: Describe the PCA dataset and projection strategy.
comments.quote: The strategy for PCA is ambiguous. Was it performed using modern West Eurasian populations with projection of ancient individuals, or using a combined dataset?

comments.issue: IBDseq parameters are not reported and more suitable tools such as ancIBD are not considered.
comments.request: Report IBD parameters and justify the tool choice.
comments.quote: The IBD analysis was conducted using IBDseq, but no parameter details are provided. More suitable tools for ancient, low-coverage DNA (e.g., ancIBD) are not considered

comments.issue: Haplogroup calling procedures, QC measures and tools are not described.
comments.request: Describe haplogroup calling procedures and QC.
comments.quote: mtDNA and Y-chromosome haplogroups are reported without any details on the calling procedure, QC measures, or tools used.

comments.issue: The ancestry estimation method and modelling details are not stated.
comments.request: State the ancestry method and report full modelling details.
comments.quote: The study reports ancestry proportions (e.g., 90% farmer, 10% hunter-gatherer) but does not state which method was used (e.g., supervised ADMIXTURE, qpAdm).

comments.issue: Supplementary tables lack introductory descriptions and use cryptic headers such as nDer_woDam.
comments.request: Add table descriptions and write out all acronyms.
comments.quote: Supplementary Tables lack clear introductory descriptions. Column headers such as “nDer_woDam” are cryptic.

reviews.assessment: Commends the exceptional data and analysis but is unconvinced by the sweeping plague and Neolithic decline interpretation and questions the journal fit.
strengths: incredible data generation and computational analysis
first detailed exploration of differences between deposition phases at a tomb
ingenious use of IBD segment-sharing to assess continuity
well written with clear and appropriate figures

comments.issue: A single tomb cannot sustain the sweeping claim of a pan-European plague pandemic collapsing megalithic societies.
comments.request: Remove or substantially scale back the continental-scale framing.
comments.quote: The continental-scale framing of the significance of the results from Bury is, I think, unjustified and unnecessary.

comments.issue: The catastrophic mortality profile cannot be interpreted straightforwardly because the buried sample is not representative of a community.
comments.request: Caveat the mortality profile given male bias and close relatives in the sample.
comments.quote: Given at Bury there are numerous reasons (male bias, occurrence of close genetic relatives) to think this is not a representative sample of a community, the catastrophic mortality profile is less easy to interpret

comments.issue: The variation in infection between phases could have occurred by chance given the very low infection rate.
comments.request: Provide analysis showing the between-phase variation is not due to chance.
comments.quote: the rate of Yersinia pestis infection is very low and unless the authors can provide analysis to the contrary it looks to me like the varied occurrence in different phases could have occurred by chance

comments.issue: Pathogen DNA preservation is poorly understood, so between-site and between-phase prevalence comparisons are unreliable.
comments.request: Acknowledge the uncertainty in prevalence comparisons due to preservation.
comments.quote: it is difficult to know to what extent within-site and between site comparisons of rates of disease represent genuine variation in prevalence or just preservation

comments.issue: Bury adds little to the argument that plague was widespread, given the earlier Orkney find.
comments.request: Downplay the contribution of Bury to the plague-widespreadness discussion.
comments.quote: I don’t think the authors’ results from Bury necessarily adds so much to the discussion of how widespread plague was in Late Neolithic Europe.

comments.issue: The discussion of the broader megalithic and Neolithic decline context is inadequate and simplistic.
comments.request: Provide a more nuanced treatment of megalithic structures and regional variation.
comments.quote: I found the authors’ discussion of the broader archaeological context of the ‘Neolithic decline’ and disuse of megalithic structures inadequate and simplistic.

comments.issue: Results are not interpreted in their local or regional context in favour of grand narratives.
comments.request: Contextualise the Bury results in the regional sequence.
comments.quote: The authors make no effort to understand their results in their local or regional contexts.

comments.issue: The demographic “Neolithic decline” is conflated with the disuse and abandonment of megalithic tombs.
comments.request: Distinguish demographic decline from monument abandonment.
comments.quote: The authors’ discussion also seems to conflate, the ‘Late Neolithic decline’ which is usually derived from measures of demographic decline with changes in the disuse/abandonment of megalithic tombs.

comments.issue: Without the grander disease and decline applications, the paper may not be well suited to Nature Ecology & Evolution.
comments.request: Reframe the paper or consider a more specialised venue.
comments.quote: without the grander applications to disease and demographic decline I’m not sure a revised version of this paper would be well-suited to Nature Ecology and Evolution and perhaps would be better placed elsewhere

comments.issue: The claim that population decline halted megalith building is too simplistic and contradicted by continued building.
comments.request: Tone down the statement significantly.
comments.quote: I appreciate this is only part of a summary, but this is too simplistic and should be toned down significantly.

comments.issue: A sentence is incomplete and “linked to” implies disputed causality.
comments.request: Complete the sentence and consider “associated with” instead.
comments.quote: This sentence is incomplete. Also ‘associated with’ rather than ‘linked to’ might be a more appropriate phrase here as ‘linked to’ implies some level of causality, which is debated.

comments.issue: The specific region of France is not stated and “French” is questionable for a Neolithic monument.
comments.request: Specify the region and use “in present-day France”.
comments.quote: I think it would be useful for the authors to include which specific region of France. Also the authors could consider whether ‘French’ works when discussing a Neolithic monument rather than ‘in present-day France.’

comments.issue: The study investigates organisation among the dead, so it cannot directly reveal societal changes.
comments.request: Lay out the reasoning linking burial organisation to social change.
comments.quote: I don’t think the authors can say that their study directly reveals societal changes, rather evidence for differences in deposition and organisation which might reflect changes in society.

comments.issue: The “end of complex megalithic architectures” framing includes structures that continue into the 3rd millennium and needs qualification.
comments.request: Clarify the scope and qualify pan-European claims.
comments.quote: this needs to be made clear from the beginning, and 2) this still doesn’t work for places like Ireland and Orkney where megalithic tombs are being built into 3rd Millennium BC

comments.issue: Demographic decline and the move away from megalith construction are bundled together as causally linked without justification.
comments.request: Outline the reasoning instead of taking the causal link for granted.
comments.quote: The way the authors bundle together demographic decline and the move away from the construction of megaliths takes for granted that the two are somehow inextricably linked and causal.

comments.issue: No account is given of decline in the Paris Basin, the tomb's own region.
comments.request: Describe the local and regional sequence to assess the narrative.
comments.quote: Given the authors acknowledge that measures of Late Neolithic decline and monument building are regionally variable across Europe, it is surprising they don’t provide an account of decline in the particular region (Paris basin) where their tomb was found.

comments.issue: The Yersinia pestis debate is not elaborated, making the steppe-expansion link a non sequitur.
comments.request: Add detail on how plague lineages were initially tied to steppe expansions.
comments.quote: I don’t think the various factors of the debate around Late Neolithic-Bronze Age Yersinia pestis are elaborated well here

comments.issue: The Late Neolithic decline is treated as a singular homogeneous pan-European process.
comments.request: Acknowledge regional variability rather than taking homogeneity for granted.
comments.quote: Again, this is treating the Late Neolithic decline as a singular homogenous pan-European process when I don’t think there is the evidence to take that for granted.
