comments.issue: The Orkney Banks tomb find is not mentioned as background, although it implies plague was widespread.
comments.request: Mention the Orkney evidence in the background.
comments.quote: Wouldn’t the (geographically) peripheral location of Orkney mean that it is already established to some extent that Yersinia pestis must have been widespread in this period

comments.issue: The term “semi-megalithic” is not defined.
comments.request: Define what semi-megalithic means here.
comments.quote: it would be useful for the authors to define what they mean by ‘semi-megalithic’ here, given it is not a common phrase

comments.issue: The mortality profile is only interpretable if the buried individuals represent who was dying in the wider community.
comments.request: Caveat that bone or individual selection complicates the mortality profile.
comments.quote: I think it would be useful for the authors to caveat that if there was some selection of bones/individuals then the meaning of the mortality profile is difficult to discern.

comments.issue: “Genetically distinct” is too absolute given possible minor continuity.
comments.request: Use “genetically differentiated” instead.
comments.quote: is genetically ‘distinct; a bit too absolute? Genetically differentiated maybe?

comments.issue: A sentence about present-day family understandings is missing a phrase about anachronism.
comments.request: Complete the sentence to state the Western, present-day comparison.
comments.quote: I feel as though there is something missing from this sentence in terms of anachronistic project of present-day understandings of family.

comments.issue: “Exogenous individual” is not clearly defined.
comments.request: Clarify what counts as an exogenous individual.
comments.quote: How are the authors defining ‘exogenous individual’ here?

comments.issue: Higher parental relatedness in Phase 1 seems to run contrary to a large pan-European population collapse.
comments.request: Reconcile the relatedness pattern with the collapse narrative.
comments.quote: doesn’t the heightened frequency of parental relatedness in phase 1 compared to phase 2 run contrary to there having been a significant pan-European population collapse? Wouldn’t increased frequency of related parents be more likely in a smaller population?

comments.issue: It is not tested whether Phase 2 shows more short runs of homozygosity, as expected after a population decline.
comments.request: Compare short ROH frequencies between phases as an Ne indicator.
comments.quote: did the population from phase 2 show higher frequencies of shorter runs of homozygosity than phase 1, indicative of a smaller effective population size?

comments.issue: “Control” implies one interpretation although alternative access arrangements are plausible.
comments.request: Soften or justify the control interpretation.
comments.quote: ‘control’ implies a particular interpretation which I don’t think the authors have justified here

comments.issue: Uncertainties in pathogen DNA recovery and false negatives are not discussed enough for prevalence comparisons.
comments.request: Discuss pathogen recovery uncertainty and what pathogen rates can mean.
comments.quote: I think there really needs to be more discussion of the uncertainties involved with the recovery of pathogen DNA.

comments.issue: “Dark Age” is contentious and anachronistic, and “should be” is prescriptive.
comments.request: Reconsider the term and the prescriptive wording.
comments.quote: Therefore, ‘Dark Age’ is an entirely inappropriate and anachronistic term to use here and I think the authors should strongly reconsider their using it.

comments.issue: The pottery and technological skills claim is vague and unreferenced.
comments.request: Discuss and reference this claim properly, possibly in the Introduction.
comments.quote: The reference to the production of fine pottery and ‘other technological skills’ is an interesting component but given this is the first mention of this in the context of the Neolithic decline, it is extremely vague as well as being unreferenced.

comments.issue: The claim that burials ended around 3,100 BCE in northwestern France and central Germany lacks a citation.
comments.request: Add a citation.
comments.quote: ‘There is also evidence from megaliths in northwestern France and central Germany that burials ended around 3,100 BCE.’ This requires a citation.

comments.issue: The novel Bury results are too ambiguous to support the strong, wide-ranging conclusions drawn from them.
comments.request: Restrict the conclusions to what the new data can support.
comments.quote: the novel results from Bury are too ambiguous to substantially support the strong a and wide-ranging conclusions the authors come to here

reviews.assessment: Praises the integration and data quality but says the continental-scale population decline claim is asserted with more certainty than a single-site case study allows.
strengths: very solid archaeological and anthropological integration
excellent laboratory methodology and sample quality
case study is highly interesting and of sufficient quality for publication

comments.issue: Phases of a single burial site cannot define a continental population decline; the hypothesis is asserted too strongly.
comments.request: Present the continental decline as a hypothesis rather than a certain conclusion.
comments.quote: suggesting that the phases of a single burial site define the scope of a population decline at the continental level is a major claim. This is a hypothesis that can certainly be discussed but not asserted with the degree of certainty presented here.

comments.issue: The manuscript lacks line numbering for review.
comments.request: Include line numbering in the resubmission.
comments.quote: For resubmission, it would be advisable to include line numbering.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the decline refers only to collective burial or to funerary activity generally.
comments.request: Specify the scope of the decline referred to.
comments.quote: Specify whether the mentioned decline refers exclusively to “collective burial activities” or to funerary activity in general.

comments.issue: The tomb statement does not indicate cultural affiliations and could wrongly apply to other regions.
comments.request: Indicate the cultural affiliations of these tombs.
comments.quote: Indicate the cultural affiliations associated with these tombs for greater precision.

comments.issue: The Fleury-sur-Orne comparison is not integrated with the new Bury data.
comments.request: Integrate the Bury and Fleury-sur-Orne analyses.
comments.quote: Since Fleury predates both phases of Bury, it would be advisable to integrate these analyses with the new data obtained from Bury for a better comparison.

comments.issue: The phase-1 and phase-2 kernel density curves overlap, so the 100-200-year gap is not clearly supported.
comments.request: Show what results support the chronological gap.
comments.quote: The Kernel density calibration curve for phase 1 and phase 2 shows some overlap. What specific results support the existence of the 100-200-year chronological gap mentioned in the abstract?

comments.issue: Figure 1 is too large for its information content and lacks a geographical map.
comments.request: Reduce and combine it with a map showing Bury and comparable sites.
comments.quote: The image is too large for the amount of information it provides. It is suggested to reduce its size and combine it with a geographical map that includes the location of Bury and other similar sites or those co-analyzed in the study.

comments.issue: The differing hunter-gatherer ancestry levels between phases are not tested with admixture dating.
comments.request: Use DATES or similar software to assess admixture timing.
comments.quote: The authors are recommended to use DATES or similar software to assess whether phase 1 shows a more recent admixture with HG compared to phase 2

comments.issue: The PCA lacks other Neolithic individuals from France, Germany and southern Scandinavia.
comments.request: Add a supplementary PCA with these comparative populations.
comments.quote: The article could benefit from a supplementary PCA that includes other Neolithic individuals from France, Germany, and southern Scandinavia.

comments.issue: The individuals added to the GLIMPSE imputation dataset are not identified.
comments.request: Clarify which individuals were imputed.
comments.quote: Clarify which individuals were added to the customized dataset on which the GLIMPSE imputation was applied.

comments.issue: The clustering criteria are unclear and close relatives may bias broad-scale analyses.
comments.request: Explain the clustering criteria and whether close relatives were excluded.
comments.quote: Discuss the criteria for the clustering levels: are they based on the length or the number of IBD segments? Additionally, in a broad-scale analysis, shouldn’t close relatives be excluded to avoid biases?

comments.issue: Genetic clusters cannot be extrapolated to population-level continuity or discontinuity.
comments.request: Rephrase the distinct-communities claim more cautiously.
comments.quote: Even if they are different communities, this result cannot automatically be extrapolated to a population scale to claim continuity or discontinuity at population level.

comments.issue: Community discontinuity and population discontinuity/decline are distinct concepts that are conflated.
comments.request: Separate the community-level and population-level claims.
comments.quote: These are distinct concepts. Community discontinuity cannot be directly extrapolated to population discontinuity/decline.

comments.issue: The clustering method lacks statistical justification and tests of within-cluster relatedness.
comments.request: Add shared-IBD matrices and statistical tests of cluster relatedness.
comments.quote: Apply statistical tests to determine whether individuals within a cluster are significantly more related to each other than to individuals in other clusters.

comments.issue: Supplementary figures are misnumbered and Supplementary Figure 7.4 does not exist.
comments.request: Correct the supplementary figure numbering and add the missing figure.
comments.quote: All figures in Supplementary 5 and Supplementary 6 are numbered in the same way (Supplementary Figure 6.1 to 6.7), which causes confusion.

comments.issue: It is not stated whether ancestry modelling used qpAdm or supervised ADMIXTURE.
comments.request: State the ancestry modelling method.
comments.quote: Specify whether the ancestry modeling is based on qpAdm or supervised ADMIXTURE, as this information is missing from the methodology.

comments.issue: Iberian hunter-gatherers are a questionable proxy because their Pleistocene ancestry barely persists in the study regions.
comments.request: Justify or replace the Iberian hunter-gatherer proxy.
comments.quote: Explain why only Iberian Peninsula HGs were chosen as a proxy. These individuals retain more Pleistocene-Magdalenian-associated ancestry than Central European HGs, but the study focuses on the Paris Basin, Central Germany, and Southern Scandinavia, where this ancestry barely persists.

comments.issue: The origin of the hunter-gatherer ancestry resurgence is not tested with local proxies.
comments.request: Compare models using local hunter-gatherers from these regions.
comments.quote: To better interpret the origin of the HG ancestry resurgence, it is suggested to perform models using local HGs from these regions and compare the fit of both models.

comments.issue: The increase in hunter-gatherer ancestry between groups is not statistically tested.
comments.request: Add a statistical test of the ancestry increase.
comments.quote: A statistical test should be included to determine whether the increase in HG ancestry between group 1 and group 2 is statistically significant.

comments.issue: The absence of multiple sexual partners is not discussed relative to other sites where it is the norm.
comments.request: Cite and discuss this finding alongside Gurgy and Hazelton.
comments.quote: It is necessary to cite/discuss that no multiple sexual partners were identified in the analysis, similar to Gurgy (Rivollat et al. 2024), because it is not always the norm (e.g in Hazelton).

comments.issue: Individuals not connected to the pedigree in Supplementary Figure 6.3 raise doubt about what “exogenous” means.
comments.request: Clarify the definition of exogenous individuals.
comments.quote: The main text states that "we find a complete lack of any exogenous individuals (aside from the first generations)", but Supplementary Figure 6.3 includes individuals not connected to the pedigree. Are these individuals not considered exogenous?

comments.issue: Strontium data appear in the supplement but are unused and unmentioned in the main text.
comments.request: Remove the strontium data or integrate it into the discussion.
comments.quote: Sr data are presented in the Supplementary, but they are not mentioned in the main text. If they are not used in the analysis, they should not appear in the Supplementary

comments.issue: Untransmitted mitochondrial haplogroups indicate errors in pedigrees 2A, 2B and 2G.
comments.request: Review mitochondrial transmission consistency and correct the pedigrees.
comments.quote: Some mitochondrial haplogroups are not transmitted to the next generation, suggesting that certain pedigrees are incorrect (this occurs in pedigrees 2A, 2B, and 2G).

comments.issue: The Figure 6.3 legend is not descriptive and lacks age at death.
comments.request: Explain the symbols and haplogroup marking and add age at death.
comments.quote: The legend for Figure 6.3 should be more descriptive, clearly specifying what circles and squares represent and how mitochondrial and Y-chromosome haplogroups are marked.

comments.issue: Women at the end of pedigrees may reflect pre-reproductive mortality rather than female exogamy.
comments.request: Include age at death and discuss how it affects the exogamy interpretation.
comments.quote: if many women appear at the end of pedigrees, it could be due to pre-reproductive mortality rather than a female exogamy model

comments.issue: The male predominance is not discussed in relation to comparable sites.
comments.request: Discuss it alongside Flury and other sites with male burial bias.
comments.quote: The predominance of males could be discussed in relation to other sites, such as Flury, where a burial bias toward males has also been documented.

comments.issue: The claim of no exogenous individuals needs a more precise explanation.
comments.request: Explain precisely what is meant by no exogenous individuals.
comments.quote: The statement "This ties in with the observation that there are no exogenous individuals in the grave" needs more precise explanation.

comments.issue: More men than women falling outside the pedigree does not fit classic reciprocal female exogamy.
comments.request: Reconcile the sex pattern with the exogamy model.
comments.quote: In female exogamy contexts, many women are absent from pedigrees because their descendants are not buried at the site. However, in this case, more men fall outside the pedigree, which does not fit a classic reciprocal female exogamy model.

comments.issue: The degree of parental relatedness behind the ROH segments is not quantified.
comments.request: Use HapROH or similar to estimate the most probable parental kinship.
comments.quote: It would be useful to quantify the degree of relatedness required to generate this ROH percentage. It is recommended to use HapROH or similar to estimate the most probable kinship between the parents.

comments.issue: The parental relationship is not resolved through the paternal line despite differing mitochondrial haplogroups.
comments.request: Determine the most plausible kin relationship from ROH and haplogroup data.
comments.quote: Since the parents do not share the same mitochondrial haplogroup, it would be relevant to analyze whether their relationship is through the paternal line and determine the most plausible kin relationship based on ROH and haplogroup data.

comments.issue: The claim that Bury provides the missing support for population dynamics is too ambitious for a single site.
comments.request: Moderate this statement.
comments.quote: The following statement is too ambitious for an analysis based on a single site and should be moderated

comments.issue: The statement should present the study as a contribution to the debate rather than definitive proof.
comments.request: Rephrase to reflect a contribution, not proof.
comments.quote: It is recommended to rephrase this statement to reflect that the study contributes to the debate but does not constitute definitive proof regarding population dynamics in this period.

comments.issue: The text assumes a strong population discontinuity although the results show no clear break between phases.
comments.request: Add caution and avoid overgeneralising the case study.
comments.quote: Assumes a strong population discontinuity, whereas the results do not show a clear break between the two phases.

comments.issue: The claims are presented as definitive proof of a pan-European phenomenon rather than valuable case-study evidence.
comments.request: Reformulate the claims to avoid definitive pan-European conclusions.
comments.quote: It is necessary to reformulate both claims to indicate that the Bury data provide valuable evidence on potential demographic processes in the Late Neolithic but without presenting conclusions as definitive proof of a pan-European phenomenon.

title: Population discontinuity in the Paris Basin linked to evidence of the Neolithic decline

study.system: global coral reef planktivorous fishes; RLS surveys and fisheries catch data

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns that must be addressed before a revised version can be considered.

reviews.assessment: Global dataset yields impressive, robust results, but the nutritional and fisheries conclusions are significantly overstated.
strengths: global reef dataset contrasting abundance, biomass and size spectra
new mechanism linking fish communities to gelatinous zooplankton
results impressive and worthy of publication

comments.issue: Several findings are significantly overstated relative to the data.
comments.request: Reframe the results to sit within the data.
comments.quote: I found several findings to be significantly overstated, and suggest the authors consider reframing their results to better sit within their data.

comments.issue: The assumption that gelatinous plankton are more nutritious is not supported; dry-weight nutrition is equal and non-gelatinous plankton may deliver more nitrogen.
comments.request: Acknowledge the unresolved nutritional evidence or analyze it.
comments.quote: First, gelatinous plankton are considered more nutritious than non-gelatinous plankton (‘assumption’ in L73), but I don’t believe you have sufficient evidence (yet).

comments.issue: Counterexamples (Micronesia, Kenya) undermine the statement that fishing pressure in the Indo-Pacific spreads across more trophic groups.
comments.request: Qualify the generality of this statement.
comments.quote: These undermine statements such as “fishing pressure in the Indo-Pacific spread across more trophic groups” (L308).

comments.issue: Caribbean fisheries degradation is attributed to missing gelatinous planktivores while many social drivers are ignored.
comments.request: Acknowledge non-ecological drivers of Caribbean fisheries collapse.
comments.quote: that Caribbean systems have become degraded because of lack of gelatinous planktivores (L304). There are many social drivers of Caribbean fisheries collapse, not acknowledged here

comments.issue: Catch data come from one timepoint 35-55 years ago; the choice of 1970s-1980s data and its limitations are not discussed in the main text.
comments.request: Justify the timepoint and discuss limitations in the main text.
comments.quote: The catch data analyzed here are also from one timepoint, and collected between 35-55 years ago. Why did you choose to analyse data from 1970s and 1980s?

comments.issue: Fisheries results should be framed for the analyzed locations and years and linked to plankton-pathway dependence and non-ecological drivers.
comments.request: Reframe the fisheries discussion accordingly.
comments.quote: In a revision I would expect fisheries results to be framed for the locations/years you have analyzed, linked to dependence/importance of plankton pathways for fisheries

comments.issue: 'Nutrient poor' is not defined at L24.
comments.request: Define whether it refers to aquatic foods or ecosystem flux.
comments.quote: L24 - what does nutrient poor mean here? For aquatic foods or ecosystem flux?

comments.issue: 'Heavily fished' is not defined at L25.
comments.request: Define heavily fished and whether the comparison only applies to depleted fisheries.
comments.quote: L25 - what do you define as heavily fished? Is this nutrient-poor comparison only true for depleted fisheries?

comments.issue: Absence of planktivores is not what focuses fishing pressure; fisheries target the most productive and catchable components.
comments.request: Revise the unsupported statement.
comments.quote: it is not their specific absence that focuses fishing pressure on other pathways, rather that fisheries will develop to target the most productive, edible, and catchable components of food webs

comments.issue: Zooplankton should be defined early at L57.
comments.request: Define zooplankton early to avoid confusion.
comments.quote: L57 - define as zooplankton early on to avoid confusion

comments.issue: Differences between gelatinous and non-gelatinous zooplankton beyond water content (size, behaviour, swimming, composition) are not described.
comments.request: Describe these differences.
comments.quote: Besides water content, are there differences between non-gelatinous and gelatinous zooplankton? Body size, behaviour, swimming capability.

comments.issue: L75 implies nutritional value is explored, but only the gelatinous trait is measured.
comments.request: Clarify what is measured versus discussed.
comments.quote: implies this paper will explore nutritional value ~ productivity, but in fact you measure plankton trait (gelatinous/non), and discuss implication of nutritional value

comments.issue: Whether biomass per capita equals average body size and could account for abundance effects is not addressed.
comments.request: Consider this equivalence as an additional check.
comments.quote: Is biomass (g per capita, or biomass / abundance) mathematically equivalent to average body size? This might provide another way of accounting for abundance effects.

comments.issue: 'Fisheries' at L198 is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify whether fisheries for humans are meant.
comments.quote: L198 - fisheries for humans?

comments.issue: Wet-weight consumption implies much higher consumption rates for gelatinous feeders, which is not estimated.
comments.request: Estimate consumption rates using zooplankton water content or consider fatty acids.
comments.quote: but prey are consumed on a wet weight basis. So this implies higher consumption rates for planktivores feeding on gelatinous plankton

comments.issue: The research needed to detect the proposed mechanisms is not outlined.
comments.request: Suggest what research would detect these mechanisms.
comments.quote: what would we need to research to detect one of these mechanisms?

comments.issue: The oceanographic and evolutionary arguments are more developed than the fisheries ones but missing from the abstract.
comments.request: Reflect these arguments in the abstract.
comments.quote: oceanographic + evolutionary arguments are more well developed than those for fisheries, but missing from abstract

comments.issue: Past work on iron enrichment of Caribbean reefs from Saharan dust is not considered.
comments.request: Consider how iron enrichment fits the arguments.
comments.quote: Also consider past work theorising iron enrichment of Caribbean reefs from Saharan dust

comments.issue: Whether gelatinous-feeding planktivores can eat larger non-plankton prey is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the diet boundaries.
comments.quote: L362 - can gelatinous feeding planktivores eat other, larger non-plankton prey?

comments.issue: Traps generally do not catch planktivores because escape gaps are too large.
comments.request: Discuss this sampling limitation.
comments.quote: L452 - traps generally don’t catch planktivores (escape gaps being too large).

reviews.assessment: Interesting and enjoyable comparison, but reservations about dataset skew, diet characterization and the fisheries data reduce enthusiasm.

comments.issue: The Indo-Pacific versus Caribbean comparison is skewed (85 versus 1000+ surveys), so differences may reflect where surveys occurred.
comments.request: Address the sampling imbalance and its consequences.
comments.quote: I’m not terribly convinced that the IP vs Caribbean comparison is terribly meaningful given the huge skew in the dataset with only 85 surveys from the Caribbean but over 1000 in the IP.

comments.issue: The absence of gelatinous feeders in the Caribbean may be an artifact of how diets were characterized.
comments.request: Assess whether gelatinous items were overlooked in diet studies.
comments.quote: I was simply surprised that the Caribbean has no gelatinous zooplankton feeders when there are likely lots of gelatinous zooplankton in the Caribbean. How much is this an artifact of diet characterization?

comments.issue: The fisheries datasets are single-place datasets 40-50 years old, with n=1 in both regions.
comments.request: Reconsider or better justify the fisheries data inclusion.
comments.quote: I didn’t find the inclusion of the fisheries datasets especially compelling to the purpose of the paper given these are individual datasets from single places that are 40-50 years old.

comments.issue: Ecoregion is only a random effect although within-Indo-Pacific comparisons may be the more interesting focus.
comments.request: Explore ecoregion-level variation instead of or alongside the two-realm comparison.
comments.quote: I was bummed that ecoregion was just simply a random effect in their models as it seems like this could be the real interesting meat of the paper.

comments.issue: The opening paragraph about human societies does not reflect the paper's main idea.
comments.request: Refocus the setup paragraph on the paper's core ideas.
comments.quote: I found this setup paragraph a bit weird as this paper really isn’t about connections between human societies and reefs/fishes.

comments.issue: 'Abundance' is used without specifying whether density or biomass is meant.
comments.request: Define which abundance measure is used.
comments.quote: And by ‘abundance’ here do you mean density of animals? Biomass is also a measure of abundance.

comments.issue: Figure 2b units appear to be kg/250m2 instead of g/250m2.
comments.request: Correct the unit to match Figure 1b.
comments.quote: Should this be g/250m2 not kg/250m2? Seems like a typo as this should match the biomass Y axis from Fig 1b

comments.issue: Figure 3c medians do not obviously add up to the overall biomass in Figure 1b.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship, possibly by presenting means.
comments.quote: shouldn’t the data in 3c (non-gelatinous and gelatinous biomass) roughly add up to the data in 1b (overall planktivore biomass)

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the zeros at line 421 mean absence of planktivores or of gelatinous planktivores, and whether they show patterns.
comments.request: Clarify the zeros and examine patterns in them.
comments.quote: Seems like the zeros (absence of planktivores? or absence of gelatinous planktivores? that’s not clear) could be interesting in themselves.

title: Missing planktivore functions drive global variation in reef fish productivity

study.system: gut bacteria pairwise co-cultures; proteomics and metabolomics

editor_summary: Reviewers raise concerns before publication; R1 wants details on sample exclusion, statistical thresholds and data access, R2 wants clearer novelty relative to previous studies.

reviews.assessment: Valuable proteomics-informed contribution, but sample exclusion, interaction typing and reproducibility need clearer justification and data access.

comments.issue: Exclusion of 106 of 768 samples is substantial and the reasons are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the reasons for sample loss.
comments.quote: Out of 768 samples, 106 were excluded (~14%) is notable and warrants clarification.

comments.issue: Species dominance patterns in Figure 1H could be presented more clearly and intuitively.
comments.request: Add a 14 x 14 matrix of stacked bar plots or pie charts.
comments.quote: However, this information could be presented more clearly and intuitively. I suggest adding a 14 × 14 matrix of stacked bar plots or pie charts (to replace Figure S1F)

comments.issue: Findings are not compared with a related colony-shape co-culture study using similar stacked bar charts.
comments.request: Compare and discuss the findings in the context of that study.
comments.quote: It may be worthwhile for the authors to consider comparing and discussing their findings in the context of this study

comments.issue: Spatially resolved proteomics at colony-colony interfaces could reveal localized molecular responses.
comments.request: Explore spatially resolved protein extraction at colony interfaces.
comments.quote: would it be feasible to perform protein extraction specifically at the colony–colony interface to capture spatial interaction zones?

comments.issue: Positive and negative interactions and the five interaction types are not defined or quantified before Figure 1J-K.
comments.request: Define the interaction types and explain how they were quantified.
comments.quote: the authors should first clearly define how negative an positive interactions, as well as the five different types of ecological interactions – how were these quantified from the dataset?

comments.issue: Excluded low-yield samples may bias interaction classifications in Figure 1K toward underrepresenting some interaction types.
comments.request: Assess whether sample exclusion introduces ecological bias.
comments.quote: this could introduce bias into the conclusions presented in Figure 1K, as certain interaction types, especially those associated with low-abundance, may be systematically underrepresented

comments.issue: It is unclear whether statistical criteria or significance tests supported the interaction typing.
comments.request: Report statistical thresholds used for interaction classifications.
comments.quote: Were any statistical criteria or thresholds applied in combination with the ecological interaction typing?

comments.issue: 'Only identified in co-culture' lacks a replicate-level definition, risking stochastic detection artifacts.
comments.request: Define detection criteria and apply reproducibility filtering.
comments.quote: Could the authors clarify how “only identified in co-culture” was defined?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether GABA pathway protein levels were checked in the co-cultures.
comments.request: Annotate and check GABA pathway proteins using eggNOG or KEGG.
comments.quote: wondering if the authors checked the protein levels related to GABA pathways in the co-cultures

comments.issue: 'Genetic dark matter' section ends with general statements instead of hypothesis-generating exploration.
comments.request: Use COG, Pfam and GO annotations and dark-matter approaches to interpret these proteins.
comments.quote: This section would benefit from a more hypothesis-generating exploration of this ‘genetic dark matter’ rather than ending with general statements.

comments.issue: The proteomics raw dataset was not available to reviewers.
comments.request: Provide access to the raw proteomics data.
comments.quote: The authors should provide reviewer access to the proteomics raw dataset. I wasn’t able to find it in among the submitted files.

comments.issue: The four phyla mentioned on line 45 are not specified.
comments.request: List the four phyla.
comments.quote: These 45 include abundant and prevalent commensal species from four phyla, better expand what these four phyla are.

comments.issue: Rationale behind the selection of the 15 species is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how species selection was designed.
comments.quote: readers may wonder about the deeper rationale behind the species selection—for example, whether the selection was linked to diverse ecological interactions

comments.issue: 'Concatenated library-free approach' is inaccessible to non-proteomics readers.
comments.request: Rephrase or briefly explain the term at first mention.
comments.quote: The term “concatenated library-free approach” may be difficult to understand for readers who are not familiar with proteomics.

comments.issue: Claim about covering the proteome by mass lacks quantitative support and overstates.
comments.request: Tone down to 'is expected to capture the majority of the proteome by mass'.
comments.quote: lacks direct quantitative evidence from this study. To avoid overstatement, tone down as “is expected to capture the majority of the proteome by mass”.

comments.issue: 'Excellent coverage' and 'good coverage' labels are subjective.
comments.request: Clarify the basis or thresholds for these categories.
comments.quote: The terms “excellent coverage” and “good coverage” for different functional categories (e.g., enzymes, ribosomal proteins, transcription factors) are somewhat subjective.

comments.issue: Use 'metaproteomics' or, better, 'proteomics' consistently.
comments.request: Standardize the terminology throughout.
comments.quote: In addition, metaproteomics is usually used to analyze complex communities, so I would recommend that the authors use proteomics throught the text.

comments.issue: 'Somewhat uniformly distributed' is not rigorous and no clear distribution pattern exists.
comments.request: Revise the description of the distribution.
comments.quote: The phrase “and were somewhat uniformly distributed” is not a scientifically rigorous description.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and impactful co-culture study with well-supported conclusions; asks for a clearer novelty discussion and optional FBA analyses.
strengths: interesting and impactful in vitro co-culture experiments
novel combination of metaproteomics and metabolomics
conclusions well supported by the data
rigorous experiments and clearly written manuscript

comments.issue: Novelty relative to the crowded field of in vitro microbe-microbe interaction studies is not discussed.
comments.request: Add a discussion section positioning the work against prior studies.
comments.quote: The authors should include a section in the discussion that highlights the novelty of this work relative to other in vitro microbe-microbe interaction studies

comments.issue: CarveMe models were built but no metabolic modelling results (FBA) appear.
comments.request: Apply FBA to a few co-culture pairs to explore mechanisms.
comments.quote: Did you try to apply FBA to these co-culture systems to further validate/explore mechanisms?

comments.issue: 'Trophic levels' is inappropriate for bacteria; 'guilds' would be more accurate.
comments.request: Replace 'trophic levels' with 'guilds'.
comments.quote: You mention 'trophic levels', but would it be better to use the term 'guilds'?

comments.issue: Copy edit: 'mouse' should be 'mice' at line 26.
comments.request: Change 'mouse' to 'mice'.
comments.quote: line 26: change 'mouse' to 'mice'

comments.issue: Clustering of genes to assign functions to non-annotated proteins deserves more exploration.
comments.request: Explore this aspect further in the results and discussion.
comments.quote: This is another relatively novel aspect of your study to highlight -- the clustering of genes to identify putative functions to non-annotated proteins. Maybe you could explore this a bit more in the results/discussion?

title: Interspecies interactions drive bacterial proteome reorganization and emergent metabolism

study.system: brown algae; comparative epigenomics of chromatin across six species

reviews.assessment: High-quality comprehensive dataset; numerous specific suggestions on DNMT classification, transposable element regulation and methylation interpretations.
strengths: exciting new view of chromatin evolution in a fascinating clade

comments.issue: Manuscript is not in journal style, so it is unclear which figures are Extended Data; some central supplementary figures are hard to access.
comments.request: Clarify Extended Data designation and move central figures to the main text.
comments.quote: Because the article is not formatted according to the Nature Ecology & Evolution style, it is currently difficult to determine which figures correspond to Extended Data.

comments.issue: DNMT search used Blastp, which is problematic for this family and may miss DNMT4/DNMT5.
comments.request: Redo the DNMT search with HMMER and phylogenetic classification.
comments.quote: use a PFAM domain search with HMMER and include a phylogenetic analysis to classify these genes, as Blastp searches are problematic for this family

comments.issue: DN4MT in Figure 1A is undefined; the Marchantia 4mC enzyme is a bacterial lateral transfer and not representative of eukaryotic DNMTs.
comments.request: Define DN4MT and reconsider its inclusion.
comments.quote: Please specify what is meant by “DN4MT” in Figure 1A. I assume this refers to the 4mC methyltransferase reported in Marchantia

comments.issue: DNMT counts are wrong: humans have three DNMT3 members and Arabidopsis not seven MET1 orthologues; CMTs may be included.
comments.request: Correct the DNMT counts and classification.
comments.quote: humans have three DNMT3 family members (including the catalytically inactive DNMT3L), not four

comments.issue: Previous classifications of eukaryotic DNMTs are not cited, and MET1 nomenclature (DNMT1) is not followed.
comments.request: Cite the previous DNMT classification literature.
comments.quote: There are several previous publications classifying DNMTs in the eukaryotes, which could be helpful here (PMID 40712095, 36894681).

comments.issue: Whether loss of H3K9/H3K27 methylation is related to histone tail substitutions is not examined.
comments.request: Check histone tail residue substitutions in brown algae.
comments.quote: Is the absence of H3K9 and H3K27 methylation related to substitutions in the histone tail residues in brown algae?

comments.issue: Protein domain expansion within each family is not discussed; conservation and direction of domain architectures are unknown.
comments.request: Analyse and discuss domain architectures across the brown algal phylogeny.
comments.quote: there is no discussion in the main text of protein domain expansion within each family. Are these domain architectures conserved across the brown algal phylogeny?

comments.issue: What regulates transposable element expression is unclear; the Repeat category may include intragenic repeats.
comments.request: Analyse young intergenic TEs by class and viral insertions.
comments.quote: It would be useful to focus on relatively young long transposable elements located in intergenic regions (to avoid overlap with protein-coding genes) and assign them to known classes

comments.issue: Pairwise orthologue comparisons at line 238 do not match phylogenetic distance.
comments.request: Explain or correct the mismatch.
comments.quote: The pairwise comparisons do not seem to match phylogenetic distance: Upin appears closer to Esp7 than to Ddud or Dher, yet the number of orthologues with similar patterns is lower.

comments.issue: Silenced 'young' genes may be misannotations or transposable element fragments.
comments.request: Filter genes for known protein domains or expression.
comments.quote: Filtering for genes that contain a known protein domain (not typical of a transposable element) or have expression in at least one sample could reduce potential noise.

comments.issue: S. ischiensis is described as an ancestor, but it is the sister group with its own history.
comments.request: Correct the evolutionary relationship.
comments.quote: S. ischiensis is not an ancestor of brown algae but their sister group, with its own evolutionary history

comments.issue: Rejecting 4mC/6mA based on less than 5% methylation is weak; gene absence is stronger evidence.
comments.request: Link the negative results to absent 4mC and 6mA methyltransferases.
comments.quote: the statement that they represent “less than 5% global methylation” is not very convincing

comments.issue: Nanopore can overestimate non-CG methylation; CHG/CHH signals may be artifacts.
comments.request: Check whether CHG/CHH contexts form enriched islands.
comments.quote: Since Nanopore sequencing can overestimate non-CG methylation, genome inspection might reveal whether these contexts form enriched “islands.”

comments.issue: Hypermethylation in S. ischiensis is not placed in the broader context of independently evolved hypermethylated genomes.
comments.request: Add broader context and citations.
comments.quote: Placing this in broader context would help readers (e.g. PMID 20395474, 31726061).

comments.issue: Maintenance MET1 may not explain the hypermethylation; de novo DNMTs could be involved.
comments.request: Examine the DNMT repertoire of S. ischiensis more thoroughly.
comments.quote: it would be worth examining the DNMT repertoire of this species more thoroughly

comments.issue: Lack of H3K36me3-5mC correlation in cluster 2 genes is not noted; hypermethylation may be convergent.
comments.request: Note this discrepancy and the independent origin of hypermethylation.
comments.quote: There is also a striking lack of correlation between H3K36me3 and 5mC in cluster 2 genes, in contrast to animals.

comments.issue: Logic that widespread 5mC explains weak histone correlations does not follow; promoter 5mC does not imply silencing.
comments.request: Reconsider this argument and the silencing interpretation.
comments.quote: I do not follow the logic of the argument that this 5mC pattern explains weak correlations between histone modifications.

comments.issue: H3K4me3 may protect against methylation rather than demethylation being required for activation.
comments.request: Consider this alternative and test expression across stages.
comments.quote: H3K4me3 may protect against methylation, as in other eukaryotes, rather than requiring active demethylation.

comments.issue: Line 385 should note that vertebrate regulation includes H3K9/H3K27me3 and cite other hypermethylated genomes.
comments.request: Rephrase and add examples of hypermethylated genomes.
comments.quote: The vertebrate regulatory system includes H3K9 and H3K27me3, perhaps rephrasing this sentence and quoting other examples of hypermethylated genomes across the eukaryotes could be useful for the readers.

comments.issue: Line 407 should consider that H3K79me2 may be a byproduct of transcription rather than repressive.
comments.request: Present both possibilities openly.
comments.quote: here the authors could simply consider the two possibilities, that H3K79me2 is indeed repressive, or that it is a byproduct of transcription

comments.issue: Similarities with other multicellular eukaryotes, especially those with similar sex chromosomes, are not spelled out.
comments.request: Spell out these similarities in more detail.
comments.quote: perhaps it would be nice to spell out the similarities with other multicellular eukaryotes a bit more in detail, especially in species with similar sexual chromosomes

comments.issue: Title verb 'underlies' is too strong; a bottleneck and simplification could instead have caused the divergent landscape.
comments.request: Soften the title's causal claim.
comments.quote: perhaps “underlies” is a strong verb, as it is also possible that a bottleneck and simplification of hPTM in the ancestor before emergence of multicellularity was the cause of such a divergent chromatin landscape

comments.issue: It is unclear which species the term 'two ectocarpales species' refers to.
comments.request: Name the species included in this term.
comments.quote: You refer to “two ectocarpales species,” but it is not clear which species are included in this taxonomic term

comments.issue: Line 155 phrase 'were strongly associated with reduced gene expression' is unclear.
comments.request: Replace with 'were anticorrelated with gene expression'.
comments.quote: The phrase “were strongly associated with reduced gene expression” could be replaced with “were anticorrelated with gene expression” for clarity.

comments.issue: Figure 2A genome browser snapshots are difficult to read.
comments.request: Increase the vertical size of the snapshots.
comments.quote: The genome browser snapshots are difficult to read. Increasing their vertical size would help readability, as the resolution deteriorates when zoomed in.

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not remind readers what chromatin states S1, S2 and S3 represent.
comments.request: Remind readers what each state represents.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to remind readers what each chromatin state (S1, S2, S3) represents, as these labels are easy to forget.

comments.issue: 'Co-sexuality' at line 297 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain briefly what co-sexuality means here.
comments.quote: Please explain briefly what “co-sexuality” means in this context.

comments.issue: Loss of DNA, H3K9 and H3K27 methylation is not unique; Capsaspora owczarzaki is not mentioned.
comments.request: Add this comparative example.
comments.quote: The loss of DNA, H3K9, and H3K27 methylation is not unique among eukaryotes; similar cases occur, for example, in Capsaspora owczarzaki

reviews.assessment: Relevant study; one major confusion about H3K79me2 enrichment, plus several figure, title and legend issues.
strengths: interesting study relevant to chromatin and genome evolution researchers

comments.issue: Young genes may simply lack regulatory elements for activation, rather than arising in heterochromatic regions.
comments.request: Consider this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: I think young genes may not yet have acquired the regulatory elements to strongly activate their expression, which would turn their chromatin signature into a more active state.

comments.issue: Claims that H3K79me2 is broadly deposited over gene bodies and differs among organisms conflict with Figure S5.
comments.request: Reconcile the text with Figure S5 and explain the correlation analysis.
comments.quote: Based on Figure S5, H3K79me2 does not show any enrichment over gene bodies (negative Log2 ChIP/H3 input) except for the outgroup.

comments.issue: The intergenic and repeat enrichment of H3K79me2 is not illustrated with examples.
comments.request: Show examples of enrichment over these regions and discuss their function.
comments.quote: It could be helpful to show some examples of this enrichment over these regions, different to the one’s shown in Figure 2A

comments.issue: Title implies chromatin changes drive the evolution to multicellularity, which is not tested.
comments.request: Revise the title to reflect the content.
comments.quote: It gives the impression that the paper reveals chromatin changes that drive the evolution to multicellularity, which is not tested here.

comments.issue: Broad peak locations look incorrect in the Upin female tracks of Figure 2A.
comments.request: Check and correct the peak locations.
comments.quote: The location of some of the broad peaks that were called seem to be off in the tracks of “Upin females”

comments.issue: H4K20me3 is not discussed in section 2 despite an interesting male-female difference in Ectocarpus.
comments.request: Discuss the H4K20me3 pattern.
comments.quote: There is no discussion on H4K20me3 in section 2. This mark seems to show an interesting difference between male and female Ectocarpus according to Figure S5

comments.issue: Wrong figure reference at lines 202-203.
comments.request: Change the reference to Figure S5.
comments.quote: Line 202 and 203: I think it should be Figure S5?

comments.issue: Figure legends are minimal.
comments.request: Expand the figure legends.
comments.quote: All figure legends are a bit minimal and could be expanded to provide more information about the data shown.

reviews.assessment: Finds the first part novel and clear, but the sex-related conclusions are hard to follow and some results lack tests.
strengths: first part on the epigenetic landscape change is novel and clear
interesting work on a lineage with independent multicellularity

comments.issue: DOT1 family pattern is key to the findings but has no panel in the main figure.
comments.request: Add a DOT1 gene family panel to the main figure.
comments.quote: I think the DOT1 gene family pattern merits a panel in the main figure

comments.issue: Expression and domain sequences of the distinct DOT1 gene copies are not compared.
comments.request: Compare DOT1 copies' coding sequences and expression patterns.
comments.quote: some clues might be gained from comparing these gene copies’ coding sequences(or their critical protein domains), as well as their different expression patterns, if any

comments.issue: Association of H3K79me2 with expression lacks a statistical test and figure; 'highly expressed' is undefined.
comments.request: Provide the test, a figure, and the expression definition.
comments.quote: the association of H3K79me2 binding levels with gene expression levels. Note there are also no figure or table linked to this very important conclusion

comments.issue: Exact correlation values and matrices at line 157 are not shown.
comments.request: Show the exact values and matrices.
comments.quote: here need to show the exact values and matrices

comments.issue: Significance of proportion differences between sex chromosomes and autosomes in Figure 4A is untested.
comments.request: Test whether these differences are significant.
comments.quote: are these difference significant between sex chromosomes and autosomes?

comments.issue: S14/S12 are labelled 'active' but show low expression and H3K79me2 binding, implying silencing; H4K20me3 pattern unstated.
comments.request: Clarify the state definitions and report H4K20me3 in these states.
comments.quote: here S14 and S12 chromatin states were further defined as ‘active’ states, and they were highlighted as in the species Upin, that they show low gene expression levels and also bound by H3K79me2

comments.issue: Upin expression at states S14/S12 differs between Figure 2C (near zero) and Figure S3C (above zero).
comments.request: Clarify and correct the discrepancy.
comments.quote: the expression levels of Upin at state S14 and S12 are close to zero in white color. But this is different from Figure S3C, where the same two values look like higher than 0

comments.issue: Sex-chromosome chromatin comparison is detached from earlier results and lacks explanations or hypotheses.
comments.request: Link these patterns to prior work and ecological context.
comments.quote: these descriptive patterns seem to lack explanations or hypotheses to be accounted for

title: Evolution of a distinct chromatin regulatory landscape in brown algae

study.system: marine phytoplankton-associated bacteria; 16S sequencing, isolate genomes, coastal time series

editor_summary: Editor notes three reviewers find considerable potential interest but substantial concerns that must be addressed; a revised version would be considered if these serious concerns are addressed.

reviews.assessment: Solid, well-written work, but cultivation confounding means it does not really address the research question, and the FDN concept is likely misleading.
strengths: utmost respect for the authors' approach

comments.issue: The fraction of picked phytoplankton cells that failed to grow is not reported.
comments.request: Report the phytoplankton cultivation failure rate.
comments.quote: What fraction of the picked diatoms and dinoflagellates failed to grow, and how does this potentially affect the results? This is crucial information.

comments.issue: The fraction of phycosphere bacteria successfully cultivated and genome-sequenced is not reported.
comments.request: Report bacterial cultivation and genome-sequencing success rates.
comments.quote: Similarly, what fraction of the phycosphere associated bacteria were successfully cultivated on the agar media and had their genomes sequenced?

comments.issue: The results text barely describes the information contained in the figures.
comments.request: Describe the figure content more fully in the results text.
comments.quote: The figures are quite nice, but all the nice information in them is barely glossed over in the text.

comments.issue: The title implies environmental data, but the data come from laboratory cultures.
comments.request: Revise the title to reflect the culture-based data.
comments.quote: The title gives the impression that the data come from the environment, when instead they come from laboratory cultures.

comments.issue: The abstract is vague and omits the metabolic interaction findings.
comments.request: Add the major metabolic findings to the abstract.
comments.quote: the abstract is vague and does not really identify any metabolic interactions that are specific to bacteria that live in diatom or dinoflagellate cultures

comments.issue: Sequencing depth and ASV counts after low-abundance read removal are missing.
comments.request: Report sequencing depth and ASV numbers.
comments.quote: you must report the sequencing depth and how many ASVs were found in all the data after removal of low abundance reads.

comments.issue: Genera shared by diatoms and dinoflagellates may simply be enriched in F/2 cultures; no control for this confound.
comments.request: Control for or discuss the F/2 cultivation confound.
comments.quote: bacteria genera common to diatoms and dinoflagellates could also be organisms that are enriched in F/2 cultures in the lab. There is a major confounding factor in the data here, and no other data to control for this.

comments.issue: The FDN concept is likely an artifact of cultivation bias; the dataset lacks a phycosphere-vs-not contrast.
comments.request: Recast FDN claims as hypothetical or test with a proper contrast.
comments.quote: I do not find the concept of FDN bacteria useful, and even if it were, it is likely a result of confounding factors like cultivation bias

comments.issue: Isolate genomes' representativeness cannot be judged without linking the isolate and community datasets.
comments.request: Demonstrate the link between isolate genomes and culture communities.
comments.quote: in order to convince the reader that the 289 genomes from isolates are representative of the true population, you must show how these 2 datasets are linked.

comments.issue: Community composition results are not novel; the metabolic pathway section is the valuable part.
comments.request: Make the metabolic pathway results the focus of the paper.
comments.quote: All the community composition results are less impressive, in my opinion (and been done before).

comments.issue: The FDN pathway claims are stated too strongly given cultivation bias.
comments.request: Present the FDN pathway results as hypothetical.
comments.quote: I might consider changing the tone of this section to be more hypothetical

comments.issue: The L194-205 section is not useful and contains handwaving.
comments.request: Tighten or remove this section.
comments.quote: L194-205: not super useful (and lots of handwaving here).

comments.issue: The claim made on L210-215 was not accomplished by the study.
comments.quote: L210-215: I do not agree that the paper accomplished this.

comments.issue: Results and discussion are repetitive; community composition gets too much space.
comments.request: Merge results and discussion and focus on metabolic pathways.
comments.quote: I would suggest combining results and discussion (since a lot of the discussion is repetitive), and focus on the metabolic pathways more than the community composition data.

comments.issue: Cultivation biases affect the dataset; culture-independent metagenomics is proposed for future work.
comments.request: Acknowledge cultivation bias and consider culture-independent approaches.
comments.quote: This removes all cultivations biases (both bacterial cultivation, as well as the diatoms and dinoflagellates).

reviews.assessment: Interesting, novel combination of taxonomic and genomic analyses, but terminology, method detail and presentation need clarification.
strengths: analyses well designed to extract relevant signals
tests ecological relevance with external datasets

comments.issue: Phycosphere-associated bacteria are never defined in the introduction.
comments.request: Define phycosphere-associated bacteria in the introduction.
comments.quote: The definition of phycosphere-associated bacteria should be stated clearly in the introduction

comments.issue: Omics jargon is used without definition at first use.
comments.request: Define technical jargon at first use.
comments.quote: the authors should avoid omics jargon that is not clearly defined upon first use

comments.issue: The ecological rationale behind the chosen metrics and categories is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for metrics and categories.
comments.quote: explain more carefully the ecological rationale behind the choice of metrics and categories used.

comments.issue: Ecological implications and interpretation of results lack specificity.
comments.request: Be more detailed about the ecological implications.
comments.quote: The authors should be more detailed and specific in the ecological implications and in the interpretation of results.

comments.issue: Category and acronym names such as "genome superior" are not intuitive.
comments.request: Rename categories and acronyms more intuitively.
comments.quote: The authors could consider renaming some categories/acronyms to make them more intuitive

comments.issue: Some figure panels are overloaded and hard to interpret.
comments.request: Restructure dense figure panels to highlight key messages.
comments.quote: Some figure panels are difficult to interpret due to information overload; consider restructuring to highlight the key messages

comments.issue: No verification that washing removed unattached or loosely attached bacteria.
comments.request: Verify that washing eliminated non-attached bacteria.
comments.quote: However, did the authors verify that such non-attached bacteria were effectively eliminated during these washing steps?

comments.issue: Phycosphere definition excludes loosely or transiently attached bacteria that are also part of it.
comments.request: Justify the attachment-based definition and discuss excluded bacteria.
comments.quote: loosely attached, transiently attached, or chemotactic bacteria that "hover" in the phycosphere without direct attachment to phytoplankton cells may also play important ecophysiological roles

comments.issue: Growth in f/2 medium may select for fast-growing bacteria, biasing the community.
comments.request: Discuss whether f/2 growth selects for fast-growing bacteria.
comments.quote: Could this step select for associated bacteria that grow well under these conditions, potentially favoring faster-growing bacteria at the expense of those adapted to slightly different conditions?

comments.issue: How the sequenced strains were selected from the isolate collection is unclear.
comments.request: Describe strain selection and state the genome subset clearly.
comments.quote: How were the strains selected for sequencing? It should be made clear in the manuscript that the data presented on genomes are based only on a subset of the isolated strains.

comments.issue: Thresholds defining characteristic and fundamental genera are not justified.
comments.request: Justify threshold choices or test their sensitivity.
comments.quote: The criteria used to define characteristic and fundamental genera should also be better justified. What is the rationale for the thresholds used

comments.issue: The title does not mention the phycosphere.
comments.request: Revise the title to include the phycosphere.
comments.quote: the specificity and universality of bacteria associated with/in the phycosphere of globally distributed phytoplankton

comments.issue: The word "rigorous" is subjective and self-promoting.
comments.request: Avoid the term "rigorous".
comments.quote: Avoid the term "rigorous," since this is subjective and may come across as self-promoting.

comments.issue: "Associated bacteria" is undefined; apparently limited to physically attached bacteria.
comments.request: Define associated bacteria and justify excluding unattached taxa.
comments.quote: Define what is meant by "associated bacteria." Based on the isolation protocol in the Methods section, the authors seem to refer specifically to bacteria physically attached to diatoms.

comments.issue: The claim that phytoplankton species recruit distinct microbiota lacks references.
comments.request: Add supporting references.
comments.quote: The statement that "different phytoplankton species recruit distinct yet diverse phycosphere microbiota" needs supporting references.

comments.issue: R2 of 0.129 is modest; the clustering is overstated as significant separation.
comments.request: Clarify statistical strength versus significance and temper the wording.
comments.quote: An R² of 0.129 indicates only modest explanatory power. Authors should clarify statistical strength versus significance and avoid overstating the clustering.

comments.issue: Negative/positive connections and their difference from correlations are undefined.
comments.request: Define connection types and distinguish them from correlations.
comments.quote: Define what is meant by negative and positive connections. Also clarify the difference between "connections" and "correlations".

comments.issue: The conclusion about distinct bacterial populations is too vague.
comments.request: Specify how the dinoflagellate- and diatom-associated populations differ.
comments.quote: This conclusion is too vague. Please specify how the bacterial populations associated with dinoflagellates and diatoms are distinct.

comments.issue: The all-three-criteria rule for characteristic genera is not stated in Results.
comments.request: State the three-criteria rule in the Results section.
comments.quote: Specify in the Results section that a genus must meet all three criteria to be considered a characteristic genus.

comments.issue: The 1% relative abundance threshold may include ecologically minor taxa.
comments.request: Justify or test the 1% abundance threshold.
comments.quote: A 1% relative abundance threshold seems low. It could still include ecologically minor taxa.

comments.issue: Terms for co-occurrence patterns differ between text and figure and are undefined.
comments.request: Use consistent terms and define their ecological meaning.
comments.quote: Use the exact same term used in the figure (e.g., co-occurrence or conjunction) and define the ecological meaning of these terms.

comments.issue: The 3-10 µm particle sampling excludes larger phytoplankton and may not target cells.
comments.request: Justify the 3-10 µm particle size cutoff.
comments.quote: Mention that "particles" are not necessarily phytoplankton cells. Why were samples taken from 3–10 µm particles? Many diatoms and dinoflagellates are larger; a cutoff of 50 µm might be more appropriate.

comments.issue: Fig 2b does not allow easy comparison and lacks error bars.
comments.request: Redesign Fig 2b and add error bars.
comments.quote: Plotting bars for FL and PA attached bacteria side by side for each genus would help compare average relative abundance and frequency.

comments.issue: Fig 2c fluctuation rates cannot support strong conclusions; significance analysis and 104%/106% unclear.
comments.request: Expand the statistical analysis and explain the percentages.
comments.quote: It's not obvious that fluctuation rate data can be used to support any strong conclusion based on this plot. Please expand on the statistical analysis used to assess significance.

comments.issue: "Homogeneously selected" is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what "homogeneously selected" means.
comments.quote: L141–142: "Homogeneously selected" is unclear. Please explain. Fig 2d: Could the authors add error bars?

comments.issue: Fig 2d lacks error bars.
comments.request: Add error bars to Fig 2d.
comments.quote: Please explain. Fig 2d: Could the authors add error bars?

comments.issue: Streaking on full 2216 MB may cause culturing bias; selection of 289 of 3,270 strains is unexplained.
comments.request: Discuss culturing bias and genome selection criteria.
comments.quote: Comment on possible culturing bias due to streaking on full 2216 MB. How were the 289 genomes selected from the total 3,270 strains?

comments.issue: Gene set selection lacks rationale and references.
comments.request: Provide rationale and references for gene set selection.
comments.quote: How were the gene sets selected? Please provide rationale and references.

comments.issue: "Genome superior" is vague and implies superiority.
comments.request: Rename to "genome enriched" or "trait-enriched".
comments.quote: The term "genome superior" is vague and potentially misleading, since it suggests superiority.

comments.issue: Fig 3a displays uncharacterized genera despite using them as a reference group.
comments.request: Reconsider showing uncharacterized genera as reference.
comments.quote: Does it make sense to display uncharacterized genera if they are used as a reference group?

comments.issue: Ecological significance of gene sets with strong negative log2 fold change is not discussed.

comments.issue: Fig 3b is dense, dot sizes are unexplained, and colors are too similar.

comments.issue: Mantel p threshold differs between main text (p<0.01) and Fig 3b (p<0.05).
comments.request: Clarify the significance threshold used.
comments.quote: In the main text it is said that community-influencing gene sets are defined by Mantel'p<0.01 (L158), but the threshold used in Fig 3b is p<0.05—please clarify.

comments.issue: The 17-of-18 gene sets result is not specified.
comments.request: State that these are 17 out of 18 gene sets.
comments.quote: Specify that these are 17 out of 18 gene sets to strengthen the point.

comments.issue: How the interspecific interactions differ is not explained.

comments.quote: please elaborate on how these interactions differ and provide an example.

comments.issue: "Common adaptation strategy" is not defined.
comments.request: Explain what "common adaptation strategy" means.
comments.quote: Similarly, explain what is meant by a "common adaptation strategy."

comments.issue: Text calls T6SS dominance promoting for dino_FDN genera, but Fig 3b shows it is not significant.
comments.request: Correct or clarify the T6SS classification.
comments.quote: Based on Fig 3b, T6SS is not classified as "dominance promoting" for dino_FDN genera (not statistically significant). Please correct or clarify.

comments.issue: The L187-193 paragraph is too dense and figure references are sparse.

comments.quote: This paragraph is too dense. Consider breaking it into shorter sentences and refer more explicitly to figures.

comments.issue: T2SS behavior is not discussed.
comments.request: Comment on the specific behavior of T2SS.
comments.quote: Could the authors also comment on the specific behavior of T2SS?

comments.issue: Enrichment evidence lacks a negative control without phytoplankton.
comments.request: Compare enrichment against a no-phytoplankton control.
comments.quote: The correlative evidence would be stronger if it showed enrichment relative to a negative control (e.g., samples without phytoplankton).

comments.issue: Biological functions of the secretion systems are not clarified.
comments.request: Clarify the functions of the secretion systems.
comments.quote: Also, clarify the different biological functions of the secretion systems to help interpretation.

comments.issue: Biases from sample preparation and analysis are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss these biases in the Discussion.
comments.quote: The biases introduced by sample preparation and downstream analysis should be discussed somewhere in this section.

comments.issue: "Universal hallmark" claim needs discussion of T2SS, T4SS and T6SS functions and differences.
comments.request: Discuss the roles and differences of these secretion systems.
comments.quote: the claim that bacterial secretion systems are a "universal hallmark of phycosphere bacteria" would benefit from a discussion of the biological functions of these systems.

comments.issue: Fig 5 is too dense, key findings unclear, and symbols such as chains are confusing.
comments.request: Simplify Fig 5 and label terms directly on it.
comments.quote: it is currently too dense, and the key findings are not clearly represented. For example, the "chains" symbol is confusing as it implies a physical link between phytoplankton and bacteria.

comments.issue: Whether "convergence" means evolutionary convergence is unclear.
comments.request: Define convergence or add a phylogenetic analysis.
comments.quote: Clarify what is meant by "strong adaptive convergence with features of their respective host". Does "convergence" mean evolutionary convergence?

reviews.assessment: Interesting contributions, but it is unclear whether the phycosphere was actually sampled and the coarse diatom/dinoflagellate comparison limits interpretation.

comments.issue: Cell isolation likely loses all but tightly attached or intracellular bacteria, so the phycosphere may not be sampled.
comments.request: Justify that the protocol samples phycosphere bacteria.
comments.quote: The algal cell isolation process, while very robust for isolating algae, will likely lose all but tightly attached, or intracellularly located bacteria

comments.issue: Timing from isolation to sequencing, standardization, replication and negative controls are unreported.
comments.request: Report timing, replication and negative controls.
comments.quote: substantially more details on the time from isolation to when sequencing was performed is needed. There are currently no details about how long after the initial isolation the bacterial community was characterised.

comments.issue: It is not stated which isolation method was used for the NCMA dinoflagellates, raising comparability concerns.
comments.request: Specify the isolation method used for each isolate.
comments.quote: which of these was it?? Is there no standardisation of the methodology used here? If not, this really creates major questions about the comparability of samples.

comments.issue: Pooling all isolates into diatoms versus dinoflagellates ignores species- and strain-level microbiome differences.
comments.request: Analyze at species/strain level or justify pooling.
comments.quote: While 196 different phytoplankton isolates were used in this study, as far as I understand the results were then pooled into two groups (diatoms vs dinoflagellates) for comparisons.

comments.issue: Predefined interaction-focused gene sets make the observed patterns unsurprising; whole-genome comparison would avoid bias.
