comments.quote: L260: "These reports 10% of the butterfly species" <- I think a word is missing here

comments.issue: The species count attributed to Pinkert et al. is queried.
comments.request: Verify the species count.
comments.quote: L261: Didn't Pinkert et al. report 19,327 species?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the study pool includes null results and whether statements are proportional to study effort.
comments.request: Clarify whether null-result studies are included and whether statements are proportional to effort.
comments.quote: One thing that is unclear in the 'Global research effort in studying butterfly species range shifts section' is whether the pool of studies you are making statements about also includes studies that did investigate range shifts but documented no change

comments.issue: The 80% figure at L315 may be the same result as the 81% in the abstract.
comments.request: Reconcile the two percentages.
comments.quote: L315: Is this 80% the same result that is cited as 81% in the abstract?

comments.issue: It is unclear what the authors are comparing 'simplified as expansion or contraction' to.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison.
comments.quote: as opposed to what? I'm not sure what the alternative the authors are trying to compare to here.

comments.issue: The tropics warm more slowly, so species there need to move less to maintain their climatic niche.
comments.request: Consider this explanation.
comments.quote: the tropics are not warming as fast as temperate areas, so species don't have to move as far to maintain their climatic niche

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the estimate at L338-340 is specific to the tropics or global.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of the estimate.
comments.quote: L338-340: unclear if this is specific to the tropics or a global estimate

comments.issue: The motivation for using both Web of Science and Google Scholar is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for using both databases.
comments.quote: Methods: why use both Web of Science and Google Scholar? Authors do not explain the motivation behind the dual effort.

comments.issue: The term horizontal range shifts is unfamiliar and confusing in the abstract.
comments.request: Define the term or use latitudinal/longitudinal in the abstract.
comments.quote: I had not heard of the term horizontal range shifts before, so its mention in the abstract confused me as I interpreted it as a longitudinal range shift

reviews.assessment: Commends the compiled dataset but finds the analysis and interpretation lacking in rigour, depth and novelty.

comments.issue: The study is descriptive rather than hypothesis-testing despite much previous work to build on.
comments.request: Frame the study around testable hypotheses.
comments.quote: I thought the study would have been stronger had it been hypothesis-testing.

comments.issue: The literature review is inadequate and gives no background specific to butterfly research.
comments.request: Add background on butterfly research and cite the suggested papers.
comments.quote: the authors did not do a good enough job reviewing the literature. There was no background given for butterfly research specifically.

comments.issue: Variation in butterfly range shifts is not adequately described.
comments.request: Describe the variation in range shifts more adequately.
comments.quote: I also think they did not adequately describe variation in butterfly range shifts.

comments.issue: Vote-counting was used instead of meta-analysis despite its limitations and variation in effect magnitude and data quality.
comments.request: Use a meta-analysis or justify the vote-counting approach.
comments.quote: It's not clear why the authors used a vote-counting method instead of a meta-analysis. Vote-counting has many limitations.

comments.issue: The time frame of the data is not stated and may strongly affect the findings.
comments.request: State the time frame of the data.
comments.quote: What time frame is this data from? The time span can have many impacts.

comments.issue: Differences between English and non-English documents and between expert assessments and studies were not examined.
comments.request: Compare English/non-English records and expert/study assessments.
comments.quote: I found it surprising that the authors didn't look to see whether were was a difference in range shifts between English and non-English documents, or between expert assessments and from studies

comments.issue: What makes climate change impacts 'indirect' is undefined.
comments.request: Define what 'indirect' means.
comments.quote: why are climate change impacts considered 'indirect'? There are many ways of thinking about 'indirect', please define

comments.issue: The text at lines 230-231 needs elaboration.
comments.request: Elaborate this passage.
comments.quote: Line 230-231- Elaboration here needed

comments.issue: The claim that butterflies are under-represented taxa is incorrect.
comments.request: Correct this claim.
comments.quote: Line 240-241- Butterflies are not under-represented taxa

comments.issue: The claim that European records reflect genuine change and detectability while tropical records reflect scarcity lacks supporting evidence.
comments.request: Compare the types of data between the Tropics and Europe.
comments.quote: Not clear what evidence there is that the European reflects "both genuine changes and stronger detectability"

comments.issue: It is unclear whether regional diversity was accounted for in the estimates.
comments.request: Account for regional diversity in the estimates.
comments.quote: Line 265-267- Was the diversity of the region taken into account with these estimates?

comments.issue: Results are not contextualized with regional differences in temperature change.
comments.request: Contextualize results with regional temperature change.
comments.quote: The results were not put into context with regional differences in temperature change.

comments.issue: The implications of differences in taxonomic coverage are not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of taxonomic coverage differences.
comments.quote: What are implications of differences in taxonomic coverage?

comments.issue: Spatial patterns are defined by geopolitical boundaries, whose ecological relevance is unclear.
comments.request: Justify or reconsider the geopolitical spatial units.
comments.quote: What is the ecological relevance of the defining spatial patterns based on geopolitical boundaries?

comments.issue: The results are mixed and would be clearer if the percentage of the regional pool assessed were given before expansion and contraction percentages.
comments.request: Reorganise the results description.
comments.quote: Further, results are mixed and could be better explained. First describe, what % of country's regional pool have been assessed, then describe percentage of expansion, contraction.

comments.issue: The drivers section is not compelling without formal analyses, and how threat importance was evaluated is unclear.
comments.request: Add formal analyses evaluating the relative importance of threats.
comments.quote: without "formal analyses" as the authors themselves acknowledge, I don't find the section on drivers of range shifts very compelling

comments.issue: More rigour is needed when presenting integrated results, which currently lean on single-species examples.
comments.request: Support the integrated results beyond single-species examples.
comments.quote: more rigour is needed when presenting them as integrated results. The authors lean on single species examples.

comments.issue: The discussion lacks substance and depth and reads as a high-level summary of mitigation strategies.
comments.request: Deepen the discussion beyond a summary of mitigation strategies.
comments.quote: I found the discussion lacked substance and depth. Instead, it was a high-level summary of some mitigation strategies.

comments.issue: The framework is not novel, helpful or integrated with the paper, and no concrete integration of citizen science and local knowledge is proposed.
comments.request: Offer concrete ways to integrate citizen science data and local knowledge.
comments.quote: I didn't find the framework to be particularly novel or helpful, and it is disjunct from rest of paper.

title: Extensive climate-induced range shifts in butterflies across the globe

study.system: European vascular plants; SDMs and >1.1M vegetation plots

editor_summary: Editor highlights the reviewers' major concerns and the work's considerable potential interest; requests a major revision.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and novel analyses, but the disturbance-disequilibrium concept is not properly tested and the title claim is unproven.

comments.issue: Disturbance disequilibrium as analysed equates with static environmental filtering, not a tested disequilibrium.
comments.request: Contrast present with past disturbance regimes to demonstrate disequilibrium.
comments.quote: disturbance disequilibrium, as discussed here, seems to just equate with environmental filtering along a disturbance gradient

comments.issue: The test may reduce to the already well known result that disturbance filters species.
comments.request: Recast the analysis and title as climate disequilibrium depending on disturbance.
comments.quote: this defaults to addressing a question whose answer is already well known; that species are strongly filtered by disturbance

comments.issue: The title claim that disturbance dominates is not proven by the analysis.
comments.request: Recast the title and analysis accordingly.
comments.quote: the claim in the title of the paper is not proven to my mind at least

comments.issue: Lag patterns may be artefacts of uneven temporal and spatial sampling of occurrences.
comments.request: Use data through 2018 with randomised representative spatial and temporal sampling.
comments.quote: So could these patterns be artefacts of the varying temporal distribution of occurrences interacting or not with the spatial location of those occurrences.

reviews.assessment: Topical and generally convincing, but several major methodological concerns could affect the main results and conclusions.

comments.issue: Discussion is rather long for a journal like Nature Ecology & Evolution and could be more concise.
comments.request: Make the discussion more concise.
comments.quote: I also think that the discussion, while thorough and generally well-written, is rather long for a journal like Nature E&E and could be made more concise.

comments.issue: Model-inherent errors are not quantified, so all mismatches are treated as ecological disequilibrium.
comments.request: Quantify model-inherent errors via split-sampling and exclude poorly performing SDMs.
comments.quote: There appears to be no attempt to quantify or correct model-inherent errors (false presences and false absences) although certainly some proportion of the mismatches between SDM predictions and data must be attributed to model-inherent errors.

comments.issue: Disequilibrium is measured as performance gain over a weak static baseline SDM.
comments.request: Quantify disequilibrium directly from projection-observation differences without the static baseline.
comments.quote: I find this approach a little unsatisfactory because the static SDM arguably underrepresents the current best practices in SDMs.

comments.issue: Randomly permuted disturbance predictors artificially penalize climate-only SDMs by forcing them to fit noise.
comments.request: Drop the permutation and compare models with unequal predictor counts directly.
comments.quote: By incorporating randomly permuted variables in the climate SDMs (presumably, both static and dynamic), I think that the authors inadvertently may have artificially penalized the climate-only SDMs by effectively forcing them to fit noise

comments.issue: Calibrating and testing across a period of rapid climate change violates the quasi-equilibrium assumption.
comments.request: Calibrate earlier or train and test within the same period and be transparent.
comments.quote: The authors calibrated their SDMs using climate data from 1981 to 2003, but the climate, of course, was rapidly changing during this period due to climate change.

comments.issue: How disturbance is incorporated into the SDMs remains a black box.
comments.request: Explain the disturbance predictors, event definition and their incorporation in the SDMs.
comments.quote: how disturbance is actually incorporated into the SDMs remains largely a black box to me

comments.issue: Disturbance severity metric misclassifies focal-species declines as low disturbance.
comments.request: Consider including focal species in community-derived indicators or otherwise resolve it.
comments.quote: Sites with large reductions predominately in the focal species would be defined as low disturbance (i.e., little community biomass loss).

comments.issue: Spatial and temporal sampling biases are not acknowledged or evaluated.
comments.request: Statistically compare regimes between periods and discuss potential biases.
comments.quote: I think that spatial bias is particularly worrisome because we have no idea whether, for example, warmer or more disturbed sites happen to be observed more frequently in recent years

comments.issue: Niche truncation could force SDMs to extrapolate incorrectly to novel climates and disturbance regimes.
comments.request: Diagnose truncation, remove affected species and discuss the issue.
comments.quote: Niche truncation could certainly be an issue with the climate variables because climate change may expose species to novel climates in which a truncated SDM may incorrectly extrapolate suitability.

comments.issue: SDM decisions are unjustified and methods are not reported in a standard protocol.
comments.request: Justify modelling decisions and report SDMs using a standard protocol.
comments.quote: Generally, I suggest that the authors justify their decisions in building the SDMs whenever possible and ideally report their SDM methods in a more standard protocol.

comments.issue: It is unclear that presences and absences reflect climate suitability 18 years earlier.
comments.request: Justify the 18-year lag interpretation.
comments.quote: how do we know that presences really indicate that the climate 18 years ago was suitable or that absences indicate that the climate 18 years ago was unsuitable?

comments.issue: Line implies light and disturbance severity are both community-level metrics.
comments.request: Clarify which predictors are species-specific versus community-derived.
comments.quote: I thought that light values were species-specific, but disturbance severely was community-derived, but this line seems to imply that all are community-level metrics.

comments.issue: Main text gives too little detail about the SDMs themselves.
comments.request: State which algorithms and whether ensembles were used.
comments.quote: Very little detail is given in the main text about the SDMs themselves. What algorithms were used? Were ensemble models used?

comments.issue: Pairwise t-test wording is confusing when more than two models are compared.
comments.request: Reword the model comparison description.
comments.quote: I was initially confused why pairwise t-tests were used to compare models when there are more than two models.

comments.issue: TSS results in the Supplementary Information are not referenced.
comments.request: Reference the supplementary TSS analyses here.
comments.quote: The authors use TSS in addition to AUC in the Supplementary Information, but this is not obviously referenced in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Cohen's D reports effect magnitude but not the direction of the effect.
comments.request: Also report the direction of model performance differences.
comments.quote: Cohen’s D gives the magnitude of the effect size difference, but we also might care about the direction of the effect in this case.

comments.issue: 'Various species attributes' is vague and biologically unjustified.
comments.request: Explain why these attributes matter biologically.
comments.quote: “Various species attributes” is somewhat vague. Why do these attributes matter biologically?

comments.issue: Disequilibrium estimates are not scaled by total presences per species.
comments.request: Scale disequilibrium by total presences.
comments.quote: would it not be more appropriate to scale the disequilibrium estimates by the total presences to control for the fact that more widely-distributed (or sampled) species may just have more chances to exhibit disequilibrium?

comments.issue: Comparison subsets at line 175 may overlap when presences were predicted absent.
comments.request: Define precisely which plots enter each subset.
comments.quote: As written, it seems like there might an issue if plots where the species was present but was predicted to be absent were included in both subsets being compared.

comments.issue: Comparative statements often omit what is being compared to.
comments.request: Always state the full comparison.
comments.quote: It might be useful to always include the group being compared to when making a comparison.

comments.issue: Sample size behind Figure 1 is not explicitly reported.
comments.request: Report the number of species in each SDM type.
comments.quote: Were 3,037 species included in each type of SDM shown in Figure 1. I would just explicitly report the sample size here.

comments.issue: Temperature annual range is not defined.
comments.request: Define the temperature annual range variable.
comments.quote: Line 216: What exactly is temperature annual range?

comments.issue: Figure panels are not referenced in results paragraphs.
comments.request: Reference the appropriate figure panels throughout.
comments.quote: I would reference the appropriate figure panels in this paragraph.

comments.issue: 'In the full model' could be confused with the full climate-plus-disturbance SDM.
comments.request: Clarify the terminology.
comments.quote: This could be confusing if one conflates the full statistical model with the “full” SDM incorporating both climate and disturbance.

comments.issue: Analyses including multicollinear variables that were then excluded are hard to interpret.
comments.request: Report only models with the collinear variables removed.
comments.quote: With multicollinearity, I am not sure how relevant the analyses are that include these two variables.

comments.issue: Nonlinear terms are included for some Figure 2 variables but not others without justification.
comments.request: Justify which variables get nonlinear terms.
comments.quote: Why do some variables include a nonlinear term and others do not?

comments.issue: Figure 2 labels have a potential red-green colourblindness problem.
comments.request: Use colourblind-safe labels.
comments.quote: Also, there is a potential red-green colorblindness issue here with the labels.

comments.issue: Numbers of over- and underpredictions are not reported.
comments.request: Report counts of overpredictions versus underpredictions.
comments.quote: “Primarily reflected overpredictions” is vague. How many overpredictions versus underpredictions were there?

comments.issue: The lags subsection placement is unclear and disrupts the paper's focus.
comments.request: Justify the rationale or move the section to Supplementary Information.
comments.quote: As is, my opinion is that this section should be moved to the Supplementary Information to focus the paper concisely around the topic of climate- and disturbance-driven disequilibrium.

comments.issue: Key findings of the detailed lag-window results paragraph are difficult to distill.
comments.request: Clarify the general insight of this paragraph.
comments.quote: I found it difficult to distill the key findings from this paragraph.

comments.issue: Figure 4b appears to show the static climate model performing best for most species, contradicting the text.
comments.request: Reconcile Figure 4b with the claim that older windows perform best.
comments.quote: Figure 4b seems to show that, for most species, the static climate model was best performing

comments.issue: Rationale and hypothesis for the trait-lag analysis are not stated.
comments.request: State the hypothesis being tested.
comments.quote: I do not fully understand the rationale for this analysis. What is the hypothesis being tested here?

comments.issue: Reason for excluding plots from certain countries is not given.
comments.request: Justify the country exclusions.
comments.quote: Lines 490-491: Why were plots in these countries excluded?

comments.issue: Plots lacking coordinate uncertainty information were retained.
comments.request: Consider excluding such plots or justify retaining them.
comments.quote: Why were plots without coordinate uncertainty information retained? Would it not be more cautious to exclude them?

comments.issue: Taxonomic names may not have been harmonized.
comments.request: Harmonize taxonomy, for example with WorldFlora.
comments.quote: Were any attempts made to harmonize the taxonomic names?

comments.issue: Choice of a fairly coarse climate dataset is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the climate dataset choice.
comments.quote: Why was this climate dataset used? The spatial resolution is fairly coarse (which the authors acknowledge).

comments.issue: Climate variables are not explained for general readers.
comments.request: Briefly explain the climate variables.
comments.quote: I would briefly explain some these variables for general readers (e.g., mean diurnal range, isothermality, temperature/precipitation seasonality, frost change frequency).

comments.issue: Eight climate variables risk overfitting the SDMs.
comments.request: Justify variable selection and reduce to 2-4 predictors.
comments.quote: I think that 8 variables is a lot and that the authors risk overfitting the SDMs.

comments.issue: Whether spatial thinning applied to both training and testing data is unclear.
comments.request: State whether both datasets were thinned.
comments.quote: Presumably, spatial thinning was done for both the testing and training datasets, right?

comments.issue: Presence thresholds of 35 training and 10 testing records are not justified.
comments.request: Justify the thresholds, e.g. against the 10-per-predictor heuristic.
comments.quote: One fairly common heuristic is 10 presences per predictor variable, which would yield a much higher threshold of 80 presences for the current SDMs.

comments.issue: The 300 km distance threshold is arbitrary and unjustified.
comments.request: Justify the 300 km threshold.
comments.quote: Why was 300km uses as a distance threshold?

comments.issue: Justification for 5-year moving windows, rather than longer windows, is missing.
comments.request: Justify the moving-window length.
comments.quote: 5-year moving windows seem reasonable, but it there justification for using say 11-year windows that might better capture decadal variation at the demographic scale of these long-lived plants?

comments.issue: It is unclear why 30% of training data was set aside but never used.
comments.request: Explain the 70% training subset.
comments.quote: Why were models trained on a 70% subset of the data from the training bin when, as far as I can tell, the remaining 30% of the data was not used at all?

comments.issue: Only GAMs were used without justification; parameter settings unstated.
comments.request: Justify GAM-only models and report parameter values.
comments.quote: Why were only GAMs used? Were standard parameter values used in the GAMs?

comments.issue: The rationale for not binarizing projections with the TSS threshold is not followed.
comments.request: Explain the decision more clearly.
comments.quote: The rational for not binarizing projections based on the threshold that maximized the TSS score has clearly been thought out, but I do not fully follow the logic here.

comments.issue: Elevation data resolution may not match the climate data.
comments.request: Confirm the elevation resolution.
comments.quote: Does the spatial resolution of the elevation data match that of the climate data?

comments.issue: Why only some variables were suspected to have unimodal relationships is unclear.
comments.request: Justify variable-specific unimodal relationships.
comments.quote: Why where these variables suspected to have unimodal relationships and not other variables?

comments.issue: Whether re-sampled sites are excluded is unclear and should appear earlier.
comments.request: Clarify the treatment of re-sampled sites in the Methods.
comments.quote: Does this mean that re-sampled sites are excluded from the dataset or simply that they could not use only re-sampled sites because there are far too few of them

comments.issue: Definition of significant disequilibrium is not given.
comments.request: Define significant disequilibrium.
comments.quote: Line 694: What exactly is meant by significant disequilibrium?

comments.issue: Number of species with climate disequilibrium does not match Figure 4c counts.
comments.request: Reconcile text numbers with Figure 4c categories.
comments.quote: There are 1,434 species with significant climate-change disequilibrium, but Figure 4c shows way more species than this in the “null” category alone.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and methodologically solid study with broad interest; mostly minor suggestions to aid interpretation and presentation.

comments.issue: Consistency of climate trends and variability across periods and regions is not discussed.
comments.request: Add a statement on climate trends and inter-annual variability.
comments.quote: Is the nature and rate of change in climate consistent across both the training and testing periods and across the study region?

comments.issue: AUC gains are not translated into changes in species range size.
comments.request: Quantify range-size change from including lags or disturbance indicators.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to complement the results based on changes in AUC with quantifying the (total or proportional) change in the species’ range size associated with the inclusion (or exclusion) of climatic lags and/or disturbance indicators?

comments.issue: Figure 3 colours are hard to distinguish with overlapping points.
comments.request: Improve colour scheme or plotting arrangement.
comments.quote: The colours used in Fig. 3 are difficult to distinguish, especially with many overlapping points; increasing the size of the symbols in the legend would be useful

comments.issue: Peak at intermediate disturbance values is not visualized.
comments.request: Add a scatterplot of selected Figure 2 results.
comments.quote: I would encourage the authors to consider visualizing a selection of the results from Fig. 2 as a scatterplot

comments.issue: Spatial patterns in the proportion of species with significant disequilibrium are untested.
comments.request: Test for spatial patterns in disequilibrium proportions.
comments.quote: Is there any spatial pattern in the proportion of species that show significant disequilibrium?

comments.issue: Expansion of the ideas beyond Europe is not speculated about explicitly.
comments.request: Add hypotheses about other regions, taxa and disturbance types.
comments.quote: Some more speculation about the expansion of these ideas beyond the European context could benefit the manuscript

comments.issue: Plot density and disturbance indicator distributions are not visualized.
comments.request: Add a supplementary map of plot and indicator distributions.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to see a visualization of the distribution (or density) of vegetation plots, and of the different disturbance indicators

comments.issue: Citations to previous studies on this question, including outside temperate ecosystems, are missing.
comments.request: Add relevant citations.
comments.quote: Providing citations to point readers to previous studies that have addressed this question (e.g. outside of temperate ecosystems) would be useful here.

comments.issue: Motivation for an expectation at lines 165-167 is not clear.
comments.request: Strengthen the motivation.
comments.quote: The motivation for this expectation is not clear from the preceding text, and should likely be strengthened

comments.issue: Motivation for expecting open-habitat species to show strongest disequilibrium is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the biological reasoning.
comments.quote: Similar to the previous comment, the motivation for why species associated with open habitats would show the strongest disequilibrium is not clear.

comments.issue: Temporal shifts in species-habitat associations are raised but never addressed.
comments.request: Expand on this idea later in the manuscript.
comments.quote: The concept of “temporal shifts in observable species-habitat associations” is raised here, but not addressed subsequently in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Spatial concentration may just reflect the distribution of adequately sampled species.
comments.request: Check against sampling coverage.
comments.quote: Does this spatial concentration just reflect the distribution of adequately sampled species?

comments.issue: 'The dominant force shaping plant distributions' is ambiguous.
comments.request: Reword to distinguish disturbance from climate-change disequilibrium.
comments.quote: “the dominant force shaping plant distributions” is a bit ambiguous here; rewording to reflect that disturbance disequilibrium is more influential than climate change disequilibrium would help avoid confusion.

comments.issue: The threshold trait-habitat idea is not further examined.
comments.request: Describe trait values around maximum-disequilibrium disturbance levels.
comments.quote: for example, what trait values (or habitat associations) do the data suggest occur around the disturbance levels associated with maximum disequilibrium?

comments.issue: Citation context is missing because the cited paper does not concern climate disequilibrium.
comments.request: Add context distinguishing what the citation supports.
comments.quote: the authors might consider adding some context when citing Salguero-Gómez et al. (2016) here, as that paper does not deal with climate change disequilibrium

comments.issue: Lines 415-416 mix this study's findings with previous studies' findings.
comments.request: Reword to separate own and previous findings.
comments.quote: the authors should consider rewording lines 415-416, as the current wording mixes the findings from this study

comments.issue: Several suggested ideas are not explained enough for readers to assess.
comments.request: Add explanation and detail, e.g. about disturbance-adapted traits and lags.
comments.quote: In all cases, very interesting ideas are suggested by the authors, but no further explanation or detail is provided for a reader to assess the ideas.

comments.issue: 'Near-surface' is not defined in the climate data description.
comments.request: Clarify what near-surface refers to.
comments.quote: it would be useful here to clarify what “near-surface” refers to.

comments.issue: 'Species aggregate values' is unexplained for readers unfamiliar with the dataset.
comments.request: Explain the term.
comments.quote: For readers unfamiliar with this dataset, consider explaining what it meant by “species aggregate values”.

comments.issue: Reference 68 does not support the statement about macro- versus micro-climatic soil effects.
comments.request: Add a suitable reference or reword the sentence.
comments.quote: Consider adding another reference or rewording this sentence slightly, since reference 68 does not deal with how soil moisture or nutrients are more strongly related to macro- than micro-climatic conditions.

comments.issue: The basis of significance for the line 694 statement is not stated.
comments.request: State that significance comes from the pairwise t-tests.
comments.quote: Consider explicitly stating that this is based on significance as assessed by the pairwise t-tests.

title: Disturbance regimes drive widespread plant range disequilibrium in Europe alongside climate change

study.system: Drosophila wing shape; lab fitness assay; OU model

editor_summary: Editor forwards Reviewer 2's correction: in comment 3, 'is an artifact like the scaling relationship' should read 'is not an artifact'.

reviews.assessment: Strong, thought-provoking study, but the low Ne estimates, unaddressed size/allometry effects, and the crossveinless argument raise major concerns.
strengths: important contribution to explaining wing-shape stasis
appropriately acknowledges the issue is not fully resolved

comments.issue: The assumed Ne of 142 seems implausibly low for drosophilids and lacks empirical support.
comments.request: Justify the low Ne estimates with empirical evidence.
comments.quote: Are these effective population size estimates truly biologically “reasonable”, as stated on line 38? To me, the reported Ne values seem extremely low for drosophilids.

comments.issue: Crossveinless phenotypes may be non-genetic aberrations (environmental or somatic), weakening the pleiotropy argument.
comments.request: Test whether crossveinless phenotypes are genetic or non-genetic.
comments.quote: The absence of crossveins can result from mutations, but it is likely to represent a non-genetic aberration.

comments.issue: Procrustes does not remove size-shape covariance, so selection on body and wing size may distort shape-selection estimates.
comments.request: Clarify how selection on size and allometry is accounted for.
comments.quote: Procrustes analysis brings all variables to the same scale, but it does not remove the covariance between (centroid) size and shape.

comments.issue: It is not stated which traits enter the selection analysis as covariates, so direct versus indirect selection is unclear.
comments.request: State explicitly which traits are included as covariates.
comments.quote: it would help to be explicit about which traits are included as covariates in the selection analysis (i.e., being explicit whether this is direct or indirect selection after taking size into account)

comments.issue: The decline in stabilizing selection strength with eigenvector rank may reflect measurement error or limited power.
comments.request: Assess this potential artifact of measurement error and power.
comments.quote: Could the decrease in the strength of stabilizing selection with increasing rank of the eigenvectors be explained by measurement error or limited statistical power

comments.issue: The alignment between the new eigenvectors and Houle et al.'s leading axes is not demonstrated explicitly.
comments.request: Compare the eigenvector structure with Houle et al.'s.
comments.quote: How similar is the original eigenvector structure compared to Houle et al.’s? How comparable are the leading axes?

comments.issue: Lab-adapted flies and lab fitness measurements limit ecological interpretation of the results.
comments.request: Discuss how lab results relate to natural field conditions.
comments.quote: The population is lab-adapted and fitness is measured under laboratory conditions. How do these patterns relate to natural field conditions?

comments.issue: The number of drosophilid generations per year is asserted without a citation.
comments.request: Provide a reference for the generation number.
comments.quote: please provide a reference for the estimated number of generations of drosophilids per year

comments.issue: The manuscript lacks a strong integrative closing paragraph.
comments.request: Add a stronger concluding paragraph.
comments.quote: I suggest adding a stronger, more integrative concluding paragraph that would help emphasize the broader implications and leave the reader with a clearer take-home message.

comments.issue: Figure 2 x-axis uses eigenvector rank rather than proportion of variance explained.
comments.request: Plot selection coefficient against variance explained.
comments.quote: consider plotting the selection coefficient against the proportion of variance explained for each matrix rather than against eigenvector rank

comments.issue: The legend in Figure 2 panel B overlaps the data.
comments.request: Move the legend.
comments.quote: In panel B (which is stunning!), please move the legend so that it does not overlap with the data.

reviews.assessment: Valuable new selection estimates that complement prior work; comments focus on presentation and connections to earlier studies.
strengths: complements previous work with new data and analyses
valuable insights into difficult-to-explain evolutionary patterns

comments.issue: Figure 2A cannot show proportionality because its x-axis is principal-component rank, not variance.
comments.request: Include plots with variances as x-axes.
comments.quote: It is not clear from Fig. 2A, however, if the relationship is “proportional”, as the X-axis is rank order of principal components rather than variance.

comments.issue: No statistic (e.g. correlation coefficient) supports the verbal proportionality claim.
comments.request: Add a statistic describing the relationship.
comments.quote: It is also desirable to have a statistic that describes the relationships (e.g., correlation coefficient) to give more support for the verbal description.

comments.issue: Calling the G, M and R patterns 'the same' overstates their qualitative similarity in Figure 2A.
comments.request: Soften the claim or explain the apparent differences.
comments.quote: In Fig. 2A, however, there appears to be some difference despite qualitative similarity. The patterns, presumably, should not be considered “the same”

comments.issue: The expectation that selection on distance from the mean produces the variance-selection pattern is neither derived nor explained.
comments.request: Present or cite the theoretical expectation linking the model to the pattern.
comments.quote: In Methods, I only found how strength of selection was estimated (line 227-238) and how the model fitting was done (line 240-258), but not theoretical expectations/predictions that would bridge the two results.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 'amount of variance' means phenotypic, mutational or genetic variance in the model's prediction.
comments.request: Clarify which variance the prediction refers to.
comments.quote: it is not said explicitly either if the “amount of variance” in line 91 refers specifically to phenotypic, mutational, or genetic variance

comments.issue: The reported M versus G/R matrix similarity from Houle et al. (2017) is exaggerated by a biased comparison method.
comments.request: Mention this caveat where the result is cited.
comments.quote: the reported similarity between the M matrix and G or R matrices, which is mentioned in line 71-74, is exaggerated due to their biased method for matrix comparison

comments.issue: Houle et al. (2020) acknowledged that their original matrix-comparison method is not informative; this is not mentioned.
comments.request: Cite Houle et al. (2020) on this point.
comments.quote: Houle et al. later proposed an alternative way of matrix comparison in a preprint, but in the same manuscript they also acknowledged that their original method is not informative

comments.issue: The low evolutionary divergence motivating the study should be clarified as not being an artifact.
comments.request: Clarify that the present study is not affected by this artifact.
comments.quote: so it may be desirable to also clarify that the present study is “safe”

comments.issue: Jiang and Zhang's (2020) mutational-variance scaling relationship is consistent with this study but not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention this prior result around lines 112-117.
comments.quote: The scaling relationship between mutational variances and evolutionary rates of wing shape traits reported in Jiang and Zhang (2020), which was interpreted as that phenotypic dimensions with more mutational variance were under stronger (apparent) stabilizing selection

comments.issue: Jiang and Zhang (2020) proposed an apparent-stabilizing-selection explanation but could not test it; this connection is missing.
comments.request: Mention this near lines 105-106.
comments.quote: They demonstrated using simulations that such a model can reproduce observed patterns, but could not directly test if the same mechanism did contribute to fly wing evolution

comments.issue: 'Evolvability' is used as a synonym for additive genetic variance, which is conceptually wrong.
comments.request: Use 'additive genetic variance' or 'phenotypic variance' instead.
comments.quote: I consider evolvability as a property that is affected by many factors including genetic and phenotypic variances and thus not a synonym of the latter.

comments.issue: Cheverud (1984), an early theory paper linking variation to developmental constraints, is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Cheverud (1984) here.
comments.quote: Cheverud (1984) would be relevant to cite here, as it was an early theory paper that connected variation to developmental constraints.

comments.issue: The 'selection line of least resistance' idea (Arnold, 2023) is relevant but not cited.
comments.request: Cite Arnold's idea here.
comments.quote: There has been some hypothesis about this though, and the idea of a “selection line of least resistance” may be relevant to cite here

comments.issue: Figure 2A is hard to read with four overlapping datasets, three in transparent colour.
comments.request: Plot the four datasets separately side by side.
comments.quote: I find it a bit difficult to read Fig. 2A with four sets of data points put together and three of them (G, M, R) in somewhat transparent color.

comments.issue: 'glmm' is used without expansion, and abbreviations are inconsistently capitalised.
comments.request: Expand glmm/GLMM at first use and use capitals.
comments.quote: I think it is better to note that “glmm” means “generalized linear mixed model” when it appears for the first time (line 96), in case readers get confused.

title: Apparent stabilizing selection explains micro- and macroevolution of Drosophila wings

study.system: virtual species simulations; SDMs and population models

editor_summary: Editor: two reviewers find the work of potential interest but raise substantial concerns; a revised version addressing the criticisms is invited.

reviews.assessment: Important message, but unconvinced that the simulation methods are the most appropriate demonstration.

comments.issue: A beta regression fitted to bounded data can never be linear; a formal comparison against a linear model is missing.
comments.request: Show that the non-linear model fits better than a linear one.
comments.quote: Fine, but since you fitted your data with a beta regression model, it could never have been linear! A more convincing argument would be to show first that it fits better than a linear one.

comments.issue: Explanations about non-linearity and individual distributions are overinterpreted because the curve shape was imposed by the statistical model.
comments.request: Extract actual individual distributions from the simulations as empirical support.
comments.quote: I believe this is a bit of an overinterpretation since it is based on the shape of a curve that is just derived from a statistical model that itself imposed a non-linear relationship.

comments.issue: Range-shifting species become threatened only after they stop shifting, so the short warning time may be an artefact of the setup.
comments.request: State this clearly and test cases with more room for shifts.
comments.quote: from what I understand, these species become threatened precisely because at some point they cannot shift their range anymore (i.e. they shift up to the ‘northern’ boundary then get extinct because of a lack of suitable habitat, just like range contracting species)!

comments.issue: The added value of using SDMs is unclear when simulations already provide full distributions, and the role of ecological knowledge is not investigated.
comments.request: Justify the SDM component of the design.
comments.quote: Finally, my last major comment is that I don't really see the point of using SDMs here. Isn't all the information regarding species distributions already available just based on the simulations?

comments.issue: The claim that SDMs overpredict future range size by omitting dispersal limitation is not necessarily true; no-dispersal projections and microclimate refugia predict underpredictions.
comments.request: Qualify the statement about SDM overprediction.
comments.quote: I don’t think this is necessarily true. It is possible to project SDM predictions while assuming that no dispersal will take place, i.e. modelling range loss only.

comments.issue: The number of virtual species and simulation scenarios is not stated early as a sample size.
comments.request: Report the number of species and scenarios at the start.
comments.quote: L 93: you should probably write from the start how many virtual species / simulation scenarios you computed. This is a measure of sampling size that should be immediately available to readers.

comments.issue: 'Landscape' is defined by climatic conditions, which is unusual in ecology.
comments.request: Use the term landscape more carefully or define it explicitly.
comments.quote: L 96, 114, 124, etc.: Be careful with your use of landscape, here they are defined by climatic conditions, which is unusual in ecology.

comments.issue: Figure 4 does not make clear whether results are from simulations or SDM estimates.
comments.request: Clarify what Figure 4 shows.
comments.quote: Fig 4: this is unclear if you show results from the simulations or estimates from SDMs.

comments.issue: The numbers and statistics supporting the classification-time statement are missing.
comments.request: Provide the supporting numbers and statistics.
comments.quote: The numbers and statistics that would support this statement are lacking.

comments.issue: The 10-year time frame of IUCN criteria may itself be a problem given uncertainties and management delays.
comments.request: Discuss the IUCN time frame as an additional limitation.
comments.quote: Table 1 and conclusion: couldn’t we say that one of the problems is the time frame of IUCN criteria? 10 years may just be too short given the uncertainties, the time required to implement management actions,

comments.issue: The simulation code was not provided.
comments.request: Share the simulation code.
comments.quote: the simulation code was not provided

reviews.assessment: Very nice study that valuably improves risk assessments, though some modelling choices and interpretations need clarification.
strengths: well designed, clearly written and well structured
valuable contribution to extinction risk assessment

comments.issue: The simulation framework is overly simplified: unclear warming rate, static precipitation and no extreme events, with limitations not acknowledged.
comments.request: Justify the climate assumptions and acknowledge their limitations.
comments.quote: The simulation framework is elegant but overly simplified, and some choices are not sufficiently justified. For example, temperature is described as increasing linearly over 90 years, but by how much per year?

comments.issue: The simulated niches are not contextualized: value ranges, gradient coverage and comparability to real species are unclear.
comments.request: Report niche value ranges and add example response curves.
comments.quote: It would be useful to better contextualize the simulated niches. What is the range of values used for temperature and precipitation?

comments.issue: Initial conditions are not detailed: number of individuals, cells occupied and equilibrium variation are missing.
comments.request: Report the initial population sizes, ranges and their variation.
comments.quote: The manuscript does not provide enough detail on initial conditions. How many individuals are present at the start, and in how many cells are they distributed?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the three replicate landscapes represent different environments or stochastic replicates.
comments.request: Explain the role of landscape replication.
comments.quote: The rationale for using three replicate landscapes is unclear. Are these intended to represent fundamentally different environments or simply stochastic replicates?

comments.issue: Range-shifting versus range-contracting is an outcome of dynamics, not a species trait; the binary framing may create artefacts.
comments.request: Clarify the conceptual basis and discuss the categories as a simplification.
comments.quote: A central distinction in the manuscript is between “range-shifting” and “range-contracting” species. However, I find this distinction somewhat problematic. Unlike life-history traits such as dispersal or growth rate, “range-shifting” versus “range-contracting” is not a species-level trait but rather an outcome of climate-driven dynamics

comments.issue: Marginal-niche species are assumed to occur mainly in the north, which biases them toward contraction; southern marginal niches are not represented.
comments.request: Explain this asymmetry and represent northern and southern marginal niches.
comments.quote: In line 113, it is stated that species with marginal niches occur mainly in the northern part of the landscape. Why not equally in the south?

comments.issue: 'Population' in the extinction probability calculation is undefined (whole landscape versus cell) and may not match IUCN criterion E.
comments.request: Define population and consider a measure aligned with criterion E.
comments.quote: However, it is unclear what is meant by “population” in this context: is it the total number of individuals across the entire landscape, or the number in a given cell?

comments.issue: The text claims growth rate and dispersal strongly affect extinction dynamics, but Fig. S1 shows similar curves.
comments.request: Reconcile the interpretation with Fig. S1.
comments.quote: In lines 116–118, the text suggests that growth rate and dispersal strongly affect extinction dynamics. However, Fig. S1 shows very similar curves across columns, which suggests that these traits have comparatively little effect relative to niche position.

comments.issue: The logic for concluding that SDMs underestimate range loss is unclear; SDM range loss should be compared with simulated range loss.
comments.request: Clarify and correct the comparison underlying this conclusion.
comments.quote: However, shouldn’t range loss estimated by SDMs be compared directly to simulated range loss? Clarifying this logic is important, since it underpins one of the central conclusions of the paper.

comments.issue: Highest abundances at the range periphery contradict the abundant-center hypothesis.
comments.request: Explain this abundance pattern.
comments.quote: Furthermore, according to the figure it seems that the highest abundances are found at the periphery of the range, which clearly contradicts the abundant-center hypothesis. How do you explain this pattern?

comments.issue: Convex/concave patterns are less clear under loess smoothing, weakening the claim that SDMs systematically misestimate risk.
comments.request: Do not overstate consistency and explain why the patterns differ.
comments.quote: The convex/concave patterns are not always as clear when loess smoothing is applied. This weakens the clarity of the claim that SDMs systematically over- or underestimate risk. The authors should be careful not to overstate the consistency of these patterns

comments.issue: The classification-time methods (lines 415-423), moving windows and thresholds are unclear.
comments.request: Explain the procedure more carefully, ideally with a worked example.
comments.quote: Some sections of the methods are difficult to follow. For instance, lines 415–423 (on classification times under Red List criteria) are not clear as written.

comments.issue: In Fig. 4 the mean extinction time is much higher than the median, which is counterintuitive.
comments.request: Explain why the mean and median diverge.
comments.quote: Some figures could be clarified: e.g., in Fig. 4, the mean extinction time is much higher than the median, which is counterintuitive. Please explain why this occurs.

title: Models used for Red List assessments underestimate climate-related extinction risk of range-shifting species

study.system: nematode phylogenomics; molecular dating and lifestyle evolution models

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers are interested but a key issue is untangling the many methods used and their rationale; suggests a table or schematic of which method was used where and why, and clearer methods reporting.

reviews.assessment: Praising the work as incredible and interesting, with no substantial issues, but suggests a workflow schematic and clarifications to make arguments more robust.

comments.issue: The huge volume of methods and priors makes the reasoning, inputs and outputs hard to follow.
comments.request: Add a schematic workflow.
comments.quote: This makes it hard to follow the reasoning behind each method choice, as well as the inputs and outputs of each step.

comments.issue: Calling previous divergence estimates overestimates is unclear without a comparison.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison.
comments.quote: Previous divergence time estimates are suggested to be “overestimates”, but it’s not clear what this is in comparison to, and/or why the ‘right’ answer is younger.

comments.issue: How major conclusions were determined from the many analyses is not described.
comments.request: Describe how conclusions were determined.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to have an extra sentence here briefly describing the procedure for determining major conclusions from the plethora of analyses conducted

comments.issue: The preference for morphological clades over genomic results, and the choice of genomic over total-evidence, are not justified.
comments.request: Justify the preference for morphological clades.
comments.quote: It’s not clear why this opinion is held by the authors, why should we trust the morphological analyses?

comments.issue: Priors are blamed for uncertainty, yet many prior configurations are tested, which looks like indiscriminate model fitting.
comments.request: Justify the Bayesian approach and prior choices.
comments.quote: The implementation of so many prior configurations could be seen as fitting a large volume of models indiscriminately rather than following specific hypotheses.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the analysis combining prior choices with most convergence is a good summary of the results.
comments.request: Justify the choice of main analysis.
comments.quote: I assume there is some sort of assumption that this analysis represents the ‘best’ convergence somehow, but does that necessarily make it a good summary or representation of the results as a whole?

comments.issue: What the 115 trees represent and how branch lengths were summarised is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the tree set.
comments.quote: It’s not completely clear what these 115 trees represent. Are these summary trees, meaning that 115/432 branch length analyses converged and could be summarised?

comments.issue: 'Further refine' is unclear for trees that are already inferred.
comments.request: Clarify the step.
comments.quote: I don’t understand what “further refine” means here.

comments.issue: Known external evidence falsifies inferred ancestral states; why they remain interpretable needs explanation.
comments.request: Explain the validity of the ancestral states.
comments.quote: I think more explanation is needed as to why it is still valid to interpret the inferred ancestral states despite knowing that, at least in this specific part of the tree, they are not correct

comments.issue: The choice of 90 Ma as the break point for evolutionary rates is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the 90 Ma break point.
comments.quote: It would help to state clearly here how/why 90 Ma was chosen as the break point for evolutionary rates.

comments.issue: Incorporating fossils as tips could improve future analyses.
comments.request: Mention fossil tips.
comments.quote: Incorporating fossils as tips could also be mentioned as a way to improve future analyses

comments.issue: The Methods section is very brief.
comments.request: Expand the methods.
comments.quote: The Methods section in the manuscript is very brief, I think more details could be added

comments.issue: Why the five species were selected for sequencing is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the species selection.
comments.quote: Why or how were these five species selected for sequencing beyond what was already available online?

comments.issue: Differences between the sequence types are not explained for non-specialist readers.
comments.request: Describe the sequence types.
comments.quote: it would help those less familiar if there was a brief description here of the differences between these different sequence types

comments.issue: Whether the taxonomic sample includes all available sequences or reflects active choices is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling choice.
comments.quote: Does the taxonomic sample represent all available appropriate sequences/species, or were active choices made in which to include in the study?

comments.issue: How the locus criteria were selected and whether cut-offs are justified is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the locus criteria.
comments.quote: how were these criteria selected, and were the cut-off values justified or arbitrary?

comments.issue: Whether the same trees were passed to HiSSE and PAML priors recapitulated is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the tree and PAML linkage.
comments.quote: Are these the same trees then provided to HiSSE, and if so, is this PAML prior information recapitulated in the speciation and extinction rates inferred using HiSSE?

comments.issue: Sampling fractions are not related to the fixed PAML values.
comments.request: Relate sampling fractions to PAML.
comments.quote: how do these sampling fractions relate to the fixed values used in the PAML analyses?

comments.issue: How diversification results complement or conflict with PAML and HiSSE is unclear.
comments.request: Reconcile the methods' results.
comments.quote: how do these results theoretically complement or conflict with the PAML priors and inference results from HiSSE?

reviews.assessment: Strongly positive: comprehensive, convincing and valuable, with only a suggestion to note sampling bias and fix a corrupted code file.
strengths: convincing demonstration of a free-living ancestor

comments.issue: Parasitic species are disproportionately described relative to free-living ones, biasing apparent lifestyle prevalence.
comments.request: Note the sampling bias.
comments.quote: The authors might consider noting the recognised disproportionate description of parasitic relative to free-living species, largely reflecting their economic importance.

comments.issue: One code repository file is corrupted.
comments.request: Fix the corrupted file.
comments.quote: The file NematodaTreeTaxonLifeStyle.xlsx was accessible via LifeStyleEvolution but the version in 7.AncestralStateReconstruction was corrupted.

reviews.assessment: Considers the results sound and the paper important, but wants missing ecdysozoan genomes and the fossil calibration table addressed.

comments.issue: Recent relevant ecdysozoan genomes (Priapulida, Onychophora, Nematomorpha) are not incorporated, potentially explaining outgroup problems.
comments.request: Incorporate the relevant published genomes.
comments.quote: I am referring to several recent published genomes of ecdysozoan taxa that are highly relevant, including Priapulida, Onychophora and most importantly, Nematomorpha.

comments.issue: A table summarising new and existing data is missing.
comments.request: Add a data summary table.
comments.quote: I missed a table with information about the new data and the existing data

comments.issue: Fossil calibrations are relegated to the supplement despite being crucial.
comments.request: Move the fossil calibration table to the main text.
comments.quote: The list of fossils is one of the most important parts of this study. Don’t make the reader have to go to suppl. materials in order to see the fossil constraints.

comments.issue: The Enoplia early-branching statement could be phrased more clearly.
comments.request: Rephrase the divergence statement.
comments.quote: Maybe you could say that the deepest divergence is between Enoplia and the remaining nematodes or something like that.

comments.issue: The composition of the second reduced dataset is not explicit.
comments.request: State the dataset composition.
comments.quote: I assume that the second reduced data set is for 43 nematodes without outgroups? Please, be more explicit about this.

comments.issue: Newer editions of Brusca et al. and Nielsen discussing these relationships are not cited.
comments.request: Cite the newer sources.
comments.quote: There is a newer version of Brusca et al. where these relationships are explicitly discussed.

comments.issue: Most cited studies did not include Loricifera or Nematomorpha, so citations should be specific.
comments.request: Cite specific papers for specific relationships.
comments.quote: However, most of these studies did not include Loricifera or Nematomorpha.

comments.issue: Lineages cannot be described as paraphyletic or polyphyletic; taxa can.
comments.request: Rephrase using taxa.
comments.quote: Taxa, like the ones listed, can be paraphyletic or polyphyletic, but lineages are lineages, so they cannot be paraphyletic or polyphyletic.

comments.issue: Two line-level wording fixes (rRNA versus rDNA; 'sister to' versus 'sister group to').
comments.quote: Line 138 (and elsewhere): “sister to XXXX” should be “sister group to XXXX”

comments.issue: The seven quality metrics are not identified.
comments.request: Explain the seven quality metrics.
comments.quote: Line 364: What “seven quality metrics” does this refer to?

title: The timescale of nematode evolution reveals late and convergent radiations of parasitism

study.system: plant non-structural carbohydrates; global trait database

editor_summary: Editor: four reviewers found the work of considerable potential interest but raised substantial concerns; a revision addressing these serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Interesting global overview, but organ-specific sampling and measurement issues may bias the phylogenetic results and much of the discussion.
strengths: comprehensive overview of NSC distribution across organs, evolution and biomes

comments.issue: Fructans are excluded from total NSC, which may bias phylogenetic results in fructan-rich groups.
comments.request: Analyse fructans as a separate pool or justify their omission.
comments.quote: I believe that the phylogenetic results may be biased by the omission of fructans from the calculation of total NSCs

comments.issue: Non-standardised extraction methods (HCl/HNO3) may overestimate NSC and this bias was not excluded.
comments.request: Restrict analyses to enzymatic-method studies or correct for method bias.
comments.quote: Many used outdated procedures, such as starch or sugar degradation with HCl or HNO₃, and measure sugars with nitrate, which often leads to overestimation.

comments.issue: Stem NSC varies among stems, twigs, branches and trunks but this was not accounted for.
comments.request: Account for organ type within stems in the analyses.
comments.quote: The concentration of NSC differs among stems, twigs, young branches, and the trunk, but from the Methods section, it does not seem that this aspect has been taken into account.

comments.issue: Sampling time of day was not considered, affecting carbohydrate amounts and leaf starch/soluble ratios.
comments.request: Account for sampling time in eligibility criteria and analyses.
comments.quote: In the eligibility criteria, the time of day when the samples were collected was not taken into account.

comments.issue: Temporally inconsistent sampling may undermine the discussion of leaf versus stem and root NSC.
comments.request: Explain how the models address temporal inconsistency in sampling.
comments.quote: if the initial data are inaccurate due to a lack of temporal consistency in sample collection, there is a risk of undermining a large portion of the observations and interpretations presented

comments.issue: The term 'heterotrophic organs' is inappropriate because stems are often photosynthetic.
comments.request: Avoid the term 'heterotrophic organs' for stems.
comments.quote: I suggest avoiding the term “heterotrophic organs,” since stems are green in most herbs and young woody plants

comments.issue: Acronym NSC is not defined at first use.
comments.request: Define the NSC acronym.
comments.quote: L21. I think the acronym NSC is missing.

comments.issue: 'Soluble sugars' is redundant since sugars are soluble by definition.
comments.request: Remove the redundant qualifier.
comments.quote: L23. Sugars are soluble by definition.

comments.issue: 'However' mislinks sentences because sugars and fructans are both NSC.
comments.request: Fix the syntax around 'however'.
comments.quote: L24. I think that “however” links the second sentence with the previous one.

comments.issue: Lipids and polyalcohols are carbon reserves, not carbohydrate reserves.
comments.request: Correct the reserve classification.
comments.quote: L25. Lipids and polyalcohols are not carbohydrate reserves but carbon reserves.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'immediate' in the osmotic adjustment sentence is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify or remove 'immediate'.
comments.quote: Furthermore, I do not understand the use of “immediate” — to which conditions does it refer?

comments.issue: 'Metabolic demand' is inaccurate; the concept is a concentration-driven flux from sources to sinks.
comments.request: Rephrase using the source-to-sink flux concept.
comments.quote: L29. It is not exactly the metabolic “demand”, but rather the ability to sustain a concentration-driven flux (Münch theory) from sources to sinks through the phloem.

comments.issue: Suggested rewording of the hydraulic recovery sentence.
comments.request: Change the sentence as suggested.
comments.quote: L32. I suggest changing to: “In some cases, NSC can sustain hydraulic recovery.”

comments.issue: Text refers to Fig. 3b–e but appears to mean Fig. 3a–f.
comments.request: Check and correct the figure panel reference.
comments.quote: L155. I do not understand why the text refers to Fig. 3b–e. I think it should be Fig. 3a–f.

comments.issue: Percentages in the text do not match Fig. 4.
comments.request: Reconcile text and figure values.
comments.quote: L174. Why do the percentages reported in the text not correspond to those in Fig. 4?

comments.issue: R2C is defined differently in the Fig. 4 caption and the text.
comments.request: Make the text and caption definitions consistent.
comments.quote: in the caption R2C represents the percentage of variance explained by both environmental factors and evolutionary history, whereas in the text it refers to Overall, evolutionary history

comments.issue: The claim that stems are heterotrophic is wrong for grasses, forbs and many woody plants.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence to acknowledge stem photosynthesis.
comments.quote: L191. I cannot agree with the sentence, since the paper also considers grasses and forbs, where the stem is photosynthetic.

comments.issue: The growing season is not a period without NSC change; variation can be high.
comments.request: Revise the statement and cite relevant studies.
comments.quote: I think that “growing season” cannot be considered a period during which NSC do not change.

comments.issue: Literature on allocation is missing.
comments.request: Cite and discuss papers on allocation.
comments.quote: I think the authors can find in the literature several papers disentangling the relevance of evaluating allocation

comments.issue: The intense-radiation statement is obvious.
comments.quote: L213–215. The statement “Under intense radiation, can lead to high sugar loading and exporting in leaves” seems somewhat obvious.

comments.issue: The water-supply statement contradicts evidence that growth reduction uncouples storage and NSC.
comments.request: Reconsider the statement and cite McDowell 2011 and Muller et al. 2011.
comments.quote: L221–222. I am not fully convinced by this statement. Low water supply primarily reduces plant growth, leading to an uncoupling between storage and NSC accumulation

comments.issue: Monocot stem NSC patterns may reflect herbaceous, photosynthetic stems and storage function rather than the proposed explanation.
comments.request: Consider these alternative explanations.
comments.quote: L242–244. I think monocots display higher NSC concentrations in stems because most of the species considered are herbs and therefore photosynthetically active.

comments.issue: The dominance of evolution over environment may be scale-dependent, weakening at family or order levels.
comments.request: Discuss how the conclusion depends on taxonomic scale.
comments.quote: I think the major role of evolution compared with environmental traits is evident considering the broad clades analyzed.

reviews.assessment: Strong, well-written study with compelling figures, but the phylogenetic conservatism framing must go because signal tests cannot test process.

comments.issue: Phylogenetic signal (a pattern) cannot test phylogenetic conservatism (a process); the two are conflated.
comments.request: Remove the conservatism framing and present signal and PGLS results only.
comments.quote: evidence for phylogenetic signal (a pattern) doesn’t tell us much about the evolutionary process leading to it, so the pattern of phylogenetic conservatism cannot be tested with tests of phylogenetic signal

comments.issue: Unclear whether lipids count as carbohydrate reserves.
comments.request: Clarify the definition.
comments.quote: L96: would lipids be considered a carbohydrate reserve?

comments.issue: Six line-level copy edits (L101, L413, L416, L452, L460, L513).
comments.quote: L101: remove the word “for”.

comments.issue: 'Phylogenetic conservatism' is used without definition in the introduction.
comments.request: Define the concept before using it.
comments.quote: L157: phylogenetic conservatism as a topic or a process that may be influencing NSC patterns worldwide hasn’t been defined yet in the introduction.

comments.issue: The signal test is presented as a test of phylogenetic niche conservatism.
comments.request: Correct this claim.
comments.quote: L228: the test of phylogenetic signal does not test for phylogenetic niche conservatism.

comments.issue: It is unclear how phylogeny can be accounted for and then its effect tested.
comments.request: Clarify the logic of the phylogenetic analyses.
comments.quote: L247: I do not understand how can evolutionary history can be taken into account and then the effect of phylogeny be tested.

comments.issue: The variables used in the Pearson correlation matrix and the multivariate redundancy analysis are unclear.
comments.request: State which variables were used.
comments.quote: L465: multivariate redundancy of? what were the variables used for the Pearson correlation matrix?

comments.issue: Suggested using the SDSR acronym.
comments.request: Use the SDSR acronym.
comments.quote: L471: why don’t use the acronym SDSR for surface downwelling shortwave radiation?

comments.issue: Signal test again described as a conservatism test (L506).
comments.request: Correct the wording.
comments.quote: L506: again, the phylogenetic signal test is not a test of phylogenetic conservatis.

comments.issue: Unclear whether 'alter' or 'select' is meant (L532).
comments.request: Clarify the intended word.
comments.quote: L532: alter or select?

comments.issue: Unclear why CHELSA data were not used for the Whittaker plot as in the random forest models.
comments.request: Use consistent climate data or explain the difference.
comments.quote: L810: why not use the data extracted from CHELSA for the Whitaker plot if the random forest models use the CHELSA data.

reviews.assessment: Promising synthesis undermined by a repetitive, sloppy discussion, overstated claims and unaddressed lab variation in NSC values.
strengths: good analysis with some redundancy across statistical approaches

comments.issue: Discussion is highly repetitive and the later text is sloppy, with inaccurate statements and grammar problems.
comments.request: Rewrite and condense the discussion and fix the language.
comments.quote: Particularly the discussion is highly repetitive, and in need of a lot of work.

comments.issue: Terms like 'long-term evolution', 'deep-time evolution' and 'adaptive evolution' are undefined and unclear.
comments.request: Define these evolutionary terms or avoid them.
comments.quote: but what is 'long-term evolution'? 'deep-time evolution'? 'adaptive evolution'?

comments.issue: The cited source-sink paper is misrepresented as challenging source-driven growth, when it argues the opposite.
comments.request: Correct the citation and discuss the source-sink literature in depth.
comments.quote: The reference to the ample C source-sink literature is utterly wrong, L. 346: 'this challenges the prevailing assumptions of source-driven growth' - the cited paper argues the opposite!

comments.issue: Lab-to-lab discrepancies in absolute NSC values are not addressed and may invalidate comparisons.
comments.request: Discuss this variation, or analyse relative changes over time.
comments.quote: Another major issue is the Quentin paper, that showed the huge discrepancies in absolute NSC values between labs.

comments.issue: Use 'phylogenetic effect' rather than 'phylogeny effect' (L131 and elsewhere).
comments.request: Correct the wording.
comments.quote: 131 and elsewhere: I think it should be 'the phylogenetic effect' not the 'phylogeny effect'

comments.issue: Line-level language problems throughout (L228, L239, L244, L300, L310ff, L324/325, L336ff, L362ff, L382).
comments.quote: 324/325 fix English, I am guessing what you mean

comments.issue: A gap remains in the interpretation of the carbon balance indicator (L353).
comments.request: Explain the indicator's interpretation.
comments.quote: 353 there is a gap on the interpretation of the indicator of carbon balance?

comments.issue: 'Species adaptations' is undefined (L365).
comments.request: Define what is meant.
comments.quote: 365 what are 'species adaptations'?

comments.issue: The Conclusion repeats earlier material.
comments.request: Condense the Conclusion.
comments.quote: The Conclusion is repeating a lot of what has been said earlier.

comments.issue: The claimed 'paradigm shift' in C cycling is overstated.
comments.request: Tone down the paradigm-shift claim.
comments.quote: The statement that the work suggest a 'paradigm shift' in C cycling is well overstated

comments.issue: The vegetation modelling integration statement is generic and needs detail.
comments.request: Explain concretely how the information would be integrated.
comments.quote: Integrating 'this information into vegetation modelling' is a generic statement that would need a lot more detail/explanation.

reviews.assessment: Potentially interesting premise, but it lacks justification, environmental analyses lack rationale, and the framing is teleological.
strengths: potentially interesting assessment of phylogenetic and taxonomic influences

comments.issue: The premise that phylogenetic and taxonomic factors explain NSC variation lacks solid justification.
comments.request: Provide a stronger theoretical justification for the premise.
comments.quote: there is no solid background behind this premise, i.e. this important premise lacks sufficient justification

comments.issue: The sink-limitation premise is only one hypothesis; carbon gain may also control NSC storage.
comments.request: Justify why carbon demand rather than carbon gain regulates storage.
comments.quote: The premise that NSC storage is regulated by C demands is not unequivocal, it is just one of the hypotheses in the literature

comments.issue: Major drivers such as herbivory and defoliation risk and other sources of variation were excluded without justification.
comments.request: Include or justify the exclusion of these drivers.
comments.quote: the inclusion of herbivory or defoliation risk by abiotic factors, which is a very major driver of NSC variability), remained unresolved and eluded in this study

comments.issue: No a priori theoretical justification is given for the climatic and edaphic variables.
comments.request: Provide a rationale for each variable included.
comments.quote: First, which is the theoretical justification for each one of this variables?

comments.issue: The study uses largely the same data and analyses as previous studies and reaches similar conclusions, adding little progress.
comments.request: Clarify the advance over previous global studies.
comments.quote: It appears that performed similar analysis (eg correlations between NSC and environment or climate) and arrived at similar conclusions.

comments.issue: The discussion is speculative and a posteriori, and explanations are applied inconsistently across organs.
comments.request: Base interpretations on a priori predictions and apply them consistently.
comments.quote: the discussion is very, very, speculative and entirely built up an "a posteriori" frame

comments.issue: Restricting the data to the growing season is unjustified.
comments.request: Justify the growing-season restriction or include other seasons.
comments.quote: I found no reason to use NSC data of the growing season. NSC data come only from the growing season.

comments.issue: Information on taxonomic coverage is missing although it is the study's key novelty.
comments.request: Report and analyse the taxonomic coverage.
comments.quote: I missed information on the taxonomic coverage of this study. There is a very solid geographical coverage, but the taxonomic coverage seems to be most relevant

comments.issue: Writing frames traits teleologically, with a Lamarckian imprint, lacking a natural selection frame.
comments.request: Reframe trait statements within natural selection.
comments.quote: I consider misleading to frame these characteristics in particular purposes, as this study does

title: Evolutionary history drives organ-specific variability in plant non-structural carbohydrates

study.system: grasslands and forests; biodiversity effects under drought and heat extremes

reviews.assessment: Well-designed, appropriately analysed and novel synthesis with robust causal evidence, but the forest null needs stronger caveats and geographic limits discussion.
strengths: robust causal evidence from compiled experiments
timely reiteration of biodiversity's importance for productivity

comments.issue: The forest null finding is emphasised despite low power, lagged and late-season drought effects, and weak growth indicators.
comments.request: Caveat the forest null more strongly and avoid emphasising the system contrast.
