comments.quote: Therefore, this conclusion should be explicitly limited to the experimental forest communities examined here.

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 2 are overly dense and the line types are not explained.
comments.request: Simplify the figures and clarify whether lines were tested across or pooled across life forms.
comments.quote: Figures 1 and 2 are informative but overly dense. Consider simplifying by grouping trophic levels or adding schematic legends to enhance readability.

comments.issue: Figure 3 SEM is visually complex with detailed SEMs in Figure 4.
comments.request: Move detailed SEMs to the supplement and keep a simplified main-text version.
comments.quote: Figure 3 (SEM) is visually complex. I recommend moving the detailed trophic-level SEMs (currently Fig. 4) to Supplementary Materials and keeping a simplified version in the main text

comments.issue: The discussion lacks a limitations section on tree age, canopy closure and missing litter measurements.
comments.request: Add a study limitations section.
comments.quote: The Discussion would benefit from a short section on study limitations, particularly: (a) the relatively young age of the MyDiv trees (six years), (b) potential underestimation of aboveground effects due to canopy closure stage

comments.issue: Applied implications for restoration and carbon sequestration are not operationalized.
comments.request: Discuss how tree-mycorrhiza diversity could be operationalized in practice.
comments.quote: this point could be strengthened by discussing how tree–mycorrhiza diversity might be operationalized in restoration or carbon sequestration programs

comments.issue: The results are not linked to projected global-change shifts in EcM versus AM tree dominance.
comments.request: Link the findings to future global change projections and cite recent studies.
comments.quote: the practical significance of this study could be strengthened by linking the results to forest dynamics under future global change

comments.issue: The title omits mycorrhizal type, which is central to the hypotheses and results.
comments.request: Include mycorrhizal type in the title.
comments.quote: “Mycorrhizal type” is important in the hypotheses and results, which I think should be included in the title.

comments.issue: Additive and synergistic effects are used repeatedly but never defined or quantified.
comments.request: Define these effects and state how they were evaluated.
comments.quote: Some key concepts—particularly additive effects and synergistic effects—are used repeatedly but are not clearly defined or quantitatively described.

comments.issue: Trophic level classification is unclear, including predator size classes, nematode group criteria and omnivory.
comments.request: Clarify trophic classification criteria and acknowledge trophic flexibility.
comments.quote: The classification of trophic levels in the manuscript is somewhat unclear and could be improved for greater ecological accuracy and reader comprehension.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, robust and novel study with comprehensive data; only moderate suggestions on statistical transparency and comparisons.
strengths: highly novel and well contextualized in BEF theory
comprehensive integration of above- and belowground data with excellent figures

comments.issue: Standardized slopes and CIs are hard to interpret biologically.
comments.request: Provide absolute abundance or richness changes alongside standardized effects.
comments.quote: While standardized slopes and 95% CIs are shown, their biological magnitude is sometimes difficult to interpret.

comments.issue: The claim that belowground responses are stronger rests on comparing standardized effect sizes rather than an explicit test.
comments.request: Test effect magnitude between strata, e.g. with stratum × log(tree richness).
comments.quote: The paper would benefit from a more explicit statistical test comparing the magnitude of diversity effects between strata (e.g. hierarchical models with stratum × log(tree richness)).

comments.issue: Model formulae, plot numbers per treatment, Type I error handling and SEM fit statistics are not reported.
comments.request: Add formulae, plot counts, error-control statement and SEM fit table.
comments.quote: transparency and reproducibility could be improved by 1) providing model formulae (e.g. lme(response ~ log(tree richness) + mycorrhiza + interaction + month + (1|composition/month)) in the supplement

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits (dashes, articles, wording, statistical notation).
comments.quote: Statistical notation should be consistent (e.g. p ≤ 0.05 v P < 0.05, Log v log₁₀).

comments.issue: Significance is sometimes interpreted at p < 0.1.
comments.request: Use marginal significance cautiously.
comments.quote: Significance is sometimes interpreted at p < 0.1 (marginal) which needs to be used cautiously.

comments.issue: Italics marking the marginal predator richness effect cannot be found in the supplementary tables.
comments.request: Mark the marginal result consistently in the tables.
comments.quote: L110: “only marginal effects on predator richness (p = 0.07; Tables S4-5)” – I cannot see any figures in italic to signify this in the supplementary tables.

comments.issue: Summary R² values are buried in supplementary tables.
comments.request: Move summary R² values into the main text.
comments.quote: Suggest moving summary R² values from Tables S4-S8 into the main text to help readers interpret model performance.

comments.issue: Whether multitrophic metrics were equally weighted or missing groups excluded is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the weighting of multitrophic metrics.
comments.quote: Can you clarify whether multitrophic abundance/diversity metrics were equally weighted or if trophic groups with missing data were excluded in each case.

title: Tree diversity and mycorrhizal type independently shape multitrophic biodiversity, with stronger effects belowground than aboveground

study.system: European summit plant communities; 21-year vegetation and temperature monitoring

reviews.assessment: Rich, key dataset; asks to move hypotheses earlier, clarify models and results, and test climate interactions with local context.
strengths: combines macro- and microclimate with plot context

comments.issue: Hypotheses appear too late in the introduction to frame the variables described earlier.
comments.request: State the hypotheses earlier in the introduction.
comments.quote: I appreciate the clear hypotheses setup in the introduction (L184 - 193), however I think they need to be stated earlier in the introduction to give some conceptual bearing to the range of variables quantified described in the previous section.

comments.issue: The methods paragraph is hard to follow and mixes unrelated variables.
comments.request: Separate the text at L157-162 to distinguish variables per question.
comments.quote: Currently, the paragraph briefly describing the methods is difficult to follow and the individual sentences describe unrelated variables.

comments.issue: Results sections are not clearly tied to specific hypotheses, and elevation gradients are not introduced.
comments.request: Tie each results section to a specific hypothesis.
comments.quote: there needs to be more clarity in what sections of the results are directly related to the hypotheses tested. I would encourage directly tying each section to a specific hypothesis.

comments.issue: Model structures in the results (L282-285, L254-255) are difficult to follow.
comments.request: Simplify the model descriptions in the results.
comments.quote: In the results, the model structures used to analyze the patterns are difficult to follow (L282-285, L254-255).

comments.issue: Climate variables were modeled separately and interactions with local context were excluded.
comments.request: Explain the choice and test additive and interactive climate-context effects.
comments.quote: Please include an explanation of why the climate variables were modeled separately as opposed to as additive or interactive predictors.

comments.issue: “Actually” at L146 is unnecessary.
comments.request: Remove “actually”.
comments.quote: L146 – Remove ‘actually’

comments.issue: The sentence at L160 on temperature data types is hard to follow.
comments.request: Remove the commas to clarify the sentence.
comments.quote: L160 – the types of temperature data used is difficult to follow in this sentence – I suggest removing the commas

comments.issue: The comparison underlying the calculated difference is unclear and appears to use only the initial survey.
comments.request: Explain the comparison and why no dynamic metric is used.
comments.quote: The comparison that allows for the calculation ‘of the difference’ is not clear. I would add here that is based on only the initial survey

comments.issue: Figure 1b shows only fit lines, not the underlying data.
comments.request: Include the underlying data in panel b.
comments.quote: Figure 1. I think it would be helpful to Include the underlying data, not just fit lines for panel b

comments.issue: Figure 2 does not show the novel thermophilization-climate relationship and could be supplementary.
comments.request: Move Figure 2 to the supplement.
comments.quote: This could possibly be in the supplement. The novel component of this paper is how the thermophilzation trends covaries with rates of change in climate conditions, which can’t be gleaned from this figure.

comments.issue: The choice of focal temperature metrics and exclusions (snow, degree-days) is unexplained.
comments.request: Justify metric selection and consider snow and degree-days.
comments.quote: How were the focal temperature metrics chosen? Why were interactions between climate variables excluded? What about snow (L389)?

comments.issue: Figure 4 effect sizes are hard to compare across predictors.
comments.request: Overlay density plots with decreased alpha.
comments.quote: Overlaying the density plots (with decreases alpha) may allow easier comparison across the effect size of the different predictors

comments.issue: Figure S3 is not highlighted in the main text.
comments.request: Highlight Figure S3 for a subset of climate variables.
comments.quote: Figure S3 may be worth highlighting in the main text for a subset of the climate variables considered

reviews.assessment: Valuable contribution; suggests using pre-2001 temperature data to better link thermophilization to warming, plus many clarifications.
strengths: valuable summary of summit vegetation change
range of macro- and microclimate estimates

comments.issue: Data start only in 2001, yet community composition reflects temperatures of preceding years.
comments.request: Estimate temperature change using pre-2001 5-year averages, complementing current analyses.
comments.quote: Ideally, one should therefore have temperature measurements available for a time period prior to 2001 (e.g. a five- or ten-year period from 2001 and backwards).

comments.issue: Elevational rank is not sufficiently explained; methods depend on Gottfried et al. and Table S5 lacks references.
comments.request: Explain the ranks independently, noting the seven versus six levels.
comments.quote: Information about the elevational rank is not sufficient to make a reasonable interpretation as a reader.

comments.issue: No reference to a table or list of the variables actually used.
comments.request: Point readers to a table or list of variables.
comments.quote: Line 175-178: I would like to see a reference to a table or list of the actual variables used.

comments.issue: The expectation that bare soil increases thermophilization seems counterintuitive, as bare soil may indicate harsher conditions.
comments.request: Reconsider or justify the predicted direction.
comments.quote: Not sure if I would expect an increase in thermophilization in areas with high cover of bare soil. Bare soil would to me in many cases indicate rougher climatic conditions (e.g. wind conditions).

comments.issue: Plot numbers do not add up: 53 summits times four directions gives 848 plots, but 724 are used.
comments.request: Explain the sampling scheme and discarded plots.
comments.quote: There are 53 summits each with 4 plots in each of the four cardinal directions. This makes up 848 plots deviating from the 724 plots used.

comments.issue: Figure 1b is not helpful given the sampling confusion.
comments.request: Revise or remove Figure 1b.
comments.quote: Given the confusion of the sampling protocol, I dd not find Figure 1b helpful

comments.issue: The “null models” at line 210 are confusing before reading the whole manuscript.
comments.request: Clarify what the null models are at first mention.
comments.quote: What are the null models referring to here? It is understandable what is meant after reading the whole manuscript, but I found the ‘null’ here only to be confusing

comments.issue: The magnitude of elevational shift lacks context about vegetation belt levels.
comments.request: Explain the vegetation belt levels so the shift is interpretable.
comments.quote: The information about the magnitude of elevational shift is interesting (0.06 vegetation belts per decade), but some more context about the levels of vegetation belts are needed for this result to make meaning for the reader.

comments.issue: The text emphasizes variability of climate estimates over the more interesting mean changes.
comments.request: Focus on mean differences in this part.
comments.quote: The text focuses on the variability of the climatic estimates. But are these more interesting than the actual changes estimated.

comments.issue: The L246-252 text mixes thermophilization and temperature change.
comments.request: Focus first on thermophilization rate, then temperature change.
comments.quote: I would recommend focusing first on the thermophilization rate, and then on temperature change. The first sentence describes a model including both thermophilization and temperature change but only report on the former.

comments.issue: Figure 4 may be unnecessary; its message is conveyed in the text.
comments.request: Replace it with a direct thermophilization-colonizer/rock cover relationship.
comments.quote: I am not sure if this figure is needed in the main document. My feeling is that the main message of this figure is equally well conveyed in the text

comments.issue: A p-value of exactly 1.000 for macroclimatic minimum summer temperature is questionable.
comments.request: Check the Table S2 p-value.
comments.quote: Table S2: Is the p-value of 1.000 for the macroclimatic min summer temperature correct?

comments.issue: The origin of the ERs in Table S5 is unreferenced.
comments.request: Cite the source of the elevational ranks.
comments.quote: Table S5: Is there a reference for where these ERs come from?

title: Widespread thermophilization but weak link to climate warming in Europe’s summit plant communities

study.system: marine oligochaete Olavius algarvensis and other animals; PHAD enzymes

reviews.assessment: Satisfied that previous concerns were addressed and has no further comments; finds the work very interesting.
strengths: enzymatic assay convincingly shows enzyme activity

reviews.assessment: Supports publication of this important contribution; asks only for similarity values and an alignment figure.

comments.issue: Only identity values, not similarity values, are given for the aligned proteins.
comments.request: Provide similarity values and a supplementary alignment figure.
comments.quote: please provide also similarity values (not only identity values) of the aligned proteins. Perhaps a suppl. Fig. showing the two aligned (domain) amino acid sequences would be also good.

reviews.assessment: Acknowledges the functional evidence but wants caveats that substrates may not be native and would welcome solid kinetic data.
strengths: preliminary data strongly suggest the enzymes are functional

comments.issue: Functional evidence is preliminary; solid kinetic data on enzyme turnover are missing.
comments.request: Provide strong kinetic data on enzyme turnover.
comments.quote: While this is positive, strong and solid kinetic data on enzyme turnover would be favorable.

comments.issue: Promiscuous alpha-beta hydrolases may turn over non-native substrates, so PHAs may not be the natural substrates.
comments.request: State clearly that the converted substrates may not be the enzymes' natural substrates.
comments.quote: I would urge the authors to clearly state that the substrates converted might not be the natural substrates of the enzymes detected. It is well known that alpha-beta hydrolases are highly promiscuous enzymes

title: Animal degradation of microbial storage polyhydroxyalkanoates

study.system: tropical forests; global spatial overlay of regeneration cost and benefit layers

editor_summary: Work of considerable potential interest, but four reviewers raised substantial concerns; cannot accept, but a revised version addressing the serious concerns would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Interesting article with potential for the journal, but the simple overlay approach needs substantial methodological strengthening on displacement, populations and country-level analyses.
strengths: interesting article with potential for the journal

comments.issue: No minimum regeneration-probability threshold is stated; very unlikely areas would be costly and pointless to include.
comments.request: State and justify the minimum regeneration probability threshold used for inclusion.
comments.quote: Is there a minimum threshold value of regeneration probability for areas to be included in the assessment? If so, what is the value?

comments.issue: Analyses ignore displacement of anthropogenic land uses; no quantification of which land uses are displaced and where.
comments.request: Quantify the land uses displaced by regeneration in each country.
comments.quote: it would be useful also to include some direct quantification of what land uses are being displaced in what countries

comments.issue: The analysis does not show what land uses would be displaced where, despite contrasting social contexts of low- and high-cost areas.
comments.request: Overlay regeneration classes with land-use types and discuss policy implications.
comments.quote: it might be useful to conduct an overlay with the regeneration classes to see what types of landuses are being displaced where, and how this might affect the policy implications of these results

comments.issue: Displacement of human populations is not considered; population density data are absent from priority identification.
comments.request: Include gridded population data as a cost or in priority mapping, or clarify if already used.
comments.quote: I would expect that displacement of populations would be considered in some way in the analyses, either as a direct cost (using relocation reimbursement values) or indirectly as part of the identification of priority areas

comments.issue: Inputs have strong country-level biases; a global analysis biases some countries and neglects others.
comments.request: Re-run the analyses with inputs normalised at the country level.
comments.quote: it would be useful to run the same analyses but with the inputs normalised at a country level to identify country-specific priority regions

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the 12.89% species-range increase is calculated per species or as richness times regeneration probability.
comments.request: Explain how the 12.89% increase was calculated and reword for clarity.
comments.quote: From the methods it is not completely clear if the increase in habitat area following regeneration is calculated for each species individually or simply by multiplying species richness by probability of regeneration

comments.issue: Species that lost most habitat may be least likely to benefit; no species-level breakdown of regeneration benefits is given.
comments.request: Provide a species-level breakdown of how regeneration classes cover habitat, including non-habitat-loss threats.
comments.quote: If it has been calculated at a species-level, it would be very interesting to see some breakdown of how the regeneration classes cover different species habitat areas

comments.issue: 30 km resolution is very coarse and inconsistent with the resolution of other datasets.
comments.request: Use species range vector data converted to 1 km rasters.
comments.quote: 30km resolution (I’m guessing 30km x 30km which is 900km2) is a very broad resolution for analyses, particularly compared to the resolution of other datatsets

comments.issue: Sensitivity analyses are hard to understand as currently reported.
comments.request: Add a scatter plot comparing country-level hotspot proportions across methods.
comments.quote: add a scatter plot showing the proportion of land in each country in the ‘holisitic hotspot’ category when using the reported method versus the alternatives

comments.issue: Plot colours are counterintuitive: high-high and holistic hotspot classes are not the most prominent.
comments.request: Make high-high and holistic hotspot classes visually dominant in plots.
comments.quote: the current colours for the classes in the plots are a bit counterintuitive. I would expect the high-high classes to be darker than the two high-low groups

comments.issue: The meaning of expansion of available distribution of threatened species in the abstract is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what this measure means in the abstract or main text.
comments.quote: it is not immediately clear to me what an expansion of available distribution of threatened species means?

comments.issue: Dense populations and agricultural export economies in the hotspot countries, plus Indonesian permitting rules, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss these socio-political factors and their impact on regeneration delivery.
comments.quote: these countries are densely populated and key exporters of agriculture products to the rest of the world, factors that would seriously impact delivery of regeneration in these countries

comments.issue: It is unclear whether fire guards or another type of guard is meant.
comments.request: Specify what type of guard is meant.
comments.quote: Page 2, line 54: fire guards or another type of guard?

comments.issue: The area underlying the US$0.725 billion economic return is not given.
comments.request: Convert the dollar amount to a rate per hectare.
comments.quote: over what area are these economic returns calculated? Can you convert this raw dollar amount to a rate per area?

comments.issue: Biodiversity conservation is described as an ecosystem service, which is not standard usage.
comments.request: Call carbon and biodiversity outcomes environmental benefits.
comments.quote: I don’t think biodiversity conservation is typically considered an ecosystem service? I think it would be better to refer to carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation as ‘environmental benefits’ or similar

comments.issue: Figure 1 text is too small and panels (a) and (b) largely duplicate information.
comments.request: Simplify the figure so the text can be larger and readable.
comments.quote: I imagine the text used in this figure is too small to meet the publisher guidelines? Also part (a) and (b) seem to largely show the same information just in a different way?

comments.issue: No calculation of how long areas need to become profitable under carbon pricing.
comments.request: Add a rough profitability-timescale calculation under carbon pricing.
comments.quote: With the carbon accumulation rates and implementation and opportunity costs you could make a rough calculation of how long it would take for areas to become profitable under a carbon pricing scheme

comments.issue: Socioeconomic barriers to regeneration implementation, especially in the IndoMalay archipelago, are not mentioned.
comments.request: Briefly mention these barriers and cite Zeng et al. 2020.
comments.quote: I think it is crucial to at least briefly mention here that there are significant socioeconomic barriers to widespread regeneration implementation, particularly in the IndoMalay archipelago

comments.issue: Implications of the small holistic-hotspot area for carbon/biodiversity credit markets are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how holistic credit markets would function given these results.
comments.quote: The fact that a very small proportion of the area was identified as ‘holistic hotspots’ compared to hotspots for just carbon or just biodiversity would then effect how these holistic credits function

comments.issue: Displacing rural poor subsistence farmers may be an unaddressed social and economic justice issue.
comments.request: Discuss these justice issues and assess land use and population density.
comments.quote: If land in Southeast Asia has low opportunity costs due to the prevalence of small-scale and subsistence farming, are we just going to be displacing rural poor populations?

comments.issue: The livelihoods paragraph is vague and omits holistic/bundled credits, now increasingly popular.
comments.request: Discuss holistic/bundled credits, which link directly to the analyses.
comments.quote: it would be good to touch on holistic/bundled credits as they are increasing in popularity and directly linked to your analyses and results

comments.issue: It is unclear how forest regeneration would improve livelihoods and community resilience.
comments.request: Explain the mechanisms by which regeneration improves livelihoods.
comments.quote: can you touch on how forest regeneration can improve livelihoods and community resilience?

comments.issue: Implementation cost layer ignores remoteness and travel time to sites.
comments.request: At least mention this limitation of the cost layer.
comments.quote: another significant limitation of the implementation cost layer is that it does not consider remoteness or travel time to sites in the cost

comments.issue: Relevant cost-assessment literature (Brancalion et al. 2019) is not linked.
comments.request: Link Brancalion et al. 2019 on restoration cost components.
comments.quote: Brancalion et al. 2019 “What makes ecosystem restoration expensive? A systematic cost assessment of projects in Brazil” is a paper on the costs of different components of restoration that you could link here

comments.issue: Policy obstacles and interventions relevant to regeneration are not discussed.
comments.request: Add a sentence or two on relevant policy obstacles and interventions.
comments.quote: at least a sentence or two discussing some of the policy obstacles/interventions of relevance would be useful

comments.issue: One discussion paragraph does not link to the analysis and results.
comments.request: Remove or rework the paragraph to link to the findings, citing existing work.
comments.quote: this paragraph doesn’t really link well to the actual analysis and results in this manuscript, so I would suggest removing it to focus more on sections more related or rework it to link to the findings presented here

comments.issue: The sentence on seed dispersal for restoration lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Cite studies on seed dispersal for restoration.
comments.quote: there are plenty of studies on seed dispersal etc as important for restoration that could be referenced here to strengthen this sentence

reviews.assessment: Strongly positive: a notably novel integration of costs with carbon and biodiversity benefits, though the implementation-cost equation needs a major fix.
strengths: first to combine carbon and biodiversity benefits with NR costs

comments.issue: Figure 1 attributes only Cook-Patton et al. 2020 to its data circle; the other two studies are not similarly placed.
comments.request: Place the other two study citations under their respective circles.
comments.quote: The authors place “Cook-Patton et al. 2020” directly under the name of the circle to which it pertains, i.e., “Carbon accumulation.” They should do the same for the other two studies.

comments.issue: Claims to be the first comprehensive pantropical and first spatially explicit analysis overreach; Busch et al. 2024 did similar work.
comments.request: Temper the first-ness claims to the carbon-plus-biodiversity combination.
comments.quote: These sentences overreach. Busch et al. (2024) provide a spatially explicit analysis of NR costs and carbon sequestration benefits for LMICs, including tropical countries.

comments.issue: The paper presents an overly optimistic view of the forest carbon market, ignoring integrity concerns.
comments.request: Consult the 2025 State of the Voluntary Carbon Market and West et al. 2023.
comments.quote: The middle paragraph and some other parts of the paper present an overly optimistic view of the forest carbon market, which has been rocked in recent years by deep suspicions about its integrity.

comments.issue: The claim that natural regeneration is the most cost-effective pathway is contradicted by Busch et al.
comments.request: Qualify the cost-effectiveness claim with the conditions identified by Busch et al.
comments.quote: Busch et al. demonstrate that this statement is not true. NR is more cost-effective than planting only under certain conditions, which include sufficient natural seed sources being present, wood prices being low

comments.issue: It is unclear whether opportunity costs are annual or capitalized, and mixing annual costs with implementation costs is invalid.
comments.request: State the opportunity-cost measure and use a consistent capitalized measure.
comments.quote: I cannot determine whether the authors are using a capitalized opportunity cost measure. They should. Using an annual opportunity cost measure with the implementation cost estimates from Busch et al. does not make sense.

comments.issue: Including tree planting in natural regeneration implementation costs contradicts the Busch et al. estimates.
comments.request: Remove tree planting from the description of NR implementation costs.
comments.quote: The inclusion of “tree planting” must be a typo, as Busch et al. do not include it in their NR implementation cost estimates, which refer to NR systems that do not include tree planting.

comments.issue: The tropics are defined as 25°S-25°N rather than the standard 23.5°.
comments.request: Use the standard tropical boundaries or justify the choice.
comments.quote: The authors define the tropics as 25 S to 25 N. I know I’m being picky, but why not use the standard 23.5 S to 23.5 N?

comments.issue: Global Forest Watch data include all tree systems, so 'current forest cover' mislabels the data.
comments.request: Write 'current tree cover' instead of forest cover.
comments.quote: I believe the authors should write “current tree cover,” as the GFW data include all manner of tree systems, not only forests.

comments.issue: Stating that the authors determined regeneration likelihood overstates what was an assumption.
comments.request: Use 'We assumed' instead of 'We determined'.
comments.quote: We determined that natural regeneration is more likely

comments.issue: The equation C=(1−PNR)*I drives implementation cost to zero at full NR potential, inconsistent with data showing no zero-cost projects.
comments.request: Use the proposed adjusted equation scaling unassisted NR costs by 40%, as Vincent et al. did.
comments.quote: this result is inconsistent with the project-level implementation cost dataset analyzed by Busch et al. Their dataset includes no cases of zero implementation costs, not even for unassisted NR projects

comments.issue: The Busch et al. cost layer is misinterpreted as assisted NR; it refers to unassisted NR, which also incurs costs.
comments.request: Correct the NR definitions and revise the cost equation accordingly.
comments.quote: the modeled implementation cost layer that Busch et al. developed by analyzing their dataset refers to unassisted NR, not assisted NR as the authors of the current manuscript state on p. 17

reviews.assessment: Interesting synthesis addressing a broad question, but the biodiversity metric and cost adjustment lag behind best practice and likely bias the hotspot results.
strengths: addresses a question of broad interest

comments.issue: Increase in threatened species with some habitat restored does not capture spatial variation in extinction-risk reduction.
comments.request: Use per-species area of habitat tracking or the LIFE metric layer instead.
comments.quote: using the increase in the number of threatened species who have some of their habitat restored as your measure of biodiversity benefits does not properly capture spatial variation in how restoration can reduce species extinction risks

comments.issue: Southeast Asian hotspot finding likely reflects high threatened-species counts, including species threatened mainly by hunting, not restoration benefits.
comments.request: Reassess whether the hotspot pattern reflects genuine restoration benefits.
comments.quote: your finding that ‘holistic hotspots’ are focused in in Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia is largely driven by the preponderance of threatened species here

comments.issue: Zeroing implementation costs when NR potential is one is unrealistic; NR costs are about 66% lower than active restoration, not zero.
comments.request: Scale NR costs to 66% below active restoration, as Vincent et al. did.
comments.quote: The manuscript adopts an approach in which the implementation costs for natural regeneration when the potential for NR = 1 is zeroed out

comments.issue: Cook-Patton 2020 carbon data are outdated compared with Robinson et al., based on far more observations and nonlinear modeling.
comments.request: Consider using the updated Robinson et al. carbon accumulation layers.
comments.quote: We recommend that the authors consider employing the updated Robinson et al data

comments.issue: The carbon credit valuation cited covers all project types, including renewable energy, so it is misleading for restoration.
comments.request: Correct or qualify the carbon credit market valuation.
comments.quote: This is misleading as that is the total valuation of carbon credits across all project types, including renewable energy projects

comments.issue: Zero-cost areas are likely cyclical, ephemeral regeneration that is non-additional; persistent recovery requires some cost.
comments.request: Discuss that converting cyclical regeneration to persistent forest requires cost.
comments.quote: areas with very low costs (0, in your study) are likely to be areas already undergoing cyclical natural regeneration & disturbance cycles and might be ephemeral or “non-additional” from an intervention standpoint

comments.issue: Cost data rest on very few observations and are therefore highly uncertain.
comments.request: Note the limited observations underlying the cost data.
comments.quote: while the cost data is the best available dataset, they are built on very few observations (several hundred for all LMICs) and are therefore subject to great uncertainty

title: Variation in the costs and ecological benefits of tropical natural forest regeneration

study.system: global forest birds; incidence, forest cover and temperature data

reviews.assessment: Congratulates the authors on an elegant, well-supported study and offers major comments mainly to improve interpretation and framing.
strengths: conceptually elegant integration of macroclimate, microclimate and global bird data
central idea clearly supported by the analyses
strong fit for Nature Ecology & Evolution

comments.issue: Tmax from coarse range polygons represents an upper macroclimatic envelope, not temperatures experienced in forest microhabitats.
comments.request: Discuss that species may not occupy the hottest parts of their ranges.
comments.quote: it is best interpreted as the upper envelope of regional macroclimatic conditions associated with the mapped range, rather than temperatures necessarily experienced in the forest microhabitats where many populations occur

comments.issue: Tmax distance may reflect restricted climatic breadth for species spanning few ERA5 cells.
comments.request: Clarify the interpretation for species with narrow climatic ranges.
comments.quote: Please clarify how the Tmax-distance interpretation applies to species whose ranges span relatively few ERA5 grid cells or limited climatic variation.

comments.issue: Logger placement details are missing for the four validation datasets used to validate the microclimate model.
comments.request: Report logger height and forest cover/type for each validation dataset.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors provide a bit more detail on logger placement (height above ground and forest cover/type) for each validation dataset

comments.issue: The mechanistic microclimate component is not introduced early enough, so the study may seem purely macroclimate-driven.
comments.request: Introduce microclimate modelling briefly in the introduction.
comments.quote: Because mechanistic microclimate modelling is a major element of the analyses, I recommend introducing it more explicitly in the introduction

comments.issue: BIO05 may be sensitive to interannual variability, and it is unclear whether year 2000 was checked against longer-term climate.
comments.request: State whether 2000 was validated against a longer-term climate.
comments.quote: I suggest adding a brief statement on whether 2000 was checked against a longer-term climate for BIO05.

comments.issue: Figure 2C shows substantial species-level variation with slopes opposite to the mean trend, which is not quantified.
comments.request: Quantify the heterogeneity, e.g. proportions of positive and negative sensitivities.
comments.quote: It would be useful to explicitly quantify this heterogeneity (e.g., proportion of species with positive vs negative forest sensitivity at low vs high Tmax distance

comments.issue: Realm-level differences may reflect reduced power and uneven sampling rather than biology.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling limitations and report within-realm Tmax distributions.
comments.quote: This makes it difficult to distinguish genuine biological differences from reduced statistical power and uneven sampling.

comments.issue: The latitudinal narrative is not directly analysed and realms are internally heterogeneous.
comments.request: Add a latitude or biome analysis, or soften the latitudinal mechanism to a hypothesis.
comments.quote: latitude is not directly analysed, and realms contain substantial internal heterogeneity

comments.issue: Forest cover proportion does not capture forest structural variation across diverse biomes.
comments.request: Discuss this limitation to avoid overgeneralising the buffering mechanism.
comments.quote: a brief discussion acknowledging that “forest cover proportion” does not capture forest structural variation

comments.issue: Global-percentile Tmax distance bins are not comparable across species with different range sizes.
comments.request: Acknowledge that closeness to the warm limit is not comparable across species.
comments.quote: the same Tmax distance does not mean the same “closeness to the warm limit” for all species

comments.issue: How abundance or relative abundance was converted to incidence is not described.
comments.request: Clarify the conversion to incidence.
comments.quote: I suggest authors clarify how abundance/relative abundance were converted to incidence.

comments.issue: Random intercepts do not correct detection biases that covary with forest cover.
comments.request: Add a sentence clarifying this limitation.
comments.quote: random intercepts do not correct for detection biases that covary with forest cover

reviews.assessment: Praises the question and effort but doubts that forest cover effects can be interpreted as deforestation effects, and raises collinearity and analytical concerns.
strengths: great effort and care with extensive sensitivity analyses

comments.issue: Baseline forest cover confounds the analysis, so forest cover effects cannot be interpreted as effects of deforestation.
comments.request: Use matched deforested/baseline sites or reframe the question around forest cover.
comments.quote: the effect the study found of forest cover on species incidence (and its dependence on climate conditions) cannot provide really inference on possible effects of deforestation

comments.issue: The macroclimate metric may be collinear with seasonality and disturbance history, offering non-thermal explanations.
comments.request: Discuss alternative interpretations and be cautious about the thermal niche conclusion.
comments.quote: this metric could also be collinear with some other factors that can potentially affect how species responds to forest cover and that do not necessarily operate through the thermal niche angle

comments.issue: It is unclear why macroclimate rather than microclimate was used in the GLMMs testing incidence responses.
comments.request: Justify using macroclimate instead of going straight to microclimate.
comments.quote: Why not go straight to using microclimatic conditions – the actual climate conditions that are ecologically relevant to particularly forest species?

comments.issue: Using a blanket year-2000 forest cover layer may confound comparisons because surveys differ in year.
comments.request: Compile temporally relevant forest cover data for each study or address the confounding.
comments.quote: why the study did not choose to compile more temporally-relevant forest cover data for each primary study (presumably doable), but instead used a blanket time point of year 2000

comments.issue: Forest habitat dependence, a key trait, is not included among the functional traits considered.
comments.request: Include or discuss forest dependence given the loose species selection criteria.
comments.quote: the list of traits considered does not include what seems to me to be a most relevant trait – i.e., the level to which a given species is dependent on (native) forest habitat

comments.issue: It is unclear how the interspecific models test intraspecific variation and what the derivatives/partial effects provide.
comments.request: Explain or directly test intraspecific variation.
comments.quote: It is not clear to me why this is (why not more directly test for intraspecific variations), or how the interspecific models could inform on the intraspecific variations

comments.issue: Phylogenetic non-independence is not accounted for with phylogenetic regressions.
comments.request: Use phylogenetic regressions or justify the current approach.
comments.quote: why did the study not directly use phylogenetic regressions to account for species’ phylogenetic non-independence?

comments.issue: Key methodological information is missing from the main text, including species selection criteria, the 600-m buffer rationale and model structure.
comments.request: Move or clarify this information in the main text.
comments.quote: some important methodological information is missing from the main text (even though it is provided later in Methods)

comments.issue: How several methodological decisions were made is unexplained, including database timestamps, random intercept structure and trait list rationale.
comments.request: Explain how these methodological decisions were made.
comments.quote: for a number of important methodological decisions, the manuscript did not explain how they were made or done

title: Temperature mediates variation in avian sensitivity to forest cover

study.system: central-eastern Siberian intact forest landscapes; Landsat road mapping 2000–2023

editor_summary: Editor finds the work of considerable potential interest but says the substantial concerns raised must be addressed; a revised version would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Important objective and valuable insights, but findings largely repeat existing work and the data and methods are not novel.

comments.issue: Conclusions closely align with existing studies, which limits the novelty of the findings.
comments.quote: The conclusions closely align with existing studies, which may limit the novelty of the findings.

comments.issue: Data and methodology are not unique and have already appeared in numerous publications.
comments.quote: The data and methodology are not unique and have already been published in numerous publications

comments.issue: Global Forest Watch tree-cover-loss data are accurate enough to produce comparable results.
comments.quote: it is sufficiently accurate to produce results comparable to this analysis

comments.issue: Coarse Landsat resolution may miss roads; higher-resolution and radar or LiDAR data are recommended.
comments.request: Use higher-resolution and radar or LiDAR satellite data.
comments.quote: I recommend using higher-resolution data to identify locations that may have been missed due to coarse resolution and incorporating radar or LiDAR satellite data into the analysis

reviews.assessment: Clear, well written and suitable for publication after revisions, mainly better justified thresholds and a better explained GWR analysis.

comments.issue: Thresholds for indirect forest loss, edge effects and patch sizes are arbitrary and not grounded in the ecological literature.
comments.request: Justify thresholds with the literature or adopt established distances.
comments.quote: the thresholds for calculating indirect forest loss linked to roads, edge effects, and patch sizes seem arbitrary and do not appear to be well connected to existing literature

comments.issue: GWR is poorly explained: response and predictor variables, fitting function, package and spatial scale are unclear.
comments.request: Describe GWR variables, fitting method and spatial scale in the Methods.
comments.quote: the geographically weighted regression analysis does not appear to be well explained in the methods

comments.issue: Whether GWR residuals were tested for spatial autocorrelation is unclear, and residuals appear autocorrelated.
comments.request: Test and report spatial autocorrelation in the model residuals.
comments.quote: It is also not clear if the results were tested for spatial autocorrelation, and from the relevant supplementary figure it appears as if there remains spatial autocorrelation in the residuals.

comments.issue: Road widths may be inflated by the Landsat pixel size, biasing the digitized widths.
comments.request: Address the influence of pixel size on digitized road widths.
comments.quote: Roads may be smaller but would still appear as >30m width due to the Landsat pixel size?

comments.issue: Unclear whether forest types are over-represented in road expansion or simply dominate the area.
comments.request: Compare expansion shares against area shares with a chi-square test.
comments.quote: For example, ~83% of expansion was in forests, but if forests occupy ~83% of the study region than it is fairly represented

comments.issue: Road expansion at certain latitudes or elevations may just reflect the area distribution.
comments.request: Test whether these patterns differ from random chance.
comments.quote: In general, we expect to see more road expansion in flat areas and lowlands, but you can test if this is the case or if there is no difference from random chance.

comments.issue: The 100 m buffer is very narrow given evidence of road effects at 2-5 km, so forest loss is underestimated.
comments.request: Use wider buffers consistent with the literature.
comments.quote: 100m is a very narrow threshold for indirect impacts of roads on forest loss

comments.issue: Unclear whether remaining forests still qualify as frontier forest by any road-density threshold.
comments.request: Define a road-density threshold for frontier forest status.
comments.quote: Is there some threshold road density that would need to be met before it could not be considered “frontier forest”?

comments.issue: Which analysis supports the logging attribution is unclear; such loss may be classified under the forestry driver class.
comments.request: Show the analysis and consider newer driver-classification maps.
comments.quote: which specific analysis showed this? A lot of the forest loss was linked to logging which comes under the ‘forestry’ loss driver class from Curtis et al.

comments.issue: Code for this analysis is not available to readers.
comments.request: Make the code available or reference existing scripts.
comments.quote: is it possible to make the code for this available for readers? Or to reference where such scripts are already available?

comments.issue: How roads were digitized (polygons versus lines, binary raster) is confusing and unclear.
comments.request: Add a supplementary image showing digitized roads and how area and length were derived.
comments.quote: Were roads digitized by tracing polygons around the road pixels or by drawing a line through road pixels?

comments.issue: Validation may underestimate mapping consistency because of pixel-level labelling differences.
comments.request: Convert validation sets to 100 m presence/absence rasters and recalculate the matrix.
comments.quote: I would recommend perhaps also converting these validation datasets to 100m resolution presence/absence rasters and calculate the same validation matrix to get a better idea of the functional validity

comments.issue: The biomass product may poorly separate plantations from natural forest.
comments.request: Consider the Spatial Database on Planted Trees dataset.
comments.quote: how well does this data product separate plantations from natural forest? I believe in my experience it does a fairly poor job.

comments.issue: Narrow buffers for indirect road loss contradict evidence of strong effects at 2-5 km.
comments.request: Use wider buffers such as 2 km for indirect effects.
comments.quote: why choose such narrow buffers for the indirect forest loss due to roads? Other existing studies show that the indirect effects of roads are still strong at 2km and can extend to 5km or more

comments.issue: The fragment-size classes are not the most ecologically or conservation-relevant.
comments.request: Report more useful classes such as <1, 1-10 and 10-100 km2 fragments.
comments.quote: these classes for fragment sizes aren’t necessarily the most informative in terms of ecological or conservation relevance

comments.issue: Edge-effect buffer distances are less informative than distances reported in the literature.
comments.request: Use edge-effect distances reported in earlier studies.
comments.quote: It is generally reported that edge effects are strong up to 100m from the road and many persist up to and beyond 1km from the road

comments.issue: Small buffers for indirect loss likely underestimate biomass loss from road expansion.
comments.request: Use 30-60 m for direct loss and 1-2 km for indirect loss.
comments.quote: by using these small buffer distances you are likely underestimating the biomass loss associated with road expansion

comments.issue: Pearson correlation is inappropriate because road expansion and biomass loss are spatially autocorrelated.
comments.request: Use autologistic or residual autocovariance models and check residual autocorrelation.
comments.quote: both road expansion and biomass loss will be spatially autocorrelated and hence a Pearson correlation is likely not the best method to use here

comments.issue: Panel (a) lacks an extent indicator for the study region.
comments.request: Add an extent indicator like the one in Fig. S1.
comments.quote: Please include an extent indicator for the study region shown in panel (a)

comments.issue: Area and length axis labels waste space with full unit values.
comments.request: Report area and length in thousands of kilometres.
comments.quote: You can report area and length measurements in 1000’s kms to reduce the space taken up by the axis labels

comments.issue: Discrete buffer distances are less informative than a continuous distance-to-road variable.
comments.request: Use Euclidean distance to roads as a continuous variable.
comments.quote: rather than using discreet buffer distances, you can create a Euclidean distance to road layer and summarise IFL and biomass loss by distance to road as a continual variable

comments.issue: Logging roads hidden under the canopy mean the road-logging link is underestimated and its implications need discussion.
comments.request: Discuss that roads may be more tightly linked to logging and forest loss.
comments.quote: most logging roads would likely be difficult to digitize using Landsat imagery as they are under the forest canopy, and hence logging is probably more tightly linked to road expansion than you are able to quantify with your methods

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation may persist in the GWR residuals; Moran's I was not reported.
comments.request: Calculate Moran's I and consider a spatial Durbin model.
comments.quote: did you test if spatial autocorrelation was still present in the model residuals from the Geographically weighted regression?

comments.issue: The GWR remains insufficiently explained for readers.
comments.request: Explain the GWR analysis adequately for readers.
comments.quote: the GWR is not sufficiently explained for readers to understand what has been done

comments.issue: The methods behind Fig. S9 are unexplained, including how road versus logging or mining fragmentation was separated.
comments.request: Explain how road-driven and logging or mining fragmentation were separated.
comments.quote: I do not understand the methods that went into creating this figure

reviews.assessment: Well written and ambitious, but the methods and results need substantial revision before the implications can be realized.

comments.issue: Road delineation is not described well enough to replicate; unclear how width is mapped at 30 m and whether road or corridor is mapped.
comments.request: Describe road-versus-corridor mapping and how width was resolved at 30 m.
comments.quote: The method for road delineation is not described in enough detail that I could confidently replicate the method

comments.issue: Accuracy assessment compares pixel typing rather than vector mapping and reports substantial commission error.
comments.request: Explain the format mixing and adjust area estimates using the accuracy assessment.
comments.quote: the accuracy assessment evaluates the agreement of the coauthors typing of road/non-road pixels, rather than the vector format of the road mapping

comments.issue: Buffers of 30, 60 and 100 m differ from the 1 km buffer in the original IFL definition, making baseline and new IFL maps incomparable.
comments.request: Apply consistent IFL criteria across time points.
comments.quote: In the fragmentation analysis, using a different buffer means that the baseline IFLs (2000) and 2010/2023 IFLs (author generated) aren’t directly comparable

comments.issue: Fragmentation and edge results apply only to IFLs but are labelled as forest-wide.
comments.request: Rename to IFL fragmentation and edge areas or analyse all forests.
comments.quote: fragmentation and edge results should refer to ‘IFL fragmentation’ not ‘forest fragmentation’ and ‘IFL edge areas’ not ‘forest edge areas’

comments.issue: How vector road buffers were reconciled with the 100 m CCI biomass grid, and how partial overlap was handled, is unclear.
comments.request: Describe resolution reconciliation and handling of partial overlap.
comments.quote: it is unclear how the resolution of the vector format roads data (and its buffers in the edge effect biomass loss analysis) was reconciled with the resolution (100m) of the CCI biomass product

comments.issue: Losses are not tested for persistence, so deforestation versus temporary degradation cannot be distinguished.
comments.request: Discuss disturbance duration and re-evaluate the deforestation conclusions.
comments.quote: Without evaluating the duration of disturbance associated with road development, it isn’t possible to determine if road development is resulting in deforestation (permanent forest loss) or degradation (temporary forest loss)

comments.issue: Missing discussion of IFL management implications and differing perspectives on their relevance.
comments.request: Add discussion of IFL management implications with relevant literature.
comments.quote: The paper is missing critical discussion of the management implications of IFLs and the different perspectives on their relevance

comments.issue: No evaluation of whether protected areas are affected by road development.
comments.request: Assess impacts on protected areas using the WDPA.
comments.quote: the authors have missed an opportunity to evaluate if protected areas are impacted by road development

comments.issue: The phrase 'is a phenomenal feature' is unclear.
comments.request: Use 'is characteristic' instead.
comments.quote: “is a phenomenal feature” perhaps more clear as “is characteristic”

comments.issue: Manual digitization is no longer the primary method for forest road mapping.
comments.request: Acknowledge recent automated road-mapping literature.
comments.quote: Manual digitization is no longer the “primary method” for forest road mapping

comments.issue: Areas and lengths are reported to two decimal places, which is excessive precision.
comments.request: Round to the nearest whole number.
comments.quote: no need to present areas and lengths to 2 decimal places, round to nearest whole number

comments.issue: Changes in road length or area may simply reflect republic size rather than road development.
comments.request: Normalise by republic area or existing road length.
comments.quote: These results on changes in road length (or area) may be more useful if normalized (e.g., per km2 of republic area or per km of existing road)

comments.issue: Elevation does not indicate flatness; slope rather than elevation should support the flatter-areas claim.
comments.request: Analyse road distribution by slope instead of elevation.
comments.quote: the presence of roads in “flatter areas” would be indicated by the distribution of roads by slope, not by elevation

comments.issue: Discussion text is placed in the results section.
comments.request: Move the bolded text to the discussion.
comments.quote: Line 114-118: Bolded text is discussion, not result.

comments.issue: The unit of road expansion is unclear in the results, making the sentences appear contradictory.
comments.request: Include the scaling and unit in the results.
comments.quote: it is unclear what the unit of road expansion is in these sentences, so it is hard to understand why the sentences are contradictory

comments.issue: Total multi-year carbon loss is compared with annual sequestration rates, overstating the impact.
comments.request: Annualize the total carbon loss before comparison and revise the conclusions.
comments.quote: The total carbon loss should be annualized for a proper comparison and the associated conclusions in lines 199-202 should be reevaluated

comments.issue: The 'long lasting' edge-effects claim lacks a reference; the cited work concerns tropical biomass recovery.
comments.request: Add a reference supporting long-lasting edge effects.
comments.quote: Edge effects are “long lasting” requires a reference. The reference in the next line refers to recovery of biomass, not recovery of forest structure

comments.issue: Supplemental Fig 11, an ecoregion map, appears irrelevant to the sentence.
comments.request: Remove or replace the irrelevant figure.
comments.quote: Supplemental Fig 11 is an ecoregion map and seems irrelevant to this sentence

comments.issue: Details of Russia's climate, biodiversity and sustainability commitments are missing from this context.
comments.request: Add information on Russia's relevant commitments.
comments.quote: Additional details on what, if any, commitments Russia has made to climate, biodiversity, and sustainable is relevant and should be included here

comments.issue: The ecoregional analysis appears in the methods but not in the results or discussion.
comments.request: Remove it from the methods or report it.
comments.quote: the ecoregional analysis is not described in the results or discussed, so could be excluded from the methods

comments.issue: Lines connecting points on a non-linear axis misleadingly suggest trends.
comments.request: Use a linear x-axis or plot points without connecting lines.
comments.quote: either use a linear x-axis scale or only plot the point (no line connecting points)

title: Fourfold increase in fragmentation from road expansion in Siberian intact forests since 2000

study.system: North American forests; tree insects and pathogens, FIA data

editor_summary: Reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but Reviewer 2 raises major conceptual and analytical criticisms; editor requests a revision with point-by-point responses.

reviews.assessment: Novel, useful study with well-articulated motivation, but projections beyond the US and future forest structure inputs need justification.
strengths: important insight into forest pest and pathogen dynamics
useful to researchers, land managers and policy makers

comments.issue: US-only data are used to infer and project across all North American forests.
comments.request: Justify projecting beyond the US in the text.
comments.quote: Your empirical data are constrained to the United States, yet you make inferences and projections for all North American forested areas.

comments.issue: Future forest structure inputs (source, time period, scale mismatch) are unspecified.
comments.request: Describe the future forest structure data and scale handling.
comments.quote: Yet, you do not specify what future forest structure data were used to generate your projections.

comments.issue: Disturbance-driven changes in forest structure (outbreak feedbacks, wildfire) are ignored, likely overestimating incidence.
comments.request: Account for disturbance-induced structure change or temper projections.
comments.quote: Failing to account for disturbance-induced forest structure change may therefore lead to overestimates in future insect and pathogen incidence.

comments.issue: Forest area statistics at L36-38 rely on sources over 20 years old.
comments.request: Update with recent estimates or add a caveat.
comments.quote: These statistics and cited study were published over 20 years ago.

comments.issue: Whether both models operate at the tree population level is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the level and covariates of both models.
comments.quote: It seems that both models reflect pest incidence at the tree population level (i.e., trees of a single species within a plot), with the second model including more species-level covariates. Please clarify.

comments.issue: The 'j' index makes the model notation hard to parse.
comments.request: Remove the unnecessary index if models are fit separately.
comments.quote: I found the notation here difficult to parse due to the inclusion of the ‘j’ index in the equations.

comments.issue: Multiple tree populations per plot are combined without a plot random effect.
comments.request: Add a random effect for plot location.
comments.quote: That being the case, I would suggest also include a random effect for plot location to account for the spatial structure of the data.

comments.issue: How the binary indicator variable entered the model is unclear; host-only filtering may be better.
comments.request: Explain the indicator's role or filter to host trees.
comments.quote: How was the binary indicator variable incorporated into the model? Was it included as a covariate with a coefficient that was estimated by the model?

comments.issue: Posterior summary statistics and diagnostics are not provided.
comments.request: Add posterior summaries and diagnostics to the supplement.
comments.quote: Please provide posterior distribution summary statistics and diagnostics in the supplemental materials.

comments.issue: The projection resolution is unclear.
comments.request: Confirm whether projections are at 5 arc-minute resolution.
comments.quote: Does this mean your projections are 5 arc-minute resolution? Please clarify.

comments.issue: Fig. 1b color scale is counterintuitive.
comments.request: Flip the scale so blue is cool and brown is warm.
comments.quote: I suggest flipping the color scale so that blue corresponds with “cool” and brown corresponds with “warm”.

comments.issue: Color scales are not colorblind-friendly.
comments.request: Use a colorblind-friendly scale.
comments.quote: In these panels and elsewhere, I suggest changing the color scale to one that is colorblind-friendly.

comments.issue: Fig. 4d y-axis label does not match the caption.
comments.request: Change the y-axis label to match the caption.
comments.quote: Fig 4d: Change y-axis label to

reviews.assessment: Impressive, timely dataset, but the thermal mismatch framing, combined FIP models and forecasts are not convincing without major rework.

comments.issue: The thermal mismatch hypothesis is conceptualized incorrectly (hot places stressed by cold weather).
comments.request: Rethink the hypothesis or use a different one.
comments.quote: The thermal mismatch hypothesis (Fig 1) is conceptualized in a way that unfortunately I fundamentally disagree with.

comments.issue: Interaction design captures nonlinear FIP fitness curves, not thermal mismatches.
comments.request: Redesign the model to capture the TMH or reframe as a climate-impacts analysis.
comments.quote: Currently I think your design with interactions of historical climate is capturing nonlinear fitness curves of FIPs, not their mismatches

comments.issue: The drought mismatch explanation is unclear and unsupported.
comments.request: Justify the directionality of the drought mismatch.
comments.quote: Much more justification and clarification are needed to support this directionality of your TMH.

comments.issue: Mismatch should focus on hot/dry places becoming hotter/drier; cold-shock reasoning ignores plant-FIP differences.
comments.request: Reframe the hypothesis around hot/dry intensification.
comments.quote: I would expect that most of the mismatch in fitness that is likely quantifiable in your data would occur when hot or dry places become hotter or drier or both

comments.issue: Insects and pathogens should not be modelled together given highly unbalanced data.
comments.request: Model and forecast insects and pathogens separately.
comments.quote: at minimum I would not model FIPs in one model, especially if you have highly unbalanced data

comments.issue: Climate-insect/pathogen relationships are likely nonlinear but models do not account for this.
comments.request: Model the nonlinearities or show they are absent.
comments.quote: I would expect that the underlying relationships between climate and insects and pathogens are nonlinear (especially looking at Fig 3); the models should account for these nonlinearities

comments.issue: Tree-level models lack plot random or fixed effects.
comments.request: Add plot effects to control diversity and density.
comments.quote: Tree-level models should include plot random effects or fixed effects; these would help control for tree diversity and density effects as well

comments.issue: Many interaction terms and the climate niche variable are unjustified and may bias climate estimates.
comments.request: Justify interactions and remove distracting trait analyses.
comments.quote: Models include a lot of interaction terms; why is climate niche included, how is it quantified?

comments.issue: Forecasts from the combined FIP models are inconsistent and should be removed.
comments.request: Remove forecasts using FIP models.
comments.quote: Remove forecasts using models of FIPs – both insects and pathogens. The combined model is giving inconsistent results for pathogens anyway

comments.issue: Forecasting beyond US FIA data will produce biased results.
comments.request: Constrain forecasts with CABI data or drop them.
comments.quote: Since you don’t have observations outside of the US—forecasting beyond the FIA data will produce very biased results.

comments.issue: Calling these species 'pests' is misleading in forest systems.
comments.request: Use 'insects' and a different umbrella term such as FIPs.
comments.quote: Many of these species are not pests—they are important disturbance agents that can support forest resilience.

comments.issue: Multiple terms are used for the thermal mismatch hypothesis.
comments.request: Define each term carefully.
comments.quote: Authors use many terms to describe thermal mismatch hypothesis–define each carefully

comments.issue: How severity and incidence were estimated is barely explained.
comments.request: Clarify the estimation of severity and incidence.
comments.quote: unclear how severity and incidence are estimated; little explanation in the methods; please clarify how you estimated these results

comments.issue: Climate scenarios are not always stated when discussing outcomes.
comments.request: State the scenario and use the more realistic one.
comments.quote: When explaining climate change outcomes, please be careful to state which scenario is being used

comments.issue: Pathogen identification likely yields more false negatives than insect IDs.
comments.request: Explain this in the methods and caveat the differing impacts.
comments.quote: you likely have a lot more false negatives for pathogens, particularly those with symptomology that is difficult to detect in the field

comments.issue: Log transformation and min-max normalization are unjustified.
comments.request: Justify them and show sensitivity to normalization choice.
comments.quote: Justify use of log transformation and min-max normalization; add a supplement showing the choice of normalization does not produce your desired results

comments.issue: The negative precipitation-FIP relationship contradicts pathogen moisture requirements.
comments.request: Do not use the general model to explain these relationships.
comments.quote: Why would increases in precip lead to decreases in FIPs? Many pathogens require high moisture to reproduce; you would expect the opposite to be true for many pathogen species.

comments.issue: How intensification was quantified is unclear.
comments.request: Define the intensification metric.
comments.quote: L401: how is intensification quantified exactly?

comments.issue: Significance testing is unhelpful with such a large sample size.
comments.request: Report differences instead of significance.
comments.quote: why is significance testing necessary? Such a large sample size is very likely to produce significant results? Stating the differences is more meaningful

comments.issue: The L140 claim may not hold given pathogen false negatives.
comments.request: Reconsider this statement.
comments.quote: L140: not sure this is true given many false negatives of pathogens

comments.issue: Whether L71 uses an average of climate variables over the survey period is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the climate variable definition.
comments.quote: is this an average of the climate variables during survey period?

comments.issue: Marginal effects of interactions are not shown.
comments.request: Add a figure of marginal interaction effects.
comments.quote: A figure showing the marginal effects of the interactions of interest is important – otherwise it’s hard to interpret the interaction effects (they can be negative at some ranges and positive at others)

comments.issue: Figure 3 shows a nonlinear relationship that should be modelled directly.
comments.request: Model the nonlinear relationship instead of separated effects.
comments.quote: Figure 3 is showing a nonlinear relationship; I would just model this nonlinear relationship and show that rather than the separated effects

reviews.assessment: Excited by the creative use of FIA data and strong Bayesian models; asks about dataset bias and climate extrapolation.
strengths: creative and effective use of FIA data
Bayesian models balance complexity and generality

comments.issue: Potential spatial bias between ERA5 and Worldclim 1.4 could confound interaction coefficients.
comments.request: Comment on and rule out this bias.
comments.quote: Could the authors comment on the potential for bias, or known bias, in the relationship between those 2 data sources (ERA5 Reanalysis, Worldclim 1.4)?

comments.issue: Projections extrapolate into locally novel future climates without quantifying this.
comments.request: Quantify extrapolation and add uncertainty figures.
comments.quote: Can the authors comment on the role of extrapolation in the model projections to future climates? In every location, under intense warming, the conditions will be locally novel.

comments.issue: The model type is not specific at L110.
comments.request: Name the model, e.g., Bayesian hierarchical binomial regression.
comments.quote: I suggest being a little more specific about the model here - e.g. Bayesian hierarchical binomial regression?

comments.issue: Wording at L195 ('intensify') is queried.
comments.request: Reconsider the wording.
comments.quote: 195 — “intensify”

comments.issue: Aggregating monthly climate to a single year is not justified; a 3-5 year average may be more stable.
comments.request: Explain the timescale choice.
comments.quote: My intuition would be that a more stable estimate of contemporary climate that might better explain pest and pathogen patterns would be something more like an average of the previous 3 to 5 years

comments.issue: Wording at L262 ('databases') is queried.
comments.request: Reconsider the wording.
comments.quote: L262 — “databases”?

comments.issue: Wording at L346 ('Identity') is queried.
comments.request: Reconsider the wording.
comments.quote: L346 — “Identity”?

comments.issue: Min-max scaling was chosen over standard-deviation scaling without explanation.
comments.request: Justify the scaling choice.
comments.quote: I have no huge objection to min-max scaling, but wonder why it was chosen rather than the more-robust-to-outliers and more common scaling by standard deviation?

comments.issue: The trait figure S7 could be moved to the main text.
comments.request: Consider moving Fig. S7 to the main text.
comments.quote: in general, these are outstanding. I’d consider moving the trait figure (S7) to the main text if there’s room.

title: Spatially explicit forecasts of tree insect and disease incidence across North American forests under future climate scenarios

study.system: flatworm and cnidarian cell types; single-cell ATAC/RNA and deep learning

editor_summary: Editor finds potential interest but decides against publication because reviewers doubt the strength of the novel conclusions that can be drawn at this stage.

reviews.assessment: Very valuable, well-written and meticulous study with no major issues, only minor clarity and reporting points.

comments.issue: Absence of line numbers makes citing specific parts difficult.
comments.request: Add line numbers.
comments.quote: There are no line numbers which make pointing to particular parts of the manuscript difficult

comments.issue: No dimensionality reduction plot shows the identified clusters although UMAP is mentioned.
comments.request: Show the cluster UMAP.
comments.quote: A dimensionality reduction plot showing the clusters identified for snRNAseq and snATACseq datasets would be useful

comments.issue: Whether bulk or single-cell/nuclei ATACseq and RNAseq are used is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the data types explicitly.
comments.quote: it is unclear which types of ATACseq and RNAseq data are referred to. Bulk or single cell/nuclei?

comments.issue: Which data identified clusters and how the two modalities were integrated is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the clustering inputs and integration.
comments.quote: It is unclear which data was used to identify the clusters, snRNAseq or snATACseq or both, and how the integration of the two was performed.

comments.issue: The type of motifs should be made clear for non-specialist readers.
comments.request: Clarify what type of motifs are meant.
comments.quote: when writing “motifs”, it would be better to make clear what type of motifs, to make it easier to understand also for a non specialized reader

comments.issue: The base pair range around gene bodies is unclear.
comments.request: State the range used.
comments.quote: the base pair range around gene bodies is unclear

comments.issue: What patterns means in the matched patterns sentence is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify what is meant by patterns.
comments.quote: specify what is meant by “patterns”

comments.issue: SAMap applied to snATACseq data is new and unexplained.
comments.request: Explain how SAMap works on such data.
comments.quote: Since it is the first time that this algorithm is used on such data, it would be appropriate to mention how it works in this regard.

comments.issue: Whether conserved across evolution rather than within a cell type family is correct is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the direction of conservation.
comments.quote: in this case, conserved across evolution, not within a cell-type family, is it correct?

comments.issue: Table S1 is cited but does not exist in the document.
comments.request: Identify the correct table file.
comments.quote: Table S1 is mentioned but there is no such table in the document.

comments.issue: Which type of clusters is meant at Page 5 is unspecified.
comments.request: Give specifics on the clusters.
comments.quote: give specifics on which type of clusters

comments.issue: The Page 6 sentence appears out of place and the data type behind accessibility is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the data type and context.
comments.quote: seems a bit out of place written as it is. The paragraph above does not explicitly specify which data type is referred to, so it is unclear where accessibility comes from

comments.issue: Technical phrases like average motif deviations and minimum conserved structure are undefined.
comments.request: Define these phrases.
comments.quote: Meaning of phrases such as “motifs dictating accessibility”, “average motif deviations”, “minimum conserved structure” is unclear.

comments.issue: Descriptions of chromVar and ChromBPNet mechanisms are too short.
comments.request: Extend the explanations of these tools.
comments.quote: It would be useful if short descriptions of functions and mechanisms of chromVar and ChromBPNet could be extended

comments.issue: No pipeline flowchart of datatypes, software and models.
comments.request: Add a pipeline flowchart.
comments.quote: A pipeline flowchart with all the datatypes, software and models used could be very useful.

comments.issue: What family-level accessibility refers to is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify that it means cell type families.
comments.quote: is cell type families referred to here and in other places where family-level is mentioned?

comments.issue: The purpose of accessibility predictions is unclear and Fig. 5 omits them alongside actual data.
comments.request: Explain the predictions and show them with actual data.
comments.quote: it is unclear why the predictions were made in the first place if actual data was generated? Why do the plots in Fig.5 not show predictions along with actual data?

comments.issue: Motif vocabulary is not well defined, especially for distant comparisons.
comments.request: Define the term clearly.
