comments.quote: Meaning and definition of “motif vocabulary” used throughout the text is not well explained.

comments.issue: The scope of the collective maintenance model is not discussed.
comments.request: Comment in the discussion on how far the model extends.
comments.quote: it would be interesting to know to which extent the ‘collective maintenance’ model proposed in Fig. 1b could be extended. The authors should comment on that in the discussion.

comments.issue: Extended Data Fig. 4a legend omits (bottom).
comments.request: Add (bottom) to the legend.
comments.quote: Extended Data Fig. 4a: add “(bottom)” in the figure legend.

comments.issue: Fig. 4b and d identify motif clusters only by colour.
comments.request: Add cluster ID numbers in the plotted boxes.
comments.quote: Fig. 4b and d could benefit from motif cluster identities specified not only by a color but also by an ID number of the cluster stated in the plotted boxes.

comments.issue: Arrowheads on heatmap x axes are confusing and inconsistently directional.
comments.request: Replace arrows with plain lines or blunt ends.
comments.quote: Why are arrows used in x axes in heatmaps? Also, sometimes they are unidirectional some other times are bidirectional, this is confusing.

comments.issue: Software versions are not stated for most packages.
comments.request: Report versions for all software.
comments.quote: Versions are not stated for most software packages e.g. for Chromap, createArrowFiles, kallisto-bustools, STARsolo, Signac and others?

reviews.assessment: Exciting new approach, but major claims about motif vocabulary conservation and synonymy lack convincing support.
strengths: exciting new approach to cell type evolution
comparative single-cell ATAC analysis across platyhelminths

comments.issue: Genome accessibility evolving independently of sequence is difficult to conceptualise.
comments.request: Reframe around evolving TF activity and resulting chromatin landscapes.
comments.quote: it is challenging to conceptualize how “genome accessibility” can independently evolve

comments.issue: SAMap cell types based on gene scores may add little; comparison with expression-based typing is missing.
comments.request: Compare with gene expression-based cell type comparisons.
comments.quote: the SAMap-aligned cell types based on gene scores seem to offer limited additional value

comments.issue: The claim that accessibility is conserved within families rather than cell types is confusing and could reflect lack of correspondence.
comments.request: Test whether expression data align cell types better.
comments.quote: Alternatively, could this result simply reflect a lack of conservation between the species’ cell types rather than a specific property of chromatin accessibility?

comments.issue: Raw data visualizations such as 2D projections and accessibility heatmaps are absent.
comments.request: Include these visualizations.
comments.quote: The raw data, such as 2D projections of single-cell data or accessibility heatmaps used to derive clusters, is noticeably absent. Including such visualizations would greatly enhance interpretability.

comments.issue: Extended Data Figure 1 QC plots show only pre-filtered data.
comments.request: Show all data points.
comments.quote: In Extended Data Figure 1 the authors should show all data points in the QC plots, not pre-filtered.

comments.issue: Only 8 cell types were retained despite many more being identified, e.g. neuronal types.
comments.request: Justify the cell type retention criteria.
comments.quote: the authors seem to have identified many more than 8 cell types in their data, which is more in agreement with published scRNA-seq atlases

comments.issue: The deep learning motif approach is not benchmarked against classic enrichment or other DL approaches.
comments.request: Compare performance with MEME/Homer and alternative DL designs.
comments.quote: It would be important to compare the performance of this approach (in finding sequence motifs) with (a) more “classic” de novo motif enrichment analyses

comments.issue: Strategy for reducing redundancy in TF-MoDISco motifs is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the motif grouping and redundancy criteria.
comments.quote: The authors should discuss their strategy for reducing redundancy in TF-MoDISco-identified motifs in greater detail.

comments.issue: Keeping JASPAR reference motifs instead of DL-inferred versions needs justification.
comments.request: Explain this choice and how novel motifs relate to references.
comments.quote: When compiling a consensus set of motifs, the authors chose to keep JASPAR reference motifs rather than the similar motifs inferred from the data using deep learning (DL) models.

comments.issue: How contribution-score filtering handles JASPAR motifs missed by DL models is unclear.
comments.request: Explain and report the final number of motifs per peak.
comments.quote: how does this method handle JASPAR motifs not detected by DL models? It would also be informative to report the final number of motifs per peak.

comments.issue: Evidence that motif combinations are poorly conserved is unconvincing without positive controls.
comments.request: Compare combinations for strongly conserved genes and quantify conserved versus divergent combinations.
comments.quote: The lack of "positive control" examples of conservation puts in question that the reported lack of conservation could be a methodological issue, rather than a biological signal.

comments.issue: It is not clear that deep learning models learn conserved vocabularies from the deviation correlation analysis.
comments.request: Check whether the analysis also works for specific cell type definitions.
comments.quote: From this analysis alone it is not directly clear if deep learning models indeed learn the conserved motif vocabularies.

comments.issue: The cnidarian comparison is underwhelming because data resolutions are not comparable.
comments.request: Temper the cnidarian claims.
comments.quote: The comparison with cnidarians is rather underwhelming, despite this analysis is highlighted in the abstract.

comments.issue: The neural-muscle association, a major claim, is insufficiently supported.
comments.request: Show motifs and accessibilities supporting this association directly.
comments.quote: showing in more detail the motifs and accessibilities supporting the neural-muscle association, which is a major claim of the article (insufficiently supported)

comments.issue: Results do not robustly support the vocabulary conservation hypothesis.
comments.request: Strengthen the support and discuss the CoRC model implications.
comments.quote: the results and their presentation do not robustly support this hypothesis, even across the three platyhelminth species analyzed

reviews.assessment: Elegant design but claims about accessibility evolution and synonymous motifs are overstated or unsupported.
strengths: addresses deep properties of chromatin accessibility evolution

comments.issue: The claim that accessibility evolves faster than sequence is overly broad and misleading.
comments.request: Qualify the generalisation.
comments.quote: The statement “This suggests that genome accessibility evolves even faster than the sequence itself” appears to be overly broad and potentially misleading.

comments.issue: Second paragraph on Page 5 lacks cohesive flow and integration of accessibility and transcription data.
comments.request: Integrate the two aspects and add UMAP visualizations.
comments.quote: The second paragraph lacks cohesive flow and clear logical connections between its components.

comments.issue: The Page 6 conclusion about accessibility conservation is disconnected from the evidence.
comments.request: Provide direct evidence or revise the conclusion.
comments.quote: the final statement about chromatin accessibility conservation seems unsupported by the presented data

comments.issue: Motif analysis is not validated against expression of the corresponding transcription factors.
comments.request: Check whether enriched motifs match cognate TF expression.
comments.quote: The analysis of cell type-specific motifs should be complemented by examining the expression patterns of their corresponding transcription factors in each cell type.

comments.issue: How motifs are classified as shared versus cell-type specific is unexplained and unsupported.
comments.request: Explain the classification system and quantitative criteria.
comments.quote: the authors need to better explain their classification system. How exactly are motifs categorized as both "shared" and "cell-type specific"?

comments.issue: P-value framework, background model, multiple testing and artifacts of motif co-occurrence are unaddressed.
comments.request: Describe the statistics and validate the biological relevance of co-occurrences.
comments.quote: the statistical framework for calculating P-values in motif co-occurrence analysis needs to be explicitly described

comments.issue: Extent and artefact risk of the 25 cnidarian neuron motifs are unclear.
comments.request: Quantify enrichment and rule out species-specific sequence artefacts.
comments.quote: To what extent are these 25 motifs enriched? Also, is the combination of these 25 motifs functionally meaningful and not the result of artifacts?

comments.issue: How divergent motif combinations yield conserved expression in homologous cell types remains unexplained.
comments.request: Explore the regulatory mechanism resolving this paradox.
comments.quote: How do these divergent regulatory patterns ultimately result in conserved gene expression patterns in homologous cell types?

comments.issue: Peaks at similar positions are not validated as truly homologous.
comments.request: Test whether positional similarity is coincidental.
comments.quote: the authors need to validate whether these peaks are truly homologous. The mere presence of peaks at similar locations does not necessarily indicate functional homology.

comments.issue: Synonymous motifs is overstated; only predictive capability is shown, not functional equivalence.
comments.request: Demonstrate functional substitution or temper the term.
comments.quote: The claim of "synonymous motifs" appears to be overstated based on the presented evidence.

comments.issue: Abstract phrase evolve into a hierarchy is logically flawed.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence.
comments.quote: The phrase "evolve into a hierarchy" is logically flawed - the hierarchy is an organizational concept we use to describe relationships, not something cell types evolve into.

comments.issue: Conclusion overclaims providing stability and constraining diversification beyond predictive evidence.
comments.request: Rewrite the concluding sentence as proposed.
comments.quote: The conclusion makes a broad claim about "providing stability" and "constraining diversification" that goes beyond the evidence presented, which only shows predictive relationships.

comments.issue: Figure 3a lacks bootstrap values and linkage to gene expression.
comments.request: Report bootstrap support and relate it to expression.
comments.quote: Is there bootstrap value for the clustering of neural-muscle-parenchymal? How is this related with gene expression?

comments.issue: Figure 3 is missing the panel label d.
comments.request: Add the missing panel label.
comments.quote: Figure 3. The panel label 'd' is missing.

title: Flexible use of conserved motifs constrains genome access in cell type evolution

study.system: plant–pollinator networks; global dataset of >3,400 networks

editor_summary: Editor finds the work of potential interest but cites substantial concerns on presentation and interpretation of results and the conclusions; a major revision is invited.

reviews.assessment: Sees a valuable dataset but argues the LSG evidence is weak and inconsistent, needing clearer definitions, marginal R² reporting, restructuring and bias acknowledgement.
strengths: relevant potential issues and biases considered

comments.issue: The LSG definition is too vague, encompassing any non-random latitudinal variation, so evidence criteria are unclear.
comments.request: Define the LSG precisely and specify predictions that count as evidence.
comments.quote: This definition is too vague, potentially encompassing any non-random variation in interaction specialization

comments.issue: No schematic summarizes predicted versus observed LSG patterns.
comments.request: Add a schematic figure of predicted and observed patterns.
comments.quote: I suggest including a schematic figure (e.g., something like Fig. S1) summarizing predicted and observed patterns.

comments.issue: The claim that the LSG exists is internally contradictory and not supported by weak, inconsistent results.
comments.request: Revise the interpretation to reflect weak and inconsistent support.
comments.quote: In my view, this sentence is internally contradictory, and it is not well supported by the results.

comments.issue: Marginal R² and marginal effects are missing, so variance explained by climatic predictors is unknown.
comments.request: Report marginal R² and marginal effects for all models.
comments.quote: since marginal R2 values are not presented, it is not possible to infer how much variation in interaction specialization the selected climatic predictors actually explain

comments.issue: Presenting three datasets in the main text is confusing; functional-group networks should be the focus.
comments.request: Focus on functional-group networks and move other datasets to the supplement.
comments.quote: The presentation of the results for the three datasets in the main text is unnecessary and a source of confusion

comments.issue: Differences among pollinator groups need a better discussion of underlying mechanisms.
comments.request: Discuss potential mechanisms behind pollinator-group differences.
comments.quote: These results show some interesting differences and similarities among pollinator groups that demand a better discussion of potential mechanisms

comments.issue: Geographic and taxonomic clustering means region captures biogeographic differences confounded with latitude.
comments.request: Acknowledge these biases and discuss limits to latitudinal inference.
comments.quote: The dataset exhibits substantial geographic clustering that may confound latitudinal interpretation.

comments.issue: Hemispheric asymmetry claims are hard to interpret given sparse Southern Hemisphere coverage.
comments.request: Acknowledge limited Southern Hemisphere data when interpreting asymmetry.
comments.quote: Claims about “hemispheric asymmetry” are difficult to interpret biologically given the limited Southern Hemisphere data

comments.issue: Using sampling completeness as model weights may systematically downweight tropical networks.
comments.request: Use a completeness threshold or covariate instead of weights.
comments.quote: Using sampling completeness as model weights is problematic and might introduce systematic bias.

reviews.assessment: Finds the dataset remarkable and the topic compelling, but cannot match the text's latitudinal claims to the figures and doubts that climate is the main driver.
strengths: topic of great interest to the field

comments.issue: The tropics and northern mid-latitudes are undefined and unmarked, so text claims cannot be matched to Figure 3.
comments.request: Define latitudinal zones and add reference lines to Figure 3.
comments.quote: I don't see a definition of what is considered the “the tropics” or “northern mid-latitudes” in the text, and they are not marked on the x axes.

comments.issue: Whether main pattern descriptions hold under alternative tropical/subtropical definitions is untested.
comments.request: Show robustness to latitudinal definitions or report sensitivity.
comments.quote: I think the description of the main patterns should be robust to +/– a few latitudinal degree differences in e.g., what the tropics are defined as, or this sensitivity should be reported

comments.issue: Model-selection criteria are unclear: MAT x MAP was chosen for pollinators despite not having the lowest AIC.
comments.request: Explain best-model criteria and report AICs in the main text.
comments.quote: I don't understand why MAT x MAP was chosen as the best predictor for pollinators when it does not have the lowest AIC

comments.issue: The provided code fails to run and the README lacks setup instructions.
comments.request: Add instructions for running the code.
comments.quote: running the code I got “Error: Could not connect to database: unable to open database file” so some additional instructions in the README would be helpful

title: Global patterns in plant–pollinator specialization

study.system: salmonid gene-regulatory evolution; multiomics across development and tissues

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers raised concerns to address before publication; invites a revision responding to all reviewer and editorial comments, with changes highlighted in Word.

reviews.assessment: Incredible, well-written resource; comments focus on technical validation, reproducibility and clarity and should be straightforward to address.
strengths: unprecedented insights into ohnolog regulatory evolution

comments.issue: The high-quality dataset claim lacks quality-control metrics.
comments.request: Add mapping, duplication and FRiP metrics to Table S3.
comments.quote: I would recommend more rigorous technical validation, such as adding quality control metrics in Table S3 for the RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and ChIP-seq libraries.

comments.issue: Replicate reproducibility is not demonstrated.
comments.request: Add a BAM coverage correlation matrix or heatmap.
comments.quote: a BAM coverage correlation matrix (Pearson or Spearman) or a heatmap would greatly strengthen the evidence for the reproducibility and technical integrity of their replicates

comments.issue: IDR merged peak numbers per replicate set are missing from Figures S5-S9.
comments.request: Include the IDR merged peak number for each replicate set.
comments.quote: Please also include the IDR merged peak number for each set of replicates.

comments.issue: Gonad ChIP-seq is missing in trout, and downstream cross-species analyses rely mainly on salmon.
comments.request: Assess whether the design asymmetry affects cross-species comparisons.
comments.quote: The experimental design is largely consistent between Atlantic salmon and rainbow trout, except for the lacking of Gonad ChIP-seq in trout.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether one third of genes were excluded from the DevMap and BodyMap analyses.
comments.request: Clarify the gene sets and discuss representativeness biases.
comments.quote: If so, does that mean at least one third of genes in each genome were excluded? Please clarify and discuss any potential biases would be introduced due to limited representativeness.

comments.issue: SOM grid dimensions and topology lack justification.
comments.request: State how grid dimensions were determined and any optimization criterion.
comments.quote: Please specify how the grid dimensions (e.g., x‑y size, topology) were determined. Was an optimization criterion used (e.g., minimal quantization error)?

comments.issue: Criteria distinguishing constitutive and condition-specific SOM clusters are unclear.
comments.request: State quantitative thresholds used for the classification.
comments.quote: beyond visual inspection, were any quantitative thresholds applied (e.g., coefficient of variation, proportion of samples showing activity)? Explicitly stating the criteria would improve reproducibility.

comments.issue: Figure 2 is difficult to read, especially the Sankey diagrams.
comments.request: Split heatmap and Sankey panels and place legends adjacent.
comments.quote: Figure 2 is rich in information but quite difficult to read, particularly the Sankey‑style diagrams linking salmon and trout SOM clusters.

comments.issue: The UMAP caption phrasing is ambiguous about what each dot represents.
comments.request: Rephrase to say the UMAP shows each feature’s multivariate profile.
comments.quote: This phrasing is ambiguous. I assume the UMAP embeddings are calculated from the normalized expression/accessibility profiles across stages, and each dot corresponds to a gene or a chromatin region.

comments.issue: Whether Early and Late rediploidization classes enrich in specific SOM clusters is untested.
comments.request: Trace ohnolog partitioning into SOM clusters by rediploidization class.
comments.quote: It would be very informative to know whether these two classes are enriched in specific SOM clusters from the DevMap or BodyMap analyses.

comments.issue: Exclusive enhancers may lie farther from TSSs where TE content is higher, confounding the TE-overlap result.
comments.request: Repeat the TE-overlap analysis binning enhancers by distance to TSS.
comments.quote: One potential confounding factor is that exclusive enhancers might be located farther from transcription start sites on average, and TE content is known to increase with distance from genes.

reviews.assessment: Most impressive, nearly immaculate dataset and original focus, but interpretation loose ends and language consistency need attention.
strengths: original focus on rediploidization and ohnolog evolution

comments.issue: Differences in developmental rate between species are not explained or put in perspective.
comments.request: Explain how developmental rate is accounted for and discuss its implications.
comments.quote: How the developmental rate is taken into account in the analyses needs to be better explained and put this into perspective when discussing the results.

comments.issue: The motivation statement at lines 66-67 is too vague.
comments.request: Make specific how functional outcomes of rediploidization inform species radiations.
comments.quote: Lines 66-67: I suggest making this motivation statement more specific. How does knowing the functional outcomes of rediploidizations help to understand species radiations?

comments.issue: Ohnolog evolution may be interdependent, so divergence-time strata are not independent.
comments.request: Articulate how interdependence between ohnologs is handled.
comments.quote: My concern here is that if ohnolog evolution is interdependent on evolution of other ohnologs, evolutionary trends in, say, late rediploidization ohnologs becomes dependent on rediploidization of early rediploidization ohnologs

comments.issue: The enhancer-CNE section reports general statistics without biological interpretation.
comments.request: Add sequence motif analysis and biological interpretation.
comments.quote: While I find the results of this section interesting in describing general tendencies of enhancer-CNE conservation across phylogenies and rediploidization states, many of the results here describe general statistics without much biological interpretation.

comments.issue: The enhancer-evolution section is hard to follow and stylistically inconsistent.
comments.request: Rephrase and clarify what results are compared, editing for consistency.
comments.quote: This section is clearly in need of rephrasing and clarification of sentences. It is hard to follow what are the exact results and what is being compared.

comments.issue: The motivation at lines 249-250 is weak and unspecific.
comments.request: Elaborate what new evolutionary knowledge the analysis creates.
comments.quote: The motivation for this analysis is weak and unspecific – please elaborate in more specific terms what new knowledge of the evolutionary process this analysis creates.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 250-252 has an unclear message.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence.
comments.quote: Lines 250-252: I suggest rephrasing this sentence because it is not immediately clear what is the message here.

comments.issue: The paragraph at lines 264-274 is wordy.
comments.request: Condense the message without elaborate justification.
comments.quote: This paragraph is more wordy than other paragraphs and the message could be condensed here without elaborate justification of the analyses.

comments.issue: Regulatory classes may reflect expression level rather than variable versus conserved regulation.
comments.request: Account for total expression level in the classification.
comments.quote: My concern here is that lower expression correlation may be driven by lower expression, so can these classes simply reflect groups of genes with higher or lower expression instead of variable or conserved regulation?

comments.issue: Expression noise or lower expression could explain more active enhancers in the conserved-regulation class.
comments.request: Account for expression noise in this analysis.
comments.quote: My concern here is that if you define the regulatory classes based on expression correlation, genes with lower correlation may be those with lower overall expression

comments.issue: How the two analyses at lines 284-288 differ is unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase to distinguish the questions.
comments.quote: It is not clear how these two analyses (questions) are different, please rephrase.

comments.issue: “Decreased” and “more variable” statements are not quantified.
comments.request: Quantify these statements.
comments.quote: Lines 288-289: Please quantify these statements of "decreased" and "more variable" in some way.

comments.issue: It is not stated stronger than what at lines 291-293.
comments.request: State the comparison explicitly.
comments.quote: Lines 291-293: Please state stronger than *what*.

comments.issue: What is being compared at lines 293-295 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison.
comments.quote: Lines 293-295: It is not clear what is being compared here.

comments.issue: The conclusion at lines 296-297 is self-evident and does not explain how regulatory evolution affects expression.
comments.request: Elaborate the mechanism rather than stating that elements evolve.
comments.quote: This is not a strong conclusion and it's self-evident that regulatory elements will evolve across time - this conclusion is simply saying regulatory elements evolve

comments.issue: The novelty of the perspective at lines 397-399 relative to previous knowledge is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain succinctly how this perspective is novel.
comments.quote: In this context it would be helpful if you could succinctly explain how this perspective is novel from previous knowledge.

comments.issue: What “robust” means at line 101 is unexplained.
comments.request: Briefly explain “robust” in this context.
comments.quote: Line 101: Please briefly explain what is “robust” in this context.

comments.issue: “Closely related” at line 129 is misleading without analyses of associated changes.
comments.request: Use “similar” instead.
comments.quote: “Closely related” is a bit misleading in this context because you have not analyzed associated changes in SOM cluster genes and e.g. their proximate ATAC-seq peaks.

comments.issue: Why ohnolog expression divergence decreases across embryogenesis is not explained.
comments.request: Elaborate the reasons and general implications.
comments.quote: Lines 162-163: Could you please elaborate briefly on the reasons/logic on why ohnolog expression divergence decreases across embryogenesis.

comments.issue: The ovary-specific pattern at line 176 is not explained.
comments.request: Elaborate why divergence differences are smallest in ovaries.
comments.quote: Line 176: Can you please elaborate briefly why do you think the difference in divergence between early and late rediploidization genes is smallest in ovaries and markedly different from other tissues.

comments.issue: The constrained expression of ohnologs versus singletons is not interpreted.
comments.request: Explain what this means for ohnolog and singleton functional roles.
comments.quote: Can you please briefly elaborate what does this mean in terms of gene (regulatory) evolution in general. Why is expression evolution more constrained in ohnologs vs singletons during later stages of embryogenesis?

comments.issue: Why the pattern is conserved across osmoregulatory organs is unexplained.
comments.request: Test whether specific conserved transcripts drive it.
comments.quote: Lines 197-198: Why is this pattern conserved across these main osmoregulatory organs? Is it driven by a specific set of transcripts that have conserved roles

comments.issue: “Pleiotropic constraints” at lines 204-205 is undefined.
comments.request: Elaborate the conclusion and define the term.
comments.quote: Lines 204-205: Could you elaborate on this conclusion/argument in a more explicit manner. For example, what is meant with “pleiotropic constraints” in this context?

comments.issue: It is not stated whether gonads are female, male or both.
comments.request: Specify the gonad sex.
comments.quote: Line 242: Please specify female or male gonads (or both).

comments.issue: “Constraints” at lines 302-303 is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify what constraints means here.
comments.quote: Lines 302-303: It is not clear what is meant with "constraints" in this context.

comments.issue: Most sentences at lines 299-309 start with subordinate clauses.
comments.request: Use more direct sentences.
comments.quote: I’d like to point out that all but two sentences in this paragraph start with a subordinate clause

comments.issue: “Influences” at line 339 implies causation without support.
comments.request: Use “associates” instead.
comments.quote: Line 339: "Influences" indicates a causal relationship so I think "associates" would be more appropriate here.

comments.issue: “Shape” at line 367 implies a causal direction that was not shown.
comments.request: Use “reflect” instead.
comments.quote: Line 367: I think "reflect" is more suiting than "shape" because you have not argued/showed whether the causality goes from sequence conservation -> regulatory activity or vice versa.

comments.issue: Inferring selection at line 403 is not justified since selection was not measured.
comments.request: Remove or qualify the selection inference.
comments.quote: Line 403: Is the inference of "selection" really justified here? You have not measured selection

comments.issue: Calling the system “ideal” at line 413 overstates its status.
comments.request: Rephrase “ideal”.
comments.quote: Line 413: I would rephrase “ideal” here - ideal means that there is no better model system, and many arguments could be made pointing to the contrary.

reviews.assessment: Data are useful, but conclusions are ambiguous about the conceptual advance and the description ranges too broadly across WGD events.
strengths: useful data for the polyploid research community

comments.issue: Criteria defining “active promoters” and “active enhancers” are missing, and the marks logic is questionable.
comments.request: Define the criteria and show expected mark overlaps.
comments.quote: What are the criteria for the definition of “active promoters” and “active enhancer”?

comments.issue: Figure 1B is simulated without biological correlation and Figure 1G is hard to interpret.
comments.request: Ground the diagram in biology and label all lines.
comments.quote: The diagram in Fig. 1B was simulated and did not corelate with biological functions.

comments.issue: Figure 2 would be more informative comparing species within each developmental stage.
comments.request: Compare within stages and explain the y-axis.
comments.quote: If the purpose is for comparative analysis between species, it would be better to compare them within each of individual stages of development. The y-axis should be explained.

comments.issue: “Regulatory” should be “expression” evolution, and ohnology versus orthology is conceptually confused.
comments.request: Clarify the terminology and how divergence values were computed.
comments.quote: The gene “regulatory” evolution should be changed to gene “expression” evolution in the text and figure. They used both ohnology and orthology in the analysis, which caused conceptual confusion.

comments.issue: The regulatory elements section comes too late in the Results.
comments.request: Move it early to support the functional annotation.
comments.quote: This part should come early in the Results to help understand and interpret functional annotation data.

comments.issue: The role of TEs is not discussed given that animals lack the RdDM pathway.
comments.request: Discuss TE regulatory roles.
comments.quote: The role of TEs should be discussed since animals don’t have RdDM pathway.

comments.issue: It is conceptually unclear how enhancers could be stage-specific if they are DNA sequences.
comments.request: Clarify enhancer presence/absence versus function throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: It’s unclear how enhancers could be present in one developmental stage but absent in other stages?

comments.issue: Citation problems remain at lines 301, 306 and 312.
comments.request: Fix the citations, likely leftovers from a previous format.
comments.quote: Minor: citation problems such as in lines 301, 306, 312 (52?), etc., probably from a previous format?

comments.issue: The paper ranges broadly across 1R-4R WGD events although the strongest findings concern 4R.
comments.request: Focus on post-4R conservation and divergence and clarify the conclusions.
comments.quote: Perhaps the authors should focus on the conservation and divergence of gene expression and regulatory elements after 4R WGD and clarify the data interpretation and conclusions.

title: Developmental contexts of gene-regulatory evolution following whole genome duplication in salmonids

study.system: Drosophila species; activity timing, genetics and neurobiology

editor_summary: Reviewers see a spectacular, data-rich study but find it overpacked; they ask to explain genetic manipulations for a broad readership, decompress the writing, support comparative and sleep conclusions with more species, conditional manipulations and sample size, and improve scholarship.

reviews.assessment: Spectacular neurogenetic dissection of temporal niche, but the evolutionary angle and genetic manipulations need clearer presentation for a broad readership.
strengths: elegant dissection of temporal properties of socio-sexual interactions

comments.issue: The evolutionary component of the study is underplayed.
comments.request: Strengthen the evolutionary framing.
comments.quote: although the evolutionary component (see below) was rather underplayed

comments.issue: Genetic manipulations and notation are incomprehensible to non-specialists and only neurogeneticists will follow the paper.
comments.request: Add a table explaining every genetic manipulation for non-fly readers.
comments.quote: Can the authors provide a table with every genetic manipulation in the and explain to non-fly neurogeneticists what this means.

comments.issue: The abstract is very intense and would benefit from simplification.
comments.request: Simplify the abstract.
comments.quote: Abstract is very intense. A bit of simplification would go a long way.

comments.issue: Fig 1a axis label and the meaning of n=30, N=8 are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the axis and sample-size annotations.
comments.quote: Fig 1a What does 0 refer to on X-axis- midnight? What does n=30, N=8 mean?

comments.issue: The experimental temperatures are modest; behavior at higher continental-European temperatures is unknown.
comments.request: Discuss behavior when day temperatures reach 30 degrees C.
comments.quote: The temperatures presented are quite modest in Versailles. What happens when day temp reaches 30oC which happens quite regularly in continental Europe?

comments.issue: per splice-locked mutants, suggested to underlie seasonal activity shifts, were not tested.
comments.request: Consider using per splice-locked mutants or discuss them.
comments.quote: Also per splicing has been suggested to determine seasonal activity shifts by Edery’s group. Did the authors ever try to use the per splice-locked mutants?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether day-shifting species show a more nocturnal shift in activity.
comments.request: Clarify the direction of activity shifts in day-shifting species.
comments.quote: Do the day shifting species produce a more nocturnal shift in activity?

comments.issue: Fig 1b point ordering, n/N notation and the N labels in 1c are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify point ordering and the N annotations.
comments.quote: Fig 1b – within spring summer and autumn are the points in a temporal order? What does n=30, N=8 mean?

comments.issue: The melanogaster-simulans comparison, relevant to temporal partitioning and hybridisation avoidance, was not pursued.
comments.request: Pursue the melanogaster-simulans comparison.
comments.quote: I’m surprised the authors did not pursue further the melanogaster-simulans comparison where temporal partitioning in these two cosmopolitan sympatric species would avoid sterile hybridisation.

comments.issue: Y-axis units switch between activity/min and activity per 30 min, and mean plus SEM is shown inconsistently.
comments.request: Use consistent units and show mean and SEM for all activity panels.
comments.quote: The authors keep switching the Y axis from activity/min to activity per 30 min (also for other figures).

comments.issue: The N peak intensifies at high night temperatures and could be a stress response like the Trp-mediated A peak.
comments.request: Consider whether the N peak has a similar stress-related modulator.
comments.quote: The N peak rears itself more at high night temperatures (reminiscent of the high temperature A peak). Could it be a stress response?

comments.issue: The claim that the N peak does not correlate with phylogeny is not supported by quantitative analysis and contradicts similar sociosexual profiles among related species.
comments.request: Tone down the phylogeny statement or support it quantitatively.
comments.quote: Perhaps the author’s statement could be toned down, particularly as there is no quantitative analysis to support it.

comments.issue: Character displacement between melanogaster and simulans could also explain the pattern at L263.
comments.request: Consider character displacement in the discussion.
comments.quote: not sure that character displacement is not going on with melanogaster-simulans- could certainly be seen in that light

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and carefully conducted study with important new insights; asks to address sympatric species comparisons and decompress the dense writing.
strengths: new and important insights into temporal activity plasticity

comments.issue: The timing strategies of sympatric species that should avoid competition and interbreeding are not highlighted.
comments.request: Compare temporal niche distributions of sympatric species under crowded conditions.
comments.quote: I believe it is extremely important to compare the temporal niche distribution of these species under “crowded” conditions.

comments.issue: The writing is so compressed that sentences are difficult to understand on first reading.
comments.request: Decompress the writing style.
comments.quote: The manuscript is written in such a compressed manner that it is difficult to understand. I had to read many sentences two or three times to grasp their meaning.

comments.issue: 'Circadian fixity' is misleading: the study was not under constant conditions and the circadian system is plastic.
comments.request: Reword the summary and avoid 'circadian fixity'.
comments.quote: In particular, the term “circadian fixity” is misleading. First, this study was not conducted under constant conditions, which is why there is no circadian behavior, but rather daily behavior.

comments.issue: Menegazzi et al. (2012) first proposed the afternoon peak as an escape response and is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Menegazzi et al. 2012.
comments.quote: Menegazzi et al. (2012, JBR 27) were the first to suggest that the afternoon peak represents an escape response. In the interest of fairness, this article should also be cited.

comments.issue: Drosophila species are not gregarious insects in the strict sense.
comments.request: Avoid describing Drosophila as gregarious.
comments.quote: I don't think Drosophila species can be classified as gregarious insects in the strict sense of the term.

comments.issue: The 'N-peak' abbreviation conflicts with N used for sample size, and N versus n is unclear in Figures 1 and 2.
comments.request: Avoid the N-peak abbreviation and clarify N versus n.
comments.quote: In my opinion, it is not necessary to abbreviate the night peak as “N-peak,” especially since “N” is also used to denote the number of individuals.

comments.issue: Several line-level wording and clarity edits (italics, rephrasing, reordering, difficult sentences and a difficult discussion paragraph).
comments.quote: Line 86: “contrasting directions” sounds strange. What about “opposite directions”?

comments.issue: TH is not explained in Figure 4i.
comments.request: Explain TH in the figure.
comments.quote: Figure 4 i: TH has to be explained

comments.issue: Strain provenance attribution: Peter Deppisch from the University of Würzburg provided the strains.
comments.request: Correct the strain-provider attribution.
comments.quote: Supplementary Table: I think that Peter Deppisch from has provided the strains from the University of Würzburg.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive but overpacked study; comparative and sleep conclusions need more species, conditional manipulations, larger samples and deeper scholarship.

comments.issue: Too much is packed into a single manuscript; each component deserves more attention and rigor.
comments.request: Split or deepen the components across several studies.
comments.quote: A major concern is that this is too much to pack into a single manuscript.

comments.issue: The claim of a dopamine-based mechanism across Drosophila is based on only 3-4 species for dopamine effects, four for brain anatomy and two for tarsal removal.
comments.request: Test dopaminergic manipulations across more of the 21 species.
comments.quote: But such a conclusion would require a much more comprehensive assessment of dopaminergic manipulations across more Drosophila species than the 3-4 examined in the current manuscript for dopamine effects.

comments.issue: Tetanus toxin expression and Kir silencing during development interfere with neural development, making phenotypes hard to interpret.
comments.request: Use conditional adult-stage neuronal manipulations and additional challenge experiments.
comments.quote: the expression of this toxin is expected to interfere with normal neural development, making phenotypes difficult to interpret

comments.issue: Key sleep experiments have very low sample sizes, e.g. some Ca-LexA experiments with only four flies.
comments.request: Increase sample sizes for the sleep experiments.
comments.quote: Key experiments have low sample sizes (e.g., some Ca-LexA experiments appear to involve only 4 flies).

comments.issue: The sleep work is not convincing; recent work suggests dFB and R5 neurons are not likely sleep regulation centers.
comments.request: Reconsider the sleep-center interpretation in light of recent literature.
comments.quote: Furthermore, recent work suggests that the neurons being examined, dFB and R5 neurons of the central complex, are not likely centers of sleep regulation.

comments.issue: A substantial body of relevant work on environmental, social-sexual and cuticular hydrocarbon effects on daily timing is not acknowledged, including Fujii and Amrein.
comments.request: Acknowledge and discuss the relevant literature in detail.
comments.quote: there is a substantial body of work on environmental and social-sexual influences on daily timing in Drosophila, the effects of female mate availability on the daily timing of male activity, the roles of cuticular hydrocarbons in mating induced effects

title: Mating imperatives drive plasticity of the daily temporal niche in fruit flies

study.system: yeast colony resistance evolution; spatial assay and computational model

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers raised concerns that must be addressed before publication; invites a revision responding to all reviewer and editorial comments, with changes highlighted in Word.

reviews.assessment: Promising experimental-computational study, but calibration undermines independent validation, the phase transition term is unsupported and translational claims need caution.
strengths: single-cell-derived colony assay with fluorescent resistance tracking
mechanism may apply to biofilms and tumours

comments.issue: The model is calibrated to properties tied to the main claims, so validation is not independent.
comments.request: Separate fitting and test data, report parameter uncertainties, and propagate them to the optimal ridge.
comments.quote: The current model calibration approach undermines independent validation. The digital twin is interesting, but the model is calibrated to experimental properties that are closely tied to the main claims

comments.issue: Experimental validation of the predicted sweet spot uses only three schedules at a single tau_off value.

comments.issue: Some figures are incorrectly referenced in the main text.

reviews.assessment: Really exciting natural experiment and valuable addition, but minor parent ancestry, timing, and RAD data resolution need attention.

title: Rapid genome-wide purging following tsunami-induced hybridization in a stickleback population

study.system: grassland communities; 13-year multifactor global change experiment

editor_summary: Three reviewers find the work of potential interest but raise a number of concerns that must be addressed before a final decision.

reviews.assessment: Clearly written and well-structured study with sound statistics, plus minor suggestions on model selection, figure labelling and code reproducibility.

comments.issue: AIC rather than AICc is used for model comparison with many predictors, risking overfitting.
comments.request: Use AICc as the default comparison metric.

comments.issue: Figures 3 and 4 captions do not use the searchable term 'path diagrams'.
comments.request: Refer to these figures as path diagrams in the captions.
comments.quote: I would suggest referring to Figures 3 and 4 as 'path diagrams' in their caption

comments.issue: Arrow widths in Figures 3 and 4 vary without explanation.
comments.request: Explain the arrow thickness or make all arrows the same size.
comments.quote: The arrows in Figure 3 and 4 vary in width/thickness with no explanation given.

comments.issue: Extended Data Fig.4 caption mentions warming, which is absent from the figure.
comments.request: Align the caption with the figure content.
comments.quote: In Extended Data Fig.4, warming is mentioned in the caption but does not appear to be included in the figure.

comments.issue: Bootstrapping approach in Extended Data Tables 1-3 is not specified.

comments.issue: Several code chunks fail with errors (annotate/label, case mismatch, svd), hindering reproducibility.

comments.quote: The code supplied all appears to run well in most cases, however, I do encounter some issues:

comments.issue: setwd() calls with personal paths reduce clarity and portability.

comments.quote: a setwd() is called with a personal path, this line should probably be removed for clarity sake.

comments.issue: Code lacks comments and a README explaining what each file and chunk does.

comments.quote: For the sake of reproducibility, and particularly in the absence of a README file, code should be commented throughout with a short explanation as to what each file and 'chunk' is for/does

reviews.assessment: Interesting, timely and long-term study with important insights, but several analyses, initial-condition details and overstated language need attention.
strengths: fits the journal scope with high potential

comments.issue: Contradiction: N alone reduces productivity via water deficit, yet N with reduced rainfall increases productivity.
comments.request: Discuss and resolve this apparent contradiction.
comments.quote: I think it needs some further discussion why N alone led to lower biomass due to reduced soil moisture, but to higher biomass when water limitation was actually added as a treatment, this appears somehow contradictory.

comments.issue: Claim that asynchrony stems from reduced legume dominance lacks species-level biomass data.
comments.request: Provide species-level biomass data or temper the claim.
comments.quote: Do you have data to support that, or was aboveground biomass harvested for the communities as a whole, rather than separated by species?

comments.issue: Assumption of filtering toward resource-conservative species lacks a supporting reference or figure.
comments.request: Cite the figure or table supporting this assumption.
comments.quote: What is this assumption based on; shifts in functional composition? If so, please add reference to figure/table supporting that statement.

comments.issue: How the 10 x 100 cm harvest strip was selected within the 2 x 2 m plots is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain how the sampling area was selected.
comments.quote: Biomass was harvested from a 10 x 100 cm strip per plot; plot size was 2 x 2 m, how was the sampling area selected for?

comments.issue: Changes in ambient conditions over 13 years and stability of treatment intensities are not reported.
comments.request: Report ambient conditions and whether treatment differences stayed constant.
comments.quote: How did the ambient conditions change over the 13 years and how might that affect the treatment intensities

comments.issue: Non-independence of replicates sharing CO2 rings is not accounted for.
comments.request: Account for the CO2-ring random effect.
comments.quote: Did you somehow account for non-independence of replicates from the same CO2-rings?

comments.issue: Initial differences among and within treatment combinations, and management history since 1997, are not described.
comments.request: Describe initial community differences and management history.
comments.quote: The authors mention that initial differences had lasting effects (L. 206 ff.), so it might be worth having a closer look at initial differences among and withing treatment combinations.

comments.issue: Claim that treatments simulated ecologically realistic changes is not specified.
comments.request: Specify what makes the treatments realistic.
comments.quote: In L. 79 you say: "treatments simulated ecologically realistic environmental changes", can you specify that a bit more?

comments.issue: How infrared lamps produce +2.5 °C warming at 1 m soil depth is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the soil warming mechanism and measurement.
comments.quote: you say that there was a temperature increase of +2.5 °C in 1 m soil depth. I was wondering how that should work with infrared heating lamps

comments.issue: No ANPP measurements were made in 2020 without explanation.
comments.request: Explain why 2020 lacks ANPP data.
comments.quote: There were no ANPP measurements in 2020, why?

comments.issue: Only three replicates per treatment combination is low given expected variance among communities.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of low replication more thoroughly.
comments.quote: Replication, with 3 replicates per specific treatment combination, appears to be rather low.

comments.issue: Abstract 'ecosystem stability emerges' implies combined global change factors generally increase stability, which is misleading.

comments.issue: Claim of stronger nonlinearities in three-way interactions is not backed by a comparison with two-way effects.

comments.quote: With such a strong emphasis on the "stronger nonlinearities" and thus indicating a comparison of non-additive effects of the two-way and three-way interactions, talking about these comparisons would also be helpful.

comments.issue: 'Sharply' at L157 overstates the contrast with similar-strength two-way effects.

comments.issue: 'Dampened' at L166 mischaracterizes the reversal of eCO2 effects when combined.

comments.issue: Temporal language is too strong: Fig 5 confidence intervals overlap zero yet effects are called 'initially negative'.

comments.issue: Unexpected destabilizing effect of species richness deserves more discussion.

comments.issue: Bivariate analysis at L129 is never described in the methods.

comments.quote: I cannot find any further information about the bivariate analysis, there is no additional information in the methods section.

comments.issue: Figure 2 uses symbols (µ, σ) instead of terms.

comments.quote: please specify the abbreviations used in the figs. For example, in Fig. 3, SR, σ, µ, ΔCWMpc₁, ΔCWMpc₂.

comments.issue: Final paragraph of the temporal pathways section fits better in the synthesis section.

comments.issue: Three sentences need grammar or clarity fixes (L61ff, L228, L239).

comments.issue: Code annotations and comments are sparse.

comments.issue: L60 sentence meaning is unclear.

comments.issue: 'Species diverse' at L63 needs a hyphen.

comments.issue: 5-year rolling averages reduce independence and overrepresent trends, dampening the interannual variability of interest.
comments.request: Justify the 5-year window or use annual data.
comments.quote: Lumping into 5 year rolling averages decreases independence of your datapoints since they are all mathematically linked.

comments.issue: 'Delayed moisture limitation' at L123 is ambiguous.

comments.issue: L147 numbers are hard to match to effects; whether the interaction is compared to control is unclear.

comments.issue: L159 statement about three-way interactions is incomprehensible.

comments.issue: Temporal stability and interannual variability are not distinguished.

comments.issue: Whether stability is evaluated at plot or treatment level is unclear.
comments.request: State the level at which stability is calculated.
comments.quote: Is it evaluated at the plot level or at the treatment level?

comments.issue: Figures 3 and 4 are overwhelming and hard to distill.
comments.request: Make the figures easier to understand.
comments.quote: Fig 3 and 4 are a lot. Hard to distill what we should look at.

comments.issue: Fig 5 caption says middle year while the x-axis gives a range.
