title: Ecosystem stability is shaped by resource–trait coordination under multiple interacting global change factors

study.system: metazoans; IL-1 cytokine evolution, structure prediction and functional assays

editor_summary: Three reviewers find the work of considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns that must be addressed; a revised version would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, wide-ranging and well-written study, but the ancient-origin claim needs phylogenies and functional evidence before it is fully supported.
strengths: interesting study with wide breadth of analysis

comments.issue: Structural similarity is not proof of ancient origin; phylogenies are needed.
comments.request: Build alignments and phylogenies of IL-1/IL-1anc.
comments.quote: Given that a major claim is an ancient origin, it would be necessary that the authors do phylogenies, to really demonstrate the evolutionary origin of IL1 in IL1anc.

comments.issue: Systematic homolog searches are limited; other clades and archaea/bacteria are unexplored.
comments.request: Phylogeny of all homologs and searches in archaea and bacteria.
comments.quote: Additionally, have the authors tried to do systematic homologs searches in archaea and bacteria ?

comments.issue: Localisation study lacks ER markers and live imaging to test trafficking and secretion.
comments.request: Add ER co-localisation markers and live microscopy.
comments.quote: Consider ER markers for potential co-localization. This would help determine whether certain IL-1anc proteins accumulate in the ER, especially those predicted to have signal peptides.

comments.issue: PDZ presence/absence is not shown for the tested orthologs.
comments.request: Annotate PDZ presence/absence in the figure.
comments.quote: I also suggest to explicit, in the current figure, the presence/absence of PDZ for the different orthologs tested.

comments.issue: Cross-species specificity of caspase cleavage is untested; cleavage sites are not analysed.
comments.request: Test an invertebrate caspase on human IL-1 and display cleavage sites.
comments.quote: Testing an invertebrate caspase on human IL-1 could clarify cross-species specificity.

comments.issue: PDZ domain function is underexplored despite being a probable key feature.
comments.request: Run functional assays with PDZ truncations or chimeras.
comments.quote: This domain seems to remain underexplored despite being a probable key feature of some IL-1anc proteins.

comments.issue: Functional conservation claims outrun the preliminary experimental evidence.
comments.request: Tone down the functional conservation claims.
comments.quote: In general, some claims should be toned down, notably on the functional conservation aspect, as the current experimental evidence are interesting but still preliminary.

comments.issue: Reference is lacking at line 132.
comments.request: Add the missing reference.
comments.quote: Line 132: reference is lacking

comments.issue: PDZ putative properties are not detailed at line 136.
comments.request: Provide more details on PDZ properties.
comments.quote: Line 136: more details on PDZ putative properties should be provided

comments.issue: Lines 391-395 are unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase or add detail.
comments.quote: Lines 391 - 395: this is unclear to me, should be rephrased, or be more detailed

comments.issue: Lines 441-447 blur the claims and should be discarded.
comments.request: Remove this part.
comments.quote: Lines 441- 447: I would discard this part as it dampens and blur the claims of the study

comments.issue: Fig. 4D lacks a histogram with means and paired statistics.
comments.request: Provide a histogram with the mean and paired test.
comments.quote: Fig. 4D: could you provide a histogram with the mean for the 3 individuals (with paired stat test)?

comments.issue: Fig. 5 lacks an empty vector control.
comments.request: Include an empty vector control.
comments.quote: Fig. 5: including an empty vector control would strengthen interpretation of expression and localization data

comments.issue: Fig. 6 legend does not call out panels A, B and C.
comments.request: Label panels in the legend.
comments.quote: Fig. 6, legend: lacking A, B and C calling

comments.issue: Fig. 6A could move SpurIL-1.4 and 1.5 to extended data.
comments.request: Move these blots to extended data.
comments.quote: Fig. 6A: SpurIL-1.4 and 1.5 could go in extended data

comments.issue: Fig. 6C faint bands need a longer exposure.
comments.request: Provide a longer-exposure blot.
comments.quote: Fig. 6C: another version of the Blot with longer exposure should be provided in which faint bands would be clearer

comments.issue: No alignment shows conservation of cleavage residues with human as reference.
comments.request: Provide the alignment, perhaps in extended data.
comments.quote: please provide an alignment for the conservation of these residues over these species, with human as ref (it could go in extended data)

comments.issue: Name 'ILanc' is potentially misleading because 'ancestral' is used broadly.
comments.request: Consider a different appellation.
comments.quote: I would also recommend proposing another appellation than ILanc. "Ancestral" is largely used to describe genes conserved over major phyla such as bacteria/eukaryotes, thus, it could be misleading at first glance.

reviews.assessment: Exciting, ambitious and convincing study, with needed fixes to over-strong historical statements, figure quality, statistics and caspase-1 interpretation.
strengths: convincing deeply conserved IL-1 family across Eumetazoa
impressive integration of computational and experimental approaches
broad interest to immunologists and evolutionary biologists

comments.issue: Abstract second sentence is clunky and needs smoother progression.
comments.request: Rephrase the second sentence.
comments.quote: The second sentence of the abstract reads as a little clunky and would benefit from rephrasing for flow and readability.

comments.issue: Abstract third sentence ignores described IL-1 homologues in cartilaginous and jawless vertebrates.
comments.request: Revise the sentence and related statements to reflect the literature.
comments.quote: Several IL-1 family homologues have been described in cartilaginous fish, including IL-1β and IL-18, and there is evidence for IL-1 receptor antagonist in these groups

comments.issue: Absolute statements about absence of IL-1 homologues overstate the gap.
comments.request: Temper absolute phrases about detection.
comments.quote: absolute phrases such as "have not been detected", "have never been found" or similar should be tempered

comments.issue: Figure 1 and Extended Data Figures 2 and 6 look like low-quality screenshots.
comments.request: Regenerate these figures at publication quality.
comments.quote: Figure 1, Extended Data Figures 2 and 6 currently look like screenshots, with visible pixelation and borders that interfere with labels.

comments.issue: Figure 1 relies only on structural superposition; sequence-level evidence should be added.
comments.request: Add an alignment or strand-correspondence panel to Figure 1.
comments.quote: Without this, Figure 1 risks looking like a set of qualitatively similar folds, rather than a rigorously supported homology claim that is also underpinned by synteny and gene structure.

comments.issue: PDZ domain is under-explained for non-specialist readers.
comments.request: Define the PDZ domain and its canonical role early.
comments.quote: for readers outside protein interaction or cell polarity fields the functional significance of PDZ domains will not be obvious

comments.issue: Figure 2 is cluttered and its vertebrate taxonomy is unclear.
comments.request: Improve spacing/typography and clarify Osteichthyes relationships.
comments.quote: The current layout, however, is a little cluttered. The spacing between boxes and the relative size of fonts make it difficult to read quickly.

comments.issue: Figure 4A uses multiple unpaired t-tests, inappropriate for the multi-group design.
comments.request: Log-transform, check assumptions, then use ANOVA with Tukey.
comments.quote: For Figure 4A, the use of multiple unpaired t-tests is not appropriate given the design and the multiple groups being compared.

comments.issue: Statistics section does not describe the overall statistical framework.
comments.request: Describe transformations, tests, multiple comparisons and software in one place.
comments.quote: More broadly, the Statistics section feels underdeveloped relative to the sophistication of the biological story.

comments.issue: Figure 4 Y-axis capitalisation and the 'Methos' typo need fixing.
comments.quote: Correct "See Material and Methos for details" to "See Materials and Methods for details".

comments.issue: cGAMP treatment is not explained in the figure legend.
comments.request: Expand cGAMP at first mention and describe its use.
comments.quote: Expand "cGAMP-treated" in the figure legend at first mention and briefly describe what 2′3′-cGAMP is and how it was used in this context

comments.issue: Figure 5 localisation is only qualitative; nuclear versus cytosolic signal is not quantified.
comments.request: Quantify localisation and analyse NLS/NES predictions.
comments.quote: Provide a more systematic analysis of localisation, for example by quantifying nuclear versus cytosolic fluorescence for each construct across multiple cells, even if only semi-quantitatively.

comments.issue: The nuclear versus cytosolic pattern is not related to phylogeny, domains or signal peptides.
comments.request: Discuss this pattern in mechanistic context.
comments.quote: Is this pattern consistent with any phylogenetic or domain-architecture differences, or with the presence or absence of PDZ domains and signal peptides

comments.issue: Raw uncropped blots are not provided.
comments.request: Provide raw uncropped blots for all panels.
comments.quote: Please provide the raw, uncropped blots for all panels, including the actin controls, as supplementary material.

comments.issue: Figure 6 layout misaligns bands and labels and contains stray borders.
comments.request: Re-layout the figure with aligned lanes and clean borders.
comments.quote: The current figure layout is hard to interpret. The housekeeping bands do not appear to line up cleanly with the corresponding lanes, panel labels are slightly misaligned, and there are several stray borders.

comments.issue: Legend says 'anti-actin body' instead of 'anti-actin antibody'.
comments.request: Correct the legend wording.
comments.quote: The legend states "To illustrate that the lysates contained comparable concentrations of proteins, an anti-actin body was used". This should be corrected to "anti-actin antibody".

comments.issue: Activation state of the HsCASP1 construct (zymogen versus active) is unclear.
comments.request: Describe the caspase-1 construct and its activation state.
comments.quote: It is not clear whether the HsCASP1 construct used corresponds to the zymogen (pro-caspase-1) or a constitutively active form.

comments.issue: Heterologous system limitations and off-target cleavage risks are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge limitations and frame results as proof-of-principle.
comments.quote: At minimum, the limitations of the heterologous system should be acknowledged, and it may be worth explicitly framing these data as proof-of-principle

comments.issue: SERPINI1 label in Extended Data Figure 4 does not fit its box.
comments.request: Adjust the box or font.
comments.quote: in Extended Data Figure 4, the SERPINI1 label currently does not appear to fit comfortably within its box.

comments.issue: Figure 3 legend does not explain the ancestral locus gene blocks.
comments.request: Reiterate the ancestral locus model in the legend.
comments.quote: It might be worth briefly reiterating this model in the legend so that the reader can fully appreciate what the coloured gene blocks represent without having to refer back to the main text.

comments.issue: Nomenclature is inconsistent and typographical errors remain ('Methos', 'boarders').
comments.request: Standardise nomenclature and proof-read.
comments.quote: Check for typographical errors such as "Material and Methos", "boarders" instead of "borders", and similar small issues.

comments.issue: The lumpfish 'novel IL-1' is not explicitly placed in the IL-1anc clade.
comments.request: State that the analyses place this protein within IL-1anc.
comments.quote: Where you refer to previous work that unknowingly discovered an IL-1anc family member (for example the lumpfish "novel IL-1"), it may help to explicitly state that your structural and synteny analyses now place this protein within the IL-1anc clade.

reviews.assessment: Interesting bioinformatic question, but the functional evidence is minimal: cleavage is unconvincing and inflammatory activity is untested, so the orthologue conclusion is not supported.

comments.issue: There is minimal evidence that the IL-1anc orthologues are bona fide IL-1 family members.
comments.request: Provide stronger functional validation.
comments.quote: there is minimal evidence that the IL-1 family orthologues are bona fide IL-1 family members, as they are not cleaved by caspases efficiently

comments.issue: Flagellin induction of PmarIL-1 is 1-50 fold weaker than TNF, limiting confidence.
comments.request: Test additional PAMPs beyond flagellin.
comments.quote: This weak level of induction limits confidence in the importance of data presented.

comments.issue: Figure 6 cleavage data are unconvincing compared with mammalian pro-IL-1 cleavage.
comments.request: Use recombinant proteins with appropriate controls.
comments.quote: Unfortunately, this data is rather unconvincing, especially when considering the beautiful cleavage observed for mammalian pro-IL-1 in the same assay.

comments.issue: Inflammatory mediator activity of the putative IL-1 orthologues is never tested.
comments.request: Verify that these proteins act as inflammatory mediators.
comments.quote: In order to accept the proposed conclusion that these proteins are IL-1 orthologues, the authors would need to verify that they are inflammatory mediators. No activities of this sort are performed in this study.

comments.issue: Introduction omits pro-IL-18 as a caspase-1 substrate and presents pyroptosis as the only GSDMD outcome.
comments.request: Adjust the introduction accordingly.
comments.quote: The authors also suggest that pyroptosis is the outcome of GSDMD pore formation. This is one outcome, not the only (PMID: 29195811) with physiological consequences (PMID 38870946).

title: An ancient evolutionary origin for IL-1 cytokines

study.system: migratory birds worldwide; migration timing, population trends

editor_summary: Revise addressing all reviewer comments; R1 and R3 positive with minor points, while R2's confounding concerns (study period, migration distance, spatial bias) must be addressed; retaining the theoretical model is acceptable.

reviews.assessment: High-quality, compelling study with major conceptual advances; only clarity and interpretation questions, mostly about post-breeding advancement and geographic bias.

comments.issue: Post-breeding advancement is unexpected since warmer temperatures delay autumn; the proximate cause is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the proximate cause and test for differences between advancing and delaying species.
comments.quote: I would expect that species show no advancement but a delay. Warmer temperatures delay the onset of autumn/winter.

comments.issue: Whether Figure 1c combines pre- and post-breeding change rates is unclear, and change rate is undefined.
comments.request: Define change rate clearly in the main text.
comments.quote: Is Fig. 1c the change rate of both seasons? How are post-breeding and pre-breeding combined?

comments.issue: Species are heavily skewed toward Europe and North America, which may bias or confound the patterns.
comments.request: Discuss geographic representation and test for regional differences.
comments.quote: The species seem to be heavily skewed toward European and North American species. Are the observed patterns driven by geographic bias? Could this confound the results?

comments.issue: What 'paired pre- and post-breeding data' means and how many species were included is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the pairing requirement and report species numbers.
comments.quote: Does that mean species were only included if both stages were measured? How many of all species were there?

comments.issue: Population decline could itself slow migration advancement through reduced condition or fewer migrants.
comments.request: Consider reverse causation from population decline to migration advancement.
comments.quote: Could population decline cause slower migration advancement (e.g. due to reduced condition or fewer individuals able to migrate)?

comments.issue: Whether relative advancement in Figure 2c equals the change rate is unclear and affects interpretation.
comments.request: Clarify how relative advancement is calculated.
comments.quote: The difference between pre- and post-breeding advancement rates is strong, but the interpretation depends on how this is calculated.

comments.issue: The body-size and reproduction relationships at line 170 may reflect study or resilience bias rather than real effects.
comments.request: Consider selection bias as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: This could reflect selection bias in that larger species may be more studied, or more resilient due to other factors

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the full-annual-cycle contribution but raises substantial concerns about study-period mismatch, unaccounted confounds and the value of the theoretical model.
strengths: full-annual-cycle approach is a nice contribution
synthesized a very large amount of data

comments.issue: Study periods span a century while IUCN trends cover about a decade, mismatching phenological and demographic data.
comments.request: Include study period as a variable in the model.
comments.quote: I suggest the authors look into the effect that study period has on the relationship between phenological response and population trend (i.e., include this variable in the model).

comments.issue: Migration distance, spatial biases and habitat loss are unaccounted confounds in the phenology-demography relationship.
comments.request: Include migration distance and latitude in the model.
comments.quote: I think the authors should include migration distance (which could be derived from range maps) in the model, when estimating the effect of phenology on population trends.

comments.issue: Categorising population trends into three groups discards the numerical trend data, and Figure S2 is not described in the methods.
comments.request: Use the actual numerical abundance trend as the response variable.
comments.quote: Rather than simplifying trends into three categories, one could use the actual trend in abundance as the response variable.

comments.issue: It is unclear why multiple models were used instead of a single model with all predictors.
comments.request: Consider including all predictors in a single model, particularly for the SEMs.
comments.quote: It was also unclear to me why multiple models were used to look at the relationship between population trends and phenological change/environmental variables.

comments.issue: Explicit model equations are missing and it is unclear whether uncertainty in responses and predictors was accounted for.
comments.request: Provide explicit equations and account for predictor uncertainty to avoid regression dilution.
comments.quote: more explicit equations for the statistical models would be helpful. Was uncertainty in either the response or predictor variables accounted for?

comments.issue: 'Stage-dependent' suggests life-history stages rather than annual-cycle stages.
comments.request: Use a clearer phrase such as 'migratory stage-dependent' or 'time of year-dependent'.
comments.quote: This phrase suggests to me that some life history stages (e.g., juveniles vs. adults) are doing better than others.

comments.issue: The results are not discussed relative to phenological change in the environment and other trophic levels.
comments.request: Discuss migration phenology in the context of environmental and trophic mismatch.
comments.quote: This study does not capture phenological changes in the environment, which I think is fine. However, I think it important to discuss the results in this context.

comments.issue: The theoretical model makes many assumptions, features little in the results, and its added value is unclear.
comments.request: Strengthen the model's mechanistic basis or justify its role in the study.
comments.quote: while I think the theoretical model is an interesting idea, I am unsure what it adds to this study. It doesn’t feature heavily in results and makes a large number of assumptions.

comments.issue: The introduction does not explicitly connect migration timing to environmental phenological change, requiring a mental jump.
comments.request: Set up the study with the resource-tracking and mismatch logic at L16/33.
comments.quote: I think a more explicit connection to phenological change in the environment (i.e., the abiotic environment and other trophic levels) should be made to setup this study.

comments.issue: 'Confer demographic benefits' at L38 is less accurate than ameliorating negative climate impacts.
comments.request: Use 'ameliorate negative impacts of climate change' at L38.
comments.quote: Suggest ‘ameliorate negative impacts of climate change’ rather than ‘confer demographic benefits’. It is allowing animals to cope with change.

comments.issue: The claim at L45 that migration timing shifts affect life-history strategies via trade-offs is inaccurate.
comments.request: Reframe L45 around phenological mismatch.
comments.quote: I’m not sure there are any examples of shifting phenology resulting in changes in life history strategies (on contemporary time scales).

comments.issue: Figure 1 colour labels 'habitat types' conflate breeding/non-breeding grounds with habitat.
comments.request: Relabel the colours as breeding/non-breeding grounds.
comments.quote: Suggest ‘Colour represent breeding/non-breeding grounds’ rather than ‘habitat types’, as this is usually reserves for the type of habitat (forest, grasslands, etc.).

comments.issue: 'Relative advancement' is not a clear term for pre minus post advancement.
comments.request: Use a better term than 'relative advancement'.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I would call pre advance – post advance ‘relative advancement’. Perhaps there is a better term for this.

comments.issue: What 'median interval' means in Figures 1 and 2 is unclear.
comments.request: Define median interval in the figures.
comments.quote: What is meant by ‘median interval’? Is this the 95% credible interval?

comments.issue: Figure S2 does not state whether it uses abundance data.
comments.request: State the data source in the Figure S2 caption.
comments.quote: Is this using the abundance data? If so, it would be worth stating in the caption.

comments.issue: The citation at L136 would be better replaced by an avian study.
comments.request: Use an avian citation at L136.
comments.quote: I think an avian citation would be more appropriate here

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not explain the bold line or what 'reproduction' is.
comments.request: Add this information to the Figure 3 caption.
comments.quote: What is the bold line? What is ‘reproduction’? It would be helpful to have this information in the caption.

comments.issue: Somveille et al. 2015 may not support the notion cited at L181.
comments.request: Check or replace the Somveille et al. 2015 citation.
comments.quote: I’m not sure that Somveille et al. 2015 (65) addresses this notion at all.

comments.issue: Whether the climate data time period matches each time series is unclear.
comments.request: Match and report the climate data time periods.
comments.quote: Was the time period of the climate data matched to the time period of each time series? If not, they should be.

comments.issue: 'Autocorrelation' at L342/481 should be 'correlation'.
comments.request: Replace autocorrelation with correlation at L342/481.
comments.quote: I think the authors mean ‘correlation’ rather than ‘autocorrelation’

comments.issue: Figure S2d seems to show only the difference, not pre- and post-breeding separately.
comments.request: Show plots for pre-breeding, post-breeding and the difference.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to see plots for each of these (pre-breeding, post-breeding, and difference). It seems like just the difference is displayed?

comments.issue: Figure S4 does not specify which migration is timed.
comments.request: Specify whether Figure S4 shows breeding or non-breeding migration timing.
comments.quote: Timing of which migration? To breeding grounds or non-breeding grounds?

comments.issue: 'Variances' is used for uncertainty in a slope estimate in Appendix S2 L314.
comments.request: Use 'uncertainty' or 'standard error' instead of variances.
comments.quote: I suggest using a word other than ‘variances’. Maybe uncertainty. Or standard error.

comments.issue: Whether random intercepts, slopes or both were fitted is unclear at Appendix S2 L413.
comments.request: Specify the random-effect structure.
comments.quote: Random intercept, random slope, or both?

comments.issue: The full model, including parameters and error distributions, is not written out at Appendix S2 L465.
comments.request: Write out the full model.
comments.quote: writing out the full model (what are the different parameters of the model, what distribution do the errors follow, etc.) would be helpful for the reader.

comments.issue: Appendix S2 L483 uses 60% where 0.6 seems intended.
comments.request: Use 0.6 rather than 60%.
comments.quote: Appendix S2 L 483: 0.6 rather than 60%?

reviews.assessment: Very positive with no major concerns, only minor requests for clearer terminology, context and tables.

comments.issue: 'Pre-breeding stage' and 'post-breeding stage' can be misread as life-cycle rather than annual-cycle stages.
comments.request: Add 'annual-cycle' terminology to the abstract.
comments.quote: For someone skimming the abstract, “pre-breeding stage” and “post-breeding stage” can read as life-cycle stages instead of annual-cycle stages.

comments.issue: Other meta-analyses including post-breeding migration found similar patterns, but this context is missing.
comments.request: Put the work into context with Bitterlin and Van Buskirk (2014).
comments.quote: However, this isn’t the only meta-analysis that includes post-breeding migration.

comments.issue: Relationships that should not depend on migration stage change between Figure 3 panels, with reproduction even changing sign.
comments.request: Explain why reproduction has a negative effect in the second SEM.
comments.quote: Interesting that relationships that shouldn’t depend on the stage of migration examined also change between panels a and b.

comments.issue: 'Migration timing measurement' is not distinguished from effect size or data collection method.
comments.request: Clarify these terms at lines 275-277.
comments.quote: How does “migration timing measurement” differ from the effect size and from “data collection method”?

comments.issue: Categorising population trends discards information; the actual estimates are not analysed.
comments.request: Analyse the actual estimates of population trends.
comments.quote: I can understand putting population trends into categories to align with the IUCN categories, but (in my opinion) it’s throwing away information.

comments.issue: 'Respectively' at lines 331-334 implies mismatched comparisons between trend sources and migration stages.
comments.request: Clarify the respectively sentence at lines 331-334.
comments.quote: The use of “respectively” here implies that IUCN trends were compared with pre-breeding migration change rate and abundance database trends were compared with post-breeding migration change rate.

comments.issue: The 'respectively' at lines 335-338 is uninterpretable.
comments.request: Clarify the respectively sentence at lines 335-338.
comments.quote: I don’t even have a guess what the “respectively” implies here. The authors should clarify.

comments.issue: Converting actual trend estimates to categories and back to numeric for the SEM is questionable.
comments.request: Justify or avoid the categorical conversion for species with actual estimates.
comments.quote: For the species with actual estimates of population trend, why convert them to categorical variables when they have to be converted back to numeric variables for the SEM to work?

comments.issue: Two copy edits: 'egger's' at line 360 and 'state' at Supplement 2 line 413.
comments.quote: Line 360: “egger’s” should be “Egger’s.”

comments.issue: Equation 1 uses lambda where r is the standard instantaneous growth rate term.
comments.request: Use r for the instantaneous rate and lambda = exp(r).
comments.quote: r is the standard term used in this equation, not lambda.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether migration is treated as instantaneous at lines 379-386.
comments.request: Clarify whether migration is modelled as instantaneous.
comments.quote: So treating migration itself as instantaneous?

comments.issue: The energetics model conclusions depend on the assumption that breeding-season energy intake exceeds non-breeding intake.
comments.request: Provide empirical support or consider alternative simple models.
comments.quote: the conclusions reached here seem dependent on the assumption that daily energy intake rate is greater in the breeding season than in the nonbreeding season. Is there any empirical support for this assumption?

comments.issue: Table S1 inconsistently reports statistical test results for one comparison row.
comments.request: Make Table S1 cells consistent in content.
comments.quote: Why does the cell for Comparison between two stages/Linear-mixed effects model have statistical test results (not quite as good) instead?

comments.issue: Table S9 does not define abbreviations in the header and reports trend counts rather than the trends themselves.
comments.request: Define abbreviations in the header and report the trends more usefully.
comments.quote: The header of this table should define all abbreviations, symbols, and codes used, instead of putting them as a note at the bottom (several pages later).

comments.issue: Code, data and README were provided and look good, but the available abundance data contain only categorical trends.
comments.request: Provide the numerical estimated trends in the shared data.
comments.quote: the authors did provide R code and data, as well as a README file. It all looks good

title: Avian migration timing advances linked to season-dependent population benefits

study.system: prairie grassland plants; field biodiversity experiment

editor_summary: All three reviewers valued the contribution but raised concerns about pesticide methods and efficacy verification, treating all fungi as pathogens, and unclear results and discussion; revision should address these.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, commendable multi-factor study, but the abstract's attribution to plant-fungal interactions and unverified fungicide effects need attention.

comments.issue: The abstract first invokes interactions among all manipulated groups, then attributes the results solely to plant-fungal interactions.
comments.request: Attribute the results consistently and address the other interactions.
comments.quote: authors claim ecosystem scale impacts of the interactions among soil fungi, foliar fungi, arthropods, and plant diversity impacted observed trends, but in lines 39-41 attributed all of these observations solely on plant-fungal interactions

comments.issue: Whether foliar fungi were actually removed is unverified, and the fungicides' target spectra are not reported.
comments.request: Verify removal efficacy and report fungicide target groups.
comments.quote: Was foliar fungi removal verified? Were the fungicides listed in the manuscript broad spectrum acting ( i.e. against both Ascomycota and Baidiomycota)?

comments.issue: The opening line of the abstract could be stronger.
comments.request: Replace it with a stronger opening line.
comments.quote: A stronger opening line could replace the existing line.

comments.issue: 'Similar plant biomass' is ambiguous: same plant composition or per-gram value regardless of plant type?
comments.request: Clarify what similar plant biomass refers to.
comments.quote: Similar plant biomass here refers to the same plant compositions contributing to biomass or the overall value of measured biomass in terms of per gram carbon regardless of plant types

comments.issue: Lines 60-67 could be placed further down in the manuscript.
comments.request: Move this section further down.
comments.quote: Lines 60-67: This could be moved further down.

comments.issue: Introduction sections are ordered poorly; the plant-consumer and plant diversity sections should be rearranged.
comments.request: Reorder the introduction sections as suggested.
comments.quote: This section could be moved up to follow the mention of plant-consumer interactions in the introduction

comments.issue: Several passages use a different font and look copied and pasted without citation.

comments.issue: Predictions in Table 1 and the introduction are unconvincing and insufficiently clear.

comments.quote: I’m not entirely convinced by some of the predictions in Table 1 and in the introduction – this may be because further clarity regarding predictions is needed.

comments.issue: Small k for some moderators (travel cost k=1, k=3) may drive effects and bias interpretation.
comments.request: Remove factor levels with k < 5 and re-run as robustness check.
comments.quote: I would consider removing factor levels with k < 5 and re-run the models so assess if results are robust

comments.issue: No references are given for responses to predation risk.
comments.request: Provide references for predation risk responses.
comments.quote: Please provide some references for responses to predation risk.

comments.issue: The nine moderators and the categorical environmental-factor moderator are not described.
comments.request: Describe the moderators and note the environmental-factor moderator.
comments.quote: Please briefly describe what your nine moderators were (perhaps referring to Table 2 and supplementary material).

comments.issue: Whether phylogeny improved model fit is not shown; it may waste degrees of freedom.
comments.request: Report delta AIC with and without phylogeny and consider removing it.
comments.quote: did including phylogenetic history improve model fit (you could report delta AIC with and without it included)?

comments.issue: How environmental conditions correspond to a 'low cost of choice' is not intuitive.
comments.request: Make the link to the cost-of-choice framework clearer.
comments.quote: It isn’t intuitive how the effects of the different environment conditions correspond to a ‘low cost of choice’ for the mating behaviours.

comments.issue: Figures 2-4 do not indicate the direction of environmental effects.
comments.request: Label the direction of environmental factors in Figs 2-4.
comments.quote: you could include the direction of the environmental factors on effect size in Figs 2-4 to make the interpretation of the effect sizes easier.

comments.issue: Terminology differs between results and discussion ('choosiness' vs 'mating preferences').
comments.request: Use 'choosiness' consistently.
comments.quote: Using ‘choosiness’ instead of ‘mating preferences’ will make terminology consistent between results and discussion.

comments.issue: Conclusions about responsiveness are too strong given the non-significant overall effect and small k for travel cost.
comments.request: Make the responsiveness conclusions more tentative.
comments.quote: conclusions around effects of environment on responsiveness need to be a bit more tentative

comments.issue: 'Preference type' in Table 2 is called 'choice type' in Fig 4.
comments.request: Use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: ‘Preference type’ is referred to as ‘choice type’ in Fig 4. Use consistent terminology.

comments.issue: 6 line-level copy edits.
comments.quote: Page 14, line 287: ‘In order’ instead of ‘I order’

reviews.assessment: Well-written with appropriate methods; asks why sex was excluded and how time and travel cost confounding was handled, plus minor text fixes.

comments.issue: Sex was not added as a factor despite supplementary claims that it was non-significant; testing approach is unclear.
comments.request: Add sex as a fixed effect and clarify how it was tested.
comments.quote: I am still unclear as to why sex wasn’t added as a factor in any of the models.

comments.issue: Inclusion of time and travel cost is arbitrary given the physical environment is mostly excluded.
comments.request: Explain in the introduction why mostly social factors are modelled.
comments.quote: Can this be expanded on further in the introduction, why largely the social environment is accounted for, with only a few physical environmental variables?

comments.issue: Time cost may confound with OSR and travel cost depends on the physical environment; confounding is not addressed.
comments.request: Address confounding and re-run models without time cost and travel cost.
comments.quote: the physical environment variable, time cost, can confound with OSR – as mating season shortens or draws to a close the OSR will also decrease, how is this accounted for in the model?

comments.issue: The sentence about asking three questions misleads because the questions are scattered.
comments.request: List the questions after the sentence or remove it.
comments.quote: implies that the questions will be listed right away, but instead, they are scattered throughout this paragraph

comments.issue: The title overstates the rigour of the analysis; 'weak' evidence may reflect noise from confounders.
comments.request: Consider changing the title.
comments.quote: I suggest a slight change in the title as the “weak” evidence may also be “noise” due to confounding factors in the social and physical environment

reviews.assessment: Important topic and well-written, but shortcomings in separate meta-regressions, unclear predictions and moderator coverage (species traits, study types).

comments.issue: Moderators were analysed separately; effects may not hold after accounting for other moderators such as publication year.
comments.request: Run a multiple meta-regression with all moderators in one model.
comments.quote: It would be much better to conduct a multiple meta-regression with all the moderators entered into a single model.

comments.issue: Species characteristics that shape behavioural plasticity are not included as moderators.
comments.request: Incorporate species characteristics into the moderator analysis.
comments.quote: The MS does not include any species characteristics in the moderator analysis.

comments.issue: Control conditions used for comparing environmental manipulations are not defined.
comments.request: Describe the control conditions.
comments.quote: What are the control conditions used for comparing the effects of environmental manipulation?

comments.issue: Correlational and experimental studies are pooled, though correlational studies are more prone to confounds.
comments.request: Analyse correlational studies separately from experimental ones.
comments.quote: If the dataset contained correlational studies, they need to be analysed separate from the experimental ones given that correlational studies are more likely to be subject to potential confounds.

comments.issue: Predictions are given only for environmental factors, not for all moderators.
comments.request: State predictions for every moderator.
comments.quote: The predictions (or lack of) for every moderator need to be clearly stated in the MS. At present, the paper only contained predictions for the environmental factors.

comments.issue: Some predictions are not clear-cut because alternative theoretical models predict different outcomes (e.g., terminal investment).
comments.request: Clarify the competing theoretical predictions.
comments.quote: some of them are actually not as clear-cut as presented because different theoretical models can predict different results

comments.issue: Parasitic risk is treated as a form of predator risk, though the two may influence mating behaviour differently.
comments.request: Separate parasitic from predator risk and revisit predictions.
comments.quote: I find it strange that parasitic risk is considered a form of predator risk. I am not sure if they influence mating behaviour in the same manner.

comments.issue: Grey literature was excluded, which matters given the potential publication bias.
comments.request: Include grey literature or address the bias.
comments.quote: The MS did not include any grey literature. The inclusion of grey literature is important given the results suggested some potential publication bias.

comments.issue: Forest plot shows only significant moderators and lacks sample sizes.
comments.request: Show all moderators and their sample sizes.
comments.quote: I would like to see the forest plot with all the moderators and not just the significant ones and the breakdown of their sample sizes.

title: Meta‐analysis shows the evidence for context‐dependent mating behaviour is inconsistent or weak across animals

study.system: marine phytoplankton and protists; cell size and shape data

editor_summary: Editor says both referees find the manuscript well written and interesting, but both identify areas needing clarification and revision, and encourages the authors to address all comments in detail.

reviews.assessment: Cool analysis of a novel question; comments mainly improve presentation and interpretation, including adding Stoke's Law/CFR and clarifying taxonomic aggregation.
strengths: insight into constraints on algal evolution

comments.issue: Modified Stoke's Law and form resistance (CFR) are absent from the motivation and shape-complexity analysis.
comments.request: Include CFR/Stoke's Law literature and analysis.
comments.quote: I would love to see the authors add in CFR to their measures of cell elongation on page 5-6 and include CFR/Stoke’s Law in their analysis of phytoplankton shape complexity

comments.issue: Whether analyses use species or genus-level averages is unclear and unjustified.
comments.request: Clarify aggregation level and test its effect on results.
comments.quote: the choice to use genera vs species needs to be clarified and better justified in the text

comments.issue: How the diversity-size/shape equations were fitted and selected is not described.
comments.request: Describe fitting and model selection in methods/supplement.
comments.quote: it’s not clear how these models were developed. How exactly were the parameters for these equations fit (shown in Table 1)?

comments.issue: Whether diversity-shape relationships hold across datasets and ecosystems is untested.
comments.request: Analyse datasets and ecosystems separately as robustness check.
comments.quote: Do the two datasets show the same relationships if analyzed separately? Do the different ecosystems in the 2nd dataset yield different patterns?

comments.issue: The main take-home result appears too late in the Discussion and Results.
comments.request: Reorganize to present it earlier.
comments.quote: I would try to reorganize the Discussion to get to this important point earlier (as well as in the Results).

comments.issue: Monitoring frequency and whether each of the 23 ecosystems was sampled once are unstated.
comments.request: Add monitoring frequency information.
comments.quote: In addition to information on the duration of monitoring, I would love to see information on the frequency of monitoring

comments.issue: Check whether the years should be 2011 and 2012.
comments.request: Confirm the years.
comments.quote: Page 4, line 37: do you mean “2011 and 2012”?

comments.issue: Dataset citations appear only in the data availability section, not in the text or reference list.
comments.request: Cite datasets in the text and references.
comments.quote: add the data citations into the text and cite them in the references, not just in the data availability section

comments.issue: 'Regular screening' and 'single screenings' are undefined.
comments.request: Clarify these terms.
comments.quote: not sure what “regular screening” means or “single screenings” (line 45)

comments.issue: What 'ecoregions' refer to is not explained in the dataset description.
comments.request: Define ecoregions in the dataset description.
comments.quote: not sure what “ecoregions” are referring to; this needs to be added into the dataset description above

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: missing article (P5 L40), 'are less' (P7 L5), 'constraint' (P7 L21), 'Sea' capitalization (Fig S2).
comments.quote: Page 7, line 21: constrained, not constraint

comments.issue: Shape-type illustration appears too late (Fig 2B); embedding it earlier would help.
comments.request: Add shape illustration earlier or with Fig 1.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to see a figure illustrating the differences among prolate, oblate, and compact shapes earlier on in the manuscript

comments.issue: A sentence repeats nearly the same statement earlier in the paragraph.
comments.request: Delete the repeated sentence.
comments.quote: The sentence “However, taxonomic diversity changes with shape type” repeats nearly the same sentence earlier in the paragraph - I would delete

comments.issue: Calling an R2 of 0.89 'worse' is inappropriate.
comments.request: Replace “worse” with “less strong”.
comments.quote: I don’t think that an R2 value of 0.89 is worse! I would replace “worse” with “less strong”

comments.issue: Figure 1 could be used to define prolate, oblate and compact shapes.
comments.request: Use Figure 1 to define the shapes.
comments.quote: Fig 1: can you use this beautiful figure to define prolate, oblate, and compact shapes somehow?

comments.issue: Figure 2 labels are hard to read and its colour scheme is inconsistent with Figures 3-4.
comments.request: Enlarge labels and harmonize colours across figures.
comments.quote: can you make the labels bigger and use the color scheme from Figures 3 and 4 for each shape so there is congruence across figures?

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the analysis and geometry, but wants low-Reynolds-number context, resource dynamics, and many specific corrections.
strengths: shape variability reflects pelagic environmental variability

comments.issue: It is unclear why a simpler elongation metric (product of maximal linear dimension and S/V) was not used.
comments.request: Justify the choice of elongation measure.
comments.quote: it is not fully clear to me why the authors did not use a simpler approach to evaluate elongation like the computation of the product of maximal linear dimension and S/V

comments.issue: The low-Reynolds-number physical context of phytoplankton is missing and should be introduced early.
comments.request: Introduce low Reynolds number conditions early in the paper.
comments.quote: I missed information about the fact that the “star” of this story is a group of organisms living at low Reynolds numbers

comments.issue: Compact shapes with spines or papillae can hydrodynamically mimic elongated shapes, complicating the shape categories.
comments.request: Discuss how surface structures affect the shape categories.
comments.quote: Some “compact” shapes can have spines or papillae on their surface which can increase the effect of viscosity on cell surface and “mimic” the effect exerted by more elongated shapes

comments.issue: How resource availability varies in aquatic environments is not explained.
comments.request: Add lines on resource variability in aquatic environments.
comments.quote: a few lines explaining how the availability of resources can change in aquatic environments should be added

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: singular 'phytoplankton' (P3 L22), 'South-western Pacific' (P4 L27-28), 'assemblages' (P4 L36), 'affects' (P12 L41), five reference-detail fixes.
comments.quote: Page 12, line 41: “effects” should be “affects”

comments.issue: Cells are said to adjust their shape, but selection by the environment is the correct mechanism.
comments.request: Rephrase shape variation in terms of environmental selection and plasticity.
comments.quote: Cells do not adjust their shape: it is the environmental scenario that selects those individuals in the population which show the shape best fitting the scenario itself.

comments.issue: Including heterotrophic dinoflagellates contradicts the stated photosynthetic-microbe scope; their shape variability may be differently driven.
comments.request: Exclude heterotrophic organisms from the analyses.
comments.quote: I would suggest not to consider these organisms in the analyses.

comments.issue: Comparability of the two datasets collected with integrated and net sampling methods is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why the two sampling methods are comparable.
comments.quote: Here we have two datasets collected with very different methods (integrated samples and net samples). A line explaining why these two methods can allow comparability should be added.

comments.issue: Utermöhl microscopy is unsuitable for species identification, especially after Lugol preservation.
comments.request: Correct or justify the identification method.
comments.quote: Utermöhl method is ok for abundance and biovolume but not for species identification (especially after the samples have been preserved with Lugol's solution).

comments.issue: The new explanation for cell's longest linear dimension is unconvincing and irrelevant here.
comments.request: Delete this paragraph.
comments.quote: I think that the new suggestion advanced by authors to explain cell’s longest linear dimension is not fully convincing.

comments.issue: Choice between 'depends on' and 'determine' in the section title needs resolving.
comments.request: Pick the appropriate phrasing.
comments.quote: “Taxonomic diversity depends on cell volume and surface extension” or “Cell volume and surface extension determine taxonomic diversity”?

comments.issue: A sentence with a reference appears in the Results section.
comments.request: Move the sentence to the discussion.
comments.quote: should be moved to discussion (the results section should not contain references)

comments.issue: The constraint on wide oblate cells may simply reflect geometric impossibility or ecological limits.
comments.request: Consider these alternative explanations.
comments.quote: This in some case could be simply because some shapes are geometrically impossible and or because some shapes are not ecologically “fruitful”.

comments.issue: 'Fitness' is difficult to define because all functions must be satisfied simultaneously; intermediate compact cells are a compromise, not the single optimum.
comments.request: Rephrase the fitness claim as a compromise.
comments.quote: “Fitness” is thus difficult to be defined: everything depends on compromises.

comments.issue: The wall-elasticity sentence is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what is meant.
comments.quote: the sentence “Furthermore, an elongated shape requires some internal structures or varying wall elasticity, as a soft elastic wall would mostly favour a spherical shape” is unclear to me

comments.issue: The nutrient-rich elongation hypothesis is already well known and discussed in Reynolds 1997/2006.
comments.request: Acknowledge this prior work.
comments.quote: this is really well known and discussed in details

title: Shape matters: the relationship between cell geometry and diversity in phytoplankton

study.system: vertebrate hosts; life-history theory and infectious disease; review

editor_summary: Editor says all three reviewers find the review not coherent or comprehensive: two liked it but want major structural revision, one flags missing literature; a comprehensive revision must broaden coverage, define terms, add pathogen life history and restructure.

reviews.assessment: Major concern is omission of key literature, making the novelty positioning misrepresent the state of research; otherwise ambitious with potential.

comments.issue: Key papers integrating life history into disease models are omitted (de Leo & Dobson 1985; Bolzoni; Han; Downs et al.).
comments.request: Cite and discuss these key works.
comments.quote: the article omits several key papers that lay the groundwork for integrating life history theory with disease ecology theory

comments.issue: How the current model differs from previous life-history/disease modelling approaches is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify distinctions from previous approaches.
comments.quote: the distinctions between the current approach and previous approaches must be made clear, especially in a review

comments.issue: Novelty positioning falsely implies that life-history integration into disease ecology was never attempted before.
comments.request: Reposition the novelty relative to existing work.
comments.quote: gives the false impression that this integration has not been attempted before

comments.issue: Figure 1, especially the right panel, takes a while to grasp.
comments.request: Improve its clarity.
comments.quote: It took me awhile to grasp this figure, particularly the right hand panel

comments.issue: The claim about empirical validations across the tree of life lacks references.
comments.request: Add a review or studies from other branches of life.
comments.quote: could authors reference a review, or to other studies on more distant branches of the tree of life?

comments.issue: Terminology is not organized and synonyms and definitions are not consolidated.
comments.request: Add a terminology box with concise definitions.
comments.quote: I suggest to add a box to organize terminology, clarify any synonyms, and provide concise definitions

comments.issue: Literature joining life-history theory and allometric scaling with infectious disease theory is not cited from L124 onward.
comments.request: Review and cite this literature.
comments.quote: I suggest authors review and cite the literature joining LHT and allometric scaling with infectious disease theory

comments.issue: Whether beta-adjusted population depression equals differential population invasibility from the disease allometry literature is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between these concepts.
comments.quote: is this the same as differential population invasibility observed across hosts whose life history traits influence pathogen transmission

reviews.assessment: Excellent, timely and novel paper; main critique is dense writing that limits accessibility, plus many line-level suggestions.
strengths: diversity of fields is a real strength

comments.issue: Writing is too tight and intense to be readily accessible to a general audience.
comments.request: Improve sign-posting, e.g. outline the model in the introduction.
comments.quote: the writing is currently a bit too tight, which (in my opinion) means that the paper is a bit too intense to be readily accessible for a general audience

comments.issue: Technical terms from diverse fields are used without definition or explanation, and biological examples are missing.
comments.request: Define key terms and add biological explanations.
comments.quote: There are also multiple quite technical terms from diverse fields (the diversity I think is a real strength of the paper) used without definition/explanation

comments.issue: Sections end on specific points, missing opportunities for synthesis and links between sections.
comments.request: Improve synthesis within and between sections.
comments.quote: some of the sections end on rather specific points/examples, which loses some important opportunities for synthesis

comments.issue: A similar model paper (Trends in Ecology & Evolution 2005) is not cited.
comments.request: Cite and discuss it alongside this model.
comments.quote: The model used in that paper has some similarities to the one used here and so it would be great to discuss both alongside each other.

comments.issue: Implications of model assumptions (transmission mode, density versus frequency dependence) are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the model assumptions.
comments.quote: it would perhaps be worth discussing the implications of some of the assumptions made more clearly

comments.issue: 'Transient' is not clearly defined.
comments.request: Define transient dynamics explicitly.
comments.quote: It would perhaps be useful to more clearly define transient if mentioned?

comments.issue: The L138 section ends without linking to a broader message.
comments.request: Finish with a broader message or link back to disease ecology.
comments.quote: it doesn’t really go anywhere or link to anything. It would perhaps be good to finish with a broader message about what is needed?

comments.issue: A central slow-fast concept at L142-145 is covered very tersely.
comments.request: Explain it in more depth.
comments.quote: Here is an example of a concept that is absolutely central to the paper and a key difference across the slow-fast continuum but it is covered very tersely

comments.issue: Types of immunity and resistance versus tolerance are mentioned too briefly, and why innate immunity is less costly is not explained.
comments.request: Expand on these concepts and their costs.
comments.quote: talk in a little more details about these important but very briefly mentioned concepts (types of immunity, behavioural responses etc). Resistance versus tolerance seems like a particularly crucial one

comments.issue: The L169 section ends very specifically without synthesis.
comments.request: Add synthesis and clarify the key message.
comments.quote: Here is another example of a section that ends very specifically without any synthesis.

comments.issue: Lions and hyenas may differ in other important ways; alternative explanations need caveats.
comments.request: Caveat other explanations and distinguish decline versus recovery.
comments.quote: It seems likely that that lions and hyenas may differ in many other ways that might be important and that it would be good to caveat or mention other possible explanations?

comments.issue: The L197 section ends specifically without synthesis.
comments.request: Add synthesis.
comments.quote: Another example of a very specific end to a section missing out on an opportunity for synthesis

comments.issue: The L253-254 statement is a throwaway without implications discussed.
comments.request: Discuss implications for disease ecology or co-evolution.
comments.quote: This is a bit of a throwaway statement at the moment, it would be very useful to link it/discuss the implications for disease ecology or host-parasite co-evolution more clearly.

comments.issue: The model appears from nowhere without sign-posting in the introduction or section setup.
comments.request: Sign-post the model earlier.
comments.quote: Currently the model appears from nowhere! It would be very helpful to have pointed towards it when providing an outline for the paper in the introduction

comments.issue: Copy edits: typo 'modulateS' (L269) and a missing number (L623).
comments.quote: L623: Looks like there is a missing number here?

comments.issue: Model results at L268-384 are fired at the reader too fast without intuitive biological explanations.
comments.request: Add simple biological explanations and examples.
comments.quote: it would be very helpful to provide some simple/intuitive biological explanations and examples to help a general audience follow the results more clearly

comments.issue: Whether the same parasite R0 assumption holds across fast and slow hosts is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the validity of the equal-R0 assumption.
comments.quote: feel it might be valuable to discuss somewhere whether differences between fast and slow hosts might lead to this assumption being valid/not valid

comments.issue: The recovery parameter value is not justified in the text and sensitivity analyses are absent.
comments.request: Justify fixed parameters and report sensitivity analyses.
comments.quote: It would be good to provide (and perhaps justify) the parameter value picked for recovery in the main text as well as the figure legend.

comments.issue: Interpreting L445 purely on a fast-slow axis ignores alternative life-history axes.
comments.request: Consider additional axes of life-history variation.
comments.quote: It is perhaps a bit naïve to interpret this purely on a fast-slow axis (and so point to intermediate pace-of-life) without considering alternative life-history axes

comments.issue: The L449 paragraph ends very specifically.
comments.request: Add a broader closing message.
comments.quote: Another example of a very specific end to the paragraph

comments.issue: The evolution of plasticity, linking the ecological and evolutionary sections, is missing.
comments.request: Discuss the evolution of plasticity.
comments.quote: One thing that is missing currently, and seems to link the ecological and evolutionary sections here would be to discuss the evolution of plasticity

comments.issue: Reaction norms are introduced too late at L609.
comments.request: Move this concept earlier or remove it.
comments.quote: it is very late to introduce a new concept. Perhaps use this elsewhere or leave out?

comments.issue: Resolution of Figures 1 and 3 is low in the review PDF.
comments.request: Provide higher-resolution figures.
comments.quote: Resolution of Figures 1 and 3 is a bit low in my review pdf.

reviews.assessment: Very well-written, clear and broad-interest review with a well-detailed model; asks for better novelty framing, parasite traits and definitions.
strengths: very well-written, clear and easy to follow
topic of broad interest and high conservation relevance
model development well detailed and explained

comments.issue: Reproducibility details such as software used and number of model runs are missing.
comments.request: Add these details, perhaps in the supplement.
comments.quote: additional details should be included (perhaps in the supporting material) – this includes for instance information about the software used or the number of model runs

comments.issue: The individual-level idea that host life history influences disease impact is not new; only the review and the proportional-impact proposal are.
comments.request: Position novelty accordingly.
comments.quote: The idea that host life history may have an influence on how diseases will impact hosts at the individual level is not new

comments.issue: The text implies host traits matter more than parasite traits; the host perspective needs justification.
comments.request: Discuss parasite traits in the introduction.
comments.quote: The main text might leave the reader with the impression that host (life history) traits are potentially more important than any variation in parasite traits

comments.issue: Intra-specific and inter-individual heterogeneity in life-history traits is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss whether such heterogeneity matters.
comments.quote: There is strong focus in this review on inter-specific differences in life history strategies, but nothing is said about intra-specific / inter-individual heterogeneity in life history traits.

comments.issue: 'Disease ecology' and 'eco-immunology' are not clearly introduced or defined.
comments.request: Define both disciplines and their questions.
comments.quote: ‘disease ecology’ should probably be introduced and defined more clearly, and I suggest that ‘eco-immunology’ is also mentionned

comments.issue: The slow-fast axis would be strengthened by citing Healy et al. 2019.
comments.request: Add this reference.
comments.quote: I think this paper would be a nice additional reference and justification of the importance of this axis in life history theory

comments.issue: The role of epigenetic mechanisms linking life history and disease is not mentioned.
comments.request: Consider discussing epigenetics as a research avenue.
comments.quote: I wondered if there was anything known on the role of epigenetic mechanisms in linking host life history traits

comments.issue: L47 should also acknowledge the absence of knowledge on parasite characteristics.
comments.request: Add this caveat.
comments.quote: Line 47: And also without knowledge on parasite characteristics?

comments.issue: Whether age at first reproduction is equally relevant for seasonal versus year-round breeders is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the trait's comparability.
comments.quote: Is age at first reproduction equally relevant for species with seasonal breeding than for species that breed throughout the year

comments.issue: Behavioural resistance and tolerance are used frequently but not defined.
comments.request: Define these terms.
comments.quote: I suggest to define behavioural resistance and tolerance, as these terms are used frequently in the review

comments.issue: The L175-176 formulation suggests the position itself limits population growth rate.
comments.request: Rephrase as an influence on the constraint exerted.
comments.quote: The formulation seems to suggest that the position per se limits the population growth rate.

comments.issue: References for the definition of demographic compensation are missing at L200-203.
comments.request: Add the references.
comments.quote: I suggest to add again here references for the definition of demographic compensation

comments.issue: Whether the compensation mechanisms come from previous studies or the authors is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the provenance of the mechanisms.
comments.quote: It is not entirely clear to me if these mechanisms were clearly defined in previous studies or if they originate from the authors of the review

comments.issue: Copy edits: reference brackets (L219), missing 'of' (L382), wording at L583.
comments.quote: Line 382: the “of” is missing in “this type compensation”

comments.issue: Figure 1 community icons show species that do not co-occur; grey eggs and orange arrow sizes are unexplained.
comments.request: Use co-occurring species and explain the symbols.
comments.quote: I would suggest to choose icons of wildlife species that do live in the same ecosystem/habitat

comments.issue: Figure 2a lacks an on-figure legend, y-axis numbers are vertical, and life-history positions of pictured species are not shown.
comments.request: Add the legend, rotate labels and indicate slow-fast positions.
comments.quote: I recommend to add a legend for the black and grey lines directly on the figure and to put the numbers on the y-axis horizontally

comments.issue: Supporting figure S1 legend repeats 'fixed' and uses A./B. labels inconsistent with the main text.
comments.request: Fix the legend wording and panel labels.
comments.quote: rephrase first sentence of the legend as “fixed” appears twice

comments.issue: Table S2 could report studies finding no plasticity and include species positions along the slow-fast continuum.
comments.request: Add this information to the table.
comments.quote: Would it also be interesting to report studies where no plasticity in life history traits has been detected?

comments.issue: Table S2 is hard to read across pages and the first column is not repeated.
comments.request: Reduce font or column width so it fits.
comments.quote: the table is not very easy to read as it spreads on many pages and the trait considered (first column) does not appear on each page

title: Why disease ecology needs life‐history theory: a host perspective

study.system: ecophylogenetics; community ecology; review and synthesis

editor_summary: Editor and reviewers found it well written, but most felt it reads as a traditional review lacking the forward-looking synthesis ELE expects; author should push the field forward.

reviews.assessment: Mixed: authoritative and well-written history, but it reads as a traditional review whose sections do not build toward the future synthesis ELE expects.
strengths: well put together and clearly written
phylogeny as null model section is most interesting

comments.issue: Historical section does not clearly motivate the future directions section, the key part of an ELE reviews and synthesis piece.
comments.request: Strengthen the link between the history and the future directions.
comments.quote: it is not super clear to me how this section helps to motivate the future directions section, which to me is really the most important part of an ELE reviews and synthesis piece

comments.issue: Pairwise distances section lacks direction and repeats the pattern-process challenges it summarises.
comments.request: Add big-picture vision or structure to this section.
comments.quote: its not clear to me what this section is building towards or, on some level, how it has escaped some of the challenges about connecting pattern and process

comments.issue: Historical review is too long relative to the new ideas it should promote.
comments.request: Condense the historical review and expand the forward-looking sections.
comments.quote: I wish the entire historical review was condensed greatly, with more space given to new exciting ideas such as this to help drive the field forward

comments.issue: Dispersal, births and deaths are described as inherently stochastic processes, which depends on context and model assumptions.
comments.request: Qualify the characterisation of these processes as stochastic.
comments.quote: not sure if I agree with dispersal, births and deaths as being described as inherently stochastic processes

comments.issue: Type II error/species pool result is attributed to a review rather than the original study.
comments.request: Cite the original authors of the result.
comments.quote: Why not cite the folks who actually did the hard work here to show this?

comments.issue: Critique of Godoy's generalizability is unclear relative to other studies discussed.
comments.request: Clarify why this study is considered less generalizable.
comments.quote: not sure what this critique of Godoy is getting at with regards to generalizability

comments.issue: Elliot and Davies counterexample misrepresents Godoy's parameterized niche and fitness quantification.

comments.issue: Short paragraph on introspection and reexamination lacks context.

comments.issue: Phylogenetic signal section is well written but does not push the discussion forward for an ELE paper.

comments.issue: Phrasing about Webb 2002's intention could be more direct.

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic: well-summarised, well-written and provocative synthesis; only minor comments and literature suggestions, including feature versus functional diversity and additional references.
strengths: clearly explains caveats and proposed solutions

comments.issue: Conclusions of Gerhold et al. (2015) on using phylogenetic information are not referred to.

comments.issue: Statement that food web phylogenies cover few species misses examples spanning many species.

comments.issue: Typo 'Davies at al. (2012)' in citation.

comments.issue: 'Ecologically symmetrical' at line 44 is unnecessary jargon.

comments.issue: 'These stochastic processes' at line 45 does not specify which processes are meant.

comments.issue: Using Cam's first name at line 54 seems too familiar in style.

comments.issue: Long sentence at lines 93-96 is hard to read.

comments.issue: Better technology for fitting PGLMMs is not mentioned.
