title: A shift from phenol to silica‐based leaf defences during long‐term soil and ecosystem development

study.system: macroecology; MaxEnt-based dynamic theory of communities

editor_summary: Editor notes all reviewers saw potential in an important paper, but the theory is dense and difficult to penetrate, and needs a stronger connection to empirical data and tests.

reviews.assessment: Important, nearly unique dynamic macroecological theory, but very mathematical and needing clearer presentation and stronger empirical tests.
strengths: dynamic theory almost unique in macroecology

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the discrete-time formulation is a numerical discretization of an underlying continuous-time system.
comments.request: Clarify what the discrete time represents.
comments.quote: My understanding is that this is basically a discretization to allow numeric approximation somewhat like Runge-Kutta or lattice analysis of a PDE

comments.issue: The 1/3 energy scaling derivation is not connected to the well-known M^1/4 metabolic-rate literature.
comments.request: Present the M^1/4 derivation and cite that literature.
comments.quote: Scaling birth and death rates with energy (1/3) comes from E=m^(3/4) so E^(1/3)=M^(1/4), no?

comments.issue: The derivation of equations 27 and 28, including the immigrant-species probability, is incomprehensible.
comments.request: Explain the probability calculation behind equations 27 and 28.
comments.quote: Maybe I'm being obtuse but I in no way understand the deriviation of equations 27 & 28.

comments.issue: Speciation-rate formulations are well trodden in neutral theory but are not cited.
comments.request: Cite neutral-theory work on speciation rates.
comments.quote: Appropriate speciation rates including proportional to # individuals or # species and intermediate and saturating is well trodden in neutral theory

comments.issue: The functions f, h and q in equations 35-37 are not recalled and notation could help.
comments.request: Add notation or a table describing these rate equations.
comments.quote: I cannot remember by here what the functions f, h, q stand for. Could some notation help?

comments.issue: The transition from model/theory to results around page 22 is unclear.
comments.request: Add headings to help navigation.
comments.quote: about here I found myself wondering if we had transitioned from model/theory to results. Could headings help navigate this?

comments.issue: SI-C is a technical morass whose approximations hold only in some parameter ranges and appear to conflict with scaling literature.
comments.request: Add a biologically motivated summary of SI-C or explain why it works.
comments.quote: S1-C is massively complex and have some approximations that work only in some ranges of parameter space

comments.issue: Empirical testing is limited to two figures and looks handwavy; replication is needed.
comments.request: Replicate the empirical tests on one or two more datasets.
comments.quote: the degree of empirical testing of this theory is rather less (and less obvious) than I would expect in a paper in Ecology Letters

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important development, but the approach has a fundamental causality problem and its usefulness over simpler models is unclear.

comments.issue: METE may fail because its constraints are mis-specified, not because state variables change; this must be acknowledged.
comments.request: Note this alternative explanation in the Discussion.
comments.quote: traditional METE does not work because the specific constraints chosen or the way they are specified is just incorrect

comments.issue: No strong test against data; it is unclear whether DynaMETE outperforms traditional METE.
comments.request: Quantitatively compare DynaMETE and METE predictions with data.
comments.quote: a major short coming of this paper is that it is not clear if DynaMETE performs better than traditional METE

comments.issue: The implied causal structure, predicting state variables to feed MaxEnt, is questionable and self-referential by design.
comments.request: Justify the causal structure from first principles.
comments.quote: my concern with DynaMETE is with its implied causality and the high degree of model complexity required to accomplish this feat

comments.issue: The complex model (37 equations, ~10 free variables) is not shown to beat simpler size-structured neutral models, despite papers calling SAD/MRDI artifacts.
comments.request: Make the case that DynaMETE is better than simpler approaches.
comments.quote: the onus is on the authors to make a clear case for why this approach is significantly better than using a simpler approach like parameterizing a size-structured neutral model

comments.issue: The log-normal versus log-series SAD distinction should be explained in terms ecologists understand.
comments.request: Describe it via rare-tail length or degree of unevenness.
comments.quote: you note that an SAD can be either more log normal or more log series can you instead describe what this means in terms of the length of the rare tail or degree of unevenness

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the state variables are hard or soft constraints, which changes the MaxEnt solution.
comments.request: Clarify the constraint types and their consequences.
comments.quote: Can you please be clear if these are hard or soft constraints (sensu Haegeman and Loreau 2008)

comments.issue: It is unclear which METE variant (single-shot or recursive) is used for the SAR comparison.
comments.request: State which METE version is used.
comments.quote: Which version of METE are you using for the SAR comparison - single shot (Harte et al. 2008) or recursive (Harte et al. 2009)?

comments.issue: Two line-level fixes: a typo on Pg23 and a very confusing sentence on Pg28.
comments.request: Fix the typo and rewrite the confusing sentence.
comments.quote: This sentence is very confusing.

reviews.assessment: Interesting work undermined by poor readability and a fundamental concern about the two time scales in the iterative scheme.
strengths: novel idea of adding dynamic constraints

comments.issue: The manuscript is not reader friendly; excessive derivation details overshadow the key novelty of dynamic constraints.
comments.request: Provide a simpler illustrative example, e.g. only an LV-type dynamic constraint.
comments.quote: The manuscript is not reader friendly, while the key novelty of adding dynamic constraints was overshadowed by excessive details in deriving these transition functions

comments.issue: The relationship between iteration steps and dynamic time t is unclear and seemingly contradictory.
comments.request: Clarify the two time scales and their consistency.
comments.quote: My main concern, however, is regarding the two time scales – iterative steps (step i to i+1) and the time of the dynamic constraints (t).

comments.issue: If transition functions are specified, it is unclear why the dynamics are not solved directly as ODEs instead of re-solving MaxEnt each step.
comments.request: Justify solving the MaxEnt structure at each iteration.
comments.quote: I wonder whether the dynamics can be directly calculated from solving these time derivatives (ODEs). It is unclear why the MaxEnt structure has to be solved in each step.

title: DynaMETE: a hybrid MaxEnt‐plus‐mechanism theory of dynamic macroecology

study.system: metabolic theory of ecology; equal fitness paradigm; cross-taxon review

editor_summary: Editor notes all reviewers' significant concerns: derivations need fuller explanation, the framework is oversold without limitations, and the overlap with the authors' recent NEE paper must be addressed by highlighting new material.

reviews.assessment: Conceptual advance beyond the earlier EFP paper is insufficient for a synthesis, and scaling claims need more balance.
strengths: Figure 1 gives a more complete energy budget

comments.issue: Conceptual advance beyond the earlier EFP publication in Nature Ecology and Evolution is insufficient.
comments.request: Add further insight or quantitative examination beyond Brown et al. 2018.
comments.quote: at present, the conceptual or synthetic advance beyond Brown et al (2018) is not sufficient

comments.issue: A unique testable prediction of EFP about tissue energy content is not examined.
comments.request: Test whether species with lower tissue energy content replace themselves with more individuals.
comments.quote: species with lower tissue energy content (those closer to 17 kJ/g than to 37 kJ/g) should replace themselves with more individuals per generation, all else being equal

comments.issue: Lifetime growth figure is referred to as 'not shown' and within-group variation is not discussed.
comments.request: Refer to the reproduced figure and discuss the variation.
comments.quote: Given that you reproduce Hatton’s lifetime growth figure in your Figure 2, why not refer to that figure here, rather than say “not shown”?

comments.issue: Unclear whether metabolic rate correlations are size-driven or mass-independent.
comments.request: Be explicit and add citations, noting correlations are not ubiquitous.
comments.quote: Do you mean that these rates are correlated with each other because they all co-vary with size, or because they exhibit mass-independent correlations?

comments.issue: Species selection criteria are not described.
comments.request: Explain how and why these species were chosen.
comments.quote: it would be valuable for the reader to know how and why these species were chosen

comments.issue: The field metabolic scaling exponent is asserted as 0.75 although it differs among taxa.
comments.request: Correct the exponent and cite Speakman and Krol 2010 and Nagy et al. 1999.
comments.quote: The scaling exponent of field metabolic, the rate emphasised here, is most certainly not 0.75.

comments.issue: History of related ideas on time is not reviewed or cited.
comments.request: Review and synthesise the history, e.g. Ginzburg and Damuth 2008.
comments.quote: Information regarding the history of related ideas should be reviewed and synthesised for a manuscript such as this.

comments.issue: Recent work on cardiovascular scaling is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Seymour et al. 2019.
comments.quote: There is also a recent study of scaling of cardiovascular variables in the circulatory systems of mammals (Seymour et al. 2019).

comments.issue: Selected citations emphasise the central tendency and ignore variation around the 0.75 exponent.
comments.request: Acknowledge variation and cite Glazier 2005, Uyeda et al. 2017 and White et al. 2019.
comments.quote: The citations you have selected emphasise the central tendency, whereas others emphasise the variation (e.g. Glazier 2005)

reviews.assessment: Interesting and highly general topic, but equations, figures and key concepts need substantial clarification.
strengths: data drawn from studies across a long time span

comments.issue: Unclear whether the EFP value is an average with deviations or a lower fitness threshold.
comments.request: Distinguish these interpretations.
comments.quote: Fitness will not be literally equal for all species, so the questions is what this EFP value represents.

comments.issue: Alternative fitness currencies (numbers, biomass, power) are not explored.
comments.request: Explore the consequences of other possible currencies.
comments.quote: Without any priors, the fitness equivalence could be in terms of numbers or biomass or energy or power or something else.

comments.issue: Derivation in Eq. 1 where Q and E cancel is not understood.
comments.request: Explain whether a specific E value is chosen to simplify.
comments.quote: In Eq. 1, I don’t understand that idea that Q can be expressed in terms of mass such that Q and E cancel out.

comments.issue: Symbol T is used for time but should denote temperature.
comments.request: Use T for temperature and t for time.
comments.quote: T should be used for temperature and t saved for time

comments.issue: Units of the terms in Eq. 6 are not shown to be consistent.
comments.request: Explain the unit consistency.
comments.quote: I don’t understand how the units for the terms in Eq. 6 are all consistent.

comments.issue: Biomass balancing in Eqs. 6-7 conflicts with energy balancing.
comments.request: Clarify whether energy and biomass are being balanced interchangeably.
comments.quote: In Eqs. 6 and 7 I don’t understand the balancing of biomass because isn’t it energy that must be balanced or are you saying those are the same thing.

comments.issue: Simultaneous equivalence of energy, biomass and numbers seems impossible.
comments.request: Explain how these balances can coexist.
comments.quote: It now seems like almost everything is being balanced and equivalent, but I don’t even see how it’s possible to simultaneously balance (have equivalences) for energy, biomass, and numbers.

comments.issue: In Eq. 8 one alpha becomes -1/4 while another stays arbitrary.
comments.request: Explain this choice.
comments.quote: In Eq. 8 why does on alpha become -1/4 while one is still left as an arbitrary alpha.

comments.issue: Unclear whether power and biomass must each be equivalent or only their ratio.
comments.request: Clarify what must be equivalent across species.
comments.quote: Therefore, do power and biomass each have to be equivalent across species or can biomass and power both vary a lot as long as their ratio is held equivalent.

comments.issue: Figure 2 reproduces Hatton's analysis without explaining what is new.
comments.request: Explain in text and caption how this differs from Hatton.
comments.quote: It says data from Hatton, so it would be worth it in text and caption to explain how this analysis and these results are different from what Hatton already did.

comments.issue: Figure 4 axis labels are difficult to read.
comments.request: Improve the axis labels.
comments.quote: At least in my version, the axis labels for Fig. 4 are difficult to read and understand.

comments.issue: Blue movement directions in Fig. 6 are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what the arrows represent.
comments.quote: In Fig 6, are the horizontal blue directions of movement supposed to correspond to trait distributions or niche axes or both?

comments.issue: Table 1 formatting is difficult to read.
comments.request: Improve the table layout.
comments.quote: The formatting of Table 1 makes it difficult to read.

reviews.assessment: Useful review but the claimed applications are unconvincing, the H-W analogy needs justification and limitations are not acknowledged.

comments.issue: Generality of the described patterns is questionable because examples cover only 8 species.
comments.request: Acknowledge this limitation.
comments.quote: The examples nicely illustrate the concepts presented in the paper, but cover only 8 species, so the generality of the “patterns” described is somewhat questionable.

comments.issue: The analogy with Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is asserted without adequate justification.
comments.request: Justify the comparison beyond the shared steady-state assumption.
comments.quote: As the current manuscript stands, some readers will be sceptical of these claims, and the comparison with the H-W equilibrium warrants justification beyond the sharing of an assumption of steady-state

comments.issue: EFP's usefulness beyond restating population growth is unclear; departures from stable fitness offer no obvious insight.
comments.request: Clarify the ecological and evolutionary insights offered.
comments.quote: The authors could make clearer what ecological/evolutionary insights are offered by departures from a stable mean energetic fitness other than population growth or decline.

comments.issue: Red Queen dynamics imply perpetual selection, contradicting the EFP steady-state assumption.
comments.request: Reconcile this contradiction.
comments.quote: How does this scenario of perpetual natural selection represent the steady state of the EFP when the authors have previously stated (lines 118-119)

comments.issue: EFP transmits only energy, not genetic material, so its contribution to evolutionary dynamics is unclear.

comments.quote: Could the authors give an indication of how the EFP would contribute to an evolutionarily explicit model of ecological interactions?

comments.issue: Dynamic energy budget theory and related literature are absent.

comments.quote: The authors could strengthen their review by placing the EFP in the context of the wider literature on energetics in ecology and life history, and explaining what advantages the EFP holds over alternative theories and approaches.

comments.issue: Fitness is discussed interchangeably at species, population and individual levels.

comments.issue: Fitness on line 92 is presumably individual-level but this is not stated.

comments.issue: Generation time definition says parents leave two offspring, implying population growth.

comments.issue: The AmP database already collates metabolic life-table data for about 2000 species.

comments.issue: Claim that F varies about 25-fold across taxa rests on only 8 species.
comments.request: Temper the claim.
comments.quote: This statement could be tempered a bit by acknowledging that these results are based on only 8 species.

comments.issue: The 'currencies' of evolution are not described.
comments.request: Describe evolutionary currencies such as allele frequencies and genetic variances.
comments.quote: In the following sentences I missed a description of the “currencies” of evolution - additive genetic variances, allele frequencies, rates of change of heritable traits?

comments.issue: Dynamic energy budget theory, which has very similar aims, is not acknowledged here.
comments.request: Acknowledge this alternative theory.
comments.quote: This is practically the definition of dynamic energy budget theory - it would be remiss to not at least acknowledge the existence of a well-developed alternative theory with very similar aims.

comments.issue: Table 1 is poorly rendered and reports ratios to nine decimal places.
comments.request: Fix the rendering and reduce decimal places.
comments.quote: Table 1 is difficult to read because it has presumably been poorly rendered during pdf conversion.

title: Universal rules of life: metabolic rates, biological times and the equal fitness paradigm

study.system: Diversity and equity in ecology and evolutionary biology; BIPOC scholars

editor_summary: Editor strongly supports the piece, noting that both reviewers agree the topic is important and provide constructive suggestions to increase its impact.

reviews.assessment: Praise for a well-thought-out paper; minor suggestions to clarify 'fair', emphasize long-term commitment and add an actionable summary.
strengths: well-thought out paper on a critical issue
builds individual recommendations into actions for organizations

comments.issue: 'Fair representation' is subjective and needs a citation or clarification.

comments.issue: Diversity training is portrayed without noting that it must be a long-term commitment and that short-term approaches can backfire.

comments.issue: High-level decision makers may not read the full paper; a short list of key action items is missing.

comments.issue: Sentence at L44-45 is uninformative about the hypothesised pathways.

comments.issue: Expression "major niche axis" at L87 is unclear.

comments.issue: Assembled communities do not exist in nature and the reason is unclear.

comments.issue: Fixed terms of the models are not specified.

comments.issue: Linear regression fitted to an apparently non-linear relationship.

comments.issue: Figure 2 colours are not colour-blind friendly.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic, but the analyses and presentation are unclear and the manuscript needs restructuring.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important contribution, with many detailed comments to clarify methods and interpretation.

comments.issue: Sentence implies LUE was independently measured, which it was not.

comments.issue: Unclear how the results help design or manage mixed-species communities.

title: Enhanced light interception and light use efficiency explain overyielding in young tree communities

study.system: Mediterranean coralligenous assemblages; 10+ year photographic records and trait analysis

editor_summary: Both reviewers appreciated the thrust and writing, but raised the same substantive concern that 'ecosystem function' was poorly defined; the editor finds this version unacceptable and notes supplemental material issues.

reviews.assessment: Nice, well-written study of temperate assemblages; asks for clearer definitions of ecosystem function and integrity.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks examples of the functions that could be lost.
comments.request: Give illustrative examples early, e.g. from Table S1.
comments.quote: I miss some examples of functions - what are we supposed to be aware of losing?

comments.issue: 'Ecosystem functioning' is not defined as structure, stability/resilience or ecosystem services.
comments.request: Clarify what ecosystem functioning means in this study.
comments.quote: What do the authors mean by ‘ecosystem functioning’ – is it structure/ecosystem regimes, stability/resilience, ecosystem services?

comments.issue: 'Ecosystem integrity' is defined only as average trait value, which is abstract.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of ecosystem integrity.
comments.quote: I encourage the authors to clarify what they mean by ‘ecosystem integrity’, beyond the current definition

comments.issue: The appropriate reference for response diversity (Elmqvist et al. 2003) is missing.
comments.request: Add the Elmqvist et al. 2003 reference.
comments.quote: Elmqvist et al. 2003 is the appropriate reference here

comments.issue: A map of the study sites would be more useful than the coordinates in Table 1.
comments.request: Add a study site map.
comments.quote: I would rather have a map showing the study sites than information of longitude and latitude found in Table 1.

comments.issue: Depth may confound the trait composition because transects span 18-29 m and depths appear lumped.
comments.request: Test depth as a confounding variable.
comments.quote: I am curious to know if the authors tested ‘depth’ as a confounding variable?

comments.issue: The C. rubrum response curve with two data points appears fitted to the P. clavata curve without stating this.
comments.request: Clarify this in the figure legend.
comments.quote: I think it is important to clarify that the response curve for C. rubrum, which only contains two data points was fitted to the curve of P. clavata

comments.issue: Thermotolerance should be specified as first signs of necrosis.
comments.request: State that thermotolerance refers to first signs of necrosis.
comments.quote: I would clarify that thermotolerance refers to ‘first signs of necrosis’

comments.issue: Table S1 linking traits to functions would be valuable in the main manuscript.
comments.request: Include a condensed version of Table S1 in the main text.
comments.quote: I would like to see a condensed version of this in the main manuscript, where traits are linked to the functions they underpin.

comments.issue: The two axes explaining 54% of the variation are not named in the text.
comments.request: Mention the two axes in the text.
comments.quote: Please mention the two in the text.

comments.issue: Figure 5 lacks an integrated diversity index across panels.
comments.request: Add a diversity index integrating panels g-k and l-p.
comments.quote: I would have appreciated some short of diversity index (e.g. Shannon-W, or similar) that integrates panels g-k, with l-p.

comments.issue: Whether MHWs occurred before the baseline (T0) and already eroded trait distributions is unknown.

comments.issue: The relevant Loya et al. 2001 reference on coral bleaching winners and losers is missing.
comments.request: Add the Loya et al. 2001 reference.
comments.quote: A relevant reference here is Loya et al. ‘Coral bleaching: the winners and the losers’, Ecology Letters (2001) 4: 122-131.

comments.issue: 'Final direction' is too strong; 'trajectory' better conveys multiple possible paths.
comments.request: Replace 'final direction' with 'trajectory'.
comments.quote: I disagree there is a “final direction”. I would rather use “trajectory”

comments.issue: Whether redundancy and response diversity were truly lost depends on how the function is defined; the habitat function may persist to a lesser extent.
comments.request: Define the function and discuss partial persistence versus loss.
comments.quote: The fundamental question here is how the function is defined.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-illustrated study, but the link from traits to ecosystem functioning is weak and conclusions too broad.
strengths: well written with very well done figures

comments.issue: The link between trait changes and ecosystem functioning is weak; many traits reflect biotic filtering rather than functions, and functioning is never defined.
comments.request: Translate trait changes into ecosystem functions and define what functioning means.
comments.quote: I find the provided link between the described changes in trait composition and the resulting implications for ecosystem functioning sadly a bit weak

comments.issue: The study design and results are hard to follow, partly because crucial information is spread over 13 supplementary files.
comments.request: Improve clarity of each step of the study design.
comments.quote: I would recommend the authors to try to improve clarity of each step in the study design

comments.issue: The conclusions are too broad because they rest on one key species, and the decline in critical functions is not fully interpreted.
comments.request: Narrow the conclusions and interpret the functional consequences.
comments.quote: it seems that their conclusions may be formulated a little too broad, based on one key species being a main driver of their findings

comments.issue: The results extend existing knowledge rather than reveal novel ecological phenomena required for Ecology Letters.
comments.request: Articulate the novelty and significance more strongly.
comments.quote: I feel that the results only extend current existing knowledge further rather than reveal novel ecological phenomena

comments.issue: The decline of critical functional groups is stated without brief insight into why the group is critical.
comments.request: Add brief context on the critical functional groups.
comments.quote: It would be informative for the reader to get some more (very brief) insight to the decline of critical functional groups instead of just stating the fact.

comments.issue: What 'functional stability at risk' means, and how it differs from resilience, is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of functional stability.
comments.quote: What do the authors explicitly mean by that?

comments.issue: Representative references for the statement at lines 66-67 are missing.
comments.request: Add representative references.
comments.quote: Please add representative references for this statement.

comments.issue: The depth interpolation from 15 and 20 m to 18 m is poorly justified, and loggers may not have been deployed at sampling depth.

comments.quote: having a clearer picture of the reasoning and the accuracy of the used data is quite critical, since this measure basically affects the study significantly

comments.issue: The definition of a marine heatwave is not provided in the manuscript, and whether Tmax below the thermotolerance limit counts is unclear.
comments.request: State the MHW definition briefly in the manuscript.
comments.quote: What is the definition of a MHW here? The applied definition of the approach should be at least briefly included in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Circle sizes in Figure 1 conflict with the x-axis for Passe_cor (2009 larger than 2014 despite fewer MHW days).
comments.request: Explain the size encoding.
comments.quote: when e.g. looking at Passe\_cor, the 2009 circle is larger than the 2014 circle although the x axis suggests in 2009 a duration of less than 30 days

comments.issue: Figure 1 includes 2-5 years per site while analyses use three sampling times.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy.
comments.quote: It is also unclear to me why in figure 1 there are 2 to 5 years included per site while the analysis is always based on 3 sampling times T1, T2, T3

comments.issue: How sites were classified as MHW-impacted or non-impacted from logger data is not explained.
comments.request: Describe the classification procedure.
comments.quote: How was that done? This is not clear from the manuscript.

comments.issue: The relationship between 24 quadrats of 25x25 cm and the stated 5000 cm2 sampling unit is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the sampling unit was derived.
comments.quote: To the reader this section is unclear.

comments.issue: Table S5, referenced at L188, cannot be found.
comments.request: Correct the table reference.
comments.quote: I could not find the referenced table S5

comments.issue: What 'trait values' means (fuzzy coded value?) is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of trait values.
comments.quote: What is meant by trait values here and in the subsequent section? The fuzzy coded value?

comments.issue: The meaning of alpha = 5% is not indicated.
comments.request: Explain what alpha = 5% means.
comments.quote: The authors should indicate what alpha = 5% means.

comments.issue: The number of modalities among the 12 traits is not stated.
comments.request: Mention how many modalities the traits include.
comments.quote: Here and already in the methods the authors should also mention how many modalities the selected 12 traits include.

comments.issue: The results are left for the reader to observe in figures instead of being presented.
comments.request: Present and explain the results before referencing the figures.
comments.quote: The authors should present the results and explain what the figure shows and then reference it

comments.issue: 'Functional stability' is used inconsistently: impacted sites are described as stable in one place and changing in another.
comments.request: Formulate and use the term consistently.
comments.quote: The term functional stability is somewhat unclear, used in different contexts in the manuscript and needs better formulation and interpretation.

comments.issue: What the functioning of ecosystems refers to, given that assemblages with different functional identity still function, is unclear.
comments.request: Define the value of ecosystem function being referred to.
comments.quote: What is meant by the functioning of ecosystems? Assemblages of different FI may still function as such.

comments.issue: The information at lines 421-422 is not located for the reader.
comments.request: Refer to where this information is shown.
comments.quote: Please refer to where this information is shown.

comments.issue: How the resilience of key species could be promoted is not addressed.
comments.request: Suggest how to promote resilience of key species.
comments.quote: How can one promote the resilience of those key species?

title: Climate change transforms the functional identity of Mediterranean coralligenous assemblages

study.system: temperate oak savanna-forest ecotone; 35-yr survey, fire experiment, model

editor_summary: All three reviewers support the paper's merits but ask for greater generality, more methods/system detail, and serious attention to model design (equilibrium assumption, monospecific design, spatial dynamics).

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed this nice blend of long-term empirical ecology and modelling; several comments on contextualizing results and clarifying methods.
strengths: nice blend of long-term empirical ecology and modelling

comments.issue: Results are not contextualized for different disease time-scales or fire-vegetation feedback directions.

comments.quote: How would your results change if the progression of the disease was slower - would you see the same interactions?

comments.issue: Model collapses species and space; assumptions are not stated and spatial effects not discussed.
comments.request: State these assumptions in the main text and discuss spatial dynamics and seed supply.
comments.quote: Both of the processes (fire and disease) that you consider in the model are inherently spatial but the model itself is non-spatial processes

comments.issue: Methods are sparse, with important model details and results buried in the supplement.
comments.request: Move important model details and results into the main text.
comments.quote: I found the text describing the methods a little sparse in places

comments.issue: Several line-level wording fixes (L6 'differential', L17 'pervasive', L82 'Q.', L110 'surface fire').
comments.quote: Are disturbances playing a more 'pervasive' role? Isn't it rather than regimes are shifting quickly and some ecosystems are struggling to 'keep up'.

comments.issue: The importance of disturbance sequence (priority effects) is not considered.

comments.quote: The sequence of the events can also be important (e.g. Fukami, Oikos 92: 215-224).

comments.issue: Context on oak wilt (endemic status, spread, mortality rate) is missing for non-specialists.
comments.request: Add pathogen context, including mortality rates and age specificity.
comments.quote: A little more context for readers not familiar with the system/pathogen would be useful here.

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'largest' means at L127.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of 'largest' at L127.
comments.quote: Line 127 - What does 'largest' mean here - I assume stem density?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the 93rd percentile refers to this species or all stems at L135.
comments.request: Clarify the percentile reference.
comments.quote: Line 135 - I assume this refers to the 93 percentile for this species not all stems?

comments.issue: Whether standing dead trees killed by oak wilt influence fuel characteristics is unaddressed.
comments.request: Address the fuel influence of standing dead trees.
comments.quote: Lines 210-214 - Do standing dead trees (i.e. killed by the oak wilt) also influence fuel characteristics?

comments.issue: The sentence on sapling 'birth' at L220-222 is unclear and seems to mean recruitment.
comments.request: Rewrite to describe sapling recruitment and its decreasing function.
comments.quote: I assume you don't mean 'birth', but rather recruitmment rate of saplings?

comments.issue: Whether adult trees can suffer fire mortality is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify adult fire-mortality in the model.
comments.quote: Lines 222-224 - So adult trees can not suffer fire-mortality?

comments.issue: Empirical support for the disease transmission function is missing and its shape is not described.

comments.quote: Line 226-227 - Empirical evidence for this transmission function? And you could (at least) describe its shape here.

comments.issue: The statement at L304-306 reads as a truism.
comments.request: Revise or remove the truism at L304-306.
comments.quote: Line 304-306 - This statement seems to be a truism?

comments.issue: Applicability to other disturbance systems and the role of feedback direction and time scales need discussion.

comments.issue: Code should be archived in a repository.

comments.issue: Figure 1 components (d) and (e) lack a sense of scale.

comments.issue: The fire-frequency colour scale in Figure 2a duplicates the x-axis.
comments.request: Remove the redundant colour scale.
comments.quote: a - Do you really need the colour scale for fire frequency given it is on the x-axis?

comments.issue: Thick and thin lines in Figure 2b are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Make the line types easier to distinguish.
comments.quote: b - It is hard (almost impossible) to delineate the thick and think lines here (and on the other similar graphs).

comments.issue: The contrasting groups in the Figure 2b plots are unexplained.

comments.issue: Blue and purple are hard to distinguish in Figure 5.

comments.quote: Figure 5 - The blue and purple are hard to distinguish

comments.issue: Whether soils mediate savanna-forest interactions in this system is not addressed.
comments.request: Clarify the role of soils.

comments.issue: Whether species-level equations exist for the two Quercus species is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify species-level equations for the two Quercus species.

comments.issue: It is unclear why plot-level random effects are included in some analyses but not others.
comments.request: Explain the inconsistent inclusion of plot-level random effects.
comments.quote: Lines 444-451 - Did you include a plot-level effect here (e.g. as a random variable) - you do in other places

comments.issue: It is unclear whether multiple cores were taken for within-tree cross-matching.

comments.quote: Line 457 - Did you take multiple cores for within-tree cross-matching?

comments.issue: Whether age-to-coring-height was accounted for is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how age to coring height was handled.
comments.quote: Line 458-9 - Did you account for age to coring height (and Fig. S5)?

comments.issue: The frequency of rotten cores is not reported.
comments.request: Report how often rotten centres were encountered.

comments.issue: Whether subtle aspect effects are included in the model is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether aspect effects are in the model.
comments.quote: Lines 481-486 - These subtle aspect effects are included in the model are they?

comments.issue: The text at L517-519 appears to contradict the emphasis on heterogeneity elsewhere.
comments.request: Reconcile the treatment of heterogeneity.

comments.issue: The basis for the 20 cm adult threshold is not explained.
comments.request: Justify the 20 cm adult threshold and its link to fire persistence.
comments.quote: Lines 539 - Why 20 cm for the adult threshold? is this related to ability to persist through fire?

comments.issue: The reviewer expects data to exist for the quantity discussed at L564.
comments.request: Provide the available data for this quantity.

comments.issue: The description of the optimisation approach at L613-617 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the optimisation approach.

comments.issue: Figure S6 lacks error terms or full data display.

comments.issue: Figure S11 could be simplified by plotting differences between simulations.

comments.issue: Plot sizes are not reported.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and compelling, but the model's equilibrium and monospecific design raise serious doubts and some claims, such as 54 years, are oversold.
strengths: unique long-term experiment with compounding disturbances
valuable combination of experiment and modelling

comments.issue: The abstract omits central details (study location, pathogen) and trims ecological information for a broad audience.
comments.request: Include pertinent ecological details in the abstract and text for an ecological readership.
comments.quote: As it is the central parameters of study, such as where it was conducted, the name of the pathogen under study etc. are omitted from the abstract.

comments.issue: Claims are oversold, e.g. the 54-year title versus 25 years of analyzed data.
comments.request: Tone down claims and make the text fit the data.
comments.quote: While the title talks about a 54-year experiment, actual data analyzed for the study only go back 25 years

comments.issue: Results specific to two tree species and one pathogen are not critically appraised for generalization.
comments.request: Critically reflect on what is generalizable versus system-specific.
comments.quote: I thus strongly suggest to more critically reflect about what is generalizable from your study, and which aspects emerge from the idiosyncrasies of your particular study system.

comments.issue: The first discussion paragraphs mainly re-narrate results and could be shortened.
comments.request: Shorten the results re-narration in the discussion.
comments.quote: the first paragraphs of the discussion mainly re-narrate the results and could be shortened considerably for a more critical appraisal of the findings

comments.issue: The equilibrium assumption does not make sense for a heavily disturbed system.
comments.request: Reconsider the equilibrium assumption.
comments.quote: the equilibrium assumption doesn't make sense for a heavily disturbed system such as the one studied here

comments.issue: Reproducing dynamics is not a strong test because a wrong model with many free parameters can fit.
comments.request: Provide a stronger test of the model than reproducing the data.
comments.quote: even an ecologically “wrong” model with enough free parameters (and you have a lot of them here!) would be able to reproduce the data after model fitting

comments.issue: The monospecific model mismatches the study's two species with differential sensitivities.
comments.request: Align the model design with the two-species experimental findings.
comments.quote: there seems to be a clear mismatch between what was found experimentally and how the model was designed

comments.issue: The meaning of '(MS)' at l81 is unclear.
comments.request: Define the abbreviation.
comments.quote: l81: what does “(MS)” mean here?

comments.issue: The text conflates individual-level and population-level effects of fire on survival and growth.
comments.request: Clarify whether survival and growth effects are independent or linked.
comments.quote: are these independent effects at the level of individuals, or are these population level effects where one (survival) determines the other (growth)?

comments.issue: Growth and survival should be treated as independent demographic processes.
comments.request: Treat growth and survival as two independent demographic processes.
comments.quote: I'd strongly suggest to treat growth and survival as two independent demographic processes

comments.issue: The paragraph at l215-231 describes methods but sits in the results.
comments.request: Move this paragraph to the methods.
comments.quote: this paragraph describes methods, it should not be in the results section but in the M&Ms; section

comments.issue: The discussion at l266-303 is largely a redundant re-narration of results.
comments.request: Condense this discussion section considerably.
comments.quote: although nice, this part of the discussion is mainly a re-narration of the results, and is thus largely redundant

comments.issue: Generalizability is insufficiently explored, including contingency on species traits and pathogen biology.
comments.request: Expand the generalizability discussion, possibly with more model simulations.
comments.quote: this paragraph on the generalizability (or not) of your findings is important, and should be expanded considerably

comments.issue: Plot sizes are essential but not reported.
comments.request: Report plot sizes.
comments.quote: it would be essential information to know how large these plots are

comments.issue: The title alludes to a 54-year experiment though data collection started 25 years ago.
comments.request: Do not mislead readers about the study duration.
comments.quote: the title alludes to a 54-year experiment, yet the data collection seems to have only started 25 years ago

comments.issue: The strict pre/post disease separation ignores gradual disease spread.
comments.request: Use a different proxy for disease pressure.
comments.quote: I find the strict separation in pre and post disease years to be problematic, to say the least

comments.issue: Which statistical models and tests were used is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the statistical models and tests.
comments.quote: can you be a bit more specific, which models, which tests, etc.?

comments.issue: Transect lengths and widths are not reported.
comments.request: Report transect dimensions.
comments.quote: you here talk about transects without mentioning how long and how wide they were

comments.issue: The single-species model is weak given the importance of species-specific traits.
comments.request: Consider species-specific trait differences in the model.
comments.quote: l517: the model is rather weak, considering only one species

comments.issue: Equilibrium stem density is inappropriate in a disturbance experiment across a forest-grassland gradient.
comments.request: Reconsider the use of equilibrium stem densities.
comments.quote: I have a hard time understanding how working with an equilibrium density concept can make sense in a disturbance experiment across a gradient from forest to grassland

comments.issue: The meaning of 'long-term' at l621 is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the timescale meant by long-term.
comments.quote: l621: how long is “long-term”?

reviews.assessment: Valuable contribution from a rare long-term dataset; asks for more context on spatial dynamics, study area and alternative drivers.
strengths: rare long-term record capturing a new disturbance
rich empirical record combined with a simple model

comments.issue: Extending the insight to other regions requires considering spatially spreading fire and disease.
comments.request: Consider spatially interactive feedbacks when extending the findings.
comments.quote: extending this insight to other regions requires careful consideration of how the dynamics might play out when both disturbance types are able to spread across the landscape

comments.issue: Which findings are specific to the controlled burning experiment is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how results might differ outside a controlled burning experiment.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to provide a little more context/discussion of which of the findings were specific to the controlled burning experiment

comments.issue: The 'diseased woodland' state seems ephemeral without artificial fire protection.
comments.request: Explain how diseased woodlands could be stable given fire spread.

comments.issue: Historical ignition sources, pre-1964 forest distribution and natural fire breaks are not described.
comments.request: Provide this study-area context and discuss whether forests could persist with fire spread.
comments.quote: It would be useful to know the historical ignition source (presumably these are predominantly human-ignited fires), and whether/where forests existed in the broader landscape prior to the experimental removal of fire

comments.issue: Deer browsing could alter oak regeneration dynamics but is not addressed.

comments.quote: is there any information about herbivory, particularly by deer, in this study area?

comments.issue: Northern red oak is mentioned but ignored, though its traits could influence dynamics.
comments.request: Explain the treatment of Q. rubra and its potential influence.
comments.quote: there is no further mention of northern red oak. Most of the results and discussion are presented as if bur oak and northern pin oak were the only oak species in this system.

comments.issue: The phrase 'the two oaks' is ambiguous after mentioning four species.

comments.quote: replace “the two oaks” with “the two dominant oak species of the savannas”

comments.issue: The 14% chance of reaching 5 cm dbh assumes normal growth and 100% survival, which is unlikely.
comments.request: Explain and justify the assumptions behind the 14% estimate.

comments.issue: Mortality would be more comparable if presented as annual rates.

comments.quote: The mortality values would be more intuitive and more easily compared to other studies if they were presented as an annual mortality rate over the interval from 2010-2018

comments.issue: 'Landscape' at line 199 is inappropriate for plot-level processes.
comments.request: Change 'landscape' to 'stand' or 'plot'.
comments.quote: change “landscape” to “stand” or “plot”

comments.issue: Lower fire temperature does not show that forests are stable where fire can spread.

comments.issue: Data on fire effects in long-unburned forests are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss available data on fire effects in long-unburned forests.
comments.quote: If data are available to evaluate the effects of fire in long-unburned forests in this region, it would be useful to discuss it

comments.issue: Why disease plus reduced fire frequency yields a novel state is unclear.
comments.request: Explain why disease leads to a state unattainable by fire regime alone.

comments.issue: Different responses to increases versus decreases in fire frequency need discussion.

comments.quote: it seems that the different responses to increases and decreases in fire frequency with and without disease could use further discussion

title: Disease and fire interact to influence transitions between savanna–forest ecosystems over a multi‐decadal experiment

study.system: beta diversity; tree and coral community time series

editor_summary: Compelling topic of broad interest; most importantly one reviewer finds the method description insufficient for assessment; authors must address all comments with a major revision.

reviews.assessment: Calls the method a significant advance, clearly written, with only minor suggestions on nestedness, scaling and metacommunity context.

clearly written with logical development and notation
ability to distinguish unchanged versus changing beta diversity cases

comments.issue: The connection to Baselga's nestedness-turnover decomposition is unclear; the approach ignores nested subsets and may not distinguish them.

comments.issue: The role of the scaling factor G is only clear after reading the appendix.

comments.issue: Whether the relativization accounts for temporal changes in local alpha diversity is unclear.

comments.issue: The literature often computes p-values from non-independent beta diversity values; the appropriate test on the tree data should be highlighted.

comments.issue: Metacommunity theory on spatial isolation and colonization-extinction dynamics is not engaged.

title: Temporal changes in spatial variation: partitioning the extinction and colonisation components of beta diversity

study.system: coral reef fish metapopulation; 7-yr field survey and parentage data

editor_summary: Editor: one negative review with fundamental concerns; concerns 1-2 (metapopulation definition) must be addressed carefully; IPM age-vs-size clarification also needed.

reviews.assessment: Well-executed, novel and excellently written study; only minor comments on clarity, density dependence and robustness.

comments.issue: The density-dependence portion of the text is written inaccessibly.
comments.request: Improve the clarity of this section.
comments.quote: I do find the writing a bit unaccessible for this portion of the text.

comments.issue: Density dependence in growth and dispersal is not considered or excluded.
comments.request: Discuss the evidence on other forms of density dependence.
comments.quote: What is the evidence for other forms of density dependence, e.g., growth and dispersal. Can you exclude those are relevant?

comments.issue: Unclear whether size was included in survival models, although size-dependent mortality is usually more appropriate.
comments.request: Explain and, if missing, include size in the survival models.
comments.quote: What is the evidence for size-dependent mortality and did you fit your survival models with size included, if not, why not.

comments.issue: How catchability is estimated at L.252 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how catchability was estimated.
comments.quote: L. 252 - how is catchability estimated? I think this needs to be addressed.

comments.issue: The description at L.236 is cryptic.
comments.request: Clarify this description.
comments.quote: L. 236 - the description is cyptic to me.

comments.issue: The paper relies heavily on the appendix, and Fig. D1 belongs in the main text.
comments.request: Move Fig. D1 to the main text with a panel figure of key processes.
comments.quote: In general, the reliance to the appendix is a bit heavy and Fig. D1 should be in main text together with panel based figure to show all key estimated processes

comments.issue: Genotyping error and its effect on the results are not addressed.
comments.request: Assess and report robustness of results to genotyping error.
comments.quote: Did the author address genotyping error and how robust are the results to this error?

comments.issue: The assumed closure of the 30 km study area conflicts with reliance on external sources.
comments.request: Speculate on where the external source populations are.
comments.quote: Can the author speculate where the sources that maintain the meta-populations are?

comments.issue: The deviation of the study's results from other studies is stated without explanation.
comments.request: Speculate on why the study deviates from others.
comments.quote: saying that your study deviates strongly from others is good, but why? Please speculate.

reviews.assessment: Concerns that study design and data resolution predetermined the result, so the study may not provide sufficient novel insight.
strengths: commendable effort collecting subtidal marine data

comments.issue: The study region may be a patchy population within a larger metapopulation, not a metapopulation.
comments.request: Justify the metapopulation framing or reframe the study system.
comments.quote: I believe the authors have defined a region within a much larger metapopulation that’s effectively functioning as a patchy population

comments.issue: Field sampling may not match the scale of demographically relevant connectivity; unsampled source populations likely exist nearby.
comments.request: Assess the connectivity scale and unsampled populations.
comments.quote: this is a question of scale, and whether the field sampling has been appropriate relative to the scale over which demographically relevant connectivity is operating

comments.issue: Parentage sampling recovered only about 10% of juveniles, so the kernel is unknown for most recruits.
comments.request: Address the limited parentage coverage and kernel uncertainty.
comments.quote: the study only found 71 parent-offspring matches out of 791 juveniles over 7 years

comments.issue: Population units are not defined and breeding numbers are very low.
comments.request: Define populations and report occupancy and breeding numbers.
comments.quote: How are populations defined and at what spatial scales? How many individuals make up a population?

comments.issue: It is unclear what "20% of the habitat was sampled" means.
comments.request: Clarify whether 20% refers to reef habitat or suitable habitat.
comments.quote: It is unclear what the authors mean by 20% of the habitat was sampled.

comments.issue: Growth and survival exclude fish under 6 cm, missing early post-settlement size-dependent effects.
comments.request: Address the missing small-size demographic effects in the IPMs.
comments.quote: Growth and survival are calculated from only fish >6 cm in length, correct? Much of the growth and mortality post-settlement happens in individuals smaller than this.

comments.issue: The model is age based while the data are size based, and the size-age relationship is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain how size and age were reconciled in the IPMs.
comments.quote: the model is age based (annual age classes). All the data, however, are presented as size dependent.

comments.issue: Dispersal, growth and fecundity are not estimated per population, omitting patch quality and demographic heterogeneity.
comments.request: Estimate rates per population or discuss the consequences of heterogeneity.
comments.quote: the dispersal kernel, growth and fecundity were not estimated at an individual population level

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and analysis, well written and important; minor comments on kernel biases and figure clarity.
strengths: contrast with previous results explained well

comments.issue: Unclear whether the dispersal kernel likelihood includes sampling biases such as unsampled adults and habitat availability.
comments.request: Clarify the kernel methods and how these biases were addressed.
comments.quote: does the dispersal kernel really represent dispersal only, or could it also include biases like effects of under sampling at greater distances

comments.issue: The claim that persistence has never been quantified for a continuous marine population may be overstated.
comments.request: Rephrase or tone down this novelty claim.
comments.quote: “Persistence has yet to be quantified in the field for a continuous marine population” Is that really true?

comments.issue: Fig. 1 caption does not define the numbered circles or the black lines.
comments.request: Define the circles and explain the black lines in the caption.
comments.quote: Need to define what the three circles with numbers are in a) – d) in the caption.

comments.issue: What uncertainty the grey line in Fig. 3 represents is unspecified.
comments.request: State exactly what the grey line shows.
comments.quote: what exact “uncertainty” is the grey line showing – is it 95% confidence interval, or something else?

title: Persistence of a reef fish metapopulation via network connectivity: theory and data

study.system: marine Micromonas virus-phytoplankton; lab cultures and global model

editor_summary: Editor: valuable study merging lab, models and global patterns; systematically state assumptions; discuss local adaptation, scales, depth, sensitivity and host feedbacks; R0 is a poor fitness proxy; cite Rohwer and broader climate-disease literature.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and clearly modeled, but novelty over previous work is unclear and global predictions may not be broadly relevant.
strengths: modeling conducted in a clear and sensible way

comments.issue: The novelty relative to the authors' previous work is unclear; most empirical temperature dependencies were published before.
comments.request: Articulate in the introduction what was already learned and what this study adds.
comments.quote: I think it would help if the authors could more clearly articulate in the introduction what they have already learned from their previous work, and what they hope to learn from this modeling study.

comments.issue: Parts of the work may not be of broad enough interest for Ecology Letters.
comments.request: Clarify the broad significance of the contributions.
comments.quote: I think #1-2 are valuable contributions, though maybe not of broad enough interest for Ecology Letters.

comments.issue: The global extrapolation is unlikely to be predictive because other factors control host and viral populations (e.g., Micromonas is coastal and nutrient-rich).
comments.request: Temper the global predictions and discuss additional controlling factors.
comments.quote: #4 is a useful thought experiment but seems unlikely to be very predictive in reality, given all the other things that could effect host and viral populations.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether %infectivity of viral particles was measured or only model-estimated.
comments.request: State the source of the infectivity estimates.
comments.quote: The authors find a temperature dependent tradeoff between viral production and infectivity, but it is unclear from the discussion whether they have lab measurements of %infectivity of viral particles, or whether this results comes solely from the model-estimated parameters.

comments.issue: No standard errors or confidence intervals are reported for the hyperparameters.
comments.request: Report uncertainty for the hyperparameters.
comments.quote: There are no standard errors / confidence intervals reported for the hyperparameters.

comments.issue: A previously described non-lysis strategy at high temperatures is not mentioned.
comments.request: Discuss the non-lysis strategy and why it is not considered.
comments.quote: The authors’ 2017 paper states that at high temperatures the virus may switch to a strategy that produces virions from the host without lysis. Is there a reason this is not mentioned here?

reviews.assessment: Approach is interesting and well worked through; no suggestions for improvement.
strengths: interesting and well worked through approach
clear combination of lab experiments, model fitting and application

comments.issue: The simple host-virus model omits zooplankton grazers and nutrients, limiting the generality of the conclusions (though this is also a strength).
comments.quote: The host-virus model is relatively simple and does not consider the complexities of interactions with e.g. zooplankton grazers and nutrients.

title: A thermal trade‐off between viral production and degradation drives virus‐phytoplankton population dynamics

study.system: soil organic matter; Tibetan Plateau radiocarbon survey and global synthesis

editor_summary: Editor: reviewers recognize the importance and novelty but want the advance over Chen et al. 2019 highlighted and clarifications made, without substantially lengthening the manuscript.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, ambitious global study with a novel NPP-SOC turnover result; asks for clearer concept introduction and discussion refinements.

comments.issue: The title does not mention the study's large scale.
comments.request: Mention the large scale in the title.
comments.quote: The title should mention the large scale taken by the study.

comments.issue: The recommendation at L49-50 is reductionist and the priming effect is missing from the abstract.
comments.request: Include plant C input and priming in the abstract.
comments.quote: this recommendation is to reductionist: they should also include the role of plant C input

comments.issue: Key processes and terms such as climate stabilization and plant C input are introduced too quickly.
comments.request: Explain these concepts more fully for a broad audience.
comments.quote: The introduction of processes controlling SOC turnover is too fast.

comments.issue: The gradients of NPP and soil variables along the plateau are not shown.
comments.request: Add maps of these gradients.
comments.quote: I suggest to include some maps showing the gradient of NPP and soil variables along the plateau.

comments.issue: The equations at L197-203 and their assumptions are introduced too quickly.
comments.request: Explain the equations and the BNPP/root distribution assumption.
comments.quote: The introduction of these equations are too fast. I was constrained to read Yang paper to understand your calculation.

comments.issue: The text does not inform readers about the NPP and soil-variable gradients.
comments.request: Describe these gradients at L305-307.
comments.quote: It is important to inform the readers here about the gradients of NPP, soil variables along the plateau.

comments.issue: "SOC dynamics" is used although only residence time/turnover was analysed.
comments.request: Use turnover or MRT terminology.
comments.quote: The term “SOC dynamics” is abusive here because you only analysed the effect of variables on SOC residence time (or turnover).

comments.issue: The rationale for the two-pool incubation equation is not explained and fitting results are not shown.
comments.request: Justify the incubation analysis and cite relevant studies.
comments.quote: Moreover, we do not see the rationale behind this 2 pools equation.

comments.issue: The decline in molar ratio could also be explained by higher SOC content.
comments.request: Consider this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: but the significant decline in the molar ratio could also be explained by a higher SOC content no?

comments.issue: Deep patterns are also explained by declining root biomass and C input with depth, and deep C can be primed.
comments.request: Acknowledge this mechanism.
comments.quote: and of course by the exponential decrease in root biomass and their C input with depth

comments.issue: Minerals also preserve SOC by retaining it within the profile.
comments.request: Add this retention mechanism.
comments.quote: I think that the effect of soil minerals on SOC persistence is also due to their role in the retention SOC within the soil profile.

comments.issue: The assertion that C input always increases soil C is contradicted by context-dependent outcomes.
comments.request: Revise this assertion.
comments.quote: I disagree with this assertion and citation. Carbon input to soil may decrease soil C content, or increase it depending on various environmental conditions

comments.issue: The statement at L450-451 treats a fact as an eventuality.
comments.request: Rephrase as an established fact.
comments.quote: This is not an eventuality, but a fact

reviews.assessment: Valuable advance, but the Δ14C interpretation, the framing of C inputs and abstract balance need attention.
strengths: valuable advance consolidating topsoil and subsoil drivers

comments.issue: The interpretation of Δ14C values and the uncertainty in contrasting geographically dispersed soils are inadequately explained.
comments.request: Explain the Δ14C interpretation and its limitations.
comments.quote: inadequate attention to explaining interpretation of 14C values and acknowledging uncertainty surrounding the exact meaning of contrasting 14C between geographically dispersed soils

comments.issue: Plant C input is framed as a C stabilization process, although it is the substrate for stabilization.
comments.request: Reframe C inputs as the substrate, not a stabilization process.
comments.quote: Plant C input is framed as a C stabilization process, however it seems more accurate to state that plant C inputs form SOC

comments.issue: The abstract and conclusions present C input as the sole driver of topsoil Δ14C.
comments.request: Balance the abstract/conclusions and trim the ESM sentence.
comments.quote: A balanced presentation of results in the abstract (and conclusions), noting that C input was not the only driver of topsoil 14C, would be ideal

comments.issue: Grammar and wording edits throughout: verb conjugation, L48, L49, L90-91, L128, L243, L306, L370, L411-412.
comments.quote: I found many instances where attention to verb conjugation is needed

comments.issue: The statement that negative Δ14C values indicate older 14C atoms needs checking.
comments.request: Check the interpretation of positive and negative Δ14C values.
comments.quote: Here the authors assert that negative 14C values indicate that the 14C atoms in a sample are older

comments.issue: The 13C glucose addition experiment lacks a brief description in the main text.
comments.request: List manipulated variables and measured outcomes.
comments.quote: A few further details about the 13C labelled glucose addition experiment are called for here

comments.issue: The mass-balance explanation at L359 is unclear, including whether dilution and SOC increases are implied.
comments.request: Clarify and test the dilution explanation.
comments.quote: I am not certain what is meant by ‘simple mass balance between new and older preexisting C’ as potentially explaining this

comments.issue: The L403 paragraph conclusion is weak and the Carvalhais citation is not justified.
comments.request: Strengthen the conclusion and justify the citation.
comments.quote: I wonder if there is a way to conclude this paragraph with something stronger or more specific

comments.issue: A citation supporting the increased proportion of mineral-associated SOM at depth is missing.
comments.request: Add a supporting citation.
comments.quote: A citation supporting “increased proportion of stabilized SOM involved in mineral-organic associations at depth.” is called for here.

comments.issue: A relevant paper juxtaposing soil C stocks and flows is not considered.
comments.request: Consider this paper.
comments.quote: I wondered if the authors had considered their findings in light of the below paper juxtaposing soil C stocks and C flows

reviews.assessment: Important and valuable study; two major concerns about its relationship to Chen et al. 2019 and the literature discussion.
strengths: dataset of value to the community

comments.issue: The relationship to the authors' published work in Chen et al. (2019) is not clarified.
comments.request: Clarify the advance beyond Chen et al. 2019.
comments.quote: Relationship to published work in Chen et al (2019)

comments.issue: The discussion of literature and connection to prior work is weak.
comments.request: Strengthen the literature discussion.
comments.quote: Discussion of literature and connection to prior work needs to be strengthened

reviews.assessment: Potentially substantial contribution, but the priming-effect attribution needs stronger justification and the writing needs work.
strengths: addresses important controls of soil C decay

comments.issue: The positive C input-Δ14C relationship is attributed to priming, but it could reflect recent C incorporation if soil C is increasing.
comments.request: Provide stronger justification or avoid a definitive priming attribution.
comments.quote: the relationship between C input and delta 14C does not equate to the priming effect, it would simply reflect the prevalence of the recently incorporated C in the soil

comments.issue: The writing has awkward sentence structures, redundancy and grammatical mistakes.

comments.quote: the sentence structure is often awkward, messages in the sentences are often redundant, and there are some grammatical mistakes

comments.issue: The significance of the Δ14C-SOC stock association is not shown in Fig. 1.
comments.request: Add the correlation coefficient and significance to the legend.
comments.quote: Please include the correlation coefficient and its significance in the figure legend.

comments.issue: Fig. 2 may be redundant with Fig. 3.
comments.request: Justify or merge the figure.
comments.quote: Does this figure convey any important messages that are not conveyed in figure 3?

comments.issue: The sample size may be too small for partial correlations among 23 predictors.
comments.request: Assess statistical power for this analysis.
comments.quote: I am wondering if the sample size was large enough to explore the partial correlations among 23 predictors?

comments.issue: The ISRaD sample size is lower than in Shi et al. 2020 without explanation.
comments.request: Explain any exclusions of samples.
comments.quote: Sample size for the ISRad database seems much lower than the one used in Shi et al.’s analysis

comments.issue: Multiple line-level wording and shortening edits (L42, L46, L55, L58, L59, L61-69).
comments.quote: L61-65: these two sentences seem to convey the same message, so I suggest shortening and merging them.

comments.issue: The L48-51 model implication ignores that many ESMs already simulate multiple soil depths.
comments.request: Explain insights for model parameterization or benchmarking.
comments.quote: Can this study provide any insights for model parameterization or benchmarking?

comments.issue: Climatic effects are mediated by microbes and are not purely abiotic.

comments.issue: The text at L101-105 belongs in the Methods.
comments.request: Move this text to the Methods.
comments.quote: I think this text is better suited for the Methods section

comments.issue: How the averages at L174 were standardized is not explained.

comments.issue: The spatial resolution of the MODIS NPP data is not reported.

comments.quote: What was the spatial resolution of the MODIS-derived NPP?

comments.issue: Topsoil NPP may be overestimated because litter C is partly mineralized.

comments.quote: The NPP for 0-10 cm may be overestimated, because a portion of litter C will be mineralized.

comments.issue: The BNPP equation may produce negative values.

comments.issue: The incubation experiment cannot link the in situ C input-Δ14C relationship as it ignores background fresh C input.
comments.request: Address this limitation, e.g. with labelled background litter.
comments.quote: I do not this this experiment can link the in situ relationship between C input and dC14, because it ignores the background fresh C input

comments.issue: The t-test at L252 is never followed up and sample size is missing.
comments.request: Report the test result and sample size.
comments.quote: There was no follow-up on this t-test in the results. Were the dC14 significantly different between the two soil layers?

comments.issue: The normality test is not described.
comments.request: Describe how normality was tested.
comments.quote: How did you test the normality of the distributions?

comments.issue: The PC1 factor loadings are not reported.
comments.request: Include the PC1 linear combination in the supplement.
comments.quote: Could you include the linear combination of the factors in PC1 in the supplementary info?

comments.issue: The correlation at L313 lacks a coefficient and significance.
comments.request: Include the correlation coefficient and significance.
comments.quote: please include a correlation coefficient and its significance

title: Soil carbon persistence governed by plant input and mineral protection at regional and global scales

study.system: native understory perennials and Alliaria petiolata invader; 14-year field experiment

editor_summary: Editor reports three essentially very positive reviews on a timely, broadly interesting study, but extensive and substantial comments require a major revision.

reviews.assessment: Convinced of the study's importance and writing quality, but results need better presentation and rebalanced sections.
strengths: interesting for plant ecophysiology and invasion scientists

comments.issue: Results lack units, a GLM table, log-transformation notes, and Fig. 6 trend line rationale.
comments.request: Add units, analysis table, caption details and remove the unjustified trend line.
comments.quote: There is no unit to present the variables measured

comments.issue: Choice of main results should be reconsidered; Fig. 2 seems unnecessary.
comments.request: Promote Figures S1-S2 and fitness results; drop Figure 2.
comments.quote: To my opinion, figure 2 is not necessary (it can be fully written in the text)

comments.issue: Optimisation modelling of relative growth rate could anchor the plasticity idea.
comments.request: Explore this modelling approach further.
comments.quote: This is something that could be further explored here to better anchor the idea of the species plasticity required to maintain a given carbon return and a given fitness at the whole plant level.

comments.issue: The Narea increase should be linked to chlorophyll content to support least-cost theory.

comments.issue: Sections are unbalanced: introduction and methods too long, results and discussion too short.

comments.issue: Implications of the limited SLA response are unclear.

comments.issue: Moisture should be called water to match other resources.

comments.issue: Average climatic data and soil type for the site are missing.

comments.issue: The 36 subplots are mentioned but appear unused; their role is unclear.

comments.quote: The 36 subplots is confusing. This is reported here but seems never used in the experiment or in the analyses.

comments.issue: Soil pH and moisture should be measured, not extracted.
comments.request: Replace extract with measure.
comments.quote: It does not make sense to extract soil pH and moisture to me. Please use measure instead of extract.

comments.issue: The light level of 800 umol m-2 s-1 may not be saturating for understory plants.
comments.request: Explain the light level in the understory context.
comments.quote: 800 umol m-2 s-1 seems not very saturating level. Please better explain with the understory context.

comments.issue: How stomatal conductance was measured is not stated.
comments.request: Describe the gs measurement.
comments.quote: How was measured the gs values presented?

comments.issue: The PNUE formula is wrong or badly presented.
comments.request: Correct or clarify the PNUE formula.
comments.quote: The formula of PNUE is either wrong or badly presented. Please modify to make it clear.

comments.issue: Text cites hyphal length of AM fungi but it is absent from Fig. 3.
comments.request: Add the missing data or fix the citation.
comments.quote: There is no hyphal length of AM fungi in Fig. 3.

comments.issue: Bulk and mineral are used inconsistently between figure and text.
comments.request: Use mineral throughout.
comments.quote: Please replace bulk with mineral to have a consistent terminology between the figure and the text.

comments.issue: The leaf respiration to nitrogen ratio would link plasticity to nitrogen cost.
comments.request: Present this ratio if possible.
comments.quote: it would be useful to present if possible the ratio between leaf respiration and nitrogen content

comments.issue: Figure 6 presentation is not conclusive about treatment differences.

comments.quote: I find the presentation of the figure not very conclusive to show the differences between weeded and ambient treatment. I would rather recommend going with box plots.

reviews.assessment: Creative and novel, but references and hypothesis framing need work and the provisioning claim is stronger than the data.

comments.issue: References are misused or missing in the introduction and discussion.

comments.issue: The common invasion-driven increase in soil resources is not integrated into the prediction.

comments.issue: The claim of only two hypotheses is phrased poorly or inaccurate.

comments.quote: you can think through other hypotheses that might drive such impacts, and then include these.

comments.issue: Data may not support the provisioning disruption claim as strongly as communicated; only one species fits.
comments.request: Present results less definitively and discuss all three species carefully.

comments.issue: The fundamental assertion rests on correlation and should be recognized as such.

reviews.assessment: Very good paper overall, but the plot design is confusing and the results are suggestive rather than decisive.

comments.issue: Experimental plot design description is confusing and hard to follow.

comments.issue: Results are suggestive not decisive and population consequences remain unclear.

comments.quote: the authors need to acknowledge that while they documented some soil and plant changes due to the presence of A. petiolata, other changes were not found, and that the changes that were found were mostly modest

title: Invasion‐induced root–fungal disruptions alter plant water and nitrogen economies

comments.issue: Conclusion that invasion triggers short-term benefits is not supported by Figure 1.

comments.issue: Effect sizes are difficult to discern; percentage changes should be reported.

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits (line 231 grammar, line 319 typo).

comments.request: Acknowledge possible effects on other insects and survey them.
