comments.quote: it may be noted that I recently had a discussion with chemical-analytical colleagues who specified that aromatic acids are not phenolics

comments.issue: Compound concentrations were matched by mass rather than molarity, so diets differ in the number of active molecules and synergy cannot be assessed fairly.
comments.request: Consider molarity when preparing diets and reassess comparisons.
comments.quote: the authors did not consider the molarity of the different compounds when doing the calculations for the diet, but rather went for the concentration

title: Interaction diversity explains the maintenance of phytochemical diversity

study.system: ectomycorrhizal Pinus sylvestris; field and greenhouse experiments plus model

editor_summary: Referees disagree: R1 likes the data but flags alternative explanations; R2 and R3 find missing measurements, methods and design details. Editor invites resubmission if concerns and suggested additional measurements are addressed.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, novel study of host carbon allocation and fungal nitrogen supply, but carbon exports were not measured and key methods are missing.
strengths: novel ecological insights into host C allocation and fungal N supply

comments.issue: C exports to fungi and networks were not measured; indirect pot respiration estimates lack methods and results.
comments.request: Report the pot respiration analysis methods and results.
comments.quote: I cannot find information on how these analyses were conducted and the results from these measurements.

comments.issue: The model's assumption that C supply is reduced proportionally to the strangled fraction is not supported.
comments.request: Justify or validate the proportional C-supply assumption.
comments.quote: In the model, it is assumed that the C supply to the fungi is reduced in proportion to the strangled fractions, but the support for this assumption cannot be evaluated.

comments.issue: Experimental section lacks soil N content, 15N tracer addition, KNO3 rationale and isotope analysis details.
comments.request: Add the missing experimental and isotope-analysis details.
comments.quote: more detailed information must be given on the pot and field experiments. I lack information on the N content of the soils, how the 15N tracer was added

reviews.assessment: Strong complementary lab and field experiments plus a model, but interpretations, especially of the lab experiment, need more care.
strengths: important new information on C and N movement in EM plants

comments.issue: Shading and strangling effects may reflect normal conifer physiology, not fungal mediation; no non-mycorrhizal control.
comments.request: Cite non-mycorrhizal studies and acknowledge non-fungal physiological responses.
comments.quote: Because there was no NM control, studies about the effect of shading and strangling on the distribution of C and N in NM seedlings should be cited

comments.issue: Model assumes N delivery depends on relative C supply, so it cannot independently test the C-N relationship.
comments.request: Explain how the model can test a relationship it assumes.
comments.quote: How can the model evaluate the C-N relationship when a dependence of N on C supply is a built-in assumption of the model?

comments.issue: Assumed C-N dependency is contradicted by AM-system and other studies; choice needs justification.
comments.request: Justify the assumed C-N dependency in light of conflicting evidence.
comments.quote: So, there is evidence for both and against a strong C-N dependency. What is the justification for choosing the assumption used here?

comments.issue: Significance of the one-tree-strangled result in Fig 5 lacks statistical support.
comments.request: Provide F, df and P values for the Fig 5 comparison.
comments.quote: The figure caption states that this difference was significant, but the statistical support for this statement must be provided.

comments.issue: The non-significant difference between strangled and non-strangled trees when more than one tree was strangled is ignored.
comments.request: Discuss how this result fits the overall interpretation.
comments.quote: is not acknowledged in the remainder of the paragraph. How does this result fit with the interpretation of the results overall?

comments.issue: The phrase 'in exchange for' implies a direct membrane link that is under investigation.
comments.request: Use less charged language in the abstract.
comments.quote: why "in exchange for"? No direct link exists at the membrane level. Given that this relationship is the subject of investigation in this paper, could less charged language be used?

comments.issue: Abstract does not name the tree species or mycorrhizal type.
comments.request: State species and mycorrhiza type in the abstract.
comments.quote: so that the abstract is more informative in isolation, the name of the tree species and the type of mycorrhiza should be stated.

comments.issue: Seedling growth conditions during the first two years are not described.
comments.request: Describe how seedlings were grown during the first two years.
comments.quote: please include how the seedlings had been grown over the first two years.

comments.issue: Whether the 10:90 mix ratio is by weight or volume is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the basis of the 10:90 ratio.
comments.quote: Line 131 – 10:90 by weight or volume? Line 132 – please provide a few more details about the commercial mix

comments.issue: Commercial potting mix composition and sterility are not described.
comments.request: Describe the potting mix, including brand and sterility.
comments.quote: please provide a few more details about the commercial mix, including brand. Was it compost-based? Peat-based? Soil-based? Sterile or non-sterile?

comments.issue: Greenhouse irradiance, temperature and fertilization are not reported.
comments.request: Report greenhouse conditions and whether seedlings were fertilized.
comments.quote: state conditions in the greenhouse in terms of irradiance and temperature. Were the seedlings fertilized over the 53 days?

comments.issue: The latitude of the field site is missing.
comments.request: Give the latitude of the field site.
comments.quote: Line 141 – latitude? Line 144 – how long had the experimental treatments been imposed before transfer back into the greenhouse?

comments.issue: Timing of treatments before transfer to the greenhouse is unclear; a timeline is needed.
comments.request: Provide a timeline of the lab experiment.
comments.quote: how long had the experimental treatments been imposed before transfer back into the greenhouse?

comments.issue: Lines 309-310 and 317-318 seem to show the opposite relationship to the model's assumption.
comments.request: Explain this apparent contradiction with the model.
comments.quote: L309-310 and 317-318 – isn't this the opposite relationship to that assumed in the model?

comments.issue: Fig 5 caption does not define what the control treatment is.
comments.request: State what 'control' refers to in the Fig 5 caption.
comments.quote: So that the figure makes sense in isolation, in the figure caption, please state what the 'control' refers to.

reviews.assessment: Elegant idea and valuable field manipulations, but data and design cannot rigorously test the proposed trade dynamics.
strengths: potential to be exciting and novel

comments.issue: No direct measurement of C allocation to fungi or fungal biomass, only model estimates.
comments.request: Measure root colonization and fungal biomass in pots and field.
comments.quote: However, there appear to be no measurements of fungal biomass – only estimates via model parameters. Determining fungal root colonization and biomass seems essential

comments.issue: Introduction does not clearly present the hypotheses or the data used to test them.
comments.request: Rewrite the introduction to state hypotheses and data clearly.
comments.quote: the introduction needs to be re-worked to make clear the hypotheses being tested, and what type of data are being gathered to test those ideas.

comments.issue: Unclear whether arbuscular or ectomycorrhizae are meant; type affects exchange patterns.
comments.request: State the mycorrhizal type clearly from the start.
comments.quote: it is not clear if the authors are referencing arbuscular mycorrhizae or ectomycorrhizae (or both). To use the vague term in association with "trees" is difficult

comments.issue: Why trees cannot 'buy their way out' is unexplained; the phrase needs definition.
comments.request: Define what 'buying its way out' means.
comments.quote: Line 71-73 are the crux of the argument, but its not well explained why the trees cant "buy its way out". Can this "buy out" be better defined?

comments.issue: Line 75 lacks a reference and the multiple-partner issue is not set up.
comments.request: Add a reference and set up the multiple-partner issue.
comments.quote: Line 75 needs a reference. If the authors are talking about tragedy of the commons, they need to better set up the multiple partner issue.

comments.issue: Framing the two hypotheses as 'alternate' is inappropriate; self-demand comes first.
comments.request: Do not present the hypotheses as mutually exclusive alternatives.
comments.quote: why is this considered an "alternate" model? It is safe to assume that an organism in symbiosis will always first use resources to satisfy its own demand

comments.issue: Predictions of the strangling manipulation are not stated.
comments.request: State the expected outcome of the strangling treatment.
comments.quote: the experiments are briefly outlined, but not the hypotheses: what is the prediction of the experimental manipulation of strangling? what is expectation?

comments.issue: Basic experimental design and expected treatment effects are never explained or justified.
comments.request: Lay out and justify the full experimental design upfront.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if the authors laid out the basic experimental design as the first part of the methods, so the reader knows what to expect.

comments.issue: Pre-existing root fungi were not excluded or characterized, weakening design power.
comments.request: Quantify extra fungal symbionts or acknowledge the limitation.
comments.quote: I am concerned that the authors did not exclude fungal species already present on the root. I appreciate this is hard to do, but it makes the experimental design less powerful.

comments.issue: No evidence that the strangling treatment works on seedlings.
comments.request: Confirm that strangling effectively reduces C supply.
comments.quote: What is the evidence that the strangling treatment works on seedlings – is there a way to confirm?

comments.issue: Cannot distinguish 15N in root tissue from N in symbiotic fungal tissue.
comments.request: Clarify or validate separation of root and fungal N.
comments.quote: For the 15N measurements, how can the authors be sure the N is in the root versus the fungal tissue in symbiosis with the root.

comments.issue: Field tree spatial structure could matter; space was not used as a covariate.
comments.request: Use tree spatial position as a covariate if maps exist.
comments.quote: The spatial structuring of the trees in the field experiment could be important. Were maps taken so that space among trees could be used as a covariate?

comments.issue: The proportional C-reduction assumption remains untested.
comments.request: Test whether C supply scales with strangled fraction.
comments.quote: Is there a way to test the assumption that C supply to fungi is reduced in proportion to the fraction of seedlings that were strangled?

comments.issue: Fungal partners are uncharacterized yet assumed attached to all plants.
comments.request: Characterize fungal biomass, e.g. via qPCR.
comments.quote: the authors assume that the fungi are attached to all plants – but what is "the fungi". This hasn't been characterized at all

comments.issue: Claim that C allocation fuels N immobilization is unsupported; allocation never measured directly.
comments.request: Temper the claim or measure allocation directly.
comments.quote: I would disagree that the authors show that "C allocation to mycorrhizal fungi can fuel N immobilization" – there are some data to support this idea, but allocation was never directly measured.

title: The mycorrhizal tragedy of the commons

study.system: butterfly phenology distribution data; response to a data-management critique

reviews.assessment: Finds the criticisms largely valid and both the original and reanalysis statistically unconvincing, but notes the reanalysis contains its own errors.

comments.issue: The statistical defence is weak and the original approach was not robust.
comments.request: Acknowledge the weakness and provide a robust reanalysis.
comments.quote: the authors’ statistical defence of their original analyses was rather weak

comments.issue: The Larsen and Shirey reanalysis contains errors that actually support the original results, contrary to their conclusions.
comments.request: Have Larsen and Shirey confirm this point.
comments.quote: it appears that they in turn introduced error into their analyses such that the original results published by Fric et al. (2020) are supported in their reanalysis, contrary to their stated conclusions.

comments.issue: No strong confidence in either analysis; the suggested Bayesian hierarchical reanalysis was not followed.
comments.request: Reanalyse within a Bayesian hierarchical framework.
comments.quote: This suggestion was not followed, and I therefore do not have strong confidence in either the original analysis by Fric et al. or the reanalysis by Larsen and Shirey.

comments.issue: Using a single record to represent both onset and termination is indefensible.
comments.request: Exclude these records from the analyses.
comments.quote: The use of a single record to represent both onset and termination does not seem defensible. These data should be excluded from the analyses.

comments.issue: Small sample sizes inflate Type I errors; partial pooling by species would resolve this.
comments.request: Fit a Bayesian or mixed-effects model grouping by species with partial pooling.
comments.quote: This issue could be simply resolved by fitting a Bayesian or mixed-effects model grouping by species and allowing partial pooling.

comments.issue: Important predictors omitted from single-term models can still mislead inference.
comments.request: Include all relevant predictors in a full model.
comments.quote: Fric et al. also argue that intercorrelated predictors are not a problem in single-term regression, but important predictors not included in single-term models can still mislead inference. These predictors should be included in a full model.

comments.issue: Seventeen species were mistakenly included in the original analysis.
comments.request: Exclude the 17 mistakenly included species.
comments.quote: Fric et al. mistakenly included 17 species in their original analysis. These species should be excluded.

comments.issue: About 10,000 GBIF records with impossible locations (below sea level, offshore) should not be retained.
comments.request: Exclude records with known location errors.
comments.quote: we will inevitably include some erroneous records, but this does not mean we should include data with known errors.

reviews.assessment: Wants a more direct, detailed rebuttal and flags unclear wording and an unsupported claim about information loss.
strengths: authors presented the reasons for their errors and problems in the LS paper

comments.issue: The rebuttal should be more direct and detailed.
comments.request: Refute the criticisms more directly and in detail.
comments.quote: However, I suggest Fric et al. refute more directly and in details.

comments.issue: The sentence about congruent results at page 4, lines 25-26 is not clear.
comments.request: Make clear that the two results are congruent with each other.
comments.quote: You should make it clear that two results are congruent with each other, although you did refer to Supplement S1.

comments.issue: The explanation about low data-point numbers in single-species regressions is strained and rests on common sense.
comments.request: Provide a stronger statistical justification for this point.
comments.quote: the reason was also very strained. The viewpoints related to statistical criteria were just a viewpoint of common sense.

comments.issue: The species-selection problem raised by Larsen and Shirey is not solved.
comments.request: Explain how the species-selection problem was resolved.
comments.quote: How to solve the problem 3 LS put forward about the selection of species?

comments.issue: The claim that stringent data handling may cause critical information loss is not supported by sound data.
comments.request: Demonstrate the information-loss effect with sound data.
comments.quote: Maybe it is a scale problem, but you did now show the effects of this by sound data.

comments.issue: The reference format at the beginning of the main text is not formal.
comments.request: Use a formal reference format at the start.
comments.quote: the reference format was not so formal.

title: Radical pruning of distribution data may result in loss of knowledge (Response to Larsen & Shirey)

study.system: flowering plant families; traits, threat and naturalisation

reviews.assessment: Praises the clear, robust results and well-explained models, asking why data-deficient species were treated as not threatened and to justify the 80% credible interval.

comments.issue: IUCN data-deficient species were classified as not threatened, which may bias the results.
comments.request: Explain the reason and rerun analyses excluding data-deficient families.
comments.quote: Why species labeled as "data deficient" by the IUCN were classified as "not threatened".

comments.issue: The 80% credible interval is an unusual threshold and is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the choice of an 80% credible interval.
comments.quote: Why 80% credible interval was used? I know that 95% is a frequentist arbitrary convention but many readers will find 80% a strange threshold too. Please, justify your choice.

comments.issue: The explanation based on different processes for young and old clades is not statistically tested.
comments.request: Statistically test the explanation for the low phylogenetic signature.
comments.quote: I wonder whether you could statistically test such an explanation.

reviews.assessment: No methodological flaws, but the motivation, scientific importance and macroevolutionary justification are unclear, including the use of family-level summaries.
strengths: no flaw seen in the methods

comments.issue: There is no clear reason to expect opposing trait and macroevolutionary relationships for threat versus naturalisation, nor a case for broad importance.
comments.request: Justify the expectation of opposing relationships and the question's scientific importance.
comments.quote: There is no clear indication to why should expect that proportion of threaten and naturalized species should show opposing relation with traits and macroevolutionary related variables.

comments.issue: Whether family-level summaries are adequate cannot be judged because the goals are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the study goals so the family-level unit can be assessed.
comments.quote: is hard for me to assess if the use of family-level summaries is adequate since I don’t know your goals beyond the questions you post at the end of the intro.

comments.issue: The justification for including macroevolutionary variables and the expected directions of their effects is fuzzy.
comments.request: State why and in which direction diversification and phylogenetic effects should affect threat and naturalisation.
comments.quote: the justification to why these matter as a factor determining the patterns of threat and naturalization, and how the variables used to test this idea are relevant is, “fuzzy”, to say the least.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the dataset and surprising results, but finds the writing confusing and questions the phylogeny, diversification model and priors used.

comments.issue: The writing is confusing, and the methods lack background on dataset choice and why these analyses were used.
comments.request: Rewrite for clarity and explain the rationale for datasets and analyses.
comments.quote: I found the writing confusing, especially for the Material and Methods section. The authors do not provide enough background on their choice of dataset or why they used a particular suite of analyses.

comments.issue: Terms are loosely defined and inconsistent, including family-level versus family-specific effects, standard deviation versus variance, asexual reproduction, autogamy and the meaning of 0.5.
comments.request: Define terms consistently and clarify the 0.5 polymorphism coding.
comments.quote: terms are loosely defined, for example, different names are given to the same factor or variable

comments.issue: Figure captions are deficient and the table at the end lacks a legend.
comments.request: Improve figure captions and add a legend for the table.
comments.quote: Figure captions are also deficient (What is SD in Fig. 2?) and there is no legend for the table at the end of the manuscript, so I did not understand its actual meaning.

comments.issue: The Zanne et al. 2014 phylogeny is outdated and pruning to one species per family loses its taxon completeness.
comments.request: Rely on the Magallón (2020) dated angiosperm timetree.
comments.quote: The dated phylogeny of angiosperms used for estimating the effects of age and diversification rates analysis is quite old (Zanne et al. 2014).

comments.issue: A single-sigma Brownian model is used to estimate diversification variation instead of branch-specific rate models.
comments.request: Use branch-specific diversification rate models such as BAMM or BRD.
comments.quote: why do not use a branch-specific diversification rate model to estimate diversification rates per family?

comments.issue: Excluding the extinction parameter from the diversification estimator is not tested for sensitivity.
comments.request: Compare diversification estimates with and without the extinction parameter.
comments.quote: I think a sensitive analysis comparing estimates with and without the extinction parameter is needed here

comments.issue: No rationale is given for using stem ages rather than crown ages.
comments.request: Explain the choice of stem ages over crown ages.
comments.quote: Also, I missed a rationale on why they used stem-ages rather than crown-ages, since results could be quite different.

comments.issue: Uniform or normal priors are used for regression coefficients instead of a conjugate beta prior.
comments.request: Justify the prior choice or use a beta prior.
comments.quote: I found strange the authors used uniform priors (or normal, 0,1) for the regression coefficients.

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 3 show linear credibility intervals rather than posterior densities.
comments.request: Show parameter estimate densities instead of linear intervals.
comments.quote: Also, why use linear ranges as credibility intervals around the mean in Figures 2 and 3?

title: Opposing macroevolutionary and trait‐mediated patterns of threat and naturalisation in flowering plants

study.system: temperate forest chronosequence; plant, soil and microbial responses to disturbance

editor_summary: Study breaks new ground with a substantial dataset and well-designed analysis; all three reviewers are generally positive but raise concerns that need addressing.

reviews.assessment: Novel multi-facet study of above- and belowground disturbance impacts using SEM, but several design and measurement concerns must be addressed before acceptance.
strengths: novel exploration of above- and belowground interactions
SEM differentiates direct and indirect impacts

comments.issue: The assumption that disturbed and undisturbed forests were identical before disturbance is unjustified.
comments.request: Justify the pre-disturbance similarity assumption.
comments.quote: The assumption of comparing these disturbed forests with un-disturbed forests was that forest ecosystems (forest and soil conditions) were identical prior to the disturbance. This has to be justified.

comments.issue: Only fire frequency is considered although fire intensity is often the dominant driver.
comments.request: Justify excluding fire intensity and frequency-interval effects.
comments.quote: In some cases, fire intensity is the dominant factor to the impacts of fire. In this study, only the fire frequency is considered, which needs justification.

comments.issue: Fuel load, slope, moisture and climatic factors driving spatial variation in fire impacts are not addressed.
comments.request: Elucidate these additional drivers of spatial variation.
comments.quote: impacts of fire on the ecosystem depend upon many factors, including fuel load, slope, moisture, climatic conditions (temperature and wind..), and all these will contribute to the spatial variation of fire impacts, which has to be elucidated in this study.

comments.issue: The differential impacts on surface soil and subsoil are not explained in the Discussion.
comments.request: Explain the depth-specific differences.
comments.quote: Fire frequency, logging and post-fire logging showed differential impacts on surface soil (0-10cm) and subsoil (20-30cm), which was not clearly explained in the Discussion.

comments.issue: Climate change and fire intensity are discussed in the introduction but not studied.
comments.request: Align the introduction with what was actually measured.
comments.quote: Lines 60-63, climatic change, human disturbance and wildfire compounding impacts were discussed, however, in this study, climatic impacts and fire intensity were not studied.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a paragraph on logging and post-fire logging despite logging being a key driver.
comments.request: Add a paragraph on logging impacts.
comments.quote: Line 76, it was suggested to add one paragraph on the impacts of logging and post-fire logging on forest ecosystems since logging is the key driver in this study.

comments.issue: Percentage cover is used instead of biomass for aboveground abundance.
comments.request: Justify using percentage cover rather than biomass.
comments.quote: Line 92, why did you measure the abundance (percentage cover) of the above-ground parts instead of biomass?

comments.issue: Microbial biomass was not measured.
comments.request: Explain why microbial biomass was not measured.
comments.quote: Line 93, why did you not measure microbial biomass?

comments.issue: Available nutrient pools may be poorer long-term indicators than total pools.
comments.request: Justify or use total nutrient pools.
comments.quote: this study aimed to look into the long-term impacts, and so soil total nutrient pools (total P, total K) are better indicators of the change than the available pools

comments.issue: The choice of 0-10 cm and 20-30 cm depths is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the depth selection.
comments.quote: Lines 96-97, please explain why the depths of 0-10cm and 20-30cm were selected.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether pH(H2O) or pH(CaCl2) was used.
comments.request: Clarify which pH measurement was used.
comments.quote: Line 96, please check if pH (H2) or pH (CaCl2) was used since both were measured in Method section.

comments.issue: The P result appears to contradict published findings on frequent fire and available P.
comments.request: Discuss this discrepancy with the literature.
comments.quote: Line 155, In the literature, many studies showed that frequent fire increased available P in surface soil unless there was a rainfall event immediately after fire.

comments.issue: The clearcut logging treatment also included re-seeding and should be labelled accordingly.
comments.request: Indicate re-seeding in the treatment label.
comments.quote: Lines 469-470, ‘clearcut logging’ treatment actually included both ‘logging’ and ‘re-seeding’, and therefore, it may be good idea to indicate ‘re-seeding’ in the ‘treatment’

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the same species were re-seeded after salvage logging.
comments.request: Clarify the re-seeding species.
comments.quote: Lines 473-476, re-seeded with the same species after salvage logging?

reviews.assessment: Novel and complex study with a huge sampling effort, well-designed display items; recommends publication after moderate revision of text, figures and site description.
strengths: huge data collection effort, especially belowground

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 3 contain the same information except significance levels.
comments.request: Merge Figures 2 and 3.
comments.quote: The display items are very well designed, while I wonder if Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 can be merged

comments.issue: Figure 4 would be easier to understand summarised in the format of Figure 1.
comments.request: Add a summary figure in the style of Figure 1.
comments.quote: if Fig. 4 can be summarized in an additional figure following the conceptual Fig. 1

comments.issue: The introduction contains too many subclauses and is hard to read.
comments.request: Simplify the sentence structures.
comments.quote: The text contains a lot of subclauses, making the introduction a bit more complicated to read than necessary.

comments.issue: A clean objectives statement and working hypotheses are missing.
comments.request: Add objectives and hypotheses before the methods.
comments.quote: Further, I think it would be helpful to add a clean objectives statement, maybe also working hypotheses, before describing materials and methods.

comments.issue: Increasing fire frequency is described as changing the disturbance regime rather than being part of the altered regime.
comments.request: Correct the disturbance-regime wording.
comments.quote: l. 60 The increase in frequency does not change the disturbance regime, but is part of the altered disturbance regime

comments.issue: The sentence at l.67-69 is cumbersome.
comments.request: Re-format the sentence.
comments.quote: l. 67-69 for instance, this reads a little cumbersome. Consider re-formatting the sentence

comments.issue: An example would help at l.69-71.
comments.request: Add an example.
comments.quote: l. 69-71 an example would be helpful here

comments.issue: Chao1 is used before being explained.
comments.request: Explain Chao1 at first use.
comments.quote: l. 94 Chao1 has not been explained, yet

comments.issue: The line between soil microbes and plants in Figure 1a may need to be an arrow.
comments.request: Check and correct the Figure 1a path.
comments.quote: Fig. 1a Shouldn’t the line between soil microbes and plan be an arrow?

comments.issue: Fungi are excluded from “forest microbes” in Figure 1 but included in Figure 4.
comments.request: Make the wording consistent across figures and text.
comments.quote: Based on Fig. 1, fungi are not part of forest microbes, but they are in Fig. 4 and are included in the plant-soil-microbial feedback. The authors should be consistent with the wording

comments.issue: Several sentences in the results are complicated and read poorly (l.144-145, l.184-185).
comments.request: Simplify the sentence structures.
comments.quote: Overall well written and balanced. But also here avoid complicated sentence structures.

comments.issue: Several line-level edits (stray parentheses, negative coefficient note, carbon stock wording, comma, underlining).
comments.quote: l. 356 is carbon stock a better word here?

comments.issue: “The total number of disturbance impacts” is undefined and cannot be assessed in its entirety.
comments.request: Clarify that these are numbers of significant effects.
comments.quote: l. 148-149 Here and in the following, do you mean the number of significant disturbance effects on ecosystem properties? “The total number of disturbance impacts” can unlikely be assessed in its entirety and it is unclear what is affected.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether l.167 reports abundance or species share.
comments.request: Clarify the metric for plants and trees.
comments.quote: l. 167 really abundance or rather species share (%)? Same for trees.

comments.issue: Eucalyptus and Acacia abundances may be strongly correlated with tree abundance affected in the opposite direction.
comments.request: Address this potential correlation.
comments.quote: Also abundance of Eucalyptus and Acacia species would likely be highly correlated with tree abundance which was affected in the opposite way as those species?

comments.issue: The site description is vague and some quantities are not given (l.456, l.527-528).
comments.request: Improve and quantify the site description.
comments.quote: The site description can be improved a bit.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether all or only some Mountain Ash forests got younger and more fire-prone.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of this statement.
comments.quote: l. 464-469 unclear if all or just some Mountain Ash forests got younger and more fire-prone

comments.issue: The clearing description is logically inconsistent if remaining vegetation was burnt.
comments.request: Clarify the clearing and burning sequence.
comments.quote: l. 470-473 If something remains after clearing and is burnt, not all vegetation can have been cleared right?

comments.issue: “From the initial wildfire” is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify whether “following wildfire” is meant.
comments.quote: l. 476 from the initial wildfire = following wildfire?

comments.issue: The sentence at l.488-489 does not belong in this section.
comments.request: Move or remove the sentence.
comments.quote: l. 488-489 doesn’t fit here as this isn’t about the analysis

comments.issue: The site description should come before the study design.
comments.request: Reorder the methods sections.
comments.quote: l. 490-501 I would expect the site description before the study design

comments.issue: The percentage of unassigned OTUs is not reported.
comments.request: Report the percentage of unassigned OTUs.
comments.quote: l. 519-520 Do you know the percentage of unassigned OTUs?

comments.issue: A reference is needed for the statement at l.550-552.
comments.request: Provide a reference or point to the supplement.
comments.quote: l. 550 – 552 Can you provide a reference here? Alternatively, you could refer to the supplement.

comments.issue: The scaling procedure is not specified.
comments.request: Specify how scaling was done.
comments.quote: l. 601 Scaling is not one universal method. Better be specific here how scaling was done.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting fieldwork, but terminology is inconsistent and logging effects are confounded with fire, simplifying the message about disturbance impacts.

comments.issue: “Indirect” and “cascading” are used synonymously and inconsistently.
comments.request: Use only one term.
comments.quote: the terms "indirect" and "cascading" are used synonymously. Sometimes both are mentioned, sometimes only one of them. I suggest to use only one term

comments.issue: Logged and salvage-logged plots also burned, so logging effects are always additional to fire but labelled as logging effects.
comments.request: Address the confounding of logging with fire.
comments.quote: I find it very strange that the analysis is based on the comparison of burned, logged and salvage logged plots but that also the latter two involve fire effects.

comments.issue: Two line-level wording fixes (L33 tense; L158 garbled sentence).
comments.quote: L158: sth wrong in "a reduced the abundance of trees"

comments.issue: No explanation is given for why human disturbances have more negative effects.
comments.request: Add a sentence explaining this result.
comments.quote: L45-47: would be good to provide one more sentence explaining why human disturbances have more negative effects.

comments.issue: Climate change is mentioned in a misleading way, as if it were a studied impact.
comments.request: Revise the climate-change statements.
comments.quote: L60: I think here and elsewhere the way you mention climate change is sometimes misleading: as if climate change was a specific impact you studied

comments.issue: The novelty of the research is not made clear (L67ff, L269).
comments.request: Specify the novelty with an example.
comments.quote: L67ff: I find this very theoretical and general: could you be a bit more specific, making clear what is new about your research with an example or so?

comments.issue: The expected difference between salvage and conventional logging is not framed with hypotheses.
comments.request: Add hypotheses or conceptual framing.
comments.quote: L99-100: Could you formulate hypotheses or some conceptual framing why you expect a difference between salvage and conventional logging

comments.issue: The difference between Figure 1a and 1b is confusing despite the caption.
comments.request: Clarify the figure panels.
comments.quote: L132: I only got the difference between figure 1a and b after several times reading the captain and text.

comments.issue: The L148 formulation implies many disturbances.
comments.request: Delete “disturbance” as suggested.
comments.quote: L148: This formulation is weird, as if there are many disturbances. I think maybe deleting the "disturbance" would help.

comments.issue: Counts of significant effects are not given relative to the number tested.
comments.request: Report significant counts out of tested.
comments.quote: L172: you could mention that these are "xxx significant (out of yyy tested) relative direct

comments.issue: The text should state that direct impacts match Figure 2.
comments.request: Add this cross-reference.
comments.quote: L226: I would mention with a sentence here that the direct impacts are the same as in figure 2

comments.issue: The 65 impacts from the abstract and discussion are not clearly linked to the figures and net impacts.
comments.request: Show net impacts and refer to the 65 impacts in the results.
comments.quote: Here finally the figures show the 65 impacts you mention in the abstract and discussion. Before I had understood that the direct impacts are the net impacts but here they seem separated again?

comments.issue: “Top-down” and “bottom-up” are used only in a directional sense.
comments.request: Use different words or justify this usage.
comments.quote: L261-262: I wonder if "top-down" and "bottom-up" are the right words here since you simply use them in the "directional" sense "from above vs. from below"

comments.issue: The discussion covers fire but not why logging and salvage logging have strong effects.
comments.request: Discuss the strong logging effects.
comments.quote: L272: the entire discussion that follows is about fire but not really why logging and salvage logging have such strong effects.

comments.issue: The disturbance interaction is not analysed although salvage logging interacts with fire in the design.
comments.request: Analyse the interaction between the disturbances.
comments.quote: L326: I find it misleading that you do not analyse the interaction of the disturbances given that salvage logging interacts with fire in your study design.

comments.issue: Management implications should separate intentional logging from fire.
comments.request: Separate fire from logging and salvage logging in the discussion.
comments.quote: L342ff: for the section on management implications, I think it would make more sense to separate the discussion of fire from logging and salvage logging since the latter is happening on purpose while the former is not.

comments.issue: The purpose of the sentence at L358 is unclear.
comments.request: Remove or justify the sentence.
comments.quote: L358: it is unclear why this sentence is needed here

comments.issue: The expectation that anthropogenic disturbances will increase is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the basis for this prediction.
comments.quote: L366: why do you expect anthropogenic disturbances to increase? because of increased salvage logging?

comments.issue: Mountain Ash is not identified as Eucalyptus regnans.
comments.request: Add the species synonym.
comments.quote: L460: I think you should clarify that mountain ash is synonymous with eucalyptus regnans as not every reader might know that.

comments.issue: The difference between salvage-logged and logged plots is unclear if both burned.
comments.request: Clarify the treatment difference.
comments.quote: L471: So what is the difference between salvage logged plots and logged plots if both have been burned?

title: Direct and indirect disturbance impacts in forests

study.system: bacteria and archaea traits compared with vascular plants

reviews.assessment: Interesting, timely synthesis; main concern is that Figure 4 and the final synthesis do not integrate the candidate traits fully.
strengths: nicely illustrated with boxes and supplementary material

comments.issue: Figure 4 does not use the shortlisted traits and its three-dimensional presentation lacks rationale; a global pattern integrating candidate traits is expected.
comments.request: Integrate the candidate traits into a synthetic figure placed in the conceptual strategy context.
comments.quote: In view of the substantial structuring work presented in the manuscript, I found Figure 4 a little frustrating, as it shows some of the traits evoked in the study

comments.issue: The metabolic categories in Figure 4 overlap (denitrification and sulfate reduction are heterotrophic).
comments.request: Present metabolic types in a more comprehensive, non-overlapping way.
comments.quote: Also, the right part of figure 4 is a bit frustrating – as it only lists the main metabolic types (but for instance, ‘heterotrophy’, ‘denitrification’ and ‘sulphate reduction’ are not distinct categories as denitrifying and sulfate-reducing bacteria are heterotrophs).

comments.issue: The bibliography needs editing: incomplete references, inconsistent capitalization, and near-duplicate Madin et al. 2020a/b entries.
comments.quote: Complete ref Basan et al. 2020, Steen et al. (2019), Wood et al. (2018)

reviews.assessment: Interesting and welcome, but the plant-bacteria comparison, strategy links and originality relative to companion papers need work.
strengths: welcome attempt to link plant trait literature to bacteria and archaea

comments.issue: The introduction lacks general principles explaining why trait covariations should be shared between plants and bacteria (also raised for L70).
comments.request: Add a road map or a priori hypotheses for shared trade-offs.
comments.quote: I would have expected in the introduction some general principles/theories that could explain why we should expect commonalities in trait covariations in plants and bacteria. Why should we compared them?

comments.issue: The links between the listed traits and ecological strategies are weak, and how trait combinations describe strategies is unclear.
comments.request: Strengthen the trait-to-strategy links.
comments.quote: The authors list a series of traits as candidate traits to describe general leading dimension for bacteria and archaea. However the links with ecological strategies were quite poor.

comments.issue: Originality relative to two companion papers under review is unclear because the papers look very similar.
comments.request: Clarify how this contribution differs from the companion studies.
comments.quote: Looking at it in more depth, the two papers look really similar to the present paper and it is not clear how original is this contribution compared to the two other companion studies that are currently under review?

comments.issue: Figure 4 is not readable or informative.
comments.request: Redesign Figure 4 for clarity.
comments.quote: Some figures were not very informative. For instance I don’t know how to read figure 4.

comments.issue: It is unclear how concepts such as copiotrophy can be made quantitative.
comments.request: Explain how to operationalize such concepts.
comments.quote: But it is not clear whether they actually propose how to do so. For instance, how to build quantitative muscle into concept such a copiotrophy is not explained.

comments.issue: The Suding et al. 2003 road map for linking traits to response and abundance is not mentioned.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Suding et al. 2003.
comments.quote: This reminds me an excellent paper from the early 2000’s of Suding et al. (2003 in Ecology).

comments.issue: Whether plants respond to temperature itself or to frost and drought is unclear at L375.
comments.request: Clarify the temperature drivers.
comments.quote: Do plants respond to temperature itself or underlying drivers such as frost and drought? It is not clear here.

comments.issue: Competition is not the only driver of abundance and niche deviation; positive interactions and other processes are omitted.
comments.request: Acknowledge additional drivers at L380.
comments.quote: Competition is not by far the only driver of species abundance and deviation from fundamental niche. Many other processes including positive interactions are also important please acknowledge here.

comments.issue: Summarizing plant life as doing the same things at different magnitudes oversimplifies response versus effect traits and contrasting effects.
comments.request: Qualify the plant generalization at L450.
comments.quote: Plant do not do always the same things in different magnitudes? It depends if you talk about response or effect traits? Right?

comments.issue: Trophic interactions, such as nematodes feeding on bacteria, are not discussed as a dimension.
comments.request: Discuss trophic interactions as an additional dimension.
comments.quote: A dimension that is not clearly discuss in this paper is trophic interactions. Many organisms feeds on bacteria such as nematods. This might be quite important in term of ecology.

title: Trait dimensions in bacteria and archaea compared to vascular plants

study.system: mammals; body size-population density over 50 years

editor_summary: Editor finds the analysis exciting if results hold; both reviewers request refinements to ensure robustness and clearer text; editor also objects to the unreferenced 'immutable relationships' strawman and asks to clarify the equilibrium null expectation.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and polished analysis of broad interest; the statistical choices need confirmation and the bold claims stronger evidence.
strengths: top 5-10% paper in terms of polish

comments.issue: The analysis compares species across communities rather than species within one community, and the implications of this scale are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge the scale of application and its possible impacts.
comments.quote: this is a rather particular form of the relationship in that it is comparing usually only one species in a community with other species in other communities

comments.issue: What was done with the PCA on the phylogenetic distance matrix is not stated.
comments.request: State how the phylogenetic PCA was used in the regressions.
comments.quote: and after all this work to make PCA on phylogenetic distance matrix, what did you do with it?

comments.issue: Using species as a random effect may remove much of the effect under study.
comments.request: Provide a confirmatory analysis without the species random effect or with species means.
comments.quote: I find it a little worrisome that species was used as a random effect. It will effectively remove the mean from each species which could remove much of the effect under study.

comments.issue: Whether abundance was transformed, or a Poisson model used, is unclear.
comments.request: Report and justify the transformation or model family.
comments.quote: I missed whether any transformation (square root or log or 1/4 power) was used? It would seem like it would be a good idea (or equivalently to use a Poisson regression rather than normal)

comments.issue: Table 1 lacks estimated slopes and intercepts for 1970 and 2020.
comments.request: Include effect sizes in Table 1.
comments.quote: please include estimated slopes and intercepts for 1970 and 2020 in this table so effect sizes are included

comments.issue: Confidence intervals overlap for most groups in Figure 3, and Figure 4 lacks confidence intervals.
comments.request: Add 95% confidence intervals to Figure 4 and clarify Figure 3 intervals.
comments.quote: I think Figure 4 should include not just start end dots, but dots with 95% confidence intervals on them so that uncertainty vs effect sizes can be better understood

comments.issue: Rejecting Damuth's law and firm attractor patterns is a bold claim based on only three of eight groups showing strong differences.
comments.request: Strengthen the argument and evidence for this claim.
comments.quote: is it really strong ground to argue for throwing out Damuth's law, its energetic resource availability and indeed the notion of firm attractor patterns in macroecology

comments.issue: Russo et al. 2003, an influential contribution on the topic, is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Russo et al. 2003.
comments.quote: I didn't see Russo et al 2003 cited although that is an influential contribution on the topic in my mind

reviews.assessment: Highly interesting and likely publishable once the temporal area-selection confound, diet categories and many minor points are addressed.
strengths: highlights a tricky point to incorporate into future thinking
deserves publication once points are addressed

comments.issue: Temporal patterns in study-area selection could confound the results if older and newer studies sampled areas of different quality.
comments.request: Add human footprint and its interaction with body size as predictors.
comments.quote: I would want to see some explicit analytical way to convince me that their patterns are not at least partly driven by temporal patterns where older studies are from either more or less pristine areas than newer ones

comments.issue: The herbivore versus folivore distinction is unclear and partly taxonomic, excluding elephants while grouping two orders of hoofed mammals.
comments.request: Justify or revise the diet categories.
comments.quote: I do not understand the distinction between herbivores and folivores which I am not convinced is accurate.

comments.issue: The SDR abbreviation is not defined at first use and reduces readability.
comments.request: Define SDR at first usage or omit it.
comments.quote: Line 30. Define abbreviation (SDR) at first usage. I would also prefer to omit it entirely.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 58-60 is hard to understand.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: This sentence should likely be rewritten. I had to read it three times to understand it.

comments.issue: The examples at lines 68-72 are systems out of equilibrium rather than shifting equilibria.
comments.request: Explain the point in the non-equilibrium context.
comments.quote: This is an important point but it is in my mind not examples of shifting equilibria but rather of systems not being in equilibrium.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 78-83 is extremely long and grammatically problematic.
comments.request: Shorten and fix the sentence.
comments.quote: Extremely long sentence which I think also has some grammatical problems

comments.issue: The Felissa Smiths database, the source of EltonTraits diet and body size data, is not cited.
comments.request: Cite the Felissa Smiths database.
comments.quote: Since EtonTraits get all diet body size info from Felissa Smiths database I think the authors ought to cite that as well.

comments.issue: The passage at lines 194-202 would be clearer as a table.
comments.request: Present this part as a table.
comments.quote: This part would likely be easier to understand if written as a table?

comments.issue: The sentence 'every species MAY respond differnetly' is too strong.
comments.request: Weaken the sentence.
comments.quote: Line 236-237. Weaken the sentence “every species MAY respond differnetly”

comments.issue: The claim about stability of pre-anthropogenic versus Anthropocene patterns is counterintuitive and uncited.
comments.request: Provide citations or revise the claim.
comments.quote: This is in my mind a very weird claim. Since humans are important and human effects are changing rapidly it is very likely that a system not influenced by humans would be more stable.

title: Rapid Anthropocene realignment of allometric scaling rules

study.system: post-dispersal seed removal by rodents; reanalysis of a literature synthesis

editor_summary: Editor asks for a stronger conclusion focused on the issue at hand and to remove the out-of-place reference to another Technical Comment on transparency.

reviews.assessment: The reanalysis is probably right but incomplete: missing cage controls and seed density effects leave rodent attribution and the hump-shaped pattern unresolved.
strengths: explores the dataset more judiciously than the original study

comments.issue: Much of the discussion focuses on data sharing practices and is tangential to the main findings.
comments.request: Make the discussion more pertinent to the original study.
comments.quote: The comment then spends much of its discussion focusing of data sharing practices and seems to be tangential to the main findings of the comment.

comments.issue: Without cage controls, rodents cannot be confirmed as the only seed removers; birds, ants and beetles may have accessed seeds.
comments.request: Examine the studies for evidence on other seed predators.
comments.quote: if there is no cage control treatment you can't be certain that rodents were the only agents removing seeds

comments.issue: Seed density differences could bias discovery and removal rates and produce the hump-shaped relationship.
comments.request: Account for seed density effects in the reanalysis.
comments.quote: If small seeds tend to be presented at higher density than large seeds, this would introduce a significant bias and could account for a hump shaped relationship.

reviews.assessment: The reanalysis improves on the original approach, but the justification for the linear or exponential decline models should be developed further.

comments.issue: Justification for the linear or exponential decline models is thin; multiple censuses could test which model fits better.
comments.request: Justify the decline models and test their fit where possible.
comments.quote: the authors could have justified their approach in a little more detail

comments.issue: The original paper infers plant community trade-offs from a single guild of seed predators.
comments.request: Consider discussing this additional criticism.
comments.quote: There are other reasons that the original paper might be criticized – including inferring trade-offs that influence plant community structure based on the activity of a single guild of seed predators.

title: Exposure time is an important variable in quantifying post‐dispersal seed removal

study.system: roe deer; LRS distributions in stochastic environments

editor_summary: All reviewers believe the contribution is valid but question its significance in different ways; R2's framing and context comments are easiest, the others also need addressing.

reviews.assessment: Sees the work as a valid but not unexpected extension, with major problems on references, the relevance of LRS and context.

comments.issue: Key papers on the silver spoon effect and early-summer effects in cervids are missing.
comments.request: Cite van de Pol et al. 2006 and related studies.
comments.quote: References to key papers dealing with the silverspoon effect is missing (e.g, van de Pol et al. 2006 and several others).

comments.issue: LRS relates poorly to dynamics because it accumulates environmental variation across years.
comments.request: Discuss this limitation of LRS in the Discussion.
comments.quote: LRS is clearly an important component of fitness but the major problem is that this measure does only poorly relate to dynamics because it accumulates the effects of environmental variation across several years

comments.issue: Alternative stochastic demography approaches (Ellner, Lande) are not positioned against the method.
comments.request: Place the method's advantages and disadvantages in a wider context.
comments.quote: The authors mostly discuss their approach in relation to their own previous work without including references to alternative approaches in stochastic demography

reviews.assessment: Likes the framework and its potential; asks to justify LRS as a fitness measure and improve presentation.
strengths: novel framework decoupling birth environment and phenotype
potential important contribution to evolutionary ecology

comments.issue: The manuscript would be better suited as a Methods rather than a Letters contribution.
comments.request: Consider submitting it as a Methods article.
comments.quote: given the style in which the manuscript is written, it would best serve as a Methods contribution to the journal as opposed to a Letters contribution

comments.issue: The conditions under which LRS is a useful fitness measure are not described; the Brommer citation is missing.
comments.request: Describe the merits and shortcomings of LRS, including timing of reproduction.
comments.quote: Further description of the conditions when LRS is ‘useful’ is required.

comments.issue: 'Random events' at L47 may be misread as environmental rather than individual stochasticity.
comments.request: Introduce individual stochasticity early or clarify the term.
comments.quote: some might interpret ‘random events’ as being random environmental events

comments.issue: 'Stochastic' is used loosely without distinguishing environmental from individual stochasticity.
comments.request: Clarify which type of stochasticity is meant throughout.
comments.quote: the term stochastic is used loosely through the paper, without clarifying whether a given usage pertains to environmental or individual/demographic stochasticity

comments.issue: Whether phenotype can change with development is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether phenotype changes with age and growth.
comments.quote: Can the phenotype change with development (i.e., age and growth)?

comments.issue: The finding at L349-353 is not clearly depicted in the figures.
comments.request: Fuse the two panels of Fig. 2 into one.
comments.quote: This is an interesting finding, but the figures do not clearly depict this.

comments.issue: L27 lacks detail for interpretation.
comments.request: Add detail, e.g. that individuals share vital-rate expectations.
comments.quote: Perhaps provide the reader a touch more detail for interpretation

comments.issue: The humidity example at L72 is less impactful for a roe deer study.
comments.request: Choose a more demographically relevant example.
comments.quote: out of curiosity, why choose ‘humidity’ as an example?

comments.issue: Figs 2 and 3 could be improved with ggplot.
comments.request: Hone the figures using ggplot.
comments.quote: Figs 2 & 3 could be honed by using, e.g., ggplot in R.

comments.issue: Roe is capitalized inconsistently at L336.
comments.request: Make capitalization consistent.
comments.quote: Elsewhere, Roe is capitalized but not here.

comments.issue: At L387 it is unclear whether individual or environmental stochasticity is meant.
comments.request: Specify the type of stochastic variation.
comments.quote: Again, which stochastic variation are you referring to? Individual or Environmental?

reviews.assessment: Finds the topic and results very interesting but the model presentation opaque and not self-contained.

comments.issue: Whether the framework allows permanent effects of initial environment and phenotype is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss the fading of initial effects and how permanent effects could be modelled.
comments.quote: I was wondering whether the model framework also allows the initial environment and phenotype to have permanent impacts on an individual's life history

comments.issue: The expected mean environment over a lifetime and the behaviour under extreme autocorrelation are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the combined Markov chains and different autocorrelation assumptions in words.
comments.quote: What is the expected mean environment over the typical lifetime (not over an infinite time interval) of a roe deer born in a poor vs good environment when rho is high?

comments.issue: LRS counts only offspring number and ignores offspring quality.
comments.request: Discuss extending the method to accumulated offspring size or quality.
comments.quote: the model framework is focusing much on initial phenotype of the offspring, but then not including this aspect in the measure of the LRS (here only offspring number counts)

comments.issue: The model presentation is not self-contained; the earlier paper and Table 1 do not convey the method.
comments.request: Improve the model presentation so the paper stands alone.
comments.quote: from my first reading of the manuscript I did not get a good understanding of the model and I had to read the earlier paper to understand the essence of the method

comments.issue: Code for the roe deer example is not provided.
comments.request: Provide the code for the roe deer example.
comments.quote: Providing the code for the roe deer example would greatly improve the applicability of the results for readers and thus the impact of the paper.

comments.issue: The phrase at L33 is vague about what chance means.
comments.request: Clarify that chance means demographic stochasticity.
comments.quote: is a bit vague, as environmental stochasticity also implies chance?

comments.issue: LRS is called fitness rather than an important fitness component, ignoring reproductive timing.
comments.request: Refer to LRS as a fitness component and mention timing.
comments.quote: Would it not be more precise to refer to LRS as an important fitness component, than fitness?

comments.issue: The claim at L53-57 that traits are positively related to fitness is too absolute.
comments.request: Add 'often' or 'typically' to the sentence.
comments.quote: These traits or properties may often be positively related to fitness, but not always?

comments.issue: The statement at L63-66 is unclear, especially for permanent early-environment effects.
comments.request: Clarify the statement and its relation to permanent effects.
comments.quote: I don't understand this statement, which seems relevant to my question about permanent effects.

comments.issue: L93 talks about birth size only rather than phenotype.
comments.request: Use 'phenotype' for consistency.
comments.quote: Here you talk about birth size only, perhaps use “phenotype” to be consistent/general

comments.issue: 'Result' is an odd headline for the section at L114.
comments.request: Consider renaming it 'Model description'.
comments.quote: I found the word “Result” a bit odd for this section headline. Perhaps “Model description” is better?

comments.issue: Whether birth environment varies among individuals within a time point or only among cohorts is unclear at L120.
comments.request: Clarify the birth environment variation.
comments.quote: Does birth environment vary among individuals at a given time point, or only between individuals of different years (cohorts)?

comments.issue: The statement at L122-124 should acknowledge demographic stochasticity.
comments.request: Specify that differences at birth are due to phenotype.
comments.quote: But two individuals born in the same birth phenotype can still have different life histories due to demographic stochasticity?

comments.issue: The gamma definition at L133 omits i on the left-hand side.
comments.request: Include the phenotype index in the function definition.
comments.quote: In the definition of the distribution birth phenotype i is included on the righthand side, but not in the function on the left hand.

comments.issue: The notation at L189 does not show the conditional arguments.
comments.request: Include i and alpha in the function notation.
comments.quote: Same here, if it is conditional on i*alpha, include these in the function

comments.issue: The masses corresponding to size classes 50-90 are not stated at L228.
comments.request: State the masses and justify the initial size choice.
comments.quote: In addition to stating the range of size classes (50-90) it would be good to state what masses they correspond to

comments.issue: The phrase about 'runs' at L249 does not explain autocorrelation.
comments.request: Describe autocorrelation in clearer words.
comments.quote: I'm not sure the phrase “describes the “runs” of the current environmental state” helps readers understand what the autocorrelation parameter is doing.

comments.issue: 'Sticky' at L252 is imprecise.
comments.request: Use 'more likely to be the same as the current'.
comments.quote: Instead of “sticky” I would use “more likely to be the same as the current”.

comments.issue: L256 likely means the distribution of LRS rather than LRS.
comments.request: Correct the wording.
comments.quote: I guess you mean “distribution of LRS” rather than LRS?

comments.issue: Birth size effects are not shown although mentioned at L294-297.
comments.request: Report the birth size results.
comments.quote: Do you explore effects of birth size here? If so it would be good to see these results.

comments.issue: The method focuses on individual transitions and does not capture population structure at L301-302.
comments.request: Clarify the individual-level scope of the method.
comments.quote: I think your method does not capture the population aspect because it does not account for how parents may produce offspring of different types

comments.issue: Other studies have separated initial phenotype and environment effects, so the novelty claim at L330-332 needs care.
comments.request: Cite prior work such as the pike IPM study and specify the claim.
comments.quote: I suppose others have quantified similar effects before too with other models, so would be a bit careful to say this has never been done for fitness

comments.issue: Underlying vital rates and the speed of effect fading are not reported at L336-344.
comments.request: Report vital rates and transition probabilities behind the results.
comments.quote: it would be good to mention underlying mechanisms (vital rates - e.g. how much higher is first year survival in the poor and good environment)

comments.issue: The competition and resources discussion at L344-364 goes beyond what the model includes.
comments.request: Trim discussion of factors not in the model.
comments.quote: I found the discussion of competition and resources a bit too much on the side here, given your model does not include resources, competition, nor effects of individual size (state) on competition.

comments.issue: The sentence at L350-353 is confusing about demographic stochasticity and cohorts.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence and clarify the stochasticity assumptions.
comments.quote: Does this mean that you did not include demographic stochasticity (I thought this was incorporated, and that the variance in LRS increased with the mean because of some assumptions regarding mean and variance in the distribution of offspring, for instance)?

comments.issue: Table 1 is not self-explanatory: headers, abbreviations and vector meanings are missing.
comments.request: Explain each table step and spell out abbreviations.
comments.quote: Table 1 is not easy to understand, I suggest to go through this again to make sure each step is explained and well defined

comments.issue: Whether the framework can handle the non-Markov environmental model at L396-399 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether such environmental models can be included.
comments.quote: I think this would require an environmental model that was no longer a Markov chain? Can your framework include this?

comments.issue: Figure 1 has overlapping y-axis labels and unclear axes.
comments.request: Combine the panels and clarify axis labels and units.
comments.quote: y-axis labels are overlapping between the two panels. Perhaps the two distributions could be plotted together on one panel

comments.issue: Figure 2 has overlapping y-axis labels and no x-axis labels.
comments.request: Add x-axis labels and fix overlapping labels.
comments.quote: y-axis labels are overlapping between upper and lower panels. It would be good to add an x-axis with labels

comments.issue: Figure 3 lacks an x-axis with labels.
comments.request: Add an x-axis with labels.
comments.quote: Figure 3: Suggest to add an x-axis with labels.

comments.issue: The roe deer example does not explore initial offspring size despite the phenotype focus.
comments.request: Report birth size effects or simplify to an age-structured model.
comments.quote: I was a bit surprised that the roe deer example did include results for different initial offspring sizes as well, since the main idea is to separate effects of initial state of the individual (phenotype) and environment

comments.issue: No step-by-step appendix or baseline vital rates are provided.
comments.request: Add an appendix with the step-by-step LRS calculation and baseline vital rates.
comments.quote: I think it would be very useful to add an appendix where you show the step by step approach to calculate the distribution of LRS with the roe deer model.

title: Distributions of LRS in varying environments

study.system: Swedish boreal forests; soil carbon and Cortinarius fungi across 300+ sites

editor_summary: All reviewers agree there is much to like, but causality criticized by two reviewers must be addressed carefully, along with other points.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written paper with a contrary-to-belief message; asks to refocus the disturbance section and strengthen weak arguments.
strengths: interesting message contrary to common belief

comments.issue: The last discussion section reads like a hobby-horse against clear cutting rather than about disturbance as an ecological factor.
comments.request: Refocus the section on disturbance, with forestry cutting as one aspect.
comments.quote: At the moment this reads like a bit a hobby-horse, we do not like clear cutting.

comments.issue: The phrase 'Physical protection in aggregates' at page 3 line 13 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify or explain this phrase.
comments.quote: Page 3 line 13 Physical protection in aggregates

comments.issue: What is meant at page 3 line 28 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the point at page 3 line 28.
comments.quote: Page 3 Line 28. Why

comments.issue: Arguing from absence of literature support is weak because unpublished cases may exist.
comments.request: Strengthen or remove this argument.
comments.quote: It maybe that it finds no support in the literature, but this does not exclude that it may be the case

comments.issue: 'Less resilient to forestry?' at page 16 line 17 is a weak sentence.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence.
comments.quote: Page 16 line 17. Less resilient to forestry? This is a weak sentence. It could be better phrased.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and interesting study with solid, high-value a priori hypotheses; only asks for more speculative language in places.
strengths: clear patterns testing a priori hypotheses

comments.issue: The correlative approach cannot support saying C. acutus definitively decreased carbon storage.
comments.request: Use more speculative language.
comments.quote: Because the approach was correlative I don't think that you can say that Cortinarius acutus definetively decreased carbon storage

comments.issue: 'Weak decomposers' is a relative term with no stated comparison.
comments.request: Specify what the comparison is.
comments.quote: P10 L46 'weak decomposers' is a relative. Compared to white-rot fungi? Compared to bacteria?

comments.issue: 'Disprove' overstates what the results show; they do not support the claims.
comments.request: Replace 'disprove' with 'do not support'.
comments.quote: I disagree with the use of 'disprove' here. I think the results 'do not support' these claims

comments.issue: The P13L58 sentence is inaccurate and the local-scale experiment is incorrectly cited.
comments.request: Correct the statement and cite Fernandez et al. 2020.
comments.quote: the experiment that tests this hypothesis at a local scale, which is incorrectly cited (it should be Fernandez et al. 2020)

comments.issue: Figures 3 and 4 bin the x axes instead of using continuous axes.
comments.request: Present these data with continuous x axes.
comments.quote: Perhaps a matter of style-but why weren't these data presented with continuous x axes instead of binning?

reviews.assessment: Impressive, large-scale dataset, but causality claims lack experimental support and need a substantial rewrite.
strengths: impressive amount of data across >300 sites
impressive scale allowing truly general questions
authors emphasize the study is correlational

comments.issue: No experimental evidence that C. acutus accelerates decomposition; the correlation may reflect an unmeasured third variable.
comments.request: Provide experimental evidence or substantially temper the causal claims.
comments.quote: authors do not present or cite evidence that Cortinarius acutus causes an acceleration of decomposition in any experimental context

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the relationship is causal or whether C. acutus indicates an unmeasured variable.
comments.request: Acknowledge and discuss this ambiguity.
comments.quote: its still not clear if the relationship is causal, or if C. acutus is a predictor of some third, unmeasured variable that ultimately explains the SOM patterns

comments.issue: Only C. acutus correlates, found by sequentially testing species, which challenges the claim of a priori hypotheses.
comments.request: Acknowledge the inductive nature of this discovery and revise the hypothesis narrative.
comments.quote: here there is no relationship between the entire genus and SOM, only w/ C. acutus, which authors only discover by sequentially testing each abundant mycorrhizal species

comments.issue: The claim that species-level groupings outperform higher groupings is not tested.
comments.request: Scale back this claim.
comments.quote: Yet, authors do not test this claim. Its still possible that higher level (family or greater) groupings would work better

comments.issue: Different transformations are applied to predictors without justification, including pH on a log scale.
comments.request: Justify the choice of transformations.
comments.quote: Authors use a variety of transformations of predictor variables. The relative abundance of certain microbial groups is square root transformed, while others are log transformed.

comments.issue: Model fit is not reported; R2, observed-vs-fitted and partial residual plots are missing.
comments.request: Report R2 and provide fitted and partial residual plots.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if authors could at least report the total model R2 metric, and plot (perhaps in the supplement) observed vs. fitted values

comments.issue: It is unclear why presence/absence of C. acutus was used instead of the quantitative data.
comments.request: Justify or use the quantitative information.
comments.quote: Is there a reason authors focused on the presence vs. absence of C acutus, rather than using the quantitative information available

comments.issue: The Schmidt argument ignores large amounts of unprotected POC in mineral soils.
comments.request: Acknowledge this caveat at lines 13-15.
comments.quote: there is still large amounts of unprotected "POC" in mineral soils across the world

comments.issue: Typo at line 24: 'Schimmel' should be 'Schimel'.
comments.quote: Line 24- typo. I believe "Schimmel" should be "Schimel".

comments.issue: Figure 4 shows Cortinarius abundance exceeding ECM abundance, lacks error bars and has mismatched bar/axis placement.
comments.request: Fix the abundance comparison, add error bars and align bars with axes.
comments.quote: How can Cortinarius relative abundance be greater than ectomycorrhizal relative abundance, given that cortinarius is ectomycorrhizal?

title: A group of ectomycorrhizal fungi restricts organic matter accumulation in boreal forest

study.system: plant naturalisations; British introduction records, survival analysis

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers found the topic interesting but one referee raised serious data-quality concerns about introduction and establishment dates and revised records; acceptance depends on the author's replies.

reviews.assessment: Serious data-quality concerns: introduction and naturalisation dates do not measure what is claimed, and recording effort biases lag times.

comments.issue: First published records are not true introduction or naturalisation dates.
comments.request: Acknowledge and address this mismatch.
comments.quote: The author thinks he has two dates for each taxon used, the date of introduction and the date of establishment (or naturalisation). Neither date is what he says it is

comments.issue: Increasing recording effort over time could itself produce shortening lag times.
comments.request: Assess and discuss the recording-effort bias.
comments.quote: Therefore, the chance of a new occurrence of an alien species outside cultivation to be recorded has increased over the time frame of this analysis, potentially contributing to shortening lag times

comments.issue: First records often relate to casual occurrences; naturalisation status is rarely known.
comments.request: Clarify how naturalisation dates were validated.
comments.quote: It is well known that first records often relate to casual records, once the species is naturalised, it will get assigned naturalised status, but the first record date remains

comments.issue: Recently revised BSBI records invalidate many dates in the dataset.
comments.request: Update the dataset with revised first records.
comments.quote: The 2000 Atlas is therefore now no longer considered a complete record with regard to the dates, with the reviewers stating that they have found new first records in the wild for over 1000 of the 2000 taxa covered

comments.issue: Species introduced for non-horticultural reasons are not excluded from the dataset.
comments.request: Explain how these species were handled.
comments.quote: in the methodology, there is no reference to how species that may have been introduced for other reasons have been excluded from the dataset

comments.issue: Claim that recently introduced species are planted in higher numbers is unsupported.
comments.request: Provide evidence or revise the statement.
comments.quote: I disagree with these statements. First, there is no evidence that more recently introduced species would be more popular, or if there is, it should be presented

comments.issue: Forecasting future naturalisations is impossible without including the pool of introduced species.
comments.request: Include the size of the introduced-species pool in the projection.
comments.quote: it is unclear to me, how this claim can be made, if the total number of introduced species is nowhere included in this analysis?

reviews.assessment: Clever use of invasion data, but the theoretical justification, model diagnostics and broader relevance need much improvement.
