comments.quote: Line 78. Here I would use “transience” rather than “dispersal”.

comments.issue: All dispersing individuals were female, and sex biases in dispersal propensity may matter.
comments.request: Discuss the sex bias and possible physiological link.
comments.quote: The dispersing individuals were all females. It is often the case the one sex has a higher dispersal propensity to disperse. Could this be linked to physiology?

comments.issue: Non-specialists may not understand 'recorded continuously at 1 Hz' on line 133.
comments.request: Add a simple explanation of the recording frequency.
comments.quote: Non-specialists may not know what it means when you write “were recorded continuously at 1 Hz”. Could you add a simple explanation?

comments.issue: No link to the Movebank repository is given on line 147.
comments.request: Add the Movebank link.
comments.quote: Line 147. Please add a link to the Movebank repository.

comments.issue: The VO2 equation predicts 27.2 for stationary birds while line 248 gives 19.1 ml O2, which is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy in the metabolic equation.
comments.quote: If v (=velocity) is zero, then the only the intercept (27.2) remains. On line 248 you write that consumption for stationary birds is 19.1 ml O2*kg-1*min-1. Can you explain this?

comments.issue: Values on line 292 are not provided per individual.
comments.request: Provide these values per individual.
comments.quote: Line 292. Please provide these values on a per-individual basis.

comments.issue: Dispersers consumed less oxygen yet paid a higher metabolic cost, which seems contradictory.
comments.request: Explain the oxygen consumption versus metabolic cost result.
comments.quote: Here you say that dispersers consumed less oxygen (line 328) yet they paid a higher metabolic cost (line 334). I didn’t understand this. Please explain.

comments.issue: The claim that Bonte et al. 2012 overstated movement costs is not expanded.
comments.request: Expand the argument about overstated dispersal costs.
comments.quote: Why did Bonte et al. 2012 overstate the assumed movement costs of dispersal? Please expand this argument.

comments.issue: 4 line-level copy edits and reference fixes (lines 375, 484, 513, 531).
comments.quote: Line 484. This reference is incomplete.

comments.issue: The examples on lines 381-382 are all mammals, with no non-mammal examples.
comments.request: Add non-mammal examples.
comments.quote: All these species are mammals. Are there examples for non-mammal animals?

reviews.assessment: Very interesting, well-conceived and well-written study; the main comment concerns the unclear choice of random effects in the LMMs.
strengths: well conceived with clear research questions
novel insights expanding knowledge of animal movement

comments.issue: The random-effects structure of the LMMs is not justified, and alternatives such as social group, nested slopes or day are not considered.
comments.request: Explain and justify the random structure, using ecological reasoning or AIC.
comments.quote: My main comment is that it is not entirely clear how the random effects in the LMMs have been chosen, which may partly affect some of the results.

comments.issue: The term 'bird day' on l. 95 is not defined.
comments.request: Define what a bird day is.
comments.quote: It is not clear what is a bird day (l. 95). Is it just a day?

comments.issue: A brief description of the species' ecology is missing for readers unfamiliar with guineafowl.
comments.request: Add a brief description of guineafowl ecology.
comments.quote: A brief description of the ecology of the species would help understanding better some experimental procedures for people not familiar with the species.

comments.issue: The third recording protocol on l. 136-138 was not used and can be removed.
comments.request: Remove the unused recording protocol description.
comments.quote: A third recording protocol is described at l. 136-138. As this was not used in this study, these lines can be removed.

comments.issue: The number of dispersing individuals (8 of 23 versus 20) is inconsistent across the manuscript.
comments.request: Use 20 or 23 consistently.
comments.quote: I would consider to be consistent with the number 20 or 23 throughout the manuscript, as it may otherwise cause confusion.

comments.issue: Instantaneous speed was used for metabolic costs while mean velocity over a rolling window was used elsewhere, which may introduce inaccuracies.
comments.request: Explain or reconcile the use of different speed measures.
comments.quote: Wouldn’t this introduce inaccuracies in the metabolic costs?

comments.issue: The Net Displacement models and their quadratic terms in Fig. 4 and supplementary tables are not described in the main text.
comments.request: Describe these models and quadratic terms in the text or supplement.
comments.quote: I am not sure where this model is described in the main text or why quadratic terms appears in some of them, e.g. Table S22.

comments.issue: Goodness-of-fit measures and random effect estimates are missing from the tables.
comments.request: Report conditional and marginal R2 and random effect means.
comments.quote: I miss a measure of goodness-of-fit (e.g. conditional and marginal R2) and the estimated mean of the random effects in the supplementary tables and possibly Results

comments.issue: It is unclear why individuals frequently switch between fast straight and slow tortuous movement, e.g. foraging versus other reasons or Levy-like flight.
comments.request: Discuss the reasons for the frequent transitions.
comments.quote: Are the individuals foraging or slowing down for some other reason? Would this be similar to a Levy flight?

title: Efficient movement strategies mitigate the energetic cost of dispersal

study.system: simulated native and exotic species richness; covariate-based statistical models

editor_summary: All reviewers agree the contribution is important; several suggestions on how the comment could be more persuasive and more general.

reviews.assessment: Interesting simulation, but it should better replicate zero-inflated field data and bound the conditions that produce artifacts.
strengths: simulation captures the low proportion of non-native species and high plot numbers

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the simulation replicates the zero-inflated distribution of non-native species across plots.
comments.request: Show that the simulation reproduces zero-inflation and test its influence.
comments.quote: Beaury et al. (2020) had many plots with no non-native species (12 359 to be precise) and it is unclear whether the simulation adequately replicated this zero-inflated distribution

comments.issue: The range of covariate co-variation that produces spurious results is not bounded.
comments.request: Test correlations such as 0.5 versus 0.7 to bound the artifact.
comments.quote: the author could put bounds on the extend of co-variation that might lead to spurious results

comments.issue: The simulation appears at the end of the paper instead of being integrated into the main text.
comments.request: Integrate the simulation and finish with a concluding paragraph.
comments.quote: the simulation comes at the end of the paper but should be integrated with the main text so that the manuscript finishes with a concluding paragraph

reviews.assessment: Two major issues: the title claim is incorrect and Beaury et al. are mischaracterised.

comments.issue: The title claim is wrong: total species number is usually known and large-scale native-exotic relationships are positive.
comments.request: Revise the title and the claim it makes.
comments.quote: the title that “Native and exotic species richness will always be negatively correlated when the total number of species is known” does not seem correct

comments.issue: Beaury et al. assessed the probability of non-native establishment, not a universal negative richness relationship.
comments.request: Represent Beaury et al.'s conclusions accurately.
comments.quote: Beaury et al. did not specifically state that natives are always negatively related to exotic richness

reviews.assessment: The critique is valid but currently applies only when total species pools are well modelled; wants a broader discussion.
strengths: the argument put forward is valid

comments.issue: The critique applies primarily when total species pools are well modelled; its broader limitations are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of this model structure more broadly.
comments.quote: I would like to see the discussion of this critique perhaps talk about the limitations of this method more broadly

comments.issue: Proportion of introduced richness may not be the response we mean by biotic resistance.
comments.request: Clarify the response variable in relation to biotic resistance.
comments.quote: it is unclear that proportion of species richness that is introduced is really the response that we think of in biotic resistance

comments.issue: The model predicts the proportion of exotic species, not the number of exotic species.
comments.request: Clarify what quantity is being predicted.
comments.quote: the authors are predicting not the number of exotic species, but the proportion of the plant community that is exotic

title: The relationship between native species richness and exotic species richness or occurrence will always be negative when the total number of species is accounted for in statistical models: A response to Beaury et al.

study.system: bumble bees foraging on artificial flower arrays; functional response model

editor_summary: Editor: reviewers impressed by the data and model-empirics interplay, but the model is too system-specific; present it in general form and parameterize it with the data; see Reviewer 1.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and clearly described study, but too system-specific for a general journal and the model-mutualism link needs strengthening.
strengths: careful and clear descriptions of experiment, modeling and statistics

comments.issue: Trial replication is very low despite the large individual-level dataset.
comments.request: Acknowledge the low level of trial replication.
comments.quote: This produces a large detailed dataset of many individual-level foraging bouts (although trial replication is very low).

comments.issue: Introduction, discussion and the core model are too system- and design-specific for a general ecology journal.
comments.request: Modify the model into a stand-alone general description and relegate the experiment to a parameterization.
comments.quote: this manuscript’s introduction and discussion are very system-specific for a general ecology journal such as Ecology Letters

comments.issue: Theoretical framework omits resource competition; nectar depletion could be an indirect interaction pathway.
comments.request: Include resource competition alongside interference competition in the framework.
comments.quote: including the possibility of resource competition together with interference competition would make the theoretical framework more complete and general-interest, regardless of whether or not you detected the effect empirically

comments.issue: The behavioural mechanism of interference (displacement versus avoidance) is not shown.
comments.request: Add qualitative observations of bee behaviour at flowers.
comments.quote: Are they physically displacing each other at flowers? Or do they simply avoid flowers with a current visitor, and therefore take more time to locate the remaining free flowers?

comments.issue: Conceptual distance between the model and the mutualism; per-capita visit declines coexist with large increases in absolute bee abundance.
comments.request: Connect model outputs to plant-level consequences of the mutualism.
comments.quote: It would be good to close the conceptual distance between the model and the mutualism.

comments.issue: Visitation rate may not measure bees' energy intake; visits may not equal complete nectar consumption.
comments.request: Provide data or observations on net/gross energy intake.
comments.quote: I’m not sure that visitation rate has consistent functional meaning for bees, especially within individuals and in presence of interference competition.

comments.issue: Positive honey bee effect should be related to the Greenleaf et al. 2006 sunflower study.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Greenleaf et al. 2006.
comments.quote: The positive effect of honey bees on bumble bee visitation rates (Fig 1a) reminds me of a field study which found that the presence of bumble bees increases honey bee pollinator effectiveness in hybrid sunflowers

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits and word choices (abstract, L55, L107, L138).
comments.quote: Abstract - “proxy to” -> “proxy for”

comments.issue: Abstract methods sentence is too compressed and the second main question is missing from the opening.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract to state both main questions clearly.
comments.quote: The single methods sentence has way too much compressed information for me to absorb as a naive reader.

comments.issue: Passive structures and ornate clause links make the introduction harder to read.
comments.request: Rephrase the passive and ornate constructions.
comments.quote: the writing could be made clearer by rephrasing some passive structures (“There exists”) and ornate links between clauses

comments.issue: Key terms at lines 3-9 are not explained clearly enough for a non-pollination audience.
comments.request: Explain these terms more clearly.
comments.quote: all these need to be explained more clearly, especially for a non-pollination audience

comments.issue: Pollinator-pollinator interactions, the paper's main idea, are introduced only in the third paragraph.
comments.request: Restructure the introduction to open with this idea and set up the context-dependency question earlier.
comments.quote: Pollinator-pollinator interactions are really the main idea of this paper! so introducing them in the third paragraph of the introduction feels a bit late.

comments.issue: Time between visits is hard to interpret; visitation rate would be easier for readers.
comments.request: Convert results back to visitation rate, especially in figures.
comments.quote: I understand that the data is best analyzed as time between floral visits, but converting back to visitation rate would make results easier to interpret, especially the figures.

comments.issue: Figure 3 axes show refill time although it is interpreted as resource availability.
comments.request: Reverse and relabel the axes as resource availability.
comments.quote: Similarly, “time between floral refill” is interpreted as resource availability, but those are inversely related, so the axes on Fig 3 should perhaps be reversed and re-labeled as resource availability

comments.issue: 'At least two replicates' does not convey actual replication across factorial combinations.
comments.request: Present a table of factorial combinations with replicate trials and tracked foragers.
comments.quote: “at least two replicates” - this is not a particularly informative way to summarize replication in your study design.

comments.issue: 'At the species scale' is unclear and 'species abundances' may be the wrong term.
comments.request: Clarify the wording and consider 'species richness'.
comments.quote: l 119 I’m not sure what “at the species scale” means. “species abundances” -> “species richness”?

comments.issue: Pesticide effects in Figure 4 are weak and variable despite being retained in the best model.
comments.request: Compare the treatment model against one without pesticide.
comments.quote: Fig 4, the pesticide effects seem very weak and variable, despite being included in the best model. Did you consider competing the treatment model with one that includes resource availability but not pesticide treatment?

comments.issue: Discussion stresses already-known context dependency, undercutting the study's novel contribution.
comments.request: Reframe the discussion to highlight the novel contribution.
comments.quote: This presentation undercuts the case that this study makes a significant novel, contribution that might change the way ecologists think about mutualism

reviews.assessment: Great study with two innovations and wide reach, but important clarifications and modeling questions remain.
strengths: reach from basic to applied ecology

comments.issue: Unclear whether other bee species also fed on the pesticide and how many bees were significantly exposed.
comments.request: Report which species were exposed and how many bees fed on the toxic food.
comments.quote: First, did other bee species also feed on the pesticide, or only the bumblebees? L 95-97 doesn’t make this explicitly clear

comments.issue: Claim that pesticide increases floral visits may be misleading; the effect may only be a weaker decrease.
comments.request: Recheck the direction of the pesticide effect and rephrase the claims accordingly.
comments.quote: is the interpretation correct that pesticide increases the number of floral visits under some conditions, or did the pesticide always decrease floral visits, but this effect was weaker under some conditions?

comments.issue: Predictions beyond the manipulated pollinator densities are not justified; Fig. 2 interpretation should show where data exist.
comments.request: Indicate data ranges and reconsider the density axis labelling and intercept.
comments.quote: How well are “predictions beyond the pollinator densities manipulated” (L 213) justified here? The interpretation of Fig. 2 should be supported by indicating for which values / ranges actual data exist.

comments.issue: Only a type 2 functional response was considered although results and cited references suggest a type 3 response.
comments.request: Justify the type 2 choice and say whether it affects the main interference results.
comments.quote: Why was only a type 2 functional response considered, when results and cited references (e.g. L 271-281) suggest rather a type 3 functional response, with reduced foraging effort under low resource conditions?

comments.issue: Unlike cited studies, bees could not leave low-resource areas; aggregative versus local functional response should be discussed.
comments.request: Comment on this difference in terms of aggregative versus local functional response.
comments.quote: The findings discussed in L 271-281 are actually interesting, given that in comparison to the cited studies bees could not leave low-resource areas to go to high-resource areas. I would comment on that

comments.issue: Discussion lacks explanations for why species differed and how bees actually interfered with each other.
comments.request: Discuss possible mechanisms of interference.
comments.quote: The discussion could talk a bit more about possible explanations for the effects observed (e.g. why species differed the way they did, etc.). Currently, the reader is left pondering about mechanisms and how the bees actually interfered with each other.

title: The context dependency of pollinator interference: How environmental conditions and co‐foraging species impact floral visitation

study.system: metacommunity simulation model; priority effects, niche evolution, speciation and extinction

editor_summary: All reviewers appreciated the focus and found the results potentially interesting, but raised major issues needing discussion (e.g. numerical priority effects) and presentation improvements; reviewer 3's request for code is reasonable.

reviews.assessment: Compelling, well-reasoned simulation; suggestions to clarify model justification and add interpretation of niche breadth and OVR.

comments.issue: The justification for the model specifications in lines 157-166 is hard to follow for readers unfamiliar with Gillespie 1977.
comments.request: Add more detail to explain these model specifications.
comments.quote: I had a hard time following the justification for the model specifications detailed in lines 157 - 166.

comments.issue: The distribution of nearest neighbour distances and whether OVR oscillates or converges to a mean is not reported or interpreted.
comments.request: Comment on the OVR distribution and its impact on interpretation.
comments.quote: I am curious what the distribution of nearest neighbor distances is throughout the simulation. Does the magnitude of OVR oscillate widely or does OVR tend strongly toward a mean given the other parameters in the model?

comments.issue: The consequences of holding niche breadth constant are under-interpreted, including links to explanations such as the latitudinal diversity gradient.
comments.request: Expand the justification and interpretation of constant niche breadth.
comments.quote: I wonder if the authors might add more to their comment on line 207 to give the reader a better understanding of how varying niche breadth would add biological reality but is untenable given the requirements of the simulation.

comments.issue: A priori hypotheses about how the simulation scenarios should skew the test values are not stated.
comments.request: Add a priori hypotheses about the direction of scenario effects.
comments.quote: I wonder if the authors have generated a priori hypotheses about how the simulation scenarios will skew these values in any particular direction.

comments.issue: New sites arising over macroevolutionary scales and their effect on stochasticity are not considered.
comments.request: Discuss the possibility of new sites appearing over time.
comments.quote: Isn't it possible that, over macroevolutionary scales, new sites may crop up over time? In that case, it seems like equivalent dispersal ability among species would lead to a greater amount of stochasticity than in the present simulation.

comments.issue: Figure 1 is confusing because arrival order coincides with increasing position along the niche axis.
comments.request: Clarify this in the figure legend.
comments.quote: Figure 1 is good, but I found it confusing that the order of arrival matched an increase along the niche axis. Perhaps a comment or clarification in the legend would be helpful.

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: typo "expended" at L215 and an errant comma at L468.
comments.quote: Line 215 - typo "expended" Line 468 - errant comma

reviews.assessment: Well-written and interesting simulation, but reservations about the fitness-difference interpretation, Gillespie implementation and missing analyses.

comments.issue: Code was not made available during review, preventing verification of the implementation.
comments.request: Make code available to reviewers and as supplementary material.
comments.quote: Not having access to the code prevents me from verifying that it's actually doing what the authors say it should be.

comments.issue: The biological interpretation of the positive/negative priority-effect fitness differences is obscure, especially in the IS model where invaders switch from advantage to disadvantage.
comments.request: Clarify the biological basis of the fitness differences.
comments.quote: The biological interpretation of this dramatic change in competitive advantage is a little obscure to me.

comments.issue: In the Gillespie implementation, the population undergoing an event is selected independently of per-species rates, uncoupling process rates from species.
comments.request: Clarify or fix how populations are selected for events.
comments.quote: This effectively means that the rates of the processes are uncoupled from the actual species that experience them.

comments.issue: The discussion (11 paragraphs) is too long relative to the model description (5 paragraphs), and only one figure depicts model behaviour.
comments.request: Expand the model description, shorten the discussion and add model-behaviour figures.
comments.quote: I think the limited space in the manuscript could be better used by expanding the model description in the methods (I address several ways this can be done in my minor comments below), and reducing the length of the discussion.

comments.issue: Alpha diversity is not evaluated and residence time is not considered.
comments.request: Add analyses of alpha diversity and residence time.
comments.quote: The authors quantify beta and gamma diversity of the model through time, but I find it odd that alpha diversity is not evaluated.

comments.issue: The paragraph at L71 is too methods-like and disrupts the introduction.
comments.request: Move this paragraph to the methods.
comments.quote: This whole paragraph is pretty "methods-y". The reader gets a little swamped by the details and loses the thread of the introduction. Perhaps move to the methods?

comments.issue: "One-directional" competition is not defined at L88.
comments.request: Define one-directional competition.
comments.quote: Line 88: At this point it's not clear what is meant by "one-directional" competition.

comments.issue: Brownian motion allows niches to become more similar under competition, whereas niche partitioning seems more sensible.
comments.request: Justify why niches can become more similar in the competition model.
comments.quote: In an environment that includes competition it makes more sense to me that niches would evolve to be more dissimilar (niche partitioning), rather than BM where they can randomly become _more_ similar.

comments.issue: Whether the 5x5 grid boundaries are periodic or absolute, and how edge effects are handled, is unclear.
comments.request: State the boundary conditions and account for edge effects.
comments.quote: Are boundary conditions of the 5x5 grid periodic or absolute? If they are absolute how do you account for edge effects?

comments.issue: What "population" refers to in the lineage-based model is unclear and creates confusion with species.
comments.request: Rephrase and drop the populations language.
comments.quote: It's not exactly clear what a "population" is referring to here. Can you rephrase this for clarity?

comments.issue: Anagenetic speciation would be more natural than dispersal-speciation for single-population species, and the processes become confounded.
comments.request: Reconsider the dispersal-speciation process and its counting toward colonization.
comments.quote: If a species undergoing speciation only has one population, it's much more natural for this to be anagenetic speciation, rather than this "dispersal-speciation" process.

comments.issue: The extinction-rate equation appears to need mu_zero plus mu_max, and the mu_max/mu_realized usage is difficult to understand.
comments.request: Check the equation and clarify mu_max versus mu_realized.
comments.quote: Shouldn't this be mu_zero + mu_max? This is what the equation on line 172 indicates.

comments.issue: Extinction is a global parameter rather than emerging from local competition.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism of the extinction process.
comments.quote: What is the mechanism of the extinction process? It seems more natural to have extinction emerge from the process of local competition, rather than it being a global parameter of the model.

comments.issue: The biological interpretation and prior art for the trait boundary at L144 are unclear.
comments.request: Give a biological interpretation and prior art for this boundary.
comments.quote: Is there a biological interpretation for this boundary? Is there prior art for applying this in trait diversification theory?

comments.issue: The symbol for the repulsion parameter does not render at L145.
comments.request: Fix the missing symbol.
comments.quote: Line 145: The symbol for the repulsion parameter doesn't show up for me.

comments.issue: The concept of "realised rates" at L163/165 is not explained.
comments.request: Define realised rates.
comments.quote: The concept of 'realised rates' hasn't been explained, or at least I don't see it. Please clarify.

comments.issue: When niche overlap is below psi the right-hand term turns negative and reduces background extinction; whether this is intended is unclear.
comments.request: Confirm or explain this behaviour of the equation.
comments.quote: If niche overlap is smaller than this psi parameter the right hand term will be negative, which will reduce the background extinction rate. Is this intended?

comments.issue: It is unclear how arrival order can be permuted, since it is a simulated value, and it should not matter under symmetric competition.
comments.request: Clarify the arrival-order permutation.
comments.quote: How can arrival order be permuted? Arrival order is a simulated value. Also, if competition is symmetric then arrival order shouldn't matter.

comments.issue: The niche-incumbency signal and the exact result behind the L371 conclusion are not specified.
comments.request: Specify the result supporting the niche-incumbency conclusion.
comments.quote: The signal of niche incumbency being referred to is not clear at this point. The exact result that leads to this conclusion is not specified.

comments.issue: The mass extinction paragraph at L375 is a tangent that lengthens the discussion.
comments.request: Remove this paragraph.
comments.quote: This paragraph about mass extinction feels like a tangent that could be removed to reduce the length of the discussion.

comments.issue: The bounded versus unbounded niche-space discussion is not supported, as Fig. S3 shows virtually no difference.
comments.request: Temper or support the bounded niche-space claim.
comments.quote: Here the discussion is about the effect of bounded versus unbounded niche space on phylogenetic tree balance, but in figure S3 there appears to be virtually no difference between these models.

comments.issue: The paragraph at L444 is largely redundant with earlier discussion.
comments.request: Remove or condense the redundant paragraph.
comments.quote: Line 444: This paragraph is largely redundant with previous discussion.

comments.issue: The statement about spatial turnover differences is not warranted given the small differences in Fig. 2h.
comments.request: Temper the statement about spatial turnover.
comments.quote: The difference in spatial turnover among the models appears quite small (figure 2h), so I'm not sure this statement is warranted.

title: Priority effects and the macroevolutionary dynamics of biodiversity

study.system: ray-finned fishes; four body-size datasets, nine taxonomic scales

editor_summary: Three reviewers find the study straightforward, novel and important, but criticize poor presentation of methods and results; many other issues must be addressed; only a deeply improved manuscript could be resubmitted.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and statistically strong, but the size-habitat result is not really new and the theory discussion is superficial; major revision needed.
strengths: sophisticated statistical analyses of huge datasets
pattern emerges on nine taxonomic levels

comments.issue: The main size-habitat result largely repeats Olden et al. (2007); the nine-scale extension is the only novelty.
comments.request: Acknowledge the earlier result and clarify what is new.
comments.quote: Well, this is an interesting finding, although it is not really new (for example, see Olden et al., 2007, quoted by the author)

comments.issue: Theory discussion is superficial: the eight mechanisms are not tested or directly addressed by the analyses.
comments.request: Design analyses that test some of the eight hypotheses.
comments.quote: the discussion about these theories is very superficial and none of these assumptions is directly addressed by the analytical work

comments.issue: Very few fish clades are discussed as case studies; clade data in Figure 1b are ignored.
comments.request: Discuss representative clades shown in Figure 1b.
comments.quote: It is also frustrating that very few mentions of fish clades appear in the discussion to illustrate the hypotheses or to serve as case studies

comments.issue: Paper reads as a methods article rather than biology; its biological contribution is unclear.
comments.request: Strengthen the biological results and discussion; major revision.
comments.quote: In short, for me, this article is more like an article on methods than on biology

comments.issue: Lines 476-485 repeat the previous paragraph.
comments.quote: lines 476-485 is a repetition of the previous paragraph

comments.issue: Figures are too dense and nearly impossible to read.
comments.request: Simplify the figures.
comments.quote: The figures are too dense and almost impossible to read.

reviews.assessment: Solid answer to the central size-habitat question and fundamentally advocates publication, but clarity, unjustified taxonomic-rank assumptions and redundant analyses need major work.
strengths: very firm conclusion on the central question
solid job answering the habitat-size question

comments.issue: Manuscript is very difficult to read; grammar, sentence construction and paragraphing need extensive revision.
comments.request: Extensively revise for clarity and flow.
comments.quote: I felt like I was reading an 8000-word Twitter post, with all the abbreviated language, incorrect grammar and aggravating loss of clarity.

comments.issue: Analyses at taxonomic ranks assume an equivalence among families and orders that does not exist.
comments.request: Justify or abandon ranks; use meaningful lineages and streamline this presentation.
comments.quote: What is a taxonomic rank? What is a family? What is an order? These ranks do not capture anything natural or real.

comments.issue: Almost every question is addressed with multiple redundant analyses, costing clarity.
comments.request: Select the best method per question and relegate the rest to supplements.
comments.quote: I think a better approach is to select the best method in each case, and relegate the redundancy to supplemental material.

comments.issue: Figures 2-4 are overloaded with taxonomic ranks; Figure 2 contains about 180 separate graphs.
comments.request: Show fewer ranks in the main figures; move full versions to supplements.
comments.quote: Surely the key points in Figure 2 could be made with fewer than 180 separate graphs?!

comments.issue: Nine line-level copy edits: awkward sentences, grammar slips, 'fulfil' spelling, 19-sentence paragraph, 'Clupeoformes' typo, 'pertinently' wording.
comments.quote: L44. This sentence about '~10,000 and ~26,000 species data sets' is really awkward.

comments.issue: The argument for larger size in marine fish is too abbreviated; the cited differences are not specified.
comments.request: Explain the food web, habitat area and complexity differences; expand the discussion.
comments.quote: I don't follow this argument for larger size in marine fish. What differences in food web structure, habitat area, and habitat complexity are you referring to?

comments.issue: The meaning of 'habitat use in fishes is especially complex' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify; presumably means fish crossed the salinity divide repeatedly.
comments.quote: What does it mean that 'habitat use in fishes is especially complex'?

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'richness of each habitat' refers to (species richness? nitrogen?).
comments.request: Specify which richness is meant.
comments.quote: reflect expectations given the richness of each habitat..' What richness? Species richness? Available nitrogen?

comments.issue: The claim that patterns are similar in the 31k tree is too vague to be falsifiable.
comments.request: Specify which patterns are similar and what 'similar' means.
comments.quote: Please be more specific about what patterns are similar in the 31k tree, and be specific about what you mean by similar?

comments.issue: 'Raw mean' vs phylogenetically corrected mean is undefined (untransformed values? log values?).
comments.request: Define both means precisely.
comments.quote: What do you mean by 'raw mean' vs phylogenetically corrected mean? Is raw mean the mean of untransformed values in centimeters?

comments.issue: 'Largely' is vague; it is unclear how well the patterns hold.
comments.request: Be specific about the extent to which patterns hold.
comments.quote: Could you be more specific? "Largely" is another vague term that makes this reader rather uncomfortable.

comments.issue: The simulation ANOVA (Garland, Revell 2012) reportedly does not work (Adams & Collyer 2018).
comments.request: Do not use the simulation ANOVA if it is invalid.
comments.quote: I believe that Adams and Collyer 2018 showed that the simulation ANOVA of Garland, and I think implemented in Revell 2012, does not work.

comments.issue: Describing some tests as more 'sensitive' is misguided; smaller p-values reflect bias, not sensitivity.
comments.request: Correct the discussion of test sensitivity and method choice.
comments.quote: If the correct way does not give as small a p value that's not because it's less 'sensitive', it's because the other method is biased.

comments.issue: 'Theory' is misused: theories explain patterns rather than generate them.
comments.request: Rephrase the role of theory.
comments.quote: Theories don't generate patterns of body size variation. They attempt to account for or explain those patterns and propose the specific mechanisms that produce them

comments.issue: The goby discussion is circular and does not explain the counter-trend.
comments.request: Rewrite the goby argument.
comments.quote: I am having a hard time understanding this discussion of gobies. The reasoning seems circular to me.

comments.issue: Extended Data Table 1 is missing, so the migratory-proportion claim cannot be verified.
comments.request: Provide the table and report migratory fractions per habitat in the text.
comments.quote: there is no Extended Data Table 1 in the manuscript or the supporting material on the website, so I was not able to verify the point

comments.issue: Saying migratory taxa 'can be larger' is too vague.
comments.request: State that large size may be adaptive for two main reasons.
comments.quote: I think you mean that large size may be adaptive in migratory taxa for two main reasons, but saying that they 'can be larger' is too vague.

comments.issue: Claim that migratory taxa 'may occupy the highest trophic levels' is too vague; they may occupy any level.
comments.request: State which trophic levels they actually occupy and why.
comments.quote: They MAY occupy any trophic level. This is too vague. Do they, in fact, occupy the highest trophic levels?

comments.issue: 'Swimming efficiency' is used loosely without specifying which energetic metric is meant.
comments.request: Specify the metric (e.g., cost of transport) and clarify the argument.
comments.quote: This is a sloppy discussion of the effect of body size on swimming efficiency. For example, what do you mean by 'swimming efficiency' here?

reviews.assessment: Finds the study original and the analyses sound, but wants the theories named, macroevolutionary context added and tree-placement artifacts checked.
strengths: analyses well suited to the question

comments.issue: The eight theories behind the size-habitat expectations are discussed without names or references.
comments.request: Name the theories and give references.
comments.quote: In the discussion, you state, "I consider at least eight theories", but which ones? Please provide the names and the references.

comments.issue: No discussion of macroevolutionary theories of speciation and diversification or of key relevant studies.
comments.request: Add a clear macroevolutionary discussion with the cited references.
comments.quote: Overall, a clear discussion regarding macroevolutionary theories is needed.

comments.issue: TACT can graft species outside their family; rogue species may bias family-scale results.
comments.request: Test how much TACT placement errors affect the family-scale results.
comments.quote: The TACT method used in Rabosky et al. (2018) is not conservative in the sense that species can be grafted outside their original family

comments.issue: Key reference on productivity and diadromous fish migration is missing.
comments.request: Cite Gross et al. (1988).
comments.quote: Please add this important reference about the link between productivity and diadromous fishes

title: Evidence for general size‐by‐habitat rules in actinopterygian fishes across nine scales of observation

study.system: grassland microcosms; plant and soil biodiversity manipulations

editor_summary: Editor: methods need to be clearer, especially the microbial measures, and the authors should be careful about what can be generalized from this short-term greenhouse experiment.

reviews.assessment: Well-designed experiment on an important question; asks to fix an overstatement about soil biodiversity and to discuss single-season limitations and method details.

comments.issue: Stating that soil biodiversity is necessary for stability misrepresents results where plant diversity acts independently.
comments.request: Describe soil biodiversity as an alternate or additive pathway instead.
comments.quote: there is an assertion that soil biodiversity is necessary for maintaining stability in several places (e.g. line 301 and 324). Given that plant diversity is positively related to stability independent of soil biodiversity, I feel that this misrepresents the results.

comments.issue: Stability is measured within a single season with clipping, excluding reproduction and recruitment dynamics.
comments.request: Discuss this limitation relative to field experiments.
comments.quote: The temporal stability that is assessed is response to different watering regimes followed by clipping within a single season. This prevents any population dynamics through differences in reproduction/recruitment from influencing the results

comments.issue: It is unclear whether wilting-based watering was consistent across treatments.
comments.request: Report whether some treatments were watered more or earlier.
comments.quote: During the dry periods, watering only occurred when “most of the plant species started to wilt.” Was this consistent across treatments or did some treatments receive more/earlier watering than others?

comments.issue: Soil DNA was extracted only from 12-species microcosms at the end, which conflicts with results referring to initial soils.
comments.request: Clarify when and from which microcosms DNA was extracted.
comments.quote: Why was soil DNA only extracted from the 12-species microcosms at the end of the experiment. This is particularly confusing as the results seem to refer to DNA extractions from soils from the start of the experiment.

comments.issue: The calculation of standardized richness values is not explained.
comments.request: Explain whether observed richness was divided by planted or realized maximum richness.
comments.quote: Please provide more information on how the standardized richness values were calculated. I am assuming that you divided observed richness by max richness, but was this planted richness or realized richness?

comments.issue: Trait-based patterns proposed at lines 304-309 are testable with the measured traits but are not tested.
comments.request: Test and report whether the measured traits support these patterns.
comments.quote: Given that you have measured these traits in this experiment, do you find any evidence for these patterns? This should be testable

reviews.assessment: Timely, well-designed contribution; requests additional DNA sampling, clearer experimental details and broader references to strengthen it.
strengths: timely contribution bridging a knowledge gap

comments.issue: Soil DNA was sampled only at the start and final harvest, missing temporal dynamics.
comments.request: Extract soil DNA at all six sampling points.
comments.quote: it would be great if soil DNA can be extracted all the six sampling points to fully capture the temporal patterns of soil biodiversity

comments.issue: The statement at line 84 relies mainly on the authors' own work.
comments.request: Add references beyond Yang et al. 2018.
comments.quote: I would suggest adding more references beyond the authors’ own work (Yang et al., 2018) to support this statement

comments.issue: Sterilization effectiveness, the sand:field soil mixture and the inoculum amounts need clarification.
comments.request: Provide evidence that autoclaving removes soil biota and clarify the soil setup.
comments.quote: Do the authors have experimental evidence that autoclaving at 121 degree for 90 min could effectively remove soil biota? Why using a sterilized 1:1 sand:field soil mixture?

comments.issue: Water sources are not reported and watering may introduce microbes, especially in low-diversity treatments.
comments.request: Report water sources and whether water was sterilized.
comments.quote: if water was not autoclaved for this experiment, I would expect watering may significantly disturb the level of soil biodiversity especially for the low soil biodiversity treatments

comments.issue: Rarefaction curves for sequenced samples are not provided.
comments.request: Provide rarefaction curves in the supporting files.
comments.quote: It would be great if authors could provide rarefaction curves for the sequenced samples in supporting files.

comments.issue: How fungal mutualists and pathogens were identified is not described.
comments.request: Describe the identification of mutualists and pathogens in the Methods.
comments.quote: The information for how to identify fungal mutualists and pathogens in the section of Materials and Methods

comments.issue: Soil microbial diversity is used as a proxy for soil biodiversity, ignoring protists, archaea, viruses and soil fauna.
comments.request: Acknowledge the narrower scope of the biodiversity measure.
comments.quote: Apart from bacteria and fungi, other microbes including protists, archaea and virus, and soil fauna such as the abundant nematodes, are highly diverse in the soil environment. Therefore, I disagree that soil microbial diversity was used for soil biodiversity

comments.issue: The number of sequences used for diversity calculations is unclear and ASV values look low.
comments.request: Report sequence numbers used for diversity calculations.
comments.quote: Could the authors provide more information for how many sequences were used for diversity calculations? The values of ASVs for bacteria and fungi look very low to me.

comments.issue: 'Multitrophic diversity' is not explicitly defined.
comments.request: State that it means soil plus plant diversity.
comments.quote: Please clarify clearly that ‘multitrophic diversity’ here means “soil biodiversity and plant diversity”

comments.issue: Why soil biodiversity matters more for herbs than grasses is not explained.
comments.request: Elaborate on this mechanism.
comments.quote: It would be great if authors could elaborate a bit more why soil biodiversity is more important for herbs than for grasses?

comments.issue: No mechanism is given for increased legume growth under soil biodiversity loss in monocultures.
comments.request: Provide a mechanistic explanation for the legume response.
comments.quote: This paragraph lacks a proper explanation why soil biodiversity loss can increased the growth of legumes in the monocultures, any mechanistic explanation?

comments.issue: Soil respiration is used to infer microbial abundance although abundance was not measured directly.
comments.request: Acknowledge that respiration is only a proxy for abundance.
comments.quote: Actually, the current study did not directly measure the microbial abundance, soil respiration rate was measured to infer the abundances of microbes, which may be not necessarily correct

reviews.assessment: Interesting question and novel knowledge, but pseudoreplication and microbial recolonization make the design and conclusions questionable.
strengths: potential novel knowledge on multitrophic biodiversity
important conclusions raised by the authors

comments.issue: The design mixes true replicates per richness level with pseudoreplicates of the same plant community composition.
comments.request: Clarify what the 123 microcosms correspond to and distinguish replicates in Table S1.
comments.quote: as you used a pool of 12 plant species in total for the experiment, it seems that your design mixes true replicates per species richness with pseudo-replicates of the same plant community composition

comments.issue: Pseudoreplicates may not have been distinguished from true replicates in the statistical analyses.
comments.request: Confirm and correct the treatment of pseudoreplicates in the analyses.
comments.quote: I have an issue with the statistical analyses, as I fear that pseudo-replicates have not been distinguished from true replicates

comments.issue: It is not clear that Fig. 2 and lines 204-210 refer to initial soil microbial diversity before inoculation.
comments.request: State this clearly in the caption and text.
comments.quote: I advice that the authors more clearly state in Fig 2 caption and on Lines 204-210 that they are referring to the initial soil microbial diversity before inoculation of the soil microcosms

comments.issue: Microbial diversity was quantified only in 12-species microcosms, and realized versus sown diversity gradients differ greatly without discussion.
comments.request: Measure or discuss microbial diversity across treatments and the realized-sown discrepancy.
comments.quote: I do not understand why soil microbial diversity was quantified only in the 12 species microcosms (actually 12 times the same plant community if I am right)

comments.issue: The reverse direction, plant diversity influencing soil microbial diversity, is not discussed or evaluated.
comments.request: Discuss how plant richness and composition may shape microbial diversity.
comments.quote: many studies indicating that plant diversity influences soil microbial abundances and diversity. Specifically, here it can be expected that plant community species richness and composition strongly influence soil microbial diversity, but this is not evaluated.

comments.issue: Recolonization of the 6.8 kg microcosms is not described; actual microbial abundances are unknown and plant composition may distort the gradient.
comments.request: Describe the recolonization process and provide data on realized microbial diversity.
comments.quote: nothing is said about the recolonization process in the 7 kg microcosms. All this raises three important issues: (i) the actual abundances of microorganisms in the microcosms are basically unknown

comments.issue: These methodological limitations largely obscure interpretation and are not adequately discussed.
comments.request: Seriously take these aspects into account and discuss them adequately.
comments.quote: I do not say that this makes this ms. not interesting and possibly important. I just say that these aspects should be very seriously taken into account and discussed adequately

comments.issue: The hypotheses remain vague and do not specify expected microbial effects or plant attributes.
comments.request: Specify the major processes and the roles of beneficial versus pathogenic microbes.
comments.quote: The objectives of the study are clear, but the hypotheses remain vague/weak (Lines 84): please specify which microbial effects on plants, which plant attributes

comments.issue: Figures 3, 4 and 5 are overloaded with panels and Fig. 5 may not be needed.
comments.request: Select panels better and consider moving Fig. 5 to the supplement.
comments.quote: I find figures 3, 4 & 5 heavy, a bit as if the authors would like to present too many things. I advocate for a better selection of panels

comments.issue: Statistical results are not provided in more figures.
comments.request: Add statistical results to Fig. 2 and supplementary figures.
comments.quote: It would be good to provide statistical results in more figures

comments.issue: Two seminal papers on the suspension-dilution approach are missing.
comments.request: Cite Wertz et al. 2006 and 2007.
comments.quote: I missed two seminal papers regarding the suspension-dilution approach for soil microbial community: Wertz et al. 2006 Env. Microbiol. 8: 2162-2169; and Wertz et al. 2007 Env. Microbiol. 9: 2211-2219.

comments.issue: The wording at line 45 risks over-generalization.
comments.request: Use more precise wording.
comments.quote: Line 45: more precisely “maintaining both plant and soil biodiversity for sustainable

comments.issue: NGS can detect low-abundance taxa and diversity was dynamic during the experiment, so claims that diversity was absent need revision.
comments.request: Rephrase affected interpretations.
comments.quote: do not forget that NGS approaches cann detect low abundance taxa ; and that the microbial community diversity was likely very dynamics during step 3 and 4 of your experiment

title: Plant and soil biodiversity have non‐substitutable stabilising effects on biomass production

study.system: freshwater mesocosms; plankton communities under pesticides and nutrients

editor_summary: All reviewers agree the paper needs simplifying and hypotheses must be less vague and more mechanistic; reviewers differ on theory, synthesis and population-level results.

reviews.assessment: Carefully conducted, well-presented experiment; asks for better theoretical expectations, a synthetic summary and clearer model specification.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a dedicated theoretical paragraph on how dimensionality of stability should respond to multiple stressors.
comments.request: Add theoretical expectations citing Radchuk, Dominguez-Garcia and Yang.
comments.quote: I would suggest having a dedicated paragraph in the introduction that summarizes expectations about how the dimensionality of stability should behave under multiple stressors based on theory

comments.issue: A synthetic summary of when community and population patterns align is missing.
comments.request: Add a graph or table summarizing the correlations and take-home message.
comments.quote: I really missed a synthetic summary of the findings: when do we see systematic patterns between the community and population level?

comments.issue: Average effects of stressors are not presented alongside covariance effects.
comments.request: Present average stressor effects, at least in the supplement.
comments.quote: While the focus of the paper is patterns of covariance among stability components, I was wondering about the average effects of stressors?

comments.issue: Random structure of the mixed models is unclear: random slope per community type, no random intercept, and justification missing.
comments.request: Clarify and justify the random-effect structure.
comments.quote: The text only specifies random slopes (lines 187-188), does this mean no random intercept was included? If so, why?

comments.issue: Figure 2 should show individual data points in addition to box plots.
comments.request: Add individual data points to Figure 2.
comments.quote: I suggest to show the individual data points in addition to the box plots.

comments.issue: Jittering across treatments in Figures 3-5 makes variation hard to judge.
comments.request: Keep individual points on the same vertical axis as the average.
comments.quote: Currently it is very cumbersome to judge the variation of coefficients within treatments due to the jittering of points across treatments.

comments.issue: The argument that negative diversity-functional stability relationships are misleading is unconvincing.
comments.request: Rephrase the paragraph and embrace negative diversity-stability relationships.
comments.quote: I think this whole paragraph needs to be rephrased. I am not convinced by this argument about negative diversity-functional stability relationships being misleading.

comments.issue: Eleven line-level copy edits and typos throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: line 28: with "trophic status" you mean "trophic level"? (there is multiple place to fix this)

reviews.assessment: Important, novel experiment; paper is hard to digest and needs individual stability metrics shown and population-level results removed.
strengths: novel combination of stressors, stability dimensions and organisation levels

comments.issue: No section explains how individual stability metrics responded, preventing mechanistic understanding.
comments.request: Add a section on individual stability metric trends.
comments.quote: The main problem (and that's my major concern with this paper) is that there is no explanation as to how the individual stability metrics respond.

comments.issue: Population-level stability is based on only two species per community, making population-community comparisons meaningless.
comments.request: Remove the population-level stability results.
comments.quote: it is very difficult to link both, as population-level stability is explored solely for 2 species per trophic community, so comparisons between population and community level responses become meaningless

comments.issue: The comparison of nutrient-enriched and non-enriched communities is not motivated by the diversity-stability debate.
comments.request: Motivate the nutrient comparison and mention the diversity-stability debate in the Introduction.
comments.quote: I suggest to motivate better the comparison between communities with added and non-added nutrients

comments.issue: Lines 50-53 should clarify that maximizing one stability metric will not affect the others.
comments.request: Make this limitation clear.
comments.quote: what needs to be clear is that this action will not have an effect on other stability metrics

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits (article removal; genus spelling).
comments.quote: Line 65: remove "the" before "data"

comments.issue: Hypothesis 1 is too general and lacks a predicted direction.
comments.request: Rephrase the hypothesis with an expected direction.
comments.quote: Hypothesis 1 is too general- I would suggest the authors rephrase it and suggest a directionality of the effect

comments.issue: The term 'networking' for species is strange.
comments.request: Replace 'species networking' with clearer wording.
comments.quote: species "networking" sounds strange- what about "from stress-driven changes in species that propagate throughout the food-web

reviews.assessment: Timely idea, but the current paper is not insightful; a single small mesocosm cannot support the broad hypotheses.
strengths: timely connection of multiple-stressor research with stability theory
clear and concise introduction and Figure 1
interesting stressor effects on functional/compositional stability (H2)

comments.issue: Introduction, conclusions and title do not align with the methods and results.
comments.request: Align the framing with what the study actually does.
comments.quote: I feel that the introduction, conclusions and title of the paper do not align with its methods and results.

comments.issue: One mesocosm experiment with n=3 cannot address general multiple-stressor questions.
comments.request: Narrow the scope or justify the design.
comments.quote: A single mesocosm experiment with a very low number of replicates (24 mesocosms, 8 treatments, n=3), is not the best approach to explore a general idea

comments.issue: The introduction and Figure 1 read as a literature review rather than identifying knowledge gaps.
comments.request: Rework the introduction to identify the knowledge gap.
comments.quote: The introduction and figure 1 are clear and concise, but they feel more like a literature review, rather than an identification of knowledge gaps.

comments.issue: The link between multiple-stressor research and ecological stability is underdeveloped.
comments.request: Develop the conceptual connection between the two fields.
comments.quote: I think that the connection between multiple-stressor research and ecological stability is underdeveloped.

comments.issue: Hypotheses H1 and H3 are beyond the scope of the experiment.
comments.request: Scale the hypotheses to what the experiment can test.
comments.quote: The general hypotheses tested (H1 and H3) seem well beyond the scope of a single mesocosm experiment with one community, low replication and few stressors.

comments.issue: Highly uncertain stability estimates are used to quantify dimensionality of stability, which seems meaningless.
comments.request: Show uncertainty and reconsider the DS quantification.
comments.quote: using these highly uncertain estimates of stability metrics to quantify overall dimensionality of stability (in two different ways) seems a bit meaningless

comments.issue: The usefulness of measuring dimensionality of stability and what different results mean is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the usefulness and meaning of DS.
comments.quote: I don't see where the authors explain the usefulness of measuring the dimensionality of stability and what different results for different stressors would actually mean?

comments.issue: A more theoretical approach is needed to link multiple stressors and stability before experiments test it.
comments.request: Develop the theoretical links and test specific hypotheses.
comments.quote: I think that a more theoretical approach is needed to establish the potential links between multiple stressors and ecological stability

comments.issue: Too few references; connections between stability metrics and multiple stressors need development.
comments.request: Add references and develop these connections.
comments.quote: there are probably too few references. The connections between different stability metrics themselves and multiple stressors is one area that could be developed further.

comments.issue: Mesocosm experiments are designed to test mechanisms, so the scope excuse at L344 is inconsistent.
comments.request: Reconsider the scope argument.
comments.quote: but mesocosm experiments are specifically designed to tease apart specific mechanisms, rather than to identify general patterns

comments.issue: Figure 2 should show raw data points or sample sizes.
comments.request: Add raw points or sample sizes to Figure 2.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to see the raw data points (or at least the sample sizes for each boxplot)

comments.issue: Figures 3-5 use medians without spread and show only noise.
comments.request: Show spread/error bars and reduce jitter.
comments.quote: It would definitely be good to show a measure of spread (error bars) for the mean/median.

title: Effects of multiple stressors on the dimensionality of ecological stability

study.system: PUFA distributions and metabolism across ecosystems; synthesis

editor_summary: Editor praises writing and figures, but all reviewers agree novelty is not yet top quality; suggests stronger links to ecological stoichiometry and range expansion, a further figure, and reconsidering the term 'metabolic trait'.

reviews.assessment: Well written and useful overview; suggests stronger links to ecological stoichiometry and range-expansion literature and a few copy edits.
strengths: useful overview of fatty acid geography

comments.issue: The geographic overview largely documents information that has been published before.
comments.quote: As the authors note, this information, has been documented before, but the overview is useful.

comments.issue: The review makes too few connections to the broader ecological stoichiometry literature.
comments.request: Briefly link the content to ecological stoichiometry.
comments.quote: Because this manuscript is intended for an ecological audience, I think that more connections could be made with ecological stoichiometry

comments.issue: The metabolic processes section is complex and long enough to be a paper in itself.
comments.request: Condense this section or consider it for another paper.
comments.quote: I wonder if the material here could be condensed somewhat and perhaps the material as a whole go into another paper.

comments.issue: Only one ecological example (stickleback) is described in detail.
comments.request: Describe another example in some detail.
comments.quote: The stickleback is a key example, but it seems to be the only ecological example described in any detail. Is there another example that could be described in some detail?

comments.issue: The paper does not connect to the ecological literature on range expansions accompanied by trait change.
comments.request: Relate the ideas to range-expansion and trait-change literature.
comments.quote: But again, I think the authors should do more to relate this to the large ecological literature on range expansions that are accompanied by changes in traits

comments.issue: The references rely on Simpson from the 1940s and 50s, ignoring more recent literature.
comments.request: Cite relevant literature from after the 1950s.
comments.quote: It is also odd that the references rely on George Gaylord Simpson from the 1940s and 50s.

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits on pages 7, 10 and 13.
comments.quote: Page 7, Line 10. Change 'fatty acids as' to 'fatty acids such as'

reviews.assessment: Innovative, well-written review that needs clearer structure, systematic introduction of terms, and an additional summary figure.

comments.issue: The paper is sometimes too complex because pathway and species/ecosystem information are presented together.
comments.request: Untangle pathway information from species and ecosystem differences.
comments.quote: This paper is well written but sometimes a bit too complex structured as FA pathway and species/ecosystem differences are mentioned at once.

comments.issue: The first introduction paragraphs lack a stringent line of thought, and key information is scattered throughout.
comments.request: Restructure the first paragraphs to introduce the individual terms clearly.
comments.quote: I suggest restructuring the first paragraphs of the introduction to gain more clarity aiming for a more stringent line of thought introducing the individual terms.

comments.issue: The term dietary quality is ambiguous and should be tied to fatty acids as a specific measure.
comments.request: Specify dietary resource quality and introduce fatty acids as the quality measure.
comments.quote: The term dietary quality can mean different things for different people as it can mean: energy content (kJ), macronutrient composition (C, N, P), amino acids, but also fatty acids.

comments.issue: The paragraph combining term introduction, FA biosynthesis and species information is too dense to follow.
comments.request: Restructure the paragraph to reduce the information presented at once.
comments.quote: This paragraph includes a lot of information about term introduction and also the FA biosynthesis together with the information about the different species. This combination makes it difficult to understand the whole content.

comments.issue: n-3 and n-6 PUFAs are used as synonyms for specific fatty acids such as DHA, EPA, ALA and ARA.
comments.request: Name the specific fatty acids or define n-3 and n-6 PUFA clearly.
comments.quote: it seems that the authors use n-3 and n-6 PUFAs as synonyms for DHA, EPA and LIN, ALA, ARA but the authors should be careful because more FAs are part of the n-3 and n-6 PUFAs

comments.issue: No figure summarises the evolution of fatty acid pathways across the tree of life.
comments.request: Add a figure summarising fatty acid pathway evolution.
comments.quote: I suggest adding a figure that summarize and maybe make the evolution of fatty acid pathway clearer across the tree of life

comments.issue: Figure 1 panels are referenced out of order and panels A and B are never mentioned.
comments.request: Reference figures and panels in the correct order.
comments.quote: Panel A and B are not mentioned at all. Please reference figures and panels accordingly.

comments.issue: LIN is used for the first time without its full name.
comments.request: Give the full name of LIN at first mention.
comments.quote: LIN is mentioned here the first time, please give the whole name.

comments.issue: Examples for different environmental conditions are requested.
comments.request: Give examples for different environmental conditions.
comments.quote: Give examples for different environmental condition although the authors

comments.issue: The term network is used instead of metabolic pathway throughout the text and legends.
comments.request: Use metabolic pathway instead of network throughout.
comments.quote: I suggest use metabolic pathway instead of network throughout the manuscript and in the figure legends

comments.issue: Figures 4 and 5 are mentioned before Figure 3, which is first cited on page 16.
comments.request: Cite figures in the order they appear.
comments.quote: Fig 4 and Fig 5 mentioned before Fig 3 which is mentioned the first time on page 16 L43

comments.issue: The referent of "these" metabolic traits at page 10 L54 is unclear.
comments.request: Specify which metabolic traits are meant.
comments.quote: Page 10 L54: which are “these” metabolic traits?

comments.issue: SFA is defined earlier but redefined at page 11 L15.
comments.request: Just use SFA without redefining it.
comments.quote: SFA were defined before so just say SFA

reviews.assessment: Covers the field well with an ecological perspective and will be an excellent platform, but needs a more critical voice.
strengths: covers much of the knowledge in the field

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a critical voice, presenting only examples where PUFA has positive fitness effects.
comments.request: Add a more critical discussion including contrasting findings.
comments.quote: it lacks a critical voice on the importance of PUFA as it brings only examples in which PUFA gives some positive effect or increases fitness

comments.issue: An example is requested and the cited 1953 Simpson reference is missing from the bibliography.
comments.request: Give an example and add the missing reference.
comments.quote: Page 4 line 28– please give an example. The 1953 Simpson reference is missing in the bibliography.

comments.issue: A conclusive statement about fitness variation lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Support the statement with strong references.
comments.quote: Such a conclusive statement needs few strong references to be supported.

comments.issue: The claim that terrestrial consumers are fundamentally limited by EPA and DHA may be wrong.
comments.request: Specify or cite details on terrestrial consumer adaptations.
comments.quote: I’m not sure this is right – for many terrestrial consumers there is no need for EPA and DHA.

comments.issue: Why peroxidation is more significant in terrestrial environments is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism behind greater terrestrial peroxidation.
comments.quote: why peroxidation is more significant in the terrestrial environment?

comments.issue: Latitude as a driver of marine DHA and EPA abundance is not mentioned.

title: The evolutionary ecology of fatty‐acid variation: Implications for consumer adaptation and diversification

study.system: tritrophic food web model; body size and mesohabitat productivity

editor_summary: Two relatively positive reviews; the first reviewer's concerns require major revision; the second reviewer notes the lack of associated code, which Ecology Letters requires to be available.

reviews.assessment: Deeply thought-provoking and a pleasure to read; the simplification is warranted, but the model code must be released.
strengths: warranted simplification of food webs to modules

comments.issue: No model code is associated with or publicly released, preventing reproduction and further investigation.
comments.request: Deposit the code in a repository such as Zenodo or figshare.
comments.quote: My only concern about the manuscript is that there is no code associated or publicly released.

reviews.assessment: Relevant and potentially important model study with well-supported conclusions, but key assumptions need discussion and further analysis.
strengths: conclusions well supported by model analyses
generally well written with a logical structure

comments.issue: The question is not entirely novel, though still of considerable interest.
comments.request: Position the work relative to classic contributions such as Post et al. 2000.
comments.quote: The question is not entirely novel (classic related contributions are e.g. Post et al. 2000), but would still be of considerable interest to readers interested in community ecology.

comments.issue: The Discussion lacks an explanation of the mechanisms causing the observed patterns and of how assumptions affect conclusions.
comments.request: Explain why the results occur and how assumptions shape them.
comments.quote: Discussion: lacks an explanation of why the results occur (i.e. the mechanisms) and most importantly, a discussion of how the model assumptions affect the outcome and thus the conclusions.

comments.issue: The no-maintenance assumption makes large individuals competitively superior and likely shapes the coexistence results.
comments.request: Complement the analyses with maintenance costs or thoroughly discuss the consequences.

comments.issue: The methods imply individuals can both grow and reproduce on the same ingested energy, using it twice.

comments.issue: The lack of predator size-structure and the size-selective predation are not discussed as drivers of the results.
