title: Resilience or Catastrophe? A possible state change for monarch butterflies in western North America

study.system: migratory birds of the Americas; optimal-redistribution model vs tracking and banding data

editor_summary: All reviews see potential but raise substantial concerns: clarify density dependence and the ideal free distribution, explain the model to avoid circularity, address data biases, and show effect sizes rather than only significant correlations.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important framework with a good fit, but the abundance-equals-carrying-capacity assumption and sampling bias may make the result circular.
strengths: important framework for predicting migratory connectivity
allows identifying deviations from the expected pattern

comments.issue: Abundance is unlikely to equal carrying capacity on the non-breeding grounds, especially at continental scales.
comments.request: Justify or relax the abundance-equals-carrying-capacity assumption.
comments.quote: Therefore, it seems unlikely that abundance = carrying capacity on the non-breeding ground.

comments.issue: Good fit may be circular: samples over-represent high-density areas that are also classified as high carrying capacity.
comments.request: Show that the fit is not an artifact of sampling bias.
comments.quote: The consequence of this is then that the observed connectivity is not arising because more birds move to the areas of highest carrying capacity, but instead because a greater proportion of the sample comes from high density areas.

comments.issue: If abundance-equals-carrying-capacity holds mainly in Central America, the theory becomes less general.
comments.request: Discuss the generality of the assumption across regions.
comments.quote: Land area is less in Central America so perhaps abundance=carrying capacity much more in this region. If that is a special case though then this makes the theory less general.

comments.issue: The ideal free distribution requires perfect knowledge, which cannot apply to juveniles on their first migration.
comments.request: Reframe or justify the IDF assumption, for example as a simple null model.
comments.quote: How can these be a reasonable assumption when juveniles arrive after their first migration in an area where they can have no prior knowledge

comments.issue: Ringing recoveries reflect observer distribution rather than actual bird distribution, and this bias is not mentioned.
comments.request: Acknowledge and address biases in ringing data.
comments.quote: recoveries better reflect distribution of observers or people rather than actual distributions

comments.issue: Tracking and genetic data differ greatly in spatial resolution, which may affect model precision and is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how variable data resolution affects the models.
comments.quote: Tracking studies give variable accuracy of non-breeding locations, and the accuracy for the genetic data is at much lower resolution.

comments.issue: Unclear whether the effect of data type on correlation strength was tested as an interaction.
comments.request: Test correlation strength as a function of data type.
comments.quote: Was this tested with a main effect of data type or as an interaction, whether the strength of the correlation between breeding and non-breeding distribution depended on data type?

comments.issue: Criteria for selecting the 24 species are unclear and many recent available datasets were not used.
comments.request: Clarify species inclusion criteria and why newer datasets were omitted.
comments.quote: The criteria for the choice of 24 species is not clear.

comments.issue: The assumption that local abundance indicates local energy supply is tenuous at continental scales.
comments.request: Justify the abundance-energy-supply assumption at large scales.
comments.quote: if there is a further assumption resting on this that abundance = energy supply, the whole seems to become very tenuous

comments.issue: The role of assumption (iv) on density dependence in the model is not explained.
comments.request: Explain what assumption (iv) does in the model.
comments.quote: Assumption (iv) is in there to capture density dependence? So not all individuals end up in the one best area?

comments.issue: Stronger correlations for high-connectivity species may again reflect where tracked individuals are sampled.
comments.request: Check whether this result is also driven by sampling bias.
comments.quote: Where there is a higher density of species, then any tracked individuals are more likely to have this as their location when tracked

comments.issue: That energy efficiency defines migration patterns is not novel; the value lies in explaining deviations.
comments.request: Reframe the contribution around deviations from the energy-efficiency pattern.
comments.quote: This is not novel or the value of the approach in this paper - if it works. The value is identifying deviations from this, and the circumstances that lead to the deviations.

reviews.assessment: Valuable and exciting approach, but the energy framing, unclear null models and missing effect sizes need to be addressed.

comments.issue: The manuscript is framed as energy optimization, but the model really minimizes distance; the energy claim oversells it.
comments.request: Reframe the model in terms of distance minimization.
comments.quote: I think it would be more clear to talk about distance minimization rather than energy as we know from various resources multiple other factors have to be taken into account

comments.issue: Assumptions behind the three null models are hard to understand from the text.
comments.request: Explain each null model and its real-world counterpart.
comments.quote: I have some trouble completely comprehending form the text assumptions behind these models

comments.issue: Null model 2 does not preserve the winter distribution and seems unrealistic and uninformative.
comments.request: Justify or drop null model 2.
comments.quote: First I think model two is a rather strange model as it does not really maintain the consistency of the distribution in the wintering grounds.

comments.issue: Only significance relative to null models is shown; effect sizes and distance distributions are missing.
comments.request: Report effect sizes and distributions of distances for all models.
comments.quote: I do however think it is important to not only show significance but also provide the reader with an idea of effect size and how different these models are.

comments.issue: The statement that predictions are accurate is not supported without a measure of accuracy or effect size.
comments.request: Provide an accuracy measure before claiming accurate predictions.
comments.quote: As long as there is no clear insight in the effect sizes it is not possible to back up the statement that the predictions are "accurate".

comments.issue: The grid used and its linear resolution are not specified.
comments.request: Name the grid (e.g. ISEA3H resolution 7) and give its linear resolution.
comments.quote: Please mention the name of the grid used (e.g. ISEA3H resolution 7), it would also be good to mention a linear measurement of the resolution

comments.issue: Sentences about relative abundance are very hard to follow.
comments.request: Rephrase these sentences more clearly.
comments.quote: I had to read these sentences 3 times to understand them, It would be good to phrase this more clearly.

comments.issue: Averaging abundance over grid cells that partly cover sea may inflate coastal densities; summing may be needed.
comments.request: Reconsider summing relative abundances instead of averaging.
comments.quote: should in the first step the relative abundances not be summed as now the mean of a grid cell that partially covers seas would also be virtually applied to this area

comments.issue: Rationale for excluding low-distance and non-migrating individuals is missing, though the model should predict them.
comments.request: Explain why non-migrating individuals are excluded.
comments.quote: Please provide the logic why these low distance/non-migrating individuals are excluded. I do not see why the model should not predict these.

comments.issue: Location errors reach about 4000 km, nearly full ranges, and may distort the validation.
comments.request: Consider excluding samples with large location errors.
comments.quote: I think some of these errors are rather big (up to 4000 km) and correspond to nearly full ranges. Would it be valuable to omit samples with high errors?

comments.issue: IDF assumptions for the breeding and wintering ranges are not needed because distributions are taken as given.
comments.request: Clarify why these assumptions are included.
comments.quote: As the distributions in the ranges are taken as a given I am not sure if these assumptions corresponding to the IDF in the ranges are really needed.

comments.issue: The energy-equals-distance assumption is strong and its cited support is weak.
comments.request: Strengthen support for the energy-distance assumption.
comments.quote: This is a rather strong assumption that definitely warrants backing up. I do not know the Somveille paper but at least the Wikelski paper does not seem a strong supporter of this assumption

comments.issue: Faster EMD implementations (FastEmd) are not mentioned and could allow finer grids.
comments.request: Mention FastEmd and its ecological applications.
comments.quote: Besides mentioning the EMD it might also be worth mentioning the FastEmd (pele 2009 and its application in ecology kranstauber 2017) as these might allow for faster calculation of finer grids.

comments.issue: The validation figure S3 is hard to understand in the supplement and would work better in the main text.
comments.request: Bring Fig. S3 into the main text.
comments.quote: It might be worth bringing S3 into the main text as it makes it much easier to understand the validation.

comments.issue: Validation locations are highly non-random, biased by banding effort, special interest and human population density.
comments.request: Discuss how these biases affect model evaluation.
comments.quote: the locations of the validation data are likely highly non-randomly distributed. Biases could originate from the distribution of banding effort, the special interest in a specific population with banding or tracking.

comments.issue: These results depend on the exact EMD implementation and discretization and may not be biological.
comments.request: Back up or omit these results and the S12 maps.
comments.quote: I do wonder how valuable these results are as they are very dependent on the exact implementation and discretization setting. They assume no error redistribution of birds.

comments.issue: Right-hand panels of Figs S5-S7 lack a 1:1 aspect ratio and a reference line.
comments.request: Fix the aspect ratio to 1:1 and add a 1:1 line.
comments.quote: For the most right plots it would be good to fix the aspect ratio to 1:1 as it eases comparison. Furthermore, the addition of a 1:1 line might help spot deviations from the expected.

reviews.assessment: Really nice, well-written analysis addressing an important gap; main suggestions concern validation metrics and transferability.
strengths: approach of interest to ecologists more widely

comments.issue: The Mantel validation metric tests migratory distance, not direction, and p-values are uninformative.
comments.request: Present rM distributions per null model and direction metrics, plus a connectivity-strength test.
comments.quote: I'm not totally convinced by the main validation metric presented in Fig 2 and Table 2 (Mantel correlation coefficient between empirical and simulated pairwise distances between breeding and wintering grounds)

comments.issue: The discussion lacks testable hypotheses about barriers, winds, social transmission or species traits.
comments.request: Add hypotheses about factors expected to improve or worsen model performance.
comments.quote: It would be nice to see some simple hypotheses presented in the discussion relating to how your model could be used to understand the importance of barriers, headwinds, social transmission, etc.

comments.issue: Transferability of ORSIM to other flyways is unclear because eBird abundance maps are unavailable elsewhere.
comments.request: Discuss transferability and whether simpler versions are possible.
comments.quote: How transferable is ORSIM to other systems / flyways? The eBird abundance maps which form the basis of ORSIM are not, to my knowledge, available for other parts of the world due to data sparsity.

comments.issue: The definition of species-specific annual cycles is not given.
comments.request: Explain how annual cycles were defined.
comments.quote: How were species-specific annual cycles defined? Also L129, L131

comments.issue: Constraint (4) is not explained well enough to follow.
comments.request: Explain constraint (4) more clearly.
comments.quote: I don't follow constraint (4), so this may need more explanation

comments.issue: Terminology mixes empirical "locations" with simulated "sites".
comments.request: Use consistent terminology throughout.
comments.quote: In Fig S3 you refer to empirical "locations" and simulated "sites" - but here in the main text the terminology is mixed.

comments.issue: The text refers to panel c of Fig. S3, but that panel does not exist.
comments.request: Fix the panel reference or add the missing panel.
comments.quote: L272 There is no panel c in Fig S3.

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: "an hexagon" should be "a hexagon", and caption cross-references are wrong.
comments.quote: L125 Replace "an hexagon" with "a hexagon"

title: A general theory of avian migratory connectivity

study.system: avian haemosporidian parasites in wild birds; Western Ghats field survey

reviews.assessment: Important question and exciting results, but the competence measure, missing vector data and results presentation leave key claims unconvincing.
strengths: large dataset across a large spatial scale

comments.issue: The abstract does not convey what was done.
comments.request: Add specifics of the methods and results to the abstract.
comments.quote: Based on this abstract, I have no idea what you did. Please include more information about the specific methods and results of this study

comments.issue: Methods are not linked back to the main question.
comments.request: Explain why each method was chosen relative to the question.
comments.quote: As you describe your methods, please link them back to your main question throughout so that readers know why you are choosing specific methods.

comments.issue: Results are a long list of significant values rather than a biological discussion.
comments.request: Reorganize results and lead with the specialist versus generalist question.
comments.quote: These results would be stronger if you reorganized them as a biological discussion, rather than a long list of significant values.

comments.issue: The 'Results and Discussion' section contains no discussion.
comments.request: Add actual discussion to the section.
comments.quote: You have a section labeled “Results and Discussion” However I see no discussion in this section.

comments.issue: The community competence measure is questionable, and it is unclear whether it is separate for the two parasite genera.
comments.request: Clarify and justify the community competence measure for each genus.
comments.quote: I’m unconvinced that the measure for community competence is appropriate. First, it is unclear whether there is a separate measure of community competence for plasmodium vs. haemoproteus

comments.issue: Figure 2 red and green colours are indistinguishable to colourblind readers.
comments.request: Choose different colours for Figure 2.
comments.quote: The red and green colors look identical to colorblind individuals. Please choose different colors.

comments.issue: Figure 2 variable labels such as HPP and HCCH are not descriptive.
comments.request: Use more descriptive variable labels.
comments.quote: Please choose more descriptive variable labels. Labels like “HPP”, “HCCH”, etc. make it very difficult to interpret figures.

comments.issue: No figure demonstrates that Haemoproteus is more specialist than Plasmodium in these data.
comments.request: Add a figure showing host numbers per parasite genus.
comments.quote: Please include a figure demonstrating how the Haemoproteus genera is more of a specialist than the Plasmodium genera.

comments.issue: Vector data are completely absent, so the mechanistic understanding sought cannot be achieved.
comments.request: Include vector information or discuss its implications.
comments.quote: For all the data the authors have on bird hosts and landscape variables, the lack of vector data is a glaring omission.

comments.issue: Line-level edits: missing word at L93, query about '4 major categories' at L448, missing parenthesis at L139.
comments.quote: Line 93: missing a word Line 448: 4 major categories? Line 139: missing a parenthesis

reviews.assessment: Likes the concept and question, but doubts the specialist/generalist classification, sampling representativeness and missing vector context.
strengths: likes the overall concept of the study

comments.issue: Sentence implies direct effects of human disturbance on disease dynamics, but effects can only be indirect.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence to reflect indirect pathways.
comments.quote: Maybe I am being picky here but human disturbances cannot impact directly disease dynamics, it can be only indirect.

comments.issue: Vectors, the key actors in this parasite system, are not discussed, although the two genera have different vectors.
comments.request: Discuss how disturbance affects vectors and may explain parasite patterns.
comments.quote: I would like to add here that authors did not talk at all about the vectors, which are the key actors in the parasite system used in this study

comments.issue: Host specificity is treated as a dichotomy, but specialization is a continuum, and a species can be specialist in one community and generalist in another.
comments.request: Replace the specialist/generalist dichotomy with a continuous host specificity index.
comments.quote: Specialization is not black or white; it is rather a gradient, a continuum from highly specialist to highly generalist, with a lot of grey in between.

comments.issue: 'Avian malaria' is correct for Plasmodium but not for Haemoproteus, which is a haemosporidian parasite.
comments.request: Use the correct terminology for Haemoproteus.
comments.quote: Avian malaria is the right term for the genus Plasmodium, but I think it’s not correct for Haemoproteus.

comments.issue: The ū in Valkiūnas is incorrect at line 83.
comments.request: Correct the spelling of Valkiūnas.
comments.quote: Line 83. Correct the ū in Valkiūnas

comments.issue: Characterizing whole genera as specialist or generalist ignores within-genus variation in host number.
comments.request: Account for variation in host specificity within each genus.
comments.quote: However when looking at the MalAvi database, Haemoproteus can still show variation in the number of host infected (from 1 to 24)

comments.issue: Many studies on ecological and phylogenetic drivers of host specificity are not cited.
comments.request: Cite more studies, e.g. Loiseau et al. 2012, Clark and Clegg 2017, Fecchio et al. 2019, Ellis et al. 2020.
comments.quote: I think there are many other studies (other than Fallon et al 2005) that found different kind of patterns related to both ecological variables and phylogenetic relationships of host

comments.issue: It is not explained how host specificity was calculated; the genera were simply assumed to be specialist and generalist.
comments.request: Describe the host specificity analysis and consider a continuous index.
comments.quote: we do not know how they calculated the host specificity of parasites. Authors directly assumed that Haemoproteus are specialists and Plasmodium are generalists, but they do not give information about the variability

comments.issue: With 1172 samples across 28 species and 42 sites, many species have few samples, so recovered diversity is likely unrepresentative.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited per-site sampling and its effects.
comments.quote: Authors collected 1172 samples for 28 species in 42 sites, which means that a lot of species has probably few samples per site and therefore the diversity recovered is probably not representative of the parasite communities.

comments.issue: Raw observed data ignore sampling effort and rare lineages, biasing parasite diversity estimates.
comments.request: Use Chao estimators of diversity instead of raw figures.
comments.quote: Using the observed data does not take into account differences in sampling effort, particularly when many rare lineages might occur and could introduce biases.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether year and season effects on prevalence were controlled.
comments.request: Report how year and season were handled in prevalence analyses.
comments.quote: It is possible that prevalence will vary through time but I do not see the information about controlling for the year and/or season effect?

comments.issue: The measure of bird species susceptibility to parasites is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how susceptibility was assessed.
comments.quote: I would appreciate to have more information about this measure of susceptibility of each bird species to parasite. How is the susceptibility assessed exactly?

comments.issue: Prior research on land-use change and avian blood parasites is undercited, making the topic seem unexplored.
comments.request: Cite more previous work on avian blood parasites.
comments.quote: I think the authors do not cite enough previous research work; especially all the studies that have been done on avian blood parasites.

comments.issue: The claim that the data support the hypothesis is too assertive given the weak host specificity characterization.
comments.request: Soften the claim or better justify the lineage groupings.
comments.quote: I would not be that assertive (i.e. saying that their data support the hypothesis), because to my point of view, authors are not doing the best job in characterizing the host specificity

title: Anthropogenic disturbance favours generalist over specialist parasites in bird communities: Implications for risk of disease emergence

study.system: arthropod crop pests; pesticides and natural enemies; models and meta-analysis

editor_summary: Editor says three expert reviews raise concerns that must be considered: the quality of the meta-analysis and its real-world applicability need clarifying, the discussion needs more nuance, and the data and analysis more transparency.

reviews.assessment: In-depth and interesting modelling study, but meta-analysis conclusions overreach and the discussion is weak and insufficiently contextualized.

comments.issue: The meta-analysis shows pesticide ineffectiveness, not pest resurgence as the models predict.
comments.request: Temper the claim that the meta-analysis confirms the model predictions.
comments.quote: the meta-analysis results do not provide evidence of pest resurgence as their models predict, but only for the ineffectiveness of pesticides in the presence of natural enemies

comments.issue: The 'no-predator' class is unreliable because unreported enemies may still be present.
comments.request: Address this limitation and temper conclusions from the meta-analysis.
comments.quote: absence of recorded natural enemies does not imply proof of their absence

comments.issue: Boundary conditions (tightly linked short-generation systems; greenhouse versus open crops) are not stated up front.
comments.request: State the boundary conditions from the introduction.
comments.quote: All these boundary conditions would need to be stated in the introduction from the start.

comments.issue: Applicability to mixed specialist-generalist communities and longer-generation pests and predators is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss these limits to generality.
comments.quote: The implications of pest control in mixed specialist and generalist predator communities and potential application of results to the many pests and predators with longer generation times

comments.issue: The stage-structured third model is hard to interpret and adds little beyond the first two models.
comments.request: Remove it or move it to the supplementary materials.
comments.quote: The manuscript would benefit from its removal (or moving to supplementary materials) to better streamline

comments.issue: Figure 4 effect sizes are relative with no predator-present treatment within the same study, giving a misleading impression.
comments.request: Clarify the comparability of effect sizes.
comments.quote: The effect size is relative and possibly the abundances are higher when no predators are present, but this cannot be ascertained since there is no predator-present treatment in the same study.

comments.issue: Discussion conclusions are not clearly linked to results and read as cherry-picking.
comments.request: Rewrite with transparent caveats and tempered conclusions.
comments.quote: the conclusions made in the discussion are not clearly linked to the results

comments.issue: Results are not placed in the broader conservation biological control and community ecology literature.
comments.request: Contextualize the findings in this literature.
comments.quote: the authors fail to put their results into the broader context of what is understood from the huge amount of conservation biological control, pest control and indirect interaction/community ecology literature

comments.issue: Page numbers restart on every page.
comments.request: Use continuous page numbers.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if page numbers were continuous rather than restarting every page.

comments.issue: Colour schemes are not accessible, including for colour-blind readers.
comments.request: Use accessible colour schemes.
comments.quote: Color schemes need to be changed to be more accessible (also to color blind persons).

comments.issue: The apparent competition-mutualism continuum is not connected to the study's hypotheses and conclusions.
comments.request: Discuss it or remove it.
comments.quote: how does the theory that apparent competition and apparent mutualism are on a continuum with each other and may in fact drift back and forth depending on community size and structure affect your hypotheses/conclusions?

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: L51 repeated phrase, pg11 typo, delete 'could be', 'therefore', 'furthermore', 'a slight', period after S2, 'reinvade', '(negative)', and missing words around B and D.
comments.quote: L51 pg5 typo- delete replicate “so-called apparent competition or apparent mutualism”

comments.issue: Citations are needed to support the equilibrium density statement at pg 9.
comments.request: Add supporting citations.
comments.quote: More citations are needed here to support this statement as based on model results

comments.issue: The sources of temperature data are unstated.
comments.request: Report the temperature data sources.
comments.quote: what were the sources of temperature data?

comments.issue: The sources of pest generation times are unclear and possibly unreliable.
comments.request: Use peer-reviewed sources and be consistent.
comments.quote: what sources did you use to find generation times of pests? Peer reviewed is more reliable than “the web”.

comments.issue: 'Moderators' should be 'fixed effects' (pg 13 L30 and L43).
comments.request: Use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: use fixed effects rather than “moderators”, delete factors

comments.issue: The random-effect time structure and continuous autoregressive model are unclear.
comments.request: Cite a method reference and explain the model.
comments.quote: time as a random effect and continuous autoregressive model used. This is a bit unclear. Cite method reference.

comments.issue: The claim that the meta-analysis largely supports model predictions is questionable.
comments.request: Clarify or temper this statement.
comments.quote: meta-analysis largely supports the theoretical model predictions

comments.issue: How many time series the 12 come from is unstated.
comments.request: Report the total number of time series.
comments.quote: Pg 15 L 36, 12 time series out of how many?

comments.issue: The pg 15 reference to model simulations is unclear and lacks figure pointers.
comments.request: Clarify and refer to the relevant figures.
comments.quote: simulations from the theoretical mode? Clarify, refer to relevant figures here.

comments.issue: Which natural enemies have the shorter life cycle is unclear; many predators live longer than their prey.
comments.request: Give examples and clarify.
comments.quote: which natural enemies (examples) are reflected by this shorter life cycle?

comments.issue: Pg 16 L40-55 lacks reference to the literature.
comments.request: Add relevant references.
comments.quote: Pg 16 L40-55 this section needs a lot more reference to the literature

comments.issue: The assumption of immediate negative pesticide effects is not always true.
comments.request: Acknowledge variable and delayed effects with references.
comments.quote: it is not necessarily true that pesticide use will have an immediate negative effect on pest densities

comments.issue: The claim that non-native arthropods are impervious to native predators is wrong.
comments.request: Correct the claim and cite relevant literature.
comments.quote: It is not at all the case that all non-native arthropods are impervious to native predators.

comments.issue: More citations are needed at pg 17 L33.
comments.request: Cover the known literature.
comments.quote: Pg 17 L 33 More citations needed in this section.

comments.issue: 'Solid lines' is clearer than 'drawn curves' in legends and text.
comments.request: Use 'solid' versus 'broken' consistently.
comments.quote: solid lines rather than drawn curves is a clearer word choice (solid vs broken lines)

comments.issue: Line-type terminology varies (broken, interrupted, dashed).
comments.request: Use one consistent term.
comments.quote: be consistent between, broken, interrupted and dashed throughout manuscript when referring to line types

comments.issue: The pg 24 figure caption is confusing and should describe effects on density and long-term averages.
comments.request: Rewrite the caption as suggested.
comments.quote: Pg24 L20 Confusing sentence and structure, suggest “The effect of natural enemy presence and pesticide application method on pesticide efficacy.

comments.issue: Figure 2 is confusing: third column mixes averaged stages, panels G-I are unclear, and x-axis scales differ.
comments.request: Clarify and align the figure.
comments.quote: confused about figure 2. Why is the third column using average of diff stages of pest vs the predator sensitive stage of the stage structured pest model?

comments.issue: Figure 3 panel letters are inconsistently placed and x-axis scales differ.
comments.request: Standardize panel labels and axis scales.

comments.issue: Figure 4 parentheses, axis labels and label placement need clarification.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and thoughtful, but wants more nuanced framing on effective enemies and is concerned about the small-plot scale of the meta-analysis.

title: Pesticides do not significantly reduce arthropod pest densities in the presence of natural enemies

study.system: species abundance distributions; ~22,000 empirical communities

editor_summary: Appreciated but critical concerns: introduction too technical and needs more ecological focus; sampling variance in small samples must be addressed, e.g. by resampling.

reviews.assessment: Convincing large-scale analysis of SAD deviations; minor requests on assumptions, the N:S ratio and clarity.
strengths: addresses important issue of separating ecological processes from statistical artifacts
large number of datasets convincingly analysed
useful conclusions on deviation patterns and system size

comments.issue: Alternative assumptions about species and individual uniqueness may affect evenness and skewness.
comments.request: Discuss how uniqueness assumptions would change the results.
comments.quote: It would be nice if the authors could address (speculate on), in the Discussion, the issue of how alternative assumptions about uniqueness might influence evenness and skewness.

comments.issue: Whether deviations relate to the ratio of individuals to species is not explored.
comments.request: Discuss any pattern between deviation and the N:S ratio.
comments.quote: Do the authors see any pattern in the relationship between deviation from feasible set and that ratio?

comments.issue: The first sentence of the introduction is awkward and uses a plural verb.
comments.request: Rewrite it with 'the number' as singular.
comments.quote: The first sentence in the Introduction is a bit awkward.

comments.issue: The axes of the hollow-curve SAD plot are not stated.
comments.request: State explicitly what x and y are.
comments.quote: The authors should state explicitly what x and y are.

comments.issue: Excluding S = N, S = N+1 and S = 1 systems appears incompatible with N = 3.
comments.request: Explain how N can be as small as 3.
comments.quote: If you exclude systems with S = N or S = N+1, and systems with S = 1, then how can you have an N as small as 3

reviews.assessment: Potentially useful contribution, but sampling variance is ignored and the magnitude of the deviations is unclear.
strengths: uses the Locey & White expected distributions
could be a very useful contribution

comments.issue: Abundances are treated as fixed, ignoring sampling variance that could swamp the subtle deviations.
comments.request: Use Monte Carlo or jackknife resampling to quantify sampling variability.
comments.quote: The fundamental issue, then, is whether the relatively subtle differences seen here fall inside or outside of the cloud of responses obtained when allowing abundance lists to vary.

comments.issue: The variance explained by the deviations is not reported, so biological relevance is unclear.
comments.request: Report how much variance the deviations account for.
comments.quote: Nowhere did I see any indication of just how much variance is being accounted for in these deviations from expected.

comments.issue: Simpson's index weights abundant species and is used without justification.
comments.request: Defend the choice and test robustness across evenness metrics.
comments.quote: No rationale is given for why Simpson's Index is solely used to document evenness.

comments.issue: Background literature is too recent and misses key statistical-mechanics work.
comments.request: Cite earlier work such as Preston, Maurer and Nekola & Brown.
comments.quote: the background literature for this topic really needs to be broadened

reviews.assessment: Novel, well-written and statistically sound; two broad suggestions to broaden ecological relevance and add a power figure.
strengths: novel push to understand sample size in SADs
well written, easy to follow and statistically sound
within scope of Ecology Letters and a great contribution

comments.issue: The manuscript is narrow and does not link statistical deviations to ecological interpretation.
comments.request: Expand ecological interpretation of skewness, evenness and rare species.
comments.quote: Currently, while it is interesting and novel – the pitch of the manuscript is rather narrow, focused on the statistical deviations of the feasible set.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the 50-100 individual guideline was determined.
comments.request: Explain how the small-community threshold was determined.
comments.quote: However, it isn't immediately clear to a reader how this was determined.

comments.issue: A key figure showing statistical power against community size is missing.
comments.request: Add a size-versus-power scatter plot for all ~22,000 communities.
comments.quote: I do believe that there is a key figure missing to immediately illustrate the point made in the abstract and throughout the paper

comments.issue: Data and code are only released after acceptance.
comments.request: Make data and code available with submission.
comments.quote: I would have liked to see the link to the data/code available with submission.

comments.issue: Important feasible-set sampling details are hidden in Appendix S3.
comments.request: Move the GitHub sampling details into the main text.
comments.quote: I think some of the details from Appendix S3 describing the neat-looking GitHub feasible set sampling could be moved to the main text

title: Empirical abundance distributions are more uneven than expected given their statistical baseline

study.system: European butterflies; reflectance spectra and climatic niche data

reviews.assessment: Liked the study and found the analyses adequate, but the climatic-variable selection and partial interpretation of the climate axes need clarification.
strengths: photographic approach to retrieve reflectance values

comments.issue: The selection of the nine climatic niche variables is not justified; other factors such as humidity are ignored.
comments.request: Develop the reasoning for the variable selection with more detail.
comments.quote: one of the major concerns is the selection of the nine climatic niche variables. Why only those, and no other factors (e.g. humidity)?

comments.issue: PC1 and PC2 are interpreted partially; solar radiation, water vapour pressure and precipitation seasonality are ignored.
comments.request: Address all loadings driving PC1 and PC2, not only temperature.
comments.quote: I find it hard to state that PC1 is a proxy for only temperature. In the same vein, why omitting the strong negative effect of precipitation seasonality for PC2?

comments.issue: Body size is analysed but never introduced despite its role in thermoregulation.
comments.request: Add a paragraph on body size in the introduction.
comments.quote: I strongly recommend including a paragraph or at least address this variable in introduction due to its regulative role on the thermal balance of organisms

comments.issue: The UV, Vis and NIR spectral ranges are depicted incorrectly or confusingly.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction between human and animal visual ranges from the start.
comments.quote: I urge the authors to clarify since the beginning of the manuscript the distinction between human Vis range and the studied animal Vis range

comments.issue: The atypical photographic acquisition procedure is not illustrated.
comments.request: Show a step-by-step diagram, in the supplement if space is limited.
comments.quote: Given the atypical acquisition methodology, I believe it will tremendously help to show a diagram depicting the step-by-step acquisition procedure of this technique

comments.issue: Discussion statements are not linked to the corresponding table outputs.
comments.request: Reference the relevant table outputs when discussing specific results.
comments.quote: when addressing specific results, it would be useful to reference the corresponding table outputs for a better interpretation

comments.issue: 'Climate' in the abstract is too broad and unspecified.
comments.request: Be specific about the climatic factors retrieved.
comments.quote: Climate is a broad term that includes multitude, and, to a certain extent, contrasting factors

comments.issue: The word 'pivotal' for body regions is confusing, as all regions influence thermal balance.
comments.request: Say the regions were previously shown to be pivotal.
comments.quote: I find the word pivotal confusing. Why the head would not be that important?

comments.issue: The link between camouflage and hotter, more humid regions is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how camouflage relates to these climatic regions.
comments.quote: I do not really see how camouflage relates to hotter and more humid regions

comments.issue: The visible spectrum is described as extending below 380 nm, which is incorrect.
comments.request: Correct the visible spectrum range.
comments.quote: the visible spectrum spans from 380 (400)-to-700 nm ca.. For sure not below 380 nm, which is the UV range

comments.issue: 'Direct sunlight' is used where sun's energy-rich radiation is meant.
comments.request: Use the term sun's energy-rich radiation.
comments.quote: did the authors mean sun’s energy-rich radiation instead of direct sunlight?

comments.issue: The strong statement that Vis-NIR reflectance has only been examined for thermal ecology ignores earlier work.
comments.request: Review the literature and rephrase the statement.
comments.quote: Hutchinson and Larimer (1960)* investigated the effect of the Vis-NIR range on the coloration of lizards, linking it to solar irradiance

comments.issue: Generalising Australia as hot and dry ignores its many climate zones.
comments.request: Specify the study areas supporting the hot and dry characterisation.
comments.quote: I find it hard to generalize that Australia is a hot and dry continent (country). There are many different climate zones in Australia

comments.issue: The phrase 'light manipulation' on line 78 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant by light manipulation.
comments.quote: Line 78: light manipulation? As for integument reflectance? Please clarify this.

comments.issue: All butterflies are ectotherms, so saying 'primarily ectotherms' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether other mechanisms are involved.
comments.quote: are not butterflies all ectotherms? Why primarily ectotherms? Are there other mechanisms?

comments.issue: The distinction between dorsal, lateral and ventral regions is unclear, and 'both' is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clearly define the body regions and what 'both' refers to.
comments.quote: the distinction between dorsal, lateral, and ventral regions are not clear, especially to a non-butterfly expert

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the ventral reflectance prediction is specific to butterflies.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of the prediction.
comments.quote: there are few studies in the literature indicating that high ventral reflectance in reptiles may be selected for cooling in heat-stress environments

comments.issue: Stating only 'whether climate predicts the reflectance' is too vague.
comments.request: Provide the general climate variables measured in the study.
comments.quote: provide general climate variables that have been measured in this study

comments.issue: 'Controlling for phylogeny' is technically incorrect; phylogeny is accounted for, not controlled.
comments.request: Reword the phylogeny statement.
comments.quote: technically we do not control for a phylogeny, but we account for it

comments.issue: The claim that the data cover 70% of all European species lacks a reference.
comments.request: Add a supporting reference.
comments.quote: of all species found in Europe”. Consider adding a reference here.

comments.issue: Climate information is placed in the photography methods paragraph.
comments.request: Start methods with a 'Species selection and collection' paragraph.
comments.quote: I do not see the reason to have information on average temperature and precipitation, in a paragraph called “photography”

comments.issue: How the overlap between visible and NIR spectral ranges was treated is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how spectral range variations were handled.
comments.quote: I see there is a small overlap between the visible and NIR spectral ranges. How those were treated in the analyses?

comments.issue: The statement that NIR is approximately 80% of solar irradiation lacks a reference.
comments.request: Add a supporting reference.
comments.quote: It is quite an important statement, which requires a reference to support this.

comments.issue: The reason for filter-specific shutter speeds is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how shutter speeds were chosen for replicability.
comments.quote: Was a light meter used to select different shutter speeds? It would be nice to see a brief explanation for that, as future studies will not be able to replicate the methods without knowing such details.

comments.issue: The Dcraw version is not specified.
comments.request: State which version of Dcraw was used.
comments.quote: Line 154: which version of Dcraw?

comments.issue: The text implies only thorax-abdomen matters for thermoregulation, and head measurement is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the choice of measured body regions.
comments.quote: as it is written, it seems that only thorax-abdomen is important for thermoregulation; I do not think this was the intention of the authors

comments.issue: How pixel values were selected and averaged on body regions is not described.
comments.request: Describe the pixel selection and the software used.
comments.quote: how did the selection and averaging of pixel values take place on different body regions? Where these values were obtained from?

comments.issue: The concept of animal visual range is introduced only in the methods.
comments.request: Clarify the animal visual range early in the manuscript.
comments.quote: I urge the authors to clarify early in the manuscript the distinction between what we commonly assume as Vis spectral range and animal visual range

comments.issue: Whether wing area is a proxy for body size is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the body size proxy.
comments.quote: is the wing area a proxy for body size in butterflies? If so, please clarify this

comments.issue: The choice of the one-year-different time periods for distribution and climate data is not justified.
comments.request: State whether this was a data limitation or explain the choice.
comments.quote: It will be good to state if that is the case; alternatively, provide reasonings for the selection of this time period.

comments.issue: The phylogenetic tree is insufficiently described.
comments.request: Report the genes, taxa and whether the tree is ultrametric.
comments.quote: more information on the phylogenetic tree should be provided. For example, how many genes was it based on, how many taxa, was it ultrametric

comments.issue: 'High correlation' between Vis and NIR is undefined and unsupported.
comments.request: Provide the correlation method, coefficient and p-value, plus a supplementary figure.
comments.quote: what is a high correlation? Please provide both the method (e.g. Pearson, Spearman) and the associated coefficient and p-value.

comments.issue: Explained variance of PC1 and PC2 is not reported in the main text.
comments.request: Report the explained variance for both PCs in the main text.
comments.quote: please provide the explained variance for both PC1 and PC2 in the main text

comments.issue: Which variables were excluded from the model is unclear.
comments.request: List the excluded variables and reference the output table.
comments.quote: I am not sure I understand which other variables were excluded from the model

comments.issue: Low solar radiation and low water vapour pressure are omitted from the interpretation.
comments.request: Discuss these drivers alongside temperature.
comments.quote: But why omitting low solar radiation and low water vapour pressure?

comments.issue: 'No other variables remained significant' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what this statement refers to, e.g. size.
comments.quote: please clarify what “no other variables remained significant” refers to. Here perhaps no significance for size?

comments.issue: Tables S5-6 indicate only Vis VE is more robust than NIR VE, contradicting the text.
comments.request: Reconcile the text with the tables.
comments.quote: accordingly to tables S5-6, only Vis Ventral entire wing (VE) is more robust than NIR VE

comments.issue: Only hotter environments are discussed, omitting solar radiation and water vapour pressure.
comments.request: Include these drivers in the interpretation.
comments.quote: only hotter environments? what about high solar radiation and high water vapour pressure?

comments.issue: Only colder environments are discussed, again omitting solar radiation and water vapour pressure.
comments.request: Include these drivers in the interpretation.
comments.quote: Line 298: same as above, only colder environments? Also lower solar radiation and lower water vapour pressure.

comments.issue: A statement that did not test thermoregulation is placed in the results.

comments.quote: the last statement should be placed in discussion, as no analysis specifically tested for thermoregulation

comments.issue: The discussion does not summarise what was analysed and which climate variables were used.
comments.request: Add a brief summary in the first discussion paragraph.
comments.quote: I think that briefly summarizing in the first paragraph what was analysed, and which climate variables were considered will benefit the flow and understanding of discussion.

comments.issue: Effects of solar radiation and water vapour pressure are left out of the discussion.
comments.request: Discuss these effects.
comments.quote: why leaving out the effects of solar radiation and water vapour pressure?

comments.issue: The statement following 'however' does not contrast with the previous one.
comments.request: Remove or replace 'however'.
comments.quote: I do not see how the statement following “however” contrast with the previous one.

comments.issue: 'Clearly demonstrate' overstates the evidence because no direct thermal analyses were conducted.
comments.request: Replace with 'likely suggest'.
comments.quote: “clearly demonstrate” is too strong here, as no direct thermal analyses on butterflies were conducted in this study. Consider replacing with “likely suggest”.

comments.issue: Table 1 does not report any coefficient as implied by the text.
comments.request: Add the coefficients or correct the text.
comments.quote: Line 322: Table 1 does not report any coefficient.

comments.issue: Camouflage is suddenly introduced in the paragraph.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence to connect camouflage smoothly.
comments.quote: Camouflage is suddenly thrown in. I would rephrase this sentence

comments.issue: The link between warm humid environments and darker vegetation is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what drives the darkness of the environment.
comments.quote: why warm and humid environments would display darker vegetations? Is there a difference in plant reflectance across environments?

comments.issue: The sentence on lines 332-333 lacks a reference.
comments.request: Add a supporting reference.
comments.quote: this sentence (up to “spectrum”) needs a reference

comments.issue: The sentence about evolution and competing functions should be moved and reworded.
comments.request: Move it after 'benefits' and use the suggested rewording.
comments.quote: Given all this, the evolution of butterfly reflectance is likely to be affected by thermoregulation coupled with multiple competing functions, including camouflage and signaling

comments.issue: It is unclear why colour is described as independent of climate when PC1 and PC2 correlate with DE and VE.
comments.request: Reconcile this statement with the significant correlations.
comments.quote: why independent of climate? I understand why colour is not dependent on NIR reflectance, but why climate?

comments.issue: 'Cryptic NIR adaptions' is unclear.
comments.request: Define or rephrase 'cryptic NIR adaptions'.
comments.quote: Line 354: what are cryptic NIR adaptions? Unclear.

comments.issue: Why heat transfer should be greater for larger wings is not explained mechanistically.

comments.issue: The larger-species-reflect-less claim holds only when climate conditions are accounted for.
comments.request: Make the statement conditional on climate.
comments.quote: the statement that larger species have lower NIR reflectance than smaller species to modulate the amount of reflected energy is valid only if accounting for climate conditions

comments.issue: Table 1 caption does not identify the drivers of PC1 and PC2.
comments.request: Indicate the most influential drivers in the caption.
comments.quote: please indicate in the caption the most influential drivers of PC1 and PC2

comments.issue: Figure 1 caption and figure report different explained variance for PC1 (68% vs 57.2%).
comments.request: Reconcile the two values.
comments.quote: Caption of Figure 1 indicates that PC1 explains 68% of the variation, but within Figure 1 PC1 reports 57.2%. Please clarify.

comments.issue: The ancestral state visualisation lacks a time scale and panel labels.
comments.request: Add a time scale and label the panels.
comments.quote: Please provide a time scale in the ancestral state visualisation of Figure 1 (right panel). Also, it would be more convenient to label the two panels instead of referring “left-or-right panel”.

comments.issue: Mapping climatic PC1 in the tree and reflectance PC1 in heatmaps seems reversed.
comments.request: Swap the mapped variables if they were intended the other way.
comments.quote: I find no sense to have climatic PC1 mapped in tree and reflectance PC1 in heatmaps

comments.issue: Ancestral state reconstruction is not shown for PC2.
comments.request: Show the ancestral state reconstruction for PC2 as well.

comments.issue: Only temperature is reported although PC1 also reflects solar radiation and water vapour pressure.
comments.request: Report all PC1-associated drivers.
comments.quote: Why reporting only temperature (cold-warm gradient) when PC1 is also strongly associated with solar radiation and water vapour pressure?

comments.issue: Figure 3 labels PC1 as temperature although solar radiation and water vapour pressure also load strongly, and the same applies to PC2.
comments.request: Present all strongly associated drivers in the figure and text.
comments.quote: In figure 3, PC1 is associated with temperature, but in figure 1 and table S2, we can also see that solar radiation and water vapour pressure are strongly positively associated with PC1. Why only selecting temperature?

comments.issue: Table S5 omits size among the coefficients.
comments.request: Report size among the coefficients.
comments.quote: I believe it will help to report size among the coefficients to directly see the lack of significance of this variable

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits (misspelled author name; stray 'a' on line 316).
comments.quote: Trullas should read Clusella-Trullas.

reviews.assessment: Valuable separation of visible and near-infrared reflectance; most points are minor, with some clarifications needed.
strengths: phylogenetically controlled comparative methods appear sound
distinguishes the study from simple coloration-climate correlations

comments.issue: Altitude is absent from both the analysis and the discussion, although butterfly coloration is famously darker at high altitudes.
comments.request: Report collection altitudes and link them to the climatic data.
comments.quote: I was surprised to see nothing about altitude in either the analysis or the discussion

comments.issue: The rationale for ventral surfaces being more involved in cooling than heating is not explained in the introduction.

comments.quote: The explanation behind the prediction that ventral wing surfaces are more involved in cooling than heating needs expanding, and expanding here in the intro

comments.issue: It is not stated how many photographs were taken per butterfly.

comments.issue: What 'maximum' refers to on line 132 is unclear.

comments.quote: l.132. What does the ‘maximum’ refer to?

comments.issue: The wavelength values 60 and 360 do not match the stated ranges (400-320 and 700-320).

comments.issue: The climatic data may not represent the microhabitat a species actually experiences, e.g. canopy versus understory.

comments.quote: Just how specific are the climatic measurements to the niche of a particular species?

comments.issue: Reducing climatic variables with PCA may obscure the specific variables that Gloger's and Bogert's rules relate to.
comments.request: Justify the PCA against testing specific climatic variables.
comments.quote: Why reduce the climatic variables using PCA? Yes, the variables recorded will be correlated, but does that matter for the hypothesis under test?

comments.issue: MCC is not defined at first use.
comments.request: Define MCC at its first occurrence.
comments.quote: l.211. Define MCC where first used; here, not l. 215.

comments.issue: The claim that thermal benefits clearly drive reflectance patterns is too strong; alternatives are untested and correlation is not causation.

reviews.assessment: Valuable, robustly collected reflectance data and sound analyses, though the novelty is somewhat eroded by a related Australian study.
strengths: valuable data collected more robustly than guidebook-based studies
nice comparisons of visible and NIR reflectance and body regions
data collection and analyses well implemented

comments.issue: The novelty is somewhat eroded by a related analysis of Australian butterflies (Munro et al. 2019).
comments.request: Position the study relative to Munro et al. 2019.
comments.quote: However, the novelty is eroded somewhat by a related analysis of Australian butterflies (Munro et al 2019), but the data here cover a broader climate gradient.

comments.issue: The relationship to previous guidebook-colour analyses is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether the reflectance data correspond with guidebook-based analyses.
comments.quote: Might be worth discussing whether the reflectance data in the manuscript correspond with previous analysis based on color in guidebooks

comments.issue: Annual mean, minimum and maximum climatic variables averaged across ranges may be too coarse for the organism's experienced climate.

comments.quote: I wondered about the appropriateness of the relatively coarse climatic variables. Are annual mean, minimum, and maximum averaged across the range appropriate?

comments.issue: Climate predictor descriptions lack coefficients showing directionality.
comments.request: Include coefficients to indicate the direction of effects.
comments.quote: In the description of climate predictors, including coefficients to indicate directionality would aid interpretation.

comments.issue: The thermal implications of size in terms of cooling and thermal inertia are not discussed explicitly.
comments.request: Discuss cooling and thermal inertia more explicitly.
comments.quote: Would be helpful to discuss the thermal implications of size a bit more explicitly in terms of cooling and thermal inertia.

comments.issue: Whether species are dorsal or ventral baskers is not distinguished.
comments.request: Test whether delineating basking types strengthens the thermoregulation signal.
comments.quote: Is it feasible to delineate whether a subset of species are dorsal or ventral baskers to refine the reflectance comparison and strengthen thermoregulation as a mechanism?

comments.issue: Table 1 is hard to read.
