title: Response to Comment on ‘Soil carbon persistence governed by plant input and mineral protection at regional and global scales’

study.system: wild bees and plant–pollinator networks; model and pollen data

editor_summary: Reviewers are split; editor disregards format complaints but suggests reformatting to ELE, stresses the paper compares two empirical systems to a model, advises on taxonomic splits and two-genera generality, and wants the discussion closer to the results.

reviews.assessment: Interesting work combining a theoretical model with empirical data, but the empirical side needs much more clarity and justification.
strengths: nice combination of model predictions and empirical data
topic of broad interest to network and plant-animal ecologists

comments.issue: The paper's structure is odd, with methods at the end and a discussion largely outside the study's scope.
comments.request: Reorganise the manuscript and refocus the discussion.
comments.quote: I found the structure of the paper a little odd – why is the methods section relegated to the end

comments.issue: “Temporal resource overlap” is ambiguous and easily read as pollinator–resource rather than plant–plant overlap.
comments.request: Explain upfront that overlap refers to flowering plants.
comments.quote: Use of the term “temporal resource overlap”, starting in the abstract (line 55-56), could be quite confusing

comments.issue: The sentence at line 111 states the opposite of the intended prediction about reduced flowering overlap.
comments.request: Correct the direction of the predicted effect.
comments.quote: I believe that the sentence starting at the end of line 111 is incorrect – and states the opposite of what the authors intend

comments.issue: The main text does not explain how adaptive foraging models work or which variables evolve.
comments.request: Explain the model structure and evolving variables in the main text.
comments.quote: more information needs to be included in the main text to explain how adaptive foraging models work

comments.issue: Methods appear at the very end, after the results, and the Overview section should be part of them.
comments.request: Move the methods before the results and include the Overview in the methods.
comments.quote: I would strongly urge the authors to move the methods section up and to include the Overview section in the methods.

comments.issue: Whether phenological windows can change during simulations, and what “temporal plasticity” means, is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what is fixed and what is dynamic during model runs.
comments.quote: it wasn’t at all clear to me whether the phenological windows (Tp, Ta) can change over the course of the model

comments.issue: Empirical flowering overlap uses phenology data from plants that do not co-occur at a site, so it is not what a bee sees.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction between model and empirical overlap measures.
comments.quote: the empirical flowering overlap data for both UK and Michigan, but especially UK, come from phenology data for flowering plants that don’t necessarily co-occur together at a site

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the sampled species represent comparable fractions of the flora in the two regions.
comments.request: Assess and report comparability of the regional sampling.
comments.quote: it seems important to address whether the sampling of species in the two regions are comparable

comments.issue: How potential pollen sources were determined for the DFG metric is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how available pollen sources were defined for each specimen.
comments.quote: It’s not at all clear how the actual pollen load were used to figure out what pollen species/genera were available to a particular pollinator

comments.issue: Tables S9 and S10, which document pollen loads and sampling, were not included in the submission.
comments.request: Provide the missing supplementary data tables.
comments.quote: these are excel files that weren’t included in the submission

comments.issue: Bee specimen sampling details, such as number of sites and specimens per site, are not described.
comments.request: Describe how specimens were obtained.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if the authors said more about how the bee specimens were obtained – how many sites, how many specimens per site.

comments.issue: Sampling focused on polylectic Andrena and seven oligolectic bees were added without pollen data, so specimens are not representative.
comments.request: Justify or address the non-representative sampling.
comments.quote: the sampling was focused on polylectic species and so the specimens weren’t representative of the whole Andrena fauna of Britain

comments.issue: Sympatric samples of both genera could be compared directly instead of across regions.
comments.request: Compare pollen diversity of Andrena and Lasioglossum collected at the same site and time.
comments.quote: Are there not pollen load data from Andrena and Lasioglossum bees collected at the same site (and preferably time period) that could be compared directly for pollen diversity?

comments.issue: The Discussion is short, and only the first paragraph addresses the study's model and data.
comments.request: Expand the discussion of the model and results.
comments.quote: The Discussion is quite short and only the first paragraph really deals with the focus of the paper (model and empirical data)

comments.issue: The claim on line 230 that a short season mandates specialization is logically unclear.
comments.request: Clarify why multiple short-season resources would force specialization.
comments.quote: Why, if there are multiple resources all available during a short season, would a bee have to specialize on just one or a few of those resources?

comments.issue: The discussion gives no recommendations for strengthening the empirical side of the work.
comments.request: Add recommendations for future empirical work.
comments.quote: what recommendations would the authors make for strengthening the empirical side of the work?

comments.issue: The role of phytochemical specialization in pollinator diet breadth, and floral versus leaf chemistry, is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how phytochemistry relates to pollinator diet breadth.
comments.quote: I was confused, however, about what role the authors think phytochemical specialization plays in diet breadth in pollinators

comments.issue: The Supplementary Discussion on phytochemistry does not belong in this paper.
comments.request: Consider removing the Supplementary Discussion.
comments.quote: I’m not really sure that the Supplementary Discussion on this topic belongs in this paper.

reviews.assessment: Applauds the model but is not convinced the empirical analysis tests it; suggests demoting the empirical part and revising strongly.
strengths: compelling phenology method for dynamic network models
timely topic rooted in long-standing questions
ambitious integration of theory and data

comments.issue: Regions and genera differ in many ways beyond flowering overlap and flight period, so the comparison is confounded.
comments.request: Strengthen the empirical test of the hypothesis.
comments.quote: The selected pair of regions and bee genera is not a strong test of the hypothesis.

comments.issue: Bee species selection is not systematic; bivoltine generations are treated as species and seven oligoleges were added without pollen data.
comments.request: Use a systematic, comparable species selection across regions and genera.
comments.quote: The selection of bee species is not clearly systematic or performed the same way for both regions or genera.

comments.issue: Pollen load sampling is not standardised, and niche breadth from fewer than ten records per species is incomplete.
comments.request: Standardise sampling and take sample biases seriously.
comments.quote: Sampling of pollen loads was not well standardized.

comments.issue: Treating all regional plants as available to every bee inflates specialization via added zeros and differs between regions.
comments.request: Report the number of available plant taxa and justify the availability definition.
comments.quote: The specialization metrics used here are strongly influenced by the number of plant taxa considered available.

comments.issue: Flowering overlap is compared across mismatched resolutions and extents: UK country-level monthly versus Michigan site-level daily data.
comments.request: Make the flowering overlap data comparable between regions.
comments.quote: the comparison of flowering overlap between UK and MI is not meaningful

comments.issue: The empirical data describe specialization at genus or family level while the model uses species level.
comments.request: Align the taxonomic level of model and empirical analyses.
comments.quote: Empirical data evaluate specialization on the genus or family level, whereas the model considers specialization on species level

comments.issue: The model represents a local network while the empirical data characterise state-wide specialization.
comments.request: Reconcile the spatial scales of model and empirical data.
comments.quote: The scale of model and empirical data differs: the model is more for a local network (adaptive foraging choices), the empirical data aim at state-wide characterization.

comments.issue: Model and empirical patterns do not match as well as claimed; Lasioglossum shows an opposite trend.
comments.request: Temper the claim that empirical patterns corroborate the model.
comments.quote: Patterns for model results and empirical results are not matching as well as claimed.

comments.issue: The paper overemphasises phenology as a driver, and synchronous specialization cannot be explained by the model mechanism.
comments.request: Temper the phenology claims and acknowledge synchronous specialization.
comments.quote: it overemphasizes the potential importance of phenology for driving specialization in pollinators (bees)

comments.issue: The discussion paragraph L221-239 misleadingly implies synchronous specialization is unique to short-season deserts.
comments.request: Revise the misleading paragraph.
comments.quote: I find the discussion paragraph L221-239 quite misleading in this regard

comments.issue: How the proposed mechanism differs from Encinas-Viso et al. (2012) is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the novelty relative to Encinas-Viso et al. (2012).
comments.quote: I would be curious to know in what respect the mechanism proposed here is fundamentally different from the one proposed by Encinas-Viso et al. (2012)

comments.issue: The discussion focuses on macroecological patterns far from the results, and the classical view predicts the opposite pattern.
comments.request: Refocus the discussion on the model and address the opposite expectation.
comments.quote: The strong focus on macroecological patterns of specialization of pollinators vs. herbivores etc. is quite far from the own results

comments.issue: The Fig. 1 example is constructed, and a slightly longer flight period would show overlap effects for long periods.
comments.request: Present the conditional effect less categorically.
comments.quote: the example in Fig. 1 seems a bit constructed

comments.issue: The x-axis ranges differ between Fig. 2 panels, exaggerating differences between flight periods.
comments.request: Use the same x-axis range in all four panels.
comments.quote: The same range should be used for the x-axis in all four panels of Fig. 2

comments.issue: The model gives bees either short or long flight periods and omits competition, while the empirical genera co-occur.
comments.request: Discuss flight period effects on overlap, resource extraction and competition.
comments.quote: in the model, all bees have either short or long flight period, but in the empirical data, Andrena and Lasioglossum co-occur with each other

comments.issue: The spatial–temporal resource distribution analogy on L94-108 is not well argued.
comments.request: Replace it with discussion of plant-pollinator literature on phenology and specialization.
comments.quote: I find the analogy between spatial and temporal resource distribution not well argued and not very enlightening for the paper

comments.issue: How the specialization metrics complement each other is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the relationship between the specialization metrics.
comments.quote: in what way do the specialization metrics complement each other?

comments.issue: Simple standard errors are shown in Fig. 4 despite the data being deeply non-normal.
comments.request: Use error estimates appropriate for the data distribution.
comments.quote: why are simple standard errors shown in Fig. 4, if data were “deeply non-normal”?

reviews.assessment: Nice and substantial contribution with novel methods and mostly justified conclusions; only two minor concerns about generality and effect sizes.
strengths: clear manuscript with novel and effective methods

comments.issue: Empirical results from two bee genera and two locations are hard to generalise, and pollen may come from other sources.
comments.request: Broaden taxa and locations or temper generality claims.
comments.quote: it still seems very difficult to generalize the empirical results that are limited to 2 genera (albeit diverse) from 2 locations

comments.issue: The DFG and CV specialization measures are hard to interpret, and Figures 2-4 report P-values without effect sizes.
comments.request: Provide parameter estimates and benchmarks for interpreting effect sizes.
comments.quote: the authors need to provide more perspective to interpret effect sizes associated with statistical models

comments.issue: The claim that specialization progress comes from herbivory studies overlooks the many pollination specialization studies.
comments.request: Acknowledge pollination network studies of specialization.
comments.quote: there are a large number of pollination studies that are focused on specialization, especially in the network literature

comments.issue: Herbivore specialization is actually more restricted than the manuscript states.
comments.request: Correct the characterisation of herbivore specialization.
comments.quote: Levels of specialization in insect herbivores are actually more restricted than this

comments.issue: The temporal accessibility statement also applies to herbivores, but this literature is not cited.
comments.request: Cite recent tropical herbivore and temporal rewiring work.
comments.quote: This is also true for herbivores (several recent papers in tropical systems demonstrate this

title: Phenology and flowering overlap drive specialisation in plant–pollinator networks

study.system: tank-bromeliad aquatic microcosms; warming and predator-loss experiment

editor_summary: Editor notes all three reviewers see merit and novelty, but concerns are substantive enough to require a major rewrite; reanalysis and changes to some statistical models are needed, with a revision invited.

reviews.assessment: Timely and interesting and mainly well written, but methods need more detail and stability estimated from only four time points needs scrutiny.
strengths: well-designed 2x3 experiment analysed with piecewise SEM

comments.issue: Method section is vague and missing details needed to understand the study.
comments.request: Rewrite the methods more clearly and add the missing details.
comments.quote: The method section could be formulated more clearly and is missing a few details.

comments.issue: Using only four time points, one at the very start, may not give representative stability or synchrony estimates.
comments.request: Assess or discuss the uncertainty introduced by four time points.
comments.quote: I do think that using 4 time points (one of which is the very start of the experiment) to measure stability is borderline sufficient and I am not sure how much uncertainty is introduced as a consequence.

comments.issue: 25 line-level copy edits (wording, spelling, punctuation).
comments.quote: l.56-7: Please correct the second part of the sentence.

comments.issue: Confusion between weakening the diversity-stability relationship and reducing diversity itself.
comments.request: Clarify what "weaken DSRs" means and use the terms consistently.
comments.quote: To me “weaken DSRs” means that the slope coefficient of the relationship between diversity and stability will decrease.

comments.issue: The term "mesopredator outbreak" is not defined.
comments.request: Define what is meant by a mesopredator outbreak.
comments.quote: l.143: What do you mean by “mesopredator outbreak”?

comments.issue: Sentence about bromeliads per block is confusing and needs rephrasing.
comments.request: Rephrase to make the number of bromeliads per block clear.
comments.quote: l.159: I was confused by this sentence. It sounds like there were more than six bromeliads in one block.

comments.issue: Number of sampling occasions and interval are inconsistent with the stated 75-day duration.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling interval and number of measurements.
comments.quote: Were asynchrony and stability calculated with only 4 measurements over time? Or what was the sampling interval?

comments.issue: Unclear what the taxon grouping includes.
comments.request: Specify which groups the category includes.
comments.quote: l.187: I guess this includes the mesopredators and top predators?

comments.issue: Statistical analysis section is disorganised, with model structure and technical details mixed together.
comments.request: Describe model logic first, then technical details such as transformation and tests.
comments.quote: There are a number of different models, but the structure and differences are described in bits an pieces throughout

comments.issue: Temperature measurement details are placed in the statistical analysis instead of the experimental setup.
comments.request: Move temperature measurement details to the experimental setup section.
comments.quote: Details on temperature measurements could go in the section on experimental setup and measurements.

comments.issue: No information on diversity variation across experimental units and time, which matters because diversity was not manipulated.
comments.request: Report diversity measures across units and time to aid interpretation.
comments.quote: it would be interesting to include information on diversity across the different experimental units and time

comments.issue: A claimed consequence is trivially expected from reduced grazing pressure, and "vulnerable" may be the wrong word.
comments.request: Clarify the logic and reconsider the wording.
comments.quote: Isn’t that a logical consequence of reducing grazing pressure on the mesopredators? Not sure whether vulnerable is the right word here..

comments.issue: Calling the consumer groups "various intermediate levels" is questionable if mesopredators feed on all lower levels.
comments.request: Reconsider the trophic level terminology.
comments.quote: Is it correct to talk about “various intermediate levels” if the mesopredators feed on all of the lower trophic levels

comments.issue: Use of "DSR" is again unclear; a change in diversity cannot itself be a driver of the diversity-stability relationship.
comments.request: Clarify the DSR argument and distinguish vertical from within-level diversity change.
comments.quote: Again I am not sure about the use of the term DSR. How can a change in diversity be a driver of the diversity-stability relationship?

reviews.assessment: Well written given the complexity, and the main result is a major strength, but trophic cascade terminology and mechanism need clarification.
strengths: main result that predator loss destabilizes the system
manuscript generally well written given system complexity
clear distillation of complex pathways in the introduction

comments.issue: Complexity of system and mechanisms overwhelms the predictions, leaving the impression anything can happen.
comments.request: Simplify the predictions in Lns 119-140 to make outcomes predictable.
comments.quote: by the time the reader gets to Lns 119-140 one is left with the feeling that anything can happen and it is impossible to predict a likely outcome

comments.issue: Essential methods details (placement of bromeliads, volume range, sampling context) are missing from the main text.
comments.request: Add where bromeliads were placed and their volume range in the main text.
comments.quote: A few more short details of the methods would be very helpful to include in the main text rather than referring to previous publications and the supplementary information.

comments.issue: Effectiveness of the warming treatment is not demonstrated, so the null warming result may be methodological.
comments.request: Report warming treatment validation to rule out methodological explanations.
comments.quote: it would be good to comment on the effectiveness of warming as a treatment in order to determine if the lack of warming effect that was observed could possibly have methodological explanations

comments.issue: The DSR prediction at line 123 contradicts the following lines and the portfolio-effect reasoning is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the contradiction and the reason to expect suppression of the portfolio effect.
comments.quote: is there a specific reason to believe warming would suppress the portfolio effect?

comments.issue: "Trophic cascade" is used although only mesopredators increase and producer density is unchanged.
comments.request: Use the term trophic cascade consistently with its definition or reframe the mechanism.
comments.quote: In this experiment the term trophic cascade is used repeatedly yet only the mesopredator community increases after the top predators are removed while the producer density remains unchanged.

comments.issue: Results may reflect compensation between edible and resistant producers rather than a density-mediated cascade.
comments.request: Elaborate this alternative compensation mechanism in the discussion.
comments.quote: This to me is not a ‘trophic cascade’ as overall density is not affected, but instead suggests broad compensation between edible and vulnerable species

comments.issue: The asynchrony statistic is a very coarse measure of asynchrony.
comments.request: Acknowledge the coarseness of the asynchrony metric or use a better one.
comments.quote: the asynchrony statistic used here which is a very coarse measure of asynchrony

comments.issue: LNS 356-368 arguments could be clearer; the trophic cascade driver statement should be phrased more generally.
comments.request: Reword to say trophic cascades determine the degree of species asynchrony.
comments.quote: This section could stand to be reviewed to try to make the arguments clearer.

comments.issue: Predation-resistant species may be released from competition and respond complementarily, opposite to the proposed synchrony mechanism.
comments.request: Consider the alternative complementary response of resistant species.
comments.quote: I could see this argument going the other way where predation resistant species could be responding in a complementary way by being released from competition from the more vulnerable species

comments.issue: Underlying producer dynamics (oscillation versus species compensation) behind destabilisation are not identified.
comments.request: Examine producer time series for oscillations versus compensation among species.
comments.quote: Is it possible to look at the producer data over the 4 time periods to determine more specifically what underlying pattern was that contributed to the observed effects on producer

comments.issue: It is unclear whether using abundance rather than biomass affects the results.
comments.request: Repeat or compare analyses using biomass instead of abundance.
comments.quote: does the choice to use producer abundance vs biomass affect the interpretation of the results? Would the results be similar if biomass was used?

comments.issue: About 18 line-level copy edits (wording, spelling, punctuation).
comments.quote: Ln 57 ‘attribute is reduced or lower’ rather than ‘lesser’

comments.issue: The meaning of the net-effects sentence is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether net effects vary from weaker to stronger with warming.
comments.quote: Do you mean here that ‘net effects on trophic dynamics can vary from becoming weaker to become stronger with warming?

comments.issue: What a tank-bromeliad system is should be explained in the main text, not only in the supplement.
comments.request: Briefly explain the tank-bromeliad system in the main text.
comments.quote: can you briefly explain what is meant by a ‘tank-bromeliad’ system here rather than just in supplementary information?

comments.issue: The description of tanks per block and random selection is confusing as worded.
comments.request: Reword the experimental design description clearly.
comments.quote: Ln 157-159 6 tanks per block, randomly selected 6 tanks. Confusing as worded.

comments.issue: Missing description of how the warming system controlled mean temperature while allowing daily variation.
comments.request: Add a phrase describing the warming system's control and daily variation.
comments.quote: Add a brief phrase here indicating the warming system allowed mean temperatures to be controlled while also allowing them to undergo typical daily variation.

comments.issue: The dilution of 400 ul to 1 ml is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the dilution procedure and volumes.
comments.quote: Ln178 – 400ul were diluted to a total volume of 1ml (?)

comments.issue: It is unclear whether average density is meant to represent overyielding.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between average density and overyielding.
comments.quote: Ln 234 by average density I assume you mean overyielding here?

comments.issue: Figure references (3c,d versus 3b) do not match the claim about richness effects.
comments.request: Check and correct the figure references.
comments.quote: Lns 294-296. The line refers to the lack of richness effect within trophic levels for trophic level stability (i.e. Figure 3c,d) correct?

comments.issue: Producer density being much higher than other groups should be stated for context.
comments.request: Point out how many times higher producer density was.
comments.quote: It might be appropriate here to point out that producer density was on average XX times higher than the other groups (Figure 4d).

comments.issue: The phrase "differential relevance between the effects of trophic cascades" is confusing.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence more clearly.
comments.quote: differential relevance between the effects of trophic cascades

comments.issue: It is not clear that the passage discusses other work rather than this experiment's results.
comments.request: Rewrite so the attribution to previous work is explicit.
comments.quote: Ln394 – it is not clear that you are discussing other work, not the results of this experiment.

comments.issue: Suggest elaborating that within-trophic-level diversity may matter less than trophic structure.
comments.request: Add this nuance to the discussion.
comments.quote: Perhaps it is worth pointing out that diversity within trophic levels may not be as important in determining community stability as does trophic structure (or vertical diversity) in multi-trophic systems.

comments.issue: Table SX needs to be fixed.
comments.request: Fix Table SX.
comments.quote: Ln673-Table SX needs to be fixed.

comments.issue: "Species asynchrony" in the table may need to be "community asynchrony".
comments.request: Clarify or correct the term.
comments.quote: Ln686 b) species asynchrony – should this be ‘community’ asynchrony?

reviews.assessment: Neat, novel experiment, but warming should be analysed as designed, overyielding and productivity metrics are questionable, and conclusions need toning down.
strengths: novel mechanistic exploration of global change effects on stability
effort to tease apart different stabilising mechanisms

comments.issue: Warming is a categorical three-level treatment but is analysed as a continuous variable.
comments.request: Analyse warming as designed, with two-way ANOVA of warming by predator loss.
comments.quote: The experiment sets up warming as a categorical factor with three levels (ambient, ambient +2, ambient +4), yet the analysis treats it as a continuous variable.

comments.issue: Overyielding is not quantified in the classic monoculture-polyculture sense; total density is an unjustified proxy.
comments.request: Quantify overyielding properly or justify the density proxy.
comments.quote: overyielding does not seem to be quantified in the classic sense (relating performance of individual species in monoculture to their performance in polyculture)

comments.issue: Productivity-stability relationships cannot be analysed with standing stock alone, since stocks can be low in productive systems.
comments.request: Acknowledge that density is a standing stock, not productivity.
comments.quote: I am also not convinced that “productivity-stability” relationships were analysed when only a standing stock (average density over four sampling points) was quantified. Stocks can be low even in a very productive system.

comments.issue: Assertions in the discussion about the strength and applicability of conclusions are too strong.
comments.request: Tone down the strength and breadth of the conclusions.
comments.quote: I would encourage the authors to tone down some of assertions in the discussion about the strength of their conclusions and their applicability in a broader context.

comments.issue: Findings from microcosms are presented as definitive for all natural communities and cannot be generalised so widely.
comments.request: Avoid overselling the significance and reach of the findings.
comments.quote: I worry that the findings are presented as the definitive word for all natural communities, when in fact they are the natural equivalent of communities in glass jars in the laboratory.

comments.issue: "Species stability" is confusing; the paper actually addresses temporal variability.
comments.request: Use temporal variability terminology throughout.
comments.quote: I think that terminology would be better throughout than “species stability”, which I actually find to be pretty confusing.

comments.issue: About 21 line-level copy edits (wording, spelling, punctuation).
comments.quote: Ln140. Should this be “amplify” instead of “amply”?

comments.issue: References are missing for two stated points.
comments.request: Provide references for these points.
comments.quote: Ln125 and 127. Provide references for these points.

comments.issue: Summarising results at the end of the introduction is jarring and comes before methods.
comments.request: Delete the paragraph or move it to the start of the discussion.
comments.quote: I find the summary of the results at the end of the introduction to be oddly jarring. Why tell us the results before you have even presented the methods?

comments.issue: Potential lasting effects of chemicals on bromeliads or colonising fauna are not addressed.
comments.request: Report whether the chemicals leave lasting effects.
comments.quote: Do these chemicals leave any lasting effects on the bromeliads or the subsequent fauna that colonise them?

comments.issue: How the 15 source units supplied organisms and how variable starting communities were is unclear.
comments.request: Explain organism allocation and starting community variability.
comments.quote: How variable were the starting communities? More information needed here, which is quite crucial to the robustness of the experimental design.

comments.issue: Experimental design is presented in a confusing order.
comments.request: State treatments, levels, replicates and block structure explicitly.
comments.quote: I find this to be a very confusing way of presenting the experimental design.

comments.issue: The study organism is not identified by a common name or description.
comments.request: Give a common name or broad description of the organism.
comments.quote: It would really help to have a common name here, or a broad description of what this organism is, e.g. a dragonfly nymph?

comments.issue: Total bromeliad volume and whether extracted water was replaced are not reported.
comments.request: Report total volumes and replacement of extracted water.
comments.quote: What was the total volume of the bromeliads? Did you replace the extracted volume with clean water?

comments.issue: Sample volumes differ between phytoplankton and zooplankton, risking zooplankton under-sampling.
comments.request: Justify sample volumes or address under-sampling concerns.
comments.quote: Is this normal or should we be concerned about under-sampling of zooplankton from such a small sample volume?

comments.issue: Volume quantification and extrapolation of abundance estimates are not described.
comments.request: Explain how liquid volume was quantified and estimates extrapolated.
comments.quote: Did you quantify the volume of liquid before doing this and extrapolate abundance estimates accordingly

comments.issue: "Secondary consumers" likely contain multiple trophic groups that should be made explicit.
comments.request: Discuss the mixed nature of the secondary consumer level.
comments.quote: It seems likely to me that there are in fact multiple trophic groups in these “secondary consumers”.

comments.issue: "Microbiota" is misleading because it covers all trophic levels, not only the basal level.
comments.request: Use a clearer term for the whole community.
comments.quote: It is not immediately clear here that “microbiota” refers to all trophic levels in the system. I initially thought it might just be the basal level.

comments.issue: It sounds like average species richness was divided by experimental time.
comments.request: Clarify that richness was averaged over the four sampling points.
comments.quote: I presume it is just the average of the species richness recorded at each of the four sampling points within each bromeliad?

comments.issue: Unclear why the metric is multiplied by 100.
comments.request: Explain the multiplication by 100.
comments.quote: Ln209. Why multiply it by 100?

comments.issue: How overyielding presence was evaluated is not described.
comments.request: Explain how overyielding effects were evaluated.
comments.quote: It is not clear to me exactly how you “evaluated the presence of overyielding effects”.

comments.issue: Using LMEs instead of a two-way ANOVA with block as error term is not justified.
comments.request: Consider a standard two-way ANOVA with block as error term.
comments.quote: Why LMEs? Wouldn’t it be easier just to have experimental block as an error term in a standard two-way ANOVA?

comments.issue: It is unclear why Culicidae are treated as a separate mesopredator category from secondary consumers.
comments.request: Clarify the trophic categorization and number of levels.
comments.quote: Why just Culicidae? I think it only now becomes clear to me that Culicidae as mesopredators is a separate category to the secondary consumers you mentioned at Ln196

comments.issue: The interaction network of the system is not visualised and is more complex than it seems.
comments.request: Add a network figure in the supplementary information.
comments.quote: It might be interesting to see a network of the interactions in SI to better visualise this system because it is more complex than it initially seems.

comments.issue: Average density is not an appropriate measure of stability, and species stability versus temporal stability is unclear.
comments.request: Reconsider the stability metric and clarify the distinction.
comments.quote: How is average density a measure of stability?

comments.issue: How the food-web stability claim was evaluated is not described.
comments.request: Explain how food-web stability was evaluated.
comments.quote: Ln247. How did you evaluate this? Also, change to “on the microbial food web, as well as how the food web”

comments.issue: It is unclear whether direct effects were assumed absent a priori or tested and discarded via AIC.
comments.request: Clarify whether direct effects were tested and say "direct effects".
comments.quote: Why would you assume a priori that there were no direct effects of experimental drivers on stabilising mechanisms? Or did you actually test this and discount them through AIC selection?

comments.issue: The complex SEM figure does not clearly show the main experimental effects.
comments.request: Add simple bar charts of predator-loss and warming effects on stability.
comments.quote: Might you consider presenting some simple bar charts that show the main effects of predator loss and warming on community stability?

comments.issue: A results passage reads like methods and should be moved.
comments.request: Move the passage to the methods.
comments.quote: This bit sounds more like methods than results. Move there?

comments.issue: The detailed trophic level analysis adds little, merely confirming the main predator-loss result.
comments.request: Condense it and move Figure 3 to the supplementary information.
comments.quote: I also wonder if this more detailed trophic level analysis adds anything to the manuscript? It simply confirms the previous assertion that top predator loss drives the changes in stability.

comments.issue: Disproportionate producer contribution may reflect their greater abundance; biomass standardisation untested.
comments.request: Test whether using biomass instead of abundance changes the pattern.
comments.quote: Could this disproportionate contribution of primary producers be due in some way to their much greater abundance, relative to other trophic groups?

comments.issue: Stating that producers are stable "despite being abundant" contradicts the expectation that abundance increases fluctuation.
comments.request: Reconsider the "despite being abundant" framing.
comments.quote: Why “despite being abundant”? If anything, I would expect that their greater abundance makes them more susceptible to large fluctuations.

comments.issue: The damselfly larvae identity of the top predator emerges only late and should come much earlier.
comments.request: Introduce the organism identity much earlier.
comments.quote: Ah, so this is the first point where I realised we are actually dealing with damselfly larvae in the experiment! This needs to come much earlier.

comments.issue: The phrase "even marine ecosystems" suggests an unexpected difference and references are not grouped.
comments.request: Say "other aquatic ecosystems" and group the references.
comments.quote: I would just say “other aquatic ecosystems” here and group all the references together.

comments.issue: The overyielding claim is not supported, as only stocks rather than productivity were quantified.
comments.request: Remove or support the overyielding claim with adequate evidence.
comments.quote: you only quantified stocks not productivity, so do you really have enough evidence to make this claim? I’m not convinced you do.

comments.issue: Calling a mechanism "irrelevant" is a very strong statement given overyielding was not adequately quantified.
comments.request: Tone down the statement.
comments.quote: Note that this statement is very strong (i.e. “an irrelevant mechanism”) when I’m not even sure you have adequately quantified overyielding. Tone this down?

comments.issue: Figure 1 is too complex; panel a is unnecessary and the boxes are confusing.
comments.request: Simplify Figure 1 and restructure its panels.
comments.quote: Figure 1. I find this figure too complex. I think panel a is unnecessary.

comments.issue: "Horizontal diversity" is a strange term for within-trophic-level diversity.
comments.request: Call it species richness instead.
comments.quote: And why “horizontal diversity”? This is a strange term and suggests you are only talking about diversity within a trophic level

title: Trophic downgrading decreases species asynchrony and community stability regardless of climate warming

study.system: coast redwood soil/root fungi; landscape fragmentation

editor_summary: Editor finds the manuscript well written with great potential and broad appeal, but says reviewer 2's considerations require additional assessment before acceptance.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and well-written study, but the methods detail, results reporting and island-biogeography framing need extensive additional work.
strengths: novel report of rhizonodes in redwood

comments.issue: The computational tests in the Methods lack sufficient detail.
comments.request: Expand the Methods description of the computational tests.
comments.quote: I found myself wanting more detail in the Methods for computational tests

comments.issue: Analysis code is not available.
comments.request: Include the R code in the Appendix.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to include the R code in the Appendix

comments.issue: Only the final two best-fit variables are shown, so relative variable importance cannot be judged.
comments.request: Present intermediate model-testing results or summaries of all conditions tested.
comments.quote: I would like much more presentation of the intermediate results from model testing, or summaries of all the conditions tested, as it is hard to gauge the relative importance of variables

comments.issue: A priori hypothesis variables are dropped by backwards elimination, hiding the focal hypothesis test.
comments.request: Include habitat cover and fragmentation in all models.
comments.quote: I also suggest that they include the variables “habitat cover” and “habitat fragmentation” in each model since they are the focus of hypothesis 1

comments.issue: The Discussion interprets results without justifying the metrics as island-biogeography proxies or comparing methods.
comments.request: Discuss why the metrics are valid proxies and their benefits and limitations.
comments.quote: The Discussion jumps to quickly to interpretation – I would like to see a discussion on why the metrics measured are appropriate proxies for testing island biogeographical hypotheses

comments.issue: The results appear to conflict with Peay et al. 2007, which found a species-area relationship for host-associated fungi.
comments.request: Discuss why the results differ from Peay et al. 2007.
comments.quote: is this work going to counter Peay et al. 2007, which found a strong species area relationship for host-associated ectomycorrhizal fungi?

comments.issue: The sampling looks like a transect rather than a nested biogeographical design; 'nested' is not defined early.
comments.request: Describe the nested design and clarify the terminology early.
comments.quote: this overall design looks more like a transect, rather than a nested biogeographical design

comments.issue: Location names and coordinates of the eight sites are not reported.
comments.request: Provide site names and GPS coordinates.
comments.quote: Provide the location names and GPS coordinates for the 8 sites, either here or in Supplemental

comments.issue: A paragraph is placed before the Site Description it depends on.
comments.request: Move the paragraph after the Site Description.
comments.quote: This paragraph would make more sense to follow the Site Description

comments.issue: The acronym DBH is never spelled out.
comments.request: Spell out DBH.
comments.quote: What is DBH? Acronym not spelled out anywhere

comments.issue: The location name for Site 8 is missing.
comments.request: Provide the location name for Site 8.
comments.quote: What is the location name for Site 8?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether bulk soil or rhizosphere soil was extracted.
comments.request: State whether soil samples were bulk or rhizosphere soil.
comments.quote: What type of soil was extracted? Was it the soil washed off the roots (rhizosphere soil), or the bulk soil?

comments.issue: Primer names are not given.
comments.request: Provide primer names.
comments.quote: Line 124: Provide names of primers

comments.issue: The recovered fragment length is not reported.
comments.request: Report the fragment length recovered.
comments.quote: Line 128: Report the fragment length recovered

comments.issue: Whether sample loss affected statistical power is not addressed.

comments.quote: Lines 149-151: Did the loss of samples affect your ability to do statistics?

comments.issue: The sentence at line 153 about GDMs is incomplete.

comments.quote: Used GDMs to assess the strength of the relationship between microbial community structure and habitat cover and fragmentation?

comments.issue: The two focal variables are not named explicitly when the hypothesis test is described.
comments.request: Name habitat cover and habitat fragmentation with their metrics.
comments.quote: I would name the variables you’re testing “habitat cover (percent redwood cover in buffer zone)” and “habitat fragmentation (weighted edge density, WEDG).”

comments.issue: Methods for plant and soil variables such as AET, pH, CEC, C:N and decomposition are not described or located.

comments.quote: or direct the reader to the supplemental so they know where to find the methods used to generate the data for these variables

comments.issue: The figure shows only the final variables, so the three focal variables cannot be compared.
comments.request: Include habitat cover, fragmentation and pH in the figure.
comments.quote: Perhaps include all 3 variables/lines (habitat cover, habitat fragmentation, pH) in the figure so the viewer can assess the influence of these 3 variables on community structure.

comments.issue: The variables retained in the parsimonious models are not stated.
comments.request: State which variables were retained.
comments.quote: Line 163: State what variables were retained for the parsimonious models

comments.issue: It should be made explicit that the groups are FUNguild functional groups.
comments.request: Clarify that these are FUNguild functional groups.
comments.quote: Line 171: Clarify that these a “FUNguild functional groups”

comments.issue: The phrase 'underlying patterns of shifts' is vague; species turnover is meant.
comments.request: Say species turnover instead.
comments.quote: Line 173: Vague, what “underlying patterns of shifts”? Perhaps it would be better to say “species turnover.”

comments.issue: Nestedness, species losses and species replacement are not defined or distinguished.
comments.request: Define nestedness and distinguish replacement from loss.
comments.quote: Explain what “nestedness” means here, and how it is equivalent to species losses. Also, how is species replacement different from a species loss?

comments.issue: The rationale for calculating beta-dispersion and correlating it with richness/diversity is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the beta-dispersion analysis and its link to the hypotheses.
comments.quote: It’s not clear to me why this is a useful analysis and feels like a tangent.

comments.issue: Four line-level copy edits (missing verb, model terminology, citation format, wording).
comments.quote: Lines 181-183: This sentence is missing something. A verb?

comments.issue: The most parsimonious model and model scores are not reported, making model reduction opaque.
comments.request: State the parsimonious model and add a scores table.
comments.quote: Line 185: State the most parsimonious model. Maybe it would be useful to include a table showing the scores in the supplemental?

comments.issue: It is not explained why the GDM analysis was not done for the rhizonodes.
comments.request: Explain why rhizonodes were excluded from the GDM analysis.
comments.quote: Line 195: Why did you not do the GDM analysis for the rhizonodes?

comments.issue: The results paragraph lacks structure and clear topic sentences.
comments.request: Restructure into paragraphs with clear topics.
comments.quote: I think this paragraph could use better structure, and perhaps needs to be multiple paragraphs, each with a clear topic sentence.

comments.issue: Full F tables with tested variables and their statistics are not provided.
comments.request: Provide full F tables in the Supplemental.
comments.quote: Line 213: Provide full F tables showing variables tested and their F-values/p-values/r2 values in the Supplemental

comments.issue: How the other variables compared with the reported ones is not shown.
comments.request: Report comparisons with the other variables.
comments.quote: Line 215: How did the other variables compare to these?

comments.issue: The variance-partitioning sentence is unclear without a lead-in.
comments.request: Start the sentence by naming the partitioning analysis.
comments.quote: Otherwise it’s not clear you’re talking about variance partitioning.

comments.issue: The terms habitat fragmentation and connectivity are used interchangeably.
comments.request: Use one term consistently.

comments.issue: The claim that saprotrophs dominate the soil environment is not supported by presented data.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether free-living symbiotrophs or spores are meant in the soil section.

comments.quote: To be clear, are you talking about “free-living” symbiotrophs or spores? Because this section is on the soil, not the roots

comments.issue: The section reads as a grab bag; a summary table would clarify how variables compared.
comments.request: Add a summary table of the variables.
comments.quote: This section feels like a grab bag of results, and it’s not clear how the different variables stacked up against each other. Perhaps make a table as a summary?

comments.issue: The comparison behind 'emerged as an important predictor' is unspecified.
comments.request: State what the predictor is compared to.
comments.quote: Line 245: Emerged as an important predictor compared to what?

comments.issue: A results paragraph belongs in the Discussion.
comments.request: Move the paragraph to the Discussion.
comments.quote: Lines 260-269: This paragraph should probably go in the Discussion

comments.issue: The reference point for the 20-fold enrichment is missing.
comments.request: State what the 20-fold enrichment is relative to.
comments.quote: Line 293: 20-fold relative enrichment compared to what?

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 294-296 is confusing.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence for clarity.
comments.quote: Lines 294-296: This sentence is confusing

comments.issue: The analyses are not placed in an island-biogeography framework or linked to its classical predictions.
comments.request: Frame methods and results within island biogeography and discuss limitations.
comments.quote: first I think you need to make clear in the results or discussion your methods are appropriate for testing theories of island biogeography

comments.issue: 'Decoupled' is not unpacked; which part of island biogeography is decoupled from is unclear.

comments.issue: Citations for landscape heterogeneity in island biogeography are missing; forest cover's role as proxy is unclear.

comments.quote: Line 318: Provide citations for importance of landscape heterogeneity on island biogeography. Also, is forest cover a proxy for island size or landscape heterogeneity?

comments.issue: The direction of the correspondence is not stated.
comments.request: State whether the relationship increased or decreased.
comments.quote: Line 323: Corresponded how, increased or decreased?

comments.issue: The speculation about the decoupling is not adequately supported.
comments.request: Temper the speculation.
comments.quote: Line 327: I would temper this speculation

comments.issue: Terminology for sample variability is inconsistent; beta-dispersion is meant.
comments.request: Use consistent terminology for beta-dispersion.
comments.quote: Line 332: Use consistent terminology, I’m guessing your talking about variability between samples (beta-dispersion)

comments.issue: It is not explained how decomposition rates were inferred.

comments.issue: The causes of decomposition declines, such as water limitation, are not considered.

comments.issue: The argument at line 338 is a speculative jump unsupported by the reasoning.
comments.request: Support or remove the speculative argument.
comments.quote: Line 338: This is a jump and a speculation, not following your reasoning here

comments.issue: The significant pH relationship for root communities, opposite to expectation, is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss why root communities respond to pH but free-living ones do not.
comments.quote: But you do see a significant relationship with pH for the root-associated communities that you didn’t see for the free-living communities. That seems worth mentioning.

comments.issue: The link drawn to a bird microbiome study is a big leap and the reference's relevance is unclear.
comments.request: Unpack the bird microbiome comparison or use a more relevant reference.
comments.quote: Wow, the relationship between your results, the bird microbiome, and landscape heterogeneity is a big leap, could you unpack this

comments.issue: The text suggests the analysis was done for roots only, not rhizonodes, contradicting earlier methods.
comments.request: Clarify which compartments were analysed.
comments.quote: Line 357: Based on the methods (see line 192) I thought this analysis was only done for the roots, not rhizonodes?

comments.issue: Context on mycorrhizal nodules in other trees is missing.

comments.issue: The nested sampling design is not clearly shown in Figure 1.

comments.issue: The colors and shapes in the circles are not explained.

comments.issue: The arrows in Figure 1 are unexplained and their placement is confusing.

comments.issue: The Figure 2a caption does not say the x-axes apply to both panels.

comments.issue: The units of partial ecological distance are missing.

comments.issue: The figure legend label is incomplete.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written and conceptually compelling study; pleased overall, but wants the conflicting bacterial results discussed and several points improved.
strengths: smart to contextualize predictions in island biogeography
reasonable that biotic and abiotic features were not manipulated

comments.issue: The companion 2020 bacterial study found environmental structuring in roots, opposite to this paper's plant-selection argument.
comments.request: Discuss why bacterial and fungal results differ and when the theories should apply.
comments.quote: The findings for the previous paper appear to be counter to the argument made in this paper that soil communities are structured by the environment but that this breaks down in roots due to selection by plants.

comments.issue: The connectivity metrics are not explained for a broad audience.
comments.request: Briefly explain the connectivity metrics.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to explain these connectivity metrics briefly. They are not as standard for the broad Ecology Letters audience as many of the other metric and they are important to interpreting the study.

comments.issue: Negative control details are insufficient.
comments.request: Describe the number and handling of negative controls.
comments.quote: Can you elaborate a little on the negative controls? How many negative controls and were the negatives exposed to the extraction process or were they simply sterile water placed into the 96-well plates?

comments.issue: Cited papers (Gao et al. 2018 and Taylor et al. 2016) are missing from the reference list.
comments.request: Add the missing references.
comments.quote: both this paper and the Taylor et al 2016 paper were not in the references section. Please add.

comments.issue: The percentage of OTUs mapped to FUNguild guilds in each compartment is not reported.
comments.request: Report the percentage of OTUs mapped to guilds.
comments.quote: What % of the OTUs actually mapped in funguild to symbiotroph, etc in the roots and rhizonodes? How about in the soils?

comments.issue: The confidence level required for guild classification is not stated.
comments.request: State the surety level required for guild assignment.
comments.quote: What level of surety was require to classify taxa into guilds (e.g. probable, highly probably, etc)?

comments.issue: Rarefaction curves are not shown.
comments.request: Include rarefaction curves in the supplement.
comments.quote: Line 147-149: Could you include the rarefaction curves in the supplement?

comments.issue: Whether removed samples are evenly distributed among sites and trees is unknown.
comments.request: Report how sample loss was distributed across sites and trees.
comments.quote: I’m curious if the any particular trees or sites that had more samples lost at this stage. In other words, are the removed samples distributed pretty equally among sites and trees within sites?

comments.issue: Why symbiotrophs decline above 50% redwood cover is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the decline in symbiotrophs above 50% redwood cover.
comments.quote: Ok it seems intuitive why the symbiotrophs may decline below 20% redwood cover, why do they decline when redwood cover is above 50%?
