title: A plant–pollinator metanetwork along a habitat fragmentation gradient

study.system: coastal soil testate amoebae; field survey and palaeoecological cores

editor_summary: Editor: all reviewers find the work important but raise substantive issues: missing covariates (soil chemistry, plants), conductivity as sole salinity proxy, and unsupported ecosystem-functioning claims.

reviews.assessment: High-quality, original and timely; main concern is that the ecosystem-function claim is not supported.

comments.issue: Whether TA community change indicates changes in soil and ecosystem functions is unsupported.
comments.request: Discuss which functions would be impacted or tone down the claim.
comments.quote: My biggest concern is whether a change in testate amoeba communities can indicate changes in soil and ecosystem functions.

comments.issue: Other predators such as foraminifera could replace TA with little change in predator biomass.
comments.request: Examine TA-foraminifera correlations in the historical data.
comments.quote: it would be interesting to look at the correlation between TA and foraminifera in historical data

comments.issue: Other environmental variables that could explain TA changes are not considered.
comments.request: Add discussion of other environmental variables and their roles.
comments.quote: which other variables are important to consider (if any)? What is their role for TA and for the functioning of soil ecosystems?

comments.issue: Responses of other functionally important taxonomic groups to salinization are not discussed.
comments.request: Add lines on other groups' salinity tolerance relative to TA.
comments.quote: I would like to see a few lines about how other functionally important taxonomic groups respond to salinization in these ecosystems. Are they more or less tolerant than TA?

comments.issue: "Microbial" may not be a good keyword.
comments.request: Reconsider the keyword choice.
comments.quote: L. 33: Is “microbial” a good keyword?

comments.issue: The claim at L.175 that TA are representative microbial eukaryotes needs support or qualification.
comments.quote: L. 175: TA are representative microbial eukaryotes

comments.issue: Sampling dates of the various datasets are not reported.
comments.request: Add sampling dates to the methods and/or Extended Data.
comments.quote: I did not find the information about the date of sampling of the various datasets

comments.issue: It is unknown whether TA communities lose species or undergo true turnover with salinity.
comments.request: Compute Baselga's nestedness/turnover metrics for community composition.
comments.quote: I suggest computing the nestedness/turnover metric of Baselga (2012; GEB)

comments.issue: Extended Data Fig. 3 lacks a combined CA across the three habitat types.
comments.request: Add a CA including the three habitat types.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to see a CA that includes the three habitat types in addition to the individual analyses.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written study making a strong case for TA as sea-level indicators; mostly minor edits and suggestions.
strengths: combined N and S hemisphere datasets
strong case for TA as indicators

comments.issue: Beta diversity was not examined despite the steep ecological gradient.
comments.request: Consider examining beta diversity as a metric.
comments.quote: it could have been interesting to look at beta diversity as a metric

comments.issue: DCA followed by correlation is less direct than RDA for the salinity gradient.
comments.request: Consider RDA on Hellinger-transformed data instead.
comments.quote: I was wondering why not use a RDA rather than a DCA followed by correlation

comments.issue: Several copy edits: soften "will" at L36, update taxonomic names and authorities, fix a typo, homogenize reference format.
comments.quote: L 36. Perhaps replace “will” by “is expected to” to be slightly less affirmative

comments.issue: Studies on road-salt effects on soil protists are not cited at L54.
comments.request: Cite relevant studies, e.g. Roe and Patterson (2014).
comments.quote: You may want to cite here some study on the effect of road salt on soil protists

comments.issue: Productivity is inferred from density counts, but production/biomass ratios vary and living and dead shells were not separated.
comments.request: Clearly state what was measured versus inferred and note this caveat.
comments.quote: I suggest clearly indicating what was measured (density and conductivity) and what was inferred from these measurements (productivity and salinity).

comments.issue: The closeness of Euglyphids and forams is overstated given their >500 million year divergence.
comments.request: Acknowledge the deep divergence in the text.
comments.quote: Ok Euglyphids are closer to forams, but still these two groups diverged >500 million years ago.

comments.issue: "Population" is used where "community" is meant; the two are not interchangeable.
comments.request: Review and correct population/community usage throughout.
comments.quote: Often the word “population” is used instead of community. The two are not exchangeable!

comments.issue: A relevant reference on TA for sea-level rise and tectonic activity is missing at L129.
comments.request: Consider citing Shennan et al. (1999).
comments.quote: This ref may be of interest regarding the use of testate amoebae for both sea-level rise as well as tectonic activity

comments.issue: Wording at L138 could be improved, and singular/plural usage for testate amoeba is inconsistent.
comments.request: Rephrase as suggested and review singular/plural usage.
comments.quote: Perhaps better “TAs can serve as early indicators”

comments.issue: The statement on TA diet omits other protists and invertebrates.
comments.request: Add the cited food sources to this statement.
comments.quote: TA also feed on other protists (including testate amoebae) and invertebrates

comments.issue: Peat is called a sediment, which is inaccurate.
comments.request: Replace "sediment" by "sample".
comments.quote: Sediments are deposited in a water column. Peat is therefore generally not a sediment. Replace “sediment” by “sample”.

comments.issue: The chronology appears to assume a constant 1 mm/yr accumulation rate without this being stated clearly.
comments.request: State clearly that the chronology is approximate and illustrative.
comments.quote: was the chronology only based on the assumption that the accumulation rate was constant at 1mm/yr?

comments.issue: Fig. 1D axis legend and caption do not indicate it is a DCA; same for Fig. 3 and Ext. Table 2.
comments.request: Update the axis legends and captions accordingly.
comments.quote: Fig 1. D is DCA, right? then modify y axis legend and caption. Also fig. 3, Ext. Table 2

comments.issue: Ext. Fig. 6 caption does not say where the sites are.
comments.request: Add site location information to the caption.
comments.quote: In the caption you may want to give a little more info about where the sites are.

reviews.assessment: Well written and neat, but reservations about missing covariates, untested causal effects and unsupported functional claims.
strengths: well written and easy to read
new and important information on TA as bioindicators

comments.issue: Conductivity is the only environmental variable considered, though soil and plant variables co-vary with it.
comments.request: Include other environmental variables to disentangle the drivers.
comments.quote: Plant composition, soil chemistry, soil water content are important drivers of microbial communities and are likely to change both within ecosystem types and across ecosystems

comments.issue: The effect of salinization is not directly tested; systems differ in communities, vegetation and soils.
comments.request: Test salinization directly, e.g. with salt-addition treatments.
comments.quote: Connected to my previous comment, the effect of salinization is not directly tested here.

comments.issue: The assumption that TA shifts trigger shifts in soil microbial functioning is unsupported; functional redundancy could compensate.
comments.request: Add functional traits/indices or soften the claim.
comments.quote: shifts in testate amoebae will trigger important shifts in soil microbial functioning. This assumption is not supported by the data

comments.issue: The palaeoecological section is superficial and poorly connected to the first part of the paper.
comments.request: Deepen and better integrate the palaeoecological analyses.
comments.quote: I found this section too superficial and not well connected with the first part of the paper.

comments.issue: Fig. 2 shows the response of TA to time, not the response to state change.
comments.request: Present the state-change response instead.
comments.quote: Fig. 2 does not show the response of TA to state change but their response to time

comments.issue: Indicator-species and broken-line analyses could identify and track salinity-driven state change.
comments.request: Use TITAN and broken-line models to identify indicator species and thresholds.
comments.quote: I would run an analysis such as TITAN (doi: 10.1111/j.2041-210X.2009.00007.x) which identifies the species that respond positively and negatively to increasing salinity

comments.issue: "Productivity" is used to describe abundance, which is inappropriate.
comments.request: Use a term appropriate to abundance rather than productivity.
comments.quote: I struggled with the term ‘productivity’ to define the abundance of individuals.

comments.issue: Relative and absolute abundance and living and dead individuals are mixed confusingly.
comments.request: Clarify and justify these data choices and whether results agree.
comments.quote: Relative and absolute abundance data are used in a mixed way and this is confusing.

comments.issue: How z-scores were obtained and how they relate to the linear regressions is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the derivation of z-scores and their uncertainty.
comments.quote: This is not clear how ‘z-scores’ have been obtained.

comments.issue: The data compilation lacks detail on how sample environments differ along transects.
comments.request: Add details on the sampled transects and environments.
comments.quote: More details on this would be really useful to better understand the paper.

comments.issue: Calling testate amoebae a "study system" is inaccurate.
comments.request: Use "a model organism" instead.
comments.quote: I would not call testate amoebae a ‘study system’. Perhaps ‘a model organism’.

comments.issue: The idea of "generalist" species is not clearly defined or justified.
comments.request: Clarify how generalist species are defined and identified.
comments.quote: I did not fully understand the idea of ‘generalist’ species in the paper.

comments.issue: Species tolerance cannot be tested reliably with relative abundance data; null models would be better.
comments.request: Use null models to test the tolerance assumptions.
comments.quote: Using relative abundance data to test the tolerance of species to certain conditions may be not the best approach. The use of null models would be more appropriate to test such assumptions.

title: Low‐salinity transitions drive abrupt microbial response to sea‐level change

study.system: grassland aboveground biomass; 72 global NutNet sites

editor_summary: Editor: two reviewers see high novelty potential with major revision; third objects to inclusion of successional/non-grassland sites; reject with option to resubmit substantially revised.

reviews.assessment: Finds the findings extend understanding of micronutrients but requires SEM pathways and missing analyses to be shown.
strengths: extends understanding of micronutrients and their interaction with macronutrients

comments.issue: Soil predictors are treated as independent of climate in the SEM, omitting climate-to-soil pathways.
comments.request: Add pathways linking climate and soil predictor groups.
comments.quote: soil physicochemical properties (e.g. CEC, SOM, C: N, and pH) are primarily controlled by climate factors (e.g. mean annual precipitation and mean annual temperature). Therefore, the authors need to add pathways between the three groups and predictors.

comments.issue: The analysis accounting for management effects is not described or presented.
comments.request: Describe it and show results, at least in supplementary material.
comments.quote: The authors should clearly state what kind of analysis was performed to reduce the noise derived from management practices on biomass variation?

comments.issue: The additional analysis excluding high-pH calcareous sites is neither described nor shown.
comments.request: Describe it and present the results.
comments.quote: What additional analysis you performed? Can the relevant data be presented in results?

comments.issue: The model-selection index (e.g. AIC/AICc) used in glmulti is not stated.
comments.request: State which index was used.
comments.quote: The authors should clearly state what kind of index (e.g. AIC, AICc or others?) was used to determine the factors that best explain the variation in biomass?

comments.issue: Two reference formats need checking (lines 160-161, 217-218).
comments.request: Check the reference formatting.
comments.quote: Line 160-161, checking the format of reference. Line 217-218, checking the format of reference.

reviews.assessment: Considers the study worthy of publication but wants more applied discussion and better justification of site splitting and nutrient terminology.
strengths: important advance showing micronutrients explain among-site variation

comments.issue: The discussion is mundane and does not explain which soils or climates make micronutrients limiting, so readers cannot apply the findings.
comments.request: Discuss how soil type/structure and climate affect micronutrient availability.
comments.quote: some discussion of the exact manner in which soil type/structure and climate influenced the level of micronutrient availability

comments.issue: The high/low splits of N deposition and soil C:N lack rationale and ignore the data distribution.
comments.request: Justify the split or try low/mid/high categories.
comments.quote: I’d like to see some rationale behind the way that N deposition and soil C:N were split into high and low categories, ideally linked to an examination of the distribution of the data

comments.issue: The primary versus secondary nutrient distinction is unfounded; all are essential elements.
comments.request: Use a more nuanced, defensible terminology.
comments.quote: I really hate the introduction of the concept of primary and secondary nutrients. They are ALL essential elements, required for the primary metabolic processes of plants.

comments.issue: The abstract is vague and does not reflect the paper's content.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract to reflect the content.
comments.quote: Abstract. The results and conclusions are very vague and don’t reflect the content of the paper.

comments.issue: 8 line-level copy edits (hyphens, word choice, grammar, tense).
comments.quote: l. 203. Why the inverted sentence? It is ugly.

comments.issue: 'Secondary nutrient concentration' is undefined and the sentence about NP limitations is sloppy.
comments.request: Define the term and rephrase the sentence.
comments.quote: l. 144-5. What is a “secondary nutrient concentration”? What nutrients are secondary?

comments.issue: The idea of a 'secondary nutrient' has no basis; less-studied nutrients are not secondary.
comments.request: Replace the secondary nutrient label.
comments.quote: l. 148. Again, where does this idea of a “secondary nutrient” come from?

comments.issue: How management effects were excluded is not demonstrated, and management may contribute to the important soil properties.
comments.request: Show the management-exclusion analysis in the supplement.
comments.quote: I think it is important to demonstrate, at least in supplementary materials, how management effects were excluded.

comments.issue: The primary/secondary distinction is defined only at line 264 and is disliked.
comments.request: Adopt 'commonly studied macro-nutrients' and 'less-studied nutrients' instead.
comments.quote: l. 264. Ah, finally we have the definition of “secondary” nutrients as distinct from “primary”.

comments.issue: The high/low cut-off is defined far from where the idea is introduced.
comments.request: State the cut-off when the split is introduced.
comments.quote: l. 283. What was the cut-off for the two categories of both variables into high and low?

reviews.assessment: Not compelled by the topic or results; questions the definition of grassland and finds the analyses too complicated and arbitrary to accept.

comments.issue: Analyses use variable numbers of sites across subsets, making them hard to interpret.
comments.request: Report and justify the varying site numbers across analyses.
comments.quote: the very complicated analyses that included the variable numbers of sites used in subsets of the analyses

comments.issue: Sites with high precipitation are likely successional vegetation rather than true grasslands, which could drive the precipitation-biomass relationships.
comments.request: Define grassland and address the influence of wet, successional sites.
comments.quote: What is a grassland? It appears that the authors assume that any location that is dominated by herbs, many of which are grasses or graminoids, qualifies as a grassland.

comments.issue: The analysis description is overly complicated with seemingly arbitrary decisions, undermining confidence in the results.
comments.request: Simplify and justify the analytical decisions.
comments.quote: I found the description of the analyses in this manuscript to be so complicated, with many what seemed to be arbitrary decisions that it completely undermined both my interest and willingness to accept the results and conclusions of the manuscript.

comments.issue: The data and analyses are too complex for most readers, who may rely only on the abstract's claim.
comments.request: Make the manuscript more accessible.
comments.quote: My final concern is that many if not most readers will not be willing to invest the time it will take to understand the data and analyses

title: Soil properties as key predictors of global grassland production: Have we overlooked micronutrients?

study.system: empirical plant-animal mutualistic networks; eco-evolutionary simulations

editor_summary: Reviewers were generally positive but want methods clarified and analyses expanded, with Reviewer 2 suggesting analytical approximations in addition to simulations.

reviews.assessment: Important topic, but the abruptness metric and the causal role of individual variation are questioned, along with model presentation details.
strengths: important topic: interaction loss threatens biodiversity
important to know if populations can evolve fast enough

comments.issue: It is unclear which of the many per-step slopes is used as the abruptness metric.
comments.request: State which slope is used (average or largest before collapse).
comments.quote: I do not understand very well the use of the metric for "abruptness" of the collapse, the slope of decline of total community abundance, i.e., the quantity (N(t+1) - N(t))/(γ0(t+1)-γ0(t))

comments.issue: Abrupt collapse may reflect density scale and strength decrease rather than individual variation; the slope metric is scale-dependent.
comments.request: Use a relative slope divided by pre-change density N(t).
comments.quote: The problem in my opinion is that the slope metric is affected by the scale of population densities.

comments.issue: Model symbols such as N and the density functions p(z) are not explained and notation is inconsistent.
comments.request: Explain all symbols and use uniform notation, e.g. vector N and tau for handling time.
comments.quote: In the presentation of the model (pages 5-6 of 24) some symbols are not explained, such as N (sum of all Ni) and the probability density functions p(z).

comments.issue: The interaction-width parameter w is not expressed so that width matches trait units.
comments.request: Write w squared in the interaction strength function.
comments.quote: For the interaction strength function gamma(z,z') in line 136-137, I suggest writing the "w" squared, so that the width is in the same units as the trait variable.

comments.issue: No table lists the model symbols and parameters.
comments.request: Add a table of symbols and parameters.
comments.quote: It would be nice if there is a small table listing the symbols and parameters from the model.

comments.issue: Figure citations in the extinction results paragraph are wrong (Fig. 2A should be Fig. 3; Fig. 3B should be Fig. 3C).
comments.request: Correct the figure references.
comments.quote: In Page 11 of 24 the author describes the results about extinction simulations and refers to Fig 2A in line 263. I think he should be referring to Fig. 3 instead.

reviews.assessment: Finds the work interesting and valuable, but asks for analytical approximations, noise robustness checks and clearer notation.
strengths: results beneficial to understanding ecological transitions

comments.issue: Results rest purely on simulations with no analytical support.
comments.request: Provide analytical arguments, at least for the reduced model.
comments.quote: This work seems to be driven merely by simulations. However, theoretical illustrations and approximations are necessarily important to demonstrate the rigorousness of the main results.

comments.issue: Robustness of results to noise perturbations is untested.
comments.request: Test additive and multiplicative noise perturbations.
comments.quote: It is not clear about the robustness of the current results against the noise perturbations. Both additive noise and multiplicative noise are suggested to be taken into account.

comments.issue: The choice of uniform competition coefficients is unjustified and may drive the results.
comments.request: Justify the distribution and test its influence on results.
comments.quote: In the simulations, the competition coefficients are sampled from the uniform distribution. It is not clear that why such a specific distribution is used. Does this specific configuration influences the main results majorly?

comments.issue: Variables and notations of the differential and integral equation models are not fully explained in the main text.
comments.request: Provide more readable explanations of variables and notation.
comments.quote: The variables and notations in those models of differential and integral equations are not fully illustrated illustrated in the main text.

title: The impact of individual variation on abrupt collapses in mutualistic networks

study.system: soil and litter microbiome; forest plots resampled over years

editor_summary: Editor notes R1 found limited novelty and a descriptive paper, R3 asks to separate results and discussion, and careful consideration of all referee comments is required.

reviews.assessment: Well-written with an interesting dataset, but descriptive, speculative and lacking mechanistic or climate analyses.

comments.issue: Results and discussion are merged; little discussion and mostly speculative.
comments.request: Present results and discussion separately, methods and results before discussion.
comments.quote: in my opinion a stronger paper would have been obtained if the results and discussion were presented separately and the Materials and Methods and Results were presented before the Discussion

comments.issue: Paper is descriptive with no mechanistic drivers or ecosystem-functioning implications and no clear novel insight.
comments.request: Move beyond describing change to mechanistic understanding.
comments.quote: without a mechanistic understanding of the drivers of temporal turnover or the impact of temporal turnover on ecosystem functioning, this paper does not provide any particular novel insights

comments.issue: Figure 2 lacks assessment of direction and components of turnover; more advanced turnover methods exist.
comments.request: Use methods decomposing turnover into loss, gain and replacement.
comments.quote: There are more advanced ways to assess temporal turnover than performing an NMDS or calculating Sorensen similarities.

comments.issue: Climate was not included in the analysis, so drivers of temporal turnover remain unexplored.
comments.request: Include climate variables to investigate drivers of turnover.
comments.quote: Climate (e.g. prolonged periods of drought) can be expected to have a pronounced impact on microbial communities, but this variable was not included in the analysis.

reviews.assessment: Solid sampling and analyses with novel first quantification; strengthen by testing climate drivers and adding seasonal comparison.
strengths: solid sampling design and statistical analyses
first quantification of year-to-year variation across functional groups

comments.issue: Observed compositional changes could partly reflect temperature and precipitation, but weather data were not compared.
comments.request: Compare local weather-station data with compositional changes.
comments.quote: If no temperature and precipitation data are available for the site, then the closest weather station should still give valuable data to test if indeed the observed compositional changes can be explained in part by differences in temperature and/or precipitation

comments.issue: Seasonal comparisons are missing; seasonal versus yearly turnover rates should be compared.
comments.request: Add a seasonal versus yearly turnover comparison, e.g. in the discussion.
comments.quote: I miss the seasonal comparisons even though it has been studied before. In this case, it would have been interesting to compare the seasonal vs. yearly turnover rates.

comments.issue: Line 253: latitude and longitude are switched and the degree symbols are misplaced.
comments.request: Correct the coordinates and symbols.
comments.quote: Please, correct latitude and longitude, currently the values are switched, also delete the ' after N and put an ' after 19

reviews.assessment: Important gap and thorough setup, but presentation, statistical rigor and data availability require substantial improvement.

comments.issue: Joint results/discussion section leaves both sections incomplete.
comments.request: Separate and rewrite the results and discussion sections.
comments.quote: The presentation of a joint results/discussion section leaves both sections wanting of further information. I would advise that these be separated and rewritten.

comments.issue: Model estimates are missing and compositional differences are not tested rigorously.
comments.request: Report model estimates and perform PERMANOVA on multivariate analyses.
comments.quote: For example, models are run but model estimates are not provided. Differences in community composition are mentioned, but not assessed rigorously, which undermines the findings.

comments.issue: Imprecision throughout, with missing units at many lines.
comments.request: Add units and precise values throughout.
comments.quote: The lack of precision is a serious problem throughout the manuscript, some examples are L133, L136L146 (units missing), L152 (unit), L155-166, etc.

comments.issue: How much variability in community composition is explained by time is not quantified.
comments.request: Run an RDA to quantify variance explained by time.
comments.quote: In addition to determining the turnover rate, I would also be curious to see how much of the variability in community composition is explained by time (hint: an RDA).

comments.issue: Data were not made publicly available.
comments.request: Make the data publicly available.
comments.quote: I was disappointed to see that the authors have not made their data publicly available. Please amend!

comments.issue: Averaging C and N measurements may impede assessing their combined effect with time.
comments.request: Explain why C and N were averaged and address the implications.
comments.quote: Why did the authors average C and N measurements (L296)? Doesn't this impede assessing the combined effect of these abiotic variables and time (L370-378)?

comments.issue: Presence/absence versus relative abundance choice and dormant taxa effects are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this decision and the dormant taxa literature (Lennon).
comments.quote: The decision to perform all assessments using presence/absence data rather than relative abundance is an important one, as it would highlight the effect of dormant taxa on turnover rates (L222) but is not discussed anywhere in the manuscript

comments.issue: Fungal trait framework and bacterial taxonomic binning are treated as equivalent although they are not.
comments.request: Explicitly discuss the non-equivalence of the two approaches.
comments.quote: The authors also decide to use a trait framework for fungi and a taxonomic approach to binning bacteria, but treat them as equivalent. They are not and this should be explicitly discussed.

comments.issue: Relevance of model intercepts given the experimental setup is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the meaning and relevance of model intercepts.
comments.quote: I would expect further discussion on the relevance of the intercepts in the models, given the particular experimental setup in this experiment

comments.issue: Relevance of precise spatial sampling is unclear because samples per plot were homogenized.
comments.request: Explain the purpose of the spatial sampling given homogenization.
comments.quote: However, I have a hard time finding the relevance of the spatial sampling given that samples from each plot were homogenized in the end anyway (L274-279).

comments.issue: Shaded error in Figure 2 appears too small for the variance in the data.
comments.request: Check and correct the error shading in Figure 2.
comments.quote: The shaded error in figure 2 seems too small for the variance in the data

comments.issue: Many unsupported claims in L199-201 and L204-209.
comments.request: Support these claims with additional statistics.
comments.quote: there are many unsupported claims throughout the manuscript (additional statistics would help but not entirely fix the following): L199-201, L204-209

comments.issue: Two important microbiome turnover articles are missing from the discussion.
comments.quote: Two important articles looking at turnover in microbiomes should be added to the discussion in this manuscript

comments.issue: L103: mentioning resilience is misleading because sites were specifically disturbed.
comments.request: Revise the resilience wording.
comments.quote: in L103 the mentioning of resilience is misleading as the authors specifically disturbed sites

comments.issue: Methods lack information, e.g. how the fungal traits database was used (L338).
comments.request: Describe how the fungal traits database was used.
comments.quote: further information is needed in the methods, for example how was the fungaltraits database used (L338)

comments.issue: Sampling design and its relevance are unclear, giving the impression of repeated experiments in different forests.
comments.request: Describe the sampling design more thoroughly.
comments.quote: Until the end of the manuscript, I had the impression that the authors had repeated the experiment in different forests.

title: Temporal turnover of the soil microbiome composition is guild‐specific

study.system: simulated and bacterial communities; time series, interaction Jacobian networks

editor_summary: Serious issues: misleading notation and 'time-varying interactions' terminology, missing methodology, false nonlinear-dynamics claims, and unclear scope/limitations; reframe around Jacobian elements, drop the topology analysis, and prove robustness.

reviews.assessment: Appealing method but finds the 'time-varying interactions' framing misleading and raises concerns about truncation, informativeness, thresholds and keystone claims.
strengths: very appealing to the readership of Ecology Letters

comments.issue: Jacobian elements are time-varying by definition, but the paper did not infer genuinely time-varying interaction matrices despite the title and abstract.
comments.request: State clearly that the method infers Jacobian elements, not time-varying matrices.
comments.quote: I thought the authors solved the latter case, i.e., inferring the time-varying M matrix in the Ricker model or the time-varying A matrix in the GLV model.

comments.issue: Only the last 100 of 1000 simulated steps were used, with no practical guidance for choosing time steps in real data.
comments.request: Provide practical guidance for choosing time steps.
comments.quote: For real time series, how shall the end users of their method choose the appropriate time steps for further analysis? The authors didn't offer any clear and practical guidance.

comments.issue: It is not shown that the time series are informative enough, for example via persistent excitation or shuffled-data tests.
comments.request: Test informativeness, for example with shuffled time series.
comments.quote: For both the model and real time series analyzed in this paper, how can the authors ensure the temporal data is informative enough to infer interactions?

comments.issue: Species below the arbitrary 0.1% relative abundance threshold are ignored without justification or sensitivity testing.
comments.request: Justify the threshold and test its sensitivity.
comments.quote: First of all, the threshold 0.1% is quite arbitrary. The authors didn't offer clear justification why they chose this threshold.

comments.issue: Keystone species are claimed from node centrality without evidence of disproportionate impact, and true keystones may have been excluded.
comments.request: Demonstrate disproportionate impact or avoid the keystone label.
comments.quote: But the authors didn't provide any evidence that the keystone species identified by them do have such a large impact on the system.

reviews.assessment: Critical: claims about steady state and firstness are false, the synthetic validation uses constant interactions, and forecasting, code and references are inadequate.

comments.issue: The claim that many other techniques require steady state is false; transients are easiest to learn and steady state is essentially unidentifiable.
comments.request: Correct this claim about steady state.
comments.quote: The authors state that many other techniques require the dynamics to be at steady state. This is false.

comments.issue: The method is claimed for time-varying interactions, yet the synthetic validation uses discretized GLV/Ricker dynamics with constant parameters.
comments.request: Use synthetic models with genuinely time-varying interactions.
comments.quote: The authors claim the method is for time varying interactions but choose to use for synthetic data the discretized glv dynamics

comments.issue: The method is not benchmarked against simple regression on the synthetic and real data.
comments.request: Benchmark against simple regression.
comments.quote: How would simply performing regression as above perform on your synthetic AND real data?

comments.issue: Single timepoint forecasting is insufficient; performance degradation over longer horizons is not shown.
comments.request: Evaluate longer forecast horizons.
comments.quote: Single timepoint forecasting is not sufficient. You will want to show how the performance of the algorithms degrade as the forecast horizon is extended

comments.issue: Code is promised only after acceptance instead of being released now.
comments.request: Release the code on GitHub now.
comments.quote: I am not sure in this day and age one can say they will release the code "after" acceptance.

comments.issue: Key references on inference of GLV dynamics for microbiomes are missing.
comments.request: Cite these works.
comments.quote: missing many references to authors performing inference on glv dynamics for the microbiome/bacteria some of these authors have multiple papers on the topic beyond these

comments.issue: The claim of being the first to learn high-dimensional dynamics is incorrect given prior literature.
comments.request: Soften the firstness claim and cite prior work.
comments.quote: The statement in the end saying that this is the first paper to learn high dimensional dynamics is not correct.

comments.issue: Both k and t index time, and the mathematics in the supplement needs extensive cleanup.
comments.request: Clean up the notation and mathematics.
comments.quote: Be careful with notation both k and t are used to index time. In general the mathematics in the supplement needs to be extensively cleaned up.

comments.issue: Forecasting details are insufficient and data leakage is not ruled out.
comments.request: Describe the forecasting setup and avoid data leakage.

title: A genetically based ecological trade‐off contributes to setting a geographic range limit

editor_summary: Three reviews found the paper interesting but raised moderately strong concerns about its conceptual connection to the literature, real-world applicability and case-study specifics; a revision could be resubmitted.

reviews.assessment: Novel and important concept, but its applicability beyond seed-tray experiments and the validity of the experimental assessment are doubtful.

comments.issue: The framework seems confined to sand-tray GUD experiments, limiting its relevance to real resource patches and community ecology.

comments.issue: The experimental setup is poorly described: patch distances, deployments, sites and independence of sampling units are unclear.
comments.request: Provide more setup details and figures, including distances and deployments.
