comments.quote: I have the impression that the results reported here are just reflecting results on trend analysis done elsewhere because of the way resilience is measured.

comments.issue: Time series span different periods, which is counterintuitive for a global assessment of current resilience trends.
comments.request: Present the decade-resolved results as the main global assessment.
comments.quote: for a global assessment of resilience- as the title of the paper implies- it seems a bit counterintuitive that the timeseries were used span different periods of time

title: Global patterns of resilience decline in vertebrate populations

study.system: grazing ecosystems; phase-separation model of herbivore-plant dynamics

editor_summary: All three referees like the idea but find the manuscript difficult to read and hardly accessible to a wide ecological audience; asks for major revision, real-world relevance, and better justified model assumptions.

reviews.assessment: Original and interesting idea, but the introduction and discussion are too narrow and lack real-world empirical examples.
strengths: novel alternative to classical Turing pattern explanations

comments.issue: The introduction is too narrow because it ignores existing literature on grazing-driven patterns such as shifting mosaics and power-law patchiness.
comments.request: Broaden the introduction to cover previously advanced grazing-pattern mechanisms.
comments.quote: I feel that the rather quick focus on regular patterns in grazed ecosystems makes the introduction is too narrow here.

comments.issue: No empirical example shows whether the patterns are regular or grazing-caused, and coarsening is never checked in real systems.
comments.request: Analyse real patterns for regularity and coarsening, or name specific ecosystems.
comments.quote: but these examples are not analyzed in any way to see if the patterns are indeed regular and caused by grazing

comments.issue: The discussion of trophic interactions as pattern drivers is too shallow and ignores earlier studies.
comments.request: Expand the discussion and cite earlier trophic-pattern studies.
comments.quote: I think it would be worthwhile to touch upon this topic more in-depth in the discussion as this is not the first study revealing how trophic interactions generate regular patterns

reviews.assessment: Intriguing alternative to Turing patterns that should interest a wide audience, but technical and lacking real-data tests.
strengths: nice and intriguing alternative pattern formation process

comments.issue: There appear to be little to no concrete real-life data studies of this pattern-formation process.
comments.quote: there appear to be little to no concrete studies of real-life data on this type of pattern formation process

comments.issue: The manuscript is quite technical and mathematical at times, reducing its appeal to non-theorists.
comments.quote: I do think it is quite technical/mathematical at times

comments.issue: The specific functional form of equation (1) is not general, and the consequences of these choices are unexplored.
comments.request: Explain how the functional-form choices matter and explore a general V(P,H).
comments.quote: The choice of functional form in equation (1) is specific and not general as said in the text.

comments.issue: It is unclear at what simulation times the pattern snapshots were taken.
comments.request: State which simulation times the snapshots represent.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me at what times of the simulations these snapshots were taken

comments.issue: Whether equilibrium patterns and long-term behaviour were inspected at all is unclear.
comments.request: Inspect equilibrium patterns and long-term behaviour of the model.
comments.quote: so I wondered if equilibrium patterns and long-term behaviour was inspected at all

comments.issue: The model and results are not sufficiently related to the physics theory of phase separation.
comments.request: Add text connecting the model and results to phase-separation theory.
comments.quote: It might also be good to include a bit more text relating model and results to the physics theory of phase separation.

comments.issue: Discussion of movement limitations is vague and does not point to the taxis literature.
comments.request: Make these limitations explicit and cite taxis/chemotaxis studies.
comments.quote: I think these could be a bit more explicit and point to existing literature exploring these

comments.issue: It is unclear why all uniform steady states must be unstable and why condition (S14) must hold for all p0.
comments.request: Explain why all steady states need to be unstable.
comments.quote: Why is that? It could well be that just some of these are unstable, while others are stable, right?

comments.issue: Whether restricting parameters to these conditions affects the emerging patterns is unknown.
comments.request: Assess the effect of parameter restrictions on pattern dynamics.
comments.quote: I am also wondering if restricting parameters to these conditions has any effect on the (transient of) patterns that emerge?

comments.issue: The cubic dispersion relation may allow positive growth rates with sigma''(0) < 0, an unexplored regime.
comments.request: Consider whether this alternative parameter regime exists in the model.
comments.quote: Did you consider this possibility and do you know if this is this actually possible in the model?

comments.issue: Table S1's specification does not say it refers to initial conditions; the reviewer had to check the code.
comments.request: State clearly that this specification refers to initial conditions.
comments.quote: and had to look into the code to figure out that this is about the initial conditions

comments.issue: The scalings on Page 5 may be incorrect or inconsistent with the rest of the text.
comments.request: Check the scalings for correctness and consistency.
comments.quote: Could you make sure the scalings given are correct and consistent with the rest of the text

comments.issue: In (S7) the definitions of N12 and N21 are switched.
comments.request: Correct the swapped definitions.
comments.quote: The definitions of N12 and N21 are switched (though consistent with the rest of the text).

comments.issue: For the sign of N21 it would help to recall that v(p) = alpha p^2 + beta p + 1 > 0.
comments.request: Add this reminder to clarify the sign of N21.
comments.quote: For the sign of N21 it might be useful to recall that v(p) = alpha p^2 + beta p + 1 > 0

reviews.assessment: Novel and interesting idea, but several model assumptions and technical terms make the paper inaccessible to most readers.

comments.issue: Gradient operators in equations 2-3 are not defined or explained for non-specialists.
comments.request: Define and explain the gradient operators.
comments.quote: need to be defined and explained to readers that do not work with spatial systems in continuous time and space

comments.issue: The herbivore flux J lacks an intuitive explanation.
comments.request: Give a more intuitive explanation of the herbivore flux.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to get a more intuitive explanation of the herbivore flux (J).

comments.issue: The overcrowding-prevention term comes out of nowhere, is unrelated to the model premise, and its necessity is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain its justification, necessity and the consequences of omitting it.
comments.quote: comes out of nowhere and has nothing to di with the underlying premise of the model

comments.issue: Coarsening is not explained, nor why it is crucial for evaluating the model.
comments.request: Explain what coarsening means and why it matters.
comments.quote: It would be good explain what is meant by coarsening and why it is crucial feature in evaluating the model.

comments.issue: Technical terms such as spatial wavelength, structure factor analysis and hyperuniform structure make the paper read like theoretical physics.
comments.request: Move these technical analyses to the supplementary material.
comments.quote: These technical analyses would make more sense in supplementary material. Including them here makes the paper rad much more like a submission to a theoretical physics journal than Ecology Letters.

comments.issue: Figure 5 will not make sense to most ecologists.
comments.request: Make Figure 5 comprehensible to ecologists.
comments.quote: The figures are terrific, with the exception of Fig. 5, which won't make any sense to most ecologists.

comments.issue: Positive first- and second-order P coefficients imply herbivores prefer sites with no plant resources, contrary to foraging theory.
comments.request: Use a negative first-order and a positive V^2 coefficient instead.
comments.quote: It would be more consistent with foraging theory to have a negative coefficient for the first order term and positive coefficient for V^2 term

comments.issue: Background on previously published lattice models of resource-dependent herbivore movement is missing.
comments.request: Cite and discuss these earlier lattice models.
comments.quote: It might help readers better understand the resource-dependent movement hypothesis if the authors provided background on previously published models of lattice cell models for herbivores

title: Foraging behaviours lead to spatiotemporal self‐similar dynamics in grazing ecosystems

study.system: Trinidadian guppies; multi-generational capture-mark-recapture and pedigrees

editor_summary: Editor sees potential for an important contribution but notes all reviewers' concern about the dispersal definition limiting generalisability, plus uncontrolled confounds (longevity, size) obscuring causality; asks for greater analytical rigour.

reviews.assessment: Finds the dispersal–fitness link impressive and interesting, but questions the dispersal metric and whether phenotype-driven alternatives were ruled out.
strengths: rare attempt to link dispersal and fitness in the wild
novel use of mark-recapture with pedigrees

comments.issue: The reasoning behind the prediction and the theory on dispersal–life history relationships are not developed.
comments.request: Expand the introduction on expected positive or negative dispersal–fecundity relationships.
comments.quote: Expanding the introduction to the theory about the possible relationships between dispersal and life-history traits

comments.issue: Whether the dispersal–reproduction relationship varies in time and space is untested.
comments.request: Test interactions of dispersal with season, stream and position in stream.
comments.quote: Another interesting possibility would be to test whether the relationship between dispersal and reproduction differ in time and space

comments.issue: Cumulative distance moved is prospection, not dispersal distance; fish returning to their start are counted as dispersers.
comments.request: Use distance from initial location or dispersal probability and rename the metric.
comments.quote: I am surprized by the metric of dispersal distance used. Classical dispersal kernels are defined as distance from the natal/initial position.

comments.issue: The offspring ratios are not corrected for size, and larger males may be both more dispersive and preferred.
comments.request: Correct the ratios for size to remove this confound.
comments.quote: are these ratios corrected for e.g. size?

comments.issue: The alternative that reproduction-favouring phenotypes drive dispersal or survival was not ruled out.
comments.request: Discuss and rule out phenotype-driven dispersal as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: I however missed how you ruled out the alternative: individuals with traits favouring reproduction (like size, color or other phenotypic attributes) are more likely to disperse (or survive dispersal)?

comments.issue: Dispersal mortality and movements outside focal areas, and whether survival correlates with fecundity, are not considered.
comments.request: Quantify dispersal mortality and test the survival–fecundity correlation.
comments.quote: How much dispersal mortality or movements outside the focal areas can play here? Does survival correlate to fecondity?

comments.issue: Why within-population movement counts as dispersal and why 10 m is the threshold need justification.
comments.request: Clarify the dispersal definition and justify the 10 m threshold.
comments.quote: it would be worth clarifying why movements within each of these populations can be defined as dispersal

comments.issue: It is unclear whether pedigree and mark-recapture periods match and whether last sampling periods were excluded.
comments.request: Clarify the period overlap and the exclusion of last sampling periods.
comments.quote: Data used to reconstruct pedigrees has been collected during the same period as the mark-recapture data?

reviews.assessment: Values the mark-recapture and pedigree data but doubts that small-scale movement is dispersal and worries longevity confounds the headline result.
strengths: detailed mark-recapture information combined with pedigrees

comments.issue: The same data resource has been analysed in other work, which the reviewer notes.
comments.quote: I note however that the same data resource has been analysed in other work

comments.issue: Distances travelled are small (<20 m) and likely reflect routine daily activity rather than dispersal.
comments.request: Show that the recorded movement really represents dispersal.
comments.quote: Yet, if we examine the data tables the distances traveled are quite small – average dispersal distances are <20m

comments.issue: Movement is strongly correlated with longevity, and longer-lived fish also have more mating opportunities.
comments.request: Disentangle movement from longevity in the analyses.
comments.quote: Have the variables of movement and longevity been sufficiently disentangled in the analyses?

comments.issue: No analysis restricts the dataset to longer-lived individuals to check the movement–fitness link.
comments.request: Repeat the analysis on individuals that lived at least five months.
comments.quote: a separate analysis focussing just on the individuals that lived for a reasonable number of (at least 5) months

comments.issue: The title implies a causal relationship although the evidence presented is correlational.
comments.request: Temper the causal implication of the title.
comments.quote: the title ‘fitness benefits of dispersal’ implies a causal relationship

comments.issue: The rationale for the work is insufficiently justified and the core question needs tightening.
comments.request: Tighten the core question and its justification.
comments.quote: A further concern is that the rationale for the work is insufficiently well justified

comments.issue: If dispersal reduces inbreeding, the authors apparently have data to test this benefit.
comments.request: Test whether dispersal reduces inbreeding with the existing data.
comments.quote: if an advantage of dispersal is that it reduces inbreeding, presumably the authors have the data to test this?

comments.issue: Classic work, particularly by Haskins, is not referenced.
comments.request: Cite Haskins and related classic work.
comments.quote: The authors fail to reference some classic work, particularly that by Haskins, which is relevant here

comments.issue: Field assistants central to the study are not named, and some may warrant co-authorship.
comments.request: Name the field assistants in the acknowledgements and consider co-authorship.
comments.quote: I am sorry to see that the many field assistants whose role in field work was central to the study are not even named in the acknowledgements

reviews.assessment: Very good paper documenting rare wild movement data, with many suggestions to clarify methods, expand context and strengthen analyses.
strengths: documents animal movement in the wild
breadth and depth of the larger dataset

comments.issue: The dispersal measure conflates active and passive (flood-driven) downstream movement.
comments.request: Clarify and separate active versus passive downstream movement.
comments.quote: I think the authors should clarify that some downstream movement is active and some is passive

comments.issue: Downstream movement during and after high water is not quantified and “flooding” is undefined.
comments.request: Quantify movement during versus outside high water and define flooding.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to quantify downstream movement during and after high water levels versus at other times?

comments.issue: The paper is about consequences of moving, not decisions to move, but the Introduction does not emphasize this.
comments.request: Emphasize in the Introduction that the focus is consequences of movement.
comments.quote: it would be useful to emphasize in the Intro that the paper is not about how the fish decided when to move, but it is about the consequences of moving

comments.issue: What drives movement, such as pool/riffle morphology and local density, is not analysed.
comments.request: Use stream morphology data to model the probability of moving.
comments.quote: It would be useful to learn about the probability of moving (or not moving), based on the morphology of the specific pools/riffles

comments.issue: Male maturity at the start of dispersal events and the timing of size measurement are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify male maturity and whether size was measured at start or end.
comments.quote: At the start of each dispersal event, were all of the males already mature?

comments.issue: Male colouration, which females may prefer, is not included in the reproductive success analysis.
comments.request: Include male colouration, at least orange area, as a covariate.
comments.quote: it would be very useful to include some information about the males’ colouration (at least the area of orange if that is what females in these populations prefer)

comments.issue: Immigrants from the introduction experiment may confound male success; a single male's hybrid index cannot capture social effects on female choice.
comments.request: Account for immigrant phenotypes and their effects on female choice.
comments.quote: including the hybrid index of a single male doesn’t account for the effects of these individuals on female choice and other males’ fitness

comments.issue: Immigrants could inflate apparent novelty effects on male reproductive success.
comments.request: Repeat the fitness analysis on the first 13 months when immigrants were rare.
comments.quote: Can you look at fitness measures within that first 13 month period when immigrants (from the artificial introduction experiment) were not common?

comments.issue: It is not stated whether predictions differ between males and females.
comments.request: State whether predictions are the same for both sexes.
comments.quote: Are the predictions the same for males and females?

comments.issue: A relevant paper on dispersal benefits to pregnant or inseminated females is not cited.
comments.request: Cite the paper on establishing new populations by pregnant females.
comments.quote: I recommend citing this paper about the fitness advantage of dispersal to pregnant/inseminated females—the opportunity to establish new populations

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits: missing or extra words on lines 145, 245, 358, 329 and wording at line 114.
comments.quote: 114 2014), guppies from a downstream site in From a high predation downstream site.

comments.issue: Model fit was selected with AIC rather than checked through residuals.
comments.request: Check model residuals, e.g. with the DHARMa package.
comments.quote: Instead of using AIC for this, shouldn’t you check the model residuals for fit? The DHARMa package works for GLMs

comments.issue: It is unclear whether upstream and downstream movements were recorded separately.
comments.request: Clarify whether upstream and downstream movements were distinguished.
comments.quote: This was confusing because I thought up versus downstream movements were not recorded separately

comments.issue: The inability of fish in the top pool to move upstream may not be accounted for.
comments.request: Account for the upstream boundary in the analysis.
comments.quote: if it was not possible for guppies in the top pool to move upstream, was that accounted for in the analysis?

comments.issue: Behaviour of fast versus slow growing individuals was not examined.
comments.request: Compare behaviour of fast and slow growing individuals.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to know if there was a difference in the behavior of fast versus slow growing individuals

comments.issue: Line 206 repeats the beginning of the statistics section, which could be streamlined.
comments.request: Streamline the statistics section and state shared model choices once.
comments.quote: Line 206: Repetitive with the beginning of the stats section.

comments.issue: The choice of zero-inflated negative binomial over hurdle models is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the choice of model distribution once.
comments.quote: Can say why zero-inflated negative binomial and not hurdle once, if it applies to all.

comments.issue: The number of times each fish was sampled is not reported.
comments.request: Add the number of sampling events.
comments.quote: Line 233 – it would be useful to add the number of times sampled

comments.issue: With large sample sizes, significance does not show how large the effects are.
comments.request: Report effect sizes for the key results.
comments.quote: With such large sample sizes, small differences are going to be highly significant. So would be useful to know how big an effect this is.

comments.issue: Being swept downstream during floods may not qualify as dispersal, affecting the measure used.
comments.request: Test effects during non-flood periods for all measures.
comments.quote: Is this really dispersal if they're just being swept downstream?

comments.issue: It is unclear which dispersal status level is plotted on line 282.
comments.request: State which level of dispersal status is shown.
comments.quote: Line 282 - Which level of dispersal status (Y or N)?

comments.issue: An additional relevant paper is suggested for page 14.
comments.request: Consider citing the suggested paper.
comments.quote: For page 14, this paper might be of interest

comments.issue: What might trigger dispersal is not discussed.
comments.request: Add conjecture about triggers of dispersal.
comments.quote: Some conjecture about what might trigger dispersal would be useful

comments.issue: The claim that larger males are in better condition may not hold; a size threshold or juvenile condition could explain dispersal.
comments.request: Reconsider the condition interpretation for males.
comments.quote: Are larger males in better condition? I would agree with this statement for females, but not necessarily for males.

comments.issue: Whether dispersal probability stays constant through adult life is unknown.
comments.request: Check whether dispersal probability changes with age.
comments.quote: Can you check to see if the probability remains constant through adult life or if it actually goes up or down in later months?

comments.issue: Dispersal and longevity estimates are biased because emigrants and dead fish are unobserved.
comments.request: Remind readers of this sampling bias.
comments.quote: samples are biased because individuals that move beyond the study area and those that have died cannot be accounted for

comments.issue: A non-significant trend on lines 342-343 is presented as if significant.
comments.request: Focus the paragraph on the significant dispersal effect.
comments.quote: I thought this was a non-significant trend? If so, this is overstated.

comments.issue: Line 362 contradicts line 355, where increased encounters were said to be insufficient.
comments.request: Reconcile the statements about encounter rates.
comments.quote: Just above, line 355, the authors state that increased encounters is not sufficient

comments.issue: Local density could apparently be derived from known dispersal locations at sampling events.
comments.request: Estimate local density from sampling locations and include it.
comments.quote: Wouldn't the authors be able to gauge local density at a given time point as they know the dispersal location of all fish at sampling events?

comments.issue: “Dispersal within streams” on line 360 is imprecise.
comments.request: Specify “dispersal between pools within streams”.
comments.quote: Extend and specify to be “dispersal between pools within streams”

comments.issue: Brighter colouration should be mentioned explicitly in the predation-cost argument.
comments.request: Explicitly mention brighter colouration.
comments.quote: I would explicitly mention brighter colouration

comments.issue: The logic of the sentence on lines 414-415 is not followable.
comments.request: Rewrite that sentence.
comments.quote: I didn’t follow the logic of this

comments.issue: It is not stated whether the focal populations experience high or low predation.
comments.request: State the predation regime of the focal populations.
comments.quote: Are the focal populations high or low predation?

title: Reproductive benefits associated with dispersal in headwater populations of Trinidadian guppies ( Poecilia reticulata )

study.system: freshwater biodiversity research; global survey of 211 researchers

editor_summary: Timely topic with potential, but too broad and lacking detail; all reviewers want fuller description of the five research areas and Figure 1 improved; editor also stresses stakeholder engagement, restructuring bullets, author information, and citing recent works.

reviews.assessment: The goal is laudable and valuable, but the agenda lacks the detail, consistency and citation base to define research priorities effectively.

comments.issue: The 15 needs lack detail and a consistent format, and are not rooted in problem statements; main text and supplement should be streamlined.
comments.request: Rework each need with problem statement, challenge type, examples, solutions and recommendations.
comments.quote: lacks detail needed to sufficiently define a research agenda. Many of the bullet points in the main text are inconsistent in format and content and are not rooted in core problem statements

comments.issue: Citations are sporadic and some agenda items have none, even for well-studied challenges; GBIF is undefined and uncited.
comments.request: Add citations throughout, including for GBIF and well-studied topics.
comments.quote: citations are sporadic throughout, with some agenda items including no citations – even for challenges that are well-studied and have been for decades

comments.issue: The agenda confounds research knowledge gaps with disconnects among researchers, managers and policy makers, calling for more research where existing work suffices.
comments.request: Distinguish the challenge types and cite review papers for well-studied topics such as environmental flows.
comments.quote: the manuscript tends to confound challenges of knowledge gaps due to limited research with challenges of applying existing, ongoing, or future research for more efficient and effective conservation of freshwater ecosystems and their biota

comments.issue: The main text does not say who the authors are, how they were selected, or which communities and sectors they represent, including indigenous knowledge.
comments.request: Summarize author backgrounds, survey selection and representation in the main text.
comments.quote: The manuscript would benefit from more discussion in the main text about who the authors are, why/how they were selected, and which communities they represent.

reviews.assessment: The topic is pressing, but the contribution lacks quantitative evidence and novelty, and its broad scope yields vague, shallow recommendations.

comments.issue: The structured consultation scores and current research effort are not reported, so perceived needs cannot be judged objectively.
comments.request: Report the scores and contrast them with attention such as funding and publications.
comments.quote: the manuscript lacks quantitative evidence: the scores from the “structured consultation” reflecting perceived needs in the field are not reported, nor are current efforts related to each of the proposed recommendations

comments.issue: Much of the content duplicates recent review or perspective papers, limiting novelty.
comments.request: Explain how the global angle builds on or differs from similar papers.
comments.quote: I found much of the content within each of the areas to be rather duplicative of what has already been written (in a more detailed form) in recent review or perspective papers on the topic

comments.issue: The scope is too broad, making recommendations vague and shallow, with technologies such as remote sensing and AI only mentioned in passing.
comments.request: Narrow the focus to fewer areas and go deeper into them.
comments.quote: Third, the scope of the agenda is very broad, which leads to vague recommendations. Even the “concrete actions” or “steps” listed in each area are rather shallow.

comments.issue: Recommendations are not qualified by context or scale, so they lack real-world policy relevance and nuance.
comments.request: Qualify recommendations with scales, contexts and examples of practice.
comments.quote: many recommendations should be qualified to have any real-world policy relevance (e.g. in what cases and at what scales would you “recommend to coordinate monitoring programs”, are you thinking across states/provinces, internationally?

title: A global agenda for advancing freshwater biodiversity research

study.system: mechanically transmitted bee gut pathogens; dose-response and transport models

editor_summary: Editor sees merit but finds the main questions and broad applicability unclear, positioning in epidemiology theory weak and results not comprehensive; inclined to decline with possible resubmission, suggesting type and target reproduction number literature.

reviews.assessment: Thorough, clear framework with only minor suggestions about framing as fomite transmission and a schematic emphasis.

comments.issue: Mechanical vectors should be connected to the common fomite transmission terminology.
comments.request: Emphasise transport or traffic-related fomite transmission earlier.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to emphasize that mechanical vectors can be viewed as a sub-type of fomite transmission

comments.issue: Figure 2 emphasises dose-splitting although the default models re-shed all pathogen in one feces.
comments.request: Focus the schematic on mechanisms behind Figure 3b and Figure 5.
comments.quote: I found the emphasis on dose-splitting a little misleading given that the default in the models is that the mechanical vector re-sheds all surviving pathogen in a single feces

comments.issue: Two line-level typos: faeces/feces in Figure 6d and it will allocates/it allocates on Page 33.
comments.quote: Page 33, lines 13-14: it will allocates -> it allocates

reviews.assessment: Finds the paper interesting and well written but questions the emphasis on mechanical vectors and several statements.
strengths: main results in clear and accessible language

comments.issue: Novelty of focusing on mechanical vectors rather than dose-response is unclear; positioning in dilution theory missing.
comments.request: Connect the study to broader diversity-disease theory.
comments.quote: It’s not clear to me that the main novelty is in studying mechanical vectors (rather than, say, the influence of dose-response relationships) in the context of disease dilution/amplification

comments.issue: Abstract arguments apply to any multi-host system, so the specific focus on mechanical vectors is unjustified.
comments.request: Reframe, e.g. around the role of mechanical vectors in pollinator decline.
comments.quote: These arguments seem like they would equally apply to any system with multiple hosts (or vectors) that vary in competence, so then I wonder why *specifically* we need to study this in mechanical vectors.

comments.issue: The attogen limit could be seen as a binary infection process; the model variant's name is unhelpful.
comments.request: Clarify the interpretation and give the variant a descriptive name.
comments.quote: Is another way of interpreting the “attogen” limit model that infection is essentially a binary process (infected, not)?

comments.issue: Expected statement that mechanical vectors always increase R0 barring feedbacks is missing or delayed.
comments.request: State this expectation explicitly and discuss feedbacks.
comments.quote: I was expecting a strong statement that Equation 2 shows that adding a mechanical vector should always increase R0, barring any feedbacks on the other parameters.

comments.issue: Figure 3 caption's criterion for when mechanical transmission matters is conceptually odd.
comments.request: Reconsider the criterion, e.g. R0 rising above one.
comments.quote: won’t it “matter” in a biological sense any time the contribution raises the R0 above 1, which can happen with substantially lower relative contributions to R0

comments.issue: The no intrinsic reason statement conflicts with the model setup where mechanical vector loads are lower.
comments.request: Reconcile the statement with the setup.
comments.quote: This line is also strange to me given that the set up is that mechanical vectors should have substantially lower pathogen loads than biological vectors or hosts

comments.issue: Calling bees both biological vectors and hosts is confusing when comparing vector types.
comments.request: Use distinct terminology.
comments.quote: bees being referred to both as biological vectors and hosts is quite confusing

comments.issue: Application to zooprophylaxis-type management is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss conditions under which seeding mechanical vectors could reduce disease.
comments.quote: what are the conditions under which seeding communities with mechanical vectors could reduce the spread of disease in pollinators?

comments.issue: No example is given for the food-borne pathogen mentioned at p3, l.19.
comments.request: Give an example.
comments.quote: can you give an example of such a “food-borne pathogen” here?

comments.issue: Whether re-isolate implies infectivity is unclear at p3, l.24-26.
comments.request: Clarify, or drop the example.
comments.quote: Does “re-isolate” imply that they were infective? Clarify if so, and if not, consider dropping this example.

comments.issue: Two line-level wording fixes: becomes/become at p5 l.29 and pre-splint/pre-split in the Fig. 2 caption.
comments.quote: p5, l. 29 - “becomes” -> “become” in “for a bee to becomes”

comments.issue: Five notation corrections in the supplement (S1 pages, equations S3, S4, S6, S10, Table S1).
comments.request: Check and correct the equation subscripts.
comments.quote: S1, p2, line 15. Should n\_q^feces be n\_h^feces?

title: Pathogen transport amplifies or dilutes disease transmission depending on the host dose‐response relationship

study.system: temperate trees; daily radial stem growth, 47 Swiss sites

editor_summary: Editor asks the authors to adequately address the minor points raised by the referees.

reviews.assessment: Clarification requests on concepts, wording and the variance-partitioning model, with no doubts about the core results.

comments.issue: The concept of source and sink limitation is not explained for unfamiliar readers.
comments.request: Explain source and sink limitation more clearly.
comments.quote: it could be useful to better explain the concept of source and sink limitation, since some reader could not be totally familiar with it

comments.issue: The link between source-sink limitation and tree water relations is not spelled out.
comments.request: Add a sentence connecting the concept to tree water relations.
comments.quote: it could be good to spend a sentence to explain in which way it connects with tree water relations, stated right after

comments.issue: The dendrometer mounting description is ambiguous and can be misread as parallel to the slope.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence clearly.
comments.quote: I guess it means that the dendrometers were mounted on the side of the tree which faces the bottom of the slope, but expressed in this way it may sound as the dendrometer is parallel to the slope

comments.issue: The variance-partitioning model is mislabelled and species, site and year should arguably be fixed effects.
comments.request: Reformulate the model specification and wording.
comments.quote: the factors "species", "site" and "year" should be the fixed and not the random ones, since they are the ones of which we actually want to detect the influence on the variance

comments.issue: The paper analyses volumetric diameter growth, not biomass growth, and this distinction is not clear.
comments.request: Specify volumetric growth and cite Cuny et al. (2015) and Lehnebach et al. (2021).
comments.quote: The Authors should specify more clearly that they are dealing with "volumetric growth" (i.e. "increase in diameter") and not considering the "growth in biomass"

comments.issue: Interannual growth differences mentioned in the methods are not visible in the figures.
comments.request: Show interannual growth differences in the figures.
comments.quote: Interannual growth differences are mentioned in the statistical methods, but they are not visible in the figures

comments.issue: It is unclear whether a specific photoperiod length triggers growth at the species level.
comments.request: Clarify the photoperiod-growth initiation link or state that it is absent.
comments.quote: it is not clear if a certain photoperiod length can be associated to the triggering of growth, at least at a species specific level

reviews.assessment: Novel and valuable study with clear methods, but the results text is hard to follow and several details need clarification.

comments.issue: Frequent references to different pictures in the results make the text difficult to read and understand.
comments.request: Make the picture references clearer.
comments.quote: the frequent appearances of different pictures in describing the results made it difficult to read the text and understand the meaning

comments.issue: Previous studies at L109-111 are listed without their results or conclusions.
comments.request: Summarize these studies' conclusions to show the lacking systematic assessment.
comments.quote: in this sentense some previous studies were listed, but no related results. It is suggested that the conclusions of these studies be summarized

comments.issue: Daily growth rate is a time series while other predictors have one value per year; how they fit one regression model is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how these variables were fitted together.
comments.quote: For most variables contain only one value in a year, while "daily growth rate" contains a time series in a single year. My concern is how do these variables fit together in a regression model?

comments.issue: The nesting of year, tree and site is not explained.
comments.request: Explain in detail how the three variables are nested.
comments.quote: there is a need to explain in detail how three variables (year, tree and site) are nested

comments.issue: The abbreviation SWP is used without earlier definition.
comments.request: Define SWP at first use.
comments.quote: the abbreviation "SWP" has not mentiond in the previous text

comments.issue: Figure 3b lacks letters indicating significant ANOVA differences.
comments.request: Add significance letters to Figure 3b.
comments.quote: Figure 3b does not show the letters which give the results of significant differences tested by ANOVA.

comments.issue: Shaded areas indicating 25% and 75% quantiles are described but not visible in Figures S4 and S5.
comments.request: Show the shaded quantile areas as described.
comments.quote: it is mentioned that "shaded areas indicate the 25% and 75% quantiles". However, the shaded part is not shown in the figure somehow.

reviews.assessment: Well planned and important contribution; suggests adding alternative explanations to the discussion.
strengths: well planned, well written and important contribution

comments.issue: The early-wood/late-wood explanation does not explain the distinct break between the two growth peaks.
comments.request: Consider internal rhythmic shoot elongation as an additional driver.
comments.quote: However, that does not explain the distinct break between the two processes. Internal and genetically fixed factors as the rhythmic shoot elongation (also in two peaks) should be taken into consideration

comments.issue: The simple wood-density explanation for species differences in absolute growth rates is not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention wood density as an explanation in the discussion.
comments.quote: the simple explanation for the specific differences in absolute growth rates (wood density) should also be mentioned

title: Number of growth days and not length of the growth period determines radial stem growth of temperate trees

study.system: rapid evolution of life-history traits; 58 studies

editor_summary: Two very positive reviews with minor changes; the editor stresses looking at variance changes, testing whether small effects reflect non-parallel replicate responses, and rewriting the murky inclusion criteria.

reviews.assessment: Very enthusiastic and detailed; strong support with substantial suggestions on inclusion criteria, variance responses and multilevel models.

comments.issue: Many studies appear missing, notably plants, raising questions about taxonomic coverage.
comments.request: Broaden the search or recast and retitle the paper as animal-focused.
comments.quote: I can’t help but think that many studies are missing. For example, plants are largely missing.

comments.issue: The inclusion criteria and data-processing steps leading to the final dataset are hard to grasp.
comments.request: Rewrite the criteria clearly, possibly with a flow chart.
comments.quote: the inclusion criteria and data steps taken to get to the final analyzed data set are difficult to grasp

comments.issue: Order is not a meaningful independence control; species and phylogeny matter more.
comments.request: Include species/phylogeny as random effects and report the variance explained.
comments.quote: I am not convinced that order is that important to include or takes into account any kind of meaningful lack of independence to be controlled for

comments.issue: Evolution can act on variances without mean changes, which the mean-focused analysis misses.
comments.request: Quantify variance responses (Nakagawa et al. 2015) or discuss this point.
comments.quote: Selection and adaptive evolution also regularly work on the variances (e.g., stabilizing or disruptive selection) with no changes in means.

comments.issue: Common themes among studies that did document rapid evolution are not explored.
comments.request: Tally biologically meaningful common themes among the positive studies.
comments.quote: of those studies that do document rapid evolution are there any common themes to them, that are biologically meaningful

comments.issue: Line-level edits: L52 wording (studies examined vs documented) and remove the extra 'had' at L260.
comments.request: Apply these wording corrections.
comments.quote: Given the results presented here, it seems more accurate to say that studies examined for rapid evolution. Very few found it, so it is not documented.

comments.issue: The terms 'non-selective predation' (L65) and 'non-stressfull range' (L68) are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify these terms.
comments.quote: What is meant by “non-selective predation” if the focus here is on the effect of selection by predators.

comments.issue: Selection and adaptive evolution are treated as the same (L90, L124).
comments.request: Distinguish selection from adaptive evolutionary response.
comments.quote: selection and adaptive evolution are not the same. Selection can readily occur, but there may simply be no adaptive evolution.

comments.issue: The cited studies at L98-99 did explicitly examine the strength and direction of selection.
comments.request: Correct the characterization of these studies.
comments.quote: Those studies explicitly looked at the strength and direction.

comments.issue: Evolutionary limits may be practically finite but should not be treated as nonexistent.
comments.quote: Maybe practically finite, but there is a limit somewhere!

comments.issue: Screening on titles only may have missed studies.
comments.request: Explain why only titles were screened.
comments.quote: Why the title only? Could studies not have been missed otherwise?

comments.issue: Reported generations are not necessarily generations of selection, and whether selection was constant is unknown.
comments.request: Clarify generation counting and selection regime.
comments.quote: This is merely the number of generations, not generations of selection. Was the same selection pressure always imposed each generation.

comments.issue: The 'rapid' framing is unnecessary because evolution is inherently generation-by-generation.
comments.request: Consider dropping the 'rapid' framing.
comments.quote: I think the work stands on its own merit and need not tie itself to “rapid” or not.

comments.issue: Shared measurements and control groups within studies create non-independence not handled by the current model structure.
comments.request: Adopt hierarchical multilevel models (Nakagawa et al. 2017) to use more data and obtain I².
comments.quote: I believe the kind of hierarchical models the latter paper details can also be useful to deal with the removal of various elements of each study noted in the inclusion criteria

comments.issue: Investigating magnitude may require absolute values as the response.
comments.request: Consider using absolute values to assess magnitude.
comments.quote: Would investigating magnitude not require using absolute values as your response?

comments.issue: The planned post-hoc comparisons are not stated.
comments.request: State where the post-hoc comparisons are defined.
comments.quote: Where are these planned post-hoc comparisons stated? Is this in reference to Table 1?

comments.issue: Generation is not included in all models.
comments.request: Include generation in all models.
comments.quote: Why not include generation in all models?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether a numerical meta-regression of evolution on temperature differences was used.
comments.request: Clarify the meta-regression specification.
comments.quote: Was a meta-regression model then used, with your explanatory factor being numerical. The fixed effect would then be a slope of evolution regressed on temperature differences?

comments.issue: Weighting by sample size assumes equal outcome variances and ignores sampling-error methods.
comments.request: Consider imputing sampling errors and using standard meta-analysis methods.
comments.quote: weighting by the sample size as a control for sampling error would seem to assume then that the variances in outcomes is the same among all studies. Is that reasonable?

comments.issue: Population-level replication non-independence in effect size estimation is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how population-level non-independence was handled.
comments.quote: It’s unclear how the lack of independence of the population level replication is dealt with here in estimating the effect size.

comments.issue: Genomic resources are not necessarily a mechanistic understanding.
comments.request: Soften the mechanistic claim for genomic resources.
comments.quote: It’s not clear to me that genomic resources necessarily provide a ‘mechanistic’ understanding.

comments.issue: How 'most relevant' and a 'reasonable' scenario were decided is unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify these selection criteria.
comments.quote: How is ‘most relevant’ decided, what is a “reasonable’ scenario?

comments.issue: Selecting on directional/linear evolution biases results when traits fluctuate across generations.
comments.request: Account for non-linear trait dynamics.
comments.quote: Does doing so, though, not assume that any evolution is perfectly directional and linear?

comments.issue: Generation times were assigned arbitrarily, and the justification is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the assignment or remove these data points.
comments.quote: Why is this arbitrary assignment done. What is the justification?

comments.issue: Different forms of warming (constant change vs heat wave) may impose different selection.
comments.request: Categorize warming forms and test whether more can be learned.
comments.quote: These difference in the way “warming” occurred might be relevant. A constant temperature change vs a rapid heat wave might impose different selection pressure.

comments.issue: The discussion could invoke limited heritability and selection-genetic variance covariance (Wood & Brodie 2016).
comments.request: Consider this explanation for the weak responses.
comments.quote: The largest constraint may be that while warming, predation, and competition, all impose strong s, the response may be so limited because of h2.

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic about the surprising results; asks about non-parallel replicates, predation-competition covariation and broader implications.

comments.issue: Weak overall results may arise from non-parallel responses across replicate populations.
comments.request: Explore and address replication non-parallelism.
comments.quote: to what extent are the weak results observed within your focal studies due to non-parallel responses observed across replicate populations?

comments.issue: Predation often covaries with competition, so predation effects may be mediated by increased competition.
comments.request: Consider this alternative mechanism in the interpretation.
comments.quote: differences in predation will (often?) covary with competition (declines in predation may lead to increased competition)

comments.issue: The broader meaning for detecting evolution in nature and eco-evolutionary interactions is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the broader implications of the results.
comments.quote: what does this mean for the likelihood of detecting evolution in nature and the potential for ongoing interactions between ecological and evolutionary forces?

comments.issue: No comparison of themes between studies with and without significant responses.
comments.request: Compare insights from significant vs. non-significant studies.
comments.quote: are there any new insights or themes that emerged for studies that detected significant responses vs. those that did not?

title: Rapid evolution of life‐history traits in response to warming, predation and competition: A meta‐analysis

study.system: producer communities in complex food webs; simulation experiment

editor_summary: Model outcomes may be guaranteed by model structure; need much more model detail and clearly stated hypotheses; multitrophic results weak with large error bars; resubmission possible.

reviews.assessment: Positive about the contribution and communication, but doubts whether complementarity's importance is guaranteed by the model and wants animal community representation clarified.
strengths: good communication of a complex modelling framework
nice contribution filling an important gap in the BEF literature

comments.issue: Complementarity beating selection seems guaranteed by the model because monoculture productivity is identical for all species.
comments.request: Reconsider the identical monoculture productivity assumption and its consequences.
comments.quote: you argue in several places that complementarity is more important than selection, but it seems that your model was structured to guarantee that.

comments.issue: The representation of animal communities, including higher trophic levels, is not described in the methods.
comments.request: Describe the animal community model, including functional responses and prey selection.
comments.quote: It is confined almost entirely to L158-9, there is nothing about functional responses, prey size selection, generalism vs. specialism, etc.

comments.issue: The design description at L162 should state the full factorial crossing of animal and plant richness and RUD.
comments.request: Clarify the full factorial design at L162.
comments.quote: L162, full factorial with all levels of animal and plant richness, and RUD.

comments.issue: Point 2 at L186-7 is unclear; why only two resources are used is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the choice of two resources.
comments.quote: L186-7, point 2 is unclear. Why are there only 2 resources?

comments.issue: Line-level corrections: richness of one rather than zero at L226; Figure 3 rather than 4 at L232.
comments.quote: L226, richness of one, not zero. L232, fig. 3, not 4.

comments.issue: It is unclear what happens with more than two limiting resources; plants could access up to 16 compartments.
comments.request: Clarify resource access with more than two limiting resources.
comments.quote: Supplement 1, L32-34, what happens with >2 limiting resources? Plants could access up to 16 compartments, no?

comments.issue: Referring to plants as 'resources' is confusing given the resource compartments.
comments.request: Avoid calling plants resources.
comments.quote: Supp. 1, L66, it is confusing to refer to the plants as “resources” since you also talk about the resource compartments.

comments.issue: Gamma is not explained.
comments.request: Define gamma.
comments.quote: L68, what is gamma?

comments.issue: Consumer interference is oddly specific and lacks a mechanistic basis.
comments.request: Justify the consumer interference term.
comments.quote: what does consumer interference represent? It seems somewhat oddly specific to have in the model without reference to any mechanism.

reviews.assessment: Supportive and sees the study as suitable, but asks for clearer novelty, hypotheses, mechanism discussion and parameter documentation.
strengths: model follows up-to-date and well-accepted principles
results interesting and contribute to understanding BEF

comments.issue: Novelty relative to prior work (Loreau, Thebault, Brose) is unclear, and 'selection' is underdeveloped.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution and define selection in this context.
comments.quote: the way in which the present study captures something really novel is somewhat unclear, i.e. what is currently known and what precisely aims the present study to contribute

comments.issue: The paper lacks hypotheses, and the many results are hard to follow.
comments.request: Formulate a priori predictions that the modelling can test.
comments.quote: For this reason I miss hypotheses. To me it seems possible to formulate a priori predictions, based on known mechanisms and principles.

comments.issue: How herbivory affects plant growth and nutrient uptake, and how it interferes with apparent competition, is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss these mechanisms and their possible effects on the results.
comments.quote: I miss the way in which predation (herbivory) may affect the prey (plants) and hence nutrient uptake by the plants.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the key outcome parameter Y is uptake at equilibrium.
comments.request: Clarify Y and add a table of all model parameters with definitions and units.
comments.quote: for getting a clear understanding of the equations of the modeling I recommend to include a table with all model parameters along with their definition, dimension/units and value-intervals

reviews.assessment: Mixed feelings: the topic is a priority, but many results may be guaranteed by model design and trophic effects are overemphasized.
strengths: integrates horizontal and vertical diversity with resource use complementarity
priority topic of integrating trophic interactions into BEF

comments.issue: Model outcomes may be direct consequences of initial conditions, e.g. monoculture performance declines with RUG by assumption.
comments.request: Show the model can produce non-obvious outcomes or acknowledge the limitation.
comments.quote: My main concern is about the ability of the model to generate outcomes that are not obvious consequences of the initial conditions.

comments.issue: Trophic interaction effects are overemphasized given very large error bars and the overwhelming RUG effect.
comments.request: Acknowledge the uncertainty in the trophic interaction results.
comments.quote: I believe the effects of trophic interactions are overemphasized given the degree of uncertainty in model output and this should be acknowledged

comments.issue: It is unclear which kind of communities the model intends to simulate, including 70 consumer species.
comments.request: Describe the simulated communities more clearly.
comments.quote: I would also appreciate a better description of which kind of communities the model intends to simulate. Trophic interactions that include 70 species of consumers deserve clarification.

comments.issue: Density-dependent processes and substitutive versus additive designs may confound diversity effects with RUG.
comments.request: Clarify density handling and the design in the main text.
comments.quote: it is important to clarify if intraspecific density-dependent processes (positive or negative) may have confounded the effects of species diversity on productivity

comments.issue: Model assumptions and limitations need clearer articulation and more conservative interpretation of outcomes.
comments.request: Articulate assumptions and limitations and temper the interpretation.
comments.quote: I believe the manuscript would benefit from clarification of the points above, with a better articulation of model assumptions and limitations and a more conservative interpretation of outcomes

comments.issue: The text is not simple enough to follow.
comments.request: Simplify the text.
comments.quote: Simplifying the text would contribute to improve the clarity of the manuscript.

title: The hidden role of multi‐trophic interactions in driving diversity–productivity relationships

study.system: microbes, phytoplankton, plants; 46 factorial biodiversity experiments

editor_summary: Editor finds the study important but considers the analytical and statistical concerns substantial, agrees driver differences are unclear, and asks for thorough reanalysis and rewrite.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and timely meta-analysis with sound methodology, though search-term choices, effect-size metric and heterogeneity need clarification.
strengths: methodology seems sound with publication-bias check

comments.issue: Search terms vary inconsistently across the four environmental-change searches.
comments.request: Explain the inconsistent search-term choices.
comments.quote: I was surprised by the inconsistencies of search terms between types of environmental changes

comments.issue: Using log response ratio per diversity level may inflate sample sizes; variance handling is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the effect-size metric and clarify variance calculation.
comments.quote: I am wondering if there is a risk of over-inflating the sample sizes, particularly because studies use many biodiversity levels to derive curves

comments.issue: Heterogeneity of effect sizes across studies is not quantified or discussed.
comments.request: Report Cochran's Q and I2 for heterogeneity.
comments.quote: The manuscript lacks a discussion of the heterogeneity of effect sizes between studies

comments.issue: Complementarity and temporal conclusions rely on only 12 and 5 studies and a biased selection effect.
comments.request: Soften the claims based on these small subsets.
comments.quote: I would be careful with this as the complementarity effects rely on only 12 studies and the temporal effects only on 5 studies

comments.issue: Abstract lacks a summary of deltaNBE by manipulation type and taxonomic group.
comments.request: Add this summary to the abstract.
comments.quote: I would also give a summary on the main results on deltaNBE as a function of type of manipulation and taxonomical group

comments.issue: Introduction should note that local effects of global change on biodiversity can be positive or negative.
comments.request: Add this nuance with references.
comments.quote: Note that at the local scale, effect of global environmental changes on biodiversity may range from negative to positive

comments.issue: Selection effects may weaken over time via evolutionary rescue, opposite to the paper's expectation.
comments.request: Consider this alternative temporal dynamic.
comments.quote: Intuitively I would have thought that evolutionary effects and selection effects would have the opposite effect

comments.issue: Introduction should state taxonomic coverage per driver and study numbers.
comments.request: Add this information with numbers of studies.
comments.quote: I think it is useful to state in the introduction that only warming could be assessed on several taxonomic groups, and that drought, nutrient addition and CO2 enrichment were only assessed on terrestrial plants

comments.issue: Non-independence from multiple effect sizes per study needs a robustness check.
comments.request: Check results accounting for non-independence.
comments.quote: It could be good to check that these results are maintained when taking into account this source of non-independence

comments.issue: Standardisation of environmental manipulation level is only explained in Fig S2.
comments.request: Explain the standardisation in the main text.
comments.quote: How did you standardise the level of environmental manipulation across different treatments to fit it in the model? It is explained in Fig. S2, but might be useful in the main text as well

comments.issue: It is unclear whether SE and CE were calculated only for biomass.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of SE/CE calculations.
comments.quote: Clarify that SE and CE are calculated only for biomass if this is the case?

comments.issue: Appendix S3 and Table S2 should mark the 12 CE/SE studies and link data points to references.
comments.request: Annotate the tables accordingly.
comments.quote: maybe highlight or mark the 12 studies for which SE and CE were extracted?

comments.issue: Number of exclusions and whether whole studies were excluded is unclear.
comments.request: Report exclusion numbers.
comments.quote: This led to how many exclusions? Did some studies end up completely excluded, or only some CE and SE within studies?

comments.issue: Why slopes are used only for stress effects and not main effects is unclear.
comments.request: Test main effects with slopes too.
comments.quote: Why only using slopes to test for stress effects? Would it be possible to use them as well to test for the main effects and check for the consistency of results?

comments.issue: Whether models were weighted by inverse variance is unclear.
comments.request: Confirm the weighting.
comments.quote: I assume that the models were weighted by the inverse of the variance and not the variance?

comments.issue: Stress models omit random effects and interactions that would show whether stress effects are general.
comments.request: Add random effects and interactions to the stress models.
comments.quote: Why not add the type of environmental manipulation, taxonomic group and ecosystem function as random effects in the models for the effect of environmental stress, as in the main model of line 326?

comments.issue: Results start without a summary of study types and design characteristics.
comments.request: Add a brief summary of study types.
comments.quote: It would be useful to have a rapid summary of the type of studies (mesocosm, microcosm, average duration, range of species richness used in the study

comments.issue: General statement is too broad: many stability and biogeochemical NBEs are non-significant.
comments.request: Qualify the statement.
comments.quote: I feel that this sentence is a too broad statement. If I look at stability for instance, the NBEs seem to be mainly non significant

comments.issue: Number of studies should accompany N values in the text.
comments.request: Add study counts in parentheses.
comments.quote: I would include the number of studies in addition to the N in the parentheses

comments.issue: Variation among studies is weak evidence that the same change is perceived differently; within-study variation would be better.
comments.request: Use within-study variation to support the claim.
comments.quote: I wonder if a large variation among studies is a proof that the same environmental variation could be perceived more or less stressful by different species. Variation within studies would maybe be a better proof

comments.issue: Sentence on L462 is oddly worded.
comments.request: Rephrase more simply.
comments.quote: The sentence is a bit odd, why not more simply: deltaNBE increased with increasing values of environmental stress?

comments.issue: Should clarify that most environmental changes did not alter NBE magnitude.
comments.request: Add this clarification.
comments.quote: It would be useful to clarify that most of the environmental changes did not change the magnitude of NBE, i.e. most of the data on plants

comments.issue: Figures 2-3 should add study counts and fix the 'confidence interval not confident' label.
comments.request: Add study numbers and correct the label.
comments.quote: It would be useful to add the number of studies in addition to N for each NBE in the figure. Also, confidence interval not confident

comments.issue: Figure 5 panels need study counts.
comments.request: Add N and study numbers to Figure 5.
comments.quote: Please add the number of studies in the panel a, and add the N and number of studies for panel b and c

comments.issue: Supplementary figures and tables lack N, study counts, level counts, and abbreviations are not spelled out.
comments.request: Add these details to all supplementary legends.
comments.quote: Please add the N and number of studies for each figure to the legend

reviews.assessment: Very thoughtful and comprehensive synthesis that will be an important contribution, with only minor clarifications requested.
strengths: evaluation of different taxa and multiple functions

comments.issue: Independent roles of environment and diversity, and possible environmental confounding, are not evaluated.
comments.request: Analyse direct environmental effects and their interactions with diversity.
comments.quote: The factorial manipulation of environment and diversity makes this is a unique opportunity to evaluate the independent roles of environment and species diversity, plus their interactions

comments.issue: Justification for the four specific environmental drivers is missing.
comments.request: Justify the driver selection and note omitted drivers.
comments.quote: These are all reasonable, but seem oddly specific. A short justification of the relevance of these changes specifically would be helpful

comments.issue: Microbial abundance and resistance to infection are questionable as ecosystem functions.
comments.request: Justify linking these responses to functions.
comments.quote: Some of these responses seem odd to call “ecosystem functions”. For example, microbial abundance; abundance alone isn’t a function

comments.issue: Range of richness manipulated and its influence on effect sizes are not reported.
comments.request: Report richness ranges and test their influence.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to know the range of richness manipulated in each study, and whether this has any influence on variation in effects across studies

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic and useful dataset, but nonlinearity, effect-size bias, autocorrelation and mixing of drivers and functions raise significant concerns.
strengths: results provide insights into climate-change effects

comments.issue: Nonlinear B-EF relationships may bias NBE estimates; deltaNBE versus duration should be analysed.
comments.request: Analyse how deltaNBE changes with experimental duration.
comments.quote: if the impact of biodiversity on function is nonlinear, the very general conclusion, as highlighted by the title, might be biased. As shown in Fig. 4, it seems the authors have ignored the nonlinearity issue

comments.issue: LnRR may be biased by ignoring sample sizes and SDs; homogeneity and SD handling are unclear.
comments.request: Test homogeneity (Q statistic) and describe SD use.
comments.quote: I have some concerns with using the LnRR in these meta-analyses as the authors only used mean values and did not consider potential bias linked to sample sizes and standard deviations

comments.issue: Nutrient addition mixes different nutrient types, whose equivalence is questionable.
comments.request: Define nutrient addition and justify mixing nutrient types.
comments.quote: The Definition of nutrient addition in this study is unclear. How did the authors consider the different types of nutrient, e.g., N, P, and K?

comments.issue: Whether in situ and greenhouse or culture-dish experiments are equivalent is not justified.
comments.request: Justify or test the equivalence of experimental settings.
comments.quote: The study did not mention whether data come from in situ manipulations or experiments from culture dish in the greenhouse. Is it reasonable to treat them as equivalent in the statistical analysis?

comments.issue: Multiple effect sizes per study create autocorrelation, but it is not addressed.
comments.request: Explain how non-independence was handled.
comments.quote: Considering the statistical assumption of independence among observations, how the authors dealt with the autocorrelation issue in their analyses?

comments.issue: Mixing biomass, biogeochemical and stability functions may be inappropriate.
comments.request: Justify or separate the function categories.
comments.quote: They may have different response patterns with species richness. Does this mix of their response appropriate

comments.issue: Separate analyses for C3/C4 or annual/perennial plants are suggested.
comments.request: Test consistency across plant functional groups.
comments.quote: The plants probably include C3 and C4 species, which may differ in how they conduct photosynthesis and use nutrients. I think authors should conduct separate analyses

comments.issue: Title overstates taxonomic coverage; only warming experiments span taxonomic groups.
comments.request: Adjust the title claim.
comments.quote: However, only the warming experiments involve ecosystem functioning from different taxonomic groups (namely microbes, phytoplankton, and plants)

comments.issue: Whether conclusions are limited to specific experimental or vegetation types is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of inference.
comments.quote: other vegetation types, such as forest, are not included in this study. Whether the conclusion of this study is limited to a specific experimental type or vegetation type?

comments.issue: Statistical information for general results in Figures 2 and 3 is missing.
comments.request: Provide the statistics.
comments.quote: Provide the statistical information for some general results in Figure 2 and Figure 3

comments.issue: Sample sizes in figures and results should equal manipulated-environment numbers.
comments.request: Correct the sample sizes.
comments.quote: Please correct the sample sizes of △NBE, △CE, and △SE in figures and results, which should equal the numbers under manipulated environments

comments.issue: How the Lines 418-429 conclusion follows from the results is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the reasoning.
comments.quote: How to make this conclusion “In plant communities, the responses of biodiversity effects to environmental manipulations varied strongly among studies, resulting in non-significant overall effects

comments.issue: Figure 2-3 labels contradict the method descriptions (NBEM/NBEA versus CEM/SEM).
comments.request: Check whether the error is in the description or the data.
comments.quote: It contradicts the descriptions in the Method (line 230-231). It is necessary to check whether the errors exist in the description or the data

title: Biodiversity promotes ecosystem functioning despite environmental change

study.system: European mountain, forest and grassland plant resurveys; range sizes from GBIF

editor_summary: Reviewers split: reservations about novelty, methods and data; even positive reviewers want more development; recommends standard Introduction-Methods-Results-Discussion format.

reviews.assessment: Positive about the topic and analyses, but wants more developed introduction, results and discussion and clearer methods.
strengths: topic of wide interest to ecologists
nice exploration of many drivers and outcomes
writing style clear and easy to follow

comments.issue: Details of supplementary results should be presented and interpreted in the main text.
comments.request: Move more result details and interpretation into the main text.
comments.quote: I think it would be nice to read more details about these results (supplementary) in the main text along with some interpretation.

comments.issue: Introduction, results and discussion need more development.
comments.request: Develop the introduction, results and discussion further.
comments.quote: The manuscript would be improved with a more developed introduction, results (with effect sizes reported in text), and discussion.

comments.issue: Effect sizes are not reported in the text.
comments.request: Include effect sizes in the text.
comments.quote: It would help the reader to include effect sizes in the text

comments.issue: Language such as 'tend to' makes it unclear when results are conclusive.
comments.request: Make clear when results are conclusive.
comments.quote: to make it clear when results are conclusive (language like ‘tend to’ was a bit confusing for me)

comments.issue: Figure 1 colors are hard to see and the figure is not needed in the main text.
comments.request: Improve the colors and replace Figure 1 with the richness figure.
comments.quote: I understand that the colors are matching the habitat colors on the map, but they are a hard to see. Also, I do not think this figure is needed in the main text.

comments.issue: In Figure 2a the stacked bars and missing persistent species are not understandable; gains and losses should be separated.
comments.request: Show losses as negative and gains as positive bars.
comments.quote: Are the stacked bars representing the total number of species (richness, n) found at a site? If so, where are the persistent species?

comments.issue: Figure S1 caption may need to say credible interval.
comments.request: Check whether the caption should say credible interval.
comments.quote: Fig S1. Should the caption say “credible interval”?

comments.issue: Discussion does not develop the ideas in the context of the literature, e.g. nutrient deposition change.
comments.request: Add discussion and literature context, including nutrient deposition.
comments.quote: I would be interested and excited to see the ideas presented here further developed and in context with the literature.

comments.issue: Range sizes estimated from all years may be circular: gained species are inevitably also expanding their range.
comments.request: Explain how this circularity is accounted for.
comments.quote: If all data for all years are used, I would expect that species that are spreading into new habitats (i.e. those that are gained) are inevitably also growing in range size. Thus, it’s a bit circular

comments.issue: The 66% and 95% credible intervals are not justified and conclusions rest mainly on the 66% interval.
comments.request: Justify the choice of credible intervals in the methods.
comments.quote: Why were the 66% and 95% credible interval chosen? Please justify these choices in the methods as it seems like the results/conclusions are largely based on the 66% rather than the 95% credible interval.

comments.issue: Whether areas kept the same size and land use between surveys, and whether sites were dropped, is unclear.
comments.request: Report how habitat or land-use change and site criteria were handled.
comments.quote: Did all areas studied remain the same size with the same land use between the initial survey and the resurvey?

comments.issue: Range sizes from GBIF are likely underestimated because occurrences are incompletely recorded.
comments.request: Explain how incomplete spatial data were handled and their effect.
comments.quote: I would think that range sizes are largely underestimated from GBIF/biodiversity databases, as it’s likely that not every species occurrence has been recorded. How were incomplete spatial data handled?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 'vegetation' at line 135 means composition or vegetation characteristics.
comments.request: Clarify what 'vegetation' refers to.
comments.quote: is “vegetation” in this sentence referring to composition (Figure S6) or more generally to a shift in vegetation characteristics that reflect a larger range size?

comments.issue: The term 'statistically clear' is unfamiliar and undefined.
comments.request: Clarify whether it means significant.
comments.quote: I’m not familiar with the term “statistically clear”. Is that the same as significant?

comments.issue: 'Traditional land use' at line 246 is not defined.
comments.request: Define traditional land use.
comments.quote: Line 246 – what is ‘traditional land use’?

comments.issue: 'Semi-natural vegetation' at line 280 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain what semi-natural vegetation is.
comments.quote: Line 280 – please explain what ‘semi-natural vegetation’ is

reviews.assessment: Trusts the analyses but finds the framework underdeveloped and the results insufficiently novel for Ecology Letters.
strengths: materials and methods very well written

comments.issue: Results are not novel: larger-ranged species replacing smaller-ranged species is expected, and the 1999 TREE paper already covers it.
comments.request: Develop the framework and demonstrate the novel contribution.
comments.quote: My primary concern with this paper is in its framework and the lack of novelty in the results. I can’t think of any reason why a spp. with a bigger range wouldn’t replace a spp. with a smaller range.

comments.issue: Three-paragraph introduction is too short and lacks theoretical development justifying the study.
comments.request: Connect the study to theory on range limits, source-sink dynamics and dispersal.
comments.quote: The three paragraph intro is far too short and lacks the theoretical development to provide justification for the study at hand.

comments.issue: No competing hypotheses are laid out; the alternative to large-ranged species displacing small-ranged ones is unclear.
comments.request: Present multiple competing hypotheses, possibly in a conceptual figure.
comments.quote: The authors would also benefit from laying out the groundwork for multiple competing hypotheses in the introduction. The authors hypothesize that large-ranged spp. will displace small-ranged spp – and then that is what they find. What is the alternative here?
