comments.issue: Habitat differences in propagule pressure, dispersal and anthropogenic drivers are not integrated into background and hypotheses.
comments.request: Incorporate habitat-specific nuance into the background and hypotheses.
comments.quote: I think it would strengthen the paper to incorporate some of this nuance into the background and hypotheses.

comments.issue: The introduction gives no justification for discussing nutrient demands; a generalist-specialist framing might unite both.
comments.request: Consider reframing around generalist versus specialist species.
comments.quote: Have the authors considered shifting the framing of this manuscript to be more about generalist vs. specialist species rather than small vs. large geographic range?

comments.issue: The word 'systematic' is an odd word choice throughout the manuscript.
comments.request: Replace 'systematic' with 'consistent'.
comments.quote: I find the use of the word “systematic” here (and other places in the manuscript) a bit of an odd word choice. Do you mean, consistent?

comments.issue: The shift at line 153 to geographic range is abrupt and underdeveloped.
comments.request: Develop the transition to geographic range.
comments.quote: Abrupt shift here to discussion of geographic range. This needs better development.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the claim that larger-ranged species gained ground is supported by the data.
comments.request: Point to the figure or table supporting this statement.
comments.quote: “plant species with larger ranges gained ground” – is this statement supported by the data? If so, in which Fig / table?

comments.issue: Material at lines 202-208 belongs in the introduction.
comments.request: Move this material into the introduction.
comments.quote: This is the type of material I’d like to see in the introduction.

comments.issue: Ending with a broad claim about informing conservation efforts is weak without specific recommendations.
comments.request: Provide concrete conservation recommendations or soften the statement.
comments.quote: I find it to be a bit weak when papers end with a broad statement about “informing conservation efforts”. If this paper does in fact inform conservation efforts, what are the recommendations?

comments.issue: Whether plot size was accounted for is unclear.
comments.request: State whether plot size was taken into account.
comments.quote: Line 319: Also taking into account the size of the plot?

comments.issue: How varying time between baseline and resurvey was accounted for is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the varying time intervals were handled.
comments.quote: I’d like to know more about how the authors took into account that the time between the baseline and resurvey varied between studies in their assessment of temporal change.

comments.issue: Figure 3 x-axis uses scientific notation and panel d units are missing.
comments.request: Write out x-axis numbers and add units to panel d.
comments.quote: I’d like to see the numbers of the x-axis written out, instead of in scientific notation. Panel d: units?

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the clear synthesis but finds the GBIF range data inadequately validated and the competitive displacement claim unproven.

comments.issue: No attempt is made to show that patchy GBIF data are adequate for estimating range sizes.
comments.request: Assess GBIF data adequacy and test robustness of the results.
comments.quote: My main concern is that no attempt was made to convince readers of the adequateness of GBIF data for estimating range sizes.

comments.issue: Limitations of GBIF data and a justification for using them in this way are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations and justify the use of GBIF data.
comments.quote: At the very least, I would expect more discussion of the limitations, and a statement supporting the use of GBIF data in this way.

comments.issue: The influence of the grain size used to estimate range size is not tested.
comments.request: Analyse how grain size affects the results.
comments.quote: I would also like to have seen some analysis of the influence on the results of the grain size used to estimate range size.

comments.issue: Competitive displacement of small-ranged by large-ranged species is suggested but not conclusively demonstrated.
comments.request: Temper the competition claim or provide direct evidence.
comments.quote: the authors appear to suggest that the observed patterns are the result of competitive displacement of small-ranged by large-ranged species. This may well be the case, but is not conclusively demonstrated in this study.

comments.issue: Abstract mixes tested results with suppositions such as reduced beta diversity and increased competition.
comments.request: Distinguish tested results from speculation in the abstract.
comments.quote: in general it is unclear which of the statements made in the abstract relate to results in this study, and which are just suppositions based on the results.

comments.issue: Absolute change in richness d is likely influenced by sampling effort; percentage change may be preferable.
comments.request: Address the sampling-effort dependence, possibly using percentage change.
comments.quote: Surely the absolute value of change in species richness will be affected by sampling effort, because sites with higher sampling effort will have higher absolute measures of species richness

comments.issue: The precise use of 'occupancy' is defined only in the methods, after the results.
comments.request: Define occupancy before the results are presented.
comments.quote: the precise use of “occupancy” needs to be defined before the results are presented (currently, this is only made clear in the methods section, which is at the end of the manuscript)

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits (grammar at line 174; 'back-transformation' at line 402).
comments.quote: I think “having higher dispersal ability” would be better grammatically than “better dispersed”.

comments.issue: The first sentence of the line 201 paragraph redundantly repeats earlier text.
comments.request: Remove the redundant sentence.
comments.quote: The first sentence of this paragraph only repeats what has been said previous, and so is redundant, I think.

comments.issue: Calling disproportionate vulnerability of small-ranged species a confounding effect misuses the term.
comments.request: Reconsider describing it as a confounding effect.
comments.quote: Would a disproportionate vulnerability of small-ranged species at low abundance really be a “confounding effect”? This seems to me consistent with the hypotheses of the study.

comments.issue: The logic at lines 357-358 about stochasticity and plot number is hard to follow.
comments.request: Clarify the reasoning about stochastic changes and plot numbers.
comments.quote: I am not sure I follow the logic here. Is it just that inferred changes will be more stochastic with a smaller number of plots, so that both probability of loss and of gain would be more likely with a smaller number of plots?

comments.issue: It is not stated that the quantities at line 417 are sums across species.
comments.request: Specify that these were sums across species.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to specify explicitly that these were sums across species.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 425-428 belongs in the results, not the methods.
comments.request: Move the sentence to the results.
comments.quote: This sentence should be in the results, not the methods.

comments.issue: Calculation of overall similarity between species pools in different habitats lacks detail.
comments.request: Describe the similarity calculation in more detail.
comments.quote: I think there needs to be more detail on the calculation of overall similarity between species pools in the different habitats.

reviews.assessment: Finds the macroecological approach appealing and the main claim probably true, but raises effect-size, circularity and succession concerns.
strengths: topic of interest to Ecology Letters readers

comments.issue: Bayesian results may not be interpretable to readers more comfortable with frequentist statistics.
comments.request: Present results so non-Bayesian readers can follow them.
comments.quote: But if the results are not obvious to readers who are more comfortable with frequentist stats, then a significant part of the readership is lost.

comments.issue: Shape of the Y=f(X) relationship, r-squared and partial r-squared are not reported, and no graph of Y=f(X) is shown.
comments.request: Report variance explained and show a graph of Y=f(X).
comments.quote: Ideally, I would like to see a graph of Y=f(X). I didn’t see that in the present study (cf. Fig. 3).

comments.issue: With very large n, significant relationships may explain under 0.5% of variance; effect strength is unclear.
comments.request: Quantify how much variance range size explains.
comments.quote: With this sample size, a relationship Y=f(X) may be statistically significant, but account for <0.5% of the variance in Y.

comments.issue: Occupancy in quadrats is used as a surrogate for abundance, conflating two related but distinct measures.
comments.request: Justify or revise using occupancy as an abundance surrogate.
comments.quote: Since the dependent variable in this study is presence/absence in a quadrat, using presence/absence in multiple quadrats as a surrogate for abundance seems likely to introduce an unknown degree of circularity in the analyses.

comments.issue: The analysis flips the mechanistic logic from persistence=f(range size) to range size=g(persistence) without flipping the hypothesis.
comments.request: Align the causal direction of the analysis with the hypothesis.
comments.quote: You cannot flip the causation statistically unless you also flip the causation of your hypothesis.

comments.issue: Succession and self-thinning could produce the patterns without invoking climate change or eutrophication.
comments.request: Consider succession as an explanation and test disturbance history and successional status.
comments.quote: So, the patterns observed in this study are expected from natural ecological processes; there is no obvious need to invoke climate change, eutrophication, Anthropocene, etc.

comments.issue: The statement about nutrient demands and range sizes is not accurate; Figure 4a relationships are heteroscedastic.
comments.request: Reword to say low-nutrient-demand species may have any range size.
comments.quote: This is not exactly true. The relationships in Fig. 4a are clearly heteroscedastic.

comments.issue: The phrase 'tend to be adapted to' infers causation from correlation.
comments.request: Avoid causal language for this correlational result.
comments.quote: this is an inference of causation from a correlation

comments.issue: Speculation about biological mechanisms is unnecessary when random demographic fluctuations predict the same outcome.
comments.request: Acknowledge random demographic fluctuations as an explanation.
comments.quote: Is it necessary to speculate about biological mechanisms when random fluctuations predict the same outcome?

comments.issue: Under random demographic fluctuations, expanding populations would also be larger, matching the observed pattern.
comments.request: Reconsider whether the observed pattern supports the stated mechanism.
comments.quote: If demographic fluctuations are random, wouldn’t populations that are expanding tend to be a larger than populations that are contracting? That is exactly what you see.

comments.issue: The claim of higher vulnerability of small-ranged species is not evident.
comments.request: Support or remove the higher-vulnerability claim.
comments.quote: I don’t see it.

comments.issue: Whether 'abundance' here means the proportion of occupied plots is unclear.
comments.request: Confirm the definition of abundance used.
comments.quote: “Abundance” in this study means the proportion of occupied plots in the survey. Is that correct?

comments.issue: Whether 'occupancy' equals AOO, the total number of occupied plots, is unclear.
comments.request: Confirm the definition of occupancy used.
comments.quote: “Occupancy” = AOO = the total number of occupied plots. Is that correct?

comments.issue: Correlating occupancy proportion O/T with O may be circular.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between O/T and O in the correlation.
comments.quote: In this case, does that amount to relating O/T (number of occupied plots divided by the total number of plots) to O?

comments.issue: Because richness is a decelerating function of sampling effort, d should be a peaked function of effort, not unaffected by it.
comments.request: Reconsider the claim that d is unaffected by sampling effort.
comments.quote: R would be expected to be a decelerating, plateauing function of E. Therefore, d would be expected to be some peaked function of E.

comments.issue: Whether resurveys were designed to use the same sampling effort as the first survey is unclear.
comments.request: Confirm that sampling effort was matched between surveys.
comments.quote: Were the resurveys, in all cases, specifically designed to use the same sampling effort as in the first survey?

comments.issue: The model specification is unclear: site as random effect versus number of quadrats as fixed effect.
comments.request: Clarify the random and fixed effects in the model.
comments.quote: This sounds like you included site as a random effect in your model, as opposed to the number of quadrats as a fixed effect. Is that correct?

comments.issue: Whether a 'varying effect' means a random effect is unclear.
comments.request: Define 'varying effect' as used.
comments.quote: Is a “varying effect” the same as a random effect?

comments.issue: If species is a fixed effect and range size is a species characteristic, the range-size effect may not be identifiable.
comments.request: Explain how range-size effects are estimated with species in the model.
comments.quote: If this is the case, I don’t understand how there can be an effect of range size, since range size is a characteristic of each species.

comments.issue: Excluding small-ranged species ignores that random demographic fluctuations may drive their extinction.
comments.request: Explain the purpose of excluding small-ranged species.
comments.quote: Isn’t one possible that large-ranged species tend to replace small-ranged species because random demographic fluctuations are more likely to drive the latter to extinction?

comments.issue: Stacked bars in Figure 2 do not address a clear question; scatterplots of gained versus lost proportions may be better.
comments.request: Present gained and lost species as scatterplots.
comments.quote: I don’t understand why the data are presented in stacked bars. Does this presentation address a particular question or hypothesis?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Figure 3a shows the difference between prior and posterior distributions.
comments.request: Clarify what Figure 3a shows.
comments.quote: Do I understand correctly that this panel shows the difference between the prior and posterior distribution, the former having been set to zero?

comments.issue: Figure 3c shows a posterior distribution without explaining what is controlled for.
comments.request: Explain what is controlled for and how the posterior was derived.
comments.quote: Controlling for what? I don’t understand how this is a posterior distribution.

comments.issue: Figure 3d raises the same problem; the simple ratio of range sizes is not shown.
comments.request: Explain the posterior or show the simple range-size ratio.
comments.quote: Same problem. Why would one not show the simple ratio of range sizes?

title: Directional turnover towards larger‐ranged plants over time and across habitats

study.system: birds; comparative phylogenetic analysis of sex roles

editor_summary: Editor finds the negative review persuasive: unclear contribution, proxies cloud rather than clarify; requires consistent terminology, re-analysis beyond significance dredging, and a clear hypothesis framework.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and readable introduction, but the proxies, conceptual framework and statistical analyses raise major doubts about the advance.
strengths: mostly very well written, especially the introduction

comments.issue: Traits are used as synonyms for sex role components (SSD=competition, plumage=attraction, mating system=bonding).
comments.request: Name measured traits directly rather than their intended sex role components.
comments.quote: I find it confusing and misleading that the authors use sexual size dimorphism (SSD), plumage dimorphism and mating system as synonyms of competition for mates, mate attraction and pair bonding, respectively.

comments.issue: SSD can arise from natural selection, so its validity as a proxy for mate competition needs stronger justification.
comments.request: Provide a detailed critical justification that SSD reflects mate competition across birds.
comments.quote: I would expect a more detailed and critical justification of why the authors believe that SSD still provides a meaningful proxy for mate competition across all bird taxa

comments.issue: Plumage dimorphism captures mate attraction only partially; courtship and song are ignored.
comments.request: Incorporate courtship behaviour such as song into the mate attraction score.
comments.quote: One of the most conspicuous and especially elaborated behavioural trait that is possibly as important in mate attraction as plumage ornamentation is bird song.

comments.issue: Mating system is treated as a sex role component although it is a correlate or driver of sex roles.
comments.request: Justify mating system as a component coherent with previous work.
comments.quote: To me sex roles constitute traits that are sexually dimorphic such as competition, attraction and parental care (as mentioned by the authors) but mating system represents a correlative of sex roles

comments.issue: The theoretical basis for the extensive list of predictors is not developed.
comments.request: Give theoretical background and predictions for each predictor trait.
comments.quote: I missed a more detailed description of the underlying theory that motivated the authors to test the quite extensive list of predictor variables.

comments.issue: Maternal investment predictor may autocorrelate with the parental care response, creating the positive correlation.
comments.request: Test and account for autocorrelation between predictor and response.
comments.quote: there is still scope for an autocorrelation between predictor and response variable, which might be the reason for the detected positive correlation.

comments.issue: The study uses ASR although theory centres on OSR; the two are often not equivalent.
comments.request: Justify the choice of ASR versus OSR and clarify the proxy relationship.
comments.quote: the vast majority of theoretical work on sex roles and sex ratios is about the operational sex ratio (OSR)

comments.issue: Novel aspects of the study are impossible to identify relative to previous comparative work.
comments.request: Clarify how this study advances the field beyond comprehensiveness.
comments.quote: based on the information provided in the manuscript it is almost impossible to identify the novel aspects of the presented study apart from the fact that this one seems to be the most comprehensive one

comments.issue: Conclusion of remarkable lability conflicts with phylogenetic signal lambda=0.73 (75% explained).
comments.request: Explain the contradiction or reformulate the lability conclusion.
comments.quote: I agree that this study illustrates a remarkable variation in sex roles across birds but phylogeny explains almost 75% suggesting to me that this trait is not labile at all.

comments.issue: 50 simultaneous tests give a 92% chance of a false positive; correction is mandatory.
comments.request: Apply false-discovery rate correction across the tests.
comments.quote: Thus the authors test 50 (!) hypotheses simultaneously, meaning that we have a 92% chance (1-(1-0.05)^50) of observing at least one significant result

comments.issue: The Euclidean-distance score conflates male and female bias and lacks a clear hypothesis.
comments.request: Explain the rationale and hypotheses for this fifth response variable.
comments.quote: species showing a strong male bias are attributed a similar value as species showing a strong female bias in whatever trait (PC axis)

comments.issue: PCs each explain about one fourth of variance, making the PC analysis redundant.
comments.request: Justify what the PC analysis adds beyond the correlation matrix.
comments.quote: it is surprising that the obtained PCs explain a very similar amount of variance, i.e. one fourth each. If correct, this outcome makes the use of principal components somewhat redundant.

comments.issue: Models with one response and many predictors are called multivariate, which is incorrect terminology.
comments.request: Rename them multiple regressions rather than multivariate models.
comments.quote: the presented "multivariate" models only include many predictors but only a single response variable, which might be called 'multiple' regressions rather than multivariate models

comments.issue: Table 2 is hard to interpret with a categorical predictor; t-tests are inadequate.
comments.request: Present an ANOVA F-test table with slope estimates instead.
comments.quote: I propose to present an ANOVA (F-test) table together with the slope estimates instead of the t-tests.

comments.issue: Consecutive line numbers and supplementary page numbers are missing.
comments.request: Add line numbers throughout and page numbers to the supplement.
comments.quote: Please add consecutive line numbers throughout the main text and the Supplementary Material and please add page numbers to the Supplementary Material.

comments.issue: Mean number and duration of pair bonds cannot differ between sexes; variance would be more informative.
comments.request: Clarify why means are used and consider variance instead.
comments.quote: Assuming a 50:50 sex ratio the mean number of mates and the mean duration of bonding must be equal among males and females. Hence, we might be more interested in the variance rather than the mean number of pair bonds.

comments.issue: Abstract reports 9994 species although no statistical test uses them, which is misleading.
comments.request: Report the sample size actually analysed in the abstract.
comments.quote: Given that no statistical test includes those 9994 species, I find it somewhat misleading to report this sample size in the abstract.

comments.issue: No page number is given for Darwin's 'fast males' term.
comments.request: Provide the source page for the term.
comments.quote: Could you please provide the page number where Darwin coined that term?

comments.issue: The prediction at P6 L12 lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Provide references backing this prediction.
comments.quote: P6, L12: Please provide references to back this prediction.

comments.issue: Study-design information essential for understanding is relegated to the supplement.
comments.request: Move essential design information into the main text.
comments.quote: I believe that a lot of information provided in the supplementary material is essential to understand the study design and should therefore should go to the main text.

comments.issue: Copy edits: "as mean" (P7 L34); Cornwallis et al. 2010 missing from the reference list.
comments.quote: Supplementary material: Cornwallis et al. 2010 is not listed in the references.

comments.issue: Unclear whether temperature variation or temperature range is meant.
comments.request: Specify which temperature measure is used.
comments.quote: P7, L36: Do you mean temperature variation or temperature range?

comments.issue: A linear relationship between mean precipitation and harshness may be inappropriate.
comments.request: Justify or model a non-linear precipitation optimum.
comments.quote: Did you expect a linear relationship between mean precipitation and harshness?

comments.issue: Unclear whether P9 L12-15 estimates are Euclidean distances and whether differences are significant.
comments.request: Specify and report standard errors or deviations for these estimates.
comments.quote: Are these estimates Euclidian distances? Please specify and provide standard errors/deviation to get an additional idea whether to postulated differences are statistically significant

comments.issue: Unclear whether SDs or explained variances of the four PCs are reported.
comments.request: State explicitly what these values represent.
comments.quote: Unclear. Do you report "standard deviations" or explained variances of the four PCs?

comments.issue: Multicollinearity in the multivariate models is not checked.
comments.request: Report multicollinearity checks for these models.
comments.quote: Did you check for multicollinearity in those so-called "multivariate" models?

comments.issue: The link from weak correlations to different fitness routes is not explained.
comments.request: Explain this reasoning in more detail.
comments.quote: Why do weak correlations among sex role components indicate different routes to gain fitness? Please explain in more detail.

comments.issue: The theory referred to at P15 L12 is not identified.
comments.request: Specify which theory is meant.
comments.quote: P15, L12: Which theory are you referring to here?

comments.issue: Unclear how many species Figure 1 includes.
comments.request: State whether all 9994 species or only the analysed subset are shown.
comments.quote: How many species are included in this graph? All 9994 or only those for which you had data for all four sex role components?

comments.issue: Figure 2 panels have two differently scaled axes without explanation.
comments.request: Explain the dual axes.
comments.quote: Figure 2: Why do all PCs have two differently scaled axes (upper and lower)?

comments.issue: Figure 3 colour coding is redundant with circle size; scatter plots would be clearer.
comments.request: Replace with scatter plots for each relationship.
comments.quote: I think the colour coding is a bit redundant given that the strength of the correlation is already indicated by the size of the circle and the actual value of the correlation coefficient.

comments.issue: Residual distributions, especially pair bonding, appear inconsistent with the claimed normality.
comments.request: Re-examine residual normality assumptions.
comments.quote: Seeing these distributions I am more than surprised that the residuals of the models did not deviate from normality especially for pair bonding.

comments.issue: Strongly male-biased ASR values may reflect confusion with OSR and need explanation.
comments.request: Comment on why ASR is male-biased and whether OSR confusion contributes.
comments.quote: Overall the graphs suggest that there is a strong male biased sex ratio in birds, which I would have expected for the OSR but not necessarily for ASR. Are there any ideas why the ASR is on average so male-biased?

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written study with novel insights; one serious statistical concern about body mass and missing data plus many minor points.

comments.issue: The mammal comparison at line 27 page 5 is off-topic and unnecessary.
comments.request: Delete this phrase.
comments.quote: I think you don't need this phrase, as it is off the topic and there is no need to discuss why this isn't a mammal paper

comments.issue: Taxonomic categories in the examples are unbalanced (flies, fish, amphibians versus shorebirds, passerines).
comments.request: Use consistent taxonomic units such as insects, amphibians and birds.
comments.quote: Balance in the taxonomic categories would be good here

comments.issue: The brief sentence on female mating systems is not connected to the aims.
comments.request: Add explanation relating female mating systems to the aims.
comments.quote: another sentence of explanation regarding female mating systems and how they are related to the aims would be helpful, this sentence is very brief

comments.issue: The point at line 12 page 6 lacks a reference and a clue about the hypothesis's origin.
comments.request: Add a reference and indicate where the hypothesis comes from.
comments.quote: needs a reference to this specific point, and ideally a clue to where this hypothesis comes from

comments.issue: "Latter scenario" at line 16 has an unclear antecedent.
comments.request: Clarify what "latter scenario" refers to.
comments.quote: It is unclear what part of the preceding sentence 'latter scenario' is refering to

comments.issue: The introduction does not say what systems the alternative hypotheses came from.
comments.request: State the taxa and type of evidence for these hypotheses.
comments.quote: you should mention what system these alternative hypotheses came from- what taxa (any birds?) and what sort of evidence.

comments.issue: "Virtual incomparable" is an uninformative description of the dataset.
comments.request: Rephrase this description.
comments.quote: rephrase 'virtual incomparable' as this is not a very informative description of the dataset.

comments.issue: The stated aim lacks evolutionary context and predictions about linkage.
comments.request: State the aim with theory-based expectations and trade-offs.
comments.quote: needs a stated aim with more evolutionary context than just because the components are unexplored- how might theory predict that they should be linked?

comments.issue: Breeding season is undefined and climate variables are restricted to it without justification.
comments.request: Define breeding season and justify this climate window.
comments.quote: How do you define breeding season? Is it mating, incubation, chick rearing, or fledging, or all? The supplementary methods does not explain this.

comments.issue: Temperature range may correlate with breeding period length, confounding the analyses.
comments.request: Check and account for this correlation in the models.
comments.quote: The measure temperature of the hottest minus coldest month during this restricted part of the year is likely to be correlated with the length of the breeding period. Is this taken into account in the statistical analyses?

comments.issue: Use of breeding-season climate only, instead of annual means and inter-year variation, is unjustified.
comments.request: Consider inter-year variation and annual means as alternatives.
comments.quote: It's not clear to me why not to use inter-year variation and annual means (as in Jetz & Rubenstein for example).

comments.issue: Body mass is residualized rather than interacted with other life-history traits, biasing inference.
comments.request: Allow body mass to interact with clutch mass and related traits.
comments.quote: Rather than putting a residual in the model, it would be better to allow body mass to also interact with clutch mass in the same model, and interpret the interaction

comments.issue: Missing-data handling is undocumented; casewise deletion can substantially bias multiple regressions.
comments.request: Describe and justify the missing-data treatment.
comments.quote: It seems that you have used a casewise deletion method, which can lead to substantial bias in multiple regressions

comments.issue: Copy edits: missing "and"/"in animals" (p5 L33); repeated phrase (P10 L15); "associated to" should be "associated with".
comments.quote: Page 10 L15 'even when controlling for female body mass' is repeated in this sentence.

comments.issue: Interpretive statements such as "should be taken with caution" belong in the discussion.
comments.request: Move this interpretation to the discussion.
comments.quote: Some interpretation in the results that should be in the discussion

comments.issue: The results read as a list of associations without linking them to the aims and hypotheses.
comments.request: State which hypotheses the associations support or not.
comments.quote: The results section needs to state what the associations mean in terms of addressing the aims as well (which hypotheses are being supported or not).

comments.issue: Allometric effects and the clutch size-egg mass trade-off are glossed over without prior literature context.
comments.request: Add context on previous conclusions and how this analysis advances them.
comments.quote: There needs to be more context of previous literature in the discussion explaining other authors' conclusions

title: Sex roles in birds: Phylogenetic analyses of the influence of climate, life histories and social environment

study.system: mutualistic interactions; synzoochory dataset of 647 plant species

editor_summary: Editor sees potential in the quantitative framework and unique dataset, but reviewers found the patterns unsurprising and the framework perhaps uninformative; readability and basic definitions and assumptions need drastic revision.

reviews.assessment: Admires the ambition and dataset but was not convinced the quantity component or landscape framework is informative, and found the manuscript long, dense and hard to follow.
strengths: ambitious attempt to apply an influential mutualism framework
remarkable dataset from over a thousand seed dispersal studies
builds on past work while being new and ambitious

comments.issue: The manuscript is very long and dense, making it harder to follow than necessary.
comments.request: Shorten and streamline the manuscript.
comments.quote: It is very long and dense, which made it harder to follow than it should have been.

comments.issue: Many terms are undefined, defined later, used before they become relevant, or defined incomprehensibly.
comments.request: Define terms at first use and make definitions understandable.
comments.quote: Many terms are undefined; some are defined later in the paper (e.g., isotropy-anisotropy, finally defined in the Discussion, which I still don’t understand), some are used before they become relevant

comments.issue: Using pollen grains landing on a stigma as the quantity component of pollination seems wrong; pollinator visits would make more sense.
comments.request: Reconsider the definition of the quantity component.
comments.quote: For example, I have a hard time seeing the number of pollen grains landing on a stigma as a measure of the “quantity” component of a pollination mutualism.

comments.issue: Context dependence of both components is not developed until the Discussion, where it markedly affects the empirical results.
comments.request: Develop the context dependence of quantity and quality earlier.
comments.quote: Both components, but especially the quantity component, should be highly dependent upon context, a point that isn’t really developed until the Discussion and then ends up having a marked effect on the empirical results.

comments.issue: The effectiveness landscape is extremely difficult to envision from the opening paragraphs.
comments.request: Introduce and walk through Figure 1 earlier.
comments.quote: the effective landscape set up in the first few paragraphs is extremely difficult for the reader to envision

comments.issue: The paper does not state the questions the effectiveness framework is meant to answer about biotic seed dispersal.
comments.request: Set up orienting questions and arguments for the framework.
comments.quote: The authors do not tell us what questions they are using the effectiveness framework to answer about biotic seed dispersal.

comments.issue: Results and conclusions are not framed as cautiously as the limitations of the proxy data require.
comments.request: Frame the results and conclusions with appropriate caution.
comments.quote: While these limitations were mentioned, however, the results and conclusions did not seem to be framed in an equally cautious manner.

comments.issue: The very long Discussion includes observations that do not emerge from this analysis.
comments.request: Cut discussion content not supported by the analysis.
comments.quote: The Discussion section, which is very long, includes many insightful observations about seed dispersal that don’t really emerge from this analysis

comments.issue: The key result suggests the quantity component carries minimal information, so Figure 2 bears little relation to the framework in Figure 1.
comments.request: Reconcile the results with the effectiveness landscape framework.
comments.quote: The key result from the authors’ analyses, as I read it, was that the quantity component of seed dispersal carried minimal information.

comments.issue: The authors never made a case that applying the effectiveness landscape is informative beyond quality or quantity alone.
comments.request: Make a stronger, shorter case for the informativeness of the framework.
comments.quote: I think the authors need to think over how they can make a better case that applying the effectiveness landscape to real systems is in fact deeply informative in a way that quality alone or quantity alone wouldn’t.

reviews.assessment: High opinion of this important and novel contribution, with just a few comments mainly about dense writing and some classification details.
strengths: important and novel contribution to synzoochory research
impressive dataset of 647 plant species and 24 animal families
quantitative framework assigns meaningful positions along well-defined axes

comments.issue: The writing is dense; the abstract and introduction are difficult to absorb because of specialized terms.
comments.request: Make the manuscript, especially the abstract and introduction, more accessible.
comments.quote: I do not find the Abstract particularly informative. For example, understanding what it means that “The synzoochory landscape was clumped, quality-driven anisotropic and exhibited positive component correlation” (page 2, lines 16-18) was possible only after reading the manuscript.

comments.issue: The phrase 'the effectiveness landscape is surely well amortized' is hard to understand.
comments.request: Rewrite the phrase more plainly.
comments.quote: “the effectiveness landscape is surely well amortized” – can this be written more plainly?

comments.issue: Isotropy-anisotropy is explained only much later and remains unclear.
comments.request: Explain isotropy-anisotropy at first use or without jargon.
comments.quote: Can you explain “isotropy-anisotropy” here? Or, even better, describe this property without jargon?

comments.issue: The distinction between incidental and accidental is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the difference between incidental and accidental.
comments.quote: I had to check the difference between “incidental” and “accidental” in a vocabulary, and I suppose that many other writers will have a similar issue.

comments.issue: The significance of the chosen traits for seed dispersal is not obvious.
comments.request: Justify the choice of traits.
comments.quote: Consider providing a brief justification for choosing these traits. Their significance for seed dispersal is not always immediately obvious.

comments.issue: Quadratic effects of seed and disperser mass were not checked.
comments.request: Check for quadratic effects of seed and disperser mass.
comments.quote: Have you considered checking for quadratic effects of the seed and disperser mass (e.g., Munoz and Bonal 2008)?

comments.issue: The disperser behaviour classification seems wrong for some species (Apodemus, Tamias striatus).
comments.request: Check the classification or provide more details on its rules.
comments.quote: Please check the classification or provide more details on its rules.

comments.issue: The 1192 entries are study x plant species combinations, not studies; there are only 361 unique studies.
comments.request: Report the number of unique studies and combinations correctly.
comments.quote: Strictly speaking, these are 1192 study x plant species combinations. The number of studies is much lower (R counted 361 unique entries in the “Source” column) because many studies investigated >1 plant species.

comments.issue: Appendix 1 was not included in the files sent for review.
comments.request: Ensure Appendix 1 is provided.
comments.quote: The files that I received for review did not contain Appendix 1.

comments.issue: Quality depends on the same extrinsic drivers, so it may not explain the greater spread of quantity values.
comments.request: Reconsider this explanation for the spread of quantity values.
comments.quote: The quality of seed dispersal (i.e., the decision to cache rather than immediately consume) depends on exactly the same (as well as other) extrinsic drivers

comments.issue: The belief that SDE is determined mainly by quality can be tested in a model controlling for seed size.
comments.request: Test whether the proportion of cached seeds is affected by dispersal mode controlling for seed size.
comments.quote: this belief can be tested in a model that controls for seed size

comments.issue: Pooling mast and non-mast years hides the masting route from low- to high-quality regions.
comments.request: Consider masting as an additional variable, now or in future work.
comments.quote: This shift is not evident in this manuscript because data from mast and non-mast years were pooled.

comments.issue: Table 2 shows a mismatch between the number of categories and the degrees of freedom.
comments.request: Correct the degrees of freedom in Table 2.
comments.quote: In Table 2, there seems to be a mismatch between the number of categories and the number of degrees of freedom (generally, df = # of categories -1).

title: The ecological and evolutionary significance of effectiveness landscapes in mutualistic interactions

study.system: blue carbon ecosystems; biotic interactions; literature review and meta-analysis

editor_summary: Both reviewers find the study novel and interesting but note shortcomings; address R1's concern about quantitative CO2 influx/efflux balance and the technical questions.

reviews.assessment: Important and novel review with a strong conceptual model and useful meta-analysis; only minor revisions suggested.
strengths: important contrast between mangrove and saltmarsh/seagrass

comments.issue: The manuscript is over-long and its discussion could be abbreviated.
comments.request: Abbreviate the discussion.
comments.quote: The manuscript is over-long, and the discussion within this section of the manuscript could be abbreviated.

comments.issue: It is not specified whether productivity and decomposition effects concern above- or below-ground carbon.
comments.request: Specify whether effects refer to above- or below-ground carbon.
comments.quote: Greater care could be given to specifying whether effects on productivity or decomposition are in relation to above-ground carbon or below-ground carbon.

comments.issue: How climate conditions were used in laboratory-based studies is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how source-region and laboratory conditions were handled.
comments.quote: It's not clear how climate conditions were used in the laboratory-based studies. You mention that the abiotic conditions of source regions were considered but what about the conditions in the laboratory?

comments.issue: The mangrove versus saltmarsh herbivory result is not positioned in the existing literature debate.
comments.request: Couch the mangrove result in the literature debate.
comments.quote: this could be couched in relation to an interesting debate on this issue in the literature (not wholly “unexpected” in this regard: line 562)

comments.issue: He et al. 2020 did not explore mangrove herbivory per se, so the citation is misleading.
comments.request: Soften or correct the characterization of He et al. 2020.
comments.quote: be careful in your citing He et al. 2020 that “herbivory effects on marsh and mangrove productivity have recently been revealed as being at least comparable in magnitude

comments.issue: The phrase 'in relation to' in sentence 558-559 misleadingly suggests a mangrove-saltmarsh interaction.
comments.request: Replace 'in relation to' with 'in comparison to'.
comments.quote: The sentence 558-559 is potentially confusing – the use of “in relation to” can give the impression that the plant-plant interaction is between mangrove and saltmarsh

comments.issue: Larval export, an important biological flux, is not mentioned.
comments.request: Add larval export with the Saintilan and Mazumder reference.
comments.quote: Larval export from coastal wetlands is an important biological flux in many wetlands (see Saintilan and Mazumder 2017 for a review).

reviews.assessment: New and interesting angle with a clear structure, but key soil processes are missing and the conclusions are generic.
strengths: clear structure and easy to read
organization by scale from rhizosphere to landscape

comments.issue: Microbe-microbe interactions are excluded even though they may most strongly tip the carbon balance.
comments.request: Discuss how unquantified microbe-microbe interactions could tip the carbon balance.
comments.quote: This is also one of the weak points, as most probably, these form of interactions are the most important processes that might tip the balance in BCE's turning them from a sink of C to a source of C.

comments.issue: The global change section is short and omits relevant terrestrial literature.
comments.request: Expand the global change section with terrestrial literature.
comments.quote: The part on biotic interactions under global change is however rather short.

comments.issue: Carbon residence time in the rhizosphere and the aggregatosphere concept are missing.
comments.request: Reflect on carbon residence time and the aggregatosphere.
comments.quote: What about the duration of the carbon stored in the rhizosphere? It is not only about what goes in and what goes out.

comments.issue: The meta-analysis response-variable calculation has no literature reference and may be non-standard.
comments.request: Provide references for the response-variable calculation or justify it.
comments.quote: In the meta-analyses there is no literature reference used. Is this a standardized way also used by others to calculate the response variables?

comments.issue: Temperature-related effects are not incorporated; the section focuses on flooding.
comments.request: Incorporate temperature-related effects beyond flooding.
comments.quote: how do you incorporate temperature related effects like faster decomposition and faster nutrient uptake on biotic interactions and carbon cycling? Now it seems rather focused on the flooding aspect.

comments.issue: Consequences of the results for ocean carbon uptake and acidification are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss consequences for ocean carbon uptake and acidification.
comments.quote: Why is there nothing on how and if this potentially has consequences with carbon uptake and acidification in the ocean off the shore?

comments.issue: It is unclear where Part 3 begins.
comments.request: Clarify the numbering of Part 3.
comments.quote: Part 3 is not clearly numbered so I was wondering whether it starts at results and discussion or at data gaps and perspective?

comments.issue: The conclusion is generic and did not need the meta-analysis.
comments.request: Provide specific guidelines on the missing information.
comments.quote: a conclusion that didn't really needed the meta-analysis, and is also the easy generic conclusion of this kind of studies

title: Biota‐mediated carbon cycling—A synthesis of biotic‐interaction controls on blue carbon

study.system: two-patch meta-ecosystem; mobile consumers and nutrient recycling model

editor_summary: Exciting potential contribution; all four reviewers positive. Carefully address Reviewer 2 and 3 concerns about feeding versus habitat preference implementation and downstream analyses, and clarify writing and literature links.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and sound model study; asks mainly for clearer writing and tighter integration of text and figures.
strengths: writing very precise and generally clear

comments.issue: Heavy meta-ecosystem jargon and long sentences make key points hard to follow for a broad audience.
comments.request: Shorten sentences and add ecological intuition for the scenarios.
comments.quote: I often had trouble following certain key points because of the high level of jargon associated with meta-ecosystem ecology

comments.issue: Ecological insight is buried in the Ei equation; the top-down/bottom-up quantification is not explained.
comments.request: Split the Ei equation and explain the delta C minus delta P logic.
comments.quote: It might be helpful to break the Ei equation (p. 9 ln 54) into two smaller chunks

comments.issue: Coexistence ideas and meta-ecosystem results feel disjointed, and Figures 5-6 are poorly linked to the text.
comments.request: Integrate the sections and highlight the quantitative domains in the text.
comments.quote: the connections between the coexistence ideas and the meta-ecosystem models could be better integrated

comments.issue: Figure 6 results receive little attention in the discussion.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of Figure 6 for coexistence.
comments.quote: I also think the results presented in Figure 6 might warrant more attention in the discussion.

comments.issue: Chase et al. (2002) on predation-competition interaction is a potentially relevant missing reference.
comments.request: Cite this reference where appropriate.
comments.quote: Chase et al. (2002) The interaction between predation and competition, Ecology Letters, seems like a reference that might belong here too, if appropriate.

comments.issue: Phrase 'cascade up the ecosystem to impact higher trophic levels' is imprecise.
comments.request: Reword as 'cascade up the food web to influence biomass at higher trophic levels'.
comments.quote: instead of “cascade up the ecosystem to impact higher trophic levels”, perhaps “cascade up the food web to influence biomass at higher trophic levels”?

comments.issue: Two redundant uses of 'that' at p. 4 ln 35-42.
comments.quote: Consider just removing the two uses of “that”

comments.issue: Sentence at p. 5 ln 15-22 is long and complex.
comments.request: Shorten or split this sentence.
comments.quote: This is a long and complex sentence. I had trouble following it.

comments.issue: Results are previewed at p. 5 ln 26-40 instead of introducing the three scenarios.
comments.request: Introduce the three Figure 2 scenarios instead.
comments.quote: Rather than preview the results here, an alternative approach might be to introduce the three scenarios you’ll be exploring (Figure 2)

comments.issue: The transition where the direction of effects reverses at p. 12 ln 37-44 is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the pi range or the reversal point.
comments.quote: I think this could be made clearer in the text, either by specifying the range of pi values that the first half of this paragraph is discussing, or by explicitly specifying this transition point where the direction reverses.

comments.issue: The link between net effects approaching zero and pi approaching 0.5 is not stated.
comments.request: Clarify this relationship in the text.
comments.quote: is this indicated by the fact that the net effects, E, approaches zero as the preference, pi, approaches 0.5?

comments.issue: The cause of the spatial flux at p. 13 ln 35-39 could be reinforced.
comments.request: Point out the consumer transport mechanism here or in the discussion.
comments.quote: perhaps worth pointing out here or in the discussion that this spatial flux is because consumer transport moves resources produced from one ecosystem (where consumption occurred) to another

comments.issue: The mechanism behind the p. 14 ln 8-13 result is not made explicit.
comments.request: Explain that broad foraging plus strong habitat preference concentrates recycling.
comments.quote: perhaps worth pointing out here or in the discussion that this is because the lack of feeding preferences allows the consumer to forage and acquire resources from across the broader meta-ecosystem

comments.issue: The results paragraph at p. 16 ln 13 would benefit from a recap.
comments.request: Add a summary sentence after this paragraph.
comments.quote: a summary sentence after this results paragraph might be helpful

comments.issue: The scale-discrepancy mechanism at p. 17 ln 5-8 is unclear.
comments.request: Describe this mechanism more clearly.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I follow what this means as a mechanistic explanation for the patters described earlier in the sentence

comments.issue: The clear spatial-cascade phrasing at p. 17 ln 31-33 would work better in the introduction.
comments.request: Move this phrasing to the introduction.
comments.quote: I found this a much clearer and intuitive explanation of spatial cascades than what was presented in the introduction

comments.issue: Figure 4 caption does not explain the x-axis biologically or note that the inset is a zoom.
comments.request: Explain pi = 1 and pi = 0.5 and label the inset as a zoom.
comments.quote: Maybe remind the reader what the x-axis means, biologically, when pi = 1 or pi = 0.5. Also note that the inset is a closeup/zoom showing what happens near pi = 1.

comments.issue: Figure 5 reverses the consumer preference convention used in earlier figures, which could disorient readers.
comments.quote: For a reader this switch could be disorienting because the coexistence regions are depicted as a function of consumer 2’s habitat and feeding preferences

reviews.assessment: Excited by the question, but the decoupling of feeding preference from time spent in habitats is a fundamental sticking point.
strengths: results on recycling novel, interesting and well-presented
nice definition of the net effect of consumer recycling

comments.issue: With a type II functional response, feeding preference may be inconsistent with the time spent in each habitat.
comments.request: Clarify how feeding preference interacts with time spent and consumption rates.
comments.quote: It seems potentially problematic that in this time-limited feeding rate, they may not literally have the “time” to consume their preferred resource

comments.issue: Interpretations attribute effects to feeding preference, but realized consumption rates are never used as predictors.
comments.request: Relate realized consumption rates to the results and discussion.
comments.quote: The actual consumptive effects (realized feeding rates) however, are never shown as predictor variables for meta-ecosystem dynamics although they are likely better predictors than the feeding preference.

comments.issue: Terms 'preferred' and 'habitat' are jarring because feeding locations are also habitats.
comments.request: Consider alternative terminology.
comments.quote: Feeding locations are habitats too, and so to define feeding preferences and habitat preferences felt jarring.

comments.issue: The definition of spatial cascade is unclear and could also apply to a one-patch system.
comments.request: Tighten the definition and clarify what is spatial about it.
comments.quote: It’s unclear to me why this is necessarily a spatial cascade. A similar thing could happen in a one-patch ecosystem

comments.issue: Figure 3a lacks a reference line for the non-preferred resource held constant.
comments.request: Add a blue dashed reference line.
comments.quote: could you show a blue dashed line for what level the non-preferred resource would be at, since it is the one being held constant for the scenario shown by the red dashed line?

reviews.assessment: Excellent conceptual study; asks to connect the results to landscape-of-fear and food-web theory and to add model details.
strengths: results described in a very accessible way

comments.issue: The negative correlation scenario is not linked to the landscape-of-fear literature.
comments.request: Mention this research field and cite related case studies.
comments.quote: Specifically the case of negative correlation between habitat and prey preference reminds me a lot on systems investigated in the context of “landscape of fear”

comments.issue: Producer differences in edibility or nutritional value are not considered.
comments.request: Discuss or add an appendix case with dissimilar producer parameters.
comments.quote: a case where the producers also differ in their edibility to the predator (different nutrient uptake rates/growth rates of producers between the two habitats), or are of less nutritional value

comments.issue: Results are not discussed in the context of Gounand et al. 2014.
comments.request: Discuss the findings in relation to Gounand et al. 2014.
comments.quote: I am also missing a discussion of the presented results in context of Gounand et al. 2014

comments.issue: Findings are not strongly connected to non-spatial food web theory.
comments.request: Relate the results to coupled food chain and stage-structure theory.
comments.quote: Findings from this work could also be more strongly related to (non-spatial) food web theory.

comments.issue: Analysis is limited to stable point equilibria; dynamic behaviour is not examined.
comments.request: Consider a dynamic analysis of stability and alternative states.
comments.quote: it could also be interesting to use a dynamic approach, using an ode solver within Matlab, to solve the differential equation system

comments.issue: Parameter table S1 is in the supplement rather than the main manuscript.
comments.request: Move the parameter table to the main manuscript.
comments.quote: It would be nice if the parameter table S1 would be part of the main manuscript.

comments.issue: Units are not indicated and parameter values are not motivated.
comments.request: Report units and justify the parameter values.
comments.quote: The authors do not indicate any units and do not motivate the choice of parameter values.

reviews.assessment: Praises the introduction and discussion, but finds the decoupling of pi and w biologically impossible and the results hard to match to figures.
strengths: nice decoupling of spatial cascades due to redistribution versus numeric feedbacks

comments.issue: Treating feeding preference and time spent as independent is biologically impossible; travel and handling time are ignored.
comments.request: Reconsider or redefine w and discuss travel between feeding and excretion sites.
comments.quote: There is only a finite amount of time in a day, the animal can’t spend all its time in one place yet spend time foraging in another place.

comments.issue: Verbal results are difficult to match to figures; top-down and bottom-up components are not shown separately.
comments.request: Add an Ei schematic, show the two components, and align text with figures.
comments.quote: I found it difficult to match up the verbal description of the Results to the actual figures, or to interpret the findings of some of the figures.

comments.issue: Rationale for allowing nutrient input and export from outside the system is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain whether this is for realism or to prevent collapse.
comments.quote: Curious why the authors allow nutrient input/export from outside the system? Was this just for realism or is it needed to prevent collapse?

comments.issue: 'Productivity gets strengthened' implies a relationship; 'increased' is clearer.
comments.request: Replace 'strengthened' with 'increased'.
comments.quote: for this and other similar phrases, I think it’s best to just say it increased – strengthened sounds like a relationship between two things

comments.issue: Meaning of C1 being a better competitor 'when confined to a single local ecosystem' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what this statement means.
comments.quote: do the authors mean that if C1 and C2 were both trapped in either ecosystem, C1 would win? Regardless of ecosystem type?

comments.issue: The negative versus positive correlation description for the Figure 2 scenarios is confusing.
comments.request: Use a more biologically intuitive descriptor.
comments.quote: For some reason the description negative vs positive correlation is confusing to me, even though I understand the purpose being excretion where you eat or not.

comments.issue: What the change in consumer stocks in Figure 3 is relative to is unclear, and the figure lacks context.
comments.request: Explain the baseline and the figure's purpose.
comments.quote: What is the change in consumer stocks relative to? With vs without the spatial cascade, or relative to 0 or complete preference?

comments.issue: Phrasing may confuse preference for eating a producer with preference for spending time in an ecosystem.
comments.request: Carefully distinguish the two preferences in the text.
comments.quote: the authors could be super careful that the reader doesn’t mix up preference for eating a particular producer with preference for spending time in a particular ecosystem

comments.issue: Figure 4 caption does not bracket Ei or reference numbered equations, and x-axis landmarks are under-described.
comments.request: Reference the equations and describe where to look on the x-axis.
comments.quote: Could the authors put Ei in brackets and reference the equation (the equations need numbers!!) in the caption?

comments.issue: An empirical paper that could support arguments in the Introduction is not cited.
comments.request: Cite this suggested empirical reference.
comments.quote: I legit think this would be a good reference to an empirical paper to support some arguments in the Introduction

title: Traits affecting nutrient recycling by mobile consumers can explain coexistence and spatially heterogeneous trophic regulation across a meta‐ecosystem

study.system: mature oak canopy; leaf chemistry, predation, herbivores

editor_summary: Reviewers find the study original and well conducted but split on framing and design; editor asks to better frame it in the literature and stress novelty, and clarifies the mosaic concept and volatile signalling.

reviews.assessment: Rigorous canopy-crane study, but small tree number and uniform MeJA induction limit inference; results confirmatory and abstract overstates the predation link.
strengths: one of few studies of defense induction in mature trees
rigorous manipulation using a canopy crane
data rigorously analysed and paper nicely written

comments.issue: Only 8 trees; leaf-flush asynchrony means much variation is explained by tree rather than treatment.
comments.quote: The number of subject trees used in the study is rather small at 8, which coupled with the asynchrony in leaf flush

comments.issue: MeJA elicitation likely produces more uniform, less mosaiced induction than herbivore elicitation.
comments.quote: the induction is more uniform (and less ‘mosaiced’) at the branch level than would be by a similar degree of elicitation by herbivores

comments.issue: MeJA induction effects on chemistry are confirmatory given the many existing MeJA studies.
comments.quote: it is notable that a large number of studies have been conducted with MeJA as an elicitor. Hence, this comes across as a fairly confirmatory observation

comments.issue: Abstract and introduction imply the predation cascade is linked to induction, but induction did not affect caterpillars.
comments.request: Revise the abstract and introduction to remove this implication.
comments.quote: The statement in the abstract that ‘increased predation cascaded to caterpillar assemblages by decreasing their abundance’ is slightly misleading

comments.issue: Four line-level copy edits: undefined DBH, misspelled linalool, italics for (E)- and (Z)-, wording on line 403.
comments.quote: In general, remember to italicize the (E)- and (Z)- denoting trans and cis in compound names.

reviews.assessment: Sees much to like, but framing is phenomenological, hypotheses are untested, and the design cannot test treatment effects on herbivore communities.
strengths: chemical analyses are fantastic and thorough
design good for testing chemical induction and predation

comments.issue: Does not articulate how the study builds on previous work showing similar induction and trophic effects.
comments.request: Explain how this study builds on previous work.
comments.quote: did not clearly articulate how this study builds on previous work

comments.issue: Study remains phenomenological and does not test specific hypotheses.
comments.request: Move beyond phenomenological expectations and test specific hypotheses.
comments.quote: to move beyond a strictly phenomenological set of expectations

comments.issue: Novelty of this specific study is not described, reducing its broader impacts.
comments.request: Describe clearly what is novel about this study.
comments.quote: The authors need to take greater care to both describe the novelty of this work

comments.issue: Trees were sampled only once, three days after treatment, a limited test of induction effects.
comments.request: Justify the single sampling time point and acknowledge its limits.
comments.quote: I was surprised though, given the well-known effect of early-season induction on later season herbivory, that trees were only sampled once three days after treatments

comments.issue: Herbivore sampling three days after treatment leaves too little time for community effects; movement assumptions unjustified.
comments.request: Justify the herbivore sampling timing and movement assumptions on line 217.
comments.quote: Three days after induction treatments is great for sampling chemistry but does not give much time for treatments to modify the insect community

comments.issue: Discussion does not acknowledge the limitations of the experimental design.
comments.request: Acknowledge the design limitations in the discussion.
comments.quote: They seem to acknowledge this in the discussion, but don’t seem to acknowledge the limitations of their design

reviews.assessment: Technically excellent and statistically sound, but the results are unsurprising and the existing literature is ignored.
strengths: technically very well done and statistically sound

comments.issue: Results are interesting but not surprising, since canopy gradients are well known.
comments.quote: I find the results described herein very interesting, but also not very surprising

comments.issue: Extensive existing literature on canopy effects, oak VOC emissions and oak herbivory is neither cited nor discussed.
comments.request: Cite and discuss the existing canopy and oak VOC literature.
comments.quote: This extensive literature on canopy effects is not considered at all and addressed in the discussion

comments.issue: Data are not put in the context of within-crown VOC signalling, plant-internal signals, distances or air chemistry.
comments.request: Broaden the discussion beyond insect interactions to VOC signalling context.
comments.quote: Points I am missing here is plant-internal signaling, where VOCs might play a role

comments.issue: The 10 mM MeJA solution is very high and artificial, and treatment was repeated weekly.
comments.request: Justify the MeJA concentration and weekly repetition.
comments.quote: the MeJA solution of 10 mM is very high and artificial. Why was not a lower conc. applied

comments.issue: Radiation and temperature measurements and the justification for branch selection are missing.
comments.request: Report radiation and temperature data and justify branch selection.
comments.quote: Are there radiation and temperature measurements on each of the selected branches in the canopy?

comments.issue: Bag enclosure and passive VOC collection artefacts (CO2 depletion, condensation) are not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of the bag and passive collection method.
comments.quote: Closing the bags around the branches for 24 hours very much affects photosynthesis (CO2 depletion) and thus light-dependent VOC emissions

title: A mosaic of induced and non‐induced branches promotes variation in leaf traits, predation and insect herbivore assemblages in canopy trees

study.system: annual plant metacommunities; stochastic simulation model with seed banks

editor_summary: Editor: model identifies nonlinear dispersal-dormancy interactions; discussion clear; intro could engage Modern Coexistence Theory, clarify local vs regional stabilization and differentiate from Wisnowski et al. 2019.

reviews.assessment: Useful extension of process-based metacommunity models, but finds the dormancy-dispersal interaction not novel and wants stronger links to existing theory.
strengths: useful extension of Thompson et al. 2020 framework

comments.issue: The dormancy-dispersal interaction is not novel; prior community-ecology work is not engaged.
comments.request: Engage the prior literature and clarify the advance.
comments.quote: I felt that the result that dormancy and dispersal interactively influence community dynamics in competitive systems is not in and of itself novel.

comments.issue: The Snyder and Chesson 2006 framework is not used to structure hypotheses.
comments.request: Use it to frame expectations and intuition.
comments.quote: I think that the current manuscript could be greatly strengthened if the authors were to make more explicit use of the developments from this manuscript to structure hypotheses and provide intuition about results.

reviews.assessment: Excited by the topic and model realism, but wants a deeper introduction and more mechanistic analysis of why dormancy-dispersal patterns arise.
strengths: great writing with lots of potential

comments.issue: The introduction spends its opening on generic metacommunity background and underdevelops the seed-bank goals and underpinnings.
comments.request: Deepen the seed-bank framing and theory links.
comments.quote: The first two paragraphs could be applied to any paper examining metacommunity dynamics. As such, there isn’t as much space dedicated to important underpinnings of the papers’ main goals

comments.issue: Mechanisms named in the introduction (temporal buffering, dispersing propagules) are not implemented in the simulations.
comments.request: Implement or clearly discuss these mechanisms.
comments.quote: Two mechanisms by which dormancy can affect communities are mentioned (lines 78-84): buffering populations from temporal fluctuations, and dormant propagules dispersing, but neither of these mechanisms are built into the simulations

comments.issue: Dormant seeds do not disperse, so the fitness-density covariance mechanism should be discussed and tested.
comments.request: Discuss this mechanism and test dispersing dormant seeds.
comments.quote: dormancy could be something that affects the fitness-density covariance in a way that helps coexistence even if dispersal is eroding beta diversity

comments.issue: The germination-survival interplay is unsurprising and the interest in the 0.1 threshold is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain why this dynamic is interesting.
comments.quote: I didn’t find the interplay between germination and survival to be surprising

comments.issue: 'Reproductive sinks' appears too late in the narrative.
comments.request: Introduce it earlier.
comments.quote: ‘Reproductive sinks’ came up in the Discussion, which is a neat way of thinking about it, but I think it came up a bit too late in the narrative.

comments.issue: The abstract is too abstract to convey the key result or the nature of the interaction.
comments.request: State the key result concretely.
comments.quote: Perhaps a little too abstract – I can’t easily tell what the key result is beyond the broad interpretation of the result as showing that seed banks are important

comments.issue: Simulation run length and whether diversity was measured at equilibrium are unstated.
comments.request: Report iterations and equilibrium status.
comments.quote: How many iterations did each simulation run for? Was diversity measured at equilibrium?

comments.issue: Equation 1 should indicate which components refer to germinated versus ungerminated seeds.
comments.request: Annotate the equation.
comments.quote: Eq 1: “Seed survival” – would be great if it was clear this was of the germinated seeds

comments.issue: Equation 2's germination term should be explicitly identified as germinated individuals, not a rate.
comments.request: Make this explicit.
comments.quote: Eq 2: Germination = germinated individuals right? Not germination rate? I could see someone missing this and getting confused

comments.issue: Equation 7 should note that the rate d maps onto distance via the kernel.
comments.request: Clarify the kernel-distance relationship.
comments.quote: Eq 7: could be clear that although d is a rate, it typically translates onto distance by nature of the kernel

comments.issue: The number of species (30) and the initial seeding of the landscape are not described.
comments.request: State species number and initial conditions.
comments.quote: There were 30 species in the simulations yes? For the life of me I must have missed this detail and couldn’t find it but am guessing from the figures. Would be good to repeat.

comments.issue: Patch pixel counts, inter-patch distances and the fate of seeds landing off-patch are unclear.
comments.request: Describe patch geometry and off-patch seeds.
comments.quote: Line 163: How many pixels were each patch, and how close were patches to each other on average (+range) so this can be compared relative to the dispersal kernel?

comments.issue: The maximum population size in an optimal environment is not stated (line 195).
comments.request: State the maximum population size.
comments.quote: Line 195: Could say what the max population size is in an optimal environment – 20 individuals?

comments.issue: Whether dormant/non-surviving seeds enter the diversity surveys is unclear (lines 213-215).
comments.request: Clarify which life stages are surveyed.
comments.quote: Lines 213-215: Were dormant or non-surviving seeds counted in the diversity surveys?

comments.issue: The near-exponential increase with germination at low values is not captured by the gradual-transition description.
comments.request: Describe this pattern in the text.
comments.quote: Lines 248-249 and Fig. 3: It almost looks like an exponential increase with germination – huge difference at between very very low germination and very low germination, but small differences when germination rates are intermediate to high.

comments.issue: The wording at line 321 should say 'above a threshold level of germination, here, 0.1'.
comments.request: Adopt the suggested wording.
comments.quote: Line 321: Perhaps instead of “intermediate germination”, say, “above a threshold level of germination, here, 0.1, which is surprisingly low”.

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 3 repeat the same data; repetition may not be the best solution.
comments.request: Reduce the duplication and use the space.
comments.quote: Figure 2 vs Figure 3: These data are repeated in both eh? I get that it’s easier to see the extremes in Fig. 2 but I’m not super sure if repeating this is the best solution here.

comments.issue: The discussion does not cover natural scenarios or mechanisms behind the patterns.
comments.request: Add natural scenarios and mechanism discussion.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful to discuss the kinds of natural scenarios where one might expect to observe these results in experiments

comments.issue: The 'temporal dispersal' mechanism needs expansion.
comments.request: Expand its treatment.
comments.quote: Line 427: I think the “temporal dispersal” mechanism could be expanded a little bit.

reviews.assessment: Nice contribution; major concerns about identical rates across species and limited interaction scenarios, plus suggestions to interpret results ecologically.
strengths: nice contribution to coexistence mechanisms at different scales

comments.issue: All species share identical germination, survival and dispersal rates; a seed-mass trait would add realism.
comments.request: Include species-level seed mass variation.
comments.quote: the equal germination rate, seed survival, and dispersion for all species. I would suggest the inclusion of one functional trait, the seed mass

comments.issue: Competition scenarios are limited; rock-paper-scissors or facilitation could be explored.
comments.request: Broaden scenarios or acknowledge the limitation.
comments.quote: the competitive scenarios could explore a wider domain of interactions, by including not only stable coexistence, but also other stable dynamics such as rock-paper-scissors, or facilitative interactions

comments.issue: How to move the simulation work toward empirical settings is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss empirical translation.
comments.quote: yet the authors do not discuss how to move their simulation work toward empirical settings

comments.issue: The many results make the messages sometimes confusing; a mind-map and ecological definitions of diversity changes would help.
comments.request: Add a mind-map and define diversity changes.
comments.quote: As the authors have many results, the messages are sometimes a little bit confusing.

comments.issue: An ecological interpretation of the results is missing.
comments.request: Relate results to ecological implications.
comments.quote: an ecological interpretation of the results is missing

comments.issue: Figure 1 is not cited in the introduction.
comments.request: Cite it in the intro.
comments.quote: Fig. 1 could be cited in the intro to help the reader visualised the different concepts

comments.issue: The title omits dispersal.
comments.request: Add dispersal to the title.
comments.quote: Why the title does not include dispersal, like: 'the interactive effects of competition, dispersal, germination, and survival?

comments.issue: Line 56 uses both 'in parallel' and 'alongside'.
comments.request: Keep only one.
comments.quote: Line 56, either “in parallel” or “alongside”, not both.

comments.issue: 'Seed survival' should be added to Equation 1.
comments.request: Add the label.
comments.quote: Equation 1, add “seed survival” would avoid confusion

comments.issue: The assumption that one plant equals one produced seed is not stated.
comments.request: State this assumption.
comments.quote: I suppose that the authors make the assumption that one plant is equal to one seed produced. This assumption should be clearly stated.

comments.issue: Sentence 391 is confusing due to repeated 'low dispersal' wording.
comments.request: Rewrite it.
comments.quote: sentence 391 is confusing due to the repetition of “low dispersal” and “dispersal-limited communities”

comments.issue: 'Risky' at line 403 should be defined as survival=0.1,0.5.
comments.request: Define the term consistently.
comments.quote: Line 403, when using the word “risky”, I would state that it means ( survival=0.1,0.5) similarly to line 415.

comments.issue: The result at lines 428-429 is confusing; why low germination and survival cause seed-bank losses needs explanation.
comments.request: Explain this result.
comments.quote: Line 428:429: this result is confusing. How low germination and seed survival promote losses from the seed bank? Is the seed survival low as well? Need further explanations.

title: Seed banks alter metacommunity diversity: The interactive effects of competition, dispersal and dormancy

study.system: forest carbon use efficiency; plant physiological model and global data
