comments.issue: Fission-fusion is not unique to MLS; atomistic and molecular forms differ.
comments.request: Distinguish MLS fission-fusion from that of other societies.
comments.quote: these fission-fusion dynamics are not unique to MLS but also characterize other types of societies

comments.issue: The hamadryas description omits daily-scale fission-fusion.
comments.request: Include daily fission-fusion dynamics (Kummer's work).
comments.quote: this description of the fission-fusion dynamics of hamadryas baboons emphasizes only the seasonal aspects of grouping fluidity

comments.issue: The claim that ecological factors drive MLS across a wide range of taxa is a stretch.
comments.request: Qualify the broad ecological-driver statement.
comments.quote: the statement that ecological factors drive the formation of MLS across a wide range of taxa seems to be a bit of stretch

comments.issue: Kummer (1968) did not collect genetic relatedness data and is unsuitable for kin structure.
comments.request: Cite Staedele et al. (2015) instead.
comments.quote: Kummer (1968) may not be the best reference for kin-structure in hamadryas as he did not collect data on genetic relatedness among individuals

comments.issue: Labelling the community level 'apex' conflicts with the Grueter et al. (2020) framework.
comments.request: Call it the 'upper level' and note facultative intermediate/apex levels.
comments.quote: if the authors want to adopt the framework of Grueter et al. (2020), then labelling communities as the apex level may not be in line with that framework

comments.issue: The Discussion does not follow the results/aims order.
comments.request: Discuss the comparative study before the fairy wren example.
comments.quote: why not discuss the results of the comparative study before delving onto the fairy wren example? This is how the results were set up and also the aims at the end of introduction

comments.issue: No speculation on why cooperative breeding-MLS links have not been detected in other taxa.
comments.request: Speculate why no such links appear in e.g. primates.
comments.quote: Perhaps the authors may want to speculate as to why no such links have been detected in other taxa (e.g. primates)

comments.issue: The stated MLS criterion is insufficient; core units must amalgamate into higher-level entities.
comments.request: Correct the MLS definition at Line 394.
comments.quote: the mere fact that two or more stable social units seasonally emerge throughout the year doesn’t qualify as MLS; there needs to be an amalgamation of core units into higher-level entities

comments.issue: 'Social viscosity' is used repeatedly without adequate explanation.
comments.request: Explain the term.
comments.quote: the term ‘social viscosity’ is used repeatedly but not explained adequately

comments.issue: 'Hierarchical social structure' is ambiguous.
comments.request: Use 'multilevel social system' instead.
comments.quote: ‘hierarchical social structure’ is ambiguous; it’s better to use ‘multilevel social system’ instead

comments.issue: Bell et al. 1980 at Line 416 is missing from the reference list.
comments.request: Add the missing reference.
comments.quote: Line 416: Bell et al 1980 is not listed in the References

comments.issue: Geladas are not true baboons, so 'gelada baboons' is incorrect.
comments.request: Use 'geladas' or 'gelada monkeys'.
comments.quote: geladas are members of Theropithecus and not true baboons and should thus simply be called ‘geladas’ or perhaps ‘gelada monkeys’ but not ‘gelada baboons’

comments.issue: The order of increasing association levels is written in reverse.
comments.request: Correct the order to unit, team, band, community.
comments.quote: the correct order of increasing levels of associations should be 1) unit, 2) team, 3) band and 4) community (not the other way round, as currently written)

comments.issue: The semi-colonial description is imprecise; absence of between-group agonism does not make a society multilevel.
comments.request: Revise the definition and criterion.
comments.quote: the description of semi-colonial species is lacks precision; lack of between-group agonism is not sufficient to designate a society as multilevel

comments.issue: Table 1 references lack bibliographic details in the reference list.
comments.request: Add full bibliographic details for these references.
comments.quote: Table 1: why are these Refs not included in the reference list with all the relevant bibliographic details?

title: Cooperative breeding and the emergence of multilevel societies in birds

study.system: grassland plant communities; 4-yr field experiment and meta-analysis

editor_summary: Editor notes referees differ in enthusiasm about generality: an impressive experiment but with a very limited number of species and treatments; revision may be re-reviewed.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive and meticulously conducted experiment; asks the authors to explain the surprising nitrogen result and its relevance to natural conditions.
strengths: study conceived and conducted very well

comments.issue: Finding that nitrogen addition does not alter the diversity-invasibility relationship conflicts with studies showing N increases invasibility; the disconnect is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain how the negative relationship is maintained and address the disconnect.
comments.quote: Numerous studies have shown that increased levels of soil N results in increased invasibility of the environment. If the diversity-invasibility relationship can be maintained in the face of increasing invasibility, the authors need to explain how this occurs.

comments.issue: Unclear how far garden-experiment results apply to natural conditions with long-term nitrogen deposition.
comments.request: Discuss whether the diversity-invasibility relationship would persist under real conditions.
comments.quote: while the results may be highly replicable in other short-term garden experiments, the question remains as to what extent the results are actually relevant to natural conditions

comments.issue: Line-level edits: split the overlong sentence at lines 299-304; change 'Comparing' to 'Compared' (line 323).
comments.request: Split the sentence and correct the word.
comments.quote: I thought the sentence running from line 299-304 was too long and as a result, difficult to follow.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, well-articulated study of important topics, but its single-invader single-site design cannot support broad diversity-invasibility claims.
strengths: excellent, well-articulated study exploring important topics
addresses global change, invasion, biodiversity loss and N deposition

comments.issue: A single invader species, single site, two N levels and one propagule pressure level cannot support a general diversity-invasibility conclusion.
comments.request: Modify the claims or provide stronger arguments for generalizability.
comments.quote: One cannot, robustly extrapolate from a single study of Ambrosia artemesiifolia to a test of the diversity-invasibility hypothesis.

comments.issue: It is unclear why the selected traits are the right ones; a sensitivity analysis or PC loadings could identify key traits.
comments.request: Justify trait selection and identify the key traits.
comments.quote: it is unclear why traits such as C:N ratio, C:P ratio, SLA, WUE, etc., are the right traits to select

comments.issue: The complementarity and sampling ideas are not new, and a single-system study does not support the broad claim that protecting biodiversity safeguards communities.
comments.request: Modify the claims or strengthen the generalizability arguments.
comments.quote: these ideas are not new and while can criticize existing literature for lacking empirical support, a study of a single species in a single system, does not provide support for so broad a claim

comments.issue: Use of the word 'mechanism' is unclear; trait correlations are not a mechanism.
comments.request: Clarify or avoid calling trait correlations a mechanism.
comments.quote: The use of the word “mechanism” is unclear. Possession of functional traits correlated with particular responses may not be seen as a “mechanism” by many

comments.issue: FDis and CWM are phenomenological and sensitive to trait selection (e.g. flower colour versus rooting depth).
comments.request: Acknowledge the sensitivity of these metrics to trait choice.
comments.quote: the metrics (FDis and CWM) are phenomenological and likely to be quite sensitive to the traits selected

comments.issue: The experiment did not directly manipulate the mechanistic factors and possible covariates are not eliminated.
comments.request: Add text clarifying what the experiment does and does not manipulate.
comments.quote: the experiment did not directly manipulate the mechanistic factors, but the authors do not see this as a problem

comments.issue: Unclear why 200 invader seeds were used and what prevented additional seeding from nearby arable fields.
comments.request: Explain the seed number and potential additional seeding.
comments.quote: Why 200 seeds of the invader and what prevented additional seeding from the nearby arable fields?

comments.issue: PC loadings are not reported.
comments.request: Provide the PC loadings in supplementary information.
comments.quote: What were the PC loadings? Might be useful to provide in supplementary information.

comments.issue: Figure 1 uses species richness although the study is about functional traits; FDis and CWM would be more relevant.
comments.request: Plot FDis and CWM for each plot.
comments.quote: Figure 1 – what’s the point of using species richness? This study is all about functional traits, so functional diversity metrics would be more relevant, no?

reviews.assessment: Very well-conducted experiment with thorough trait exploration and clear writing; only minor comments on figures, multiple testing and wording.
strengths: thorough exploration of traits including the SEM analysis

comments.issue: Figure 4 is less readable than Fig. S3, which uses conceptual labels like 'invader-resident dissimilarity'.
comments.request: Modify Figure 4 using the labelling approach from Fig. S3.
comments.quote: Figure S3 is easier to read than Fig 4, because it includes conceptual labels like “invader-resident dissimilarity”

comments.issue: The many statistical comparisons in Table S3 risk inflated type I error.
comments.request: Use a False Discovery Rate approach (Storey et al. 2004).
comments.quote: The large number of statistical comparisons in Table S3 makes me wonder about whether inflated type I error could be a problem here.

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits (Ln 385, 427, 459).
comments.quote: Ln 385: change “showed” to “shown” Ln 427: “more an important” to “a more important” Ln 459: replace “despite the” with “while”

title: Functional traits explain the consistent resistance of biodiversity to plant invasion under nitrogen enrichment

study.system: bacteria and diatom; genome-scale metabolic networks, flux balance analysis

editor_summary: Improve clarity of the methodology; discuss the relationship between niches and traits rather than picking one; clarify the methodological details raised by Reviewer 2.

reviews.assessment: Novel and potentially useful framework, but presented too complexly, with unstated assumptions and telegraphic use-cases.
strengths: potentially useful tool to obtain ecological information from genomic data

comments.issue: The framework is presented in an overly complex and difficult way.
comments.request: Explain the methodology more clearly and concisely.
comments.quote: the way that the framework is presented is overly complex and difficult to follow, the authors should make an effort to explain the methodology in a more clear and concise way

comments.issue: Assumptions for the computations and weaknesses of the methods are not clearly stated.
comments.request: Thoroughly address the limitations and caveats of the methodology.
comments.quote: the assumptions for the computations and the possible weaknesses of the methods are not clearly stated

comments.issue: The aims and results of the E. coli, prokaryote and Phaeodactylum use-cases are almost telegraphic.
comments.request: Focus on one example or explain all use-cases in detail.
comments.quote: the explanation of the methods, aims of application of their model to each use-case and results are almost telegraphic

reviews.assessment: Argues the study characterises metabolic trait volumes rather than niches and finds the flux parameterisation and methods under-explained.
strengths: timely attempt to link genome-scale modelling with niche theory

comments.issue: The predicted fluxes are functional traits, not niches, so the metabolic niche concept is misapplied.
comments.request: Reframe the study or justify the niche terminology.
comments.quote: I would argue that what the authors attempted to do was characterise metabolic trait volumes rather than metabolic niches

comments.issue: Flux parameterisation is unspecified: the substrate, temperature and units behind 0.874 mmol g DW-1 h-1 are unknown and affect the Cartesian niche.
comments.request: Specify substrates, temperatures and flux parameterisation.
comments.quote: Are the authors referring to glucose, acetate, or succinate, for example? All of the fluxes will vary depending on the particular substrates and environmental conditions.

comments.issue: Temperature treatment, species-specific flux bounds and elemental stoichiometry are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify temperature handling, species-specific fluxes and stoichiometry.
comments.quote: Does that mean that the authors focused on a fixed temperature, don't know the temperature at which the reaction rate was measured, or did in fact control somehow for temperature?

comments.issue: It is unclear what the 0.874 value refers to and at what temperature the organism was grown.
comments.request: State the substrate and temperature.
comments.quote: p.5,54: mmol of what? What was the temperature of the organism?

comments.issue: The units of 0.7 are unclear: 70% of the growth rate or a minimum flux of 0.7 mmol/gDW/h.
comments.request: Clarify what the 0.7 value means.
comments.quote: What are the units of 0.7? Do the authors mean 70% of the growth rate or a minimum flux for survival of 0.7 mmol/gDW/h?

comments.issue: The 0.01 mmol/gDW/h value is called a death rate but is a minimum survival flux, and its choice is not justified.
comments.request: Correct the terminology and justify the threshold.
comments.quote: The value of 0.01 mmol/gDW/h is a minimum flux for survival, not a "death rate".

comments.issue: The 86e6 estimate depends on units and should be expressed dimensionlessly.
comments.request: Re-express this estimate in dimensionless units.
comments.quote: Is the estimate of 86e6 dependent on specific units. If so it should be re-expressed instead in dimensionless units

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the point at p.6,77 is that traits are correlated and effective dimensionality is lower.
comments.request: Clarify this point.
comments.quote: Unclear what the authors are getting at. Do they mean that the traits are highly correlated, so the effective dimensionality is substantially lower?

comments.issue: The stoichiometric notation may need a reaction index, and the system of equations lacks a reference.
comments.request: Check the notation and add a general reference.
comments.quote: shouldn't you have $\lvert a_{ij} \rvert$ rather than $\lvert a_{i} \rvert$ given that the stoichiometry of a given metabolite varies from reaction to reaction?

comments.issue: Whether v_j is always positive is unclear because line 280 implies negative values.
comments.request: Clarify the sign convention.
comments.quote: Are $v_j$ defined such that they are always positive? The wording on line 280 suggests that $v_j$ can be negative, indicating a reverse reaction.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether external metabolites are tracked in a separate vector, given steady state requires exchange.
comments.request: Clarify the external metabolite representation.
comments.quote: Does that mean there is another set of metabolites maintained in a column vector $\textbf{Mex}$ that are being kept track of?

comments.issue: What is meant by 'secreted' is unclear.
comments.request: Define 'secreted'.
comments.quote: By "secreted", do the authors mean that the metabolites leave the organism's body?

comments.issue: The claim that solutions satisfying the bounds are biochemically accurate is wrong: they are feasible, and steady state may require a smaller space.
comments.request: Clarify the feasibility and steady-state relationship.
comments.quote: I would replace the word accurate with feasible. And even if these bounds are satisfied, this does not necessarily imply steady state does it?

comments.issue: How influxes and effluxes are predicted from Eq. 1 is not clear.
comments.request: Explain how fluxes are predicted.
comments.quote: but is not at all clear how influxes/effluxes are predicted from Eq. 1. Further clarification needed.

comments.issue: The sentence at p.13,302 is unclear about whether growth rate corresponds to v_biomass.
comments.request: Clarify this sentence.
comments.quote: Sentence unclear. Does growth rate correspond to $v_{biomass}$ in the equation below?

comments.issue: The units of v_biomass and d_rate are unclear and a simpler notation is suggested.
comments.request: Clarify the units and notation.
comments.quote: Are unit for $v_{biomass}$ and $d_{rate}$ both $h^{-1}$.

comments.issue: Whether 'exchange reactions' means movement both into and out of the organism is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the term.
comments.quote: So, "exchange reactions" refers to movement of elements both into and out of the organism?

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits: 'encompasses' for 'resumes', 'emergent' for 'emerged', an awkward sentence at p.4,23-25, and singular/plural wording at p.12,269.
comments.quote: p.3, 4: "encompasses" rather than "resumes"?

reviews.assessment: Excellent, word-perfect study that fits Ecology Letters, with no suggestions for improvement.
strengths: explains the framework to a broad audience while detailing the mathematical theory

title: Contribution of genome‐scale metabolic modelling to niche theory

study.system: adaptive radiation model; intraclade consumers, resource productivity

editor_summary: Editor says all reviewers find the work novel and of broad interest, but the 'diversity hinders diversity' message is oversold, model specifics need explanation, and frameworks and terms must be clarified.

reviews.assessment: Praises the challenge to convention but finds the result unsurprising, the Abrams et al. explanation wrong and the message oversold.
strengths: challenges a widespread assumption about intraclade predation
can significantly change thinking about adaptive radiations

comments.issue: The main result is less surprising than presented: predation lowers density, fixing the fitness landscape and preventing frequency-dependent diversification.
comments.request: Acknowledge that the outcome follows directly from first principles.
comments.quote: At low density, the resource dynamics becomes independent of the ecomorphs and therefore the fitness landscape becomes fixed

comments.issue: The Abrams et al. 2008 explanation is incorrect: there, convergence stability is fixed and evolutionary stability changes with mortality, the opposite of this model.
comments.request: Correct the comparison with Abrams et al.
comments.quote: This explanation is not correct. In Abrams et al., the singular trait value is always convergence stable and it is evolutionary stability that changes with mortality.

comments.issue: The claim that diversification stops immediately is an artifact of the example; counter-adaptation or parameter changes could allow continued diversification.
comments.request: Soften the claim and discuss counter-adaptation and parameter dependence.
comments.quote: The authors say that diversification stops immediately when intraclade predation appears, which happens to be the case in the example shown in the ms but need not be the case in reality.

comments.issue: The title's 'diversity hinders diversity' overstates the mechanism, which is the addition of a single predatory species.
comments.request: Revise the title and message to reflect the actual mechanism.
comments.quote: The title goes even further when it claims "diversity hinders diversity".

comments.issue: The model mixes quantitative genetics and adaptive dynamics frameworks, using Lande's equation yet expecting evolutionary branching.
comments.request: Adhere to one framework or justify the combination.
comments.quote: The ms mixes the frameworks of quantitative genetics and adaptive dynamics.

comments.issue: Equidistant resources with equal productivity form a cartoon setup without robustness checks on distances.
comments.request: Test robustness to variation in resource distances and productivities.
comments.quote: The set-up of equidistant resources with largely equal productivity is a cartoon model

comments.issue: Assuming a moderate trait difference enables intraclade predation is a considerable simplification.
comments.request: Show that the result is robust to this simplification.
comments.quote: The assumption that a moderate difference in the single evolving trait value enables intraclade predation is also a considerable simplification.

comments.issue: The evolution of intraclade predation is trivial in this model and should not be highlighted as a result.
comments.request: Stop presenting the emergence of predation as a key result.
comments.quote: the evolution of intraclade predation is trivial and hardly a result to highlight in the Discussion

comments.issue: Excluding self-predation is inconsistent with predation depending only on trait proximity, and cannibalism is common.
comments.request: Justify or reconsider the no-cannibalism assumption.
comments.quote: The model assumes that an ecomorph never preys upon itself (eq. (3) and later equations exclude j from the summation for k).

comments.issue: It is unclear why population dynamics cycle with a linear functional response, and repeated branching per cycle conflicts with time-scale separation.
comments.request: Explain the cycles and reconcile them with the time-scale separation assumption.
comments.quote: It is unclear to me why the population dynamics exhibit cycles (the functional response is linear).

comments.issue: The principal branch of the Lambert function is unfamiliar to readers and not defined.
comments.request: Define W0 or at least state that it increases with W0(0)=0.
comments.quote: But at the very least, say that W0 is an increasing function with W0(0)=0, that's all what is needed to see the effect of mortality.

comments.issue: Figure 4C shows a diversity difference of +2 although the model allows at most +1.
comments.request: Check and explain the Figure 4C values.
comments.quote: in Fig 4C, how can the difference in diversity be +2? The model set-up allows for +1 at maximum.

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the study and values its contribution, but wants the DBD message scaled back and the generality and model assumptions discussed more.
strengths: important contribution to understanding adaptive radiations

comments.issue: The broader insight about predation on adaptive radiation is more important than the narrower intraclade framing and may be missed.
comments.request: Broaden the framing to predation in general, not just intraclade predators.
comments.quote: To me, these broader insights seem more important than the narrower ones that pertain to the evolution of predators within a radiation.

comments.issue: The relevance to the diversity-begets-diversity debate is strained; the work cannot prove diversity hinders diversity generally.
comments.request: Scale back DBD claims and limit them to the Discussion.
comments.quote: The work here is relevant to the impact of predation on the within-clade generation of additional diversity, but it falls well short of proving that diversity hinders diversity more generally.

comments.issue: The contrast with Janzen-Connell facilitation of coexistence is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this apparent paradox and its phylogenetic implications.
comments.quote: This apparent paradox seems potentially interesting to discuss, and could have implications for the expected phylogenetic structure of assemblages in areas with low or high predation.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the parameter lambda, representing small individual predator effects, changes the effect of predation on diversification.
comments.request: Test how varying lambda influences the results.
comments.quote: Does changing the value of this parameter influence the effect of predation on diversification?

comments.issue: It is unclear how much the central result depends on discrete, fixed resource optima versus a continuous resource distribution.
comments.request: Discuss the influence of the discrete-optima assumption explicitly.
comments.quote: It's not clear, however, how much the central result depends on this property of the model, and whether we might expect a similar outcome from a continuous resource distribution.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 'density' and 'abundance' mean the same thing.
comments.request: Clarify the terminology.
comments.quote: 62 - is "density" the same as "abundance" here?

comments.issue: The symbols Ri and delta are not defined.
comments.request: Define these symbols.
comments.quote: 91 - Ri not defined 117 - delta not defined

comments.issue: Given tao's orientation, the index is better described as generalization than specialization.
comments.request: Rename the index to reflect generalization.
comments.quote: given tao's orientation (small values = more specialization), I think it would be better described in this context as a generalization (not specialization) index

comments.issue: 'Intraclade consumer evolution' could be generalized to 'Predation'.
comments.request: Use the more general term.
comments.quote: 'Intraclade consumer evolution' could be generalized to "Predation", I think.

comments.issue: The cyclical diversification of the predator lineage in Figure 1b is not mentioned in the caption.
comments.request: Mention and discuss the cyclical diversification explicitly.
comments.quote: the cyclical diversification of the predator lineage at the bottom right of 1b is worth explicit mention in the caption

comments.issue: Figure 1C does not allow contrasting fitness profiles between scenarios A and B.
comments.request: Add the fitness profile of scenario A.
comments.quote: for Panel C, it would be helpful to be able to contrast the fitness profiles of the scenario in A to the one from scenario B currently depicted.

comments.issue: All Figure 1 fitness profiles precede the evolution of a specialist predator.
comments.request: Add a fitness profile from another time point.
comments.quote: Also, all of the fitness profiles depict fitness surfaces that precede the evolution of a specialist predator. Could another time point be added?

reviews.assessment: Very intriguing, valuable contribution, asking mainly for clarification of reproductive isolation, mortality, diversification terminology and model intuition.
strengths: valuable and needed contribution to micro- to macro-scale evolutionary theory

comments.issue: Reproductive isolation is implied by the simulations, since recombination would break down divergent selection, but the text implies ambivalence.
comments.request: Clarify that reproductive isolation is implicitly assumed.
comments.quote: given the way you simulate the divergences, I would argue that you do imply reproductive barriers, since without them, recombination between the ecomorphs would break down the result of the divergent selection

comments.issue: Whether a lineage or morph can go completely extinct through mortality is unclear.
comments.request: Make the role of mortality and extinction explicit.
comments.quote: you do include mortality, but it is unclear whether a lineage/morph could go completely extinct based on this?

comments.issue: 'Diversification' is used in an intermediate sense without definition, although the term differs across fields.
comments.request: Define diversification early and use the term consistently.
comments.quote: I think you should define somewhere early on in the paper how you intend to use the term ‘diversification’

comments.issue: 'Ecological attractor' and 'repellor' are central but unexplained, including why populations evolve towards a repellor.
comments.request: Explain these concepts for a broad audience.
comments.quote: I was wondering whether the meaning of ‘ecological attractor’ (e.g., line 121) and ‘repellor’ (e.g., line 141) should be explained a bit more?

comments.issue: Why lineages evolve towards optima 1 and 2.5 rather than 1 and 2, and how the fitness landscape shifts, is not intuitively clear.
comments.request: Explain this logic early and consider expanding Figure 1.
comments.quote: Possibly, clearing this up would also make clearer why on line 175ff., the lineages evolve towards optimum 1 and 2.5, instead of just 1 and 2

comments.issue: It is unclear how the model scales to species numbers typical of real large adaptive radiations.
comments.request: Discuss whether the process speed is comparable to real radiation rates.
comments.quote: do you have a sense on how this model scales with species/ecomorph numbers more akin to actual large adaptive radiations?

comments.issue: The one-dimensional gradient forces a highly pectinate tree, unlike real radiations, which affects how niche space fills.
comments.request: Address the implications of the ladder-like tree structure.
comments.quote: your model implies lineages to evolve along one gradient, meaning that only the population on the leading edge will further diversify, while all others stay static once they established in their niche, leading to a highly pectinate (ladder-like) tree

comments.issue: The absence of other clades in the model is a limitation that could be addressed.
comments.request: Discuss whether other lineages' ecomorphs would lessen predator effects.
comments.quote: I was wondering about the effect of the absence of other clades in this model

comments.issue: Choosing D to ensure disruptive selection strongly shapes the findings and should be restated when discussing results.
comments.request: Re-state the implications of the choice of D.
comments.quote: This seems like a sensible choice, but I presume that it has strong implications on finding the results you did find?

comments.issue: It is unclear why several resources are considered but only one predator type, and whether cyclic consumers feed on two subsets.
comments.request: Explain the cyclic evolution of the two consumers and the predator setup.
comments.quote: You refer to how single food resources are rare in adaptive radiations and thus consider several here, but only employ one type of predator?

comments.issue: Whether the patterns break down if ecomorphs can feed on multiple resources or shift opportunistically is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of opportunistic feeding.
comments.quote: do you anticipate the patterns you found to break down if ecomorphs can feed on multiple resources or can shift opportunistically?

comments.issue: The two opposing effects of productivity could look contradictory and their interaction is not elaborated.
comments.request: Elaborate how the two productivity effects interact in net terms.
comments.quote: I was wondering whether it might be good to explicitly elaborate a little how those two effects of productivity interact, e.g., in terms of net effect?

comments.issue: Non-gradual evolution could allow lineages to cross fitness valleys and access niches despite earlier predators.
comments.request: Consider whether non-gradual evolution can overcome the predator effect.
comments.quote: couldn’t non-gradual evolution allow lineages to access more niches DESPITE the earlier emergence of the predators (e.g., by allowing to cross valleys on the fitness landscape)?

comments.issue: It is untested whether a predator optimum nested within the trait space, rather than at an extreme, changes the dynamics.
comments.request: Test a predator optimum nested within the other traits.
comments.quote: I was curious whether the dynamic would change if the trait optimum for the intraclade consumer was not on one of the extremes of the trait space but nested within the others?

comments.issue: Several sentences are long and convoluted, and small language and caption edits are needed (49, 153ff, 164, 167, 171ff, 292ff, Fig. 3).
comments.request: Shorten and simplify the convoluted sentences.
comments.quote: I found that there were a few sentences throughout the manuscript that felt rather long and convoluted

title: The enrichment paradox in adaptive radiations: Emergence of predators hinders diversification in resource rich environments

study.system: spatially coupled population oscillators; stochastic models and synchrony theory

editor_summary: Editor finds the paper clearly written, accurate and interesting; reviewer 1's concern about ecological relevance must be addressed and the broader message made accessible to non-theorists.

reviews.assessment: Nice and educational paper with interesting ideas, but the main new science lies elsewhere and the spatially independent noise is a substantial weakness.

comments.issue: The main new science is in Noble et al. (2015); this paper's benefits are mainly educational.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution relative to Noble et al. 2015.
comments.quote: It seems to me the Noble et al (2015) paper has the main new science in it, the benefits of this paper being more along the lines of teaching ecologists how to understand and interpret these kinds of ideas

comments.issue: The Kendall reference is pure theory; Sheppard et al. 2019 provides the first empirical example of interacting Moran effects.
comments.request: Also cite Sheppard et al. 2019.
comments.quote: The Kendall reference is pure theory, you should also cite Sheppard et al (2019), Plos Comp Biol 15, e1006744, which appears to be the first empirically substantiated example of interactions

comments.issue: Mean field synchrony measures from Sheppard et al. 2016 are not cited.
comments.request: Consider citing Sheppard et al. 2016.
comments.quote: For other non-pairwise measures of synchrony, in some ways also inspired from physics, see the mean field techniques of Sheppard et al (2016), Nat Clim Change, 6, 610, which you may consider citing here

comments.issue: Axis labels in the Figure 1a bifurcation diagram are too small to read.
comments.request: Enlarge the axis labels.
comments.quote: The axis labels in the bifurcation diagram in panel a are too small to read

comments.issue: The paragraph at L64 is confusingly long.
comments.request: Split the paragraph.
comments.quote: this paragraph is confusingly long, and should be split up

comments.issue: What values of j the sum in equation 1 runs over is not specified.
comments.request: State that the sum is over nearest neighbours.
comments.quote: The sum is over j, but it needs to be specified in the text what values of j the sum is over.

comments.issue: N_i should likely be inside the sum and indexed by donor patch j, so the model description may contain an error.
comments.request: Fix or clarify the N indexing in equation 1.
comments.quote: The second term on the right side of 1 represents contributions to patch i that come from nearest neighbors. But then shouldn’t the N_i be inside the sum, and indexed by j instead of i?

comments.issue: Whether the Gaussian noise is independent across space and time is not stated explicitly.
comments.request: State the independence assumption for the noise.
comments.quote: I am *assuming* they are also taken to be independent across space and time, but this needs to be specified explicitly.

comments.issue: The same imprecisions recur in Appendices A and B, where e.g. <;> is undefined.
comments.request: Fix the notation in the appendices.
comments.quote: All or most of these failures to describe the model in a way that admits only one interpretation are repeated in various ways in Appendices A and B, so need to be fixed there, as well.

comments.issue: The green area in Figure 1f is never explained when first cited.
comments.request: Explain the green area at first mention.
comments.quote: Fig 1f is cited in the first paragraph of 2.1, but I cannot see any explanation of what the green area represents. Please add one.

comments.issue: Axis labels and numbers are too small to read on printouts across figures.
comments.request: Make axis labels and numbers much larger.
comments.quote: the axis labels and numbers are too small to see unless I blow the pdf up enormously. This means they won’t be decipherable on a printout. Please make them a lot bigger.

comments.issue: Figure captions do not state the scenario covered in the first line.
comments.request: Indicate the scenario in the first line of each caption.
comments.quote: It would be helpful for readers who are viewing or re-viewing the figures for the sake of comparing the dynamics of your different scenarios if you indicated the scenario covered by the figure in the first line of the figure caption.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether “kurtosis” means excess kurtosis.
comments.request: State which kurtosis definition is used.
comments.quote: You say “kurtosis” but you appear to mean “excess kurtosis”.

comments.issue: The inference only holds when synchrony is caused by dispersal, limiting applicability to real systems synchronised by Moran effects.
comments.request: Discuss the limits imposed by Moran effects and other synchrony sources.
comments.quote: It’s important to recognize that this is only the case in your model scenario, where the mechanism of synchrony is dispersal.

comments.issue: The abstract sets up an expectation that the paper does not satisfy.
comments.request: Revise the abstract to represent the actual result.
comments.quote: I would just like you to revise the abstract to represent the result you actually produced instead of setting up an expectation that is not, in the end, satisfied.

comments.issue: The noise is iid across space and time, whereas real environmental noise is spatially and temporally correlated.
comments.request: Discuss how spatially and temporally correlated noise would change the results.
comments.quote: But real environmental noise will be heavily correlated across space, and often also autocorrelated through time. How would this change things?

comments.issue: The paper could be framed around the debate over dispersal versus Moran effects as causes of synchrony.
comments.request: Consider discussing the dispersal-versus-Moran-effects debate.
comments.quote: It may be possible to frame the paper in another way, as well. There has been some debate about whether dispersal or Moran effects are “more important generally” for causing synchrony in real ecological systems.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and novel idea, but the ecological value of identifying cycle origins is unclear and robustness to autocorrelated noise is untested.

comments.issue: It is unclear what value is added by knowing the origin of cyclic dynamics.
comments.request: Show the reader what this information is useful for, e.g. forecasting.
comments.quote: it isn’t clear what value is added when we do understand the origin of the cycles

comments.issue: Findings may not hold under spatially autocorrelated noise, which is common in nature.
comments.request: Test robustness to spatially autocorrelated noise.
comments.quote: it might be useful to also consider how robust the findings are to spatially autocorrelated noise in addition to the spatially independent noise considered here

comments.issue: The abstract and introduction do not highlight the motivation of the work.
comments.request: Strengthen the motivation in the abstract and introduction.
comments.quote: The abstract and introduction don’t do a great job to highlight the motivation of this work.

comments.issue: Results are organised cyclically; local dynamics are presented after the synchrony material.
comments.request: Reverse the order to use local dynamics to frame synchronisation.
comments.quote: I might suggest reversing the order and using the discussion of local dynamics to highlight why synchronization can or cannot occur in the various regimes

comments.issue: Whether the threshold in Figures 1f, 3 (center) and 4a is derived from one of the paper's metrics is unclear.
comments.request: State how the threshold was determined.
comments.quote: It wasn’t immediately clear in the MS if the threshold shown in figure 1f, 3(center) and 4a is determined using one of the metrics in this paper.

comments.issue: The disordered region likely contains emerging synchronised clusters (Stone et al. 2002) that are not examined.
comments.request: Show the spatial ACF in a plot like Figure 3.
comments.quote: It has been described elsewhere that the transition from ‘disordered’ to synchronous follows a pattern in which clusters of synchronized patches begin to emerge across the landscape

comments.issue: Whether the results hold for period-4 and greater cycles, or for continuous-time models, is untested.
comments.request: Discuss or test other cycle types and continuous-time approaches.
comments.quote: would the results here hold for oscillations that arise in these different types of circumstances ?

comments.issue: Prior work noting that synchrony mostly occurs in inherently cyclic systems is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Strogatz, Ranta, Becks, Haynes and Vasseur and Fox for context.
comments.quote: All of these citations may be useful in helping to build some greater context for this work.

title: Noise‐induced versus intrinsic oscillation in ecological systems

study.system: Soay sheep MHC genes; 30-year fitness and genotype records

editor_summary: Editor notes referees were enthusiastic about the unique dataset but felt it was underexploited; supports additional analyses and rewriting, and wants a profound revision addressing all points.

reviews.assessment: Likes the dataset and haplotype-frequency plots, but finds the study largely standard and the analyses do not test the claimed mechanisms.
strengths: graphs of haplotype frequency change over time
power to address MHC polymorphism controversies

comments.issue: The study largely repeats standard MHC-fitness association approaches and does not stand out from earlier work.
comments.request: Make better use of the unique dataset to go beyond earlier studies.
comments.quote: As it is now, the manuscript does not go much beyond standard ways of studying selection acting on MHC, and associations of MHC/MHC heterozygosity with fitness components were reported by several earlier studies.

comments.issue: Total fitness and adult lifetime breeding success are defined identically, so total fitness is not truly measured.
comments.request: Measure total fitness as number of grandoffspring and clarify the distinction.
comments.quote: But I’m confused how the fitness is actually measured, because definitions of total fitness and adult lifetime breeding success (adult LBS) do not differ (“the number of offspring an adult produced over its lifetime”).

comments.issue: NFDS and fluctuating selection are not explicitly tested; year-by-haplotype interactions are missing from models.
comments.request: Test year*haplotype interactions and simulate fluctuation versus neutrality.
comments.quote: Both NFDS and FS, however, predict that fitness associations of MHC haplotypes would vary with time; this can be tested as year*haplotype interaction, but such interaction was apparently not included in the models.

comments.issue: Support for multiple selective mechanisms is claimed without showing HA and NFDS act on true total fitness.
comments.request: Test HA and NFDS on true total fitness before claiming multiple mechanisms.
comments.quote: I disagree with the authors that their results support multiple mechanisms (eg heterozygote advantage (HA)on juvenile survival, but NFDS on male fitness), unless both HA and NFDS are shown to act on true total fitness

comments.issue: In simulations no haplotype except D is ever lost by drift, which is suspicious and unexplained.
comments.request: Remark on this in the results and comment in the discussion.
comments.quote: I find it curious that except for haplotype D, none of the hapotypes ever gets lost in simulations by drift.

comments.issue: The claim that heterozygote advantage cannot be demonstrated without same-locus alternatives is conceptually wrong.
comments.request: Reconsider the statement given the antigen-presentation mechanism of HA.
comments.quote: I disagree with the statement that “heterozygote advantage cannot be demonstrated without knowing that alleles are alternatives at the same locus”.

comments.issue: Adult LBS is defined identically to fitness, and the life stage at which offspring are counted is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the measures differ and when offspring are counted.
comments.quote: Adult lifetime breeding success (adult LBS) is defined in the same way as fitness, i.e. “the number of offspring an adult produced over its lifetime” – do these measures differ in any way?

comments.issue: It is unexplained why total fitness is tested against haplotype H while other components are tested against the mean.
comments.request: Justify the different reference categories used in Figure 1.
comments.quote: Results, Fig. 1 – why is total fitness tested against haplotype H, and other components against the mean?

comments.issue: Haplotypes with opposite male fitness effects both raise anti-helminth IgE, which is left uninterpreted.
comments.request: Comment on this contradictory IgE pattern in the discussion.
comments.quote: this is rather remarkable that alleles associated with high and with low fitness in males (D and C, respectively) are both associated with increased anti-helminth IgE levels

comments.issue: References 58 and 59 are identical.
comments.quote: Minor points: Refs 58 and 59 are identical

reviews.assessment: Exceptional, important contribution; no major concerns, only suggestions to clarify definitions and engage with prior literature.

comments.issue: The distinction between fitness measurements and fitness components, and between total fitness and adult LBS, is confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the difference between these fitness measures.
comments.quote: I find the somewhat artificial distinction between ‚fitness measurements‘ and ‚fitness components‘ a bit confusing.

comments.issue: The claim that only a few studies tested MHC-fitness associations in the wild is incorrect.
comments.request: Remove these statements; the work remains exceptional regardless.
comments.quote: I find statements such as „only a few studies have tested associations between fitness and MHC variation in the wild“ (L108) incorrect.

comments.issue: The latest MHC review detailing open questions is not cited.
comments.request: Add Radwan et al. 2020 (Trends in Genetics) to the introduction.
comments.quote: I would suggest to add the latest MHC review by Radwan et al. 2020 (Trends in Genetics) in the introduction, detailing the remaining open questions.

comments.issue: Work elaborating divergent allele advantage is not cited, and the divergence metric could be improved.
comments.request: Add Pierini & Lenz 2018 and consider Grantham distance over p-distance.
comments.quote: I would suggest to add Pierini & Lenz 2018 MBE here for an elaboration and evaluation of the divergent allele advantage.

comments.issue: A helpful visual description of the mechanism is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Lenz 2018 PNAS where the process is described.
comments.quote: Lenz 2018 PNAS provides a succint and visual description of this process that might help to picture this mechanism.

comments.issue: Saying heterozygote advantage cannot be evaluated where allele number proxies heterozygosity is misleading.
comments.request: Acknowledge that allele number is often used as a heterozygosity proxy.
comments.quote: The number of alleles is often used as a proxy for ‚heterozygosity‘, so it’s a bit misleading to say that the heterozygote advantage cannot be evaluated in such systems.

comments.issue: Only linear associations are tested, though an optimal MHC diversity would imply quadratic associations.
comments.request: Test whether divergence-fitness associations are quadratic.
comments.quote: The authors here only test for linear associations between allele divergence and fitness, but some studies also suggest that there could be a quadratic association, implying an optimal MHC diversity/divergence.

comments.issue: Whether the selected haplotype is favoured because of unusually high divergence is untested.
comments.request: Test the relative average divergence of the selected haplotype.
comments.quote: Did the authors test the relative average divergence of the selected haplotype? Could it be that it provides a particularly high divergence and is therefore selected for?

comments.issue: The claim to be the first study of this kind is incorrect.
comments.request: Remove or rephrase the statement.
comments.quote: This statement is not correct. Clearly this is not the first study of this kind, it might be the largest though.

comments.issue: Table 1 abbreviations are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the abbreviations in the Table 1 legend.
comments.quote: Please provide explanations for the abbreviations in table 1 in the legend.

title: Contemporary selection on MHC genes in a free‐living ruminant population

study.system: temperate trees; IDENT-MTL diversity experiment, 11 years

editor_summary: Reviewers found the study timely and relevant; address their suggestions and clarify whether diversity effects could involve reduced natural-enemy impacts, and whether fencing excluded only large vertebrate herbivores or also invertebrates.

reviews.assessment: Timely and readable, with questions 1-2 clear, but wants deeper analysis and clearer justification of the question 3 functional identity results.
strengths: answers to questions 1 and 2 clear and believable

comments.issue: Explanations for the functional identity results are high level, and whether the Figure 5 patterns are driven by particular treatments or are statistically robust is untested.
comments.request: Inspect the raw data, test Low versus Medium robustness, and identify driving treatments.
comments.quote: I found the authors’ explanations in the Discussion to be very high level and, while not necessarily wrong, could probably be improved upon by closer inspection of the raw data.

comments.issue: Basal area is standing biomass rather than productivity, and its cumulative nature is not made clear.
comments.request: Clarify that G is cumulative net productivity over 11 years, not annual productivity.
comments.quote: I would normally interpret basal area as a measure of standing biomass rather than productivity.

comments.issue: The strength of the diversity-productivity relationship and per-treatment productivity are not extractable from the paper.
comments.request: Add a productivity versus treatment figure showing each mixture, with discussion.
comments.quote: The reader will be immediately curious as to how strong the relationship between diversity and productivity actually is. What was the productivity of each treatment?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the Appendix S4 confidence intervals are standard errors of the mean.
comments.request: State what the Appendix S4 intervals represent.
comments.quote: Are the 95% confidence intervals here based on standard errors of the mean?

comments.issue: Whether trees died, and how deaths and replanting affect treatment categories, is not described.
comments.request: Describe tree mortality and replanting procedures.
comments.quote: Have any of the trees died over the course of the experiment? Presumably, yes. What is done in such cases?

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits: 'A NE 0' at L208, missing parentheses at L225, and 'confident interval' at L519.
comments.quote: L519: “confident interval” -> “confidence interval”

comments.issue: The equation at L215 is improperly formatted.
comments.request: Format the equation with equals and multiplication signs and non-italic cov, per Loreau & Hector (2001).
comments.quote: Please format this equation properly. I believe there should be an equals sign at the start of the second line, and that the “x” should be a multiplication sign.

comments.issue: Figures 4 and 5 use different colour schemes for Low, Medium and High.
comments.request: Use the same colour scheme in both figures.
comments.quote: Is there a reason why the colours used for Low, Medium and High are different in each of the figures?

comments.issue: The units of net diversity effects are not given on the axes of Figures 4 and 5.
comments.request: Add units to the axes.
comments.quote: Are the units of NE also m^2/ha? It would seem so. If so, put the units on the axes.

comments.issue: The L351 statement about diverse stands being more productive is not shown in any figure.
comments.request: Show the diversity-productivity relationship in a figure if it is a new result.
comments.quote: Was this a new result or a prior result? If it’s a new result, the diversity–productivity relationship should be shown in a figure.

comments.issue: L424 cites Appendix S4 where Figure 3 is the appropriate reference.
comments.request: Correct the figure callout at L424.
comments.quote: The appropriate figure reference here would appear to be Figure 3, not Appendix S4.

comments.issue: L446 lacks a figure callout and misstates conifer dominance as increasing productivity.
comments.request: Add the Figure 4 callout and reword around conifer dominance reducing productivity.
comments.quote: I assume the relevant figure here is Fig. 4. Please add a callout to the figure.

comments.issue: The surprise at functional identity mattering is overstated given multiple possible causes; seed-mass treatments may drive the pattern.
comments.request: Unravel the functional identity result with raw data, e.g. Betula and Larix mixtures.
comments.quote: Is this really so surprising though? Isn’t it possible for there to be multiple causes of diversity effects on productivity?

comments.issue: The Discussion cites Figures 5 and 6 although only five figures exist, and lacks callouts.
comments.request: Fix the figure numbering and add callouts in the Discussion.
comments.quote: The Discussion refers to Figures 5 and 6, but there are only five figures in the paper. The figure references appear to be misnumbered.

reviews.assessment: Likes the manuscript and accepts the main finding, but disputes the competition-complementarity interpretation and finds the discussion speculative.
strengths: confirms forest diversity effects increase over time
novel crossed richness by functional diversity design

comments.issue: Only cumulative basal area is analysed; yearly increments are not examined.
comments.request: Add analyses of yearly increments in G, perhaps in the appendix.
comments.quote: it would be nice if the authors could add analyses of yearly increments in G, perhaps in the appendix

comments.issue: G is used simultaneously as a productivity measure and a competition measure.
comments.request: Use separate measures for productivity and competition.
comments.quote: I would not at the same time use G as productivity measure AND as competition measure, even though accumulated productivity can cause light competition.

comments.issue: G versus biodiversity over time is not plotted, and Figure S4 shows G levelling off while complementarity increases.
comments.request: Add G versus biodiversity versus time plots and explain the levelling-off.
comments.quote: Now we only have Fig. S4, which is a bit "disturbing" because G levels off yet complementarity effects increase.

comments.issue: Self-thinning is misused for mixtures where mortality is largely not self-thinning.
comments.request: Use mortality instead of self-thinning for mixtures.
comments.quote: I really find it problematic to use the term self-thinning also for mixtures where most of it is alien thinning.

comments.issue: Mortality results are not reported.
comments.request: Add mortality results as an appendix.
comments.quote: It would be useful if you could add mortality results as an appendix.

comments.issue: The interpretation linking competition to complementarity is illogical because complementarity reduces competition; competition relates to selection effects.
comments.request: Revise the competition-complementarity interpretation and stop mis-citing Williams et al. 2017.
comments.quote: I have a problem with the interpretation that competition is related to complementarity effects. I think this is not logical, because complementarity reduces competition.

comments.issue: Which statistical models were fitted is unclear and the results are not reproducible.
comments.request: Report models and use functional contrasts to test linearity of year effects.
comments.quote: For me, it is not entirely clear which statistical models were fitted and how I would reproduce the results if I had the data.

comments.issue: The Discussion and Conclusion are speculative and contain sloppy argumentation about self-thinning and competition.
comments.request: Remove the speculative and sloppy argumentation.
comments.quote: In particular the sloppy argumentation about "self-thinning", G=competition, competition=complementarity etc. (see above) should be removed.

comments.issue: Huang et al. 2018 and Chen et al. 2020 are not cited where forest complementarity over time is discussed.
comments.request: Cite Huang et al. 2018 (and Chen et al. 2020) at lines 70-76, 96-97, 122 and 348.
comments.quote: Huang et al. 2018 should be mentioned here as well as the first study showing that complementarity effects in forest biodiversity experiments can increase over time

comments.issue: Awkward genitive constructions appear throughout.
comments.request: Omit unnecessary genitives at lines 80 and 82.
comments.quote: often there are awkward uses of genitive in the manuscript. Like here, they could mostly simply be omitted.

comments.issue: 'Plots' and 'plot' at line 175 should read 'species composition'.
comments.request: Replace plots/plot with species composition at line 175.
comments.quote: 175: replace "plots" and "plot" by "species composition"

comments.issue: G is equated with competition at line 196 after being defined as productivity at line 191.
comments.request: Remove the confusing G=competition statement.
comments.quote: here it is really confusing to say G=competition when on line 191 you had G=productivity.

comments.issue: The random-term structure at lines 284-287 is unclear, including species composition random slopes and centering of contrasts.
comments.request: Describe the random terms and contrast centering.
comments.quote: where is species composition as random term? I assume you need this because the replicate plots within species compositions must have the same Fdis

comments.issue: A section ends with a citation at lines 367-368.
comments.request: Delete the references at the end of the section.
comments.quote: It is always bad to end a section with a citation.

comments.issue: Evidence that high competition produces high selection effects in early dense stands is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Williams et al. 2017 and Luo et al. 2020 at line 378.
comments.quote: Williams et al. 2017 and Luo et al. 2020 (Oikos) show high selection effects under high competition during early stages in dense stands.

comments.issue: The findings of Williams et al. 2017 are inverted at lines 401-403.
comments.request: Correct the account of Williams et al. 2017.
comments.quote: please don't invert the findings of Williams et al. 2017 who found that physical crown complementarity (=competitive hierarchy) was more strongly correlated with selection than with complementarity effects.

comments.issue: The phrasing at line 427 should refer to root space closure.
comments.request: Change the wording at line 427 to root space closure.
comments.quote: 427: perhaps more to "root space closure" (see above).

comments.issue: 'Intraspecific' at line 432 seems incorrect.
comments.request: Check the term 'intraspecific' at line 432.
comments.quote: - 432: “intraspecific”??

comments.issue: The claim at lines 442-443 about vertical stratification contradicts Williams et al. 2017.
comments.request: Reframe vertical stratification as a sign of competitive hierarchy.
comments.quote: once more, Williams et al. 2017 would suggest that vertical stratification increases selection effects and should thus be seen as a sign of (light) competitive hierarchy.

comments.issue: The passage at lines 450-468 is not surprising and weakens the main message.
comments.request: Shorten or reframe the passage at lines 450-468.
comments.quote: 450-468: not so surprising and weakening your main message.

comments.issue: Species interactions were not measured, making much of the Conclusion speculative.
comments.request: Remove the speculative conclusion about species interactions.
comments.quote: You did not measure species interactions! Much of the Conclusion is highly speculative and overall rather weakening your message.

comments.issue: Table 1 does not explain s and ti, random terms, or whether year is linear or a factor.
comments.request: Clarify Table 1 symbols and model terms.
comments.quote: Table 1: what does s and ti mean? Which random terms were included? Is year a linear term or a factor?

comments.issue: Figures 2-5 do not state the fitted models or y-axis units.
comments.request: Report the models used and add the m2/ha unit to the y-axis.
comments.quote: Figs 2-5: which models were used for the fits? Please add the unit to the y-axis (m2/ha)

title: No complementarity no gain—Net diversity effects on tree productivity occur once complementarity emerges during early stand development

study.system: sex-specific inbreeding depression; 47 species, experimental studies

editor_summary: Four expert reviewers find the manuscript interesting, high quality and methodologically rigorous but requiring substantial revision; editor highlights clearer hypotheses, the metafor omnibus test, publication bias, purging vs directional dominance, and sexual size dimorphism.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and general question, pleased to see the meta-analysis, with suggestions on purging explanations and many line-level clarifications.
strengths: meta-analysis is valuable for the field

comments.issue: Parts of the introduction could be clearer and shorter.
comments.request: Improve clarity and shorten the introduction.
comments.quote: Parts of the introduction could be made clearer and made shorter in places.

comments.issue: Purging-based explanations are overused even though purging generally plays a small role in inbreeding depression.
comments.request: Temper purging explanations throughout the paper.
comments.quote: There is also a tendency to reach for purging based explanations throughout the paper although purging in general plays a fairly small role in inbreeding depression.

comments.issue: Stronger selection can increase inbreeding depression through directional dominance, an alternative not explained.
comments.request: Add lines explaining the directional dominance mechanism.
comments.quote: I think you should add some lines explaining how stronger selection can actually increase inbreeding depression because of directional dominance.

comments.issue: The logic that female mutational load is purged at the expense of males during male-male competition is unclear.
comments.request: Explain this purging argument more clearly.
comments.quote: I’m not following why female mutational load would be purged at the expense of males during male-male competition.

comments.issue: The sentence on line 142 is fragmented and difficult to read.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: This sentence is broken into many smaller parts and is difficult to read.

comments.issue: The phrasing on line 163 is unclear about whether positive effects concern females or sexual selection.
comments.request: Clarify the phrasing.
comments.quote: Are the positive effects greater in females or the sexual selection? The current phrasing is a little unclear.

comments.issue: The sentence on line 328 does not make sense and may be a typo.
comments.request: Fix the sentence.
comments.quote: This sentence doesn’t make sense, it may be a typo

comments.issue: Whether the sex × inbreeding coefficient interaction supports the female-bias conclusion is not discussed, and sex alone is only borderline significant.
comments.request: Add a sentence explaining whether the interaction supports the conclusion.
comments.quote: Is it fair to say that this interaction between sex and inbreeding coefficient also supports your conclusion that females suffer greater inbreeding?

comments.issue: The wording on line 469 about traits not being prevented from reduction is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the intended meaning.
comments.quote: do you mean that you observed inbreeding depression despite potential purging at high inbreeding coefficients?

comments.issue: The paragraph on line 467 should lead with the sex interaction and discuss purging in males but not females.
comments.request: Reorder the paragraph and end with the purging evidence.
comments.quote: Move this last sentence about the sex interaction earlier in the paragraph

comments.issue: An alternative argument predicts stronger inbreeding depression in males via directional dominance.
comments.request: Consider this directional dominance argument, which is easier for selection to act on.
comments.quote: Alternatively, you could argue that stronger sexual selection in males would lead to stronger inbreeding depression in males because strong selection leads to greater directional dominance.

comments.issue: No proxy for sexual selection was included, although it may be the main driver of sex differences.
comments.request: Consider a species-level proxy for sexual selection.
comments.quote: It’s a shame that you didn’t include a proxy for sexual selection as I would expect this is be the main selection pressure driving differences between the sexes.

comments.issue: The two sentences on lines 578-582 are hard to follow and the purging argument is not consistent with the results.
comments.request: Rewrite these sentences.
comments.quote: These two sentences are difficult to follow. I think the first sentence is arguing that high female inbreeding depression is good for population growth because purging will reduce female inbreeding depression.

comments.issue: In the PRISMA figure, the reasons for exclusion are placed under the Included section.
comments.request: Move the exclusion reasons next to the excluded-study counts.
comments.quote: the “reasons for exclusion” list should be displayed on the side next to where the number of excluded studies are reported

comments.issue: Figure column titles are unclear abbreviations.
comments.request: Rename columns to “female effect sizes” and “Female studies”.
comments.quote: consider changing the column titles from “Female” and “No\_Studies\_female” etc to “female effect sizes” and “Female studies”

reviews.assessment: Congratulates the authors on a thorough meta-analysis but requires significant improvements to hypothesis framing, data analysis and conclusions.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks conceptual synthesis of the factors that may drive sex differences, so it is unclear why one sex would generally be more sensitive.
comments.request: Provide a greater conceptual synthesis of potential drivers in the introduction.
comments.quote: The quality and impact of this paper would be greatly improved providing a greater conceptual synthesis of the potential factors that may drive sex-differences in the Introduction

comments.issue: The analysis is exploratory without a priori hypotheses or pre-registration, yet broad confirmatory conclusions are drawn.
comments.request: State exactly what is tested and why, label the analysis exploratory, and avoid confirmatory conclusions.
comments.quote: A limitation is that, due to the lack of a priori hypotheses (and lack of pre-registration), the analysis here is exploratory, and the authors make no specific predictions about what they expect to find.

comments.issue: The metafor Qm omnibus test has limited descriptive value and is used as the primary basis for conclusions.
comments.request: Use post hoc linear hypothesis tests for specific comparisons such as male versus female effects.
comments.quote: I also have some concerns about the data analysis, and particularly the use of the Qm (omnibus test for moderators) from metafor as the primary basis for many of the conclusions

comments.issue: The abstract states as fact that one sex tends to be more vulnerable, which is the very thing being tested.
comments.request: Rephrase the overly general statement.
comments.quote: This statement is overly general. This study is testing whether ‘one sex tends to be more vulnerable than the other’, so it sounds odd to state that as fact right from the start.

comments.issue: It is unclear why effects are usually expected on line 61.
comments.request: State what the expectation is based on.
comments.quote: Usually expected why? Expected based on inbreeding depression alone?

comments.issue: “Quality” is undefined on line 62.
comments.request: Clarify what quality means here.
comments.quote: Unclear what ‘quality’ means here.

comments.issue: The statement on lines 69-72 is unclear and unsupported by citation.
comments.request: Clarify the statement and add citations.
comments.quote: This statement is unclear and not supported by citation.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether males having fewer deleterious recessive alleles is supported by literature.
comments.request: Cite support for this general sex difference.
comments.quote: Is there literature support for this being a general pattern between sexes.

comments.issue: The syntax on lines 78-82 needs fixing.
comments.request: Reword the sentence as suggested.
comments.quote: Yet sexual selection does not act solely on male-specific alleles, as sexually selected traits likely share a common genetic basis with traits that determine the overall health and vigour of individuals of both sexes

comments.issue: The conclusion on lines 82-83 does not follow because sexual selection is a form of natural selection that purges alleles in both sexes.
comments.request: Revise this inference.
comments.quote: I don’t think this necessarily follows, as the last sentence suggests that sexual selection should be able to purge deleterious alleles in both sexes, but not any more than natural selection generally.

comments.issue: “Purged” and “purified” on lines 84-85 imply all deleterious alleles are removed.
comments.request: Reword to avoid this implication.
comments.quote: ‘purged’ and ‘purified’ suggest that ALL deleterious alleles in the genome have been removed, which I imagine wouldn’t be the case.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the female benefit on lines 87-88 means fewer deleterious alleles or higher heterozygosity.
comments.request: Clarify the mechanism by which females benefit.
comments.quote: I am again not sure how this follows. Females may benefit more from sexual selection because they get deleterious alleles purged without being the direct subject of selection.

comments.issue: Sexually antagonistic genes are not defined on line 92.
comments.request: Define or briefly describe sexually antagonistic genes.
comments.quote: Consider defining/briefly describing what a sexually antagonistic gene is.

comments.issue: The R2 of 0.6% is very low.

reviews.assessment: Valuable contribution with thorough analyses, but the introduction needs reworking and the results section is too brief.

comments.issue: The introduction reads like a discussion, covering untested ideas and omitting tested ones such as trait effects and inbreeding coefficient.
comments.request: Refocus the introduction on the traits and variables actually investigated.
comments.quote: The introduction reads more like a discussion, covering a number of ideas that are not directly tested in the paper and missing out others that are included.

comments.issue: The argument that sexual selection causes sex differences in inbreeding depression via purging is confusing and unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify how sexual selection causes species-level sex differences without invoking sex chromosomes.
comments.quote: Can the authors clarify how sexual selection causes sex differences in inbreeding depression at the species level without invoking sex chromosomes?

comments.issue: The rationale of lines 128-130 for how heterogamety leads to sex differences is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism.
comments.quote: How can it lead to differences in inbreeding depression between the sexes?

comments.issue: The purpose of the paragraph on lines 142-150 is unclear and the introduction is long.
comments.request: Shorten or remove this paragraph.
comments.quote: I was unsure what the purpose of this paragraph was. The introduction was already quite long and so this might be a place where it can be shortened.

comments.issue: It is unclear why sexual selection benefits females more and why stress exaggerates the difference.
comments.request: Clarify these assumptions.
comments.quote: Is it not clear to me why sexual selection has greater fitness benefits for females (or in general has positive effects on fitness) and why stressful conditions generally exaggerate such differences, surely it can go both ways?

comments.issue: The results section is extremely brief and buries moderator results in the supplement.
comments.request: Move key moderator figures and effects into the main manuscript and report non-significant effects too.
comments.quote: The results section is extremely brief, especially the part on moderators, with a lot of interesting information buried in the supplementary html file.

comments.issue: The first results paragraph reads like methods.
comments.request: Open the results with lines 369-375 instead.
comments.quote: The first paragraph of the results seems more like methods

comments.issue: Data limitation paragraphs are scattered through the discussion.
comments.request: Combine them into one section to shorten the discussion.
comments.quote: It might be good to combine these into one section

comments.issue: Only pedigree-based inbreeding studies were included, excluding genetic marker studies.

comments.quote: Why are only include studies where inbreeding was measured using pedigrees included? Why not studies using genetic markers as well?

comments.issue: Some paragraphs, such as lines 209-244, are extremely long.
comments.request: Break long paragraphs into shorter ones.
comments.quote: Some paragraphs are extremely long (e.g. lines 209-244). It would help readability to break these up.

comments.issue: Only three to four sex chromosome systems are represented, raising power concerns for heterogamety tests.

comments.quote: How many independent sex chromosome systems did the data encompass? From figure 2 it looks like 3 to 4. Is there enough power here to test the effects of heterogamety?

comments.issue: The phrasing on line 459 implies reduced inbreeding depression when only non-zero difference can be shown.

comments.issue: Table 1 does not report the number of species.
comments.request: Add species numbers alongside effect sizes.
comments.quote: It would be useful to include number of species here as well as number of effect sizes.

comments.issue: The osf material was not accessible, so the screening and exclusion process could not be checked.
comments.request: Ensure the osf materials are openly accessible.
comments.quote: it was not possible to examine which studies were retrieved by literature studies and why they were excluded or included as I couldn’t access the osf material

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and timely meta-analysis, generally well written with a nuanced discussion; mostly minor comments plus sexual size dimorphism.

comments.issue: The statement on lines 82-83 is far from settled and likely taxa-specific.

comments.quote: There is some evidence to back up this statement but this is far from being a settled matter and is likely hugely taxa-specific

comments.issue: It is questionable whether purging benefits females more than males on lines 83-86.
comments.request: Clarify the asymmetry claim.
comments.quote: I’m not sure you can say this benefits females more than it does males.

comments.issue: The claim on lines 86-88 that a male-specific selective sieve reduces inbreeding more in females is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the logic.
comments.quote: Why? This seems to say that a male-specific selective sieve (due to stronger sexual selection) will reduce inbreeding more in females than in males?

comments.issue: On line 121, neutral or slightly deleterious mutations can be maintained in males.

comments.quote: Note that this is not necessarily the case. Neutral or even slightly deleterious mutations can be maintained in males

comments.issue: X-linked deleterious mutations cannot be purged in only one sex; the key is differential homozygosity.
comments.request: Revise the argument on lines 123-125.

comments.issue: A new paragraph may be needed at line 125.

comments.issue: The statement on lines 137-139 is contradicted by Sultanova et al. 2018.

comments.issue: The meaning of lines 163-165 is unclear.

comments.issue: Males under stronger sexual selection may be more condition-dependent and thus more stress-sensitive.

comments.issue: The 18% disagreement rate between screeners is very high.

comments.issue: The “n=6” bracket on lines 239-240 is misplaced.

comments.issue: Competition on line 278 may not qualify as a stressful environment.

comments.issue: The paragraph on lines 369-371 would make a better opening.

comments.quote: I would open the paragraph with this.

comments.issue: The structure of lines 445-455 breaks the flow between paragraphs.

comments.issue: The meaning of lines 457-460 is unclear.

comments.issue: Sex-specific ageing and the unguarded-X hypothesis are not discussed.

comments.quote: I think the authors should also discuss the implications regarding sex-specific ageing/lifespan and the unguarded-X hypothesis, if only briefly.

comments.issue: Sexual size dimorphism was not controlled for despite readers expecting it.

comments.quote: many readers will wonder why you didn’t aim to control for sexual size-dimorphism. Have you considered running this analysis?

comments.issue: Inbreeding effects on mating success may capture male condition-dependence more than survival or fecundity.
