comments.issue: 'Plurality of species' is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify what plurality means.
comments.quote: I don't understand what is meant by 'the plurality of species'. It sees to imply: “if more than one species”, but that doesn't work somehow. Please clarify.

comments.issue: The most frequent habitat need not be the ancestral state, biasing transition timing and polarity.
comments.request: Explain the potential consequences of this assumption.
comments.quote: The most frequent state is not necessarily there state at the base of the clade. This decision could therefore result in over-estimation of the timing of habitat transitions, and mis-estimation of their polarities.

comments.issue: Internal parasites may create pseudoreplicated habitat transitions following their hosts.
comments.request: Run analyses excluding internal parasites.
comments.quote: Please consider doing analyses that exclude internal parasites and they could cause pseudoreplicated habitat transitions but following their hosts.

comments.issue: Dividing phylogenetic diversity by habitat area lacks a process-based justification.
comments.request: Explain why larger environments should have higher phylogenetic diversity.
comments.quote: I'm uncomfortably with this step because there does not seem to be a process-based reason to expect higher phylogenetic diversity in larger environments (see above). This ought to be explained.

comments.issue: Coding whole groups by their most species-rich habitat introduces a bias when diversification rates differ among habitats.
comments.request: Address this coding bias.
comments.quote: This is especially problematic if there are indeed differences in diversification rates among habitats because this would cause more species, on average, to exist for some habitats than others, introducing a coding bias

comments.issue: Assigning a single colonization date per habitat is a dangerous simplification given many independent transitions.
comments.request: Use clade-level dates instead of one date per habitat.
comments.quote: I think you are saying that you simply assigned one date to each of the habitats (or, one date per analytical focus (e.g. for plants, for animals, etc) - i.e., three dates in total per focus:

comments.issue: The palaeontological review is relegated to the supplement without a main-text overview.
comments.request: Give an overview of key palaeontological messages in the main text.
comments.quote: It is likely that palaeontology had a lot to say on this topic. It may be appropriate to give some overview of the key take-home messages in the main text.

comments.issue: Calling the MS estimator 'standard' implies a consensus that does not exist.
comments.request: Remove the word 'standard'.
comments.quote: I'm not clear on what the word 'standard' means here. It seems to imply that there is a consensus that this approach will work, and that this is uncontentious, with almost everybody in agreement.

comments.issue: Averaging diversification rates hides whether patterns are widespread or driven by particular higher taxa.
comments.request: Present the distribution of rates with key taxa labelled.
comments.quote: Why was the mean calculated right away. Ideally you would present the distribution of diversification rates, labelling/colouring points that correspond to particular higher taxa (e.g. insects, gastropods, etc).

comments.issue: A correlation between per-habitat richness and per-habitat rate can arise from total richness-total rate correlation, so the analysis does not test the hypothesis.
comments.request: Dissect the parameters and use an analysis that tests the per-habitat question.
comments.quote: But the authors want to ask specifically whether differences in species richness among habitats (i.e. per-habitat, not summed) result from differences in diversification across habitats. So I think they are not doing the right analysis

comments.issue: It is not explained what 'fail' means for SSE methods with rare states.
comments.request: Explain what failure means and under what conditions it occurs.
comments.quote: Please provide more information on what is meant by 'fail', and what conditions lead to this?

comments.issue: Scoring tips by their most frequent state assumes it is plesiomorphic, underestimating transitions and over-estimating their ages.
comments.request: Justify or work out the consequences of this assumption.
comments.quote: I am also concerned about the use of tip values that are just the most frequent state within each clade - which assumes that the most frequent state is also the plesiomorphic state for the clade.

comments.issue: The extant-richness question is obscured by post-terrestrialisation diversification and the relevant literature is not used.
comments.request: Acknowledge the literature and address the simpler ancestry questions.
comments.quote: However, it does not speak closely to the generalities of the process of terrestrialisation because that process is obscured by the process of diversification (i.e. increases in species richness) -after- terrestrialisation.

comments.issue: The phylum-level analysis hides that arthropods include several independent terrestrial transitions, mostly insects.
comments.request: Increase the taxonomic granularity of the analysis.
comments.quote: I think it is important to note that arthropods include several different groups that independently became terrestrial. The most species on land by far are insects. I think that level of granularity is quite important give the questions and scope of the study.

comments.issue: The proportion of semi-aquatic species (e.g. aquatic insect larvae) is not reported.
comments.request: Report the semi-aquatic fraction for context.
comments.quote: It would be useful to know, here and in other places, what proportion of these are 'semi-aquatic', including aquatic larvae of some insect species.

comments.issue: Colonization time is treated differently from diversification rate; a clade-level analysis of origin time versus rate is needed.
comments.request: Quantify the importance of origin time versus diversification at clade level.
comments.quote: Ideally we would see one analysis, at clade-level, that quantified the importance of origin time versus diversification rate in explaining variation in species richness, potentially quantifying such relative variation using R2.

comments.issue: The palaeontological review is a meta-review that should be cited in the main text and used to access wider literature.
comments.request: Cite the review papers in the main text.
comments.quote: This 'review' is a review of review papers, or a 'meta-review'. Because it can be dealt with concisely, it would be more straightforward just to cite those review papers in the main text rather than relegating the discussion of them to the supplement.

comments.issue: Transition numbers are described rather than analyzed; probabilities and AIC support are missing.
comments.request: Estimate transition probabilities with model support.
comments.quote: This is description rather than analysis or generalisation. I would like to know the transition probabilities, and the support from e.g. AIC for differences in transition frequencies.

comments.issue: Statements confirming older findings lack citations.
comments.request: Add relevant citations.
comments.quote: This and other statements that confirm he findings of older works should be accompanied by the relevant citations.

comments.issue: The discussion relies on Wiens papers and misses older, diverse literature (e.g. marine vertebrate adaptation reviews).
comments.request: Integrate work from a wider range of authors and disciplines.
comments.quote: The work here could be much more closely integrated to work from a diverse range of different authors and sub disciplines.

comments.issue: The sentence about readers dismissing conclusions is ad hominem.
comments.request: Rephrase to speak about evidence and observations.
comments.quote: This is a ad hominem statement. Please rephrase this so it speaks to the nature of evidence and observation instead of 'what people think'.

comments.issue: Scholarship of previous fossil-based work is incomplete.
comments.request: Improve engagement with previous fossil-based scholarship.
comments.quote: However, the scholarship of previous works, which have often used fossil evidence, is quite incomplete, and I regard that as a shortcoming.

comments.issue: The claim that sampled-tree reconstructions reflect a complete species-level tree is not necessarily true.
comments.request: Work out the consequences of the most-frequent-habitat assumption.
comments.quote: This is not necessarily true given that the primitive habitat for each group is assumed to be the most frequent habitat among its constituent species. I'd like to see more working-out of this issue.

comments.issue: Fossil evidence is dismissed as not central even though it is relevant to the question.
comments.request: Engage better with fossil-record studies of terrestrialisation.
comments.quote: Fossil evidence is clearly relevant to this question (see comments above), even if the goal is not to understand each timepoints in the past. In general, better scholarship of fossil record studies of terrestrialisation would be helpful.

comments.issue: The long history of palaeontological investigation and its mixed support for the hypotheses are underplayed.
comments.request: Discuss fossil evidence such as freshwater ancestry of ammonites.
comments.quote: But it doesn't touch on the fossil evidence that e.g. ammonites evolved from freshwater ancestors, and similar. The work in general has substantially underplayed the long history of paleontological investigation and the extent to which it does/does not support these hypotheses.

comments.issue: The summary confirms established patterns and a circular correlation; findings are not novel and scholarship is poor, leading to over-claiming.
comments.request: Temper the novelty claims and improve scholarship.
comments.quote: The findings cannot be said to be novel at the level that I think is required. Crucially, the scholarship is poor in general and this results in over-claiming with regard to novelty.

comments.issue: The 'to our knowledge' claim about habitat areas ignores Earth sciences literature.
comments.request: Refer to literature on land area and marine flooding over geological time.
comments.quote: Earth Sciences/geology does provide some insights into questions of this type, replacing the need to write “to our knowledge” here. It would be useful to refer to some of the literature about how land area and marine flooding might have varied through geological time.

comments.issue: Figure 2 selection of phyla is confusing; variation among all phyla would be more informative.
comments.request: Show the variation in richness among all phyla per environment.
comments.quote: I find this figure confusing. How was it selected to display which phyla on each level? It may be more useful to graphically show the variation in richness among all phyla in each environment instead.

comments.issue: Figure 3 is abstract and hard to follow.
comments.request: Add labels such as 'older/younger' and 'faster/slower'.
comments.quote: I find this quite confusing too because ti is relatively abstract in nature. Consider adding some arrows reading 'older/younger' , 'faster/slower' etc.

comments.issue: Figure 4 is descriptive rather than showing estimated transition frequencies.
comments.request: Present estimated transition frequencies instead.
comments.quote: This is descriptive of data. But ideally instead the transition frequencies would be estimated and presented.

title: The origins of global biodiversity on land, sea and freshwater

study.system: invasive Ambrosia artemisiifolia and beetle Ophraella communa; multi-generation field experiment

editor_summary: All four referees find the study interesting and novel, but methods description must improve; discuss the broader plant-herbivory context cautiously because the artificial manipulation precluded insect evolution, and explain the difference from Sun et al. 2020.

reviews.assessment: Well-designed, data-rich study with sound conclusions; asks to temper the biocontrol claim and clarify several details.
strengths: large amount and wide range of data

comments.issue: Rapid adaptation may not extend to non-weedy species; the invasive-species lens could be interpreted otherwise.
comments.request: Reproduce the experiment with a non-weedy or endangered species.
comments.quote: It would be interested to reproduce the same experiment with another species that may not be so weedy, a rare or endangered species.

comments.issue: The biocontrol conclusion is overstated because beetles were prevented from evolving, making the arms race artificially uneven.
comments.request: Tone down the biocontrol conclusion and acknowledge beetle evolution.
comments.quote: I think that the conclusion that climate change can decrease biocontrol efficiency can be tone down a little bit.

comments.issue: No co-author from Italian institutions despite extensive fieldwork in Italy.
comments.quote: I was surprised not to see any co-author from local Italian institutions.

comments.issue: Unclear whether Ophraella feeds on Ambrosia artemisiifolia in its native range.
comments.request: Clarify the beetle's feeding relationship in its native range.
comments.quote: It is not clear if Ophraella feeds on Ambrosia artemisiifolia in its native range. Could the authors clarify this?

comments.issue: Origin of the beetles used in experiments across years is not described.
comments.request: Provide information on beetle origins.
comments.quote: nothing is said about the origin of the beetles in the different experiments across the different years they have been running

comments.issue: Unclear whether the number of F1 individuals growing in the second year was controlled.
comments.request: State whether F1 numbers in the second year were controlled.
comments.quote: Did they authors control the number of F1 individual growing in the second year?

comments.issue: Generation labels are questionable: plants called "Ambrosia offspring" appear to be F2.
comments.request: Correct the generation labels.
comments.quote: P12 l 272 "Ambrosia offspring" These are F2, right?

comments.issue: The choice of a fourth-root transformation is unusual and unexplained.
comments.request: Explain why the fourth-root transformation was chosen.
comments.quote: This is really fourth-root, not square-root? I have never seem this transformation before, so perhaps the authors could provide a bit more explanation on this choice.

reviews.assessment: Elegantly designed and well-executed study with informative figures, but the writing is awkward and design details are hard to follow.
strengths: fills a gap in understanding climate change and biocontrol
highly informative and beautifully drawn figures
diversity of measurements and depth of analyses

comments.issue: The abstract wording "their associated ecosystem services" wrongly implies all plant-herbivore interactions provide services.
comments.request: Rephrase this wording in the abstract.
comments.quote: Line 43 the wording 'their associated ecosystem services' sounds as if all plant-herbivore interactions provide services

comments.issue: Awkward wording and sentence structure occur throughout, with many lines listed by the reviewer.
comments.request: Revise the writing for clarity and readability.
comments.quote: Similar sentences with awkward wording and structure are abound in the text.

comments.issue: Fig. 1 legend has grammatical errors and needs more detail, including for panels C and D.
comments.request: Correct and expand the Fig. 1 legend.
comments.quote: Fig 1 legend: "causes" instead of 'causing' 'Feed on' instead of 'are feeding on'

comments.issue: Unclear whether potted plants or seedlings planted directly in soil were used.
comments.request: Clarify the planting method.
comments.quote: Were there potted plants used or seedlings planted directly in the soil?

comments.issue: Origin of seeds used in the common garden is unclear, and methods cannot be understood without the Appendix.
comments.request: Spell out the seed origin in the main methods.
comments.quote: I know that the Appendix is referenced but the methods should be understandable without going back and forth between the supplement and the main text.

comments.issue: Sampling and pooling of parents and F1 for molecular analyses are confusing; RDA is not defined.
comments.request: Describe the molecular sampling and pooling clearly and define RDA.
comments.quote: These may be very basic questions but for someone not familiar with the ins and outs of molecular analyses the current description of methods is confusing. What does RDA stand for?

comments.issue: "Between groups" on Line 244 is vague and its meaning is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what "between groups" refers to.
comments.quote: Line 244: What does 'between groups' mean? Between treatments?

comments.issue: Fig. 2 legend wording ("offspring Ambrosia plant") is odd.
comments.request: Reword the Fig. 2 legend.
comments.quote: Fig 2 legend. 'offspring Ambrosia plant' odd wording

comments.issue: The four treatments are hard to follow; describing the beetle treatment as herbivory would be clearer.
comments.request: Describe treatments more clearly throughout.
comments.quote: I think it would be clearer if instead of 'beetle' treatment it was described as plants that experienced herbivory.

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: add "plant" before "genetic" (L358) and use "fewer" instead of "less" (L439).
comments.quote: Line 358: add 'plant' before 'genetic'

comments.issue: "All data" on Line 372 is not explained for readers who skip the methods.
comments.request: Spell out what "all data" refers to.
comments.quote: I would spell out what 'all data' means on Line 372 because for people who skip reading the methods/results (as many readers do) it will not be clear.

reviews.assessment: Very well executed and well written; the only concern is how well results from artificial conditions translate to nature.

comments.issue: Two generations may be too short to capture realistic evolutionary changes; longer experiments might change results.
comments.request: Discuss how experiment duration limits translation to nature.
comments.quote: The experimental study was conducted for only two generations which appears short to capture realistic evolutionary changes.

comments.issue: Genetic variation among experimental plants was inflated beyond realistic natural levels and may affect outcomes.
comments.request: Discuss how inflated genetic variation affects the results.
comments.quote: The genetic variation among the experimental plants was increased beyond what appears realistic for natural populations (2 individuals from 60 maternal families sampled from 19 populations).

comments.issue: Maintaining about 50% leaf damage by adding or removing beetles may moderate the results.
comments.request: Discuss how the imposed herbivory level may affect results.
comments.quote: Approximately 50% leaf damage was maintained during the study by adding or removing beetles. How could the herbivory levels moderate the results?

comments.issue: Monoculture in field cages without competition may limit realism; results could differ in complex communities.
comments.request: Discuss how the simplified plant community affects the results.
comments.quote: The experiment was conducted in field cages where the invasive plant was grown in mococulture, apparently free from competition with other weeds. Might the results change in more complex plant communities?

comments.issue: The final conclusion about other plant types is not supported, as unexpected results lack mechanistic explanations.
comments.request: Remove or temper the final conclusion about other plant types.
comments.quote: I'm not sure how you can draw this final conclusion. Some of the results were unexpected and no clear explanations for them were presented.

reviews.assessment: Novel and important study, but the methods description lacks clarity and the statistical analyses suffer from pseudoreplication.

comments.issue: Design and set-up of field and common garden experiments are described less clearly than the metabolomics approach.
comments.request: Improve the methods description and link main text to the Appendix.
comments.quote: the manuscript would benefit from more clarity and a better link between information presented in the materials & methods section of the main text and details shown in the Appendix

comments.issue: How experimental populations were established (seedlings vs direct sowing) and their spatial arrangement is not described.
comments.request: Describe population establishment and spatial arrangement.
comments.quote: I could, however, not find any information how the populations were established, neither in the main text nor in the Appendix. Were seedlings planted on the field plots or were the seeds directly sown on the plots?

comments.issue: Whether failed seedlings were replaced is unclear and would affect the initial genetic composition of populations.
comments.request: State whether seedlings were replaced before treatments started.
comments.quote: Did you replace seedlings that could not establish prior to the start of the warming and beetle treatments? This would clearly affect initial genetic composition of experimental populations.

comments.issue: Number of F1 plants sampled per plot, their selection, and whether seeds were pooled or families kept separate are unclear.
comments.request: Report and justify the F1 sampling scheme in the main methods.
comments.quote: it remains unclear (1) how many F1 plants were sampled on each field plot, (2) how these F1 plants were selected to represent a random sample of each experimental population

comments.issue: If seeds were pooled, whether they were mixed according to F1 fecundity is not stated or justified.
comments.request: Justify the pooling or fecundity-weighting approach.
comments.quote: if seeds were pooled, were they mixed according to the fecundity of each F1 individual in order to ensure that the proportional contribution of each genotype to follow-up experiments reflected its relative fitness on field plots?

comments.issue: The Appendix seed morphology and germination trial is not mentioned in the main methods.
comments.request: Add this information to the main text.
comments.quote: The Appendix describes a "seed morphology and germination" trial which is not referred to in the materials & methods section of the main text. Please add this information.

comments.issue: Field analyses treat 40 cage-by-generation combinations as replicates; the correct units are the 20 caged populations.
comments.request: Re-analyse with the 20 caged populations as experimental units.
comments.quote: the correct replicates for the effects of beetles and warming, are the n=20 caged populations (with a total of 19 d.f.) and not the 40 cage x generation combinations

comments.issue: Temporal autocorrelation among generations is not accounted for, despite the repeated-measures structure.
comments.request: Account for temporal autocorrelation among generations.
comments.quote: I didn't find information how the models account for the temporal autocorrelation among generations which is a typical feature of repeated measurements

comments.issue: Assays (50 cages, 474 assays, 432 pots) far exceed the 20 experimental units, indicating unaccounted pseudoreplication.
comments.request: Account for pseudoreplication in the assay analyses.
comments.quote: Again, the number of assays is much larger than the number of experimental populations in the field experiment (n=20 experimental units, see above) indicating pseudoreplication.

comments.issue: Adding plot as a random term is insufficient because error degrees of freedom still exceed the number of experimental units.
comments.request: Use an analysis that respects the experimental unit.
comments.quote: I would like to emphasize that just adding plot as a random term (lines 199-200) is insufficient as there would still be more error d.f. than experimental units!

comments.issue: Chi-square and likelihood ratio tests hide pseudoreplication because they do not show the level of independent replication.
comments.request: Report the replication level behind these tests.
comments.quote: the problem of pseudoreplication becomes less obvious, but is still present, in cases where Chi-square (or likelihood ratio) tests are shown (Table S1) as they provide no information on the level at which treatments were independently replicated

comments.issue: Degrees of freedom are not reported for all tests.
comments.request: Give degrees of freedom for all tests presented.
comments.quote: Please give degrees of freedom for all tests presented.

comments.issue: Generation labels F0, F1, F2 are questionable and not consistently defined.
comments.request: Define and apply generation labels consistently.
comments.quote: These labels should be defined right at the beginning and consistently applied throughout the manuscript to avoid confusion.

comments.issue: The term "population" confusingly refers both to source field populations and caged experimental populations.
comments.request: Distinguish the two kinds of populations consistently.
comments.quote: The term "population" is used in a slightly confusing way because it refers to different items

comments.issue: "Two-level factorial" may be misread as hierarchical rather than crossed factors.
comments.request: Clarify the factorial design terminology.
comments.quote: What does "two-level factorial" mean? It could be misunderstood as an experiment comprising two hierarchically arranged rather than crossed factors

comments.issue: Unclear whether the seeds "collected in the field" came from the field experiment or local populations.
comments.request: Clarify the origin of these seeds.
comments.quote: I guess these seeds were collected in the field experiment rather than in local field populations. Please clarify.

title: Climate warming can reduce biocontrol efficacy and promote plant invasion due to both genetic and transient metabolomic changes

study.system: birds (1,350 species); eggshell stiffness and nest traits

editor_summary: All reviewers find the scope novel and interesting, but framing and analyses need work: evidence for nest instability, added variables (latitude, body size), eggshell trait contributions, phylogenetic comparisons and predation.

reviews.assessment: Fine study with an impressive dataset, but lacks evidence for nest instability and needs stronger phylogenetic analyses and nest-egg framing.
strengths: functional links to nest morphology and placement
valuable to researchers despite the weaknesses

comments.issue: No evidence is provided that nests differ in instability, the proposed selective pressure.
comments.request: Quantify instability among nests.
comments.quote: There is no evidence, that I can find, that would suggest some nests are more instable than others. To do this, you would need to quantify the instability among nests.

comments.issue: The claim that using the C of the collision vector makes no difference is not shown, and C is strongly skewed.
comments.request: Show these results and use the collision-vector C metric.
comments.quote: You state that using the C associated with the vector with which they collide makes no difference, but you didn't show these figures.

comments.issue: Nest biomechanics and stabilization are considered only from the egg side; nests should also adapt.
comments.request: Give nests and the nest-egg complex equal consideration.
comments.quote: I would encourage a deeper consideration of the biomechanics of this situation – which is heavily egg-biased currently (give the nests and nest-egg complex equal consideration as you placed on the eggs).

comments.issue: The Fig. 3 analysis of node depth versus log C appears to lack any phylogenetic control.
comments.request: Clarify the analysis and use a phylogenetic framework such as BAMM.
comments.quote: its unclear to me how you analyzed your data in Figure 3 (node depth vs log C). It looks like you calculated this directly, and I can see no phylogenetic control

comments.issue: Nest site and nest structure are not included in all models; passerine status is only a proxy for instability.
comments.request: Include nest site and nest structure in all models.
comments.quote: Instead, I think you need to include nest site and nest structure in similar analyses so that your initial analyses feed into your subsequent analyses.

comments.issue: No evidence is given that collision-caused egg loss is common enough to act as the selective pressure.
comments.request: Provide evidence that egg loss from collisions is a major pressure.
comments.quote: I did not see statements regarding how common egg loss due to collisions are. This is important if it's the purported selective pressure acting on eggs.

comments.issue: The enclosed nest category also includes cavity nests, which is not reflected.
comments.request: Clarify whether enclosed includes cavity nests.
comments.quote: Line 51: Enclosed also would include cavity nests.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the text means higher or increasing (rate of change).
comments.request: Clarify whether higher or increasing is meant.
comments.quote: Line 52: Do you mean higher or increasing (rate of change)?

comments.issue: The level of the claim (interspecific versus within species) is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the level at which the claim applies.
comments.quote: Do you still mean at the interspecific level? Seems like you mean within species.

comments.issue: 'Prime (stable) nest habitat' is not defined and the scale of the work is unclear.
comments.request: Define prime or stable nest habitat for this study.
comments.quote: How is prime (i.e., stable) nest habitat within/across species defined in this research?

comments.issue: Suggested rewording of the sentence introducing hypotheses on nest-egg connections.
comments.request: Reword the sentence as suggested.
comments.quote: Therefore many hypotheses on the functional connections between nests and eggs have been proposed, especially between egg shape and nest site or structure

comments.issue: The link between enclosure levels and accidental damage is unclear as written.
comments.request: Explain why enclosure levels would result in accidental damage.
comments.quote: Line 88: why would “enclosure levels” result in accidental damage? This is unclear as written.

comments.issue: A claim is made without a supporting citation.
comments.request: Cite the claim.
comments.quote: Line 92: Please cite this claim

comments.issue: The choice of three focal nest types is not justified as the riskiest.

comments.issue: The alternative that the nest-egg complex adapted so breakage is rare is important but unaddressed.

comments.quote: Or critically, that the nest-egg complex has adapted such that breakage is rare.

comments.issue: Two conflicting explanations for rare broken eggs are presented without clarification.

comments.issue: A connector is needed at this location.

comments.issue: The cuckoo ideas should not be separated; cuckoo eggs may resist damage from hosts and from laying.

comments.issue: A clearer summary of what the C metric is and estimates is needed.

comments.quote: It would be useful to provide a clearer (and more complete) simple summary about what this metric is and what it calculates/estimates.

comments.issue: The phrase 'the proposed collision hypothesis' should be replaced by the actual hypothesis.
comments.request: Replace the phrase with the actual hypothesis or mechanism.
comments.quote: I would replace “the proposed collision hypothesis” with the actual hypothesis/mechanism as in

comments.issue: The sentence about relationships evolving across broad taxonomic groups needs work.

comments.issue: Modeled eggshells are easily confused with real eggshells.

comments.issue: The pixel-based rules are harder to follow than a plain statement of the rules would be.

comments.issue: 'Across the avian phylogeny' and 'over the evolutionary history' appear to be used interchangeably.

comments.issue: The claim that eggs will jostle more lacks supporting evidence.

comments.issue: The section is hard to follow.

comments.issue: Nest types are presumed rather than shown to be unsteady.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether stiffness or the decline in stiffness evolved in non-passerines.

comments.issue: It is confusing whether values remain relative to egg size and thickness; a different analysis may be needed.

comments.issue: The statement that nests and eggs may reciprocally illuminate bird evolution is incomprehensible.

comments.issue: The statement about evolutionary time is incorrect; passerines more recently diverged is meant.
