comments.issue: Equations for each treatment are missing at line 223.
comments.request: Provide the equations.
comments.quote: 223. Please provide equations for each treatment.

comments.issue: The text at lines 235-237 should explain the liana effect on log(W)-Log(D) given the system is unsuitable for -3/2 predictions.
comments.request: Modify the text and discuss niche differentiation.
comments.quote: As pointed out previously, the forest system studied in this paper is not proper to test predictions of the -3/2 rule.

comments.issue: The mean slope and range of control plots are not given at line 238.
comments.request: Report them.
comments.quote: 238. Please put the mean slope and range of the control plots.

comments.issue: The stronger early-succession liana effect is not discussed (lines 269-271).
comments.request: Discuss this expectation.
comments.quote: The effect of lianas on tree-by-tree competition would be stronger during the first two decades of succession when light-demanding trees are vigorously growing

comments.issue: Ideas at lines 351-356 should be framed as future hypotheses/predictions.
comments.request: Frame them as predictions.
comments.quote: Propose these ideas as possible hypotheses/predictions to be tested by future works.

comments.issue: The relevance of these ideas as a coexistence mechanism is not discussed (lines 359-363).
comments.request: Comment on coexistence relevance.
comments.quote: Comment on the relevance of these ideas as a possible mechanism enabling tree species coexistence in highly diverse tropical forests.

title: Lianas decelerate tropical forest thinning during succession

study.system: leaf trait networks; 394 tree species, nine Chinese forests

editor_summary: Editor asks to address referee concerns, especially the dubious novelty of the study.

reviews.assessment: Sound framework and interesting findings; two concerns about LTN definitions and hub-trait analysis.

comments.issue: How a broad LTN is defined is unclear.
comments.request: Define what a broad leaf trait network means.
comments.quote: the authors concluded that temperate forest had broad LTNs, how to define a “broad” LTN?

comments.issue: Hub-trait conclusion based on stability may be confounded by differing trait numbers.
comments.request: Use another approach to identify hub traits.
comments.quote: I am more or less doubt this, as the number of traits is obviously different (Table S2). Any other approach to analyze this?

comments.issue: Redundant descriptions in lines 142-162 should be omitted.
comments.request: Remove repeated descriptions.
comments.quote: Some description should be omitted if they had been reported early.

comments.issue: Ecological meaning of path is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what path means ecologically.
comments.quote: What is the real mean of “path” here, ecologically?

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits (deletion, missing periods).
comments.quote: Line 39: delete “with greater species numbers”, anyone know this.

reviews.assessment: Well-written study, but novelty is limited and hypotheses are too general.
strengths: well written with clearly presented results
original method based on trait networks

comments.issue: Results largely confirm known patterns; unclear how trait network analysis advances the field.
comments.request: Demonstrate the advance beyond known patterns.
comments.quote: Overall, I was not clear for me based on this ms how traits network analysis will really significantly progress the field of trait community ecology.

comments.issue: Hypotheses are too general; need to show how trait networks enable new tests.
comments.request: Build more specific hypotheses tied to ecological questions.
comments.quote: I think it would be important to build hypothesis more specific and to more clearly show how the traits network approach allow new test of key ecological hypothesis.

comments.issue: Figure 1 pattern was already shown in He et al. 2020; new analyses do not change the message.
comments.request: Clarify the added value and discuss the species-richness driver.
comments.quote: The results of Figure 1 were already presented in He et al. 2020 in box 2.

comments.issue: Intraspecific trait variability and species abundance are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how to include them in trait network analysis.
comments.quote: it would be interesting to discuss how including intraspecific traits variability and species abundance could be included in trait network analysis

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits (missing spaces at lines 91 and 92).
comments.quote: Line 91 “2017)and” change to “2017) and”

comments.issue: Use of module is confusing versus statistically estimated module letters; use traits category consistently.
comments.request: Use consistent wording distinct from module.
comments.quote: I think that this is confusing to use the word “module” here are the module letter in the analysis are statistically estimated

comments.issue: Sentence on lines 193-194 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence.
comments.quote: This sentence is unclear. Change to “It quantifies for each trait in the network, the average that the traits to which it is connected are themselves inter-connected”?

comments.issue: Betweenness score was not fully defined before use.
comments.request: Add a forward reference to its equation.
comments.quote: “betweenness score” was not fully defined before. Maybe you can add that its equation will be given later?

comments.issue: Section describing module estimation is unclear; the supplementary version is better.
comments.request: Clarify the module estimation section.
comments.quote: This section describing the estimation of the module is unclear. The section in the suppl mat is better.

comments.issue: Mean-sd relationship may arise by construction for strictly positive metrics, so the index may not reflect stability.
comments.request: Address this artifact in the index construction.
comments.quote: If the trait network metrics are strictly positive it is possible that there is a positive relationship between the mean and the sd by construction.

comments.issue: What a decentralized trait network is remains unclear.
comments.request: Define decentralized trait networks.
comments.quote: Line 371: Unclear what is a decentralized trait network.

comments.issue: Prior studies on trait correlation variation across climate are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Cite and discuss these studies.
comments.quote: Numerous studies have explored traits correlation vary across climate.

reviews.assessment: Interesting method and data, but theory formulation, module calculation and results presentation need major work.
strengths: great leaf data across a cline

comments.issue: Theory development is haphazard; assumptions about fewer correlations under resource limitation are questionable.
comments.request: Reformulate the hypotheses with better justification.
comments.quote: Development of theory about how networks should behave is a bit haphazardly formulated.

comments.issue: Leaf density, not thickness, is the key LES factor; thickness as hub trait is questionable.
comments.request: Reconsider the hub-trait interpretation.
comments.quote: Is it really leaf thickness that is expected the central hub trait?

comments.issue: How trait modules are calculated is not understandable.
comments.request: Expand the explanation of module calculation.
comments.quote: notwithstanding the explanation, I do not understand how the trait modules are calculated

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not show what the networks are or whether traits correlate positively or negatively.
comments.request: Improve Figure 1 to show network structure and correlation signs.
comments.quote: I even cannot see properly from Fig 1 what the networks exactly are, and also not whether traits are positively and negatively correlated

comments.issue: Trait set has redundancies (Chl a/b ratio, NSC/SSC, LMA/LA/LDM).
comments.request: Justify or remove redundant traits.
comments.quote: Moreover, I find some redundancy among traits unnecessary.

comments.issue: Figure 4 variables should be grouped by trait group, not alphabetically.
comments.request: Group variables in Figure 4 by group.
comments.quote: would it not be better to group the variables in Fig. 4 not by alphabet, but by group?

comments.issue: Whether results change on a fresh-mass versus dry-mass basis is unknown.
comments.request: Consider or test a fresh-mass basis.
comments.quote: I wonder whether the trait-correlation network would be different if all variables were expressed on a fresh mass basis rather than a dry mass basis.

comments.issue: Results are scattered across figures and supplement; poor overview.
comments.request: Provide a clearer overview of results.
comments.quote: I do not get a good overview of the results. Fig. 2 shows some, fig 3 some others, the remainder I have to find in the supplement.

comments.issue: MAP and MAT correlation unknown; hypotheses too loose; a null hypothesis would be better.
comments.request: Report MAP/MAT correlation and frame a null hypothesis.
comments.quote: I also do not know to what extent MAP and MAT are correlated. And if the relationship is a different direction from hypothesized, they are even not given

comments.issue: Alternative explanations for network changes (species composition, environment) should be discussed.
comments.request: Discuss alternative drivers of network change.
comments.quote: But there are alternative explanations for changes in the network as well.

comments.issue: Why the patterns are controversial is unclear.
comments.request: Explain why they are controversial.
comments.quote: l31. Why are they controversial?

comments.issue: Reason given for using simple axes (commonness) is questionable; convenience is more likely.
comments.request: Correct the justification.
comments.quote: I do not think that people have used simple axes because the commonness, but rather that PCA's are convenient to use.

comments.issue: Meaning of unprecedented resolution is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: l66. “with unprecedented resolution”: what do you mean?

comments.issue: Claim of full-light exposed leaves needs substantiation.

comments.quote: So it would be good that the authors do substantiate this - important - claim a bit further. How can they guarantee us they were full-light exposed.

comments.issue: A part appears to be missing at line 175.
comments.request: Check the missing part.
comments.quote: l175. Part missing?

comments.issue: How STN is expressed and its units are unclear.
comments.request: Report the units of STN.
comments.quote: l257. How is STN expressed? What are the units?

comments.issue: Statement that more diverse communities resolve trait correlations is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the statement.
comments.quote: l328. I do not understand: "more diverse communities are more likely to resolve trait correlations.

comments.issue: Biological grounding is missing for this claim.
comments.request: Add the biological context.
comments.quote: l414. For such a claim I miss the biology in this analysis

title: Leaf trait network architecture shifts with species‐richness and climate across forests at continental scale

study.system: plant-plant interactions; global database of 10,502 pairs

editor_summary: Editor is mixed and finds the reviewer concerns substantial, requiring revision, re-analysis and possibly more data; a resubmission could be suitable but should go to the Synthesis section with more information on included studies and novelty.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the dataset but raises major methodological concerns about the NIntc metric, model choices and significance versus effect size.
strengths: most sweeping summary of plant-plant interactions

comments.issue: Hypotheses lack risky predictions or clear questions; H1 is uncontroversial.
comments.request: State testable predictions or reformulate as questions.
comments.quote: would benefit from either a) making risky or declarative (of strength and direction) predictions to test, which cannot be done in hindsight; or b) being reformulated into questions

comments.issue: The NIntc metric violates model assumptions and ignores sampling variance in control and treatment estimates.
comments.request: Use a suitable effect size such as Hedges' d that accounts for variance.
comments.quote: this method of quantifying net interaction effect does not consider variance in the estimates of control and treatment effects from the published studies

comments.issue: The hierarchical data structure is not modeled with appropriate random effects.
comments.request: Use mixed-effects models with study and other random effects.
comments.quote: The data is highly hierarchical and requires random effects/mixed effects models that account for this data structure.

comments.issue: GAMM assumptions are violated by NIntc; Figure 4 would fail residual checks.
comments.request: Report the distribution and validate model assumptions.
comments.quote: Figure 4 demonstrates this- this model would not pass usual model checks (residual normality, etc.)

comments.issue: GAMs are unjustified for hypotheses better suited to linear models; the spline use is unclear.
comments.request: Justify GAMs or use linear models.
comments.quote: GAM’s may be appropriate, but this is a much more complex model that requires strong justification over simpler, more common models for this question

comments.issue: Significant but tiny effects are treated as evidence for competition without reckoning with biological significance.
comments.request: Reckon with effect sizes and add a vote-counting summary.
comments.quote: there may be significant effects, but they are very small (biological versus statistical significance)

comments.issue: Whether glasshouse experiments are included at L95-97 is unclear.
comments.request: State whether glasshouse experiments are included.
comments.quote: Line 95-97- does this include glasshouse experiments?

comments.issue: L100-102 does not explain why experiments would not be on the same spatial and time scale.
comments.request: Provide an example.
comments.quote: Lines 100-102- Maybe provide an example? Not immediately clear why an experiment would not be on the same spatial and time scale for treatments.

comments.issue: L104-107 could be revised for brevity with the suggested wording.
comments.request: Adopt the shorter wording.
comments.quote: Maybe revise for brevity to “Weed/crop experiments were not included given agricultural systems are not natural plant communities and crop species or varieties are usually artificially selected for high productivity.”

comments.issue: Independence holds within a study but not at other hierarchical levels (L109-112).
comments.request: Acknowledge the non-independence at higher levels.
comments.quote: the data is (maybe) independent within the study. Not at other hierarchical levels.

comments.issue: L126-130 needs more detail and revision about metric selection order.
comments.request: Add detail on the hierarchical metric selection.
comments.quote: Line 126-130- add a bit more detail and revise

comments.issue: Whether the L149-152 information is reported in the supplement is unclear.
comments.request: State where this is reported.
comments.quote: Lines 149-152- Is this reported in the supplement?

comments.issue: Mixed versus non-mixed neighbor types are not defined.
comments.request: Define the neighbor-type categories.
comments.quote: What is mixed versus non-mixed neighbor types? I assume intraspecific is mixed?

comments.issue: 'Wiggly patterns rather than normal distributions' is unclear; the distribution family is unstated.
comments.request: Explain the term and the distribution family.
comments.quote: What is meant by “wiggly patterns rather than normal distributions”. What distribution family was used for this analysis?

comments.issue: The univariate model's spline and random effects at L180 are not described.
comments.request: Describe the model and its random effects.
comments.quote: By univariate do you mean that a spline (GAM) was fit to latitude and longitude? What hypothesis does this test?

comments.issue: 'Wiggly pattern' at L223-224 is used repeatedly without definition.
comments.request: Define it in the methods.
comments.quote: “Wiggly pattern” is used often but is not defined.

comments.issue: A vote-counting summary of competition versus facilitation data points is missing.
comments.request: Add vote counting of all data points.
comments.quote: I would be interested in the vote counting of all data points in the instances of competition versus facilitation.

comments.issue: L294-295 is unclear.
comments.request: Revise this passage.
comments.quote: Lines 294-295- Unclear what is meant- consider revising

comments.issue: The meaning of s(climate) in Table 1 conflicts with the simple linear models shown in Figure 4.
comments.request: Clarify what the spline terms represent.
comments.quote: What does the s(climate) mean? Is this indicating that a spline was fit for each climatic variable? Then why does figure 4 show simple linear models?

comments.issue: 'V' is not described and violin plots extend beyond the possible -1 to 1 range.
comments.request: Describe 'V' in methods and legends and fix the violin ranges.
comments.quote: “V” is reported often but I don’t think it is described in the methods and not well in the figure legends. Additionally, the violins extend beyond -1 and 1, which is impossible based on the interaction metric.

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: L12, L13, L99-100, L123 and the incorrect scaling rationale at L178.
comments.quote: Line 178- Drop “to ensure model convergence”. That’s not the reason for scaling.

reviews.assessment: Meticulous, strong global study; mostly minor suggestions on search terms, spatial predictors, model selection and cross-biome climate effects.
strengths: very good from theory to interpretation

comments.issue: Microclimate is not considered alongside soil and disturbance.
comments.request: Add microclimate to the discussion.
comments.quote: consider adding microclimate (or e.g., climatic conditions at ecologically relevant scale) in addition to soil and disturbances

comments.issue: Seasonality of interaction outcomes is not discussed; snapshot studies miss other seasons.
comments.request: Discuss seasonal dependence of interactions.
comments.quote: the same species-pair could have positive interaction in winter (e.g. the taller species trapping protective snow cover to protect the shorter species from extreme colds) and negative interactions in summer

comments.issue: Search terms omit 'fitness', 'occurrence/occupancy', 'abundance' and 'growth', potentially biasing results.
comments.request: Explain the choice of search terms and their omissions.
comments.quote: Could omission of these search terms bias the query results? What was the reasoning for the search terms you used?

comments.issue: Latitude and longitude may be insufficient spatial predictors; semivariograms already show autocorrelation.
comments.request: Clarify the spatial-predictor rationale.
comments.quote: I am hesitant if latitude and longitude are sufficient to represent “spatial predictors”.

comments.issue: Both AICc and p-values are used to select predictors without explanation.
comments.request: Explain the model selection approach.
comments.quote: Why you use both AICc and p-values?

comments.issue: How correlated variables were dropped at L191 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the collinearity handling.
comments.quote: did you drop both A and B, or only A or B? If the latter, how did you choose which variable to remove?

comments.issue: The L208-211 sentences would read better combined.
comments.request: Combine the sentences as suggested.
comments.quote: The paragraph would be more readable, to my opinion, if these sentences were combined.

comments.issue: The biome results description at L214-211 is too long.
comments.request: Shorten it as suggested.
comments.quote: For readability, I recommend shortening the description of results related to biomes.

comments.issue: L308 should clarify that the third hypothesis is meant, not the second.
comments.request: Add the clarifying phrase.
comments.quote: to make the distinction that you refer now to the third hypotheses and not the second as referred to at the beginning of the paragraph

comments.issue: The L321-324 phrasing about seedling emergence and growth is unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase as outcomes/effects for each indicator.
comments.quote: should these be written something like ‘outcome for seedling emergence’ or ‘effect for seedling emergence’

comments.issue: Cross-biome comparison of NInt_c against individual climatic variables may dilute climate effects.
comments.request: Assess NInt_c-climate relationships within biomes.
comments.quote: The current cross-biome examination of NInt_c vs. climatic predictors, could dilute climate dependence of interactions

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: L13, L23, L246, L261 and L302.
comments.quote: L261: Is there a word missing in the sentence?

reviews.assessment: Challenges the headline conclusion that competition prevails, says the results are expected and misses key literature on niche-based outcomes.
strengths: impressive amount of data from about 1000 papers
paper reads well and looks appealing

comments.issue: The data show large variability with positive and negative interactions co-occurring, not dominance of competition.
comments.request: Reframe the main conclusion around variability.
comments.quote: what I see here is that positive and negative are co-occurring within plant communities not that competition predominate

comments.issue: The lack of clear spatial or climatic patterns is expected from niche-based theory, and key prior papers are not considered.
comments.request: Cite and discuss the suggested literature.
comments.quote: There have been many papers on the outcomes of plant-plant interactions that the authors did not consider in their paper.

comments.issue: The performance-facet approach yields little generalization, and the negative growth result is already known.
comments.request: Focus on community-level patterns and acknowledge prior work.
comments.quote: it is difficult to find any generalization from that. Seeing that growth are in general more negative is indeed interesting but it is somehow already known

comments.issue: The facilitation patterns in dry, hot and cold biomes could be explained by Berdugo et al.'s work, which is not cited.
comments.request: Consider this work when interpreting the pattern.
comments.quote: I encourage the authors to look at the work of Berdugo et al. 2008 in Journal of ecology where they find consistent positive association in shrub land and savannas.

comments.issue: The list of selected publications is not accessible.
comments.request: Provide the list of included papers.
comments.quote: However, I struggle to find the paper list.

comments.issue: Whether removal experiments only or also open-area versus vegetated comparisons were included is unclear.
comments.request: Distinguish the two study types.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me whether this include removal experiments only or if the authors also included comparison between naturally vegetation free area (open area) vs vegetated areas?

title: Net plant interactions are highly variable and weakly dependent on climate at the global scale

study.system: annual plants in Western Australia; neighbour-removal experiment and Bayesian coexistence models

editor_summary: Editor: both reviewers are enthusiastic about the paper's potential importance but feel it needs more work; the authors are encouraged to consider all suggestions in revision.

reviews.assessment: Impressive attempt at a hard problem, but sources of uncertainty and joint distributions need clarification before conclusions can be drawn.
strengths: combines field experiment and Bayesian modelling

comments.issue: Individual variation, demographic stochasticity and observation error are lumped in the posteriors without identifying their sources or proportions.
comments.request: Partition the sources of variation and guide readers on what the uncertainty means.
comments.quote: I don’t see anywhere in the methodology where the variation is associated specifically with any of these factors.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the distributions of coexistence mechanisms are treated as independent, ignoring correlations.
comments.request: Account for the joint distribution and correlations.
comments.quote: It’s unclear whether the distributions of coexistence mechanisms are treated as independent or if correlations between the distributions is appropriately accounted for.

comments.issue: Mutual invasibility and the rho/kappa ratio give different answers although they are mathematically equivalent.
comments.request: Clarify the joint distributions and consider sticking with mutual invasibility.
comments.quote: I’m struck by the result that the same estimates provide different answers in using the two different measures.

comments.issue: Shared natural enemies are omitted from the theory description at line 67.
comments.request: Mention apparent competition with shared natural enemies.
comments.quote: The theory includes shared natural enemies as well.

comments.issue: Frequency-dependence is used where density-dependence is meant.
comments.request: Use density-dependence, which is more general.
comments.quote: Frequency-dependence often occurs, but the correct phenomenon here is density-dependence.

comments.issue: Fitness differences are defined in a way only experts understand.
comments.request: Use the clearer Chesson (2018) definition.
comments.quote: Fitness differences are notoriously difficult to define in layman terms.

comments.issue: The low-density growth rate is called a parameter although it is a derived measure.
comments.request: Call it a measure rather than a parameter.
comments.quote: the low density growth rate is a measure, an emergent outcome of the combined effects of other parameters

comments.issue: The description of Hart et al. (2016) misrepresents their conclusion that intraspecific variation inhibits coexistence.
comments.request: Rephrase to represent their conclusions accurately.
comments.quote: I thought Hart et al (2016) essentially find that coexistence is nearly always inhibited by intraspecific variation

comments.issue: How the "other" category was treated in the simulations is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain whether it has dynamics or is omitted.
comments.quote: How was the “other” category treated in simulations?

title: Accounting for demographic uncertainty increases predictions for species coexistence: A case study with annual plants

study.system: trees; global seed production, climate and productivity datasets

editor_summary: Editor says all found the latitudinal seed-production pattern impressive but the framing overemphasizes species interactions; asks to focus on empirical results, better use conceptual Fig. 1a, and specify the Panama data bias.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and valuable data, but the species-interaction framing outruns the correlative data and the logic is often hard to follow.
strengths: in-depth data and methods beyond the previous synthesis
timely topic of great interest to Ecology Letters readers
study and data definitely have merit

comments.issue: The pitch based on species interactions is disconnected from the data, and the robustness of the inference from abiotic predictions is not argued in the introduction.
comments.request: Clarify and argue the inferential logic linking abiotic predictability to species interactions.
comments.quote: I feel that there is a disconnect between the pitch (based heavily on species interactions) and the data (seed production and large-scale abiotic data – ie no data on species interactions).

comments.issue: The prominence of species interactions in the title, abstract and introduction is overplayed given the correlative data.
comments.request: Temper the interactions angle throughout the paper.
comments.quote: I still think the prominence of interactions (title, abstract, intro) is overplayed given that there are no data on interactions and all the analyses are correlative

comments.issue: The generic term 'interactions' is used where statements concern competition or granivory specifically.
comments.request: Use more specific terms instead of 'interactions' where appropriate.
comments.quote: Might help to move away from ‘interactions’ when statements are more specific to competition vs granivory?

comments.issue: The contribution of the paper is unclear: why the study is needed and how it changes understanding beyond previous smaller studies is not stated.
comments.request: Clearly outline the study's importance, problem and contribution in the introduction.
comments.quote: The contribution of the paper is not clear from the Introduction. Why do we need this study? How does it really change our understanding of Ecology beyond the smaller (but still good) studies that existed previously?

comments.issue: The logic is hard to follow within sentences, across arguments and between components of the paper.
comments.request: Revise the manuscript to make the argumentation easier to follow.
comments.quote: I found the logic hard to follow in many places in the paper, within individual sentences, within arguments across sentences, and sometimes in how different components of the paper matched up.

comments.issue: The text asserts a coincidence of high diversity with intense competition before making that case.
comments.request: Establish the coincidence before asserting it.
comments.quote: text has not yet made the case that these coincide (arguments have been about NPP & competition, previous sentence is hypothesis)

comments.issue: Vague pronouns ('this', 'these', 'in one', 'them', 'it') make the text harder to read than necessary.
comments.request: Replace vague pronouns with specific referents throughout.
comments.quote: The writing was a bit more work to read than it needed to be as there were lots of vague pronouns – eg ‘this’ or ‘these’ or ‘in one’, where it wasn’t clear what the pronoun was referring back to.

comments.issue: The questions are stated without context on why the mechanism driving the latitudinal seed-production gradient matters.
comments.request: Explain why the answer matters and clarify how productivity could increase seed production.
comments.quote: would be great if authors could clarify why this distinction matters (ie why do we care which mechanism drives the latitudinal gradient in seed production?)

comments.issue: The argument that selection to offset granivory would intensify competition is not intuitive.
comments.request: Clarify or revise this mechanism.
comments.quote: If selection for high seed production is to offset losses due to granivores, why would it intensify competition?

comments.issue: The logic that generalist seed consumers impose indirect competition is unclear, since consumers lower density and should alleviate competition.
comments.request: Reconsider or clarify the indirect-competition argument.
comments.quote: not following the logic that generalist seed consumers impose indirect competition among trees, as a consumer will always lower density and therefore alleviate competition

comments.issue: The claim that interactions are more intense in tropical forests lacks a citation.
comments.request: Add a citation for more intense tropical interactions.
comments.quote: L186 – need citation for interactions being more intense in tropical forests (then in temperate forests presumably?)

comments.issue: The acronyms ISP and CSP are uncommon, not intuitive (ISP is size-standardized) and used infrequently.
comments.request: Reconsider the acronyms or use more intuitive names.
comments.quote: I would reconsider the acronyms ISP and CSP – they are not common acronyms (I’ve never heard of them at least and I study seeds) and so require work from readers to remember.

comments.issue: It is a leap to conclude that steeper-than-predicted fecundity gradients mean climate drives intense biotic interactions; other mechanisms such as evolutionary history are possible.
comments.request: Clarify the directionality of the logic and justify the inference.
comments.quote: If fecundity gradients are steeper than predicted from size or NPP alone, why would that mean the climate was driving intense biotic interactions?

comments.issue: The proposed arms-race mechanism is unclear, including what mortality is involved.
comments.request: Clarify the arms-race argument.
comments.quote: L221 – mortality of who? Seeds? Trees? Not following how this arms race would work

comments.issue: The logic connecting biome differences in Moles et al. to the need to separate fecundity from abundance is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify why looking within forests adds something important.
comments.quote: Biome differences probably meaningfully contribute to latitudinal gradients in seed production – authors need to clarify their argument that looking within forests specifically (I think that’s what they are arguing with ‘tree abundance’?) adds something important to the larger question.

comments.issue: Moles et al., the previous review on latitudinal seed-production gradients, is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss Moles et al. in the discussion to contextualize the results.
comments.quote: given that Moles et al is THE previous review on latitudinal gradients in seed production, I would expect it to come up in the discussion as well to help put results into context

comments.issue: The reasons for including variables such as shade class and soil cation exchange capacity are not stated.
comments.request: Explain why these variables matter before the methods.
comments.quote: L233 – I would add a few words here (before methods) to indicate why these variables matter (esp shade class and soil cation exchange capacity – what is that representing?)

comments.quote: I’m not familiar with ‘redistribution models’. Suggest a few additional words re what class of models these are (generalized linear models? Bayesian approach)

comments.issue: It is unclear how 98% of sites can be temperate while 80% of observations are tropical, or what 'observation' means here.
comments.request: Clarify the site and observation definitions at L348.
comments.quote: clarify how its possible that 98% of sites are temperate but 80% of observations are tropical? Is ‘observation’ being used only for crop-counts?

comments.issue: Crown class is not defined.
comments.request: Define crown class at L355.
comments.quote: L355- define crown class – preferred light-habitat of mature trees?

comments.issue: Why leaving out standardization enables comparisons among sites is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify this and the SPEI standardization for unfamiliar readers.
comments.quote: not clear why leaving out standardization enables comparisons among sites. Doesn’t standardization usually enables better comparisons?

comments.issue: No reference supports cation exchange capacity as a measure of soil fertility.
comments.request: Add a supporting reference at L372.
comments.quote: L372 – need reference that cation exchange is a good measure of soil fertility

comments.issue: The methods paragraph does not explain how the data are used in the modelling framework or how data and parameters line up.
comments.request: Explain the link between data and model parameters at L379.
comments.quote: I don’t have a sense from this (main Methods) paragraph of how the data described above are used within this modelling framework – ie how data and model parameters line up

comments.issue: 'Weighted mean fecundity' appears only once and its derivation is unclear.

comments.quote: this is the only time in the paper that the term ‘weighted mean fecundity’ is used so its hard to see where its coming from / how its derived

comments.issue: The equation description is hard to follow; the relation between equation 4 and equation 1 for ISP is unclear.

comments.quote: I’m not following this description. Might be easier to follow if authors clarified how do equations 4 for Individual mean fecundity relates to eq 1 for ISP.

comments.issue: The ISP flatness argument is unclear, and curves on the back-transformed scale can result from non-normal error distributions.
comments.request: Clarify the ISP argument and the back-transformation issue at L245.
comments.quote: Mean would be a straight line? (that argument’s not great (as simply written) either as curves on back-transformed scale can result just from non-normal error distributions)

comments.issue: The take-home argument about small seeds is unclear, including whether small seeds were captured or excluded.
comments.request: Clarify the small-seed argument at L290.
comments.quote: L290 – logic not clear. What is take home argument re small seeds? Why are vertebrate seed predators particularly important (or are they)?

comments.issue: The claim that concentrating consumption implies specialist consumers is unclear, since generalists should consume proportionately.

comments.quote: L295 – concentrating consumption means consumption by specialist consumers? Generalists would be expected to still consume seeds/tree species proportionately to seed production/tree species, no?

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the dataset and the 250-fold result, but the diversity/interaction emphasis is speculative and tropical coverage is heavily biased to Panama.
strengths: impressive number of tree reproduction datasets

comments.issue: The link between high seed production and higher diversity via biotic interactions is speculative; seeds could die in non-density-dependent ways, and alternatives cannot be tested.
comments.request: Restrict the conclusions to what the data can test.
comments.quote: I found the emphasis on diversity and biotic interactions to be odd since it was highly speculative based on the actual data.

comments.issue: Nearly all tropical observations come from Panama, so representativeness for 'the tropics' is questionable and site contributions are wildly unequal.

title: Globally, tree fecundity exceeds productivity gradients

comments.issue: Extrapolation beyond the data is as problematic for process-based models as for statistical models, and this limitation is not acknowledged.

reviews.assessment: Welcomes the study as timely and well designed, but wants validation of the models and some empirical verification of the findings.

comments.issue: The process-based models' prior validation and empirical verification of the findings are missing.

title: The functional form of specialised predation affects whether Janzen–Connell effects can prevent competitive exclusion

editor_summary: Both reviewers see great potential but find the organization and presentation need substantial improvement before publication; the editor will consider the paper again if all comments are addressed.
