title: No robust multispecies coexistence in a canonical model of plant–soil feedbacks

study.system: North American trees; forest inventory data and IPMs

editor_summary: Editor: all impressed by the scope and advance; R1 and R3 question where competition and climate enter the models and want clearer methods; R2 asks how sensitive results are to model inaccuracies; discuss these limitations.

reviews.assessment: Enjoyable, thorough paper; needs clearer demographic data description and perturbation analysis mechanics.

comments.issue: The introduction paragraphs supporting Q3 are not tied directly to demographic compensation, weakening continuity.
comments.request: Reframe the climate-biotic comparison in terms of demographic compensation.
comments.quote: with the focus on DC throughout the manuscript, it would be useful to directly tie climate and biotic impacts to DC rather than demographic spatial variation more generally.

comments.issue: Key details of the underlying demography data (census times, DBH cut-off, recruit designation) are missing from the main methods.
comments.request: Add a short description of the demography data in the first methods section.
comments.quote: I think a short (2-3 sentences) description of the underlying demography data is needed in the first section of the materials and methods in the main text.

comments.issue: The mechanics of the perturbation analysis for climate and competition are unclear, and competition was excluded from recruitment models.
comments.request: Explain the perturbation analysis and why competition was not included for recruitment.
comments.quote: I found the methods overall to be very clear and well-organized, however couldn’t completely follow the mechanics of how the perturbation analysis that looked at the impact of climate and local competition on lambda, DC was done for all species.

comments.issue: For species whose final models included no climate variables, how the perturbation was done and whether cross-species comparison is valid is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the perturbation for species without climate variables and address comparability.
comments.quote: And even more broadly, for the species that had final models that did not include any of these variables (ex. Acer macrophyllum) how was this perturbation analysis done?

comments.issue: Commonalities among the species showing demographic compensation are not described.
comments.request: Report any commonalities among DC species.
comments.quote: D (results). Are there are any commonalities in the species that were found to show DC (L321)?

comments.issue: Leading/trailing edge terminology adds unnecessary complexity compared with expansions and contractions at low/high latitude.
comments.request: Use one consistent set of terms.
comments.quote: L78 It may be clearer to directly mention expectation of expansions and contractions at high, low latitude as opposed to leading/trailing edges.

comments.issue: The Oldfather citations at L90 and L95 may be swapped.
comments.request: Swap the two citations.
comments.quote: L90 and 95 – I think the citations Oldfather et al 2021 and Oldfather & Ackerly 2019 may be more appropriate switched for these two sentences.

comments.issue: Figure S3 is hard to read and missing red font.
comments.request: Enlarge the figure and restore the red font.
comments.quote: Fig S3 – Difficult to read at current size and missing red font

comments.issue: Figure S5 is hard to read at its current size.
comments.request: Enlarge Figure S5.
comments.quote: Fig S5 – Difficult to read at current size

reviews.assessment: Timely, well-written macroecological study; methods and results need clearer data descriptions and assumptions.
strengths: nicely written with clear and consistent structure

comments.issue: The title is an open statement rather than a clear result statement.
comments.request: Write a title that states the most relevant result.
comments.quote: I would recommend a title that contains a clear statement about the most relevant result of the study, rather than an open sentence like

comments.issue: Local adaptation or plasticity may underlie demographic compensation and is not noted.
comments.request: Note local adaptation and plasticity as possible mechanisms.
comments.quote: L83-87: Note that local adaptation or plasticity may underlie demographic compensation

comments.issue: The criteria at L195 lack a summary sentence of their main aspects.
comments.request: Add a summary sentence for the criteria.
comments.quote: L195: It would be nice to have a summary sentence suggesting the main aspects of those criteria.

comments.issue: Information on individuals per population, per population and census, and plots per species is missing, so data quality for lambda estimation cannot be judged.
comments.request: Report these means and ranges.
comments.quote: please include information on the mean and range (or something similar) of 1) number of individuals per population and 2) number of individuals per population AND census, to have an idea of the quality of data for demographic analyses

comments.issue: Whether population is equivalent to plot is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the population/plot terminology.
comments.quote: L212: Is population equivalent to plot in this study? Please clarify so

comments.issue: The all-subsets regression approach is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the all-subsets regression approach.
comments.quote: L222: it might be good to explain what “all-subsets regression approach” is

comments.issue: Assuming all individuals reproduce probably overestimates reproduction; the size of this overestimation is unknown.
comments.request: Quantify or qualify the overestimation.
comments.quote: This is a relevant assumption, which probably overestimates reproduction and thus population growth rates. The key is to know how big the overestimation is. Could specify a little more “generally”? Which percentage? Is it similar across species?

comments.issue: How time and multiple demographic transitions are accounted for when censuses vary from 2 to 5 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how transitions were modeled.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me how time is accounted for in these models. You say somewhere in the paper that the number of censuses varies between 2 and 5.

comments.issue: The percentage of populations with lambda greater than 1 is not reported as a complementary assessment.
comments.request: Report the percentage of populations with lambda > 1.
comments.quote: L273: A complementary way to assess the effectiveness of compensation would be to look at the % of populations with lambdas >1

comments.issue: Whether all vital rates or only negatively correlated ones were randomized is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the randomization procedure.
comments.quote: L274: Did you randomise all vital rates, or only the ones predominantly involved in negative correlations as in Villellas et al 2015?

comments.issue: Imprecise reproduction data may underestimate demographic compensation and should be discussed.
comments.request: Address this limitation in the Discussion.
comments.quote: The fact that the study lacked precise information about reproduction might be underestimating the presence of demographic compensation, it would be nice to address this in Discussion.

comments.issue: Transitions were calculated over multi-year periods, which may hide interannual variation and affect DC detection.
comments.request: Discuss the effect of multi-year transitions.
comments.quote: Another potential issue for discussion is the fact that transitions were calculated for periods of several years instead of annual censuses.

comments.issue: Why growth shows an opposing pattern to recruitment size while survival and recruits do not is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain this pattern in Fig. 2.
comments.quote: L325-328: Do you have any idea of why growth shows an opposing pattern than recruitment size in Fig. 2, but survival and number of recruits do not, despite their negative correlations with recruitment size?

comments.issue: The part at L331 should move to the next subsection for consistency with the methods structure.
comments.request: Move this part to the next Results subsection.
comments.quote: L331: I would recommend the authors to move this part to the next subsection in Results, to keep consistency with structure in methods, for easier reading.

comments.issue: Whether 45% refers to the species where survival is the most influential rate is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the 45% value in the text.
comments.quote: L337: Is 45% the percentage of species for which survival is the most influential rate for lambda, so that there isn’t any other vital rate showing a higher such percentage? If so, please explain it in the text.

comments.issue: The statement about southern mean lambda for six species at L346 is confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the significance statement.
comments.quote: L346: but mean lambda in the south for those 6 species was not significantly lower than 1, right? (that is why they don’t have a black border in Fig. 3, right? The text as it is written now is confusing.

comments.issue: In Fig. 4 the total species numbers for MWMT and BA look similar; differences appear mainly among DC species.
comments.request: Revise the description of Fig. 4.
comments.quote: Looking at Fig. 4, to me it seems that the total number of species for which MWMT and BA have the greatest negative effect is very similar (size of red bars)

comments.issue: Results may depend on the predictors chosen; unmeasured variables could be more important.
comments.request: Acknowledge this dependence at L408.
comments.quote: L408: I would suggest acknowledging that these results might depend on the predictors chosen by the authors. Although in principle they seem appropriate, other variables not measured could be more important, or change results.

comments.issue: Figures S3 and S5 are difficult to view.
comments.request: Enlarge or split these figures.
comments.quote: Figs. S3, S5: It is very difficult to look at these figures, consider making them larger, possibly dividing each of them into 2 or more figures

comments.issue: Four line-level wording and cross-reference edits (L113, L207, L302, L303).
comments.quote: L303: adding “separately” after “each factor” may improve reader’s understanding

reviews.assessment: Remarkable scope and advance, but trust in the simple population models and their sensitivity to data limitations needs evaluation.
strengths: huge step forward for demographic compensation research

comments.issue: The gap between detailed single-species models and the simpler models for 81 species is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss whether ecological details matter for these questions or justify the simplification.
comments.quote: But perhaps the authors could address the gap between how challenging it appears to be to build robust population models for one species when examined in great detail, compared to the relative ease and simpler models for 81 species.

comments.issue: Sensitivity of the results to inaccuracies in the population models from simple structures and coarse inventory data is unknown.
comments.request: Evaluate model performance and sensitivity, e.g. via a data-rich species comparison.
comments.quote: So the key concern/question is perhaps: how sensitive are the study’s results to inaccuracies in the population models, arising out of the relatively simple model structures and/or the coarseness of the inventory data?

comments.issue: The interaction between climate and competition is not accounted for.
comments.request: Justify or include climate-by-competition interactions.
comments.quote: As acknowledged in the discussion, don’t account for interaction of climate and competition. Why not? Seems like an important process?

comments.issue: How seedlings enter the analyses is unclear, and the recruit definition (saplings crossing 12.7 cm) should be clarified in the main text.
comments.request: Clarify the seedling and recruit definitions.
comments.quote: Unclear how / if seedlings are used in the analyses. Recruits are defined (supplement L85, although should be clarified in main text) as: “DBHs smaller than 12.7 cm in the preceding census but larger than 12.7 cm in the next census.”; So these are saplings?

comments.issue: Only trees larger than 12.7 cm DBH are evaluated, so 'recruitment' represents old trees and its effect is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the consequences of the DBH threshold.
comments.quote: only evaluated trees larger than 12.7 cm DBH. Trees this size obviously can be many decades old. Not clear what effect this has on model results to consider this “recruitment”

comments.issue: Competition is just total basal area in a plot without accounting for relative size of the target tree.
comments.request: Consider a relative competition index such as Hegyi's.
comments.quote: Competition is just total BA in a plot (not subplot?), without accounting for relative size compared to the target tree as many competition indices often allow for (e.g. Hegyi).

comments.issue: Reproduction is binary with all large trees assigned 1, ignoring fecundity differences.
comments.request: Consider size-dependent offspring production.
comments.quote: Reproduction is a binary 1/0 (with all trees assigned 1 since they are large), and no allowance for larger trees producing more offspring?

comments.issue: All vital rate models are simple GLMs, while other studies recommend incorporating more heterogeneity.
comments.request: Consider richer vital rate model structures.
comments.quote: All vital rate models are very simple GLMs. Other studies have suggested need to incorporate more heterogeneities in vital rate models for forest trees (e.g. Needham et al. 2018)

comments.issue: Including recruit size among vital rates is confusing given the fixed 12.7 cm threshold.
comments.request: Clarify why recruit size is a vital rate.
comments.quote: The four vital rates (L 245) include recruit size? I don’t understand this, as I thought there was a fixed (and large) threshold (12.7cm) for when they were considered recruits.

comments.issue: The large contribution of recruit size distribution to lambda is questionable given the limited monitoring of seedlings and saplings.
comments.request: Interpret this contribution given the data limitations.
comments.quote: What does this mean, given that only saplings of a certain size begin to be monitored in FIA data, and the seedling plots are very small and notoriously inadequate for capturing recruitment.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether edge lambdas use plot random effects or incorporate stand structure differences.
comments.request: Explain how edge lambdas are calculated.
comments.quote: The growth and survival data was pooled across all population for a species. Are the lambdas calculated for geographic range edges just using the plot random effects, or also somehow incorporating any differences in stand structure in those specific plots?

comments.issue: Whether recruitment data were pooled across all sites is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the pooling of recruitment data.
comments.quote: A bit unclear to me whether recruitment data was also pooled across all sites?

comments.issue: Apparent tree shrinkage due to measurement error may not have been handled.
comments.request: Report how measurement error and shrinkage were treated.
comments.quote: Did the authors have to deal with apparent shrinkage of trees due to measurement error? Has arisen in other studies and in personal exploration of FIA data.

title: The role of demographic compensation in stabilising marginal tree populations in North America

strengths: methods mostly the same as the original

comments.issue: Lines 11-14 contradict each other about sampling-intensity in the original study.

comments.quote: I find lines 11-14 contradictory and confusing since the authors successively say

reviews.assessment: Fundamental concern that the sampling-intensity metric conflates network structure with sampling effort, so the analyses do not address sampling effort.

comments.issue: 'Sampling-intensity' conflates sampling effort with network structure.

comments.issue: Central analyses do not address sampling effort and control for an inappropriate variable.

strengths: timely ecological angle on pesticide resistance

comments.issue: The manuscript does not clearly answer the two goals it sets up.

comments.issue: Ecological consequences section is unclear; the summary list and the traits link should open the section.

comments.issue: Readers are not referred to Box 3 where terms are defined.

study.system: population growth models; invasibility of rare species from synthetic time series

reviews.assessment: A better way to quantify invasibility than the classic growth-rate criterion, with wide-ranging implications; should be published after minor suggestions.
strengths: could have wide-ranging implications in ecology

comments.issue: Supplemental material was not included with the manuscript; the review assumes it is correct.
comments.quote: I am assuming that this supplemental material is correct and primarily contains technical details.

comments.issue: "Mean growth rate when rare" is grammatically misleading; the population, not the rate, is rare.
comments.request: Rephrase this phrase throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: the phrase "mean growth rate when rare" is grammatically misleading. It's not the growth rate that's rare, but the invader population is rare.

comments.issue: What it means that the time series is rarified is not explained.
comments.request: Explain clearly what rarifying the time series means.
comments.quote: what does it mean that "the time series is rarified"? Please explain clearly.

comments.issue: No explanation of how the main formulas arise or what they mean, including the 1/n decay.
comments.request: Explain how the formulas arise and what they mean.
comments.quote: some discussion should be given to give the reader a sense of how these formulas arise and their meaning

comments.issue: The clause "before going extinct" is unnecessary; the criterion should be reaching n_f from a small start.

comments.issue: Fig. 1 caption does not remind readers what V_d and V_e mean.

comments.issue: The term "decent-size" is vague.
comments.request: Make "decent-size" more precise.
comments.quote: the term "decent-size" is vague and should be make more precise.

reviews.assessment: New expression for expected intrinsic growth is interesting, but the methods, supplement and figures are hard to follow and the claim to replace E[r] is unsubstantiated.

comments.issue: References are scant; long unsupported statements, and seminal Chesson papers on coexistence theory are missing.

comments.issue: "Coherently" is unclear.

comments.issue: The logic at lines 527-531 is unclear and the point seems unimportant.
comments.request: Clarify or remove this passage.
comments.quote: 527-531: the logic here is not clear to me - this seems like an epiphenomenon rather than something important

comments.issue: Lines 531-541 do not clearly relate to the 'third parties' theme.
comments.request: Clarify the link to third parties.
comments.quote: 531-541: not entirely clear how this passage relates to "third parties"

comments.issue: The biofilm analogy at lines 548-559 is tenuous and may be unnecessary.
comments.request: Reduce the passage, perhaps keeping only the second half.
comments.quote: 548-559: the analogy here seems a bit tenuous - perhaps not necessary for this paper?

comments.issue: About 50 line-level edits suggested for length and clarity (deletions, wording, redundancy).
comments.quote: 58: the word "exchanges" is used several times throughout the paper. This may be a difference in usage between the US and UK, but I would think "interactions" would be clearer for a global audience

title: The overlooked complexity of avian brood parasite–host relationships

study.system: north-west European pollen records; Holocene plant functional traits

editor_summary: Major revisions: attend to R1's statistical concerns; handle radiocarbon uncertainty with Bayesian age-depth models; clarify that landscape opening is already known (R3); follow Neotoma's data citation format (R2).

reviews.assessment: Novel and valuable method for reconstructing plant traits from pollen; supports publication, but data attribution, the conversion table and many clarifications are needed.
strengths: novel method to reconstruct community trait composition from pollen
of interest to ecology, palaeoecology and archaeology

comments.issue: Neotoma data-use policy requires a database acknowledgement statement, which is missing from the manuscript.
comments.request: Add the Neotoma acknowledgement text to the acknowledgements.
comments.quote: I did not manage to find the Acknowledgements in the manuscript I have been reviewing, where the following text or a similar one should appear

comments.issue: Most datasets come from the European and Alpine Pollen Databases, but these constituent databases are not cited.
comments.request: Indicate the constituent databases and cite Fyfe et al. (2009).
comments.quote: most of the data sets used in this study are part of the European and the Alpine Pollen Databases and this should be indicated somewhere in the text

comments.issue: Neotoma's third attribution level, citations for each dataset and original investigator, is not met.
comments.request: Credit the original data contributors where the word limit allows.
comments.quote: Probably the authors of the datasets do not get a citation in the Web of Science or Scopus anyway but at least they see their work in the *.pdf file of the paper.

comments.issue: The table linking pollen types to plant species is missing, so linkage specificity cannot be judged.
comments.request: Provide the pollen type-to-species conversion table.
comments.quote: I did not find the table where the relationship between pollen types and plant species is established. This is very important for the reader to assess how specific these linkages are.

comments.issue: Magnitude of uncertainty from assigning traits to broad pollen types (e.g. Poaceae vs Fagus) is not indicated.
comments.request: Quantify trait-value dispersion within pollen types.
comments.quote: I also miss the authors to indicate the magnitude of such potential uncertainties.

comments.issue: Reviewer points to Sobral (2021) arguing all traits are functional, questioning the use of the term.
comments.request: Consider the 'all traits are functional' viewpoint.
comments.quote: Regarding the use of the term “functional trait”, extremely widespread in the literature, I found interesting and inspiring to read the following paper hot off the press

comments.issue: 'Agriculture' should be 'farming' because livestock husbandry is also relevant in some regions.
comments.request: Replace 'agriculture' with 'farming'.
comments.quote: I would suggest replacing “agriculture” with “farming”, as livestock husbandry has also been very relevant in some regions.

comments.issue: The Europe-wide sentence cites only central European and British Isles evidence.
comments.request: Refer to one or two southern European case studies.
comments.quote: but later one can only find references to central Europe and the British Isles. The authors may consider referring to one or two southern European case studies.

comments.issue: The statement applies to central and northern Europe but not to southern Europe.
comments.request: Consider thermomediterranean sites from Spain or Italy.
comments.quote: The content of this sentence applies to central and northern Europe, but not to southern Europe.

comments.issue: Windthrow and other disturbances are ignored; 'disturbance' would be more general.
comments.request: Use 'disturbance' instead.
comments.quote: Also windthrow and other disturbances may have played a role. I would recommend using “disturbance” to stay more general.

comments.issue: Claim overlooks that farming, not climate, dominated Late Holocene vegetation change.
comments.request: Cite Vannière et al. (2016) and qualify the claim.
comments.quote: Climate was the main driver of vegetation change during the Early and Middle Holocene, but during the Late Holocene at least it did not play a prominent role compared to farming

comments.issue: Pollen-independent temperature reconstructions are not cited.
comments.request: Check and cite pollen-independent temperature reconstructions.
comments.quote: Please, check and cite pollen-independent temperature reconstructions.

comments.issue: The statement only holds for central European low and mid elevations, not southern or northern Europe and mountains.
comments.request: Qualify the statement.
comments.quote: Again this holds true for central European low and mid-elevation areas, not for southern and northern Europe and the mountains, where evergreen species were dominant or co-dominant.

comments.issue: 'BP' is not defined at first use.
comments.request: Define BP.
comments.quote: First time that “BP” appears in the text, please define its meaning.

comments.issue: A recent Mediterranean study relevant to the geographic scope is missing.
comments.request: Consider Connor et al. (2021) to broaden southern European interest.
comments.quote: A recently published Mediterranean study that is probably worth reading to expand the interest to southern Europe

comments.issue: No convincing explanation is given for focusing on north-western Europe.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for the regional focus.
comments.quote: I miss a convincing explanation on why the authors have focused on north-western Europe.

comments.issue: An outdated pollen nomenclature table is used instead of the updated EPD version.
comments.request: Use the updated EPD nomenclature table (Giesecke et al. 2019).
comments.quote: An updated and more complete table concerning pollen nomenclature is on the EPD website (http://www.europeanpollendatabase.net) and the relevant publication is Giesecke et al. (2019).

comments.issue: The proportion of the dataset represented by these species is not reported.
comments.request: Report the proportion.
comments.quote: Which proportion of the dataset represents these species?

comments.issue: Site-level information is missing from the Appendix S2 table.
comments.request: Add columns with site information to Appendix S2.
comments.quote: These data are relevant and it would be interesting to find the information concerning each of the study sites. The authors may consider adding columns to the table in Appendix S2.

comments.issue: 'Pastoral farming' does not necessarily mean agriculture; the terms need correcting.
comments.request: Use 'pastoralism' and 'farming' instead.
comments.quote: I suggest replacing “pastoral farming” with “pastoralism” and then “agriculture” with “farming”

comments.issue: The statement should specify north-western Europe.
comments.request: Specify 'north-western' Europe.
comments.quote: Please, specify that it refers to “north-western” Europe.

comments.issue: No numerical estimate of the performance of the adjusted models is provided.
comments.request: Provide numerical model performance estimates.
comments.quote: I wonder whether the authors could provide any numerical estimate of the performance of the adjusted models.

comments.issue: The text says 'steadily', which the graphs do not support.
comments.request: Revise the 'steadily' statement.
comments.quote: By looking at the graphs, I would not say steadily.

comments.issue: The statement should be limited to the period investigated.
comments.request: Specify the period investigated.
comments.quote: I suggest specifying that for the period investigated in this study.

comments.issue: The statement lacks a supporting reference.
comments.request: Provide a reference.
comments.quote: L255-256 Please, provide a reference supporting this statement.

comments.issue: Detection of farming via anthropogenic pollen indicators (Rey et al. 2018) is not considered.
comments.request: Consider anthropogenic pollen indicators for identifying farming.
comments.quote: If the pollen records are detailed enough, farming is revealed by the presence of anthropogenic pollen indicators (see Rey et al., 2018).

comments.issue: The tree-height sentence adds little; forest clearing obviously lowers community height.
comments.request: Consider removing or reframing the sentence.
comments.quote: I am afraid that this sentence is not adding much. One expects that community tree height decreases when forests are cleared.

comments.issue: The curves show seed number as stable as seed mass, contrary to the text.
comments.request: Check the seed number statement.
comments.quote: Looking at the curves, seed number looks as stable as seed mass.

comments.issue: The seed discussion lacks detail, e.g. pioneer trees with light seeds like Betula.
comments.request: Discuss Betula and other light-seeded pioneers.
comments.quote: It would be nice to go more into the details here. What about pioneer trees with light seeds like Betula?

comments.issue: Reviewer reiterates that data analysts and stewards must be credited to sustain open databases.
comments.request: Ensure data contributors receive credit.
comments.quote: If the work done by analysts and data stewards/curators is properly acknowledged and gets credit in scientific terms, maintenance and enlargements of open databases will be encouraged

comments.issue: Taxonomic resolution is not 'relatively low' here; the situation is worse elsewhere.
comments.request: Qualify the taxonomic resolution statement.
comments.quote: Taxonomic resolution is “relatively” low in this region, where pollen morphology has been widely investigated and plant diversity is not particularly high.

comments.issue: Confidence intervals may be too narrow given the dispersion of data points.
comments.request: Reconsider the confidence intervals.
comments.quote: I was wondering whether the confidence intervals are too narrow considering the dispersion of the data points

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important use of palaeodata, but the statistical methods need better justification, uncertainty handling and robustness checks.
strengths: interesting and important way of using paleodata
could be published with major revisions

comments.issue: Methods appear ad hoc and the modelling choices are not adequately justified.
comments.request: Rework the methods to justify the statistical choices.
comments.quote: I had to look at the JAGS code to understand the statistical notation and as written these methods seem somewhat ad hoc

comments.issue: PCA is applied to posteriors although it is normally a pre-modelling exploration step.
comments.request: Justify using PCA on posteriors.
comments.quote: PCA is typically used as a data exploration of dimension reduction exercise before fitting any model. Using on posteriors when you already have distribution weights seems to be an odd choice.

comments.issue: No explanation is given for using univariate rather than multivariate normal likelihoods despite the focus on trait covariation.
comments.request: Justify not using a multivariate normal likelihood.
comments.quote: there is no explanation of why the multivariate normal was not used in the likelihood. It seems that since one of the main concerns of the paper is how the traits covary that this would be the obvious choice.

comments.issue: Pollen samples are assumed independent with no spatial or temporal component; the second model does not feed back.
comments.request: Justify the independence assumption or add spatial and temporal structure.
comments.quote: It seems that a big assumption was made that each pollen sample is independent which is not justified in the paper.

comments.issue: Model inadequacies and assumptions are not discussed.
comments.request: Add discussion of modelling assumptions and limitations.
comments.quote: At the very least, there needs to be discussion of the inadequacies/assumptions of the modeling in the discussion.

comments.issue: Time-series figures are not compelling and poorly characterize uncertainty.
comments.request: Improve the figures and their uncertainty representation.
comments.quote: The time series figures are not compelling. There are many questions that are raised about the characterization of uncertainty with those figures in the main text.

comments.issue: Radiocarbon dating uncertainty is not accounted for.
comments.request: Account for radiocarbon dating uncertainty.
comments.quote: For instance, how did you account for radiocarbon dating uncertainty?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the trends are robust to omitting sites.
comments.request: Add a robustness analysis omitting sites.
comments.quote: And if some sites were omitted would the trends still be the same? i.e., how robust are these trends?

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits: two 'reword' requests, capitalisation, equation numbering and punctuation.
comments.quote: methods 158 (and further below): even displayed equations should be made part of sentence with punctuation

comments.issue: Dawson (2016) is not cited where relevant.
comments.request: Cite Dawson 2016 as well.
comments.quote: methods 110: see Dawson 2016 as well

comments.issue: Choice of the most common species over a weighted average is not justified.
comments.request: Justify or use a weighted average.
comments.quote: methods 123: could you have done a weighted average instead? What's the rationale behind taking most common?

comments.issue: Inconsistency between lines 157 and 158 about beta versus log-normal.
comments.request: Clarify which distribution is used.
comments.quote: methods 157: should line 158 be beta or should here say log-normal?

comments.issue: The likelihood function is not identified.
comments.request: State that this is the likelihood function.
comments.quote: Also, I think this is your likelihood function? Make mention of that somewhere.

comments.issue: Equation notation is incomplete and inconsistent (missing left-hand side, indexing, parameter notation).
comments.request: Fix the notation and explain the indexing.
comments.quote: methods 164: something should go on the left hand side of the tilde here.

comments.issue: The univariate normal choice and the trait independence assumption are unjustified.
comments.request: Justify the univariate normal and iid assumptions.
comments.quote: I'm wondering why you choose univariate instead of multivariate normal? Would you mind providing justification that the traits are iid or that this simplifying assumption is valid?

comments.issue: The R functions used are not provided.
comments.request: Add the R functions used.
comments.quote: methods 173: add R functions used here

comments.issue: No citation supports posterior simulation as a model-fit test.
comments.request: Provide a citation for this validation approach.
comments.quote: methods 183: provide a citation that simulating datasets from posterior is a good test for model fit assessment

comments.issue: No GAM with temperature alone, without agriculture, is fitted.
comments.request: Fit a GAM with temperature only.
comments.quote: methods 202: is there another gam fit to just temperature not agriculture?

comments.issue: Correlation values are not reported in this section.
comments.request: Report correlation values in parentheses.
comments.quote: results 235: report correlation values in parentheses in this section

comments.issue: The discussion statement is not linked to figures or calculated statistics.
comments.request: Refer to figures or statistics for the statement.
comments.quote: discussion 247: refer to figures or calculated statistics here

comments.issue: Citation missing after 'not terribly surprising'.
comments.request: Add the relevant citation.
comments.quote: discussion 283: provide citation after 'not terribly surprising'

comments.issue: Caption numbers are not shown in figure 1 itself.
comments.request: Add the caption numbers to the figure.
comments.quote: figure 1: add numbers from caption to figure itself.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not cover the GAM methodology.
comments.request: Include the GAM methodology in figure 1.
comments.quote: Would it also be possible to include the gam methodology in this figure?

comments.issue: The post-agriculture PCA spread suggests expanded niche space, which is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss whether agriculture opened niche space.
comments.quote: it's interesting that the pca distributions overlap but that after agriculture is bigger. Do you think agriculture could have opened up more niche space for a larger variety of plants?

comments.issue: Deep-time data sparsity and its uncertainty are not reflected in the GAM fits.
comments.request: Account for fewer deep-time points and their uncertainty.
comments.quote: figure 3: how did you account for inherently fewer data points in deep time? The uncertainty does not seem to be reflected in the gam fits (blue lines)

reviews.assessment: Interesting imputation approach and elegant analysis, but plant height may reflect community structure rather than functioning and the model description hinders reproducibility.
strengths: novel trait imputation approach for historical macroecology
well written and easy to read

comments.issue: Plant height measures community structure rather than ecosystem functioning, so the functioning shift may be structural.
comments.request: Clarify the interpretation of plant height as a functional trait.
comments.quote: I understand why plant height is usually included as a functional trait, but I am wondering whether this is more related here with changes in the structure of the community due to agriculture onset.

comments.issue: The PCA plots suggest an expansion rather than a shift in functioning, driven by plant height.
comments.request: Clarify whether the pattern is expansion or a functional shift.
comments.quote: For instance, your PCA plots suggest not a shift in functioning, but an expansion of it.

comments.issue: No correlation matrix of the functional traits is provided to judge collinearity.
comments.request: Provide a correlation matrix of the functional traits.
comments.quote: Unfortunately, I didn’t find a correlation matrix of your plant functional traits.

comments.issue: Results may be driven by plant height; analyses excluding it or by plant group are needed.
comments.request: Repeat analyses without plant height and by plant groups.
comments.quote: To make your analysis more convincing I would try to remove plant height from the analysis and/or repeat analysis for different plant groups (e.g., herbs, shrubs, and trees).

comments.issue: The meaning of 'species trait composition' is unclear; intraspecific trait change would undermine the fixed-species imputation.
comments.request: Clarify and discuss whether intraspecific variation invalidates the imputation.
comments.quote: It is unclear what you refer to species trait composition. Do you mean that the same species has different trait composition before and after agriculture?

comments.issue: A statement implies community-level trait uncertainty was analysed, which it was not.
comments.request: Remove or qualify the statement.
comments.quote: I see that you report uncertainty of your GAM models, but not so much on the community level trait reconstruction.

comments.issue: GBIF search criteria, species-name standardisation and coordinate cleaning are not explained.
comments.request: Describe these steps and provide a supplementary table.
comments.quote: It is not enough to acknowledge the packages, please explain which were your search criteria in the GBIF database, or any other important aspect you might have taken into consideration when standardizing species names or deleting invalid coordinates

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the species-to-pollen assignment was site-specific or global.
comments.request: Explain whether the imputation was site-dependent.
comments.quote: you didn’t explain whether the spatial imputation of species to the pollen dataset was made as a whole or was site dependent

comments.issue: Calculation of pollen-taxon trait values is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how pollen taxon trait values were derived.
comments.quote: Neither you explain how you calculated the pollen taxon trait values. Are they mean values across the species in each pollen taxon?

comments.issue: The section name does not match the information presented in it.
comments.request: Rename the section.
comments.quote: Hence, the section name doesn’t seem appropriate for the information dispatched on it.

comments.issue: The section name does not fit its content.
comments.request: Rename the section.
comments.quote: Similarly, the name of the section doesn’t entirely fit its content.

comments.issue: The model explanation is unclear and requires reading the code, hindering reproducibility.
comments.request: Rewrite the model explanation for a general audience.
comments.quote: I still do not understand how you used the species trait values to constrain your model, since you have multiple species in the same pollen taxon.

comments.issue: The appendix lacks details on the input data format needed to replicate the analysis.
comments.request: Document the input data structure in the appendix.
comments.quote: The code provided is useful to understand the methods, but further details in the appendix would be needed to any user being able to replicate the analysis.

comments.issue: Sentence starts with the figure '18' instead of the word 'eighteen'.
comments.request: Write 'eighteen' instead of '18'.
comments.quote: L195: Consider change ‘18’ by ‘eighteen’ to not start a sentence with a figure.

comments.issue: Figures and tables in the appendices are not numbered.
comments.request: Number the supplementary figures and tables.
comments.quote: Figures and tables should be numbered here. For instance, there are two figures in appendix S8.

comments.issue: Captions and legends are too poor to understand the supplementary figures and tables.
comments.request: Provide fuller captions and descriptions.
comments.quote: Captions or legends are poor and do not allow to fully understand the figures and tables.

title: Pollen‐based reconstruction reveals the impact of the onset of agriculture on plant functional trait composition

study.system: temperate rocky reef; 22-year subtidal kelp and urchin monitoring

editor_summary: Reviewers generally positive but concerned: R1 doubts novelty beyond the authors' PNAS paper; R2 wants more data on recruitment and Pycnopodia; R3 asks for analysis clarifications; reject with encouragement to resubmit.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and solid, but the findings largely repeat the authors' PNAS paper and lack the novelty expected by Ecology Letters.
strengths: a lot of work went into this study

comments.issue: The PNAS paper already made the same point and described the sampling scheme; this manuscript adds depth but nothing really new.
comments.request: Make a convincing case for a substantial novel contribution beyond the PNAS paper.
comments.quote: Thus, in my view, the present MS mainly provides greater depth in the analysis of sea urchin activity patterns, but does not present anything really new.

comments.issue: The more complex southern California situation, including alternative predators, is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss southern California studies and alternative kelp-maintaining predators.
comments.quote: The situation in southern California is actually more complex but not really discussed much by these authors.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written and important, but the recruitment and Pycnopodia contentions need stronger data before the conclusions hold.
strengths: important contribution on the neglected role of behavior
impressive scale of field surveys (285 sites)

comments.issue: The authors may underestimate urchin recruitment and its interaction with behavior; regional population explosions suggest an alternative scenario.
comments.request: Provide stronger evidence that population sizes did not increase before the behavioral shift.
comments.quote: An alternative/plausible scenario is that many of these factors interacted – e.g., increased urchin recruitment, warm water, loss of kelp – all contributing to the shifts in behavior described here.

comments.issue: The Figure 3 size-frequency data, the basis for ruling out recruitment, lack documented methods and sites.
comments.request: Explain how the Figure 3 data were collected, from which sites, and how pooled.
comments.quote: But it is not clear how these data were collected and from which study sites. (The authors cite an in press paper by Malone et al. as the source, but I could not find this paper online.)

comments.issue: The Pycnopodia loss conclusion is speculative without density data and should be framed as a hypothesis.
comments.request: Treat the predator-cue conclusion as a hypothesis, not a supported conclusion.
comments.quote: the conclusion that urchin behavior switched in part due to changes in predator cues seems highly speculative and should be treated in the paper as a hypothesis

comments.issue: Warm temperatures increase metabolic costs and grazing rates, an additional driver of behavioral shifts beyond food depletion.
comments.request: Mention temperature-driven energetic demands as an additional mechanism.
comments.quote: Warmer temperatures are associated with increased metabolic costs, which might have led to increased demand for food resources at the same time that kelp populations were crashing during the heatwave.

comments.issue: The timeline is wrong: sea stars declined from 2013 but the marine heatwave began in California in mid-2014.
comments.request: Correct the marine heatwave timeline throughout.
comments.quote: Sea stars began declining with the disease epidemic in 2013, but the marine heatwave did not begin in California until mid-2014.

comments.issue: The text implies urchins increased in Baja California, but they decreased there.
comments.request: Correct the statement about Baja California.
comments.quote: The text implies that sea urchins also increased in Baja California, Mexico, but they actually decreased in that region, correct?

comments.issue: The text implies the entire southern Monterey Bay region is protected from harvest.
comments.request: Clarify that only the survey region is protected.
comments.quote: This sounds like the entire southern Monterey Bay region is protected from harvest. I assume you mean just the area shown in Figure 1

comments.issue: No data support the claim that Pycnopodia was extirpated at the survey sites in 2013, earlier than elsewhere.
comments.request: Present local Pycnopodia abundance data supporting the 2013 extirpation timing.
comments.quote: Can you present some data to support that Pycnopodia was extirpated at your survey sites in Monterey Bay in 2013? This is earlier than at other sites in California and along the west coast

comments.issue: The extirpation was not just local to Monterey Bay but occurred throughout California.
comments.request: Mention the spatial scale of the extirpation.
comments.quote: Not just locally in Monterey Bay, but throughout CA. The scale of this extirpation might be mentioned as it is relevant to prospects for Pycnopodia to recover quickly.

comments.issue: The 12 PISCO sites are not identified and it is unclear how they relate to Figure 1.
comments.request: Clarify which 12 sites were used and whether they are in Figure 1.
comments.quote: Where were the 12 sites? Are these sites included in Figure 1? Clarify what you mean be a "subset of 12 sites"?

comments.issue: Some sites are in Pacific Grove, so the location label may be inaccurate.
comments.request: Change the location label to Monterey Bay.
comments.quote: Change to Monterey Bay? Some sites are in Pacific Grove, correct?

comments.issue: Framing recruitment and behavior as alternatives is artificial; recruitment could have contributed to the behavioral shift.
comments.request: Consider a scenario where recruits in refuges emerged later when food was depleted.
comments.quote: This seems like an artificial dichotomy. What if an increase in recruitment contributed to a shift in behavior?

comments.issue: It is unclear how terrain ruggedness, slope and relief were tested and where results are reported.
comments.request: Explain the test and include results in the supplement.
comments.quote: How was this tested, and should these results be included in the supplement?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether yearly sampling sites were selected in a stratified or random manner.
comments.request: Describe how sampling sites were selected each year.
comments.quote: Were sites sampled each year selected in some stratified manner to sample across the entire Figure 1 study region, or were they selected randomly from the set of 285?

comments.issue: The minimum urchin size included in analyses is not stated, and small urchins may be invisible in photos.
comments.request: Report the minimum urchin size included.
comments.quote: Mention the minimum size urchin included in these analyses? Presumably the smallest urchins were not always visible in photos and thus were not included?

comments.issue: The kelp cover threshold used to classify forested patches is not given.
comments.request: State the kelp cover threshold for forested classification.
comments.quote: Was there some threshold of kelp cover to be classified as forested?

comments.issue: Which 12 PISCO sites were used and how they were selected is not explained.
comments.request: Provide details on the 12 sites and their selection.
comments.quote: Provide more information (here or in supplement?) regarding which 12 sites were used. How were these 12 sites selected from among other PISCO monitoring sites?

comments.issue: The increase from 152 to 6092 urchins is hard to interpret without survey area and pooling details.
comments.request: Report the survey area and sampling design behind these counts.
comments.quote: It is difficult to interpret this increase from 152 to 6092 urchins. This is pooled over 12 sites?

comments.issue: How the size data were collected is unclear and the cited source is not yet available online.
comments.request: Describe how the urchin size data were collected.
comments.quote: How were these size data collected? It appears that this paper is not yet available online.

comments.issue: Regional urchin population explosions require a more thorough analysis of whether recruitment contributed to the behavioral changes.
comments.request: Analyse whether increased recruitment contributed to the observed behavioral changes.
comments.quote: So a more thorough analysis is needed to consider whether increased urchin recruitment contributed to the behavioral changes you report at your study sites.

comments.issue: The model actually supports a recruitment contribution (RVI = 0.514), which the authors downplay.
comments.request: Acknowledge recruitment and test interactions between factors.
comments.quote: The model is consistent with the hypothesis that recruitment contributed to increases in urchin populations (RVI = 0.514), but it seems like you downplay recruitment as an important factor.

comments.issue: More data and details are needed to support the claim that recruitment did not contribute to changes in adult behavior.
comments.request: Provide the additional data and details supporting this claim.
comments.quote: As noted elsewhere in my comments, more data and/or details are needed to support the hypothesis that recruitment did not contribute to these changes in adult behavior.

comments.issue: The predatory release claim is speculative without historical Pycnopodia density and extirpation timing data.
comments.request: Add historical Pycnopodia density and extirpation timing data.
comments.quote: As noted above, this seems speculative and you don’t provide evidence to support this hypothesis. Can you strengthen this support by adding historical data regarding the density of Pycnopodia and the timing of their extirpation at these sites?

comments.issue: A uniform increase in urchin density cannot be claimed from pooled density data.
comments.request: Clarify how uniformity across sites was assessed.
comments.quote: Clarify how we know it was a "uniform increase" in urchin density? Aren’t the density data plotted in Figure 2 pooled across multiple study sites?

comments.issue: Wolf eels are not among the five predators listed, so calling them urchin predators is inconsistent.
comments.request: Clarify whether wolf eels prey on sea urchins.
comments.quote: Clarify: Are wolf eels predators on sea urchins? They are not among the five predators listed in line 378.

comments.issue: Figure 2 data need more explanation, including whether counts are pooled across the 12 sites.
comments.request: Explain the Figure 2 data and site locations.
comments.quote: (Figure 2) More explanation is needed regarding these data. These are total counts in all quadrats pooled across 12 sites?

comments.issue: The Figure 3 caption does not explain whether data come from the same 12 sites or define test diameter.
comments.request: Explain the Figure 3 data and specify that size is test diameter.
comments.quote: (Figure 3, caption) More explanation is needed regarding these data. Are these data from the same 12 sites as in Figure 2?

title: Alternations in the foraging behaviour of a primary consumer drive patch transition dynamics in a temperate rocky reef ecosystem

study.system: boreal larch forest soil; 10-year N addition experiment

editor_summary: Four referees found the long-term experiment and data interesting but flagged the abstract's lack of quantitative information, presentation, unclear aspects and numerous typos; thorough revision and careful English editing required.

reviews.assessment: Timely long-term dataset, but the novelty, statistical clarity and integration with the wider context need substantial improvement.
strengths: timely topic relevant to global carbon cycling
first long-term N-enrichment study with continuous respiration measurements

comments.issue: Numerous line-level copy edits: articles, agreement, spacing, word choices and a unit reference.
comments.quote: Due to time I’m not going to mention all typographical errors, but in many cases the articles ‘the’ or ‘a(n)’ are either not needed or missing.

comments.issue: The added benefit and novelty of continuous measurements, and of the study overall, are not convincingly demonstrated.
comments.request: Explain what continuous measurements add beyond existing long-term studies.
comments.quote: I do not become fully convinced there is clear added benefit or that this study clearly added new/a missing piece of evidence or changes or mechanistic understanding

title: High‐level nitrogen additions accelerate soil respiration reduction over time in a boreal forest

study.system: savanna tree-grass water uptake; isotope tracers and soil water models

editor_summary: Editor values the tracer-plus-modelling novelty and context dependence but echoes the reviewer: do not dismiss fire/herbivore mechanisms and avoid over-selling competitive-advantage results.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, novel tracer and modelling study, but the competitive-advantage framing, dismissal of top-down mechanisms, and some methods details need revision.
strengths: impressive isotope tracer work over two seasons at four sites
integrates empirical findings with water-uptake modelling
Figures 1 and 2 are very nice and easy to interpret

comments.issue: “Competitive advantage” is conflated with niche partitioning and it is unclear whether it means a fitness difference.
comments.request: Define what is meant and use clearer coexistence terminology.
comments.quote: The use of language about “competitive advantage” throughout is confusing, because niche partitioning is rather about minimizing competition via divergent resource use, and it’s not clear whether “competitive advantage” here is supposed to mean a fitness difference

comments.issue: The predictions of the two-layer hypothesis being tested are not clearly articulated or situated in coexistence theory.
comments.request: Articulate the tested predictions and coexistence-theory context.
comments.quote: This manuscript could benefit from a clearer articulation regarding what predictions of the two-layer hypothesis are being tested, and perhaps also situating this more clearly within the broader context of coexistence theory.

comments.issue: The study implies absolute water uptake equals fitness without measuring water use efficiency or productivity.
comments.request: Avoid equating water uptake with fitness or justify the comparison.
comments.quote: This also implies that absolute water uptake = fitness, but without information about water use efficiency and productivity, it’s hard to make that comparison between grasses and trees.

comments.issue: Introduction and Discussion dismiss top-down fire and herbivory mechanisms as an either-or alternative.
comments.request: Treat mechanisms as non-exclusive and discuss their synergy.
comments.quote: I also found that the Introduction and Discussion were needlessly dismissive of top-down mechanisms of tree-grass coexistence in savannas, treating this as an either-or matter when it need not be.

comments.issue: The logic linking grass suppression of trees to proof or disproof of the two-layer hypothesis is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how suppression relates to niche partitioning.
comments.quote: L65 – Does grass competitive suppression of trees prove or disprove the 2-layer hypothesis? If niche partitioning is successful, wouldn’t that decrease the degree to which grasses can suppress trees?

comments.issue: The tested assumption is presented as relative water amounts, whereas the hypothesis concerns different water pools.
comments.request: Reframe the question around how distinct the water sources are.
comments.quote: Isn’t the core of the hypothesis that they are absorbing different pools of water (rather than relative amounts) and so the trees get more water than they would if they had shallower roots?

comments.issue: The water-depletion statement needs framing against earlier statements about shallow roots.
comments.request: Clarify and frame the paragraph around root distributions versus water uptake.
comments.quote: L77-80 – Perhaps clarify that this statement about shallow soils being water-depleted is in contrast to earlier statements about more roots being found shallowly.

comments.issue: The study measures water uptake but the overarching interest is plant growth and fitness.
comments.request: State clearly how water uptake is linked to growth and abundance.
comments.quote: There is still a leap here, between what can be measured and what the overarching hypothesis is really about – what we’re really interested in is plant growth and fitness, but the approach allows for quantifying water uptake

comments.issue: The design description is insufficient to envision the study or reproduce it without other sources.
comments.request: Add grid placement, species, site and isotope method details.
comments.quote: There is not enough detail here to fully envision the design of the study.

comments.issue: “Proportion of tracer uptake” is ambiguous and one sentence is incomplete.
comments.request: Clarify the proportion’s denominator and fix the sentence.
comments.quote: L133-134 – Is “proportion of tracer uptake” a proportion out of the total tracer injected, or the total tracer taken up by all plants? This phrasing is confusing.

comments.issue: Using an alfalfa sub-model for trees is not obviously appropriate given their height and differences.
comments.request: Explain the choice and its assumptions and limitations.
comments.quote: The use of an alfalfa sub-model jumped out here, because it seems trees are quite different from alfalfa and much taller than 60 cm

comments.issue: It is unclear whether precipitation values are averages, identical across sites, and from which years.
comments.request: Report site precipitation values and study years.
comments.quote: Was annual precipitation the same at both sites within each category? It’s not clear if these reported values are averages

comments.issue: The simulation setup is hard to follow and may be circular when water uptake predicts tree cover.
comments.request: Explain what was manipulated and address the circularity.
comments.quote: I couldn’t quite follow how this approach avoids circularity when evaluating whether modeled differences in water uptake predict tree cover

comments.issue: Unique hydrological niches are more relevant than total water uptake but are under-emphasised.
comments.request: Emphasise the unique hydrological niches in the results.
comments.quote: This concept of unique hydrological niches in space and time is useful, and seems more relevant than comparing total water uptake of trees vs. grasses, so it would be good to see this emphasized more in the results.

comments.issue: Species composition similarity among sites and trait conservation are not reported.
comments.request: Report species composition and trait conservation.
comments.quote: L211-212 – Speaking of highly conserved traits, how similar was species composition among sites?

comments.issue: The “advantage” framing implies a winner and is confusing for a coexistence argument.
comments.request: Use “favour” rather than “advantage” language.
comments.quote: L226 – As noted above, this framing as competitive “advantage” is confusing. It implies either the trees or the grasses win.

comments.issue: Total water uptake is treated as production or fitness, which need not follow.
comments.request: Soften the advantage interpretation.
comments.quote: Total water uptake does not necessarily equal production or fitness; if grasses use less water in total but also persist and thrive, are they at a disadvantage?

comments.issue: Temporal water-uptake niches deserve more attention than they receive.
comments.request: Extract and present seasonal water-uptake patterns.
comments.quote: L273-275 – This idea of different temporal niches of trees vs grasses deserves more attention, especially because earlier (e.g. L180) hinted at the idea that this method could quantify unique hydrological niches.

comments.issue: Positive frequency dependence alone would discourage coexistence, so calling it a coexistence mechanism is confusing.
comments.request: Discuss the additional processes needed for coexistence.
comments.quote: It’s somewhat confusing here to focus only on the positive frequency dependence and call this a coexistence mechanism, because on its own that would seem to discourage coexistence.

comments.issue: The grey outlines around the light-green overlap area in Figure 2 obscure the overlap.
comments.request: Remove the grey outlines.
comments.quote: Fig 2 – Minor aesthetic suggestion, perhaps remove the gray outlines around the areas of light green so it’s more obvious as an area of overlap where the colors blend.

comments.issue: It is unclear what Figure 3 is meant to show.
comments.request: Clarify the purpose and content of Figure 3.
comments.quote: Fig 3 – It was much less clear to me what this figure was meant to show – relating in part to the concerns/confusion noted above about circularity in the simulation methods.

comments.issue: The Figure 3 relationship may be circular because root abundance is a function of plant abundance.
comments.request: Explain why the correlation is not circular.
comments.quote: Is root abundance in the soil not a function of plant abundance, such that we would expect these values to be correlated? Or am I misunderstanding the point of this analysis?

comments.issue: Inset photographs in Figure 3 are unhelpful and the dotted zero line looks like data.
comments.request: Revise the figure visuals as suggested.
comments.quote: Visually, I would note that the inset photographs inside the boxes are not particularly helpful to interpretation, over-emphasizing spatial patterns rather than comparative amounts of tree cover

comments.issue: Figure 4’s 3D surfaces mostly extrapolate and add little information from only four sites.
comments.request: Replace with a qualitative comparison of the four sites.
comments.quote: It was not clear to me how much it adds to display these 3D surfaces representing water uptake across all soil and rainfall parameter combinations.

editor_summary: Editor: timely and well-executed, but it reads as a technical note on Chesson's theory; narrow the claimed scope and improve accessibility via worked examples, standalone figures and clearer exposition.

reviews.assessment: Clear and well-presented but narrowly tied to Chesson's theory, with unrealistic fast-evolution assumptions in rare populations.
strengths: analysis well presented and easy to follow
chosen examples stress the salient points

comments.issue: The manuscript is narrowly about Chesson's coexistence theory, and this strict application is less compelling than general evolution-coexistence interplay.
comments.request: Broaden the scope or justify the narrow focus and its interest.
comments.quote: While I feel that understanding the interplay of eco-evolutionary dynamics and coexistence is an important current topic, the strict application to Chesson’s coexistence is, in my opinion, less compelling.

comments.issue: Mutual invasibility only works for two species; general statements about coexistence in empirical systems are risky.
comments.request: Be careful with general coexistence statements; consider multispecies mechanisms.
comments.quote: I would be very careful in making general statements on coexistence in general in empirical systems

comments.issue: Previous works linking evolution and coexistence are mentioned only in passing, without their mechanisms.
comments.request: State the mechanisms at hand in previous works.
comments.quote: previous works are simply mentioned in passing, with mechanisms linking evolution and coexistence left uncovered

comments.issue: Fast adaptation of rare populations is unrealistic given drift and limited genetic variability, and cyclic dynamics reach unrealistic lows.
comments.request: Address the realism of fast evolution in rare populations.
comments.quote: A rare mutant, being rare by definition, would have its evolution dominated by genetic drift. Its adaptation is unlikely in most cases

comments.issue: The title is misleading: Chesson's theory is not prone to extinction, and the title is not explicit.
comments.request: Modify the title.
comments.quote: It may be a good idea to modify the title. Chesson’s theory is in no way prone to extinction.

comments.issue: Passages at lines 39-40, 41 and 204-205 are unclear or too narrow.
comments.request: Rewrite these unclear passages.
comments.quote: lines 39-40: this makes for a quite narrow issue. Rewrite?

comments.issue: The graphical construction method is not illustrated on the figure.
comments.request: Show the construction with arrows and possibly additional panels.
comments.quote: It would be good to show it on the figure, using arrows (and possibly additional panels, for instance one showing the construction along the x axis, and the other along the y axis)

comments.issue: Figure 2 uses species 1 and 2 while the caption uses species i and j.
comments.request: Homogenize species labels between figure and caption.
comments.quote: the figure mentions species 1 and 2, while the caption mentions species i and j. The authors may want to homogeneize.

reviews.assessment: Very well written and elegant, though it may read as a technical note; asks to highlight new insights.
strengths: nice unifying framework linking previous theory papers

comments.issue: Unclear whether the paper pushes the field forward or is a technical note; it provides no new insights or mechanisms.
comments.request: Highlight how this changes thinking about the topic and what new insights are gained.
comments.quote: My main concern is more about whether this is pushing the field forward or whether this is more a technical/theoretical note.

comments.issue: Criticizing previous models for not crossing the coexistence region is a straw man under transient dynamics.
comments.request: Make clear that the parameter space is not predictive of the outcome.
comments.quote: there is no reason to believe that the coexistence region has to be cross for species to coexist given that this region is based on equilibrium conditions

comments.issue: The framework cannot accurately predict equilibrium coexistence states, limiting its scope.
comments.quote: I understand why the proposed framework does not accurately predict equilibrium state when species coexistence at equilibrium, but this does make the framework more limited

comments.issue: The rapid-evolution assumption is hard to verify empirically; no rule of thumb links evolution rate to population changes.
comments.request: Ideally provide a rule of thumb for when rapid evolution applies.
comments.quote: Ideally we’d have some rule of thumb that links rate of evolution to population changes, so we can determine whether exclusion happens faster or slower than rapid evolution to save the system.

comments.issue: Figures use –ln(p) while the text uses NDEE for the same quantity.
comments.request: Use the main-equation expression as axis labels, or both.
comments.quote: In text and equations you mostly us NDEE while in the figures you use the term –ln(p). While both are the same thing, I would find it easier if you use the expression from the main equation as axis labels

comments.issue: The graphical inference steps at L266 are not linked to the underlying equations.
comments.request: Connect each graphical step to the respective equation term.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to link the steps to your respective equation.

comments.issue: Box 1 repeats well-known Chesson reviews and uses space that could hold novel material.
comments.request: Drop Box 1 or replace it with a reference to reviews and a worked example.
comments.quote: Box 1 is really unnecessary in my view. It's a review of Chesson's work, and there are already so many reviews

title: Integrating eco‐evolutionary dynamics and modern coexistence theory

editor_summary: Editor finds the review useful but a bit light; wants clarity on what 'complexity' means, on requiring correlation with biodiversity, on information versus geometric measures, and misses temperate reef literature.

strengths: information dimension development would be a step forward

comments.issue: The paper lacks a definition of complexity that explains how the metrics capture it.

comments.issue: Information-based and geometric measures are inappropriately compared; they measure fundamentally different things.

comments.issue: Requiring scale-free metrics while rejecting fractal dimension is inconsistent.

comments.quote: The authors seem to box themselves into a corner by requiring metrics to be scale-free, but then rejecting a fractal as a possible descriptor

comments.issue: Alternative spatial distribution models are not considered when dismissing fractal models.

comments.issue: Requiring correlation with biodiversity confuses the purpose of a complexity metric.

comments.quote: The authors require that an ideal metric be strongly correlated with biodiversity measures – this seems to miss the point of having a metric of habitat spatial distribution, which is to test the hypothesis that biodiversity is strongly constrained by either habitat geometry

reviews.assessment: Very well written, jargon-free review whose arguments seem sound; only asks for a real-world worked example.

comments.issue: No worked example shows whether the caveats matter in practice.
comments.request: Add a real-data worked example testing the practical impact.
comments.quote: My only suggestion is to include a worked example, ideally based on a ‘real world’ data set
