title: Strategy maps: Generalised giving‐up densities for optimal foraging

study.system: forested lake islands chronosequence; plants, herbivores, predators

editor_summary: Promising study with supportive reviewers, but field methods and analytical approaches need clarification before revision can be considered adequate.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important study, but the composite island-size variable, spatial correlation, unmeasured nutrient limitation and small SEM sample size leave causal conclusions uncertain.
strengths: interesting and important concept for ecology
extensive sampling across trophic levels supported by good analyses

comments.issue: Nutrient limitation is not measured or manipulated, so causal conclusions cannot be established (also L122, L133-134, L165, L341, L355).
comments.request: Measure nutrient availability directly or temper the causal claims.
comments.quote: The conclusions are drawn in the context of nutrient limitation, which has not been measured or manipulated separately, so it is not possible to establish causal relationships.

comments.issue: The composite island-size variable intertwines retrogression, island size, disturbance and fire frequency with nutrients.
comments.request: Untangle island size from retrogression and disturbance effects.
comments.quote: This composite variable raises my biggest concerns about whether there is an effect of retrogression or island size on nutrients and plant community composition and how it is intertwined with disturbance intensity and nutrients with fire frequency.

comments.issue: Adjacent lakes create spatial correlation that is not tested or modelled.
comments.request: Test for spatial correlation and use random effects or a hierarchical design.
comments.quote: There were two adjacent freshwater lakes, which argues for a random effect or hierarchical design. Spatial correlation could also be an issue? Has this been tested?

comments.issue: Thirty islands may be too few for the complex SEM to estimate parameters reliably.
comments.request: Justify the sample size for the SEM or simplify the model.
comments.quote: My final concern is the sample size (30 islands) in the analysis of SEM. I have always believed that SEM requires many data points to reliably estimate parameters unless the relationships within the data are relatively strong.

comments.issue: Retrogression disappears mid-paper and is used interchangeably with island size and unmeasured nutrient limitation.
comments.request: Clarify whether retrogression, island size and nutrient limitation are distinct concepts.
comments.quote: the concept of retrogression appears at the beginning, but then disappears later in the paper, only to reappear at the end. On the other hand, the results are interpreted from the perspective of island size and (unmeasured) nutrient limitation.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether predator biomass causes the trophic flip or is independent of retrogression.
comments.request: Explain the cause of the bottom-up to top-down flip and its relation to retrogression.
comments.quote: I wonder what the authors think caused the flip in tropical control? Is the increased biomass of predators a consequence of the retrogressive changes? Or are they independent? It is not clear to me from the text.

comments.issue: It is repeatedly unclear whether predators means birds or invertebrate predators (also L135, L265, L367, L424).
comments.request: Specify the predator group in each statement.
comments.quote: Also, in many places in the paper, it was difficult for me to understand what type of predators the authors were referring to: birds or invertebrate predators?

comments.issue: The weak effect of insectivorous birds on herbivores and invertebrate predators is not discussed.
comments.request: Add discussion of the weak bird effect.
comments.quote: I also miss a discussion of the weak effect of insectivorous birds on herbivores and invertebrate predators.

comments.issue: Predator abundance is treated as independent although it may depend on asynchronous dynamics of connected habitats.
comments.request: Justify the independence of predator abundance.
comments.quote: Is the variation in predator abundance really independent? The abundance of predators on a given islant may depend on the asynchronous dynamics of the two connected habitats, or other forested islands.

comments.issue: Temporal variability in invertebrate biomass and abundance is not reported or considered.
comments.request: Report temporal variability and its possible effect on conclusions.
comments.quote: Are there data on temporal variability in invertebrate biomass/abundance? How might this variability affect the conclusions?

comments.issue: High variability in invertebrate biomass and abundance may distort correlations.
comments.request: Assess whether this variability affects the correlations.
comments.quote: Line 229: With the high variability in invertebrate biomass and abundance, could this cause problems with correlations?

comments.issue: The average of the log ratio differs from the log ratio of averages.
comments.request: Acknowledge or correct the log-ratio calculation.
comments.quote: I just want to point out that the average of the log ratio is not the same as the log ratio of the averages.

comments.issue: The herbivory estimate is likely biased towards chewing herbivores.
comments.request: Check and discuss the bias in herbivory estimates.
comments.quote: Line 243: This estimate will be biased in favor of the chewing herbivores, will not it?

comments.issue: Lines 268-270 read like results but are placed elsewhere.
comments.request: Move this passage to the results.
comments.quote: Lines 268 - 270: This seems to be part of the results.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether predator biomass was categorical and what the ranges were.
comments.request: Describe the predator biomass categories and their ranges.
comments.quote: Line 272: Was a categorical value assigned to predator biomass? High, moderate and low? What were the exact ranges?

comments.issue: The total number of individuals and total weight do not match, suggesting some groups were excluded.
comments.request: Reconcile the totals or report only included insects.
comments.quote: Lines 296 - 299: Total number of individuals 18979 and total weight do not match (herbivores and predators). Were some groups excluded?

comments.issue: Figure references appear off by one (L314, L315, L316).
comments.request: Correct the figure references.
comments.quote: Line 314: Should not this be Fig. 5?

comments.issue: The statement that the effect could not be explained by herbivore biomass is confusing, and Figure 2 does not distinguish high and low pathways.
comments.request: Clarify the statement and annotate high/low pathways in Figure 2.
comments.quote: The authors write: "This effect could not be explained by the herbivore biomass". Do you mean that it can only be explained by it?

comments.issue: Testing the allochthonous-predator hypothesis requires abundance comparisons across trophic levels.
comments.request: Examine differences in abundance across trophic levels.
comments.quote: to test the plausibility of this hypothesis, differences in abundance at different tropical levels would need to be examined.

reviews.assessment: Impressive sampling effort with relevant questions, but unclear SEM feedback modeling, unsupported aquatic-subsidy claims, unrepresentative phytometers, and inconsistent figure/table presentation obscure the conclusions.

comments.issue: Phytometers are broad-leaved plants absent from the islands, so only generalists could use them, limiting generalization.
comments.request: Justify or replace the phytometer species and discuss the limitation.
comments.quote: I noticed the plants used are broad leaves not present in any of the islands. This limits the interpretation of the phytometer results, given only broad generalists would be able to switch host

comments.issue: The SEM feedback loop is incoherent: predator biomass affects herbivores yet is caused by them, and figures and tables disagree on path directions.
comments.request: Explain and consistently present the SEM specification and causality.
comments.quote: you add an interaction between plant and predator biomass causing herbivore biomass, but there is no effect of predator biomass, and that is actually caused by herbivore biomass. Feedback loops are not possible to determine is such a manner

comments.issue: The aquatic-community explanation is presented as a solid result in the conclusion without supporting data.
comments.request: Provide data or present the aquatic subsidy as speculation.
comments.quote: A large part of the discussion is dedicated to the role of aquatic communities influencing the results seen here. However, no data is presented to support this claim.

comments.issue: Figure numbers across the text do not match after a reorganization; the uncited Figure 4 is the most compelling evidence.
comments.request: Fix all figure numbering and cite Figure 4 correctly.
comments.quote: It looks like the manuscript went through some major reorganization that was not properly applied, with Figure numbers across the text not matching in any way.

comments.issue: Table 1 is never used and makes Figure 1 harder to read.
comments.request: Use or remove Table 1.
comments.quote: Additionally, Table 1 is not used in any way in the results or discussion, and makes reading Fig. 1 harder, not easier.

comments.issue: The number of excluded individuals at line 207 is not given.

comments.issue: Exact sample sizes per treatment group and assurance of genetic variation sampling are missing at line 215.

comments.issue: 'Assay status' at line 241 should read 'immune assay status'.

comments.issue: An energy/amino-acid trade-off between encapsulation and pathogen defence could explain Figure 3 and growth differences.

title: Use of an exotic host plant reduces viral burden in a native insect herbivore

study.system: plant-pollinator networks; individual-level interactions, SW Spain

reviews.assessment: Exciting results of broad interest from an impressive dataset; clarifications needed on methods terminology, taxonomic resolution and result contextualisation.

comments.issue: The method for partitioning networks by variation level is hard to follow and uses 'high'/'low' inconsistently.
comments.request: Add a preamble and reframe the sets as percentiles of flower production.
comments.quote: The description of how the authors partitioned networks by level of variation needs to be clarified, as it is currently difficult to digest

comments.issue: The term 'degree' is unintuitive and could confuse readers.
comments.request: Use 'pollinator richness' or 'relative specialization' instead.
comments.quote: while I understand the use of the term “degree” in a network context (e.g., line 144), the authors may also consider using a more intuitive phrase, such as “pollinator richness” or “relative specialization.”

comments.issue: Calling taxa species is misleading because only 27% of pollinators were identified to species.
comments.request: Use 'morphotype', move Table S2 to the main text and list taxa.
comments.quote: The use of the terms morphospecies and species is misleading. While I am sure this is not the intention of the authors, less than one third of the pollinators observed were IDed to species (27% as per the supplement).

comments.issue: Values for beta diversity, CV and skewness are reported without context or comparison.
comments.request: Provide ranges and interpretation rather than isolated averages.
comments.quote: In the results section, there are several values given on their own that need to be contextualized for better interpretation.

comments.issue: 'Significance' is treated as yes/no instead of reporting exact p-values and effect sizes.
comments.request: Report exact p-values and effect sizes for these tests.
comments.quote: It would be more useful for the authors to provide exact p-values and effect sizes for these tests.

comments.issue: The conservation/restoration discussion is abrupt and overreaches, claiming support for specific strategies.
comments.request: Soften the applied claims and improve the transition.
comments.quote: The authors should also be careful not to overreach here. Lines 484-485 states that this paper supports specific restoration strategies, which does not reflect the objectives or analytical approach of the study.

comments.issue: The introduction's plant-pollinator network paragraph has a disjointed flow.
comments.request: Start the second paragraph with the content around line 90.
comments.quote: The introduction of plant-pollinator networks in the second paragraph, before pivoting away to networks broadly, then back to plants and pollinators felt disjointed.

comments.issue: The connection between global change, population homogenisation and the study is not made explicit.
comments.request: Make this connection explicit.
comments.quote: Here, I believe the authors are suggesting that global change is making populations more homogenous. If this is correct, the authors should consider explicitly making this connection.

comments.issue: 'Key plant trait' is not clearly identified.
comments.request: Clarify which trait is meant.
comments.quote: Line 141: Please clarify what “key plant trait” is referenced here.

comments.issue: The wording implies separate systems although all sites belong to one system.
comments.request: Reword accordingly.
comments.quote: Line 155: Consider rewording slightly as these sites are all in the same system.

comments.issue: 'Completely captured' is unclear in this context.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning.
comments.quote: Line 232: I am unclear what “completely captured” means in this context, it would be helpful for the authors to clarify.

comments.issue: The null model used in bipartite is not specified.
comments.request: State which null model was used.
comments.quote: Line 242: The authors could consider including what null model in bipartite they used.

comments.issue: The number of parameters or the parameter-to-data ratio is not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of parameters or their ratio to data points.
comments.quote: Line 321: It would be useful for the authors to make a statement about ratio of parameters to data points, or at least the number of parameters.

comments.issue: 'Interestingly' reads as persuasive rather than neutral.
comments.request: Remove or rephrase the emotional emphasis.
comments.quote: While I believe the authors intended that “interestingly” provide emphasis here, the emotional tone instead comes across as persuasive.

comments.issue: The wording at line 354 is cumbersome.
comments.request: Simplify, e.g. to 'individual plant traits'.
comments.quote: Line 354: Cumbersome wording, consider rephrasing for clarity. For example, “set of traits of plant individuals” could be simplified to “individual plant traits.”

comments.issue: The ideas at lines 445-452 are tenuous and need more depth and an example.
comments.request: Add depth and an illustrative example.
comments.quote: Line 445-452: These ideas are nice, but in their current form are a bit tenuous. Please provide some more depth and perhaps an example to help clarify the ideas.

comments.issue: The statement at line 455 lacks a citation.
comments.request: Add a citation.
comments.quote: Line 455: Please add a citation for this statement.

comments.issue: Whether floral abundance is an independent trait or simply plant size is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss plant size and the independence of floral abundance.
comments.quote: Line 463: Please discuss the potential importance of plant size here. Is floral abundance really an independent trait, or is it simply the size of the plant?

comments.issue: The ideas on the niche continuum need further unpacking.
comments.request: Unpack these ideas further.
comments.quote: Line 466: It would be useful for the authors to further unpack these ideas on the niche continuum.

comments.issue: The extinction-rate citation is 25 years old.
comments.request: Update with a more recent reference.
comments.quote: Line 504: The citation for “current” extinction rates is 25 years old. Consider updating with a more recent reference.

comments.issue: 'Degree' is not defined in the Table 1 and Figure 3 captions.
comments.request: Define 'degree' in the captions or use another term.
comments.quote: Table 1 & Figure 3: The authors should provide a definition of “degree” in these captions or choose another term (see above).

reviews.assessment: Interesting but under-studied idea; questions whether neighbour measurements are independent and whether nestedness results hold when controlling for network size.
strengths: scarce attention to intraspecific variability effects

comments.issue: Neighbour cover may not be independent across individuals sampled on the same plot, affecting degree and niche overlap.
comments.request: Account for or discuss this non-independence among neighbours.
comments.quote: considering that several individuals of the same plant species were sampled on the same plot, these might not have independent conspecific and heterospecific neighbor measurements

comments.issue: Nestedness is not independent of network size, so results may not hold when size is controlled.
comments.request: Test whether the results hold when controlling for network size.
comments.quote: the authors use a measurement of nestedness that, according to Song et al. (JAE 2017, ´Why are some plant–pollinator networks more nested than others?´), is not independent of network size.

comments.issue: 'Plant variation' is not defined: phenotypic variation or partner use?
comments.request: Specify what variation is meant.
comments.quote: L50: what plant variation are you referring to here? Phenotypic variation? Partner use variation?

comments.issue: 'Intraspecific variation' is used without specifying what varies.
comments.request: Be more specific.
comments.quote: L52: again, what do you mean by ´intraspecific variation´? Please be more specific.

comments.issue: It is unclear that resources refer to reproduction rather than feeding.
comments.request: Clarify that reproductive resources are meant.
comments.quote: L84: It might be worth clarifying you refer to resources for reproduction (and not feeding resources).

comments.issue: It is unclear whether partner variation or morphological traits are meant at line 98.
comments.request: Clarify which is meant.
comments.quote: L98: are you referring here to partner variation among individuals or about morphological traits?

comments.issue: The meaning of 'plant traits' is unclear and morphological traits are not developed in the introduction.
comments.request: Develop this literature in the introduction, citing Dai et al. 2016.
comments.quote: Morphological traits and their potential influence on species interactions has not been clearly developed in the introduction.

comments.issue: Individual-based networks per species and plot could reveal environmental and spatial effects.
comments.request: Build such networks and assess environmental variation.
comments.quote: L177: would it be possible to build an individual-based network for each plant species for each plot and then be able to assess the effects of environmental variation?

comments.issue: It is not explained that interactions refer to interactions per time after standardisation.
comments.request: Explain this in the main text.
comments.quote: L280: it might be worth explaining in the main text that due to your standardisation method for interactions you will refer to interactions per time.

comments.issue: The choice of binary rather than quantitative interaction networks is not justified.
comments.request: Justify using binary networks.
comments.quote: L293: why not quantitative interaction networks?

comments.issue: Other plant traits such as height and phenology are not addressed.
comments.request: Explain what happened to these other traits.
comments.quote: L354: what about the other plant traits (i.e., plant height and phenology)?

comments.issue: Flower production per individual may not be independent of plant species abundance in the plot.
comments.request: Check whether abundant species also produce more flowers per individual.
comments.quote: L380: was the flower production per individual independent from the plant species abundance in the plot?

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the angle and breadth, but wants the niche overlap definition justified and the disparate methods better united.
strengths: careful quantification of individual-level pollinator visits
angle and breadth of the study

comments.issue: The niche overlap definition (Bray-Curtis similarity from Dorman et al.) is not justified or discussed conceptually.
comments.request: Justify the metric and place it among existing niche overlap definitions.
comments.quote: One important aspect that could use some more justification is how Niche Overlap between individuals was defined. It seems like the working definition used by the authors stems from Dorman et al.’s (2008) work, but this is only briefly touched on.

comments.issue: Saavedra et al.'s structural niche overlap could have been used instead of Bray-Curtis similarity.
comments.request: Consider using or discussing Saavedra's structural niche overlap.
comments.quote: Since the authors use the feasibility concept for the last part of their paper, it had me wondering if something akin to Saavedra’s structural niche overlap could have been used instead of a Bray Curtis similarity index.

comments.issue: Similarity metrics differ across analyses (Jaccard in feasibility vs Bray-Curtis earlier), fragmenting the methods.
comments.request: Unite the frameworks or explain why not and note limitations.
comments.quote: the use of a Jaccard similarity index in the feasibility section instead of a Bray-Curtis distance earlier

comments.issue: 'Generalized individual' is unusual terminology.
comments.request: Use 'specialists' and 'generalists' instead.
comments.quote: I am surprised by the expression “generalized individual”. I understand that the structure mimics “specialized individual”, but “generalized” is not usually used in this context.

comments.issue: The statement at line 70 needs more, recent citations.
comments.request: Add citations such as Violle et al. 2012.
comments.quote: this could use a few more citations, including recent ones. Violle et al. (2012) comes to my mind, but I am sure there are others.

comments.issue: Seven line-level copy edits and typos.
comments.quote: Line 470: this should read “It has been previously demonstrated that there is a”

comments.issue: The nature of the problem at lines 105-106 is imprecise.
comments.request: Be more precise about the problem.
comments.quote: can the authors be a little more precise here about what the problem is? In their paper, it seems somewhat straightforward to do (basically using some weighted average of the individual links).

comments.issue: How 'aggregating' is done in practice is not defined.
comments.request: Define the aggregation procedure.
comments.quote: It could be useful to define how “aggregating” (regularly comes up in the text) is done in practice, even if it is straightforward.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 136-138 is difficult to read.
comments.request: Rewrite it more clearly.
comments.quote: that sentence doesn’t read super well (I keep wondering where the verb is); it could be rewritten more clearly.

comments.issue: Neighbour cover is listed as a plant trait but is not a property of individual organisms.
comments.request: Do not treat neighbour cover as a trait.
comments.quote: Since traits are usually defined as properties of individual organisms that can be measured, I would be hesitant in calling these “traits”.

comments.issue: The introduction of 'flowering synchrony' at line 188 is confusing.
comments.request: Reword, e.g. starting with 'We also calculated...'.
comments.quote: I was confused about “flowering synchrony”, since the sentence structure made me think it had been introduced before (even though it hadn’t).

comments.issue: 'Pollinator assemblage' first appears without definition.
comments.request: Define the concept when first introduced.
comments.quote: This is the first time “pollinator assemblage” is mentioned. Does it refer to lines 173-175? Maybe defining the concept up there could improve clarity.

comments.issue: Calling Bray-Curtis distance 'pairwise beta-diversity' may not be standard.
comments.request: Add a supporting reference.
comments.quote: is it standard to refer to such Bray Curtis distance between pollinator assemblages as a “pairwise beta-diversity”? Maybe a reference could be added?

comments.issue: Why binary networks and qualitative overlap replace the available quantitative visitation data is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the loss of quantitative information.
comments.quote: why do we rely on a binary plant-pollinator interaction networks for the feasibility part of the study and compute a qualitative overlap, when we earlier had the full information on flower visitation frequency and could compute a quantitative overlap?

comments.issue: Coefficient of variation receives only one line while skewness and kurtosis are discussed extensively.
comments.request: Interpret the coefficient of variation more.
comments.quote: the authors discuss their results on skewness and kurtosis a lot, while only devoting one line to the coefficient of variation. Can’t we say/interpret more about CV?

comments.issue: 'Many individuals' is misleading; Fig 4 describes a few extreme individuals.
comments.request: Reword to match the figure legend.
comments.quote: maybe the “many individuals” is slightly misleading? Like the legend of Fig 4 says, "a few plant individuals that play extreme roles" so "many" might not be the word.

comments.issue: The feasibility formula is not given and gamma_ij is mislabelled as y_ij.
comments.request: Fix the labelling and add a precise formula.
comments.quote: Also, it wouldn’t hurt to have the sentence “Therefore, we calculated the size of the feasibility domain by exponentiating the feasibility value by the inverse of the number of species in the community” accompanied by a precise formula.

title: Intraspecific variation in species interactions promotes the feasibility of mutualistic assemblages

study.system: bean plants, aphids and parasitoids; root exudate bioassays

editor_summary: Reviewers are generally positive but raise substantial suggestions; editor asks to make data and R code publicly available and is unsure the study is fully reproducible.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and novel, with a comprehensive set of experiments, but the identification of L-DOPA as 'the' signal and the ecological relevance need more support.
strengths: potentially highly novel contribution to plant-plant communication
comprehensive and logical set of experiments

comments.issue: Conclusion that L-DOPA is 'the' signal is unsupported; compounds underlying other chromatogram peaks were not tested.
comments.request: Test the other candidate peaks/compounds and report their effects.
comments.quote: it was unclear to me how the authors arrived at the conclusion that it is “the” signal

comments.issue: Second highly active fraction 1d is ignored and its compounds could equally contribute to the effects.
comments.request: Analyse compounds in fraction 1d or explain why they can be excluded.
comments.quote: their guided fractionation approach yields a second highly active fraction “1d” that seems to be ignored in the rest of the paper. Were compounds from this fraction analysed?

comments.issue: Application procedure and rationale for the chosen 0.1/0.01 ppm concentrations are unclear.
comments.request: Explain how concentrations were chosen and how they relate to exuded amounts.
comments.quote: And does it mean that we are not dealing with concentrations as they are exuded by the roots, but with “chosen” concentrations of 0.1 or 0.01 ppm? How were these chosen?

comments.issue: Hydroponics and sterile soil prevent microbial breakdown, likely overestimating the signal's field role.
comments.request: Discuss this limitation and the field relevance of the set-up.
comments.quote: these experiments were performed in hydroponics or sterile soil. This means that signaling molecules that, in field situations, would be easily broken down by members of the soil microbial community

comments.issue: Whether L-DOPA can travel through the soil matrix to neighbouring plants is unknown.
comments.request: Address L-DOPA mobility in soil and its ecological relevance.
comments.quote: is L-DOPA a compound that would easily travel through the soil matrix to a neighbouring plant?

comments.issue: Realism of using 100 aphids on a young bean plant is not addressed.
comments.request: Justify the aphid density used.
comments.quote: is 100 aphids on a young bean plant a realistic density?

comments.issue: The phrase 'before testing' is unclear because the set-up has not yet been explained.
comments.request: Clarify what 'before testing' refers to.
comments.quote: Unclear what “before testing” refers to as the set-up has not yet been explained.

comments.issue: Plant age at the time of infestation is not reported.
comments.request: State the age of plants when infested.
comments.quote: What age were plants at the time of infestation?

comments.issue: The PHC solution (P+A?) is not defined.
comments.request: Define the PHC solution.
comments.quote: What is PHC solution? P+A?

comments.issue: How L-DOPA was applied to the soil is not described.
comments.request: Describe the soil application method.
comments.quote: How was L-DOPA applied to the soil?

comments.issue: 'On the contrary' mischaracterizes the results; the volatiles are upregulated but not significantly.
comments.request: Correct the statement.
comments.quote: Why do you say “On the contrary”? The volatiles that you are mentioning next are upregulated, just like the volatiles that you mentioned before

comments.issue: Fig. 2B was converted from histogram to line plot but legends were not adjusted.
comments.request: Use different line colours, explain them next to the panel, and remove 'histogram'.
comments.quote: It looks like this figure has been converted from a histogram to a line bar but the legends have not been adjusted.

comments.issue: Stray line numbers/footers from a previous version plus four line-level grammar fixes.
comments.request: Remove the stray material and apply the grammar corrections.
comments.quote: It looks like here and there line numbers and footers of a previous version have been accidentally copied into the text (line 119, 188-189). Please remove.

reviews.assessment: Very positive; the only request is to discuss the ecological and evolutionary meaning of this communication.
strengths: interesting and very well executed study
careful analysis and experimentation in Fig. 1
convincing evidence for L-DOPA as an underground messenger

comments.issue: Discussion should address the communication's ecological and evolutionary meaning; benefit to the signaller is assumed, not established.
comments.request: Discuss the broader ecological and evolutionary context, including conspecific-only limitation.
comments.quote: The paper assumes this is beneficiary for the signalling plant, but such communication may not be always mutualistic between the individual players

comments.issue: Parasitoid biology nuance is missing: parasitized hosts keep feeding, though parasitism can reduce aphid population growth.
comments.request: Discuss these parasitoid dynamics in the broader context.
comments.quote: parasitoids, in contrast to predators, often do not reduce herbivory as their parasitised host continues in feeding, sometimes even longer than a healthy host

title: L‐DOPA functions as a plant pheromone for belowground anti‐herbivory communication

study.system: theory synthesis; fitness value of information in variable environments

editor_summary: Positive and well written; engage with Gil's referenced papers, keep Box 1 math but add schematics by trimming Figure 1, and fix several figure/caption issues.

reviews.assessment: Likes the FVOI review but questions what is new, wants the species-interaction work removed from this synthesis, and found Box 1 unclear.
strengths: discussion of information stored in phenotypes

comments.issue: Unclear how much prior quantitative FVOI work exists and whether the Box 1 ideas are new or review.
comments.request: Clarify what was already done versus new, and what remains for the future.
comments.quote: I’m not entirely sure how much previous work has been done quantitatively using FVOI. I’m not entirely sure whether the ideas from box one are new or part of the review.

comments.issue: Species-interaction material occupies three of five figures and one of two boxes, disproportionate and out of place in a synthesis.
comments.request: Significantly remove this part of the work from the review.
comments.quote: From my understanding, there was no prior work on this, however, three of the 5 figures and one of the two boxes are dedicated to this aspect solely.

comments.issue: Figure 2 shows unlimited growth; unclear whether informed species reach higher abundance or the same abundance faster.
comments.request: Add self-limitation and explain the expected abundance outcome.
comments.quote: Figure 2 shows how two communities would differ if they do or do not use information, however, the growth seems to be unlimited.

comments.issue: Connections between Box 1 and Figure 1 are unclear; equation terms lack graphical representations.
comments.request: Improve the link between Box 1 and Figure 1 with graphical representations of each term.
comments.quote: I have the impression that one could improve the connections between box1 and figure 1 to improve clarity, especially to people less familiar with entropy and KL-divergence.

comments.issue: Box 1 is hard to follow; the role of x(e) versus r_e is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what x(e) is and why it is needed in addition to r_e.
comments.quote: Specifically, I did not understand what x(e) is. Mathematically, it depends only on e, but so does r_e, so why do you need both terms?

comments.issue: Abbreviations for information theory and mutual information are unnecessary and confusing.
comments.request: Do not abbreviate information theory and mutual information.
comments.quote: L91: I don’t think it’s worth to abbreviate information theory and mutual information, you use them rarely but will likely lead to confusion

comments.issue: Mutual information could be mistaken for a correlation; this should be clarified early.
comments.request: Mention early that MI is not a correlation.
comments.quote: I initially thought that MI is a correlation, might be worth to mention that it is not

comments.issue: Box 1 is introduced too late for readers to encounter it early.
comments.request: Mention Box 1 earlier in the manuscript.
comments.quote: You should mention box 1 earlier in general in hope that a reader might read it early.

comments.issue: Notation P(E|C) = 0 misleadingly suggests zero probability rather than no information.
comments.request: Use notation that does not suggest a probability of zero.
comments.quote: I find this notation very suboptimal, as p suggests a probability, so I would interpret P(E|C) = 0 to imply that there’s a zero chance, not no information.

comments.issue: FVOI and MI are not explicitly visible in Figure 1.
comments.request: Revise Figure 1 so FVOI and MI are explicitly visible.
comments.quote: FVOI and MI are not explicitly visible in figure 1, please change accordingly

comments.issue: A stated result may simply follow from Jensen's inequality, making the point trivial.
comments.request: Clarify whether the result is more than a Jensen inequality consequence.
comments.quote: Isn’t this always the case because of the Jensen inequality? Assuming sum(odds) =1 -> 1/sum(1/odds)<1

comments.issue: What has been done theoretically, empirically and suggestively about MI is not stated clearly.
comments.request: State more clearly what has been done theoretically, empirically and suggestively.
comments.quote: I think it youl help the reader if you state more clearly what has been done, theoretically, empirically and just suggestively.

comments.issue: The coexistence/competition section is too much new work and too little review.
comments.request: Remove this part from the review and use it elsewhere.
comments.quote: As mentioned before, I would remove this part from the review, it seems to much additional work and to little review.

comments.issue: Expected prisoner's-dilemma-like dynamics and a stronger negative storage effect are not considered.
comments.request: Consider whether mutual information use worsens both species via stronger competition.
comments.quote: I initially would have expected that if both species use information we would see a similar effect as in the prisoner’s dilemma.

comments.issue: Unclear whether FVOI based on phenotypic distributions is immune to informational traps.
comments.request: Clarify whether phenotypic-distribution FVOI escapes such traps.
comments.quote: Would it be correct to assume that FVOI based on phenotypic distributions are immune to such traps

comments.issue: Box 2 leaves too many details in the appendix.
comments.request: Remove Box 2.
comments.quote: I think there are way to many details left out/in the appendix. I suggest you remove this box.

reviews.assessment: Praises the framework as an important theoretical contribution, asking only for discussion of data availability plus a few references and figure fixes.
strengths: well suited to a top-tier journal

comments.issue: Applicability of the framework is unclear because the empirical data needed to estimate FVOI are difficult to obtain.
comments.request: Discuss data availability and feasibility across a diversity of ecological systems.
comments.quote: it is not clear how generally applicable this modeling framework will be to ecological systems (at least in the near term) because of the difficulty of acquiring empirical insights

comments.issue: Gil et al. (2017) already models how species interactions mediate the fitness value of information.
comments.request: Cite and discuss Gil et al. (2017).
comments.quote: There is an additional theoretical work that seems particularly appropriate to this synthesis that is not currently cited: Gil et al. AmNat (2017)

comments.issue: Gil et al. (Ecology) 2019 offers a distinct information-mediated coexistence mechanism relevant to the coexistence discussion.
comments.request: Discuss this alternative coexistence mechanism.
comments.quote: this was the major focus of Gil et al. (Ecology) 2019, which is cited elsewhere and which provides a distinct information-mediated coexistence mechanism than the one discussed in this paragraph

comments.issue: Gil et al. (PNAS) 2020 shows social information use can increase collapse risk under anthropogenic change.
comments.request: Mention this paper in the changing-world subsection.
comments.quote: Gil et al. (PNAS) 2020, which describes how, through positive density dependence, social information use can leave consumer communities and, consequently, ecosystems at greater risk of collapse

comments.issue: Figure 3 panels are out of order.
comments.request: Reorder the Figure 3 panels.
comments.quote: Fig. 3 panels are out of order.

comments.issue: Figure 5 caption does not point readers to Box 2.
comments.request: Reference Box 2 in the Figure 5 caption.
comments.quote: Fig. 5: I would reference Box 2 in the caption, so the reader can easily find the motivating text for this figure.

comments.issue: A leftover parenthetical placeholder about Mary's refs remains in the text.
comments.request: Replace the parenthetical with the actual references.
comments.quote: I’d replace the parenthetical with Mary’s refs :).

reviews.assessment: Likes the ideas and the coexistence connection but finds the information-theory presentation hard to follow and parts of the framework misleading.
strengths: efforts to connect to coexistence models

comments.issue: The manuscript is difficult to read and may be hard to convey to a general audience.
comments.request: Improve readability and accessibility for general readers.
comments.quote: work on information theory can be difficult to read. I had to read this manuscript several times understand the thrust of the argument.

comments.issue: The notion of information is used inconsistently, shifting between general information processing and population growth under uncertainty.
comments.request: Circumscribe clearly how the notion of information is used.
comments.quote: Circumscribe how you use the notion information. Sometimes the manuscript describes general issues of information theory/processing, but in other places the focus is on population growth under uncertainty.

comments.issue: Previous work on stochastic population growth and bet hedging is only lightly touched on in the introduction.
comments.request: Emphasize this previous work and its limitations in the introduction.
comments.quote: previous work is touched on lightly in the intro and reviewed extensively in the centre of the review

comments.issue: Box 1 derivations are challenging to follow.
comments.request: Simplify Box 1 and describe KL-divergence and mutual information qualitatively.
comments.quote: The derivations in box 1 are challenging to follow. I’d just refer readers to Cover and Thomas, and use this space to qualitatively describe KL-divergence and mutual information.

comments.issue: The uniform maximum-entropy baseline is unjustified because many variables, like precipitation, are unbounded and organisms may not default to uniform.
comments.request: Justify the uniform baseline biologically or compare against an arbitrary strategy.
comments.quote: The uniform is only the maximum entropy state for variables that are bounded (i.e. between 0 and 1) the example of precipitation provided in the figures is unbounded

comments.issue: The opening paragraph never defines information, so the boundary with uncertainty and bet hedging is unclear.
comments.request: Define information and clarify where uncertainty and bet hedging begin.
comments.quote: it doesn’t actually define information and that makes it hard to spot the precise problem you are tackling here

comments.issue: The specific problem addressed by equation 3 is not motivated from bet-hedging and variability work.
comments.request: Motivate equation 3 and show how information theory improves on bet-hedging approaches.
comments.quote: I think even here you need to motivate the specific problem described in equation (3). If possible, explain how previous approaches to bet hedging/variability could be improved using tools from information theory.

comments.issue: The claim that information theory lacks biological meaning or value is contrary to intuition; information quantifies uncertainty.
comments.request: Reconsider and rephrase the claim about information's biological meaning or value.
comments.quote: This runs contrary to my intuition. In my opinion, information doesn’t have biological meaning or value in and of itself, it quantifies uncertainty.

comments.issue: The explanation of why information theory is useful is underdeveloped and would be stronger against a published non-IT model.
comments.request: Introduce a published model without IT, its limits, then show how IT clarifies it.
comments.quote: here is the explanation of why information theory could be useful, but I think the idea is underdeveloped

comments.issue: It is unclear whether strategies in the species-indexed equation act on species, individuals or genotypes, and p is not indexed by species.
comments.request: Clarify the indexing and what strategies act on.
comments.quote: L189- the equation is indexed by species, but are you intending for different strategies to act on species, individuals or genotypes? Also, your equation for “p” (195) doesn’t index by species?

comments.issue: It is not explained that the growth rate discussed is the geometric mean growth rate.
comments.request: Explain that this is the geometric mean growth rate.
comments.quote: L199- Is it worth explaining this is the geometric mean growth rate?

comments.issue: Uncorrelated is used at L229 where independent is used elsewhere.
comments.request: Use terminology consistently.
comments.quote: L229 Here you use uncorrelated, elsewhere independent?

comments.issue: KL divergence is treated as a distance although it violates the triangle inequality.
comments.request: Acknowledge that KL divergence is not a distance.
comments.quote: 235- Some IT folks insist that KL divergence is not a distance, because it does not obey the triangle inequality.

comments.issue: The indexing by species, environmental states and cue at L247 is hard to parse.
comments.request: Make the indexing explicit and easy to follow.
comments.quote: L247 I’m having a hard time parsing the indexing, I personally want indexing for species, environmental states and the cue, because these are all described and it is easy to get confused at each indexing step.

comments.issue: The GitHub repository was not accessible to the reviewer.
comments.request: Ensure the repository is publicly accessible.
comments.quote: I couldn’t get access to the github repository, so I apologize if it is hidden there.

comments.issue: The summary of existing models does not explain their limitations that information theory could address.
comments.request: Explain the limitations of existing models that IT might address.
comments.quote: 261-277 This summary is good, but it could be even better if you explained the limitations of existing models which might be addressed with information theory.

comments.issue: Indexing between species, populations and decisions at 289-306 is confusing.
comments.request: Start with one entity to reduce indexing confusion.
comments.quote: 289-306 Here again, I get indexing confused between species, populations, “decisions”. I suggest starting with one.

comments.issue: No biological example of a naive bettor is given, and organisms may use heuristics rather than the maxent solution.
comments.request: Give an ecological example and evidence for maxent behaviour.
comments.quote: L307 Give an example of a naiive bettor in ecology. Do organisms actually ever use the maxent solution? Behavioural econonomics makes quite clear that human agents use heuristics instead of a maxent solution

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the model concerns environmental states or organismal actions.
comments.request: Clarify whether environmental states or actions are modelled.
comments.quote: L319 are you interested in the states of the environment or the actions of the organism?

comments.issue: The claim that information typically increases mean fitness ignores models where relative fitness gains cost absolute fitness.
comments.request: Qualify the claim about information increasing population mean fitness.
comments.quote: 402-403, I’m not convinced that information typically increases population mean fitness. Presumably there are are models where strategies can use information to maximize relative fitness at the expense of absolute fitness.

comments.issue: Social information is not defined in the main text.
comments.request: Define social information in the main text.
comments.quote: 470 Main text should define social information.

comments.issue: Shannon entropy of the environment is not clearly defined.
comments.request: Clarify what the Shannon entropy of the environment means.
comments.quote: 718 I’m not sure Shannon entropy of the environment is clearly defined. Do you mean the uncertainty in time t of what strategy is best?

comments.issue: Figure 1 is too complex; a categorical variable would make the arithmetic easier to picture.
comments.request: Simplify Figure 1 using a categorical variable and simpler icons.
comments.quote: I think figure 1 should be simpflied. It would be easier to picutre the arithmetic if you replaced the continous variable (rain) with a categorical variable (wet/dry).

title: The fitness value of ecological information in a variable world

study.system: 14 herbaceous plant species; field competition experiment, IPMs, elevation gradient

editor_summary: Editor highlights the novelty of translating competition effects into demography across an elevation gradient; asks to state the main hypothesis in the introduction, highlight main findings in the discussion, and make the title catchier.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, intuitive study, but the impact of competition on lambda appears incorrectly calculated and competitor density is artificial.
strengths: growth as the biggest competition effect lines up with previous research
large species set in controlled experiments

comments.issue: The authors call 'complementary' what the cited literature calls 'compensation', confusing readers.
comments.request: Use the established term 'compensation' instead.
comments.quote: Much (maybe all) of the work the authors cite have used the term “compensation” to describe what the authors call “complementary”. Why the sudden change in terminology? For clarity, I’d suggest using the same term as the existing literature.

comments.issue: Competitor density in the experiment is inherently artificial, so the full impact of competition cannot be quantified.
comments.request: Determine the natural density range and adjust population growth estimates accordingly.
comments.quote: given the experimental design the density of the competitors is inherently artificial. Is there any way to know what a natural range of variation in the density of these species is and adjust the population growth estimate accordingly?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 'allometric models' would be a more appropriate term.
comments.request: Consider using the term 'allometric models'.
comments.quote: 151: Would the term allometric models be more appropriate here?

comments.issue: How lambda was calculated is not stated.
comments.request: State whether lambda is the dominant eigenvalue of the discretized IPM under the stable size distribution.
comments.quote: 166: How was lambda calculated? As the dominant eigenvalue of the discretized IPM, assuming stable size distribution (SSD)?

comments.issue: Calling lambda an invasion growth rate conflicts with the stable size distribution assumption.
comments.request: Use 'low-density' instead of 'invasion growth rate'.
comments.quote: Can it really be called an invasion growth rate if we assume the population has already reached SSD, even if at low density? Maybe just using “low-density” would be most appropriate?

comments.issue: The impact of competition on lambda uses a difference instead of a ratio or log difference, biasing comparisons across lambda values.
comments.request: Recalculate the impact as a ratio or log difference.
comments.quote: Since population growth is multiplicative this difference should be the ratio, or log difference between the two IPMS. Otherwise you would inherently see larger differences at larger lambda values.

comments.issue: The Figure S4 standardization by the sum of population growth estimates has no clear meaning.
comments.request: Justify or replace the standardization and write the equation in the methods.
comments.quote: But it does seem a little weird to rescale by the sum of the two population growth estimates. What does that mean? Using the example above (1-2)/(1+2)=-0.333. What does the -0.333 mean?

comments.issue: A 55% decrease is probably not the correct interpretation of the Figure S4 equation.
comments.request: Correct the percentage interpretation of the competition effect.
comments.quote: 244: Similar to above, If the equation I’m not sure a 55% decrease in population growth is the correct interpretation of the equation used to create Figure S4.

comments.issue: The basis for determining competitive exclusion or persistence from a single asymptotic growth estimate is not described.
comments.request: Explain how exclusion and persistence were determined.
comments.quote: I’m curious what the basis for determining competitive exclusion (or not) or population persistence was? This wasn’t really covered in the methods or supplement.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether vital rates vary randomly or in response to factors that do not covary with competition.
comments.request: Clarify what drives variation in the vital rates.
comments.quote: 404: Vary randomly? Or they vary in response to other factors (e.g. abiotic conditions) that do not covary with competition.

reviews.assessment: Important, well-written study that underplays its relevance; terminology and discussion emphasis need fixing.
strengths: remarkably well written and easy to follow

comments.issue: The authors use 'complementarity' instead of the established term 'demographic compensation'.
comments.request: Revert to 'demographic compensation' throughout.
comments.quote: First, I do not understand why the authors use the term "complementarity" instead of "demographic compensation". I believed "demographic compensation" was now established in the literature (Doak & Morris 2010; Villellas et al. 2015; Sheth & Angert 2018).

comments.issue: There is no introductory or final discussion paragraph emphasizing the main findings or hypotheses.
comments.request: Add opening/closing discussion paragraphs that emphasize the main findings.
comments.quote: You do not have an introductory or final discussion paragraph to emphasize your main scientific findings or hypotheses. Right now, you seem to emphasize only the advantages of studying competition using the entire life cycle of species.

comments.issue: Discussion paragraphs lack clear topic sentences and often bury the main finding at the end.
comments.request: Put main findings at the start of paragraphs and explain the interpretation.
comments.quote: Throughout the discussion, you do not emphasize your main findings with clear topic sentences at the beginning of each paragraph. Rather, your discussion has a discursive structure which at times reminds of a results section.

comments.issue: The claim that competition is size asymmetric is not accompanied by any mechanism, such as light competition.
comments.request: Discuss the mechanisms of asymmetric competition and test whether light competition explains it.
comments.quote: In the first paragraph of the discussion, you suggest that competition is size asymmetric. What are the mechanisms by which this could happen? Asymmetric competition usually results from light competition. Could this be the case in your experiment?

comments.issue: The claim that low-elevation species are 'faster' is not supported by any metrics, and Figure S7 shows species are very similar.
comments.request: Support the claim with metrics such as generation time or longevity.
comments.quote: However, what metrics do you have to support this claim? Could you for example employ generation time, longevity, or other metrics (e.g. those used in Franco & Silvertown 2004)?

comments.issue: 'Complementary responses' is not defined at first use.
comments.request: Define it as a compensatory response at first use.
comments.quote: 37-38: "complementary responses" is not defined. People will not understand it is a compensatory response (positive response that partially offset negative responses).

comments.issue: The last sentence of the aim is too generic.
comments.request: Specify, e.g. 'investigate the full life cycle of species'.
comments.quote: 40-41: This last sentence is too generic. Maybe you should say something like "investigate the full life cycle of species".

comments.issue: The model fitting information comes out of the blue and is insufficient for the average reader.
comments.request: Give a cursory explanation of the rationale and structure of the analyses.
comments.quote: This model fitting information comes out of the blue. I understand that you refer to Lyu & Alexander, but this is insufficient for the average reader. Please provide a cursory explanation of the rationale and structure of the analyses

comments.issue: Lines 220-239 are too complicated and hard to follow.
comments.request: Write the formulas of these models in the appendix.
comments.quote: 220-239: This is too complicated and hard to follow. I suggest you to write down the formulas of these models in the appendix.

comments.issue: A random factor is mixed with fixed factors in the model description, confusing readers.
comments.request: Separate random and fixed effects in the description.
comments.quote: Moreover, you should separate your random from fixed effects. In line 223, "identity of focal and competitor species", a random factor, is mixed with all other factors, which are fixed. This is a bit confusing to the reader.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether plot identity as random factor includes both random intercept and slope.
comments.request: State whether the plot identity term includes a random slope.
comments.quote: 227: is "plot identity as an additional random factor" also referring to both random intercept and slope? Or only intercept?

comments.issue: Line-level edits: fix 'might be give' and spell out PVA.
comments.quote: 456: "might give" instead of "might be give"

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'background plants' refers to and whether they are in the experimental plots.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning and placement of background plants.
comments.quote: 31: What do you mean by "background plants"? Are these in the experimental plots or not?

comments.issue: It is not clear that 'competition' in the supplement refers to both interspecific and intraspecific competition.
comments.request: Clarify that competition includes both inter- and intraspecific competition.
comments.quote: 37-48: one quibble: clarify that "competition" here refers to both interspecific and intraspecific competition. This was unclear to me at first.

reviews.assessment: Likes the design and analysis, but research questions lack hypotheses and novelty, and the altitudinal gradient is underdeveloped.
strengths: visible effort behind the experimental setting

comments.issue: The title provides no valuable information to readers.
comments.request: Make the title informative and specific.
comments.quote: The title does not provide any valuable info to the readers (different things have different effects).

comments.issue: Research questions are purely descriptive with no hypotheses behind them.
comments.request: Identify and state the hypotheses behind the research questions.
comments.quote: Research questions are purely descriptive and there is no hypothesis behind.

comments.issue: Most results are in line with what was already known, and the study's contribution is not articulated.
comments.request: Explain the contribution this study provides to ecological research.
comments.quote: Discussion shows that most results are in line with what was already known, which is not very novel.

comments.issue: The discussion does not connect the results to community ecology theory.
comments.request: Go further in the discussion and connect results with community ecology theory.
comments.quote: I recommend authors to revisit the whole manuscript, identify the hypotheses behind the research questions and go further in the discussion, particularly connecting their results with community ecology theory.

comments.issue: Calling the dynamics 'competitive' is inaccurate because some dynamics involve positive effects or no competition.
comments.request: Change 'competitive population dynamics' to 'population dynamics' or 'growth rates'.
comments.quote: The use of competitive dynamics has some problems (some dynamics are not competitive as there are some positive effects, there is the dynamic of species in plots with no competition etc.) and makes the reading difficult

comments.issue: The altitudinal gradient is treated as a side effect, ignored in the title and underdiscussed relative to its prominence in the questions.
comments.request: Reconsider the contribution of environmental gradients and rewrite accordingly.
comments.quote: the altitudinal gradient seems a side effect of the experimental design and not a truly component of the study. It is ignored in the title, and much less discussed than species specific effects

comments.issue: Vital rates are not defined with examples despite their central importance.
comments.request: Define vital rates and connect them to fitness.
comments.quote: L45, due to the key importance ‘vital rates’ play in this study, it would be very convenient to define it/put examples here so readers do not have any question about what authors are talking about.

comments.issue: 'Complementary effect' is used although the cited references do not mention it; it is really a compensatory effect.
comments.request: Replace 'complementary' with 'compensatory'.
comments.quote: I do not understand the use of the wording ‘complementary effect’. Indeed, there is no mention about this effect in neither of the two references supporting this sentence.

comments.issue: The sentence is confusing because positive vital-rate effects are also due to competition.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence for clarity.
comments.quote: L64, this sentence seems confusing as those positive effects of vital rates are also due to competition. Rewrite for clarity.

comments.issue: The difference from the previous paragraph's claim about missing information is not evident.
comments.request: Make the difference from the earlier statement more evident.
comments.quote: in the previous paragraph authors say that there is no info about how different growth rates contribute to declines in competition. I see it is not exactly the same as what is said here

comments.issue: Why only 8 heterospecifics were used, and how they were selected, is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the number and selection of the 8 heterospecifics.
comments.quote: L134, why growing with 8 heterospecific and not all of them? An explanation will be welcomed. Indeed, how were those 8 heterospecific selected among the 14 focal species?

comments.issue: Intraspecific competition is central to coexistence theory but absent from the discussion.
comments.request: Discuss intraspecific competition in relation to coexistence theory.
comments.quote: L136, intraspecific competition is at the core of coexistence theory, but there is nothing about it in the discussion.

comments.issue: Opportunities to compare intra- versus interspecific competition and same- versus different-origin species pairs are missed.
comments.request: Run intra/inter and altitudinal-origin comparisons.
comments.quote: it is a missed opportunity not conducting an analysis comparing intra- and inter-. Similarly, a comparison between competition among species of the same altitudinal origin and among species of different altitudinal origin could be worth it.

comments.issue: The number of individuals is not stated before the formula, obscuring replication.
comments.request: State the number of individuals before the formula.
comments.quote: L136-137, I recommend saying the number of individuals also before the formula so readers get the idea of replication clearly.

comments.issue: 'Invasive' is a poor word choice that evokes invasion ecology.
comments.request: Call it 'competitive' growth rate instead.
comments.quote: L166, I think invasive is not a good word choice. I see the individuals invade the monocultures but why not simply call ‘competitive’ growth rate to be in line with the aim of the study?

comments.issue: 'Low-density' is irrelevant at this point.
comments.request: Remove 'low-density'.
comments.quote: L166, I do not see the relevance of including ‘low-density’ here. I suggest removing.

comments.issue: 'Perturbated' evokes the perturbation literature.
comments.request: Use 'modified' or 'vital rate' growth instead.
comments.quote: L182, as before, perturbated remembers to perturbation, which is a specific field in ecology. I will call it ‘modified’ or ‘vital rate’ growth instead.

comments.issue: The sum in this calculation should probably be of the absolute total contributions.
comments.request: Check whether absolute contributions should be summed.
comments.quote: L206, in this calculation I think the sum is of the absolute total contributions. Check.

comments.issue: The criterion for including invasion IPMs with 1+ positive contributions, and cases with two or more, is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify what happens when two or more vital rates show positive contributions.
comments.quote: L209, here any invasion IPM is included as long as it has 1+ positive contributions? Specify what happens if two or more vital rates showed positive contributions.

comments.issue: Interactions between explanatory variables are used in the models but not mentioned in the text.
comments.request: Mention the interactions between explanatory variables.
comments.quote: L220, there is no mention about interactions between explanatory variables, although in the models it is clear that interactions were included. Include that info here.

comments.issue: A correlation table between growth rates would help visualize the data.
comments.request: Add a correlation table and per-rate histograms.
comments.quote: L244, maybe including a correlation table between the five growth rates together with the histogram for each growth rate individually could be interesting to visualize the data.

comments.issue: 'Low-density' at line 244 can be removed with no harm.
comments.request: Remove the redundant 'low-density'.
comments.quote: L244, I imagine this low-density connects to the low-density above. I think can be removed with no harm.

comments.issue: The -0.1 threshold is highlighted in the text but not shown in the plot.
comments.request: Add the threshold line to the plot.
comments.quote: L264, if this threshold of -0.1 is highlighted, then it would be good to see it in the plot. Add the line for clarity.

comments.issue: Post-hoc comparison procedures for significant interactions are not described.
comments.request: Describe the post-hoc comparisons in the methods.
comments.quote: L267, when significant interactions were found, how were post-hoc comparisons done? Include that info in methods.

comments.issue: Almost all species pairs have only one complementary vital rate; why compensation rarely involves multiple rates deserves discussion.
comments.request: Discuss why only one vital rate compensates and which rates do so.
comments.quote: if 243 species pairs showed a complementary vital rate and 373 vital rates were complementary, then almost all species pairs have only one complementary vital rate. This could be something worth discussing

comments.issue: The source of 'significantly' is unclear and 7% does not look like a big effect.
comments.request: Clarify the significance and effect size behind this statement.
comments.quote: I do not see where this ‘significantly’ comes from. To me 7% does not seem a big effect

comments.issue: The sentence ignores the previous paragraph and is not connected to growth and establishment.
comments.request: Connect the sentence to growth and establishment.
comments.quote: L359-361, but this sentence totally ignores the previous paragraph where two rates with strong effects are presented. This need to be connected to growth and establishment.

comments.issue: Calling competition an 'environmental perturbation' is not appropriate.
comments.request: Use 'presence of competitors' instead.
comments.quote: Besides, calling competition an ‘environmental perturbation’ does not sound good to me. Maybe better ‘presence of competitors’.

comments.issue: Trait information for the study species would help support this statement.
comments.request: Provide trait information for the species.
comments.quote: L375-377, it would be good if there is some trait info that could support this for the species in the study.

comments.issue: The clarification at L404-407 is unnecessary given the statistical testing.
comments.request: Remove the sentence.
comments.quote: L404-407, I appreciate this clarification, although this is the reason why we do statistical testing. I would remove this sentence as we already have the results from the models.

comments.issue: The nice coexistence result should be discussed in relation to facilitation, limiting similarity and other community ecology topics.
comments.request: Add discussion linking population and community ecology beyond modern coexistence theory.
comments.quote: L430-434, This is a nice result, and I would like to see some discussion related to works on facilitation, limiting similarity or other big topics of community ecology.

comments.issue: The sentence is not straightforward about how positive contributions weaken negative effects.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence for clarity.
comments.quote: L436-439, this sentence is not straightforward? I mean, if there are vital rates with positive contributions, then negative effects (competition) is weaker. This can be clearly seen in the figure S8 were all arrows go always to higher coexistence.

comments.issue: It is unclear how Figure 3 can show values above 1:1.
comments.request: Explain the values above 1:1 in Figure 3.
comments.quote: Figure 3, how it is possible to have values above 1:1?

comments.issue: How invasion by natural species was prevented in the monocultures is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how establishment of other species was prevented in monocultures.
comments.quote: L10, how was the establishment of species other than the ones grown prevented in the monocultures (invasion from natural species)?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether early deaths were counted as competition deaths in survival calculations.
comments.request: State how deaths at the beginning were treated in survival estimates.
comments.quote: L21, species death at the beginning were considered as death by competition for calculating the survival?

comments.issue: Using monocultures to estimate plant size confounds the baseline with intraspecific competition.
comments.request: Justify or change the use of monocultures to estimate plant size.
comments.quote: L27, why using species form the monocultures to estimate plant size? Besides, monocultures would represent the intraspecific competition case rather than absence of competition.

comments.issue: The sentence appears to be repeated.
comments.request: Check and remove the repeated sentence.
comments.quote: L42-45, it is this sentence repeated? Check it.

title: Compensatory responses of vital rates attenuate impacts of competition on population growth and promote coexistence

study.system: plankton time series; 17 lakes and 4 marine sites

editor_summary: Reviewers agree it is well-analyzed and important, with no major issues, but all three ask for clarifications and better explanations of wording and methods.

reviews.assessment: Well-analyzed, data-rich contribution; minor suggestions to clarify transient instability theory and methods.
strengths: supports the general theme that chaos is prevalent

comments.issue: Transient instability can arise from local phase-space instability or from environmental parameter changes, and the 'edge of chaos' framing may mislead.
comments.request: Point out the distinction and its management implications.
comments.quote: periods of transient instability could arise as the system moves through regions of phase space where there is local instability

comments.issue: The local weighting parameter and leave-one-out cross-validation are not explained in the main text.
comments.request: Describe these methods sufficiently for an intuitive understanding.
comments.quote: the local weighting parameter is first mentioned without any explanation for how it’s used. Similarly, it is unclear how leave-one-out cross validation is used for model selection.

comments.issue: How fluctuating population stability offers evolutionary advantages or speeds adaptation is not mechanistically explained.
comments.request: Provide more explanation or omit the paragraph.
comments.quote: How does transient local instability in population numbers, per se, alter a population’s genetic structure to speed adaptation?

comments.issue: Positive local Lyapunov exponents can occur with exponential growth or stable equilibria at low densities, so spring bloom results may not be surprising.
comments.request: Point this out in the interpretation.
comments.quote: even deterministic models with a strongly stable equilibrium will display a positive local LE if population densities are small and in the high growth phase

reviews.assessment: Novel, interesting application of state-of-the-art time-series methods; comments are minor but clarifying.
strengths: finding of widespread chaos and intermittent instability is new
less variability with greater aggregation is important

comments.issue: Treating the systems as relatively closed is a large assumption given external environmental changes and food-web connections.
comments.request: Assess whether external conditions could drive the observed patterns.
comments.quote: it seems like a large assumption that these systems can be considered closed

comments.issue: Table S1 only shows zooplankton data, and whether individual phytoplankton species were measured is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phytoplankton data used.
comments.quote: Table S1 only shows data on zooplankton, not phytoplankton.

comments.issue: Terms such as step-ahead divergence, log variance expansion ratio and volume contraction rate are unfamiliar and only briefly defined.
comments.request: Provide more intuitive descriptions.
comments.quote: Can more description be given of what is ‘step-ahead divergence’, ‘log variance expansion ratio’, and ‘volume contraction rate’?

comments.issue: Whether nutrient reduction or zooplankton predation causes the spring bloom crash is not determined.
comments.request: Address the cause of the bloom instability and crash.
comments.quote: Does the analysis help determine the cause of the instability of the spring bloom and its crash?

comments.issue: The claim that chaos may resolve the paradox of the plankton is questioned because resources include many micronutrients.
comments.request: Qualify the claim.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me that ‘chaos may resolve the paradox of the plankton’

comments.issue: The complementarity explanation for decreased variability with aggregation is unclear; aggregation may simply increase opposite-phase fluctuations.
comments.request: Clarify the interpretation.
comments.quote: I am not sure I understand this. Does increasing aggregation simply increase the probability of species fluctuations being opposite in phase?

comments.issue: Why absolute seasonality in local stability is unrelated to environmental seasonality is not understood.
comments.request: Explain this result.
comments.quote: I am not sure I understand why “absolute seasonality in local stability was

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the extent of intermittent instability; asks to connect to dynamical-systems theory and clarify terminology.
strengths: most advanced methods and relevant references

comments.issue: Connections to dynamical-systems insights on the type and mechanism of intermittency are not made.
comments.request: Relate the findings to intermittency theory (e.g. Ott 2002) and explain the choice of terminology.
comments.quote: I am wondering whether any connections can be made to the insights available in dynamical systems, e.g. with respect to the type of intermittency or to the mechanism(s) driving it.

comments.issue: The role of noise and seasonal forcing in driving the intermittency is not assessed.
comments.request: Discuss seasonal forcing and noise-induced instability.
comments.quote: I am also curious about the role of noise and seasonal forcing in driving the intermittency.

comments.issue: Phrases such as 'globally unstable', 'globally stable time series' and 'local instability' are confusing or undefined.
comments.request: Define these terms clearly.
comments.quote: The sentences phrased in the manuscript sometimes makes me feel confused.

comments.issue: What 'temporal resolution' and 'spatial variation' refer to in this paper is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify these terms.
comments.quote: I do not get what 'temporal resolution' refers to in this paper

comments.issue: Writing 'global stability (chaotic dynamics)' suggests the two expressions correspond.
comments.request: Clarify or separate the two concepts.
comments.quote: This seems to suggest correspondence between these two expressions.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'first difference' is not explained.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: What is the 'first difference'?

comments.issue: Several small technical edits (italic 'top row', wording at l.227, capitalisation of 's-map').
comments.quote: l. 259 "s-map" Should this be a capital S?

comments.issue: What matrix S is at line 219 is not explained.
comments.request: Define matrix S.
comments.quote: l. 219, What is matrix S?

comments.issue: The meaning of 'median instability' is unclear.
comments.request: Define the metric.
comments.quote: l. 242 I am not sure what exactly "median instability" is.

comments.issue: How the percentage numbers can be 'seen' in Fig. 1 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how Fig. 1 shows these percentages.
comments.quote: l. 271 How can these percentage numbers be "seen" in Fig. 1?

comments.issue: The range of behaviours and seasonalities should be illustrated with example time series.
comments.request: Write more about this range and give examples.
comments.quote: I think it would be nice to write a bit more about this "range of different behavior and seasonality"

comments.issue: Fig. 3b appears to show greatest local instability in late summer/early fall, not spring.
comments.request: Reconcile the text with the figure.
comments.quote: In Fig. 3b, it looks to me that the greatest local instability is in late summer/early fall.

comments.issue: Relevant state-dependent management work (Desharnais et al. 2001; Hilker & Westerhoff 2007) is not discussed.
comments.request: Cite and discuss this work.
comments.quote: Hilker and Westerhoff (2007, Am. Nat., Vol. 170, pp. 232-3241) identify "alert zones" from time series

comments.issue: In Fig. 3b it is hard to see whether the Lyapunov exponent is zero, negative or positive.
comments.request: Improve the figure's legibility.
comments.quote: It is sometimes hard to see whether the Lyapunov exponent =0, <0, or >0

comments.issue: The bands in Fig. 6 are hard to see.

comments.quote: Fig. 6: On my printout (it might be a printer issue), the bands are hard to see.

comments.issue: The meaning of variables and abbreviations in Table S2 is not explained.

comments.quote: Tab. S2: Please explain the meaning of variables and abbreviations.

title: Intermittent instability is widespread in plankton communities

study.system: Canary Islands plants; functional traits and climate rarity

reviews.assessment: Interesting idea and hypotheses; asks for clearer scope and terminology, metric details, and consideration of data biases.
