comments.issue: The focus on oceanic and volcanic archipelagos is not stated early in the introduction.
comments.request: Outline the island type focus early in the intro.
comments.quote: I would perhaps outline early in the intro that you are focused on oceanic / volcanic isolated archipelagos

comments.issue: Dispersal filters also apply to non-endemic species, which may explain trait similarity between groups.
comments.request: Consider this shared filtering in the framing.
comments.quote: As the islands are oceanic, dispersal filters will also apply to non-endemic species.

comments.issue: The statement about adaptive radiations and endemic species is confusing.
comments.request: Say that many adaptive radiations involve endemic species.
comments.quote: Probably better to say many adaptive radiations involve endemic species, as currently written is confusing as many endemic species are not part of ARs

comments.issue: Allopatric divergence is conflated with non-adaptive speciation.
comments.request: Distinguish allopatric speciation from non-adaptive divergence.
comments.quote: You seem to conflate allopatric divergence with non-adaptive speciation in various parts of the paper, but these are not necessarily the same.

comments.issue: It is not always clear that statements about trait data scarcity refer to plants only.
comments.request: Specify that the statements concern plants.
comments.quote: You also need to make clearer in certain places you are talking about plants.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the studies at lines 16-20 concern plants.
comments.request: Clarify whether these studies concern plants.
comments.quote: Linked to the previous point, Lines 16-20 (P.7) – are these studies in relation to plants?

comments.issue: Climatic rarity, habitat rarity and environmental rarity are used interchangeably.
comments.request: Define and distinguish these rarity terms.
comments.quote: I was a bit confused as you seem to interchange between climatic rarity, habitat rarity and environmental rarity. Are these all used interchangeably?

comments.issue: The Kraemer et al. 2022 paper on functional diversity and the GDM is not discussed.
comments.request: Consider citing Kraemer et al. 2022.
comments.quote: a recent paper by Kraemer et al in GEB also discusses functional diversity in the context of the GDM, and may be of interest

comments.issue: It is unclear whether functional distinctiveness was calculated at archipelago or island level.
comments.request: State the level of calculation.
comments.quote: For the functional distinctiveness metric, is this just calculated at the archipelago level, or the individual island level as well?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether traits were scaled before calculating distinctiveness.
comments.request: Explain trait scaling before the metric calculation.
comments.quote: should the traits also be scaled before calculating functional distinctiveness? As otherwise the distance could be dominated by the trait with the largest range?

comments.issue: Species from the rarest habitats may be missing trait values, biasing the rarest NENs.
comments.request: Check and address this missing-trait bias.
comments.quote: could there be a potential bias in that the rarest NENs are those missing trait values, i.e. those associated with the rarest habitats?

comments.issue: The rarity results may simply reflect that the oldest islands have few rare climate areas.
comments.request: Discuss this driver of the results.
comments.quote: are lots of these results (regarding climatic rareness) simply driven by the fact that, judging by your figure, the two oldest islands don’t have many rare climate areas?

reviews.assessment: Agrees with the trait-based approach but questions climatic uniqueness estimation, endemism definition and discussion breadth.
strengths: logical next step for island biogeography

comments.issue: Climatic uniqueness may reflect island location and size rather than island age.
comments.request: Interrogate this alternative and correct for island size.
comments.quote: is it not possible that island location and size would also influence the climatic uniqueness/rarity?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether maximum trait values are island-level or archipelago-level.
comments.request: Clarify the trait value level and discuss plasticity implications.
comments.quote: Is this at the island-level or archipelago level i.e. does each island community have a maximum trait value or is there only one trait value used for all islands?

comments.issue: The definition of endemism is not evolution-oriented.
comments.request: Consider defining endemism by time on island or archipelago endemism.
comments.quote: would it not make sense to define endemism in terms of 'time present on island'/time since colonisation?

comments.issue: Other island biogeography dynamics such as isolation and connectivity are under-discussed.
comments.request: Discuss additional factors linking island biogeography to traits.
comments.quote: I cannot help but feel that more should be made in terms of providing a discussion to other factors that are traditionally considered under the umbrella of island biogeography and how these can be linked to traits

comments.issue: The trait-based framework's practical implications need more development.
comments.request: Expand these concepts in the introduction and concluding remarks.
comments.quote: there is value in spending more time in discussing the practical implications and considerations for a trait-based framework

comments.issue: The relationship between island age and climatic rarity is not plotted.
comments.request: Add a plot, e.g. a background line in figure 6.
comments.quote: Could the authors perhaps show the relationship between island age and climatic rarity as a plot

comments.issue: The name of H2 in the Figure 1 caption does not match the main text.
comments.request: Make the H2 naming consistent.
comments.quote: Just check the figure legend/caption as the name of H2 does not match the term you use in the main text.

comments.issue: The caption description of the shaded humps is unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase as a cross-section of islands at different stages.
comments.quote: Also maybe instead of saying "Beneath the graph is a schematic diagram: the shaded humps represent islands at different stages" in the caption rephrase it

comments.issue: Arrows between panels a-b and b-c imply a process rather than different states.
comments.request: Remove the arrows between panels.
comments.quote: maybe remove the arrows between panels a-b and b-c. These make it appear as if there is a process which goes a -> b -> c when these are really just different potential states

reviews.assessment: Nice, sound paper; main concern is that occurrence-data bias may inflate rarity estimates, with suggestions for more robust metrics.
strengths: nice paper on a seldom addressed topic
sound hypotheses and trait distinctiveness approach

comments.issue: Occurrence data quality is overestimated; uneven coverage biases mean-based rarity, as noted for this database by Hortal et al. 2007.
comments.request: Use median rather than mean rarity and discuss the bias.
comments.quote: My main criticism is that I believe that you’re being too optimistic with regard to the quality of occurrence data.

comments.issue: Alternative rarity measures such as the first quartile or maximum are not evaluated.
comments.request: Test upper-range rarity metrics, especially the first quartile.
comments.quote: species evolving the capacity of using rarer climates may also hold the capacity of using more common ones, so perhaps it would also be advisable to test measures of the upper range of rarity distribution per species

comments.issue: The claim that most island speciation is allopatric is questionable and citations are incomplete.
comments.request: Qualify the claim and cite additional literature.
comments.quote: I'm not sure that most speciation on islands is allopatric (as you cite in page 5 lines 46-50 quoting Stuessy 2006) is true for all islands

comments.issue: The Canary Islands are close to the mainland, limiting generality of the conclusions.
comments.request: Add the Canary Islands context and discuss this limitation.
comments.quote: Note that despite being oceanic, the Canary Islands are relatively close to the mainland, so there is a much higher flux of inmigrants than in, e.g., Madeira, Azores, Galapagos or Hawaii.

comments.issue: The higher distinctiveness of multiple island endemics could reflect success at exploiting unique resources.
comments.request: Consider and discuss this interpretation.
comments.quote: Could the higher distinctiveness shown by Multiple Island Endemics be a signal of their higher success in exploiting unique resources - that would allow them to colonize more islands of the archipelago successfully?

comments.issue: 'The right traits' at page 17 line 39 is too colloquial and unclear.
comments.request: Explain which traits are meant and why.
comments.quote: please explain what do you mean by the right traits

comments.issue: The first discussion paragraph repeats the hypotheses instead of evaluating them.
comments.request: Delete the sentence at page 15 lines 37-43 and merge with the next paragraph.
comments.quote: I don't think you should use the first paragraph of the discussion to recall the three hypotheses you test, but rather to identify which one(s) work in the Canary Islands

comments.issue: The earlier Santos et al. 2016 paper is not acknowledged relative to recent papers.
comments.request: Cite and credit Santos et al. 2016.
comments.quote: to be fair, the thoughtful paper by Santos et al 2016 (different from the revision you cite before) precludes these recent papers by Weigelt and Hanz

comments.issue: The reason for splitting SIE and MIE is not explained.
comments.request: Provide the rationale for the split.
comments.quote: Provide a reason for splitting between SIE and MIE, because it may not be straightforward for the reader

comments.issue: The GDM acronym is not reintroduced and the term should be more precise at page 15 line 28.
comments.request: Add 'of oceanic island biogeography (GDM)' and reintroduce the acronym.
comments.quote: add “of oceanic island biogeography (GDM)” to be more precise, and reintroduce the acronym

comments.issue: The phrase at page 18 line 6 needs correction.
comments.request: Revise 'Island endemics have fuelled'.
comments.quote: Page 18 line 6 "Island endemics have fuelled"

comments.issue: Figure 5 may not need to be in the main text.
comments.request: Consider moving figure 5 to supplementary materials.
comments.quote: Perhaps figure 5 could go to the supplementary materials

title: Links to rare climates do not translate into distinct traits for island endemics

study.system: angiosperm clades; 152 studies using SSE diversification models

editor_summary: Editor recommends thorough revision: major concerns are not distinguishing hidden-state models, exclusive focus on SSE methods, and journal fit (2 of 4 reviewers); Conclusions especially inconclusive.

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the study and finds the analyses sound, but doubts the journal's fit and suggests examining effect sizes rather than binary outcomes.
strengths: analyses straightforward with nothing critically wrong
documentation of how researcher behaviour changed is interesting

comments.issue: Doubts whether an ecology journal is the right venue for this method-focused work.
comments.request: Consider whether the paper fits Ecology Letters.
comments.quote: I worry whether this journal is the right venue for this type of work

comments.issue: Binary response coding may miss meaningful model-averaged rate differences among states.
comments.request: Consider effect sizes or model-averaged rates as evidence.
comments.quote: The response variable seems to be, by design, binary

comments.issue: Tree-size effect may be a power artifact rather than evidence of trait dependence.
comments.quote: are these differences meaningfully different? I could imagine no, due to statistical artifacts of having more data, and more power to uncover "significance"

comments.issue: HiSSE misspecification results are characterised unfairly; CID-4 was omitted, later work shows better performance and similar rate estimates.
comments.request: Discuss Caetano et al. (2018) and the proper model set.
comments.quote: They inexplicably did not include the CID-4 (which is an independent model that is of equal complexity of the character-dependent HiSSE model)

reviews.assessment: Finds the topic very interesting but faults lumping methods with different false-positive risks instead of comparing them.
strengths: timely synthesis of an interesting literature
cool and broadly useful trait ontology

comments.issue: Methods with high false-positive risk are pooled; results and guidelines should be assessed by method.
comments.request: Compare SSD evidence across methods (e.g. BiSSE versus HiSSE).
comments.quote: all the SSE papers were lumped for the analysis although we know that at least some of the methods are highly susceptible to false positives

comments.issue: Paper could be shortened if organised around the specific questions raised.
comments.request: Focus and shorten the paper around these questions.
comments.quote: I think the paper could be shortened if focused around particular questions, such as those outlined above

comments.issue: Scoring best-fitting models as significant SSD may overstate evidence when the next-best model lacks SSD.
comments.request: Account for model support when scoring evidence.
comments.quote: the best fitting model (e.g. lowest AIC) may not be much better than the next best model, which might have no SSD

comments.issue: 'Traits' versus 'states' distinction is presented as clear without citing the literature debating it.
comments.request: Cite papers discussing this terminology.
comments.quote: This line made it sound like the 'traits' vs 'states' distinction is clear

comments.issue: The 'meaning that only three' part of the sentence is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence.
comments.quote: I didn't follow the 'meaning that only three' part

comments.issue: Supplementary csv appears to contain only two lines of data.
comments.request: Check and fix the supplementary dataset file.
comments.quote: When I opened the csv file I found only two lines in the table

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic; high praise with a single question about best practices for ecological-context traits and GeoSSE.
strengths: machine-learning approach will advance the field

comments.issue: Best practices for analysing traits in an ecological context (e.g. GeoSSE) are not discussed.
comments.request: Comment on how ecological-context traits should be analysed.
comments.quote: Can the authors comment on what they consider best practices for analyzing the effects of a trait within an ecological context?

reviews.assessment: Mixed: sees strengths but questions the paper's interest for Ecology Letters readers and its exclusive SSE focus.
strengths: well written with coverage of a huge number of studies
statistically appropriate analyses with effective display
useful best-practice recommendations and future directions

comments.issue: Uncertain that the paper will interest Ecology Letters readers.
comments.request: Strengthen the case for broad reader interest.
comments.quote: I have mixed feelings about the level of interest that this paper will generate among readers of Ecology Letters

comments.issue: SSE methods may not effectively address the general question of angiosperm diversification drivers.
comments.request: Acknowledge and address this limitation.
comments.quote: these methods (and their typical implementation) may not be the most effective approach to addressing the general question of drivers of diversification in angiosperms

comments.issue: Studies using alternative approaches are excluded and not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss results from non-SSE approaches for comparison.
comments.quote: Many papers have used alternative approaches, and they are not included here

comments.issue: Hodges and Arnold spur-mediated diversification example has been questioned.
comments.request: Consider a different example.
comments.quote: The authors might want to reconsider the Hodges and Arnold example of spur-mediated diversification

comments.issue: Many line-level grammar/contraction edits (L35, L67, L120, L249, L527).
comments.quote: The authors should not use contractions in the paper; here, wasn't should be was not

comments.issue: Expectation that the same traits matter across a huge clade and long timespan needs justification.
comments.request: Address whether this perspective is realistic.
comments.quote: why would it be the same trait(s) have been important across such a big clade over so much time?

comments.issue: Early focus on SSE methods seems problematic without signposting that these issues are addressed later.
comments.request: Note upfront that method issues are recognised and addressed below.
comments.quote: Perhaps it would be useful for the authors to note that they recognize that issues have been raised regarding these methods and that these are addressed further below

comments.issue: Comparing a trait within one clade versus across angiosperms raises unresolved homology issues.
comments.request: Discuss trait homology and context-dependent expectations.
comments.quote: This raises the important question of homology of traits; the only way that the effect of a trait can be evaluated is if it appears in multiple places on a tree

comments.issue: An analysis cannot address the biologically interesting part of the study.
comments.quote: This is too bad because this is the biologically interesting part of this study, and this analysis seems not to be able to help with it

comments.issue: Unclear how a study's focus on one or several clades was determined, given nested clades.
comments.request: Explain the classification rule.
comments.quote: I found this an interesting statement because clades are nested, so how was it determined that a study focused on one or a set of clades?

comments.issue: Unclear whether 'its' at L291 refers to FitzJohn et al. (2009).
comments.request: Clarify the reference.
comments.quote: By its, do the authors mean FitzJohn et al. (2009)? Perhaps clarify?

comments.issue: Genera are not always clades, so the L458 sentence is conceptually inaccurate.
comments.request: Revise the sentence.
comments.quote: it is not always certain that genera are clades (a lot of work is still needed!)

title: Trait‐dependent diversification in angiosperms: Patterns, models and data

study.system: community ecology; state diagrams applied to empirical datasets

editor_summary: Editor agrees with reviewers that the study is interesting and timely but central concerns about fixed-point definitions, the PCI algorithm, thresholds, multistability and waiting time must be addressed.

reviews.assessment: Novel and interesting approach; asks about practical applicability, timescales and several implementation assumptions.

comments.issue: The approach needs the complete interaction network as a Lotka-Volterra model, which is rarely available and context-dependent in practice.
comments.request: Discuss how the approach could be applied when interactions are incompletely known.
comments.quote: how the fact that the complete interaction network is needed (as well as in the form of a Lotka Volterra model) would render this approach applicable in practice

comments.issue: Validation in a simple experimental system would be ideal, though not requested for this paper.
comments.quote: I would ideally expect a validation of the algorithm in a simple experimental system, although this is not something I would ask to provide in this paper

comments.issue: How the algorithm would be applied to experimental systems, e.g. chemostats versus batch cultures, is not discussed.
comments.request: Improve the discussion of practical experimental application.
comments.quote: the authors could improve how they think the algorithm could be applied in practice to experimental systems

comments.issue: Timescales of waiting actions are unclear, and whether waiting time enters the cost calculation is not explained.
comments.request: Comment on expected stabilisation times and include waiting time in the cost.
comments.quote: For the waiting actions which seem quite important to reduce the cost of the control, how long is it expected for a given community to stabilize itself?

comments.issue: Whether the algorithm could be adapted to other interaction types or consumer-resource frameworks is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss adaptation to other interaction types.
comments.quote: I wonder then to which extent this algorithm could be adapted to other interaction type or a consumer-resource framework

comments.issue: It is unclear whether actions are followed by waiting time or their outcome is instantaneous, and how that differs from the wait action.
comments.request: Clarify the timing of actions versus waiting.
comments.quote: is an action followed by waiting time to check for the consequences of the action or is the outcome supposed to be instantaneous

comments.issue: It is not clear how intermediate stable states are obtained in the state graph.
comments.request: Explain how intermediate states arise in the implementation.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me how the intermediate stable states are obtained in the graph

comments.issue: Assuming the initial state is unstable seems unrealistic.
comments.request: Justify or relax the unstable-initial-state assumption.
comments.quote: it seems unrealistic to me to assume that an initial state is an unstable state

comments.issue: It is unclear whether interaction matrix elements can be positive (facilitation).
comments.request: State whether positive interactions are allowed in A.
comments.quote: are the elements of A all negative or is it possible to have facilitation/positive interactions?

comments.issue: How the algorithm handles alternative stable states with the same natural transition is unclear.
comments.request: Explain handling of alternative stable states.
comments.quote: how would the algorithm handle the possibility of alternative stable states (two possible outcomes obtainable by the same natural transition) ?

comments.issue: The environment is treated as abiotic with no community-environment feedback.
comments.request: Discuss cases with feedback between community and environment.
comments.quote: Would the approach be suited to cases with feedback between the community and the environment?

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 2 appear to use different parameters, so the action sequence cannot be reconstructed.
comments.request: Use the same system for figures 1 and 2.
comments.quote: Maybe the authors could use the same system so that the reader can reconstruct the sequence of actions presented in figure 1 using the state diagram of figure 2

comments.issue: How species removal is implemented, including any antibiotic effect, is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how removal actions are modelled.
comments.quote: how is the removal implemented? Is the antibiotic effect on dynamics explicitly modelled, or is it a simple « presence/absence » action?

comments.issue: How the nominal solution is chosen is unclear; an optimal path may itself be a nominal path.
comments.request: Explain the choice of nominal solution.
comments.quote: line 247: how is the nominal solution chosen? For instance in the supplementary files, page 8, the optimal path could be a nominal path

comments.issue: Line 90: unclear note about 'two points'.
comments.quote: Minor points: Line 90: two points ..

comments.issue: 'Active intervention' is not defined.
comments.request: Define what active intervention means.
comments.quote: Line 91: what do author mean by active intervention

comments.issue: Line 167 wording: 'environmental' should be 'environmental factors' or 'environment'.
comments.request: Adjust the wording.
comments.quote: Line 167: “environmental” → “environmental factors”? Or “environment”

reviews.assessment: Interesting question and clear analysis, but the discrete-environment and waiting-time assumptions are hard to justify for real systems.

comments.issue: The discrete-environment assumption is hard to parameterize; nature has many unknown environments.
comments.request: Discuss and justify the discrete-environment assumption.
comments.quote: there can be hundreds of or thousands of different environments in nature and the majority of these environments are unknown to us.

comments.issue: Systems may not reach equilibrium quickly, making the 'waiting for a natural transition' action unrealistic.
comments.request: Consider including waiting time in the criteria for optimal paths.
comments.quote: My only concern is that it is hard to guarantee the systems reach equilibrium over a short time. So how realistic is the action of “waiting for a natural transition”.

comments.issue: The '+' symbol is used without definition; 'both...and...' would be clearer.
comments.request: Replace '+' or clearly define the symbol.
comments.quote: Line 146, 227, 247, and so on: replace “+” with

comments.issue: It is unclear how the length of a path is defined and compared.
comments.request: Define and compare path length.
comments.quote: Line 152: how to define and compare the length of a path?

comments.issue: U(0,1) and the ifelse functions are not defined.
comments.request: Define U(0,1) and the ifelse functions.
comments.quote: Line 212, 213, 220, 221: what is U(0,1)? Also, it would be better to define the ifelse functions.

comments.issue: How the single nominal solution is chosen is unclear, including why sequential removals then additions.
comments.request: Explain the choice of nominal solution.
comments.quote: Line 248, 249: how to choose the single nominal solution specifically? Why choose the ones comprising sequential removals and then sequential additions?

comments.issue: How PCI is calculated and what it means ecologically is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the PCI calculation and its ecological meaning.
comments.quote: Line 250, 251: how to calculate PCI specifically? What is the difference between two paths and what is the ecological meaning of it?

comments.issue: The phrase 'the value of the pathfinding approach' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase and how criteria identify the optimal path.
comments.quote: Line 252: what do you mean by “the value of the pathfinding approach”? How do the criteria help to identify the optimal path?

comments.issue: The use of Jaccard similarity is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the choice of Jaccard similarity.
comments.quote: Line 262: why use the Jaccard similarity?

comments.issue: The removal of extreme values is not justified; finite values preserving the inequality relations between A and r could be kept.
comments.request: Justify or revise the treatment of extreme values.
comments.quote: Line 264: it would be better to justify the removal of extreme values. Why not choose finite values and keep the inequality relations between A and r?

comments.issue: The choices of random-forest parameters 'mtry' and 'ntrees' are not justified.
comments.request: Justify the mtry and ntrees choices.
comments.quote: Line 265: it would be better if the choices of “mtry” and “ntrees” can be justified.

comments.issue: 'Net richness' is not defined.
comments.request: Define net richness.
comments.quote: Line 307: what is “net richness”?

comments.issue: It is unclear why mean A and mean r indicate competitive exclusion rather than e.g. the fraction of negative interactions.
comments.request: Justify the use of mean A and mean r.
comments.quote: To talk about competitive exclusion, could you justify the use of mean A rather than the fraction of negative interactions, etc.?

title: Navigation between initial and desired community states using shortcuts

study.system: Prymnesium parvum toxic mixotroph isolates; cell-level predation behaviour experiments

editor_summary: Editor: revision much improved and both experts satisfied; minor points to address; authors should caution readers about inferences that are tenuous pending further data.

reviews.assessment: Positive; finds the revised manuscript well written with many strengths and remaining strain-coverage weaknesses.
strengths: integrates phylogeny, functional diversity and strain experiments
complex figures are intuitive and stand alone

comments.issue: Only two low-toxicity strains are available; a third is lacking and likely unobtainable.
comments.quote: A lack of a 3rd low toxicity strain is still a weakness

comments.issue: Some TOX+ and TOX- strains did not fit expectations, so the evidence may be insufficient for this format.
comments.request: Isolate strains from a third bloom event to strengthen the evidence.
comments.quote: Can the authors consider isolating a handful of strains from a 3rd bloom event (possibly this year?) to more clearly show experimental evidence in support of their findings?

reviews.assessment: Satisfied with the revision; the only remaining point is a discrepancy between the uploaded movies and the numbered movies.
strengths: valuable new experiment showing contact is needed to kill prey

comments.issue: Only 13 movies are uploaded although the manuscript refers to movies 1-14.
comments.request: Upload the missing movie and make movie names follow the numbering.
comments.quote: there are only 13 movies uploaded and the manuscript has movies 1-14

title: Behavioural differences underlie toxicity and predation variation in blooms of Prymnesium parvum

study.system: ectotherms; individual-based simulations of thermal performance curves

editor_summary: Potentially suitable and original; both reviewers found problems: present the thermodynamic effect better, add methods detail, and balance the discussion on generation time and GSTO/TDE constraints.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-executed simulation study; asks for clearer presentation of the thermodynamic effect, generation time effects and constraint evidence.
strengths: well-written and easy to understand by a broad audience

comments.issue: The thermodynamic effect is not sufficiently described, and its incompatibility with the generalist-specialist trade-off unless relaxed is not explained.
comments.request: Describe the TDE and its relation to GSTO better in the Introduction and/or Figure 1.
comments.quote: I find that the "thermodynamic effect" (TDE; also known as "hotter-is-better") is not sufficiently described.

comments.issue: Generation time is fixed at 150 days although it is temperature-dependent, so thermal fluctuations within a generation differ among populations.
comments.request: Comment on how temperature-dependent generation time would affect the results.
comments.quote: The simulations conducted for this study have a fixed generation time (150 days). However, the generation time is also temperature-dependent, given the effects of temperature on development rate

comments.issue: The Discussion implies GSTO and TDE constraints are ubiquitous and unavoidable, ignoring studies finding weak or absent constraints.
comments.request: Restructure the Discussion to cite evidence for and against these constraints.
comments.quote: I got the impression that the authors claim that GSTO and TDE constraints are ubiquitous and unavoidable.

comments.issue: The projected increases in mean temperature and thermal variability are mentioned twice in the Introduction.
comments.request: Merge the two passages to improve flow.
comments.quote: The authors mention the projected increases in mean temperature and thermal variability twice in the Introduction: lines 58 – 60 and 92 – 95.

comments.issue: Copy edit: 'axis' should be 'axes' at line 88.
comments.quote: Line 88: "axis" -> "axes"

comments.issue: The statement about increasing thermal variability ignores places where variability is expected to decrease.
comments.request: Add 'on average' at lines 109-110.
comments.quote: In some places, however, thermal variability is expected to decrease. Thus, I suggest that authors add "on average" in lines 109 – 110.

title: Evolutionary constraints mediate extinction risk under climate change

study.system: matrix population models across plants and animals; comparative analysis

editor_summary: Editor finds the idea interesting but flags R1's concerns about excluding age-structured models and high-lambda matrices, and R2's point that statements about entropy concern models.

reviews.assessment: Finds the near-neutral result interesting but doubts the animal sample and high-lambda matrices, and finds the entropy language confusing.
strengths: interesting finding that life-course variation is close to neutral

comments.issue: Animal inclusion is biased toward plant-like growth forms; representativeness of the animal sample is questionable.
comments.request: Justify including animals or restrict claims to plant-like taxa.
comments.quote: I am somewhat skeptical about the inclusion of animals in this paper at all - the animals that are included are almost exclusively species with more plant-like growth forms and life histories

comments.issue: Relationship between stochasticity/luck theory and the genetic theories discussed is not explained, nor what selection on entropy means.
comments.request: Explain this theoretical relationship and the meaning of selection for entropy.
comments.quote: I wonder if the authors could explain a bit more about what it means for there to be positive or negative selection for population entropy.

comments.issue: Language around population entropy is inconsistent (diversification, diversity, rate of diversification).
comments.request: Use clear and consistent terminology for population entropy.
comments.quote: I request that the authors be more clear and consistent in how they refer to population entropy

comments.issue: Matrices with very high lambda values are included and may drive the weak-selection-for-diversification assertion.
comments.request: Justify or exclude extreme-lambda matrices and test their influence.
comments.quote: I have some concerns about the inclusion of population matrices with very high lambda values

comments.issue: Introduction and Abstract state no strong evidence for selection while the Discussion claims weak selection for greater diversification.
comments.request: Make the strength of the selection claims consistent across sections.
comments.quote: the end of the Introduction states that there is no strong evidence for selection in either direction with respect to population entropy, while the beginning of the Discussion argues that there is weak selection for greater diversification

comments.issue: Phrasing about low entropy and life course groups is confusing.
comments.request: Simplify the sentence.
comments.quote: I find this phrasing very confusing. Can you simplify this sentence?

comments.issue: It is not checked whether extreme sensitivities come from transition rates close to 1 or 0.
comments.request: Test the origin of extreme sensitivity values.
comments.quote: Did you look into whether those extreme sensitivities do tend to come from transition rates that are close to 1 or 0?

comments.issue: Justification for using a different threshold (0.02) for the plant data is missing.
comments.request: Explain the choice of threshold relative to the 3 sd criterion.
comments.quote: How does 0.02 compare with 3 times the sd for sensitivities of lambda in the plant data? Why did you use a different number for this data set?

comments.issue: Green top-left box in Fig 1 is not explained in the legend.
comments.request: Explain or fix the colour coding.
comments.quote: Why is the top left corner box green? This is not indicated with the legend information.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether divisible matrices were used and how matrices with multiple offspring types were handled.
comments.request: Describe the matrix selection and offspring handling.
comments.quote: Did you use divisible matrices from COM(P)ADRE where you could look at both fertility and survival/growth/retrogression transitions? How did you deal with matrices that have multiple types of offspring?

comments.issue: Fig 1 caption formula is written incorrectly.
comments.request: Correct the formula in the caption.
comments.quote: Fig 1 caption typo: “n=1-(Number of non-zero column elements)” should be “n=(Number of non-zero column elements)-1.”

comments.issue: Supplemental figure S1 is too pixelated to read when zoomed.
comments.request: Increase resolution or split the panels.
comments.quote: Supplemental figure S1 needs to be higher-resolution or re-formatted to split up the panels.

comments.issue: The fitness-diversification relationship may be driven by extreme-lambda models and the sentence is misleading.
comments.request: Re-run the slope analysis using only models shown in Fig 2.
comments.quote: If you restrict to the models shown in Fig 2, is the slope different from 0?

comments.issue: Zero slopes are not examined; it is unclear if sensitivities are near zero or points are uncorrelated.
comments.request: Investigate sensitivities and slopes among individual matrices and studies.
comments.quote: Did you investigate some of the sensitivities and slopes from individual matrices or among the matrices from the same species/study?

title: Adaption, neutrality and life‐course diversity

study.system: conceptual viewpoint on eco-evolutionary integration

editor_summary: Two reviewers found little new and questioned clarity/structure; a third saw value after initially struggling; normally a rejection, but the positive review earns a chance to extract and expand the gold nugget.

reviews.assessment: Initially disinclined but found the argument useful, interesting and reasonably novel; merits must be made clear much earlier, with reframing and missing literature added.
strengths: the main point is valuable once seen

comments.issue: The paper's merits are not apparent early enough; readers may stop after the abstract.
comments.request: Make the main point and its value clear much earlier.
comments.quote: The current problem is that these merits need to be clear much earlier – or everyone will just write it off and it won’t have any impact.

comments.issue: The point that microbial evolution can be studied in the lab is not made clearly.
comments.request: State more clearly that lab approaches can already study microbial evolution.
comments.quote: The authors should make this point more clearly – that it can be done in the lab with current approaches.

comments.issue: The paper would be stronger if framed around fundamental tenets of evolutionary biology that must be broken down.
comments.request: Reframe the paper around the two (or three) tenets blocking integration.
comments.quote: I feel the paper would be much stronger and attract much more attention if it was set up that way

comments.issue: Prior attempts to break down the wall (group selection, community heritability, functional traits, Price equation, gene-frequency approaches) are not explicitly discussed.
comments.request: Explicitly list and explain these previous attempts.
comments.quote: In addition to this small reframing, I think the paper would be better for more explicitly listing and explaining a few instances where ecologists have – in fact – tried to break down the wall by doing more-or-less what the authors suggest.

comments.issue: The Hendry reference is the 2020 re-issue and the Goevert et al. eco-evo feedback review is missing.
comments.request: Replace Hendry (2020) with Hendry (2017) and cite Goevert et al.
comments.quote: Please replace Hendry (2020) with Hendry (2017). The later one is just the soft-cover re-issue of the older one.

reviews.assessment: The disciplinary-wall setup is an overreaching strawman and the two reasons are disconnected; the microbial genotype/species points are more novel but need reframing.
strengths: arguments about genotypes vs species are among the more novel views
hierarchies section is more interesting as tangible concepts

comments.issue: The premise that ecology and evolution are separate disciplines is an overreaching strawman.
comments.request: Revise the setup to acknowledge the many threads uniting the fields.
comments.quote: The setup from the beginning seems an overreaching strawman to me, ie, that ecology and evolution are separate disciplines.

comments.issue: The two reasons for breaking down the wall are discrete and seemingly disconnected, making the connection feel forced.
comments.request: Reframe, perhaps as a context for studying microorganisms rather than an artificial wall.
comments.quote: It further struck me as oddly distracting that two identified reasons to break down the wall are so discrete and seemlingly disconnected –(1) microorganisms (2) response to environmental change.

comments.issue: The levels of selection/adaptation paragraph has unclear context and is not connected to the two named benefits.
comments.request: Connect the hierarchy section to the paper's theme.
comments.quote: I found the levels of selection (adaptation) paragraph (134-160) to be of unclear context. It wasn’t clear to be why this hierarchy was central to the theme

comments.issue: The final pages on hierarchies are interesting but not linked to the original premise.
comments.request: Reframe the beginning so the hierarchy material fits the premise.
comments.quote: The (roughly) last two pages focused on hierarchies, which I found more interesting as a set of tangible concepts, but was not linked to the original premise in a clear way.

reviews.assessment: Agrees integration matters but finds the wall metaphor a strawman, the history caricatured, the two suggestions disconnected, and the structure weak and superficial.
strengths: agrees greater integration between the disciplines is needed
interesting challenge in applying evolution practices across microbes and macroorganisms

comments.issue: The manuscript does not articulate a clear perspective that would help lead the field forward.
comments.request: Propose a genuinely new perspective that advances the field.
comments.quote: My main criticism with the current manuscript is that it doesn’t articulate a clear perspective that would actually help lead the field forward.

comments.issue: The paper breezes over progress and caricatures the history of eco-evo, misrepresenting evolutionary biology's integration.
comments.request: Acknowledge the integrative progress in evolutionary biology and ecology.
comments.quote: One of my concerns is that the paper breezes over the substantial progress that has been made, and in doing so makes a caricature of the history of eco-evo that is not entirely accurate.

comments.issue: The wall metaphor is overblown and functions as a strawman motivating the paper.
comments.request: Temper or justify the wall metaphor.
comments.quote: Overall, in the lead-up to this paper, I think the “wall” metaphor seems a bit overblown, and a bit of a strawman hypothesis to motivate the importance of the paper (i.e. leading up to L69).

comments.issue: The two suggestions are disconnected and look like tinkering with the authors' own previous ideas rather than responses to the grand challenge.
comments.request: Motivate the problem better and show how the two issues address it.
comments.quote: Integrating 2 disciplines is presented as a major challenge, but these two suggestions seem like just tinkering with 2 somewhat unrelated ideas that stem from the authors’ own previous work.

comments.issue: It is unclear what ecology and evolution mean in the horizontal gene transfer context, as HGT fits both disciplines.
comments.request: Clarify how ecological versus evolutionary processes are defined here.
comments.quote: Ecology is a discipline and ecologists have decided to call several processes “ecological processes”, but is horizontal gene transfer (HGT) an ecological or evolutionary process.

comments.issue: Abstraction failures are misdiagnosed as a disciplinary wall, and microbial evolution is less neglected than claimed, with relevant HGT literature omitted.
comments.request: Reframe the problem and cite ongoing ecological-evolutionary HGT efforts.
comments.quote: Such failures of abstraction are not about “breaking down the wall” between the disciplines, but rather ecologists trying to cling to abstractions that don’t work in some cases.

comments.issue: The microbial section is unfocused, not particularly novel, offers no path forward, and skips complex adaptive systems work.
comments.request: Focus the section and provide a clear way forward.
comments.quote: But just saying that doesn’t get us very far, is not a particularly novel point, and offers no particular path forward (other than telling people to study microbes).

comments.issue: Definitions of adaptation and adaptedness are inaccurate and presented without the necessary history or nuance.
comments.request: Present the definitions and their history carefully.
comments.quote: Here as well, these definitions of adaptation and adaptedness are not entirely accurate, and not carefully presented. If you are proposing to redefine adaptation, then getting the history and nuance right is really important.

comments.issue: The argument for measuring improved performance is unconvincing and does not show a useful way forward.
comments.request: Rework or drop the performance-measurement argument.
comments.quote: I’m not sure your argument of measuring “improved performance” is very convincing, and I don’t find it a useful way forward.

comments.issue: Boundary objects and resilience/resistance are underexplored tangents, and the paper ends abruptly.
comments.request: Explain these concepts usefully or remove them, and provide a clear ending.
comments.quote: but it doesn’t really explain in any useful detail why they are useful, and so they feel like underexplored tangents. The paper then ends rather abruptly

comments.issue: The overall structure is weak with too many superficial and disconnected ideas.
comments.request: Restructure into a coherent narrative that proposes something new.
comments.quote: Overall, I am left with the impression that the structure of the paper is weak, too many ideas are addressed superficially, and there are too many unexplained tangential ideas that are not stitched together into a useful narrative.

title: Opportunities to advance the synthesis of ecology and evolution

study.system: ferns and angiosperms; leaf pressure-volume and economics traits

editor_summary: Editor asks to solve the substantial concerns of referees 1 and 3; acceptance is not assured, but the interesting story makes the effort worthwhile.

reviews.assessment: Exciting topic, but the analyses are insufficient to test the interrelated traits and the discussion needs rewriting.
strengths: links pressure-volume parameters to the leaf economics spectrum

comments.issue: Pressure-volume curve estimation is error-prone; quality controls are not described and the curves are not shown.
comments.request: Describe data quality controls and show all pressure-volume curves.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors provide the details of data quality controls and show all the pressure-volume curves in supplementary

comments.issue: Calling saturated water content easy to measure is misleading because tissues can be over-saturated and corrections are needed.
comments.request: Discuss the measurement limitations and corrections for intercellular water.
comments.quote: The authors highlight the important role of SWC in plant functional trait net and claim that the SWC is an easy-to-measure parameter. However, this is misleading, in my opinion.

comments.issue: Using mean values in all plots discards individual variation, overinflates estimates and overfits the model.
comments.request: Re-analyse using individual sample values rather than means.
comments.quote: In all the plots, the mean values were used which is not appropriate. This throws away relevant variation that is occurring with individual samples and overinflates estimates.

comments.issue: Driven language implies causation where only regressions were performed.
comments.request: Use correlated to unless causal evidence is provided.
comments.quote: I would use 'correlated to' rather than 'driven'. In Bartlett 2012 paper, they simply did some regression analyses.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic but very hard to follow: unclear terms, too many parameters, and an inconclusive discussion.
strengths: topic of interest to a broad range of ecologists

comments.issue: The term leaf water relations is not clearly defined or motivated.
comments.request: Define leaf water relations and explain its relevance.
comments.quote: I did not clearly understand the term 'leaf water relations': what is precisely meant and why this is relevant

comments.issue: Too many parameters with complex relations overwhelm the reader; the paper should focus on its new results.
comments.request: Focus the manuscript on the key new results.
comments.quote: I was overwhelmed by the many parameters introduced and their complex meanings and relations.

comments.issue: The introduction leaves the term unclear, excludes stomatal conductance and transpiration, and does not state the questions.
comments.request: Define the term and clarify the questions addressed.
comments.quote: I was surprised that stomatal conductance and transpiration were not part of 'leaf water relations'.

comments.issue: The Box equations are hard to follow because many parameters are unfamiliar.
comments.request: Explain the equations and parameters more clearly.
comments.quote: The Box presents a set of equations with many parameters, many of which I was unfamiliar with. Therefore I was not able to understand and follow the equations.

comments.issue: The abbreviation SWC conflicts with soil water content.
comments.request: Rename SWC to SLWC.
comments.quote: I was confused by the abbreviation SWC for 'saturated leaf water content' as it often stands for 'soil water content'.

comments.issue: Whether and how the measured trait data will be made available is not stated.
comments.request: State how trait data will be made available.
comments.quote: I did not find if and how the measured trait data would be made available.

comments.issue: The results are hard to follow and Figure 4 cannot be understood without better parameter explanations.
comments.request: Improve parameter explanations and figure clarity.
comments.quote: I also could not fully understand Figure 4 because when I came to the Figure, I still had a poor understanding of the meaning of the leaf water relations related parameters.

comments.issue: The discussion offers only a basis for further work rather than conclusive insight.
comments.request: Strengthen the conclusions.
comments.quote: I had hoped for conclusive insight, not the basis for further analyses.

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed the manuscript; supports integrating water relations into the LES and asks for methodological clarifications.
strengths: addresses a long-unresolved topic since Wright et al. 2002
good job integrating water relations into the LES
manuscript was a pleasure to read

comments.issue: How species appearing more than once in the dataset were handled in analyses is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify the handling of repeated species.
comments.quote: How did the authors handle the species that appeared more than once in the dataset during analyses?

comments.issue: Calling assimilation light-saturated is questionable because irradiances may not saturate without response curves.
comments.request: Provide light response curves or revise the term.
comments.quote: I’d be cautious about calling this “light-saturated” CO2 assimilation when the range of irradiances looks hardly saturating (300-600 umol m-2 s-1), unless light response curves were generated.

comments.issue: 3 line-level copy edits (wording, a typo and a missing word).
comments.quote: L173 Leaf mass, not leaf weight.

comments.issue: The number of measurements per leaf is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the number of measurements per leaf.
comments.quote: Three to six measurements per leaf? Please specify.

comments.issue: Epidermis cell area is an imprecise term for the measured structure.
comments.request: Use crossectional area of epidermal pavement cells.
comments.quote: I suggest the use of “crossectional area of epidermal pavement cells” instead of epidermis cell area.

comments.issue: Two methods sections lack descriptive methodology and references.
comments.request: Add summary sentences and appropriate references.
comments.quote: These two sections could benefit from a more descriptive methodology and additional references.

comments.issue: The cell wall composition section appears without rationale and is not linked to the introduction or hypotheses.
comments.request: Explain why these variables were measured.
comments.quote: The “Cell wall composition” section of the methods feels like it is coming out of nowhere.

comments.issue: The R version is not stated and packages and functions are not cited.
comments.request: Report the R version and cite packages and functions.
comments.quote: Please mention the R version and cite packages and functions appropriately.

comments.issue: What scaled means in this context is not defined for non-R users.
comments.request: Define scaled.
comments.quote: Please quickly define what “scaled” means in this context for non-R users.

comments.issue: Box 1 is not clear enough to follow the authors' reasoning and equation solving.
comments.request: Add full equation solving and rationale, if needed in the supplement.
comments.quote: Box 1 needs more clarification. I am an ecophysiologist marginally involved in the field of hydraulics, so needed to do a significant amount of research on my own to fully understand the author's thought process.

comments.issue: Operations are missing mathematical symbols; multiply by is absent from equations 1, 3 and 4.
comments.request: Use mathematical symbols for all operations.
comments.quote: Please use mathematical symbols to indicate all operations. The “multiply by”, for example, is missing in equations 1, 3 and 4.

comments.issue: The Box lacks references at several sentence endings.
comments.request: Add references in the Box.
comments.quote: I’d also like to see more references in the box. For example, the sentence endings of lines L791, 793, 800 and 801.

comments.issue: Line 801 is unclear and the role of added constants in the equation is not explained.
comments.request: Explain each term and why constants were added.
comments.quote: Clarify what is said in line 801 and add references; why were these constants added if the equation previously described was po=Nos/DM?

comments.issue: Equations 3 and 4 lack introductions and step-by-step explanations of each term.
comments.request: Explain each term and step of the equation solving.
comments.quote: Equations 3 and 4 are the main points that need more though introductions and explanation of each term and step of equation solving

title: Incorporating pressure–volume traits into the leaf economics spectrum

study.system: global terrestrial vertebrates; fire, NPP and richness

editor_summary: Reviewers are excited and consider the ideas novel, but all three question analytical rigour and discussion depth; they ask about the 20-year fire data, alternative fire metrics and conceptual models of mechanisms.

reviews.assessment: Interesting broad-scale question, but statistical modelling is unclear, CV does not measure predictability, and the writing and hypothesis need work.
strengths: little prior research on vertebrate-fire diversity patterns

comments.issue: Model evaluation relies on R2 rather than significance, so it is unknown whether predictors explain significant variance.
comments.request: Report statistical significance rather than relying on R2.
comments.quote: It seems based on R2 (which is a poor measure of the goodness of fit) and not on statistical significance, so we do not know whether the variables in the model explain a significant part of the variance.

comments.issue: The selection procedure for fixed factors in the most parsimonious model is unclear.
comments.request: Describe how the most parsimonious model was selected.
comments.quote: It is also unclear the selection procedure for obtaining most parsimonious model; apparently the authors use AIC for selecting the random model, but it is unclear how they select the fixed factors.

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation is expected in a 1x1 degree grid, but its role in the modelling results is not shown.
comments.request: Address spatial autocorrelation in the models.
comments.quote: given that the data is a geographical grid (1x1 degrees), the spatial autocorrelation is expected to be high, so what is the role of this in the modelling results?

comments.issue: Coefficient of variation is not a measure of predictability, so it cannot test the predictability hypothesis.
comments.request: Use a proper measure of predictability rather than CV.
comments.quote: The coefficient of variation around the mean of a parameter over time (e.g., CV of the monthly NPP; i.e, temporal variability or dispersion) is not a measure of predictability.

comments.issue: Writing is immature, no clear hypothesis, and text is misplaced between Introduction, Methods and Results.
comments.request: Rewrite and restructure, stating a clear hypothesis.
comments.quote: The writing seems quite immature and requires more work. It lacks a clear hypothesis. Some text in the Introduction and some bits in Results would be better placed in Methods.

comments.issue: Title oversells by referring to animal richness while only a small proportion of terrestrial vertebrates is studied.
comments.request: Revise the title to reflect the limited taxonomic scope.
comments.quote: it's a bit daring to talk about “animals richness” when you are studying a proportion of the terrestrial vertebrates only

comments.issue: Pausas & Ribeiro (2017) example of fire-productivity interaction in richness patterns is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Pausus & Ribeiro (2017).
comments.quote: I miss Pausus & Ribeiro (2017 GEB) as it is an example of how fire and productivity interacts in global species richness patterns.

comments.issue: The claim that predictability matters for evolution is questionable and unsupported regarding stability and extinction of fire-prone environments.
comments.request: Back up or revise the claim about fire-prone environments and extinction.
comments.quote: Are fire-prone environments more stable and have lower extinction rates than non-fire-prone ones? If so, please back it up.

comments.issue: Reporting first findings with a figure reference is not appropriate in the introduction.
comments.request: Move or rephrase this sentence.
comments.quote: this doesn’t seems very appropriate for an introduction

comments.issue: Calling terrestrial vertebrates animals while excluding reptiles is misleading.
comments.request: Do not label the vertebrate subset as animals.
comments.quote: We focus on terrestrial vertebrates (hereafter “animals”): But reptiles are not included!!

comments.issue: Page 4 lines 44-53 read like methods rather than introduction.
comments.request: Move this text to Methods.
comments.quote: Page 4, lines 44-53: this seems more methods than introduction

comments.issue: The hypothesis to be tested is not stated.
comments.request: State the hypothesis explicitly.
comments.quote: What is the hypothesis to be tested?

comments.issue: Figure 1 contains too many small, unnecessary maps.
comments.request: Keep the two main maps and move the rest to supplementary information.
comments.quote: Some maps are unnecessary, and they are too small. So I would report here the two main ones

comments.issue: It is unclear whether islands were excluded and whether mainland was retained for mixed ecoregions.
comments.request: Clarify the island exclusion procedure.
comments.quote: I understand that all islands were excluded, is that right? So for ecoregions that have islands, you excluded the islands and retain the mainland, right?

comments.issue: Whether ecoregion area was recalculated after excluding islands is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how ecoregion area was computed.
comments.quote: I suppose this was corrected after excluding all islands. Please clarify.

comments.issue: Whether ecoregion mean values were grouped is unclear.
comments.request: Make the grouping procedure clearer.
comments.quote: do you mean that the ecoregion mean values were grouped? If so, please make it clearer.

comments.issue: Count data were log-transformed and modelled as Normal instead of using a Poisson generalized mixed model.
comments.request: Use a generalized mixed model with a count distribution.
comments.quote: Given that number of species are counts, why not using generalized mixed models with Poisson distribution (or similar) instead of the log-transformation

comments.issue: It is unclear whether fire losses is the same as fire consumption used elsewhere.
comments.request: Use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: is this the same as “Fire consumption” used in other parts of the manuscript

comments.issue: Page 7 lines 28-34 may be a priori restrictions rather than results.
comments.request: Move this text to Methods if it is not a result.
comments.quote: Are these results? Or a priori restrictions (methods)?

comments.issue: Comments about latitudinal patterns are not supported by any statistics.
comments.request: Support these statements with statistics or remove them.
comments.quote: all these comments about latitudinal patterns are not supported by any statistics

comments.issue: Figure 2 does not show variability and its purpose is unclear.
comments.request: Replace with boxplots showing variation across ecoregions.
comments.quote: I do not see the point of this figure; the variability is missing.

comments.issue: Page 8 lines 41-56 text belongs in Methods, not Results.
comments.request: Move this text to Methods.
comments.quote: This text is related to Methods, not Results

comments.issue: Terms such as statistically clear and clear effects are ambiguous and should not replace statistical significance.
comments.request: Define or replace the term, perhaps using gradual evidence language.
comments.quote: “Statistically clear”, “clear effects” “clear trend”: do you mean “Statistically significant”?

comments.issue: Table 1 lacks standard deviations per biome.
comments.request: Add SD for each biome across ecoregions.
comments.quote: Table 1: could you add SD? (for each biome, across ecoregions)

comments.issue: It is questionable whether models with different dependent variables can be compared.
comments.request: Clarify how models with different response variables were compared.
comments.quote: Can you compare models with different dependent variable?

comments.issue: Negative richness-area trends suggest an important variable is missing from the model.
comments.request: Investigate the missing variable behind the area result.
comments.quote: negative species richness trends with area! - Of course, this cannot be “real”, but may suggest that some important variable is missing in the modelling.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether after removing means a backward procedure or after accounting for.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: is this a backward procedure? Or do you mean “after accounting for”?

comments.issue: Area appears on both sides of the model, suggesting species density rather than richness was modelled, which is not described in Methods.
comments.request: Clarify the model specification and whether density was modelled.
comments.quote: I’m surprised that area (Km2) are in both the dependent and the independent part of the model. Is that correct? This is not mentioned in the Methods.

comments.issue: Abstract claims phylogenetic effects were considered, but the Results do not show this.
comments.request: Show the phylogenetic analysis or revise the abstract.
comments.quote: the abstract suggest that the analysis consider phylogenetic effects, but it doesn’t seems the case after reading the Results

reviews.assessment: Interesting and novel fire analysis with strong correlations; queries about habitat structure, body size and the short fire record.
strengths: surprisingly strong correlations with birds and mammals
important addition to the species-richness question

comments.issue: Fire affects habitat structure and succession, an alternative pathway to richness distinct from the fire-NPP connection.
comments.request: Discuss fire effects on structure separately from NPP.
comments.quote: I think fire effects on structure (biomass) rates some mention distinct from the fire/NPP connection.

comments.issue: End-Pleistocene mammal extinctions and body-size effects may underlie the richness patterns and warrant follow-up.
comments.request: Consider body-size and historical extinction effects in follow-up work.
comments.quote: I wondered how the patterns had been impacted by end Pleistocene mammal extinctions but then assume that most of the species underlying the pattern are probably small mammals.

comments.issue: Fire cycle estimates in Table 1 far exceed the 18-year record; how they were derived is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the assumptions behind the fire cycle estimates.
comments.quote: Some explanation is needed on how these estimates, which greatly exceed the data record, were made.

comments.issue: Extending the short satellite record across all biomes likely misses longer-term fire patterns, which needs discussion.
comments.request: Discuss the limitation of the short fire record.
comments.quote: It does worry me that extending the short satellite record across all biomes must miss these longer term patterns.

reviews.assessment: Novel, exciting first global animal-fire analysis that is robust and well communicated, but fire-data timing and interpretation need improvement.
strengths: first comprehensive global analysis of animal-fire relationships
eye-catching figures and links to a wealth of literature

comments.issue: 1997-2015 fire data mixes up relationships: high-richness tropical areas may reflect human-induced transformation rather than fire promoting biodiversity.
comments.request: Disentangle areas with recent fire-regime changes from long-term fire patterns.
comments.quote: But in this case it doesn’t reflect that fire promotes biodiversity – it means biodiversity hotspots have been disproportionately subject to human-induced landscape transformation.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether other fire activity measures such as area burnt, hotspot counts or radiative power were explored.
comments.request: Report preliminary analyses with alternative fire measures.
comments.quote: Were other measures of fire activity explored before settling on the fraction consumed variable?

comments.issue: Fire cycle and fire consumption cycle are described but not included in the models or preliminary exploration.
comments.request: Include fire cycle variables in model exploration.
comments.quote: they seem such useful descriptors that I wasn’t sure why there weren’t included in the models or preliminary model exploration.

comments.issue: Pooling 10 km biodiversity and 0.25 degree fire data to ecoregions may mask patterns; the case for pooling is not made in the main text.
comments.request: Justify pooling to ecoregions and test whether averaging masks patterns.
comments.quote: Why was the data pooled to ‘ecoregion’? Could some interesting patterns be masked by averaging the data across very large ecoregions?

comments.issue: Discussion misses the opportunity to present a formal list of mechanisms underlying fire-biodiversity relationships.
comments.request: Add a formal list of candidate mechanisms to the Discussion.
comments.quote: I think the Discussion would better orient new research (and perhaps be more citable, too) if it included a more formal (numbered or tabulated or graphically expressed) list of mechanisms

comments.issue: Abstract sentence suggests amphibians were remarkably sensitive to fire, contrary to the weak associations found.
comments.request: Reword the abstract sentence.
comments.quote: the construction of this sentence suggests that species richness of amphibians was remarkably sensitive to fire. Suggest reword.

comments.issue: Correlation between NPP and fraction consumed by fire is not reported and may affect models containing both.
comments.request: Report the NPP-fire correlation and address collinearity.
comments.quote: what was the correlation between the predictor variables NPP and fraction consumed by fire?

comments.issue: The number of ecoregions actually retained in the study is not stated.
comments.request: State the number of ecoregions retained.
comments.quote: it would be useful to state here what the actual number of ecoregions retained in the present study was, in addition to the number available.

comments.issue: The term statistically clear is not defined early and its intended interpretation is unclear.
comments.request: Define the term, ideally in the Methods.
comments.quote: the term ‘statistically clear’ needs to be defined early on, ideally in the Methods

comments.issue: The muted species-area relationship may result from excluding small ecoregions, narrowing the range examined.
comments.request: Assess the effect of excluding small ecoregions.
comments.quote: The muted or unexpected relationship with area may be because small ecoregions were not included in the analyses.

comments.issue: Primarily ecological versus primarily evolutionary is used without definition or examples.
comments.request: Define or illustrate the ecological-evolutionary distinction.
comments.quote: It would help the discussion if clearer examples or a brief definition were give here to show the author’s interpretation of ‘primarily ecological’ or ‘primarily evolutionary’.

comments.issue: Figure 2 panels would be more informative as boxplots showing within-biome variation.
comments.request: Convert Figure 2 panels to boxplots.
comments.quote: Most of these panels would be more informative as box plots. Boxplots would show variation in the data within each biome

comments.issue: Figure 3 panel a is split and the legend placement is suboptimal.
comments.request: Use a continuous axis and move the legend outside the panel.
comments.quote: Why is panel ‘a’ broken into two panels? Couldn’t the R-squared values be plotted with a continuous axis from 0.0 to ~0.75?

comments.issue: Table 1 lacks ranges or standard errors.
comments.request: Add ranges or mean ± standard errors to Table 1.
comments.quote: If there is space showing ranges or mean ± standard errors would help interested readers to interpret the data.

comments.issue: Figure S6 panels associated with the fire variable are not clearly labelled.
comments.request: Re-label Figure S6.
comments.quote: It wasn’t immediately clear to me which panels were associated with the fire variable. I suggest re-labelling this figure.

title: The role of fire in terrestrial vertebrate richness patterns

study.system: songbirds; insect food availability and breeding success; global meta-analysis

editor_summary: Editor is very supportive and calls it a model paper; asks for a deeper focus on biological results, more heterogeneity results, and careful consideration of the statistical methodology questions.

reviews.assessment: Praises the rigorous, well-written synthesis but asks to foreground biological results and reduce methods-heavy presentation and figures.
strengths: incredible amount of work collecting and synthesising data
top-notch pre-registered methods with many bias checks
clear results and a discussion that does not exaggerate

comments.issue: The Results section is dominated by methods-focused results, overshadowing the biological findings.
comments.request: Move methods-background results to a subsection or the Methods.
comments.quote: The Results section also contains a number "methods results"- background information on analyses.

comments.issue: Only Figure 4 presents results; other figures are background and methods.
comments.request: Add results figures, e.g. a summary of effect sizes.
comments.quote: only Fig. 4 is a results figure while all other figures are background information on the data structure or analysis methods

comments.issue: Figure 3 is not needed in the main text.
comments.request: Move Figure 3 out of the main text.
comments.quote: In particular, I don't thing Fig. 3 is needed in the main text.

comments.issue: 'Food availability' is too broad in the opening lines.
comments.request: Change to 'Insect declines' or similar.
comments.quote: I would change "Food availability" to "Insect declines" or something along those lines as "food availability" is quite broad here

comments.issue: Long sentences at lines 38-39 and 457 should be split.
comments.request: Break into two sentences starting the second with 'However'.
comments.quote: Break into two sentences with second sentence starting with "However,"

comments.issue: The objective of the analysis at line 240 is not stated clearly.
comments.request: Explain the objective, i.e. within-study biological relationships.
comments.quote: It would help the reader to add a bit more on the objective on this analysis which I think is to examine relationships between biological variables within studies.

comments.issue: Supplement figures are unlabelled and their text overlaps.
comments.request: Label supplement figures and fix overlapping text.
comments.quote: These do not seem to be labeled (e.g. S3) next to the Figures. Some text within Supplemental Figures is overlapping and hard to read.

reviews.assessment: Strongly supportive of the synthesis but asks for clearer methods, experimental-only sensitivity tests, and acknowledgement of causal-inference limits.
strengths: topical and overdue question given insect declines

comments.issue: Observational studies cannot separate insect-bird associations from unmeasured habitat quality.
comments.request: Acknowledge confounding in observational results.
comments.quote: both insect and bird outcomes could be driven by an unmeasured habitat variable

comments.issue: Pooled effects mix observational and experimental studies; study type may drive results.
comments.request: Run a sensitivity analysis using experimental studies only.
comments.quote: I would be much more convinced if you were able to demonstrate that the results were similar when based only on the experimental/manipulative studies.

comments.issue: Causal-inference problems are not recognised in the Discussion.
comments.request: Discuss the limits to causal inference.
comments.quote: At the very least the author should recognise in the Discussion the problems of inferring causality

comments.issue: Unclear whether covariate effects were established before adjustment; unnecessary adjustment adds error.
comments.request: Test covariates before adjusting effect sizes.
comments.quote: Did you first establish that there was an effect of bird family or habitat classification before attempting to adjust for them?

comments.issue: Bird family is less ecologically meaningful than foraging guild as covariate.
comments.request: Consider using foraging guild instead.
comments.quote: Wouldn't foraging guild instead of bird family have been more ecologically meaningful?

comments.issue: Adjustment uncertainty in effect sizes is not propagated into the covariance matrix.
comments.request: Include adjustment error in the pooling step.
comments.quote: Did this adjustment also affect the covariance matrix? It should have introduced some additional error to the effect size

comments.issue: Adjusting rather than modelling modifiers prevents estimating explained heterogeneity.
comments.request: Model habitat and family/guild as modifiers.
comments.quote: Wouldn't it have been neater to included habitat and bird family (or foraging guild or % insects in diet from the Elton database) as modifiers in the model

comments.issue: Relative change in insect availability is an obvious candidate covariate/dose-response term.
comments.request: Test or adjust for manipulation size.
comments.quote: One variable I could imagine being appropriate for this covariate adjustment step is the relative change in insect food availability among treatments within a study.

comments.issue: Data description outweighs results plots three to one.
comments.request: Plot study-level effect sizes, covariate effects and correlations.
comments.quote: The balance between data description and results plots is rather skewed 3:1. I would rather see more of the results!

comments.issue: Number of studies contributing to each meta-analysis is not shown.
comments.request: Add a figure showing study counts.
comments.quote: I would have also liked to see the number of studies in each part of the meta-analysis.

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not merit a main-text figure.
comments.request: Move Figure 3 to the supplement or text.
comments.quote: I am not so convinced that Figure 3 is really a main text figure, neither for me nor for the general reader.

comments.issue: Line 124: 'mediated' seems to be used where 'modified' is meant.
comments.request: Use 'modified'.
comments.quote: Line 124 - I don't think you mean mediated ('acted through') here, but rather modified ('affected by').

comments.issue: Semicolon makes the line 142 sentence awkward.
comments.request: Remove it and split the sentence.
comments.quote: the semi-column made this sentence rather awkward to read. I'd just remove and break into two sentences.

comments.issue: Phrasing at line 148 is awkward; observational/experimental distinction is meant.
comments.request: Rewrite as measured versus manipulated food availability.
comments.quote: this phrasing is a bit awkward. Do you mean observational or experimental that either measured or manipulated food availability, respectively?

comments.issue: Comparator is missing from the study inclusion criteria although needed for effect sizes.
comments.request: State the comparator criterion.
comments.quote: I am bit surprised you don't say anything about a comparator in your study inclusion criteria since that is needed to estimate an effect size.

comments.issue: Body condition is not defined.
comments.request: Provide the definition of body condition.
comments.quote: provide your definition of body condition then.

comments.issue: Broad concepts are buried in the SI instead of the main text.
comments.request: Mention these concepts in the text.
comments.quote: its worth mentioning these broad concepts here rather than buried in the SI.

comments.issue: 'Element' and 'concept' are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Check the terminology.
comments.quote: You previously used the term 'element' (line 146), check whether you mean element here instead of concept.

comments.issue: Rule for retaining duplicates at line 166 is not explained.
comments.request: State the duplication rule.
comments.quote: Presumably you just removed one of the duplicates? Did you have a rule for which to retain?
