comments.quote: it also raises the potential for a confounding effect of birds at lower altitudes being more likely to desert nests, which were then secondarily predated, which would not be possible to detect in your overall data.

comments.issue: The caveat at 8, 27 is a distraction rather than an important limitation.
comments.request: Remove or de-emphasize this caveat.
comments.quote: You’re comparing like with like so I think this is something of a red herring and a distraction from the other important caveats.

title: Changing patterns of nest predation and predator communities along a tropical elevation gradient

study.system: 16 lake types across Europe; plankton phenology simulations

editor_summary: Interesting study with the potential to make a stimulating contribution; both reviewers identify valid issues about the analysis and framing that need to be addressed.

reviews.assessment: Valuable and well-written simulation study with excellent figures, but model validation is inadequate and several analyses risk circularity and overstatement.
strengths: likely of interest to a broad readership
generally well written with excellent figures

comments.issue: Model validation relies on slope and intercept tests that can fail for reasons other than poor prediction.
comments.request: Use RMSE and meaningful, comparable units to assess predictive performance.
comments.quote: The authors test whether the slope of observed regressed on predicted deviates from 1 and the intercept deviates from 0.

comments.issue: Validation results are buried in the supplement even though the simulations depend entirely on model validity.
comments.request: Present validation prominently in the main text, ideally at the start of the results, and rewrite methods and discussion.
comments.quote: As the value of the simulations is entirely reliant on the models being valid then the results of model validation need to be prominent for the reader to check in the main ms

comments.issue: OAB and OD both depend on Kd, so OD cannot be claimed to drive OAB variation without a major caveat.
comments.request: Caveat or disentangle the shared Kd dependence.
comments.quote: you would expect some association between OAB and OD due to variation in Kd affecting them both

comments.issue: The phenology equations are already known, so the advance for Kharouba and Wolkovich's second question is limited.
comments.request: Clarify what the equations add beyond existing knowledge.
comments.quote: given that the equations to model phenology are known already, to what extent do these equations alone provide an answer to Kharouba and Wolkovich's second question?

comments.issue: Lake types are defined by the same variables (Kd, zmax) used to calculate OD, making OD-driven differences trivial.
comments.request: Redefine or justify the lake-type comparison.
comments.quote: seems to be trivial when these lake types are defined based on the same variables used to calculate OD (Kd and zmax)

comments.issue: Year-to-year variation in asynchrony, which matters for trophic interactions, is not summarised.
comments.request: Summarise interannual asynchrony variation in the results and supplement.
comments.quote: it is also interesting to know how much asynchrony varies from year to year under current and future conditions

comments.issue: A uniform +4°C scenario is questionable; a +2°C scenario would be testable sooner.
comments.request: Justify the warming scenario or use +2°C.
comments.quote: The value of using 4C temperature increases seems to be rather questionable. Why not instead make predictions for 2C that may then be testable in a few decades.

comments.issue: It should be clearer that the lakes are hypothetical simulations at 1,907 locations, and how the maps were derived is unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify the nature of the simulated lakes and map derivation earlier.
comments.quote: It could be made clearer earlier on that these are hypothetical lakes simulated for 1,907 locations for which there are data, rather than simulations of conditions in actual lakes.

comments.issue: The spatial distribution of the 1,907 locations is not shown.
comments.request: Add a map of the locations.
comments.quote: It would also be useful to see a map of how the locations are distributed.

comments.issue: Local adaptation likely makes phenological parameters vary geographically but is not considered.
comments.request: Consider local adaptation in the introduction and discussion.
comments.quote: the phenology of both Daphnia and algae will exhibit local adaptation. This may mean that parameters that govern these phenological responses vary geographically.

comments.issue: Line numbers do not match the text and restart on every page.
comments.request: Fix the line numbering.
comments.quote: The line numbers don't match up with the lines of text and restart of every page.

comments.issue: Temporal coherence is ambiguous; a clearly defined synchrony term would be better.
comments.request: Use asynchrony or synchrony with a clear definition.
comments.quote: The meaning of temporal coherence is a little ambiguous. Suggest sticking with a term like asynchrony (or synchrony) that has a clear definition.

comments.issue: Saying 1,891,744 lake years is misleading because yearly variation is averaged per lake.
comments.request: Clarify the basis of this number.
comments.quote: I think saying 1,891,744 lake years is potentially misleading when the yearly variation is averaged for each lake.

comments.issue: Four line-level wording edits: remove 'predictably' (Pg2 L23-24), write PLD in full (Pg10 L6), 'net' to 'average' (P14 L31-34), and 'phenological delays between the two trophic levels' (P17 L33).
comments.quote: P14. L31-34 Suggest changing net to average.

comments.issue: Climate variability across the simulations is not documented.
comments.request: Indicate how variable climate conditions are in the supplement.
comments.quote: it would be nice to have an indication of how variable climate conditions are in supplementary information

comments.issue: The 1979-2009 baseline includes substantial climate change, so it is not the pre-change reference state.
comments.request: Use a true pre-climate-change baseline.
comments.quote: the baseline period selected in this study (1979-2009) included substantial climate change, which means that it is expected to differ substantially from the true phenological synchrony reference state

comments.issue: Assuming the OAB threshold is constant across all locations conflicts with local adaptation.
comments.request: Justify or relax the constant threshold assumption.
comments.quote: is it reasonable to assume that this threshold is constant across all locations?

comments.issue: The section at Pg7 L11-19 is difficult to follow and lacks explanation.
comments.request: Explain why this is the case.
comments.quote: This section was difficult to follow and it could benefit from some further explanation of why this is the case.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the depth should be the upper 5 m rather than 2 m.
comments.request: Check and correct the depth.
comments.quote: Pg7 L50 should this be the upper 5 m rather than 2 m?

comments.issue: GAM motivation appears late and p-values are uninformative given the large number of simulations.
comments.request: Move the GAM rationale earlier and focus on trends rather than p-values.
comments.quote: Our focus is on the trends in the simulated data rather than the p values, which are always significant due to the high number of simulations.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 46 days is the SD; if so the 95% range would be about 90 days.
comments.request: Clarify the 46-day value and its uncertainty range.
comments.quote: Is the value of 46 days the SD? If so then in 95% of years the range of days would be +/90.15 days.

comments.issue: The text should note that OAB and the Daphnia maximum would never coincide even with matched timings.
comments.request: Make clear that some delay is always expected.
comments.quote: Should make it clear that the onset of algal bloom and the Daphnia abundance maximum wouldn't be expected to coincide, even if their timings were matched, so some delay is always expected.

comments.issue: Daphnia local adaptation may reduce the local asynchrony.
comments.request: Consider local adaptation as an explanation.
comments.quote: Daphnia may well show local adaptation to reduce the local asynchrony.

comments.issue: 'Lake type-for-time substitution' is undefined and how the study identifies space-for-time substitution is unclear.
comments.request: Define the term and explain the substitution logic.
comments.quote: what is meant by 'lake type-for-time substitution'? And please can you expand on how the study identifies space-for-time substitution as this wasn't obvious.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether light extinction and light attenuation coefficients are the same, including in the Fig 3 legend.
comments.request: Use one term consistently.
comments.quote: Is the light extinction coefficient the same as the light attenuation coefficient? Also applies to Fig 3 legend.

comments.issue: The plots show smooth-function partial effects rather than the stated relationships, including figure 4c-f.
comments.request: Correct the description of the plots.
comments.quote: The plots don't depict the relationship as such, rather it is a plot of the smooth functions, showing the partial effect of the predictor on the response.

comments.issue: Standard errors are not visible on any plot; it is unclear whether they are missing or too small.
comments.request: Show or explain the standard errors in the legend.
comments.quote: standard errors are not visible on any plot. Are they missing or are they all too small to be visible? If so, please mention this in the legend.

reviews.assessment: Interesting simulation, but it does not address Kharouba & Wolkovich's first question and the uniform +4°C warming scenario is unrealistic.
strengths: models a vast range of climatic conditions and lake properties

comments.issue: The first question is not Kharouba & Wolkovich's first question, which concerns the pre-climate-change reference state.
comments.request: Model the pre-change reference state, e.g., 1960-1980.
comments.quote: The first question is not really the first question of Kharouba & Wolkovich 2020.

comments.issue: The uniform +4°C warming scenario is unrealistic; unequal warming drives many trophic mismatches.
comments.request: Use proper climate scenarios with unequal warming.
comments.quote: the scenario used is that there will be uniform warming by +4°C. That is not what the climate models show

comments.issue: The abstract does not make clear what was actually done.
comments.request: Mention the 16 lake types, three decades, two scenarios and 1,891,744 lake years.
comments.quote: Abstract read well but not clear what the authors actually did.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the empirically determined Icrit holds for all 16 modelled lake types.
comments.request: Justify Icrit across lake types.
comments.quote: Is the empirically determined value for Icrit (1.3 mol photons⋅m-2⋅d-1) true for all the 16 lake types modelled?

comments.issue: The comparison between simulated and hypothetical OAB timing is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what this comparison is trying to achieve.
comments.quote: this section is quite unclear to me. Perhaps this is basic aquatic knowledge but it would still be good to get a feel for what the authors are trying to do here.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the TDM-TT regression holds for all 16 lake types.
comments.request: Confirm the generality of the TDM regression.
comments.quote: generally true, i.e. does it hold for all 16 lake types?

comments.issue: How often TDM was set to day 366 and what this means for PLD is unclear.
comments.request: Report the frequency and consider treating these cases as missing values.
comments.quote: How often was the TDM was set to day 366? And what does this mean for PLD? Would it not be better to use these year-lake combination as missing values?

comments.issue: The origin of the 1,891,744 simulated lake years is not explained.
comments.request: Show the calculation behind this number.
comments.quote: Where does the number of 1,891,744 simulated lake years comes from? What do I need to multiply to get to this number?

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 3 cannot be compared easily although the comparison is interesting.
comments.request: Put the two figures side by side as panels.
comments.quote: The way the figures are now organised it is not easy to compare Fig 1 with Fig 3 while that is quite an interesting comparison.

title: Impact of climate warming on phenological asynchrony of plankton dynamics across Europe

study.system: tropical soil animals; trenching and litter-removal experiment in Sumatra

editor_summary: Editor stresses the topic is important and the experiment well designed, but reviewers' concerns about overall novelty and implications require major revisions.

reviews.assessment: Well-designed, reasonable and timely study with clear writing; the reporting of the statistical methodology needs improvement.
strengths: replicated fully factorial manipulation across three systems

comments.issue: The abstract sentence is hard to understand and the 60% biomass reduction seems to contradict the claim that litter removal had little effect.
comments.request: Clarify the reduction and reconcile it with the claim of little effect.
comments.quote: This sentence is hard for me to understand. Was there a 60% reduction in animal biomass and, if so, doesn’t this contradict the claim that litter removal had little effect?

comments.issue: 8 line-level copy edits: wording, comma, verb forms, word choices and package name.
comments.quote: 63: Perhaps “and thereby to be of crucial importance”?

comments.issue: The response variable measured is unclear: whether animals were dried, weighed or counted.
comments.request: State what the response variables were.
comments.quote: 157-70: It is unclear from this passage what the response variable(s) measured was/were. Were animals dried and weighed? Counted?

comments.issue: The modelling approach is hard to follow, including the parallel creation of ~20 models and the fixed effect of taxonomic group.
comments.request: Explain the models and the role of taxonomic group more clearly.
comments.quote: I am having trouble understanding the modeling approach in this passage. My reading is that the authors here describe the parallel creation of ~20 models, one for each taxonomic group.

comments.issue: It is unclear what analysis is described, whether a third set of linear models or a prelude to PCA/Permanova.
comments.request: Clarify the analysis and the model structure used.
comments.quote: I am also unclear about what analysis is being described here. Is this a third set of linear models or a prelude to the discussion of PCA/Permanova?

comments.issue: The negative inference that trenching had no effect on diversity in some cases is not explicitly stated.
comments.request: Explicitly state the non-significant trenching results.
comments.quote: 239-41: Did trenching have no effect on diversity in rubber plantation soil and in the litter layer and deep soil of palm plantations? This appears to be the negative inference but is not explicitly stated.

comments.issue: Only one ANOVA table is provided although there are several main models.
comments.request: Summarize statistical output for each main model in Table 1.
comments.quote: Table 1: Why is an ANOVA table only provided for one model? Given that there is just a single table in this manuscript draft, it seems possible to summarize statistical output for each main model.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not show the litter types that the ecosystem comparisons rely on.
comments.request: Add an inset photo of representative litter from each of the three systems.
comments.quote: Figure 1: Would it be possible to include as an inset a photo of representative litter from each of the three systems?

reviews.assessment: Interesting and generally well-executed study, but the trenching artefact of increased soil moisture threatens the root-effect conclusion and many details need clarification.
strengths: many ecologists would be interested in the topic
strong point: 30 soil animal taxa analysed
great effort maintaining 48 plots over a year

comments.issue: Trenching raises soil moisture, an unmonitored artefact that could explain reduced soil animal abundance instead of root exclusion.
comments.request: Show that soil moisture and other environmental conditions did not differ between trenched and control plots.
comments.quote: It would be necessary to show that the soil moisture content (and ideally other environmental conditions) did not differ significantly between the trenching and control plots

comments.issue: 5 line-level wording and clarity edits (lines 45, 111-116, 279-281, 308, 378).
comments.quote: Line45: It may be better to describe “30 taxonomic groups of soil animals”.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether litter and root effects concern abundance or taxonomic composition.
comments.request: Clarify what the reported effects refer to.
comments.quote: Line 50: Litter and root effects on abundance or taxonomic composition? Please clarify.

comments.issue: The plantation types examined are not described.
comments.request: Describe what kind of plantations were examined.
comments.quote: Line 83: Please describe what kind of plantations were examined in the study.

comments.issue: The claim about litter resource depletion in plantations lacks references.
comments.request: Add references for litter depletion in plantations.
comments.quote: Line 227: Regarding the depletion of litter resources in plantations, references should be needed here.

comments.issue: How soil food webs are expected to be restructured is not explained in enough detail.
comments.request: Explain more fully how soil food webs are expected to be restructured.
comments.quote: Line 130: It may be better to explain in more detail how soil food webs are expected to be restructured.

comments.issue: Basic climatic information for the study sites is missing.
comments.request: Describe the climatic conditions of the study sites.
comments.quote: Line 135: Please describe the basic information on the climatic condition of the study sites.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the plastic screens were buried level with the soil surface so as not to block litter-dweller migration.
comments.request: State how the plastic screens were installed relative to the soil surface.
comments.quote: Line 148-149: Were the plastic screens buried in the ground to the soil surface level so as not to affect the migration of litter-dwellers?

comments.issue: No photographs of the plastic bamboo litter are shown.
comments.request: Add photos of the plastic bamboo in a supplementary figure.
comments.quote: Line 153: It may be useful for readers to show the photos of the plastic bamboo in a supplementary figure.

comments.issue: The way effect size was estimated is not explained explicitly.
comments.request: Explain the effect-size estimation procedure explicitly.
comments.quote: Line 177: The way how to estimate effect size should be explained more explicitly.

comments.issue: The model selection process is unclear and AIC values are not shown.
comments.request: Present the AICs of the models examined.
comments.quote: Line 184: The model selection processes are unclear. Please consider presenting the AICs for the models examined.

comments.issue: No data directly show soil animal abundance or treatment and layer differences.
comments.request: Provide data showing soil animal abundance and treatment or layer differences.
comments.quote: In the current version, there are no data directly showing soil animal abundance and the difference between the treatments or soil layers.

comments.issue: It is unclear what the GLMM response variables were and whether GLMMs tested treatment effects on abundance.
comments.request: State the response variables and role of the GLMMs.
comments.quote: Line 187: Were the GLMMs used to test the effect of litter and root treatments on soil abundance? What were the response variables in the GLMMs?

comments.issue: Effect-size estimation based on GLMM and LMM is unfamiliar to many readers.
comments.request: Add explanations and references for GLMM/LMM effect sizes.
comments.quote: I think that many readers (including me) are not familiar with the methods to estimate effect size based on GLMM and LMM. Please add explanations together with relevant references.

comments.issue: Trait data for the soil animal groups are not provided.
comments.request: Present the trait data as a supplementary file.
comments.quote: Line 203: The trait data for soil animal taxonomic groups would need to be presented probably as a supplementary file.

comments.issue: The planned contrasts used are not explained for non-specialists.
comments.request: Explain the planned contrasts.
comments.quote: Line 222: Please explain the planned contrasts for those who are not familiar with this statistical method.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether litter amounts differ between rainforests, rubber plantations and oil palms.
comments.request: Report whether litter amounts differ among the three systems.
comments.quote: Line 313: Are there differences in the amount of litter between rainforests, rubber plantations, and oil palms?

comments.issue: The link between the study and carbon modelling or ecosystem-friendly management is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the study relates to carbon modelling and management.
comments.quote: Line 393: It is unclear how this study can be related to animal-centered carbon modelling and ecosystem-friendly agricultural management. Please explain.

comments.issue: Figure 3 panels use the same colour for different treatments and confusing axes.
comments.request: Revise Figure 3 for clarity.
comments.quote: Fig. 3: The panels (b,c, and d) of this figure are difficult to read because the same color was used for different treatments and axes of x and y.

comments.issue: Figure 4 uses percentages instead of the effect sizes shown elsewhere.
comments.request: Explain or change the use of percentages in Figure 4.
comments.quote: Fig. 4: Are there any reasons to use the percentage for the panels (a) and (b) instead of effect sizes as shown in other figures?

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and competently analysed study, but its novelty is overstated given earlier work and several methodological details need clarification.
strengths: important tropical extension of earlier root-versus-litter work
likes the replacement of litter with plastic bamboo leaves

comments.issue: The novelty is overstated: Pollierer et al. (2007) already showed the importance of root carbon over litter carbon, though not in the tropics.
comments.request: Reframe the emphasis on showing similar results in tropical systems and amend the introduction.
comments.quote: Therefore, emphasis should be drawn to the fact you have shown similar results in these tropical systems. This emphasis also needs to be amended within the introduction section

comments.issue: Previous litter-versus-root research is not considered in relation to soil fauna functional groups such as anecic and epigeic earthworms.
comments.request: Consider functional groups rather than temperate versus tropical location when interpreting resource use.
comments.quote: Earthworms particularly anecic/epigeic species usually consume litter, therefore more likely that litter is important compared to roots. Need to think about the functional group of the soil fauna rather than whether they are located in temperate or tropical climates.

comments.issue: The term root trenching is used without being defined early enough.
comments.request: Define root trenching earlier in the manuscript.
comments.quote: Also, I think "root trenching" needs to be defined earlier within the manuscript, I had not heard of it described in this way before.

comments.issue: It is not reported whether any fauna lived in the plastic litter.
comments.request: State in the results whether fauna were found in the plastic litter.
comments.quote: Did you find any fauna living in the plastic litter? This should be stated in results.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the amount of plastic leaves matched the amount of litter removed, which has different consequences.
comments.request: Clarify how much plastic leaf litter was deposited relative to litter removed.
comments.quote: can you clarify whether the amount of plastic leaves deposited was kept the same across treatments OR was the same size as the amount of litter remove from each of the treatments?

comments.issue: Earthworm abundance and trench depth are unknown; fauna could move in from below the trench and compromise root exclusion.
comments.request: Report earthworm abundance and soil depth and address movement from below the trench.
comments.quote: How abundant were earthworms in these treatments, how deep is the topsoil/subsoil and trenching - could the earthworms (or other fauna) move in from below the trench?

comments.issue: Stating that litter removal 'little affected' animals conflicts with the reported 60% reduction in abundance.
comments.request: Reconcile the wording with the 60% reduction.
comments.quote: Line 48-49 states litter removal "little affected" but abundance was reduced by 60%? That's much more than a little affect!

comments.issue: The statement that root-derived resources matter more than litter for springtails seems obvious.
comments.request: Reconsider the novelty value of this statement.
comments.quote: Line 97-98 "root derived resources have been found to be more important for soil than litter dwelling springtails"

comments.issue: The carbon pulse from trenched plots would have disappeared before sampling a year later.
comments.quote: Line 330 the pulse of carbon from the trenched plots would have disappeared by the time these plots were sampled a year later.

comments.issue: Line 339 wording: 'to' should replace 'on'.
comments.quote: Line 339 to not on.

comments.issue: The link to the enigma of soil animal diversity could be included.
comments.request: Consider including the link to the enigma of soil animal diversity.
comments.quote: Line 341 this links to enigma of soil animal diversity, might want to include.

comments.issue: A strong sentence on lines 393-394 could be added to the end of the abstract.
comments.request: Add the sentence to the end of the abstract.
comments.quote: Line 393-394 this is a great sentence - I would add to end of abstract.

title: Plant roots fuel tropical soil animal communities

study.system: phenotypic plasticity in ecological interaction networks; conceptual perspective

editor_summary: Editor praises the review and its potential reach but asks to more strongly address how plasticity affects networks, present a compelling framework or data, and emphasize the novel perspective with concrete next steps rather than reading like a review.

reviews.assessment: Solid, innovative analysis of variation in interaction networks, but it reads too much like a review and should focus more on broad phenotypic variation.
strengths: bridges genomics, ecomorphology and interaction ecology

comments.issue: The manuscript focuses narrowly on plasticity and misses broader phenotypic variation, which also shapes interactions.
comments.request: Discuss plastic variation within the broader framework of phenotypic variation.
comments.quote: I’d like to see more emphasis, or at least mention, just variation

comments.issue: The PV–ITV discussion reads as an isolated review and does not keep the essay's novel interaction-network theme central.
comments.request: Refocus the variation discussion on ecological interactions.
comments.quote: I miss this discussion more focused to ecological interactions; now it reads quite isolated from the main theme of the MS

comments.issue: Too many examples before p8 divert attention from the link to ecological interactions.
comments.request: Reduce the number of examples and tighten the text.
comments.quote: The high number of examples is probably not necessary and really deviates the main attention from an effective link with ecological interactions

comments.issue: Additional scenarios, such as core versus peripheral species and effects on nestedness or centrality, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how plasticity may affect nestedness and centrality.
comments.quote: to what extent PV may influence other structural properties such as nestedness or centrality

comments.issue: Van Valen's early work on phenotypic variation and niche width is not acknowledged before the rediscovery.
comments.request: Cite Van Valen and related early work on variation.
comments.quote: This ignored even earlier analysis and emphasis on the importance of phenotypic variation in niche theory by Van Valen

comments.issue: The Fig. 2 discussion is not linked to Thompson's geographic mosaic of interactions.
comments.request: Connect the discussion to Thompson's geographic mosaic perspective.
comments.quote: recalls what J.N. Thompson brilliantly discussed in relation to geographic mosaics of interactions

comments.issue: Material up to p8 reads like a review of plasticity sensu stricto and deviates from the main theme.
comments.request: Summarize and edit the pre-p8 material.
comments.quote: I think the material present up to p. 8 (except the Intro) can be summarized and edited as it reads as we were reading a review of PV sensu stricto

comments.issue: A formal definition of “the interaction niche” and its components is missing.
comments.request: Provide a formal definition of the interaction niche.
comments.quote: Is there a more formal definition of “the interaction niche”?

comments.issue: The polyphenism discussion omits ontogenetic variation and sexual dimorphism.

title: The role of phenotypic plasticity in shaping ecological networks

comments.issue: Additional references should be included in the discussion to broaden the scope.

comments.issue: The timing of mass-gain effects and possible lag effects, such as poor condition during nursing increasing next-year skipping, are not addressed.

reviews.assessment: Well prepared, novel, sound and interesting manuscript with a clear logical flow, requiring only two very minor corrections.

title: Long‐term trajectories of non‐native vegetation on islands globally

study.system: eco-evolutionary dynamics; conceptual Viewpoint

editor_summary: Editor asks for conceptual clarification: define adaptation, show how the listed processes are not natural selection, restructure the Viewpoint beyond a shopping list, and revisit the selection-gradient model, multilevel selection and the bibliometric argument.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and timely; supports publication but finds the four 'underappreciated' processes may already be studied and need clearer novelty.
strengths: well written and an easy read

comments.issue: The four 'underappreciated' processes appear to have been dealt with in existing, sometimes uncited literature.
comments.request: Acknowledge prior work and clarify what is genuinely new.
comments.quote: I am just not entirely convinced that many of these have not been dealt with. They may not have been in the literature that ecologists typically read, but this is different than saying they are unexplored.

comments.issue: The drift example may instead reflect selection on unknown traits unless the populations are clonal.
comments.request: Clarify clonality and consider selection as an alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Just because the genetic differences are not known does not mean that there are not any.

comments.issue: Extinction vortices are a long-known, well-studied phenomenon.
comments.request: Acknowledge existing extinction vortex work.
comments.quote: This is an example of a long-known phenomenon, at least in theory. Is there not much work on extinction vortex’s?

comments.issue: The argument that population size affects mutation fixation under drift conflicts with the mu x N x 1/N result.

comments.quote: It is true that the number of new mutations in a population depends on population size. That does not, however, mean that the population level fixation rate of new mutations under drift depends on population size.

comments.issue: Fitness metrics beyond little r and soft selection have long been studied by evolutionary biologists.
comments.request: Acknowledge this existing evolutionary literature.
comments.quote: while it may be new to the ecologist, it is not new to the evolutionary biologist or even the evolutionary ecologist

comments.issue: The integration argument is not framed to persuade evolutionary biologists, who see rapid evolution as long established.

comments.issue: Cooperation and similar processes already involve eco-evolutionary game-theory scenarios.

comments.issue: The key message should be the shorter timescale, not that ecology-evolution interactions were unstudied.
comments.request: Reframe the message around timescale.
comments.quote: the key point to be made is not that interactions between ecology and evolution have not been studied, but that the timescale over which it occurs is much shorter than previously thought

comments.issue: The cited discussion of Bell et al. has a long history that is not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge the earlier history.
comments.quote: Bell et al may be the most recent discussion of this, but this has a long history.

comments.issue: The role of genetic architecture could be fleshed out given the extensive existing work.
comments.request: Expand the genetic architecture discussion.
comments.quote: This is interesting, that is how the genetic architecture influences eco-evo. This could be fleshed out more.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and clear overview that brings important future directions together; only minor clarifications requested.

comments.quote: The authors might consider citing Govaert et al. (2021), Functional Ecology which discusses a conceptual framework based on the interaction between evolutionary (selection, gene flow, mutation and drift) and community (selection, dispersal, speciation and drift) processes

comments.issue: The microbiology highlight disrupts the flow and lacks justification.
comments.request: Explain or relocate the microbiology point.

title: Beyond simple adaptation: Incorporating other evolutionary processes and concepts into eco‐evolutionary dynamics

study.system: Neotropical Ithomiini mimetic butterflies; occurrence, SDM and phylogenetic data

editor_summary: Editor praises the study but asks to make the message clearer; highlights Reviewer 1's concern about how bioclimatic niche versus distributions were estimated.

reviews.assessment: Likes the idea and finds the niche analyses sound, but flags circularity risks and unclear niche/distribution estimation methods.

comments.issue: Mimicry-niche convergence may be reversed: co-mimics could converge because they already share niche space.

comments.issue: Unclear whether bioclimatic niches use real occurrences or SDM presences; the latter would be circular.
comments.request: Use actual occurrences and state the data source clearly.
comments.quote: Are these actual species occurrences from the database of c. 29,000 records you mention in 2.1.2., or presences assumed from the results of your SDMs?

comments.issue: Bray-Curtis distances may come from SDM projections, replicating the niche analysis rather than measuring distributions.
comments.request: Clarify the data used and justify this analysis.
comments.quote: How did you compute the Bray Curtis distances? From species occurrences or from predicted SDMs? There is no way of knowing it from your text and Fig. 2, which depicts both occurrences and SDM predictions.

comments.issue: Euclidean distance between centroids may not capture niche similarity; overlap metrics are more appropriate.

comments.issue: SDM outputs represent potential, not actual, distributions; constructed communities are potential communities.

comments.issue: Only realized niches are analysed, so niche-evolution conclusions ignore biotic causes of absence.

comments.issue: "Convergence" implies fundamental-niche evolution but only realized niches were measured.

comments.quote: First, there are several instances (eg L 131, 142, 150 and many other places) where the authors use the term "species" but perhaps the correct term should be OMUs.

comments.issue: Unclear whether multiple OMUs of the same species are collapsed in phylogenetic analyses.

reviews.assessment: Generally supportive; three major comments on justifying ES and trait completeness, adding methodological detail, and discussing biological mechanisms.

comments.issue: The manuscript suffers from excessive eclecticism; many parts read like footnotes and digress from the main scope.

comments.issue: Several sentences on the listed pages are unclear.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and informative, but repetitive writing, an unclear abstract and missing citations undermine the clarity and value of the framework.

comments.issue: The trait database is not open and the R code archiving location is not stated, preventing reproduction.
comments.request: Provide the data for review and state where the code will be archived.
comments.quote: Unfortunate that the trait database is not open data. Unless the data used in this ms are also in the dryad data, it will not be possible to reproduce the results.

comments.issue: TRY trait values are potentially biased towards lower elevations; alternative databases and source proportions are not examined.
comments.request: Compare TRY with the Tundra trait database and report data sources.
comments.quote: The TRY data for widespread taxa are potentially biased towards measurements from lower elevations where plants might be taller.

comments.issue: Normalising to 0-1 rather than standardising variances lets high-variance traits dominate the integrated functional distance.
comments.request: Standardise trait variances.
comments.quote: This will cause some issues when calculating the integrated functional distance as traits with a higher variances will have more influence

comments.issue: Focal plants within a neighbourhood are not independent, inflating degrees of freedom and reducing p-values.
comments.request: Correct for the non-independence of focal plants.
comments.quote: the different focal plants in a neighbourhood are not independent as they comprise each others neighbourhood. I think this will inflate the number of degrees of freedom available and reduce the p-values.

comments.issue: A brief description of community change in the transplants is missing.
comments.request: Add a description of community change.
comments.quote: I think a brief description of the community change in the transplants would be useful.

comments.issue: Figures are placed at the end rather than integrated into the text.
comments.request: Integrate figures into the text.
comments.quote: I would have greatly preferred for the figures to have been integrated into the text. Having them at the end is an anachronistic.

comments.issue: Figure 1 would be clearer in colour.
comments.request: Use colour in Figure 1.
comments.quote: Figure 1 would be easier to interpret with colour (at least for the online version)

comments.issue: The Fig. 2 caption does not clarify the regression line and the whiskers are redundant.
comments.request: Improve the caption and remove redundant whiskers.
comments.quote: The caption needs to make it clear that this figure shows the regression line as the two points are potentially confusing. The whiskers on these points are redundant.

comments.issue: The integrated metric resembles height, raising questions about what it measures.
comments.request: Explain why the metric tracks height.
comments.quote: Why does the integrated metric so resemble height, at least for the alpine?

comments.issue: Fig. 3 panel order does not match Fig. 2 orientation.
comments.request: Reverse the panel order.
comments.quote: It might make sense to reverse the order of the panels so that it mathes the intercept/largest distance orientation in figure 2

comments.issue: The Figure S1 legend is unnecessary.
comments.request: Remove the Figure S1 legend.
comments.quote: Figure S1 - legend is unnecessary - all the information is in the strips.

comments.issue: The provided code does not run without missing arguments and is very slow.
comments.request: Provide runnable, efficient code.
comments.quote: As provided it does not run - arguments to the main functions are missing. When they are provided, the code was very slow so I reduced the number of iterations and it crashed.

comments.issue: The code duplicates functions and lacks a reusable package.
comments.request: Turn the functions into a package and remove duplication.
comments.quote: If the method works, I strongly recommend the authors put their functions into a package others can use.

comments.issue: The null model keeps the focal species fixed while randomising neighbours, biasing large-neighbourhood functional distances.
comments.request: Randomly assign both focal plant and neighbourhood.
comments.quote: for larger neighbourhoods, the null model is biases towards large functional distances. The solution is to randomly assign both the focal plant and the neighbourhood.

comments.issue: Shrub and wetland taxa were not excluded and extreme trait values need checking.
comments.request: Remove inappropriate taxa and check extreme trait values.
comments.quote: Juniperus communis is a shrub and has not been excluded. Also, there are wetland taxa such as Menyanthes, Phragmites and Sparganium that should probably be removed.

reviews.assessment: Positive; one of the best prepared manuscripts with solid methodology, though the writing and null model need refinement.
strengths: one of the best prepared manuscripts reviewed

comments.issue: The writing is complex and many concepts (e.g. hierarchical competition) are not explained accessibly.
comments.request: Simplify the text and explain concepts more clearly.
comments.quote: My main criticism is about the writing that is sometimes quite complex, and the multitude of concepts could be explained better.

comments.issue: The abstract emphasises conclusions and omits methods and actual results.
comments.request: Add methodology and results to the abstract.
comments.quote: The abstract is actually mostly about the conclusions, and it does not introduce the actual results which these conclusions were drawn from.

comments.issue: Figure 1 is complex and hard to interpret, with too many arrows and lines.
comments.request: Split into subpanels, use contrasting colours and show the sampling design.
comments.quote: I like the idea of having a conceptual figure (Figure 1), it is useful, but the figure is also quite complex and hard to interpret.

comments.issue: The null model ignores species abundances, over-weighting rare species, and missing-trait species are a non-random subset.
comments.request: Assess how these issues affect the null models and results.
comments.quote: As you use all possible species in the area without accounting their commonness or abundances the rare species will contribute to the null model much more than what they actually do in the ecosystem.

comments.issue: Statements that there is no facilitation are too strong for what the co-occurrence matrix can show.
comments.request: Soften the facilitation statements.
comments.quote: I think that this cannot be interpreted so simply from the co-occurrence matrix but may need information of the species abundances and the whole community context as well.

comments.issue: The studied communities and dominant species are not described.
comments.request: Describe the communities and common species.
comments.quote: I would also like to see some kind of description about the species communities and the most common and dominant species in the studied plots.

title: A spatially explicit trait‐based approach uncovers changes in assembly processes under warming

study.system: birds; simulation model plus phylogenetic comparative analysis of >6500 species

editor_summary: Three reviewers find the work conceptually interesting; main points: confusing structure with methods split across sections, unclear definition of cooperative breeding, missing methods detail, and requests for model code and simulation justification.

reviews.assessment: Interesting line of questioning with real potential, but analysis decisions, classification sensitivity, simulation integration and uncertainty propagation need attention.
strengths: interesting line of questioning set up by prior work
combination of model and meta-analysis has potential

comments.issue: Analysis decisions are not explained; the rationale appears late or never.
comments.request: Explain why each analytical choice was made as it is introduced.
comments.quote: in general the authors don't always explain why they have made certain choices and either you never find out or only find out when later steps indicate why the prior decision was necessary

comments.issue: Assigning one social system per species ignores within-species variation; a binary cooperative/non-cooperative split loses natural variability.
comments.request: Justify the single-system binary classification.
comments.quote: is it reasonable to assign a single social system to a species (L160-162)? You have also reduced social system to a binary of cooperative or not

comments.issue: The sensitivity of results to where the cooperative/non-cooperative line is drawn is not tested.
comments.request: Explore sensitivity of results to the classification cutoff.
comments.quote: Choosing where to draw the line could influence results, so have you explored the sensitivity of your results to this decision?

comments.issue: The meta-analysis is convoluted; a flow diagram of the analytical steps would help.
comments.request: Add a flow diagram explaining each analysis step.
comments.quote: Perhaps a flow diagram demonstrating the different steps would help explain what is piece of analysis is doing?

comments.issue: Many separate models trace a chain of predicted causal effects rather than demonstrating them; one path analysis might be better.
comments.request: Consider a single phylogenetic path analysis instead of repeated models.
comments.quote: is there not a single phylogenetic path analysis (or perhaps just fewer than you are currently doing) you could do that would get at these hypothesised relationships?

comments.issue: Simulations appear only in the Results, so they read as an afterthought and do not integrate with the meta-analysis.
comments.request: Present the simulation methods first and integrate simulation and meta-analysis.
comments.quote: The integration of the simulations into the rest of the MS needs more work, at the moment the outline of the simulations are all in the Results so they feel very much like an afterthought.

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: the very long sentence at L71-78 should be split, and Brooks et al. is missing its year.
comments.quote: L71-78 very long sentence, suggest splitting in 2.

comments.issue: A recent review of abiotic change and social interactions (Fisher et al. 2021) is missing.
comments.request: Cite Fisher et al. 2021.
comments.quote: also recently reviewed in Fisher et al 2021 "Anticipated effects of abiotic environmental change on intraspecific social interactions" Biological Reviews

comments.issue: Why these six environmental variables were chosen is not explained.
comments.request: Justify the choice of the six variables.
comments.quote: L174-183 why these 6?

comments.issue: The text should be clear that the fifth and sixth variables capture spatial versus temporal variation at different scales.
comments.request: Clarify the spatial and temporal scope of the variables.
comments.quote: so this is spatial variation – worth being clear and that your 5th and 6th variables above cover temporal variation at different scales.

comments.issue: How environments were chunked into harsh/variable versus benign/stable categories is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the two environmental categories were derived.
comments.quote: ok so are you chunking all kinds of environments into 2 categories? Did you do this by hand or with some kind of statistical classification?

comments.issue: Collinearity was avoided although it is not necessarily a problem when coefficients are interpreted correctly.
comments.request: Reconsider the collinearity-driven modelling choices (Morrissey and Ruxton 2018).
comments.quote: Collinearity is not necessarily a problem if you can interpret the resulting regression coefficients correctly

comments.issue: Lumping predictors into three categories loses variation and the p < 0.25 threshold is unjustified.
comments.request: Standardise predictors and report the full distribution of effect sizes.
comments.quote: Lumping into 3 categories loses a lot of variation and no good justification of using p < 0.25 is given

comments.issue: Uncertainty in the cooperative-breeding–climate relationship is not carried over, which can inflate type 1 errors.
comments.request: Propagate uncertainty through the linked models.
comments.quote: You are also currently not carrying over uncertainty in the cooperative breeding – climate relationship, which can lead to elevated type 1 errors.

comments.issue: The alternative that abundance influences range size is not considered.
comments.request: Consider the abundance-to-range-size direction of causality.
comments.quote: What if abundance influences range size – i.e., larger populations spread out more into less suitable habitat to reduce resource competition?

comments.issue: Lines 253-291 are methods and belong in the Methods section.
comments.request: Move methods text out of the Results.
comments.quote: L253-291 this is all methods and so should be in the Methods section.

comments.issue: The choice of a 23x23 setup is not justified.
comments.request: Explain why a 23x23 setup was used.
comments.quote: L256 why 23x23? Seems a very odd number.

comments.issue: The evolution of CA benefits under low external resources may be a trivial consequence of the chosen parameters.
comments.request: Show that the result is not a direct consequence of parameter choices.
comments.quote: is it surprising that CA benefits, which as set up by you in the simulations increase resource availability, evolve when external resource availability is low?

comments.issue: Assuming the harshness–CA relationship for part of the analysis risks circularity.
comments.request: Clarify how circularity is avoided.
comments.quote: So assuming it is true for part of your analysis runs the risk of being circular?

comments.issue: It is not tested whether clades without a sociality–environment relationship show no such pattern.
comments.request: Run the same comparison in clades lacking the relationship.
comments.quote: Should there be no such relationships in the clades without a sociality – environment relationship, and can you test this by running the same comparison in those species?

comments.issue: A simulation is called a formal mathematical framework, which it is not.
comments.request: Correct the description of the model.
comments.quote: A simulation is not a formal mathematical framework, that would be a series of equations.

comments.issue: The closing remark about humans does not fit the paper.
comments.request: Remove or reframe the human remark.
comments.quote: L536 this final remark about humans does not fit for me.

reviews.assessment: Innovative and potentially broadly interesting; major concerns are the unclear sociality/cooperative-breeding distinction and treating CA and RD cooperation as mutually exclusive.
strengths: potentially interesting to a broad audience
simulation predictions seem confirmed by the statistical models

comments.issue: Sociality and cooperative breeding are used interchangeably, and labelling social non-cooperative breeders 'non-cooperative' is misleading.
comments.request: Define sociality versus cooperative breeding and classify non-cooperative social species properly.
comments.quote: Throughout the manuscript, the distinction between "regular" sociality and cooperative breeding is not very clear. The terms sociality and cooperative breeding seem to be used interchangeably.

comments.issue: The CA/RD dichotomy is unclear: one individual could do both, and the two benefits may not be mutually exclusive.
comments.request: Clarify the dichotomy and explore combining both cooperation types.
comments.quote: Why can't one individual do both cooperation types? And why is resource defense always against conspecifics while collective action is always against other species?

comments.issue: The model code is not shared.
comments.request: Share the model code with readers.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to share the code of the model with readers.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether harsh environments must satisfy all conditions or only one.
comments.request: Explain the criteria for classifying an environment as harsh.
comments.quote: Do harsh environments satisfy all of these conditions, or are considered harsh even if only one condition occurs?

comments.issue: Several grammatical errors, e.g., 'it may success' in the SI and the sentence at L228-230.
comments.quote: There are several grammatical errors to correct, for example "it may success" (line 42 in SI).

comments.issue: The uniform distribution used for sampling is not supported by evidence.
comments.request: Justify the uniform sampling distribution from the literature.
comments.quote: Is there any evidence from the literature to support the sampling from a uniform distribution?

comments.issue: Whether individuals can change their cooperation level or type, and under what rules, is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the rules governing changes in cooperation.
comments.quote: Do individuals change their level of cooperation and the cooperation type? According to which rules?

comments.issue: The Methods section contains no details of the model.
comments.request: Add the model details to the Methods.
comments.quote: Actually there are no details on the model in the Methods section.

comments.issue: Lines 301-304 appear to contradict the statement at lines 83-87.
comments.request: Reconcile the contradictory statements.
comments.quote: L 301-304: This seems to contradict the statement at lines 83-87

comments.issue: R0 in SI equation 2 is not defined.
comments.request: Define R0.
comments.quote: SI equation 2: What does R0 represent?

comments.issue: The proportion of cooperators ignores cooperation level, counting 0.1-level cooperators as full cooperators.
comments.request: Account for cooperation level when calculating the proportion of cooperators.
comments.quote: When calculating the proportion of cooperators, is the level of cooperation ignored? For example, if most cooperators are at the 0.1 level, they are actually not cooperating much but would be considered full cooperators here.

reviews.assessment: Finds the article interesting, comprehensive and essential and recommends acceptance after mainly structural corrections, but the climate-change conclusion should be more modest.

comments.issue: Methods, results and discussion are systematically confused; methods text is repeated and results are overloaded.
comments.request: Restructure the paper so methods, results and discussion are separated clearly.
comments.quote: My main comment is that the authors systematically confuse methods, results, and discussion.

comments.issue: Some findings need more detail while other important findings get little attention.
comments.request: Rebalance the emphasis given to findings.
comments.quote: I also think that some findings needed to be more detailed, while other important findings received only a little attention.

comments.issue: The climate-change conclusion is too firm; CA specialists are vulnerable to ecological traps and disturbance, and other regions may favour generalists.
comments.request: Write a more modest conclusion about range shifts under desertification.
comments.quote: I would suggest the authors be more modest and write a slightly less firm conclusion

title: Environmental quality mediates the ecological dominance of cooperatively breeding birds

study.system: deadwood beetles; 332,557 individuals, 901 species, 49 tree species

editor_summary: Reviewers praise the novelty and writing; one doubts the conclusions are strong enough, so tone down claims and provide support for the concluding remarks (L477-481).

reviews.assessment: Well-written and broadly interesting, but the trophic-level conclusion rests on very few significant associations.
strengths: broadly interesting ideas with potential to inspire studies

comments.issue: Evidence for the population-size mechanism linking energy to diversity is not provided, though it is testable.
comments.request: Test whether diversity per individual tracks diversity if data allow.
comments.quote: A testable prediction would be that diversity per individual should exhibit less of a trend that diversity itself.

comments.issue: The trophic-level conclusion rests on very few significant associations.
comments.request: Provide stronger support or temper the conclusion.
comments.quote: the major conclusion drawn by the authors, that ambient energy was a major driver of diversity for higher trophic levels and substrate energy for lower trophic levels, appears to be based on very few significant datapoints

comments.issue: Significant temperature-seasonality associations that muddle the pattern are never discussed.
comments.request: Discuss these associations and their implications.
comments.quote: temperature seasonality (which should be negatively correlated, or perhaps uncorrelated, with ambient energy) is associated with greater diversity in mycetophagous and zoophagous beetles

comments.issue: Several line-level wording, formatting and figure-reference errors.
comments.quote: Line 162: Coleoptera is a family and shouldn't be italicized

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important data synthesis; needs a clearer justification of the beetle system and fixes to sloppy errors.
strengths: synthesis of a huge amount of data

comments.issue: Introduction does not justify why deadwood beetles are a suitable system to test the energy hypotheses.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for the beetle deadwood system.
comments.quote: The authors need to make clear in their Introduction as to why a comparison using the dead wood assemblage of beetles is an appropriate way to test the ambient/substrate hypotheses

comments.issue: Numerous sloppy errors and incomplete references throughout.
comments.request: Fix the listed spelling, wording and reference errors.
comments.quote: At the trivial level the authors need to fix a number of sloppy errors

reviews.assessment: Excellent data set on a highly relevant question; requests concern deadwood descriptors, sampling clarity and discussion logic.
strengths: excellent study system and data set
easy to read and well written

comments.issue: Sunlight is not the only factor limiting plant production; N, P or water may be.
comments.request: Qualify the statement about sunlight and plant production.
comments.quote: other factors than sunlight (like N or P or water) may be the limiting factors for plant production

comments.issue: Size, age and diameter ranges of deadwood objects are not described, though they affect the decay proxy.
comments.request: Report deadwood size, diameter and age ranges and comment on wide spans.
comments.quote: Especially, what was the minimum and maximum size (especially diameter) and the minimum and maximum age (as a proxy for decomposition rate) of dead wood objects included in the study?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether whole deadwood objects were sampled and whether trap area was standardized.
comments.request: Clarify sampling standardization in the methods.
comments.quote: When using stem-emerging traps it is possible to adjust the surface area that are surveyed by the traps, to get a standardized sample size.

comments.issue: Minor text edits: delete 'other', split long paragraphs, reorder a discussion paragraph, keep discussion at object level.
comments.quote: This is a long paragraph, which could be splitted into two or three paragraphs.

comments.issue: Discussion of regional diversity patterns would be more compelling with data on species pools or tree volume.
comments.request: Provide regional data to support the proposed mechanisms.
comments.quote: It would be nice if the authors could provide some data on this from the studied regions, to allow us to understand what are likely mechanisms behind the patterns in this study system.

comments.issue: The deadwood size effect could be a sampling artifact because sampled volume increases with object size.
comments.request: Clarify sampling and consider the sample-effect explanation.
comments.quote: the observed effect of size is only due to a sample effect – the sampled volume of dead wood increases with the size of the dead wood object

comments.issue: The rationale that large-scale variables reflect nearby dispersal sources is not explained.
comments.request: Explain this logic, perhaps in a separate paragraph.
comments.quote: it is easier for the reader to follow the logic here if you explain that these variables may be relevant because they reflect the amount of dispersal sources

title: Ambient and substrate energy influence decomposer diversity differentially across trophic levels

study.system: Mosquito-borne disease; temperature-humidity interactions in vector thermal biology

editor_summary: Editor sides with the detailed review: the review components are thorough but the humidity-modeling advocacy, citation precision and title (mosquito focus) require substantial revision.

reviews.assessment: Exceptionally well-written and useful perspective; asks for better justification of vapor pressure deficit and precise terminology.

comments.issue: The role of vapor pressure deficit in ectotherm water loss is a cornerstone but is not well described or justified.
comments.request: Better describe and justify the vapor pressure deficit effect.
comments.quote: The effect of vapor pressure deficit on water loss in ectotherms is a cornerstone of the demonstration and thus could be better described and justified.

comments.issue: 'Disease transmission' is technically incorrect because pathogens, not diseases, are transmitted.
comments.request: Replace 'disease transmission' with 'pathogen transmission'.
comments.quote: the authors use the phrase “disease transmission”, which is technically incorrect because a pathogen is transmitted, not a disease.

comments.issue: It is unclear what is meant at Line 165.
comments.request: Clarify whether mosquito-borne pathogens are meant.
comments.quote: Line 165: do you mean different mosquito-borne pathogens?

comments.issue: 2 figure cross-reference corrections (Fig. 1 should be Fig. 2; Fig. 2 should be Fig. 3).
comments.quote: Lines 195, 215 and 287: Fig. 1 should probably read Fig. 2.

comments.issue: 'Equilibrium water vapor pressure' is not defined; saturation vapor pressure may be meant.
comments.request: Define the term or clarify it as saturation vapor pressure.
comments.quote: equilibrium water vapor pressure has not been defined; do you mean saturation vapor pressure?

reviews.assessment: Questions whether the piece meets the journal's Perspective goals and whether it demonstrates added value beyond reiterating that temperature and humidity matter.

comments.issue: The manuscript may not deliver the new view or framework expected of a Perspective.
comments.request: Restructure to deliver a new view or framework.
comments.quote: I think this manuscript could be reorganized and edited to do this but question whether or not the text is addressing the journal’s goals for Perspective contributions

comments.issue: The claim that non-temperature variables are neglected is uncontroversial; studies using proxies are conflated with true neglect.
comments.request: Motivate more specifically and separate proxy use from true neglect.
comments.quote: Stating that variables other than temperature have been neglected (e.g., line 105) is not controversial, and most practitioners would readily agree.

comments.issue: The paper does not demonstrate how better humidity measures and responses would change inference or predictive skill.
comments.request: Demonstrate how humidity data change inference and predictions.
comments.quote: I had hoped the paper would move the needle a bit further in demonstrating how incorporating better humidity measures and mosquito responses could change current inference and predictive skill.

comments.issue: Studies are lumped together, missing the chance for a new mechanistic synthesis of humidity effects on specific traits.
comments.request: Unpack mechanisms and provide specific evidence-based synthesis.
comments.quote: I think this is a missed opportunity for really unpacking and drawing new synthesis from what is known (and unknown) about how humidity mechanistically influences specific mosquito survival and fitness traits

comments.issue: Citations are used loosely, making it hard to tell which source supports which statement or implies causation.
comments.request: Standardize citation practice and clarify evidence versus ideas.
comments.quote: the use of citations seems a bit loose (not standardized) – and it is distracting to try to parse out when citations support a general idea versus when they actually reflect data-based evidence

comments.issue: Citations at Line 73 are lumped together instead of paired with each listed consequence.
comments.request: Pair citations with the specific consequences.
comments.quote: it would be more informative to have citations paired with the specific consequences listed rather than lumped all together at the end.

comments.issue: Qualitative and quantitative thermal performance metrics are not defined.
comments.request: Define both metric types, preferably with examples.
comments.quote: I recommend adding a sentence or two here to define what this means (perhaps with an example of each type of performance curve).

comments.issue: The phrase 'significantly enhanced our ability' implies validated metabolic-theory predictions that are not evident.
comments.request: Temper this claim or cite the validating studies.
comments.quote: leads to the expectation of citations showing metabolic-theory based process models generated predictions that were validated in new climate scenarios. That is pretty specific and not really evident.

comments.issue: The subheading scope at Line 187 is unclear relative to the previous subheading.
comments.request: Streamline this section around what temperature alone predicts.
comments.quote: It isn’t clear from text that there is really a difference in scope (both seem to be review of studies that report influences on population growth and transmission potential).

comments.issue: The explanation of humidity measurement would work better as a box connected to why humidity matters.
comments.request: Move this material into a box and link it to importance.
comments.quote: it may be better presented in something like a box and used to highlight why humidity is an important metric to consider, as well as why it is often overlooked

comments.issue: The referent of 'this deficit' at Line 263 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what this deficit refers to.
comments.quote: Unclear what ‘this deficit’ refers to in sentence structure

comments.issue: The list after the Patz citation is not a list of mechanisms as implied.
comments.request: Correct the description of this list.
comments.quote: The list that comes after the Patz citation is not a list of mechanisms, as implied in prior clause.

comments.issue: The target of 'This limits' at Line 284 is unclear.
comments.request: Add a clearer transition linking the limitations.
comments.quote: The target of ‘This limits’ is unclear from sentence structure.

comments.issue: The shift from humidity to water constraints at Line 293 is confusing.
comments.request: Define how humidity influences body temperature and water balance regulation.
comments.quote: There is a subtle but potentially important shift here from humidity to water constraints in this first sentence that seems unnecessary

comments.issue: The meaning of 'to a point' at Line 319 and whether cited patterns are causal are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence and the nature of the evidence.
comments.quote: I’m not clear as to what this sentence really means, specifically the ‘to a point’.

comments.issue: Subsection 5 meanders without a discernible synthesis or specific support.
comments.request: Restructure this subsection around clear evidence and synthesis.
comments.quote: This section seems to encompass several short reviews with some meandering logical connections to the manuscript’s thesis.

comments.issue: Figure 3 is never mentioned in the text.
comments.request: Cite Figure 3 in the text.
comments.quote: Figure 3 is not mentioned in text.

title: Humidity – The overlooked variable in the thermal biology of mosquito‐borne disease

study.system: old field grassland; 22-year disturbance and nitrogen experiment

editor_summary: Reviewers see considerable potential interest but raise substantial concerns; editor asks particular attention to study design and data analyses.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive analyses with convincing convergence results, but the framing as a test of competing theories is not justified.
strengths: nicely complements a recent study on the same system

comments.issue: Work is presented as a test of competing theories, but it only shows patterns consistent with one of them.
comments.request: Stop stating that competing theories were tested; report evidence for one theory.
comments.quote: the authors present their work as a “test” of competing theories, whereas they are analyzing data patterns that are (strongly) consistent with one of them

comments.issue: Sinuosity needs a 2D representation and omits part of the multivariate variance, unlike the ecotraj metric.
comments.request: Justify the choice of sinuosity over the distance-based ecotraj metric.
comments.quote: the authors should justify this choice, as its application means that part of the overall variance is not represented in the analysis of directionality

comments.issue: Text at P3 L5 and P5 L92 claims a comparison of models, but no model comparison or fit evaluation was done.
comments.request: Reword the claim that models were compared.
comments.quote: The sentence is a bit misleading. I do not see a “comparison of models”, in the sense of evaluating their fit to data.

comments.issue: Sinuosity is evaluated in a 2D space.
comments.quote: P5 L120-121 But sinuosity is evaluated in a 2D space, isn’t it?

comments.issue: Unrestricted permutations may conflate treatment indicators with persistent field differences.
comments.request: Consider restricting permutations within replicate plots of the same field.
comments.quote: P10 L191-194 – Did you consider restricting permutations within replicate plots of the same field?

comments.issue: Text could use beta-diversity terminology for within- and among-treatment temporal trends.
comments.request: Refer to temporal trends of beta-diversity within and among treatments.
comments.quote: here you could refer to the temporal trend of “beta-diversity” within treatments (and in the next paragraph to the temporal trend of “beta-diversity among treatments”)

comments.issue: Sentence at P11 L202 is unclear.
comments.request: Revise the unclear sentence at P11 L202.
comments.quote: P11 L202 – Sentence not clear, please revise.

comments.issue: PCoA axes are not characterized before trajectories are described by their coordinates.
comments.request: Characterize the PCoA axes and add an indicator-species arrow plot.
comments.quote: I would characterize the PcoA axes before describing trajectory by reference to coordinates in them. Otherwise the reader cannot interpret dynamic changes.

comments.issue: Fig. 2 does not clearly show trajectories moving towards lower PCoA axis 2 values.
comments.request: Make the direction along PCoA axis 2 clearer in Fig. 2.
comments.quote: Not so clear in Fig. 2 that trajectories move towards lower values of PCoA axis 2.

comments.issue: Temporal evolution of dissimilarity between disturbed and undisturbed centroids is not shown.
comments.request: Show how centroid dissimilarity between disturbance treatments changes over time.
comments.quote: You could also show the temporal evolution of the dissimilarity between undisturbed and disturbed centroids of the same fertilization treatment.

comments.issue: Stronger priority effects under low fertilization, or persistence of low-nutrient-adapted species, could explain the result.
comments.request: Consider these alternative explanations for the low-fertilization result.
comments.quote: This results could point out to stronger priority effects on plots with low or none fertilization.

comments.issue: Figure reference at P19 L392 may be wrong.
comments.request: Check whether the reference should be Fig. 3-ab.
comments.quote: P19 L392 – Shouldn’t it be Fig. 3-ab?

reviews.assessment: Wonderful, well-written study with a clear message, but the 'undisturbed' label and lack of remnant comparison are major concerns.
strengths: excellent historical and contemporary framing of succession models
extremely well written with logical flow
clear, novel take-home message of broad interest

comments.issue: 'Undisturbed' and 'intact' mislabel previously tilled old fields, which readers will confuse with never-tilled remnants.
comments.request: Use different terminology, e.g. 'control', and state in the methods these are not remnants.
comments.quote: The un-manipulated grid (E001) in each of this (old) field is thus not ‘undisturbed’ or ‘intact’ at all--and getting the terminology correct is critical here

comments.issue: Past tillage may have left altered soil nutrients, so the undisturbed treatment may not be comparable to a true remnant.
comments.request: Provide soil nutrient data in the supplement to assess this.
comments.quote: It is also very likely that tillage agriculture in the past also led to increased/altered soil nutrients.

comments.issue: Without a true remnant comparison, the compositional trajectories are hard to interpret.
comments.request: Add old-growth grassland composition data for comparison.
comments.quote: I suggest adding even a single data point of an old-growth grassland composition at some time point

comments.issue: The example at lines 55-58 is not a plant example and is less appropriate for this paper.
comments.request: Replace it with a plant example.
comments.quote: Could you replace this with a plant example since that would be more appropriate for this paper?

comments.issue: Adjectives such as 'classic' for studies are subjective.
comments.request: Refrain from using adjectives like 'classic' for studies.
comments.quote: I suggest refraining from using adjectives like ‘classic’ for any studies since one could argue that what is and is not a classic is fairly subjective

comments.issue: Statement at line 94 flagged: This IS an ideal.
comments.quote: Line 94: "This IS an ideal

reviews.assessment: Important long-term dataset with appropriate analyses, but wants the full N gradient, among/within-field distinction and extended time series.
strengths: unique long-term 22-year experiment manipulating disturbance and nutrients

comments.issue: Only the first four of nine nitrogen levels are analysed; the high-N treatments are omitted.
comments.request: Analyse and report the full nitrogen gradient.
comments.quote: I strongly recommend the authors present analyses of the full N gradient, to see whether a higher or lower N addition rate would show similar or different temporal patterns

comments.issue: Convergence could arise among fields or among replicate plots within fields; the two sources are not separated.
comments.request: Distinguish among- and within-field variation and show trajectories within each field.
comments.quote: it would be critical to distinguish the contribution of among and within-field variation to the overall trends the authors found

comments.issue: Disturbance was annual while nutrient addition was applied once, so effects may reflect application frequency rather than the drivers themselves.
comments.request: Mention this treatment-application caveat in the discussion.
