comments.issue: Data after 2004 are not reported, so persistence of equilibria over ~40 years is untested.
comments.request: Report the whole time series, including post-2004 data if available.
comments.quote: I strongly recommend the authors report the whole time-series data (~40 years)

comments.issue: Species names are reported instead of life-history shifts from weedy herbs to longer-lived perennials.
comments.request: Show whether composition shifted from short-lived to longer-lived species.
comments.quote: I think it is more important to show whether community compositions shifted from short-lived weedy herbs to longer-lived perennials?

comments.issue: Figure 2 could be merged into one panel with colours for N treatments and arrows for trajectories.
comments.request: Merge panels a, c, e, g, i and consider dropping Fig. 4c,d.
comments.quote: Is it possible to merge panels a, c, e, g, i into the same one to show the trajectories of different treatments?

title: Disturbance alters transience but nutrients determine equilibria during grassland succession with multiple global change drivers

study.system: competition and predation niche-clustering models

reviews.assessment: Finds the extension to predation a useful contribution and recommends publication once interaction conditions and cluster dynamics are clarified.

comments.issue: Effective prey interactions are assumed to depend on niche distance, but this should follow from the structure of the three-trophic interactions.
comments.request: Derive the conditions on fundamental interactions that give niche-distance dependence.
comments.quote: Could you elaborate on the conditions on the fundamental interactions that would lead to the hypothesized dependence of theta\_ij, gamma\_ij on niche-space distances?

comments.issue: Cluster richness declines over time in Fig. 3, suggesting the simulations have not reached the asymptotic state, which could be competitive exclusion.
comments.request: Comment on the asymptotic state and the impact of transient states on the results.
comments.quote: In Fig. 3, the richness of species inside the clusters decreases in time, so that it seems that the system has not reached its final asymptotic state by the time considered.

comments.issue: 'Box-like normal distribution' is wrong: the stretched exponential is Gaussian only for Q=2.
comments.request: Omit the word 'normal' when naming the interaction functions.
comments.quote: Please do not use the expression 'box-like normal distribution'. The authors use a stretched exponential function with Q=4 for their interaction functions, and this is a normal (=Gaussian) function only for Q=2.

comments.issue: The extinction threshold is a defining element but is described in the clustering metrics section.
comments.request: Move the extinction threshold statement to the simulations of model section.
comments.quote: The statement about the use of an extinction threshold is a very important defining element of the dynamics. Thus, please move it from the 'clustering metrics' section of the Methods to the 'simulations of model' section.

reviews.assessment: Accepts the main point but warns that the linear functional response is unrealistic and that cycles or chaos may explain the diversity.
strengths: shows convincingly that emergent neutrality can occur with predation
clear point for a short article

comments.issue: Linear functional response with no asymptotic maximum predation rate is unrealistic, and other functional responses are not explored.
comments.request: Test Holling type 2 or other functional responses.
comments.quote: The authors assume a basic linear functional response, which makes cycles less likely to occur. Especially the lack of a asymptotic maximum predation rate seems not realistic as most predators will need time to search or digest food

comments.issue: Cycles and chaos under other functional responses could be an alternative cause of high diversity; other consequences of predation are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss cycles, chaos and other consequences of predation as alternative explanations.
comments.quote: I think that with a Holling functional response type 2 (as most commonly found in practice), the probability of limit cycles will increase, dependent on parameters though. In a multi-species setting such cycles can easily lead to chaos

title: Emerging niche clustering results from both competition and predation

study.system: animal responses to fire; sensory ecology and predator-prey theory

editor_summary: Finds the topic timely but wants better organization into thematic sections with clear take-home messages, and a more nuanced account of when the predator-prey framework applies and what modulates fire responses.

reviews.assessment: Well composed and insightful; convinced of the framework's utility, asking for more literature examples and minor fixes.

comments.issue: More examples and citations are needed to support the predicted responses and suggested mechanisms.
comments.request: Provide more literature examples and citations for the predicted responses.
comments.quote: I think the greatest opportunity for improvement would be to provide more examples from the literature of predicted responses.

comments.issue: Scientific names are missing at lines 263 and 522, and there is a typo at line 291.
comments.quote: Line 263 and Line 522: Need scientific names for species. Check throughout.

reviews.assessment: Admires the coverage but says the framework needs to address its shortcomings, especially the timing mismatch with predator responses.

comments.issue: Vigilance may not be possible for species with specialized antipredator responses, but the framework assumes it is.
comments.request: Mention this and add an arrow from P(fire)>0 to Cue Perception in Figure 1.
comments.quote: Animals that have specialized antipredator responses and morphologies for a very particular threat may lack some adaptive traits entirely that would allow for vigilance.

comments.issue: The paper lacks a discussion of how sensory and predator-prey ecology fall short for fire, especially the timing of responses.
comments.request: Add a section on the framework's shortcomings, including response timing.
comments.quote: One of the biggest missing pieces from this paper is a discussion of how sensory ecology and predator-prey behavior falls SHORT of explaining responses of fire or are inappropriate for fire responses.

comments.issue: The claim that animals attend to small differences in fire cues is unsupported conjecture.
comments.request: Provide evidence or soften the claims about fine cue discrimination.
comments.quote: I’m skeptical of this ability for many/most animals and this section feels like conjecture or simply a stretch

comments.issue: Figure 1 is not informative; the meaning of costs, arrow directions and dashed versus solid arrows is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify Figure 1 and consider integrating it with Figure 2.
comments.quote: This figure isn't the most informative. What are the "costs" referring to here and why are the arrows pointing away here?

comments.issue: Figure 2 omits a No Response option, both appropriate and inappropriate.
comments.request: Add No Response options to Figure 2.
comments.quote: There should be an option of No Response on the bottom, both appropriate and inappropriate.

comments.issue: 'Fire cue receptivity' is not defined in Figure 3 or Box 2.
comments.request: Define fire cue receptivity.
comments.quote: It’s not clear what "fire cue receptivity" actually means here or in box 2.

comments.issue: Box 3 is too long in exposition.
comments.request: Shorten Box 3.
comments.quote: Box 3: This box is a bit too long in exposition

comments.issue: Box 3 does not address navigation back to former habitat with lost landmarks, altered cues and smoke disorientation.
comments.request: Address navigation and disorientation during escape in Box 3.
comments.quote: needs to address the issue of whether an animal can navigate back to their former habitat when there has been a loss of landmark cues, changes in olfactory and visual cues, and possible disorientation during escape due to smoke

comments.issue: Known morphological and behavioral adaptations to fire are not reviewed.
comments.request: Add a section reviewing morphological and behavioral fire adaptations.
comments.quote: a section that specifically reviews some of the morphological and behavioral adaptations to fire that are known would be good

reviews.assessment: Strong ideas on an exciting topic, but the manuscript is excessively long, a laundry list rather than synthesis, and needs justification for claims.

comments.issue: The manuscript is excessively lengthy and unwieldy, requiring several rounds of revision for flow and clarity.
comments.request: Cut and revise the text to be clearer and more precise.
comments.quote: the text is excessively lengthy (49 pages plus seven lengthy text boxes!), unwieldy in parts

comments.issue: The manuscript reads as a laundry list of theory rather than a synthesis that weighs predictions against each other.
comments.request: Synthesize ideas and discuss when different theories apply.
comments.quote: The manuscript currently reads as a bit of a laundry list of theory that could be brought to bear on understanding animal responses to fire, whereas I would hope to see more synthesis.

comments.issue: Ideas are suggested with little justification or reference to supporting evidence.
comments.request: Support ideas with reasoning, theory and references.
comments.quote: Ideas seem to be suggested in places with little justification or reference to evidence from previous literature that would support them

comments.issue: The time scales over which fire regimes shift versus predation pressure is experienced are not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the relevant time scales for fire regime shifts.
comments.quote: Some habitats might shift their fire regimes over decades to hundreds of years through habitat conversion, for example the shift from long unburnt tree forests to grassy woodlands with increasing fire frequency

comments.issue: 'Longer than when?' at L71 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison at L71.
comments.quote: L71: again, longer than when?

comments.issue: 'The lens of plants' is awkward phrasing.
comments.request: Rephrase 'the lens of plants'.
comments.quote: L75: “the lens of plants” is awkward phrasing

comments.issue: What plants rely on these for is not specified at L82.
comments.request: Add specificity at L82.
comments.quote: L82: what do plants rely on these for? More specificity is required

comments.issue: How effective the responses are and what effectiveness is needed for population persistence is not considered.
comments.request: Raise questions about response effectiveness and population persistence.
comments.quote: It is also important to understand how effective those responses are, and whether they save your life 99% of the time, or maybe 25% of the time

comments.issue: Words like 'clearly' are used without evidence.
comments.request: Avoid words like clearly, obviously and evidently.
comments.quote: I would almost always avoid using words like clearly, obviously, evidently, etc in a paper

comments.issue: The eco-evolutionary interest of fire questions is underplayed in favour of management framing.
comments.request: Frame fire questions as inherently interesting evolution and ecology questions.
comments.quote: these questions are inherently interesting in themselves as questions about evolution and ecology

comments.issue: Responses are framed as only behavioural although dormancy is physiological.
comments.request: Discuss responses more broadly, including physiological defences.
comments.quote: Only behavioral? dormancy is physiological right? consider talking about responses more broadly.

comments.issue: The ant/termite example is weak if it involves different species and other drivers.
comments.request: Clarify or replace the example at L94-98.
comments.quote: If different species, it could be so many things other than fire driving this that I'd question whether it's a useful example?

comments.issue: Statements at L124-142 are speculative and should be framed as hypotheses with supporting reasoning.
comments.request: Frame these as hypotheses and explain why they are expected.
comments.quote: And really, they should be framed as hypotheses, which they currently aren’t.

comments.issue: No argument is made at L178 for why a new framework is needed before presenting it.
comments.request: Make the case for a new framework at L178.
comments.quote: Here you should be giving a good argument for why we need a new framework – you jump into the framework in the next section without having really made an argument for why it is needed.

comments.issue: The claim that fire is usually rare does not hold in frequently burnt habitats.
comments.request: Consider local fire frequency relative to generation length and innate recognition.
comments.quote: I’m not sure that “fire is usually rare”. Some habitats – e.g. Northern Territory Australia - burn almost every year.

comments.issue: Whether responses save enough individuals for long-term population persistence is not assessed.
comments.request: Discuss how responses affect survival and population persistence.
comments.quote: what is missing is whether these responses are any good at saving enough individuals to make a difference to the population persistence over the long-term

comments.issue: Why species should be expected to respond to fire cues at L245 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why this response would be expected.
comments.quote: sure it *could* happen, but WHY would we expect it?

comments.issue: Why smoke is responded to rather than other salient smells, and what signals danger, is not elaborated.
comments.request: Elaborate on what makes smoke a dangerous cue.
comments.quote: But WHY respond to smoke and not, say, the smell of your mate and offspring sleeping next to you? What tells them what is dangerous?

comments.issue: The proposed mechanism linking predator and fire cues at L234 is unclear beyond generalization.
comments.request: Explain the proposed mechanism in detail.
comments.quote: Different threats might have very different cues so I'm not sure what the proposed mechanism is here, besides "generalization"

comments.issue: 'General vigilance' at L236 is undefined and its targets and cues are unclear.
comments.request: Define general vigilance and specify targets and cues.
comments.quote: What exactly is meant by “general vigilance”? What are they vigilant for? Which cues? etc

title: Integrating sensory ecology and predator‐prey theory to understand animal responses to fire

study.system: gene drive suppression; two-species/predator-prey spatial models

editor_summary: Editor asks to address reviewer comments and better highlight the most novel results, noting one reviewer found some results somewhat obvious.

reviews.assessment: Well-written, repeatable study with sound conclusions, but the Results are too long and the effects not surprising.

comments.issue: Results text is overly long given that most figures are supplementary.
comments.request: Shorten the Results section.
comments.quote: The Results section is too long, despite the fact that the majority of Figures have been included as supplementary

comments.issue: Including two models may be unnecessary; the mosquito-specific model could suffice.
comments.request: Justify or drop the general model.
comments.quote: In part this is because two models have been included for the analysis. Is this necessary? The paper is introduced with mosquitoes as the main gene drive target

comments.issue: The reported effects are not surprising.
comments.request: Better highlight what is novel.
comments.quote: None of these effects are surprising, yet they are important not only in terms of predicting gene drive efficacy

comments.issue: Four minor grammatical errors on pages 2, 5 and 22.
comments.quote: Page 5, line 55: Sentence starting "This multiplies interaction" makes not sense as written.

reviews.assessment: Interesting simulation results, but the models are under-documented and many parameter choices appear arbitrary.

comments.issue: Model assumptions and parameter choices are under-documented.
comments.request: Discuss the model equations and justify choices.
comments.quote: my major concern is a lack of detail where appropriate. This is most apparent when seemingly arbitrary assumptions and parameter choices are made. The mathematical model/equations should be discussed in more detail especially

comments.issue: Ten generations may be too short for 50,000 individuals to reach equilibrium.
comments.request: Justify the equilibration period.
comments.quote: Is 10 generations long enough for a population of 50,000 individuals to reach equilibrium? This seems like a short amount of time

comments.issue: The fitness cost value appears to be 0.95 instead of 0.05.
comments.request: Check and correct the fitness cost parameter.
comments.quote: I believe you meant the fitness cost to be 0.05 and not 0.95, the latter being the relative fitness

comments.issue: The 20-mating cap for fertile females is unjustified.
comments.request: Justify or remove the mating cap.
comments.quote: Why does a fertile female have only 20 chances to choose any male to mate with? If this is arbitrarily chosen it should be stated explicitly

comments.issue: The 'i' in the omega variable should be a subscript.
comments.request: Fix the notation in Lines 35 and 38.
comments.quote: I believe the “i" in the omega variable should be a subscript in Lines 35 and 38

comments.issue: Reflective boundaries may create border density artefacts affecting drive dynamics.
comments.request: Test alternative boundary conditions.
comments.quote: Have different boundary conditions been considered? If so, do they make a difference? Do reflective boundaries lead to high densities of organisms near the borders?

comments.issue: Assumptions behind the expected-competition equations (e.g. uniform distribution) are unclear.
comments.request: Explain the equations and assumptions.
comments.quote: for the calculated expected competition for either species, does this assume a uniform distribution of organisms in the environment? The equations and their corresponding assumptions should be discussed more fully

comments.issue: Parameters are scattered rather than tabulated.
comments.request: Compile parameters and values in one table.
comments.quote: Model parameters should be compiled, defined, and their model values given in a single table for ease of viewing

comments.issue: Parameter sources and the five-fold larval competition are unjustified.
comments.request: Cite sources and justify the values.
comments.quote: Are their references for the parameter values used? Why do older larvae exert five-fold higher competition?

comments.issue: Derivation of the 0.285724 tuning parameter is unexplained.
comments.request: Describe the derivation and equations.
comments.quote: The 0.285724 parameter is described as a tweaking parameter to ensure a fixed number of adult females---was this derived numerically or analytically? Please describe the equations more thoroughly

comments.issue: Capped survival and long lifespans lack justification or sources.
comments.request: Justify survival ceilings and lifespans.
comments.quote: Why the capped survival? Are a lot of mosquitoes living to this imposed ceiling? Also, the lifespans chosen are quite long---where were these obtained?

comments.issue: Survival rate vectors are hard to interpret.
comments.request: Explain the vectors and their sources.
comments.quote: The vectors on Page 7, Lines 11-4 are confusing. Taking the adult male survival rates vector as an example, how is one to read this?

comments.issue: The 50% offspring-production probability is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the mating and oviposition rule.
comments.quote: is this for the sperm of every male, per genotype, or only once, i.e. the female only has a 50% probability of ovipositing per week?

comments.issue: Predator effects are modelled as interspecific competition without justification.
comments.request: Explain the predator-prey formulation.
comments.quote: “The predators have the same effect on the prey species as a competing species,” and so predators affect the fecundity of female prey? Competition in the predator-prey model should not be treated the same as the interspecific case

comments.issue: Predator parameter choices appear oddly specific and arbitrary.
comments.request: Justify or source the choices.
comments.quote: The assumptions in the middle of Page 9 seem oddly specific---are all these choices made arbitrarily or are they inspired from real examples?

comments.issue: 'Population capacity' is confusing word choice.
comments.request: Clarify the term.
comments.quote: “In another form, the population capacity remained at its maximum or minimum levels for 22 weeks.” What population capacity? Confusing word choice

comments.issue: Boundary accumulation of wild types may bias chasing and other measurements.
comments.request: Assess this measurement bias.
comments.quote: The increased density of individuals near the BC has to do with the choice of reflective boundaries. Wild-type individuals will tend to build up, and could possibly sway measurements of chasing

comments.issue: Whether movement is allowed in the Fig 1B framework is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how movement is handled.
comments.quote: Is movement allowed for the framework illustrated in Fig 1B? If so, how is it handled?

comments.issue: 'Long term' in Fig 2 is undefined.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: For Fig 2, what is the definition of “long term”?

comments.issue: The drive cannot suppress without competition in Fig 2; whether this is expected is unclear.
comments.request: Explain this outcome.
comments.quote: From the plots in Fig 2, it seems that for low competition between the two species, suppression is never achieved. So, without the assistance of competition, the gene drive used is incapable of suppressing the population. Is this normal?

comments.issue: Figure 5 caption is separated from the figure.
comments.request: Place the caption on the same page.
comments.quote: The caption for Fig 5 should be on the same page

comments.issue: Figure 7 x-axis definition and the meaning of a zero value are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the axis and provide more detail.
comments.quote: is the x-axis the seasonality constant? If so, a seasonality constant of 0 would mean the population is 0, which is not reflected in the plots?

comments.issue: The simplified two-species subsection is underdeveloped and misplaced.
comments.request: Expand or remove the subsection.
comments.quote: This subsection feels underdeveloped (only two paragraphs) and does not fit well into the narrative of the present draft. Why do we need this?

title: Adversarial interspecies relationships facilitate population suppression by gene drive in spatially explicit models

study.system: temperate forest trees; plot demography, co-occurrence and gene expression

editor_summary: Piece is well written; editor and reviewers want alternative theoretical hypotheses in the introduction, sensitivity analyses and discussion of low replication, a deeper discussion rather than a results re-write, and shorter paragraphs.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and generally agrees with the conclusion, but consistency issues, limited data and single-site generality must be resolved before the contribution can be assessed.

comments.issue: Much of the data (co-occurrence, soil moisture, gene expression) was already published in Swenson et al. 2017.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution relative to the earlier paper.
comments.quote: It should also be noted that a substantial proportion of the data used in this paper (plot-level species co-occurrence, soil water content and gene expression) was already published in a previous paper

comments.issue: Range overlap and range quantile effects are confounded, and the text results do not always match the figures.
comments.request: Disentangle the two predictors and reconcile text with figures.
comments.quote: in several parts of the ms (see specific comments below) the effects of range overlap and range quantile seem to be confounded, and the results reported in the text do not always conform to what is presented in the figures

comments.issue: Effects are shown at only one site, a suture zone where they are predicted to be maximal.
comments.request: Discuss the limited generality of a single suture-zone site.
comments.quote: this is only shown for one site and precisely in an area (a suture zone) where these effects are predicted to be maximal

comments.issue: Analyses rely on limited data (one soil water measurement, a single 5-year demographic interval); limitations and variable choices are not justified.
comments.request: Justify the variables and discuss the limitations of the data.
comments.quote: many of the analyses are based on rather limited data (e.g., one single measurement of soil water content for the topmost 10 cm of soil, demographic data for a single 5-year interval)

comments.issue: Only the first demographic interval is used although a longer period appears available.
comments.request: Use the whole available period to assess demographic responses.
comments.quote: why not use the whole period that appears to be available to assess demographic responses

comments.issue: 'Biogeographic history/legacies' are invoked but only current distribution ranges are measured.
comments.request: Measure or reframe what 'biogeographic legacies' means.
comments.quote: the authors talk about 'biogeographic history' or 'biogeographic legacies' but in fact only assess species current distribution ranges

comments.issue: Available functional trait data are not used in the demographic model.
comments.request: Include functional traits in the Figure 5 model.
comments.quote: Why not use this information in the model presented in Figure 5 to assess to what extent functional traits (even if they are only 'soft' traits) drive species demographic responses

comments.issue: It is unclear why species should share gene expression responses relating to basic molecular functions.
comments.request: Justify the expectation for molecular functions.
comments.quote: why should they also share gene expression responses that relate to basic molecular functions?

comments.issue: Twelve line-level wording edits: L66, L82, L111, L206, L240, L310, L373, L438, L439, L440, L471, L510.
comments.quote: L82: replacing 'whereas' by 'co-occurring' and deleting 'may have lowered rates' (or a similarly oriented change) would be clearer in that you are comparing populations within a community.

comments.issue: Claims at L74-87 and L115-117 lack supporting references, and novel hypotheses are not flagged as such.
comments.request: Add references or state explicitly that claims are novel hypotheses.
comments.quote: additional references are needed to support the claims that are being made, unless they are novel hypotheses in which case this should be stated explicitly as such

comments.issue: It is inconsistent whether 31 or 21 species are analysed, and no species list or dominance data are provided.
comments.request: Clarify the species count and provide a species list and dominance information.
comments.quote: do you focus on 31 or 21 species? It would be nice to provide a species list and information on species dominance in the supporting information.

comments.issue: The linked species range maps could not be found, and it is unclear whether they are global or USA-only.
comments.request: Clarify the map coverage and discuss the limitations.
comments.quote: I was unable to find the species range maps in the link provided. Could you clarify whether these maps are global or only refer to the USA?

comments.issue: The equation at L223 is unclear, including the meaning of the final 'j' sign and the delta calculation.
comments.request: Explain the equation and the delta calculation.
comments.quote: this equation is not very clear to me. What does the final 'j' sign mean?

comments.issue: The torus translation randomization is unfamiliar and not described or referenced adequately.
comments.request: Provide a reference or explain the method in more detail.
comments.quote: Could you please provide a reference where the method is implemented in a similar manner or explain it in more detail?

comments.issue: The equation at L272 is unclear: which species' range overlap the R values represent and how they differ from delta.
comments.request: Explain the R values and their difference from delta.
comments.quote: Again, I did not find this equation entirely clear. The R values are the range overlap between what species exactly?

comments.issue: JAGS is used without a citation.
comments.request: Provide a reference for JAGS.
comments.quote: L318: please provide a reference for JAGS.

comments.issue: Small actual effects are described in the Discussion as large impacts or the primary determinant of performance.
comments.request: Soften the Discussion to match the small effect sizes.
comments.quote: the fact that the actual effects are small, as recognized here, is lost in the Discussion, where biogeographic legacies are described as having a large impact

comments.issue: A single soil water content measurement is a poor measure of water availability; the map is not shown.
comments.request: Add the soil water content map as a panel in Figure 3.
comments.quote: At the very least I would add the soil water content map as an additional panel in Figure 3.

comments.issue: Figure 4 does not show range overlap as claimed; overlap and quantile are confounded and dots are plots rather than species.
comments.request: Revise Figure 4 and clarify what the dots and axes represent.
comments.quote: I do not see any data on range overlap in Figure 4. Range overlap and range quartile seem to be confounded here or in the figure (and in other parts of the ms).

comments.issue: The interaction effects in Figure 5 are hard to interpret from coefficients alone.
comments.request: Plot the interaction in a figure.
comments.quote: it would be extremely useful to plot this interaction in a figure, as these interactive effects can be quite difficult to interpret from the coefficients alone

comments.issue: A claim about range overlap is not shown, since Figures 3-5 report range quantiles.
comments.request: Show the range overlap result or correct the claim.
comments.quote: but where is this shown? Most of the paper results (Figures 3, 4 and 5) refer to range quantiles, not to range overlap.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the L397 statement concerns growth or survival; the interaction is significant only for survival.
comments.request: Clarify which response variable is meant.
comments.quote: do you mean growth or survival? The interaction term seems to be significant only for survival, according to Figure 5.

comments.issue: It is unclear from Figure 5 that the legacy impact is large.
comments.request: Estimate variance explained with and without range quantile variables.
comments.quote: Can you estimate the amount of variance explained by the models in Figure 5 with and without range quantile variables?

comments.issue: The implications of the results for anthropogenic global warming are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the results in the context of global warming.
comments.quote: I find it surprising that the effects of anthropogenic global warning are not mentioned here, and the implications of the results are not discussed in this context.

comments.issue: The text overlooks that conspecific density has a significant negative effect on growth.
comments.request: Correct the statement about conspecific density effects.
comments.quote: but the effect of conspecific density on growth appears to be significant (and negative), according to Figure 5.

reviews.assessment: Robust, impressive and fresh work with good potential, but one substantive concern that theory motivation and interpretation ignore alternative hypotheses.
strengths: robust and impressive datasets and analyses
fresh perspective on spatial structure and dynamics
good potential for an important contribution

comments.issue: The Introduction may not correctly motivate predictions from theory or consider equally plausible alternative hypotheses.
comments.request: Develop contrasting predictions of alternative mechanisms in the Introduction.
comments.quote: My concern is that the Introduction may not be correctly motivating the predictions from theory (or may not be considering alternative hypotheses that are equally plausible), which feeds into a tension over aspects of the interpretation in the Discussion.

comments.issue: Predictions for core-versus-marginal demographic rates ignore evidence that core survival is limited by density and that adaptive genetic variation exists.
comments.request: Acknowledge alternative expectations for core and marginal populations.
comments.quote: development of predictions for the contrast in demographic rates between core and marginal populations is also incomplete

comments.issue: The title's emphasis on 'Biogeographic legacies' reverses the Abstract's framing and implies lagged temporal phenomena.
comments.request: Align the title with the paper's actual framing.
comments.quote: This introduces a confusing logical disconnect for a reader new to the paper, especially as 'legacies' implies lagged temporal phenomena that don't seem relevant in this context.

comments.issue: Community attributes are described inconsistently across the title, Abstract and Introduction.
comments.request: Unify the terminology for community attributes.
comments.quote: the title refers to 'community structure and dynamics', the first line of the Abstract refers to 'species diversity and distributions' and the first line of the Introduction reverts to 'community composition and dynamics'

comments.issue: The gene expression section needs clearer expression, elaboration of its relevance and a reference.
comments.request: Rewrite the section and cite the relevant study.
comments.quote: This section needs more careful expression, elaboration of the relevance of gene expression to species distributions and a reference to the study being discussed

comments.issue: Predictions are made about phenomena such as physiological adaptations that were not measured.
comments.request: Remove or reframe predictions about unmeasured phenomena.
comments.quote: It seems inappropriate to make specific predictions in relation to phenomena such as physiological adaptations that were not measured as part of this study.

comments.issue: The second prediction assumes no general latitudinal gradient in demographic rates.
comments.request: Justify or reframe the second prediction.
comments.quote: This (second) prediction is only relevant if there is no general selection for a latitudinal gradient in demographic rates

comments.issue: The third prediction is circular; framing goals as questions or competing hypotheses would help.
comments.request: Phrase the goals as research questions or tests of competing hypotheses.
comments.quote: On balance I suspect many of the difficulties highlighted in this review could be eliminated if the goals of the study were phrased in terms of research questions or tests of competing hypotheses, rather than predictions.

comments.issue: Soil water content is a crude proxy for water availability, and linking it to drought is inappropriate; gravimetric versus volumetric measurement is also confused.
comments.request: Clarify the measurement and stop equating soil water content with drought.
comments.quote: Generally soil water content provides only a crude measure of soil water availability such as matric potential (the relationship between these metrics is highly non-linear), and linking this to 'drought' would not be appropriate.

comments.issue: GO terms and gene set enrichment tests are not defined or explained for an ecological readership.
comments.request: Define these concepts and explain the links to biological processes and molecular functions.
comments.quote: Please define 'GO terms' and 'gene set enrichment test' and explain how these entities are 'linked to biological processes and molecular functions'.

comments.issue: How the quantile score was computed is described only in a figure legend.
comments.request: Describe the quantile score computation in the main text.
comments.quote: I was expecting a description of how the quantile score was computed in the text rather than figure legend.

comments.issue: It is not tested whether gene expression or spatial distribution are linked to phylogenetic similarity.
comments.request: Test for phylogenetic signal or control for relatedness.
comments.quote: Were gene expression profiles and/or spatial distribution on the plot linked to phylogenetic similarity?

comments.issue: The sign contrast between molecular functions and biological processes cannot be interpreted because the terms are undefined.
comments.request: Define the terms and interpret the contrast.
comments.quote: Because molecular functions and biological processes are not defined (see comment above), the significance of this contrast in the sign of their relationships to species range overlap is unclear.

comments.issue: It is unclear how Figure 4 shows the difference in gene-expression variation between northern and southern species.
comments.request: Clarify how Figure 4 displays this difference.
comments.quote: It's not clear to me how Figure 4 displays the stated difference in variation in genes associated to responses to drought between northern and southern species.

comments.issue: Range quantile is spatially confounded with microhabitat variation, so their effects on survival cannot be distinguished.
comments.request: Include microhabitat terms and their interaction with range quantile in the model.
comments.quote: it doesn't seem possible to distinguish the range quantile and microhabitat effects on survival

comments.issue: The difference in negative density dependence between southern and northern species is not displayed graphically.
comments.request: Display this result graphically.
comments.quote: Is there a way of displaying this result graphically to give it further emphasis?

comments.issue: The wording about range overlap and gene expression responses is ambiguous (absolute reduction or relative difference).
comments.request: Clarify the wording to convey the intended meaning.
comments.quote: Does large species range overlap correlate with reduced gene expression responses to drought, or should this be 'correlated with reduced difference in gene expression responses to drought'?

comments.issue: Physiological adaptations are invoked although they were not measured, and the gene expression-physiology link is indirect.
comments.request: Remove or qualify the physiological adaptation claim.
comments.quote: The reference to physiological adaptations doesn't seem appropriate, since these were not measured. The linkage between gene expression and physiology could be very indirect.

comments.issue: Two line-level wording edits: 'higher individual performance' (L460-461) and 'in studied forest' (L471).
comments.quote: Lines 460-461. 'higher individual performance' is not precise: I suggest 'greater growth and survival'.

comments.issue: The statement overlooks the significant effect of conspecific density on growth.
comments.request: Acknowledge the significant density effect on growth.
comments.quote: However there was a significant effect of conspecific density on growth.

comments.issue: Local species composition is treated as a biogeographic legacy although it is an emergent property, not a lagged legacy effect.
comments.request: Reframe composition as emergent rather than a legacy.
comments.quote: I don't see local species composition as having a biogeographic legacy – species composition is an emergent property of processes operating over multiple scales, which is not equivalent to legacy effects.

title: Biogeographic context is related to local scale tree demography, co‐occurrence and functional differentiation

study.system: 2242 plant and animal populations; matrix models and climate data

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers saw value but two had difficulty penetrating the methods and inference, which must be clarified for a broad readership.

reviews.assessment: Careful and convincing refutation of the exposure-resilience link; supports publication despite finding the tested hypothesis conceptually odd.

comments.issue: The hypothesis that exposure increases resilience seems conceptually odd, since exposure could reduce population variability instead.
comments.quote: if anything exposure to environmental variability might reduce variability in a population and thus make it less resilient

reviews.assessment: Interesting and original study, but disturbance terminology, methods clarity and several analyses need substantial improvement.
strengths: combination of climate data and 2242 matrix population models

comments.issue: Disturbance is never clearly defined and is used interchangeably with environmental stochasticity.
comments.request: Define disturbance clearly at the start and distinguish it from stochasticity.
comments.quote: I think the use of "disturbance" is confusing in the paper as no clear definition of a disturbance is given

comments.issue: Expected effects of disturbances on population size and demographic structure are not stated.
comments.request: Add clear expectations based on explicit ecological processes.
comments.quote: What are the expected effects of such disturbances on the size and demographic structure of natural populations?

comments.issue: Key methods elements are in the supplement while some main-text paragraphs are overly detailed and hard to follow.
comments.request: Shorten the methods and improve clarity for a broad readership.
comments.quote: key elements are presented in the Supplementary Information but not in the main text (notably in S4)

comments.issue: Figure S2 lacks a colour legend and the red-blue gradient direction is unclear; metric ranges are not given.
comments.request: Add a legend and report the range of the five metrics.
comments.quote: the colour gradient in Fig. S2 has no legend, and negative values correspond to red colours while positive values are in blue. Should not be the opposite?

comments.issue: It is unclear how resistance, reactivity and recovery are measured from the data.
comments.request: Provide more information on this critical methodological step.
comments.quote: I did not fully understand how you measure population resistance, reactivity and recovery

comments.issue: The time step of the measurements is not stated.
comments.request: State whether measurements are monthly or yearly.
comments.quote: what is the time step of the measurements? Monthly? Yearly?

comments.issue: The minimum time step for observing transient dynamics is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the minimum time step was determined.
comments.quote: How did you determine what was the minimum time step to observe transient dynamics?

comments.issue: It is unclear how life-cycle variation among species was handled and whether plants and animals were analysed separately.
comments.request: Explain how life-cycle variation was handled and report separate analyses.
comments.quote: How did you deal with the important variation of life cycles among species in the analysis?

comments.issue: Resilience to what is unclear in the title, and resilience is a confusing term in ecology.
comments.request: Use transient dynamics or transient demography instead.
comments.quote: Title: resilience to what? As resilience is a confusing term in ecology, I suggest to replace it by "transient dynamics"

comments.issue: Using disturbances in the abstract instead of environmental stochasticity misrepresents the study.
comments.request: Replace disturbances with environmental stochasticity in the abstract.
comments.quote: I think that using the word "disturbances" in the abstract, instead of "environmental stochasticity" is misleading and do not summarize precisely the content of the manuscript

comments.issue: An expectation is not stated before the unexpected result at line 36.
comments.request: State the expectation before this sentence.
comments.quote: Why unexpectedly? An expectation should be stated before this sentence.

comments.issue: Affected by implies causality where only correlation is certain.
comments.request: Replace affected by with correlated with.
comments.quote: Consider replacing "affected by" by "correlated with", the causality is not certain.

comments.issue: The classical assumption that stochasticity predicts resilience better than traits is not substantiated or referenced.
comments.request: Justify or remove the classical assumption with relevant references.
comments.quote: I am not aware of a "classical" assumption stating that environmental stochasticity can better predict population resilience compared to demographic and life history traits

comments.issue: How transient metrics offer greater insight is unclear and needs an example.
comments.request: Give a specific example.
comments.quote: Can you be more specific here, with maybe one example? It is not fully clear how transient population metrics can offer greater insight.

comments.issue: Frequent disturbances wrongly suggests punctual disturbance responses rather than stochasticity.
comments.request: Replace with high environmental stochasticity.
comments.quote: Consider replacing "frequent disturbances" by "high environmental stochasticity", otherwise this suggests the paper will address population responses to punctual disturbances.

comments.issue: The word disturbances is used where fluctuations are meant at lines 83 and 100.
comments.request: Replace disturbances with fluctuations throughout.
comments.quote: again, I would replace "disturbances" by "fluctuations"

comments.issue: Hypothesis 2 lacks specific expectations linking vital rates to the three resilience metrics.
comments.request: Extend H2 with expected vital-rate effects to aid interpretation of Figure 3.
comments.quote: H2 could be extended in order to provide more specific expectations on the links between vital rates and population resilience

comments.issue: The homogeneity of MPM structures is not specified.
comments.request: Specify how homogeneous the MPM structures are.
comments.quote: Please specify how homogeneous/heterogeneous the MPMs structures are.

comments.issue: It is unclear why there are more MPMs than populations and whether this weights some populations.
comments.request: Explain multiple models per population and any weighting.
comments.quote: Please specify why there is more MPMs than populations.

comments.issue: The disturbance magnitude gauge uses only mean thermal range, omitting precipitation.
comments.request: Justify the use of thermal range only or add precipitation.
comments.quote: Why the "gauge of disturbance magnitude" is estimated with mean thermal range only? What about mean precipitation range?

comments.issue: Table 2 results, such as the negative progression-compensation link, need interpretation and expected assumptions.
comments.request: Discuss the vital rate-resilience links and expected patterns.
comments.quote: These results need further interpretation/discussion. For example, why progression is negatively linked to compensation?

comments.issue: The shading gradient in Table S2 looks arbitrary, with different colours for -0.06 and 0.06.
comments.request: Fix the shading scale in Table S2.
comments.quote: The shading gradient looks arbitrary in Table S2. Why -0.06 and 0.06 do not have the same colour?

comments.issue: Figure 1 explains only part of the methods; how MPM data feed into resilience metrics is not clear.
comments.request: Modify Figure 1 and perhaps add a panel linking vital rates to resilience metrics.
comments.quote: Figure 1 should be modified so one can get easily how data from matrix population models will be used to understand population resilience

reviews.assessment: Ambitious and intriguing project, but readability, disturbance definitions and conceptual issues must be resolved for this journal.

comments.issue: The paper is very difficult to read, with much method detail but little guidance on assumptions for outside readers.
comments.request: Add overview and guidance on assumptions for general ecologists.
comments.quote: The paper is very difficult to read with often little help to guide the reader.

comments.issue: It is never clearly stated what kind of disturbance the transient metrics follow, including stage and magnitude.
comments.request: State the disturbance type, affected stages and magnitude.
comments.quote: Transient metrics following what kind of disturbance exactly? This is never stated clearly.

comments.issue: The meaning of space-for-time is mentioned once and never explained.
comments.request: Explain the space-for-time substitution explicitly.
comments.quote: It is not at all clear what the space-for-time means in this case as it is mentioned once but never explained.

comments.issue: Matrix parameters may be confounded with environmental variation during the sampling period.
comments.request: Address whether matrix parameters average out environmental dependence.
comments.quote: Is it then not a problem that the matrix model parameters are confounded with the environmental variation during the period of sampling?

comments.issue: If testing resilience to population size disturbances, the environmental factor should affect populations that way rather than through growth parameters.
comments.request: Match the disturbance type to the environmental driver tested.
comments.quote: If you test resilience towards population size disturbances, then one might have to look at an environmental factor that actually affects a population this way

comments.issue: Ecological resilience refers to state shifts between attractors, which is not what is studied here.
comments.request: Avoid mingling this definition with engineering resilience measures.
comments.quote: Ecological resilience refers to a state-shift between multiple concurrent attractors. This does not seem to be what you are studying.

comments.issue: The resilience expectation may refer to fitness rather than population size.
comments.request: Clarify whether resilience refers to fitness or population size.
comments.quote: Maybe resilience of fitness, not sure about population size!

comments.issue: Structural composition of populations needs clarification for non-specialists.
comments.request: Clarify population structure composition.
comments.quote: for non population ecologists, clarify population structure composition

comments.issue: The definition may need to refer to avoiding a decline in fitness, and compensation to returning to pre-disturbance levels.
comments.request: Clarify the fitness and compensation definitions.
comments.quote: should it not be a populations ability to avoid a decline in fitness?

comments.issue: It is unclear how well founded the hypotheses at lines 80-94 are.
comments.request: Justify the hypotheses.
comments.quote: P4 l80-94: How well founded are these hypotheses?

comments.issue: The consequences of the space-for-time substitution are not clearly addressed.
comments.request: Address how disturbances and recovery time can be discussed under space-for-time.
comments.quote: the consequences of space for time need to be addressed much more clearly

comments.issue: It is unclear whether frequency is expressed relative to generation time.
comments.request: Clarify frequency relative to generation time.
comments.quote: P4L101: frequency in relation to generation time, right?

comments.issue: The disturbance at P11 is unclear; a biomass change resembles a predation rather than environmental disturbance.
comments.request: Define the disturbance type at this point.
comments.quote: WHAT disturbance? Change in biomass? That seems more like a predation disturbance rather than an environmental driver disturbance.

comments.issue: The PCA plots do not add much.
comments.request: Reconsider or remove the PCA plots.
comments.quote: Frankly I did not find the PCA-plots to add much

comments.issue: Species selection for population studies may bias the dataset toward vulnerable or representative species, independent of stability traits.
comments.request: Account for or discuss the selection bias in species inclusion.
comments.quote: Have you, or can you, account for the bias of why the species were chosen for population studies in the first place?

title: Recent exposure to environmental stochasticity does not determine the demographic resilience of natural populations

study.system: Andean hummingbirds; blood traits across elevational gradient

editor_summary: All reviewers found the study very interesting. Editor asks for sensitivity analyses of small per-species sample sizes (weights, metafor, excluding small-n species), tests of trait variability along elevation, clearer model-selection explanation, and several line edits.

reviews.assessment: Strongly positive; novel and robust, but variation in sample sizes among species is a major concern.
strengths: high novelty; first shown in birds

comments.issue: Sample sizes vary hugely among species; species means from fewer than five individuals may bias the models.
comments.request: Weight by sampling effort or re-run key analyses excluding poorly sampled species.
comments.quote: My only major concern is related to huge variation in sample sizes between the species, including taxa with very modest sampling.

comments.issue: The scale-dependency example may reflect genetic adaptation, not only short-term acclimatization.
comments.request: Qualify the claim that the example reflects acclimatization.
comments.quote: I am not sure if this may be used as a reliable example of scale dependency, as higher Hb concentrations at high elevations may also have a genetic component

comments.issue: Sentences at L56-61 are repetitive and could be merged.
comments.request: Merge the two sentences into one.
comments.quote: These two sentences contain largely repeatative information content, maybe consider merging in a single sentence?

comments.issue: No reference is given for the statement that about one third of erythrocyte mass is haemoglobin.
comments.request: Cite a source for this statement.
comments.quote: Ca 1/3 of erythrocyte mass? Any reference for this statement?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the nine clades correspond to a particular taxonomic rank.
comments.request: Clarify the taxonomic basis of the nine clades.
comments.quote: Do these nine clades refer to any particular taxonomic rank?

comments.issue: A statement at L105 is too bold given the evidence presented.
comments.request: Tone down the statement.
comments.quote: This is a very bold statement. Although the results are novel and interesting, I think this should be toned down.

comments.issue: Outlier-removal criteria and the numbers of outliers removed per trait are not reported.
comments.request: Provide outlier criteria and counts per trait.
comments.quote: Qualitative criteria for outlier removal should be provided. The number (or proportion) of outliers removed per trait should also be explicitly stated

comments.issue: What "the nearest relatives" means is not explained.
comments.request: Define "nearest relatives" in the Supplementary Information.
comments.quote: It should be explained in the Supplementary Information what is exaclty meant by “the nearest relatives”

comments.issue: It is unclear whether wing loading was a control variable or a tested hypothesis.
comments.request: State the expectations for wing loading explicitly.
comments.quote: Did you simply control for variation in wing loading or rather tested any specific hypotheses associated with this parameter?

comments.issue: Ten thousand MCMC iterations may be too short; convergence and autocorrelation are not checked.
comments.request: Report convergence diagnostics and test longer chains.
comments.quote: Ten thousand iterations seem like a surprisingly short Markov chain length. Did you check if running longer chains would not improve convergence?

comments.issue: The filtering that removed a couple dozen individuals from the dataset is not described.
comments.request: Describe the filtering criteria.
comments.quote: what kind of filtering was used to remove a couple dozen individuals from the dataset?

comments.issue: Rationale for including the species-level Hb genotype in within-species analyses is unclear.
comments.request: Justify including Hb genotype in within-species models.
comments.quote: As far as I understand, Hb genotype is a species-specific rather than an individual-level trait, so what was the rationale for including this variable

comments.issue: Collinearity between elevation and elevational position as simultaneous predictors is not checked.
comments.request: Check collinearity between the two predictors.
comments.quote: Did you check for the issue of collinearity between elevation and elevational position included as predictors in the same models?

comments.issue: Within-species models without a species random effect risk pseudoreplication from repeated measurements.
comments.request: Compare models with species identity as a random factor.
comments.quote: Lacking the random effect of species in the models that assessed within-species variation could introduce a problem of pseudoreplication

comments.issue: The purpose of testing a clade-by-elevation interaction is not explained.
comments.request: Briefly state the aim of this interaction test.
comments.quote: The aim of testing for an interaction between clade and elevation should be explained here briefly.

comments.issue: The inclusion threshold differs from earlier models (>1 vs >2 individuals) without explanation.
comments.request: Clarify why the inclusion threshold changed.
comments.quote: All previous among-species models were run for species with >1 individual sampled, whereas here the dataset was limited to species with >2 individuals sampled.

comments.issue: Rhat is not clarified as the potential scale reduction factor.
comments.request: Define Rhat in the text.
comments.quote: I expect that Rhat refers to the potential scale reduction factor, please clarifyin the text.

comments.issue: Table S5 reports summary statistics pooled across species, not per-species reference values.
comments.request: Provide per-species reference values in the Supplementary Information.
comments.quote: In Table S5 summary statistics for haematological parameters were provided jointly across all the species, so the table does not actually provide complete reference values for each species.

comments.issue: The description of results at L304-305 is enigmatic; directions of associations are not given.
comments.request: Describe the direction of the associations.
comments.quote: This is a very enigmatic description of the results, directions of these associations should at least be described.

comments.issue: Analyses at L308-312 appear without prior announcement in the methods.
comments.request: Announce these analyses earlier in the methods.
comments.quote: These analyses come as a surprise to the reader, they should have been preceded with some brief announcement earlier in the methods sections.

comments.issue: lambda = 0.44 is treated as no phylogenetic signal, which overstates the result.
comments.request: Acknowledge moderate phylogenetic signal and test phylogeny in the CeNS model.
comments.quote: Although phylogenetic signal in the CeNS Index was not significant, I would not interpret lambda = 0.44 as “no phylogenetic signal”.

comments.issue: Phylogenetic signal in mean elevation range is not assessed, which could explain low signal in blood traits.
comments.request: Assess phylogenetic signal in the mean elevation range.
comments.quote: It could be informative to assess phylogenetic signal in the mean elevation range to gain a better understanding of low phylogenetic signal in haematological traits

comments.issue: Weak phylogenetic signal is interpreted as species idiosyncrasies although species responded similarly and consistently.
comments.request: Reconsider the idiosyncrasy interpretation.
comments.quote: I am also not sure if weak phylogenetic signal should necessarily be interpreted in terms of species idiosyncrasies

comments.issue: "et al." is used for a single-author reference.
comments.request: Remove "et al." from the citation.
comments.quote: As the sole author of the cited paper I feel obligated to remark that “et al.” is not necessary in this citation.

comments.issue: The biological meaning of the clade-elevation interaction is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the interaction or remove that analysis.
comments.quote: The biological meaning of this interaction is unclear to me and I suggest providing a more thorough explanation for this result

reviews.assessment: Very positive; excellent large dataset, but within-species variability and genotype effects need more exploration.
strengths: excellent organization and presentation of a large dataset
very good contribution to blood-oxygen capacity mechanisms

comments.issue: Within-species variability of blood traits along elevation is not analysed, limiting acclimation-versus-adaptation inference.
comments.request: Explore trait variability within species and across altitudinal ranges.
comments.quote: I believe the authors need to explore variability of blood traits within a species and at different altitudinal ranges in order to help delineate acclimation vs. adaptive responses.

comments.issue: Inconsistent British/American spellings of haemoglobin and haematocrit throughout the manuscript.
comments.request: Use one spelling convention throughout.
comments.quote: The authors are inconsistent in their use of h(a)emoglobin, h(a)ematocrit, etc. throughout the manuscript.

comments.issue: The abstract's example of covariation is questionable; an inverse supply-usage relationship is also plausible.
comments.request: Reconsider or justify the covariation example.
comments.quote: I’m not sure this is the best example of covariation. Increasing blood carrying capacity is not necessarily expected to covary with oxygen usage pathways.

comments.issue: "affect" should read "increase" at line 61.
comments.request: Change "affect" to "increase".
comments.quote: Introduction Line 61 – Change ‘affect’ to ‘increase’

comments.issue: Confidence that Hb genotype similarly affects oxygen affinity across 77 species is questioned; a waterfowl study found no parallel adaptation.
comments.request: Discuss the waterfowl discrepancy and genotype-oxygen affinity variation.
comments.quote: Since the referenced study was done on 10 species, while your work examines 77 different species, how confident are you that the Hb βA13–βA87 genotype would result in similar changes in oxygen binding affinity?

comments.issue: Own data suggest genotype effects on blood traits vary greatly; this is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this possibility in interpreting the results.
comments.quote: Your own data suggest that Hb βA13–βA87 genotypes have a greatly varied affect on blood traits. I believe that you should discuss this possibility here

comments.issue: Data showing no age effects on blood traits are not reported.
comments.request: Add the age-effect results to the Supplementary Information.
comments.quote: It would be nice to include some of the data that showed no effects of age on blood traits.

comments.issue: Genotype is absent from the best model, and its parameter estimates are not shown.
comments.request: Provide a full-model summary including genotype estimates.
comments.quote: It’s interesting that genotype is not included in the best fitting model. Can you include a “full model” summary to show the parameter estimates for genotype?

comments.issue: Altitude covaries with temperature and humidity; the effects are not delineated.
comments.request: Clarify how altitude and temperature effects were separated.
comments.quote: surely altitude will affect both the temperature and humidity of the sampling location. How did you delineate the effects of altitude and temperature?

reviews.assessment: Excellent, exhaustive work with important results; only the literature search is incomplete.

comments.issue: Literature search is incomplete; relevant works by Gonzales-Morales and Guadarrama are missing.
comments.request: Cite the additional relevant literature.
comments.quote: I only have the observation that a complete information search was not carried out.

title: Hummingbird blood traits track oxygen availability across space and time

study.system: urban bird communities; 5M eBird checklists, 137 cities

editor_summary: Editor says the paper could make an interesting contribution but the framing must be rethought (retention vs other processes; introduced species), analyses redone (spatial pseudoreplication, variable checklist numbers), and the title and methods clarified.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the dataset but raises major concerns about retention framing, variable overload, checklist bias, realm imbalances and presentation.
strengths: potential important contribution to urban avian diversity

comments.issue: 'Retention' implies species were present before cities and conflates two different processes.
comments.request: Use neutral terminology instead of 'retention'.
comments.quote: This implicitly assumes that all birds in cities were present there 'before' cities were established, and gives the impression that the current species pool are those that have not gone extinct.

comments.issue: 47-69 explanatory variables risk overfitting and misleading conclusions; collinearity not handled.
comments.request: Reduce the variable list and check collinearity.
comments.quote: I worry that using so many variables may lead to overfitting, and thereby some misleading conclusions

comments.issue: No specific predictions are presented and several variables such as 'Happiness' are unmotivated.
comments.request: Justify each variable and state predictions.
comments.quote: The Introduction does not present any specific predictions, but it seems clear to me that some variables (e.g. habitat variables) should be included because of previous knowledge, whereas other variables (in particular 'Happiness') are not motivated at all

comments.issue: Random sampling does not remove the checklist-number bias in species richness.
comments.request: Test and control for checklist number.
comments.quote: I'm not convinced that this removes the bias (that total number of bird species that can be sampled increases with number of checklists).

comments.issue: Large differences in data amount between realms; no checks that few cities affected results.
comments.request: Run sensitivity analyses excluding data-poor realms.
comments.quote: I could not find any information that you have tried to check whether few cities in some realms affected results.

comments.issue: Appendices and supplementary material are poorly organized and hard to navigate.
comments.request: Reorganize appendices and supplementary material.
comments.quote: I found it hard to get an oversight of all the material presented in appendices and supplementary material. You need to organize this information much better

comments.issue: Figs 1 and 5 show only selected variables without explaining the selection or the missing reference realm.
comments.request: Explain variable selection and reference realm in figures.
comments.quote: Please explain the background for why exactly these variables are shown in the figures.

comments.issue: Reference list has missing volumes and pages, mixed journal abbreviations, ordering and punctuation errors.
comments.request: Fix the reference list.
comments.quote: The reference list needs to be improved considerably. There was an unusually large number of references that lacked information on volume and page numbers.

comments.issue: Non-urban sites such as Nairobi National Park were included despite the urban focus.
comments.request: Exclude non-urban sites.
comments.quote: Nairobi National Park was included in the data set despite not being a part of an urban area, only bordering urban areas on one side.

comments.issue: Central Park's 56 hotspots are not independent and create pseudoreplication.
comments.request: Merge nearby hotspots into single sites.
comments.quote: these are so close to each other and with no obvious boundaries so that they are not truly independent data points, and using all of them may create problems with pseudoreplication

comments.issue: Text mentions historical geological processes and governance, which were not analysed.
comments.request: Focus on the variable types actually included.
comments.quote: I could not find that 'historical geological processes' were included or analysed in this paper. Few variables have any relation to 'governance'.

comments.issue: Figure 3 is referenced before Figure 2.
comments.request: Switch the figure numbering.
comments.quote: Reference to Figure 3 is made before Figure 2 has been mentioned. Switch figure numbering.

comments.issue: Text statement contradicts Figure 5, which shows Australasia highest.
comments.request: Correct the statement.
comments.quote: Figure 5 actually showed that the Australasian realm was highest.

comments.issue: Two line-level terminology fixes ('nectivore', 'realm vectors' for biomes).
comments.quote: Number of biomes is explained as the number of realm vectors. Should probably be number of biome vectors.

comments.issue: Figure 3 legend shows eight realms though only six were used.
comments.request: Fix the realm legend.
comments.quote: The legend shows eight realms, but only six were used. Please remove Antarctica, and I expect that Australasia and Oceania are the same.

comments.issue: Dot sizes in fig. A1.2 are unexplained and do not correspond to elevation delta.
comments.request: Explain the dot sizes.
comments.quote: It is unclear what the different dot sizes represent. There were no cities with elevation delta of 5000 m (cf. figure A3.2), so this does not appear to be the case.

reviews.assessment: Finds the study well conducted with interesting results; only asks to discuss citizen-science weaknesses and add references and terminology fixes.
strengths: well conducted study with interesting results

comments.issue: Potential weaknesses of citizen-science data are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of citizen-science data.
comments.quote: I would suggest to the authors just highlight better on some sections of the Discussion, about the main potential weakness related to the use of citizen-science datasets

comments.issue: Loss of evolutionary distinctiveness and biotic homogenization are not introduced.
comments.request: Add these topics and their references.
comments.quote: I would suggest introducing also two important topics here, related to the main effects of urbanization on reducing overall biodiversity

comments.issue: Ecological resilience and functional redundancy are introduced without explanation or examples.
comments.request: Explain resilience and functional redundancy.
comments.quote: I think the authors need to do an additional effort here, to explain the concept of ecological resilience, and how could be connected to a degree of functional redundancy.

comments.issue: FDiv is mislabelled as functional diversity when it is functional divergence.
comments.request: Correct the FDiv terminology.
comments.quote: while FRic corresponds to the functional richness, as correctly the authors claim, the FDiv is not “functional diversity” but “functional divergence”

comments.issue: Morelli et al. 2016 is a relevant missing citation.
comments.request: Add the Morelli et al. citation.
comments.quote: I suggest to cite also Morelli et al. 2016 in this sentence

title: Avian diversity and function across the world's most populous cities

study.system: computer vision deep learning for entomology; literature review

editor_summary: Editor asks for accessible terminology and a glossary, clearer scope and structure, a vision for the future and a case study; questions the L60 ethics claim and ArXiv-only references.

reviews.assessment: Timely and refreshing review, but the vision for global-scale deep learning and the context of the technical methods need deeper discussion.
strengths: refreshing focus on deep learning challenges in entomology
valid point about shifting from niche applications to broader scale
reads well and is timely for ecologists
