study.system: fungal fruiting records; 6.1 million GBIF records

editor_summary: Editor finds the topic and dataset extremely interesting; R1 identifies flaws that may be fixable and R2 asks for clearer data and methods reporting; revision encouraged if the issues can be addressed.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and clearly written; asks for clearer data documentation, lifestyle assignment details and climate-data reporting.

comments.issue: The species list and lifestyle assignments behind the analyses are not available or documented.
comments.request: Provide a supplemental list of species, their lifestyles and richness.
comments.quote: I think it is really important to provide the reader with a list (it could be a Supplemental file) of the species included in the dataset and the lifestyle that was assigned to each one.

comments.issue: The rationale for using the 2010-2021 subset 'to reduce climate warming effects' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the purpose of this subset.
comments.quote: This period includes 9-10 of the ten warmest years on record, so do you really mean "to reduce climate warming effects" here?

comments.issue: Consistency of results with the 2010-2021 subset removed entirely is not tested.
comments.request: Repeat the analysis using only 1977-2009.
comments.quote: don't you need to also explore the consistency of results obtained by removing the subset entirely (i.e. just using the period 1977-2009)?

comments.issue: Species numbers per lifestyle are not reported, only total record counts.
comments.request: Report how many species each lifestyle contains.
comments.quote: This is where it would be good to indicate how many species are represented in each lifestyle, not just the total number of records.

comments.issue: It is unclear how lifestyles were assigned, including whether assignment stopped at genus level despite within-genus lifestyle variation.
comments.request: Explain exactly how lifestyles were assigned to observations.
comments.quote: It would be best to clarify exactly how you are assigning lifestyles to each observation.

comments.issue: WorldClim 2.1 covers 1970-2000, so the source of 2001-2021 climate data is unclear.
comments.request: State the source of the post-2000 climate data.
comments.quote: WorldClim 2.1 is currently available and covers the period 1970-2000. Where did you obtain data for the period 2001-2021?

comments.issue: The current WorldClim reference is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Fick and Hijmans 2017.
comments.quote: Note current reference is: Fick, S.E. and R.J. Hijmans, 2017.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether a single seasonality value per biome was used across all years.
comments.request: Clarify how seasonality values were calculated.
comments.quote: So you have calculated a single mean value for temp and precip seasonality across all records (all years) within each of the six biomes?

comments.issue: The temperature seasonality values appear unusually high and may have been multiplied by 100.
comments.request: Confirm the units and scaling of temperature seasonality.
comments.quote: Did you also multiply by 100? That would explain the high values.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the climate data cover the same period as the fruiting records.
comments.request: State whether periods match.
comments.quote: It would be good to know if the data used here covers the same period as the fruiting records as that is currently unclear.

comments.issue: The precipitation seasonality metric needs confirmation as a coefficient of variation.
comments.request: Confirm the precipitation seasonality definition.
comments.quote: So in this case you are using the ratio of the st.dev. of the monthly total precip to the mean monthly total precip (i.e. the CV).

comments.issue: The description of the seasonality-fruiting relationships is too brief and uses single 1970-2000 values for 1977-2021 data.
comments.request: Clarify the analysis and consider finer time intervals.
comments.quote: Too brief. I would like to see some more clarity here over exactly what you are exploring in terms of these relationships.

comments.issue: Literature on how temperature intensity affects fungal fruiting is not cited.
comments.request: Refer to relevant literature and future climate models.
comments.quote: At the very least I think you need to refer to any literature on how temperature intensity affects fungal fruiting.

comments.issue: Figure 1a dots do not correspond to biome colours.
comments.request: Colour the map dots by biome.
comments.quote: Is it possible to change the colour of the dots on the map to correspond to the biomes?

comments.issue: Figures 2 and S3 lack units for temperature and precipitation seasonality.
comments.request: Add units to these figures.
comments.quote: Need to add units. Unclear to the reader what temp and precip seasonality is being measured in.

reviews.assessment: Attractive dataset and clear writing, but the modeling cannot support the magnitude and tradeoff conclusions; substantial reanalysis needed.
strengths: good effort to address data quality

comments.issue: Conclusions about fruiting peak magnitude are invalid because data were independently scaled to 0-1 per condition.
comments.request: Avoid magnitude conclusions from scaled data or rescale appropriately.
comments.quote: Drawing conclusions about the ”magnitude” of the fruiting peak, and its variation between different biomes and ecological niches, when all data for different conditions have been independently scaled to the range 0-1.

comments.issue: Biome-level aggregation of five world regions cannot demonstrate an ecological tradeoff.
comments.request: Restrict claims or reanalyse at finer spatial scales.
comments.quote: interpretation of the results for this level of aggregation, dividing the world into just 5 regions, is not evidence of an ecological ”tradeoff” in anything like the usual sense

comments.issue: The comparison of temperature versus precipitation seasonality is confounded by differences in spatial coordination across biomes.
comments.request: Account for spatial coordination when comparing drivers.
comments.quote: temperature seasonality in the boreal and temperate zones is highly coordinated; the same seasons are warmer vs. colder in the entire climate zone

comments.issue: Fruiting timing and duration are modelled from a single curve per biome rather than per site and year.
comments.request: Bin data spatially and model timing and duration explicitly.
comments.quote: Any stronger conclusions about the duration of fruiting and its correlates would require the data to be spatially binned in a more fine-grained way, and to model the timing and duration of fruiting more explicitly

comments.issue: Uneven sampling and relative scaling mean fruiting magnitude is not identifiable from these data.
comments.request: Do not assess magnitude variation without addressing sampling effort.
comments.quote: global variation in the magnitude of the fruiting peak, or its correlates, cannot be meaningfully assessed from these data at all

comments.issue: An additive random effect for interannual variation is unrealistic; a multiplicative model with log link is expected to fit better.
comments.request: Use a log link with Poisson or negative binomial distribution.
comments.quote: The model used by the authors treats inter-annual variation as an additive random effect. This strikes me as unrealistic

comments.issue: A non-cyclical model for week-of-year seasonality is inappropriate and produces unrealistic results.
comments.request: Use cyclical cubic splines for the week-of-year smooth.
comments.quote: The use of a non-cyclical model for seasonality data is inappropriate.

title: Temperature affects the timing and duration of fungal fruiting patterns across major terrestrial biomes

study.system: canopy arthropods; rainforest vs plantations; stable isotopes and energy fluxes

editor_summary: Merit acknowledged, but p-values reported after model selection must go, Figure 2 pie charts exaggerate differences, and methods/results need fixes.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and sensible study; suggests additional diversity and food-web metrics to reveal mechanisms.

comments.issue: Community structure changes are not characterized with diversity indices or ordinations.
comments.request: Calculate diversity indices and NMDS by site and season.
comments.quote: Calculating (1) some conventional diversity indices such as Shannon H' or Pielous's J and/or (2) nonmetric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) to group different sites and seasons by the arthropod community structure would help here.

comments.issue: Only the green (leaf-based) food chain is considered, not the brown (detritus-based) chain.
comments.request: Consider the brown food chain starting from soil detritus.
comments.quote: I would suggest the authors shed light not only on the green food chain starting from plant leaves, but also on the brown food chain starting from soil detritus.

comments.issue: Functional diversity may actually be higher in plantations, which Layman niche indices could test.
comments.request: Apply Layman et al. (2007) niche-width indices to the isotope data.
comments.quote: Layman et al. (2007) proposed six indices for calculating the niche width in terms of resource use and trophic structure

comments.issue: Food web architecture metrics are needed to support the simplification argument at lines 345-347.
comments.request: Analyse connectance and food chain length between habitats.
comments.quote: it would be nice to analyze the difference in food web architecture between natural and altered sites

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and comprehensive study; a few clarifications on methods and wording.
strengths: novel food web and energy flux perspective

comments.issue: Fogging machine, time of day and weather conditions are not reported.
comments.request: Specify fogging equipment and conditions.
comments.quote: Can you please specify the fogging machine that was used as well as the time of the day and the weather conditions during fogging?

comments.issue: Abundance is count data but modelled with a Gaussian distribution.
comments.request: Use quasi-Poisson or negative binomial models.
comments.quote: Since abundance is count data, I think (quasi)poisson or a negative binomial distribution should be used..

comments.issue: Sensitivity analyses are not described in the main text.
comments.request: Summarize the sensitivity analyses in the main text.
comments.quote: I think it would be good to describe in a few words which sensitivity analyses were done also in the main text

comments.issue: 'Such as selective logging' is mentioned although selective logging was not studied.
comments.request: Drop the selective logging example.
comments.quote: I suggest to drop "such as selective logging" since selective logging was not included in this study

reviews.assessment: Extremely interesting and impressive study; methodological caveats about fogging and sampling need discussion.

comments.issue: It is unclear how sensitive results are to the identity of reference leaves and arthropod subsamples.
comments.request: Assess and discuss sensitivity to sample identity.
comments.quote: Would identity of leaves selected as reference samples from rainforest plots make much difference to the results?

comments.issue: Canopy height differences mean fogging samples different strata across habitats, biasing comparisons.
comments.request: Discuss the strata sampled and state whether pesticide coverage was checked.
comments.quote: presumably fogging in these habitats will sample the whole canopy, while in rainforest and jungle rubber, fogging from the ground will presumably only effectively sample the lower strata

comments.issue: Trays spaced from oil palm trunks catch only frond arthropods, potentially explaining high herbivore incidence.
comments.request: Discuss this sampling limitation for oil palm.
comments.quote: I think this could affect results quite a lot for this habitat, as the trays would only catch arthropods from fronds

comments.issue: More fogging subsamples were collected in forest and jungle rubber than other habitats.
comments.request: Consider how unequal subsample numbers affect means.
comments.quote: whether the higher number of fogging sub-samples collected in forest and jungle rubber compared to other habitats could affect abundance and biomass results?

comments.issue: Abstract line 44 needs 'being' for clarity.
comments.request: Add 'being' between 'rapidly' and 'converted'.
comments.quote: 44 – Add "being" in between "rapidly" and "converted" for clarity

comments.issue: The oil palm impact review cited is outdated and the spatial scope of lines 62-63 is unclear.
comments.request: Cite a more recent oil palm review and clarify the scope.
comments.quote: I would cite a more up-to-date oil palm impacts review than Fitzherbert et al. 2008

comments.issue: 'Done' at line 92 should be 'studied'.
comments.request: Replace the word.
comments.quote: 92 – suggest replacing "done" with "studied".

comments.issue: Trophic redundancy is not defined for this study context.
comments.request: Define trophic redundancy.
comments.quote: it would be useful to define what you mean by trophic redundancy in this study context

comments.issue: 'As control' at line 119 is unclear.
comments.request: Reword to 'as a control habitat'.
comments.quote: suggest rewording "as control" to "as a control habitat" to clarify?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether lines 126-129 give the number of trees sampled per plot.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: is this the number of trees sampled per plot? Please tweak wording to clarify.

comments.issue: 'Communities of' at line 272 should be 'communities across'.
comments.request: Reword for clarity.
comments.quote: Suggest reword "communities of" to "communities across" for clarity.

comments.issue: The sentence at line 320 is unclear.
comments.request: Reword, possibly as 'are reliably predicted by taxonomic identity'.
comments.quote: this was a bit unclear – suggest reword for clarity. Do you mean "are reliably predicted by taxonomic identity"?

comments.issue: The 13C-enriched signal at lines 321-333 could reflect epiphytes being eaten.
comments.request: Consider the epiphyte explanation.
comments.quote: could this also be related to epiphytes being eaten, as I think these can also be 13C-enriched compared to trees

comments.issue: The selective logging sensitivity claim at lines 393-394 is only supported by regional differences.
comments.request: Cut the selective logging line.
comments.quote: I think this is only really supported by the differences observed between regions in this study (which could also be due to other factors) – suggest cutting this line.

comments.issue: Figure 4 outlying plots are hard to read and group names are incomplete.
comments.request: Simplify the plot and define group abbreviations.
comments.quote: the outlying plots in this figure are quite hard to read and I think should be simplified for clarity

comments.issue: 'Pack hunting' is an unusual term for social insects in Box 1.
comments.request: Use 'group foraging' instead.
comments.quote: "pack hunting" is an unusual term for social insects, perhaps say "group foraging" instead?

comments.issue: The grey and white circles in Figure S1 are unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify the symbols.
comments.quote: I am not sure what the grey and white circles in the top right refer to?

comments.issue: Panel order in Figures S3 and S4 is inconsistent with previous figures.
comments.request: Swap panel order for consistency.
comments.quote: consider swapping panel order for consistency

comments.issue: Two Chapter S1 sentences have grammatical errors.
comments.request: Fix the wording of both sentences.
comments.quote: Suggest rewording "taxonomic groups also depended season" to "taxonomic groups also depended on season"

comments.issue: 'Carnivory' in Figure S8 is inconsistent with 'predation' elsewhere.
comments.request: Change the label to 'predation'.
comments.quote: change "carnivory" to "predation" in figure for consistency

title: Rainforest conversion to plantations fundamentally alters energy fluxes and functions in canopy arthropod food webs

study.system: urban pollinators and pollination; meta-analysis of 133 studies

editor_summary: Important, timely and well-written study; editor asks to lead with significant results and drop non-significant directionality, and all reviewers had major comments on the discussion.

reviews.assessment: Outstanding, long-overdue meta-analysis; only minor presentation and discussion-end improvements.
strengths: high statistical standard using raw data

comments.issue: Non-significant results are described as if an effect had been found.
comments.request: Separate significant from non-significant results clearly.
comments.quote: I would like to separate the significant results, i.e. the real effects, more clearly from the non-significant results.

comments.issue: The first discussion paragraph is too long.
comments.request: Shorten the first discussion paragraph to the highlights.
comments.quote: I would shorten the first paragraph (L335-346) a bit, and bring only the real highlights.

comments.issue: The closing sentence of the discussion is weak and vague.
comments.request: End with specific research questions.
comments.quote: not only write that there is still a lot to do, but get specific and list research questions that urgently need to be addressed

reviews.assessment: Well-crafted and potentially highly cited, but the discussion and conclusion are one-sided and do not exploit the paper's potential.

comments.issue: Discussion and conclusion only address the overall negative effect and miss bigger questions about cities in conservation.
comments.request: Address bigger questions about the role of cities for pollinators.
comments.quote: The discussion and conclusion only focus on the overall negative effect of urbanization and feels at time one-dimensional and mechanistic.

comments.issue: The large heterogeneity, with many positive responses, is not discussed, making the discussion one-sided.
comments.request: Discuss the heterogeneity and positive effects.
comments.quote: Many observations/studies (30-40 % in case of some responses) indicate positive effects. But this is not really addressed in the discussion leading to a one-sided discussion.

comments.issue: The most extreme urban/non-urban contrasts were chosen, which may drive the overall outcomes.
comments.request: Assess how the choice of contrasting categories affects results.
comments.quote: The authors also went for the categories that would yield the highest possible contrast between the urban and non-urban treatments and I wonder how this might have affected the overall outcome of the study

comments.issue: Light pollution is not mentioned among urbanization drivers.
comments.request: Mention light pollution.
comments.quote: Consider mentioning also light pollution.

comments.issue: Intrinsic value of biodiversity and designing natural cities are not addressed.
comments.request: Touch on intrinsic value and more natural cities.
comments.quote: One might also touch upon on the intrinsic value of biodiversity and for the need to design more natural cities that increase human-wellbeing

comments.issue: The fact that most future urbanization will occur in the tropics is not stressed.
comments.request: Stress that most urbanization will happen in the tropics.
comments.quote: But the vast majority of urbanization will happen in the tropics. I think it is really important to stress this here.

comments.issue: Line-level wording edits (L71, L75, L76, L88, L276, L335, L363).
comments.quote: Repetitive wording: You already talk about interest in line 67. Consider using a different term here, like ‘concern’.

comments.issue: General conservation status of pollinators is not introduced.
comments.request: Add a sentence on pollinator conservation status.
comments.quote: Maybe it is a good idea to add a sentence or two on the general conservation status on pollinators?

comments.issue: The scale of urban agriculture and its reliance on pollinators is not mentioned.
comments.request: Add a sentence on current and future urban agriculture.
comments.quote: It would be worthwhile to add a further sentence on the scale of current and future urban agriculture to underline the functional importance of pollinators in urban environments.

comments.issue: The large overlap of temperate studies is not mentioned early enough.
comments.request: Mention the temperate-study overlap at this point.
comments.quote: It might be good to mention here already the great overlap of temperate studies.

comments.issue: The claim about tropical urbanization is presented as fact and may be context-dependent.
comments.request: Rephrase the tropical urbanization claim cautiously.
comments.quote: Maybe consider rephrasing this more carefully. Currently it is presented as a fact.

comments.issue: Study design differences in baseline (control) and urban (treatment) habitat are not considered.
comments.request: Acknowledge and discuss baseline/treatment differences among studies.
comments.quote: One important aspect that is missing here in this list is study design. What was considered as baseline habitat (i.e. the control), and what has been considered as the urban habitat (i.e. the treatment)

comments.issue: How the choice of extreme comparisons affects results is not examined.
comments.request: Report control-category distribution and test less extreme contrasts.
comments.quote: Would the results change if you would have taken the decision to go for the less extreme comparisons?

comments.issue: The Wan et al. extraction method is not described concretely.
comments.request: Describe the Wan et al. extraction method.
comments.quote: Could you put this into concrete terms what the method from Wan et al. entails?

comments.issue: How often each data-extraction method was used is not reported.
comments.request: Report the frequency of each extraction method.
comments.quote: Can you report roughly how often you used which method to extract the relevant data?

comments.issue: How the highest-activity period was determined is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how the highest-activity period was determined.
comments.quote: Do you mean here the period (i.e. time of year, month or even day) that can generally be expected to have the highest activity?

comments.issue: The moderator-variable paragraph lacks an opening sentence explaining their logic.
comments.request: Add an introductory sentence on the moderator logic.
comments.quote: Consider starting this paragraph with one short and very general sentence that describe the logic behind the use of these moderator variables.

comments.issue: It is unclear which studies reported the extracted variables.
comments.request: Clarify which studies reported these variables.
comments.quote: Where possible I guess? Not all studies will have reported these, right?

comments.issue: The honey bee category is not defined (Apis mellifera only or tropical species too).
comments.request: Define the honey bee category precisely.
comments.quote: By honey bees, do you mean Apis mellifera or did you also include tropical honey bee species in this category

comments.issue: Sources for trait data are not given beyond Michener.
comments.request: Report sources for trait data, e.g. a table column.
comments.quote: What sources did you use to determine these traits? You only cite Michener – Bees of the world.

comments.issue: 'Qualitatively' similar is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what 'qualitatively similar' means.
comments.quote: Please explain better what you mean with ‘qualitatively’ similar?

comments.issue: A statement lacks a concrete citation.
comments.request: Add a citation supporting the statement.
comments.quote: A concrete citation might be good here.

comments.issue: The pollination result may not hold in the tropics, but climatic region is not tested as a moderator.
comments.request: Add climatic region as a moderator or acknowledge the tropical limitation.
comments.quote: Could you add climatic region as further moderator into the analysis of pollination?

comments.issue: The conclusion is not a dedicated paragraph.
comments.request: Give the conclusion its own paragraph.
comments.quote: Shouldn’t the conclusion be an extra dedicated paragraph?

comments.issue: Figure 1 circle sizes are ambiguous and panels b/c may not help.
comments.request: Clarify circle scaling and consider dropping panels b/c.
comments.quote: I am little unsure if circle sizes refer to the number of studies within a single location (i.e. city) or within a region.

comments.issue: Marginal effects are not marked and some labels have poor resolution.
comments.request: Mark marginal effects and fix label resolution.
comments.quote: A small suggestion would be to add a sign for marginally significant effects (a small cross or circle).

reviews.assessment: Timely, solid meta-analysis with interesting results, but many clarifications and improvements are needed to be publishable.

comments.issue: The running title is uninformative.
comments.request: Use a more informative running title.
comments.quote: Running title: I suggest changing to a more informative one such as “Meta-analysis on urban pollinators”

comments.issue: Newer references are missing.
comments.request: Add the suggested newer references.
comments.quote: Line 62: I suggest adding other newer references like Beninde et al 2015 (DOI: 10.1111/ele.12427) and Piano et al 2020 (DOI: 10.1111/gcb.14934)

comments.issue: Faeth et al. 2011 is not an appropriate reference for the statement.
comments.request: Replace or justify the Faeth et al. reference.
comments.quote: Line 75: I think Faeth et al. 2011 is not the most appropriate reference to support what you say.

comments.issue: A statement lacks a reference.
comments.request: Add a reference for that sentence.
comments.quote: Lines 103-104. It is necessary a reference for that sentence

comments.issue: Ollerton et al. 2007 and Willmer 2011 are not cited for the floral-visitor statement.
comments.request: Cite Ollerton et al. 2007 and Willmer 2011.
comments.quote: The references of Ollerton et al. 2007; Willmer 2011 should be used to sustain the first part of the sentence

comments.issue: The flower-symmetry sentence misleadingly implies radial flowers are less sensitive to urbanization.
comments.request: Rewrite to avoid the misunderstanding.
comments.quote: I suggest re-writing it to avoid misunderstanding: flower symmetry is somehow mediating the effects of urbanization on pollinators/pollination.

comments.issue: Other reviews on urban bees are not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention the additional bee reviews.
comments.quote: There are other reviews on the topic, especially on bees, that deserve to be mentioned as well

comments.issue: The pollination-service goal is not clearly expressed with its tested moderators.
comments.request: State the pollination-service goal and tested moderators clearly.
comments.quote: The goal referring to the effects of urbanization on the pollination service should be better expressed, indicating the moderators that were tested

comments.issue: It is not justified why flower availability and pollinator origin were not tested.
comments.request: Justify excluding these moderators.
comments.quote: I wonder why you did not test the effects of flower availability or pollinator origin on pollination. Please, justify.

comments.issue: Phenology is not defined and is separated from functional traits inconsistently.
comments.request: Define phenology and use terminology consistently.
comments.quote: I do not know why you separate functional traits from phenology (see lines 125 or 258) if those two characteristics represent traits as well

comments.issue: Visitation duration and number are not listed among the examined variables.
comments.request: State that visitation duration and number were also examined.
comments.quote: Line 147. Please add that you also looked at other variables like visitation duration and visitation number.

comments.issue: Appendix 1/2 order and naming are wrong; 'months' is misspelled for 'moths' at L357.
comments.request: Reorder appendices and fix the misspelling.
comments.quote: Line 152. Appendix 1 should appear before Appendix 2. Re-assign the names of the tables, please.

comments.issue: Taxonomic groups are not used consistently at class/order level.
comments.request: Use consistent class/order-level taxonomy throughout.
comments.quote: I suggest dividing it into Aves, and Mammalia (both at Class level), then for Insecta class divide it into Hymenoptera, Lepidoptera, Diptera, and Coleoptera orders.

comments.issue: Sources for trait measurements are not given.
comments.request: Give sources for all trait measurements.
comments.quote: You should give the sources (web pages, references) that you used to collect the trait data.

comments.issue: Hymenoptera trait results are generalized to all pollinators in the discussion.
comments.request: Restrict trait conclusions to Hymenoptera.
comments.quote: Most of the traits were measured for Hymenoptera, but then in some parts of the article, especially the discussion, you talk about traits of pollinators in general.

comments.issue: The response variables used for all categorical traits are not specified.
comments.request: Specify response variables for all categorical traits.
comments.quote: You should specify that you took the abundance and species richness of all categorical traits (not just seasonality) as the response variable.

comments.issue: Continuous traits were compared among pollinator groups but other traits were not; the inconsistency is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain or harmonize the group comparisons.
comments.quote: Why for the two continuous traits (body size and activity length) did you compare between pollinator groups (Fig S4 and S5) and for the others not?

comments.issue: The flowering-plant analysis lacks theoretical predictions in the Introduction.
comments.request: Add predictions for flowering-plant effects.
comments.quote: As you tested the effects of urbanization on flower abundance and richness, I suggest giving more theoretical support (predictions) on this aspect in the Introduction.

comments.issue: Results on flowering plants and pollinators are presented in the wrong order.
comments.request: Reorder the results presentation.
comments.quote: I would first mention the effects of urbanization on flowering plants and then the effects of flowering plants on pollinator richness and abundance.

comments.issue: Statistics for Fig. 4 are not reported.
comments.request: Report the statistics for Fig. 4.
comments.quote: Lines 296-303. Why did you not report the statistics for Fig 4? Please, include them.

comments.issue: Text implies a flower-symmetry moderator effect although it was not significant.
comments.request: Clarify that only the urbanization effect was detected.
comments.quote: The moderator flower symmetry was not significant according to Table 2. Please clarify that only the effect of urbanization was detected for radial flowers.

comments.issue: The significant urbanization effect on reproductive success is not marked in Fig. 5.
comments.request: Mark the significant effect in Fig. 5.
comments.quote: The significant effect of urbanization on reproductive success (Table 2) is not marked with an asterisk in Fig 5. Why that?

comments.issue: Reproductive success is largely based on proxies such as visit rate, which needs caution.
comments.request: Discuss the proxy nature of reproductive success measures.
comments.quote: some caution must have in the discussion on this aspect, since the larger samples come from “proxies” of reproductive success such as visit rate and visit number, and not from real values

comments.issue: Fig. 2 lacks moderator names on the left side.
comments.request: Add moderator names to Fig. 2 as in Fig. 4.
comments.quote: Fig. 2. It should have the names of the moderators on the left side, not only the categories. Please follow the design of Fig 4.

comments.issue: Funnel-plot results indicating possible bias are not carefully considered.
comments.request: Discuss funnel-plot indications of bias.
comments.quote: The results of funnel plots for certain variables should be carefully considered, especially in the Discussion.

comments.issue: 'Poorly known' mischaracterizes the existing literature.
comments.request: Rephrase the knowledge-gap claim.
comments.quote: I would not say “poorly known” since there is a lot of literature on the topic.

comments.issue: The discussion attributes the pollination effect to generalist and managed species rather than Apis mellifera.
comments.request: Attribute the effect specifically to Apis mellifera.
comments.quote: I suggest replacing “due to the high abundance of generalist and managed pollinator species” with “due to the high abundance of Apis mellifera, a generalist and managed pollinator species

comments.issue: The lack of effect should be clarified as occurring in the tropics.
comments.request: State that the lack of effect is in the tropics.
comments.quote: Lines 373-374. Please clarify first that the lack of an effect is in the tropics

comments.issue: The intended season ('early spring') is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the 'early spring' statement.
comments.quote: Line 400. I think that you mean “early spring”, please clarify.

comments.issue: The claim that the plant-pollinator richness relationship is rarely explored in cities is unsupported and doubtful.
comments.request: Support or revise the rarity claim.
comments.quote: Please provide a reference to support that the relationship between flowering plant richness and pollinator diversity has rarely been explored in urban habitats. I do not think that was so rare.

comments.issue: The conclusion that bumble bees and honey bees drive the pollination effect is not supported, as only honey bees were significant.
comments.request: Correct the interpretation of the pollination driver.
comments.quote: Why did you conclude that the positive effect of urbanization on pollination was driven by bumble bees and honey bees when the effect was significant only for the last group?

comments.issue: The conclusion lacks a strong management and conservation message.
comments.request: Strengthen the management and conservation message.
comments.quote: I think that the conclusion should give a more powerful message in terms of management and conservation.

comments.issue: Implications of relying on managed honey bees, including risks to native mutualisms, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss implications of relying on managed honey bees.
comments.quote: you could not be assured that plant reproductive success could be even higher if native wild species were not detrimentally affected by urbanization

title: The effects of urbanization on pollinators and pollination: A meta‐analysis

study.system: bi- and tritrophic communities; feasibility domain models

editor_summary: Editor: all reviewers agree the paper must be more accessible (rearrange main text/supplement, add conceptual figures) and the weak empirical example must be strengthened; consider van Nes and Scheffer 2004.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and potentially useful, but the mathematical context and weak empirical test need clearer explanation.
strengths: good job citing relevant previous work

comments.issue: The premise and context of the mathematical analyses are not explained enough; readers are assumed to know the cited body of work.
comments.request: Introduce the key concepts, findings and novelty of the study more clearly.
comments.quote: While I understand the authors decision to just cite previous work and build on it, I am worried that in the current format the manuscript might be of interest only to a small group of Ecology Letters readers.

comments.issue: Parameter definitions and the justification of modelling choices (closed form approach, intermediate size) are missing.
comments.request: Add a parameter table and justify the choices.
comments.quote: Mathematical analyses: I would suggest adding a table with all the parameters and their definitions.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the empirical results truly support the mathematical analyses; alternative reasons for species return are not addressed.
comments.request: Clarify the relevance of the empirical test to the theory.
comments.quote: While I appreciate the attempt to test mathematical analyses with empirical data, it was unclear to me whether the results truly support the data.

comments.issue: Assuming each trophic level is regulated only from below omits top-down effects, which may influence the result that only mean responses matter.
comments.request: Justify the no-top-down-effect assumption and test its influence.
comments.quote: 89-91: Why is every level only regulated by the trophic level below it? An important aspect of 3 trophic levels is the top-down effect. Is this assumption of no top-down effect somehow influential in the result that only species mean responses are important?

comments.issue: 'Understood entrywise' is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the term.
comments.quote: 108: unclear what “understood entrywise” means

comments.issue: The multiplicative form of environmental effects is not justified.
comments.request: Explain why environmental effects are multiplicative.
comments.quote: 113-114: Why are the environmental effects multiplicative?

comments.issue: The formula for Xi is only in the supplement.
comments.request: Include the formula for Xi in the main text.
comments.quote: 120- Maybe include the formula for Ξ in the main text?

comments.issue: The metacommunity aspect (lines 141-146) feels forced and is not motivated in the introduction.
comments.request: Motivate or move the metacommunity discussion.
comments.quote: 141-146: This meta-community aspect felt forced. There was no indication that this would be considered based on text in the intro. It was also unclear to me why this was being discussed.

comments.issue: The parameters delta and zeta are not explained enough.
comments.request: Explain what delta and zeta are.
comments.quote: 202-205: I needed more explanation for what δ and ζ are.

comments.issue: The link between the field data (Fig. 6) and the mathematical analyses is not demonstrated.
comments.request: Link each variable to a model parameter or remove the empirical section.
comments.quote: Based on the results in Fig 6, I am not sure how this data actually supports the mathematical analyses.

comments.issue: Whether the intrinsic growth vector b could be shown in Fig. 1a.
comments.request: Consider showing the growth vector b.
comments.quote: Fig 1a: Would it make sense to show the intrinsic growth vector ‘b’?

comments.issue: Fig. 1b lacks explanation, including what the dashed lines mean.
comments.request: Explain Fig. 1b and the dashed lines.
comments.quote: Fig 1b: I needed more explanation for this. What are the dashed lines?

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 4 use non-descriptive delta and zeta axes.
comments.request: Use more ecologically descriptive axis labels.
comments.quote: Fig 2, 4: Could you use a more ecologically descriptive x and y axes instead of just δ and ζ

comments.issue: Fig. 3 lines may be regressions but lack R2, and panel 3 has narrow range with high variation.
comments.request: Report R2 and address the panel 3 fit.
comments.quote: Fig 3: Are the lines actual regressions? If yes, could you add a R2. Also, in panel 3, the range seems too narrow and the variation seems too high to be able to fit those lines.

reviews.assessment: Technically sound and novel, but the main text does not stand alone and the empirical example is unconvincing.
strengths: novel derivations and extensions of the feasibility domain approach

comments.issue: Neither main text nor supplement stands alone; too much is in the supplement and supplement figures are out of order.
comments.request: Move the key derivations to the main text and the simulations/metacommunity model to the supplement.
comments.quote: One of the main problems I encountered when reading this manuscript was that neither the main text nor the supplementary materials stand on their own. The main text is incomprehensible without the supplementary text.

comments.issue: The empirical example applies a linear approximation over the full range of chemistry values where linear responses may not hold.
comments.request: Restrict or qualify the empirical analysis to small environmental changes.
comments.quote: But this is partly true because the growth rates and interaction rates change linearly with changes in the environment (as presented by fi and gi), however, many species responses to environmental change are not linear.

comments.issue: The supplement sentence explaining fi = 1 and gi = 1 is very hard to understand.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence about species responses.
comments.quote: Line 20 in the supplement the authors state: “When species do not respond to environmental change, fi = 1 and gi = 1, implying no effect of the change on the model parameters.

comments.issue: Equation 19 in the supplement does not match the bitrophic Mathematica document.
comments.request: Reconcile the equation definitions.
comments.quote: Equation 19 in the supplement does not match with the final equation in the bitrophic mathematica document.

comments.issue: A Mathematica notebook referenced in supplement line 135 is not supplied.
comments.request: Provide the missing Mathematica notebook.
comments.quote: Line 135 of the supplement it says: Replacing E1 and d with E1,ε and dε in eq. 21 yields Ξε (Mathematica notebook). But no other mathematica notebook is supplied other than bitrophic and tritrophic documents.

comments.issue: Section 3.2 reports no closed-form results and jumps to simulations.
comments.request: Report the closed-form results in this section.
comments.quote: The results of section 3.2 in the main text (Larger communities) does not report any results about the closed form results and just starts discussing the simulation results.

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 3 appear in the wrong order relative to the text.
comments.request: Flip Figures 2 and 3.
comments.quote: Figure 2 and 3 should be flipped in order because figure 3a shows the results of the bitrophic closed form derivation which are discussed first.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether removing taxa occurring in at least 10% of sites removed abundant taxa.
comments.request: Clarify the taxon filtering criterion.
comments.quote: L 165 main text, the authors state “We removed taxa that occurred in at least 10% of the sites”. Does this mean that the authors removed abundant taxa?

comments.issue: Two line-level corrections: g3 should be gi (line 8) and r1/r2/r3 should be r1f/r2f/r3f (Eq. 19).
comments.quote: Line 8 g3 should be gi

reviews.assessment: Strong theory package with clear explanation, but figures and the weak real-world test need improvement.
strengths: good balance of equations and words

comments.issue: Only Figure 1 is useful; the other figures add little and appeal mainly to theoreticians.
comments.request: Create more conceptual figures illustrating the take-home messages.
comments.quote: I think the authors should try to be much more imaginative and include some more conceptual-type figures that actually illustrate the take-home messages of their paper more clearly. The risk they run is that they are only appealing to theoreticians.

comments.issue: The real-world test is weak and poorly described; whether identical communities across sites exist is unclear.
comments.request: Describe the empirical test and address whether communities can be compared across sites.
comments.quote: The real-world test is rather weak. It’s not described well enough. For example, I wasn’t at all clear whether they were looking for communities of identical species across sites.

comments.issue: If the real-world test is retained it needs better description, re-wording and a much better figure.
comments.request: Rewrite and re-illustrate the real-world test.
comments.quote: If the authors want to retain the real-world test (and I understand why they probably do) then it needs a bit more description, some re-wording and a much better figure.

comments.issue: No reason is given for removing taxa occurring in at least 10% of sites.
comments.request: Explain the taxon removal criterion.
comments.quote: Section 2.5 We need a reason why you removed taxa occurring in at least 10% of sites.

comments.issue: Figures 2 and 6 are unhelpful and use unintuitive region labels.
comments.request: Label regions more intuitively, e.g. domain size larger/smaller.
comments.quote: Figures 2 and 6 not really very helpful. What’s the take-home message? Can you label the regions more intuitively: e.g. domain size larger/ domain size smaller, rather than dxe/de.

comments.issue: Figure 4 panels look very similar and convey no clear message.
comments.request: Consider a different figure summarizing the take-home messages.
comments.quote: Figure 4 – all panels look very similar. I’m not sure what message I’m supposed to be taking home from this. Perhaps consider a completely different kind of figure

comments.issue: Figure 5 title does not say these are metacommunity model outcomes and is too long.
comments.request: Clarify and shorten the figure title.
comments.quote: Figure 5 – need to make it clearer in title of figure that these are outcomes from a metacommunity model. The first sentence (title) is far too long and confusing.

comments.issue: Section 3.5 is confusing and too compressed; 'communities', 'used range' and 'found back' are undefined and the figure does not help.
comments.request: Rethink and expand this section with a helpful figure.
comments.quote: Section 3.5 is confusing. It might really benefit from a figure! What do you mean by ‘communities’ – must these have identical species compositions?

title: Mean species responses predict effects of environmental change on coexistence

study.system: herbaceous plant community; 15N transfer, phenology, mycorrhizal networks

editor_summary: Editor: reviews were disparate with editorial debate; novelty concerns should be addressed by incorporating the forest literature, and Reviewer 1's concerns about experimental design and inference should be addressed head on.

reviews.assessment: Transfer of 15N is shown, but the experiment is not rigorously controlled and does not establish direct mycorrhizal transfer.

comments.issue: The idea of plants sharing resources via mycorrhizal networks has been extensively explored, so the novelty is overstated.
comments.request: Acknowledge and engage with the existing mycorrhizal network literature.
comments.quote: However, the general idea (plants interacting/sharing resources via mycorrhizal networks) has been extensively explored, at least in forests

comments.issue: The field experiment is not rigorously controlled, so direct N sharing cannot be unequivocally demonstrated.
comments.request: Strengthen controls so direct sharing can be distinguished.
comments.quote: there are so many things you cannot control through this approach, it is difficult to unequivocally demonstrate that plants are directly sharing N

comments.issue: The study does not rigorously establish that N movement occurs via direct mycorrhizal transfer.
comments.request: Provide evidence for the mycorrhizal transfer mechanism.
comments.quote: I am not as confident that this study has rigorously established that the movement of N occurs via direct mycorrhizal transfers

comments.issue: Missing LeRoy reference and unwarranted passive tense throughout.
comments.request: Add the reference and revise passive constructions.
comments.quote: Page 3, Line 32 – I find the use of passive tense here (and in places throughout the manuscript) is unwarranted and distracting

comments.issue: The sentence about contrasted nutrient gradients on page 2 is unclear and the benefit beyond reduced competition is vague.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence and the additional benefit.
comments.quote: This sentence is unclear (“contrasted gradients of nutrients”), and the benefit beyond reducing competition should be clarified

comments.issue: Experimental design is unclear; a proper control would disconnect plants from the mycorrhizal network, and 'isolated' is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify the design and add a network-disconnected control.
comments.quote: To me, the most appropriate control for this experiment would be one that has been disconnected from the adjacent mycorrhizal network

comments.issue: No photo or figure shows how the label was applied, making methods hard to reproduce.
comments.request: Add a photo or figure of the label application.
comments.quote: A photo or figure showing how the label was applied is critical, I would argue

comments.issue: Soil could mediate 15N transfer within 9 days; soil/rhizosphere label was apparently not tested.
comments.request: Test 15N in soil and rhizosphere to rule out soil transfer.
comments.quote: It certainly seems possible that 15N could be transferred via the soil in 9 days even without considering litter production

reviews.assessment: Absolutely stellar, admirably careful study with a meticulous design and no major concerns about methods or conclusions.
strengths: effective discussion of nitrogen sharing mechanisms

comments.issue: Water limitation results and predictions are not addressed in the discussion.
comments.request: Add a discussion paragraph on how water limitation affects the message.
comments.quote: I think that it would be important to add a paragraph to the discussion where you specifically address these results

comments.issue: A new paragraph should start after the contrasting phenology sentence on page 3.
comments.request: Start a new paragraph at this point.
comments.quote: I would suggest that you start a new paragraph after

comments.issue: The lme4 package underlying lmerTest is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Bates et al. 2015 for lme4.
comments.quote: I think you should also cite the lme4 package, as that is the main bit of code running beneath the lmerTest package

comments.issue: The regular cor() function ignores hierarchical data structure.
comments.request: Justify or replace the correlation approach given the data structure.
comments.quote: Is there a reason that you use the regular cor() function here? My understanding is that it will not account for any of the hierarchical structures in your data

comments.issue: Unclear whether the GLM was fitted with the glmer function.
comments.request: State which function was used for the GLM.
comments.quote: Pg. 6, L53: For the GLM, did you fit this with the glmer function?

comments.issue: Species names should be listed rather than abbreviations on page 7.
comments.request: Use full species names.
comments.quote: I would suggest listing the species names here, rather than abbreviations

comments.issue: 21 line-level spelling and grammar corrections throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: Pg. 5, L12-13: “after 3 months being buried in the soil under” -> “after 4 months buried in the soil under”

title: Nitrogen transfer between plant species with different temporal N‐demand

study.system: Pararge aegeria butterflies; replicated common-garden experiments on seasonal plasticity

editor_summary: Editor praises the study but requires: distribution-appropriate models for development time and confidence intervals for diapause; discussion of paternal effects (F1 vs F2) and of site phenology changes beyond adult emergence.

reviews.assessment: Timely and interesting, but major concerns about terminology, adaptive evidence, population comparison and experimental controls.
strengths: wide interest to Ecology Letters readers

comments.issue: Phenotypic plasticity, genetic evolution and the evolution of plasticity are used without distinguishing them, and evolutionary change is inferred without gene expression evidence.
comments.request: Explain the differences between the terms with climate-change examples and justify the evolutionary interpretation.
comments.quote: It would be useful if the authors could explain the differences between these terms, and provide examples of each one in the context of climate change.

comments.issue: Local adaptation is invoked without direct evidence that the patterns are adaptive or linked to fitness.
comments.request: Provide evidence such as a translocation experiment, and address costs and limits of plasticity.
comments.quote: they do not have direct evidence on whether and to what extent these patterns are actually adaptive, i.e. associated with fitness benefits

comments.issue: The two populations are analysed separately rather than compared directly in a single model.
comments.request: Build a single model including population ID as a factor or random factor.
comments.quote: Indeed, the authors are not comparing the two populations directly as they are building separate analyses for each one.

comments.issue: The amount of variation explained by photoperiod is not quantified.
comments.request: Report statistics such as R-squared or deviance for photoperiod.
comments.quote: it would be good to show here some statistics (r-square, deviance) showing the amount of the variation explained by photoperiod

comments.issue: It is unclear whether humidity levels were matched to the historic experiment.
comments.request: Report whether the same humidity levels were used.
comments.quote: Did they also keep the same levels of humidity?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the design was balanced for sex, matched to the historic experiment, and whether trial duration was controlled.
comments.request: Report and include these factors as random effects in the model.
comments.quote: was the experiment fully balanced, such that the same number of males and females for each population featured each photoperiod level?

comments.issue: The text at L69 does not acknowledge that different life stages may depend on different environmental cues.
comments.request: Acknowledge that phenology depends on multiple plastic decisions and cues.
comments.quote: phenology depends on multiple plastic decisions of different climate cues. Indeed, different life-stages may depend on different environmental cues.

comments.issue: Ransvik individuals may differ between the May-June and July-August flight periods, yet only the later period was sampled.
comments.request: Explain why Ransvik individuals were not collected from the earlier period.
comments.quote: As you collected individuals from Riala in June, why you did not collect individuals from Ransvik from the earlier period?

comments.issue: It is unclear which period the mean annual temperature refers to, and conditions after development should not affect the traits.
comments.request: Specify the reference period for mean annual temperature.
comments.quote: are you estimating it for a calendar year (i.e. from 1st Jan to 31st Dec)? or for the year before each life history trait starts?

comments.issue: Figure 1 is confusing and it is unclear which data were used for it.
comments.request: Clarify the data used in Figure 1.
comments.quote: I find Figure 1 a bit confusing, please see my comment below

comments.issue: The distribution of residuals of the response variable is not checked.
comments.request: Report whether residuals are normally distributed.
comments.quote: Were the residuals of the response variable linearly distributed?

comments.issue: The change in photoperiod over the years is not shown graphically as was done for temperature.
comments.request: Plot the change in photoperiod over time.
comments.quote: Could you please represent graphically the change of the photoperiod (i.e. the same as you did for temperature)?

comments.issue: Photoperiod is treated as a categorical rather than continuous factor.
comments.request: Explain why photoperiod was treated as categorical.
comments.quote: L229: Why photoperiod is treated as a categorical factor?

comments.issue: The statement at L378 lacks references.
comments.request: Provide references for this statement.
comments.quote: L378: please provide references to this statement

comments.issue: The statement at L391 is too strong for only two data points in space and time.
comments.request: Temper the statement.
comments.quote: this statement is very strong considering that you have only two data points in space-and-time

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks axis labels.
comments.request: Add labels or names to the axes.
comments.quote: Figure 1: could you please add labels/names to the axes?

comments.issue: The interpretation assumes co-gradient variation, but counter-gradient variation is also possible for genetically different populations.
comments.request: Consider counter-gradient variation as an alternative.
comments.quote: it seems to me that you are assuming co-gradient variation. But counter-gradient variation could also be the rule, especially if you have genetically different populations.

comments.issue: The Figure 2 caption should describe inter-annual variation with Julian date on the x-axis.
comments.request: Clarify the Figure 2 caption.
comments.quote: I would say inter-annual variation (x-axis being Julian date) of the mean temperature for historic and contemporary data.

comments.issue: Tables S1 and S2 compare means of fluctuating climate variables, which is uninformative.
comments.request: Analyse climate variability rather than only mean differences.
comments.quote: Usually, climate is fluctuating, so just comparing the means is not very informative.

comments.issue: The discussion of the appendices is separated from the main text.
comments.request: Move the appendix discussion into the main text.
comments.quote: I would place the Discussion of the Appendices in the main text.

reviews.assessment: Nice historical comparison with an interesting result, but vague framing, missing confidence intervals and unexamined model assumptions need attention.
strengths: no change in critical photoperiod for diapause is interesting

comments.issue: No field phenology data are presented, so it is unknown whether diapause timing or larval diapause incidence is changing in nature.
comments.request: Discuss the lack of field phenology data and its consequences for inference.
comments.quote: the question that kept nagging me as I read through the manuscript was whether there are any observed changes in phenology in the field between the historical and contemporary samples

comments.issue: There is no clear rationale for why extending the growing season would be beneficial, and the predictions about optimal diapause timing are hard to follow.
comments.request: Explain the predictions and rationale more clearly, perhaps with a third Figure 1 panel on seasonal timing.
comments.quote: I think a much clearer, more detailed, and thoughtful explanation is necessary here to set up the study.

comments.issue: The writing, especially the introduction, is vague and reads like an early draft, and the figures are drafty with missing information.
comments.request: Polish the narrative and figures.
comments.quote: Particularly in the introduction, I found the writing to be very vague in places – it felt like a solid, early draft that could use a lot more refining.

comments.issue: The study is framed narrowly around photoperiod, ignoring literature on life-cycle variation in seasonal responses, much of it on temperature.
comments.request: Broaden the framing to consider the wider literature on life-cycle seasonal responses.
comments.quote: When I read the title, I was expecting a broader consideration of the literature on variation in seasonal responses across the life cycle going beyond just responses to photoperiod.

comments.issue: The analysis focuses on null hypothesis testing without discussing effect magnitudes, and confidence intervals are missing from Figures 3 and 4 (also L261).
comments.request: Add confidence intervals and discuss the biological magnitude of differences.
comments.quote: Lack of, e.g., 95% CI in Figure 3 (and where relevant in Figure 4) makes it difficult to gauge the precision of the estimates and how different they might plausibly be.

comments.issue: Development time distributions are skewed and variances heterogeneous, threatening the assumptions of the linear models.
comments.request: Report goodness of fit and check model assumptions.
comments.quote: looks like some of those distributions are pretty skewed, and variances are pretty heterogenous, both potential problems for the null hypothesis testing that is used liberally here

comments.issue: The phrase at L56 about life history plasticity determining phenology is vague.
comments.request: Give concrete examples of plasticity determining timing.
comments.quote: This is a good example of loose narrative that leaves the reader guessing at what the author is intending.

comments.issue: The phrase 'inappropriate plastic responses' at L63 is confusing.
comments.request: Clarify that the plastic response would produce the wrong phenology under warming.
comments.quote: I think you mean that current plastic response would produce the ‘wrong’ phenology with a warming climate?

comments.issue: 'Physiological development' at L72 is undefined.
comments.request: Define what is meant by physiological development.
comments.quote: L72 – what is ‘physiological development’?

comments.issue: The distinction between in concert and independent evolution at L74 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the conceptual distinction.
comments.quote: In concert vs. independent evolution is really unclear.

comments.issue: 'Strong' at L78 sounds awkward and vague.
comments.request: Use a more precise term or state the voltinism pattern directly.
comments.quote: ‘strong’ sounds awkward. Maybe ‘marked’, or ‘pronounced’? Though, even that is vague.

comments.issue: The statement at L96-97 that something 'would be expected' is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why this pattern would be expected.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I understand why it would be expected. Another vague statement that could benefit from clarification.

comments.issue: The term 'allochronic' at L98 is unnecessary or undefined in context.
comments.request: Define or remove 'allochronic'.
comments.quote: is ‘allochronic’ necessary here? If so, what does it mean in this context?

comments.issue: 'Direct development' at L103 means something different in other disciplines.
comments.request: Define or change the terminology.
comments.quote: People who study insect diapause probably all define it the same way, but in many other disciplines it means a life cycle where juvenile forms closely resemble adult forms.

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks axis labels and a legend for the dashed and solid lines.
comments.request: Add axis labels and a line legend.
comments.quote: Figure 1 – no axis labels. Also, a legend for the dashed and solid line would make it easier to interpret

comments.issue: 'Distinctly different phenologies' at L114 is vague.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant.
comments.quote: what do you mean by ‘distinctly different phenologies’?

comments.issue: In Figure 2 the green sites are hard to see and axis labels and descriptive panel labels are missing.
comments.request: Enlarge the sites, add axis labels and descriptive panel labels.
comments.quote: The green ‘site’s in panel a are very small and hard to see, also no axis labels

comments.issue: 'Pupal development time' at L80 is misleading because the studies measure diapause incidence and timing of initiation.
comments.request: Be transparent about what traits are measured and rename the term.
comments.quote: ‘pupal development time’ is misleading. Though I guess it’s related, these studies are measuring diapause incidence.

comments.issue: The key figure from the original paper is not reproduced, so the historic data and site differences are hard to evaluate.
comments.request: Reproduce the key figure from the original paper.
comments.quote: I think it would be really useful to have some reproduction of the key figure from the original paper here

comments.issue: 'Weighed' is misspelled at L211.
comments.request: Correct the spelling.
comments.quote: L211 – I think it should be ‘weighed’

comments.issue: It is unclear why one procedure was more appropriate than the other at L237.
comments.request: Justify the choice of procedure.
comments.quote: why was one procedure more appropriate than the other?

comments.issue: 'Meaningfully' at L265 is undefined.
comments.request: Define what 'meaningfully' means in this context.
comments.quote: L265 – what does ‘meaningfully’ mean?

comments.issue: Data for the different sexes are not plotted separately even though responses may depend on sex.
comments.request: Plot the sexes separately.
comments.quote: if the responses depend on sex, I don’t understand why the data for different sexes are not plotted separately

comments.issue: It is unclear what quantity accompanies '3.8+-2.2' at L309.
comments.request: State whether it is a standard error or confidence interval.
comments.quote: ‘3.8+-2.2’ plus or minus what quantity? SE? lower/upper CI?

comments.issue: Discussing the frequency of individuals with a given development time treats a continuous variable as discrete.
comments.request: Frame the results as differences in mean development time.
comments.quote: talking about the frequency of individuals with a given development time is strange, as development time is not a discrete variable

comments.issue: The reaction norm changed shape but did not shift horizontally as predicted, contrary to the text's framing.
comments.request: Give a more nuanced explanation of the reaction norm change and its consequences for seasonal timing.
comments.quote: The shape of the reaction norm seems to have changed, but it’s not a clear horizontal shift as predicted.

comments.issue: The point at L393 is speculative and relates to the repeatability of evolutionary outcomes.
comments.request: Discuss the repeatability and predictability of evolutionary outcomes.
comments.quote: fair, though somewhat speculative point – might also speak to the repeatiblity/predictability of evolutionary outcomes

reviews.assessment: Important and innovative retrospective experiment, with parental effects (F1 vs F2) as the main concern, plus requests for clearer figures and interpretation.
strengths: important and interesting question addressing a key gap
excellent job maintaining similarity between the two studies

comments.issue: The historic study used F1 offspring while the current study used F2, so the comparison is confounded by generation.
comments.request: Address the parental-effect confound more clearly and its implications for inferring evolutionary change.
comments.quote: it seems like the comparison between historical and current studies would still be confounded by the generation used

comments.issue: The consequences of phenological mismatch at L50 are stated too strongly.
comments.request: Say 'potentially severe' ecological consequences.
comments.quote: it might be more accurate to say “potentially severe” ecological consequences

comments.issue: The expectations at L104-107 focus on early-season phenology, leaving late-season autumn phenology unaddressed.
comments.request: Clarify whether expectations also apply to autumn phenology.
comments.quote: Do these expectations intentionally or implicitly focus on the early season phenology? What about late season autumn phenology?

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks axis labels.
comments.request: Add axis labels.
comments.quote: Fig. 1: These figures need axis labels.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 10 km between sites represents meaningful climatic variation.
comments.request: Assess the climate gradient, possibly with interpolated climate models such as CHELSA.
comments.quote: What is the expectation of meaningful climatic variation across this scale? 10 kilometers could involve a strong climate gradient.

comments.issue: Parts of the discussion at L359 are hard to follow without referencing specific figures.
comments.request: Reference specific figures in the discussion.
comments.quote: it would be a lot easier to understand some parts of this discussion if specific Figures were referenced

comments.issue: The idea of 'developmental traps' from non-integer voltinism is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss developmental traps and whether the central population shows evidence of them.
comments.quote: It might be useful to discuss the idea of “developmental traps”, where longer seasons could favor multivoltinism in theory, but non-integer voltinism is selected against?

comments.issue: The lack of change in pupal diapause is interpreted as evidence of a changing reaction norm, which is confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the logic, including possible compensatory countergradient selection.
comments.quote: This is a bit confusing, as it seems like the lack of change in pupal diapause is being interpreted as evidence of a changing reaction norm.

comments.issue: The careful discussion of alternative explanations at L395-410 is not extended to the main findings.
comments.request: State that results are consistent with evolutionary change and discuss potential confounds.
comments.quote: I think it might be sufficient to say “We found evidence consistent with evolutionary change”, but to also discuss explicitly and clearly the potential for confounding effects.

comments.issue: The fascinating sentence at L419-421 needs more explanation.
comments.request: Elaborate on this sentence in more detail.
comments.quote: This is a fascinating sentence that needs more elaboration - please explain this in more detail.

title: Evolution of butterfly seasonal plasticity driven by climate change varies across life stages

study.system: Caribbean coral reefs; coral and gorgonian recruitment niches

editor_summary: Editor: paper favorably reviewed; the review offers suggestions for improving presentation and clarity; authors encouraged to respond fully.

reviews.assessment: Fascinating, well-executed study with no major faults; only minor clarity and presentation suggestions.

comments.issue: Recruits were not identified to species; different species may occupy different benthic niches and explain the wider scleractinian niche.
comments.request: Discuss whether weedy and stress-tolerant species differ in habitat suitability.
comments.quote: Fundamentally I’m really wondering if there is a difference in habitat suitability between weedy and stress-tolerant species, and if that explains the wider niche breadth.

comments.issue: Whether recruitment or conditions differed between the two collection times, and whether this was tested, is unclear.
comments.request: Test or discuss differences between collection times.
comments.quote: Did anything change between the two collection times, or were there different levels of recruitment during those times that would impact the analysis? Did the analysis do anything to test for differences between collection times?

comments.issue: It is surprising that %algae cover did not predict settlement and settlement cues do not stand out.
comments.request: Discuss settlement cues more comprehensively.
comments.quote: It was surprising that %algae cover did not predict settlement, and that settlement cues do not stand out in this analysis.

comments.quote: In the end the manuscript reads more as a review of eco-evolutionary stoichiometry than as a conceptual framework.

comments.issue: Readers already convinced of the integration are not guided toward testable predictions.

comments.quote: we are exposed to the complexity of this integration without being guided through that complexity to formulate testable predictions

comments.request: Define elemental traits as material fluxes measured in elemental units.
comments.quote: defining elemental traits as ‘an abstraction of this complexity’ is rather vague

comments.quote: I for example don’t see why shedding or reproduction rates are by definition elemental traits. They become so once they are measured in units of elements.
