title: A general framework to quantify and compare ecological impacts under temporal dynamics

study.system: large-river food webs; sonar habitat mapping and energetic models

editor_summary: Editor sees a large conceptual leap from data to ecosystem stability without direct stability measures; warns heterogeneity may be confounded with productivity; and notes that energetics methods may trivially lower interaction strengths as prey richness rises; major revision needed.

reviews.assessment: Highly impressed by the creativity and sophisticated methods; finds the habitat-diversity-interaction-strength result convincing, with mostly minor comments on balance and references.

comments.issue: The abstract implies that productive habitat patches are rare, which is not always true.
comments.request: Qualify the claim that productive patches are rare.
comments.quote: In the Abstract, they mention the importance of rare patches of habitat that can have high production and reduced interaction strengths (more on this below). Not all productive habitats are rare.

comments.issue: The 2% wood estimate from an Australian river is not representative; North American studies report much higher wood coverage.
comments.request: Acknowledge other wood-quantification studies and avoid implying wood habitat is always rare.
comments.quote: There are other studies on wood quantification in North America such as Wallace and Benke (1984) on a low gradient river (Ogeechee River) that estimated wood surfaces ranged from 20 to 50% of the river habitats

comments.issue: The phrase 'mesh bags and scrubbed' for woody debris sampling is unclear.
comments.request: Use only 'mesh bags' for clarity.
comments.quote: When they say “mesh bags and scrubbed” for woody debris, this is unclear. Probably just saying “mesh bags” is sufficient.

comments.issue: Fish prey identified to species are never mentioned in the Results.
comments.request: Mention the fish prey species somewhere.
comments.quote: I don’t recall any mention of fish prey species in the Results. Wouldn’t this be good to mention at some point?

comments.issue: The statement that large woody debris patches are rare is unbalanced, as wood can cover much more habitat elsewhere.
comments.request: Add balance to the statements about production hotspots.
comments.quote: The problem with this statement is that patches of large woody debris are often not rare.

comments.issue: Benke (2018, Ecology), a detailed food-web flow and interaction-strength analysis, is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Benke (2018) here or elsewhere.
comments.quote: Benke (2018, in Ecology) is probably the most detailed analysis of food web of flows and interactions strengths, although limited to invertebrates on snags

comments.issue: The claim about three factors at line 352 seems incomplete; species number is also a factor.
comments.request: Reconsider the number of factors, including species number in the web.
comments.quote: Line 352. Wouldn’t there be more than 3 factors? e.g., numbers of species in the web.

comments.issue: The sentence at line 360 omits other predator groups such as invertebrate predators and large-bodied fishes.
comments.request: Add these predator groups for the general case.
comments.quote: Perhaps the invertebrate predators aren’t of any significance, but it wouldn’t hurt to add this in the sentence for the general case

comments.issue: 'Approaches such as ours' at lines 363-365 is ambiguous given the multiple approaches used.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant and cite Benke (2018) if TBP is meant.
comments.quote: What do they mean by “approaches such as ours”? They used multiple approaches to deal with the major question.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and needed empirical work; mostly minor comments asking for more discussion of assumptions, robustness and definitions, and clearer framing of the sturgeon focus.
strengths: needed work on homogenization and interaction strength

comments.issue: The gross energetic estimates are error-prone, and error propagation and sensitivity to assumptions are not addressed.
comments.request: Add supplementary analyses and discussion arguing for the qualitative robustness of results.
comments.quote: The manuscript, to me, would benefit from more comments on the assumptions and their implications for the general results (e.g., sensitivity to the 3km assumption and other assumptions)

comments.issue: The definition of interaction strength used here is not set up clearly given the many possible estimators.
comments.request: Discuss the definition of interaction strength more explicitly.
comments.quote: perhaps a little more discussion on the definition of interaction strength used here would be warranted

comments.issue: The relationship of this work to the closely related Belmore et al. paper is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the progress relative to Belmore et al.
comments.quote: I think it would help to explain the relationship of this papers progress relative to the closely related Belmore et al. paper

comments.issue: The Shannon habitat diversity index is never defined in the main text.
comments.request: Define the index and clarify whether species diversity was also measured.
comments.quote: I do not see the Shannon Habitat diversity index explained or defined in the main text

comments.issue: The sturgeon focus only appears at the very end of the introduction.
comments.request: Make clear earlier that the food-web structure is examined through this sturgeon module.
comments.quote: The fact that this is a paper focused around Sturgeon does not materialize in the introduction until the very end

comments.issue: The claim that IS > 1 is theoretically impossible holds only at equilibrium.
comments.request: Acknowledge that such relationships can be transient.
comments.quote: I think this is only true under the assumption that the system is at an equilibrium. Such relationships can be transiently true.

comments.issue: The results may suggest a stabilizing role of spatial foraging that is not discussed.
comments.request: Consider discussing across-habitat foraging and consumptive pressure.
comments.quote: I wonder if the spatial results also potentially simultaneously suggest the stabilizing role of across spatial foraging

reviews.assessment: Novel and important study with clear, convincing results, but the underlying mechanism is not identified and several methodological details and the sturgeon focus need clarification.

comments.issue: The mechanism driving the habitat-diversity-interaction-strength relationship is not identified.
comments.request: Test whether prey diversity, abundance or composition drives the relationship.
comments.quote: it does not identify the underlying mechanism driving the relationship between habitat diversity and interaction strength

comments.issue: The introduction lacks justification for focusing on two sturgeon species, and the sink-web nature is made clear too late.
comments.request: Justify the sturgeon focus and clarify early that these are sink webs.
comments.quote: I found the introduction was lacking a justification for focusing on two species of sturgeon, which makes these sink food webs, not whole-ecosystem networks

comments.issue: The key methodological approach from Scholl et al. (2021) is not described enough to be understood.
comments.request: Include a brief summary of the Scholl et al. (2021) approach.
comments.quote: This seems like a key methodological point, but there is not enough information in the paper to understand it. I suggest including a brief summary of the approach detailed in Scholl et al. (2021).

comments.issue: Why woody debris was not quantified by sonar is unexplained, raising doubts about method accuracy for other habitats.
comments.request: Reassure readers about the accuracy of the method for other major habitat types.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 25 samples capture habitat diversity in a 38-km stretch, or how much habitat they cover.

comments.quote: Are 25 samples sufficient to capture the diversity of habitats in a 38-km river stretch?

comments.issue: A single set correction factor may not be appropriate for taxa with different ash content.

comments.quote: Is a set correction factor appropriate, e.g. wouldn’t hard-bodied snails have a much greater ash content than soft-bodied fly larvae?

comments.issue: Key methodological steps are summarised too briefly to be reassuring.

comments.quote: This paragraph summarises a lot of key methodological steps in a very short space and with few reassuring details.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the two sturgeon are the only fish species and how other fish were handled.

comments.issue: The same 3-km stretches are resampled many times, which may be problematic.

comments.quote: the river stretch is 38-km long, so you must be resampling the same 3-km stretches many times, right? Is that problematic?

comments.issue: The origin of the 1,000 bootstrapped estimates and their relation to the 100 random locations are unclear.

comments.quote: I’m unclear where the 1,000 bootstrapped estimates are coming from or why you would want to do this.

comments.issue: The X symbols in equations may be confused with independent parameters.

comments.quote: I assume the X’s in this equation are multiplication signs? I would replace them with full stops or asterisks to avoid confusion that they are independent parameters.

comments.issue: '<600m' at line 234 is unclear and the value may be mislabelled.
comments.request: Clarify '<600m' and check whether it should read '0.125 for adult sturgeon'.
comments.quote: I don’t understand what you mean by <600m here. Also, I assume it should be “0.125 for adult sturgeon”.

comments.issue: Equation 3 lacks introduction or context.
comments.request: Introduce Equation 3 and explain how it is used.
comments.quote: Equation 3 lacks any introduction or context for how it is used.

comments.issue: The 10,000 production estimates come from a single river and are non-independent, raising pseudoreplication concerns.
comments.request: Explain how the pseudoreplication is dealt with.
comments.quote: It’s also important to note that you have just one river, so these are 10,000 non-independent estimates of what is going on in that single river. How do you deal with that pseudoreplication?

comments.issue: The frequency of 'infrequent' cases is not quantified.
comments.request: Give the exact percentage of cases in brackets.
comments.quote: State how “infrequent” they were, i.e. give the exact percentage of cases in brackets.

comments.issue: The 3 km foraging distance is inconsistent with the reported mean of 7.6 km and median of 1.6 km.
comments.request: Justify the 3 km choice or use the median given the non-normal distribution.

comments.issue: The interaction-strength metric may simply be a proxy for invertebrate production.
comments.request: Add SI scatterplots of habitat diversity versus production and production versus interaction strength.
comments.quote: is there a concern that your metric of interaction strength is just a proxy for (or negatively correlated with) invertebrate production?

comments.issue: The tables in the diet paragraph are dry and hard to digest.

title: Landscape diversity promotes stable food‐web architectures in large rivers

title: Changes in vertical and horizontal diversities mediated by the size structure of introduced fish collectively shape food‐web stability

study.system: multispecies communities; structural stability metrics, Mediterranean grassland data

editor_summary: Editor: reviewers appreciate the theoretical advances but question novelty versus prior metrics, robustness and generality, and the link between metrics and abundance.

reviews.assessment: Timely and exciting theory with a well-written use case, but some metrics are not novel and the regression analysis does not support the predictive claim.
strengths: well-written with a field-parametrized use case
interesting use of shape measures as predictors

comments.issue: Exclusion distance was already introduced as full resistance and eta; only the average probability of exclusion is a clear novelty.

comments.issue: The current regression does not test within-species predictive relationships and ignores autocorrelation.

comments.issue: Asymmetry of interactions and asymmetry of the feasibility domain are used interchangeably though they are not equivalent.

comments.issue: Box 2 feels disjoint from the main body of the paper.

comments.quote: This box feels quite disjoint from the main body of the paper.

comments.issue: The closest-edge distance approximation may not fully characterize extinction likelihood.

comments.issue: The abstract is hard to understand without prior knowledge of structural stability.

comments.quote: It is not easy to understand for people without a good knowledge of structural stability.

comments.issue: Lines 23-25 should be combined into one sentence.

comments.issue: The organization level at L28 is unclear; the paper focuses on the community level.

comments.issue: Calling machine learning in general a black-box approach is inaccurate.

comments.quote: I would not call machine learning in general as black-box approach.

comments.issue: A relevant field test of structural stability is not cited.

comments.issue: 3 line-level copy edits.

comments.request: Simulate communities with many species and varying symmetry.
comments.quote: Not having a discussion and numerical results of how asymmetry in biotic interactions influence the persistence in many species community through the paper and supplementary materials is the major caveat I found about this study.

comments.issue: Stability is set aside though it is required for stable coexistence; asymmetric interactions can produce unstable fixed points.
comments.request: Discuss stability conditions more thoroughly.
comments.quote: the authors clarified that they would focus on feasibility while give up the discussion on stability, which seems unsatisfying

comments.issue: The interaction matrix is assumed independent of abiotic environment, contrary to empirical evidence.
comments.request: Discuss environment-dependent interactions.
comments.quote: the authors assumed that only intrinsic growth rates change under environmental fluctuations, while the interaction matrix is purely biotic and independent on abiotic environmental fluctuations

reviews.assessment: Interesting contributions and impressive dataset, but concerns about metric novelty, redundancy, and the rationale for short-term empirical predictions.
strengths: well written and precise mathematical calculations

comments.issue: Species exclusion distance was already defined by Medeiros et al. 2021; what is novel must be specified and compared.
comments.request: Clarify novelty and compare with Medeiros et al. 2021.
comments.quote: I believe that Medeiros et al (2021, Journal of Animal Ecology) used the exact same measure of distance to a border of the feasibility domain.

comments.issue: The probability of exclusion may simply reflect border length and add no new information.
comments.request: Show what information the probability adds over border length.
comments.quote: It seems that this probability may be computed simply by computing the length of the respective border.

comments.issue: The equilibrium-based framework's ability to predict short-term abundance changes, and the hypotheses in Fig. 3, are not justified.
comments.request: Better justify the link between metrics and short-term abundance.
comments.quote: If the structural framework is based on the equilibrium of LV systems, which can take many generations to be achieved, how can the authors metrics be used to predict short-term abundance changes?

comments.issue: The abstract sentence lacks specifics about the empirical results.
comments.request: Make it more specific.
comments.quote: I think this sentence needs to be more specific about the results of the empirical application.

comments.issue: Whether vulnerability relates to the perturbation regime or domain shape is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the role of perturbation direction.
comments.quote: Is this related to the perturbation regime or to the shape of the feasibility domain?

comments.issue: The equivalence of the LV model to more complex formulations is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the sense of equivalence.
comments.quote: In what sense is the LV model equivalent to other population models with more complex formulations?

comments.issue: How intrinsic growth rate contains biotic effects is unclear.
comments.request: Explain this.
comments.quote: How does intrinsic growth rate contains biotic effects?

comments.issue: 'Equivalent models' are not defined and it is unclear whether metrics apply to them.
comments.request: Define equivalent models.
comments.quote: Can these metrics be computed for “equivalent models”? It is also not clear what are these equivalent models.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 255-257 cannot be understood.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: I cannot understand this sentence, please consider rewriting.

comments.issue: How the interaction matrix was parameterized is not explained in the SI.
comments.request: Explain the interaction matrix estimation.
comments.quote: I could not find in the SI how the authors parameterize the interaction matrix. Since the whole approach depends on an accurate estimation of this matrix, I think this should be explained here.

comments.issue: Whether the models were forecasting out-of-sample or just fitting is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the forecasting procedure and report accuracy.
comments.quote: It was not clear to me whether the authors were forecasting or simply fitting the GLM models to the data.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not explain why species C is more susceptible when exclusion distances are equal, and domain size is not reported.
comments.request: Explain and report domain size in the caption.
comments.quote: It is not clear from the figure why species C is more susceptible to be excluded than species A. Why is this so, if their exclusion distances are the same?

comments.issue: Figure 2 caption lacks probabilities of exclusion and exclusion ratios.
comments.request: Report these values in the caption.
comments.quote: It would be helpful if probabilities of exclusion and exclusion ratios were reported for each case in the caption.

comments.issue: The log scale in Figure 4 makes predictions appear closer than they are.
comments.request: Use the natural scale.
comments.quote: Actually, it is the opposite, the log scale makes points appear closer than they actually are.

title: Structural asymmetry in biotic interactions as a tool to understand and predict ecological persistence

study.system: food webs; topological and bioenergetic network models

reviews.assessment: Interested but increasingly lost in the methods and results, wanting plain-language interpretation, empirical grounding and open code.
strengths: important qualitative results of interest beyond food-web specialists
appreciates the difficulty of simulating many constrained networks

comments.issue: The work is not repeatable without the source code for the feasible-network algorithm.
comments.request: Make the code open access in line with journal policies.
comments.quote: Given the complexity of the algorithm for identifying feasible networks I do not believe this work is repeatable without the source code.

comments.issue: The abstract implies comparison of model results with empirical observations, but none are presented.
comments.request: Add empirical comparisons or correct the abstract.
comments.quote: I took from the abstract that there would be comparison of model results to empirical observations, but I didn't see any.

comments.issue: Environmental change is implemented only as changes in feeding preferences without justification or examples.
comments.request: Justify this choice and consider attack rates, carrying capacity or producer growth rates.
comments.quote: However, a more typical place to implement environmental change in this type of model would be through predator attack rates, carrying capacity or primary producer growth rates. So I think some justification is needed here for this to link to environmental change.

comments.issue: Mathematical language from the L143 paragraph dominates the results, obscuring the main findings.
comments.request: Rewrite the terms in plain language any ecologist can understand.
comments.quote: The paragraph L143 was where I started to struggle with the math language. That language then comes to dominate in the results, so by the end I wasn't really sure what the main findings were.

comments.issue: The type of food web the model represents is never stated, nor how common 22-species webs are.
comments.request: Clarify the represented food-web types and how datasets map to natural webs.
comments.quote: Finally, its never stated what type of foodwebs this model aims to represent. How common are foodwebs with 22 species?

comments.issue: Work on optimally managing interaction networks is not mentioned in the introduction.
comments.request: Mention optimal resource allocation and management literature, e.g. McDonald-Madden et al. 2016.
comments.quote: So I think the first para of introduction would benefit from mentioning not just theoretical/empirical work on interaction networks, but also work that has looked at how you optimally manage such networks.

comments.issue: The statement on line 37 about species' effects on themselves is intangible.
comments.request: Give an example of such an interaction.
comments.quote: this is getting all a bit intangible at this point, can you give an example of such an interaction?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the food web is intended to be aquatic, given aquatic and terrestrial size structuring differ.
comments.request: State the intended food-web type.
comments.quote: so is this foodweb intended to represent an aquatic foodweb? Aquatic and terrestrial foodwebs have very different size structuring.

comments.issue: It is unknown whether the model and network-design algorithm reproduce realistic emergent size-based constraints.
comments.request: Verify emergent properties against observed size constraints, e.g. Trebilco et al. 2013.
comments.quote: As a verification step, I wondered if the model + algorithm for network design produce realistic emergent properties, e.g. commonly observed size based constraints

comments.issue: The ecological relevance of a random change in feeding preference is unclear.
comments.request: Explain whether this represents an evolutionary shift or an environmental impact.
comments.quote: What’s the ecological relevance of a random change in the feeding preference? Is it intended to represent how stability changes with an evolutionary shift, or an environmental impact on a species?

comments.issue: It is not described how subsets of species were determined.
comments.request: Explain the subset definition and whether subsets come from the 22-species network.
comments.quote: I don’t remember reading how ‘subsets’ of species were determined, are they subsets of the 22 in the (typical) network?

comments.issue: The paragraph at line 174 is long and complex.
comments.request: Break it into multiple paragraphs with topic sentences.
comments.quote: this is a long and complex paragraph, it would be easier to read if you can break it into multiple paragraphs with appropriate topic sentences

comments.issue: Line 188 is not tangible about which systems have these properties.
comments.request: Give concrete examples of such systems.
comments.quote: can you make this more tangible, what types of systems have these properties?

comments.issue: The statement at line 304 is speculative because it rests on a very abstract model.
comments.request: Provide a real example to support the statement.
comments.quote: it would be more compelling if you had a real example here, otherwise the statement seems somewhat speculative because it is based on the findings of this very abstract model

reviews.assessment: Positive about the modeling and writing but notes the linear functional response and the difficulty of ground-truthing theoretical findings.
strengths: clarity in presenting a large modeling effort
interesting classification of systems with different behaviour sets

comments.issue: The linear functional response assumption may not match natural systems, where nonlinear responses are often argued to be more realistic.
comments.request: Discuss the consequences of the linear functional response for the findings.
comments.quote: However, ecologists often argue that the non-linear functions better match observed natural system behavior.

comments.issue: The theoretical findings cannot easily be ground-truthed against real systems.
comments.request: Propose how the modelling results could be validated empirically.
comments.quote: It is not clear to me how we might “ground-truth” these theoretical findings.

title: Five fundamental ways in which complex food webs may spiral out of control

study.system: meta-food-web simulations; plant diversity-productivity across space

editor_summary: Editor says the three reviewers are broadly supportive and find the work of potential general importance, but asks the authors to revise, paying particularly close attention to Reviewer 2's points about unclear methodology.

reviews.assessment: Relevant and well-presented simulation with intuitive findings; suggests further explorations and empirical links.
strengths: very well presented with appropriate length and display material
findings intuitively sensible yet not a-priori obvious

comments.issue: Empirical results from the literature could support the simulations.
comments.request: Link the results to empirical studies.
comments.quote: it would have been nice if at least some empirical results from the literature could have been added to support the results

comments.issue: Pathogen-niche complementarity as an alternative mechanism is not considered.
comments.request: Consider pathogen-niche complementarity.
comments.quote: often we think in addition to resource-niche complementarity pathogen-niche complementarity (see e.g. Turnbull et al.) underpins BEF relationships

comments.issue: Herbivores and predators are not separated into generalists and specialists.
comments.request: Separate generalists and specialists.
comments.quote: It seems that herbivores and predators are not explicitly separated into generalists and specialists.

comments.issue: No intermediate plant-species richness level to reveal the shape of BEF relationships.
comments.request: Add an intermediate richness level.
comments.quote: Including an intermediate plant-species richness level would allow the authors to say something about the shape of the BEF relationships.

comments.issue: Diversity of higher trophic groups is not varied.
comments.request: Test higher-trophic diversity.
comments.quote: how does the diversity of higher trophic groups itself affect the BEF relationships?

comments.issue: The keyword 'selection' is dangerous without additive partitioning context.
comments.request: Reconsider the term.
comments.quote: I find the keyword "selection" dangerous, including its use in the text

comments.issue: Fig. 1A does not clearly show increasing spatial overlap.
comments.request: Improve the overlap illustration.
comments.quote: for me it was unclear how Fig. 1A should indicate increasing spatial overlap from left to right

reviews.assessment: Novel insights but the modelling description is hard to follow and replicate, movement is unclear, and hypotheses cannot be 'tested' by a model.
strengths: novel insights and interesting hypotheses for empirical testing

comments.issue: The history of trophic diversity-BEF research is not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge the earlier literature.
comments.quote: In the interest of scholarly rigor, this history should be acknowledged better on lines 58-60.

comments.issue: It is not clear how the analyses were executed.
comments.request: Elaborate the analysis description.
comments.quote: But the explanation of how the study got to this point needs more elaboration. As currently written, it is not completely clear how the analyses were executed.

comments.issue: The allometric size-class machinery is unnecessarily complicated.
comments.request: Simplify or justify the size-class approach.
comments.quote: What becomes confusing is why go through this, since it makes things unnecessarily complicated.

comments.issue: Replication of stochastic seeding is not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of replicates.
comments.quote: So how many replicates of a particular treatment combination are there?

comments.issue: Animal movement is not described; without it the study concerns spatial nestedness, not movement.
comments.request: Describe animal movement explicitly.
comments.quote: If there is no explicit movement (i.e., consumer-resource effects are merely determined by Supplementary Equations 1 -9 with accounting spread over the particular spatial domain of patches), then this MS is really only about spatial nestedness, not movement.

comments.issue: How the dynamical systems model and the 8x8 grid interact is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the model-grid interaction.
comments.quote: The section would be improved by providing more detail on how the dynamical systems model and the grid interact.

comments.issue: Plant and animal biomass share variable names and subscripts.
comments.request: Use distinct variable names.
comments.quote: specifying plant and animal biomass (Equations 6 and 7) using the same variable names and subscripts (dBik/dt) is highly confusing

comments.issue: The modelling cannot be replicated from the Methods and supplement.
comments.request: Improve reproducibility.
comments.quote: it would be difficult to replicate the modeling described in the study simply by reading the Methods and Supplemental Information

comments.issue: A model cannot 'test' hypotheses generated by its own assumptions; this circularity should be acknowledged.
comments.request: Present hypotheses as needing empirical testing.
comments.quote: A model cannot test hypotheses because it is not independent of the assumptions and internal premises of causation specified by the mathematics

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed the useful synthesis; methods logical but the supplement is hard to follow and several mechanistic questions remain.

comments.issue: Supplemental methods are hard to follow; Table S1 should summarize all parameters and functions.
comments.request: Summarize parameters in Table S1.
comments.quote: I did find the supplemental methods a little hard to follow simply due to the complexity of the model used and large number of functions

comments.issue: Results may be driven by interaction strengths and top-down control in non-nested scenarios.
comments.request: Test this driver.
comments.quote: Is it possible that much of the results are driven by increased interaction strengths and strong top-down control in non-nested (homogenized) scenarios?

comments.issue: Whether diversity-productivity relationships reflect selection for resource efficiency is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss complementarity-resource efficiency trade-offs.
comments.quote: I would like to know if diversity-productivity relationships in any cases are driven by selection for resource efficiency that then indirectly impact the community’s total uptake

comments.issue: Stability appears only in the discussion without prior mention.
comments.request: Connect the results to stability.
comments.quote: I felt this came out of nowhere since stability was not mentioned in the methods or results

comments.issue: How 'relatively stable plant diversity' is measured is unclear.
comments.request: Define the stability measure.
comments.quote: Line 347: how is “relatively stable plant diversity” measured?

comments.issue: No figure shows biomass dynamics or stability.
comments.request: Add biomass dynamics or stability.
comments.quote: None of the figures display biomass dynamics (or any other measure of stability), which would be useful information

comments.issue: A partially nested scenario has not been tested.
comments.request: Test a partially nested scenario.
comments.quote: I am curious if the authors considered an intermediate partially-nested scenario?

comments.issue: Explicit predictions across spatial scales are missing.
comments.request: Add scale predictions.
comments.quote: some explicit predictions, based on a summary of the results, for how variation in BEF relationships may occur across spatial scales

comments.issue: Question mark at the end of a non-question sentence.
comments.request: Fix the punctuation.
comments.quote: Line 71: Question mark at end of sentence doesn’t seem appropriate

comments.issue: Assignment of herbivore, omnivore and carnivore roles is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the trophic composition.
comments.quote: could you clarify if when assigning functional roles of animals, the animals deemed “herbivores” but not “strict herbivores” are considered omnivorous

comments.issue: The total productivity calculation and resource supply rates are not detailed.
comments.request: Explain the productivity calculation.
comments.quote: More details on how exactly total productivity is calculated would be appreciated

comments.issue: The type III functional response assumption is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the type III response.
comments.quote: could you explain why herbivorous interactions are assumed to follow a type III functional response?

comments.issue: 'B' is used for both plants and animals.
comments.request: Use distinct symbols.
comments.quote: Why use ‘B’ to represent both plants and animals?

title: Animal and plant space‐use drive plant diversity–productivity relationships

study.system: two-patch predator-prey metacommunity model; perturbation simulations

editor_summary: Extensive critical comments: test robustness to independent variation in omega and gamma, investigate negative prey correlation between patches, run more simulations, and address the editor's list (equations placement, two-patch generalisation, terminology).

reviews.assessment: Likes the results but asks to demonstrate that the resource-supply asymmetry omega does not drive stability.
strengths: I really liked the authors results

comments.issue: It is not demonstrated that resource-supply asymmetry (omega) is unimportant; coexistence requires omega=gamma.
comments.request: Add figures with omega on the x-axis, or qualify claims to include omega's role.
comments.quote: In order to better justify that the asymmetry of resource supply rate (omega) does not affect stability, I suggest the authors to make new figures, similar to Figs. S2-14 and S2-15, but with omega in the x axis.

reviews.assessment: No major concerns; finds the work novel, inspiring and well written, with only specific and minor suggestions.

comments.issue: Differences from Rooney et al. 2006 in stability concept and perturbation design are not explicit.
comments.request: Make the differences from Rooney et al. 2006 explicit in the introduction and methods.
comments.quote: The different focuses/approaches between your study and Rooney et al. 2006 can be made even more explicit in the introduction (in ecological languages) & methods

comments.issue: Divergent conclusions from Rooney et al. may stem from different approaches and are not discussed.
comments.request: Expand on why the conclusions differ in the discussion.
comments.quote: some of the divergent conclusions between your study and Rooney et al.’s may due to such different approaches. I expect to see at least of bit of expansion on this in the discussion.

comments.issue: The three-trophic-level scenario is barely mentioned in the main text.
comments.request: Integrate parts of the longer-chain scenario into the main text.
comments.quote: I feel that this additional scenario has additional indications that make your model discoveries more complete. Thus, I would suggest integrating some bits of it to the main text.

comments.issue: The claim that mechanisms act only on the dispersing species is untested for other trophic levels dispersing.
comments.request: Simulate scenarios with each trophic level as the disperser.
comments.quote: you could only firmly say so unless you have also tested the scenarios with 3 trophic levels and each trophic level in turn being the disperser (now you have only covered the predator dispersing case)

comments.issue: The super-fast disperser assumption (d2=10^6) is not explored; slower dispersal rates may change results.
comments.request: Discuss or simulate dispersal rates comparable to other rates.
comments.quote: I cannot help but wondering, what if the disperser’s dispersal rate is not at a totally different scale in comparison to other rates?

comments.issue: The mechanism is not connected firmly to the generic concept of spatial heterogeneity.
comments.request: Link the mechanism to habitat types and species composition.
comments.quote: I just feel it would be good if you could establish a firmer connection to the generic idea of spatial heterogeneity.

comments.issue: Fast and slow patch terminology is not used consistently after clarifying patch identities.
comments.request: Use 'fast patch' and 'slow patch' throughout.
comments.quote: you could then use the terms “fast patch” and “slow patch” throughout.

comments.issue: The sentence at L48-L52 is logically incoherent.
comments.request: Rephrase or explain L48-L52 in more detail.
comments.quote: I do not follow L48-L52 and I feel this sentence is logically incoherent; please rephrase or explain with more details.

comments.issue: The sentences at L143 and L149 divide one idea across two places in a paragraph.
comments.request: Combine the related sentences.
comments.quote: I feel these sentences is somewhat dividing one thing to two places in a paragraph.

comments.issue: The destabilising/stabilising legend in Figure 2 is confusing about scale and trophic level.
comments.request: Clarify the legend's scale and trophic-level meaning.
comments.quote: The “destabilising effect” and “stabilising effect” legend on Fig. 2 is somewhat confusing: stabilising at which scale and of which trophic level?

comments.issue: The sentence at L195-L198 is hard to follow.
comments.request: Clarify whether a synergistic effect is meant.
comments.quote: I do not fully follow this sentence. Do you refer to a synergistic effect that makes the response even slower?

comments.issue: Asymmetric interactions and perturbation sizes are not linked to real-world mechanisms for empirical readers.
comments.request: Link these conditions to real-world mechanisms in the introduction or discussion.
comments.quote: it would be good if you could, either in the introduction or discussion, link your “asymmetric interaction/feeding” and “moderate/small perturbation” to real-world mechanisms that can possibly bring about these conditions.

title: Spatial heterogeneity of biomass turnover has contrasting effects on synchrony and stability in trophic metacommunities

study.system: Amazon and Tonlé Sap freshwater fisheries; nutrient traits

editor_summary: Editor finds the study provides another example of prior findings without crediting them, overstates novelty, and leaves methods, data availability and interpretations unaddressed; cannot recommend publication here.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, creative application of multifunctionality theory, with major requests on conceptual clarity, data documentation and statistical reporting.
strengths: moves biodiversity science to the real world

comments.issue: It is unclear whether BEF manipulations match a managed fishery and whether all or only harvested fish are analysed; sampling is not representative.
comments.request: Clarify whether all or only harvested fish are considered.
comments.quote: It appears to me that there is a nested subset of species within the freshwater ecosystem that is harvested by humans. The sampling was not representative of the biodiversity of the ecosystem.

comments.issue: Because only species eaten by humans are used, results may not apply to studies modifying existing communities.
comments.request: Discuss how the harvested-species subset limits comparison.
comments.quote: Because the authors are already choosing a subset of species that are eaten by humans, the results of this study may not apply 1:1 to studies where an existing plant community is modified.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the ecosystem is the human consumer or the freshwater system, and what the ecosystem functions are.
comments.request: Clarify what the ecosystem and its functions are.
comments.quote: Is the ecosystem the human that consumes the fish whose nutrition is then maximized? Or is the ecosystem the freshwater system that should be managed to maintain high functional diversity?

comments.issue: Species are hardly described: no discussion of trait values or phylogenetic relationships.
comments.request: Describe species trait values and phylogenetic relationships.
comments.quote: there is almost no discussion on the relative trait values for the different types of species and their phylogenetic relationships

comments.issue: Data availability statement violates Ecology Letters policy; data, scripts and novel simulation code are not archived.
comments.request: Archive data and code in a public repository with DOI.
comments.quote: Data available upon request is not sufficient. Ecology letters requires that all scripts are made available in a public repository with a DOI.

comments.issue: Nutrient units are not provided.
comments.request: State the nutrient units.
comments.quote: Please state the units of the nutrients used in the present study. These are not provided

comments.issue: The nutrient analysis methods are insufficiently described, including what protein form was analysed.
comments.request: Describe the nutrient assay methods in detail.
comments.quote: Please describe the methods used here “A muscle fillet was dissected from each fish, and analyzed for nutrients at the Instituto Tecnológico Pesquero in Lima”. What form of protein was analyzed etc.

comments.issue: The rationale for measuring only six nutrients, and whether others were measured, is not stated.
comments.request: Justify the six selected nutrients.
comments.quote: Please state exactly which nutrients you set out to measure in Peru and why you only include the following: Ca, Fe, O3, Protein, VitA, Zn.

comments.issue: The species used are not provided.
comments.request: Provide species binomials and families in a supplemental table.
comments.quote: The species used in this study are not provided. Please provide the species Latin binomial and families in a supplemental table

comments.issue: The phylogeny used for trait imputation is not provided.
comments.request: Provide the phylogenetic tree used for imputation.
comments.quote: The phylogeny of these species used to impute the traits is not provided. Please provide the phylogenetic tree of the species used in the present study to impute the trait values.

comments.issue: The biplot scaling used in Figure 1 is not stated.
comments.request: State the Figure 1 biplot scaling.
comments.quote: State the scaling term used in the biplot in Figure 1

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Figure 3 and S4 lines are fitted values, and their uncertainty is not shown.
comments.request: Explain the fitted lines and add error bars.
comments.quote: Explain what you mean by “Lines represent linear mixed effect models for each threshold with the simulation as a random factor (see methods).” Are these fitted values? How wide is the standard error around your prediction?

comments.issue: Potential non-linearities in the Figure S3 relationships are not assessed.
comments.request: Test for non-linearities in Figure S3.
comments.quote: Are there non-linearities in the relationships presented in Figure S3?

comments.issue: 3 line-level copy edits (L33, L54, L291).
comments.quote: L33: There may be a missing “the” in this sentence. sustains “the” multiple contributions.

comments.issue: Increasing harvesting of the recommended species could cause overfishing.
comments.request: Consider overfishing risk in the recommendation.
comments.quote: Would increasing harvesting of any of the species you suggest should be included as part of a functionally diverse diet cause overfishing?

comments.issue: The abstract's claim about absence of nutritionally complete species contradicts the result that one species met all six RDAs.
comments.request: Resolve this inconsistency.
comments.quote: Is there an absence of nutritionally complete species or not?

comments.issue: 'Unique' species is unclear; Eltonian niche is presumably meant.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of uniqueness.
comments.quote: Are there any species that are not unique? I think you mean in terms of its eltonian niche.

comments.issue: The claim that few studies quantified the functional diversity-multifunctionality link is inaccurate and should be reframed.
comments.request: Cite Jochum et al. (2020) and soften the claim.
comments.quote: I am not sure if this is an accurate statement. Does this need to be your unknown here?

comments.issue: The second introduction paragraph has a mismatched topic sentence and tries to do too much.
comments.request: Split and rewrite the paragraph.
comments.quote: I recommend a revision of this paragraph. The topic sentence does not match the argument provided.

comments.issue: The 54 kg fish per year figure lacks comparative context.
comments.request: Provide a percentile or comparison statistic.
comments.quote: How does 54 Kg of fish per year compare to elsewhere? Is this a lot? Can you provide a percentile or some other statistic relative to other countries?

comments.issue: The 'key tenets' to be tested are not specified.
comments.request: State which tenets are tested.
comments.quote: Please explain what you mean by key tenets

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the fish biodiversity sample is random or biased.

comments.issue: Dataset S1 with trait values is not supplied.

comments.issue: Too little basic information is given about the trait data used.

comments.issue: Units for biomass and traits are not stated.

comments.issue: Non-linearities in nutrient-vulnerability trait correlations are not described.

comments.issue: Important nutrient-trait correlations are not described in the text.

comments.quote: It seems like you have space to describe a few correlations that you deem important to the reader.

comments.issue: The correlation plot text is too small to read.
comments.request: Increase the text size.
comments.quote: The correlation plot is a bit hard to read with the text being small.

comments.issue: The relationships referred to on line 251 are not identified.
comments.request: Specify which relationships.
comments.quote: Line 251: Which relationships?

comments.issue: More summary statistics on common versus rare nutrients are needed.
comments.request: Provide summary statistics for nutrients.

comments.issue: The species meeting all RDAs, its family and phylogenetic conservation are not discussed.

comments.issue: The results may be a foregone conclusion given the sampling design and traits; no null hypothesis is apparent.

comments.issue: Complementarity is not defined in this context.

comments.issue: Figure 4 lacks error bars to support the 'sharply' comparison.

comments.issue: 'Little effect' is not quantified.

comments.issue: Statements lack statistics that could be compared with other studies.
