comments.issue: Results may be highly biased by the sampling design and trait choice.
comments.request: Address potential sampling bias.
comments.quote: The results of your study may be highly biased based on your sampling design and the traits chosen.

comments.issue: Harvest recommendations may overfish rare or at-risk species; nutrient-rarity tradeoffs are not considered.
comments.request: Consider rare and at-risk species in the recommendation.
comments.quote: If you are recommending from a policy perspective that a greater diversity of fish should be harvested, could this cause rarer species to be overfished? Are there any species-at-risk in your system?

comments.issue: Yellow points in Figure 1 are hard to see on a white background.
comments.request: Add outlines or darken the background.
comments.quote: The yellow points are hard to see on a white background. Consider using a black color outline to define the circles or a darker background.

comments.issue: The Figure 2 caption claim contradicts the reported result of a species meeting all six RDAs.
comments.request: Fix the caption.
comments.quote: This seems like an odd statement to me to include in a figure caption. Also why do you say “if any” when you state in the results that there is a species that met all 6 RDAs?

comments.issue: Figure 3 gradient is described incorrectly and fitted values lack error bars.
comments.request: Fix the gradient description and add error bars.
comments.quote: I believe your color gradient goes from blue 1% to yellow 100% not red. Would be nice to see some error bars around these fitted values.

comments.issue: Figure S1 resolution is low.
comments.request: Increase the dpi.
comments.quote: The resolution here is low. Considering increasing the dpi.

comments.issue: Figure S2 lacks nutrient units.
comments.request: Include units per 100 g.
comments.quote: Include the units of nutrient per 100 g.

comments.issue: Figure S3 text is too small and non-linearities are not shown.
comments.request: Increase text size and show non-linearities.
comments.quote: Consider increasing the text size. Also it would be useful to show if there are non-linearities in these correlations.

comments.issue: Figure S4 legend is mislabelled and the fitted lines are unclear.
comments.request: Fix the legend and line description.
comments.quote: Legend is incorrectly labelled and reference to fitted lines is not clear.

comments.issue: Table S1 lacks MAE, cites Pagel incorrectly and uses unclear acronyms.
comments.request: Fix labels and define acronyms in Table S1.
comments.quote: MAE is missing. Should Pagel 1999 be cited in this paper? Capital P for pearson. Pr is the elemental symbol for Praseodymium.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and well-conducted study; asks for more discussion of simulation limitations, a calorie-based metric and fairer comparison with prior EMF studies.
strengths: addresses a question not studied before

comments.issue: Current fish consumption already reflects biodiversity change, so the baseline is status quo rather than pristine.
comments.request: Discuss this baseline caveat.
comments.quote: the current baseline represents the status quo, but not necessarily ‘pristine’ fish biodiversity

comments.issue: The non-random biodiversity loss scenario is extreme and ignores that species mostly become rarer and food-web changes favour other species.
comments.request: Discuss these scenario limitations.
comments.quote: it is quite extreme, and might deviate from actual future biodiversity loss. For example, often, species don’t go extinct, but mostly become rarer.

comments.issue: Nutrient provisioning should also be assessed per standard calorie intake rather than per gram of fish.
comments.request: Analyse RDAs met per standard calories.
comments.quote: I was wondering whether the authors could also analyse another metric, whereby it is assessed how many RDAs are met, when consumers eat a standard amount of calories, rather than grams of fish.

comments.issue: The claimed deviation from van der Plas et al. (2016) and Gamfeldt & Roger (2017) is unsupported because EMF metrics differ.
comments.request: Analyse an equivalent EMF metric before comparing.
comments.quote: I don’t think that the results of this study really deviate from those of van der Plas et al (2016) or Gamfeldt & Roger (2017).

comments.issue: The abstract is cryptic and 'functionally diverse fish portfolios' is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify the abstract and the term.
comments.quote: On a related issue: what are ‘functionally diverse fish portfolios’? Fish communities with a high functional diversity? Or harvest fish assemblages with a high functional diversity?

comments.issue: The 'paucity of research' claim ignores existing biodiversity-multifunctionality studies.
comments.request: Cite Lefcheck et al. and related studies.
comments.quote: I would argue that nowadays, quite a few studies have investigated relationships between biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality (see e.g. Lefcheck et al, 2015, Nat. Comm.)

comments.issue: Fishbase body size and trophic level data completeness is not reported.
comments.request: Report data coverage completeness.
comments.quote: since Fishbase does not always has 100% complete data coverage (although it might be different for this specific case study), it would be good to report how complete body size / trophic level data was

comments.issue: Comparability of nutrient methodology between Tonlé Sap and Amazon species is not addressed.
comments.request: Compare the nutrient methodologies.
comments.quote: it would be good to mention how comparable the methodology of nutrient content levels for the Tonlé Sap species was with the Amazonian species

comments.issue: A high fraction of vitamin A values were imputed, raising reliability concerns.
comments.request: Justify the imputation or drop vitamin A.
comments.quote: 45 out of how many? Line 147 suggests that the total number of species is 59, so it seems that a very high fraction of vitamin A values had to be imputed

comments.issue: The equation is a Community Weighted trait Mean but is not named or cited.
comments.request: Use the CWM term and cite Garnier et al. (2004).
comments.quote: this equation has been described before as the Community Weighted trait Mean (CWM) and is commonly used in trait based studies

comments.issue: The vulnerability calculation is circular: it requires knowing the least vulnerable species first.
comments.request: Rephrase to clarify the vulnerability method.
comments.quote: I am a bit confused here. To calculate species vulnerability, we first need to know which species is least vulnerable. There does seem to be a slight chicken-egg problem here

comments.issue: Studies showing positive diversity-stability relationships are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge these contrasting studies.
comments.quote: on the other hand, there are also various studies that show positive relationships between diversity and stability

reviews.assessment: Well-structured and valuable test of multifunctionality in fisheries; concerns about imputed nutrient data and missing slope statistics.
strengths: good test of multifunctionality in non-plant systems

comments.issue: Global imputation of nutrient values may bias results; the Peruvian Amazon data allow a direct test.
comments.request: Validate predicted against measured nutrient values.
comments.quote: If the authors can show that predicted values of different nutrients for fish species in Peruvian Amazon are strongly correlated with the measured values, it would provide a test of their method.

comments.issue: Most Tonlé Sap values are imputed while Amazon values are measured, which may distort site differences.
comments.request: Consider imputing both sites or correcting the comparison.
comments.quote: If the variability in imputed data is lower than measured data, one might over- or under-estimate the differences between the two sites.

comments.issue: The claim that random and non-random loss slopes are similar is not statistically tested.
comments.request: Include statistics comparing the slopes.
comments.quote: Could the authors include relevant stats to show that the slopes were not different?

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a summary of studies on biodiversity and human nutrition to set expectations and novelty.
comments.request: Add this literature summary.
comments.quote: I felt that the introduction would benefit from a summary of studies that have explored the role of biodiversity on human nutrition.

comments.issue: 'Fish are remarkably variable in nutrients' appears to contradict phylogenetic conservation of nutrient concentrations.
comments.request: Specify the context or say 'fish species'.
comments.quote: I felt that “fish are remarkably variable in nutrients” would contradict the statement “ Nutrient concentrations are phylogenetically conserved across fish taxa” in line 170 if the context were not clearly specified.

comments.issue: The contrast set by 'Yet' on line 85 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the contrast.
comments.quote: Unclear about the contrast being set by ‘Yet’

comments.issue: The choice of six nutrient concentrations is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the nutrient selection.
comments.quote: Could you add in a justification for why these 6 concentrations were chosen?

comments.issue: The use of a 5-year-old's intake rate rather than an adult's is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the age choice.
comments.quote: Is there a reason intake rate of a 5 year old is used and not that of an adult?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether household surveys were used only to generate the species list.
comments.request: Clarify the role of household data.
comments.quote: Just to be clear, the data from household surveys were used only to generate a species list for the region (and Fig 1)?

comments.issue: Including species from other continents may bias imputed values; narrowing the region could help.
comments.request: Consider narrowing the imputation region.
comments.quote: would it not be better to narrow the region to avoid biases that may arise from including species from other continents with potentially very different evolutionary and ecological histories?

comments.issue: The large difference in species numbers eaten between sites is not discussed in the results.
comments.request: Discuss species richness differences early in the results.
comments.quote: there seems to be a huge difference in the number of species eaten between the two sites. It might be important to talk about in the first part of the results section.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether lost species' mass is redistributed or total consumed mass declines.
comments.request: Explain this in the methods.
comments.quote: When species were lost, was it assumed that the weight would be made up equally by the remaining species or is there a loss in total consumed mass too? Please add this in the methods section.

comments.issue: Site differences may stem from different nutrient estimation methods.
comments.request: Assess the effect of estimation method.
comments.quote: Is there a possibility that this difference stems from the different methods of estimation of the nutrient contents?

comments.issue: Stronger Tonlé Sap relationships may reflect phylogenetic correlation of nutrients in the global imputation data.
comments.request: Test this explanation.
comments.quote: Similarly, were the relationships stronger for Tonle Sap because the nutrients are strongly correlated across the phylogeny in global data?

comments.issue: Figure 3 suggests steeper slopes for random than non-random loss, which is not noted.
comments.request: Note this pattern in the text.
comments.quote: Fig 3 also seems to suggest that the slopes are steeper for random loss rather than non-random species loss. It might be important to note that here.

comments.issue: The conclusion may assume equal fish sizes; size variation could affect portion-size results.
comments.request: Consider fish size variation.
comments.quote: Does this statement assume that all fish are of equal size? I am wondering how variation in fish size or weight (which might directly influence portion size) would affect this specific conclusion.

comments.issue: The jack-of-all-trades counterclaim may depend on gradient range and weak nutrient correlations.
comments.request: Reduce emphasis on countering the jack-of-all-trades effect.
comments.quote: given that elements are weakly positively correlated, maybe it is harder to find a negative trend for high thresholds? If true, then the emphasis on these results countering jack-of-all-trades effect should be reduced.

comments.issue: Positive relationships may arise because consumed species are already culturally filtered for high nutrients.
comments.request: Consider whether including all fish would change the pattern.
comments.quote: are only a subset of fish species consumed due to historical or cultural reasons? In which case, is there already a filter that is maximizing nutrients and that is why you see only a positive relationship.

comments.issue: The reason Amazon species have lower nutrient content is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the lower Amazon nutrient content.
comments.quote: Is there a reason for why the Amazon species would be even lower in their nutrient content?

comments.issue: The comparison to Mekong River fish specifically is unclear given the Amazon data source.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison.
comments.quote: unclear why the comparison is being made to Mekong River fish specifically? I thought that most of the data for Amazon comes from an earlier study in the region.

comments.issue: It is unclear why increased biomass should automatically decrease nutrient concentrations.
comments.quote: Is there reason to expect that increase in biomass would automatically decrease nutrient concentrations?

reviews.assessment: Well-written and timely, but contribution is incremental, the trait-function analysis is circular, and code/data reproducibility problems undermine confidence.
strengths: household consumption data a real strength

comments.issue: The contribution is incremental rather than transformative relative to Remans et al. 2011, Wood 2017 and Bernhardt & O'Connor 2021.
comments.request: Articulate the additional insight beyond prior studies.
comments.quote: I feel its contribution to ecological science is incremental, rather than transformative.

comments.issue: Household consumption data are not used to ground-truth biodiversity changes over time, missing the study's strongest opportunity.
comments.request: Use household data to inform biodiversity change.
comments.quote: it is a pity that the most exciting part of the study (the household consumption data) isn’t used to inform the changes in biodiversity over time

comments.issue: The analysis is not reproducible: data files are missing and the code contradicts the paper.
comments.request: Make data and code complete and consistent.
comments.quote: I was disappointed that the analysis was not reproducible (e.g. data files were missing), and in some cases the code clearly contradicted what was stated in the paper

comments.issue: The 'biodiversity effect' metric is never defined and equations for metrics are missing.
comments.request: Define the metric and include equations.
comments.quote: the paper refers to a “biodiversity effect” (i.e. y axis of Figure 4), but never defines how the biodiversity effect was calculated. It is important to include equations for all of the metrics displayed.

comments.issue: Traits and functions are both derived from nutrient concentrations, making the multifunctionality finding circular and inevitable.
comments.request: Reframe the analysis around ecological traits.
comments.quote: the analytical approach (as I understand it) is somewhat circular in the sense that the “traits” and “functions” are both derived from the same data (i.e. the nutrient concentrations)

comments.issue: 'Functional diversity' is actually nutritional diversity derived from nutrient data; it should be renamed nutritional functional diversity.
comments.request: Rename the metric to nutritional functional diversity.
comments.quote: what the paper refers to as “functional diversity” is actually derived from the nutrient data directly, and so is a measure of nutritional diversity, not of species’ traits relating to their ecological roles

comments.issue: The abstract and introduction promise an analysis of species traits and their nutritional benefits that the paper does not deliver.
comments.request: Align the framing with the actual analysis.
comments.quote: I found the abstract and the introduction a bit misleading in that it seems like the paper will address this relationship (i.e. the relationship between species traits and their nutritional benefits), but it really doesn’t deliver on this.

comments.issue: A complementarity-driven biodiversity effect requires negative nutrient correlations, but positive correlations are observed.
comments.request: Reconsider the complementarity interpretation.
comments.quote: in order to observe a biodiversity effect driven by complementarity among nutrients (consistent with biodiversity ecosystem functioning theory), the authors would need to observe a negative correlation between nutrients, but instead they observe positive correlations among nutrient concentrations

comments.issue: Phylogenetic imputation, especially for over half of Tonlé Sap species, is a large uncertainty source with low lambda and R2 values.
comments.request: Test robustness using only observed nutrient data.
comments.quote: This is potentially a large source of uncertainty in the analysis, and seems a major leap to make, given the major uncertainly inherent in phylogenetic imputation, and the fact that the lambdas and R2 in some cases were quite low (0.2).

comments.issue: The vulnerability-based approach to biodiversity loss is not justified over alternatives such as range shifts.
comments.request: Justify the vulnerability approach.
comments.quote: I do appreciate that the authors used a vulnerability based approach to biodiversity loss, but this should be better justified (i.e. why not also simulate biodiversity change due to species range shifts?)

comments.issue: The code is poorly documented and includes analyses not discussed in the text.
comments.request: Document the code and explain extra analyses.
comments.quote: the code was not very well documented and appeared to contain analyses that were not discussed in the text (i.e. compensation vs. No compensation — what is this?)

comments.issue: Small values (1e-8) are added where zeros should be, without justification in the methods.
comments.request: Justify this data manipulation in the text.
comments.quote: it appears the authors are adding very small numbers to the dataset, where there should be 0, this isn’t discussed in the methods, why? This is concerning, and I would like to see this justified in the text.

comments.issue: The text says dbFD was used but the code used fdisp instead.
comments.request: Correct the function named in the text.
comments.quote: I searched the code for the dbFD function, and couldn’t find it

comments.issue: The logic of the distance-based vulnerability index and how the least vulnerable species was determined are unclear.
comments.request: Explain the vulnerability index rationale.
comments.quote: I understand that the authors wish to take into account body size, trophic position and in one location, migration type, but why is a distance-based approach used?

comments.issue: Reference data, DOIs and data-synthesis details (search range, exclusions, averaging) are missing.
comments.request: Provide reference data and document the synthesis.
comments.quote: a little more information on how the synthesis were done (what time range was searched, were any studies excluded?

comments.issue: The Figure 4 caption claims estimates come from Figure 1, which is a PCA with no slope estimates.
comments.request: Fix the caption and include equations and confidence intervals.
comments.quote: but Figure 1 is a PCA — there are no slope estimates from there. This needs to be fixed, please include equations and confidence intervals.

comments.issue: The total number of Amazon species is not reported.
comments.request: State the Amazon species total.
comments.quote: Line 168 — how many species total in the Amazon?

comments.issue: Line 235 calls Pmin a biodiversity effect, but no biodiversity effect appears to have been estimated.
comments.request: Correct the metric label.
comments.quote: the biodiversity effect Pmin — as far as I can tell a biodiversity effect wasn’t estimated? Just the minimum portion size?

comments.issue: Figure S2 lacks nutrient concentration units.
comments.request: Add units to Figure S2.
comments.quote: Figure S2, what are the units of the nutrient concentrations? I imagine protein was in g, while the micronutrients were in mg?

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not show the actual simulation data and lacks error estimates.
comments.request: Plot the actual data and add error estimates.
comments.quote: Why not plot the actual data from the simulations?, provide error estimates for the slopes etc

comments.issue: 'Functionally unique/diverse' is ambiguous between ecological and nutritional traits.
comments.request: Specify which trait type is meant.
comments.quote: When talking about something being “functionally unique” or “functionally diverse” be clear about whether you’re referring to the functionally unique in terms of ecological traits or nutritional traits (i.e. nutrient concentrations).

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not state the species richness levels used to create the functional diversity levels.
comments.request: State the species richness levels.
comments.quote: Figure 3 — what levels of species richness were used to create those levels of functional diversity?

title: Species trait diversity sustains multiple dietary nutrients supplied by freshwater fisheries

study.system: biodiversity-productivity partitioning; annual plant and tree diversity experiments

editor_summary: Editor and all reviewers are extremely positive about the method and expect wide use; major revisions requested only for clarity, including restructuring Box 1 and figures, explaining yield calculations, and discussing limitations.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and valuable expansion of biodiversity partitioning, with useful suggestions to reorganize Box 1 and Figures 1-2 and to discuss limitations.
strengths: logical separation of productivity into density and size components

comments.issue: Box 1 and Figure 1 bury the useful descriptions of terms and mixture labels behind equations and generic titles.
comments.request: Move the descriptions to the top of Box 1 and use informative titles in Figure 1, reducing white space.
comments.quote: I would suggest: (1) pulling these descriptions to the top of the box, adding formatting to highlight their importance, and then reference relevant equation terms

comments.issue: The additive relationships among panels (C = D+E, F = G+H, B = C+F) are not clear from Figure 2's structure.
comments.request: Add a smaller version of Fig 1A with matching coloration to show the relationships.
comments.quote: the fact that C = D+E and F = G+H and B = C+F (or) B = D+E+G+H isn’t clear from the structure of panels

comments.issue: The manuscript focuses only on overyielding although density and size partitioning also applies to underyielding communities.
comments.request: Mention underyielding applications, particularly in future applications.
comments.quote: it is possible to partition density and size components in underyielding communities too, where these effects occur but are skewed towards less productive species?

comments.issue: The method will likely be extended to natural communities, but limitations and considerations are not discussed overtly.
comments.request: Discuss limitations and considerations for natural communities.
comments.quote: It may be prudent to discuss limitations and considerations more overtly.

reviews.assessment: Elegant and adoptable method demonstrated on modest case studies; suggests spelling out the phenomenological limitation and interpretation of negative values.
strengths: simple and easy to implement with an R package

comments.issue: Like the original additive partitioning, the approach is phenomenological and does not directly demonstrate mechanisms such as niche partitioning versus facilitation.
comments.request: Clearly state this limitation in the manuscript.
comments.quote: the additive partitioning approach is ultimately phenomenological. Mechanisms are inferred from patterns of the relative performance of species in monocultures and mixtures, but biological mechanisms are themselves not directly demonstrated

comments.issue: Negative values of the size- and density-mediated partitions are less intuitive than positive ones and their interpretation is not spelled out.
comments.request: Explain how to interpret both negative and positive partitions.
comments.quote: it could be helpful for the authors to spell out how to interpret both negative and positive size- and density- mediated complementarity and selection effects

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the approach is useful beyond experimental conditions.
comments.request: Elaborate briefly on applications beyond experiments.
comments.quote: do the authors envision these approaches being useful beyond experimental conditions? If so, could they briefly elaborate on this.

comments.issue: No example is cited for the relationship discussed at line 43.
comments.request: Cite an example that has examined this relationship.
comments.quote: Citing an example that has examined this relationship would be informative.

comments.issue: How expected yield is calculated is not explained (lines 72 and 447).
comments.request: Add an explanation of the expected yield calculation.
comments.quote: Could the authors add an explanation of how the expected yield is calculated?

comments.issue: How relative yields are calculated is not explained (lines 73-74).
comments.request: Add an explanation of the relative yield calculation.
comments.quote: Could the authors add an explanation of how relative yields are calculated?

comments.issue: The description at line 158 does not state that plants were harvested, dried and weighed.
comments.request: State that plants were harvested, dried and weighed.
comments.quote: Here it would likely be appropriate to state that plants were harvested, dried and weighed.

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: grammar at L142 and L147 and a wrong table reference in the supplement (S2 instead of S1).
comments.quote: Line 142. Replace “an multi-species” with “a multi-species”

comments.issue: In Figure 2 the density plot extends beyond the data points in some panels, e.g. panel H.
comments.request: Explain why the density plot extends beyond the data points.
comments.quote: Why does the density plot extend beyond the data points shown in the corresponding figure panel in some cases (e.g. panel H)?

comments.issue: A few pots in Figure 3 fall below the dotted lines with much lower size for a given density, and this pattern is unexplained.
comments.request: Elaborate on what explains the density-size relationship in these pots.
comments.quote: Only a handful of pots are below the dotted lines, with much lower plant size for a given plant density. Could the authors elaborate on what might explain the relationship between density and size in these pots?

comments.issue: Some points in Figure 4 extend beyond the axes limits.
comments.request: Resize the axes accordingly.
comments.quote: Some points extend beyond the limits of the axes; it might make sense to resize axes accordingly.

title: Partitioning the biodiversity effects on productivity into density and size components

study.system: coexistence theory; invasion graphs and community assembly models

editor_summary: Two of three reviewers saw an important and useful paper; all three renowned experts have substantial concerns; Reviewer 1 doubts the premise, and these concerns must be carefully considered and rebutted.

reviews.assessment: Doubts the general validity of invasion graphs; counterexamples and extra assumptions mean the approach is overstated, so recommends rejection.
strengths: the idea of invasion graphs is appreciated

comments.issue: Coexistence can occur without an invasion pathway, as shown by a three-species community where no pair coexists, so the criterion is not general.
comments.request: Address this counterexample to the invasion graph criterion.
comments.quote: it is a counterexample of the invasion graphs criterion. Coexistence can occur without necessarily having a pathway in the invasion graph.

comments.issue: A positive invasion growth rate does not guarantee coexistence, as an invader can collapse a community (Case 1995), so extra assumptions are needed.
comments.request: State the additional assumptions required for the invasion graph criterion.
comments.quote: Thus, the invasion graph criterion certainly needs additional assumptions to work, as is assumed that a positive invasion growth rate implies coexistence.

comments.issue: Applying pairwise MCT metrics to species-rich systems may produce square roots of negative numbers and imaginary niche or fitness differences.
comments.request: Show what happens when interactions have negative signs.
comments.quote: What happens, on line 683, if one of the interactions as the negative sign ? Mathematically speaking will it result in the square roots of a negative number and thus an imaginary niche and/or fitness difference ?

comments.issue: The paragraph on lines 90-98 wrongly presents MCT metrics and the structural approach as the same species-rich framework.
comments.request: Correct the conflation of pairwise MCT metrics and species-rich coexistence theory.
comments.quote: This paragraph completely entangled these two approaches like they are the same, which is wrong.

comments.issue: The text implies a positive invasion growth rate for species with an Allee effect, which is impossible by definition.
comments.request: Correct the statement about Allee effects and invasion growth rates.
comments.quote: Lines 178-181 seems to say that the invasion growth rate of a species exhibiting an Allee effect is positive. How that can be the case ?

reviews.assessment: Novel, technically sound approach; questions whether it really solves MCT's issues or addresses a distinct question.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the uninvasibility result is definitive or contingent on the reference species pool, which questions the 'other side of the coin' framing.
comments.request: Clarify how pool-specific the results are and add context.
comments.quote: I am wondering if I learn something definitive about this k species community, or if it is highly contingent on the reference pool of species I started with

comments.issue: Whether the approach still solves the same problem as MCT, rather than fixing it by fiat, is not clear.
comments.request: Clarify whether the approach can predict coexistence from invasion growth rates alone.
comments.quote: I couldn’t quite figure out if this is still solving the same problem that MCT papers attempt to.

comments.issue: Several typos (L80, L147, L190) and a hard-to-parse sentence at L231-233.
comments.request: Fix the typos and rephrase the L231-233 sentence.
comments.quote: I also found the sentence L231-233 a bit hard to parse---maybe it could be rephrased.

comments.issue: Figure 1 is confusing because only the first invasion graph has associated growth rates.
comments.request: Add a growth-rate table next to each invasion graph.
comments.quote: So I wasn’t sure initially if all three were supposed to be the same system somehow.

comments.issue: The four advertised parts of the paper do not align with the subsection headings.
comments.request: Align the subsection headings with the four advertised parts.
comments.quote: The authors introduction advertises four main parts to the papers, but these did not align with subsection headings in a totally obvious way.

reviews.assessment: Tremendously important, rigorous update to coexistence theory; asks for improved accessibility and a more accurate account of prior literature.
strengths: beneficial to both theoreticians and empirical users

comments.issue: The manuscript is not accessible enough: it needs fuller explanations, less technical language and clearer advice to users.
comments.request: Revise for accessibility and clarify the advice to users.
comments.quote: More effort could put into making it more accessible through fuller explanations, elimination of unnecessary technical language, and further thought as to what the advice to users really should be.

comments.issue: The data-based examples are treated too briefly.
comments.request: Expand the treatment of the data-based examples.
comments.quote: They might also think about the rather brief treatment of data-based examples.

comments.issue: The diversity of approaches within MCT (Chesson versus Ellner) is not recognized.
comments.request: Acknowledge the different MCT approaches without making the paper unwieldy.
comments.quote: Recognition at least of the diversity of approaches would be helpful without making the paper unwieldy.

comments.issue: Awkward phrasing and clashing tenses remain in the text.
comments.request: Edit for awkward phrasing and clashing tenses.
comments.quote: the authors could pay more attention to editing to eliminate awkward phrasing and clashing tenses

comments.issue: Cycles in the invasion graph (rock-paper-scissors) can be compatible with a globally stable equilibrium even when single invasions cannot assemble the community.
comments.request: Clarify the issue of cycles in the invasion graph.
comments.quote: An issue to clarify later on is that cycles can occur in the invasion graph, as in rock-paper-scissors, compatible with there being a globally stable equilibrium embracing all of the species in the cycle

comments.issue: Stabilizing and equalizing mechanisms are described as disentangling mechanisms, although most mechanisms are neither purely equalizing nor stabilizing.
comments.request: Say 'disentangling stabilizing and equalizing components of mechanisms'.
comments.quote: This would be better as “disentangling stabilizing and equalizing components of mechanisms,” because Chesson 2000 in fact emphasizes that most mechanisms are neither purely equalizing nor purely stabilizing.

comments.issue: The conditions for invasion growth rates should mention long-term stable fluctuations, not only equilibrium.
comments.request: Say 'at equilibrium or with long-term stable fluctuations'.
comments.quote: It is better to say “at equilibrium or with long-term stable fluctuations”

comments.issue: The serious foundation of the decomposition is Chesson 1994, updated in Chesson 2020, which is not cited here.
comments.request: Cite Chesson 1994 and Chesson 2020 as the foundation.
comments.quote: The serious foundation for this is actually Chesson 1994, updated more concisely in Chesson 2020.

comments.issue: The phrasing about positive invasion growth rates should ask in what sense they ensure coexistence.
comments.request: Rephrase as 'in what sense does their being positive ensure coexistence?'.
comments.quote: Better as “in what sense does their being positive ensure coexistence?”

comments.issue: Calling two-species competitive communities the bedrock of MCT takes a narrow view of the theory.
comments.request: Acknowledge that Chesson 1994 focused on multispecies communities.
comments.quote: Saying that “two species competitive communities” are “the bedrock of MCT,” takes a narrow view on what it is.

comments.issue: The references on lines 90-98 are wrong: Chesson 2018, 2020a and 2020b are needed, and the Barabas et al. 2018 reply must be cited.
comments.request: Correct and extend the citations so earlier literature is accurately represented.
comments.quote: There is a problem here in these references. First of all Chesson 2018 draws attention to the issue as an update to the foundational paper, Chesson 2000

comments.issue: Six line-level edits (L110-1 rewrite; L117 wording; L202-205 typo 'T'; tense error at line 374-375; Box 2 item 4 missing '> 0'; number assumptions as introduced).
comments.quote: Typo here: it should be “transitioning to subcommunity T.”

comments.issue: Stochastic persistence theory is attributed to Schreiber 2000 although it began with Chesson 1978-1989, and Hening et al. 2021 is not cited.
comments.request: Cite the earlier stochastic persistence literature and Hening et al. 2021.
comments.quote: Mathematical theory for the stochastic cases starts much earlier than Schreiber 2000. The stochastic boundedness concept, which is now called “stochastic persistence” was first discussed in Chesson 1978

comments.issue: The claim that MCT rests on positive invasion growth rates implying coexistence is the naive take; Chesson 2018 gives a more nuanced view.
comments.request: Present the more nuanced view from Chesson 2018.
comments.quote: This is the naive take on it. A more nuanced view was given in Chesson 2018

comments.issue: The rock-paper-scissors discussion omits the three-species equilibrium and its directed edges.
comments.request: Elaborate the rock-paper-scissors discussion for clarity.
comments.quote: I recommend elaborating your discussion of rock-paper-scissors to make these additional points for greater clarity.

comments.issue: The invasion graphs on pages 10-12 are not as well labeled as in Hofbauer and Schreiber 2022, and scenarios lack their own graphs.
comments.request: Give each scenario its own well-labeled invasion graph.
comments.quote: Each of the particular scenarios you discuss would be better illustrated with its own well-labeled invasion graph that makes all the distinctions that mention in the text.

comments.issue: The examples analyse only some species of the final community (e.g. species 4 and 6 are not analysed).
comments.request: Analyse more assembly pathways and community transitions.
comments.quote: How about choosing some pathways to community assembly, specific community transitions that standout, even if you do not do them all.

comments.issue: The text attributes recommendations to Chesson 1994, which did not make them but took the mutual invasibility condition for granted.
comments.request: Correct the characterization of Chesson 1994.
comments.quote: Actually, the Chesson 1994 paper did not make recommendations.

comments.issue: MCT concepts were developed for guilds, so comparing predators and prey lies outside the theory's domain.
comments.request: Restrict the discussion to guild communities.
comments.quote: They were developed for the community as a guild. For instance, comparing average fitness of a predator and its prey is outside of the domain developed for the theory.

comments.issue: The paper does not end with a summary of how the approach improves understanding.
comments.request: Sum up how the new approach improves understanding.
comments.quote: At this point, you should sum up. Simply state how this new approach has greatly improved understanding.

comments.issue: The claim that the approach explains a result is not backed by an actual explanation.
comments.request: Provide the explanation rather than describing what was done.
comments.quote: You say your approach explains it, but you do not in fact give an explanation.

comments.issue: The opening statement about MCT not applying to why species do not coexist lacks context and casts undue doubt on prior analyses.
comments.request: Rewrite to state that the analysis extends beyond two-species and diffuse cases.
comments.quote: The quotation above is just the kind of statement that gets picked up and requoted restricting conclusions and casting unnecessary doubt on perfectly good analyses.

comments.issue: Failure to predict coexistence may reflect the missing spatial dimension, which needs further development.
comments.request: Consider extending the framework to the spatial domain.
comments.quote: There is actually a strong likelihood that failure of models to predict coexistence of species that are in fact found to cooccur in nature is due to failure to consider the spatial dimension

comments.issue: Negative storage effects were demonstrated before Schreiber 2021, 2022, e.g. by Chesson 1982.
comments.request: Cite the earlier demonstrations of negative storage effects.
comments.quote: Negative storage effects were demonstrated in models long-before Schreiber 2021, 2022.

comments.issue: The regional species pool versus local community is a crude construct that needs more realistic spatial consideration.
comments.request: Consider more realistic spatial structure.
comments.quote: this regional species pool versus local community is a construct of the human mind, and is but a crude approximation to nature

comments.issue: Computational difficulty depends on model complexity, not only species number, and may not persist.
comments.request: Frame computational limits in terms of model complexity.
comments.quote: How difficult this is also going to be depends a great deal on the complexity of the model, not just the number of species.

comments.issue: The discussion on lines 451-463 is too obscure and lacks context about appendix B.
comments.request: Explain what appendix B does to give context.
comments.quote: This discussion here is a little too obscure to be of much help. You need to indicate a little better what appendix B does to give it context.

comments.issue: Realistic stochastic temporal variation makes the whole state space accessible, so the problem concerns models with too little realism.
comments.request: Recast the stochastic problem around the stationary distribution and quasi-stationarity.
comments.quote: When you realistically include stochastic temporal environmental variation in your model, every part of a state space with all species present is accessible from every other part.

comments.issue: Box 1 leaves a gap around 'indecomposible (i.e. ergodic)' without explaining when the methods apply.
comments.request: Explain when these methods apply.
comments.quote: you should be giving the reader a better understanding of when these methods apply, or least some circumstances when they should, or where the problem is discussed in a helpful way

comments.issue: Box 2 uses >= and <= for directed edges whereas the text and Hofbauer and Schreiber 2022 use > and <.
comments.request: Make the edge conditions consistent with the text.
comments.quote: The conditions in the box for a directed edge have ≥ and ≤ whereas in the text and in Hofbauer and Schreiber 2022 they are > and <.

comments.issue: Terms like 'codimension' and the notation |S| are too technical for Ecology Letters.
comments.request: Replace technical terms with plain English.
comments.quote: The word “codimension” and the notation |S| are fine for a math journal, but I would not use them in Ecology letters, even I defined them there.

comments.issue: Growth rate decompositions are restricted to the endpoint community, so some species are never assessed and assembly is not fully analysed.
comments.request: Extend the analysis to the full assembly process and summarise it.
comments.quote: If you really want to put community assembly in “MCT” why not employ it for a full understanding of the assembly process?

comments.issue: Appendix A is hard to read because of unnecessary technical terms and long paragraphs.
comments.request: Drop technical terms and restructure the paragraphs.
comments.quote: You can make this appendix more accessible by dropping unnecessary technical terms.

comments.issue: The claim about neutral species and coexistence theory is incorrect: they simply do not form stable communities.
comments.request: Correct the statement about neutral species.
comments.quote: Neutral species not excluded from quantitative coexistence theory. They simply do not form stable communities

comments.issue: The term 'generalized Lotka-Volterra model' is used differently from the general Lotka-Volterra model defined on line 556.
comments.request: Clarify the Lotka-Volterra terminology.
comments.quote: But you also use the term “generalized Lotka-Volterra model,” which is often just a differential equation model with an analytic per capita growth rate, bounded in bounded regions.

comments.issue: Appendix C does not explain how to obtain niche and fitness differences.
comments.request: Flesh out appendix C with practical guidance.
comments.quote: All this is very interesting, but it does not tell anyone how to get the niche and fitness differences.

title: Building modern coexistence theory from the ground up: The role of community assembly

study.system: montane lizard; 18 mountain ranges resurveyed, genomic data

editor_summary: High-quality, valuable contribution likely acceptable after minor revision; editor asks authors to address reviewer #1's suggestions and points of clarification.

reviews.assessment: Clear and compelling study making an important contribution; only minor comments and suggestions, mostly on reporting and framing.
strengths: relevance of genetic data to population vulnerability

comments.issue: Correlation structure among the five climate variables is not reported, complicating interpretation of the GLM results.
comments.request: Report the correlations among climate variables, in the appendix.
comments.quote: What is the correlation structure among the five climate variables (this might be relevant when interpreting the glm results, e.g. L 233, 242)?

comments.issue: Missing reference to Kardos et al. 2021 in the discussion of conservation genetics.
comments.request: Cite Kardos et al. 2021 PNAS where relevant.
comments.quote: it would be worth citing Kardos et al. 2021 PNAS (“The crucial role of genome-wide genetic variation in conservation”) somewhere in here

comments.issue: Discussion does not note that loss of populations erodes genetic diversity and population sizes even without imminent species extinction.
comments.request: Add a brief comment on these within-species losses.
comments.quote: some brief comment on the importance of loss of populations within species and erosion of both genetic diversity and effective/census population sizes that accompany these losses would be meaningful here

comments.issue: Figure 2 x-axis labels and caption use inconsistent wording.
comments.request: Label axis “Historical”/“Recent” and replace “historic” with “historical”.
comments.quote: Label x axis “Historical” and “Recent”; also change “historic” (used twice in the caption) to “historical”.

comments.issue: A useful statement in the appendix should also appear in the main text.
comments.request: Move the statement into the main text.
comments.quote: Might be worth adding this statement into the main text as this was one of my main questions when reading the manuscript.

comments.issue: Number of loci in the LFMM genind object (1,609) conflicts with the 3,218 SNPs in Figure S5.
comments.request: Clarify the loci versus SNP counts.
comments.quote: Says the genind object for LFMM analysis had 1,609 loci, but Figure S5 says 3,218 SNPs – can the authors clarify?

reviews.assessment: Novel, well-written and methodologically robust study of climate-driven extinctions, with requests for clarification and stronger genomic analyses.
strengths: contributes to understanding climate change impacts

comments.issue: Non-observation may reflect behavioural change rather than population extinction.
comments.request: Address whether behavioural changes could explain the missing populations.
comments.quote: Is it possible that the reason why the species has not been observed is behavioural changes linked to climate change, i.e. the lizards stopped basking on large rocks during daylight hours, rather than the populations going extinct?

comments.issue: Climate and land-use change effects are not disentangled.
comments.request: Explain how habitat changes between survey periods were quantified.
comments.quote: How did you tease apart the effect of climate change and land use change? Expand on how changes in habitat between survey periods were quantified.

comments.issue: Variable time between surveys (4-9 years) may bias extinction probability estimates, with no correction explained.
comments.request: Explain how the differing survey intervals were corrected.
comments.quote: Explain how you corrected for differences in time between surveys (4-9 years) when analysing population extinction probability.

comments.issue: Selecting top SNPs from a single GEA method without cross-validation inflates false positives.
comments.request: Use two GEA methods and intersect their candidate loci.
comments.quote: This is a more robust approach than using a single method and then arbitrarily deciding only to include in the analysis the top 3 SNPs associated with each environmental variable.

comments.issue: LFMM alone is less robust for identifying adaptive loci than RDA.
comments.request: Use RDA, or a combination of RDA and LFMM.
comments.quote: Authors should either use RDA or a combination of RDA and LFMM.

comments.issue: ~1600 SNPs may be too few to identify patterns of adaptive variation.
comments.request: Discuss whether the reduced representation dataset is sufficient.
comments.quote: The authors should discuss whether this small reduce representation dataset is sufficient to identify patterns of adaptive variation

title: Accelerating local extinction associated with very recent climate change

study.system: aquatic food webs; food chain length meta-analysis and competition-colonisation model

editor_summary: Editor agrees the novelty is not entirely clear, especially differentiation from Takimoto & Post (2013); asks to improve integration of modelling and empirical analyses and give a clear take-home message.

reviews.assessment: Interesting question and a satisfying empirical match, but the meta-analysis adds little and the mechanism's realism is doubtful.
strengths: nice match between model and empirical data

comments.issue: Meta-analysis largely repeats Takimoto et al. (2013) without new conclusions.
comments.request: Clarify the added value of the meta-analysis.
comments.quote: The meta-analysis felt very similar to what has already been done. It only includes 14 papers so does not represent a substantially larger exploration than previous work

comments.issue: Realism and ubiquity of the basal-resource mechanism are not convincing.
comments.request: Develop evidence for the mechanism and compare with prior work.
comments.quote: I find it hard to imagine a gradient where one would see these strong oscillating responses in basal resources.

comments.issue: Discussion is brief and does not link to prior mechanistic work or real-world systems.
comments.request: Expand the Discussion and compare with prior models.
comments.quote: It also did not go into as much depth as I would have liked in linking this work to previous modeling/mechanistic work on food chain length

comments.issue: Term 'site-occupancy dynamic framework' may need definition.
comments.request: Define or rephrase the term.
comments.quote: Is “site-occupancy dynamic framework” general enough to be clear to a wide audience without further definition?

comments.issue: 'Benign' is ambiguous at line 49.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: Line 49: Does “benign” = “low disturbance”?

comments.issue: DDR acronym appears only once.
comments.request: Remove the acronym.
comments.quote: I don’t remember seeing “DDR” used again so not clear this needs to be an acronym.

comments.issue: Alternative hypotheses are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss alternative hypotheses.
comments.quote: I was left wondering what alternative hypotheses were.

comments.issue: How common displacement competition is across aquatic systems is unclear.
comments.request: Discuss its prevalence across systems.
comments.quote: I was questioning how common this was and whether it was more common in some aquatic systems relative to others.

comments.issue: The large/small classification method is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the split was made.
comments.quote: How was the split of large/small etc. made? Was the aim to create equal bins across all studies or was there some definitive large or small?

comments.issue: Disturbance incorporation is confusing and its scope undefined.
comments.request: Clarify disturbance implementation and types represented.
comments.quote: I found some of the explanation of how disturbance was incorporated confusing. I had to reach lines 252-254 several times and was still not quite sure I followed.

comments.issue: 'System analysis' at line 288 lacks a brief definition.
comments.request: Add a brief definition.
comments.quote: I think a brief definition of what “system analysis” is would be helpful

comments.issue: The niche model referenced at line 302 is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the niche model.
comments.quote: Line 302: What niche model is this referring to?

comments.issue: Methods text is repeated in the Results at lines 327-331.
comments.request: Remove methods from the Results.
comments.quote: These are methods so in my opinion they do not need to be repeated in the results.

comments.issue: Figures are referenced in a block and Fig. 2's range component is unmentioned.
comments.request: Reference figures throughout the results.
comments.quote: I would have preferred the figures to be referenced throughout this section instead in a block at line 360.

comments.issue: 'Turning points' are not discussed and lack empirical evidence.
comments.request: Discuss turning points and empirical support.
comments.quote: I was intrigued by this idea of “turning points” and would have liked to see some discussion of this.

comments.issue: Realism of oscillating basal-resource dynamics is questioned.
comments.request: Discuss the realism of these oscillations.
comments.quote: Line 390 – 393: How realistic are these oscillating dynamics in basal resources?

comments.issue: Realism of the scenario at lines 489-491 is questioned.
comments.request: Justify the scenario's realism.
comments.quote: Line 489 – 491: How realistic is this?

comments.issue: Whether predators can switch in response is not addressed.
comments.request: Address predator switching.
comments.quote: Line 504 – 505: Can predators switch in response?

comments.issue: Bottom-up focus may not reflect the strong top-down control in many systems.
comments.request: Discuss top-down control.
comments.quote: This focus on bottom-up control is interesting as many aquatic systems are thought to have quite strong top-down control.

comments.issue: Applied recommendations are largely already known.
comments.request: Sharpen the recommendations.
comments.quote: I agree with these applied recommendations but I think in most cases these are already things we are aware of.

comments.issue: 'Case identity' in Fig. 1 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the label.
comments.quote: I wasn’t sure what “case identity” meant on first reading.

comments.issue: Small and large range in Fig. 2 are undefined.
comments.request: Define them in the figure.
comments.quote: Could one specify in the figure what small and large range are referring to?

comments.issue: Realism of oscillating responses remains unaddressed.
comments.request: Provide empirical examples.
comments.quote: These oscillating responses are really interesting. I just keep wondering how realistic they are.

reviews.assessment: Enjoyable and promising contribution with nicely put-together figures, but the methods lack important details.
strengths: nice approach coupling meta-analysis and model
niche model used for initial conditions

comments.issue: Meta-analysis search methods and eligibility criteria are missing.
comments.request: Describe the search, dates, terms and criteria.
comments.quote: The paper lacks details on the methods used to conduct your meta-analysis. How did you find and identify the 14 papers included in this dataset?

comments.issue: The S parameter conflates continuous site availability with discrete habitat sites, and P_i is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify S and define P_i clearly.
comments.quote: I think it is the continuous value parameter S\in[0,1] blurred with the notion of a discrete number of habitat sites each allowing a single (discrete) individual to occupy it that is confusing me.

comments.issue: Table 1 lacks units.
comments.request: Add units to Table 1.
comments.quote: Please include units in Table 1.

comments.issue: Transient duration and its parameter dependence are not reported.
comments.request: Report simulation durations and transient behaviour.
comments.quote: How long did you run the model to ensure transient dynamics were finished? I also wonder if the time scales for the transient dynamics varied much with different parameter values.

comments.issue: How equilibrium was determined under periodic disturbance is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the equilibrium calculation.
comments.quote: For the periodic disturbance how did you then determine “equilibrium” values numerically?

title: Towards a mechanistic understanding of variation in aquatic food chain length

study.system: terrestrial mammals; global richness and environmental drivers

editor_summary: Two referees agree the paper is potentially suitable pending revision; editor asks for finer diet subdivisions, more cautious wording, accounting for spatial autocorrelation, and greatly reducing the climate-change links.

reviews.assessment: Clear, well-written and hypothesis-driven paper of broad interest, with two minor concerns about range-map resolution and trophic categories.
strengths: broad interest to Ecology Letters readers

comments.issue: Range maps are used at 30 km resolution although previous literature argues they are unreliable below 200 km.
comments.request: Justify the resolution or change it, citing Hurlbert & Jetz and Hawkins et al.
comments.quote: Previous literature has argued that range maps can not be used reliably at resolutions higher than 200km

comments.issue: The three broad trophic categories are not justified; finer diet classifications are readily available.
comments.request: Add a methodological argument for not breaking the trophic categories down further.
comments.quote: I believe they should discuss in the methods why they do not further break down some of these trophic categories

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: spell out GPP at first use, spell it out again at line 79, and fix the misspelling of Herbivore in Figure 2.
comments.quote: Line 41: The first instances of abbreviations should always be spelled out (GPP)

comments.issue: The abstract does not mention the hypotheses that were tested.
comments.request: Add the tested hypotheses to the abstract if space allows.
comments.quote: I noticed that you didn’t mention the hypotheses that you tested in the abstract

comments.issue: The temperature threshold and its importance are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the temperature threshold, referencing Boag et al. 2021.
comments.quote: It might be interesting to discuss the importance (if there is any) of this temperature threshold

reviews.assessment: Well-written and interesting, but wording is too causal for correlative models, and human influence and spatial autocorrelation are unaccounted for.

comments.issue: Wording is more definitive and causal than the correlative models allow; other drivers such as human influence, trophic interactions and other taxa are unaccounted for.
comments.request: Temper causal wording and acknowledge unaccounted drivers, possibly with SEMs.
comments.quote: the text is generally worded in a more definitive and causal sense than I would expect given the nature of the models

comments.issue: Focusing on environmental hypotheses implicitly ignores human influence on global biodiversity patterns.
comments.request: Acknowledge human influence or repeat analyses with natural ranges or human drivers.
comments.quote: Hence the focus in the manuscript on environmental hypotheses for these patterns implicitly ignores the influence of humans.

comments.issue: The coarse trophic groupings, especially the predator group, may drive results.
comments.request: Test the sensitivity of results to finer trophic groupings.
comments.quote: I think that the sensitivity of the results to the trophic groupings could be investigated

comments.issue: The title is unilluminating and does not convey key take-home messages.
comments.request: Revise the title to convey key messages.
comments.quote: ‘Global patterns in mammal trophic diversity are structured by environmental drivers’ – I find the title unilluminating.

comments.issue: GPP is used in the abstract without being defined or explained.
comments.request: Define or explain GPP in the abstract.
comments.quote: as this is in the abstract, I think GPP either needs defining or explaining what it means

comments.issue: Previous work on trophic richness patterns is not specified and the advance over it is unclear.
comments.request: Spell out previous findings and how this analysis advances them.
comments.quote: I think it would benefit the reader to spell out specifically what has been done previously

comments.issue: The three hypotheses lack key references at the point they are introduced.
comments.request: Add a key reference to each hypothesis.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful if each of these hypotheses had a key reference at this point

comments.issue: Acronyms GPP, NPP and NDVI are not defined for a broad ecological readership.
comments.request: Define these acronyms.
comments.quote: these acronyms are not defined before here and may not be known by all ecological readers

comments.issue: 'Environmental variability' in the heterogeneity hypothesis is ambiguous.
comments.request: Define it and give examples such as precipitation and temperature seasonality.
comments.quote: what is meant by environmental variability here? This term means many different things to different people

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation in the gridded biodiversity patterns is not acknowledged or accounted for.
comments.request: Account for spatial autocorrelation, citing the suggested literature.
comments.quote: the spatial autocorrelative nature of gridded biodiversity patterns has not been acknowledged or accounted for in this analysis

comments.issue: The variable selection sentence is opaque: which variables were excluded, how MSE and VIF were used, and what thresholds applied.
comments.request: Explain the variable selection procedure and thresholds.
comments.quote: I find this sentence a little opaque. What variables were excluded? How were MSE and VIFs actually used to select variables?

comments.issue: The criterion for retaining the six most important variables is not stated.
comments.request: State how the six variables were chosen.
comments.quote: most important according to what? Are they the six that most frequently were in the most important variables across the trophic groups?

comments.issue: The climate-change sentence should be moved or deleted because the climate-richness link is weak.
comments.request: Move or delete the sentence and temper the climate link.
comments.quote: I think this sentence should be moved later or deleted. At this point the link between climate and richness is quite weak.

comments.issue: The decline in omnivore proportion with increasing GPP is not explained.
comments.request: Offer a hypothesis for this decline.
comments.quote: is there any hypothesis or suggestion of why the proportion of omnivores slightly declined with increasing GPP?

comments.issue: Inferences extend beyond the non-causal, non-temporal evidence by linking GPP to climate change and richness declines.
comments.request: Temper the definitive wording of these inferences.
comments.quote: linking the importance of GPP for mammal richness, through to changing GPP over time (based on Xu et al., 2019), through to climate change, and then to declines in mammal richness seems like extending the inferences beyond the evidence

comments.issue: The dispersal statement lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Add a reference after the word 'requirements'.
comments.quote: I think a reference here (after the word requirements) would help provide support and evidence for this statement

comments.issue: The precipitation-seasonality result is not compared with previous mammalian richness studies.
comments.request: Put the result in the context of previous global studies.
comments.quote: I think it would be good for the reader to see this result in the context of the many other studies that have investigated mammalian richness globally

comments.issue: 'expensive' should be 'expense'.
comments.quote: (383) ‘expensive’ should be “expense”

title: Environmental variables drive spatial patterns of trophic diversity in mammals

study.system: Mastomys natalensis rodent reservoir; aerial imagery and trapping in West Africa

editor_summary: Editor finds the method promising; asks authors to address reviewers' clarifications and double-check analyses, articulate caveats of the M. natalensis data, and discuss alternative approaches such as SAM or other ensemble algorithms.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and clear method, but the small number of cities limits generalization and the comparison with the buildings model is unclear.
strengths: vision part and fine-scale feature extraction efficient

comments.issue: A CNN could have been used to link images directly to capture success for a performance comparison.
comments.request: Consider adding a direct CNN comparison.
comments.quote: it could have been envisaged by the authors to use a CNN model to directly link aerial images to the prediction of capture success at least for a performance comparison

comments.issue: With only three cities in two countries, the city used for training or validation strongly influences model selection, and SLTA behaves differently.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited generalizability and the influence of city composition.
comments.quote: the city chosen in train or in validation has a strong influence on the selection of the model, in particular the city labelled SLTA (the only one in its country) seems to have a very different dynamic from the other two

comments.issue: The rice-crop effect could be a bias or autocorrelation in SLTA, especially since the effect is not observed in GTB despite rice cultivation.
comments.request: Verify the rice-crop effect or present it as a possible bias.
comments.quote: it seems difficult to draw conclusions on the effect of rice crops, given that for SLTA it could very well be a bias or a strong self-correlation with another variable in this city

comments.issue: Trap positions, a possible bias source, are not mapped.
comments.request: Provide a map of trap positions, at least outdoor ones, possibly in the appendix.
comments.quote: it might be interesting to provide a map of the positions of the traps at least the outdoor ones (potentially in the appendix)

comments.issue: The 'buildings' model is only briefly described, so the comparison with the proposed method is hard to understand.
comments.request: Clarify the buildings model and how it differs from the proposed method.
comments.quote: I therefore ask the authors A) to clarify the “buildings” model and the difference with the proposed method to better understand the comparison of the two models

comments.issue: The 'biologically informed' argument for the buildings model is unclear, and advantages 1, 3 and 4 seem to apply to both models.
comments.request: Clarify which advantages are specific to the proposed method.
comments.quote: it seems to me that points 1, 3 and 4 of the advantages presented in the discussion apply to the main method as well as to the “buildings” model

comments.issue: Differences in model selection across train/val/test city sets may be bias, overfitting or autocorrelation rather than relevant effects.
comments.request: Verify or highlight that these differences are not artifacts of the low number of sites.
comments.quote: to verify or highlight the elements that confirm that the differences in model selections according to the sets of cities chosen in train/val/test are relevant and not the simple result of bias, overfitting or auto-correlations

comments.issue: Figure 3A trap location at highest feature importance disagrees with the text or Appendix Figure 1.
comments.request: Check and correct Figure 3A.
comments.quote: there appears to be an error in Figure 3 A, Trap location at highest feature importance, which appears to be at disagreement with the text or Figure 1 in the Appendices

comments.issue: The maps lack a spatial scale.
comments.request: Add spatial scale to the maps.
comments.quote: add spatial scale to the maps

comments.issue: Ranks are used in testing instead of the MAE without explanation.
comments.request: Explain why ranks rather than MAE are used in testing.
comments.quote: Why use ranks in test and not the MAE?

comments.issue: The buildings model appears worse than random for indoor traps in Figure 5B, and averages are missing from Figure 2B.
comments.request: Clarify this result and add averages or a table to Figure 2B.
comments.quote: From Figure 5 B, the “buildings” model appears to be worse than random at predicting indoor trap success.

comments.issue: The circular shape of the SLTA predictions in Figure 4 is not explained by the methods.
comments.request: Explain how the SLTA prediction gets this shape.
comments.quote: Why does the prediction on SLTA in figure 4 have circles? Reading the method I don't understand how it can have this shape.

comments.issue: Figure 4 shows only exterior predictions; it is unclear whether indoor predictions are similar only in form.
comments.request: Add the indoor prediction map to the appendix.
comments.quote: Figure 4 only shows the predictions for the exterior and states that the prediction for the interior is "similar". Is it similar only in form because the other results show poor model performance on indoor traps?

reviews.assessment: Finds the CV methods outdated and the performance evidence unconvincing, requesting more models, test-set importance and forward-only predictions.

comments.issue: The CV methods are outdated because pre-existing segmented overhead maps and SAM approaches overlap with what the authors built.
comments.request: Rationalize the choice of approach despite existing alternatives.
comments.quote: I find the methods described fairly outdated since there are pre-existing segmented maps of overhead classes that overlap substantially with what the authors had to build.

comments.issue: Model performance is not demonstrated convincingly.
comments.request: Show raw predictions as scatter plots and/or a cumulative error distribution.
comments.quote: the performance could use more convincing analysis, such as simply showing the actual raw predictions by scatter plotting the GT vs. predicted values

comments.issue: Only boosted regression trees are tested, so the robustness of the claims is not established.
comments.request: Test at least 3-4 additional models.
comments.quote: I would ideally like to see at least 3-4 other models in addition to boosted trees given it should be fairly easy to re-run the experiment and the results might add to the robustness of the claims

comments.issue: Variable importance is analysed on the training data, which is low value and potentially misleading.
comments.request: Redo the importance analysis on the test set and test performance after excluding features.
comments.quote: I think it'd be good to redo the analysis but for the test set. In general, any analysis done directly on the training data is fairly low value and has great potential to be misleading.

comments.issue: Testing allows non-forward predictions, risking contamination from temporally correlated test data.
comments.request: Restrict testing and validation to forward predictions only.
comments.quote: I would find the results more convincing if the models were only allowed to make forward predictions during testing/validation.

title: Predicting the fine‐scale spatial distribution of zoonotic reservoirs using computer vision

study.system: simulated three-species food-web modules; invasions along temperature and productivity gradients

editor_summary: Editor finds the theoretical exercise interesting and well presented; reviewers agree it has great potential if links to empirical reality are developed, and additional analysis beyond discussion is requested.

reviews.assessment: Interesting question and useful inclusion of understudied modules, but underwhelmed: the advance and testable predictions remain unclear.
strengths: application to invasive species and global change
includes multiple food web interaction types
apparent competition and IGP are rarely studied

comments.issue: Unclear how the paper substantially advances understanding of invasion; predictions stay context-dependent rather than general.
comments.request: Clarify how the study advances the field and identify its novel contributions.
comments.quote: I am not quite sure how this paper substantially moves our understanding of invasion forward

comments.issue: Take-home message that smaller animals are better invaders seems obvious and possibly not new.
comments.quote: I’m not sure if this prediction is new in the literature, but it seems obvious to me

comments.issue: Relative terms 'larger' and 'smaller' are undefined, so the predictions are not testable.
comments.request: Define 'large' and 'small' in testable terms.
