comments.issue: Figure 3B-C cannot be explained as done; latitude versus ratio should be analysed directly.
comments.request: Analyse latitude directly against the N resorption/requirement ratio.
comments.quote: Fig.3 B-C cannot be explained in this way. It should be more helpful to directly analyze the relationship between latitude (x-axis) and the ratio of N resorption to N requirement (y-axis).

comments.issue: The discussion mixes latitude zones, hydrothermal conditions and mycorrhizal distributions.
comments.request: Reorganize the discussion for clarity.
comments.quote: The discussion attempts to explain the unimportant role of climate conditions, but it mixes latitude zones, hydrothermal conditions, and mycorrhizal type distributions together.

comments.issue: Global atmospheric CO2 is unevenly distributed, so sampling-year values may not represent the site.
comments.request: Use site-representative CO2 values.
comments.quote: The global atmospheric CO2 concentration is unevenly distributed, and the CO2 concentration value of the sampling year may not represent the concentration of the study site.

comments.issue: Relevant Terrer et al. studies on mycorrhizas and CO2 are not cited.
comments.request: Reference Terrer et al. (2016) and (2021).
comments.quote: The authors may consider referencing previous studies on this topic, such as Terrer et al. (2016) and Terrer et al. (2021), which have investigated the mycorrhizal association as a primary control of the CO2 fertilization effect

comments.issue: 'Resoprtion' is misspelled in figure axis titles, with similar errors elsewhere.
comments.request: Correct the spelling in all figures.
comments.quote: The y-axis titles of B and C should be corrected from “resoprtion” to “resorption”. There are similar errors in other figures.

comments.issue: AM and EM are represented with different colours/lines across figures.
comments.request: Use the same colours or lines as in Figure 1.
comments.quote: The authors may consider using the same color or line as that in Fig.1 to represent AM and EM trees.

reviews.assessment: Well written and pleasant to read, but the global analysis is confounded and other nutrient limitations, especially P, are ignored.
strengths: well written and pleasant to read
co-occurring AM and EM comparison convincing

comments.issue: The paper ignores other essential nutrients, especially P limitation in tropical and subtropical forests.
comments.request: Include the state-of-the-art view of global N and P limitation in the introduction and discussion.
comments.quote: The authors ignore the importance of other essential nutrients, especially P limitation in tropical and subtropical forests. The state-of-art view of global N and P limitation should be included in the introduction and discussion section.

comments.issue: Global analysis cannot separate drivers (MAT, MAP, CO2) from other factors; simple linear regression is insufficient.
comments.request: Control for confounding factors such as soil nutrients and forest age, and amend the global analysis.
comments.quote: Otherwise, effects of factors other than AMvsEM should be well controlled in the statistical analysis. I don’t think a simple linear regression analysis can identify separate effect of each driver (i.e., MAT, MAP, CO2).

comments.issue: The N limitation framing is outdated and ignores tropical P limitation.
comments.request: Adopt an updated view of N and P limitation (e.g. Du et al. 2020).
comments.quote: This is an old view of N limitation. I would expect an updated view of N (and P) limitation (e.g., Du et al., 2020 Nat Geo).

comments.issue: Latitude is not an environmental factor.
comments.request: Do not call latitude an environmental factor.
comments.quote: We may not call latitude as an environmental factor.

comments.issue: The exact variables collected are not clear.
comments.request: Clarify the exact variables collected.
comments.quote: Please clarify the exact variables collected.

title: Ectomycorrhizal trees rely on nitrogen resorption less than arbuscular mycorrhizal trees globally

study.system: plant pollination and seed dispersal mutualisms; conceptual framework

editor_summary: Editor and all reviewers like integrating pollen limitation into the SDE framework, but critical issues remain: oversimplification and omitted factors, inaccurate literature review, inadequate conceptual logic, and missing secondary dispersal.

reviews.assessment: Likes the idea but finds the treatment oversimplified, missing key concepts and literature, and in places inaccurate.
strengths: likes the idea of linking pollination and seed dispersal research
conceptual and historical parallels with SDE are promising

comments.issue: Pollination effectiveness concept and its parallels with SDE are not mentioned.
comments.request: Integrate pollination effectiveness into the framework.
comments.quote: the concept of pollination effectiveness (e.g. Schupp et al. 2017) is not even mentioned despite the obvious (conceptual and historical) parallelisms with SDE

comments.issue: State of the art from the 328 existing studies linking pollination and dispersal is not reviewed.
comments.request: Provide a state-of-the-art review based on those studies.
comments.quote: It is not enough to state that only 328 studies link pollination and seed dispersal. Readers would expect you to provide a view of the state-of-the-art based on knowledge generated by those published studies.

comments.issue: Fine-scale genetic structure, a critical determinant of pollen limitation, is not developed.
comments.request: Develop and discuss FSGS effects on PL and SDE.
comments.quote: The fine scale genetic structure (FSGS) of plant populations is a critical determinant for the magnitude and spatial heterogeneity of PL

comments.issue: Future research approaches are not specific enough.
comments.request: Propose specific experiments such as hand pollinations and camera traps.
comments.quote: Please, propose more specific approaches for future studies linking pollination (PL) and seed dispersal (SDE).

comments.issue: Statement on plant dynamics and distribution ignores many other factors.
comments.request: Acknowledge the other factors involved.
comments.quote: This sentence oversimplifies an actually complex reality. Plant dynamics and distribution can be certainly affected by plant-disperser interactions but there many other factors involved that cannot be ignored.

comments.issue: Claim about frugivore fruit handling is inaccurate.
comments.request: Correct the statement about frugivore behaviour.
comments.quote: This is not accurate. Many frugivores remove fruits, move away, and then ingest the fruits far away from mother plants.

comments.issue: Aborted fruits become available to terrestrial consumers earlier, a timing effect not considered.
comments.request: Consider earlier availability of aborted fruits.
comments.quote: For the Iberia pear, which fruits fall to the ground due to deficient pollination, such fruits become available to terrestrial consumers earlier than fully-developed fruits.

comments.issue: Ants can extract seeds directly from partly opened fruits, an alternative removal route.
comments.request: Consider direct seed extraction by ants.
comments.quote: In Helleborus foetidus, and likely in other small plants with pod-like fruits, ants often climb to the plant infrutescences while fruits are only partly opened and then, extract the seeds directly from the fruits.

comments.issue: Two line-level wording fixes (P9 L27, P17 L57).
comments.quote: P17 L57. maximum *dispersal distance

comments.issue: Frugivore physiology such as seed retention times is not included as a key factor.
comments.request: Consider frugivore physiology.
comments.quote: Frugivore physiology (e.g. seed retention times) is also key for seed dispersal.

comments.issue: Foraging decisions at larger spatial scales are overlooked.
comments.request: Consider larger-scale foraging decisions.
comments.quote: Depending on their body size and mobility, frugivores also take foraging decisions at larger scales.

comments.issue: Sobral et al. (2010) is cited but missing from the reference list.
comments.request: Add the missing reference.
comments.quote: P11 L14. Sobral et al. (2010) is missing in the list of references

comments.issue: Changes in pulp chemical composition and toughness are also likely.
comments.request: Consider pulp chemical composition and toughness.
comments.quote: Based on Fedriani et al. 2020, changes in pulp chemical composition and toughness are also likely.

comments.issue: The claimed link depends on crop size: large pollen-limited plants may still dominate dispersal.
comments.request: Account for crop size in this claim.
comments.quote: This is not necessarily true. It largely depends on crop size. Large individual plants can be severely pollen-limited but still be the ones within the population that most contribute to seed dispersal.

comments.issue: Shifts in frugivore assemblages via novel trait matchings are not mentioned or developed.
comments.request: Mention and develop novel trait matchings.
comments.quote: The possibility that PL results into shifts in frugivore assemblages as a consequence of fruit/seed trait changes leading to ‘novel’ trait matchings must be mentioned and developed.

comments.issue: Linear relationships are assumed where saturating responses are expected.
comments.request: Use nonlinear response relationships.
comments.quote: I would not expect linear relationships (Holling 1959).

comments.issue: How distance distributions were simulated and whether they are empirically representative is not stated.
comments.request: Describe the simulation of distance distributions.
comments.quote: How did you ‘simulate’ such distance distributions? Are these distributions representative of empirically-observed ones?

comments.issue: Perea et al. 2013 is suggested as a missing relevant reference.
comments.request: Cite Perea et al. 2013.
comments.quote: P21 L3-7. See Perea et al. 2013. Perea R, M Delibes, Polko M, Suárez-Esteban A, JM Fedriani 2013.

comments.issue: Plant density and pollinator assemblage are misclassified as extrinsic factors.
comments.request: Do not qualify these factors as extrinsic.
comments.quote: Plant density and the pollinator assemblage don’t seem to me extrinsic to neither plant-pollinator interactions nor PL

comments.issue: Passage is too speculative.
comments.request: Reduce the speculation.
comments.quote: P22 L16-23. Too speculative.

comments.issue: Claim about human-modified landscapes oversimplifies PL heterogeneity and ignores invasive species.
comments.request: Acknowledge context dependence and counterexamples.
comments.quote: This is also an oversimplification. Heterogeneity in magnitude of PL is expected to occur in most landscapes. PL depends more on factors such as population size or FSGS.

comments.issue: Argument about incompatible genotypes and floral traits is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the argument.
comments.quote: This argument is unclear. For instance, PL often results from the cross of incompatible genotypes.

reviews.assessment: Excited by the attempt but finds the manuscript hard to follow, over-speculative, and conceptually muddled about dispersal quality; wants a major revision.
strengths: exciting attempt to integrate pollen limitation into SDE
commends the authors on these efforts

comments.issue: Manuscript is very difficult to read and follow; no roadmap at the end of the introduction.
comments.request: Add a detailed outline and clearer subsections.
comments.quote: Unfortunately, I find it very difficult to read and follow.

comments.issue: Literature is misinterpreted in places and major complexities are overlooked.
comments.request: Correct the literature interpretation and address the complexities.
comments.quote: I think some of the literature is being misinterpreted, and where some major complexities seem to be overlooked

comments.issue: Speculation outweighs support; the manuscript should be drastically shortened to its core.
comments.request: Shorten the manuscript drastically.
comments.quote: I suggest that it might be best if it is drastically shortened to present the core of the idea

comments.issue: An edited PDF with writing suggestions is provided separately.
comments.quote: In addition I will upload an edited version of the pdf manuscript with suggestions on writing.

comments.issue: Potential effects of PL on offspring quality and selective abortion are not considered.
comments.request: Consider PL effects on offspring quality.
comments.quote: Also consider the potential effects of PL on the offspring quality (e.g., germinability, vigor) which feeds indirectly into the quality of dispersal

comments.issue: 'Few' and 'several' are vague and interchangeable.
comments.request: Replace vague quantifiers.
comments.quote: ‘few’ and ‘several’ are both vague words with no standard definitions

comments.issue: Claim about smaller diaspores in myrmecochores is purely speculative.
comments.request: Add evidence or revise the speculation.
comments.quote: this seems to be purely speculative with nothing empirical to back it up

comments.issue: Paragraph contradicts itself: later statement conflicts with the earlier one.
comments.request: Make the paragraph internally consistent.
comments.quote: now you seem to be saying what I was saying, but not shat you said earlier in this paragraph

comments.issue: Dispersal quality is conflated with measured/perceived quality that includes seed quality.
comments.request: Distinguish dispersal quality from measured quality.
comments.quote: In a sense it seems we are not talking about dispersal quality, but rather measured or perceived dispersal quality

comments.issue: Seed size is treated as the only PL effect on seed vigor.
comments.request: Consider other drivers of seed vigor.
comments.quote: do you really think the only impact of PL on seed ‘vigor’ is seed size?

comments.issue: Seed dispersal is wrongly described as a product.
comments.request: Rephrase the product framing.
comments.quote: Page 10, line 33 – seed dispersal is not a product.

comments.issue: Indirect effects are claimed to be the main mechanism despite extremely weak support.
comments.request: Remove or temper the claim.
comments.quote: I do not see at all how you can claim this extremely speculative outcome is more important than the less speculative outcomes on seed numbers and size

comments.issue: Foraging is more complex: diet mixing and satiation also drive departure from fruiting trees.
comments.request: Consider these additional foraging behaviours.
comments.quote: But foraging can actually be much more complex. Birds may leave a fruiting tree in order to mix diets with complementary resources

comments.issue: Direct and indirect effects are not clearly distinguished; single-plant versus neighbourhood scope is confused.
comments.request: Clarify direct versus indirect effects.
comments.quote: I am getting confused about what is a direct effect and what is an indirect effect

comments.issue: Gape limitation means larger fruits may not be dispersible.
comments.request: Account for gape limitation.
comments.quote: A larger fruit might seem more desirable, but if it can’t be swallowed it is not going to be dispersed.

comments.issue: Crop size affects bird residency and seed dropping beneath the canopy.
comments.request: Consider crop-size effects on residency.
comments.quote: Crop size affects how long a bird stays in the tree and thus the probability of dropping seeds beneath the canopy versus dispersing them away

comments.issue: Schupp et al. 2010 does not support the statement that dispersal away implies long-distance dispersal.
comments.request: Find another reference or revise the claim.
comments.quote: sorry, but Schupp et al 2010 does not support any statement like this

comments.issue: Long-distance dispersal is used without a definition despite contested meanings.
comments.request: Define LDD with citations.
comments.quote: early in this manuscript you need to define, with citations, what you mean by ldd

comments.issue: The distance-distribution exercise and figure are unnecessary and obvious.
comments.request: Remove or justify this exercise and figure.
comments.quote: is this exercise and figure necessary? Isn’t this completely obvious if all that changes is the number of dispersal events?

comments.issue: Reviewer disagrees with the content of the passage at Page 18, lines 27-31.
comments.quote: Page 18, lines 27-31 – I don’t agree with this.

comments.issue: Claim that long-distance dispersal equals high-quality dispersal is wrong.
comments.request: Correct the LDD-quality claim.
comments.quote: You seem to be still claiming that ldd = high quality, which it does not.

comments.issue: Seed vigor is said to affect dispersal quality, but it only affects measured quality.
comments.request: Distinguish seed vigor from dispersal quality.
comments.quote: seed vigor is not really affecting seed dispersal quality. It affects our measurement of quality, our perception of quality

comments.issue: Passage is entirely speculative with little support.
comments.request: Add support or remove the passage.
comments.quote: this appears to be entirely speculative with little support for it being a real issue

comments.issue: 'Plants within what' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrasing.
comments.quote: Page 20, line 21 – plants within what? This does not make sense to me.

comments.issue: Wording error: 'animal-dispersal' should be 'animal-dispersed'.
comments.request: Fix the wording.
comments.quote: Page 20, line 31 – ‘animal-dispersed’ not ‘animal-dispersal’

reviews.assessment: Welcomes the framework and asks to add secondary seed dispersal; remaining comments concern citations, wording, figure panels and paragraph structure.

comments.issue: Secondary seed dispersal (e.g. by dung beetles) is missing from the framework.
comments.request: Add secondary seed dispersal to the framework and discussion.
comments.quote: I think it would be interesting to add a discussion about another post-dispersal event which is the secondary seed dispersal

comments.issue: The quality side of the dispersal-unit statement lacks a citation; Knight et al. 2005 covers only quantity.
comments.request: Cite support for the quality claim.
comments.quote: you cited earlier in the introduction Knight et al 2005 which is a perfect citation for the decrease in dispersal unit quantity; but what about the dispersal unit quality?

comments.issue: Sentence on neutral or positive effects on pre-dispersal predation is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify the direction of the effect.
comments.quote: a little difficult to follow. What is a positive effect on pre-dispersal predation?

comments.issue: Lower fruit set may increase foraging distances and thus long-distance dispersal, the opposite prediction.
comments.request: Consider the increased foraging-distance alternative.
comments.quote: This possible increase in foraging distances might lead to increased dispersal distances, don´t you think?

comments.issue: The distance relationship assumes frugivores do not adjust foraging strategy to fruit abundance.
comments.request: Consider this alternative hypothesis.
comments.quote: this relationship is based on the assumption that the frugivore will not change its foraging strategy (and movement patterns) according to the fruit abundance in the tree

comments.issue: Paragraph announces dispersal-unit traits but discusses disperser traits first.
comments.request: Make the trait discussion more explicit.
comments.quote: You begin this paragraph talking about seed dispersal unit´ s traits but first discuss seed disperser traits.

comments.issue: Two paragraphs repeat the same argument and should be merged.
comments.request: Merge the two paragraphs.
comments.quote: Therefore, I suggest going more directly to the point and merge the paragraph P18L12-44 with this one.

comments.issue: Figure 2 panels appear to be labelled the wrong way round.
comments.request: Swap the panel labels.
comments.quote: Isn´t it the contrary? A) not pollen-limited plants (since the number of seeds is higher (1000), and B) pollen-limited plants

title: Linking pollen limitation and seed dispersal effectiveness

study.system: periodical cicada emergence holes and soil respiration; Indiana forests

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the multi-scale analysis but finds the effects small, the importance oversold and several methods details missing.
strengths: impressive integration of data across scales
good job explaining weaknesses and alternative explanations

comments.issue: The saturation/anaerobic mechanism is unconvincing as burrow effects would be transient.
comments.request: Revise the saturation mechanism.
comments.quote: I find this latter mechanism to be less convincing than the first because I think it is unlikely the burrows create anything more than a transient effects on anaerobic conditions during rain events

comments.issue: The importance of cicada burrow impacts on C flux is oversold given small effects.
comments.request: Tone down the importance claims.
comments.quote: I think the author oversell the importance of the potential impacts of cicada burrows on C flux

comments.issue: Trend significance and the eddy covariance conclusions are hard to interpret.
comments.request: Clarify the figures and eddy covariance interpretation.
comments.quote: I had difficulty interpreting the significance of trends shown in a couple of key figures and I struggled to understand the conclusions about the cicada effects in relation to the long-term eddy covariance data

comments.issue: Preferential flow can bypass matrix flow, so the saturation mechanism is questionable and aeration likely dominates.
comments.request: Reconsider the saturation versus aeration mechanisms.
comments.quote: Preferential flow pathways can increase infiltration but can also bypass matrix flow

comments.issue: Methods lack site selection and sampling details, making extrapolation hard to assess.
comments.request: Describe site selection and sampling representativeness.
comments.quote: I had some issues with lack of information provided in the methods, which made it difficult for me to assess whether their sampling approach was sound

comments.issue: The unit of 120 trees (per plot) is ambiguous.
comments.request: Specify trees per plot.
comments.quote: Line 137. Specify here that it is 120 trees per plot, not hectare or some other unit.

comments.issue: Tree-base distance, transect type and collar deployment are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify transect and collar placement.
comments.quote: How close to the base of the tree were the squares placed? And I am unclear about the transects.

comments.issue: The number of collars deployed at one time is not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of collars.
comments.quote: Line 147 You state that the collards were deployed systematically but you do not indicate how many collars were deployed at one time (N=?).

comments.issue: Whether hole numbers changed during collar deployment is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify hole dynamics during deployment.
comments.quote: Were there any situations when the number of holes in the collar changed during the collar deployment?

comments.issue: Soil moisture probe placement (in or adjacent to collar) is unclear.
comments.request: Specify probe placement.
comments.quote: Did you measure soil moisture with TDR probes in the soil in the collar or adjacent to the collar?

comments.issue: Q10 estimates may be confounded because moisture varied while temperature overlapped.
comments.request: Account for moisture confounding in Q10.
comments.quote: Other factors like soil moisture also changed over this time and you had different time periods where temp was similar but moisture different

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits (L255 Zendo, L309 missing word).
comments.quote: Line 309. Should there be “cicadas” after “with” on this line?

comments.issue: The text misstates August temperature, which was as low as early June.
comments.request: Correct the temperature statement.
comments.quote: As shown in Fig. 2a Temperature during the August measurement was as low as the early June temperature, not higher as indicated in the text.

comments.issue: Significance notation in Fig. 3 conflicts with the text explanation.
comments.request: Clarify the significance notation.
comments.quote: Clearly, that is not true based on the text and figure plots but I found the statistical asterisks to be confusing.

comments.issue: Whether temperature sensitivity was measured only during the emergence period is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the measurement period.
comments.quote: Line 330. Was this temperature sensitivity measured only during the predicted emergence period?

comments.issue: Comparing 0.3 Gg with 34 Tg and fossil fuel declines overstates cicada relevance.
comments.request: Remove or temper the claim.
comments.quote: The predicted decline in fossil fuel emission over the coming decades will have nil effect on the relative importance of cicadas to CO2 efflux.

comments.issue: Cicada carcasses or exoskeletons in chambers could confound the burrow effect.
comments.request: Clarify carcass presence in chambers.
comments.quote: did you have cicada carcasses or exoskeletons in your measurement chambers?

comments.issue: The EcM/AM prediction difference should be cross-referenced to the text.
comments.request: Cross-reference the explanation.
comments.quote: Explain that differences in prediction for EcM and AM are explained in the text.

comments.issue: Fig. 6 letter notation does not follow mean magnitude.
comments.request: Order the letters by mean magnitude.
comments.quote: I would normally expect the a b c notation to follow the magnitude of the mean

comments.issue: Fig. S1 legend says holes per collar while the graph shows holes per m2.
comments.request: Fix the legend units.
comments.quote: S1. Figure legend refers to holes per collar but data in graph are holes per m2.

reviews.assessment: Finds the study novel and well-written but has major concerns about the soil respiration definition, flux interpretation and regional uncertainty.

comments.issue: Rs is defined as microbial plus root respiration, excluding soil fauna, which conflicts with the classic definition.
comments.request: Clarify or adopt the classic Rs definition.
comments.quote: This study defined Rs as the sum of microbial and root respiration (Lines 81-82), which may confuse some readers.

comments.issue: Large differences between the 2004 and 2021 emergence events are not compared or explained.
comments.request: Compare the two emergence events.
comments.quote: I want to recommend that the authors compare these two events and explore the factors contributing to their difference.

comments.issue: Fig. 3 shows only 0-2 holes while the text describes site-level hole densities.
comments.request: Double-check the figure and make results apparent.
comments.quote: Strangely, the L270-275 described the hole densities at different sites, but Figure 3 only showed three groups of hole numbers

comments.issue: Higher Q10 may stem from moisture or porosity rather than the holes.
comments.request: Rule out moisture and porosity drivers.
comments.quote: it is unclear whether the higher Q10 in Fig. 4 resulted from the holes or other factors, such as soil moisture and porosity

comments.issue: The county-level Rs upscaling carries large uncertainty that is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the regional-estimate uncertainties.
comments.quote: There is considerable uncertainty in the estimation of Rs across eastern US counties based on the current data (L306-310).

comments.issue: Tree species proportions and AM/EcM dominance are not reported.
comments.request: Report tree species proportions.
comments.quote: It would helpful if they can provide more information about the proportions of different species, especially the difference of dominance between AM and ECM trees

comments.issue: Which hourly fluxes form the baseline is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the baseline averaging.
comments.quote: It is unclear which “hourly fluxes” were averaged to represent the baseline C fluxes.

comments.issue: Q5.5 and Q89 are not explained.
comments.request: Explain Q5.5 and Q89.
comments.quote: L316-317: It is better to explain Q5.5 and Q89.

comments.issue: Readers unfamiliar with cicada emergence would benefit from photographs.
comments.request: Add photographs to the supplement.
comments.quote: some pictures of the holes and measuring plots could be added to the supplementary file

title: The forest, the cicadas and the holey fluxes: Periodical cicada impacts on soil respiration depends on tree mycorrhizal type

study.system: Hetaerina rubyspot damselflies; ecological niche models

editor_summary: Editor agrees with the major criticism that the aquatic larval phase is under-emphasized; asks for a section on how environmental variables relate to aquatic and terrestrial stages and discussion of both phases.

reviews.assessment: Niche models are well done, but conclusions are unconvincing because aquatic nymphal niche variables are omitted and may bias the results.
strengths: ecological niche models thoroughly done and clearly explained
emphasis on environmental variables is a good direction
well written and clear even for non-specialists

comments.issue: Niche variables cover only the terrestrial adult stage, ignoring the freshwater nymphal stage, so niche breadth and overlap measures may be biased.
comments.request: Include aquatic nymphal variables or justify their omission.
comments.quote: the environmental variables that they use are exclusively relevant to the aerial/terrestrial adult stages and the modeling thus ignores environmental variables important to the freshwater nymphal stages

comments.issue: Reproductive interference is flagged at line 53, where the term first appears, and may need clarification.
comments.request: Define reproductive interference at first use.
comments.quote: Line 53. “reproductive interference”

comments.issue: Reproductive experience on line 172 is an odd term and may be meant as interference.
comments.request: Clarify or replace the term reproductive experience.
comments.quote: “reproductive experience” is an odd choice of word. Do you mean "interference"? or something else?

comments.issue: Recently split on line 174 does not say from what or which the sister group is.
comments.request: Specify the sister group and the split.
comments.quote: “recently split”. split from what? what is the sister group?

comments.issue: The niche analysis omits aquatic environmental variables, and landcover categories for water are too crude for Calopterygidae.
comments.request: Justify the omission or incorporate aquatic variables into the niche analysis.
comments.quote: It seems to me you need to justify this rather large omission from the niche analysis, or better yet, incorporate some of the aquatic variables into the niche analysis.

comments.issue: The conclusion that H. titia occupies a niche near the genus centroid may depend on ignoring the nymphal niche.
comments.request: Test whether the centroid conclusion holds with nymphal variables.
comments.quote: This conclusion may depend heavily on ignoring the niche of the nymphs.

comments.issue: The narrow niche of H. titia may be an artifact of ignoring the nymphal niche.
comments.request: Reassess narrow niche with aquatic variables included.
comments.quote: The narrow niche of *H. titia*. Again, this may be dependent on ignoring nymphal niche.

comments.issue: Niche overlap results may be a product of ignoring aquatic niches.
comments.request: Reassess niche overlap with aquatic variables included.
comments.quote: I can’t help thinking these results are a product of ignoring the aquatic niches.

comments.issue: Allopatric on line 338 should be specified as allopatric to all other congeners.
comments.request: Add to all other congeners.
comments.quote: “allopatric” add: “to all other congeners”

comments.issue: Whether the niche is narrow on line 349 may depend on whether aquatic variables were included.
comments.request: Reassess narrowness with aquatic variables included.
comments.quote: See previous comment: would niche be narrow if variables from the aquatic environment were included?

comments.issue: Niche expansion when released from reproductive interference cannot be ruled out without the nymphal niche, because wider aquatic habitats may become exploitable.
comments.request: Rule out niche expansion using nymphal niche data.
comments.quote: I don't think you have convincingly ruled out niche expansion when relieved from reproductive interference, or any other process limiting geographic distribution.

comments.issue: Conspecific density and intraspecific competition may also shape habitat and oviposition choice but cannot be evaluated without the aquatic niche.
comments.request: Consider conspecific density and intraspecific competition.
comments.quote: Conspecific density is another factor that can affect habitat selection (e.g., ideal free distribution models)

comments.issue: Similar climatic niches are not equivalent to similar overall niches for species with a complex life cycle and extensive aquatic phase.
comments.request: Use overall niche similarity rather than climatic similarity.
comments.quote: More similar climatic niches is not necessarily equivalent to more similar overall niche for species with complex life cycles and an extensive aquatic phase.

comments.issue: Unmeasured variables also influence the niche breadth and overlap measures central to the arguments.
comments.request: Account for unmeasured niche variables in the central measures.
comments.quote: Those unmeasured variables also influence niche breadth and overlap, which are central to your arguments.

comments.issue: Niche modelers cannot understand complex-life-cycle species by focusing on only one conspicuous life stage.
comments.request: Broaden niche modelling to all life-cycle stages.
comments.quote: ecological niche modelers cannot advance our understanding by focusing only on one lifecycle stage, in one distinct environment, even if it is the most conspicuous stage to us.

reviews.assessment: Analyses appear appropriate and the discussion interesting; suggests phylogenetic and extinction perspectives plus minor corrections.
strengths: important dimension to understanding Rubyspot damselfly communities
very interesting discussion with general implications

comments.issue: Whether sympatric species tend to be phylogenetically closely related is not tested, though it would support the reproductive interference argument.
comments.request: Test phylogenetic relatedness of sympatric species.
comments.quote: If possible, it would be interesting if there is the tendency that sympatric species are phylogenetically closely related.

comments.issue: The arguments assume no extinction, but species with narrow fundamental niches under reproductive interference may have gone extinct.
comments.request: Consider extinction of non-aggressive narrow-niche species.
comments.quote: It is additionally possible that species with narrow fundamental niche and subjected to reproductive interference have become extinct.

comments.issue: 4 line-level copy edits (word corrections and a duplicated word).
comments.quote: L127 “be” appears twice.

comments.issue: Narrow niche width in environmental space does not imply the niche environment is rare in nature; mapping niche to geographic range is a separate question.
comments.request: Address how the niche maps to geographic range.
comments.quote: Species may show relatively narrow niche width in environmental space, but such niche environment may be widely available in nature.

comments.issue: A similar point about niche conservatism was already made by Warren et al. (2014).
comments.request: Cite Warren et al. (2014).

reviews.assessment: Clear, well-written paper on an important topic; only several methods clarifications are requested.

comments.issue: Experimental evolution procedures are not described for readers unfamiliar with the earlier studies.

title: A grazer's niche edge is associated with increasing diet diversity and poor population performance

title: How collectively integrated are ecological communities?

study.system: Penicillium fungi; phylogenomic gene trees and pairwise competition assays

editor_summary: Enthusiastic about using gene trees to find loci linked to coexistence, but doubts the approach extends beyond simple traits and organisms; also non-independence and accessibility; rejects with invitation to resubmit.

reviews.assessment: Core framework idea has merit, but layered variance sources, limited power and heavy data filtering raise substantive methodological concerns; does not support publication as is.
strengths: ambitious scope bringing together competition, genotype-phenotype and genomic discordance
general construction of the analysis is sensible
core idea of the analysis framework has merit

comments.issue: Stacked variance layers make results hard to interpret and may leave very limited power.

comments.issue: The empirical example required very heavy filtering of usable genes and has limited functional information.

comments.issue: Phylogenetic distances should be topological distances on a tree, not rates of pairwise molecular distances.
comments.request: Measure topological tree distances rather than molecular distances.
comments.quote: For a particular gene tree, this means measuring topological distances on a tree, not rates of pairwise molecular distances.

comments.issue: Pairwise phylogenetic distances reuse branches and are not independent across pairs; multi-gene conditioning may amplify this.
comments.request: Use a phylogenetic independent contrasts approach.
comments.quote: The study here appears to do all pairwise phylogenetic distances rather than using a Phylogenetic Independent Contrasts approach. When the same branch distances are re-used, there is the potential for auto-correlation in the data.

comments.issue: Making mutation rate decrease with population size may alter gene trees, distances and inferred population sizes.

comments.quote: changing the mutation rate I think would have substantial effect on gene tree and phylogenetic distance calculations

comments.issue: Figure 1 is too simple to aid understanding of the methods and should be removed.
comments.request: Remove Figure 1.

comments.issue: A clear species phylogeny figure is missing, making expected relationships hard to follow.
comments.request: Replace Figure 1 with a clear species phylogeny, reusing the later colour scheme.
comments.quote: Recommend replacing Figure 1 with a clearer view of the proposed species phylogeny.

comments.issue: The gene tree underlying Figure 5 is not shown.

comments.quote: Recommend showing the gene tree for Figure 5.

comments.issue: The introduction is too methodological and assumes knowledge of introgression, gene duplication and incomplete lineage sorting.

technique applied to a relevant trait in Penicillium fungi
well written in terms of grammar and structure and a good length

comments.issue: Environmental variables as alternative causes are not sufficiently removed or the rationale explained; a formal comparison is needed.
comments.request: Explain the rationale and compare the correlation coefficients formally.
comments.quote: I don't think the authors do enough to remove these potential effects, or at least the approach should be better explained.

comments.issue: Supplementary model diagnostics are missing (R-hats, effective sample sizes, chain details and plots).
comments.request: Provide diagnostic tables and chain plots in the supplement.
comments.quote: I would expect to see some diagnostic graphs and tables from the models: 1) A table with actual R-hats, effective sample sizes and details on how many chains were run and for how long.

comments.issue: The custom Stan code is not shared.
comments.request: Share the code as a repository or electronic supplement.
comments.quote: given custom models were built directly in Stan, I think it is quite important to share the code directly as a repository or electronic supplement.

comments.issue: "Informal" calibration for multiple comparisons is insufficient for discussing specific species.
comments.request: Provide a threshold for which moth species reliably affect tit populations.
comments.quote: I do not think that is sufficient, especially if the authors want to discuss the effect of specific species. It would be important to have a threshold of which of the 11 moth species are reliably affecting tit populations.

comments.issue: Figure 1 and its repetitive legend are cluttered; posterior histograms could be replaced by trend lines with shading.
comments.request: Simplify the legend and consider trend lines with 95% and 80% shading.
comments.quote: Regardless of following this suggestion, the figure legend should definitely be simplified, as its extremely repetitive.

comments.issue: Lines 134-145 are hard to follow despite being central to the manuscript.
comments.request: Rewrite this section for clarity.
comments.quote: Lines 134-145 are quite hard to follow. Given how important understanding this is for the whole manuscript, I think the authors could try to rewrite this section a bit.

comments.issue: 5 line-level typos/language issues (L133-4, L285, L332, L386, L408).
comments.quote: Lines 133-4: This sentence is a bit too informal (“lots of moths” especially)

title: Population links between an insectivorous bird and moths disentangled through national‐scale monitoring data

study.system: phytoplankton; Droop nutrient-uptake model with temperature-dependent rates

editor_summary: Editor found the work timely, rigorous and elegant; reviewers raised mostly minor points and the editor urges the authors to address R2's suggested sensitivity analyses.

reviews.assessment: Extremely positive about the mechanistic model, with only minor comments on figures, terminology and a missing citation.
strengths: mechanistic Droop model of nutrient uptake

comments.issue: The implication that equilibrial biomass is a poor estimate under warming is under-discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this point more thoroughly.
comments.quote: I think the authors could discuss this point more thoroughly, since many of our conclusions to date have been based on how warming impacts equilibrial biomass in thermally constant environments

comments.issue: Figure 4 time scales are subtle and x-axes in panels A-C are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Make the time scales and x-axes clearer.
comments.quote: I only suggest that the time scales on figure 4 were kind of subtle, and I had to look very closely at the x-axes in panels A-C to distinguish between the scenarios

comments.issue: Figure 3 and terms such as dynamic temperature regime are difficult to follow.
comments.request: Simplify the terminology for a general audience.
comments.quote: I didn't really understand Figure 3, nor the term Dynamic Temperature Regime. I think much of the terminology could be clarified to be simpler to understand.

comments.issue: The LKE model of nutritional mismatches is not cited.
comments.request: Cite and discuss the Loladze et al. LKE model.
comments.quote: I noticed that the LKE model hasn't been cited, and it is perhaps the first model to consider the importance of nutritional mismatches in population dynamics.

reviews.assessment: Commends the rigor and clarity and supports publication, but wants the phytoplankton-specific assumptions justified and tested.

comments.issue: Model choices rest on an unpublished study, so assumptions about temperature dependence need justification and sensitivity tests.
comments.request: Explain the model choices and run sensitivity analyses on temperature-dependence assumptions.
comments.quote: I believe you should put more effort into explaining the choices you made in the model, and potentially run some extra model sensitivity analyses

comments.issue: One citation is insufficient to justify both V_max and mu_max being unimodal functions of temperature.
comments.request: Anchor the unimodal assumptions in empirical literature.
comments.quote: I am not sure if this is enough to convince your readers that both maximum nutrient uptake rate V\_max as well as maximum nutrient assimilation rate mu\_max should be unimodal functions of temperature

comments.issue: Making both V_max and mu_max unimodal may double-account; growth is already unimodal with V_max alone.
comments.request: Run a sensitivity analysis with a constant, temperature-independent mu_max.
comments.quote: it feels like you make your algae respond unimodally to temperature in a double manner - first by V\_max, and then by mu\_max

comments.issue: An alternative, more realistic assumption of Q_min increasing with temperature is not tested.
comments.request: Run a sensitivity analysis with constant mu_max and Q_min increasing with temperature.
comments.quote: A more interesting assumption - and potentially more relatable by specialists in the field - would be to assume the minimum nutrient quota Q\_min as an increasing function of temperature.

comments.issue: The nutrient considered is not identified, though internal nutrient dynamics differ among elements.
comments.request: State which nutrient is represented or discuss this in the discussion.
comments.quote: More specialized readership will also notice that you do not identify what nutrient you are considering.

comments.issue: Model parameters are given without units.
comments.request: Mention parameter units in a general manner.
comments.quote: I always shudder when I see parameters without any units in ecological models.

comments.issue: Three line-level typos: 'very' for 'vary' (L237), 'vial' for 'via' (L568), 'os' for 'is' (L666).
comments.quote: (line 237) Vary, not very?

comments.issue: It is the realized uptake rate, not the maximum, that saturates.
comments.request: Correct the statement about which uptake rate saturates.
comments.quote: (line 568-569) Isn't it the realized nutrient uptake rate that saturates, not the maximum?

reviews.assessment: Thought-provoking and enjoyable; offers many suggestions to clarify the narrative and terminology for a general audience.
strengths: does a lot across dimensions, which is a strength
connections to Vinton & Vasseur 2022 support the framework

comments.issue: Population structure is left undefined and readers will interpret it differently.
comments.request: Define population structure.
comments.quote: Depending on your reader, individuals will interpret population structure very differently. Perhaps define.

comments.issue: The statement at L49 lacks references.
comments.request: Add references at L49.
comments.quote: L49: Needs references.

comments.issue: The topic sentence at L55 is too long and obscure.
comments.request: Split it into two sentences.
comments.quote: This reads a bit too long and obscure for a clear topic sentence. Perhaps cut into two sentences?

comments.issue: The critical gaps at L66-73 are not conveyed clearly enough.
comments.request: Make L66-73 clearer and to the point.
comments.quote: Since these two ideas are critical to relaying the novelty, I would recommend making L66-73 much clearer and to the point

comments.issue: Introductory words like 'Importantly,' weaken topic sentences and sentence structure is monotonous.
comments.request: Vary sentence structure and remove such introductory words.
comments.quote: Weirdly, enough “Importantly,” makes the topic sentence less punchy. Perhaps try without and see how it reads?

comments.issue: Introduction paragraphs 2 and 3 overlap and the shift from vital rates to biomass is abrupt.
comments.request: Add signposting to distinguish the paragraphs.
comments.quote: Paragraphs 2 and 3 of the introduction seem to overlap an awful lot in their function.

comments.issue: Vital rates are not clearly defined or related to biomass.
comments.request: Define vital rates and their relation to biomass.
comments.quote: Also, a clear definition of vital rates and how they relate to biomass is also necessary.

comments.issue: Mechanism/mechanistic appears first at L95 without earlier preparation.
comments.request: Integrate mechanistic understanding earlier in the introduction.
comments.quote: this is the first time mechanism/mechanistic is being referred to

comments.issue: The difference between quota and assimilated nutrients is unclear in the methods.
comments.request: Clarify the quota definition in the methods.
comments.quote: From the methods, I am not quite sure what the difference is between quota and assimilated nutrients. Please clarify.

comments.issue: The scope of generalisation (phytoplankton, primary producers, all populations) is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the scale of generalisation.
comments.quote: But perhaps clarify if this is generalizable across phytoplankton, primary producers or all populations. A sense of scale would help.

comments.issue: No table of terms, definitions and values is provided.
comments.request: Add a table of terms, definitions and values.
comments.quote: A table containing terms, definitions and values would be very helpful for the reader.

comments.issue: The direction in which the parameters usually covary is not stated.
comments.request: State the direction of covariation.
comments.quote: L164: In what direction do they usually covary?

comments.issue: Why no sensitivity analysis was performed is not made explicit.
comments.request: Explain the decision not to run a sensitivity analysis.
comments.quote: L192: Please can this be made a bit more explicit. Why not a sensitivity analysis?

comments.issue: No justification for removing transients is given.
comments.request: State the burn-in time used.
comments.quote: L198: Any evidence for the removal of transients? A simple statement about a burn-in time should suffice.

comments.issue: The key sentence at L207 on purposes and novelty comes too late.
comments.request: Convey this point earlier.
comments.quote: This sentence is perhaps the most enlightening and explicit in relaying the purposes and novelty of this work. Any attempt to convey this earlier would be very beneficial.

comments.issue: The introduction does not connect the narrative to r in addition to K.
comments.request: Add a connection to r in the introduction.
comments.quote: Perhaps some connection to r (in addition to K) in the introduction would also be useful.

comments.issue: The paragraph at L245 tries to do too much without signposting.
comments.request: Split the paragraph or add signposting.
comments.quote: The paragraph could benefit from either a split or additional signposting.

comments.issue: The Figure 2 legend is not self-contained.
comments.request: Fill out the Figure 2 legend.
comments.quote: perhaps worth filling out the legend for figure 2 to make it fully self-contained

comments.issue: Quota as 'potential for biomass growth' is defined too late.
comments.request: Relay the quota definition earlier, e.g. in a glossary or table.
comments.quote: So quota represents “potential for biomass growth.” Could this be relayed earlier in the text?

comments.issue: The temporal lag linking rates and their mismatch appears only at L263.
comments.request: Introduce the temporal component earlier and explicitly.
comments.quote: this is the first time (if I am not mistaken) that a temporal component (i.e., a lag) is being connected to the rates and their mismatch

comments.issue: The temporal-scale point at L307 is not generalised beyond this model.
comments.request: Make the temporal-scale problem more general.
comments.quote: I think the problem of temporal scale could be made more general. In other words, time matters.

comments.issue: Two line-level edits: number at L320 may be wrong and 'vial' should be 'via' at L568.
comments.quote: L320: Should this be 500,000?

comments.issue: The rationale at L354 was expected earlier with the previous paragraphs.
comments.request: Move this rationale earlier.
comments.quote: I like this rationale. Although, I was expecting this a bit earlier with the previous three paragraphs.

comments.issue: The text should restate that r and K emerge from the mechanistic system rather than being predefined.
comments.request: Restate that r and K emerge from underlying rates.
comments.quote: I think it is important to restate that r and K are not predefined terms (as in previous attempts to model their interplay) but emerge as a consequence of a mechanistic system of underlying rates.

comments.issue: Figure 3A lacks a y-axis for the TPC and curves are not on the same scale.
comments.request: Add a right-hand y-axis and scale both curves to the same height.
comments.quote: This figure (showing the thermal mismatch between Tr and Tk would be nice if the TPC had a y-axis on the right hand side of the graph and both curves were scaled to the same height.

comments.issue: Figure 4 labels are too small.
comments.request: Make the figure labels bigger.
comments.quote: Perhaps the figure labels could be a bit bigger but otherwise thumbs up.

title: Interactions between temperature and nutrients determine the population dynamics of primary producers

study.system: plant specialised metabolites; synthesis of evolutionary chemodiversity models

editor_summary: Both reviewers enthusiastic; editor asks to make the paper useful to a broader audience, explain model types, redesign figures, and address R2's concerns on quantitative metabolites and alpha/beta diversity.

reviews.assessment: Very enthusiastic; a valuable, timely synthesis that could be more useful to chemical ecologists with an introduction to model types.
strengths: valuable contribution; no other review covers this topic
summarizes key hypotheses in simple, precise and accurate terms
could connect chemical ecologists and modellers

comments.issue: Model types (individual-based, mutation-selection-drift, game-theoretical) are named but never explained, so chemical ecologists without modelling background learn little.
comments.request: Add a short section or text box before Section 3 explaining basic model types and their overlap.
comments.quote: There are many other types of models mentioned in the text that are never defined or explained (e.g. mutation-selection-drift models, game-theoretical models)

comments.issue: Categorisation of models in Section 3 and Figure 1 is hard to follow; grouping by the questions answered would be clearer.
comments.request: Reorganise hypotheses by the questions they answer (fitness benefits, differences among plants, coevolution).
comments.quote: A second major comment is that I struggled some with the categorical organization of models in Section 3 and Figure 1.

comments.issue: Optimal defense theory, a key verbal model for within-plant chemodiversity, is missing from the synthesis.
comments.request: Add optimal defense theory and its quantitative modelling literature (Van Dam; Iwasa).
comments.quote: Finally, a last major comment, what about optimal defense theory? I would consider that one of the most important verbal models for within-plant chemodiversity

comments.issue: The advantage of models for simulating macroevolutionary processes over long timescales is not highlighted.
comments.request: Highlight that models can simulate macroevolutionary processes impossible to test experimentally.
comments.quote: One great advantage of modeling approaches that I think could also be highlighted here is that it allows the simulation of macroevolutionary processes that play out over long time scales

comments.issue: Rationale for grouping AMF with resource-availability hypotheses is unclear; the mechanism (improved resource access) is not made explicit.
comments.request: Make the hypothesized AMF mechanism explicit to justify the grouping.
comments.quote: Presumably, the main hypothesized mechanism here is that AMF fungi increase access to resources? Making that explicit would help connect the dots

comments.issue: The 'mechanistic' category is confusing because all hypotheses in the review are mechanistic.
comments.request: Regroup these models as explanations of fitness benefits of diversity.
comments.quote: I struggled a bit with this grouping of models/hypotheses into a category called “mechanistic”. Aren’t all the hypotheses presented in this review mechanistic?

comments.issue: Description of the screening hypothesis misses its core: mutations raising metabolic capacity are favoured regardless of next-generation effects.
comments.request: Reword to present the screening hypothesis correctly.
comments.quote: As written, I think this misses the core idea of the screening hypothesis, which is just that any given mutation that leads to more complex metabolic capacity at a low enough cost

comments.issue: Reviewer says the Firn and Jones counter-argument does not rely on rapid adaptation as the paper states.
comments.request: Correct the account of the Firn and Jones counter-argument.
comments.quote: I don’t think the Firn and Jones counter-argument rested on any assumption about rapid adaptation. They argue that individual plants that possess more complex metabolic capacity are likely to be favored

comments.issue: Microbial pathogens, a major selective pressure on chemodiversity, are omitted from the ingredients and the paper.
comments.request: Add pathogens to the main text, not only the R code.
comments.quote: One gaping hole in these ingredients (and the paper in general) seems to be microbial pathogens.

comments.issue: Which hypotheses could share a unified modelling framework, what models are needed, and the key challenges remain unclear.
comments.request: Give specifics on combining hypotheses in one framework and the challenges.
comments.quote: it’s not really clear to me which could be combined, what types of models would be necessary, and what the key challenges would be

comments.issue: Reviewer disagrees with abandoning alpha, beta and gamma terminology; these concepts aid cross-field links.
comments.request: Keep alpha/beta/gamma terms and instead state the scale explicitly.
comments.quote: But I would argue it is counter-productive to stop using the terms alpha, beta, and gamma.

comments.issue: Figure symbol system is hard to follow and the figures give no references for models that exist.
comments.request: Add a supplementary table of models and simplify the figures.
comments.quote: the figures tell us that a model exists or doesn’t exist, but doesn’t provide any references for the interested reader who might want to follow up

reviews.assessment: Supportive; an important, useful synthesis, but chemical diversity should be treated as quantitative and alpha/beta terminology retained.
strengths: important contribution to the chemodiversity field
useful overview of hypotheses across levels of organization
highlights gaps and need for more formalized quantitative models
useful for scientists outside chemical ecology

comments.issue: Chemical diversity is discussed only as compound number; compound similarity is largely ignored.
comments.request: Acknowledge compound similarity as a central aspect of chemodiversity.
comments.quote: the authors discuss chemical diversity in the context of compound number, and largely ignore the aspect of compound similarity

comments.issue: Chemical diversity is treated as binary (presence/absence), but induced defence and relative compound abundance are quantitative.
comments.request: Incorporate quantitative/relative compound abundance into the discussion and models.
comments.quote: the authors discuss chemical diversity exclusively as a binary variable, e.g., plants either produce or don’t produce a compound

comments.issue: Evenness is mentioned in a box but not linked to the hypotheses that may explain such patterns.
comments.request: Highlight evenness better in the context of relevant hypotheses.
comments.quote: The authors mention evenness in one of their boxes, but again this could be highlighted better in the context of which hypotheses may explain such patterns.

comments.issue: Reviewer disagrees that alpha/beta/gamma terminology should be avoided; the proposed alternative is not a solution.
comments.request: Improve this section and keep using clearly defined alpha/beta diversity concepts.
comments.quote: In general, I think it there is a big advantage in using clearly defined concepts such as alpha and beta diversity also in chemodiversity

comments.issue: Reference formatting is wrong and a sentence is an incomplete fragment.
comments.request: Fix reference formatting and complete the sentence.
comments.quote: check formatting of the reference. Second sentence seems to be a fragment: ‘a more abstract numerical’

comments.issue: 'Rendered in red' is indirect; the meaning should be stated directly.
comments.request: State 'considered quantitative (coloured red in Fig. 1 and 2)' directly.
comments.quote: instead of ‘rendered in red’, it seems to be more straightforward to directly state what this means

comments.issue: The abbreviation IBM is never defined in the text.
comments.request: Define IBM at first use.
comments.quote: ‘IBM’ is never defined anywhere in the text.

comments.issue: Figure 2 is too complex: legend unhelpful, colours and symbols confusing, nested levels unclear.
comments.request: Redesign Figure 2 more simply, e.g. columns for within/between and rows per level.
comments.quote: This figure is too complex and the figure legend is not very helpful. Even though it states to ‘please refer to Fig.1’

title: The evolution of chemodiversity in plants—From verbal to quantitative models

study.system: red kites (Milvus milvus); GPS tracking and food-supplementation experiment

editor_summary: Reviewers found the experiment and dataset impressive and the contribution potentially valuable; concerns about social behaviour versus social environment, longer-term implications, metric clarity and statistics can be met by additional analyses, discussion and presentation changes.

reviews.assessment: Finds the work interesting, well-written and novel but questions the long-term dispersal claims and clarity of the overlap analyses.
strengths: elegant demonstration of developmental effects on space use

comments.issue: Long-term effects of prospecting movements are stressed although the findings cover only the first months of independence.
comments.request: Provide evidence that prospecting predicts future breeding sites or temper long-term claims.
comments.quote: The authors make a link between the observed prospecting movements and dispersal, stressing the long-term effects of the findings

comments.issue: Choice of segregation, aggregation and clustering metrics is unclear and may be misunderstood.
comments.request: Restructure the analysis or explain the method more clearly to readers.
comments.quote: I couldn’t easily understand the choice of segregation, aggregation, and clustering and may have misunderstood how the analysis was performed.

comments.issue: Clustering peers may be restricted to the same natal group; model structure should use overall density or all individuals.
comments.request: Justify the grouping or include overall density or all tracked individuals as predictor.
comments.quote: If it is the case, I wonder if the authors can justify this decision or consider a different way to structure the models, such as, including a predictor that represents overall density or all tracked individuals.

comments.issue: Early natal dispersal is not properly defined, and dispersal and pre-migration are used interchangeably.
comments.request: Define early natal dispersal and use the terms consistently.
comments.quote: In case the focus is on early natal dispersal, I think a proper definition would help and perhaps in later cases don’t mention both dispersal and pre-migration.

comments.issue: The term "natal legacies" may be unfamiliar and broader than what the study reports.
comments.request: Define natal legacies and its specific use in this work.
comments.quote: Is the term "natal legacies" commonly used? I was not familiar with it, and it seems to encompass a broader phenomenon than what is reported in this work.

comments.issue: Information linking population density to social interactions appears too late, only in the discussion.
comments.request: Move or add this explanatory material to the earlier text.
comments.quote: More information on how population density translates to social interactions may help readers to understand the nature of social interactions in this system.

comments.issue: Unclear whether the buffer areas referred to are the 2 km buffers.
comments.request: Clarify what the buffer areas are.
comments.quote: Are these the 2 km buffer areas?

comments.issue: The number of singletons is not reported.
comments.request: Specify the number of singletons.
comments.quote: Can you specify the number of singletons?

comments.issue: Calculating both daily home range size and step length is redundant, given their correlation and paper length.
comments.request: Consider focusing only on home ranges to reduce complexity.
comments.quote: What is the added value of calculating both daily home range size and step length?

comments.issue: Unclear whether UD overlap belongs to the spatial phenotype or the social environment in the framework used.
comments.request: Clarify the classification of UD overlap within the framework.
comments.quote: However, I wonder whether UD overlap fall under spatial phenotype or social environment.

comments.issue: Consistency of results across years is questionable: Table 3 shows segregation effects that are less clear in Table S7.
comments.request: Address or explain the across-year inconsistency in results.
comments.quote: Are the results truly consistent across years, e.g., in the model (Table 3) there is evidence for segregation between the groups

comments.issue: The term social landscapes appears only once and is not integrated into the paper.
comments.request: Rephrase or integrate the term consistently.
comments.quote: The term social landscapes is mentioned only here, consider rephrasing.

comments.issue: No evidence is given that the mentioned breeding areas are favorable in terms of breeding success.
comments.request: Provide information on breeding success in those areas.
comments.quote: Are the mentioned breeding areas favorable in terms of breeding success?

comments.issue: Nature of interactions, their location (foraging, roosting) and effects of spatial overlap remain unexamined.
comments.request: Relate interactions to foraging or roosting and test effects of overlap.
comments.quote: It raises the question of where interactions take place and what’s their nature. Is it possible to relate the interactions to foraging or where birds roost?

comments.issue: Paragraph central to the argument appears too late, far from the UD overlap introduction.
comments.request: Move parts of the paragraph to where UD overlap is introduced.
comments.quote: If this argument is central to the paper, consider moving parts of this paragraph to where UD overlap is introduced.

comments.issue: The strong conceptualization of results deserves a more central place in the paper.
comments.request: Give this conceptualization a more prominent position.
comments.quote: Great conceptualization of the results. I wonder if it can get a more central place in the work.

reviews.assessment: Fascinating question and impressive dataset, but the social phenotype is defined only by 250m co-occurrence, so claims about social behaviour are unsupported.
strengths: fascinating question about space use and social behaviour
clear, well-written methods and rigorous analyses

comments.issue: Social phenotype is defined by co-occurrence within 250m, which may not represent a meaningful social encounter.
comments.request: Justify the 250m threshold or test co-occurrence against chance expectations.
comments.quote: My biggest concern is in the definition of “social phenotype,” which rests on measuring whenever two individuals cooccur within 250m of one another.

comments.issue: Social phenotype is not separated from spatial phenotype; additional analyses could isolate actual social behaviour.
comments.request: Run analyses distinguishing social from spatial behaviour (attraction/repulsion, 5 m threshold, network comparison).
comments.quote: What if you defined “social phenotype” as being “when you get within sight of another bird, do you get closer or further?”

comments.issue: If only the social environment is shown, the paper must be reframed around that question rather than social behaviour.
comments.request: Reframe the introduction around the social environment question.
comments.quote: you would need to reframe the introduction around the social environment question to highlight its importance

comments.issue: Strength of the reported effects cannot be judged; descriptive information and effect magnitudes are lacking.
comments.request: Report how often individuals interact, distance distributions and effect sizes.
comments.quote: It is interesting that there is a predicted increase in the number of encounters for last hatched individuals who were supplemented, but what does that actually mean?

comments.issue: Bayesian priors are not specified, so results cannot be interpreted.
comments.request: Specify prior assumptions and prior parameters, and justify them.
comments.quote: you should specify what you used for priors, both intuitively (what’s your prior assumption and why) and explicitly (what are the parameters of your prior)

comments.issue: Analysis code is not shared although data will be public.
comments.request: Post the analysis code alongside the data.
comments.quote: While you’re at it, you could share the code itself. Since you’re making the data public, you might as well post the analysis as well.

comments.issue: Logic of the hypothesis is unclear; predictions for low-resource birds should come first.
comments.request: Swap the order to highlight low-resource bird predictions first.
comments.quote: The logic of the hypothesis is a bit unclear, maybe it would make more sense if you swapped the order, highlighting their predictions for low-resource birds first

comments.issue: What "climbed it" means, and how it differs from visiting, is unclear.
comments.request: Explain red kite nesting, how nests were climbed and define the first visit.
comments.quote: It’s unclear to me what “climbed it” means exactly, and especially how that is different from “visiting”.

comments.issue: Temporal and spatial resolution of GPS tracking and scope of data treatments are unclear.
comments.request: State resolution and whether data treatments apply generally or to specific questions.
comments.quote: perhaps you could be slightly more clear in your methods what the temporal (and spatial) resolution of the GPS tracking is

comments.issue: MCP is used without being defined.
comments.request: Define MCP.
comments.quote: MCP should be defined

comments.issue: "Tendentially" is jargon for a weak effect and should be replaced.
comments.request: Say "slightly" instead.
comments.quote: “Tendentially” is a very jargony way to say “there might be a weak effect”. I know that people use this from time to time, but I still don’t like it.

comments.issue: Figures are not informative or compelling and fail to highlight the dataset.
comments.request: Improve the figures to showcase the results better.
comments.quote: I don’t think your figures are that informative or compelling, and I think improving this would dramatically increase the quality of the paper

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 2 lack raw data and could show more information.
comments.request: Add scatterplots, extra panels and a regression plot of the main interaction.
comments.quote: Why not overlay a scatterplot of the raw datapoints? You could probably add some more panels, for example I would love to see the overall network summed across the entire season.

comments.issue: Figure 2b (and maybe 1a) lacks a color key.
comments.request: Add a color key to Figure 2b and possibly Figure 1a.
comments.quote: Figure 2b (and maybe Figure 1a) would probably benefit from a color key like you have for Figure 1b.

comments.issue: Figure 3 map lacks scale bars and direct density comparison; food availability is never depicted.
comments.request: Add scale bars and a fifth panel overlaying group densities and patch quality.
comments.quote: The map figures could use scale bars. I also think it might be more compelling if you had a bigger, fifth panel where you overlayed the densities for each group

reviews.assessment: Likes the framework, creative statistics and findings, but asks for clearer hypotheses and sensitivity analyses for daily networks and ranges.
strengths: interesting findings with potential for Ecology Letters

comments.issue: Hypothesis and objectives are unclear and predictions lack precision and justification.
comments.request: Overhaul the paragraph with a clear hypothesis and justified predictions.
comments.quote: My suggestion would be to overhaul this paragraph and state a clear and precise hypothesis with accompanying predictions that are justified by relevant literature.

comments.issue: Assumption that food-supplemented early-hatched males are most competitive lacks justification or citation.
comments.request: Justify or cite the competition assumption, ideally with behavioural observations.
comments.quote: is it assumed that food supplemented and early hatched males are most competitive? Or are there any behavioural observations of aggression to justify this assumption?

comments.issue: Citations supporting the predictions come from other species and may not be relevant here.
comments.request: Use system-relevant literature to justify the predictions.
comments.quote: I do wonder if these citations from other systems are necessarily relevant here?

comments.issue: The prediction at lines 120-121 is unclear and unjustified.
comments.request: Clarify what the prediction means and justify it.
comments.quote: not really sure what this prediction means and the justification

comments.issue: 293 daily networks may be sparse snapshots; number of edges per network is unknown.
comments.request: Report edge counts and justify whether this maximizes usable data.
comments.quote: My concern here is that these networks are just snap shots and the data going into each network might be sparse. How many edges are present in each network?

comments.issue: Daily home ranges from as few as 5-12 relocations are not meaningful and are not really home ranges.
comments.request: Justify or rename daily ranges and address the small input sample.
comments.quote: I’m also not convinced that a daily home range is really meaningful

comments.issue: Short temporal window may drive results; results at weekly or monthly scales untested.
comments.request: Generate weekly/monthly ranges and networks and compare them with daily results.
comments.quote: the solution is to generate ranges (and networks) for weeks/months and compare these to the daily ranges/networks to ensure the short time scale of data inclusion isn’t driving the results

comments.issue: Error from daily range estimation propagates into overlap estimation but is not accounted for.
comments.request: Account for error propagation from range estimation into overlap analysis.
comments.quote: the potential for error in step 1 (estimate daily ranges) is carried forward into step 2 (estimate overlap), but not accounted for.

comments.issue: The phrase "home range information" is imprecise.
comments.request: Use a more precise term.
comments.quote: what is “home range information”? perhaps more precision is needed here.

comments.issue: Independence is not defined.
comments.request: Define independence.
comments.quote: what is independence?
