comments.request: Strengthen the theoretical justification.
comments.quote: The theoretical justification for the study is weakly developed in such a way that it is unclear where the uncertainty lies.

comments.issue: Inclusion of demographic stochasticity and its model complexity is not justified.
comments.request: Justify including demographic stochasticity.
comments.quote: it is hard to imagine why we might need to include the model complexity that accompanies demographic stochasticity

comments.issue: Coexistence pitch falls flat: the introduction discusses a single species, so what coexists with what is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what is coexisting and with what.
comments.quote: The pitch that the authors are studying species coexistence falls slat because the authors talk in the introduction almost exclusively about a single species.

comments.issue: Deterministic and individual-based models differ in many ways, confounding the source of outcome differences.
comments.request: Isolate the effect of demographic stochasticity.
comments.quote: There are many differences between the deterministic model and the individual-based model (IBM) that make it difficult to understand the causative agent of the differences in model outcomes.

comments.issue: Competition mechanism in the model is unclear; whether food can be depleted is unknown.
comments.request: Explain the competition mechanism in the model.
comments.quote: It's not clear how competition works in the model, either deterministically or in the IBM. Can the food source be depleted in the model?

comments.issue: Randomly drawing founding populations is unrealistic; within-host and colonization dynamics should be modelled jointly.
comments.request: Model within-host and colonization dynamics jointly.
comments.quote: I find the modeling choice to randomly draw founding populations to be an unrealistic one.

comments.issue: The model is poorly described and it is hard to see what was done and which parameters matter.
comments.request: Describe the model more clearly.
comments.quote: The model is poorly described and it makes it difficult to understand what is done and modeling parameter are relevant to the question of plasticity and coexistence.

comments.issue: Parameter f and the summation term A_i in Eqn 1 are undefined.
comments.request: Define f and A_i in the equations.
comments.quote: The parameter f is not defined, and there summations in the second and third equations are over A\_i, which is undefined.

comments.issue: Letter x denotes several different objects (strain type, spatial position, brood size), confusing readers.
comments.request: Use distinct notation for distinct objects.
comments.quote: The letter x is used as notation for multiple, different objects in the model at different points in the paper.

comments.issue: Figure captions for figures 2 and 3 have been switched.
comments.request: Fix the switched figure captions.
comments.quote: It appears the figure captions for fig 2 and fig 3 have been switched.

comments.issue: Figure 6 strain colours are undefined and one strain's failure to survive alone needs explanation.
comments.request: Clarify colours and the strain failure in Fig. 6.
comments.quote: Which strains are red and which are blue in each figure? And why does one strain fail to survive alone in many simulations of A-C in the E. coli food treatment?

title: The role of plasticity and stochasticity in coexistence

study.system: species interaction networks; Nature's Contributions to People framework

editor_summary: Impressed with the clarity and elegance of the novel framework; reviewers want improved clarity and Reviewer 1 worries about overextending beyond the framework's defined scope.

reviews.assessment: Novel and valuable combination of network theory with the NCP cascade model; minor requests to define terms and fix an unrealistic example.
strengths: novel approach linking NCPs to species interaction networks
well written and straightforward to follow

comments.issue: The term 'antagonistic interaction' is undefined and used differently across network fields.
comments.request: Define antagonistic interaction in the Figure 1 legend.
comments.quote: Please define this term in the legend as different network fields probably use this term in different ways

comments.issue: What 'effective diversity' measures is not stated in the legends of Figures 2 and 3.
comments.request: State exactly what effective diversity means in the figure legends.
comments.quote: it would be worth stating exactly what is meant by effective diversity in the figure legends in Fig 2 and 3

comments.issue: The generalist butterfly pollination example is unrealistic; butterflies are poor pollinators.
comments.request: Change the example to a generalist fly.
comments.quote: there are very few cases (in fact I can’t think of a single one) where a generalist butterfly pollinates most crops

comments.issue: The distinction between food and feed is subtle and may be lost on readers.
comments.request: Rewrite the food versus feed passage to make the difference clear.
comments.quote: What is the difference between food and feed? For human versus animal consumption I suspect but I’d rewrite this

reviews.assessment: Very interesting, clearly presented framework linking NCPs to interaction networks; asks to reconsider the change framing and the speculative large-scale section.
strengths: interesting contribution connecting NCPs with ecological theory

comments.issue: Objectives refer to changes in NCP demand, but the manuscript presents scenarios, not changes; time is missing as a variable.
comments.request: Reframe the objectives from changes to scenarios.
comments.quote: In my opinion the manuscript does not address changes but rather different scenarios and the concept of change in objectives may be a bit misleading.

comments.issue: The large-scale analysis of NCP supply is speculative and lacks spatial or scale aspects, adding little value.
comments.request: Revise or drop the speculative large-scale section.
comments.quote: I think the last section of the ms (Large-scale analysis of NCP supply) is a bit speculative since the proposal does not include spatial or scale aspects

comments.issue: The separation between NCP regulators and providers of supporting-environment organisms is hard to understand.
comments.request: Describe and discuss this subsystem and its links to NCP regulators and providers.
comments.quote: It is also difficult for me to understand the separation between NCP regulators and providers of the organisms that make up the supporting environment.

title: A quantitative framework for identifying the role of individual species in Nature's Contributions to People

study.system: pumpkin toadlets and skin bacteria; drought field monitoring

editor_summary: Editor stresses that outstanding questions remain about the statistical analyses, especially the teleconnection analyses, whose lack of clarity made reviewers question the strength of evidence for the main conclusions.

reviews.assessment: Novel, rigorous and well-written study that warrants publication; the concerns are relatively minor and mostly about clarity of the teleconnection analyses.

comments.issue: High-resolution temperature data were collected but not used in the statistical models.
comments.request: Include temperature in the models or state that it was not a significant predictor.
comments.quote: I was confused that they collected high-resolution (every 6 hours at each site) temperature data but don’t seem to have included temperature variables in any of their statistical models.

comments.issue: Teleconnection analysis descriptions are hard to decipher for a broad ecological readership.
comments.request: Rewrite the teleconnection sections accessibly.
comments.quote: I think the authors should rewrite descriptions of teleconnection analyses to try to speak to a broader ecological readership.

comments.issue: 'Predicted' in the abstract implies an a priori quantitative prediction, but the finding is a posteriori.
comments.request: Replace with 'affected' or 'was an indirect predictor of'.
comments.quote: Using ‘predicted’ in this context implied to me (on my first read at least) an a priori quantitative prediction.

comments.issue: The abstract's final teleconnection sentence will be unfamiliar to most readers.
comments.request: Rephrase to clarify the purpose of teleconnection analysis.
comments.quote: I suspect that most readers, like myself, will be unfamiliar with teleconnection analysis.

comments.issue: 'Stochastic' misdescribes the AKP hypothesis; 'destabilizing' would be a better term.
comments.request: Reconsider the terminology.
comments.quote: Stochastic implies that there is random variation involved, but there’s basically always random variation involved so that didn’t mean much to me.

comments.issue: The dysbiosis statement on P4 is clearer than the paragraph opening; the paragraph could start with it.
comments.request: Restructure the paragraph as suggested.
comments.quote: I suggest starting the paragraph with a sentence along these lines, and then following up with the other info.

comments.issue: The question and purpose of the teleconnection analysis are never clearly stated.
comments.request: State the question and explain the method for non-specialists.
comments.quote: At this point, I would have appreciated a clearer statement of the question to be addressed via telekinection analysis

comments.issue: Acronyms (LDA, LEfSe) are not defined and the LDA score is not described.
comments.request: Define the acronyms and describe the LDA score.
comments.quote: Acronyms should be defined, ideally both in the main text and in figure legends.

comments.issue: Why both Kruskal-Wallis and Wilcoxon tests are used for each sOTU is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the use of both tests.
comments.quote: Why is it necessary to use both a Kruskal-Wallace test and a Wilcoxon test for each sOTU?

comments.issue: The response/predictor wording on P12 is confusing; the independent variables are unstated.
comments.request: Fix the response/predictor terminology.
comments.quote: I’m confused. The previous sentence made it sound like “alpha diversity metrics” were your response (dependent) variables for these models. What are your independent variables?

comments.issue: The assumption that isolates absent from the Bd-inhibition database are non-inhibitory needs discussion.
comments.request: Discuss this assumption.
comments.quote: The authors seem to assume that if isolates are not found in the Bd-inhibition database, that this means they probably aren’t inhibitory.

comments.issue: Which test supports 'significantly more anti-Bd sOTUs' and what comparison is being made is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the test and the comparison.
comments.quote: Was this the Fisher exact test mentioned in the Methods section? Does that mean this is just a test of whether 0/5 is significantly different from 5/7?

comments.issue: 'Plummeted' implies Bd caused the diversity decline, but the direction may be bidirectional.
comments.request: Use non-directional wording.
comments.quote: This makes the relationship sound directional, i.e., high Bd load caused the decrease in microbiome diversity. The opposite effect seems equally plausible to me, or a bidirectional effect.

comments.issue: The Jaccard-Bd relationship is described causally although Fig. 5 suggests bidirectionality.
comments.request: Soften the causal language.
comments.quote: Again, this sounds like a conclusion about causal direction, but the direction appears to be bidirectional in Fig 5.

comments.issue: 'Post-drought period' should explicitly be identified as February.
comments.request: State the month explicitly.
comments.quote: I assume this means February, based on Fig 4, but it would be helpful to say so more explicitly.

comments.issue: Rainfall flux, climate anomaly data and their positive correlations are unexplained; implications for drought threat are unclear.
comments.request: Explain these terms and their implications.
comments.quote: What exactly does “climate anomaly data stemming from land use changes” mean exactly, and what does it mean that these data have positive correlations (with each other?) that spatially overlap with a deforested area?

comments.issue: The northern-wind correlation's implications for drought threat and wind trends are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning and the trends.
comments.quote: One fairly clear statement was about the positive correlation between northern winds and local rainfall, but even here it’s not clear to me what this means for the threat of drought in this area.

comments.issue: The 'no anti-Bd bacteria' statement ignores untested, potentially inhibitory sOTUs.
comments.request: Qualify the statement as known anti-Bd bacteria.
comments.quote: It still seems possible to me that some of the enriched sOTUs are inhibitory but haven’t been tested yet, and thus haven’t shown up in the database.

comments.issue: The discussion's deforestation-drought conclusion is not supported by a clear Results statement.
comments.request: Add a clear Results statement or temper the claim.
comments.quote: If so, that’s an interesting result. However, this was unclear to me in trying to follow this part of the Results section.

reviews.assessment: Ambitious, coherent and largely convincing study; three analytical concerns about Jaccard, AKP generality and especially NMDS scores need clarification.

comments.issue: Jaccard ignores abundance and is strongly affected by richness, possibly underestimating dispersion.
comments.request: Justify the choice of Jaccard.
comments.quote: some of the most interesting results about microbiome changes in this paper are about dramatic differences in abundance, which Jaccard of course ignores

comments.issue: The AKP stress-dispersion prediction is opposite to non-microbiome community ecology; this contrast merits discussion.
comments.request: Discuss this contrast for a broad ecological audience.
comments.quote: this is the opposite of what we tend to see in non-microbiome community ecology--in plants and animals, usually (but not always) stressors lead to convergence, not dispersion

comments.issue: NMDS Axis 1 scores are arbitrary, unitless and non-reproducible, so their use in the SEM with a signed slope is unjustified.
comments.request: Clarify how NMDS scores were used in the SEM or revise the analysis.
comments.quote: As I'm sure the authors know, NMDS axes have no units and are therefore uninterpretable. They are also arbitrary and non-reproducible, because each NMDS run can and often does produce different NMDS scores for each datapoint.

reviews.assessment: Well-written study with clear figures, but the title's claim that microbiome disturbance predicts disease is oversold and several analyses need strengthening.

comments.issue: The title and main claim that microbiome disturbance predicts infection and disease are oversold given the data.
comments.request: Temper the claim and the title.
comments.quote: I think that the authors are overselling the idea that microbiome disturbance predicts infection and disease (starting with the title) without having the data to support it

comments.issue: Low R² of the Jaccard analyses may reflect violation of the PERMANOVA homogeneity-of-variance assumption.
comments.request: Check the homogeneity assumption.
comments.quote: the R2 were low, and this could be a technical bias as one of the core assumptions of the PERMANOVAs is homogeneity of the variances

comments.issue: The Bd load-alpha diversity relationship is driven by five dead or dying individuals.
comments.request: Test the influence of these points.
comments.quote: The relationship between Bd load and alpha diversity is driven by 5 points of dead/dying individuals (Page 16, Fig. 3).

comments.issue: The mechanism by which microbiomes become more variable is weak or unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism.
comments.quote: In addition, the mechanism by which microbiomes become more variable is weak or barely explained.

comments.issue: No data on infection intensity over time, frog abundance or age structure are integrated.
comments.request: Integrate these lines of evidence.
comments.quote: For example, the authors do not show any data on infection intensity over time, the changes in frog abundance or age structure of the population, which all contribute to disease dynamics.

comments.issue: No consistent increase in infection after dry months; data may not be robust enough to detect thresholds.
comments.request: Test whether infection rises after dry months.
comments.quote: Is there a consistent increase in infection right after dry months? If so, I would have expected increased infections in the months of June and July when the patterns of rainfall are the lowest (Fig. 1).

comments.issue: Rationale for the 1-month rainfall lag is missing; other lags are not explored.
comments.request: Run a sensitivity analysis across 1-month, 7-day and 3-day lags.
comments.quote: The authors should also expand on why “1-month lagged rainfall” was chosen as a variable. Exploring different times (e.g., 1 month, 7 days, 3 days) as part of a sensitivity analysis might be helpful

comments.issue: Phylogenetic diversity of the microbiomes is not examined; unclear whether specific bacterial groups are lost.
comments.request: Analyse phylogenetic diversity and which taxa are lost.
comments.quote: What about phylogenetic diversity of the microbiomes? Are frogs losing specific groups of bacteria or is it completely random?

comments.issue: Anti-Bd OTUs are only assigned at genus level and 99% similarity; interpretation needs caveats.
comments.request: Discuss caveats and show how these taxa change over time.
comments.quote: Because these anti-Bd OTUs are only taxonomically assigned at the genus level, and at 99% sequence similarity, I think the authors should be more careful about the interpretation of these results or at least discuss potential caveats.

comments.issue: Anti-Bd OTU relationship to Bd loads is not shown.
comments.request: Add it as an additional panel on Figure 3.
comments.quote: I think it would be appropriate to show how anti-Bd OTUs are related to Bd loads as an additional panel on Figure 3.

comments.issue: The teleconnection analysis does not fit a single-location study.
comments.request: Reframe or link it to the distribution of reported declines.
comments.quote: The teleconnection analysis is interesting; however, it does not fit well in this paper.

comments.issue: Figure 1 could be moved to supplementary materials.
comments.request: Move Figure 1 to the supplement.
comments.quote: Page 9 (51-54). Figure 1 could be move to supplementary materials.

comments.issue: Which isolate was used as the standard curve is not stated.
comments.request: Provide this information.
comments.quote: Page 10 (8). Could you provide information on which isolate was used as standard curve?

comments.issue: PCR pooling method is underexplained; exact pooled amounts matter for read numbers.
comments.request: Describe the pooled PCR amounts.
comments.quote: Please expand on this part of the method as it can have important downstream effects in terms of the number of reads.

comments.issue: 1300 reads per sample is low and decontamination is done after rarefaction.
comments.request: Do decontamination before rarefaction.
comments.quote: 1300 reads per sample seems like a low number. Decontamination should be done before rarefaction.

comments.issue: Model selection is performed despite explicit alpha-diversity hypotheses.
comments.request: Justify the model selection.
comments.quote: I’m not sure why model selection was performed if there are explicit hypotheses about alpha diversity.

comments.issue: Rationale for the SEM and the Bd load by rainfall deficit interaction is missing.
comments.request: Provide the rationale.
comments.quote: Please provide a rationale for the structural equation models and the interaction term between Bd load and rainfall deficit.

comments.issue: Microbiome dispersion and composition may be redundant in the SEM.
comments.request: Check for redundancy.
comments.quote: Looking at the SEM boxes, I wonder if microbiome dispersion and composition are redundant in the analysis.

comments.issue: February had peak rainfall while the drought was in December; the statement is only partly true.
comments.request: Correct or qualify the statement.
comments.quote: This statement is partly true, because based on Figs. 1&4, the month of February had a peak in rainfall activity, whereas the drought was reported in the month of December.

title: Skin microbiome disturbance linked to drought‐associated amphibian disease

study.system: global bird assemblages; traits, phylogeny, IUCN data

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers found the study very interesting but questions the simplistic questions/title and the single extinction scenario that removes all threatened species; a substantially revised resubmission would be required.

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the novel concept and robust test, asking for presentation tightening and additional extinction, trait and raw-metric analyses.
strengths: robust test of a novel concept

comments.issue: Paragraphs are too long and sentences could be tightened; presentation could be sharper.
comments.request: Split long paragraphs and shorten wordy sentences.
comments.quote: Some paragraphs are quite long (split them?), and there is potential to shorten some sentences, remove wasted words

comments.issue: Non-natives and natives are not compared within spatially constrained regions; national-level inference may hide biome-level losses.
comments.request: Compare (dis)similarity within spatially constrained groups.
comments.quote: Without spatially constraining the inference, one could erroneously conclude that there has been a retention/loss, when in fact there was a loss in one biome and a gain in another

comments.issue: Extinction modelling only uses the combined threatened-species scenario; threat-category scenarios should be run iteratively.
comments.request: Run CR, CR+EN and CR+EN+VU extinction scenarios.
comments.quote: I would like to see the extinction modelling conducted iteratively as well as the combined analysis already conducted.

comments.issue: Functional traits focus on demography-related traits; diet, a key trait, is missing.
comments.request: Incorporate bird diets, e.g. from EltonTraits.
comments.quote: Functional traits have focused mainly on those relevant to demography, but a key trait is related to diet.

comments.issue: Standardized effect sizes control for richness and hide whether total FRic/PRic is retained, which matters for compensation.
comments.request: Show raw change metrics and revise the main text.
comments.quote: Please show the raw change metrics too and revise main text accordingly.

comments.issue: Figure 3 should show how total FRic/PRic changes after extinctions and non-native arrivals.
comments.request: Include total FRic/PRic changes and revise the text.
comments.quote: I think how the total amount of FRic or PRic changes (ie is retained, lower or higher after extinctions + non-native arrivals) is of interest.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and important topic, but novelty over earlier work is doubted and the extinction scenarios and spatial resolution are seriously flawed.

comments.issue: Topic has been addressed by several earlier papers, often on birds with similar data; novelty is unconvincing.
comments.request: Clarify what is fundamentally new relative to existing studies.
comments.quote: I am not convinced that the paper shows fundamental results not seen as good or better elsewhere.

comments.issue: Using present-day assemblages ignores already extinct species, making them a wrong baseline for biodiversity loss.
comments.request: Adopt a pre-extinction baseline (e.g. 1500 AD) including historical extinctions.
comments.quote: I find it conceptually wrong to ignore previous loss. A paper focusing on biodiversity loss cannot meaningfully use now as a starting point.

comments.issue: Scenario assumes every threatened species goes extinct while no non-threatened species does, which is unrealistic.
comments.request: Use extinction probabilities based on threat categories.
comments.quote: It seems hard to conceive a scenario where all threatened species goes extinct but not a single non-threatened species goes extinct.

comments.issue: Range declines and local extinctions of species surviving elsewhere are ignored; continental regions make this invalid.
comments.request: Estimate local extirpations, e.g. from national red lists.
comments.quote: I cannot find any logical scenario where all globally threatened species goes extinct but where there is not a single region al extinction of a species surviving elsewhere.

comments.issue: Calling simple removal of all threatened species a 'simulation' is inaccurate.
comments.request: Rephrase or justify the simulation terminology.
comments.quote: it seems inaccurate to call the current analyses a simulation (lines 116-118).

comments.issue: National spatial resolution is too coarse; biogeographic units such as botanical countries would be better.
comments.request: Improve spatial resolution using botanical countries with GAVIA.
comments.quote: The authors need to work on improving the spatial resolution. A full proper spatial resolution is not possible due to lack of polygon data

comments.issue: Title is too absolute and untrue at face value.
comments.request: Change the title to something more accurate.
comments.quote: The title is problematic. Taken at face value it is not true because at some point it will

comments.issue: The newer AVONET bird trait database should be used instead of Amniote.
comments.request: Consider using AVONET instead of Amniote traits.
comments.quote: I think the authors should consider relying on the newer bird data base AVONET

comments.issue: Missing species appear to be added basally within genera, making them unjustifiably distinct.
comments.request: Add missing species randomly within genus or rewrite the section.
comments.quote: Missing species needs to be added randomly within the genus rather than basal as they appear to be doing

comments.issue: Imputing missing values on PCA scores rather than raw traits is odd and unjustified.
comments.request: Justify this choice or impute raw trait values.
comments.quote: I find it odd that the missing values are inferred for the PCAs rather than for the raw values?

comments.issue: AVONET covers multiple taxonomies and could allow a larger species subset.
comments.request: Consider AVONET to include more species.
comments.quote: if the authors relied on that they would likely be able to use a larger subset of bird species

comments.issue: Regions are not independent units, so this analysis is invalid without accounting for spatial autocorrelation.
comments.request: Use spatial regression or show residuals lack autocorrelation.
comments.quote: Since the regions are not independent units this part does not seem valid.

comments.issue: How continents were defined for the analysis is never stated.
comments.request: Define continents in the text.
comments.quote: the authors need to define how they define continents

comments.issue: 'Global functional diversity loss' is not meaningfully defined and may mean functional homogenization.
comments.request: Define the term or switch to functional homogenization.
comments.quote: The authors here refer to global function diversity loss (which I am not sure is meaningfully defined)

comments.issue: 'Syndromes' is used oddly.
comments.quote: Line 409. Very weird use of the word syndromes.

comments.issue: Figure reference to New Zealand data in figure S3 cannot be understood; no such data appear there.
comments.request: Fix the figure referencing.
comments.quote: I do not understand this figure referencing. No explicit data on New Zealand is present in figure S3.

comments.issue: Text confuses taxonomic opinion with missing information; the taxonomy followed is never stated.
comments.request: State the taxonomic treatment and distinguish opinion from missing data.
comments.quote: The authors seem so mix up differences in taxonomic opinion with missing information.

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic and supportive, but cannot accept the 'compensation' framing and asks for better metrics, trait data and many clarifications.

comments.issue: The paper should lead with the joint extinction-plus-introduction scenario rather than the individual components.
comments.request: Restructure results and discussion around scenario 3.
comments.quote: I think in terms of structure I would start and focus on the joint results (scenario 3), since this is the most likely story.

comments.issue: Equating metric similarity with full 'compensation' is unacceptable; species cannot fully replace each other's functions.
comments.request: Restrict compensation wording to the trait functions measured.
comments.quote: Just because some functional metrics might give the same values doesn’t mean the species replace other species in highly complex world of relationships and ecosystem functions.

comments.issue: Richness metrics cannot capture niche position or similarity; distinctiveness/divergence measures are more appropriate.
comments.request: Consider divergence/distinctiveness metrics and clarify the metric choices.
comments.quote: Moreover, why richness? Since when does a metric capturing an amount describing properly a niche position and its similarity with other niches?

comments.issue: Amniote morphological traits poorly capture functional niches; AVONET traits would be better, or justify not using them.
comments.request: Use AVONET traits or justify neglecting them.
comments.quote: more morphological charaters like in the Avonet database support a better definition of niches

comments.issue: Phylogenetic uncertainty is tested extensively but the trait approach's robustness is not.
comments.request: Test the trait approach, e.g. with an AVONET test dataset.
comments.quote: Be as similar thorough with traits. Maybe you can run a test data set and convince me here (and the readers) that your trait approach would not change with Avonet data.

comments.issue: Introduction does not specify which taxa the arguments and cited studies refer to.
comments.request: Focus on bird knowledge and name taxa for non-bird studies.
comments.quote: Make sure to mention taxa group your text/arguments refer to.

comments.issue: The research gap is justified by underciting existing extinction/extirpation work such as Daru.
comments.request: Cite existing extinction studies and clarify which extinctions are meant.
comments.quote: Cite & acknowledge properly the work out there using extinctions and clarify what extinctions you refer to.

comments.issue: Plant and fish studies are cited in a bird paper despite ample bird research (e.g. Sayol, Sol).
comments.request: Cite bird studies directly.
comments.quote: citing plant and fish studies in a bird focused study doesn’t make sense if there is enough bird research

comments.issue: A 13-year-old study is described as recent.
comments.request: Correct the recency claim.
comments.quote: 13 years old is anything else than “recent”.

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks scenario numbers.
comments.request: Add scenario numbers to Figure 1.
comments.quote: What scenarios? No scenario numbers in Fig 1?!

comments.issue: Global IUCN status is used for local assemblages without justification; regional red lists may be more appropriate.
comments.request: Justify global threat status or use regional red lists.
comments.quote: Please justify the use of a global red list if you look at local assemblages?

comments.issue: The database used is not cited or locatable.
comments.request: Cite the database properly.
comments.quote: Where can someone find this database? Please cite it properly here.

comments.issue: Number of regions retained and handling of mismatched or island distributions are unreported.
comments.request: Report region counts and data-coding decisions.
comments.quote: How many regions you ended up with? What happened with regions where Gavia and ICUN are in full alignment.

comments.issue: How many traits and species required imputation is unclear; a Venn diagram or table would help.
comments.request: Report imputation counts and add a Venn diagram or table.
comments.quote: For how many traits and species you had to run the imputation? Make a venn diagram or a table or so

comments.issue: Whether species with only one trait remain, and what NRMSE means ecologically, is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the imputation extent and error meaning.
comments.quote: Does it mean you have species left in your data set, which had only one trait? And did you imputed the other seven traits then?

comments.issue: The GBIF taxonomy workflow (backbones, recognized names, packages, resolution counts) is not reproducible.
comments.request: Describe the taxonomy workflow and report resolution counts.
comments.quote: With this information I would not be able at all to reproduce what you did.

comments.issue: Whether the 8,718 species with functional information include aliens is unclear; a flow chart would help.
comments.request: Clarify dataset composition with a flow chart or table.
comments.quote: Does the 8.718 species with functional information include aliens? maybe a little flow chart with original data set size and main steps and final data set size would help

comments.issue: Imputation reliability is not validated against in-situ measured traits.
comments.request: Test imputation against measured trait values.
comments.quote: if you test the reliability of your imputation, I would test it with in situ measured data itself

comments.issue: Almost 20% of alien and threatened species are dropped; identity and spatial/phylogenetic bias are unreported.
comments.request: List dropped species and test for biases.
comments.quote: Is there a spatial or phylogenetic bias in those species not in the final data set?

comments.issue: PD is likely driven by species richness and may not reflect phylogenetic divergence.
comments.request: Use richness-independent measures or PD~SR residuals, or explain the metric.
comments.quote: Please convince me that this is not 99% driven by species richness.

comments.issue: Jaccard index is biased by different assemblage sizes.
comments.request: Address the assemblage-size bias.
comments.quote: The Jaccard index is affected by different assemblage sizes. How do you deal with this bias?

comments.issue: Differences in recording effort between alien and threatened species across regions are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss recording-effort differences.
comments.quote: how generally do you see (discuss it) the differences in recording effort for alien and threatened species in the different regions?

comments.issue: What 'simulated' assemblages are and their size relative to real communities is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the simulation and match real community sizes.
comments.quote: This is not 100% clear to me. The simulated assemblages are (I guess) random communities drawn from the regional species pool.

comments.issue: Null model randomizes introductions only; threatened-species assignment is not randomized.
comments.request: Add a null model randomizing which species are threatened.
comments.quote: But why isn’T(and again sorry if I’m mistaken, then you have write clearer ;O) the Null model when adding threatened species letting random species being threatened?

comments.issue: Species richness of the random assemblages is unspecified; it should match the observed distribution.
comments.request: Match null richness to the observed frequency distribution.
comments.quote: Assemblages with which species richness? Maybe use the same richness frequency distribution or so.

comments.issue: 'Identical' is too strong; assemblages can only be highly similar.
comments.request: Replace 'identical' with 'highly similar'.
comments.quote: Don’t use “identical” . It cannot be for both aspects.

comments.issue: The first results paragraph explains how to read figures and belongs in methods.
comments.request: Move it to methods and start with real results.
comments.quote: I would move this 1st para into methods. Start the results with the real results and not the way how the figures needs to be read

title: recolorize: An R package for flexible colour segmentation of biological images

study.system: ant plants (Rubiaceae epiphytes); phylogenetic comparative models

reviews.assessment: Excited by the question and dataset but concerned about sparse methods, inflated type 1 error and overinterpretation of macroevolutionary patterns.
strengths: impressive, valuable trait dataset and tree

comments.issue: How mutualism traits 1-4 were measured is not described, making the measurements hard to replicate.
comments.request: Describe where, how and with which tools the traits were measured.
comments.quote: How were mutualism traits 1-4 (lines 229-233) measured? It would be difficult for someone to replicate the measuring of these traits

comments.issue: Molecular methods are not detailed; whether new specimens were sequenced and whether protocols follow Chomicki & Renner 2017 is unclear.
comments.request: Describe DNA extraction, amplification, primers and sequencing.
comments.quote: More information on the molecular methods would be useful under “taxon dataset.” Did the authors sequence new specimens?

comments.issue: The number of MCMC chains run is not reported.
comments.request: Report how many MCMC chains were run.
comments.quote: key component of the molecular methods. - How many MCMC chains were run?

comments.issue: It is unclear which traits the 18 literature citations code and which citation applies to which trait.
comments.request: Map each citation to the traits it codes.
comments.quote: Line 235 states “These traits were coded based on the literature” with a large list of citations. Which traits exactly does “these” refer to?

comments.issue: Stem and leaf sampling details (plant part, number of stems/leaves, area measurement method) are missing.
comments.request: Describe stem and leaf sampling and area measurement.
comments.quote: What part of the stem was chosen for stem cross section area? Which part of the plant was the stem taken from?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether minimum, maximum or mean values were used for traits taken from sources.
comments.request: State which summary statistic was used.
comments.quote: In cases where trait data was used from sources (e.g., corolla or petiole length), was reported minimum, maximum, or mean used?

comments.issue: How the three sets of climate residuals entered the downstream models is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the residual sets were incorporated into each model.
comments.quote: the specifics of how the three sets of residuals (one for PCA 1, PCA2, and PCA3) incorporated into the downstream analyses is unclear

comments.issue: Type 1 error inflation is not accounted for, so the robustness of the differences is unclear.
comments.request: Account for hidden states, e.g. with the HOUWIE method.
comments.quote: the authors do not account for known type 1 error rate inflating issues in this approach, making it difficult to know whether the differences found in the paper are robust

comments.issue: Significance is discussed but no method for assessing it is described.
comments.request: Add a significance criterion or use effect sizes and confidence intervals instead.
comments.quote: The results section of the paper refers to “significant” or “non-significant” differences in parameter estimates several times (e.g., line 359), but no mechanism for assessing significance is described in the methods.

comments.issue: Macroevolutionary patterns are conflated with processes; 'mutualisms drive' claims ignore alternatives such as pleiotropy.
comments.request: Rephrase as patterns consistent with mutualism driving trait evolution.
comments.quote: the authors make the “correlation does not equal causation” mistake, conflating macroevolutionary patterns of trait evolution with specific processes that may or may not have generated these patterns

comments.issue: OU model parameters are linked one-to-one to microevolutionary processes such as selection.
comments.request: Add nuance on what OU models can and cannot show.
comments.quote: parameters in OU models cannot be linked in a one-to-one fashion to specific microevolutionary processes such as selection

comments.issue: The homostyly result is buried in the supplement with no research question or methods.
comments.request: Integrate the analysis fully into the paper or remove it.
comments.quote: This is an interesting result but it is buried in the supplement. This research question was never raised in the introduction

comments.issue: Results outside the parameter range -10 to 10 are excluded from plots although model averaging could down weight them.
comments.request: Include these results in the plots.
comments.quote: I would argue that these should be included as they are part of the results, as they should be down weighted by the model averaging if they do not fit the data well.

comments.issue: No justification is given for choosing these particular non-mutualistic traits.
comments.request: Provide an a priori justification for the trait selection.
comments.quote: Why were these non-mutualistic traits chosen specifically? Is there a justification for selecting these traits, like an a priori reason

comments.issue: The results section reviews methods (e.g. ancestral state estimation) rather than presenting results.
comments.request: Streamline the text to Ecology Letters format.
comments.quote: the results section contains a lot of review of the methods (e.g., the “Ancestral state estimations of discrete mutualistic traits” section is just methods review)

comments.issue: "Non-mutualistic" is inaccurate for traits such as corolla length that are mutualistic with pollinators.
comments.request: Use a label such as "not ant-associated" instead.
comments.quote: Consider using something like “not ant-associated” instead of “non-mutualistic” for the continuous traits, as at least one of these (corolla length) is arguably mutualistic

comments.issue: Allometry is invoked as a mechanism but is poorly explained; pleiotropy and developmental constraints are not discussed.
comments.request: Expand on allometry, pleiotropy and developmental constraints.
comments.quote: Allometry is mentioned several times as a reason that the evolution of mutualistic and non-mutualistic traits are tied, but the concept isn’t very well explained or justified.

comments.issue: The second goal is unclear because "mutualistic strategies" are not yet defined at that point.
comments.request: Clarify the goal and define mutualistic strategies.
comments.quote: The second goal outlined in the introduction (line 180) is difficult to interpret because it is not yet clear what “mutualistic strategies” are this point in the paper

comments.issue: WorldClim data are coarse climate data and cannot represent microclimate.
comments.request: Reword to refer to climate rather than microclimate.
comments.quote: Line 328 refers to “microclimate” but WorldClim data represent a course measurement of climate, I would argue you cannot get microclimate data from WorldClim.

comments.issue: The phrase "other non-mutualistic traits" for discrete traits conflicts with the continuous-trait terminology.
comments.request: Use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: Line 358 uses the phrase “other non-mutualistic traits”, presumably to describe discrete traits not associated with mutualism. This is confusing given the continuous “non-mutualistic” trait language

comments.issue: Evolutionary rates are described as quantifying "impact", but stabilizing selection is also an impact.
comments.request: Adjust the wording about impact on evolution.
comments.quote: Evolutionary rates are not necessarily a quantification of the “impact” on evolution, as stabilizing selection does not indicate lower impact on evolution per se.

comments.issue: Environmental filtering and eco-evolutionary feedbacks are speculative and would need much more data.
comments.request: Temper or remove these speculations.
comments.quote: Line 417 – 419 about environmental filtering and eco-evolutionary feedbacks feel like a big reach to me.

comments.issue: Corolla length differences are too small to distinguish in Figure 1.
comments.request: Scale continuous traits rather than only centering them.
comments.quote: While the differences in leaf area are clear, the differences in corolla length is too small to be distinguishable in the figure.

comments.issue: Figure 1 mutualist trait diagrams lack panel names referenced in the text.
comments.request: Name the panels and reference them in the text.
comments.quote: It would be nice in the mutualist trait legends to give these diagrams panel names (e.g. fig 1A, fig 2B) and then reference them in the text

comments.issue: Mutualistic trait names differ between the Figure 1 legend and the phylogeny.
comments.request: Make trait names consistent.
comments.quote: The names of the mutualistic traits between the legend and the phylogeny are not consistent (e.g. domatium entrance holes vs domatium diameter)

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the group produces several food body types or only extrafloral nectaries.
comments.request: Clarify this in the text and Figure 1.
comments.quote: Does this group produce several types of food body, or only extrafloral nectaries? This should be clarified in the text and fig. 1.

comments.issue: 7 line-level copy edits (dashes, symbols, wording).
comments.quote: Line 411 “most” should be “more” and “that” should be “than”

reviews.assessment: Important question and novel approach, but the manuscript lacks clarity and methodological information throughout.
strengths: clear explanation of the trait data

comments.issue: Background is unclear: how the question is explained and how the study fits ongoing work.
comments.request: Provide a clearer background and context.
comments.quote: it would be helpful for the author to provide a clearer background for their study, both in terms of how they explain the question and how it fits into work being carried out in this area

comments.issue: It is not clear how the study addresses the three limitations said to hamper progress.
comments.request: Explain how each of the three limitations is addressed.
comments.quote: The authors mention three main limitations that have “hampered progress” up to now in solving this question of how mutualisms affect non-mutualistic traits.

comments.issue: Terminology such as allometric relationships and Hansen-based Brownian motion is not explained and lacks references.
comments.request: Define these terms and add references.
comments.quote: providing a definition of what is meant by “allometric relationships” or “Hansen-based Brownian motion”. The latter also does not have any references

comments.issue: It is unclear why mutualistic traits are discrete and non-mutualistic ones continuous, and why these continuous traits were chosen.
comments.request: Justify the trait types and the trait selection.
comments.quote: It is not clear however why discrete traits are used to describe the mutualistic traits and continuous for the non-mutualistic.

comments.issue: The climate-variable section does not explain the justification for using "residuals of all models".
comments.request: Explain the residuals approach in more detail.
comments.quote: The section on climate variables could be explained in more detail, especially the justification for using the “residuals of all models” and what this means.

comments.issue: The dual discrete-continuous model is unclear: software, packages, how traits interact, and prior testing of the approach are not described.
comments.request: Explain how the analysis was run, how traits interact, and whether the approach was tested before.
comments.quote: The authors could provide more information here explaining how they ran the analysis and exactly how the continuous and discrete characters interact in the models.

comments.issue: The GitHub link does not work, hindering understanding of the analysis.
comments.request: Fix the GitHub link.
comments.quote: The github link is currently not working so it is difficult to understand how this step was carried out.

comments.issue: Models are not linked to their biological interpretation.
comments.request: Explain what preference for each model means biologically.
comments.quote: It was also helpful if the authors could link the different models to the biological interpretation, as in if model X is preferred what this says about the relationship of the traits.

comments.issue: The Yule tree prior and node calibrations (island age 4 Ma) are not well justified.
comments.request: Justify the tree prior and calibrations.
comments.quote: The decisions in the time calibrated tree inference do not seem well justified. The authors use a Yule (i.e., pure birth) tree prior.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the sensitivity analysis shows robustness to phylogenetic uncertainty.
comments.request: Explain how robustness to phylogenetic uncertainty was assessed.
comments.quote: For the section on the sensitivity analysis, it is currently not clear how the results are robust to phylogenetic uncertainty based on what is written.

comments.issue: Figures 2-4 are difficult to interpret.
comments.request: Add explanations or a dummy plot.
comments.quote: The plots in Fig. 2-4 are a bit difficult to interpret. Adding more explanation in the text/figure caption or providing a “dummy plot” to aid the reader in the understanding would help here.

comments.issue: Typo on line 300 ("7eltaictaAIC").
comments.request: Fix the typo.
comments.quote: would help here. - Typo on line 300 “7eltaictaAIC”.

reviews.assessment: Potential important contribution, but clarity, model rationale and figure presentation must be thoroughly addressed.
strengths: potential important contribution to the field

comments.issue: Introduction and Results lack articulation and fail to introduce the questions addressed.
comments.request: Improve clarity and introduce the questions properly.
comments.quote: Clarity of the manuscript is undermined by a lack of articulation in several sections, especially in Introduction and Results sections, which fail to properly introduce the questions addressed.

comments.issue: Theoretical and modelling works are not presented coherently around the Red King hypothesis.
comments.request: Present them coherently when introducing the hypothesis.
comments.quote: In Introduction, all the theoretical and modelling works can be presented in a coherent paragraph while introducing ‘the Red King’ hypotheses.

comments.issue: No visualization contrasts the study's result with prevailing theory.
comments.request: Add a visualization for the discussion.
comments.quote: a visualization showing the contrast between the summarized result of this study and the prevailing theoretical understanding of trait evolution under mutualism can be illustrated for the discussion

comments.issue: The rationale for using complex OU models appears only in a late summary line.
comments.request: Explain in the methods how these models reveal evolutionary patterns.
comments.quote: the rationale behind using such complex OU models was explained only in a summary line late in the introduction. For general readers, the manuscript will be more meaningful if the authors explain in the method section

comments.issue: The GTR+G model choice lacks AIC/BIC support and the partition scheme is unclear.
comments.request: Report model-testing statistics and state the partition scheme.
comments.quote: The authors have considered GTR+G substitution model for phylogeny reconstruction. This should be substantiated with model-testing statistics such as AIC or BIC values.

comments.issue: The first two Results sections should be collated and the trait analyses split by topic.
comments.request: Reorganize the Results sections.
comments.quote: The first two short sections in Results describing phylogeny and ancestral state reconstruction can be collated together for better readability.

comments.issue: Figures 2-4 are repetitive and overloaded with minor nuances.
comments.request: Simplify the figures to highlight overarching trends.
comments.quote: Figures 2–4 describing OU model parameters depicting the effects of mutualistic traits on the evolution of non-mutualistic traits are somewhat repetitive and with too many nuances.

comments.issue: Lines 107-110 and 133-137 are long sentences.
comments.request: Break them up for readability.
comments.quote: Lines 107-110, and 133-137: These are long sentences. Break them up to make them more readable.

comments.issue: Typos at lines 298 and 300 (O-MVA; "7eltaictaAIC").
comments.quote: Line 298: The O-MVA may be a typo for OUMVA and if not then need a brief introduction similar to other variations of the OU model.

comments.issue: Principal component summaries and PGLS are mixed in supplementary tables.
comments.request: Present them in separate tables.
comments.quote: In supplementary materials, principal component summaries and PGLS can be presented in separate tables.

title: Mutualisms drive plant trait evolution beyond interaction‐related traits

study.system: migratory landbirds; phenology model and NDVI data

editor_summary: Editor sides with reviewer 2: novelty insufficient because the model is unvalidated and assumes mismatch causes declines; presentation of mismatch effects is biased; forecasting at continental scale is premature.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and insightful conceptual model; all suggestions are minor, covering context, figure panels, parameter justification and wording.
strengths: builds well on previous empirical evidence

comments.issue: The manuscript lacks continuous line numbering, making it hard to comment on.
comments.request: Include continuous line numbering in the resubmission.
comments.quote: Can the authors please include numbering in the resubmission?

comments.issue: Real-world context on springs becoming longer is missing or understated.
comments.request: Add real-world context on changing spring duration.
comments.quote: I think it would be useful to incorporate a bit of "real-world" context here, which is currently missing/understated.

comments.issue: Figure 1 shows only two of the four duration-variability combinations.
comments.request: Expand Figure 1 to four panels covering all combinations.
comments.quote: Perhaps it would be worth expanding this figure to four panels to include these other combinations?

comments.issue: The model assumes timing match is the sole determinant of reproductive success, which is unrealistic.
comments.request: Discuss model limitations and other drivers of reproductive success.
comments.quote: It's clear that reproductive success is affected by more than the timing of reproduction in relation to spring green-up.

comments.issue: The provenance of the short and long spring duration values appears after the values.
comments.request: Move the provenance sentence up to follow the values.
comments.quote: I recommend moving this sentence up to follow the stated values.

comments.issue: Stochasticity set at 10% of model values confounds spring duration with variability.
comments.request: Use consistent stochasticity and test variability independently.
comments.quote: As it is, these two variables (spring duration and spring variability) seem to be confounded.

comments.issue: The chosen rate of 0.1 days per year phenological advancement is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the empirical basis of this rate.
comments.quote: How was this rate of phenological advancement chosen? Is it empirically defined?

comments.issue: The statistical models behind the estimates and p-values are not detailed in the Methods.
comments.request: Detail the statistical models in the Methods.
comments.quote: It's possible I've just overlooked it, but any statistical models should be detailed in the Methods.

comments.issue: Locations where populations are increasing are not considered.
comments.request: Include a comparison of population increases for completeness.
comments.quote: It may be worth including a comparison of population increases for completeness.

comments.issue: The Figure 3 inflection point is unexplained and the "trend of change" facet label is inaccurate.
comments.request: Explain the inflection point and relabel the facets as anomalies.
comments.quote: I'm not sure the facet label of "trend of change" is completely accurate here

comments.issue: The buffering effect contradicts the authors' hypothesis and needs interpretation.
comments.quote: I wonder whether this result is surprising (I guess so, since it contradicts the authors' hypothesis).

comments.issue: "Species-specific traits" should read "population-specific" because populations differ in migration strategy.
comments.request: Change species-specific to population-specific.
comments.quote: For clarity, I would change this to "population-specific", rather than "species".

comments.issue: Two typographical fixes: a missing article and a Figure 2 facet label typo.
comments.quote: The facet label for the right column has a typo. Should be "High" variability of spring onset.

comments.issue: The described NW-SE gradient may actually be NE-SW.
comments.request: Check and correct the gradient direction.
comments.quote: I might be confused, but should this be a "NE-SW" gradient, as is described in the following sentence?

reviews.assessment: Good concept and interesting application, but the model is unvalidated, novelty is below the journal's bar and mismatch importance is overstated.
strengths: good concept combining model and real-world analysis
interesting and novel patterns in spring green-up

comments.issue: The importance of phenological mismatch for populations is overstated and does not reflect current evidence.
comments.request: Revise the framing and discussion to reflect the current state of knowledge.
comments.quote: I believe that the importance of this mismatch for populations is generally overstated through the manuscript

comments.issue: The framework's novelty is similar to Durant's work and the width-mismatch link is long-inferred.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution beyond previous frameworks.
comments.quote: I am not convinced that the novelty of the framework achieves the high bar required by the journal.

comments.issue: The origin and real-world basis of the model parameter values are unclear.
comments.request: Show that parameter values are based on real-world biology.
comments.quote: It is not clear where the values used in the model originate from

comments.issue: The NDVI-prey relationship may not hold across habitats, as supporting evidence comes from grasslands.
comments.request: Discuss the appropriateness of NDVI across habitats and scales.
comments.quote: the manuscript could include more of a consideration of the appropriateness of this single measure of phenology across such a large spatial scale and multiple habitats

comments.issue: The model is not validated, so the plausibility of its projections cannot be judged.
comments.request: Validate the model against observed bird population data such as PECBMS.
comments.quote: I believe the authors miss an important opportunity to validate their model by using their model to predict spatio-temporal variation in short and long-distance migratory bird populations based on the observed phenological patterns in Figure 3

comments.issue: It is unclear from the conceptual model and Figure 1 how long springs differ from variable springs.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction in the figure legend.
comments.quote: I’m afraid I don’t understand from the conceptual model and this diagram how long springs differ from variable springs in the model or in the analysis

comments.issue: The claim that foodpeak width effects have not been tested ignores many published examples.
comments.request: Cite and discuss these existing examples.
comments.quote: Has the effect of foodpeak width on mismatch really not been tested?

comments.issue: This statement reflects the model setup rather than an empirical finding.
comments.request: Acknowledge that this result follows from the model setup.
comments.quote: Again, isn’t this a function of how the model is set-up, rather than demonstrating something empirical with real-world variation between bird species?

comments.issue: More recent references question the pivotal role of phenological change in population dynamics.
comments.request: Cite more recent references that challenge this role.
comments.quote: many more recent references than these call into question the importance of phenological changes playing a pivotal role in population dynamics.

title: Duration and variability of spring green‐up mediate population consequences of climate change

study.system: 78 Greenlandic lakes; stickleback traits, char presence and zooplankton communities

editor_summary: Editor enjoyed the paper and finds the results interesting, but the four reviews raise many statistical questions needing clarification and extension; spatial aspects of lake size and location are emphasized, as are raw data access and data collection details.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and easy to follow; asks about the unbalanced design, region effects and clearer labeling of prey communities.
strengths: different analysis steps easy to follow

comments.issue: The lake design is highly unbalanced (34 fishless versus 8 char-only lakes), which is not accounted for in the analyses.
comments.request: Use analyses suitable for unbalanced designs, e.g. Type III ANOVA.
comments.quote: This means that the dataset is highly unbalanced. Did the authors consider this unbalanced design when performing statistical analyses?

comments.issue: Lake chemistry differs among the three sampling regions and may influence composition, but region is not included in the analyses.
comments.request: Consider including sampling region in subsequent analyses.
comments.quote: There is a difference in lake chemistry between the sampling region, and lake chemistry does seem to influence community composition (Figure 4). Do the authors think that somehow sampling region should therefore be included in the subsequent analyses?

comments.issue: The text often says "community" without specifying prey/zooplankton community, which is confusing (L69, L72-73, L222-223, L457).
comments.request: Explicitly add prey or zooplankton before community throughout, and consider adding prey to the title.
comments.quote: Often the authors don't specify 'prey' community structure, which can read confusing as one could equally investigate how trait variation in the consumer feeds back to alter consumer communities.

comments.issue: Jaw protrusion affects zooplankton composition even though the trait does not differ significantly between the two stickleback population groups.
comments.request: Explain why the jaw protrusion effect appears without trait divergence.
comments.quote: jaw protrusion itself is not significantly different between stickleback populations from these two lakes. Do the authors have an idea of why this effect here shows up?

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits: missing space at L112 and a broken micro symbol at L165.
comments.quote: L112: I think a space is needed between 'conditions.Specifically'.

comments.issue: Abbreviations KT, JP, LR and SI are not written out at L256-261.
comments.request: Write the abbreviations out in full once.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to write the abbreviations (KT, JP, LR, SI) once full out again.

comments.issue: Whether water chemistry relates to lake morphometry across all lake types is not reported (L274-285).
comments.request: Report the water chemistry-morphometry relationship for the full dataset.
comments.quote: Was there a relation found between water chemistry and lake morphometry for the total dataset including all lake types?

comments.issue: The divergence evidence covers only one of four foraging traits, but is not formulated that way (L318-320).
comments.request: Reformulate to reflect that only one trait diverged.
comments.quote: This evidence of divergence in foraging morphology occurred only for one of the four traits, perhaps this could be slightly reformulated.

reviews.assessment: Interesting results and good trait data, but missing environmental drivers and unaddressed spatial effects may create spurious correlations.
strengths: fish traits are functionally relevant and measurable from morphology
unique contribution connecting fish traits to prey communities

comments.issue: Key environmental drivers (temperature, phosphorus, nitrogen, pH) were not measured, risking spurious correlations between fish metrics and zooplankton composition.
comments.request: Address this limitation in the discussion.
comments.quote: Missing important environmental drivers could result in spurious correlations between fish metrics and zooplankton composition. This seems like a major limitation of their study, and must at least be addressed in their discussion.

comments.issue: Space is ignored although sites span three distinct regions, and dispersal limitation is known to structure zooplankton communities.
comments.request: Include the different regions in the analysis.
comments.quote: the authors do not address the importance of space in their study, even though their sites are far apart in three distinct regions

comments.issue: Only PC axis scores are given, without ranges or means of the lake environment variables.
comments.request: Report lake environment values, at least in the supplement.
comments.quote: we need more context about these lakes beyond PC axis scores - at least in the supplement if not in the main paper

comments.issue: Calcium is invoked as a driver, but its effect likely reflects an acidification gradient and buffering capacity rather than calcium itself.
comments.request: Reconsider the calcium interpretation.
comments.quote: But Calcium only limits cladocerans at extremely low levels - some the papers they cite likely reflect an acidification gradient where calcium represents a buffering capacity, not an effect of Calcium per se.

comments.issue: Relationships between fish density, fish traits and environmental variables are not shown.
comments.request: Include these relationships.
comments.quote: I suggest the authors include the relationships between fish density, fish traits, and environmental variables.

comments.issue: The relative importance of environment, fish composition and stickleback traits is not quantified.
comments.request: Provide effect sizes or variation partitioning.
comments.quote: Please provide some sort of effect size or variation partitioning analysis to strengthen the argument that intraspecific variation in fish traits are important in determining patterns of zooplankton composition in nature.

comments.issue: The "release from piscivory" argument implies a CPUE change, but CPUE did not differ between lake types (L446-450).
comments.request: Explain the reduced predation pressure argument more explicitly.
comments.quote: The CPUE did not differ between lakes, so is this an argument about stickleback habitat use and behavior? The term "release from piscivory" suggests a change in CPUE, but that was not found in this system.

comments.issue: Zooplankton body sizes were measured but analyses beyond community composition are not presented.
comments.request: Analyse body-size shifts in addition to community composition.
comments.quote: The authors measured body sizes in zooplankton (SI), and it would be useful to include more analyses beyond community composition.

comments.issue: Standardizing traits to one body size removes potentially important intraspecific variation related to body-size distributions (L208).
comments.request: Consider removing the size standardization.
comments.quote: By standardizing to one body size it seems to me that it removes a component of intraspecific variation in traits that is related to body size distributions that is potentially important. Consider removing this standardization

comments.issue: Table 1 does not indicate which models and variables explain significant variation.
comments.request: Mark significant models and important variables in Table 1.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to indicate which models explain significant variation in zooplankton community structure, and which variables were important in the models.

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not report the variation explained by each axis.
comments.request: Add the variation explained by each axis.
comments.quote: Figure 3 - add how much variation is explained by each axis

comments.issue: Figure 3 shows a possible arch or horseshoe effect, so axis 2 should not be over-interpreted (e.g. L328).
comments.request: Reduce interpretation of axis 2.
comments.quote: some sort of arch or horseshoe effect, so would not put much interpretation in axis 2

comments.issue: Line-level clarity edits: add "of consumers" at L72, missing space at L112, and specify zooplankton community structure at L263.
comments.quote: L263: indicate that this is zooplankton community structure

reviews.assessment: Impressive field study, but spatial effects, top-down assumptions and missing raw data leave alternative explanations open.
strengths: interesting field study from a remote area
impressed by the number of lakes and fish included
detail of the stickleback trait analyses

comments.issue: Spatial aspects are not analysed; environmental and spatial components of variation should be separated.
comments.request: Provide GPS coordinates or a distance matrix of the lakes.
comments.quote: Many studies of (not only) zooplankton communities separate the environmental and spatial components of variation in community structure. At the very least, the authors should provide the GPS coordinates or a distance matrix of the lakes.

comments.issue: The abstract assumes top-down control of the food web, but bottom-up control is equally plausible.
comments.request: Discuss the possibility of bottom-up control.
comments.quote: The last sentence in the abstract implicitly assumes a top-down control of the food web, but a bottom-up control is also plausible

comments.issue: Experiments on intraspecific predator size variation (Rudolf and co-workers) are not credited at L71.
comments.request: Cite the relevant Rudolf papers.
comments.quote: Several experiments investigated the effects of intraspecific variation in predator size - see e.g. papers by Volker Rudolf and co-workers

comments.issue: Sizes of the sticklebacks measured and dissected, and sizes and abundances of juvenile planktivorous char, are not reported.
comments.request: Report fish body sizes and char abundances.
comments.quote: could not find any information on the size of sticklebacks found in the lakes and dissected for the morphometric measurements and gut content analyses. Juvenile char can also be planktivorous, but their sizes and abundances are not given.

comments.issue: The range of sampling dates and possible seasonality or year effects are not reported (L126).
comments.request: Report sampling dates and consider season/year as nuisance variables.
comments.quote: The exact range of sampling dates is not given but could be important given the very short summer season in the Arctic. What about possible seasonality and year effects?

comments.issue: The local environment description lacks bottom substrate, macrophytes and benthic macroinvertebrate information (L136ff).
comments.request: Describe the local environment more thoroughly.
comments.quote: The answers to these questions might be trivial but a more thorough description of the local environment would be very helpful for readers that are not familiar with those lakes.

comments.issue: The lake morphometry metric is essentially lake size and central to the analyses but lacks clear biological meaning (L141).
comments.request: Test robustness by replacing morphometry with lake area.
comments.quote: I think additional analysis (e.g. replacing the morphometry variable with lake area) should test if the results are robust.

comments.issue: Temperature is excluded and the choice of the 0-3 m stratum for environmental variables is not justified (L150-152).
comments.request: Explain variable and stratum choices and provide raw environmental data.
comments.quote: Why was temperature not included in the analyses? Why was the 0-3m stratum chosen to represent the environmental variables?

comments.issue: No figure shows the environmental values for the different lakes (L156).
comments.request: Add a figure showing lake values.
comments.quote: A figure showing the values for the different lakes would be really helpful here.

comments.issue: Whether the tow represents the whole zooplankton community, including littoral species, is unclear (L165).
comments.request: Discuss tow representativeness and spatio-temporal overlap.
comments.quote: How representative is the tow of the whole zooplankton community? Are there any littoral zone species that could be under-represented?

comments.issue: Whether the dissected fishes were chosen randomly is unclear (L182).

comments.issue: Gut contents were not analysed although they could support the main findings (L185).

comments.issue: Results at L259-261 cannot be assessed because raw data are not given.

comments.issue: The fishery methods are inconsistent and may affect the results and conclusions.

comments.issue: It is not tested whether foraging traits or merely fish presence and abundance shape the zooplankton community.

comments.issue: The title should include "fish" and "zooplankton" to attract readers.

comments.issue: Basic lake characteristics are not mentioned at L105.

comments.issue: How the deepest point was estimated is unclear (L137).

comments.issue: It is unclear which data the conductivity, fDOM and Chla variables explained 41% of (L156).

comments.issue: Table S2 contains key information and should be in the main manuscript (L168).

comments.issue: It is unclear why the large Eurycercus is grouped with Chydorus (L169-170).

comments.issue: Trap duration and timing were not standardized, so fishless status and catches may be biased (L174-187).
comments.request: Clarify and standardize the fishing strategy and gillnet timing.
comments.quote: Thus, whether the lake was fishless or not may have depended on the length of the catching period. Please clarify how you overcame this issue with the chosen fishing strategy.

comments.issue: Photos of the jaw traits are only in the supplement (L193-196).
comments.request: Include the jaw trait photos in the main text.

comments.issue: How KT can be calculated from photos is not explained (L205).
comments.request: Explain the KT calculation from photos.

comments.issue: "Per population" at L212 should be clarified as per lake, and the four traits as stickleback traits (L213).

comments.issue: "Gradients" and "configurations" at L217 should be "variables" and "composition".

comments.issue: Findings presented at L223-224 belong in the results, not here.

comments.issue: Lake altitude is not included in the analysis (L243-246).
comments.request: Include lake altitude in the analysis.

comments.issue: Stickleback density may mix gillnet and minnow-trap catches with variable fishing periods (L256-261).

comments.issue: The range of water chemistry variability is unclear (L265).
comments.request: Report the variability range.
comments.quote: It is a bit unclear to me how large the water chemistry range is.

comments.issue: Fish population and abundance may be the main driver and should be pulled forward with literature support (L274-285).
comments.request: Emphasize fish population and abundance earlier.
comments.quote: I guess the main driver for the zooplankton community is the fish population and fish abundance. I suggest pulling this forward also in this paragraph.

comments.issue: There is no real evidence for a jaw protrusion effect; the result may mainly reflect a general fish effect (L292-293).
comments.request: Mention the general fish effect instead.
comments.quote: In principle there is not really evidence for a jaw protrusion effect. This underlines a general fish effect, which I suggest mentioning.

comments.issue: The sentence at L297 should be more specific.

comments.quote: Please be more specific with the sentence: "To explore the effects of stickleback traits and density independent of fish-configuration

comments.issue: The L314-316 sentence refers to zooplankton results that Fig. 1 does not show.

comments.quote: I suggest modifying this sentence as figure 1 doesn't show zooplankton results, despite the text refers to zooplankton community structure.

comments.issue: The zooplankton community might have been shaped the same way irrespective of fish phenotypic variation (L322-325).
