comments.quote: Here one can ask if the zooplankton community wouldn't have been shaped the same way irrespective of the phenotypic variation in fish. Please include such considerations in the discussion.

comments.issue: Sentences at L263 and L457-458 do not specify whether fish or zooplankton communities are meant.
comments.request: Be clear about which community is meant.
comments.quote: L 457-458. Be clear about what communities you are thinking of; fish or zooplankton communities?

comments.issue: The conclusion (L453-480) is too long and contains speculative discussion.
comments.request: Shorten the conclusion and move speculation to the discussion.
comments.quote: The conclusion is too long. Focus on the concluding lines and leave the more speculative and discussing parts in the discussion.

comments.issue: Figure 5 y-axis should mention zooplankton and explain the abbreviations Sl, KT, LR, JP.
comments.request: Update the y-axis and explain abbreviations.
comments.quote: Include "zooplankton" in the y-axis text and to help the reader please explain the different abbreviation in the figure text (Sl, KT, LR, JP).

title: The role of fish predators and their foraging traits in shaping zooplankton community structure

study.system: aquatic virus-host infection networks; 37 published cross-infection matrices

editor_summary: Praises the potential novel contribution; asks to update network data or explain, test alternative null models, reorganize the introduction around dimensionality testing, fix the code, and define space, networks, dimensionality and nestedness.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic and appreciated code, but the reasoning is poorly organized, the main question is unclear, and mechanisms are not addressed.
strengths: interesting topic of interest to a wide audience
provided code and example data for the review process
Figure 1 expresses the main ideas well

comments.issue: The introduction mixes drivers of dimensionality, nestedness and modularity without showing why the metrics matter.
comments.request: Reorganize the introduction, treating the metrics one by one.
comments.quote: Some reorganization of the Introduction would be good. Now the text becomes a mixture of potential drivers of dimensionality, nestedness and modularity.

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks an extended caption; panel f is unclear.
comments.request: Extend the Figure 1 caption and clarify panel f.
comments.quote: I think Figure 1 needs to get an extended figure text, e.g. f) is not really clear to me.

comments.issue: The introduction ends without a clear aim or expectation; the main question remains unclear.
comments.request: State a clear aim and expectations at the end of the introduction.
comments.quote: I would also like to see a clearer aim in the end of the Introduction – did the authors for example expect any particular result?

comments.issue: Results focus on one-dimensional sorting and errors, which the introduction never introduces.
comments.request: Introduce the sorting/error analysis in the introduction.
comments.quote: In the Results much focus is on the sorting in one dimension and how many errors that result in. This comes as kind of a surprise as there is no discussion on that aspect in the Introduction.

comments.issue: It is unclear why dimensionality is used rather than modularity, and which metric is the focus.
comments.request: Clarify which metric matters and why, making this section less confusing.
comments.quote: why then go the way over dimensionality and not only check modularity? Here again comes the confusion about what metric that is important in the first place.

comments.issue: The Figure 3 legend sentence about red lines and mismatched strains is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the red lines and mismatched strains in the Figure 3 legend.
comments.quote: In the legend for Fig 3 “Red lines connect two mismatched strains to their position on the phylogeny” – what does that mean?

comments.issue: The sentence at line 350 belongs at the start of the Results, and the main question stays unclear.
comments.request: Move the line 350 statement to the beginning of the Results.
comments.quote: Line 350: it feels like this should be the first line in the Result section.

comments.issue: Mechanisms behind dimensionality are discussed but not addressed with data, e.g. species traits.
comments.request: Use traits or genotypic characteristics of example networks to probe mechanisms.
comments.quote: Even just some example networks would really strengthen the manuscript and perhaps allow for some indication of the mechanisms in play.

comments.issue: The multiple regression at line 361 is not mentioned in the Methods.
comments.request: Describe the multiple regression in the Methods section.
comments.quote: This approach should be mentioned in the Method section.

comments.issue: There is no table listing each network's dimensionality.
comments.request: Add a table of networks and their dimensionality.
comments.quote: There should be a table stating which networks having respective dimensionality.

comments.issue: The abstract does not explain what dimensionality is or how it helps between the two sentences.
comments.request: Add an explanation of dimensionality and its usefulness to the abstract.
comments.quote: Would be good to have an explanation of what dimensionality is and how it can help understanding of the principles between these sentences.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'similar' is undefined in the abstract and at line 61.
comments.request: Define what 'similar' means in these statements.
comments.quote: l. 61 “may be associated with similar network structures

comments.issue: The claim that virus networks are more complex than predator-prey networks is questionable.
comments.request: Justify the comparison with predator-prey networks.
comments.quote: Are these networks more complex than e.g. predator-prey networks. The “multifaceted coevolutionary arms races” are indeed prevalent also in those networks.

comments.issue: Nestedness and modularity are used without explanation.
comments.request: Add a quick explanation of nestedness and modularity.
comments.quote: l. 98 A quick explanation for nestedness and modularity could be added.

comments.issue: Text at line 115 repeats earlier statements and should be reorganized.
comments.request: Reorganize or remove the repeated statement at line 115.
comments.quote: l. 115 Already stated above. Reorganize?

comments.issue: It is unclear why only 'cross-infection matrices' are mentioned and whether other data formats exist.
comments.request: Explain whether interaction data exist in other formats.
comments.quote: why do the authors specifically state “cross-infection matrices” – are interaction data not available in other formats as well?

comments.issue: The range of numbers of interactions across datasets is not reported.
comments.request: Add the range of interaction numbers.
comments.quote: l. 174. Add the range of number of interactions in the datasets.

comments.issue: The host direction and its meaning are not explained.
comments.request: Explain host direction, perhaps in the introduction.
comments.quote: l. 232 What about the host direction? What does that mean?

comments.issue: No explanation is offered for why the two largest networks have low dimensionality.
comments.request: Discuss why the two largest networks have low dimensionality.
comments.quote: Figure 4: Do the authors have any idea why the two largest networks have low dimensionality?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether nestedness counts as a type of host partitioning.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between nestedness and host partitioning.
comments.quote: l. 308 “Many networks display substantial evidence of both host partitioning and nestedness

comments.issue: The claim that complexity could lead to high-dimensional dynamics conflicts with the expectation that coevolution yields low dimensionality.
comments.request: Explain why coevolution would not lead to low dimensionality.
comments.quote: Wouldn’t one expect co-evolutionary dynamics to lead to low dimensionality?

comments.issue: Line 409 contradicts line 399 and lacks a reference.
comments.request: Resolve the contradiction and add the missing reference.
comments.quote: l. 409 Contradicts what is stated on line 399. And a reference missing.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and interesting low-dimensionality result, but wants more interpretation and robustness checks, plus a better term than 'errors'.
strengths: interesting that these systems appear to have low dimensionality
liked the depictions of network structures in Figure 1

comments.issue: The most recent eukaryotic phytoplankton cross-infection matrix is over eight years old.
comments.request: Update the datasets or discuss the lack of recent data.
comments.quote: I note I am a little surprised that the most recent eukaryotic phytoplankton cross-infection matrix is from over 8 years ago

comments.issue: The term 'errors' implies wrongdoing and may misrepresent the quantity.
comments.request: Choose an alternative term for this quantity.
comments.quote: I think care must be taken to refrain from implying wrongdoing

comments.issue: It is not said which network structures produce low or high dimensionality.
comments.request: Characterize quantitatively or qualitatively which structures yield low/high dimensionality.
comments.quote: I wonder if there is more that one could say, either quantitatively or qualitatively, with respect to the kinds of network structures that may result in low/high dimensionality?

comments.issue: Networks represent one time and place; effects of temporal, spatial or phylogenetic sampling scale are unknown.
comments.request: Discuss how changing sampling scales would affect dimensionality.
comments.quote: If we altered time-, spatial- (e.g. Flores et al. 2013, ISME J) or phylogentic- scales (e.g. Kauffman et al., 2022) of sampling do the authors have a sense of how this may impact potential dimensionality?

comments.issue: Results were evaluated against only one probabilistic null model.
comments.request: Test alternative null models, e.g. fixed row and column totals.
comments.quote: I like this analysis, but I do wonder if similar results would be obtained for other null models?

comments.issue: Dimensionality is not compared with prior studies such as Eklöf et al. 2013.
comments.request: Compare these networks' dimensionality with prior findings and expectations.
comments.quote: How does the dimensionality in these examined systems compare to that found in other networks (e.g. the study of Eklöf et al., 2013).

comments.issue: The broader interpretation and lessons of the results are not developed.
comments.request: Discuss how researchers should interpret and build on these results.
comments.quote: I’m also interested to hear more about how the authors think their results should be interpreted.

comments.issue: The Readme description for the third script is incomplete.
comments.request: Complete the Readme description for the third script.
comments.quote: In the Readme file associated with the code, the description for the third script is incomplete.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the original Nestedness Calculator implementation was used.
comments.request: State which Nestedness Calculator implementation was used.
comments.quote: Was the original Nestedness Calculator (Atmar and Patterson, 1993) used?

comments.issue: Non-circle error symbols are hard to spot in Figure S1 and the total error count is missing.
comments.request: Add the total number of errors to the Figure S1 caption.
comments.quote: Fig S1 – note the ‘errors’ (non-circle symbols) are very difficult to spot in this figure.

reviews.assessment: Confident in the technical correctness and finds the low-dimensionality result worthy of publication, but the presentation omits key underpinnings and may confuse readers.
strengths: interesting finding with far-reaching implications, worthy of publication
strong confidence in the technical correctness

comments.issue: It is not made clear what kind of space the reported dimensionality describes.
comments.request: Explain that this is an embedding dimensionality and what it means.
comments.quote: The manuscript talks about dimensionality, but it does not make very clear what kind of space this dimensionality describes.

comments.issue: What the nodes and links represent is not stated explicitly.
comments.request: State explicitly what nodes and links represent near the start.
comments.quote: In any discusssion of networks it is good style to make very clear what exactly is represented by the nodes and links.

comments.issue: The discussion focuses on nestedness, distracting from dimensionality, and ignores the nestedness sampling-bias controversy.
comments.request: Refocus on dimensionality and discuss nestedness as sampling bias.
comments.quote: The discussion focusses strongly on nestedness which distracts somewhat from the point of dimensionality that could ultimately more interesting.

title: The dimensionality of infection networks among viruses infecting microbial eukaryotes and bacteria

study.system: greenhouse experiment; Scirpus mariqueter genotypes and Spartina alterniflora invader

editor_summary: Both reviewers find the topic not entirely novel but value the microbial mechanism; editor asks for more experimental and analysis detail, Monte-Carlo details, and native plant performance data.

reviews.assessment: Well-designed, well-analyzed experiment, but the soil-mediated invasion resistance claim needs stronger caveats and more discussion.

comments.issue: Soil-mediated invasion resistance is claimed although the native species' response to conditioned soils was not measured.
comments.request: Strongly caveat the claim or provide native plant performance data.
comments.quote: If native plant species also perform worse on soils conditioned by diverse populations, then the soil may have no net effect on interactions between native and invasive plant species.

comments.issue: It is striking that genotypic diversity matters with no genetic-identity effect; whether genotypes differed at all is not shown.
comments.request: Report whether genotypes differed in biomass or soil properties.
comments.quote: The effect of genotypic diversity absent an effect of genetic identity in monoculture (or in improving model fit when genotypic composition was considered) is striking

comments.issue: Strong positive nonadditive effects in sterilized soil are not discussed and hypothesized mechanisms only hinted at.
comments.request: Discuss these effects and the hypothesized mechanisms.
comments.quote: In sterilized soil, there were strong positive nonadditive effects. It may be worth mentioning this in the discussion.

comments.issue: Line 81 wording edit: 'attention to explain' should read 'explanations'.
comments.request: Replace 'attention to explain' with 'explanations'.
comments.quote: 81: “attention to explain” instead use “explanations”

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed the paper; mostly clarification and presentation requests, with some statistical and methodological suggestions.
strengths: well thought out and neatly presented research
compelling story on mechanisms of invasion resistance

comments.issue: The introduction lacks clear testable hypotheses and presents some unsupported ideas as empirical statements.
comments.request: Set up the latter parts of the introduction as explicit hypotheses.
comments.quote: I would suggest that the latter parts of the introduction be set up as hypotheses (see comment regarding L99-100), as I found any clear and testable predictions/hypotheses to be lacking

comments.issue: Replication was low, leaving large error bars, though the reviewer notes it does not undermine the story.
comments.request: Consider increasing replication in future work.
comments.quote: Increased replication would have potentially reduced some of the variability in the data (some large error bars) but is not a problem

comments.issue: How the genotype combinations in Table S1 were chosen is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how genotype combinations were decided.
comments.quote: How were the genotype combinations that are presented in Table S1 decided? Some information around the thinking here would be useful to the reader.

comments.issue: FUNGuild and BugBase usage is undocumented, so the microbial results are not replicable.
comments.request: Document database versions, taxon selection rules and provide brief descriptions.
comments.quote: none of this information is provided in the main text or the supplement, meaning that the results are not replicable

comments.issue: Some relationships look non-linear, e.g. microbial biomass carbon vs. genotypic diversity.
comments.request: Consider polynomial regression models.
comments.quote: Some of the data appear to show non-linear relationships, e.g., microbial biomass carbon and genotypic diversity. Were polynomial regression models considered?

comments.issue: The results section needs more detail to flesh out the findings.
comments.request: Add more detail to the results section.
comments.quote: I think a little more detail in the results section would help to flesh some of it out further

comments.issue: The paper cites 82 references, which is excessive and dilutes focus.
comments.request: Cut down the number of references.
comments.quote: 82 references are a lot. Cutting down the number of references would save space and focus the paper

comments.issue: Seeds were collected from a single 1x1 m plot; whether this minimised invader genetic diversity is not justified.
comments.request: State and justify the seed collection approach in the methods.
comments.quote: Was this to minimise genetic diversity for this species? If so, this should be stated and justified in the methods.

comments.issue: Invader genetic diversity, which could interact with native diversity, is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss invader genetic diversity as a future research direction.
comments.quote: what about the genetic diversity of the invader, which might interact with (and help to overcome) native genetic diversity? This should be discussed as a future research direction

comments.issue: Numerous line-level wording, deletion and terminology edits throughout (e.g. L49-L149, L244, L313, L395, L607, L612, supplement L116-L131).
comments.quote: L119 and elsewhere: Either “salt marsh” or “saltmarsh” is generally accepted.

comments.issue: Community-level diversity and species/population-level genotypic diversity are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Use clear and consistent terminology throughout.
comments.quote: Wouldn’t this be at the community level (i.e. community diversity increases resistance to invasion) and genotypic diversity at the species/population level?

comments.issue: The term 'dilution effect' is used without clarification.
comments.request: Clarify what the dilution effect means.
comments.quote: It is not clear what is meant by “dilution effect”, please clarify. Does this mean lower relative abundance on a host?

comments.issue: Unclear whether the described pattern is a type of inverse selection effect.
comments.request: Clarify whether this is an inverse selection effect.
comments.quote: Is this some type of inverse selection effect?

comments.issue: Diversity effects on pathogens and mutualists might cancel or be additive, but this is not posed as a hypothesis.
comments.request: Mention this as a final hypothesis linking both interaction outcomes.
comments.quote: Could the effects of diversity on pathogens and mutualists also either cancel each other out, or contribute to additive effects?

comments.issue: 'Invasion' is not specified; it could mean growth or survival.
comments.request: Be more specific than invasion.
comments.quote: Can you be more specific than invasion? Growth? Survival?

comments.issue: The term plant-soil feedbacks is introduced too late in the introduction.
comments.request: Link the term to the earlier description of plant-soil biota interactions.
comments.quote: this is the first time the term “soil feedbacks” or “plant-soil feedbacks” has been introduced. It needs to be linked in earlier in the introduction

comments.issue: The reason for sterilizing corms is not justified.
comments.request: Justify each step taken in the methods.
comments.quote: Why were the corms sterilized? Please justify each step taken in the methods.

comments.issue: Proportion of seedlings replaced or lost and whether this differed among genotypes or treatments is missing.
comments.request: Add this information, perhaps as a supplementary table.
comments.quote: Can you add information on what proportion of seedlings needed replacing and whether this differed among genotypes or treatments

comments.issue: Soil sampling procedure is unclear: sample size and whether one sample or several sub-samples were used.
comments.request: Describe how the sampling was done.
comments.quote: How was this sampling done? How much soil is a “small proportion”? Just one random sample per pot, or a combination of several smaller sub-samples?

comments.issue: Unclear whether available phosphorus was sampled differently and whether all pots were measured for other variables.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling and measurement of soil variables.
comments.quote: Was this sampled differently from the other variables? Were all pots measured for the other variables?

comments.issue: Basis for choosing log or square-root transformations is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the need for transformation was determined.
comments.quote: How was it determined whether a log or square root transformation was necessary?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether random effects were omitted from all models or only the soil abiotic models.
comments.request: Clarify which models included random effects.
comments.quote: Does this mean that all models did not include a random effect, or just for the soil abiotic variables?

comments.issue: Only model fit was checked; whether adding random effects changed significance of variables is not reported.
comments.request: Report qualitative changes in model output when random effects are included.
comments.quote: Fits may not have improved, but were there qualitative changes to the output of the model (i.e., did some variables change from significant to non-significant or vice-versa)?

comments.issue: Sterilization effects on soil abiotic properties were tested for only one variable without justification.
comments.request: Justify or extend the analysis to other soil properties.
comments.quote: why was this analysis only conducted for one of the variables, when soil sterilization may have affected other abiotic soil properties too?

comments.issue: No random effects are mentioned for the microbial community model.
comments.request: Clarify whether random effects were included.
comments.quote: No mention of random effects for this model?

comments.issue: Ramet number is count data but was apparently not analysed with a Poisson GLM.
comments.request: Justify or use an appropriate count model.
comments.quote: Ramet number is count data, which is generally analysed using a generalised linear model with a Poisson error distribution. Is there a reason why this model type was used instead?

comments.issue: Aboveground and belowground biomass could be combined into a ratio approximating allocation.
comments.request: Consider using the biomass ratio as a response variable.
comments.quote: Have you considered swapping out aboveground and belowground biomass for their ratio, which would approximate biomass allocation

comments.issue: Claim that biotic properties matter more is not formally tested and the sentence repeats the methods.
comments.request: Present clearer evidence and a formal statistical test.
comments.quote: it would be better to present clearer evidence of exactly how biotic properties had a greater influence

comments.issue: Results around L303-305 are too vague.
comments.request: Be more specific regarding these results.
comments.quote: Can you please be more specific regarding these results?

comments.issue: 'Intensity of invasion' was not measured; only plant growth variables were.
comments.request: Be more cautious and align conclusions with the data collected.
comments.quote: You did not measure “intensity of a species’ invasion” but rather some plant growth variables.

comments.issue: The logic that intensified competition reduces invader performance is unclear and seems reversed.
comments.request: Explain the competition logic, perhaps via complementarity and niche space.
comments.quote: I don’t find the logic to be clearly explained here. How would intensified competition lead to reduced invader performance?

comments.issue: The pattern could be explained by pathogen presence/absence without invoking competition intensity.
comments.request: Consider this simpler alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Couldn’t this also be explained simply by presence/absence of pathogens, without having to invoke changes in intensity of competition

comments.issue: Reviewer asks whether the described mechanism is a selection effect.
comments.request: Clarify whether this is a selection effect.
comments.quote: a selection effect?

comments.issue: Missing caveat that high pathogen abundance does not mean those pathogens attack the focal host.
comments.request: Add this link or caveat.
comments.quote: I think something is missing here – perhaps the link that higher pathogen relative abundance does not necessarily mean that those are pathogens that attack the specific host plant

comments.issue: 'Generalists' should be 'specialist enemies', since invaders do not escape generalists.

comments.quote: I would recommend changing to “specialist enemies”, as there is mounting evidence that invaders do not escape from generalists

comments.issue: Other nutrients were not tested the same way as phosphorus.
comments.request: Explain why other nutrients were not analysed similarly.
comments.quote: Why were other nutrients not tested in this same way?

comments.issue: The weakness of the phosphorus effect relative to soil biota should be stated explicitly.
comments.request: Mention this explicitly.
comments.quote: Presumably this means that the phosphorous effect was weaker than those imposed by soil biota in live soils, because it would have been present in both soil types, right?

comments.issue: Fig. 1 caption does not mention pathogens and mutualists.
comments.request: Integrate pathogens and mutualists into the caption.
comments.quote: Can you integrate pathogens and mutualists into the caption?

comments.issue: Fig. 3 presents photos before the data panels.
comments.request: Reorder the figure to show data panels (a) and (b) before the photos.
comments.quote: You may wish to consider changing the order to present the data in (a) and (b), followed by the photos.

comments.issue: Line fitting, shading and transparent points in the figure are not explained.

comments.quote: How was the line fitted? What does the shading represent? What are the transparent points?

comments.issue: Fig. 4 does not use shape to distinguish abiotic and biotic variables and omits the Hill number.
comments.request: Use different symbol shapes and note the Hill number in the caption.
comments.quote: Consider using different symbol shapes for abiotic and biotic variables to further assist people with colour blindness.

comments.issue: L623 caption mischaracterizes the figure, which shows importance of abiotic vs. biotic variable suites.
comments.request: Correct the caption wording.
comments.quote: The figure does not show “the relative importance of each predictor”. Instead, it appears to show the relative importance of the suite of abiotic vs. biotic variables.

comments.issue: Fig. 5 caption lacks context on data sources and interpretation.
comments.request: Expand the caption so the figure stands alone.
comments.quote: More context is needed in the caption to fully understand the figure (without having to refer to the main text).

comments.issue: Table S1 includes a '<6-FAM>' tag that is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the tag in the caption if it is intended.
comments.quote: am wondering if the “<6-FAM>” in the first sequence is meant to be there? If so, it might need explanation in the caption

comments.issue: Table S3 omits degrees of freedom.
comments.request: Add degrees of freedom to the table.
comments.quote: Consider adding degrees of freedom to the table too.

comments.issue: Fig. S1 caption does not explain interpretation of q = 0 and q = 2 or panel labels.
comments.request: Add this information to the caption.
comments.quote: More information is needed on how to interpret q = 0 and q = 2 for readers that are unfamiliar

comments.issue: Fig. S3 caption does not explain line fitting, shading, transparent points, or why some panels lack fitted lines.
comments.request: Explain these elements in the caption.
comments.quote: As above - how were the lines fitted? What does the shading represent? Why do some panels have fitted lines and others do not?

comments.issue: Fig. S4 lacks raw data and explanation of percentage axis labels and ordination interpretation.
comments.request: Add raw data and caption guidance.
comments.quote: It would be nice to see the raw data included here too, if possible? The percentage values in the axis labels are not explained in the figure caption.

comments.issue: Fig. S5 needs the same caption improvements as similar figures.
comments.request: Apply the comments on similar figures to Fig. S5.
comments.quote: See comments on similar figures and apply to this one too.

comments.issue: Fig. S6 analysis is not described in the methods and the caption is insufficient.
comments.request: Describe the analysis and expand the caption.
comments.quote: I don’t recall this analysis being described in the methods section? Moreover, not enough information is provided in the figure caption to fully interpret the figure.

comments.issue: Fig. S7 caption is insufficient for readers unfamiliar with this plot type.
comments.request: Expand the caption to explain all plotted elements.
comments.quote: more information is needed in the caption so the figure can be understood by readers who may not be familiar with how to interpret this type of plot

title: Genotype diversity enhances invasion resistance of native plants via soil biotic feedbacks

study.system: snail microcosm experiment and agent-based model; disease transmission

editor_summary: Both reviewers offer substantive comments to improve the article, especially tightening the link between models and experiment and making language more precise.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and compelling modelling, but the experiment-model link and the constant-resource-density premise need stronger support.
strengths: very well-written and easy to follow
timely combination of experiments and modelling

comments.issue: Resource density is not held constant; depletion feedbacks could drive the results.
comments.request: Show that depletion feedbacks do not affect the results.
comments.quote: In the experiment and simulations, hosts deplete resources, but (in the simulations at least) resources do not regenerate. Thus, the duration of the simulation/experiment could have a major effect on results.

comments.issue: The main result is supported only by the model, not by the experiment.
comments.request: Clarify the experimental support for this result.
comments.quote: it is only the model that is supporting the main result that non-random foraging reduced host contacts

comments.issue: No formal model comparison identifies the foraging level consistent with the data.
comments.request: Run model selection (e.g., ABC) against experimental data.
comments.quote: Did the authors consider any type of formal model comparison to identify the level of nonrandom foraging most consistent with the experimental data (e.g., model selection with ABC)?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the ABM captures the mechanisms behind the experimental patterns.
comments.request: Test alternative movement mechanisms against the data.
comments.quote: As presented, this makes me wonder if the correct mechanisms are being captured in the ABM.

comments.issue: General mechanism linking patch residency to saturating contact functions needs expansion.
comments.request: Expand on patch-residency mechanisms beyond optimal foraging.
comments.quote: does this lead to non-instantaneous contacts and a saturating contact function? So generalizing beyond optimal foraging, will any kind of mechanism inducing patch residency (e.g., refugia for predators) produce a similar effect?

comments.issue: Typo 'trail' at pg. 4 line 36.
comments.request: Change to 'trial'.
comments.quote: pg. 4, line 36: Change from “trail” to “trial”

comments.issue: Averaging across the whole simulation may not yield a valid R0.
comments.request: Explain how R0 was calculated.
comments.quote: Since R0 is calculated from the beginning of an epidemic in a completely susceptible population, I not sure how averages across the entire simulation are giving you a valid metric for R0.

comments.issue: Contact rate formula (contacts x timesteps) does not have units per time.
comments.request: Correct the rate calculation.
comments.quote: How is # host contacts x number of timesteps a rate (with units per time)? Should is be # host contacts / number of timesteps?

comments.issue: Equation at pg. 7 divides H_j by 1.
comments.request: Fix the equation.
comments.quote: pg. 7, equation: Why are you dividing H\_j by 1? Isn't this just H\_j?

comments.issue: Heavy aggregation seems impossible given the two-snail patch occupancy limit.
comments.request: Reconcile the aggregation claim with the occupancy limit.
comments.quote: But how is heavy aggregation possible if only 2 snails can occupy a patch at one time?

comments.issue: Figure 2 legend uses two different fonts.
comments.request: Use a consistent font.
comments.quote: The figure legend (figure 2) is two different fonts

comments.issue: Why means and confidence intervals come only from the first replicate is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the use of the first replicate.
comments.quote: “Experimental mean values and confidence intervals are from the first replicate” what does this mean and why are they only considered from the first replicate?

comments.issue: Typo 'dechloraminated' at page 21 line 37.
comments.request: Correct to 'dechlorinated'.
comments.quote: Page 21 line 37 “dechloraminated” should be dechlorinated

reviews.assessment: Strong synthesis of modelling and microcosm work; terminology and GLM collinearity need clarification.
strengths: synthesis of modelling and microcosm work is a big strength
broad interest to theoreticians and empiricists

comments.issue: Encounter rate and contact rate are too similar and easily confused.
comments.request: Use more distinct terms such as host-resource and host-host rates.
comments.quote: does encounter rate refer to snail- resource interaction whereas contact rate refers to snail-snail interaction?

comments.issue: 'Contact duration' is used for handling time although it refers to snail-resource contacts.
comments.request: Clarify the term.
comments.quote: “contact duration” is used referencing handling time. I believe this is snail-resource contact duration, not snail-snail contact duration?

comments.issue: 'Stochasticity' for deviation from optimal foraging is confusing.
comments.request: Rename as foraging strategy and add a figure legend.
comments.quote: The term stochasticity, used to denote deviation from optimal foraging, could also be clarified.

comments.issue: Aggregation index correlates with the grouping variable, potentially compromising GLM interactions.
comments.request: Report VIF or fit group as a random effect.
comments.quote: Could the authors include something like a variance inflation factor to show that including an interaction between group and aggregation index doesn’t compromise interpretation of the GLMs?

comments.issue: Low-variance models may yield artificially low p-values.
comments.request: Add a disclaimer about potential false significance.
comments.quote: it seems there is still the potential for false significance

comments.issue: Claim of qualitatively similar results lacks a supporting example.
comments.request: Add a small example in the supplement.
comments.quote: results were qualitatively similar—could you put a small example in the supplement?

comments.issue: Prevalence results are absent from the main text while Figure 2C remains.
comments.request: Move Figure 2C to the supplement.
comments.quote: Results on prevalence do not appear in the main text. Would Figure 2C be better suited as a supplementary figure?

comments.issue: Units for encounter rate, handling time and patch duration are missing.
comments.request: Add units to Figures 3 and 4A.
comments.quote: What are the units for encounter rate, handling time, and patch duration?

title: Nonrandom foraging and resource distributions affect the relationships between host density, contact rates and parasite transmission

study.system: trichostrongylid helminths of herbivores; lab traits, meta-analysis and climate models

editor_summary: Editor agrees with reviewers: the approach is strong but methods need clarification; the sensitivity analysis and extrapolation beyond the observed climate range could affect interpretation, and the meta-analysis methods and data sharing need attention.

reviews.assessment: Considers the approach great and the system relevant, but says the meta-analysis underpinning the model needs clearer description and shared data.
strengths: great approach to an interesting and relevant question

comments.issue: The meta-analysis underlying the model parametrisation is not well described.
comments.request: Describe extracted information, rules and constraints.
comments.quote: I think that the meta-analysis that much of the underlying parametrization is based on is not well described in the methods

comments.issue: L54-55: 'selectively targeting' is an odd phrase.
comments.request: Reword the phrase.
comments.quote: a minor point, but 'selectively targeting' is an odd way to describe this, consider a reword.

comments.issue: L56-57: parasite ectothermy should be integrated as an expansion of the previous sentence.
comments.request: Frame the sentence as an expansion.
comments.quote: many infections are caused by parasites that are themselves ectotherms, which could be useful to incorporate into how you state this second sentence

comments.issue: Extracted meta-analysis data are not shared with reviewers.
comments.request: Share the extracted data.
comments.quote: It would also be helpful to have this data shared with the reviewers.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not show how many species or studies underlie each panel.
comments.request: State species and study numbers per panel.
comments.quote: It is unclear what the underlying structure of the data that is being represented here is. For example, how many different species are included in each figure?

comments.issue: Legend calls the models 'climate-driven' although most are driven by temperature only.
comments.request: Use 'temperature-driven' instead.
comments.quote: the legend refers to these as 'climate-driven' models, but most models are driven only by temperature. I would suggest that 'temperature-driven' models be used instead.

comments.issue: Fig. 1h raises questions about low-humidity coverage; only two sub-100% temperatures are visible.
comments.request: Clarify low-humidity data coverage.
comments.quote: I am curious about the use of humidity here. From what I can tell from this figure, there are only two temperatures that were measured at lower than 100% humidity levels

comments.issue: Line 355: 'both helminths' is confusing when referring to two groups.
comments.request: Reword to make the two groups clear.
comments.quote: referring to the two groups of helminths as 'both helminths' is a bit confusing.

comments.issue: Lines 351-367: within-group co-infection is not explored and the co-infection language is inconsistent.
comments.request: Clarify that co-infection is between host locations.
comments.quote: Presumably there could be co-infection within helminth group, which you are not exploring. I think it would be good to be clear about the language here

comments.issue: Climate and temperature are used interchangeably in S1.2 and elsewhere.
comments.request: Distinguish climate from temperature.
comments.quote: climate is used interchangeably with temperature. Temperature is just one aspect of climate, and so the two words should not be used interchangeably.

reviews.assessment: Very favorable overall but wants a trait-level sensitivity analysis, justification for extrapolation beyond the data, and discussion of simplifying assumptions.
strengths: important question, solid overall approach and interesting findings
loves the Figure 1 design incorporating the life cycle diagram

comments.issue: Sensitivity analysis on climate-response parameters gives no mechanistic insight into which traits drive risk.
comments.request: Redo the sensitivity analysis at the level of biological traits.
comments.quote: I think the authors should revise their sensitivity analysis to be based on biological traits rather than the climate response parameters

comments.issue: Hypercube sampling only shows average effects over the thermal gradient; trait effects at specific temperatures are hidden.
comments.request: Consider a partial-derivative sensitivity analysis as in Mordecai et al. 2013.
comments.quote: Another (in my opinion better) option could be to do the sort of partial derivative sensitivity analysis utilized by Mordecai et al. 2013

comments.issue: The specific role of humidity in stomach helminth risk is not isolated.
comments.request: Add a counterfactual analysis with humidity fixed at 100%.
comments.quote: they could do a counterfactual analysis where they calculate infection risk for stomach helminths with and without humidity inputs (i.e., assume humidity = 100%)

comments.issue: Text and abstract treat larval mortality as one of many equally important traits.
comments.request: Revise the text and abstract to stress larval mortality.
comments.quote: the text on lines 266-269, 290-294, and 303-307 should be revised to emphasize that larval mortality is vastly more important than the other traits

comments.issue: Simplifying assumptions are not revisited in the Discussion despite limiting interpretation.
comments.request: Discuss these assumptions and their impacts.
comments.quote: However, none of these assumptions are revisited in the Discussion section, despite being important limitations on the results of this study.

comments.issue: Trait responses are projected beyond the fitted data range without biological justification; winter zero-risk may be an artefact.
comments.request: Justify extrapolation or constrain projections to observed conditions.
comments.quote: My primary concern re: the climate-trait responses is that the authors are using them to project beyond the range of the data they were fit to, and without a biological/theoretical argument for why the functions should hold beyond those limits.

comments.issue: Experimental and projected humidity minima are not reported.
comments.request: Report the lowest experimental and EUROCORDEX humidity values.
comments.quote: What was the lowest humidity used in the experiments and what are the lowest humidity values predicted by the EUROCORDEX data?

comments.issue: Projections may use climate values below the experimental range.
comments.request: Apply conservative cut-off points for climate inputs.
comments.quote: one possible solution is to have conservative cut-off points for climate inputs to the infection risk equation that are equal to the lowest values used in the experiments that generated the data

comments.issue: The linear humidity response lacks justification or supporting evidence.
comments.request: Justify the linear response and add an SI figure.
comments.quote: I would like more information on why the authors chose a linear response for humidity, and possibly a figure in the SI showing that the response is indeed approximately linear

comments.issue: The origin and derivation of equation 7 are not explained.
comments.request: Explain where equation 7 comes from.
comments.quote: Where did equation 7 come from? "We can calculate" is too vague. Has it been used before? Did the authors derive it?

comments.issue: The order-of-magnitude risk difference between the two groups is unexplained.
comments.request: Briefly explain this difference.
comments.quote: The predicted infection risk differs by an order of magnitude between the stomach and intestinal groups. It's not obvious to me why that would be the case just looking at the thermal responses.

comments.issue: A relevant recent study on temperature-humidity interactions is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Brown et al. 2023.
comments.quote: Here is a recent paper by Brown et al. 2023 in Eco Lett that touches on how temperature and humidity interact to impact mosquito traits that is probably worth citing

comments.issue: Several sentences are too long and clause-heavy to follow.
comments.request: Shorten or split long sentences.
comments.quote: The paper is generally well-written, but there are several places where sentences are too long or have too many clauses and become hard to follow as a reader.

comments.issue: Line 66: 'to result in' is better than 'the result of'.
comments.request: Rewrite the phrase.
comments.quote: would be better than "the result of" - because the hump-shaped thermal response is the result, not causing some other result

comments.issue: Line 72: 'Seasonality' is misused as a causal driver, making the argument circular.
comments.request: Use 'seasonal environmental forcing' or similar.
comments.quote: I don't like the use of the "Seasonality" as a causal driver here - "seasonality" can be used to describe anything with a seasonal pattern.

comments.issue: Seven line-level copy edits (lines 95, 163, 212, 413, 438, 446-7, 457).
comments.quote: Line 212: double space

comments.issue: Lines 113-117: the sentence should be split and 'population' pluralised.
comments.request: Split the sentence after the list of genera.
comments.quote: I would split this sentence after the list of genera. New sentence starting

comments.issue: Lines 113-119: grouping by infection location is not foreshadowed for readers.
comments.request: Add a sentence on the stomach/intestine grouping.
comments.quote: Somewhere in here I would add a sentence about grouping the parasites by infection location (stomach/intestine) to provide foreshadowing/context for the methods and results

comments.issue: Lines 157-179: expected shapes and directions of trait responses, especially humidity, are not set up.
comments.request: Describe the expected response shapes.
comments.quote: I would add in a little more information re: the shape/direction of responses to foreshadow the results and prepare the reader.

comments.issue: Equations 2 and 4 are mathematically equivalent but presented separately.
comments.request: Combine equations 2 and 4.
comments.quote: I would combine equations 2 and 4 with a more general specification/description, since they are mathematically equivalent only for two different traits.

comments.issue: Line 184-6: wording, punctuation and 'respectively' are confusing.
comments.request: Split and reword the sentence.
comments.quote: I would split this off from the first half of the sentence, and maybe even break it into two sentences. The wording/punctuation/structure is very confusing.

comments.issue: Line 219: 'multiple helminth species and/or groups' is a red herring.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: "among multiple helminth species and/or groups" is confusing - this is a red herring for the reader

comments.issue: Line 231: climate-trait results are buried in a long paragraph.
comments.request: Add a paragraph break and name the two groups.
comments.quote: I would add a paragraph break here to create structure that makes it easier to read.

comments.issue: Line 327: 'the demographic rates' needs qualification.
comments.request: Add 'for the different types of helminths'.
comments.quote: I would add "for the different types of helminths" after "the demographic rates"

comments.issue: Lines 395-400: the immune-function argument is unclear for free-living stages.
comments.request: Clarify whether adaptation or plasticity is meant.
comments.quote: This point re: immune function was confusing to me, given that the stages modeled here are free-living, and not inside a host.

comments.issue: Lines 400-403: the sentence should be split at 'However'.
comments.request: Split the sentence or use a semicolon.
comments.quote: Line 400-403: I would split the sentence at "However", or at least change the comma before "however" to a semi-colon.

comments.issue: Lines 440-442: the sentence should be split at 'However'.
comments.request: Split the sentence or use a semicolon.
comments.quote: Line 440-442: I would split the sentence at "However", or at least change the comma before "however" to a semi-colon.

title: Helminth ecological requirements shape the impact of climate change on the hazard of infection

study.system: wild vertebrates; ALAN and melatonin suppression, 127 experiments

editor_summary: Editor likes the approach; reviewers suggest improvements to presentation of results and discussion.

reviews.assessment: Important, transparent synthesis with novel insights; only a few suggestions on framing, reporting and interpretation.

comments.issue: The rebuttal of Sanders et al. reads as defensive; the earlier meta-analysis had a different purpose.
comments.request: Reframe it as a starting point for further investigation.
comments.quote: this part reads a bit defensive – this is not necessary as the meta-analysis by Sanders et al had a different purpose than this one.

comments.issue: The article selection process at line 167 is not described.
comments.request: Explain how articles were selected.
comments.quote: Line 167: how where these articles selected?

comments.issue: Model assumption checks are not reported.
comments.request: Describe how assumptions were checked.
comments.quote: Line 204: Maybe add how you checked for model assumptions.

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks a scale for the number of studies.
comments.request: Add a scale for the number of studies.
comments.quote: Figure 1, consider adding a scale for number of studies.

comments.issue: The taxonomic and context bias of the two datasets may affect outcomes and is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how these dataset characteristics affect the analysis.
comments.quote: Maybe add to the discussion how the two datasets (1) mostly diurnal, free-living birds and (2) mostly nocturnal and captive mammals may affect the outcome of the analysis.

comments.issue: The white-light focus and taxonomic bias are not mentioned in the abstract.
comments.request: Add them to the abstract.
comments.quote: this focus on white light is important to mention as is the taxonomic bias – consider adding something to the abstract

comments.issue: Cases of increased melatonin responses, including in Figure 3, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss these opposite responses.
comments.quote: Figure 3: there are clearly some positive responses here that are opposite to the main result, I would discuss this.

comments.issue: The number of studies behind line 498 is not given.
comments.request: Report how many studies were included.
comments.quote: Line 498: how many studies were included here?

comments.issue: Studies using high light intensities above 100 lux may not represent ALAN impact.
comments.request: Reanalyse excluding high-intensity studies.
comments.quote: I am a bit concerned about the inclusion of the studies with high light intensities, I would consider anything above 100 lux outside of ALAN impact.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the species level or a higher taxon level matters at line 689.
comments.request: Clarify the relevant taxonomic level.
comments.quote: Line 689: is the species level important here or more the higher taxon level?

reviews.assessment: Very well executed, high-standard meta-analysis whose findings are valid, with requests to expand the light-measurement discussion.
strengths: experimental design meets the highest standards
findings valid and confirm single studies

comments.issue: Light measurement and characterisation problems in the literature need more discussion and references.
comments.request: Expand this discussion with key references.
comments.quote: One general aspect I want to highlight is that the methodolgy behind light measurements and light characterization is still highly problematic

comments.issue: Very low species sample sizes for nocturnal species limit the paper's generality.
comments.request: Acknowledge this limitation explicitly.
comments.quote: Another aspect that limits the overall generality of this paper is the very low species sample sizes in the data set for nocturnal species, that are usually those considered to be most negatively affected.

comments.issue: Too many human-health references for an ecology paper; reduce to a few issues.
comments.request: Cut the list to 3-4 human health issues with one reference each.
comments.quote: I feel this paragraph has too much of them for an ecology paper (particularly given that word count is restricted for Ecology Letters)

comments.issue: Osteichthyes and Actinopterygii are shown separately although fish species are all Actinopterygii.
comments.request: Merge these categories in Figure 1.
comments.quote: As the four species of «fish» reported in Figure 3 are all Actinopterygii: Teleostei these two categories here should be merged into one group for this figure.

comments.issue: Typo: 'piratical' instead of 'practical'.
comments.request: Correct the typo.
comments.quote: p.35 l.744: practical rather than piratical?

reviews.assessment: Timely, well-written and solid quantitative synthesis; discussion should better contextualise the results and clarify study numbers and light levels.
strengths: well structured, clearly written and easy to follow

comments.issue: The abstract's 127 studies conflicts with the 38 eligible studies in the methods.
comments.request: State the actual number of included studies.
comments.quote: The abstract states that the database consisted of 127 studies, but in the methods (line 193) we learn that only 38 studies were identified as eligible and included for data extraction.

comments.issue: The white-light effect on response variability and its mechanism are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this result, including the broad-spectrum explanation.
comments.quote: White light increased response variability by 28.9% while other colors did not have statistically significant effect: this result deserves discussion.

comments.issue: The contradictory finding that prior light exposure was not an important moderator needs elaboration.
comments.request: Discuss its mechanism or possible methodological confounding.
comments.quote: Can the authors elaborate more on the contradictory result that prior light exposure was not found to be an important moderator for the impact of ALAN?

comments.issue: It is questionable whether captive versus free-living status proxies prior light exposure history.
comments.request: Justify or revise this interpretation.
comments.quote: Can living conditions (captive vs free-living species) really be interpreted as animals with and without prior light exposure history?

comments.issue: The adaptive-mechanism argument conflicts with significant melatonin suppression after long exposure.
comments.request: Reconcile this inconsistency.
comments.quote: but the melatonin suppression was still statistically significant after longer exposure, correct? How does this play in the above-mentioned argument?

comments.issue: Timing and location moderators highlight the need to standardise melatonin measurements.
comments.request: Emphasise this standardisation need.
comments.quote: it emphasizes the need for standardization of melatonin measurements for better comparability of results

comments.issue: Implications for conservation and wildlife management are not specific.
comments.request: Specify the ecological implications of melatonin suppression.
comments.quote: The authors could be more specific in what their results imply for conservation and wildlife management practices. What are the ecological implications of melatonin suppression by ALAN in wildlife?

comments.issue: The range of light levels and their real-world relevance, including skyglow, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss light levels and identify research gaps.
comments.quote: What is the range of light levels studied, and how do these light levels relate to lighting conditions in the real world?

comments.issue: Reducing light levels is a supported mitigation measure missing from the recommendations.
comments.request: Add reducing light levels as a recommendation.
comments.quote: given their result that “Higher light intensity at night was found to associate with more severe melatonin suppression” (Lines 592-593), another mitigation measure that can be recommended based on their results is reducing light levels.

comments.issue: Figure 1 label typo.
comments.request: Change the label to 'Melatonin location'.
comments.quote: Typo in Figure 1: Figure label should write “Melatonin location”

comments.issue: Incomplete sentence at lines 560-562.
comments.request: Revise the sentence.
comments.quote: 560-562 Incomplete sentence, needs revision.

title: Species sensitivities to artificial light at night: A phylogenetically controlled multilevel meta‐analysis on melatonin suppression

study.system: freshwater lakes; global ecosystem services valuation; review

editor_summary: Challenging, well-written and novel perspective; both reviewers suggest revisions, R2 specifically on valuation theory and on author examples that may inform the perspective.

reviews.assessment: Interesting update of global lake values, but the valuation philosophy, discounting debate and distributional claims need better treatment.
strengths: interesting update of annual and global lake values

comments.issue: The general methods lack a supporting reference.
comments.request: Add an IPBES or recent assessment reference for the methods.
comments.quote: can you add a reference for general methods? Either the latest from the IPBES and/or from recent assessments

comments.issue: It is unclear whether values were updated to 2020 prices.
comments.request: State whether values were updated to 2020 prices.
comments.quote: if you updated this to 2020 prices, please say so because you do refer to 2020 prices in the next section, but this is unclear here

comments.issue: The philosophy and rationale of valuation are not explained before the estimates are presented.
comments.request: Explain the valuation philosophy first, then present the range of estimates.
comments.quote: This section would be much improved if the philosophy and rationale was explained clearly first, and the range of estimates produced then presented.

comments.issue: The discount rate choice is presented one-sidedly rather than as a debated range.
comments.request: Present a discount rate range and the views supporting each.
comments.quote: You might present a range with the upper limit of 3.5% (Which personally, I think is way too high) and a lower limit of 0.1%. This allows you to present the views supporting each more neutrally.

comments.issue: Discount rates used for the social cost of carbon are generally below 3.5% and are not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention the lower social cost of carbon discount rates.
comments.quote: Note also the discount rates being used for the social cost of carbon. They are generally lower than 3.5%.

comments.issue: The time period used for the capital value is not stated.
comments.request: State the time period used for the capital value.
comments.quote: You did not state the time period used for the capital value. Was it 1,000 years? Please says so.

comments.issue: A sequence adapted from earlier studies is not cited.
comments.request: Cite the earlier studies for the adapted sequence.
comments.quote: if your sequence on page 5 lines 5–30 is adapted from earlier studies please cite them

comments.issue: The claim that the lake value is shared equally by all is only an average and ignores access issues.

comments.issue: The biosphere as a planetary life-support system is a stronger point than the distributional one.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and clearly explained perspective for ecologists, but the justification for the discount rate choice is unconvincing.

comments.issue: Rising value estimates reflect more papers and valuation methods rather than real value increases.
