comments.quote: Line 96: Error on the reference, it should be Li et al., (2019)

comments.issue: Two paragraphs on lines 265-281 share a theme but are separate.
comments.request: Unite the two paragraphs.
comments.quote: Lines 265-281: I think these two paragraphs should be united, because they share the same theme.

comments.issue: The meaning of D (difference) is not explained where it appears.
comments.request: Explain the meaning of D for clarity.
comments.quote: Line 266: For clarity, explain the meaning of D (difference) here, so the reader can follow the text in an easier way

comments.issue: The three strains are named twice where a shorter phrase would do.
comments.request: Simplify the text using 'these strains were present'.
comments.quote: Instead of naming two times these three strains, maybe simplify the text

comments.issue: The phrase 'The value was even highest' on line 276 is grammatically wrong.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence correctly.
comments.quote: Line 276: “The value was even highest” is not correctly written, please modify

comments.issue: The text on lines 378-387 is smaller and its opening lines are unclear.
comments.request: Enlarge the text and clarify its first lines.
comments.quote: Lines 378-387: This text is smaller and the first lines could be clearer.

comments.issue: Figure 4 is missing from the manuscript.
comments.request: Add Figure 4.
comments.quote: Line 406: Figure 4 is missing

reviews.assessment: Valuable and timely study, but the simplified system, presence/absence treatment of interactions and narrow literature coverage raise substantial concerns.
strengths: valuable work including an assessment of invader functionality
combination of ecological and mathematical approaches is a great asset

comments.issue: Most hypotheses discussed are not new, and citations rely heavily on the coauthors' articles.
comments.request: Cite pioneer and previous invasion-ecology work beyond the coauthors' papers.
comments.quote: most of the hypotheses that are discussed in the introduction (in the discussion also) are far from being new

comments.issue: It is unclear why MSH1 was inoculated with the resident community rather than after its establishment.
comments.request: Explain or change the timing of invader inoculation relative to community establishment.
comments.quote: If MSH1 is the invader, why inoculating this strain together with the SFI and not after the establishment of the SFI in the sand microcosms

comments.issue: The mathematical approach and its results are hard for non-specialists to follow.
comments.request: Make the mathematical approach, results and figures easier to understand for non-specialists.
comments.quote: it would be nice to find a way to make the mathematical approach and the related results easier to understand for non-specialists (this also applied to the figures)

comments.issue: Residents are analysed only as presence/absence although interactions can be density-dependent, and initial proportions likely became uneven.
comments.request: Discuss the density dependence and uneven proportions after range expansion.
comments.quote: The major weakness of this work is that SFI are analyzed using only presence and absence (see my other comments below) while it is well known that interactions can also be density-dependent.

comments.issue: It is unclear how exploitative and interference competition are distinguished from the results.
comments.request: Explain how the two competition types were distinguished.
comments.quote: I don’t fully understand how the authors are distinguishing exploitative and interference competition in their results.

comments.issue: The negative relationship holds only because of Smsh1 data at Rsfi=0 and 1; no trend is visible at higher richness.
comments.request: Emphasize this limitation when presenting the negative relationship.
comments.quote: I think that it is important here to emphasize that this negative relationship is true only because of the data for Smsh1 at Rsfi=0 and1. It is difficult to see any trend when more than 2 SFI were present.

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not add much to the paper.
comments.quote: Figure 3 is nice but it doesn’t’ add much.

comments.issue: The word 'prove' is too strong for such a simple experimental system.
comments.request: Replace 'prove' with a weaker claim.
comments.quote: please replace “prove” since the experimental system used here is too simple for such strong statement

comments.issue: The statement on line 67 also applies to microbial inoculants used as biocontrols and biofertilizers.
comments.request: Mention biocontrol and biofertilizer inoculants as additional examples.
comments.quote: True and it also applies to microbial inoculants used as biocontrols, biofertilizers

comments.issue: Abiotic factors and environmental filtering are likely as important as the biotic interactions discussed.
comments.request: Acknowledge abiotic factors and environmental filtering.
comments.quote: true but abiotic factors and environmental filtering are likely as important

comments.issue: The meaning of 'more subtle direct interaction' on line 108 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what 'more subtle direct interaction' means.
comments.quote: “more subtle direct interaction”: what do you mean?

comments.issue: The size of the sand microcosms and whether and how the sand was sterilized are not reported.
comments.request: Report microcosm size and the sand sterilization procedure.
comments.quote: How big are the sand microcosms? Was the sand sterilized and how?

comments.issue: The 7-day range expansion period seems short and it is unclear whether microcosms were fully colonized.
comments.request: Justify the 7-day period and report whether biotic capacity was reached.
comments.quote: Why only 7 days? It sounds very short in a complex environment. Were the sand microcosms entirely colonized after 7 days (in other words, was the biotic capacity reached?)

comments.issue: It is not stated whether SFI proportions in the inoculum or sand were checked after range expansion.
comments.request: Report whether SFI proportions were verified after range expansion.
comments.quote: Was the proportion of the SFI in the inoculum or in the sand after the range expansion phase checked?

comments.issue: The rationale for adding 14C-BAM after rather than before range expansion is not given.
comments.request: Explain why 14C-BAM was added after the range expansion phase.
comments.quote: What is the rationale for adding the 14C-BAM after the range expansion phase and not from the beginning?

comments.issue: More diverse communities are also more likely to contain residents that benefit the invader, complicating the negative relationship.
comments.quote: More diverse community also has a greater probability of containing resident organisms that positively impact the invader

comments.issue: The word 'grows' on line 335 should be replaced.
comments.request: Replace 'grows' with a more appropriate word.
comments.quote: L. 335: please replace “grows” here

comments.issue: Keystone species is a fuzzy, debated concept that is unnecessary at such low diversity.
comments.request: Remove or replace the keystone species terminology.
comments.quote: Keystone species is a fuzzy concept which is also quite debated. I know that it is trendy but there is really no need to use it here especially with such a low level of diversity.

title: Cooperative interactions between invader and resident microbial community members weaken the negative diversity‐invasion relationship

study.system: Arabian babbler groups; 6-year field study with remote sensing

editor_summary: All reviewers enjoyed the paper but R1 and R2 recommend statistical changes (Cox models, multiple testing, sex as predictor, continuous habitat variable) that may alter conclusions; clarify models, define group size and pace of life, tone down causal claims.

reviews.assessment: Timely, easy-to-read study with clear results, but asks for clarification of background, pace of life, habitat classification and methods details.

comments.issue: The ecological constraints explanation is out of place in the group augmentation paragraph.
comments.request: Move it to a separate paragraph and link it to the following points.
comments.quote: The explanation on ecological constraints seems out of place in this paragraph that is more focused on group size and its effect on fitness (group augmentation).

comments.issue: Background on how habitat modification may affect life history is lacking; expectations such as dispersal rates or age at first breeding are not stated.
comments.request: Add specific expectations for life-history effects and group productivity.
comments.quote: The authors first mention how habitat modification may affect life history but there is not much background information explaining what they specifically mean here.

comments.issue: 'Pace of life' is used in the title, abstract and discussion but never explained.
comments.request: Elaborate what pace of life means and how habitat modification should affect it.
comments.quote: it would be worthwhile for the authors to elaborate here on what they mean by “pace of life” (POLS, Reale et al. 2010?) mentioned in the title, abstract (L34), and discussion (L460)

comments.issue: Individual reproductive output is not explicitly compared between fast/short and slow/long males, although the contrast is implied.
comments.request: Make clear that individual reproductive output was not compared between habitat types.
comments.quote: it is important to be clear that individual reproductive output is not explicitly compared across these two males

comments.issue: Duration of the habitat modification in the region and whether classification used 6-year averages are unclear.
comments.request: Report how long modification has occurred and whether habitat classification used multi-year averages.
comments.quote: How long has this type of habitat modification been occurring in the region? And has that changed over the 6 years of the study?

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'locations' are and how they were collected, including GPS device details.
comments.request: Describe how locations were recorded and with what equipment.
comments.quote: What do you mean by “locations” and how where these collected?

comments.issue: Rainfall is annual while temperature is monthly, which may affect models of breeding variables.
comments.request: Assess and discuss the effect of mismatched temporal resolutions on the models.
comments.quote: Rainfall was measured by annual values whereas temperature was monthly; would that have affected models that address breeding variables (i.e., nesting success)?

comments.issue: A table may summarise all the GLMMs more effectively than Figure 1 alone.
comments.request: Add a table providing an overview of all GLMMs.
comments.quote: I am wondering if a table would be more effective in providing an overview of all the GLMMs generated for this study

comments.issue: More couples with known breeding age than groups that raised fledglings seems inconsistent.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy in sample sizes between these subsets.
comments.quote: How is it that there were more couples with a known age (at breeding) than all groups that raised fledglings?

comments.issue: The age variable 'days to the beginning of the year' is not explained or justified.
comments.request: Explain this age measure and why it was used instead of days since hatching.
comments.quote: I would also like clarification on age of individuals and what it means to “days to the beginning of the year”. Why did the authors use this age as opposed to days since the bird hatched?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether floaters, coalition dispersers or chased individuals were included in the Cox proportional hazards models.
comments.request: State which individuals were included in the survival models.
comments.quote: Did the CPHMs include any individuals that were observed floating, dispersed in coalitions, or chased?

comments.issue: Whether floating, coalition dispersal and chasing differ between the two habitat types is not tested.
comments.request: Compare these life-history events between modified and natural habitats.
comments.quote: And on a related note, were there differences in these life history events between the two habitat types?

comments.issue: Breeding season length is mentioned but never tested despite detailed demographic data.
comments.request: Test breeding season length or remove the mention.
comments.quote: Breeding season length is mentioned here but not actually tested? Was it not possible to test this given the detailed demographic data collected?

comments.issue: The choice of a Poisson distribution for the GLMMs is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why a Poisson distribution was used.
comments.quote: Provide a short explanation as to why Poisson distribution was used for the GLMMs.

comments.issue: The referent of 'these cues' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what 'these cues' refers to.
comments.quote: What do “these cues” refer to? The presence of smaller groups that may induce dispersal?

reviews.assessment: Interesting study, but the theoretical background, remote sensing justification and especially the survival and model-selection analyses need substantial revision.
strengths: shows faster pace of life in modified habitats

comments.issue: The theoretical background is too general; the bold abstract claim that modification is especially detrimental to social species is poorly justified.
comments.request: Elaborate on the Arabian babbler as a special case, including data on population trends and the role of sociality.
comments.quote: is poorly justified in the Introduction. You need to elaborate on the AB as a special case.

comments.issue: The purpose of remote sensing is unclear; it mainly seems to assign groups to a binary habitat category.
comments.request: Explain what remote sensing added beyond classifying mango orchards versus wadis.
comments.quote: I don’t really understand what exactly was the idea behind using remote sensing in your study.

comments.issue: Cox PH models ignore non-independence within social groups and season random effects.
comments.request: Recalculate the Cox models as mixed-effect models with group and season random effects.
comments.quote: Cox PH models have to be recalculated because you did not control for non-independence of individuals within social groups and for the random effect of seasons.

comments.issue: The 2x2 chi-squared test for renesting tendency is an oversimplification.
comments.request: Test renesting differences with a binomial GLMM including group:year as a random effect.
comments.quote: Tendency for renesting should be treated as other life-history traits and differences between groups in modified vs natural habitats should be tested using binomial GLMM (with group:year as a random effect).

comments.issue: Reducing models to only significant predictors is stepwise modelling, which is problematic.
comments.request: Report all fixed effects and beta coefficients from the original unreduced models.
comments.quote: Why did you reduced your models so that they included only significant prediction variables? This is a big issue

comments.issue: Multiple line-level edits (incomplete comparisons, abbreviation consistency, wording, citation formatting).
comments.quote: Correct the sentence so that the comparison was complete, i.e. Groups in modified habitats comparing to groups in

comments.issue: The claim that inexperienced young males led to reduced nesting success is presented as a result although experience was not tested.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence to present male experience as a hypothesis.
comments.quote: You only have a correlative evidence for age, you did not test the effect of experience.

comments.issue: The results section would be easier to follow if divided into paragraphs per life-history trait.
comments.request: Split the section into one paragraph per life-history trait.
comments.quote: Maybe it would be better to divide this part into several paragraphs (without subtitles), each one about a single life-history trait

comments.issue: Results and their explanation are mixed; male inexperience is asserted without measurement.
comments.request: Clearly separate results from explanation and state the experience claim as a hypothesis.
comments.quote: You mix, in an obscure way, reporting the results with their explanation. How do you know that males were “inexperienced”?

comments.issue: Claiming empirical evidence of fitness costs is too strong for a correlative single-species study.
comments.request: Tone down the strength of the empirical evidence claim.
comments.quote: Maybe too strong. Remember that your study was correlative and you studied only one species

comments.issue: The conclusion that cooperatively breeding species are vulnerable is overstated because the study is correlative.
comments.request: Soften 'evidence' to reflect the correlative design.
comments.quote: And, again, this study is correlative, thus “evidence” is too strong.

comments.issue: Per-group results may not scale: more groups could inhabit modified areas, giving higher landscape-level recruitment.
comments.request: Discuss the geographical-scale picture and any long-term monitoring data.
comments.quote: But maybe the total number of groups is higher in modified areas and a large-scale ARS is thus higher than in such settings?

reviews.assessment: Interesting with an impressive suite of analyses, but organization, hypotheses framing and several methodological choices need clarification and possible modification.
strengths: valuable contribution to the anthropization literature

comments.issue: The large number of analyses and variables makes the organization hard to follow; more signposting and scaffolding are needed.
comments.request: Guide the reader through the analyses and scaffold concepts and variables.
comments.quote: the manuscript will be stronger if the authors make an extra effort to guide the reader through the analyses and scaffold the concepts and variables

comments.issue: The introduction lacks broad hypotheses and a clear distinction between hypotheses and predictions for the tested variables.
comments.request: State general hypotheses, or add a prediction for every variable tested.
comments.quote: The introduction would benefit from broader hypotheses and a clearer differentiation between hypotheses and predictions.

comments.issue: Variables are referred to inconsistently (e.g. success vs breeding success; attempts vs events).
comments.request: Use consistent variable names throughout.
comments.quote: For example, is “success” the same as “breeding success”? On line 322, is “breeding attempts” the same as “breeding events”?

comments.issue: Model formulas are missing from the methods.
comments.request: Add model formulas to the methods section.
comments.quote: Adding model formulas to the methods section could help the reader keep the models straight.

comments.issue: The discussion is not organized in parallel with the introduction.
comments.request: Organize the discussion along the same broad categories.
comments.quote: Organizing the discussion in parallel with the introduction, perhaps along the broad categories of “life history” and “fitness” once again.

comments.issue: The role of group size in the conceptual framework is unclear: response, fitness measure or life-history measure?
comments.request: Clarify how group size fits into the overall framework.
comments.quote: I would appreciate a clarification as to how group size fits into the overall conceptual framework of the analysis

comments.issue: Group size is defined inconsistently across methods, results and Figure 4A (adults plus subadults vs individuals vs adults).
comments.request: Define group size consistently.
comments.quote: Then, in the results section, “group size” is defined as the “average number of individuals”, but Figure 4A only refers to the number of adults.

comments.issue: The claim that smaller group size induced earlier dominance acquisition and dispersal was not tested as a predictor.
comments.request: Remove the causal claim or justify it with a proper analysis.
comments.quote: I don’t think that the analyses actually tested group size as a predictor for these life history traits

comments.issue: The introduction and discussion present findings granularly without synthesizing them or linking to broader life-history and pace-of-life theory.
comments.request: Draw broad conclusions and connect findings to life-history theory.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to spend more time on drawing broad conclusions about the benefits and drawbacks of habitat modification, and its general effects on the babblers.

comments.issue: Many analyses share the same habitat-type predictor, raising a multiple comparisons problem.
comments.request: Apply statistical corrections or justify their absence.
comments.quote: With so many analyses run with the same predictor variable (habitat type), I worry about the multiple comparisons fallacy. Have any statistical corrections been considered?

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'group location' means and how tightly clustered group members are.
comments.request: Define group location and explain how it was computed.
comments.quote: What is meant by “group location”? For those of us who are not used to the movements of babblers: how tightly clustered are the individuals in a group at any given time?

comments.issue: '4665 locations' does not specify whether these are group, individual or independent locations.
comments.request: Clarify the unit of the location count, perhaps using 'relocations' or 'sightings'.
comments.quote: “4665 locations” Does this refer to group locations (see my comment about 123), individual locations, or locations independent of the presence of individuals?

comments.issue: How the 0.7 threshold and manual classification were combined is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how automatic and manual habitat classification were used together.
comments.quote: The 0.7 threshold value suggests automatic classification of the landscape into modified vs. not, but then the next sentence suggests manual classification based on observation of the landscape.

comments.issue: The SDM approach models potential rather than realized territories and may under-predict avoided habitats; justification is insufficient.
comments.request: Justify the SDM method or use observed locations or MCP/KUD territories instead.
comments.quote: By obtaining per-pixel suitability values, the SDMs run here seem to be returning information about the groups’ potential territories, rather than their realized or actual territories.

comments.issue: Habitat was made categorical although it likely varies continuously, reducing statistical power.
comments.request: Use distance to modified habitat as a continuous variable or justify the binary split.
comments.quote: Why was this continuous variable made categorical? It would increase the statistical power of the models to use “distance to modified habitat” as a continuous variable

comments.issue: The difference and purpose of the group-level versus couple-level analyses is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify how the two analysis levels differ and why both were run.
comments.quote: Add clarification about the difference between the group-level and couple-level analysis. This confused me throughout–if each group has one breeding pair, then what is the difference between these two?

comments.issue: Why two different datasets were used, and how their results were expected to differ, is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the purpose of using two datasets.
comments.quote: Add explanation of why there were two different datasets used. How did you expect the results to differ? Why not pick one?

comments.issue: The abbreviation 'CPHMs' is used without definition or citation.
comments.request: Define and cite CPHMs.
comments.quote: Define and cite “CPHMs”. I was able to figure it out from the figure caption, but it wasn’t clear what this referred to.

comments.issue: How predictors were chosen for each model, and why models differ in predictors, is unclear.
comments.request: Justify predictor selection or report any automatic model selection procedure.
comments.quote: How were the predictor variables for each model chosen, and why did different models include different predictors?

comments.issue: Separate models for males and females were used instead of sex as a categorical predictor.
comments.request: Include sex as a predictor in a single model.
comments.quote: Why were separate models used for males and females, instead of including sex as a categorical predictor?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the listed models are final reduced models or the initial variable set, and final formulas are not given.
comments.request: Provide justifications for initial variables and formulas for final models.
comments.quote: It is unclear whether this means that every model started with every predictor and was reduced down to what is listed here (i.e. the listed models are the final models)

comments.issue: Multiple line-level copy edits (citations, wording, terminology, parenthetical placement).
comments.quote: 132 Should be “Israel Nature and Parks Authority”

comments.issue: 'Resources' is used vaguely and never specified (water/nutrients/biomass?).
comments.request: Clarify what 'resources' means throughout.
comments.quote: Clarify what is meant by “resources”--primarily water/nutrients, leading to increased biomass?

comments.issue: The paragraph shifts abruptly from ecosystem-level to species- and individual-level impacts.
comments.request: Signpost the change of level for the reader.
comments.quote: This paragraph begins with very broad statements about ecosystem-level impacts of anthropization, and then it moves down to the species and individual level

comments.issue: The relevance of the ecological constraint hypothesis to environment-fitness relationships is not fleshed out.
comments.request: Make the connection between the ecological constraint hypothesis and fitness clearer.
comments.quote: Flesh out the relevance of the ecological constraint hypothesis to the relationship between environment and fitness

comments.issue: The section lacks a reference to Figure 2 and the map lacks reserve boundary labels.
comments.request: Add a Figure 2 reference and label reserve boundaries.
comments.quote: Add a reference to Figure 2–it’s helpful to look at the map when reading this section. Consider also adding a label to Figure 2 to indicate reserve boundaries?

comments.issue: The reason for excluding individuals that moved to a different group is not given.
comments.request: Explain the exclusion criterion.
comments.quote: Why exclude individuals that moved to a different group?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the renesting independence test was a separate analysis or a preliminary check, and it is missing from the diagram.
comments.request: Clarify the role of the renesting independence test.
comments.quote: Unclear whether this was a separate analysis (in which case, why is it omitted from the diagram?) or a preliminary check in order to be able to use the variables in a bigger model

comments.issue: Assumptions testing is described in more detail than needed in the main text.
comments.request: Condense the assumptions testing description.
comments.quote: Seems like assumptions testing; maybe doesn’t need to be described in detail in the main text.

comments.issue: 'Strong evidence' and 'moderate evidence' are used as if standardized but are not defined.
comments.request: Define these terms or remove some instances.
comments.quote: The results section uses the terms “strong evidence” and “moderate evidence” in a way that implies that these are standardized terms. If they are standardized, define what is meant

comments.issue: Strong causal language such as 'affected' is used throughout despite the correlative design.
comments.request: Tone down causal language throughout the paper.
comments.quote: Careful with the use of “affected” and other strong causal language throughout the paper.

comments.issue: Panels 4b and 4c have non-descriptive y-axis titles.
comments.request: Use descriptive y-axis titles such as 'age of dispersal'.
comments.quote: 4b and 4c–include more descriptive y axis titles, such as “age of dispersal” and “age of dominance acquisition”

comments.issue: Whether individuals can belong to more than one group during a season is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the group membership criterion.
comments.quote: can an individual ever be part of more than one group, or different groups over the course of the season?

title: Living fast, dying young: Anthropogenic habitat modification influences the fitness and life history traits of a cooperative breeder

study.system: grassland plant communities; foliar fungal diseases across 63 Chinese sites

editor_summary: Critical but positive reviews; editor asks for revisions addressing nestedness, explanation of the Leps framework, and careful improvement of the Discussion.

reviews.assessment: Novel comparison of turnover and intraspecific variation in the dilution effect, but the methods are hard to follow and some analyses need clarification.
strengths: novel comparison of species turnover and intraspecific variation
contributes to understanding the generality of the dilution effect

comments.issue: The Methods are hard to follow; levels of analysis and model responses and predictors are unclear.
comments.request: Reorganize the Methods and state response and predictors for every model.
comments.quote: the authors should re-organize their Methods section to make it easy to follow. Particularly, the authors should explicitly indicate the response and predictors when mentioned a statistical model.

comments.issue: Whether the study was a field survey or a control experiment with fixed richness (1, 2, 4) is unclear.
comments.request: Separate study area and experimental design, or provide more detail.
comments.quote: The authors said they did field survey, but it seems more likely that they did control experiments as the species richness was fixed as 1,2,4.

comments.issue: The effect of nestedness on the diversity-disease slope is not tested, though it is proposed as the reason temperature matters.
comments.request: Test the effect of nestedness on the diversity-disease slope.
comments.quote: Why not also test the effect of nestedness on the slope of diversity-disease relationship.

comments.issue: The Leps framework (species turnover and intraspecific variation) is explained too briefly for non-experts.
comments.request: Expand the explanation of the Leps framework in the Introduction.
comments.quote: I suggest to give more explanation of the Leps framework (i.e., species turnover and intraspecific variation) in INTRODUCTION, as these concepts are fundamental for the study.

comments.issue: “Biodiversity-disease relationship” is too broad a term; the study addresses host plant diversity only.
comments.request: Use “diversity-disease relationship” instead.
comments.quote: the “biodiversity” means “host plant diversity”. Therefore, I suggest to use “diversity-disease relationship”.

comments.issue: Both non-random diversity loss and low-competent host effects are prerequisites of the dilution effect, but this is not made clear.
comments.request: State both prerequisites and cite Huang et al. 2016.
comments.quote: This means that both the non-random diversity loss and the negative effect of low-competent hosts should be meet to generate the dilution effect.

comments.issue: The Lacroix et al. 2014 reference for non-random biodiversity loss is missing.
comments.request: Add “Lacroix et al. 2014” as a reference.
comments.quote: also add “Lacroix et al. 2014” here as a reference for the non-random biodiversity loss.

comments.issue: “Non-hosts” is misleading for multi-host pathogens with variable competence.
comments.request: Use low-competent or low-quality hosts instead of non-hosts.
comments.quote: I would prefer to use low-competent hosts or low-quality hosts rather than non-hosts.

comments.issue: Distances between sites are not reported.
comments.request: Report the shortest, mean and longest distances between sites.
comments.quote: Line 118: Please indicate the distances between sites (the shortest, mean and longest distances)

comments.issue: Vegetation types in the text do not match those in Figure 1.
comments.request: Keep vegetation type naming consistent between text and figure.
comments.quote: The three vegetation types mentioned here are not consistent with those in Figure 1, please keep the manuscript consistent

comments.issue: Community pathogen load is disease burden, not the single-disease risk usually studied in diversity-disease work.
comments.request: Discuss the difference between disease burden and single-disease risk.
comments.quote: this pathogen load should be considered as disease burden rather than the disease risk traditionally considered in the diversity-disease relationship

comments.issue: How disease severity (vi) was calculated is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how disease severity was calculated from the 25 leaves.
comments.quote: Line 150: How to calculate the disease severity (vi)? I mean did you calculated it by dividing all disease area by the sum of 25 leaf areas?

comments.issue: The Fisher Z transformation is justified only by the ratio scale of the data, not by non-normal residuals.
comments.request: Justify the transformation also by non-normality of model residuals.
comments.quote: the reason is not only that intraspecific variation of pathogen load is ratio data from -1 to 1, but more importantly that the transformation can overcome non-normality of the residuals of the model

comments.issue: Handling of non-significant coefficients is not described.
comments.request: State whether non-significant coefficients were set to zero or kept.
comments.quote: How to deal with the non-significant coefficients? As zeros or original coefficents?

comments.issue: “Stronger” is ambiguous between effect size and coefficient significance.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence as at Line 254.
comments.quote: Line 251: I think here it’s not appropriate to use “stronger” which could be either effect size or coefficients’ significance.

comments.issue: The sentence at Lines 258-259 is difficult to follow.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence.
comments.quote: Line 258-259: Difficult to follow, please rephrase the sentence.

comments.issue: The stated positive effect of MAT on nestedness contradicts the figure, where low T-value means high nestedness.
comments.request: Correct the direction of the MAT effect on nestedness throughout.
comments.quote: so I think it should be “The MAT had a negative effect on community nestedness”

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits (wording, deletions, abbreviations).
comments.quote: Line 105-106: should be “ranged from” instead of “range of”

reviews.assessment: Important content and potentially novel claims, but the Introduction and Discussion need restructuring and justifications.

comments.issue: Soil sampling appears in the Methods without introduction or rationale.
comments.request: Introduce soil sampling and its rationale in the Introduction.
comments.quote: the method of soil sampling is mentioned in the Methods section without prior mention in the Introduction, and its rationale is not provided

comments.issue: Community nestedness is not properly introduced.
comments.request: Introduce nestedness earlier in the paper.
comments.quote: Additionally, the aspect of community nestedness is not properly introduced.

comments.issue: Only the argument that resistant individuals are lost at higher rates is developed.
comments.request: Also develop the argument that susceptible individuals are lost at higher rates.
comments.quote: while it is argued that resistant individuals are lost at higher rates, it could also be argued, based on other studies, that susceptible individuals are lost at higher rates

comments.issue: The mapping of species turnover and intraspecific variation onto mechanisms is not stated explicitly.
comments.request: State explicitly which parameter represents which mechanism.
comments.quote: “Species turnover” is used to represent non-random species loss (mechanism 3), and “Intraspecific variation” to represent specific biotic interactions (mechanisms 1 and 2), if so it should be stated explicitly

comments.issue: It is unclear how natural plots could have distinct biodiversity levels of 1, 2 or 4 species.
comments.request: Explain how plots with fixed richness levels were obtained without an experiment.
comments.quote: It was not clear (line 128) how you can you have plots with distinct biodiversity levels (1, 2, 4 species) if you are not performing an experimental study, but are sampling natural plots?

comments.issue: Host regulation and encounter reduction are claimed as detected, though methods assess them jointly as biotic interactions.
comments.request: Show how host regulation and encounter reduction can be distinguished.
comments.quote: can you really distinguish the host regulation effects from the encounter reduction effects?

comments.issue: Whether grassland type influenced results, given it was accounted for in sampling, is unclear.
comments.request: Report whether grassland type played a role in the results.
comments.quote: does the grassland types played any role as they were accounted for sampling?

comments.issue: The Discussion needs thorough restructuring around the key findings and their implications.
comments.request: Rewrite the Discussion with clear implications of the main findings.
comments.quote: The discussion section requires a thorough re-analysis, particularly regarding the most prominent results concerning the general prevalence and temperature-dependence of negative biodiversity-disease relationships

comments.issue: The claim that results provide a basis for conservation and disease control lacks discussion of how they support it.
comments.request: Explain how the results support the conservation and disease-control claims.
comments.quote: this claim lacks a clear discussion on how their results support it

reviews.assessment: Interesting and valuable contribution, but several concepts, methods and figures need clearer explanation.
strengths: strong field test for the dilution effect
large number of plots and sites
valuable contribution to the dilution-effect literature

comments.issue: The contrast between host community composition, host regulation, encounter reduction and non-random biodiversity loss is confusing.
comments.request: Introduce these terms differently or state clearly how they are distinguished.
comments.quote: We felt like the differentiation between the importance of host community composition on host regulation, encounter reduction, and non-random biodiversity loss was a little confusing.

comments.issue: Plot selection within sites is not described, nor whether sites were chosen to contain 1, 2 or 4 species.
comments.request: Report how plots were placed and whether richness levels were selected or observed.
comments.quote: were sites selected explicitly to contain 1, 2, or 4 herbaceous species or are you merely reporting the outcome that those were the only values of species richness recording within these plots?

comments.issue: Species turnover and interspecific variation are used without detailed definitions, relying on a citation.
comments.request: Provide detailed definitions of these terms in the section.
comments.quote: We would strongly suggest providing detailed definitions of these terms in this section rather than merely citing the Leps et al. 2011 paper.

comments.issue: The STE equation is hard to follow; it is not clear it is calculated at plot level or how subscripts work.
comments.request: Clarify the subscripts and plot-level calculation of the STE.
comments.quote: it was not immediately clear that the STE was calculated at the plot-level from the equation

comments.issue: The snapshot design cannot exclude other processes such as phenological differences among sites.
comments.request: Discuss whether phenology or other processes could drive the apparent effects.
comments.quote: phenological differences across sites that vary significantly in mean temperature could be driving the apparent effects

comments.issue: It is unclear whether points in Figure 3 represent sites or plots.
comments.request: Clarify what points represent in each figure.
comments.quote: It would be helpful for readers to clarify what the points represent in each figure, since the study has a hierarchical design.

comments.issue: The takeaway message of Figure 4, especially panel b, is hard to distill.
comments.request: Stress the main points of Figure 4 in the text and caption.
comments.quote: we struggled to distill down a clear, concise takeaway message from this figure, especially panel b

comments.issue: Figure 4a causal relationships run sideways rather than top-to-bottom.
comments.request: Flip the figure so causal relationships move top-to-bottom.
comments.quote: It may be more visually pleasing to flip the figure so that the causal relationships move top-to-bottom.

title: Diversity inhibits foliar fungal diseases in grasslands: Potential mechanisms and temperature dependence

study.system: simulation study of ectotherm thermal performance curves

editor_summary: Reviewer 1 had no scientific concerns but asked to remove condescending or sarcastic remarks; reviewer 2 gave an exceptionally detailed report that the response should benefit from.

reviews.assessment: Detailed critique: the response is too dismissive, the simulation is essentially genotype sorting, and the G-matrices are invalid.
strengths: right that all parameters are simulated at once
right that no equilibrium claim was made

comments.issue: 'Constraint' is misused for any covariance; only covariation opposing selection is a constraint.
comments.request: Use 'constraint' only for covariances opposing selection.
comments.quote: although I would not call just a covariance going in the direction of selection a “constraint” in any context, this seems to me an abuse of vocabulary

comments.issue: Without mutation, segregation or recombination the simulation is mere sorting of pre-existing genotypes, adding little value.
comments.request: Add segregation/recombination or derive the results from the G-matrix.
comments.quote: the total absence of mutation, segregation and recombination in the original simulation is making the evolutionary process a mere “sorting” of pre-existing genotypes

comments.issue: The simulated population grows unrealistically fast (lambda near 6-12), making the climate scenarios overly optimistic.
comments.request: Justify or correct the overly optimistic population growth rates.
comments.quote: the authors are simulating a particularly thriving (though density-regulated) population, while real populations should have a lambda closer to 1

comments.issue: The response is too dismissive and misses the core concern about temporal temperature variation.
comments.request: Engage with the temporal-variation concern directly.
comments.quote: it is very unclear how their assumption that the species is thermoconformer should justify low temporal (daily) variation in their simulations

comments.issue: The response fails to address whether standing variation is enriched in pre-adapted genotypes; the G-matrix could be swapped for the M-matrix with identical results.
comments.request: Address the pre-adapted genotype issue directly.
comments.quote: the authors could replace the G-matrix by the M-matrix (the mutation matrix), ignoring mutation afterwise, with the exact same results in their simulation

comments.issue: The G-matrices are not positive-semidefinite, so the simulations are not numerically correct.
comments.request: Use valid positive-semidefinite G-matrices and rerun.
comments.quote: the G-matrices used in the scenarios GSTO and GSTO+TDE are NOT proper variance-covariance matrices, as they are not positive-semidefinite (one of the eigen-values is negative)

comments.issue: The corrections for overlapping critical temperatures introduce hidden covariances absent from the G-matrix.
comments.request: Reflect these covariances in the G-matrix.
comments.quote: the “corrections” for, e.g. when the critical temperatures overlap Topt, are also introducing hidden covariances that should rather have been reflected in the G-matrix

comments.issue: Both sides wrongly focus on Pmax variance; marginal variances are equal and the real issue is the Topt-Pmax covariance.
comments.request: Refocus the argument on the Topt-Pmax covariance.
comments.quote: On average, the starting variation in Pmax should be the same for all scenarios, because they share the same marginal variance

comments.issue: CTmax is the key evolving parameter, and its negative covariance with Pmax constrains its evolution.
comments.request: Acknowledge this true constraint on CTmax evolution.
comments.quote: there is a very important constraint, a true one, in these scenarios for the population to evolve their CTmax to bear higher temperatures

comments.issue: Daily temperature variance is fixed to 1 instead of being derived from empirical expectations, affecting quantitative conclusions.
comments.request: Base the daily temperature variance on empirical expectations.
comments.quote: the daily variance in temperature should as well, and not be fixed to 1 because it seems convenient

comments.issue: Five generations are unlikely to bring the population close to equilibrium given the lack of segregation.
comments.request: Justify or extend the burn-in period.
comments.quote: I am extremely doubtful such equilibrium is reached in 5 generations, especially given the lack of segregation

comments.issue: 'Tmins' should be 'CTmin' to match the original paper.
comments.request: Use 'CTmin' consistently.
comments.quote: l.59: “Tmins”, I would rather use “CTmin” like in the original paper.

comments.issue: The claim about narrow daily variation is ill-posed and the emphasis on 'fitness TPC' is unclear.
comments.request: Reframe the argument and clarify the fitness TPC emphasis.
comments.quote: I believe this is ill-posed, since the problem is rather that are few (maybe a cave, or even a particularly stable tropical island) such thermal environment with narrow daily variation

comments.issue: Misunderstandings about the theory are shared by both sides of the exchange.
comments.quote: There are indeed misunderstandings about the structure of the simulations, but I find the misunderstandings of theory is quite shared here.

comments.issue: Calling the simulation 'the appropriate way to model fitness for thermoconformers' is an overstatement.
comments.request: Temper this claim about fitness modelling.
comments.quote: I do not see how the original paper simulation is “the appropriate way to model fitness for thermoconformers”, I think this is an overstatement

comments.issue: The initial trait distribution and equal genetic variances across parameters are not biologically realistic.
comments.request: Use realistic, parameter-specific genetic variances.
comments.quote: the G-matrix is not realistic because it is highly unlikely for the genetic variances to be on the same scale for all parameters

comments.issue: Schluter's result is misstated: correlations create a greater-variation axis, not more variation in original traits.
comments.request: Correct the description of Schluter's result.
comments.quote: the main result from Schluter is that correlations generate a particular axis with greater variation (gmax in the paper), not that it generates more variation in the original traits themselves

comments.issue: The description of VS et al's stance is unfair; they recognise that correlations play a strong role.
comments.request: Represent the comment's stance fairly.
comments.quote: I am not sure that this is a fair description of VS et al stance, they do recognise that the correlations play a strong role

comments.issue: 'Pre-adaptive' is new terminology and not a conclusion from the original paper.
comments.request: Clarify or drop the new term.
comments.quote: note that “pre-adaptive” is new, and not a conclusion from the original paper, however

comments.issue: The 'counter-intuitive' framing originates from the original paper, which should be acknowledged.
comments.quote: I would say the notion of it being “counter-intuitive” comes from the original paper.

comments.issue: The claim that Pmax is adjusted to maintain a constant integral misdescribes the simulation process; all parameters are drawn at once.
comments.request: Correct the description of the simulation process.
comments.quote: the idea that Pmax is adjusted after the other parameters to meet a constraint of a constant integral being maintained does not reflect my understanding of the original paper simulation process

comments.issue: Calling the standing-variation problem 'unsupported' is too strong, as it follows directly from the G-matrix covariances.
comments.request: Soften the 'unsupported' claim.
comments.quote: I would not go as far as to say “unsupported”, since this issue of what the standing variation is composed of directly comes from the covariances in the G-matrices

comments.issue: The consequences expected from the low-temperature-variation issue are not made clear.
comments.request: State clearly how the temperature issue affects the results.
comments.quote: In any case, this is my own take and VS et al should be clearer in the consequences they expect with regard to their first point raised.

title: Response to von Schmalensee et al.

study.system: bats and arthropods; white-nose syndrome declines; paired roost and control sites

editor_summary: Work is clear and important but needs major reorganization for Ecology Letters: abstract context, separate Results and Discussion, figure clarity, and SI metadata.

reviews.assessment: Likes the approach and robust analysis; asks about control-site landscape features and additional checks.

comments.issue: Control sites only 50-100m from treatments may differ in landscape features such as standing water.
comments.request: Check whether landscape features differ between paired sites.
comments.quote: Are there particular landscape features (e.g. available standing water) that might be different (or the same) between sites?

comments.issue: The concern about overlap with 1 for ratios versus contrasts is unclear at Line 106.
comments.request: Clarify whether the concern applies to ratios or contrasts.
comments.quote: Maybe I misunderstand, but shouldn't the concern be overlap with 1 if it is a ratio (e.g. 0.93)

comments.issue: Whether contrasts track the relative decline is untested, and community composition shifts are not assessed.
comments.request: Test the contrast-decline relationship and run NMDS.
comments.quote: is it worth analyzing the community composition using NMDS and assess directional shifts?

comments.issue: Figure 2 lacks the Wisconsin border and inset, and the US map scale bar is inaccurate.
comments.request: Add the Wisconsin inset and remove or fix the scale bar.
comments.quote: On Figure 2, is it possible to add the Wisconsin border and associated inset from Figure 4?

comments.issue: Figure 4B includes Site D, which was excluded from the analysis.
comments.request: Remove Site D from Figure 4B.
comments.quote: I don't think you need Site D because it was excluded from the analysis.

reviews.assessment: Exceptionally well-written and transparent, but the predator-release conclusion is overstated and sites are not truly paired.
strengths: extremely clear and transparent hypotheses, data and analysis
reports all results and effect sizes

comments.issue: Predator release is overstated: few effects exclude zero and there is no consistent arthropod response.
comments.request: Temper the predator-release conclusion.
comments.quote: Of the 64 estimated effects in Figure 3a, four have confidence intervals that do not overlap zero, and three of those are for the same year.

comments.issue: Control sites up to 10km away cannot be treated as paired given strong spatial variation in insects.
comments.request: Acknowledge that sites are not truly paired.
comments.quote: the control sites (i.e. low bat activity) are up to 10km away from the treatment sites (i.e. roosts). Insects vary so much across space that these cannot reasonably be considered as paired sampling sites

comments.issue: Fewer samples in 2015 suggest unusual site conditions or small-sample bias.
comments.request: Explain the reduced 2015 sampling and its consequences.
comments.quote: There is also overall fewer samples (supplemental data) in 2015

comments.issue: Patterns at the two abandoned bat roosts are not examined.
comments.request: Check whether the abandoned-roost patterns support the hypothesis.
comments.quote: I am curious if the authors looked to see what the patterns of arthropod abundance were between treatment and control sites for the two bat roosts that were abandoned

comments.issue: The supplemental file name 's3.bug.declines' is inaccurate.
comments.request: Rename the supplementary data file.
comments.quote: Supplemental Data s3.bug.declines should be renamed because a) not all the arthropods are bugs, and b) not everything is declining

title: Heterogenous effects of bat declines from white‐nose syndrome on arthropods

study.system: seven grass species with Epichloë endophytes; removal experiment and demographic models

editor_summary: Editor: four substantive, generally very positive reviews; looks forward to a revised version.

reviews.assessment: Real pleasure to read; critical, innovative and carefully explained work with only two minor concerns.

comments.issue: Conclusions should be tempered because spatial variation and habitat heterogeneity are not addressed; study covers a small, homogeneous portion of the range.
comments.request: Temper conclusions and acknowledge spatial and habitat limitations.
comments.quote: The first is a suggestion to temper their conclusions because the study still does not address the role of spatial variation and habitat heterogeneity, which may change these results in unpredictable ways.

comments.issue: The P. sylvestris Spikes/Infl. model fits poorly at the left of the abscissa despite the largest sample size.
comments.request: Check and explain the poor model fit.
comments.quote: the model of P. sylvestris of Spikes/Infl. in page 25 does not fit well the data in the left portion of the abscissa range

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed the paper; asks for broader evolutionary context, clarity on methods-results links, more reported estimates, and better variance figures.

comments.issue: Missing discussion relating results to broader evolutionary ideas (phenotypic variance, bet hedging, conservative bet hedging).
comments.request: Add broader-context discussion including recent symbiont literature.
comments.quote: I am missing some discussion on such points, that put the results of this study in a broader context and that include other recent ideas on how symbionts may benefit hosts under changing environments.

comments.issue: It is not clear the analysis actually tests context-dependency, since endophyte effects are generally positive across years.
comments.request: Clarify how context-dependence is tested.
comments.quote: I am not convinced that this is what is actually tested (but maybe I’m missing something).

comments.issue: No conceptual figure illustrates the hypothesis or the study design and approach.
comments.request: Add a conceptual figure and study-design schematic.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to illustrate their hypothesis (L134) in a conceptual figure early on in the manuscript, and perhaps even adding a schematic overview of the study design and approach

comments.issue: Link between methods and results is hard to follow; how core parameters are calculated and linked to Eq. 2 and Fig. 1 is unclear.
comments.request: Improve clarity and explicitly link equations, parameters and results.
comments.quote: My main suggestion here is to improve clarity, as I found it not always easy to follow the text, in particular the link between the methods and results sections.

comments.issue: Coefficient estimates, credible intervals, variance components and lambda estimates are not provided.
comments.request: Provide all estimates, intervals and variance components.
comments.quote: Please provide all coefficients, credible intervals, and variance components (either in the main text or in an appendix).

comments.issue: Fig. 1D-E and similar appendix figures are difficult to interpret.
comments.request: Visualise endophyte effects on inter-annual variance differently.
comments.quote: I appreciate the attempt to show the amount of variation between years in Fig. 1D-E, but these graphs are difficult to interpret

comments.issue: Fig. 4 decomposition is not broken down by vital rate, so drivers and climate sensitivity are unclear.
comments.request: Extend the decomposition across vital rates.
comments.quote: Could this analysis be extended, further decomposing it into the contributions through each of the different vital rates?

comments.issue: Mean predictions fit poorly in some cases (adult growth in P. sylvestris and P. alsodes, flowering in L. arundinacaea).
comments.request: Explain the poor fits.
comments.quote: there are a few cases where the mean predictions seem to be quite off, not following the data so well

comments.issue: Strength of phylogenetic signal in life-history traits is not reported.
comments.request: Report phylogenetic signal estimates.
comments.quote: L382: How strong was the phylogenetic signal in each of the life history traits?

comments.issue: Asks whether the bottom-left corner of Fig. 2C represents conservative bet hedging.
comments.request: Clarify the interpretation of Fig. 2C.
comments.quote: Is the bottom left corner where the symbionts lead to conservative bet hedging?

reviews.assessment: Well-written, timely and impressive dataset; many clarity points, mainly around methods, terminology and additional life-history analyses.

comments.issue: Keywords duplicate title words.
comments.request: Use keywords not already in the title.
comments.quote: Keywords: I would recommend using keywords not already in the title.

comments.issue: Claim that global change increases variability everywhere is inaccurate; should cite Bathiany et al. and reframe around high-biodiversity areas.
comments.request: Cite Bathiany et al. and qualify the claim.
comments.quote: GCC is not increasing environmental variability everywhere. See Bathiany et al. (2018) Science Advances.

comments.issue: Final sentence at L98 needs citations (Tuljapurkar papers, Doak et al.).
comments.request: Add the recommended citations.
comments.quote: This final sentence needs some citations for this sort of claim.

comments.issue: Equation 1 log symbol renders like three variables; italics should be removed.
comments.request: Fix the equation typesetting.
comments.quote: Right now, log is being rendered looking like three separate variables. Perhaps remove the italics and make normal text.

comments.issue: Point flagged at L116: negative correlations among vital rates need attention.
comments.request: Address negative correlations among vital rates.
comments.quote: L116: Negative correlations among vital rates

comments.issue: Transition to the microbe paragraph is abrupt; the introduction is lean and could start from general buffering mechanisms.
comments.request: Smooth the introduction and add buffering-mechanism context.
comments.quote: The introduction starts with a very concise journey through the fundamental ideas of stochastic demography that support the paper, and then, out of nowhere, a first-time reader is told about the roles of symbiotic microbes.

comments.issue: Variance and stochasticity terms are ambiguous (temporal versus spatial); 'temporal' should be added where appropriate.
comments.request: Specify temporal before these terms.
comments.quote: throughout the introduction, many terms such as variance and stochasticity have been stated. I would highly recommend adding the word temporal before quite a few of them

comments.issue: 'Buffer hosts against variability' is too vague; what is buffered and whether it is individual or population level is unclear.
comments.request: Be explicit about what is buffered and at what level.
comments.quote: This (“buffer hosts against variability”) is too vague to the non-buffering indoctrinated reader.

comments.issue: Sentence at L141 could be inverted for a smoother transition.
comments.request: Invert the sentence.
comments.quote: Would make the transition to the new paragraph a little smoother.

comments.issue: 'Variance buffering' and 'demographic buffering' are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Standardise terminology across the manuscript.
comments.quote: Throughout the introduction, “variance buffering” has been used. This is the first introduction of “demographic buffering.”

comments.issue: Reviewer asks whether an estimate of the size is available at L194.
comments.request: Provide the relevant size estimate.
comments.quote: L194: Any estimate of the size?

comments.issue: Model is effectively a generalized integral projection model with two states but is not described as such; a life cycle graph would help.
comments.request: State the model type and add a life cycle graph.
comments.quote: isn’t the model a generalized integral projection model with two states? If this is the case, I don’t see why this is not stated

comments.issue: Matrix/kernel stochastic approach is unjustified versus parameter stochastic, and lambda-s is not standardised across variance treatments.
comments.request: Justify the approach and standardise lambda-s.
comments.quote: Is there are reason the methods includes a matrix stochastic approach instead of parameter stochastic approach

comments.issue: 'Reference condition' at L377 is undefined.
comments.request: Define reference condition.
comments.quote: L.377: What is meant by reference condition?

comments.issue: 'Average' is loaded since lambda-s is also an average; terminology should distinguish arithmetic and geometric means.
comments.request: Standardise to arithmetic and geometric means.
comments.quote: Saying average is a bit loaded, lambda-s is also an average. I would recommend thinking of standardizing terminology to the arithmetic and geometric means.

comments.issue: Sentence at L443 is very hard to read.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: L.443: This is a very tricky sentence to read and understand.

comments.issue: Fig. 3 uses only longevity; other pace-of-life components and R0 or Demetrius entropy should be analysed; seven points is weak.
comments.request: Broaden the life-history trait analyses.
comments.quote: To show the impact of life history, I would recommend showing the impacts of other components of POLS (e.g., generation time, Keyfitz entropy).

comments.issue: Unclear whether buffering rescues populations across scenarios.
comments.request: Show persistence outcomes across scenarios.
comments.quote: does the increased positive effect of symbiosis on lambda-s rescue the populations?

reviews.assessment: Appropriate system and approach, but vital-rate correlations and elasticities are overlooked and the variance result is long known.

comments.issue: The simulation result that lower variance raises long-term growth is already well known.
comments.quote: The authors provide simulations that demonstrate what has long been known – that decreasing variance in vital rates (and thus in annual population growth rates) increases long-term stochastic population growth rates.

comments.issue: Eq. 1 omits vital-rate correlations and elasticities; the small-noise approximation would give a more complete picture.
comments.request: Incorporate or note correlation and elasticity effects.
comments.quote: long term population growth rates depend not just on the variability (or noise) in population vital rates, but also upon the correlations between these vital rates
