title: Time is of the essence: A general framework for uncovering temporal structures of communities

study.system: long-term studies; mentorship and inclusion survey in ecology

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers suggest improving generalization beyond the co-authors' specific experience; and stresses that the survey's IRB/human-research ethics status must be formally clarified or the data removed.

reviews.assessment: Good points but presented as an unachievable, self-congratulatory model from one well-resourced programme; key terms are undefined and the survey lacks human-research ethics approval.

comments.issue: The programme is the exception to the rule, but the manuscript reads as self-congratulatory and unachievable for most ecologists.
comments.request: Acknowledge this and include insights from less well-resourced systems and countries.
comments.quote: it really, genuinely, is the exception to the rule. That must be acknowledged more as, at present, this reads as mostly a self-congratulatory pat on the back that is unachievable by the overwhelming majority of ecologists.

comments.issue: Many statements are unreferenced.
comments.request: Add references, e.g. at L107.
comments.quote: While I recognize this is a “viewpoint” article, many statements (e.g., L 107) are unreferenced.

comments.issue: The manuscript implies that only long-term studies can yield the desired benefits, although many are possible elsewhere.
comments.request: Acknowledge that these benefits are achievable in other research contexts.
comments.quote: many are indeed possible in other research contexts, contrary to the presentation that only long-term studies can yield the benefits needed/desired

comments.issue: 'Long-term study' is never defined, though it is central to the thesis.
comments.request: Define what counts as long-term, e.g. duration or secure multi-year funding.
comments.quote: How are you defining “long-term study” here? This seems quite central to your thesis. Is this simply duration (if so, how many years?), or something with escablished and secure multi-year funding?

comments.issue: The claimed benefit of large data volume for independent projects is unconvincing.
comments.request: Reconsider whether data volume is a distinctive benefit.
comments.quote: The authors argue that, basically, the volume of data is a particular benefit, but I am not convinced.

comments.issue: Student-driven research over long periods is possible in other programme types.
comments.request: Acknowledge other forms of student-driven research.
comments.quote: many other forms of student-driven research are possible, including those for much longer periods (e.g., in one or two year masters courses, honours projects, etc)

comments.issue: 'Internship' is not distinguished from technicians and trainees.
comments.request: Define internships and what makes them less amenable to research.
comments.quote: how are you defining “internship” here that differs from “technicians and trainees” (L60)?

comments.issue: The collection and analysis of ecologically rich data is not exclusive to long-term studies.
comments.request: Soften the claim about long-term studies and rich data.
comments.quote: the collection and analysis of “ecologically rich” data is not strictly the pervue of “long-term studies”!

comments.issue: 'Field assistant' and 'intern' are not distinguished.
comments.request: Clarify how these roles differ.
comments.quote: two additional terms here - “field assistant” and “intern”. How do these differ?

comments.issue: A non-American example is missing.
comments.request: Add a non-American example.
comments.quote: L131 - a non-American example would benefit the authors’ case here

comments.issue: No human research ethics approval appears to have been obtained for the survey.
comments.request: Provide ethics approval or remove the survey data.
comments.quote: the authors do not appear to have obtained human research ethics approval for this survey. This is fundamental and the survey data can not be published without it.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and mostly agreeable, but the advantages are not clearly unique to long-term studies, short-term studies are unfairly belittled, and student payment needs more emphasis.
strengths: agrees with much of the essay

comments.issue: It is unclear why the advantages are restricted to long-term studies, and short-term studies are belittled as a straw man.
comments.request: Justify the uniqueness of long-term studies and stop disparaging short-term research.
comments.quote: it is not clear why the presented advantages are restricted to long-term studies. Other times, there seems to be a somewhat unwarranted belittling of short-term studies, that sounds like a straw man.

comments.issue: The positive portrayal does not match the reality that half of long-term studies do not pay assistants.
comments.request: Emphasize the need to pay students and state that the potential is often not achieved.
comments.quote: The very positive portrayal of long-term studies reported here in many cases does not match the reality.

comments.issue: Some advantages may apply only to the Año Nuevo seal research logistics.
comments.request: Acknowledge that other long-term studies with remote sites may not achieve the same.
comments.quote: some specific advantages suggested here for long-term studies may apply only to the particular logistics of the Ano Nuevo seal research

comments.issue: It is unclear how vehicles broaden participation when insurance restricts who can drive.
comments.request: Explain the link between vehicles and broader participation.
comments.quote: not clear how the first part of this sentence leads to the second part. How do vehicles broaden participation in fieldwork, especially when insurance requirements often restrict who can drive them?

comments.issue: Expecting students to provide their own binoculars is unreasonable.
comments.request: Reconsider this expectation.
comments.quote: Right, but it is unreasonable to expect students to provide binoculars to start with

comments.issue: Experience alone does not make a better candidate, and incompetent field workers can damage long-term studies.
comments.request: Qualify the claim about experience and data collection.
comments.quote: an experienced person will look like a better candidate for any kind of research. An incompetent field person can seriously damage long-term studies if that person does not know how to collect data.

comments.issue: Network exposure only helps if the PI makes an effort.
comments.request: Note the PI's role in ensuring network exposure.
comments.quote: Very true, but only if the PI also makes an effort to ensure that trainees are exposed to the network.

comments.issue: The hidden curriculum is not explained or exemplified.
comments.request: Define the hidden curriculum and give examples of dismantling it.
comments.quote: Not clear to me what this hidden curriculum is, or how one would go about dismantling it. Examples would be useful.

comments.issue: The paragraph at L112-120 applies to any research, not specifically long-term studies.
comments.request: Explain how this paragraph relates specifically to long-term studies.
comments.quote: This paragraph applies to any research. Not clear how it specifically relates to long-term studies.

comments.issue: The NSERC example where training including living wages is evaluated is not included.
comments.request: Consider including the NSERC training-evaluation example.
comments.quote: NSERC (Canada) grants: 1/3 of evaluation is on training of Highly Qualified Personnel, and that includes a living wage for all. HQP includes field assistants.

comments.issue: The suggested practice cannot be done at remote field sites.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limitation of remote field sites.
comments.quote: Excellent, but that cannot be done if the field site is remote.

comments.issue: The survey result means half of the studies did not pay assistants.
comments.request: Acknowledge that half did not pay.
comments.quote: Right, so half did not pay!

comments.issue: Unpaid assistants are also normal at European institutions, including Britain, which disadvantages underprivileged applicants.
comments.request: Discuss this broader unpaid-labour context.
comments.quote: I strongly suspect it was also associated with European-based institutions, including Britain, where it is still considered normal not to pay assistants.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not specify that red text marks problems, and its short-term programme depiction is a straw man.
comments.request: Specify the colour coding and present short-term programmes fairly.
comments.quote: Apparently text in red is for problems - that should be specified. Also, the way short-term programs are presented looks somewhat like a straw man.

title: Long‐term studies should provide structure for inclusive education and professional development

study.system: Florida Scrub-Jay; 34-year demographic and environmental dataset

editor_summary: Editor says four reviewers question the core analyses and framework: more explicit hypotheses, model structure, stage classes and alternative explanations are needed, likely requiring new analyses and reframing; also clarify the density concept.

reviews.assessment: Significant, robust contribution, but limitations of the analytical approach, including zeroing non-significant effects, need discussion.
strengths: robust analysis of a large detailed dataset

comments.issue: The text assumes readers are more familiar with the study than many will be.
comments.request: Explain study specifics for general readers.
comments.quote: in places the authors may be assuming that readers have a greater familiarity with their study than all readers will.

comments.issue: Potential limitations of the analytical approach are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of the analytical approach.
comments.quote: They also need to do a better job of acknowledging and discussing some of the potential limitations of their analytical approach.

comments.issue: The sentence on L123-124 has a superfluous first half.
comments.request: Trim and merge the sentence.
comments.quote: the first half of this sentence seems superfluous, and the second half could be tacked onto the previous

comments.issue: Whether a 1:1 sex ratio is appropriate for each life stage is not justified.
comments.request: Justify or use stage-specific sex ratios.
comments.quote: is the 1:1 sex ratio used here appropriate for each life stage or can you actually adjust appropriately based on known sex ratios from a sampled or known subset of the population

comments.issue: A flat growth rate is called stability, but stability means lack of year-to-year fluctuation.
comments.request: Distinguish stability from a flat growth rate and flip the sentences.
comments.quote: this does not indicate stability, it indicates a flat growth rate; there is an important difference. Stability implies that the population does not fluctuate from year to year

comments.issue: The supplementary figure is hard to follow without cross-checking the table.
comments.request: Label the figure and reference stage distribution.
comments.quote: I found it very difficult to figure out which lines corresponded to "proportion of the population" in new and established pairs until after I cross-checked with the table.

comments.issue: Inconsistent significance claims; the helper-pairing and fecundity correlation is not cited.
comments.request: Address the inconsistency and cite the correlation.
comments.quote: inconsistency in what you are calling significant here? Why not also cite correlation between prob of helpers pairing and fecundity of new pairs?

comments.issue: Fig 3 groups of vital rates are hard to distinguish visually.
comments.request: Add separator lines to Fig 3.
comments.quote: Also suggest you add lines between groups of vital rates in Fig 3 to help readers more easily distinguish amongst them visually.

comments.issue: The acorn trend is weak relative to annual fluctuations, but the statement does not reflect this.
comments.request: Rephrase the acorn trend statement.
comments.quote: there is an downward trend in acorn abundance over time, true, but it is relatively weak compared to the annual fluctuations. This would be better stated in a way that reflected this reality

comments.issue: Inbreeding changes are dynamic, so a linear trend is overly simplistic and its limitations must be addressed.
comments.request: Address the limitations of the linear inbreeding trend.
comments.quote: This all suggests that the rates of inbreeding may be quite dynamic over time and a linear trend is not a good model for these data.

comments.issue: The results section is very dry.
comments.request: Improve the readability of the results.
comments.quote: Results: this was particularly dry, even for a standard results section.

comments.issue: "Remarkably stable" is used without qualifiers despite dramatic year-to-year fluctuations.
comments.request: Qualify the stability claim.
comments.quote: again disagree with calling this population "remarkably stable" without additional qualifiers such as "on average" or similar.

comments.issue: No discussion of what a female-only model would produce.
comments.request: Add a counterpart about a female-only model.
comments.quote: suggest you add counterpart about what would happen if you took the more common approach of fitting a female only model (overestimating some components)

comments.issue: Model assumptions and their violations, such as non-linear covariates, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss model assumptions and violations.
comments.quote: needs some mention of the assumptions of the model structure that you used, potential violations of it (e.g., that some of your covariates were not linear as assumed) and potential implications of that for your results and conclusions.

comments.issue: Setting all non-significant effects to zero is drastic and may inflate confidence and produce spurious results.
comments.request: Justify or avoid zeroing non-significant effects.
comments.quote: setting all non-significant effects to zero is pretty drastic. That means that something with a beta very different from zero but with a confidence interval that was just barely non-significant would be set to zero

reviews.assessment: Impressive integration of demography and genetics, but some modelling choices need justification and one matrix specification appears erroneous.
strengths: integration of divorce rates and genetics
good job with the matrix model

comments.issue: Whether all analyses, especially LTRE and covariation in rates, are needed is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the LTRE and covariation analyses.
comments.quote: I am not for example entirely convinced we need all of the analysis (LTRE, covariation in rates). I think better justification is required here

comments.issue: Squared survival terms equate individual and partner survival, producing wrong derivatives and flawed sensitivity analysis.
comments.request: Rewrite elements using partner survival to fix derivatives.
comments.quote: I believe that here an error has been made, because individual survival (e.g. P_b) is equated to "partner survival" (which I will call P_p), and hence, P_bxP_p is often written as (P_b)^2

comments.issue: Immigration is assumed proportional across all life stages despite dispersal occurring mostly at the helper stage.
comments.request: Model immigration at the helper stage as described.
comments.quote: I read (L 174-175) that dispersal occurs mostly at the 'helpers' state. Why would you then not model it like that, and instead assume proportionality across all four life stages?

comments.issue: Goals and novelty are unclear and no clear hypotheses are tested.
comments.request: State goals, novelty and hypotheses clearly.
comments.quote: I think the goals and novelty of this research is not clearly stated. Except for a marginal expectation statement in the last paragraph of the introduction, I see no other clear hypothesis being tested.

comments.issue: Why two single-gender models are used instead of a two-gender model is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the two single-gender models.
comments.quote: Why not use a 2-gender model? Why are two models (one for each gender) more insightful?

comments.issue: Gender-biased immigration with differential gender-specific survival is not discussed or modelled.
comments.request: Discuss or model gender-specific survival.
comments.quote: While I understand gender bias in immigration may be important, I do not know how this would play out in the case of differential gender-specific survival.

comments.issue: The "helper" state name implies helping that is not modelled.
comments.request: Rename the helper state or justify it.
comments.quote: perhaps "floater" is a better state name instead of "helper", since none of the 'helping' is modelled anyway?

comments.issue: A table of vital rates and which are assumed constant is missing.
comments.request: Add a vital rate table.
comments.quote: I further miss a table of vital rates, in addition to the figures, and description of which vital rates are assumed to remain constant.

comments.issue: "Area" and "frequency" are interchanged between L156 and L57.
comments.request: Rephrase to fix the interchange.
comments.quote: L156 vs L57 Confused about interchange of "area" and "frequency" here, Perhaps rephrase

comments.issue: The claim that something is low on L176 lacks data or references.
comments.request: Back up the claim with data or references.
comments.quote: L176 I find this a little weak. How do you know it is low? Do you have any data or references to back this up?

comments.issue: Whether "experience" applies to individuals or pairs is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether experience is individual or pair level.
comments.quote: If "experience" is key, then I expect this to apply to each individual, rather than the experience that a pair has had together.

comments.issue: "Remarkable stability" is inconsistent with 60% increases and 30% declines.
comments.request: Qualify the stability claim.
comments.quote: L232 I am unsure whether "Remarkable stability" is present given year to year increases of 60% of declines of 30% (Fig 1).

comments.issue: Whether the mean or the annual estimate was used is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether the mean or annual estimate was used.
comments.quote: L161 "mean variable x" Did you really use the mean? Or the annual estimate?

comments.issue: The word "both" on L224 is unclear in a chain-rule context.
comments.request: Clarify the word "both".
comments.quote: L224 I do not understand the word "both" in this context. It's a chain-rule application and all environmental factors should act through vital rates. Right?

comments.issue: Modelled results do not fit observed population growth well.
comments.request: Discuss the mismatch with observed growth.
comments.quote: Table S1. I find the modelling results not to fit well with observed population growth. This may be serious and warrants discussion, if not more research.

comments.issue: LS 89-90 likely should read Fe and De.
comments.request: Correct to Fe and De.
comments.quote: LS 89-90 I think you mean Fe and De?

comments.issue: Setting non-significant effects to zero may discard effects relevant to population development.
comments.request: Avoid zeroing or test both approaches.
comments.quote: LS156-S157 I would recommend against setting to zero (or at least try both). Statistically insignificant effects need not be insignificant to population development.

reviews.assessment: Engaging, well-composed study with clear writing and rigorous analysis; a few tweaks would further enhance its impact.

comments.issue: Predictions and hypotheses could be more ambitious, with census numbers and rival explanations.
comments.request: Present census numbers and rival explanations.
comments.quote: I think that you could be more ambitious in its predictions and hypotheses with a more assertive stance on the population stability by e.g. presenting the census numbers.

comments.issue: The population model and how immigration is included are described too little and too late.
comments.request: Describe the population model and immigration in the main text.
comments.quote: is this inferred or actually measured? It feels like a bit too much detail has been relegated to supplementary materials

comments.issue: Vital rates should be modelled at population level; individual-level modelling creates non-independence.
comments.request: Confirm and explain the level of vital rate modelling.
comments.quote: These should be modelled at the population level, with repetitions being the number of years. If you model vital rates per individual, then you have non-independence within years

comments.issue: Species could be listed on L60-62.
comments.request: List the species there.
comments.quote: L60-62 Consider listing species here as well.

comments.issue: More detail on the inbreeding coefficients is needed.
comments.request: Provide more detail on inbreeding coefficients.
comments.quote: L162-164 I would like to know more about the inbreeding coefficients here.

comments.issue: Whether unsexed individuals are unsexed at random is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the unsexed individuals.
comments.quote: L197 Are these unsexed individuals unsexed at random?

comments.issue: Conditional/unconditional parts are explained only in a figure legend.
comments.request: Explain conditional/unconditional in the main text.
comments.quote: The only explanation of conditional/unconditional parts comes in a figure legend, I think this needs clarification in the main text.

reviews.assessment: Novel, very well written study with a compelling story; only a few suggestions for clarity and presentation.
strengths: novel study with rare long-term data
very well written, concise and easy to follow
results well integrated with existing knowledge

comments.issue: The direction of density effects on vital rates is not specified.
comments.request: State the direction of density effects.
comments.quote: please specify the direction of the effects here, for how population density impacts these vital rates. For example, higher population density is associated with lower fecundity, etc.

comments.issue: The main conclusion is not visually supported in a single figure.
comments.request: Add a figure supporting the main conclusion.
comments.quote: this is the main conclusion from your study – is there a way to visually support this more clearly in a figure?

comments.issue: SI line 90 likely should read Dn and De.
comments.request: Correct to Dn and De.
comments.quote: Supplementary Information 90: Dn and De 103-104: it would be helpful to provide an explanation in words for the components involved in calculating each transition probability

comments.issue: Transition probability components are not explained in words.
comments.request: Explain the transition components with an example.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to provide an explanation in words for the components involved in calculating each transition probability, perhaps by using one of the transitions as an example.

title: Density dependence maintains long‐term stability despite increased isolation and inbreeding in the Florida Scrub‐Jay

study.system: yellow-bellied marmots; long-term individual fitness data

editor_summary: Editor recommends recasting the perspective as a research article centred on marmot findings; notes limited transferability and established CEA, and asks for comparisons, thresholds, provenance and all reviewer comments addressed.

reviews.assessment: Interesting framework valuable in some systems, but its utility is oversold and it demands data and knowledge few systems have.
strengths: addresses an important need for integrating multiple stressors
framework could be a useful advance

comments.issue: The utility of the approach is oversold and its limitations are insufficiently emphasized.
comments.request: More clearly highlight the limitations of the approach.
comments.quote: I think the authors have oversold the utility of this approach and I think that the manuscript should be revised to more clearly highlight the limitations of this approach

comments.issue: Applying the framework requires knowing stressor impacts and rare, decade-long data, so the marmot example is deceptively simple.
comments.request: Emphasize how much data and knowledge each step requires.
comments.quote: The example with marmots provided in this paper is deceptively simple because the authors had 60 years of detailed data on this population.

comments.issue: Comparing models with different thresholds and cutoffs is informative only where much is already known.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited value of threshold comparisons in data-poor systems.
comments.quote: this was useful in a system where so much is known, but would be relatively uninformative in systems wild animal populations where less is known

comments.issue: Multimodel fitting without mechanistic understanding gives little predictive power or extrapolation.
comments.request: Develop mechanistic understanding to enable extrapolation.
comments.quote: without a mechanistic understanding, provides little in the way of predictive power for other situations

comments.issue: Reducing stressors to vote counting ignores their relative impacts and variable strengths.
comments.request: Consider weighting or accounting for stressor intensities.
comments.quote: the reduction of stressors to a vote counting process (how many stressors are present above a certain threshold) while ignoring the relative impacts of those stressors has limited use

comments.issue: The data demands mean poor return for effort, and findings may not transfer to other systems.
comments.request: Temper claims about the general value of the approach.
comments.quote: given the effort that would be required to collect the data required to use these methods, I think the bang for the buck is lacking

comments.issue: Four line-level copy edits (capitalization, wording and missing words on lines 30, 124, 232 and 456).
comments.quote: Line 30: It is not clear why ‘Anthropogenically’ is capitalized here.

title: Cumulative adversity and survival in the wild

study.system: polar bears; Canadian Arctic; genomic offset to climate

editor_summary: Two enthusiastic reviews, but important concerns about the genomic analyses must be addressed in a revision.

reviews.assessment: Captivating, cleanly executed study; only minor questions on climate scenarios and dispersal barriers.

comments.issue: Only RCP8.5 is used; lower forcing scenarios are not projected.
comments.request: Consider projections under lower forcing scenarios.
comments.quote: why limit analysis to RCP8.5, and not also propose projection under lower forcing scenarii (which may hopefully start to be equally realistic)?

comments.issue: CMIP5 outputs are used instead of CMIP6.
comments.request: Consider including CMIP6 model outputs.
comments.quote: would the overhead for including CMPI6 model outputs (rather than CMIP5) be prohibitive in this study?

comments.issue: Which CMIP5 models were used and how they were selected is unclear.
comments.request: List the models and their selection and compare predictions.
comments.quote: which models in the CMIP5 panel were used, how were they selected, and how to their predicitons differ?

comments.issue: Dispersal barriers coincide with environmental transitions, inducing covariance between neutral IBD turnover and environment.
comments.request: Map the steepest-gradient areas and note this limitation.
comments.quote: Sea ice and overall climate parameters are also expected to change around the same open sea / archipelago transitions, which may induce forced covariance between (neutral, IBD-driven) allele turnover and environmental parameters.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and well-written study, but batch effects, clustering and terminology need attention.
strengths: impressive dataset with substantial statistical power
avoids a pitfall of earlier genetic offset studies

comments.issue: Samples span 40 years and two SNP chips with different sequencing technology, risking batch effects on genetic offset.
comments.request: Include sequencing run and sampling year as predictors.
comments.quote: differences in sequencing coverage, read length, molar concentration, and other technical artifacts might lead to batch effects, which could in turn impact estimated genetic offset

comments.issue: Strong isolation-by-distance complicates discrete cluster assignment by sNMF.
comments.request: Use a clinal clustering approach such as conStruct.
comments.quote: it seems important to maximize accuracy by using an approach that accounts for underlying clinal variation

comments.issue: What locally adapted phenotypes drive genotype-environment associations, and the role of pleiotropy, is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss possible adaptive phenotypes and pleiotropy.
comments.quote: some discussion of what locally adapted phenotypes might be driving genotype-environment associations seems warranted, however speculative

comments.issue: Maladaptation is conflated with lack of adaptive potential, and abundance is treated as separate from genetic variation.
comments.request: Use population genetic terms precisely.
comments.quote: maladaptation is conflated with lack of adaptive potential, and abundance (census population size) and genetic variation are treated as separate determinants of adaptive response

comments.issue: The manuscript switches between 'high Arctic' and 'high Canadian Arctic'.
comments.request: Choose one term and use it consistently.
comments.quote: I think it would be clearer if you chose either "high Arctic" or "high Canadian Arctic" rather than switching between the two

comments.issue: The sentence at L64-65 conflates existing maladaptation with increased risk of maladaptation.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence as suggested.
comments.quote: *maladaptation* might already be widespread, and a variety of processes (e.g. accelerated warming or gene flow from central populations) might increase risk of maladaptation

comments.issue: Several small rephrasing suggestions (L110, L248, L278, L383, L387).
comments.request: Apply the suggested rephrases.
comments.quote: L248: Suggested rephrase: "R2 values"

comments.issue: Coverage depth differences between chips and batch-effect tests are not reported.
comments.request: Report coverage differences and batch-effect tests.
comments.quote: Were there differences in depth of coverage between SNP chips? Did you apply any tests for the presence of batch effects?

comments.issue: Abundance is presented as directly mediating adaptive potential, whereas it acts only through effective population size.
comments.request: Clarify the role of Ne in adaptive responses.
comments.quote: Abundance (i.e., census population size) will only mediate a response to selection to the extent it is correlated with effective population size

comments.issue: High genetic offset is wrongly equated with low adaptive potential.
comments.request: Rephrase to separate offset from adaptive potential.
comments.quote: High genetic offset scores should not be seen as indicative of low adaptive potential

comments.issue: It is unclear whether figure colours are similar or shared at L722.
comments.request: Clarify the colour scheme.
comments.quote: Do you mean similar colors (e.g. pale yellow and peach) or shared colors?

title: Assessing the risk of climate maladaptation for Canadian polar bears

study.system: tropical birds; precipitation niche breadths from eBird records

editor_summary: Both reviewers find the topic and analyses interesting and clear; invites authors to address remaining questions and clarification requests to improve impact.

reviews.assessment: Clear and interesting study, but niche breadth measured as a proportion of the gradient is flawed and the discussion is superficial.

comments.issue: Proportion of the precipitation gradient is not a comparable measure of niche breadth across gradients of different widths.
comments.request: Compare actual precipitation ranges of species between gradients.
comments.quote: The proportion of the precipitation gradient occupied is not a useful measurement of niche breadth because—for example—a 0.5 proportion could mean a precipitation niche breadth of 500mm in one gradient and 1000mm in another.

comments.issue: Niche breadth should depend on the pool of actual competitors rather than the total regional species pool.
comments.request: Test with guild-specific competitor pools or at least discuss this.
comments.quote: I think tighter species packing resulting from competition should depend on the regional species pool of actual competitors.

comments.issue: Positive interactions such as mixed flocks could increase niche breadth instead of competition narrowing it.
comments.request: Discuss the role of positive interactions in niche breadth.
comments.quote: This is likely more difficult to test, but the role of positive interactions in niche breadth should be mentioned in the discussion.

comments.issue: The argumentation is unfocused and superficial; the discussion should address niche ecology more directly.
comments.request: Focus the discussion on niche ecology and the proposed mechanisms.
comments.quote: I find the argumentation a little unfocused and superficial.

comments.issue: The ecological relevance of precipitation as a niche dimension is not explained.
comments.request: Add one or two sentences on why precipitation matters as a niche dimension.
comments.quote: I suggest including one or two sentences explaining the ecological relevance of precipitation as a niche dimension.

comments.issue: The second and third introduction paragraphs overlap.
comments.request: Merge these paragraphs.
comments.quote: Consider merging the second and third paragraph in the introduction as they touch on similar topics.

comments.issue: Figure 2 lacks a panel showing the range of precipitation across regions.
comments.request: Add a panel showing precipitation ranges per region.
comments.quote: I think you should include a panel showing –with bars, boxplots, or histograms for example –the range of precipitation across each region.

comments.issue: Bird checklist terminology at line 123 is not explained for non-specialists.
comments.request: Add a sentence describing what constitutes a bird checklist.
comments.quote: Perhaps you can add a sentence describing what constitutes a bird checklist.

comments.issue: Whether higher elevations were excluded to remove the temperature dimension is unclear.
comments.request: State whether higher elevations were excluded and why.
comments.quote: Line 135. Did you exclude higher elevations to exclude the temperature dimension of the niche?

comments.issue: The reason for excluding other bird groups at line 150 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the exclusion criteria.
comments.quote: Its not clear to me the reason behind excluding all the other groups.

comments.issue: Area of the precipitation gradient is not included as a fixed factor in the models.
comments.request: Add gradient area as a fixed factor.
comments.quote: I think models should also include the area of the precipitation gradient as a fixed factor.

comments.issue: The unit of the 'total number of forest bird species' variable at line 157 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether this is the number of species per gradient region.
comments.quote: Is this the number of species per precipitation-gradient region (i.e. n-19)? My understanding is that each precipitation-gradient region is one unit of analysis.

comments.issue: 'Mountain region combination' at line 173 is unclear and the N may be wrong.
comments.request: Correct the wording and check the N.
comments.quote: Mountain region combination? I think you mean precipitation gradient region. Check if the N in parenthesis is right.

comments.issue: Limiting analysis 2 to species in five or more regions discards informative species.
comments.request: Include species occurring in 2-4 regions.
comments.quote: Why limit it to 5 or more regions? It seems to me that species occurring in 2 to 4 regions may also add useful information.

comments.issue: 'Directly compared' at line 187 is undefined.
comments.request: Explain what 'directly compared' means.
comments.quote: Line 187. What do you mean by "directly compared"?
