comments.issue: Unclear how the species mixtures were combined and in what proportions.
comments.request: Clarify whether the mix was equitable or give the proportions.
comments.quote: L126: how were the mixtures combined? Please clarify there was an equitable mix of the species or if not what were the proportions.

comments.issue: The timing of non-invaded control sampling relative to invasion and disturbance is hard to follow.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling timeline.
comments.quote: L129: I am finding it difficult to get the invasion times clear; the non-invaded controls were sampled at invasion day 6

comments.issue: No non-invasion controls for each treatment, so the effect of disturbance alone cannot be seen.
comments.request: Add or explain controls for disturbance without invasion.
comments.quote: Was there non-invasion controls for each disturbance invasion treatment to see how the community altered with just the disturbance?

comments.issue: Figure 1 uses CFU rather than a comparable per-volume unit.
comments.request: Use CFU/ml on the axis.
comments.quote: Figure 1: Why is the axis CFU and not a more comparable CFU/ml?

reviews.assessment: Very nice, interesting study, but the propagule-pressure by timing interaction may be a scale artefact and needs additional analyses and softer language.

comments.issue: Multiplicative effects of propagule pressure and timing can masquerade as interactions in linear models, so the detected interaction may be an artefact.
comments.request: Add analyses covering multiplicative alternatives and moderate the interaction claims.
comments.quote: It seems likely to me that these observations mean you cannot claim with so much confidence that you have detected real interactions effects between propagule size and timing of invasion relative to a disturbance.

comments.issue: Inferring true interactions may require time-series density measurements rather than only final densities.
comments.request: Assess densities at all time points in future experiments.
comments.quote: It may require time series measurements to truly make that inference.

comments.issue: The phrase “fourth invasion day” is confusing before the experimental structure is explained.
comments.request: Reword, e.g. as “on day 8 of the experiment”.
comments.quote: 1) L 109 – what is the “fourth invasion day”? This seems confusing, can be reworded?

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: reword the mixture sentence and change a comma to a period.
comments.quote: 10) L 250: make the comma into a period

comments.issue: Unclear whether the 42 microcosms were only resident communities and never invaded.
comments.request: Clarify whether these microcosms were invaded.
comments.quote: 3) L 128-132: My understanding is that these 42 microcosms were just the resident community, and were never invaded? Please clarify.

comments.issue: Unclear whether the timing factor had 7 or 8 levels for day 8 pre- and post-disturbance invasions.
comments.request: Clarify the number of factor levels.
comments.quote: 5) L 197: Can you please clarify if this factor had 8 levels, including two values for the pre- and post-disturbance invasion possibilities on day 8, or 7 levels

comments.issue: The model at L198-202 is not described in enough detail to be understood.
comments.request: Explain the model in sufficient detail.
comments.quote: 6) L 198-202: More detail describing this model is needed.

comments.issue: Readers should not have to read the code to understand the analysis, and the code citation is too broad.
comments.request: Describe the analysis in a new SI section and cite a specific function.
comments.quote: 7) L 219: Asking people to read the code, here, would be somewhat non-standard.

comments.issue: A log-transformed (multiplicative) analysis is needed; the current linear-scale interaction test may be wrong.
comments.request: Log-transform the response and report whether the interaction remains.
comments.quote: 8) L 233-240: One can argue that population processes are multiplicative, not additive, so that a better, or supplementary way to test for interaction effects would be if you first log-transformed your response variable.

comments.issue: A log-scale version of Figure 1 would help judge the multiplicative patterns.
comments.request: Provide a log-scale version of Fig. 1.
comments.quote: It would be useful, also, to see a version of Fig. 1 where the y axis is plotted log scale.

comments.issue: Density dependence can generate apparent interactions, so this complication must be acknowledged.
comments.request: Be upfront about density dependence and add the suggested analyses.
comments.quote: 9) Density dependence also plays a role here, and that relates to some of the text at L 182-202.

comments.issue: The second part of the L266-268 sentence is undermined by the scale and density-dependence concerns.
comments.request: Discuss this doubt openly and moderate the claim.
comments.quote: 11) L 266-268: This is an important sentence. I believe the first part. I think the comments 8 and 9 above cast doubt on the second part.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the L272-276 results come from the never-invaded communities, and the wording is misleading.
comments.request: Clarify the communities and reword using experiment days.
comments.quote: 12) L 272-276: I think these results must come from the 42 never-invaded (as far as I understand – see my comment 4 above) communities described on L 128-132? Please clarify.

comments.issue: L301 wording formally contradicts the preceding sentence.
comments.request: Reword as suggested to avoid the contradiction.
comments.quote: 13) L 301: replace with “except communities invaded right after disturbance and communities invaded on day 7” to avoid formally contradicting the statement in the sentence just before this one.

comments.issue: The cell density corresponding to 0 CFU (detection limit) is not given.
comments.request: Report the approximate cell density equivalent to 0 CFU.
comments.quote: 14) Given the discussion on 330ff, I think it would be useful for you to indicate the approximate density of cells in a microcosm (units such as cell/mL) which translates to 0 CFU.

comments.issue: The denominator of the 6.67% figure is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether it refers to species-microcosm pairs.
comments.quote: 15) L 333-334: Do you mean 6.67% of populations, i.e., species-microcosm pairs? Please clarify.

comments.issue: The L369-372 language overstates the results given the unresolved statistical concerns.
comments.request: Soften the language unless additional analyses address the concerns.
comments.quote: 16) L369-372: I do not fully buy this, see my earlier comments. Likely the language here needs to be softened unless additional (unknown to me) analyses are done to address some of my comments above.

comments.issue: A no-disturbance control would test whether disturbance benefits pre-disturbance invaders.
comments.request: Consider running no-disturbance control cultures.
comments.quote: It would be interesting to compare your results to similar experimental setups without the disturbance happening at all.

comments.issue: The non-result at L416-417 may be an artefact of variance handling; heterogeneous variance was visible.
comments.request: Check residuals and consider log or negative binomial error structures.
comments.quote: 18) L 416-417: This non-result may further have been an artefact of the way variance was handled in your statistical models.

comments.issue: The probiotic statements extrapolate too far from lab communities to human guts.
comments.request: Delete or heavily caveat the probiotic claims.
comments.quote: 19) L 459ff: I find the statements here about probiotics to be too much of a supposition.

reviews.assessment: Well written and a significant contribution, but lacks controls to disentangle disturbance and invasion effects and could connect better to invasion theory and mechanisms.
strengths: well written and a significant contribution
explores disturbance facilitating invasions already present in the community

comments.issue: Introduction is not sufficiently rooted in the conceptual framework of invasion ecology.
comments.request: Emphasize invasion framework and disturbance contingencies first.
comments.quote: I would have preferred the manuscript to be more deeply rooted in the framework of invasion ecology.

comments.issue: Third and last introduction paragraphs are disconnected and lack specific hypotheses and predictions.
comments.request: Add mechanisms, hypotheses and predictions.
comments.quote: Enhanced manuscript's clarity could be achieved by incorporating specific hypotheses or mechanisms that underline the significance of the relative timing of disturbance and invasion, along with predictions.

comments.issue: No controls without invasion or without disturbance, so the individual effects cannot be disentangled.
comments.request: Add such controls or discuss why they are infeasible.
comments.quote: I believe the most significant weakness of the study is the lack of controls for both invasion and disturbance.

comments.issue: Time since invasion differs among treatments and could explain the final abundance differences.
comments.request: Account for the differing invasion durations.
comments.quote: some communities would have experienced 8 days of invasion, while others only 1. This discrepancy could partially explain the differences in final abundances observed.

comments.issue: No conceptual figure of the experimental design.
comments.request: Add a conceptual design figure.
comments.quote: This section would benefit from a conceptual figure illustrating the experimental design.

comments.issue: Too little information about the study communities and their species.
comments.request: Describe the species and community.
comments.quote: Readers who are not specialized in bacterial communities, like myself, could gain a deeper understanding from the manuscript if it included more information about the type of study communities and their species.

comments.issue: Discussion is superficial and phenomenological and lacks proposed mechanisms and trait-based interpretation.
comments.request: Propose specific mechanisms and discuss species traits.
comments.quote: As it stands, the discussion appears somewhat superficial and phenomenological to me.

comments.issue: Prior invasion may exacerbate disturbance impacts or feed back on invasion success.
comments.request: Consider and discuss this possibility.
comments.quote: Have you considered the possibility that prior invasion could exacerbate the impact of disturbance on the resident community or even feedback on invasion success?

comments.issue: Biotic resistance explanation does not fit the higher pre-disturbance invader abundance.
comments.request: Clarify this apparent inconsistency.
comments.quote: However, this explanation seems to fall short when considering the results of the pre-disturbance invasions.

comments.issue: Figure 3 is hard to interpret and cumulative bars hide variability.
comments.request: Clarify the y-axis and use scatter or box plots.
comments.quote: I found some difficulties interpreting Figure 3.

comments.issue: Running title is incomplete.
comments.request: Complete the running title.
comments.quote: Line 20: The running title seems incomplete to me.

comments.issue: Abstract lacks global-change and multiple-stressor context.
comments.request: Add a sentence on multiple stressors to the abstract.
comments.quote: Line 32: Adding a line about how multiple stressors (such as invasions and disturbances) can affect communities under global change could add meaningful context to the abstract.

comments.issue: Abstract omits the propagule-pressure timing result.
comments.request: Add this result to the abstract.
comments.quote: Lines 41-42: It might be a good idea to include in the abstract the results showing that propagule pressure had a stronger effect before than after disturbances.

comments.issue: Relevant studies on invasion timing and context-dependency are missing.
comments.request: Cite and discuss these studies, including phenology differences.
comments.quote: While I agree with you that the role of the relative timing of invasion and disturbance is yet to be clarified, several studies have addressed similar topics (e.g., Crawley 2004; Marushia et al. 2010; Torres et al. 2024).

comments.issue: Questions, hypotheses and predictions are underdeveloped.
comments.request: Develop testable hypotheses and predictions.
comments.quote: It would be beneficial to have a more developed presentation of these questions and associated hypotheses/predictions that could be tested with your experimental setup.

comments.issue: The biotic resistance assumption lacks supporting data.
comments.request: Test whether invader success relates to resident abundance or diversity.
comments.quote: While this is a plausible explanation, it would greatly improve the manuscript if you could provide data supporting this idea.

comments.issue: Interesting notion introduced too late in the manuscript.
comments.request: Introduce it earlier.
comments.quote: Lines 83-86: This notion is interesting and could be introduced earlier in the manuscript.

comments.issue: The prediction for small invading populations under post-invasion disturbance is not justified.
comments.request: Justify or revise the prediction.
comments.quote: Lines 98-101: Why do you suggest that small invading populations might perform worse under post-invasion disturbance only? Is it not possible that small populations have low performance even when invading after a disturbance?

comments.issue: Relative timing, order and timing are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Define and use these terms consistently.
comments.quote: In this design, what are the specific differences between relative timing and order?

comments.issue: Day-of-invasion versus invasion-event terminology is inconsistent.
comments.request: Unify the terminology throughout.
comments.quote: Consider replacing ‘on one of seven days’ with ‘on one of eight invasions events’.

comments.issue: Species characteristics, interactions and habitat are not described.
comments.request: Add brief species descriptions.
comments.quote: I would be worthwhile to add a brief description of the characteristics of each species, how they interact and where this community is commonly found

comments.issue: Disturbance description is awkwardly placed.
comments.request: Move it to a different sentence.
comments.quote: Consider moving ‘Disturbance consisted of fully homogenising each microcosm, before 60 uL (1% by volume) was transferred into fresh media’ to a different sentence.

comments.issue: The realism of the homogenisation disturbance versus natural disturbances is not discussed.
comments.request: Explain the realism of the disturbance.
comments.quote: Also, how realistic is this type of disturbance? Is it commonly found in natural bacterial communities? Is it comparable to, for instance, the use of antibiotics as stated in the discussion?

comments.issue: Unclear how invader abundance was estimated.
comments.request: Explain the abundance metric.
comments.quote: Line 182: How did you estimate abundance? Is in CFU too?

comments.issue: Density, abundance and success are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Homogenise these terms.
comments.quote: Please, try to homogenize the use of terms ‘density’, ‘abundance’, and ‘success’.

comments.issue: Link function not reported.
comments.request: Report the link function.
comments.quote: Lines 194-198: Please, clarify the link function used.

comments.issue: Model selection procedure is not fully reported.
comments.request: Report initial and removed variables/interactions.
comments.quote: Could you please provide some extra information about which variables/interactions were initially included and sequentially removed from the models?

comments.issue: Effect sizes are not reported.
comments.request: Report effect sizes.
comments.quote: It would have been helpful to report the effect sizes of the results, in addition to information on whether the response variable increased/decreased with the treatments.

comments.issue: No statistical test reported for this claim.
comments.request: Provide the test.
comments.quote: Lines 226-228: Is there a specific statistical test of this?

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits (spacing, duplicated parentheses, wording).
comments.quote: Lines 350-356: Check for extra spaces before periods and commas.

comments.issue: Paragraph should start with the main results; delete the preamble.
comments.request: Delete lines 359-363.
comments.quote: I would prefer this paragraph to jump in into the main results. Thus, I would delete lines 359-363.

comments.issue: The two questions are not clearly stated in the introduction.
comments.request: State them clearly in the introduction.
comments.quote: I don´t think these two questions are as clearly stated in the introduction, which would be great.

comments.issue: The exclusion claim ignores priority effects as an alternative mechanism.
comments.request: Consider priority effects in the argument.
comments.quote: However, if priority effects determine species coexistence between resident species and the invader, then it could be expected that resident species could not colonize/succeed when arriving after the invader.

comments.issue: Paragraph lacks a closing sentence.
comments.request: Add a closing sentence.
comments.quote: Line 392: Adding a closing sentence would really help the reading of this paragraph.

comments.issue: The proposed mechanism is not tested against resident abundance data.
comments.request: Test invader success against resident species abundance.
comments.quote: I think that you have the data to test this hypothesis, right? You could evaluate invader success in days 9, 10, and 11 as a function of the abundance of resident species.

comments.issue: The statement is not clearly supported by the presented data.
comments.request: Show which results support it.
comments.quote: Again, I am not sure that your data reflects this result. Are you basing this statement on Figure 2?

comments.issue: The passenger explanation conflicts with the high pre-disturbance invader abundance.
comments.request: Clarify the apparent contradiction.
comments.quote: However, I think this explanation fall short when considering the results of the pre-disturbance invasions, since Figure 1 shows that the abundance of the invader is higher in pre-disturbance treatments

comments.issue: Discussion does not acknowledge differences from real-life cases.
comments.request: Add caveats about disturbance type, invader and resident communities.
comments.quote: However, I think some acknowledgement of the differences between your experimental set-up and ‘real-life’ cases would be needed

title: Disturbances can facilitate prior invasions more than subsequent invasions in microbial communities

study.system: non-native ornamental plants; historical U.S. nursery catalog records

editor_summary: Reviewers raised valid concerns about unclear language (definitions, terminology), literature contextualization, and how data are defined; editor asks for transparent discussion of spatial aggregation and distributional issues.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-prepared paper with clear motivation and a valuable contribution, needing clarity fixes and a closer look at the propagule pressure calculation.
strengths: one discussion paragraph is really nice and clear

comments.issue: The introduction is too long; several passages, examples and sentences are redundant.
comments.request: Shorten the introduction, combine paragraphs and remove redundant sentences.
comments.quote: I feel that for what is quite a clear premise, the introduction is too long, and could be made snappier.

comments.issue: The sentence on lines 166-168 is unclear: the USDA code, 'status' and 'habit' are unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify these terms and their relevance for non-US readers.
comments.quote: This sentence lacks a bit of clarity. Non-US readers may not know what the USDA code is or its relevance (I don’t!).

comments.issue: The number of species analysed and excluded at each step is hard to follow.
comments.request: Add a PRISMA-style flow diagram showing species numbers at each step.
comments.quote: I am finding it slightly hard to follow the total number of species that were analysed, or how many were excluded at each step.

comments.issue: The unique city/state location measure of propagule pressure may bias results towards states with better records or more cities.
comments.request: Explain how the city- versus state-level record structure was accounted for.
comments.quote: I am concerned that this method (“unique city/state locations”) biases the data towards states with better records/more cities

comments.issue: The analysis predicting the established group relative to the introduced group is not explained.
comments.request: Explain what was predicted and how.
comments.quote: Apologies if I am missing something simple, but I don’t understand this analysis. What do you mean by “we predicted the established group relative to the introduced group”?

comments.issue: Two line-level edits: a missing '%' after '95' and 'weather' for 'whether'.
comments.request: Make these two small text corrections.
comments.quote: For clarity can you add ‘%’ after ‘95’

comments.issue: Figure 1b x-axis is strongly left-skewed and high values are being excluded.
comments.request: Log-transform the x-axis so all data can be shown.
comments.quote: could you log-transform the x-axis? The data is clearly strongly left-skewed; log-transforming would reduce the high number of outliers and probably mean that all the data could be shown

comments.issue: Discussion language suggests introduction history does not predict invasion, whereas only the established-to-invasive transition was tested.
comments.request: Rework the wording to say introduction history is unimportant in the established-invasive transition.
comments.quote: At times, the discussion veers towards saying that introduction history is not a good predictor of whether a species becomes invasive. I think this is slightly misleading

reviews.assessment: Valuable contribution with many positive aspects, but invasion terminology is used confusingly and the discussion needs more nuance about propagule pressure.

comments.issue: 'Invasion' is used interchangeably for different invasion stages; terminology needs to distinguish introduction, establishment and invasiveness.
comments.request: Use invasion for the whole process and invasive for the establishment-to-invasive step.
comments.quote: My main comment is that seems to me confusing use of invasion terminology throughout the manuscript that complicates the message

comments.issue: The discussion is too strong in saying propagule pressure does not predict invasiveness, overlooking complexity and context dependence.
comments.request: Add nuance about the multiple factors and context driving invasiveness, citing Catford et al. 2021.
comments.quote: It is perfectly possible that propagule pressure does play a role in driving a transition from naturalised to invasive, but in fact whether a species becomes invasive is more complicated than simply measuring propagule pressure alone

comments.issue: Figure 1 colours may not be colour-blind friendly; green and dark blue lines are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Change the colour scheme to be colour-blind friendly.
comments.quote: I would check that the colour scheme you are chosen is colour-blind friendly, as I find the green and dark blue lines on the density plots hard to distinguish

comments.issue: Figures 1-3 x-axis labels say propagule pressure although unique locations are only a proxy, and units are missing.
comments.request: Relabel the x-axes as the measured proxy and add units.
comments.quote: The use of propagule pressure seems a bit off for the x axis labels as this is not what is measured here (number of unique locations is a proxy for propagule pressure, which is what you have actually measured)

comments.issue: Confidence intervals appear in Figure 3 but not Figure 2A/B, and are undefined in captions.
comments.request: Explain the confidence intervals and add them consistently.
comments.quote: Why are there no confidence intervals on Fig. 2 A and B but there is in Fig. 3? Or are they too small to see?

comments.issue: Interactions between propagule pressure and residence time are not explored, potentially missing explained variation.
comments.request: Test the propagule pressure by residence time interaction.
comments.quote: I would consider exploring interactions between propagule pressure and residence time. Propagule pressure may help species overcome lag periods that is linked to residence time, so there may be some variation explained through their interaction that you are missing.

comments.issue: Lines 316-318 repeat a line from the introduction, and lines 323-325 are also repetitive.
comments.request: Rewrite these passages to be less repetitive.
comments.quote: This line is essentially a direct copy of a line in the introduction. Would consider altering to be less repetitive. See also L323 - 325

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset effort, but the finding is not novel, the term invasive is poorly defined, and the data are not suited to support the invasion message.
strengths: huge effort to compile the data

comments.issue: The overall message is not novel; similar results exist and the finding may be a construct of the terminology used.
comments.request: Better justify the novelty of the findings.
comments.quote: The overall message that propagule pressure determines establishment but not invasion is not an astounding finding.

comments.issue: 'Invasive' is so poorly defined that it is a messy dependent variable, inflating uncertainty in parameter estimates.
comments.request: Use a standardised definition of invasive, such as official lists.
comments.quote: the term "invasive" is so poor;y defined that it almost becomes pointless to use it as a dependent variate unless the term is used in a standardized way such as on official lists

comments.issue: Dataset details are too sparse to judge adequacy; the cited data paper is little more than an abstract.
comments.request: Present the dataset structure and contents clearly in the manuscript.
comments.quote: I examined the cited data paper (Fertakos, 2023) but this is little more than an abstract and the reader has to download the data to assess its structure

comments.issue: Spatial biases in catalog coverage (e.g., coasts versus Midwest) are not addressed or mapped.
comments.request: Map the spatial distribution of catalog sources to rule out inherent spatial bias.
comments.quote: I would like to see a map of the spatial distribution of the data sources for catalogs to confirm that there was no inherent spatial bias

comments.issue: Multiple catalogues from the same nursery in consecutive years are not independent and were not addressed.
comments.request: Use a stratified sample of catalogues or otherwise handle non-independence.
comments.quote: No consideration of data independence and the authors do not make clear how they might have dealt with multiple catalogues from the same nursery in the same or consecutive years

comments.issue: The message that propagule pressure only predicts establishment may be misleading because the data cannot show spread effects.
comments.request: Temper the message in light of the data limitations.
comments.quote: Overall I would be worried that a message such as "propagule pressure should only be considered as an important predictor of the establishment stage of the invasion process" could be misleading based on the underlying data problems

title: Propagule pressure from historic U.S. plant sales explains establishment but not invasion

study.system: deep metric learning toolkit; damselfly image dataset

editor_summary: Editor supports the toolkit, agrees documentation should be extended for non-deep-learning users, asks to fix the A6000 GPU name, distinguish BioEncoder from classification tools like MegaDetector, and resolve GitHub issues in a citable release.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and thorough description of a valuable software contribution; only major request is literature context on deep metric learning in ecology.
strengths: specializes in underused deep metric learning

comments.issue: The manuscript lacks a summary of current deep metric learning applications in evolutionary biology and ecology.
comments.request: Summarize this literature (Miele et al. 2021; Karaderi et al. 2022).
comments.quote: it would be good to briefly summarize the current literature on deep metric learning as applied in evolutionary biology/ecology

comments.issue: Using the first six years for training and last four for testing rather than a random split may introduce temporal bias.
comments.request: Justify the temporal data split.
comments.quote: Why did you choose to use the first six years as training data and the last four years as test data, and not a random split?

comments.issue: HueSaturationValue augmentation may erase colour signal and explain confusion between the O- and I-morphs.
comments.request: Justify or reconsider this augmentation.
comments.quote: I’m curious as to why HueSaturationValue was used as an augmentation parameter considering that the three morphs being distinguished are color morphs.

comments.issue: Case-study augmentation parameter values and BioEncoder defaults are not reported.
comments.request: Report used and default augmentation parameters.
comments.quote: I think you should mention what parameter values you used for the case study augmentations in the supplement, and perhaps also what the default settings are in BioEncoder

comments.issue: Mislabeled images were noted but apparently never confirmed.
comments.request: Confirm and correct the labels.
comments.quote: The way this is written implies that you did not actually go back and confirm whether these images were, in fact, incorrectly labeled. Why not?

comments.issue: The Supplemental Files contain a DeepBryo paper PDF instead of BioEncoder supplement.
comments.request: Replace the incorrect supplemental file.
comments.quote: the file included under “Supplemental Files” appears to be incorrect

comments.issue: 5 line-level copy edits (L119-120 formatting, L122, L139, L141, L147).
comments.quote: Fix formating on lines 119-120 (unitalicize references, insert space between name of package and reference).

comments.issue: Line 203 should reference Figure 3, not Figure 4.
comments.request: Correct the figure cross-reference.
comments.quote: It seems to me that this line should should be referencing figure 3 and not figure 4.

reviews.assessment: Polished and accessible toolkit description that will be widely adopted; asks for more documentation, worked examples and clearer model-stage distinctions.
strengths: excellent contextualization of the toolkit's need
toolkit well constructed and easy to use

comments.issue: It is unclear how users analyse trained model results beyond the built-in visualisations, e.g. exporting embeddings or predicting new data.
comments.request: Document or add functions for embeddings and prediction.
comments.quote: does BioEncoder provide functionality for (i) outputting the image embeddings (i.e. those summarised by PCA in Fig. 3c) for downstream analysis, or (ii) predict classes on a new dataset using the trained model?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether BioEncoder supports unsupervised learning; the option is not documented.
comments.request: Make unsupervised functionality apparent, ideally with a worked example.
comments.quote: We were also unsure whether BioEncoder is designed only for supervised contrastive learning (using labelled data) or if there is also functionality for unsupervised learning (e.g. SimCLR-type applications).

comments.issue: The full range of methodological options (architectures, loss functions, augmentations) is not documented.
comments.request: Provide a detailed list of methodological options.
comments.quote: it would be useful if somewhere a detailed list of the full range of methodological options could be provided

comments.issue: The difference between stage 1 and stage 2 models must be gleaned from the training sections.
comments.request: State the stage 1 versus stage 2 difference clearly.
comments.quote: it would be useful to have a clearer statement of difference between stage 1 and stage 2 models

comments.issue: YAML configuration files are not explained for non-specialist users.
comments.request: Briefly explain YAML configuration files.
comments.quote: L93 – briefly explain what YAML configuration files are

comments.issue: UMAP is a popular visualisation approach that could be considered alongside PCA and t-SNE.
comments.request: Consider adding UMAP.
comments.quote: In addition to PCA and t-SNE, UMAP is also a popular visualisation approach the authors may wish to consider

title: BioEncoder : A metric learning toolkit for comparative organismal biology

study.system: 27 bird populations from 7 species; genetic connectivity and simulations

editor_summary: Both reviewers find the study interesting and potentially suitable, but raise concerns about overstated climate conclusions, the limited species set, ORSIM's missing climate, climate-data reporting, ecoregion weighting and conservation speculation; some may need new analyses.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and innovative, but the broad claim that climate tracking does not drive migration is overstated given the limited species set.
strengths: innovative combination of citizen science, genetic data and simulations

comments.issue: Only six species, a limited subset of North American avifauna, may not be a good suite for testing the hypotheses.
comments.request: Justify the species selection or temper the general claims.
comments.quote: The study focuses on 6 species representing a clearly limited subset of species of North American avifauna.

comments.issue: The broad conclusion that seasonal climate tracking is not a primary driver of migration is too strong given the number of species considered.
comments.request: Soften the broad-scale climate conclusion.
comments.quote: The broader conclusion that that seasonal climate tracking is not a primary driver of intraspecific migration patterns on a broader scale is a strong statement given the number of species considered

comments.issue: The ORSIM simulation omits climate, so it is unclear whether resource access is captured independently of indirect climate effects.
comments.request: Justify that ORSIM adequately captures resource access without climate.
comments.quote: Can you provide further justification that accessing environmental resources (independent of indirect climate effects on resource availability) is adequately captured by the ORSIM.

comments.issue: The climate data are not described in enough detail (which statistic, why a 13-year average, and the two-month June-July period).
comments.request: Specify the climate statistics and averaging period.
comments.quote: there is no information as to whether this is maximum or maximum temper or total precipitation or some other kind of climate statistics

comments.issue: Aggregating abundance by ecoregion assumes one breeding sample represents a whole ecoregion and may introduce bias.
comments.request: Justify the ecoregion stratification or use an alternative classification.
comments.quote: It seems like a large assumption that one sample of a breeding sample is all that is needed to suggest that the entire ecoregion is occupied.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and comprehensive study with clear limitations; asks for more justification of climate niches, migration distances, sampling biases and conservation context.

comments.issue: Using only temperature and precipitation to define species' climate niches is restrictive and not justified.
comments.request: Elaborate and justify the choice of climate variables.
comments.quote: I suggest further elaboration and justification for the choice of climate variables used to define species’ climate niches.

comments.issue: There is no precedent or reference for the way migration distances were calculated.
comments.request: Provide references supporting the migration-distance calculation.
comments.quote: is there precedence (i.e. references) for calculating migration distances in this way?

comments.issue: A map of the ecoregions used in the analyses is missing.
comments.request: Provide a map of the ecoregions in the supplemental information.
comments.quote: providing a map of the ecoregions used in analyses in the supplemental information would be helpful

comments.issue: Sample sizes and spatial biases are not clear for species other than the Yellow Warbler.
comments.request: Report sample sizes in figure legends and discuss inferential limits.
comments.quote: providing sample sizes in the supplemental figure legends would be helpful as it is difficult to sum up the number of black dots

comments.issue: Conservation implications are presented mostly as speculation without evidence from the studied or similar species.
comments.request: Add evidence and examples strengthening the conservation discussion.
comments.quote: while I generally agree that populations that track climate seasonally are potentially at higher risk from climate change, I think that this is mostly discussed as speculation in the final paragraph of the paper

comments.issue: A conceptual figure walking the reader from hypotheses to expectations to implications is missing.
comments.request: Consider adding a conceptual Figure 1.
comments.quote: I am curious whether a third conceptual figure may be helpful (as Figure 1) that visually captures the ideas described in the Introduction

comments.issue: The ORSIM simulator is not described sufficiently, forcing readers to consult Somveille et al. 2021.
comments.request: Add details on the software and the species it was developed for.
comments.quote: can a few more details be provided on this simulator without the reader having to review Somveille et al. 2021? What software is it implemented in, etc?

title: Broad‐scale seasonal climate tracking is a consequence, not a driver, of avian migratory connectivity

study.system: global mountain bird elevational distributions; Oecophylla ants and diet guilds

editor_summary: Four reviews span the spectrum; findings are potentially very important but robustness of evidence is questioned: aridity, biogeographic and spatial confounds may drive patterns, the Oecophylla impact needs direct demonstration, and density-richness mechanistic links need more evidence.

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic support; results robust to covariates, with a suggestion to make the Himalaya contrast explicit.
strengths: results robust to various covariates and datasets

comments.issue: The contrast between the western (no Oecophylla) and eastern (Oecophylla) Himalaya is not made explicit, although adjacent regions are a valuable control.
comments.request: Add this comparison as a figure and in the main text.
comments.quote: The supplemental information mentions that the western Himalaya does not have Oecophylla while the eastern Himalaya does. Why not make this comparison explicit in a figure and in the main text?

comments.issue: Category definitions are inconsistent across figures.
comments.request: Check that categories are consistent across figures.
comments.quote: Check to see that the categories are consistent across figures, as I don't think they are.

comments.issue: Outlier points are double-plotted in Figures 2 and 4.
comments.request: Fix the double-plotted outliers.
comments.quote: Outlier points are double-plotted in Figures 2 and 4

reviews.assessment: Well-written and seemingly well-supported, but aridity and questionable Oecophylla occurrence data may drive the patterns.
strengths: reveals a clear difference between regions

comments.issue: Arid-based mountains have sparse vegetation and few low-elevation birds; this effect is stronger than acknowledged and could confound the patterns.
comments.request: Account for aridity effects more thoroughly.
comments.quote: A comment on arid-based mountains is given in line 248-250, but I think the effect is much stronger than suggested

comments.issue: Oecophylla likely does not occur in many mountain areas marked as occupied (e.g. Somali Mts, Miombo, Cape region, Tibetan/Chinese plateaus, Australian highlands, Tasmania).
comments.request: Verify occurrence evidence or remove these regions from the analysis.
comments.quote: Unless you find evidence of occurrence in these highlands, they must be removed from the analysis!

comments.issue: For Mt region 32, Oecophylla occurs only along southern foothills, so species from other slopes and endemics from eastern Tibet, Sichuan and Yunnan should be excluded.
comments.request: Restrict the dataset to species present on the southern slope.
comments.quote: So this means that you can only include the elevational distributions of species, which are present on the southern slope

comments.issue: Using a single global elevational range per species is a severe generalization, since widespread species use different elevations in different regions.
comments.request: Account for regional variation in elevational ranges.
comments.quote: Also, it is a severe generalization that the Quintero & Jetz dataset employs a single global elevational range for each species

comments.issue: The delHoyo et al. reference does not specify which of the 17 Handbook of the Birds of the World volumes is meant.
comments.request: Specify the volume.
comments.quote: The17-volume 'Handbook of the Birds of the World' was published from 1992 to 2017. So which volume do you refer to?

reviews.assessment: Well-written and novel, but methodological issues (collinearity, model distributions, missing code) must be resolved before publication.
strengths: well-written exploration of competition as a driver of range limits
novel focus on distantly related taxa

comments.issue: Whether Oecophylla and birds actually consume the same insects is unknown, so diet overlap cannot be assumed.
comments.request: Add language acknowledging uncertainty about diet overlap.
comments.quote: The fact that both groups consume insects doesn't necessarily imply that they feed on the same kinds of insects.

comments.issue: Maximum productivity and maximum precipitation elevations are likely correlated, so including both in model 1 may bias results.
comments.request: Check the correlation and address collinearity.
comments.quote: Have the authors looked at the correlations between these two variables? High precipitation regions are often highly productive, and if this correlation is true here as well, then having both variables in the model could introduce a significant bias.

comments.issue: The R function used to fit model 1 is not reported.
comments.request: Report the function and software used.
comments.quote: There is also no information as to what function was used to fit model 1 in R (I presume R was used here, but I am not certain of that either). This needs to be remedied.

comments.issue: Species richness is an integer variable but model 2 was fitted with a Gaussian distribution, and its parametrization is not described.
comments.request: Fit richness with a Poisson distribution and describe the model.
comments.quote: Species richness in an integer variable and must be fitted with a Poisson distribution, rather than Gaussian distribution (which is almost always a default in any statistical function).

comments.issue: No R code is provided to reproduce the analyses.
comments.request: Provide the analysis code before publication.
comments.quote: There is also no R code provided for anyone to reproduce the analysis (I would request that this last point is remedied before the manuscript is published).

comments.issue: Line-level copy edit: replace the comma after Oecophylla with a period at line 120.
comments.quote: Line 120: replace comma after Oecophylla with a period.

title: Ant impacts on global patterns of bird elevational diversity

study.system: seven LTER forest communities; mast seeding synchrony across 103 woody species

editor_summary: Editor: all three reviewers are enthusiastic about the work even though there is room for improvement, and strongly encourages the authors to follow all reviewer suggestions.

reviews.assessment: Noteworthy, well-analyzed paper; asks for a much deeper theoretical framework and more differentiated null hypotheses.
strengths: novel findings on drought effects and traits

comments.issue: The introduction does not lay out a clear structure of theoretical expectations for between-species synchrony.
comments.request: Build a clear theoretical framework for BSS in the introduction.
comments.quote: I think the current MS does not quite seize the chance to lay out in the Intro a clear structure for what the theoretical expectations would be for BSS

comments.issue: Conclusions drawn from rejecting the artificial null go too far, since several causes are possible.
comments.request: Temper conclusions drawn from rejecting the mathematical null.
comments.quote: So I think they go too far in what can be concluded from the rejected null, when there are several possible causes

comments.issue: The paper should explain why masting is studied within species and why selective benefits of BSS are hard to envisage.
comments.request: Explain the economy-of-scale framework and why BSS is harder to explain.
comments.quote: it is much harder to think of good plausible selective benefits of BSS (especially among distantly related species)

comments.issue: Questions about selective benefits of BSS and how they could be tested are not spelled out.
comments.request: Lay out whether BSS can be selectively beneficial and how to test it.
comments.quote: they now want people to think about whether there could be selective benefit of BSS, how that might work, how it could select for increased synchrony over time, and what the definitive tests of key parts might look like

comments.issue: Possible scenarios and null hypotheses for BSS are not defined, nor are non-selective drivers of synchrony.
comments.request: Define the possible scenarios and null hypotheses.
comments.quote: So what this paper has the opportunity to do is to define better what the possible scenarios and null hypotheses are.

comments.issue: Several prior references relevant to these ideas are not cited.
comments.request: Cite the prior literature on the proposed scenarios.
comments.quote: There are also a number of prior references to some of these ideas, as listed below, some of which are not cited in this MS.

comments.issue: The mathematical null has limited biological relevance because randomisation ignores environmental variation and resource constraints.
comments.request: Reframe what rejecting the null actually shows.
comments.quote: it’s of limited biological relevance, as the randomised dataset assumes the plant is completely unaffected by environmental variation

comments.issue: The Moran effect should be treated as the real null hypothesis, with interest in departures from it.
comments.request: Adopt the Moran effect as the default expectation and analyse departures.
comments.quote: I expect this is the real null hypothesis, and as the default expectation

comments.issue: Moran effect by veto does not merit a separate category for between-species synchrony.
comments.request: Merge the veto scenario into the general Moran effect.
comments.quote: so I think Moran by veto is not worth a separate category

comments.issue: Moran effects by shared cue are mentioned but not integrated into a systematic framework, and the Schauber et al. year is wrong.
comments.request: Integrate the shared-cue scenario and correct the reference year.
comments.quote: This point is made in the MS, but not in the context of a systematic framework.

comments.issue: The conditions for selectively beneficial BSS are raised only generally.
comments.request: State clearly the conditions for adaptive between-species synchrony.
comments.quote: The current MS keeps raising this idea in a rather general way, but it should be laid out more clearly at the start what the conditions are.

comments.issue: The scenarios and prior literature are not laid out in the introduction, so the data are not linked to the possible outcomes.
comments.request: Lay out the scenarios in the introduction and state how the data test them.
comments.quote: So I think this should be laid out in the Introduction, including the prior literature, and this MS should then say how their data are going to test the more detailed list of various possible outcomes.

comments.issue: Downstream community effects are scattered and overemphasized relative to their interest.
comments.request: Group them at lines 417-421 and keep the treatment brief.
comments.quote: I suggest these all be grouped together in one place (put it all at about line 417-421), and kept brief because in general I think this is not particularly interesting.

comments.issue: The end of the discussion is vague because hypotheses are not well differentiated.
comments.request: Restructure the discussion around the defensible conclusions.
comments.quote: The end of the Discussion (lines 459-519) is really rather vague, I think because of the lack of well differentiated hypotheses.

comments.issue: The CWD and shared development-time results are not interpreted as evidence for Moran effects.
comments.request: Interpret these results as evidence for Moran effects.
comments.quote: The very interesting effect of drought (CWD) is probably good evidence for the existence of Moran effects.

comments.issue: Within-genus pairs are not tested separately even though close relatives may show enhanced synchrony.
comments.request: Test statistically for within-genus versus other pairs.
comments.quote: I think it would also be worth testing statistically for an effect of being very close relatives (within-genus vs all other pairs)

comments.issue: Allen & Platt 1990 is an odd citation and was not the first to make the pollination-efficiency point.
comments.request: Cite the appropriate original studies (e.g. Norton & Kelly, Kelly et al.).
comments.quote: Allen & Platt 1990 seems an odd citation here. That is a good case study of pollination efficiency in Nothofagus, but it wasn’t the first paper to make that point

comments.issue: Line 155 should mention shared seed predators, pollinators, traits and phylogeny.
comments.request: Add the full list of shared factors.
comments.quote: line 155 should perhaps say “due to shared seed predators, shared pollinators, shared plant traits or phylogeny”

comments.issue: Spearman correlations are safe but lower powered than Pearson on log-transformed data.
comments.request: Consider Pearson correlations on log-transformed data.
comments.quote: I did wonder if the use of Spearman correlations was sub-optimal. They are safe but lower power.

comments.issue: The text at lines 339-340 contradicts Figure 5 for Dispersal Syndrome and Shade Tolerance.
comments.request: Reconcile the text with the figure.
comments.quote: Text seems at variance with Fig 5, where Dispersal Syndrome has higher mean synch with shared dispersal (text says lower)

comments.issue: The paragraph at line 399 needs rewriting and omits key within-genus synchrony examples.
comments.request: Rewrite and include Schauber et al. 2002 and within-genus examples.
comments.quote: This paragraph needs major rewriting, as even some of the examples given are not all closely related species

comments.issue: Cleavitt and Fahey 2017 is an odd citation for a pattern shown more broadly elsewhere.
comments.request: Cite the broader studies (e.g. Schauber et al. 2002, Kelly et al. 2013).
comments.quote: Cleavitt and Fahey 2017 seems an odd citation here when all they show is that two co-occurring species (Acer saccarum and Fagus grandifolia) at two sites both respond to warm summers the year before

comments.issue: Calling mast seeding a community-level phenomenon is wrong; it is a population-level phenomenon with community-level effects.
comments.request: Correct this distinction at line 507.
comments.quote: I disagree. In evolutionary terms, it’s clearly a population-level phenomenon, which then has community-level downstream effects.

comments.issue: Figure 1 would read better starting with the map.
comments.request: Swap the left and right sides of Figure 1.
comments.quote: This is a lovely figure. I would swap the left and right sides, so start with the map (c) then give two examples.

reviews.assessment: Largest study of cross-species masting synchrony with interesting outcomes, but model structure, baseline comparisons and trait selection need work.
strengths: worth prime time in a journal such as Ecology Letters

comments.issue: Traits and climate are analysed in two separate models although interactions between them are expected.
comments.request: Combine them into one model that includes interactions.
comments.quote: There are two sperate models created to test for the effects of traits and climate on synchrony. Unclear why that is not one model

comments.issue: Comparing synchrony to randomised time series is less informative than comparing it to within-species synchrony.
comments.request: Compare across-species with within-species synchrony, including climate effects.
comments.quote: ecologically more interesting question appears to be how across-species synchrony compares to within species than to random

comments.issue: Why these traits were selected is unclear, although other relevant traits exist, and trait pooling creates researcher degrees of freedom.
comments.request: Justify the trait selection and show it is not outcome-driven.
comments.quote: I am not suggesting that the traits selected are wrong, but it is unclear why these, while not others that are available and known to correlate with masting are not used.

comments.issue: Referencing is sparse and the economies-of-scale citations are outdated.
comments.request: Update citations (e.g. Zwolak 2022, Kelly 2001, Rapp 2013, Bogdziewicz 2020) and position the paper in the literature.
comments.quote: For example, please update citations on economies of scale. It has currently 4 citations only, and three of them are from 1990 or before.

comments.issue: The economies-of-scale paragraph is disconnected from the study topic.
comments.request: Shorten it or link it to the questions tested.
comments.quote: Paragraph on Economies of Scale is now disconnected from the topic of the study.

comments.issue: No rationale is given for why among-species synchrony in masting is a worthy topic.
comments.request: Explain what is gained from studying interspecific synchrony.
comments.quote: the text basically points towards the gap but does not say why that gap requires closing, and what important comes from studying the interspecific synchrony

comments.issue: The sentence at L124 wrongly excludes satiation through across-species synchrony as an ecological consequence.
comments.request: Remove or revise the sentence.
comments.quote: L124: improved satiation through across-species synchrony is also an ecological consequence, I think.

comments.issue: The introduction does not name the traits expected to matter or cite Journe et al. 2023.
comments.request: Name the predicted traits and add the citation.
comments.quote: After reading the Introduction, is not clear what traits are going to be tested, other than pollination type.

comments.issue: The statement at L140 lacks supporting references.
comments.request: Support it with references (e.g. Wion, Pesendorfer et al. 2016).
comments.quote: I think that sentence could be backed up by some references

comments.issue: The statement at L141 about mutualist availability needs a citation.
comments.request: Add a supporting citation.
comments.quote: citation that would support that statement is required (higher mutualists availability in less harsh conditions)

comments.issue: The abbreviations at L176 are unexplained.
comments.request: Define the site abbreviations.
comments.quote: L176: unclear what these abbreviations mean (AND, CDR, SEV etc)

comments.issue: 'Ordered' at L195 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning.
comments.quote: L195: unclear what ordered means here?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the L249 analysis is at tree/plant or population level.
comments.request: State the level of analysis.
comments.quote: L249: is that done on tree/plant level or population level?

comments.issue: 'Relative contribution' at L292 is unclear for what appears to be a simple mixed model.
comments.request: Explain how relative contribution was quantified.
comments.quote: L292: unclear what is relative contribution here, as the model appears to be a simple mixed model

comments.issue: What the green/gray points in Fig. 5 represent is unclear given the 'across all sites' legend.
comments.request: Clarify the points and legend.
comments.quote: Fig. 5: unclear what each green/gray point is. I would guess that is within-site synchrony (across-species), but the legend says “across all sites” implying that it also includes synchrony across-sites.

comments.issue: The significance of shade tolerance is not justified by the data distribution.
comments.request: Reconsider or qualify this significance.
comments.quote: The significance of the shade tolerance appears unjustified by the data distribution.

comments.issue: What 'actual' traits in Fig. 6 means is unclear.
comments.request: Define the term in the figure.
comments.quote: Fig. 6: unclear what “actual” traits are

comments.issue: The general importance of synchrony is not stated for the journal's scope.
comments.request: Explain why synchrony is a key aspect.
comments.quote: L386: given the general scope of the journal, I think that it is important to say why synchrony is a key aspect

comments.issue: How forest community dynamics can be affected is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the consequences for community dynamics.
comments.quote: L388: for same reason, I think that it is important to say how these forest community dynamics can be affected

comments.issue: Lines 386-398 only summarize results instead of highlighting key insights and their importance for theory.
comments.request: Highlight the most important insights and implications.
comments.quote: in addition to a summary of results, it would be great to hear why these outcomes are important and what all that means for ecological theory

comments.issue: The paragraph at L412 ends with a broad, low-information statement.
comments.request: Name what specifically is learned.
comments.quote: that paragraph ends with a broad statement that has low information value

comments.issue: Why asynchrony would be beneficial is unclear at L428.
comments.request: Revise the sentence.
comments.quote: L428: please revise, it is unclear why asynchrony would be beneficial from that sentence.

comments.issue: The statement at L436 is contradicted by the finding that synchrony was higher in animal-pollinated species.
comments.request: Reconcile the sentence with the results.
comments.quote: L436: Isn’t that sentence contradicted by the results?

comments.issue: Table 2 suggests phylogeny was simply not a predictor, not a poor one.
comments.request: Reword 'poor predictor'.
comments.quote: L463: Table 2 suggest phylogeny was just not predictor of synchrony, not a poor predictor

comments.issue: Calling masting a community-level phenomenon is hard to accept; it is a population-level phenomenon that can extend across populations and species.
comments.request: Justify or revise the statement at L507.
comments.quote: L507: well, I think that it is hard to agree with such statement. Masting seeding is actually a population-level phenomenon and can extend across populations and species.

comments.issue: Forecasting at L509 should cite Pearse et al. and Journe et al. 2023.
comments.request: Add these citations.
comments.quote: L509: if forecasting is mentioned, then it is worthy to cite Pearse et al. from PTRSB and Journe et al. 2023 New Phytologist.

title: Community Synchrony in Seed Production is Associated With Trait Similarity and Climate Across North America

study.system: tree phyllosphere; arthropods and microbes

editor_summary: Reviewers find the study interesting and original but want thorough revision: recognize two-way insect-microbe effects, detail sampling and conditions, explain year differences, and contextualize natural shelter prevalence.

reviews.assessment: Mostly well-described experiment, but leaf sampling positions, sampling units and temporal replication need clarification.
strengths: sample numbers and tree distances reported

comments.issue: Position of the five sampled leaves within the canopy is not described.
comments.request: Describe where in the canopy the five leaves were sampled.
comments.quote: the sampling site of leaves was not shown in the article. So, I did not understand how the five leaves distributed across the canopy, bottom, middle or upper?

comments.issue: Sampling units differ between trials (one swab per five leaves versus per leaf) and the leaf-tree relationship is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling unit and leaf-tree relationship in each trial.
comments.quote: one swab was used for each leaf in trial 2, the phyllosphere bacteria samples were from one single leaf. Regretably, how the authors treated the relationship between sample leaf and sample tree was not shown in the article.

comments.issue: Raw microbial data are not deposited in a public repository.
comments.request: Deposit the raw microbial data at NCBI.
comments.quote: I suggest the raw data of microbes should be deposited at NCBI.

comments.issue: Each trial has only one sampling time, so between-trial differences rest on unreplicated time points.
comments.request: Add temporal replication or temper the between-trial comparison.
comments.quote: The lack of sampling time replicates increased the risk of impartial analysis on the differences among the two trials.

comments.issue: Leaf rolling alters leaf physiology and VOCs, an alternative driver of the microbiome not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the physiological and VOC consequences of rolling.
comments.quote: the rolling treatment changed the leaf shape, which would affect the phyisological trait (like VOCs, volatile organic compounds) which often play important roles in shaping the phyllosphere microbial community

comments.issue: 2 line-level copy edits
comments.quote: 2.L 354, (Wetzel et al., 2016) should be changed to Wetzel et al.(2016), the same mistake also exist at L356

reviews.assessment: Interesting field experiment, but the one-way causal framing, contamination risk and year-specific results raise concerns.
strengths: field experiment repeated in two years

comments.issue: A one-way causal link from herbivores to microbes is asserted without support; the reverse is plausible.
comments.request: Recognize and substantiate bidirectional arthropod-microbe effects.
comments.quote: The assumption that there is a causal link from herbivore presence to microbes is stated as a fact in several places in the text. I have not been able to find any reference that this is a general fact.

comments.issue: Shelter construction is not described and contamination precautions are unknown.
comments.request: Describe how shelters were made and how sterility was maintained.
comments.quote: There is no description of how the shelters were made in any detail. For example, what measures that were taken to keep the hands and material sterile while constructing the shelters.

comments.issue: Main conclusions rest on the 2018 results although only that year showed significant effects.
comments.request: Temper conclusions or justify using 2018 as the basis.
comments.quote: Still, the authors use the results from 2018 as a basis for their main conclusions. To me, this is stretching the ‘truth’.

comments.issue: How common natural leaf shelters are, and thus how much their effects matter, is not established.
comments.request: Report and cite shelter abundance data to gauge importance.
comments.quote: If the shelters are not very common, their importance may be minute. I have been able to find one paper reporting about the abundance of leaf shelters: Baer & Marquis (2014)

comments.issue: Artificial shelters may differ in effect from natural shelters.
comments.request: Discuss the artificial-versus-natural shelter difference.
comments.quote: Could there be a difference in the effect between artificial vs natural leaf shelters? If so, how large a difference?

comments.issue: Causal one-way wording at lines 57, 187-8, 251, 253-4, 257, 273 and 305.
comments.request: Rephrase these statements to allow bidirectional effects.
comments.quote: Li 251 ‘had a positive impact’ indicate a strong causal relationship.

comments.issue: The temperature variable is not defined.
comments.request: State whether temperature is mean daily or otherwise.
comments.quote: Li 125 What does the temperature refer to? Mean daily or what?

comments.issue: Basis for the 0.6 cm leaf-roll diameter and whether inner or outer is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the diameter and specify inner or outer.
comments.quote: Li 135 The choice to make the leaf rolls having a diameter of 0.6 cm what is based on? Does the figure refer to inner or outer diameter?

comments.issue: Shelter construction details, including contamination handling, are missing.
comments.request: Describe how the shelters were made in more detail.
comments.quote: Li 135 A more detailed description about how the shelters were made would be good, including how the risk of contamination was handled.

comments.issue: Pin diameter is not reported.
comments.request: Report the pin diameter.
comments.quote: Li 136 What size (diameter) were the pins?

comments.issue: Tree size, height and age are not reported.
comments.request: Report tree characteristics.
comments.quote: Li 137 How tall/large/old were the trees?

comments.issue: Inspection procedure is undescribed; arthropods may drop off when approached, biasing counts.
comments.request: Describe the arthropod inspection procedure.
comments.quote: Li 140-2 How was the inspection done? It is likely that some arthropods leave (e.g. drop off the leaves) when approached by a human.

comments.issue: 4 line-level copy edits (Li 148, 332, 337, 357)
comments.quote: Li 332 Insert a space between ‘2007).’ and ‘Other’.

comments.issue: Too many significant figures are reported throughout lines 212-256.
comments.request: Reduce the number of significant figures throughout.
comments.quote: The number of significant figures are too many. That kind of accuracy in the measurements indicate that there were tens of thousands of observations, which there were not.

comments.issue: p=0.06 is treated as significant although the stated threshold is p=0.05.
comments.request: Apply the stated significance threshold consistently.
comments.quote: Li 219 p=0.06 is taken as a significant effect although it is stated that the authors generally use p=0.05 as a limit.

comments.issue: 'Nevertheless' at line 265 makes the sentence out of place.
comments.request: Rephrase or remove it.
comments.quote: The use of ‘Nevertheless’ here is not clear to me. The whole sentence becomes out of place.

comments.issue: Humidity was not measured.
comments.request: Add humidity measurements if possible.
comments.quote: Li 297 Would have been interesting to see some measurements of humidity levels.

comments.issue: Text implies all herbivores always increase bacterial diversity.
comments.request: Reformulate unless the statement is universal.
comments.quote: As it is stated, one gets the impression that it is always only herbivores that contribute to increased bacteria diversity. But if this is not universal, the sentence should be reformulated.

comments.issue: The conclusion at lines 324-325 may be premature given the experiment.
comments.request: Reformulate the conclusion.
comments.quote: Li 324-5 As the experiment was done, this conclusion may be premature.

comments.issue: 'Nevertheless' at line 327 is confusing.
comments.request: Reformulate the sentence.
comments.quote: Li 327 The use of the word ‘Nevertheless’ is confusing here. Consider reformulation.

comments.issue: Referent of 'its' at line 335 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether it refers to bacteria or microbiome.
comments.quote: Li 335 It is unclear if ’its’ refer to the specific bacteria or the microbiome.

comments.issue: Ecosystem-engineer conclusion rests on human-made, not insect-made, shelters.
comments.request: Reformulate the conclusion about ecosystem engineers.
comments.quote: Li 346-8 This conclusion may need to be reformulated as the leaf shelters in the present study were made by humans and not by what we normally refer to as ecosystem engineers in this case.

comments.issue: Statement at line 371 is only true for one year or part of the year.
comments.request: Clarify the time restriction.
comments.quote: Li 371 This is only true for one year or part of the year. Could be clarified here,

comments.issue: 'Critical' role depends on how common the phenomenon is; evidence of high leaf manipulation is missing.
comments.request: Consider replacing 'critical' with 'potential'.
comments.quote: Li 372 Whether the role is ‘critical’ or not depend to some extent on how common the phenomenon is.

comments.issue: Appendix Figure 5S implies a clear causal relationship.
comments.request: Revise the figure to avoid implying causality.
comments.quote: Appendix Figure 5S – Figure implies a clear causal relationship.

title: Leaf Shelters Facilitate the Colonisation of Arthropods and Enhance Microbial Diversity on Plants

study.system: trees; maturation size vs maximum size; five continents

editor_summary: Editor cannot accept the current version but invites resubmission; reviewers raised model complexity and unclear R0 link, presentation and narrative problems, unclear aims, model assumptions and uncertainty, and data description issues.

reviews.assessment: Sees a valuable piece of work but finds the presentation poor, with unclear aims, weak structure and unsupported or contradictory claims.

comments.issue: Manuscript is extremely long (about twice the needed length) and unpleasant to read.
comments.request: Shorten substantially and focus on the main story.
comments.quote: The tiny font and dense single-spacing make the manuscript unpleasant to read but fail to hide that the manuscript is extremely long

comments.issue: Hypotheses and aims are unclear, and the analyses run (e.g. phylogenetic) do not obviously follow from the introduction.
comments.request: Align the questions and analyses and state the aims clearly.
comments.quote: We emerge from your introduction unclear as to what your hypothesis/aims are and are then surprised in the methods when you set out to do analyses that aren’t obviously related to the introduction

comments.issue: Paragraph structure is weak and disjointed; broader structure spans unrelated topics and repeats ideas.
comments.request: Restructure paragraphs and remove repetitions.
comments.quote: The structure within paragraphs is weak (often feeling like a series of disjointed sentences), and the broader structure is weak too

comments.issue: The text diverts into detailed commentary on specific topics instead of the main message.
comments.request: Focus on the main message.
comments.quote: You often divert into very detailed commentary on specific topics/examples instead of focusing on the main message that you are trying to convey.

comments.issue: Stating the conclusion at the end of the first introduction paragraph is unusual.
comments.request: Move or remove the premature conclusion.
comments.quote: Stating the conclusion at the end of the first paragraph in the introduction is most unusual.

comments.issue: The writing does not convey the narrative: the problem, knowledge gap and current understanding are not explained before the analyses.
comments.request: Explain the knowledge gap and why solving it matters.
comments.quote: you launch into models/analyses without clearly explaining to the readers what the problem/knowledge gap is that you are trying to address

comments.issue: The importance of the positive but sub-proportional maturation-size relationship for plant ecology and coexistence is not explained.
