study.system: grassland plant communities and soil fungi; Jena biodiversity experiment

editor_summary: Mixed reviews; substantial concerns about the experimental approach and novelty because prior papers used the same data; reviewer 2 and 3 points also important; hard to accept now but could be publishable if addressed.

reviews.assessment: Recommends against further consideration: novelty undermined by prior papers using the same data, take-home messages unclear and unsupported, and the disturbed experiment confounds interpretation.
strengths: framing around the recent root economics spectrum
long-term Jena Experiment dataset with reuse value

comments.issue: Fine root biomass-trait axis correlations are circular because both variables are root traits from the same syndrome.
comments.quote: both the response (i.e. fine root biomass) and the predictor (PCA axes) were root traits belonging to a single syndrome of traits

comments.issue: Rationale for using the plant diversity experiment and gradient instead of a grassland network is not motivated.
comments.request: Justify the experimental design or reframe the study rationale.
comments.quote: the authors do not motivate sufficiently why it was important to use the specific experimental design

comments.issue: Plant richness is confounded with microbial biomass and likely drives the weak trait-fungus relationships.
comments.request: Account for the richness gradient when interpreting trait effects.
comments.quote: The inherent plant diversity gradient becomes an issue exactly because of the strong relationship between plant richness and microbial biomass

comments.issue: Richness was fitted after trait axes with Type I sums of squares, so richness was not properly controlled.
comments.request: Refit models so species richness is properly accounted for.
comments.quote: they fitted species richness after the trait axes, which given that these models used Types I Sums of Squares meant that not only did they not account for species richness

comments.issue: Much data already published with comparable conclusions; unclear how this study differs.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution relative to earlier papers.
comments.quote: a lot of those data have already been published in studies with very comparable conclusions and the authors do not make clear how this study differs from those earlier ones

comments.issue: Previously published dataset and metabarcoding methods are re-described without clear disclosure.
comments.request: State that the dataset was previously published and cite it.
comments.quote: I also find it a little dodgy that the authors here do not make it clear that they are referring to an already published dataset and they redescribe the metabarcoding approaches

comments.issue: Earlier results from the same system and exact data are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge and cite prior papers using these data.
comments.quote: the study does not acknowledge earlier results from the exact system with the exact data

comments.issue: Take-home messages are unclear; key concluding sentences are empty of content.
comments.request: Rewrite the take-home messages to state concrete findings.
comments.quote: some key sentences, including those that articulate take home messages such as those in the conclusions paragraph of the manuscript, are (relatively) empty of content

comments.issue: Claim that root economics space and richness jointly determine fungal communities is unsupported without richness correction.
comments.request: Correct for species richness or temper the conclusion.
comments.quote: I think it is unsupported from the results (i.e. the author did not correct for species richness in any of their analyses

comments.issue: Figures lack effect sizes and test statistics, hindering assessment of rigour.
comments.request: Add effect sizes and statistics to the figures.
comments.quote: The authors nonetheless in many cases either do not present effect sizes (e.g. correlation coefficients in Fig. 2) or any statics (e.g. Fig. 4)

comments.issue: Figure colour palettes are unattractive.
comments.request: Improve the figure colour palettes.
comments.quote: Some of the palettes used for the figures look ugly!

comments.issue: Code and data were embargoed, so the analyses could not be checked.
comments.request: Make data and code accessible during review.
comments.quote: I tried the long link to zenodo and it also appeared to be embargoed

comments.issue: Uneven deweeding disturbance across plots likely confounds fungal biomass and community patterns.
comments.request: Report the disturbance regime or discuss it as a confounder.
comments.quote: the intensity of disturbances was uneven across the experiment with one species plots requiring more deweeding than 60 species plots

comments.issue: Sequencing depth was not normalized across metabarcoding samples, possibly affecting guild classification.
comments.request: Normalize sequencing depth or demonstrate it was sufficient.
comments.quote: the authors did not engage into any actions to normalize the sequencing depth across their metabarcoding samples

reviews.assessment: Positive: novel community-level trait approach with appropriate methods, but the abstract, hypothesis links and novelty framing need improvement.
strengths: community-level test of multiple root economics space dimensions
novel results of interest to Ecology Letters readers

comments.issue: Abstract omits key results on how root trait gradients affect fungal guild composition.
comments.request: Add specific root trait-guild results to the abstract.
comments.quote: I found the abstract somewhat 'dry' about the effects of root trait gradients on the composition of soil fungal guilds

comments.issue: Results and conclusion do not link back to the stated hypotheses.
comments.request: Refer to the hypotheses when reporting results and concluding.
comments.quote: I miss some reference to them in the result section when reporting results that test them, and also perhaps in the conclusion

comments.issue: First-time claim for community-level RES evidence ignores earlier studies; discussion unbalanced.
comments.request: Temper the novelty claim and discuss prior community-level studies.
comments.quote: There have been previous studies providing evidence for RES gradients at the community level, there are just a few examples (Erktan et al. 2018; Prieto et al. 2015)

comments.issue: Meaning of 'quantitative and qualitative measures of fungal communities' is undefined and confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction between quantitative and qualitative measures.
comments.quote: What is a bit unclear what do you mean by 'quantitative and qualitative measures of fungal communities' in that context

comments.issue: Unclear which trait-based approaches could be reconciled.
comments.request: Specify the trait-based approaches being referred to.
comments.quote: It is unclear to me what are these trait-based approaches that could be reconcile here

comments.issue: Key results on plant community effects on fungal guilds are missing from the abstract.
comments.request: Add the key results on plant community effects on fungal guilds.
comments.quote: No key results about plant community effects on fungal guilds?

comments.issue: The result is misstated as showing that species richness increases root biomass and reduces litter quality.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence to reflect the actual finding.
comments.quote: this result do not 'suggests that plant species richness effects increase root biomass and reduce litter quality'

comments.issue: Unclear why AM fungal relative abundance is not derived from AMF-specific sequencing reads.
comments.request: Explain or use read-based relative abundance for AM fungi.
comments.quote: Isn't possible to use OTU read number from sequencing with AMF-specific primers to compute relative abundance of the AM fungal guild

comments.issue: The logic of the passage at L321-324 is incomprehensible.
comments.request: Clarify the argument and rewrite the passage.
comments.quote: I do not understand the logic of the idea expressed here.

comments.issue: Unstandardized estimates in Table 2 are difficult to interpret.
comments.request: Provide standardized estimates as in Table 1.
comments.quote: The unstandardized estimate provided are somewhat difficult to interpret

reviews.assessment: Positive: fits the journal with solid data, but asks to validate community-level trait data and clarify several logic and reporting points.
strengths: addresses an important knowledge gap on root economics-microbe feedbacks
solid data from the Jena Experiment
topic well suited to Ecology Letters

comments.issue: Community-level trait data are not directly validated against species-averaged or database trait values.
comments.request: Compare community trait axes with community-weighted means from databases.
comments.quote: to prove the point that community-based trait data reflect those of species-based trait data, would it not be needed to directly compare the root economic space spun up by community data and species-averaged data?

comments.issue: The proposed link between low litter quality and higher saprotroph diversity is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the mechanism linking litter quality to saprotroph diversity.
comments.quote: The logic how litter quality and saprotroph diversity are linked could be expressed in more detail

comments.issue: Explaining how richness regulates pathogens is superfluous if pathogens did not vary with richness.
comments.request: Revise or remove the superfluous explanation.
comments.quote: If plant pathogenic fungi did not vary with plant species richness, is not then the explication how plant richness regulated pathogen density and diversity (Lines 236) superfluous?

comments.issue: Sample numbers (80, 46, 26) and subset selection are unexplained; distribution across richness unknown.
comments.request: Clarify the sample reduction and how the subset was chosen.
comments.quote: There were 80 plots/samples in total, but only 46 random N samples and N transmission was finally only measured for 26 samples

title: Plant Species Richness and the Root Economics Space Drive Soil Fungal Communities

study.system: bacterial communities; species sorting, evolution, ciliate predation

editor_summary: Editor: exciting manuscript assessed by two experts who shared the editor's excitement; comments were fair and constructive, the discussion is too long and should be broken up with sub-headings; major revision recommended.

reviews.assessment: Singular, exceptionally interesting experimental evaluation of eco-evolutionary dynamics that merits publication, with some clarity issues in methods and results.
strengths: unique experimental evaluation of ecological and evolutionary dynamics

comments.issue: Methods and Results are hard to follow because of disciplinary jargon.
comments.request: Improve readability for readers from both disciplines.
comments.quote: Maybe it’s because the authors are trying to bridge two disciplines with their own jargon and standard methodologies

comments.issue: It is unclear why side experiments are termed 'defense' and 'carrying capacity' at the community level.
comments.request: Clarify what these traits indicate at the community level.
comments.quote: I wasn’t quite sure I understood why the side experiments to measure ‘defense’ and ‘carrying capacity’ were given those terms

comments.issue: Few trait evaluations contrast with many community composition measurements; whether this was intentional is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the imbalance in sampling effort.
comments.quote: It also wasn’t completely clear why there were so few evaluations of these traits

comments.issue: The section estimating contributions of species sorting and evolution is hard to digest despite being the key novelty.
comments.request: Add much more explanation and detail to this section.
comments.quote: This needs a lot more explanation and detail to be digestible

comments.issue: Fig. 2 colours are poorly described and the arrows are hard to see.
comments.request: Describe the colours better and make arrows clearer.
comments.quote: The colors need a better description and the arrows are a bit hard to see

comments.issue: Fig. 4 'segment length' is not intuitive.
comments.request: Label it as community change (1/day).
comments.quote: It seems like you might just label this community change (1/day) and avoid some confusion

reviews.assessment: Important contribution with no major comments; only minor methods clarifications and figure improvements are requested.
strengths: important contribution to eco-evolutionary community dynamics
no major comments on the study

comments.issue: Figure 1 text is difficult to read.
comments.request: Enlarge the font and box c.
comments.quote: The text in Figure 1 is difficult to read, consider making the font size larger

comments.issue: Figure 2 needs clarity improvements for symbols, error bars and temporal arrows.
comments.request: Use filled symbols and lighter error bars.
comments.quote: Figure 2 needs to be improved for clarity. Please use filled symbols, and place error bars to the back in a possible lighter color

comments.issue: L192 seems contradictory: communities dominated by 8 species yet diversity maintained.
comments.request: Clarify whether the other 16 species were still present.
comments.quote: Despite this, bacterial diversity was maintained? Somehow this sounds a bit contradictory to me. Were the other 16 bacterial species still present?

comments.issue: Figure 6 uses boxplots for only three values.
comments.request: Show mean symbols with standard errors and smaller replicate symbols.
comments.quote: instead of using boxplots (which is a bit odd when one only has 3 values), one could consider having a larger sized symbol to reflect the mean values

comments.issue: The sentence on L429-433 is long and complex.
comments.request: Split the sentence to clarify the message.
comments.quote: This was a long and complex sentence to follow. Consider splitting the sentence to clarify the message of this sentence

comments.issue: Extended Data Figure 9 does not state whether bars are means or medians, the number of replicates, or error bars.
comments.request: Report replicate numbers and add error bars.
comments.quote: Are the bars representing mean or median values? And how many replicates were they? Should there not be error bars added to these values?

comments.issue: Whether OD measurements in the presence of the predator follow the L763-764 method and whether cultures were predator-free for 96 h is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the OD measurement conditions.
comments.quote: When OD is measured for the bacterial cultures, in the presence of the predator, is this done using the method described in L763-764?

comments.issue: The sentence on L793-794 about four species improving both traits is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether improving one trait reduced the other.
comments.quote: This sentence is a bit unclear. 4 species were able to improve both traits. But do you mean that for the other species then improving one trait resulted in a decline in the other trait?

comments.issue: The section on L789-799 reads like results.
comments.request: Move these sentences to results and/or discussion.
comments.quote: This entire section reads as a result section, so consider moving these sentences to results and/or discussion

comments.issue: Community trajectory analysis is not done separately for predator-free communities despite different sampling intervals.
comments.request: Run the trajectory analysis on predator-free communities separately.
comments.quote: I understand that the predator-free communities were sampled at different time intervals, but it would still be possible to do the community trajectory analysis on the predator-free communities separately

comments.issue: It is unclear what identifying species with significant impact on community trajectories involved and what the envfit function does.
comments.request: Explain the envfit analysis and its place in the workflow.
comments.quote: I wasn’t sure what you meant with “species with significant impact to community trajectories were identified”

comments.issue: Patterns in abundance of the seven bacterial species the ciliate evolved on are not examined, though they may explain the stronger prey evolutionary history effect.
comments.request: Report how these species responded to evolved predators.
comments.quote: I was wondering if there was any pattern found between the abundance of the 7 bacterial species the ciliate predator was evolved to

title: Temporal Changes in the Role of Species Sorting and Evolution Determine Community Dynamics

study.system: aquatic ciliate microcosms; 110 experimental time series with Lotka-Volterra models

editor_summary: Editor finds the core claim robust and important but says all reviewers think it exceeds the evidence; asks authors to show the problem generalizes beyond their model/data and to discuss what successful management modelling looks like.

reviews.assessment: Strongly disagrees with the premise; the simple model is a straw man that ignores alternative models and methods.

comments.issue: The design sets up a straw man by denying alternative models and methods, limiting the scope of the investigation.
comments.request: Consider alternative models and methods instead of dismissing them.
comments.quote: I find that the design of the study sets up a straw man of a model that limits the scope of their investigation because it denies the presence of alternative models and methods.

comments.issue: The simple generalized Lotka-Volterra model is not justified for these data; nonlinearity, openness and interaction form are unexamined.
comments.request: Justify the model form or use a more appropriate functional form.
comments.quote: The model used is very simple and the paper lacks any evidence that it is a reasonable model to use for these specific data.

comments.issue: The model is not contextualized and qualitative knowledge is ignored in favour of quantitative results.
comments.request: Contextualize the model and consider qualitative observations.
comments.quote: This paper also focuses very heavily on quantitative results but qualitative observations are also vital to consider.

comments.issue: The paper ignores the wealth of modelling studies with important conservation-management implications.
comments.request: Acknowledge this modelling literature.
comments.quote: The paper does not acknowledge the wealth of modeling studies that have had important implications in conservation management and other related fields.

comments.issue: Results might improve with model selection, a priori parameter restrictions, advanced statistical methods, and reframed claims.
comments.request: Use model selection, parameter restrictions and more advanced statistical methods.
comments.quote: Perhaps more promising results would be obtained if, for example, the authors used model selection, made a priori restrictions on parameters based on what is known about the system, integrated more advanced statistical methods

reviews.assessment: Interesting, timely use of experimental data with excellent figures, but the general claims are overgeneralized and would be stronger with model selection.

comments.issue: Results from one model class and dataset are overgeneralized to the utility of ecosystem models in general.
comments.request: Temper the general claims by the study's limitations.
comments.quote: However, the claim that mechanistic ecosystem models in general are not useful should be tempered by the limitations of this study

comments.issue: The analysis lacks model or variable selection showing that interaction estimates are ambiguous yet significantly different from zero.
comments.request: Add model selection to strengthen the inference about interspecific interactions.
comments.quote: I think this claim would be stronger if there is some sort of model selection or variable selection to show that estimates of interspecific interactions are both ambiguous across models AND significantly different than 0

comments.issue: It is unclear whether there were replicated ecosystems or species sets and whether models were fit to one or multiple time series.
comments.request: Clarify replication and how many time series each model was fit to.
comments.quote: I am curious if all models were fit to one time series or multiple time series (in the case of replicated ecosystems/species sets).

comments.issue: The introduction is framed as addressing structural uncertainty, but the study addresses only parameter uncertainty.
comments.request: Reframe the introduction so it does not claim to address structural uncertainty.
comments.quote: but this is also the primary limitation in this study. This study addresses parameter uncertainty but not structural uncertainty

comments.issue: The introduction should name the specific model used, since results concern Lotka-Volterra models rather than ecosystem models generally.
comments.request: Mention the specific ecosystem model in the introduction.
comments.quote: It’s probably worth mentioning the specific ecosystem model used here, since the results show that multi-species Lotka-Volterra models produced inaccurate forecasts, rather than ecosystem models, generally.

comments.issue: The null model ni(t=19) = ni(t=18) may be inappropriate; a stochastic-mean null would be better and 'evidently false' is too strong.
comments.request: Reconsider the null model and the claim that it is evidently false.
comments.quote: I’m wondering if the null comparison should therefore be ni(t=19) = mean(ni)?

comments.issue: No sensitivity analysis of the perturbation magnitude; removing a species may change forecast ambiguity.
comments.request: Provide detail and a sensitivity analysis for the perturbation value.
comments.quote: One could imagine that the consistency of model predictions in response to a perturbation would be very sensitive to the magnitude of the perturbation.

comments.issue: Oscillating interaction estimates interpreted as ambiguity may actually indicate a true interaction of zero.
comments.request: Use bootstrapping, variable selection or model selection to test whether interactions differ from zero.
comments.quote: I’m a bit skeptical about the interpretation of interspecific relationships as “ambiguous.”

comments.issue: The claim that ecosystem models are not useful for decisions is too strong because failure could stem from structural uncertainty or insufficient data.
comments.request: Weaken the claim and acknowledge these alternative explanations.
comments.quote: However, the claim that ecosystem models are not useful for supporting decisions seems too strong, since the results could be related to structural uncertainty

comments.issue: The text conflates testing numerous conflicting models with testing parameter sets of a single model.
comments.request: Highlight that numerous fits to one model, not multiple models, were tested.
comments.quote: I think it’s worth highlighting that this study did not test numerous conflicting models, but rather tested numerous fits (or parameter sets) to one model.

comments.issue: The discussion of linearity assumptions and high-dimensional models should be fleshed out with examples.
comments.request: Flesh out this idea and cite examples of mechanistic models with p >>> n.
comments.quote: Is it possible to flesh this idea out further? Do mechanistic models always assume linear relationships? Is it possible to cite examples of mechanistic models where p >>> n?

comments.issue: The call for innovation should mention machine learning approaches that outperform mechanistic models.
comments.request: Add references on machine learning outperforming mechanistic models.
comments.quote: It would be useful to include references to examples where machine learning approaches outperform mechanistic models

comments.issue: Figure 1 y-axes appear to be labelled incorrectly.
comments.request: Check whether the y-axes should be n1(t) to n4(t).
comments.quote: Figure 1: Should the y-axes be n1(t)

comments.issue: Figure 4 caption says 'Ability ... to identify' although the figure compares agreement across models.
comments.request: Change the caption to 'Agreement of the ecosystem models in identifying the character'.
comments.quote: This figure compares the consistency of inference across models, rather than comparing the estimate to the true (unknown) character of interspecific interactions.

comments.issue: Five line-level edits: confusing wording at 104-105, strange sentence at 113-114, 'While this produces a measure' at 132, an extra semicolon at 312 and a duplicated reference at 460.
comments.quote: Line 132: Should read “While this produces a measure”.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and comprehensive work that is an important step, but the claims are too bold and are not shown to follow from the results.

comments.issue: The study uses one model type, one system and one fitting method but suggests all ecosystem models are questionable.
comments.request: Be more nuanced about the contributions and implications.
comments.quote: The authors have fit one type of ecosystem model to a specific type of system, using a single method for model fitting, for near-term forecasting

comments.issue: The null model choice matters; mechanistic models should not be expected to beat simple constant, linear or exponential nulls for near-term forecasts.
comments.request: Reconsider the null-model benchmark used to judge model usefulness.
comments.quote: I would not expect a mechanistic model fit to data to be better than one of these null models, in general.

comments.issue: The iterative near-term forecasting literature is not cited.
comments.request: Engage with the iterative near-term forecasting literature.
comments.quote: It seems like it would be worth engaging with the iterative near-term forecasting literature in ecology, I did not find any of this literature cited in the reference list.

comments.issue: Only one type of ecosystem model was tested, so claims about mechanistic ecosystem models in general are not defensible.
comments.request: Restrict the conclusions to the model type tested.
comments.quote: I’m not sure that only using one type and then suggesting that mechanistic ecosystem models – in general – shouldn’t be used is defensible

comments.issue: Numerical optimisation for fitting is outdated and its effect on the conclusions is unclear.
comments.request: Test how the fitting procedure affects the conclusions, e.g. with Bayesian inference.
comments.quote: This isn’t the most up-to-date approach, which the authors allude to 294 and 295 (EG using Bayesian inference). It raises the question of how much the fitting procedure affects the conclusions.

comments.issue: The assessment ignores that interaction strength and sign may depend on relative abundances in these systems.
comments.request: Assess realistic expected performance and abundance-dependent interactions.
comments.quote: in some microcosm systems we might expect the interaction strength (and even sign) to be a function of relative abundances

comments.issue: State-space approaches are not compared with the same datasets to quantify relative performance.
comments.request: Compare state-space or autocorrelation approaches on the same datasets.
comments.quote: These have been around in ecological forecasting for some time, and there are established methodology for them. They could be compared to the same datasets to quantify relative performance.

title: Calibrated Ecosystem Models Cannot Predict the Consequences of Conservation Management Decisions

study.system: mountain lions (Puma concolor) in California; GPS telemetry

editor_summary: Editor: well-written, interesting paper with impressive data; one reviewer highly positive, the other ambivalent; editor leans positive; numerous suggestions for clarifications should be considered.

reviews.assessment: One of the most compelling papers reviewed; comments are limited to validation and interpretation clarifications.

comments.issue: Whether the mortality risk layer was validated is not reported, despite being central to all analyses.
comments.request: Report validation of the mortality risk layer.
comments.quote: I was left wanting more information about if/how this layer was validated, given that it is so central to all of the analyses.

comments.issue: Larger roads and medium/large development were excluded from the risk model but may shape risk patterns.
comments.request: Run sensitivity analyses or integrate these covariates rather than excluding them.
comments.quote: I’d like to see some sensitivity analysis that proves otherwise or some way to integrate them into the models (for example, combining all roads into one covariate, and all development into one covariate) rather than exclude them entirely.

comments.issue: It should be shown that mountain lions respond to perceived risk rather than to a confounding factor shaping both habitat use and mortality.
comments.request: Discuss the contents of the risk layer and address the confounding concern.
comments.quote: I was wanting to be extra-sure that the mountain lions were responding to perceived risk, rather than some confounding factor that shaped both mountain lion habitat use and mortality.

comments.issue: The percentage of deaths from depredation permits and the lethal removal methods are not reported; other mortality causes are not discussed.
comments.request: Report these mortality details and discuss other anthropogenic causes.
comments.quote: I was interested to know slightly more on the estimated percentage of animals that die from this cause, and what the method(s) of lethal removal is/are

comments.issue: How habitat selection processes shape actual mortality risk is not explored; individual variability in avoidance could affect being killed.
comments.request: Explore the link to mortality if sample size allows, or set it up as a future direction.
comments.quote: Could the sample size allow for an exploration of how individual variability in risk avoidance then affects likelihood of being killed? The study design may not permit it, but at minimum, it could be set up as an interesting future direction.

comments.issue: The common name of the study species is missing from the abstract.
comments.request: Add the common name to the abstract.
comments.quote: Lines 57-58: Tell us the common name of the species in the abstract!

comments.issue: The comparison for lower survival rates at lines 124-125 is unspecified.
comments.request: State what survival rates are compared with.
comments.quote: Lines 124-125: Lower survival rates relative to what?

comments.issue: Oceans and water bodies may not have been excluded from available habitat, potentially biasing second-order selection.
comments.request: Exclude or justify water bodies as available habitat.
comments.quote: Were oceans or other water bodies excluded from “available” habitat for the second-order resource selection? Seems like their inclusion could bias results as they aren’t truly available (much like habitat on the other side of a freeway, which was excluded).

comments.issue: Conclusions about stronger risk avoidance than resource selection may be overconfident given imperfect proxies.
comments.request: Temper these conclusions with more uncertainty.
comments.quote: The conclusions about how mountain lions avoided depredation risk more strongly than they selected resources may need to be couched in more uncertainty. Both mortality risk and resource availability are measured imperfectly as proxies,

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not highlight the quadrant representing the study prediction.
comments.request: Add a box around the top-left quadrant.
comments.quote: Figure 1: Consider adding a box or something around the top left quadrant to indicate that this is the prediction in this study?

comments.issue: The color gradient in Figure 1 is not explained and color-blind friendliness is unconfirmed.
comments.request: Explain the gradient in the caption and confirm accessibility.
comments.quote: Figure 1: What does the gradient of color represent? Indicate in caption, and confirm color-blind friendly.

comments.issue: The California inset and north arrow in Figure 2 distract from an already complex figure.
comments.request: Remove the inset and north arrow.
comments.quote: Figure 2: Not sure an inset of California is necessary, and it distracts from what is already a complex figure. North arrow also not necessary.

comments.issue: Figure 3 points are small and confidence interval bars are wide.
comments.request: Enlarge points and narrow or remove CI bars.
comments.quote: Figure 3: Minor aesthetic point, but consider making the points larger, and the width of the confidence interval bars narrower (or remove them entirely as in Figure 4).

comments.issue: Figure 4 axis labels are not specific enough.
comments.request: Use more specific axis labels.
comments.quote: Figure 4: Consider making the x and y axis labels more specific, given the complexity of the analyses.

comments.issue: Figure 5 color-blind/greyscale friendliness is unconfirmed.
comments.request: Confirm Figure 5 is accessible in greyscale.
comments.quote: Figure 5: Confirm color-blind/greyscale friendly.

comments.issue: The expectation of sex differences in resource selection is not justified.
comments.request: Explain why sex differences are expected.
comments.quote: Supplementary material: Briefly explain why there is reason to believe that there are sex differences in resource selection.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and solid, but adaptation and fitness claims are invoked without proximate tests, and several methods need clarification.
strengths: careful two-step statistics accounting for coefficient variance

comments.issue: Adaptation is invoked without proximate tests of the behavioural trade-off, and the hypothesis framing distracts from the novelty.
comments.request: Be careful with adaptation claims and clarify what makes this functional response novel.
comments.quote: I think that the authors should be careful with invoking adaptation without having any proximate tests of whether their behavioral trade-off in selection for two representative habitat types.

comments.issue: The mechanistic link between Holling's functional response and functional responses in habitat selection is not articulated.
comments.request: Articulate the process or mechanism linking the two concepts.
comments.quote: I think that being able to articulate – even in narrative form – how the functional response to habitat selection might be a proxy for “attack”, handling, etc..

comments.issue: The predictive capacity of the risk and reward layers is not evaluated with out-of-sample validation.
comments.request: Add k-fold cross validation or another hold-out analysis.
comments.quote: I checked the appendix and it clearly articulated the methods, but I didn’t see anything like k-fold cross validation or other out-of-sample/hold out analysis to evaluate how effective these layer are.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether available steps were sampled from fitted HMM distributions or raw empirical steps, and why an SSF was chosen over an iSSA.
comments.request: Clarify the availability sampling and justify the SSF choice.
comments.quote: What I can’t tell is if that sample was from the fitted distributions of the data in the HMM or if the raw empirical steps and turn angles were used for the available steps. There’s a gap there for me.

comments.issue: Using only RSF/SSF coefficients rather than RSSs may lose precision and require stats-on-stats.
comments.request: Consider RSS-based approaches such as those suggested by Avgar et al. 2017.
comments.quote: But one thing I think we’ve seen is that just using RSF (or SSF) coefficients and not RSSs, which illustrate changes in selection across availabilities for an individual, sometimes results in information that is not as precise as it could be.

comments.issue: The text should illustrate precisely how understanding is limited; Morris and Rosenzweig address density-dependent habitat selection, not resource selection.
comments.request: Clarify the limits and avoid conflating classical theory with resource selection.
comments.quote: It isn’t that I disagree. I agree. But I think it would be more useful to precisely illustrate how the ‘understanding’ is limited.

comments.issue: The Rosenzweig citation is less apt at lines 87-88, and 'habitat suitability' introduces an unnecessary concept.
comments.request: Reconsider these citations and concepts.
comments.quote: I think the first two citations work really well here, but less so the Rosenzwieg citation. I also wonder if the authors need to introduce ‘habitat suitability’, another concept, when the paper really only talks about resource selection?

comments.issue: Fitness remains an assumed outcome, so the line at 90-91 may set unrealistic expectations.
comments.request: Acknowledge that fitness benefits are assumed.
comments.quote: I totally agree. But fitness remains an assumed outcome in this paper, so maybe this line sets up unrealistic expectations.

comments.issue: The objectives statement does not say fitness-limiting factors are assumed and unnecessarily claims a unifying framework.
comments.request: Frame the study as a solid empirical example rather than a unifying framework.
comments.quote: It isn’t clear in this objectives statement that fitness-limiting factors are assumed or purported.

comments.issue: The phrase 'depredation risk' including mortality risk at line 186 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the terminology.
comments.quote: Line 186: Can one have ‘depredation risk’ that does include the risk of mortality?

comments.issue: 'Individual level functional response' at line 306 conflicts with prior usage in the literature.
comments.request: Avoid or clarify this terminology.
comments.quote: But introducing or perpetuating an “individual level functional response” might be a bit confusing, particularly when tying to previous literature where that language isn’t used to describe how selection changes across an availability gradient.

comments.issue: The hypothesis at line 312 may be a stretch of the Rettie and Messier citation.
comments.request: Soften the attribution to Rettie and Messier.
comments.quote: Here is an example, despite the use of ‘should’, that posits the hypothesis that Rettie and Messier articulate, but is maybe a stretch of that citation.

comments.issue: The caveat about human attitudes at line 398 is unnecessary in the main text.
comments.request: Move the caveat to an appendix.
comments.quote: as reader I didn’t need this caveat to be convinced that the science in this article was valid. Perhaps others would, but maybe this sentiment is OK to be in an appendix.

comments.issue: The claim at line 428 that Rettie and Messier's hypothesis was effectively tested overstates a putative fitness benefit.
comments.request: Temper the claim about testing the hypothesis.
comments.quote: I’m not sure this is true. Though I think every paper that articulates a risk-reward trade-off within or across scales is really cool. I don’t think the authors can associate their outcome with anything other than a putative fitness benefit.

comments.issue: The use of 'true' or 'truth' at line 145 is inappropriate for a likelihood-based result.
comments.request: Rephrase in terms of relative likelihood.
comments.quote: Line 145: Is there ‘true’ or ‘truth’ in science? I think the analysis tells us that one outcome is more likely than another, not that one is true and another false.

comments.issue: The distinction between predation and depredation is unclear throughout.
comments.request: Use the terms consistently and define them if needed.
comments.quote: Throughout: I don’t really know the difference between predation and depredation. This could totally be a ‘me’ thing.

comments.issue: The study area map may not add value in the main text.
comments.request: Move the map to the appendix unless it adds data.
comments.quote: I don’t recall seeing study area maps Ecology Letters papers, recently. I’m sure I could be wrong. But unless there are value added data in the map, maybe it should be in the appendix.

title: A Functional Response in Resource Selection Links Multiscale Responses of a Large Carnivore to Human Mortality Risk

study.system: urban parks; pollinators, 3-year natural experiment and occupancy modelling

editor_summary: Reviewers agree on novelty but have reservations; asks to address general messages, especially restoration contexts, and clarify shortcomings; potential for a great contribution.

reviews.assessment: Strong praise for the scale and design, with many requests for clarification and figure improvements and some doubts about d' and ecological traps.
strengths: great and much needed scale and design
results will be welcome and widely cited
inclusion of a pollen limitation experiment

comments.issue: Baseline pre-enhancement data are missing, limiting inference about change.
comments.request: Include pre-enhancement baseline data if available.
comments.quote: If I could wish for something else in the study design, it would be baseline data in all the parks pre-enhancement.

comments.issue: The enhancements may create novel habitat rather than restore; 'restoration' is not defined or justified.
comments.request: Define restoration, state what is restored, or use another term.
comments.quote: I had some difficulty thinking of the herbaceous enhancements as ‘restoration.’ It wasn’t clear to me that these enhancements were ‘restoring’ something, vs. creating a novel habitat.

comments.issue: Introduction does not set up the metacommunity components or predictions for colonization and persistence.
comments.request: Spell out predictions for colonization and persistence.
comments.quote: The final paragraph of the introduction provides a prediction only for year-one differences between control sites and enhanced sites, but not for colonization or persistence.

comments.issue: Enhanced sites also had the most woody floral resources, so enhancement and woody plant effects may be confounded.
comments.request: Address the confounding between enhancements and pre-existing woody plants.
comments.quote: To what extent are herbaceous enhancements and pre-existing woody plants confounded?

comments.issue: d' is not convincing as the sole indicator of specialization.
comments.request: Justify d' as a specialization measure or use additional evidence.
comments.quote: I didn’t feel completely convinced by d’ as the sole indicator of specialization

comments.issue: Context for the Clarkia pollination results is insufficient.
comments.request: Provide more context for the Clarkia pollination results.
comments.quote: The manuscript could use a little more context for the Clarkia pollination results.

comments.issue: Discussion asserts what results demonstrate without explaining how.
comments.request: Explain how the results support each statement.
comments.quote: the discussion had a tendency to jump to conclusions in places, making statements about what the results demonstrate without explaining HOW they demonstrate that thing

comments.issue: Spatial relationship between herbaceous and woody plant surveys is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify where woody plants were sampled relative to quadrats.
comments.quote: I’m not clear on the spatial relationship between the herbaceous and woody plant surveys.

comments.issue: Survey sequence and whether it was randomized are not reported.
comments.request: State the order and randomization of surveys.
comments.quote: in what order were the 18 sites surveyed? It would be helpful to state whether the survey sequence was randomized, paired, always the same, etc.

comments.issue: Species concepts used for identification are not specified.
comments.request: State species concepts and cite taxonomic references.
comments.quote: need more information about which species concepts were used; please cite taxonomic references

comments.issue: Pooling dates may make spring insects look more specialized, potentially driving the specialist-woody interaction.
comments.request: Test whether phenology drives the apparent specialist interaction.
comments.quote: Could this potential phenological artefact of d’ drive the apparent interaction between specialists and woody floral resources?

comments.issue: d' is not validated against established pollen-specialization classifications.
comments.request: Compare d' with external pollen-specialization classifications.
comments.quote: I would be very interested to see a comparison between d’ and a more old-school classification of pollen specialization that draws on observations and natural history from outside this study

comments.issue: Per-species d' values are not reported, so readers cannot assess them.
comments.request: Provide per-species d' values in a supplemental table or figure.
comments.quote: At a minimum it would be helpful to provide each species’ d’ value in a supplemental table/figure so readers can get a sense of whether and how d’ matches up to more broadly established life history traits

comments.issue: Common-garden observations cannot support the in-situ pollen limitation result.
comments.request: Use or remove the common-garden observation data.
comments.quote: I was disappointed that the pollinator observations (Table S6) did not occur in situ.

comments.issue: Taxonomic errors in Table S6: Apidae is a family, not an order, and excludes Halictus.
comments.request: Correct the taxonomy in Table S6.
comments.quote: If the table is kept, please correct taxonomic errors: I’m sure the authors know this, but ‘Apidae’ is a family, not an order, and the family Apidae does not contain the genus Halictus.

comments.issue: Readers are not told that Clarkia is pollinated by the focal bee and syrphid taxa.
comments.request: Add a statement of Clarkia's pollinators to the methods.
comments.quote: I did want a statement of who pollinates Clarkia, so perhaps these common-garden observations, along with prior literature, could provide such a general statement for the methods section.

comments.issue: Species names in Fig. S4 are illegible.
comments.request: Provide a reader-friendly table of species names with numbers.
comments.quote: The species names in Fig. S4 are not legible (they very small, and when you zoom in they are very pixelated).

comments.issue: The 50% BCI is used but not interpreted here.
comments.request: Interpret the 50% BCI where it is used.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to include the interpretation of the 50% BCI here, too, since that is also used/ presented in some of the results.

comments.issue: Fig. S12 panels c and d lack supporting analyses and the caption refers confusingly to Fig. S7.
comments.request: Add analyses for panels c and d or drop them.
comments.quote: The differences in Fig S12 look pretty modest and are difficult to interpret until you get to Fig S13, which provides statistical backing for panel a (marginal effect) and panel b (significant effect)

comments.issue: Summary statement overstates the enhancement effect on floral abundance.
comments.request: Soften the statement to reflect the weak effect.
comments.quote: it seems like the summary statement in line 301 should be softened or qualified to reflect the numerical results that enhancements were weakly associated with greater floral abundance

comments.issue: Fig. S17 caption and panel labels disagree about which panel shows enhancements.
comments.request: Fix the caption or the labels.
comments.quote: The caption says the top panel shows the enhancements, but the labels within the figure say that the top panel shows the controls.

comments.issue: Fig. S18 is hard to read and hides the species list.
comments.request: Reorient or tabulate Fig. S18 and color-code bees versus syrphids.
comments.quote: The figure is really hard to read, and if someone wants to know which species were collected in this study, this figure is the main place to get it

comments.issue: Continuous prediction lines are shown for categorical axes in Fig. 3.
comments.request: Show point estimates with CIs for categorical panels.
comments.quote: I don’t understand why the panels with a categorical X-axis (enhancement category) show a continuous line (panels a, b, e, f, i, j)

comments.issue: 'Woody plants' at line 312 should be specified as woody plant floral abundance.
comments.request: State the metric explicitly.
comments.quote: I believe this is referring to woody plant floral abundance (as opposed to canopy cover or some other metric of woody plant abundance)

comments.issue: 'Positive interaction' is unclear.
comments.request: Reword to state the effect of woody floral abundance was stronger for specialists.
comments.quote: wording isn’t very intuitive, hard to say what a ‘positive interaction’ between specialization and woody plants actually means

comments.issue: Raw observed richness is not compared with model-derived estimates.
comments.request: Show observed richness alongside model outputs and compare conclusions.
comments.quote: It would be nice to see the average observed richness per site type per year alongside the model outputs.

comments.issue: The nature and magnitude of the agricultural-urban contrast is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the agricultural-urban difference and time scale.
comments.quote: Please spell out the contrast being made between agricultural and urban results: Is it that colonization occurred at all? That colonization was slow vs rapid?

comments.issue: Claim that enhancements must be carefully planned does not follow from the results.
comments.request: Revise the planning claim to match the results.
comments.quote: There wasn’t any interaction between enhancement and pre-existing woody floral abundance, so it seems like even if planners were not careful and did not consider the pre-existing vegetation, they would get the documented benefits of the enhancement.

comments.issue: The community-level data cannot demonstrate species-specific ecological traps.
comments.request: Skip the ecological trap concept.
comments.quote: I’m not sure the results presented are really conclusive about ecological traps, which are a behavioral phenomenon affecting individual animals

comments.issue: The bonanza-seeking generalist explanation conflicts with the weak generalist colonization effect.
comments.request: Reconcile the interpretation with the interaction results.
comments.quote: If mobile bonanza-seeking generalists were driving the colonization, then we should also see a big effect of woody veg on their colonization, but this is not what we see in Fig 3h

comments.issue: A single species cannot support a broad claim about desired plants, and Clarkia was pollination-constrained.
comments.request: Narrow the claim and acknowledge Clarkia's pollination limitation.
comments.quote: This is a broad statement about ‘desired plants’ based on results from a single species!

comments.issue: The last sentence implies woody plants were part of the enhancement.
comments.request: Reword to clarify woody plants were pre-existing.
comments.quote: the last sentence in this paragraph makes it sound like the woody plants were included as part of the habitat enhancement, but they were not

comments.issue: N line-level copy edits (missing word line 97, typo line 386, extra comma line 832).
comments.quote: line 97 – missing word (are more likely TO colonize)

comments.issue: The spatial scale of landscape metrics is not stated in the text.
comments.request: State that landscape metrics are within 500 m of site centroids.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to mention here that the percentages of impervious surface and tree cover are within 500m of the site centroid so readers know the scale at which the landscape is characterized

comments.issue: Text contradicts itself about whether honey bees were captured.
comments.request: Make lines 167 and 174 consistent.
comments.quote: line 167 says only wild bees + hover flies were captured; line 174 mentions that honey bees were also captured.

comments.issue: The comparison at line 321 is unclear.
comments.request: State explicitly that specialists had lower colonization than generalists.
comments.quote: clarify what comparison is being made: specialists had lower rates of colonization THAN GENERALIST SPECIES.

comments.issue: The sentence does not say it concerns pollinator species richness.
comments.request: Clarify the subject of the sentence.
comments.quote: clarify that this sentence is about POLLINATOR species richness

comments.issue: The comparison baseline for 'effective strategy' is unclear.
comments.request: State what the strategy is being compared to.
comments.quote: Please clarify - an effective strategy compared to what? Compared to land sparing/ wildland conservation? Or compared to un-enhanced urban landscapes?

reviews.assessment: Praise for the well-formulated occupancy model, but major concerns that the 3-year duration does not justify 'long-term' claims and that the title overstates persistence.
strengths: well-formulated and appropriate dynamic occupancy model
novelty of testing effects via species specialization

comments.issue: The 3-year duration is not justified as long-term for this taxon.
comments.request: Justify treating 3 years as long-term.
comments.quote: At this point, and as a major issue, it would be important to explain and justify why and if, for this biological group, 3 years can be considered sufficient to be regarded as a long-term study.

comments.issue: Species could be grouped post hoc by specialization instead of testing a priori interactions.
comments.request: Consider the alternative model grouping species post hoc.
comments.quote: This way, they could test these hypotheses posteriori from the grouping of species and not a priori.

comments.issue: Title and conclusions imply restoration drives persistence, but persistence was high regardless.
comments.request: Clarify this in the conclusions and correct the title.
comments.quote: According to the title, and main conclusions, it might seem that the high persistence is due to restoration, which can be misleading.

comments.issue: The recommended study duration from the cited review is not stated.
comments.request: Report the recommended number of years.
comments.quote: Please clarify how many years of study are recommended according to this review.

comments.issue: Site climate and survey season are not described.
comments.request: Describe the climate and survey season.
comments.quote: Please clarify a bit more about the study site. What is the climate like? During which climatic season of the Northern Hemisphere do the surveys occur?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the survey timing meets the occupancy closure assumption.
comments.request: Show that the closure assumption is met.
comments.quote: Please clarify if the time elapsed between the 6 surveys l taking place between May and August (indicated in line 152-153) allows for meeting the closure assumption

comments.issue: Only BCI intervals are reported; mean posteriors of covariate effects are missing.
comments.request: Add a table or figure of mean effects with BCIs.
comments.quote: include parameter mean posteriors of the covariate effects, not only BCI intervals, despite presenting the figures

comments.issue: Table S7 describes gamma-6 and phi-6 as detection parameters, but they are colonization and persistence parameters.
comments.request: Correct the Table S7 description.
comments.quote: but as I understand this are colonization and persistence parameters, not detection ones

comments.issue: N line-level copy edits (line 97 'to colonize', line 120 'absence').
comments.quote: Line 97: please correct “to colonize”.

title: Habitat Restorations in an Urban Landscape Rapidly Assemble Diverse Pollinator Communities That Persist

study.system: Southeast Asian insects; occurrence records, publication and social media review

reviews.assessment: Important topic and good data collation, but research questions and methods are mismatched and the social media analysis is weak.
strengths: important topic very worthy of publication
good effort collating multiple data sources
easy to read with visually appealing figures

comments.issue: Research questions and methods are mismatched; methodological limitations need analyses, reframing or acknowledgement.
comments.request: Address or acknowledge the methodological limitations.
comments.quote: My main concern is there are some mismatches between the research questions and the methods described. There are a few limitations in the methodology that the authors should address, either through additional analyses or by reframing the goals of the search.

comments.issue: "Insect records" is imprecise.
comments.request: Use "online insect biodiversity records".
comments.quote: ‘insect records’ – perhaps it’s more accurate to use ‘online insect biodiversity records’

comments.issue: "Public perceptions" mislabels what is actually social media content.
comments.request: Rename the measure, e.g. social media content.
comments.quote: simply looking at post keywords/content doesn’t necessarily represent public perceptions

comments.issue: "Insect research" is too broad for what the methodology can support.
comments.request: Narrow the scope or reframe the question.
comments.quote: ‘insect research’ – this is really such a broad and ambiguous term. Insect research could encompass ecology, conservation, pest science, ag science, entomology, biomedical, disease biology etc.

comments.issue: The search string is too limited and misses taxonomic terms.
comments.request: Broaden the search string with taxa and ecology terms.
comments.quote: the search string is quite limited, and doesn’t meet the goals of a comprehensive synthesis of published research. It also doesn’t address the ‘taxonomic’ part of the first research question.

comments.issue: It is unclear what study density per area and GDP comparisons reveal about research effort.
comments.request: Explain what these metrics tell us.
comments.quote: not clear how informative these are, given that some studies will be published by authors outside the country?

comments.issue: "Social media" is used generically although only Twitter is analysed.
comments.request: Refer to the specific platform.
comments.quote: The generic use of the term ‘social media’ throughout the paper, although only one platform is analysed.

comments.issue: A single hashtag severely limits the Twitter search and introduces biases.
comments.request: Improve the Twitter search strategy.
comments.quote: a single hashtag severely limits the search parameters – why not include other relevant terms and hashtags, e.g. ‘insect ecology’, ‘insect conservation’, nature etc.

comments.issue: Figure 3E caption says the wrong label.
comments.request: Change to "research theme and country".
comments.quote: caption for part (E) should read ‘research theme and country’

reviews.assessment: Important topic meeting journal standards, but the title/abstract promise solutions not delivered and references and regional representation need work.
strengths: important research on SE Asian insect data gaps

comments.issue: Title and abstract claim solutions are provided, but the results contain none.
comments.request: Align the title and abstract with the delivered content.
comments.quote: The authors highlight in both the title and abstract that they have provided solutions in the manuscript, but there is no such thing in the results.

comments.issue: The methods section is overly long at 140 lines.
comments.request: Move detailed methods to the supplement.
comments.quote: The method section is quite extensive, spanning 140 lines. It might be beneficial to consider moving some of the detailed parts to the supplementary section.

comments.issue: Many references are incorrect or missing for key statements.
comments.request: Check and correct the references.
comments.quote: I noticed that many references have been used improperly. For instance, in P5, from lines 6-17, most references are incorrect.

comments.issue: The discussion omits other social media platforms as biodiversity data sources.
comments.request: Discuss social media data integration.
comments.quote: I think it’s important to highlight in the discussion that there are other social media platforms that might have more observation data than GBIF, which could eventually improve conservation assessments.

comments.issue: Solutions proposed mostly by Singapore-based authors may not transfer to other countries.
comments.request: Highlight this regional limitation.
comments.quote: For example, the solution that would be applicable to Singapore might not work in Myanmar. The authors should also highlight this limitation.

comments.issue: The first sentence of the abstract is unnecessary.
comments.request: Remove the first abstract sentence.
comments.quote: I don’t think the first sentence of the abstract is needed.

comments.issue: Hashtag formatting error on P3 line 8.
comments.request: Correct to '#conservation'.
comments.quote: P3 Line 8: Should be ‘#conservation’ Line 67: Is it an appropriate way to cite the GBIF datasets?

comments.issue: The GBIF datasets may not be cited appropriately.
comments.request: Check the GBIF data citations.
comments.quote: Line 67: Is it an appropriate way to cite the GBIF datasets?

comments.issue: Relevant categories outside the two chosen fields are ignored.
comments.request: Justify the choice of categories.
comments.quote: There are several relevant categories outside these two fields. I am unsure why the authors chose these two!

comments.issue: Lines 263-265 oversell the findings.
comments.request: Delete or temper this information.
comments.quote: The authors could delete this information; too much overselling!

title: Identifying the Knowledge and Capacity Gaps in Southeast Asian Insect Conservation

study.system: Boechera stricta; 4-yr drought and herbivory field experiment

editor_summary: Editor: reviews generally positive; more detail needed; rewrite requested and implications beyond the specific study system should be added.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the experiment's scale; results complex but well navigated; asks for more explicit methods, figure clarity, and discussion of what the vital-rate analyses add.
strengths: acknowledges caveats of the demographic analysis

comments.issue: Figure 1 is difficult to interpret, particularly the dashed lines indicating herbivory levels.
comments.request: Revise Figure 1 to aid interpretation.
comments.quote: I found Figure 1 difficult to interpret, particularly the dashed lines indicating levels of herbivory.

comments.issue: Table S6 should be moved to the main text to support interpretation of driver impacts on vital rates.
comments.request: Move Table S6 to the main text.
comments.quote: to support the interpretation of driver impacts on different vital rates, it would be useful to have Table S6 in the main text.

comments.issue: How and why data were combined across years and cohorts is only justified briefly in the appendix.
comments.request: Explain data combination more explicitly in the main-text methods.
comments.quote: I would encourage authors to be more explicit in the main text (e.g. methods) as to how and why data were combined across years and cohorts

comments.issue: Differences from the related Carley et al. (2021) study, including its fitness estimation, are not explained.
comments.request: Expand lines 148-151 to contrast the studies.
comments.quote: could you elaborate on the difference between that study and this one (e.g. expand lines 148-151)?

comments.issue: What the vital-rate analyses add beyond complex interaction effects is unclear.
comments.request: Explore in the discussion what was learnt from the vital-rate analyses.
comments.quote: it was not clear to me what we learnt from studying effects of drivers on individual vital rates beyond complex interaction effects.

comments.issue: How volumetric water content was measured is not described in the main text.
comments.request: Add the measurement method to the main text.
comments.quote: Volumetric water content – how was this measured – with sensors? I think this should be added to main text.

comments.issue: Evidence for the predicted regional aridity increase under climate change scenarios is not given.
comments.request: Provide evidence or citations for the aridity prediction.
comments.quote: Is there evidence for the predicted increase in aridity in the region under relevant climate change scenarios?

comments.issue: Figure 3 legend describes the conditions for higher BB lifetime fitness incorrectly.
comments.request: Correct the legend to 'high moisture, low herbivory'.
comments.quote: The conditions under which the BB genotype has higher lifetime fitness are described incorrectly – I think they should be “high moisture, low herbivory”

reviews.assessment: Novel demographic insights; well-written with clear figures; asks to connect questions to analyses, unpack vital-rate mediation, and caveat extrapolations.

comments.issue: The three introduction questions cannot be mapped onto specific analyses and figures; directional hypotheses are missing.
comments.request: Streamline questions with analyses and state directional hypotheses.
comments.quote: It was hard for me to map the 3 questions posed in the introduction onto specific analyses and figures in the Results.

comments.issue: It is unclear which vital rates were most affected and how their effects on lambda are mediated.
comments.request: Unpack mediation of driver effects on lambda via vital rates.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to further unpack how the effects of environmental drivers on lambda are mediated through their effects on individual vital rates.

comments.issue: Limitations of projecting lambda beyond observed environments are not discussed.
comments.request: Add caveats and mark observed bounds in Figs. 2-4.
comments.quote: What are the limitations or caveats of projecting lambda beyond observed environments (in other words, 100% herbivory or the high end of soil moisture)?

comments.issue: Individual fitness is not explicitly linked to lambda before lambda is called 'total fitness'.
comments.request: Link individual fitness to population growth rate with a citation.
comments.quote: it would be nice to explicitly link individual fitness to population growth rate (lambda) before starting to refer to lambda as “total fitness”

comments.issue: Context on the genotypes and expected responses to drivers comes too late (only in the Discussion).
comments.request: Add this context to the last paragraph of the Introduction.
comments.quote: I think a bit more context early on about these genotypes and how the authors expect them to differ in their responses to environmental drivers

comments.issue: Replication per genotype per treatment is only given as a table in the supplement.
comments.request: Report range and mean replicates in this section.
comments.quote: can the authors provide a range and mean number of replicates per genotype per treatment in this section?

comments.issue: Why year was not included as a random effect is not understood.
comments.request: Explain the treatment of year in the models.
comments.quote: I don’t fully understand why year wasn’t included as a random effect in these models.

comments.issue: Phrasing at L273 suggests all genotypes went into one model, but they were modelled separately.
comments.request: Clarify the modelling per genotype.
comments.quote: this phrasing initially led me to believe that vital rate data from all genotypes went into a single model, but genotypes were modeled separately, correct?

comments.issue: No clear hypotheses are outlined in the introduction.
comments.request: State the hypotheses in the introduction.
comments.quote: related to my major comment above, there weren’t clear hypotheses outlined in the introduction

comments.issue: Analyses are not explicitly mapped onto the study objectives and hypotheses.
comments.request: Map analyses to the objectives and hypotheses.
comments.quote: here is where more explicitly mapping these analyses onto the study objectives and hypotheses outlined in the introduction would be helpful.

comments.issue: Subheadings do not match the objectives stated in the introduction.
comments.request: Use subheadings matching the introduction objectives.
comments.quote: L340: similar point as above; use subheadings that match objectives in introduction.

comments.issue: The expectation at L355-358 should be introduced earlier.
comments.request: Include this expectation in the Introduction.
comments.quote: L355-358: it would be valuable to include this expectation in the Introduction

comments.issue: Figure 1 panel A lacks a y-axis label and dashed line types are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Add the y-axis label and differentiate the lines.
comments.quote: y-axis label is missing in panel A. Overall it’s hard to distinguish the different types of dashed lines.

title: Increasing Aridity May Threaten the Maintenance of a Plant Defence Polymorphism

study.system: eastern African large herbivores; stable isotopes from LGP fossil tooth enamel

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers support the novelty but find methods needing extensive strengthening: mismatched modern and ancient datasets and indices, limited modern ecology review, insufficient strontium, chronology and diagenesis information; recommends reject with option to resubmit.

reviews.assessment: Especially impressed; striking, generally important conclusions, with only a wish for more conservation implications.
strengths: succinct problem, system and methods presentation
on the vanguard of this type of study

comments.issue: The manuscript does not go far enough in drawing implications for modern conservation biology.
comments.request: Expand the implications for conservation.
comments.quote: my only complaint about this MS is that it does not go far enough in pointing at the implications of the results for modern conservation biology

reviews.assessment: Nice, convincing study with exciting results, but the abstract overstates data novelty and two statistical concerns need addressing.
strengths: results crucial for understanding selective forces
reads very well and is convincing

comments.issue: Abstract is ambiguous, almost suggesting strontium data are original when only carbon and oxygen are new.
comments.request: Clarify which data are original in the abstract.
comments.quote: The abstract is a bit ambiguous, almost suggesting that Strotium data would also be original.

comments.issue: The oxygen isotope results are unclear; the firm conclusion rests on carbon isotopes and prior migration classification.
comments.request: Be more explicit about what the oxygen results can support.

comments.issue: Subsampling protocol is ambiguous (8 versus 24 units), with implications for Kruskal-Wallis power.

comments.issue: GAM is not appropriate for a binomial migration response.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, potentially novel concept, but many clarifications are needed, especially chronology and diagenesis support.
strengths: new framework for comparing past and modern communities

comments.issue: LGP is capitalized and undefined; an alternative time framework could be used.
comments.request: Define the period and consider a framework not limited to absolute dates.

comments.issue: The behaviorally non-analog concept is not developed enough.

comments.issue: Mineralization differences between equids and bovids systematically damp serial amplitude.

comments.quote: This variability between major groups means that serial amplitude will be systematically damped in Equids, less so in bovids

comments.issue: Supplemental datasets were not included in the review package.
comments.quote: The supplemental datasets (including summarized and raw data) were not included in the review package.

comments.issue: Five line-level wording corrections at Lines 91, 92, 93, 144 and 251.
comments.quote: Line 93. Suggest replacing “grass intake” with “grazing”

comments.issue: Chronology and context of the assemblages are not conveyed; wide age ranges raise time-averaging questions.
comments.request: Synthesize site context and chronology in the narrative or a figure.
comments.quote: some more detail about the context of each assemblage (taphonomy, depositional setting, stratigraphic units, etc.) could be briefly synthesized in the narrative or a figure

comments.issue: It is unclear if second and third molars are upper, lower or both.
comments.request: Specify which molars were sampled.
comments.quote: Multiple 2nd and 3rd molars. Upper? Lower? Both?

comments.issue: Basis of the 93% and 94% figures is unclear (species versus specimens).
comments.request: Clarify the basis and provide raw data references.
comments.quote: Does 93% and 94% refer to % of taxonomic list (i.e., % of species) or to raw number of identified specimens?

comments.issue: Material at Lines 138-166 belongs in methods, not results and analysis.
comments.request: Move this material to the methods.
comments.quote: These things are usually discussed in methods, not analysis.

comments.issue: The ~1mm sampling depth rationale is unclear.
comments.request: Explain whether it reflects enamel thickness or is arbitrary.
comments.quote: Is this an arbitrary estimate? Or does it reflect the thickness of enamel in most species.

comments.issue: Pretreatment success at one depositional environment does not demonstrate absence of diagenetic overprint at all sites.
comments.request: Address the differing diagenetic pathways across sites.
comments.quote: just because the different pretreatments provide the same results from ONE depositional environment doesn’t mean that the same diagenetic pathways are relevant at the OTHER sites

comments.issue: Instrumental errors are not reported.
comments.request: Provide batch and/or long-term instrumental errors.
comments.quote: either for the batch, long term, or both

comments.issue: Cerling et al. cutoffs are opaque and require looking up another paper.
comments.request: Explain or convert d13C to diet or %C4 values.
comments.quote: Is there a reason why d13C values aren’t just converted to d13Cdiet or %C4, then analyzed?

comments.issue: What synthesized means and how records were judged is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the synthesis procedure.
comments.quote: What do you mean by “synthesized”? Is this just going through record by record and making a judgement call based on a visual analysis?

comments.issue: Serial range is affected by sampling resolution and mineralization, confounding amplitude conclusions.
comments.request: Account for or remove these other sources of variation.
comments.quote: Is there a way to account for and/or remove these other sources of variation?

comments.issue: Counts at Lines 227-235 do not add up; a summary table is needed.
comments.request: Check the numbers and add a summary table.
comments.quote: Check numbers (e.g., 59/79, 10 individuals, one individual, 1 browser, 11 mixed feeders). They don’t seem to add up.

comments.issue: Amplitudes of equids and bovids are not directly compared.
comments.request: Compare equid and bovid amplitudes for taxon-specific differences.
comments.quote: This might be a good place to also directly compare the amplitude of equids and bovids to see if there are taxon-specific differences.

comments.issue: Samples per individual does not measure sampling resolution; a linear unit is needed.
comments.request: Standardize resolution per linear unit, e.g. samples per cm.
comments.quote: Number of samples per individual is not a good measure of sampling resolution/effort. This should be standardized by a linear unit, e.g., 3 samples per cm.

comments.issue: Whether hypoplasia d18O values differ statistically from the rest of the series is untested.
comments.request: Test this difference.
comments.quote: Are d18O values from the hypoplasia statistically different from the rest of the series?

comments.issue: Strontium interpretation is farmed out to another paper; the manuscript must stand alone.
comments.request: Recap and integrate the strontium interpretation here.
comments.quote: The interpretation of Sr in these datasets is farmed out to another paper. This is fine, but it needs to be re-capped in this paper and integrated into these datasets.

comments.issue: The migrant classification metric and whether all individuals migrate are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what determines migrant status.
comments.quote: what determines whether an individual is a migrant? What is the metric?

comments.issue: How body size was estimated is not explained.
comments.request: State whether body size is measured from specimens or a published dataset.
comments.quote: How is body size estimated? Is this a metric derived from the sampled dataset (e.g., molar measurements) or is there a published, “species average” body size dataset that is being used?

comments.issue: Peaking during the LGM is hard to support given the temporal resolution and non-overlapping sites.
comments.request: Temper this claim.
comments.quote: This is very tough to say given the temporal resolution of your dataset (and two sites that don’t overlap in time with the LGM).

comments.issue: Whether the stressed specimen is the hypoplasia one is unclear.
comments.request: Specify the specimen.
comments.quote: Is this the specimen with the linear hypoplasia—or something else? Please specify.

comments.issue: Figure 1 is difficult to read and interpret.
comments.request: Highlight key messages with labels or color.
comments.quote: I like that fact that all of your data are plotted on these figures, but they are difficult to read and interpret.

comments.issue: Figure 4 comparisons are hard; fossil versus modern is not consistent.
comments.request: Connect datasets with dotted lines and use Last Glacial Period in the legend.
comments.quote: Could the datasets be connected for better comparison? i.e., a dotted line connecting fossil/modern dots for each taxon for ease of comparison (high/low plot).

comments.issue: Figure 5 does not distinguish LGP from modern assemblages.
comments.request: Color code sites by age.
comments.quote: Can sites be color coded to distinguish between LGP and modern assemblages?

title: Non‐Analog Behaviour of Eastern African Herbivore Communities During the Last Glacial Period

study.system: zebra finches; multigenerational maternal age and telomere length experiment

editor_summary: Both referees find the topic broadly relevant but identify major problems; editor shares the concern that the telomere-longevity link is absent and that the body-condition alternative must be ruled out.

reviews.assessment: Important, well-conducted multigenerational result with appropriate methods, though the unconventional organization and supplementary material should be fixed.
strengths: important result in parental age effects
valuable linkage with a specific mechanism (telomere shortening)
hypothesis-driven with appropriate methods and statistics
