comments.issue: Materials and Methods are in the supplement, which is atypical and hinders understanding of the results.
comments.request: Move the Materials and Methods to the main text.
comments.quote: The manuscript's length is far from the word-count limit for the journal, so I think the authors should move the Materials and Methods to the main text.

comments.issue: Supplementary materials are unnecessary; the short paper would stay concise if they were incorporated.
comments.request: Incorporate the supplementary materials into the main text.
comments.quote: it's not clear to me why anything needs to be in the Supplementary materials. The paper is very short, and would still be concise if the Supplementary materials were incorporated into the main text.

comments.issue: Additional Statistics and Results section is uncited and disconnected.
comments.request: Incorporate it into the main text.
comments.quote: the Additional Statistics and Results section in the Supplementary Material does not appear to be cited anywhere, and therefore seems disconnected from the rest of the manuscript.

comments.issue: Results may reflect repeated breeding effects rather than grandmaternal age per se.
comments.request: Include a treatment where F0 breeds only at older age.
comments.quote: I wonder if the authors have considered whether their results are predominantly due to grandmaternal age, per se, or due to repeated breeding effects.

comments.issue: Lifespan of F2 birds is not determined, leaving the longevity link untested.
comments.request: Comment on the feasibility of a study measuring F2 lifespan.
comments.quote: It would be good to have a similar study that determines the lifespan of the F2 birds.

comments.issue: About ten line-level copy edits (citation style, punctuation, spacing, missing words).
comments.quote: Page 2, Line 35. There is a missing period in the citation (should be "Wylde et al.").

comments.issue: 'Selective disappearance effects' at Page 3, Line 52 is not elaborated.
comments.request: Elaborate on selective disappearance effects.
comments.quote: I recommend elaboration on "selective disappearance effects". This would make it easier for the reader to follow.

comments.issue: Table numbering is unconventional: S1 is cited before S0 and indexing is zero-based.
comments.request: Renumber the tables conventionally.
comments.quote: Tables are usually numbered in the order they are cited, but Table S1 is currently cited before Table S0.

comments.issue: Two sentences at Page 5, Lines 22-31 contradict each other about male age compensation.
comments.request: Reconcile the two statements.
comments.quote: If the authors don't know about the combined effects of old grandfathers and old grandmothers, how can they say that "male age does not compensate for intergenerational effects operating through maternal age"?

comments.issue: Fig. 2B sample size for the F1 bar appears to be 12, not as shown.
comments.request: Correct the sample size in Fig. 2B.
comments.quote: In Fig. 2B, shouldn't the sample size for the F1 bar be 12 (per Page 10, Line 17)?

comments.issue: Female-biased sex ratio in F2 offspring from old grandmothers is not commented on.
comments.request: Comment on the biased sex ratio.
comments.quote: I think the authors should comment on why the sex ratio was so female biased in the F2 offspring that emerged from old grandmothers. Does that mean anything?

comments.issue: Fig. 1 panels A and B have misaligned axes and different y-axis ranges.
comments.request: Align the axes and use the same value ranges.
comments.quote: I recommend the authors make the horizontal axes in panels A and B line up, and make the vertical axes have the same range of values.

comments.issue: Only averages of ages are given; spread of ages is missing at first mention.
comments.request: Provide the range of ages alongside the averages.
comments.quote: I recommend the authors provide some measure of the spread of these ages, in addition to the averages. The range of ages might be the best choice for this.

comments.issue: Page 10, Line 49 sentence implies F1 birds performed qPCR.
comments.request: Split the sentence into method and subjects.
comments.quote: I recommend breaking this up into two sentences, one for the method of measuring telomere length, and one for the birds to which that method was applied.

comments.issue: 'Final model' implies pre-final models but is unexplained at first mention.
comments.request: Elaborate on model selection at first mention.
comments.quote: This appears to imply there were "pre-final models" as well. I think the authors should elaborate.

comments.issue: Table description 'showing fixed factor estimates in parenthesis' seems inaccurate.
comments.request: Correct the table description.
comments.quote: The phrase "showing fixed factor estimates in parenthesis" doesn't appear to accurately describe the tables.

reviews.assessment: Interesting observation, but the assumed telomere-longevity link is unsupported, condition transfer explains the pattern, and the effects are intergenerational, not transgenerational.

comments.issue: Motivation assumes telomere length affects longevity, but there is no evidence for this; telomeres indicate condition, not mechanism.
comments.request: Justify or abandon the telomere-longevity mechanism assumption.
comments.quote: there is no indication in this study, nor in any of the previous studies, that telomere length affects longevity in this species (or any other species)

comments.issue: Condition transfer from old grandmothers is an alternative explanation: adverse parental environment effects can persist beyond F1.
comments.request: Rule out condition-transfer before claiming germline ageing.
comments.quote: I am not sure how this conclusion can be reached using this data. It is quite possible for adverse effects of parental environment to go beyond F1 as has been demonstrated in the literature.

comments.issue: F2 primordial germ cells can be directly affected by the P0 environment, so effects are intergenerational, not transgenerational.
comments.request: Use the correct intergenerational versus transgenerational terminology.
comments.quote: The effects described here are intergenerational, not transgenerational (cf. page 1 of Introduction).

comments.issue: Observation does not support conclusions about germline ageing; poor somatic condition of old mothers is more parsimonious.
comments.request: Temper the germline-ageing conclusions.
comments.quote: Old mothers could be in a poor somatic condition and producing poor quality F1 and F2, which is reflected in the telomere length. In my view, this is the most parsimonious explanation.

title: Hidden Causes of Variation in Offspring Reproductive Value: Negative Effects of Maternal Breeding Age on Offspring Telomere Length Persist Undiminished Across Multiple Generations

study.system: caterpillars on synthetic diet; toxin spatial heterogeneity

editor_summary: Complex but original and interesting; pre-review concerns cleared. Reviewer 2's issues should be addressed though no new experiments are required; a modest revision.

reviews.assessment: Interesting question but notable flaws in the feeding design undermine the conclusions.
strengths: interesting and relevant study of phytochemistry effects on herbivore behavior

comments.issue: The test of toxin-free food appears to lack a no-toxin centre block, so prior exposure effects are not properly tested.
comments.request: Add a no-toxin centre-block treatment to the design.
comments.quote: as described in figure S7 (as far as I can tell) there is no diet block presented to the larvae. A true test might instead be a diet with no toxin in the center block

comments.issue: Pre-experiment diet quality is unreported; previous exposure can confound herbivore behaviour and question the conclusions.
comments.request: Report the rearing diet quality and address prior exposure.
comments.quote: no information is given (as far as I can tell) about the previous exposure of diet quality to the larvae used in the main experiment

comments.issue: RGR declines exponentially in later instars; body-size effects may be physiological artifacts rather than toxin effects.
comments.request: Account for instar-related RGR declines in the interpretation.
comments.quote: RGR decreases exponentially in later instar lepidopteran larvae the relationships of later instar larval RGR with spatial variation in toxins could simply be an artifact

reviews.assessment: Great, novel question and a well-designed experiment, but the complex results need extra clarity and real-world framing.
strengths: novel, creative, likely of broad interest

comments.issue: The optimal strategy question should be framed via the relative weight of arrestment versus immigration parameters.
comments.request: Frame optimal strategy in terms of arrestment vs immigration weights.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors more clearly frame the question of optimal strategy in terms of the relative weight of the parameters in their behavior model (arrestment vs immigration)

comments.issue: Discussion should connect to natural sources of defence variation and insect dispersal and diet specialization.
comments.request: Ground the conclusions in real-world context.
comments.quote: I’d like to see the discussion come back around to consider the sources of spatial variation in chemical defenses in nature and variation in insect dispersal and diet specialization and ground the conclusions of the paper in the real world

comments.issue: Line-level edits: clarity rewrites at L348-352 and L380-382, 'whole-plant' at L372, missing KBS number at L457.
comments.request: Apply these line-level corrections.
comments.quote: Lines 348-352: This sentence could be improved for clarity.

comments.issue: Arrestment is described as a strategy to find preferred food rather than to remain on it.
comments.request: Describe the strategy via relative propensity for arrestment vs immigration.
comments.quote: Is this mis-written? Why would arrestment be a strategy to find preferred food (as opposed to remaining on preferred food once it is found)?

comments.issue: The 'purple' (missing data) colour is hard to distinguish from the blue scale, and its meaning is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the purple colour and whether those areas are herbivory holes.
comments.quote: It isn’t clear what color is “purple” (missing data) because the color scale appears to range from dark blue to light blue

comments.issue: Panel label 'A' is missing from the figure.
comments.request: Add the missing panel label.
comments.quote: I don’t see “A” on the figure

comments.issue: Fig. 3c excludes pre-weight information shown in the other panels.
comments.request: Revise panel c to show time to pupation vs pre-weight with colour-coded variation.
comments.quote: Why does panel c exclude the information about pre-weight that is included in the other three panels?

title: Large Differences in Herbivore Performance Emerge From Simple Herbivore Behaviours and Fine‐Scale Spatial Heterogeneity in Phytochemistry

study.system: nectar microbial communities; 31 plant species inoculation

editor_summary: Both reviewers find the study interesting and well presented, but the editor and reviewers want more emphasis on novelty and relevance to other systems, expanding the scope of the text.

reviews.assessment: Nice, methodologically robust study; asks to emphasise the 'so what' factor, novelty and wider relevance, plus minor clarifications.

comments.issue: The 'so what' factor and relevance to a wider audience of ecologists are underemphasised.
comments.request: Highlight the broader significance and relevance to a wider audience.
comments.quote: My only general comment would be to emphasise the “so what” factor a little more. I know it’s there, but it could be highlighted further.

comments.issue: The abstract does not mention potential implications or applications of the findings.
comments.request: Briefly mention implications such as impacts on plant health or pollination.
comments.quote: It could briefly mention the potential implications or applications of understanding these microbial communities, such as impacts on plant health or pollination.

comments.issue: The novel aspects of the study are not emphasised early enough in the introduction.
comments.request: Emphasise the novel aspects earlier in the introduction.
comments.quote: While the introduction mentions gaps in current research, further emphasising the novel aspects of this study early on could make the significance clearer.

comments.issue: The microbe species are not named and their type (bacteria, fungi, protozoa) is not stated in the text.
comments.request: Name the microbes and state whether they are bacterial or fungal.
comments.quote: I would probably name the ‘microbe species’ in the text here – and state whether they’re bacteria, fungi, protozoa etc.

comments.issue: The reason for excluding plant species with low sample sizes is not stated.
comments.request: State why low-sample-size plant species were excluded.
comments.quote: Perhaps state why certain plant species with low sample sizes were excluded from the analysis.

comments.issue: How microbial identification by morphology was validated and its limitations are not described.
comments.request: Describe validation of morphological identification and its limitations.
comments.quote: Include more information on how microbial identification by morphology was validated and any potential limitations of this method.

comments.issue: P values are not italicised and species names in Figure 4 are not italicised.
comments.request: Italicise P values and Figure 4 species names.
comments.quote: Italicise your ‘P’ when reporting your stats.

comments.issue: The discussion could further emphasise the biological and ecological relevance and implications of the findings.
comments.request: Discuss implications for plant-pollinator interactions and ecosystem functioning with references.
comments.quote: I recommend further emphasising the biological/ecological relevance and implications of the findings, e.g., how they might affect plant-pollinator interactions and ecosystem functioning

comments.issue: Limitations and assumptions, including the generalisability of the selected taxa and plant species, are not discussed explicitly.
comments.request: Discuss the study's limitations and assumptions more explicitly.
comments.quote: Also, discuss the limitations and assumptions of the study more explicitly, such as the potential impact of the selected microbe taxa and plant species on the generalisability of the results.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not indicate the direction of pipetting, which could confuse readers.
comments.request: Add a small arrow showing the pipetting direction in Figure 1.
comments.quote: To prevent confusion, perhaps add a small arrow indicating the direction of the pipetting (i.e., upwards for A and downwards for B).

reviews.assessment: Ambitious, comprehensive and well-supported study; asks to broaden the impact and clarify controls, measurements and several figures.

comments.issue: The manuscript does not highlight enough how the results might inform researchers in other systems.
comments.request: Add sentences, especially in the conclusion, on how the work informs others theoretically.
comments.quote: a few additional sentences, especially in the conclusion about how this might inform others’ work on a theoretical level would add to the manuscript

comments.issue: The role of the control experiment, testing inoculants and synthetic nectar rather than negative controls, is not clearly explained.
comments.request: Explain more clearly what the control experiment tested.
comments.quote: I would more clearly explain your control experiment. These were not negative controls for your inoculation experiment, but rather, to test your inoculants (and synthetic nectar)?

comments.issue: Hydrogen peroxide was measured in different flowers than the inoculation experiment; microbial induction or background growth may make it unrepresentative.
comments.request: Confirm whether peroxide in uninoculated flowers represents inoculated flowers.
comments.quote: your hydrogen peroxide measurements were on different flower’s nectar than your inoculation experiment. Could there be induction of the hydrogen peroxide production in individual flowers due to the presence (inoculation) of microbes?

comments.issue: Differences between flowers with and without nectar across species and treatments were not examined.
comments.request: Optionally test for differences between flowers with and without nectar.
comments.quote: Was there a difference between species/treatments/etc. in flowers that contained no nectar and those that did contain nectar?

comments.issue: The sucrose control and artificial nectar cluster into different groups in Figure 4A/S5, which is not explained.
comments.quote: Figure 4A/S5 - It is interesting that the sucrose control and artificial nectar cluster into different groups.

comments.issue: Why Neokomagataea was the only microbe whose growth was uncorrelated with others is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss why Neokomagataea growth is uncorrelated with other microbes.
comments.quote: You state that “Neokomagataea was the only microbe whose growth was not associated with that of any other microbe across plant species”. This is so fascinating and surprising to me. Why do you think that is?

comments.issue: The relationship between hierarchical clustering of microbial densities and plant phylogenetic relatedness is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this relationship and revise the visual presentation.
comments.quote: What is the relationship between the hierarchical clustering based on microbial densities (Fig S5) and phylogenetic relatedness of the plants?

comments.issue: Figure 4A colours resemble the clade colours used elsewhere, causing confusion with hierarchical clustering.
comments.request: Use a different colour scheme for hierarchical clustering.
comments.quote: I would choose a very different color scheme for Fig 4A or any figures that use color to denote the hierarchical clustering and not the clade so others don’t get confused.

comments.issue: Figure S3 axis units and whether values are final densities are unclear, implying a massive die-off.
comments.request: Clarify the units and whether values are final densities.
comments.quote: Second, are you missing units? According to the main text, you created inoculants of 5 x 104 total cells μL-1 and inoculated 1 μL.

comments.issue: Figure S7 X axes are not labelled.
comments.request: Label the X axes in Figure S7.
comments.quote: Figure S7 - please label the X axes in the figure.

comments.issue: Figure 1 panel labels are not aligned and temperature icons do not match other illustrations.
comments.request: Bottom-align the panel labels and match the temperature icons.
comments.quote: I suggest bottom aligning the figure panel labels so they are all at the same height. Use temperature icons that match the other illustrations in the figure.

title: Seasonal Assembly of Nectar Microbial Communities Across Angiosperm Plant Species: Assessing Contributions of Climate and Plant Traits

study.system: ectothermic animals; reanalysis of thermal tolerance acclimation experiments

editor_summary: Editor agrees the paper reads easily but went through theory too quickly, did not test taxonomic variation, and has methodological/statistical shortcuts (rate vs capacity computation, acclimation temperature used twice, multiple response variables); requests the article list, variance scaling and R².

reviews.assessment: Interesting and clear contribution, but needs contextualisation of theory and clarifications on the plasticity metrics and their interpretation.
strengths: addresses a key aspect of plasticity variability

comments.issue: The title should read 'High capacity FOR physiological plasticity'.
comments.request: Change the title wording.
comments.quote: The title should be “High capacity FOR physiological plasticity”.

comments.issue: The claim that plasticity variability results from selection rather than drift, and the meaning of 'divergence in plasticity rate', are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what is known and still open about the origin of variability in plasticity rates.
comments.quote: It would be important to make very clear what we know and what are still open questions about the origin of variability in plasticity rates

comments.issue: The sentence at L53-55 is heavy and unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence after clarifying 'divergence'.
comments.quote: The sentence L. 53-55 is also quite heavy to read, and would require rephrasing

comments.issue: The introduction implicitly assumes plasticity is adaptive without discussing whether it increases environmental match.
comments.request: Hedge with 'might' and discuss the potential adaptiveness of plasticity in the introduction and discussion.
comments.quote: The introduction of phenotypic plasticity implicitly assumes adaptiveness, but whether plasticity adaptively increases the match to the environment is often an open question

comments.issue: The prevalence of plasticity is presented too categorically, ignoring alternatives such as bet hedging and dispersal and their dependence on timescale and predictability.
comments.request: Add nuance, cite Botero et al. 2015, and state the focus on adaptive reversible plasticity.
comments.quote: Related to that, the authors may be too categorical regarding the prevalence of plasticity (e.g., L. 34-35)

comments.issue: The theoretical work behind the predicted negative rate-capacity relationship is not explained, including its dependence on predictability and reversibility.
comments.request: Detail the theory and its predictions for different fluctuation regimes.
comments.quote: Further explanation of this theoretical work and how it results in this prediction of a negative relationship between rate and capacity would be important to detail here

comments.issue: The alternative expectation of a positive rate-capacity correlation proposed by Siljestam & Östman is neglected.
comments.request: Include this alternative in the introduction and discussion.
comments.quote: we feel that the opposite expectation proposed by Siljestam & Östman is clearly neglected in this paragraph

comments.issue: The manuscript does not follow the journal's classical structure with Methods after the Introduction.
comments.request: Restructure the manuscript to match journal requirements.
comments.quote: Ecology Letters only publishes papers with a classical structure, where Methods are just after the Introduction

comments.issue: The reasoning for computing capacity as a log2 subtraction is unexplained, and the resulting log(log2·°C) scale is hard to interpret biologically.
comments.request: Explain why a log2 subtraction was chosen.
comments.quote: why did the authors choose a log2 subtraction of phenotypic values

comments.issue: Capacity is normalised by temperature change while rate is not, and acclimation temperature is also a fixed effect, so capacity is corrected twice.
comments.request: Clarify the double correction and consider computing capacity similarly to rate or with a single decay model.
comments.quote: acclimation temperature is also included in the model as a fixed effect, so why correct the capacity values themselves?

comments.issue: Table 1 lists four statistics lines but only three candidate model lines.
comments.request: Clarify or correct Table 1.
comments.quote: There are 4 lines for statistics, but apparently only 3 lines of candidate model are shown

comments.issue: The fixed effects are described only by reference to the methods, not in the table legend.
comments.request: Briefly describe the fixed effects in the legend.
comments.quote: It would also be helpful to provide a brief description of the fixed effects in the legend of the figure, not only pointing to the methods

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the reported 'sensitivity' reflects correlation among fixed variables or interactive effects.
comments.request: Clarify how these variables correlate and distinguish the two scenarios.
comments.quote: Such “sensitivity” might result from two aspects: correlation between fixed variables, or interactive effects

comments.issue: Whether the rate-capacity relationship varies among phylogenetic groups is not tested, although only a random intercept is included.
comments.request: Test taxonomic group interactions, spline regressions per group or random slopes.
comments.quote: could you test for an interaction between taxonomic group and capacity, or with spline regressions for each taxonomic group

comments.issue: The bottom panels of Fig. 1 have no clear purpose.
comments.request: Justify or remove the bottom panels.
comments.quote: what is the rational for keeping the bottom panels? What do they bring?

comments.issue: Fig. 2 may belong in the supplementary information rather than the main text.
comments.request: Move Fig. 2 to the SI and refer to it in the text.
comments.quote: we feel that this figure may better belong to the SI, while being referred to in the Methods and Results

comments.issue: The X axis meaning regarding phylogenetic signal in Fig. 2 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the X axis.
comments.quote: may you clarify what is the exact meaning of the X axis about phylogenetic signal?

comments.issue: Figure S1 is not illustrative because final values are all close to z-infinity, and the computation of both key variables is not shown in the main text.
comments.request: Move an enhanced Figure S1 to the main text and add more illustrative raw data cases.
comments.quote: An enhanced version of Figure S1 would be important to include in the main text, to show how the two key variables were computed and scaled

comments.issue: Time to death is used before being introduced or defined.
comments.request: Explain time to death earlier, e.g. by moving the methods before the results.
comments.quote: time to death is not introduced nor defined before

comments.issue: Framing the meta-analytical results bluntly in the context of environmental change at the start of the discussion is too bold.
comments.request: Reframe the discussion around testing a key theoretical hypothesis.
comments.quote: it seems a little bold to frame these meta-analytical results in a context of environmental change so bluntly, in the very beginning of the discussion

comments.issue: Other scenarios producing similar patterns, such as a simple trade-off between capacity and speed of plasticity, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss alternative explanations such as the Dupont et al. 2024 trade-off.
comments.quote: other possible scenarios that might lead to similar patterns, such as a simple trade-off between capacity and speed of plasticity

comments.issue: The discussion does not consider the context-dependency of plasticity rate.
comments.request: Consider context-dependency of plasticity rate, as outlined in Box 3 of Dupont et al. 2024.
comments.quote: We think that this discussion would benefit from including a consideration of potential context-dependency of plasticity rate

comments.issue: If acclimation and phylogenetic signal explain all variation, nothing would be left for capacity to explain.
comments.request: Clarify how variance is partitioned among acclimation, phylogeny and capacity.
comments.quote: But then acclimation and phylogenetic signal would explain all variation, with nothing explained by the capacity, right?

comments.issue: It is unclear where tolerance curve data entered the analyses.
comments.request: State where tolerance curve data were used.
comments.quote: Where did you included tolerance curves data in the analyses?

reviews.assessment: The topic fits the journal but the objective and hypotheses lack clarity, and confounding, trait choice and literature interpretation need attention.
strengths: important topic in the context of global change
subject fits the journal's aim and scope

comments.issue: The objective and hypotheses are lacking and the manuscript jumps too quickly to the prediction, obscuring the novelty.
comments.request: State the hypotheses and the kind of selection acting on plasticity rate.
comments.quote: Objective and hypothesis of the study is lacking, jumping too quickly in the prediction.

comments.issue: The prediction is easy to follow only under a linear reaction norm, and it is unclear whether it holds for non-linear reaction norms.
comments.request: Discuss whether the predictions apply to non-linear reaction norms.
comments.quote: Are these predictions also expected for non-linear reaction norms?

comments.issue: The statement at lines 42-44 is only true for a linear reaction norm.
comments.request: Reformulate the sentence.
comments.quote: This affirmation is only true for linear reaction norm. I would suggest the author to reformulate the sentence.

comments.issue: It is not stated what kind of selection the rate of plasticity could undergo.
comments.request: Briefly mention the possible selection on plasticity rate.
comments.quote: I would suggest the authors to mention rapidly what kind of selection the rate of phenotypic plasticity could undergo

comments.issue: The pattern could be an artefact of using critical temperature, for which adjustment may reflect passive rather than active plasticity.
comments.request: Address the possibility that the pattern arises from passive plasticity.
comments.quote: Could this be an artefact due to the trait chosen for the study (critical temperature) for which the adjustment is more likely the result of passive plasticity

comments.issue: The justification for choosing whole-body thermal tolerance as the study phenotype is missing.
comments.request: Briefly justify the choice of phenotype.
comments.quote: Justification of the studied phenotype choice (whole-body thermal tolerance to temperature change in cold-blooded organisms) is lacking.

comments.issue: Using temperature implies both passive and active plasticity, and it is unclear how the two were disentangled.
comments.request: Explain how active and passive plasticity were distinguished.
comments.quote: How both active and passive plasticity were disentangle in such choice of trait?

comments.issue: It is unclear how variable thermal tolerance plasticity is within and among species, and it may be weak or absent in some taxa.
comments.request: Quantify trait plasticity variability and assess its influence on the expected signal.
comments.quote: to what extent this trait is variable in terms of plasticity, both within and among species?

comments.issue: CTmax, CTmin and TTD have different limitations, but trait type was not accounted for in the analyses.
comments.request: Include phenotype type in the analyses, e.g. as a random effect.
comments.quote: each of these trait have their own limitations (concerning their measurements, but also their effect on and variation among organisms), but this seems to not have been taking into account in the analyses

comments.issue: Phylogeny and acclimation temperature are both confounding, but partial residuals were computed for each separately.
comments.request: Remove both confounding factors simultaneously and explain the procedure.
comments.quote: as both factors are confounding, it would be better to calculate the partial residual by removing the effect of both confounding factors at the same time

comments.issue: The statement at line 89 cannot be checked in Figure 2 because the legend does not explain the phylogenetic signal parameters.
comments.request: Adjust the legend so the phylogenetic signal can be interpreted.
comments.quote: Please adjust the legend for the interpretation of the phylogenetic signal parameters

comments.issue: Figure S3 suggests no rate-capacity correlation for CTmin and time to death, so the correlation may not hold across response metrics.
comments.request: Repeat the analysis by trait to test whether the correlation is consistent.
comments.quote: Figure S3 is very difficult to interpret, I would suggest the authors to perform their analysis by traits

comments.issue: Chevin et al. 2010 is misinterpreted: plasticity evolution depends on environmental predictability, and less plastic levels are expected under less predictable change.
comments.request: Correct the interpretation and include predictability of changes in the discussion.
comments.quote: Interpretation of Chevin et al. 2010 is not correct here, as the evolution of plasticity depend of environmental predictability

comments.issue: The claimed 'consistency across analyses' is questionable if the two studies did not use identical analyses of plasticity rate.
comments.request: Explain whether the same analysis of plasticity rate was used in both studies.
comments.quote: Could the authors explain the “consistency across analyses”, to conclude for the robustness of their conclusion, if the two study (Einum & Burton 2022 and this current ms) used exactly the same analysis of plasticity rate?

title: High Capacity for Physiological Plasticity Occurs at a Slow Rate in Ectotherms

study.system: Drosophila mesocosms; multigenerational warming and competition

editor_summary: Editor rejects but invites resubmission: novelty is overstated and key literature undercited; reconsider the analytical approach and how findings are presented given reviewers' concerns.

reviews.assessment: Creative, neat test of coexistence theory, but the model is fitted to the same data used for testing, so forecasting claims and coexistence framing need care.

comments.issue: The model is fitted and tested on the same data, so it is not an independent forecasting test.
comments.request: Use a training/test data design or frame the study as explanatory.
comments.quote: the experiment appears to serve as the basis for both parameterising the model and testing the model predictions, and therefore is really a test of explanatory power for the data in hand

comments.issue: Prediction and forecasting terminology is used loosely.
comments.request: Use these terms with caution.
comments.quote: I think more general use of terminology such as prediction and forecasting need to be implemented with caution

comments.issue: How the study goes beyond previous work is not contextualised.
comments.request: Provide more context on the study's advance.
comments.quote: perhaps the author could provide a little more context on how it goes beyond previous studies (even if it falls short of a 'true' predictive test)

comments.issue: The case for interpreting predictions through coexistence theory rather than the model directly is not made.
comments.request: Discuss how niche and fitness differences shift with temperature.
comments.quote: I don't think the manuscript makes nearly a strong enough case for interpreting the predictions through the lens of coexistence theory, versus taking the coexistence/exclusion predictions directly from the model

comments.issue: The mechanism of competition in the experimental system is not stated.
comments.request: Clarify the competition mechanism for non-Drosophila readers.
comments.quote: there was no mention of the mechanism of competition in this experimental system - presumably solely through resource consumption, but it would be good to clarify this for non-Drosophila researchers.

comments.issue: The lack of a combined competition-by-stochasticity effect on extirpation is not discussed.
comments.request: Offer plausible explanations for this result.
comments.quote: A result which I thought was particularly intriguing but did not receive much attention was the observation that competition and stochasticity did not have any combined impact on extirpation rate

comments.issue: The Ellner partition was not used to quantify competition with and without variability.
comments.request: Implement the partition to verify the absence of fluctuation-dependent mechanisms.
comments.quote: It could be valuable to implement the partition to quantitatively verify this.

comments.issue: Frequency dependence is confused with density dependence.
comments.request: Change frequency-dependence to density dependence.
comments.quote: Suggest changing frequency-dependence to density dependence given that a change in interspecific densities independent of a change to intraspecific densities will not typically lead to an Allee effect?

comments.issue: Monocultures were not conducted for D. pandora, which is not stated.
comments.request: Clarify this in the methods.
comments.quote: Helpful to clarify that monocultures were not conducted for D. pandora (I only realised this after seeing Fig S4).

comments.issue: Other applied coexistence-theory papers are not cited.
comments.request: Mention these additional papers.
comments.quote: Could mention several other papers pursuing alternative applied applications of coexistence theory (as noted in Terry and Armitage 2024): Ocampo- Ariza et al., 2018; Huntly et al., 2021; Letten et al., 2021.

comments.issue: Species-initial indexing makes the model hard to read.
comments.request: Simplify the indexing.
comments.quote: The indexing with species initials makes the model harder to read than it needs to be. Perhaps simplify to 'n' and 'l' or some alternative shortened index?

comments.issue: How generation-to-generation transitions were quantified is not explained.
comments.request: Describe how transitions were quantified.
comments.quote: Ln 201-202. How are the observed generation-to-generation population transitions quantified?

comments.issue: The threshold for predicted exclusion is not stated.
comments.request: Confirm the exclusion threshold.
comments.quote: Ln 246. Presumably the threshold for predicted exclusion is when >50% of the posterior predictions indicate exclusion?

comments.issue: The extirpation time should be qualified as D. pallidifrons.
comments.request: Add the species qualification.
comments.quote: Ln 259. Helpful to qualify that this is the mean observed extirpation time of *D. pallidifrons*.

comments.issue: The discussion does not start with a summary of main results.
comments.request: Resummarise the main results at the start of the discussion.
comments.quote: Ln 267-282. It would be useful to resummarise the main results at the start of the discussion.

comments.issue: The framing of the results is overly pessimistic.
comments.request: Make the framing a little more optimistic.
comments.quote: More generally, I appreciated the author's candid discussion of the results but in places it seemed the framing could be a little more optimistic.

comments.issue: The sentence suggests technical biases rather than unavoidable confounding.
comments.request: Revise this characterisation.
comments.quote: this sentence seemed suggestive of more technical biases of the approach rather than the unavoidable confounding effects of natural systems

reviews.assessment: Lots to like and statistically diligent, but the most pessimistic reading is that exclusions peak where coexistence is predicted, and several analyses need reconsideration.
strengths: one of the few tests of methods for predicting competitive outcomes
would serve as an example for others

comments.issue: Exclusions peak at the region of greatest predicted coexistence, which could mislead management.
comments.request: Take a more pessimistic reading of the predictive value.
comments.quote: since the highest frequency of exclusions are observed to occur at the region of greatest predicted coexistence, this could easily lead us down the wrong path if such predictions were being used to make management recommendations.

comments.issue: Traditional ND-FD is used for static but simulation-based approaches for fluctuating environments without comparison.
comments.request: Use one approach for both or verify they agree.
comments.quote: I don't fully understand the motivation for using the traditional ND-FD decomposition for predicting coexistence in static environments but then the simulation-based approach for predicting it in fluctuating environments.

comments.issue: The non-exponentiated model form was used despite the exponentiated form fitting best.
comments.request: Analyse the best-fitting model or justify the choice.
comments.quote: even though the exponentiated Beverton-Holt model was selected as having the best fit using ELPD-LOO, the non-exponentiated form was used here for computational convenience.

comments.issue: The simulation-based approach and its assumptions are not described in enough detail.
comments.request: Define the E and C components and discuss the unmet assumptions.
comments.quote: For example, how were the E and C components of the models defined?

comments.issue: The actual predictions are not plotted in Figure 3b.
comments.request: Plot the predictions in Figure 3b.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to plot the actual predictions in figure 3b as well, rather than only discuss it briefly at the end of the results.

comments.issue: Coexistence mechanism values such as relative nonlinearity are not reported.
comments.request: Present the values of the coexistence mechanisms.
comments.quote: why not present the values of the coexistence mechanisms like relative nonlinearity in competition or temperature?

comments.issue: Results are benchmarked for only one species.
comments.request: Also predict invasion growth rates for D. pandora.
comments.quote: why were the results only benchmarked for one species (D. pallidifrons) and not the other? Couldn't they also predict invasion growth rates of D. pandora from the model

comments.issue: Equilibrium invasion predictions are estimated from non-stationary environmental data.
comments.request: Address the challenges of non-stationarity.
comments.quote: all of these long-term predictions of invasions at equilibria are actually being estimated from data collected along a non-stationary environment.

comments.issue: Heat-hardening acclimation or rapid adaptive evolution could confound the results.
comments.request: Test growth rates of gradual-ramp versus spike populations.
comments.quote: how can we be sure that heat-hardening acclimation or even rapid adaptive evolution is not occurring in these tubes?

comments.issue: It is unknown whether lab dynamics reflect the species' natural thermal distributions.
comments.request: Benchmark the lab results against field distributions.
comments.quote: It would be very interesting to know if the dynamics in the lab reflect the observed thermal distributions of these species

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and a novel set of methods, but major missing details and conceptual simplifications make it hard to follow and to see the added value.
strengths: tests results across multiple model functional forms
combination of classic Chesson and Ellner methods
good job explaining statistical methods with code and outputs in supplement

comments.issue: It is hard to follow which best practices and established methods were actually applied.
comments.request: Specify which methods from each cited paper were used and describe them.
comments.quote: I find it very hard to follow which “best practices” and “established methods” you apply in your paper

comments.issue: The study addresses a simple, largely solved pairwise-competition problem, so the novel insights are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what the statistical methods add beyond classic analyses.
comments.quote: I was a bit disappointed by the fact that your study sticks to relatively simple, and in my opinion largely solved, problem – pairwise competitive interactions, defined by a relatively simple model

comments.issue: What the newer methods add beyond Chesson's original approach is not clear.
comments.request: Explain the added value of the Ellner approach.
comments.quote: it is not very clear to me from the current text what these additional analyses actually yielded that would not have been apparat from a simple analysis as might have been done ten years ago

comments.issue: The observed-predicted temperature difference is hard to read from the figures.
comments.request: Present this comparison more clearly.
comments.quote: it is also very hard to read off of your figures, at least in my opinion (as far as I can tell, at least, the reader has to combine information from across Figs. 2-3 to reach this conclusion)

comments.issue: The paper should be realigned around the multi-model and multi-method tests.
comments.request: Reframe as a test of what new methods add.
comments.quote: my suggestion would be that you realign your paper to better highlight the multi-model and multi-method tests that you implemented

comments.issue: The prediction mismatch could be reframed as an important result.
comments.request: Treat the mismatch as a feature rather than a bug.
comments.quote: still can’t make accurate predictions of temperature impacts on extinctions, then I think this is a very important result in its own right

comments.issue: The criteria for stable coexistence from invasion rates are oversimplified.
comments.request: Draw on the fuller literature on invasion-rate criteria.
comments.quote: Fulfilling the criteria for identifying stable coexistence based on invasion rates is not quite so simple

comments.issue: The brief niche and fitness difference definitions are imprecise.
comments.request: Use the more precise definitions from the cited sources.
comments.quote: E.g. as you have them defined in the equations around page 7, fitness differences can be arbitrarily large and still allow for coexistence.

comments.issue: The problem with invasion rates is one of scope, not merely assumptions.
comments.request: Discuss the scope of the tests needed.
comments.quote: I think it’s important to stress that the problem is not merely one of assumptions, but rather one of scope.

comments.issue: The eight phenomenological models and the meaning of poor convergence are not given.
comments.request: List the models and explain poor convergence.
comments.quote: Again, I would suggest that you either list the eight phenomenological models here, or that you point to a specific part of the supplement where they are listed.

comments.issue: The kernel selection criteria are not stated.
comments.request: List the quantitative indices used for kernel selection.
comments.quote: Again, I’m a bit confused by what you mean by “the selected” kernel. Based on what criteria?

comments.issue: The “standard approaches” followed from four different papers are not specified.
comments.request: Specify which approaches were followed from each paper.
comments.quote: Again, I find “standard approaches” to be needlessly cryptic here.

comments.issue: Many different definitions of niche and fitness differences yield different answers.
comments.request: Provide a derivation and justification for the chosen terms.
comments.quote: there are lots of different ways to define niche and fitness differences, and they often yield subtly different answers

title: An Experimental Validation Test of Ecological Coexistence Theory to Forecast Extinction Under Rising Temperatures

study.system: pollinator research literature; taxonomic and geographic biases

editor_summary: Both reviewers see merit in this timely viewpoint but require major revision: use pollinator ecology as a case study for broader biases in ecology and offer more nuanced, concrete recommendations.

reviews.assessment: Valuable paper highlighting biases in pollinator studies; suggests broadening the scope and questions the causal direction of one driver.
strengths: important contribution highlighting several biases in pollinator studies

comments.issue: An additional bias is not discussed: most pollinator studies come from agricultural systems and cultivated crops.
comments.request: Add this bias in the distribution of pollinator studies.
comments.quote: The majority of all ecological studies on pollinators (at least if we disregard eco-evolutionary studies on plant-pollinator interactions) are from agricultural ecosystems and focus on pollinators of cultivated crops

comments.issue: The paper stays narrow instead of highlighting the broader biases in ecological research that it reflects.
comments.request: Broaden the scope, using pollinator studies as an example of more general biases.
comments.quote: This makes me wonder if it would be worth broadening the scope of the paper, and use pollinator studies as an example to highlight these more general biases?

comments.issue: 'Isolated decision-making' may be an effect rather than a driver of biased pollinator research.
comments.request: Provide evidence that biased policies drive research focus rather than follow from it.
comments.quote: I am not completely convinced that this is a driver of biases in pollinator studies. In my view, it is at least as likely to be an effect of these biases

comments.issue: Two line-level edits: use 'butterflies and moths' on L108 and correct the spelling 'Bartomeues' on L187.
comments.quote: change “butterflies” to “butterflies and moths” (since you mention moths on the next line

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the cited papers counted nocturnal pollinators, so the visit percentage may be understated.
comments.request: Clarify whether the cited papers considered nocturnal pollinators.
comments.quote: Did these papers consider nocturnal pollinators? If not, then non-bee pollinators most likely perform an even higher percentage of the total number of flower visits.

comments.issue: Citizen science may reinforce geographic and taxonomic biases rather than counteracting them.
comments.request: Address the risk that relying on citizen scientists reinforces current biases.
comments.quote: there is a clear risk that reliance on citizen scientists would reinforce the bias on a few charismatic and easily identified pollinator taxa

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written viewpoint whose solutions are underdeveloped; asks for more explicit, nuanced and practical recommendations.
strengths: novel contribution discussing drivers of bias

comments.issue: Proposed solutions, the aspect readers value most, are not discussed explicitly enough.
comments.request: Discuss proposed solutions more explicitly.
comments.quote: when my colleagues and I read papers about biases in ecology, the most read and most discussed aspects are always proposed solutions

comments.issue: Solutions are buried in the last paragraph of each driver section.
comments.request: Add 'solutions' subheaders or separate driver and solution sections.
comments.quote: it would be good to include “solutions” sub headers on the last paragraph of each “driver” section where solutions are currently discussed

comments.issue: The discussion of proposed solutions is too brief and not nuanced.
comments.request: Expand existing paragraphs into a more holistic and nuanced discussion.
comments.quote: existing paragraphs should be expanded for a more holistic and nuanced discussion of proposed solutions

comments.issue: The proposed solution is obvious and ignores practical constraints such as taxonomic expertise and agriculturally targeted funding.
comments.request: Offer more nuanced, impactful and achievable solutions.
comments.quote: Needing to study other organisms is a bit too obvious – and doesn’t address several practical issues

comments.issue: By-catch data on non-target flower visitors could fill knowledge gaps where taxonomic precision is impossible.
comments.request: Suggest that scientists report by-catch data on non-bee insects.
comments.quote: suggesting scientists report “by-catch” data on the number of non-bee / non-target insects could increase knowledge of fly or beetle abundance on flowers

comments.issue: Reviews and meta-analyses overlook non-bee insects because of narrow keyword searches.
comments.request: Make keyword searches in pollinator meta-analyses include other insects.
comments.quote: Meta-analyses and reviews about pollinator decline could also consider being more mindful in their key word searches to pull in data about other insects besides bees

comments.issue: Concrete ways to overcome language barriers are not suggested.
comments.request: Suggest using translation tools or contacting authors for unclear translations.
comments.quote: authors could use ChatGPT or google translate to translate papers in other languages and/or reach out to the study authors

comments.issue: Suggestions for balanced international funding lack concrete collaboration strategies.
comments.request: Add concrete suggestions for collaborating effectively and sharing resources.
comments.quote: concrete suggestions for how to collaborate more effectively and “share the wealth” would be constructive

comments.issue: Information access is framed as mainly a language barrier, omitting publishing costs and paywalls.
comments.request: Expand the section to cover other dimensions of information access.
comments.quote: peer-reviewed journals often charge too much money and/or require that authors pay for open access, and this also creates imbalance

comments.issue: Seven line-level wording suggestions (Lines 33, 78, 82, 88, 105, 106-107, 179-180).
comments.quote: Line 78 – should be “have been” instead of “has been”

comments.issue: African Journals Online is a relevant resource that is not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention African Journals Online.
comments.quote: Line 139 - African Journals Online (https://www.ajol.info/index.php/ajol) is worth mentioning.

title: Global Biases in Ecology and Conservation Research: Insight From Pollinator Studies

study.system: diazotrophic cyanobacterium; lab N-gradient cultures

editor_summary: Both reviewers and editor find the objectives interesting but the methods and results presentation needs strengthening; ionome results should move to the main text and the N:P framing and 'evolution' terminology reconsidered.

reviews.assessment: Interesting study whose message is hard to grasp; the title, abstract, design description and figures need substantial clarification.

comments.issue: Title and abstract are vague and do not advertise the results or name the key traits.
comments.request: Make the title specific and state the key traits and findings in the abstract.
comments.quote: The title and abstract do a poor job in advertising the results of this paper: they are both vague/unspecific. Please make the title more attractive.

comments.issue: Text describes element contents while results are shown as C:element ratios, confusing readers.
comments.request: Use consistent ratios throughout.
comments.quote: However, your results are presented as C:S, C:Mo and C:Fe contents (Tables S1 and S2), which makes the interpretation difficult for the reader.

comments.issue: The experimental design cannot be grasped from the methods; pre-adaptation and experimental N:P sets differ.
comments.request: Add a conceptual figure and explain the design in detail.
comments.quote: I have trouble grasping the experimental design from the description in the Methods section. Could you please provide a conceptual figure of the setup?

comments.issue: Pre-adaptation used a non-clonal stock culture, so calling it evolution is controversial.
comments.request: Address this issue and consider renaming it pre-adaptation.
comments.quote: This study does not use clonal cultures, but a stock culture consisting of an unknown number of clones (see e.g. Yoshida et al 2003). This issue (i.e. using a stock culture with an unknown number of clones) should be addressed by the authors.

comments.issue: Cross-references to the supplemental information are missing for key methods.
comments.request: Refer to the supplement where relevant.
comments.quote: In the methods section (and other sections), make sure you refer to the Supplemental Information when relevant.

comments.issue: The purpose of cumulative N fixation and P uptake rates is unclear; normalised rates would be better.
comments.request: Report Nfix:C and Pup:C and add ratio figures.
comments.quote: I am confused about the ‘cumulative N fixation rates’ and the ‘cumulative P uptake rates’: I do not understand the purpose of these two parameters.

comments.issue: Statistical results in Table 1 could move to the supplement.
comments.request: Move them to the Supplementary Information.
comments.quote: Table 1: Maybe move the statistical results to the Supplementary Information.

comments.issue: How pairwise element ratios yield a PCA with per-element arrows is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the PCA construction.
comments.quote: I have trouble understanding how including every possible pairwise ratio of the elements (line 247), yields a PCA with arrows with each specific element (Fig. 3).

comments.issue: Most ionome results are only in tables; figures like Fig 2 would aid interpretation.
comments.request: Add supplementary figures of Tables S1 and S2 results.
comments.quote: Please add (Supplementary) Figures that shows the bottom 2/3 of the results in Table S1 and S2 in a similar way to Fig. 2. Results in Figures are so much easier to interpret than data in Tables!

comments.issue: The meaning of 'low resource N:P populations' is unclear.
comments.request: Define which N:P treatments are meant.
comments.quote: What exactly do you mean by ‘low resource N:P populations’: ‘N:P = 2’, or ‘N:P = 2 and N:P = 10’?

comments.issue: Plotting variables against PLS axis 1 is hard to interpret; N:P on the x-axis would be clearer.
comments.request: Replot Figure 4 with N:P on the x-axis.
comments.quote: Figure 4 would make more sense to me if you had plotted the phytoplankton N:P on the x-axis.

comments.issue: Plastic versus adapted responses are hard to distinguish in Figures 1 and 2.
comments.request: Emphasise the adapted treatments or express plastic responses relative to them.
comments.quote: The visualize the plastic versus the adapted response better, in Figure 1 and 2, it would make sense to emphasize the difference between the pre-adapted and the phenotypic response.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the point at lines 304-305 could be shown.
comments.request: Show this result.
comments.quote: Lines 304-305: can you somehow show this?

comments.issue: Element content terminology gives opposite patterns to the C:element ratios, confusing readers.
comments.request: Use the same ratio convention throughout.
comments.quote: as I mentioned before, the terminology used in the text (as contents) show the opposite patterns as the element:C ratios you show in Tables S1 and S2: this is confusing.

comments.issue: The relevance of lines 365-367 in this context is unclear.
comments.request: Explain or remove this passage.
comments.quote: Lines 365-367: why is this relevant in this context?

comments.issue: 'Stoichiometric knife edge' is not defined.
comments.request: Explain the term.
comments.quote: Lines 383: explain what a ‘ stoichiometric knife edge’ is please.

comments.issue: Significance brackets and p-values in Figures 1 and 2 are messy.
comments.request: Use post-hoc letter groups instead.
comments.quote: The visualization of statistical differences within different Resource N:P ratios in Figures 1 and 2 is messy and difficult to read.

comments.issue: Trace elements are not listed.
comments.request: List the trace elements.
comments.quote: Lines 100-101: list the trace elements please.

comments.issue: Generations corresponding to 45 months are not reported.
comments.request: Report generation numbers for each treatment.
comments.quote: please for each ‘evolution’ N:P treatment, indicate how many generations 45 months corresponds to.

comments.issue: Figure 1 x-axis titles differ between panels.
comments.request: Use consistent x-axis titles.
comments.quote: X-axes of panels A and C versus panel B: what is the difference between ‘Resource N:P (mol)’ and ‘Growing Conditions N:P’? Please use the same x-axis titles consistently.

reviews.assessment: The experimental design constrains the interpretations far more than realised, especially the N:P framing and 'evolution' terminology.

comments.issue: N:P is treated as the sole independent variable, but only N was manipulated and all N:element ratios varied.
comments.request: Revise the text and hypotheses to reflect N supply as the variable.
comments.quote: The paper incorrectly presents N/P as the only independent variable which is incorrect: N is the only independent variable because all of the other elements were kept constant.

comments.issue: Results from small culture bottles cannot be scaled to whole-lake CHAB dynamics.
comments.request: Remove or temper the scaling claims.
comments.quote: I am extremely skeptical that results from cultures in small bottles can be scaled up to the whole-lake level to help better understand CHAB ‘dynamics’ as suggested in lines 55 and 56.

comments.issue: High external nutrient supplies mean C:element ratios cannot be read as element demand.
comments.request: Test much more dilute media, e.g. 0.1% BG11.
comments.quote: This means that no change in a C/element ratio does not necessarily mean no change in demand. Resolving this problem requires much more information on ionomes from cultures grown in BG11 media diluted much more than 5% for comparison.

comments.issue: The long-term sampling day is not stated, so short- and long-term results may not be comparable.
comments.request: State the sampling day or delete the evolution section.
comments.quote: comparing the short-term (27 day) adaptation to long-term (45 month) adaptation requires that sampling of the latter occurred on or near the 27th day of the last transfer because traits vary with time during a batch growth cycle.

comments.issue: Critical ionome results are only in supplementary tables and lack published context.
comments.request: Move these tables to the main text and compare with published ionomes.
comments.quote: Surprisingly, the ionome results (as C/element ratios) were not presented in the main text but only in supplementary Tables S1 and S2. These tables are critical evidence to both hypotheses and should be moved to the main body of the paper.

comments.issue: 'Evolution' is unjustified because genomes were not analysed.
comments.request: Use 'short-term' and 'long-term' adaptation instead.
comments.quote: The authors use the term ‘evolution’ to refer to their 45 month experiment but I would not use this term because there is no evidence that the genomes changed – for the simple reason that they were not analyzed.

comments.issue: The prediction that low N supply increases N fixation and Fe/Mo is obvious and not novel.
comments.request: Move this prediction to the Discussion and cite prior work.
comments.quote: falls into the category of obvious and is not an original contribution to the literature

comments.issue: TN/TP ratios of 2 are extremely rare in nature, so extrapolation needs caution.
comments.request: Caution readers against extrapolating based on TN/TP.
comments.quote: Readers should be cautioned that responses of Dolichospermum should not be extrapolated from this study to natural systems based on TN/TP.

comments.issue: Long-term lab adaptation is not relevant to short-lived CHAB dynamics.
comments.request: Reconsider the relevance claim and sampling design.
comments.quote: I do not see how long-term adaptation of a lab strain that had been grown in full strength media for thousands of generations to diluted media helps us understand short-term CHAB dynamics occurring over a month or two.

comments.issue: The distinction between drivers of bloom onset and regulators of composition/toxicity is missing.
comments.request: Make this distinction.
comments.quote: The distinction between drivers of onset and regulators of toxicity and species composition should be made.

comments.issue: Ni is required for N fixation but is not included in the element list or BG11.
comments.request: Consider Ni in the analyses and media discussion.
comments.quote: Include Ni which is required for hydrogenase processing of H2, an N fixation end product. As noted above, BG11 media does not include Ni.

comments.issue: 'Current' and 'evolved resource N:P' are inaccurate labels.
comments.request: Use 'short-term' and 'long-term' batch cultures.
comments.quote: ‘current’ and ‘evolved resource N:P’ cannot be understood without reading the paper and as mentioned above, are inaccurate descriptions.

comments.issue: The methods do not state that only N varied and other elements were constant.
comments.request: State this clearly, including that nutrients were in excess.
comments.quote: The authors should make very clear in the Methods section that only N varied and all other elements were kept constant.

comments.issue: Glassware type and volumes, which affect trace element impurities, are not reported.
comments.request: Report glassware materials and volumes in the methods.
comments.quote: list the type of ‘glassware’ used in preparing and storing stock solutions and as growth vessels – borosilicate, polypropylene, polyethylene, etc? Volumes?

comments.issue: 'Three subcultures' should be 'four subcultures' at line 162.
comments.request: Correct the number.
comments.quote: Line 162: Change ‘three subcultures’ to ‘four subcultures’

comments.issue: The N:P list at line 164 omits 76.
comments.request: Correct the ratio list.
comments.quote: Line 164: change ’10, and 50’ to 10, 50 and 76’ (based on Tables S1 and S2 and Figures 1 and 2).

comments.issue: Replicate numbers for the 45-month experiment are not stated.
comments.request: State the number of replicates.
comments.quote: Lines 162-164: State the number of replicates in the 45 month experiment.

comments.issue: It is unknown whether power outages or equipment failures occurred over four years.
comments.request: Report any such incidents.
comments.quote: Line 166: Did you suffer any power outrages or equipment failures during this almost 4 year experiment? If so, what type, how many and how long?

comments.issue: Analytical detection limits are not listed.
comments.request: List detection limits for all elements.
comments.quote: Lines 210-211: List the analytical detection limits for all of the elements.

comments.issue: Ionome and trait comparisons lack statistical significance tests.
comments.request: Add significance tests.
comments.quote: Comparison of ionome and other traits under different N concentrations should include tests for statistical significance.

comments.issue: The Discussion should summarise significant differences for hypotheses 1 and 2 and reflect the constraints.
comments.request: Revise the Discussion accordingly.
comments.quote: Summarize the statistically significant differences pertinent to hypotheses 1 and 2 and revise the Discussion in light of the numerous constraints described above.

title: Current and Historical Resource Nitrogen Supply Affects the Eco‐Physiological Traits and the Ionome of a Diazotrophic Cyanobacterium

study.system: Cedar Creek grassland; 22-yr N addition and soil disturbance experiment

editor_summary: Topic of broad interest, but reviewers doubt the work reaches the level expected for Ecology Letters and see considerable room to improve the presentation; Reviewer 1 also raises analysis concerns, though a careful revision could merit publication.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and potentially valuable study, but the introduction, results logic and discussion need substantial restructuring and correction.
strengths: explores an under-appreciated topic of transient versus post-transient effects

comments.issue: The introduction is not well organized or concise and does not set up the main hypotheses.
comments.request: Restructure the introduction around the scientific questions.
comments.quote: The introduction is not well organized and concise enough, and does not set up the main hypotheses of the paper well.

comments.issue: Too much emphasis on the importance of synchrony, which is already well studied, instead of the study's own novelty.
comments.request: Highlight the novelty of the interacting drivers over transient versus post-transient phases.
comments.quote: Instead, I think the authors should highlight the novelty of their own study, with the interacting effects of nitrogen addition and disturbance on community stability over transient versus post-transient being such one.

comments.issue: The discussion repeats the introduction and results instead of interpreting the findings in depth.
comments.request: Rewrite the discussion to interpret the major findings.
comments.quote: The discussion repeats much information from Introduction and Results instead of interpreting their major findings in-depth.

comments.issue: Some discussion passages are logically incorrect and need revision.
comments.request: Correct the logically incorrect discussion passages.
comments.quote: Besides, the authors make some logically incorrect discussion which should also be revised (see my specific comments below).

comments.issue: The title uses short-term/multi-decadal while the text uses transient/post-transient, and says multiple drivers for only two.
comments.request: Use consistent terms and name the two global change drivers in the title.
comments.quote: I suggest keep the terms consistent in the title and the text. Besides, I think it should specify the two global change drivers (nitrogen addition and disturbance) instead if using “multiple global change drivers”.

comments.issue: The introduction paragraphs are poorly organized, with topic sentences not summarizing their content.
comments.request: Restructure the paragraphs around clear topic sentences.
comments.quote: The paragraphs are not well organized. I suggest the authors make the first sentence as the summary of the content of the paragraph.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the control is 0 g N + micronutrients or 0 g N.
comments.request: Clarify which treatment is the actual control.
comments.quote: In Line 123, the authors wrote that they used the 0 g N + micronutrients as their control, but in Line 136 they wrote that the control is 0 g N. Which one is the actual control? Please clarify.

comments.issue: Seven nitrogen addition levels are claimed but only six are listed.
comments.request: Correct the number of nitrogen levels.
comments.quote: The authors wrote that there were seven levels of N addition, but gave only six levels (1.0, 3.4, 5.4, 9.5, 17.0, 27.2). Please correct.

comments.issue: It is hard to tell from Fig. 2 whether mean biomass or variability increased more in fertilized plots.
comments.request: Use explicit statistics to support the statement.
comments.quote: I find it very hard to tell from Fig.2 whether the mean biomass or the variability increased more in the fertilized plots. I suggest the authors use explicit statistics to support their statement.

comments.issue: Statements about slopes and synchrony-stability relationships do not match the figures, and the referenced periods are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify which figures and periods each statement refers to and correct the described patterns.
comments.quote: Maybe I misinterpret the authors’ statements, but I think the authors should make it very clear which Figures and which periods (transient or post-transient) they are talking about.

comments.issue: The word similarly has no clear referent and the two statement sets are not similar.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the claim of similarity.
comments.quote: Similarly to what? I don’t think there is similarity between the statements in L274-278 and the statements in L279-281.

comments.issue: The paragraph on lines 281-283 lacks the parallel post-transient disturbance-synchrony-stability statement.
comments.request: Add a sentence on the post-transient disturbance-synchrony-stability relationship.
comments.quote: To keep the overall structure of the paragraph consistent, I think the authors should also add a sentence talking about the disturbance-synchrony-stability relationship in the post-transient phase.

comments.issue: The sentence on lines 283-286 does not clearly describe the patterns shown in Fig. 5.
comments.request: Revise to state that disturbance dominates transiently and nitrogen post-transiently.
comments.quote: This sentence is not very clear. Fig. 5 shows that in the transient phase, disturbance had stronger effects on both synchrony and stability than nitrogen addition

comments.issue: The sentence on lines 290-292 interrupts the paragraph flow and is misplaced.
comments.request: Move the sentence ahead of the last sentence.
comments.quote: I find this sentence interrupts the fluency of the paragraph.

comments.issue: The paragraph on lines 301-308 is confused and decomposes synchrony when stability components are discussed.
comments.request: Revise the paragraph to match its stated focus on stability patterns.
comments.quote: I think this whole paragraph is very confused and should be revised.

comments.issue: Saying nitrogen led to compensatory dynamics is inaccurate because mean synchrony is also below one at lower nitrogen levels.
comments.request: Say higher nitrogen led to more compensatory dynamics.
comments.quote: since the mean synchrony is also lower than one in the lower nitrogen levels

comments.issue: Fig. 3B shows roughly equal effects on mean biomass and SD at low nitrogen, not a shift from promoting biomass.
comments.request: Revise the description of the nitrogen effects.
comments.quote: Fig. 3B shows that within the lower ends of nitrogen addition, effects of nitrogen addition on mean total biomass and SD are approximately EQUAL

comments.issue: The early-successional species are not identified.
comments.request: State which species are early-successional.
comments.quote: L323: I was wondering what are the early-successional species?

comments.issue: The link between species replacement and persistent nitrogen versus faded disturbance effects is not interpreted in depth.
comments.request: Interpret how species replacement relates to these effects.
comments.quote: I think the authors should give more in-depth interpretations about how species replacement with time is related to the persistent strong effects of nitrogen addition and the faded effects of disturbance.

comments.issue: The sentence on lines 325-328 is vague about what changes and what remains consistently negative.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant.
comments.quote: Of course both synchrony and stability - as most, if not all, metrics - are subject to change, that is a no-brainer, but the synchrony-stability relationship is consistently negative. I suggest the authors make it more clear about what they mean.

comments.issue: The logic on lines 331-334 is wrong because direct negative effects can make overall effects negative despite positive synchrony-mediated paths.
comments.request: Revise the reasoning about direct and indirect effects.
comments.quote: However, because soil disturbance and nitrogen addition also directly (instead of mediated by synchrony) negatively affect stability, their overall effects on stability can be negative.

comments.issue: Adding 'at low nitrogen levels' is unnecessary because disturbance increased aggregated population variance at all levels.
comments.request: Remove the low-nitrogen qualifier.
comments.quote: What is the necessity to add “at low nitrogen levels” since disturbance increased aggregated population variance at all nitrogen levels (Fig. 3)?

comments.issue: Decoupling at high nitrogen occurred only in disturbed plots, which is not made clear.
comments.request: Make clear that decoupling occurred only in disturbed plots.
comments.quote: Fig. 4 shows that the negative synchrony-stability relationship decoupled at high nitrogen levels ONLY in disturbed plots. Please make this clear.

comments.issue: The decoupling phenomenon referred to on L345 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify which decoupling phenomenon is meant.
comments.quote: L345: Which “decoupling phenomenon”?

comments.issue: The first clause of the sentence on lines 352-354 is irrelevant.
comments.request: Delete the irrelevant clause.
comments.quote: I think the first part of this sentence, i.e., “though the effects of disturbance on all community properties diminished in the post-transient phase”, is irrelevant and should be deleted.

comments.issue: The statement about no effect of disturbance on stability contrasts with the earlier statement on L318-320.
comments.request: Correct the contradiction.
comments.quote: contrasts with that in L318-320 “In the early transient phase, disturbance and nitrogen treatments negatively affected richness, evenness, synchrony, and stability.” Please correct.

comments.issue: The synchrony passages repeat well-established knowledge and add little value.
comments.request: Revise the synchrony passages to add value.
comments.quote: Synchrony has already been included and explored in-depth in numerous ecology studies. These sentences add little value and should be revised.

comments.issue: Direct and indirect effects are treated as if direct effects were dampened by indirect ones, but they are independent paths.
comments.request: Revise the logic on direct versus indirect effects.
comments.quote: The direct effects and indirect effects are two independent paths. Therefore, the direct effects are not dampened by the indirect effects. Please revise.

comments.issue: The statements on lines 366-374 are not supported by Fig. 5.
comments.request: Revise the unsupported statements.
comments.quote: L366-374: These statements are not supported by Fig. 5. Please revise.

comments.issue: Lines 385-406 repeat information from the introduction.
comments.request: Revise to avoid repetition.
comments.quote: L385-406: This sentence is highly repetitive with information in the Introduction. Please consider revising.

comments.issue: The first sentence of the Fig. 1 caption is not an overview of the figure.
comments.request: Rewrite the first caption sentence as an overview.
comments.quote: Fig.1: The first sentence in the figure should be an overview of what is in the figure. Please revise.

comments.issue: The colours for the 17 and 27.2 nitrogen addition levels are hard to distinguish in Figs. 3 and 4.
comments.request: Choose more distinguishable colours.
comments.quote: I find the colors for the 17 and 27.2 nitrogen addition are difficult to distinguish.

comments.issue: A right bracket is missing after '(lower panels' in Fig. 4.
comments.request: Add the missing bracket.
comments.quote: Fig.4: A right bracket is missing following “(lower panels”. Please add it.

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the long-term dataset but finds the writing and logic confusing and raises several methodological concerns that need fixing.
strengths: provides evidence for incorporating synchrony into global change research

comments.issue: The title's phrase multiple global change drivers is inappropriate because only two drivers are studied.
comments.request: Replace 'multiple' in the title.
comments.quote: The terms “multiple global change drivers” in the title is inappropriate, as the study only involves two global change drivers. Typically, “multiple” implies three or more.

comments.issue: The abstract and introduction are confusing, lack logical coherence and fail to highlight key points.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract and introduction for clarity and focus.
