comments.quote: L159, I recommend that viable seed production be mentioned in the abstract.

comments.issue: The specific ecosystem should be named at L285-288.
comments.request: Mention the specific ecosystem.
comments.quote: L285-288, the specific ecosystem shall be mentioned here.

comments.issue: The suggestion at L290-291 implies a comparison among alternative approaches.
comments.quote: L290-291, this suggestion implies a comparison among alternative approaches.

comments.issue: Disagrees that higher-order interactions are unimportant; they exist in theory and reality.
comments.request: Rephrase the higher-order interaction conclusion as conditional on the study system and assumptions.
comments.quote: I actually disagree with this. HOIs shall exist in theory and reality.

comments.issue: Observer effort may affect the outcome at L302.
comments.request: Address whether observation effort influences the results.
comments.quote: L302, can the effort of observations affect the outcome?

title: A Continuum From Positive to Negative Interactions Drives Plant Species' Performance in a Diverse Community

study.system: Brassica rapa plants and Pieris rapae butterflies; temperature experiment

editor_summary: Reviewers praise the work but ask to move critical information from supplement to main text, reduce chemical-trait dimensionality via PCA, address multiple testing, state clear hypotheses, add a trait figure, and acknowledge that only plants experienced the temperature treatments.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by this innovative reciprocal-selection experiment, but asks for clearer presentation of traits and results and notes that differing trait sets make the two temperature models hard to compare.
strengths: impressive work examining both selection partners

comments.issue: Too many critical results and their rationale are relegated to the supplement, making the main text hard to follow.
comments.request: Move essential information into the main manuscript within length limits.
comments.quote: However I did find it tough to wade through the supplementary material and come back to the main text to try to follow the results.

comments.issue: Rationale for the chosen plant and butterfly traits is missing, and too many flower size measures were taken.
comments.request: Explain why these traits were measured and simplify flower size measures.
comments.quote: The brief text also means that much of the reason why things were done are missing from the descriptions. For example, why these plant traits or butterfly traits (and not others?).

comments.issue: A main-text figure showing the plant and butterfly traits and how they change with temperature is missing.
comments.request: Add an introductory figure illustrating measured traits and temperature effects.
comments.quote: It might help to have a first figure of the plant and butterfly with the traits pointed out and maybe the highlight of which changed with the two temperatures?

comments.issue: The focus should be described as microevolutionary patterns of coevolution rather than speciation.
comments.request: Use microevolutionary terminology for the coevolutionary focus.
comments.quote: I think this would be better described as microevolutionary patterns of coevolution since the focus is on natural selection rather than speciation?

comments.issue: The abbreviation GMC is non-intuitive and rarely used, so readers must remember it.
comments.request: Write out 'geographic mosaic of coevolution' instead of GMC.
comments.quote: I found the GMC abbreviation non-intuitive. First, this is also the car company abbreviation and second it is not used frequently in the manuscript

comments.issue: Figure 2 does not explain arrow types or values and does not match the supplementary tables.
comments.request: Explain the arrows, values and model-output links in Figure 2 and its caption.
comments.quote: Figure 2: explain why some arrows are one-way and others are double-headed. I am also not sure what these values represent, they don’t seem to match the supplementary tables of values

comments.issue: Supplemental methods order is confusing and contains a circular cross-reference.
comments.request: Reorder the first supplemental methods sections and remove the circular reference.
comments.quote: I think the order of the first three sections in the supplemental methods should be arranged to have the information about the butterfly and plant populations first.

comments.issue: The paragraph reveals how nectar was collected only at its end, leaving readers wondering.
comments.request: Reorder the paragraph so nectar collection is explained earlier.
comments.quote: This order of the paragraph leaves one wondering how you collected nectar until you get to the end of the paragraph.

comments.issue: Classifying flowering time as a morphology trait is questionable.
comments.request: Reconsider the classification of flowering time.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I would classify flowering time as a morphology trait.

comments.issue: Rationale for traits entering particular models, VIF-based reductions and exclusion of flowering time from butterfly models is unclear.
comments.request: Explain trait inclusion decisions and model reduction criteria in detail.
comments.quote: It would be great to include more details about why the traits were used in particular models. Are the model reductions because of the correlations (VIFs)?

comments.issue: Ambient and hot models include different trait sets, so selection estimates are not directly comparable and differences may reflect trait inclusion.
comments.request: Use a common trait set or otherwise address comparability of selection estimates.
comments.quote: While this follows from the removal of traits using VIFs, it does mean that these models are not directly comparable.

comments.issue: Whether traits were standardized and by which method (variance or mean) is not stated.
comments.request: Report the trait standardization method used.
comments.quote: Were the traits standardized for these models? I would assume so based on the output but please include the method of standardization (eg variance or mean).

comments.issue: The asterisk in Tables S3 and S4 is not explained.
comments.request: Define the asterisk in the table legends.
comments.quote: In Table S3 and S4 * is not explained.

comments.issue: Treatment names are inconsistent, with 'cold' used where 'ambient' is meant.
comments.request: Use 'Ambient' and 'Hot' consistently throughout.
comments.quote: Stick to Ambient and Hot for the treatments (in some places it is cold instead)

reviews.assessment: Impressive experiment, but high trait correlations and non-comparable models raise doubts about whether some reciprocal selection estimates are artefacts.
strengths: well written and delightful to read

comments.issue: The title is too long and slightly dramatic.
comments.request: Shorten the title, e.g. 'Elevated temperature alters reciprocal selection in an experimental plant-pollinator-herbivore system'.
comments.quote: I think, the title is too long and sounds slightly dramatic. I would remove the first part as it is sufficient although not very informative.

comments.issue: Micro- versus macro-evolution terminology is confused (abstract L44-46 and methods L171); selection and coevolution are micro-evolution.
comments.request: Correct the micro/macro-evolution usage throughout.
comments.quote: I regard any sort of selection and co-evolution as micro-evolution, i.e. acting on the level of interacting populations and species.

comments.issue: 'Network of traits' is inappropriate wording.
comments.request: Replace with 'complexity of traits'.
comments.quote: I find “network of traits” inappropriate, perhaps better use “complexity of traits”?

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits (plural forms, grammar, wrong preposition).
comments.quote: This needs to be slightly rephrased, because the grammar does not work when leaving out the brackets from reading.

comments.issue: It is unclear how coevolutionary patterns allow predicting community resilience.
comments.request: Elaborate the link between coevolution and community resilience.
comments.quote: I am not clear how one would predict community resilience from coevolutionary patterns. Could the authors please elaborate?

comments.issue: The manuscript is repeatedly vague; the L118 working hypothesis does not convey what changes or why.
comments.request: Rephrase vague statements, including the hypothesis, more concretely.
comments.quote: I do not think that “somethings changes and that changes something else” is a good working hypothesis.

comments.issue: Final sample size is unclear and no table summarises replicates, trait means or variation.
comments.request: State the final sample size and add a summary table of replicates and trait variation.
comments.quote: I am not clear here about the final sample size of the experiment. Does this mean there are 49 plants the hot and 49 plant in the ambient treatment?

comments.issue: Flower color is missing from the trait listing.
comments.request: Add flower color to the trait list.
comments.quote: L150: Add flower color to the listing.

comments.issue: Only plants, not butterflies, developed under the two temperature regimes, making the experiment incomplete for reciprocal selection.
comments.request: Acknowledge and discuss this design limitation in the main text.
comments.quote: this was included in the experimental design only for the plants side but not for the butterflies

comments.issue: 'Butterfly exposure' wording is confusing in a plant-pollinator context.
comments.request: Replace 'butterfly exposure' throughout the manuscript and supplement.
comments.quote: I find the wording “butterfly exposure” confusing. I assume you refer here to the completed metamorphosis, but in the context of a plant-pollinator interaction experiment this implies to me something about that experimental plants were exposed to pollinators.

comments.issue: The reason for removing larvae is explained only in the supplement, not in the main text.
comments.request: Briefly mention or refer to the larvae-removal rationale in the methods.
comments.quote: Though the reason for larvae removal is explained at another place in the Supplemental n detail, it would be good to briefly mention here as well or refer to the explanation in the Supplement.

comments.issue: Fruit set values greater than 1 are confusing and may be measurement errors.
comments.request: Clarify how fruit set can exceed 1.
comments.quote: I am confused how fruit set can be > 1? Are this perhaps measurement errors?

comments.issue: The VIF threshold of 5 is too high and reciprocal selection estimates may be artefacts of correlated traits.
comments.request: Lower the VIF threshold and report trait correlations.
comments.quote: I find VIF > 5 is relatively high chosen. Most literature suggest 2-4 is acceptable, why higher 5 clearly indicated warrant and further investigation.

comments.issue: An interpretive statement appears in the results and belongs in the discussion.
comments.request: Move the statement to the discussion.
comments.quote: This statement seems interpretation of results to me and might appear only in the discussion (where it is repeated already).

comments.issue: The expected direction of the nectar-volume effect is unclear; lower volumes should deepen contact for short-tongued butterflies.
comments.request: Explain the direction of the nectar-volume effect.
comments.quote: Would not the opposite be expected as lower volumes would force the butterflies with shorter tongues to delve deeper improving the physical contact between butterfly and flower?

comments.issue: Reduced selection on nectar may reflect shifted trait ranges, higher fitness or lack of nectar variation.
comments.request: Consider these alternative explanations for weakened selection.
comments.quote: I wonder if reduced selection involving nectar amounts is because of a lack of variation in nectar among plants.

comments.issue: The discussion order does not follow the sequence of species interactions.
comments.request: Reorder the discussion accordingly.
comments.quote: L438: I suggest to reorder to follow the sequence of how species interact.

comments.issue: The interpretation confuses corolla tube depth with nectar amount.
comments.request: Correct the tube-depth/nectar-amount confusion in the main text.
comments.quote: I think, this interpretation confuses tube depths with nectar amount. The authors correct this in the Supplemental material.

comments.issue: An acknowledged person lacks a surname, or prefers not to be named.
comments.request: Clarify the acknowledgment.
comments.quote: L512: Does this person has a last name or does she not want to be recognized for her support?

comments.issue: The shift from tongue length to wing size may be an artefact of non-random butterfly sampling and follow-up analysis.
comments.request: Show that the selection shift is not a sampling artefact.
comments.quote: Might this be an artefact of "non-random" butterfly sampling and follow-up analysis?

comments.issue: A passage repeats material already given in the supplemental methods.
comments.request: Remove the redundant passage.
comments.quote: L87: Remove as this is already the Supplemental method.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether a described item appears above or below in the supplement.
comments.request: Fix the ordering of this description.
comments.quote: Maybe I missed it, but I don’t think it was described above. I believe what you are referring to here is coming below?

comments.issue: Selection analyses use different numbers of traits per environment, making reciprocal selection estimates non-comparable.
comments.request: Analyse a common trait set across environments.
comments.quote: I dislike the fact that selection analysis in the two environments was done including different numbers of traits. In my opinion, this makes the estimates of reciprocal selection not comparable between treatments.

comments.issue: A published framework for analysing selection on floral volatiles (Opedal et al.) is not used.
comments.request: Consider the Opedal et al. approach for selection on volatiles.
comments.quote: L204: As a general comment perhaps use the approach of Opedahl for analysis of selection on volatiles?

comments.issue: Butterflies were not reared in two environments, so it is unclear whether they were drawn randomly from one source pool.
comments.request: Clarify butterfly sampling and assignment.
comments.quote: But as I understand, butterflies were not reared in two different environments, so this suggests butterflies were not randomly drawn from the same source pool?

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic about the novel interaction-gradient approach and clear temperature result, but replication, standardization and multiple-testing concerns temper confidence.
strengths: novel approach estimating interaction gradients in both taxa
important and novel result on reciprocal selection changes

comments.issue: The introduction omits a general explanation of how plastic shifts in an abiotic parameter alter reciprocal selection.
comments.request: Add a general explanation of plasticity-driven shifts in the selection landscape.
comments.quote: I do wonder if it would be helpful to some readers to offer another line or two explanation of (generally) how shifts in an abiotic parameter, through plasticity, might affect reciprocal selection.

comments.issue: The commercial Brassica source lacks population-of-origin and historical information, limiting relevance.
comments.quote: the lack of information on population of origin and historical context limits a lot of the relevance of the study

comments.issue: Much critical supporting information and analyses sit in the supplement, weakening the main text.
comments.request: Move essential supporting information into the main text.
comments.quote: there is SO much here that is critical to the story and understanding and evaluating the data in the main text

comments.issue: Replication of the temperature treatments could not be tracked; lack of treatment replication would be a serious design flaw.
comments.request: Clarify the replication structure of the temperature treatments.
comments.quote: If there is not replication of the temperature treatments, then I think we have a more serious design issue.

comments.issue: Trait standardization for the non-linear selection gradients is described only briefly and unclearly.
comments.request: Describe exactly how traits were centered and scaled.
comments.quote: I found mention of standardization on l 259-260, but nowhere else. I think this need to be more specific (what is “centered and scaled”? to what?).

comments.issue: Standardized selection gradients near or above 1 are implausibly high, suggesting a standardization problem.
comments.request: Check and correct the standardization underlying the reported betas.
comments.quote: many of the values of the betas (which would be standardized gradients in units of standard deviation if standardization were done right) reported in supplemental are extremely high

comments.issue: Over 100 simultaneous tests inflate false positives; P<0.05 betas may not survive correction.
comments.request: Apply a false-discovery correction and reassess the narrative.
comments.quote: I am concerned about the staggering number of statistical tests on selection gradients (over 100 in Table S8 alone!).

comments.issue: Treating many compounds as individual traits makes the dimensionality unwieldy and gradients hard to trust.
comments.request: Reduce chemistry dimensionality, e.g. with PCA.
comments.quote: the large number of compounds treated as individual traits makes the dimensionality of the analysis unwieldy and contributes to the lack of confidence in any one gradient

comments.issue: Fitness axes in F3 and F4 use different scales, making panels hard to compare.
comments.request: Standardize the fitness axis across panels.
comments.quote: the fitness axis in F3 and F4 should be standardized – it is difficult to interpret with the scales of the surface so different in the different panels

comments.issue: F3 surfaces of the same traits are rotated 180°, making plant-butterfly comparisons misleading.
comments.request: Orient the surfaces consistently.
comments.quote: in F3 the surfaces of the same traits are oriented 180º different making comparisons misleading between plant and butterfly fitness

comments.issue: The rationale for which fitness surfaces appear in F3 and F4 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how surfaces were chosen for F3 and F4.
comments.quote: What is the logic behind which surfaces are presented in F3 and F4?

comments.issue: The discussion is sparse on the changing trait networks and sign changes in reciprocal selection.
comments.request: Expand discussion of temperature-induced changes, including sign changes.
comments.quote: not much discussion of the nuance of the changing networks of interacting traits, or the fact that not only does reciprocal selection change from weak to strong, but sometimes in the sign of interaction

comments.issue: Specific compounds are analysed without biochemical rationale or motivation for why they should matter.
comments.request: Justify compound selection with biochemical understanding.
comments.quote: Instead there just seems to be a shotgun approach that limits the interpretability of the data set.

comments.issue: The number of trait and trait-combination tests approaches or exceeds the number of individuals assayed.
comments.request: Reduce the number of tests relative to sample size.
comments.quote: the data set approaches being overleveraged, with more tests than individuals!

title: Elevated Temperature Diminishes Reciprocal Selection in an Experimental Plant‐Pollinator‐Herbivore System

study.system: plant-frugivore interaction networks; 354 networks, global

editor_summary: Editor finds the synthesis timely with a large dataset but not publishable as is: clarify hypothesis-method links, add methodological checks (spatial autocorrelation, imputation, randomisation), expand discussion of mechanisms, and report percentiles and weighted metrics.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and interesting patterns, but the discussion of underlying processes is vague and the metric captures only part of the picture.
strengths: interesting patterns that challenge classical hypotheses
liked the general setting of the study

comments.issue: No explicit discussion of which eco-evolutionary processes are consistent with the observed patterns.
comments.request: Discuss which processes fit or contradict the observed geographical patterns.
comments.quote: Potential eco-evolutionary processes are discussed, but an explicit discussion about what processes are consistent (and which of the ones previously hypothesized are not) with the observed patterns is missing.

comments.issue: The mean trait dissimilarity alone cannot distinguish very different matching distributions.
comments.request: Use other moments of the matching distribution, such as 10, 50 and 90% percentiles.
comments.quote: The mean alone (even if standardized) may not be enough to inform about trait matching patterns, because the same mean value can be obtained for very different distributions of trait matching

comments.issue: The weighted dissimilarity metric available for a subset was not analysed.
comments.request: Repeat the analysis using the frequency-weighted metric to reinforce and extend the results.
comments.quote: Why not repeating the analysis using this metric? It would not only reinforce the conclusions, but also provide extra insights useful for interpretation.

comments.issue: Direction of the effects is not actually reported at L38-40.
comments.request: Report the direction of the effects.
comments.quote: It would be better to actually report the direction of the effects.

comments.issue: Fruit diet prevalence is not identified as a measure of trophic specialization.
comments.request: Make explicit that this measure reflects trophic specialization.
comments.quote: When first reading this, I did not realize that this is actually a measure of “trophic specialization” (isn’t it?). I suggest you make this explicit in this paragraph.

comments.issue: No justification for using beak width instead of gape size.
comments.request: Add a brief justification for the beak width choice.
comments.quote: Why do you use the beak width and not gape size, as in many other trait matching studies?

comments.issue: L160: temperate may be a typo for temperature.
comments.request: Correct the word if it is a typo.
comments.quote: L160. Should “temperate” be temperature?

comments.issue: Source of fruit diet prevalence values is unclear (Wilman database or field data).
comments.request: State whether these are database or field values.
comments.quote: this is the mean value of the Wilman data, right? Or did you have field data from the network studies?

comments.issue: Meaning of swallowing fruits in different directions is unclear.
comments.request: Explain this statement.
comments.quote: What do you mean by “as birds can swallow fruits in different directions”?

comments.issue: Sentence at L203 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence.
comments.quote: L203. Unclear – can you clarify the sentence?

comments.issue: Last sentence of the paragraph at L323-325 breaks the flow.
comments.request: Delete the sentence.
comments.quote: This last sentence seems a bit out of place, breaking the flow of the discussion. I suggest you delete it.

comments.issue: Missing "that" at L326 and "corresponding biotic factors" is unclear.
comments.request: Add "that" and clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: Add “that” in “We found *that*”. In addition, what do you mean by “corresponding biotic factors”?

comments.issue: Higher matching at northern latitudes might indicate selection on beak morphology, not weak plant selection.
comments.request: Consider this alternative selection-pressure explanation.
comments.quote: in more northern latitudes, where there are less fleshy-fruited plants, the higher trait matching might indicate a selection pressure on beak morphology

comments.issue: Discussion at L346-347 is general and offers no new insight.
comments.request: Use this space to expand on eco-evolutionary processes.
comments.quote: I think the discussion in this paragraph is a bit general and does not really offer a new insight.

comments.issue: Conclusion at L366-367 is too strong given the speculative discussion.
comments.request: Relate the results more explicitly to mechanistic explanations.
comments.quote: this conclusion reads rather strong given the rather speculative discussion

reviews.assessment: Well-written and novel global study, though the latitudinal conclusion and several methods need strengthening.
strengths: first global test based on whole-community interaction data

comments.issue: Some predictions, especially those on abiotic factors, lack detail.
comments.request: Add more detail to the abiotic predictions.
comments.quote: I felt that there could be a little more detail for some of the predictions, specifically related to abiotic factors

comments.issue: It is unknown whether trait data show a geographical pattern matching the island generalist assumption.
comments.request: Check whether plant or bird trait data show such a geographical pattern.
comments.quote: I wondered whether the available trait data for plants or birds showed any geographical pattern that might match this assumption

comments.issue: Phylogenetic signal was apparently not tested before phylogenetic imputation of fruit length.
comments.request: Report the phylogenetic signal test and imputation performance checks.
comments.quote: Applying a phylogenetic imputation method assumes a phylogenetic signal in the trait of interest. I wondered if the authors formally tested for a phylogenetic signal in fruit length prior to the imputation.

comments.issue: Plant trait coverage per network is not reported and could bias results.
comments.request: Report trait coverage and consider it as a covariate.
comments.quote: I wondered what the trait coverage for plant species in each network was and if it could be helpful to include the percentage of plant trait coverage as a covariate in the models

comments.issue: Random network numbers and standardization directions are inconsistent between modularity and dissimilarity calculations.
comments.request: Explain the differences or correct them, and present the formulas.
comments.quote: if the approaches were indeed different between calculating standardized modularity and mean dissimilarity, please briefly explain why. If not, please correct it in the text.

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation in model residuals was not tested or accounted for.
comments.request: Test for spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I) and account for spatial biases.
comments.quote: Since the dataset has a spatial component, I suggest testing for spatial autocorrelation in model residuals (with Moran’s I statistic)/ accounting for potential spatial biases in the models.

comments.issue: The latitudinal relationship looks weak and variable, so rejecting Wallace's assumption is not convincing.
comments.request: Test whether latitude matters beyond insularity and the biotic factors.
comments.quote: I am not 100% convinced the authors can reject Wallace’s assumption based on their findings.

comments.issue: Where high fruit diet prevalence and low fleshy-fruited prevalence co-occur is not described.
comments.request: Describe the ecosystems and biogeographical conditions where these conditions co-occur.
comments.quote: it might be nice to mention where high fruit diet prevalence and low fleshy-fruited species prevalence co-occur

comments.issue: Discussion implies an interaction between the two prevalence predictors that the models do not test.
comments.request: Clarify whether the effects are independent or test their interaction.
comments.quote: in the mixed-effect models, the authors do not test for an interaction effect of these predictors

comments.issue: Average beak size as a driver of trait matching through beak width constraints is not considered.
comments.request: Consider whether average beak size relates to trait matching strength.
comments.quote: whether average beak size in a network would be a biotic factor that could be related to trait matching strength

comments.issue: Multiple line-level wording corrections suggested throughout.
comments.quote: L 329 and elsewhere in the manuscript: “interactive pairs” sounds a little bit strange to me.

comments.issue: Number of weighted networks in the dataset is not reported.
comments.request: Report how many networks were weighted.
comments.quote: How many networks in your dataset were weighted?

comments.issue: Results text reports p-values without model estimates, standard errors and t-values.
comments.request: Report estimates, standard errors and t-values for the main relationships.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to provide the model estimates, standard errors, and t-values along with the p-values for the main relationships in the results text.

reviews.assessment: Enjoyed the study; hypotheses, methods description and discussion need restructuring and clearer links.
strengths: novel assessment across large spatial scales

comments.issue: Hypotheses do not mirror the model structure; why three different approaches were used is unclear.
comments.request: Align hypotheses with the models and explain why the different approaches were used.
comments.quote: Part of the problem resides on the fact that it’s not completely clear why three different methodological approaches were conducted to test the hypotheses

comments.issue: Only significant variables were used in the SEM but this step is not stated in the Methods.
comments.request: State this methodological step clearly and list all direct and indirect paths.
comments.quote: only after checking the code provided by the authors I could confirm that only significant variables were used in the SEM

comments.issue: Figure S5 does not show all variables included in the SEM.
comments.request: Show all SEM variables and paths in Figure S5.
comments.quote: Fig. S5 should show all the Variables that were included in the SEM

comments.issue: Results contradicting previous studies are not discussed mechanistically.
comments.request: Explore why the latitudinal results differ from previous studies such as McFadden et al. 2022.
comments.quote: I feel that the authors should explore more why the latitudinal results found here were contrary to those published by previous studies

comments.issue: Darwin and Wallace do not belong in the title as their ideas concern interaction strength.
comments.request: Remove Darwin and Wallace from the title.
comments.quote: I would not include this in the title. Both Darwin and Wallace ideas refer more to “interaction strength’ than to “trait matching”, which is what you actually measured (and tested) in this ms.

comments.issue: The abstract's last sentence is not the main conclusion; poorly matched interactions can also be strong.
comments.request: Focus the abstract conclusion on the actual findings.
comments.quote: I don’t believe this is the main conclusion of your manuscript. Its true that trait matching can indicate interaction frequency (strength), but poorly-matched interactions can also have a high strength.

comments.issue: Multiple line-level wording and copy edits suggested.
comments.quote: This sentence could be improved. Maybe something like: “The matching between beak size and fruit size was significantly stronger towards higher latitudes and on islands”.

comments.issue: Why the point at L55 remains unclear is not explained.
comments.request: State the reason it remains unclear.
comments.quote: why does it remain unclear? Is it because of the relatively low number of studies, methodological issues, or some other factor?

comments.issue: What "more simplified" means at L77 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning of more simplified.
comments.quote: Line 77: more simplified in what sense?

comments.issue: "Prevalence" implies a high proportion and misnames the variables.
comments.request: Rename the variables proportion of frugivory and proportion of fleshy-fruited species.
comments.quote: I’d instead call these variables “proportion of frugivory” and “proportion of fleshy-fruited species”.

comments.issue: An alternative explanation for the food-choice pattern (lower pressure when food is ample) is not considered.
comments.request: Discuss this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Alternatively, when there is ample food choice, the “pressure” for selecting the most profitable fruit available might be lower

comments.issue: Modularity is a network property, not a driver, and trait matching may cause modularity rather than the reverse.
comments.request: Justify modularity's inclusion in the SEM or remove it.
comments.quote: I don’t fully understand why modularity was included in the analyses. Modularity is not a biotic or abiotic factor (but rather a structural property of networks)

comments.issue: Beak width data mix sources and measurement methods.
comments.request: Use AVONET beak width data consistently across all networks.
comments.quote: I suggest the authors to be consistent and use beak width data from Avonet for all of their networks

comments.issue: Spatial resolution of climate data and extraction method are not described.
comments.request: Report the resolution and whether values come from a cell or buffer.
comments.quote: What is the resolution of these data? Did you retrieve bioclimatic values from the cell where the network was located, or did you generate a buffer zone around each network site?

comments.issue: Fleshy-fruited species prevalence is calculated at a much larger scale than the network data.
comments.request: Make the scale mismatch and its limitations clear throughout.
comments.quote: The authors should make clear throughout the manuscript that prevalence of fleshy-fruited species was calculated at a much larger scale when compared to the network data

comments.issue: Botanical countries are unfamiliar to many readers.
comments.request: Add a supplementary map showing network sites within botanical countries.
comments.quote: A map in the supplements showing the network sites in their respective botanical countries would help readers to get a sense of the distribution of your data.

comments.issue: How interactions were assigned in each trait-matching scenario is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the scenario attribution rules.
comments.quote: It’s not clear how interactions were attributed to the combinations that are not described in each trait-matching pattern scenario.

comments.issue: It is unknown whether the matching metric depends on gulper versus masher handling assumptions.
comments.request: Test whether the metric changes under all-gulper or all-masher assumptions.
comments.quote: it’d be interesting to know how your trait matching metric changes (or not) depending on whether you assume that all species in your dataset are gulpers or mashers

comments.issue: Text does not mention that the binary metric captures forbidden links while the weighted one may capture fruit selection.
comments.request: Add this clarification.
comments.quote: I'd also mention here that the binary metric only captures forbidden links, whereas the weighted measure may also capture "fruit selection".

comments.issue: Text switches from trait dissimilarity to trait matching strength without explaining the transformation.
comments.request: Explain how mismatching was converted to matching strength.
comments.quote: The metric you described so far measures trait dissimilarity (i.e., trait mismatching), but here you refer to trait matching strength. How did you transform trait mismatching into trait matching strength?

comments.issue: Sentence at L234-238 is too long and confusing.
comments.request: Break up and clarify the sentence.
comments.quote: this sentence is too big and quite confusing

comments.issue: Values at L245-247 are not shown in the supplements.
comments.request: Show these values in the supplements.
comments.quote: Please show these values in the Supplements.

comments.issue: Sentence at L280-281 does not match Figure 4 coefficients.
comments.request: Correct the sentence to match the figure.
comments.quote: This sentence does not seem to match what is being shown in Figure 4.

comments.issue: Statement at L288-289 is questionable given the cited literature.
comments.request: Check the statement against the cited study.
comments.quote: I’m not sure if this is true (see, for example, doi: 10.1126/science.adj1856)

comments.issue: Sentence at L294-295 is vague.
comments.request: Make the sentence more specific.
comments.quote: Lines 294-295: This sentence seems quite vague.

comments.issue: Network diffuseness does not explain why matching is weaker in the tropics.
comments.request: Offer mechanisms other than diffuseness for the observed pattern.
comments.quote: Even if plant-frugivore networks are relatively diffuse, you could still expect trait matching to be stronger in the tropics when compared to the poles.

comments.issue: Associating low competition with fleshy-fruited prevalence ignores the scale mismatch.
comments.request: Be more careful with this association.
comments.quote: I’d be careful when associating “low competition” and the prevalence of fleshy-fruited species.

comments.issue: Competition may also prevent birds from consuming the best-matched fruits.

comments.quote: Note that competition for resources may also lead species to not consume the best-matched fruits available

comments.issue: The frugivory dependence argument deserves more emphasis than direct competition.

comments.quote: This sounds like a stronger argument for the effect of frugivory than the direct competition between bird species

comments.issue: Figure 4 omits non-significant paths.

comments.quote: You should also show the non-significant paths in Figure 4 (maybe as dashed arrows).

comments.issue: Model selection table is not provided in the supplements.
comments.request: Add the model selection table including predictors of best-fitting models.
comments.quote: Consider adding the model selection table in the Supplements.

comments.issue: No correlation plot between trait mismatching and interaction frequency per network.

comments.quote: You could add here a correlation plot between trait mismatching and interaction frequency for each network.

comments.issue: Some estimates appear to be missing from Table S1.
comments.request: Complete the missing estimates.
comments.quote: Table S1: Some estimates seem to be missing.

title: Weaker Plant‐Frugivore Trait Matching Towards the Tropics and on Islands

study.system: plant disease; global database of 4339 populations

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers see merit but raise considerable concerns about methods and analyses, and recommends additional analyses to clarify validity and context.

reviews.assessment: Serious data-distribution and methods-reporting limitations, and conclusions about warming need to be more cautious.
strengths: good discussion of thermal performance curves

comments.issue: Wild and agricultural data come from different climate distributions, confounding the wild/agricultural comparison.
comments.request: Re-analyse a subset with similar historical climates.
comments.quote: there are unequal distributions of data from wild and agricultural systems from both historical and contemporaneous climate

comments.issue: Types of parasites and pests included are not described (soil-borne vs foliar, taxa, orders).
comments.request: Describe the parasite and pest categories in detail.
comments.quote: Not enough information is provided about types of parasites and pests included in the analyses

comments.issue: How pests were surveyed, identified and enumerated is not described.
comments.request: Briefly describe pest survey methods.
comments.quote: please provide a brief description of how pests were typically surveyed/identified/enumerated in the included studies

comments.issue: Specific combinations of search terms are not reported.
comments.request: Provide the search terms, e.g. in the supplement.
comments.quote: I would also like to see more details on the specific combinations of search terms queried (this could be added to the supplement)

comments.issue: Criteria for underrepresentation and the decision not to search Canada, Russia and Eastern Europe are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain these criteria and search decisions.
comments.quote: what criteria were used to determine that a geographic region was underrepresented? From the map in Fig. 1, it appears that Canada, Russia, and Eastern Europe are also lacking in study representation

comments.issue: Abstract's warming-disease conclusion ignores non-linear thermal performance curves.
comments.request: Qualify the conclusion and note the need for experimental data.
comments.quote: the overall conclusions of the paper should be more cautious in stating the predicted directional response of disease to increasing temperature

comments.issue: Potential biological mechanisms behind the results are not explained.
comments.request: Discuss mechanisms, e.g. heat stress effects on disease resistance.
comments.quote: I would like to see more explanation of potential biological mechanisms underlying the results

comments.issue: The paper's 'incidence' definition matches what others call 'prevalence'.
comments.request: Provide a citation for the incidence definition used.
comments.quote: the definition of incidence you are using (number infected divided by number total plants surveyed) is the same as what many disease ecologists call “prevalence.”

comments.issue: Figure 1 needs better colour contrast, a y-axis break and handling of overlapping points.
comments.request: Improve the colour scheme, rescale and declutter the map.
comments.quote: More contrast between blue and green colours is needed

comments.issue: Figure 2 lacks labelled arrows indicating more/less disease risk.
comments.request: Add labelled arrows under the x-axis.
comments.quote: I suggest adding arrows pointing to right and left under x-axis that are labelled “more disease risk” (right arrow) and “less disease risk” (left arrow)

reviews.assessment: Important, novel topic, but the climate variable is poorly justified and annual averages confound seasonality with warming.

comments.issue: Use of annual average temperature as historical climate is poorly justified.
comments.request: Justify or replace the annual-average climate variable.
comments.quote: I found the calculation of the climate variable was poorly justified and the use of annual averages made the interpretation of the results confusing

comments.issue: Historical weather from the study period was not extracted, so seasonality cannot be separated from warming.
comments.request: Extract study-period weather to test temperature anomalies.
comments.quote: the authors did not extract historical weather data from the study period to be able to correlate disease incidence with temperature anomalies

comments.issue: 'Historical climate' is confusing; the variable represents seasonality or climate zones.
comments.request: Use a different term for this variable.
comments.quote: Throughout the manuscript I found the language “historical climate” confusing. Because this variable is attempting to represent seasonality/climate zones I would chose a different word to represent it

comments.issue: Abstract does not explain what the historical climate variable represents.
comments.request: Specify its meaning in the abstract.
comments.quote: I would at least specify in the abstract what this historical climate variable means.

comments.issue: Introduction does not describe the climate-plant disease literature being built on.
comments.request: Add the relevant literature background.
comments.quote: I feel the introduction is missing a description of the climate/plant disease literature that this study is building on.

comments.issue: A citation is missing at Lines 70-72.
comments.request: Add the citation.
comments.quote: Line 70-72: Add citation

comments.issue: Search-string details are missing.
comments.request: Provide the word combinations used in the search.
comments.quote: Line 130: Provide more details about the search string, what were the combinations of words

comments.issue: Whether wild-plant studies were conducted within the species' native range is unknown.
comments.request: Clarify whether studies are within native ranges.
comments.quote: Line 155: I’m curious if the studies evaluating wild plants are conducted within the plants native range?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether study area size affects the precipitation calculation.
comments.request: Clarify how precipitation was calculated.
comments.quote: Was the area evaluated considered in the calculation of precipitation? If not, it seems studies with larger ranges might have artificially higher rainfall

comments.issue: Analysis on L223 is flawed because historical data are annual averages and seasonality varies haphazardly.
comments.request: Replace with an analysis of within-window historical vs current differences.
comments.quote: This analysis does not make sense to me given that the historical data is an annual average

comments.issue: No model outputs or tables are provided for any analysis.
comments.request: Report model outputs for all analyses.
comments.quote: There are no model outputs included in the text for any results. I also don’t see any tables outlining the model outputs

comments.issue: Figure 1 legend lacks units (degrees Celsius).
comments.request: Add degrees Celsius to the figure legend.
comments.quote: Fig 1. Add degrees Celsius to the figure legend.

comments.issue: Overlapping points reduce Figure 1 readability.
comments.request: Shrink the point size.
comments.quote: the overlapping of the points decreases the readability. Just shrinking the size of the points might help?

comments.issue: Unclear whether Figure 3 shows the full dataset or the 10-90% quantile subset.
comments.request: Clarify the subset and justify the quantiles.
comments.quote: I am confused if they represent a subset of the data within the 10 and 90% quantiles. The sample sizes at the top seem to indicate that this reflects the whole data set

comments.issue: Blue colours in Figure 3c are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Use more distinguishable colours.
comments.quote: Panel 3c: These blue colors are difficult to differentiate.

comments.issue: Supplementary figures are numbered out of order (S6 appears before S3-S5).
comments.request: Renumber figures in order of appearance.
comments.quote: Make sure figures are number in the order they appear in the text – it seems S6 appears before S3, 4 and 5

comments.issue: 'Synergistic effects' on L260 are not specified.
comments.request: Specify what the synergistic effects are.
comments.quote: Line 260: Specify what the synergistic effects are.

comments.issue: How the odds ratio was calculated is not described.
comments.request: Add the odds ratio calculation to the methods.
comments.quote: Line 273: How was the odds ratio calculated? I would add this to the methods.

comments.issue: Figures already shown in Results are re-cited in the Discussion.
comments.request: Remove figure references from the Discussion.
comments.quote: It is typically not standard practice to cite figures that have already been presented in the results section in the discussion. I would recommend removing the figure references from the discussion

comments.issue: Wording 'agricultural plants from warm climates' suggests origin rather than growth location.
comments.request: Say 'agricultural plants grown in warm climates'.
comments.quote: I think the language here “agricultural plants from warm climates” is a bit confusing because it seems like it’s referencing the climate where the plant originated rather than where it was observed growing

comments.issue: Paragraph on warming effects goes beyond what the study evaluated.
comments.request: Add the anomaly analysis or caveat that warming was not tested.
comments.quote: This paragraph focuses a lot on the effects of warming, which is not what was evaluated in the paper

comments.issue: Information on L411 belongs in the methods.
comments.request: Move this information to the methods.
comments.quote: Line 411: I would move this information to the methods

comments.issue: Claims about 'novel' weather are not tested.
comments.request: Avoid or qualify novel-weather claims.
comments.quote: Again I would be wary about making claims about ‘novel’ weather when that was not tested in this study

comments.issue: Distinct temperate-climate patterns deserve more discussion.
comments.request: Comment on warming magnitude in temperate regions versus tropical sensitivity.
comments.quote: Given the authors found distinct patterns for temperate climates, I think it would be worth commenting on this more in the discussion

reviews.assessment: Well-written and valuable comparison of wild and agricultural disease systems, but pathogen-type confounding and missing statistics need clarification.
strengths: important topic in plant ecology and global change biology

comments.issue: Wild data come from only 17 studies, dominated by two systems, and group composition is unclear.
comments.request: Show which pathogen types fall in each climate group.
comments.quote: the wild populations come from just 17 studies. Looking at table S1, this is strongly dominated by two studies

comments.issue: Distribution of viruses versus parasites across temperature is not visible.
comments.request: Colour-code Figure S2 points by pathogen type.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to color code the points in Fig S2 so the reader could see the distribution of viruses vs parasites with regard to temperature?

comments.issue: Pathogen type is confounded with climate adaptation; the interaction was not tested.
comments.request: Test the pathogen type x climate interaction and temper the mismatch interpretation.
comments.quote: if there is an issue of cold-adapted vs warm-adapted natural plant pathogens being confounded with pathogen type, then more caution is needed with the interpretation of thermal mismatch

comments.issue: Model fit and overdispersion are not reported; model statements are not given in the supplement.
comments.request: Report model statistics, fit and overdispersion handling.
comments.quote: It is unclear how well the models actually fit the data, if there was over-dispersion, and if so, how it was delt with

comments.issue: 'Eukaryotic parasite' category is not defined (fungi or oomycetes?).
comments.request: Specify which groups it includes.
comments.quote: Line 190: By ‘eukaryotic parasite’ does this mean fungi or oomycetes? Or were there additional eukaryotic parasites beyond these two groups?

comments.issue: Table S1 lacks host and pathogen species identities and growth forms.
comments.request: Add species names to Table S1.
comments.quote: It would be nice if table S1 also included the host and pathogen species in addition to their higher order classification

comments.issue: It is unclear why pests are included and what counts as a pest.
comments.request: Define what counts as a pest.
comments.quote: It seems strange that pests are included in this study (and if they are, that there are not more studies as there have been lots and lots of herbivory studies in natural populations). What counts as a ‘pest’?

comments.issue: Paragraph from L200 is in present tense while the rest is past.
comments.request: Make the tense consistent.
comments.quote: The paragraph starting on line 200 is partially written in the present tense, while the rest of the document is written in the past

title: Impacts of Weather Anomalies and Climate on Plant Disease

study.system: subarctic mountain birch forest; girdling and litter decomposition over 4 years

editor_summary: Both reviewers positive; make use of their suggestions with a thorough rebuttal; the editor does not favour Referee 1's proposed change in story line.

reviews.assessment: Praises the sound design and clear writing, but asks for nuance in interpretation and clarification of methods.
strengths: high relevance for ecology and ecosystem functioning
clear results and right level of information

comments.issue: Root and leaf litter differ in species composition and bag placement, which could explain their contrasting responses.
comments.request: Discuss these litter-type differences and their effects.
comments.quote: Firstly, the leaf litter that was collected is solely containing mountain birch leaves while the root litter contains 4 plant species, including understory species.

comments.issue: Equating lower decomposition with higher soil carbon accumulation is an oversimplification.
comments.request: Add nuance to the soil carbon accumulation statement.
comments.quote: This suggests that lower decomposition = higher soil carbon accumulation. However, the linkages between litter decomposition and carbon accumulation are not that clear (ref 2).

comments.issue: Ectomycorrhizal fungi were central to the hypotheses, yet their abundance in bags was under 1% and the discussion is very short.
comments.request: Expand discussion of the low ectomycorrhizal abundance and its implications.
comments.quote: Yet, the results do not really confirm this, as the relative abundance of ectomycorrhizal fungi was very low (<1%) in the litter bags.

comments.issue: Whether the mountain birch stands are pure or mixed with other tree species is not stated.
comments.request: State whether the stands are pure birch or mixed.
comments.quote: Mountain birch stands: are they pure birch stands or mixed with other tree species?

comments.issue: How many stands provided the litter and whether it was pooled and homogenized is unclear.
comments.request: Report the number of stands and the pooling procedure.
comments.quote: Leaf and root litter was collected from the study area: from how many stands? Was everything pooled together and homogenized?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether distance to trees was considered in the 20 m plot design.
comments.request: State whether distance to trees was taken into account.
comments.quote: 20 m diameter plot: is the distance to tree taken into account in the design?

comments.issue: The number of replicate litter bags per plot is contradictory (4 versus 16 bags).
comments.request: Clarify the correct number of replicate bags per plot.
comments.quote: Confusion about number of replicates: first on page 8 ‘two root and two leaf litter bags in each of these paired plots’ (=total of 4 bags per plot)

comments.issue: The number of pairs retrieved on August 10, 2022 is not reported.
comments.request: Report how many pairs were retrieved on August 10, 2022.
comments.quote: On August 10, 2022, how many pairs were retrieved?

comments.issue: No schematic of the experimental plots and litter bag locations is provided.
comments.request: Add a schematic overview of plots and litter bag locations.
comments.quote: Recommendation: adding a schematic overview of the experimental plots and litter bag location.

comments.issue: Retrieval dates are not converted into the number of months used later in the manuscript.
comments.request: Add the corresponding number of months to retrieval dates.
comments.quote: Dates of litter bag retrieval: can you add the corresponding number of months? This is what is used later in the manuscript.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether litter was weighed before or after freeze-drying.
comments.request: State when litter was weighed.
comments.quote: Not clear if the litter was weighed after freeze-drying or before.

comments.issue: Soil type, pH and soil organic matter are not reported.
comments.request: Provide soil type, pH and SOM information.
comments.quote: No info on soil type, pH, SOM

comments.issue: It is not stated explicitly that birch is an ectomycorrhizal tree.
comments.request: State that birch is an ECM tree.
comments.quote: It should be explicitly stated that birch is an ECM tree.

comments.issue: Figure 5 has an x axis but no y axis and does not clearly support the findings.
comments.request: Clarify what Figure 5 represents and revise it to support the findings.
comments.quote: There is an x axis but no y axis. What is this representing? This conceptual figure is not supporting the findings very clearly.

reviews.assessment: Positive about the timely experiment, but recommends reframing the story around tree removal and revising figures.

comments.issue: The storyline focuses on tree effects although the treatment removes belowground tree carbon allocation; the title and 'forest expansion' term should change.
comments.request: Revise the storyline and Figure 5 around tree removal/mortality.
comments.quote: I strongly recommend revising the storyline (including Figure 5) to focus on the effects of tree removal/mortality on decomposition.

comments.issue: Statistical models lack details and quality checks, such as misfit and outlier diagnostics.
comments.request: Provide complete scripts and summary model outputs.
comments.quote: The manuscript and supplements lack sufficient details on the statistical models and quality checks. The authors should provide the complete scripts along with summary outputs.

comments.issue: Calendar dates are less clear than decomposition duration on the x-axis; degree days could account for climate variability.
comments.request: Use decomposition duration or degree days on the x-axis.
comments.quote: I would suggest using the decomposition duration as the x-axis rather than the calendar date for clarity.

comments.issue: Table 1 is busy and largely replicates Figure 4.
comments.request: Consider moving Table 1 to the supplement.
comments.quote: Table 1 appears quite busy. Is it necessary to include it in the main text? It seems to largely replicate the findings in Figure 4.

comments.issue: The title is overstated because effects are more pronounced for root than leaf decomposition.
comments.request: Soften the title to reflect the root-litter effect.
comments.quote: The title might be slightly overstated since the observed effects are more pronounced in root decomposition rather than leaf decomposition.

comments.issue: The introduction does not cite the 2021 IPCC report for up-to-date climate information.
comments.request: Cite the 2021 IPCC report.
comments.quote: Consider citing the 2021 IPCC report for more up-to-date information:

comments.issue: The link between increased decomposition, microbial necromass and long-term carbon storage is not developed.
comments.request: Discuss necromass formation and cite relevant references.
comments.quote: increased litter decomposition is linked to the transformation of accessible organic matter into more recalcitrant forms like microbial necromass, which promotes long-term carbon storage

comments.issue: Averages are reported without standard deviations.
comments.request: Provide standard deviations with averages.
comments.quote: Please provide standard deviations along with averages.

comments.issue: Sorting criteria and contamination found in bags are not described.
comments.request: Describe the sorting criteria and contamination.
comments.quote: Could you describe the sorting criteria and possibly provide information about the contamination found in the bags?

comments.issue: The experiment was limited to 47 months without paired sampling at the final point.
comments.request: Explain why 47 months was chosen.
comments.quote: Why limit the experiment to 47 months? This final point occurs significantly later without the paired sampling observed in previous years.

comments.issue: The R version and packages used are not specified.
comments.request: Specify the R version and packages used.
comments.quote: Please specify the version of R and the package used.

comments.issue: The prediction in Figure S3 could be added to Figure 1.
comments.request: Add the prediction to Figure 1.
comments.quote: would it be possible to add this prediction to Figure 1 to highlight the general patterns?

comments.issue: Figure S6 shows time and treatment effects and might replace Figure 3.
comments.request: Consider replacing Figure 3 with Figure S6.
comments.quote: I find this figure important as it shows both time and treatment effects, I am wondering if it could not even replace Figure 3.

title: Trees First Inhibit Then Promote Litter Decomposition in the Subarctic

study.system: soil bacteria; 2650 genomes and continental metagenomes; carbon metabolism

editor_summary: Editor: four reviewers found merit, but all raise substantive concerns including overstatements, limitations, biases, causality direction and the need for isolate experiments; address each carefully.

reviews.assessment: Positive; finds the study timely with interesting correlations, asking for precise wording and methodological clarifications.
strengths: interesting correlations that can inform future models

comments.issue: Genome size is written as an agent (contributes, controls, shapes) in the abstract and elsewhere.
comments.request: Rephrase so genome size is a trait linked to other traits.
comments.quote: Genome size is not an agent that can have actions. Instead, genome size is a trait that can be linked to different other traits

comments.issue: Percentages shown in the line-140 plots are not explained or defined.
comments.request: Clarify how the percentage was calculated and what it means.
comments.quote: the plots show a % and you need to further clarify how you calculated that % and what it means

comments.issue: Representativeness of the 175 MAGs and 113 isolate genomes is unknown.
comments.request: Report the percentage of raw reads recruited to these genomes.
comments.quote: How well are your 175 MAGs and 113 genomes from isolates representing your dataset?

comments.issue: Unclear whether assembly size or estimated genome size of MAGs was used.
comments.request: Clarify here and in the methods.
comments.quote: It is unclear to me if you are using the assembly size or the estimated genome size of your MAGs

comments.issue: Whether assemblies were single-sample or coassemblies is not specified at L394.
comments.request: Specify the assembly approach.
comments.quote: were the assemblies single-sample assemblies or coassemblies? Please specify

comments.issue: MAG de-replication at 95% ANI is not reported.
comments.request: State whether MAGs were de-replicated.
comments.quote: Did you de-replicate your 175 high-quality MAGs?

comments.issue: Figure 1's y-axis is not described precisely.
comments.request: Be more specific about the y-axis.
comments.quote: Can you please be more specific about what the y-axis is showing?

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the multi-scale work but flags speculative Y/A proxies, uncorrected multiple testing, MAG-quality issues and possible reversed causality.
strengths: adds valuable insight on genome size and life-history strategies
multi-scale combination of independent datasets appreciated

comments.issue: Y versus A strategist classification rests only on marker gene copy number, which does not ensure activity.
comments.request: Acknowledge this limitation (experimental validation being out of scope).
comments.quote: It solely depends on copy number of marker genes (Tables S1 and S2), which I feel is somewhat speculative (i.e., presence of specific genes does not ensure the corresponding activity)

comments.issue: No adjustment for multiple comparisons in exploratory Spearman tests (Table S4, S3, Fig S1).
comments.request: Apply adjustments such as Holm's correction.
comments.quote: It appears that adjustments for multiple comparison were not performed anywhere in this study

comments.issue: Fig 1B includes low-completeness MAGs with non-negligible contamination.
comments.request: Restrict or justify the MAG set used.
comments.quote: This fact makes me wonder why the authors present Fig 1B, which includes all the MAGs with lower completeness and inneglible amount of contaminations

comments.issue: AGS marker genes may overlap the Y/A hallmark genes, which would make AGS scores artefacts.
comments.request: Declare any overlap and explain how AGS tools work.
comments.quote: The marker genes used by AGS tools must NOT overlap with those used as hallmarks of Y/A strategies (otherwise the high scores of AGS in Fig 2B should be interpreted as artefact)

comments.issue: Fig S3B rrn copy numbers far exceed the plausible 1-15 range, suggesting AGS/ACN tools may have failed.
comments.request: Check and validate the tool outputs.
comments.quote: this figure shows that some metagenomes far exceed the upper limit of this range. This makes me worry that AGS-and-ACN tools may not have worked soundly in this study

comments.issue: Tables S1 and S2, core methodology, are only in the supplement.
comments.request: Move Tables S1 and S2 to the main text.
comments.quote: Tables S1 and S2 should be moved to the main text as they represent the most important part of methodology used in this study

comments.issue: MGEs are often mis-incorporated into MAGs, so Table S5 analysis may be unreliable.
comments.request: Redo this analysis using isolate genomes only.
comments.quote: MGE often fails to be correctly incorporated into MAGs (due to binning problems – see https://doi.org/10.1099/mgen.0.000436), so I think this analysis should be done using only isolate genomes

comments.issue: Figure 6 causal directions may be reversed (e.g. soil carbon favouring A/Y strategists; A/Y driving GS evolution).
comments.request: Assess accuracy and limitations of the causal hypothesis.
comments.quote: In my intuition, it is possible that some of the causal relationships may be reversed

comments.issue: 'Major advancement' at L321 is a subjective expression.
comments.request: Remove or reword the subjective claim.
comments.quote: L321, "major advancement": Although this is up to the editors' policy, I feel conflict with this kind of subjective expression

comments.issue: Line-level wording fixes: HiSeq capitalisation (L388), e-5 superscript (L401/435), 'blasted' (L403/454), assembled-constructed (L427), Sanger phrasing (L453).

comments.issue: Culture media composition at L442 is not described.

comments.issue: Phylogenetic methods at L476 are insufficiently detailed (concatenation, multi-copy genes, alignment, software, parameters).

comments.issue: Fig 4A is not intuitive.
comments.request: Replace with a simple table or bar charts.
comments.quote: Although the data presented here is quite simple, this figure is not intuitive (at least to me). Could be replaced with a simple table or bar charts

comments.issue: Table S3 analyses are not mirrored for biomass yield genes.

comments.issue: Fig S5 panels lack y-axis labels, disadvantaging colour-blind readers.

reviews.assessment: Impressive and novel study recommended for publication, with requests for a concept diagram, experimental validation and clarifications.

well-written and relevant to Ecology Letters

comments.issue: The concept diagram underpinning the hypotheses is only in the supplement (Fig. S11).

comments.quote: I suggest the authors integrate a concept diagram into the background section of the main text rather than placing it in the supplemental materials (Fig. S11)

comments.issue: Genomic findings lack direct experimental validation.

comments.issue: 'Control' at L58-60 is too definitive, and terminology for the two processes is not unified.

comments.issue: The knowledge gap about microbial traits controlling soil carbon cycling is not specified.

comments.issue: Abbreviations used without full names at first use: MAGs (L109), MGEs (L270), GHs (L470).

comments.issue: MAG quality class of the 175 MAGs is not stated.

comments.issue: Definition of the novel species-level taxa is not provided.

comments.issue: Sentence at L247-251 refers to total microbial communities although only bacteria were studied.

comments.issue: L287 should refer to soil organic carbon pools (SOC and DOC) as actually measured.

comments.issue: Conclusions at L317-336 are too long.

comments.quote: The conclusions should be more concise to provide a summary of novel insights from your investigation

comments.issue: Megahit version is not reported at L393.
