title: A Global Relationship Between Genome Size and Encoded Carbon Metabolic Strategies of Soil Bacteria

study.system: bacterial taxa; multiple-stressor performance curve experiments

editor_summary: Editor: exciting study that may break new ground in analysing multiple-stressor effects; reviews give valuable guidance on the introduction, statistics, and linking concept to empirical analyses.

reviews.assessment: Interesting study combining a clear conceptual argument with robust empirical demonstration; wants a clearer distinction between intrinsic and emergent interactions.

comments.issue: Intrinsic stressor interactions and emergent statistical non-additivity are not clearly distinguished, and disentangling them is not discussed.
comments.request: Distinguish the two interaction types and discuss how performance curves can study intrinsic interactions.
comments.quote: I think the authors could be clearer about the distinction between “intrinsic” stressor interactions and the “emergent” statistical interactions that are observed by statistical models

comments.issue: Taxa are pooled in Fig. 2 but not Fig. 4, and Fig. 2 shows no variation or confidence intervals; conclusions may depend on pooling.
comments.request: Justify pooling and test whether the message holds without it.
comments.quote: it isn’t immediately clear to me why the different taxa were pooled in Figure 2 but not in Figure 4

comments.issue: Required package versions are not documented, so the code may not run.
comments.request: Add package versions (e.g. package_version()) to the README.
comments.quote: It is great to see that the code and data are available, but it would be good to include the versions of the packages that are required

comments.issue: Only one alternative null model (dominance) is mentioned, while multiplicative models are more common.
comments.request: Discuss other null models, especially multiplicative.
comments.quote: It feels odd to just mention one alternative multiple-stressor null model but not others (multiplicative is far more common than dominance).

comments.issue: Linearity assumptions are attributed to experimental design rather than statistical model choice.
comments.request: Correct this framing of linearity assumptions.
comments.quote: Aren’t assumptions of linearity related to the choice of statistical model, rather than to the design of the experiment?

comments.issue: It is unclear how additional stressors were coded and how pairwise interactions were still quantified.
comments.request: Explain the factor coding and pairwise interaction estimation.
comments.quote: Why were the additional stressors all combined into one categorical factor?

comments.issue: Bounding the additive null model at zero may bias outcomes toward antagonism.
comments.request: Assess the influence of bounding the null model at zero.
comments.quote: How does this decision (additive null model bounded at 0) influence the results?

comments.issue: The discussion omits limitations: single level of the second stressor, additive expectation for a bounded response, feasibility for larger organisms.
comments.request: Expand the discussion of these limitations.
comments.quote: I expected some sort of discussion about the potential limitations of the experimental design

comments.issue: How results scale from populations to communities is unclear, and species interactions may alter performance curves.
comments.request: Explain the scaling approach or temper the claim.
comments.quote: I don’t follow how these results could be scaled up from populations to communities?

comments.issue: Negative AIC values could be misread as indicating worse fit.
comments.request: Emphasise that more negative AIC values indicate better fit.
comments.quote: it may be worth emphasising that models with more negative values show a better fit?

reviews.assessment: Extremely interesting and well written; no major concerns, but wants statistical clarifications and broader literature engagement.
strengths: well written and easy to follow
experimental test of a critical consideration

comments.issue: The paper does not position its results within the wide existing literature on multiple stressors.
comments.request: Expand the Intro and Discussion to engage this literature.
comments.quote: I suggest expanding in the Intro and Discussion on how these results sit in the wide literature that has previously tackled this topic

comments.issue: Alternative terminology for performance curves (dose-response, reaction norms) is not mentioned.
comments.request: Discuss the terminology and cite Segurado et al. 2022 and Rosenfeld et al. 2022.
comments.quote: Here is where you could expand on the different terminology used to refer to performance curves (e.g. dose-response curves, stressor-response functions, reaction norms).

comments.issue: The text understates the evidence that non-linearity drives inconsistent outcomes.
comments.request: Rephrase as suggested ("This non-linearity ... helps explain").
comments.quote: It is more than just possible; I think the studies cited above clearly demonstrate (in various ways) that non-linearity is indeed the root of these inconsistencies.

comments.issue: Relevant studies are not cited at page 4, line 7.
comments.request: Cite Boyd et al. 2018, Pirotta et al. 2022 and Segurado et al. 2022 here.
comments.quote: I think some of the studies in the list above should be cited here as well, because they make this exact point

comments.issue: The paper's experimental contribution relative to prior theoretical discussions is not highlighted.
comments.request: Highlight the experimental test as a strength.
comments.quote: A way to reinforce the relevance of this work may be to highlight here how most studies that have discussed this problem to date have done so largely from a theoretical perspective

comments.issue: Whether the growth conditions are standard for these taxa is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the growth conditions used.
comments.quote: Can these be considered standard growing conditions for these taxa?

comments.issue: How the quadratic term mitigates multicollinearity and concurvity is not explained.
comments.request: Provide these statistical details and clarify parameter versus variable usage.
comments.quote: How does the quadratic term mitigate multicollinearity? What about concurvity?

comments.issue: The choice of quadratic models over GAMs is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the model choice relative to GAMs.
comments.quote: Indeed, an alternative could have been to use GAMs here – although I’m in support of guiding modelling decisions in light of biological mechanisms

comments.issue: It is unclear whether "comparing growth rate and the stress response" includes interactions.
comments.request: Clarify this description.
comments.quote: By “comparing growth rate and the stress response”, do you mean including stress factor as a main effect, without the interactions?

comments.issue: The rationale for the additive null model formula (S - C) is not explained.
comments.request: Provide more justification for this null model.
comments.quote: Could you provide some more justification for this null model?

comments.issue: It is unclear why the formula can produce unreasonable negative predictions.
comments.request: Explain the negative predictions.
comments.quote: Why would you get negative predictions from this formula, if they are unreasonable?

comments.issue: Two typos: "assess" and "affect".
comments.quote: Page 8, line 48: Typo, ‘assess’.

comments.issue: Model checks, goodness of fit and uncertainty propagation across analytical steps are not reported, and some curve fits are poor.
comments.request: Report validation and propagate uncertainty through the analyses.
comments.quote: There is no discussion of model checks and validation, nor any mention of goodness of fit.

comments.issue: Curves at page 9, line 31 lack uncertainty.
comments.request: Plot uncertainty around these curves.
comments.quote: I would plot the uncertainty around these curves.

comments.issue: Details of the additional analysis at page 9, lines 51-52 belong in the Methods.
comments.request: Move these details to the Methods.
comments.quote: I think the details of this additional analysis should go into the Methods.

comments.issue: Comments at page 10, lines 46-56 and page 11, lines 6-11 belong in the Discussion.
comments.request: Move these comments to the Discussion.
comments.quote: shouldn’t these comments go into the Discussion?

comments.issue: Fitted curves at page 13, line 43 lack confidence intervals.
comments.request: Report confidence intervals around the fitted curves.
comments.quote: Again, please report confidence intervals around the fitted curves.

comments.issue: The Discussion points at page 14 lack citations to the studies mentioned in the Intro.
comments.request: Expand with the relevant citations.
comments.quote: Please expand with citations to the studies mentioned in the Intro that discuss these points in detail

comments.issue: The management implications are overstated, ignoring that such experiments are infeasible for most taxa and communities.
comments.request: Rephrase or expand to highlight these challenges.
comments.quote: This comment on management ignores that, for the vast majority of taxa and communities, it will not be possible to design a set of experiments in a lab, such as the setup presented here.

reviews.assessment: Super interesting and compelling; encourages multi-method comparisons and better linkage of shape changes to interaction outcomes.
strengths: strong inference from pooled and taxa-level results

comments.issue: Only one method (Hedges' D) is used, so it is unknown whether insights hold across alternative multiple-stressor methods.
comments.request: Repeat the Fig. 2 analysis with more than one method and compare.
comments.quote: I would very much encourage the authors to analyse the data in Fig 2, for example, using more than one method to assess whether there are qualitatively similar insights across the other methods

comments.issue: The link between curve shape changes and transitions among additive and non-additive outcomes is not made explicit.
comments.request: Add this mapping to the Fig. 1 legend and introduction text.
comments.quote: It would be great to see if one could map these shape changes specifically to transitions among additive and non-additive.

comments.issue: Fig. 3 results are not quantified against the claimed dominance of one interaction type.
comments.request: Report relative frequencies of outcome types overall and per primary stressor.
comments.quote: for each panel, the relative abundance of each type of interaction would be valuable overall

comments.issue: Results are not compared with the studies referenced in the introduction.
comments.request: Compare results with this literature in the text and discussion.
comments.quote: in the text/discussion, compare your results to the ones referenced in the introduction

comments.issue: No figure connects the conceptual diagram to the data to show how outcome distributions change with shape.
comments.request: Add a figure linking Fig. 1 to Figs 2-3.
comments.quote: This would specifically connect Fig 1 to Fig 2/3 data and allow the MS to showcase how shape change drives outcomes

comments.issue: "Pooled" data in Fig. 2 are actually model fixed effects with taxon as a random effect.
comments.request: Relabel and clarify as model fixed effects.
comments.quote: It is not clear in Fig 2 what ‘pooled’ data means. I believe these are model fixed effects, not pooled data

comments.issue: The "massive variation" statement does not reflect the mixed-model fixed effect and is hyperbolic.
comments.request: Rephrase as suggested to link the result to the mechanistic agenda.
comments.quote: Not sure this is communicating effectively what you’ve done and does not reflect the fixed effect from the mixed model. And `massive` is a bit hyperbole.

title: Reconciling Variability in Multiple Stressor Effects Using Environmental Performance Curves

study.system: three plant species; stochastic integral projection models

editor_summary: All three reviewers find merit in the original approach but are unconvinced by the findings; they require an explicit link to the demographic buffering hypothesis, clear comparison with previous work, detailed methods including scripts, and better treatment of scaling.

reviews.assessment: Timely and methodologically ambitious, but the metric choice, species selection, hypotheses and methods clarity need stronger justification.
strengths: timely topic in a dynamic research area
ambitious combination of IPMs and stochastic elasticities

comments.issue: The term 'demographic characteristics' is used without definition; unclear whether it means pace of life.
comments.request: Define 'demographic characteristics' or clarify whether it refers to pace of life.
comments.quote: L. 46: “Demographic characteristics”: are you referring to species’ pace of life? Please, clarify.

comments.issue: The choice of the sum of stochastic elasticities as the buffering metric is not justified against alternative metrics.
comments.request: Justify the added value of this metric relative to other buffering metrics.
comments.quote: Several metrics have been used to quantify demographic buffering in previous studies. Why focusing specifically on the sum of stochastic elasticities of variance?

comments.issue: The rationale for selecting these three plant species in particular is not explained.
comments.request: Explain and justify the choice of the three study species.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to better explain the rationale behind the choice of these three plant species in particular?

comments.issue: H2a and H2b are difficult to understand; the hypotheses need more detail.
comments.request: Clarify H2a and H2b and provide more detail on the hypotheses.
comments.quote: Predictions on page 5: H1 is well defined, but I have some trouble to understand H2a and H2b.

comments.issue: Information on the species' life histories and how environment affects their vital rates is missing.
comments.request: Provide more information on the species and on environmental effects on vital rates.
comments.quote: more information on the species used, as well as on the effects of environmental conditions on their vital rates, would be valuable.

comments.issue: A sentence is confusing about whether autocorrelation refers to environmental conditions or vital rates.
comments.request: Clarify whether temporal autocorrelation refers to environmental conditions or vital rates.
comments.quote: are you referring to temporal autocorrelation in environmental conditions or in vital rates?

comments.issue: The method section is heavy and the several analytical steps are not summarized.
comments.request: Summarize the general approach in a figure or in the text.
comments.quote: There are several steps, and it would be very helpful if they could be summarized in a figure or in the text

comments.issue: Methods are complex and appear difficult to replicate on another study system.
comments.request: Improve the clarity and reproducibility of the methodological pipeline.
comments.quote: From my reading, it can seem challenging to replicate a similar analysis on another study system.

comments.issue: Data and code are not provided, hindering reproducibility.
comments.request: Provide the data and the code.
comments.quote: Along the same line, it would be very helpful if the data and the code could be provided.

comments.issue: Relation to previous work on population-structure elasticities (Haridas et al. 2009) is missing.
comments.request: Discuss how the work relates to Haridas, Tuljapurkar and Coulson 2009.
comments.quote: how the present work relates to previous studies, in particular to Haridas, Tuljapurkar and Coulson 2009

comments.issue: The link between heterogeneity and transient dynamics is unclear and needs expansion.
comments.request: Expand and clarify the link between heterogeneity and transient dynamics.
comments.quote: I am not sure to fully understand the link between heterogeneity and transient dynamics. Please, expand a little bit and clarify?

reviews.assessment: Impressive simulation-based analyses, but the whole-life-history definition, variance scaling, statistical pipeline and climate-change assumptions need clarification.
strengths: impressive combination of extensive simulations with deep analytical insights

comments.issue: The paper's whole-life-history definition of demographic buffering differs from within-life-history definitions in the literature.
comments.request: Make the distinction clear and link it to the final analysis.
comments.quote: This is therefore a definition that considers the whole life history, whereas many papers that have addressed demographic buffering were interested in what happens within a life history

comments.issue: The approach assumes different environmental variables are on the same variance scale, which is hardly the case.
comments.request: Specify and discuss the scaling assumption and its consequences.
comments.quote: Using the same relative change in the variance of different demographic rates, or as in this paper, of the environmental variables, assumes that they are on the same scale, which is hardly the case

comments.issue: The regression-based approach and the scaled buffering values are not explained clearly.
comments.request: Explain the regression approach explicitly and provide the equations in the SM.
comments.quote: I was struggling to understand the regression-based approach defined after l. 251.

comments.issue: The reader is not told early that the sum of stochastic elasticities of variance is negative.
comments.request: State early that the sum of stochastic elasticities of variance is negative.
comments.quote: It could help the reader with a “slow” brain to write early on that the sum of stochastic elasticities of variance is negative

comments.issue: No note that using the standard deviation instead of the variance does not change the patterns.
comments.request: State that SD and variance give equivalent patterns.
comments.quote: It could also help (again it might be “trivial”) to write that using the standard deviation (as in eg Morris et al. 2008 or Westerband and Horvitz 2017) or the variance will not affect the patterns

comments.issue: The empirical basis (Westerband and Horvitz 2017) mixes temporal, spatial and detailed studies, limiting inference about environmental variance.
comments.request: Clarify the nature and limitations of this empirical basis.
comments.quote: This is fine as a basis of simulations but a bit more problematic as an empirical basis for assessing how environmental variability relates to demographic rate variance.

comments.issue: Combining AIC model selection with significance tests is bad practice; tests are irrelevant for simulation data.
comments.request: Keep AIC only as a predictive criterion, conditional on the simulations used.
comments.quote: You combine AIC based model selection and significance tests – this is bad practice as they correspond to different objectives

comments.issue: The claim that environmental stochasticity increases with climate change depends on drivers and is not consistent.
comments.request: Revise the climate-change narrative and its autocorrelation implications.
comments.quote: You mention that environmental stochasticity may increase with global climate change, but I would argue that it depends on what drives the environmental stochasticity.

comments.issue: The product autocorrelation*variance is called an interaction term, although it is only one specific functional form.
comments.request: Call the product term 'product' rather than 'interaction' throughout.
comments.quote: You include a product autocorrelation*variance as a predictor and call it an interaction term.

comments.issue: The R2 values (0.99 for the full model; 94% for variance) are not clearly described.
comments.request: Describe the R2 values in more detail, also in the methods.
comments.quote: Is the R2 given here (0.99) for the full model with all predictors and the 94% for the variance the partial R2?

comments.issue: Not needing the linear autocorrelation term only implies a zero slope when autocorrelation is zero.
comments.request: Consider that an overall negative relationship could still be nonlinear.
comments.quote: that you do not need to include the linear term of autocorrelation just implies that the slope of the relationship sum elasticities – autocorrelation is 0 when autocorrelation is 0

comments.issue: The precision of the R2 estimates is not demonstrated when claiming R2 is exactly 1.
comments.request: Assess the precision of the R2 estimates.
comments.quote: You seem to imply that the precision is enough to write that R2 is exactly 1 vs 0.9995.

reviews.assessment: The paper addresses an important question, but without the underlying theory and relevant literature the significance of the conclusions cannot be assessed.
strengths: addresses an important question about population buffering

comments.issue: The basic theory behind cumulative elasticity and the parameters driving it are not outlined or linked to the simulations.
comments.request: Outline the theory and reconcile the autocorrelation definitions with the simulations.
comments.quote: The basic theory leading to the central concept, which is the cumulative elasticity, must be outlined and the key parameters affecting its sensitivity to different demographic traits outlined.

comments.issue: The literature on autocorrelated age-structured population models is rudimentary and omits relevant general results.
comments.request: Cover the relevant literature on autocorrelated age-structured models better.
comments.quote: The literature on environmental autocorrelated age-structured population models are , at best, rudimentary included.

title: Structured Demographic Buffering: A Framework to Explore the Environmental Components and Demographic Mechanisms Underlying Demographic Buffering

study.system: Caenorhabditis nematodes; reproductive interference experiments and models

editor_summary: Four reviews range in assessment; R1 unconvinced by mechanism evidence, R2 questions novelty, R3/R4 see potential but find Methods/Results unclear. Editor invites revise and resubmit.

reviews.assessment: Findings publishable but novelty and significance insufficient for this journal; several literature citations missing.

comments.issue: Novelty and significance may be insufficient given the many existing RI studies across taxa, including nematodes.
comments.request: Better position the study against existing RI literature.
comments.quote: the novelty and significance may be insufficient in the context of ecology and evolution when asked if this paper is acceptable in this journal

comments.issue: 3 line-level edits (new paragraph L81; italics for t, df, p L202; avoid "dramatic" L225).
comments.quote: Line 225, “dramatic”: Please avoid emotional words in the Result section.

comments.issue: Many studies on reproductive interference exist but are not cited at lines 88-90.
comments.request: Cite some of the RI studies.
comments.quote: No. There are many studies on RI. Please cite some of them.

comments.issue: RI can occur in any reproductive process, not only mating, as shown by acoustic interference examples.
comments.request: Broaden the definition of reproductive interference.
comments.quote: No. RI can occur in any reproductive process. For example, heterospecific mating calls hamper the mate-searching of female frogs (Amézquita et al. 2011)

comments.issue: Superiority in resource competition may differ from greater fecundity (line 183).
comments.request: Distinguish competitive superiority from fecundity.
comments.quote: It may differ between superiority in resource competition and greater fecundity.

comments.issue: Inter-specific mating may not be an "error" but an evolutionarily stable strategy under sexual selection.
comments.request: Consider this alternative interpretation of mating errors.
comments.quote: inter-specific mating may not be an “error” but be an evolutionarily stable state due to sexual selection

comments.issue: The "previous theoretical work" at line 260 is not cited.
comments.request: Cite proper theoretical studies.
comments.quote: Line 260, “Previous theoretical work”: Cite proper studies.

comments.issue: The result at line 336 may be an artifact or analytical problem.
comments.request: Check for artifacts or analytical problems.
comments.quote: Line 336: Possibility of an artifact or analytical problem?

comments.issue: Coexistence under RI with ephemeral resources was modelled by Ruokolainen and Hanski (2016), which is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Ruokolainen and Hanski (2016).
comments.quote: Coexistence, when RI occurs between two species sharing ephemeral resources, was modeled by Ruokolainen and Hanski (2016).

comments.issue: Character displacement through RI literature (Grether et al. 2020; Konuma and Chiba 2007) is missing.
comments.request: Cite the character displacement literature.
comments.quote: Reproductive and ecological character displacements through RI have been discussed by Grether et al. (2020), Konuma and Chiba (2007), and other studies.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and well-written, but the evidence is not strong enough to robustly infer the mechanisms of reproductive interference.

comments.issue: The mechanism cannot be inferred because the reciprocal mating direction and conspecific combinations were not tested.
comments.request: Provide data from other mating combinations, including conspecific ones.
comments.quote: But it is possible that the heterospecific mating in the other direction (C. macrosperma female x C. nouraguensis male) also exhibits ectopic sperm migration.

comments.issue: Other mechanisms besides ectopic sperm (toxic ejaculate chemicals, physical damage) are possible and should be acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge alternative mechanisms of reproductive interference.
comments.quote: It may be difficult to empirically disentangle the contributions of these possible mechanisms, but at least these possibilities should be acknowledged.

comments.issue: A refractory period after heterospecific mating could cause conspecific sperm limitation and faster decline than the Leslie projection predicts.
comments.request: Consider mating order and behavioural change in the interpretation.
comments.quote: If heterospecifically mated females do not readily accept conspecific mating, the population decline would be quicker than predicted from Leslie projection

comments.issue: Progeny counted in Fig. 2 may include hybrids, which would overestimate fitness.
comments.request: Verify whether progeny are pure-bred or hybrids.
comments.quote: I wonder if the progeny are all pure-bred, or it is possible that some of them are hybrids. If they can be hybrids, this is an overestimation of fitness.

comments.issue: The advantage of C. macrosperma when rare may reflect density-dependent competition rather than reproductive interference.
comments.request: Test density dependence against the RI explanation.
comments.quote: Advantage of C. macrosperma when rare (Fig. 6) might be due to density-dependent resource competition, rather than reproductive interference

comments.issue: 2 line-level edits (L77 "exact" to "exert"; L431 unclear "L4").
comments.quote: L77 exact -> exert?

comments.issue: The point at L102-106 was theoretically investigated by Kishi and Nakazawa (2013).
comments.request: Cite Kishi and Nakazawa (2013).

title: Reproductive Interference Alters Species Coexistence in Nematodes due to Asymmetric Sperm‐Induced Harm

study.system: juvenile Chinook salmon and predators; telemetry, CFD and attack data

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers liked the data integration but raised outdated framing, unclear scope, missing sensitivity analyses and methods details; concludes the scope is not broad enough for Ecology Letters and suggests a behaviour or fish journal.

reviews.assessment: Promising, methodologically strong study whose introduction lacks rationale and whose discussion misses ecological context and limitations.
strengths: voluminous movement data and counterfactual scenarios

comments.issue: The conceptual frame starts with Laundre 2001, though risk effects on prey decisions date much earlier.
comments.request: Adopt a wider conceptual frame and sharpen the knowledge gap.
comments.quote: Laundre’s seminal paper in 2001 was no doubt influential, offering a useful metaphor for understand how risk mediates behavior, but the idea that risk of predation influences prey decision making dates much earlier

comments.issue: Risk-reward trade-offs have been studied for decades, so the claim that strategies remain unknown needs nuance.
comments.request: Be explicit about what is actually unknown.
comments.quote: there is need in my view to be much more explicit and nuanced about what is actually unknown

comments.issue: The 2001 paper is used as a stand-in for earlier food-safety trade-off work.
comments.request: Avoid recency bias and cite earlier trade-off literature.
comments.quote: I would recommend against using the 2001 paper as a stand-in for, or review of, the considerable work on food-safety trade-offs that occurred before the term landscape of fear was coined.

comments.issue: The fear-opportunity interaction is a stronger rationale than the one used.
comments.request: Center this dimension of novelty as the paper’s rationale.
comments.quote: Namely, there is a need to better understand the dynamic interactions between landscapes of fear and opportunity, especially outside of the classical food-safety (or starvation-predation) trade-off

comments.issue: Recent work on how migrating prey deal with risk is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Sabal et al. 2021 TREE.
comments.quote: there remains need for more work on how migrating prey deal with risk (see recent review by Sabal et al. 2021 in TREE)

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a priori hypotheses or expectations.
comments.request: Add expectations to make the introduction more compelling.
comments.quote: I like this final Introduction paragraph but wonder if the authors had any a priori hypotheses in mind when the work was conceived.

comments.issue: The predators and why they were chosen are not identified clearly.
comments.request: Identify the predator species and the selection rationale.
comments.quote: the authors could identify what the predators are, and why they were chosen (I reread the earlier sections of the paper and found this to actually be unclear).

comments.issue: The interpretation needs caution because largemouth bass attack-rate data were unreliable.
comments.request: Add caveats about the unreliable attack-rate data.
comments.quote: Some caution in the interpretation is advised here given that the attack rate data for largemouth bass were unreliable, correct?

comments.issue: The material on page 10 is a more compelling setup than the introduction’s opening.
comments.request: Move this material into the introduction.
comments.quote: These lines offer a much more compelling set up for the paper than do the first two paragraphs of the introduction

comments.issue: It is not unpacked whether predators affect migrants consumptively or through fear, or with what fitness consequences.
comments.request: Discuss the consumptive-versus-fear implications and needed future work.
comments.quote: Specifically, what do the authors think this pattern means for how the predators are primarily affecting the migrants (primarily consumptively or LOF)?

comments.issue: The discussion does not address the limitation of robust predation data for only one of two predators.
comments.request: Add a paragraph on this limitation and its implications.
comments.quote: at the very least the authors should add a paragraph addressing the implications of only having robust predation assay data for one of the two predators

comments.issue: The opportunity concept is narrowly limited to migration energetics.
comments.request: Broaden the discussion of other underexplored opportunities.
comments.quote: the authors focus somewhat narrowly on their measure of opportunity – migration energetics/efficiency

comments.issue: Word choice at page 2, line 13 should be “facilitate”.
comments.request: Change to “facilitate”.
comments.quote: Page 2, line 13: Suggest changing to “facilitate”.

comments.issue: The scientific name for Chinook salmon is missing.
comments.request: Add the scientific name.
comments.quote: Page 3, line 33: Scientific name for Chinook salmon?

comments.issue: More scientific names are needed.
comments.request: Add the missing scientific names.
comments.quote: Page 4, line 12: More scientific names needed.

comments.issue: Delete “that” before “were” at page 5, line 16.
comments.request: Delete “that”.
comments.quote: Page 5, line 16: Suggest deleting “that” before “were”.

comments.issue: Insert “what” after “computing” at page 9, line 7.
comments.request: Insert “what”.
comments.quote: Page 9, line 7: Insert “what” after “computing”.

comments.issue: Insert a comma after “on” at page 11, line 30.
comments.request: Insert the comma.
comments.quote: Page 11, line 30: Insert a comma after “on”.

comments.issue: Delete the parenthesis after “analysis” at page 17, line 51.
comments.request: Delete the parenthesis.
comments.quote: Page 17, line 51: Delete the parenthesis after “analysis”.

reviews.assessment: Interesting data integration, but without defined hypotheses, sensitivity analyses or methodological detail, it reads as a methods paper and does not fit the journal.
strengths: interesting, successful integration of data streams

comments.issue: Hypotheses and research questions are not clearly defined and are buried in Methods and Results.
comments.request: Define clear hypotheses and broad ecological gaps in the introduction.
comments.quote: There are no clearly defined hypotheses or research questions, particularly in the Introduction. Rather, they are buried in the Methods and even in the Results.

comments.issue: Methods and interpretation are placed in the Results, against convention.
comments.request: Restructure so methods and discussion sit in their proper sections.
comments.quote: the manuscript’s style simply did not meet convention. There was a lot of methods placed in the Results, and a lot of interpretation of results (discussion) in the Results

comments.issue: Methods rely on cited papers and reader trust rather than detail, e.g. tethering and work calculations.
comments.request: Provide methodological details, including calculations and assumptions.
comments.quote: the authors rely far too heavily on 1) readers reading cited papers to understand methods, and 2) having readers trust assumptions of the authors rather than providing methodological details

comments.issue: Telemetry processing details are missing: erroneous positions, positioning errors and reception rate.
comments.request: Report filtering and positioning accuracy details.
comments.quote: No mention of how many erroneous positions were removed, how more subtle potential positioning errors were handled, nor the rate at which positions were received.

comments.issue: No sensitivity analyses test robustness to predator densities or smolt paths.
comments.request: Add sensitivity analyses of key inputs.
comments.quote: This is largely a modeling paper, and yet there are no sensitivity analyses. How robust are these findings to varying inputs, particularly in predator densities and paths taken by smolts?

comments.issue: Results are conversational with few numbers and no effect sizes.
comments.request: Report effect sizes and actual numbers.
comments.quote: The results is written in a conversational way, with very few numbers mentioned and at times purely qualitatively (no effect sizes).

comments.issue: Citations on smolt migration and predator-prey dynamics are sparse.
comments.request: Cite Ibbotson and Clark et al. on nocturnal migration.
comments.quote: The paper also seems pretty light on citations, particularly given how much work has gone into predator-prey dynamics of smolts as well as smolt migration behavior.

comments.issue: “Smolt” is not defined and “juvenile” is not qualified to life stage.
comments.request: Define smolt and specify the life stage studied.
comments.quote: the word "smolt" should be used and defined. It pops up later in the manuscript without reference, and juvenile should be qualified to the specific life stage

comments.issue: The text implies a purely exploratory paper without a priori expectations.
comments.request: Either couch the paper as a methods demonstration or state expectations.
comments.quote: the way this is written, it implies the paper is purely exploratory, with no a priori expectations, questions, or hypotheses

comments.issue: The assumed survival bottleneck from predator density is unsupported without survival estimates.
comments.request: Provide segment-specific survival estimates relative to nearby landscapes.
comments.quote: can you really assume a "survival bottleneck" due to a high density of predators. A lot of work has been done in this system I believe with telemetry - can't specific survival rates or segment specific survival estimates be given relative to other nearby landscapes?

comments.issue: The map figure is not cited in the first methods paragraph.
comments.request: Cite the map figure.
comments.quote: p 4 First paragraph of methods - should the map figure be cited somewhere here?

comments.issue: The spatial coverage of the ADCPs is not stated.
comments.request: State what portion of the study system the ADCPs covered.
comments.quote: p 4 L20 - what portion of the study system did the ADCPs cover?

comments.issue: Position filtering, ping rate and interpolation details are missing.
comments.request: Describe filtering, ping rate and interpolation reproducibility.
comments.quote: need more info on how this was done, what % of positions were removed, what was the general ping rate of the original tags relative to the 2-s interpolation, etc.

comments.issue: “Smolt” first appears at p4 L40 without definition.
comments.request: Define smolt before first use.
comments.quote: p4 L40 - I believe this is the first mention of "smolt" even though this hasn't been used/defined prior

comments.issue: The role of cloud cover is not considered.
comments.request: Consider cloud cover in the analyses.
comments.quote: p4 L46 - what about the role of cloud cover?

comments.issue: Methods at p5 L6-17 lack detail and Figure S6 is rudimentary and possibly not to scale.
comments.request: Provide method details and a proper figure.
comments.quote: p5 L6-17 - need more detail - shouldn't be forced to read several other papers to assess validity of methods. And Figure S6 is pretty rudimentary - is that to scale?

comments.issue: How work was computed for living fish is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the work calculation, including fish size and metabolism.
comments.quote: p6 L12 - how was work computed? Doesn't this require information on fish size, metabolism, etc? This is a living organism, not an inanimate object.

comments.issue: “Prey presentation” at p7 L21 is undefined.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: p7 L21: What is a "prey presentation"?

comments.issue: Migrants “accept” predator encounters is odd wording.
comments.request: Choose a different word.
comments.quote: p9 L12 - migrants "accept" predator encounters? Consider word choice.

comments.issue: “Dramatically increase” is used without effect size in the results.
comments.request: Report quantities instead of dramatic language.
comments.quote: do not use "dramatically increase" when no effect size or quantity is given - this is a results section.

comments.issue: “Instigate” at p11 L21 is poor word choice.
comments.request: Consider a different word.
comments.quote: p11 L21 - consider a different word than "instigate"

comments.issue: Lower visual predator effectiveness at night is already well established.
comments.request: Acknowledge prior work on this idea.
comments.quote: the idea that visual predators are less effective at night or low vision (high turbidity) times is not - quite a bit of work on this both experimentally

comments.issue: A citation at p11 L52 appears as a superscript 2.
comments.request: Fix the citation.
comments.quote: p11 L52 - fix citation that is currently a superscript 2?

comments.issue: Predator behaviour is not discussed though Figure 1 suggests diel habitat shifts.
comments.request: Discuss whether striped bass use the main channel more at night.
comments.quote: the paper's focus is on how prey respond to variations in landscape of fear, but it might be worth discussing the predator's behavior

comments.issue: Figure 3 y-axis units are missing.
comments.request: Add units to the y-axis.
comments.quote: Figure 3- units on the y axis?

reviews.assessment: Interesting, compelling study that needs major revision to integrate energy-landscape concepts and update its framework.
strengths: combination of movement, predation and CFD data
compelling study of interest to the journal’s readers

comments.issue: The paper’s framework is not up to date with current concepts, especially for this journal.
comments.request: Update the conceptual framework.
comments.quote: The primary issue is that the framework of the paper is not up to date with current concepts and this is particularly an issue for a journal like Ecology Letters.

comments.issue: The energy landscape concept is never discussed despite being what was measured.
comments.request: Frame the study around energy landscapes.
comments.quote: At no point in the manuscript do they discuss an energy landscape, or the spatial representation of the power requirements to move throughout the environment.

comments.issue: Prior work already integrates fear and energy landscapes and is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Gallagher et al. 2017 and Papastamatiou et al. 2024 and rewrite the introduction.
comments.quote: I believe this paper should be framed within this landscape to provide very nice empirical support for how these landscapes integrate. In my opinion a substantial re-write of the introduction may be required.

comments.issue: The equations used are not included.
comments.request: Include the equations for readers unfamiliar with them.
comments.quote: Pg 6 line 9: Include the equations used. While I understand these are basic physics some readers may be unfamiliar with the equations.

comments.issue: The discussion may need rewriting once the frameworks are integrated.
comments.request: Revise the discussion accordingly.
comments.quote: The discussion may also require some degree of rewrite based on the integration of the frameworks listed above.

comments.issue: It is unexplained why flow increases at night, which would make the energy landscape dynamic.
comments.request: Explain the diel flow pattern and its behavioural implications.
comments.quote: Why does flow increase at night? This isn’t mentioned in the text but is interesting if correct as it means the energy landscape is also dynamic and changing over the diel cycle.

comments.issue: Figure 1e does not indicate significance.
comments.request: Indicate significance in the figure.
comments.quote: Fig. 1e can you indicate significance in these figures?

comments.issue: Figure 2 is confusing with missing axis labels.
comments.request: Add x-axis labels and explain the inset.
comments.quote: Fig. 2 becomes very confusing. There is no x-axis labels in any panel other than 1b. I couldn’t follow what they were all trying to show.

title: Integrating Landscapes of Fear and Energy Reveals the Behavioural Strategies That Shape Predator–Prey Interactions

study.system: Qinghai-Tibet Plateau; shrubs, understory plants and nematodes

editor_summary: Editor asks to better contextualize nematode findings and emphasize novelty, address causal interpretation and low explained variance, and share code and data.

reviews.assessment: Interesting study, but the causal direction is not established and the core Price-equation analysis appears purely descriptive.

comments.issue: Shrub establishment is not random; soil properties could drive both shrub presence and understory biomass.

comments.issue: Opening description of biodiversity drivers should be reworded at l.76 and l.78.

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits at l.85 and l.267, plus vegan citation formatting.

comments.issue: 'Sensitive to the presence of shrubs' is repeated; unclear whether a second item was intended.
comments.request: Clarify the repetition and any missing second item.
comments.quote: l.113-114 repetition of “sensitive to the presence of shrubs”. Was there a second thing?

comments.issue: Two relevant references are suggested for citation.
comments.request: Cite the suggested references.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether 'three shrubs' means individuals or species and whether species are shared across locations.

comments.issue: The WorldClim version used is not specified.

comments.issue: Both glmmTMB and lme4 were used although their functionality overlaps.

comments.issue: Price equation components lack uncertainty estimates and any formal statistical analysis.

comments.issue: Boxplot elements in Figure 1 are undefined.

comments.issue: Figure 3 x-axis titles do not match the caption.

comments.issue: Dynamite plots in Figs S4-S5 obscure the data distribution.

comments.issue: Analysis code was not made available alongside the data.

comments.issue: Results are not placed in the context of previous Price-equation applications.

comments.issue: Species identity effects are not benchmarked against the range of possible effects.

comments.issue: A few grammatical errors remain throughout the manuscript.

comments.issue: 'Experimental design' mislabels what is an observational study.

comments.issue: Uncertainty of the estimates at Lines 153-158 is not reported.
