comments.issue: Direct inclusion of phylogeny is questioned since phylogeny matters only through trait similarity.
comments.request: Justify modelling phylogeny directly.
comments.quote: Why to consider phylogeny directly? If phylogeny is important it is because of similar traits, not in itself, I guess.

comments.issue: Figure B1 may be unnecessary.
comments.request: Consider removing it.
comments.quote: Figure B1 (in Appendix B) may not be important.

comments.issue: Biogeographical realms are an artificial categorisation with little functional relevance, unlike island versus mainland.
comments.request: Justify or drop the realm variable.
comments.quote: I do not see why the biogeographical realms would be relevant here.

comments.issue: Lipid-poor is treated as a binary variable although lipid content is continuous.
comments.request: Consider lipid content as a continuous variable.
comments.quote: Is there any chance to consider "lipid-poor" as a real variable, not a binary value?

reviews.assessment: Well-prepared study with a thorough analysis; only minor suggestions on writing, captions and wider biological discussion.
strengths: complex analysis explained in a clear narrative
supplementary material including data and code

comments.issue: Wording is unnecessarily convoluted and repetitive, with long complex sentences and passive voice.
comments.request: Simplify wording across the manuscript.
comments.quote: In many places, your wording is unnecessarily convoluted. Avoid long and overly complex sentences.

comments.issue: Figure captions lack the variable explanations given in the Methods and do not explain what the patterns mean.
comments.request: Add variable explanations and pattern interpretation to all captions.
comments.quote: These should be included in all figure captions, like Fig 4. Additionally, you should briefly explain what the patterns mean and why readers should take note of them.

comments.issue: Subfigures of Figure 3 are not neatly aligned.
comments.request: Align panels, e.g. with the patchwork package.
comments.quote: The subfigures on Fig. 3 are not neatly aligned. The patchwork package could handle that

comments.issue: Fruit colouration and pigments, which affect plumage and health, are not discussed.
comments.request: Address fruit pigments at least in the discussion of results.
comments.quote: You did not really discuss fruit colouration and pigments. Pigments obtained from friuts can enhance the birds' plumage coloration

comments.issue: Insularity and latitude may be associated, and associations among explanatory variables are not shown.
comments.request: Show associations among explanatory variables, at least in the appendix.
comments.quote: Is insularity independent from latitude? I think it would not hurt to see how much all the explanatory variables are associated (at least in the appendix).

comments.issue: Seasonality and food availability changing with latitude could affect results, e.g. seasonal shifts in fruit preference.
comments.request: Discuss seasonality and food availability effects.
comments.quote: I do not think that you discuss enough how seasonality and food availability throughout the year change with latitude, and that could affect the results.

comments.issue: Explanatory power of the model is not reported.
comments.request: Report how much variation the model explains.
comments.quote: Do you have any ways to measure the explanatory power of your model? It would be informative to see how much is explained by the model, and how much is left out.

comments.issue: Frequent use of the term network is misleading since no network analysis is performed.
comments.request: Consider calling them frugivory data.
comments.quote: given the fact how many times you use the term network in the MS, I find it a bit unintentionally misleading

comments.issue: Introduction ends by describing results that belong in the results section.
comments.request: Remove the results summary from the introduction.
comments.quote: I'm not sure if you should end the introduction by describing the results. There are dedicated chapters for that.

comments.issue: A sentence in the introduction is filler with no meaningful message.
comments.request: Rewrite or remove the sentence.
comments.quote: This sentence feel like a filler. It has no real, meaningful message. You can do better.

comments.issue: The mechanism sentence is dry, and saying animals choose invites debate about choice and preference; simpler to say what they eat.
comments.request: Avoid choose and preference wording and rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: It is easy to argue about what choice means, how much freedom they have, and how much evolutionary and ecological pressure influences them

comments.issue: Variance in trait distributions and homogeneous distributions are presented as opposites although not mutually exclusive.
comments.request: Rephrase for clarity.
comments.quote: This sentence sounds like you are contrasting the two concepts, but I don't think they are opposing.

comments.issue: Claim that high richness makes extreme trait values easier to find via sampling effects seems doubtful, as small things are harder to find.
comments.request: Rephrase or justify the sampling-effect statement.
comments.quote: I would guess smaller things, for example, are harder to find and not easier.

comments.issue: The word insularity is uncommon and not defined at first use.
comments.request: Introduce its meaning at first use.
comments.quote: This a beautiful, but not commonly used English word. Maybe you could consider gently inducing its meaning the first time you use it.

comments.issue: 3 line-level copy edits (contrasting latitudes, credible intervals, a typo).
comments.quote: I'm not sure if contrasting is the best choice here, if you meant that you have samples from a wide range of latitudes.

comments.issue: Detailed model scaling and convergence diagnostics sentences are too detailed for the main text.
comments.request: Move them to the appendix.
comments.quote: I think these sentences could go in the appendix, you did not describe anything with this accuracy in the main text.

comments.issue: Burn-in phase of the MCMC is not mentioned.
comments.request: State whether burn-in was used.
comments.quote: Did you have a burn-in phase? Or that was not necessary here?

comments.issue: Definition of functional complementarity is convoluted.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: This is really convoluted. I have seen you can write better!

comments.issue: Sign-change multiplier procedure is described in a needlessly complicated way.
comments.request: Describe it as taking the absolute value.
comments.quote: You could have just written that you took the absolute value of it.

comments.issue: Sample sizes appear in the results rather than the methods, where they are needed to judge accuracy.
comments.request: Move sample sizes to the methods.
comments.quote: In my opinion, sample sizes should go in the methods, because I need that information to judge the potential accuracy of the analysis

comments.issue: Sentences describing tropical assemblages and negative responses are convoluted.
comments.request: Simplify the sentences.
comments.quote: they tended to do it negatively" Convoluted sentence, please simplyfy.

title: Global Trends of Trait Matching in Avian Frugivory and Its Consequences for the Complementarity and Irreplaceability of Birds

study.system: European great tit populations; 32 sites, 67 years of breeding data

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers highlighted multiple areas needing significant content development or clarification of assumptions and methods, and encourages the authors to address these as completely as possible.

reviews.assessment: Finds the dataset impressive and most comments easy to address, but questions the claimed implications of age-structure synchrony for conservation.
strengths: impressive long-term collection of population structure data

comments.issue: The introduction and discussion present age structure as a predictor of population processes rather than an outcome.
comments.request: Clarify whether age structure predicts or reflects population processes.
comments.quote: the introduction and discussion suggest that age structure is important for predicting population processes, as opposed to being the outcome by which we learn about population processes

comments.issue: The importance of age-structure synchrony for climate change responses is asserted without demonstration.
comments.request: Provide a specific demonstration of how and when synchrony matters.
comments.quote: spatial synchrony in age structure is implied to be important for understanding how populations will respond to things like climate change

comments.issue: The ages considered are not clearly defined, and 'juvenile' is used for breeding individuals.
comments.request: Clearly define the age classes.
comments.quote: There needs to be a clear definition of the ages considered - you use the term juvenile for breeding individuals which seems like a contradiction.

comments.issue: The 15.3% and 20.1% values and the effect of unassigned animals are unexplained; age-1 identification and recruitment timing are unclear.
comments.request: Explain these percentages, assignment bias and age identification.
comments.quote: It also in not clear what the 15.3% and 20.1% refer to and how they were calculated and the degree to which animals that could not be assigned may bias or affect estimates.

comments.issue: Bottom 5% and top 5% extremes together cover about 10% of events, not the stated 5%.
comments.request: Correct or clarify the extreme-event definition.
comments.quote: since it is highly unlikely to have both at the same time, they are effectively independent and do add up to ~10% of the events rather than 5%

comments.issue: A proportion response may be better modelled with a logistic or probit link.
comments.request: Consider a binomial link function or justify the current model.
comments.quote: since y is a propotion, would it be more appropraite to use a logistic regression with a logit or probit or other binomial appropriate link function?

comments.issue: A clutch size effect of 0.437 is impossible for a proportion response, suggesting a scale or transformation problem.
comments.request: Explain or correct the effect size scale.
comments.quote: The effect of the clutch size int he previous year is 0.437, which should not be possible

comments.issue: The parameter l is treated as a threshold although synchrony declines steadily with distance.
comments.request: Justify why l is treated as a point of interest.
comments.quote: This is a steadily declining function rather than a function that has a distinct threshold.

comments.issue: The claim that mortality is unimportant is not demonstrated, only the reproduction relationship is shown.
comments.request: Demonstrate or temper the mortality claim.
comments.quote: You directly show a relationship between reproduction and age structure, but where is it demonstrated that mortality is not important or less important?

reviews.assessment: Finds the study informative and within scope, but questions the juvenile-proportion proxy and the exclusion of asynchrony from the analyses.
strengths: quantitative framework has potential to advance metapopulation dynamics

comments.issue: The juvenile-to-adult ratio does not capture multivariate age structure, only the number of new individuals per year.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limitation and analyse mean age deviations, or drop 'age structure'.
comments.quote: this univariate ratio does not adequately capture age structure, rather it captures the number of new individuals occurring in a population in a given year

comments.issue: The synchrony method excludes negative synchrony, removing potentially important information.
comments.request: Use a method that allows asynchrony or justify the exclusion.
comments.quote: The authors employ a type of spatial synchrony analyses (sensu Engen et al. 2002) that exclude the possibility of spatial asynchrony (or negative synchrony) of populations and environmental variables

comments.issue: Supplementary age-structure metrics are not described or discussed in the main text.
comments.request: Acknowledge these metrics in the main findings.
comments.quote: none of these metrics or associated analyses are described in the main text aside from a brief mention on L184-186 of the methods

comments.issue: Density-dependence is discussed although the analyses do not capture population size.
comments.request: Bridge the gap between density-dependence claims and the analyses.
comments.quote: extending these results to explain density-dependence or alternatively explain these results through the lens of density-dependence presents a challenge given that the analyses do not capture attributes of population size in response variables

comments.issue: Beech masting may mask or mediate the effect of temperature metrics on synchrony.
comments.request: Discuss what drives masting synchrony and possible indirect effects.
comments.quote: What drives the referenced “spatial synchrony in beech masting”? Could the effect of temperature metrics (winter lows, ECEs, etc.) be masked by variation in beech masting – their effect is indirect?

comments.issue: The conclusion passage rehashes prior discussion instead of broadening the message.
comments.request: Broaden the conclusion.
comments.quote: The conclusion passage should be broadened rather than as a rehash of prior discussion points.

comments.issue: The causal logic at L134-135 seems backwards: coherence in fluctuations cannot decompose mechanisms of coherence.
comments.request: Correct the causal logic.
comments.quote: It seems backwards to assume that spatial coherence in fluctuations decomposes the mechanisms of coherence. Shouldn’t it be the other way around?

comments.issue: The statement that climate change affects populations through survival is too broad.
comments.request: Be more explicit about climate impacts.
comments.quote: This is fairly broad. Can the authors be more explicit about climate impacts?

comments.issue: Information on data collection is very limited and methodological detail needs significant expansion.
comments.request: Expand the data collection and metadata methods.
comments.quote: Information regarding data collection is very limited and it falls on the reader to find information and metadata for how data and metadata are collected.

comments.issue: It is unclear how individual identity was known and the related assumption needs a reference.
comments.request: Explain whether birds are tagged and cite the assumption.
comments.quote: it is unclear how identity was known for birds. Are these tagged individuals?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether mean clutch size accounts for population size at a location.
comments.request: Clarify the clutch size estimate.
comments.quote: Does this estimate consider the population size at a location?

comments.issue: The spatial location and resolution of environmental data collection are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Report the spatial location and resolution of environmental variables.
comments.quote: there should be some acknowledgement of the spatial location and/or resolution of collection

comments.issue: Several lines need clarity edits (L107, L120, L214, L338).
comments.quote: What is the specific scale of “vary at a large spatial scale”?

comments.issue: The weak trend in Figure S3a is hard to interpret and does not belong in the first results paragraph.
comments.request: Move or remove this result from the opening paragraph.
comments.quote: This pattern seems very difficult to interpret from this figure. Additionally, it doesn’t appear to be highly relevant to the overall results

comments.issue: A table reference is missing for the result at L310.
comments.request: Add the table reference.
comments.quote: L310: Provide a table reference for this result.

comments.issue: The section at L384-389 is confusing, with hypotheses generated before the main message.
comments.request: Clarify the hypotheses before stating the main message.
comments.quote: The authors appear to be generating multiple hypotheses for why low winter temperatures could result in differential mortality.

comments.issue: The paragraph at L381-403 is not well constructed and would benefit from restructuring.
comments.request: Restructure the paragraph around explicit hypotheses.
comments.quote: The various mechanisms provided by the authors appear valid, but the argument is not well constructed.

comments.issue: Figure 3 needs an in-plot colour legend and Figure S2 needs defined facet labels and axis titles.
comments.request: Add the colour legend and label Figure S2 axes.
comments.quote: Figure S2: Need to better define facet labels, add axis titles. Are these estimates normalized, what are the units?

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic about the novelty and appropriate methods, but wants clearer caveats about distance-decay inference and a broader discussion.
strengths: novel study of spatial synchrony in age structure
important topic for stability and persistence

comments.issue: Inference about synchrony drivers from distance-decay similarity is weak because multiple mechanisms produce similar patterns.
comments.request: State the assumptions and caveats of this inferential approach clearly.
comments.quote: this approach provides weak inference about drivers because multiple mechanisms can produce similar patterns

comments.issue: The discussion should speculate on how general synchrony in age structure is across species and habitats.
comments.request: Broaden the discussion and outline a research agenda.
comments.quote: I wonder whether the Discussion could be broadened somewhat with additional reasoned speculation about how general the results of this study might be for synchrony in age structure.

comments.issue: The denominator of the juvenile proportion is unclear (all juveniles, total population or breeding population).
comments.request: State exactly what the denominator includes.
comments.quote: To be crystal clear, what is the denominator here? The number of juveniles (including breeding and non-breeding) or the total population (including breeders and non-breeders) or the breeding population (including breeding juveniles and adults).

comments.issue: Time series lengths vary widely, which affects precision, and increasing synchrony over time may bias estimates.
comments.request: Run a sensitivity analysis with more comparable time series and state overlap criteria.
comments.quote: Maybe what’s warranted is a sensitivity analysis comparing the results from the full dataset to one with a restricted dataset where the time series length and recency of the data record are more comparable.

comments.issue: Key modelling details are missing, including that the synchrony statistic is effectively Pearson correlation and how the autocorrelation function was fitted.
comments.request: State the statistic plainly and describe the fitting method.
comments.quote: Given the construction of the variance-covariance matrix, the synchrony statistic is effectively Pearson correlation, as is often used, but this could be plainly stated.

comments.issue: The sentence at L276-279 is unnecessary and not fully accurate, since nonparametric approaches yield similar information.
comments.request: Revise or remove the sentence.
comments.quote: I don’t think this sentence is necessary or fully accurate.

comments.issue: Assumptions and limitations of the inferential framework are not described.
comments.request: Describe the assumptions and limitations at L299.
comments.quote: This would be a good place to describe some assumptions/limitations of the inferential framework.

title: Continent‐Wide Drivers of Spatial Synchrony in Breeding Demographic Structure Across Wild Great Tit Populations

study.system: European forest trees; SDM/PEM hindcasting over 12,000 years

editor_summary: Editor notes a careful piece but finds many ad hoc, unexplained calibration/simulation choices (e.g., four predictors, 30-year periods); results not novel; wants a balanced discussion of CSDM/PEM value.

reviews.assessment: Valuable model comparison, but migration simulations create nonindependence that challenges the main conclusion.
strengths: builds a strong case in the introduction
tests a wide array of models against fossil data

comments.issue: Migration starting from the 12kBP prediction creates nonindependence that drives the performance-dissimilarity trend.
comments.request: Re-evaluate the workflow so timeframes are tested independently.
comments.quote: performance along the x axis (dissimilarity) is limited by performance further along the x axis, which presents a problem of nonindependence between these samples

comments.issue: Whether thresholding in the migration simulation is annual or at 30-year steps is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify when thresholding occurs.
comments.quote: this could be stated more clearly in the “Migration Simulation” section, which leaves room to interpret as thresholding occurring on an annual basis during the migration simulation

comments.issue: Performance-testing frequency and the temporal/spatial coverage of pollen records are not stated.
comments.request: State testing frequency and pollen record coverage.
comments.quote: It appears only every other 250-year SDM is performance tested to the 500-year pollen samples (Fig S10a), but I don’t think this is explicitly stated, nor is the temporal or spatial extent of pollen records

comments.issue: The sentence/figure reference at line 231 is wrong.
comments.request: Change the reference at line 231.
comments.quote: note that I think the sentence/figure reference in line 231 needs to be changed

comments.issue: Fossil record availability per species and performance testing with missing records are unclear.
comments.request: Indicate data availability, e.g. with a timeline figure.
comments.quote: the manuscript would benefit from more clarity regarding when fossil records are available for each species, and how/whether model performance is tested when they are missing

comments.issue: Differences between high- and moderate-performance models within groups are not tested.
comments.request: Run a sensitivity test comparing high- and moderate-performance models.
comments.quote: it would be useful to see, at least as a sensitivity test, whether the high-performance models (as deemed by ref 51: BRT, MaxEnt, RF) perform differently than the moderate-performance choices (GAM, Lasso GLM)

comments.issue: Terminology is inconsistent (time period names; fitted PEMs).
comments.request: Use one term per element throughout.
comments.quote: Consistent internal terminology will improve the reader’s ability to follow. I recommend authors choose one term for each element and use it throughout

comments.issue: Figure 2 lacks an indication of model performance.
comments.request: Add a performance inset to each panel.
comments.quote: could add an addition level of information to the reader by adding an indication of model performance inset within each panel

comments.issue: The number of model runs at line 173 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the model count.
comments.quote: Line 173: should it read “10 times for each of the 9* models”? (5 CDMSs, 2 expert PEM, 2 fitted PEM)?

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks Early and Late-Middle Holocene labels.
comments.request: Add the Holocene period labels.
comments.quote: Please add labels on Fig 1 indicating the “Early Holocene” and “Late-Middle Holocene” periods (similar to labeling on Fig S1) since these timeframes are later referenced repeatedly

comments.issue: Line 81 phrasing is hard to follow.
comments.request: Reword the sentence.
comments.quote: “which effects depend on their occurrence relatively to the development stages” is difficult to follow, consider rewording

comments.issue: 'Expert knowledge' at line 87 is undefined and not compared to occurrence-derived distributions.
comments.request: Elaborate on expert knowledge and its role.
comments.quote: Unclear what “expert knowledge” means- line 87. I suggest adding a brief sentence to elaborate on this and how it compares to occurrence-derived distributions

comments.issue: The utility of CSDMs for broader species application is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss when and how CSDMs remain useful.
comments.quote: it could be useful to discuss when and how CSDMs are useful to the extent that they can be applied presumably to more species

comments.issue: Figure S8 caption lacks panel descriptions.
comments.request: Add descriptions of panels A, B and C.
comments.quote: Fig S8 please add descriptions of A, B, and C to caption

comments.issue: 'Late Quaternary' heading is inconsistent with Holocene terminology.
comments.request: Rename the heading for consistency.
comments.quote: Just a note that line 120 heading is the only use of the words “Late Quaternary,” throughout the manuscript and might unclear for SDM users who might not think on geologic timescales

comments.issue: The statement at lines 248-250 lacks a supporting figure reference.
comments.request: Add the supporting figure reference.
comments.quote: Line 248-250 add reference to a figure to support this statement

comments.issue: Historical period is undefined in Figure S8.
comments.request: Add '(1901-2000)' after historical conditions.
comments.quote: Fig S8, please add “(1901-2000)” after “historical conditions”

comments.issue: The 'more accurately' claim for PEM refugia lacks pollen evidence for that period.
comments.request: Clarify the basis for the accuracy claim.
comments.quote: Line 224 states that PEMs predicted -12kyr BP refugia “more accurately” but it’s unclear how this is determined if no pollen samples were found during that period (Fig 2)

comments.issue: Line-level copy edits at lines 224, 288, 313, 272 and 43 (punctuation and word errors).
comments.quote: Line 313: warranty seems like the wrong word here. Did you mean guarantee? Please check.

comments.issue: Captions S4-S7 lack scientific names.
comments.request: Add scientific names to the captions.
comments.quote: Please add scientific names to figure captions S4-7 so they can be more easily compared to Fig S9 and elsewhere where scientific names are used (Results)

comments.issue: Figure 3A marking is inconsistent with panels B and D.
comments.request: Use a labelled vertical dashed line.
comments.quote: Fig 3, change triangle to vertical dashed line with labels “Early Holocene” and “Late-Middle Holocene” on panel A to be consistent with panels B and D

comments.issue: Figure S10d lacks grouping letters.
comments.request: Add grouping letters or explain their absence.
comments.quote: Fig S10d: please add grouping letters or clarify that the lack of them indicates no difference

comments.issue: The figure reference at line 323 may not match the no-migration point.
comments.request: Double-check the reference.
comments.quote: Line 323; I am not sure this figure reference to no-migration models is the same as this point about models after 11kyr BP, please double check

comments.issue: Whether five species or four genera were modelled is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the species/genera grouping.
comments.quote: Line 58, condense to 4 genera? It is not clear whether the SDM is different for each of 5 species or if two are grouped

comments.issue: Figure S10a is never cited in the text.
comments.request: Cite Figure S10a.
comments.quote: Fig S10a is not referenced

comments.issue: Figures S4 and S5 are not cited in the text.
comments.request: Cite Figures S4 and S5.
comments.quote: Figs S4 and S5 are not referenced (I think)

reviews.assessment: Well-written and relevant, but findings are unsurprising, methods lack detail and CSDMs deserve a more balanced treatment.

comments.issue: Findings are unsurprising; PEM transferability is already recognized and CSDMs can be improved and scaled.
comments.request: Clarify the novel contribution relative to prior work.
comments.quote: the conclusions, in my opinion, are not a surprise. CSDMs need simple data (only species occurrences and environmental predictors), PEMs require a number of parameters

comments.issue: The continued usefulness of CSDMs is not acknowledged in the interpretation.
comments.request: Discuss CSDM value and cite the recent Global Change Biology work.
comments.quote: the alternative interpretation can be that CSDMs are still helpful (though not as powerful as PEMs)

comments.issue: Methods lack detail on PHENOFIT parameters and occurrence records.
comments.request: Provide detailed explanations, e.g. in the Supporting Information.
comments.quote: Maybe due to the word limit, this manuscript lacks details in the methods. For instance, how to obtain the parameters for PHENOFIT, how to obtain species occurrence records

comments.issue: Whether CSDM algorithm parameters were optimized is unclear.
comments.request: State whether and how parameters were optimized.
comments.quote: Did authors optimize the parameters for GLM, GAM, BRT, random forest, and MaxEnt? If so, how? Please make it clear

comments.issue: Niche estimation from occurrence data ignores non-climatic drivers and ecological marginalization.
comments.request: Address ecological marginalization in niche estimation.
comments.quote: which highlights that ecological marginalization is widespread. If this is also true in tree species (I believe so), then we cannot accurately estimate species niche from occurrence data

title: Paleorecords Reveal Biological Mechanisms Crucial for Reliable Species Range Shift Projections Amid Rapid Climate Change

study.system: coho salmon in California; individual movement and population dynamics

editor_summary: Editor reports reviewers appreciated the study's quality and clarity; asks for more environmental and management context, and defends the paper against a reviewer's concern that its conceptual advance is limited.

reviews.assessment: Publishable with revisions: asks for clearer result presentation, corrected figure references, and more discussion of implications.

comments.issue: Ongoing restoration, which could drive the life history variation studied, is not described.
comments.request: Describe the ongoing restoration and its potential role.
comments.quote: This is a missed opportunity as that restoration can potentially play a role in driving the life history variation on which the authors base their study

comments.issue: Line-level figure-reference corrections at Lines 245, 269 and 274.
comments.quote: There are some confusing points in the presentation of the results.

comments.issue: Down-migration and emigration may be conflated, with a wrong figure reference at Line 250.
comments.request: Distinguish the two terms and correct the figure reference.
comments.quote: Either the figure reference is wrong, or the authors are conflating the two terms.

comments.issue: Text says natal rearers are over-represented among adult returns, but Fig. 5A shows 61% non-natal.
comments.request: Resolve whether the statement or the figure is wrong.
comments.quote: there is a problem in that the figure shows 19/31 (61%) of adult returns coming from non-natal rearing individuals

comments.issue: The analysis behind Fig. 5C and its standardization to the group long-term mean are not explained.
comments.request: Explain this analysis more fully.
comments.quote: More explanation of that analysis would make it easier to see the value in, and interpret, Fig. 5C

comments.issue: Methods do not make clear when the samples behind Fig. 5E were taken.
comments.request: Add detail on sampling times for this figure.
comments.quote: Some more detail in the methods would be good as to confirm when these samples were taken - i.e., I got lost in where the data for this figure came from.

comments.issue: Gray boxes for the 14-day flow window are not visible in Fig. 6A.
comments.request: Make the gray boxes visible.
comments.quote: I am not able to see gray boxes encompassing the 14-day flow window following the release period

comments.issue: Discussion unnecessarily restates results, delaying the evolutionary mechanisms section.
comments.request: Cut the restatement and reach the mechanisms sooner.
comments.quote: The Discussion section is generally well thought out, though there is a bit of restatement of results, which is unnecessary.

comments.issue: Implications of stream-overwintering and a third rearing strategy elsewhere are not discussed.
comments.request: Speculate on how a third rearing strategy would affect stability.
comments.quote: would you speculate that the third rearing strategy might add to the stability of populations even over the two strategies in your system

comments.issue: Management implications of in-stream habitat restoration for rearing diversity are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how restoration might reduce or enhance intrapopulation diversity.
comments.quote: what about in-stream habitat restoration? Treating impacted habitat with enhancing features might drive increased residence time in the natal streams.

reviews.assessment: Very positive on the study itself but doubts it fits Ecology Letters or has broad appeal beyond salmon science.
strengths: convincing demonstration of stabilizing behavioural variation

comments.issue: Weak fit with the journal and limited conceptual advance; doubts about broader appeal.
comments.request: Consider that case studies or straight empirical journals may fit better.
comments.quote: My only serious reservation for this paper is a weak fit with this journal which has seemed to emphasize development of new theory

title: Variation in Salmon Migration Phenology Bolsters Population Stability but Is Threatened by Drought

study.system: field aphids, Hamiltonella symbionts and parasitoids; 1000+ samples

editor_summary: Editor notes both reviewers question whether Hamiltonella-parasitoid correlations are confounded by aphid phylogenetic relatedness and asks for phylogenetic analyses to support the main conclusions.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and credible result, but host specialization makes the parasitoid-Hamiltonella association almost unavoidable without correcting for aphid relatedness.
strengths: impressive sample set of over 1000 parasitized aphids
interesting result with a credible explanation

comments.issue: Narrow host ranges of parasitoids and Hamiltonella strains make a statistical association almost unavoidable even without a causal link.
comments.request: Correct for aphid relatedness using a phylogenetic distance matrix, e.g. partial Mantel or MMRR.
comments.quote: I fear that it is almost unavoidable to find a statistical association between Parasitoid species and Hamiltonella strains, even if their variation is not causally related

comments.issue: Whether symbiont DNA is always detectable in aphid mummies was not validated with known samples.
comments.request: Report a detection test with known samples.
comments.quote: Did the authors test with known samples if they can always detect the symbiont DNA in aphid mummies?

comments.issue: Molecular parasitoid identifications were not sanity-checked morphologically; the Lysiphlebus testaceipes record is doubtful for the UK.
comments.request: Verify identifications, including morphologically where possible.
comments.quote: Was there a sanity check of the molecular identifications of parasitoid species by also identifying some of the parasitoid wasps morphologically

comments.issue: The abstract omits the potential role of parasitoids as vectors of symbionts.
comments.request: Mention this role in the abstract.
comments.quote: The potential role of parasitoids in shaping Hamiltonella genotype distributions not only as selective agents but also as vectors of symbionts is adequately discussed in the manuscript but not mentioned in the abstract.

comments.issue: Line 116 wording is imprecise: Hamiltonella prevents parasitoid development after attack rather than protecting from attacks.
comments.request: Correct the wording.
comments.quote: Hamiltonella does not really protect aphids from the attacks of parasitoids, but it prevents the parasitoids’ development after attack/oviposition.

comments.issue: The sampling strategy (mummified and live aphids plus an additional sample set) is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the sampling design.
comments.quote: The sampling strategy is not entirely clear. Probably just a matter of wording.

comments.issue: Results are mixed with discussion and methods text, with redundant or misplaced passages (L151-155, L190-198, L209-222, L294-297, L385-389) and a light discussion.

comments.issue: Data and code are not provided, making the study impossible to reproduce without the species list.

comments.issue: The study relies entirely on one phylogeny without sensitivity analysis (also L302).

comments.issue: The meaning of 'ordination space' at L123-124 is not obvious.

comments.issue: The objective is not split into classification and impact prediction components.

comments.issue: It is unclear how Fig. S1 illustrates the L155 claim.

comments.issue: Units for phylogenetic diversity are missing at L160 and L311.

comments.issue: The analysis behind results at L201-205 is not described in the Methods.

comments.issue: Results at L223-238 lack a detailed discussion relative to the literature.

comments.issue: Line-level edits: 'in other global regions' wording (L195) and phrasing at L257-259.

comments.issue: Submodels are named inconsistently across the paper.

comments.issue: Text at L330-338 refers to material not presented in the paper.

comments.issue: R² is missing for the composite models (L375-377, Table S9).

title: What Is a Specialist? Quantifying Host Breadth Enables Impact Prediction for Invasive Herbivores

study.system: animal dispersal; bioenergetic model of maximum dispersal distances

editor_summary: Editor: reviewers recognize the importance and applaud the efforts, but share significant concerns about logic and methodology; assumptions need validation, the work needs broader framing, and the conclusion reads like a summary.

reviews.assessment: Elegant, clearly derived bioenergetic dispersal model with great potential, though it should engage more with movement ecology and validate a key assumption.
strengths: crisp writing and clear model derivation

comments.issue: Nathan et al. 2008, the standard movement ecology framework, is not cited or engaged with.
comments.request: Position the dispersal model within the Nathan et al. movement framework.
comments.quote: Nathan et al. 2008 PNAS has been the go-to theoretical framework for movement ecology since its publication

comments.issue: Adjacent mechanistic models of movement, such as PDE and integro-difference equation models, are overlooked.
comments.request: Consider and cite other mechanistic models of animal dispersal.
comments.quote: At present, it feels like the paper is overlooking some adjacent literature with some common goals (i.e., mechanistic models of movement)

comments.issue: The comparison with the Hein et al. 2012 migration model appears too late.
comments.request: Present the comparison with Hein et al. 2012 earlier in the manuscript.
comments.quote: I encourage the authors to present this comparison earlier in the ms

comments.issue: The statement on L91-95 feels out of place in the introduction.
comments.request: Move the statement to a more appropriate place.
comments.quote: The statement on L91-95 felt a bit out of place here

comments.issue: L146-148 could simply refer to equations 2 and 3.
comments.request: Replace the text with references to equations 2 and 3.
comments.quote: Would it be better to just refer to equations 2 and 3 here?

comments.issue: The 10% energy storage requirement upon arrival lacks empirical support and sensitivity testing.
comments.request: Provide empirical evidence or a sensitivity analysis for this assumption.
comments.quote: It would be even better if the authors could provide some empirical evidence to support this assumption and/or a sensitivity analysis to demonstrate how this assumption impacts estimates of maximum dispersal distance

comments.issue: How the statements or actions on L199-203 differ from L216-218 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the difference between these passages.
comments.quote: How do the statements or actions in L199-203 differ than on L216-218. Can the authors clarify?

comments.issue: 'This' on L293 has no clear referent.
comments.request: Clarify what 'this' refers to.
comments.quote: 11) L293. What is “this” in the sentence?

comments.issue: The model omits the reverse interaction, energy spent avoiding predation.

comments.quote: I suppose the model also does not consider interactions in the other direction, i.e., energy used to avoid predation

comments.issue: Data points above the model prediction line are not investigated for alternative explanations.
comments.request: Examine the outlier species for alternative explanations.
comments.quote: why not look into some of those species/data points that lie above the model prediction line to see if alternate explanations arise to explain these data points?

title: A Mechanistic Approach to Animal Dispersal—Quantifying Energetics and Maximum Distances

study.system: food webs; 144 empirical and 2,687 simulated webs

editor_summary: Both reviewers like the manuscript and see potential; editor asks for clarity for a broad audience and better communication of its significance.

reviews.assessment: One of the most interesting recent articles; only minor clarifications about model assumptions and parameters.
strengths: interesting to a very broad ecological audience
well-written with clearly presented methods and results

comments.issue: Two line-level wording corrections (missing and misplaced words in comments 1 and 6).
comments.quote: A word seems to be missing/misplaced here. Maybe:

comments.issue: Whether the minimum stability value of s biases the results is unchecked, though the reviewer does not demand new runs.
comments.request: Explain whether a less conservative s could change results qualitatively.
comments.quote: Can this assumption (i.e., the minimum value of s to ensure community stability) be a potential source of error? Would the results change qualitatively if less conservative (i.e., giving "more" stability) value of s had been used?

comments.issue: The two-step assimilation efficiency (e and f) is redundant and its empirical basis is questionable.
comments.request: Justify or combine the two assimilation parameters and their values.
comments.quote: Basically, parameters e and f seem to have the same meaning, so in principle they could be combined into a single one.

comments.issue: The meaning and value of parameter v in equation 5 are not explained.
comments.request: Define parameter v and state its value.
comments.quote: What is the meaning and value of parameter v? Maybe nutrient-to-biomass ratio of the species B?

comments.issue: The use of a type III functional response is not stated in the Methods.
comments.request: Mention the type III functional response in the Methods.
comments.quote: It could be good to mention somewhere here that a type III functional response has been used.

comments.issue: Why simulated webs split bimodally into bottom- and top-heavy types, and the provenance of size-scaling parameters, is unexplained.
comments.request: Explore parameter ranges and combinations and document the sources of the scaling parameters.
comments.quote: I am not sure I fully understand the reasoning behind the assumptions that led to the distribution of bottom- vs. top-heavy food webs in the models. Figure 2 (i) shows an unusual bimodal (with two peaks) distribution.

comments.issue: Attack rate loses meaning under a type III response, so the Rall et al. size scalings may not apply.
comments.request: Check that the assumed body-size scalings make sense for a type III response.
comments.quote: with a type III functional response, the attack rate loses its meaning as it is strongly coupled with the exponent. Do the assumed body size scalings from Rall et al. (2012) make sense for a type III response?

comments.issue: An extra stable state produced by the type III response may explain the predominance of top-heavy simulated webs.
comments.request: Consider this mechanism when interpreting the web distribution.
comments.quote: A type III response is known to produce an additional stable point of modeled food webs, that is, at low prey population biomass. This might correlate with more top-heavy food webs

comments.issue: Empirical marine webs are bottom-heavy while simulated webs are mostly top-heavy; the discrepancy is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain why the simulated webs differ from empirical ones.
comments.quote: In general, it is striking that empirical marine food webs were nearly always bottom-heavy, yet the simulated food webs (based on some marine invertebrate parameters) were mostly top-heavy. Why this discrepancy?

comments.issue: Readers may not realize that biomass always refers to whole-population biomass.
comments.request: State early that biomass means population biomass.
comments.quote: It could be good to early on, maybe just once, write explicitly (alongside "body mass" as here) "POPULATION biomass", just so the readers know that the word "biomass" refers always to the whole population.

comments.issue: The choice of per capita rather than total net effects is not justified.
comments.request: Explain the choice of per capita net effects and which measure is more relevant.
comments.quote: So there is a difference between using a per capita vs. total net effects approach. Why did you choose to use the per capita one? Which one is more relevant?

reviews.assessment: Challenges the loose keystone-ness and press-perturbation definitions and the equilibrium assumption behind the empirical analyses.

comments.issue: The headline conclusion largely restates the Introduction and prior expectations about large species.
comments.quote: The conclusion reached by the present authors is “Our findings reveal that larger, more generalistic species at higher trophic levels are more likely to be keystone species in food webs with negative scaling”

comments.issue: Keystone-ness is never formally defined before use and the operational metric may not represent it.
comments.request: Define keystone-ness explicitly before using the term.
comments.quote: One needs to explicitly define keystone-ness before one writes an entire ms about it.

comments.issue: Chronic and global disturbances are labelled press perturbations, overextending the classic definition.
comments.request: Use the classic Bender et al. definition or justify the extension.
comments.quote: I think the present authors are taking excessive liberties in what they refer to as press perturbations.

comments.issue: Real press disturbances affect many species, so single-species net effects cannot be isolated.
comments.request: Acknowledge this limitation of the single-species perturbation approach.
comments.quote: Given the context that the authors are examining food webs, there is little opportunity to predict net effects based on one perturbed species. On the contrary, any natural press experiment would typically involve many species being affected by the disturbance

comments.issue: Whether the 144 empirical food webs were at equilibrium, as the inverse-matrix approach assumes, is questionable.
comments.request: Assess and discuss the equilibrium assumption for the empirical webs.
comments.quote: I also question whether any of the 144 empirical food webs represented communities and / or species at equilibrium, an assumption of the approach used by the present authors

comments.issue: The empirical food web data and analysis are described too thinly to judge their appropriateness.
comments.request: Describe the raw empirical data and analyses in more detail without referring to SI.
comments.quote: While the modeling approach is much more clear, the description of the analyses of the empirical food webs seems insufficient for a reader to judge the appropriateness of the analyses.

comments.issue: OLS regressions may be driven by high-leverage points and no diagnostics are reported.
comments.request: Report model diagnostics or use a robust regression approach such as Huber regression.
comments.quote: OLS is quite sensitive to high-leverage points, and the visual representation of the data (e.g., Fig. 1a, 1b, 1c, 2e, 2g, 2h, S11g, S11h, S12g, S12h, S14b) suggest that high-leverage points might be present in those models.

comments.issue: Criteria for the scaling-exponent ranges and bins used in the regressions are unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the scaling-exponent ranges and bins were chosen.
comments.quote: It is unclear from the Methods in the main text what the criteria were for how these values were chosen.

comments.issue: Separate models per exponent range were built instead of one global model with exponent as a predictor.
comments.request: Justify or replace the separate regressions with a single global model.
comments.quote: Finally, it’s not clear why the present authors did not add a scaling exponent as a predictor term in one global model instead of building separate models?

comments.issue: Data-related limitations such as proxy body masses and equal parameters are not discussed.
comments.request: Address these limitations in the Discussion.
comments.quote: There are several potential limitations to this study that can be attributed to the limited data availability and so I would have like to have seen some of these limitations addressed in the Discussion.

comments.issue: No hypotheses are offered for why patterns differ between bottom- and top-heavy webs.
comments.request: Suggest why the observed patterns depend on web structure.
comments.quote: For example, the authors emphasize that some patterns depend on whether the web is bottom- or top-heavy (line 347), but there are no suggestions on why this might be the case.

comments.issue: The abstract does not explain what bottom-heavy and top-heavy food webs refer to.
comments.request: Explain these terms in the abstract.
comments.quote: Abstract is too vague on what "bottom-heavy" or "top-heavy" food webs reference.

comments.issue: The distinction between species body mass and biomass is not made clear.
comments.request: Use wording that distinguishes body mass from biomass.
comments.quote: Perhaps, wording like “scaling/relationship among species' body mass and its biomass within ecosystem” would make this distinction more clear.

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'scaling' means in this context.
comments.request: Use clearer wording such as 'directional relationship'.
comments.quote: It is also unclear what “scaling” is in this context. Maybe, “directional relationship” may be better.

comments.issue: No formal definition of keystone species is given despite the term's central role.
comments.request: Clarify the keystone species definition early on.
comments.quote: The whole manuscript rotates around the term “keystone-ness”, but there is no formal definition of what a keystone species is before this point.

comments.issue: 'Biomass spectrum' is used once and is redundant.
comments.request: Remove or properly use the term 'biomass spectrum'.
comments.quote: The term “biomass spectrum” is mentioned, but it appears to only be used once, thus redundant and superfluous to the manuscript.

comments.issue: Community matrix and inverse community matrix are explained too late.
comments.request: Explain these terms at their first mention.
comments.quote: A reader might find it unclear what a “community matrix” or “inverse community matrix” is, so its first mention would be a better place for explanation instead of lines 126-127.

comments.issue: Nonlinear responses are not defined.
comments.request: Define nonlinear responses.
comments.quote: Unclear what is meant by nonlinear responses - define.

comments.issue: Five line-level copy edits: minus signs, unit formatting, sentence structure and range wording.
comments.quote: a math pedant would like to see a minus sign (−) rather than a hyphen (-) where appropriate.

comments.issue: The number of models built and how many reached stable equilibrium are not reported.
comments.request: Report how many models were built and how many reached stable equilibrium.
comments.quote: Please report on how many models did the authors attempt to build (from line 248 it can be assumed that 5,000 were initially built) and then how many reached a stable equilibrium.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the community matrices operate on species or on trophic groups.
comments.request: Describe the data structure clearly, including species versus trophic group levels.
comments.quote: It is unclear whether the community matrices used in this study operate on species levels. One would assume that yes, because the narrative throughout the manuscript suggest so

comments.issue: How keystone-ness was quantified is glossed over and introduced too late.
comments.request: Provide the quantification in the Introduction and Abstract.
comments.quote: This important point on how keystone-ness was quantified seems to be glossed over. As mentioned above, this should be provided in the Introduction and Abstract.

comments.issue: Trait calculations are only described in the Supplementary Methods.
comments.request: Give a brief explanation of each trait calculation in the main text.
comments.quote: The paragraph refers to the Supplementary Methods regarding details on calculation of traits, but it would be helpful to provide a brief explanation for each in the main text.

comments.issue: The study is descriptive and does not really investigate trait effects on keystone-ness.
comments.request: Reword to say the study investigated relationships among traits.
comments.quote: I am not sure I agree that this study investigated the effects of traits on keystone-ness as the study itself is quite descriptive

comments.issue: It is unclear whether species playing an important role are meant to be keystones.
comments.request: Clarify the sentence.
comments.quote: Do the authors mean that the species that play important role are keystones?

comments.issue: The importance of identifying keystone species is not highlighted enough.
comments.request: State it as a main premise in the Abstract.
comments.quote: I think the point on the importance of identification of keystone species should be highlighted more, perhaps even stated as a main premise in the Abstract.

comments.issue: 27% of webs is described as 'only', understating a considerable proportion.
comments.request: Remove or soften the word 'only'.
comments.quote: 39 out of 144 is 27%, one wouldn't call it "only" as this is quite a considerable proportion of food webs showing negative relationship between keystone-ness and the node degree.

comments.issue: The Taylor series sentence is hard to follow without prior introduction.
comments.request: Elaborate on linear approximations earlier or drop the Taylor series mention.
comments.quote: The sentence on how an approximation of nonlinear responses of the system is representative could perhaps stand on its own without mentioning a Taylor series given that they have not been mentioned prior to this in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Fig. 1i duplicates Fig. S2d.
comments.request: Remove the duplicate figure panel.
comments.quote: Fig. 1i is the same as Fig. S2d, it is unclear why the authors are presenting it twice.

title: Body Mass–Biomass Scaling Modulates Species Keystone‐Ness to Press Perturbations

strengths: mechanistic model adds an additional dimension

comments.issue: Epigenetic inheritance of host resistance is only mentioned late, not introduced early in the introduction.

comments.quote: It would be great to acknowledge epigenetic inheritance of host resistance in the second paragraph of the introduction so that readers are prepared to return to this idea later in the paper

comments.issue: The nematode and pathogen maintenance description is poorly organised for clarity and flow.

comments.issue: 'Infection exposure' is used inconsistently with 'pathogen exposure' elsewhere.

comments.issue: The concluding statement that a warmer world is more infectious overstates the complex climate-disease relationship.

comments.issue: Arrows in Figure 1 are misaligned vertically and vary in size.

comments.issue: Figure 2 caption does not state that results are from the single-generation experiment.
comments.request: State this in the caption.

comments.issue: Several typographical errors (van Baalen references, verb forms, figure captions).
