comments.quote: Lines 221-222 – see my comment above, could provide more details on these analyses.

comments.issue: The provenance of the 95% and 60% figures at line 263 is unclear.
comments.request: Cite the source of these figures.
comments.quote: the figures presented in this sentence (95%, 60%) – it is not clear from which part of the analyses they come from

comments.issue: Figure 2 lacks panel labels A-D.
comments.request: Add panel labels.
comments.quote: Figure 2 – don’t forget to add the panel labels (A-D).

title: Island Plant Species Distributions Contracted at the Cooler Edge Compared to Mainland

study.system: wild birds; egg hormones and fitness proxies, meta-analysis

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewers found much to like but raised many thoughtful comments essential to address before judging suitability; authors strongly urged to address them carefully.

reviews.assessment: Robust and admirably thorough meta-analysis with convincing negative results, but one conceptual concern about the adaptive interpretation.
strengths: results convincingly show no generalizable fitness association

comments.issue: Conceptual framework needs better explanation and justification.
comments.request: Better explain and justify the conceptual framework.
comments.quote: the authors need to better explain and justify their conceptual framework, and seriously reconsider (or better support) their broad conclusions

comments.issue: Evidence is judged insufficient for the conclusion doubting an adaptive role of egg hormones.
comments.request: Reconsider or better support the broad conclusions.
comments.quote: I am not sure the evidence is sufficient to support this conclusion.

comments.issue: Adaptive plasticity predicts null correlations; the key contrast of individuals unable to adjust hormones is missing.
comments.request: Assess the reframed adaptive predictions with the meta-analysis data.
comments.quote: with natural correlations, the important contrast is missing: that of the individual or population that is unable to adaptively adjust egg hormones

comments.issue: Methods wording is excessive; methodology could be summarized in main text and expanded in supplement.
comments.request: Shorten methodological wording.
comments.quote: the manuscript could be shortened by reducing wording around this methodology

comments.issue: Line 56-57 is confusingly worded about the size of maternal effects.
comments.request: Clarify the magnitude statement.
comments.quote: Maternal effects contribute to half of all observed phenotypic variation, or half as much as additive genetic effects do?

comments.issue: Biological and methodological 'hypotheses' mostly present predictions; underlying theory is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the theory behind the predictions.
comments.quote: These are described as biological and methodological "hypotheses" but most only present predictions. The underlying theory supporting these predictions should be better explained

comments.issue: Maternal versus offspring fitness proxies are conflated; 'controlled by her' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction between maternal and offspring fitness proxies.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to clarify how maternal and offspring fitness are different, and whether they would be expected to have different fitness associations.

comments.issue: Too many random intercepts for a small dataset; many explain little variation.
comments.request: Consider reducing the random effect structure.
comments.quote: That's a lot of random intercepts for a relatively small dataset. Did the authors consider any variation in random effect structures before running their main analyses?

comments.issue: Figure 1 colors are not colorblind-friendly.
comments.request: Use colorblind-friendly colors.
comments.quote: Figure 1 – would be great to use colorblind-friendly colors

comments.issue: 'Tended to be' is used for non-significant relationships with CIs fully overlapping zero.
comments.request: Avoid trend language for non-significant results.
comments.quote: the authors use the phrase "tended to be" several times to describe non-significant relationships with relatively high p-values and large CIs that fully overlap zero

comments.issue: Thyroid hormone p-value and means look inconsistent with Figure 4 and the data distribution.
comments.request: Check and explain this apparent inconsistency.
comments.quote: this p-value for thyroid hormones seems lower than you would expect given the results (and largely overlapping CIs) in figure 4

comments.issue: Figure 5A mean for 'after independence' does not fit the scattered data; points may be hidden.
comments.request: Explain the low mean and whether points are hidden.
comments.quote: the mean effect size in panel A for "after independence" doesn't seem to fit with the scattered data - why is it so low, relative to the distribution of the data?

comments.issue: Predictions at lines 619-621 rest on a flawed premise and misunderstanding of adaptive plasticity.
comments.request: Clarify the thinking around adaptive plasticity.
comments.quote: these predictions seem based on a flawed premise, and a misunderstanding of adaptive plasticity

reviews.assessment: By far the best meta-analysis in this area, thorough and well pre-registered, but asks for clearer methodology, hypothesis rationale and better conclusions.
strengths: by far the best study in this respect
applaud the pre-registration of methods and hypotheses
thorough in testing hypotheses with up-to-date methodology
very thorough study with an important message

comments.issue: Advanced meta-analytic methodology, such as orchard plots, is not explained enough for general readers.
comments.request: Add more explanation to aid digestibility.
comments.quote: to my knowledge the orchard plots are only a few years ago invented but what the plots really mean is not well explained

comments.issue: Preregistered files could not be accessed or found.
comments.request: Make the preregistered files accessible.
comments.quote: For some reason I could not access or even found the preregistered files.

comments.issue: Hypotheses lack argumentation; explanatory sentences about them are needed.
comments.request: Add explanatory sentences for the hypotheses.
comments.quote: Perhaps adding one or two explanatory sentences of the hypotheses in this manuscript would be good anyway

comments.issue: Conclusions stress doubtful evolutionary relevance while the discussion lists reasons the signal may be masked.
comments.request: Make the message consistent between discussion and conclusions.
comments.quote: the authors clearly state that the data cast doubt on the evolutionary relevance of these egg hormones, but on the other hand they discuss a series of reasons why this may be masked

comments.issue: No concrete suggestions for how the field should move forward; paper risks discouraging research.
comments.request: Provide concrete ways forward for the field.
comments.quote: There are no concrete suggestion of how to move forward.

comments.issue: Unclear whether analyses differentiate adaptive function within nests, between nests, and between species.
comments.request: Clarify whether and how analyses separate these levels.
comments.quote: The adaptive function of egg hormones may be different at different levels, such as within a nest for adjustment of sibling competition, between nests depending on ecological or parental conditions, and between species depending on life history.

comments.issue: If parents optimize hormone levels per nest and egg, null correlations are expected while manipulations become detrimental.
comments.request: Consider this optimality scenario when interpreting results.
comments.quote: If parents optimize for each nest and egg the best hormone concentration, correlations would not find anything whereas experimental manipulation may have often detrimental effects

comments.issue: Corticosterone assays in yolk or albumin are unreliable; antibodies were not designed for egg hormones.
comments.request: Address the reliability of corticosterone measurements.
comments.quote: I am still not convinced that the determination of yolk or albumin corticosterone is reliable.

comments.issue: Including maternal manipulations tests a different mechanism from egg hormone effects.
comments.request: Justify or separate the maternal manipulation category.
comments.quote: I realize that the type of manipulation (mother or egg) was included for the experimental part but even in that case to me this seems to test two different mechanisms.

comments.issue: Mixing indirect and direct fitness proxies may add substantial noise.
comments.request: Assess the noise introduced by diverse proxies.
comments.quote: Some of these are to my knowledge quite indirect measures such as gape width of chicks whereas others are much more direct such as survival.

comments.issue: Focus is on maternal fitness but most dependent variables are chick traits, and mother and chick interests may conflict.
comments.request: Explain how mother-chick conflict is incorporated in the analyses.
comments.quote: However, most of the dependent variables are chick traits. And the interest of the mother and chick may not always align.

comments.issue: Hypothesis BH 1.2 wrongly assumes corticosterone has a negative effect on fitness.
comments.request: Reconsider the premise that corticosterone reduces fitness.
comments.quote: Over the past decades it has become clear that the negative connotation of this hormone is not justified and that it act to adjust the organism to its environment.

comments.issue: MH 1's expectation that injection studies show stronger fitness effects is not understood.
comments.request: Explain the reasoning behind MH 1.
comments.quote: MH 1 assumes that hormone injection studies would have stronger fitness effects than correlational studies. I do not understand why.

comments.issue: Eggs collected during laying have hormone levels that deviate from what the mother deposited.
comments.request: Consider splitting the dataset by egg collection type.
comments.quote: Eggs collected during egg laying likely have hormone levels that deviate very much from what the mother had put in.

comments.issue: Unclear whether 'wild birds' means undomesticated species and field studies only.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of 'wild birds'.
comments.quote: The study is performed on wild birds. Does that mean undomesticated species and also only field studies?

comments.issue: Definition of maternal effects ignores their genetic basis and control.
comments.request: Adjust the definition of maternal effects.
comments.quote: Perhaps the definition of maternal effects may be adjusted. They are not completely independent from genes.

comments.issue: Study area variables are mentioned as covariates but absent from the analyses.
comments.request: Clarify whether these variables were registered but unused.
comments.quote: Study area variables are mentioned as taken into account but they are not mentioned in the analyses themselves, so was this registered but not used?

comments.issue: 'Experimental study object' is ambiguous about whether correlational studies are included.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the term 'experimental'.
comments.quote: Does experimental here means studies were egg or mother were manipulated or does this analysis includes also correlational studies?

comments.issue: Fig. 3 thin whiskers are invisible and the meaning of distances and mean placement is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the plot elements and why the mean is off-center.
comments.quote: I did not see the thin whiskers. Also, please explain what the distance between the horizontal line and the individual dots means and why the mean is not in the middle of the distributions.

comments.issue: Post hoc tests are reported without the interaction term itself.
comments.request: Report the interaction term.
comments.quote: Posthoc tests are reported but not the interaction term itself.

comments.issue: Line 620 predicts a positive thyroid hormone effect, contradicting the stated lack of directional prediction.
comments.request: Resolve the inconsistency in the hypothesis direction.
comments.quote: Here you hypothesize that thyroid hormones increase fitness whereas in the introduction with hypotheses you write that you did not have a prediction about direction

reviews.assessment: Timely, rigorous, pre-registered meta-analysis whose negative results are a strength; only minor comments.
strengths: negative results viewed as a strength

comments.issue: List of the 57 included studies is missing; authors should be credited via the cited literature.
comments.request: Provide the list of included studies.
comments.quote: I miss the list of 57 studies included in the meta-analysis (Supplementary Figure 3).

comments.issue: Excluded studies are not documented; e.g., Remes 2011 is missing, so screening cannot be judged.
comments.request: Report which studies were excluded and why.
comments.quote: Without detailed information about excluded studies, it is unclear whether this study was missed during the search, excluded during screening, or failed some selection criteria.

comments.issue: References for three studies are missing in Supplementary Information S1.
comments.request: Add the missing references.
comments.quote: References for Freeberg et al. 2024, Holman et al. 2015, and Keaney et al. 2024 are missing in the Supplementary Information S1.

comments.issue: Pearson's r values outside -1 to 1, unlike Zr, need explanation.
comments.request: Explain any transformation producing values outside this range.
comments.quote: Pearson's r is limited to values between -1 and 1, unlike Zr. If values outside this range appear as a result of any transformation, this should be explained.

comments.issue: Extreme correlation values are associated with the largest sample sizes, which is highly unusual.
comments.request: Investigate this unusual association.
comments.quote: the extreme values of the correlation coefficient seem to be associated with the largest sample sizes (largest symbols, i.e., smallest SE), which is highly unusual

comments.issue: Tables 1, 2 and 4 duplicate Figures 3, 4 and 6; only p-values are unique.
comments.request: Remove the redundant tables and report p-values in the text.
comments.quote: Tables 1, 2, and 4 repeat information already provided in Figures 3, 4, and 6, respectively. They are redundant and should be removed.

comments.issue: The term 'intercept' in orchard plots and Table 3 is difficult to understand.
comments.request: Explain what 'intercept' means here.
comments.quote: I find it difficult to understand what the term "intercept" means in the context of orchard plots (e.g., Figure 2) and in Table 3.

comments.issue: Study is not framed against previous reviews; overlap in studies and effect sizes is unknown.
comments.request: Frame differences from earlier reviews and report overlap.
comments.quote: The study could better frame how it differs from previous reviews, such as Podmokla et al. 2018 and Moore et al. 2019, including information about the number of studies and effect sizes overlapping between these reviews.

comments.issue: Heterogeneity paragraph is long, highly technical, and relies heavily on one unpublished study.
comments.request: Condense the paragraph and reduce reliance on the unpublished study.
comments.quote: The paragraph on lines 673–701, which discusses the heterogeneity of effect sizes at various levels (e.g., between and within studies), is very long and highly technical.

comments.issue: Heterogeneity is not compared with previous meta-analyses of maternal effects.
comments.request: Compare heterogeneity levels with previous meta-analyses.
comments.quote: I recommend comparing the heterogeneity levels in the present study to those reported in previous meta-analyses of maternal effects.

comments.issue: Zero among-study variation in all models seems unusual and needs explanation.
comments.request: Discuss possible reasons for zero among-study variation.
comments.quote: the finding of zero among-study variation in all models (lines 678-679) seems unusual. Typically, some variation between studies is expected.

title: Do Egg Hormones Have Fitness Consequences in Wild Birds? A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis

study.system: three North American ungulates; GPS tracking, migration plasticity

reviews.assessment: Questions the novelty and broader significance, since plasticity and repeatability are well documented and acclimation is not actually tested.
strengths: topic has implications for understanding acclimation

comments.issue: Novelty is unclear because plasticity and repeatability are already well documented; the paper adds another trait-taxon case.
comments.request: Articulate the novel advance beyond documenting plasticity and repeatability.
comments.quote: As a result, the novelty of this paper is unclear given that empirical evidence of plasticity and repeatability is well documented and taxonomically widespread as described in the paper’s introduction.

comments.issue: The broader significance and knowledge gap are not conveyed in the abstract or introduction.
comments.request: Describe the knowledge gap and why it matters to a broad readership.
comments.quote: The authors could better convey the broader significance of their research if they included text in the Abstract and/or Introduction that describes the knowledge gap addressed by the study and why this gap is generally important.

comments.issue: “Both” at line 65 has no clear referent.
comments.request: Clarify what “both” refers to.
comments.quote: Line 65: ‘both’ of what? Line 107-108: Has any study demonstrated that population persistence is actually linked to migration timing?

comments.issue: No evidence is cited linking population persistence to migration timing.
comments.request: Provide a supporting reference or revise the sentence.
comments.quote: Has any study demonstrated that population persistence is actually linked to migration timing? If so, provide the supporting reference. If not, revise the sentence.

comments.issue: Statements about acclimation and repeatability are a tease because the paper does not assess these potentials.
comments.request: Soften statements that imply acclimation is demonstrated.
comments.quote: The potential for plasticity to serve as an acclimation mechanism is certainly interesting, but this statement (and others like it) is a bit of tease since the paper does not actually assess this potential.

comments.issue: “Anthropocene” has been formally rejected as a geological epoch term.
comments.request: Reconsider the use of “Anthropocene” at line 432.
comments.quote: Reconsider use of the term ‘Anthropocene’ given its recent formal rejection as a term to describe the current geological epoch.

reviews.assessment: Unique dataset but analyses underpowered, methods inconsistent, interpretation too definitive; regrets not offering a more positive assessment.

comments.issue: The discussion is too long and speculative, and the low statistical power is not acknowledged.
comments.request: Add caution and temper the conclusions.
comments.quote: I found the discussion section too long and often too speculative or broad, especially as I consider that the study has a low power that is not well acknowledged by the authors. More caution in the interpretation of the results is needed.

comments.issue: Most individuals have only three years of data, giving three points for slope estimation and very low power.
comments.request: Acknowledge the low power and test the robustness of the random slopes.
comments.quote: there are only three data points available for each individual to establish a relationship between the timing of spring green-up and variables related to migration timing

comments.issue: Repeatability may reflect local spatial context rather than intrinsic differences; spatial autocorrelation is not analysed.
comments.request: Explore spatial autocorrelation in migration timing and include it if significant.
comments.quote: I advocate for an exploration of the level of spatial autocorrelation in migration timing and for the inclusion of this autocorrelation in the analyses if found to be significant.

comments.issue: The selection analysis assumes independent locations while the Brownian bridge assumes non-independence; GPS fix rates are also missing.
comments.request: Justify or revise the selection analysis and report GPS fix rates.
comments.quote: there appears to be a contradiction in the methods employed: the Brownian bridge model is designed for use when successive locations can be considered non-independent

comments.issue: Whether seasonal ranges are stable between years is not described, so earlier arrival could reflect earlier halting.
comments.request: Describe how seasonal ranges were defined and whether they are stable across years.
comments.quote: I note a lack of information regarding the stability of seasonal ranges between years.

comments.issue: The justification for withholding raw location data conflicts with the project's public migration data initiative.
comments.request: Reconcile the data availability statement with the initiative's stated policy.
comments.quote: the discrepancy between the justifications provided in the manuscript and the ones provided on the website questions about the validity of the statement made in the manuscript

reviews.assessment: Potentially impactful study, but BLUP-based selection measures and repeatability estimates raise statistical concerns.

comments.issue: Using BLUP individual slopes in downstream analyses produces anticonservative p-values and incorrect inferences.
comments.request: Fit the logistic regression and slope correlations within a single joint model.
comments.quote: In short, a stats-on-stats approach leads to anticonservative p-values and therefore can lead to incorrect inferences.

comments.issue: Adjusted repeatabilities alone do not show the magnitude of among-individual variation.
comments.request: Present unadjusted repeatabilities and among-individual variances.
comments.quote: to have a better sense of the magnitude of variation present, it would be useful to present unadjusted repeatabilities

comments.issue: Definitions and naming in the migration section are not concrete.
comments.request: Define statistical parameters explicitly and clarify the DIC table.
comments.quote: I’d encourage the authors to be more concrete in their definitions and naming in the defining migration section—particularly given the section name.

comments.issue: The species name for elk is not provided at line 145.
comments.request: Provide the elk species name.
comments.quote: l. 145: The species name for elk should also be provided

comments.issue: IACUC information is incomplete.
comments.request: Provide additional IACUC details following the Animal Behavior Society guidelines.
comments.quote: Additional IACUC information should be provided (see, for example, the Animal Behavior Society’s guidelines).

comments.issue: The sampling breakdown in Table S1 is not given in the main text, hiding how little elk sampling there was.
comments.request: Move the sampling breakdown into the main text.
comments.quote: I would have appreciated the clear break down of sampling given in the top two rows of TS1 being in the main text. From what was provided, it wasn’t clear how little sampling there was of elk.

comments.issue: How standard deviations for repeatabilities were obtained is unclear, and the uncertainties seem too narrow.
comments.request: Clarify the uncertainty calculation and review the estimates.
comments.quote: I’m not sure how they’re getting SDs for their repeatabilities. Are they just calculating the standard deviation of the posterior?

comments.issue: Which model repeatability was calculated from and what variance was excluded is not stated.
comments.request: State the model used and the sources of variation excluded.
comments.quote: Also, which model was repeatability calculated from? This is necessary knowledge given that they provided adjusted repeatabilties: what sources of variation were excluded

comments.issue: The species order in Figure 2 follows neither phylogeny nor geography.
comments.request: Order species by a biologically relevant criterion.
comments.quote: The presentation of species isn’t consistent with either phylogeny (the elk are split) or geography (not corresponding to N->S or S->N based on Figure 1).

title: Consistent Individual Differences and Plasticity in Migration Behaviour of Three North American Ungulates

study.system: Drosophila melanogaster; experimental evolution at three temperature regimes, fitness, behavior, proteomics

editor_summary: All three reviewers were enthusiastic and recommend revision; the editor urges the authors to address all reviewer comments in the manuscript itself, not just in the response letter.

reviews.assessment: Novel and interesting question, appropriate methods and high-quality manuscript; the reviewer's comments are few and overall minor.

comments.issue: Unclear why both mated and unmated males were assayed and what can be learned from mated males.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for assaying both mating states.
comments.quote: The content of the mated male accessory gland could very indirectly tell what males transferred at mating, but no comparison was done between the set of proteins of virgin and mated males.

comments.issue: Sentence about bottles with 200 individuals each is ambiguous.
comments.request: Reword the sentence about the bottles.
comments.quote: Line 128-129 is it one or two bottles with 200 individuals each? Please reword that sentence.

comments.issue: Reproductive success may combine survivorship and productivity, and the standardization is unexplained and possibly confounded by survival.
comments.request: Explain the standardization and test robustness to survival differences.
comments.quote: How was standardization done? Is it robust to temperature dependent survival differences independent of mating system effects?

comments.issue: Bretman and Fricke 2019 is an odd citation; none of the mentioned parameters are assessed there.
comments.request: Replace or justify the citation.
comments.quote: Reference to Bretman and Fricke 2019 seems an odd citation here as none of the mentioned parameters are assessed in that study

comments.issue: Unclear whether one unknown sperm storage protein or several are meant.
comments.request: Clarify whether one or several proteins are meant.
comments.quote: is it an unknown sperm storage protein or is the name of a specific SFP missing if you refer to 'the sperm storage protein XXX'?

comments.issue: The claim that the cold regime is uniquely unpredictable is unconvincing since all regimes fluctuate similarly.
comments.request: Reconsider the reasoning about the cold regime.
comments.quote: also the cold regime fulfils the criteria of being constant, predictable and on a fine-grained ecological scale, just a few degrees colder. As such I do not find your reasoning here convincing.

comments.issue: "Differential evolution of SFP" is too general and should specify abundance and composition.
comments.request: Specify abundance and composition differences.
comments.quote: I find the mention of 'differential evolution of SFP' too general. I think it should be specified that you investigated differences in abundance and likely composition.

reviews.assessment: Highly engaging and important study; very positive overall, but the introduction needs work and the assays may not have been common garden.
strengths: significantly advances understanding of thermal stress and sexual conflict
results important and support the conclusions

comments.issue: The overview of previous work on environmental effects on sexual conflict is too brief.
comments.request: Expand the literature overview of environmental effects on sexual conflict.
comments.quote: I believe this section should provide a more comprehensive overview of the state of the art on the tested questions.

comments.issue: Tested hypotheses are introduced vaguely and late, without theory-based predictions.
comments.request: State the hypotheses and theory-based predictions upfront.
comments.quote: the manuscript would benefit from a more explicit introduction to the tested hypotheses early on.

comments.issue: It is unclear why the three approaches and GxE interactions were needed to address the aims.
comments.request: Explain how the approaches and GxE tests address the aims.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to clarify why the different approaches taken in the study were necessary to explore the hypotheses

comments.issue: Assays for the three temperature treatments may have been run at different times, confounding treatment with timing.
comments.request: Confirm whether all final assays were conducted simultaneously.
comments.quote: I hope this is simply a misunderstanding and that the authors can confirm that the evolutionary treatment is not confounded by the timing of the assays.

comments.issue: Theoretical work on condition-dependent sexual selection is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Lorch et al. (2003), Martinez-Ruiz and Knell (2017) and Martinossi-Allibert et al. (2019).
comments.quote: Maybe add some theoretical work here such as Lorch et al. (2003); Martínez‐Ruiz and Knell (2017); Martinossi-Allibert et al. (2019)

comments.issue: Whitlock and Agrawal (2009) is relevant but not cited.
comments.request: Consider citing Whitlock and Agrawal (2009).
comments.quote: Whitlock and Agrawal (2009) might also be very relevant here.

comments.issue: "Incredibly" is subjective and unnecessary.
comments.request: Remove "incredibly".
comments.quote: 'incredibly' is very subjective and not needed here.

comments.issue: "Far more complex" is not comparable across trait categories.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison or rephrase.
comments.quote: "far more complex" compared to what? To pre-copulatory male harassment? I think it is very difficult to compare the complexity between different trait categories.

comments.issue: The L79-81 sentence is very dense.
comments.request: Split the dense sentence into two.
comments.quote: This is a very dense sentence. Maybe split it into two?

comments.issue: The study aims on L98-99 are stated too vaguely.
comments.request: Be more specific when pointing to the study aims.
comments.quote: Please be more specific when pointing to the study aims (see major comments).

comments.issue: Incubator effects may be confounded with temperature treatment.
comments.request: Clarify replication across incubators and avoid confounding.
comments.quote: Were all 4 independently evolving lines of each temperature treatment kept in the different incubators such that you can discern incubator effects from temperature treatment effects?

comments.issue: No estimate of effective population size is provided for interpreting the setup.
comments.request: Estimate effective population size for the setup.
comments.quote: Can you provide an estimate for the effective population size (taking the sperm precedence patterns into account)

comments.issue: What "unimportant for females" means is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what "unimportant for females" means.
comments.quote: it is unclear to me what and why is meant to be "unimportant for females" here.

comments.issue: The replication structure of factor combinations is unclear.
comments.request: Confirm the replication structure.
comments.quote: Is it correct that each factor combination was replicated 5 times (4 lines per evolutionary treatment x 3 temperature treatments x 2 mating system treatments x 5 replicates)?

comments.issue: Residual normality was not checked; offspring counts are typically modelled with a Poisson distribution.
comments.request: Check normality and consider Poisson models.
comments.quote: Did you check residuals for normality? Offspring data are count data, which are typically modelled assuming Poisson distribution.

comments.issue: Error distributions, link functions and overdispersion are not specified.
comments.request: Report error distributions, link functions and overdispersion checks.
comments.quote: Could you please specify for each response variable the assumed error distribution and the applied link function? Did you need to account for overdispersion?

comments.issue: Only extreme temperature pairs were treated as non-adapted, unlike other tests including moderately non-adapted treatments.
comments.request: Explain or harmonize the non-adapted treatment contrasts.
comments.quote: I'm a bit puzzled about why you only considered the most extreme temperature pairs (hot-cold and cold-hot) as non-adapted lines and contrasted only those to the adapted temperature treatments.

comments.issue: Inconsistent use of "mated and virgin males" versus the slash used earlier for "per".
comments.request: Use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: Consider "mated and virgin males". Note that before (L125) you used the forward slash in the meaning of 'per' when writing 'replicates/treatment'.

comments.issue: The reason for assessing the proteome of both virgin and mated males is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for the mating-state comparison.
comments.quote: Could you provide a brief explanation for why you assessed the proteome of virgin and mated males.

comments.issue: The results section should lead with the significant three-way interaction.
comments.request: Start by mentioning the three-way interaction.
comments.quote: maybe just start by mentioning that you detected significant three-way interaction between experimental evolution regime x temperature treatment x mating system

comments.issue: The reported degrees of freedom on L270 seem too low.
comments.request: Check the degrees of freedom.
comments.quote: Unclear why the dfs are that low? Please check.

comments.issue: Terminology for copulatory versus post-copulatory conflict is inconsistent.
comments.request: Use one consistent term throughout.
comments.quote: Do you consider effects on the proteome as signatures of 'copulatory' or 'post-copulatory' sexual conflict.

comments.issue: Fig 1 would be clearer with final temperature nested in evolutionary treatment.
comments.request: Reorganize the Fig 1 panels.
comments.quote: I was wondering whether it might be easier to read if you present the final temperature treatment nested in the evolutionary treatment

comments.issue: The per-line standardization in Fig 1 is not explained and seems inconsistent.
comments.request: Explain the standardization procedure.
comments.quote: Please provide more details on how you standardized the data. I don't understand why you would do this for each evolutionary line separately.

comments.issue: Statistical tests of non-significant results are not reported.
comments.request: Report non-significant test results.
comments.quote: Please also report statistical tests of non-significant results.

comments.issue: Several typos, including P-'vlaue' and Temperature 'tratment'.
comments.request: Correct the spelling errors.
comments.quote: There are several typos: Please check spelling of P-'vlaue' and Temperature 'tratment'.

comments.issue: The abbreviation LRS is never defined.
comments.request: Define LRS.
comments.quote: 'LRS' is never explained neither in the SI nor the main text. I assume this means lifetime reproductive success

comments.issue: Explained variance estimates are missing, so effect magnitudes are unclear.
comments.request: Report explained variance for all models.
comments.quote: For all models: Could you also provide estimates of the explained variance such that readers get a glimpse on the magnitude of the observed effects?

comments.issue: "df" in table headers mixes numerator and denominator degrees of freedom.
comments.request: Use different abbreviations for the two df types.
comments.quote: In table headers 'df' refers sometimes to the numerator degrees of freedom, sometimes to the denominator degrees of freedom. Please use different abbreviations.

comments.issue: 't.ratio' should be called "t-value".
comments.request: Rename 't.ratio' to "t-value".
comments.quote: The t-statistic is a ratio but it's more common to call it "t-value" not 't.ratio'.

comments.issue: All standard errors in Table S1c are identical.
comments.request: Check the Table S1c standard errors.
comments.quote: Table S1c: all SEs are identical, please check whether this is correct.

comments.issue: Degrees of freedom in Table S3b need checking.
comments.request: Check the Table S3b degrees of freedom.
comments.quote: Table S3b: Please check the degrees of freedom.

reviews.assessment: Large, impressive experimental evolution study with a very positive overall impression, but the male harm depiction and two main analyses need revision.
strengths: enormous amount of research effort and analyses
interesting temperature-dependent patterns of male harm

comments.issue: Using "warm" for one temperature treatment is confusing.
comments.request: Use a single word for each temperature treatment.
comments.quote: Abstract: I suggest using a single word for each temp treatment. The use of "warm" is confusing.

comments.issue: The writing on harm to females does not reflect recent literature on SFP function.

comments.issue: The text of the short section on line 307 is not clear.

title: Temperature Drives the Evolutionary Diversification of Male Harm in Drosophila melanogaster Flies

study.system: Decade-long grassland biodiversity experiment; plants, insects and fungi

editor_summary: Editor notes all three reviewers appreciate the work but raise substantive issues that preclude publication; constructive solutions are provided and a revision would be considered.

reviews.assessment: Valuable long-term results, but deer exclusion and narrow literature coverage qualify the general conclusions, and the terminology needs settling.
strengths: rare long-term experiment in a well-studied ecosystem
generally well written and admirably concise

comments.issue: Cedar Creek plots exclude deer, so general conclusions about top-down effects ignore the key herbivore of the system.
comments.request: Qualify the conclusions in light of deer exclusion.
comments.quote: The Cedar Creek plots fence out deer, which is done explicitly to reduce grazing!

comments.issue: Literature coverage is narrow, minimizing multitrophic meta-analyses, predator-cascade work and the Jena experiments.
comments.request: Broaden the literature coverage and the underexplored claim.
comments.quote: On a related topic, the literature coverage seems a bit narrow.

comments.issue: Diversity is referred to as plant richness, horizontal complexity, ENS and Shannon H' without clear distinctions.
comments.request: Settle on consistent, intuitive terminology throughout.
comments.quote: Most important is getting clarity on terminology related to diversity.

comments.issue: The numbered hypotheses in Figure S1 are never discussed or keyed to path combinations.
comments.request: Key the hypotheses to the SEM paths.
comments.quote: these numbers are not discussed anywhere else as far as I can tell and the hypotheses are not keyed to particular path combinations in the figure

comments.issue: Nearly identical figures and tables with cryptic captions tax the reader.
comments.request: Differentiate ENS and S-W in the bolded captions and standardize.
comments.quote: Figs 4 and S7 and their respective captions are nearly identical except that plant diversity is represented by ENS in one and S-W in the other.

comments.issue: Model names are inconsistent: LMs versus mixed-effects models (MEMs).
comments.request: Standardize model naming and link Table S3 to the models.
comments.quote: Table S3 refers to LMs, which are elsewhere called mixed-effects models or MEMs. This needs to be standardized.

comments.issue: The 96-97% variance explained in Table S6 looks like an artifact because community stability is constructed from the same components.
comments.request: Reconsider presenting this variance-explained result.
comments.quote: community stability is a metric constructed from species stability and covariance (essentially, the inverse of asynchrony). So I am not sure how useful it is to say that these component metrics “explained” X% of variation in community stability.

comments.issue: Comparing mathematically constrained richness effects on evenness with vertical complexity effects is an apples-versus-oranges comparison.
comments.request: Rework the comparison on lines 245-247.
comments.quote: Increasing plant (horizontal) diversity necessarily changes ENS and reduces evenness, which is maximal when S = 1.

comments.issue: Captions for Figures S3-S6 do not specify plant community biomass/diversity quantities.
comments.request: Clarify the wording of these captions.
comments.quote: Add “Effects of biological complexity on the temporal mean and standard deviation of plant community BIOMASS.”

comments.issue: Figure S2 shows no data on horizontal complexity effects.
comments.request: Correct the figure or its citation.
comments.quote: No data on horizontal complexity effects shown in Fig S2.

comments.issue: The source of the conclusion on lines 335-337 is unclear.
comments.request: Explain where this conclusion comes from.
comments.quote: Line 335-337: Not clear where this conclusion comes from.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Table S3 reports simple or partial correlations and which models they derive from.
comments.request: State the correlation type and source models.
comments.quote: Are these simple bivariate correlations or partial correlations (which would be more informative) and if the latter, which models are they derived from?

reviews.assessment: Finds the question important and the experiment robust but struggled with jargon-heavy writing and wants evidence that the treatments worked.
strengths: important general question with conservation applications

comments.issue: The text is jargon-heavy with many sentences over 30 words, making it hard to follow.
comments.request: Unpack jargon and break up long sentences.
comments.quote: there are many very long sentences (e.g., sentence on line 71-77 has > 50 words) and I think Schimel (Book Writing Science) would recommend breaking many of these 30 word plus sentences up.

comments.issue: The flow of ideas does not match the expected narrative, e.g., gap ordering and a redundant 'further'.
comments.request: Reorganize the narrative flow and remove 'further'.
comments.quote: I found the flow of ideas often did not often match with my expectation or the narrative.

comments.issue: No evidence is provided that the heterotroph (pesticide) treatments actually worked.
comments.request: Provide data demonstrating pesticide treatment efficacy.
comments.quote: I think the conclusions would be stronger if a) the authors provided evidence that their heterotroph treatments “worked”

comments.issue: The results contrast with Kohli et al. 2019; invoking study length alone is weak.
comments.request: Give concrete reasons for the contrasting results.
comments.quote: can the authors give any more concrete reasons than study length why the results contrast?

comments.issue: Switching between 'loss', 'destabilize' and 'increasing' phrasing is hard to follow.
comments.request: Make the phrasing more consistent.
comments.quote: The phrasing of “loss” to “destabilize” to “increasing” is tricky to follow throughout.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether other herbivores (rabbits, small mammals) are present in the system.
comments.request: Report other herbivores in the study system.
comments.quote: Are there other herbivores in the system, rabbits, small mammals?

comments.issue: Treating a three-category plant-diversity treatment as continuous is unjustified.
comments.request: Justify or change the continuous treatment coding.
comments.quote: Why include horizontal complexity as a continuous variable? What are you assuming by treating a 3 category treatment as continuous?

comments.issue: 7 line-level copy edits (typos, repeated words, long sentence, wording).
comments.quote: I recommend you remove the first two “plant” in this sentence.

reviews.assessment: Finds the topic novel and the experiment valuable but worries that the trophic-complexity manipulation is a black box and that autocorrelation was ignored.

comments.issue: The trophic complexity treatment is a black box: its actual effects on insect and fungal communities are assumed, not measured or documented.
comments.request: Document and summarize what the manipulation did.
comments.quote: the trophic complexity treatment appears less well recorded and monitored. The report is based on the assumption that the manipulation is working in creating different levels of consumer complexity rather than being measured.

comments.issue: The mechanism by which trophic complexity affects stability is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the direct mechanism, including host and feeding ranges.
comments.quote: Maybe explain the direct mechanism how you think that trophic complexity will affect community stability.

comments.issue: Repeated measures could induce autocorrelation that is not tested in the mixed models.
comments.request: Test and add autocorrelation to the LME models.
comments.quote: I would suggest testing for and adding autocorrelation if necessary to the linear mixed effects models, in nlme this is possible.

comments.issue: The first sentence about complexity is vague and should describe what was tested.
comments.request: Rewrite the opening sentence about complexity.
comments.quote: I am not sure the first sentence about complexity is clear enough, complexity is a vague term.

comments.issue: Trophic complexity is not defined in relation to the actual manipulations and target groups.
comments.request: Define trophic complexity and why these groups were targeted.
comments.quote: I wonder if complexity needs to be better defined regarding the actual manipulations (whole insect food webs and fungal networks).

comments.issue: Species loss over the long time series is not accounted for.
comments.request: Address species loss through time.
comments.quote: I guess you also lost species over the long time.

comments.issue: Belowground biomass was not measured despite the soil fungicide treatment.
comments.request: Consider belowground biomass and reallocation responses.
comments.quote: Considering that you used soil fungicide I am surprised that belowground biomass was not measured.

comments.issue: A statement at Line 155 lacks supporting data.
comments.request: Provide data supporting this statement.
comments.quote: Line 155: do you have any data showing this?

comments.issue: Lines 271-275 mix results and discussion.
comments.request: Separate results from discussion there.
comments.quote: This seems a mix of result and discussion.

comments.issue: The claim linking plant diversity to vertical trophic complexity needs references.
comments.request: Add references for this statement.
comments.quote: greater plant diversity is often associated with greater vertical trophic complexity

comments.issue: Figure 1 colours and arrows are not explained.
comments.request: Explain colours and arrows in Figure 1.
comments.quote: Figure 1: maybe explain colours and arrows

comments.issue: 5 line-level copy edits (typos, grammar).
comments.quote: Line 592: “The intact of diverse heterotrophs?” community?

title: Consumers Modulate Effects of Plant Diversity on Community Stability

editor_summary: Both reviewers found merit but raised substantial concerns; editor shares reviewer 2's worry that the work is too niche for Ecology Letters' broad readership, though a fully revised resubmission could be considered.

reviews.assessment: Excited and convinced by the synthesis, but finds the manuscript heavy and hard to follow, with many clarity fixes needed.
strengths: achieves the goal of a synthesis
clear and insightful Sections I and II

comments.issue: Manuscript is heavy and hard to follow; overall accessibility needs improvement.

comments.issue: Boundary equilibria and labels are unclear until the nullcline subsection; Section III structure loses the reader.

study.system: European landbirds; ringing data on survival, productivity and abundance synchrony

editor_summary: Editor praises the thorough reviews; reviewers support the aims and data but raise statistical concerns about transients and uncertainty, clarity and repeatability issues, and request a less jargon-heavy abstract and better migrant classification.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, data-rich multi-species study, but some statistical choices, especially around transients and uncertainty, may have led to erroneous conclusions.

comments.issue: Transients are modelled in survival but ignored for population index and productivity, which may bias and distort temporal variation.
comments.request: Account for transients when deriving population indices and productivity estimates.
comments.quote: I suggest that the occurrence of transients should also be taken into account when deriving population indices and productivity estimates

comments.issue: Second-stage analyses use point estimates only, ignoring estimation uncertainty and making results overly precise.
comments.request: Propagate uncertainty through all stages of the analysis.
comments.quote: only the point estimates are taken, but the uncertainty in these estimates is ignored

comments.issue: The term 'counts' is misleading since these are capture totals; 'population index' would be better.
comments.request: Use 'population index' instead of 'counts'.
comments.quote: I found this a little misleading because the numbers are not really counts in the strict sense, but rather capture totals

comments.issue: The sudden 'Statistical analysis' title in Materials and Methods is confusing.
comments.request: Fix the section structure.
comments.quote: after descriptions of some statistical analyses, there is suddenly the title 'Statistical analysis'. This is confusing.

comments.issue: Claim that population growth is more sensitive to adult survival than productivity is not generally true; it depends on life history.
comments.quote: I do not think that this statement is generally true, because whether the population growth is more sensitive to adult survival than to productivity depends on the life history of a species

comments.issue: Box 1 is really a figure rather than a box.
comments.request: Reformat Box 1 as a figure.
comments.quote: Box 1: to me this is rather a true figure than a box

comments.issue: Table 2 reports infinite degrees of freedom without explanation or implications.
comments.request: Explain why degrees of freedom are infinite and what this implies.
comments.quote: Table 2: why are the degrees of freedom infinite? And what are the implications?

comments.issue: Priors dunif(0, 1) and dbeta(1, 1) in Table S3 are identical.
comments.request: Make the priors consistent.
comments.quote: Table S3: the priors dunif(0, 1) and dbeta(1, 1) are the same. Consider making this consistent.

reviews.assessment: Excellent dataset and sophisticated approach, but unclear methods, questionable migration and age classification, and missing biological interpretation undermine understanding.

comments.issue: Methods are not described in sufficient detail for a third party to understand what was done.
comments.request: Describe the analyses and models in sufficient detail.
comments.quote: the methods are not described in sufficient detail for a third party, at least me, to fully understand what exactly has been done

comments.issue: No R code or data were provided, so analyses cannot be checked.
comments.request: Provide the R code and data.
comments.quote: e.g. no R code and no data are provided

comments.issue: Migration classification lumps residents, facultative and obligate pre-Saharan migrants together, though the groups differ biologically.
comments.request: Reclassify birds into residents, pre-Saharan and trans-Saharan migrants.
comments.quote: By distinguishing only between trans- and pre-Saharan migrants, the authors lump together resident, facultative and obligate pre-Saharan migrants

comments.issue: Aging all birds as juvenile or adult is not possible for some species with the described methods.
comments.request: Clarify and validate how birds were aged.
comments.quote: the age of birds was assigned to juveniles (1st cy birds) and adults for all species, although this is not possible with the methods described for some species

comments.issue: A falcon (Common Kestrel) is included although the paper states it studied Passeriformes.
comments.request: Correct the taxonomic scope statement.
comments.quote: I also wonder why the authors state that they have studied Passeriformes, when the Common Kestrel is also included

comments.issue: Biological significance of statistically significant effects and differences is not assessed.
comments.request: Assess the biological significance of the effects.
comments.quote: the authors did not assess the biological significance of the statistically significant effects/differences

comments.issue: The term 'bird count' misleadingly suggests birds were counted rather than caught in mist nets.
comments.request: Use a different term or explain that counts are mist-net captures.
comments.quote: To me “bird count” strongly suggests that birds were counted

comments.issue: Many statements are not supported by references.
comments.request: Add appropriate references throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: There are many sentences in which the authors state something but do not support this by references

comments.issue: Exact model structures and random-effect specifications (intercepts vs slopes) are missing.
comments.request: Provide exact model structures and specify random intercepts vs slopes.
comments.quote: it would be extremely helpful if the authors could provide the exact model structure of all models considered

comments.issue: The chain of models is hard to follow; a flowchart and simple explanation would help.
comments.request: Add a flowchart showing how models feed into each other.
comments.quote: I wonder if a flowchart or something like that, showing which model generates what kind of data that is then used in other models

comments.issue: Models mix Bayesian and frequentist frameworks without justification.
comments.request: Justify or reconcile the mixed statistical frameworks.
comments.quote: I was also surprised to see that the authors fit models in a Bayesian framework on the one hand and use frequentist statistics on the other

comments.issue: Whether model assumptions were violated (residuals, overdispersion) is not stated.
comments.request: Report assumption checks such as residual analyses and overdispersion.
comments.quote: the authors should state in the manuscript whether the model assumptions’ were violated or not (residual analyses, overdispersion, etc.)

comments.issue: How unageable birds were handled and how many were excluded is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how unageable birds were treated in the analyses.
comments.quote: What have the authors done with these birds? What ages were used in the analyses for these birds?

comments.issue: 'Abundance' on line 86 is not specified or explained.
comments.request: Specify what abundance refers to.
comments.quote: Line 86: “abundance” of what? Please, specify or explain.

comments.issue: 'Demographic synchrony' is not defined for readers.
comments.request: Explain explicitly what demographic synchrony means.
comments.quote: It is unclear to me, and I suspect to many readers, what the authors mean by ‘demographic synchrony’

comments.issue: Which of the four demographic rates were considered is not stated at the start or in the abstract.

comments.quote: Authors must explain at the beginning of the manuscript which demographic rates have been considered

comments.issue: The abstract sentence on lines 93ff contains empty phrases such as local impact and dampening effects.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence without empty phrases.
comments.quote: I found it difficult to understand this sentence because is contains many empty phrases

comments.issue: Abstract should be rewritten for a general audience and state the data type and demographic rates used.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract for a general audience.

comments.issue: No references are cited on lines 112-117.

comments.quote: Lines 112-117: I was surprised that the authors did not cite any references here.

comments.issue: Lines 123-129 oversimplify the complex, sex- and age-specific migration phenology.

comments.issue: Table S2 lists many non-passerines, making the species set included in the analyses confusing.

comments.issue: The study assesses no hypotheses or predictions about the direction of correlations.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether adult, juvenile or general survival was analysed.

comments.issue: The criterion of two or more adults over 20 years does not indicate breeding and may bias the resident-migrant comparison.

comments.quote: Two or more adults captured at a site over a period of 20 years is not very indicative of the species breeding at that particular CES site!

comments.issue: A 'first' requires a 'second', which is not described on lines 176-178.

comments.issue: Why only year is the independent variable in both models on lines 184-189 is not justified.

comments.issue: It is not specified whether the random effect on line 187 is an intercept or a slope.

comments.issue: The rationale for the priors in Table S3 is not given.

comments.issue: How the data were detrended is not explained in enough detail.

comments.issue: When count versus rate estimates were used on line 220 is unclear.

comments.issue: 'Pairwise correlation' on line 227 does not state what is correlated.

comments.quote: Line 227: “pairwise correlation” of what? Please, state.

comments.issue: The term 'minimum distance' for the lowest maximum distance is confusing.
comments.request: Use clearer terminology.
comments.quote: I find the term “minimum distance” for the lowest value of maximum distance a bit confusing

comments.issue: The reason for the procedure on lines 234f is not given.

comments.issue: Lines 240ff are confusing and use 'minimum distance' while Figure S1 uses 'minimum maximum scale'.

comments.issue: In Figure S1 all points with relative scale = 1 lie on the angle bisector; the reason and consequences are unclear.

comments.issue: 'Which rate estimates' on line 250 is imprecise.
comments.request: Be more precise about the rate estimates.

comments.issue: Only two of the four demographic processes are considered here.

comments.issue: The GAMs on line 253 are not described beyond the response variable.
comments.request: Describe the GAM structure.

comments.issue: How species-level weighted estimates of relative scale and strength were calculated is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the weighted estimation procedure.

comments.issue: Results are described only as general patterns; the magnitude of effects such as the interaction weakening synchrony is not quantified.

comments.issue: Figure 2 shows no visible resident-migrant difference despite the significant model result.

comments.issue: Line-level reference and typo corrections: missing Shepard et al. reference, typo on L157, and Schaub et al. citation error.
comments.quote: Something went wrong with this citation: Schaub, M., Hirschheydt, J. V., Grüebler, M. U., & Schaub, M. (2015)

reviews.assessment: Very interesting with great potential, but the model description is unclear and the lack of a scale-specific strength test risks misinterpreting the dampening result.
strengths: great potential to deepen understanding of population synchrony
results could greatly advance the field

comments.issue: The GLMM/GLM description is unclear, including what the predictor is and how year was coded.

comments.issue: Abstract should say 'both survival and productivity' instead of 'both demographic rates'.

comments.issue: Abstract sentence on lines 92-93 should be reworded to contrast residents and migrants more accurately.

comments.issue: The description of when site is treated as a fixed effect is missing.

comments.issue: Numbers for abundance are missing from the results, unlike productivity and survival.

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 2 would benefit from violin plots behind the boxplots.

comments.issue: Line-level wording edits on lines 332 and 333 and use of * instead of a formal multiplication sign.
