title: How Do Synchrony in Survival and Productivity Influence Abundance Synchrony in European Landbirds?

study.system: speciation and secondary sympatry; literature synthesis

editor_summary: Editor doubts sorting is under-recognised and that displacement is the default; major revisions needed to distinguish the two processes, engage community-structuring/ecophylogenetics literature, and cut repetition.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and stimulating, but introduces a false dichotomy and uses two inconsistent definitions of sorting.
strengths: enormous diversity of references handled well

comments.issue: Some passages, e.g. ls.213-326, are redundant and wander across topics.
comments.request: Reduce or tighten these passages.
comments.quote: In general, the authors have done an excellent job of not falling into this trap, but there are places that could be reduced.

comments.issue: The paper presents sorting and displacement as clear alternatives, a false dichotomy.
comments.request: Treat sympatry establishment as involving both processes.
comments.quote: It seems as if this paper is introducing a false dichotomy (in many places we read of “The alternative predictions of the two frameworks”)

comments.issue: Two different definitions of sorting are used: filtering versus establishment of allopatric differences.
comments.request: Clarify and reconcile the two definitions.
comments.quote: At least in appearance – two definitions of sorting being used. One is filtering, and the other is establishment of differences in allopatry that require little further evolution in sympatry.

comments.issue: Absence of fusion and subsequent coexistence is treated as evidence for sorting, but character displacement could equally explain it.
comments.request: Acknowledge that coexistence does not distinguish sorting from displacement.
comments.quote: an absence of competitive exclusion/fusion and subsequent coexistence, does not necessarily mean sorting under the author’s first definition: it could easily involve character displacement

comments.issue: "Sorting and displacement families" should be reframed as exclusion and displacement with degrees of displacement.
comments.request: Reframe the comparison and add a continuum figure.
comments.quote: That is replace “The sorting and displacement families” with “exclusion and displacement families”.

comments.issue: Displacement also requires allopatric differences and ecological opportunity, and reinforcement needs both pre- and post-mating isolation.
comments.request: Incorporate these mechanistic requirements into the framework.
comments.quote: for ecological character displacement, one still needs differences to be present in allopatry for divergence to happen

comments.issue: Time could create divergence unrelated to coexistence; the time confound in displacement tests is not addressed.
comments.request: Address whether time enables sorting or drives unrelated divergence.
comments.quote: Is it not possible that time creates differences that have nothing to do with coexistence?

comments.issue: Other mechanisms at L.49 (sympatric speciation, drift, founder effects, sexual selection) are not considered.
comments.request: Consider these additional mechanisms.
comments.quote: Sympatric speciation, role of drift and founder effects, importance of sexual selection

comments.issue: "Non-adaptive" at L.86 is undefined.
comments.request: Define what non-adaptive means here.
comments.quote: L.86 what does non-adaptive mean? Drift? Genomic conflicts?

comments.issue: How allopatric differences that enable sorting are generated is not explained; clinal variation would favor convergence.
comments.request: Explain how allopatric differences arise.
comments.quote: I would like to see how the authors think differences in allopatry might be generated to enable sorting.

comments.issue: A relevant reference on divergence and seasonal migration is missing at L.103, 201.
comments.request: Consider Delmore et al. 2015.
comments.quote: Might have a look at: Delmore KE, Kenyon HL, Germain RR, Irwin DE. 2015.

comments.issue: The claim at l.195 about postzygotic isolation is contradicted by cases of collapse with strong isolation.
comments.request: Qualify the statement and cite Liou and Price 1994.
comments.quote: actually even with reasonably strong post zygotic isolation one can get collapse (Liou and Price 1994)

comments.issue: "Mean fitness" at l.197 is not defined.
comments.request: Define mean fitness in this context.
comments.quote: l.197: what is mean fitness here?

comments.issue: The two-seed scenario ignores what happened before secondary contact; character displacement may explain the finch pattern.
comments.request: Address the pre-contact history of this scenario.
comments.quote: One might ask in the presented scenario what was happening in the location with two seeds before secondary contact.

comments.issue: The requirement that species must increase when rare is questioned; equal-sized populations can persist.
comments.request: Clarify this coexistence requirement.
comments.quote: is it always true that the ability to increase when rare is a requirement?

comments.issue: Calling elevational habitat segregation sorting conflicts with Freeman's displacement/release evidence.
comments.request: Expand and justify this interpretation.
comments.quote: so the argument is that species segregating by habitat along elevational gradients are sorting?

comments.issue: The zone at l.374 is not a tension zone, which ignores ecology and parental fitness.
comments.request: Correct the tension-zone terminology.
comments.quote: not a tension zone? Tension zones explicitly ignore ecology and parental fitness (cf. l.372) is the same; the zone is maintained only by selection against hybrids

comments.issue: More relevant references at l.377 are not cited.
comments.request: Consider Liou and Price and Goldberg and Lande 2008.
comments.quote: l.377 Liou and Price, and Goldberg and Lande 2008 perhaps more relevant.

comments.issue: The l.403 example of a moving hybrid zone appears incorrect; the mtDNA distribution could be static.
comments.request: Correct it or use documented moving hybrid zones.
comments.quote: This example seems to be incorrect. Silu Wang has shown that we have essentially an interior and coastal species and the mtDNA distribution could be static.

comments.issue: It is unclear what the exaggeration at l.433 is compared to.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison and consider Coyne & Orr's prediction.
comments.quote: l.433: not sure what the exaggeration is being compared to? As sorting predicts no evolution (I think)

comments.issue: The claim that complete sorting is prevalent is doubtful given evolution nearly always occurs.
comments.request: Justify or qualify this claim.
comments.quote: is it true that sorting is an oft presented case? I still can’t quite see how “complete” sorting could be that prevalent

comments.issue: Tests must exclude clinal variation and resource-distribution differences, not just compare sympatry and allopatry.
comments.request: Control for clinal variation and resource distributions.
comments.quote: It is not enough to demonstrate greater differences in sympatry than allopatry, but (1) greater differences than predicted from clinal variation

comments.issue: The statement at l.481 contradicts the early part of its paragraph.
comments.request: Resolve this contradiction.
comments.quote: l.481 seems to negate the early part of this paragraph

comments.issue: Losos's findings at l.511 are mentioned but not reported.
comments.request: Report what Losos found.
comments.quote: l.511 and what did Losos find?

comments.issue: A relevant reference on hybrid inviability is missing at l.521, 577.
comments.request: Consider citing Coyne (1974).
comments.quote: l. 521, 577 but see: Coyne (1974) The evolutionary origin of hybrid inviability, Evolution 28 505–506

comments.issue: The phrase "relationship between pair age and divergence-time" at l.572 reads as a tautology.
comments.request: Rephrase this phrase.
comments.quote: “relationship between pair age and divergence-time” reads as a tautology

comments.issue: The l.582 pattern could equally reflect time-to-sympatry correlating with time-to-trait-divergence.
comments.request: Consider this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: But could equally be ‘time to sympatry’ correlates with ‘time to trait divergence’?

comments.issue: The logical link between the two statements at ls.585-586 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how the statements relate.
comments.quote: ls. 585-586. Hard to see how one follows from the other!

comments.issue: "Exponentially more" is too strong for shorter wait-times.
comments.request: Rephrase as "much more".
comments.quote: shorter wait-times are exponentially more -> shorter wait-times are much more

comments.issue: Faster postmating isolation evolution via migratory divides in northern birds may also explain the pattern.
comments.request: Consider this additional explanation.
comments.quote: It does appear likely that in the north for birds, we have more rapid evolution of postmating isolation through migratory and other divides

comments.issue: Other explanations for the l.637 pattern are always possible and several were raised.
comments.request: Consider the alternative explanations raised in the review.
comments.quote: perhaps it is testable, but one can always come up with other explanations

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive, well-written overview; wants the simulation methods better organised and a few terminology fixes.

comments.issue: The simulation methods are incompletely described, missing a character-displacement simulation, and Fig. 3 shows only sorting.
comments.request: Describe both sorting and displacement simulations and their comparison, or remove the methods.
comments.quote: When describing the simulation approach (L 459), I lack a description of the simulation of an alternative, namely character displacement.

comments.issue: Two copy edits: Box 1 omits "SPECIES" and Box 3 omits "ARE".
comments.quote: Box 3: “pairs that neither” should probably read “pairs that ARE neither”.

comments.issue: "Microbial" should be excluded from the species-sorting definition, as the term is used broadly in ecology.
comments.request: Remove "microbial" and acknowledge the broader usage.
comments.quote: I strongly suggest to exclude “microbial”, because it is commonly invoked in ecology quite broadly

comments.issue: The abbreviation RI for reproductive interference clashes with reproductive isolation.
comments.request: Spell out reproductive interference throughout.
comments.quote: I suggest not to use the abbreviation RI for reproductive interference, because it is commonly used for reproductive isolation in evolutionary biology.

comments.issue: L572 should refer to trait divergence rather than divergence-time.
comments.request: Reword to "relationship between pair age and trait divergence".
comments.quote: “relationship between pair age and divergence-time” should probably include “trait divergence” instead of “divergence-time”

reviews.assessment: Excellent synthesis, but too long and theory-heavy; the premise lacks citations and inconsistent empirical evidence is not integrated.
strengths: strong case for sorting as an unrecognised mechanism

comments.issue: The manuscript is much longer than needed and repeats points.
comments.request: Cut at least 10% from most sections.
comments.quote: it feels much longer than needed. Many of the points made are made several times throughout the manuscript

comments.issue: The "Empirical Tests" section presents simulations and is wordy; guides for data generation were expected.
comments.request: Reframe the section and tighten it.
comments.quote: I found the section on “Empirical Tests of Species Sorting” quite ironic, given that it discussed the outcomes of various mathematical simulations.

comments.issue: The evidence section is 2.5 pages with only 7 references and could be blended with the previous section.
comments.request: Blend the sections to guide needed data collection.
comments.quote: This 2.5 page section only includes 7 references, which suggests there is not much evidence (of the empirical type).

comments.issue: The opening premise of an exaggerated trait disparity pattern is asserted without a single citation or null-model context.
comments.request: Support the premise with evidence and context on when it fails.
comments.quote: Ironically, this much remarked-upon pattern does not receive even a single citation.

comments.issue: The manuscript relies on theory while ignoring empirical evidence inconsistent with limiting similarity and related ideas.
comments.request: Present the support and lack of support for major assumptions.
comments.quote: this manuscript seems to be relying very heavily on other theoretical treatments of the underlying assumptions while not integrating empirical evidence that is not consistent

comments.issue: Co-occurrence patterns can arise from sorting or interactions, creating the same inference problem.
comments.request: Make this inference problem explicit and favour direct tests.
comments.quote: It may be worth being a bit more explicit that these, too, can be created through both species sorting (filtering) and species interactions (competition).

title: Secondary Sympatry as a Sorting Process

study.system: semiarid grasslands, China; plant traits and productivity stability

editor_summary: Suggest looking for literature datasets to support the greater importance of acquisitive strategies, or discussing similar findings in other ecosystems and for other response variables.

reviews.assessment: Important finding, but trait-stability analyses, PCA-based overall stability and pseudoreplication issues need attention.
strengths: important finding counter to other systems

comments.issue: Storage is not the only basis for resistance; investment in durable tissues is a separate factor.
comments.request: Separate storage from tissue durability in the resistance explanation.
comments.quote: Storage is not the only reason for this resistance ability. Investment on more durable tissues is a major factor that is separate to storage (i.e. storage in specialised organs).

comments.issue: The strategy framework at L113 is not specific to semi-arid grasslands; rooting depth, deciduousness and storage organs are not placed.
comments.request: Clarify where these traits fit in the avoid/escape framework.
comments.quote: Where does rooting depth, deciduousness and storage organs fit in here? Deep roots are typically aligned with "avoid" and deciduousness + storage is aligned with "escape" in the forest literature.

comments.issue: How control plots were located and allocated at L157 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain control plot location and randomization.
comments.quote: I assume the control plots were located inside the blocks (two per block). Explain this, and also how control plots were located.

comments.issue: The purpose of grid cells at L175 is unclear since individual grid cell data seem unused.
comments.request: Explain the role of grid cells.
comments.quote: What was the purpose of grid cells? It doesn't look like you use information collected in individual grid cells, unlike the experiment.

comments.issue: Trait measurement methods lack detail for reproduction.
comments.request: Provide enough trait measurement detail to reproduce the work.
comments.quote: I read the methods text for trait measurement and there was not enough detail presented

comments.issue: 'Florescence length' at L187 is never explained.
comments.request: Explain what florescence length is.
comments.quote: Here and later, please explain what "florescence length" is. Even after reading the supps I couldn't work it out.

comments.issue: Single-season community data may not capture escape strategies, which must be acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge this limitation.
comments.quote: You are assuming that all strategies were present at the time of these surveys, when they may not have been evident in the case of escape strategies.

comments.issue: The supplementary table is called a 'logic' table rather than logistic.
comments.request: Correct the table name.
comments.quote: you call this a "logic" table in the supps. Logistic would be quite different.

comments.issue: Calling this 'functional' stability is confusing when only productivity stability is measured.
comments.request: Use 'temporal stability of productivity'.
comments.quote: Here and below, what is "functional" about this? In your definitions of terms you are just looking at the stability of productivity.

comments.issue: The L275-278 PCA description is unclear about orthogonal strategy axes.
comments.request: Clarify the PCA procedure.
comments.quote: This is not clear. DO you mean you used PCA to create orthogonal strategy axes that you then related to stability components?

comments.issue: PCA loadings are not reported.
comments.request: Report PCA loadings in the supplement.
comments.quote: We need more information about how the PCA axes described the economic and size axes. Report loadings etc. in the supps, not just the biplots.

comments.issue: A PC axis not loaded by functional stability is treated as 'overall stability', ignoring orthogonal dimensions.
comments.request: Do not extract a specific eigenvector as overall stability in the linear model.
comments.quote: I wouldn't extract scores along a specific eigenvector and say that they represent "overall stability" in a subsequent linear model.

comments.issue: Clustering of quadrats within sites is not accounted for.
comments.request: Account for the nested structure in the analysis.
comments.quote: See comments on figures - your analysis has not accounted for the clustering of quadrats inside sites as far as I can tell.

comments.issue: The point at L381 reiterates the previous paragraph.
comments.request: Remove the reiteration.
comments.quote: I do not think you need to reiterate this point here

comments.issue: The paragraph should start at L386.
comments.request: Start the paragraph at L386 with minor wording tweaks.
comments.quote: Just start the paragraph here (with a few wording tweaks as suggested).

comments.issue: Other escape strategies such as storage organs (geophytes) are not considered.
comments.request: Consider storage organs as escape strategies.
comments.quote: What about other escape strategies like storage organs (geophytes).

comments.issue: Figure captions begin with interpretation rather than describing the content.
comments.request: Describe precisely what is in each figure.
comments.quote: for all of these, tell us more precisely what is in the figures rather than starting with notes on interpretation

comments.issue: Figure 1A arrows and dashed line are ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify what the arrows and dashed line represent.
comments.quote: The arrows pointing down shows deviation from normal, not the normal level. The dashed line is normal, right?

comments.issue: Figure 1B line colours are not defined.
comments.request: Define the line colours.
comments.quote: Figure 1B: What do the differen line colours represent?

comments.issue: Figure 1C uses confusing terms and undefined line styles.
comments.request: Use 'dominates', clarify fast/slow and spell out line meanings.
comments.quote: Use dominates rather than predominates. And you interpret both economics and size in terms of fast versus slow, which is confusing.

comments.issue: Figure 2 caption describes error bars for box plots, which is inappropriate.
comments.request: Describe box plot elements correctly.
comments.quote: Box plots have a specific meaning - they represent the median, interquartile range and overall range. Here you say they include error bars which suggest some parametric calculation of error.

comments.issue: Figure 3 caption is not informative and 'mean effect size' is misleading.
comments.request: Expand the caption and call them effect sizes.
comments.quote: This caption is not informative enough in my view. I can not interpret the figure with the information presented in the methods.

comments.issue: Figure 4 caption should explain that only productivity stability was measurable.
comments.request: Explain the stability of productivity and why compositional metrics were not possible.
comments.quote: Explain that this is stability of productivity (or functional stability if you prefer). Explain that it was not possible to measure compositional stability metrics because your data are a snapshot of composition.

comments.issue: Figure 4A uses a different symbol for productivity stability than earlier figures.
comments.request: Use consistent symbols.
comments.quote: The symbol used here for productivity stability is not the same as in the previous figure. Use consistent symbols.

comments.issue: Figure 4B,C regressions treat plots within sites as independent, which is pseudoreplication.
comments.request: Account for the non-independence of plots.
comments.quote: You seem to have used the eight plots from each of the 10 sites to fit this regression, but the plots are not independent observations. This is pseudoreplication if analysed using simple regression.

reviews.assessment: Addresses key goals, but the vague concept of ecosystem stability and generalization beyond productivity need clarification.
strengths: attempts to address key ecological goals
better understanding of stability emergence at ecosystem scale

comments.issue: 'Ecosystem stability' is very vague and not defined in the introduction or methods.
comments.request: Better present and justify what ecosystem stability means here.
comments.quote: the notion of "ecosystem stability" needs to be better presented to clarify this paper (in the introduction and the choice you make in the methods), as the term stability is very vague in ecology

comments.issue: The message is generalized although only productivity, one facet of ecosystem functioning, is examined.
comments.request: Avoid generalizing beyond productivity stability.
comments.quote: You're generalising the message of your discussion when it seems that you're looking at one facet of ecosystem functioning: productivity.

comments.issue: The abstract mixes 'overlooked' and 'prevailing belief' confusingly.
comments.request: Clarify whether few studies exist or a real advance is claimed.
comments.quote: "overlooked" vs l.67: "prevailing belief", this is a bit confusing. Do you mean to say that there have been few studies and that you have found results that can be confronted with these studies?

comments.issue: 'Multidimensional stability' in the abstract is unclear.
comments.request: Specify what multidimensional refers to.
comments.quote: the multidimensional aspect is not clear in the abstract; it is not clear whether this refers to the dimensions of the ecological niche, to a multi-trait approach, or to the different facets of stability.

comments.issue: The introduction should be restructured to cover stability challenges and justify the chosen dimensions.
comments.request: Add paragraphs on global change and the concept of stability.
comments.quote: A paragraph on the challenges of better understanding the stability of ecological systems in the context of global changes

comments.issue: Paragraph 2 does not link back to the stability dimensions and omits resilience.
comments.request: Link the paragraphs and mention resilience.
comments.quote: and what about the 'resilience'? you don't mention resilience in this paragraph, although it seems to be central to this study.

comments.issue: It is unclear which stability dimensions are tested with each of the two datasets.
comments.request: Specify the dimensions per dataset and whether they are complementary.
comments.quote: It seems important to specify which 'dimensions' of stability you are going to test with these two independent datasets.

comments.issue: The simultaneous use of the two datasets and the management status of the grasslands are not justified.
comments.request: Justify the two datasets and state whether grasslands are natural.
comments.quote: Why you mobilize simultaneously these two datasets?

comments.issue: Figure S7 on trait correlations should be mentioned in the trait measurement section.
comments.request: Refer to Figure S7 there.
comments.quote: Figure S7 should, perhaps, be mentioned in this section, since we can already question the correlation between the measured traits.

comments.issue: The community and ecosystem levels of stability should be introduced earlier.
comments.request: Develop these elements in the introduction.
comments.quote: For greater clarity, I think these elements should be developed in the introduction.

comments.issue: 'Normal growing season' at l.234 is undefined.
comments.request: Define the reference state or baseline.
comments.quote: "normal growing season", what does it mean? Does a 'normal growing season' include the pressure of certain global change factors?

comments.issue: Why productivity represents ecosystem stability rather than other facets is not explained.
comments.request: Justify productivity as the stability variable.
comments.quote: You use productivity (biomass) as a variable to characterise the 'stability of the ecosystem', it's not very clear, explain why.

comments.issue: The Bray-Curtis dissimilarity metric at l.244-245 needs explanation.
comments.request: Add supplementary text on this metric.
comments.quote: "Bray-Curtis dissimilarity metric", maybe add some supplementary text for more clarity on this metric.

comments.issue: 'Normal year' at l.255 is undefined.
comments.request: Specify what a normal year is.
comments.quote: l.255: "normal year", specify what you consider a normal year.

comments.issue: The statistical analysis section at l.275-278 could be more direct.
comments.request: Focus the methods on what was used and move preliminaries to the supplement.
comments.quote: it seems possible to be more direct in this 'Methods' section to make it easier to read

comments.issue: The consistent spatial and temporal pattern, a strong finding, is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this consistency.
comments.quote: The same spatial and temporal patterns are being observed. This is a strong finding that is not discussed.

comments.issue: 'Contrary to the prevailing belief' at l.347 lacks references.
comments.request: Add supporting references.
comments.quote: l.347: "Contrary to the prevailing belief", references?

comments.issue: The consistency across space and time should be stated explicitly at l.350-352.
comments.request: Add a sentence making this clear.
comments.quote: This is a strong result, you have observed a consistent pattern across space and time! Add a sentence to make this clear.

comments.issue: Paragraph 2 presents results without discussing them and could merge with paragraph 1.
comments.request: Merge and discuss the results.
comments.quote: Could be merge with the first paragraph, you present your main results without really discussing them.

comments.issue: The first half of the l.356-367 paragraph belongs in the introduction.
comments.request: Move these elements to the introduction.
comments.quote: This first half of the paragraph would be better used to complete the implicit elements of the introduction.

comments.issue: Examples of annual plants at l.371 are missing.
comments.request: Give examples of the annual plants.
comments.quote: "the proliferation of annual plants" such as? Give examples.

comments.issue: The l.418-421 statement conflates productivity stability with overall ecosystem stability; size traits may link to other functions.
comments.request: Temper the statement and consider other functions.
comments.quote: You are studying the stability of productivity, not the overall stability of the ecosystem? Could it be that size traits are linked to other functions / facets / dimensions of the ecosystem?

title: Plant Acquisitive Strategies Promote Resistance and Temporal Stability of Semiarid Grasslands

study.system: social foragers; birds and ungulates; model plus meta-analysis

editor_summary: Model plus data paper broadly interesting; reviewers 1 and 2 have significant concerns about theory, confounding and analysis, and the journal's data and code policy is not met.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and timely theory-data study with strengths, but model assumptions, data transparency, interpretation and generality need major revision.
strengths: combines competition and predation in one model
empirical test using data from multiple taxa

comments.issue: The assumption that predator abundance is directly proportional to prey abundance is not discussed and may limit model applicability.
comments.request: Explicitly discuss this assumption and its limits.
comments.quote: The assumptions in the model could be more explicitly discussed, particularly the assumption of predator abundance being directly proportional to prey abundance.

comments.issue: Resource availability and habitat heterogeneity are not considered; resource clustering could alter competition and predation effects.
comments.request: Discuss how these factors might affect the model's predictions.
comments.quote: The model does not account for variations in resource availability and habitat heterogeneity, which are known to influence group sizes in social foragers.

comments.issue: Dataset selection and quality criteria used in the Web of Science search are not explained.
comments.request: Explain how datasets were selected and screened for quality and relevance.
comments.quote: While the authors mention using terms in Web of Science, there is no clear explanation of how datasets were selected and what criteria were applied to ensure data quality and relevance.

comments.issue: The mixed-effects model does not control for confounders such as environment or species behaviour.
comments.request: Discuss these limitations or run robustness checks.
comments.quote: The linear mixed-effects model used to estimate the power-law relationship does not appear to control for confounding variables that might affect group size independently of population density

comments.issue: The power-law coefficients are not interpreted, compared with previous studies, or explained for different taxa.
comments.request: Clarify coefficient interpretation and compare with earlier estimates.
comments.quote: The interpretation of the power-law coefficients lacks clarity. While the findings suggest that the group size scaling is sublinear, there is no discussion on how these coefficients compare to those derived from previous studies

comments.issue: A general phenomenon is claimed from data covering only birds and ungulates.
comments.request: Add broader taxa or discuss the limits of generalisation.
comments.quote: The authors propose that their findings support a general phenomenon across social foragers, but the datasets cover only birds and ungulates.

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not show confidence intervals or parameter details for the coefficients.
comments.request: Show confidence intervals and parameter values in Figure 3.
comments.quote: the power-law coefficient values presented in Figure 3 could be more effectively emphasized by showing confidence intervals or including additional details on the parameter values used.

comments.issue: Figure 1 legends and description of parameter choices and their ecological relevance are insufficient.
comments.request: Improve legends and explain parameter choices.
comments.quote: Figure 1 would benefit from clearer legends and a better description of parameter choices and their ecological relevance.

comments.issue: Recent literature on power-law group-size distributions and scaling laws is neglected.
comments.request: Review this literature and discuss the results in light of it.
comments.quote: Recent works on power law groups size distribution and its relation to population growth and scaling law, have, unfortunately, been neglected.

comments.issue: The discussion does not consider how ecological interactions or scaling laws might vary across habitats, including marine or tropical systems.
comments.request: Broaden the discussion to other habitats and environments.
comments.quote: The discussion could benefit from a broader consideration of how ecological interactions might vary across habitats, or if the scaling laws found might differ in marine or tropical environments.

editor_summary: Reviewers agree the manuscript is novel and creative but need more methodological detail, articulation of assumptions and alternative mechanisms, and less declarative spillback claims, including the title.

reviews.assessment: Detailed critique requesting clearer model specification, data and code, control of survey timing, and warning that site characteristics may confound the pheasant effect.

comments.quote: The detail of model formulation and inclusion of different effects is unclear.

reviews.assessment: Enthusiastic about this simple, clean survey and its public-health importance, but asks to address confounding, temporal dynamics, robustness and broader framing.

comments.issue: The introduction could clarify that range limits are a likely context for gradient metapopulation dynamics.
comments.request: Add this clarification about applicability.
comments.quote: range limits are arguably a context where we are most likely to see metapopulation dynamics in a more limited, gradient form

comments.issue: Whether adjacency matters for immigration depends on dispersal details, which is not acknowledged.
comments.request: Note this caveat about propagule pressure.
comments.quote: It depends on the details of dispersal whether adjacency is a factor in immigration.

comments.issue: More prominent and foundational citations are needed at line 135.
comments.request: Add these citations.
comments.quote: I would cite additional more prominent and foundational work.

comments.issue: The alphabetical citation order may not follow the editorial convention.
comments.request: Check the journal's citation-order convention.
comments.quote: I typically order citations by date rather than alphabetical. This is not important to the review, yet it made me wonder if there is an editorial convention here.

comments.issue: The statement at line 388 should specify that it is empirically unclear, not theoretically.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: Perhaps clarify that it is unclear empirically. The theory is fairly well understood.

comments.issue: The discussion does not consider whether rates are stationary or vary in time and place.
comments.request: Discuss temporal variation in rates versus the theory's constant-rate assumption.
comments.quote: The discussion could be enriched by considering whether rates are indeed stationary in time or might vary in time and place in an idiosyncratic or predictable manner

comments.issue: The discussion should distinguish finite from infinite patch-number metapopulation cases.
comments.request: Make this distinction and cite the relevant work.
comments.quote: you could make the distinction between the finite and infinite patch-number cases

comments.issue: Posterior MCMC samples could replace the bootstrap for the ensemble plot, with bootstrap moved to the supplement.
comments.request: Combine panels a and b and use MCMC posterior samples.
comments.quote: my preference would be to make one plot combining a) and b), and instead of a bootstrap, use posterior MCMC samples to make the ensemble

comments.issue: Sample size covaries with the gradient, which could be visualized or addressed by thinning.
comments.request: Visualize sampling density across the gradient or thin the samples.
comments.quote: Also, the sample size appears to covary with the gradient. I doubt that is a factor in the result, yet it might be useful to visualize the sampling density as a function of the gradient.

comments.issue: Internal variation in the gradient could be checked with a median quantile spline.
comments.request: Try a median quantile spline as a robust alternative.
comments.quote: A median quantile spline might also be an interesting way to look at the data to see if there is any internal variation in the gradient.

reviews.assessment: Impressive, enjoyable empirical test, but it should go further in stating new insights and clarifying methods.
strengths: extraordinary sampling effort across two years

comments.issue: The first-time novelty claim is overstated because several theoretical papers already modelled range limits.
comments.request: Clarify the novel insights gained beyond existing theory.
comments.quote: The stated novelty is that this is the first time meta-population theory has been applied to a real species range limit. However, several theoretical papers have used meta-population models to understand range limits and to build competing expectations.

comments.issue: The less-than-or-equal-to symbol at line 79 may be reversed.
comments.request: Check and correct the symbol.
comments.quote: I think the lessor-than-or-equal-to symbol needs to be reversed?

comments.issue: It is unclear which hypothesis line 99 refers to.
comments.request: Specify the hypothesis.
comments.quote: Line 99: Which hypothesis?

comments.issue: The range of plot-to-coastline distances is not given.
comments.request: Report the range of distance values.
comments.quote: It would be helpful for the readers to imagine these distances from the plots to the coast line—can you give the range of values?

comments.issue: The 'adjacent areas' procedure at line 220 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how adjacent areas were defined.
comments.quote: Which “adjacent areas?” I think this procedure needs more explanation.

comments.issue: How the spatial Gaussian covariance structure was included in models is unclear.
comments.request: Describe the covariance structure in detail.
comments.quote: It’s not clear how the “spatial Guassian covariance structure” was included in models. More detail would be helpful.

comments.issue: The n* section lacks ecological background and justification, so its importance is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what n* means ecologically and why it is important.
comments.quote: What does n* represent biologically/ecological? Why is it important? This section gets difficult to follow and could use more ecological background and justification for the approach.

comments.issue: The paragraph at lines 291-296 is confusing as written.
comments.request: Rewrite the paragraph.
comments.quote: Confusing paragraph as written, but the idea is quite straightforward. Perhaps have another go at editing.

comments.issue: The p-value at lines 391-393 is unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify what this p-value tests.
comments.quote: Lines 391-393: I’m not following. What is this p-value?

comments.issue: The discussion does not state how findings advance or intersect with theory on range limits.
comments.request: Discuss the new insights and cite Case et al. 2005.
comments.quote: So, does your work give new insights into what causes species range limits? And how have your findings intersected with expectations from theory on meta-populations and range limits?

comments.issue: Figure 2's caption mentions models not shown and overlapping abundance percentiles are confusing.
comments.request: Describe better or add another panel.
comments.quote: I found this figure with the presentation of extra significant models in the caption than what’s illustrated plus overlapping local abundance and initial plot abundance percentiles confusing.

reviews.assessment: Timely, novel and sound study, but the predictions, isolation calculation and reporting of analyses need clarification.
strengths: easy to follow and scientifically sound

comments.issue: An abbreviation is used in the Introduction at L90.
comments.request: Avoid this abbreviation in the Introduction.
comments.quote: I would not recommend using this abbreviation in the Introduction.

comments.issue: Prediction 3 omits isolation from other suitable plots, unlike prediction 1.
comments.request: Extend prediction 3 for parallelism.
comments.quote: this prediction 3 should include something like “and are more isolated from other suitable plots”

comments.issue: The prediction that suitable area decreases towards the range limit is missing from the introduction.
comments.request: Add this prediction to the introduction.
comments.quote: Another relevant prediction would be that suitable area (either suitable area within plots, or number of plots with suitable area) decreases towards range limit.

comments.issue: Supporting Fig. 1 shows an unexplained gap in occupied dots in North California.
comments.request: Explain this gap.
comments.quote: Why is there a long stretch in the coast of North California without red dots (panel b)? This area is theoretically occupied by the species according to GBIF

comments.issue: Colonization was only modelled to suitable plots; colonization of unsuitable areas is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss colonization to unsuitable areas and its implications.
comments.quote: Could colonization to “unsuitable areas” be important to the process of range limit establishment? (perhaps transitorily helping to establish in suitable areas?)

comments.issue: The sentence at L243-244 should start the next paragraph.
comments.request: Move this sentence to the beginning of the next paragraph.
comments.quote: Please move this sentence to the beginning of next paragraph.

comments.issue: Distances to nearest suitable plots may not measure habitat isolation if plot distribution is irregular.
comments.request: Correct distances using nearest plots regardless of suitability.
comments.quote: But does the set of analysed plots have a regular spatial distribution? Otherwise (which seems to be case, because the authors refer to randomness), distances to the five nearest suitable plots may not properly inform on real habitat isolation.

comments.issue: The relation between extinction and plot isolation was not analysed.
comments.request: Add this analysis.
comments.quote: the authors could also analyse the relation of extinction with plot isolation

comments.issue: Whether causes of plot extinction were analysed and which processes dominated is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify or report the analysis of extinction causes.
comments.quote: Were the causes of plot extinction analysed, so that the authors could conclude which were the dominant extinction processes?

comments.issue: The choice to use only plots experiencing extinction for the suitability analysis is unjustified.
comments.request: Clarify the rationale and describe the analysis in Methods.
comments.quote: Why did the authors only include plots experiencing extinction, and not all plots, for testing whether distance to range limit predicted habitat suitability?

comments.issue: Results reported in the figure legend should be in the main text.
comments.request: Move these results to the main text.
comments.quote: I would recommend moving the results reported in the legend to the main text (same for other figures), unless there is a specific reason for doing this.

comments.issue: The dashed line for the 75th percentile of local abundance is not clearly indicated.
comments.request: Make the dashed-line legend clearer.
comments.quote: the visual legend should more clearly indicate that the 75th percentile of local abundance is depicted with a dashed line (include more than one stretch)

comments.issue: Non-significant results and interactions are unreported, and the model-selection steps are unclear.
comments.request: Report all statistics and clarify the analysis steps.
comments.quote: Results for non-significant variables should also be reported (statistics’s values, p-values, etc). The same for interactions, which were mentioned in the Introduction but not in Results.

comments.issue: Table S1 is not cited in Results and uses 'Patch size' instead of 'Suitable plot area'.
comments.request: Cite the table and rename the column.
comments.quote: for clarity and consistency with Fig. 2, please refer in this table to “Suitable plot area” rather than “Patch size”

comments.issue: The analysis of predictor variation with distance to the range limit is not described in Methods.
comments.request: Describe its details and objectives in Methods.
comments.quote: The authors have not explained previously (in Methods) the details and objectives of analysis of whether potential predictors of colonisation and extinction vary with distance to range limit.

comments.issue: The interpretation of absolute versus proportional colonization and extinction numbers is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the differences and implications of both approaches.
comments.quote: The authors should better explain the differences/similarities, and the potential implications, of using either absolute or relative (proportional) numbers for analysing colonisation and extinction events.

title: Evidence That Metapopulation Dynamics Maintain a Species' Range Limit

study.system: coastal wetland soils; 8-year warming experiment, plant and microbial carbon

editor_summary: Four knowledgeable reviewers found this a very interesting and important study that may be accepted subject to revisions addressing their specific comments.

reviews.assessment: Interesting results on phase-dependent SOC responses, with requests to explain anomalies, SEM hypotheses and species-shift causality.

comments.issue: The significant SOC increase in the control in year six is unexpected and unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the control-treatment SOC increase.
comments.quote: It seems that there is a significant increase in SOC in the control treatment in the sixth year after warming. This is unexpected.

comments.issue: Panels a-d of Figure 3 are crowded.
comments.request: Improve the layout of Figure 3.
comments.quote: The panels a-d in figure 3 are crowed.

comments.issue: The construction of the SEM and its underlying hypotheses are not explained.
comments.request: Explain how the SEM was built and the hypotheses behind it.
comments.quote: Not sure how did they build the SEM model? What are the hypotheses behind the model?

comments.issue: Highlighting the sixth year is odd because SOC also decreased in the last three years.
comments.request: Justify or revise the emphasis on the sixth year.
comments.quote: why do you highlight the sixth year of your warming experiment? Actually, there are similar decreases in SOC during the last three years in your figure 1.

comments.issue: The claim that plant species shifts mainly caused the pattern is not demonstrated.
comments.request: Show how plant species shifts were demonstrated to drive the pattern.
comments.quote: How did you demonstrate that shifts in plant species mainly caused the pattern?

reviews.assessment: Interesting coastal wetland warming study, but key drivers, carbon fluxes, soil layers and robustness need addressing before publication.
strengths: assesses warming impacts on coastal wetland SOC

comments.issue: Changes in plant species biomass, not changes in plant species, are claimed to explain the pattern.
comments.request: Distinguish species composition change from biomass change.
comments.quote: I read through the paper and felt that “the changes in plant species biomass” not “the changes in plant species” explained this phenomenon.

comments.issue: Water table levels, crucial for wetland SOC, are not reported across the warming experiment.
comments.request: Report how warming affected water table levels.
comments.quote: I wonder how warming affected the water table levels across the 6-year warming experiments. This is very crucial for us to understand the temporal patterns of SOC in this study.

comments.issue: Vertical CH4 and horizontal DOC/POC fluxes that shape SOC are not considered.
comments.request: Report how these carbon fluxes changed over the warming period.
comments.quote: the C released vertically in the form of methane (CH4) and horizontally input and export in the form of DOC and POC, also shaping the changes in SOC of wetland due to warming

comments.issue: Soil respiration and its heterotrophic and autotrophic components are not reported.
comments.request: Present soil respiration and its components over the experiment.
comments.quote: I wonder how the soil respiration and its components heterotrophic and autotrophic respiration changed across the 6-year warming experiments

comments.issue: Results are presented only for the whole 0-30 cm profile, not by soil layer.
comments.request: Report SOC contents and stocks for each soil layer.
comments.quote: how the coastal wetland SOC contents and stocks respond to warming in different soil layers (e.g., 0-10, 10-20, 20-30 cm)

comments.issue: Robustness of the results is not tested beyond the single case study.
comments.request: Cross-validate with a global meta-analysis of wetland SOC responses to warming.
comments.quote: how to test the robustness of results of this study? A global-scale meta-analysis of wetlands SOC response to warming combined with the current case study could cross-validated the warming impacts

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-conceived warming experiment; revisions needed on hypotheses, salinity confounding and methodological details.

comments.issue: The paper explores the data instead of testing explicit hypotheses about soil carbon mechanisms.
comments.request: Adopt a hypothesis-testing approach and detail the necromass mechanisms.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors incorporate a hypothesis testing approach, rather than simply exploring the data

comments.issue: Warming is confounded with salinity, so their effects on P. australis and other species cannot be distinguished.
comments.request: Discuss salinity effects and the possible role of salt intolerance.
comments.quote: The warming treatment was confounded with salinity, making it quite difficult to distinguish their effects

comments.issue: Framing SOC storage as a natural solution to rising CO2 is a popular misconception.
comments.request: Revise this framing.
comments.quote: the idea that SOC storage is a “natural solution to rising atmospheric CO2 levels” is a popular misconception

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits: “stable” should be “steady-state”, and “significant reduction” is redundant.
comments.quote: L 92: change “stable” to “steady-state”. L 115: The reference Qin et al (2024) is missing from the list.

comments.issue: The reference Qin et al. (2024) is missing from the reference list.
comments.request: Add the missing reference and check all references are complete.
comments.quote: The reference Qin et al (2024) is missing from the list. Please double-chech that all references are complete.

comments.issue: Whether the same ANPP plots were clipped yearly, and whether clipping and soil sampling from these plots affected responses, is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the clipping design and report root biomass and BNPP changes.
comments.quote: were the same ANPP plots clipped each year? If so, is it possible that the observed responses could have been partly due to the clipping effect?

comments.issue: Mechanisms likely differ little between phases; the best overall SEM for the whole experiment is not given.
comments.request: Provide the best overall SEM explaining SOC patterns across the experiment.
comments.quote: I am skeptical that the mechanisms would be so different in the two phases. What is the best overall mechanism (SEM) to explain the SOC patterns for the duration of the experiment?

comments.issue: Figure S6 caption says five years when only five years of measurements exist.
comments.request: Correct the Figure S6 caption.
comments.quote: There were only five years for these measurements, please correct the caption.

comments.issue: Figure S7 does not state what each data point represents.
comments.request: Indicate what each point represents in Figure S7.
comments.quote: Please indicate what each data point represents. I assume the response ratio from one replicate pair (n=4) in one year (n=5), so 20 total?

comments.issue: The graphic behind the Figure 4 SEM diagram is distracting.
comments.request: Simplify the Figure 4 background.
comments.quote: SEM diagram is nice but the graphic behind it is distracting.

reviews.assessment: Well-designed and robust study; only minor suggestions to clarify methods and presentation.

comments.issue: The mangrove example is less relevant; more comparable coastal wetland literature could be used.
comments.request: Add examples from more similar coastal wetlands.
comments.quote: the example from mangroves is useful but perhaps less related to the studied ecosystem. Are there any other literature examples more related to the type of coastal wetland studied?

comments.issue: The amino sugar derivative extraction is only referenced, breaking the flow.
comments.request: Add one sentence summarising the extraction.
comments.quote: although the method is referenced, an additional one sentence summarising how the amino sugar derivatives were extracted would be useful

comments.issue: Vegetation rooting depth is not reported.
comments.request: Add the vegetation rooting depth, e.g. in parentheses.
comments.quote: L222 – what was the vegetation rooting depth (suggest add in parentheses).

comments.issue: How the contributions to variation for each factor in Figure 3e were calculated is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the calculation in the legend or methods.
comments.quote: Please give a little information (either in the legend or methods) on how the contributions to variation for each factor was calculated.

comments.issue: The plant species responsible for the shift is only named in the discussion.
comments.request: State which plant species shifted at L323/324.
comments.quote: suggest here state which plant species was responsible this shift, as at present this is not clearly stated until the discussion

comments.issue: The L386 statement about hydrology is out of order and dismisses then discusses the topic.
comments.request: Discuss hydrological processes first, then state the study's situation.
comments.quote: suggest to put this after the discussion of lateral and vertical hydrological processes. At present, L386 states not important but then discussed anyway.

comments.issue: The plant species that shift are not stated at L398-403.
comments.request: State the shifting plant species here as well.
comments.quote: I would suggest (in parenthesis perhaps), the plant species which shift are stated here also.

title: Warming‐Induced Plant Species Shifts Lead to Substantial Losses of Wetland Soil Carbon

study.system: North American soil fungi; eDNA datasets and wind connectivity models

editor_summary: Three reviewers find the question highly relevant but raise major concerns about the statistical analyses, missing environmental covariates, and insufficient methods detail; revision is invited if these are convincingly addressed.

reviews.assessment: Original large-scale analysis of wind effects on soil fungal communities, of broad interest; many clarifications and justifications are requested.
strengths: original analysis with new findings of broad interest
no prior quantitative estimate of wind's role at this scale

comments.issue: The text says fungi are detected, but it is eDNA that is detected, which may not represent active fungi.
comments.request: Clarify that eDNA, not fungi themselves, is detected.
comments.quote: Clarify it is eDNA of soil fungi (which may or not represent active fungi), that is being detected, not fungi themselves

comments.issue: Population genetic assessments of gene flow are not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention population genetic assessments of gene flow.
comments.quote: Worth mentioning population genetic assessments of gene flow (e.g. Bergemann et al. 2006 New Phytologist).

comments.issue: The discussion of Borgmann-Winter et al.'s wind and rodent dispersal may misrepresent that study.
comments.request: Check the interpretation of Borgmann-Winter et al.
comments.quote: Check interpretation of Borgmann-Winter et al, wind and rodent dispersal not necessarily as discussed here.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether soil samples included roots.
comments.request: State whether roots were included or sieved out.
comments.quote: Clarify whether soil samples include roots, or if these were sieved out.

comments.issue: The volume and depth of the soil cores are not reported.
comments.request: Report the volume and depth of soil cores.
comments.quote: 5, 16. Volume and depth of soil cores?

comments.issue: The 97% identity and 25-sequence cutoffs are not justified.
comments.request: Justify the 97% and 25-sequence thresholds.
comments.quote: 5, 23-24. Justify 97% and 25 sequences.

comments.issue: The choice of 5,000 sequences is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the 5,000-sequence choice.

comments.issue: It is unclear why sequences were removed rather than re-assigned.
comments.request: Explain why removal was chosen over re-assignment.
comments.quote: 5, 45. Why remove these instead of e.g. re-assigning?

comments.issue: The choice of 10 and how it was confirmed are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the value 10 and how it was confirmed.
comments.quote: 5, 46. Why 10 and how confirmed?

comments.issue: What 'distributed' NEON plots are and their size are unclear.
comments.request: Define distributed plots and state their size.
comments.quote: Clarify what are “'distributed' (i.e. non-core) NEON plots”, and state their size

comments.issue: Wind data at 10 m may not represent conditions at sporocarp level.
comments.request: Discuss whether the 10 m wind height is adequate.
comments.quote: Discuss whether 10m height is adequate/ideal; wind speed and direction at ground sporocarp level could be different?

comments.issue: Annual wind connectivity may miss the winds dominant during the fruiting season.
comments.request: Consider wind connectivity during the peak fruiting season.
comments.quote: Why use wind connectivity calculated across the whole year(s) when dominant winds might differ during peak mushroom fruiting season?

comments.issue: The 30 km breakpoint is not justified given site distances range from 0.3 to 8,000 km.
comments.request: Justify the 30 km breakpoint.
comments.quote: 6, 52. Why 30km as breakpoint when site pairs range from 0.3 to 8,000km?

comments.issue: The imprecise 'over 50%' should be the exact value.
comments.request: Write 50.8% instead of 'over 50%'.
comments.quote: 8, 40. Be precise, instead of “over 50%” write 50.8%.

comments.issue: Table S2 and Figure 2 are separated, making the Results hard to follow.
comments.request: Merge Table S2 information with Figure 2.
comments.quote: Merge information in Table S2 with Fig. 2; it will make Results text easier to follow.

comments.issue: The 5.2% of variation is not mentioned in the text.
comments.request: Mention the 5.2% of variation.
comments.quote: 9, 20. Mention 5.2% of variation.

comments.issue: Atmospheric nitrogen deposition is not considered among the drivers.
comments.request: Add atmospheric nitrogen deposition to the discussion.
comments.quote: 10, 37. And atmospheric (i.e. nitrogen deposition).

comments.issue: Calling the dispersal finding 'surprising' is unwarranted since propagule dispersal is expected to matter.
comments.request: Reconsider describing this finding as surprising.
comments.quote: Why is this 'surprising'? Propagule dispersal can reasonably be expected to be important for community composition.

comments.issue: The argument is hard to follow and seems tenuous.
comments.request: Rewrite or clarify this argument.
comments.quote: 11, 39-45. This argument is hard to follow and seems tenuous.

comments.issue: Recent work on fungal ecoregions and stochastic atmospheric movement is not linked to the findings.
comments.request: Link the findings to these recent studies.
comments.quote: Worth linking with recent findings on fungal ecoregions, where sporocarp type is also important

comments.issue: A statement in the discussion lacks supporting evidence.
comments.request: Provide evidence for this statement.
comments.quote: 12, 22. Evidence?

reviews.assessment: Exciting finding, but the correlative design cannot support causal conclusions about wind dispersal, and sampling effort and spatial structure are not adequately handled.
strengths: sound research question with a large dataset

comments.issue: Correlative patterns cannot establish wind-mediated dispersal as the cause; other processes may explain them.
comments.request: Acknowledge alternative processes and temper the causal conclusions.
comments.quote: How do we know that the large-scale observed patterns that correlated with the historic windflow patterns are due to the role of wind-mediated dispersal and due not other processes

comments.issue: The strong wind-connectivity conclusion is misleading because the variable covaries with many others.
comments.request: Soften the conclusion given wind-connectivity's covariation with other variables.
comments.quote: I find a bit misleading the strong conclusion about the role of wind-connectivity in soil fungal communities given that this variable covaries strongly with many other variables

comments.issue: The number and time span of pooled samples per site are not accounted for in the analyses.
comments.request: Account for sampling effort variables in the analyses.
comments.quote: I did not see anywhere how the difference in the number of pooled samples per site influences the observed fungal communities per site.

comments.issue: Rarefying after pooling confounds sequencing depth with ecological differences, so endemism may be a sampling effect.
comments.request: Use a more robust approach to account for sequencing depth.
comments.quote: I don’t think that in this case rarefying after pooling is the best strategy since we may not have different sequencing depths among samples just due to sequencing stochasticity, but also due to ecological differences among samples

comments.issue: Sites are spatially clumped and non-uniform, which the current treatment does not adequately address.
comments.request: Account for the spatially clumped structure of sites.
comments.quote: The spatially clumped structure of the sites should be accounted for in the analyses for robust inference.

comments.issue: The wind- versus animal-dispersal dichotomy is oversimplistic since many agaricoid fungi are also animal dispersed.
comments.request: Refine or drop the dispersal-mode classification.
comments.quote: The authors classify the species in the two groups of wind-mediated dispersal and animal-mediated dispersal but I find this classification oversimplistic.

comments.issue: The claim that wind-dispersing fungi are influenced by wind connectivity conflicts with the non-significant agaricoid result.
comments.request: Explain the inconsistency with the non-significant agaricoid result.
comments.quote: I don’t understand the conclusion that wind-dispersing fungi are particularly influenced by wind connectivity, since according to the results wind connectivity was not significant for agaricoid fungi

comments.issue: Rarefaction at 5,000 sequences is not justified and seems very low.
comments.request: Better justify the 5,000-sequence rarefaction depth.
comments.quote: Why was rarefaction done at 5000 sequences? a better justification is needed for this.

comments.issue: Figure 3 classifies species as agaricoids, ascomycota and hypogeous, but the dispersal type assumed for ascomycota is unclear.
comments.request: State the dispersal type hypothesized for ascomycota.
comments.quote: what type of dispersal was hypothesized for ascomycota?

comments.issue: Classifying species only as ascomycetes versus basidiomycetes cannot support lineage-level conclusions.
comments.request: Perform a more in-depth phylogenetic analysis.
comments.quote: a more in depth phylogenetic analysis is needed than classifying species as ascomycetes and basidiomycetes for concluding anything about the effects along fungal lineages

comments.issue: The claim that spores cannot be observed or tracked conflicts with cited studies that trap propagules from air.
comments.request: Correct the claim that propagules cannot be tracked.
comments.quote: In fact, fungal dispersal propagules can be directly trapped from the air as in some of the cited studies.

comments.issue: Likely wrong word: altitude should be latitude.
comments.request: Correct 'altitude' to 'latitude' on p3 l39.
comments.quote: p3, l39: altitude->latitude?

reviews.assessment: Novel, welcome approach to wind dispersal, but collinearity, missing environmental controls and thin methods reporting leave the conclusions unconvincing.
strengths: novel approaches to measuring wind characteristics
welcome contribution on an understudied process

comments.issue: Geographic distance and wind connectivity are highly collinear, so including both in model simplification distorts variable importance.
comments.request: Present final models with geographic and wind distance considered separately.
comments.quote: Geographic distance and wind connectivity are highly correlated: multivariate r2 of 0.63 (or r of approximately 0.8). This level of collinearity can seriously undermine explanatory modelling approaches

comments.issue: The Mantel analysis omits environmental differences, so the west-east diversity gradient could be driven by other environmental conditions.
comments.request: Discount other environmental effects in the Mantel analysis.
comments.quote: I think at least as parsimonious a conclusion would be that other environmental conditions ultimately drive fungal diversity

comments.issue: Methods and results lack detail; basic sequencing information such as OTUs or reads per group is missing.
comments.request: Provide basic sequencing data per group and fuller methods detail.
comments.quote: there was no basic information about the sequencing data in this respect, not even number of OTUs or reads per group

comments.issue: How many OTUs could be assigned morphologies, and the resulting coverage, is not reported.
comments.request: Report morphology assignment success and coverage.
comments.quote: how successful was morphology assignment – what fraction of OTUs could be assigned morphologies and what coverage did this provide within measured communities?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether environmental conditions were included in the Mantel analysis and what 'partial' means.
comments.request: Clarify what was partial about the Mantel analysis.
comments.quote: I think environmental conditions were not included in the ‘Mantel’ analysis, but this was not completely clear to me (in what sense was the analysis partial?)

comments.issue: R scripts and a fuller description of the analyses are not available.
comments.request: Provide R scripts and a fuller analysis description.
comments.quote: It would have been useful to see a fuller description and/or R scripts corresponding to the analyses.

comments.issue: Two line-level wording edits (P3 L7; P8 L33).
comments.quote: P3 L7 suggestion: delete ‘particularly for microbial taxa’ to avoid repetition of ‘microbes’

comments.issue: 113 is not the sum of 47 and 68, leaving two samples unaccounted for.
comments.request: Explain why the two samples are missing.
comments.quote: P5 L6 nb 113 is not the sum of 47 and 68 (so perhaps explain why two are missing)

comments.issue: Why NEON samples need specific treatment is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify why NEON samples need specific treatment.
comments.quote: P5 L25 please clarify why NEON samples need specific treatment

comments.issue: The meaning of 'individual assignment' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what 'individual assignment' means.
comments.quote: P5 L45 clarify what this ‘individual assignment’ means

comments.issue: The meaning of 'distributed (i.e. non-core) NEON plots' is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what distributed NEON plots are.
comments.quote: P5 L51 explain what ‘distributed (i.e. non-core) NEON plots’ means?

comments.issue: A method described as 'briefly' covered is not described at all.
comments.request: Actually describe this method.
comments.quote: P6 L11 not really ‘briefly’ - more not at all!

comments.issue: How the metadata correspond to the elemental analysis is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how the metadata correspond to the elemental analysis.
comments.quote: P6 L13 how do these metadata correspond to the elemental analysis described in the previous sentence?

comments.issue: It is implausible that all locations were connected to some degree, which questions the connectivity model's realism.
comments.request: Explain why all locations are connected to some degree.
comments.quote: P6 L30-33 I’m (perhaps naively) surprised that all locations were at all connected to some degree.

comments.issue: It is unclear what quantity the reported mean refers to.
comments.request: State what the mean is calculated over.
