title: Positive Density Dependence Promotes Host Persistence in the Face of Infectious Disease

study.system: interplant nitrogen transfer; 26 15N-labeling studies

editor_summary: Editor notes the referees' differing viewpoints and says the major concerns of reviewer 3 must be addressed; acceptance is not ensured and referees will see the paper again.

reviews.assessment: Interesting topic, but the soil pathway cannot be ruled out, the network treatments are ambiguous, and the data are not shown.
strengths: focus on N transfer rather than C transfer

comments.issue: The soil pathway cannot be ruled out; NoM versus MN comparisons are not conclusive.
comments.request: Rule out the soil pathway properly.
comments.quote: I don’t think the study allows the authors to conclude that the soil pathway (‘NoM’) had a minor contribution to the interplant N transfer.

comments.issue: Mesh pore size affects N flow independently of hyphae, and N-fixing may be confounded with the network treatment.
comments.request: Clarify network treatments and confounding.
comments.quote: The effect of ‘N-fixing’ may be confounded with the network treatment, or not. It’s not clear in the text.

comments.issue: No data points are shown in any figures.
comments.request: Show the data in figures.
comments.quote: My other major issue was that the data were not shown on any figures. This is unacceptable in my opinion.

comments.issue: How arbuscular fungi mine N is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the N-mining mechanism.
comments.quote: 50: How do arbuscular fungi ‘mine’ N?

comments.issue: The original source of the CMN definition is not cited.
comments.request: Cite the original definition.
comments.quote: Karst et al. 2023 are not the original source of this definition. Please cite the original source for the definition of CMN.

comments.issue: The new term 'MN' may not represent the synthesized treatments; CMN or CFN should be used as appropriate.
comments.request: Use CMN or CFN consistently.
comments.quote: This is confusing and it is questionable whether this new term even represents the treatments in the synthesized studies.

comments.issue: Evidence on interplant C transfer is used as evidence for N transfer.
comments.request: Do not substitute C-transfer evidence for N transfer.
comments.quote: the authors substitute evidence/lack of evidence for interplant C transfer with N transfer. I don’t think this is appropriate.

comments.issue: Cahanovitc et al. 2022 examined C transfer, not N transfer.
comments.request: Correct the citation.
comments.quote: Cahanovitc et al., 2022 did not test N transfer between plants. They examined C transfer.

comments.issue: 'Mycorrhiza' is used to mean fungi rather than the association.
comments.request: Specify the partner being discussed.
comments.quote: ‘Mycorrhiza’ is the term to describe the association. It doesn’t mean ‘fungi’.

comments.issue: N fixation is not a continuous trait, so the proposed N gradient between distant species is illogical.
comments.request: Clarify the N-gradient logic.
comments.quote: The ability to fix N by plants is not a continuous trait. So how could N gradients exist between phylogenetically distant plant species?

comments.issue: Pickles et al. 2017 examined C transfer, not N transfer.
comments.request: Do not swap C for N evidence.
comments.quote: Pickles et al. 2017 examined C transfer not N. I don't think you can swap C for N as evidence for N transfer.

comments.issue: Kiers et al. 2011 examined C for P trade, not N.
comments.request: Correct the description.
comments.quote: The cited study (Kiers et al. 2011) examined C for P 'trade'. Precision in language is important.

comments.issue: 27% of studies were excluded for measuring only leaf 15N; whether pairings were heterospecific is unclear.
comments.request: Reconsider or justify the exclusion.
comments.quote: 15/54 studies (27%) of studies are excluded because they did not measure root 15N, only leaf 15N.

comments.issue: Whether all plants were mycorrhizal is unclear; the mesh/rotated-core/inoculant breakdown is missing.
comments.request: Clarify colonization and add the breakdown.
comments.quote: This is an important point that needs clarification. All plants across experiments were mycorrhizal?

comments.issue: How MN treatments cross with microbial mutualism treatments is unclear.
comments.request: Describe the treatment combinations precisely.
comments.quote: It is not clear how the MN treatments cross with the ‘microbial mutualism’ treatments and I encourage more precision in how the treatments are described.

comments.issue: Sensitivity analyses omit the mycorrhizal inoculant and non-rhizobial N-fixer subsets.
comments.request: Include these subsets in sensitivity analyses.
comments.quote: This information must be included in the sensitivity analysis.

comments.issue: How restricted soil volumes affect interplant N transfer is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the soil-volume effect.
comments.quote: I am not clear how this would affect interplant N transfer.

comments.issue: The three mutualism types are miscounted; there are two mutualisms plus a hyphal-contact treatment.
comments.request: Fix the mutualism terminology throughout.
comments.quote: There are not three mutualisms. There are two: one formed between plants and mycorrhizal fungi and the other formed between plants and N-fixing microbes.

comments.issue: A bold claim about MN promoting N sharing lacks references.
comments.request: Add references.
comments.quote: This is a rather bold statement and there are no references to back it up.

comments.issue: The study provides no evidence to advocate a particular network definition.
comments.request: Justify the definition advocacy.
comments.quote: What evidence does the current study provide to advocate for a particular definition of a fungal network?

comments.issue: Kinship was not tested in this study.
comments.request: Remove the kin claim.
comments.quote: ‘kin’ was not tested in the current study.

comments.issue: A single data point is treated as a phylogenetic gradient.
comments.request: Remove or temper the claim.
comments.quote: This is a single data point, it does not represent a phylogenetic gradient.

comments.issue: A broad colonization-transfer statement rests on a single study.
comments.request: Add support for the relationship.
comments.quote: I would like to see more support for the proposed relationship between colonization and N transfer from mycorrhizal fungi.

comments.issue: 'Connections to MN' is unclear and confusing.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.
comments.quote: What is meant by ‘connections to MN’? This language is unclear and confusing.

comments.issue: Foliar uptake of atmospheric N is an alternative explanation for shoot 15N.
comments.request: Address foliar uptake as an alternative.
comments.quote: Were there controls put in place in the synthesized studies to account for foliar uptake of atmospheric NO3- or other gaseous forms of N?

comments.issue: Two supplemental copy edits (verb tense in Text 1 and 3; grammar in Table 8).
comments.quote: Supplemental Text 1 & 3: verb tense switches between past and conditional. It should be written in past tense.

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the synthesis and finds it compelling, but the confounders in the MN experiments and the inadequate sensitivity analysis remain problematic.
strengths: statistical analysis largely appropriate, rigorous and creative
more compelling than the previous version

comments.issue: Removing mesh and rotated-core studies is not an appropriate sensitivity analysis for limited soil volume.
comments.request: Subset studies more carefully for this confounder.
comments.quote: simply removing the studies that used mesh or rotated cores is not an appropriate sensitivity analysis for this issue

comments.issue: MN manipulations also change fungal community composition and traits; this alternative explanation cannot be addressed by sensitivity analysis.
comments.request: Acknowledge this alternative explanation alongside the CMN interpretation.
comments.quote: alternative explanations (such as the possibility that the MN manipulation had effects via changes to the fungal community composition & traits) need to be acknowledged alongside the CMN interpretation

comments.issue: 'Mycorrhizal species' should be 'mycorrhizal fungal species'.
comments.request: Fix the wording.
comments.quote: Line 187: change “mycorrhizal species” to “mycorrhizal fungal species”

comments.issue: Square-root sample size is used as weight instead of the standard inverse-variance weight.
comments.request: Justify the weighting method.
comments.quote: Why was this used as the weight, instead of the inverse of the study-specific variance estimate

title: Mycorrhizal Network and Symbiotic N‐Fixer Jointly Enhance the Interplant Nitrogen Sharing

study.system: Malagasy endozoochorous plants and frugivores; 361 assemblages

editor_summary: Editor notes three positive reviews and appreciation of the problem, data and methods; asks to address sensitivity to trait imputation, soften correlative conclusions, discuss spatial scale, and cite Ganzhorn et al. 1999.

reviews.assessment: Really enjoyed this rare, well-written and timely paper; only minor methodological clarifications and suggestions.
strengths: addresses questions raised while reading in the discussion

comments.issue: The abstract's statement about mega-seeded plants could suggest species-level comparisons, but the analysis is assemblage-level.
comments.request: Clarify the scale of the analysis in the abstract.
comments.quote: I suggest clarifying this point in the abstract to avoid potential confusion about the scale of the analysis

comments.issue: The link between hypotheses and results should be more explicit; Figure 3 panels should indicate which hypothesis they address.
comments.request: Add visual cues in Figure 3 or its caption linking panels to H1 and H2.
comments.quote: would it be possible to indicate in Figure 3 which panels correspond to which hypothesis?

comments.issue: The number of species without available trait data is not specified.
comments.request: Specify how many species had no data available.
comments.quote: Please specify how many species had no data available.

comments.issue: The choice of Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations over phylogenetic trait imputation is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the imputation method or consider phylogenetic trait imputation.
comments.quote: I wonder why the authors did not use Phylogenetic Trait Imputation, or whether it might have been a more appropriate choice in this context.

comments.issue: The 30 x 30 km grid choice may affect model outcomes and its robustness is not assessed.
comments.request: Discuss the scale's influence or test alternative grid sizes.
comments.quote: did the authors consider testing how alternative grid sizes might affect the results, or could they elaborate on why the selected scale is considered robust despite this potential limitation?

comments.issue: Why the human footprint was averaged per assemblage is not explained.

comments.quote: Here the authors state that the average value of the cumulative human footprint was calculated for each assemblage, but it is not clearly explained why an average was used.

comments.issue: The assumption of potential plant-disperser interactions at assemblage level and its implications are not clarified.
comments.request: Clarify the extent of this assumption and its implications.
comments.quote: Clarifying the extent of this assumption and its possible implications would strengthen the interpretation of the results.

reviews.assessment: Very interesting and timely with an impressive dataset and strong support for both ideas, but imputation sensitivity, causal language and length need attention.
strengths: very interesting and a pleasure to read
impressive dataset of over 2,800 plant species
moves the field forward through scale and quantitative approach

comments.issue: The manuscript relies heavily on imputed seed width data but does not test the sensitivity of results to the imputations.
comments.request: Compare key outcomes with and without imputed values.
comments.quote: Even a brief comparison of key outcomes with and without imputed values would help support the robustness of conclusions drawn from trait distributions.

comments.issue: SEM outcomes are described in causal language, overstating inference from observational, correlational data.
comments.request: Soften causal language to reflect associations.
comments.quote: Several passages currently describe the SEM outcomes in causal language, which overstates the strength of inference that can be drawn from observational, correlational data.

comments.issue: The introduction and discussion are long, with multi-topic paragraphs that obscure the flow of ideas.
comments.request: Tighten the introduction, condense the discussion and break long paragraphs into shorter ones.
comments.quote: Several paragraphs in the intro and discussion are also quite long and cover multiple conceptual steps, which can obscure the flow of ideas.

comments.issue: The 15 species classified as mega-seeded are not listed with their traits and conservation status.
comments.request: Provide a table or figure listing the mega-seeded species.
comments.quote: Consider providing a table or figure listing the 15 species classified as mega-seeded, along with relevant traits and conservation status.

comments.issue: Spatial bias and uncertainty in extinct frugivore ranges are acknowledged but not fully addressed for the legacy conclusions.
comments.request: Detail how uncertainty in extinct ranges was handled or present it as a limitation.
comments.quote: I recommend adding more detail on how uncertainty in extinct frugivore ranges was handled in the analysis or presenting this as a limitation in the discussion.

comments.issue: The term 'human footprint' refers to a specific composite metric but is used as a general noun without definition.
comments.request: Define the metric early and use broader terms where appropriate.
comments.quote: I suggest reconsidering how the term “human footprint” is introduced and used throughout the manuscript.

comments.issue: The abstract phrase 'we test this hypothesis' is vague about which hypotheses are tested.
comments.request: Briefly state the main hypotheses tested in the abstract.
comments.quote: The phrase “we test this hypothesis” is vague. It would help to briefly state the main hypotheses being tested (e.g., legacy and downsizing effects on seed size).

comments.issue: The abstract's phrasing implies a strong causal effect of human footprint on seed size.
comments.request: Soften the wording to reflect association.
comments.quote: Since the analysis is correlative and based on SEM, softening this to reflect association would be more appropriate.

comments.issue: The carbon-storage claim at Line 59 reads as a study conclusion rather than a potential implication.
comments.request: Reword it as a potential implication.
comments.quote: sounds like it is a conclusion of your study instead of a potential implication

comments.issue: The >=50% fruit diet cutoff excludes small omnivorous frugivores and tortoises, which may affect the 95th percentile.
comments.request: Note the rationale for these exclusions and their potential role.
comments.quote: it may be helpful for the authors to briefly note this rationale in the methods or discussion to clarify why omnivores or facultative frugivores were excluded

comments.issue: The variance explained by PC1 and PC2 of the environmental PCA is not reported.
comments.request: Report the variance explained by PC1 and PC2.
comments.quote: Report variance explained by PC1 and PC2 from the environmental PCA.

comments.issue: The justification for using the 95th percentile is too thin.
comments.request: Expand the justification of the 95th percentile and its relevance to the hypotheses.
comments.quote: expanding slightly your justification of using 95 percentile (beyond minimizing effects of outliers) would help readers understand its relevance to hypotheses

comments.issue: Work linking seed downsizing and carbon storage in Madagascar is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Razafindratsima et al. (2018).
comments.quote: The link between seed downsizing and carbon storage has been studied in Madagascar but is not cited.

comments.issue: Invasive pigs may also disperse large seeds, which is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the potential role of invasive pigs in seed dispersal.
comments.quote: Invasive wild and feral pig species may also contribute to dispersal of large seeds as has been found in many tropical systems

comments.issue: The figures are visually complex and overwhelming because of detailed icons.
comments.request: Simplify the icons used in the figures.
comments.quote: Simplifying icons (a seed instead of a seed being measured- an elephant bird instead of an elephant bird on a scale etc..) would make the figures less visually-complex and overwhelming.

comments.issue: The PCA figure's interpretive value may be unclear; the ecological meaning of PC1 and PC2 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain PC1 and PC2 in the text and move the PCA plot to the supplementary materials.
comments.quote: The authors might consider explaining the ecological meaning of PC1 and PC2 directly in the text (e.g., PC1 reflects seasonal drought; PC2 differentiates upland vs. lowland sites), and moving the PCA plot or loadings to the supplementary materials.

comments.issue: Figure 3 is complex and visually overwhelming, with distracting colours and symbols.
comments.request: Simplify icons, colours, symbols and variable names in Figure 3.
comments.quote: I love the use of path analysis here but this figure is complex and visually overwhelming.

comments.issue: Figure S2 may be better placed in the main text.
comments.request: Consider moving Figure S2 to the main text.
comments.quote: Figure S2- consider moving this figure to the main text.

comments.issue: The phrase 'whether they hold signatures of past trait matching' is unclear.
comments.request: Reword it to say distributions still reflect historical trait matching.
comments.quote: The phrase “whether they hold signatures of past trait matching” could be clarified.

comments.issue: Two line-level edits: 'Univeristy' at Line 8 and inconsistent capitalization at Line 440.
comments.request: Fix these typos.
comments.quote: Line 8: “Univeristy” should be “University.” Line 440: “downsizing-effect hypothesis” lacks capitalization used in other hypothesis references.

reviews.assessment: Very well written and important, with sound interpretations; only the MICE imputation details need clarification.
strengths: very well written and clearly organized

comments.issue: Details of the MICE imputation procedure (number of imputed outputs, selection, pooling) are not described.
comments.request: Provide more details on how the MICE imputation was performed.
comments.quote: My only minor comment is to provide a little bit more details on how the MICE imputation was performed

title: Legacy of the Lost and Pressure of the Present: Malagasy Plant Seeds Retain Megafauna Dispersal Signatures but Downsize Under Human Pressure

study.system: competitive communities; generalized Lotka-Volterra coexistence models

editor_summary: Editor says all reviewers appreciate the significance and novelty but want more intuitive mechanism explanations, especially without trade-offs; the editor questions whether the third model really excludes trade-offs and asks about mechanistic resource competition.

reviews.assessment: Recommends acceptance pending comments, impressed by how minimal assumptions generate emergent coexistence.
strengths: impressed by minimal assumptions generating emergent coexistence

comments.issue: Facilitation could change which species pairs coexist and how assembly proceeds, but is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how facilitation might influence coexistence outcomes.
comments.quote: In models that incorporate facilitation (positive interspecific effects), I would expect a larger proportion of pairwise coexistence involving lower-ranked species, as demonstrated in microbial systems in Chang et al. (2023), where cross-feeding is prevalent.

comments.issue: A recent preprint with similar indirect-interaction-chain findings and different assumptions is not positioned in the discussion.
comments.request: Emphasise the universality of growth-competition trade-offs in the discussion.
comments.quote: Given the potential universality of such trade-offs, I think this aspect warrants emphasis in the discussion.

comments.issue: The network structure promoting emergent coexistence in the third model without higher-order interactions or facilitation is unexplained.
comments.request: Characterise the structure and report the fraction of feasible communities.
comments.quote: Specifically, what is the structure that promotes emergent coexistence when only pairwise competitive interactions are present and higher-order interactions (HOIs) and facilitation are absent?

comments.issue: How many random assemblies are discarded as infeasible, and how this relates to diversity, is not reported.
comments.request: Report the fraction of feasible assemblies and its relation to final diversity.
comments.quote: How many of the randomly generated assemblies need to be discarded because they are not feasible?

comments.issue: The biological interpretation of the directed-triangle ratio is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what a ratio of one directed triangle per 100 triangles indicates.
comments.quote: although such triangles are rarer than expected by chance, what does a ratio of 1 directed triangle per 100 possible triangles indicate biologically? How should we interpret this measure?

comments.issue: Intransitivity may require specific conditions such as spatial heterogeneity, making it less common than hierarchical structures.
comments.request: Acknowledge this as a direction for future research.
comments.quote: This suggests that intransitivity might be less common than strict hierarchical structures, as it requires more specific conditions.

comments.issue: The abstract does not state the competition-growth trade-off assumption of the minimal model.
comments.request: Emphasise the trade-off assumption upfront in the abstract.
comments.quote: I recommend explicitly emphasizing in the abstract that your minimal model depends on a key assumption: the competition-growth trade-off.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the distribution of a_ij values affects the fraction of pairwise coexistence.
comments.request: Clarify the role of the a_ij distribution.
comments.quote: Does the distribution of the a_{ij} values matter for the fraction of pairwise coexistence?

comments.issue: The necessity of the condition at line 126 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain why this condition is necessary.
comments.quote: At line 126, could you explain why this condition is necessary?

comments.issue: Figure 1C lacks l_1, l_2 and similar labels.
comments.request: Add the labels for clarity.
comments.quote: In Figure 1C, it would be helpful to mark l_1, l_2, etc for clarity.

comments.issue: Figure 3 refers to Fig SXXX instead of Figure S3.
comments.request: Correct the figure cross-reference.
comments.quote: In Figure 3, I believe you mean Figure S3 instead of Fig SXXX.

comments.issue: Equation S7 appears to be missing the r_i - r_{i-1} term.
comments.request: Correct Equation S7.
comments.quote: For species i- Equation S7, it should be r_i - r_{i-1}

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the manuscript and sees a good contribution, with minor clarifications on definitions, title and the direction of inference.

comments.issue: The title is mystifying and suggests pairwise exclusion drives multispecies coexistence.
comments.request: Revise the title to better describe the contents.
comments.quote: I found the title of the manuscript to be somewhat mystifying, and after reading the manuscript I’m not sure the title describes its contents well.

comments.issue: It is not spelled out exactly what additive and emergent coexistence mean, e.g. for pairs versus triplets.
comments.request: Define additive and emergent coexistence explicitly.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful if the authors spelled out exactly what “additive” and “emergent” coexistence is.

comments.issue: The claimed link between sequential assembly and emergent coexistence does not hold in general.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between assembly and emergent coexistence.
comments.quote: To be sure, if zero species pairs can coexist, then sequential assembly is impossible, but beyond that it’s not clear to me that the possibility of sequential assembly and emergent coexistence are necessarily related.

comments.issue: The hierarchical competition model would be more accessible with an ecological verbal cartoon.
comments.request: Provide an ecological example or mental image of the model.
comments.quote: I think it would help with accessibility somewhat if the authors could provide a verbal cartoon of what the model here represents in more ecological terms.

comments.issue: The text for Fig. 3 references Fig. SXXX.
comments.request: Correct the cross-reference.
comments.quote: In the figure text, there is a reference to Fig. SXXX.

comments.issue: The direction of inference is reversed: the paper shows full coexistence says little about pairwise coexistence, not the converse.
comments.request: State the directionality of inference correctly and what it means for pairwise experiments.
comments.quote: The claim on L365 is that pairwise coexistence holds little information regarding full community coexistence, but what the authors actually have demonstrated is that full community coexistence holds little information regarding pairwise coexistence.

reviews.assessment: Praises the contribution but is left wanting stronger explanations of the mechanisms and the role of trade-offs.
strengths: elegant mathematical analyses on a minimal model
results contribute greatly to understanding coexistence

comments.issue: The mechanism behind emergent coexistence is unclear and the role of trade-offs becomes irrelevant if random communities show it anyway.
comments.request: Strengthen the logical connection between the trade-off models and the random model.
comments.quote: While all the mathematical arguments make sense, I was wondering what exactly the mechanism is behind such emergent coexistence.

comments.issue: The positive transitivity-emergent coexistence relationship in larger communities is absent or reversed in smaller ones.
comments.request: Explain why this pattern differs with community size.
comments.quote: there seems to be a positive relationship between transitivity and emergent coexistence in communities with more species, but that relationship is not obvious, or even in the contrary direction, in smaller communities (comparing Figure 5 and Figure S4). Why is that the case?

comments.issue: Whether the growth-rate distribution is linear or concave is judged visually.
comments.request: Quantify coexistence fraction as a function of trade-off concavity.
comments.quote: I think the point is well illustrated in the current figure, but the argument could be even stronger with a more quantitative analysis

comments.issue: The coexistence fraction limits change with species number without explanation.
comments.request: Explain why the limits shift and whether it is ecologically meaningful.
comments.quote: It seems to me that the lower limit of the coexistence fraction is increasing, and the upper limit is decreasing with more species in the community. Why is that the case, and is that ecologically meaningful?

title: Multispecies Coexistence Emerges From Pairwise Exclusions in Communities With Competitive Hierarchy

editor_summary: Both reviewers agree the manuscript is of interest to general ecologists, but both flagged missing explanations, especially the spatial distribution of prey item samples; revision invited.

reviews.assessment: Very positive about the framing, topic and study; suggests clarity improvements and asks whether sampling method confounds the urban-nonurban comparison.
strengths: coyote is a great study species

comments.issue: Sections after the introduction do not follow the predictions, disrupting cohesion.
comments.request: Align the sections with the predictions from the introduction.
comments.quote: the sections after the intro don't really follow the predictions brought up in the introduction, which makes it a bit harder to follow and disrupts cohesion

comments.issue: Sampling method (roadkill vs live capture) may confound the urban-nonurban dietary comparison.

comments.quote: is the comparison between S.F. and Marin County coyotes an artifact of sampling or true differences between populations?

comments.issue: The abstract lacks quantitative results for its correlational claims.

editor_summary: Fascinating study of a timely topic, but the flow of arguments and clarity of writing must be improved, mainly in the introduction and discussion.

reviews.assessment: Values the experimental contribution but wants mechanisms reviewed and the introduction and discussion substantially edited.

comments.issue: Mechanisms linking temperature and diversity to density-mass scaling are only briefly presented and need a proper review.

comments.issue: In several paragraphs the flow of ideas is not straightforward.
comments.request: Edit for articulation and clarity.
comments.quote: In several paragraphs, the flow of ideas is not straightforward. Sentences related to the idea of the paragraph are presented but not well articulated.

comments.issue: Abstract could highlight the key contributions more.
comments.request: Revise the abstract to foreground key contributions.
comments.quote: I wonder if the abstract can further highlight the key contributions.

comments.issue: Mechanisms by which diversity reduces density, such as interference, are not mentioned.
comments.request: Mention interference mechanisms and cite Turchin, Finke & Denno, DeLong.
comments.quote: I recommend mentioning those mechanisms through which diversity can reduce density, as a reduction in efficiency by interference between several competitors (Turchin 2003; Finke & Denno 2005; DeLong 2021).

comments.issue: Average body sizes of the six species are not reported.
comments.request: Report the average body sizes.
comments.quote: In method, it can be important to report the average body sizes of the six species.

comments.issue: Discussion lacks a strong treatment of mechanisms and of the study's contribution, alternatives and global-change relevance.
comments.request: Strengthen the discussion of mechanisms, framework contribution and implications.
comments.quote: I miss a strong consideration of the mechanisms through which richness and temperature affect scaling and the contribution of the present study to this framework

comments.issue: Different scaling reported for body-size distributions and within-community density-size relationships is not discussed.
comments.request: Consider this contrasting evidence in the discussion.
comments.quote: when the frequency distribution of individual or species body sizes, or when the population density and body size of species within communities were considered, different scaling were reported and the pattern is not always evident.

comments.quote: I am okay with the table, but consider that if this information is included within the plots of Figure 2 they can be interpreted with the pattern, and no space in text is used for reporting parameters.

comments.issue: 'Simulated communities' in Figure 4 could be read as modelling dynamics.
comments.request: Use an alternative term such as 'no interaction expectation'.

title: Delicate Trade‐Offs: Nonlinear Multiple Biotic Constraints on Absorptive Fine Root Lifespan Across Trees

study.system: Serengeti lions; hunting group size and predator-prey dynamics

editor_summary: Nice results with great potential; one reviewer raises valid criticism and major concerns, especially about the complexity of the model, which must be addressed.

reviews.assessment: Appreciates the modelling but questions key assumptions (search efficiency, no group-size effect, single prey) that may limit generality.
strengths: solid description of lion subgroup-size distribution
convincing fit of the negative exponential distribution

comments.issue: Reduced searching efficiency for larger groups is questionable because prey is often predictably distributed; the assumption and its violation are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss this assumption and how violating it would affect the results.
comments.quote: Hence, I am not convinced that larger groups have a reduced searching efficiency than smaller groups or solitary lions, as groups of any size benefit from this predictable spatial distribution of prey

comments.issue: The model assumes group size does not affect hunting success, ignoring nonlinear and large-prey effects; general statements need nuance.
comments.request: Add nonlinear group-size effects on hunting success and nuance the general sentences.
comments.quote: I would suggest emphasizing the often-demonstrated non-linear effect of group size on the hunting success of carnivores on "normal" prey

comments.issue: The claim that lions do not cooperate overlooks cooperative hunting of difficult prey, limiting generality to other ecosystems.
comments.request: Acknowledge cooperative hunting and temper the strong statements.
comments.quote: lions can develop complex cooperative strategies to catch difficult prey, such as giraffe for example

comments.issue: Only wildebeest is considered as prey although lions feed on several species, and this choice is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the single-prey simplification.
comments.quote: From my understanding, the Authors considered only wildebeest as prey for lions in this work. To me, this needs some justification, as lions feed on several other prey species, even in the study ecosystem.

comments.issue: The heavy emphasis on the Serengeti lion in the Introduction is unexplained.
comments.request: Develop what makes Serengeti lions different or remain more general.
comments.quote: Why are the Authors emphasizing so much on the Serengeti in the Introduction? Is it on purpose?

comments.issue: Details of the data are missing (collection years, survey overlap, number of prides, seasonality).
comments.request: Provide the missing data details.
comments.quote: Years of data collection for both prey and lion group size. Were the 2 surveys done over the same period? How many prides in total?

comments.issue: The results rest on strong assumptions whose limits are not highlighted.
comments.request: Explicitly highlight and discuss the limits of the assumptions.
comments.quote: I know simplifications are needed for modelling exercise but it is important that the Authors highlight and discuss the limits of these assumptions

comments.issue: Figures 1 and 5 present the two variables with different axis ranges.
comments.request: Use the same variables and axis ranges in both figures.
comments.quote: I think it would be better if the 2 figures would be presented with the 2 variables and same range for the axis's variables

comments.issue: Relevant studies (Mbizah et al. 2020, Smith et al. 2008, Macnulty articles) are missing from the discussion.
comments.request: Discuss these studies in the Discussion.
comments.quote: I think some relevant studies are worth mentioning in the discussion

comments.issue: Group hunting is presented as a violation of the solitary-hunting assumption rather than an existing strategy.

comments.quote: I would suggest presenting both solitary and group hunting as two existing strategies in predators, and not one as an exception

comments.quote: there is a need to show that this is potentially a different mechanism, food intake being linked to the amount of meat consumed by all individuals of a pack

comments.quote: the Authors should specify the hyaena species referred to here; i.e., spotted hyaena

comments.quote: As the introduction rapidly focuses on large mammalian carnivores, the ref Brock and Riffenburgh 1960 appears isolated.

title: Fission‐Fusion Group Dynamics and Cooperative Hunting Stabilise Social Carnivore Populations

study.system: urban ponds and terrestrial food webs; eDNA metabarcoding, Zurich

editor_summary: Editor welcomes the interesting manuscript; all three reviewers see real merits and provide thoughtful, constructive comments to improve it before revision.

reviews.assessment: Valuable dataset and compelling predator-loss patterns, but the coupling framing, metric interpretation and SEM description need work.
strengths: relatively large dataset from pond sites
strong basis for broad ecological questions
compelling patterns related to predator loss

comments.issue: Aquatic-terrestrial coupling is used ambiguously, shifting between resource use across boundaries and nutrient or energy fluxes.
comments.request: Define coupling consistently and state what the data can address.
comments.quote: A central term in the manuscript is “aquatic-terrestrial coupling,” but its use remains somewhat ambiguous.

comments.issue: Without biomass or resource-use evidence, food web metrics cannot support inferences about energy flux or coupling strength between habitats.
comments.request: Temper coupling interpretations or add flux evidence.
comments.quote: without biomass estimates or evidence of resource use, it is difficult to infer anything about energy flux between habitats

comments.issue: The introduction does not explain how each network metric relates to aquatic-terrestrial coupling or food web stability.
comments.request: Give a focused rationale linking each metric to the hypotheses.
comments.quote: it is not always clear how each metric relates to the central theme of aquatic-terrestrial coupling or to food web stability

comments.issue: It is unclear whether modularity changes reflect cross-compartment linkages or internal changes within aquatic or terrestrial modules.
comments.request: Show what specifically drives the modularity changes.
comments.quote: It is possible, for instance, that increased modularity reflects internal changes within either aquatic or terrestrial modules, rather than the erosion of cross-ecosystem connections.

comments.issue: Figure 1 does not convey how metrics assess aquatic-terrestrial coupling across the urban gradient.
comments.request: Add a clearer conceptual diagram linking metrics to connectivity.
comments.quote: Figure 1 does not clearly convey how the metrics are being used to assess aquatic-terrestrial coupling across the urban gradient

comments.issue: Connectance, nestedness and generality seem tangential because their relationship to aquatic-terrestrial coupling is not explained.
comments.request: Justify why these metrics were chosen.
comments.quote: while connectance, nestedness, and generality are standard food web descriptors, their direct relationship to aquatic-terrestrial coupling is not well explained

comments.issue: The introduction contradicts itself on generalists: urbanization favours destabilizing generalists at line 83, but generalist predators stabilize webs at line 94.
comments.request: Reconcile the statements about generalists and stability.
comments.quote: At line 83, the authors suggest that urbanization favors generalists and destabilizes food webs, but later (line 94), they suggest that generalist predators enhance food web stability.

comments.issue: SEM model structures are not justified and no schematic of hypothesized pathways is given; fit, comparisons and robustness are under-reported.
comments.request: Provide a pathway table or schematic and report model fit.
comments.quote: it is unclear how the model structures were selected or justified. No table or schematic is provided to illustrate hypothesized pathways

comments.issue: The justification for using SEM is unclear and simpler statistical approaches might suffice for the stated goals.
comments.request: Justify SEM over simpler alternatives.
comments.quote: The current application of SEM adds complexity but may not clearly support the narrative on aquatic-terrestrial coupling.

comments.issue: The paper could be reframed around predator loss and trophic structure rather than speculative coupling claims.
comments.request: Reframe the interpretation around food chain length and predator loss.
comments.quote: the authors could reframe their interpretation around changes in food chain length or trophic structure, which are more directly supported by their data

comments.issue: It is unclear whether bolstering predators means abundance, biomass or diversity, and whether predator diversity could decline while abundance rises.
comments.request: Clarify what bolstering predators refers to.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to clarify whether “bolstering predators” refers to an increase in their abundance, biomass, or diversity.

comments.issue: The term metaweb is used before being defined.
comments.request: Define metaweb and justify its use early.
comments.quote: The term "metaweb" is introduced without prior definition in the introduction.

comments.issue: One hypothesis restates the modularity prediction and is not conceptually distinct.
comments.request: Rephrase the redundant hypothesis.
comments.quote: One of the hypotheses listed appears to restate the prediction about modularity. Consider rephrasing to avoid redundancy

comments.issue: The focus on predator proportions as a response variable was not established in the introduction.
comments.request: Justify why predator proportion is central.
comments.quote: this focus was not clearly established in the introduction. Please clarify why predator presence or proportion is a central component of the study's research questions

comments.issue: Predators were replaced by basal consumers is ambiguous about whether predators disappeared or relative abundances shifted.
comments.request: Clarify what replacement means.
comments.quote: The phrase “predators were replaced by basal consumers” is somewhat ambiguous. Does this mean that predators disappeared and novel primary consumers emerged

comments.issue: The basis for judging food web changes as positive or negative is not stated or referenced.
comments.request: State and support the criteria used.
comments.quote: It is not clear how the authors determined whether changes in food web structure were positive or negative.

comments.issue: The cascading effect and enemy release hypotheses are invoked without explanation.
comments.request: Briefly describe these hypotheses and their relevance.
comments.quote: The manuscript refers to the cascading effect hypothesis and the enemy release hypothesis but does not explain them in detail.

comments.issue: Loss of aquatic-terrestrial linking nodes is claimed but not clearly shown in results or figures, which mainly show predator proportions.
comments.request: Show linking node loss in results and figures.
comments.quote: The claim that aquatic-terrestrial linking nodes were lost in urbanized systems is compelling, but it was not clearly shown in the results or figures.

comments.issue: How direct versus indirect effects on omnivory were distinguished is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the direct-indirect distinction.
comments.quote: the effect of urbanization on omnivory is said to be “indirect,” but it is unclear how the distinction between direct and indirect effects was determined in this study

comments.issue: The link between omnivory and aquatic-terrestrial coupling is not made explicit.
comments.request: Integrate omnivory into the coupling narrative.
comments.quote: the connection between omnivory and aquatic-terrestrial coupling is not clearly made and could be more explicitly integrated into the broader narrative

comments.issue: Why basal consumer is used instead of primary consumer is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the choice of the term basal consumer.
comments.quote: It may be helpful to explain why “basal consumer” was chosen instead of the more common term “primary consumer.”

comments.quote: The discussion on niche overlap and habitat quality is difficult to follow. The rationale for why reduced niche overlap indicates improved habitat quality and stability is not well established

comments.issue: Calling the study a compromise suggests intentional avoidance of interaction strengths rather than a data limitation.
comments.request: Rephrase to reflect methodological constraints.
comments.quote: it may be more accurate to acknowledge that interaction strengths were simply not available due to methodological constraints

comments.issue: The metaweb assumes a consistent species diet across sites, which may not be realistic and should be acknowledged as a limitation.
comments.request: Add this assumption as a potential limitation.
comments.quote: I do not think the metaweb approach allows species diet to shift with urbanisation? I think it assumes consistent diet of a species across sites

comments.issue: Generating 100 community structures per local web and averaging modularity is not explained, including the null model comparisons.
comments.request: Give more detail on this procedure and null models.
comments.quote: this is not clear to me. Please give a bit more detail here and in the comparisons to null models.

comments.issue: It is not clear from the start that these are invertebrate webs with aggregated producers and vertebrates ignored.
comments.request: State the taxonomic scope clearly at the outset.
comments.quote: It took me a while to realise these are really just invertebrate webs - it should be clearer from the start that producers are aggregated and vertebrates are ignored

reviews.assessment: Convincing, well-executed study with sound analyses; a few remarks on cascades, multiple testing and metric redundancy.

comments.issue: The reverse direction is not considered: urbanization may also reduce terrestrial prey inputs and leaf litter into streams.
comments.request: Consider the reverse pathway of terrestrial inputs.
comments.quote: Urbanization may also reduce the input of terrestrial prey into streams and of leafs as relevant food source

comments.issue: 3 line-level copy edits (capitalization, rationale spelling, caption wording).
comments.quote: Figure 4 caption: Should be „non-significant“, not „insignificant“

comments.issue: Composition of what is unclear, and structural change may be a more logical second aspect to test.
comments.request: Clarify and reorder the second aspect.
comments.quote: composition of what? Wouldn’t structural change not be a more logical second aspect to test

comments.issue: The extent to which differences on lines 199-202 would affect the results is untested.
comments.request: Test how these differences affect the results.
comments.quote: To which extent would differences affect your results? Could you test this?

comments.issue: Whether all Table 1 metrics are needed is unclear, and modelling them with the same predictor requires correction for multiple testing.
comments.request: Reduce redundant metrics and account for multiple testing.
comments.quote: Did you consider the similarities among these metrics, are really all of them needed?

comments.issue: Marginal significance is discussed instead of reporting exact p-values and sticking to a threshold interpretation.
comments.request: Report exact p-values and avoid marginal significance.
comments.quote: rather report exact p-values and avoid talking of marginal significance

comments.issue: The degree of correlation on line 248 is not reported.
comments.request: Report the degree of correlation.
comments.quote: 248 what is the degree of correlation?

comments.issue: The disconnect may also arise bottom-up through poor habitat quality reducing emerging prey and then predators; top-down and bottom-up cascades are not distinguished.
comments.request: Distinguish top-down from bottom-up explanations.
comments.quote: Could the disconnect also be a consequence of bad habitat quality, reducing emerging prey and this in turn driving predator reduction?

title: Urbanisation Drives the Decoupling, Simplification, and Homogenization of Aquatic and Terrestrial Food Webs

study.system: 42 angiosperms and AM fungi; comparative genomics, transcriptomics and GWAS

editor_summary: Editor: novel and interesting topic with merit, but reviewers raise significant conceptual and methodological limitations about representativeness of results and accessibility to the journal's broad audience.

reviews.assessment: Groundbreaking topic, but the logic, representativeness and methodological detail need substantial work.

comments.issue: The 42 species are not clearly representative of gene family expansion patterns across plants; lineages may be over- or underrepresented.
comments.request: Show that the sampled species adequately represent plants or discuss representation limits.
comments.quote: Is there sufficient evidence that the selected plants adequately represent gene family expansion patterns across the entire plant kingdom?

comments.issue: The criteria and thresholds defining gene family 'expansion' are not clearly specified or shown to apply uniformly.
comments.request: Define expansion thresholds and how expansion is distinguished from maintenance.
comments.quote: What constitutes a threshold for expansion? How is expansion distinguished from maintenance?

comments.issue: The stress treatments cover only a few stresses and it is unclear how the setup mimics natural, long- versus short-term environmental change.
comments.request: Justify the stress choice and mimicry of natural conditions.
comments.quote: How does the experimental setup accurately mimic natural environmental changes, especially distinguishing between long-term and short-term stresses?

comments.issue: Benjamini-Hochberg correction may be overly conservative or insufficiently stringent for large datasets.
comments.request: Consider stricter multiple-comparison correction methods such as Holm-Bonferroni.
comments.quote: The study employs Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons, which might be overly conservative or insufficiently stringent when handling large datasets.

comments.issue: Functional interpretations of the k-means co-expansion patterns lack independent biological evidence.

comments.issue: The GWAS relies on 212 M. truncatula populations whose genetic background and geographic diversity may not capture broad variation.

comments.issue: MCScanX and the custom duplicate gene classifier may not be stringent or comprehensive enough, and evolutionary differences among species are not considered.
comments.request: Compare with alternative duplication-classification methods and consider evolutionary differences.
comments.quote: these classification standards might not be stringent or comprehensive enough

comments.issue: Conclusions are based only on angiosperms and may not extend to other plant groups.
comments.request: Discuss or test generality to mosses and ferns.
comments.quote: Can these findings be directly generalized to other plant groups (e.g., mosses, ferns)?

comments.issue: Lines 90-95 do not connect with the preceding content and lack logical sequence.
comments.request: Improve the logical flow of this passage.
comments.quote: does not naturally connect with the preceding content and lacks a clear logical sequence

comments.issue: Lines 100-105 do not explain why understanding the two evolutionary mechanisms matters for context dependency.
comments.request: Explain the relevance of these mechanisms.
comments.quote: does not clearly explain why understanding these mechanisms is important for studying context-dependency

comments.issue: Lines 125-130 do not explain why AM symbiosis is uniquely advantageous for studying gene family expansion and context dependency.
comments.request: Explain the unique advantages of this system.
comments.quote: does not sufficiently explain why this symbiotic relationship holds unique advantages in studying gene family expansion and context-dependency

comments.issue: The method referred to at lines 255-258 is not identified.
comments.request: Name and describe the method.
comments.quote: Lines 255-258: What is the method referred to here?

comments.issue: How SEH1, NUP85 and NUP133 were obtained is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how these nucleoporins were selected or obtained.
comments.quote: How are the three nucleoporins SEH1, NUP85, and NUP133 obtained?

comments.issue: How the 160-200 million year timeframe was established is not explained.
comments.request: Describe how this timeframe was estimated.
comments.quote: How was this time frame of approximately 160 to 200 million years ago established?

reviews.assessment: Recognizes the innovation but doubts the credibility of broad conclusions from 42 species and the limited stress treatments.
strengths: first link between gene family expansion and context dependency of AM symbiosis
reveals the role of tandem duplications

comments.issue: The small sample of 42 plants, with no location or habitat information, is insufficient for the broad title conclusion.

comments.issue: Only phosphorus, potassium and drought were used as stresses, and there are no drought results, reducing reliability.
comments.request: Add the missing drought results or temper the conclusions.
comments.quote: Moreover, the authors only used phosphorus, potassium, and drought as stress factors. Especially when there are no results for drought, the reliability of the conclusions in this paper is further reduced.

comments.issue: A significant relationship does not prove that gene family expansion drives context dependency as claimed.

comments.issue: The article does not actually study how species regulate interactions.
comments.request: Correct this framing claim.

comments.issue: The distribution characteristics of the 42 angiosperms are not described.

comments.issue: Selecting species considered important suggests artificial selection of targets, so results may not represent all plants.

comments.issue: Results are unreliable when based on only one species.

comments.issue: The results section contains too much introduction and discussion material.

comments.issue: The claim about pods and fitness is wrong: pods are a reasonable fitness index because the species mainly self-pollinates by cleistogamy.

reviews.assessment: Compelling core findings, but the context and implications must be made accessible to the journal's broad readership.

comments.issue: The context and implications are not clear for the broad Ecology Letters readership.

comments.issue: The co-expansion finding deserves more discussion, especially the shared regulatory processes and grass modifications.

comments.issue: Several word- and sentence-level edits (undergird, generic sentence, outsized role, 80% statistic).

study.system: animals; sexual signals; meta-meta-analysis of 41 meta-analyses

editor_summary: Editor invites resubmission: clarify selection criteria for included meta-analyses, define terminology and theoretical framing, improve figure readability, remove invalid funnel-plot advice, report prediction intervals, and archive data and code in a citable repository.

comments.issue: The word 'display' is absent from the main text though it is standard field terminology.

comments.issue: Discussion of what conspicuousness means comes too late in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Attractiveness is fuzzily defined and its measurement across studies is not described.

comments.issue: Unclear how a meta-meta-analysis differs from a meta-analysis of previous meta-analyses.

comments.issue: Search and selection of the 41 meta-analyses are delegated to another paper.

comments.issue: Beneficial (external) condition remains poorly explained and mixes loosely connected metrics.

comments.quote: Another example of confusing terminology: What exactly is beneficial (external) condition?

comments.issue: Unclear how the strength of sexual selection was measured and by whom.

comments.issue: Passage about earlier timing needs explanation.
comments.request: Clarify what earlier timing refers to.

comments.issue: Divergent transitions are mentioned without explanation.
comments.request: Explain what divergent transitions are.

comments.issue: Discussion is too vague and restates known mechanisms without substantive insight or clear future-work rationale.
comments.request: Make the discussion more substantive and justify future research directions.
comments.quote: In several places I think the discussion falls into the trap of being too vague.

comments.issue: Large colour blocks in Figures 3-5 are visually overwhelming and hide white points.
comments.request: Change point colours, add labels, or use coloured text.
comments.quote: The large blocks of colour on Figure 3, Figure 4, and Figure 5 are a bit visually overwhelming.

comments.issue: Discussion sentence seems to contradict the introduction's argument about narrowly focused meta-analyses.
comments.request: Reword the sentence or the earlier criticisms.
comments.quote: I found this sentence confusing as it seems to be the exact opposite of the argument that was made in the introduction

comments.issue: Claim that researchers assume conspicuous traits are attractive without evidence lacks a citation.
comments.request: Add a supporting citation.
comments.quote: I think the statement that researchers often assume conspicuous traits are attractive without evidence warrants a citation

comments.issue: Four line-level copy edits (missing word, typos).
comments.quote: L79: Missing word. “assume that THE conspicuous traits”

comments.issue: A key sentence is wordy and would benefit from an example.
comments.request: Rephrase the sentence and add a hypothetical example.
comments.quote: I get what you mean but this is quite a wordy sentence and given it’s importance I would recommend rephrasing.

comments.issue: Unclear whether 'we' in the methods refers to all authors.

comments.quote: I’m not super familiar with the MeRIT guidelines – when the text says we (e.g. L223) does this mean all authors?

comments.issue: Sentences about benefits shared with mates are confusing.
comments.request: Rephrase these sentences.
comments.quote: These sentences are a little confusing since you already specify that benefits are to the bearer and its mates so why would a reader be surprised

reviews.assessment: Interesting and timely, but aims and theoretical framing are unclear and study selection is insufficiently reported, raising bias concerns.
strengths: preregistration and open data and code

comments.issue: Unclear whether the aim is testing if conspicuous traits are sexually selected or if presumed signals are.
comments.request: State the aims and theoretical background precisely.
comments.quote: it remains unclear whether the authors intend to test (i) whether conspicuous traits are typically sexually selected, or (ii) whether traits presumed by researchers to be sexually selected are indeed sexually selected.

comments.issue: Non-random sampling of species may bias the dataset and inflate the conspicuousness-attractiveness effect.
comments.request: Assess and discuss the extent of this sampling bias.
comments.quote: This, I believe, can introduce a potential sampling bias, possibly inflating the overall effect size for the relationship between conspicuousness and attractiveness.

comments.issue: Rationale for testing the association between attractiveness and benefit effect sizes is not developed.
comments.request: Develop the theoretical expectations for this analysis.
comments.quote: the rationale for testing the association between effect sizes linking conspicuousness to attractiveness, and those linking conspicuousness to other fitness components (‘benefits’), is not well developed in either the Introduction or the Discussion.

comments.issue: No conceptual path diagram clarifying relationships among trait expression, mating success and reproductive success.
comments.request: Add a conceptual path diagram of the key variables.
comments.quote: a conceptual figure, such as a path diagram, could help to clarify the relationships among the key variables

comments.issue: Paper does not explain why the positive association is meaningful for understanding trait evolution.
comments.request: Explain the significance and contribution of this association.
comments.quote: the manuscript does not address why this positive association is meaningful or how it contributes to our understanding of the evolution of conspicuous traits

comments.issue: No sufficient information on how the 41 meta-analyses were identified and selected.
comments.request: Provide search and selection details, systematic protocol and PRISMA diagram.
comments.quote: I was unable to find sufficient information on how the 41 meta-analyses included in this study were identified and selected.

comments.issue: The reported 8% of species tested for attractiveness is highly sensitive to inclusion criteria.
comments.request: Show how inclusion criteria affect this figure.
comments.quote: However, this number is likely highly sensitive to the inclusion criteria for the meta-analyses.

comments.issue: Unclear which fitness traits capture benefits specifically to mates rather than the bearer.
comments.request: Clarify which traits measure mate benefits.
comments.quote: it remains unclear which of the fitness traits, if any, are intended to capture benefits specifically to mates

comments.issue: The term 'within-study variation' is ambiguous.
comments.request: Clarify whether it means sampling variance or variation among meta-analyses.
comments.quote: L 35: Unclear what is meant by "within-study variation." Do you refer to the sampling variance of the effect sizes

comments.issue: The term 'odd' is overly anthropocentric for scientific writing.
comments.request: Clarify if it is Darwin's wording or use a neutral term.
comments.quote: The term ‘odd’ may be overly anthropocentric for scientific writing.

comments.issue: Missing citation to another relevant review by Kuijper et al. 2012.
comments.request: Cite Kuijper et al. 2012.
comments.quote: Another nice review has been published by Kuijper et al. 2012.

comments.issue: Foundational genic capture hypothesis (Rowe and Houle 1996) not cited or introduced.
comments.request: Cite Rowe and Houle (1996) and mention the hypothesis.
comments.quote: the concept originates from Rowe and Houle (1996), who proposed the genic capture hypothesis. This foundational work should be cited

comments.issue: Paragraph states aims too vaguely without hypotheses and predictions.
comments.request: Specify the aim, hypotheses and predictions explicitly.
comments.quote: Please specify what you mean by “outstanding issues”, “unified knowledge”, and “patterns”.

comments.issue: The phrase 'on our results' needs clarification.
comments.request: Clarify what the analysis tests.
comments.quote: L 97: “on our results” could benefit from clarification.

comments.issue: Predictions for flexible versus fixed traits and other traits are not stated.
comments.request: State predictions for all trait classes.
comments.quote: Does this mean that you predict stronger effect sizes for the relationship between flexible traits and condition compared to fixed traits?

comments.issue: Unclear what theory is being tested; cited Johnstone et al. 1996 does not address the question.
comments.request: Clarify the theory the study aims to test.
comments.quote: Johnstone et al. 1996 do not seem to focus on this particular question, which makes me wondering even more what kind of theory are you aiming at testing here.

comments.issue: Correlational versus experimental primary studies could be an important moderator.
comments.request: Account for study design as a moderator.
comments.quote: Since the latter are more robust as they can establish causality, this distinction could represent an important moderator.

comments.issue: Randomly assigning effect direction for ambiguous cases is less rigorous than excluding them.
comments.request: Exclude ambiguous studies or justify the random assignment.
comments.quote: wouldn't this lack of clarity constitute a strong argument for excluding those primary studies?

comments.issue: The term 'unfit' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what 'unfit' means.
comments.quote: L 191: Unclear what “unfit” means here.

comments.issue: Trait ID is defined as both a random term and a fixed effect.
comments.request: Clarify this apparent duplication.
comments.quote: Why did you define trait ID as a random term when it is also specified as a fixed effect (L 214-215)?

comments.issue: Unclear whether all fixed moderators were fitted in one model or separately.
comments.request: Specify the model fitting strategy.
comments.quote: Please specify whether all fixed moderators were included altogether in one model or one by one in several models.

comments.issue: Unclear whether values were inverted (reciprocal) or signs were flipped.
comments.request: Clarify the transformation applied.
comments.quote: Did you really invert the value (computing the reciprocal) or did you actually invert the sign of the value?

comments.issue: Proportion of studies with inverted signs or removed is not reported.
comments.request: Report these proportions.
comments.quote: What is the proportion of studies in which you inverted the sign and/or were removed?

comments.issue: The section on predictor and response variables and their uncertainty is difficult to follow.
comments.request: Explain how variables were defined and uncertainty handled.
comments.quote: After reading it three times I still don’t understand how you defined predictor and response variable and how you dealt with the fact that both are estimated with some uncertainty.

comments.issue: Saying a trait is 'related to attractiveness' is circular or imprecise.
comments.request: Rephrase in terms of mating success.
comments.quote: it seems somewhat circular, or at least imprecise, to argue that a trait is “related to attractiveness”.

comments.issue: Section header about strength of sexual selection is uninformative.
comments.request: Make the header more informative.
comments.quote: I believe that the entire manuscript is centering on the “strength of sexual selection” which makes this header rather uninformative.

comments.issue: Species-level correlations lack statistical foundation given negligible between-species variance.
comments.request: Drop or qualify species-level moderator tests.
comments.quote: Given the very low between-species variance in one or both variables, I believe this test has limited interpretive value.

comments.issue: High heterogeneity does not imply that not all traits are sexually selected.
comments.request: Soften this conclusion.
comments.quote: High heterogeneity does not necessarily indicate that not all traits are sexually selected.

comments.issue: Unclear what the timing refers to.
comments.request: Specify the event whose timing is meant.
comments.quote: L 393: Timing of what? Pair formation?

comments.issue: Theoretical foundations are introduced only in the Discussion.
comments.request: Present the tested theory in the Introduction.
comments.quote: the manuscript would benefit from presenting the theoretical foundations underlying the tested hypotheses in the Introduction, rather than introducing them in the Discussion.

comments.issue: Claim that signals have no connection to sexual selection ignores post-copulatory selection.
comments.request: Write more cautiously about this claim.
comments.quote: I would advise more caution when writing ‘these signals have no connection to sexual selection’.

comments.issue: Unclear whether primary studies measured pre- or post-copulatory success.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of mating success measures.
comments.quote: clarifying whether the primary studies included in the analysis focused exclusively on pre-copulatory mating success, or whether some also assessed post-copulatory mechanisms

comments.issue: Why sexual selection on conspicuousness should intensify condition dependence is not explained.
comments.request: Explain this expectation.
comments.quote: Please explain more why sexual selection on conspicuousness is expected to intensify condition dependence.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive, robust and well-written synthesis of broad interest; only minor clarifications and additions requested.
strengths: well written with a good discussion

comments.issue: Mating system and sexual dimorphism were not considered as moderators.
comments.request: Consider adding these moderators to the meta-regression.
comments.quote: Why were mating system or degree of sexual dimorphism not considered as moderators in the meta-regression?

comments.issue: Phrase 'Despite varying their expectations' is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the phrase.

comments.issue: The word 'variables' is unclear in context.
comments.request: Clarify the meaning.

comments.issue: Findings on lines 152-156 are not discussed.

comments.quote: Not sure if you maybe also want to discuss the findings from lines 152-156?

comments.issue: Unclear whether the reported number is after deduplication.
comments.request: Clarify the deduplication status of the number.
comments.quote: Line 171 – unclear if this is when deduplicated or ?

comments.issue: Interesting observation on lines 182-183 deserves mention in the discussion.
comments.request: Add it to the discussion.
comments.quote: Lines 182-183 – this is an interesting observation. I feel it deserves a mention in the discussion.

comments.issue: Phrase 'distinct variables' is unclear.

comments.issue: Inconsistent use of PP and We misattributes who conducted analyses.

comments.issue: Long results section lacks a summary table or figure of main findings.
comments.request: Add a summary table or figure.
comments.quote: maybe it would be good to have a table or a figure that would summarise the main findings for the reader?

comments.issue: Generalisability information is reported inconsistently across results.

comments.quote: I noticed some inconsistencies in mentioning generalisability for different results. Sometimes this info is mentioned, sometimes it is not.

comments.issue: Introduction lacks a short general opening.
comments.request: Add a brief general start to the introduction.
comments.quote: I lack a short general start of the introduction

comments.issue: Unclear what the 'all' effect sizes in Figures 3 and 4 combine.
comments.request: Clarify what 'all' represents.
comments.quote: Fig 3 and 4 – effect sizes ‘all’- is this combining effect sizes for males and females that are also shown in the graph, or something else?

comments.issue: Seven line-level copy edits and textual changes suggested.
