title: Geography, Environmental Conditions and Life History Shape Patterns of Within‐Population Phenotypic Variation in North American Birds

study.system: 18 mammal species in Brazil; GPS tracking and home range scaling

editor_summary: Reviewers and editor found the work novel and well executed; asks whether female constraints are seasonal and whether pregnant or caring individuals can be identified in the data.

reviews.assessment: Clearly written and important topic; asks about excluded animals, generality across systems, guild-level results and figure clarity.
strengths: broad implications for animal space use

comments.issue: Sex ratios of excluded non-resident animals are not reported, and their exclusion may bias results.
comments.request: Report the sex ratios of excluded animals and discuss how exclusion affects results.
comments.quote: I think providing the sex ratios of animals excluded from analyses (in Table S4 or elsewhere) would provide valuable information to the reader.

comments.issue: Findings are limited to mammals in Brazil with relatively small home ranges.
comments.request: Add a limitations paragraph and discuss other systems, including migratory species.
comments.quote: I believe a paragraph in the Discussion would be helpful to note the limitations of your study and the need for broader work across other systems and other species.

comments.issue: Results are not separated by diet group (herbivores, carnivores, mixed feeders).
comments.request: Provide group-level results and restructure Figure 2 accordingly.
comments.quote: Can you take your results a step further and separate your findings between different groups (i.e., herbivores, omnivores, herbivores)? Are results consistent between herbivores, carnivores, and mixed feeders.

comments.issue: Interspecific references in Figure 3 resemble male estimates; comparability with sex-specific estimates is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what the interspecific reference estimates represent.
comments.quote: I wonder if I am missing something. If the interspecific estimates from other studies include males and females, why aren’t these estimates and associated confidence intervals more representative of your male and female estimates?

comments.issue: The abstract and methods say 475 individuals were tracked, though analyses use 349.
comments.request: State that 349 individuals were analyzed to avoid inflating the sample.
comments.quote: I believe it would be more appropriate to state that you analyzed 349 individuals from 2007-2024 across Brazil.

comments.issue: Morato et al. 2016 on jaguar sex differences is relevant but not included in the Introduction.
comments.request: Include the Morato et al. 2016 sex-difference findings.
comments.quote: They explicitly investigate differences in sex, findings that would seem valuable to include in the Introduction.

comments.issue: Male willingness to take greater risks is not included among the proposed drivers.
comments.request: Add risk-taking as a driver of male space use.
comments.quote: I agree with these statements, but think that the willingness of males to take greater risks should also be included.

comments.issue: The discussion could cite Morato et al. 2016 on jaguar responses to human population.
comments.request: Cite Morato et al. 2016 in the discussion.
comments.quote: I believe this is another opportunity cite the work of Morato et al. 2016, with a specific focus on jaguar in Brazil.

comments.issue: The risks of the male strategy of increasing home range are not cited.
comments.request: Add a citation about risks undertaken by males.
comments.quote: While not the focus of your research, I think it’s important to note that this strategy has risks. Perhaps a citation exists that could be cited here about the risks undertaken by males.

comments.issue: Sample sizes are only in Table S5 and not shown in the figure.
comments.request: Include sample sizes in the figure.
comments.quote: Perhaps too much information and while sample sizes are provided in Table S5, I had to dig to find out this important information. Would it be possible to include sample size in this Figure?

reviews.assessment: Important and straightforward study; asks to test male-female differences explicitly, discuss parturition and report credible intervals.
strengths: argument straightforward and easy to follow

comments.issue: A non-significant female slope does not show females differ from males, but the abstract implies a difference.
comments.request: State the male-female interaction result explicitly and align the abstract with line 71.
comments.quote: a reader might wonder whether there is a significant difference between males and females in the first place (i.e., female not being different from zero does not imply they are different from males)

comments.issue: Combining females with and without young may blur the female pattern.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of parturition status, or test unexplained variation.
comments.quote: I doubt the authors have the data to formally include parturition as a covariate in the analysis, but at a minimum, it might be good to discuss the implications of this in the discussion.

comments.issue: The discussion has redundant sections repeating earlier content.
comments.request: Remove redundant sentences.
comments.quote: The discussion has a few redundant sections. Most notably, the first few sentences of the third paragraph repeat content presented earlier.

comments.issue: Line-level copy edit at line 155 (“males to show”).
comments.quote: 4. Line 155: “males to show”. 5. Line 168: Since the methods come later, I initially expected to see two separate regressions

comments.issue: Line 168 suggests two regressions when a single interaction model was used.
comments.request: Adjust the wording to make the single-model structure clear.
comments.quote: Since the methods come later, I initially expected to see two separate regressions, but it is a single model with an interaction. Consider adjusting the wording to make this clearer.

comments.issue: Credible intervals are not reported alongside p-values.
comments.request: Report credible intervals for the Bayesian estimates.
comments.quote: While many prefer the simplicity of p-values, in my experience with Bayesian statistics, readers often expect to see credible intervals reported as well.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, valuable study; suggests testing seasonal female constraints, better habitat quality metrics and more statistical detail.

comments.issue: Gestation and lactation constraints should be seasonal; the hypothesis can be tested by removing those periods.
comments.request: Re-calculate AKDEs excluding gestation/lactation points and check semivariograms.
comments.quote: It could therefore be possible to test this hypothesis, for example by removing gestation/lactation points from the tracking data and re-calculating the AKDEs.

comments.issue: Proportion of dominant habitat type may not measure habitat quality.
comments.request: Use a more nuanced habitat quality metric such as productivity or tree cover.
comments.quote: I am not convinced that the proportion of the dominant habitat type is an appropriate proxy for habitat quality.

comments.issue: The variance in body mass and home range is ignored, though weaker female scaling may reflect smaller variance.
comments.request: Analyse how scaling relationships relate to species-level and sex-specific variances.
comments.quote: could the weaker scaling in females be due to a smaller variance in body masses and home range sizes?

comments.issue: Sex bias in tracked animals and its implications are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of telemetry sex bias.
comments.quote: Many/most telemetry studies have some sex bias in tracked animals, whether because of behavioral differences related to capture, size constraints on tagging, etc.

comments.issue: Variables were standardized before logging rather than after transformation.
comments.request: Justify the standardization order or redo it after transformation.
comments.quote: Why were these variables standardized and then logged, rather than standardized after transformation? If distributions are skewed, then standardizing after transformation would provide a better estimate of the “mean.”

comments.issue: Uncertainty in home range size may scale with home range size, biasing model results.
comments.request: Check the uncertainty-size relationship, e.g. with a coefficient of variation.
comments.quote: Was uncertainty in HR size related to HR size? I expect it could be (with larger HRs having higher uncertainty), in which case model results could be biased by a relationship between variance and mean.

comments.issue: Distributions of model inputs are not shown.
comments.request: Add plots of home range and body mass distributions.
comments.quote: I would have been interested see plots of data inputs into the models somewhere in the manuscript (or supplement)

comments.issue: Four line-level edits (L68 wording, L102 superscript, L119 wording, L163 figure reference).
comments.quote: 119: Suggest replacing “forage” with “move to acquire”

comments.issue: The basis for the metabolic expectation of 0.75 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the 0.75 expectation for non-specialists.
comments.quote: L103-104: Suggest explaining the basis for the metabolic expectation of 0.75 for readers who are not familiar with this literature.

comments.issue: Which rationale corresponds to which hypothesis is unclear.
comments.request: Split the hypotheses and their rationales.
comments.quote: It was not clear to me which rationale corresponded to which hypothesis (i.e., larger HR vs. steeper scaling). Suggest splitting the hypotheses and corresponding rationale for each.

comments.issue: “Positive effect of sex” lacks a stated reference level, also in the Figure 2 legend.
comments.request: State the sex reference level or rephrase.
comments.quote: Please note the reference level for sex or rephrase – “positive effect of sex” is not clear on its own! This is also true for the Figure 2 legend.

comments.issue: The hypothesis that larger females occupy higher-quality habitats is not tested.
comments.request: Test whether larger females occur in higher-quality habitats.
comments.quote: This hypothesis/explanation could also be tested. Did you see larger females in higher-quality habitats?

comments.issue: Spatial correlation and population-level structure are not accounted for.
comments.request: Consider spatial distances or a study area/population term.
comments.quote: Did you consider including spatial as well as phylogenetic distances, or a term that accounts for study area/population (for species that were tracked in multiple locations)?

title: Sex Drives Intraspecific Scaling of Home Range Size in Mammals

study.system: old-field ecosystem; 3-yr grasshopper predator common garden experiment

editor_summary: Both reviewers were principally positive, but mortality and the addition of new individuals created new treatments over time, making it hard to attribute patterns to initial treatments; revisions beyond a major revision are needed.

reviews.assessment: Impressive multi-year experiment, but the changing design and the G1/G2 contrast do not convincingly isolate transgenerational plasticity.
strengths: discrete grasshopper generations provide a good model
diverse old-field resource base for measuring ecosystem effects

comments.issue: The number of treatments changed across years and randomization may not have been preserved, so end-of-experiment differences may not be attributable to treatments.
comments.request: Show that randomization was preserved as treatments changed.
comments.quote: The first is about the change in the number of treatments over the years, and issues associated with whether randomization was preserved across the experiment such that differences at the end of the experiment could be attributed to the treatments.

comments.issue: It is not reported how many mesocosms were restocked or how balanced the new G1 treatment was, and density changes could explain the results.
comments.request: Report restocking numbers, treatment balance and density changes.
comments.quote: It’s not mentioned how many mescosms needed to be stocked, and thus how balanced or not these new treatments were.

comments.issue: Mesocosms without reproduction may not be a random subset, and without year-2 ecosystem measurements divergence cannot be excluded.
comments.request: Provide evidence that failed-reproduction mesocosms were a random subset.
comments.quote: As the ecosystems were not measured after the second year (and I understand the argument why) there is no way to be sure that the mesocosms diverged in the ecosystems between those with successful reproduction and those without.

comments.issue: The G1 versus G2 contrast is overly optimistic because G2 combines parental mesocosm experience with juvenile development, so transgenerational plasticity is not isolated.
comments.request: Use a common garden or ecosystem reset design to isolate transgenerational effects.
comments.quote: This contrast is used to argue for transgenerational plasticity, but I think this might be overly optimistic.

comments.issue: The mechanism of transgenerational plasticity (maternal effects, epigenetics, habitat matching) is not well described on lines 16-18.
comments.request: Describe the mechanisms of transgenerational plasticity more clearly.
comments.quote: This section does not really describe the mechanism of transgenerational plasticity very well.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the mechanism on line 20 is directional selection or repeated plastic response to a persistent environmental factor.
comments.request: Clarify the mechanism behind directional changes.
comments.quote: I think the underlying mechanism here is important. Is this directional selection (e.g. the response to predator-mediated natural selection), or the persistence of an environmental factor (e.g. predation) that evokes the same plastic response (e.g. of prey) every generation?

comments.issue: The hypotheses on L26 are weakly linked to why effects would amplify, which requires increasing effects at a given predator density.
comments.request: Link the hypotheses to the amplification mechanism.
comments.quote: These are useful hypotheses, but are weakly linked to why they might amplify or not each generation?

comments.issue: The paragraph on L28 is thin on details and does not explain how evolution or eco-evolutionary feedbacks are involved.
comments.request: Explain the evolutionary and eco-evolutionary context.
comments.quote: This paragraph is a bit thin on details that advance the main questions of the paper. It’s not clear to me how evolution is involved, or eco-evolutionary feedbacks?

comments.issue: The choice of four source populations and their elevation differences is not justified from a design perspective.
comments.request: Justify the choice of four populations.
comments.quote: Why four populations? Are there genetic or phenotypic differences among populations that are relevant to this choice?

comments.issue: Herbivores were not also hatched from non-predator enclosures, so enclosure-reared and non-enclosure-reared grasshoppers may differ in condition.
comments.request: Hatch herbivores from non-predator enclosures as a control.
comments.quote: Why weren’t herbivores also hatched from non-predator enclosures? Otherwise you might be comparing “enclosure” reared grasshoppers to “non-enclosure” reared grasshoppers.

comments.issue: Centering by population on L251 is not justified given population was previously a non-significant random effect.
comments.request: Justify centering or use population as a random effect.
comments.quote: This centering is not clearly justified. In previous analyses population was not a significant random effect, but is it here?

comments.issue: Multiple respiration estimates per individual are first mentioned on L259-261 and the number of replicates is not stated.
comments.request: Explain the respiration measurements earlier and report replicate numbers.
comments.quote: Here you mention for the first time that you made multiple respiration estimates per individual. But you should also explain this earlier around L202-217. How many replicate measures did you make per individual?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the pattern on L317 is plasticity and what the primary agent of plasticity is.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant by plasticity and its cause.
comments.quote: I’m not sure this is plasticity. Perhaps it would be helpful to clarify what you think the primary cause or agent of plasticity is in these mesocosms.

comments.issue: The section on L346 is speculative about mechanisms and vague about what organisms do differently.
comments.request: Make the mechanism discussion less speculative and more specific.
comments.quote: This section is pretty speculative about possible mechanisms underlying the observed patterns, and also pretty vague about what organisms would actually be doing differently

comments.issue: The design element on L372 does not isolate transgenerational plasticity from differential plasticity in adjacent generations.
comments.request: Clarify what the design can and cannot isolate.
comments.quote: This design element is useful, but it doesn’t isolate the mechanism to transgenerational plasticity, but rather potentially differential plasticity in adjacent generations

reviews.assessment: Highly interesting and welcome experiment, but the absence of a G2-only treatment leaves some conclusions less solid than suggested.
strengths: highly interesting paper on transgenerational predation effects
likes the experiment's general idea and set-up
first such study for terrestrial invertebrates

comments.issue: A G2 grasshoppers-without-predator treatment is missing, so G2 top-down effects cannot be separated from predator presence and the abstract claim is not justified.
comments.request: Add or account for a G2-only treatment to justify the conclusions.
comments.quote: My main concern is that I miss an important treatment in year 3: G2 grasshoppers without a predator.

comments.issue: The label 'herbivores-only' is misleading because it sounds like a treatment without vegetation.
comments.request: Rename the herbivores-only treatment.
comments.quote: Line 96: “herbivores-only” is a bit misleading because it sounds like “without vegetation”

comments.issue: Details such as vegetation composition in mesocosms, group abundances, natural grasshopper densities and natural hatching are missing.
comments.request: Provide these experimental details for cross-study comparisons.
comments.quote: I miss a bit some details of the experiments which I think are interestingly to know and also might be useful for cross-study comparisons.

comments.issue: Hatchling numbers likely varied substantially and grasshopper densities are not reported or considered in the analyses, though core results depend on them.
comments.request: Report hatchling variability and grasshopper densities and their treatment in the analyses.
comments.quote: There are no information given on the variability of number of hatchlings and if and how this was considered in the analyses.

title: Ecosystem Effects of Predators Are Amplified Across Generations Through Prey Behavioural Plasticity

study.system: European plants; native vs non-native microherbivore richness

editor_summary: Editor: both reviewers found the manuscript interesting with valuable results, but asked for clarification of trophic integration, dataset details including data inclusion and sampling effort, and generalist versus specialist definitions.

reviews.assessment: Good first draft with a valuable comparison; specific suggestions mainly concern terminology, definitions and dataset reporting.
strengths: valuable comparison of native and non-native plant interactions

comments.issue: The abstract uses 'non-natives' instead of a more specific term despite available word space.
comments.request: Use 'non-native plants' or 'introduced plants'.
comments.quote: Rather than just saying “non-natives,” could you say, “non-native plants,” “introduced plants,” or something else more specific?

comments.issue: Colons are used to define concepts on lines 61, 83 and elsewhere.
comments.request: Rephrase these colon constructions.
comments.quote: other places where you use the colon to define a concept

comments.issue: Whether the 26,140 microherbivores are all native to Europe or include introduced species is unclear.
comments.request: State the native status of the microherbivore species.
comments.quote: Are all 26,140 microherbivores included in the dataset native to Europe or have any of them been introduced like the non-native plant species included in this study?

comments.issue: Eight line-level wording edits (L142, L148, L188, L190, L265, L272, L278, L384, L391).
comments.quote: Line 190: Add comma to “e.g.” for consistency. Also on line 208, etc.

comments.issue: Why 130 species could not be classified as woody or not is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the classification failures.
comments.quote: So, you were unable to use these methods to successfully classify 130 species as woody or not? Did you just not have any other plants in the genus to infer from?

comments.issue: The rationale for the year 1500 cutoff and effects of pre-1500 introductions are unexplained.
comments.request: Justify the 1500 cutoff and discuss pre-1500 species.
comments.quote: How would the species introduced pre-1500 skew the analyses? What makes the year 1500 the cutoff? Are the records just inaccurate before this point in time?

comments.issue: Sample sizes for native plants, non-native plants and microherbivores are not reported.
comments.request: Report the sample sizes.
comments.quote: What were your sample sizes for native plant species, non-native plant species, and microherbivores for this analysis?

comments.issue: Generalists and specialists are not defined.
comments.request: Define generalists versus specialists.
comments.quote: How do you define generalists versus specialists in this study?

comments.issue: Why ranges vary between woody and non-woody species is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the range variation, moving lines 312-314 to the methods.
comments.quote: Why do the ranges vary for woody vs. non-woody species? Perhaps move the sentence on lines 312-314 to the methods to help partially explain this

comments.issue: Whether introduction time or range size affects specialist microherbivore numbers is not analysed.
comments.request: Test the drivers for specialist microherbivores.
comments.quote: Does time since non-native plant introduction or range size have any impact on the number of specialist microherbivores that interact with the non-native plant species?

comments.issue: Standard errors for the reported averages are missing.
comments.request: Report standard errors.
comments.quote: Do you have standard errors for these averages?

comments.issue: Passages on lines 282-284 and 329-330 read like methods.
comments.request: Move these passages to the methods.
comments.quote: Lines 282-284: This sentence reads a bit like methods

comments.issue: Counting host species does not demonstrate specialisation or generalisation of a microherbivore.
comments.request: Reconsider the specialist versus generalist definition using host phylogeny.
comments.quote: Simply counting the number of individual host species/taxa does not demonstrate the specialization or generalization of a microherbivore

comments.issue: The guild of the organism may affect the results but is not considered.
comments.request: Consider guild identity, such as gall-makers versus leaf feeders.
comments.quote: I’m also curious if the guild of the organism has anything to do with these results

comments.issue: Interactions dominated by generalists are not truly native-like.
comments.request: Soften the native-like interaction claim.
comments.quote: Not truly native-like interactions, if they are all generalists that do not have close relationships with the host

comments.issue: The defense-free space and host naivete hypotheses could explain the results.
comments.request: Consider these hypotheses.
comments.quote: If so, you might consider the defense-free space hypothesis (https://doi.org/10.1007/s10530-009-9627-9) or host naïveté hypothesis (https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.224) to explain your results

reviews.assessment: Likes the interesting large-scale study, but trophic integration is vague, dataset sampling effort is unclear, and the integration conclusion is overstated.
strengths: interesting finding that non-native herbivore richness follows macro-ecological patterns

comments.issue: The vague concept of 'trophic integration' obscures that the study is about herbivore species richness.
comments.request: Focus the title and abstract clearly on herbivore richness.
comments.quote: at present, it focuses on the concept of ‘trophic integration’, which is pretty vague

comments.issue: The European scale may be too large to preclude spillover of herbivore communities among plant species.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of spatial scale for the results.
comments.quote: I think there could be some further discussion about scale, as the scale of Europe is pretty big compared to what might allow spillover of herbivore communities among plant species

comments.issue: Concluding that non-native plants are rapidly integrated into food webs goes beyond richness estimates.
comments.request: Avoid the rapid integration conclusion.
comments.quote: I’d shy away from a conclusion, though, that non-native plants are rapidly integrated into food webs just like native plants

comments.issue: The dataset covers leaf miners, gallers and fungi, not free-feeding insects, and this scope is not made clear.
comments.request: State the scope of herbivores considered.
comments.quote: it would appear that the dataset is about leaf miners and galling insects as well as fungi. Thus, it would not appear to include free-feeding insects, but may include some non-arthropods

comments.issue: Non-interactions are inferred from absence of records without any measure of sampling effort.
comments.request: Assess sampling effort or use a well-sampled subset.
comments.quote: the matrix of plant-herbivore interactions infers non-interactions from the absence of the mention of an interaction between two species. How reasonable an assumption is this?

comments.issue: L83 should indicate that interactions are with the plant species, not individual plants.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction.
comments.quote: It might be useful to indicate that this is the total interactions with the plant species – not the interactions with a given individual

comments.issue: Taxonomic idiosyncrasies could be avoided by mapping plants onto large phylogenies.
comments.request: Map plants onto large phylogenies.
comments.quote: It would be easy enough to avoid the idiosyncrasies of taxonomy by mapping the plants onto large phylogenies

comments.issue: Assessing relatedness at the scale of Europe may be too coarse, as local oak diversity affects damage.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of the relatedness comparison.
comments.quote: Having a congener or confamilial at scale of Europe is also quite a large scale to make this comparison at

comments.issue: The thesis of the L431 paragraph is a bit of a strawman, though it is walked through well.
comments.request: Reconsider the framing of this argument.
comments.quote: I think I like this paragraph, though I would consider its thesis a bit of a strawman

comments.issue: Line-level edits on L413 and L450.
comments.quote: L413: in shaping richness of herbivorous insects L431: I think

comments.issue: The 'qualitative' versus 'quantitative' contrast on L456 is inaccurate; both measures are quantitative.
comments.request: Rephrase and clarify the focus on richness.
comments.quote: I don’t like the ‘qualitative’ versus ‘quantitative description here, as both measures (species richness and host breadth) are equally quantitative

comments.issue: The L490 paragraph is overstated unless restricted to generalist herbivores.
comments.request: State that the conclusion applies only to generalists.
comments.quote: I think some statement in here that this is really only true of generalist herbivores would be useful, as I think this paragraph is a bit overstated otherwise

title: Non‐Native Plants Attain Native Levels of Microherbivory Richness With Time and Range Expansion

study.system: European plant communities; 698,692 vegetation plots, machine learning

editor_summary: Both reviewers are positive but raise statistical concerns: explore proper scoring rules and deviation from 1:1 prediction, add confidence intervals to Figures 2–3, clarify how the common machine-learning methods are novel, and add values to Figure 1 scales.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and important study with broad interest, but validation may be inflated by non-independent train/test plots and the testing scheme is unclear.

comments.issue: High same-dataset model performance may be inflated because train and test plots are geographically and temporally close.
comments.request: Use spatial and/or temporal block cross-validation to test model performance.
comments.quote: could the plots being used to test and train these models be really close in geographic and temporal space? A way of assessing whether this is inflating model performance could be using spatial and/or temporal block cross validation techniques

comments.issue: What “static data” means and how models are tested across time periods is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the static-data concept and the testing procedure clearly.
comments.quote: I felt a bit confused about what static data means and about how it can be used to estimate species richness across different time periods.

comments.issue: Predictions are apparently not validated against observed richness at the same plot and time.
comments.request: Validate predictions against observed richness at time X for repeatedly sampled plots.
comments.quote: I was expecting predicted species richness for a given plot at time X to be compared against the observed species richness at time X for that same plot, but it doesn’t seem that this is case.

comments.issue: Interpolated trend figures lack confidence intervals showing trend variability.
comments.request: Add confidence intervals to Figures 2-3 and a map of gain/loss ranges.
comments.quote: For the figures that show the interpolated trends in species richness (e.g., Figures 2-3), I think it would be nice to have confidence intervals to show how variable those trends are.

comments.issue: The baseline for 1960-1980 gains and losses is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the baseline used for the 1960-1980 estimates.
comments.quote: it seems that only plots after 1960 were considered for the interpolation, but it is not clear to me what the baseline would be in those cases

comments.issue: The average interval between first and last sampling, and its effect on prediction ability, is not reported.
comments.request: Report the sampling interval and relate it to interpolation performance.
comments.quote: Is there a relationship between the number of years between the two sampling events and the ability of the interpolation to predict changes in species richness?

comments.issue: The percentage of plots sampled per habitat type is only in the supplement.
comments.request: State the per-habitat plot percentages in the methods.
comments.quote: What is the percentage of plots that were sampled at each habitat type? I see this information in the supporting material, but I think it would be useful to state it in the methods too.

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation in residuals was assessed only visually, without a formal test.
comments.request: Test residual spatial autocorrelation using Moran’s I.
comments.quote: I think you could also explicitly assess the presence of spatial autocorrelation in the residuals using tests such as Moran’s I.

comments.issue: The higher-latitude richness increase is not formally tested.
comments.request: Correlate species gain/loss with plot latitude.
comments.quote: This idea that communities at higher latitudes are increasing in species richness could be tested by looking at the correlation between species gain/loss and plot latitude.

reviews.assessment: Innovative, creative and worthwhile machine-learning approach to infer richness trends; asks only for minor clarifications and transparency about model tuning.

comments.issue: The time period behind the “near-zero net change” is not stated in the abstract.
comments.request: State explicitly that the near-zero net change refers to 1960–2020.
comments.quote: Please clarify the time period associated with the reported “near-zero net change in species richness.”

comments.issue: The text refers to magnitude while discussing both losses and gains.
comments.request: Rephrase to reflect both magnitude and direction of change.
comments.quote: I’d suggest rephrasing to reflect both magnitude and direction of change—since both clearly matter here.

comments.issue: The spatially structured nature of biodiversity change could serve more strongly as a framing element.
comments.request: Pull the spatial-structuring idea earlier and emphasize it as framing.
comments.quote: You might even consider pulling this idea up earlier or emphasizing it more as a framing element.

comments.issue: How the best node size and mtry combination was chosen is not explained.
comments.request: Describe the tuning procedure and robustness to choices.
comments.quote: I was left wondering—how was the “best” combination chosen? Was it based on out-of-bag (OOB) error, cross-validation, or something else?

title: Six Decades of Losses and Gains in Alpha Diversity of European Plant Communities

study.system: grassland ecosystems; mathematical partitioning of resistance and resilience

editor_summary: Editor says the topic is important and the text clear, but Reviewer 1's concern about lacking a real grassland experiment makes the paper read as pure theory; applying the method to real data is encouraged.

reviews.assessment: Strongly positive about the mathematical insight but wants the model illustration replaced by a real grassland biodiversity experiment.
strengths: novel mathematical analysis with a significant insight meriting publication
math was well explained and easily followed
no errors seen in the derivations

comments.issue: The abstract implies real grassland data and this paper's own mechanistic model, but neither was used.
comments.request: Make the abstract accurately describe the illustrative model.
comments.quote: I had thought that its relevance would be demonstrated for real grassland ecosystem data, and that the "mechanistic model" mentioned was the model developed in this paper. However, this was not the case.

comments.issue: The illustration analyses the Loreau 1998 competition model rather than an actual grassland biodiversity experiment.
comments.request: Apply the new method to a real grassland biodiversity experiment.
comments.quote: I feel that an even better possibility could be to replace it with an analysis of a grassland biodiversity experiment to demonstrate the utility of the novel math developed in the paper

comments.issue: The Loreau 1998 model section may confuse readers unfamiliar with that model.
comments.request: Delete the model or describe it in enough detail for an intuitive understanding.
comments.quote: For any reader who does not know the Loreau 1998 model well, this section of the paper could be rather confusing.

title: Partitioning Net Biodiversity Effects on Ecosystem Resistance and Resilience

study.system: crops, pests and natural enemies; global synthesis of 116 studies

editor_summary: Much to like but much confusion and need for clarity, particularly in data extraction and analysis; a third handling editor suggested desk reject; authors must clarify analyses before publication.

reviews.assessment: Important question with potential, but clarity, data extraction, analysis reporting and discussion need substantial revision.

comments.issue: The abstract alone does not make clear what the three tested hypotheses are.
comments.request: Clarify the hypotheses in the abstract.
comments.quote: not clear for me, reading only the abstract what are the “we tested the ‘natural enemy’, ‘resource concentration’, and ‘agronomic quality’ hypotheses.”

comments.issue: "Landscape composition" and what the larger scales are need to be defined in the abstract.
comments.request: Define landscape composition and the scales used.
comments.quote: better describe/define “landscape composition”? -Same for larger scales.

comments.issue: The abstract gives no indication of the magnitude of scale-dependent effects on yield.
comments.request: Report the magnitude of scale-dependent yield effects.
comments.quote: Provide some indication of the magnitude of the scale-dependent effects on yield ?

comments.issue: Introduction framing is not explicitly connected to the sustainable intensification debate and landscape ecology.
comments.request: Connect the framing to sustainable intensification and landscape ecology.
comments.quote: the framing could benefit from a more explicit connection to the broader debate on sustainable intensification and the role of landscape ecology in achieving it

comments.issue: The introduction acknowledges inconsistent previous findings but does not critically analyse why they differ.
comments.request: Analyse whether discrepancies are methodological, spatial or ecosystem-related.
comments.quote: While the introduction acknowledges the inconsistency in previous findings, it could be more critical in analyzing the reasons for these discrepancies.

comments.issue: The natural enemy hypothesis oversimplifies natural enemy interactions; configuration, habitat quality, alternative prey, intraguild predation and hyperparasitism matter.
comments.request: Consider these modulating factors in the hypothesis.
comments.quote: Factors like landscape configuration, habitat quality, and the presence of alternative prey can significantly modulate natural enemy efficacy. The role of intraguild predation and hyperparasitism also warrants consideration

comments.issue: Resource concentration needs careful definition when applied across heterogeneous landscapes.
comments.request: Define how resource concentration translates across landscape heterogeneity.
comments.quote: The concept of resource concentration is sound, but its application to landscape scales requires careful definition.

comments.issue: The agronomic quality hypothesis is circular if defined by yield; it needs independent, measurable variables.
comments.request: Define agronomic quality independently and separate site quality from management.
comments.quote: this hypothesis risks circularity. If 'agronomic quality' is defined solely by yield outcomes, it becomes a tautology. It needs to be defined by measurable, independent variables

comments.issue: The three hypotheses are presented in isolation without considering how they interact.
comments.request: Discuss interactions among the hypotheses.
comments.quote: The hypotheses should not be viewed in isolation. How do they interact with each other?

comments.issue: Repeated references to Fig. 1 make the hypothesis presentation not self-contained.
comments.request: Make the text self-contained.
comments.quote: throughout the hypothesis presentation could be problematic-> The text should be more self-contained

comments.issue: It is unclear how heterogeneity in study designs, agricultural systems and contexts will be addressed.
comments.request: Explain how heterogeneity will be handled.
comments.quote: Given the broad scope of the meta-analysis, how will you address potential heterogeneity in study designs, agricultural systems, and environmental contexts?

comments.issue: It is unclear how functional traits will be measured and classified, including herbivore specialization and pollinator dependence.
comments.request: Explain trait operationalization across crops and scales.
comments.quote: Lacks clarity on how traits will be measured/classified. How to quantify herbivore specialization? Pollinator dependence

comments.issue: The rationale for using SEM is not sufficiently explained.
comments.request: Explain why SEM suits the research questions.
comments.quote: While SEM is mentioned, the paragraph could provide a slightly more detailed rationale for its use. Why is SEM particularly well-suited to address the research questions?

comments.issue: "Landscape complexity" is vague and some predictions are phrased vaguely.
comments.request: Define landscape complexity and sharpen vague predictions.
comments.quote: “Landscape complexity” is still vague, and need to be defined.+ Some of the predictions are phrased vaguely.

comments.issue: How the Karp et al. (2018) database was originally compiled is not described, and it may need updating.
comments.request: Describe database compilation and justify not updating it.
comments.quote: The MM states the data comes from Karp et al. (2018), but it doesn't detail how Karp et al. (2018) initially compiled their database.

comments.issue: Data extraction and formal study quality assessment (variables, units, risk of bias, inter-rater reliability) are not described.
comments.request: Describe extraction and quality assessment procedures.
comments.quote: A detailed description of the data extraction process and a formal assessment of study quality are essential.

comments.issue: It is not fully explained how heterogeneity was explored or accounted for.
comments.request: Explain how heterogeneity was explored and accounted for.
comments.quote: while the MM standardizes data, it doesn't fully explain how heterogeneity was explored or accounted

comments.issue: No formal assessment of publication bias is reported.
comments.request: Assess publication bias (funnel plots, Egger's test).
comments.quote: The MM doesn't mention any formal assessment of publication bias (e.g., funnel plots, Egger's test)

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the study qualifies as a meta-analysis under CEE or Cochrane guidelines or is better described as a global analysis.
comments.request: Justify the meta-analysis label against established guidelines.
comments.quote: Could this method be considered a meta-analysis, defined as a systematic review combined with statistical quantitative analyses

comments.issue: Landscape measurement scales may mismatch the scales at which ecological interactions occur.
comments.request: Test and discuss potential scale mismatches.
comments.quote: A mismatch could occurs when the scale at which landscape data is measured doesn't align with the scale at which ecological interactions occur

comments.issue: The 250, 750 and 1250 m decay rates may not reflect the actual influence of distance on different insect species.
comments.request: Justify the decay rates for different species.
comments.quote: The decay rates (250, 750, 1250 meters) may not accurately reflect the actual influence of distance on different insect species

comments.issue: Matrix influences vary with habitat connectivity, edge effects and organism dispersal but this is not accounted for.
comments.request: Account for matrix-related variability.
comments.quote: The degree to which the landscape matrix influences in-field interactions can vary depending on factors like habitat connectivity, edge effects, and organism dispersal.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the time frame of landscape features aligns with the dates of yield, pest and predator measurements.
comments.request: Report and address temporal alignment of landscape and response data.
comments.quote: Does the time frame of landscape feature characteristics always align with the date of crop yield, pest, or predator measurements?

comments.issue: The reason for focusing on the subset with low variation in agricultural and natural cover is not emphasized.
comments.request: Justify the subset selection more clearly.
comments.quote: The exclusion criteria are clear, but the why behind focusing on this specific subset needs more emphasis

comments.issue: The herbivore classification's "additional knowledge" is not precisely defined, nor are its sources and consistency checks.
comments.request: Define the additional knowledge and its sources.
comments.quote: What are the « additional knowledge »? This needs to be precisely defined. What were the sources, and how was consistency ensured?

comments.issue: The database lacks descriptive analyses of crop distribution, landscape characteristics and geography.
comments.request: Add descriptive analyses of the database.
comments.quote: To enhance the reader's understanding and contextualization of the results, it would be highly beneficial to include descriptive analyses of the database.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether other aspects of collection effort, such as transects or traps, were standardized.
comments.request: State whether transects and trap numbers were considered.
comments.quote: Were other aspects of collection effort considered, such as the number of transects or traps?

comments.issue: The yield variables and the yield-type test are not explained clearly.
comments.request: Explain the yield variables and yield-type test.
comments.quote: What are the yield variables? (i.e. “we selected the landscape and yield variables”)-> Not explained, clear.

comments.issue: The meaning of the 'log + 3' and 'log + 2' transformations needs explicit clarification.
comments.request: Clarify these transformations.
comments.quote: the meaning of ‘log + 3’ and ‘log + 2’ transformations in Supplementary Material 3 needs explicit clarification

comments.issue: Model assumptions, outlier handling and residual diagnostics are not discussed in detail.
comments.request: Discuss assumptions, outliers and residual diagnostics.
comments.quote: The authors mention checking for normality and heteroskedasticity, but a more detailed discussion of model assumptions is crucial. How were outliers handled? Were residual diagnostics thoroughly examined?

comments.issue: Independence of predictors is not discussed, and dropping natural habitat at other scales may lose information.
comments.request: Discuss independence and manage the loss of information.
comments.quote: The assumption of independence needs explicit discussion. Are there potential correlations between predictor variables, and if so, how were they addressed?

comments.issue: The paragraph relating models to hypotheses is difficult to understand.
comments.request: Improve the clarity of the model-hypothesis presentation.
comments.quote: The paragraph explaining how the models relate to the hypotheses is difficult to understand.

comments.issue: Random-effect rationale is unjustified, whether separate models were built per dependent variable is unstated, and Supplementary Fig. 1 appears to be the species list.
comments.request: Justify the random effect, state the model-per-response design, and fix the SI figure reference.
comments.quote: The rationale behind the ‘year nested within a study’ random effect also requires more detailed justification. Were alternative random effect structures explored?

comments.issue: The dredge-based variable selection lacks detail on tied models, interactions and retention thresholds.
comments.request: Explain tied models, interactions and the retention rule.
comments.quote: The use of the dredge function for variable selection needs more detailed explanation. How were tied models handled? Were interaction terms considered ? only additive models?

comments.issue: Which transformations were applied and why is not specified.
comments.request: Specify transformations and their rationale.
comments.quote: The authors mention applying transformations but do not specify which transformations were used or provide their rationale.

comments.issue: SEM structure justification, derivation of independence claims, and the Fisher's C and 'missing links' procedures are all vague.
comments.request: Strengthen the SEM justification and describe the d-separation and Fisher's C procedures.
comments.quote: The justification for the specific SEM structure needs strengthening. Why were these particular pathways chosen over others?

comments.issue: Stepwise model modification criteria are unstated and bias/overfitting risks are not addressed.
comments.request: State the criteria and explain how bias was mitigated.
comments.quote: The criteria for adding or removing paths in the stepwise model modification process should be explicitly stated.

comments.issue: It is not explained why the full model with all traits failed to converge or what was done about it.
comments.request: Explain the convergence failure and its resolution.
comments.quote: The authors should provide more details on why the full model with all traits did not converge.

comments.issue: The text describing the models is suboptimally structured and lacks subheadings.
comments.request: Use subheadings to organize the modelling text.
comments.quote: Subheadings should be used to break down complex procedures into manageable sections

comments.issue: It is not stated whether the proportions of agricultural and natural land are correlated.
comments.request: Clarify the correlation, e.g. with a supplementary correlation matrix.
comments.quote: The results fail to explicitly state whether the proportion of agricultural land and the proportion of natural areas are correlated.

comments.issue: Results report only increases/decreases without path coefficients, confidence intervals or effect sizes.
comments.request: Report path coefficients, confidence intervals and effect sizes.
comments.quote: Instead of general statements of 'increase' or 'decrease,' authors should provide path coefficient values, confidence intervals, and effect sizes.

comments.issue: 'Proportion of agriculture' is not precisely defined, including whether grasslands are included.
comments.request: Define 'proportion of agriculture' precisely.
comments.quote: A precise definition of what constitutes the 'proportion of agriculture' is required. Specifically, it must be clarified whether grasslands are included.

comments.issue: Path coefficients are presented without explaining their meaning or how they differ from correlations.
comments.request: Explain path coefficient interpretation to readers.
comments.quote: The presentation of path coefficients necessitates a more detailed explanation of their meaning and interpretation.

comments.issue: Typographical error at line 334 (extra period or missing capitalization).
comments.request: Correct the typo at line 334.
comments.quote: At line 334, there appears to be an extra period or a missing capitalization. A correction is necessary for textual clarity.

comments.issue: The small-scale negative effect of natural habitat needs more nuanced discussion of its strength and implications.
comments.request: Discuss the magnitude and ecological/agronomic implications at small scales.
comments.quote: would benefit from a more nuanced discussion. An examination of the strength and magnitude of these effects, along with a discussion of their ecological and agronomic implications at small scales, is warranted.

comments.issue: The pollinator-dependence comparison is implied but not directly statistically tested.
comments.request: Test whether parameters differ between crop types.
comments.quote: the results do not present a direct statistical test of this difference. It is important to indicate whether a statistical method was used to directly test if the parameters are statistically different

comments.issue: The discussion often merely reiterates results without in-depth interpretation or ecological mechanisms.
comments.request: Rewrite the discussion to provide genuine analysis.
comments.quote: The discussion exhibits sometimes a tendency to merely reiterate the results obtained, without providing genuine analysis or in-depth interpretation.

comments.issue: The missing pest-yield link is explained only by damage thresholds; mechanisms and agronomic factors are not explored.
comments.request: Explore mechanisms, compensatory responses and agronomic factors.
comments.quote: Simply attributing this to pests being 'below damage thresholds' is inadequate/insufficient?. A more comprehensive exploration of potential ecological mechanisms is recommended.

comments.issue: Interpretations about marginal lands and edge effects remain speculative without empirical support from the meta-analysis.
comments.request: Substantiate or temper the speculative interpretations.
comments.quote: The interpretations regarding the negative effects of small-scale natural habitats on yield, particularly concerning 'marginal lands' and 'edge effects,' remain largely speculative.

comments.issue: The ecological rationale for scale-dependent parasitoid-predator shifts is not adequately explained.
comments.request: Explain dispersal, habitat preferences and functional roles.
comments.quote: Merely stating that generalist predators are 'more resilient' is insufficient. A deeper exploration of species-specific dispersal capabilities, habitat preferences, and functional roles within the ecosystem is needed

comments.issue: The discussion does not adequately address meta-analysis limitations, publication bias and study quality.
comments.request: Discuss limitations, biases and quality assessment.
comments.quote: The discussion fails to adequately address the inherent limitations of meta-analysis, particularly concerning potential biases.

comments.issue: Temporal and spatial autocorrelation in the dataset is completely overlooked.
comments.request: Acknowledge and address autocorrelation.
comments.quote: The discussion completely overlooks the potential impacts of temporal and spatial autocorrelation within the dataset.

reviews.assessment: Excellent, well-replicated study using up-to-date statistics with broad relevance; only minor comments.
strengths: broad relevance for ecology and stakeholders

comments.issue: Conclusions remain too generic to provide specific management recommendations.
comments.request: Provide more management recommendations for specific situations.
comments.quote: I would prefer to see more management recommendations for specific situations.

comments.issue: Temporal dynamics of landscapes, such as crop rotation, are not considered.
comments.request: Consider temporal landscape dynamics (e.g. Schneider et al. 2015).
comments.quote: The authors did not consider temporal dynamics in the landscape, which could play a role for pest control in areas were landscapes change frequently due to crop rotation

comments.issue: The agronomic quality hypothesis could be supported by Neyret et al. (2023), which is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Neyret et al. (2023) in support.
comments.quote: The newly developed agronomic quality hypothesis can be backed by results of Neyret et al. (2023)

comments.issue: The introduction cites mostly older literature.
comments.request: Search for more recent papers for the introduction.
comments.quote: the authors could search for some more recent papers for the introduction.

title: The Importance of Landscape Composition for Pest Control and Crop Yield: A Global Quantitative Synthesis

study.system: monarch caterpillar gut bacterial communities; 16S metabarcoding

editor_summary: Reviewers commend novelty and theory grounding but raise concerns about the immigration and ontogeny components; the editor notes the manuscript may not fully prove the results and its breadth may need reducing.

reviews.assessment: Well-written, theory-grounded study, but inadequate sampling and a very short 3rd-instar timeframe undermine confidence in the results.

comments.issue: Total of 92 samples with only 5-9 per instar-treatment combination is too low.
comments.request: Increase replication to about 30 samples per combination.
comments.quote: The manuscript is based on a total of 92 samples. This is an extremely low sample size for contemporary 16S metabarcoding

comments.issue: Third-instar samples taken only 24h after feeding make those results trivial and possibly transient.
comments.request: Sample more densely across ontogeny rather than two timepoints.
comments.quote: the 3rd instar samples (50 of 92) were collected only 24 hours after the larvae were experimentally fed bacteria. This is a very short timeframe and, in my opinion, renders the 3rd instar results fairly trivial.

comments.issue: Duplicated wording 'lineages lab-reared lineages' at L156.
comments.quote: L156 "four full-sib lineages lab-reared lineages"

comments.issue: Sequence data are not yet publicly available despite the accession.
comments.request: Deposit the data and make them public.
comments.quote: the data are not available in NCBI/ENA/DDBJ. The bioproject accession PRJNA1106479 has the following message on the ENA

comments.issue: Numbers of discarded mitochondrial and chloroplast reads are not reported.
comments.request: Report how many reads were discarded.
comments.quote: Report the numbers of reads discarded. It is pretty clear that mt/chloroplast reads are inversely correlated with bacterial biomass.

comments.issue: Number of discarded non-aligning reads is not reported.
comments.request: Report how many mystery reads were discarded.
comments.quote: likewise, how many of these mystery reads were discarded?

comments.issue: Non-focal bacterial diversity is collapsed into a single grey bar in Figure 2.
comments.request: Summarise non-focal taxa at higher ranks in supplementary figures.
comments.quote: The diversity of the "non focal" bacteria are not presented and is simply summed to a single grey bar.

reviews.assessment: Innovative design and robust analyses, but the 'immigration' treatment may not represent true immigration, questioning the central interpretation.

comments.issue: Frass-amended leaf discs may enhance the phyllosphere rather than create a true immigration event.
comments.request: Justify or redesign the treatment as a true immigration event.
comments.quote: using frass to amend leaf discs may not represent a true immigration event but rather an artificial enhancement of the milkweed phyllosphere

comments.issue: Within-gut spatial turnover is not considered in the design.
comments.request: Consider whether gut spatial structure matters for the treatment.
comments.quote: I wonder if there is spatial turnover as there is with gut microbiomes of larger hosts

comments.issue: Inoculum relatedness (frass microbes already passed through a gut) may drive dominance, confounding immigration effects.
comments.request: Account for inoculum relatedness when interpreting divergence patterns.
comments.quote: The relatedness of the 'immigrating' consortia is crucial, as they are organisms that have already survived the caterpillar's digestive system and are likely to dominate in subsequent rounds.

comments.issue: Introduction oversimplifies the field and omits many relevant studies.
comments.request: Cite a broader set of studies to give a comprehensive overview.
comments.quote: the introductory statements oversimplify a subfield that has already addressed many of the issues raised

comments.issue: Composition and diversity of the inoculum isolate set are unclear.
comments.request: Report within-family diversity and isolate-to-ASV mapping.
comments.quote: What is the within family diversity? It is a frass microbiome converged to just 5 ASVs, spanning 5 families?

comments.issue: Retention of phyllosphere versus frass microbes through the coalescence event is not quantified.
comments.request: Quantify retention of the different source communities.
comments.quote: you could determine individual microbial retention through your experimental coalescence event using approaches from those tackling community coalescence

comments.issue: Muted effect of frass amendment in 5th instars may reflect similarity to their own frass microbiome.
comments.quote: So adding more microbes sourced from the frass of older caterpillars has a muted effect on gut diversity of older caterpillar, since I imagine the gut microbiome of 5th instar is more similar to the frass microbiome.

comments.issue: Reintroducing later-stage microbiome may artificially hasten third-instar convergence.
comments.quote: The time to convergence for a 3rd instar seems like it would decrease with the 'immigration' of later microbiome to the foregut?

title: Experimental Immigration Mediates Ecological Selection and Drift in Monarch Microbiome Assembly

study.system: freshwater phytoplankton; biodiversity and CuO nanoparticles; microcosms

editor_summary: Both reviewers find the study interesting and conclusions supported, but the introduction, methods and results need more explanation.

reviews.assessment: High-quality and sound study, but the novelty is limited and some results need more emphasis.

comments.issue: Nanoparticle effects in monoculture versus mixture are not compared or emphasised.
comments.request: Correlate monoculture and mixture effects and highlight them.
comments.quote: It would be nice to see some correlations of these effects in monoculture and mixture.

comments.issue: The facilitative interaction analysis is in the methods but barely discussed.
comments.request: Move this analysis into the main text.
comments.quote: I would move some of this analysis that examines how these interactions change into the main text.

comments.issue: The choice of day 21 as the start of the biomass window is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the time points used.
comments.quote: Why did you choose 21 as the start day for the biomass data?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether biodiversity effects were calculated from averages per richness level.
comments.request: Clarify how biodiversity effects were computed.
comments.quote: I'm assuming that the biodiversity effects were calculated from averages for a given richness value?

comments.issue: Model equations or R formulas are not shown.
comments.request: Provide the model equations or R formulas.
comments.quote: it would be nice to, at minimum see the R-formulas for the models but the full model equations would be better

comments.issue: Model fit statistics and observed-versus-predicted plots are missing.
comments.request: Show model fit statistics and diagnostic plots.
comments.quote: I would like some tables showing model fit statistics and/or observed versus predicted value plots

comments.issue: Typo 'respones' on Line 286.
comments.request: Correct to 'response'.
comments.quote: Line 286: respones should be response.

comments.issue: Only processed data were shared, not raw data and processing steps.
comments.request: Share raw data and processing code.
comments.quote: It would be more in line with open science principles to share the raw data and how it was processed.

reviews.assessment: Relevant topic with some prior work; many methodological details on pH, sterility and biomass need clarification.

comments.issue: Previous work on biodiversity and nanoparticle stress (Kulacki & Cardinale 2012, Dauda et al. 2020) is not cited.
comments.request: Cite these earlier studies.
comments.quote: It is true that the role of biodiversity in maintaining ecosystems exposed to nanoparticles remains a largely unexplored field but there is some previous work.

comments.issue: The wide variation in final monoculture biomass across species may affect mixture outcomes.
comments.request: Assess how species-level biomass variation affected multispecies results.
comments.quote: To what extent do the authors consider this to have affected the outcome of experiments with multiple species.

comments.issue: COMB0 recipe, pH buffering and pH variation are not reported, though pH can affect copper oxide dissolution and growth.
comments.request: Report the recipe, pH control and measured pH variation.
comments.quote: Was the pH adjusted by use of a buffer as pH has been reported to vary considerably in the media and pH may affect dissolution of copper oxide nanoparticles.

comments.issue: The composition of the transparent test-tube covering is not stated.
comments.request: Describe the covering material.
comments.quote: What was the composition of the transparent covering on the test tubes?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether media were sterile-filtered or autoclaved, with particulate risks.
comments.request: State the sterilization method.
comments.quote: Was the media sterile-filtered prior to use, or was it autoclaved, the latter risking particulate formation?

comments.issue: Axenic status of the cultures and potential bacterial effects are not stated.
comments.request: Report whether cultures were axenic and discuss bacterial effects.
comments.quote: Were the cultures axenic? If not, would bacteria have played a role in the outcome of the experiments?

comments.issue: Biomass formulae were calibrated only on unexposed cells, with no check for nanoparticle-induced cell volume changes.
comments.request: Test for species-specific cell volume changes under exposure.
comments.quote: Was there evidence of species-specific changes in cell volume associated with exposure to nanomaterial?

title: Biodiversity Buffers Phytoplankton Biomass Production Against Nanoparticle Pollution Through Increased Facilitation

study.system: aphids and parasitoids; metacommunity model plus microcosm experiment

editor_summary: Editor values the integrated approach but reports mixed feedback: the main concerns are the model-experiment alignment (R1) and the artificial experiment restricting natural dispersal (R2), which cannot be fixed post hoc; revision must answer these convincingly.

reviews.assessment: Strong, clearly written and timely contribution; only minor comments on figures and data archiving.
strengths: nice balance between generality and realism

comments.issue: Treatment mean points in Figure 2 are hard to discern among individual observations, especially the filled points.
comments.request: Adjust the layering so treatment means stand out.
comments.quote: It is difficult to discern the treatment mean data points, particularly the filled points, among the individual observations/simulation points.

comments.issue: Simulation and experimental results are hard to distinguish in grayscale.
comments.request: Use a more distinct colour scheme or shading.
comments.quote: if printed or viewed in grayscale, it is very difficult to distinguish between the simulation and experimental results, I suggest considering a more distinct color scheme or shading to make this more accessible.

comments.issue: How effect sizes in Figure 3 were calculated is not immediately clear.
comments.request: Outline one worked example to orient readers.
comments.quote: it took me a bit to grasp how the effect sizes were calculated, whether the % increase was based from a fixed ‘baseline’ treatment or from the individual community food web treatments on the y-axis

comments.issue: Archived data use xlsx format with limited metadata, hindering long-term cross-platform use.
comments.request: Expand metadata and archive data as csv or tsv.
comments.quote: I would suggest the authors consider expanding the associated metadata and using platform-independent, standard data formats such as csv or tsv rather than xlsx format to ease long-term and cross-platform use.

reviews.assessment: The experiment and model are too artificial: tube-crawling dispersal and adjacent-patch-only movement ignore real flight dispersal, a fundamental flaw.
strengths: much effort went into parameterizing the model

comments.issue: The experiment forces crawling through tubes between close containers, unlike real flight dispersal, so rates are unrealistic.
comments.request: Rework the dispersal experiment to reflect natural flight dispersal.
comments.quote: the presented experiment is so artificial that it has little or nothing to do with the actual process of dispersal in these aphids and parasitoids in the field

comments.issue: The stepping-stone assumption restricts movement to adjacent patches, excluding the jumps that occur in the field.
comments.request: Allow longer-distance and skipped-patch dispersal in the model.
comments.quote: All insects can only move between adjacent patches. But this is not how dispersal wil invariably happen in the field.

comments.issue: No data on flight behaviour or movement patterns of the study species are used, leaving the work isolated from field reality.
comments.request: Ground the study in empirical movement data for these species.
comments.quote: The whole paper refers to no data at all (!) about the flight behaviour and movement patterns across plants, patches of vegetation and landscapes of the studied species.

reviews.assessment: Exciting, well-written and timely study, but the relationship between model predictions and experiments needs a clearer, more consistent focus.
strengths: one of the most exciting manuscripts I have read
intriguing combination of lab experiments and modelling

comments.issue: A priori modelling choices are parameterised rather than tested, and the Supplement does not explain how experiments informed them.
comments.request: State clearly how experimental data influenced the modelling choices.
comments.quote: there are a-priory modelling choices about the mechanisms included and their shape/mathematical formulations (e.g., linear prey density dependence of the parasitoid’s clearance rate) that are not tested but parameterized with experiments

comments.issue: Simulations with larger landscapes are an extrapolation, not a prediction tested against the empirical results.
comments.request: Reframe the larger-landscape simulations as extrapolation, not prediction testing.
comments.quote: The modelling with the larger landscapes now is more of an extrapolation then a prediction to be tested against the empirical results.

comments.issue: The paper's two goals, testing model predictions versus generalizing findings, are not clearly distinguished and the structure distracts from the message.
comments.request: Clarify the goal and align simulations with experiments, revising Figure 1.
comments.quote: This structure is a bit confusing to me and might distract from the central message.

comments.issue: The composite complexity measure and its implications, such as modularity and changing motifs, need more discussion.
comments.request: Discuss how network structure and motifs affect colonization and the dispersal versus local-dynamics balance.
comments.quote: I think some more discussion on this would be good when discussing the relative contributions of dispersal and local dynamics.

comments.issue: Simulations disagree substantially with the experiment in the 2 aphids, 1 parasitoid treatment.
comments.request: Address this simulation-experiment mismatch.
comments.quote: Interestingly, in your 2 aphids, 1 parasitoid treatment the simulations disagree quite a bit with the experiment (Figure 2, panel A).

comments.issue: Extrapolating the model to more complex food webs is likely infeasible because it needs species-specific parameters.
comments.request: Acknowledge this limitation when discussing extrapolation.
comments.quote: an extrapolation to more complex food webs in the simulations are likely infeasible as this model requires species-specific parameterizations

comments.issue: Synchrony is introduced without explaining its relevance and is not part of the analyses.
comments.request: Explain why synchrony matters for recovery or drop the topic.
comments.quote: It is unclear to me why synchrony is introduced here. It could maybe be explained that (spatial) synchrony needs a landscape scale perspective and may matter for recovery, colonization and large-scale disturbances.

comments.issue: The introduction's stated focus on testing model predictions conflicts with its broader ecological framing.
comments.request: Make the introduction's focus consistent.
comments.quote: Here it reads to me as the main focus would be testing model predictions. Else, the introduction reads to me more as the ecological question of how landscape structure and food-web complexity interact in affecting restoration.

comments.issue: Whether movement between containers is metacommunity-scale dispersal is questionable, especially for parasitoids where it may be foraging.
comments.request: Discuss the scale interpretation of movement, especially for parasitoids.
comments.quote: Is this really at the scale of a metacommunity? I am inclined to agree for aphids as probably most individuals that do move from container to container are dispersal morphs

comments.issue: How the perishing plant resource is handled in model fitting is unclear.
comments.request: Explain where the perishing resource effect goes in the fitting.
comments.quote: First, where does the effect of the perishing resource go in the model fitting? Is that implicitly captured indirectly through the density effects in the competition coefficients?

comments.issue: A patch slowly becoming non-habitat is unrealistic and its effect on simulated patterns is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how habitat loss over the plant lifespan affects simulated patterns.
comments.quote: Second, how is the fact, that a patch is slowly turning into a non-habitat patch affecting the simulated patterns? This would not be a very realistic scenario for real landscapes, right?

comments.issue: Mechanism-disentangling results such as Figure S6 are not prominent enough.
comments.request: Make these results more prominent.
comments.quote: I think the very interesting results from Figure S6 or similar could be a bit more prominent.

comments.issue: Emigration rates estimated as net migration in the experiment may be used as true emigration rates in the model.
comments.request: Clarify how emigration rates were parameterised.
comments.quote: In the experiment for parameter estimation, the emigration rates encompass the net migration (including individuals that go back again) right? The model, however, uses that as a true emigration rate, or did I misunderstand?

comments.issue: Many results make it hard to link results to the discussion.
comments.request: Add subheadings on space and food-web complexity in results and discussion.
comments.quote: Maybe a few more subheadings within the effect of space and of food-web complexity in the results and discussion would help.

comments.issue: The 'contrasting finding' may simply reflect that the central patch is the only colonisable empty patch.
comments.request: Reconsider whether this finding is truly contrasting.
comments.quote: Is this really a contrasting finding? As the authors then also state, the central patch is then the only empty one that can be colonized.

comments.issue: Figure 1 is very busy, especially part A.
comments.request: Simplify the figure and reduce the food-web complexity combinations shown.
comments.quote: I find this one to be very busy though, especially part A. Does it really need to have all the combinations/levels of food web complexity here?

comments.issue: Model predictions in Figure 2 are hard to see, especially the orange points in dense panels.
comments.request: Improve the visibility of model predictions.
comments.quote: I find the model predictions hard to see, especially the orange ones and in all the left boxes where the point density is higher.

comments.issue: Figure S2 is never referenced in the text.
comments.request: Reference Figure S2 in the text.
comments.quote: I believe Figure S2 is not referenced anywhere in the text.

comments.issue: 'Evolution' appears to be the wrong word in figure captions.
comments.request: Replace 'evolution' with the appropriate term in captions.
comments.quote: Also, is “evolution” really the right word here (and in other Figure captions)?

title: The Roles of Space and Food‐Web Complexity in Mediating Ecological Recovery

study.system: wild black rats; host-microbe networks along a land-use gradient

editor_summary: Both specialists found the paper interesting and relevant but raised questions that must be addressed before a final decision.

reviews.assessment: Innovative and well-structured, with major comments on focus, network visualizations and site-level inference.

comments.issue: The introduction spends five paragraphs reviewing existing assembly methods although the approach is adopted from refs 43 and 44.
comments.request: Streamline the introduction for focus and conciseness.
comments.quote: the authors devote five paragraphs to a detailed review of existing methods for studying microbial community assembly

comments.issue: No network module visualizations are presented in the results despite modularity being a key component.
comments.request: Add network module diagrams of core and non-core microbes at the 0.2 threshold to the supplement.
comments.quote: Although a conceptual schematic is briefly provided in Figure 1, no corresponding network visualizations are included in the results.

comments.issue: High rat mobility makes it unclear whether captured individuals reflect local site conditions.
comments.request: Justify site-level inference in the study site and sampling section.
comments.quote: given the high mobility of rats, it is unclear how one can ensure that individuals captured at a given site are primarily influenced by the local environmental conditions of that site

comments.issue: An extra period follows 'respectively' at line 155.
comments.request: Remove the extra period.
comments.quote: There is an extra period following the word “respectively”; please remove it.

comments.issue: Reference entries have missing page numbers and inconsistent title capitalization.
comments.request: Complete missing details and standardize the reference formatting.
comments.quote: Some entries are missing page numbers (e.g., refs 17 and 24), and there is inconsistency in the capitalization of article titles

comments.issue: Figure S3 lacks a scale bar.
comments.request: Add a scale bar to Figure S3.

editor_summary: Both reviewers relatively positive; editor wants the fish productivity index properly described and justified, seasonal comparability addressed, and native-speaker proofreading, plus specific line edits.

reviews.assessment: Positive and finds the study robust and relevant, with editorial suggestions to sharpen presentation.
strengths: robust and carried out with appropriate care
relevant for publication in Ecology Letters
