comments.issue: Figure 3 panels a and b are very difficult to decipher for an average ELE reader.

comments.quote: Fig. 3 a and b panel are still very difficult to decipher for an average ELE reader

comments.issue: Dissolved oxygen saturation is not a functional metric per se and responds directly to physical and chemical processes.

comments.issue: Potential drivers of asynchrony (producer biomass, consumer abundances) are neither provided nor analysed, leaving the discussion speculative.

comments.issue: Nutrient effects can go either way (increased respiration or net productivity) and both possibilities should be acknowledged.

comments.issue: L110-114 do not explain which stressors are expected to behave similarly.
comments.request: Rework the lines for clarity.
comments.quote: These lines are a bit unclear to me because they don’t explain which stressors are expected to behave similarly.

comments.issue: L186-188 should make clear that synchrony is measured within each experiment.
comments.request: Clarify this point.
comments.quote: Suggest making clear that synchrony will be measured within each experiment

comments.issue: Whether Wilcoxon p-values were corrected for multiple comparisons is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the multiple-comparison handling.
comments.quote: Were Wilcoxon test p-values by multiple comparisons? How?

comments.issue: The post-hoc tests used are not specified.
comments.request: State which post-hoc tests were used.
comments.quote: Which post-hoc tests were used?

comments.issue: L354-56 are speculative because community biomass and structure are unknown.
comments.request: Temper these statements.
comments.quote: These lines are a bit speculative. Without information on community biomass / structure is impossible to understand what happened here.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and innovative mesocosm study, but representativeness, theory-experiment linkage, design explanation and statistical choices need improvement.

comments.issue: Introduction and conclusions assume mesocosm results represent real global change situations; limitations are not discussed.
comments.request: Add a detailed discussion of representativeness limitations.
comments.quote: some of the introductory and concluding remarks take it a little too much for granted that the experimental situations are representative of a global change and can be translated to a real situation

comments.issue: The link from theoretical concepts to the experiment is implicit and left to the reader.

comments.quote: I miss a more explicit part of the paper where the leap from the theoretical to the experimental is better linked

comments.issue: Some experimental design choices are poorly explained in the materials and methods.
comments.request: Rewrite the design description to be clearer.

comments.issue: The abstract lacks the theoretical context and knowledge gap expected for a broad-audience journal.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks a paragraph on why freshwater ecosystems can contribute and what generalises.

comments.issue: Spearman correlations may not fully capture temporal effects; time-series methods are not explored.

comments.issue: Replications are not formally accounted for in the statistical analysis.

comments.issue: Why Spearman is used first while other analyses use Morlet/LLM time-series methods is unclear.

title: Experimental Evidence for the Desynchronization of Ecosystem Dynamics by Global Change

editor_summary: Three reviewers mixed: one favorable, one critical, one middle; R3's fundamental concerns about setup and model structure require substantial alteration before resubmission.

comments.issue: Framing conflates local stability of random networks with temporal invariability of community metrics.

comments.issue: Use of the equals sign in the diversity-stability phrase is unclear.

comments.issue: Central message that population structure influences community stability is not novel.

comments.issue: Text revisits foundational dynamical-systems and May stability material in excessive detail.

comments.issue: Random assignment of interaction strengths and signs oversimplifies trophic structure, trait filtering and modularity.

comments.issue: Gamma_1 is described both as same-stage interaction strength and among total population abundances.

title: Population Structure Plays a Key Role in Community Stability

study.system: Daphnia growth experiments and bioenergetic DEB model; temperature and food

editor_summary: Reviewers positive about potential but want large revisions; editor finds the model poorly described, asks for maturation to be better explained and motivated, more emphasis on results, and a section on the model's domain of applicability.

reviews.assessment: Enjoys the ideas and finds the study valuable, but the model description and presentation are extremely hard to follow.

comments.issue: Model description and parameter presentation are incomplete and extremely hard to follow.
comments.request: Revise the entire model description and parameter presentation.
comments.quote: My main suggestion for improvement is the presentation of the model and its parameters, as I found this to be extremely hard to follow.

comments.issue: Equations are not numbered and cannot be referenced.
comments.request: Number equations and reference them in the text.
comments.quote: I’m missing equation numbering (and thereby also references to relevant equations throughout the text).

comments.issue: Parameters p_um and v are missing from Table 1.
comments.request: Add these parameters to Table 1.
comments.quote: I can’t find p\_{um} and v, mentioned in the main text, in Table 1.

comments.issue: Symbols e_a and e_d clash with the mathematical constant e.
comments.request: Rename these symbols.
comments.quote: It’s confusing that symbols e\_a and e\_d are used (in the same equation as the mathematical constant e!).

comments.issue: Two different equations define q(T), and which processes they describe is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the two q(T) equations.
comments.quote: It’s confusing that there are two equations defining q(T); I’m not sure which two processes they describe?

comments.issue: The word 'steepness' is used as a variable and its value 0.6 is unjustified.
comments.request: Use a symbol and justify the 0.6 value.
comments.quote: Variable name ‘steepness’: I suggest to choose a symbol instead of using the word steepness.

comments.issue: Symbol t(T) for first adult instar duration conflicts with t for time, and 'd' is undefined.
comments.request: Use tau instead of t and define 'd'.
comments.quote: I find is confusing to use t(T) to describe the first adult instar duration, as t is typically used to represent time

comments.issue: L127 defines t(T) while the next equation defines T(t).
comments.request: Disambiguate the two definitions.
comments.quote: L127 defines t(T), whereas the next equation (L133) defines T(t). This is extremely confusing.

comments.issue: X in Table 1 is not explained.
comments.request: Define X.
comments.quote: What is X in Table 1? (likely food concentration, but this is nowhere mentioned)

comments.issue: Which parameters depend on temperature and how is unclear.
comments.request: Mark temperature-dependent parameters with (T) and explain them.
comments.quote: It is difficult to extract which parameters are a function of temperature. I suggest to make this clear by adding (T) to all these parameters.

comments.issue: Fig. 5 is unclear and never referenced in the text.
comments.request: Clarify Fig. 5 and refer to it.
comments.quote: It may also help to visualize some of the important functions. I think this is attempted in Fig. 5, but I find this figure not very clear.

comments.issue: Abstract phrase 'connecting the right dots' is unclear.
comments.request: Rewrite the abstract sentence.
comments.quote: Without having read the paper and seen the figures, the words ‘connecting the right dots’ are unclear what they refer to.

comments.issue: Introduction lacks ecological context and basic information on Daphnia.
comments.request: Add ecological context and describe Daphnia.
comments.quote: I’m missing some ecological context, relevance and information on Daphnia (it is not even mentioned in the manuscript that they are aquatic organisms).

comments.issue: Research questions and hypotheses are not stated.
comments.request: State the study's research questions and hypotheses.
comments.quote: It would help to state the research questions (and possibly hypotheses) that the study aims to answer.

comments.issue: Clutch-size data are collected but never reported or used.
comments.request: Report or explain the clutch-size data.
comments.quote: What is done with the collected data on clutch size? These results are nowhere mentioned?

comments.issue: Growth rate is not defined or its calculation described in the methods.
comments.request: Define growth rate and report its calculation.
comments.quote: How is growth rate calculated? Also, I suggest to clarify that this is about somatic growth rate, and not intrinsic population growth rate

comments.issue: The text does not indicate where the non-monotonic response is shown.
comments.request: Point to the relevant figure.
comments.quote: L177: In which figure can I see this non-monotonic response?

comments.issue: Circumstances of the shift from TSR to reverse TSR are vague.
comments.request: Specify when the shift occurs.
comments.quote: This is very vague, I suggest to specify what these circumstances are and when the shift from TSR to rev TSR does or doesn’t occur.

comments.issue: Whether model selection supports the complex four-way interaction is untested.
comments.request: Use model selection to test parsimony.
comments.quote: Did the authors use any model selection to test different models (is the model with the complex four way interaction indeed the most parsimonious?)

comments.issue: Extended table numbering appears incorrect.
comments.request: Fix the extended table references.
comments.quote: Should this be Extended Table 2 (and not 1)? Same for Extended Tables 2-3.

comments.issue: The text does not say which figure panel shows the result.
comments.request: Point to the specific panel.
comments.quote: L231: Which figure panel shows this?

comments.issue: Claims are not clearly tied to specific figures and panels.
comments.request: Refer specifically to the relevant results and panels.
comments.quote: I do not see how Fig. 3, Extended Data Fig. 2 and Extended Table 4 show this. I suggest to be more specific in refering to particular results

comments.issue: The text does not indicate where this result can be seen.
comments.request: Point to the relevant figure.
comments.quote: L249: Where can I see this?

comments.issue: Mechanisms behind treatment effects are speculated rather than decomposed with the model.
comments.request: Run a decomposition analysis replacing each model function.
comments.quote: Could the authors do a decomposition analysis, one by one replacing each of the different functions in their DEB model by different food and temperature treatments, and see through which processes TSR shifts to non-TSR?

comments.issue: Growth-rate contours in Fig. 1 are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what the contours show and their basis.
comments.quote: I don’t understand what the growth rate contours show and what they are based on

comments.issue: Squares and triangles in Fig. 2 are hard to distinguish.
comments.request: Make the symbols distinguishable.
comments.quote: It is almost impossible to distinguish between the squares and triangles. Maybe put these symbols on top of the arrows?

comments.issue: Relation between Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 and Fig. 3's added value are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify or provide an overview comparing theory and data.
comments.quote: I’m confused as to how Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 are related. While I really like Fig. 4, I’m not sure about the added value of Fig. 3

comments.issue: Figures are not readable in greyscale.
comments.request: Make figures greyscale-friendly.
comments.quote: All figures are extremely difficult to read when printed in grey scale.

comments.issue: Response types are not indicated in Figures 2-4.
comments.request: Indicate TSR/reverse-TSR outcomes on these figures.
comments.quote: Would it help to indicate the different responses (TSR, reverse TSR, not TSR) in these figures, maybe with transparent arrows or in a small subpanel next to the figures?

comments.issue: Extended tables lack coefficients showing effect strength and direction.
comments.request: Provide all coefficients in Extended Tables 2-4.
comments.quote: I recommend to also provide all coefficients to show the strength and direction of estimated effects.

reviews.assessment: Provides new insights into temperature-size responses, but the expectations and model assumptions need stronger justification.
strengths: new insights into diversity of temperature effects in previous studies

comments.issue: The expectation linking faster growth to larger mature size is not justified.
comments.request: Justify or revise the growth-size expectation.
comments.quote: why is there an expectation that faster growth rates should lead to larger body sizes (at maturity)? Isn’t it just as likely to expect this to cause a reduced age at maturity, but no change in size.

comments.issue: An optimality explanation is conflated with a mechanistic model assumption.
comments.request: Separate the ultimate explanation from the model assumption.
comments.quote: This explanation that warm conditions favor faster reproduction to mitigate higher mortality risk is an optimality (ultimate) explanation for TSR.

comments.issue: Model assumption choices lack rationale and conflict with published alternatives.
comments.request: Justify assumptions and test alternative thermal dependencies.
comments.quote: Rationale for choice of model assumptions are unclear, and not necessarily consistent with literature.

comments.issue: 6 line-level copy edits (wording and phrasing at Ln 60, 76, 109, 247, 276, 310).
comments.quote: Ln. 247: move “towards colder temperatures” to end of sentence

comments.issue: Jar volumes are not reported.
comments.request: Report the jar volumes.
comments.quote: Ln. 146: what were the volumes of the jars?

comments.issue: Jar-level non-independence is not accounted for in the statistical model.
comments.request: Use a mixed-effects model with jar as a random effect.
comments.quote: it seems like you should be running a mixed effect model with jar as random effects?

comments.issue: Extended table numbering is wrong.
comments.request: Fix the extended table numbering.
comments.quote: Ln. 226: something wrong with numbering of extended tables, I don’t think you refer to extended table 1

comments.issue: Fig. 1 is hard to understand without later context and may be unnecessary.
comments.request: Consider removing or reworking Fig. 1.
comments.quote: It is difficult to understand this figure without the context that comes later in the ms. Also, I don’t think it is required.

comments.issue: Symbols are small and the coloured background hinders readability.
comments.request: Enlarge symbols and use a white background.
comments.quote: the symbols are small and difficult to observe. This is made extra difficult by the background colour of the figures, I would do the background in white

comments.issue: Fig. 5 appears not to be referenced in the text.
comments.request: Refer to Fig. 5 or remove it.
comments.quote: Fig. 5: is this figure referred to?

title: Ectotherm Size‐ and Age‐At‐Maturity in a Warmer, Variable and Resource‐Poor World

study.system: tropical plant-frugivore networks; trait matching across 102 networks

editor_summary: Editor notes all four referees acknowledge relevance; asks for key citations on spatial trait-matching patterns, and a sensitivity analysis with better-curated data distinguishing endozoochorous from non-endozoochorous dispersal.

reviews.assessment: Clearly written, robust study with a relevant question; four main concerns on novelty framing, dataset curation, weighting and upsizing/island effects.
strengths: very relevant question with logical rationale

comments.issue: The knowledge gap is mostly formal; classic downsizing papers already imply declining trait matching.
comments.request: Reframe the novelty of the knowledge gap.
comments.quote: In that sense the knowledge gap is mostly formal/technical but not conceptual, which limits the novelty (or at least the surprising factor) of the findings.

comments.issue: The dataset mixes endozoochoric and non-endozoochoric interactions with different trait-matching rules.
comments.request: Curate the dataset to separate dispersal modes.
comments.quote: the dataset combines endozoochoric and non-endozoochoric interactions (L290), which seems problematic as the rules guiding trait-matching on both processes are potentially very different.

comments.issue: Weighting aggregated networks above observed ones may create artifacts.
comments.request: Repeat analyses on non-composite networks.
comments.quote: If the results could stand when based only on observed (i.e. non-composite) networks, it would provide important support to the patterns found.

comments.issue: Upsizing by invasive animals and island effects (e.g. Hawaii) may confound the downsizing signal.
comments.request: Check upsizing and island effects.
comments.quote: As Hawaii stands out as a point of low trait-matching, it seems worth checking the potential effect of islands driving this trend.

comments.issue: The epizoochory sentence disrupts the endozoochory flow of ideas.
comments.request: Explain or remove the epizoochory reference.
comments.quote: Epizoochory is performed by many groups, notably by mammals, so this reference to epizoochory and particularly to parrots, doesn’t seem to make much sense here, unless better explained.

comments.issue: Claims about frugivore selectivity are insufficiently supported.
comments.request: Support or soften these generalizations.
comments.quote: Maybe tone down or offer more conclusive support to the claims that "Frugivores that rely heavily on fruit tend to be more selective

comments.issue: "Novel plant trait data" is ambiguous.
comments.request: Use "original" or "new" instead.
comments.quote: "novel plant trait data" not very clear what "novel" implies in this context (evolutive?) maybe "original" or "new" is clearer.

comments.issue: The rationale linking benign conditions to frugivory degree needs strengthening.
comments.request: Strengthen the rationale for this assumption.
comments.quote: It would be good to strengthen the supporting rationale behind the assumption that "benign environmental conditions influence the average degree of frugivory".

comments.issue: Restricting to tropical networks is odd if results are generalizable to lower-frugivory regions.
comments.request: Justify the tropical restriction.
comments.quote: truncating the dataset to tropical networks based on the rationale that frugivores are more important there seems a bit odd if the results are assumed to be also generalizable to regions were the degree of frugivory is lower.

comments.issue: Disperser group representation (76% birds, 23% mammals, 1% reptiles) may be biased.
comments.request: Comment on possible disperser representation bias.
comments.quote: Please comment on whether the representation of disperser groups in the dataset (76% birds, 23% mammals, 1% reptiles) is likely representative of the natural community of dispersers or if it could represent some bias?

comments.issue: Fruit size to body mass is less intuitive than size-size or mass-mass relationships.
comments.request: Defend the chosen trait pairing.
comments.quote: Fruit mass – animal mass, or fruit size – animal size relationships would be more intuitive than fruit size – animal mass. The rationale is still valid, but it should be more clearly assumed and defended.

comments.issue: The lack of biogeographic structure is presented too briefly.
comments.request: Expand on this important message.
comments.quote: it feels like a very important message presented too swiftly. Consider expanding a bit on the details for improving clarity.

reviews.assessment: Clever, well-written global study; main concerns are the mutualism assumption and missing chemical and seed-dispersal context.
strengths: well written and easy to follow
original idea and impressive species coverage

comments.issue: All interactions are treated as mutualistic although many are antagonistic or do not disperse seeds; trait matching need not equal dispersal success.
comments.request: Discuss the mutualism assumption and dispersal outcomes.
comments.quote: Authors are addressing all interactions from their database as mutualistic, which is clearly the bias of their study since the Introduction.

comments.issue: Previous work on constraints in recording large-bodied frugivores is missing.
comments.request: Cite Vidal et al. 2013 and related work.
comments.quote: I also miss some previous work highlighting the potential constraints in recording large-bodied frugivores in fruit-frugivore networks and some of the consequences

comments.issue: Recent work on functional versus structural robustness after defaunation is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Campagnoli et al. 2025.
comments.quote: About the impacts of downsizing of frugivore communities to structural and functional integrity of seed dispersal networks, see recent article by Campagnoli et al. 2025.

comments.issue: Fruit chemistry and its link to frugivory degree are not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss fruit chemistry.
comments.quote: I miss here some words about the chemical components in fruit pulp, as there is evidence (mainly for birds) that certain micronutrients or the main chemical components of fruits

comments.issue: Source information for the Kennedy et al. 2020 dataset reference is missing.
comments.request: Complete the reference.
comments.quote: Check reference Kennedy et al. 2020,source information is missing

comments.issue: Quantitative information on non-endozoochorous interactions is missing.
comments.request: Quantify non-endozoochorous interactions.
comments.quote: "Not all recorded interactions involved endozoochory". If you can add some quantitative information here, it would be welcome.

comments.issue: Sampling completeness of the original studies is not investigated.
comments.request: Assess sampling completeness.
comments.quote: I still do not understand how so many original studies about plant-animal interaction networks are performed without investigating sampling completeness.

comments.issue: Post-2000 sampling methods may confound the human disturbance signal.
comments.request: Check the temporal-method confound.
comments.quote: More recent studies (e.g. after 2000) are more likely to employ a different set of methods to sample fruit-frugivore interactions (e.g. camera-trap data, metabarcoding) that are more likely to uncover nocturnal, rare or subtle interactions

comments.issue: Invasive surrogate dispersers are not discussed in the seed-dispersal context.
comments.request: Cite Campagnoli et al. 2025 and Pedrosa et al. 2019.
comments.quote: In that study the largest species that took part in the network of interactions and disperse at least some of the seeds is an invasive species, the wild-boar, as large-bodied native dispersers got extinct.

comments.issue: Rodents as substitute dispersers of megafaunal seeds are not cited.
comments.request: Cite Jansen et al. 2012.
comments.quote: But please see Jansen et al. 2012. Thieving rodents as substitute dispersers of megafaunal seeds.

comments.issue: A key quotation on the consequences of disperser loss is missing.
comments.request: Cite Cordeiro and Howe 2003.
comments.quote: A good quotation here about the consequences of the loss of seed dispersers is Cordeiro & Howe 2003.

reviews.assessment: Timely, comprehensive and well-written study; no major criticisms, only clarifying suggestions.

comments.issue: A conceptual diagram of how trait matching is measured would aid understanding.
comments.request: Add a conceptual trait-matching diagram.
comments.quote: I think that a conceptual diagram –as Fig. 1– depicting how trait matching is measured in this study could help the readers to better understand both the response variable and the different hypothesis and the direct and indirect effects.

comments.issue: Recent Ecology Letters papers on trait matching are overlooked.
comments.request: Cite Morán-López et al. 2025 and Huang et al. 2025.
comments.quote: The papers by Morán-López et al. 2025 and Huang et al. 2025, both in Ecology Letters, are overlooked in the Introduction, which is strange considering the topic.

comments.issue: Network weighting may disadvantage inherently low-diversity systems such as islands.
comments.request: Add a sensitivity analysis for the weighting.
comments.quote: I think this weighting deserves some sensitivity analysis, in the same way the potential temporal and spatial biases are addressed in the Supporting Information.

comments.issue: Seasonality is not included as a predictor of frugivory degree.
comments.request: Add a seasonality predictor.
comments.quote: It would be important to include a predictor variable accounting for seasonality, given that seasonality has been identified as an important driver for the latitudinal patterns of the degree of frugivory

comments.issue: Log transformation details and choice of log over log10 are not explained.
comments.request: Clarify the log transformations.
comments.quote: In the M&M I missed that the Pearson correlation coefficient was computed on the log-transformed fruit sizes and body masses.

comments.issue: Stomatochory literature is not cited at L111.
comments.request: Cite the stomatochory paper.
comments.quote: L111: Stomatochory? (https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.14501) L117-119: Recent papers compiling and relating data on frugivore movement, dispersal distances and gut retention time with body size

comments.issue: Recent papers linking movement and gut retention to body size are missing.
comments.request: Cite these movement papers.
comments.quote: L117-119: Recent papers compiling and relating data on frugivore movement, dispersal distances and gut retention time with body size

comments.issue: The L159-161 sentence is long and complex.
comments.request: Split or rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: L159-161: Long complex sentence. Please, consider splitting or rewriting.

comments.issue: Wrong verb choice at L238.
comments.request: Use "was imputed" rather than "was inferred".
comments.quote: L238: Should it be "was imputed" rather than "was inferred"?

comments.issue: Figure 2 error band is unnecessary for correlation coefficients.
comments.request: Omit the error band and note the line is illustrative.
comments.quote: Given that you are targeting correlation coefficients, not linear regressions (with intercept and slope), I think the error band could be omitted

comments.issue: Uncertainty of coefficients in Figure 3 and Figs. S2-S3 is not shown.
comments.request: Provide standard errors or confidence intervals.
comments.quote: The standard error or confidence intervals of each coefficient should be provided in the Figure or elsewhere (e.g. supplementary Table). The same for Figs. S2 and S3.

comments.issue: The reference to Figure S2 on L451 lacks context.
comments.request: Add context to the Figure S2 reference.
comments.quote: L451: Please, add some context to what do you mean/aim with "but see Figure S2"

comments.issue: It is unclear how many networks come from forest interiors.
comments.request: Provide information on forest interior networks.
comments.quote: L522: "forest interior"; I guess most networks are from forests, but some information on this would be important.

comments.issue: The saturating relationships in Fig. S1 are not discussed.
comments.request: Comment on the saturation.
comments.quote: I realize here that, actually, both relationships seem saturating, which makes sense: the slope of trait-matching is expected to be higher among smaller-sized frugivores.

comments.issue: The role of non-native species in the compiled networks is unexamined.
comments.request: Assess the role of invasive species.
comments.quote: Do they have a role on the observed trends in trait matching?

comments.issue: Frugivory and seed dispersal are not distinguished.
comments.request: Differentiate frugivory from seed dispersal.
comments.quote: It would be nice at some point to differentiate between frugivory and seed dispersal, as many frugivory interactions do not entail seed dispersal

reviews.assessment: Important, well-written study, but novelty claims overlook existing literature and methods lack transparency, requiring substantial revision.
strengths: ambitious assessment of trait matching under disturbance

comments.issue: The claim that downsizing impacts on trait matching are poorly understood is inaccurate.
comments.request: Revise the claim and acknowledge existing studies.
comments.quote: is not entirely accurate, as several studies have already addressed this topic from a macroecological perspective.

comments.issue: Trait matching pervasiveness and defaunation sensitivity are already established, so the novelty framing must be qualified.
comments.request: Qualify the novelty of the findings.
comments.quote: several high-impact studies have already established both the pervasiveness of trait matching in frugivory systems and its sensitivity to anthropogenic disturbances—particularly defaunation—at macroecological scales.

comments.issue: The introduction needs better structure, a clearer research gap and a concise novelty statement.
comments.request: Restructure the introduction.
comments.quote: it would benefit from improved structure, clearer focus on the research gap, and concise articulation of the study’s novelty.

comments.issue: The last introduction paragraph does not frame why trait matching underpins network functionality.
comments.request: Strengthen this framing and mention consequences of disruption.
comments.quote: the last paragraph would benefit from a slightly stronger framing of why trait matching is a critical mechanism underpinning network functionality and ecological resilience.

comments.issue: The introduction contains redundant statements.
comments.request: Reduce redundancy.
comments.quote: Consider reducing redundancy (e.g., reiterations of size-based matching and niche partitioning) to make room for a sharper focus on what remains unknown.

comments.issue: Hypotheses H1 and H3 lack specificity in drivers and causal logic.
comments.request: Sharpen H1 and H3.
comments.quote: H1 could benefit from explicitly stating potential drivers of variation in matching strength (e.g., ecological context or interaction asymmetry), since this sets the stage for the subsequent hypotheses.

comments.issue: The study's theoretical and applied relevance is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how results advance theory or practice.
comments.quote: I also miss an explanation on how the results might advance ecological theory or have applied relevance (e.g., conservation of functional diversity or network resilience).

comments.issue: Source-study methods, protocols and sampling effort are not described.
comments.request: Report method proportions and sampling protocols.
comments.quote: ‘Plant-frugivore network data’ section mentions that data were obtained from "direct observations" or "seeds retrieved from captured animals," but it does not specify: What proportion of networks used each method?

comments.issue: Binary networks discard interaction strength, which may bias network metrics.
comments.request: Discuss the consequences of using binary networks.
comments.quote: By discarding frequency information authors lose valuable information (e.g., interaction strength), which may bias network-level metrics and underrepresent core interactions.

comments.issue: Merging repeated samples into composite networks may obscure temporal variation and create pseudo-replication.
comments.request: Assess temporal independence before merging.
comments.quote: it may obscure temporal variation and create pseudo-replication if interactions are not temporally independent.

comments.issue: Using interaction number as a proxy for sampling effort is problematic.
comments.request: Test weighting against direct effort measures.
comments.quote: it assumes that the number of interactions is a valid proxy for effort—a premise that is problematic.

comments.issue: The discussion overreaches in linking patterns to long-term ecological and evolutionary consequences.
comments.request: Separate supported findings from speculation.
comments.quote: The discussion sometimes overreaches in linking observed patterns with long-term ecological or evolutionary consequences

comments.issue: "Trait matching strength" is not clearly defined or used consistently.
comments.request: Define it early and use consistent language.
comments.quote: Authors refers "trait matching strength" throughout, but it is not always clear what it refers to.

comments.issue: The limitations section is too long and does not pair caveats with robustness arguments.
comments.request: Condense the limitations section.
comments.quote: this section could be more concise. Suggestion: Focus the critique on the most relevant and impactful limitations and pair each caveat with a justification for why the results remain robust despite them.

comments.issue: The absence of biogeographical structure is underdeveloped.
comments.request: Discuss potential explanations.
comments.quote: Please, briefly discuss potential explanations for the lack of biogeographical signal (e.g., convergence, scale of analysis, sampling heterogeneity) and whether this was expected or not.

title: Human‐Induced Downsizing of Animal Communities Weakens Trait Matching Between Tropical Plants and Frugivores

study.system: global cereal agroecosystems; meta-analysis of sustainable management practices

editor_summary: Consider the referee comments, especially those of referees 1 and 2.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and relevant global meta-analysis; mainly asks for clarification of the environmental data extraction and for toning down one claim.
strengths: methods clearly explained and well documented
study-wise comparisons help filter out confounded effects
aggregating effect sizes into six service categories aids interpretability

comments.issue: Seminal papers on sustainable versus conventional yields are not cited.
comments.request: Cite key literature, e.g., Seufert et al. 2012.
comments.quote: some seminal papers on this topic are not cited (e.g., Seufert et al: Comparing the yields of organic and conventional agriculture, Nature, 2012)

comments.issue: Environmental raster values extracted from single pixels; no spatial buffering or averaging described.
comments.request: Explain the extraction procedure and whether buffering or averaging was applied.
comments.quote: it would be helpful if the authors explained in more detail how environmental values were extracted from raster data, particularly whether any spatial buffering or averaging was applied

comments.issue: Typical spatial extent of the included case studies is not reported.
comments.request: Summarize the typical area covered by the included studies.
comments.quote: Summarizing the typical area covered by the studies included in the meta-analysis would also add valuable context

comments.issue: Claim that results challenge the value of single practices is overstated; they confirm existing knowledge.
comments.request: Rephrase to say findings support existing knowledge, or define the challenged narrative with references.
comments.quote: these results actually confirm, rather than challenge, the widely accepted view that implementing multiple sustainable practices tends to yield better outcomes

comments.issue: Only four publications for Eastern Europe; regional findings may be unreliable or unrepresentative.
comments.request: Address whether the small regional sample undermines the findings.
comments.quote: It appears that only four publications were included for Eastern Europe. Could this limited sample size undermine the reliability or representativeness of the regional findings?

comments.issue: Intensive-management explanation is counterintuitive for Eastern Europe and it is unclear which regions it covers.
comments.request: Clarify which regions the explanation refers to and add context or citations.
comments.quote: If this explanation is meant to apply to Eastern Europe, it seems counterintuitive

comments.issue: A UN reference is missing on line 46.
comments.request: Add the UN reference.
comments.quote: Line 46, please add UN ref.

comments.issue: Three line-level wording and terminology edits (L85, L177, L302).
comments.quote: I recommend using the term “agroecosystem services” throughout the methods and results sections, instead of alternating between “ecosystem services” and “agroecosystem services.”

reviews.assessment: Values the global synthesis but finds the analysis too coarse, ignoring interactions and context, and missing a cost-benefit analysis.
strengths: fills the research gap on how many sustainable practices are needed

comments.issue: Interactive effects among practices (additive, synergistic, antagonistic) are ignored in the analysis.
comments.request: Include interactions among management practices in the analysis.
comments.quote: authors tend to evaluate how increasing number of management practices alter ecosystem service but ignore the interactive effects of different management practice

comments.issue: Effects of pooled practices (up to 7–8) vary with soil, crop and climate, but only overall response ratios are reported.
comments.request: Analyse practice subtypes and context-dependence rather than overall response ratios.
comments.quote: Authors pile together multiple management practices up to 7 or even 8, how can you reasonable evaluate their effects on different soil and environmental conditions

comments.issue: Some indicators overlap (e.g., SOC sequestration and soil fertility), so service categories are not distinct.
comments.request: Clarify or separate overlapping indicators.
comments.quote: And some of the indicator has overlap, for example, SOC sequestration and soil fertility.

comments.issue: No cost-benefit analysis of the proposed practices.
comments.request: Add cost-benefit analysis for the different proposed practices.
comments.quote: Authors need to add cost-benefit analysis under different proposed practices.

comments.issue: Low R² for Fig. 3a,b is not justified given the climate and soil predictors.
comments.request: Justify the low R² or discuss factors limiting model explanatory power.
comments.quote: The R² values reported in Fig. 3(a) and (b) appear relatively low for an international-scale study

comments.issue: Harmonization of multi-resolution climate and soil data into the 25 km map is not described.
comments.request: Describe resampling/aggregation used to harmonize the multi-resolution datasets.
comments.quote: The Materials and Methods section does not clarify how these multi-resolution datasets were harmonized

comments.issue: Abstract statement (L11-13) lacks specific meaning about the research.
comments.request: Make the abstract's message more specific.
comments.quote: L11-13 The authors need to give more specific meaning for your research.

comments.issue: Missing reference at L42-43.
comments.request: Add the reference.
comments.quote: L42-43: please add the reference.

comments.issue: Sentence at L80 is awkward and needs reorganizing.
comments.request: Reorganize the language of this sentence.
comments.quote: Today, many croplands claim to be sustainable but are they really? reorganize the language.

comments.issue: Discussion does not explain the reasons for the results or differences from other studies.

study.system: arthropods; metabolic scaling with activity, winged vs wingless

editor_summary: Editor says all three reviewers acknowledge the work's potential importance but raise concerns about hypothesis statements, literature coverage and result interpretation; better acknowledging existing literature and clarifying novelty is unavoidable, plus methodological issues; reject-and-resubmit is fair.

reviews.assessment: Ambitious and potentially important synthesis, but missing key literature, unclear temperature handling and possible unit-conversion errors raise concerns.
strengths: potentially important addition on running metabolic scaling in winged vs wingless insects
nothing currently like this in the literature

comments.issue: Metabolic rates during running increase with speed and temperature, and it is unclear how these were controlled across studies.
comments.request: Explain how speed and temperature were standardized for active and inactive data.
comments.quote: we know that metabolic rates during running increase with speed in animals and higher temperatures, and how this was controlled for by the authors is unclear

comments.issue: A recent paper finding biphasic scaling of insect flight metabolism is missed and its data should be incorporated.
comments.request: Incorporate Duell et al. 2022 data and test for biphasic scaling.
comments.quote: I would urge the authors to check to see if they find a similar biphasic pattern for the scaling of insect flight metabolic rates, as this would definitely affect their conclusions regarding support for the metabolic boundaries hypothesis.

comments.issue: The Dryad data link is not provided, so the data cannot be checked.
comments.request: Provide the Dryad link.
comments.quote: While the authors say that all data are available on Dryad, they did not provide the link

comments.issue: The paper is framed only around the metabolic boundaries hypothesis while multiple other hypotheses for metabolic scaling exist.
comments.request: Include recent work on the causes of metabolic scaling.
comments.quote: the paper is completely framed around the metabolic boundaries hypothesis, but there are multiple proximate and ultimate hypotheses related to metabolic scaling that have been put forward

comments.issue: Testing whether slopes equal 0.75 is outdated given documented clade variation and hypometric scaling models.
comments.request: Reconsider the 0.75 expectation and cite clade-variation literature.
comments.quote: This approach seems out of date, given that many authors have concluded that scaling slopes differ among clades, and since there are many models that predict hypometric scaling.

comments.issue: It is unclear what nonflight activities besides running were included.
comments.request: Clarify which nonflight activities the data cover.
comments.quote: What types of nonflight activity data other than running were used? Caterpillar crawling? Generalized motion in a respirometer? Climbing? Please make this clear.

comments.issue: Relevant vertebrate data on metabolic scaling are not mentioned.
comments.request: Include relevant vertebrate data.
comments.quote: Another general point that I would make is that there is also considerable relevant data from vertebrates that is not mentioned.

comments.issue: Wing possession is a poor proxy for flight ability, e.g. flightless beetles with elytra and brachypterous orthopteroids.
comments.request: Clarify how insects were classified relative to the hypotheses tested.
comments.quote: This raises questions about the classification of insects by wing possession relative to the hypotheses tested.

comments.issue: The first paper showing higher resting metabolic rates in flying insects is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Reinhold 1999.
comments.quote: The introduction also does not cite the first paper to provide evidence that flying insects have higher resting metabolic rates than nonflying insects

comments.issue: Using rates measured at 22C is problematic because insect metabolic rates increase with muscle temperature up to the mid 30s.
comments.request: Justify or correct the temperature selection.
comments.quote: This seems a strange choice since for most insects, both resting and active metabolic rates increase with flight muscle temperature up to at least the mid 30’s.

comments.issue: Not correcting metabolic rates for temperature variation is a mistake given strong thermal dependence.
comments.request: Correct for body or muscle temperature using established Q10 relationships.
comments.quote: Second, I think that this is a mistake, though obviously it should be done with body temperatures (or even better, locomotory muscle temperatures).

comments.issue: Oxygen consumption is not metabolic rate and should not be labelled as such.
comments.request: Call the rates oxygen consumption rates or convert to watts.
comments.quote: It is not correct to use oxygen consumption as metabolic rate; which should be in units such as watts. If you are going to use oxygen consumption rates, call them that, not metabolic rate.

comments.issue: The oxyjoule conversion is misused for CO2-to-O2 conversion, units are missing, and unknown RQ adds error.
comments.request: Recalculate conversions correctly and report units.
comments.quote: This makes no sense. You only need the oxyjoule conversion if you are trying to calculate joules/sec or watts from oxygen consumption.

comments.issue: Nonintuitive findings may reflect differences in animal condition or in the type of nonflight locomotion among clades.
comments.request: Verify that behaviours are comparable across clades.
comments.quote: Some of the findings are quite nonintuitive to me, which causes me to wonder if animal condition or type of nonflight locomotion differed among the clades studied.

comments.issue: Resting metabolic rate results are the opposite of Reinhold's and differ from McCue et al., possibly due to missing temperature corrections.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancies with prior reports.
comments.quote: It is reported here that winged insects have a lower resting metabolic level than nonwinged insects. This might be right, but it is interestingly the opposite of the Reinhold finding.

comments.issue: The x-axis masses in Figure 1 are not labelled as wet mass.
comments.request: State that masses are mg wet mass.
comments.quote: Please make it clear that the masses on the x axis are mg wet mass

comments.issue: The label at line 502 says active when it should be resting.
comments.request: Correct the label.
comments.quote: Line 502: Here “active” should be “resting” (black lines)

reviews.assessment: Interesting comparative analysis with phylogenetically informed methods, but four major concerns about interspecific scaling, curvilinearity and missing literature.
strengths: first comparison of active metabolic scaling among winged insects, wingless insects and spiders

comments.issue: Interspecific scaling analyses are confounded by taxonomic, lifestyle and methodological variation; intraspecific comparisons test the MLBH better.
comments.request: Emphasize the interspecific limitation and consider intraspecific comparisons.
comments.quote: The authors should emphasize that they have focused on interspecific rather than intraspecific metabolic scaling relationships, which may affect their conclusions.

comments.issue: An intraspecific wolf spider study found b increases with activity, contradicting the authors' spider conclusion.
comments.request: Mention this intraspecific evidence and reconcile it with the results.
comments.quote: Note that although the authors found no significant difference in b for resting and active metabolic rates based on interspecific analyses of spiders, an intraspecific study of the wolf spider did show a significant increase in b with activity, as predicted by the MLBH

comments.issue: How much activity increased during active measurements was not quantified, and it likely depends on body size.
comments.request: Quantify activity levels to test whether the MLBH prediction applies.
comments.quote: This may be because the authors did not quantify how much activity level increased during measurements of active metabolic rate, which probably depends on body size

comments.issue: Curvilinear log-log relationships may fit the wingless insect and spider data better than linear fits.
comments.request: Test curvilinear versus linear fits.
comments.quote: Did the authors test whether curvilinear log-log fits were better than linear fits? Visual inspection of the data points for wingless insects and spiders (Figure 1b, c) suggests curvilinear relationships, concave downward.

comments.issue: Traditional and phylogenetically informed regression results are not both shown.
comments.request: Present both traditional and phylogenetic analyses.
comments.quote: It would also be useful to readers if the scaling results were presented for both traditional and phylogenetically informed regression analyses.

comments.issue: Weak versus strong fliers are not compared, though the MLBH predicts weaker activity effects in weak fliers.
comments.request: Compare scaling in weak fliers such as stoneflies with strong fliers.
comments.quote: if sufficient data are available, it would also be useful to compare metabolic scaling relationships for weak fliers (e.g., stoneflies and mayflies) with those for strong fliers (e.g., dragonflies, bees, etc.)

comments.issue: The paper implies it is first to compare these groups, but Glazier 2010 already compared resting metabolic scaling.
comments.request: Acknowledge prior comparisons and explain the differences.
comments.quote: The authors should acknowledge that they are not the first to compare metabolic scaling in winged insects, wingless insects and spiders, as implied in their Introduction.

comments.issue: The type of activity considered is unspecified, and the MLBH also predicts steeper slopes below resting states.
comments.request: Specify the activity type and note the predicted U-shaped b-L relationship.
comments.quote: It would be useful to specify what kind of activity is being considered here. Do you mean behavioral (locomotory) activity?

comments.issue: Body temperature changes during activity may be a consequence rather than a driver of metabolic scaling changes.
comments.request: Discuss this alternative interpretation.
comments.quote: as pointed out by Glazier (2009a), changes in metabolic scaling during activity in ectothermic animals are probably not simply due to increases in body temperature

comments.issue: It is unclear what spiders have a lower b compared to and whether this concerns active or resting rates.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison.
comments.quote: L 36-37: Spiders have a lower b compared to what? Is this for active or resting spiders? Please clarify.

comments.issue: Recent reviews on intrinsic and extrinsic effects on metabolic scaling are not cited.
comments.request: Cite Glazier (2014, 2022), Glazier and Gjoni (2024) and related reviews.
comments.quote: recent reviews of the effects of various intrinsic and extrinsic factors on metabolic rate and its scaling with body mass include Glazier (2014, 2022) and Glazier and Gjoni (2024)

comments.issue: The MLBH allows both intrinsic and extrinsic factors to affect metabolic level and b; activity is intrinsic.
comments.request: Clarify this aspect of the hypothesis.
comments.quote: Both intrinsic (e.g., physiological and behavioral) and extrinsic (environmental) factors may affect metabolic level (L), and in turn b, according to the MLBH.

comments.issue: The sentence about Marden and Allen is awkward and should be reworded.
comments.request: Reword the sentence about maximum net force.
comments.quote: Perhaps reword “In accordance with isometric scaling of maximum metabolic rate or power predicted by the MLBH, (Marden & Allen 2002) found that maximum net force by both flying animals and many human-made motors was proportional to mass.”

comments.issue: Glazier 2010 already tested the MLBH for resting metabolic rate across spiders, wingless and winged insects.
comments.request: Acknowledge this prior test.
comments.quote: Note that Glazier (2010) tested the MLBH by comparing the elevations and slopes for resting metabolic rate of several animal taxa, including spiders, wingless insects, and winged insects

comments.issue: Glazier 2010 already showed a lower resting scaling exponent for winged versus wingless insects.
comments.request: Acknowledge this prior result.
comments.quote: Note that Glazier (2010) has already shown that the scaling exponent for resting metabolic rate (at 25o C) is significantly lower for winged versus wingless insects

comments.issue: Glazier 2010 did consider wings for resting metabolic rate, but not for active rates.
comments.request: Clarify the novelty claim accordingly.
comments.quote: Please clarify because Glazier (2010) did consider the presence/absence of wings when examining the scaling of resting metabolic rate in insects

comments.issue: Hypothesis 1 is contradicted by Glazier 2010 data and conflicts with hypothesis 3.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for hypothesis 1 and resolve the inconsistency.
comments.quote: The first hypothesis is contradicted by data analyzed in Glazier (2010). See Table 1 for b values (e.g., at 22o C, b is significantly higher in spiders than winged insects, the opposite of the authors’ hypothesis 1).

comments.issue: Glazier 2009b is cited where Glazier 2010 would be more appropriate.
comments.request: Replace the citation.
comments.quote: Why is Glazier (2009b) cited in this context? A better reference would be Glazier (2010)

comments.issue: The conclusion ignores MLBH predictions such as the inverse b-L relationship, athleticism effects and steeper intraspecific spider scaling.
comments.request: Revise the conclusion to account for these predictions.
comments.quote: This conclusion ignores that the MLBH correctly predicts that (1) b and L should be inversely related among spiders, wingless insects and winged insects

comments.issue: The L method is not described in Glazier 2005; the citation should be corrected.
comments.request: Cite Glazier (2009, 2010) instead.
comments.quote: Change “(Glazier 2005, 2009)” to “(Glazier 2009, 2010)”. The L method mentioned here is not specifically described in Glazier (2005).

comments.issue: Several line-level copy edits and citation corrections throughout.
comments.quote: L 48: Change “have” to “has” (verb for singular noun “variation”).

comments.issue: The explanation at lines 270-271 is already part of the MLBH as presented by Glazier.
comments.request: Acknowledge the prior presentation.
comments.quote: This explanation is also part of the MLBH as presented by Glazier (2005, 2010).

comments.issue: The resting spider b (0.64) is much lower than Glazier's 0.781, possibly due to larger species included.
comments.request: Explain the discrepancy with Glazier 2010.
comments.quote: The b reported for resting spiders is also significantly lower than that reported by Glazier (2010): 0.64 versus 0.781.

comments.issue: Activity increases may decline with body size in larger spiders, which could reconcile the results with the MLBH.
comments.quote: Lower increases in activity during locomotion in larger spiders may also explain why b for active metabolic rates did not exceed that for b for resting metabolic rates.

comments.issue: The MLBH predicts that taxa with lower metabolic level should have higher, not lower, b values.
comments.request: Consider this prediction direction in the interpretation.
comments.quote: Note that Glazier (2009b, 2010, 2014) has argued that species and taxa with lower L (and slower lifestyles) should have higher (not lower) b values, which is consistent with the data that he presented.

comments.issue: The finding that flying insects have lower resting metabolic rates contradicts Reinhold 1999 and needs explanation.
comments.request: Explain why the conclusions are opposite to Reinhold's.
comments.quote: It would be useful if the authors could explain why highly active flying insects have lower resting metabolic rates than less active wingless insects and spiders of similar size

comments.issue: The paragraph promises two reasons but provides none, and the anaerobic respiration possibility is unsupported.
comments.request: Reword the paragraph and support or remove the anaerobic claim.
comments.quote: The authors say there may be “two reasons” why spiders appear to have lower metabolic rates than insects of similar size, but two reasons are not provided.

comments.issue: Figure 1 lacks units for metabolic rate and body mass.
comments.request: Add axis units.
comments.quote: Figure 1: Please provide units for metabolic rate and body mass.

comments.issue: Sample sizes underlying Table 1 are not reported.
comments.request: Report sample sizes for Table 1.
comments.quote: Table 1: What were the sample sizes for these data?

title: Locomotion Reveals Contrasting Responses in Body Mass‐Scaling of Metabolic Rates Between Winged and Wingless Arthropods

study.system: soil organic matter models; eco-evolutionary optimization approaches

editor_summary: Reviewers value the synthesis but find the benefits case and classification unclear; editor asks for more Box 3 development, clearer math and a roadmap for comparing and validating approaches.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive overview, but the benefits of EEO and of the proposed classification are not convincingly argued.
strengths: comprehensive overview of EEO approaches in SOM models
incorporating eco-evolutionary dynamics into SOM models is a logical next step

comments.issue: The manuscript does not convey a compelling case for the benefits of EEO or of its framework.
comments.request: Strengthen the argument for EEO benefits with concrete examples.
comments.quote: the manuscript somehow did not convey a particularly compelling argument for the benefits of doing so, nor for the framework presented.

comments.issue: The abstract implies concrete evidence for EEO benefits that the introduction does not provide.
comments.request: Use existing examples to illustrate the theoretical benefits of EEO.
comments.quote: the abstract implies via this statement: “recent literature shows that EEO can be a powerful tool to parsimoniously paramaterize models while improving process representation”, that there is concrete evidence

comments.issue: It is unclear why the classification is needed or what it adds over other approaches.
comments.request: Explain in the Section 3 introduction why the classification is needed and its benefits.
comments.quote: The authors also present a classification for EEO, but do not clearly state why this is needed and do not articulate the benefits that arise from the classification approach taken here compared to other potential approaches.

comments.issue: Section 4 reads as a study summary rather than a comparison of results and classification.
comments.request: Rework Section 4 to deliver its stated aims and highlight the added insights.
comments.quote: However, this did not come through very well and it instead reads largely as a summary of previous studies.

reviews.assessment: Necessary and timely synthesis, but core sections need substantial revision: clearer examples, notation and comparison of approaches.
strengths: necessary and timely synthesis and framework
interesting overview of EEO for SOM decomposition

comments.issue: Approaches are not compared for validity or resolution, and no outlook is given on how to proceed.
comments.request: Compare outcomes, explain divergences and provide a roadmap for proceeding.
comments.quote: while multiple approaches are introduced, there is no discussion of their validity or a meaningful comparison of the outcomes. The authors merely note that the results may differ significantly but fail to provide any further explanation or potential resolution.

comments.issue: Function notation and parameter vector conventions are unconventional and italics are used in formulas.
comments.request: List state variables before parameters, use vector notation and avoid italics in formulas.
comments.quote: When writing functions O, B and C, I suggest listing the state variables first, followed by the parameters, e.g. B(x, u, p), since this is the convention commonly used in dynamical systems and optimization problems.

comments.issue: Example 1 does not specify its state, control and parameter variables, and the quadratic term is unexplained.
comments.request: Specify variables and parameters and explain the quadratic term x_s^2 in B.
comments.quote: Specify the state and control variables of the model, as well as the parameters.

comments.issue: The growth-rate equation omits terms such as maintenance respiration, making the formulation inconsistent.
comments.request: Clarify whether the equation represents net growth rate and include missing terms.
comments.quote: Does the eq. on line 978 represent the net growth rate? I would think that there would be additional terms, such as maintenance respiration there.

comments.issue: The proportionality symbol for k_e disagrees with the cited source and the value's maximum status is unstated.
comments.request: Use the ~ symbol for k_e and note that the value is a maximum.
comments.quote: for k_e the "\propto" symbol should be changed to "~" to agree with Calabrese et al 2022

comments.issue: The C=0 assumption in Example 2 is unjustified and the adaptable costs framework is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the cost assumptions and introduce the examples better.
comments.quote: Furthermore, I would not assume that C is equal 0 in this case, as enzymes require costs that impact growth.

comments.issue: Expressing uptake as a function of the decomposition rate is unintuitive and its assumptions are unstated.
comments.request: State the assumptions, such as substrate abundance, behind this expression.
comments.quote: Given that the objective is to maximize uptake, the direct expression of uptake as a function of the decomposition rate within B is not immediately intuitive.

comments.issue: D_{tot} is never defined and makes the notation redundant.
comments.request: Define or remove D_{tot} to simplify the notation.
comments.quote: A minor note: the use of D\_{tot} on line 991, together with B, appears redundant and unnecessary, particularly since D\_{tot} is never explicitly defined.

comments.issue: The invasion example's interaction terms, adaptable costs and benefits are unexplained and the equation appears incorrect.
comments.request: Explain how the framework applies to this system and correct the equation.
comments.quote: The authors need to provide a more explicit explanation of how their framework applies to this specific system and ensure that the equation is corrected accordingly.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'environment' is ambiguous and feedbacks are not separated from parameters and state variables.
comments.request: Clarify the environment concept and distinguish parameters from state variables.
comments.quote: This sentence, as some others seem to introduces ambiguity by implying feedbacks, without clearly distinguishing between parameters and state variables.

comments.issue: The time-period optimization section and Box 2 are unclear and under-referenced.
comments.request: Distinguish autonomous and non-autonomous systems and add supporting references.
comments.quote: The section on time period optimization (and Box 2) is not very clear. It may be helpful to distinguish between autonomous and non-autonomous systems, as parameters do not always need to be time-dependent.

comments.issue: The expression of u* on line 1031 lacks explanation and an example.
comments.request: Explain the u* expression and add an illustrative example.
comments.quote: Further explanation is also needed for the expression of u* (as a function, f) given on line 1031. This is the only part of the manuscript that lacks a proper example.

comments.issue: Box 3 does not use the same notation as Box 1.
comments.request: Harmonize Box 3 notation with Box 1.
comments.quote: In Box 3, please ensure that the same notation is used as in Box 1. This would make it easier to compare the two expressions for the enzyme production rates.

comments.issue: The expression for g omits microbial biomass in the positive term and is not compared with Calabrese et al.
comments.request: Correct the g expression and discuss it against Calabrese et al. (2022).
comments.quote: The first (positive term) should not only depend on DOM, but also on the microbial biomass.

comments.issue: Calabrese et al. results are not included in Figure 4.
comments.request: Add results from Calabrese et al. to Figure 4.
comments.quote: Additionally, please consider including the results from Calabrese et al. in Figure 4.

comments.issue: Figure 4's SOC percentage, x-axis range and apparent convergence need explanation.
comments.request: Clarify the SOC percentage, axis range and convergence of inst* and eq*.
comments.quote: In Figure 4, SOC is expressed as a percentage. Could you please clarify what this percentage represents? Why the x axis only goes to 20%?

comments.issue: The line 1096 statement is unexplained and the example is too technical and lengthy, without intuition.
comments.request: Explain the statement and present the example more concisely with intuition.
comments.quote: I think this example is too extensive and too technical. Authors also do not provide an intuition of the final result. I think the authors should rethink on how to present it more concisely.

reviews.assessment: Compelling summary, but the ecology-versus-evolution labelling is confusing and model summaries lack context.
strengths: compelling summary of the diversity of eco-evolutionary dynamic models
nicely advances the future of model integration

comments.issue: The labels 'ecology' and 'evolution' are used inconsistently because the models do not discriminate these processes.
comments.request: Clarify how ecology and evolution differ and are integrated in models.
comments.quote: My main point of confusion throughout is the explicit use of either "ecology" or "evolution" in model parameters or assumptions. To me, the models do not really discriminate between these processes

comments.issue: Model summaries give no context within the paper's framework and need restructuring.
comments.request: Restructure and tighten the model summaries to connect them to the paper's framework.
comments.quote: Further, I find the summary of the models themselves to be lacking context. The summaries presented briefly describe the model and a result of the model's assumptions or parameters, but provides no context to the overall framework of the paper.

comments.issue: The difference between individual-level trait trade-offs and community-level evolution, and what fitness means, is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify individual versus community trait trade-offs and the definition of fitness.
comments.quote: In the above section (lines 173-175), the assumption is that the community "evolves" and there is no consideration of individual taxa. However, traits trade-offs assume individual taxa parameters?

comments.issue: Alternative electron acceptors with reduced energetics are not considered.

comments.quote: I find this part pretty interesting and especially how these models may incorporate redox chemistry and electron acceptors for metabolism. Are there considerations for alternative electron acceptors with reduced energetics (Gibbs energy) and how might that scale across systems?

comments.issue: Traits relevant to microbial fitness are undefined given limited knowledge of soil microbial physiology.
comments.request: Define what functional traits can be considered fitness-relevant.
comments.quote: not sure I followed how "functional trait that is relevant both to an organism's fitness" are defined. For most soil microbes, we do not understand their physiologies, so what traits might be relevant for fitness?

comments.issue: Evolution and ecology are again conflated, including invasion framed as dispersal versus mutation.
comments.request: Differentiate ecology and evolution for trait shifts and invasion.
comments.quote: again, unclear on the differences between "evolution" and ecology here. Isn't it possible just shifts in composition impact trait values? Or is evolution being loosely applied here to refer to any changes in trait variation?

comments.issue: The minimal toy model is never related to the complex models that follow, which read as an unstructured list.
comments.request: Relate Box 3 ideas to the subsequent complex model observations.
comments.quote: It would be nice, given the inclusion of a minimal model, to relate these ideas in Box 3 to the subsequent observations in the complex models.

comments.issue: How genomic predictions map to functional groupings and at what resolution is unclear.

comments.quote: not sure how genomic predictions correspond to functional groupings. Are the authors suggesting that the genomic data guide functional clustering? What resolution will this be applied at?

comments.issue: Known limitations of soil community annotation, published as a response, are not acknowledged.

comments.quote: there are known limitations (published as a response to the cited paper) with annotating soil communities, both from a functional and taxonomic perspective that provide only a biased picture of these communities.

comments.issue: Abstract sentences about EEO models could be combined for clarity.

comments.issue: The abstract mentions model assumptions without saying what they are.

comments.issue: The introduction provides no real background on model variations.

comments.issue: The phrase 'proved successful' is vague.

comments.issue: It is unclear what kinetics refers to and how it differs from compositional changes.

comments.issue: Natural selection (evolution) and environmental selection (ecology) are mixed up.

comments.quote: lines 103-105 - mixing up natural selection (evolutionary process) and environmental selection (ecological process)

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'constraints can be lifted' means.

comments.issue: 'Scales' is again undefined.

comments.issue: Adaptation is confused with environmental filtering.

comments.issue: The Levins triangle is not explained.

comments.issue: Examples appear only in the figure rather than in the text.

comments.issue: 'EEO problem' and 'ingredients' are unexplained.

comments.issue: How enzyme production costs are weighted across functional groups is unclear.

comments.issue: No examples show how the choice would impact results.

comments.issue: 'Ecologically constrained' is ambiguous between environment and species interactions.
