title: Linking Community‐Climate Disequilibrium to Ecosystem Function

study.system: deciduous perennial plants; common-garden experiments and life-history model

editor_summary: All three reviewers see potential in the general predictive framework; revisions should integrate current literature, discuss mismatches between model and data, and outline model assumptions and future extensions.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written extension of optimal allocation theory; minor comments on model applicability and analysis choices.
strengths: enriches understanding of flowering phenology under climate change

comments.issue: The model may not suit alpine plants that keep growing after flowering and store resources underground.
comments.request: Discuss model limitations for alpine and herbaceous plants.
comments.quote: alpine plants may not be entirely suitable for this model

comments.issue: Flowering time relative to growing-season onset may be doubly affected by interannual variation.
comments.request: Consider using Julian time for the analysis.
comments.quote: would it be more reasonable to uniformly adopt Julian time (i.e., January 1st of each year as the first day) for further analysis?

comments.issue: The model may not apply to species that flower before photosynthesis begins.
comments.request: Discuss applicability to species that flower first and photosynthesize later.
comments.quote: for species that flower first and then enter rapid photosynthesis, especially those plant groups that exist only underground during the non-growing season, the model may not be applicable

comments.issue: Using a 5°C threshold to define growing-season boundaries may introduce large errors.
comments.request: Justify the temperature-threshold definition of season boundaries.
comments.quote: Is it reasonable for the authors to replace the time of the start of spring phenology and the end of autumn phenology with a consistent and stable average daily temperature above the 5°C threshold?

comments.issue: The basis for the environmental growth conditions is unsupported.
comments.request: Add references or historical data for the growth conditions.
comments.quote: What is the basis for setting environmental conditions for plant growth?

comments.issue: The recording frequency of Lythrum flowering phenology is not stated.
comments.request: State how often flowering phenology was recorded.
comments.quote: How often is the flowering phenology of Lythrum salicaria recorded?

comments.issue: Asexual bud banks may disrupt late-flowering observations.
comments.request: Explain how bud banks were handled.
comments.quote: Are asexually propagated bud banks considered when represented by a single plant? It's maybe disrupting late-flowering phenology observation.

comments.issue: Flowering phenology may have been observed for only one year.
comments.request: Clarify the number of observation years and its robustness.
comments.quote: Was the flowering phenology of the plant observed for only one year? I'm not sure if this is a robust model.

comments.issue: Figure 3's vertical axis lacks units.
comments.request: Add units to the vertical axis of Figure 3.
comments.quote: Figure 3. Adding units to the vertical axis

comments.issue: Common-garden and in situ data show different predictive trends for Lythrum.
comments.request: Explain why the Lythrum trends differ between common gardens and in situ.
comments.quote: Why do common gardens and in situ show different predictive trends in the Lythrum?

comments.issue: The claim that two experiments validated the nonlinear shape does not hold for Lythrum.
comments.request: Clarify the validation claim for Lythrum.
comments.quote: two independent common-garden experiments validated this nonlinear functional shape, but this does not seem to be the case in the Lythrum

comments.issue: Common-garden validation may not transfer to natural environments.
comments.request: Acknowledge potential bias of garden validation in natural settings.
comments.quote: they also only simulate natural environments to a certain extent and cannot fully replicate the complexity and diversity of field environments

comments.issue: Related references are missing at lines 448-450.
comments.request: Add related references.
comments.quote: Lines 448-450. Please add related references.

reviews.assessment: Positive overall; the framework is elegant, but more plant biology and annual variation in growing season length should be addressed.
strengths: good linking of phenology to life history theory
common garden data illustrate the framework's power
clear description of the underlying theory

comments.issue: Previous-season conditions and pre-formed inflorescences are not connected to the framework.
comments.request: Discuss how cross-year carry-over connects to the life-history framework.
comments.quote: conditions in the previous growing season affect the phenology in the present growing season

comments.issue: Growing season is defined only by air temperature; alternative definitions and spring ephemerals are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss other ways to define the growing season and fit of spring ephemerals.
comments.quote: can the authors say something about how growing season might be defined other than by air temperature

comments.issue: Plants cannot sense growing season length before flowering, so annual variation is unexplained.
comments.request: Discuss reliable spring cues and whether the theory explains annual variance.
comments.quote: a plant can not sense season length before starting reproduction in a given year

comments.issue: The domain of the predictions should be explicitly restricted to geographic variation among populations.
comments.request: State the restricted domain of the theory's predictions.
comments.quote: please be explicit about the domain of the life history theory predictions being restricted to geographic variation among populations

comments.issue: Mean growing season length ignores interannual variance and asymmetric costs of mistimed flowering.
comments.request: Consider metrics accounting for variance among years or asymmetric costs.
comments.quote: Instead of using the mean growing season length, how about a metric that takes into account the variance among years?

reviews.assessment: Novel and relevant approach, but model assumptions, parameterization, and positioning against contrasting empirical work need clarification.
strengths: relevant to phenology and climate change questions
applies long-term common garden data in a new mathematical context

comments.issue: The 'length of the growing season' terminology is confusing since phenology also determines season length.
comments.request: Clarify the climatological growing season definition and use consistent terminology.
comments.quote: As changes in the 'length of the growing season' in many systems is determined by the timing of leaf out though leaf senescence so the phenological schedules themselves determine the growing season length, not vice-versa

comments.issue: The model does not distinguish reproductive phases, so fitness effects of flowering-time changes are unknown.
comments.request: Test whether flowering time correlates with fruit production.
comments.quote: it would be good to know whether flowering time correlates linearly with fruit production (reproductive output) in this system?

comments.issue: The biological rationale for the inverse, accelerating f(T) function is not explained.
comments.request: Expand the mechanistic hypothesis for the f(T) parameterization.
comments.quote: biologically why would this be the case? That a longer climatic growing season would have a more rapid downturn after peak flowering?

comments.issue: The higher elpd difference for the less-curved Lythrum model seems counter-intuitive.
comments.request: Explain the elpd comparison between Lythrum and Solidago models.
comments.quote: yet the elpd difference of the linear vs nonlinear model is higher (almost 3x) for Lythrum than for Solidago. This seems counter-intuitive to me.

comments.issue: The assumption that spring onset and season length change together does not hold in all systems.
comments.request: Discuss the limits of this assumption for other systems.
comments.quote: But this is not found everywhere- globally we saw that the start of spring and autumn changed in divergent ways across tundra systems

comments.issue: It is unintuitive why a longer growing season would promote earlier flowering.
comments.request: Explain why longer seasons promote earlier flowering rather than using spring timing.
comments.quote: I'm having a hard time understanding intuitively why a longer climatic growing season length (T) would promote earlier flowering than a shorter climatic growing season

comments.issue: Published work found the opposite latitudinal pattern in thermal sensitivity.
comments.request: Discuss the discrepancy with Prevey et al. 2017.
comments.quote: Prevey and colleagues (2017) found the opposite pattern whereby species at higher latitudes had higher thermal sensitivities and thereby stronger advances in flowering times across tundra species

comments.issue: Relevant work showing tundra growing-season lengthening is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Collins et al. 2021 at line 387.
comments.quote: our results find consistent autumnal delay (and spring advancement) leading to a lengthening of the growing season in tundra systems globally

comments.issue: The assumption that population differentiation in flowering time is adaptive conflicts with other evidence.
comments.request: Discuss evidence that reproductive losses need not affect fitness (Iler et al. 2019).
comments.quote: But other experimental evidence suggests that changes in flowering time and even resulting reproductive losses do not necessarily affect fitness outcomes in a widespread perennial herb

comments.issue: Recent publications in this field are missing from the citations.
comments.request: Update citations to include recent work.
comments.quote: the citations throughout the paper should be updated to include more recent publications

title: Testing a General Theory for Optimal Flowering Time in Deciduous Perennial Plants as a Function of Growing Season Length

study.system: great tits; two-year playback experiment at nest boxes

editor_summary: Results important but major revisions needed: focus the framing on plasticity/habituation, use planned contrasts (human vs birdsong vs null) instead of overall ANOVA, correct for multiple tests, and generalize the discussion beyond great tits.

reviews.assessment: Liked the manuscript: important topic, well-designed experiment, clear results that exclude many confounds; only a few presentation requests.
strengths: important topic: mechanisms of tolerance to humans

comments.issue: Table 1 lacks estimates and p-values.
comments.request: Add estimates and p-values to Table 1.
comments.quote: I’d prefer estimates and p-values in table 1.

comments.issue: Figure S4 is informative but buried in the supplement.
comments.request: Move Figure S4 to the main text.
comments.quote: I think Figure S4 should be in the main text

comments.issue: 'Human talk' is the wrong term for the playback type.
comments.request: Use 'human speech' or 'talking humans' instead.
comments.quote: In the Supplement they refer to ‘human talk’ but I think it should be ‘human speech’ or ‘talking humans’.

reviews.assessment: States the experiment and findings neutrally and gives only minor line-level comments, plus requests for multiple-comparison correction and reliability checks.

comments.issue: The abstract phrase 'after standard disturbances in human disturbance' is awkward.
comments.request: Reword the abstract phrase, e.g. 'after the playbacks of the human disturbance'.
comments.quote: “after standard disturbances in human disturbance” is awkward

comments.issue: The scope of human disturbance is unclear: fragmentation and industrial noise are not meant, only physical stimuli of human presence.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of human disturbance in the opening paragraph.
comments.quote: make it clear to readers you are not talking about things like forest fragmentation on the one hand or traffic / industrial noise on the other hand, but rather physical stimuli of human presence.

comments.issue: Calling playback stimuli 'records' is confusing and dated.
comments.request: Use 'playback variant' or 'variant' throughout instead.
comments.quote: the authors refer to playback stimuli as “record” or “records”. I am old enough to know that a ‘record’ refers to a physical LP vinyl record.

comments.issue: Birds might respond to a bizarre, atypical sound stimulus rather than human voices per se.
comments.request: Rule this out, e.g. by comparing normal versus very low intensity human sounds.
comments.quote: Can the authors rule out the possibility that the birds were responding to a bizarre and atypical sound stimulus in the environment rather than human voices per se?

comments.issue: No inter-observer reliability estimates are provided for the video data coding.
comments.request: Calculate inter-observer reliability from the videos.
comments.quote: For the data collected via video recording, the authors have the videos and so can carry out inter-observer reliability estimates of the data coding

comments.issue: Over ten statistical comparisons for three response variables are run without multiple-comparison correction.
comments.request: Apply a correction, e.g. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, at least for the three sets of tests.
comments.quote: it seems like the authors should carry out a correction for multiple comparisons that can at least adjust for the fact they are doing over 10 statistical comparisons for three different DVs

comments.issue: Several line-level wording and grammar errors throughout the manuscript.
comments.quote: Replace “stimuli that is” with “stimuli that are”

reviews.assessment: Relevant, novel study, but results are hard to interpret, sample size is small, models too complex, and habituation evidence needs strengthening with more cautious interpretation.
strengths: relevant, novel and of broad interest
playback experiment can separate learning from selection
generally well designed, addressing important confounds
experimental evidence on tolerance remains scarce

comments.issue: The first test did not involve human voice, weakening its link to the human disturbance treatment.
comments.request: Clarify or strengthen the link between the test and the treatment.
comments.quote: in the first test, no human voice was associated with the stay-leave response during the test, weakening the link to the human disturbance treatment.

comments.issue: Tolerance increased in both human and birdsong treatments, so changes may not be specific to human stimuli.
comments.request: Address the lack of specificity to human stimuli.
comments.quote: Additionally, tolerance increased in both the human and birdsong treatments, suggesting that the observed changes might not be specific to human stimuli.

comments.issue: Remaining on the nest may reflect fear-induced freezing rather than tolerance.
comments.request: Consider this alternative interpretation of the staying response.
comments.quote: remaining in the nest may not necessarily reflect higher tolerance; it could alternatively reflect fear-induced freezing behavior.

comments.issue: The latency treatment effect is non-significant in Table 1 but significant with the Cox model in Table S2.
comments.request: Reconcile the inconsistent results between the two models.

comments.issue: Latency increased in second broods, contrary to the expectation under habituation.

comments.issue: The small sample size combined with many interactions makes parameter estimates unreliable.
comments.request: Simplify models and acknowledge the sample size limitation.
comments.quote: A related concern is the relatively small sample size, which further complicates the interpretation of the results.

comments.issue: Significance is marginal in places and results are inconsistent across behavioural metrics.

comments.quote: in some cases statistical significance is marginal, and results are not consistent across behavioral metrics

comments.issue: Figures do not show raw data points, limiting assessment of the underlying patterns.

comments.issue: Confidence intervals are inconsistently presented, missing from Figs 1 and 3 and very wide in Fig. S5.

comments.issue: Including second clutches is not justified; conditions differ and those individuals were already tested.

comments.issue: Text and Fig. S1 disagree about the number of nest boxes (50 vs 150).
comments.request: Reconcile the reported nest box number.
comments.quote: Earlier text and Fig. S1 suggest a larger number of nest boxes than 50 (150).

comments.issue: Switching treatments between years could bias tolerance estimates as previously exposed individuals enter control groups.

comments.quote: Switching treatments between years could bias tolerance estimates. Some individuals initially exposed to disturbance may appear in bird control groups later.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the playback device stayed in the nest box and when the camera was removed.

comments.issue: How captured individuals with prior negative experiences were handled analytically is not stated.

comments.quote: How were individuals captured in the study years, which had prior negative human experiences during nest checking, handled analytically?

comments.issue: Vigilance may decline across the three repeated measurements and mask treatment effects; this was not tested.

comments.quote: Did you test for differences in vigilance across the three measurements? One would expect vigilance to decline with repeated measures, potentially masking treatment effects.

comments.issue: Why and how the four-level vigilance score was reduced to binary is unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify the justification and procedure for the binary transformation.
comments.quote: Please clarify why a four-level vigilance score was reduced to a binary variable and how exactly this transformation was performed.

comments.issue: How the number of researcher visits was estimated is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether visits were accumulated before the test.
comments.quote: If your level of analysis is the flying/staying response per test, how did you estimate the number of visits? Is this the accumulate number of visits prior to the test? This needs to be clarified.

comments.issue: Laying date, linked to reproductive motivation and latency, was not included in the model.

comments.quote: I also wonder why you did not include laying date in the model. In great tits, laying date is linked to reproductive success

comments.issue: It is unclear why brood ID is needed given female ID already accounts for multiple broods.
comments.request: Clarify the random effect structure.
comments.quote: Is not female ID already controlling for multiple broods per female?

comments.issue: Small samples can make random effects look unimportant; dropping forest block may violate independence assumptions.
comments.request: Keep forest block as a random or fixed effect for valid inference.
comments.quote: Small sample size can make random effects look unimportant purely for statistical reasons. This may be the case for forest block.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether all individuals were banded.
comments.request: Clarify the banding status of individuals.
comments.quote: But all individuals were not banded, right?

comments.issue: Robustness to including second clutches has not been tested.
comments.request: Reanalyse excluding all second clutches.
comments.quote: To test robustness, consider reanalyzing the data excluding all second clutches, as already suggested.

comments.issue: The latency analysis should use a Cox proportional hazards model, which handles censoring and skew better.
comments.request: Use a Cox proportional hazards model in the main text.
comments.quote: Why not use a Cox proportional hazards model for the latency analysis in the main text (i.e. Table 1)? This method better handles censored data and the biased distribution of the data.

comments.issue: Increased tolerance in the birdsong treatment suggests general habituation rather than human-specific habituation.

comments.quote: Why is there no habituation with the number of visits in the control group? If tolerance also increased in the birdsong treatment, it suggests a general habituation, not one specific to humans.

comments.issue: Fig. S5A does not show a clear pattern.
comments.request: Improve or explain Fig. S5A.
comments.quote: Fig. S5A does not show a clear pattern to me.

comments.issue: The habituation conclusion is too strong: latency is higher in second broods and only 9 boxes were in the human treatment in 2022.

comments.quote: I would be more careful concluding so. First, fig. 3 suggests that the latency to return to the nest box after the disturbance is higher (not lower) for the second brood, which does not suggest habituation.

comments.issue: The described changes are not actually long-term changes.
comments.request: Rephrase to avoid calling these long-term changes.
comments.quote: Page 15, Line 35: These are not actually long-term changes.

comments.issue: Table 1 lacks sample sizes.
comments.request: Add sample sizes to Table 1.
comments.quote: Tables and Figures • Table 1: Please add sample sizes.

comments.quote: Fig. S1: As nest boxes are close together (even between treatments), please discuss how proximity might have affected results.

comments.request: Clarify the differences between Fig. S4C and D.
comments.quote: Fig. S4: Clarify the differences between panels C and D.

title: Behavioural Effects of Persistent Human Disturbance: A Playback Experiment in a Forest Bird

study.system: Aedes albopictus in Spain; human mobility metapopulation model

editor_summary: Editor asks to write out temperature-dependent functions, justify the extinction threshold, address detection probability, explain the sharp human-dispersal threshold and how dispersal types combine.

reviews.assessment: Timely, policy-relevant modelling study; suggests sharper policy outputs, detection sensitivity and dispersal justifications.
strengths: mechanistic modelling beyond static niche models

comments.issue: The permanent-occupancy assumption ignores imperfect detection and may overestimate persistence.

comments.issue: No out-of-sample or spatial cross-validation test of the predictions.

comments.quote: the authors might consider conducting an out-of-sample test to see how well their mechanistic predictions align with newer/out-of-sample data

comments.issue: Socio-economic factors beyond trip volume are not discussed.

comments.quote: Adding AUC, sensitivity and specificity would be better than the visual summary in fig. 2A

comments.issue: Seasonal or one-off increases in human flows could alternatively explain the data.

comments.issue: Criticisms of previous work and claimed advances are exaggerated or unjustified.

comments.issue: No limitations section despite important data, modelling and scope limitations.

comments.quote: The discussion section does not include a limitations despite important limitations to the data, modelling approach and scope of interpretations

comments.issue: Figure 2b log10 axis scale is ambiguous.

comments.issue: Repetitive sentences in Discussion paragraph 2.

comments.issue: Direct effects of root traits versus indirect effects mediated by exudates are not distinguished.
comments.request: Use a structural equation model to partition direct and indirect pathways.
comments.quote: it remains unclear how the authors distinguish the direct effects of root traits on microbial communities from their indirect effects mediated by exudates

comments.issue: 'Acquisitive roots' and 'conservative roots' are inferred from traits rather than directly measured.
comments.request: Use precise descriptions such as roots with higher/lower tissue density.
comments.quote: These terms are inferred from root traits rather than directly measured strategies. I suggest using more precise descriptions such as “roots with higher/lower tissue density”.

comments.issue: PCA interpretation and the conservation gradient need clarification; RNC loads more on the collaboration gradient.
comments.request: Discuss this and provide full PCA statistics.
comments.quote: In particular, Figure 5 suggests that RNC is more strongly correlated with the collaboration gradient. This may be due to the inclusion of additional traits in the PCA that shift the loadings of individual traits.

comments.issue: Chemical richness and functional diversity are highly correlated and likely redundant.
comments.request: Retain only one metric.
comments.quote: Chemical richness and functional diversity of root exudates appear to be strongly positively correlated, likely due to similarities in how they are calculated. Including both metrics may therefore be redundant.

comments.issue: The null effect of root diameter may reflect limited variation among the 13 species.
comments.request: Provide species-specific trait values and acknowledge the limited trait gradient.
comments.quote: Could this be due to the limited variation in root diameter among the 13 studied species?

comments.issue: Exudate-fungi associations differ from exudate-bacteria associations in Fig. S15 but are not analysed further.
comments.request: Analyse and discuss the differential influence.
comments.quote: the exudate–fungi associations appear simpler than the exudate–bacteria associations. The potential differential influence of root exudates on rhizosphere fungi versus bacteria therefore warrants deeper analysis and discussion.

comments.issue: The method used to separate rhizosphere soil from roots is not specified.
comments.request: Describe the separation method.
comments.quote: the method used to separate rhizosphere soil from roots is not specified

comments.issue: The rhizosphere-bulk soil contrast is only briefly addressed.
comments.request: Elaborate on the ecological implications of the contrast.
comments.quote: Although the authors report compositional differences in fungal and bacterial communities between rhizosphere soil and bulk soil, this aspect is only briefly addressed.

reviews.assessment: Study of interest, but the vague introduction and questionable exudate collection and trait measurement procedures raise major concerns.

comments.issue: Introduction is vague, mixes terminology and ideas, and does not discuss the implications of different strategies.
comments.request: Clarify terminology and set up the hypotheses in context.
comments.quote: The introduction of this paper is a bit too vague—there are several bits of terminology, and many different ideas discussed, but very little discussion of what the implications of different strategies might be.

comments.issue: Exudates were collected from intact fine roots, but soil sampling used different root orders, whose exudates differ; proportions across species are unknown.
comments.request: Justify or harmonise the root orders used for exudate collection.
comments.quote: But in the soil sampling parts, the authors chose different order (1-3 order) roots in this study. Root exudates of different root oder roots are quite different.

comments.issue: Root traits were measured on segments from the bearing coarse root rather than the exudation segment itself.
comments.request: Measure traits on the exudation segment.
comments.quote: the root traits were measured on additional root segments taken from the coarse root that bore the exudation segment, rather than on the exudation segment itself. This would also cause difference in the results.

comments.issue: '13 tree species' and '13 woody species' are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Use one term throughout.
comments.quote: The authurs used ‘13 tree species’ and ‘13 woody species’ in different places in this study. It would be better to keep the same.

title: Root Exudate Chemodiversity Bridges Acquisitive‐Conservative Strategy Synergy Between Roots and Rhizosphere Microbes in a Subtropical Forest

study.system: coral communities, Moorea; 19-year cover time series

editor_summary: Editor says the manuscript is below Ecology Letters standards for clarity and novelty, cannot support publication, but would reconsider a revised version addressing the reviewers' comments.

reviews.assessment: Sophisticated analysis, but results appear already well known and the paper needs substantial reframing and new analyses.

comments.issue: Complex wavelet analysis yields results that are already known or unclear.
comments.request: Simplify and demonstrate added value.
comments.quote: I have a concern that the study uses an overly-complex analysis that may be difficult to interpret for reef ecologists (the wavelets) to reveal results that are either already well-known or are unclear.

comments.issue: Needs reframing around stability/resilience and interpretable metrics.
comments.request: Reframe and add among-genera analyses.
comments.quote: (1) better highlight the importance of quantifying asynchrony for “stability” or “resilience” in the core analyses, (2) expand to include among-genera asynchrony (in addition to within)

comments.issue: No test linking asynchrony to maintenance of coral cover or diversity.
comments.request: Quantify how much cover asynchrony maintains.
comments.quote: test the relationship between asynchrony and the capacity for reefs to maintain total coral cover

comments.issue: Title's 'metapopulations' overpromises.
comments.request: Drop or justify the word.
comments.quote: when I saw ‘metapopulations’ in the title I was hoping for more in-depth analysis of how local-scale population growth and variation in connectivity interact

comments.issue: Title's claim about spatiotemporal asynchrony is not matched by the study.
comments.request: Revise the title.
comments.quote: Did the study actually address “spatiotemporal asynchrony in environmental conditions”.

comments.issue: Use 'asynchrony' consistently.
comments.request: Reword.
comments.quote: I suggest limiting the wording to “asynchrony” as opposed to “synchrony” as much as possible, especially during the introduction and discussion.

comments.issue: Claimed test of spatial portfolio effects is absent.
comments.request: Link asynchrony to stability or resilience.
comments.quote: I did not see a direct “test for spatial portfolio effects” in terms of linking asynchrony to some measure of stability or resilience.

comments.issue: Habitat-difference message is well understood.
comments.request: Play it down and quantify habitat contributions.
comments.quote: I suggest playing down the “habitats behave differently” message in the core results and abstract because the different responses among habitats (and their role in preventing total coral loss) is well understood

comments.issue: Spatial portfolio, insurance effects and response diversity are not tied together.
comments.request: Clarify their relationships.
comments.quote: the concepts of “spatial portfolios” and “insurance effects” and “response diversity” need to be tied together more effectively to give context to the study.

comments.issue: 'Species losses' and 'extirpate' are too strong and debated.
comments.request: Soften the wording.
comments.quote: The extent to which “species losses” are ubiquitous (as opposed to community reassembly/ecosystem degradation, for example) are an ongoing debate

comments.issue: Environmental stability statements are unclear.
comments.request: Reword for simplicity.
comments.quote: The “environmental stability” statements are unclear. Reefs are naturally prone to disturbance and are inherently dynamic.

comments.issue: Spatial portfolio is not defined; its relation to metapopulation concepts is unclear.
comments.request: Define and distinguish the concepts early.
comments.quote: Carefully defining the meaning of spatial portolios is critical, because it could reflect a large part of readers interpretation of the paper.

comments.issue: The coral–algal lag is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify.
comments.quote: I was unsure what was meant by the “lag” between coral and algal cover. Please clarify.

comments.issue: 'Within metapopulations' needs clarification.
comments.request: Reframe as within-species asynchrony.
comments.quote: But “within metapopulations” (L99) still needs to be clarified.

comments.issue: Section on habitat differences is hard to follow.
comments.request: Condense it.
comments.quote: I found this section on the importance of habitat differences especially difficult to follow. Can it be condensed?

comments.issue: Scale and Figure 2 statement belongs in the results.
comments.request: Reframe as a question or move it.
comments.quote: It seems strange to mention this statement on scale and Figure 2 in the introduction. Should this be more of a result, and thus reframed as a question in the introduction?

comments.issue: Variation and asynchrony may be conflated.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction.
comments.quote: Surely variation in coral population size is the same thing as population asynchrony?

comments.issue: The level of the spatial portfolio (population vs community) is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify.
comments.quote: A spatial portfolio at the population rather than the community level?

comments.issue: Non-disturbance years in the 2-4 timeframe are unaddressed.
comments.request: Clarify.
comments.quote: What about non-disturbance years? Presumably the 2-4 timeframe also includes lack of disturbance?

comments.issue: Alignment of the 5-10 year window with diurnal temperature range is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify.
comments.quote: How is the 5-10 year window more closely aligned with diurnal temperature range? Please clarify.

comments.issue: Habitats versus depths are confusing.
comments.request: Delete the depths or rename habitats.
comments.quote: Confusing as three habitats but only two depths are mentioned. Delete the depths here as they are mentioned more clearly later.

comments.issue: Duplicate 'were' at L150.
comments.request: Delete it.
comments.quote: L150. Delete the second “were”

comments.issue: 'Modulate' may be the wrong word.
comments.request: Consider rewording.
comments.quote: L202. Is “modulate” the right word?

comments.issue: 'Periods between years' is unclear.
comments.request: Reword.
comments.quote: L204. “Periods between years” ?

comments.issue: Topic sentence uses inaccessible words.
comments.request: Reword.
comments.quote: L206. Is it possible to use more accessible words in the topic sentence of this paragraph?

comments.issue: Homophyly analysis addresses a simple problem.
comments.request: Justify its necessity.
comments.quote: “Homophyly of synchrony” sounds exciting, but summarises my key point above that this could be seen to reflect a complex analysis that addresses a simple problem

comments.issue: 'Connections' is undefined with respect to Equation 1.
comments.request: Define and interpret it.
comments.quote: “Connections” needs to be defined with respect to Equation 1.

comments.issue: Wording at L266 is flagged.
comments.request: Clarify.
comments.quote: L266. “Within-shore or among-habitat heterogeneity” ?

comments.issue: Figure 2 panel labels are missing.
comments.request: Add the A-D labels.
comments.quote: Figure 2: The A-D labels are missing.

comments.issue: Figure 3 message reduces to a known pattern; the cyclone effect is unexplained.
comments.request: Simplify and explain the cyclone result.
comments.quote: all the reading about synchrony (L278 - 301) is a complex way of saying that larger portions of corals die during mass bleaching

comments.issue: Figure 4 analysis is hard to interpret.
comments.request: Break it down and present a clear subset.
comments.quote: I find this analysis very difficult to interpret.

comments.issue: Wording at L347 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify.
comments.quote: L347: “were not associated with Pocillopora cover” , do you mean synchrony in cover?

comments.issue: Among-genera asynchrony is under-addressed.
comments.request: Expand the among-genera analyses.
comments.quote: Among-genera variation in synchrony did not receive as much attention as I would have thought. Among-genera asynchrony cannot be ignored

comments.issue: The scales at L457-460 are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify.
comments.quote: What scales are being referenced here? Across all sites/habitats?

comments.issue: 'Temporal stationarity' is undefined.
comments.request: Define it.
comments.quote: L504. What is “ temporal stationarity” ?

title: Spatial Portfolios in Coral Metapopulations Are Shaped by Spatiotemporal Asynchrony in Environmental Conditions

study.system: European pollen records (109 sites); floristic diversity, Common Era

editor_summary: All reviewers see strong potential; asks to address spatial variation and overstatements, reformat to journal guidelines, and respond point by point; R1 and R3 comments are in separate files.

reviews.assessment: Valuable and ambitious, but temporal resolution, spatial overgeneralisation and the definition of abandonment need attention.
strengths: ambitious linking of palaeoecological data with historical land-use change

comments.issue: Text says diversification where the hypothesis concerns floristic diversity.
comments.quote: floristic diversity (not diversification, as stated in the text) increased with human land use prior to the Black Death

comments.issue: Rationale for using tree cover as a landscape-structure proxy is unclear; modelling logic lacks context.
comments.request: Explain the tree-cover rationale and add context for the modelling approach.
comments.quote: The rationale for focusing on tree cover as a proxy for landscape structure could be explained more clearly

comments.issue: High temporal resolution claim is undefined; actual sample spacing and samples per century unclear.
comments.request: Report sample spacing and how many samples fall within each century.
comments.quote: It’s not clear what this means in terms of actual sample spacing.

comments.issue: Continental-scale trends are not stratified by region or biome; conclusions feel overgeneralised.
comments.request: Analyse and discuss spatial variation by region, biome or cultural zone.
comments.quote: There is no stratification of results by region, biome, or cultural zone, nor any discussion of how the ecological impacts of the Black Death may have varied geographically.

comments.issue: Defining abandonment as any reduction in cereal pollen blurs partial decline and complete cessation.
comments.request: Define abandonment more narrowly, distinguishing partial decline from land-use cessation.
comments.quote: The definition of “abandonment” as any reduction in cereal pollen counts may be too broad.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-prepared study of broad interest, but organisation and pollen-record selection need major revision.

comments.issue: Organisation and content follow a Nature-portfolio style and do not meet Ecology Letters requirements.
comments.request: Reorganise and reformat the manuscript to meet Ecology Letters guidelines.
comments.quote: the organisation and content of the manuscript, probably prepared for a Nature portfolio journal, that does not meet those of Ecology Letters

comments.issue: Pollen records need more careful selection, with more samples for the period and high pollen sums.
comments.request: Increase samples for the period of interest and select records with high pollen sums.
comments.quote: a more careful examination and selection of the pollen records used that would involve increasing the number of pollen samples for the period of interest and focusing on records with relatively high pollen sums

title: Black Death Land Abandonment Drove European Diversity Losses

study.system: global tree-ring records; growth mean and variance, 1401-2010

editor_summary: Editor says Reviewer 2 raised several major issues that need thorough addressing or may prompt resubmission elsewhere; recommends resubmit only if fully addressed.

reviews.assessment: The massive dataset is impressive, but the detrending approach cannot answer the paper's question and the results contain numerous inconsistencies and errors.
strengths: original use of Taylor's power law in forestry

comments.issue: Detrending removes long-term trends, so it cannot study determinants of long-term growth variation.
comments.request: Model date and climate interactions without detrending time series.
comments.quote: Detrending methods are used to remove long-term trends in order to study the determinants of interannual growth variations. They are not the correct method for studying the determinants of long-term growth variations.

comments.issue: The method is hard to follow and ignores sources of variability such as climatic zone or species.
comments.request: Account for these variability sources with mixed-effect linear models.
comments.quote: All analyses should take into account the different sources of variability, such as the climatic zone effect or the species effect, with at least some mixed-effect linear models.

comments.issue: The Dicker-Fuller test is presented as a result rather than a method.
comments.request: Present the test in the methods and the statistic in the results.
comments.quote: the “Dicker-Fuller” test should be presented as a method and the stat as a result.

comments.issue: The caption says a pseudo R2 was calculated but gives the R2 formula.
comments.request: State which formula was used for the pseudo R2.
comments.quote: In the figure 1 caption it is indicated that the pseudo R2 has been calculated but the formula is that of the R2. What formula did you use for the pseudo R2?

comments.issue: The y-axis title 'global temperature' is inconsistent with the text 'global average temperature anomalies'.
comments.request: Make the axis title and text terminology consistent.
comments.quote: The y-axis title says “global temperature” and the text “global average temperature anomalies”.

comments.issue: The choice of 1961-1990 as the reference period is not justified.
comments.request: Explain why 1961-1990 was used as the reference period.
comments.quote: Why did you choose 1961-1990 as the reference period?

comments.issue: The claim that values 'increased significantly' is not backed by a stated statistical test.
comments.request: Report which statistical test supports this result.
comments.quote: L264: “they increased significantly” on which statistical test is this result based?

comments.issue: Pseudo R2 is mischaracterized as the percentage of variance explained; it is only a relative measure among similar models.
comments.request: Correct the interpretation of pseudo R2.
comments.quote: L 272 - 273: pseudo R2 does not give an indication of the percentage of variance explained by the model, pseudo R-squared measures are relative measures among similar models indicating how well the model explains the data.

comments.issue: AIC of the best model alone says nothing about variable relevance; comparison models are missing.
comments.request: Report AIC for the best, second-best and climate-free models.
comments.quote: A best model doesn't give any information about the relevance of the variables used, it's a measure that gives information when used relative to another model

comments.issue: The temperature relationship may be driven by the ~10% of points at high temperature, since 90% sit in a narrow low range.
comments.request: Assess the influence of these few high-temperature points on the results.
comments.quote: the temperature distribution is very uneven, with 90% of the points in a narrow, low temperature range and the relationship seeming to hold on the remaining 10%

comments.issue: Significance is treated as importance, although standardized coefficients should be used instead.
comments.request: Base claims on coefficient values rather than significance.
comments.quote: The significance of an effect does not indicate its importance. You have to rely on the values of your coefficients, since all the variables are standardized.

comments.issue: The analyses cannot attribute the temporal trend in b to a change in temperature.
comments.request: Temper the causal claim linking the temporal trend to temperature.
comments.quote: your analyses do not allow you to say that the temporal trend observed is due to a change in temperature.

comments.issue: Goodness-of-fit statistics for the Taylor model are missing.
comments.request: Report goodness-of-fit statistics for the Taylor model.
comments.quote: L290: Statistics on the goodness of fit of the Taylor model are missing.

comments.issue: Figure 2's right y-axis label and range are inconsistent with Figure 1 and the text.
comments.request: Clarify whether the axis shows temperature or anomalies and reconcile the range.
comments.quote: the y-axis on the right goes from -0.2 to 0.4. Are we really talking about “global temperature” as it is written, or about temperature anomalies?

comments.issue: The legend reports an R2 between the b coefficient and temperature but it is unclear whether it is an R2 or pseudo R2.
comments.request: Specify whether the reported statistic is R2 or pseudo R2.
comments.quote: The legend mentions that an R2 has been calculated between the b coefficient and global temperatures. Is this an R2 or a pseudo R2?

comments.issue: Calculating an R2 between averaged b and MAT is illogical because MAT was already modelled in Table 2 and was not relevant.
comments.request: Remove or justify this R2/pseudo R2 calculation.
comments.quote: I don't understand why the authors calculate an R2 or pseudo R2 between an averaged b coefficient (they've already modeled it Table 2) and MAT (previous analyses have shown that variable to be unlikelihood Table 2)

comments.issue: No plot compares model-predicted b with observed b over time.
comments.request: Plot predicted and observed averaged b on the same graph.
comments.quote: If we wanted to compare the data predicted by this model with the observed data (b calculated) over time, for example, I'd put the predicted data and the b observed averaged across all the population on the same graph

comments.issue: Differences between climate zones are tested without a linear mixed model.
comments.request: Use a linear mixed model to test differences between climate zones.
comments.quote: 296 - 298 A linear mixed model is requiered to test differences between climate zone.

reviews.assessment: Clearly written and convincing; only minor comments on wording, cautious interpretation of variability, and quantifying an end bias.

comments.issue: Calling climatic unpredictability a problem for trees is anthropocentric.
comments.request: Use a less anthropocentric formulation about more variable and unprecedented conditions.
comments.quote: I would not consider that climatic unpredictability per se is a matter for trees, unless we consider that trees are able to predict future climate and adjust their growth based on their predictions.

comments.issue: The phrase at L46 needs rephrasing.
comments.request: Rephrase 'while largely neglecting'.
comments.quote: L 46: “while largely neglecting”

comments.issue: Growth variability can reflect either low resistance or stronger responses to favourable years, and the cited studies do not directly link variability to mortality.
comments.request: Give more cautious explanations here and in the Discussion.
comments.quote: Fluctuating tree growth could mean that tree growth is little resistant to detrimental climatic variations, but also that trees could benefit more from favorable years for above average growth.

comments.issue: 'were much reduced' is repeated twice in the L109 sentence.
comments.request: Remove the repetition.
comments.quote: L 109 “were much reduced” is repeated twice in the sentence.

comments.issue: Fig. S8 shows a small increase in growth variance, so claiming the end bias does not exist is too strong.
comments.request: Quantify the end bias relative to the post-1975 increase.
comments.quote: There is a small increase in growth variance in Fig. S8, although it is much smaller than the one observed after 1975.

title: Variation in Tree Growth Increases With Global Warming

study.system: wild bee communities and honeybee colonies; virus prevalence and R0 modelling

editor_summary: Reviewers see great potential but flag critical issues: R0 calculation limitations, weak justification for Vaznull null models, and framing of key-host versus community hypotheses as competing rather than simultaneous processes.

reviews.assessment: Positive about the innovative approach and solid results; main concerns are that key-host and community hypotheses are not mutually exclusive and that site random effects are inadequate.
strengths: innovative approach of estimating R0 per species

comments.issue: Key-host and community hypotheses are treated as competing although both processes likely operate simultaneously.
comments.request: Run a combined model incorporating both processes.
comments.quote: wouldn’t it make more sense to incorporate both processes in one model, rather than considering them as competing hypotheses?

comments.issue: Site random effects are questionable given one or two samples per site; spatial structure would be better.
comments.request: Add explicit spatial structure (e.g. Gaussian Process) instead of site random effects.
comments.quote: I’m not sure that this is the most sound strategy, as all sites are sampled only once or twice

comments.issue: The abstract does not name the viruses studied.
comments.request: Mention the viruses explicitly.
comments.quote: Consider explicitly mentioning the viruses that you study

comments.issue: 'Their populations are threatened' is odd wording because population refers to one species.
comments.request: Rephrase, e.g. widespread declines in abundance and diversity.
comments.quote: L18: “their populations are threatened” sounds a little weird

comments.issue: Varroa should be capitalized and italicized as a genus name throughout.
comments.request: Fix capitalization and italics throughout.
comments.quote: varroa => Varroa? Since it is a genus name, capitalize and italicize? Check throughout manuscript

comments.issue: The very large activity radius of honeybees is not mentioned.
comments.request: Add this factor to the introduction.
comments.quote: Another important factor that you did not mention is the very large activity radius

comments.issue: No examples are given of honeybee viruses with little or no replication in wild bees.
comments.request: Give one or two examples.
comments.quote: Can you give one or two examples here of honey bee viruses that show little or no replication in wild bees?

comments.issue: The three focal viruses are not named at L80.
comments.request: Mention the three focal viruses explicitly.
comments.quote: L80: consider explicitly mentioning the three focal viruses here

comments.issue: Habitat classification, principal crops and landscape context are not described.
comments.request: Describe the landscape and classification scheme used.
comments.quote: What kind of habitat classification did you use? EUNIS or others? What were the principal crops in the fields?

comments.issue: 'Quantum GIS' is the outdated name of QGIS.
comments.request: Rename to QGIS.
comments.quote: I think that “Quantum GIS” is the old name, and the program is now simply called QGIS

comments.issue: The site sampling design across 2021 and 2022 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the number of sites per year at the section start.
comments.quote: If I’m correct, you used 16 sites in 2021 and the same 16 and an additional 16 sites in 2022? Please clarify this in the beginning of the section to avoid confusion

comments.issue: 'Nucleus colony' is not defined.
comments.request: Define it in the text.
comments.quote: Stupid question, but what is a “nucleus colony”? Please clarify in the text

comments.issue: Whether 84 colonies per site is correct is unclear.
comments.request: Verify and clarify this number.
comments.quote: Is the number of 84 colonies per site correct?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the seven transect walks per site were on the same day.
comments.request: State the timing of transect walks.
comments.quote: Were all seven transect walks per site completed on the same day or were they spread out to correct for weather events, phenology

comments.issue: It is unclear whether flower cover was a simple visual estimate.
comments.request: Describe how flower cover was measured.
comments.quote: Was flower cover measured as a simple visual estimate?

comments.issue: Botanist experience and app reliability for the vegetation survey are unclear.
comments.request: Describe the surveyor expertise and method reliability.
comments.quote: Was the vegetation survey carried out by a more or less experienced botanist? If not, how reliable is the app?

comments.issue: Using vaznull is questionable; a network-size covariate with raw metrics may be better.
comments.request: Condition on network size instead of using vaznull.
comments.quote: Wouldn’t it make more sense to, rather than using vaznull, just use a metric for network size as a covariate

comments.issue: Cross-contamination when using a net is not addressed.
comments.request: Discuss the potential for cross-contamination.
comments.quote: Is cross-contamination a potential issue when using a net?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether B. terrestris was distinguished from the B. lucorum complex.
comments.request: Clarify and use B. terrestris agg. if needed.
comments.quote: Were you able to discern B. terrestris from members of the B. lucorum complex?

comments.issue: Whether males and females were both collected is unstated.
comments.request: State the sex of collected bees.
comments.quote: Did you collect both male and female bees, or only females?

comments.issue: The formula description would be more readable as bullet points.
comments.request: Use bullet points for the formula elements.
comments.quote: I think that using bullet points, rather than a continuous text would greatly improve the readability

comments.issue: The definition and abbreviation of P*i (versus P*ij) are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the prevalence difference and abbreviation.
comments.quote: is this the difference in prevalence between both (i.e. Pi – Pj)? If so, why use P*i as abbreviation and not P*ij?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether vij should be θij.
comments.request: Check and correct the symbol.
comments.quote: L160: should vij be θij?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether βi should be βii.
comments.request: Check and correct the symbol.
comments.quote: L163: Should βi be βii?

comments.issue: Which quantity is drawn from the half-normal distribution is confusing.
comments.request: State explicitly what is drawn and how βij and Rij relate.
comments.quote: I’m suspecting that βij is the value you are drawing from the distribution, since βii is fixed per species

comments.issue: Rij clashes with the notation R0,i; an alternative symbol would be clearer.
comments.request: Rename Rij, e.g. M for Morisita index.
comments.quote: Rij is somewhat confusing as it uses the same letter as R0,i, the reproduction number. Consider substituting it for e.g. M (Morisata index)?

comments.issue: The reasoning behind the half-normal distribution with z-score-based SD is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the rationale for this distribution choice.
comments.quote: am I correct in assuming that the modelled niche overlap is drawn from a half-normal distribution with the raw (untransformed) niche overlap as mean and the SD based on the z-score of the niche overlap

comments.issue: Prevalence model description in the main text is too concise; random-effects structure is unclear.
comments.request: Add model detail and confirm the random-effects structure.
comments.quote: If the word limit allows it, please add one or two additional sentences

comments.issue: MCMC chains and iterations are not reported.
comments.request: Report the number of chains and iterations.
comments.quote: Please mention the number of chains (4?) and the number of iterations of your MCMC

comments.issue: Priors are described as non-informative but are weakly informative.
comments.request: Correct the description of the priors.
comments.quote: I’d say that your priors are not really “non-informative”, but rather “weakly informative”

comments.issue: Species names in the Appendix are not italicized.
comments.request: Italicize A. mellifera and B. lapidarius.
comments.quote: italicize A. mellifera & B. lapidarius

comments.issue: The Appendix does not stand alone; explanatory variables need more detail.
comments.request: Make the Appendix self-contained by explaining the variables.
comments.quote: the Appendix should imo be able to stand alone, without having to switch between the MS and the Appendix

comments.issue: Using host density (not +1) may yield zero exposure where primary hosts were unobserved.
comments.request: Clarify and correct the exposure calculation.
comments.quote: for the sites where the primary host was not observed (but probably present), your viral exposure would be zero, which is an underestimation

comments.issue: Temporal turnover in floral resources and mass-flowering crops could affect the results.
comments.request: Discuss whether this turnover affects the results.
comments.quote: Floral density and resource availability can have a very strong temporal turnover, especially in agricultural landscapes with mass-flowering crops

comments.issue: B. terrestris naming is inconsistent with the L139 remark.
comments.request: Use consistent naming (B. terrestris or agg.).
comments.quote: See my remark on L139: please be consistent (either B. terrestris or B. terrestris agg.)

comments.issue: Why R0 uses a single year rather than both years is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain or justify using one year.
comments.quote: Why do you calculate R0 based on the data of a single year, rather than using both years?

comments.issue: Common names are used inconsistently except for honeybees.
comments.request: Use scientific names consistently for all species.
comments.quote: Minor detail: except for honey bees, I would consistently use scientific names for the species

comments.issue: 'Floral generalist' is ambiguous; it could refer to flowers.
comments.request: Use 'polylectic species' instead.
comments.quote: instead of “floral generalist” you could say “polylectic species” to clarify that you are talking about pollinators, and not about flowers

comments.issue: Different ABPV genotypes infecting different taxa could explain the pattern.
comments.request: Consider and discuss genotype differences.
comments.quote: Could this be because of different genotypes of ABPV infecting different taxa of pollinators

comments.issue: An interaction between viral exposure and resource overlap is not tested.
comments.request: Test an interaction effect between exposure and overlap.
comments.quote: Adding an interaction effect between viral exposure and resource overlap could perhaps solve this?

comments.issue: The choice of connectance as the key network metric is not justified.
comments.request: Justify connectance and consider modularity or nestedness.
comments.quote: What was the reasoning behind specifically using connectance as the most meaningful network metric?

comments.issue: The Fig 3 colour gradient is unclear and grey tiles do not stand out.
comments.request: Improve the colour contrast.
comments.quote: the colour gradient could be more clear. In particular, the grey tiles (removed key host) do not really stand out

comments.issue: Fig S5 shows >9 instead of <9.
comments.request: Correct the symbol.
comments.quote: Fig. S5: >9 instead of <9

reviews.assessment: Very positive: praises originality and the hypothesis-driven framework, with minor suggestions on baseline virus screening, environmental persistence and a citation.
strengths: timely questions of broad ecological interest

comments.issue: Introduced honeybee colonies were not screened for viruses before deployment.
comments.request: Screen before placement or acknowledge this limitation.
comments.quote: A key concern regarding this experimental design is the absence of baseline screening for virus prevalence in the introduced honeybee colonies

comments.issue: Untested assumptions about virus persistence on flowers and bee behavioural responses could affect transmission.
comments.request: Discuss these possible mechanisms in the interpretation.
comments.quote: differences in virus persistence across floral species, and different environmental conditions across the experimental landscapes, could influence transmission dynamics in host-specific ways

comments.issue: The Mauss (1994) identification key reference is incomplete.
comments.request: Provide the full citation.
comments.quote: The reference “Mauss (1994). Identification key” appears to be incomplete. Please provide the full citation

reviews.assessment: Finds the topic interesting but is hesitant about the validity of the R0-based methods, on which two main results depend.
strengths: interesting manuscript on emerging disease spread
methods have potential in wider contexts
clear with comprehensive details and limitations

comments.issue: R0 estimation relies on transmission proxies and the unverified assumption that non-Apis species are competent hosts.
comments.request: Justify the proxies and the host-competence assumption.
comments.quote: This transmission would require non-Apis species to be competent hosts of honeybee diseases. This is something we simply don’t know if it is the case

comments.issue: Key host identification and exclusion depend on the uncertain R0 quantification, so conclusions are doubtful.
comments.request: Temper conclusions or better justify the assumptions.
comments.quote: two of the main results of the paper (identification of a key host and removal of a key host) are underpinned by this R0 quantification and these assumptions

title: Multiple Key Hosts and Network Structure Shape Viral Prevalence Across Multispecies Communities of Bees

study.system: alpine grassland CO2 enrichment; global experiments and EC-LUE model

editor_summary: Reviewers raise considerable concerns about the logical organization and presentation of the observation results and the model's modification and validation; authors should focus on the novel elevation-dependent CFE finding and its contribution to global modeling.

reviews.assessment: Timely, well-executed multi-approach study; asks to strengthen physiological mechanisms, model limitations and confounding controls.
strengths: impressive and valuable meta-analysis across eCO2 experiments
valuable overall structure and analytical scope

comments.issue: The Naqu field study does not report leaf internal CO2 measurements central to the physiological interpretation.
comments.request: Include Ci data if available, otherwise acknowledge and discuss this limitation.
comments.quote: I noticed that the Naqu field study doesn’t explicitly report measurements of Cᵢ. If these data are available (e.g., from gas exchange), including them would greatly strengthen the physiological interpretations.

comments.issue: Elevation correlates with water and nutrient availability, so the meta-analysis may not isolate eCO2 effects.
comments.request: Add moderator variables, subgroup analyses or sensitivity tests for site-level water and nutrient variation.
comments.quote: Including moderator variables, conducting subgroup analyses, or performing sensitivity tests would help demonstrate that the reported eCO₂ effects are not unduly influenced by these confounding factors.

comments.issue: TRENDY models do not integrate elevation or topography, missing pressure, lapse-rate and vegetation-structure effects; many are static.
comments.request: Note these structural constraints and contrast dynamic versus static models.
comments.quote: while most TRENDY models do simulate Cᵢ within their photosynthesis modules, they don’t integrate elevation or topography into these simulations

comments.issue: Photosynthetic acclimation (Vcmax/Jmax downregulation) and its variation across PFTs and elevation are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss acclimation and its interactions with resources and elevation.
comments.quote: I suggest the authors add some discussions about how photosynthetic acclimation to eCO₂, as reflected by downregulation of Vₐₘₐₓ and Jₐₘₐₓ, plays a role in their findings.

comments.issue: Limited sink demand at high elevation may suppress CO2-induced photosynthetic gains and is not incorporated.
comments.request: Discuss source-sink balance as a mechanism.
comments.quote: Plants at high elevation often face limited sink demand due to short growing seasons and lower resource availability, which can suppress CO₂-induced gains in photosynthesis and Ci.

comments.issue: The range of the elevational gradient across sites is not defined.
comments.request: Define the elevational gradient range.
comments.quote: P6, L121: Define what range the "elevational gradient" spans across sites.

comments.issue: The usage and units of 'elevational gradient' are not specified.
comments.request: Specify units or context such as metres above sea level.
comments.quote: P7, L131: Clarify the usage of “elevational gradient”, especially specifying units or context (e.g., meters above sea level, m a.s.l.).

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the gradient reflects climate variables or topographic effects.
comments.request: Indicate what the gradient represents.
comments.quote: P13, L253: Indicate whether this gradient reflects climate variables or topographic effects directly.

comments.issue: Whether the gradient reflects absolute altitude or derived factors is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify absolute altitude or derived factors such as lapse rates.
comments.quote: P14, L278: Specify whether the “gradient” reflects absolute altitude or derived factors (e.g., temperature lapse rates).

comments.issue: It is unclear whether root biomass includes only fine roots or all root types.
comments.request: Define what root biomass includes.
comments.quote: P15, L300: Indicate whether root biomass includes only fine roots or all root types.

comments.issue: Whether nitrogen is expressed per leaf mass or per area is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the nitrogen basis.
comments.quote: P16, L313: Clarify whether nitrogen was expressed per leaf mass or per area—important for photosynthesis scaling.

comments.issue: Whether allocation was derived from destructive sampling or modeling is not stated.
comments.request: Specify the source of the allocation data.
comments.quote: P16, L314: It might be helpful to specify whether this allocation was derived from destructive sampling or modeling.

comments.issue: The elevation ranges of the sites are not provided.
comments.request: Provide elevation ranges to frame representativeness.
comments.quote: P16, L324: Provide the elevation ranges for these sites to frame their representativeness.

comments.issue: How elevation was represented in the models is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how elevation enters the models.
comments.quote: P17, L343: Clarify how elevation was represented in the models (e.g., input climate, site metadata).

comments.issue: Whether a quantity is observed or inferred from trait models or measurements is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the source of this quantity.
comments.quote: P20, L397: Clarify whether this is observed or inferred from trait models or field measurements.

comments.issue: Whether leaf nitrogen status was measured or inferred is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how leaf nitrogen status was obtained.
comments.quote: P24, L482: Explain if the “leaf nitrogen status” was measured or inferred from physiological traits.

reviews.assessment: Clearly written and well structured; asks for stronger focus, seasonality framing, and clearer data descriptions.

comments.issue: Seasonality and its impact on ecosystem processes appear in figures but are not introduced.
comments.request: Introduce seasonality in the introduction.
comments.quote: I have not read anything about how seasonality impact ecosystem processes (e.g. CO2 exchange) in the introduction that I read in the figures (June, July, August).

comments.issue: Lines 117-121 and 124-127 overlap and could be merged.
comments.request: Merge the overlapping passages.
comments.quote: For me, line 117-121 and line 124-127 sort of overlap each other. Maybe this could be merged to reduced?

comments.issue: The section 2.6 description is too brief to understand how the data were obtained.
comments.request: Expand the description of how data were obtained.
comments.quote: Line 250, 2.6, I think the description could be more in depth. I was not able to understand how the data are obtained after reading the text twice.

comments.issue: Seasonality should be introduced before section 4.2.
comments.request: Introduce seasonality earlier.
comments.quote: Line 366 4.2 how seasonality impact ecosystem processes (e.g. CO2 exchange) should be introduced first.

comments.issue: Lines 417-421 repeat material already presented in the introduction.
comments.request: Delete the repetition.
comments.quote: Line 417-421, repeated, these have been presented in introduction. Delete here?

comments.issue: The link between lines 433-437 and stronger CFE at high elevation is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the link to the main result.
comments.quote: Line 433-437, I do not know how these sentences linked to Stronger CFE on ecosystem photosynthesis in the high elevation

comments.issue: The passage at lines 481-431 seems inessential to the study's main purpose.
comments.request: Consider removing or refocusing this passage.
comments.quote: Line 481-431not sure how essential is this to this study.

reviews.assessment: Interesting question and informative three-pronged approach, but global importance is unclear, the synthesis may be underpowered and presentation needs work.
strengths: interesting question about elevated CO2 and high elevation ecosystems

comments.issue: The field experiment does not explicitly compare different elevations, so it only partly addresses the overarching question.
comments.request: Acknowledge this design limitation.
comments.quote: Of the three approaches, the experiment doesn’t explicitly compare different elevations to address the overarching question

comments.issue: The global importance of elevation-dependent CFE variation is not established.
comments.request: Clarify the global relevance of the elevation effect.
comments.quote: More generally, it was not clear how important variation in CFE with elevation actually is in a global context.

comments.issue: The claim that alpine biomes cover more than 30% of global terrestrial area lacks support and overstates their prevalence.
comments.request: Clarify and provide stronger support for the 30% figure.
comments.quote: I can’t find where the figure of 30% terrestrial cover for alpine biomes would come from, so this needs clarification and stronger support.

comments.issue: The wider context and overall importance of the work need clarifying, and the arguments about prior CFE work are inconsistent.
comments.request: Develop the context in the introduction and place results in it in the discussion.
comments.quote: As mentioned above, the wider context of this work and overall importance needs clarifying

comments.issue: Widespread unnecessary acronyms (e.g. AGB, ST, SWC) and brief context make the paper hard to follow.
comments.request: Review acronyms and use only necessary ones.
comments.quote: I found the manuscript at times difficult to follow. In part, this is a result of the relatively brief set up of the wider context (see previous point), but also the widespread use of acronyms in the results and discussion.

comments.issue: The synthesis rests on 10 experiments and elevation effects are driven by only two high-elevation sites.
comments.request: Assess robustness or use a qualitative comparison of the most relevant grassland sites.
comments.quote: elevation effects are essentially driven by just the two high elevation sites. Given this, is this analysis sufficiently robust

comments.issue: The abstract could better explain the different approaches taken.
comments.request: Use the structure/phrasing from the end of the introduction in the abstract.
comments.quote: The abstract could better explain the different approaches taken, perhaps using the structure/phrasing used at end of introduction (lines 113-124).

comments.issue: It is not stated that the control is also an OTC with the same setup minus CO2.
comments.request: State the control setup explicitly.
comments.quote: Section 2.2 (methods) – make it clear that the control is also an OTC with same setup minus CO2.

comments.issue: Whether the experiments are separate but at the same study site is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the relationship between experiments and site.
comments.quote: Lines 154-156: I assume these are separate experiments but based on the same study site?

comments.issue: The number of data points extracted per experiment is not stated.
comments.request: State whether one or multiple data points are extracted per experiment.
comments.quote: Lines 219-229: How many data points are extracted from each experiment? Is it one data point per experiment or multiple?

comments.issue: Statistical methods are not explicitly linked to the relevant study parts, and lines 277-279 are too brief.
comments.request: Link statistics to each study part and specify the drivers tested.
comments.quote: Statistical methods could be more explicitly linked to the relevant part of the study

title: Stronger Sensitivity of Plant Photosynthesis to Rising CO 2 in High Elevation Ecosystems

study.system: annual plant Erythranthe laciniata; elevational common gardens

editor_summary: Editor notes all reviewers found the topic of broad interest but the manuscript is not publishable: elevation confounds, missing methods and statistical support, and exclusion of non-flowering blocks bias conclusions; reject with option to resubmit.

reviews.assessment: Impressive provenance test with solid evidence for disequilibrium, but several major clarifications and figure improvements are needed.
strengths: impressive provenance test design across an elevation range
clear implications for plant responses to climate change

comments.issue: The introductory paragraph flows awkwardly and is poorly structured.
comments.request: Delete the Clausen, Keck and Heisey sentences and move the final sentence.
comments.quote: This paragraph flows very awkwardly. I recommend deleting the first two sentences about Clausen, Keck and Heisey

comments.issue: The prediction about adaptive differentiation is not specific enough to test.
comments.request: Clarify what would count as evidence for greater adaptive differentiation.
comments.quote: Please clarify this prediction- what specifically would be evidence for greater adaptive differentiation? A greater relative fitness advantage to the home population?

comments.issue: The first sentence of a paragraph is incomplete.
comments.request: Complete the sentence, e.g. 'common gardens were established'.
comments.quote: First sentence of the paragraph is incomplete- should be “common gardens were established “

comments.issue: It is never stated whether the statistical analyses used 2009, 2021 or both years of data.
comments.request: Clarify and justify which years each analysis uses.
comments.quote: throughout this section, it is never stated whether these analyses were performed on the 2009 data, the 2021 data, or both. Please clarify and justify this!

comments.issue: It should be explicit that lifetime fitness includes survival and fecundity with zeros for non-survivors.
comments.request: State that flower counts include zeros for non-survivors.
comments.quote: Please be clear that flower counts do include zeros for non-survivors, so “lifetime fitness” includes both survival and fecundity components.

comments.issue: The estimation of survival and its components is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how survival was estimated, including emergence and survival to reproduction.
comments.quote: Please explain at the end of the paragraph above how you estimated survival. Does it include both emergence and survival to reproduction?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether a procedure was applied to both years.
comments.request: State whether this was done for both years.
comments.quote: P. 6, l 19: Was this done for both years?

comments.issue: The calculation of climate distances and choice of BIOCLIM factors are not explained or justified.
comments.request: Describe climate distance calculation and justify the BIOCLIM factors.
comments.quote: More information is needed about the calculation of climate distances and the justification for the BIOCLIM factors used.

comments.issue: Absolute climate transfer distances lose direction, and the elevation-fitness relationship may be nonlinear.
comments.request: Analyse signed elevational transfer distance and test a polynomial term.
comments.quote: Might be interesting to also do a simpler analysis with elevational transfer distance (negative or positive). If power permits, it would be good to include a polynomial term to look for an “optimal” elevation of origin for each site.

comments.issue: It is unclear why some analyses use both years while others use only 2009.
comments.request: Explain and strongly justify the choice of years per analysis.
comments.quote: I was confused throughout as to why some of the analyses used data from both years, and others only from 2009.

comments.issue: Figure references in the text appear to mismatch the actual figures.
comments.request: Correct the figure references throughout.
comments.quote: Also I was very confused by apparent mismatches between the figure references in the text and the actual figures.

comments.issue: Survival values are reported in text where a figure would be clearer.
comments.request: Present survival values as a figure, e.g. extra panels in Figure 3.
comments.quote: The survival values given in the text are cumbersome to read. They should be given in a figure, perhaps additional panels in figure 3

comments.issue: Figure 3 does not show populations, interaction effects or survival as claimed.
comments.request: Overlay population reaction norms on Figure 3 and check the figure reference.
comments.quote: Figure 3 does not illustrate populations or population interaction effects, and does not show survival.

comments.issue: Error bars are not defined in any figure.
comments.request: State what the error bars represent in all figures.
comments.quote: Also please state what the error bars represent in all figures.

comments.issue: Population may be better modelled as continuous elevation of origin.
comments.request: Test elevation of origin as a continuous variable.
comments.quote: What happens if you include elevation of origin in the model as a continuous variable instead of population?

comments.issue: Significant interactions do not by themselves indicate adaptive genetic variation.
comments.request: Show that interaction effects are in the predicted direction.
