comments.quote: Does this part of GDUM carry the same assumption as GDM—that “dissimilarity between site-pairs increases monotonically from 0 to 1” with environmental distance?

comments.issue: λ is fixed across sites although environmental effects likely vary (e.g. non-linear temperature effects).
comments.request: Handle or mention site-varying λ.
comments.quote: λ is fixed across sites, but in reality, the effect of environmental variables can vary across sites.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether users can add random slopes so each site has its own slope instead of a constant λ.
comments.request: Support random slopes and explain their benefits.
comments.quote: Can users also add random slope into GDUM – something like (Temperature | Site) (lmer syntax)?

comments.issue: 'Average dissimilarity' wording misdescribes what vi and vj capture.
comments.request: Reword this passage.
comments.quote: “Average dissimilarity” sounds like just calculating average across observed dissimilarity across all pairs for each site, which is not what vi and vj capture?

comments.issue: Whether the relationship holds when random slopes are added is unclear.
comments.request: Check and explain this case.
comments.quote: I am just wondering what would happen if users add random slope to the model? does the relationship still holds?

comments.issue: Run time and parallel-computing support are not reported.
comments.request: Report run time and parallel options.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful to add a sentence here indicating how much time is required to run the analysis

comments.issue: The beta distribution cannot handle zeros and ones.
comments.request: Note the zero/one limitation.
comments.quote: I would note that beta distribution can’t handle one and zero, although there are ways to transform the data.

comments.issue: Specific coverage numbers (50% vs 80%+) would better highlight the approach's power.
comments.request: Add these numbers at L197.
comments.quote: I think it’s good to highlight some numbers here instead of just saying “higher” and “lower”

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the contributions of the dissimilarity gradient and direct effect can be quantified directly (e.g. variance partitioning).
comments.request: Mention variance/hierarchical partitioning as a possible extension.
comments.quote: I am just wondering if there are ways to directly quantify the contributions of the dissimilarity gradient and the direct effect only to the observed pairwise dissimilarity matrix.

comments.issue: Tsang et al. (2023) is misrepresented as 'a dissimilarity model' rather than per-site models.
comments.request: Reword to 'fitting dissimilarity models for each site separately'.
comments.quote: I feel like the approach in Tsang et al. (2023) is misrepresented here (I am the author of the paper).

comments.issue: Tsang et al. (2023) can handle non-linear change and was not designed to disentangle directional change, so the comparison should be fairer.
comments.request: Revise the characterization of Tsang et al. 2023.
comments.quote: I think Tsang et al. (2023) should be able to handle non-linear community change because the dissimilarity models are built using GAMMs

comments.issue: A sentence on forecasting beta-diversity change under human activities would be valuable.
comments.request: Add this forecasting point to the discussion.
comments.quote: I would suggest adding a sentence or two about how GDUM not only helps us understand the drivers of beta diversity, but also can aid in forecasting changes in beta diversity due to human activities

comments.issue: Terminology across figures and introduction is inconsistent (dissimilarity gradient only vs directional effect).
comments.request: Use consistent wording.
comments.quote: Again I am unsure whether dissimilarity gradient only is equivalent to “directional effect” in the introduction, while “direct effect only” is equivalent to “non-directional effect”.

comments.issue: Figure 3C subpanel order differs from 3A/3B; title should be 'Conventional uniqueness model'.
comments.request: Fix the order and title.
comments.quote: The subpanel order in Fig. 3C is different from that in Figs. 3A and 3B.

comments.issue: Case-study code should be included as package vignettes.
comments.request: Add the case studies as vignettes.
comments.quote: I think it would be great to include the code for the two case studies as vignettes in the package.

title: Accounting for the Influence of Community Turnover Along Environmental Gradients on Compositional Uniqueness

study.system: trophically transmitted helminth parasites; 207 studies, 1635 observations

editor_summary: Editor notes referees liked the study and that it is the largest meta-analysis of parasite manipulation to date, but asks to address requests for a whole-life-cycle category, statistical modelling, and phylogeny topology concerns.

reviews.assessment: Comprehensive and adequately analysed, but the patterns are already known and novelty is limited.

comments.issue: Reported patterns were already known and obvious; no new or surprising pattern emerges.
comments.quote: My feeling is that practically all the patterns reported were known to me, and really pretty obvious to anyone who has been following the literature on this topic.

comments.issue: Host-type categorisation ignores integrative life-cycle classes that may better explain manipulation.
comments.request: Test life-cycle classes based on intermediate-to-definitive host links.
comments.quote: perhaps categorising the observations based on a more integrative view of the life cycle would be preferable

comments.issue: Writing needs proof-reading and polishing (e.g. lines 49, 53).
comments.quote: The writing would need proof-reading and polishing in several places, e.g. line 49, “transmission to its final host” and not “of its final host”; line 53, “a trait” and not “a traits”; etc.

comments.issue: Scope reminder (trophically transmitted parasites only) should appear at the end of the Introduction.
comments.request: Mention this scope at the end of the Introduction.
comments.quote: maybe remind the reader that these include only trophically transmitted parasites

comments.issue: Results text is crowded with parenthetical numbers and hard to read.
comments.request: Lighten the text and avoid repeating numbers already in tables.
comments.quote: The Results text is crowded with parentheses filled with numbers and is a little challenging to read.

comments.issue: Trends are reported even when HPD ranges overlap zero.
comments.request: Avoid calling such patterns trends or flag their uncertainty.
comments.quote: In several places in the Results, trends are reported, followed by an admission that their high posterior density range overlaps zero.

comments.issue: Absence of a temporal decline is called contrary to Poulin (2000) although it is expected.
comments.request: Reframe the comparison with the earlier study.
comments.quote: it is clear from his figures (and from common sense) that effect sizes could not go on to decrease forever

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and suitable models, but interpretation exceeds the strength of evidence.
strengths: impressive analytical scope and dataset breadth
valuable synthesis of behavioural effect sizes

comments.issue: Abstract and discussion statements extrapolate beyond the statistical results.
comments.request: Rephrase conclusions to reflect the limits of variance partitioning.
comments.quote: The models detect limited phylogenetic signal, but this does not exclude correlated evolutionary constraints or data imbalance.

comments.issue: Stage and co-infection contrasts are correlational but described causally; immature HPDs overlap zero.
comments.request: Use conditional phrasing instead of causal verbs.
comments.quote: The contrast between mature and immature parasite stages is central but remains correlational. HPD intervals for immature parasites fully overlap zero, and co-infection effects are interpreted causally without experimental evidence.

comments.issue: Publication-bias conclusions rest only on standard-error covariates; diagnostics missing.
comments.request: Add a funnel plot or posterior predictive check and report Egger estimates.
comments.quote: Strong statements on publication bias rely solely on model covariates (standard error effects). A graphical diagnostic (e.g., funnel plot) or posterior predictive check should be included.

comments.issue: No full model diagnostics (R-hat, ESS, pareto k, pp_check) are reported.
comments.request: Include model diagnostics and pp_check graphs as supplementary material.
comments.quote: The manuscript refers to brms models with priors and settings but does not provide full diagnostic summaries.

comments.issue: Avian systems are overrepresented; stronger bird manipulation may reflect sampling imbalance.
comments.request: Discuss sampling imbalance and alternative explanations.
comments.quote: The dataset is unevenly distributed across host groups, with avian systems overrepresented.

comments.issue: Predation terms alternate and Cohen's d standardisation and effect direction are undefined.
comments.request: Standardise terminology and define effect-direction metrics.
comments.quote: The manuscript alternates between “predation susceptibility”, “predation risk”, “predation enhancement”, and “predation suppression”.

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits: duplicated word, unclosed parenthesis, wrong verb form.
comments.quote: Line 166: Parenthesis unclosed after “Egger’s regression”; fix punctuation.

comments.issue: HPD and ΔELPD are not defined at first mention.
comments.request: Define both abbreviations at first mention in the methods.
comments.quote: Define HPD and ΔELPD at first mention in the methods.

comments.issue: Axis label and PRISMA diagram fonts are too small.
comments.request: Increase font size in figures.
comments.quote: Figures: Increase font size for axis labels and in the PRISMA diagram.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and clearly presented study, with comments to improve scope and statistical clarity.

comments.issue: Helminth-only scope appears in the abstract but not the title.
comments.request: Add the helminth scope to the title.
comments.quote: While this is mentioned in the abstract, it should also be clearly stated in the title.

comments.issue: Exclusion of other parasite taxa such as Toxoplasma is not justified.
comments.request: Justify exclusions or expand the scope.
comments.quote: it is unclear why other parasites such as Toxoplasma were excluded from the analysis. If it was intentionally omitted, a brief justification should be provided.

comments.issue: Unusual Pancrustacea topology (hexapods inside crustaceans) may have influenced results.
comments.request: Check the phylogeny topology and its influence on the results.
comments.quote: I am wondering whether this structure may have influenced the results of the meta-analysis.

comments.issue: Statistical values and 95% CIs are repeated in the text despite being in tables.
comments.request: Remove repeated statistics from the main text.
comments.quote: Please avoid repeating statistical values and 95% confidence intervals in the main text when they are already presented in tables.

comments.issue: Link between SE and publication bias is not explained for non-specialists.
comments.request: Briefly explain why SE indicates publication bias.
comments.quote: The link between SE and publication bias is not immediately clear. A brief explanation or clarification would be helpful here to guide readers less familiar with meta-analytical methods.

comments.issue: Weak immature-stage effect appears to contradict Parker et al. (2009).
comments.request: Briefly discuss the discrepancy.
comments.quote: The observed weak effect in immature host stages seems to contradict the prediction by Parker et al. (2009)

comments.issue: Evidence for a correct vs dead-end predator difference is weak.
comments.request: Remove or soften the sentence.
comments.quote: The evidence supporting a difference between correct and dead-end predators is weak. I suggest removing or softening this sentence to better reflect the strength of the data.

comments.issue: Sentence at lines 372-373 is unclear and needs rewording.
comments.request: Rephrase for clarity and fluency.
comments.quote: This sentence is a bit unclear and would benefit from rewording. Consider rephrasing for clarity and fluency.

title: The Evolution and Ecology of Host Manipulation in Helminth Parasites: A Phylogenetic Meta‐Analysis

study.system: fishes (freshwater, marine, brackish); 3000+ heat tolerance records

editor_summary: Editor's chief concern: variability was measured as spatial CV of weekly means across species ranges rather than temporal fluctuations, mismatching the hypotheses; hypothesis-testing framework also weak.

reviews.assessment: Very positive; well written, concise and digestible, with only minor edits and clarifications suggested.

comments.issue: Four line-level copy edits (commas and a figure citation format).
comments.quote: Page 9, line 49: “(S4)” should be “(Fig S4)”

comments.issue: Fig. 1 lacks symbology showing which groups differ statistically.
comments.request: Add symbology for statistical differences in panels A and C.
comments.quote: It would be helpful to have symbology indicating which groups are statistically different from one another for panels A and C.

comments.issue: Panel letters are small and their placement is distracting.
comments.request: Enlarge, bold and reposition the panel letters.
comments.quote: the panel letters are kind of small and their placement is a little distracting. I suggest making them slightly larger (and maybe bold) and move them further into their respective corners

comments.issue: Multiple levels of standardization make the Fig. S5 ARR values hard to interpret.
comments.request: Clarify how ARR at habitat temperature is calculated versus standardized ARR.
comments.quote: I think I am confused because there are multiple levels of standardization happening here

comments.issue: Text says ARR values lower at habitat temperature, but Fig. S5 appears to show increases.
comments.request: Reconcile and edit the results text.
comments.quote: The text states that ARR values “lower” when ARR is plotted at habitat temperature

comments.issue: Higher plasticity at low latitudes could be an experimental effect of acclimating fish to high temperatures.
comments.request: Consider and discuss this experimental explanation.
comments.quote: So, could the higher plasticity shown at lower latitudes in Fig. S5 be an experimental effect?

comments.issue: The sentence starting 'Full capacity' belongs with the introduction of Fig. 5 in the results.
comments.request: Move the sentence to the results.
comments.quote: The sentence that starts with “Full capacity” would be useful to have in the results section when introducing Fig. 5.

comments.issue: Alternative explanation: marine fish can move to cooler areas whereas freshwater fish must acclimate.
comments.request: Consider this movement-based alternative explanation.
comments.quote: It could be that marine fish are more often able to cope with warm temperatures by moving to a new area, while freshwater species more often need to acclimate because they have nowhere to go

comments.issue: Rubalcaba et al. 2020 may be the wrong reference for exponential metabolic scaling.
comments.request: Cite Fry 1947 or related work instead.
comments.quote: I’m not sure this is Rubalcaba et al., 2020 is the proper reference here.

comments.issue: The phrase 'a difference of say 2 degrees' reads awkwardly.
comments.request: Reword the sentence and add an example reference.
comments.quote: “a difference of say 2 degrees” reads awkwardly. Could re-word this sentence to something like

comments.issue: Only 35 references, 9 of them by the first author (a 26% self-citation rate).
comments.request: Credit more background work where space allows.
comments.quote: As is, there are only 35 references listed in this paper and the first author of this manuscript is an author on 9 of them. This is a 26% self-citation rate.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and promising ideas, but temperature data comparability and the analytical framework raise substantial concerns.
strengths: promising approach focusing on fishes from both realms

comments.issue: Parts of the Methods are inadequately described, so the analyses cannot be fully understood.
comments.request: Describe the methods adequately.
comments.quote: some portions of the Methods are not adequately described and so I haven’t been able to fully comprehend what had been done and why

comments.issue: Thermal exposure is characterised across the species range rather than where individuals were captured, skipping population-level processes.
comments.request: Use maximum temperature and variability where individuals were captured.
comments.quote: Why not using the thermal maximum and variability where the individuals were captured?

comments.issue: The hypothesis concerns temporal thermal variability experienced by organisms, but spatial variability across ranges was measured.
comments.request: Align the variability metric with temporal fluctuations experienced.
comments.quote: for me this relates to the temporal thermal variability experienced by the organisms, not the spatial variability across their range

comments.issue: Temperature data differ between realms (weekly versus monthly, different spans and likely resolutions), questioning comparability.
comments.request: Harmonise datasets in temporal and spatial resolution.
comments.quote: using weekly temperature data for freshwater fish and monthly temperature data for marine fish over different time spans, I wonder whether these values, maximum temperatures and variability, can be directly compared

comments.issue: Results are difficult to interpret because acclimation temperature is not adjusted for as study duration was.
comments.request: Adjust for acclimation temperature using the same modelling approach.
comments.quote: why not using the same approach for the temperature of acclimatation (e.g., 10.1073/pnas.1316145111; 10.1038/nclimate3382)?

comments.issue: It is unclear which analysis or interaction term tests which hypothesis.
comments.request: Provide a clearer conceptual framework and clarify hypothesis-to-analysis mapping.
comments.quote: providing a clearer conceptual framework and clarifying which analysis (or component of the analysis such as the interaction between Tacc and Thab) allows to test which hypothesis

comments.issue: The warming tolerance comparison is not insightful, does not relate to the hypotheses and the dependence is already known.
comments.request: Remove this section from the manuscript.
comments.quote: I don’t find the comparison between the warming tolerances accounting of not for the temperature of acclimation particularly insightful (Fig. 3)

comments.issue: Which model corresponds to which table and panel, and what the three R2 values mean, is unclear.
comments.request: Map each model to its table, panel and statistic.
comments.quote: Which table is associated with each model, is panel C associated with Table S2 and so includes both maximum temperature and temperature variability or only the later?

comments.issue: What the dots, lines and colours in Fig. 2 represent is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the points, lines and colours in Fig. 2.
comments.quote: Are the dots on Fig.2 the population-specific values (hence the color gradient) and the lines the predictions of the model for each species for two contrasted conditions for visualization purposes (hence two colors)?

comments.issue: A third-degree latitude polynomial is used without explanation, inconsistent with the second-degree term elsewhere, producing odd lines.
comments.request: Explain and harmonise the polynomial terms.
comments.quote: Table S1 also shows that a 3rd degree polynomial term was used to test the effect of latitude (which is not explained in the Methods)

comments.issue: The origin of the lambda values and the phylogeny used are not reported.
comments.request: Report how lambda values and the phylogeny were obtained.
comments.quote: L14-15 P6, how the lambda values were calculated, do they come from the PGLS? Which phylogeny was used (i.e. the one represented in Fig. S3)?

comments.issue: How ARR was calculated and projected is unclear and hard to follow.
comments.request: Describe the ARR calculation and projection clearly in the Methods.
comments.quote: Also, I am unclear how the ARR were calculated and projected. In general L37-51 are difficult to comprehend despite several rounds of readings.

comments.issue: Estimating ARR between two points may not capture the shape of the thermal curve.
comments.request: Estimate ARR by integrating differences along the whole curve.
comments.quote: ARR could be estimated using an average value integrating differences along the entire curve using the same interval for all species

comments.issue: A quadratic model may be inappropriate because some curves unrealistically decrease and ARR is underestimated.
comments.request: Consider an asymptotic model instead.
comments.quote: Here I also wonder whether a quadratic model is the best choice (given that for some species the curve decreases at the end of the temperature acclimation gradient, which is not realistic and can underestimate ARR).

comments.issue: How the map was produced from species range overlap is not described.
comments.request: Add a Methods section detailing the map analysis.
comments.quote: Also, how was the map obtained, by averaging the ARR predicted across species occurring in a given pixel based on the overlap of their range maps?

reviews.assessment: Substantial computational effort and a clever standardisation, but the plasticity metric confounds local adaptation and the freshwater conclusion is uncertain.
strengths: careful design and handling of heterogeneous data sources

comments.issue: The writing needs clarification in many places.
comments.request: Clarify the writing throughout.
comments.quote: I also felt that the manuscript could be improved by clarifying the writing in many places.

comments.issue: ARR combines populations and is confounded by local adaptation, so it may not measure phenotypic plasticity.
comments.request: Use same-population data, or discuss this limitation and temper the plasticity claim.
comments.quote: If populations have locally adapted heat tolerance, the ARR is not only capturing variation due to phenotypic plasticity but is also confounded by evolutionary differences in thermal tolerance across populations.

comments.issue: The logic of the dissolved oxygen hypothesis is not understandable as explained.
comments.request: Explain the oxygen-limitation logic more clearly.
comments.quote: First, I do not understand the logic of this DO hypothesis the way that the authors explained it.

comments.issue: The extra freshwater plasticity could be methodological error from different modelled temperature sources rather than biology.
comments.request: Acknowledge this alternative source of between-realm differences.
comments.quote: the additional variation in plasticity not explained by thermal variation might not be biologically meaningful but rather might come from methodological error

comments.issue: A finer-scale temperature variability metric might explain the additional plasticity variation.
comments.request: Test variability calculated from daily or sub-daily temperatures.
comments.quote: I wonder if a more precise measure of variation (e.g., coefficient of variation calculated using daily or sub-daily rather than weekly temperatures) might have explained the additional variation in plasticity

comments.issue: The discussion does not recognise the precision and accuracy of the temperature data.
comments.quote: The discussion section is overall lacking recognition of the precision and accuracy of the data used and its possible effect on the results.

comments.issue: Alternative hypothesis: greater spatial thermal variation gives freshwater species refugia, so they may be less plastic.
comments.request: Test this alternative hypothesis about spatial variation and thermal refugia.
comments.quote: an alternative hypothesis that immediately came to mind is that freshwater species might have less plastic heat tolerance limits because the greater spatial variation in freshwater temperatures allows them access to thermal refugia

comments.issue: The introduction's hypotheses, known patterns and literature review need more clarity.
comments.request: Write out the hypotheses and known patterns more clearly.
comments.quote: I found the hypotheses and review of the literature in the introduction to need a bit more clarity.

comments.issue: The novel freshwater-versus-marine plasticity hypothesis is not highlighted in the introduction.
comments.request: Highlight this hypothesis more in the introduction.
comments.quote: I also felt that the novelty in the study lies in the testing the hypothesis that thermal tolerance limits of freshwater fish are more plastic than those of marine fish due to the greater thermal variation in freshwater bodies.

comments.issue: The claim that direct tests are few is disputed; many studies relate tolerance to thermal conditions.
comments.request: Reframe the novelty around marine versus freshwater plasticity.
comments.quote: I disagree that direct tests are few. Many papers look at the relationship between thermal tolerance limits/breadth/plasticity and experienced thermal conditions across latitude

comments.issue: The abstract speculates about water oxygenation, which the study does not measure or test.
comments.request: Remove the oxygenation speculation from the abstract.
comments.quote: This is misleading since this manuscript does not measure fluctuations in water oxygenation or test its relationship to plasticity.

comments.issue: It is unclear what 'latitudinal clines', 'distinct patterns' and 'species' vulnerability' mean.
comments.request: Unpack these terms and the patterns they refer to.
comments.quote: Not clear to the reader what “latitudinal clines” and “distinct patterns” in “species’ vulnerability” means.

comments.issue: The hypotheses-and-patterns paragraph is hard to follow.
comments.request: State the hypotheses and known patterns more clearly.
comments.quote: I found this paragraph hard to follow - the hypotheses and known patterns could be more clearly stated.

comments.issue: The point that air temperature does not represent aquatic thermal regimes needs to be made clear.
comments.request: Make this rationale explicit.
comments.quote: it helps to understand the thermal regime experienced by aquatic ectothermic organisms since the temperatures they experience are not well-represented by air temperature measurements

comments.issue: Terrestrial and aquatic experimental methods differ (e.g., righting versus running), possibly driving observed differences.
comments.request: Acknowledge this methodological difference.
comments.quote: Experimental methods also differ greatly between terrestrial and aquatic organisms which might contribute to these observed differences.

comments.issue: Realm hypotheses appear too late in the introduction.
comments.request: Add an earlier paragraph on realm hypotheses.
comments.quote: I think it would be useful to have an additional paragraph describing hypotheses about thermal tolerance of marine versus freshwater species further up

comments.issue: It is unclear whether duplicated data (GlobTherm, Comte & Olden) were removed.
comments.request: Report how duplicates were handled.
comments.quote: Did you remove duplicated data? I know there is some in GlobTherm and Comte & Olden

comments.issue: The sample size drops from 569 to 514 species without explanation.
comments.request: Explain why species were lost (e.g., missing realized ranges).
comments.quote: Why did sample size go from 569 spp to 514 spp? Were realized ranges not available?

comments.issue: Thermal exposure is characterised at species level although population-level data and collection latitudes exist.
comments.request: Characterise exposure per population at collection coordinates.
comments.quote: Why not characterize thermal exposure for each population separately by calculating the metrics at the latitude of collection/collection coordinates?

comments.issue: The latitude measure used is confusing relative to the range-wide exposure metrics.
comments.request: Explain the choice of latitude and why it matches the exposure metrics.
comments.quote: I’m confused about the latitude measurement used here. You mean you c hose the median latitude where heat tolerance measurements were tested?

comments.issue: Habitat type is included in the model but not mentioned in the methods.
comments.request: Specify habitat type as a model term.
comments.quote: Figure 1 shows habitat type was also included in the model – specify this here.

comments.issue: How thermal limits were standardised using acclimation and maximum exposure temperature is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the standardisation procedure precisely.
comments.quote: How did you “standardize” the thermal limits using acclimation temperature and max temperature of exposure?

comments.issue: The methods do not explain how plasticity in thermal tolerance was measured.
comments.request: Describe how plasticity was quantified from the measurements.
comments.quote: Not clear at all from any part of the methods section how you measured plasticity in thermal tolerance from the heat tolerance measurements?

comments.issue: 'Thermal niche' is used confusingly without distinguishing realized and fundamental niche.
comments.request: Define which niche is meant or avoid the term.
comments.quote: Thermal niche is confusing – are you talking about realized niche (i.e., your measurements of exposure) or fundamental niche (i.e., heat tolerance measurements).

comments.issue: Sample sizes are missing from all figures; Fig. 1 appears to show one point per species.
comments.request: Report sample sizes and clarify the unit of observation in captions.
comments.quote: missing statement of sample size (as are all other figures). Important since I believe this plot shows 1 point per species whereas all others have intraspecific measurements.

comments.issue: The figure references for the results described at page 7 lines 17-18 are wrong.
comments.request: Correct the figure references.
comments.quote: Figure 1B and 1C do not show this - references are wrong

comments.issue: How many intraspecific tolerance measures entered each ARR, and how ARR entered the model, is unclear.
comments.request: Report ARR counts and how ARR was modelled.
comments.quote: Unclear until now that acclimation response ratios were at all measured. How many intraspecific measures of thermal tolerance went into each?

comments.issue: Fig. 2C does not visibly show higher acclimation responses at low thermal variability.
comments.request: Show the slopes differently, e.g., with a zoomed inset.
comments.quote: In Figure 2C (which I think was meant to show increasing ARR with variability) I am not seeing higher acclimation responses (steeper slopes of curves?) when thermal variability is low (purple?).

comments.issue: Fig. 2 legend does not explain the colours and panel labels are missing.
comments.request: Explain the colours and add A, B, C labels.
comments.quote: Figure 2: Legend needs to better explain what the colours mean. Missing A B C labels.

comments.issue: It would help to compare Fig. 2B with and without adjusted acclimation temperatures within Fig. 3.
comments.request: Add the unadjusted version alongside Fig. 2B.
comments.quote: It would be nice to see version of Fig 2B with and without the adjusted acclimation temperatures beside each other as a part of Fig 3.

comments.issue: The global projection ignores likely geographic bias of points toward the Northern Hemisphere.
comments.request: Show the distribution of points on the map.
comments.quote: As with most ecological data, they are likely highly geographically biased to the Northern Hemisphere (Europe, North America) and should not be extrapolated elsewhere.

comments.issue: ARR estimates are too uncertain to project globally given local adaptation and methodological differences.
comments.request: Temper or remove the global ARR projections.
comments.quote: I have my hesitations about attributing all the observed variation in heat tolerance to phenotypic plasticity since the heat tolerance estimates came from different populations and some might be due to local adaptation

comments.issue: The different grey shades and many missing values in Fig. 5 are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the grey shades and missing values.
comments.quote: What are the different grey shades in this figure? (Why are there so many missing values?)

comments.issue: Relevant literature that already tested this is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Comte & Olden, Pinsky et al. and Gunderson & Stillman.
comments.quote: Cite the relevant literature that has already tested this (Comte & Olden 2016, Pinsky et al., 2019, Gunderson & Stillman 2015).

comments.issue: How greater heat tolerance plasticity helps species avoid oxygen limitation is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the adaptive logic linking plasticity and oxygen limitation.
comments.quote: I am not sure I understand how greater plasticity in heat tolerance helps species to avoid oxygen limitation. In warm waters, where oxygen is more limited, why is plasticity in heat tolerance adaptive?

title: Heat Tolerance and Its Plasticity in Freshwater and Marine Fishes Reflect Exposure to Extremes and Seasonal Variation in Habitat Temperatures

study.system: urban biodiversity; conceptual perspective on biotic homogenization

editor_summary: Editor notes the perspective generated challenging reviews requesting substantial revision; careful responses needed, though some controversial points may be intentional; substantial revisions required.

reviews.assessment: Timely and potentially influential perspective, but the criticisms of UBH are overstated and often unsupported or cherry-picked.
strengths: potential to be very influential and well cited

comments.issue: 'Facets' are actually premises of the argument, so the term misrepresents their role.
comments.request: Rename and treat these points as premises.
comments.quote: I don’t really like the term facets, because these are actually premises to their argument. If the premises are true, then their argument is logically supported. If untrue, then their argumentation is logically untenable.

comments.issue: The premises have no citations and it is unclear what is being argued or how well supported they are.
comments.request: Add citations and clarify the arguments.
comments.quote: First, none of them have citations associated with them. This is very important. Second, it is not always clear what they are arguing, or whether their arguments are well supported.

comments.issue: 'Habitat patches' is undefined and is organism-dependent.
comments.request: Define habitat patches clearly and justify the definition.
comments.quote: First, what do the authors mean by “habitat patches”. To a cockroach an urban apartment is their habitat. To a rat it maybe a sewer or suburban backyard. To a red-eyed vireo it might be the local woodlot.

comments.issue: The claim that urban patches are more heterogeneous than nonurban areas is debatable and scale-dependent.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison and its scale dependence.
comments.quote: are the authors arguing they are more heterogenous in space and time than nonurban areaa? That is debatable and likely depends on the spatial and temporal scale one is looking at

comments.issue: The statement that fragmentation between habitat patches is 'common' is a truism.
comments.request: Reword to say urbanization leads to fragmentation of natural, restored and built environments.
comments.quote: Here I don’t think the authors need to say it is common, they can just say “urbanization leads to fragmentation of natural, restored and the built environment”.

comments.issue: The habitat heterogeneity section makes many bold claims with no citations at all between lines 120-143.
comments.request: Support the claims with citations.
comments.quote: This section starting at line 119 makes many bold claims without supporting citations. For example, from lines 120-143, there isn’t a single citation.

comments.issue: Examples appear cherry-picked to support the authors' view and the conjectures rest on weak ground.
comments.request: Provide a more careful and accurate revision of these arguments.
comments.quote: The few examples chosen seem cherry picked to support the authors’ preferred view. A careful and more accurate revision is very important because readers will take these statements as truth, even though the authors’ conjectures stand on very weak ground.

comments.issue: Published evidence (Santangelo et al. 2022) shows cities are more similar to each other and internally more homogeneous, contradicting the assertions.
comments.request: Engage with and reconcile this published evidence.
comments.quote: we found that urban and nonurban environments were differentiated from one another, whereby on average two different cities (e.g. Tokyo and Toronto) were more similar to one another in these environmental features

comments.issue: Many arguments are untrue in many contexts; some features converge across cities while others diverge.
comments.request: Reconsider the arguments and acknowledge context dependence.
comments.quote: So I think the authors need to reconsider the arguments they are making. Many of their arguments are untrue in many contexts.

comments.issue: Citations are missing or dated at multiple lines (129-132, 150-153, 334, 344-345, 360, 426-427).
comments.request: Add missing citations and use more recent, robust references.
comments.quote: As previously mentioned, citations are often missing, or recent or more robust citations would be better. Here is an incomplete list:

comments.issue: The fragmentation paragraph cites dated and cherry-picked literature instead of key recent syntheses.
comments.request: Cite recent synthetic analyses of fragmentation effects on dispersal and gene flow.
comments.quote: The literature cited in this paragraph is dated and seemingly cherry-picked. There have been several important synthetic analyses of the literature on the effects of fragmentation on dispersal and gene flow.

comments.issue: The claim that UBH does not match modern metacommunity theory or case-study literature is unsupported.
comments.request: Justify why UBH conflicts with metacommunity theory.
comments.quote: on line 239 they state “[UBH] does not match modern meta-community theory, or the existing literature of case studies”.

comments.issue: Lokatis and Jeschke, who find the hypothesis supported a majority of the time, are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss Lokatis and Jeschke.
comments.quote: Why also not discuss Lokatis and Jeschke here, which does find that the hypothesis is supported a majority of the time.

comments.issue: Line 374 overgeneralizes that urbanization does not generate biotic homogenization, the same fallacy the paper criticizes.
comments.request: Remove the overgeneralization and embrace nuance.
comments.quote: Another example is line 374: “the process of urbanization occurs differently across cities and thus does not generate biotic homogenization”.

comments.issue: Figure 1 axes are treated as orthogonal although intensity and goals overlap, and habitat placements imply a quantitative analysis that was not done.
comments.request: Rethink Figure 1 and make clear the placements are speculative.
comments.quote: First, the authors have drawn the y- and x-axes as orthogonal variables, but there is a lot of overlap here. Indeed, is not cultivated areas by definition intensively managed? Are not truly "wild" areas unmanaged?

comments.issue: Box 1 Question 3 is unclear.
comments.request: Restate Question 3 more clearly.
comments.quote: 6. Box 1 - Question 3 could be stated more clearly

comments.issue: For Box 1 Question 4, the interaction between urbanization and local climate may matter more than climate change.
comments.request: Reframe Question 4 around urbanization-by-climate interactions.
comments.quote: Question 4: I agree it is an interesting question, but probably the more important effect will be the interaction between urbanization and local climate and not necessarily climate change.

comments.issue: Box 1 Question 5 assumes biotic differentiation is good, but it can be detrimental.
comments.request: Qualify the assumption that differentiation is desirable.
comments.quote: this statement is written with the assumption that biotic differentiation is a good thing. Is that always the case? Might increased biotic differentiation be detrimental to a given population, species, community or ecosystem process?

comments.issue: The phrase about homogenization across a city at line 63 is flagged.
comments.quote: leading to biotic homogenization ACROSS A CITY

comments.issue: Line 72 is missing a citation (likely Lokatis and Jeschke); whether 55% support is high needs context.
comments.request: Add the citation and contextualize the 55% figure.
comments.quote: Line 72: Missing citation. I assume this is the Lokatis and Jeschke citation? In some ways 55% of studies supporting the hypothesis seems quite high?

comments.issue: 'Typology' is a core argument but is not clearly defined for a broad readership.
comments.request: Define typology clearly.
comments.quote: Line 129: “Typology” needs to be clearly defined, both because it is a core argument throughout much of the paper, and because Ecology Letters' readership is broad and most readers will not be familiar with intricacies of urban ecology

comments.issue: 'Intra-city differentiation' is used without specifying what differentiates.
comments.request: Specify what is differentiating.
comments.quote: Line 134: “intra-city differentiation” in what?

comments.issue: Whether urban heterogeneity exceeds nonurban heterogeneity is not addressed, though it is the crux.
comments.request: Compare urban heterogeneity to nonurban heterogeneity.
comments.quote: Line 233: But is this heterogeneity more or less than what occurs in nonurban areas. This is not addressed and at the crux of the matter.

comments.issue: A counter-reference (Schmidt et al. 2020) should be cited at line 402.
comments.request: Cite Schmidt et al. 2020 at line 402.
comments.quote: Line 402: But see: Schmidt, C, Domaratzki, M, Kinnunen, R, Bowman, J, Garroway, CJ. 2020. Continent-wide effects of urbanization on bird and mammal genetic diversity. Proc. Biol. Sci. 287: 20192497.

comments.issue: 'Positively' is a value adjective; the intended meaning is increased heterogeneity.
comments.request: Avoid value adjectives and say 'increase urban biotic heterogeneity'.
comments.quote: Line 457: Do the authors mean "increase urban biotic heterogeneity". Avoid value adjectives like "positively"

comments.issue: The result at lines 463-464 may actually support UBH.
comments.request: Address whether this result supports UBH.
comments.quote: Line 463-464: Wouldn’t this support UBH?

comments.issue: Interactions between typology and climate are important and should be discussed at line 530.
comments.request: Discuss typology-by-climate interactions.
comments.quote: Line 530: The interactions between typology and climate are very important, as we discovered in our 2022 paper, although there was not space to tease it out there.

reviews.assessment: The core premise that UBH is overstated is not convincingly supported; the manuscript needs reframing and more cohesive arguments.
strengths: acknowledges that urban areas are diverse in form

comments.issue: Some city-scale homogenization is almost inevitable from extirpation and introduced species, and the paper's mechanisms do not exclude it.
comments.request: Acknowledge the inevitability of some homogenization at the city scale.
comments.quote: I would have expected the authors to point out that some level of homogenization across urban areas is almost inevitable at the scale of entire cities

comments.issue: The diversity arguments do not support the core premise that UBH has been overstated.
comments.request: Provide evidence that the premise is supported.
comments.quote: I do not find that these arguments support the core premise that the UBH has been overstated.

comments.issue: The 2022 meta-analysis supporting the premise is mentioned but not cited.
comments.request: Cite the meta-analysis the premise relies on.
comments.quote: This premise, instead, is much better supported by the 2022 manuscript the authors mention that performs a meta-analysis (though this paper was not actually cited, so I was unable to look up which paper it was specifically

comments.issue: The manuscript needs reframing to show where the field fell short or when homogenization operates consistently.
comments.request: Reframe the manuscript with cohesive arguments about UBH's limits.
comments.quote: the authors would need to reframe the manuscript. I think it would be important for the authors to identify where the field has fallen short because of focus on biotic homogenization as a pattern.

comments.issue: The language needs editing for specificity, e.g. line 392's claim about encompassing a majority is too vague.
comments.request: Edit the language for specificity.
comments.quote: Importantly, the language would also need to be edited for specificity.

comments.issue: The claim that niche-based organization should arise lacks evidence; fragmented habitats may instead produce dispersal-based organization.
comments.request: Abandon or flesh out the niche-based organization argument.
comments.quote: This claim that niche-based organization should arise is a big one without convincing evidence. I’d like to see this argument abandoned or fleshed out more

comments.issue: It is unclear how fitness relates to what appears to be a population genetic structure study.
comments.request: Clarify the role of fitness.
comments.quote: Line 155: It is unclear how fitness plays in here. Wasn’t this study about population genetic structure? If not, please clarify.

comments.issue: 'Increased' implies time although the comparison seems to be urban versus rural.
comments.request: Clarify the comparison.
comments.quote: Line 153: “Increased” conjures time, but I think you are comparing urban to rural? I’m unsure.

comments.issue: 'Disturbance' is not defined and is used with different meanings in ecology.
comments.request: Provide a concrete definition of disturbance.
comments.quote: Line 204: “Disturbance” is not defined. This needs a concrete definition because it is a word people often use in ecology to mean different things.

comments.issue: Homogenization can operate at some scales while urban areas remain heterogeneous; the paper does not resolve 'compared to what'.
comments.request: Specify the baseline and scale for homogenization claims.
comments.quote: Lines 243-246: These lines characterize my core issue with the manuscript, which is that biotic homogenization can operate at some scales, and urban areas can be heterogeneous.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the described 'trap' is real and who falls into it.
comments.request: Specify who is falling into the trap or remove the claim.
comments.quote: Line 521: Is this trap actually happening? If so, who is falling into it? Ecologists? Managers?

comments.issue: The premise that people view urban areas as 'wastelands' seems untrue and potentially offensive.
comments.request: Reframe the argument or specify who makes these assumptions.
comments.quote: Line 535: Again, this premise that people believe urban areas are “wastelands” seems untrue, antiquated and potentially offensive to scientists and managers who spend their lives thinking about urban diversity.

title: Re‐Thinking the Urban Biotic Homogenization Hypothesis

study.system: squamate reptiles; elevational gradients; phylogenetic meta-analysis

editor_summary: Editor says all reviewers emphasize major shortcomings preventing publication: unclear methods (screening, extraction, models, moderators, random effects, family analyses), confusing reporting of non-significant trends, uninformative figures; novelty framing and a tighter, negative-result focus are needed.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and reliable study, but statistical methods need fuller explanation and non-significant results are consistently over-interpreted.
strengths: good addition to the POLS literature

comments.issue: Number and structure of models are lacking; family and suborder analyses appear in results but not methods; final random effects unclear.
comments.request: Describe the models, their structure and retained random effects.
comments.quote: the statistical analyses require more explanation. Information on the number and structure of models is lacking.

comments.issue: Results are interpreted without regard to effect size or significance; the main negative result is under-discussed relative to weak family patterns.
comments.request: Focus on the lack of support for POLS and label non-significant results as such.
comments.quote: results are often reported and interpreted in a similar manner regardless of their effect size, statistical significance or confidence interval

comments.issue: Google Scholar is inappropriate for systematic reviews and its reproducibility is low; search personnel, dates and repetitions are not reported.
comments.request: Acknowledge this limitation and report search details.
comments.quote: Google scholar can be seen as inappropriate for conducting systematic reviews or meta-analyses

comments.issue: Maternal body size versus adult/female body size are conflated.
comments.request: Keep only one consistent term.
comments.quote: The fact that it is later called female body size reinforces this confusion, only one term should be kept.

comments.issue: 95% confidence intervals or SEs are not given in the results text.
comments.request: Report CIs or SEs in the text.
comments.quote: Authors should provide the 95% confidence intervals (or the SE) directly in the text too.

comments.issue: Wording such as 'increased non-significantly by 8%' is ambiguous about significance.
comments.request: State direction only for significant results.
comments.quote: “lifespan increased non-significantly by an average of 8%”: This kind of wording makes it hard to understand whether the authors consider this result to be non-significant

comments.issue: Statistical significance of the differences on line 219 is unclear and the test lacks a hypothesis.
comments.request: Report significance and justify the test.
comments.quote: But were those differences statistically significant? It is not clear where these differences are estimated.

comments.issue: Low sample sizes for Serpentes make effect sizes prone to bias and false positives.
comments.request: Report sample sizes and refer to the figures.
comments.quote: sample sizes for Serpentes are much lower and may be more prone to biased effect sizes and false positive findings

comments.issue: Stating non-significance and CIs crossing zero is redundant.
comments.request: Delete one of the two statements.
comments.quote: delete one or the other as it is most likely 100% redundant with 95% confidence intervals crossing zero

comments.issue: Snake sample sizes are low and their small, non-significant adult body size effect may be unreliable.
comments.request: Acknowledge the sample size limitation.
comments.quote: the sample size is much lower for snakes hence more prone to biased effect sizes and false positive findings

comments.issue: Longevity increase with elevation is described as a trend despite being non-significant.
comments.request: Label the result as non-significant.
comments.quote: “longevity increased with elevation”: on average/although not statistically significant.

comments.issue: Viviparity is not tested as a moderator that could explain POLS-elevation relationships.
comments.request: Include viviparity as a moderator.
comments.quote: Would it be possible to include viviparity as a moderator in models?

comments.issue: Claim about oviparous populations retaining eggs longer needs a reference.
comments.request: Add a supporting reference.
comments.quote: “high elevation oviparous populations tend to retain eggs longer before laying than low elevation populations”: we think this requires a reference.

comments.issue: Results on lines 425-427 appear non-significant but are not discussed as such.
comments.request: Label and discuss these results as non-significant.
comments.quote: It feels like all these are not significant and not discussed as such.

comments.issue: Statement that the study showed no evidence for heat variation mischaracterises the alternative-hypothesis logic.
comments.request: Correct this characterisation.
comments.quote: No, it didn't show evidence for heat variation. This is different

comments.issue: Excluding non-English literature may bias results and should be acknowledged.
comments.request: Mention this as a limitation and cite relevant sources.
comments.quote: Note (and acknowledge) that excluding non-english literature may bias results

comments.issue: Legend placement in Figure 1 is confusing.
comments.request: Move the trait legend to the bottom and taxa shapes to the top or an inset.
comments.quote: The location of the legend for the taxa's shapes is disturbing as it feels like it represents the x axis.

comments.issue: Viperidae legend is unnecessary and the plot type could match the appendix.
comments.request: Remove the unused legend and use the appendix plot style.
comments.quote: Viperidae are not present on the figure so the legend is not needed.

comments.issue: Unclear whether reference lists of all 401 articles were checked.
comments.request: Clarify the reference-checking procedure.
comments.quote: “Afterwards, we also looked at references in the downloaded articles for other records which we might have missed during our database search.” in all 401 of them?

comments.issue: No reference is given for the summary-statistic conversion formulas.
comments.request: Cite a reference for these formulas.
comments.quote: Any reference for the use of these formulas in meta-analyses?

comments.issue: Number of papers using each extraction method is not reported and methods per paper are not documented.
comments.request: Add counts and a method column in Appendix S1.
comments.quote: the authors should add a column in Appendix S1 indicating the method used for each paper to improve reproducibility

comments.issue: The value 3.92 is used without explaining its relation to CI and sample size.
comments.request: Give the relationship rather than the number alone.
comments.quote: how is 3.92 calculated in relation to CI and sample size? Better put this relationship rather than just the 3.92 number.

comments.issue: The function and package behind 'selected dfs = contain' are not specified.
comments.request: Name the function and package.
comments.quote: in which function of which package?

comments.issue: Two line-level copy edits (find/found; missing 'in').
comments.quote: Abstract: Line 35. “find” should be “found”.

comments.issue: Criteria for including moderators based on I2 are not given.
comments.request: State the inclusion cut-off.
comments.quote: which criteria/cut-off was used for inclusion?

comments.issue: Ultrametric is not explained.
comments.request: Explain or cite a reference.
comments.quote: What does ultrametric means (at least give a reference)?

comments.issue: Different buffers (1 km versus 5 km) are used without explanation.
comments.request: Explain the different buffer sizes.
comments.quote: explain why using a different buffer

comments.issue: Funnel plots are not provided.
comments.request: Add the funnel plots to the appendix.
comments.quote: Could you provide these funnel plots in the appendix?

comments.issue: Some elevation pairs span huge longitudes and may differ in other aspects, blurring POLS patterns.
comments.request: Check the impact of these pairs on the results.
comments.quote: these pairs could have been isolated from one another for a long time and differ widely in other aspects than elevation, thus blurring POLS changes

comments.issue: The data range is not visible in the 3D plots of Figure S10.
comments.request: Show data points or rug plots on the axes.
comments.quote: It would be useful to see where the data is in these 3D plots (and hence were is the actual range of the data).

reviews.assessment: Powerful and necessary meta-analysis, but novelty is unclear, the modelling framework is hard to follow and figures waste ink.

comments.issue: Conclusions about ambiguous within-species POLS evidence have already been highlighted in past work.
comments.request: Articulate the novelty more clearly.
comments.quote: I had a difficult time gauging novelty of the manuscript, as some of its conclusions seem to have been already highlighted in past work

comments.issue: Model structure is hard to follow; single-predictor models and loss of statistical power are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the modelling framework and why predictors were not combined.
comments.quote: Initially when reading the results I found the model structure hard to follow, and therefore the interpretation of the figures and tables difficult to parse.

comments.issue: Model equations are not written out; I2, study and location terms are undefined and location appears twice in Table 1.
comments.request: Write out the equations and define all model terms.
comments.quote: actually writing out the model equations would be helpful to give the reader a sense of what is actually contained within the models

comments.issue: Figures show coefficients and SEs but not the raw effect size distributions, using much ink for little information.
comments.request: Show the distribution of raw effect sizes.
comments.quote: What I would especially like to see is the distribution of the raw effect sizes (the actual data) rather than just the coefficient estimates and standard errors.

comments.issue: Family-level analyses appear to subset data rather than use a family factor with post-hoc tests.
comments.request: Use a family factor with formal post-hoc testing.
comments.quote: I think the former would be preferable on statistical grounds (both because of information sharing, as well as the ability to formally test which families are different from others)

comments.issue: The abstract sentence about decoupling heat tolerance and climate is unparsable.
comments.request: Unpack what this sentence means.
comments.quote: Unpack what this means. I can’t parse the sentence. What does it mean to “decouple heat tolerances and climate”.

comments.issue: Iteroparity is not defined.
comments.request: Define iteroparity.
comments.quote: L20: iteroparity --define

comments.issue: Thermoregulators versus thermoconformers are not considered.
comments.request: Consider this breakdown in the analyses.
comments.quote: Somewhere in here needs to be some consideration of the breakdown between thermoregulators and thermo conformers

comments.issue: 'Shared measurements' is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify the term.
comments.quote: What is meant by “shared measurements”?

comments.issue: Which factors are random is not specified.
comments.request: Specify the random factors.
comments.quote: Specifically what factors are random?

comments.issue: How phylogeny is accounted for (Brownian motion, Pagel's lambda, species effect) is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the phylogenetic model, with formulas.
comments.quote: Not clear here or from the supplement how phylogeny is actually accounted for. Needs to be explained more clearly, with formulas if needed.

comments.issue: Rationale for log-transforming latitude is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the transformation.
comments.quote: I do not understand the rationale for log transforming latitude.

comments.issue: The time-lag bias is not explained and is absent from the discussion.
comments.request: Explain the bias and address it in the discussion.
comments.quote: Need to explain what this time lag bias means, either here, or present it as a result and explain what it means there.

comments.issue: Results lump all low and high populations rather than expressing effects per unit elevation change.
comments.request: Report effects per specified elevation increment.
comments.quote: Shouldn’t all results be reported as an effect of increasing some specified amount in elevation, not just lumping all low and all high populations together?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether family variation is a formal statistical interaction or eye-balling of separate analyses.
comments.request: Clarify with model equations.
comments.quote: Is the variation between different families, etc, a statistical statement? I.e. there was an interaction effect of families, which was significant?

comments.issue: How moderators were incorporated and why not a priori is unclear.
comments.request: Define moderators and their place in the model.
comments.quote: Hard to understand how moderators were incorporated here, and why they weren’t incorporated a priori.

comments.issue: 'Intercept models' is undefined and confusing.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: I don’t think what is meant by “intercept models” has been introduced yet. As opposed to what?

comments.issue: 'Taxonomic' ranks wording is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: L276: “taxonomic” ranks?

comments.issue: Gene flow preventing local adaptation is the obvious alternative explanation and is not addressed.
comments.request: Unpack this point with examples and discuss selection versus plasticity.
comments.quote: Otherwise the obvious critism of the work is that geneflow is preventing local adaptation, and so is preventing any pace of life differences from manifesting

comments.issue: No hypotheses are offered for how and why families should differ, nor alternative explanations for the lack of patterns.
comments.request: Float explicit family hypotheses and alternative scenarios.
comments.quote: to be useful scientifically some hypotheses regarding how different families will behave differently and why needs to be floated

comments.issue: Discussion is too long and discusses non-significant results in excessive depth.
comments.request: Shorten the discussion and delete the tangential climate change section.
comments.quote: I found the discussion to be too long given the findings. The various non-significant results are discussed in too much depth

comments.issue: Table 1 body size CIs exclude zero and beta_0, suggesting a missing negative sign.
comments.request: Check and correct the CI values.
comments.quote: I was initially confused by the upper and lower CI for body size. These exclude 0, and so the result should be significant.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and timely meta-analysis with appropriate methods, but screening, predictions, theory integration and discussion need improvement.
strengths: statistical methods appropriate for data dependencies

comments.issue: Question title is vague about the negative answer.
comments.request: Use a more specific and clear title.
comments.quote: I am generally not a fan of question titles when the answer could be summarised as 'not really'. Better to be more specific and clear up front.

comments.issue: Several line-level grammar edits (abstract, discussion, conclusions).
comments.quote: Abstract – line 36: Grammar. Should be ‘found’ instead of ‘find’.

comments.issue: Other meta-analyses reporting weak POLS evidence are not mentioned.
comments.request: Cite Royauté et al. 2018 and Mathot et al. 2019.
comments.quote: A variety of other meta-analyses have also reported weak evidence for the POLS hypothesis (particularly concerning behaviour). These should also be mentioned here.

comments.issue: 'Most diverse' is misleading given Teleostei are more species-rich.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: If you are referring to species richness, the wording may be somewhat misleading: Teleostei are far more species-rich than squamates.

comments.issue: The prediction linking reduced food availability to increased life history variation is not explained.
comments.request: Expand the rationale for this prediction.
comments.quote: It is not immediately clear to me why reduced food availability would predictably lead to increased life history variation.

comments.issue: Search is limited to one database without benchmark testing of the search string.
comments.request: Broaden the search and report benchmark testing.
comments.quote: Why not broaden the database search to include Scopus and others? Did you do any preliminary testing with benchmark articles to see if your search string retrieved those?

comments.issue: Screening procedure, screeners and consistency are not described in the methods.
comments.request: Report abstract and full-text screening details.
comments.quote: Did you do abstract and then full text screening? Who performed the screening? Was this consistent between screeners?

comments.issue: Unclear how many articles were excluded for lacking summary statistics and whether authors were contacted.
comments.request: Clarify the exclusion process.
comments.quote: Was this only after trying to contact authors etc.? Please clarify.

comments.issue: Only the lowest and highest elevation populations were extracted instead of all data.
comments.request: Use all populations or justify the extreme-only extraction.
comments.quote: Why not include all of this data, and compare it to the lowest elevation population with the corresponding differences in elevation?

comments.issue: Maternal body size and adult female body size are not distinguished.
comments.request: Clarify the difference.
comments.quote: What is meant by maternal body size here? What is the difference between adult female body size and maternal body size?

comments.issue: It is unclear how lifespan was measured rather than age of focal individuals.
comments.request: Clarify the lifespan measure.
comments.quote: Unclear how this is lifespan, and not just the age of focal individuals?

comments.issue: Statement about data recovery from Africa is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the wording.
comments.quote: Do you mean that you recovered the least amount of data from Africa? The way this is currently written is a little unclear.

comments.issue: Statement on lines 198-199 is redundant.
comments.request: Remove or reword.
comments.quote: This statement is a little redundant and probably unnecessary.

comments.issue: Percentages in the results text lack uncertainty estimates.
comments.request: Give SD, SE or CI around percentages.
comments.quote: Can you give uncertainty estimates (e.g. SD, SE, CI) around the percentages reported in the results text?

comments.issue: Reporting a logically impossible outcome on lines 247-248 is strange.
comments.request: Remove or reframe this statement.
comments.quote: It is not clear why you are reporting this here, as such an outcome is not logically possible?

comments.issue: Resource acquisition and competition gradients are not accounted for and could mask POLS patterns.
comments.request: Consider resource competition as an alternative driver.
comments.quote: if there was higher competition for resources etc. at low elevation populations/reduced competition at high elevations, this could potentially shift life-history strategies that mask the predicted POLS differences

comments.issue: Line 370 about heat tolerance is not specific.
comments.request: State the direction of the change.
comments.quote: Be more specific. Heat tolerance declined at higher elevations?

comments.issue: Relevant work on thermal physiology syndromes is missing.
comments.request: Cite Michelangeli et al. 2018.
comments.quote: Lines 391-392: Also see:

comments.issue: Traits on lines 400-403 may relate to foraging success and resource acquisition.
comments.request: Connect these traits to resource acquisition.
comments.quote: these traits could predictably be associated with foraging success and resource acquisition

comments.issue: Viviparity is not included as a moderator.
comments.request: Include viviparity as a moderator in the analysis.
comments.quote: Good point. Why not include viviparity as a moderator in your analysis?

comments.issue: Unclear whether 'adult' on line 502 includes only males.
comments.request: Clarify and justify.
comments.quote: Does adult here only include males? If so, why? Please clarify.

comments.issue: Reduced density and intraspecific competition at high elevations are not considered.
comments.request: Consider this additional explanation.
comments.quote: Yes, but there is also likely reduced density and intraspecific competition at these sites.

comments.issue: Lines 515-517 are unclear about why the pattern must hold.
comments.request: Clarify the argument.
comments.quote: Could this be clearer? It is not immediately clear to me why this would necessarily be the case?

comments.issue: Lines 520-521 may explain the results better than thermoregulation costs.
comments.request: Emphasise this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: This is a key point which I think could likely explain this results, rather than greater costs of thermoregulation per se.

comments.issue: Discussion is lengthy in parts.
comments.request: Make the discussion more concise.
comments.quote: I also found the discussion very lengthy in parts and feel it could be made more concise to ease readability.

comments.issue: Conclusion phrasing is too strong because trait covariation was not directly tested.
comments.request: Rephrase around lack of support for expected divergence.
comments.quote: I think this phrasing is likely too strong. The POLS hypothesis centrally revolves around trat covariations (something you did not test per se).

comments.issue: Figure 1 layout and caption are unclear.
comments.request: Explain the panels more clearly in the caption.
comments.quote: So, the top half of the figure just indicates for which families there were sig/non-sig differences in different traits?

title: No Evidence for Pace of Life Evolution Along Elevational Gradients in Squamate Reptiles

study.system: freshwater fishes; 2704 lakes; temperature-size rule

editor_summary: Editor reports all three reviewers were very positive and saw high conceptual novelty; two had minor comments while one raised substantive concerns on analysis, presentation and interpretation, but revision is expected to succeed.

reviews.assessment: Well-conducted study with an impressive dataset, but presentation, concept definitions and several methodological caveats need attention.
strengths: highly relevant for the journal's audience

comments.issue: The original TSR formulation does not predict smaller maximum size, contrary to the paper's framing.
comments.request: Clarify this and cite Audzijonyte et al. 2025.
comments.quote: the original formulation of the temperature-size rule (TSR) does not include a prediction that maximum animal size will get smaller

comments.issue: Different concepts of fish body size (average, asymptotic, community-level, size-at-age) are conflated in the introduction and references.
comments.request: Clarify the distinctions and cite Lindmark et al. 2023.
comments.quote: the introduction and to some extent also the discussion of this study (like many other papers) confuses different concepts of fish body size and relevant references

comments.issue: The change-point growth model may not work for natural populations; convergence and parameter reliability are not demonstrated.
comments.request: Show that analyses converged and estimates are reliable.
comments.quote: It would be important to convince the reader that your analyses all converged and parameter estimates were reliable.

comments.issue: Ageing methods (scales, otoliths, spine) have different biases that are not accounted for.
comments.request: Add ageing method as a random factor in the models.
comments.quote: Ideally, ageing method should be added to the models as a random factor, and given the large dataset available, there should hopefully be sufficient contrasts for the models to identify the potential effect of the ageing methods.

comments.issue: Most ages come from age-length keys rather than direct measurements, giving false precision.

comments.issue: How maximum size was estimated, and uncertainty propagation, are not explained.

comments.issue: Recreational fishing pressure is unaccounted for and makes maximum age and size estimates dubious.

comments.issue: The practical meaning, units and interpretation of parameters such as b1 and Amat are unclear.

comments.issue: Lake identifiers in the archived data are cryptic and not explained.

comments.issue: 'Thermal preferenda' may not be the accepted term.

novel field evaluation of TSR expectations

comments.issue: Common and scientific names are used inconsistently across sections.

title: Mixed Support for the Temperature‐Size Rule in Wild Freshwater Fishes

study.system: global range shifts and genetic diversity of 1888 animal and plant species

comments.issue: No tests were applied to detect selective signals in the markers, so the adaptive interpretation is unsupported.

comments.issue: The symbols POS, DTy and SDes are unclear.

comments.issue: A relevant reference on combining niche modelling and landscape genetics is missing.

reviews.assessment: Two addressable critiques: the interaction rationale is unclear and the evolutionary rescue language is overstated.

title: Genetic Diversity Impacts Climate‐Induced Species Range Shifts

study.system: annual plants; germination plasticity and storage effect models

editor_summary: Editor asks to clarify how ecological assumptions affect results, discuss the cost of plasticity, and improve presentation of the individual-based model and its code.

reviews.assessment: Very important contribution, but the advance over prior work, unrealistic assumptions and unused analytical results need attention.
strengths: novel treatment of temporal assortative mating and explicit genetics

comments.issue: The contribution relative to Kortessis and Chesson 2021 is not distinguished enough.

comments.issue: Key analytical results are relegated to the appendix and not discussed.

comments.issue: References at Line 21 concern fire, not the weather variation studied.
comments.request: Use references relevant to between-year weather variation.

comments.issue: Fixed seedbank size is unrealistic and the constant-N assumption's impact is unaddressed.

comments.issue: Modelling competition among seeds is an unrealistic approximation.

comments.issue: More realistic competition assumptions could be tested in simulations.

comments.quote: you could also use more realistic competition assumptions, for example have the competition occur for seed production, not for membership of the seedbank, which could then vary in size

comments.issue: Fire-prone perennials with overlapping cohorts limit the relevance of the mating result.
comments.request: Acknowledge this scope limitation.

comments.issue: Robustness could be assessed against Kortessis and Chesson's more realistic formulation.

comments.issue: The arbitrary scaling of z-units is not clarified.

comments.issue: Normal-distribution results lack a statistical reference.

comments.issue: Differences from Kortessis and Chesson's formulation are not explained.

comments.issue: Analytical results are under-used for drawing conclusions.

reviews.assessment: Conceptually innovative, well-executed study; minor improvements to model description, code structure and a figure.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and worthy of publication, but similar results already exist and the cost of plasticity is not considered.

comments.issue: The cost of plasticity is not considered; it could shrink the parameter space for diversity.

comments.issue: Excluding studies without variance data may bias the dataset; the number excluded is not reported.

comments.issue: Statistical methods at lines 156-158 lack model structure and software details.

comments.issue: Numerical values at lines 217-219 are unclear.

comments.request: Add the ecological relevance of each trait to Table 1.

comments.issue: Biomass estimates based solely on PhytoPAM are not justified; counts or biovolumes would be stronger.
comments.request: Justify or replace the PhytoPAM biomass estimates.
comments.quote: Biomass estimates based solely on PhytoPAM need justification; counts or biovolumes would strengthen conclusions.

comments.issue: 'Trade-off' is used without demonstrated fitness costs or benefits.
comments.quote: "Trade-off" should only be used if fitness costs/benefits are demonstrated.

comments.issue: How field data relate to monocultures and how nutrient limitation was defined in natural samples are unclear.
comments.request: Explain these methods.
comments.quote: Clarify how field data were related to monocultures; specify how nutrient limitation was defined in natural samples.

comments.issue: The metric 'eq. chlorophyll a' is undefined and its use over cell counts is not justified.
comments.request: Define this metric and justify it over cell counts.
comments.quote: Define "eq. chlorophyll a." Why not use cell counts given flow cytometry data?

comments.issue: Focusing on chlorophyll and phycocyanin to infer N or light limitation is not justified given more traits were measured.
comments.request: Justify the focus on these two pigments.
comments.quote: Justify focus on chlorophyll and phycocyanin to infer N or light limitation when more traits were measured.

comments.issue: The ecological implications of differing results are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss these implications.
comments.quote: L337–339: Discuss the ecological implications of differing results.

comments.issue: Guedes et al. (2019) does not fully support the authors' claim.
comments.request: Correct the claim or the citation.
comments.quote: Guedes et al. (2019) does not fully support the authors' claim—please correct.

comments.issue: Results may reflect physiological or energetic constraints rather than adaptive synchronization.
comments.request: Consider this alternative explanation.
comments.quote: Consider whether results reflect physiological or energetic constraints rather than adaptive synchronization.

comments.issue: The sinking explanation is framed as an adaptive trade-off rather than a physiological consequence of N limitation.
comments.request: Reframe the explanation.
comments.quote: Reframe the sinking explanation as a physiological consequence of N limitation rather than an adaptive trade-off.

comments.issue: It is unclear why Microcystis traits were not separated if the flow cytometry data were at cell level.
comments.request: Clarify this analytical choice.
comments.quote: Clarify why only Microcystis traits were not separated if flow cytometry data were at cell level.

comments.issue: The approach associates traits with environmental conditions but does not directly uncover mechanisms.
