comments.request: Soften the mechanistic claims.
comments.quote: The approach associates traits with environmental conditions, but does not directly uncover mechanisms.

reviews.assessment: Recommends major revisions: the trait-based approach is sound but the extrapolation from single-cell lab responses to colonial field communities is not justified.
strengths: clearly articulated introduction and research questions

comments.issue: There is a mismatch between the comprehensive trait-based approach described in the methods and the limited evidence supporting the conclusions.
comments.request: Use the full trait-based approach for the field analysis or justify the narrower scope.
comments.quote: There is a substantial mismatch between the comprehensive trait-based approach described in the methods and the limited evidence ultimately used to support the study's conclusions.

comments.issue: The extrapolation to natural populations uses only two pigments and only nitrogen and light, ignoring other measured traits and treatments.
comments.request: Analyze the full trait set in relation to all treatments.
comments.quote: the extrapolation to natural populations analyzes and reports changes in only two pigments (chlorophyll-a and phycocyanin) and only in relation to nitrogen and light

comments.issue: It is not justified why laboratory responses from single cells without species interactions represent natural communities.
comments.request: Justify that laboratory responses represent natural communities.
comments.quote: why laboratory responses (conducted out of ecological context with single cells and no species interactions) can be used as representatives for natural communities

comments.issue: Laboratory experiments exclude species interactions that influence size and pigment profiles in nature, and this assumption is not justified.
comments.request: Justify this assumption or address species interactions.
comments.quote: The authors do not justify the assumption that species interactions do not alter these phenotypic patterns.

comments.issue: Single-cell laboratory responses are extrapolated to colonial field populations, questioning the validity of the extrapolation.
comments.request: Address the validity of this extrapolation.
comments.quote: This raises questions about the validity of extrapolating single-cell laboratory responses to colonial field populations.

comments.issue: Relationships between pigment responses and phosphorus or CO2 treatments are not discussed for natural communities.
comments.request: Discuss pigment responses to phosphorus and CO2.
comments.quote: the authors do not discuss relationships between pigment responses and phosphorus or CO₂ treatments in the context of natural communities

comments.issue: Interpretations about N2-fixing cyanobacteria remain speculative without species composition or density data.
comments.request: Support these interpretations with species composition data.
comments.quote: Several interpretations, particularly regarding the role of N₂-fixing cyanobacteria in natural populations, remain speculative without supporting data on species composition or relative densities.

comments.issue: The intended role of the integrated phenotype and fingerprint is unclear and is not consistently applied to the field data.
comments.request: Clarify and consistently apply the integrated phenotype.
comments.quote: The authors should explicitly clarify the intended role of the integrated phenotype and fingerprint in both the introduction and discussion.

comments.issue: The scope of the field flow-cytometry data (cells, colonies or all phytoplankton) is not explained.
comments.request: Clarify the scale and scope of the field data.
comments.quote: Explain in detail whether field flow-cytometry data included only cells, cells and small colonies, or covered all phytoplankton including eukaryotes

comments.issue: Bioassay methods and results are not in the main text, so readers cannot assess their importance.
comments.request: Move bioassay methods and results to the main text.
comments.quote: Move bioassay methods and results to the main text to allow readers to assess their importance for the main message

comments.issue: The text is not streamlined; results paragraphs and the discussion carry unnecessary content.
comments.request: Streamline the text and focus the discussion on the laboratory-field comparison.
comments.quote: Shorten the discussion to focus more directly on the comparison between laboratory and field patterns

comments.issue: The advantages and limitations of the approach are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the approach's advantages and limitations.
comments.quote: Discuss the advantages and limitations of the approach, particularly regarding the narrow scope of laboratory assays and the potential impact of species interactions on field responses.

comments.issue: Species composition data to substantiate claims about diazotrophs and other community members are missing.
comments.request: Add species composition data from microscopy, pigments or molecular tools.
comments.quote: Include species composition assessment using microscopy, pigment signatures, or molecular tools alongside flow cytometry measurements

comments.issue: Dimensionality reduction flattens and makes the perceived trait space convex, which is not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge this effect on the perceived trait space.
comments.quote: Note that dimensionality reduction may significantly affect the perceived trait space, which will be flattened by such methods and made convex.

comments.issue: The promised intraspecific and multidimensional trait variation is not delivered in the natural community analysis.
comments.request: Address this gap in the natural community analysis.
comments.quote: The narrative emphasizes the importance of intraspecific trait variation and multidimensional trait responses, yet this expectation is not met in the analysis of natural communities.

comments.issue: Flow cytometry measures individual-particle level, not cell level; colonial organisms represent the colony.
comments.request: Correct the terminology.
comments.quote: Note that flow cytometry allows individual-particle level phenotype, not cell level.

comments.issue: Hypotheses need more detail and references, and the hypothesis that laboratory responses represent natural communities is missing.
comments.request: Add this hypothesis and explain the hypotheses with references.
comments.quote: A critical hypothesis is missing regarding why laboratory responses can represent natural communities.

comments.issue: No phosphate measurements or environmental data are reported for the field analysis despite the expectation set in the text.
comments.request: Report phosphate or environmental data for the field analysis.
comments.quote: no phosphate measurements or corresponding environmental data are reported in the field analysis

comments.issue: 'Individual particle level' is not used explicitly and consistently throughout.
comments.request: Use this term consistently throughout the paper.
comments.quote: "Individual particle level" should be explicit throughout the paper.

comments.issue: The log10 transformation loses variation and may bias phenotypic diversity measures, and its rationale is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the rationale and its effect on diversity measures.
comments.quote: The rationale for log10 transformation should be clarified, as this loses substantial variation and forces phenotypes to be very similar in log space

comments.issue: The functional dispersion and resilience narrative applies to all functional diversity measures but is not elaborated for them.
comments.request: Elaborate this for all metrics used.
comments.quote: The narrative regarding functional dispersion and its relationship to resilience applies to all functional diversity measures

comments.issue: Whether field tests focused on single cells or small colonies is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the unit used in field tests.
comments.quote: Clarify whether field tests focused on single cells or small colonies, as cyanobacteria typically grow as colonies in nature.

comments.issue: Section 2.4 is cited but does not exist.
comments.request: Verify and correct the section number.
comments.quote: Section 2.4 is referenced but does not exist in the manuscript. Verify and correct the section number.

comments.issue: How functional clusters were defined and how this chapter contributes to the main message are unclear.
comments.request: Explain the cluster definition and its contribution.
comments.quote: Clarify how functional clusters were defined and explain how this results chapter contributes to the main message

comments.issue: The descriptive chapter's contribution to the main message is unclear and it is too long.
comments.request: Substantially reduce this chapter.
comments.quote: This descriptive chapter's contribution to the main message is unclear and could be substantially reduced.

comments.issue: The claim about functional capabilities is overstated given only pigment profiles and a few morphological characters.
comments.request: Soften or delete this claim.
comments.quote: The claim about functional capabilities is overstated, as it is based only on pigment profiles and a few morphological characters.

comments.issue: 'Integration' is used although only pigments are analyzed.
comments.request: Clarify this terminology.
comments.quote: Clarify why "integration" is used when only pigments are analyzed.

comments.issue: 'Driven by' implies causality that is not established; only correlation is demonstrated.
comments.request: Avoid causal language or include bioassay support in the main text.
comments.quote: "Driven by" implies causality that is not established in this study—only correlation is demonstrated.

comments.issue: The statement that changes were primarily in phycocyanin contradicts Figure 2, which shows changes in both pigments.
comments.request: Correct the statement to match Figure 2.
comments.quote: The statement that changes were observed primarily in phycocyanin contradicts Figure 2, which shows apparent changes in both pigments

comments.issue: The text discusses trait variation but the figure shows only treatment means.
comments.request: Add supplementary figures with individual cell-level variation or standard errors.
comments.quote: The text discusses trait variation, but the figure shows only mean values per treatment.

comments.issue: 'High light' is stated although low light likely prevailed in early spring in this temperate lake.
comments.request: Confirm and correct the light characterization.
comments.quote: "High light" is stated, but given the seasonal timing and temperate lake setting, "low light" conditions likely prevailed in early spring.

comments.issue: The reference to Figure 6C appears incorrect because no such figure exists.
comments.request: Verify and correct the figure reference.
comments.quote: Reference to "Figure 6C" appears incorrect, as no such figure exists in the main text.

comments.issue: Attribution of pigment deviations to N2-fixing cyanobacteria is speculative without density or composition data.
comments.request: Support this attribution with data.
comments.quote: Attribution of pigment content deviations to N₂-fixing cyanobacteria remains speculative without supporting data on relative densities or species composition.

comments.issue: The expectation for multidimensional trait responses is again not fulfilled in the natural population analysis.
comments.request: Address the unfulfilled expectation.
comments.quote: This reinforces the expectation for multidimensional trait responses that is not fulfilled in the natural population analysis.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the measured particles are cells or small colonies.
comments.request: Clarify the unit.
comments.quote: L650: Clarify whether these are cells or small colonies.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written study; minor comments on justifying functional traits, verifying nutrient limitation, and discussing culture limitations.
strengths: flow cytometry attributes shown to vary across treatments

comments.issue: Justification of the attributes used as functional traits and identification of the best differentiators are lacking.
comments.request: Justify the functional traits and identify the best differentiators.
comments.quote: I think some further justification of the attributes used as functional traits would be useful.

comments.issue: The definition of nutrient limitation is ambiguous and there is no independent evidence that cells were N or P limited.
comments.request: Provide independent evidence that cells were nutrient limited.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to have some independent information or measure that the cells were in an N or P limited state

comments.issue: Long-established cultures may have diverged genomically, limiting their relevance to field studies.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of long-established cultures.
comments.quote: I suggest it is worth discussing the limitations of using cultures which have been established over long timeframes, in the context of their relevance to field studies.

comments.issue: Information about the strain and where and when it was isolated is missing from the Methods.
comments.request: Report the strain's origin and isolation details in the Methods.
comments.quote: it would be helpful to have some more information in the Methods about the strain, and where it and when it was isolated

title: Individual‐Level Trait Responses in Cyanobacterial Populations and Communities

study.system: biological sex definitions; ecology and evolution discourse

editor_summary: Editor acknowledges strong reactions; revision should clarify disputed facts and interpretations, respond to each reviewer, and note that reviewer 1 may publish a Viewpoint on the subject.

reviews.assessment: Agrees with the aims, but questions the framing of the debate, the novelty, the animal focus and the confusing figures.
strengths: agrees with the aims and goals of the authors
specific examples in the action section are useful

comments.issue: The manuscript frames McLaughlin et al. and Sharpe as proposing multivariate definitions, but they offer a critique rather than a new definition.
comments.request: Reconsider the framing of the two definitions as opposed.
comments.quote: But I read McLaughlin et al. not as a new definition of sex, but rather a critique that genetic sex is a weak predictor of bodily and behavioral variation.

comments.issue: The contribution to the current discourse is unclear and overlaps with prior calls for specificity.
comments.request: Clarify the added value and provide more in-depth guidelines.
comments.quote: I am not quite sure what the manuscript adds in terms of a contribution to the current discourse.

comments.issue: The manuscript focuses on animals while plant and fungal sexual diversity is ignored.
comments.request: Make the zoological scope explicit or broaden it.
comments.quote: The manuscript is very focused on animals and discourse in zoology. This should be made explicitly clear because sexual diversity in plants and fungi has been discussed for much longer than in animals

comments.issue: The figures are more confusing than clarifying.
comments.request: Revise the figures to clarify their message.
comments.quote: See more detailed notes below on the figures, which I found to be more confusing than clarifying.

comments.issue: The paragraph misrepresents the gametic definition: Griffiths does not dismiss reproductive approaches and the definition does not fail for hermaphrodites.
comments.request: State clearly which authors are referred to and portray their positions accurately.
comments.quote: This paragraph doesn’t accurately portray the gametic definition of sex. I think the authors need to be very clear about which writer they are referring to.

comments.issue: The claim that the multivariate framework causes reproducibility problems is unsupported.
comments.request: Provide evidence for a reproducibility issue.
comments.quote: This seems like a dubious scenario. Is there evidence that a multivariate framework has actually led to a reproducibility issue?

comments.issue: The problem at lines 115-120 is imagined; gametic proponents argue the definition is anti-essentialist.
comments.request: Reconsider the criticism of the gametic definition.
comments.quote: This paragraph again seems like an imagined problem.

comments.issue: The phrase 'current sex definitions' in Figure 1 is undefined and slippery.
comments.request: Define what 'current sex definitions' means.
comments.quote: What is meant by “current sex definitions”? A lot of what the authors are using to make this table seem to be slippery definitions.

comments.issue: No commonly accepted cross-species definition excludes hermaphrodites, contrary to the slipper limpet example.
comments.request: Point to a definition that excludes hermaphrodites or revise the example.
comments.quote: Can the authors point to a commonly accepted cross-species definition of sex that does not accept hermaphrodites into its framework?

comments.issue: The whiptail lizard example ignores that gametic definitions are relative within species and that unfertilized eggs may not be gametes.
comments.request: Address whether all-female species have definable females.
comments.quote: Whiptail lizards – the gametic definition of sex is relative to other within-species individuals. If the gametes are all one size, can you really define these as females?

comments.issue: Gender is treated as separate from sex, but it is also a social construct used differently across fields and time.
comments.request: Be specific about what is being argued against and acknowledge the history of gender definitions.
comments.quote: like the definition of “sex”, “gender” is also a social construct. It’s used differently by different biologists and has changed over time.

comments.issue: Figure 2's male-classification scenario is unrealistic; no accepted definition would classify a large-gamete individual as male.
comments.request: Revise or remove the imagined scenario.
comments.quote: Would anyone in the field realistically classify the first-row individual as a male if they knew the individual had large female gametes?

comments.issue: The female in Figure 2 is depicted as a darkened version of the male.
comments.request: Depict the sexes accurately.
comments.quote: Also, I’m slightly sad that the female is a darkened version of the male when that’s not what they really look like!

reviews.assessment: Engaging viewpoint but disagrees with its central claim, arguing there is actually broad consensus on gamete-based sex definitions.
strengths: engaging read that challenges the reader

comments.issue: The conclusion that there is no consensus on biological sex is misleading; anisogamy is firmly established among ecologists.
comments.request: Reconsider the central conclusion.
comments.quote: I believe the authors’ conclusion that there is no consensus on the biological definition of sex is misleading.

comments.issue: No examples are given of organisms where the gamete-based definition fails and is actively debated.
comments.request: Provide specific examples of systems where the gamete definition fails.
comments.quote: It would strengthen their argument if they could provide specific examples of organisms for which the gamete-based definition fails, and for which ecologists and evolutionary biologists actively debate on how to determine sex.

comments.issue: What the authors call a trait-based definition is actually a set of operational proxies used to determine, not define, sex.
comments.request: Distinguish operational proxies from conceptual definitions.
comments.quote: In my opinion, what the authors label a “trait-based definition” of sex represents a set of proxies that ecologists and evolutionary biologists use to determine, but not to define sex.

comments.issue: The recommendations and Figure 1 arguments largely repeat existing literature, so the piece's contribution is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what this piece adds beyond previous essays.
comments.quote: Consequently, it is unclear to me what this opinion piece contributes beyond previous essays that have already addressed this debate across other disciplines.

comments.issue: Sperm and egg are animal-specific terms; microgametes and macrogametes would apply across taxa.
comments.request: Use taxonomically general terminology throughout.
comments.quote: The terms sperm and eggs are specifically used for animals. In plants, for instance, pollen and ovules are used instead.

comments.issue: The introduced 'multivariate definition of sex' has no reference.
comments.request: Provide a reference for the multivariate definition.
comments.quote: L65: Please provide a reference for the introduced “multivariate definition of sex.”

comments.issue: No examples are given of studies where a single non-gametic trait proved problematic.
comments.request: Include such examples.
comments.quote: L72: Please include examples of studies that used a single non-gametic trait to define sex, where this approach proved problematic.

comments.issue: Gamete-based definitions of sex predate Roughgarden's work and earlier sources are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge earlier work such as Bateman 1948.
comments.quote: The idea of defining sex based on gametes predates Roughgarden’s work. For example, Bateman (1948) described “the specialization into large immobile gametes and small mobile gametes produced in great excess” as “the primary sex difference.”

comments.issue: The statement at L121-124 contradicts the gametic definition: large-gamete producers are always female regardless of behaviour.
comments.request: Correct the statement using sex-role-reversed examples.
comments.quote: According to the gametic definition of biological sex, an individual producing large gametes is always considered female, regardless of behavior or appearance.

comments.issue: Political statements about human rights seem out of place and insufficiently contextualized for this journal.
comments.request: Contextualize the political remarks more carefully.
comments.quote: political statements such as this seem out of place in a journal aimed at ecologists and evolutionary biologists. Such remarks should be more carefully contextualized.

reviews.assessment: Strongly supportive, important and timely; comments are minor suggestions to strengthen nuance and context.
strengths: important and relevant scientifically and socially
strong parallels to species concept debates

comments.issue: The distinction between primary sex characters and sex-differing phenotypes with intrasexual variation is not made clear.
comments.request: Clarify what is general phenotypic variation versus variation of biological sex.
comments.quote: I think it is worth being clear that there is a difference between primary sex characters that relate to gametic sex and some of the phenotypes that often—though not always—differ between gametic sexes

comments.issue: Guidance on when to use which definitions across taxa and questions is missing.
comments.request: Add language on taxonomic context, proxy strength and variable choice.
comments.quote: I think the authors could potentially add language on taxonomic context for when to use which definitions, the strength of different proxies, or which variables to consider given the question at hand

comments.issue: 'Transgender' is used for animal phenomena although the term refers to human gender identity.
comments.request: Avoid using transgender for these phenomena.
comments.quote: I think it may be worth noting that this term is not nor should it be used to describe these phenomena.

comments.issue: The piece does not call for dialogue and collaboration with queer theorists and scholars.
comments.request: Argue for academic collaboration with queer theorists.
comments.quote: perhaps it would also be good to argue for further dialogue and active academic collaboration/co-authorship with queer theorists and scholars to better navigate the implications of our language and research questions around biological sex

title: There is No Consensus on Biological Sex

study.system: plant species richness; 465 global change experiments, 6832 comparisons

editor_summary: Editor acknowledges the merits and potential but says methodological concerns and discussion/perspective issues need drastic improvement; proposes rejection with the option to resubmit a substantially revised manuscript.

reviews.assessment: Positive overall: well-executed and valuable, but treatment strength is unaccounted for and several claims are overstated.
strengths: data collection and analysis well executed

comments.issue: Treatment strength is not considered and varies non-randomly, so interaction and gradient interpretations are weakly supported.
comments.request: Include treatment strength or clearly discuss the limitation.
comments.quote: the \*strength\* of the treatment (e.g., warming by 1 degree vs warming by 3 degrees), that is not considered in the analysis

comments.issue: Plot size is treated as a treatment when it is actually a limitation.
comments.request: Rephrase plot size as noise, not a treatment.
comments.quote: the text treats plot size as a kind of treatment – which it is not, it is a bug, rather than a feature

comments.issue: The diversity of experimental facilities studied is not introduced.
comments.request: Add a paragraph on the experimental facilities.
comments.quote: I think it would be useful to add a paragraph about the different experimental facilities studied

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits (L70 wording, L78 typo, L118 incomplete sentence).
comments.quote: L70: unpredictably? Change to “many”?

comments.issue: 'Global change manipulative experiments' is an odd phrase.
comments.request: Use a more descriptive phrase.
comments.quote: the term “global change manipulative experiments” sounds a bit weird?

comments.issue: 'Revealed' is too strong a verb.
comments.request: Use a weaker verb.
comments.quote: L113: “revealed” sounds too strong for me (as if revealing a natural law).

comments.issue: Whether the full text of 63k studies was really screened is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the screening process.
comments.quote: did you really reviewed the \*full text\* of 63k studies?

comments.issue: Meta-regression is not explained at first use.
comments.request: Define meta-regression at first use.
comments.quote: L183: please explain the term meta-regression at first use

comments.issue: The lnRR++ notation is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the ++ notation.
comments.quote: L219: please explain the lnRR++ (specifically the ++)

comments.issue: The saturating response in Fig. 4g is an artifact of comparing -100% and +100% on one scale.
comments.request: Reconsider the saturating response interpretation.
comments.quote: Seeing a “saturating” response is pretty logical, when you compare \*reduction\* (up to 100%) and additional water provided on the same scale

comments.issue: The discussion over-interprets relationships and mechanisms given data uncertainty.
comments.request: Tone down the language and shorten the discussion.
comments.quote: Overall, I think the manuscript over-dos it with finding “relationships” and providing mechanistic explanations for what you find in the data.

comments.issue: Negative asymmetric precipitation effects are overstated for a -100% to +100% comparison.
comments.request: Tone down the claim.
comments.quote: “suggest negative asymmetric effects of precipitation anomalies on diversity” just is over the top when you compare -100% precip to +100% precip

comments.issue: The claim that sandy soils alleviate decreased-precipitation impacts is not supported.
comments.request: Soften or remove the claim.
comments.quote: I don’t think that the data really shows that soils > 40% sand “alleviate negative impacts of decreased precipitation”

comments.issue: Plot size is described with mechanistic language instead of as noise; experiment duration also matters.
comments.request: Describe plot size as noise and consider duration.
comments.quote: Just say that plot size introduce a lot of noise to the treatment signal

reviews.assessment: Methods are sound and presentation good, but the story is flat and unappealing and the response-ratio approach ignores community dynamics.
strengths: methods standard for meta-analyses and well executed

comments.issue: The context-dependency conclusion is obvious and uninteresting; the story remains flat.
comments.request: Provide more reasoning for why these responses matter.
comments.quote: which I found somewhat too obvious and relatively uninteresting

comments.issue: Response ratios ignore inherent community dynamics between experiment start and measurement.
comments.request: Integrate initial or repeated richness measurements.
comments.quote: This approach neglects entirely inherent ecosystem and community dynamics over time.

comments.issue: A single response variable limits interpretation; richness is never critically reflected on.
comments.request: Add Shannon diversity, turnover and species-identity analyses.
comments.quote: the inclusion of the Shannon diversity index, which includes also some measure of abundance, in the analysis would considerably strengthen the paper

comments.issue: Data collection description omits field-only criterion, the response variable, and which plants were counted.
comments.request: Describe inclusion criteria and which plants were counted.
comments.quote: The description of data collection and compilation on pages 8 and 9 is not sufficiently detailed.

comments.issue: Distinguishing rain exclusion from water addition is hard to communicate.
comments.request: Compare dry versus wet instead.
comments.quote: Does it make sense to distinguish rain exclusion experiments from water addition experiments ?

title: Global Synthesis Reveals Context‐Dependent Plant Diversity Responses to CO 2 , Climate Change, and Nitrogen

study.system: biodiversity time series; multiple datasets and metrics

editor_summary: Referees find the study interesting and novel but doubt the mechanisms generating fat tails and the generality across metrics; editor asks for goodness-of-fit tests and a null model for biodiversity change.

reviews.assessment: Finds the fat-tailed observation intriguing and novel but doubts the specific Laplace claim and the proposed mechanisms, suggesting a heterogeneity null model.
strengths: fat-tailed observation is intriguing and generally novel

comments.issue: Only a subset of fat-tailed distributions was fitted, so Laplace is the best of this subset rather than the correct distribution.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited set of candidate distributions.
comments.quote: it’s only reasonable to say that the Laplace is the best fitting of this subset, which is not the same as saying that the Laplace is the correct (or even “best” in some broader sense) distribution to describe the data

comments.issue: Many histogram bins in Figure 2 fall outside the 95% confidence intervals, so the Laplace may fail model validation.
comments.request: Comment on the model adequacy test and points outside the intervals.
comments.quote: This would seem to suggest that the Laplace model would fail simple model validation test and is not an adequate description of the data in an absolute, rather than a relative, sense.

comments.issue: The claim that the mechanisms apply equally to multipoint OLS slopes lacks justification or derivation.
comments.request: Derive or justify the extension of the arguments to regression slopes.
comments.quote: This is an important claim to the paper with no justification or derivation, and I think something will need to be included to make this case to readers

comments.issue: It is unclear how the statistical arguments extend to composite community metrics such as Jaccard or BBS S.
comments.request: Explain how the derivations apply to composite metrics.
comments.quote: it is not as clear how these statistical arguments should apply to the more complex composite metrics at the community scale

comments.issue: Heterogeneity among communities could create apparent fat tails through a Gaussian mixture, an alternative to the proposed mechanisms.
comments.request: Test the Gaussian mixture null by subsetting into homogeneous groups.
comments.quote: Rejecting this “Gaussian mixture” null model would require showing that the “fat-tailed-ness” of the data does not decrease if the data are subset to separate groups

comments.issue: The consequences of wrongly assuming normality for confidence intervals and P-values are not stated explicitly.
comments.request: Point out that CIs will be too small and significance overstated.
comments.quote: these CI’s will be too small and investigators will be more likely to report significant changes than the data actually support

comments.issue: The comment that the mean does not exist is a distracting aside for less mathematical readers.
comments.request: Remove or soften the 'mean does not exist' remark.
comments.quote: the comment about the mean “not existing” is not false, but this seems to be an unnecessarily distracting point to make here

comments.issue: The meaning of 'slope' is more complex for nonlinear trends.
comments.request: Clarify what slope means for nonlinear trends.
comments.quote: this is all simple and true if the trend is linear but the meaning of “slope” is more complex if the trend is not a line

comments.issue: The lognormal expectation from multiplicative factors is not mentioned in the main text.
comments.request: Mention the lognormal alternative supported by the central limit theorem.
comments.quote: if the factors that lead to the biodiversity metric are multiplicative rather than additive

comments.issue: The argument for preferring BIC over AIC is unsatisfying and AIC results are not shown.
comments.request: Explain the BIC preference and show AIC results.
comments.quote: this does not seem to be a satisfying argument as to why BIC is in fact the \*better\* choice here (particularly since the AIC results are not even shown)

comments.issue: Why discretized bins were used in the fitting is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the binning procedure in the fitting.
comments.quote: Is this simply a parametric bootstrap aside from the binning procedure? Why were the discretized bins used?

comments.issue: Citations are missing at L219.
comments.request: Add the specific citations at L219.
comments.quote: L219 – these should probably be specifically cited here again

comments.issue: The potentially large finding at L263 is reported without supporting evidence or exploration.
comments.request: Support the claim rigorously or remove it.
comments.quote: it seems odd to report a potentially large finding like this just as something the authors noticed but without other evidence or exploration

comments.issue: The conservation section does not specify what attention or efforts are envisioned.
comments.request: Specify the conservation actions implied.
comments.quote: given that this section is about conservation, what types of attention or efforts are the authors envisioning here?

comments.issue: Figure 1 may refer to an orange line incorrectly.
comments.request: Check the colour reference in the Figure 1 caption.
comments.quote: Fig 1 – should this be “orange line”?

reviews.assessment: Finds the approach novel but wants closer engagement with prior ecological literature, a different interpretation, and clearer presentation.
strengths: relevant contribution if corrected as suggested

comments.issue: Specific ecological literature on this topic is not cited, so findings are not discussed against prior theoretical and empirical work.
comments.request: Cite and discuss the relevant ecological literature.
comments.quote: they did not cite some specific ecological literature analizing this specific topic (see below some suggestions) and thus the do not discuss their findings with respect to previous (theorethical and empirical) findings

comments.issue: The rich-get-richer interpretation of the Laplace distribution is not convincing.
comments.request: Reframe around the full distribution of biodiversity changes.
comments.quote: I do not fully agree with the “rich get richer” interpretation of the Laplace distribution.

comments.issue: The mean is always significantly different from zero by signed rank test despite being close to zero, which needs explanation.
comments.request: Explore the sign, relevance and scale of the location shift.
comments.quote: In every case μ was very close to zero but a simple signed rank test always indicated it was highly statistically significantly different from zero (p<1E-6)

comments.issue: The claim that the mean does not exist is unnecessary and weakens the point about variability.
comments.request: Make the variability point without the philosophical claim.
comments.quote: I think you could make the same point about the relevance of understanding variability or the full shape of the distribution of biodiversty fluctuations without such a claim.

comments.issue: Prior uses of the Laplace for community metrics and theoretical derivations are not cited.
comments.request: Cite Segura et al. 2017, 2019, 2021.
comments.quote: For other uses of Laplace for community metrics and a theoretical derivation applied for community fluctuations

comments.issue: It is unclear why only one year is used for BBS population change.
comments.request: Clearly explain the data used.
comments.quote: Why do you use only one year to population change in the BBS? Please clearly explain the data used here.

comments.issue: The Student's t distribution is said to have a center parameter although it is centered on zero.
comments.request: Explain which distribution was fitted.
comments.quote: The Student’s t distribution is centered on 0 with no center parameter. Please better explain which is the fitted distribution.

comments.issue: Symmetry of the Laplace could be formally tested.
comments.request: Test symmetry following Segura et al. 2021 and 2017.
comments.quote: You can formally test the symmetry of the Laplace (e.g. from Segura et al 2021 and 2017).

comments.issue: Table 2 is hard to read and differences in BIC should be reported.
comments.request: Report delta BIC and provide AIC differences in supporting material.
comments.quote: Please use the difference in BIC as to better understand differences among models. As it stands table 2 is hard to read.

comments.issue: The parameter values of the six models are not visible in Table 1.
comments.request: Show the estimated parameter values in Table 1.
comments.quote: I can not see the values of the parameters of the six models fitted in table 1.

comments.issue: Whether the Subbotin shape parameter confidence interval overlaps one is not reported.
comments.request: Report the confidence interval of the shape parameter.
comments.quote: Do the parameters confidence interval overlap one?

comments.issue: The general hypothesis sentence should focus on the Laplace rather than the Subbotin distribution.
comments.request: Refocus the sentence on the Laplace and its generating mechanisms.
comments.quote: I think it is better to focus on the Laplace instead of Subbotin distribution as it help to focus on specific properties of the distribution

comments.issue: The claim that the pattern holds regardless of metric or aggregation level ignores required conditions on variance distributions.
comments.request: Specify the conditions for the Laplace to emerge.
comments.quote: I do not agree with the generalization “regardless of metric or level of aggregation”.

comments.issue: References on Laplace fits to ecological data and macroecological theory are missing.
comments.request: Cite the suggested examples of Laplace fits and theory.
comments.quote: Please see references below for some examples of the fit of a Laplace to ecological data and a theoretical work relating it to metabolism, body size and other macroecological laws.

comments.issue: The section on prior demonstrations of the Laplace could be expanded with community ecology papers.
comments.request: Expand with Segura and Perera 2019 and Segura et al. 2017, 2021.
comments.quote: Expand this section with the mentioned papers applied to community ecology would be interesting

comments.issue: The rich-get-richer metaphor does not fit, since rich species can also become poor.
comments.request: Drop the metaphor and emphasize the inadequacy of the normal null model.
comments.quote: I can not understand the methapor on the “rich-get-richer” applied to this problem.

comments.issue: 'Outliers' are defined relative to a normal distribution, which the paper argues against.
comments.request: Say 'large fluctuations' instead of outliers.
comments.quote: Outliers are defined assuming a normal, and you are trying to emphasize that trends are not normal.

comments.issue: The Subbotin measure of central tendency is missing from Table 1 without explanation.
comments.request: Present or explain the missing central tendency measure.
comments.quote: Subbotin measure of central tendency is not presented neither explained its absence from the table.

comments.issue: Figure 2 lacks axis labels, unexplained vertical lines and clear dataset identification.
comments.request: Add axis labels, explain the lines and label datasets or metrics.
comments.quote: It is hard to identify the different data sets and metrics in the figure. Add labels or letters.

reviews.assessment: Likes the main message but found the abstract hard to follow and questions why Levy-stable distributions were not considered and how priors versus likelihoods affect inference.
strengths: agrees with the main message that variance structure matters more than the mean trend

comments.issue: The abstract and introduction are difficult to follow and do not provide expected information.
comments.request: Revise the abstract, especially its first sentence.
comments.quote: Somehow surprisingly, I found the Abstract, and, to some extent, the Introduction, difficult to follow.

comments.issue: Levy-stable distributions, which have a CLT-like justification, are not mentioned or considered.
comments.request: Explain why Levy-stable distributions were not fitted.
comments.quote: However, the authors neither mention these distributions nor consider them in their analyses. Why not?

comments.issue: The Laplace is a composite distribution applying when low and high values arise under different conditions, which could justify its use.
comments.request: Consider this interpretation to justify the Laplace fit.
comments.quote: I wonder if this observation could help the author’s justifying the use and the good fit provided by the Laplace distribution?

comments.issue: 'Probability' should be 'probability density' for the continuous Laplace distribution.
comments.request: Use the term probability density.
comments.quote: Given that the Laplace is a continuous (not a discrete) distribution I recommend using the term “probability density” as it is more accurate.

comments.issue: The statement that the mean does not exist is philosophical rather than informative.
comments.request: Replace it with a statement about what the mean fails to capture.
comments.quote: For the purposes of this study, wouldn’t it be more informative to say

comments.issue: The text says Ti is positive or zero but does not mention it can be negative.
comments.request: Correct the description of Ti to include negative values.
comments.quote: “So Ti will be positive if the metric is increasing through time, and zero if it is not changing systematically.” Can’t it be negative?

comments.issue: Total community abundance and log(N) are not defined.
comments.request: Define total community abundance and N.
comments.quote: “Total community abundance”? What is this, the number of individuals, total biomass?

comments.issue: The claim that normal priors make Bayesian models inaccurate overlooks that likelihood misspecification is the main concern.
comments.request: Correct the statement about priors versus likelihoods.
comments.quote: The main concern should be with the choice of the likelihood function.

comments.issue: The Figure 2 axis is described as semi-log but is simply logarithmic.
comments.request: Correct the axis description in the Figure 2 caption.
comments.quote: Figure 2: “semi-log y-axis”, I think the axis is simply logarithmic.

title: Biodiversity Trends Show an Excess of Both Near Stasis and of Very Large Change

study.system: grassland plants; 15-month mesocosm drought and soil-inoculation experiment

editor_summary: Editor: reviewers find the study highly relevant; asks to discuss the 15-month duration limitation and report overall SEM fit before individual paths; two reviewers recommend including functional or phylogenetic relatedness.

reviews.assessment: Ambitious and valuable experiment, but the introduction, concepts and several analyses are unclear enough to question the reliability of conclusions.

comments.issue: "Environmental stress" is undefined, broader than the drought treatment, and may be problematic for drought-adapted plants.
comments.request: Replace "stress" with "drought" or define it clearly.
comments.quote: I would just simply avoid confusion and say ‘drought’ whenever “stress” is mentioned.

comments.issue: Key concepts and calculations (intransitivity, competition balance, dominance, Elo scores, multifunctionality) are poorly explained.
comments.request: Explain the concepts and calculations in the manuscript.
comments.quote: Key concepts (intransitivity, competition balance, dominance) and methods (intransitivity calculations, Elo scores, multifunctionality calculations) remained poorly explained and the manuscript heavily relies on references for even brief explanations.

comments.issue: The abstract term "interaction metrics" is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the term in the abstract.
comments.quote: The term interaction metrics is not clear in the abstract as it is.

comments.issue: The abstract's independence-from-functional-diversity claim lacks an introduced hypothesis.
comments.request: Introduce the hypothesis before this claim.
comments.quote: This sentence comes out of blue when the hypothesis is not introduced before. We do not know why we should expect a dependence.

comments.issue: Competition, facilitation and intransitivity are processes, not diversity metrics, so the claimed complementarity is vague.
comments.request: Clarify the contrast with classical diversity metrics.
comments.quote: This sounds unclear because competition, facilitation and intransitivity are processes and not a diversity metric.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks clear motivation, knowledge gap and hypotheses, making the paper hard to follow.
comments.request: Restructure the introduction around motivation, gap and hypotheses.
comments.quote: The introduction requires better structuring. The motivation and the knowledge gap are not clear.

comments.issue: "Stressor" is introduced at L46 before being defined.
comments.request: Use "environmental change" or "drought".
comments.quote: too early to introduce the term “stressor”

comments.issue: The BEF relationship is a general trend, not specific to drought as stated.
comments.request: Rephrase to match the cited literature (e.g. resilience under drought).
comments.quote: Biodiversity and ecosystem functioning relationship is a general trend and not specifically under drought.

comments.issue: Dividing the environment into biotic and abiotic conflicts with established terms such as environmental filtering and biotic interactions.
comments.request: Use established terminology.
comments.quote: To me, defining the environment as biotic and abiotic is confusing and would be confusing to many community ecologists

comments.issue: The explanations of competitive balance and intransitivity need illustrations and examples.
comments.request: Add illustrations and examples.
comments.quote: These explanations on competitive balance and intransitivity requires illustrations and examples.

comments.issue: Intransitivity is first opposed to competition and later renamed intransitive competition.
comments.request: Harmonise the terminology.
comments.quote: Above intransitivity was opposed to “competition” but now defined as a new term “Intransitive competition”.

comments.issue: Why facilitation and intransitivity are expected to increase under stress is not justified.
comments.request: Justify this expectation.
comments.quote: Not clear why “Nevertheless, because both facilitation and intransitivity are expected to increase under stress”?

comments.issue: How pathogen and coalescence risks of whole-soil inoculation were controlled is not explained.
comments.request: Explain how these risks were controlled.
comments.quote: how did you control for these in your experiment? Especially because you counted the OTUs only on fungi.

comments.issue: Several very long sentences with abstract concepts need simplifying (L47-51, L61-63, L78-80).
comments.request: Simplify these sentences.
comments.quote: Very long sentences with many abstract concepts. Please consider simplifying

comments.issue: Several sentences lack precision or referents (L79 balance/hierarchy, L79 dominance, L80 decline, L80 detrimental, L86 microbial context, L87 em dash, L88 interaction structure).
comments.request: Make these sentences precise and consistent.
comments.quote: “balance and hierarchy of interactions” because now you are also talking about plant-soil interactions please precise

comments.issue: How the experiment was initiated (transplants vs seeds, soil legacy, control of individual numbers) is unclear.
comments.request: Describe how plants were established and how abundances were handled.
comments.quote: It is not clear from the methods section how the plants are planted.

comments.issue: Dominance is based on biomass and may differ if based on abundances.
comments.request: Check whether dominance patterns hold for abundances.
comments.quote: the dominance is also determined by the biomass and it remains to be seen if it would be the same for abundances

comments.issue: Species selection is not justified: whether communities reflect natural co-occurrence and how functionally distinct species are.
comments.request: Justify species selection and show species in functional space.
comments.quote: It is not clear to me how functionally different these species are to start with and if this was considered when the experiment was designed.

comments.issue: The intransitivity calculation is unclear, including how the pairwise competition matrix was obtained and undefined terms at L211.
comments.request: Explain the intransitivity calculation and define the terms.
comments.quote: Overall the calculation of the intransitivity was not at all clear and I needed to look at the cited reference to understand the calculation.

comments.issue: How functional diversity could vary enough in this controlled experiment without measuring plasticity is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the sources of functional-diversity variation.
comments.quote: it is not clear to me how functional diversity could have differentiated to create enough variation to be included in SEM in this controlled experiment especially if the plasticity is not measured

comments.issue: Repeated harvests are used as replicates although time effects and community equilibrium are never quantified.
comments.request: Justify repeated harvests and the equilibrium assumption.
comments.quote: It is unclear to me why the authors harvested the plants multiple times when the effect of time is never quantified.

comments.issue: "Competitive reversal" (L215) and "community properties" (L229) introduce new terminology.
comments.request: Harmonise the terminology throughout.
comments.quote: L215: “Competitive reversal” this term was never introduced before and now, it is confusing.

comments.issue: "Weighted averaging" (L234) and "checking assumption" (L243) lack referents.
comments.request: Specify what is averaged and which assumptions are checked.
comments.quote: L234: “weighted averaging” of what?

comments.issue: The Elo rating system is not explained.
comments.request: Briefly explain the Elo rating system.
comments.quote: L244: “Elo rating system” I do not know what is this and it is not clearly or briefly explained.

comments.issue: The purpose and hypothesis linked to the neighbour-productivity calculation at L250-251 are unclear.
comments.request: Explain what this calculation tests.
comments.quote: It is not clear to what (or which hypothesis testing) is this related and why it is quantified?

comments.issue: "Sensitivity analysis" at L252 is unspecified.
comments.request: Specify what the sensitivity analysis tests.
comments.quote: L252: “Sensitivity analysis” of what?

comments.issue: The Results are too abstract and should be restructured to illustrate changes in plant-plant interactions.
comments.request: Restructure the Results to clarify the interaction changes.
comments.quote: I suggest a restructuring of the results section by illustrating better the changes in plant-plant interactions.

comments.issue: Species interaction matrices and their treatment responses are not shown.
comments.request: Show the species interaction matrices.
comments.quote: it is a little disappointing to not see the species interaction matrices and how they change with the treatments

comments.issue: The SEM's R2 for competitive balance is very low, raising questions about the reliability of the conclusions.
comments.request: Address the low explained variance.
comments.quote: Overall, in SEM, the R2 for competitive balance is quite low. How do you explain that and how reliable are the whole conclusions then?

comments.issue: "Shifting the competitive balance towards stronger competition/facilitation" is overly complex.
comments.request: Say "increased competition/facilitation" instead.
comments.quote: The overall usage of “shifting the competitive balance towards stronger competition/facilitation” is overly complex instead of saying “increased competition/facilitation”.

comments.issue: "Environmental variation" at L284 is imprecise.
comments.request: Be explicit whether drought is meant.
comments.quote: “environmental variation” do you mean drought? Please be more explicit.

comments.issue: The claim at L281-283 about increased relevance of interaction metrics is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify this statement.
comments.quote: Overall, drought – when combined with whole-soil inoculation – increased the relevance of plant–plant interaction metrics in shaping ecosystem functioning (Fig. 2A, B).

comments.issue: The discussion does not address generalizability or links to more observational studies.
comments.request: Discuss broader results and generalizability.
comments.quote: What is missing for me is a discussion on broader results, how the results relate to other studies especially more observational ones and how these experiments can inform us on the general trends?

comments.issue: Figure 1 repeats Fig. 2 and does not clarify the hypothesised relationships or setup.
comments.request: Link each arrow to hypotheses and references and cite the figure more often.
comments.quote: I think Figure 1 does not improve our understanding of the hypothesized relationships and the experimental setup.

comments.issue: Fig. 2B y-axis direction is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain what negative and positive values mean.
comments.quote: There should be helpers for the y axis of the panel B. Example, what does a negative/positive value mean for competitive balance: more or less competition?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether Fig. 4 values pool all experimental treatments.
comments.request: Clarify the treatments shown.
comments.quote: It is not clear if these values are from all experimental treatments.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and well-organised; comments are mostly minor and focus on methodological detail.

comments.issue: Whether additional monocultures were inoculated is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the inoculation status of monocultures.
comments.quote: Were these additional monocultures inoculated or not and why?

comments.issue: Plant establishment details (seed vs transplant, sterilisation, replacement of dead plants) are missing.
comments.request: Provide these experimental details.
comments.quote: Were plants germinated from seed? Did they start in the mesocosms or were they transplanted in after germination?

comments.issue: The claim that soils were low in microbial diversity lacks justification and quantification details.
comments.request: Justify the claim and describe OTU quantification.
comments.quote: How do you know the soils were low in microbial diversity?

comments.issue: Autoclaving soils for 24 hours is excessive and unusual.
comments.request: Verify or clarify the autoclaving protocol.
comments.quote: Were the soils really autoclaved for 24 hours? That seems excessive and not really feasible.

comments.issue: The "full range of soil biota" claim is not supported by AM-fungi-only data.
comments.request: Soften the claim.
comments.quote: You say ‘the full range of soil biota’ but figure S1 just shows AM fungi.

comments.issue: The growth assay lacks detail, including how many individuals per soil sample were grown.
comments.request: Describe the growth assay.
comments.quote: It would be nice to have a bit more detail about the growth assay. How many individuals were grown in each soil sample?

comments.issue: The multiple-threshold approach is not explained, hindering interpretation of Fig. S4.
comments.request: Explain the multiple-threshold approach.
comments.quote: Please provide more detail about what the multiple-threshold approach entails.

comments.issue: The statement at L261-262 applies to Fig. 2B but not 2A.
comments.request: Reconcile the statement with the figure.
comments.quote: This statement is clearly relevant to Fig. 2B but not really apparent in 2A.

comments.issue: Fig. 3A and 3B references at L288-290 are swapped.
comments.request: Swap the figure references.
comments.quote: I think the references to figs. 3A and 3B are mixed up here (3B shows competitive balance and 3A shows intransitivity).

comments.issue: The inclusion of dominant species in the SEMs is only reported in the Results.
comments.request: State this in the methods section.
comments.quote: You should state that dominant species were included in the SEMs in the methods section, not just here in the results.

comments.issue: Differential nematode effects on forbs and grasses are not clearly a negative plant-soil feedback.
comments.request: Justify the feedback claim or reword it.
comments.quote: I’m not sure I would consider differential effects of nematodes on forbs and grasses to be a negative-plant soil feedback.

comments.issue: Grammar edits: em dash placement at L87 and "Decrease" at L396.
comments.quote: L396: ‘Decrease’ should be ‘decreased’

reviews.assessment: Very supportive; suggests engaging the indirect-effects literature, accounting for phylogeny, and discussing generalizability.
strengths: strong step for integrating abiotic and biotic factors into BEF
great integration across factors and levels of organisation

comments.issue: The indirect-effects literature is underrepresented.
comments.request: Add context from indirect-effects work (Ohgushi, Bailey et al. 2009, Langley & Megonigal 2010).
comments.quote: I did think the authors could have done more to represent that field a bit.

comments.issue: The non-independence of species is not accounted for; results can change when hierarchical genetic structure is considered.
comments.request: Account for phylogenetic relatedness of the species.
comments.quote: there is a lot of emerging data that clearly show how the strength and direction of results can change by accounting for hierarchical genetic structure

comments.issue: Results come from a single community representing one site, limiting generalizability.
comments.request: Discuss the limits to generalizability.
comments.quote: it is difficult to know how generalizable the results are as they are focused on a community, representative of a site in an ecosystem

title: Plant Competitive Balance and Intransitivity Shape Ecosystem Multifunctionality in Grasslands Under Drought

study.system: temperate forest beetles; replicated forest heterogeneity experiment

editor_summary: Reviewers see many useful contributions; editor suggests enriching the functional ecological perspective and strengthening community ecology discussion of beetle interactions.

reviews.assessment: Impressive experiment with robust, highly relevant results; suggests simplifying the paper by removing the phylogenetic dimension.
strengths: novel combination of aggregation and complexity manipulations
clear combination of theory and experiment

comments.issue: The introduction is only accessible to readers who already know metacommunity archetypes deeply.
comments.request: Make the introduction more accessible.
comments.quote: the current version (especially the introduction) requires readers who understand the archetypes/metacommunity theory deeply, and this should be made more accessible for a general readership

comments.issue: Relative abundance, functional and phylogenetic dimensions are not justified and add no novelty or robustness.
comments.request: Justify or remove the FD/PD and abundance dimensions.
comments.quote: I do not believe the inclusion of this is bringing any novelty or robustness to the conclusions.

comments.issue: PD adds nothing beyond taxonomic diversity and rests on taxonomy as a phylogeny surrogate.
comments.request: Remove the phylogenetic analyses.
comments.quote: PD is not bringing anything potentially new to the results.

comments.issue: Species identification resolution, trait selection rationale and PD construction need more detail.
comments.request: Document identification resolution, trait rationale and PD construction.
comments.quote: What is the taxonomic resolution of the identifications—100% at the species level? Why were those traits selected?

comments.issue: No figures show correlations among the biodiversity dimensions.
comments.request: Add correlation figures among diversity dimensions.
comments.quote: I suggest adding some figures showing the correlations between different biodiversity dimensions (TD, FD, PD alphas, betas, gammas, and q = 0, 1, and 2).

reviews.assessment: Strong praise for integrating metacommunity theory with empirical data; no criticisms raised.
strengths: timely integration of metacommunity theory with empirical data
well aligned with Ecology Letters scope

reviews.assessment: Impressive well-replicated study with clear results and sound conclusions; only two very small suggestions.

comments.issue: The title sounds like tree veteranization rather than structural heterogenization.
comments.request: Revise the title to reflect heterogenization.
comments.quote: Title “Old-growth attributes by chain-saw” may be misleading, as it sounds like tree veteranization to me, to create wounds and microhabitats.

comments.issue: Conceptual Figure 1 is very complex and the gamma/alpha/beta division is hard to understand.
comments.request: Simplify Figure 1.
comments.quote: The figure is very complex. The yellow triangle above the figure (“meta-analysis” ) of gamma-diversity and its division to alpha and gamma-diversity components is difficult to understand.

comments.issue: 'Archetype' in the text and 'paradigm' in the figure are used inconsistently.
comments.request: Harmonize the terminology.
comments.quote: in the text you use term “archetype”, but in the figure you have term “paradigm”. To make it clearer for the reader, I would harmonize this.

reviews.assessment: Important topic with valuable results; asks for clearer wording and more specific beetle community results.
strengths: valuable new results with conservation applications

comments.issue: The beetle community results lack detail: traits of the 60 new species and absences versus controls are not reported.
comments.request: Report the identity/traits of new species and absences.
comments.quote: The manuscript notes that 60 species appeared on the experimental plots, but it provides no information on their traits, or whether certain species were absent compared to the control plots.

comments.issue: A result is mentioned in the Introduction.
comments.request: Move or remove the result from the Introduction.
comments.quote: Lines 185–187: Why is this result mentioned in the Introduction?

comments.issue: It is unclear how mass-effect can increase gamma diversity if the species pool is unchanged; H1 and Fig. 1 may need reformulation.
comments.request: Explain and reformulate H1/Fig. 1.
comments.quote: I am wondering how an increase in α-diversity (and a concurrent reduction in β-diversity) through a mass-effect within the examined area (as outlined in Figure 1) can lead to an increase in γ-diversity.

comments.issue: The description of 22 districts with 9 or 15 experimental patches is confusing given 11 controls.
comments.request: Clarify the district and patch description.
comments.quote: Shouldn’t there be only 11 experimental districts, since the other 11 represent controls?

comments.issue: The opening of the environmental and spatial difference section is confusing.
comments.request: Rewrite the opening statement.
comments.quote: why do they begin the section “Environmental and spatial difference” with the rather confusing statement

comments.issue: The gamma/alpha/beta accounting is unclear; a 60-species gamma increase seems inconsistent with a 30-species patch increase.
comments.request: Explain the diversity partitioning and report disappearances.
comments.quote: I would expect that if γ-diversity increased by 60 species compared to the control, then the total increase in new species at the patch scale should also be 60 species (rather than 30, as the authors report).

comments.issue: Effects of structure on species distributions in control districts suggest controls may not be homogeneous.
comments.request: Address whether control forests were homogeneous.
comments.quote: doesn’t this suggest that forest structure in the control districts was not actually homogeneous?

comments.issue: The proportions of rare, common and dominant species and their change are not reported.
comments.request: Report community proportions and their change.
comments.quote: readers would also appreciate knowing what proportion of the community was composed of rare, common, and dominant species, and how this proportion changed as a result of structural heterogenization

title: Forest Heterogeneity by Chain Saw: How Between‐Patch Variation in Old Growth Attributes Changes the Metacommunities of Beetles

study.system: 41 stream sites; nutrient diffusing substrata and biofilm biomass

editor_summary: Both reviewers are generally positive; they ask for more detail on metal chemistry and anoxia in the NDS, reject single imputation of missing data, temper conclusions given snapshot sampling of few streams, and clarify co-limitation and taxonomy.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and interesting, with two main requests: detail the metal chemistry and anoxia of the NDS, and replace single imputation with multiple imputation.
strengths: topic of great interest to aquatic ecologists

comments.issue: The chemical form of metals added to the NDS and anoxia-driven sorption/desorption could confound comparisons with the natural water column.
comments.request: Discuss metal forms and anoxic sorption effects as potential confounding factors.
comments.quote: I would like to see more information on the chemical form of the metals added to the NDS and if those forms differ from what may be naturally available in the water column.

comments.issue: Missing data were handled with single median imputation, which is ill-advised and understates uncertainty.
comments.request: Use multiple imputation instead of single imputation.
comments.quote: I urge the authors to not use single imputation for the missing data. Single imputation of missing data with a central tendency (median) is common, and unfortunately accepted, despite being very ill-advised

comments.issue: The role of 'substitution' at line 86 is not explained (whether it is good or bad).
comments.request: Clarify the role of substitution for readers.
comments.quote: It may help readers to clarify the role of substitution here.

comments.issue: The deployment time of year of the NDS is not reported.
comments.request: State when the NDS were deployed and whether all were deployed in the same period.
comments.quote: What time of year were the NDS deployed? Were they all during the same period?

comments.issue: It is unclear what the median was computed over and whether the RF interpretation changes with mean imputation.
comments.request: Specify the imputed quantity and test sensitivity to the imputation choice.
comments.quote: The median of what exactly? Does your interpretation of the RF model change if you use the mean for missing data?

comments.issue: The statement that DRP concentrations were 'high' lacks context; 5 or 10 ug/L would not usually be considered high.
comments.request: Provide context for the 'high DRP' statement.
comments.quote: I think this sentence warrants context for ‘DRP concentrations were high’. I doubt many people would consider 5 or 10 ug/L as high.

reviews.assessment: Novel and well-executed experiment, but snapshot sampling of few streams and coarse taxonomy limit the strength and representativeness of the conclusions.
strengths: relatively novel and highly relevant question

comments.issue: A relatively small number of streams sampled at a single time point limits the generality of the conclusions.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limited sample basis when drawing conclusions.
comments.quote: the study is based on a relatively small number of streams (from a statistical perspective, not from a logistic perspective of course) measured in a single time point

comments.issue: The conclusions drawn in the discussion are stronger than the data support.
comments.request: Temper the conclusions, including those at L300-302.
comments.quote: Consequently, the conclusions that I would draw from this study are not as strong as those that the authors draw in the discussion

comments.issue: The snapshot design leaves the temporal stability of limitation and representativeness of the findings unknown.
comments.request: Discuss limitation in other seasons and the temporal stability of results.
comments.quote: What do we know about the limitation in other seasons or the temporal stability of limitation?

comments.issue: Only a subset of elements was tested; adding more nutrients and metals would likely increase co-limitation frequency and change conclusions.
comments.request: Discuss the potential of other elements to limit primary producers.
comments.quote: It is likely that we would see a higher frequency of co-limitation if we expanded the number of tested elements.

comments.issue: The predictive model performed poorly for N, P and iron, especially for predicting non-limitation, and was not improved.
comments.request: Adjust or develop the model to improve performance.
comments.quote: The performance of the predictive model was overall poor for N, P, and iron.

comments.issue: Limitations of the predictive model and of the conclusions derived from it are not discussed.
comments.request: Add a discussion of model limitations and their consequences.
comments.quote: I miss a discussion of its limitations and of those of the conclusions derived from it.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the model predictors cover the same time period as the experiments, which could explain poor model performance.
comments.request: Clarify the temporal coverage of the predictor data.
comments.quote: Do the data used for the predictive model cover the same time as the experiments, or are they from a different time point, or averaged over the year?

comments.issue: Taxonomic responses are limited to very coarse groups based on the benthotorch data.
comments.request: Analyse community composition at higher taxonomic resolution and with a second method.
comments.quote: Taxonomic responses are limited to very coarse taxonomic groups (i.e., based on the benthotorch data).

comments.issue: Microscopic identification data were collected but are not reported.
comments.request: Report and use the microscopic data to evaluate methodological limitations.
comments.quote: Samples for microscopic identification have been described but their data are not reported (L175/176).

comments.issue: Cyanobacteria are treated as algae at L48 and elsewhere.
comments.request: Correct the treatment of cyanobacteria as algae.
comments.quote: L48 and elsewhere: cyanobacteria are not algae as implied here.

comments.issue: Per-element limitation frequencies imply more multi-element limitation than the reported co-limitation counts, and the discrepancy is unexplained.
comments.request: Rephrase the results and explain the discrepancy in the methods.
comments.quote: the frequency of limitation to N, P, and Fe (i.e., x out of 40 streams) suggest that several streams showed limitation to more than one element

comments.issue: Co-limitation and the classification model are not explained in the main text, which refers to a supplementary figure caption.
comments.request: Explain co-limitation and the classification scheme in the main text.
comments.quote: Co-limitation needs to be explained clearly in the main text. Fig. 2 refers to a caption of a supplementary figure, which is insufficient for such an important definition.

comments.issue: The scale of the Fig 1C and 1D heatmaps is unclear, and model predictions could be used for heatmaps of all elements.
comments.request: Explain the heatmap scales in the caption and consider model-based heatmaps.
comments.quote: the scale of the heatmaps in Fig. 1C and Fig. 1D is unclear and needs to be better explained in the caption

title: Anaemic Streams: Iron and Essential Trace Metals Frequently Limit Primary Producer Biomass

study.system: grass community assembly; Cedar Creek biodiversity experiment biomass data

editor_summary: All reviewers liked the topic but found the introduction's theory and mechanisms lacking; two flagged symmetric light competition. Address coexistence measurement, other-model comparisons and applicability to other systems.

reviews.assessment: Interesting, thought-provoking redundancy among mechanisms, but the introduction, niche-overlap variable and generality discussion need work.

comments.issue: The introduction lacks depth on the ecological mechanisms tested and their motivation.
comments.request: Move the l.137 paragraph up and expand the literature context.
comments.quote: I felt it lacked depth on the ecological mechanisms being tested, and their motivation. The paragraph starting l.137 could be moved higher up

comments.issue: Competition and niche differentiation terminology conflates distinct mechanisms.
comments.request: Use explicit terms for nutrient competition and spatiotemporal niche differentiation.
comments.quote: The terminology around competition and niche differentiation (e.g. l.487-8) is confusing.

comments.issue: The niche overlap variable needs justification; root overlap and temporal activity calculations are unexplained.
comments.request: Justify and explain how niche overlap, root overlap and activity periods are calculated.
comments.quote: The "niche overlap" variable seems a little rough to me, and could do with some further justification and explanation in the Methods and possibly Discussion.

comments.issue: Height overlap assumes symmetric light competition and averaging overlaps weakens the variable.
comments.request: Model asymmetric light competition and reconsider the averaged overlap measure.
comments.quote: Given asymmetric competition for light, this seems unlikely, and that averaging the overlap of height, roots, and phenology will weaken how informative this variable is likely to be.

comments.issue: Model performance relative to other mechanistic models, especially Cedar Creek models, is not assessed.
comments.request: Compare explanatory power with other models of this system.
comments.quote: I would be curious to know how the explanatory power of this model performed relative to other mechanistic community models addressing individual mechanisms, and especially relative to other models from Cedar Creek.

comments.issue: Little discussion of how the approach transfers to other, non-experimental communities.
comments.request: Discuss required modifications and how system features affect predictive power.
comments.quote: I would have appreciated more discussion of how well the approach would apply to other communities, what modifications or other processes might be included in other systems

comments.issue: Calling population growth rates a mechanism of community assembly is conceptually wrong.
comments.request: Specify dispersal-colonization trade-off as the mechanism.
comments.quote: i think it would be better to specify "dispersal-colonization trade-off" as the mechanism; "population growth rates" is not a mechanism of community assembly, but underlies the three previous mechanisms.

comments.issue: The wording at l.68 should specify observations of biomass or abundance.
comments.request: Specify "observations of biomass [or abundance]".
comments.quote: l.68 specify "observations of biomass [or abundance]"

comments.issue: The statement at l.80-8 is a straw man and unnecessary as motivation.
comments.request: Remove or rework this motivation.
comments.quote: I personally feel that this statement is a bit of a straw man and isn't really needed as a motivation for this study.

comments.issue: The trait-mechanism link is not explained at l.83 where it first appears.
comments.request: Spell out the logic linking traits to mechanisms.
comments.quote: The link between traits and mechanisms makes sense in the context of the model proposed here, but isn't clear to the reader at this point in the MS - please spell-out the logic here.

comments.issue: The relation and advantages of this approach relative to existing model types are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify how the model fits the described taxonomy.
comments.quote: Im asking because the relation/advantages of the current approach relative to existing ones isn't clear.

comments.issue: The notation for the sum over R* terms is incorrect and Bj is not specified.
comments.request: Fix the equation notation and specify Bj.
comments.quote: I think the term "sum[all R\*j < R\*i]" specify Bj somehow in this equation (mathematical notation doesn't look correct to me)?

comments.issue: 'Non-tuned' is used without definition.
comments.request: Define what non-tuned means.
comments.quote: what do the authors mean by "non-tuned"? I was also unsure about this when described in the Methods and Results.

comments.issue: 'Vanishingly few' is vague and should be quantified.
comments.request: Clarify whether there are any.
comments.quote: l.445 - "vanishingly few" - are there any?
