comments.request: Present and discuss community-level (per-area) rates to avoid misreading future ecosystem functions.
comments.quote: As shown in Fig S6, once standardized per surface area, the rates are very different, with no gain in either photosynthesis nor nutrients uptake.

comments.issue: The choice to standardize functions per biomass rather than per surface area is not justified.
comments.request: Argue why biomass-standardized rates were chosen.
comments.quote: I would appreciate if the authors could argue why the choice of using biomass standardized rates was made. Is it to be able to get more broad insights (not limited to this specific ecosystem)?

comments.issue: The conclusion discusses diverse ecosystems but gives no implications for the Mediterranean ecosystem studied.

comments.issue: The dates of the historic tile time points are not given.

comments.issue: Typo 'modesl' for 'models' at line 200.

comments.issue: The conclusion lacks a sentence summarizing the results and Mediterranean insights.

comments.issue: The reported 108% biomass reduction under ambient versus 0-3% under extreme seems incorrect.

comments.quote: Line 262 to 266 - Are these correct? A 108 % reduction in biomass under ambient conditions vs just 0 to 3 % under extreme conditions?

comments.issue: The subheading claims trade-offs although trade-offs were not measured.
comments.request: Remove 'trade offs' from the subheading.
comments.quote: technically you didn't measure trade offs, you measured a bunch of proxies and will look for potential trade offs by comparing the results, which will come in the discussion. Remove the "trade offs" from this sub heading.

comments.issue: Lines 269-271 are hard to follow and inconsistent in structure.
comments.request: Make the statements clearer and parallel.
comments.quote: Line 269 to 271 - a bit hard to follow. Try to be clearer in your statements. The first sentence is good, but the second one needs to follow the same structure to be easier to read

comments.issue: The calcification decrease reflects loss of function through species loss, not a trade-off between functions.
comments.request: Discuss the distinction and whether dissolution reflects algal death.
comments.quote: This indicates that it is not a trade-off between functions but a loss of function due to the loss of the species that provide that function, the calcified species.

comments.issue: Line 276 needs an explicit comparison sentence for clarity.
comments.request: Add the suggested comparison wording.
comments.quote: Line 276 - add "In comparison to the extreme treatment, gross photosynthetic rates were consistently

comments.issue: The dark respiration pattern at line 278 should be described specifically.
comments.request: Describe whether there was no change over time or between treatments.
comments.quote: Line 278 - OK for dark respiration, but perhaps describe the pattern that was seen, i.e. no change in time or between treatments - be a bit more specific.

comments.issue: Nutrient and photosynthesis results are associated too early in the results.
comments.request: Describe nutrient results independently and leave comparisons to the discussion.
comments.quote: I would rather you didn't associate these rates until the discussion. Just describe here the nutrient results independently from the photosynthesis results

comments.issue: The response array is not complex; the chosen functions are interrelated and responded clearly.
comments.request: Avoid calling the responses complex.
comments.quote: Line 310 to 311 - I wouldn`t call this a complex array of responses.

comments.issue: The ecosystem function responses are not nuanced or complicated.
comments.request: Remove the nuanced/complicated characterization.
comments.quote: Line 312 - I don't see how the EF responses are nuanced or complicated, they are quite clear.

comments.issue: The main result shows no trade-offs, just calcifiers doing poorly and fleshy algae thriving.
comments.request: State the main result plainly without trade-off framing.
comments.quote: this is indeed your main result, and it has no indication of trade-offs or anything like that - just that simply calcified algae don't do well but fleshy algae does

comments.issue: The results do not show differential impacts across marine systems; only three assumed communities from one system were measured.
comments.request: Tone down the hyperbole and stay faithful to the results.
comments.quote: Line 317 to 319 - No, these results do not highlight differential impacts of OA across marine systems - you only measured the change in three assumed communities from a specific system when moved from low pCO2 to high pCO2

comments.issue: Only Kroeker et al. 2011 is cited for the calcification response; more references exist.
comments.request: Add more references, e.g. Brown et al. 2017.
comments.quote: Line 322 - Surely there are more references than just Kroeker et al 2011 by now? Brown et al 2017 in GCB perhaps.

comments.issue: It is unclear at lines 323-325 whether the authors refer to their results or the literature.
comments.request: Be specific about which results are being discussed.
comments.quote: Sometimes I get the feeling you spend a lot of time talking about the literature rather than talking about your results. For example, line 323 to 325 is not clear if you are referring to the results from this study

comments.issue: Calcifiers are described as having a narrow niche, but the sensitivity comes from calcification, not niche breadth.
comments.request: Correct the niche argument.
comments.quote: Outside of the OA context I wouldn't say that being a calcifier is a particularly narrow niche in the marine realm. It isn't their niche or its size that makes them sensitive here, it is specifically that they calcify.

comments.issue: Lines 325-332 are repetitive about OA reinforcing an OA shift.
comments.request: Rewrite this paragraph to make the simplification result obvious.
comments.quote: this part is a bit repetitive - you describe an OA shift then in the next sentence say that OA further reinforces this shift, that OA already made.

comments.issue: The grassland example at lines 337-340 is redundant and lacks marine examples.
comments.request: Replace with relevant marine/OA examples or remove.
comments.quote: Lines 337 to 340 - are there no marine examples? I'm sure there must be. I also think that this part is a bit redundant.

comments.issue: The -omics discussion at lines 352-362 takes too much space without supporting data.
comments.request: Cut the -omics discussion to a passing mention.
comments.quote: Line 352 to 362 - I don't think that this discussion on -omics is necessary enough to take such space. Perhaps in a passing mention.

comments.issue: 'Multifaceted implications' overstates two weak examples of benefits from fleshy algal systems.
comments.request: Reduce the claim to the two examples actually supported.
comments.quote: Line 364 - "multifaceted implications"? You provide two examples of the benefit of a fleshy algal system

comments.issue: The lines 369-372 sentence is meaningless because the results are neither complex nor beyond expectations.
comments.request: Stop the sentence at 'dominated by macroalgal communities'.
comments.quote: Line 369 to 372 - This is a fancy sounding sentence but is ultimately meaningless, your results are not complex or multidimensional and they absolutely did not go beyond the expected declines in EF and abundance, nor can your interpretations.

comments.issue: The conclusion never states whether trade-offs were found and is vague and generic.
comments.request: Rewrite the conclusion to answer the question and state the advances.
comments.quote: 4.4 Conclusion - no mention of if you found trade offs! The conclusions should give the answer to your title and abstract, but here they do not.

comments.issue: The discussion consists of five long subsections with unclear focus.
comments.request: Use shorter paragraphs with clear topic sentences.
comments.quote: the discussion needs some work, and a lot of toning down-refocusing. I find a lot of the information presented would go well in a literature review

title: Unravelling Marine Benthic Functioning Shifts Under Ocean Acidification

study.system: soil mites; male phenotype, population recovery after heat stress

editor_summary: Reviews are consistent: the experiment is well designed and executed, but framing and hypothesis development need substantial work, and sexual selection is portrayed too simply (intersexual conflict vs intrasexual competition).

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-replicated experiment, but the strength-of-selection framing is inappropriate and the introduction and discussion need refocusing.
strengths: well replicated and unique experimental approach
well suited for a high-impact synthetic outlet

comments.issue: The manipulation of a sexually selected male phenotype is equated with manipulating sexual selection strength, obscuring the treatment.
comments.request: Refocus the manuscript on the effects of the male phenotype.
comments.quote: the authors manipulated male mating morph - a sexually selected phenotype. However, they consider their treatment to be a manipulation of sexual selection strength.

comments.issue: The introduction meanders and lacks a clearly stated hypothesis and predictions.
comments.request: Rewrite the introduction around a clear hypothesis and predictions.
comments.quote: The introduction would benefit from a focused rewrite and inclusion of a clearly stated hypothesis and related predictions that can be evaluated with the evidence collected.

comments.issue: Justification based on gaps in the literature is weak; the study needs an argument based on the merit and novelty of the hypothesis.
comments.request: Provide a more compelling, merit-based motivation.
comments.quote: Thus, justifying any research effort with claims of ‘gaps in the literature’ are rather impotent.

comments.issue: Manipulating male morph frequency changes the mode of sexual selection, not its strength, and strength was never measured.
comments.request: Describe the manipulation as the mode of selection.
comments.quote: It’s not clear to me that manipulating the frequency of male morphs can be described as a change in the strength of sexual selection.

comments.issue: The manuscript frequently switches between male morph and selection strength contexts, making it inconsistent.
comments.request: Rectify or minimize the switching and use the mode-of-selection context.
comments.quote: The frequent switching of study context—from sexually selected morph (fighter vs scrambler) to selection strength (strong vs weak)—needs to be rectified or minimized

comments.issue: Line 40 does not introduce why sexual selection and eco-evolutionary dynamics matter for population recovery.
comments.request: Add a sentence introducing this idea.
comments.quote: It’d be nice to have a sentence justifying or introducing the idea that sexual selection and eco-evolutionary dynamics are relevant for population recovery.

comments.issue: 4 line-level copy edits (a comma and several word choices).
comments.quote: Line 271: replace ‘higher’ with ‘larger’ or ‘greater’

comments.issue: Le Galliard 2005 and 2008 are not cited in the introduction although they are relevant cases of sexual selection effects on demography.
comments.request: Cite Le Galliard 2005, 2008 in the introduction.
comments.quote: see Le Galliard - 2005, 2008 for additional cases of sexual selection effects on demography

comments.issue: The phrase positive or negative effects on demography is too vague about the demographic effects.
comments.request: Be more specific about the demographic effects.
comments.quote: I think it’s important here to be more specific about the effects on demography.

comments.issue: The link between population size and rate of adaptation is asserted without explanation or citation, and the male mortality-extinction claim is unsupported.
comments.request: Explain or cite the link and support the mortality claim.
comments.quote: Explain the link between population size and rate of adaptation. Or at least cite a paper to support this claim.

comments.issue: The sentence on lines 99-104 is too long.
comments.request: Abbreviate or divide the sentence.
comments.quote: This sentence is too long and needs to be abbreviated or divided.

comments.issue: Objectives ii and iii seem redundant; what objective ii seeks to satisfy is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify and distinguish the objectives.
comments.quote: Objectives ii and iii seem awfully similar. Is ii, just asking about the magnitude of population decline immediately after the perturbation?

comments.issue: Genetic variance confounding the population size treatments is dismissed at line 158 before the issue is articulated.
comments.request: Raise and address the genetic variance confound explicitly.
comments.quote: Perhaps raise the issue of genetic variance confounding your population size treatments before you dismiss it?

comments.issue: Response variables should be introduced before the modeling approach and predictors.
comments.request: Reorder this part of the methods.
comments.quote: It seems more logical to introduce your response variables before your modeling approach and predictor variables?

comments.issue: The paragraph on lines 241-245 does not belong in its current section.
comments.request: Move the paragraph to methods or discussion, or delete it.
comments.quote: This paragraph seems like it should be moved to the methods, the discussion, or deleted.

reviews.assessment: Impressive, thought-provoking experiment; asks for clearer treatment of intersexual conflict, the stability concept and several details.
strengths: thought-provoking and a joy to read

comments.issue: Intersexual conflict (fighter males harming females) fits the male-biased sex ratio but is treated speculatively and only late, while intro and methods focus on intrasexual conflict.
comments.request: Address intersexual conflict early and throughout the results.
comments.quote: Several of the findings seem consistent with the idea that fighter males also harm females (as indicated by the male-biased sex ratio), yet the introduction and methods focus almost exclusively on intrasexual conflict among males.

comments.issue: Which male morph mated with females in the post-heat-stress fecundity assays is not stated.
comments.request: State whether fighter or scrambler males were used in the assays.
comments.quote: this raised a question about which males mated with females in the fecundity assays after heat stress (l. 191) : were these fighter or scrambler males?

comments.issue: Population stability is repeatedly invoked without defining whether it means within-replicate fluctuations over time or among-replicate variability.
comments.request: Define stability and specify how it was quantified.
comments.quote: Another point needing clearer definition or careful explanation is the concept of "population stability," which is mentioned repeatedly.

comments.issue: Broader ecological implications for natural populations are somewhat lacking.
comments.request: Discuss broader ecological implications for natural populations.
comments.quote: This may also help in providing context to discuss further broader ecological implications for natural populations, which I find is somewhat lacking as is.

comments.issue: The evolutionary part of eco-evolutionary dynamics is unclear because the examples concern ecological effects of traits.
comments.request: Clarify the evolutionary component.
comments.quote: Could you clarify the evolutionary part of “eco-evolutionary” dynamics as all the subsequent examples seem to refer to the ecological effects of traits and not so much the evolutionary aspects.

comments.issue: Lorch 2003 and Flintham 2003 are relevant but not cited at line 86.
comments.request: Cite Lorch 2003 and Flintham 2003.
comments.quote: it would be relevant to cite Lorch 2003 and Flintham 2003

comments.issue: Flintham 2003 is relevant but not cited at line 93.
comments.request: Cite Flintham 2003.
comments.quote: it would be relevant to cite Flintham 2003

comments.issue: The expectation about growth rates omits sexual conflict between males and females.
comments.request: Consider sexual conflict among males and females.
comments.quote: What about sexual conflict among males and females ?

comments.issue: Population density was not controlled, so population size and conflict intensity may be confounded.
comments.request: Control for or discuss density as a confound.
comments.quote: Did you also control for densities ? Population with greater densities may be expected to show heightened conflict so that here population size and conflict may be confounded.

comments.issue: How CV was defined and measured is not specified.
comments.request: Clarify the definition and measurement of CV.
comments.quote: L. 217 Please clarify how you defined and measured CV.

comments.issue: The reason for computing realized growth rate over four time steps is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the four-time-step growth rate.
comments.quote: Why is the realised growth rate over four time steps (N\_{t+4}/ N\_{t}) ?

comments.issue: The more female-biased sex ratio in the weak-selection treatment may reflect fighter males killing females, which is not addressed.
comments.request: Explain whether male harm drives the sex ratio result.
comments.quote: “weak sexual selection resulting in a more female-biased sex ratio than the strong sexual selection treatment” is that because fighter males kill females ?

comments.issue: The lower number of males to females in the scrambler treatment may also be due to male harm.
comments.request: Clarify whether male harm explains this pattern.
comments.quote: “the scrambler treatment had a lower number of males to females” Again : due to male harm ?

reviews.assessment: Interesting, well-written study, but the manipulation concerns male aggression rather than sexual selection strength, with statistical and context questions.
strengths: well-structured introduction giving a good overview of theory
elegant experimental design and great model system

comments.issue: The manipulation alters only one pre-copulatory male trait, yet is framed as changing net sexual selection strength, ignoring post-copulatory selection and sexual selection in females.
comments.request: Narrow or justify the sexual-selection-strength framing.
comments.quote: the reasoning that the experimental design manipulated net sexual selection strength is not as straightforward as it is presented here

comments.issue: The fecundity assay counted only eggs, so whether eggs were fertilized or viable is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify whether counted eggs were fertilized or viable.
comments.quote: in the fecundity assay only the eggs were counted, right? This means it is not clear if these are fertilized or viable eggs.

comments.issue: There was no control group for the heat stress treatment, so CV changes may reflect general temporal drift rather than heat stress.
comments.request: Add or discuss a no-heat-stress control.
comments.quote: I am wondering if there should not have been a control group for the heat stress treatment

comments.issue: The procedure for selecting the final models is unclear.
comments.request: Describe the model selection procedure.
comments.quote: I am unsure about the procedure to select the final models (see comment below).

comments.issue: With only 16 replicates and 4 per treatment, models including interactions risk overfitting.
comments.request: Justify model complexity given the small sample size.
comments.quote: I am afraid, that the limited sample size (16 replicates with 4 per treatment) might lead to overfitting, if interactions are included in the models.

comments.issue: The generation time and the number of generations observed are not reported.
comments.request: Report generation time and number of generations observed.
comments.quote: I think it would be very valuable to know the generation time of the study system. Currently it is unclear to me how many generations were observed

comments.issue: Males were constantly replaced from the stock population, making inferences about actual selection strength difficult.
comments.request: Address how male replacement affects selection inferences.
comments.quote: males were constantly replaced during the experimental period with males from the stock population, which makes inferences about actual selection strength difficult

comments.issue: Repeated measures on populations risk pseudoreplication because the time component is not accounted for; variance explained by population ID is not reported.
comments.request: Account for time in the random effects and report variance explained.
comments.quote: I seems to me, that for most models, repeated measures from the populations were entered, which has the risk of pseudo-replication

comments.issue: Stating that sexual selection significantly affected the sex ratio is an interpretation, not a neutral description, especially as cannibalism drives it.
comments.request: Describe the result neutrally and separate cannibalism from sexual selection.
comments.quote: the Authors say in Line 259 that ‘sexual selection significantly affected the sex ratio’. I think this is an interpretation of the result, but not a neutral description.

comments.issue: The discussion lacks limitations, including the unclear diet stress and male condition differences between fighter and scrambler males from the stock.
comments.request: Discuss these limitations.
comments.quote: I was missing a discussion of the limitations. For example, the unclear diet stress (that was not the focus of the study) and the question of male condition in fighter vs scrambler males

comments.issue: The manipulation is not placed in the species' ecological context; natural fighter frequency is much lower, so the scenario may be artificial and wider conclusions compromised.
comments.request: Place the experiment in the species' ecological context.
comments.quote: This makes the presented experimental scenario potentially quite artificial, I think. This could compromise the wider conclusions drawn by the Authors

comments.issue: Incomplete recovery is a matter of the time frame examined; no populations crashed, so slower recovery may be more accurate.
comments.request: Rephrase incomplete recovery as slower recovery.
comments.quote: I would argue that this is a matter of the time frame examined. None of the populations completely crashed, right?

comments.issue: Toxic ejaculates is too specific among otherwise broad examples; a broader term with the example would be better.
comments.request: Use sexual conflict as the broader term.
comments.quote: Maybe change this to ‘sexual conflict’ as a broader term and maybe mention toxic ejaculates as an example?

comments.issue: The phrase have population dynamic consequence is unclear.
comments.request: Rephrase to affect population dynamics.
comments.quote: Not quite sure what the Authors mean here.

comments.issue: The type of environmental stressor is not specified at line 122.
comments.request: Specify the stressor.
comments.quote: L122: ‘an environmental stress’ – Specify the type of stressor?

comments.issue: The pilot study information in the Supplement is not cross-referenced at line 157.
comments.request: Point readers to the pilot study in the Supplement.
comments.quote: Mention that we can find the information about the pilot study in the Supplement?

comments.issue: How many fighter males actually developed in the experimental populations is not reported.
comments.request: Report how many fighter males developed.
comments.quote: Also, how many fighter males actually developed in the experimental populations? Is this zero or only very few?

comments.issue: Replacing the same percentage of males is not explained in practice.
comments.request: Specify how male replacement was carried out.
comments.quote: ‘replacing the same percentage’ – Could you specify what this means in practice? Were all of the males replaced over time?

comments.issue: The choice of 40 degrees C for 90 hours is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the heat stress temperature and duration.
comments.quote: How was this temperature and duration chosen? Is there anything known about the effects of this?

comments.issue: Lines 183-185 are unclear about the constraints and generation time for readers unfamiliar with the system.
comments.request: Add context for non-specialist readers.
comments.quote: What are the constraints here? It is the generation time? I think more context is needed here for a reader not familiar with the system to follow this reasoning.

comments.issue: The wording in the after heat stress period needs revision.
comments.request: Revise the wording.
comments.quote: ‘in the after heat stress period’ – Revise wording?

comments.issue: The total number of females tested is not given.
comments.request: Report the total number of females tested.
comments.quote: Maybe give the total number of females tested too?

comments.issue: When the females were counted is not stated.
comments.request: State when counting occurred.
comments.quote: ‘and counted them’ – When? Directly after the 16 hours?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether population dynamics vial refers to all 16 experimental vials.
comments.request: Clarify what population dynamics vial refers to.
comments.quote: ‘population dynamics vial’ – These are just all the experimental vials (n = 16), right?

comments.issue: How non-significant terms were dropped from models is vague and full models are not presented.
comments.request: Describe the dropping order and present full models.
comments.quote: Does that mean non-significant terms were dropped from the models? In what order? I think more details are needed here.

comments.issue: It is confusing that fighters were replaced in the scrambler treatment after the methods state populations had virtually no fighters.
comments.request: Clarify the replacement of fighters with scramblers.
comments.quote: I am confused here. Did the Methods not say that the populations had virtually no fighters, as the diet was too limited (L171)?

comments.issue: Sex ratio results are not translated into actual values such as percentage females.
comments.request: Report sex ratio as percentages.
comments.quote: Could you please add what this means in actual SR (e.g., give the percentage females)?

comments.issue: Were more likely to recover misstates the test, which concerned the degree or speed of recovery, not whether recovery occurred.
comments.request: Rephrase to match what was tested.
comments.quote: I don’t think this is what was tested here. If I don’t misunderstand, here the degree (or speed) of recovery was tested and not if the population recovered or not

comments.issue: Females may bias the sex ratio of their offspring in response to the unnaturally high frequency of fighter males.
comments.request: Consider female-driven sex ratio bias.
comments.quote: Could females also have biased the SR of their offspring production in response to the unnaturally high frequency of fighter males?

comments.issue: Positive feedback is used although the OSR change is not described as directional and the feedback loop is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify or replace the positive feedback terminology.
comments.quote: Why is this termed ‘positive feedback’? The change in OSR is not described as directional here.

comments.issue: Strong sexual selection is said to arise only from exaggerated weaponry and male-male conflict, which is too narrow.
comments.request: Broaden the statement about sources of strong sexual selection.
comments.quote: I would argue that strong sexual selection can not only arise from ‘exaggerated weaponry and aggressive male-male conflict’.

comments.issue: The claim that treatments were established by replacing the wrong male morphs misdescribes the procedure; scramblers were also replaced.
comments.request: Correct the description of treatment establishment.
comments.quote: This is not quite true, if I understood the Methods correctly. Also, scramblers were replaced in the scrambler treatment to make up for the low number of developing fighters, right?

comments.issue: Figure 1 omits population size and therefore 8 replicates.
comments.request: Add population size to Figure 1.
comments.quote: But could the population size also be added here? Otherwise, 8 replicates are missing in this representation.

comments.issue: Panel labels are inconsistently placed above or below panels across figures.
comments.request: Place panel labels consistently on top.
comments.quote: The panel labels are inconsistent (A, B, C etc.) either on top or below. I would also put them on top, but I any case consistently.

comments.issue: Raw data points in Figures 3-6 are too small and invisible inside same-colored boxes.
comments.request: Increase point size and use different colors or alpha for boxes.
comments.quote: But these are too small to see and are invisible in the boxes as they have the same color. Please increase size and use a different color or alpha for the boxes.

comments.issue: Figure 3B and 3D lack a 1:1 sex ratio reference line and an explanation of SR values.
comments.request: Add a dotted 1:1 line and explain the SR values.
comments.quote: Could it be helpful to add a dotted line for a 1:1 SR? And maybe explain in the legend how to interpret the SR values?

comments.issue: The consistent male bias across all populations is unexplained (normal, resource limitation, or cannibalism?).
comments.request: Explain the male bias in all populations.
comments.quote: I am wondering why there seems to be such a male bias in all of the populations. Is that normal?

comments.issue: The number of data points in Figure 4 and how CVs were calculated are unclear.
comments.request: Specify the CV calculation in the methods.
comments.quote: I am confused about the number of data points here. Should this not be four per treatment?

comments.issue: Figures do not indicate significant differences between groups.
comments.request: Indicate significant differences, for example with letters.
comments.quote: I think it would be helpful to indicate significant differences between groups. Maybe by letters above?

comments.issue: The Figure 6A y-axis label is imprecise and may be read as a 100% decline.
comments.request: Relabel the axis as proportional decline.
comments.quote: I think the y-axis label is not precise. This is the proportional decline, as described in the legend, right?

title: Sexual Selection Associated With an Aggressive Male Phenotype Reduces Population Size and Hinders Population Recovery After Heat Stress

study.system: pine sawfly larvae; group-size manipulation experiments

editor_summary: Editor notes reviewer concerns: the free-loader definition may be problematic, sex differences need justification, speculation should be avoided, and selfish versus cooperative behaviour should be discussed in relation to kin structure.

reviews.assessment: Clever, carefully executed experiments with strong data, but the free-loader interpretation and some speculative discussion need better justification.
strengths: data are strong and experiments carefully executed

comments.issue: Characterising non-contributors as free-loaders is problematic when large groups need less defence.
comments.request: Justify the free-loader definition and discuss cheater definitions when benefits are nonlinear.
comments.quote: the characterisation of non-contributors as free-loaders is potentially problematic if there is simply less sticky-stuff required in large groups

comments.issue: Hypotheses are not framed in the abstract and introduction; facultative versus obligate distinction and sex differences are unexplained.
comments.request: Frame the specific hypotheses in the introduction.
comments.quote: The abstract and the introduction could do more to frame the specific hypotheses being tested

comments.issue: Significance of the U-shaped defensive posture and comparison with fluid-based defence is unclear.
comments.request: Explain what to take from the U-shape comparison.
comments.quote: I didn’t really understand what I was supposed to do with information about the U-shape defensive posture. What is the significance of the comparison with fluid-based defence?

comments.issue: Lines 72-75 misstate the tragedy-of-the-commons argument about resource competition and cooperation.
comments.request: Clarify and correct this point.
comments.quote: The prevailing argument (based on the tragedy of the commons) is that intensive resource competition is reduced by cooperation not increased.

comments.issue: Paragraph on Lines 266-282 is hard to follow, jumping between posture and fluid defence.
comments.request: Restructure this paragraph.
comments.quote: This paragraph was hard to follow. I think because it jumps between the U-shaped posture and fluid-based defence

comments.issue: Several discussion points are overly speculative (fluid as signal; female pre-adaptation) and drift from what the data can address.
comments.request: Remove or temper the speculative interpretations.
comments.quote: Some of the discussion points are a bit of a stretch and detract from the interesting simple points to be made about the results

title: Group Size Dependent Selection for Cooperation Versus Freeloading in Collective Chemical Defence

study.system: temperate semiarid grassland; 7-year N x warming experiment and global meta-analysis

editor_summary: Editor says reviewers agree the topic is important and results interesting, but a major revision is needed: methods and meta-analysis clarifications, introduction rethinking with mechanistic hypotheses, Figure 2 questions, baseline SOC data, and meta-analysis and discussion points.

reviews.assessment: Relevant and timely but needs a rewritten introduction with mechanistic hypotheses, baseline SOC data, and a more critical meta-analysis.
strengths: combination of field experiment and global meta-analysis

comments.issue: The introduction lists factors instead of developing testable, mechanistically informed hypotheses.
comments.request: Develop mechanistic hypotheses.
comments.quote: I recommend a substantial rewrite of the Introduction to move beyond listing various factors that influence soil organic carbon (SOC).

comments.issue: The rationale for measuring POM and MAOM fractions is not justified mechanistically.
comments.request: Justify the SOC fraction measurements.
comments.quote: The Introduction would benefit from a clearer justification for measuring these specific SOC pools.

comments.issue: One SEM spread over three panels is not useful; divergent POM and MAOM pathways should be tested.
comments.request: Compare POM and MAOM pathways.
comments.quote: I'm not sure how useful it is to present the results of one structural equation model (SEM) in three separate panels.

comments.issue: Baseline SOC data are needed to quantify change over time; a large baseline loss is implied.
comments.request: Provide baseline SOC data.
comments.quote: Are there any data on SOC concentration at the start of the experiment to help quantify SOC changes over time?

comments.issue: Soil variables come from uncertain global maps, likely biasing the importance ranking toward MAT.
comments.request: Account for soil map uncertainty.
comments.quote: Many of the environmental variables used (e.g., pH, CEC, texture, bulk density, and soil P) were derived from global soil maps, rather than field measurements.

comments.issue: Key mediators such as extracellular enzyme activity are omitted from the model.
comments.request: Consider missing mediators.
comments.quote: The model omits variables that have been identified in prior work as key mediators of SOC response to N enrichment, such as extracellular enzyme activity.

comments.issue: Previous meta-analyses conflict about the MAT-SOC relationship and are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss the contrasting findings.
comments.quote: Some do not support the relationship between SOC response and MAT (e.g., Chen et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2011), while others do (e.g., Liu et al., 2023).

comments.issue: The discussion digresses into organic fertilization and inorganic carbon instead of the warming-N interaction.
comments.request: Focus the discussion on interactions.
comments.quote: The discussion contains a lot of commentary on organic fertilization and soil inorganic carbon, which, although important, are somewhat misaligned with the manuscript's main theme.

comments.issue: The claim that little mechanistic research exists on N and warming interactions is too strong.
comments.request: Soften the claim and cite prior work.
comments.quote: The claim that there's little mechanistic research on N and warming interactions is too strong.

comments.issue: Two line-level proofreading edits (mismatched phrase, land-use type).
comments.quote: The manuscript would benefit from a careful and thorough proofreading throughout

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the 0.2% SOC increase is relative or absolute.
comments.request: Clarify the units.
comments.quote: please clarify whether this is a relative or absolute increase

reviews.assessment: Interesting, novel and well-written; several clarifications are needed, mainly on the meta-analysis and data sharing.

comments.issue: The meta-analysis infers warming effects from sites at different temperatures, unlike the direct warming experiment.
comments.request: Discuss the space-for-time mismatch.
comments.quote: in the meta-analysis, the effect of warming was demonstrated by experiments with N additions at sites with different temperatures, not results of the warming-by-N experiments

comments.issue: Calculation equations for the meta-analysis are not given.
comments.request: Add the calculation equations.
comments.quote: Please clarify the specific calculation equations (e.g., the weighted mean response ratio) in Supplementary

comments.issue: Publication bias is not evaluated.
comments.request: Add Rosenthal's fail-safe number.
comments.quote: I would also include the Rosenthal’s fail-safe number to evaluate the impact of publication bias on the meta-analysis results

comments.issue: Fig. 5 and supplementary Fig. 9 could be combined.
comments.request: Combine the figures.
comments.quote: Therefore, I would combine the two figures as Fig.5 in the main text.

comments.issue: Only the R script, not the dataset, is available.
comments.request: Share the dataset.
comments.quote: The authors should provide both the R script and the dataset in this database to allow verification of the statistical analyses.

title: Warming Reduces the Positive Effect of Nitrogen Addition on Soil Organic Carbon in Grasslands

study.system: birds; ALAN meta-analysis of 36 studies across 30 species

editor_summary: Reviewers find it strong and timely; they ask for transparency on light intensities and effect-size sign changes, a clearer introduction, discussion of low-study categories, and softening of the life-history conclusion given first-clutch and body-size issues.

reviews.assessment: Well-conducted and valuable meta-analysis with only suggestions to streamline the introduction, clarify methods and qualify low-study results.
strengths: valuable contribution to the ALAN literature

comments.issue: The introduction is too long and should focus on background, known effects, the knowledge gap and the study aim.
comments.request: Streamline the introduction around the four essential elements.
comments.quote: The introduction is rather long. It would benefit from focusing more directly on the essential background

comments.issue: Field versus laboratory studies may differ in effect sizes and are not tested as a moderator.
comments.request: Test study environment as a moderator or discuss it as a heterogeneity source.
comments.quote: it would be interesting to test whether study environment (field vs. lab) influences effect sizes. If feasible, this could be explored as a moderator or discussed as a potential source of heterogeneity.

comments.issue: Very low ALAN levels are still constant and additive light, and effects occur at 0.1 lux, which the 0.2 lux cutoff obscures.
comments.request: Note the nuance about very low light levels.
comments.quote: ALAN at very low levels (e.g., 0.1 lux) is still fundamentally different from natural nocturnal light because it is constant and additive.

comments.issue: A statement contradicts the point on page 8, line 18.
comments.request: Clarify the contradiction.
comments.quote: This statement appears to contradict the point on page 8, line 18. Please clarify to avoid confusion.

comments.issue: It is unclear which "both groups" are meant.
comments.request: Specify which groups are referred to.
comments.quote: Please specify which "both groups" you are referring to.

comments.issue: How 171 studies were reduced to 36 is not explained.
comments.request: Describe the exclusion process.
comments.quote: How were the studies reduced from 171 to 36? A short explanation of the exclusion process

comments.issue: The first model combines biologically and statistically different response variables, which is questionable.
comments.request: Remove the combined model or justify it more strongly.
comments.quote: the usefulness of the first model that combines very different response variables is questionable

comments.issue: Species representation and potential taxonomic bias (are all species diurnal?) are not summarised early.
comments.request: Summarise species representation in the Methods or Results.
comments.quote: Are all included species diurnal? Given potential taxonomic and ecological bias (e.g., toward a few common model species), it would be helpful to provide a brief summary of species representation.

comments.issue: Many Table 4 categories have very low study numbers but are interpreted with too much emphasis.
comments.request: Reduce emphasis and explicitly note low confidence for these categories.
comments.quote: Many of the categories are represented by very low study numbers. It would be appropriate to reduce emphasis on these results and explicitly note the low confidence when presenting or interpreting them.

comments.issue: Figure 2 does not show the number of independent studies behind each estimate.
comments.request: Add study numbers to Figure 2.
comments.quote: Please add the number of independent studies contributing to each estimate

reviews.assessment: Well-conducted and interesting, but the introduction, the 'avian performance' construct, the life-history conclusion and grey-literature coverage need major work.

comments.issue: The introduction reads as disconnected facts rather than building toward a defined knowledge gap and conceptual advance.
comments.request: Restructure the introduction around what is known, what is equivocal and the gap.
comments.quote: paragraphs 2 and 3 read as lists of disconnected facts about ALAN and birds, rather than building toward a defined knowledge gap

comments.issue: The umbrella construct 'avian performance' adds no conceptual clarity and is a retrospective grouping of disparate variables.
comments.request: Drop the vague umbrella term or define it mechanistically.
comments.quote: the umbrella construct of "avian performance" does not add conceptual clarity. It appears to be a retrospective grouping for disparate response variables rather than a mechanistic or theoretical framework.

comments.issue: The claim that ALAN does not affect life-history traits ignores the body-size effect and first-clutch-only reproductive data.
comments.request: Acknowledge the limitation and soften the life-history conclusion.
comments.quote: The statement that ALAN did not affect life-history traits seems too strong. The meta-analysis found effects on adult body size

comments.issue: Grey literature was not searched, risking publication bias.
comments.request: Justify the exclusion and discuss potential publication bias.
comments.quote: It is standard practice to include searches of grey literature in ecological meta-analyses to mitigate publication bias.

comments.issue: The inclusion criteria are not articulated clearly (e.g., must all criteria be met?).
comments.request: Clarify the inclusion criteria with examples.
comments.quote: The inclusion criteria require clearer articulation: Must all criteria be met for a study to be included?

comments.issue: It is not stated whether effect sizes from the same paper were treated as non-independent.
comments.request: Report multilevel or robust variance modelling for non-independence.
comments.quote: The manuscript should clarify whether effect sizes from the same paper were treated as non-independent (e.g., multilevel or robust variance modelling).

comments.issue: Population origin (urban vs rural) and historical light exposure are ignored, yet adaptation could explain the responses.
comments.request: Test or discuss historical exposure and adaptive responses.
comments.quote: There is no information on the origin of study populations (urban vs. rural). Populations with historical exposure to ALAN may exhibit adaptive responses

comments.issue: The background literature is taxon-biased toward marine examples.
comments.request: Use 'invertebrates' and add non-marine examples.
comments.quote: I would make this 'invertebrates' and add some non-marine examples. In general the background literature is very taxon biased.

comments.issue: A reference is missing at Page 3, Line 24.
comments.request: Add references.
comments.quote: Line 24: references required

comments.issue: 'Interfaces' is unclear at line 18.
comments.request: Clarify what 'interfaces' means.
comments.quote: 18: 'interfaces'? Not clear what you mean here.

comments.issue: The causal direction is reversed: circadian disruption is presented as affecting melatonin rather than being caused by it.
comments.request: Correct the direction of the melatonin relationship.
comments.quote: you are suggesting circadian disruption affects melatonin secretion, rather than circadian disruption being caused by disruption to melatonin signalling.

comments.issue: The comparison with mammals is outside the study's focus.
comments.request: Consider removing the mammal comparison.
comments.quote: I am not sure you need to compare to mammals as it is not a focus of your investigation.

comments.issue: 'Endocrinological challenges' is undefined in this context.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant.
comments.quote: 33: what are endocrinological challenges in this context?

comments.issue: 'Ecological outcomes' is too vague.
comments.request: Replace the vague term.
comments.quote: 22: 'ecological outcomes' is too vague to be useful

comments.issue: The text does not highlight the need for this meta-analysis.
comments.request: Strengthen the justification for the meta-analysis.
comments.quote: 27-29: this needs work to highlight the need for your MA

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 38-40 is unclear and the origin of the number 27 is unexplained.
comments.request: Edit the sentence and explain the 27.
comments.quote: 38-40: This sentence needs editing for clarity. Where did the 27 come from?

comments.issue: 'Studies' should be 'papers' because papers can contain multiple studies.
comments.request: Use 'papers' where appropriate.
comments.quote: I would refer to 'papers' rather than studies, as papers can have multiple studies within them.

comments.issue: The high heterogeneity is not acknowledged or interpreted.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of heterogeneity for generality.
comments.quote: The manuscript would benefit from an explicit acknowledgement that the high heterogeneity observed in the dataset is not unexpected

comments.issue: The result is called 'remarkable' when it is merely consistent.
comments.request: Tone down the wording.
comments.quote: 33: not really 'remarkable', just consistent.

comments.issue: Using signed rather than absolute time-disturbance values may misestimate the impact of ALAN.
comments.request: Consider using absolute values of time disturbance.
comments.quote: Is there a reason why you did not take the absolute values of time disturbance, so that the impact of ALAN on traits could be estimated more accurately, ie with temporal disturbance patterns?

comments.issue: Reviews on sexual selection and urbanisation are not cited.
comments.request: Cite these reviews.
comments.quote: There are some nice reviews on sexual selection and urbanisation, these should be cited.

comments.issue: The claim of accelerated aging contradicts the admission that gene expression may not translate to organismal ageing.
comments.request: Clarify the ageing statement.
comments.quote: The authors state that 'Adults displayed accelerated aging', but then later in the same sentence say that whether gene expression translates to accelerated organismal ageing is unknown.

comments.issue: Upregulation of reproductive maturation during both day and night is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify what is meant.
comments.quote: how can 'reproductive maturation' be upregulated during the day and night. It is not clear what you mean but this.

reviews.assessment: Timely, thorough synthesis with a valued integration of mechanisms, but needs transparency on light intensities and sign changes plus more literature comparison.

comments.issue: The context and real-world spread of the ALAN intensities used are not reported transparently.
comments.request: Report the lux levels used and how widespread they are in nature.
comments.quote: the authors need to be more transparent about the context of the ALAN intensities used in their meta-analysis and provide readers with some context of how widespread lux values are across space

comments.issue: Findings are not compared with relevant large-scale studies that fell outside the study criteria.
comments.request: Compare and contrast findings with these omitted studies.
comments.quote: I also see some opportunities for the authors to compare and contrast their findings with those in the literature from some studies that appear not to have met the study criteria and perhaps they were unaware of

comments.issue: The changing of effect-size signs is unexplained, so readers cannot judge whether it is reasonable.
comments.request: Explain why and when effect-size signs were changed.
comments.quote: the changing of effect size signs when suspected to be negative needs more details so readers can understand why this was done and for what conditions

comments.issue: Large-scale multi-species studies (Senzaki et al. 2020; Wilson et al. 2021) that support the claim are not cited.
comments.request: Cite these supporting studies.
comments.quote: There are some large-scale, multi-species studied that seem to more directly support the claim in this sentence

comments.issue: Ferraro et al. (2020) appears to be cited in both clauses, implying birds both did and did not change.
comments.request: Check the citation and clarify the claim.
comments.quote: As written, it appears as though Ferraro et al. (2020) might be mistakenly cited in both clauses of this sentence. Did birds both not change and also lose weight with ALAN?

comments.issue: The leap from results to biodiversity conservation is boilerplate and skips intervening steps.
comments.request: Temper the conservation claim.
comments.quote: This feels very boiler plate. There are a lot if really important intervening steps to really rounding out our understanding of real costs of ALAN besides leaping to biodiversity conservation.

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits: 'among' vs 'between' (P4 L47), wrong transition (P10 L55), and Table S3 vs Table 6 (P12 L16-17).
comments.quote: P10 L55: "In contrast" does not seem like the right transition here.

comments.issue: Large-scale studies using remotely-sensed light (nanowatts) were omitted from the search.
comments.request: Explain whether spectral simplification to lux caused the exclusion.
comments.quote: I'm surprised by the omission of several large-scale studies that used remotely-sensed measurements of light, typically expressed in nanowatts.

comments.issue: Averaging migratory tendency into categories discards inter-specific variation.
comments.request: Consider the hand wing index as a continuous migratory tendency measure.
comments.quote: The authors might consider using the hand wing index (HWI) as a continuous measure of migratory tendency rather than averaging away inter-specific variation with the categories used.

comments.issue: The sentence at P7 L20-22 is unclear about the nine authors contacted.
comments.request: Clarify whether the nine authors did not reply.
comments.quote: P7 L20-22: This is sentence is unclear. Is it that 9 authors contacted did not reply?

comments.issue: Sign flipping is not explained; it is unclear why original effect sizes were not already negative.
comments.request: Explain and justify each sign change.
comments.quote: The change of the sign of the effect size is really strange and really needs more explanation.

comments.issue: It is unclear how directional influence on traits can be assessed when many effect sizes were assigned negative.
comments.request: Explain how direction was assessed after sign assignment.
comments.quote: P9 L17-20: This seems related to the last comment. How can one assess the directional influence on the trait when you assigned many to be negative?

comments.issue: A negative trend for open-habitat species conflicts with forceful statements that habitat has no effect.
comments.request: Be more nuanced about habitat effects, considering captive studies.
comments.quote: This apparent trend for a negative influence on open habitat species should guide the authors to be a bit more nuanced in their forceful statements in the discussion that habitat had no effect.

comments.issue: The distribution of lux values in captive versus wild settings is not shown.
comments.request: Add density plots or histograms of lux values for the two settings.
comments.quote: it would be extremely helpful to provide a figure that displays lux values considered in these two settings. Density plots or histograms would be very useful.

comments.issue: It is unclear how lux variation affects models combining lab and field studies, and whether an interaction was needed.
comments.request: Consider a lab-by-field interaction in the models.
comments.quote: How does this variation in lux potentially influence models where lab and field were used together? Should there have been an interaction?

comments.issue: Kempenaers et al. (2010), direct evidence for fitness benefits of earlier activity, is not used.
comments.request: Cite Kempenaers et al. (2010) here.
comments.quote: I believe Kempenaers et al. (2010) provides direct evidence for the link between earlier activity due to ALAN and male benefits through extra-pair paternity.

comments.issue: The habitat interpretation needs more nuance given studies finding habitat variation.
comments.request: Add nuance about habitat effects (Senzaki et al.; Wilson et al.).
comments.quote: This might be a place where more nuance on the interpretation of the influence of habitat should be considered

comments.issue: The longer-exposure result is not placed in the context of residents versus migrants.
comments.request: Discuss the finding relative to resident and migrant exposure durations.
comments.quote: Can the authors place this in the context of the differences between residents and migrants?

comments.issue: The P18 L14-17 statement is too strong given limited life-history and trait coverage and small sample sizes.
comments.request: Soften the statement.
comments.quote: This statement seems too strong. The study has a limited consideration of life history strategies and functional traits

comments.issue: The lack of a phenology link is not reconciled with broader literature; only five species were included.
comments.request: Reconcile the result with Senzaki et al. and the broader literature.
comments.quote: Can the authors reconcile their lack of a link to phenology to evidence from the broader literature? Only five species were included for this response.

title: Artificial Light at Night Consistently Impacts Avian Physiology and Behaviour: A Meta‐Analysis

study.system: birds; global collision and innovation databases

reviews.assessment: Intriguing question and analysis, but the innovation-rate measure is noisy and research effort should be included; the interpretation and explanation of the positive relationship remain unconvincing.

comments.issue: Research effort, recommended as a covariate for the noisy innovation-rate measure, was dropped in favour of abundance.
comments.request: Explain why research effort was dropped and include it in the models.
comments.quote: Given that Lefebvre is fairly clear in his paper that (log transformed) research effort be included, I wonder why this was dropped in favour of abundance?

comments.issue: Research effort may inflate innovation reports and is not controlled for.
comments.request: Reanalyse with research effort as a covariate, dropping abundance if collinearity is high.
comments.quote: I suggest that the authors include it in a reanalysis as a covariate, dropping abundance if collinearity is high.

comments.issue: Raw collision-event data underrepresent rare species, so analyses of raw data are not very informative.
comments.request: Tone down the opening discussion sentences based on raw data.
comments.quote: Therefore, if the y axes in Fig 1 report raw collision events, I am unconvinced that the analyses of raw data is very informative

comments.issue: No plausible explanation is proposed for why innovation should be detrimental in collisions.
comments.request: Propose and explore plausible explanations for the detrimental association.
comments.quote: the authors do not propose a plausible explanation of why innovation, which previously has been correlated to fitness gains in novel environments, should be detrimental in the case of collisions

comments.issue: The argument that a generalist lifestyle necessarily exposes birds to more threats is unconvincing and lacks nuance.
comments.request: Make the generalist argument more nuanced.
comments.quote: I’m unconvinced by the argument that a generalist lifestyle necessarily exposes a bird to more threats.

comments.issue: The claim at L346 that rarer towers and masts minimise innovation opportunities is not justified.
comments.request: Provide a clearer justification for this argument.
comments.quote: I don’t understand the argument that rarer towers and masts minimise opportunities to be innovative and thus less likely to be the sites of collisions. This needs a clearer justification.

comments.issue: Differences in strikes among structure types may relate to bird body size.
comments.request: Consider body size when comparing collisions across structure types.
comments.quote: I wonder if differences in strikes between objects may also relate to body size of the bird.

reviews.assessment: Interesting and readable, but the general conclusion is misleading given the hazard-specific results, the spatial interpretation is preferred, and the statistical approach needs rethinking.

comments.issue: The final dataset context (blind spots, species used, dataset overlap) is not summarised for readers.
comments.request: Add summaries and supplemental information about the final data.
comments.quote: Since the data stem from monitoring or citizen science programs, I felt that summaries and supplemental information about the final data could be useful

comments.issue: The general conclusion that more innovative species suffer more collision mortality is not supported by the hazard- and metric-specific secondary analyses.
comments.request: Revise the conclusions to reflect the nuance of the secondary results.
comments.quote: The main conclusion is that more innovative species have more collision-driven mortality (L31 and elsewhere). This is a very general conclusion that I am not sure the authors are able to make given the secondary analyses

comments.issue: A spatial explanation (species near buildings collide more and also use novel resources there) may fit better than behavioural plasticity being maladaptive.
comments.request: Place less emphasis on the maladaptive interpretation and consider a spatial explanation.
comments.quote: I wondered whether the conclusion from this work is more of a spatial one where simply: species that are closer to buildings tend to collide with them more.

comments.issue: The abstract does not list the confounding biases that were accounted for.
comments.request: List a few confounding biases in the abstract.
comments.quote: I acknowledge that the abstract word limit is quite short but, if possible, it could strengthen the abstract to list a few “confounding biases”.

comments.issue: 'Maladaptive consequences' in the abstract is too strong since evolutionary processes were not examined.
comments.request: Use 'fitness consequences' instead of 'maladaptive consequences'.
comments.quote: I found this wording a bit strong since evolutionary processes are not examined here, so concluding on adaptation seemed a bit speculative?

comments.issue: 'Temporally expansive' is vague.
comments.request: Say plainly that collisions have occurred over time.
comments.quote: I thought the use of “temporally expansive” vague.

comments.issue: The statement about declining bird populations is not specific.
comments.request: Specify whether some populations or populations on average are meant.
comments.quote: Not all bird populations are declining, so you mean some specific populations or bird populations on average?

comments.issue: Calling life-history a single trait is odd.
comments.request: Refer to traits related to body size and life-history.
comments.quote: I also find it odd to refer to life-history as a trait rather than a suite of traits

comments.issue: The sentence at L90 is too strong about behavioural plasticity predicting resilience.
comments.request: Soften it, e.g. 'could be an' instead of 'is also an'.
comments.quote: I wonder if this sentence could be softened, especially given the ending. Maybe “could be an” instead of “is also an”?

comments.issue: The definition of behavioural plasticity is loose for a central concept.
comments.request: Tighten the definition (genotypes/individuals, behavioural phenotypes, different environments).
comments.quote: I wondered whether this definition of behavioral plasticity could be tightened up a bit

comments.issue: The claim that plasticity sits on a continuum is confusing and the continuum is not theoretically developed.
comments.request: Clarify what the continuum of trait complexity means.
comments.quote: I found this sentence about plasticity being on a continuum a bit confusing

comments.issue: 'Complex end of the spectrum' is vague and confusing.
comments.request: Revise this terminology so key concepts are clear.
comments.quote: I find the use of “complex end of the spectrum” vague and a bit confusing.

comments.issue: Innovation and behavioural plasticity are used interchangeably without a theoretical basis.
comments.request: Clarify the distinction between innovation and behavioural plasticity throughout.
comments.quote: I am not as sure if innovation and behavioral plasticity can be used interchangeably? Is there a theoretical basis for this?

comments.issue: The claim about strong cognitive and neurobiological candidates is not substantiated.
comments.request: Set out the evidence for this conclusion more specifically.
comments.quote: I would be more specific here to set out the evidence for this conclusion

comments.issue: The aim about hazard type and innovation metric reads like an afterthought.
comments.request: Introduce these aspects and explain why the relationship may vary by context, or state that they are exploratory.
comments.quote: Since testing whether the relationship between innovation and collisions varies depending on hazard type or metric of innovation, it may be useful to introduce these aspects briefly?

comments.issue: Geographic coverage and the definition of an observation are unclear.
comments.request: Report coverage over time and regions and explain whether observations are summed collisions per species.
comments.quote: is an observation equal to the total number of collisions of a species summed over time and space? So in your main model each species level would have 1-3 observations?

comments.issue: The habitat context of wind farms and their distance from built-up areas is not reported.
comments.request: Add a brief note on wind farm habitat types and distance to built-up areas.
comments.quote: Which types of habitats were windfarms located in? How far on average (and range) away from built-up areas?

comments.issue: The three datasets do not overlap in time, space or species, which may explain context differences.
comments.request: Report dataset overlap and consider whether conclusions differ because of non-overlap.
comments.quote: Are conclusions different between contexts because the datasets don’t overlap in time, space, or species?

comments.issue: 'Tally' appears to be the total number of innovation events, not a rate.
comments.request: Clarify why rate rather than number of innovations is used.
comments.quote: I am assuming here “tally” means this is the the total number of documented innovation events for a species. If this is the case it is not a rate, right?

comments.issue: 'Collision incidence' is the total number of collisions, so the term is misleading.
comments.request: Use 'number' instead of 'incidence'.
comments.quote: Is there a reason why the authors use incidence and not number of collisions? I feel it would be more straightforward and clearer to use “number”.

comments.issue: Global abundance may not represent abundance within each dataset's spatial extent.
comments.request: Assess how global versus regional abundance affects estimates and robustness.
comments.quote: wondered about how “global abundance” and abundance within the spatial extents of each dataset (e.g., global vs USA abundance for windfarms) may affect estimates and robustness of results?

comments.issue: It is unclear why brain size and innovation give different results when swapped in the model.
comments.request: State that brain size had no clear effect and report the innovation-brain size correlation.
comments.quote: Maybe the authors could say here that brain size didn’t have a statistically clear effect? If brain size and innovation are correlated, then why do they give different results when swapped in the model?

comments.issue: Distributions and correlations among the variables are not shown.
comments.request: Add a supplementary figure showing distributions and correlations among variables.
comments.quote: A nice addition would be to add a supplementary figure showing the distributions and correlations between variables described in this paragraph.

comments.issue: GVIF/VIF results and their calculation are not reported in the manuscript.
comments.request: Report GVIF values and how they were calculated for all models.
comments.quote: Include results? All VIFs less than 3? I see this in the reply letter, but this should be reported in the manuscript.

comments.issue: The variable section is placed far from the model description.
comments.request: Move the section down to where the model structure is described.
comments.quote: Move this section down to where structure of model is described (e.g., 239)?

comments.issue: Secondary models omit collision context and innovation metric, so the main conclusion is not representative.
comments.request: Fit one model including collision context and innovation metric as interacting variables.
comments.quote: I wondered whether authors could conduct one single model where they include “collision context” as a variable instead of conducting secondary models.

comments.issue: Log-transformed collision counts may not meet Gaussian assumptions and may be overdispersed.
comments.request: Check diagnostics and consider Poisson or negative binomial error structures.
comments.quote: Since I am assuming this is the number of collisions, would Poisson or negative binomial error structures that deal with counts be more appropriate here?

comments.issue: Log transforming the response is argued to improve interpretation, which is questionable.
comments.request: Remove or adjust the claim that log transformation improves interpretation.
comments.quote: I would maybe argue that log transforming a variable does not improve interpretation because you are no longer on the data scale

comments.issue: Medians are not back-transformed to the data scale.
comments.request: Back transform medians to give collisions per innovative category.
comments.quote: Back transform medians to give number of collisions per innovative category?

comments.issue: The broad claim that innovation drives collisions is not supported given the secondary results (L304, L372).
comments.request: Restrict the conclusion to what the hazard-specific results show.
comments.quote: I am not sure you can conclude broadly that innovation drives collisions when you found it doesn’t in secondary models?

comments.issue: The claim of stronger positive associations was not tested statistically.
comments.request: Test it with a single interaction model.
comments.quote: “stronger positive associations” has not been tested statistically. This could be accomplished if a single model with interactions was used

comments.issue: The conclusion at L369-372 does not follow from the results.
comments.request: Reframe the wider implications and conclusions.
comments.quote: Not sure I agree with this conclusion, linked to my general comment above on wider implications and framing of results.

comments.issue: Figure 1 legend says confidence intervals but may show quantiles of raw data.
comments.request: Clarify the shaded area and add sample sizes.
comments.quote: Legend says “confidence intervals” when I wondered if this was quantiles since text says this is raw data?

comments.issue: The cut-off between innovative and non-innovative species is undefined.
comments.request: State how innovative versus non-innovative species were defined.
comments.quote: How did the authors decide a cut-off for an innovative and non-innovative species?

comments.issue: No figure shows the main effect on the real data scale.
comments.request: Add a figure of the main effect, e.g. foraging innovation on building collisions.
comments.quote: I would also be in favor of including a figure of the main effect (e.g., foraging innovation on building collisions) as this would help show the relationship on the real data scale.

comments.issue: Minor wording fixes (e.g. 'coherent' at L111, 'recognized' at L202, 'lifestyles' at L290).
comments.quote: L290: remove “lifestyles”?

reviews.assessment: Novel and exciting idea with robust datasets and suitable models; remaining issues concern sample-size transparency, statistical power, research effort as a predictor, and interpretation of generalism.
strengths: robust datasets for both collisions and innovations

comments.issue: Exact sample sizes for each analysed subset are not presented, including whether zero-innovation species were included.
comments.request: Give raw sample sizes (species, collisions, innovations) for each subset of data.
comments.quote: The exact sample sizes of the datasets included in the analyses are not presented in the manuscript.

comments.issue: Analyses of towers and turbines may have lower power because about three times fewer species are available than for buildings.
comments.request: Assess and discuss whether power differences explain the null tower and turbine results.
comments.quote: If these analyses use different number of species that may result in lower power for tower and turbine collisions, because approximately three times more species are available for the building analyses than for the other two types

comments.issue: Research effort was removed, but it directly affects the chance of observing and reporting innovations.
comments.request: Include research effort as a predictor even with abundance controlled.
comments.quote: the authors may consider to include research effort as a predictor, even if abundance is included as a control variable for encounter rate with structures

comments.issue: GVIF results are only reported for one model in the response letter.
comments.request: Present GVIF results for all models in the paper or supplementary tables.
comments.quote: I suggest to present thr results of GVIF analyses in the paper, and not only for the model presented in Table S2 but for the other models too.

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the innovation-collision relationship is independent of ecological generalism.
comments.request: Report collinearity between innovation frequencies and habitat/diet generalism.
comments.quote: Providing explicit information of possible collinearity between innovation frequencies and habitat/diet gerelaism would be useful for a better understanding the mechanism behind the innovation - collision relationship

comments.issue: The definition of innovative versus non-innovative species is missing from the legend and methods.
comments.request: Define innovative and non-innovative species.
comments.quote: I can’t find how “innovative” versus “non-innovative” species were defined, neither in the figure legend nor in the methods.

title: Innovative Behaviour Is Associated With Increased Collision Incidence in Birds

study.system: black-browed albatross; two populations, long-term monitoring

editor_summary: Reviewers enthusiastic about the exceptional dataset; revise framing of some points and add a small 'statistics on statistics' error-propagation assessment.

reviews.assessment: Broad-interest study with clear methods, but population differences beyond environmental variability call for more caution in the title and discussion.
strengths: topic of broad interest in evolutionary ecology
well written with excellent literature overview

comments.issue: The two populations differ in many parameters besides environmental variability, so differences cannot be attributed to variability alone.
comments.request: Be more cautious about environmental attribution in the title and discussion.
comments.quote: they compare two populations that differ not only in environmental variability, but also in several other parameters. I think that this aspect is overlooked throughout the manuscript.

comments.issue: 'Environmental conditions' at line 118 is vague.
comments.request: Specify what environmental conditions means, e.g. weather.
comments.quote: Line 118: environmental conditions: be more specific, are you referring to weather conditions?

comments.issue: The cited publication does not contain the food-resource variance data attributed to it in the introduction.
comments.request: Check the citation or move the detailed description to the discussion.
comments.quote: I did not find in the cited publication data on the temporal and spatial variance of food resources of the two populations studied.

comments.issue: The choice of a four-year time span is not justified with the dataset.
