editor_summary: Editor sees potential for a good contribution but requires standardized variables (true effect sizes), attention to plot size and spatial scale, replacing 'home range' with 'native range', discussion of political-boundary data limitations, and clearer presentation of negative results.

reviews.assessment: Easy to follow and data-supported, but the home-range terminology, missing phylogenetic description, geopolitical data, unscaled covariates and novelty claims raise serious concerns.
strengths: results seem supported by the data

comments.issue: 'Home range' is undefined and conflicts with the established animal ecology concept.
comments.request: Reframe the manuscript to avoid the term, e.g. using 'native range'.
comments.quote: Throughout their manuscript, the authors use the term home-range-PD, but it is neither defined in the introduction nor in the methods.

comments.issue: The EIH overlaps with historical contingencies and evolutionary legacies, but similar hypotheses are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge similar hypotheses and state the key differences.
comments.quote: the authors should acknowledge that similar hypotheses exist and also indicate the key differences (if any) between the EIH and similar hypotheses widely existing in the literature

comments.issue: PD is used as a covariate although phylogenies only inform trait-based processes when there is a phylogenetic signal.
comments.request: Include analyses of phylogenetic signal in the traits.
comments.quote: it would be beneficial to include some analyses of phylogenetic signal to see if the phylogeny used in this study informs trait-based processes

comments.issue: The phylogenetic hypothesis used to calculate PD is not described.
comments.request: Describe the phylogenetic hypothesis well.
comments.quote: The phylogenetic hypothesis used in this study is not described. Given the focus on phylogenetic diversity (PD) as a covariate, the phylogenetic hypothesis used must be well described.

comments.issue: Faith's PD is highly correlated with species number, so it may be an inadequate surrogate for the EIH.
comments.request: Confirm robustness of PD relative to metrics not correlated with species richness.
comments.quote: it may not be an adequate “surrogate” for testing the EIH. Additional analyses are necessary to confirm the robustness of PD relative to other metrics that are not correlated with species richness.

comments.issue: TDWG Level 3 data use political boundaries, so species presence is not eco-evolutionary, and aggregation effects on PD are not assessed.
comments.request: Discuss the limitations of political-boundary data and how aggregation influences PD.
comments.quote: Species don’t have political borders, but eco-evolutionary limits; in this sense, a species present in country A may not be distributed entirely in country A but just in a small area within that country.

comments.issue: Covariates on different scales make coefficients hard to interpret and are not true effect sizes.
comments.request: Scale covariates to 2 standard deviations following Gelman 2008.
comments.quote: As the covariates have different scales, I found it challenging to interpret the model coefficients. Given the different nature of the covariates, I strongly recommend scaling the covariates to 2 standard deviations

comments.issue: Testing an existing hypothesis with different data does not confer novelty, contrary to the 'first study' claim.
comments.request: Tone down the novelty claim.
comments.quote: testing an existing hypothesis (i.e., EIH), using a different set of data, in my opinion, does not confer novelty to a study. I strongly recommend toning down this claim.

reviews.assessment: Really strong, thoughtful and novel test of the EIH; asks for clearer description of response variables and more explicit consideration of spatial scale.

comments.issue: It is unclear how response variables such as 'number of plants' were calculated and at what spatial scale they were measured across experiments.
comments.request: Describe thoroughly how response variables were calculated for each experiment and clarify the measurement scale.
comments.quote: I believe the readers would benefit from a more thorough description of how response variables were calculated for the purposes of this paper (especially when figures or analyses are drawing on multiple experiments, with different treatments).

comments.issue: The interpretation may change at landscape scales, where small per-plot effects could aggregate into persistent populations.
comments.request: Consider landscape-scale implications and explore aggregate analyses across plots.
comments.quote: So, my question is really whether any of the interpretation in the ms would change if this larger spatial scale were considered, relative to the importance of invasion dynamics.

title: Plants That Evolved Under High Phylogenetic Diversity Have Higher Invasion Success, Particularly in Undisturbed Communities

study.system: rainforest trees; multispecies population genomics, eastern Australia

editor_summary: Both reviewers acknowledge the topic's importance and the effort, but raise substantial concerns that go beyond revision; editor cannot recommend further consideration in the present form.

reviews.assessment: Impressed by the dataset but finds the methods not cutting edge and thinks the paper does not fit Ecology Letters at this time.
strengths: prodigious genetic dataset with broad geographic sampling
many loci for many species across a large spatial extent

comments.issue: Comparative phylogeography and its available methods are never discussed, so the motivation for side-stepping them is unclear.
comments.request: Engage with comparative phylogeographic methods and justify the chosen approach.
comments.quote: The authors have in hand a very, very nice comparative phylogeographic dataset, so it would help to understand better the motivation for side-stepping the numerous available comparative phylogeographic methods

comments.issue: Biogeographic regions are defined from previous studies rather than testing whether the rivers act as barriers for the focal species.
comments.request: Test with the presented data whether the rivers are barriers.
comments.quote: The geographic sampling and genetic data presented in this study would be enough to establish whether these rivers are in fact acting as barriers for the focal species, rather than relying on previous work.

comments.issue: Calling the suite of analyses a 'framework' makes it look like a software paper and distracts from results and interpretation.
comments.request: Focus less on the 'framework' label and more on results and interpretation.
comments.quote: Referring to the suite of analyses that were run in this paper as a 'framework' I think gives the impression that this is a software paper, when in fact it seems not to be.

comments.issue: The introduction provides no hypotheses, so the links between methods, rationale and results are unclear.
comments.request: Develop and state hypotheses up front near the end of the Introduction.
comments.quote: The introduction does not provide hypotheses to be explored in the methods and evaluated in the results.

comments.issue: 'Macrogenetic' implies global or continental scale, but the study area is regional.
comments.request: Reconsider the scale terminology.
comments.quote: To me "Macrogenetic" means global or continental scale. I would rather consider the focal study area to be "Regional" scale.

comments.issue: The paragraph at L140-154 reads more like an introduction.
comments.request: Move or reframe the paragraph.
comments.quote: This is a nice paragraph but it feels a bit more like introduction.

comments.issue: 'Non-mutually exclusive site' is undefined.
comments.request: Define the term.
comments.quote: What is a 'non-mutually exclusive site'?

comments.issue: How the filtering cutoffs were applied is unclear, including the '>80-90%' and '>20-30%' soft filters.
comments.request: Explain how the soft filtering thresholds were applied.
comments.quote: For filtering the data, can you clarify how the cutoffs were applied? For example, what does it mean to remove individuals with ">80–90%" missing data?

comments.issue: The filter 'reproducibility <0.96' is unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify what reproducibility <0.96 means.
comments.quote: L178: What is "reproducibility <0.96"? Please clarify.

comments.issue: 'Redundant' is the wrong label for SNPs in linkage disequilibrium.
comments.request: Use 'SNPs in linkage disequilibrium (one per locus retained)'.
comments.quote: Instead of 'redundant' I would 'SNPs in linkage disequilibrium (one per locus retained)'.

comments.issue: The rationale for the cline transformation and what the two-dimensional rotation matrix does are unclear.
comments.request: Motivate the procedure and explain the rotation matrix.
comments.quote: This paragraph could do a bit more to motivate the reasoning for this procedure. As a reader who is not deep in the Cline Analysis literature, I have no idea what would be gained by applying this transformation

comments.issue: The point in Figure 1C does not appear to be the northernmost, and 'predicted latitude' in the caption is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify the reference frame and the caption wording.
comments.quote: the point indicated in Figure 1C doesn't \_appear\_ to be the northernmost. Is what is meant the 'northernmost' with respect to the frame of reference of the plane of the regression?

comments.issue: 'Population' is used in the methods without being defined.
comments.request: Define population at first use.
comments.quote: Please define what is meant by 'population'. This is the first occurrence of 'population' in the methods, but you haven't established what this is yet.

comments.issue: The goal of the broad-scale analysis (sorting species into the three landscape-level patterns) is not stated clearly.
comments.request: State the goal of the analysis explicitly.
comments.quote: In the section about Broad-scale patterns it would help to be clear that the goal of this analysis is to identify species that fall into the three "landscape-level" genetic patterns

comments.issue: The level at which expected heterozygosity was normalised is unclear.
comments.request: State whether He was normalised within species, clusters or populations.
comments.quote: Was heterozygosity normalized within species, within clusters, within populations or some other way?

comments.issue: 'Spatial inconsistencies' are undefined and their evaluation is not described.
comments.request: Define spatial inconsistencies and explain how they were evaluated.
comments.quote: What are 'spatial inconsistencies' and how were these evaluated?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether the groups at L281 are the broad- and fine-scale clustering groups.
comments.request: Clarify which groups are meant.
comments.quote: Presumably these groups are the fine-scale and broad-scale groups from the Genogeographic Clustering.

comments.issue: The name 'Alternating' group is unexplained.
comments.request: Explain why the group is called Alternating.
comments.quote: L349: Why is it called the "Alternating" group?

comments.issue: The CRC acronym is not expanded at first use.
comments.request: Expand CRC.
comments.quote: First occurrence of CRC, please expand the acronym here.

comments.issue: The dot colour meaning in Figure 1C and the overlaid red line are not explained.
comments.request: Explain the panel C colour scale and red line.
comments.quote: It currently says that the dot color represents "the rotated axis distance centred around a reference point", but it's not clear what this means or how it should be interpreted.

reviews.assessment: Clearly written, novel and integrative framework; only asks for discussion of two-dimensional extension and acknowledgement of partial cluster overlap.

comments.issue: The framework's extension to two-dimensional or elevation-including landscapes is not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss how the framework could extend to two-dimensional environments.
comments.quote: a brief discussion of how the framework might be extended to explicitly two-dimensional spatial environments, or even to landscapes incorporating elevation, would increase the generality of the approach

comments.issue: Northern-Broad and Alternating clusters show broadly similar isolation-by-distance and D-index decay patterns that are not acknowledged.
comments.request: Acknowledge and discuss the partial overlap between clusters.
comments.quote: it may be helpful to explicitly acknowledge and briefly discuss this partial overlap in genetic patterns

comments.issue: Three line-level copy edits: an extra parenthesis (main text L101), 'cantered' for 'centered' and 'companions' for 'comparisons' in Mat. Sup.
comments.quote: Line 63 Mat. Sup. "centered" not "cantered"

title: Macrogenetic Alignment in Ecological Strategies Better Interprets Assembly Processes Than Pre‐Determined Functional Groupings

study.system: urban vs non-urban wild animal populations; meta-analysis of phenotypic variation

editor_summary: Substantial revision: clarify what among-individual variance measures (drop 'fixed'), use residual/within-individual variance terminology, engage missing literature, and improve clunky English.

reviews.assessment: Many conceptual and literature-engagement concerns: among-individual variance and plasticity concepts are muddled and the meta-analysis misses substantial relevant literature.

comments.issue: Urban heterogeneity assumption is contested; an 'anthropogenic blender' view predicts urban similarity, so the claim needs softer phrasing.
comments.request: Phrase the urban heterogeneity assumption more subtly.
comments.quote: while that has been postulated, the combined set of urban stressors repeatedly present (built-up areal, pollution of various sorts, heat etc.) has also been evaluated as an anthropogenic blender

comments.issue: The distinction between 'average' phenotypic responses and 'total phenotypic variation' is unclear; what is being compared is not defined.
comments.request: Clarify and expand what is being compared.
comments.quote: The nuance between ‘average’ phenotypic responses ‘total phenotypic variation’ is not entirely clear.

comments.issue: The meaning of 'eco-evolutionary importance' and how it differs between within- and among-individual variation is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the concept or add more detail.
comments.quote: What is meant with eco-evolutionary importance and how does it become distinct between within individual vs. among-individual variation.

comments.issue: Statement implies plasticity operates independently of genetic change; plasticity itself can evolve, so multiple interacting mechanisms must be clarified.
comments.request: Clarify that rapid responses may involve genetic, plastic and evolved-plastic mechanisms.
comments.quote: The phrase “when genetic changes cannot explain the speed of response” incorrectly implies that plasticity operates entirely independently of genetic change.

comments.issue: Relevant literature is missing from the introduction; several studies the reviewer expected are not cited.
comments.request: Include and engage the listed studies.
comments.quote: Upon reading the introduction, it seemed indeed relevant literature is missing.

comments.issue: Positioning in the urban evolution literature is too narrow; a substantial body of work is not engaged, yielding an incomplete narrative.
comments.request: Integrate these works and derive a priori moderator predictions.
comments.quote: A substantial body of work on urban adaptation, plasticity, and their interplay is not engaged, leading to an incomplete narrative and missed hypotheses/moderators.

comments.issue: Describing among-individual variation as a 'fixed level of variation' is conceptually unclear; such variance can evolve dynamically.
comments.request: Rephrase to distinguish static differences from evolved changes in plasticity.
comments.quote: The paragraph describing among-individual variation as “a fixed level of variation present in a population” is conceptually unclear.

comments.issue: The logic at L123-124 is too simplistic: selection on increased plasticity can also homogenize or diversify variation and aid coping.
comments.request: Add the more nuanced dynamics to this section.
comments.quote: if there is selection on increased plasticity you get increased ability of populations to cope with future environmental conditions

comments.issue: Rationale that reduced interspecific competition lowers among-individual variation is unconvincing and conflates inter- with intra-specific variation.
comments.request: Rework the paragraph to separate levels and justify the predicted direction.
comments.quote: Conceptually, the authors seem to conflate inter-specific and intra-specific levels of variation.

comments.issue: Meta-analysis excludes urban quantitative-genetics studies using reaction-norm approaches, leaving a coverage gap.
comments.request: Include or explain the exclusion of reaction-norm studies.
comments.quote: urban ecology met-analyses seem to exclude all urban quantitative genetics studies that have assessed evolution of plasticity (reaction norm approach)

comments.issue: Paper steers toward personality research without saying so; the link between personality and within-individual variation is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the personality focus and its relation to within-individual variation.
comments.quote: From the introduction it seems authors want to steer this review towards ‘personality’ research (within-individual variation), but not explicitly mention this.

comments.issue: The homogenization hypotheses should be reformulated in light of the earlier conceptual comments.
comments.request: Reformulate the homogenization hypotheses accordingly.
comments.quote: L144: homogenization hypotheses: formulate it keeping in mind the comments that were suggested.

comments.issue: The search query behind the L158 claim is not specified.
comments.request: State the search query used.
comments.quote: L158: based on what (query)?

comments.issue: Repeated measures are undefined; unclear whether clonal genotypes count as within-individual variation and how such datasets were handled.
comments.request: Define repeated measures and explain handling of clonal-lineage data.
comments.quote: define repeated measures (same genotype in different stressor environments, same individual in different stressor environments

comments.issue: The introduction should refer readers to the table listing all 33 studies.
comments.request: Add a cross-reference to the table.
comments.quote: L177 refer to the table where all 33 studies are list.

comments.issue: The L191 statement on within-habitat variation does not convey the needed point; a review of urban-rural stressor variation should be cited.
comments.request: Reframe the statement and cite a relevant environmental-variation review.
comments.quote: Even though among-habitat variation is large, the essence should be that within-habitat variation in environmental conditions is larger in urban compared to rural areas

comments.issue: Aims and focus are confusing because the personality orientation only becomes clear in the discussion.
comments.request: Make the aims and personality focus explicit in the introduction.
comments.quote: from the discussion it becomes clear the authors are more focusing on personality research, however this seems to be not explicitly mentioned in the introduction, therefore the clear aims and focus of the paper is confusing

comments.issue: Inclusion/exclusion criteria are not motivated, so the meta-analysis appears incomplete and relevant studies are missing.
comments.request: Motivate exclusion criteria in the methods and set criteria in the introduction.
comments.quote: they should motivate the criteria of exclusion in more detail in the methods and introduce some criteria in the introduction

comments.issue: The urban-heterogeneity premise is unverified, conflicts with the paper's own narrative, and needs multivariate environmental analysis.
comments.request: Address the assumption with means and variation of urban conditions.
comments.quote: environmental heterogeneity is assumed to be higher in urban compared to rural settings (paper and goal of study is based on this criterion), but no paper included could verify this criteria, or no general paper was cited

reviews.assessment: Relevant, valuable synthesis; results unsurprising because context-dependence is widely found, and taxa differences should be considered before generalising.
strengths: highly relevant to understanding urbanisation effects on wildlife resilience
potential to predict and manage the future of wildlife

comments.issue: Results are not surprising: most studies find context-dependent urban effects, so the general conclusion is already known.
comments.quote: The vast majority of studies attempting to identify common processes and mechanisms across species or taxa that explain how organisms cope with urbanization have reached a similar conclusion

comments.issue: Before generalising, differences between taxa/species and among functional groups should be considered because organisms perceive heterogeneity differently.
comments.request: Consider taxa and functional-group differences before generalising.
comments.quote: future studies should consider possible differences between taxa and species, or within taxa among functional groups

reviews.assessment: Timely, well-written and transparent; requests mostly reporting clarifications and one additional sensitivity analysis.
strengths: data and code available with README files

comments.issue: PRISMA-EcoEvo checklist not provided, making reporting completeness hard to check.
comments.request: Provide a completed PRISMA-EcoEvo checklist as a supplementary table.
comments.quote: Please fill in and provide as a supplementary table a PRISMA-EcoEvo checklist

comments.issue: Study not registered; which hypotheses and analyses were a priori versus post hoc is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify a priori versus post hoc hypotheses and analyses.
comments.quote: This study is not registered, so it is not clear which hypotheses and analyses (or examined moderators) are a prior vs. post hoc.

comments.issue: Scope of the research question is vague; aim does not match methods criteria and the outcome-type requirement lacks justification.
comments.request: Frame the scope explicitly with PECO and specify eligibility criteria.
comments.quote: Scope of the study in terms of research question is not clear from the introduction

comments.issue: Linguistic scope not stated; English-only searching may bias the evidence base.
comments.request: State language scope and acknowledge the English-only limitation.
comments.quote: Please explicitly state linguistic scope of the meta-analysis and acknowledge as a study limitation that searches were only conducted in English

comments.issue: Excluded studies and reasons are not listed; PRISMA-EcoEvo requires a list.
comments.request: Add a supplementary table of excluded papers with reasons.
comments.quote: Please make a supplementary table of papers excluded during or after the 4th screening phase, with explicit reason for each study

comments.issue: Screening personnel and whether screening was duplicated are not stated.
comments.request: State who screened and whether it was single or duplicate.
comments.quote: Please state for all screening stages whether it was done by single person or in duplicate and who performed the screening.

comments.issue: Who extracted/categorised data and ran models, and whether steps were validated, is not stated.
comments.request: Report who did extraction and modelling and any validation.
comments.quote: Who did data extractions/categorisation and ran variance partitioning models? Who validated these steps

comments.issue: 'Raw data' undefined; raw data, model code and intermediate results are not archived.
comments.request: Define and share raw data, code and intermediate results.
comments.quote: please define and describe what you mean by “raw data” here. Please provide this raw data (if licences allow)

comments.issue: Handling of urban gradient studies is not described.
comments.request: Explain how urban gradient studies were dealt with.
comments.quote: Data collection – how did you deal with urban gradient studies, if you had any?

comments.issue: No leave-one-out analysis of influential studies.
comments.request: Run leave-one-out sensitivity analyses for key models.
comments.quote: Potentially they could do additional sensitivity analysis for individual influential studies by removing one study at a time and re-running key models (leave-one-out).

comments.issue: Additional analyses mentioned at line 381 were not reported.
comments.request: Report those analyses in the supplementary files.
comments.quote: Line 381: “We did not report those additional analyses.” – please do, in the supplementary files.

comments.issue: Location of the IO-LMM versus AD-LMM sensitivity analysis results is unclear.
comments.request: Report where those results are.
comments.quote: Results - section “Sensitivity analysis – IO-LMMs versus AD-LMMs” – where the results are reported?

comments.issue: Species of included studies are not listed in Suppl. Table S3, limiting context.
comments.request: List species in supplementary Table S3.
comments.quote: Explicitly list species for included studies in Suppl. Table S3, to provide context to the measures extracted for meta-analysis.

comments.issue: Migration/mobility status may explain null differences but was not tested; mobile species spend only part of their time in urban areas.
comments.request: Include sedentary versus migratory status as a moderator.
comments.quote: Consider (ideally, explicitly include as a moderator) whether species are sedentary or migratory (or highly mobile).

title: Phenotypic Flexibility in the City: A Meta‐Analysis on Variation

study.system: subtropical forest trees; BEF-China experiment, 12 years growth data

editor_summary: All agree on the valuable dataset; R1 criticizes framing and lack of theory. Rewrite the introduction, clarify a priori versus a posteriori hypotheses, report effect sizes and discuss past literature critically; very major revision.

reviews.assessment: Well-written, robust study with valuable long-term data; asks for clearer methods, better hypothesis justification and effect-size interpretation.
strengths: well written with clear structure and strong theory

comments.issue: How tree density and mortality were handled in the neighbourhood metrics is unclear.
comments.request: State whether dead trees were excluded and whether NR affects mortality.
comments.quote: The manuscript would benefit from a clearer description of how tree density and mortality were handled, as both can affect the calculation of neighbourhood richness (NR), basal area (NBA), and niche difference (NDIF).

comments.issue: Data imputation procedures and outlier treatment are not described in enough detail.
comments.request: Report imputed percentages, validation steps and outlier treatment.
comments.quote: describe data imputation procedures in more detail, e.g., percentage of imputed values, validation steps, and how potential outliers were treated

comments.issue: Tree growth and above-ground biomass calculation is only described in the supplement.
comments.request: Add a concise explanation of these calculations to the main text.
comments.quote: add a concise explanation in the main text of how tree growth and above-ground biomass (AGB) was calculated since tree growth is the central response variable

comments.issue: The temporal resolution of climatic variables is not stated.
comments.request: Describe whether climate variables are yearly or monthly.
comments.quote: describe how climatic variables were computed in the main text (yearly? monthly?)

comments.issue: The classification of species into functional groups and group sizes are not described.
comments.request: Explain the functional group classification and report species numbers.
comments.quote: provide details on how species were categorized into functional groups (fast vs. slow, water spender vs. saver), how many species belong to each group?

comments.issue: Spatial autocorrelation in data or residuals is not checked.
comments.request: Clarify whether residuals show spatial autocorrelation.
comments.quote: Given that trees within plots or microsites may share environmental conditions, please clarify whether data/residuals show spatial autocorrelation.

comments.issue: Hypothesis 3 lacks theoretical justification for climatic and trait effects.
comments.request: Justify why climate modifies neighbourhood effects and fast species respond more.
comments.quote: Hypothesis 3 would benefit from a stronger theoretical justification, i.e., why climatic variability should modify neighbourhood effects, and why fast species are expected to respond more strongly?

comments.issue: Some significant effects are very small and their biological meaning is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify effect-size interpretation relative to p-values.
comments.quote: Some statistically significant effects are small (e.g., NDIF ~ 0.03–0.07). The authors could clarify how they interpret effect size relative to p-value and discuss whether such small effects are biologically meaningful.

comments.issue: Later-stage SEMs fit poorly, likely from a missing residual correlation between NBA and NDIF.
comments.request: Justify the misfitting model or test the added correlation.
comments.quote: The SEMs for later stages show poor fit (Fisher’s C < 0.05), likely due to a missing residual correlation between NBA and NDIF. It would be helpful to explicitly discuss this issue.

comments.issue: The statement at line 104 lacks a supporting reference.
comments.request: Add a supporting reference.
comments.quote: Line 104: Please add a reference supporting this statement.

comments.issue: The importance of climatic variability is not justified and H3 is weakly motivated.
comments.request: Clarify the importance of climate variability and better justify H3.
comments.quote: Lines 136–147: Clarify why understanding the effects of climatic variability is important despite current knowledge gaps. This paragraph should also better justify H3

comments.issue: It is unclear whether a stronger response is expected for all metrics.
comments.request: Clarify the expected response for each metric.
comments.quote: Line 161: Is a “stronger response” expected for all metrics? Please clarify

comments.issue: The definition of plot condition is only given in the supplement.
comments.request: Add a brief definition of plot condition to the main text.
comments.quote: Also add a brief definition of plot condition (despite being fully explained in the Supp Mat.).

comments.issue: How growth stages were defined and whether data were pooled is unclear.
comments.request: Justify the three growth stage definitions.
comments.quote: Was growth data pooled by stage? Please justify how the three growth stages were defined.

comments.issue: The detrending procedure is not fully explained.
comments.request: Explain the detrending and whether it removed the age effect.
comments.quote: The detrending procedure is not fully clear. Please explain in more detail how it was applied. Did it effectively remove the age effect on biomass increment?

comments.issue: The wording at line 225 should be softened.
comments.request: Rephrase to 'weak positive and not significant'.
comments.quote: Line 225: Consider rephrasing to “weak positive and not significant.”

comments.issue: Weak correlations at line 260 are not flagged as weak.
comments.request: Note the weakness of these correlations in the text.
comments.quote: Line 260: Correlations of 0.1 and 0.19 are weak; please note this in the text.

comments.issue: The description of total effects at lines 290-292 is overly detailed.
comments.request: Simplify by explaining that effects are products of paths.
comments.quote: Lines 290–292: Simplify the description of total effects by explaining that they were calculated as products of relevant paths rather than describing each one.

comments.issue: Temperature results at lines 314-325 are not described.
comments.request: Include the temperature results.
comments.quote: Lines 314–325: The results related to temperature are not described. Please include these.

comments.issue: 'Unfavourable climatic conditions' at line 342 is undefined.
comments.request: Clarify what this phrase means.
comments.quote: Line 342: Clarify what is meant by “unfavourable climatic conditions.”

comments.issue: Relative importance of variables was not computed.
comments.request: Explore and present a relative importance analysis.
comments.quote: Line 395: The relative importance of variables was not computed; Consider exploring and presenting this analysis, if feasible.

comments.issue: The paragraph at lines 467-488 lacks theoretical grounding and conflicts with the stress-gradient hypothesis.
comments.request: Strengthen the theoretical grounding of this discussion.
comments.quote: This paragraph would benefit from stronger theoretical grounding. for example, the stress-gradient hypothesis predicts that positive interactions increase with stress, which contrasts with the claim that greater resource availability promotes “mutual growth”

reviews.assessment: Harsh critique: lacks theory, explorative analyses presented as hypothesis-testing, missing effect sizes; writing and discussion need work.

comments.issue: The study lacks theory; hypotheses appear out of the blue and the introduction is superficial.
comments.request: Ground the hypotheses in theory and develop the conceptual setting.
comments.quote: The study lacks theory. The hypotheses appear out of the blue.

comments.issue: Explorative analyses are presented as hypothesis-testing with inappropriate testing.
comments.request: Present the analyses as exploratory or test hypotheses appropriately.
comments.quote: The analyses are explorative (as stated by the authors: line 85) but are presented as hypothesis-testing, with inappropriate testing.

comments.issue: With 432 possible combinations, p-values must be corrected for multiple testing.
comments.request: Divide p-values by at least 432 or drop p-values.
comments.quote: but then the P-values must be divided by the number of possible combinations that can be tested, i.e. at least by 432

comments.issue: Effect sizes and confidence intervals are missing from Figures 1-4.
comments.request: Present effect sizes and confidence intervals.
comments.quote: The authors do not present effect sizes (such as R2) for Fig. 1, Fig 2 (a), Fig. 3 and Fig. 4. Also, they do not provide confidence intervals for the regression lines.

comments.issue: The writing is verbose and repetitive and the discussion is unfocussed.
comments.request: Tighten the writing and focus the discussion.
comments.quote: the unnecessary verbose and repetitive writing, nor the unfocussed discussion

comments.issue: Too many abbreviations; AM, EcM and PES should be written out.
comments.request: Reduce abbreviations and write out rare ones.
comments.quote: The authors should avoid abbreviations: there’re too many. AM and EcM and PES appear only very few times and should be written out.

comments.issue: Variable abbreviations use inconsistent case conventions.
comments.request: Use a consistent abbreviation scheme.
comments.quote: The abbreviations used for the variables in the analysis are very inconsistent: some are upper case (NR, NBA), some lower case (gd, h), some mixed (NDiv).

comments.issue: 'Diversity' in the title and introduction is undefined and actually means species richness.
comments.request: Use species richness and SPR terminology explicitly.
comments.quote: The title and intro does not make clear what is meant by “diversity”. As a catch-all phrase it is void of meaning until specified, and in this case we are talking about species richness

comments.issue: SPR references (Duffy, Liang) are cited uncritically and do not convincingly show the relationships.
comments.request: Discuss the literature more critically (e.g. Chisholm & Gupta 2023).
comments.quote: The much-claimed SPR relationships are likely correct, but the references do not show them convincingly.

comments.issue: How PES were defined and split into categories is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the PES categorization.
comments.quote: I could not find any reference to how PES were defined. While clear enough for leaf habit and mycorrhiza, PES and water use seem more continuous and thus the decision where to cut them into two categories must be justified

comments.issue: 'Fast-strategy' is imprecise; the life history, not the strategy, is fast.
comments.request: Use 'fast/slow life history strategies'.
comments.quote: line 121/123: “fast/slow life history strategies”, not “fast-strategy” (I would not even know what such a word may mean: the strategy is not fast, the life history is).

comments.issue: Calling the topic 'poorly understood' signals insufficient literature engagement.
comments.request: Engage with the relevant literature instead.
comments.quote: Such a “poorly understood” is a red flag for a reviewer. It typically means that the authors didn’t bother to read the relevant literature or did not want to formulate some theory themselves

comments.issue: 'Acquisitive' and 'fast' are used for the same concept.
comments.request: Use one term consistently.
comments.quote: l 160: “acquisitive” = “fast”? If so, use one term and stick with it.

comments.issue: Imputing response variables risks circularity and its effect on results is not reported.
comments.request: Justify imputation and report results without imputation.
comments.quote: In this case, gd and h were imputed. How many data points were imputed? What are the results without imputation

comments.issue: Only directly neighbouring trees are used; larger or distance-weighted neighbourhoods are not justified.
comments.request: Justify the neighbourhood definition.
comments.quote: l 197: Why only the directly neighbouring trees? I have seen in other studies larger neighbourhoods, and a distance-weighted crowding coefficient based on either height or DBH.

comments.issue: The crowding index is not weighted by height despite light competition asymmetry.
comments.request: Consider height weighting in the crowding index.
comments.quote: l 201: Why no weighting by height? If a neighbour is (much) smaller than the target, light competition is no issue. That’s why some crowding indices use height as weight.

comments.issue: Which traits were used and why is only in the supplement.
comments.request: Report the traits and rationale in the main text.
comments.quote: l 204: Which traits, and why? This should be in the main text, not the supplement. Links back to theory.

comments.issue: 'Plot conditions' at line 225 is undefined in the main text.
comments.request: Define plot conditions in the main text, e.g. topographic variables.
comments.quote: l 225: What are “plot conditions”? Put into main text, not supplement, e.g. “topographic variables”.

comments.issue: How 'metadata' enters a linear model and how annual effect sizes were computed is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the metadata and effect-size computation.
comments.quote: l 230: How can “metadata” be used in a linear model? Annual effect sizes of what? Computed how?

comments.issue: The notation 'tag:idh(site)' and the need for commercial software are unexplained.
comments.request: Explain the random-effects notation and software choice.
comments.quote: l 250: What does “tag:idh(site)” mean? Why was a commercial software needed, and what did it do that lme4/nlme/glmmTMB/brms cannot do?

comments.issue: The model's conditional R2 and the relevance of effect sizes at lines 255-262 are not reported.
comments.request: Report the conditional R2.
comments.quote: l 255-262: These results look like ecologically irrelevant effect sizes. What’s the model’s (conditional) R2?

comments.issue: The discussion mixes generic statements with hesitant, incomplete synthesis.
comments.request: Be more daring in describing the interrelations.
comments.quote: The discussion is a mixture of general statements that were true before this study and have no further bearing, of specific results discussed only in relation to very similar studies

comments.issue: Confidence intervals are missing from regression lines in Figures 1-3.
comments.request: Add confidence intervals to all regression lines.
comments.quote: Fig. 2: Add confidence intervals to all regression lines.

comments.issue: The three SEMs look extremely similar and are not tested against each other.
comments.request: Test differences, e.g. with a repeated-measures or all-year SEM.
comments.quote: The three SEMs look extremely similar to me. Since this is a major part of the story told in the discussion, I would like to have this tested.

comments.issue: Figure 4 is confusing because the colour is a predictor rather than the response.
comments.request: Reconsider the Figure 4 design.
comments.quote: Fig. 4: I found this confusing. Normally I expect that the predictors form the axes, and the response is the 3D/colour. Here, the colour is one of the predictors.

comments.issue: Explorative plots do not show the underlying data.
comments.request: Show the data points in the figures.
comments.quote: I have a severe allergy against explorative plots without data.

title: Neighbourhood Diversity Effects on Tree Growth Shift Over Time in a Long‐Term Forest Biodiversity Experiment

study.system: soil fauna feeding modes; stable isotopes from 228 forest sites

editor_summary: Editor finds the dataset valuable but says the framing, isotopic interpretation and hypothesis support are insufficient: d13C/d15N signals are oversimplified, enrichment factor and %C proxies unjustified, and climate/litter gradients too coarse; resubmission possible after thorough revision.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and important topic, but the climate and litter-quality gradients are too coarsely characterised.

comments.issue: Line numbering does not fit the double-spaced lines, making precise comments impossible.
comments.request: Provide proper continuous line numbering.
comments.quote: It is difficult to comment with precision without adequate line numbering. The automatic line numbers do not fit the double-space lines, making it impossible to cite a specific line.

comments.issue: The decomposition contribution literature is mostly mesofauna-based, while macrofauna contributions rise in warm and dry biomes.
comments.request: Consider macrofauna and dry-biome evidence.
comments.quote: recently, Sagi and Hawlena (2024) showed that the relative contribution of macrofauna to decomposition increase in warm and *dry* biomes. This could alter the hypothesis.

comments.issue: Climate is reduced to temperate vs tropical; other biomes and continuous MAT/MAP are ignored.
comments.request: Use continuous climate variables and more biomes.
comments.quote: is there a reason why the authors focused on temperate and tropical systems? What about other biomes? Mediterranean, arid, semi-arid, boreal, etc. How are the 222 sites distributed?

comments.issue: Litter quality is represented only by %C, a rough proxy when %N and C:N are available.
comments.request: Use %N or C:N instead of %C.
comments.quote: Litter quality here is only characterized by the C concentration in plant litter. However, this is only a rough proxy of litter quality.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and important question, but analysis robustness, isotope interpretation and gradient characterisation need major clarification.
strengths: important contribution for carbon cycle understanding

comments.issue: The title is hard to follow and omits the forest context.
comments.request: Change the title to include forest context.
comments.quote: I find this title difficult to follow for a wider audience and missing the forest context of the data (which could also be emphasized throughout).

comments.issue: It is unclear whether feeding-preference shifts are at community or individual level.
comments.request: Clarify community versus individual feeding shifts.
comments.quote: Do the authors mean functional shifts in the community or within individual feeding preferences? Please explain.

comments.issue: The claim about mesofauna food selection lacks a citation.
comments.request: Add a citation.
comments.quote: Better ability to select food in mesofauna? Perhaps a citation?

comments.issue: Decomposition is also controlled by hyper-local conditions and fungi, not consistent macroclimate predictors.
comments.request: Discuss this alternative view and cite Bradford et al.
comments.quote: Variation in decomposition is also thought of as controlled by hyper local conditions and the fungal community, where macroclimate conditions are not consistent predictors.

comments.issue: The assumed ca. 3 per mil N enrichment factor is problematic in soil food webs and unjustified.
comments.request: Justify the 3 per mil enrichment factor.
comments.quote: Assuming an N isotope ratio increase in food chains by ca. 3‰ may be problematic in soil food webs because feeding relationships are not always clear, and the amount of N may vary. Please justify your use of 3‰

comments.issue: %C is not a robust proxy for litter quality; %N or C:N is standard.
comments.request: Justify %C or switch to %N/C:N.
comments.quote: Please justify the use of %C as a metric for soil litter quality. I have concerns that the use of % C to represent litter quality is not robust, and more common would be % N or C:N ratio.

comments.issue: Study selection and inclusion criteria and the range of collection designs are not described.
comments.request: Report study inclusion criteria.
comments.quote: What was the author’s selection criteria for studies that were included? What is the range of study and collection designs? Did you have inclusion criteria for study design?

comments.issue: No map shows the distribution of the 222 sites.
comments.request: Add a global site map.
comments.quote: A global map of all your sites would be helpful to visualize the distribution of your 222 sites.

comments.issue: The null climate result may stem from wider temperate than tropical ranges.
comments.request: Report litter value ranges per climate region.
comments.quote: Could the insignificance of climate be due to narrow ranges in the tropics and wider ones in the temperate categories?

comments.issue: Sites are not independent; multiple sites come from the same dataset and spatial autocorrelation is untested.
comments.request: Test spatial autocorrelation and adjust statistics.
comments.quote: Please conduct a spatial autocorrelation analysis on all your ‘sites’ to identify what are true independent sites

comments.issue: The categorical climateType is too coarse; continuous temperature or precipitation should be used.
comments.request: Use continuous temperature/precipitation variables.
comments.quote: The authors should justify the use of a categorical variable "climateType" (two levels: temperate and tropical) to account for a possible causal pathway of climatic impact

comments.issue: Sample preparation and mass spectrometry details, and how an observation is defined, are missing.
comments.request: Describe sample preparation and analysis.
comments.quote: I’d like more information on how isotope mass spectrometry was performed on soil fauna. Was analysis done at the individual level (unlikely for mesofauna), was it done at the individual level for macrofauna

comments.issue: The additional information did not answer the methods questions.
comments.request: Answer the outstanding methods questions.
comments.quote: The additional information did not have answers to the questions above

comments.issue: Whether trophic groups use high-rank taxonomy or finer resolution is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify trophic group assignment.
comments.quote: did they categorize trophic groups based on high-rank taxonomic groups or of the finer resolution identification and then scale?

comments.issue: Predictor collinearity may bias the results.
comments.request: Check predictor collinearity.
comments.quote: The authors should carefully consider how their variables are related and potential collinearity within your predictors which may be introducing bias.

comments.issue: f- and p-values are reported without percent explained or uncertainty.
comments.request: Report effect sizes and uncertainty.
comments.quote: The use of f-values and p-values should be further evaluated. More typically in ecology we look at the percent explained

comments.issue: Why a term is squared across one continuous and two categorical variables is not justified.
comments.request: Justify the squared term.
comments.quote: I don’t understand why you’re squaring a term across a continuous and two categorical variables (D13C ~ (percentClitter + sizeClass + climateType)^2). Please justify in the methods.

comments.issue: Causal language such as "results in" is used for observational data.
comments.request: Remove or justify causal language.
comments.quote: Please carefully consider and justify your use of causal language from an observational dataset. (phrases such as ‘results in’).

comments.issue: Whether the table is an ANOVA summary is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the statistics.
comments.quote: This is the summary from the ANOVA, correct? Please clarify the statistics.

comments.issue: Fig 1B shows temperature as continuous although the text treats it as a category.
comments.request: Make Fig 1B a boxplot.
comments.quote: the figure 1B shows temperature as a continuous variable. Although the authors do have a subtitle that says temperate v tropical, it is not accurately represented as a category in the figure. Please make figure 1B a boxplot

comments.issue: No raw-data figure accompanies hypothesis 2, unlike hypothesis 1.
comments.request: Add a raw-data figure for hypothesis 2.
comments.quote: I’m curious why the authors didn’t follow up Figure 1B with a figure in the results/discussion of raw data as they have in Figure 2 for hypothesis 1?

comments.issue: No version control is used for the analysis code.
comments.request: Use version control for reproducibility.
comments.quote: Thank you for supplying R-code and data that works! I’d recommend using some kind of package for version control to ensure reproducibility.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and important question, but the core assumption that d13C tracks microbivory is not established and alternative drivers are not ruled out.

comments.issue: The paper hinges on d13C representing microbivory, which is not shown to hold across systems.
comments.request: Show the d13C-microbivory link or exclude alternatives.
comments.quote: this manuscript largely hinges on the assumption that D13C represents microbivory and its not clear that this is true across systems

comments.issue: Line numbers do not run continuously through the document.
comments.request: Add continuous line numbers.
comments.quote: This would be a lot easier to track with proper line numbers that run continuously through the document

comments.issue: Calling the functional role of soil animals little understood is a straw man; the topic has decades of attention.
comments.request: Soften the claim that the topic is little understood.
comments.quote: This topic has received widespread attention for decades now, and many of the authors of this paper have published work directly on the topic.

comments.issue: The cited DOI does not exist and no sharable link is given.
comments.request: Provide a valid link.
comments.quote: This DOI does not exist, need to provide sharable link unless its been published.

comments.issue: What d13C and d15N represent, and how they are interpreted, is never defined.
comments.request: Define what d13C and d15N represent.
comments.quote: Think it needs to be clear here what D13C and D15N actually represent, or at least how they are being interpreted.

comments.issue: Many alternative drivers of bulk d13C and d15N in soils and animals are ignored.
comments.request: Address alternative drivers of bulk isotope values.
comments.quote: There are numerous mechanisms that can impact bulk d13C and d15N values in both soils and animals, and it feels like that’s being ignored here.

comments.issue: %C may reflect inorganic material; C:N is a more proximate litter quality index.
comments.request: Use C:N as the litter quality metric.
comments.quote: Seems like variation in %C could be a function of inorganic material, while C:N gives more proximate index of organic litter quality.

comments.issue: Categorical climate type is oversimplified; direct temperature/precipitation measures should be used.
comments.request: Use continuous temperature/precipitation.
comments.quote: climate "type" seems overly simplified when you’ve already introduced temp/precip as the primary drivers of quality – why not use those direct, continuous measures instead of categorical biome?

comments.issue: The random effects hierarchy and which models were run are unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the random effects structure and models.
comments.quote: Whats the hierarchy here? Are these nested or individual REs? I read this as (1|locationID) + (1|locationID_Group), or is it (1|location/group)?

comments.issue: Modelling d13C and d15N separately ignores that they covary through shared mechanisms.
comments.request: Use a multivariate approach.
comments.quote: unless you expect the measures to be independent or to be influenced by independent mechanisms it seems oversimplified. Here, so far as I can tell, the proposed mechanism behind both D13C and D15N changes are trophic enrichment

comments.issue: "Confirming" overstates the support for the hypothesis.
comments.request: Use "supporting" instead of "confirming".
comments.quote: "confirming" is a strong word. Supporting maybe.

comments.issue: No clear link is shown between d13C and microbial contributions, which is the crux of the paper.
comments.request: Establish the link with data or prior studies.
comments.quote: I think the authors have not presented a clear link between d13C/D13C and microbial contributions, either with their own data or previous studies. That is the crux of this paper and I do not think it is clear

comments.issue: A sentence on Pg12, L36-41 is confusing.
comments.request: Say depleted d13C values in macrofauna.
comments.quote: Confusing sentence, just say depleted D13C values in macrofauna

comments.issue: Sites within climate type categories may not be comparable and categories may not separate temperature/precipitation drivers.
comments.request: Assess how well categories separate the climate drivers.
comments.quote: how comparable are the sites in the "climate type" categories? As above, if the mechanisms are really temp/precip, how well do these categories separate those drivers?

title: Shift in Soil Fauna Feeding Mode With Litter Quality Across Forest Biomes

study.system: angiosperms; clonality and diversification rates across 2997 genera

editor_summary: Both reviewers raise significant concerns about conceptual framing and analytical approach: interpret phylogenetic models primarily, justify tip-rate metrics on the inserted phylogeny, define diversification precisely, and temper mechanisms.

reviews.assessment: Compelling question and monumental dataset, but conflicting rate estimates and the phylogenetic/non-phylogenetic mismatch weaken the core findings.
strengths: monumental data compilation for over 16,000 species

comments.issue: Multiple rate estimation methods give conflicting evidence; DR and BAMM results are essentially opposite.
comments.request: Reconcile or explain the conflicting rate estimates.
comments.quote: when comparing DR vs. BAMM results you find basically the opposite

comments.issue: Non-phylogenetic models are given equal weight despite the trait's high phylogenetic signal.
comments.request: Base the analysis on phylogenetically informed models.
comments.quote: They should just use the phylogenetic, taking into account the high phylogenetic signal of the trait.

reviews.assessment: Impressive dataset and clear writing, but conceptual framing, phylogenetic interpretation and tip-rate sensitivity need substantial strengthening.
strengths: clearly written with generally informative figures

comments.issue: Diversification is conflated with evolutionary change; the macroevolutionary definition should be used consistently.
comments.request: Define diversification precisely and state the focus of the analyses.
comments.quote: The manuscript occasionally conflates diversification with evolutionary change more generally.

comments.issue: Conclusions lean on non-phylogenetic models whose significance disappears after accounting for phylogeny.
comments.request: Treat non-phylogenetic models as descriptive and base conclusions on PGLS.
comments.quote: I strongly recommend reframing the non-phylogenetic analyses as descriptive or complementary, while basing evolutionary conclusions primarily on the phylogenetically informed results.

comments.issue: DR tip rates on a phylogeny with extensive V.PhyloMaker insertions may reflect imputed branch lengths.
comments.request: Justify insertions and run sensitivity analyses on backbone taxa or genera.
comments.quote: the resulting tip-rate estimates may partly reflect how those lengths are assigned rather than underlying diversification processes

comments.issue: DR is sometimes called a speciation rate; whether line 207 refers to BAMM or DR rates is unclear.
comments.request: Distinguish diversification proxies from speciation rate estimates.
comments.quote: it is not explicitly stated whether the “tip speciation rates” being log-transformed refer to BAMM-derived speciation rates or to DR-based metrics

comments.issue: The rationale for log-transforming DR values at line 178 is not stated.
comments.request: Justify the transformation explicitly.
comments.quote: the rationale for log-transforming DR values (line 178) is not clearly stated and would benefit from explicit justification

comments.issue: BAMM genus-level rates mapped onto species-level data may inflate significance in non-phylogenetic models.
comments.request: Discuss the implications of mapping genus rates to species.
comments.quote: genus-level diversification and speciation rates are mapped onto species-level data, assuming identical rates for all species within a genus

comments.issue: Mechanisms linking clonality to diversification are under-specified and presented as established.
comments.request: Specify the mechanisms or frame them as hypotheses with citations.
comments.quote: it remains unclear whether clonal species experience fewer meiotic events per reproductive episode, per unit time, or simply invest less frequently in sexual reproduction

comments.issue: The low/medium/high categorisation of rates in Figure 2 is not explained.
comments.request: Explain the categorisation and consider a categorical DR analysis.
comments.quote: The categorisation of diversification rates into “low”, “medium” and “high” in Figure 2 should be explained in the Methods (e.g. tertiles, quantiles).

comments.issue: Figure 1 is not integrated into the main argument.
comments.request: Integrate the figure or justify its conceptual role.
comments.quote: Figure 1 is visually appealing but not fully integrated into the main argument

comments.issue: Boldface in Table 1 does not consistently indicate statistical significance.
comments.request: Clarify or remove the boldface coding.
comments.quote: The use of boldface in Table 1 is confusing and does not appear to correspond consistently to statistical significance.

comments.issue: Some cited references, e.g. Dimitrov et al. 2024, are missing from the bibliography.
comments.request: Add the missing references.
comments.quote: Please ensure that all cited references (e.g. Dimitrov et al. 2024) are included in the bibliography.

comments.issue: Several statements and methodological choices lack supporting citations or justification.
comments.request: Add citations and justify these choices.
comments.quote: several statements and methodological choices would benefit from additional citations or clearer justification

title: Comparative Analysis of Diversification Rates in Clonal and Non‐Clonal Flowering Plants

study.system: model communities; Modern Coexistence Theory and secondary extinctions

editor_summary: Editor: methodology insufficiently described, novelty relative to prior work unclear, coexistence definitions inconsistent, limitations should be stated and notation typos fixed.

reviews.assessment: Uses established methods on empirical models; asks what is genuinely new, how the decomposition is mechanistic, and how it handles high-density cases.

comments.issue: It is unclear how the paper advances beyond applying existing MCT machinery to IGR<0 cases.
comments.request: Give a more didactic treatment of the invasion graph and its implications for disassembly.
comments.quote: It is not clear how the manuscript goes beyond applying MCT for the case where IGR<0.

comments.issue: The context of how the IGR partition was performed is not described, so results feel unmotivated.
comments.request: Explain how the IGR partition was done and where results come from.
comments.quote: Also, some context of how the IGR partition was done would be useful, as the reader might feel they don’t understand where the results come from and why.

comments.issue: The decomposition resembles a statistical outcome rather than a demonstrated mechanism.
comments.request: Clarify the mechanistic added value of decomposing IGRs.
comments.quote: In essence, the decomposition is very much like a statistical outcome, not a real mechanism.

comments.issue: No analytical toy example shows how parameter combinations determine network fate after removal.
comments.request: Add an analytical decomposition of a simple toy example.
comments.quote: It would have been nice to see a decomposition done analytically on a simple toy example to showcase how parameter combinations dictate the fate of a network following species removal.

comments.issue: Using low-density IGR to infer secondary extinction may conflict with candidate extinctees being at high density.
comments.request: Address the density inconsistency and possible Allee effects.
comments.quote: The approach uses the IGR to determine secondary extinction. But isn’t this at odds with the fact that a candidate secondary extinctee may be at high (or at least non-negligible) density whenever a species is removed?

comments.issue: Extinction in nature is often environment-driven, which the manual-removal framework does not cover.
comments.request: Discuss extending the approach with feasibility results under environmental change.
comments.quote: I am curious if the authors have ideas on how to expand the ideas in this paper with results on feasibility, where parameters change as a function of environmental condition.

comments.issue: 'Robustness' is not introduced early enough.
comments.request: Refer to robustness already at lines 17-23.
comments.quote: L17-23: It could be useful to refer to ‘robustness’ already here.

comments.issue: The phrase 'have a negative IGR' is confusing given the S, T notation used elsewhere.
comments.request: Restate the 2022 result and explain how it formalises secondary extinction.
comments.quote: L106: “have a negative IGR”: I suppose this refers to secondary extinction already? Is a bit confusing, given the S, T notation also used in Hofbauer and Schreiber 2022, section 2.2, to formalise successful invasion.

comments.issue: Fig. 1A edge labelling and the red 'secondary extinction of interest' label are unclear, and B/C panels are referenced late.
comments.request: Clarify the edge labels and panel referencing.
comments.quote: Fig1A: Edge labelling not clear to me. The yellow vertex signals a secondary extinction, and the label tells us the identity of the species going secondarily extinct.

comments.issue: Grey arrows in Fig. 3 are hard to see behind yellow arrows.
comments.request: Change the colours or make grey arrows black.
comments.quote: Fig3: the grey arrows are hard to see when there’s a yellow arrow behind. Consider changing colors and/or making the grey arrows black.

reviews.assessment: Satisfied with a cleanly executed approach; suggests linking to topology and random-community work, acknowledging scalability limits and reframing conceptually.
strengths: systematic approach to identifying causes of secondary extinction
methods cleanly executed and clearly explained

comments.issue: The study is not linked back to topological analyses of secondary extinctions from food webs.
comments.request: Make the contrast with purely topological approaches explicit.
comments.quote: Link back to analyses of secondary exactions based on food-web topology alone. You last example demonstrates how this can fail and it's worth making this explicit

comments.issue: Limitations for complex communities are not acknowledged; graphs grow exponentially and become impractical.
comments.request: State scalability limitations explicitly.
comments.quote: Acknowledge the limitations of the approach for more complex communities. The size of the invasion or disassembly graphs grows exponentially (or similar) with species richness.

comments.issue: The work is not connected to research on large random communities where simplicity emerges at high richness.
comments.request: Link to this body of work and discuss consistency between approaches.
comments.quote: while complexity increases tremendously as we consider communities with more and more species, there is simplicity at the extreme end of very complex communities

comments.issue: The manuscript is framed as a methodological rather than a conceptual contribution.
comments.request: Reframe it around conceptual development of cause-of-extinction questions.
comments.quote: You might consider framing the study a bit more in terms of conceptual development (as it presents a way to meaningfully answer the Q: what just caused this secondary extinction??) than as a methodological development

comments.issue: The decomposition of invasion growth rates is not clearly explained.
comments.request: Clarify the decomposition, as detailed in the inline comments.
comments.quote: The methods is cleanly executed and clearly explained (except for the decomposition of invasion growth rates, see my inline comments).

title: Using Modern Coexistence Theory to Understand Community Disassembly

study.system: consumer-resource model; microbial time-series reanalysis

editor_summary: Editor says both reviewers support the work but offer many suggestions that could significantly improve it; all comments must be explicitly addressed.

reviews.assessment: Well-written and mathematically sound, but the NO-versus-YDM framing, the correlation metric and the time-scale separation need further justification.

comments.issue: Niche overlap is described as an equilibrium property, but it derives from invasion of a rare species.
comments.request: Reframe NO correctly in the manuscript.
comments.quote: NO is presented as a property related to equilibrium conditions. I don’t think this is fully accurate. NO is typically obtained by considering the invasion of a rare species, which is everything but an equilibrium condition

comments.issue: Paper is framed as a contest between NO and YDM, though NO was never meant to predict dynamics.
comments.request: Reframe the study away from a NO-versus-YDM contest.
comments.quote: I don’t think the paper needs to present this a contest between NO and YDM. For one thing, NO was never conceived as predictive of anything but long-term species coexistence

comments.issue: Classic Loreau and de Mazancourt 2013 results on NO and temporal correlations are not cited.
comments.request: Mention these classic results in the introduction and discussion.
comments.quote: The influence of NO on temporal correlations has been partly addressed by Loreau and de Mazancourt in 2013 (L&dM). The intro and discussion would benefit from mentioning these classic results where relevant

comments.issue: Mean temporal correlation vanishes for large n, so the metric is problematic for large systems.
comments.request: Discuss this limitation and propose alternative metrics.
comments.quote: The choice for temporal correlation to describe population dynamics is not optimal when systems grow large because the mean correlation coefficient becomes vanishingly small for large n

comments.issue: Unclear whether NO's failure reflects NO itself or the time-scale separation used to calculate it.
comments.request: Test whether relaxing the time-scale separation changes the conclusion.
comments.quote: I’m in doubt if the unrelatedness of NO and temporal correlation is due to limitations of NO itself or of how it was calculated

comments.issue: 'Out-of-niche' wording needs justification for unambiguous interpretation.
comments.request: Justify or remove the 'out-of-niche' wording.
comments.quote: Not sure where the ‘out-of-niche’ wording comes from. If kept in the paper, it needs justification, so its interpretation is unambiguous

comments.issue: Rationale for examining growth-rate correlations is unclear.
comments.request: Explain how growth-rate correlations fit the story.
comments.quote: Not sure why growth rate correlations are examined. How does this fit the story if the paper is about population dynamics?

comments.issue: Abstract's claims that the model is 'generalized' and a 'framework' are unexplained.
comments.request: Clarify or reword these terms in the abstract.
comments.quote: Abstract: How is the model “generalized”, and how it is a “framework”?

comments.issue: Several copy edits and notation fixes (hyphenation, index k, give->giving, cases->case).
comments.quote: P21, L36, Eq. A2: index needs to be “k” here.

comments.issue: Equilibrium density calculation is missing from Supp A and the alpha matrix setup is unclear.
comments.request: Add the calculation and state whether alpha is symmetric.
comments.quote: P5, L58: Calculation of equilibrium density not found in Supp A. Also, was a symmetric alpha matrix chosen?

comments.issue: How NO and correlations were obtained from the microbial data is unclear.
comments.request: Explain the empirical calculation of NO and the correlation pooling.
comments.quote: P7, section C: explain explicitly how NO was obtained from the data. It was also not clear to me if the correlations were indeed temporal correlations and why correlations were computed across environmental conditions instead of per condition

comments.issue: Figure 5 correlation ranges differ from Figure 2 for the same alpha.
comments.request: Reconcile or explain the difference.
comments.quote: Fig5: ranges of the correlation coefficient look different from those in Fig2 for same alpha.

comments.issue: Example on P12 L52 is too unclear for many readers.
comments.request: Explain the example more explicitly.
comments.quote: P12, L52: be more explicit about this example as it will be unclear to many readers.

comments.issue: Figure 6 panel order does not match the text's order of D_T and D.
comments.request: Swap the panels to match the text.
comments.quote: Fig6: swap the panels so it matches the order of D_T and D in the text.

comments.issue: Claim that McA stochasticity is less phenomenological than LV is arguable.
comments.request: Reconsider or discuss this claim.
comments.quote: P20, L42: One could argue that the stochasticity itself is equally phenomenological in the McA model as in the LV model.

comments.issue: Necessity of the three-species example is unclear.
comments.request: Justify or remove the example.
comments.quote: P21, L16-30: Why this 3sp example? Is it needed?

comments.issue: Section B1 overlaps with work by J.F. Arnoldi et al. and is not cited.
comments.request: Cite Arnoldi et al. where appropriate.
comments.quote: P26, Section B1 is quite similar to what J.F. Arnoldi et al have done in several of their paper. Cite where appropriate

comments.issue: Phrase 'find actual name' on P39 is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify this phrase.
comments.quote: P39: What does ‘find actual name’ mean?

reviews.assessment: Important message about inferring population parameters from fluctuations, but the biology, generality of measure D and treatment of environmental fluctuations need much more work.
strengths: commendable robustness tests in the appendix

comments.issue: Paper needs more biology: when measure D is nonzero is not explained, nor that different species are compared.
comments.request: Present biological scenarios for nonzero D in the introduction.
comments.quote: I urge you to put more biology in, especially in explaining when your measure D will be nonzero

comments.issue: Measure D does not capture several intuitive yield-depletion mismatch scenarios.
comments.request: Generalize D or acknowledge its limitations.
comments.quote: it is not entirely clear that your mismatch measure is general enough

comments.issue: Environmental fluctuations are introduced only in resources; other fluctuation modes and coexistence effects are not discussed.
comments.request: Discuss other fluctuation modes and their implications.
comments.quote: there are many other ways in which environmental fluctuations affect community dynamics and species interactions

comments.issue: Title's 'Opposite Dynamics' casts unfounded doubt on niche overlap.
comments.request: Retitle to 'Same Overlap, Contrasting Fluctuations'.
comments.quote: I suggest changing the title to “Niche Overlap Is Not Enough: Same Overlap, Contrasting Fluctuations.”

comments.issue: Abstract claim that YDM determines abundance correlations is too strong given narrow circumstances tested.
comments.request: Soften the abstract claim about YDM.
comments.quote: In my opinion, this statement is too strong. It seems to me that there are still many questions about how well your YDM criterion works broad

comments.issue: Equation (1) is a stochastic differential equation but written as an ODE without a calculus interpretation.
comments.request: State the calculus interpretation (Ito vs Stratonovich) and consult Turelli 1977.
comments.quote: Later on you identify it as Gaussian white noise, which means it is not in fact an ordinary differential equation but a stochastic differential equation, requiring special treatment

comments.issue: Stochasticity is only in resource growth rates; effects of stochasticity in other parameters are not examined.
comments.request: Discuss or test how other stochastic parameters affect the outcome.
comments.quote: The question is, how would stochasticity in other parameters affect the outcome? The answer is that the effects could be quite large

comments.issue: Using alpha for niche overlap conflicts with standard competition-coefficient notation.
comments.request: Use the standard rho notation.
comments.quote: Your use of Greek alpha, instead of Greek rho for niche overlap, is at odds with the common use in the literature where Greek alpha is used for competition coefficients

comments.issue: 'Generalized Lotka-Volterra' is used for linear per capita growth equations where the term is inappropriate.
comments.request: Call these equations just 'Lotka-Volterra'.
comments.quote: in my view “Generalized Lotka-Volterra” is bad terminology. It should be just “Lotka-Volterra” defined by the fact that per capita growth rates are linear in population densities

comments.issue: Figure 1 understates the redundancy between dynamical parameters and dynamics.
comments.request: Qualify the figure legend claim.
comments.quote: In fact mappings of dynamical parameters to dynamics are in general much more redundant than you represent here

comments.issue: Derivation from the full MacArthur equations is more redundant; measures should extend to general cases.
comments.request: Extend the measures to more general MacArthur situations.
comments.quote: It would be nice to see your measures extended so that they work across more general situations for the MacArthur equations

comments.issue: The standard assumption that makes D zero is deferred rather than discussed at first mention.
comments.request: Discuss deviations from proportional loss earlier.
comments.quote: the usual assumption in the MacArthur equations is that loss to the resource is proportional to benefit to the consumer. This means that your measure D is zero

comments.issue: Measure D ignores vector magnitudes and is invariant to swapping lambda vectors, missing intuitive mismatches.
comments.request: Show these cases do not invalidate D or extend the measure.
comments.quote: Since you base it on cosine distances, you have the situation where swapping the lambda vectors of two species, while keeping their gamma vectors the same, does not change D

comments.issue: Figure 3 scenarios (e.g. generalist dependence with specialist depletion) lack biological explanation or real examples.
comments.request: Discuss the biological circumstances and give examples.
comments.quote: The scenarios depicted in these figures are possible, but not what is generally expected, especially the positive correlation panel where there is generalist dependence but specialist depletion

comments.issue: Time-averaged neutral limit section adds little and could be omitted.
comments.request: Consider omitting this section.
comments.quote: this section adds very little, and you might want to omit it

comments.issue: 'Proportional' is the wrong word for a roughly linear relationship in Fig 5.
comments.request: Use 'linear' instead.
comments.quote: The correlations in the right panel are not proportional to niche overlap. “Proportional” is the wrong word

comments.issue: Serial dilution experiments do not follow the model, and how D was estimated is sketchy.
comments.request: Describe in detail how the D quantities were determined.
comments.quote: The fact that these are serial dilution experiments means they do not follow the equations in the manuscript. So there seems to be a gap here in how the measure D is defined in this case

comments.issue: Significance in Figure 6 may be driven by one outlying minimum-D point.
comments.request: Refit without the outlier and report significance.
comments.quote: I cannot help being concerned that much of the significance comes from 1 outlying point, i.e. that with the minimum value of D

comments.issue: F1 and F2 are not defined in the text.
comments.request: State what F1 and F2 represent.
comments.quote: you need to say what F1 and F2 are supposed to represent

comments.issue: Discussion content is not foreshadowed in the introduction; pairs with substantially nonzero D are not discussed.
