comments.quote: This discussion would have been beneficially foreshadowed earlier in the document. In particular, the introduction could mentioned these findings so that the development of D would have been better motivated

title: Niche Overlap Is Not Enough: Same Overlap, Contrasting Fluctuations

study.system: Dutch vegetation plots; species-accumulation curves over 90 years

editor_summary: Both reviewers highlight the novelty and importance but raise significant concerns about the species-area analysis: Reviewer 2 wants it statistically analysed rather than described, and Reviewer 1 sees diversity-distance and plot-density confounded with diversity-area.

reviews.assessment: Values the documentation of protected-area effects and grassland recovery, but wants the SAC variability statistically analysed rather than described.
strengths: documentation that protected areas are working
recovery in species numbers in the last 30 years

comments.issue: SAC variability is only described; drivers of biodiversity loss and recovery are not analysed.
comments.request: Analyse changes in SAC parameters as a function of local features.
comments.quote: My suggestion is to analyze the data, not just report it (SAC are just a way to report richness over space).

comments.issue: The title implies the loss was hidden, but biodiversity loss is already known and the latest trend is recovery.
comments.request: Revise the title framing.
comments.quote: not sure about the word ‘hidden’, the lost is already known and the latest trend is towards recovery

comments.issue: Period criteria, design layout and curve construction are insufficiently described to replicate the analysis.
comments.request: Describe the design and construction fully.
comments.quote: If one were to repeat this analysis, I’m not sure there is enough detail to replicate it

comments.issue: Figure 3 panels use different y-axis scales, preventing protected versus unprotected comparison.
comments.request: Use the same y-axis scale across panels.
comments.quote: it would be good to have the same scale in the y-axis to be able to compare between protected and unprotected

reviews.assessment: Sees strong merit but cannot recommend publication because species-accumulation curves from disjunct plots cannot be interpreted as species-area relationships.
strengths: strong merit in the general thesis

comments.issue: Species-accumulation curves from disjunct plots conflate beta diversity with plot area and are not species-area relationships.
comments.request: Recast the analysis and its interpretation.
comments.quote: it mixes the effects of beta diversity between plots with the area of plots, and so does not allow you to interpret the graphs you make as species-*area* relationships

comments.issue: Differences in plot placement and distances between time periods confound rarefaction comparisons.
comments.request: Analyse plot placement through time and standardize it.
comments.quote: changes in the spatial distributions of plots will affect the results of rarefaction, and thus any graphs against area or plot number

comments.issue: Unequal plot numbers and sizes across periods confound within-plot beta diversity with total area.
comments.request: Standardize plot density and size across periods.
comments.quote: you have more plots in the first and third time period than in the second, but the second has more total area sampled (larger mean plot size)

comments.issue: Ecoregion and protected-area comparisons are confounded by distances between subregions and beta diversity within single reserves.
comments.request: Do these comparisons carefully or not at all; assess sampling bias.
comments.quote: comparison across ecoregions and between PAs and non-PAs needs to be done very carefully—or not at all

comments.issue: Claims that more area is needed and that species-area relationships shifted are unsupported because plot distances differ.
comments.request: Remove or revise these statements.
comments.quote: we can’t tell if the differences in richness between time periods for a given area or number of plots is due to real changes in richness or with differences in distances between plots

comments.issue: Plot placement and density must be standardized before comparisons are valid.
comments.request: Thin plots to similar densities, sizes and distances per period.
comments.quote: you could thin (subsample/discard) the plots so there are similar densities, sizes, and between-plot distances in each time period

comments.issue: The data availability statement wrongly denies custom code; the analysis scripts should be provided.
comments.request: Provide the analysis code.
comments.quote: The statement, that “[t]his study did not involve custom code,” is untrue

comments.issue: Keywords duplicate terms already in the title or abstract, reducing search reach.
comments.request: Choose keywords not in the title or abstract.
comments.quote: I would suggest trying to select keywords that do not appear in the title or abstract

comments.issue: The native-species-only scope is absent from the abstract and title.
comments.request: State the native-species scope in the abstract and title.
comments.quote: That the analysis focused on just native species is an important “detail”. It should appear in the abstract

comments.issue: Whether plots sampled the same regions or had spatial biases that changed over time is unknown.
comments.request: Provide plot maps for each time period.
comments.quote: Did plots representatively sample the same regions, or were there notable spatial biases, and did these persist or change through time?

title: A Century of Shifting Native Species‐Accumulation Curves Reveals Long‐Term Biodiversity Loss

study.system: Weddell seals, Antarctica; lifetime reproductive success distributions

editor_summary: Premise enticing but revisions extensive; reviewers provided extensive feedback; manuscript needs significant reworking but could be valuable if suggestions addressed.

reviews.assessment: Valuable theory-data comparison, but the environmental and heterogeneity comparisons are hard to understand and interpret.
strengths: valuable opportunity to compare theory to data
close agreement between theory and data
important question of luck vs quality

comments.issue: The two LRS comparisons (environmental periods; individual heterogeneity) are difficult to understand and interpret.
comments.request: Be more explicit about methods, rationale and interpretation of these comparisons.
comments.quote: My main criticism of the paper concerns these two comparisons, which I find difficult to understand and interpret.

comments.issue: It is not obvious that vital rates were time-averaged because the LRS method assumes a constant environment.
comments.request: Make the time-averaging step and its assumptions explicit.
comments.quote: The time-averaging is necessary because Tuljapurkar et al derive LRS distributions under the assumption of a constant environment

comments.issue: The implications of comparing hypothetical constant-environment populations to real heterogeneous populations are unclear.
comments.request: Explain how to interpret the period comparison.
comments.quote: The implications of this for real populations of heterogeneous individuals under varying environmental conditions are not clear to me.

comments.issue: Constructing models with a fixed random effect for all individuals is confusing and its rationale is unclear.
comments.request: Clarify the fixed-random-effect approach and whether these are matrix models.
comments.quote: I am confused by this approach. Is the idea that the LRS distribution could shift to the right when the whole population is “higher quality” (RE = 1) than “lower quality” (RE = -2)?

comments.issue: Why LRS distributions are identical across quality scenarios needs discussion, including random-effect scale and correlations.
comments.request: Discuss why the distributions do not differ and the effect of RE correlation.
comments.quote: Is the negative correlation between random effects on survival and reproduction responsible for the unchanged LRS distributions?

comments.issue: Predicted distributions are hypothetical, time-invariant and homogeneous, not the real seal population; this distinction is unclear.
comments.request: Make this distinction explicit throughout.
comments.quote: Therefore none of these hypothetical populations corresponds to the actual seal population in which demographic and environmental stochasticity and individual heterogeneity occur simultaneously.

comments.issue: "Individuals with high IH" is wrong because heterogeneity is a population quantity.
comments.request: Rephrase using "quality" or similar.
comments.quote: my interpretation of ‘high heterogeneity’ would be ‘highly variable’ which is not applicable to an individual. Perhaps the terms “quality” is better?

comments.issue: 9 line-level writing edits (lines 52, 94, 122, 151, 154, 166, 181, 233, 234).
comments.quote: 151: Can the definition of longevity be expressed more directly?

comments.issue: It is unclear whether individual quality is already incorporated into the population models used.
comments.request: Clarify how individual quality enters the models.
comments.quote: Isn’t individual level quality incorporated into integral population models? Or matrix population models with individual random effects on vital rates?

comments.issue: The paragraph at lines 85-90 applies only to the first of the four questions but reads as if it covers all analyses.
comments.request: Clarify the scope of the paragraph.
comments.quote: This paragraph only applies to the first of the four questions posed after it, but the opening sentence suggests it applies to all analyses.

comments.issue: The Tuljapurkar et al. (2020) method and its assumptions are not introduced.
comments.request: Devote a paragraph to the method and how to interpret it.
comments.quote: It might help readers to devote a paragraph of the introduction to the method of Tuljapurkar et al (2020), describing it’s assumptions, and how analyses using it can be interpreted.

comments.issue: "Across periods" is ambiguous given that vital rates are assumed constant over time.
comments.request: Use "across environmental periods" or similar.
comments.quote: “across periods” can be interpreted as “across time periods” which is then confusing because the vital rates are assumed constant over time

comments.issue: phi and psi appear synonymous with s and r, mixing notation.
comments.request: Use a single notation throughout.
comments.quote: Are phi and psi synonymous with s and r, respectively? If so, I suggest only using one or the other in the notation.

comments.issue: Calling hypothetical populations "skewed" above/below average implies within-population variation that does not exist.
comments.request: Rephrase the description of the hypothetical populations.
comments.quote: I find it confusing to refer to the population as being ‘skewed’ above/below average, because that implies there is variation in the random effect within the hypothetical population

comments.issue: Uncertainty in vital-rate estimates is not propagated, so three-decimal reporting is overly precise.
comments.request: Propagate uncertainty and reduce reported precision.
comments.quote: there is uncertainty in these estimates, and this is not propagated through to the LRS distributions

comments.issue: The sentence starting at line 350 is unparseable.
comments.request: Rewrite the sentence.
comments.quote: 350: I cannot parse the sentence starting on this line.

comments.issue: It is unclear how "lucky" individuals could be identified if exceptional reproduction is chance-driven.
comments.request: Clarify the practical implication at line 433.
comments.quote: How would one identify these “lucky” individuals if it is mostly chance that results in their unusually large reproductive output?

comments.issue: Theoretical and empirical distributions are not plotted together in Figure 2.
comments.request: Plot both distributions on the same plot.
comments.quote: Figure 2: I would suggest plotting the theoretical and empirical distributions on the same plot to facilitate comparison.

comments.issue: The increased death probability at age 30 in Figure 3 may be a model artifact.
comments.request: Check and explain the age-30 mortality spike.
comments.quote: Figure 3 (top): the increased probability of death age 30 is presumably an artifact of some model assumptions?

reviews.assessment: Promising but currently a disjointed collection of results; a coherent story linking findings to earlier work is needed.
strengths: possibility for a really nice paper
lively and exciting read if explained

comments.issue: The paper reads as a collection of results with little connecting narrative.
comments.request: Tell a coherent story explaining the findings and their agreement with earlier work.
comments.quote: it feels like a collection of results and earlier findings with little binding them together

comments.issue: IH is an inappropriate label because heterogeneity is a population quantity; RE is vague.

comments.issue: Different statistics are reported for theoretical and empirical LRS distributions.

comments.issue: Theoretical and empirical results are placed side by side, preventing accurate comparison.

comments.issue: The argument about the unexpected historical mortality rate and study-period differences is confusing.

comments.issue: The probability calculations at line 263 are unclear and unexplained.

comments.issue: Section 4.3 could be shortened for length.

comments.issue: The story in section 5.3 is difficult to follow and lacks follow-up.

comments.issue: The recommendation to target individuals that dominate reproduction conflicts with the finding that success is largely luck.
comments.request: Reconsider the intervention-practice implication.
comments.quote: If that's the case, who is to say that an individual who has been lucky so far will continue to be lucky? There is nothing that distinguishes that individual from others.

comments.issue: "An extreme environmental event for lifetime" at line 93 is awkward.

comments.quote: I tripped over “an extreme environmental event for lifetime” and eventually decided that you probably meant “an extreme environmental event for their entire life.”

comments.issue: The longevity definition at line 151 is indirect.

comments.quote: the text could more clearly articulate how this perspective is distinct from ecological limits

comments.issue: The likelihood specification, optimisation strategy and LTT envelope-testing workflow need more detail.

comments.issue: Some results and discussion subsections are redundant.

comments.issue: The 8 Myr lag statement in the abstract needs more context to avoid confusing readers.

comments.quote: probably needs more context to avoid confusing the reader already in the abstract

comments.issue: How grid-cell size connects to speciation and colonisation processes is unclear.

comments.issue: The paragraph at line 136 does not explain why secondary sympatry is distinct from the ecological-limits hypothesis.

comments.issue: The clarity of the methods paragraphs should be transferred to the introduction.

comments.issue: How the likelihood was calculated and local optima avoided is not explained.

comments.issue: The LTT workflow (empirical versus simulated LTTs and model envelope) needs clarification.

comments.issue: The middle part of the results (lines 336-357) is redundant and its implications unclear.

comments.issue: The third discussion paragraph (lines 409-422) is redundant and could be merged.

comments.issue: The distinction between 'time for colonisation' and 'time for speciation' should be raised in the introduction.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 29-30 is unclear.

comments.issue: 'What is accumulating?' at line 36 does not specify species, lineages, branches or co-occurrences.

comments.issue: The sentence at lines 45-51 is very long.

comments.issue: Lines 151-154 do not state which data are used, which processes are estimated, or what historical distribution data exist.

comments.issue: The rationale for analysing both empirical and simulated data is unclear.

reviews.assessment: Values the integrated framework and rich dataset but flags a major conceptual issue with inferring climate adaptation from common-garden phenotypes.
strengths: integrates three major frameworks in one experiment

comments.issue: Adaptation is inferred from traits measured in one benign common-garden environment, ignoring plasticity, GxE and unmeasured population-structure covariates.
comments.request: Discuss plasticity, GxE and population structure limitations before claiming adaptation.
comments.quote: A major conceptual issue in my opinion is that requires clearer justification concerns the inference of climate adaptation from phenotypes measured exclusively under a single, benign common-garden greenhouse environment.

comments.issue: Correlations are repeatedly interpreted as adaptation although population structure, non-adaptive covariance and spatial autocorrelation cannot be excluded.
comments.request: Provide stronger evidence for adaptive evolution or temper the adaptation claims.
comments.quote: the manuscript frequently interprets these patterns as evidence of adaptation. However, without explicit evolutionary modeling, alternative explanations such as population structure, non-adaptive trait covariance, or spatial autocorrelation cannot be fully ruled out.

comments.issue: Trait-climate correlations are weak; significance likely reflects large sample size, so biological predictive power is low.
comments.quote: although the relationships between stomatal traits and climate variables are statistically significant, the correlation coefficients are relatively weak. I guess the significance is driven by the sample size, but bilogical predictive power is low.

comments.issue: High trait heritability but no significant individual SNP associations; the discussion should explain this null GWAS result given Arabidopsis's well-mapped pathways.
comments.request: Better contextualize why GWAS found no individual SNPs in Arabidopsis.
comments.quote: The reliance on top SNP enrichment is a valid approach, but the discussion could better contextualize why Arabidopsis—a model organism with well-mapped stomatal development pathways (e.g. SPCH, MUTE et al.).

comments.issue: The stress-avoidance argument assumes anatomical gmax translates into realized gas exchange, but conductance dynamics and photosynthesis were not measured.
comments.request: Measure or acknowledge the missing link to realized gas exchange.
comments.quote: The argument for stress avoidance highlight the assumption that higher anatomical gmax translates to higher realized gas exchange during favorable windows. However, no direct measurements of stomatal conductance dynamics or photosynthesis were collected.

comments.issue: Lines 346-365 read like Results rather than Discussion.
comments.request: Move or rewrite these parts as discussion.
comments.quote: Line 346-365, the parts are more like a Results sections rather than discussion sections

title: Dovetailing the Genetic, Developmental and Functional Bases of the Adaptation of Stomatal Traits to Climate
